name: For The King II
detailed_description: Once beloved by her people, Queen Rosomon has turned against her subjects, casting them into servitude in the darkness of Fahrul’s mines whilst building alliances with sinister and malevolent forces. Gather your party in four player co-op or adventure alone through Fahrul as you risk everything to fight the tyrannical queen and bring an end to her oppressive reign. From the creators of For The King, the much-loved RPG that blends roguelite and tabletop gameplay comes a new chapter in Fahrul’s history, designed on an updated engine bringing innovation and gameplay refinement for returning heroes and new adventurers alike. For The King II is easy for anyone to pick up and play, but takes skill, patience, and strategic excellence to master whilst remaining infinitely replayable with a procedurally generated map that ensures no two playthroughs will ever be the same. Unique yet familiar dice roll inspired movement, encounter and combat mechanics add even more spontaneity and variety as your fortunes rise and fall on the roll of the dice. For The King II provides a complete campaign with over 30 hours of gameplay, split into 5 separate adventures, each narratively linked. The journey is long and the path is treacherous but fear not, if your party fails you will start stronger and wiser on your next playthrough with better starting items to draft into your loadout. Roll up, roll up! Put your skills to the ultimate test with the infinite dungeon mode - Dark Carnival. Led by the devious Ringmaster, your goal is to conquer as many floors as possible before you meet your inevitable demise. Collect carnival tickets to explore new paths, discover a host of themed rooms and spin the Wheel of Death as you try to escape your fate. How far will you make it through the Dark Carnival? Traverse Fahrul solo or with up-to three friends in four-player co-op. As a solo player you can control all characters in your party, giving you complete ownership of the campaign map and combat strategy whilst in four-player co-op you must coordinate and negotiate with your party members. Play online multiplayer with your friends controlling your own character(s) or play offline co-op on the same PC. Offline co-op supports multiple controllers; each controller will have input control on everyone’s turn. Inspired by turn-based classics, For The King II adds strategic depth to much-loved combat mechanics with the new Battle Grid, where movement and position provide you and your enemies with strategic buffs and penalties. Defend the back row by equipping a mighty Tower Shield, push enemies into lethal pools of burning fire, or entangle melee troops with dark magic cast with weapons looted from vanquished foes. The choice is yours! Fahrul is both beautiful and deadly in equal measure. On your journey you will encounter a wealth of diverse biome environments brought to life in a breathtaking art style. From lush forests, toxic swamps and lava-filled wastelands to pirate (no scratch that!) Merling-infested tropical seas, For The King II transports you deep into the wonders of Fahrul, leading you further than ever before into this stunningly-imagined land of adventure.

short_description: Battle against Fahrul's tyrannical Queen alone or as a party of four players in the sequel to For The King, the massively popular turn-based roguelite tabletop RPG. Will you unravel the once beloved Queen's terrible secret?

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is a fun experience, and I found enjoyable. The issues with this game lie in the performance issues that exist. For me, they have not been game breaking so far, but I have noticed some performance issues here and there. The game at its root is fun, and I have faith the devs will work to patch the game. Disappointing that it has these issues, but the game is fun and for that I will rate it positively.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play FTK I. Overall I find this game not that fun and that there are real/amateur mistakes or game design flaws.Pros:-Graphics-Progression to unlock traits and powers-Classic fantasy feel-Surprise elements during adventures-I did not experience any crashes/bugsCons / To Improve:-Everything is slow/too many pauses, or poorly responsive, for example even with the combat speed at the highest level it feels sluggish and unexciting, as well as the pauses between heroes and die rolls to move on the map--between 4 heroes, combats and events, this really adds up. Loading times between combat and the map. Altogether, you see your real life time wasting away in this ultra time consuming experience to get the simplest things done, which you can do in 1/3 or half the time in other games. Feels like an unrewarding use of time and anticlimactic.-They use an archaic turn-based combat like in Final Fantasy games but in comparison, very few options per character. Most of the time, you'll use 1-2 of the same actions per character, and the grid is so small-8 places for 4 heros, a simple AI could be playing combat instead of you. If they don't improve on this, they could just implement an auto-battle choice.  -Controls and design are very poor. Ex. If you play with a mouse you have to use the keyboard to inspect instead of right click, in combat you can't click on a square to move there. -Game does not scale to starting with 2 or 3 heroes instead of 4-Furthermore, if the most reward is obtained from traveling together with all 4, just play Songs of Conquest. There needs to be rewards for spreading out like real significant XP for the entire party and not just from a dainty quest. Also, you can't group heroes innately (without a vehicle).Altogether, the game feels like a lackluster or hodgepodge experience and therefore not that fun compared to other titles. I would refund if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a challenge-based tactical combat game. It has two modes: (1) a birds-eye-view strategic mode where you explore the world, gather resources, and pick fights, and (2) the fighting mode of JRPG-like tactical combat. THE GOOD:- Learning the game mechanics and figuring out how to succeed in the game can be really fun.- The game takes the challenge seriously. For example, there's no save-scumming.- The harder difficulty levels can be quite tense.- Supports co-opTHE BAD:- This game is virtually identical to the original For the King. There is almost nothing new to learn in terms of strategy or tactics.- The dice-rolling mechanic is quite random. Even at max skill level, your characters will miss frequently and they never really feel competent. Failing all the time feels frustrating.- The plot and dialogue are paper-thin.- The game theoretically has a lot of replayability, but I found that the game got old rather quickly.- The character special abilities and the combat status effects are not explained in the game. I had to search online to know what they did.- Relative to FtK 1, it felt like the sequel had a lot less to offer in terms of interesting new locations and items you could buy with Lore points.THE UGLY:- I had some trouble playing co-op with me using the keyboard, and my partner using a controller. There kept being weird glitches where menus or the map would scroll endlessly in one direction. It took me a while to realise that the problem was that I'd left the (now invisible) mouse pointer on the edge of the screen.- In the original For the King, on the overland map, if you tried to move too far the game would automatically move you as far as you could go.  In FtK 2, the game just doesn't allow you to move. Sometimes, it's hard to understand why your character is not moving, especially when using the controller.- The game crashed on me once. Not a big deal, since it auto-saves every turn.- There is still a Hobo character class
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I loved FtK1 and love this game too. Still has a few bugs, maybe should have done a few more bug cycles before release, but the devs have been good about putting out hotfixes. My one issue with the game is that if you don't know how the game plays (i.e are a first time player) there are not enough tooltips/tutorials to explain what things do and how the game works. This game is built to be a "learn as you play" style game, but they might have gone a bit too far with that this time. That all being said, I am having a blast and the story and lore are cool!
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'm very happy that I can change this review back to recommend! The game was not working for a while, but that is now resolved, thanks to the avesome devs of this game!It's obvious that they really care about the product. As a fan of their first game, It was very sad to see how it was received upon launch. Although there were some bugs here and there, those 60% were just not deserved.However after some time, the game stopped working for me. Later a developer got in touch with me via their active community discord and we spend like two hours straight debugging the game. We eventually repaired it again.Given the current state of the gaming industry, It feels really rare to see a team caring about their community this much.And by the way, the reason why it was not working, was a bit anticlimactic.. Avast was was quarantining some key files. So if you face issues with a black screen on start, try disabling your third party antivirus and see if it works then.

_childDocuments_.review: The first chapter was fun, however the game is divided into 5 chapters and the second chapter is all luck based depending on your movement rolls and how quickly you find the randomly generated towns in randomly generated biomes. I spent an hour of my time just looking for the towns in chapter two on my day off after being excited to download and try this game.Ontop of the mission design being poor it is no where near what I was expecting for tile based FTK. I was expecting to be able to walk around on a tile map so my melee fighters could chase/trap archers and my mages could stay at a range and attack. Instead there is this goofy front and back row system where you're 10 feet from your enemy but cant walk any closer. Melee range doesnt matter you can attack corner to corner, the entire tile system was done poorly.Its also a rushed product that crashes quite frequently for many people on the discord.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the first installment, this is essentially a more polished and refined version with some new added features and I highly recommend picking it up.If you haven't played the first game, there will be a higher learning curve but this is a fun turn-based tabletop style RPG that doesn't take itself too seriously story-wise. Best experienced when playing with friends, but also plenty of fun solo. It's the type of game that's relatively easy to jump into but takes a while to master if you want to be efficient and play at higher difficulties.

This game really only relies on randomness to artificially increase difficulty of a game that is so trivially simple. _childDocuments_.review: Game is fun, runs well, visuals are nice, and etc, but there are a lot of bugs concerning general game features, as well as relatively frequent soft-locks forcing you to restart the game session. The Wet status effect literally did not function when applied to enemies until around 3 months post-launch. Tactics activating soft-locked my session. Generally speaking, upgraded pipes don't work when they're used between rooms in dungeons. You can change which player controls each character, which is great, but you can't change this unless you're on the world map. If a player disconnects in a dungeon, or for whatever other reason, the character controls are not assigned as you want, then you can't reallocate until the dungeon is over.Aside from bugs, there are plenty of problems with clarity on mechanics. For example, while there is an in-game encyclopedia of status effects, rules, and such, it's incomplete. This leads to frequent misunderstandings of game mechanics despite great effort on the players' part. Many items, attacks, and such have vague or misleading descriptions. Does this "full heal" include focus restoration? Does it include recovering statuses? Does it include removing curses? How am I supposed to know? Testing isn't exactly encouraged when confronted with a rare consumable item, or a precious turn in pretty punishing combat. Teleport scrolls have varying range based on your intelligence stat, but how do I know how far they'll go without just buying it and testing it out? The game should tell you these sorts details in item descriptions, and/or in the game encyclopedia.Separate from bugs and frustrating oversights from the developers, the gameplay is pretty fun. Your choices always feel meaningful, whether it's a decision of what to buy, where to go, what enemies to attack, or what goals/quests to prioritize. Most weapons do fill a purpose, and the secondary action system is a really great improvement that makes combat a lot more strategic, largely by allowing you to use many different weapons at once. Class choice is interesting, though I do wish there were a few more to choose from, and I especially miss the minstrel from the first game. Some status effects are a bit underwhelming like burn and daze, meanwhile shock is so important that my group relied on it very heavily throughout every session. Some imbalance is fine, and often RPGs have to rely on the players to simply not abuse the broken strategies. But I do think status effects and their associated weapons could use some serious tuning.Overall, I did enjoy the game, but I would have enjoyed it 10x more if it weren't for the constant soft-locks, confusion on mechanics, and other miscellaneous bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. The animations are enjoyable to watch, they've increased the amount of weapons you receive and the balancing of them, and its an overall enjoyable gameplay experience. Then there is everything else.I loved the first ♥♥♥ and many decisions for QoL really ruin the experience of this game. The extra loading screens entering a fight and leaving a fight just pad your playtime for no reason and becomes very frustrating immediately.  The pacing of the game is a lot more sped up with less time to meander as reducing chaos is not as common to come by. This makes doing side quests or exploring POI that appear on the map a big risk for little payout. At the time of writing this review, the game is littered with bugs that cause constant soft-locking, multiplayer disconnects, and problems restarting a previous run with friends.The devs are working hard to listen to all the players and fix bugs with the consistent patches but at its current state, I can't recommend this game unless you are a huge fan of the original and don't mind playing single player.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is, except for the graphics, mostly a downgrade compared to the first game.The fights are still plagued by random events, usefull traits like tactitian are based on pure chance and cannot be controlled by the players. Bosses are extremely imbalanced, dealing massive amounts of damage and sometimes being able to attack and/or call for backup without taking an actual turn. The campaigns so far have been quite boring, especially Chapter 2 is very tedious. All melee is more or less objectively worse than ranged attacks as melees are influenced by shields, can be completely countered by various status effects, and have smaller AoEs. Technically, the game is also still plagued by performance issues. I noticed increasing RAM consumption over time hinting at quite a lot of memory leaks. We also encountered various UI bugs so far. Also a lot of quality of live improvements are still necessary. Inventory UI closes when players move around on the map making inventory management very annoying, secondary actions can only be performed before primary actions, the alchemist cannot craft potions while on a landboat, ... All in all, the change in the combat system introducing two combat rows is interesting but severly underdeveloped and all other aspects of the game are done at most as best as in the previous game.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really enjoyable, some changes from the first game I really like, some changes I don't. Overall it's a fun game despite that.There are bugs and issues, but they're are getting fixed very quickly, one of the biggest multiplayer bugs got patched basically the day after launch, and other things are being fixed at a rapid rate as well. The game is in a much better state than it was a few days ago and definitely has earned a thumbs up from me.One thing that does kind of annoy me is that using an identify scroll on a chest. If it's a mimic, there's nothing special you can do, you can't get a free hit on it or anything you just know that it's a mimic now. Which means ♥♥♥♥ all in terms of the fact that you wasted a resource on figuring that out. You still have to fight it normally, and you get no bonuses afaik to fighting it. It's genuinely just better to sell the scroll to a vendor, which seems counter intuitive to me. Maybe I'm missing something tho.Anyways, fun game. will play more.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: *This review has been edited for clarity and after more time in game*I put in 180 hours into the first one and unlocked everything in the Lore Store.*Warning Spoilers*The positives :combat -This game improves a lot on the combat of the first game. The tile system is a interesting twist that gives the players more choices than in the previous game. I honestly wish there was more interaction and movement with the tiles possible. Various aoe patterns like a V shape, W shape, diagonals, outside tiles, inside tiles, etc. should be added to weapons or attacks for more variety.items - The item drops are more interesting with their varying stats and unique mechanics that can entirely change how your character plays. Some of the items from the Dark Carnival are really interesting and super fun to use.The maps - I like exploring each of the maps so far and discovering new enemy types and the various ways of dealing with the chaos countdown. I appreciate that they use multiple types of chaos in certain campaigns based on your progress.Enemy challenge - The enemies are varying difficulty based off what type of enemy they are. I love that a level 1 golem will absolutely ruin a party because they tried to fight it too early. The game makes you pick fights based off enemy type and your gear which makes it rewarding when you do take down a tough enemy. This information about enemies can be a bit of a learning curve at first and may discourage new players but I really like this approach of level isn't the only thing to pay attention to when picking fights/quests.The negatives:Class Balancing - Alchemist, Shepherd, and Pathfinder Alchemist is a near copy of the Scholar with vary similar stats however the alchemist has lower intelligence and talent which seem to be the primary stats for the class. It just doesn't seem like a smart choice to ever take the Alchemist when it doesn't have high enough talent to accurately throw bombs and the passive of creating bombs doesn't trigger nearly often enough for the choice to be worth it. An increase in odds of making bombs or an increase in Talent would let this class shine.Shepherd is basically useless unless you high roll and get the wolf especially compared to the scarecrows from Farmer. If the sheep did something that would be nice but at 1 hp and does nothing but hope to get hit I really don't like the design of a follower slot being taken up by a 1 hp mob that can't attack. Pathfinder dungeon scout ability doesn't work. This should be an easy fix and hopefully will get patched soon. The other ability to discover areas is really strong and very helpful.The Scourges - Bog Drinker, Lucky, Foul PreistessThis version of the game has improved on the variety of scourges able to be faced and lets you pull your party to you for the scourge fight. This doesn't move you on the map it just acts like a global fight range which is nice. This is actually a great change. However, the scourges have some pretty big issues currently.Bog Drinker is a early game nightmare as he will often out heal your parties dps while also poisoning people mid combat often lowering their potential to out dps his heals. This enemy is fine mid and late game but if he is the level 1 scourge you basically need to reset the run because you won't be able to kill this enemy until about level 3 with good gear. Meanwhile he will be poisoning the map and making it near impossible to progress with lowered stats. His heal needs to scale with his level and the number of player characters.Lucky is fine other than the fact he will sometimes just steal and run over and over before you can kill him even if you all crit. It just feels like a waste of time having to load into the fight just to watch him take 10 gold and then run over and over. A fix for this would be that he can't steal on turn one so you have at least 2 turns of combat to kill him.Foul Priestess is actually a relatively easy fight but I think that may be because she seems to be bugged currently. She does a animation where she creates a dark mist over the team once you get her low but it doesn't seem to do anything other than make certain allies get an extra turn. I'm not sure if this is intended or her attack isn't working but some clarity with text of what happened would be helpful.Scourge item drops -Currently the Scourge item drops are a joke and do not scale or have variety to them. Why does a level 1 scourge in one play through drop the same quality item as a level 6 scourge in another? Even adding something like a couple stats to the items would be nice or giving them a unique buff based on the scourge level would really help make these items actually useful.Playing with less than 4 characters-There can be a lot said about the insane difficulty hike that is playing with less than a party of 4. The scourge and boss combats do not scale well to less characters as they will often spawn more enemies than you can handle unless both of your characters have very strong aoe and your characters are 2-3 levels up on the enemies. Even with good gear it can still be  impossible to win certain fights especially when an enemy can skip your turn.The minecart level isn't manageable with less than 3 characters. They will simply spawn too far apart and too often for you to be able to manage them. I'm aware that you can turn down the chaos frequency in the options but by default this map especially should check the amount of player characters and lower the frequency accordingly. (I am not sure at this time if changing these settings lowers the amount of lore books).Overall - I genuinely like this game a lot and want to see it be very successful. For The King 2 has a really solid foundation but it definitely needs some balance passes and bug fixes before I will give it a positive review. It currently feels like a early access title and that is not what it is listed as.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it because it's For The King, and I liked that game so much, it's really good.For The King 2 isn't ready yet. Come back in 6 months or so when it's actually finished and playable. There are so many annoying softlocks and crashes, you really have to be in the mood for a bugfest and enjoy how badly a lot of stuff is programmed. It looks like they've built everything from the very beginning again, and it's ended up a lot worse. Really bad UI, and some pretty poor balance decisions that will obviously be patched, but that just give the impression they never tested their own game. Porting over exact stats for enemies from For The King 1 seems reasonable, but now everyone gets the same amount of turns, Speed is only turn order. The result is that slow but strong characters/enemies like jelly cubes are -ridiculously- overtuned, which is a learning curve like any RPG, but just also reeks of a lack of care when making the game. Combat is really slow, it doesn't flow well with all the loading screens. For overworld balance, it's nice the Chaos progression is different, but... the execution of it is awful. In For The King 1, Chaos was consistent in how it progressed or was stopped. For The King 2 seems to have plot points that completely erase the current Chaos meter, to start a new one. Meaning that you're really punished if you get the reset too early, since you get no value for it, losing out on a whole load of turns that you could've been grinding. Tutorial for this is bad, advising players to hurry which is the wrong play.Difficulty for the game is fine, it doesn't seem any harder/easier than the first overall, once seeing past the poor tutorials and design choices. It just feels like a beta/early access game - which I'm sorta okay with, but can't recommendEdit 09/12/2023: It's nice to see the game being hotfixed for things, so credit there. Everything from the above still applies to the current state of the game though. A lot of items don't work how the tooltip states, a lot of weapons/attacks don't function correctly.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to see this game releasing but alas, it has failed to meet even the bare minimum of my expectations. I won't lie and say I'm some expert at the first game, so I expected to have issues related to skill, but the issues with this sequel are not at all what I thought they would be. This is most definitely not good enough for release and frankly just feels bad to play. There are quite a few glitches and while there  an option to send a bug report via the "Esc" menu, the bug report feature. . . also doesn't work! One of the biggest issues I have with the game currently are that there are no instructions on how to do many basic things, or what many things do, etc. I don't expect games to hold my hand but I  expect them to at least give you an inkling of how the actual controls function. There's nowhere that explains how to actually utilize focus in-combat, for example; are you supposed to hold keys on the keyboard and then click a roll slot? Is there some random arcane key combination I'm supposed to enter? Who knows! If a character dies in-combat and you want to revive them, the UI has nothing that tells you how many lives you have left in your pool, and in fact it's never even explained whether or not you  a life pool to begin with. If you go to a market and want to buy a weapon, or loot one, and it has all kinds of symbols on it, you have to guess what they mean as there's nothing that explains it .  I got a staff that had Protect on it, awesome! What does Protect do? Something! Is this weapon two-handed? Maybe! Better hope it's worth it or you've just blown your gold on trash! Want to turn the camera to help you target things better? No, sorry, that sucks for you, the characters are rendered in 3-D but you can only see one side of them at a time!While the developers have reacted quickly with hotfixes, I can't imagine they're going to spend the time to completely overhaul the UI of the game to address many of the glaring issues of which I detailed just the barest few of, and unfortunately for that reason I have to recommend against this purchase. I've requested a refund myself and can only hope it will be approved.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it hard to believe that anyone has actually play tested this game and said "yup, we can ship this."Here's the average gameplay experience when using an ability:1. You select the ability.2. You put focus points into it.3. It doesn't work. It simply does not put focus points.4. You switch to a different ability.5. You switch back to the original ability that you want to use.6. You're now allowed to use focus points.7. You put your focus points into the ability.8. You select an enemy.9. The game has now removed all the focus points.10. You use your focus points, again.11. You click on the enemy, again.12. You've now successfully used an ability.More fun stuff:- Everything feels super clunky and laggy. Even rolling for movement and actually moving on the map feels HORRIBLE.- The UI/UX is the worst I've ever had to experience. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You can't see your party's items or stats whenever anything at all is happening.- Enemies just randomly despawn on the world map, including some shops and other NPCs. It's so incredibly frustrating. Apparently it's when daytime changes but the game never tells you this and imo it just feels awful even if you know about it.- Auto end turn will end your turn even if you could still move or interact with an object on the world map. It's unusable.- Every enemy has at least three different immunities. It's already incredibly hit or miss to use CC abilities, but the fact that 90% of the enemies are also immune against all kinds of ♥♥♥♥ is extremely unfun game design. You basically just end up spamming one damage ability every fight.- 80% of chests are mimics. They also drop the worst ♥♥♥♥ imaginable. It's unfun and unrewarding.- Randomly wiping (yes, wiping. This means you have to restart) three fights into a new playthrough because you came across three slimes on YOUR LEVEL that absolutely ass blast you.- You can't save in a dungeon, which can have up to five fights.- Loading a multiplayer game will always reset who controlled which hero.- Enemies will put effects on certain tiles - but the fun part is you don't know what they are or what they do. You can't hover over the tile to find out, and if you don't just eat it and pray, you'll never actually find out.- Drop tables are generally terrible. You'll find the same bland items for literally hours. There is little variation and no interaction.- It's almost impossible to see your character's traits inside of combat. We eventually got to some party overview because someone randomly held mouse wheel and moused to the side (?). However this only works sometimes.- No one will introduce you to aggro range, support range and smaller aggro and support range in swamps (I think?)- Some dungeons have the same enemy group three times in a row. Why?- Your party will be randomly spread out across the board sometimes. Why? When? I still don't know. But I didn't want my tank in the back row.- The music is unbearably monotonous. I usually like ingame music but I had to turn it off.- The game will disconnect you from multiplayer at will.- You can unlock new characters in game (but no one tells you how), which you can then buy from the lore store (but no one tells you what they do or what stats they have before).Bonus treat: This is all from just the first of five chapters. And I'm sure there'll be more.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The core of this game is magnificent and a joy to play despite some of its flaws.Playing solo and the game is fun, challenging, and rewarding. Play on Apprentice difficulty to begin with TRUST ME. You get the same Lore rewards regardless and it will help you make quick inroads into the real game which IMO starts in Chapter 2. You can always go back and play on higher difficulties for the challenge later. I see lots of reviews/complaints about UI and some minor bugs, and I will say this game is gloriously vague with mechanics/terms at times which can be frustrating, and a clean up of the UI would massively improve that. There is also some simple fixes like overlapping windows that need addressing. Any bugs I've encountered have not been game breaking or seriously effected my enjoyment though. Most of the complaints you read from others are true and valid, but perhaps a bit harsh. If you don't mind using the encyclopedia in game, or a bit of trial and error, you'll get a grasp of the game and UI pretty quick. Hopefully they patch the game and make it less vague and add tool tips on mouse over for conditions, traits, and skills. I can't speak for multiplayer as I haven't tried it, but it looks like it has its own bugs and challenges right now. Multiplayer would also certainly add some difficulty due to less party co-ordination in an already tough game, so again swallow your pride and play on apprentice at least to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first game, quickly became a favorite of mine. The second has improved on many things from the first game, including the extra character. _childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been great! I really enjoyed the first game and I can easily say I am very excited to play the second game. The original game was a very good version of simple DND style turn based combat (sort of like Final Fantasy turn based) and this new game has a few added elements. So far it has been a blast to learn the new ins and outs of the game. I think there is so much more content that it's a much harder game to learn from the first but I also enjoy the added dynamics of a 4 person party and more elements to consider in your combat and composition.Pros:- It's 4 player now!- The story is continuing off of a really basic but fun premise of the land- The combat is much more straight forward with more obvious explanations- The characters are definitely more individualized- There is way more lootCons:- This isn't as easy to pick up as the first game was- Enemy combat is sort of overwhelming at times and not as easily predicted- The map is insanely larger, like 4-5x as large which is more difficult to traverse- Some attacks/abilities feel entirely useless-- Overall this game get's a 8.5/10 already out the gates for me. It's a great DND inspired RPG game to play with friends or solo. The game itself is more complex and seemingly more difficult than it's earlier version. This is not a bad thing. I have not encountered any bugs or glitches so far and hope to continue this adventure with my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I was really looking forward to the release of For the King 2. When I pre-ordered the whole thing and finally started it last night and started the first campaign with my wife, the euphoria was unfortunately quickly gone. Starting with the UI, which is a complete step backwards from the first part. For example, you can no longer glide over all the icons with the mouse and get an information text, instead you have to go to the encyclopedia and read what status X or hero skill Y does. The next thing is the optimization, I know the second part is a bit prettier and looks fresher and more modern, but it can't be that I have +160fps in the first part and have to struggle with 60 fps in this part. Also, the fights are insanely drawn out, I remember that in the first part you only needed 2-3 hits for the enemies and the fight in "quick mode" lasted 30 seconds at most. In this part, an animation to take a healing herb alone takes almost 5 seconds. (Yes, I know, you can speed up the fight by left-clicking, but if you're playing with several people, it's easy to press the buttons in such a way that you skip your colleague's move and click on something).Also not being able to see party stats without opening the inventory is a pain. I don´t know why you just don´t implemented everything from FTK1 and then improved from there. In addition, the combat camera is set absolutely unfavorably, I have already clicked on a lot of wrong fields because the angle of the camera is sometimes so badly positioned behind my character, that I no longer have the opportunity to click on the enemy. To be honest, I´m refunding this game and maybe come back again in some months when some of the things are fixed or either modding has taken over. I´m gonna play FTK1 in the meantime.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRA mechanically and visually better version of For the King 1, even if I had to get over my love for low poly graphics. Common complaints are the chapter system and the absence of bards on the release day.The best and most prevalent new features are with the improved combat mechanics. All of this I will explain:Firstly, bards are returning soon in a coming update, and there are tons of new classes to keep you occupied in the mean-time.Secondly, I think the chapter system is great. Chapters still take several hours, like campaigns in the first game, so long term planning is still required. However, nothing is carried between runs. Not players, nor items. Some people dislike this feature, but I think it is great because with the massive amounts of added build variety thanks to new classes and traits, it gives me an opportunity to try other builds for my characters and keeps the game-play fresh across a long period of time.Additionally, I absolutely love the new combat system, which allows for much more strategy than the original game. New secondary actions allow players to do support actions and use their weapon on the same turn. Gone are the days of wasting turns from reloading, switching weapons or taunting, and say hello to the new depth of strategy gained from using secondary actions to move around the battle grid to get in formation.Also, Hildebrant is still alive <3 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite fun, a compelling improvement on the first one. Graphics are much nicer, new tactics via the battle grid are fun, and a much easier to understand tutorial in the first chapter of the campaign. For those new to the franchise, the game has a very boardgame-y feel, in particular the time mechanic and skill rolls remind me a lot of Arkham Horror.Since a lot of people have commented on the difficulty, here's my opinion. If you have played For the King I, I don't think this game is harder, but it it certainly isn't easy. For reference I completed the first and second chapters both on the first try, the first on apprentice difficulty and the second on journeyman difficulty, but on the original game I lost multiple times before every completing a single campaign on the easiest difficulty. For those considering the game without having played the first one, I definitely think this is the superior version. Just be prepared to TPK while learning the mechanics and strategies, and use the difficulty sliders if you're feeling frustrated.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, Just not so great balancing issues:Main Issues: Starting items/equipment: Money is hands down the best thing you can start with, easy to unlock lots of it after your first run and it's starting point cost effective. why start with a 0-9 damage hammer and +2 armour boots when you can straight away buy 3-4 times better equipment in the starting town.Fix: Buff starting equipment, or make it more about utility rather then equipment, herbs, drinks, hard to obtain items, etc.Starting Traits: Deep thinker, Gifted, nimble and maybe Lucky, they are the only reliable and useful starting traits. why take a 25% chance to get first turn in combat when you can have +3 to ALL stats? I'm fine with chance based effects, that's what make games like this fun, but there's no point when the effects are useless.Fix: Buff other traits, make Tactician permanently active or an action, make Supportive stack or just remove it, Navigator needs to be active in all cases, make it a flat +2 or +1 to movement. And lastly make Eager always activate upon combat start or buff it to a 50% or higher.Performance: Game runs like a obese hampter on a wheel, the more the game runs the worst frames and load times get, The frames and over all just performance of the game feels slow, chucky and unpleasant. Swapping between characters with shops open or mid dungeon is painful and buggy.Fix: Not sure on frames and such, but you should consider making the UI more simplistic and user friendly, think of quality of life over looks, as well as give each player more freedom on others turns, you basically become a prisoner anytime a party member starts their turn.Positioning: PLEASE let us pick where or character will start on the field, i can understand for an ambush if your displaced but why after walking 10 tiles to a single wood wolf would you be out of place? Certain classes and weapons are useless because of this, Friar is one of them, a magic tank but if you put a magic staff or wand on him he starts in the back?????, it's pointless to have random positioning other then to annoy your players, it barely effects game-play and is just a pain.Fix: Just let us as a party and as a single player select your spot in the field before hand or out of combat.Game Balance as a whole: unfair events, bosses that are much harder then implied, and fair to may unfair or unfun moves from enemies, almost very enemy has armour or resistance penetration, pushing and shoving enemies is mostly pointless, daze just doesn't work on anything other then movement for enemies, (merling gunner reloading while dazed, etc), level 1 and 2 bosses one shotting a level 4-5 party, necromancer spawns 7 allies every 4 or so rounds which is impossible with out a over leveled party or two mages all with good AOE weapons.Fix: Rethink or redo most of the things listed above or don't, it's not unplayable in this state, it takes a few runs ending or save scumming to get the tricks and tips of most of that above and there is counter play to SOME of it or at least steps you can take to stop it. aside from daze and such obviously.In the end i can't really be bother to explain each little issue in detail, I'm sure others are have these problems in one way or another, I'll never refund or uninstall this game, I just hope one day they fix it or improve this stuff.7/10 A good sequel with a long way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should have an early access label on it just for the balancing alone. not to mention how much worse the game runs than the last one. They split up the singular long campaign from the first game into a bunch of smaller chapters, which is good in theory bc it means you don't have to replay the start of the campaign as much, but in reality it just makes the game more repetitive as because there isn't much difference in the early parts of any of the levels. furthermore the balancing in this game is atrocious a ring that gives you a +2% chance to hit is valued the same as a ring that gives you +2 attack damage, and  books are several orders of magnitude stronger than any other of the magic weapons, not to mention that the extremely short duration of the levels make healing between fights almost trivial as opposed to the major strategic decision it was in the first game. On top of this, the game is just generally pretty buggy, especially in multiplayer. Even if you don't encounter any crashes (I haven't had any in singleplayer) the game will often behave weirdly with things like inflation behaving weirdly or certain things just not triggering.TLDR: If you have played the first game and enjoyed it it could be worth a play, if you have not played the first game play it instead and save your money.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Builds on every system of the previous game, and combat has evolved in a way that gets your team planning and working together more with new abilities and builds. The writing and art is more mature and less whimsical but still the same recognisable style. To those criticising that each chapter your character resets, you are completely misguided. Each chapter is long enough that by the end your build is finalised and there's nowhere left to go. Restarting next chapter gives you a chance to try new builds and buy more unlockables which is the bread and butter of roguelites. Additionally, RNG is part of the game and by nature it can feel unfair at times but that's part of what you're signing up for.

_childDocuments_.review: While the gameplay loop is very fun, the UI decisions are very questionable and some of the bugs are gamebreaking. _childDocuments_.review: Edited Review.Originally, my review was pretty negative...and while there are still issues, my opinion has changed from don't get this, to get it if you really want it, but beware. The game still has plenty of bugs, but they are working hard to address all of the issues. Nothing seems to be game breaking..and if you save scum because something completely unfair happens, then the game is extremely playable / enjoyable. (ie. player with 8 health heals himself and then chooses to revive an ally. After reviving, the player who healed reverted back to 8 health and lost his healing item....we had to reload the game bc that was BS)Overall, it's a great game so far. Nice continuation from the first game with new battle mechanics that add a new layer of depth. That said, some of the overlay decisions they made leave much to be desired. IE. I don't know if they did this to have a cleaner look, but in the old one you could just always see everyone's player stats at the bottom of the screen. Now you have to click on their player portrait to see what their stats are, and if you're in certain menus, you can't see it at all. It makes passing gear around way more clunky.Here's my reasoning behind the major change of heart. The game has / had a GAME BREAKING BUG! ....BUT..... FEAR NOT!!!!! The issue was that I was a BETA player and I guess I never uninstalled the game. I then purchased / installed the actual game. Afterwards, I realized that I still had BETA installed as well, so I uninstalled it. Apparently, BETA and the actual game install to the same place, so when I uninstalled, it removed files from the actual game.WARNING!!!!!! If you played BETA, uninstall first and then install the actual game. If you didn't do this in the correct order, just uninstall the real game and reinstall it. I don't think verifying files is enough to fix it (I could be wrong). If you don't, when you run into the bug, your whole save file will become corrupted.

_childDocuments_.review: I love those kind of games and at first glance For the king 2 seemed to be a relaxed adventure rpg. It turns out that in the long run your skills are about 30-40% of the game and everything else is rng.Things I do like: -battle system-huge variety of weapons and armour-a lot of classes and some customisation-Random encountersThings I do not like:-Mediocre-boring travelling system-Too much rng involved to everything (from looting to hits and encounters)-Should have a proper save feature. So far you can only continue. I hate having to restart after several hours into a campaign that got ruined by one mistake, or by bad luck, in one battle. My humble opinion is that this "roguelike" element do not bond well with this type of game.-Enemy camps and world encounters should have duration visible! So many times I have travelled long distances only for the desired encounter-camp to disappear.I really wanted to like this game, but at the end i found it tiring and at times boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much like what I see off the launch. No bugs thus far, so can't comment on that, but here's a few things instantly noticeable:Changes from FTK:- Extra Character to control (Player 4)- Pets! Some encounters when successfully passed allow companions to join the battle (Even if you have a full party, Max 4).- Class selection is now more tailored specific in roles IE: Blacksmith used to be STR based, now HP/Tank based, Stablehand (New Class) leans more STR/SPD. If you're looking for specific build types, you're in luck.- Tons of new equipment, and even at lower levels the gear rating/stats on them are nice.- Graphics overhaul, now with Dream mode, makes the characters look like active claymation. Tim Burton would approve.- Soundtrack is fuller/richer, overall quality is audible.- Multi-classing feels like a much more viable option now. In FTK you were scraping the barrel to try to cover all the bases with Talent, Luck, and Speed and with these stats not being a main build, it made it sometimes infuriatingly difficult to do the random quests that would require members of your party to have these more obscure stats. With FTK2 the gear alone leans in different directions, so that Rogue/Mage build you thought about last time, isn't just an idea or wish.- 8 more colors to choose from for your character's base gear... (expected a little more effort put into the character creator in FTK2)- Herbs are now subtly different. The effects have changed slightly, so read before you use.- The Tutorials are now an option in the settings menu, so if you're familiar with the previous FTK, you can skip over some of the basics, though I would recommend turning it on as their are so many additional changes.- Tactics - 4x2 grid allow more AOE attack tactics, and some defensive strategy as well.Areas that need tweaking:- Mimics have always been obnoxious, but the frequency in which they pop up needs to be toned down, especially at beginner level (0-2). It's difficult enough to start getting good gear, only to have it eaten directly off your character.- The timing feels rushed, and this applies to both Apprentice & Journeyman settings. It's a new game, I don't want to fly through it, and I don't want to have my squad not even partially geared going into level 3, but having to sprint away because the 2nd chaos just locked in, and the group is 20 hexs away from the 3rd.- 4x2 combat is great, but it doesn't feel like the front row is really tanking all that well. They're called meatshields for a reason, they should be taking more damage vs. those on the back row instead of acting like a conduit for the damage. 5% isn't much of a defensive bonus.- Combat speed - The option exists for you to increase the combat speed, but this isn't a button that you can just click in the upper hand corner of the screen and lock it in, instead you have to left click each battle and if you're late can even mean that you can potentially skip or do a move for the next character involuntarily.- Town Quests - Level balancing is off by a heavy margin. It's not feasible to run around to get to level 3 just to fight the mob for the quest because you're already under chaos penalties. One or both needs altering.- Swapping gold/inventory - Previous version had a mini menu that allowed for swift exchange in gold, and getting into your inventory also felt easier. With this release it's more muddled and nowhere near at the ready.Looking at the roadmap, QoL improvements are slated until end of the year & into the 1st qtr of the new year, so good on the IronOak/Curve crew for planning ahead. Hopefully we'll see some of these issues tamed soon.So far solid, and feels like a great continuation from FTK, thanks for all the hard work put into it.

The adventure being cut into chapters allows for more starts with different loadout options and helps maintain gameplay balance but I do miss progressing further with the same group.  Stat variety on equipment really adds to the variety.  For some reason enemy evasion still isn't displayed.  Grid based system is alright. _childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It's FTK1 with more content and a longer campaign. I love the art style and the visuals. The balancing is very tight and filled with a lot of fun options. All of the archetypes are uniquely viable and the item system makes it easy to compensate for any piece you're missing. The map is chock full of evens, items, enemies, and curiosities to explore.  That being said, if you're not a fan of For the King already, this game has a pretty heinous burden of knowledge you have to overcome to survive, and I'm not really here to sugar coat that. Basically everything you fight is deadly (or dangerous in some unique way), you have very limited healing and resources, and if you don't know what you're looking for, you can waste all your time doing nothing.  If you fall behind the curve or attempt to fight above your level, this game gets brutal quickly. Its' basically the 'souls-like' equivalent of a turn based RPG. It's also RNG based, so expect occasional bouts of the numbers just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on you.Its weird a lot of the reviews tend to be focusing on minute things (not diminishing bugs - bug complaints are valid). I mean, It's annoying they make it so arcane to discern what all the symbols and special abilities mean, but I was really only glued to the glossary for like the first hour or so I was playing, and I playced the first FTK for well over a hundred hours, so it's really not that big of a deal comparatively.

_childDocuments_.review: With over 150 hours on FTK1, I've been waiting for this game for a while now. Sadly, in its current state, it's just a worst game than the first one, and here's why:1. UI, espacially for charachter selection and for inventory, needs upgrading. Its clunky and unintuitive. 2. Want to take your time, find the dungeons and do side quests ? You can't. The new 'chaos timer' will make it so that if you don't rush the main quest, you simply loose the game and have to start over. Think you have time to do a side quest ? It'll randomly disappear even if the timer on it says you have 3 rounds left to do it.3. Although the 2 rows fighting system seems like a nice addition, fixed camera makes it weird and clunky, sometimes making it really hard to be able to click on an enemy behind another one. I really don't understand why the devs didn't make it so we can move the camera around in a fight, makes 0 sense. Also, if you don't know what the effect of an item does, well good luck with that. No tooltip, no name for it, just an image and play the guess game on what it does !4. Finished your fight and trying to distribute loot ? You can't see your charachters inventory or stats. Wanna give gold to your char who has the highest gold multiplier ? Hope you know by heart who it is. After that, you quit the fight and come back in the overworld ? Camera is bugged, zommed in to the max and you can't zoom out until you finish your turn.5. Got to a town and you want to sell items and buy stuff in the market ? It's impossible to easily switch between charachters inventory, you have to close the market window, then close the town window, then click on another charachter and click his inventory open to see what he has. Then you close that, click back on the charachter in town, open back the town menu, open back the market menu, etc..... Why ?!6. You finally bought an item and want to equip/use it ? The tooltip for it often shows up so high in the screen that the use/equip button is unclickable. 7. You can't just save your game, like all normal games: you have to 'save and quit'. Haven't 'saved and quit' the game yet and it crashes because its buggy ? Your game is over, start again, there are no auto saves. Kinda feels like the devs never tried their game or if there's been no beta/early access at all. I would recommend waiting for a few patches before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: If judged as a standalone game, For the King 2 might be decent. However, compared to its predecessor, it’s a significant step backward. Playing this sequel feels unpleasant due to polished mechanics and a clean interface from the first game being replaced with new raw systems.The switch from voxel graphics to 3D models doesn’t work in its favor — the visuals feel bland and uninspired. Combat is chaotic and monotonous. Most weapons offer a basic attack and a secondary one with ineffective effects. Ineffective because no matter what debuff you inflict, enemies still retaliate with physical attacks. It’s often better to spam basic attacks for the highest hit chance, though even this gets frustrating, as many enemies have absurd dodge stats. Perfect attacks miss frequently because of this. Most enemies are immune to status effects, too.In the first game, the balance was flawless — every item felt valuable. Here, you’re overwhelmed with useless junk, which is only good for selling, yet you hardly need money. The wild RNG, designed to force focus usage, discourages engaging with map events, as 4 out of 5 times, you’ll lose. Even a rare success doesn’t justify the losses.The new movement system during combat is pointless, as most enemies have either AoE or heavy single-target attacks. AoE hits everyone, and heavy attacks can one-shot your tanks. Ironically, a party of four musicians at the backline performs better than a tank-dps/support setup.Other issues include painfully slow scene transitions before every battle, an inconvenient and confusing interface, and a complete lack of emotional connection to the characters. Quests feel unbalanced, and there are countless small annoyances, such as the end-turn button being reassigned from Space to DEL, forcing heavy mouse reliance. Constant stuttering, like when changing a hero’s class, makes the game feel like an unfinished alpha version but certainly not a completed product.And again, this comparison is to the near-perfect original game. I'm disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It does all the things the first game does, but basically nothing new - and many things plain worse. A lot of the issues seem to be due to the game being essentially early access with many things still missing or incomplete. However, it isn't being sold as early access - so I kinda expect a somewhat finished product.So what are the positives and negatives?The bad:> UI. It's absolutely terrible and will lead to much frustration.> Controller support is essentially a lie.> Some item classes are super underrepresented. Speed weapons for example, which are the basis for an entire class, are non existent after the starter tier. A lot of this is supposed to come later but again, this is sold as a finished product.> New mechanics, sometimes introduced late in a chapter, aren't explained sufficiently, leading to you throwing a chapter after hours of gameplay because there was no way you could've known how to blow up that mining cart. Good luck.> Difficulty progression: In certain chapters, the game just jumps from level zero to level three enemies instantly, leaving you almost no chance to level.> Super underdeveloped combat mechanics: The new row function for example is...something I guess? But it is of basically no consequence. Could have done more with that. Likewise, there are weapons of a myriad of different damage types - so why are there no weaknesses? That would finally give me a reason to not just always use the bow with the biggest number. Could have done so much more while still keeping it very simple.> The new followers you can hire are absolutely useless. They last for six turns only, but usually cost as much as four or so healing items. Unless I find them in the wild for free, I don't bother.> No more electric guitar bard class.  :(> Generally much less playful art design.The good:> ...so there's a super janky physics engine now, which is entirely useless but leads to some hilarious cannonball situations I guess?...> The basic gameplay still mostly works.> The loadout system is pretty fun.> I like the alchemist. And I'm trying to fill the "good stuff" section.In conclusion, if you and your friends are desperate for more after the excellent first game, go for it. If you haven't played the first one yet, buy that. It's plain better and this one is a massive disappointment in what it brings to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to be adding to the review. Please can more developers make more games like this. The mechanics are fun. I still love playing this with my friends. The upgrades to FTK is fantastic. The weapon variety is excellent. The armours are all unique allowing for more customized gameplay. The loadout is a nice idea. Tanking is more engaging. Some interesting ideas for classes. However, the bad: I don't like how unfair some enemies feel. When taking 30 damage with 20 armour against a basic wolf 1/3 hitting me from a basic enemy is disappointing. The scourge issue needs addressing. Bandit king usually spawns at level 1 in a level 6 zone on the second chapter. Many bugs are gamebreaking. Most scourges drop hats which is a little boring and half of them aren't worth the time/resource sink. Certain adventures feel like you HAVE to pick certain characters if you want a shot at the game. The loadout while a nice idea. The summon book is so much fun, I wish some of the other weapons felt as cool as that! Shepard and Farmer feel very similar in their operation. Although I don't know if sheep was supposed to have inbuilt distract or something? 4 loadout points for a shield that gives 1 armour and 1 resistance is not worth the points! Blacksmith already starts with a 1 armour shield for free. The gold makes sense because it comes as 10, 20 and 40 respectively. I feel like everything could be lower to allow for more loadout start choices. Bandit King and Necromancer feel like the most op scourges and annoying side affects for not dealing with them. (if you are not properly prepared. I really wanna love this game as there is a lot of good going for it. But the bugs, the hard enemies and downright unfair mechanics sometimes feel like too much for a player wanting to enjoy with a couple of friends. I also wanna put out there that I'm sure plenty of people think this game can be easily exploited, but I don't want to have to go through tons of effort to play a game. I want to play it my way and everyone be allowed to play it their way too.

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus the time flew by fast...If I had to describe this game in one word it would have to be "Chaotic".I played FTK I with my friends and had a blast, then we heard about FTK II and we were hyped. So just today we played from the point that it came out, til' about now... (Off by ~30 min cause I was asleep and had to download it.) We had our 3rd run (We don't think we are crazy at the game, but I'm sure we have our moments) and we went from full health with 8 Godsbeards between the 3 of us to 1 person alive with no Godsbeards praying for a dodge to win. (Super Funny). Here are my general thoughts though:Positive:Music: Overall it is just beautiful. (we made it to a boss and we were all like "OMFG" lol.)Gameplay: It does feel like FTK I, but doesn't at the same time. The fights feel much longer, but you level up much faster. (IMO) The whole idea of the tiles make the game much more dynamic. The game still screws with you in very rough ways, but it doesn't feel as punishing for just being alive. Much more punishing for making a mistake though.Looks: Amazing! I mean I'm never really a looks kind of guy, but I love how it looks. Neutral:UI: I don't really understand it, but I have a friend that says that he can understand what some people say. I don't know, but I will see reviews here say "the UI looks like crap and the game is buggy" then not recommend it. That's rude, lol.Multiplayer: I will put it in "Neutral" cause the game JUST came out. It has some problems with connecting, loading, and some options not be available while in the game, but that shouldn't be a major "Negative". All it is, is that the game is getting its servers abused. It happens... A lot...Negatives:Buggy: I will acknowledge this problem. People have a hard time loading in, people can't access certain things, people can't play with others, and its a legitimate problem. Hell, me and my friends had a hard time connecting when we first started, then during out 3rd run the host couldn't do anything and he had to restart his game, then we couldn't access party management so he had to start the server again, then we got it working. But for crying out loud, don't "play" 30 mins, come here saying that you couldn't play cause it's too buggy and not recommend it. If you don't want to play a buggy game, then don't play during the launch, simple. Overall: Beautiful game. Do I recommend it right now? Possibly. If you are okay with having problems in a game, then yeah go for it! Games are meant to be laughed about and enjoyed. But if you need it to have no problems whatsoever while playing a game then no, don't, not yet at least. Will I recommend it later when problems have been sorted out? Most Likely. The game already is extremely fun and funnier with friends. So as the self-proclaimed "Sorcerer Supreme" (my herbalist with a fire staff), I officially claim this game as reviewed and recommend it to most people looking for good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't express enough how satisfying this sequel really is. It encompasses the entirety of the first game and adds several elements that make the game itself a little less stressful and more fun with a comedic dialog. Improved graphics, 4 player parties, traits and lore bonuses to give your game a boost and a chapter based story quest line really improves upon the replayibility of FTK2. I recommend this for group play to just have fun with some friends playing a challenging table top immersive experience. Single player is equally enjoyable and rewardable as a game to pick up and put down since it saves after each turn (doesn't save mid fight or dungeon)

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised to see so many negative reviews, as the game runs fine for me. That said, I do have a high-end PC and I have only played for four hours as I post this. My friends have less powerful PCs and have experienced no problems either.The game in my opinion is a level up from FTK1. The graphics are beautiful, and I love that they have managed to not only improve the look of the game, but kept the same appreciated artstyle. As some people have mentioned, the camera settings in some indoor dungeon battles can be a pain but I haven't found it rage-inducing. The "Chessboard" layout now really makes you think about character positioning and target-attack order which I find quite welcoming. It adds a little to the game. I'm early into this edition and while only putting in 60 hours or so into FTK1, I really appreciate this kind of game and the Devs behind it. I never would have purchased this kind of game before and FTK has encouraged me and my friends to get stuck in and appreciate games like this, Baldurs Gate 3 and more, when I previously never would have. That shows how user friendly the game is in this genre for new players.I'm not saying problems aren't happening at all - I can't comment as they aren't happening to me or my friends - but I did want to put an early feeler out there amongst the many negative reviews to say that actually, there are some positive reviews of this game so far and I have no complaints. The devs are open, fix problems quickly and add new content to the game often. I would recommend it "in it's current state" but to highlight again for what seems like the hundredth time, we have encountered zero issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I love FOR THE KING 1It's great that you can run endless dungeons with friends, but the rewards are boring and hardly available. You often get 4-5 weapons for a bard but nothing for a magician for a long time.Furthermore, the tactical options are limited, there is a lack of skills that build on each other. Of course, you can ice your opponents and then do more damage. But that's it, there are hardly any combinations in a character, only in the group are they, but these are simple and boring in the group.why aren't there more options like ultimates. Furthermore, it's boring to wait for the allies rounds - you actually know what you're doing unless you have to heal yourself.Possibilities to make the game better with little effortPossibilities to make the game better with little effort1* Increase combat speed 3x 6x2* Don't make damage dependent on the luck of the dice too much. its better if Damage only increases slightly per focus but has a special effect at 100%.3. Doesn't make the loot total (rnd) gives the game a higher chance of getting the items you need for the highest attributes.4. brings in a skill tree in which you choose your main stat and weapon and with every level up you get a box with the item or a weapon with your main stat.Increases the chance of looting items of this type and in better quality5. gives people the opportunity to choose their position, I think that's only in the game because there's not enough to do and otherwise the gameplay becomes monotonous. Nevertheless, you shouldn't bring anything into the game that is just boring,annoying and unnecessary.6.And the coolest thing would be a special ability that you have with your class depending on the weapon. like magician sometimes casts twice magic and the chance increases with luck.I think you know what's boring about the game but you don't want to take any risks, that's perfectly fine, it's your game, but I guarantee you if nothing changes you'll lose more players.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game a good rating except for one thing.The chaos mechanic is so obviously broken.So every so often you get attacks which can be changed during setup, however even at the absolute lowest level its only 10 turns between these attacks.Now firstly, these attacks are the hardest thing you will face, esp in the early game. Its normally around 5-6 enemies, heavily armoured and hard hitting. So losing lives is likely to happen.Not only this, but you get nothing from the fight either, nothing at all. No XP, no items. Nothing.So, in otherwords you have a difficult fight that likely loses your life every 10 turns, gaining no XP and no items from it. It has to be in my mind the stupidest mechanic ive ever seen in a game, because it seems to just punish the player for not being prepared, levelling and gaining gold. Id recommend playing something else, something thats fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Patience is a good thing to have in order to overcome hardships and trials.This game is testing mine, combined with all the obvious QoL or fixes people have suggested in various reviews already, and the missed opportunity to name the game For the Queen.A friend bought me this game to play and it's reminding me why I never finished much of the first one. TL:DR, cannot recommend in current state, buggy and poorly made UI and controls with atrocious balance.Questionable mechanics, such as Taunt requiring two rolls to succeed, and if you don't hit both rolls it fails and your turn is wasted, and even if it does work, you only get one round and have to retaunt next round, turning a tank into nothing other than a damage sponge. Could make it so if one of two tokens hit, you get 1 round of taunt, two rounds for two tokens letting you actually do something the next round.Multiple early game enemies having Entangle, which will seemingly always get put on a melee character locking them up from doing anything (other than the aforementioned taunt which will end up failing anyways.) Could be fixed with being able to use a bonus action to pull yourself up from the roots but stay on same tile for the turn, reapplying Entangled for the second turn when you end.One of the first required fights of Chapter 2 is a group of 4 imps, with Evasive. Evasive means you cannot hit the target unless you get a perfect attack. Have a weapon who's attack only has two tokens for a Perfect? Good luck. How about a weapon with 4? 5? You're more likely to just restart the game upon realizing you selected a couple characters with bad weapon rolls to start with. Individual XP for the group members, meaning for someone to get XP they have to be in the ongoing fight, combined with whatever Chaos time limit mechanic leaves you unable to do anything other than sticking to each other like it's a kindergarten class holding hands while crossing the street or fear of being hit by a car/ambushed by a rat that is gonna pull 3 other enemies into the fight. Adding on top of that, me and friends have only gotten a bit into Chapter 2 (chapter 1 was beaten as we found out because we got two different Cannons at the start and it carried us the entire game. Imagine having a bomb usable every single turn.) but we have to go to three separate towns that are on opposite sides of the map and fight 3 separate waves of 4-5 Goblins all with AoE attacks. Once again all on a time limit.ADDING ON TO THAT, they have this new Landboat that you can gather your party in to make sure you're the one hitting the goblins with a car, except it takes damage as it moves and uses Talent for movement rolls instead of Speed, and it doesn't actually help beyond making it so your entire party can move together using each others movement. Hope you had fun grabbing those various POIs on the way to things cause you better learn to tuck and roll.I'll edit this review as I possibly play more, but it's amazing that the first two nodes on their "Roadmap" is just marked as QoL patches while this isn't an early access game.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, really great! A mechanical upgrade to For The King that carries over the strengths while improving on the weaknesses of the original, with an exception made for the hit/damage calculations, which are no longer plainly bound to your attack rolls. A shame, that; this new take muddies up what used to be a totally elegant system.We encountered some minor bugs in multiplayer that involved the inventory window being sticky-- hard to open and close without spamming 'i' several times and hard to close, even if it appears closed-- you could very well be trying to click the map, but actually be clicking the items in your inventory that outright, which can prevent taking your turn until you fiddle with it. And we had to have everyone restart the game when we couldn't get a lobby to work after quitting a previous session and restarting. But those things are absolutely minor, and they'll get ironed out easily-- and I think it's merely those issues that have the masses up in arms in the reviews here.Apart from minor errors, the only other complaints I have are about being unable to see monster status effect tooltips when it isn't your turn, pressing your inventory button during someone else's turn pulls up their stuff instead of yours, and introducing secondary actions but not linking them to support abilities was, in my view, a missed opportunity that would have added legitimacy to support actions that otherwise remain very difficult to justify spending an attack action on.Still though- this is a success, I'd say. The bombing going on is absolutely not an indication of quality. It's a misguided "incentive" being levied by folks who don't trust developers at large-- even though this particular creator deserves more trust than they're being offered.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed all of the available chapters at least once I thought it was time to post a review. Loved FTK1 and revisit it often especially in multiplayer. FTK2 is on a par with the first. Not hugely different from the first and sadly not a great deal better.Unlike others I did not encounter any crashes or game breaking bugs.  Quite a few irritations and some flawed gameplay mechanics which for a sequel is a rather a shame as some have carried over from FTK1.Biggest difference is the combat grid system, which should/could have made this a better game. I posted at length about this on the forum, so not going to repeat myself in this review. Bottom line not control on starting formation even when you ambush, which is just daft. Result is characters often start in un-advantageous combat formation which can take several turns of moving to resolve by which time you have taken a lot of damage or died. Particularly galling if you ambushed the enemy!The game does tend to put tanks with shields at the front row, but that is about the limit of the games intelligence. Swap positions move option might help, but really an ability to predefine a formation for use when Ambushing or initiating combat would be better. If I am ambushed then fair enough, starting formation will likely be a mess.Irritations & gripes.The encyclopaedia is still missing explanations of some the abilities and affects e.g. Cleansing, Cure aura, Chaos effect. Even some of those in the encyclopaedia are a bit light on explanation. Hitting enemies can sometimes impart an effect on your character. So for example my Blacksmith might hit a guard successfully, but is then inflicted with bleeding. I have had characters start burning, become poisoned or shocked. Let me be clear, this is not as a result of the enemy hitting me, this is me hitting them. I assume this is in fact a bug, as it does not work the other way around i.e. Enemy starts burning/bleeding etc. after hitting me.  Enemy hit percentages constantly better than mine. Same as FTK1, sorry to say. You can dial this out to a degree with adjusting overall game difficulty and increasing stats as the game progresses with gear etc. Not a game breaker but irritating nonetheless.Too many enemies have too many resistances or are immune to all effects. I guess this to compensate for poor enemy AI.  Not enough items with confuse immunity. With the grid system and enemies that seems to have access to an unlimited number of bombs to throw at you, the grid too easily gets peppered with squares I cannot or don’t want to move into. I like a challenge but sometimes it does feel like the AI is taking the @#]$!. Feel like I could use the Trait ‘Batsman’ and maybe hit a few of them back! That would be funny.I admit I still have one more character to unlock, and a small number of loadout items, but so far there is only one character (Healer) that has the ability to Party Heal at the start of the game. Items dropped in game that have that ability seem pretty rare, especially early game, so I feel pressured into having to have at least one healer in my party at the start.Nice to see some new characters, however I find Shepard and Farmer a pain. The combat grid is tricky enough without uncontrollable NPC’s on the board, especially if starting combat formations are undefinable. Traits are a nice addition. I have unlocked all those available. A ‘Medic’ Trait would be a good addition and encourage me to pay some of the other characters more often.Not being able to save in a dungeon (same as FTK1) is still not option, I don’t understand why not. I would also like to see a ‘Try again’ option or ability to load an earlier save, as the last save is deleted if your team gets wiped. Bit severe after potentially hours of gameplay? You can get around this by copying off saved games yourself, but you should not have to do that.  In combat Healing has not really changed since FTK1 and makes no allowance for the fact there are now four characters in the team. As a result a party heal rarely heals the whole party even when stood next to each other.A few gripes, but nevertheless I do not regret buying FTK2 and will no doubt play it to death like I did FTK1. So pack your Godsbeard, don your hat (Too many hats in this game btw!), grab your Pointy Stick, go forth into Fahrul, and enjoy!
