_childDocuments_.review: Meh.... is the best description for this game.  I really enjoyed For The King 1 and had high hopes for this game.  It just seems incomplete.  It is not as open ended or Rogue like as the first.  The quests are all very scripted and it simply is not as adventurous or fun as the FTK 1.  The fact that there are turn limits to complete the scenarios just ruin it.  Part of the fun of the original was exploring and finding cool stuff but in FTK 2 you have no time to explore the map, in fact you only get to see about 25% of the map because of the scripted times quests.  Using Chaos to push players to hurry up as they did in FTK 1 is a way better system to use instead of turn limits. Another big problem is the game just downgraded rewards as in gives less of everything  money, treasure, weapons and makes it very difficult to have your characters level up when there is now a time limit.   When you finally move to the next level you have almost no money to buy anything.  To make it even worse after you kill some tougher opponents your reward is almost nothing.  You usually get weak weapons, very little money, and almost nothing else. You have to rely on your herbalist or scholar to find something while traveling.   The game just doesn't click like FTK 1.  The lack of open game play, scripted everything, few rewards, and the fact you are forced to play their horribly designed levels makes this game just gets old fast.  I will still play it but it is in major need of a big upgrade in open play, add 10-15% more to all rewards, add mods, make beginning characters stronger, and eliminate the max turns.   Also enemy evasion needs to be lowered 15%.  You can go 10 attacks and they will dodge everything. Again I do not hate the game but the potential was there it just didn't execute.  I do in fact like the graphics, animations, the ability to add additional characters to your team so it has some good solid upgrades but just too canned.  I will continue to play it but I give it a 3 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: The UI in this game is abhorrent and the onboarding is painful. I'm 90mins in tearing my hair out at how I'm being clumsily introduced to this game with my questions unanswered by meaningful information conveyed fluidly and I played FTK 1 extensively, so god bless if you're new. To only then be mandatory rerouted to the Discord server to have my what are painfully basic questions answered by the community, when the game has an ENTIRE encyclopedia meant for this task! For example, I don't know what the starter weapons "cure" skill does outside of defining the word myself and assuming it does what I hope it does. Did you think it cured curses? Nope, coulda fooled me. If only I could shift click over the weapon and hover over "cure" to tell me what it did in a little pop up rather than having to open an encyclopedia for every symbol and word every 5 seconds, only to find half of them not there at all including "Cure", a STARTER skill. That's just the starter weapon and skills, so what does that mean for more complex mechanics. Maybe I'm missing popups or tooltips somewhere, but it hurts to use the interface.Oddly specific you might be saying, but that was just when I stopped playing, so it's fresh in my head. It's really the egregious, offensive, dogsh1t UI that ad naus has you pausing the game (where the esc key isn't "back" by the way) to decipher some nonsense on screen that's being poorly communicated that really has me refunding this game. It's a ton of clicks opening and closing menus (all manually) for too little payoff. Too little, hard to decipher or meaningless information being displayed in poor ways that's really the cake. Using the UI and therefore playing the game is an excruciatingly monotonous, rage inducing exercise in frustration and I can't be bothered to go any further, I'm sorry, respectfully. I'll try again in a few months, but it just doesn't seem ready for a positive user experience. I can't enjoy a roguelite where difficulty traditionally directly correlates to understanding the game to improve each run and the game just fails to do this in a concise way.

_childDocuments_.review: While a fun addition to the original game the shortness of the sections and overall lower polish of features that were already in the first game makes this feel incredibly incomplete as an experience. Having basic things back such as the map updating when I use a focus to increase how many tiles I can move or even doing the same when I stop hovering over a move in combat after using focus so utilising the game mechanics actually feels more polished. There's a hell of a lot of polish this game needs, before I plan to even begin picking it up again. I really do hope to see it improve along with maybe even having a campaign that feels as long as the original as currently with each chapter resetting my party and the lore store only really serving as a micro boost without anything all that majorly interesting to pick up the power scaling of the game just feels off. I don't feel like the characters become much more powerful, instead just as stronger weapons and items start to appear and character levels get to a point where it feels like the game will pick up like the first game did the chapter ends and you have to restart all over again. Overall my current experience has been lacklustre, I really looked forward to this game but basic polish that was there in the first game isn't there in this iteration and the scaling/power growth of your team from the first game also just doesn't really feel like it's there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: My now wife introduced me to the first game years ago and it was one of the first games we ever played together. I was so excited to pre-order the sequel for both of us, especially because it came out on our honeymoon! We’ve had a wonderful time so far carousing through Fahrul, and love the new characters and mechanics from this game. It brings back a lot of the best parts of the first game as well, and it’s great to have the same humor and ragdoll mechanics. Our party of 4 pathfinders had a great time trying to get through Chapter 3 (right before it was re-balanced) and succeeding with only 1 character alive felt like a great win in spirit of the game. While there have been a few launch day bugs, the devs have been super responsive about smashing them to bits- every time we’ve come back from a honeymoon date there has been a new hot fix! They are also responsive on Discord and it’s been nice to see them fostering a good community there while helping people solve game issues.

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically all I wanted from a For The King sequel. The classes are more like characters now with more personality to them. Visually the game looks nicer and is more detailed. The new loadout system is very interesting and adds more variety in runs and how you build your team. The new grid system lets you have more strategy in battles and allows for tanks to actually do their job and block for weaker allies. If you have some friends that all want to try a 4 player coop game, or you liked the first, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD:- The new models and animations are an absolute delight to watch- Even the very few changes they made to the combat make it way more engaging- Same with the classes, not much changes but you actually notice your class abilities (and can even play around for some), unlike in FTK1 where many of the classes felt like had completely unconsequential traits- The loadout before an adventure is a fun addition, especially where you can pick a trait for everyoneTHE BAD- While the new animations and models are great, the overworld map suffered insanely with the new artstyle. It's soo difficult to read the map from a distance. Also there are some really stupid things about it, like sometimes a few branches will block a whole hex, meanwhile there are complete buildings that cover the hex they are on, but still allow you to move over them.- The ui is actually not as bad as people make it out to be (altho it was worse on launch apparently). There are some things that it does better and some things that it does worse than the previous game. HOWEVER it is objectively more difficult to open up/read things (like markets in different towns) on the other players turn.- UI again --> there are some... glitchy phenomenons that happen regularly. We regularly literally see different things on our screens with friends. Like a monster hitting their roll on his screen apparently, while missing on mine.- They could've included more unlockables NEUTRAL- The game is not that long  (currently 2/5 chapters in) HOWEVER it wasn't much longer in the previous game either - the replayability there also came from trying to complete it on master. If you expected way more content then take this as a negative. I don't really mind it because it is already quite a few hours of enjoyment, but tbh i hope they add a few more maps before doing paid dlc's.TLDR:More of the same game with graphics and ui that you will either prefer over the previous one or don't. Combat is objectively better. Don't expect more content however than the previous game had on launch. Some annoyances with multiplayer, but nothing gamebreaking as of yet (two 6 hour sessions).

_childDocuments_.review: Here are the points that are a step back from the first one:(I played with the controller)- 4Player (and 2 rows for the team and the enemies to place the characters on ) makes for a cramped battle screen.- Life Bars and stats cover the characters and enemies on the already cramped battlefield and are hard to read from afar.- the battle UI is a massive step back from the first game. In the first game, the attacks and magic spells were nicely centered on the screen so anyone could see and read them (especially if you play couch co-op).Also, if you choose to attack, the "dice roll" is not in the middle of the screen but rather moved to the bottom. now you have this very smallscreen in the bottom right corner for the attack and magic.-The overall interface is made for sitting maximum 1 meter away from the screen. Good luck reading the text if you are sitting 2 or 3 meters away.- Loading screens between the battles...- The overworld and general UI are also a massive step back. 4 character stat screens are cramped in the bottom left, and you can only see how much of the stats like luck, speed, strength, each character has if you are the actual player. If you find a random encounter requiring a specific stat, you cannot immediately see who is the best choice for the encounter.The list goes on and on. There is so much where I have to scratch my head and ask why they added something in the game or removed another thing. Everything feels like a step down from the first game.I will update this on a later time again :)

_childDocuments_.review: Even after 75 hours the ui is barely tolerable and sometimes unusable. Gets worse with a controller. Ui is the games worst opponent and even though it has gotten better with patches, it takes multiple hours to start to see everything you need so you can react to it efficiently and you dont have to go through a checklist so you dont miss a detail. I have no idea why you would make the most necessary UI elements barely visible. UI issues continue even in combat as the kraken is horrible, since the head blocks the ui element you need to click to launch the attack. Other issues are the constant resetting of ui elements, nonsensical actions in the sense that you need to know when the UI resets when using stores and even then it is not predictable most of the time. It would be nice for the cursor to stay in the same place when you sell stuff so you can trust your actions when selling stuff.We now found out that some of the chapter achievements dont spawn in multiplayer if any of the party members have completed them, this was in chapter one for the alchemist cart. Either it was a bug or it was because one of the party members had allready found it. So you cant even grind achievements as a group if someone has completed them. (Propably the kill and round counter ones still work)Great sequel to the original with lots of great ideas that made me exited to play Ftk2, but the execution makes most of the playthroughs tiring experience where you spend too much time just fighting with the UI instead of the monsters. Launch of the game was also completely unredeemable as the game was completely unplayable since day three after the launch. I honestly dont recommend this even for the fans of the original since the execution just takes a dump to your face and makes you regret paying the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow, they failed to learn any lessons from the first game. FtK2 is still an absolute train wreck in regards to quality of life features. _childDocuments_.review: I played through all the campaigns in FTK1 and would love to be able to play this game. However, game breaking bugs that the devs claim to have fixed are still present. _childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BE FOOLED, I LOVE THIS GAME. Just not in it's current state.Graphically, "For The King II" is a feast for the eyes. The developers have outdone themselves, enhancing the unique, stylized aesthetic that gives the game its charm. Character models are more refined, animations are smoother, and the environments are vividly realized, making each biome a pleasure to behold. However, this is where the game hits a snag. The very act of delving into the game's world is where the sequel loses its way. "For The King II" introduces a rapidly depleting chaos meter, which races against the player's urge to explore. In this installment, the game ends once chaos overtakes the land. This design choice, intended to raise stakes, inadvertently punishes curiosity and discourages detours in favor of a mad dash through objectives. It strips away the leisurely joy of exploration, leaving a hurried pace in its wake that feels at odds with the game's adventurous spirit.Moreover, the claim of procedural generation falls flat when the sense of the unknown is lost. Each chapter's layout, while shuffled, conforms to a predictable pattern that dulls the sense of discovery. The sanctums and stone heroes, once stumbled upon in awe during aimless wanderings, are now objectives to be ticked off a list rather than treasures unearthed in wide-eyed wonder. In "For the King II", Each biome always has 1 sanctum and 1 stone hero, just to name an example.While the original "For The King" left players to chart their own course through an opaque and mysterious world, the sequel lays down a path too clear and straight. The randomized elements feel like variations on a theme rather than entirely new compositions. For those who relished the explorative symphony of the first game, this can feel like a constrained and repetitive tune.In essence, "For The King II" excels in the heat of battle and delights the eye with its artistic tapestry but forgets that the heart of adventure lies in the freedom to roam. The game's structure, with its choking chaos and linear levels, undermines the very core of what made its forerunner a beloved gem: the liberty to get lost in a world brimming with secrets and wonder. One can only hope that future iterations or updates will recapture that spirit, allowing the franchise to fully realize its regal potential.I was tired, so I wrote my grievances to chat-gpt, it sums it up pretty well. TL:DR, Replayability is lost when the path is linear; Exploration is punished when every turn feels like a race against the clock(chaos).They can fix this, so don't feel pressured to not buy off of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first game and put about 150 hours into it, but the second one needs SO much work as it still feels like it is still in beta at best. I cannot recommend it at this point, unfortunately. I suspect the team will get it to a good state eventually, but I recommend holding off until that point.There are still a number of noteworthy balancing issues, from classes having extreme power ranges from near useless to incredibly overpowered, although a recent patch has helped this a bit. While the game provides you an option on how many characters you want in the party, it isn't really balanced around less than four. There have been a number of game freezing bugs I've encountered that require you to crash the game and redo battles.In regards to new mechanics, while the new grid-based combat system is interesting, it feels like there could have been a lot more done with it. Why can't we set a formation for battle? I could understand maybe if you were ambushed your formation is random, but when initiating combat it makes no sense that the party is all in random positions.Another issue is the gear diversity. Some stats just do not have many options for weapons. This is particularly noticeable for talent and speed builds who suffer from an extreme lack of weapon variety, although I think awareness feels a bit light on options as well. The previous game had this same issue with speed, but speed was such a niche build that it wasn't really an issue. For the King II has a primary speed character now, so this lack of variety (and availability) for speed is a little more apparent now.Lastly, the game doesn't seem to have the spark the first game had. This could admittedly be due to the first game having more of the novelty than the second, but overall the first just felt more polished, even shortly after release. The campaign maps were more interesting, the extra modes added some freshness (although those may come later for For the King II), etc.That said, I have enjoyed the expanded variety of characters. The recent patches have been solving some of the issues, or at least mitigating them. Again, I suspect this will eventually be a game worth purchasing, but at this point I feel like it needs a lot of work. I think by Christmas '24 it should be in a much better state, or at least I certainly hope so!

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, this seems like better graphics on a worse game coming from FTK1. I really don't see enough of a difference, outside of some systems getting worse and the UI being questionably worse as well. Was really looking forward to this one, but it seems like a miss for me.Edit since the dev's responded and I owe them that-I actually came back to the game to try it again over the last week, and I've pumped ~30 hours into it. It's an ok game now, but it's maybe the most frustrating experience I've had. It's sooo close to being good, but certain mechanics are so bad that you have to wonder what drugs the devs were on, because I do a lot and they're stronger than mine.First, the game's balanced around nothing happening. Missing, dodging, etc. It's loooong. There are many enemies with evade, and you can sit there just missing each other for a year. 95 in a stat and you're still not getting perfects regularly, it's... it's a something.There's a ton of crappy mechanics... like boats/landships. The durability goes way too fast for them to be useful, since there's not enough gold to repair it while also buying anything anywhere (because you had 6 wizard hats drop and everyones now hatted but otherwise naked).Speaking of, the loot drops are terrible. I guess the game is meant to be truly "random", so you might just get one item over and over and over, or you might get a bunch of things that are useless, etc. That would make more sense if you somehow had an effect on stats, but you choose your class out the gate... so good luck if all you get is walking sticks and you don't have an awareness focused class. You might just literally never get something useful.I guess it's meant to play more like a board game than an rpg experience, which is... I mean I guess. I don't know if that's fun, but it's the game.I keep playing it because it's SO CLOSE to good. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:A marked improvement over the original, although, fair criticism: this feels like FtK+ I fail to see the issue, however. More of the same is a weird argument...I try to crack that nut below. Buy it on discount if you're so inclined--I did, and I think devs deserve all the support.--------------------------------------------------------------------I don't know why other reviewers are saying "more of the same" as if that's a bad thing. They're ignoring the better visuals, overhauled combat, and plenty of new items--not to mention the UI has better conveyance than before. Skills and abilities are now properly explained in-game, so no more consulting a wiki to discover exactly what factors into your 'find herb' skill proccing or whether it works in a dungeon or no... Perhaps this is too specific an example. Suffice to say FtK2 fixed several minor grievances I had with the first game.What's new?The core gameplay remains largely the same--outside of combat. Fans of the Monster Den series will appreciate the new combat (I know I do), but I understand if you prefer the old. Also, the new loadout system is a bit restrictive, but with the addition of traits and mercs I feel it balances out.Edit: actually, the loadout is awesome if only because you can start with better weapons than the default, which was one of my minor grievances in the first game.In short, this is more of the same, yes, but they've added tons more content and improved on what made the game great to begin with. The improved visuals are the icing on the cake. I hope you found this helpful.

Please keep going IronOak Games!!! <3 OLD REVIEW STARTS HERE  - (Time played: 1.9 hours)**** I played and loved ftk1 loads. I played the alpha of ftk2 and it had loads of bugs as well as just general issues. I’m sad to say that nearly none of these issues have been addressed. Even the UI is awful. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm disappointed. I really enjoyed the first game and was hoping for improvements, not a massive downgrade. There is so little freedom to move about in this game that multiplayer exploration feels dangerous (in a game where resources are vital to survival). When breaking up the group feels this way, you don't, and makes individual turns to move around the map all but useless. Then the game introduces a landship to drive your crew around together, further cementing the lack of need to have individual turns. You end up stuck waiting for the VITALITY character's turn to do a map tile, and the others just have to sit around and wait. The game needs a better system for exploration that allows you to choose which character takes on a challenge if all players are present. And further distance to join encounters would really help keep the team spread out if individual turns remain. Otherwise just lump them together.

_childDocuments_.review: Was pretty disappointed after how much I loved FTK 1.  Was really looking forward to this, but it's essentially the same game as the first one, but somehow not as good.  The combat feels not as fun/satisfying, the start of the game is exponentially harder compared to the first game (and the first one was tough), which is fine, but I've tried to play through the start multiple times and my runs have either ended or been close enough that there's no point in continuing.  I don't mind a game being hard; that's what made the first game so rewarding when you beat it! However, the beginning is so unfriendly that it makes for a pretty lame experience.  If you don't have the best party, the right items, and good rng, good luck doing any side quests or trying to prep for mid/end game. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely has some improvements that need to be made asap, game froze in combat and I lost over an hour of progress because the only option was to quit to menu. Other impactful issues is characters that show up as in range of fights not being pulled in, buffs and debuffs that arent explained when hovering (though much of the terminology is reused from FTK1, new players won't understand these and there are a lot that make it inconvenient to look up while playing.) Also, some playthroughs the objectives are much closer together than in others and it can sometimes seem impossible to get  a whole party to a certain objective within the time limits.HOWEVER, I love this new game. 4 players instead of just 3 is huge. The graphics are really pretty and easy for me to follow. The unlockable content makes it feel like even though you lost your run, you didn't lose hours of your time for nothing. Also, I appreciate that you don't HAVE to have a group of friends to enjoy it. Playing solo doesn't feel miserable.It seems like the devs really care about the game and the players experience, so I know many of these early issues will be addressed (and sooner than 10 years or never like some other games *cough* ARK *cough).Excited to see where this game goes.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review upon completion of the 2nd chapter of the game.I find that a mixed rating does not represent what this game has to offer at all.While there are some performance issues and bugs, which can be expected since the game just released, the developers are already working on fixing those.The game offers lot's of improvements when compared to the 1st game of the series. The previous "chaos system" has had some changes, adding more variety to your adventures, while offering great timespans/negative effects to drive you to main quest completion.The unlocking of new characters, traits, items and more happens at a nice pace, almost always offering something new to look forward to, even if you fail on your quest the first time. This also adds a lot of replayability value, so you can spend lot's of hours completing adventures without getting bored.The only reason I see for disliking this game, other than some bugs and performance issues (which will likely be fixed), is if you quit after you failed for the first time. The game doesn't give you the best character's in the beginning, and you have to learn the mechanics and gain some knowledge first, so it can be tough to finish chapter I with those. Just keep in mind that you unlock various characters through playing, that might be more to your liking.Sorry for making this so long, I was just super frustrated reading some of the negative reviews made for this game. Especially those who were written after ~30 Minutes of gameplay complaining about something that turns out to not be true if you simply keep playing. :/I find the game highly entertaining and recommend it to anyone who likes rpg, strategy, co-op and/or adventure games. Definitely worth my money. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others on Steam, this is a time where I wish there was a neutral review.For The King 2 is a sequel with a refreshing spin on the existing fundamentals of For The King 1, but it's faced with a lot of problems both in terms of (online) multiplayer bugs, and UI design choices. For The King 2 at its core is exciting as a sequel to a classic, fan favorite game, but it falls short when it comes to overall polishing. There are clearly many reused assets, and things feel and look jank, arguably mostly the UI and how unintuitive it is for a variety of reasons. The game itself and its content is more than acceptable, especially for an indie release, and with some time and ironing out the aforementioned problems, I am confident that this game would become the better version between the two games, and I very much look forward to what it can and hopefully will be in the future. But as it standing as of writing this review, I think For The King 1 remains a more enjoyable experience purely for its user friendliness.Update: Ever since a recent update released making VAST improvements to networking across the board, it has become much more playable with online friends and by extension become far more enjoyable compared to the anxiety-inducing loop of desyncing and connection loss before the changes. The UI and some clarity could use a liiittle work, but otherwise I now rescind my negative rating and change it to positive. Took a little longer than it should have for these updates, but better late than never

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, I give it a solid 7/10, Great game but I think a few things can be changed that would give it a better rating in my book. If you liked the first one, it's 100% worth getting. I would pay full price all over again with no complaints.  I am hoping the Devs see this and find it in their heart to take this advice. I have well over 100 hours and plan on putting in hundreds more. Overall I love this game just as much as I did the first. PLEASE for the love of everything holy. Allow me to rotate the camera in battle or add some more spacing between the 2 "battle stages". My characters in the top row block out enemies on the other side in their front row which causes 1. I just flat cant see them and don't know they are there2. I cant fricken select them to attack and have to keep messing around for it to finally respond. This is by far my biggest complaint and the one that keeps popping up that makes me irritated as ever. Please do something about this. How hard can it be to either allow me to zoom in/out left/right or heck, just space them apart a little more. If I may be so picky as well, WHERE are all the awesome unique weapons and armors  like in 1?!!?!!??! Come on, I want more specialty things like that. It just doesn't feel like it's quite there with that, seems like everything went into the starter weapons and such. Which is cool, but i was hoping for more unique drops (yes there is a couple I love! but overall, a bit lack luster). Some of the boss fights, the loot is trash to be honest. After level 6 it seems like there is no more armor or upgrades you can get and use and your inventory becomes a small warehouse with trash items you can't refuse to take and nothing worth using (i strongly dislike that, i want to reject items, i swap builds from talent to awareness or whatever combo and keep different armor sets on my characters, but I accidentely sell them sometimes when on a "trash dump" at a merchant) Last thing, can you balance the Strength and Intel. build a bit more in the armor department? That was a huge drag on 1. Strength build? Good luck with any resistance defense at all and Intel build? Good luck getting any armor at all. Its not as bad with the layout on this because you can have people hide behind shields and so on. But why would you play as either of those when you can have Talent/Awareness or anything else and have a great balance? Does it really need to be so one sided like that? #2 does a bit better with SOME of the armor, but its only good for early/mid game. Nothing really late game. As a front line strength build, I should not have 30 armor and 3 resistance. What crap is that? I can replace my +4 strength ring for a +4 resistance, but that's still garbage for a front line tank. I lose 4 strength to just get 4 resist? COME ON!!! Its so far out of balance, Please add better mid/late game armor that can really boost players in those roles. Maybe add in some dope late game boss drops for the strength and intel builds. Please. Maybe have the bosses drop cool stuff, more stuff? How can I fight a boss and literally get worthless trash? Are these things enough for me to stop playing? Hell no, I still have hundreds more hours to play, but as someone who LOVES these games. These are my top complaints and I would love to see some changes. All in all, great game and I love playing. I won't stop playing over these, but Devs, please, hear me out on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a "Mixed" option I would. Overall, game is pretty similar to FTK1. It's got the same world, mostly works the same, and hasn't ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with too much of the good stuff. All positives on that front. Characters feel stronger, enemies are still dangerous, but it doesn't have that "useless level 0" feel that 1 had imo. Now, the bad. The "Chapter" system sucks. I don't want to go from level 0-9 or whatever each time I play a chapter. I want to keep the same character throughout. It feels like a massive cop-out of making a fully seamless game. I understand """"trying a new direction"""" with the story telling, but this should have been an option, like prestige levels in older games. _childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: You are forced to play 2 characters each, if you want to play with 1 friend.The RNG is still the same from FTK1, you can have 95 in one stat, and miss 8 "2x-rolls" in a row.All enemies after level 2 seem to have 100 main stat and never misses.Not sure if im crazy or if the RNG actually is broken, every time i play this game i feel gaslit into thinking i just have bad luck every time i speak up about it to anyone. But with the amount of hours i've put in FTK1 and now having the same experience in FTK2 im sure, this games RNG is broken.Also endless bugs, loadscreens and basically the exactly same game as FTK2 with better graphics, this is just FTK 0.5.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: It's great with friends. I'm surprised it has such mixed reviews on Steam - in my experience there's been some minor bugs but nothing gamebreaking. If you liked the first, you'll like the second. And if you like turn based progression RPGs, you'll like FTK2.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Took a chance getting this game.  Never played the previous one, but looked good despite the mixed reviews.  Truth be told, its quite frustrating the lack of being able to protect your adventurers throughout the campaign.  You follow the campaign only to be told that "your party may not be strong enough". _childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked ftk 1 you will like ftk2. However there are still a lot of things the devs need to fix. First of all is balance. The game is way too easy even on harder difficulties. Second of all, the 5 adventures are WAY shorter than the first game. Ironoak wanted to make shorter adventures that when combined told the whole narrative. However the adventures are so short that once you do like 3 or 4 quests its just over. You stay in like 1 biome the whole game. In the first game, you would explore the whole world with at least 5 biomes and it felt very grand. In terms of improvements, the grid system is more interactive than ftk 1 and with 4 people is overall more enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Since my initial negative review, the devs have pushed an update greatly improving the state of the game resolving three of my issues. There are a few remaining issues, and hopefully the planned QoL updates address these (including boomerangs being held backwards). The initial campaign (The Resistance) might be my least favorite of the campaigns across both game, and both the itemization and experience gains both feel stingy. Playing Master difficulty is more an exercise in save scumming than skill as sometimes you load into a fight and have a back line character die before you get a chance to defend them thanks to random placement on the board every load. I still feel the game is overtuned even on Apprentice difficulty, slowing down Chaos, increasing item drops, or increasing xp gains would go a long way to smoothing out the experience. Additionally I found myself using focus more on the overworld to combat the incessant negative modifiers on roll-to-move attempting to keep pace with the game's clock. That being said, the new battle mechanics are engaging and the different action system brings more to the experience than the grid. Additionally class design feels far more focused in the original with new classes being less "what if" and having clear build paths.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't tried multiplayer yet but, my friends and I played the ♥♥♥♥ out of FTK 1. So far its been fun, no issues on a solo run.I'm sure the bugs people are experiencing will be ironed out.EDIT: played multiplayer with one other buddy. we both had 2 characters in game and everything went smoothly, no issues at all. this was also done on 11/2 before current updates.Seems as though the devs are addressing any issues quickly! Still recommend
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing this game should've done was release in early access. This game is overall a complete upgrade and overhaul of For The King. Me and my friend sat down and completed the first chapter in one sitting and only experienced one bug which was unfortunate as it did soft lock our game, but it only took closing and reopening the session to fix it. Bethesda has released way buggier games at 1.0 as a AAA studio. I feel the only reason this game has been getting as much hate as it did was just because of how well polished the first For The King was. Overall this game is just a better version of the first game that was released a bit to early.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and scratches the same itch as the first game. It definitely has some bugs and issues but nothing I experienced personally was too gamebreaking. The new grid system is cool and makes combat feel much more strategic, and the loadout system is also very interesting. The 5 campaigns all feel relatively unique and fun to play, in comparison to the first game where only the main campaign felt engaging to me. Overall the game definitely still needs work done on it, but since the devs have been very active with the game, and I already feel confident recommending it as is, I think the game will eventually be much better than the first.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointingly poor encounter design. The bugs have been indeed fixed very early on, there's nothing for me to complain about there. However, when it comes to things such as entering a Level 1 dungeon and encountering four level 2 Queen's Soldiers who collectively stun and/or daze our entire party, encountering a second Kraken after wasting all of our resources for the first one or the overall terrible RNG which is visibly skewed towards the enemy way more often than is should... I had an absolute blast during For The King 1, but here and now, I'm saddened to say that we've had more of our fun taken from us by such unpleasant moments than fun in itself. It's not that the game features bad elements; it's simply that certain specific attacks are game-breaking. The ONLY thing that confidently gave us a chance on Medium difficulty is the fact that someone played Stable Boy who absolutely ABUSED the pipe that gives you one focus point and triggering Hard Work up to eight to nine times in a single turn. We had to abuse the game in order to pull through, and there was way too little fun while doing that.Other than that, the game is fantastic, just as good as the first one if not better. Lots of content, plenty of gear to have fun with and a new enjoyable perk system alongside a significant number of new encounters of all kinds, albeit few fun classes to play with as of writing this. And please, for the love of God, PLEASE NERF THE BANDING KING.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: The endless dungeon mode developer needs to play that actual game mode. Explain to me how you can have 70% luck and 29 Evasion. Still hit every bad luck spot, Cop every curse, lose my only weapon to a thieving enemy then proceed to play a full further floor. Receive no further weapons nor a shop. It truly is not fun. Actually the smile i had on my face uninstalling the game was my highlight. Only real regret is not being able to refund and it was purchased for me, i didn't even pay for it
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Had a bit of a rough start initially as one of our players got the 'can't move' bug, but we relaunched the game and everything was fine for the first session. There was a funny bug where two enemies we're stacked on top of each other in one of the squares (sadly this did not mean we could double hit them -.- ). Other than that though the game has been a blast! I've been very impressed with the new UI. It's a lot sleeker and looks amazing, as do the graphics. The spells have fantastic animations with them now and I've been loving the more strategic placement for party members. You can now move so not everyone gets hit with an AOE, which was not an option in the first game. *Note for those with color blindness, the resistance and armor indicators are a bit small on the enemies so the light blue/purple can kinda blend together.All in all, fun game! And they put out a patch for the first issue we had literally after we were done with the first session! So they're quick and responsive with the bug updates too! I'm looking forward to the Bards update down the road :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed FTK you will enjoy FTK2. They changed the experience enough to make it new, without changing the core gameplay. _childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game directly on release and encountered countless bugs. 0/5, would not recommend. Worst game of the year, can't believe they did not publish a highly polished and fully optimized game right from the beginning. They lost a lifetime customer, I will never shop here again, and I will tell all my friends and family to not come here!! i dont know who hired rthis person but i wantt hem fired immidiately!!!!!!!!!!Edit: I have played multiplayer for a bit more and I still don't like it. So far there is close to nothing I would consider an improvement to the first game, that being a sick bell sound when enemies hit you with a death mark debuff.It feels like a few unbalanced areas from the previous title got looked at and changed, although not to any kind of interesting or challenging mechanics but just "different", almost tedious. Graphics are a bit more detailed, though I feel like it lost some charm due to it. UI is now a fancy, sleek, minimalist kind of modern looking UI. Nice at first glance, but then you notice how they sacrificed a lot of visual clarity for it. Stats of the entire party used to be visible at all times, now the exact stats are only shown when a particular character is selected. This makes it much more time consuming to make an informed decision, and when certain dialogue boxes appear you don't get that ability at all. Where the probability of a given action was once shown and updated as party members used focus, you now see nothing.For what I hoped would bring fresh ideas or introduce interesting game mechanics, this title demands a 25€ price tag to make visual "improvements" that hinder your ability to gather vital information while making gameplay more tedious. Not more interesting or exciting, no thought provoking grid based mechanics. Just tedious. Largely the same game as before, but now with randomized unit placement so you get to shuffle the front line in front of the squishies every battle. I don't see where this is supposed to improve the gameplay compared to the first installment, let alone provide something new.And while I appreciate the arachnophobia option (which allows you to toggle whether spiders get displayed or not), maybe add an insectophobia toggle next, because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game is a sea of bugs. Indie dev early access levels of buggy mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I participated in the beta playtest, and to be honest, I was disappointed with the experience. However, after returning a year later, I was pleasantly surprised by the significant improvements. The game now runs smoothly, with impressive optimization, improved FPS, and fewer crashes. Kudos to the developers for their dedication—FTK 1 was a masterpiece, and FTK 2 is shaping up to be just as remarkable if not better in due time.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: A hesitant yes so far on the game, but I may change my review based on what feedback the developers take from the community.PROS:Animations are very nice, especially for casting, and the art style is very pretty.Combat is still funSoundtrack is excellentCONS:The game has several balancing issues in the first adventure from what i've seen. I have played the first game extensively and the chaos timer on the first chapter feels FAR too punishing especially for a group getting to grips with the game for the first time. There doesn't seem to be as many ways to mitigate chaos generation as there were in the first game - we did both of the quest objectives and then immediately lost because we had done two sidequests.UI Issues. The UI lacks a lot of readability. I am aware that there is an encyclopedia for the game however I shouldn't be required to use the encyclopedia to get the bare minimum of what a passive skill does. That's why tooltips exist and have generally been a part of UI design for eons now.Movement in combat is a bit clunky. This is my main criticism of the combat system - I don't feel that the movement and positioning really adds a lot beyond hiding behind someone with a shield or spreading out to avoid AOE attacks. I think the combat in the first game had a lot more polish and was generally smoother. Also enemies seem to roll far better than they should, and I feel the combat in the game should scale to the size of your party.Again, a hesitant yes so far as the devs have been very proactive on the bug fixes - I still feel the first game is a much more polished and satisfying experience at the minute.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: The only problems with this game are that it launched in a broken state and that it is not forgiving. I bought on launch and never encountered any bugs, but I understand the frustration of not getting what you paid for. It's like buying a mcdouble but they give it to you cold. Balance was something that turned many away from the first game and the devs offer difficulty tuning options to help with accessibility this time around. I do think they could have given even more tuning options as the late game difficulty and economy spike, but overall this is a great way to address concerns.Seriously a fun adventure that made the mistake of launching on a bad state. Give it a try, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a welcome addition to the FTK franchise. If you liked FTK1, you will very much enjoy this game. There are still minor UI issues, but the rapidity at which the dev team for this game have fixed similar issues, is very impressive. I play this game with a friend and we have had a blast with it so far. In comparison to FTK1, there is a much more diverse set of weapons and many more viable character builds. Gear actually makes you think about trade-offs as opposed to being straight upgrades on previous gear tiers. The RNG gods still need to be with you as not consistently upgrading weapons can still nuke your game. Having 4 characters instead of 3 is a very nice addition, and being able to move in fights to maximize cover or party heal (as a couple of examples) adds strategic depth to an otherwise simple game. Overall though, for the price, you can't go wrong if you enjoy this archetype of game!

_childDocuments_.review: A major step back from the first game, and somehow the developers manage to make the final boss fights so wholly unenjoyable by having bs backup minions spawn without warning, hints, or any indication that the fights would go that way. The game is fun, and the Dark Carnival is fun! But the final fight in the main campaign, and in the Dark Carnival, are so poorly designed and poorly planned that it removes any sense of progress from the player. The fights wouldn't be bad if you could retry them after being surprised, but in order to retry either of the final boss fights, you have to dedicate 1-3 hours of your life, and then be surprised by poor designs, planning of encounters, and a lackluster climax.The game is good. It is. It's an expansion of the first game in a lot of fun and creative ways. But the story pacing and final combats are such a slog, and such a rinse-and-repeat, and such an unfulfilling climax, that it all feels like it is for nothing. Every game requires you to suspend some disbelief for immersion and entertainment. This game just feels like it has such a short window of time before the immersion breaks, due to either infuriatingly anticlimactic boss fights, the feeling of progress being useless, or just plain burnout from a formula that feels like a rinse and repeat.3/10 game, I'd rather play the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, combat feels much better than the first game. Bought it a month or so after it came out, and it feels like most if not all of the major bugs were patched, as I've just about played through all the new campaigns and not run into a single bug. The only issue I have run into was that the game runs slower the longer I've been playing possibly owing to a memory leak, but that might also be on my computer's end. Overall, one of my best purchases this year. This game has given me hours of fun with friends, and is incredibly replayable. I can't wait to see the infinite dungeon, and the extra campaigns that will come in the next year, as I loved playing through those in the first game as well. Don't listen to the negative nancies. I'm sure as it is still a new game there will inevitably be bugs others have run into that I have not, so I admit there is some bias there, but bugs such as those are normal for the first few months of any game that comes out nowadays. The game at its core is super fun and improves upon the first in lots of ways. It is absolutely worth your money, and you will get hours of enjoyment out of it!

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure why this game has gotten so much hate. Maybe earlier builds were worse? It has a few glitches here and there, but overall I think it's more fun than the original. Four characters instead of 3 allows for more flexibility in your team setup, and the movement grid allows for meaningful interactions between your characters. Breaking things out into primary and secondary actions was a great change, as it again allows your characters to act more flexibly. Your tank can taunt and still do something else. Your herbalist can heal and still attack.There are definitely some things I'd have done differently (I hate that you restart with fresh level 0 characters for each chapter, even though it's all part of the same story) but overall the game is fun and well worth playing. If you played For the King, there is a bit of an adjustment period as you get used to the changes, but once you're used to it it's hard to imagine going back to the original.I hope they add some more heroes at some point, even if it's paid DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: They improved, expanded, optimized and most of all balanced compared to the original.  The gameplay is more diverse. I do not recommend playing this game on normal difficulty. Start out making everything as easy as possible then work your way up. If you don't do this you will feel like the game is... "Too hard"  "confusing" "unfair" "too fast paced" "frustrating" and you would be correct. This game wants to be a rogue lite with runs that take 12 hours. When the game throws you under the bus, pulls some ridiculous ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the 11th hour... Well that's rage quiting time. I can't deny this game is fantastic. It's hard AF though.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I've played two missions so far. Of the two I have played, the game feels a lot easier and more manageable than the first FTK. FTK1, I didn't beat a single mission after hours of gameplay... The time constraint was much more severe, money earned in the sparing amount of fights I had to take was only for Godsbeards (of which I was constantly forced to use many due to the weakest member in the party constantly getting hit), and I felt like if I separated for a turn from my team that the person separating was either dead or not going to catch up before the game got harder cause we spent so long regrouping. Not only that, EVERYTHING felt more punishing in the first compared to this game. This game is much more balanced and I feel like I can take my time and enjoy the side areas and shop for actual gear over just Godsbeards/pipe increases. The only things I have had issues with were some multiplayer bugs, but those were fixed by simply restarting the game and rejoining. Another huge gripe was being forced to fight the Kraken. Normally not an issue, but when I defeated it, lost two lives and a shrine breaking from the fight, I got literally no reward besides an achievement. No exp, gold, item... Heck, not even a cosmetic! Just a badge of honor saying "You did it!". It was probably the most frustrating part of the game so far. But overall the game is a very large improvement over the first!Just as a heads up: I got this game from a friend and I have been playing mostly multiplayer with them.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry but I would not recommend anyone to buy this game at all.They tried to make a better game than FTK I and they failed and made it worse.Here's the reasons why:1. They added the "Tiles combat" system, but it's so simple and pointless that it doesn't add any strategy to the game at all. Is just there, almost irrelevant, since every single encounter you do the same thing. Move tank in front of squishy on the first turn. Then that's it.2. They tried to make the game more entertaining by adding several different campaigns that I assume are connected with each other, alas I won't even bother going on with the game because having to choose your characters again and start from level 0 after every chapter/campaign kills all the immersion. Pretty bad job there if you ask me.If you are wondering, each campaign lasts only like 3-4 hours. There's absolutely no sense of continuity in this game.3. The combat is laughable, it doesn't matter what you're using or which character you are playing, the only thing to do there is damage, damage, damage and try to taunt with the frontliner. All other spells/abilities (not that there's that many) are useless in comparison to doing damage.4. Leveling up is as boring as it gets. You level up, you're given stats automatically and that's it. No choices, no nothing.5. The story is cliché, boring, and absolutely linear with 0 interesting choices to be made. (Or uninteresting, no choices at all).I would have expected a better game, honestly. It's like they just add a a bit of everything, but with the minimum or basics of it. RPG? Barely. Strategy? Barely. Story? Barely. Level up? Automatic and dull. Etc... you get what I mean.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: I've got to say, this game has been an absolute delight! It's been such a fantastic ride so far, and I've been having a ton of fun exploring all it has to offer. The combat system is just fantastic, and I can't get enough of it. Plus, the variety of character classes and the freedom to customize my characters really adds a special touch to the experience.Now, there's been some chatter about performance issues, but I feel pretty lucky because I haven't really run into any major problems myself. I think it's important to remember that game development can be a tricky business, and developers are constantly working hard to improve their creations. It's a little disheartening to see some folks not even give the devs a day to address any issues before bombarding the game with negative reviews and refund requests.We need to remember that patience is key when it comes to the world of game development. All good things take time, and that includes making a game as complex as this one run smoothly. Jumping to conclusions and branding a game as 'the buggiest ever' without giving it a fair chance just doesn't seem right. Every game has its quirks at the start, and it's awesome to see the devs dedicated to making things better.But let's get back to the game itself. It's been a revelation for anyone who, like me, loves board games and the thrill of exploration. The sense of adventure, the joy of discovering hidden gems, and the strategic decisions you get to make with every move are what make this game so special. I can't recommend it enough for those who enjoy the perfect blend of board game tactics and the excitement of uncovering new horizons
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: For The King 2 in terms of it's gameplay, graphics and new features is a very good follow up to the first instalment. It is greatly disappointing, therefore, that the game is RIDDLED with bugs. I have not had a single play session without encountering at least a couple of obvious bugs, from minor graphical glitches to being softlocked to the point I had to reload my save, this is even after several hotfix patches.According to the team's roadmap, large QoL patches and new features are coming and I'm hopeful this game will eventually be in a more playable state. Aside from bugs there are some questionable UI choices, some characters are poorly balanced and popular characters from the first game such as the minstrel/busker are missing (to be added at a later date).To anyone who enjoyed the first or who likes tabletop-style rpgs or roguelikes, you will definitely enjoy this game, but you might be better holding off until 2024 when the developers have had adequate time to address it's most glaring issues.I'm not sure what happened with the playtesting for this game, but it's clear it needed more time in the oven. All the same, it looks like the developers are listening to feedback and have already implemented some minor improvements, with more to come down the line, I'm hopeful FTK2 will eventually live up to it's potential as a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: For the King II has made some improvements from it's predecessor, like the extra slot for a teammate, some graphical improvements, battle and content I guess. But if you played the first game, it won't be difficult to understand FTK2, since it still shares a lot of similar things with the first For the King game. Only downside I have seen here, are Bugs that could sometimes ruin your campain, but in my case it didn't occure as much as to others so I guess it depends. Still though it's a nice game you can't go wrong with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I and LOVING this game! If you played the first For the King then you'll love this too. Visually it is so much cleaner and the graphics received an upgrade from the first game too. Instead of one whole ass story run, its separated into chapters so you can try out new characters and not lose a heck of a lot of story progress if you all die a horrible death.At the moment there are of course some bugs (tbh what game doesn't have bugs on release these days), but the devs are working on them as promptly as they can, and each time I start a new playing sesh there's an update ironing out some issues. Overall, I think this is a great game! If you can overlook some release date bugs I recommend buying and playing it now, if you're not that kinda person then maybe wait a lil bit so you can fully enjoy the game at its best :)
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: The UI is terrible. 1 million bugs. No tooltips explaining what anything does. How did the devs think the state of this game was okay to release. Im tired of every game release nowadays being a complete train wreck. Now all we can do it sit and wait for up to a whole additional year for the devs to try and redesign this whole game. Stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now, I can not say FtK is a worthwhile purchase over the first game.The combat is an improvement, I love the system of having a front and back row, and positioning mattering, however the inability to set a default preferred formation, instead of it just being semi random does take a little bit from that.The Looting system has been updated, which is nice, It now shows the stats of the party members and who has how many of what herbs.Unfortunately there is just too many negatives, The U.I is clunky and unintuitive, The U.I for the first game was easy to read, all the information was all there and easy to see, In FtK2 information scattered, the U.I is a straight downgrade, Ontop of that, I don't understand the change in how to spend Focus, It's fine i guess, but i don't understand why change it at all, It used to be you could just right click onto the ability you wanted to put the focus in, now you have to right click the enemy you're attacking instead, it's just a little odd. Speaking of changes, party heal is now used in combat by selecting to use the herb and then targeting a person and it heals in a 4 space T shape also healing any adjacent party members, which is cool but again, without the ability to set your party formation for battle freely, and instead having to do it in battle, this can lead to people either missing out on healing/buffs or having to spend multiple turns getting into position. Which can be even more annoying when certain enemies can disrupt and move you.Everything feels like it gets locked in place constantly when another player does anything, Towns sometimes wont let you inspect them if you're not at them while another party member is, and sometimes they will.Then there are the connectivity issues, Granted they are better from launch but they're not completely gone, While trying to open the multiplayer menu I got stuck with a loading symbol on the screen that just stopped moving and had to quit to restart, recently we also just got kicked from a campaign for seemingly no reason only to get continual errors stating the party couldn't reconnect to the host. Information no longer comes up if you hover over it, on enemies (such as debuffs) But they do if you click on the enemy to bring up a panel on the UI and then hover over the icons in there, Why not just show the information in the first location you look?And then it gets to the music, I understand that the music of FtK was great, but unfortunately there is not a lot of variety between the tracks, which leads to the music getting a little repetitive after playing for a while, But IronOak has made the bold choice to make music that is close enough to the original soundtrack of FtK that while being entirely new songs (from as far as i can tell) that still somehow sound exactly the same.Overall this game is in a weird position where it feels like it's in early access, and hell, maybe it should have launched into it, But until some major issues are fixed i cannot say it's worth getting, If you haven't played the original For the King, Just play that instead, And if you have played FtK and are looking for more, you unfortunately wont find it here yet.I don't know, maybe i'm missing something? Maybe something just hasn't clicked for me, But i really want to love this game, it just isn't quite there yet. I hope to be able to rewrite this review when some of these issues are fixed up.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: This is a clear improvement over the original. The refined graphics are great, the story has been given much more attention, and the loadout system allows for a greater variety of approaches to one's playthrough.It is disappointing that the UI navigation with a controller is as clunky as it was in the first. I end up using a combination of a mouse with a controller because of how awkward it gets. The whole thing needs to be retooled, but what we currently have seems to be a port of the old system.Additionally, at the time of writing this, the store page claims multiple controllers can be used in local multiplayer. The developers have promised to add this feature, but only hotseat style local multiplayer is currently available. The store page should really not claim that a nonexistent feature is in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: It is absolutely a step up from the previous game. All the previous reviews are from a time when the game came out in a poor state. But they ended up sticking with the game. There is more variety of weapons as well as more builds you can do than the previous game. I'm just sad that the woodcutter is not as good as he was before...
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Meanwhile I played through the whole game. I will change the review to positive because the devs seem to be working hard to fix the game and simply do not deserve that bad rating, especially compared with other games. The game is still pretty relentless and sometimes straight up unfair but it got better with the patches.  I still think that the concept of time pressure doesnt work good in that kind of game, even tho it didnt bother me in the first game(Please let us turn it off completely). I still dont get some of the design choices(e.g: The Shepherd class skill and many more). So I played through the first game and now tried the sequel,Sadly I have to say that I didnt really like it so far(currenty in Act 3)The game needs some work to be properly enjoyable. First of all please fix the technical issues. I know that some hardcore players might enjoy it in its current state and call me out for being a bad player but i wouldnt mind to customize the campaign further with less scourges and chaos events happening(customization is already possible, but not enough). Many people simply do not like rushing through the campaign due to a timer. I know this gets to a balancing problem but as this is game is no competitive pvp game i dont see a reason why there shouldnt be implemented a "hidden easy mode".Right now this game feels just unfair, not hard, simply unfair. I feel like there is little to no reward for the punishment the game throws at you. You do not have the rewarding feeling like in other games. I wouldnt mind getting a class level system. Like making the passives proc more often if leveled or adding some effects to them. This would make playing over and over way more enjoyable than just the lore points.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Dont know why so many reviews complain about bugs and dsync in multiplayer. Been playing coop with my buddy since launch without any issues. The connecting was a bit wonky on the very first day but has been perfect since then.They are fixing bugs daily and from my experience so far the first 2 Chapters at least (around 10-12 hrs of gameplay) are perfectly playable without issues.If there currently are issues with later chapters, chances are they will be fixed until you get there if you buy the game today.To the game itself, cause for some reason none of the negative reviews actually talk about the gameplay itself.Its more of For the King 1 in all the good ways. It kept its fun gameplay loop while adding cool new mechanics like the movement grid in combat, some new status effects and a bunch of new equipment and all.The game also now has a propper overarching story between each chapter. Its not a huge deal but its nice to have.Also higher difficulties no longer reduce base stats of your character making it still difficult in other ways but it makes it feel less frustrating and random to play.If you liked/loved the first game then you will like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: The game does not run beyond the opening cinematic. I am forever stuck on the loading screen following the cinematic as the game immediately becomes non responsive. I was looking forward to finally being able to play with four people but sadly the game doesn't even work.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good. The tabletop part is basically the same as in FTK1 but combat and visuals are more complex. With the new grid style you have to think about positioning, AoE Patterns etc. and an improved actionpoint system gives you more options per turn. Nice Job IronOak!I only experienced a minor UI bug which can easily be worked around by opening the game menu once. There a only few pop-up explanations about game mechanics, you have to look up most details the in-game encyclopedia.Shared joy is double joy so grab a friend and go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Since playing the first title (and loving it), I gave myself ample time to dive into the 2nd with friends and solo. I just felt very meh and underwhelmed playing For The King 2Of the pros- I will say the game is enjoyably turn based, it carries much of the same baseline from part one while adding a new element of positionals and procs during combat that can make battles feel less simple. They kept the lore books and lore store purchase perks which can add variety to each new chapter/play throughButThere are so many little nitpicks that feel minor on paper but as a player just makes me scratch my head as to why either such a mechanic was removed, or why this new mechanic was added in the first place.My biggest let down is with the classes. IMO I think tier-treeing classes as evolutions would have been better than outright re-skinning new classes while adding a few stat points difference with measly proc-type skills that feel underwhelming.Friar Imo- can drink and share mead type stats with the group but is only as useful IF there is actually mead to be found. Why bring them when base Blacksmith or farmer is better overall stat and passive wise- it could have totally been 'Barkeep or Tavern Brawler' an evolution of Blacksmith but also needing to have Alchemist> a branch of herbalist unlocked to even be able to craft meadsShepard > renamed sorceress could have been the familiar summoning branch of scholar...with way better summons than a puffy sheep... Just some Ideas that would have felt more  compelling than clearing a chapter to just receive below average reskin classes (Farmer is the one of the best I have to say) Much of the equipment stats and lore perks perks can have a base class out-perform the hidden ones so it can often feel like- why even bring a hidden class when equipment can literally grant some of their passives and vice versa.I played the game a few chapters- and then got bored, fast. Loot finding and the variety is fun but even that wears off. Skill animations are dull, I miss bard 10/10 and how in part one the class could aid in battle it made battles have a spice of variety- Farmer and the tactician perk can add those things but it doesn't feel as cohesive. I love how in some turn base games a character can just cut in- mid ally attack or skill proc and add something too it.All in all it's still a fun game...with a graphical update, but could have delivered so much more. Let's hope they are more inclined to take such feed back from the communityAlso huge props to them for the URGENT releases of patches and hotfixes they get kudos for that in my book ^^. Over all I giver the game a 3/ out of 5
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very similar to the old game and has a bunch of cool new features.Would enjoy it more if it was:1. Better optimized - sometimes freezes/crashes with online multiplayer; the loading screen is buggy2. UI was better - it's not as easy to see/visualize things versus FTK 13. It had colorblind mode - similar to point #2, it is extremely hard to see things right now in the game - yes things are more "colorful" but the colors are also more dull to provide that realism. It makes it hard to differentiate if you are colorblind.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Having put a good chunk of time into the game so far with some time in the beta as well, I can safely say the game is fairly good so far! At it's core it's still For the King and it comes with similar pros and cons like the previous game. Choose your classes, gear them up, have a good run going and then suddenly random bad luck too at times too.It seems like there were multiplayer issues but I've only played solo so I can't attest to those. However the devs have already pushed out two hotfixes the same day and are very active on the discord taking in feedback as well.- The new 4x2 grid fighting system is a nice change that encourages positioning your party strategically. Vulnerable mages can more reliably be protected without having to spam taunt or just hope the enemy ignores them. Using AoE attacks to hit groups is great, and even better if you can shove enemies together to hit more at once!- Gear is more varied than the last game and has more to offer than just an occasional +1 strength or 1 more damage compared to another item. Classes can still flex a bit between stats and even positioning between front and back row.Armor offers more considerable boosts to evasion, HP regen, bonus speed, etc. and aren't always boring minor straightforward upgrades.Weapons are more similar to the last game, but they were already more interesting to choose between in FTK 1.- Traits and loadouts give you more impact on what you can start with so starts are a bit less samey between runs.- John Robert Matz, the composer from FTK 1, is still here and the soundtrack is still excellent!- Multiplayer issues. Again didn't see them myself or if the patches fixed them but it's worth knowing all the same. I'm optimistic that it'll be ironed out fast if it hasn't been already.- It's still got rolls based on your character's speed for moving on the map. If your character is even remotely slow or just unlucky, they can really painfully lag being the rest of your squad. This is more frustrating than anything since everyone else will have to wait for them to get in range for fights, or use focus to constantly inch them closer to wherever they need to be.- UI is just a bit confusing here and there but is mostly fine. Statuses inflicted on enemies don't appear by the health bar above their head, but instead at the top right on a separate health bar. Also the stun effect is colored white while daze is colored yellow. Feel like they should be swapped but that's mostly a nitpick.- Based solely on the first mission, chaos isn't as punishing as the previous game. One section had chaos do nothing besides the big bad making comments, and that was it. Another part had groups of enemies ambush you at regular intervals that didn't drop any gold, xp, etc. unlike normal fights.The former chaos event meant that it didn't matter that chaos went up unless it filled up fully, where I'm sure it's just game over. The other has your party get assaulted by fairly tough enemies regularly that drain your resources until you got to the next area to end the attacks.- The infamous Boner enemy has returned. This is mostly good really.First impressions so far are that For the King II is mostly an upgrade over the previous game. Combat is more involved, equipment is more varied and seems to drop more often as well, and the soundtrack is excellent. Multiplayer issues were apparently present and quite bad, but may have been fixed by quick hotfixes by the devs who are actively looking for feedback.If you're unsure feel free to wait it out. Many people likely haven't even finished a single mission yet so it's a bit early to judge just how much there is to the five missions that seem to be available so far.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: My three friends and I bought in to an unplayable mess. Original game was simple and well designed (literally the only thing wrong was the confusingly dumb limit of three to a party) and this one is clearly rushed and convoluted. Tooltips are lacking and UI was made more confusing (with less info). Multiplayer bugs ruined our game. Very sad that we collectively gave them $100, hopefully the UI and server issues get ironed out asap or this will be another big steamy mistake in the odious graveyard that is my game library.
_childDocuments_.name: For The King II

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is okay, story is fine. It definitely not feels like DLC to FTK1. It feels like HOMM5 compared to HOMM3.But technically it's worse than FTK1. It's bugged as much as homeless person's bed.
