_childDocuments_.review: At the core this is a very good RTS game, not the best company of heroes but in time it definitely will be, from updates to mods, it has the potential to be on par with the other two. For the most part I have not experienced any crashes, nor have I witnessed any frame drops or performance issues, and I am running everything on max with only 8 gb of vram. The developers claim the game can only run on max with rigs that has well over the 8 gb of vram that I have but that's wrong. I run it smoothly at over 100 fps consistently, with no stuttering, crashing, or anything else the other reviewers claim to experience. Game seems very polished optimization wise so far. The balance definitely needs work, Mostly in Infantry but in other aspects as well, HMGs should be a bigger threat then what they are now, and AT guns seem good but they are way too easily dealt with atm, there are other things but I will not go into those. The audio is something I am fine with. I believe the audio might be bugged, as some reviewers say the audio is fine, others say its not, might be a bug affecting some and not others. Italy campaign is actually fun, I can see it getting better in time, would love to see a mode like that again but this time covering the entire European theatre, and give us the ability to choose what side to play for too! Other then that the only real gripe I have is the buildings, I think they are a bit too weak to use effectively, Right now it does not take long to knock buildings out, Maybe make some buildings stronger then others. It would make players value those buildings and make them want to use them as a stronghold to hold key areas. The UI is actually not too bad, though it definitely needs to be able to resized, the zoom is another thing that we should be able to tweak to our likingAll in all, the game has the potential to be great, Just give the devs some time to iron out the bugs and add more to it, mods will also add to the life of the game immensely as well

_childDocuments_.review: My main problem with this game is how rushed and unimmersive it feels. I don't know how true it is what I've heard about this trying to release on consoles, but it sure feels like it.-Many unit and ability icons are recycled from CoH2.-Many typos in descriptions, and said descriptions do not tell you a whole lot about what something does or behaves.-No scalable UI, and said UI takes 1/3 of your screen, while also changing things for the sake of changing things up. Everything you're used to from the other CoH's, Starcraft, Warcraft and other RTS's, throw it out. Keybinds are messed up and different from previous CoH's.-Unit animations for infantry feel like they were jacked straight from AoE4 (compare running animations in both games, they feel awfully similar).-Units that are supposed to have semi-automatic weapons cycle their weapons as if they were bolt-action rifles.-Unit animations when transitioning from running to any other action look and feel alpha-ish, they do not connect well and it's like they jump from one animation to another instantly, in a janky way.-Many animations feel unfinished (motorcycles, when they turn, the driver's hands are static)-Unit chatter, voice acting and announcers are in general very poorly done, compared to CoH2 where they even hired Wolf Kahler (Dietrich from Raiders of the Lost Ark and a germal general in Band of Brothers) to play the Wehrmacht announcer. It's bland, somewhat annoying and  there's no personality (it somewhat feels like going backwards to C&C, where unit responses were bland "yes, sir" comments). Most voice acting feels amateurish, rushed or placeholder.-The music has gone backwards compared to CoH2. It's no different than all the other war games out there. It sounds pre-formatted, very basic and uninspired. You hear this music and you'd think it comes from some corny war movie from the 80's.  CoH2 is great in this regard.-The sound design is TERRIBLE. Compared to CoH2, an MG42 here sounds like it shoots peas. Rifles sound dull and toned down, as if they were compressed airguns or even toy guns. Tanks are LOUD in CoH2; here they are mere family cars. Cannons shoot and there's barely any audible feedback. A huge explosion that's supposed to obliterate everything sounds like a dull fart, compared to the damage it does in game. There should be some SOUND FEEDBACK to every action. It's either amateurish or they didn't pay enough attention. It's immersion breaking and you don't feel like ducking when you hear an MG42 open fire, unlike in CoH2. You'd barely know you're fighting an MG42 unless you actively look at it.-Don't care for singleplayer but the little I played felt alpha-ish. The AI is terrible and makes dumb decisions, especially in campaign.-Unit/background contrast is bad and everything blends. Nothing pops out, you have to squint. CoH2 is also great in this regard.-VERY FEW MAPS AVAILABLE IN MULTIPLAYER!!!! Want to play 3v3 or 4v4? Here's 2 maps only. LOL. Also few maps in general.-Bugs. Graphical, sounds, and animations. Riddled but playable. Feels alpha.The good things? It runs smooth, units are responsive, the design for the DAK faction is awesome IMO. OVERALL: get it if you want more CoH, but wait out for sales or fixes. I don't know why they released it 3 months later than they announced, because this is obviously unfinished and/or developed by amateurs. I don't know what's worse.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. If you liked the first two, I really can't fathom why you wouldn't like CoH3. All four factions feel fun and unique (not to mention each has three battlegroups which has a big impact and how you play each match), and the maps feel way more dynamic than previous titles (especially the Italian maps, plenty of windy roads and chokepoints, which I enjoy). Don't be deterred by the complaints about visuals and sounds. Those honestly seem like a viral complaint that caught amongst the playerbase and is now just being repeated without question. This games looks and sounds awesome (I mean, the 17 pounder alone is just...*chefs kiss*), and though there are a few bugs I've encountered, I've had nothing game breaking.I understand some of the complaints about the Italian campaign map, and if you're a 4X fan it will feel pretty basic. But upgrading you're battle groups and unlocking new abilities is real satisfying, and the missions make the campaign worth it in my opinion (and are surprisingly challenging!). Overall, give it a try if you like CoH 1 and 2, or if you're any kind of RTS fan. Solid game!

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant at first, and held off on my pre-order because of it, but ultimately after watching plenty of gameplay and trying it out myself: -It runs great-There is a lot of unit diversity and a solid starting map pool-The battlegroups, while sure to become a premium part of the game with future content, are a good evolution of commanders from Coh2. Cons:It is a bit buggy still, and MP balance is definitely about where you would expect it to be for release start, but they are already rolling out balance patches. - Campaigns are half baked, while still an enjoyable play through, the AI doesn't always put up a consistent fight, and campaign mechanics for the Italy campaign don't feel very impactful.If you're a long time COH fan, I think you'll get the same satisfactions out of this game, but waiting for a sale is never a bad call when a game has a rocky release like this.Update - In the first 3 weeks of release, they rolled out 7 hot fixes, including a pretty sweeping balance patch, many of the cons i mentioned being at least partially addressed. This includes a dev video laying out some of their near and longer term plans, including another major patch and many community requests on the radar. Very hopeful for this games future, as COH has always been a uniquely dynamic and satisfying RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth at its full price (60$USD). Good for a free weekend or $20. Released as a skeleton game with a long road map to having basic features that have been standard in complete games for over 14 years. Feels the same as past CoH titles with a few new units and abilities.  The campaign is kind of a one and done deal. There is no co-op missions or campaigns.There are two campaigns. A north Africa German campaign. The other an allies only grand campaign in the style of a pseudo total war map. The allies grand campaign map has some frustrations but overall it plays ok. The battles become AI skirmishes with some custom missions that are slightly tweaked. Gets a little repetitive. Not sure anyone cares about story, but it is generic.The German campaign is 8 missions, standard mission, cutscene, next mission style. It is wrapped in a story about a Libyan family caught in the middle of the two armies. This story wrapping feels like a forced token effort. It's a generic story that only adds short boring comic book style cut scenes between missions. The missions were standard enjoyable CoH missions. For the price point of $60USD it is not worth it. It is evident that they have decided to release skeleton game with a long road map not to add new and original features, but to add the most basic of features. For example map pings, visual features, an option to surrender, replays, many others. All things that should have been there on release. While they are there now, it seems to have taken a toll on the player base and shows the intention and effort. Not having replays on release doesn't help build an online scene. Competitive games and tournaments can't be watched/cast. Plus imagine having a game like CoH with epic cinematic battles and you can't go back and watch them.

This game feels lot less micromanagy than COH 2 and unlike COH 2 is actually playable and stable on release. The campaign is a refreshing take on the series while still proving all the COH action I love. if your a fan of the series you'll have  no trouble settling back into the gameplay. if youve never played the a COH game in your this is a great one to pick up and get lost in!

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely poor release. This should still be considered a beta, or an early access title.I only have 3 hours in the game so far, and it feels like I already finished it. I've seen and experienced everything the game has to offer.This game still has placeholder images in it from the alpha. FROM THE ALPHA.Very few units and maps compared to previous titles. I'd say the units and map list is halved. Everything is halved or even lower.There's only 3 different doctrines you can choose from per faction, and each just buffs your units with one or two new call-ins. You don't get to choose a play style you want to go with, there's no uniqueness within the factions. Compared to CoH2 where you had over a dozen different commanders per faction, each with a distinct play style.The total war campaign map falls flat on its face. It's a neat new thing they tried, but all you do is move your unit around and capture towns. The only time it goes into actual combat is for scripted events. Outside of the events, you just move your unit to a town to capture it.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick review:It's tasteless, unfinished, soulless, raw, but it has improved mechanics. Buy it with a big discount and better play good old CoH2, which was made by professionals, except a *censored* singleplayer screenwriter, who has created a complete *hard censored* and the *censored*, who drew Ostheer commanders/soldiers portraits. Detailed review:I came here for mupltiplayer, so i won't discuss anything about singleplayer. If you've played enough of CoH games, the singleplayer is just a training ground for multiplayer, you'd probably skip it.Things i liked in CoH3:1. Improved mechanics and upgrades. You have a lot of stuff to spend resouces on, like new abilities for your squads. This addition has created a new skill layer and made your each games's strategy slightly better and unexpected for your foe.2. Levels. Nothing much about saying here, they're fancy, because it's Italy and Africa.3. Tanks move slower. It's good, that tanks don't push forward like it's F1.Things i stayed neutral to in CoH3:1. Same factions. Because it's historical in terms of this theatre(s) of war.2. New vehicles. To me half of them look like complete *censored*, but it's personal preference. They're all real, except British Black Prince, which never was in real combat.3. Technical slack. It's locked in 60 FPS for some reason and there're a few bugs. For example, when vehicles move, their tracks aren't rotate sometimes. Devs would fix it, so i won't say it's crucial for my experience. It's more than playable.4. Removing of the Soviet faction. It was the CoH2's gem. Hard to master, all-around units types, memed Axis to the ground with their Shocks and B-4s. If they won't make a further Eastern Front DLC with Soviets, i would be very dissapointed.Things i hated the most (the best part of the review):1. Absolutely tasteless, horrible, awful (and so on) art design. The whole UI is a complete *censored* *censored even harder*, which was made by complete *censored* and the whole staff did their worst. It's hard to navigate, it's clumsy, it's not what you've expected in 2023 in all the possible ways, when we talk about design. Because it matters a lot.Victory points's capturing indicator look terrible. The whole menu looks terrible. Combat interface is so clumsy, you can't fully realise, that men who did this, were actually paid for their jobs.In game it's hard to read, when you're able to upgrade your squads with weapons, because icons aren't really dark enough. Points capturing status is just a small circle, which's hard to see, when the combat's intense. The mini-map is a complete joke, because it's a square over a circle. All the units icons are located below for some reason. In CoH2 you could see yours units in the top-right with perfect clearness, especially their combat status.Overall menu art with soldiers and some random women looks like a parody to any war-themed art, which you might find in the Internet. They've probably drawn it while being really drunk.But the biggest fail is about the units and soldiers. Faction squads, their battlegroup commanders (when you choose a faction) look absolutely trash. It's not a 2D-art anymore, but some mix between 3D and a very bad taste.Wehrmacht soldiers have eated bratwursts and donuts really hard. Nothing weird, they've lost, according to this game. US riflemen look like John Travolta, MG squads look like they've escaped from the asylum and overall it's just a shame of bad taste, honestly.In CoH2 you have a beautiful art works with you enjoyed watching at (except Ostheer, of course). To me it matters a lot, when we talk about the vibe. You have to expect a real war faces, whom emotions you can just read by looking at them. None of that is here, it's fake. And yes, colours here are weird to me after grim Eastern Front.2. Self-repeating. US faction looks very similar to CoH1, especially their building with stars all around. Can say the same about Wehrmacht. Nothing new you could have created here? You always have a feeling you've seen it already. When CoH2 was released, it was a completely fresh air, it all was new and undiscovered. Until now.3. Music. It's none. The most generic, boring and lazy audio performance i could've expected. It's all nothing compared to the CoH2's Eastern Front heroic choirs, violins and all the grim combat vibe. Big thanks to Cris Velasco for his work in CoH2.4. Overall audio performance. It's very poor, more like a student's work. Weapons don't sound like weapons. They're not loud, they don't sound dangerous, they're basically a Nerf guns made with plastic. Return to CoH2 and listen to STGs/PPSh/SVT-40 and you would understand.5. Friends/enemies colour differentiation. If you play with a full stack of your friends, you might want to know, who's who, right? Not in here. When i click on friendly unit, i can't see the name of the player. And when i go to the gameplay options to fix this out, the colours become so unique, that you're playing as Red, your foes as Blue/Green/Yellow/Orange and so on. It's unreal to read of what's happening on the field, when you use the colour variety. What was the problem to just make it all the same as it was in CoH2?6. Units kill counters. It's all hidden beneath the XP bar and sometimes they don't just work. Why? In CoH2 it was perfect once again.7. Removing the Russian language. No matter if you're involved in politics or not, you have to think about your customers first, because it's all about the money. Here we play games and don't mess with politics (as i thought). When this game was announced at Steam, it had various language support. But now, there's no place for Russian language. According to Wikipedia, there're 258,2 millions of Russian language speakers worldwide. And according to the same source, there're 10,62 millions of Czech-speakers. And there's Czech localization, but not Russian. So why have they removed Russian language? Because of politics? Or because they don't want more CIS customers? They've shown their attitude, when they made their CoH2 singleplayer. And when they removed the Soviet officer from CoH2's Steam Page. That's real shame, but i didn't expect anything good from them anyway.Extra bonus deluxe edition point: Youtubers have traded their souls to Relic money. Don't listen to them (CoH fans know whom i mean). Game's not finished and it's worse than CoH2. Their job is act like it's perfect game and it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried and tried probably more than 20 times now to get into this game. I bought it day one after waiting forever in anticipation. The game launched as a buggy POS mess and remains in the current state. As soon as you get to the main menu you will wonder if you just bought a $50 title or a $5 indie game. The more I play the more I realize how much time and work you need to put in to this to even be able to lose gracefully in online skirmishes. The more I play the more I realize that I would rather be at my actual job getting paid than trying to learn how to play this game and have a somewhat decent time online. The single player is extremely boring and repetitive. The only thing that changes is the enemy AI's difficulty. I think it took me less than a week to beat the game in single player? And at no point did I learn anything new or helpful for online skirmishes, and at no point did I find myself having fun. Over 50 hours spent trying to learn online game play, watching guides, playing and practicing. It's truly NEVER a good experience for me as a new player. Maybe 1 out of 20 games you play against someone else who hasn't been playing the series competitively for a very long time. The rest of the time you're just going to be getting canned. The multiplayer is just a complete sandbox for experienced players to absolutely f*** on new players and then j*** each other off in their tournaments of 60 players. These 60 players are really the only people that enjoy the multiplayer side of this game. To add to this mess, the game just FEELS incomplete and rushed, the experienced players seem to say that the game is not enjoyable, and the balances of factions even at competition level are a complete joke. There's no actual tier system that works. You could be Bronze 3 with 10% win rate after 50 games and still be playing against extremely experienced players regularly. The only redeemable quality about this game is that THERE IS NO PENALTY FOR LEAVING/QUITTING GAMES EARLY. YOU CAN JUST LEAVE AT ANY POINT AND START UP A NEW GAME! WHAT A NIFTY TRICK! I just ended up just leaving every time the game stopped becoming fun because why not? You're going to lose anyways. Your opponent is always FAR better than you. How it took so many years and work to release this pile of hot garbage is beyond me. If you enjoy learning by losing constantly to better players, winning to players even worse than you or just not having a good time while you play video games, this game might be for you. But if you aren't interested in wasting your money and free time, I would stay away from this title. It's unfortunate that there aren't any good WW2 RTS multiplayer games anymore. After many many MANY attempts to enjoy this game in ANY capacity, I will be removing this from my library and forgetting about it. I suggest you save yourself the money unless you find this game years from now on sale for like $5 or something. That's truly all that the current content is worth. Just look at the content of the OVERWHELMINGLY terrible reviews and look at the content of the very few and far between good ones. I regret ever trying to get into Company of Heroes. I think I would rather go through learning League of Legends all over again before getting CoH 2 and 3. Look elsewhere funseekers, as you will find non here.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not very good. I am a COH 1 and COH 2 veteran. I have only played the campaign so far so I cannot speak to the multiplayer aspect. First thing you notice is how unpolished the game feels, from the lame intro to the bland story, to the opening sequence of every WW2 game of the soldier writing to his loved one. Although this can be overlooked if the game play is good, right? I have had to restart the game multiple times due to the game "bugging out" - such as after a battle the screen sit blank, or at the start of a turn I click on anything and nothing happens. Adding into the unpolished feel, I have had multiple units get stuck on something when exiting a building only for them to be left there the entire match. The other options is they get to stand by as friendly troops throw grenades and satchels at their feet. The AI may know something in the sense that getting blown up is better than playing this game. Not that many people play this for any sort of historical accuracy, but the main campaign is narrated and commanded by a corporal, a corporal is giving out orders to the whole team. Yeah OK... Additionally, in one of the first missions in the Italy campaign you are given a M24 Chaffee to use. Well the US captured Sicily in the summer of 1943, and the M24 did not enter service until late 44 and never saw combat until Korea. I know they are trying to get a roster line up and use this as a light tank option for the US but it would have been easy to just use the M5 Stuart which did see action in Italy. Just bizzare.Continuing on with the campaign, they treat the player as if they are an idiot, they hold your hand telling you what to do at every step of the way.  There is a way to turn off advice, however the game still has the scripted inputs from your "Generals" and it makes it cheesy and annoying. This all compounds into the rushed feeling of the game. It feels like none of the developers care and just put something out there they knew people would buy since it carried the "Company of Heros" title on it. To add insult to injury, they already offer a $20 DLC on launch, with a game that clearly lacks polish. This game is a slap in the face, and is a simple cash grab by relic.

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT REVIEW:Company of Heroes 3 is an ''interesting'' game, which copied many of mechanics, units and icons from its predecessors... And alongside having MANY new and interesting changes, and most of all, quality of life improvements (auto ressuply, for example), the game has proven the potential to surpass them ALL in capabilities and possibilities...But sadly, it’s still far away from that achievement, since the game is plagued by ''poor homework copying skills'' and general unfairness in development of certain factions/nations.Patches are going in the right way (outside an OOPSIE that happened with recent 1.8.0, that needed immediate hotfixing in 1.8.1. in same week), but the game still has a long way to go before it could be fully considered a successor in the series, hence why the negative review... BUT I will moderate it as the development progresses, adequately...LONG REVIEW and FACTIONS REVIEW (+ Bonus on the end)Company of Heroes 3 is a continuation in the series of RTS games that has had a long history of scratching an itch for combination of ARCADE-CAPTURE POINT WW2 RTS games, while keeping to somewhat historical accuracy for the sake of gameplay values...Hence why, it might be best to run down the 4 playable factions and how they operate, and give them a rating based on their performance AND EFFORT that was placed in making them...AFRIKAKORPS (Deutsche Afrikankorp - DAK) Rating: A, A+AFRIKAKORPS is effectively a DREAM that we all expected to see in CoH3, in all the nations... Sadly, this is the only nation that had the dream fulfilled... Having single handedly the most vehicles in base rooster than ANY nation (some combined don't have equal amount) and focused highly on mechanized assault, you will never get bored with playing them, alongside NEVER running out options to fight whatever the opposition has against you...This faction is so widely developed with equally as much unit upgrades in their natural loadout, that you would NEVER be able to field them all in a single combat, much less see them used even by your allies on a single battleground... And that says a lot about diversity and capabilities this faction can provide...WEHRMACHTRating: A-IF Afrikakorps took some incentive from OKW in CoH 2 (combined it with wehrmachts mechanized warfare), then WEHRMACHT in this game took the ELITE INFANTRY from OKW and combined it with their already extremely varied rooster of units... Having Grenadiers (basically conscripts with panzerfausts), 2 Semi-elite units (Jaegers and Panzergrenadiers) and an Elite infantry unit (STOBTROPPEN SQUAD), alongside massive bunker down mechanics, Wehrmacht is a dream nation for a player who likes more elite/defensive playstyle with open options... Their early game is a bit trickier, but having the ability to counter ANYTHING enemy can throw at you, with your base loadouts (without doctorine bonuses), is more than enough to make you scale monstrously throughout the game...BRITISH FORCES (UKF)Rating: B, B-Being more similar to Wehrmacht in a way of versatility, UKF is essentially the most beginner friendly nation to play in CoH3... Having simpler build path and more versatility to unit choices, UKF is hard ON plagued by deficiency in their abilities... Commandoes and Commando LMG squads are absolute disappointment compared to older implementations, lacking both abilities and performance, and this lacking of active abilities and utility CAN be seen in almost ALL of their units (tanks missing ANY active abilities, etc)... Compared to Afrikakorp where some units have ALL the spots on hotbar full, at UKF forces you will see your ability bars BARREN, to say the least...USF (United States)Rating: CNow, in regard to winrate (primarily on 1 on 1), most people would argue that USF should have higher rating... That would be true, since their power spike is PURELY in early game, but the issue is not there... As game progresses, they are the faction that provides THE MOST dissapointment when it comes to QUALITY of DEVELOPMENT that was given to them by the developers...  And issues are MANY... They have LEAST vehicles available to them, they have LEAST INFANTRY variants as well (outside only innovation being bazooka squads, which again aren't that long lasting) and have the WORST TANK DESIGNS I've ever seen in COH game or series... BE IT HISTORICALLY or GAMEPLAY-wise, you will be pigeon-holed into playstyle you choose to support (infantry or vehicles) and HARD punished since anything that goes more into utility, will be countered by more competent AXIS tech tree...AND NOT ONLY THAT, but this nation is also the ONLY nation that is NON-VIABLE if you don't take a DOCTORINE to fill up a HOLE in your playstyle... THAT's how bad it is...And just to point out how bad it is? CoH2 had M36 Jackson, Motorized Anti Tank destroyer, here you have M18 HELLCAT (which is lighter variant with lighter cannon) but WAS REGARDED as one of FASTEST tanks in WW2 history... Guess what? With natural tech that Afrikacorp has, Pz3s and Pz4s can outrun it... These tanks which had HALF the speed of HELLCAT (and note to players, HELLCAT doesn't have JACKSON range, he has Pz3 attack range with slight increase) will most of the time OUTPERFORM this tank in EVERY aspect, making it not only obsolete but absolutely, downright depressive to USE...AND that is not the ONLY TANK issue that is seen for Americans, so yeah... Historically and development-wise, Americans really took a hit in the KNEES when it comes to faction development... Having almost NO UTILITY, no ARTY (outside of mortars) and no dedicated ELITE infantry in their rooster (while every other faction has semi-elite units at least), they are arguably the LAZIEST example of a faction in COH3. The only way they could be fixed is if good part of doctorine units were implemented into their natural rooster, and if majority of their tanks actually started DOING their purpose... Outside some cheesy strategies, they have nothing that is long term reliable or going for them in a longrun multiplayer games, and their primary uprising is in cheesy strategies and 1v1 early advantage...BONUS 1:At the start of 2024, there was a DEV log about implementation of new factions to CoH3 , and in purpose of opening other theaters of war outside of existing ones... The suggested countries that were most voted for have a purpose, but in comparison of current quality of factions, best course of action (which I would agree upon is) to add 2 factions first...USSR - easiest to COPY from CoH2 and could be used to implement much needed mobile AT guns (SU, ISUs, etc) which allies excessively need, alongside variants howitzers that USSR loved to useJAPAN - Primarily infantry and light vehicles focused nation with lend lease german vehicles... Would definitely be an interesting nation..THIS WOULD MAKE an interesting DLC for FORCES OF THE EAST, but releasing them separated would make the game more unbalanced and more divisioned on playerbase (everyone would want to play 1 new faction, hence why they need to be released in pairs)something minor (as France, or standalone Italy) would be terrible idea especially with current state of the gameBONUS 2:I will include a link to discussion with most of the issues, unfair advantages and suggestions to the official forum of COH3 here below...CONCLUSION:For now, the game deserves negative review since some factions are in HIGH tech tree disadvantage and quality of development, but patches are going well into balancing the game (outside 1.8.0 oopsie) so we will see, and I will adjust the review accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Company of Heroes 2 and I  wanted to love Company of Heroes 3 as well. Cynical about the current state of the gaming industry, but still hopeful for Relic Entertainment, I was foolish enough to buy this game for the full price on release. "What could go wrong?", I thought, "They have the entirety of Company of Heroes 2 to use as reference! That game is great! This one will be better!". I was wrong. I was so, so, wrong. And I am disappointed: with myself for buying a game early, with Relic for delivering such a ♥♥♥♥ product. I've read and followed the online discussions. Forums, YouTube, Reddit (/r/companyofheroes), all that nonsense, and there seems to be a mixed reaction outside of Steam reviews. Let me be charitable: the  (mechanics etc.) is excellent. I can say that the foundation for an incredibly good RTS is here. In fact, and I hate to say this: Company of Heroes 3 is probably the best (recently released) RTS game out there, and will be for a long time. This frustrates me to no end, because it could have easily been so much better. Company of Heroes 3 has the audacity to re-use (art) assets from Company of Heroes 2 for units (and their portraits), to have a user interface which seems like it was created just a few days before release, a barely functional matchmaking system, a horrendous 'social system' for grouping up with friends, and a barely functioning 'new spin on the campaign' which, in reality, is just Ardennes Assault from Company of Heroes 2 but somehow . But I don't care about all these things: they are matters of appearance and, at least to me, on the sideline. They are not the main issue, but they certainly radiate this lack of polish, or dare I say . The entire experience, the entire appearance of Company of Heroes 3, is one of an unfinished product. A game which was quickly slapped together (even if it wasn't!), then sold at full price. Qua appearance, Company of Heroes 3 is a slap in the face of everyone who loved Company of Heroes 2."But Timelord148, Company of Heroes 2 also had a ♥♥♥♥ release". Yes! And you would imagine that Relic got their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ act together and learned from those mistakes! I have not played Company of Heroes 2 around release, and even I know the horror stories just from a video online and some very angry men on a subreddit. Seriously, these developers (and this studio) get paid good money for the games they make (I hope) and they undergo such basic ♥♥♥♥ ups as 'making the same mistake'? Not every lesson has to be learned twice you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiots! But it is not even that which makes me so angry at Company of Heroes 3. The chief reason why I am telling you not to get this game, is because it is utterly devoid of content. I do not even want to start up the game to look at the amount of maps, so these numbers aren't exact, but the amount of maps per gamemode (4v4, 3v3 especially) are only one or two per mode. Even in the 2v2 and 1v1 modes (which I predominantly play(ed)) the amount of content is horrid. The game . There's four factions, but if you are planning on being remotely competitive then there are only two usable factions: Wehrmacht and USF. Every faction has only three battlegroups, with clear 'best picks'. Obviously you could attempt niche strategies or play for fun, but I reckon that winning (or at least a fair fight, the ability to win) is a major contributor to playing for fun. So here we have Relic being called out for a lack of content, and what do they do? They shove the worst, most hamfisted ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ monetisation update into their game in one of the first major updates! And, in line with the rest of their user interface, it looks like ass! It introduces challenges to obtain the "free currency" with objectives such as 'build 50 grenadiers'. What is the most efficient way to achieve this? Spam grenadiers. Throw your game(s), but get the currency. In theory, this can absolutely destroy games: you troll your own team (if you play in 2v2+), but your enemy also a bad game. I have no idea if this actually happened, but I can imagine it, and that is enough for me. Seriously: community modders (re)made maps (from previous games) and they were used in "pro play" within a week or so! I am absolutely certain that modders will provide entire new factions and/or battlegroups before Relic does. In fact: if I checked, I would probably find them. I am just too frustrated with this game to check. Relic, up until this point, has just proven that .I am biased. I loved Company of Heroes 2. I am emotional, because I had such high expectations of this game. I might even be acting privileged, because I have no idea how making games works. Still: I have a right to be upset, I paid €60,- for this game and it has been nothing but a disappointment after the hype wore off. Company of Heroes 3 has the foundations in order and has the potential to be a great game. Basic gameplay is fun, but there is not enough content to  the game fun. Relic Entertainment has shown an incredible lack of care for the game and its players. I hope that Relic gets their act together, I truly do: I want to love Company of Heroes 3. I will return after x amount of updates, and I hope I will be able to change my review then.Do not buy this game. Not until the reviews are no longer 'mostly negative'. Come on: Company of Heroes 2 has more active players on average than its sequel. Come on.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game without having played any prior Company of Heroes titles, so my review is not affected by how good this game is or is not compared to its predecessor. I also played it solely for the single player campaign, not multiplayer.What I enjoyed:- Sound design is generally excellent (with some reservations, but that's coming later). Pointing an anti-tank gun or some other vehicle at a building with an entrenched enemy and letting it rip until the whole house comes crumbling down was so viscerally satisfying I'd usually wheel it up just for that, even if there were more efficient means available of removing the problem. In general, many aspects of the sound design encouraged me to play in the coolest ways instead of min/maxing for efficiency, and that's something I like.- Nice variety of historically accurate units. Each vehicle usually serves a dedicated purpose and it made switch up my unit choices depending on what kind of task I was faced with.- Decent challenge on normal difficulty, especially early game, although in retrospect I think the best experience for me would've been to go one notch higher. In the latter third of the game, I had snowballed so hard I had more units than I knew what to do with, though that did serve a power fantasy after the early game's crossfire grind through the sand, so I'm counting that as a win.- The campaign map gameplay was pleasantly enough not just moving units around between skirmishes, there were some nice things to do like breaking defensive emplacements before you can move in.- The battles are good mayhem, there's a lot to juggle and keep track of, but when you break a defensive line and send the enemy into a rout, it feels very satisfying. Only minus is that, if you produce more units than you can realistically manage in real time (or the game puts you in that situation by giving you those units), you end up with some poor Tommies sitting in a hole for 10 minutes while you sort out their buddies' predicament on the other side of the map.- Graphics are generally very good for an RTS. Being able to zoom in to look at my units doing work and seeing all the detail in their actions was fun.What I'm ambivalent or confused about:- Bridge destruction is super underutilised. I never felt compelled to destroy a bridge on the campaign map, and rarely even had the chance to in battles, apart from the one scripted sequence where you need to do that. In most locations, there was a slope small enough to be travelled anyway, so destroying the bridge wouldn't have mattered. In WW2, destroying these kinds of chokepoints for travel was essential. Why is there not more agency given to me as the player to shape the battlefield and force the enemy to fight on my terms?- Artillery is oddly underrepresented. The Indian artillery unit is a joke, it has a movement range far below that of most other units on the campaign map, and the barrage range is so short it can't cover the distance it usually falls behind faster units, so you have to wait a turn to wheel it up before you can actually use it. And, get this: The only string to its bow in battles is a self-propelled gun, which is worse than the American M8 Scott, since the British SPG cannot attack out of barrage. I would've expected to have some mobile vehicle-towed howitzers or something - especially considering they're shown *on the damn unit card* - but these aren't in the game at all. Most mystifyingly, towed AT guns exist, so they'd just have needed to give that a new model and barrage capability, and this would've been fine. In general, I found indirect fire to be a very useful tool to winning battles, and I find it baffling that it's modelled no further than mortars and SPGs.- What do you need the rest of the partisan hub abilities that aren't "recon" for exactly? Recon is king, I can reveal the fog of war for several turns without risking a plane (or anything else, kinda broken ngl, there should probably be a counterbalance here like being able to be spotted and killed by the enemy), but I never once used the "loot" and "timed explosives" functions. If the location is in your control, one would assume it's near your front line, so the location to be looted or blown up is likely to be in capture range within the next turn anyway.- Vehicle recovery is another thing I never used outside the one scripted mission where you have to. A recovery vehicle takes up a sizeable chunk of your population cap, can't be used for combat, and can bring destroyed vehicles back to life for sure, but isn't the point kinda to *not* get them destroyed in the first place?What I did not enjoy:- The units talk *way* too often, and they do not have a lot of line variation, so they get repetitive. I'm the kind of person who fidgets back and forth between units to check what abilities they have up, and change my mind about what I want to command on the fly. Given that, the units *do not* need to speak every time I click on them, or issue/cancel a movement order, or just breathe in their general direction, because that just makes their lines wear out even faster. With the sole exception of the Churchill tank, which sounds so hilariously over the top I'd click on it just to hear incoherent yelling, the other units (especially British ones) *really* began to grate me later into the campaign when they make the same "who's he calling Tommy? Only ♥♥♥♥♥ and Harrys here" joke for the 7th billionth time. The American units don't lean quite so heavily into the accents and are therefore more tolerable in the long run, but I'd still prefer if clicking on a unit didn't spawn a voice line every. single. time.- On the note of sound, the battle music is more one-note than a severely poorly maintained harp. People, do yourselves a favour and turn the music off and put on some Sabaton in the background instead - the battle experience will instantly be elevated. Although, the campaign map music is quite nice and low-key, so I ended up in this annoying situation of needing to flip-flop the music volume on and off.- It's a shame that some of the more expensive and most useful units, like the Bulldozer, are poorly suited to large campaign maps, which are usually long and feature situations where e.g. the Bulldozer's ability to go through walls and obstacles would be helpful. They usually have some sort of a time limit (friendly unit health or just an absolute time limit), and you'd have to idle for resources for a long time before you can get them. In general, I usually ended up building units up to the population cap and then had no room to spare for them when I could finally afford them. I could build them all I wanted in skirmishes, but most skirmish maps have absolutely no need for the Bulldozer and some other specialised units.- If I'm below the population cap due to some of my units being down a few men, I would prefer the game would not let me put myself in a situation where I can go over the population cap by building new units. Now, you get the situation I often found myself in, whereby my scout squad is down to one man, but I cannot replenish the unit's numbers anymore, so the lone dingus now gets to sit in a house for the rest of the skirmish.This is a bit of a hard one. I liked it because it's a historical WW2 tactics game, but it has some aspects that are quite stupid and contradictory. I suppose I liked it enough to finish it in 60 hours, and if that means one hour is worth one dollar, then I most certainly got my money's worth.Summa summarum, I think the "mixed" rating is entirely appropriate, because that's a perfect vertical slice of my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have close to thirty-five hours, roughly 8 hours in the campaigns, the rest in auto-match.I do not typically review games but the controversy of this release, my feelings about the RTS genre as a whole, and my desire for the community and developer to refine COH3 all combined push me to say a few things.The Campaign is underwhelming, it was released with numerous glitches and poorly layered triggers that made it possible to completely stall the progression of the campaign at Salerno. The very first Campaign mission area had three separate ways for me to break the game, and require a complete restart of the campaign each time. I threw in the towel on enjoying the dynamic over-map system vs real time battles, because clearly it wasn't ready yet.New patches have fixed some of the issues I experienced, which is why overall I feel I can recommend the game as an experience, but I refuse to recommend it without explaining that the state of the game today is frankly embarrassing.The Automatch is released without any clear ranking system within the game, has no Map Pool Veto, creates a replay file but lacks any proper replay saving or analysis in game, and perhaps most egregious of all there is no live in-game observer mode.Both Axis and Allies have powerful and nearly game-breaking abilities from my personal experience, in general though I feel that players of similar skill level are able to play out an intense, dogged, and absolutely lethal maneuvers. Tanks in general feel responsive and lighter vehicles feel appropriate nimble by comparison. Infantry has fewer ways to cripple a vehicle, but rifle fire is marginally effective against most light vehicles. Squads move through the terrain with more intelligence than in COH2. The command choices and point trees are a refreshing level of flexibility coming from COH2. The tech upgrades provide timings for attacks with new improvements to throw off prepared enemy defenses and counters, and I never had a game where I felt like I was incapable of producing a force that could provide some counter to even the toughest enemy composition.There are numerous active abilities that are covered or removed from units after upgrades or veteran levels, which is a baffling and incredibly costly situation. Imagine not being able to deploy smoke launchers or use a special ability on a Panzer as DAK because you decide you also wanted vehicles who could cap. (The cap passive ability icon replaces active ability icons on several DAK units, I have found through painful trials.) Instances like the former show a game with potential to balance, refine, and polish each of the four factions into an even more enjoyable state. The fun of the game is let down by seeing the obvious points where lack of care or time led to a complete destruction of the quality control.Despite all the issues I have encountered, over 20 hours of solo automatch games, I have had three epic hour long knock-down drag out games that I came out of feeling like I had just experience the real vision of the developers, despite the complete lack of polish the game suffers.In conclusion, if you are the kind of person who can suffer the failures of others and see through to the quality RTS they've created underneath, buy this. If you aren't, wait for the community to fix everything ourselves, and buy the game for 5 dollars in three years when the developer abandon it entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: Played far too many hours in CoH2, so take any gripes with a grain of salt.Coming into this game, with fond (and maybe rose tinted glasses) of the first time I played CoH2, are just completely different experiences.CoH2 on release had really cool stuff like the Blizzard system in snow based maps, freezing over water etc, could sink tanks in it with a well placed grenade and what not..Infantry could freeze to death if not near fires and what not..was amazing, the weather was another factor on the battlefield and it was great. The art direction was quite realistic with a very 'in period' look to all of UI, not to mention the commanders, skins and the intel bulletins which could give small buffs to certain units, so you could really build a deck. The Commanders also offered huge differences in capabilities and what not.. CoH3, well, the graphics look about the same as CoH2, sure they'll be higher res when you zoom in (slow clap for over 10 years difference) but outside of that, at the standard zoom level you're looking at it doesn't look much different. There is nothing factoring in the difficulties of desert fighting and the UI is some weird ultra modern, overly 'clean' look, but with icons all over the place. As far as I can see so far there isn't any different 'commanders' or skins (outside of the preorder skins, only for allies) or any intel bulletins. Outside of the very coh-centric comparisons, the game looks very much to be in an early release state, there are so many quality of life things missing or that got lost in the move from CoH2 from CoH3 it makes you think that maybe Relics time as a very 'big name' in RTS is done, given the fluster-cluck that was DOW3, this is yet another pretty rough showing from a venerable game studio that is slowly pissing its good will up against the wall.Either or, wait for it to be on sale and give it 6 months to a year for it to become..maybe...reasonable.

_childDocuments_.review: Well,16 hours in and I feel like I've done it all. Very little content in this base game for $60. The four factions, only having their respective default battlegroups, grow old quickly. As others have said, the overall production quality feels low. The graphics leave much to be desired, staying at the level of the now 10 year old CoH 2. I honestly can't see much improvement in this regard.  As for the commonly complained about camera zoom,  a simple community mod fixed this issue, so I can't really complain there, but the devs should have listened to the community when it was requested. Do I still enjoy the game? Yes. I really want to see more content and watch the game grow into what could be the best CoH yet. I just wish that upon release, this game had more content. It feels rough and unpolished. Again, this game has much potential and with future updates, I believe that potential can be realized.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's what Claude Opus thinks of this game:Company of Heroes 3 is a triumphant return for Relic's acclaimed RTS series. While it may play it safe in some areas, sticking to the tried-and-true CoH formula, the game delivers where it counts with fantastic real-time tactical gameplay, impressive graphics, and a wealth of content.The core gameplay remains as satisfying as ever, with the signature cover system and emphasis on positioning and flanking making for tense, dynamic battles 1. Relic has made some nice refinements, like better modeling of vehicle armor and the ability to tow anti-tank guns, that enhance the tactical depth without overcomplicating things 1. The destructible environments and weighty combat effects make the battlefields feel visceral and immersive 4.The two singleplayer campaigns offer very different but equally engaging experiences. The North African operation is a superb showcase of classic, linear RTS mission design 4, while the Italian dynamic campaign, despite some rough edges, provides a welcome dose of strategic decision-making with its light Total War-style overworld 45. The ability to customize your Companies with unique upgrades and abilities is a great addition 4.Multiplayer is where the game stumbles a bit, with some early balance issues and a limited unit roster hampering the experience 4. But the strong core gameplay still shines through, and Relic has a good track record of long-term support and improvement as seen with CoH2 1. With some patches and expansions, CoH3's multiplayer could really shine.Visually, CoH3 is a treat, with detailed units, great destruction effects, and a gritty WW2 aesthetic. The sound design is also excellent, though the voice mixing could use some work 1. Overall, it's a technically impressive package.In the end, Company of Heroes 3 succeeds by sticking to its roots and delivering more of the series' signature tactical action and memorable WW2 spectacle 5. What it lacks in big innovations, it makes up for in polish, variety, and sheer fun factor. Relic has delivered a robust and refined RTS experience that both long-time fans and newcomers can enjoy. If you love WW2 strategy gaming, Company of Heroes 3 is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Relic used to be cool in the DoW days and it seems like they are just throwing in the towel for mediocre releases. We should not accept that.Alright, boys. Let's talk. At the time of writing, I've played this game about 36 hours. I've been a fan of Relic since I was a kid starting with the original "Dawn of War", and this is the cliche squad based combat that you expect to see from them. However, this game is clearly incomplete. You can see it the second you launch it and make it to the title screen. You're immediately met with a stationary background and 4 options. Now, I'm not saying that a stationary background is bad or anything, just very simple compared to CoH 2 with music and flags that change based on your chosen army. Moving on, into the Skirmish menu you are faced with 4 armies to choose from at the start, which is MUCH better than CoH2, and boy was that game heavy in the microtransactions, but we will get to that. There are plenty of maps to play on with 4 full armies that have 3 different commanders each. Honestly, not too shabby compared to CoH2's launch. But when you start a match in skirmish, it immediately loses connection to the servers. Now, that's not a problem at all because it still lets you play the match in it's entirety, but it just feels like they have to rig their application in some way to include a feature that has and will always be a staple in RTSs. Clicking out of that window and continuing into the match is pretty fun. Great cover based system that encourages flanking and use of abilities to destroy your enemy, Classic relic. However, If you're some joe Schmoe like me who gets off work and just wants to vibe with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ IPA and do a "Comp-Stomp" or two this will quickly become frustrating because the CPUs CLEARLY can see through the fog of war. I've had multiple instances where I have a defensive line and the enemy is dropping smoke shells on my tanks as they are being built in my base across the map where they have absolutely no units. Is this the end of the world? No, of course not, but do we expect better from a Major developer and especially a massive publisher? Absolutely. And that's really the heart of this review, I shouldn't lower my expectations for something that I've waited on for, what, like, 5 years now? Sure, call me old because I expect a game to launch like "Dawn of War: Dark Crusade" with a kick-ass single player with exceptional elements and the ability to play multiple armies with a huge battlemap, but this game should have significantly more content for a game that was developed over 5 years. Will this keep me from buying the next game that relic puts out? No, because maybe they will listen to their fans and change this bad boy into something it should be. I just expect significantly better (I.E., a complete game) from Relic. I miss the days when you guys were cool...Pros:Launched with Modding SupportLaunched with all 4 armies availablePlenty of solid maps upon launchCons:Game feels like a beta in the MenusClunky with server connectionCPUs can and will cheat at every opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Ragdolls are fun to watch, I swear I saw one doing MC Hammer out of a turret off screen.Company of Heroes 3 offers a gameplay experience that is both familiar and fresh. The mechanics are similar to those of previous versions, but units perform their special abilities more quickly and move smoothly through the battlefield, resulting in faster-paced gameplay. Each faction in the game feels unique, with the Afrika Korps enjoying an early advantage but lacking comparable units in the mid-to-late game. The overall balance feels good, although players may find that playing as Germany puts them at a disadvantage early on compared to the Allied sides.One of the most significant improvements in Company of Heroes 3 is the AI. Gone are the days of mindless spamming of mortars and artillery. While the AI is not perfect and can occasionally waste units, it can also be a challenging opponent, countering the player's units effectively at times. One area where the AI could improve is in creating chokepoints and defending them effectively. Nonetheless, the AI is a considerable improvement over previous versions of the game.The graphics in Company of Heroes 3 are impressive and modern, with detailed and immersive environments and well-designed units. The visual effects, such as explosions and weather effects, add to the overall experience of the game. While there may be some visual distortions here and there, they do not detract from the game's quality. Players with high-end hardware will enjoy buttery-smooth performance and a more detailed and cleaner visual experience.The sound design in Company of Heroes 3 is top-notch. The music fits the game's atmosphere and adds to the immersion of the player, while the sound effects are realistic and make the game more intense and engaging. If the player has a good sound setup, they can feel the rumble of explosions and tanks firing through their desk or floor. Overall, the sound quality is impressive and would be rated highly for an RTS game.The single-player campaign of Company of Heroes 3 is engaging and challenging. The well-written story and varied missions make it an enjoyable experience. The difficulty curve is well-balanced, gradually increasing as the player progresses through the game. While there is a bit of monotony at times, with the use of the same map becoming repetitive, each fight feels unique enough, and the operations in the Africa Campaign are challenging and fun, with a great story arc. The Italian Campaign offers a similar level of engagement, but some players may find it linear.The multiplayer aspect of Company of Heroes 3 is where the game truly shines. The matchmaking system is efficient, and the community is active, making it easy to find other players to compete against. There is a variety of game modes to choose from, and the gameplay is intense and exciting, providing a thrilling challenge for fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.In conclusion, Company of Heroes 3 is an excellent real-time strategy game that offers a range of content, from engaging single-player campaigns to thrilling multiplayer battles. The fast-paced and enjoyable gameplay, impressive graphics and sound design, and active multiplayer community make it a worthwhile investment for any fan of the genre.

The gameplay is enjoyable, and I had fun playing both single-player and multiplayer modes.In conclusion, Company of Heroes 3 is an average game with some issues. If the developers can address these problems, it has the potential to be a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Many criticize this game for the lack of content (number of commanders/maps/etc), and it is absolutely deserved. However, what this game lacks in quantity it makes up for in quality. The game play from COH2 has been incredibly polished. Units have unique and interesting abilities, unit path finding is excellent (usually), and the maps the game did release with are excellent. HOWEVER, I hate the breakneck, profits first approach Sega has imposed on Relic. The lack of content is not Relics fault. _childDocuments_.review: If you like RTS games, then this might be the game for you. The Company of Heroes franchise is in a league of its own in the RTS genre: it focuses on combat and territory control (as opposed to resource gathering/management and base building, though these elements do exist in the game) which makes for fast-paced, action-packed gameplay with no dull or quiet moments. Company of Heroes 3 offers the best of this type of gameplay.It offers two separate single player campaigns. The largest campaign is set in Italy and features the US and British as playable armies. The Italian campaign features two layers, the dynamic, turn-based campaign layer which plays similar to a Total War game. You move several "armies" across Italy and attack strategic locations to move the frontline forwards. When you attack a location in the campaign layer, you move into the strategic layer where the actual Company of Heroes gameplay occurs. Here you will fight man to man against an opponent in structured story missions to accomplish tactical objectives and win the day. Succeeding in such a mission will progress your campaign layer.The second campaign takes place in North Africa where you will play exclusively as the Deutsches Afrikakorp. The African campaign is completely linear and you will go from mission to mission until the campaign ends. In between missions, there is a story about the African people and their suffering. Honestly, this part of the story is a complete miss. You can easily skip these sections though and just play the actual missions which feature none of that.Post campaigns, you can dive into a few things. There are the player versus player modes which feature an ELO and ranking system (you will have to play 10 placement matches per faction per game mode before you are given a rank...the first few games can feel a bit rough as the match maker figures out what rank you are). There is also co-op versus AI which has the same format as PvP but you play against bots which is a nice way to ease into the multiplayer scene. Lastly, there are custom games in which you can essentially do as you please and allows you to play on the vast suite of community made maps and gameplay altering mods available on the steam workshop.For the non-singleplayer modes, there are four unique factions: the British Forces and the US Forces on the allied side and the Wehrmacht and Deutsches Afrikakorp on the axis side. Each of these factions is completely unique featuring distinct units and tanks, different tech paths and completely different playstyles. The British have the most linear tech paths and so are easier for new players looking to learn the game (note, they are a force to be reckoned with. Do not think that they are a "noob" faction). Each faction has 3 battlegroups to start with (battlegroups are game altering additions to each faction which offer new units and abilities and thus new ways of playing) as well as 1 battlegroup for purchase in the store (HOWEVER, the British and Deutsches Afrikakorp expansion battlegroups are free to keep forever, you just need to claim them from the store).The multiplayer modes are extremely fun and bombastic. Gameplay is fluid and smooth, units are responsive, and the game does a good job of keeping the player informed about important battlefield information. The game looks stunning and clear in my opinion. The sound effects are probably the weakest part of the game at the moment; it is still very functional it is just not as punchy as the previous titles, a problem I suspect will be solved in time.One thing must be addressed: there is an unfortunate political landscape amongst the hardcore players of this franchise. There is a group of die hard Company of Heroes 2 players that is seemingly hell bent on slandering Company of Heroes 3 whenever they can. At CoH3s launch, many criticisms of the game were valid because the game released in a very poor state. The game's developer, Relic, has done fantastic work at addressing these concerns (the only outstanding concern is the sound as mentioned previously) yet this group of angry individuals continue to dump on the game which is currently in a fantastic state. Unfortunately, this group of individuals is doing tremendous damage to the game's reputation through continuous slander and unjust negative reviews (have a look and you will see negative reviews here from people with literally half an hours play time which is barely enough time to finish the tutorial mission). So please, just be careful of hateful negative reviews... look for logical arguments and fleshed-out thoughts if someone has marked the game as not recommended and make an informed decision from there.In summary, I highly recommend this game. There are many hours of fun to be had here and I wish you all the best as you journey through the campaigns and the online ranks!

Examples:I play German factions and many times I throw grenades at enemy troops with barely any effect while enemy grenades often nearly take down an entire squad of mortar, MG or other units. Another example are the weak Afrika Korps Panzer. Most of the time I don't dare sending them into battle because those tanks are so fragile, yet the main tank of this faction, is it not? After the update today it seemed as if the fallschirm pioneers of the wehrmacht have become obsolete. For instance I had three squads fight one american squad of 6 soldiers and the three fallschirm pioneer squads couldnt take them out even though two of them were behind cover, too. Those american squads were mowing through my troops like a knife through butter. Ridiculous.Also it seems as if the team matches are unfair. Why? _childDocuments_.review: I've sunk thousands (yes thousands) of hours on CoH games on the decades since the original released. Played countless moded and unmoded versions of the game and loved COH and COH2 so much that I thought that COH3 would be a no brainer for me. I didn't expect much, just a pretty standard experience, maybe with improved graphics and hopefully some improved mechanics. I've set the expectation fairly low, and was pretty hyped by the marketing campaign when shown the new features both campaign and multiplayer. And all that was there at release, but most of them half-baked and if we are honest, untested.Trying to be fair on my assessment, the game has clearly some new very interesting ideas (i.e. limbering artillery), and some of the game developers clearly knew what they were doing (i.e. extremely well designed maps), but in the end the defining experience which defines the success of an RTS is gameplay, and it fails miserably on that front - to such extent that it beggars belief.  This, combined with the fact that it offers a lot less content, when contrasted with moded versions of the original COH is a definite no-go. Just buy the original CoH and enjoy a wealth of content for free, or try CoH2 and explore some well thought gameplay mechanics at a fraction of a price. Sadly I can't recommend this, as it delivers a lot worse in all fronts.

_childDocuments_.review: Company of Heroes 3 ReviewCampaign Map: the campaign was enjoyable, I liked the dialogue and story. It had a pretty map with some fun missions. The only issue I have with the campaign is that the skirmishes you have on the campaign map do not match the battlefield map as they do for say in Rome Total War 2004. 9/10Ai- I played the campaign on Expert and the Ai seemed way to easy. The Ai had lots of potential weapons to use and didn't respond well to flank attacks especially AT guns. As for my units, on multiple occasions I had engineers getting stuck and separating from the group which resulted in them being unable to repair or build. Overall the Ai seemed really dumb especially when compared to the prequel of this game COH2, in that game the Ai was aggressive even on normal and each map felt like a hard fought tug of war, whereas this game scripts Ai attacks based on capture points. 5/10Maps: Besides the well designed missions, skirmish maps were very redundant. 7/10Multiplayer: There does not seem to be a lot of variety in multiplayer, it really seems like a lot of maps were just copied over from COH 2, the lobbies are dead and there really isn't a lot of selection. 6/10Replay Value: I only really see myself possibly replaying the campaign, I don't think I would play it for multiplayer since COH 2 has a greater selection. 5/10Overall Score 6.5/10, I would not recommend this game at the moment, it feels unpolished.Recommendation for this Company: I would recommend you give a free map update or open world campaign of like Greece or defending against the Japanese push southward and the fall of Singapore; something to fans to thank them for their hardcore dedication and dealing with these issues. I personally beta tested this game as well and enjoyed playing COH and Dawn of War titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited: This is a soft "recommended," at least if you are going to stick to SP like me. I still wish I had waited for a sale, bc I'll never get multiplayer hours. When DLC comes, I'll definitely play the wait and see game.I'm having some fun. I hope it will get there. I can't recommend it in its current state for full price. It's not finished. After last update we are being asked opt-in for marketing telemetry on  If I start seeing in-game ads after paying full price maaaan.tl;dr - core gameplay is still good but bugs,  EDIT italian campaign is long (38 hours for me) tho tbh a lot of its content is repetitive AI skirmishes on the same few maps, strange UI behavior, not great campaign,  I opted out, but I haven't seen an ad either. I think there's an in-game store so maybe that's where this is. Ok.Full disclosure - I suck at COH. I bought COH2 after all the content was released probably on sale and loved it, but I am not good. I abused the keyboard pause button. This is supposedly what the new tactical pause feature was going to cater to. The people like me that enjoy the tactical RTS nature of the game but can't keep up. It's flawed.  EDIT: sometimes this tactical pause pathing is an outright lie. You couldn't see this with the old keyboard pause, although you could queue order you couldn't check the queue. I have two big problems with tactical pause. 1 - the queue and "TACTICAL PAUSE" text take up too much real estate directly in the middle of the screen and 2 - the UI for giving orders in tactical pause doesn't behave the same as real-time.The latter causes a lot of confusion. For example, when you order vehicles to reverse, your cursor stays in command-reverse if you are in tactical pause, but not in real time, and it won't clear and select a new unit by clicking like it does in real time, it issues another reverse order. You have to right click to clear the reverse first, this is confusing. Ordering engineers to construct sandbags or walls also does this, but it is the same behavior as in real time, Except right clicking doesn't clear the command like it does in real time. The system feels like it tried to do too much with a simple thing. Just replicate the existing keyboard pause behavior, add a small queue tracker off to the side, and let the UI work exactly the same as it does in real time?The North Africa campaign is ok, but short. It is told from the perspective of a local fighting with the British, but you are German fighting with Rommel, which is weird. Since the war in North Africa historically has a distinct ebb and flow, it would have been cool, and could have doubled the campaigns length, to play as the British as they gain the upper hand and push Rommel back. But instead it feels like 1/3, maybe 1/2 of the COH2 campaigns. EDIT: this campaign was decent though and the single player highlightBugs: I haven't seen many in the native battles themselves, except for some bad pathfinding and dumb AI. Not as dumb as some have said, my units have generally engaged the enemy appropriately. The enemy has been dumb. The grand strategy map for the Italian campaign, though, the new centerpeice, is very buggy. I currently have a company stuck in the ocean who can't do anything. This company was granted by a setpiece conversation with the two annoying generals constantly grabbing at your attention. Engineer constructs like sandbags don't form a continuous line, even though they appear continuous. And lots of buildings like your own production buildings can be shot through, even though the UI correctly identifies that it breaks LOS. The kinds of things that indicate the game just isn't quite finished. EDIT: I do respect the Total War vibe they went for here, really going the logical steps beyond the Battle of the Bulge content in COH2, but I don't think they got it, and carried over too much COH into the grand strategy. For one, instead of a blank canvas, its a constant stream of  three npcs yelling at you to do things their way or forcing you to make arbitrary decisions at that instant and that instant only, like in missions. For another, its hard to use much of the tools available because the population cap applies to everything, even emplacements. So a single enemy town might have 6 or 8 emplacements, and I built 5 the entire campaign. AI skirmishes also become very repetitive with like 5 maps, which they try to break up by varying the formula, but it still becomes an activity to avoid. There is very little grand strategy to manage beyond moving companies and bombarding areas. And the rules are not well explained despite a lot of early tutorials HINT the pattern is heal/repair, move or move attack, then march to move again. Later, use douglas' with airdrop to gain more movement. the germans rarely counterattack except to throw themselves at your companies, so this pattern maximizes your companies. The missions themselves in the italian campaign are good.It also seems, from my experience and what I've seen elsewhere, that this is where a lot of the bugs are. EDIT; the italian campaign is definitely where the majority of bugs are

_childDocuments_.review: After enjoyed CoH1 and CoH2, I decided to pull the trigger to buy this game even though I already saw the review that said this game is "unpolished". I mean, it can't be THAT bad right? right????Turns out, even after more than a year after initial release, I kinda get what they meant by "unpolished", here is what I experienced after I played a few hours of it:-AI is dumb, really dumb. I experienced the horror of microing units in both CoH1 and CoH2, you really have to pay attention otherwise your units will vanish into thin air. In this game? Nah, you can leave your units there and AI seems to be hesitating whether my units are worth attacking or not. Most of the time the AI seems.... AFK? I played like 5 matches on 4v4 map all expert and it seems weird that the AI doesn't move that much compared to CoH2. It's frustating in a way, you expect your allies to build units, push the territory and clash with the enemy, but nah that's rarely happen and for whatever reasons, the AI NEVER BUILD RESOURCE CACHE (the one you build on your sector on CoH1? yeah that thing). The thing is, this single piece of building can improve whatever sector you build with +50% income, and why the hell the AI never build it?-Keybinds. Do you like the keybind in CoH1 and CoH2 where you press A to attack, S to stop and U to reverse? Yeah I do, but this game scrapped all of that keybinds and move on with the new one called "Grid Keybind". So in CoH3 you have this 4x3 square grid, starting from QWER, then ASDF, then ZXCV, the problem is, I am so accustomed to CoH1 and CoH2 keybind where you have to press A to attack, and guess what is the attack button in CoH3? it's the Q button! You can remap the keybind but it's only for the grid itself (like if the attack command is on the first square on the grid, yeah you have to remap the grid to whatever suits you best, but you can't bind let's say attack command to A, because you have to edit the grid!)-The campaign. The US campaign? Doesn't really like it... I prefer a linear campaign like the Africa campaign. The US campaign is comparable to CoH2 US campaign, you have to move around a map and manage your battalion and prevent their deaths.-Daily and Weekly missions. Yeah, this game has 1, the rewards? Currency to buy some items in the shop. I really like the idea to incentivise player to play at least 1 match every day. The problem? Most of the time it doesn't work. For example, you have to play x faction and build y unit and upgrade it z times, most of the time it still doesn't count on the mission progression tab.-Graphics. For comparison, CoH2 can be run on a potato pc but this game can't even though the visual in this game looks cartoonish. Also, by comparison, CoH2 explosion looks awesome compared to CoH3 explosion, I would say it looks like just a firecracker, (mind you I run the game at max settings on both game)-Difficulty. I really feel like this game is too easy. I am accustomed to the horror of CoH2 difficulties but it seems that after playing both games back to back, this game is so easy that everytime I play either skirmish or campaign I feel sleepy and bored.I truly want to love this game, but I can't. It doesn't have the same click with CoH2.Will change the review to posivite if:-they fix the AI behaviour-add the option to bring CoH2 keybinds to this game-fix progression issuesAt the state of the game right now, I can't recommend it to anyone (thank god Sega sold Relic to become independent game studio again, hope they start listening to us again)

_childDocuments_.review: Having spent hundreds of hours in the original CoH (which haven't tracked between the "new steam" version and expansion consolidations) I really did not enjoy my time with CoH 2. I was hoping this installment would be more of a return to the things that people enjoyed about the first game with less of the things people didn't like about the second game. Unfortunately this has been a botched release with a medley of the old problems from previous releases and new problems that really should have been avoided considering how long this has been in testing prior to release. Maps feel cramped and small, the camera can't zoom out worth anything, every game plays like a race to get even the lightest armored vehicles and curbstomp enemy HQs. The single player overworld in the two campaigns is trying so hard to be something this game never needed and the balancing act of appeasing the three stooges to unlock their respective nation's abilities gets tiresome quickly. The audio quality is mediocre and the art direction is somehow less appealing than games released 17 years prior. The UI has been shifted around and caters to a console demographic with a botched default control setup to pair with.For how long this game took to develop and release it sure feels like a cash grab dumped out in early access.
