_childDocuments_.review: Can't help myself but to laugh at the usual 1st wave of crying from the diehards of the older titles, or their mods, or the people with cheap PCs struggling with the tech issues.Back in the day when DoW2 came out, my GPU back then could only push medium textures, but I wasn't on the forums crying how the game looks terrible. It might be a hard pill to swallow to some people, but you need a 16GB GPU to push this one to the max. I'm running it on RX6800, and everything looks great and runs smoothly, even without me installing the latest driver that adds support for the game. Except for some bugs with controlls after using the Steam overlay I have no other issues with the game.I was in CoH2 from the day one, and this game launched in a far better state, and with more content. Which shouldn't be surprising regarding that game was developing in the middle of THQ collapse. You have 4 factions out of the box, and two dynamic campaigns. Even though after upgrade/wargear stuff from DoW2 everything is a downgrade for me, its still a decent amount of content, and even having pro players and a bunch of community members helping to design and polish the game, you just can't satisfy everyone.The game now features some nice quality of life improvements. Infantry can now autovault and even ride tanks at last, and you are able to tow AT guns with trucks and half-tracks. Improved physics allows for the buldings to be completelly leveled, not being a blockade anymore. Vehicles are incredibly detailed, almost looking better than the real thing, and explosions and fire effects are easily not only the best comparing to their previous titles but even comparing to a bunch of high profile FPS/TPS games.I see some people complaining about the ladder, not a big issue for me personally, but each to their own... But if CoH2 is any example, I can only imagine how much stuff this game is going to get in the years forward, and has so much to start with already. I'm actually surprised how small number of achievements is in there after the previous game... I guess I grew spoiled having to grind stuff for hundreds of hours in the past.

_childDocuments_.review: There’s a good game in there…. Somewhere!... and I don’t think its as far off as you might think!As Morphias once said “he’s beginning to believe”. and in all honesty. I am. Well, either that or I am blinded by faith.High level summary: Get past the UI, the shop, and some missing key features and the core game is actually game really fun! – The devs look to be moving their road map to focus on what the community want after go live – more maps etc etcMore in-depth below:Let’s get most of the bad highlights out of the way first:Most of the issues around this game come from some bad decisions at key times the key one for me was the rolling out of the shop as one of the first major updates. This was a PR nightmare. even if it was in a shippable state the income relic must have actually been made by the shop and has probably been offset by the downward trend in game sales. So it was a false economy. Also, skins aren’t that good and their price point is far too high (FPS high) – this has resulted in steam and Reddit going mad about the game.If we for a second leave the hate circle jerk that is Reddit at times (valid opinions I will agree but leaving the eco chamber for a minute) what Relic tried to give us in comparison to coh2 (which please remember was far worse of a release than this – FAR WORSE) Is a game that is comparably double the size of coh2 (4 playable factions and 2 campaigns). My summary of the released version of the game is that the size of the MVP (minimal viable product) might have been the issue. In essence, they tried to deliver 2 much as part of MVP and it meant the final version came across as unfinished. From an outside view dropping the DAK faction and the North Africa campaign a year before go live and then making them free L C 6 months after release would have been a great idea. This would have allowed them to relocate those development resources into just a nicer UI/ replay/ visible ranking system/balance/ polishing the rest of the game.So, the Good:The core games are FUN! Rolling with a group on 4v4 or 3v3 is a lot of fun and now we have seen some balancing patches come out we are seeing a broad meta start to be established – I hope these patches continue. Nothing better than balling up the tanks and plowing into the enemy line 😊 as you try and blitz krige the enemy (or the Zule bull horn Strat works just as well)The North Africa campaign was good and clean fun and the Italian campaign (what I have played of it seems an interesting take, not quite as good a Ardens from coh2, but I think it has far more replay ability.Community engagement – the game has from its offset really engaged with the community. I have a game that I felt like I wanted (we will once it’s all done) – correct theatre – more factions – new features (some old missing but hopefully they will be back TANK CRUSH) but generally it’s a game I have felt involved with which I think games need to do more. -even the new bug fixes get their own live steam.The Devs seem to be taking on board the feedback – the balancing patches are coming quite regularly and I think they are quite well thought out. not a pendulum-type fix’s which we used to happen in coh2). Also, they look like they have adapted their road map to focus more on Maps and bug fixes which I know the community want.So, I write this with hope and to stem the hate eco chamber that we are seeing atm. Give them a chance to make it right … COH 2 was worse and turned into amazing game (thanks in part to the community but still).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm here to help for people skeptical because of the poor reviews. I have over 1k hours in the COH francise. While the franchise has its problems, I love these games. If you are new to the series then this without a doubt an opportunity for you to enjoy an awesome RTS.  COH 3 is not a far departure from the previous installments meaning its still one of the best RTS games. Ill give the veterans of the community my two cents. You can take it or leave it because it really subjective.  Now, if you've been with the series for a long time you might have some reservations. The new installment has been in the works for a long time. The results are in and it appears that COH 3 isn't revolutionizing the series, but in the end I think the new gameplay is very appealing. I think the new push to make light vehicles more adapt is a very fresh take on the old formula. Bridging the gap in combat and avoiding the late game heavy tank spam that became very repetitive. The new multiplayer is won by who can navigate combined arms the best. I think the multiplayer is vastly more complex when it comes to strategy. I'm not sure why relic decided to leave out ranked matches and statistics though. I think this is basic stuff the community has always had and wanted. Hey relic where is my replay of the match? features that were always there are now missing. I'm sure it will come in the future but still disappointing.  I only have a few hours into the single player campaign. I can respect that relic tried to do something new. The single player was always a weak point in the series.  The new conquest map seem a bit linear and doesn't really compel me to come back to it. The multiplayer is so dynamic that it shadows the AI competition. The conquest battles are just a bit cookie cutter and I personally find the battles to be a bit repetitive. The AI in the campaign seems very passive. They tend to just defend what they have. I'm not sure why this is the case because the skirmish AI is exceptional and play like an organized machine.  skirmish AI is actually far more intelligent an the spamming AI in COH 2. I will go back to the conquest map when I want to change things up.  But I will spend a majority of my time in matchmaking.  Overall I think the presentation is great. Even though the graphics are not much improved over a 10 year old game. The graphics are a slight improvement to quality but also a back step when it comes to lighting and color. I'm personally here for the strategy and the gameplay, but I understand peoples frustration. The animations are impressive and the soldiers move like a squad with dynamic awareness. I personally think the movement has improved since the last game.  The battlefield feels a lot more fluid. The environment is even more destructive with combat feels more slow paced and grounded. The sounds are more realistic and much more subtle than the grandiose hollywood battlefield of COH 2. The game plays great. while I have seen a unit T-posing on an AT gun, I really haven't had any problems with bugs or optimization. The game plays very smooth and crisp. I can not say the same for COH 2 on release. I haven't played  COH 2 in a year or so. I might have love goggles for the new additions, but the mechanics feel fresh.  10 years of COH 2 and the meta became very monotonous. I look forward to the development of this game. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:If you like the following:- Eating broken glass- taking your ex wife's mother out for dinner.- take comfort in dissapointment.Then I highly recommend buying this game.Long version:I would have to preface this by saying I have well over 3000+ hours in the COH series. I really enjoyed them. But this release has so many issues and so many deep rooted problems it is an insult to the series. 1.) GraphicsThe graphics are "passable" I regret the choices they made in regards to fully destructible enviroments. But the game was released with many problems in regards to its graphics. Issues that should have been cought in alpha testing.- Airplanes were metal silver cigars- the animations that some of the planes were doing were outright wrong or just downright comedic. A stuka bomb dropping down felt like a pinata coming down. There was no oomph at all.- The infantry units sometimes hold weapons to their feet all these things are graphical in nature but overall the atmosphere this game breathes is honestly cartoonish and not gritty. I prefer COH2 graphics over this one. I dare to say COH2 might look just better because it has a more gritty approach to things. Now it just feels like American GI on mediteranian cruise. - GameplayThe gameplay has a LOT of potential but sadly it is mired in many issuess that again show a depressing theme for this game's release. Its absolute lack of polish or beta testing.  From pathfinding being horrendous, to simple bugs making entire game plans useless. To list them:- Tanks cannot drive well at all they are slow and even after 3 patches it is still a crime to try and use medium tanks. - throwing satchels in specific ways on infantry means the bag will get glued to the unit and outright kill them. - Line of sight barely works as intended. There are situations where someone is standing 2 pixels higher than my infantry gaining the advantage of height and seeing my units get slammed.For lack of a better word the german faction just outright sucks. The units they get are all early war and mid war. While the allies get Easy eights, black princes and a wide variety of tanks. The current meta is swamped with Light tank spam and the germans have no viable counter to it.Marders barely work due to the way the turning and aiming works. The developers.My biggest issue is with the development team the outright disconnect between what they are doing and projecting to what are genuine concerns is painful. I miss the old relic with bugoo and where it felt like we were listened to. When 1.2 was released they buffed the air strafe and when I told the developers how this would ruin the multiplayer I was told that they had faith in the development team ad i had to wait 3 weeks to see how things pan out.After 2 days of having as streak of losses a hotfix was released to address an issue that was flagged even BEFORE the buff. On top of that all we read is how great the team is working. But the balance in the game is nowhere to be found. It isn't fun playing germans and we are locked into one commander. I sincerly hope relic can right the ship but at this point with the developers being scaled down i worry that we might end up with this being the lat product relic releases and I find that very disturbing.Maybe in a year with 2 expansions the game will be better but honerstly for me this game is a HARD no for anyone interested in new games.------------------------------------------------I have played an additional 103 hours and witnessed the updates and the revision is as follows:- The game has been improved in some ways normally I would laud it but 70% of what they fixed should have been there on release. There is no excuse. - Pathfinding is still broken period. this after 3 patches to "improve it" - The balance in this game is honestly offensive. Relic is NOT testing a single thing they release. The latest expansion basically added a massive desynch bug. Which can happen. But to see the artillery the germans get plaster the allies into liquid tommy isn't funny and it is a blatant oversight.In the end the game is Company of heroes 0.4. IF relic continues with patches and listens more closer to the community there is a game to be found. Sadly however a year later almost and so many things that feel not finished. I don't know what else to say. I only play this game with a friend but the inbalance isn't fun for axis or allies.

_childDocuments_.review: I've sifted through a heap of reviews, and here's the skinny: the negative reviews are all correct.But wait, there's more! I also wanted to address some of the arguments mentioned in the positive reviews (by Company of Heroes 3 apologists, so to speak):1. "Remember how CoH2 was a bit of a fixer-upper at launch, too?" No, it wasn't! I started playing it in 2013, and there were no serious problems. That is why, unlike CoH3, it received 90% reviews from critics from the start.2. "CoH3 was crap when it was released, but it is a lot better now!" No, it isn't! There has been almost no improvement since the open beta. Any "improvements" are creeping along at a snail's pace, giving the impression there's just a lone junior dev behind the wheel, probably teetering on the edge of burnout.3. "The single-player campaign of CoH3 is not bad." Oh, come on! It's like watching paint dry. The campaign's a snooze-fest with no real decisions to make, stringing together a series of boring skirmishes I'd never touch with a ten-foot pole in CoH2. Sure, CoH2's campaigns were a decent tutorial, but they weren't the main feature by a long shot. Got CoH3 and stuck with it? Here's some advice: don't torture yourself. The single-player campaign is a load of garbage, and it won't get better after a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm divided on this game. The North African campaign is pretty cool, the turnbased map on the other hand is boring as hell. Everything done on the turn-based map itself (attacking positions without any possibility to fight on the real-time map) is completely superfluous. Also, many of the missions have very short timers that, again, give the game a "who clicks faster"-type C&C character, which is exactly the opposite of the slow, systematic micro-management approach that makes this franchise so cool in single player mode.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT / UPDATEIf you are planning to buy CoH3 primarily for the single player campaign, the game still currently has bugs that can break your campaign.If you are planning to primarily play pvp online matches the player base is now very small and CoH3 has even fewer players than CoH2 both on average and at peak hours(steamcharts numbers).The other game ruining issues I listed below are still in the game.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I loved the first two COH games and sunk thousands of hours into them.  When COH 3 was announced I pre purchased the Digital Premium Edition immediately because I was looking forward to this game for years, however, after playing only 10 hours I already regretted my purchase. Many reviews here have already stated the balance issues and all the features and mechanics from the past games that have been changed or removed, however, the main reason I do not recommend this title is the numerous game ruining bugs.For instanceUnresponsive units - Telling a squad to pickup/man a dropped weapon and they just wont or will run up to it but do nothing(applies to both squad weapons and unmanned heavy weapons). I have had units get stuck for no apparent reason and the simply ignore any orders given to them. Sometimes after exiting a building or retreating they will also become unresponsive.Bizarre pathing issues - Telling a vehicle to move to a location but it decides to go around in circles (this applies to both normal and reverse move orders). Sometimes when units are called into the map they get stuck outside the map and never showing up but still affect your population limit.Odd Terrain interactions for projectiles - If there are any objects in between a tank and its target a weird issue can arise where a tanks shots will always collide with terrain and always miss its target. I have had a stationary tank miss 7 shots in a row against another stationary  tank despite a clear line of sight between them. I have also seen objects like wooden barrels or bushes stop tank projectiles which makes no sense.I love the COH franchise but I cannot recommend Company of Heroes 3 in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Graphics and EnvironmentVisual quality: The graphics are good and show a significant improvement compared to COH2. Initially, the game had a cartoonish style, but this has been improved, giving it a more realistic "war" effect.Destruction effects: The destruction effects are visible and alter the map's composition and the battles, making them more interactive.Maps and environments: I believe there could be a larger number of maps as they can feel a bit repetitive. However, I expect that future updates, including community-created maps, will expand this variety.2. Gameplay MechanicsTactical gameplay: The balance between infantry, vehicles, and air support is excellent. I do miss the wide variety of commanders that existed in COH2, but I believe this will be addressed in future updates.Cover system: The cover system is intuitive and effective for troop positioning. This time, there’s a realistic animation of troops actually "taking cover" when they reach a protected area.Resource management: The game offers a good balance between managing resources (fuel, ammo, etc.) and the actions on the battlefield.4. Single-player CampaignStory: The narrative is decent, but a bit tiresome. The idea of managing resources on the tactical map is good, but I can't explain it—something like the COH2 Ardennes campaign feels unmatched. I had more fun in that campaign, as it gives the constant feeling that you need to perform miracles to preserve your troops for the next battle. In this game, I didn’t feel that.Duration and difficulty: The campaign's length is satisfactory, but I found it somewhat repetitive and counter-intuitive at times.Mission variety: There is some variety in the missions, but they do repeat quite often.5. MultiplayerMatchmaking quality: The matchmaking system is fair and efficient.Game modes: The classic Victory Point mode is sufficient, and it offers a balanced and competitive experience.Community and support: The player base is solid, and the developer has improved multiplayer significantly compared to the beta, providing good support with updates, events, and new content.6. Customization and FactionsFaction diversity: The available factions are unique and well-balanced.Unit and tech variety: Yes, the factions are amazing, especially the Afrikakorps, which stands out with excellent synergy between infantry and vehicles.I believe they could have explored more forces that fought in WWII (for example, the Canadians and Poles, who appear in the main campaign but aren't playable in multiplayer or even as a subunit via specific commanders).Note: The FEB (Brazilian Expeditionary Force) isn't even mentioned in the game. I hope the developers consider adding this force as a specific commander in future updates.7. Technical PerformancePerformance: I haven't encountered any performance issues. The game has improved a lot since the beta release. I play on an i7 + R580 8GB setup, and the game runs very smoothly.

_childDocuments_.review: Really lacking in polish.Gameplay,There are a ton of issues, from cosmetic problems like the wrong assets being used for vehicle icons, to the fact that message boxes cover critical gameplay information. During the campaign Conti's messages cover your fuel income for instance. There are also more substantial issues. On some maps when calling in the 4.2 mortar as the Royal Indian Artillery the mortar will get stuck behind one of the base building and not be able to advance. The pathfinding is also much worse than in previous CoH titles, and I frequently have vehicles when given a move order illogically spining to present their rear to the enemy, even when using the reverse command.Base building.the buildings are large, the base zone small, and the inability to rotate the buildings prior to locking them in a position after getting the yellow border means that precious time is wasted placing building in a game where the layout of your base isn't really that important.Factions.I know there are 4 and that's a lot for release, but the lack of representation in Commonwealth forces is frankly offensive. It is great to see the Indian forces, but the relegation for instance of Canadians to needing help, and then for one mission granting you one unique infantry section, given their critical role in the real historical campaign, constituting roughly 1/4-1.3 of commonwealth losses, is deeply offensive. I don't think the Australians, Canadians etc should be factions, but at least deployable companies. Also the Indian regiment really needs more unique units. Would it really have been so hard to make the rifle sections, engineers, etc a little unique.Voice actingWhy for the love of Pete do we not get British introductions when playing as British companies, and leave the American Corpral Conti for the American units. Is there no one kicking around the office with a UK/Commonealth accent who could have chipped in. Also I get it, the foot guards love to say "CHAPS." It kinda gets tedious after a while. Please add a few more phrases to the units. I love the CoH games, and I was really excited for this one. There is a lot to love in this title, and all of them. I will likely put a lot of hours into this one as I have with previous titles, but still I feel really let down at the moment. I would recommend most people wait until many of the problems have been fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of these reviewers are lunatics for voting this game down. It's launched with double the content of CoH2, and at a comparatively cheaper price when adjusted for inflation, and with fewer bugs, and more stable, and yet somehow people want to compare it with the CoH2 that's had 10 years of balance and DLC upgrades?! As for the actual game itself - Multiplayer and Compstomping is where it's at. Native day 1 workshop support with free mod editor? There are already maps coming out to suit your tastes. There are already mods to zoom the camera out just that little bit more. The armies are mostly balanced; each feels unique and fun to play in its own way and there's a large roster of viable units that you'll be required to play (unless you're Britain - just spam Infantry with Boys AT) and some excellent strategies to pull off some insane timings (RIP Tiger 1 in 8 minutes). I can see myself droppimg thousands of hours into this game with and without friends. The single player is divided into 2 campaigns - and unlike your local games journalist I will vouch that the Italian campaign is WAY better than the North African one, despite the latter letting you play The Desert Fox Rommel. (Also because it was the Yanks that bombed Benghazi in WW2, not the British). _childDocuments_.review: I bought this on sale, it is absolutely not worth full price. MP has significant balancing issues, and cut content. I was shocked when I went onto forums, reddit and community hub to be greeted by months old comments talking about my exact issues, regarding balancing and build order. The Devs know what the problems are.  This game has potential, and it can be a lot of fun with friends. But a combination of poor balancing, bad matchmaking, cut content and limited scope make this feel like a quality of life update to COH1, with worse balancing.  It is  not a successor to COH2 because of these balancing issues. To be worth full price this would need more factions, more battle groups and better balancing.  At current state I would struggle to say its worth more than £20. There are some brilliant QOL improvements over previous COH, auto-reinforce, better maps, a clearer UI and much improved graphics make this feel newer. Cover is king, you are rewarded for micro and grenades have a lot of utility in early/mid game. However arcade-like health bars, and odd explosive damage distribution, and sometimes random RNG losses mean this game leaves a lot to be desired.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't buy it in the state it's in tbh. I bought it understanding the downsides because I really enjoy CoH and I still wanted the third game because of some of the few improvements within it but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. Check back in a year or two, maybe they will have fixed the game by then. Maybe you can get it on sale then too.The first few hours was addicting as I played through the German campaign first and enjoyed a variety of interesting Italian and German troops. Then I did the Allied campaign and enjoyed the unit diversity again with the Gurkhas, American paratroopers, and the Devil's Brigade. The tactical pause feature was probably my favorite part of this game, just because it made offensive pushes in single player so much more fun and less hectic. The tactical pause let me plan my offensive so as not to waste time and to give me more mental space to focus on the individual problems my troops encounter as they move forward. Sadly, that's where most of my praise ends.I can tell there was a lack of effort on this game. The gameplay here reminded me of the GTA 6 leaks we encountered in September, where there were so many placeholders from GTA 5. Similarly here, they've reused many of the CoH2 ability emblems, and it is not only pathetic, but also insulting to anybody with even a basic knowledge of WW2. I mean when I utilize a ability with a emblem that has a picture of a Russian officer on my American tank crew, it completely takes me out of the experience. It might seem minor, but after playing CoH2 it just feels lazy for them to not even put in the effort to make a new set of icons to reflect the nations participating in this new theater of war. Especially after they put in the effort to make this vibrant, cartoony new environment. It's like Relic can't trust themselves or their playerbase to be mature and accept the horrifying realities of war, so instead they dumbed it down and made it ridiculously colorful, making it less impactful as a whole. I get it's Italy, one of the most beautiful places on Earth imo. With amazing weather and terrain, you can't make it as dark as CoH2. But I mean between the lack of impact from the audio/voice acting and the flashy lighting and color palette, it feels totally disconnected from the real historical event it is portraying. It's like playing a mobile game, where the developers have lost all time and place and twisted reality into something unreal.Hours into the game I couldn't bring myself to care about the soldiers I commanded in either campaign. In the German campaign we basically play as the historically bad guys. And the game decides instead to reflect on the experiences of Benghazi Jewish people, an interesting and thought provoking perspective no doubt, but it's hard for that to connect when I'm not even playing as the Allies in that campaign. The main characters really only exist in cutscenes, the only connection between the gameplay and story is that every battle is prefaced and ended with the main characters talking about how much worse it was going to get. Then the end of the campaign gives a basic description of what followed the final battle, as the tides turned against the Germans.. Frankly, it would have been cooler to me if we had the option to play either as the Allies or the Axis in that campaign and as a result get two different perspectives, giving extra incentive to play the campaign twice. For the German perspective, it would have been good to see the war through the eyes of a German foot soldier or officer, who perhaps could give insight to how the Germans saw a resurgence of success during the Africa campaign and how it all came to an end, between new Allied strategies to even how poor hygiene caused mass sickness within the Afrika Corp. Meanwhile, we could play with the Allies with the wide variety of units they would have had at their disposal, including indigenous soldiers, playing a defensive war that focuses on protecting key assets and objectives in order for the Allies to not lose too much.Meanwhile in Italy, we actually do play as the people whose stories we are following to some extent. I mean you can't control the main characters but all cutscenes and dialogue are from Allied forces as we make choices on our fight towards Rome. Supposedly, this is a dynamic campaign, but the lack of any dynamic forces and serious consequences and rewards make this the biggest drawback of the game. The enemy army doesn't usually make spirited attempts to take back territory and the decisions you make almost don't matter at all. I mean you get loyalty from your commanders just for breathing sometimes. I had no difficulty securing the loyalty of all three generals by mid game, just by accident. To be fair I was on an easier difficulty so perhaps that played into it, but even still, most actions I took in the game felt like they had no real impact. When I did get some sort of interesting new objective to gain a buff, the instructions weren't clear. Like when one of my commanders suggested I retire a company to the rear of my map near one of my ports to get some ice cream and rest. I was all for it but they didn't give me very clear instructions and there was no objective in the top left. It was as if the objective didn't exist at all. I moved a destroyer away from a certain port and I immediately get a dialogue from my company saying that they "just missed the boat" and that ice cream would have to wait until Rome. I had a couple of objectives like that throughout the campaign that weren't outlined or listed in any way so I would sometimes just have to assume they existed. It was annoying because, even though I'm sure some hard core players might say I'm being lazy and should acquire the skill to track all those objectives, I like having a list of things to do highlighted in my UI so I can keep it all in front of me as I make decisions. Otherwise, attrition and company damage were meaningless 9/10 because I could just spam heals and repairs without any drawback besides resource drain. It only became a problem for me mid game when my forces began to get spread out a lot and I was not getting as many supplies as I needed. Again, maybe I should just replay the campaign on harder difficulty. But I am confident in saying that even if I played on harder difficulty, the campaign as it is right now could never match something like the pre-Rome 2 Total War title campaign maps in scale or complexity.The battles meanwhile, outside of the reused assets and poor audio, are excellent. Exciting and engaging battle after battle during the German campaign. The Italian campaign is good too but sadly the interesting battles are separated by boring skirmishes. I can tell they at least tried to add some variety to the objectives in those skirmishes but honestly, you should probably play it on a harder difficulty if you want the most intense combat you can get out of the skirmishes. But thankfully at least battles like at Anzio and Monte Cassino, it feels like you get a chance to fight formidable foes and change history. If you know anything about the bombings at Monte Cassino, you'll know what a tragedy it was and how it contributed to the massive impact on the artistic world by WW2. Having your commanders discuss the consequences of Allied command decisions and how you can prevent a national treasure from being destroyed makes you feel like you're coming across one of the few meaningful and interesting decisions in the campaign.Basically, if you still enjoy the CoH2 battle style and don't mind the glitches and lackluster aspects of audio and art in the game, and you can get past the somewhat boring campaign, you'll probably be ok with it if you bought it on sale instead of full price. But if you're buying it for the campaign, save your money and come back in a couple years when hopefully things change.

It feels disingenuous, and that's before you get to the story of the game. COH and COH2 had some of the best WW2 stories in video games. COH3 is written by an MBA-brained drone who does not care at all about the NA campaign, the people, the tactics or the effect this titanic conflict had on our world. They shoehorn in a story that uses the people Bengasi as wallpaper. The narrator of the story compares the British to Nazis and implies that the fighting with them really doesn't matter, Then we get a story of what the writer really cared about, a young activist girl....The Italian campaign writing is just as poor but without the woke BS, while the voice acting is pretty stereotypical. The American sounds like a cowboy, the Brit sounds like a teacher, the Italian partisan woman is fiery, Oh My! I am glad Relic is an indy studio again, it means meritocracy will return to their firm and we will get better games, content and respect for WW2 and the people portrayed in the conflict. Overall you shouldn't pay more than $20 for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: An updated review after multiple patches:First off, let me say that the absolute gall of the game developers to try and paint the allied forces in a bad light on par with the national socialists during the north african campaign is absolutely despicable. The British Royal Air Force, not shockingly, did not have smart bombs to discriminately target Benghazi during air raids. If you thought woke politics wouldn't enter the sphere of WW2, and think that this is merely a storytelling device, head on over to their discord and see some of the taglines under creator's and others' names. Their only shame is not being able to add more pronouns to their pronoun picker. Absurd. Secondly, this is an unfinished and unpolished game. I should not be surprised because that's just what companies do now:* Entire sections of the game that were not functional at launch now are! Except that they updated the paid store microtransaction portion of the game. This game was clearly not released in a full state.* Unskippable and extremely long non-progress saveable features of the single player campaign are a huge waste of time. * Multiple things are missing/broken from multiplayer:      - You cannot change anything about your profile, as that section of the game also doesn't exist; everyone is stuck with the same title and icon.      - The stats section of the game once its finished is wonky at best and inaccurate at worst. Seriously bad. The camera zoom is a little absurd, but doable. For a game released in 2023 you'd expect more. Graphical glitches abound, from tank skins just going mute black, to vehicles having seizures because they're stationed on a slight bump, to animations not working whatsoever or stunting to the point of not working (Fire the effing panzershreck instead of constantly inching forward and re-doing your fire animation every time you even slightly shift position!). This is not a game you should buy, these are not developers or a company you should support. _childDocuments_.review: I will try to keep this short as there are so many other reviews which dive deep into the pros and cons of this game. The first game that I bought on Steam was Company of Heroes! I've been the games of this series ever since then and it is one of my favorite game series ever! Normally you'd expect some level progress and development with every game in the series. With COH 3 however, it feels like relic regressed. The feels empty and lifeless. This is the worst COH game in the series for me! Also, right now there way too many bugs, glitches and optimization issues in the game. Frequent crashes and weird texturing issues aside, the biggest issue is the freaking load times!! As you progress in the campaign, you end  more and more time on the loading screen. Currently, for me, each battle takes about 5-15 mins and my load times are nearly 20 mins plus to get back to the campaign map!!! If really love RTS games as I do, buy it, it still has most of the core elements on the COH franchise but please do yourself a favor and wait a year or two before you pick this up on sale! _childDocuments_.review: I have played +1,500 hours on COH1, and +2,000 hours on COH2. This game at best is at a level of early access, but really is at a state open-beta. I think most people who have good reviews have their nostalgia blinders on, and are ignoring a lot of issues with the game. Overall a lot of the issues are minor, this game is playable; HOWEVER, all of the issues add up to a hot mess of a game. We've waited over 10 years, and its sad the game has been released at this state.I HAVE ONLY PLAYED MULTIPLAYER PROS:- 4 playable factions - Reassigning hotkeys - No bugsplats/crashes - Faster loading screens compared to COH2  - Auto-reinforce at baseOverall gameplay is similar to COH2 & COH1. They have implemented most of the mechanics from COH2, including vaulting, reversing vehicles, etc. This is the first COH game that has been released with more than two factions. I haven't experienced any bugsplats or crashes when playing, and overall load-in times are greater than COH2. CONS:- UI, UI, UI, UI- Artwork- Audio - Lack of Commanders - Graphics/Visuals are comparable to COH2- No in-game leaderboard/rankingUI:The interface is absolutely atrocious, from the starting menu to icons. The starting menu is a homage to COH1, yet somehow looks way worse. The menu/settings/font are a far cry from any game released in the last decade.In-game is just as bad. While in-game you cannot view the name of teammates by clicking on their base or units. Even if you have unique-colors it still doesn't show any player names. To access the playerlist and see what doctrines are picked by teammates, you have to pull up the menu which covers the entire screen. Compared to COH2, where you can pull up the player list in the upper left corner. Icons like the repair icon on vehicles is minuscule. There is no build icon at all. Mousing over engineer builds has nothing. Hotkeys are reassignable but don't translate well with COH2 hotkeys. Commander choices/abilities in-game are on the far right of the screen; you tend to even forget about them  or even notice they are there. These issues may be minuscule, but a decent UI is very important in RTS games. Artwork:Abysmal. COH2 had great artwork from all of the commander icons and doctrine selection icons. COH3 doctrine/commander icons are trash. Look at COH1 doctrine selection screen. It pulls up a well-made menu with artwork and you can easily discern abilities. COH3 doctrine selection menu and icons are bland and small. Even the faceplates are terrible: one of the faceplates looks like a 2000's game artwork. This has no reflection of the gameplay, but if I only cared about gameplay, I'd go play CS-GO.Audio:Has no life to it, doesn't really wow you.Doctrines/Commanders:More doctrines and commanders would be great, but this game did just release with 4 playable factions. So this isn't really a knock on the game, but something to consider.Graphics/Visuals: This game was released about a decade later after COH2, and really doesn't improve much. This also just might be a bias because I'm already disliking many of the other issues of game. However, compared to COH2 a lot of explosions, gunfire, and effects are completely lackluster. Infantry or tanks taking damage doesn't have that great of an impact.SummaryCOH3 is a horrid successor to COH2. It barely improves on much other than different factions. The gameplay mechanics are similar but COH3 just has worse UI. This really just amounts to a Italian/Afrika corp DLC. I can't really ♥♥♥♥ on the developers. This seems like a cash-grab from Sega/Relic executives releasing this game way too early. If any triple-A game released a game at this state, people would be in uproar (I.E No Man's Sky). Yet, the COH community has an intense love for this game, because it ends up being the only game we play. Probably why there's so many mixed opinions.I expect in a year or so this game will definitely be much improved, but for now I'm pissed I bought this game for $60.TDLR; COH3 is just a bad COH2 DLC where you can RP as the Afrika Corps and Erwin Rommel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves another look.  I really feel they have turned the game around in a big way from where it started.  Yes, the launch was disappointing, I acknowledge that, but looking at where the game is now, it's way more fun.  Full disclosure, I mostly play 3v3 because I get too sore when I lose 1v1, and 2v2 I feel like if we lose it's my fault, so to counter that anxiety I focus on 3v3.  So I'll admit I have a skewed perspective, all the same the game feel is much better than it was at launch, there's a bunch of cool stratagem abilities, and one thing I didn't realize the first time I touched the game is that the Italy campaign is actually really cool.  What they did with the turn based elements in between missions and skirmishes is very satisfying, allowing you to field ships and planes to help you out on the world map before then using them as artillery call ins when you go to real time was a really cool idea.  Please give this game another chance if you hated it's initial release, and if you have never played a CoH game before and somehow found my review first, then I'll just say a few things real quick.CoH is all about positioning and territory control.  You field squads instead of units, and everything you build is displayed at the bottom of the screen, so anytime one of your squads is close to getting wiped you can retreat them.  Suppression, cover (which is directional), and firing arcs are major mechanics, so a heavy machine gun can fight hordes of infantry head on, but dies from the side, as the approaching infantry have to hit the dirt but un suppressed units do full damage.  You need combined arms to win the game, but even with your tanks and AT you need go positioning, to get those rear and side armor hits you need to finish off that tank that is decimating your forces.  There are supply lines, so if you capture a point that's in enemy territory, it's possible to cut off their entire resource line just by breaking their territory, so you can pull off some really sneaky maneuvers to unseat an entrenched position.  Unit preservation is also huge in this game, a squad at max veterancy is very valuable to have late game.  There are 3 resources, manpower, munitions, and fuel.  Manpower and fuel are your standard RTS resources, every unit and building requires MP to build, and fuel is for teching up and fielding vehicles (so you can spam light vehicles early but it will delay your tech.  Munitions is used for abilities and upgrades, including grenades and artillery strikes, as well as better guns for your squads.  There are 4 factions total, 2 allies, 2 axis (US/Brit, Wehrmacht/Afrikakorps), all each of those have 4 different battlegroups that you can choose from, so you have different ways to play the same faction.  If you have never played CoH or Dawn of War 1/2, please try it out, it's much different from other RTS games and is much more focused on the actual movements you are making with your few units to control the battlefield, and the controlling territory IS your economy in this game, so you can focus purely on movement and army composition.  They have worked really hard, with a lot of resistance, the last couple months to make the game better, and I truly think the game is in a good spot now, can't comment on high level balance since I'm not that good but I enjoy the game greatly and I think anybody with a good attitude will do the same.I will say that the menus could use some love, after playing Age Of Empires I got spoiled on being able to review what units are available to each faction, sometimes this is frustrating, like say for example I am trying to do a daily order that requires building a certain unit but I can't remember the building it comes from.  It would be nice not to have to start up a skirmish just to remind myself this kind of information, and another way I'm spoiled on AoE is that you can go into a skirmish alone with no enemy, up the resources and down the build time just to mess around with things.  So there are some features I would appreciate being added that feel noticeably absent.  I wish I could view high level replays, as a fighting gamer I get spoiled on this, most fighting games let you download and watch replays from high level players.  I would say that my biggest criticism is that viewing/editing your battlegroups is kinda obtuse and slow.  To change your loadout you have to start a lobby, pick your faction, then select your groups.  If you want to do multiple, you have to do them one at a time.  Making an option to do this from the Loadout menu would be a very nice quality of life change.  However, none of these are major concerns, I have them set up the way I like now so I won't have to deal with it again unless they add more, and these are all just things I wish they would add for quality, but the core game experience is unaffected, and these are really just minor gripes.  I just thought I should include them for the sake of a balanced perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: "Company of Heroes 3" is a disappointing installment in the popular real-time strategy game series. Despite its promising premise, the game fails to deliver a satisfying gameplay experience.One of the major flaws of the game is its unbalanced factions. The factions are not equally matched, with some being significantly weaker than others, leading to an unfair advantage for certain players. This takes away from the strategic element of the game, as players are forced to rely on certain factions to have a chance of winning.Moreover, the game suffers from a lack of innovation. It feels like a rehash of the previous games in the series, with no new features or gameplay mechanics added. This makes the game feel stale and uninspired, and does not offer enough to keep long-time fans engaged.The graphics and sound design are also underwhelming. The game looks and sounds outdated compared to other modern strategy games, which is a shame considering the potential of the franchise.In summary, "Company of Heroes 3" is a disappointing game that fails to meet expectations. The unbalanced factions, lack of innovation, and outdated graphics and sound design all contribute to a lackluster gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has solid core gameplay complexity and balance.  It's a great foundation to build upon that the previous two titles lacked (IE. CoH1 had huge swinging imbalances for 5 years ).  It's very apparent they put a strong emphasis on working with top tier players to get a solid and competitive multiplayer experience.  For me this is very important.  I enjoy the competitive multiplayer aspect to the game, not the campaign.While I'm slightly disappointed that there are no profile options and unlocks like portrait frames they will be forthcoming along with ranked play and what looks to be a slew of unit skins and doctrines as well.  Comparing this to 9 years of work and patches put into CoH2 is a little disingenuous.  Every CoH title has seen significant improvement post-launch and I am sure this will be no exception.  The difference is CoH3 is starting with a vastly better core than either previous titles ever did.

I am certain that more is to come and they wanted to release this to balance it the fastest way possible and that's why not as much content is here. In it's current state it's value is around 30-40 dollars but I believe that will increase with time and some good patches. It is very stable with a great engine and that's really all it has going for it at the moment but that's nothing to speak poorly of, most games have terrible Engines and UIs like previous the COH2 title which you couldn't even have borderless window mode or change your keybinds. The Single Player is nothing special, but that's not why you would buy this game. The future is bright for Company of Heroes and I believe this game will be way more popular than it's predecessors. Also, it has mod support! Note: Ranked is still not out so this review is based on the core game. I believe if ranked takes too long to release, people will lose interest and this game will die faster than a fish out of water. Play this with a friend, the 2v2 experience is the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Core RTS gameplay is good and still addicting sadly there are also no big suprises.The experience is held back by the lack of polish. Or heavy weapon troops getting stuck forever behind my HQ when entering the map.That was really disappointing.The strategic campaign map feels unfinished and unpolished although I must admit it shows some ambition.The core mechanics of the Italy campaign are never explained and introduced properly and then it just ends very suddenly. Like they just ran out of time.I wish they had focused on this campaign instead of forcing me to play a Nazi General like Rommel. That's a really really weird choice in 2023.Here's an idea:Instead of cutting the game in two different game modes for the Italy campaign and the africa campaign make it one big dynamic RTS map. This is an RTS game. Go all in.Graphics are terrible sometimes even laughable when the civilians wave at you with their clunky animations. I admit it made me chuckle. It made me question my settings several times but after reading through half of reddit it seems to be the best you can get out of this game in 2023. Really disappointing. It makes me wonder if my grandma could make some extra money doing animations for AA video games.Here's an idea:Save the money for those disconnected cutscenes and invest it into polish and innovation. If you want to make movies or shows start a movie studio or a netflix show.Focus on what's important.Overall performance and polish are just terrible and disappointing for a studio like Relic.There are small and big glitches and bugs frequently which will hopefully be patched over the coming years. _childDocuments_.review: COH3 combines the best elements of both COH and COH2, improving on the previous editions and elaborating on the already great sandbox elements as seen previously.  All together, the combat feel fluid and moves away from mechanised/Inf spam stages as seen in COH2 and returns towards the roots of the series, making all units feel effective and competitive. Of course, as the game develops, metas will forum however, I feel there is an great combination of combined arms emphasis, with combinations to be discovered within the combination of factions in multiplayer/coop settings. Having played parts of the Italian campaign, the inclusion of surrounding environments impacting ground/air/navel assets is interesting and adds an interesting dynamic and planning and strategic element. While it is simplistic in nature, it does not add confusion or take away from the already strong sandbox skirmishes, but further builds on it. The in-game voice lines from the men is hilarious at time in their banter and cursing out at the situation adding some flavour to the troops and their interactions/action in game. I find the updated graphics to no longer distract from the action occurring, as it removes the OVERWHELMING emphasis on explosive payloads, and distracting nature of "out of map assets" as seen in previous editions. The graphics remain engaging and immersive while removing the distractions, which was necessary. This also applies to the sound design, as it is more streamlined and realistic to the actions occurring instead of again, overwhelming the player as before. Overall, this is a great sandbox environment, more along the lines of COH with positive inclusions from COH2 . It returns back to the series roots, emphasising on the importance of combat encounters and created atmosphere within a given scenario. Graphics and sound design are more streamline and less detracting while maintaining the players engagement and providing flavourful and interesting additions to the setting. This is a great addition to the series and ultimately improves the overall great WW2 RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of CoH1 and CoH2 - however with all the hype around this game and subsequent flopped launch, I stayed away for quite a long time until recently. TLDR; I recommend this game - it is fun for me as a casual PVP player.I've seen a lot of bad reviews for this game for failing to live up to the standards of prior games, complaints about faction balance, etc. And yeah, admittedly there are a few rough points here and there. I don't think these criticisms are fair to say "this game if awful because I don't like x, y, and z". Instead, I'd balance it with pros and cons. In my opinion:Pros:-Well-paced multiplayer matches with a variety of strategies and units to choose from-Devs that seem to care about multiplayer balance and are frequently releasing patches-Great weapon / explosion sound design - feels gritty and chaotic-Clear visual graphics - easy to differentiate units/see what is happening on the field-Fun casual multiplayer experience (advise playing with friends as the community is a weird mix of super friendly and super toxic)-Factions do not have parity - that is every faction plays a bit different!Cons:-AI kinda sucks. The skirmish and coop vs. AI experience is not amazing. I think this has always been a problem with CoH though - I recall AI in CoH1&2 constantly running troops just to cap points and map hacking to avoid MGs. This hasn't changed.-The grand campaign is disappointing. Its a great idea - not executed well. The missions are awesome, the campaign skirmishes feel like lazy filler.-The unit responses and banter can be overwhelming. In big fights, your units talk so much with "fluff" it is easy to miss the important sound queues like a unit coming under fire or being destroyed.-Weird microtransaction garbage. I'm fine with skins - but the level of paywall to lock commander choices is disheartening. I've played 113 hours generally giving a decent amount of effort on earning the weekly and daily points and still haven't unlocked my first commander.Overall, I have had a lot of fun playing the game. If you've been skeptical to get it, but enjoy playing PVP - I highly suggest you give it a try once it goes on sale again.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are multiplayer focused buy this game. There are many improvements on the already solid COH core gameplay:-Increased focus on light vehicles, less rush to heavy tanks, when heavy tanks finally arrive they feel powerful-Better tank battles due to front/side/back armor system-Holding high ground actually matters-Return to command tree system is a huge improvement over COH2 commander system-More drawn out firefights compared to COH2 (another return to COH1 style play)-better faction design than previous installments   -return of a panzer elite-like faction (Afrika Korps) without the infantry blobs  -no forced sim-city, the British are a fun mobile faction like the rest  -no weird USA pizza-base, US forces play like dynamic well designed USA from COH1-so many light vehicles! did I mention I like light vehicles!?The map design is excellent and the Mediterranean scenery is a great backdrop.The single player content is very rough around the edges. If you are single player focused hold off for a few months. But overall this game has the potential to be the best of both COH1 and COH2.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the Italian Campaign, I'm not crazy invested in the story of a WWII RTS game because, well, I kinda already know how it went. I'm more interested in the things that make this game stand out to me from CoH2 (I haven't played 1 so this is my only comparison). There is several quality of life improvements that make it much easier to have a "run and gun" strategy compared to the second game. Mainly the improvements to the unit pathing, which makes the game 1000% less frustrating. I can't count how many times I've commanded a unit to go in a direction in CoH2 only for them to take the most convoluted route possible passed a machine gun nest, forcing me to retreat them. The German campaign was okay, I didn't really see the point that the story was trying to make. I think the devs should have put a bit more time into the writing of that portion of the game. It wouldn't have hurt if it was longer as well, it seems like the most effort was put into the Italy campaign. I can understand the reasons why some of the people are not recommending this game. But all I can tell you is that I had fun playing it and that I felt like it was, mechanically, a huge improvement on the second game. The 33.5 hours I have on record are how long it took for me to beat the Italy campaign and the German campaign on standard. Maybe you're less of a scrub than me it would be shorter for you, but I feel I got my money's worth. I purchased this on sale, if you are weary of the game because of the negative reviews, I suggest buying on sale like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone that's giving this a negative review is just your classic nitpicking cry baby entitled gamer that is never satisfied. I've been playing COH games since day 1. This game has a bit of work to do, yes, but so do all games when they release, because what most gamers fail to realize apparently is that you can never predict what may or may not be working fully. I mean just look at the complete dumpster fire that is Call of Duty MW 2 or BF 2042. But as far as a COH game is concerned, this is the best yet as far as features added, the ability to create multiple companies that you can reinforce and keep going way easier than the American campaign of COH 2. Upgrades and unlocking units is a different style than previously but I'd say better. The addition of Naval Ships to provide additional fire support, bombers , fighters and transport aircraft to para drop your companies right on enemy cities or locations or even just move them across the battlefield easier is a great addition. The AI enemies even on the easiest difficulty in a bot game are still a challenge. i had a 2 on one match against an AI with a friend on easy because he's not as seasoned with COH as I am and the AI almost overran our base before we pushed them back. So its definitely a challenge and lots of fun. One negative i will say is the lack of available maps for MP/coop play. and some of them are just the same maps for 4v4 as 3v3 or 2v2, just enlarged. Adding a few more maps to play would be perfect, there's plenty to work with in the Italian and North African Campaigns of WWII that you can make more maps to play. _childDocuments_.review: As a significant fan of the Company of Heroes series, it's disappointing to see the game in it's current state after significant patch updates post release in which there remains a few notable issues which deserve attention such as over the following:- You are unable to customise your profile icon and background in menu screen, significantly worse compared to CoH2. I am also unable to determine my ranking and stats which again is frustrating for a AAA strategy game.- In relation to Loadouts in menu screen, you are not able to customise the skins of vehicle call-ins (e.g. Tiger Tank for Wehrmacht and for Afrika Korps) to be more consistent with the skins you have acquired on the rest of your army (disappointing especially since the game has moved into micro-transactions for cosmetics a month after launch, I am surprised this was not considered earlier in light of significant patch updates).- Depending on the weapon upgrade of a squad, the white icon indicating the weapon does not accurately show what weapon is held. The BAR weapon icon shows for the Breda Model 30 light machine gun upgrade for Afrika Korps Bersaglieri squad (call-in unit). Surely if the design team had enough time to create the simple white weapon icon for all other units, why would this unit be treated any differently.- The Nebelwerfer 42 Rocket Launcher - the fire damage from its rockets does not count towards the kill count (small technical detail).- No "Turret destroyed" effect on tanks like the game had in CoH2.- USF Rifleman when equipped with BARs, the BARs appear to float on the ground at the feet of the infantry whether stationary or moving and not held in their hands. This is also evident with other squad units that have heavy weapons in hand like USF Captain Squad, Wehrmacht Stoẞtruppen Squad.- Heavy tanks can't crush / destroy abandoned team weapons by driving over them.- Heavy tanks can't crush infantry behind cover (perhaps in consideration of avoiding the game become tank dependent to win).- You are unable to rotate / change the direction of your machine gun team in an occupied building like you could in CoH2. You therefore lose valuable seconds and the initial machine gun burst on advancing squads as the machine gun team has to reposition itself to a different window facing the enemy before firing.- When units mount into the 2.5-tonne Medical Truck of Akrika Korps, the unit models stick outside of the truck and makes them look like they levitating and gliding next to the vehicle.- Wehrmacht Medical Bunker does not allow for an auto-reinforce ability like the HQ or the 251 Medium Carrier with the medical upgrade. Very strange not to allow this when compared to the British Forces medical tent.- The latest balance has made Wehrmacht notably more powerful than any other faction in 1v1 PvP with USF as a close second when using the Armored Battlegroup.- The British forces are not able to build the Churchill heavy tank without selecting the appropriate Battlegroup and hence British are the weakest from a tank on tank combat perspective. I would encourage new Battlegroups be released to help balance factions better.- Disappointed with the factions, given the focus on North Africa and Italian eras in that this game has lost those exiting units from CoH2 like the German King Tiger, the American PErshing tank etc. Perhaps will be addressed in future DLCs.- The AT gun weapon teams can use "Attack ground" option and allow the unit to fire through foilage and buildings and hit your tank. It's unbelievable this was permitted after the last significant balance patch.- When playing with and against AI, the AI machine gun teams will randomly keep firing on the same spot after an engagement, reload and then continuing shooting on the same spot on the ground as if there was an enemy on that spot.- The enemy AI (even on Expert difficulty level) do not retake their own abandoned weapons (machine guns, mortar, anti-tank) thus making it less competitive for players who are trying to upskill themselves to prepare them for PvP. Even AI on Expert difficulty is surprisingly not difficult to compete against.- Unit pathways, especially for vehicles, need improvement.Overall, the game is worth what I paid for it via CDKeys (under GBP 30) but I would not be prepared to pay the full retail price of GBP 49.99 on Steam for the base game based on its current state. I won't even touch on GBP 69.99 for Digital Premium Edition. My sense is that the game was released too early (seen similar issues with other AAA titles like Battlefield 2042) to meet budgets but has resulted in a significant negative response by the fans of the game series. I do appreciate game developers need to make sales to bring in cash flow and support their ongoing project to fulfil the potential this game has to be an excellent WWII strategy game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game, so a thumbs up, but be aware there might be major gripes for you:CoH2 was far better.The WH und US Army from CoH1 are back minus the more capable tanks. DAK resembles Panzer Elite minus the the infantry punch. As a vehicle focused faction, it has the weakest tanks in game and can not really defend itself against mediocre allied tanks like the M3 Lee or Sherman without using specific AT units, which can only really be deployed defensively and take so many hits to destroy an enemy tank that frankly the enemy needs to be AFK not to notice and put in reverse, whereas all german tanks are paper tanks.Allied infantry is completely superior across the board, but where WH at least gets some mildly useful infantry, DAK will remain completely reliant on light vehicles.Most vehicles are not correctly portrayed to a point that can only be called history revisionism. Suddenly M3 Lee Tanks (I think only a handful saw actual action because it was being phased out already when the war began) and Shermans dominate the battlefield and take up to 6 hits even from a PAK, whereas a bazooka is enough to crack most german vehicles (slightly exaggerated but it gets the point across).Doctrines and offmap abilities are mostly useless for axis, and superior for allies. I will just say that allies can call in loitering hurricanes that 1- or 2-hit even Panzer4s in an area so big that even if you escape ASAP your units will not have a chance to get out. AAA units do nothing against those planes either. I don't see how putting an ability in the game that requires no micromanagement or other skills and is capable of destroying however many high-value late game tanks with one click is a sensible choice.The game is still of high quality and definitely enjoyable, but the balancing in CoH2 was a million times better, and all the factions more interesting and fun.This is definitely a huge step back. The fact that there is no matchmaking frustrates you even more, as there are huge skill gaps, the already small playerbase results in repeatedly fighting the same enemies.I have zero interest in the single player modes, especially the strategic campaign, so Relic put the effort in the wrong places for my tastes.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews come from people who like CoH 2 and did very little CoH 1.From a multiplayer point of view. Company of Heroes 3 is more like the first game. The major difference between the two is units die quickly in Company of Heroes 2 and slower in Company of Heroes 1 and 3. Units dying quickly means that battles end quicker and you can't reposition your units which means less tactical involvement and more emphasis on having fast reaction times. Basically. Company of Heroes 1 and 3 test your tactical and strategical ability more than Company of Heroes 2 does. A grenade can kill a full health squad in CoH 2. In CoH 1 and 3 you would have to retreat the squad. Essentially you still lose by having to retreat a squad but it maintains units on the battlefield to keep the action high. High action is what makes CoH thrilling and exciting. In CoH 2 multiplayer there's more down time because units clash together and soon have to retreat. The bullets hardly stop flying in CoH 3.If you look at the negative complaints. There are many over reactions. You'll see this one a lot;"Unit Icons Missing"Yes. It's not great. But it's not a massive deal. The Icon still shows that something is a tank or tank destroyer. It's only a FEW units that have this issue. I'm glad that the issues are only tiny and that the core gameplay as massively prioritized which quite often, even among the negative comments, many agree is great.We've now entered an era though where apparently having the in game store and how it works is far more important than the gameplay itself. That's really upsetting.Is the game overpriced? That's subjective to you but bear this in mind. The RTS genre is not a popular one and among the RTS games. How many even bother to have multiple run cycles for infantry? How many actually have a cover system? The Company of Heroes Franchise, and this includes 3, is still one of the most technologically involved RTS games out there. If you're running a game development studio and want to make money. You don't bloody make an RTS game in this day and age. I'm not saying we should be thankful or grateful that Relic made this game but at least acknowledge that RTS games are not a genre which typically sells in a massive volume. And that may be reflected in the price.Other complaints such as audio. Audio is getting updated but even so. The audio in the game isn't BAD. It's not overwhelming great. Company of Heroes 1 had great sounds. Company of Heroes 2 was alright. Company of Heroes 3 is okay too but it's getting updated very soon with new sounds which are extremely beefy sounding.Communication? People have complained so much. They complained about the graphics and they listened. Then they complained about the graphics again after listening and changing. The game was apparently TOO colorful so they washed it out and then people complained it lost all its color. COME ON. They complained about the audio and still do but the audio is getting massively overhauled and guess what? None of the bloody reviews and comments seem to acknowledge this whilst still complaining about communication. Communication is a two way street. Relic ARE listening and they are talking. But if you aren't listening then how can you hear what they are saying?All in all. You won't be disappointed by CoH 3 if you are new to the franchise or you enjoyed CoH 1 and were disappointed by CoH 2. If you played CoH 2 heavily then you might think CoH 3 is a downgrade. CoH 2 in many ways was also a downgrade from CoH 1 but we conveniently leave that part out. You might also think CoH 3 is a downgrade if one of your opinions is "Most of the content is cut from CoH 2". Because CoH 2 had 10 years of development where it slowly added more units and commanders. CoH 3 hasn't had that time yet to add that content. It's an extremely unfair statement.Oh yeah. Maps? Single Player? They spent ALOT of time on the single player campaign and I'm a person who hates single player. I don'tlike it. I don't bother with it and I didn't enjoy it in CoH 3. Because that's me. However many people DO play single player and skirmish against AI because playing against other players is scary or unwanted. I think it was a great idea to focus on the single player experience first because it would be hard to add to that later. Unlike multiplayer which they will continue to shove updates out for. The single player experience is what gets a percentage of people to get into the multiplayer so delivering a solid experience there is important.There are many maps in the Single Player that are unique. Maps take a long time to make (as a map maker myself). The community has always been very driven to make maps for multiplayer but never single player. In CoH 2 we had a ton of community maps and the same is expected in CoH 3. So yes at the moment the map pool is small but maps will be added in the future.I hope this helps! TL:DR? If you are new to Company of Heroes. CoH 3 is great. If you played CoH 2. You may have a very fixed expectation which leads you to believe the game is bad. CoH 2 people hate CoH 3 for the same reasons CoH 1 people hated CoH 2. CoH 3 is more like CoH 1. It's slightly more tactical/strategical. CoH 2 is a bit more reactionary.

_childDocuments_.review: For now I will say to stay far away form this game. The game was clearly rushed out the door without it being done.The campaign UI is so badly done that I would think it's a pre-production UI with placeholders. E.g: They display a number, but it doesn't have enough space to display, so it goes on two lines. Many part of the UI are just a grey/colored boxes with text inside, without any texture, which makes them look so weird and out of context.The units movement on the campaign map just look ridiculous. If you ask your tank to go back, it will instantly start moving to that point while the model is spinning around, making it look like a game school project grade tier of animation.There is a "affections" system with your generals to give you some bonuses, but the system just looks tacked on at the last minute and really badly made. Your two generals just keep annoying you to do this or that and bickers like two children that wants you attention. You look at the terribly made UI for the affection "tree" and it doesn't really explain much about what each reward do.The missions looks super scripted on the campaign map, so even if it's a huge man, your generals will ask you to do this or that. So you end up following predetermined paths with main missions and secondary objectives. Which makes me wonder what is the point of the map. It doesn't seems to give me freedom to do what I want like a Total War game. Right now I just wish I could simply do the older CoH game style of campaign and have some bits of story between missions. But I'm still early in the campaign, so maybe it will change after some time.I just finished a defense mission from the campaign. They ask me to defend three objective points. They already have  maximum units deployed on all three points and nicely balance (at-tank, mg crew, engineer, etc) on each point. So I just wait for the attack to start. After the attacker started coming in, I realized after a few minutes that I don't actually need to do anything. The enemy would just walk up to the point and die over and over. I just sat there staring at the screen doing nothing and still won the mission. What a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original Company of Heroes and are focused on single player, you will probably love this game. It had several, game-breaking bugs at release that kept me from completing the campaign until very recently. But the patches have smoothed things out, and then result is a really fun and engaging game. The mix of missions and skirmish types in the Italy Campaign is solid, and you have a ton of freedom and flexibility to play the way you want to. I cannot speak to the multiplayer as I don't play that format. I appreciate the developers fixing things as they could.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: All of the below is still valid after about a month of daily patches. No major changes have been made except one:They added microtransactions for cosmetics that are garbage looking.Whenever a company says they are going to do something (like patch the problems in their software) - understand they want you to believe this so they can do the opposite.This will be the last game in the COH franchise. Sega apparently thought its been too long since someone pulled an EA-Westwood.----------"Bigger and better than ever"There is far less here then was available for COH2 on launch... FAR less."heart-pounding combat with deeper strategic choices in a stunning Mediterranean theatre of war."Translation: we stole the army movement on a large map from Total War and thought that was nifty when in reality its completely boring."every battle tells a story..."The campaign certainly does, in fact it won't stop telling the story to let me play the damn game.WTF is this relic... A TON.Campaigns are basically broken and Relic refuse to even acknowledge the problem (theyll just straight up blame your rig even if its top of the line and their binary isn't actually utilizing any resources for load). Infantry constantly leap over barriers you tell them to hide behind because one circle is on the other side (so the whole squad decides to go).
