_childDocuments_.review: Great writing, simple but fun combat, great art style. The story is very interesting and pretty original from my experiences. It apes on Groundhog's Day but with a wildly different pay off.  The looping mechanic also gives a plot reason for the limited settings. That being said, the story feels like it lasts a little longer than it needs to. That's not to say there are things i would cut (maybe trim) but because the story necessitates a few too many repeat trips through the House, later in the game I resorted to using a guide because I did not want to be bothered to search high and low for the story checkboxes that would let me proceed. On the story, there are a couple story beats that never really got resolved..My biggest nitpick, the nature of the looping leads to a lot of repeated dialog. That is eased by a skip (nod off) function, but it is limited in weird ways. If the text is something Sif is thinking then it can't be skipped, some of the dialog in the town can't be skipped, the mini quests with your team mates can't be skipped until you talk to them for a while making it tedious to do over and over again. I think this should absolutely be addressed as this felt like the most annoying time waster in this otherwise pretty great game. Also I found Bonnie pretty annoying and unlikeable but the game made sure to tell me that I do like Bonnie, which I did not. This is important for some scenes that should have been more emotionally impactful than they ended up being in practice.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I'm going to be real with you, the reader of this review.You're gonna cry. You play this game? you're gonna get some tears down your face. The writing is top notch, the characters and interactions between them feel very genuine. The world built and explored in the game are engaging to think about while leaving a lot to the imagination. I can't say much more without spoiling the game. It's a story-based experience with a lot of reading and nuances to the story. If you as a player like to be immersed within a game and feel like you are 1 for 1 with the protagonist, this game does a great job of doing that. However, if you've ever seen Bill Murray in Groundhog day, you're going to feel very similar to him. (you're stuck in a time loop, after all). Exploring new avenues to advance the story is quite nicely done due to how many hints are given and how much setup is put into the game. Frankly, I even love how some questions about the world aren't really answered.Avenues to advance your knowledge about the time loop are very naturally set up and feel satisfying to realize + act upon.There are very minor things about the game to complain about. Like seriously minor things. Isabeau's hands look like feet in certain positions (namely when he has both palms up) and I couldn't tell what was going on in some of the attack poses for the characters until quite literally my last 2 hours of playing the game and specifically studying the character portraits when they made attacks, but that could also just be me missing things. Overall experience: 9/10. My complaints are very minor and don't affect the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 100% worth your time. Turn based rock paper scissors style combat that is just so unique and satisfying, I practically never ran from battles because the combat is so fun! TONS of different dialogue depending on situations, items you interact with and which time loop you are on.Literally the most lovable group of characters, trust me, you will love them.Laughed out loud at some response options and conversations, near tears on others. (It is a pretty emotionally heavy game)OUTSTANDING ART! Literal eye candy, animation is beautiful as well.Despite the looping mechanic I'm left with the desire to replay it!Lots of LGBTQ+ representation! (Some very heartfelt convos of sexuality handled with so much care)I actually enjoyed the music more than I thought I would! I didn't expect anything stand-out from this game but I was pleasantly surprised! (Mini boss theme slaps HARD)I think this game is going to stick with me for a long time, it does a great job making you emotionally invested in your main character and their struggle trying to keep what's happening to them a secret from their friends, and watching as he fights to keep his mental state intact to keep each loop stable and consistent for his friends. (which doesn't happen EVERY loop, get ready for some pretty shocking deviations when they finally start to crack)you feel for him so deeply.And just- trust me. Play it. You will love it! Can't recommend enough! I'm already planning on getting it for the nintendo switch ;) 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much I like and so much I dislike about this gameFor one the art style and general designs are all great. The battle system is pretty neat and intuitive. Based on a rock-paper-scissors kinda of deal. Quite literally. The characters are all really sweet and are pretty distinct from each other but brings up one of the downsides. They can be outright obnoxious sometimes. Generally just whenever they get very cutesy and sappy. Still there's some charm to even that as well.That also brings up the story which sways back and forth from being really interesting and delving into how characters think and really feel like things are progressing to filling out a checklist you don't even have. Sometimes someone will just say something along the lines of "oh I remember there being windows or something" and you need to search the whole map to find out what it is. The story does have a lot of intrigue surrounding it which is the main thing that kept me pushing forward. It's a genuinely cool mystery with a lot of threads to follow up on.By far the biggest negitive for this game is the amount of content you need to replay over and over with no real changes. Thankfully you can skip forward in some sections granted you've already completed it but it requires a currency this system just eats up. I really wish there wasn't a currency for skipping forward, it would cut down a lot on the back tracking. Even if this is a time loop game you can tell this is padding. Now the time loop function does allow for cool moments where you share the characters frustration about things not changing and even from that thought new change occurs. How the enemies behave as well really adds to the padding. They are quite difficult to avoid and each fight takes a while. Now keep in mind they aren't hard. I don't think I ever even went below half health to a normal enemy but there's a host of menus and animations and load times you need to get through before you can finish. Still the story has its moments, the characters are interesting enough a good amount of the time and the battle system is legit good, which is why I reccomend it. Just be prepared for a looooot of back tracking.

_childDocuments_.review: As a game, In Stars And Time is awful. Basically from every angle I look at with its game play it is at best, a mediocre RPG maker game and at worst, legitimately boring and frustrating. If you've noticed a ton of RPG maker games having an issue where "spam basic attack" will win most encounters, know this one is no different. Basically every random encounter and boss fight can be beaten by completely ignoring the game's "unique" fighting mechanics, skills, and items in favor of just, spam basic attack and occasionally heal. Random encounters are annoying to say the least. The rewards you get from them are worthless (especially considering most of that reward is taken away per loop), and the enemies themselves serve only to make each loop and back track to be tedious and padded out rather over anything.The game has a weird issue where it can't decide what difficulty it wants. The entire game up to the king is so lazily easy, you have to wonder what's even the point of having combat in the first place. I am not joking when I say I would've enjoyed this game more with zero combat up to the king's fight because it only serves to waste your time. The only thing I would want to keep the combat for is I do like the battle portraits of the main cast.The game also takes a note from Nintendo by fluffing out the early half with a frustratingly long tutorial of its very basic mechanics. The game's tutorial takes about 18 minutes to finish, and the entire tutorial could've been summed up with "hey it goes by rock paper scissors rules" I guarantee you everyone above the age of 8 playing this game would understand the combat (other than the all-out-attack) if you had just condensed the tutorial to that. I tried early on to not let the slow start affect my opinion of the game, but it dragged on so long that the game almost feels too horrible in that aspect to not be intentionally boring and repetitive.Which wouldn't be too much of an issue if the game's dialogue was better. Don't get me wrong, I actually like the characters, and a good amount of their interactions are fun for me to read (the first time at least but we'll get to that.) There's a recurring issue that this game is written, at best, at teenager fan fiction level. The dialogue is ripped seemingly straight from 2010s tumblr humor and marvel one liners. If you enjoy that humor, that's fine. But I don't really find the "puns", the "fake cursing", and the overall children's cartoon level way these characters talk endearing at all. I would say about half of the dialogue in this game had me cringing or rolling my eyes. The other half either being tolerable or interesting. What's weird about the childishness of the writing is this game has adult themes. This is by no means a children's game. It's like if Steven Universe occasionally was broken up by adult characters talking about sex and alcohol. What is the tone supposed to be.The characters are one-note archetypes and nothing really pushes them beyond that. The main character is the only one with "depth", but the depth feels more like a self insert fan fic oc rather than a real, interesting, layered character. Which honestly feels like a disservice to how interesting they COULD be. I love all of their designs, and I love how they bounce off each other. These characters are best when they are allowed to interact and chat as people and not just make another stupid pun. Sorry, but being "Self-aware" to how puns aren't funny doesn't actually make them a good addition to the game. As a one off joke, maybe, but this game relies heavily on it being so cringe, immature, and amateurish in writing but then pretending its self aware by that. Is it really self-aware if there's not actual commentary or deviation from that style of writing? There is nothing EXCEPT immature, marvel jokes here in most of the dialogue. There's only out-dated memes and "quirky" moments that you've seen 100 times before in better games. Is that really interesting for a player just because the writers know how lazy that writing is? I don't think so personally.The most interesting part of the game's story / mechanics is the time looping. Small problem, it is the most under-baked, sad excuse of a time loop mechanic I've seen. I am not joking when I say nearly every time I had to loop was from the game FORCING me into a moment that it went "aww man, guess you gotta loop back!" The game has no puzzles. It has no player choice. It has nothing the player can do that makes them feel like they're playing a game. The puzzle the game recycles over and over is: go into new room, nothing to interact with, leave, "oh no, that room is blocked off now and there was a key in there you missed main character!! if only we had a way to loop back and get in there", die, loop back, now the game ALLOWS you to pick up the key, continue with story. There was no choice, there was nothing you failed on your part, that entire interaction was rail-roaded for you and you must do it every time you play the game. I am bored of that and this is my first play through. The designers have killed any potential and desire for anyone to want to replay it from the start.A last thing about replay-ability, the game doesn't allow you to skip dialogue until you've seen it. So a lot of times, you'll be forced to watch a text box slowly fill up with annoying text that's entirely unskippable. This is made worse when you have to re-watch some scenes especially early on as you aren't even allowed to skip repeated dialogue. Admittedly the game is aware that repeating the same dialogue over and over gets annoying, so it gives you an fast-forward button on SOME dialogue scenes. Why did I highlight some? Well that fast-forward button is only present on, I'd say, around 60% of the repeated scenes in the game. This leads to times where you actually do still have to sit through the slow text boxes, the long dialogue trees, and horrible writing in its entirety. There is no skipping it no matter how many times you see it. Why is this? I have no idea. It feels entirely arbitrary when you are allowed to skip and when you're not. The final salt rub in the wound is that the fast forward isn't even that fast. I would much prefer it just skip to the very end of the tree instantly or to my next dialogue choice rather I be forced to watch the scene play out slightly faster. Before you say, "well if the dialogue bothers you that bad, just turn off dialogue animations". Let me tell you, I did from very early on. The dialogue is still a slog to get through. It's so clunky for no reason. If you're going to write dialogue you as the writer are self aware is bad, why make the user experience so bad as to be forced to read it over and over and over again? It makes you start hating these characters for how much they yap. The middle point twist isn't even enough to save this game. By that point, I've already grown to hate the characters, the story, and the repetitive dungeon I'm forced to explore with the same 6 enemies patrolling it. I want to like this, but it truly is not worth the money or time.Before I leave though, I do want to have a positive section-The art in the game is really nice. I love the main cast's designs. They are expressive, lively, and a joy to see. Whoever made the art for the game deserves plenty praise. I am very happy of the game for having a lot of positive LGBT representation. More games need that, and even if I am not enjoying the game play that much, just for good representation alone I am happy to support the game with my money and never refund it. While I'm sure some people would find LGBT in their game to be a negative, I am actually an adult therefore I don't "eww gay = bad". The game does have good moments and interesting lore occasionally. Those moments carried me through to want to finish it. The character dynamics are fun to see. The game obviously has a lot of heart put into it. I hope it gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: A time loop RPG with interesting worldbuilding and a fun (and diverse!) cast of characters. _childDocuments_.review: 21.7 hours in. I've never cried while playing a video game before. This game had me sobbing. Actually sobbing. I don't usually get super attached to characters, but man, I would both kill and die for Siffrin. 10/10 would sob again.EDIT: It took me 37 hours, but I'm finally at the epilogue. Let me tell yall a thing.This game ripped my heart out, tore it to shreds, stomped on it, annihilated the pieces with a death ray; waited a few minutes, then fixed it better than it was before.During my play-through I saw a lot of myself in Siffrin, and it sounds odd but I honestly didn't expect a happy ending. When I first installed this game I wasn't in a good place. I felt alone, like my purpose was to always be an outsider, just like our boy. But now, months later, I've found my Mirabell, my Odile, my Bonnie... and I think I've even found my Isabeau.To the developers, thank you for giving Siffrin the ending he deserves, and thank you for reminding me that the end isn't always the end.

As you go further, this mechanic becomes your tool... and something much worse. _childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful  and heartwarming game about the connections you form and the families you find. In Stars and Time does something oddly unique, it sets up a groundhog day RPG with an honestly interesting and diverse group of characters at the end of their adventure.There is something strangely beautiful in this. I had a hard time finishing games as a kid, countless adventures would stop at the final dungeon because I couldnt give up the characters I had formed a link with and this feels the same.I could talk for hours about this game given half the chance but I will keep the review snappy.Music is amazing with a lot of hidden layers.Gameplay is simple but enjoyable. As time goes on you might neglect the RPG side in favour of the visual novel side but that is entirely valid.Artwork is adorable and lively with a lot of well drawn and interesting character art.There are a few glitches to contend with. Steam Notifications can glitch to the edge of the screen during play and conversations can glitch a little if you move while characters talk.Writing is stellar with a lot of optional dialogue and flavour text that will pull you into the world and lore.About half way through the story at time of writing but I can't wait to finish this wonderfully beautiful game.Solid 8/10 so far. Might go up after I'm finished.

_childDocuments_.review: "In Stars and Time" wants to be a game about mental health, persistence through dark times and trying to break cycles. However, it fails to be both a game, and has nothing truly interesting to say about these dark themes. The gameplay (if you can call it that) is incredibly tedious by design. You go through this rpg castle gauntlet and you are forced to repeat the same scripts, the same bosses, the same sequences over and over. Of course, the game wants to create this feeling of helplessness and frustration in the player with this intentionally boring gameplay. Unfortunately, the ends don't justify the means. The characters try way too hard to be quirky and "likeable", and the humour falls completely flat, unless you're maybe 15 years old and you think Tumblr is the peak of comedy. As for what the game is trying to say...well...There's a sequence much later on in the game where your character thinks that just maybe, 'the power of friendship' could be what breaks the curse of the timeloop. You do everything right, make everyone love you, and you go through the whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ castle from top to bottom. You reach the end - nothing changes. The game is trying to say that 'the power of friendship' is too naive and simplistic for the real world. Alright.Then at the very end of the game, something very similar happens. You've made it to the end, and then your character breaks down because they don't want their friends to leave them behind. After a lot of monologuing, it turns out that the curse would've been broken all along if you just...talked to your friends. About your feelings. Oh. I guess the world was saved by the power of friendship all along. Listen, this game is not deep or interesting enough to suffer through 23+ hours of soul draining gameplay. And even if it was, WHY make a game like this? It's not fun, it's not unique, and worst of all, it punishes you constantly! A GOOD mystery game gives you all the puzzle pieces, and rewards your interest when you, as a player, make an effort to put the puzzle pieces together. Does this game do that? No way. If you're one step ahead at any point in this never ending gauntlet, it punishes you and says 'No, no, you're not ALLOWED to solve this mystery, or find the right object in this room'. You have to wait for HOURS until the game gives you PERMISSION to notice and use the same item. This is asinine. This is not intuitive gameplay - it's more like an overwritten visual novel that forces you to wait a whole hour to turn one page. Some people may compare this gameplay to the genocide route from Undertale, however, I have to disagree. For starters, the player has agency in Undertale, and they are not forced to do anything to progress. The genocide route may be repetitive and 'boring' by design, but 1) it's making a statement that systemically killing everyone in each room WOULD be boring, that violence isn't glamorous or cool. And 2) most importantly, Undertale only takes a couple of hours to complete. So even if you find it boring, it's over quickly and doesn't waste your time. Furthermore, Undertale has a deep and fascinating world that unravels itself through characters, environmental storytelling, and your unique experience as a player. The world of 'In Stars and Time' is strictly confined to one tiny town, and a castle. That's it. The rest of the world is only learnt through endless scrolls of quirky dialogue, which is a very boring way of having the player learn about your world. Overall, this game can be compared to a very long lecture about the importance of mental health and communication, wearing the paint of fantasy and magic. It doesn't have anything interesting or challenging to say beyond the surface. And it's not really a game either.Don't buy it. If you get it for free, do what you want with it, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: I CAN'T CRABBING BELIEVE THIS.All the way through the game, EVERYTHING is fine. As the plot thickens, mysteries unveil, but they NEVER GET UNFOLDED. I enjoyed getting into Siffrin's shoes, and the author almost made it to read my thoughts. To be frank, these 28 hours has been the most engaging hours in my indie game life.  There were too many hints waiting to be explained in the end or somewhere near the end. Yet the end was, in fact, nothing. A pale, meaningless, abrupt, hasty, concluding only half way through, ending.As per said. Anticlimactic. I sincerely can not understand why the author has to do this to me.To make me feel like Siffrin themselves? To know so much yet be all in vain in the end? To be anticipating the  final revelation, yet only given VOID?Then. Congratulations. You win.I WILL NEVER RECOMMEND THIS GAME TO ANYONE.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much.A lot of the games I've played are pretty good, a nice bundle of fun gameplay and overall just a good time. You play it, you smile during it, sometimes you get frustrated, and then you finish the game, feeling great about the fact that you played it and then you move on with your life. It's a good way to spend your time, and maybe you add it to a list of games that you recommend.This game isn't like that, really. It's one of the most beautiful games that I've played in a very long time. Driving this game are a beautiful, heart-wrenching story, wonderful character moments and nice dialogue. The music captures the mood really well throughout this rollercoaster of a game. As I played this game, I found myself really caring about the characters, rooting for them and cringing, yelling at my laptop when they're about to something stupid and terrible. At its core, the combat system is based on rock-papers-scissors, and the power-ups are relatively simple. It may not have as difficult battles as some RPGs, nor does it have a particularly difficult strategy and different parts to play with. But that doesn't matter. It's really about the story, about the characters that you interact with, and about the emotional tenor and the mysterious backstory underpinning the whole game.This game stacks up with the likes of Undertale and OMORI, and I'd highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a really great, story-driven game. It's truly an amazing game and worth the 20 dollars.Siffrin, buddy, I'm going to miss you. I'm not going to forget you either.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's great, I really got into it very fast with how much attention it has been given everywhere. The 5 main characters already have so much to go for, their personality are very well written for who and what they're meant to be. The main story along every optional event really adds a lot to those characters by giving more details about them or their backstories and give them interactions with what you've seen and what you've done. I don't want to spoil anything but if you're looking for a Heavy and promising story, This game will be quite a ride.The gameplay itself is pretty charming and actually didn't even bother me one minute with how it's meant to be repetitive, I always wanted to interact with 90% of the objects in the House to see what happens or what changed and even if nothing new or special happened, I'd still go for it later, This game really encourages you to interact with objects and really take looks at what you've already seen before and that's awesome to see a game do it so well without it being boring, You'd think you would get annoyed of it after 10 times but the only person is complaining is poor Siffrin.It would also go for the combat system which I liked a lot, It didn't feel like mashing the same attacks over and over to be done quickly (Until you reached a point in the game you're so powerful that combat is just a  EXP grinder for the sake of unlocking one skill for your party member) I still kind of wish that this game got more difficult as you progress, maybe a difficulty that makes combat less of a snooze in the middle-late portion of the game but it also makes sense that it's easy because you've seen it so much that it's meant to look second hand eventually.I can talk a lot about the many details this game has but I'd like to leave this review for the people who haven't played it yet, This game has been my GOTY for 2024 and I've actually played quite a few games that we're already pretty impressive, This one takes the top! Thank you insertdisc5 for this amazing experience!!

_childDocuments_.review: I will never be normal about this game. I don't think I can ever be normal about this game.This game main feature, by a long shot, is story. It has fantastic characters, fantastic dynamics, and an incredible story.Honestly, go play the game. Even if you're not the biggest fan of the combat repetition(and the combat WILL get annoying. this is inevitable.), it is so, so worth it.To say mental illness is a struggle would be...an understatement. I absolutely adore the approach of it the developer took in ISAT. I thought it was mellow for the entire first half of the game, noticing the negative self talk but...not everything else. Not during my first playthrough.It takes the smaller things about depression and makes me feel so very called out. About the sleepiness, about doing things because there's not much better to do, about hiding away, avoiding touch, avoiding talking...all of it. The absolute spiral that Siffren goes through over the course of the game made me have to step back and re-evaluate some of things I'm doing because oh god. I could get to that same space. I really, truly could. I'm not sure I can say this changed my life, but I can say that it has made me take a step back, and acknowledge that I really do need to talk to other people about what I want, and that it's okay to be seen. Because if I don't, if I don't allow myself to be seen, I could very easily get stuck in my own loop of self doubt and spiral out of control.Play this game. Even if you don't like turn-based combat mechanics, or find the repetitive parts of time loop narratives(always getting the same things over and over again). Play it for the characters. Play it for the story.Play it for yourself.And then go talk to someone about it. Even if you don't want to talk about the game, talk to someone about your own interests.It's going to be okay, but you just have to reach out sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so lovely, I didn't expect it to make me cry so much.I see a lot of comparisons to Undertale and Earthbound, but I think outside of a few stylistic choices, it's an unfair comparison, and I think makes people expect something different than what it is. This game is it's own, and has so much life and love put into it in its own unique way.Siffrin has to repeat the same 2 days over and over, being the only one in their party that can remember past loops. The way the game changes dialogue is really intriguing, and the way that you slowly unravel what is going on is both challenging but intuitive. I think there was only one time I get stumped, but felt really proud of myself when I finally did figure it out.I think the best thing about the game is the characters and their interactions. You can tell how much they all love each other right off the bat, and it makes you feel like it really is worth going through the same day over and over again, just to keep them safe and happy. I really enjoyed experiencing Siffrin's emotions relating to them and himself, and it just felt really real. Like I've been through the same struggles as Siffrin, and it was solved in less RPG-like fashion but relatively close.I will say that I saw some people made at how long the game is, but I think 20-30 hours is perfectly reasonable. That's not even a very long game all things considered. I think it fits the tone of the game as well. It's fine to have to put a little bit of elbow grease into a game. We've all played games where we've had to grind, and the enemies aren't particularly difficult, and it's fun when you begin learning new moves. I think if you don't want to play a game that's very long, you can play the prologue. It won't be exactly the same but I think if you play that and do then feel like you can dedicate yourself to a longer game, then you can circle back to this one.TL;DR If you want a story rich game with cute characters and a very compelling protagonist, I highly recommend this one! Especially if you want something that you can dedicate yourself to for like, a week or two.

It gets some short scary moments done amazingly well, it has extra cute moments, and despite the soul crushing levels of inevitability it has just the nicest layer of hope along the way despite the odds. Things are going to hurt, and trying to get that perfect "everyone is happy" ending is going to involve you making some sacrifices to get there. But don't worry, cuz you can just loop it all over and nobody will be hurt!Right?Gameplay-wise, it's a fun and simple ATB with the most basic of 3-type charting: Rock, Paper, Scissors. If you know the game, you know the weakness chart! The jackpot system is very satisfying to get when you learn how to manage your turns, landing that fifth same-type attack to get your full team attack bonus and snag that full party heal/restore can help turn a tide if you find yourself in a tough fight.Overall, even before beating the game myself, I still highly recommend playing this, if not even just the demo to try it! I also suggest playing START AGAIN as a sort of precursor, it's not *required* but it gives you that extra emotional punch to the face to finish the prologue and then play ISAT (If you know, you know).

_childDocuments_.review: Conceptually, In Stars and Time is a very unique game. Its characters are engaging and likeable, its art is beautiful and detailed, and its "Rock Paper Scissors" style gameplay is highly entertaining. The story is, at its best, fascinating, and leaves the player wanting to discover more of the secrets about the characters and the world they inhabit, which the game does a good job of building through subtle dialogue exchanges. The game takes about 30 hours to beat.The game, however, suffers from repetition, and its story choices can often be questionable. I understand that this game is about a time loop and repetition is to be expected, but some aspects of the repetition led me to feel very exhausted and frustrated - especially at times when the game expects you to complete all floors of the game multiple times without looping forwards or backwards. The ending and certain reveals especially felt incredibly rushed, as if they were placed there for the sake of plot convenience. There were several times when I felt that more could have been done with the concepts proposed within the story. Many aspects are left ambiguous, and it can feel directionless.Overall, I would recommend this game for people who enjoy indie RPGs such as Omori and Undertale.

_childDocuments_.review: What isn't to love about this game? ISAT boasts a stellar narrative that kept me engrossed for its entire run time, a parody of generic rpg battle system that is so simple it loops back around to being oddly deep, and a quality of life so great that you're able to teleport straight to the final boss to ask him a single question before dipping and doing some other random side quest. The only true gripe I have with this game is that the loot is often just disappointing. Most of the memories simply aren't worth equipping to characters since that means sacrificing a straight plus 5, or even plus *30* stat buff across the board. The equipment itself also seems to barely change anything in combat, so I found myself never taking advantage of it all that much. Also jackpots are blatantly overpowered to the point that if combat isn't done in a round or two you're better off simply not using a character or relegating them to buffing duty (sorry Isabeau)However, the combat really isn't the main focus of the game whatsoever. Don't come in expecting this to be anywhere near the heights of xenoblade or final fantasy in that regard. The real star of the show is the expertly crafted story about trauma and the toll it takes on someone. In this domain it *easily* stands among the greats of the rpgs of old. Here it stands among the stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very much looking forward to this game ever since I saw its announcement on Twitter. Time manipulations is easily one of my favorite tropes and the excitement even drove me to play START AGAIN: a prologue. Instantly bought it on release and...I was not disappointed at all after completing my first playthrough!The music and the cartoonish, often exaggerated artstyle (Bonbon with their expression gets a shoutout especially) were really fun and lends well to the lighthearted feel of the game.  The gameplay was relatively straightforward, but allowed enough room for the player to experiment and outwit opponents thrown their way. But then there's the star of the  play: the story. Oh, where do I begin with this?The dialogue of the characters make them very lively and easily believable, like how a real person would simply talk, even with the jokes and, well, internet speak and exaggerations sprinkled in here and there. This makes you very attached to them. You want to know them, to help them realize their goals, to beat the King, so that they can go and live their life and fulfill their dreams! But, that's where the twist and the main draw of the game sets into play: the timeloops.Having put in a lot of thought into this trope, I was able to call a lot of what was going to happen in advance, but the sense of simultaneous dread and excitement as the threads, even the tiniest ones from interacting with the most random of objects, began to lead from one to another, weaving into the complete story. That was simply exemplary writing. In conclusion:You have crafted something truly incredible, and frankly, life changing. I truly appreciate being able to play this, having this added into my collage that is my own life experiences, to be treasured among other experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I initially pirated this game. I didn't have the money to buy it at the time and really wanted to play it, so I managed to play it through means of questionable morality, but that's besides the point - I loved the game so much I just had to buy it.Before playing ISaT, my favorite game ever was another similar game named OneShot, I've always had a soft spot for pixelated story indie games like these, and I'm happy to say ISaT is the only game I've ever played that has managed to compete with OneShot to take that title.Everything about this game is nearly perfect, the characters are all so charming, the art and character design is crazy good - even with the artistic choice to keep the game entirely black and white - and the writing and the narrative is outstanding and absolutely captivating. Every minute detail about this game has so much soul and passion behind it, from the small changes in UI details and item/skill descriptions as you progress to every single line of dialogue.Every line Siffrin says is necessary, cutting any of them out just won't make the scene feel the same.My favorite part about the game absolutely has to be Siffrin's inner monologues, I related to the character on a personal level and seeing him describe things I've felt before made everything he said hit that much harder. The whole story, world and concept of the game itself is just fantastic overall and there's nothing I can say to describe the emotions this game caused me to feel.All I can say is that if you're into story games and like angst (there's LOTS of it), absolutely buy this game. It is a lifechanging experience that will permanently change your brain chemistry (I finished the game over 3 months ago, and to this day still go "Siffrin reference" in my head every time I see the word "Breathe".).10/10, would loop again.

_childDocuments_.review: similarly to the prologue, i just can't get around to feeling the same way as others about this game. people act as if this is a masterpiece. it's good, don't get me wrong, but it didn't reach the peaks i expected from people's reaction.i've experienced a lot of "time loop" media. off the top of my head, there's  but i know there's more. of the ones i know, this is pretty different in that it is not a willing action of the main character (i guess in 's case, it's half willing). , but here, siffrin kinda has no choice but to keep going back. it's a neat dynamic, more going with the classics like groundhog daygameplay is fine. it's neat going around getting new info and scenes from using info you gained in past loops in new ones, but i can't ignore that the fundamental gameplay is retreading the same ground over and over. each enemy becomes boring when you've fought them so many times. exploring is a chore when you just go through the same dungeon the whole game. is this intentional? 100%. something being intentional and having narrative merit doesn't detract from how annoying it can get though.the story as a whole is good. even just making small progress feels satisfying. i mainly take issue with the ending. i see a lot of people saying the end is amazing, but it felt underwhelming to me.character-wise, they're mostly pretty good, but some dialogue makes me cringe a lot. i could go into so many facets here, but in particular, everybody acts as if puns are the epitome of humour. the protagonist is constantly spouting them and they're literally never funny. puns on their own do not make humour. being able to see a tree and say "tree-mendous" doesn't make you a comedian. on another note, i quite like the game's villain. clearly evil, but his actions have consistent logic to them even if he's obviously in the wrong. he's gone from a pretty generic fantasy villain like in the prologue (due to lack of info, not due to writing, obviously) to a cool dude that this game is also insanely wordy. so much could be told either visually or far more concisely. i genuinely started button mashing in some scenes because it would never end. this is especially bad when i was doing it during quite literally the final scene. it just wouldn't end. every character needs to go into a super lengthy monologue about how they feel. it got really annoying.anyways, overall i liked this game. it just had lots of problems that i can't ignore. this game had the potential for greatness, but i can't help but feel it squandered it.BTW for those of y'all who beat the game without reaching the secret boss, make sure you go back to act 3 or 4, investigate your coin until a cutscene occurs, then investigate it in front of loop. if you get an achievement, you've reached the conditions, and go back to the wish tree during act 6 (before talking to the head priestess). it reveals quite a bit, even showing (implied spoilers)

_childDocuments_.review: A time loop rpg where you have to re-live the same battles, maps, dialogue, and story over and over in a desperate attempt to break the loop?Time loops are a great narrative, but in a context like this, a developer treads a very dangerous line. You can only put so much of the repetition on a player's lap before it becomes too boring to play. But water it down too much and the player might not feel the emotion.Before I knew about this game, if you had told me what it was attempting to do, I'd say the developer must be out of their damn mind.But ISaT pulls it off. My god, does it pull it off.It's engaging, funny, upsetting, and all around greatly executed. The character interactions are the best I've seen in any game. Period. The game knows how to tug at your emotions, and will play with them like a marionette. It's a smart game, too. It knows whenever you know things you shouldn't. It knows when to call out the inherent troubles of a time loop, and it will play with those inconsistencies. Subtle changes are made for subtle things, and they really add up, and breathe colorful life into this greyscale world.At worst, it does some mildly inconvenient things, but I can see the philosophy behind the inconveniences and I respect it.Music is killer, characters are killer, story is killer, and this game truly oozes personality. What else is there really to add? If you like EB likes, you'll absolutely love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: If "woke" games make you cringe, skip this one.For everyone else who doesn't think having gay or trans people in a videogame is some kind of sin against God, In Stars and Time is a charming indie title that uses RPG tropes and mechanics, and player-driven curiosity to tell a complex and extremely compelling character driven story. RPG battles, levels and equipment are less about challenging the player strategically (tho that aspect does exist a little bit) and more used as tools to subtly enhance the themes of the story by tying them to mechanics.This is a full-length 40 hour game made by a tiny studio, and while it is intentionally repetitive you will always feel like you're moving forward and making progress. You'll want to check the same items, objects, and locations, talk to the same people over and over to see what changes with each new time loop - and a lot of the time that curiosity will be rewarded. Music is retro inspired, catchy, and has a lot of nuanced variations to fit different emotional tones and situations. The artwork is abundant and stylish, if simple. It conveys a lot of emotion, which I think is key for a game like this. But most of all, the writing is exceptional. This game will probably make you cry. 10 Gallons of Tears out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry over and over and over and over again everything about it is perfect and wonderful, the pacing is amazing, the world and characters are gripping, and the story is so beautifully put together! Its wormed its way to one of my all time favorite games I have ever played!!I wasn't sure if I'd even like the game (the lack of color threw me off at first, ill admit), but honestly now I think having it in black and white was one of the best choices for this game. It's such a compelling story, full of life and emotion, that I even forgot it didn't have color after just five minutes into it!Another thing is that I was worried the time loop setting would make the things too repetitive and boring (I have a hard time with things holding my attention)--but when I say it was almost the opposite I'm not lying! There's a lot that does stay the same, but there are so many tiny details that change and shift depending on your actions and choices and it's so captivating seeing all these wonderful pieces and characters develop and come to life! Game-play wise, there was an excellent balance with being able to skip certain scenes/dialogue while still allowing you to catch new pieces of information. The fighting mechanic is simple and charming, and you after a while you only really need to fight the bosses, so the regular enemies don't end up being a bother. At the end of the day it IS a time looping story, and so eventually, even the parts of the story that had me crying from emotion got smoothed out over the course of playing through the story. They don't loose their shine at all, but act more as a device that certainly enhances the connection you feel with the main character as they too, are going through these same moments over and over with you. Even though the game will remind you that doing everything, every single loop, isn't necessary--I still spent the majority of my time doing it all anyways just because the world and characters and story are all so interesting, i didn't want to miss even the smallest detail! [And I still missed stuff!! Even though I was so meticulous! so I'm forever awed that a time looping game was re-playable on top of everything else it already has going for it!]I'm blown away by how well done this game is, how everything works so perfectly together for this story to come to life with the emotional impact that is has! This is the type of game that will stay with you for the rest of your life, in the best ways. I'm already looking forward to replaying it again and again and again and again and again and again and again and--If you're debating getting the soundtrack with it I highly recommend doing so! I second guessed myself and now have to buy it separately t.t ps. LGBTQA+ family, this game sees you. And it loves you.

_childDocuments_.review: This may be one of the finest time loop games I have ever played- Many a game that follows this uses the idea of a time loop as a simple way to get information from the end of the game to apply at the beginning of a game, and generally treats it as a useful tool. This game goes much deeper into the psychology and character involved in the growth and change of a character stuck in a world where nothing else changes. Every character is deeply and intentionally created and full of story, and the entire aesthetic is fantasticMy main point against the game would be that it drags in the middle, but there is clear intent in that- every game design choice is built to further communicate the themes of being stuck in a small sequence of time, and to show how much things can change whilst staying the same are fantastic. Deeply recommended, one of the finest stories I have ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot sing enough praise for this game. In Stars and Time is a phenomenal experience that you simply must play. I love every single detail in this game: The way the story unfolds between loops is beautiful, the characters are complex and interesting, and it has some solid jokes to keep you from bawling your eyes out along the way. The developers seriously undersell themselves with that $20 price tag. I see a lot of people complaining that it can be repetitive, but that is LITERALLY THE POINT. It also really didn't bother me! Digging through the walls of text to find new information and pieces of a very complex story line is satisfying and worth the work for the end result. They actually managed to make a game that you play over and over and over again not boring! This is one of those games that I wish I could forget just to experience all over again. If your a fan of dark stories or just interested in diving into a world of puzzles and unanswered questions, BUYTHISGAME
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: Legit one of my favorite games I've ever played, and I'm not even done! Ignore how many hours I've put in because a lot that, admittedly, was leaving the game open while I did other things. BUT it feels worth playing for that long, clever dialogue, emotional, it's a journey I wish I could experience blindly all over again!
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only in act 3 of 6, but already I've fallen in love with this game- hell I fell in love with the prologue when IT first came out! The characters, the world-building, the mechanics- all of it! The characters are all so incredibly charming, whether friend, foe, or no-named side-character, interacting with them all is always ALWAYS a delight. The world-building! Good grief, the world-building- every little insignificant detail is just... genuinely amazing, I love it beyond what words can describe. They don't have to be there but they are and it just fleshes the world out so incredibly much, and it really makes the game and it's world feel so loved and cared for. And the mechanics! They're so user friendly and make good on the quality of life aspect that some games often get wrong, or just completely miss. ESPECIALLY with the genre of the loop type, it's in-game mechanics have to be done SOO particularly in regards to how it all works or else it'll feel awkward and out of place. But In Stars and Time does it exceptionally well!I play this game for hours at a time, and though I'm about what I think is halfway through, have probably way more hours in it than needed because I just have no issue looking at every little thing more than once. In other words- It feels like no time passes at all when I'm running around and doing every possible thing, it's always so fun and engaging. I spend time not playing just to theorize, think about what I should do next, try to make connections and puzzle things out- it's infesting my brain and I'm not complaining!All in all, I think it's a wonderful time. HOWEVER! It does take some patience to get through, especially if you want to find all the little things. Although that has not stopped me from enjoying it, I can see how others might find this to be a deterrent. But if you don't much care for that then BUY IT, PLAY IT! It's rad as hell!
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: CRAB this game is so amazing. I suck at writing reviews but here we go- all the art is top notch. I love every single one of the main party's expressions they are all such goobers (and when the game gets serious, every portrait feels so visceral and real to coincide with that)- the writing kicks ass. it kicks so much ass. All the witty banter is written in a very unique way that you don't see too often that really sells the tone and delivery despite just having boop-boop blips for text. I love the way punctuation is used to both add emphasis to exactly how a character is saying something, and to demonstrate pain and strife by removing said punctuation. Siffrin is an endlessly relatable character throughout the whole story, and the game puts you right alongside him in his journey.- The music is nice! I especially love the ones used in both [SPOILER. play the game] and the final boss (although every time I listen to the final boss music I want to cry. Mostly because of how it complemented the story so well lmao)- This game does have a bit of backtracking, though it never feels too intrusive as going through the House never takes too long. Even in its most frustrating moments, though, the frustration of backtracking adds to the story as well. I won't explain why. Play the game already.It's not too long, only being around 20 hours to experience the game beginning to end, but there are a NUMBER of secrets and little goodies to find if you know where to look. For the first time, maybe due to the relative obscurity of this game as of now (PLEASE let this game take off PLEAASE), I found myself actively looking for and discovering secrets BLIND! And that's a WONDERFUL feeling to have, especially nowadays where that feeling is comparatively, extremely rare! WOW!anyway yeah idk where this was going but buy the game BUY THE GAME BUY THE GAME PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE

_childDocuments_.review: This game does so many different things really well. The bit-music elements of the soundtrack are spot in. The story starts off with a strong hook, followed by a heroic story with silly moments. The visuals are amazing and on-point to the nostalgia elements. And exploring/interacting with the town is very intuitive and full of little secrets. I will say I was not a huge fan of the turn-based element. Even though the game is trying to be lighthearted adventure, the mechanic took it a bit too far (in my opinion). However, that's my only minor complain. Everything else is spot on. So I do recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is EXCELLENT. Take the trigger warnings seriously because this game absolutely deals with heavy themes. And because of that, I genuinely expected the game to have a different ending. A bad ending. All I wanted was for Siffrin to be able to rest. I love this game so much. _childDocuments_.review: This might honestly be without a doubt the most gut wrenchingly emotional game I have ever played in my life.  Seriously there's so many sections where I don't feel like I'm even playing a game anymore, I very rarely get to the point where I can't even talk or make a joke about a scene in a game but for the latter half of this whole game all I could do was watch and feel bad, but in a good way.Don't look anything up, just play the game, it's how I experienced it and I wouldn't want it any other way, try the demo if you like first but the progress doesn't carry over and you'll have to repeat the first part of the game, there's also a prologue called "Start again" if you would like to try it first and *some* things are referenced in this but it's not super important, I personally played it after.
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: Word's cannot even come CLOSE to explaining the effects that this game has had on me and my friend group as a whole. This is a game that I both adore, and do not think I would ever manage to play again. I have grown too attached to these characters and the world they inhabit to put them through it again. But the Journey this game took me on? I will never forget it. I've never had a game cause me so much emotional turmoil and delight at the same time while watching how everything unfolds, fitting pieces together and chasing leads. In Stars and Time is one part puzzle box, one part virtual novel and one part emotional roller coaster and EVERYONE will be sobbing at the end of it.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: In Stars And Time is an incredibly well-written game that had me crying more than several times with the characters, in both good moments and bad. There's a lot of well-thought out design from the way that you loop, the ability to "zone out" during repeated conversations, and even in just the way that different portions of text are broken up and delivered to the screen to maximize the impact and feeling of what's being said. The worldbuilding had me captivated with the way that the cast describes and lends their personal perspective on their respective cultures, and I'll be thinking about certain mysteries for ages to come. Really inspiring and motivating stuff that has me wanting to write and put out into the world in some way too.Just, idk, I'm not great at this review thing, the game is so good all-around. The art is fantastic, cast is diverse with some of the BEST LGBTQIA+ representation, the music highlights each moment so well and even through many many time loops, I never got tired of hearing it. There were a couple points where my memory didn't hold up for finding info in the game, so I relied on a guide, but the game DOES have tools to help you and I probably didn't utilize them well enough, haha.Anyways, highly recommend! Please play this!

_childDocuments_.review: making an actual review for anniversary! merry christmasif you like games like undertale or omori, there's a good chance you'll like this game. yes, the gameplay is repetitive, but that's a point. the narrative revolves around a timeloop, and the value of the game mostly comes FROM that narrative. so! if you want a good, emotional narrative and don't mind the content warnings that come with it (like the several mental health issues siffrin should REALLY get checked for) or the repetitive gameplay loop, play it! the characters are super well written and relatable.i don't personally mind the gameplay loop, for the record. this is one of those times where i like repetition, for the most part. there's so many little details and secrets to look around for (even on repeat playthroughs, in my case, though it might not be the same for you) that it kind of balances it out for me!also you'll probably gain at least +1 kin or similar upon game completion. sorry. that's the rules

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a masterpiece. i haven't had such a unique, invigorating experience with a video game since 2015 when undertale released, the game that ignited my love for gaming. the past few years i've had a bad habit of letting unplayed games sit on my computer or my console and collect dust, but this is the absolute gem that made me truly love video games again. if you are looking for a refreshing, unforgettable experience, look no further.in stars and time is beautifully tragic; one of those games that is truly gut-wrenching. and at the same time, it is full of little moments of hope and joy. for me personally, the most enjoyable aspect of this game was witnessing the story unfold through your actions and how generously you are rewarded for your curiosity (or punished, but still worth it nonetheless). getting to know the characters on a deep level and watching everything fall into place is incredibly satisfying and moving. the characters are quirky, lovable, and relatable, and getting to understand them all individually (as well as yourself) is so rewarding. there are several moments where i was brought to tears or had to take a moment to lie down to process what was happening in the game. there are hardly any emotions i didn't experience while playing this game. The mind-boggling story topped with the soundtrack and the unique gameplay makes for an experience i wish i could relive again, and again, and again, and again.
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to start. I wanted to make a joke but I can't, this game is too good for that. The gameplay isn't too difficult, and personally I love that because I can focus on the plot. Every character has layers and layers to themselves and finding more about them is exciting, and oh my dear Sif, I love them with all my being, Siffrin is a character so easy to relate, not to the point of "OH! HE'S JUST LIKE ME FOR REAL!!" (at least not for me), but like... I'm going through everything with you, I understand your pain because I'm looping with you, I wish I could tell you that you are a wonderful person, that you're stronger than you think, that your friends love you, that I love you, Siffrin. The ending warmed my heart, and I can feel this story being a part of me now. From the first second, I just wanted to play more, to know more, to see where the story was going. In these hard times in my life, this game feels like a blessing. You can break the loop, everything will be better, don't be afraid to talk if you need to, someone will always listen, someone will always be there to help if you let them... Someone will always love you.SPOILERS:

_childDocuments_.review: Saying this game is good is an understatement. This game was a masterpiece. _childDocuments_.review: Oh this game is so good. Writing better than maybe any game I've played. Sometimes silly and goofy, sometimes scours your emotional landscape and leaves you a wreck (positive). Has necessary quality of life features for time loop game. Art so pretty. Combat as complicated as it needs to be for the flow of the game, which is to say, relatively simple but not boring. Banging soundtrack. Only problem is that I don't have a group of friends to voice act all the dialogue with. I promise you, if you think you'll enjoy this game, you almost certainly will, because it brings so much to the table. So many games could learn from In Stars and Time, and I hope this game gets the recognition it deserves!

_childDocuments_.review: In Stars and Time is the best narrative game ever methinks, and has become my personal favourite game.For sure the best queer/neurodivergent representation I've ever experienced in any form of media. The characters think like me, have the same sense of humour, the same predictions and ideas, and an incredible depth of character without ever feeling boring. If you like 'found family' dynamics then stop reading and just play the game, you'll love it no matter what.This is half narrative and half turn-based RPG, and requires a base level of understanding of typical RPG mechanics. If you've played any game like this before then you'll be totally fine but I can probably see people who have never played video games before having issues. But like, that's only cause I wanna show this to everyone on the earth. The game never gets too difficult really, despite having a fun, strategic combat system, so it's suitable for inexperienced people for sure. I would recommend against grinding, it doesn't matter too much past early runs as you get into the rhythm of the combat system, which is incredibly fun in itself. If you're just exploring the house of change for clues and dialogue, feel free to use the esc key in battle and flee. It's guaranteed to work and has no negative consequences, it will make the mid-game much more immersive.Speaking of, the quality of life in this game is seriously good. Like amazing stupendous brilliant good. Embrace this and don't fall into the trap of rejecting help when offered, there's usually an easy way to do things, in a way that won't spoil secrets or take away cool options. Sometimes you need assistance to progress.There are amazing twists, lore-drops, and foreshadowing moments, so I will try to not spoil things even though I almost certainly have already. However, what I will say is that the  is terrifyingly and disturbingly relatable. The issues discussed are more hmm realistic(?) than similar titles like undertale or omori, but the content is much less explicit, so far fewer trigger warnings necessary, just watch yourself and  towards the end of the game. It's more emotionally harrowing than psychological horror or anything, but boy does it feel like it at times. I found the whole experience actually very therapeutic, however many times I did have to stop, save, and step away from the game for a few hours or even a whole week. I would recommend experiencing the uncomfortable periods of this game, rather than looking away and mashing the spacebar, even if you have to take a break and take some deep breaths and have some snacks. I got very invested into the story and that made it so much more impactful. Have tissues on hand and be prepared to retroactively analyse your own life.Anyway, In Stars and Time is the best game I have played, one of the best uses of the media for storytelling, and I really really really recommend it. I've never left a review for anything else, but if anything I can say will make you play this game then it is worth talking about. While I wait for this to become mega-popular, I will sit back and enjoy some refreshing, juicy pineapple slices. What do you mean they're not meant to be spicy wait wait wa-

_childDocuments_.review: the vibes are impeccable; the art is well executed and bursting with charm; the characters are written well, with distinct voices and personalities, with backstory and information about them dispensed at a pace that feels natural and not infodump-y. humor and light-hearted moments are balanced against the heavier parts of the story so that you don't get burned out on either. the combat is complex enough to not get boring even with how many times you loop through, but not so byzantine i bounced off of it, and the learning curve is very reasonable. i don't have many complaints, honestly, and the ones i have are purely personal preference - i think the devs made overall very good choices with how they made this game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: With amazingly witty writing, beautiful and striking art, fun RPG mechanics, and SNACKS?!?!  What more could you ask for!?This game was an absolute treat, from the most small conversation differences to the bitter sweet message.  The game is not perfect, as the looping system can end up becoming a bit repetitive and tedious especially toward the later half of the game, but I feel as if the repetitive nature of the looping lends itself well to the story it is trying to convey to an extent.If you, like myself, are a person who clicks on every piece of furniture in an RPG looking for fun dialogue or secret doohickeys, then this is the game for you.  8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game, attempting to put it into words, it's making me feel a bit taciturn.The characters feel like actual people, they act their age, their dialogue flows with each other so nicely, they joke until they can't, flare up, wallow in their feelings, have an unspoken bond between them.There were moments of silence, moments of explosions, moments of memories and fishing, and moments where you just had to be there to see it.At times, it felt like my mouth hurt from smiling to much, but other times it felt like burnt sugar at the back of my tongue, a tug on my stomach.It felt like seconds stretched forever, beyond the horizon, yet minutes or hours just flew by, ever fleeting.I could try to say more, but I'm not good with words, and I feel like wishing for any more would just make me go all loopy.Although I'm still riding that finale high, I'd like to say this is one of my favourite games of all time. I hope I will remember this game for years to come. I can only try to promise that I remember.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through this game, I have to leave a review, one just to express my thoughts on the game and two just to let anyone considering buying this game, to in fact buy it. First, I want to talk about the soundtrack. It is so UNBELIEVABLY good. Whenever I was walking through the different environments the game had to offer, I was always so drawn in by the music, no matter how many times I heard it. I honestly listen to the soundtrack on a daily basis now, I enjoy listening to it that much. If you care about good soundtracks in a game, you will absolutely enjoy the soundtracks this game plays during important moments and simply when roaming around.Next, I want to talk about the characters. At first, I didn't think I would grow to like the characters as much but after not even an hour of playing, I adored every character and wanted to get every piece of dialogue from them all that I could as almost every piece made you feel something, whether it be humour, joy, sadness, pity.. The game managed to perfectly convey its feelings and make the player feel what was necessary for the moment. This was done especially well in the last few chapters of the game, you really bonded and understood the characters by then, wanting nothing bad to happen to any of them and the story that unfolded during those chapters whilst feeling such emotions was extraordinarily well done, the characters felt real and everything was just done so perfectly. If you're a fan of games like OMORI or UNDERTALE, this is absolutely a must-play for you, and, even if you're not a fan of those games, this game is still worth checking out, the story is so unbelievably good and everything about the game is just really well done. This was a 10/10 game for me, the only bad thing is not having the ability to forget about it so I can experience it for the first time all over again. Phenomenal game, I would absolutely recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a tough recommend because while In Stars And Time is a extremely well-realized execution of its concept and philosophies, it mainly expresses this via 10 hours of making you chafe against every minor annoyance of its genre on purpose dozens of times in an effort to gradually drive you insane.It is in the Pathologic or Drakengard world of things where it is exceptionally good at putting you in the frame of mind of the character you're controlling, but the feeling it intends to inflict on you are mostly negative. I sometimes feel like this is a bit...too easy? As a piece of game design? Making a JRPG that's just ever so slightly too slow to be truly brisk and therefore a little annoying? It threads this needle pretty well but also it's not exactly something I haven't seen before, just most games don't do it on purpose? It's all in service of the broader themes, but I'm a little mixed on how clever I actually think it is.To move back to a positive, the writing is funny, sharp and the characters are likeable and charming, you'll spend your first five or so hours gradually growing to like your crew of the stupidest group to ever be an RPG party. You will then spend the remaining gameplay time growing to hate everything and everyone around you as you are made to notice every minor annoyance ad infinitum. Buff animations at the start of combat firing off one a time for every single combat, enemies in hallways that are just kind of too narrow to reliably avoid. It all gets in the way, it's all wasting your time, you've seen this before. Who cares, go away.This is the point, but it is a point that will divide people. Adding to this for me was some points of probably unintentional frustration where progression was gated by kind of silly adventure game-y nonsense like the lead just refusing to comment on something until something in the proper sequence had fired off did eventually have me just resorting to a spoiler-free walkthrough because my patience kind of hit a limit.A complicated game that leaves you with complex feelings. I think it's emotionally sincere writing, likeable characters and very textured and vividly expressed depiction of the lead's mental state wins out over the fact that it is, by design, sometimes just absolutely no fun at all. As a work of art, a resounding success, I can't say its vision doesn't come through in the slightest, it perfectly expresses itself. As a game that I want to enthusiastically recommend? That's....complicated. Fun to think about though.
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so normal about this game that immediately after beating it, I gifted it to five of my friends.I'm a big fan of making myself a little miserable for fun so when I heard about a time loop game where you can start the loops from the very beginning, I knew I was in for a treat. I wasn't expecting the characters to be so charming and I certainly wasn't expecting the game to call me out on my bad mental health! It felt like looking at a horrible, horrible mirror. So the game definitely inspired me to take my mental health more serious hahaIf you like a little time loop grinding, love wacky characters, and love a playable character with tons of mental health, you're gonna love this game
_childDocuments_.name: In Stars And Time

_childDocuments_.review: After mulling it over for a while, if I could give a neutral review I would.Spoilers below, reader beware.Most of the game is great, but the last two acts feel like the story ran out of time, which is ironic for a time loop. Sif abruptly looses all patience and the story just says "ah well we didnt get to that" to the built up question of the existentially redacted country, which *might* be something illuminated if I finished 100%ing the game, but having it just suddenly get dropped in a normal play-through killed all interest I had in fully completing the game, or even watching a video of someone else doing it.Honestly, my complaints might evaporate if the game ever gets a sequel, either direct or otherwise, but for now I feel genuinely frustrated that I not only didn't get an answer to the question, but it felt as though the question was simply forgotten along the way.
