_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played.I've enjoyed point and clicks before, but despite how easy it is to get immersed in them at first, they often get too difficult and therefore boring for me. Right away, this game offered a feature to highlight the important objects so I wouldn't have to pixel hunt, immediately making it more accessible for me. Sure, there are some things that might have been cool to find on my own, but the game really is difficult enough as it is if you take it seriously.And this game wants you to take it seriously.Everything is significant in the most charming of ways. If you're ever stuck, the answer is always to look a little closer (something that just feels painful and redundant in similar titles), and the game is built on that. The simple structure of every level is that if you understand the scene, you can solve it. Even the hint system reflects this, as it requires essentially a flash-card drill to access each hint. This is because in of itself, being more familiar with the objects and characters at play will help you succeed! Also, it keeps the player from cheating themself out of the full experience by digging for hints before putting in the effort of observing the whole scene.On top of excellent mechanics, I love the artfully creepy graphics and the (albeit dark) sense of humor the game has. It has familiar elements and yet feels like an entirely new presentation from any story like this one that I know.As for shortcomings: I do wish it was longer. Once I started to really understand how the game works, I blazed through it and it was over. I just bought the DLC and I hope the quality matches the base game.It would also be nice if I had more control over the music, or if it changed a little more often. The game features many great looping tracks, but a few got old for me.If you can buy this game on sale, it's a steal. If you buy it full price, I believe it's still worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely entertaining and engaging mystery detective puzzle game that involves the player deducing what happened in a certain scene depending on various contextual clues provided within said scene. The prior description may give the game a simple impression, but the execution and brilliance of the developer team turned into what may have been a dull puzzle game to play on the side into an experience unlike any other. If you enjoy doing detective work and juggling your brain around, I think you'll enjoy the game; I certainly have.Also, a quick note: if you're going to play this game, play it in the classic mode (non-Redux). I initially was under the impression that since the Redux version is the newer one, it would provide the player with a better experience. To my misfortune, the main reason Redux was created was to modify the UI to be more suitable for small screen devices like the Nintendo Switch and Steam Deck. Consequentially, this reduces the usability of the UI (or rather makes it very inconvenient) on more conventional and larger screens players may use on desktop setups. This game is also quite fun to play with friends. While lacking in traditional co-op features and functionality, solving the stages with my buddies was a highly enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: 4.65 ☆One of the best detective games, for sure, really makes you think and figure out stuff on your own. The overarching story was also really well done, how all the cases/story connects, and you figure out some stuff on the "meta" level, not when playing any particular case but by using information from multiple ones, plus I enjoy the creepiness of the story.The art is very stylish, 2D lightly mixed with 3D and kinda "ugly" and different in a very pretty way.The DLCs are good too, though sometimes the solution is a bit convoluted.It is a good game to play by yourself or with a friend, as I did, which does make it easier, but it's cool to discuss theories and solutions, even if only one friend controls the mouse. And even with someone else I still found the difficulty good, hard enough to be very satisfying to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and unique art style, great music, and an engaging story that unfolds through very creative game play. At first I was unsure of this unfamiliar style of puzzle solving as seen in the screen shots and trailer but thank goodness for the demo! After playing through it I knew I needed the whole game and the DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent excellent little detective game that constructs incredibly open puzzles with the smart vocabulary-based gameplay loop. In many ways, it's giving me the same excitement as Obra Dinn in the deduction process and the open-ended nature of the puzzles, and at the same time serving up an exciting and gripping narrative throughout a dozen seemingly disconnected murder cases. In late game it's just a straight up dopamine ride with non-stop a-ha moments.The only nitpick I have is on the puzzles: despite the high degree of freedom the puzzles give you, it doesn't really acknowledge "wrong" answers to the deduction questions, taking away a little bit fun from making unhinged yet still reasonable wrong narratives a la Heaven's Vault and Obra Dinn.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable detective game, with a lot of similarities with Return of the Obra Dinn. The story is compelling to follow, but the interplay between cases could have been developped a lot deeper. In the end the game is a bit short and most cases are quite easy, a harder challenge would have been welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem if you liked The return of the Obra Dinn.  Not to easy, Not to hard, but really satisfying resolution vibe. This game, in addition to have an interesting underlying study is really easy to handle to focus on murder resolution. I just finished it and I AM JEALOUS of you who are about to start it !
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best detective game I have ever played. The story is simple but intricate and told in a really fun patch-work kinda way that you can piece together and figure out all by yourself. There are even a lot of story details that are unnecessary to complete the game but can further enhance the plot. I highly encourage not using any hints because this game is not very solvable if you just revisit each clue multiple times (you can also use process of elimination if you're few prompts short). My favorite part of the game is a spolier so read further below if you don't care.......I was hard stuck on the last chapter, I finished all the prompts except the one for lazarus visiting the manor because I couldn't for the life of me figure out his motivation for coming here. That was until I re-read keen's letter about laz's past, and I got to thinking about his origins, at first I went back to look at the criminals from a previous chapter and none fit the bill. So, I started thinking what if someone used the idol to make themselves younger? So I went back to look at each character and their past, one character that disappeared from the story suddenly and was never mentioned again until the very end was edmund cloudsley, so after I finally figured out lazarus (ironic name) is a younger edmund, it made so much sense why he went to the manor and I solved the final case just like that!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game if you like puzzle solving and detective like games, you can see if you like the art style from the images (I personally like this kinda of art style) and the story is pretty simple, but well thought of. What really made the story good for me was the fact that they don't really tell you any of it. You have to figure everything out basically! Not too hard if you're not that good at puzzles, but also not too easy if you're looking for a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Works perfectly on steam deck. The game is going to be compared a lot to Obra Dinn, and it's definitely a similar idea. But if Obra Dinn seemed a little overwhelming for you, having this broken down into distinct cases definitely makes it more digestible.The cases ramp up in complexity in a really good, satisfying way. The story, art, and music are all very good. Took me about five hours for full completion. Definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I liked a lot about this game. The investigation mechanics are satisfying, the environmental narrative is very interesting to unfold and the overarching plot is quite captivating. While not a massive fan of the art style it gives the game extra visual personality. A bit pricey, perhaps. Money well spent if you're into the genre, though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic relatively short puzzle game that tells an interesting story in a very unique way. Each individual puzzle leaves you overwhelmed with info but then as you put it all together the the whole system seamlessly reveals story elements in a very satisfying way. My favourite part is that many of the twists in the story are discovered through deductive reasoning rather than outwardly told.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but I wish I had my expectations tempered a bit. While similar to Obra Dinn, the puzzles just aren't on the same level; they range from way too straightforward to far too ambiguous. I didn't have too many of those satisfying "aha" moments when figuring things out.Still, it's a clever game with an interesting-enough story, so I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome investigation game. It has a lot in common with Return of the Obra-Dinn. It's however faster to play (as in more focused on investigating than moving around) and somewhat more guided. The story is compeling and got me surprised up to the very end, the art is weird in a good sense. It scratches an itch that is rarely scratched, I wish there was more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: While the comparisons to Obra Dinn are well-founded (investigating snapshots in time to solve a murder) this game is far more than a 2D imitation. This game's innovation is introducing unique rules and customs in each murder that you must learn to understand the case. They're like logic puzzles that unravel themselves as you draw connections between pieces of evidence, with new ideas presented with every chapter. An absolute joy to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking to scratch that Obra Dinn itch this is the closest you can get. It's broken up into chapters with an overarching story so it's great for if you like to play in short bursts. I can't say much more without spoiling anything so if a detective game is what you're looking for you can't do much better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: As most other reviews have mentioned, this game absolutely scratches the Obra Dinn itch and it's wonderful! That said, there are enough differences that this game stands far above and beyond its itch-scratching role: The story moves linearly by chapters so the growing narrative investment isn't only "what happened?," there's a great element of "what's going to happen?" Because of this, there's a great feeling of solving mysteries that aren't included in the drag and drop boxes. You begin to notice patterns, recognize faces, belongings, etc. & to note different plots unfolding. Seriously, the joy of realizing "Oh that's actually _____" is so well done and feels so organic.The best way I could summarize this game is that it's an S-tier point-and-click where the point-and-click objects and combinations are words instead of objects. Instead of creating some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ balloon-pin combo (looking at you, Grim Fandango), you uncover a narrative.I can only hope these two games offer a metric to define a new genre & we'll find ourselves with many more similar games soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Intuitive puzzler with a lot of "Aha!" moments and being thrilled by picking up a key clue - kind of like a series of mini escape rooms where you have to piece together what has happened. Like others have mentioned, you often begin being fairly overwhelmed by all the names and characters, but the game is very good at sorting your clues for you and subtly helping you along without holding your hand. Also thankful the game doesn't do a lot to "trick" you with names that are similar, tons of red herrings and so on - while some clues are of course misleading, they are well-integrated into the small narratives. I will say that the price point of 18 euro is fairly high - each case is unlikely to take more than 20-40 minutes depending on reading speed and how much you get stuck, with the later cases being harder than the earlier cases, so I assume most players will find between 4-8 hours of content here. Which is fine, but I would consider getting it on sale for the same reason.No regrets from me though - absolutely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What a great little game. Clever and thoughtful, with a puzzle structure that relies on observation and deduction. It reminded me a bit of RETURN OF THE OBRA DINN, which is one of my favourite games. Some of the later scenarios have a confusing sentence structure that makes it hard to grasp what the puzzle is asking for, but other than that, I loved the game, the setting that was developed, and the narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well made game. If you played Return of the Obra Dinn, you will absolutely loves this game. It has a similiar concept. In this game you have to solve 11 cases. They often revolve around somebody's death and you have to figure out the names of the people participating in the scene, what happened and sometimes some extra information.At first you will think "there is no way I can solve this" but in the end you will always have that AHA moment where it clicks together. The story is complex. There are a lot of names to remember but after several chapters, you will start to recognise some of the characters and some of the later chapters will allow you to quickly jump to previous chapter to review them. So you don't really have to worry about forgetting something. At first, the individual cases may seem disconnected, but there are couple of plot twist that change your perspection.When you finish the game and revisit those earlier chapters, you will see all the clues that were carefully placed there that back then meant nothing, but now show the whole story. And that's perfect storytelling.10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Overall decent.  Great puzzles, storyline, interface, art, music.I was startled but ultimately liked that you're immediately dropped into playing the game, and then it slowly ramps up in complexity.I liked the way that details are implied without having to use exposition.  And the deduction puzzles step you through the logic of how events connect, further developing the story. (The finished level summaries felt a little obsolete to me, but were reassuring to neatly confirm after the fact)Really enjoyed the overarching story line and slow realisations.The word mechanic was hit and miss.  I tried a screen or two without indicators, but ultimately played the rest with indicators and it kind of just became a "collect 'em all" chore.  Once I realised you can move the stored words around it became easier to organise.  Mildly disappointed with a couple of redundancies in the logic puzzles, especially the DLCs.  Also spots where relevant names were in items but not underlined which was annoying.otherwise the interface was pretty decent.I didn't end up using any hints, but I did have to brute force a couple of word spots.art style great, nostalgic, although the constant jiggling animations were a little annoying at first.music setting the mood was great but sometimes discordant and grating on repeat.Very neat little game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great detective game with clever scenarios and an overarching narrative that keeps twisting and turning. The tone is wonderfully tongue-in-cheek, and the art, albeit low-res, works incredibly well. In most cases, I deduced my way up to near-solution, then applied some trial & error to carry me to the finish line. There are some moments that might frustrate the impatient player but take a step back and the solution will surely present itself. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Relatively short game. Novel premise, similar to Obra Dinn, I enjoyed Obra Dinn better but still had a good time with this game.Writing isn't great but there aren't any typos or anything like that so it's fine. Each scenario makes you think and slowly piece the scene together. If you like detective games, I highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Good attempt, but ultimately not clever. Like many similar games, it suffers from errors in framing its logic and deduction (sometimes what you are supposed to logically deduce is probably not what an intelligent person would logically deduce, or final solutions include steps of deduction that would be omitted/unnecessary). It's very hard for developers of this game to put themselves in the player's shoes, but I'm tired of half-attempts. If a game like this doesn't feel clever, it's a glorified drag and drop simulator. That's what I got out of this. I felt the gameplay was dragging words around, not figuring things out.Recommended only to fans of the genre who want to fund indie projects. For those who compare it to Obra Dinn and Outer Wilds: No, those games are clever and have excellent presentation. This isn't on the same level at all. Wary buyers heed this review well and buy those other games first if you haven't experienced them!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What to say, amazing game, it's like a sort of return to the obra dinn light. It was recommended by the developer of obra dinn no less.Some puzzles are really hard, some are too easy. I bought the game in sale so paid  15 euro for 10 hours of game time which could be less if you really really pay attention. I really recommend it, the attention to detail is awesome, some puzzles might have been made more difficult, but the story in itself was great fun. I d buy a sequel in a heartbeat. We need more games like this. But it is a lot of money for only 10 hours of gametime so be sure to buy int in a sale or when the price goes down.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Obra Dinn a lot, so when people said this was a similarly compelling mystery of course I dug in. It's not really your traditional murder mystery, you're deducing what happened from context clues - most of the time the "deaths" aren't even really the focus, I would even say this is more of an "archaeologist" game than a "detective" game.Short and sweet, and I really enjoyed the story being told. Go into it blind and you probably won't regret the time you spent playing this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a short narrative-detective kind of game. The gameplay is very similar to Return of the Obra Dinn (which I loved).You are shown a series of vignettes -- moments frozen in time. Your goals in each vignette are to identify the characters in the scene, and describe the events transpiring. Use observation and deduction to fill in the blanks to solve the puzzle. This mechanicis very fun and satisfying to solve!The Case of the Golden Idol has a delightful story, with twists, surprises, and humor along the way. It was refreshingly short, taking me only 7 hours to solve the whole story. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys engaging stories and detective gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is creative, smart and rewarding, everything I was looking for. What a way to tell a story!The only criticism I have towards this game is the sudden spike in difficulty. Scenes 1 and 2 are really easy, almost trivial, then scene 3 has a LOT going on. Also, scene 5 was the hardest one in the whole game for me. There's just too much information in that one! And it's odd that the hardest scene happens so early.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, look its not for everyone. HOWEVER I do think it is an excellent little puzzle game which streamlined the ideas in Obra Dinn to make them more generally accessible and easy to use as well as having a more interesting story. Both are good games but if I had a choice I'd probably say this one is better. Great purchase for anyone looking to enjoy some great background story telling and some really interesting puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of soul. I really enjoyed the investigative work you do in the game. You have to wear your detective hat here, but it never feels tedious or like busy work. Delving into the narrative while unraveling the ugly underbelly of its dark mysteries is incredibly rewarding, especially once you solve some of the trickier scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game and played it with my husband based on the overwhelmingly positive reviews. My initial impression before playing the game was that the art is hideous. The characters look awful and the settings lack essence. And that's not because of the 16-bit nature of the art style, plenty of games choose 16-bit art as their medium and still create rich characters and environments to help the player feel immersed in the game. The art makes it difficult to become emotionally invested in what goes on. The other reason why I didn't like it is because as a player, I don't have any involvement in the story. It doesn't matter if I figure things out, it holds no baring on the story. So I'm just an observer. And I felt the story itself wasn't really all that impressive or original, especially the anti-climactic ending. I'd probably only recommend buying this if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Did not make me feel smarter. But! Logical reasoning problems are at an appropriately challenging level, well arranged in a cohesive fashion, and even weaved with some humor. Very good for shot holidays. I don't want to make any enemies but this is more enjoyable than Aviary Attorney, honestly, because this achieves more with much less bells and whistles. And that is what a good game should do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fine, the game play is fine. Its very much like a light version of the Return of the Obra Dinn. There's some very poor musical choices, while there's a couple of great songs. However, the length of the game doesn't justify the $18 price. Took me five hours which is probably about average, and there's honestly no replayability to this game. I appreciate the artistic implementation(except for those really weird songs) and the story telling, but I don't think there's enough here for the price, I'd recommend picking it up for under $10( I know that's not what the dev/publisher want to hear).
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun to piece together all the details of the scene and figure out what might have happened. The puzzles are so well designed, largely self-contained but they reward you paying attention to how the events are unfolding. I also like how strongly it discourages you from accessing hints - I ended up solving the whole game without any which is just miles more satisfying than letting impatience get the better of you. Lots of comparisons to the Return of the Obra Dinn. I would say this game feels less difficult, but a lot of this is because it has slicker gameplay and is less frustrating from a UI point of view, so it's easier to switch between clues and make the links at the same speed your brain is whirring. Highly recommend for fans of escape rooms who are bored of the same old room escape format - this needs you to make connections in a similar way, but the puzzle mechanics are different enough ti feel fresh and new. I don't think I've enjoyed a puzzler this much since Chants of Sennaar and am super excited for the new golden idol game coming soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: + Fun caricature-esque visual style+ Nice music+ Runs smoothly (no glitches or slowdown, one random crash, no progress lost)+ Engaging gameplay and intriguing, open-ended puzzles+ Interesting story (if a bit anticlimactic in my opinion)- Very short. I'm no Poirot but still 100%'d this game in one evening.- The graphics are a bit misleading sometimes (no spoilers - Some characters appear in multiple scenes and their skin tones appear to change significantly, making ID'ing them much harder)- There are hundreds of clues in the game and every one can be spotted in plain sight, except for two that rely on timing a click on an object moving in the background. This isn't challenging at all, but obfuscating hints like this is a really weird design choice in a puzzle game and led to a lot of frustration for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, worth the spend. Gameplay was interesting and compelling enough that I was happy to see it all the way through and was satisfied it ended when it did. Can be a little easy at times, but there are enough generally compelling red herrings that get it through. Haven't played Obra Din, but this was great, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to play this game because I am a huge fan of Return of the Obra Dinn. After finishing it, I would say I was not disappointed. However, I want to point out that this game is shorter and its gameplay is less engaging than that of Return of the Obra Dinn. Though I'd say the deduction is more straightforward and nothing will really confuse and frustrate you as some of the deductions in Obra Dinn did **cough Chinese Topmen cough. The storytelling using the environments and details throughout the different chapters is superb. If you are fan of this genre, or somebody who's looking to scratch that Obra Dinn itch, I'd recommend getting it now at full price; I'd still recommend all other players to try this game when it's on sale. And please, for anyone that hasn't played the masterpieces that are Outer Wilds and Return of the Obra Dinn: please go play them without reading any review or spoilers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Solid fun with minimum fuss, distilling the detective game genre into the bare essentials, by having you examine scenes as they are happening instead of laboriously interviewing after the fact.Very reminiscent of Return of Obra Dinn, in a good way. If you liked that, you're probably going to like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game for a lazy Sunday. The artwork is unusual but suits the tone of the game. The score, which can verge on repetitive depending on how long you take to solve a case, is also pleasantly unusual.I'd love to see more games in the vein of this and Obra Dinn. 'Sherlockalikes' maybe?The only drawback was that Case 10 bugged out for me and now I can't complete the game unless I wipe my save and start from scratch, which sucks!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Loved taking the time to piece all the well-laid clues together, and took some pride in trying not using the hints system.  In contrast Return of the Obra Dinn (while still a quality title) was just a touch long and honestly very depressing, whereas this was similar in body count but the music and wavery pixel animations provide enough 'life' to make it more of an adventure.  Featuring backstory and lore that stretches over several (in-game) decades creates a sense of compulsion to continue gnawing these puzzles to the marrow.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches the Obra Dinn itch while feeling completely like its own game. It’s so unique, creative, and unsettling. Very fun for anyone who likes point-and-click games or puzzle games in general.Side note, I downloaded and played the demo for the sequel and I have no idea what happened but the devs switched up the UI and art style and I can’t for the life of me decide why they would do that. Sequel feels like a mobile game. It’s also a lot easier due to some UI changes. It kind of hurt to play because of how much I loved the original.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the Cloudsley family. They are part of the criminal underworld belonging to a secret society. Pure logic, this game operates on pure logic. Everything you need to solve the whodunit and why they did it in each of the eleven chapters is there, but you will need to have an eye for detail and need to persevere a bit.Each chapter builds on itself, gradually increasing in difficulty in:The number of items you obtain.The number of words that are highlighted.The number of people involved. You can look back in solved chapters to identify people if you need a reminder. If you don’t want to do that take pictures of the panels after you solve them.There are directions for gameplay in the game that include how to access a hint.The mouse wheel scrolls larger so you can zoom in.It does support controllers.You drag and drop the words, a right click removes them. You might need another instance of a name or item, just drag it from the panels you have it on. If you can't drag from one panel without it disappearing try another.If you prefer, you can toggle between the Thinking and Exploring panels by tapping the spacebar.I played with highlights turned on, as the game suggested. It will be a pixel hunt for some items if you do not.Click all red  or underlined wordsFocus on characters and how they fit in.Are they a friend or foe? Are they an employee?Identify all the people who are in the scenes with their first and last names. Pay attention to what is being said and what the characters look like in that moment. Are they afraid, in pain, bleeding?Sometimes the process of elimination worked well for me. If you have two or fewer errors the text will be yellow and the panel heading will say that as well.The game will try to trick you as you go along by adding evidence or characters that have no bearing on the current chapter.Thumbs up for me, good luck to you all!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game that provides the rare eureka moments that only a select few games are capable of. Most similar to games like Return of the Obra Dinn and Duck Detective mechanically, but also has some likeness to the narrative exploration of Outer Wilds. The way in which each subsequent case builds upon the previous gets you invested in the characters and gives some solid stepping stones into each new puzzle. The cases build in difficulty progressively, but mostly in a fair manner that grows alongside your skills and familiarity with the characters, motives, and mechanics. My only gripe is that the final case makes some pretty large leaps and references to past events which aren't entirely clear until same major plot points are revealed in the epilogue. Maybe I didn't pick up on some subtle hints from previous missions, but the difficulty spiked a lot in the final case. The base game and both DLC are well worth playing, and a new game "The Rise of the Golden Idol" will be coming later in the year.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I feel kinda mixed about the game overall.Gameplay-wise, this game is great. You look around a crime scene, gather a bunch of clues and keywords, then piece them together to reveal what happened. Although there is a little bit of guidance in the form of having to fill the blanks on a paper, the game mostly leaves you to figure things out. The puzzles feels logical and the clues are well-laid out with some very creative ones mixed in. On the gameplay front I don't really have anything to complain about.However, this game is a mystery game. Because of that I greatly value the writing, the story, and the feeling of mystery in the narrative. Unfortunately this is where the game kinda falls a bit flat for me.The characters are pretty flat and one dimensional. You're not a detective or anyone that can actually interact with the characters. So everyone is basically just a clue dispenser.The individual murders you're solving are not very interesting, narratively. Some light SPOILERS in this paragraph. Almost all the murders methods are completely mundane. He was shot, he was stabbed, he was poisoned. And almost all the motives are either: he was killed in an accident or he was killed because the cult ordered it. Not very interesting.And the overall narrative is not very impressive either. You can probably figure out the nature of the conspiracy pretty quickly because it's pretty shallow. And after you figure it out, there isn't any mystery anymore. You just watch the conspiracy play out exactly as you expect it would.Again, I'd like to reiterate that gameplay-wise, I had a great time. The puzzles are fun, I felt like I was genuinely putting it together myself. It's just that the mystery isn't very mysterious and the overall narrative is nothing noteworthy.Still recommend, but be aware the plot is not going to wow you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The gameplay is what you can see in the trailers. It's just inspecting crime scenes to collect names, verbs and nouns, and then arranging them to make sentences. It sounds simple, but what makes it great is how logical and accessible the puzzles are, while still offering a satisfying level of challenge. It's absolutely a must play for any fans of investigation games.My only complaint is how short it is. Discounting the amount of time I spent with the game idling while I had to do other things, it probably took me about 4h to beat it without hints. Still, as far as faults go, there not being more of it barely counts as one. I just hope that the devs can make more of it soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle-solving gameplay with an incredible narrative that manages to change up the formula each level. The DLCs are also equally amazing, expanding the world even more than the base game already did. The music is also great, especially for the DLCS, and the art style is very charming.I will say, some of the puzzles require a bit too much interpolation of information gathered. (Specifally the 9th case of base game and the 2nd case of the 2nd DLC)Even still, 9/10 puzzle game would easily recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap; very addictive, cleverly written indie. Loved it. Since having Covid-19 three times, long-term effects include my brain not functioning properly anymore, and it really worries me. It did take me far longer to suss out the nuances, admittedly, but I was able to finally finish the damned thing, and I couldn't be more pleased. Worth it. :-)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I saw it at Game Maker's Toolkit video about detective games and wanted to try it myself.Very similar to return of the obra dinn with viewing static scenes and deducting what happend. It is easy at first and gets more and more challenging and last 2 levels were quite tough and required some 200 iq deduction skills.Overall it was a great experience and I can reccomend to anyone who wants to play some fantastic investigation game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing. It eventually gets repetitive, and too many of the puzzles can only be solved by trial and error. It also suggests that fascism tries to promote individual virtue, where actually it only promotes group virtues. Maybe because the game designers don't like being virtuous, so they made the bad guys order virtue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle makers is back with another absolute banger. The only issue I had with this game was finishing it and having no more to play. Just hard enough to make you stare at the same screen for over an hour, while being intuitive enough to keep you from looking up a guide. Oh how close I came, how thrilling it was when I solved it anyways! No one makes games like this and man do I wish he made some more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A very thoughtful and well-designed deduction style puzzle game with a similar vibe to Return of the Obra Dinn. The visual style is distinct yet charming, and overall the presentation makes looking at the meticulously crafted scenes that make up the game a constant pleasure. The setting is also quite interesting, though I will let it speak for itself as you play the game. I highly recommend this game for those who enjoy exploring unique game worlds with puzzle mechanics like the aforementioned Obra Dinn or Outer Wilds where a lot of the "game" takes place in your mind as you suss out clues and attempt to string them all together in a satisfying moment of realization.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let this game fool you: the first scene is simple, without anything behind the curtains. That will quickly stop being true. An excellent little narrative that asks you to figure out what's happening in a scene. But remember: there's more happening in these lives than purely what the game asks for...During the last major level, while trying to put the right people in the right places, the big 'twist' finally hit me, and everything went from disjointed events to a full story. I could have played this game forever, and was so sad as I saw the finish line approach. Big recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - if you are on the fence about this I would wait for a sale because its going to be a one and done. Not long for some people or the frustration might turn your opinion in the last 2-3 cases from positive to negative.I played without hints and without obvious sparkles to give clues on what you had to click. Just so people understand how I played the game.Having completed the game in one sitting I would say that I think the game is fun and enjoyable BUT if I knew I was going to complete the game in less then 6 hours (most of that mainly in the last 3-4 cases) I would of held off for a sale.I did enjoy and like the collection and deduction of the cases however something I found frustrating is that in the last 2 cases the mouse would not change over 2 or 3 clues so I was stuck missing the most important ones even though I had gone over everything like 5-10 times (I am not saying it was a bug btw just that I think the "hit box" for the clue was way too small meaning I could not click it compared to every other clue even though I kept mousing over it) and that was utterly annoying and I started to hate the collection part of the game. I also found the last 2 cases to be frustrating because it required either guesswork or leaps of logic that was not very obvious (I understand the possibility that was the point to make something very obtuse but obvious once you were on the right track, but since the early cases don't really push that idea you feel like they try to be "clever" when its just changing the rules to something completely different).I feel for the price I paid for the time and enjoyment I had was positive however Its not a high positive maybe a middle to low positive. Personally I found some cases boring, some too easy and others just a slog.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the best games I've played in a while. At the start the game captured me with its mystery solving gameplay but once the story starts to form you are trapped by the conspiracy and events surrounding the idol. A must buy for anyone looking for a fun time with some good thinking along!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: , and its DLC , is a truly phenomenal puzzle game whose unique approach to mystery, puzzle design, and character story is addicting and immersive. _childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, I've been waiting for that kind of gameplay since I finished Return of the Obra Dinn. The game makes you feel like Hercule Poirot or any other meticulous detective. _childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A good, detailed puzzle game. Has just enough to the story that keeps you on your toes but not so much that it's just irritatingly confusing. Bought both the main game and the DLC, enjoyed both. Main game was definitely better but I think that's just because they really had a great vision for the main story, but had to work around that story for the DLC. I'd still buy another DLC if it released though. Note for others: this game doesn't have horror elements, despite being an ongoing murder-mystery. Death is a very casual piece of the whole puzzle. It's there to give you info, not create a specific experience. I enjoyed it a ton anyways because that's not a huge draw for me, but if you're playing for an emotionally-involved experience, you probably won't get that here. Buy it anyways, though. It's good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brilliant, it makes you think a lot and its very satisfying to solve. And the storytelling its amazing, you have to figure out every piece of story by yourself, looking at the characters, the letters and notes they have on them, objects, details on the room, etc. Nothing is explained directly to you. After solving a mistery you can feel like a big brain boy
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: More games like this is what the industry needs! Amazing mysteries that always make you think about the details without ever being overwhelming, and an overarching story with multiple twists that can be deduced if you think enough about what really happens between levels. No moon logic, wild guessing or frustrating unclarity. Perfect!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun deduction game similar to Obra Dinn in that you have to figure out what happened using clues found in the scene.The story told is very interesting, with a couple of twists that make you go "OOOOH" once you figure them out.Difficulty level and complexity of the scenes are in a nice spot, not too easy but also not so difficult you have to start taking notes.Unfortunately it's a little on the short side, I completed the game and the first DLC in less than 7 hours, without using in-game hints or looking anything up.Overall definitely recommended, maybe buy it in a sale due to the short length.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The comparison to The Return of the Obra Dinn gets made all the time, and for good reason. It scratches the same itch, not just in the way that its puzzles work almost in a satisfying jigsaw-like manner, like in Obra Dinn, but also in how its subject matter is compelling and captures your imagination.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game was excellent and I hope they make 20 more like it! It reminds me of Return of the Obra Dinn, but has its own spin on the deductive reasoning genre. I loved the characters, the art, the story, the music - altogether a wonderful game. I also love games that are 10 hours or less, and this took me about 7 hours to beat. I had such a great time playing it over a long weekend and beating it; feels like I can start the week with an accomplishment under my belt.PROS: excellent deductive reasoning puzzles, difficult but not so hard as to be frustrating, wonderful story.CONS: referring to clues you've found before can be a tad clunky, but this did not affect my enjoyment of the game too much.Overall 10/10 game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I played through this on Game Pass, but not the DLC, so after the sequel was released I decided to re-buy the original with everything in the big bundle, and I burned through the original episodes very quickly to get the achievements before starting on the DLC.Anyway, if the context of me "re-buying" a game I already beat isn't enough of an endorsement, this is an amazing game and is well worth getting if you enjoy puzzles and/or adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: + Brilliant story told over the course of several snapshots throughout time+ Great puzzles to solve - the first couple help ease you into the game and from then on they're a decent challenge but never unfair+ Just a really great "Ah ha!" feeling when you figure something out - really satisfying+ There's always a sense of intrigue into each new scene - what has transpired since you last had a view into the world?+ Really nice 2D sprites and scenes+ Music is great at setting the scene and/or adding tension to a situationFantastic puzzle and whodunit type game. As the mystery is such a great lure of the game, if you have an inkling you'd like it, you're much better off going in as blind as possible and just enjoying the ride. Don't read tons about it (let alone watch someone else play or watch a really extensive review on it!) or spoil anything for yourself - it's a few hours of brilliant puzzle-solving and seeing where the story goes next. Then it'll all be over and you'll be in my position, thinking of it fondly but envying those who have yet to experience it for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I was directed to this game by friends. I am not usually playing detective puzzle stories so this was a new experience for me. My first impression was from art and initially it felt like it is not my kind of cup. But I gave the game a shot and played it. The moment I got into the story the art together with music made so much sense to me. No other style would have worked for me. The atmosphere I felt because of this combination was spot on. If I try to describe the atmosphere I got from this, it felt like reading Dickens' story sitting next to the window in a warm room during a cold dark winter evening. You yourself feel safe and cozy, but there is suspense below the surface and you are aware of danger and darkness around you. And if at the beginning I was skeptical about this choice, at the end of the game I loved it. Story itself pulled me in immediately. I was living through story lines of characters like I was reading a good book or watching amazing TV series. I became very invested in some of the characters' lives and wanted to see more and more of them. Even though you do not know biographies of characters in this story, the creators of the game made them very real to me. I felt like I knew the people in this story. I could spot and fantasize that there are both friendship and romantic links between people and was so happy to see some of my theories confirmed or denied at the end. If I would be a streamer my watchers would have listened to me ranting about who is dating who, and who should be dating who, and why. This game was a big discovery for me and I think I might play similar things in future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This did to me what the return of the obra dinn could not. I completely finished the game without ever using a hint. This is one of the best puzzle / investigation games I have played yet. The visuals have a unique ugliness to it that I like and the soundtrack is amazing too. I highly recommend giving this game a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Pros:1. **Charming Pixelated Aesthetics:** Embarking on the journey through The Case of the Golden Idol feels like stepping into a pixelated wonderland. The game's nostalgic visuals add a unique charm to the mystery-solving experience, making it both visually delightful and engaging.2. **Connected yet Captivating Cases:** Solving the 11 mysterious cases in this game is like navigating a thrilling novel – each case is interconnected, yet possesses its own distinct charm. From mysterious artifacts to hidden secrets, the variety keeps you hooked.3. **Deep World Building:** The developers have poured creativity into the game's world-building. It's a double-edged sword – fantastic for those who enjoy diving deep, but may be overwhelming for those seeking a quicker pace.**Overall Impression:**Stepping into The Case of the Golden Idol is not just about solving mysteries; it's about immersing yourself in a pixelated world where every case is a new adventure. With connected narratives, charming aesthetics, and mystery boxes that keep you on your toes, this game is a delightful journey through the unexpected.**Recommendation:**For mystery enthusiasts and pixel art aficionados alike, The Case of the Golden Idol is a must-play. _childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute classic little number with an intricate story full of wonderful characters. Case of the Golden Idol attempts to break the most frustrating aspect of detective games which is the prospect of endlessly clicking in the hope of achieving an answer but supposed potential answers. The issue they rightfully examine is: People think differently, and often times solutions can have many forms. This game is all about the right solution with 'fill in the blanks' style prompts which can only mean correct answers in those. It is deduction in its purest form. This is where TCotGI is brilliant, it organises the snapshots of any case so that it fulfills a logical sequence; and your role as the player is to reconstruct these scenes based on the what the prompts suggest. It is a devilishly exciting detective game that weaves the 'uncovering' aspects into the narrative fabric of the game, so as you detect you find bits of the story. It is so well crafted and clever. It has you doing things you have never done in a game before. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great detective game with a vibe of Obra Dinn but with its own unique atmosphere and gameplay.Game, where solving the murders and events that led to them is so rewarding. You search for clues by investigating each involved character, going through their personal stuff and correspondence, and observing the surroundings of the murder. The game brings many Aha! moments when the pieces start to come together and you finally solve the crime.Difficulty is also nicely done, from simple cases at one location to robust deaths involving multiple people across several locations.I really recommend it! One of the best games I played in 2022.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very clever game. I find the art appealing, and the music fits the mood perfectly. Even in the scenes that are less dark, the music will take an ominous turn. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game. This is the closest experience I've had to pure bliss since Return of the Obra Dinn. _childDocuments_.review: Loved this game! Some of the comparisons with Return of the Obra Dinn are maybe a bit overstated in that this one isn't quite as complex, but it's certainly true that if you liked Obra Dinn you'll probably like this one. Not sure if this has been fixed, but if you're playing the demo, it might be worth taking a screenshot of your solutions so you can quickly get through the levels you'll have to repeat in the full version.

_childDocuments_.review: is a rare game that manages to do deduction well. If you enjoy games like , you'll find a lot to like here.The basic game play loop is clicking through interesting scenes of disaster and intrigue to discover nouns and verbs that can be plugged in mad-libs style into various sections (like one that requires you to identify the names of each character in the scene). After a few of these to demonstrate that you grasp the basics of what's going on, you can fill out the description of what you figured out happened: usually who murdered who and why.Those traumatized by pixel-hunting in adventure games in the 90's need not sweat: the default for the game is to highlight points of interest (though this can be turned off if you wish). The verb-noun system prevents easy meta-gaming of the solution and encourages the player to think before solving.The overall story is well-written and there are many surprising turns and callbacks to things earlier in the story.Sometimes filling out the final solution leads to discoveries or solutions that would not have occurred otherwise, depriving the player of the joyful "ah ha!" moment.Perhaps appropriately for a game about secrets and secret societies, you don't play a character in the narrative: you are collecting knowledge for its own sake. Your solutions don't bring villains to justice, help the lovers unite or impact the world. Giving that sort of satisfaction in a deduction game is tricky, but I missed it here.It is a little short, I finished in five hours. However, I feel like I got my money's worth having bought in during the winter sale.Not really. The only possible complaint here is how generally ugly the characters are. Not sure if it's a "the past was never a good place," a meta-statement on how generally awful people the characters in the story are, or something else.If you enjoy deduction games and want to play a well-written story with interesting clues and a progressing narrative, check out

Very satisfying to solve the cases and connect the dots that are not always as straightforward as you might think, but actually manage to be quite clever and bait you into thinking a certain way that ends being the incorrect deduction.

_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great problem-solving game that I couldn't put down once I got started.Watching the story unfold with each puzzle and having the various pieces of information come together as the story progressed was very rewarding.  The fill-in-the-blanks style gameplay was something I haven't encountered before and I really enjoyed the mechanics of it, as well as the sense of accomplishment achieved from completing each section within a case.The art style was very charming and the music provided an enjoyable ambience.  I look forward to future content released by these developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A really, really nice game. A little gem, one might say. Unique in it's style and based on a impressively well written story that allows the player to really think for themselves, I'm very happy. The base story was a bit short for the price - 7 hours for me, but since I really enjoy the production I'm okay supporting the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game. Complicated scenes are frozen in time. Their meaning unfolds gradually as you piece together what must have happened to bring them about. Each scene has a few puzzle-structures, and the initial challenge is to collect the evidence for how various actors/objects fit into those structures. You then have to look at the overall scene, make inferences as to how things turned out like they have, and write out the story. I love how the initially chaotic scene becomes one imbued with cause, effect and intention, so that when you look at it at the end, you can 'see' the four-dimensional story in the frozen image. The puzzles are challenging but very fair, but you need to be patient. There is quite a lot of going back and forth. You also have to be prepared to throw away initial assumptions and rethink things a few times. But every puzzle has eventually been solvable without guesswork or hints, so don't give up too quickly!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really clever snack of a game.   It's quite short, but very satisfying to solve each chapter.  I hope the developers make more games like this one.  I appreciated that pixel hunting was entirely optional!  The story, music, and art style were all really fun and the gameplay easily brought out that "one more turn" feeling when I solved each chapter.  Very well done!Edit: adding a comment after I finished the two DLCs.  Both of them were quite good, although the second felt a little rushed, like there was a lot of story to cram into a small package.  Even though both DLCs are prequels to the main story, they should be played after the conclusion of the main story.  The main story has an organic way that it progressively introduces the player to the game's puzzles.  The DLCs throw you into the deep end.  Highly recommend and can't wait for another game like this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a unique deductive game in a similar vein to the return Obra Dinn. Each scene/level is a crime scene frozen in time and you start by searching the point & click environment as well as the characters’ belongings for clues in exploration mode and then solving the mystery in thinking mode. While it starts out seeming rather simple it quickly grows to demand more critical thinking and deduction. It also helps that the game has an intriguing narrative and mystery. Ultimately my only complaint is it does feel a bit short, and I was left wanting even more. I would definitely recommend getting this even at full price, and if it is on sale please get it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Return of the Obra Dinn, you'll like this. If you wanted to like Obra Dinn but got bogged down in chasing around looking for tiny details with no guidance, this is more accessible: the cases are tight-knit with the interface providing just enough guidance to give you what you need to solve it. And there's some extra hints available too if you need them, but I didn't use them so I can't attest to how useful they are. Even though a couple times I spent a bit of time staring at the case feeling baffled at how to progress, eventually I was able to think my way through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: As the first, as far as I'm aware, Obra Dinn-like, The Case of the Golden Idol is a triumph of style and world-building. Few games allow you to piece together a mystery without holding your hand the whole way, but TCotGI doesn't spoon-feed you every clue you need to solve the murders, forcing you to perform lateral thinking and logical deduction to get to the solutions. It's never TOO taxing on the brain (I never needed to consult a walkthrough), yet peeling back the many-layered onions across the game's eleven scenarios makes you feel like a very intelligent person indeed.Add to that the excellent (but always effectively concise) writing, the charming pixel art, the evocative music, and the gripping story, and you've got several hours of pure delight that a hundred games of Clue couldn't replicate. Loved, loved, loved it. Very much looking forward to seeing what this studio does next. Even a game with an identical structure and gameplay to this one, but with a brand-new story, would be A-Okay in my book. If you enjoy adventure games, playing detective, and submerging yourself into labyrinthine storytelling, buy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a game to scratch that Return Of The Obra Dinn itch!Boils down to:-> Find the clues-> Understand the context-> Piece together what happenedThe story itself was fairly intriguing, having a large cast of characters who persist (mostly) to the end. I could see this format of game being a series and I would play every one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Its a hidden object game where the player has to locate clues by examining the scene. You then have to associate the various clues to deduce what had transpired in the scene. It reminds me a little of the game "Return to Obra Dinn" in this regard. The story is about the fortunes of a family and its connection to a cursed golden idol. Its a fun little game but one to pick up on a sale like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A very good murder mystery in the same vein as the Obra Dinn: A series of whodunits presented in vignettes frozen in time where you need to suss out the identities of those involved, their motivations, and the method of killing. The overarching story tying all these vignettes together is great with some intriguing twists.

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is an elaborate story involving the changing hands of a Golden Idol with magical properties and how it impacts the people in town over the years and leads to a number of deaths. It's a complex series of 11 cases and an epilogue that are all highly detailed and often difficult to solve using a fill-in-the blank deduction system with clues hidden across chapters and within the individual cases. While I really appreciate the detail involved and how connected and concise the overall mystery was, the game wasn't my favorite compared to other point-and-click mystery games in the genre and doesn't feel as fully deserving of the overwhelmingly positive reviews compared to Tangle Tower, Jenny LeClue Detectivu, and other similarly styled deduction based point-and-click games. Though, anyone who loves a good point-and-click mystery that's story rich will enjoy piecing together these cases. 6/10The DLC, The Spider of Lanka, adds some additional backstory to the mystery of the Golden Idol with 3 new cases. While I appreciate their complexity which lives up to the original story, sometimes it's tedious to switch between scenes and clues in order to piece together the full story and solve the cases. 6/10The final DLC, The Lemurian Vampire, also adds 3 new cases that explores the origins of the Golden Idol while using a new mechanic: changing the time of day. While the twists didn't feel as impactful, the exploring the same areas at different times of day added an interesting layer to these final cases. 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a child, I spent ages over books with detective puzzles in them. This takes me back - it's been a while since I've had that experience, and The Case of the Golden Idol delivers that.Had the pleasure to playtest some of the chapters, and loved the diversity of the puzzles, the sense of progress while figuring out a multi-layered challenge, and, of course, the art style.

_childDocuments_.review: The character art in this game is dreadful. It will bother you for the first few cases, then you'll stop noticing because you're too focused on the cases, then you'll begin appreciating it because it helps you keep track of different characters as they show up in later cases.And then, at the very end, in the epilogue, the game slaps you over the head and goes DO YOU GET IT NOW?? because it turns out that the awful character design was silently priming you for a post-game twist that ties everything together and blows your mind, and it only works because of the character design.Tangle Tower, this could have been you, but you were too beautiful, and too proud of your twist. You had to go and make a big deal about the "reveal," like the player was unworthy of figuring it out. The Case of the Golden Idol legit just drops it on your head like an afterthought, as though it assumed you were smart enough to have already figured it out, because you could have. You could have figured it out. But you were too busy thinking about the hideous character art.IT'S BAD FOR A REASON, YOU'LL UNDERSTAND WHY LATER.10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be reviewing the base game and the DLCs in this one review.November 1st 2022 -  - 7 h 42 m - (100%) 9/10 The Case of the Golden Idol has an interesting story that is logical and makes sense. The one inconsistency I thought of was solved in the  which is shocking but you could also deduce beforehand. The music and art style are all right. I think the game's difficulty curve is almost great, but it is spoiled by the 9th case being harder than the other cases. It doesn't have a lot of evidence and you have to make a lot of deductions. It is the only case I almost had to use hints for.May 8th 2023 -  - 4 h 6 m - (100%) 9/10 - Beat all 3 cases and investigated everything in them. The storyline of the DLC is more coherent due to its condensed format and acts as a nice prequel for the main story. The revelations in the cases make you see the base game in a somewhat different light. Overall the DLC compares well with the main game, I just have one small gripe with it. The gameplay is just as great as in the base game, however, the difficulty of cases 2 and 3 should have been swapped. Case 3 felt too easy compared to the difficulty of case 2 and this brought down the impact of the game a bit and made it end on a bit of a weak note.October 7th -  - 5 h 36 m - (100%) 8/10 - Beat all three cases. Only had to use one hint on the second case. I really liked Lemurian Vampire. It completed the prequel arch and is the bridging gap between the first DLC and the main game. The story is nice and has a twist in it although it doesn't compare to the twist in the first DLC. The problem I have with this DLC is its difficulty curve. The first case is a good level of difficulty to start out at. However, I have issues with the difficulties of the second and third cases. The second case is way too difficult and requires a lot of deduction with few clues and it's the only case I had to use a hint on. On the other hand, the final case was too easy by comparison. It was even easier than the first one, which is a little disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: A really really good puzzle/mystery game! Would give it 9/10. A few minor nitpicks and some potential missed opportunities, but nothing game breaking. I played this both on my main PC and Steam Deck and it worked fine on both.You're presented with a scene that plays a brief, animated loop. In 'Explore' mode, you can click around and read dialogue from the people in the scene, examine objects, and read letters. These will contain general clues to what/why certain events had happened, but some dialogue/text contains clickable keywords which are added to your 'inventory'. These can be names, places, actions etc. Some of the later chapters contain multiple screens too.Once you have gathered all the keywords, you then go into the 'Think' mode which presents you with some scrolls. Usually, there's a scroll that gives a summary of the events before the scene, and you must fill in the gaps using the words in your inventory. Other scrolls may require you to solve other aspects of the mystery, E.g. the names of all the people, or the meanings of some symbols.When you have solved the scrolls, you can then move onto the next chapter.I won't give away much, but all the chapters are linked together by an overarching storyline which is interesting, and requires a bit of thinking to piece together as there are some gaps in time between chapters.I think the difficulty is just about right. There aren't any major brainbusters, and all the chapters can be solved without any large leaps in logic, but aside from the earlier mysteries (which are there to ease you in), it doesn't hold your hand either. The difficulty also gradually ramps up but not too quickly.There are 11 chapters and it took me ~8hrs to complete, but you may very well do it quicker. It sounds short, but I think it was about the right length. I'd very much prefer to have a short, high-quality experience, than something that drags out too long!(These are very very minor nitpicks and are more for the developers as I really want them to do well!)The music is great, but the tracks are quite short and will keep looping. For the more ambient tracks, this is fine and actually enhances the atmosphere very nicely, but some of the more energetic songs can be a little distracting after a while. Perhaps there could be gaps filled with background noise before the song repeats again?There is a mechanic that let's you know if a scroll is nearly complete if 1-2 words are incorrect. There were a couple of times where I felt that gave me too much of a hint. For example, if the hint pops up and you replace one word with another (that is also wrong), the hint won't change and it confirms to you that it's that specific slot that's wrong. I'm not sure if there is a better way to implement a hint system that doesn't give things away, but it would have been nice to switch off that hint system altogether.Sometimes dragging the words around can be a little fiddly, especially when I'm trying to organise them in my inventory. It may very well just be me, but there are times when I drop a word, feel like it should go in a slot, but then it jumps back to it's original position. It didn't happen frequently enough to become irritating though.When you solve certain scrolls, some of the words disappear from the big inventory slot at the bottom and can only be accessible from the scroll section. This does help clear up the inventory, but it doesn't necessarily mean you are done with the word, and can make things a little awkward when trying to find that word again. There were also a couple of instances where I forgot about a word because it had been removed from the inventory. Again, it may be me being silly, but perhaps greying out or changing the background texture would have helped?Not so much a nitpick, but a maybe missed opportunity. Minor gameplay/plot spoiler (not a solution spoiler). (Minor bug) I'll need to check which chapter, but there were two words that were the wrong away around when I clicked on them (One of the later chapters). It didn't break the game, and was a very very minor bug!If you like mystery/puzzle games, it's definitely worth your time. It has a generous demo so there's no excuse to at least give it a try. (Although my savegame didn't carry over for some reason so take note of the solutions if you don't want to do the earlier chapters all over again!).Many thanks to the developers and I'm looking forward to seeing what they come up with next!

_childDocuments_.review: A short but INCREDIBLE mystery/deduction game. Each puzzle is a collection of 1 or more rooms of a specific event ("exploring" mode) and you have to fill in the blanks of who, what, when, where, and why the event happened ("thinking" mode). As you explore the environment, people, and objects, you click on/collect various nouns and verbs to fill in those blanks.However! Many environmental clues don't translate into word bank options, so it is VITAL to pay attention to all the information in a puzzle to fully understand what happened. If you only focus on the word bank and ignore other aspects of the puzzle, you're not going to solve it. There are plenty of red herrings too, so your first assumptions about who anyone is, what their motivations are, or what actions they took may be completely wrong (especially in the later puzzles).It can get a bit rough sometimes when you have 80% of the information needed to lock in an answer and you juuuuust can't get one of the names right, but it helps to take a break and return to the puzzle with a clear mind.The underlying story connecting all the puzzles is very engaging as well. I didn't figure out the big "twist" until the game spelled it out for me, but when I looked back at the puzzles, all the clues were there and it seemed so obvious in hindsight! All the puzzles help move the plot forward, none of it ever feels random or out of place.I definitely recommend this to anyone looking for an engaging mystery game!

_childDocuments_.review: Nice deduction game! The game play revolves around scenes that each depict a particular moment. Gathering  clues using point-and-click mechanisms, your job is to figure out what happened in each scene. You have to both envision what happened as well as gather the words from the clues to note your deductions. Overall, the game has an appropriately macabre story, the puzzles are good, and the UI fluent. Only minus from shortness.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game that will appeal to fans of classic point-and-click adventures and puzzle games such as Return of the Obra Dinn, or anyone who just enjoys a good logic puzzle.  Each chapter of the story gets progressively more complicated, but the story was good enough to hold my interest throughout.  I wasn't as crazy about the DLC chapters, but that's a minor compliant after playing such a gem of a game.  This is a very unique and worthwhile experience and I hope more games are created with a similar format.

The only case that I think was a little unfair on the answers was case 9, but other than that all the mysteries were fair and interesting. I only wish that it was a little longer or that it had a couple more cases, it feels a little too short in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: The easiest thing to do here would be to say "If you like Obra Dinn, you'll love this" and leave it at that, but that wouldn't be doing this game justice. This game really is an excellent example of the genre. Whilst it is true that I haven't come across a game that made me scratch my head this much since Obra Dinn, Golden Idol is also utterly oozing with charm, style, and, subtle humour. For the first couple of chapters I was a little concerned at how easy everything seemed to be, taking almost no time at all. But, the complexity slowly built with each level, and suddenly I found myself with notes scattered across my desk, frantically backtracking 3 chapters because "I recognise him!". The narrative really is this games main feature though. Its is exceptionally well written, and every scene you play out fits perfectly with each one that came before it, with subtle twists that leave you guessing as to what the characters real motives are. Phenomenal detective game. A true masterpiece

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and unusual mystery game where you're not really a character in the story, but more of a sort of godlike observer trying to figure out what's going on in certain moments of the story's evolving timeline. The retro graphics are charming and well done and the music is amazing and does not overstay its welcome considering you might be looking at one scene or another for some time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting something as good as Obra Dinn, prepare to be disappointed. I wish I hadn't read the comparisons in other comments, because I would've enjoyed this game more. I didn't need to pull out pen and paper until Case 10. I finished 1-10 in about 5 hours. I got stuck for quite a while on part of Case 11, so finished the whole game in about 6.5 hours. The gameplay itself is quite fun, but I didn't find the story particularly engaging.Final verdict: Golden Idol is not the successor to Obra Dinn. Fun, but lower your expectations and wait for a sale.
