Figuring out connections between various pieces of information, having to take into account motives, and even remembering pieces of information from earlier chapters left me feeling clever throughout most of the game. I only had to look up the solution to one piece of information online and only needed to use the in-game hint system less then a handful of times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A real gem of a game. The way that the story and lore is baked into this universe is surpassed my expectations. Essentially the entire game is told through environmental clues and the way it unfolds is captivating. It makes you feel like a detective -- Obra Dinn is really the only thing even remotely close to this experience.Animation, art style, and sound all work really well here too. The DLC is also wonderful (albeit a bit short).
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Walks the incredibly narrow tightrope of a satisfying puzzle in each level without ever feeling unfair.  Every case feels overwhelming in the first minute, but quickly turns into a satisfyingly enclosed story; changing up the information needed to "solve" each case really keeps the game feeling fresh the entire runtime. 10/10 experience, I only wish it was longer. DLC or sequel soon please
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: have no idea whats going on for a while and not sure where to start, then figure it out slowly and methodically with the clever way the keywords nudge in the right direction. very satisfying game loop the comes together nicely at the end.  banging music throughout and a great art style with a slick ui & controls.you can't go wrong purchasing this if you enjoy detective style games - sadly, for me this is not quite obra dinn but scratches the itch and is unique and enjoyable enough to not be a dull copy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Was happy with the way the story slowly unfolded and I know it's a good puzzle game for me when I have to put down the game for a bit to get through particular puzzles.There are some cases where leaps in logic have to be made through inference alone, but for the most part try not to guess the answers since the information is almost always there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I paid so much for this game. I accepted that the visuals would be terrible, but I thought what I'd get instead would be an interesting puzzle game. When in fact, it's just really boring clues to look for, trying to drag and drop names in their spaces... god, whyyy. This really makes me question whether to buy other puzzle games, even though that's a genre I love when it's well done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I love detective stuff, and I've never played a game that's better at making you feel like Sherlock Holmes. Only gripe is that the base game is just a little too short on its own - once the murder-mystery-solving momentum really gets going, the story rushes into a conclusion. It feels a lot more complete with the Spider of Lanka DLC, which is challenging and satisfying and meaningfully deepens the story. Lemurian Vampire is less essential (it adds lore but felt more like translating a story from a different language than solving a mystery).
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: It's been awhile since I play such a simple yet fun puzzle solving game. This game has a simple mechanic whereby 'you look for words and add them to the list to be used as answers in a sentence/paragraph to solve the mystery/murder/death (Sort of like a fill in the blank game)'. Sounds easy enough but with the twist and turns in the story/what you don't see (it's your job to figure it out the mystery or rather this is what the game is about [note that you are not a playable character in this story]) during your play through, this game will probably make you feel proud of yourself when you connect the dots to figure out the answer. This is a definite buy considering its price!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Puzzles are creative and well executed and the story is interesting and original. As the game progresses the difficulty ramps in a nice way, not too fast or slow, but I also enjoyed how the puzzles and story interlocks in a way that feels extremely satisfying as you progress. My only complaint is I would have loved more of it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this, I spent roughly 8 hours to beat the entire game.(Base game Plus Spider of Lanka DLC)My adventure felt short, but it was certainly fun playing!Tutorial at the start gives a really good explanation on how you can expect the game to play out mechanically. The rest of the game gives pretty interesting ways on what you need to solve how scenes played out. (But its never difficult to figure out what you need to do) The 2D & Art style was fantastic. Mysteries were wonderfully done, and the logic deduction is also really fun. There's some head scratchers but didn't feel frustrating. Overall: Really fun game :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A clever game of deduction. Hard to say more without spoilers!The difficulty felt just right. Enough that I had to really scrutinize every little scrap of evidence, and when I assembled the solutions it always felt very satisfying.The art style is not conventionally beautiful, but it complements the overall atmosphere of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an extremely fun take on logic style puzzles! In each chapter, you're presented with a murder scene. You're presented with some fill-in-the-blank sheets. Your goal is to investigate the scene, locate word clues, then fill in the blanks and tell the story of what happened.At some points, it can get downright chaotic. You really need to put on your detective hat and pay attention to what people say. There's a Hint system, but I didn't really use it because of how much it gently encouraged me to pay attention to details. And it helps, though I really had to stretch my thinking to try and make sense about some of the deductions. Especially the DLC, that was rough. Still, this was super fun, and I'm looking forward to the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The art is tragically bad, but I soon found it almost charming. The game is wonderfully designed, increasing in difficulty, but never feeling impossible. You should plan to take you time with each scene and then try to build a story of what happened. I enjoyed the challenge for this extremely charming game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I don't log many reviews here, but this hasn't been getting enough attention and is absolutely a must play if you like mystery stories or games with unique gameplay styles. It's been getting a lot of comparisons to Obra Dinn lately but it's also incredibly unique in its own right! Definitely has the same level of satisfaction that Obra Dinn gives you when you finally figure out something you've been stuck on for half an hour, though. Highly, highly recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game that excels in many aspects.  The puzzles are not trivial, but they're designed in a way that lets you piece together clues in a structured way which is quite satisfactory once you reveal the level step by step. It's a well balanced difficulty.The story itself is cohesive, intriguing and with a few unexpected turns.The graphics, despite being simple, is actually very well made and adequate to this type of puzzle solving genre.Would highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Its logic deduction, evoking the spirit of "Obra Dinn," exceeds all expectations. No arduous search through the entire vessel; it flows effortlessly.The graphics, adorably macabre with a touch of humor, bewitch the eye. The music, a harmonious companion. A treat for indulging in delightful, bite-sized moments of play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A great detective game! I find the execution a lot better than the Obra Dinn, which I disliked due to slow travel and obscure clues. Here, the different vignettes are self contained, so there's no amount of backtracking. Everything is logical, and the most obvious solution is often a red-herring: you really have to look at all the clues to uncover the true solution.I really loved that while each vignette is self-contained, there's a grander narrative across the entire game, which is coherent from start to finish.I could complain that the game is fairly short at around 6h, but at least it doesn't drag on and on, and I enjoyed every minute.TLDR: awesome game if you love detective games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: When I first tried the demo for this game It was during next fest and I wasn't too interested. Something convinced me to give it another shot months later and I found it to be excellent, really brings me back to the Professor Layton games. Also I  really love the artwork in this game, It really fits it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying frozen-moment-in-time murder-mystery puzzle game that shares DNA with Return of the Obra Dinn. The mysteries are tricky to figure out but make sense once you have. An engaging plot filled with murder, intrigue, that-escalated-quickly's and characters plotting and bouncing off one another. Gives your brain a work-out figuring it all out. I liked the two prequel DLCs too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic detective/deduction game! You explore scenes to gather information, then use that info to 'fill the blanks' and demonstrate your understanding of what happened.The story is interesting, if a little convoluted in the telling, and I found the difficulty level to be about right for me: a decent challenge at times, but never too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game. In the same vein as Return of the Obra Dinn, identify clues in scenes and fill in a story. There were a couple of places where I felt the logic leap was too great or I had to trial-and-error some things. I don't know if that was by design or if I missed something, since the story comes together very well with the epilogue and the DLC fleshes it out even better. Though I had more instances of feeling like I was guessing in the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What a gem. Loved every second of playing it.It's a game for puzzle and logic-oriented people, but even if you don't feel like you fit the archetype, it's still a great game for its story and art. One of the things I appreciated was that the story felt consistent and the puzzles felt balanced. No logical leaps felt unnatural to the plot. I say don't miss out on this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: like 1/3 of the playtime is the last 2 scenarios alone. this game really expects a lot of you, and I really REALLY appreciate that. I am proud to say I used 0 hints. Not as difficult as Obra Dinn, which it is oft compared to, but the deductions you're asked to make are good, although admittedly sometimes it results in simple trial and error.but this game is an easy recommend. VERY good detective game, the likes of which I haven't seen much of. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A thumbs up, just about. Obviously this will have been compared to Obra Dinn a million times. And this game is cute, and shares some of that similar structure in terms of piecing together information. But fundamentally this game is the same thing done multiple times over and over.Whereas Obra Dinn evolved, like peeling an onion. Each time it gave you more piece by piece, and each nugget you unlocked felt like a dopamine rush, this game is largely first of all click EVERYTHING until you get up to the required number of pieces of information. That's just a slog, particuarly on a controller. In one mission I had to go back to a mouse.Then deduce the story. And whereas Obra Dinn unlocked confirmation after three pieces of correct info, Golden Idol is kind of all or nothing. You can brute force some bits easily if you try, or sit there not knowing if you're making progress at other points.I think fundamentally my biggest issue is repetition. It doesn't feel like it evolves, it's just repeating the same stuff over and over. It scrapes by as a thumbs up as the game is nicely executed, but I won't feel compelled for the DLC or sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Really makes you *feel* like a golden idol.This is a criminally under-explored genre of puzzle game. The closest thing to it is Obradin, but both games are fairly distinct. If you like logic and deduction, this game is great fun. It also has just the right amount of quality of life features to be enjoyable without being frustrating to play.It's a little weird to interact with the story, as you play as a non-character. There are no stakes, your only goal is to figure out what's going on out of curiosity. This sometimes made it somewhat hard to care about the story, but I still found myself thinking about the events the unfolded days after I'd finished the game. So I'd say the story is satisfying, but lacks some grounding elements that could have elevated it further.Still, the gameplay is unmatched! Play this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: There are, on occasion, puzzles that are a little too cryptic or double bluffs that really make you question the purpose of their inclusion but I can only really count one or two of those throughout the course of the game. Everything else though, was a great time and made you feel like you were actually solving some large conspiracy through deduction. The DLC was good but not quite up to the main game (likely just as it was missing the larger overarching narrative that came from more scenes) but otherwise enjoyable. If you are a fan of Obra Dinn, I'd recommend checking this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice detective/investigation game with some clever puzzles and an intriguing overarching plot line. Has a structure that's fairly generous in letting you know when you're close to the right answer, and divides each individual scene in such a way that the ton of information you get can be sorted out in smaller chunks, which is a nice way to do things. Whilst each scene is self contained, it can be helpful to look back over previous chapters since there are a lot of recurring characters and details that will give you big hints later on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a terrific detective-style game that really gets you to think situations through to piece together what has happened/what is happening. Don't let the weird art-style put you off, it's a really well-made game with a great story. Some of the puzzles can seem overwhelming at first, but just work your way through and take the time to think things out. Once you have all the clues, it all starts to come together nicely.If you're really struggling, there is a hints system that is its own little mini-game to add some easier clues to help you figure things out. The two DLC are an excellent addition that tell the story of the events leading up to the main-game. The soundtrack to the game is an under-rated gem as well. I find myself looping the music in the background while I'm working at times.Very much recommended as a one of the best detective games available.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun! The Obra Dinn influence is quite clear but hey, I loved that and had a great time with this as well. Definitely less difficult and more approachable than Obra Dinn I would say, particularly given the chapter-by-chapter format. I also managed to solve the vast majority of things here through actual hints the game left me rather than the brute force, trial-and-error approach I occasionally had to resort to to get through Obra Dinn, which makes for a more satisfying experience. Backtracking to obtain all the point-and-click clues (sometimes just a word on a page or an easy-to-miss visual detail) is sometimes necessary but the tool they give you to identify all of those on a page is handy in case you don't feel like spending a couple minutes just trying to find the one clue you missed. Just completed it and it took me 15 hrs in all so not a bad deal.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Consider this a 7/10 recommend. The graphics are cartoony and memorable. There are some genuinely clever puzzles here but the game starts off very slow and I find the fact that every case is self contained makes it too easy to guess solutions without putting in the leg work (its why I see some reviews complain some puzzles are obtuse when every single one has multiple clue sets which point to a solution. I also found the story to be disappointing in that the discreet case structure with exposition dumps makes it hard to care about the over arching story or mystery. There is also a lack of context. I think being a disembodied observer makes everything less personally engaging compared to an in universe character like in Obra Dinn (the game this one globs itself onto as seen by the steam description).
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I actually felt proud of myself as an investigator playing this game. No frustration where you have no clue where to look next, no obvious hand-holding. The mechanics force your hand to draw your own conclusions and report them, and the feedback on your report pushes you into discovering the missing pieces yourself. Even some mysterious gaps that bridge the levels together that I couldn't initially figure out are exposed in the end via another puzzle, the epilogue. I also had the opportunity to figure out the entire thing before the epilogue, so nailing it without any work made me feel proud. Like I figured out a huge plot twist in a detective novel right before the big reveal.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What this game is:An innovative and unique experienceA game on which you'll feel like a detectiveA short and amazing indie gemWhat this game is not:Better than the return of the obra dinnI was led to believe this game an upgrde from the return of the obra dinn, whereas its a very different thing. Sure the music is similar and the recognizing the persons is similar, but that is where the similarities end. Both are amazing and different games and you should buy and play both.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A really funny and intriguing game! I loved the overall narrative, the atmosphere of the game and the theme music accompanying the different chapters was equally unsettling and evocative. It is a really interesting game system, something really akin to what a proper deduction process can be. I loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best detective/mystery games I've ever played, no exaggeration. I was actually sad when I completed it because I didn't want to stop piecing together the mysteries of the game.The aspect of being able to figure everything out on your own is something I find lacking in a surprising amount of other point and click detective games. This game is truly dedicated to you solving the mystery yourself, with every necessary detail laid out for you.The amount of times I had an "AH HA!" moment playing this game is incredible - the satisfaction that comes from that single moment of realization when you make the one crucial connection required to figure out the whole case is immeasurable.The game does have a built-in hint system, but I couldn't explain how helpful they are because I was insistent on never using them - I wanted to be able to say that I figured it out on my own, and I'd personally recommend avoiding hints as much as you can, because you can only learn the solution once.There were only a few times I felt "stuck", but it was never a result of the game not giving enough information. Instead it more often resulted from me straight up not making the connection, or the game including details that seem unintentionally misleading - this game trains you to look at every detail, so when some minor things seem inconsistent, whether it's part of the actual puzzle or not, you will definitely notice.Still, that hardly takes away from my enjoyment of this game. I cannot recommend it enough if you are a fan of point and click puzzle adventures or just mysteries in general!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game slaps. It's difficult to talk about this game without mentioning Obra Dinn, and it's really the next true entry in that sort of series of deep mystery deduction game. It builds on a lot of things I liked about Obra Dinn, and has a UI that's a lot more intuitive. I'm guessing a lot of the reviews will have mentioned that, and discussed the compelling and mind-blowing puzzles, the incredible art, the atmosphere conjured by the music. It's easy to talk about how much the puzzles light up my brain, and forget to mention how FUNNY this game is. It's full of weird little characters, their various schemes, and the stupid circumstances that they create for themselves and each other. Everyone has their own motivations, for better or worse, and they might be lying! When you examine everything with a fine-toothed comb, in almost every case, there's a REASON that Alice decided to do this thing, or Bob wanted that thing, or this thing happened to Carol. It hangs together, there aren't plot holes, and you eventually find yourself following along with it like a reality show or something. Alice will be dead on the floor and you'll be looking at these people and thinking [all fake examples, obviously] "oh my god, Bob and his MLM are at it again" and "wow Carol is trying to STEAL Eve's man!!" and "lmao I can't believe Eve is doing tax fraud about this murder."It's an incredible deep puzzle game that you can really sink your teeth into, and it's also a delightful romp. The DLC are also amazing; the Spider of Lanka is a decent extension of the concepts used in the base game, but the Lemurian Vampire is an absolute triumph of puzzle design, narrative, humor, and fun, the apotheosis of everything I've ever wanted in a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Undoubtedly, this is one of the most engaging detective games I’ve ever experienced. It’s a tough and frustrating challenge sometimes, but the satisfaction you experience after deducing a scenario is incredible.If you enjoyed Strange Horticulture earlier this year, or enjoy solving mysteries, then I implore you to try out the generous demo. This game is well worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little mystery experience. The game fully respects your time and competency as a player and strongly encourages you to not use hints. The art and music is stellar and fits perfectly with the atmosphere.I ended up needing some hints to push me in the right direction in the last case. The way it wants you to input some things statically can be frustrating at times, but I don't know of a better system. There were many times I had the right idea in my head of something, but I wasn't sure how the game wanted me best to describe it and it took a little trial and error.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: You may have heard about this game. VERY highly rated (98%) mystery investigation point and click game. The basic premise is you are given a scene and various people, notes and objects that you can click on. As you do this you gather key words. Names, actions and things. Then there is a separate page where you have to fill out portraits with names and a mad-lib style summary of what happened within the scene. A very simple premise. And yet it consistently seems to perfectly toe the line between too easy and too hard. The information is always there for you, you may need to think slightly outside the box. I never had to look anything up but there were times where I nearly gave up and then re-reviewed the info I had acquired and figured it out. Very satisfying!As you go through each scene and each chapter (~3 scenes to a chapter, I think 4 chapters total + a couple short DLC prequel stories), a full narrative about this golden idol becomes apparent. It's very well done storytelling.If you have even a vague interest, I recommend it for sure. Solid 9/10 maybe 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: left me wanting like 3 dozen more cases. fun as hell. a bit too short, i finished in under 4 hours, and the math puzzle in case 10 was unexpected to say the least but i had a ton of fun, thrilled to see what the devs do next. i wouldn't mind 10 more sequels of this if they're as high quality. a few cases had me quite stumped for like 20-30 minutes. more involved and deeper puzzles would be good too, though i understand the urge to keep it simple instead of needless complication but maybe it's just something to think about for a potential sequel or something. we need more pure deduction games and this scratches a specific itch no game has quite scratched. the sherlock game for when you actually want to be sherlock instead of just following markers like in the actual sherlock games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surreal mystery that'll occupy your mind and have you piecing together a magic-infused 18th century conspiracy. It turned out to be engaging and worth seeing through to the end. I've already recommended it to a friend. But it does need some criticism, and I don't think it ought to be thought of as 'Overwhelmingly Positive'. As can often happen in steam reviews, I've gotta pick "No" for the recommendation, because there isn't something more nuanced. As with all mystery games, there are two phases of play in Case of the Golden Idol: the investigation phase where the player is meant to be figuring out the mystery and the proving phase, where the player demonstrates their understanding and wins that section.The big, nasty hurdle that all mystery games have to tackle is how they intend to handle the proving phase. The game needs to make sure that the mystery isn't spoiled by the method used to test the player. Designing the perfect system to handle the proving phrase has always been a difficult undertaking that has been studied by game journalists and devs, and most mystery games fail at exactly that point. And The Case of the Golden Idol fails there as well. Sometimes, it fails pretty darn hard. It tips its hand at nearly every turn, spoiling answers by the way it asks its questions, by the answer pool it offers you, and by the unblockable feedback it offers. Being a disciplined gamer that refuses to spoil things for themselves won't help. Uniquely, Case of the Golden Idle requires you to pop in and out of the proving phase just so you have an idea of what it is you're intended to be doing in a given scene-- so the big failure point isn't avoidable by trying to play around it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: HIghly recommended. Steam rating is overwhelmingly positive for a good reason - its a puzzle game that builds momentum and never outstays its welcome. This is a point and click deduction game that has style and charm from the start, and slowly builds into an intriguing story of a cursed idol passed down from owner to owner. All the things that you find annoy about puzzle games are gone - its easy to test and adjust answers, you aren't punished by overly complex memory busting puzzles, and you get hints and clues when you are getting close. Just wish this had about 3 more scenes to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Click around a freeze-frame snapshot of a gruesome murder scene, uncover clues and make deductions, then slot keywords Obra Dinn-style into a blank summary of the crime to test your understanding. Fun stuff. There are sub-objectives you can fill in and confirm correct to help you keep track of known information, but I was pleasantly surprised by how much genuine deduction is required to reach the final answers and how much storytelling happens in those moments of realisation. If you're in the market for a detective game that's not afraid to test you a lil bit, it's well worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite gaming experiences in the last few years! There are 11 puzzles (and a couple of small bonus ones) that each take around 20-40 minutes. Some were harder for me than others. The difficulty was perfect as I had to think hard and scrounge for clues, but I never once needed to ask for a 'hint'. The answers are often more convoluted than they first appear, and the game loves things like disguises, secret identities, and red herrings.The format of filling in the blank paragraphs  (e.g., "__ __ went to __ to __ and __ _ for __ while __.") is fantastic. You enter each puzzle absolutely overwhelmed and confused by all these blanks, but it all comes together clearly in the end.It is a short game but absolutely worth the price. Hugely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing breath of fresh air in the world of point and click detective games. I loved it!Difficult, but solvable and deeply satsifying puzzles, incredible story. Good soundtrack, which you will hear plenty of on repeat, if you get stuck in some chapters like me. But it works well and doesn't get boring.Playing DLC will be just a matter of time :^)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Obra Dinn but worse in every way. My biggest gripe is that you solve murders and the killers aren't arrested or otherwise bothered. You have absolutely zero agency over the plot which makes it all meaningless. You are playing as a disembodied fart that smugly says to itself 'ha, this guy murdered this other guy in cold blood' and no one listens or cares.The deductions are fairly simple, but it was a bit fun, but I regret buying it anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, it's so great! The Case of the Golden Idol, and its sinister tale of betrayal and power, are fun and challenging to unravel.Discovering who betrayed whom, and confirming why makes you feel so smart. It's so fun to crack any stage by figuring out how a seemingly insignificant piece of information (from a ciphered letter in the pocket of a servant to the twitching eyelids of a nobleman) fits in the puzzle. Even though the later stages may need a bit of trial and error to get them perfectly right, I did not need any hints to reveal what happened in the end. Every mystery seemed fair and logical and the Epilogue tying any loose ends was the cherry on top. Have fun and always remember to practice the Four Virtues! Glory to Gryphon Reborn!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I managed to get through without hints or guides, so I feel like I played mostly as the devs intended. I just couldn't really say there was any particular moment where I was having fun. I must simply not like this type of game, and I haven't really played others, so I can't tell whether or not this is really better or worse for its genre. Regardless, I would say the story was cheesy, the art and puzzles weren't exactly spectacular, and overall I would not really feel compelled to recommend this game to a friend. I'm sure for people who like this kind of thing, it's probably pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly well-crafted detective game with mystique setting. Most similliar to Return of the Obra Dinn and when you put it side by side there are some crucial differences that make this game stand out on it's own. There is more detective elements here as you have much more to deduce than only to find out what/who killed someone, but while the story was richer I couldn't be as much invested in it as with Obra Dinn as there all the world building was solely by the world. Great game, I wish to see more games that take that direction in deduction games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the old grid-based deduction games you solved with a pencil that used to be in old newspapers, congratulations! You've found the equivalent of that game's puzzle's nicotine patch. TCotGI is loads of craic with a great sense of humour. Some people will hate the art, but it's reminiscent of the early 90s DOS games if you're into that sort of thing. Also proudly evokes the virtues of following your heart, partying with friends, and overthrowing governments. Recommended
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I hope this ushers in a wave of similar games. This takes the deduction mechanics from things like Frogware's Sherlock Holmes games and Tim Follin's Contradiction and streamlines it into a series of incredibly addictive bite-sized vignettes. This game delights at every turn.Visuals are carefully done and wonderfully weird and off-putting. The sound and music are the sleeper killer feature, just wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent point and click investigation game. I've seen some of the other reviews and they often mention games like Return to the Obra Dinn, and it definitely evokes that same feeling of discovery. My only real complaint about these kinds of games is the replayability. Once you've uncovered the mysteries it's hard to forget such a compelling story.The game took me about 6.5 hours to beat. My playtime doesn't reflect that only because I played the demo first, which took 45 minutes or so to complete. When I came back to the full game, I sped through the first few chapters since I remembered the solutions. If you're reading this and not sure if you want to play the game, absolutely check out the demo. If you're like me, you'll play it and instantly want to buy and play the full version.I was surprised at how interested I became with uncovering what was going on between each scenario. There's sort of a metagame of piecing together the clues of what's really going on. You start to spot common things between each chapter, like certain jewelry, related names and faces, and so on. These aren't always relevant to the immediate scenario and could be dismissed as background filler, but in the full context of the game, it all pieces together. I love it.The pixel art was great. It has a lot of personality, and it helps make each character distinct. The music was fun and helped set each scene a little differently. I was stuck in a few parts for a long time and had to listen to the same tunes for the long time, but they never got annoying.The UI can look cluttered and intimidating at times, but it does well to let you organize all of the clues at the bottom of the screen. You can move them around yourself or use a useful button to alphabetize them. Clues also disappear after they are successfully input into the solution "scrolls". Rarely it confused me for a moment since some of the clues are still needed elsewhere, but I had to drag them from their spots on the scroll instead of from the bottom of the screen. Overall, it worked very nicely.The game offers hints if you need them. I thought about using them twice, but the game relentlessly encourages you to face the challenges head on. It even gives you some free helpful advice, like double-checking your choices, changing your point of view, or even taking a break from the game. I ended up not using them out of spite but tried it out afterwards just to see how they are. They seem to really offer you useful hints without spoiling the answer. It's just enough information to keep moving forward if you get stuck.I'm really hoping the developer is able to make more games in this style, or that the success of this game will help inspire others to make similar ones.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: FINALLY! A perfect game has been released. I have played thousands of games in my life and this one has reached my Top 10.If you like a real detective game which an A-M-A-Z-I-N-G story, awesome yet simple characters that you will get to adore, beautiful art, surprises, this game is for you.This is an art experience. This game is inventing a genre, I think we will see many games copying it.It is also very fun to play together with a friend or a partner, trying to deduct the clues together.If you like Return of the Obra Dinn or Her Story, this game is exactly for you. I also recommend playing these two games with a someone else, but it is not a must.IMPORTANT note to enjoy the experience at it's most: please play without using "trial and error" or "hints", the same with the other 2 games I mentioned, the experience is much better if you don't do any try without understanding why you are doing it. It is a limitation of the technology, that you can just try until you get it right, but it erases the fun of this game, and all the clues are visible if you look closely. In the future games with IA will be able to understand whatever you write and this problem of trial and error won't exist.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Golden Idol is the pure essence of the "fill-in-the-blank mystery" genre established by Obra Dinn, and every bit as satisfying and intricate.There's almost nothing bad to say about it. The story is tight and unfolds with careful pacing. It's not too short to be worth the money or so long as to get dull. The most unexpectedly impressive part is the surprisingly cohesive atmosphere, with old-school music, art, and even mechanics that are all a little rough around the edges but all feed into an endearingly low-fidelity experience.No question, if you have any interest in mystery or puzzle games, this is a must-get.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A near-perfect modern adventure/mystery game. The similarities to the Return of the Obra Dinn are obvious, but while this game doesn't have the same tier of grandiose problem-solving and presentation, it does cut down on the little bits of tedium from that game by making these bite-sized mysteries as a part of a larger story. Given that you're in a two dimensional space, it was also much easier to accurately understand all parts of a scene and deduce what happens in each.My only real criticism is that the art style...is an acquired taste. It gets the job done for this type of game though, and it looked better in action for me than the screenshots alone may imply.Overall, I'm hesitant to say that it's a better game than the Return of Obra Dinn, but I'm all for more modern takes on this formula, and hope we see more going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This may have been a shorter game than I'm used to playing, but the storytelling and gameplay make up for it! I don't think I've ever played any other game where there was no protagonist for the player to assume the roll of to help with immersion. Instead, you catch glimpses of scenes as an outsider looking in. The game doesn't even tell you who's who, but instead you can examine characters' pockets, personal items, and locked areas. Solving each case does not change the outcome, but just being able to continue the story feels like its own reward. I found the ending was a little flat, but not everything needed to be complex and convoluted. While there were no protagonists, there were recurring characters and it was fun to see them evolve with the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, scratches my Return of the Obra Dinn itch.The simplest feedback I would give to the developers is working more on the UI. Moving all the words around is the core interaction the player has with the game, and it felt very tedious and clunky. Not the vibe you want when you are building your triumphant Poirot solution speech!Still, absolutely recommend to ANY AND ALL detective/puzzle/mystery fans. Best in the genre since Obra Dinn was released.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game which has streaks of conspiracy, deduction, sleuthing, and which is all tied together in a tight story. If this were a book I would read this, but the game devs actually made a coherent open-ended detective game (a la "Return of the Obra Dinn"). Connections across scenarios slowly build and add up, and there are layers of mystery that are slowly built and revealed, with a lot of the noodlier aspects of the plot left to implication and supposition. Fear not; there is an epilogue scenario to help you make complete sense of it. There is a twist, and I feel like a complete bonehead for not getting it before the final act. A wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic mystery-adventure game. the animation and music are delightful. the setting is unique and is supported by some wonderful world building thats a pretty good representation of 17th century england. the puzzles are never anything too esoteric and can always be solved by critical thinking. my biggest problem is its a bit on the short side (which isn't really that big a deal since it still makes for a fun mystery solving evening)very impressive, hope to see more from this dev!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific detective game that brings me back to playing HyperCard point and click based games on an old early 90's Mac.  All the chapters had a great progression of making me feel like a complete genius solving the first one to referencing pages of handwritten notes for the last one.  I am looking forward to playing the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A must play for anybody who loves detective games and who enjoyed Obra Dinn. Depending on your problem solving skills, it will take around 5-7 hours to completely finish the game. There is a really good story telling, and clues are just excellent. Unlike other point and click games, it is not enough to just randomly click something and hope for the result. You really have to sit down and think about the clues. Brilliant, brilliant game design, well done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely surprised with this game. My suggestion to everyone: If you slow down and take all the time you need to figure out all the small things and details you will get the GREATEST FEELING when you solve what the hell was going on....and that is pure ecstasy my friends. Use your logical brain and if you get stuck and frustrated, quit it for a day and return later, trust me.The only downside is that in the end you will WANT MORE CASES.Thanks to a friend for recommending it to me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A nice clever detective game that packs enough "Aha!" moments to keep you going. There were a few stumbling points midway through the narrative that made me think the game had a few plot holes, but these were eventually cleared up near the end in a clever way. Very much enjoyed it, and I recommend it to anyone who like Obra Din.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A great deductive puzzle game with an intricate plot and interesting art. It strikes the balance between challenge and obscurity of correct answers well. As much as i like games like Ace Attorney, those games have a tedious amount of cut scenes and text. On the other hand, this games goes straight to the interactive good stuff. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game, nice art style and fine writing.The short length works in its favor, as it does not drag on to wear out its welcome the way Obra Dinn does.. Except the DLC actually does do that. The second DLC is poorly designed and written compared to the earlier parts, and the first DLC is somewhat meaningless without the tie-in to the second.So, I'd recommend the base game as a one-shot curiosity.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fill-the-blank mystery game, with a spooky story à-la Return of the Obra Dinn (which is a masterpiece). The music and visuals are great.The full game might take between 4 and 8 hours. Try the demo first, with a caveat: the demo saves are apparently not transferable to the full version. This is not a big issue, as the first scenes are quick to go through once you know the answers.I got stumped a couple times, but the answers never felt too far-fetched and didn't have to use Hints in the end. The game avoids hard difficulty with a couple tools: 1. cut the response board in small blocks with only a limited number of blanks in each block, 2. warn the player when there are only 2 incorrect blanks left, 3. the smaller blocks give useful helpers to fill up the bigger blocks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: After finally going back to play some old classics like The Secret of Monkey Island, I'm more appreciative than ever that this game gives you the choice of whether or not to pixel-hunt and makes the setting easy to toggle on and off.I do agree with some reviewers that the the very last puzzles start getting a little too open-ended. There's challenge you can work through logically, and then there's something that's a big white space that all but requires random guessing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Ah. The detective novel.  All of us have that desire to be the next Sherlock Holmes and solve a murder mystery. The Case of the Golden Idol, if you're not turned off by the supernatural, scratches that itch with fantastic gameplay.The cases work and flow logically and no hints are ever needed (just a keen eye, notebook and diligence) and the story unfolds in front of your eyes. People may complain about the "graphic style" but to be prefectly fair, you aren't purchasing this game for the killer graphics. You're buying this game because you want to solve a mystery.8 hours in the main game with a restart to enjoy playing with my partner. No hints were used. DLC is purchased and next. I'll purchase all subsequent DLCs if you have more!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: What a game! I've seen many compare it to Return of the Obra Dinn and, while I think this is a fair comparison, I think this game more than stands on its own and ends up feeling like a fairly different experience. The mysteries are very well done and I never felt like I had to brute force the solutions with guesses. If you are at all a fan of mysteries, puzzles, or adventure games you should really just play this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The adding and subtracting puzzle was tedious (never ask me to do actual math in a video game) but everything else was excellent, the mysteries difficult enough to feel challenging but not so difficult that you'll be tearing your hair out trying to figure it out. Love a detective game that makes you actually work for the answers. Loved the art style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: if you're into point&click, escape rooms, detective games, this is "The Good Stuff."You have to make use of even the slightest hint and elimination methods to get the answers right, although some cases might seem to be rather difficult, it's surprisingly doable and an enjoyable experience at the same time. Simply by the gameplay itself I'd already give it a 9, on top of it's very unique detecting experience it's also got an intriguing main story line, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Unquestionably worth your time and money. Obviously, most importantly, the mystery is interesting, and the puzzles feel good. There's no classic point-and-click combining everything with everything here. Even the puzzles that I did get stuck on and had to get a hint for (Only two of those for me), they felt like I could have solved them if I just spent a bit more time looking and thinking.The music is wonderful and mood-setting, the graphics are interesting and fun, the gameplay is intuitive, everything about this game is absolutely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I would not say the puzzles in this game are very challenging but do take time to complete. The process of solving each senario is enjoyable never really a dull moment (very important for puzzle games). I enjoy how the scenarios get progressively more challenging while also developing the story I never really know what going to happen next.The graphics and soundtrack are great quality making it easy to stay playing for long periods of time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I'm playing this game side-by-side with my puzzle-fan 12-year-old daughter. We're having a blast! It's so much fun to find and work out the clues. Many of the puzzles are tough, but most are solvable without help. Our experience is that we play in shorter sessions (around 20 minutes), and make a little progress each time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Want more Obra Dinn? BUY THIS.Want a deduction game but found Obra Dinn too hard? BUY THIS.Want a deduction game and haven't played Obra Dinn? BUY THIS. (It will ease you into the deduction mindset better)While I love Obra Dinn, I love Case of the Golden Idol a lot more. Having each case be its own separate entity means I get frustrated a lot less and that dopamine hit that much sooner. The story is interesting and has a very satisfying ending, and it's great fun to go back to previous cases and see all the hidden details. I really hope the developer makes more games in this style!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is my kind of game and I absolutely adore it! It scratches that mystery solving itch that so many other games can’t. It makes you take in every detail presented to you and really think to figure out the solution. If you love Return of the Obra Dinn then this game is for you. I loved the pixel art style. The music really sets the tone.  The game play is unique unlike anything else I have ever played. I want more as soon as possible! The game features 11 cases to solve each with increasing scope and difficulty. It does a good job at teaching you the mechanics through game play and ramping up the difficulty at a good pace.  Each case further progresses the overarching narrative of the game. This overarching narrative really gripped me and had me wanting to know more after each case.  The game is only 4-6 hours long and I know this style of game play isn’t for everyone. That being said I would encourage anyone to download the demo and give it a go. You won’t be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and cool game. Can be pretty short depending on how well you can solve the mysteries and if you use the hint system, but it took my nearly 6 hours to beat with no hints and no guidance (choosing to have the game underline clues or not). Whether you wait for a bigger sale, or pick it up now, I think it is very worth to play through this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Played this after Obra Dinn and enjoyed my time with it. A nifty set of core mechanics each scene was satisfying to solve. Its art and music punch above their weight, although the overall experience falls short of Obra Dinn's high watermark. And its politics are under-cooked, which is a particular let down given the stories final vignette features .Fellow steam-link/PS5 controller players may want to give this one a miss, unless you have alternatives. The UI seems designed primarily for touch screens (not sure if they're actually supported), followed by mouse and keyboard, with controller support an afterthought.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: My Favorite puzzle game of all time. Such creative and engaging storytelling. Having repeat characters is such a fantastic way to simultaneously drive forward a narrative and provide clues for the puzzle. And, like any good mystery, there are bits of seemingly unimportant information that elegantly becomes important when looking back. The DLC doubly so!I also love how much the story spirals in exponential fashion. So fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great challenging game that is not impossible. This definitely scratched my point and click adventure game itch. A literary puzzle with interesting characters, story, and great art. If you liked this one check out Hob's Barrow. Very much in the same vein and has the same freaky pixel art.Edit: The DLCs were just as great and provide some wonderful context to the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle game, right up there with titles like Obra Dinn and Talos Principle, but be warned that it is very short and like most puzzle games has no replay value. I tend to go through these kinds of games a little fast and had already done the first four chapters in the demo so was able to speed through them on release and my final play time was four hours, I imagine the average play time will end up being somewhere around 6-7 but the quality of those hours will be the best you'll probably find in any puzzle game this year or the next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game if you enjoy a good mystery. This game really makes you feel like a detective investigating the scene of the crime. Trying to find evidence and solving the crime feels very rewarding.The graphics are full of pixelated charm and a slightly creepy vibe. A similar effect is created by the music which has a worthy soudtrack.The gameplay is very enganging as your really need to investigate and think about each scene to solve it.This is certainly one of the best detective games ever. Totally recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Golden Idol got me thinking about the tougher crime scenes throughout the day when I wasn't playing and I LOVED that about it. Proper head scratchers that you need to sleep on if you're like me and determined to get through the game without any online aid. Speaking of, the hint system is probably the LEAST generous I've ever encountered. And I mean that as a compliment. Just gentle nudges in the right direction.The story is just the right amount of disturbing, like the character designs themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: "The Case of the Golden Idol" is so, so, SO good. I'd probably place it in my top 20 favourite games of all time, and that says a lot. You should get it if it looks interesting at all to you, I guarantee you'll be entertained.The thing I love about it the most is that it's not super flashy, meaty, and filled to the brim with 200h of content. And this is all actually its biggest strength. It never tries to be more than it is, it never overstays its welcome, and never makes empty promises. It's masterfully and *very precisely* crafted to be the best version of itself, not more, not less.And oh boy. The visual, music, story, and puzzles, all work together super well and compliment each other, creating an absurd, challenging, dark, and a bit creepy experience - from the beginning to the very end. I haven't seen a game this consistent and solid in many, many years. It's a huge game design accomplishment, especially considering it's Color Gray's debut.The story and the puzzles are especially worth highlighting, because that's where most games from the mystery/detective genre suffer the most. This one gets eveyrthing right. The story is fascinating, the characters can be very interesting and funny, and the puzzles can be *actually* difficult and always very logical at the same time. They tingled my brain in all the right places.I was gripped and I'm amazed and I *long* for more. I'll buy whatever Color Gray make next. I'd insta-buy ten of those if I could.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: It didn't take me too long to finish but I genuinely enjoyed the mysteries and sorting it out. Just by trying to find the clues to work out who each character was my brain was making connections to solve the mystery of each case. Just challenging enough that you feel smart by solving it but not so challenging that you give up.And it wasn't until like the second last and last mystery when my brain started making connections between two characters that spoke to an overarching mystery that I didn't even know was there, pulling the individual cases together that brings it to one coherent story that doesn't spoon-feed you the answers but makes you feel very satisfied when you get to the right conclusions yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Most of this game is collecting information, putting it together and forming theories. Disproving myself and coming to new conclusions made this game a thoroughly enjoyable experience. For anyone with an interest to puzzle/detective games this is a must. The DLC is a nice addition. Some scenarios need paper and pen (I have 4 pages filled) Going to try Obra Dinn based on recommendations from reviews on here
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good for those who are sorely craving something similar to 'Return of the Obra Dinn'. I would rank this game as easier than Obra Dinn, but not to the point where it is easy. The game definitely makes you work for answers. There is the availability of hints, but I personally didn't use any during my gameplay. Solid 8/10, may there be more detective games like this and Obra Dinn.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A greatly crafted mystery solving game. While each case has you retrace a murder, extra clues in them build the world and foreshadow future connections. that tie the whole thing into one overarching story with a neat bow.The art style, animation and sound design work together to make the static scenes come to life and recurring characters are presented well and have their own little sideplots through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game with interesting story which develops over time.Gameplay-wise it's somewhat similar to Obra Dinn but with less time spent on just walking around. You just have the whole scene in front of your eyes and all the clues are there, you just need to connect them into a story.Not to hard, not to simple, just right in the middle, a little quest to entertain you during some evening. Definitely worth it's money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game in the style of Obra Dinn.  Not too long and not too difficult.Each level is a freeze frame scene right after an event.  Starting a level, you won't know how the event happened, or even who some of the people are.  You click around the scene to view things like books, notes, the contents of cabinets, or even people and the contents of their pockets.  This gains you enough info to identify each person and fill in a description of the event.  The game is good about confirming/rejecting your solution in small chunks so you'll know if you're close, or way off.It's a simple idea, but I haven't seen it done often.  Even though this feels inspired by Obra Dinn, it has its own interesting style and isn't a copy.  I've heard complaints about the art, but I thought it worked well for this game and its atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Very Different from what i excepted it be. Thought it was some kind of adventure game. But i unexpectedly (And pleasantly) got taken on a very interesting mission of intrigue and discovery. Highly recommend for anyone who likes to try to figure out situations by observations. Definitely kind of game in which you play, possibly get stuck, then come up with solution after sleeping on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Neither of the DLCs are working and I can't get a refund, so partly thumbs down.- Fantastic mystery full of excellent characters, murder, conspiracies, double-crossing, dark secrets, political upheaval... and the Occult!- Clues are everywhere. To get through them all, you will need to patient and have intermediate powers of logic, observation, memory, deduction etc... as with all the best games- It has just the right amount of creepiness and humour- Beautifully designed and inspired by 18th-century British history/geopolitics/cultureLoved this game so much. Very rewarding, plenty of content for your buck.Extra points for the dead mermaid baby hybrid thingy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The demo alone was enough to convince me that this game was great, everything informs your understanding of the various cases and the plug in nature of all the clues is surprisingly intuitive, every kernel of information is useful in solving the cases, and it rewards you for paying close attention to everything. I sincerely hope that there is more coming in the future, be it DLC, a sequel or a game set in  a completely different world using similar mechanics. Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game for those that like to do the detective work. The cases are hard enough but still possible to reason and solve, giving a very rewarding feeling when solving them. Also, the developers made good use of information obtained in previous chapters, linking them into future chapters in such a way that makes it a very entertaining story at the end of the game. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: A detective game in the vein of "Obra Din", where you first have to find the clues by clicking on text and objects in the scene and then drag those clues into the slots in the verdict text.The story is interesting, with twists and turns. Tough i found it a bit confusing to tie the diffrent scenes together time-vise. And i easily forget names. The interface is also a bit clunky, both going back to previous clues, but also entering the words.Overall i prefer "Obra Din", but really enjoyed this game too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Case of the Golden Idol is one of the only games I'm aware of that has tried to do something like Return of the Obra Dinn, and it's mostly successful in capturing a touch of that magic. That's not to say this is on the same level as Obra Dinn, but it's still an enjoyable 5 or so hours of playing detective and piecing together what's happening in each scene following the story of those that possess the golden idol.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Return of the Obra Dinn then you will almost certainly enjoy the investigator vibes of this game. I also want to emphasize the great improvements of the DLC which include longer looping OST tracks (which were already good in the original but now are great) in conjunction with more complex puzzles at the start pls animated characters in the text voice over boxes. I really hope to see further development and expansion on this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite detective games since the Return of the Obra Dinn. The art style is unique and the puzzles are challenging, yet incredibly engaging. There's no brute-forcing your way through this title; it requires your full attention and demands your critical thinking skills to be firing on all cylinders. It even has an amazingly catchy soundtrack to boot.I feel incredibly grateful to have been a part of the development and testing of this game. I can't wait to see what these developers do next.Now stop reading this review and go purchase The Case of the Golden Idol! You'll thank me later.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This game was literally.. wow.. great. So well thought out. I have about 6 pages front and back of notes, and I LOVED that I had to refer to old notes to figure some stuff out. As the story came together, things started clicking in place and multiple times I went to previous chapters and had huge "OMG" or "AHA" moments for the current chapter based on well-thought out and well-placed things within the scene. It took me until the 2nd to last chapter to figure out the TWIST once I went back and forth through chapters a couple times -- Like "where did this random Lazarus Herst guy come from idgi" then OMG it hit me so hard like 2-3 chapters later and I had to go back through each chapter looking at everything to mentally connect all the dots - HOLY MOLEY. I literally need more games like this. I don't understand why a great deduction (solo-player!) investigation game is SO hard to find. This is easily now in my top 3 favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun mystery game! I found the overall story a bit tough to follow and the lack of being able to easily reference the characters from previous chapters. Having to toggle between chapters constantly was a bit of a pain and while it's true to the classics of the genre its referencing, I really would have appreciated some kind of quality of life notebook that would make it easier to track and *potentially* something that connected the chapters together with a story more explicitly.That being said, I highly highly recommend this game. It's true to the genre and my nitpicks have more to do with the delta between contemporary game design/player expectations and the classic genre this game is designed in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible puzzle design, with a thriving a captivating  visual narrative (the aesthetics of the graphics is amazing), that keeps you hooked. I love the attention to detail on some of the puzzles. My only problem with the game is that the mechanic of filling up the blank spaces with words can get pretty old and easy to brute-force. Regardless one of the best detective games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: This was super fun if relatively short. Basically this is an old school logic problem puzzle book adapted to computers with some cool pixel art and a great overarching story.  You essentially read all the clues hidden on the screen and then place the right answers in their boxes using deduction. Definitely worth the price and I am hopeful for more along these lines!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the best games I've ever played. Pulling together all the pieces of the puzzle was definitely challenging, especially in the later acts, but by golly, it felt so rewarding when you got there. I found that all of the mysteries were solvable without using hints or trying to brute force the answer with changing out words, but solving the puzzles in Act 3 & 4 did require me to grab a notebook and write out connections and theories. It would have been cool if the game provided you with a wee pixel notepad to do this on your own so that all your deductions and clues were in the same place, but that's probably my only feedback. Can't wait to see what these developers do next!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The only game I've ever played that's inspired me to write a review. I loved it! The gameplay, the writing, the graphics all fit together. What I liked best was that the game was structured enough that it felt puzzle-like to figure out & solve each case, but there was a much larger mystery to solve that the game doesn't hold your hand for at all .. you just put it together as you go along. Also the writing was just very sharp, funny, and smart. Cannot recommend highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with my boyfriend and we had a really great time solving the puzzles in this game, as well as learning the story and uncovering the mystery. We thought it would be like the Return of the Obra Dinn, but it's different in a lot of ways that makes it stand out. The visuals are unique and the story/music are fun. As the story progresses, the difficulty increases and the more scenes you get to explore for each chapter. My only complaint is that I wish this game was longer! I think it took us a couple of nights to solve all the puzzles, but it was a great time nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I love all types of puzzles games, but I found this rather difficult - which is a very good thing!The types of puzzles games I've played before are akin to brain teasers, where I have to figure out how to release a mechanism from another etc (Refer to "The Room" games for visual explanation). I am quite new to "whodunit" style of puzzle games so this really had my head scratching. But I thoroughly enjoyed it and will definitely play other games like this. I have played both the main game and the DLCs !
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: The Case of the Golden Idol is a story about how an ancient artifact get in the wrong hands and all hell breaks loose.This is a puzzle game similar to a detective investigation where you have to piece together the details of the story in order to understand it. The clues you get to understand the story are the characters, their dialogue and the items they have on them. The story of this game is really enticing and I couldn't put it down until I finished it whole. Another thing worth mentioning is that, you as a player are just an observer. You have no power in this game other than figuring out what happened, when it happened and who it happened to. It's honestly a refreshing take of this genre and I absolutely love that every minor character matters in the grand scheme of things.No human being would be sane if they actually had this golden idol in their hand. The power would instantly go through their head and they would hunger over power and greed. It's a human condition and the game presents it beautifully.The DLCs are prequels to the main story, the order of them being: The Spider of Lanka and then The Lemurian Vampire. I honestly believe that The Spider of Lanka has an over all better story than The Lemurian Vampire, but it is still worth playing them both to get the full story. I highly recommend this game if you're into murder mysteries and piecing evidence together. I'm very excited for the sequel as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game with a friend a month again, and it was incredible. Not only the figuring out part to find the connections was incredible, but the fact you went one step above, and it's not obvious what's happened, you're trying to figure out motives and ideas and other things. This alone sets this game millions of leagues away from other games for me  I specifically bought this game to support the developers to make more games like this. Please do, I'm craving more games like that (and yes, I played DLCs already, they were also fantastic, except the stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moon orientation)
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, it gets a bit too complicated at the end and it can be challenging on people with my dyslexia when these empty boxes come up more and you almost have to piece together the *entire* thing and the words start to blend but that's moreso a me thing. Just a solid heads up to anyone else with mid/severe dyslexia.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Great detective, mystery game.  This game has the pleasure of making you have to think about both the individual case you are trying to solve, but understand the bigger picture.  It is not the most groundbreaking story or anything, but I loved the mysteries of finding out about each death.  Also, the graphics were wonderful.  9/10, highly recommend it if you like point and click detective games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the most addictive mystery games I have ever seen. You follow the tragedies and schemes of those pursuing the Golden Idol, a mysterious artifact with fabled abilities. You are shown frozen moments, most often when there is a murder involved, and have to examine every inch of the scene to decipher what happened. You get to look inside people's coats, examine paintings and rulebooks, and pick up clues from delightfully clever riddles. Backstabbing and betrayal, secret societies and strange rituals, and so much more! I highly recommend for fans of  and for any gumshoe who enjoys a story-rich narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: As hundreds of others have said already... If you liked obra dinn, you'll love this game. Very unique art style, immersive story and makes you feel like a brainiac when you manage to piece all the clues together! My only frustration is that now I've finished it, I'm craving more and there's isn't much in the way of replay value!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't many investigation games that really make you think, and then actually make sense when you figure everything out. It's challenging without ever feeling unfair.You can kinda cheat when you've got most of a scene solved, by using process of elimination to figure out the last couple of details. I'll admit I did this a few times when I was stumped, but then I always went back and figured out how I was SUPPOSED to get that answer. The clues were always there in plain sight, I just missed them until I had a better idea of what I was looking for. Honestly, outstanding puzzle design.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better point-and-click mystery games I've played.  Fun story and a good level of challenge once you get past the first few cases.  It felt a bit short, I think the main story took about 5 1/2 hours to finish without any hints, but I enjoyed my time.  I do think the price is fair with the DLC and I do hope they make another.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: How can I phrase this nicely: you probably won't like this game. If you're a puzzle diehard, then this will/should have been on your radar, and this review mostly doesn't concern you.But if you only occasionally play puzzle games, this will leave you wanting. The base game is pretty good -- a fairly smooth, deduction-based puzzle game that tells stories in quite interesting ways. The only downside -- almost certainly whined about relentlessly in the devs' Discord -- is that the base game is somewhat easy. For you, the non-puzzle player, that's a good thing: "somewhat easy" will still be 7-9hrs (among 11 scenarios) of piecing together a twisting, turning story.And then there's the DLCs. Induction-based, primarily. "Harder", with ___ more ___ and even more ____, not just ____ but also _____, leading ____ to _____. (Phrases: "red herrings", "significantly", "waste", "dollar", "money", "phrases", "time", .......) You get the picture: completing scenarios/panels becomes more about eliminating useless possibilities and testing out "theory groupings". You also have to metagame like an absolute madman if you want to get the DLC done semi-quickly.Do not waste money on the DLC unless you just like completing hard things for the sake of it. This is not a very popular game, so there's no one to impress.Base game: 8/10 (accounting for difficulty, 7.5/10)DLC 1 (Spider of Lanka): 5/10 -- very disappointing, contains the worst kind of puzzle errors: errors that are extremely obvious and yet the developers are adamant that they're intentionalDLC 2 (Lemurian Vampire): 6/10. If you enjoy Friday/Saturday NYT crosswords, this is clearly a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

_childDocuments_.review: Gave this a shot after seeing it in a "best of 2022" article - easy to pickup and very rewarding. Was hooked right from the get go. By the end of it, was not just the puzzle solving that I was enjoying but the evolution of the story itself From seeing the other reviews, it appears Obra Dinn will be next on my list!
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

I'm always itching for a 'pure' deduction game, and this one's good enough that I'll buy whatever Color Gray Games makes next. Seriously.The gameplay mechanic is brilliantly intuitive, and the mysteries are challenging without ever resorting to gimmicks. Also SO satisfying when the story starts to come together. Brb going to go recommend this to everyone I know lmao
_childDocuments_.name: The Case of the Golden Idol

Art was different and a bit reminiscent of old Lucas Arts games. For me it was quite challenging sometimes but I realized later that I needed to slow down and pay close attention to everything.
