_childDocuments_.review: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition is a remaster of the Blade Runner point-and-click game. Taking place during the first movie, we play as Ray McCoy, a Blade Runner investigating his own cases separate from Rick Deckard. There are several characters from the movie who made cameos, and most of them (sadly not Gaff) are voiced by their original actors. The artwork and atmosphere are surprisingly faithful to the movie.Despite being labeled a remaster, the graphics are the issue most people had with this game. Yes, it's not pixelated, but the levels look all smudgy and blurry, which honestly makes it uglier. Some of the textures are just gone, decreased details replaced by smudgy colors. The character models themselves, however, are not changed and stay pixelated, making them look out of place. Luckily, you can toggle this feature on/off by pressing Q, and it works everywhere, even mid-cutscenes, which for most of the time works fine with the enhanced graphics as the smudge aren't too apparent and has smoother framerate.Being an old game, don't expect it to be as clear as newer ones. Sometimes there's no indicator of what you could do, so you would have to find clues yourself. Whether it be talking to other people, finding stuff from an Esper-analyzed photo, or a pixel-hunting object you might have missed. Be prepared to consult a guide if you wanna play with less headache. They say the interface is changed to be more user-friendly, but it would be nice if they'd show interactable objects.One interesting thing is that there's some kind of randomizer for every playthrough. Like for example, character A might be human during your first run, but a Replicant in your second. Of course, there will be different dialogues and clues that might indicate that. Some characters can be in one place in one time during one run, but not in the other. This can be both a blessing and a curse, makes each playthrough unique but can also be confusing.Overall, I think the Blade Runner point-and-click game is a pretty great game, and if you like these kind of games, or just wanting more Blade Runner/cyberpunk world content you should definitely give it a try. I recommend playing mostly using the original graphics though, switching to enhanced ones only if you wanna see how it looks like. Also, don't forget to save often since some events can result in game-over and you restart from the start of the Act.

_childDocuments_.review: The "Blade Runner" game, released in 1997 by Westwood Studios, is often praised for several key aspects that contributed to its positive reception: The game is lauded for its atmospheric recreation of the dystopian world from the 1982 film. The visuals, especially for the time, were highly detailed, with impressive pre-rendered backgrounds and weather effects that enhanced the noir feel of the game. The game's story, set parallel to the events of the film, was another strong point. Players appreciated the depth and complexity of the narrative, which featured multiple endings depending on the choices made. This branching storyline provided a high level of replayability. The game introduced a unique real-time element, where characters and events would progress independently of the player's actions. This created a dynamic and immersive experience that was ahead of its time. The investigation mechanics, where players gathered clues, conducted interviews, and used the Voight-Kampff test to determine if characters were human or replicants, were also highly praised. The soundtrack, inspired by Vangelis' original score from the movie, and the sound effects were integral in building the game's mood. The voice acting was also well-received, contributing to the overall immersion. Over time, the game has garnered a cult following, with many fans appreciating its faithful adaptation of the Blade Runner universe. The recent re-release of the game in enhanced editions has reignited interest and brought it to a new generation of players. The game features several characters from the 1982 film, adding depth and authenticity to the experience: The enigmatic, origami-loving Blade Runner, voiced by Edward James Olmos, appears in the game. He serves as a link between the game’s protagonist, Ray McCoy, and the events of the film. The replicant with implanted memories also makes an appearance, further tying the game’s narrative to the movie. Dr. Eldon Tyrell, the head of the Tyrell Corporation, plays a role in the game, adding to the intrigue surrounding the replicants. The genetic designer from the film is present, with his home serving as a key location in the game. The replicant from the film's iconic Voight-Kampff scene appears in the game, adding to the sense of continuity between the game and the movie. One of the most innovative features was its real-time gameplay, where the story and world progressed even if the player didn’t take action. This created a more immersive experience compared to typical adventure games of the time. The game randomly assigned roles (human or replicant) to key characters at the start of each playthrough, making each experience unique as characters could be allies or enemies depending on the randomization. The game used a voxel-based graphics engine, allowing for detailed character models and lifelike animations. This technology was quite advanced for its time. The original source code was lost, complicating efforts to re-release the game. However, a dedicated team reverse-engineered it to create an enhanced edition, released in 2022. Developers worked closely with Syd Mead, the concept artist for the original film, ensuring the game's environments faithfully represented the film's visual style.These aspects contribute to the game’s lasting legacy in the cyberpunk genre, where it is still appreciated for its depth, innovation, and adherence to the source material.

_childDocuments_.review: Long lost in the ether following Westwood having literally misplaced the original source code, it seemed that Westwood's Blade Runner would forever be a forgotten gem. But, reverse engineering of the game had a different fate in mind, while sadly delivering results that would be met with less than warm appraisal. Yes, Nightdive's reverse engineer of the Westwood classic is deeply flawed; the visual presentation has suffered, audio cues are missing, the shooting gallery is inoperative, substantial chunks of dialogue are muted, and the shooting mechanic is extremely mixed when it comes to its responsiveness. But, it would be wrong to think of this re-issue as a failure. The game can be completed from start to finish, and the bare mechanics for the game to operate are in working order. But, for what was meant to be a labour of love, Nightdive have certainly under delivered. Thankfully, the game is also bundled with both the original CD-ROM version of the game with the fan restored content. So, while Nightdive's "enhancement" is something of a disappointment, the original game has been bundled with this release. Blade Runner, for newcomers, is a point and click adventure game based on the Ridley Scott cult classic. The protagonist, Ray McCoy, is the Deckard of the story, a Blade Runner. The game features a variety of settings and modes which allow for maximum replayability. For starters, players can opt as to the personality type of Ray McCoy, while also having the option to manually select dialogue options which they feel are relevant to their investigation. Each interaction, every kill (all in real time) creates the opportunity to access unique story paths, and endings. Blade Runner, in terms of its cyberpunk narrative branching and control of the story, is very much Deus Ex before Deus Ex but in a point and click adventure format (with some real time action sequences). As a piece of interactive story telling and gameplay, the game has aged gracefully in its simple but effective mechanics. Sadly, the visuals have dated poorly but this is to do with the fact that Blade Runner's rendering, upon release, was software based. Blade Runner was never developed with dedicated 3D accelerators for the time. But, what the game may lack in its visual clarify is more than made up for with superb voice acting (featuring Blade Runner alumni including Sean Young, James Hong, and the late Joe Turkel) and overall atmosphere with its iconic Vengelis soundtrack. Overall, Blade Runner is absolutely recommended for those who either do not already own a copy, or have a copy that they are unable to operate on a modern operating system. For those who already are able to play the original classic, the Enhanced Edition has nothing to offer, and is best avoided. Two scores:Original/Restored Version - 5 out of 5Nightdive's Enhanced edition - 1 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad to say it's bad. Blade Runner was one of my favorite games growing up and it's the reason Blade Runner is my favorite film now. But this port is basically kind of a mess. It feels like it's an emulator wrapped around the game and up-scaled with a blurry filter. Whether that  makes the pre-rendered screens look better is a matter of preference, but there's a lot of problems otherwise.Basically the two good things are: The KIA interface looks better and you can scroll with the mouse wheel. The other thing is the subtitles (except they take up too much screen space, and I don't think all of them are correct, probably because the original script is long gone).The bad is everything else. From the first scene I was disappointed. Clicking on the ground did not make McCoy walk. Though that problem only existed in the first scene, other scenes seemed to be okay. The fact that the 3D models weren't enhanced in any way kind of makes you question the "enhancement" at all. They are still the same low-res voxel technology that always stood out like a sore thumb against the pre-rendered backgrounds. To it's credit, the game was playable from start to finish without any show-stopping bugs, but there were cosmetic bugs throughout. Some of the cosmetic bugs were in the original version of the game, but may have been less noticeable due to the lower resolution, but some are definitely new to this port, for example a lot of objects showing through the background etc. There were audio bugs as well, I encountered one where the love theme for Lucy started playing and wouldn't stop long after that interaction was over, and even saving the game, quitting to the desktop, and loading the game again still kept the incorrect music playing. You also can't change McCoy's behavior after you start the game (or at least I couldn't figure out how to, and even though I chose Erratic it seemed to be User Choice anyway.)I think just looking at the main menu is kind of an indicator that this is a dud. It's these ugly square boxes slapped on some weird concept art with a McCoy that doesn't even look like the guy from the original game.There is a version on  which is the ScummVM version. That version is much more faithful to the original and overall feels better.I supposes Nightdive realized this was sub-par which is why it's on 10 bucks in the US. I didn't even know about this version of the game until the day before it came out, so it doesn't seem like they were too keen on advertising it. Realistically if you're already a fan you might as well get this one just to see what it's about, just don't expect your mind to be blown.Realistically the only good remaster of this game would be to recreate it will all new graphics assets in a 3D Engine like Unreal or something. Probably the only thing to keep from the original game would be the audio and voices. But doing something like that would probably cost more than it would ever make back (if it was made with any kind of quality).

_childDocuments_.review: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition: A Classic Retro-Adventure Reborn in Neon LightsBlade Runner: Enhanced Edition offers a profound nostalgia trip back to the golden era of adventure games. Originally developed by the iconic Westwood Studios—creators of classics like "The Legend of Kyrandia" and "Lands of Lore"—this game is a testament to the studio's legacy in pioneering rich narrative experiences.As a Blade Runner, you are equipped with investigative skills and tools essential for navigating a world that feels alive. The game showcases revolutionary lighting and visual effects that breathe life into its environment, making it one of the most immersive settings ever crafted in video game history. While the Enhanced Edition aims to modernize the visual experience, it somewhat misses the mark. The enhancements often overshadow finer details, potentially detracting from the original aesthetic. However, playing the game without these enhancements brings back the cherished nostalgic vibe that many fans appreciate.The storyline is exceptional, rivaling the narrative depth and complexity of the original "Blade Runner" film. Players will find themselves weaving through storylines that intersect with familiar characters and iconic locations from the movie. The gameplay is challenging, with a dynamic narrative that shifts based on your decisions and actions, ensuring a unique experience for every player.Final Verdict:"Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition" is a remarkable journey back in time. Despite some flaws in the visual updates, the game’s core experience remains untouched, offering a blend of nostalgia and deep, adaptive gameplay that stands the test of time. After 31 years, it continues to be a captivating adventure worth exploring.Score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: [Second Patch Edit - the purchase now comes bundled with a "classic edition", aka ScummVM version, and a toggle to use the old graphics on Enhanced Edition. While the recent patch did improve some stuff, overall there are still a bunch of rough visuals spots, so while I do consider this game worth playing, I encourage buying it for ScummVM's version, or use the classic toggle on Enhanced Edition. Original review below.]It’s too bad it doesn't live up.I get that the source code was lost, I get preserving this game by reversing it wasn't a small feat, I get the game is a bizarre technical nightmare on how it uses the voxels or whatever hell they are.I was still expecting better from NightDive. I sincerely cannot imagine anyone there looking at this and thinking it was acceptable.Let me be perfectly clear- Blade Runner is one of the best PC games you can play of the era, but just please do yourself a favor and go enjoy it on ScummVM. It's not just the small changes to movement, UI, interactables, ugly font and alike that bother me the most, it's how the visuals have been absolutely butchered due to changes in the way environmental elements (like fog) works, how the models are rendered and the hard contrast between the two- it's incredibly distracting and off-putting. It genuinely would have been better to keep everything rather compressed or compensate with similar visual tricks to mask at that point.The original Blade Runner and it's sequel are by far some of the most gorgeous visual feasts in cinema, a triumph of craftsmanship, atmosphere and design, the eternally resonant monologue by Roy in particular is easily one of the most beautiful scenes in any movie ever made- and this gem of a game lovingly captured all of that. Something this title lost in its enhancement to the point of insult.I don't know if something got messy in the end, and I hope to God almighty this can be saved or at least compensated a bit, because more people should play this game.And hell, if you don't care about any of this, fine, the game still works and is easily accessible- I am sadly incapable of recommending it if you even care a little about the actual experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "I'm walking through the desert when I see this developer lying on its back, belly baking in the hot sun -- kicking their legs, trying to turn themselves over, but they can't -- and I'm not helping....I kick some sand into their eyes for good measure."CAVEAT EMPTOR...If you are running an outdated GPU (such as ATI 5870 or 6970) the Enhanced Edition will not function properly -- even though you are within minimum specs.This is due to an error in "Shader Model 4" that Nightdive Studios is unwilling/unable to fix.(  )OTHERWISE...They have patched this title since its very poor launch -- and both the Enhanced & Standard Editions will work for everyone(else).  You can buy this title with confidence!  You take the role of Ray McCoy -- Blade Runner rookie.Uncover the identities of a rogue band of Replicants, in a narrative that takes place alongside that of the original film from 1982.  Several actors reprise their roles, here, and while gameplay can get repetitive due to limited scene structure, your choices matters and will lead to a variety of outcomes...This newly 'Enhance Edition' offers Steam Achievements, a modern overlay, and a smoothed-out/upscaled GFX renderer that reduces the original art to some smudging -- but 'Classic Mode' for the original graphics experience is thankfully just a keystroke ('Q') away.Controls are of a simple mouseclick/pixel-hunting variety-- so your off-hand is free to enjoy a tumbler of whiskey, or two, by saxophone.There is also a "Classic Edition' included with the Steam purchase, which is a basic ScummVM port.Both editions include an option to experience extra content, but bugs may be introduced that way.This is a great game, and well-worth your money & time!. . .It isn't called murder -- it's called retirement.

_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I played the "enhanced" option. This is an old-school point-n-click adventure. The art, voices, music, and story are very good. But, the graphics are extremely dated. The "enhancement" is simply a blur filter which removes detail from scenes. I do prefer it blurred since it cleans up rough pixelation, but there are times when the blur effect will make a cityscape look like a cave (you can toggle the effect on/off at any time). I would never have completed the game without a walk-thru. There is no quest journal or guide in the game. I ran around aimlessly until it triggered some progress. There are many actors from the 1982 Blade Runner movie and the scenes stay very true to the source. I generally can't recommend this, but hardcore Blade Runner fans will appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The enhanced edition gets a lot of hate but I didn't have any of the problems that people have reported. My understanding is that the bugs were fixed. This also includes the two other versions that you can play, but only the Enhanced Version allows you to obtain achievements. Over all this is a fun experience and if you're a fan of Blade Runner then you'll like the story. There are multiple endings and every play through allows for a new experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This review was originally negative but the comments were really helpful, I gave the game another try and starting to understand how this style of game works. It's a very well made game. Thank you to everyone who left a comment. Original review:Believe it or not, , not the remaster. I'm playing the original ScummVM version that got added after the remaster turned out so awful. (btw, thank you to whoever added subtitles to the original version.)I like Blade Runner, I like detective games, I've played point-and-click detective games before, but I just can't get into this one. The game gives you ZERO direction on what to do, where to go, what to pick up, if you missed something, what order to do things in, I looked up several walkthroughs and they all say to do different things, I don't get it. No hints, nothing. I'm not saying the game needs to spell it out for me, but some of this evidence is so minute and easy to miss that I flat out missed it and didn't know it was there. Like the shell casings on the floor, I never would've thought to check there or if there was a gun in the first place (there wasn't one in the opening cutscene). The walkthroughs said there was also a candy bar, I couldn't find it anywhere. And the photo enhancers, how the hell would I have known the girl had an ankle bracelet? I can't read the game's mind! At least when looking around environments for clues, the cursor turns green when hovering over something you can click on. And then I got flat-out stuck on the part where you confront the sushi chef and chase him, just leads me to a locked door and dead end. The walkthroughs say he's supposed to jump down from the ceiling and attack me, but nothing. Just a locked door. I'm NOT saying the game is bad, especially considering that it's considered a great game and cult classic. It got (poorly) remastered for a reason, after all. The game looks great for its time with its Resident Evil-style pre-rendered environments, and absolutely nails the overall Blade Runner vibe, right down to the slow pacing. I think it's cool that they even brought back the "artificial animals" subplot from the original novel (Philip K ♥♥♥♥'s , which was the basis for Blade Runner). I just shouldn't feel frustrated playing this game. I was looking forward to it, only to end up putting it down almost immediately. Maybe I'll come back to it, most likely not. Maybe point-and-click games just aren't my thing, I dunno. TL;DR game does a piss-poor job of telling you where to go, what to do, if you missed any clues, etc. I was completely lost and ended up getting stuck with no idea how to fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: I own both the GoG and this version.  I ran both at 720x480 (side by side) and here's my quick analysis.Visuals: GoG > Steam (only slightly and even at 5120x1440)Sound: GoG = SteamKIA menu = GoG < Steam (steam has a high res menu)Movement = GoG = Steam (I don't know what people are talking about not being able to walk freely.  I can walk to the same places on the GoG version)Compatibility: GoG < Steam (My GoG version doesn't close properly most times and requires me to end GoG.  I have no such issues with the Steam version.  Plus it works with the Steam deck.Notes:Steam desk... for mouse clicks you have to configure a mouse button since the touchscreen is not calibrated.Personally, I don't think there's anything wrong with this version.  The graphical different is so minor because of how dated they look anyway.  Anyway, I loved the game back in the 90's and will enjoy it again.  And, I can even play it on the go.

_childDocuments_.review: Read a detailed review here: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition has managed to ruin the unique aesthetic and feel of the original largely thanks to an inaccurate AI-upscaling method and some questionable design choices. To be honest, the only ‘upgrade’ in the remaster over the original is the addition of cutscenes and controller support. The decision to de-list the original from GOG was also a crappy move. But, as an apology, Nightdive is giving away the original, titled Blade Runner Classic when you purchase the Enhanced Edition on Steam. But, if the only selling point of your remaster is the ability to play the unaltered version, then what’s the point of remastering it in the first place? That being said, Nightdive has a good record of patching their remasters until they’re in an acceptable state (reference: Blood: Fresh Supply). If you’re desperately itching to revisit the classic, you can buy it for a reasonable $9.99 and play the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: So, first thing's first. It pays to remember that the original game honestly hasn't aged well.The writing is *abysmal* – a wellspring of second-hand embarrassment that just doesn't let up, teetering between critically failed attempts at appearing cool and successful attempts at emulating the Ford narration track of the film's original theatrical cut. That's… not a good look.The state-of-the-art-of-1997 interactive movie shell is juddery and janky and compressed all to hell, badly showing its age. Even the intro text crawl can't move in a smooth pace! Whenever pure primary colours appear in the FMV, it's soft and flickery with artifacting. Everybody in my room burst laughing and had to leave upon seeing the antagonist stride on the screen, looking like The Gap incarnate, in the opening scene.That all said, the restauration work seems merely OK. It's glitchier than the original and the bright, sharp UI clashes completely with the muddy CGI art direction. Nightdive also regrettably omitted subtitling the FMV cutscenes for some reason, a disservice since the audio is compressed, noise filtered and compressed again and the spoken lines are often…  nolaned in delivery.The best way to think of the original game is that it's a CGI kusoge along the lines of Kenji Eno's WARP output except now there's a license. A bad piece of fanfic, dripping second-hand embarrassment and nostalgic music cues (ersatz Vangelis). And the minefield puppy. Not sure what's up with this restauration, though, because it feels… off. Think I might refund a game for once.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Don’t play the Enhanced Edition. Play through the original version with a ScummVM CRT shader such as crt-mattias or crt-lottes-fast to relive the glory days. Even in 2024, Blade Runner is still an exceptional point-and-click adventure that is oozing with awesome sci-fi atmosphere. A must play for every Blade Runner and cyberpunk fan.Edit: playing the original version via Steam doesn’t count your hours played and there are no achievements. You’ll have to play it for the sheer enjoyment of it, just like the good ol’ days!

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing. Playing the classic w/ restored content. Briefly tried the enhanced edition and the "updated" graphics were like plastic and destroyed so much character and detail. You can toggle it, but I preferred to use the cut content for a complete experience. It comes with an older ScummVM, but you can obviously use a newer one and point it at the data files if you want.Considering this game was made in the mid-90's, it's amazing how much of an achievement it must have been at the time. It's a point and click adventure game that really makes you feel like a detective, and the chase/shooting sequences help make it feel deadly and need to stay on your toes.Basically, if you are looking for a game that's like Blade Runner, this is obviously the one to get as they absolutely nailed it.

_childDocuments_.review: A true masterpiece of the point and click genre. The player is a colleague of Rick Deckard humorously named Ray McCoy. McCoy is the protagonist of the sort of sequel to the Blade Runner movie. Actors from the movie appear in the same roles, most notably Sean Young as Rachael. The story is pretty good and follows the lore of the movie accurately. The gameplay is fun if not slightly frustrating due to there being a fair amount of guess work having to be done by the player to progress proceedings. I completed the game relatively easily on the hardest difficulty, and as a huge fan of the movie I felt satisfied.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Play the original. It's an option. The re-make, or re-master, or whatever was simply a bump up of original content to 60 FPS, a blur filter that covers up all the original detail, and a glitch'y marriage between original and "updated" features. They kept the original textures for the physical items you find, but when they pop up while using the "enhanced edition" they don't flow and rotate around the screen. They disappear in an instant. Not a fan of this one. But, at least, they can make money off of the original. Thank god they kept that option.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: While the game's slow pace and 'outdated' visuals and design may put off newcomers, Blade Runner proves to be an excellent point and click adventure with a truly branching narrative that kept me on my toes throughout. There are so many choices you won't even realize you're making that change the outcome, and on top of that, the game has a very innovative series of randomized elements that ensure no two playthroughs will be the same.If you enjoy a good sci-fi mystery that honors the narrative and style of the original film, you can't do much better than this. I would love to see a full remake one day that would allow this unique experience to reach more players.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. The graphics and artistic vision hold up despite being a game made for Windows 95. The game mechanics leave much to be desired however. Be expected to run around the same district for 20 minutes only to then think there's nothing else to do there only to then find out there's a person that only happens to appear randomly that you need to talk to. I still highly recommend this game but don't jump into this game expecting things to be quick and straightforward.

_childDocuments_.review: Only a first impression: I don't know if the game had have the original spoken german language, but now it has and as soon as i was in the game, i got that pleasant feeling of playing a really good adventure again. The dialogues are great with a lot of humor and the well-known German speakers of the good old 1980s and 90s of the last century seems also to be remastered and bring back pleasant memories. The game controls with mouse + keyboard work flawless and the reworked visuals look a lot nicer in my opinion. The game progress can be saved by manual saving at any time from the game menu. Fantastic work....Thank you, Nightdive Studios for bringing us back these amazing title, even better than once.
_childDocuments_.name: Blade Runner: Enhanced Edition

_childDocuments_.review: There are no "mixed" feelings about this game - it's a must have. I think recently the new updates allowed for a lot of flexibility, you can play the original Blade Runner in its original form too, so there is no need to dislike the remastered version anymore. In any case the game is getting updates so if you're on the fence then don't worry.The game is a visual masterpiece. There are multiple endings and slightly different ways to play the game. I remember when I first played this, I was 6 years old and we went to a computer store. The game had several CDs it cost about $100. Back then computers were very expensive and this was a visual masterpiece. The graphics have dated over time, but not to any point where it deters from the feeling or atmosphere. The Blade Runner universe is almost perfectly captured in this game, the art and aesthetic, the story, the lonely nature, the persistent rain - just beautiful. Westwood studios was the original creator of this title, the same company that did Command and Conquer, back then they released incredible titles, this is one of them.Overall, a must buy for any Point Click Adventure enthusiast or a person who wants a really good Blade Runner story.

_childDocuments_.review: With the recently released update the game is now running properly, at least in the first few scenes, I haven't had the time to check out the rest of the game yet. But I have to admit I'm not a fan of the 'enhanced' graphics. Yes, they are smoother, but they have also lost a lot of detail. Luckily you can switch to the original graphics by pressing Q, which looks better in my opinion. The only question is whether to install and play the enhanced version or the original version.

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is technically a movie tie-in, it's absolutely , a  in its own right.Blade runner makes the modern "cinematic experience" type game look silly, and I can't help but feel a bit sad, knowing that video games will never be this good  again.If you haven't played this gem yet, I can't recommend it enough. name: Forspoken
detailed_description: In Tanta We Trust After bringing peace to Athia, Frey’s journey continues as she searches for a way to permanently rid the land from the effects of the Break. Amid her search, she follows a mysterious voice that leads her into the past. When she emerges, Frey finds herself surrounded by chaos and destruction. Injured and draped in blood-soaked clothing, she discovers a grim truth about her fate. The recently thriving Athia is at war, but why and with whom? Accompanied by Tanta Cinta, and a new set of magic, Frey must uncover the answers and save Athia once more – and attempt to save herself. Digital Deluxe Edition The Digital Deluxe Edition on PC includes: Forspoken PC Full Game Download Forspoken Mini Artbook (Digital Download) Forspoken Mini Soundtrack (Digital Download) Prequel Story DLC ‘Forspoken: In Tanta We Trust’ (Summer 2023) Prequel Story DLC Early Access Ultra Settings OS Version: Windows® 10 64-bit (After November 2019 Update) or Windows® 11 64-bit Processor: AMD Ryzen™5 5800X (3.8 GHz or better) / Intel® Core™ i7-12700 Memory: 32GB Graphics: AMD Radeon™ RX 6800 XT 16GB / NVIDIA® GeForce® RTX 4080 16 GB VRAM DirectX Version: 12 Disk Space: NVMe SSD 150GB or more Additional Notes: 2160p 60fps About the Game Mysteriously transported from New York City, Frey Holland finds herself trapped in the breathtaking land of Athia. A magical, sentient bracelet is inexplicably wrapped around her arm, and Frey discovers the ability to cast powerful spells and use magic to traverse the sprawling landscapes of Athia. Frey nicknames her new golden companion “Cuff” and sets off to find a way home. Frey soon learns this beautiful land once flourished under the reign of benevolent matriarchs, called Tantas, until a devastating blight relentlessly corrupted everything it touched. The Break  transformed animals into beasts, men into monsters, and rich landscapes into four dangerous realms. At the center of their shattered domains, the Tantas now rule as maddened and evil sorceresses. Unaffected by the Break and desperate for answers, Frey reluctantly agrees to help the last remaining citizens of Athia who see her as their only hope. Frey’s journey through this strange and treacherous land will take her deep into the heart of corruption where she must battle monstrous  creatures, confront the powerful Tantas, and uncover secrets that awaken something much more from within. KEY FEATURES: The Odyssey of a Reluctant Hero Lead Frey on an unforgettable journey in her search for a way home after being mysteriously transported to a breathtaking, fantastical land. Unravel the mysteries of Athia as Frey travels through the calamitous Break and discovers how to wield an immense power. A Beautiful and Cruel Open-World - Explore the sprawling realms of Athia, a striking land of remarkable vistas and otherworldly creatures brought to life through stunning graphics and cutting-edge technology. Venture deep into corrupted territories where a mysterious darkness defiles everything it touches. Customizable Arsenal of Spells - Take on twisted monsters in magical combat with a wide range of powerful abilities catering to a variety of playstyles – from fast-paced and exhilarating to strategic and methodical. Intuitive, Magic-Enhanced Parkour - Scale walls, vault across canyons, leap from dizzying heights, and dash through vast landscapes. Frey's unique abilities allow her to fluidly traverse the open world with ease.

name: RoboCop: Rogue City
detailed_description: Special Offer About the Game
short_description: Become the legendary part man, part machine, all cop hero and deliver justice in Old Detroit.

_childDocuments_.review: Paul Verhoeven’s RoboCop is one of the quintessential action movies of the 1980s. It pushed the envelope with over-the-top violence, killer one-liners, and fantastic special effects, mixed with a biting anti-corporate social commentary under the surface that resonated with audiences. As for me, original Robocop (1987) is one of my favorite childhood films. Is a perfect cyberpunk dystopia. Mega-corporations with divisions affecting nearly every level of consumer need, society, and government want to control everything around them. One such mega-corporation, based on the storyline of the movie, is Omni Consumer Products (OCP) are the main antagonists of the RoboCop franchise. OCP  wants is to overthrow the current government in Detroit, which they consider to be corrupt, and assume total control over the city. After this, they plan to demolish the entire city so as to construct Delta City in it's place, their «ideal city» with fully privatized services; in fact, OCP would control every single aspect of the city. A modernist future where everything is glass-towers, rounded and smooth designs. A future that has no soul and is completely sterile, coming closer and closer...The appeal to nostalgia is strong, and that can have a significant impact on how much mileage you get out of this. As a pure shooter, Rogue City isn’t overly ambitious, but it’s a lot of fun to play even if you don’t know anything about the series. However, if you grew up with RoboCop or recently watched the movies then it is chock-full of references and nods that add a lot to the experience. I found myself laughing out loud the first time I saw someone driving a 6000 SUX or I found «Nukem» Board Game, you can't play «Nukem», but it's still an excellent detail that proves the developers are fans of the series. - "Get Them Before They Get You.". Probably exploding the groin of a baddie is a silly, but it’s so much more entertaining if you know that it’s pulled directly from the film. RoboCop: Rogue City is a pitch-perfect throwback to the action movies of the ‘80s. It’s over-the-top violence with charm, largely well put together but rough on the edges. Most importantly, it's a fun way to spend time in a beloved fictional universe that doesn’t overstay its welcome. Blasting at goons as an unstoppable walking machine remains as extremely entertaining as it seemed on the big screen, thanks in part to an impressive commitment to capturing the look and feel of the original film. Mixing in elements like routine police work and side quests does a great job changing the pace, too. Even if it’s not the best example of visual fidelity, and prone to some bugs along the way, that love of RoboCop shines through. I respect the developers, and I respect their decisions for the most part. This is a game made by people with the same type of love I have for RoboCop. I felt that. I felt it throughout the whole game.If you have seen the films, Rogue City is a triumphant return to the streets of Old Detroit. Murphy’s partnerships, weapons, voice, soundtrack and action combat will pull players back into the gritty world of OCP’s 2024 Detroit city. The gore, visuals and cast all strike the right chords and while objectives mostly follow similar lines, the action is what really makes it pop.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: It's taken thirty-six years, but a worthwhile Robocop game has finally been developed. When it comes to gaming,  the Robocop franchise has been totally devoid of hits. Consisting almost entirely of side-scroller titles, the Robocop franchise has struggled to produce an enjoyable video game, mostly due to the unreasonable difficulty, and ultimately not reflecting the spirit or style of the first two films. To be fair, making a Robocop game is a difficult prospect if the goal is to develop a product that is faithful to the source material. In the films, Robocop is depicted as being virtually unstoppable; Murphy's suit of armour can deflect bullets, he cannot jump, his footsteps are loud, and his gun packs as much punch as an assault rifle. Obviously, a video game that faithfully depicts Robocop in this way would create a game that is too easy. Therefore, previous Robocop games have gone out of their way to be needlessly difficult. Not one Robocop game has been good. Until now. Developed by Teyon (makers of the ill-fated Rambo, and the far more successful Terminator Resistance) have created a brand new story set after the events of 1990's Robocop 2, but before its lesser sequel, Robocop 3. Teyon's treatment of the IP is outstanding in visual, sound, and overall game design. Principally a first person shooter, Rogue City combines shooter, light RPG elements, point and click adventure game elements, and crime procedural mechanics. The format of the game is simple, safe, and at times predictable. But, each of the gameplay segments offers fluid pacing where no single segment of play feels prolonged. Rogue City matches the pacing of the first two films very well. Providing further authenticity to the experience, Peter Weller reprises his role as Murphy and is in fine voice. Despite being his first performance of the character since 1990, Peter has lost nothing of the character. Rogue City feels like the sequel we were deprived of with the release of Robocop 3 (the sequel where Peter did not reprise his role due to filming commitments on another project). The controls and speed movement, meanwhile, is faithful to the film where the pacing is suited to Robocop's stomped movements. Just like Weller and the soundtrack, the setting of Detroit is as grungy and grimy as ever with sleazy and shady NPCs, littered streets, graffiti vandalised walls, and a plethora of side-quests to boost the world building. Rogue City doesn't actually get anything wrong. But, it's the finer details that are lacking. For instance, the audible punch and feel of the side-arm is rewarding with each squeeze of the trigger. But, its damage is grossly inconsistent where, on the one hand, each bullet can tear off chunks of wall and column marble. But, the same weapon barely punctures a hole in a water cooler or a hostile NPC. Despite being a great looking game, it is lacking in the finer details when it comes to gore, environment damage, and overall portral of world physics (puddles, for instance, are completely lacking in animation).The game's save system, meanwhile, is exclusively limited to checkpoints that are not within close proximity of one another, thus resulting in repeat play of long slews of game segments upon character death. Some of the game's length, should it be played on the harder settings, is arguably padded out by needing to replay entire boss fights despite those events being broken down into individual acts. Aside from these issues, Robocop is one of the gaming highlights of 2023. It's fun, offers gameplay variety, is well paced, and cognisant with the source material. Another outstanding film adaption by Teyon. 4 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than it has any right to be.I've seen the Robocop films, but not a superfan, don't remember any of the characters aside from the main character, and I didn't mind the reboot. That's what you're dealing with here.That said, there are a couple of key things that really stood out to me here:*I'm just down for a solid single-player FPS game with strong story and some RPG elements. Deus Ex et al and Prey 2017 are amongst my favourite games of all time. This kinda ticks that box (albeit with a much stronger emphasis on just shooting stuff than either of those - this is NOT an immersive sim, although it adopts some ideas from that genre).*The RPG elements mean there appears to be some scope for replayability, and for me to let the nerd brain kick in and work out how to min/max. Turbo nerd yo.*This thing oozes love for the source material. I'm sure there are a million references passing me by, but I can tell they're there. This feels like a game that loves winking and nodding at people in the know, and while I'm not one of them, I also just kinda enjoy playing a title that has some love put into it.I'm coming to this well after release, it seems super solid tech wise. I've had no crashes, smooth frame rate although it started to chug after an extended session so I restarted the game in case of a memory leak. Playing on Hard which seems to have a level of challenge but I also fear (now that I'm several hours in) that I'm probably not too far off feeling OP, which, in a Robocop game, is kind of the point. A textbook example for all existing IP games to look to, especially when they don't have a AAA budget. Really well executed.

_childDocuments_.review: What seems to be a direct sequel to the 1990 film Robocop 2, Rogue City drops you into the titanium shoes of the half man, half machine, Robocop. This review is written, taking into account that the game comes from a relatively small developer and no doubt, by other games standard, a small budget.The game does an excellent job of capturing the feel of the movies, it would seem the developers have not only watched the movies but also respect them (quite rare for todays licensed materials). Enough faces from the film pop up to make it feel familiar and there are locations that im not sure how accurate they are, but you know where you are straight away. I was half expecting a button bashing shooter with little else, what you actually get is a game that feels a mix between alien isolation and la noire, whith some shooting in between.Yes there are some issues, some technical which can be patched out, but also design. Theres quite a few sections of backtracking, with little to do. The voice acting is iffy in places, although mostly on point and ive had 2, maybe 3 crashes. I think the shooting sections could be quite cool in 3rd person as well.8/10 easily, i hope they do a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Big fan of the movie? Absolutely must buy. Passing interest? Wait for a sale.I am not the biggest Robocop fan but he's a Robot Cop and that's cool. I bought this on sale.REVIEW CONTAINS GAMEPLAY SPOILERS!Robo Pros: + Excellent power fantasy. Role playing Robocop with his stompy footsteps and enviroment scanning Green HUD feels awesome.+ Enemy variety and consistant First Person Shooter gameplay that challenges the player with a customizable upgrade system.+ Robocop's voice actor, Peter Weller,  reprises his role as Alex Murphy Robocop.+ Speaking of which, amazing voice acting all round. Torch Heads gang voice is entertaining.+ Many references to the movies, it's a passion project.+ Some good character development in the story with certain characters.Robo Neutral: This is not a conventional FPS where you take cover and crouch/jump. You cannot do those things. You are supposed to tank damage and shoot them before they turn you into scrap.Robo Cons:- Many shootouts are completely silent with no music.- Some difficulty spikes like the part where you defend yourself from waves of robot droids.- For the most part, bland mission locations. So many videogame cliche's! There's a Chop-Shop, a Quarry, a Prison and even a Sewer Level! Would have preferred more modern looking interiors like the first mission had.- Janky animations from NPC models.- The save system is quite bad. No manual save and it's unclear when you get save checkpoints.Overall, I'd personally give Robocop: Rogue City a 6/10. Definitely will satisfy Robocop Fans but for casual observers I'd recommend getting it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The citizens of Detroit deserve better. And so do we, as gamers.Plenty of nostalgic throwbacks in design, visual effects and writing (including the absolutely great ads on the radio). And I can only recommend it for nostalgia alone. Maybe also to support a "small indie studio with a lot of potential", but I would be lying if I said that Teyon has potential. I gave them the benefit of the doubt with Terminator: Resistance and this game is a step back.Because as a  it'sn't great. The reason being that the developers had plenty of ideas but abandoned those ideas very quickly and did not clean up the game from those ideas' roots.There are plenty of bugs. Sadly expected, eventually fixable, but a lot of the bugs are of the " it out and ship it out" variety, pointing at a severe lack of basic playtesting.The shooting is nice but there are only two weapons better than the Auto-9. One of those weapons you get to use . So one layer of gameplay is already flat. It's fun but it's flat, since the weapon upgrades only change numbers. Endless magazines with some damage thrown on top of that is the easiest choice.Most sidequests range from tedious to formulaic - jump through a hoop, then go somewhere and slaughter everyone (fun dialogue here and there, but the gameplay is lukewarm). And then there are also "Serve and Protect" objectives, requiring you to find X violations and issue tickets or warnings for them. It's pixel hunting at its worst, honestly.The plot uses some of the most asinine tropes ever, going beyond cheesiness and outright into cringeworthiness territory. Yes, it's 80s all over, but watching idiots is more entertainig than being forced to act like an idiot.The skill system also goes out the window pretty soon. You need to invest points into "Deduction" for Robocop to be able to . And this "useful skill" can be used about two or three times throughout the game. Engineering (at a 6/10 skill level) also allows you to open safes without knowing codes and there are three safes in the first two areas, when you won't have the necessary skill points and two safes in the rest of the game. The safes contain nothing of value whatsoever. Engineering by itself is used four times, I think, but three of those times the game doesn't actually check your skill level despite claiming that you need "Engineering X" to choose the dialogue option. Armor and Vitality are practical, the other six are mostly fluff.The game severely lacks . Most of the time it's "Okay" or "Not terrible", but never "Great" or "Yeah! That's what I wanted". And that is the biggest sin. I want a hint of that childlike wonder, instead I get a dose of "Current mainstream gaming industry's hot take on nostalgia".

_childDocuments_.review: A Gloriously Violent Love Letter to the Robocop FilmsRobocop Rogue City is a true masterpiece and a love letter to the classic Robocop films that fans of the series are sure to adore. This game is by far one of the best film to game adaptions, standing tall alongside other greats such as Terminator Resistance and Alien Colonial Marines.As someone who grew up watching the Robocop films and other ultra-violent action films of the 80s, I was immediately drawn into the world of Robocop Rogue City. From the sound of my mechanical footsteps to carrying Robocop's iconic Modified M23R handgun, the game makes you feel like the cybernetic law enforcement officer himself, and it's nothing short of badass.One aspect of the game that truly stands out is its gloriously bloody and gory presentation. The level of violence is reminiscent of the films and adds an extra layer of intensity to the gameplay. The way enemies are displayed and dispatched had me feeling strong Fallout vibes, and I mean this in the best way possible.The leveling system in Robocop Rogue City adds an engaging role-playing game (RPG) element to the experience. This, combined with the visceral combat and a richly detailed world, makes for an incredibly immersive and enjoyable game.Overall, Robocop Rogue City is a masterpiece that pays homage to the classic films while still managing to stand on its own as a fantastic gaming experience. Whether you're a longtime fan of the series or just a fan of action-packed games, this title is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game and a fantastic love letter to the old school Robocop fans. Just like Terminator Resistance was a fantastic love letter to all T1 & T2 fans. The graphics in this game are amazing and very life like, you honestly feel like watching the 1987 with all its rough feeling. The only thing where you can see some downfalls is in the animation esp. character facial animations but I can give it a pass because those guys are not AAA studio for start (I definitely wouldn't let it slide if it was CDPR doing it). Sound design is also very good, although the Auto 9 doesn't exactly sound like the one from the film which may be just a copyright issue or something because I don't think those guys would mess this up (actually used the movie auto 9 mod and it sounds so great). Music is also good, just to bad there aren't many instances where the Robocop theme is played. Now the most important thing, the gameplay. I was actually very positively surprised how well the gameplay feels. Shooting punks feels so great, it has this proper old school shooter feel, the gun's got a serious punch. Every shootout is great here. My fear was it might get boring after 1 hour but none of those things, there are side missions, easter eggs, choices during conversations which will give you different endings. This is the 2nd movie franchise those guys did justice and I can't wait for their next project.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game with that perfect kind of jank: runs decently well but things are put together in a very odd & clunky kind of way; an obviously passionate development team that made a lot of missteps but the end product is hard not to love.I'm nowhere near as huge a Robocop fan as I'm sure the devs are, but I've seen 1 & 2 enough times (and read some of the later comic material) that I feel like I have a good enough grasp on the "good" Robocop material to recognize all the references and homages woven throughout here (the less said about 3 and the TV shows the better). From direct references in returning characters, locations and weaponry to more subtle twists on the work in the plot (Becker being a OCP simiulacra but similar to Ferrer in the first movie, the twist with Robocop #2 in the finale, "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ come", etc.), you can tell this game is a painstaking labor of love sometimes to the game's detriment. The environmental design & detail is extremely impressive for the budget, even on lower resolutions the use of lighting and texture is some of the most impressive I've seen as of late. The character models....eh not so much? The budget seams to start to show pretty blatantly here, looking more like TES Oblivion stand-ins of the movie counterparts and not really gelling with the rest of the style.Plot-wise, things also come out as somewhat of a mixed bag. Working as kind of an alternate version of Robocop 2, I think the writing team may have borrowed from that movie in some bad ways but iterated on it in other good ways. The bad ways are the plot mirroring the film in a kind of scattershot, loosely connected storytelling style that is a little easier to understand in a gaming format but still starts to wear when the game feels stretched a little thin. Numerous points in the narrative feel like a natural climax, but extra detail is added on. Where I think the devs were able to improve was using the longer game runtime they had carved out for themselves to really flesh out the world of Detroit here in ways that seem to harken to a somewhat down-to-earth representation seen in the first movie (as down-to-earth as Robocop can get, I guess).Though I've seen some reviewers grumble about it, I think side missions like Robo looking for a stray cat, helping out with desk duty at the police station or even fixing a light help add a layer of mundanity that helped me connect with the world more (and throw the combat sequences into sharp contrast). Did it seem a little excessive at points? Sure. Was this maybe a little too ambitious in the story department & a little overstuffed? For sure, but I think there's an earnestness to the dialogue that much to my surprise made it a better story-based game than any Bethesda release I've played in a while. Although I think the persuasion stats in this seem broadly useless (do not put points into them), I liked a lot of the dialogue exchanges & the devs giving you chance to live out the weird reality where Robo is a complete corporate stooge and total narc-bot.Of course, I saved the best for last, which is undoubtedly the combat. I remember when gameplay for this dropped, some total knuckleheads online couldn't seem to grasp the appeal of playing such a slow, plodding character like Robocop. While general traversal is a bit of a hassle (probably adds to a lot of the game's length, it'll be funny to see people mod this with "Robocop moves at normal human speed" boosts), in combat this idea creates something that felt genuinely unique in the realm of FPS games. It's not quite a light gun gallery, but your strategic options are extremely limited at your speed meaning you need to think about encounters much differently than most games. On higher difficulties, this becomes a headshot/dickshot requirement game, and that focus being put on the player meant to me that pretty much every combat sequence was intensely satisfying. Ricochet plates, shooting grenades out of hands to explode, all the little tricks you can use to get the upper hand are so so fun. The Auto-9 is all you generally need (specialty guns for some scenarios), and the chip plug-in system is a genuinely great idea that I think more games could use.Where I think the combat hits a big roadblock are in the boss encounters. At least for me, these segments did not feel ironed out enough to be fun in their own regard and took a lot of cheesing methods to finish. Most of the time, they just felt too long & drawn out (the first ED209 fight for sure) and lacked the visceral punch of the mob encounters. A minor issue, but it felt like it ground the pace to a halt more than usual. Overall though, this game was a wonderful surprise, clearly made with love & passion with it of course being a huge step up for developers primarily known for junky shovelware. Not sure how geared up I'd be to revisit this, but I am for sure keeping an eye on what this studio does next.

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of Robocop you'll love this game. it's a nice faithful recreation of the Robocop universe.The graphics are pretty decent, and using the new UE5 engine.There's nothing quite like playing as Robocop, the pacing in places can be a bit slow, and some of the side quests do become a little repetitive, and likewise the slow plodding pace of Robocop might not be to everyone's taste. If you put those aside you do get left with a decent game, that's worth the time to play. All of the achievements can be got in a single play through with no need to play on stupidly hard levels in order to unlock, I would recommend playing on hard for a slightly harder challenge, the boss battles can be a little annoying on hard, but they're still doable, although if you find it challenging you can always knock the difficulty down without penalty.My biggest gripe is with the saves, there are no manual saves and you're reliant on the autosaves, which aren't that obvious when they're happening, so you have to quickly check the savers to see the timestamp before you log off, otherwise you can find yourself having to redo bits again.The gun play is good, some weapons are better than others, and with the right PCB the only gun you'll end up using is the Auto-9. The game could do a little better explaining how the chips work on the PCB's and also about the chip merging, once you get the hang of it, it's quote easy to update. One thing to note the Weapon Spray is the only one you want to keep a low % modifier on.It's worth picking up outside of a sale, but if it's in a sale then it should be an instant buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden gem in a year full of of amazing releases. This relatively short FPS (~15 hours) is an homage to 80s action movies in general and RoboCop in particular. Please do play it if you enjoy... trouble. GOOD-- Amazing graphics with full glory of Unreal Engine 5. -- Immersive atmosphere of decaying Detroit and weird sci-fi tech of 80s movies (including RoboCop interface)-- Decent story that touches social (inequality; crime; politics) and philosophical issues (what differs human from machine)-- Fun and unique gameplay that can be best described as "slow indomitable force of nature stomps creeps"-- Great voice acting from main characters, including original RoboCop actor and his partner from the movies-- A lot of hilarious corny jokes ("you are not the only one ankle breaker on this basketball court")BAD-- Voice acting from secondary characters is pretty bad to the point of breaking immersion (I guess all voice acting budged went to original RoboCop actors)-- Game is relatively short and there is no New Game+ mode. -- Some issues with graphices on Linux including levels some times not loading. Overall it is a great game well worth its price and a steal for any sale. Please support developers that do good job and release good games that work out of the box!

_childDocuments_.review: It captures the schlock of 80's action movies to a T. This is the kind of game that I want to see more of: instead of focusing on retention/playtime metrics, microtransactions, et cetera, this game focused on FUN. You feel like RoboCop, strutting at absolute max speed, punching holes through each slime. Cheesy one-liners, ridiculous dialogue, but still having the restraint to allow serious moments. This game was so satisfying to play, and knowing that there are multiple outcomes for all the characters means I'll be playing it again soon.Pros:- Very satisfying gameplay, including punchy guns, hilarious means of killing (like throwing exploding computers at people, or hurling dumpsters across alleys), replete with gore and other means of feedback.- Wide variety of play styles, with a skill tree that feels impactful (and doesn't skimp on handing out some nice perks). For example, the "Armor" skill tree has a perk where weak guns' bullets just fly off you and hit other enemies. I was able to max out half the skill trees (after focusing on the one that increases all exp gained).- Diverse level and enemy variety, keeping things fresh throughout the whole campaign. While some features only come into play a couple times (speaking specifically about the signal tracker), none of them feel contrived. - Honors the source material, building on it in a very natural way.- Likable characters, all of which follow an action movie trope: the new guy, the witty sidekick, the sly reporter, et cetera.- Fun side quests, which (usually) don't feel contrived.- Performed relatively fine. I have an RTX 3070 and was able to run it on epic, 4K settings, running between 60-120 FPS with DLSS on auto.- It's got that je-ne-sais-quoi of a low-budget action movie, where its charm and passion got me to overlook a lot of its downsides. I'm going to list what I feel are its cons, but let me be clear: I don't think any of these were particularly egregious, nor do I think they should stop you, unless the performance requirements fully stop you.Cons:- Obvious lack of polish in some areas: the faces and animations were very minimal, with most cutscenes being basic shot-reverse shot with stock arms-crossed, lifting a hand animations while talking. I didn't mind too much, sometimes even finding it funny (literally no one ever looks scared, so all the hostages just have dead-eyed expressions). Other examples include transitions to cutscenes, where you'll still hear action happening in the game, but a cutscene has begun.- One particular objective towards the end of the game is particularly annoying. Minor spoiler warning: - I experienced lag spikes, though mostly only during cutscenes, where the framerate would go from 60-120 to the teens. It didn't seem consistent, but I did experience that lag during gameplay one time.- DLSS was pretty much necessary for my situation, though I maxed everything out and was running it in 4K. However, that did lead to the usual DLSS issues of ghosting, peoples mouths having weird artifacting (their teeth would regularly linger when they opened their mouth), papers flowing in the wind leaving trails, puddles in sunlight constantly twinkling with the upscaling, et cetera.I definitely think you should get this game. It was absolutely worth full price to me, especially because I want to support this kind of development. Teyon was clearly having fun making this game, and it shows in just about every aspect of it. If one little mission and some budget constraints are all I can point out as flaws, I think that's an absolute win in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City, a game that promised to immerse players in the gritty world of the iconic franchise, delivers a mixed bag of experiences that leaves players navigating through a maze of highs and lows. As a  fan of the RoboCop universe, I embarked on this journey with high hopes, only to be met with a plethora of issues that marred what could have been an exceptional gaming experience.Let's address the elephant in the room right away: RoboCop: Rogue City is plagued with technical issues that can't be ignored. From visual glitches to performance hiccups, and rampant crashing, the journey through Old Detroit is a frustrating one. The lackluster visuals, coupled with audio mastering problems, detract from the overall immersion in the game world. However, with some tweaks and mods, I managed to salvage a somewhat bearable experience, though the constant fear of crashing loomed over every gameplay session.The animations, or lack thereof, are another major letdown. Characters move stiffly, with facial expressions resembling drywall. Dialogue sequences feel lifeless, akin to a Bethesda title, making interactions with NPCs a chore rather than a delight. Despite these drawbacks, the game manages to shine in certain areas of graphics, particularly in smaller, detailed environments, showcasing the potential of the UE5 engine.However, where RoboCop: Rogue City truly shines is in its gameplay. Playing as RoboCop feels empowering yet vulnerable, striking a delicate balance that keeps combat engaging. The variety of weapons and enemy types adds depth to the shooting mechanics, while skill upgrades allow for customization of playstyle. The inclusion of side missions and collectibles adds replay value, though some quests suffer from unsatisfying conclusions, leaving players with more questions than answers.Despite its flaws, there's an undeniable charm to RoboCop: Rogue City. The game captures the essence of the franchise, offering fans a chance to enforce justice in a dystopian future. While I wouldn't recommend it without a laundry list of caveats, those willing to overlook its shortcomings may find enjoyment buried beneath the rubble of technical issues.In conclusion, RoboCop: Rogue City is a testament to the potential of the franchise in the gaming world, marred by execution issues and technical mishaps. It's a game of highs and lows, with moments of brilliance overshadowed by frustrating setbacks. If you can weather the storm of bugs and glitches, there's fun to be had in Old Detroit. However, approach with caution, and be prepared for a bumpy ride.Overall Rating: 6/10(Mod used: Ultra Plus Stutter Performance and Visual Hotfixes, slightly modified)

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10First and foremost this game does honor to the Robocop franchise like no other piece of content since the original 2 movies (I don't like to talk about Robocop 3). I knew the shooting would be fun, and it is. But I did not expect to enjoy the roleplaying elements of the game as much as I did. If I'm completely honest, they break up the gameplay and make it less monotonous. If every level was shooting in linear areas I wouldn't of cared about the story, which is good but not amazing. There aren't a lot of choices like in a 'Fallout' game but the dialogue choices make you feel like you are changing how Robocop is viewed and how he views himself. Now for my biggest disappointment: DLSS, ASR, and frame generation are not well optimized for this game. I had a lot of crashes during cutscenes. I had so many that I almost stopped playing until I found out other people had similar problems. I pushed through it and finished. I do not regret my time with the game, I had a great time and I loved all the Robocop references and the well thought out environments, but this game definitely has its performance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy recommendation.Now, depending if you enjoyed RoboCop the Movie and have "nostalgia" or whatever you want to call it, this will be either a "good game" or an "above average".if you have nostalgia for the Movie and what not, then this might even be a "very good game": a lot of easter eggs and movie references, amazing sound design, original RoboCop Voice Actor, top notch violence, the gameplay feels like you are actually playing RoboCop.If you don't have nostalgia, the above still applies, as well as all the quick inserted ethical and moral questions - which are just 1 or 2 sentences and then never touched again -, the 80-90s humor, the dystopian visions and ideas about a "unchecked capitalism" and so on, BUT it might not be enough to make you enjoy the game that much.If you saw the movie, this will feel "just like home", if not, you might linger for more development, more character development, more exposition and exploration of said ideas and feel like some dialogues, quests and situations are just badly done - which don't get me wrong, they are, but they feel just like the type of humor and delivery from the movie period -.With that said, the shooting / gameplay mechanics are not anything special, nothing pratically new, so as a FPS, the game is just very lacking. Same in the other departments, be it "detective" or any other "puzzle" like elements.The only major downside of the game, imho, is the lack of manual saves, you are bond to the - sometimes very much apart from one another - checkpoint system.About 20 hours for a run while checking every nook and spot, about 8 hours for the main story only.So, an easy recommendation, but this game will either be "an amazing homage to the original" or "an average FPS" depending on how much other media knowledge and "nostalgia" you have.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is an incredible gaming experience for those who grew up watching the original iconic movie or love the character. Teyon's ability to land Peter Weller to do all the voice acting work on RoboCop made this a must-play game for those who love this franchise.The beautiful graphics directly pulled everything fans loved about RoboCop and RoboCop 2 into the game, heading in a new direction. You’ll find many fun areas with movie Easter eggs sprinkled throughout Detroit as you play, which I loved. Even the intro level immediately gave me goosebumps since you got to blast enemies away to RoboCop’s main theme song. Let me tell you, I was in awe right off the bat, thanks to that moment. I was hooked and excited to sit back and continue playing from that initial rush.This game is not just some basic generic FPS game with the RoboCop license but pushes the lore forward. It’s a fun story with RPG elements and the ability to be a cop. It was fun issuing tickets in side quests and scanning for clues in RoboVision, just like in the movies. Even the targeting when ADSing is so cool since it does the famous green crosshair and everything. Again, all these little touches from the films were a rush to play since I felt like I was RoboCop.All the sound effects, gunplay, gore, and even RoboCop’s footsteps and classic one-liners are here. Whenever you breach a room, the slow-motion kills are fantastic and memorable. Honestly, if you watched the original RoboCop and RoboCop 2 movies, this video game, yes, a video game, has a much better story than RoboCop 3 to finish the trilogy. It’s better than that abysmal RoboCop 3 story, the weird RoboCop TV show, and that “meh” RoboCop remake. This game’s story goes in-depth to show you the human side of RoboCop while allowing you to RPG-decide how to handle all the situations coming your way through dialogue.RoboCop: Rogue City continues the story from the original two movies and ties everything together nicely. All the familiar faces are here, from Anne Lewis to Warren Reed. Even some magnificent flashback film moments will blow your mind when you discover them. All the tongue-in-cheek humor is here, just as it was in the movies. I laughed out loud at all the sightings of the 6000 SUX car and posters of TJ Lazer.Now, this game isn’t free of faults. I found a bunch of bugs, even what seems to be a broken level. The game played fine for the most part, except for the Street Vultures mission and area. It’s bugged since the minute you get there and start roaming around, your frames-per-second drops dramatically. I was getting 400 FPS consistently but could barely do 20 FPS at that specific level. Once I completed it, the game played fine again. Even after I restarted my game, machine, etc., that particular level did not play as intended. I have no idea why, but others have said the same thing.I also felt the voice audio was broken. The volume of when characters spoke was way too low, even for RoboCop’s lines. This drove me nuts since you can tell that Weller put a lot of time and effort into this game as he says a ton of lines, but you can barely hear his iconic voice. That’s even with the voice settings turned up to 100. The voice-acting audio levels are generally off and often end abruptly in cutscenes. At first, the side quests were fun, but many were repetitive, especially towards the end. It reached the point where you know the ending is coming, so I’m not sure why a few more side quests were added when you’re dying to get to the end. The game should have been done with side quests entirely in those final areas and be all-in on that climactic race to the end.Speaking of the ending, it was excellent! I won’t ruin anything for you, but the plot twists were great. I was very invested in the story, and overall, it delivered. It felt like a warzone, and I loved all the detailed explosions, debris flying everywhere, epic boss fights, and the fun weapons encountered along the way.This was a better way to end the RoboCop trilogy, not the nonsense called RoboCop 3. Watch the first two movies, disregard everything else after that, and then play this video game. You’ll feel complete again, that they did the story, and most importantly, Weller as RoboCop, justice. It’s a fitting way, decades later, for Weller to seal the chapter with his most famous character in a way that wasn’t dumb or embarrassingly bad.RoboCop: Rogue City is a 4/5 for being mostly a video game gem, especially for franchise fans. As a kid, I grew up watching and loving that original RoboCop movie, so this was a great trip down memory lane. I enjoyed the second movie, but the first one will always be in my heart since it was perfect, especially the movie soundtrack. Everything after these first two movies is trash, and I’m happy this game was made to make things right. The gameplay is fun, the story is memorable, and all the nostalgic sound effects, levels, guns, and recurring characters were brilliantly done. It’s not a perfect game due to bugs, glitches, and the low voice-acting audio levels, but Teyon still did a solid job here. I highly recommend this for anyone who loves RoboCop to finally play as him in a video game that does him and this franchise justice.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game, got my fair bit of fun and even managed to get all collectables. Yet I won't recommend it for the general audience. To answer why, I mainly have to counter most occurring criticisms and praises.- Reviews praised good plot, some even said it's better than in movies. It is not. The plot perhaps tried to match the naivety of action movies of 80s, and in this the authors succeeded. But it's one thing to use the historical setting, and another to match the plot trends. That's why the story is a total failure. Completely predictable, full of familiar tropes and cliches, with idiotic decisions across the board and unrealistic characters. This will only impress those who are far far from movies and even games, no matter what epoch.- Lots of criticism around easiness isn't fair. Yes, it won't be any hard for veterans of the shooter genre. But hey give me a break. What did you expect from the game with reticle so huge that it easily covers an enemy's head at a medium distance? This game isn't about flexing your shooter muscles. It is a shooting range, but it can be difficult if you allow it to be so. For those who's going to play I'd recommend at least Hard difficulty, but to challenge yourself you could further experiment with variety of guns (since Auto9 marginally still remains the best in terms of recoil, accuracy and some unbeatable perks you can unlock in higher PCB tiers). Overall, you won't sweat but you'd probably die a few times which is OK for this type of action.- Speaking of genre and gameplay, reviews praised fun and variety such as quests, dialogues, etc. Here I can argue again, saying that this fun mostly comes in the first half or even third of the game. Then everything becomes repetitive. Same precinct, same dozen of streets on a 1sqm block, same NPCs and even antagonists. It's one massive rat race and not even against time (which I normally hate). You gotta entertain yourself - same as with challenging I mentioned above - by exploring every corner, trying to suck all the fun out of this rather bland environment. What's the reward? Well, don't put much hope in the skills. Even achievements are so basic (I could've thought of at least dozen others). What else? Basically, just plain vanilla fun of "shoot-them-all" and "complete-quest-what's-next".- There was criticism about lack of optimisation and stuttering graphics. I ran game on RTX 3070 + i5 on maximums and didn't fret. Yes there were a couple of location with sudden frame drop. And a few crashes of course. But hey, look at the graphics! Even on maximum the game looks sooo dated. Something typical for Nacon's produce such as The Sinking city. It is optimised to some degree, but there's not much to optimise. Anyhow,  I'm not too disappointed here. Just wanted to make a point to not expect much from the visuals. Feel free to tweak graphics down if you got issues, you won't lose much.And that's pretty  much it. Whoever read to this line already got my major pros and cons. The final decision towards "negative" came after I had a strong feeling that Nacon just cheated on the gamers. There was so much potential (even with the outdated visuals), but instead we've got a very average shooting range with arguable value in the entire franchise. I will probably go and re-watch the original movie now just to bring back that warmer feeling. Back then it was a novelty at least. But this game is just a gimmick.
