_childDocuments_.review: Look, I won't lie: This game has a fair amount of jank, its satire never reaches the heights of its cinematic predecessor and it has production values that makes you ask "Was this financed with change found between couch cushions?". Also, its pacing borders on "catastro♥♥♥♥".But its strengths are there and their impact is huge. Like Terminator: Resistance (made by the same studio), it's clearly a love letter to its franchise, made by fans who understood the assignment and filled its playtime (about 15 hours) with fun, gory gunplay, some good laughs and a heap of fanservice. Full price may be a bit much for people who are not gigantic RoboCop-Fans, but for those who are or are willing to wait for a sale, this is a great little game. Plus: How many chances to see or hear Peter Weller as RoboCop do we have these days?

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a very fun FPS! Took me about 16 hours to complete.I won't claim to be the biggest RoboCop fan, as I have only seen the first movie a handful of times and I have only seen RoboCop 2 once. But even with that said, this game feels like the perfect RoboCop experience. Gun play feels phenomenal, Story is as campy and fun as the films, returning characters (even the actors voices) from the films are in here, the list goes on of praises I can give this game.One negative I can give though is that RoboCop: Rogue City has no manual saving. Game is auto save only and only saves at the beginning of a mission and every time you use a door to enter a new area. This wouldn't be so bad if the open area segments have you go for upwards to an hour without it saving a single time. An update that adds manual saves would be amazing.TLDR RoboCop: Rogue City is a solid 8/10 FPS. If anything, maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Good nostalgic peace. Game is somewhat slow phase story about RoboCop. If you liked the old movies, this is your game. Lots of shooting separated by finding wallets, clues and storytelling. I did laugh at loud when I realized you can daddy choke thugs and throw them ass first. Grab a first guy by his neck, throw him at the second guy killing the first guy and knocking down the second. Grab the second guy by his neck and repeat until there are no guys. You can also use other surfaces or throw upwards and use your slow time ability to savour the moment.This is from the point of players: to buy or not to buy. Yes, to buy, with full price only if you really liked the “old” RoboCop 1 and 2 movies (not 3rd, we don’t speak about it, there is only 1st and 2nd). If buying is done without that touch of nostalgia on your shoulders you might end up regretting buying it at full price. full price would be in order if game was more polished and had more overall rounded edges. At its current state the game definitely delivers good story and good combat. Puns, game deliver puns. Really. As a standalone piece "as if not knowing RoboCop" would be 6.5/10. However, adding up all the nostalgia and immersion from the RoboCop movies, storytelling and overall "vibe" it is about 8.5 and with couple of beers (whiskey) it goes easily to 9/10. I really liked to play the game.Game is a bit short; Detroit city area could be bigger and have more ambient life. After playthrough I was left with a feeling that this game could have been made longer and it would have been in a sense “better”. If speaking of that in game Detroit city section, you can only add so much happening there before player start to wonder what kind of hellhole this is and why everything happens “just here”. Still, it could be like 3 areas where you could drive your patrol car and spot criminalities or help citizens by your own choice. Now it’s a bit weird that RoboCop by his lawful righteousness outright “knows” that there are 3 things he needs to rectify and player needs to find them. IMO would be better to let player “spot” criminalities that he understands to be ones  and reward xp when he has done like 3 of them. But again, this is semantics and personal preference. I played this game on "hard" and it took 21 hours to finish, it felt quick but story did unveil and came to finish. In the end there even was some hint of sequel with Japanese buyers (No please, there is no RoboCop 3, please) Also a part from time to time "I will run to hit RoboCop with my sledgehammer just after he rammed thru wall and throw motorcycle killing my 3 gang members" there is close to none of that overwhelming power to brute force enemies in to submission. One or two "NO YOU" scenarios where thug flies thru second floor window and obtains quick serenity of realization to surrender before landing agony, would be cool addition.Overall, yes, I like the game, yes you should buy it, now or later but play it. Yes, I will play it thought again and try to make more reasonable choices with perks this time.

_childDocuments_.review: A good FPS faithful to the RoboCop movies--it's even got Peter Weller! _childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a phenomenal game. It is everything I could ever possibly want out of such a title, and then some. Since hearing about Rogue City for the first time after it was announced, it's been on my wishlist since then. I had the great pleasure of playing the Rogue City demo during Steam's latest Next Fest. Typically, I will NEVER pre-order anything, but the demo absolutely blew me away, and I was sold on it. So much in fact that I pre-ordered the Alex Murphy edition at my earliest convenience. Based on how the developers reacted to feedback from the demo, they immediately got to work fixing the bugs and further polishing the game before release, which speaks volumes to how much they care about their game's success.I can say having played the game 48 hours early due to pre-ordering it that you don't need to worry about the OCP shotgun - while fun to use, it's not pay-to-win since most weapons you can pick up are better options anyway. The OCP shotgun basically just occupies your picked up weapon slot, and once you run out of ammo, you're going to throw it away and grab something else instead. As far as I can tell, it performs identically to the sawed-off pump shotgun that you can pick up from some enemies. Aside from that, the cosmetic skins are cool but not necessary.At any rate, I have almost nothing but good things to say about Rogue City, and oh man, you're going to hear them.First, I'd like to start off by saying that this game is a love letter to the RoboCop original trilogy. I am a big fan of RoboCop 1, and having watched it, there are several aspects of Rogue City that immediately stand out as references and call backs to the movies. If you have not at least seen RoboCop 1 before playing this, you owe it to yourself - it will give you a greater appreciation for the game. However, if you have not seen any of the RoboCop movies, Rogue City is still a great place to start. Admittedly, I have not seen RoboCop 2 or 3 yet, but I will definitely be going back to watch them. Rogue City takes place between RoboCop 2 and 3 chronologically, making it a sequel to 2 and a prequel to 3. Some of the plot elements either come from or tie in to the original trilogy, adding context to Rogue City.So much of Rogue City's attention to detail and polish give it a great deal of charm. Everything, from the familiar cast of characters, to RoboCop's aloof one-liners, to the subtle dark comedy and dry wit, to small details as homage to the movies like the police cars doing a burnout out of the precinct's parking garage and the sparks when the back of the car scrapes the pavement going up the ramp, and even cracks in your visor that are consistent both in first-person as well as in cutscenes, all just adds to the experience. The city environment, fashion sense of characters, and CRT televisons and computer monitors all lends itself to that gritty, yet glamorized retro-futuristic feel of the 80's and Old Detroit. The movement, your HUD, and many interactions makes you feel like Alex Murphy, the clinically dead remains of someone trapped inside a machine. The musical score is on point, and takes me back to the movies. Rogue City is to the RoboCop Trilogy what Batman: Arkham Asylum is to The Dark Knight Trilogy - just as the Batman games make you feel like Batman, Rogue City makes you feel like RoboCop. The immersion is incredibly solid.Set pieces are absolutely beautiful. On max graphics settings, environments are almost photo-realistic. Lighting during daytime is gorgeous and casts realistic shadows over the environment. Liquid surfaces reflect the world, lighting, entities, and all that jazz. I'm personally not a fan of Nvidia DLSS, which is why I have it turned off. Even with DLSS turned off, on max settings, I'm getting a solid 40-50 FPS on my 2-generation-old RTX 2080 in most areas. I've had frame drops to the high 20's in some scenarios, but those are few and far between, and so far have only happened to me in cutscenes and dialogue where reaction time is not important. All I can say is that they've outdone themselves on how beautiful this game is.Rogue City's actual gameplay is extremely fun. Combat is anywhere between satisfying and exhilarating in any given engagement - the game will throw different flavors of goons at you, and it will be your job to mow them down; sometimes one-by-one with your trusty Auto 9, other times by throwing objects into them, shooting propane tanks to wipe out entire crowds, and grabbing punks by the neck before throwing them into each other, up into the air, or out of the plate glass window of a sky rise. Huge blood stains will show up on walls behind gunshot victims, blooming outward and dripping down the wall. Pools of reflective blood will spread under dead bodies. It's intense and action-packed, and the violence is over the top, just like in the movies.Depending on where you aim, the kill shot will have different effects: a headshot will explode an enemy's head, sending giblets flying everywhere. Arm shots will blow the arm off, sending the character screaming into a unique death animation and dialogue. Leg shots will blow the leg off, instantly dropping the attacker to the ground. Kill shots to the center of mass will simply blow enemies backwards off their feet, instantly knocking them down and clearing your line of fire - even if they are already in a death animation, meaning you can blow a hole in their chest as a quick and satisfying coup-de-grace. You even get a special achievement for shooting enemies in the crotch, and are treated to a very funny death animation where they double over clutching their obliterated manhood. I can definitely say that it hasn't gotten old for me yet.During the quiet points of the game, you largely get to explore beautifully crafted environments in Old Detroit, immersing yourself in the lore of the RoboCop series. Rogue City plays almost like an action-RPG. You can interact with civilians, listen in on conversations, do detective work, scan for clues, solve mysteries, and pick up side quests. Every little thing you do gives you a bit of XP. Leveling up gives you a skill point that you can spend increasing your stats and unlocking special abilities. Each character that you are able to interact with gives you several dialogue options, some of which will change the outcome of the conversation, or even the quest that you're doing.As Alex Murphy, you are not only the master of your own destiny, but also hold the fate of Detroit in your hands. You feel the weight of the decisions you make, and the consequences they entail. The action and combat is insanely fun and varied, and the story is compelling. It is your decision how to pursue your Prime Directives, and serve whichever directive you believe is the greater good.Rogue City is a traditional return to the actually good triple-A titles of 10 to 15 years ago which are relegated to rare gems today, that were innovative, solid, and fun. It is an homage to the RoboCop franchise. Buy the game. You will not regret it.10/10 - "I'd buy THAT for a dollar!"EDIT: Having beaten the game, I am a bit disappointed at what I believe is a lack of replayability. It would also be nice to have achievements based on which difficulty you completed the game on since I beat the game on the hardest difficulty, which all things considered wasn't that tough. Still, it's a superhero game, and more of a power fantasy than a balanced shooter, so that is not a problem.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what all of us wanted from RoboCop for the last 30 years.The characters are superb, the voice acting is very well done, and the graphics are incredibly salable.I would recommend at least 8GB VRAM for 1080p ultra settings or 2K high settings, and 12GB+ for 4K high/ultra.The music score also needs to be mentioned, as it does feature quite a bit of the original soundtrack by Basil Poledouris, with some original tracks that are incredibly haunting when roaming the streets of Old Detroit.If the soundtrack is ever released as DLC or on its own it will be an instant purchase.I can't recommend this enough, if only this could have been the 3rd movie all those decades ago!

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop Rouge City is a game that is not to be slept on. As basic as the gameplay looks, there is an RPG element to it. You have the freedom to build Robocop how you like, very tanky, extreme precision, super detective or all of the above. The choice is yours. The story takes place after Robocop 2 so it is a perfect setup for a Robocop game. There is a ton of nostalgia in this game. From characters to locations to one liners from the movies. I was really surprised by the length of the game as well. Everytime I thought the game was about to end there was a new level to tackle. The game looks stunning! I have a pretty decent setup but this was the only game I really had to  tweak settings for it to hold a stable 60fps. Some open world elements where you can do side objectives and there are instances as well that are linear. I played on the hardest difficulty available when you started the game and didn't find it too much of a challenge once I upgraded the Auto-9.The talk about this game is accurate, it is fun, entertaining and a real nod to the movies and the lore. I waited for a sale but you will get your $$$ worth for sure, especially if you are a Robocop fan. "Dead or Alive you're coming with me"

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much what it says on the label. You will get a solid - definitely NOT groundbreaking - shooter which lets you play as Robocop and turn outrageous 80's stereotype goons into strawberry jam. You'll get a basically okay Robocop story (about as well written as the movies). You'll get some one-liners. And you can write parking tickets moments after slaughtering 15 men for breaking into an apartment. Zero replayability and all the depth of a shallow puddle, but I still had a good time with it. Buy it on the deepest discount you can find and you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: At times utterly gorgeous, and at times janky, this game is a tribute to RoboCop in a way no game has achieved  to date. If you're a fan of the IP, you can't miss this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big Robocop fan, particularly of the original 1987 movie. I also enjoyed the Terminator game this game developer made a few years prior. Needless to say, I was very excited about this game when it was announced.However, I saw some video clips for the game when it first released and I wasn't as thrilled about it. I did eventually purchase the game when it went on sale.When I first started playing, I felt the game was a little underwhelming graphically. I felt the early cut scenes and voice dubs were falling a little short in quality. Then, there was a lot of dialogue to sift through. I typically don't find consequential dialogue games fun. So, it took me a little while to get into the game.However, the game started to grow on me pretty quickly. It's not the most polished game, but the action sequences are fun to play through. To me, the shooting doesn't get old quick. I played through the campaign and started in over on NG+ with the highest difficulty settings. To be fair, the harder difficulty isn't so bad when you can carryover your EXP and PCBs. Robocop's upgrades/skill tree make a massive difference in how you navigate the constant battles. In most ways, the game is much easier on the 2nd playthrough.I somewhat expected to be disappointed, so I'm happy to say that I am not!

_childDocuments_.review: Does the things you would expect out of a robocop video game and is viscerally satisfying. The people who made this have a reverence for Verhoeven and the sense of humor in those films. References abound but they're smart about it e.g. ED 209 is lovingly recreated, to say nothing about RoboCop's signature firearm.Amazingly, the game punches above its weight for what you would assume is an otherwise rote FPS. There are miniature open world sections where RoboCop wanders around to do police work. There are segments clearly inspired by things like Dear Esther and other walking simulators. It has the confidence to get weird and trippy like Condemned: Criminal Origins. You even do detective work - very light, but it breaks up the action. Text logs hint at much greater character depth not fully realized within the bounds of the game.The only downers are the skill point investment (put it all into the one tree first to get the 30% bonus and cruise through everything else) and gun upgrades (fun idea, but mechanically tedious).In short, RoboCop: Rogue City is a labor of love that does right by the source material and tries to do things no one would ever expect out of the source material. I can easily see the developers doing an adaptation of something like They Live, or Escape From New York.Funeral Bob gives it two thumbs up

_childDocuments_.review: really really fun shooter, the gore, guns, and environmental destruction are all incredibly satisfyinghowever, i would only really recommend this game if it's on sale or you're a big fan of robocop (for clarification, i'm not. i have seen the movies and enjoyed them somewhat but i bought this game because the gameplay looked fun). the developers are obviously huge fans of the movies and it shows. they even got the original voice actor for robocop.unfortunately, this game has a lot of boring parts too. the missions where you have to go around and talk to people get stale really quick. also, the plot is a bit bland and drags out forever. i found myself skipping through dialogue frequently. also, the voice acting is very amateur in some scenes, which is fine, but it really is noticeable because of robocop's voice actor doing an amazing job. the perk system is fun and all but to get a ton of skill points you have to do the boring ass fetch quests that can go on FOREVER for a very minimal reward. even though this game has a lot of flaws, the gunplay is incredibly fun and i recommend it nonetheless. i don't really like the parts where you fight robots or heavily armored soldiers though, the gunplay is definitely intended for the gangster and criminal enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a fantastic blast from the past, seamlessly blending the gritty charm of the classic 80s movie with modern gameplay and stunning visuals. Fans of the original RoboCop will appreciate the detailed homage to the iconic film, with a faithfully recreated Detroit that feels both nostalgic and immersive. The game captures the essence of being RoboCop—walking the line between man and machine, dishing out justice in thrilling first-person combat, and interacting with a city that feels alive and dangerous.The developers have done an impressive job of honoring the legacy of RoboCop, even with the challenge of lost cast members from the original trilogy. The voice acting, atmosphere, and soundtrack all evoke that retro-futuristic 80s vibe, paying respect to the film’s tone and characters while still delivering something fresh for modern players. Whether it’s the gritty storytelling, intense gunplay, or the sense of stepping right into one of the most memorable sci-fi franchises of the past, RoboCop: Rogue City is a love letter to fans and a rewarding experience for newcomers alike.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Best game from the AA market in a while.Fun shooting with some of the best ragdolls, gore and dismemberment I've seen from a game with this type of budget.The Deus Ex-lite hub world filled with side objectives, dialogue options, skills and weapon upgrades all serve to further flesh out an already great game.Story and writing that are faithful to the movies and don't bend over backwards to please the sensibilities of "modern audiences".They also got Peter Weller back to voice Robocop, which is great, because most AAA developers would have opted to cast Troy Baker and call it a day.In an industry where most studios get significantly worse with time, Teyon bucks the trend and shows steady improvement with each game and I love them for it."I'd buy that for  full price."

difficulty settings but no achievement for playing it on the highest difficulty, there are mission rankings but no trophy tied to getting a perfect score on every mission so if you wanted to you could simply not do any of the side content like issuing tickets or collecting evidence.Another gripe i have is with the weapons,there are quite a few to find off enemies or in the world but i only found myself using them at the beginning of the game because once you get good boards and chips for your pistol it will just trivialize the game from that point on because i was playing on extreme difficulty the entire game and once i got my service pistol upgraded it absolutely shredded through any enemy i came across offering no real challenge even the final boss went down in less than a few minutes .i also feel like some of the skills are next to useless and were just added in for no reason.for example the engineering skill tree,one of the perks lets you unlock safes without the code and also hack turrets but the issue is the only safes i came across were at the beginning of the game where you needed level 6 engineering to open them when you could just get the code and the thing with hacking turrets is its absolutely useless and i feel like it was only added for an achievement because you don't see hack able turrets until the very end of the game  and you can remote hack them you _childDocuments_.review: Top notch, just like Terminator game from Teyon.Not short, but not pointlessly too long. Great balance between action and detective mode, which clearly takes cue from Arkham games, which is a compliment. Skill upgrades make a lot of difference in your survivability, and they come in bursts so you always feel like you have more than enough to get what you want, plus the most fun upgrades are sitting right there at the start of the tree.Story is pretty good, it is very respectful to the original IP and it fills in few holes and unknowns that all movies after the first left open.Action gameplay feels really good as well, you feel like this big hulking tank who doesn't have nearly the same mobility as any other enemy on the screen, and while your armor protects you very well, you aren't immortal, so its mainly about smartly using your cover and your abilities that keeps you alive.Finally, a special mention and praise has to go to locations and graphics. It feels like studio went inch by inch recreating famous locations from the movies. Its like visiting all those iconic locations, like the police station, the steel mill. the OCP headquarters (including the executive conference room AND the bathrooms!), the arcades from the sequel - heck even the Old Detroit street where Boddicker and the gang tested out their Cobra guns is where majority of the gameplay happens.Music and sounds are right on spot, and the feel of your bullets hitting the enemies is really satisfying.If there's a single, tiny issue to mention... I was hoping Boddicker would somehow get written into the story, even if just in a flashback.But, this is just me being nitpicky.Easily the best Robocop work since the first movie, far better than the TV show or the 2nd and the 3rd movie.If you're a fan - totally worth your cash in full.If you aren't - still totally worth your cash, as its easily one of the best double-A cyberpunk games on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Steam review, and I honestly have to say, amazing! I could not be any happier playing this. _childDocuments_.review: I am not sure how people are so positive about this game. Even though I haven't played it much (yet a bit more than Steam says), from the first minutes it was not just smelling but stinking with low budget. This is clearly a B grade game, not AAA and neither AA. The animations, especially in dialogue (of which there is plenty here) are very stale and unimpressive, some look too genuine, as if they were downloaded for free on a preset animations marketplace. Dialogue, so far, was also feeling quite cheap - most of the jokes here aren't funny at all and there are a lot of them. Some dialogues feel empty and strange, as if the writers didn't know how people actually think and talk. The graphics are quite nice, even though strange animations and sometimes empty / inadequate level design ruin it all for me. I personally also have some strange bluriness in the picture - as if I am playing without my glasses. I can see things but I can't see the details due to blurred out edges and colors that just slightly mix with each other. I tried configuring DLSS, gamma and graphics settings, but the game remains weirdly soapy for me - though I am not sure that it should be the case for everyone. The gameplay may be the strongest part here, since the weapons feel nice, the combat and movement are quite responsive and an overall feeling of a human shaped tank is there. The only problem I have is weird reload and aiming animations for some of the weapons. The ragdoll system could also use some polish, since all the enemies drop down like the haven't got a single bone in their body.All in all, I am not sure how to judge this game. I have only played 1.5 hours, so I don't really know if it gets better later on or not - but from what I've seen up to now, I am very unsatisfied. A lot of people say that it feels like a '80s film - I say that these people don't know how neither cheap games, nor '80s films feel like, so they mistakenly confuse these two things.I really wish I liked this game but I have to make a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun.   It gets the feel and vibe of the first movie on so many levels, that anyone familiar with it will find themselves smiling at the various references and callbacks.   Robocop handles like a clunky, janky tank, but that's good, because that's what he is.  This isn't Sandevistan combat, this is slow, methodical, visceral combat that feels as chunky as it is satisfying.   I never bothered using any pickup weapons because your standard issue pistol is just too much fun.  Plus you can get a lot of fun additional combat actions to make going no gun a fairly viable combat method if you want.  Bottom line.  Super fun, it hit all the nostalgia bits I wanted it to hit, but also provided a genuinely fun gaming experience as well.Had one bug that would crash the game when on a loading screen (usually when returning to the precinct), but other than that, game was stable and responsive.  Definitely worth a look if you are a fan of Robocop.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brilliant! Please make a SEQUEL!This game brought me so much joy, I can’t express how much I enjoyed it. Great care has been taken with every aspect of this game, and it shows.It is the story I have been craving as a RoboCop fan; great care has been taken to develop the story of Murphy’s humanity, as well as the wider social & moral issues. Outstanding! This is the true RoboCop 3! Having discussions with a psych was inspired!The music and locations are spot on. Such attention to detail! From the accurate police station to the other key movie locations, without spoiling anything, I loved being immersed in the world. The developers passion really shows, and I love them for it!I also loved actually being a police officer! It’s so easy to forget that Robo can actually put his gun away… I loved conversing with citizens, helping people, looking for clues and attending to crimes. But then there is the combat… brilliant fun! Very well executed. Especially given the excellent music and sound design.And it wouldn’t have been RoboCop without Peter Weller. Fantastic to hear his voice and see his face again!For me, this game was such a treat from start to finish, it was one of those rare games where I felt sad when it ended… I didn’t want it to end! I’ve just finished it after loving it for 28 hours, and have immediately commenced my second run!I can’t recommend this game enough! Well done guys! You deserve much praise! Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the classic RoboCop from my childhood, diving into the game brought back nostalgic memories of the '90s. How can one not appreciate the concept of a walking tank like RoboCop? While my recollection of the movies might be a bit hazy, certain characters like RoboCop's partner and the police boss remained vivid in my memory, alongside the iconic figure of RoboCop himself fighting crime.The game provides a solid FPS experience, although the movement mechanics occasionally felt a touch sluggish, especially during moments demanding quick reflexes. However, given the character's robotic nature, this deliberate movement style seemed to align well with RoboCop's persona rather than aiming for high-speed maneuvers. RPG elements are present but minimal; they add a nice touch, although some abilities might come across as less useful or unbalanced.In terms of the storyline, it held my interest sufficiently to motivate me to progress to the next phase of the gameThe shooting mechanics are satisfying, complemented by impressive sound design and a well-crafted lore. Being able to target specific body parts while shooting adds an extra layer of engagement. However, when it comes to bosses, opinions might vary. Regarding the bosses, opinions may differ, but I prefer not to delve into details here to avoid spoilers.  Overall, RoboCop offers a enjoyable FPS experience that captures the essence of the character and its world.

The only negatives (so far) that I can see are that the first time I booted it up I had a black screen and had to close it out, (fixed automatically on 3rd boot) and it has some pretty big gaps in the autosaves (seriously Devs - give us manual saves).  Otherwise, it's an enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: After creating the surprisingly good Terminator Resistance, Teyon returns by making an excellent Robocop game. Rogue City takes place between the second and third film and does a great job blending the satirical dark humor of the first movie with the corny camp of the second. Alex Murphy is still trying to reconcile if he is man or machine while OCP is once again causing mayhem across the city to try and make a quick buck out of it. The game does a great job recreating the dystopian Detroit portrayed in the movies and the police precinct looks exactly the way it does in the film. As with Terminator Resistance, Rogue City is a AA experience and looks like a remaster of a game that came out 10 years ago. Peter Weller comes back to voice act Robocop and really helps to sell the cheesy robotic dialogue that enhances the experience. The gameplay is pretty decent, Robocop is a walking tank so there is little to no cover to take advantage of, just the slow walk towards gangs of enemies as you tear them to pieces, the actual combat never wore out its welcome in the 15 hours it took me to complete it. The game has RPG mechanics that like with Terminator Resistance are kind of mediocre but do not hamper the experience. There is a mechanic in the game where you can use hardware pickups to upgrade Robocops ability to use his iconic Auto 9 handgun, it is a bizarre upgrade system that is hard to explain and pretty clunky, but with enough tinkering you become overpowered. By the end of the game my Auto 9 was full auto, had no recoil, and had unlimited ammo with no need to reload. I was able to fire so fast that my screen would tear occasionally when too much was going on on screen. There are a few set pieces in the game but mainly you are dropped into a hub spot in down town Detroit during various ours of the day while you do various quests and sidequests. It is kind of repetitive going through the same area several times but since you can actively talk with the citizens of the city you can see how Robocops action do effect the area overtime. There are various moments where Robocop has bouts of PTSD that cause the gameplay to glitch intentionally. While thematically it works and makes sense, from a gameplay perspective it can get annoying and was a slog to get through. TLDR, Robocop is a fantastic continuation of the Robocop series and a great sequel to the second film. It is really cool to see a developer have such a huge passion for a property and make a well thought out game like this on a small budget that honors the source material and not cost the consumer $70. I will be excited to see what other potential 80s or 90s property Teyon might tackle next, be it Judge Dredd, They Live, or even something out of left field like Bucakroo Banzai since they already convinced Peter Weller to work on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting this one. But I can't recommend it as a whole. If you're a fan of the original 80's Robocop, you'll feel right at home from the first frame. The multiplied screen news flash intro, the greedy and heartless OCP corporation, the filthy and crime ridden streets of Detroit, the familiar characters. Even Robo's  police station looks like a complete replica of the original, down to the green floor tiles at the reception hall. If you just want to experience that through the eyes of the heavy foot-stepped half machine half human officer Murphy, go right ahead. Unfortunately, where the settings ends and the game begins, there isn't much to go on about. Don't get me wrong, playing as the gloomy, self reflecting Robocop that we all grew to know and love is a blast. You really feel like you're a walking tank with an overkill  hand gun. Even the wonderful Peter Weller - the original Robocop actor - is back to provide Robo's one-liner responses. However, a lonesome talented actor might hold an entire film, but it doesn't work that way in a video game. The shootouts quickly become repetitive and predictable. Each location will throw tons of the same look-alike baddies at you to mow through. You could either use Robocop signature handgun or pick up the weapons dropped by your victims as you chop through them, which I don't recall Robocop ever did, however they all feel pretty lacking and out of context. You got your grayish/black matted police squad vehicle, which I didn't get to drive myself - at least not in the two hours I played. There's a pretty mundane skill tree that allows you to develop your skills. You got the obvious attack / defense skills you can develop, and some engineering / deduction skills next to it. You will utilize these skills as you patrol through small open areas - in between your main objective - while you going about handing parking tickets and scolding graffiti punks and kids at the arcade, or taking complaints at the station as a desk clerk. In addition there are some very limited optioned dialog which I guess suppose to be a sort of investigation like process. You could walk about hunting for floating question marks while in investigation area, while scanning those with your robo-vision will provide you with some information regarding your case and will open a new dialog option. When you're finish, you'll be giving the chance to pass a verdict as regarding to what to do with your subject of investigation - arrest him (uphold the law), or make him make amends by other means and in that way being more attached to your human side I guess. It all might sound nice on paper but felt very bland to execute. Graphic-wise the game is nothing to write home to, but personally it never bothered me that much as long there's a  to play. NPC's around the station and on the street looks pretty much brain-dead. Standing and staring somewhere or just bumping into you.It just felt like it could have been much more. It felt like half a game or a missing opportunity. The "Epic" feel to it -as it should be - was the thing that was the most absent from it. Overall, to me the entire experience felt like that if this was any other cop in any other city, it as a very mediocre game with a very mediocre score.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunplay is fun if a bit basic, and the environment can look pretty good in certain scenarios due to its Unreal Engine chops. AI isn't amazing but also doesn't get stuck really which is a plus.It's nice being able to pick up enemy weapons to mix up the combat, and it feels nostalgic being in the police station and seeing familiar characters. Very simplistic. Not a lot of depth to the campaign. Lots of rinse and repeat gunfights in tight areas and a simple levelling system.Each fight feels very simplistic due to having enemies spawn in set spots the moment you set foot in a specific room, and feels predictable DUE to how the environments are set up.The voice acting is a mixed bag, and Robocop's voice is hard to take seriously. His delivery can be very poor. It definitely doesn't hit the middle ground they found between human and robot in the films. The character's mouths don't follow what they're saying animation-wise, so it can also look a bit silly from that perspective.If you're fond of single player FPSes and willing to push through repetitive gunfights COD-style with a lot less environmental variety and scope, then give it a shot.If you're looking for a great FPS that's going to pull you in with a deep story-based campaign, then you'd probably do better looking elsewhere. It honestly just feels like a slog.

_childDocuments_.review: When you're actually allowed to shoot bad guys, outside of some odd spongy qualities to the enemies, the game is fun. However, for the 7 hours I've played, only 2 and a half or so of those have actually been shooting bad guys. The other 5 or so hours? Talking. Lots, and LOTS of talking, along with lots of pointless wondering around. The opening is the longest, and most fun stretch of time actually fighting bad guys. MOST of the game is actually spent wondering around fairly empty environments, performing fetch quests, and a LOT of boring, dialogue based encounters. Seriously, there is SO much talking, and the majority of it is incredibly bland or repeated. I LOVE visual novels, LONG narrative driven RPGs, and so on... so please don't think it's just a case of me not liking to read. I LOVE reading books as well, but everything about this game's story, writing, plot progression, and the rest are just really mindnumbing and uninteresting.  The plot twists so far can be seen a mile away, the bad guys range from horribly stock to downright annoying, and the only decent characters are the good guys, save for one or two who are fairly annoying at where I am at the moment in the game. Pickles is the best character so far.I LOVE narrative driven games, but this isn't it. This should have been a linear, action packed FPS game filled with gore, but so far? It's been incredibly disappointing, sadly. Not the worst game I've ever played, but incredibly underwhelming, and I've genuinely had to stop playing the game due to how... well, bored I've been. It's genuinely exhausting with how little happens in the down time.Also, the checkpoint system is downright garbage. There's no manual saving, just awful auto-saves that BARELY work. I played a long stretch of one of the dialogue sections (around 10 minutes of SLOW walking and lots of talking), quit the game to go grab some lunch since I thought it saved... and I had to replay that entire section AND nab all the XP bonus items. Genuinely awful, and made me incredibly frustrated.I dunno, I'd recommend waiting for a sale if you REALLY want to play it. I do plan on beating it, but I can only really handle small bursts at a time, or else I just become bored. Seriously, please trust me: this game has a LOT of dialogue, and it's not even interesting. If you expect nothing but action, you aren't going to get that.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a lot of games this year. Most probably had way bigger budgets than this game did. I am also an enormous RoboCop fan. I have a 4K Steelbook of the film, I have the new documentary on steelbook, I have the original Hot Toys figure of the original RoboCop, I have an original copy of the VHS on the way, and I watch it almost weekly. With all that being said, this is likely the best RPG game I have played this year. And that's not even me speaking as a RoboCop fan. Your choices do actually matter. You get to see the outcome of your decisions that you have made throughout the game. Albeit they are relatively simple cause and effect changes. Comparing it to Starfield, which is a big yikes for Bethesda's latest RPG release, I felt my choices in this game had more impact on the world and characters around me than they did in Starfield. Which is a massive compliment to this game. This game looks really good for not being a AAA game, and it is pretty well optimized compared to a lot of the releases we've gotten this year. There are some minor bugs, but most you can work around. And somehow the bugs seem to fit in with the aesthetic of the RoboCop. The devs nailed the feel of how RoboCop should play on the head. The gameplay is well done and always fun to play with. The blood and gore is outrageous and hilarious, just as it should be. There are so many things the dev team did right in this game. You can tell the entire team loves RoboCop and put their heart and soul into this game. I doubt we will get more Robo from them, but I hope we get a sequel. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It does shader compilation in the background, so when you first launch it just leave it to get this done (it's why CPU usage will be at 100% for a while and everything will be choppy).  On my 12600k it only took about a minute to get this done.On my system (12600k 3070 32gb RAM installed to SSD) I have max settings @ 1080p with vsync on and DLSS set to quality (I always do this since I can't tell the difference between quality and native), in the starting area it is using 66% GPU, 7.2gb VRAM, and about 40% across the board CPU usage.Has a FoV slider that goes to 100.  Google says there is an edit to get this higher, but 100 will be good enough for me.Has camera shake when you walk, but you can (seemingly) eliminate this in the game options.  You can also reduce the sound of your footsteps.There is no hard saving, not even at a computer or something like you could in Terminator Resistance, so only autosaves.  Autosaves quite frequently though, seems to happen every time I do a checkpoint of an objective or finish an objective.

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City is a first-person shooter game set in the RoboCop universe. According to IGN, the game is a “solid first-person shooter set in the RoboCop universe” and “the most authentic adaptation the series has ever seen”. The game’s developer, Teyon, has done an excellent job of capturing the look and feel of the original film. The game’s story is nothing groundbreaking, but it’s still a good game with a compelling thematic thread. The game is violent, as it should be, with arms and heads exploding like pressurised watermelons.Game8 gave the game a score of 72/100 and said that while the game excels in putting you in RoboCop’s shoes and features a pretty good story paired with nice graphics and great voice acting, its game play doesn’t feel nearly as good as the top FPS games of the last decade.CGMagazine gave the game a score of 8/10 and said that “RoboCop: Rogue City is a shockingly complete package with terrific gameplay and level design that offers room for player agency”.Push Square gave the game a score of 7/10 and said that “RoboCop: Rogue City is an incredibly faithful exploration of the armoured enforcer, a first-person shooter with an RPG foundation underpinning the action”.

Really enojyed my playthrough.However, I wouldn't buy it at full price. 30€ is acceptable.

_childDocuments_.review: is a grand love letter to the late '80s action-satire-drama that is RoboCop.Painstaking effort has been put into making sure that that the characters, as well as the city of Detroit, look and feel like their original movie counterparts as much as possible, with lots of details large and small faithfully recreated. (modern sensibilities might even call it clunky); instead of sprinting and jumping around the place as seems to be habit of modern twitch-shooters, Murphy's top speed is that of a brisk walk and his maneuverability not much better - his lumbering steps accompanied by a heavy thunk of hydraulics and a slight shake of the straight-from-the-80s neon-green HUD that excels in selling the illusion of controlling a stiff, robotic juggernaut.When bullets start to fly and weapons are drawn, , and the loud retort of the Auto-9, while slightly different from the movies, greatly emphasizes the violent power of the pistol capable of turning outlaws into chunky red mist.While the game does allow you to pick up any weapon you find off fallen criminals or in the environment, outside of a few niche occasions (such as dealing with far-away enemy snipers) I found myself relying almost exclusively on the iconic pistol in any situation - the ability to customize the Auto-9 with various enhancement chips throughout the game swiftly made most other weapon options redundant. - Rogue City also remembers the Cop part in RoboCop. Between missions you find yourself chatting with colleagues at the Detroit Police Department and helping them with various small tasks, or patrolling the city streets investigating crime scenes and ticketing petty crimes like vandalism or an illegally parked car., with criminal gangs looking to fill the market gap left by Cain's demise in the second movie, while the OCP Corporation continues its campaign to privatize the city and rebuild the neglected, crime-ridden ruins of Old Detroit into the corporate paradise of Delta City. In all this chaos, a new player joins the criminal underworld, with unexpected ties to one of the villains of the first movie... while Murphy finds himself struggling with the ghosts of his past, and coming to terms with his half-robot, half-man nature. feeling like a beautiful return to a major narrative core of the first movie, which was squandered in the second film by resolving the issue way too quickly, and then utterly forgotten in later iterations focusing solely on the violent action and the absurdity-reaching levels of dystopian satire.While the game's  especially in regards to cutscene animations , the minor jank is oddly reminiscent of the stop-motion animation of the original movies. to plague various setups, but I personally cannot comment on them one way or another - during my playtime I suffered only a single crash, and any framerate hiccups or other oddities I experienced were playing the older version of the Demo. , which I find myself recommending to any fan of the franchise without reservation. The love and care shown towards franchise proves that Teyon's previous success with  wasn't just a fluke, and Rogue City is easily the best video game adaptation of Robocop to date. I excitedly look forward to any other retro revivals Teyon might take on in the future. The game relies heavily on instilling nostalgia through faithful recreation of the source material, and its gameplay differences compared to modern shooter conventions and its double-A standard of quality can end up as hit-or-miss depending on personal preferences.

_childDocuments_.review: Went in with extremely low expectations, got an actual solid game instead. One hell of a glow up from that Rambo game Tayon made way back. The narrative, writing, and story is surprisingly decent. The real highlight is the combat though. Simple but very satisfying. The game encourages you to fight like how Robocop does in the movies. You can pick up enemies or big objects like motorcycles or dumpsters and throw them at people. As the game goes on enemies become more armored and start wearing helmets that counter headshots so always aim for the balls. Ball shots do the same amount of damage as headshots and the enemies never protect them even in late game. Use the full auto upgrade for the auto-9 to neuter enemies more quickly. 8.5/10, would happily castrate the entire male criminal population of Detroit again.

_childDocuments_.review: You’re a walking tank spouting cheesey one liners whilst shooting bad guys in the d*ck. Solid 10/10.Ah yes, the ultimate power fantasy:delivering parking citations!Finally! You can play as the bad guy.A little disappointed that I could not freely commit police brutality like in real life though.This will be a helpful review, Citizen.One of the greatest redemption arcs in gaming history. From Rambo to Terminator to now Robocop. Maybe the company that made Gollum, Kong & that Walking Dead game will have a redemption moment too, although they've got a lot more to make up for...These devs have mastered a niche yet strangely lucrative business model of making first person shooter game based off of 80s movies and it's refreshing to see them be so successful. You can really tell the people who made it love Robocop, the game has a soul and care to it that alot of other games seem to lack. I played it not remembering much about Robocop too and came away loving it, then rewatched the films and rediscovered my love for the franchise. It’s a really great little game and I hope they do more.This game is a fantastic power fantasy that does a pretty good job of making you feel like Robocop, even down to the sound he makes when he walks. It's so fun, it had me giggling like a schoolgirl the way Robocop just slowly stomps down corridors into enemies and starts blasting them. The world is nicely crafted and truthful to the source material, which makes exploring and doing quests nice. It's an amazing homage and fun arcade shooter. It's kind of refreshing to not having to find chest high walls for cover, stealth or other things. I just walk like a fridge on wheels into a room and start blasting.Everything just felt so authentic. From the slowness of Robocop, to having to do actual police work, to even having to go around the precinct and have people sign a card. The behavior of the other cops when everything was going from bad to worse. Some were crying, others were looking for other jobs. There was so much going on that made it feel that it just wasn't about blowing up bad guys. Also, yeeting dumpsters at bikers and land mines was way more fun that I ever anticipated.The authenticity of the police station was surreal. Robo had been my favorite movie when I was 6 years old. To walk around that police station so accurately portrayed and full of life was such an experience. The mundane nature of a lot of the tasks you do, just like real police work was also so much fun. The part where you stand at the podium in the police station had me going. Whenever I see people say they hated that part, I know that person hates absurdity and fun. I just appreciated that not every quest involved shooting. I think my favorite was Robo and Pickles hanging out talking movies like a couple of bros at the video store, that was hilarious. But now that I think of it, it ended with a big shootout too, so Bonus!The story. The world building. It's all so well done and satisfying but on a much smaller scale than most games these days. Shows how games don't need to be so massively open world and a billion boring repeatative missions. The story turned out surprisingly well, enough so that it feels like it could be a genuine Robocop movie. There’s so much nuance in the way the game does some incredible continuation of its over-the-top world, and yet manages to weave in contemporary concerns about police brutality, wealth inequality, and other issues that have increased relevance. Plus the attention to detail, actually enforcing the prime directives through game play (you can't just run around guns blazing and shooting everyone), the Auto 9 always being the best gun (especially if you upgrade it). Even Robo's slow walk felt good and didn't make the game a slog.The combat is fun, the world is so lovingly crafted to the first two films, and there is a certain charm about it that reminds me of old school semi-open first person shooters like Deus ex.I loved interacting with the fellow cast back at the police station, I loved wandering around that little Detroit block and getting into shenanigans with side characters solving side plot threads that can either feel pretty major or can be something as ridiculous as Robocop finding lost cats. And I absolutely loved going through so many of those recreated locations from the first two films to have firefights where just everything is reactive. There isn't a piece of the environment that doesn't scatter with debris when you shoot it and it's awesome. I also really wasn’t expecting a lot of the depth of some of the side characters. I liked that there were 4 characters whose outcomes were determined by your interactions with them. Adds a ton of depth to the story, and gives the game a ton of replay value. Seeing how your actions affect these characters in different ways is just really cool and makes me want to go back and play again to see the possible changes. Also some of the side quests were surprisingly good. As a movie collector/fan, the quest in the video store with Pickles was really charming. Brought that heavy 80’s VHS vibe that Robocop has always had.Definitely more depth than I would have expected and really shows that the satire of the period and original film was not lost on the developers. I also loved that the political choices/path was so gray. Like, both options had major pitfalls and it frankly made me personally want to remain A-political as a roleplay of Robo. They really nailed the sense of responsibility you’re supposed to feel as Robocop. Neither side sees you as a human, and they both have their own agenda. But Robo is a genuine hero, so he’s going to do what he thinks is right, despite no one really caring for him. Because he’s the only one willing to accept the responsibility.It’s a game I actually look forward to playing. The animations are janky as all hell in dialogue and cutscenes... but the game has a certain double A charm to it for me as a late 80s millennial who grew up with RoboCop. Even if I hadn't, I think I would definitely still enjoy it for what it is. Basically parts of this game just really remind you that it's a budget title, but none of it outweighs the amount of love and care that goes into this game that ultimately pulls you into it and immerses you in it even if there are things that are distracting. I had a ton of fun. It’s MUCH better than I expected and would recommend. It’s not perfectly polished but I didn’t have any horrible issues and it’s to 100%. Who would’ve thought that a 15-20 hour Robocop game would be the best RPG/FPS of the year. The 7/10 licensed video game is back and I couldn’t be happier!As a fan that was reminded of his love for this world thanks to this game though, it’s a 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game very much.Voice actors are great!The sound level of voices changes a lot, some are quite low (Antonowsky) some are very loud (Becker) which is a bit annoying.Sounds are very good in my opinion. There was nothing that sounded wrong, cheap or misplaced.Graphics are great. Only some elements are only ok, which is some smoke, dust and mist look a bit cheap when they are moving around. Also, sometimes objects like cars or NPCs missing shadows underneath and stand out because of that.But overall there is a lot love to details.And, I have to mention this, I adore the gore...really.And these two elements, what you see and what you hear, generates a certain atmosphere that I enjoyed greatly. The debris, scrap, rubbish and dirt covers the rundown cityscape perfectly. What stopped me so that I take my time to look closer was the scenery, the items and things standing around. It looked so real for coming out of the 80/90s. I found my old Epson 9-needle printer sitting on some desks in the game, quite unreal for me.What surprised me was also the detailed walls and floors. As an example, the partly wet linoleum floor in the hospital as it was just cleaned some minutes before. The light reflection of wet and not wet parts looked amazingly real. And even better the linoleum had scratches as in reality.Gameplay is solid, skill tree is straight forward. The additional Auto-9 circuit board and chips was not bad but seemed unnecessary to me. A circuit system were you had to add circuits and chips to enlarge the skill tree would have been better in my view.The actual skill tree and this boost-bonus-construction-kit is to separate from each other.Story is decent, though not an eye opener and no real twists, but otherwise this might not have been right with the settings for a Robocop tale. The last battle felt too short and was over too suddenly. Overall the game felt a bit short, 1/3 longer would have been better.Although then it would be longer in story-telling than the movies of that time. And that might be the decision behind that.Yeah, this does not destroy my impression of the game.Initially I had a lot of problems with crashes and BSOD, where I wanted to refund the game. Steam denied as it was more than two weeks in my library, although I had only 20 minutes of “playtime”, but these were only trials to get the game running. And I was in contact with the game support that two weeks. Which was cumbersome as it seemed no one read my description, because I got always the same advice what I should do, which did not work. Eventually I received decent advice and could finally run the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If your game has a "Detect" button so they can check my specs and set my graphics accordingly, I expect that to give me 60fps and if it doesn't the feature doesn't work and you need to go back to the drawing board. I hope to one day play this game and change this review to positive but until then I'll just be waiting for patch news. This game's release makes me really happy, and when I finally got it, it's really sad. I've been looking forward to it since it was announced, Robocop is one of my favourite films ever made, and this game won't stop stuttering even when it looks like nothing but pixels on the lowest settings. Robocop is just in pieces hanging out at an abandoned factory, unable to walk or run and Anne Lewis nowhere in sight to help repair him.Okay so Anne Lewis is actually a person named Fertlou who made a guide and an ini file for this game that let me run it and it doesn't look too bad either. When I put it on it's lowest settings it looked bad and ran bad but with the Ini file it's perfectly acceptable and at 60fps. I have been really enjoying the game now. I try to find a key selling point for games I really enjoy and here it is "You can fire a Kalashnikov as Robocop" and if you don't understand why that's awesome then maybe you just wouldn't like this game, I honestly enjoy the menial police work as well, it's clear Teyon has a reverence for the character and the choices you are given all feel suitably "Robocop" things to do. So far, I really enjoy it now thanks to Fertlou, I eagerly await an official patch that can improve upon what they did. I changed my review to positive because I really like it even if I used unofficial mods to play it.Since beating the game I might just say it's my game of the year for 2023. A fantastic first person shooter and a bit of a Robo Playing Game, with a really cool level up system, and where other games have you breaking into safes to find treasure, here you find evidence of crimes for exp, perfectly fitting into the character you are playing. There are several examples of that, such as not being able to enter a place due to a lack of a warrant. I could not stop being reminded of fallout new vegas, the destitute buildings and amped up junkies, and the ending is literally the same structure as fallout new vegas just done in a robocop news broadcast and I have no complaints because it wraps up the plot and I wouldn't mind more games doing the same, wrapping up every story and sidequest with a little epilogue cutscene.I'm sure most fans are upset they can't drive around Detroit in the car but that's just the kind of thing that's out of the budget of this game and in the end I don't think it's needed. It'd be cool to drive around but I'm sure I'd get sick of L.A. Noire driving way sooner than I did just walking around cleaning up the streets on foot.My initial experience with this game was that I couldn't play it, and even with the ini file I mentioned above the game looks a bit weird in some areas, mostly day time looks a lot worse but everything is pretty in tact otherwise. The visuals of UE5 are actually really impressive, there is a consistent smear and reflection on your vision because robocop has a visor and a smudge on it. It's really subtle and not bothersome but it's those kind of crazy reflection details that you get with the engine, the game still runs really poorly on most PCs, my brother can't play it, most of my friends can't, you just need a new graphics card. Even with said upgrade this game has a bit of jank, some bad bugs. Multiple times when a scripted event was supposed to happen, like an NPC running to an objective point, wouldn't happen, the game would just get stuck on the objective like "clear out the room of enemies" and after doing it nothing happens and I have to reload to a checkpoint. It happened like 5 times throughout my entire play-through. Other than that secondary characters look not so good, be it polygons misplaced in their mouth, or their pupils being gone because the reflections of their eyes are just going crazy, the only characters that look really good are RoboCop and the main villain. Some other characters are passable but there's little things with all of them, especially Anne Lewis and the Police Chief which have a rogue one thing going on. This is RoboCop 3, and it's awesome that it's a video game, the story I found really enjoyable, good science fiction concepts, a pretty good villain, a corporate slimeball that is quite literally the most hate-able character I've seen in a while. I really enjoyed the introduction of Dr. Blanche and the ongoing exploration of RoboCop's humanity (or lack thereof if you choose) is what this game's story needed and it delivered.I think my biggest problem is the Old Man, I'm not sure what you could do without him in the plot but Dan O'Herlihy is dead and the guy you got to do his voice is really not cutting it. Even though Anne Lewis looks not so great I couldn't tell it wasn't Nancy Allen, the recast was the right move there, but The Old Man has a really distinct voice that wasn't captured here, and having him come back as RoboCop 2 for a final boss, while really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome, it's just not the right way to bring back RoboCop 2 and seems like cheap fan service where everything else in this game felt earned. I wish they could have brought back Ronny Cox or Kurtwood Smith as a villain but both of them died in the first movie, idk I just guess I wanted better actors and more of them, Peter Weller was fantastic and it's great to have RoboCop 3 as it should be.Everyone is asking what Teyon should do for their next fan-service licensed game, it's been suggested already I'm sure, but we need a Dredd 2012 sequel starring Karl Urban. I'm not sure if that's possible with the resources and producers they have, maybe that needs to be higher budget, I'm not sure what Karl Urban's asking price is, or how much he wants to do a project like that. Here's my other suggestion, any and all terrible action B movies. Cast someone as Charles Bronson and make a f'cking Death Wish game where you blast "criminal scum" indiscriminately. The Torch Heads really captured the 80s B movie drug addict goons without a speck of humanity, do more of that, it's hilarious and iconic. _childDocuments_.review: I haven't written a review in a minute, but Robocop: Rogue City is a triumph in the field of games based on entertainment licenses. It's a good movie video game! That's all you really need to know, but I'll go into more detail below.Robocop: Rogue City feels like it's come out of a bygone era. It's a semi-open world mission-based first person shooter based on a movie series from the 80's. In execution, it comes with all the things you expect from a straightforward FPS - the shooting feels good, the movement feels suitably RoboCop, and enemies are fun bags of meat to shoot, throw, and punch all around old Detroit.On top of this solid gameplay, there is a hefty upgrade system, with EXP and level-ups and everything. You can level up your RoboCop however you want. 10 hours in, my RoboCop is an unstoppable tank, with all my upgrades in defense and health. With a whole slew of build options, you just go build your RoboCop. All in all, it's a good game. The glitches are few and far between, or funny enough to elicit a giggle instead of a groan. If you like robocop and shooters just buy the game it's good go do it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this a neutral review if I could. But the performance is quite honestly, terrible and DLSS did nothing for me. I experienced some strange lighting and texture bug whenever I used it. There's a section when you exit the Steel Mill in one of the game's early levels and you encounter the Sniper enemies for the first time. (♥♥♥♥ them btw.) Performance here is some of the worst I've ever experienced and there seems to be no fix at all. I enjoyed the early sections a lot, but once the mercenary enemies make an appearance in the game, there's a noticeable difficulty spike and you really start to see the cracks in the system. Some sections genuinely feel unfair. It feels like they want this game to be an immersive sim, in how you tackle some of these encounters but the possibilities are just not there. The slow and heavy methodical movements of Robocop that make you feel like a badass in early segments, make you feel helpless. As these very movements feel awkward and limiting now.Facial animations are very poor and a lot of the voice acting is suspect. For instance, I swear the entire Torchhead gang are voiced by a single dude and it makes combat segments hilarious and ridiculous, since the enemies love to talk and you have the same guy talking the entire time. The story is not bad, if you like Robocop you'll enjoy it. Main antagonist was more irritating than anything since they use the same gimmick every time you meet him and it became stale fast. Especially since the gimmick itself was predictable. Final boss was cool though, wish there was more of that honestly.The 'morality' system in the game was very well done though. Instead of a good or bad system, since you're playing as Robocop, you work within the bounds of his morality and the devs did a good job here. Some of the themes explored are interesting but they don't delve deep enough. It's not an RPG or anything, but the choices you make seem to have some interesting consequences, whether it's truly deep or not is a matter for debate as I have no plans to replay the game and find out.If you want a good movie fps game. Go play Terminator Resistance instead. Which is made by the same people, funnily enough.

_childDocuments_.review: There are plenty of games these days having been released unfinished with the "release now, fix later" mindset and I'm glad this is NOT one of them. I like the attention to detail and faithfulness to the movies: the visuals, the sounds, the writing and the humor all proves that the people behind the game actually cared to bring us the best RoboCop experience in video game form. The game also encourages exploration to find hidden items and sidemissions, and rewards you with skill points that can be very useful on the long run. The "choices matter" aspect of the game is also very nice and provides great replay value.A minor complaint from me is that sometimes it wasn't obvious to me where I would start the game from if I restarted from a checkpoint, or quit the game and went back to it later. The game does tell you on quitting that "Unsaved progress will be lost", but how do I know at what point the game last autosaved? _childDocuments_.review: After Terminator Resistance, Teyon delivers yet another licence masterpiece with Robocop Rogue City. The game brings everything together I absolutely love: Smooth first-person-shooter gameplay with great sound, even greater visuals and extremely atmospheric leveldesign with a ridiculous ammount of attention to detail and even more 80s and 90s nostalgia.The story takes place at some point between Robocop 2 and 3 and is one of the very few weaker aspects of the game. The main antagonist may look exactly like Die Hard Hans Gruber, but that doesn't mean that he is just as charasmatic and entertaining as Alan Rickman's famous character, let alone a Charles Boddecker from Robocop 1 or Caine from Robocop 2. The plot is basically "Robocop shoot bad guys" and for a plot as basic as this the game is very long for first-person-shooter standards (close to 100% percent with almost all the sidequests, achievements etc. took me roughly about 18 to 20 hours), so the story starts to drag seriously about half-way through.The voice-acting, soundeffects and music are good, if not great (they even got Robocop himself Mr. Peter Weller to voice himself) and the visuals are even better, for the most part, but as was the case with Terminator Resistance, you can tell from the presentation that Teyon doesn't have Triple A budget levels yet: The animations are noticeably robotic, which is fine for Robocop of course, but not for the rest of the all human characters. There were two or three little gamebreaking bugs as well, which required a reload from the last checkpoint, but nothing major.Another slightly disappointing point is the gunplay, which feels a bit lackluster and not as impactful as it should in a Robocop game. Of course there is Robocops modified signature Beretta and a lot of other awesome 80s guns (Desert Eagle, SPAS-12, Uzi, AK-47 and more), but Robocop's primary weapon is downright overpowered with unlimited ammo and various options to upgrade it, while all the other weapons lack impact and feel comparatively useless. The destructible environments and gory splatter effects on the other hand capture the satirical over-the-top depiction of violence in the first two movies quite well, so in the end the shooter mechanics don't compare to Call of Duty or Doom Eternal, but are solid at the very least.The rest of the gameplay isn't the most innovative or varied, either. Teyon went the same way like in Terminator Resistance: The levels are no linear tubes, but small semi-open world hubs with quite a few optional sidequests that require some detective work in the form of scanning the environment for clues and talking to suspects and witnesses. You'll visit some of the locations repeatedly over the course of the game and most of them are mere slow-paced interlude levels with a lot of talking and little to no action at all, so even tough it is exciting to explore those levels at first, you'll be literally craving for the next shoot-out during your later revisits.What makes Robocop Rogue City so amazing is the super-immersive atmosphere. The visual style matches the movies perfectly and the game also catches the hilarious satirical humor of the movies: Some of the sidequests even include rescuing cats or handing out tickets for illegal parking. Just like Terminator Resistance, Robocop Rogue City is a simplistic shooting gallery first and foremost for the most part, but the almost flawless artstyle, unmatched care for detail and incredible faithfulness to the source material make this game much more than just the sum of it's parts and show that in some rare cases style over substance is not necessarily a bad thing. The game can get a tiny bit monotonous and dull now and then, so objectively you can't go higher than a 6/8, however, my personal preferences and nostalgia for 80s SciFi- and action movies bring it darn close to a subjective 7/8. It's nothing special for people who are not into the Robocop movies, but you don't necessarily have to be a Robocop fan to enjoy a very well-made licence-first-person-shooter. And in that regard, Robocop Rogue City is one of the most faithful and accurate licence games ever. It really brings the 80s back to life and is one of those games that I really felt the urge to take my time with to soak in all the details and explore every corner just to get the absolute maximum out of the game.When it comes to licences, those guys at Teyon know exactly what they are doing, so give them the Alien-, Predator- and Die Hard licences immediately. Don't ask questions. Just do it. Or there will be...trouble.__________________________________________________________________________ROBOCOP ROGUE CITYGenre: First-Person-ShooterRelease: Q4 2023( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay isn't actually as slow as the trailers made out - that was one thing putting me off. It's simple, but... fun. It's hard to put a word to or describe it, but it just... works. It's not complex, it's not bloated with customiseable features. It's just... go get em. Dead or alive they're coming with you. No bs.But the thing that really surprised me is the effort that's gone in to other areas of the game.I just walked past a cat pushing a bucket off a bit of scaffolding. That didn't need to be there. But it was. The attention to detail in environments really isn't something people are mentioning but it's great.The humanising elements of Robocop, and him remembering he's Murphy, are done very well indeed. It's hard to do it justice in quick words.And it has an overall vibe and charm from all of that that just makes it... great. You can tell this is made by those who loved the franchise/concept.It seems to be well optimised for me too - running it on quite high settings on a 1080, which I did not expect from AA jank.But, on the jank, a few things to note. The lip sync is a bit off, the voice acting is good but occasionally terrible, and for instance the very first guy you see has his arm clipping through an AUG. If you've played through the 360 era you've seen worse. I've had a crash or two too, and there's no manual save feature to be sure you're good. But otherwise? Genuinely a fantastic and surprisingly good game. It's one of those games where it's greater than the sum of its parts. It just all... works.Maybe wait for it on sale, and see if you can buy it for a dollar. It's sure worth a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a massive fan of the original Robocop Movies from the 80's starring Peter Weller. So for me this game had a lot to live up to and OH BOY did it deliver!!I enjoyed every second of this game and didn't want it to finish, some have criticised the graphics but for me they were perfect and felt right with the 80's grindhouse effect. This game was like playing a new movie with me at the helm and it was everything I could of hoped for and more. It had the perfect balance between action and simple puzzle solving and it had a simple progress system that was easy to follow and rewarding. At the same time I could why a younger gamer might get frustrated with the simplicity and find the graphics and game play a little dated. I don't usually go after achievements but this game had me wanting to do it all. I'm just gutted its all over because I would happily pay for a DLC to get more of this gameplay. 10/10 game for me!! _childDocuments_.review: Not sure if i should recommend this game or not. The campaign is rather short, i did miss some side missions by mistake which could've add a few more hours, but there are at least 1-2 hours I wasted being afk.PROS:- satisfying kills- interesting "crafting"- has the RoboCop feel to itCONS:- the maps are rather small, they only take a while to do because you walk rather slow, there is a fast walking which i guess makes sense for RoboCop- i had 2-3 crashes, one felt game breaking but it wasn't. and while you can't save, you can load checkpoints and autosaves- some frame drops in 1-2 cutscenes in the first 3 hours of playing, and 1 instance of frame drops during fighting, in the same first 3 hours, along with 1-2 of the crashes, BUT apart from this i didn't notice and other performance issues- i'm pretty sure some stuff can't be looted because they're right in the area you're supposed to go to and when you arrive there the cutscene starts- no NG+, this is a personal CON, i would've liked a new game to continue adding skill points and be able to do other side missions In the end I had fun, i'm recommending it only because it's a good start imo, and i wish the Devs would do a sequel/DLCs and significantly expand the city, like 2 or 3 times bigger, however for some people (probably me as well) it may not have enough playtime for how much the game costs, i'm writing this review immediately after i finished the game so i'm not sure i have my final opinions on the game yet, especially since i really loved RoboCop as a kid, so i may edit my review in the future if change my feelings about the game
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Tech-side is whack but its a great game. Let me start with the big flaw of the game: It's technical point, the Engine. It is actually really bad. I had a few crashes, the graphics and facial expressions are very outdated and I had some glitches. But all of this just proves how much of a gem this game is. This game proves that fancy graphics or a AAA price tag are not important today. The shooting is fun. You feel like the walking tank you are and have different abilities at your disposal like dash, flash, shield and slow motion aswell as the ability to grab enemies/objects and throw them. The world and other gameplay is very fitting to the narrative. Imagine this: In one level you leave a trail of blood and gore and in the next you give tickets to cars that park where they shouldn't and do the robot dance for kids. The story is good and feels like a true successor to the first two movies. I was even surprised by the last boss fight and how fitting it was. When I think about tedious things like walking around the city looking for misdemeanors I can't help but see the intended, boring and tedious shift of a cop. The walking around was actually a nice break from shredding bad guys. I highly recommend this game to anyone interested. The developers squeezed the last bit of fun out of the limited resources they had and used it well.
