_childDocuments_.review: I have watched the movies, Prime Directives, and TV shows hundreds of times (Except RoboCop 3, once was enough). This game brought the mood of the originals to life. I have been stomping around my house like RoboCop since and I can't stop. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Just quite good. Wouldn't recommend it for full price (£45 at launch) but I would do if on sale in the £15-20 mark, particularly because it's so short (12 hours to complete). + Immersive. Good voice acting. True to the RoboCop canon. + Gunplay is good and the action is fun. Good finale. + Some good mini-games such as the PCB upgrade 'puzzles' for your Auto-9, bomb defusing and challenge levels (where you get bonuses for out-competing allies). + Frequent patch fixes so far and stable game. + Good destruction, incorporation of throwable objects and gore. This all feels quite robust / weighty.  - Sidequests and extensive dialogue options are really quite dull. Whilst probably aiming to flesh out the meat-and-bones FPS aspect of this game, they just felt like a tedious chore. I'm not certain, but the choice of dialogue options didn't appear to affect the trajectory of the game or provide any tangible reward, rendering them a bit pointless. - The environment feels rudimentary and NPCs making up the public are lifeless, giving the world a cold and empty feel. - Graphics don't appear any more advanced than, say, Fallout 4 from 2014. - Some AI could be a bit basic (e.g. the ED-209 was easy to outwit by just keeping out of its visual range). - Collecting random evidence (e.g. stolen wallets) lacked any fun. Neutral comments:~ Play it on at least Hard if you've played similar games before. ~ There seemed little point in using any other weapon other than the Auto-9, apart from the occasional rocket launcher or suchlike.

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly enjoyable mix of modern FPS elements with character progression and fun police-procedural side missions. The dev team has an understanding of the license -- violent, but satirical -- and the game delivers tons of fan service with Easter eggs and callbacks a plenty. It's great to hear Peter Weller back in the role, and the sci-fi story and various side plots make sense in that action-game-based-on-an-action-movie way. It's a skillful, respectful use of the license and a heck of a lot of fun throughout.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: The studio behind the recent video game sequel Robocop: Rogue City did a reasonable job of recapturing some of the major beats from the movie - rehiring Weller for Robo's voiceovers, a voice actor who sounded very close to the Murphy's original partner Anne Lewis and Sgt Reed, and then a string of NPCs modelled on the cops and bad guys from RC1+2 squawking about striking and nuke. Even Casey Wong, the newscaster character, makes a return to walk us through events as they unfold. However the edge of the originals is dulled; they missed out on all but a single oblique voice reference to the 'I'll buy that for a dollar' skits, and there's no nudity or anything too crass, presumably out of fear of provoking the woke.  There's a lot of the polish and detail missing that we take delight in from the movies, you can easily just wave it off as missing for budgetary reasons - the city feels small and unpopulated, even for an area of real estate that's being purposefully devalued.  It would have been nice to see creeps scurry away from their deals and graffiti as soon as they see you thumping towards them, more delinquents, more 3rd person shots of Robo shooting stuff with his hand in the air.  What happened to the hand cannon attachment?  A few more layers of plot on what was going on at OCP in the wake of the old Man's health issues would have been cool, and just general world building stuff.  Encountering ED209 in the wild would have been dope, not to mention some of the other weapon tech mentioned in the films.  I'm sure it's all budgetary, but what remains is a decent Robocop story, with most of the working parts, that ties in with established canon and feels Robocoppy. In terms of gameplay, though, the 'rp' progression system is pointless, at least 4 of the skill trees literally do nothing for you, the auto-9 customisation gimmick is actually ok but the gacha style method for 'refining' the bonuses into better ones seems half thought-out since you could wind up without enough of them to actually use any motherboard and there seems to be no way of getting more besides linear story progression and no way to repeat levels for achievement hunting - and no new game + mode.Definitely get it on sale if you remotely love Robocop 1 snd 2, hell if you're a R3 fan, still get it but pay full price like the freak you are.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Well here we are, a RoboCop game that doesn't instantly suck out of the gate.  Lets do this!As always, the game is divided into the Good, the Bad and the Ugly. The Good.  This game is as quintessentially RoboCop as you can get. Sound effects, Music, weapons, people, the Auto-9, the Ka-Thunk, all of it.  Graphically it's pleasing (but not mind blowing) and it's story is exactly what a 80's action flick demands (that is to say, superfluous.)  If you are a RoboCop fan, it's very much a dream come true. You get to not only do basic police work, you get to do a lot of "I wish I saw" moments in this game. For example, 'I wish I saw RoboCop and ED209 fight side by side!', "I wish RoboCop got to use the insane Cobra rifles!" "I wish I got to fight RoboCop 2 in an epic battle!" and more. The music is fantastic, well paced and ripped right from the movies.  It's a fans wet dream. The Bad: The guys who made this had a limited amount of funds to make it, so obviously the shortfalls came in the form of things like voice acting, facial mapping, and lip syncing. When someone talks you can only tell by the voice over.  The lack of voice actors is also noticeable since a lot of baddies have -exactly- the same voice.The only downside to combat is grenade spam. There is a lot of it.  it makes the game feel like a night in a Swedish city. The Ugly: This game takes place between RoboCop 2 and 3, or as many fans say, "After RoboCop 2".  Instead of following into the more kid friendly tone, this game dives head first into the gritty violence of the first two movies.  Much like Ghostbusters, this game serves as the 'real' third movie that the fans of the franchise actually asked for.  When it comes to actual gameplay, it's a truly good game, giving you the 'feel' of being RoboCop, right down to the slow plodding pace.  The only downside of the game is that there could have been perhaps a third more gameplay and story before this game overstayed it's welcome. Elements of the gameplay that were truly fun sometimes only appear once in the game (making me want to play the first mission over and over just for the joy of throwing gangers out of twenty story windows).  You only ever get to compete with others twice in the game, ect. I hope there will be more content for this game, but overall, it's still worth getting and playing. Just don't be upset that whenever someone speaks, it's one of three actors, they all suck, and the lip sync is terrible.  Only RoboCop sounds good in this game. I wish there were more quips he could make during combat too.  If you are an 80's action fan or a RoboCop fan, get this game! otherwise, wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up because it's Robocop, however it could be a lot better. The story/missions feel clunky and patched together without flowing smoothly. It does improve as it goes along but the first few levels are a bit hard to follow. The gameplay is a standard 1st person shooter affair which again initially seems disjointed and overly complicated until you unlock the special upgrades for your gun (ie the auto-reload) which then makes you feel like Robocop. There's plenty of Easter Eggs for fans of the original films and nice subtle touches like Alex Murphy's portrait in the Lost in Line Of Duty wall display (and the database). There's also some 'comedy' missions like getting a card signed by everyone and fetching a towel for one of your colleagues who was taking a shower and forget to take a towel with him.There are elements of free-roam whilst around the town and police station parts but the game would have been much better as a full open world free roam where you could choose to go wherever you wanted to stop crime as you see fit, rather than having to strictly follow the story.Worth playing if you're a fan.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Robocop, I'd 100% recommend this game. It does fan-service perfectly, without shoe-horning stuff into the game just for the sake of it. It has lots of more subtle nods to the movies. The soundtrack is pretty good, especially during the Mall section . Old Detroit looks amazing, as does the precinct.It really does look beautiful. The reflections are quite strong, and it does follow the "puddles = next gen" formula, but it really does look good. The models for the main characters are very nice.I saw a lot of people dissing the soundtrack before release, and it's no Robocop 1 soundtrack, obviously, but the themes throughout the game aren't bad (as I said, especially in the Mall section of the game) and I don't personally mind the main theme, even if it is quite subdued.There is a good variety of upgrades, both for Robocop and the PCB for his gun.It really is faithful to the Robocop universe. A lot of love has gone into this game.I like the little scanning minigames, they remind me of the old CSI video games for example.I really like the fact it's single player. I don't have anything against DBD but the famous franchises have seemed to follow that kind of formula recently and I'm particularly upset about Evil Dead as I love that franchise.Here's the main one:It runs like total ass. I'm sorry but no matter how many updates this game has had, it runs terribly. Funnily enough, if you put the game on minimum settings, you'd expect it to run a bit better, but that's not the case at all. There's a few settings that you should actually put to Good or Ultra in order to get the game to run better. I actually followed a guide from someone here on Steam. It is a little better than when it first released but you will still get a lot of choppiness, and even the occasional UE crash, especially when changing between areas. Although we got Dr. Weller and a few other OGs, I would've liked to have heard Anne Lewis' original voice for this game. The voice actor that they chose did a brilliant job, I just wish it was the OG!Some of the upgrades aren't brilliant. The stun upgrade is actually worse fully upgraded than it is normally, imo.There are major problems with some of the NPC models. Teeth and lips glitching through the face, things like that. This has never been addressed. A minor thing but I wish Robocop's vision would highlight items on the map such as Nuke, photos, newspaper clippings etc. Even if you had to fully upgrade it to do so.--Overall it is definitely very faithful to the subject matter, is gory enough and really does feel like the movies. It looks fantastic and I hope the team learned some things in order to make their next games run a bit better. New Game + was the perfect update, and when fully upgraded you well and truly feel like Robocop, absolutely unstoppable. I can't see online, I have checked, but some of the Torch Head voices sound exactly like Ed from Ed, Edd and Eddy. I'd really like to know who voices the Torch Heads, haha.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like being in a sequel film of the original Robocop film. It's both cheesy 80s flick, and gritty dystopia. It's visually pretty good, and the gameplay is fun. It's a great mix of (robo)cop roleplay, investigation, and deadly gunplay.Dislikes: The animations are consistently a bit wonky, but can be overlooked. There are boss-type enemies that are a bit too bullet-spongey for my liking.I should point out that, while I enjoyed the gun-play, I was driven by the story and questing throughout. Blowing stuff up and blowing off heads is fun, but were it not for the story-writing and characters, I'd have lost interest overall.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously, this is a very solid game. I went in expecting to refund it and was pleasantly surprised. I will say, find a key online for $30ish and you will feel even better about the purchase being a single player only experience. Other than that, I don't have any complaints. As someone who enjoyed Robocop, as a child, I was stoked to find that same feeling and atmosphere in this game. I am guessing it is set shortly after the events of RC1, still in Detroit. You get plenty of 90s movie one liners and the bravado you would expect from the genre. Is the story/voice acting gripping and award worthy? Absolutely not, but if we're being honest, I doubt that is why anyone is here, anyhow. One thing about the story that I like is that your choices in interactions with NPCs have a direct correlation to future interactions with people. So, the nuts and bolts of the game feel like a classic/old school type FPS where you simply shoot things on your way to objectives, mixed with some RPG-like story elements on your journey. As someone who does not like RPGs, I can say that is  not enough to detract from the fun of running and gunning as Robocop.PROS:Weller is voice acting RobocopClassic FPS gunneryHeadshotting enemies with the classic Auto-9 pistol is a blastSolid graphics20+ hours of gameplayAtmosphere is loyal to Robocop moviesCONS:Singlepalyer onlySlightly overpricedTL:DR If you liked the original Robocop movie and want to roll through enemies in true Robocop fashion, with Peter Weller in your ear, voicing the legend, you are going to have a good time with this game. As someone who was on the fence about this purchase, I don't regret it, at all. NOTE: I have seen some complaints of crashes in this game. I played through it twice and I only crashed once, while streaming and bouncing in and out of the game and other windows. Not sure if I can blame the game for all that.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Robocop franchise, I couldn't wait to dive into Robocop: Rogue City, hoping to relive the gritty, futuristic world of Detroit as the iconic cybernetic law enforcer. Unfortunately, my excitement quickly turned to disappointment as I progressed through the game.Graphically, Robocop: Rogue City delivers on its promise, presenting a visually stunning rendition of the dystopian Detroit landscape. The neon-lit streets, towering skyscrapers, and menacing robotic adversaries all contribute to an immersive experience that feels straight out of the movies.However, where the game falls short is in its storyline and overall polish. While the narrative attempts to capture the essence of the Robocop universe, it ultimately feels uninspired and fails to engage players on a meaningful level. Characters lack depth, and the plotline unfolds in a predictable manner, leaving much to be desired in terms of storytelling.One of the most glaring issues with Robocop: Rogue City is its lack of challenge. Even on higher difficulties, the game feels overly easy, with enemies posing little threat to Robocop's formidable arsenal. This lack of difficulty diminishes the sense of accomplishment and fails to provide the adrenaline-pumping action that fans of the franchise crave.Furthermore, the game suffers from a noticeable lack of polish, with occasional bugs and glitches disrupting the gameplay experience. From clipping issues to AI inconsistencies, these technical shortcomings detract from the overall enjoyment of the game and highlight a rushed development process.In conclusion, while Robocop: Rogue City has its moments of graphical splendor, its lackluster storyline and underwhelming polish ultimately prevent it from living up to its potential. I would only recommend purchasing it on a 50% off or greater sale, as it simply doesn't justify its full retail price. With a resounding "meh" rating, this game unfortunately misses the mark for die-hard Robocop fans.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game to laugh at it. Seemed like the perfect intersection of graphical fidelity and unoriginality. The best effects on the best engine, in a current-year linear single-player FPS? How could this be anything but average?Many folks seem to be praising the game for forcing a slower pace, but there are plenty of "waddling FPS" games out there. The gameplay is truly nothing new, just a refined single-player experience.And yet somehow, the overproduction and loose writing make for a campy yet self-aware miracle. There is more tedium than you would expect, but it is in these mundane interactions and missions that the game seems to shine. You are a 1-ton steel cyborg killing machine. You are also just a cop. You will have to write tickets, save cats, prevent littering, find stolen cars, and carry bums into the drunk tank. Boring cop stuff. But again, you are a 1-ton steel cyborg killing machine- so it's pretty funny. Robocop is portrayed far too authentically- he bobbles around like a toddler taking it's first steps, while barking public service crap at the populace. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know what prompted to them to make a game today based on the awesome original Robocop movie from 1987, which is one of my all time favorite movies, but I'm all for it. Yes, the game is not triple-A and technical/budgetary limitations soon become evident but it doesn't matter. The respect for the source material shines through and hearing Peter Weller reprise his iconic role again is always a treat. Shooting bad guys to bits with the AUTO-9 is ever so satisfying and with upgrades the weapon stays relevant from start to end. I never got bored of the trademark stomping sound of Robo walking around. I'll this over the umpteenth iteration of pretty-but-vacant CODs and battlefields any day. Though do note there is a fair bit of walking around as there are more open and quieter sections with side missions. I suspect that's where tastes may vary. I liked those parts well enough and a lot of it skippable though then you also skip on experience used to upgrade skills and story points that help with the world building. Being Robo is not just about shooting and themes from the originals are continued here.If unsure whether to spill full price, wait for an eventual discount to make it a no-brainer deal if you have any love for the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the game for it's storyline and continuation from the movies of 2 and 3. The City, the Police Station and the different locations are outstanding. There's good story for Lewis and the rest of the Officers. The voice of Murphy is the actual actor, which is fantastic. Flashbacks feel great. These cons really are for the devs to take note on and I'm wondering WTF they were thinking. Biggest Cons: ---Whoever they got to voice Sgt Reeds doesn't sound anything like the actor from the movie. It's a complete disappointment since his "tough leadership voice" really set the mood in the movies. ----Robocop only has his iconic heavy foot stomping noises. You don't ever hear his iconic robotic sounds when he moves his legs, arms or head around. Matter of fact, he can move his body and head rapidly and nothing feels robotic about him. This was a major part of what made Robocop feel real - was the mechanical noises his body made. Hopefully there will be a Nexus Mod made. ------- Very disappointed that you don't have the option to take out his leg weapon and holster it - it's all preset combat cinema only. However I do like the modifications that you can do the to weapon with the Mother Boards. ------- His HUD is ok, but I wish they would have given you more ways to feel you're in Robocops Visor - The movies would show history and photos etc. you have to aim down the sites before it'll lock onto targets. You only get a night vision mode which seems barely usable 9.5 hours in. ____ When in Detroit, it would have been cool if you could travel across the city while in the Squad Car, instead you gotta go on a Marathon run - GOD forbid you couldn't find an objective along the way, or you're going to end up running around too much. There's only really one area of Detroit the second time you go on patrol - so it feels "reused" and makes the environment feel cramped. ___ I went on a mission that throughout the combat - I ended up winning the end of it with 1% HP left - yet in the cut scene, Robocop was in pristine looking condition. I had to switch to his Battle Damage Cosmetic to which to my disappointment, you had to go back to the MAIN MENU to switch outfits. Overall the skills you can upgrade are amazing, the graphics, lighting and effects are fantastic action packed. Overall I'd give this game so far a 8/10 - They nailed the game overall - but things from the movies that made him iconic are being left out for some reason. Other than upgrading skills and motherboards, there isn't anything cosmetic or weapon wise that advances with the game. The devs need to watch the movies a few more times and add what is apparently left out.

_childDocuments_.review: When I watched the movie back in the day I liked it well enough, but never became a huge fan of the franchise, so I was somewhat hesitant about this game. But after it received a glowing review from a Youtuber who has similar tastes as me when it comes to games like this I decided to give it a try, and it completely won me over (just like  did).The game does not feature a huge open world like , or , or . Instead the location is more similar the  games. From the police precinct you set out for investigations in Old Detroit (e.g. in a VHS rental place, if anyone still remembers what those were ^_^), then return to the precinct once the investigation is finished. The characters are interesting, progression feels good, and the gunplay is fun (even though RoboCop's iconic pistol is probably a little too overpowered, so I rarely found myself using any other weapon).I really have only two complaints. One is the first boss fight against an ED-209 unit, which not only has more firepower and heavier armor, but somehow can also move at about the same pace as the much lighter RoboCop. So you can't run, you can't dodge, and there's also no cover to speak of. Which makes for a wholly unfun boss fight. Second complaint is about how scripted the final boss fight was. Maybe it's just me, but I don't like it when boss fights are interrupted by cinematics (even though here it wasn't even remotely as bad as in ).Rating: ★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the RoboCop movies, I had high hopes for this game, and I am thrilled to say that the game exceeded all my expectations. From the moment I started playing, I was immersed in a world that perfectly captures the essence of the classic films.One of the standout aspects of the game is its story. The narrative is engaging and filled with twists that keep you on the edge of your seat. The multiple endings add a layer of replayability, making each playthrough feel unique and exciting. I found myself genuinely invested in the fate of RoboCop and the citizens of Detroit, just like I was while watching the movies.The game does an excellent job of balancing nostalgia with fresh content. The familiar characters and locations brought back a flood of memories, while the new elements and plotlines kept things fresh and intriguing. It's a perfect blend for both longtime fans and newcomers to the franchise.The gameplay is smooth and satisfying. Controlling RoboCop feels powerful, and the combat mechanics are both intuitive and thrilling. The attention to detail in the design, from the iconic RoboCop suit to the gritty streets of Detroit, is impressive and adds to the overall immersive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Part immersive sim, part FPS, all cop. An extremely fun and satisfying romp through the world of Robocop. Combat strikes a good balance between making you feel slow and powerful while not feeling overly clunky or frustrating. Upgrade system lets you tweak Robocop's main handgun to suit each encounter and while the skill system isn't super in-depth, I felt it had just the right amount of impact on the gameplay to not feel too oppressive. Graphics aren't the most top of the line, but the environmental destructibility is top notch and not only serves to make the combat more intense and fun, but also gives you tactical options like throwing explosive canisters and TVs at enemies, or even just flat out grabbing and throwing them out of windows. Story is a bit clumsy and oddly paced at times, but it's overall fun, and hearing Peter Weller as Robocop is the cherry on top. The game also features some investigative sections to split up the combat encounters, and while some of these can drag on a bit long at times, they are on the whole really fun and do a great job at fleshing out the Robocop world more. What really sells the game for me though is the dedication the devs showed in reproducing the world from the movie. Rather than trying to "modernize" the setting to reflect the modern day, the game sticks to its "near future according to the 1980s" presentation, where a police station with a spacious computer server room and an entire maintenance bay for its cyborg cop still has its officers using typewriters and reviewing security footage shot on grainy VHS tapes. And aside from a few clunky lines, the references to the films are generally used to good effect to maintain continuity.So overall, while the game can be a bit rough and clunky at times, the combat is overall visceral and satisfying and the presentation is filled to the brim with references to the movies and fun environments to shoot apart. Well worth it for fans of Robocop or anyone looking for a fun single player FPS campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wanted to like this game. I was really interested in the arcade-style shooter feel it has. I see some negative reviews that comment on how boring the side quests can be, but at first I really enjoyed the casual and mundane feel it has.However... The very first mission of this game worked flawlessly (On epic settings) for me and I was excited to play more, but as soon as I entered downtown Detroit in the next mission, I started getting a lot of stuttering/hitching problems. So I start adjusting every setting I could think of and checking Reddit and Steam forums to find out why the game kept doing this despite the fact that my FPS in/outside of combat was great up until this point. After trying to fix it for a while, I eventually decided to give up and just play the rest of the game ignoring it. I thought that would be my only hurdle, and just started playing on the lowest possible settings.Until I got to a later stage where you have to go to a hospital. My game crashed over and over again until the point where I didn't think I would be able to play it anymore. Every time I loaded the game it would crash. Eventually I was able to get past this but now every cutscene or loading screen is a 50/50 chance of a crash. Its feels like the games performance has gotten worse the further I get into the game. Also there is no manual save feature so if the game does crash you have to get lucky that you don't have to replay too much.In summary, the game is fun, but with all the performance issues I have had to deal with, it makes the gameplay harder to enjoy when I am putting in so much effort to keep the game stable. Which ultimately makes me find the game more boring because the gameplay does not outweight the performance issues.This is just my experience and I see that most reviews are positive so this may just be something only a handful of players are experiencing. Since I am outside my refund window I am playing this game on the lowest settings possible and crossing my fingers that the game doesn't crash after not autosaving for a while.But if the game works perfect for you, it's a cool game and you'll probably like it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR : Amazing game, despite its baffling lack of polish in some areas. Genuine recommendation at <=$40+++ Writing : I've never seen the movie but I know a brief synopsis. This game's main story arc is very good even without knowing the movie. The characters and especially side content is good, the random banter is sometimes quite golden. This makes this game more than just a shooter and from what little I know about the movie, it fits it quite well.++ Pickles will remember that : Actions do actually have consequences, I didn't initially think NG+ was really necessary but it really is, at least if you don't try to be as thorough as possible your first rodeo. As an aspiring game dev, this game is downright inspirational.++ Juicy : There's really nothing like grabbing some bastard by the neck and throwing him either directly into someone else, followed by beautiful bone crunching or throwing him a mile in the air and watching someone's existence end with a sickening crunch and gore explosion. The punch is just golden. Chef's kiss.+ Easy to have fun : Whether on easy or hard, this game's combat is just plain fun, most of the time.- Textual Errors : Subtitles sometimes don't accurately reflect what's being said, or are misspelled ("Ortiz singing off"). Pet peeve, for sure. An error I should find in a $50 game? No. Also, the tutorial for signal tracking says "top left" when it's top right in-game. It happens enough to where I feel it's worth mentioning.- Odd objects : I find it really funny that drywall seems to be the only thing capable of stopping physical matter when it's on a pillar. Take the very first act/chapter/whatever of the game as an example. You shoot up a pillar and you can actually walk and shoot through it. Destructible objects and environments are great but I shouldn't need to worry about not having cover because every pillar in a warehouse got shot up. Also, there's just a lot of objects baked into the map instead of being physics objects. I find plastic water bottles being one of the more effective bits of cover for my enemies. Wine bottles? Shatters to bits. - Graphical errors/polish : I don't care if a game looks like it's from 2010 or 2020, but can we at least have lips move for all spoken dialogue? In both critical cutscenes and side content, it sometimes has lip sync and sometimes it doesn't. The animations seem to kinda cut in and out to the point to where some characters are just jolting between animations. The game started with shadow clipping but I suspect that's more my end than the game.-- Clunky Environments : Grenade spam is fine, so long as you can move around the environments to actually dodge them. While movement is restrictive, it's free enough to get the job done. However, some environments combat takes place in are filled with immovable chairs and things that I would very much like to barge through in order to not sit my metal ass on a grenade that was thrown literally less than a second after breaching. There's been a handful of times I would try to strafe and then get blocked by a potted plant and then subsequently just stand out in the open thinking why in God's name I'm not moving.-- Sound Mixing : For a $50 game, the sound mixing is bafflingly awful. Some sounds are louder than I thought I set my computer too, let alone the rest of the game, let alone what's reasonable; a door opening should not be louder than the shotgun I just got shot with. Dialogue between two people might be imbalanced to the point one person is quieter than the ambient noise and the other is perfectly audible. You NEED subtitles if you have even the slightest trouble processing spoken words as I do. It's insane that I feel the need to make this point both this long and this emphasized. This issue is most prevalent on recordings and speakers, I feel.-- Neglected aspects/Low polish : Why does the skill screen not have a confirm button? Why does the map default to clipping half of it off the screen? Why did I have to write most of the negative points in this review? Why did I have to restart a campaign because a load zone consistently crashed my game? Why is RoboVision not default when out of combat, or toggle-able rather than a hold down? Why do enemies marked with RoboVision stop being marked outside of RoboVision? Why does the camera clip off the chin of everyone I'm talking to while leaving another head's worth of space above them? Why is game_logo.jpg so low-res? The worst part is that, now that I'm conscious of these things, I can quickly identify nitpicks I probably otherwise would've ignored.--- No manual saves : Is this a trend? I hope not. It's 2024. Do not tell me manual saves are old-fashioned and getting rid of them makes your game more modern. Why do I have to be constrained by unmarked checkpoints to determine when I can stop playing? Actually speechless as to why a $50 game in 2024 doesn't have something that games old enough to get college degrees have. It's like making aiming based on arrow keys again because the mouse is too old of a solution.It's a game whose story is amazing and gameplay feels really good, but there are some things in this game that make me question its $50 pricing. It feels like some aspects of the game felt VERY neglected in order to release sooner or whatever. The contrast between the quality of the gameplay and the quality of the game makes me question what in God's name happened during development. OCP wasn't investing in this thing, were they? I would like to assume that these faults are not some artistic statement on game development culture as a whole but...This isn't to say this game isn't worth it at all, it certainly feels very good, most of the time. The positives I have in this game are short because it's just something you need to experience yourself, but at the same time, this game feels like a real piece of work because of the no-manual-save that everyone and their dog already complained about (and, to be fair, is being worked on, from what I read).Post-Publish Edit :

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: NOT an action fps straight shooter. This is ROLE PLAYING GAME.If you're looking for mindless "lemme just be RoboCop shooting the baddies for an hour" game, this is absolutely not it. This game probably only appeals to people who are looking for more than a shooter, you know...like a role playing game, or who are RoboCop die hard fans.Also, I saw someone post this is the same developer that did Terminator Resistance which makes sense. They may have taken that game and just reskinned stuff because it does feel similar. So if you didn't like that game, you're not gonna like this one.Spoilers for the first 2 hrs of what I could handle playing this game following:I honestly thought you just were going to work through floors of the news tower building like some kind of "RoboCop meets Die Hard 1"... but the news tower is just a short tutorial level. You then end up at the police station where you have lots of cutscenes with bad voice acting and lip sync. You walk around to different objects re-calibrating yourself, including using a firing range which is like...why am I using a firing range to practice shoot mechanics when I literally just did a tutorial level shooting dudes..???That's when I realized this is not an action fps, it is a role playing game. You are role playing the experience of being RoboCop having to recalibrate your systems despite the fact it is not fun. It is not fun to have to do that when you just experienced the best part of the gameplay, the action fps of shooting dudes and throwing them out of a building.OK, so now you will role play as a guy who thought he bought an action fps but bought a role playing game (me).  Your HUD updates and you see you need to leave the police station. OK you walk over here, wait no I think over here. Is there a map? No...is it down stairs? Walk back here I think those were stairs. OK yes, these go down. Cool that was weird, but I did it, yay.You quick travel to a downtown area and go into an arcade. You then experience the whole "evidence collection" side of things where you're like scanning stuff, reading stuff, talking to people, etc to progress through the level. You keep walking around between objectives with nothing obvious to do. But you find out that you need a search warrant to get through a barricaded door. It takes you 10 minutes to find all of the little things you're supposed to scan and rooms where you can advance the story enough to get the search warrant issued. You go talk to the dude and tell him you have a warrant. He refuses to open the door. So you...kick the door down...like you could have done before wandering around for 10 minutes.After some shooting and resolving this stuff with dialogue options that do not excite or entice you, you quick travel to a different downtown and you learn you can issue tickets for stuff. So what do you do with this new found ability. You scan a parking meter, the time is expired. You then leave a ticket on the windshield of a car. You get a handful of XP points. Like 2% of what you need for a new skill point. So you start thinking "dude...I would need to leave 50 tickets to get a skill point. Woah, that sounds really...boring."What. In the hell. Is that. That is not action fps. That is not fun or exciting. You then see a guy spraying graffiti on a wall. You have a cutscene with bad dialogue. You then see him running off in the distance. I guess you are chasing this guy. You are slow, even when sprinting. Cause you're a tank. A tank that was built to  leave tickets on cars. He is gone. You scan a foot print with paint. Maybe he went this way. You then see no more foot prints...did you go the wrong way? You don't know, and honestly you don't care. What the hell is going on, you started the game shooting dudes and throwing them out of windows. You are now basically playing BeatCop Sim 2023. OK, holy hell you paid $50 for this you better get your money's worth let's go back and do the mission objective because what even is this experience right now. You go back and bust into a safe house. You shoot some dudes and progress through this level. You're introduced to a machine gun enemy that apparently you cannot kill that shreds your armor. You use all your stims to heal. That's OK cause these stims are laying around everywhere. You find a stairway and decide that must be the point, you have to flank this machine gunner. You shoot your way through and have a modest amount of fun. You know like, the action fps part. Like, how the game is tagged on Steam. The reason you bought the game. There are no stims anywhere. Suddenly you're like uh maybe I'm going to die? You get a little excitement at the sudden tipping of scales in the game balance. But then you just shoot everyone in the head with your pistol and finish this level, where you find a stim at the end, which is like - why...I just beat it.At this point you realize a couple things:- Combat is pretty freaking boring despite being the most fun part of the game. You know, bullet sponge, bad ai, "why not use my pistol to headshot everything", etc- The game had to include other stuff because combat is boring, hence BeatCop Sim 2023- You have an hour until work- Should you have exercised instead?- You're hungry- You probably should eat- What are you even doing with your life, in the dark, playing BeatCop Sim 2023

_childDocuments_.review: It's impressive how much Teyon has improved since their attempt at a Rambo video game, which had to be among the worst video games of that decade. They showed a lot of improvement with their Terminator adaptation and have become even better now with this version of RoboCop, which pays a lot of homage to fans of the franchise and, surprisingly, actually stays accurate to the source material. And I bought this video game solely because it seemed to stay true to the roots of RoboCop. Yes, RoboCop is actually unapologetically white male as he should be. There's none of those blatant woke tropes that we often see in modern productions these days where people have to virtue signal every time you walk around a corner or load into a new cutscene. As they like to say, it feels good to be represented for once.The game is just pure fun and carnage as video games should be. Minor destructible environments such as being able to chip away at pillars, lots of gore which is reminiscent to the bloody mess that was the F.E.A.R franchise, and even a morality system where prominent NPCs will actually remember actions that you make or dialogue that you choose in response. There's a lot of content which surprised me, as I thought this was going to be a very short video game and that it might be too overpriced at $50 USD. It is still kind of short, though, so for a lot of people, $50 USD full price might seem too steep of a price tag for a singleplayer video game. But somewhere around 50 quests, split somewhat evenly between main missions and side missions? A fun RPG system that allows you to invest points into a character build as well as being able to upgrade your pistol efficiency? And a semi-open world where you have a lot of opportunity for exploration and easter egg hunting? That's pretty good for a AA video game title.You don't need to spend the extra $12 USD or so on the current DLC as these are just cosmetic packs, but I'd recommend doing so just to support these developers in their journey to AAA status, as Robocop is a step in the right direction and I am holding onto hope that they can only continue to go up ever since their Rambo video game. On a sale? It's worth the buy even more so, especially for shooter game fans and Robocop fans in general. Maybe a Judge Dredd video game can be next.Things to dislike:-While I love the gunplay and the gore, the ragdolls need massive improvement. It is not at all realistic to the degree that you'd find from games like Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto. Corpses are constantly contorted in an unrealistic way. I love ragdoll physics but the physics here are immersion breaking.-The psychology path in the skill tree needs reworking. It is fundamentally useless and a waste of points currently. Unless it was just bugged for me. I almost always focus on maximizing the skills that allows me access to more dialogue choices such as with Fallout, but with this game, you don't actually need to do anything but put two points into it to access ALL special dialogue choices, which are very minimal. I think I did every quest and talked to as many NPCs as I could find and I only remember seeing around three or so special "psychology" dialogue choices. It sounds important when you are researching the skills tab, but it truly isn't. As of now, I don't think there's any way to reset skills points, either. Which also needs to be added as it's become the norm in modern gaming for players to be given the freedom to explore different builds without needing to restart from the very beginning.-There needs to be a "new game+" mode so that people can re-experience the video game with the skills that they've unlocked. Otherwise, XP needs to be given in greater values so that you level up more before the conclusion of the video game. There simply isn't enough to do in this game to maximize all of your character's skills. Crime evidence is littered throughout the maps, for example, and gives you a point value for collecting it but for many areas of the game, these points are redundant unless you have the quest for collecting a certain amount of crime evidence items, and this side quest doesn't exist in every map. I'd suggest converting the arbitrary points value of these items into XP points instead. It'd encourage players to find more of the secrets as well, because those stashes are otherwise pointless to look for since you are not actually being rewarded for it. -The music isn't all that great, especially during some of the more action packed sequences of the game. You'd expect something way better than what they used. Something to get you pumped as a robotic cop dispensing deathly justice to all of the criminals and thugs. The music here seemed more like something you'd hear from a Spider-Man game as you are swinging around the city or something. It's more peaceful, relaxing music rather than something that you'd expect to play during a major boss battle.-The game needs a manual save feature or better auto-saving. I had to quit playing at some point and when I came back to it, I was like 10+ minutes behind from where I signed out. I can only imagine how far back you can go if you actually die. -Difficulty is a bit too easy, but that's just a personal gripe. Even on expert mode, I only died twice. And both instances were not even to the bosses, but because I was distracted by something else going on around me and looked away from my HP bar momentarily. Other than that, I really did enjoy the 14 or so hours I put into the game. I got all of the achievements in that time frame, and playing it on an easier difficulty probably means that you can beat it even faster so take that as you will for its price tag.

The story is decent and the level design is very good, in keeping with the films. The voice acting is bad, animations are pretty poor and the graphics are... OK? I say that because no matter what I do, it's constantly screen tearing, washy and generally unpleasant. There always seems to be a noticeable amount of input lag too, which can become quite tiresome to deal with. I've never had issues with graphics in games, and this isn't exactly a demanding game so maybe I just have that weird set up that this game doesn't like, but I can't seem to find a fix for any of these issues. Will I keep playing it? Yes, I like RoboCop and it's a simple game to play. Would I recommend it? No, it's just not a good game. Any other IP and this game would have flopped. If you like RoboCop and get it on sale at half price or more, then go for it. Otherwise, buy something else or save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a suprisingly good game and a terrific movie license game. It's definitely a AA-game but a really top tier one. The game really makes you feel like RoboCop while also having a suprisingly deep story and gameplay. The developers definitely captures the feeling of the first 2 movies (I dont really count the third one). I encourage to explore in the levels because sidequests will pop up here and there which can be fairly interesting. The writing is fairly good but the voice acting is a bit hit or miss...mostly miss.The visuals are stunning from an art and technology perspective but the facial animations are rough and the animation overall isn't that impressive. But expecting more would at the same time be a bit ludicrous considering the budget the team probably was working with.What I think would have elevated the game for me is if the game had a dismemeber-system in the same level of detail like Soldier of Fortune 1/2. I think it would have been thematically appropiate and would have made the game more fun. What? Stop looking at me like that!The other thing I would have liked is if the world was more dynamic. While there are a lot of particle effects and there are some objects can be picked up like chairs or computer monitors almost everything in the world is bolted to the ground and solid objects. If the game would have had the same dynamics like for instance Half-Life 2 where almost everything is a physics objects that can you can assert agency on it would have been fantastic.For instance, in the first level you walk and have a firefight in an office space and it had been so cool if all the furniture was movable and physics objects. So when you pick up an enemy and throw him through the office (yes you can pick up enemies and throw them, so much fun!) the desks would go flying and whatnot. That also would have been thematically appropiate.With that said, those are really only nitpicks.In the end I strongly recommend it and it's an easy buy if you like FPSes (with some RPG-flair) and RoboCop.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this is a super biased review. I love Robocop lore and movies. This is Robocop, no doubts about it. The original cast is doing the voices, the locations are fantastically well recreated, the gunfight is as in the movies, the entire city is in the same grimm chaos and it is great to be able to play a new movie, sort of. So if you ask me, yeap go and buy it. If you like Robo you will like this.....unless you focus on the graphic quality, gunfight, movement, flow of the story, a more dynamic pace and next gen graphics. Why do I mention twice the graphics ? because eventhough this game has been created in Unreal 5.. this is not next gen at all. It could have been created in Unreal 4 and it wouldn t demand so much from your rig. Movement is clunky and slow even when you run, the gunfight is old school point and shoot without any finesse or dynamic, flow, of the story is slow, the missions are slow, walking is... welll... slow. So I say you check it first and if you like it you go for it.Personally I think this is a product of love. Clearly the creators wanted to keep the lore and make a videogame that is sorta kind of movie. But no next gen movie. The game looks good though and again for the fans it has everything you might look for in a Robocop videogame.So here is the biased opinion: I TOTALLY RECOMMEND IT ! It s Robocop and I don t need anything else to add to the buy decision. Go and buy it... you can always refund it if you don t like it.. just be warned it might surprise you (for good or for bad depends on you).
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: For someone who has watched the OG Robocop movie growing up in the 80s, this game really brings back all the 80s sci fi vibe from the original movie.  The game looks really good on UE5 but the same texture noise still appears in some objects when viewed at an angle, I guess Lumen still needs some optimization. The writing is good and the developers managed to capture the essence of the original movie right down to the same framing of the shots. The recent update puts the normal maps on overdrive especially on the human skins textures and it really make them look like they have a severe case of skin Eczema, the previous normal map settings are better. Noise levels seems to be brought down a bit in this update, with less texture noise artifacts. Overall this is an excellent adaptation of the Robocop franchise! I highly recommend it!!!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Simply outstanding from beginning to end.The basic game loop consists of shooting sections (where you turn bad guys into bloody gore), exploration, and side-quests. It's super satisfying, especially as you get progressively more powerful by gaining levels and customizing RoboCop's abilities.The game is stunningly faithful to the source material, with key movie locations perfectly reconstructed, familiar characters, and nice easter eggs for fans.This is also the best RoboCop story since the original movie. In fact, the story is so solid, it feels like a true bonafide sequel.If you weren't already a RoboCop fan, you will be once you play this.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Well this was a fun little bite-sized game. Definitely recommended.Tonally, they got about as close to that of the movie as you could hope. The voice acting was spotty - where it was good, it was really good, but for a lot of parts they clearly went with:"Can you do 18 different voices so we're just paying one person?""Well, I CAN but it's going to sound stilted and ridiculous when I'm doing one TOO different.""Did you miss the part where I'm not paying 17 other people?  Do it."It's not too bad for me, just worth an eye roll but I could see it being more annoying for someone else, to be honest. But getting Peter Weller was fantastic and the work he did was great. In one of the first missions, just wait for his delivery of "Pickles!" - you can't tell me he didn't do a great job with this role (again).But gameplay and level construction-wise, it mostly reminded me of Deus Ex.  Not in how responsive the world was, really.  There were very clearly only a few characters that you were having an impact on, and I don't think they really affected the progression of the plot much (though I can't say for sure, having only played it once) but:First personSkills that come in both combat and non-combat varietiesA few different main areas branching out into other areas for most of your main quests, but open enough that you'll run into random people and sidequests as you wander around.Multiple ways of resolving SOME quests (Deus Ex was richer there, obviously, but there's an attempt made here).City areas with nothing but parked vehicles, none moving.  (Yes, there are enemies on motorcycles, but that's kinda different.)Not to mention just the whole near-future, run-down-city tone of some of Deus Ex's levels that was most of the game here.Mind you, I'm not putting the two on the same level, I'm just saying that there are some comparisons there, and the vibe as I was playing struck me as pretty similar.  If that was intentional, then they really made a great choice taking inspiration there without outright trying to copy it.The plot itself, as is often the case with game plots with omniscient antagonists, is . . . a bit iffy.  You'll almost certainly make obvious connections before the characters will, and there are a lot of plans that come off like "OMG RoboCop is so unpredictable we need to control him - but also our plot hinges on we do this, so he'll inevitably do this, etc - which indicates he's actually totally predictable."It only works if you know the end you want and then write backwards, and it's really kinda obvious.  However, it's not too different from some (not great) movies, and while I normally play games for the plot here I was just playing to be RoboCop so that particular failing didn't really bother me too much. Another eye roll like the voice stuff.And I should say that my criticism of the writing is just the plotting, really - the writing for the characters was great. There were the stock characters you'd want in an experience like this, but also some fully-fleshed-out roles that really seemed like they could have taken the easy way out with just giving them standard characterization for their roles and they didn't - they actually made them understandable and human. So kudos in that regard.I'll uninstall now, waiting on new game+ (which they say is coming, so not a minus there, just not available at the moment), but all in all a good way to spend a couple days. Again, recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop: Rogue City is a love letter to the movies and is a solid (if sometimes janky) game to boot. The best part is the attention to detail, every character and set from Robocop 1 & 2 has been lovingly recreated for the game. Everything from Robocop himself to ED-209 to the West Detroit Police Station looks identical to their movie counterparts. The legacy sound effects are spot on too, Robocop's Auto-9 gun, his motor noises and foot steps sound perfect. Glad Teyon had the guts to use liberal amounts of the original RoboCop soundtrack instead of completely ignoring the original score and pumping the game full of their own background music like lots of other movie based games and franchise movie reboots do. Nostalgia is a huge positive for the game, and I'm pleased to report the game has some juicy Easter eggs peppered across the levels, Chefs kiss love 'em all!Peter Weller returns to voice Robocop which is great, thankfully his voice is on point after nearly 34 years since Robocop 2. This is nit picking but what lets his outing as Robo down a tad is his dialogue script which isn't Weller's fault, he doesn't write the thing. His dialogue could've been a bit more badass with cool one liners and some levity as Murphy/RoboCop did open up in RC2 if you remember the film (I don't mean the goofy scenes when he goes haywire). The level of voice acting in the game all in all is good enough for a AA game I have heard a lot worse in some AAA games (Starfield LOL). The story is good, better than RoboCop 3 which isn't saying much but trust me it's way better. However, like with RC3 the on-screen storytelling is let down by the cast or more specifically in this case the NPC's.Characters like Lewis, Sargent Reed and the CEO of OCP "The Old Man" look screen accurate but sadly their dialogue is unimaginative, and not helped by the fact the voice actors used don't sound anything like the movie actors. The douchebag OCP director Becker is the best written character in the game, he feels the closest to what you would expect a RoboCop human character should be like, an arrogant A-hole with a sick sense of humour.The villain is meh though! The writers should've really had fun with this guy, you know, given him the attitude and dark humour you saw with Clarence Bodicker but alas they didn't, he could've been gripping and memorable.Graphics are excellent when you consider the price of the game. Unreal Engine 5 produces amazing lighting and textures it's a good looking game for sure. The quality of the environments and visual effects are offset negatively by awkward character models, cringe facial animations and bad lip syncing, the characters mouth movements don't match the English dialogue, you would think you were playing a dubbed over Japanese game. PC performance is good at 1440p on my MSI 4090, I am getting a solid 150 fps average on Epic preset with DLSS on. However, GPU temps are really bad on this game, on Cyberpunk 2077 at 2160p 120Hz with High preset & DLSS on I see maximum GPU temperatures of 65*C but on Robocop I am touching 80*C within 15 minutes.Combat is fun and you have access to some cool skills like Ricochet, Slow-Mo, and Stun which spice up the action and there is just enough variation in enemy types to keep this relatively short game interesting. There is a good variety of your run of the mill ballistic weapons which all feel good to fire including the excellent Auto-9. I love how you can collect motherboards for the Auto-9 and upgrade it with nodes that unlock many bonuses like armour piercing, full auto mode and bullet spread. Unfortunately no futuristic laser weapons or fancy grenades but when you think about it this does make sense for a game oozing with 1987 movie nostalgia.The gameplay is faithful to Robocop, you feel slow and heavy and walking distances takes time which is exactly how it should be, Robocop is not Rambo or John Wick so don't go in thinking you can play this like you would COD or Cyberpunk 2077. Out of combat gameplay is fun if a little basic, you have dialogue options, miscellaneous police jobs, a shooting range, hidden areas to explore, exposition documents to pad out the story and XP boosting evidence to find. I would've liked some collectables and lore literature to find as well but never mind. The most recent update adding some game completion weapon skins and New Game + which gives the game some much needed replay value. The music is good when it plays especially the Robocop theme but the one thing I didn't like is when you're out of combat the game is very quiet, there is really faint BGM or sometimes none at all and there is next to no ambient noises. For example; the streets of old Detroit BGM is barely audible when it even plays, all you can hear ambience wise is the Highway above and the odd distant police siren, there are no AC units humming on apartment buildings, no buzzing from street lights, no homeless people talking, no cracking from fire barrels, no river water lapping, no splashes when you walk through puddles, no litter crashing about and no distant gunshots or screams, everything just sounds a bit lifeless. Cutscenes are awkwardly devoid of any ambience too. Lastly, the story is above average and the game has no game breaking bugs, there are a few graphical glitches like texture pop-in during cutscenes, shadows not rendering properly at times and the odd background light source clipping through foreground objects e.g I saw a squad cars red and blues shining through a SWAT captains face.I highly recommend Rogue City to every Robocop fan out there and I would also recommend it to any story driven FPS fan who enjoys COD campaigns, Far Cry 6, Halo Infinite or Starfield just don't expect the solid quest variety, sound design and voice acting you would get in those $60/$70 AAA titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop: Rogue City --- Most PlayRobocop: Rogue City is more than just a game; it's a riveting journey back into a nostalgic yet futuristic Detroit, where technology and justice entwine in a battle against crime. From the moment you don the iconic steel armor of Robocop, you're thrust into a narrative that is as engaging as it is reminiscent of the original films, especially with Peter Weller reprising his role, lending an authentic touch that fans will appreciate.The game is a visual spectacle with its cyberpunk aesthetics, bringing Old Detroit to life in a way that's both fresh and familiar. The bustling cityscape, filled with neon lights and towering skyscrapers, sets a perfect stage for the high-octane action that unfolds.At the heart of Robocop: Rogue City is its gameplay, which is an exhilarating blend of combat, investigation, and moral choices. The ability to navigate through different scenarios either with a stern hand or a voice of reason adds a layer of depth, making every encounter feel consequential. The inclusion of various side quests and the impact of your choices on the overall narrative creates a rich, immersive experience.The arsenal at your disposal, led by the classic Auto 9 gun, makes combat satisfying and robust. The upgradeable abilities add a layer of strategy, allowing for a tailored approach to different challenges. Every shootout is a thrilling dance of bullets, strategy, and justice.The storyline is compelling, filled with twists that keep you invested. The characters, both new and returning, are well fleshed out, adding to the emotional weight of the narrative. The plot unfolds at a pace that keeps you hooked, with enough suspense to keep you guessing and enough action to keep your adrenaline pumping.Robocop: Rogue City doesn't just rest on the laurels of its storied franchise; it builds upon it, creating a modern-day cyberpunk saga that is both a tribute to the past and a bold step into the future. This game is not just a trip down memory lane, but a well-crafted narrative adventure that stands tall on its own merits.In conclusion, Robocop: Rogue City is a masterful blend of action, narrative, and nostalgia. It's a game that respects its roots while offering a modern, engaging, and satisfying gaming experience. Whether you're a long-time fan of Robocop or new to the franchise, Robocop: Rogue City is a captivating adventure that is well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, folks, let's talk about stepping into the heavy, metal shoes of our favorite future law enforcement officer, shall we? You're RoboCop, right? And not the fast, sleek kind you see zipping around in those other games. No, you're the original, clunky, 'I've got all the time in the world to shoot you' kind of RoboCop. You're walking through Detroit, which, by the way, has seen better days, but hey, so have we all. And you're there to shoot the bad guys, talk to the people, and maybe, just maybe, solve a few crimes. Because, why not? You've got the armor, the guns, and the slow, methodical pace of a tortoise on tranquilizers.Now, let's get this straight. You're not just any tortoise. You're a tortoise with a mission. The game's set in this sweet spot after RoboCop 2 but before the third one, where everything goes off the rails. You've got Anne Lewis by your side, OCP in your crosshairs, and a whole lot of Detroit to save. And let's not forget the new guy in town, stirring up trouble. It's your job to figure out who he is, what he's up to, and why you're having more malfunctions than a 1980s VCR.Combat? Oh, it's a blast. Literally. You're walking through these waves of criminals like they're nothing, using your trusty handgun that's probably compensating for something. But who cares? You're RoboCop. You don't run. You don't jump. You just keep moving forward, shooting and occasionally healing yourself because even RoboCops need a little TLC.But it's not all about the shooting. No, you're a complex cyborg. You've got feelings. Well, sort of. There's this whole RPG element where you're leveling up, gaining new abilities, and engaging in what passes for heart-to-heart conversations in Detroit. And yeah, you're also playing detective, scanning for clues, and deciding whether to ticket someone for jaywalking. Because in between saving the city, there's always time for bureaucracy.And sure, the game has its moments where it forgets it's supposed to be a satire. Instead of a commentary on society, technology, and violence, it's more like, 'Hey, look at me! I'm a robot cop!' But, you know what? It's fun. It's engaging. You get to feel what it's like to be a nearly indestructible force of justice, walking slowly towards your next objective, because, let's face it, you're not in any rush.In the end, you're not just playing a game. You're living a slice of RoboCop's life, dealing with his issues, helping out the little guy, and making Detroit a better place, one slow, deliberate step at a time. And if that's not a unique gaming experience, I don't know what is.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I changed my mind. This game crashes way too often to warrant a recommendation. No amount of nostalgia-goggling is enough to overlook that. What a disappointment.Sadly, It's mid.Expect a "walking police detective and citation-issuer" simulator / collectathon on rails with the occasional shooting gallery interlude that is also on rails . Sprinkle in a reasonable amount of fan service, some wholesome moments and a little humor and you've got Robocop: Rogue City.It's not a bad game but there is so much more they could have done with it. The game is begging for more interactivity! Why not let me punch down walls on command, use more of Robo's senses beyond the "scan clues" gimmick that we've seen in a million games already. _childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent. The attention to details is perfect and you can tell that the developers actually cared about the source material. The game itself is extremely competent and well put together. It doesn't try to innovate or do anything extremely out of the box, but instead it does exactly what it needs to do: It makes you feel like Robocop. Great action sequences, perfect Robocop style dialogue and humor, excellently modelled environments. If you're looking for Call of Duty style shooting or Red Dead Redemption 2 level graphics, then this isn't for you, but if you're looking for a solid 10-15 hours of fun with over the top violence, then this is as good as it gets.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- Solid story/writing, good characters, fun but one dimensional (slow tank like) gameplay with useful skills/upgrades, nice visuals. Worth buying and playingFor this dev teams first game, it's very good. There are some rough edges certainly, but overall a very solid game and well worth playing. The story is pretty good and engaging, the characters are well done and the voice acting is really good. The writing can be odd at times but for the most part very fun. I like robocops one liners. There is alot more to this games story than expected and kinda deep at times. When certain major things happen during the story it feels right. Like nothing was forced and done poorly. Very well crafted with a good direction.The gameplay is very one dimensional, meaning you're not going to be zooming around like in cyberpunk with insane vertical movement but slow tank like movement. It is fun and has a very nice feel and is matched with a competent skill tree. You can upgrade robocops abilities and also buff his auto 9 pistol to give it new abilities like full auto, or make it strictly semi auto for increased damage output. You can easily switch between auto 9 boards to change the flow of combat whenever necessary. The game is the perfect length at 18 hours for me where I did alot of the side stuff. It also does have multiple endings and choices to be made that add to replay-ability. Using the Unreal 5 engine it looks great. The environments and lighting are really exceptional making use of some the new cool UE5 tech. The weakest point visually are the characters models which really aren't bad, but they lack the fluidity of AAA games. Not anything I knock the game for, just an observation and something than can improve for these devs for their next game.

_childDocuments_.review: They did Robocop dirty. Dont get me wrong. The graphics for the environment and Robocop are very good. But they seemed to not care about any other character or NPC. So basically you switch between this 1 map, precinct, and main mission areas. When the main mission is done you go back to the precinct. Where you do more lame stuff like get someone a towel for their shower. Than are put back on the streets to this small map. Where you do more boring/lame side quests. Than go to another main mission. The XP system and skill levels were also pointless. As you are Robocop and there is so much energy placed throughout the levels it wasnt that hard.For example. The engineering skill trait. You need to level up to open safes, but safes barely having anything of value in them and hardly any of them around. On the same skill trait you can unlock ability to disable turrets. But there was only like 5 turrets the whole game and only on last 2 or 3 levels. Which were very easy to destroy anyway. So what is the point of leveling that skill trait? Just a bad implementation of a skill tree system. Overall it was very repetitive and I really didnt have that much fun playing. It really was a pointless shooter. Terminator was so much better. I mean, if you want to play a quick mindless Robocop shooter. Id say wait for a good sale before you buy. Other than that I would not recommnend.

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop: Rogue City is a day-in-the-life-of-RoboCop simulation experience. This game turns you into RoboCop. You become RoboCop. The game initially seems like a plain shooter. RoboCop is very powerful in the movies and, in keeping with that, the gunplay will seem too easy initially. But play on the maximum difficulty and you will unearth a challenging, thrilling first-person shooter. Bullets hit heads with satisfying crunches, time slows down satisfyingly when RoboCop breaches doors, and the environment has lots of things to blow up enemies with. The physics, debris, and the overall meatiness of the gunplay all come together perfectly.RPG-like upgrade paths for RoboCop and his iconic Auto-9 sidearm add a lot of interesting, addictive gameplay loops. You must find special circuits to upgrade the Auto-9 and then configure those circuits cleverly to maximize the upgrade. Different circuits change how the gun behaves drastically and it is enormously fun to find a configuration that works best for you. While the gunplay is awesome, it is not all there is. The game is paced very well with periods of exploring a small section of Detroit, talking to citizens, solving petty crimes, and even issuing tickets. It is really like being RoboCop for a day. It also feels very much like the modern Deus Ex games.Some of the side missions have very memorable characters and laugh-out-loud storylines. A drug dealer who loves doing laundry can be convinced to give himself up by promising him that he will be assigned to laundry duty in prison. Hilarious stuff.Most of the characters are unique, well-written, and superbly voiced. However, the animations could use a lot more work because the characters' body and facial animations are stiff and robotic. But RoboCop himself was wonderfully recreated (that chrome is perfect), animated, and voiced by THE Peter Weller himself. What more could we ask for?! Robocop maintains his naive but unshakeable sense of justice at every turn and that sometimes leads to cheeky situations.Levels are vast, aesthetically varied, and suitably 80s: old steel mills, a high-security prison, a bank, etc. The graphics showcased by Unreal 5 is stupendous; Lumen lighting and Nanite are simply amazing. Some areas are photorealistic!The biggest and only flaw with the game is that the storyline is murky and confusing. I could not tell you the plot now though I paid attention to every cutscene and read every collectible. While the main theme of RoboCop has always been corporate greed and that is indeed explored here somewhat, the story feels disjointed with character motivations that are exceedingly unclear or nonsensical. Thrown into this mix is the classic theme of RoboCop's quandary - am I a man or a machine? If it were not for this muddy storyline, I would give RoboCop a 10/10. A near-perfect game that honours the spirit of the movies incredibly well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much better than it has any right to be. I went in with somewhat low expectations, as I think everyone is aware that games based on a nearly dead franchise are rarely good.. well, except that pretty much all of Paul Verhoeven's work has been made into great games recently. It's just so... right. It feels like Robocop. You feel like Robocop. You don't get some weak character and skills in order to make normal opponents feel more difficult, from start to finish you feel like that nearly unstoppable bad-ass from the original film. The music is perfect, the visuals are perfect, the story is intricate and a love letter to the original films, certainly exceeding the quality of Robocop 3 at minimum. It doesn't drop any of the satire either, going hard at being anti-corporate much like the first Robocop film. The shooting is fun as hell. The gore, language and themes are all full-fat Rated R goodness as Robocop is meant to be. Overall, I'd give this a 9 out of 10. The missing  point is for endgame and saving. There's no real save system built in, and with how the mission areas are set up its real easy to end up needing to replay some quests multiple times if you get a BSoD or have to stop mid-mission for any reason. Then at the end, there's no "plus" mode, no way to go back starting with all of the awesome things you've unlocked. If the devs could bring those two things into the game at some point, I would happily spend hours replaying parts of this and I doubt I'd get bored anytime soon.

You're a badass walking tank-man who can basically walk into the middle of a room, and headshot everyone with a single burst of your Auto-9, you are Robocop, replete with slow walk (although you can get a burst skill) and monotone disposition.I loved it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast for fans of the original Robocop movie. It nails the gritty 80s "near future" aesthetic of the movie and the whole thing feels very authentic despite some obvious budget limitations. There's less focus on satire in the game though you can still find elements of it, and it doesn't have quite the same mean-spirit to its violence despite the blood and limbs flying around during combat.The Robocop model looks great and clearly had the most time spent on it while the other character models are just ok. The OG actor returns to voice Robo but the rest of the cast aren't from the OG movie. Voice acting is mostly fine; Robo and Dr Blanche are probably the best.The actual game is an ultra violent FPS. Since you essentially control a walking tank movement is very slow for the most part, Robos run being slower than the walking speed in most FPS games. It's certainly authentic but can be tedious when traversing the free roaming area of Detroit (very small map but the movement speed makes it feel bigger). The combat is satisfyingly squishy while not requiring a great deal of strategy, but the upgrade systems for Robocop and his Auto 9 gun add some additional depth.This developer goes from strength to strength with its licensed games. Hard to believe these are the same devs that brought us Rambo in 2014! Stay safe citizen!

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop: Rogue City delivers a thrilling experience that seamlessly blends action, strategy, and the iconic RoboCop universe. _childDocuments_.review: The FPS gameplay is solid, and the dialogue and story really capture the vibe of the original Robocop movie. It's a lot of fun to play. Which is why it's a damn shame that I can't recommend this game on PC, since it has two major issues that have not yet been addressed, 9 months after the initial release:1. It runs horribly on an i7-12700K + RTX 3070 system, even at 1080p and lowest settings. My GPU is often at 100% load despite having capped the framerate at 60FPS, and in some areas of the game the performance dropped to literal slideshow levels.2. The audio balance is all sorts of messed up, and volume sliders can't fix the issue. Sounds that originate close to the camera are extremely loud, and sounds that are slightly farther away are whisper quiet. I am deafened by Robocop firing his gun, but sometimes can't hear an enemy a few meters away from me blasting his weapon at me. The same issue occurs in dialogue cutscenes, with some characters being far too quiet when the camera isn't close enough to them. I don't understand how this made it past QA.Maybe I'll change my review to a positive one in the future if I learn that these issues have been addressed, but for now, I cannot.
