_childDocuments_.review: If you are a big Robocop fan, then this game is a must have. It does a great job capturing the spirit of the movies. If you aren't a Robo fan, you can probably afford to skip it. The gameplay and design are very last gen. There is no cover system, no quick-time events, and no bells and whistles. There is a very basic leveling system that can unlock abilities for Robo to use. One of the best things the game does is, it keeps the Auto-9 (Robocop's starting weapon) relevant by making it upgradable via motherboards and chips the player can find throughout the game. The motherboards also make the weapon highly customizable, so you can have a full auto weapon or a high powered, single shot, hand cannon. It's great because the Auto-9 is iconic and it should never feel useless. Bad stuff.I would not recommend getting the Alex Murphy edition unless you really want to support the developers. It only gets you one skin for Robo, and one skin for this gun. There is no way to manually save the game and there is no easy way to know when the auto-save feature kicked in. If you are done playing, you have to just keep checking the "load game" menu and read the time stamp to see when the last save was. The only other bad thing I will say is, there are a lot of moments in the game that feel like maybe they budget was stretched thin, or maybe they were running out of time. In a apartment building? Look at the corkboard in the lobby.... weird, its the same one from the police station. Shoot a machine gun.... The shells are coming out backwards. Shooting a bunch of gang members.... its the same model used for all 3 gang members.  You like seeing the city? Can't wait to see the rest of the city?  Too bad, it's the same city block recycled 4 or 5 times. Overall, the game has some problems and it feels a little old fashioned, but if you love Robocop and want a experience that feels loyal to the films, then this kicks ass and is a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: NVIDIA users beware!If you have a modern NVIDIA gpu and the game crashes more or less at every cutscene I suggest disabling DLSS and frame generation. Enable TSR instead. It seems to remedy most (but not all) crashes during gameplay. NVIDIAS APP has a profile for this game but will recommend settings that just won't work very well.As for the game itself. If you liked the Terminator Resistance game from a few years ago you'll likely enjoy this game as well. Environments look very good and represents a nice showcase of what Unreal 5 can offer. Gameplay is kinda meh. It's a throwback to shooters around the 90s era but gets a bit long in the tooth after a few hours. The upgrade tree of skills doesn't really alter the progression that much, it's a very linear affair.

_childDocuments_.review: The real shame with this game is that it's clear that the (small) development team loved the property and wanted to make a great Robocop game. They understood the story, the questions about how much you can lose of yourself and still be human, of the loss of your connections and your friendships, of how much a corporation can dehumanize you and turn you into an agent of oppression and try to dehumanize you. Yet the gameplay just isn't there. Animations are stiff and even comical. Voice acting is repetitive, with only a few actors alongside Peter Weller, leading to the odd-sounding levels where everyone is voiced by one person. Controls are jaggy, laggy, and imprecise; if ever there were a game that called for auto-aim or aim assist, Robocop is it: They do it in the movies! Yet instead the first-person shooter gameplay feels dated and uninspired. Robocop can actually be killed by a lone ganger with a Saturday Night Special, because the gameplay doesn't understand how to make the player feel like an invincible juggernaut facing down asymmetric fights—a lesson already internalized by games like Halo for many years. The game tries to put in some detective work, dialog, and side missions to make a semi-open New Detroit, and the environments really feel like a future dystopian Detroit through the lens of the '80s, but the use of their version of "detective mode" is hampered by the same problem as other early games with that ability (there is no reason to ever NOT be in Robo-vision mode) and many of the cases are just a matter of tediously searching every nook and cranny for tiny interactions.This game could've been great, you can see greatness from here, but it just doesn't get over the hill.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played for 11 hours now, and have come back to edit a few thoughts.Overall view: It's a good game. It's not a AMAZING, KILLER, MUST NOT MISS TITLE, but a very good game, *especially* if you are a fan of RoboCop. I put it in the same category as the Mad Max game, except not quite as polished. It's an IP movie game that is fun and done well. That being said, it has flaws, and I won't make fanboy excuses for them.Pros: Starting with the visuals, The recreations of the actors from the movies are quite strong. I argue better than Johnny Silverhand from Cyberpunk 2077. It is instantly apparent who they are, and the details are very nice. The environments are done well. Textures are solid, bump maps, just all of it. The atmosphere is really good. The volume of litter, cracked pavement, graffiti, and general scum on the streets is fantastic. All in all, I think the environments are a really strong point in the game.The gameplay:Walking around feels precisely how it should. Even the "speed walk" feels like, while you are moving faster, it's evident that Robo is just a walking tank moving as fast as he can. Shooting feels great. I mean, that part of the game they nailed. All the guns have a nice kickback feel that seems appropriate to their caliber and type. I have seen people complaining about the side quests and how they think some are dumb, like giving parking tickets or issuing citations for public drinking. These things take less than a minute to complete and, in most cases, are a single click. IMO, find something better to complain about. It gives context to the fact that RoboCop isn't just a superhero taking on big bad guys all day, every day. He walks a beat and does everyday police work. It works.I also enjoy being able to upgrade his primary firearm. It's simple, but having that gun scale as the baddies get tougher is an excellent choice. The player can unlock and upgrade various properties, like armor piercing, for example. Speaking of guns... Guns and the environment! I always enjoy being able to shoot up the environment. It's not just a pointless visual, either. If a baddie is hiding around a corner, shoot at the corner, chip away all of that concrete, and then nail the baddie. The same works in reverse, so watch your cover, as it might just disappear.Now that I have dug much further into the game, not only is it not repetitive, but the skill tree does offer a few combat style changes depending on what you take to the top. Being able to dash, or use an AOE stun, or later a shock that kills all close-up enemies... Etc... It's been a lot of fun and kept me going.Sound: Generally, the ambient sound feels tight. I don't have a ton to add here. Background noises fill out the streets where appropriate, gun sounds are meaty, and Robo's walking footsteps are great. The main character NPCs are done well. Meaning the characters are based on real actors.Cons:The Visuals: The character's faces animate very clicky. The transitions from one expression to another are too "on-off" for my liking. It's because the parts that are animating are disconnected from each other. It looks like when a character raises their eyebrows, that doesn't affect any other part of the face. Same with the lips. The facial expressions are also generally stiff, and most of the eyes feel a bit dead. The lip-sync is passable but could be better, and I get artifacting in many scenes. Ghosting of the lips and jaw. All of this serves to make the game look somewhat dated, or it kicks me into analyze mode, where I critique what I am looking at rather than being invested in the game.The character's joints also have dated issues. They look like they just weren't rigged correctly. The elbows don't bend right at all. They come off like old rubber poseable toys with a wire inside that holds the rubber limb in place. The elbows and knees end up incredibly rounded and just wrong. General character proportions are off in some cases. Arms feel too small/thin for the rest of the character, plus they are not bending right; it just looks terrible. Also, animation accuracy is soft for some reason. It's pretty obvious when watching a character cross their arms or press a button. They miss. With the crossed arms, the hands float above the biceps by 3 or 4 inches. When a character presses a button, they never reach the wall. The press is just in the air. When it comes to combat, the "chunks" of baddies Robo kills are too globby. They look too much like shiny, bright red jelly or boba. It's very cartoonish. The explosions also have that cartoon feel, but they flash so fast that it's more of a nitpick.The gangs are crazy cliche. I get that RoboCop is all about pointing out cliches and elevating the ludicrous, but in this case, it doesn't come off as funny. Not to me, anyway. Mostly it's because whoever made the joke didn't know enough about those cultures to be making the joke. This might be a nice segway into...The Sound:Oooooh boy. Ok. Sound is seriously hit-and-miss when it comes to characters. Some of them sound great! Others sound like terrible voice acting from old 1980s cartoon villains. Yep, RoboCop is an 80's move. It is not supposed to be an 80s cartoon. The punks ALL sound like they have high-pitched, grainy, weasel voices. Even the motorcycle gang is all higher-pitched and grainy. OH! It sounds like they are all goblins from World of Warcraft!The Gameplay:I am editing this whole section. I was dead wrong.  The gameplay has not gotten repetitive at all. There have been 2 other side quests that were pushing what RoboCop would do. Helping a homeless guy find a VHS tape was one of them. I do wish RoboCop could crouch/take a knee. He can sit in a car, and we see him take a knee in the movie as well as in this game. Being able to use the low cover would have been nice. It could have added a little more variety. As it stands, this is another nitpick.I also really, REALLY wish the individual levels were larger.  I do understand why it is the way it is. I just want more.  lolIn short, I recommend this game to anyone who's a RoboCop fan. Just don't go in looking for Dues Ex or Cyberpunk 2077. I suggest waiting till it goes on sale. I'm just not feeling that $60 price tag. They aren't subtle issues, either.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just turned 43, was born in 81 so I grew up with the golden era of action/sci-fi.  RoboCop, Total Recall, Aliens etc and I'm all about detail when it comes to games being made off of some of these epic movies.   RoboCop is definitely one of them.  That being said I'll get into the details for any of you fellow RoboCop nerds.     Sound:  Very important to me.   The music was on ♥♥♥ point.   From the classic Robocop theme, to the memory theme in the movie when he visited his old home and the famous van chase theme when he was chasing Clarence Boddicker (best bad guy ever), all being added made the experience so much more appreciating.  His heavy thumping foot steps, Peter Weller's (OG, classic RoboCop actor) bad ass voice and lines and mechanical sounds all on point.         THE ONLY minor difference in sound from the movie, although not bad sounding at all, was his classic Auto 9 pistol.   It doesn't quite catch that same sound you remember when he was practicing at the range in the movie.    And of coarse some of the other characters in the movie that are added to the game, did not sound at all like the actors in the movie.   That of coarse can be because of them no longer wanting to act, passed away etc.      That being said, sound was still outstanding and will get your retro stiffy pretty solid.     Visuals:  At ultra settings some of the visuals were pretty damn good, others a bit out dated such as faces, facial animation and a couple other minor things.   The only thing that was a bit "eww" cringy, were faces.    The environment around you and puddle reflections for the most part was pretty good, the metal on RoboCop and other machines were  were terrific.  The gore of heads being popped off, arms being shot off, blood spray on walls behind shot person, blood spilling out of body when lifeless on the floor were friggin awesome.   Destructible environments are also added to this game.     So in the realm of visuals, its a mix of mostly great to some, "ehh"     Game play:    Now this just might be me because of my love for the franchise,  but it was hard for me to stop.  The game is fairly linear with just a few main maps you return to a couple times and some you only visit once.   The main maps have secondary missions that you can complete that make you feel like you are doing genuine cop work such as issuing tickets, solving murders or giving a statement to a news journalist.  The action and gun play, just felt bad ass because......well sh!t, you're RoboCop!   Now on normal difficulty you do feel a bit tanky especially if you level up armor to the max at first.  Being able to grab a dude and toss him into someone else or through a window off a 30+ story building is satisfying.   You are able to pick up and use other weapons, but it felt not right when you're not using the Auto 9.    Also, you do make dialogue choices and I think they have and effect on future events and maybe ending?      Story:  Without giving spoilers.........I thought it was good enough to keep me going and wanting to know more.   Prepare to run into familiar characters AND places you'll recognize from the movie which will just make you smile and enjoy the experience.     Oh and about detail, some of the places you visit from the movie, are laid out pretty damn accurate.   Not perfect but you'll easily recognize them and appreciate the love and detail the developer put into these places, and can tell the people who made this game were big fans of the movie.     Overall, if you're not familiar with OG RoboCop and you're wanting a shooter, its a pretty linear but fun game and fairly short as it takes around 16-20 hours to beat.    It took me around 16.6 hours completing nearly every secondary mission in the game.   Wait for a sale.      BUT, if you're a fan of the movie and want to live in Nostalgia for a bit (I'm a sucker for nostalgia) and appreciate the retro action life, it is worth every penny.      Best RoboCop game ever.    Bravo.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Rogue city with very low expectations. Movie based videogames are notoriously bad. And yes, it isn't a AAA game, it has rough edges and early PS4 graphics, but oh boy is it a great game. If you haven't watched the original robocop trilogy lately, the first one was great, the second one, in spite of (or because of) Frank Miller's scrip was barely watchable, and the less is said about part 3 and the soulless remake the better. (Can't comment on the TV show and animated series, haven't watched them yet.) Rogue city is the real sequel to Robocop part 1 and 2 where I'm concerned. You can tell that everyone involved loves the source material and did everything their tight budget allowed to make this the best possible Robocop game. (ok, that's not saying much, given the competition) Heck, Peter Weller voices robo, and a few other original cast members also reprise their roles. They nailed the feel and humor of the originals. Stepping into Murphys clunky shoes feels great, right away you get the "Walking Tank" feeling. Sure robocop isn't very agile or fast, but he's a bullet sponge that can tear through street scum like wet toilet paper. Aside from racking up a body count, you also do regular police work, like passing out parking tickets, responding to calls, and even saving a cat or two. (Sounds dull, but leads to some hilarious and even heartwarming scenes). Rogue city is just a blast to play. To get the full unstoppable one-cyborg-army feel, start new game plus and max out your gun's 6.2 pcb. You'll make Ed-209 looks like a roomba in comparison. Even with new game + I rarely like a game enough to play it again, but I just started my third playthrough, that ought to tell you something. In short, If you like robocop, and don't need to have the newest ray traced polish in a good game, you need to play Robocop: Rogue city.Just be sure to get it on sale, instead of the 55 Dollars it normally costs.Oh, also if you are an achievement hound, they are very doable.

The Pistol is your only permanent weapon through the game, yet its a blast to use with upgrades allowing you to modify its performance for a variety of profiles.In short: Between dedication to the source material, the spirit of robocop, and an entertaining experience that absorbed every moment of my attention? _childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, it has some quirks and challenges, but it's an interesting game to experience.  Unreal Engine 5 is looking really sexy in this game. If you are able, I recommend turning up settings and enabling lumen.  This game is very demanding on GPUs. I also was unable to get dlss 3 frame generation setting to work without the game crashing.  The game also crashed when I used a custom refresh rate.  Other than that, with those two disabled it ran, but it would have been nice to get the benefit of frame generation.The game itself is interesting and becomes quite challenging further on, as enemies can be stubborn and armor-clad.  This can sometimes lead to the sense that my weapons are rather impotent.  You don't particularly get grenades in this game, so every kill is dependent on weapon, fist, or explosives that exist in the environment.  There is a nice gore element to this game, the physics feel fun, and the overall presentation of the Unreal Engine in this game has me excited for further games to come using this graphics technology.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is deceptively fun. It's nothing to write home about but if its on sale and you like cheesy 80's action dialogue, definitely pick it up. I went in with no expectations, and the only thing I knew about it was from graphics card benchmark tests on YouTube, and I was thoroughly pleased with what the game presented and some of the mechanics, It has a surprising amount of depth for such an otherwise shallow game, but other pieces of the game felt very clunky and kind of rushed. I got it for $30 but I don't think the gameplay warrants that, I think $20 is a great price for it though. The lower the better but no higher than $20. I only have a few gripes about the game. Nothing egregious, just a couple of pet peeves and quality of life suggestions.-Movement speedWhen you're not in combat, they don't let you dash around. You have a walk, a sprint, and a dash, and the dash makes getting around the semi-open world a breeze near the end of the game. This wouldn't be such a huge deal but upon entering and exiting Old Detroit, they put 5 or 6 missions all around the map, and many of those missions have you running to another point on the map anyways. In the early game it's not a big deal because that's all you know, but once you get used to the dash, it becomes a real pain to be forced to power walking speed.-Chip mergingIts cool once you get the hang of it, but I think they should give you a handful of chips of different orientations that you can't fuse, but are all locked at like 10%. I nearly locked myself out of one of my strong Auto-9 boards because I ran out of L shaped chips in the correct orientation. Having 2 or 3 of each that you can't fuse, but keeping them locked at a lower percentage would help mitigate this a little bit. Not complicated by any means, you just have to be mindful of future boards. If you merge all your lower chips to be high percentages, it might mess you up by not having the right orientations for a better board you find later. Considering there's no way to get more without opening more chests, you could get completely screwed by RNG in theory if you aren't careful and don't know what you're doing.-Map IconsYou unlock a skill near the middle or end of one of the trees that lets you see treasure chests on the map, but I wish that it showed more than just that. I missed two entire hostage missions in the second act on my first playthrough just because I didn't know they existed, and the game doesn't tell you that until the end-of-chapter evaluation. Wish that investing in that skill tree would also show you doors or hint about other missions. Maybe it's a skill issue, I dunno. -SavingThere is no manual saving. The game is very forgiving with the auto saves, but sometimes I'll just want to see the dialogue or event unfold on one tree but actually commit to a different one. So it's not all that big of a deal but sometimes picking to go back to a previous autosave can take you back a fair amount. You can skip almost everything by clicking through or holding space bar so maybe I'm just nitpicking here.Overall I don't regret spending my money on this game, I had a great time and all my friends are getting sick of me saying things like RoboCop which is always a plus.TLDR solid game. Recommend but only for $20 or lower.

_childDocuments_.review: I may update this review as I plan to keep playing, but Robocop is right on the verge of a thumbs up for me.Look, I grew up on Robocop and Terminator, and I love that this studio is working to bring these IPs to us in video game form while being broadly respectful to the source material, but I see two large issues with this game: 1) the devs are a small studio, and the game feels very unpolished. The voice acting is pretty subpar (despite getting Peter Weller back to voice robocop). Conversations feel close to the PSX era of cutscenes where a character would say something--but the line seems to be in the wrong tone--and then there's a long pause before the next character speaks. It's sloppy. The in-game music also is a problem. On the one hand, it's a great soundtrack paying homage to the late, great Basil Poledouris (who scored the original film), but on the other hand, it sounds like it's diegetic (like it's coming out of a stereo in the game world and the in-game characters are hearing it). It's distant and it muffles a lot of the great work the composer did. As the Robocop theme gears up during the first level, it doesn't swell and make me feel like I'm in the movie. It sounds like some guy is running behind me with a bluetooth speaker playing the Robocop theme.2) The devs seem to be playing/skirting the line of trying not to be "political." I can understand this. Steam forums of games where devs are inclusive of non-traditional gamers are cesspools of anger and off-topic rants. But Paul Verhoeven (director of the first Robocop) has been explicit about this IP: it's political, it's anti-fascist, and it's anti-capitalist. So, again, it is an inherently political IP. The game doesn't appear to deal with any of this. You walk around as the judge, jury, and executioner--murdering drug dealers and drug addicts, but the difference here when compared to the film is the game lacks any form of commentary. By remaining "neutral" the devs are inadvertently siding with the fascist authority of corporate owned police forces. You see through the eyes of Robocop. When you execute bad guys quickly and efficiently, you get a higher score. When you enforce draconian laws on people who appear to be living in extreme poverty, you get notifications that you "served the public trust." Now I'm still early in the game and this could change, but Robocop walks around the city violating due process, violating civil rights, and because you play as him--you side with this anti-democratic view while in game.The original Robocop is a complex film that acts as social commentary. This game is nothing more than a shooter where you get to play a robot cop and execute "bad guys." Robocop is great not because of the design of the titular character, not because he's "so cool and tough," but because it pushes you to see through the illusion of the slick corporate marketing design of a cyborg cop--designed to look cool and be appealing--and see the corruption of the authoritarian regimes that created this machine. Murphy's arc in the original movie is to separate himself from what OCP made him--to become more human.We'll see--maybe this will come together later, but so far, it feels like the type of story a kid would write about Robocop: "Oh! He's big and shiny, and when he walks it goes "BOOM BOOM" and when he shoots it's like "ba-ba-ba-ba-bap!" And he throws bad guys through windows!"

It feels nostalgic to see RoboCop and Lewis taking the bad guys out. As RoboCop you feel powerful, like a walking tank, heavy, armored, and strong.Gunfight is simple, but very satisfying. No need for cover, just walk in and rain bullets. Breach a door or a wall and kill everything standing. Weapon selection might not be much, but all of the shine especially your main weapon. It does not get boring. Main weapon is upgradable. You can upgrade it to S tier, making it the only weapon that you need. Side quest are very good. Your choices matter and they shape the world around you. None of them are repetitive and very unique. You will be excited to do your next side mission, at the end you will get a rating directly corresponding to your level up. Corny jokes and one liners will keep you entertained. Good graphics boosts the experience to a high level. And just like that you will find yourself immersed in the story and would not notice the time fly by until the game is over.As for negative: the game gets a bit dull closer to the end. There is not much to do, but fight. You can tell the developers did not spend much time on polishing the later sections, so it feels a bit of a chore to finish up the game. If you watched the movies, I already know how the main story goes.In conclusion, you will have playing this game. I strongly recommend to pick it up! P.S. As for the achievements, you can get 100% in your first playthrough. Good eyes, Murphy! achievement easy miss as it is early on and requires an upgraded skill (I have to play New Game Plus just to get it). Everything else is easy to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop Rogue City is absolutely amazing if you like the original Robocop movies as well as early 2000s shooters. This game obviously has modern 2024 graphics, but plays like a story rich shooter from the mid-2000s. The actual game itself is fast paced with plenty of gore and explosions. There are story choices to make that influence the ending of the game and story arc within. Additionally there are numerous collectibles to acquire throughout the game, including PCB Boards and chips that make Robocop's gun better and with further abilities. This game is REALLY good - very polished, with great sound, gameplay, and graphics. The only letdown is the character Ulysses Washington who is just annoying and could have easily been left out of the story all together. That being said, it's amazing seeing Peter Weller (the original actor in Robocop) doing all the voicelines for this game. They kept things very true and one can appreciate that. On a side note, there are tons of saved game files, so going back isn't just a checkpoint. You can actually go back to specific places in case you miss something or made the wrong choice, etc.Overall this game is a solid 9.6 / 10 for single player shooters. Worth every penny of MSRP honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to say that Robocop is one of my favourite movies. It's humor, political satire, and action are just  top notch. I just love it. This game is a true love letter to it. It nearly perfectly catches it's magic. There are some things that I did not appreciate:-Poor optimization, using Unreal 5, some real nice graphical effects have been added at the cost of performance. On a 2060 Super I was getting frame drops regardless of resolution and graphic settings. From Ultra wide to 1080p, there was always frame time stutter. I believe this isn't just this game but the UE engine overall.-The voice acting for some of the main characters could have been better, like Riggs and Lewis.-The lack of varied npc models.Everything else I loved though. The music, the quest system, rpg mechanics and the shooting. Even the length of the game. I like that it has an end and doesn't take up 200 hours to finish. The achievement's were achievable. There is also a new game+ for those who want to take it up a notch or clear up anything missed on the first playthrough.What I'd like to see in the future is a better gib system that really takes the gore up to 1000 and leaving the bodies there.Overall I'd recommend if you have a beefy computer or just buy it for console where it may be only 30fps but it seems there's no stutter like in the PC version.Special thanks to my broski for hookin it up!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game that captures quite well the essence of the original movie and its sequel. As Robocop you'll do a lot of shooting, some exploration and crime solving, and get to make a few decisions on city and police matters, with some good humour throughout. Very good graphics in most areas as well.One negative aspect on the combat that I found annoying is that while head shots are instant death for human enemies without helmets, hitting anything else was quite unsatisfying. For example, shoot a punk who's not wearing any armour right in the chest, it requires multiple shots to take him down and rarely (never?) even causes staggering. Would have preferred a more realistic approach to enemy damage (and have more enemies wear bullet proof vests to make up the challenge). As you progress, you'll level up and get new abilities, some of which stretch the lore of the original Robocop (or at least the first two movies), like a temporary shield of some kind to reduce damage, and instant repairs on the spot. Overall though, it mostly feels like Robocop should, especially near the end of the game where you've leveled up several skills; you're basically unstoppable. At the default difficulty it's not hard even at the beginning, which is good for this game. It would be pretty dumb if a few punks could take you out.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made game considering the circumstances of a smaller studio. The ONLY gripe I have is the stoic and emotionless characters from time to time but you get used to it. The story, game play and graphics are extremely well done and carefully thought out. As a huge Robocop fan, I am happy to be playing this and glad it exist, it's carries the spirit of Robocop way more than Robocop 3 ever has. Thanks Peter Weller for the voice, wouldn't be the same without you.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like devs took Robocop IP and carefully created a game that from a story, setting and feel could be definitely  taking place in the first 2 movies. In the movies Robocop was a slow tank that was fighting crime on the streets of the Detroit and the game certainly gives you this feel: no hiding, no stealth, just push forward with the trusty gun in the hand. In targeting mode enemies got highlighted like in a movie, you can unlock ricochet skill to hit enemies from behind, like in the movies, you can connect to the computers...like in the movies. There are also investigation areas and during those you gather clues, interact with the people...yeah, like in the movies. There are also quite a bit of nod to the movies like SUX 6000, Sunblock 5000...etcBasically a five year old kid that saw Robocop movies on VHS for the first time imagined that being Robocop is something like that... so many years after that day he was able to experience it :P
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop will certainly appeal more to those with a passion for the films than the casual shooter fan but it is executed quite brilliantly. A faithful sequel of sorts. The story fits into the universe perfectly and there are small open world chapters and linear story moments that offset what could otherwise become repetitive shooting segments. There are some fun options and upgrades within the combat loop that keep it feeling relatively fresh throughout however. I feel very fortunate to have experienced this, Terminator Resistance (and its excellent DLC) and Aliens Dark Descent within the past year. These developers have poured their hearts into these titles with limited resources and I for one am incredibly grateful. Another reviewer mentioned how there are some other great franchises that could be looked at by Teyon (and Tindalos). The challenge will be to create something that transcends the traditional fan base in order to make sufficient sales. Us 80's/90's fans aren't getting any younger! I definitely recommend this game based on what I have mentioned above.As for performance, Unreal Engine 5 really shines. I played with all settings to ultra and it looks rather lovely. The frame rate was always above 60 (I didn't seek an actual number). The one time I had stutter both in game and in the title menu also, I used the 'Steam Verify Installation Files' or something to that effect and it resolved the issue immediately.CPU - Ryzen 5 5600XGPU - Nvidia RTX 3070RAM - 32GB

_childDocuments_.review: A huge Robocop fan so my review might be a bit biased, but this game was a really good experience. For story that is taking place between the Robocop 2 and 3 movies, it is still enjoyable.The game really honors the characters and present all of them very well. The game's respect to the source material feels during the whole gameplay, not just in cutscenes or dialogue parts. For the very reason you can't sprint or jump, instead you'll feel like you are an actual tank. A crouch could have been implemented though.I was hoping the music would be real recordings, but at least it has the original themes, and it was an amazing experience rehearing them.A few places are almost exact replicas from the movie, like the OCP courtroom, the place where Murphy died in Robocop 1, or the Police headquarters.The sounds and graphics are top notch, though I experienced some FPS drops (RTX3060 card), a few blackscreens and crashes, and one single game breaking bug that prevented me to progress in the game, but it was really early, and only once. Just finished and I feel like I'm gonna replay it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Back when I was a kid in the early 1990s, I watched first Robocop, Robocop 2, and 3 for countless times. I collect Robocop toys, and also, I used to play Robocop for the NES and arcade cabinet!Three decades later,  this game was released, and when as soon as the title screen showed up, the music hit me hard with nostalgia. It also reminds me of the long way since the Robocop NES release. The story takes after Robocop 2 and prequel to Robocop 3. Rather it canon or not, but the story is so good! There are a lot of Robocop movie references and Easter eggs in the game! The best part is that the original Robocop actor Peter Weller is back and voice Robocop!This game is FPS, and you get to feel like being in Robocop movie! It ain't fast FPS like Call of duty, Counter strike,  and any other modern FPS games. The graphic is outstanding! During gameplay, you sometimes notice the same characters' models face with different names, hair, and clothes, but hey, the gameplay and story are all the matter.I can't speak for people who have never seen the Robocop movie but highly recommand to watch all three Robocop movies before playing this game. if you're a huge fan of Robocop, this is a must play. Also, I feel bad for people who are huge fans of Robocop, who are not gamers, and never get to play this game. And hey, Robocop fans, you must buy this game now, and you can not skip this game. It's worth a full price, but if you wait for this game to finally hit the discount, you must say:  I'd buy that for a dollar!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not meant to be played as other shooters. If you are hiding behind corner/pillar you are playing this game wrong. You need to walk into the middle of the room and dispatch enemies one by one, as quickly as possible. This is where the game truly shines and stands out from the crowd. Also do not worry about head shots, body shots are just as effective and even better sometimes, as many enemies have heavily armored helmets.Is there anything wrong with the game?While you cannot fault the shooting aspect, some of the side quests (especially those without action) are painfully boring. Also the game suffers from the RPG balancing. Depending on your level and Auto-9 modifications you can make the later game way too easy (or too hard if you skip the side missions). On the NewGame+ I modified my Auto-9 with the auto-reload and full auto mode, gave it all 30-40% chips and it just made me one-shot kill every enemy and dispatch bosses within seconds, even on the new hardest difficulty (There will be trouble). I suggest to re-play the game in the normal mode, if you want to.

_childDocuments_.review: Strap in, citizens, because RoboCop: Rogue City delivers a gut-punch of a good time. It's a love letter to the classic films, oozing with that gritty 80s charm and explosive action. Stepping into the metal boots of RoboCop himself, voiced by the legendary Peter Weller no less, is an absolute thrill.The developers, Teyon, have nailed the RoboCop aesthetic. From the grimy streets of Old Detroit to the satisfyingly chunky sound effects of your weaponry, it's a full sensory experience that throws you right into the heart of the action.  Blasting through goons feels fantastically weighty, and the game doesn't shy away from the over-the-top violence that's a series staple.But it's not just mindless shooting. There's a surprising amount of depth here. You'll take on procedural missions alongside some familiar faces, like RoboCop's former partner Anne Lewis, while also uncovering a larger conspiracy that threatens the entire city.  The optional side quests add some welcome variety and a chance to explore the world further.Admittedly, the visuals might not be the absolute cutting edge, and there can be some occasional technical hiccups. But these are minor quibbles when compared to the pure, unadulterated fun of being RoboCop.If you're a fan of the franchise or just crave a good old-fashioned action romp, then RoboCop: Rogue City is a must-play. It's a game that proves that sometimes, you just need a powerful cyborg cop to clean up the streets.  Just like you, I loved every second of it.

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding FPS game, I thoroughly enjoyed playing it. It's mostly a linear shooter, with some nice open areas to explore and take things at your own pace. There are a few RPG mechanics and choices in how you interact with people. These add some flavour to the game, adding some necessary spice to what could have been a generic FPS. That said, even as a straight-up shooter, it's still brilliant.I enjoyed the game so much that I re-watched the original trilogy. There's a lot of subtle and less subtle references to the original movies that really added to my enjoyment.  There's a lot of love and passion that went into this game, and that soul shines through. Too many games follow a generic formula, and have no soul or passion. This one is definitely not one of those. Of course, with that comes a game that some people just won't like. You are Robocop, in the Robocop universe. For me it was outstanding world building and immersion, for you it might be boring. I think the added mechanics will ensure for the vast majority of people this game is arresting rather than boring. The destructible environments in particular warrant specific note. Most games are pretty static, with just basic objects exploding. In this one, entire walls get blown away...In short, I would highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the modern "immersive sims" type games struggle with combat and their inability to avoid it, see Human Revolution and Teyon's previous effort of Terminator: Resistance, the issue being so bad in the latter I ended up dropping it. Robocop: Rogue City avoids this issue by paying a lot of attention to the combat and stripping out most other ways to deal with enemies. The end result is a game that has a lot of depth and care put into it, but plays very well on a surface level as a shooter. A slow shooter that prioritizes holding angles and positioning, but that's a welcome change from the hyper active games that have proliferated nearly all FPS in recent years. The story telling and environments were perhaps the most surprising aspects, I had worries about the game leaning too hard on the anti-corporation sentiment of the original film as an excuse to embrace more politics, but the game is nearly dead on to the film, snapping between sharp satire with occasionally ridiculous humour and some legitimately emotionally compelling moments. The levels are mixed between sprawling and linear, whilst the linear ones offer a good mix up, the larger levels are packed with detail and interesting content to find. That's where the game shines, as a sort of action-focused Human Revolution style experience. The plot isn't perfect despite it's quality, the biggest flaw being the relationship system that left me unsure about where I stood with some characters, the psych upgrade just highlights the "right" choice to pick, I felt punished for deciding that Robo shouldn't campaign for either politician, and the relationship with the public boiled down to "just let them off easy" when there's no compelling reason to do so in most instances.The biggest flaw would be the checkpoint system and technical aspects, which work together horrifically. Load times were long and there was consistent slows on my build, but that might just be my PC. Checkpoints are something I always find frustrating, but often I'd turn off the game to find I lost much more progress than I'd anticipated, or would find the game auto-saves your location when leaving an area inside of the area you're leaving, thus another long loading screen should you reload that save. The gameplay is solid, but doesn't completely maintain the entire length of the game, the Auto-9 has a very cool upgrade system but that meant I relied solely on it about halfway into the game aside from occasional explosives or scoped weapons. It's a good system but I'd still like to see it developed in Teyon's next game.Takeaway from all this should be that the writing and world are great and look straight out of the movies(that one tattoo artist not with standing) and the gameplay is fun. The game was better than I expected across the board and I didn't go in with low expectations. A great game and what I would put forward as an appeal for more of these middle market gems.

_childDocuments_.review: There are good and bad aspects to this game but overall, it just feels unfinished. SLIGHT SPOILER ALERT! Starting with the bad: - If you disable the repetitive and constant music, you will hear almost nothing. They added barely any background sound effects. - Everything about this game is extremely basic. - Too many "missions" that are just tedious tasks like getting people to sign a get well soon card, fetching a towel from a locker for someone in the shower, giving a ticket, etc. Basically all side quests just feel like cheap filler quests to make the game look like it has more playable hours. In total, the game has 15 playable hours IF you do ALL side quests and spend some time just looking around at textures, bad animations, etc. like I did. There's really only a few levels and it's over before you know it. - Animations are very janky and even broken at times (like being able to see the characters eyes through their eyelids when they blink. - Some of the upgrade-able perks/skills don't actually work in the game. - You start off with infinite ammo and with one of the most powerful guns in the game (especially once upgraded). It's fine it just kind of feels a little OP. - The game feels chunky and underdeveloped. You get pretty much 3 or 4 main areas that you play in and those areas just repeat with slightly different missions and bad guys. - Barely any combat variety. You're pretty much just doing the same thing over and over again. Bad guys are all pretty much exactly the same. There is no variety to them or their actions (for instance none of them surrender, none of them run away, etc. It's like arcade-level "AI". - Unnatural cut-scenes, speech, movements/animations, etc. of the characters. Again, feels very unfinished. - You cannot manually save in this game and while you can "revert to last save checkpoint". you have no idea when that checkpoint was - it doesn't tell you. It can send you back several missions and an hours worth of game-play, which can be extremely frustrating. - The menu's are the most basic menus I have seen since I was a kid playing some indie PlayStation games. Again, feels unfinished. - Inconsistent graphics. It often feels like each level, parts of levels, characters, etc. were all designed by a different studio and it can be a bit distracting. Robocop himself (when viewed in cut scenes) looks great but then some of the other characters... well... let's just say they need a lot of work. The good: - They stuck with the original characters. In 2023 - a time when they replace characters left and right for "political correctness" or whatever their reason is - it's nice to see a dev team stick to the original material. I think that this aspect alone is what actually made this game popular. I mean it's the main reason I downloaded it. - Decent graphics for the most part. I mean it's no path tracing and it has tons of bugs in graphic fidelity but I think it's a good, early showcase/demo for Unreal Engine 5's Lumen engine. ... I sat here and really tried but those are the best things I could think of for this game. Overall it was just "okay" but mostly felt more like a demo for a game that is going to be released a couple of years from now... as in, it feels like they needed a couple more years to make this a fully fleshed-out game. It's lacking in almost every way possible. The most I would pay for this game (now, seeing what it is) is maybe $10. I would wait till it goes on DEEP sale if you are considering trying it. I really should have watched a playthrough video before purchasing this one. I actually, for the first time in my life, tried to return a game (this game) but unfortunately I had already passed the acceptable amount of play time for a return (by just a few minutes). Otherwise I would have stopped playing and just returned it. Since I couldn't return it through, I decided to just play it all the way through to see how it was... was not worth it. Why this game has such raving reviews is beyond me. I really do think it's just because they were faithful to the franchise and that's it. o other game studios should take note: What the fans want is for you to be faithful to the franchise and not change all the characters, the story, etc. with your forceful political views. 3/10 is the rating I give for this one though.

_childDocuments_.review: Small budget.  Small-ish crew of devs.  Some crashing.  Some laggy-ness.  But you can tell they LOVE their jobs, and squeezed all the value out of their budget they could, to turn out a game thats worth playing.  It could use some more aesthetic improvements, such as better, more varied score.  Some of the acting from the supporting cast is a little wooden, same with the lack of variety in the character models lol.  But for all that, Weller did good voice acting his role.  The story did good.  The direction and the cast generally did good.  The atmosphere did good, and the some of the bigger fights could get really desperate and hairy, when they didnt lag out, and drop FPS in some of the more busy fights.  Other fights could be much better structured as you can cheese your way through.  You actually have to watch your HP in many instances on harder modes.  But, its not too tough.  Still, works best on medium graphics all around, and if you try all the side quests as well as the main story, you get about 27hrs of gaming in your first go.   Some good, if a bit confusing wep upgrades make you progressively more damaging (I LOVE the exploding ammo perk), with some pretty awesome graphic effects.  The skill "lines" arent all that complex, and you can get by with only topping two-three of there.  Could be more customisation, but given the small team and budget, its forgivable.  Grainy, but often good, big maps, and a lot of fun violence, and a lot of Easter eggs lol.I say buy.  I got the Special Edition, and you get some nice stuff.  Lots of good twists in the story as well.  You'll like it, but as to the beginning, it'll crash occasionally, or get laggy as hell here and there no matter what you try to do.  For all that, the benefits outweigh the minuses to make all this still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to those people that liked the movies down to small details like Robocop's car bottoming out when he leave the station. For a indie game the gunplay is really really fun, head explode in fun and interesting ways and there is even a dedicated di*k shooting mechanic. The environments though small are well made and full of detail. The characters are much like the movie mostly cartoonish caricatures but are fun to like or hate retrospectively. Its short but sweet and I loved every minute of it.7/10 would shoot the entire gang population of Detroit in the di*k again
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: There are a ton of games out there, most a made with set of guidelines to make it a good game.Then you have something like this, the passion and work that went into this game is honestly jaw dropping. it felt like i was witnessing the Robo Cop story for the first time again. I simple can not express how amazing and incredible this game is.if any of the creators she this: thank you for a great game. it might seem greedy but i hope for more. Id buy that for a dollar
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This game... performance is abysmal, acting is meh, side quests are sometimes literally just pushing a button. But it just oozes atmosphere. I love games set in Detroit: Deus Ex Human Revolution, Detroit Become Human, and now this, and it doesn't disappoint.If you grew up in the 80s and 90s and were a fan of the films, you owe it to yourself to get this. Shooting drug-dealing punks has never been so satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: If you love the RoboCop franchise, this is the game of the century. If you didn't love the franchise, f*ck off. A game gushing with love for the classic that only true fans could create. Don't expect the modern trend of parkour and all that other BS. This game puts you in the mind of Alex Murphy and makes you feel it, clunkiness and all. You are quite literally built as a tank, but not invincible. And above anything else, you are still human (at least as much as you choose to be).
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: They did what i never thought anyone could do. Make a Robocop game that is fun, and doesn't crap all over my favorite movie. It does and has everything a Robocop game should. It made me laugh, made me tear up a bit, and has terrible violence and Peter Weller came back for this. Thank you devs for giving me something new from Robocop that is good.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: I did not think I would actually be giving GOTY to ROBOCOP but its honestly the best robocop ANYTHING weve had since the original movies.This game is so good and full of depth and so much longer than I thought that I actually started getting nervous that it was too good to be true only for the last three missions to blow my doubts out of the water. _childDocuments_.review: Tons of easter eggs for fans of the show. _childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, but sometimes crashes on me. The voice acting is not that good which is a bummer. I enjoyed it as a fan of the trilogy, but where are the comical commercials? The movies had some dark humor to them but it's pretty rare in this game. The graphics are very detailed and I was able to appreciate the controls. I do not like the selection of guns or the skills in the game. I like how the areas are huge and the missions are fairly straight forward. It's like a zone map with objectives around for exploration, although there's not much other than the occasional comical convo from NPCS. I wish there was more to scan and the enemies had more reaction to being shot, cause usually they just stand there and take multiple gunshot wounds as if they got hit with a pillow. Suddenly a limb will explode and they'll be like, "Oh my god, my hand!" What about the 8 bullet holes in you??Pros:Excellent graphicsLarge areas with clear objectivesFans of the movies will enjoy the gameDecent gameplayCons:Weak acting, dry and dull dialogDifferent guns can be annoying and pointless to pick upSome enemies are just annoying such as the motorcycle gangs, like come on, they're riding around in circles?Random crashing
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: From the 20 hours I have on the game, I can confidently say this game will splendor your police urging duties. Being able to play as RoboCop while having unique upgrades and having more than one circuit board available to you is the ultimate reason for this review. Also having the ability to merge your percentage upgrades is a feature I found neat. The only wish I have for future updates is the ability to free roam as RoboCop while also being able to govern the area you are in.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This game pays a beautiful homage to the source material, it's easy to tell how much the devs love it. The immersion works so well thanks to the heavy steps sound with clunky movements, the Auto 9 shooting mechanics with the scanning system, the fact that it is possible to go out in the streets and uphold the law doing stuff like issue parking tickets (LOL) and the dialogue options, all of this together with Peter Weller's voice acting conveys the feeling that you really are RoboCop himself and for me this is  the best thing about this game because I just love this character.If you like the original movies and also did like Teyon's previous game Terminator: Resistance then you can't go wrong here, just pick it up and show these guys some support because they deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is retro. It plays like 1990s arcade shooter remade as an FPS in Unreal 5. Robocop is Robocop, he's not the Doom Slayer. He's slow, the fun comes more from style that gameplay. There are better First Person Shooters out there gameplay wise for sure, but as an adaptation it's the only one that's don't the original Neumeier/Verhoven film any justice. Witcher 3 might be the best adaptation of any media into a video game, but this is the most faithful.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Played on AMD 6900 and the game crashed every now and then. After one crash I had to reinstall drivers because windows decided to fail back to generic drivers. It is very slow paced and you are a tank, so very easy to finish. The story is boring, gameplay is linear. Very truthful to original source and graphics are great, but not something I would play again or recommend to others. You must love the movies to appreciate the Rogue City. If you do, you will love the game too.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: RoboCop Rogue City exacerbated my expectations as I played the original RoboCop games and I didn't like it but as a die hard FPS fan I loved this game. The suspense and tension this game delivered was insane. I loved the story and the gunplay was good. The game is still really buggy but one time I was playing I got glitched out of the map which was really funny. The story driven game was a blast playing but one thing I didn't like was the lack of boss fights. I get that this is a game where you play as a police robot or a cop robot, but it would have been nice to fight against bosses. I also thought the game was too easy and the story was way too short.The game is not that well optimised and the graphics are bad in some points of the game. I think the dev team needed to work on this game for a bit longer and if they did it would have been the game of the year. Also, the game isn't worth the price, even if you got it on sale. _childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Played through this game and had some of the most fun I have had in a long while. And its not just that the game is extremely fun, but in general its probably the most competent title out right now that uses UE5 for its engine. During my run of the game, I only ran into three minor bugs, which I imagine will be patched out. If you do most everything the game can take about 20 hours to finish, give or take. Dialog choices actually matter in this game, along with how you choose to spend your XP. I beat the game using my Ryzen 5800X pc with a Radeon 7900 XT @ 4k maxed out with FSR set to quality. FPS never dipped below 45 on me, and usually just stayed in the 55-60 range. Also tested the game on my Ryzen 3600 pc that uses a RTX 2070 Super. 1080P at high settings, with FSR, basically stayed around the 60-70 range.Some of the voice acting was weak in this game though, which should be mentioned. With some voices being very mismatched to the NPC even, but not to the point that you'd hate it. Its more or less along the lines of voice acting from early/mid 2000s games before they started hiring decent experienced talent for even the most minuscule characters. Either way, off the top of my head, this year I have played through COH 3, Dark Souls Remastered, Dead Space remastered, The Last of Us, SW: Fallen Order, and this game. TBH I had more fun with Rouge City than most of those games mentioned.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all if you are not fan of the first Robocop movie this is not a game for you I think.Part human. Part Machine. All COP!Its pretty odd that a devteam that made a god awful Rambo railshooter has  managed to do pretty good Terminator game and now they do the same for Robocop. This is a linear shooterRPG you visit the same sort of HUBarea from to time to time where you can do police work: Issue tickets or go on a small side quests that mostly end up in these ultra violent shootouts where you can´t crouch but why would Robocop do that!?!? That look pretty much like the drug factory shoot in the 87 movie. Or you can be asked to finding a cat for the old lady.The game is also full of that AA yank so if thats a deal breaker don´t bother playing this. I did not encounter any gamebraking bugs or anything like that. Some times the dialogue cuts out when tou examine the plot points and that can be annoying. For the story... Its pretty much what Robocop 3 should have been. It takes place after the second movie so Teyon pretty much likes us to think that 3 does not exists. Its pretty ok nothing groundbreaking has few twists that are best to see by yourself. The devs even got Peter Weller to voice Robocop so thats a plus! But long story short: If you like the 87 movie or the chracter in general and would like to know what would it be like to blast gang members and junkies as a walking tank with your Auto 9 then buy this game! _childDocuments_.review: I want to get the biggest part out of the way. If you are looking for a run and gun style game that is full on action all the time, this game might not be for you. While I was streaming Robocop: Rogue City, I constantly explained the game more as a walking sim with shooting galley sections thrown in. Part Walking Sim - The reason I say this is more of a walking sim style game with shooting gallery sections would be based on the fact that you spend quite a bit of time walking around looking for Nuke, Fake Money, and Incriminating Documents for extra experience (if you choose to). Same thing for side quests and other collectibles (chip boards). Robocop's walking speed is what you would expect from Robocop. It's slow, it's menacing, and determined to serve some justice. Traversing around the semi open areas at this pace might deter people from exploring the areas or just be a turn off all together. It didn't bother me because it felt very true to what I thought being Robocop would feel like and enjoy a good walking sim. Each area has its fair share of world building elements as well. Turning on a radio to get a little snippet of news, reading a piece of junk mail, seeing a police taped off area just adds another layer to the game. You can sense and feel the crime, grime, and no good that is going on in game. Interacting with people in the game does seem to influence the story a little bit. I won't touch too much on this because of spoilers. There are a hand full of NPC's you get to interact with over the course of you playthrough that can change how people feel and interact about you. After playthrough 1, I went full good guy and felt like I got a heroes ending. Curious to see if I make some different choices if that changes or not.Side quests - Most side quests in Robocop really do slow the pace of the game down if all you are looking for is action. If helping someone find a cat, solving a crime on a commercial set, or issuing parking tickets sounds like something you can get behind, then you will enjoy the side content quite a bit. I can't state just how much I enjoyed doing all the small things that Robocop has to do from time to time but it definitely won't be for everyone. Combat - When you do get into a bit of action, the game is a blast. I haven't laughed so much during a gun fight in my life. Dashing in (one of you unlockables you can unlock), grabbing a baddie by their neck and throwing him back at his buddies was some of the most fun I have had. Grabbing the motorcycle riders off their bike when they are coming at you was a must. Blowing up the motorcycles as they were trying to get away makes for some real explosive moments. The guns all handle well and all serve their purpose and I don't have a whole lot to say here. Some of the upgrades also help with keeping the combat fun and fresh. The shockwave ability to stun enemies (or flat out kill them when fully upgraded) or adding extra armor (which also gives you some damage reduction) lets you feel like the relentless doom engine of justice you are. Add the ability to have a chance to ricochet bullets off walls (while using the VATS style Robocop view) made for some fun fights as well. I just wish there would have been more combat sections. After you beat the game, credits roll and that's it. No new game plus, no leader boards (not a big deal for me), no level or section select. If you want to replay the game on a higher difficulty you can and make some different choice that (might) impact the story. The story itself feels good and is the true Robocop 4 we never got. This will be a contender for my Game of the Year. Amazing game with a little bit of nostalgia thrown in.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: There is a point in this game where you really feel like RoboCop, walking about the city doing police work.  You speak and interact with civilians, influence the future of the city, and just start blasting in some violently fun shooting galleries while holding the gun we all wish we had.  This game is more fun than anyone would ever think and gives a far better story than that horrible remake.  Its amazing what a little passion for an IP can do in how it conveys its story and I really hope RoboCop fans run though this game.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of the the movie series this is a no-brainer. This game stays incredibly faithful to the source material and completely nails the thematic elements that make RoboCop what it is. For those who are new to RoboCop, you'll find a very capable shooter that is not very deep mechanically. There is a somewhat basic skill tree and upgrading system in place, as well as a choice system that seems to have very little impact on your overall experience. Graphics are excellent, with the exception of very rigid facial animation. If you are on the fence, I'd wait for a sale, but I feel this game is worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun to play (when it's not crashing) and I really feel they captured the spirit of the movie, but the execution of grand ideas requires hard work, and this game is sloppy. I crash to desktop often. No visual cue for when it saves a checkpoint. The graphics quality is dated looking and yet has highly demanding requirements. People say to wait for fixes but the game came out in November and there is still serious issues. I'm saying no to recommend unless you are willing to put up with a lot of technical issues and frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop: Rogue City is a fun game. Open enough for choices and exploration, but not so open as to be an 'Open World' where the story can be lost in meandering exploration, I found it to be the right mix of allowing me to do things as I wanted while keeping to a storyline that had a definitive time limit on things in a way that felt realistic and made sense. The gameplay is fun, and a lot of the choices it gives are meaningful.It definitely takes the stance that Robocop is Alex Murphy. While my own interpretation has always been that Robocop is more the machine, learning to be human from the memories of Alex Murphy left behind, and the game doesn't really let me explore that interpretation meaningfully, their way of looking at it isn't wrong, and is understandable from the story beats they're going for.

_childDocuments_.review: Pitch perfect requel to Robocop 2. Right off the bat, Peter Weller returns as Robo and its phenomenal to hear him again. _childDocuments_.review: Robocop was one of my favourite movies growing up. I'm really happy how faithful Rogue City is, it's so immersive. _childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolutely massive homage to RoboCop to such an extent that at times it feels like it's trying to right the wrongs of RoboCop 3 and make an open apology to Fans. I'm going to mix things up and start with The BAD first, since there's not much of it. * Facial animations are really lacking, so NPC's have a case of BethesdaFace, not a lot going on there. * Some voice acting can be a bit iffy at times, but it's pretty rare. * Some voice lines from enemies can get repetitive* If you don't explore a LOT you can miss out on missions that will pop up as failed objectives in your reviews. There's nothing telling you that these will happen while out and about. you NEED to explore. * Some iconic sounds from the film are missing such as the Auto-9, some of Robo's movement audio, ED-209's sounds, etc. The re-creations are a good attempt, but the originals are probably missing for a good reason. (Likely legal) Yeah. That's literally all i'm seeing for anything 'bad' from this game. Now the good. * Facial captures of characters from the films are uncannily real and look absolutely fantastic. * RoboCop looks stunningly good and Peter Weller reprises his role as Murphy so accurately as a voice actor you wouldn't even know a day has passed since the first film. * Getting to do day-to-day things as RoboCop actually makes him feel more real somehow and finally adds that extra depth to his character that I know Weller has been wanting to see. * Your actions and conversation choices matter heavily when dealing with characters, most NPC's have a sort of outcome in the game and based on your choices those can be pretty varied endings. * The plot takes some fantastic twists and turns in ways that may very well catch you off guard. * Gameplay is broken up into Investigations , Combat, Character Interactions and Exploration so you're always on the lookout for something cool. * Varied skill tree actually makes you feel significantly more powerful as you level up your various skills. EXP is aquired from finding loot, taking down hostiles and a huge boost at the end during your debrief based on what objectives you completed. * Detroit looks film accurate and amazingly grungy, yet still somehow not as horrible as current Real Detroit, which really says something about the state of the world today. * You are a huge chonker in combat and FEEL powerful, enemy reactions to being taken out can also be pretty hilarious. (Aim for the groin at least once, you'll thank me later.) * So much reverence for Robocop 1 and 2 that you will really feel like you're just playing what the third movie should've been. * About 9 -10 hours if you only do the story , 17 - 20 hours if you go for finding everything. Some of this is, admittedly, because Robocop can't sprint like he's in a zoomer shooter. He's a chonker. A fantastic purchase if you're just a casual shooter fan , an absolute MUST BUY if you're a fan of RoboCop.Bonus :  RoboCop can do the Robot dance for a kid at one point.

_childDocuments_.review: You are RoboCop. A half man, half machine of a being built with the purpose to protect the innocent, uphold the law and bring justice in a city where right and wrong, crime and theft and corruption are still things being dealt with everyday while those with power play gods with the lives of those beneath them. You're the only thing standing in their way.The game is set in-between the films RoboCop 2 and RoboCop 3. The story isn't all that special but rather how it handles everything makes it all that special. Corruption in the city of Detroit is a major problem and Detroit is on the brink of societal and financial collapse. Crime and theft are common place as a result. You are thrown in the middle of it all and it's up to you and key players to stop the city of Detroit from crumbling into chaos by those claiming to build a better future. 6/10I must say the gameplay was pretty good. Simple but good. I liked that they kept the 80's aesthetic of the environment. Being this iron man cop that can tank bullet makes you feel busted. Although your movement aren't so fast as you would imagine. When people see you rather than a normal cop, that's when you know this ain't a joke anymore. Playing as RoboCop, the player must clear the city of criminals, conduct investigations, and can also give out parking tickets. Issuing ticket for me felt boring lol. There's a skill tree that's fairly simple to upgrade to as well as motherboard chips you acquire or find while playing called module that can also be upgraded that strictly affect your Auto 9 pistol. While the standard skill tree helps you as you progress through the game, the module can affect how you play. I would even say it's sort of close enough to making a build of some sort. But there's 1 module in particular that just carried me from the moment i got it to the end and i just never wanted to take off. It was that good over the better more customizable ones. 7/10Combat is great but can get janky. I think the janky aspect of the game really helps it. You can throw gas tank, grab people and really throw them with so much force they turn to Tomato paste. Headshots has this weird but satisfying splat sounds effect to them lol. The headshot also causes the physics to break as dead bodies go crazy and often sent flying. Of course you can punch. Like really hard. 8/10RoboCop: Rogue City was developed using Unreal Engine 5 and at first glance you probably couldn't tell. I sure didn't know. I played this game with an RTX 4080 at 1440P with Dlss on the quality setting, Nvidia sharpness kept it at default and Frame Generation on with Reflex on. I was mostly getting 140 fps to as high 200+ fps with mixed graphics setting. Nothing was kept at max setting. Game never crashed. The game did have some visual glitch or errors but those were minor. Pretty cool destructible environment. I really shows a bit of the games physics. The game i think around the halfway mark started to stutter for a sec in key spot during various objective. Not entirely sure if it's because it's loading the next scene or event but it wasn't an issue. Didn't check gpu temps but i'm sure it stayed cool under 70° degrees. Towards the last 25% of the game is when you'll start to get some big fps lost when a lot is happening all at once. 8/10Again i couldn't tell this was made in Unreal 5 but it did look pretty good. Funny enough some assets look like ps3 graphics assets as they lack details. But that's when i realised this game only use high res assets where it's needed or when it matters. Not everything needs to graphically detailed and that's ok. It actually works with the aesthetics of the world. Facial animation is done very well even with a small lack of polish. I personally didn't have issue with it. Voice lines are good, cheesy and a small bit cringe but it works here. This seemed more like a AA title based on its quality alone. 7/10                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         They were ok aside from the iconic one that seems to play when things are getting serious. Could use some more tracks. 4/10The game wasn't all half bad. This is a well made RoboCop game and one i would recommend it if you're a fan of RoboCop or just want to turn your brain off and pretend you're Iron Man with a badge lol. But if you wait for a sale that's fair too. _childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun to play, and brought back a lot of fun memories of watching the movies as a child. It definitely felt like I was reliving those experiences, and continuing them. To those who made this, thank you for all the effort you put in to making it feel like a proper Robocop story. I am -really- hoping that there will be a sequel, or some DLC regarding that teaser at the end.On to specifics about the gameplay: Robocop is an unstoppable, slow, clunky tank that destroys just about anything he targets that isn't an even bigger war machine. Just as he's supposed to be. Even so, the skill points and customization of his Auto-9 pistol give some room for strategy and making the combat flow as it feels right to the player. There's also some fights where you definitely will need a bit of that strategy. My only complaint might be that while some of the levels and arenas feel very fun to run around in and having a moving battle with lots of weapon-swaps, it ended up not going that way for me. I pretty much just used the Auto-9 for most fights, and generally found a bit of cover to duck in and out of while I picked enemies off. It seemed like the game would actually punish you for exploring those bigger arenas for fighting in, since Robocop is absolutely terrible at dodging, or taking cover (again, as he should be.) There's things you can do to get around that a little, like using skills for shields or dashing, but that never really felt quite right to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend RoboCop: Rogue City. Take my words with a grain of salt, though. The game consists of levels you get to explore, that are also recycled throughout the campaign. Biggest example here being Downtown Detroit. I imagined the game to be open world, but it's basically just diet open world. Biggest highlight has to be the story, combat and investigation. The shooting is extremely good and when you aim it has the lock-on effect just like in the films. There have been moments where the lock-on didn't happen and I wasn't sure if it was a bug or an intended feature through damage taken. The ingame models for everyone except for RoboCop look pretty bland and are recycled for any non-story related characters. Performance can be an issue with some bugs/glitches that can and probably will impede progression. There are ingame fixes for them, but usually result in you having to reload a chapter in the story costing time and progress. Until then we can only hope the devs get on it and don't make this game into an abandonware. Investigation is pretty fun, where you scan certain objects to get very interesting details about chemicals and some cool effects to help solve a case. It can be very annoying sometimes as there are certain moments where you have to look for where you can scan and the only way to find the scan locations is to have the mouse hover over the spot exactly. Over some time of playing, you'll get experience points to put into RoboCop. They give bonuses to certain aspects plus, if you put enough into one column you'll unlock an ability/passive which can be very fun to mess around with. If you are a big fan of RoboCop, I'm sure you'll still enjoy it quite alot despite all of the flaws present in the game. If you aren't a fanatic, just wait for the game to go on discount, Because: "I'll buy that for a dollar!"7/10 I will have it a 9 or 10/10 depending on if the game gets some patches it deserves.
