_childDocuments_.review: Set right after the only robocop movies that can be considered good (admittedly they've all aged like milk by 2023 standards) Rogue City is a decent entry in an IP that has basically been dead for decades. If you want to follow the story completely though, you will need to watch those movies, the game doesn't try to explain the backstory at all.Overall it's a decent FPS game with some light RPG elements. It's not all that complex and it's pretty linear. It nails the aesthetic it was going for, although unfortunately it's held back by UE5's issue, namely stutters in some specific situations,  nanite causing pop-in (easily noticeable by just looking at the ground) and lumen (GI and reflections) being run at low resolutions which causes a lot of graphical noise and shimmering in some areas. These issues are pretty noticeable and  happen even with the relevant settings set to "Epic".If you liked RoboCop, you'll see this as a decent homage to the original movies. Otherwise this game might be a hit or miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the firm, RoboCop. The strength of reviews and my love of the film twisted my hand to delve into my shallow wallet to buy this 80's 'cyber' experience during the Christmas a sale. RoboCop: Rogue City is a game-like experience, not a game, with a largely ignorable narrative due to the games average mechanics, poor narrative editing and an intolerable amount of game breaking cut scenes. The "game' reminds of a plethora of mid 90's role playing adventure games that landed purely because CD drives arrived.The advertised love for the detailed nods to the classic film are justified. That said, beyond the callbacks & set pieces via UE5's reasonable visuals there's some truly major pacing issues with the game (and people complained about Max Payne 3).There's a myriad of relentless cut scenes, some of which incorporate needles inconsequential choices that, if you choose an option that is in stark contrast to another you'll eventually be brought back to the option the game is taking regardless of your choice. So, if you buy the game don't worry about the path you think you're taking. This is a linear game and a viel of choice. Moreover, for instance, if the cut scenes were in a film they'd immediately kill the flow and narrative. The aforementioned cut scenes are unnecessarily long - a colossal empty roll at the beginning and end of each cut...the player just sits thinking, is there more...It's like I'm watching a very poor B movie, but not B movie has ever been this bad at pacing. The cuts are frustrating, too many and like the cut scenes themselves, exist to make the game feel packed/increase game length.Unlike May Payne 3, the plot of this game isn't something I cared for in the slightest due to the awful editing and decision to have so many scenes that are all effectively interactive in the most faux manner (interactive in name only). I'm fairly sure nearly all players skipped these scenes after the first 30 minutes or less.I gavs up on the game after several hours. My fandom and love of the film couldn't balance-out how dire and plodding the game experience was. There's simply not enough action or gameplay crowbarred into the abundance of fruitless cut scene to warrant continuing. Action can last mere moments only for the player to be subjected to more dialogue that became dull and uninteresting well within the first 30 minutes of gameplay.However, if you're willing to stomach the tedium of the narrative and dire pacing then gameplay itself is barely so-so...Aiming isn't achievied via ADS. Right click offers a slight zoom, highlighting of the enemies and CRT scan lines to give a retro Robo effect. Unfortunately the aiming itself is based on mouse pointer physics - have you ever tried to get the cursor between two letters to remove a comma but miss - aiming is like that, which makes the gunplay a sod when attempting head shots or any sort of accurate shooting, especially in a hurry. Aiming and gunplay is loose and not fun, especially when you need to ditch RoboCops iconic Auto-9 to make a real dent in enemies as the game progresses. Movement is as expected. Tank-like, which is fine. However RoboCop can jump from the top of building and land with ease, with zero health hit. He can even step off a step/ledge/table, but he can't f'ing get back up the step/ledge so you have to navigate half the map to get back to where you were. He also can't crouch or go prone. You're effectively driving a very dull tank with less movement or abilities than an actual tank, not a human cyborg - for very short periods before another multitude of inevitable cut scenes continually interrupt whatever minor nugget of joy your hours of panning through cut scenes may have offered. RoboCop is a game-like experience, not a game, with a largely ignorable narrative due to the games average mechanics (if you're me).Buy Titanfall 2 if you want a brilliant action game that has mechs. Beyond the nods to the film this game is not what reviewers said. It is dull. It is lackluster. And the novelty of playing as RoboCop dies early into the game.Rogue City feels like a rushed game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amidst a glut of antiseptic, mediocre AAAs, I feel truly lucky to have run across a fair handful of Actually-Fun Videographic Games this past year or so (in the 12-month sense, 2024 is young yet).  On that short list, I'd place REmake Evil 4 as one--Loddlenaut was another... and Robocop rounds out the list.  Give me a AA with heart over your average AAA with *anything,* because there's no killer feature a sufficiently soulless production can't wreck.In a way, it reminds me of Cyberpunk 2077, but I hesitate to say that because I don't want to mislead anyone into thinking it's a big open world with lots of customization options and peripheral mechanics and side quests.  It's a fairly linear game, with hub-world sections that are semi-open, a la the first Deus Ex.  That's in its favor, though, because it maintains a certain momentum that so many bigger, broader games lose at the sag in their middle.The way it reminds me of Cyberpunk is really just in the way the story is involving, the combat is pleasingly chunky, and the dystopia is primarily technological and totally grim.  Mechanically, it's a much more sparse and spare little AA game than Cyberpunk's AAA offering, but I think I like Robocop just as much.  If anything, Robocop is the one that leaves me wanting more--I'm already looking forward to the next time Teyon's Terminator game goes on sale, because I'm officially convinced that's worth checking out.Also, I saw Robocop ages ago but I was born in 1989 and I never really worshiped Robocop as the cult classic so many others did.  I liked it fine, I'd call myself a fan, but I didn't play this game cus it was Robocop, I wasn't a *superfan,* I just played it cus I heard it was a good videogame.  And friends, I heard so very right.I never do NG+. and I still may never do it, but I'm actually considering it here for the first time, just cus it's deeply fun doing the basic combat, and in my campaign I modded up the Auto-9 (through its brilliant modular modding system, which sort of resembles the weapon modding in Control) to be basically a gore-amplified godgun, and I'm just not quite sure that I'm done spraying dudes with it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it. It's good. REALLY good.An absolute gem. Greatly satisfying shooting mechanics with punchy sounds, 90' style cinema over-the-top gore, that'll scratch that power fantasy itch (though on Hard difficulty you do need to have some tactical sense, prioritise targets and sometimes make use of cover).The game features RPG elements in the form of skills and abilities (anything from more healing charges, a damage absorbing shield, ricocheting bullets off walls like in the movie, hacking various devices etc.) and customising the iconic Auto-9 - RoboCop's gun - which is a cool little "puzzle" to solve in order to build the most optimal setup. This gun gets absolutely ridiculous later in the game, and I love it.The pace of the game is good. It introduces new enemy types, hazards and weapons at a steady pace, always sprinkling in something new, as well as NOT recycling mission structure much. It's NOT a "checklist simulator" like many recent open world games that have about 10 activities for the player to engage with, and repeat them ad nauseum across a bloated world. Nope. RoboCop: Rogue City is a narrative-driven game that does its absolute best to always present the player with something new to do.Anything that approaches "reusing" content is, in my opinion, executed well - first, the game teaches the player about a new mechanic, and some time later it comes up again, but this time the stakes are more dire, and the player has to rely on their previous experience with a similar mechanic. This is nothing but good design, and have game progression should look like.I find the story to be captivating, and the characters well written. Sure, it's not at the level of meticulous quality that some AAA titles reach, and the characters' tone and/or animations don't always match the mood of the situation, but that's a decisive minory - vast majority of the story was a pleasure to partake in.And "partake" isn't a random word - the narrative isn't just a story you passively watch unfold, as this game does present the player with choices that impact the outcome, not only for RoboCop himself, but also a cast of the few closest characters, as well as (without going into specifics) the political situation and the city of Detroit at large.The importance of choice outweighs something that I find to be a small, but noticeable shortcoming of the narrative - the quests don't really offer much in terms of a "failure state". Despite there being a fair amount of detective work and investigation, I haven't encountered a situation where RoboCop could end up drawing the wrong conclusions and arresting someone innocent.The only "failure states" are when RoboCop dies (but that just leads to reloading a checkpoint, so it doesn't really count), and on occasion failing to save hostages etc. (which impacts your mission evaluation score, and thus gained EXP points).Does the game have minor glitches and bugs? Yes.Do they hinder gameplay? Only once in the entire playthrough I've encountered a progress bug that required me to restart a mission - that's a bit sour, but the gameplay is more than fun enough, so replaying the section wasn't unpleasant. But if you dread having to replay a mission, you should probably wait a few weeks until the most pressing issues are patched.The support is responding to bug report emails very promptly, and assures that the dev team is working on rolling out patches. Given the sheer love put into this game (which shows in the little details) I'm very much inclined to believe.

_childDocuments_.review: After Terminator Resistance the devs of Teyon are back with another love letter to a classic movie franchise. This time RoboCop got the treat and this is such a fun shooter with small sandbox gameplay and main and side quests, many characters from the movies, a great story you can influence a little bit and then get a Falloutish ending that tells you what happened based on your decisions. Technically the game looks great with very detailed levels, great lightning and very sharp textures, just the facial animations of the characters are a bit stiff but that is super tricky and expensive to pull off and only a minor thing in an otherwise  good looking game. Gameplay is very fun, the guns feel great and your robocop gun may have unlimited ammo and can be upgraded, it is not a jack of all trades and the other weapons you pick up have all a purpose and change how the game plays.I encountered a few small bugs here and there, but nothing game breaking and the game never crashed and ran great in max settings in 4K and 1440p on my 4080, Ryzen 7, 32GB DDR5 Ram, 990 Samsung M2 and Windows 11 64 bit. The only thing that the game misses is a 4 in the title!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true Robocop game. Made by the same people that did Terminator Resistance; the devs of Robocop: Rogue City truly understand what Verhoeven's Robocop film was all about, and capitalized on what made the original so good.The story is fantastic and a quality entry into the Robocop franchise.It's an FPS, but it makes the ballsy move of putting you in the role of a slow moving tank that soaks up tremendous amounts of damage. It really does great in making you feel like a power house without making the game feel -too- easy.The Devs truly made a fantastic game. However, it has its flaws that betray its nature as a less-than-AAA title made by independent developers.Pros-Amazing story precisely in the aesthetic of the original Robocop film. Complete with fun retrotech feel to everything.-The combat is slow moving but it works for the feel of the game. It's less about jumping around and finding cover and more about stomping forth, killing the bad guys before they can dish more than you can take.-Peter Weller as Robocop!-Many nostalgic elements that exist for more than just fanservice. (ED-209 scenes are great!)-A very intuitive weapon upgrade system (with flaws, see the cons)-Peter Weller as Robocop!-Combination of missions with sidequests, heavy emphasis on dialogue choices that greatly influence the plot and the outcomes of characters you interact with, and open-world sections that give you freedom on how to explore things.-Peter Weller as Robocop!Neutral-Collectible ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ seems like something we should be veering away from these days. But the game doesn't make it -too- tedious. It's fun exploring rundown cityscapes for drugs, stolen materials, and incriminating documents for XP... But I personally could've done without it.Cons-This is quite possibly the only truly horrible thing about the game. The game is chock full of some strange bugs, game breaking events, and serious problems with the skill tree and weapon upgrade system.1: Numerous times I've needed to reload a game because it softlocked on me. Not sure how this happens, but in my first playthrough it happened about 5 times and required reloading the sequence. (I know one situation in particular is because I grabbed an NPC in combat and threw him into another NPC, both NPCs clipped through a wall and never 'flagged' as killed so the mission couldn't be continued.)2: Skills are bugged. As in... For some reason, at the start of a mission or loaded instance, NONE of the skills you've accumulated will function. It's as if you have 0 skills. The only fix I've discovered for this is to zone between areas a couple times until starts working again. Reloading a save doesn't seem to fix this, it seems to happen between loading screens. You won't get your skills back until you force another loading screen, which isn't always possible.3: 4: Strange flags for character interactions. I'm not sure how this happens, but occasionally I run into NPCs and it seems like it skipped something I should've encountered. Conversations happening halfway or referencing material I haven't encountered yet.In one really messed up scene: Robocop is being interviewed by a reporter. I think the devs forgot to record the Reporter's lines because the reporter just sort of stood there in total silence, not speaking a single word, as Robocop proceeded to answer her questions despite nothing coming from her.And... That's it. Really the only thing holding this game back are the silly bugs. Stuff that give it a funny little indie game charm, so they don't stop me from playing!If the devs focus on fixing all the problematic bugs over the next few months, we're looking at a fantastic game to cap off a really good year for the game industry.EDIT: The Auto-9 bug has been -verifiably- fixed! The game is only getting better as it's refined post-release.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty solid FPS adaptation of Robocop. I'm only part way through the game so I can't speak to the overall plot, but my impressions so far are as follows:* They nailed the feel of Robocop - he does feel like a tank and he's definitely not fast, but you don't really mind since that's kind of the thing with this character. Having the "speedup" button helps cut down on his slow walking getting annoying.* They also absolutely nailed the sound design; everything sounds movie-accurate - Robocop's walk, ED-209's growls, the gun sounds, and even just the general background city noise. It really helps with the immersion.* The difficulty is pretty on-point - you're definitely tough, but a few bad guys reaming you with bullets will still do significant damage. So far it doesn't feel like a walk in the park, which is good.* The variety of weapons is great. You of course have Robo's auto-9 from the movies, but you can also pick up a pretty wide range of weapons from bad guys. Also, there's plenty of objects in the environment for you to pick up and throw, like gas tanks, motorcycles...you can even pick up dumpsters if you want.* The progression mechanics are pretty well done too. You get skill points you can put into various skill branches; if you put enough in any specific branch you get special skills you can deploy, like a shockwave to stun enemies, slow-mo for a brief period, and even non-combat options like increased XP from dialogue. You can also acquire chips and circuit boards to upgrade your auto-9, so it doesn't just become the base gun you ditch as soon as you get hold of an rifle or a machine gun. It helps of course that the auto-9 has unlimited bullets but still, it's good that you can improve it.* The environment and locations are pretty well-done. You get to revisit a lot of locations from the movies, but there's a lot of other places you get to wander around in.* The side quests are pretty varied. It's kind of fun to be Robocop and giving out tickets for public urination, or collecting signatures on a get well card for a fellow officer. It all adds to the silly charm that's carried over from the movies.However, there are some things that, so far, I haven't been such a fan of. These include:* Fan service. It gets a bit on the nose occasionally. I get that the attraction of this game in the first place is to play a game version of the movies but it's not always necessary to link everything back to the movies. For example, it annoys me that they felt the need to connect one of the main characters with a character from the first movie. So far I haven't seen any evidence that there's a purpose to the connection, and it feels a bit like it's part of this trend where movie and TV continuations feel the need to make everything connected and have some kind of in-depth backstory that's totally unnecessary and distracting.* The plot (so far) seems...fine, I guess. I suppose I can't really judge it until I've completed it. I do feel like I know exactly where it's headed though. Also, while I appreciate that they tried to give the dialogue and world-building a satirical sheen like the movies, the writing falls a bit short and while most of the voice actors do a good job, the dialogue often comes across as trying a bit too hard to be clever and ends up kind of cringy.* While the graphics and enivironmental design are generally solid, it feels a bit like it could've used a couple more passes to get some more graphical detail in there. Everything feels a little bit flat, like there is a lack of texture sometimes. It's mainly noticeable in the character faces, especially up close where there just seems to be a lack of detail or something, and this is on a new PC with everything set to high/ultra. It doesn't ruin the game or anything, but it does make the game look a little like it was made 5 years ago or something.* Although it's a pretty well done Robocop game, it's probably not going to please any hardcore FPS players. It doesn't really bring anything new to the FPS genre but to be fair, that's not really necessary and it's still fun for what it is.Overall, I give the game a solid 3.75. It's not an all-time great, but it's still a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The vibe is on, the gameplay is great, and feels like your playing as a big lumbering robot cop. The dialogue choices initially felt a little forced but they became really endearing and it seems that the choices you make really do affect the outcome of the game and the other characters as well as being funny and introspective towards the themes of Robot cop.The Gunplay is mostly good, feels great to get headshots, and blow off the limbs of criminal scum. The additional weapons you can find in the environment are either amazing or terrible lending little to the variety, though you can upgrade/customize the pistol to fill different roles. By the end the pistol will likely be never reloading fully automatic powerhouse that outclasses every other weapon as long as you choose to engage with the upgrade puzzles. It can get kinda repetitive by the end, especially if you do every side quest. In additions some bossfights are bullet sponges that become slogs after you fight them once.The gun upgrades being circuit puzzles feel a little out of place in the game, and if you choose to use them when you find them in the middle of missions they can break up the pacing quite a lot. They aren't bad, but slowly placing the circuits to get the perfect stats can grind the game to a halt, especially if you don't like that kind of thing.The side missions vary in quality and content, with some your just giving traffic tickets or yelling at teenagers, and in others your solving murders with your cop buddies, or, of course, blowing through hordes of bad guys. Most are great but some are boring and confusing, I never did find one traffic violation.Overall the game Nails the vibe, is fun, and runs really well. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Robocop game we've all waited for. It's one of my favorite movies of all time, and you can tell the studio who developed this love the movie every bit as much as I do. Technical stuff first, the graphics are great, the audio is incredible, especially playing in a home theater (The Auto-9 is LOUD AF and my ears are ringing a bit), everything is smooth with little to no chop (improved over the demo, and the demo was already fairly stable). I haven't experienced any crashes or bugs yet, and I'm already several hours into the game.Gameplay is excellent. The controls are tight and accurate. The default keyboard layout is just fine, and I found myself only changing a couple of keys only out of preference. Hit detection is good, AI is serviceable, albeit not amazing. There's a fair amount to explore and find. Side missions are varied and add a lot to the feel of the world and characters. While fairly straightforward and simple, combat is never boring. The guns all feel different, with the Auto-9 feeling absolutely badass ("Check that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gun!"). Most of all, the gameplay is actually just plain fun. The rest: Story and voice acting are solid. There are a LOT of locations and characters you're gonna recognize and be happy to see. I caught myself all the time going "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, they got that right!". The dark humor is 100% bang-on. I can't remember the last time I laughed this much playing a game. they absolutely nailed it. Easter eggs and details are everywhere.I was worried this was gonna be just more movie license cash grab garbage. It is sooo not. It's a solid, well made, well crafted, and incredibly fun game. I don't review a lot of games but I feel this game is worth taking the time to do so. If you loved the movie (I ignore the sequels), you're gonna love this game. Absolute must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll start by talking about what this game isn’t - it’s not a “bold reinterpretation” or “revised for modern audiences”. It doesn’t hate itself, it doesn’t feel morally superior to its audience, and it doesn’t lecture and wag its finger at you like a schoolmarm for being problematic because you want something to stay the way you fondly remember it. What a beautiful rarity in this foul age to come across something made with love and affection for both an IP and its fans. It makes you dream of chaining those responsible to their desks and not releasing them until they have made an adaptation of every 80s/90s franchise you ever loved.So what is it? To me it feels like a hyper-condensed version of the newer Deus Ex games sprinkled liberally with 80s cheese and satisfying UE5 combat. There’s a basic skill system, and a very nice little gun customization element where you can turn your pistol into anything from an autoshotgun to a marksman weapon. These mechanics fade into the background and leave you free to enjoy exploring the dystopian urban environments and blasting their various miscreants into bloody chunks. As a heavily armored tinman, you aren’t fast and agile (no bunnyhopping or twitchy leaning); this lends itself to a uniquely slow-paced combat style that gives you time to appreciate the excellent gore and environmental destruction as furniture and masonry explodes and paper flies everywhere. Hurl CRT monitors at people! Throw punks into the air and blast them into wet pieces! Shoot biker gas tanks and watch them explode in glorious slow motion! Listen to the satisfying plink-plink of pistol rounds bouncing off your upgraded armour! It looks and sounds great, there’s a good ratio of dialogue and action, and it even spends time reflecting on what makes a man vs a machine and the possible conflicts between law and ethics. It has that oddly optimistic 80s warmth that stands at odds with the nightmarish urban decay. What an unexpectedly great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd buy this game for more than a dollar!IN the year of our lord 2023, a movie about cyborg Jesus kicking ass in a dystopian capitalist hellscape is very sorely needed, and this game delivers!As someone who has been a huge fan of the original RoboCop movie, this is as faithful an homage to that movie, and also, like me, acknowledges the 3rd movie not existing. Gameplay: RoboCop doesn't run, he doesn't duck and cover, he just, stands behind cover. Which is absolutely fine, because this isn't the crappy 2014 remake, no...  RoboCop is a tank. He takes damage like a beast, and while you can have a secondary weapon, the Auto 9 is where it's at. This almost feels like a lightweight version of a Bethesda RPG, more than a FPS, because there are stats you can dump your points into, and even your Auto-9 has a PCB modding system that allows you to add and modify your gun behaviour.Did I mention the Auto 9 has unlimited ammo?The game isn't ALL action though, there are breaks in between combat where you have to actual policework, like issuing parking tickets, investigating crimes by looking for evidence and clues left behind at the scene, etc.Story:  The story is actually pretty deep and faithful to RoboCop, though with less of an over-the-top parody of capitalism as a whole. Though these days it's kinda hard to parody society when we're literally doing everything most 80s sci-fi films and media warned us NOT to do. The subquest stories are surprisingly involved, have multiple layers,  What would SEEM like a one shot subquest suddenly opens up to have a larger narrative to the world, and to who RoboCop is. Depending on how you play the game, either by Upholding The Law, or Serving the Public Trust by giving a verbal warning for infractions, you can change the outcome of how some side characters perceive you.Easter Eggs: Don't forget to look and explore everywhere, because there are a LOT of easter eggs, and movie references? There are so damn many I can't even begin to count. I genuinely laughed when I was walking through a level, and I had to stop and take a look at one of the street graffiti which said "Can you fly, Bobby?"  Cons: I would say, the big con for me is the lip syncing and the overall flat facial textures of everyone else that isn't RoboCop, or Anne Lewis, his partner. The lip syncing is very...  dated, but considering this is a game designed by 10 people on a limited budget, this is a very minor complaint considering the polish on what matters most.Can this game fly, Bobby?  Absofreakinglutely

_childDocuments_.review: "Play the game citizen or there will be... trouble"As you play Rogue City, you decide what kind of cop you'll be. It's a brilliant combination of investigation, action and moral dilemmas, weirdly it's what I've always wanted from a Batman game.One key aspect of Rogue City is Murphy working through his own thoughts on whether he is more man or metal.And this is what I thought worked so well, the existential thoughts, the debate on whether Robocop should have human rights like the ability to vote? the politicians true to life in that neither are appealing options but a decision must be made nonetheless.And the battle of justice or serving the public trust. It just works so well and gave it a level of depth and heart it feels exactly like an important part of the Robocop series and a true entry.This isn't just an action game. Your choices have consequences, how you interact with characters will affect them later, you have to consider what you are and what you want Detroit to be. I loved this game. Just so much. It's so classicly 80's, it's voice acted to perfection, it looks grungey and grim as it should do and the one liners are great.I can't rave about it enough really.The game play is fantastic and I'm not super into shooters so I was surprised at how much I enjoyed that aspect, there's so much you can do with the PCB boards and the different effects they have. I particularly enjoyed investigating, gathering evidence and the interactions with perpetrators.* Is there any voice so iconic as Peter wellers? Reprising his role as Robocop as any good citizen should! * Sidenote, I wanted to play this on my Steam Deck but the cloud saves don't seem to work properly which is a little disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey Robocop fans outta there! Even though I would like to say a few words about this game here, you should know that this is (once again) not a real review. Thanks for your understanding. 😉So what's the best way to start? The game is a terrific adaptation of the popular RoboCop movies with - admittedly - a few unpleasant things that don't get a thumbs down in my recommendation for this review. The atmosphere in this game was too ingenious, captivating me by the second. The story with the main missions and side missions were mostly captivating and great - some were actually boring or just strange. The stories and the background of the protagonists and some of the sourpusses were wonderfully funny, but also profound - especially when it came to Alex Murphy. The ability to influence the story largely through your own decisions really appealed to me and I'm glad how the story turned out in the end.The feature that you can improve your character with many skills was logical and well implemented. I also tried to make RoboCop as "human as possible". And everyone has to find out for themselves how this is possible. 😊Now you probably want to list some negative points, right? Ok, of course they're part of it. But it's still important to know that Teyon is a small development company that somehow managed to win the rights for Terminator and RoboCop. And rightly so, in my opinion. Well, now to the negative:As I briefly mentioned above, there were some quests that were either just boring or even illogical and not really "appropriate" as far as RoboCop is concerned. But as long as I got my XPs for it, that was bearable. I also have to say that the gunplay was extremely negative. If you were involved in a shootout with several enemies, you had to struggle more to aim properly. I know what the developers were thinking, but aiming is an absolute cramp that you can't otherwise imagine. So slow and inaccurate. You had to sleep with the "bad aiming" to get to grips with it, especially in the later stages. But what I like to emphasize again and again: Just try to always aim upside down, it'll go faster 😉 Another thing I didn't like was RoboCop's very slow movement. And before the hardcore RoboCop fans jump on me. Yes, I know that RoboCop is a robot that generally moves slowly and inaccurately. But in the game I found the movements really "exhausting" at times. But you can cope with that too. And yes, there were also some in-game bugs that made you wonder why you hadn't seen them before. For example, I once saw a police officer in the station whose face was suddenly twisted 180 degrees (*) and I felt a bit sick at the sight of it. Or that I saw a "flying" cigarette at the petrol station. Or spurting blood that was just "hanging" in the air. Yes, there were bugs like this in this game, but also in many other games. That's why there's definitely no thumbs down for me in the review.(*) To summarize, I can say that the 23 Euros I paid for the game were very much worth it. Just as was the case with Terminator: Resistance. Teyon knows all too well how to "integrate" 80s/90s flair from movies into good games. I really hope that more movies will make it into games in the future from the hand of Teyon!Rating:80/100
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Only 3 hours in and loving it so far. It has an authentic early 90's vibe. The investigations are kinda like the Sherlock Holmes games but easier. The shooting is a blast and the action can get quite intense. The game is quite brutal at times with fountains of blood from certain headshots. Its a perfect follow up story wise to Robocop to Robocop 2. Performance wise everything is great running on a RTX 3090 with DLSS on quality.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic movie game from the developers that brought you Terminator: Resistance, which is also a fantastic movie game. Seriously this developer needs more attention. RoboCop: Rogue City is graphically pretty, violent as hell in the spirit of the movie, has a good story, and by some miracle they even got Peter Weller himself to voice the titular character. Not only is it a great shooter but the game is of decent length and has lots of cool side missions where you help solve crimes and do detective work. Just overall, this game is a great experience. It contains all kind of content and references from the movies, takes place shortly after the events of RoboCop 2, and feels like the proper RoboCop 3 we deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: A game that blends the plots of the original three robocop movies with interesting characters, gameplay and story with an interesting look into Alex Murphy coupled with enough easter eggs to make fans of the franchise proud, this is a solid game. The non Auto 9 gameplay is terrible and clunky, but the auto 9 is oddly satisfying to use and makes you feel like an 80s action hero. Though you're not invincible like you are in the movies, the different abilities you have and the skill points allows you to get close to that. The game is enjoyable, and a love letter to a franchise that I loved as a child. I would highly recommend this game to anyone interested in Robocop.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Robocop: Rogue City is a game I can't seem to really place as parts of it felt new while others felt dated both as far as overall game play, audio and graphics go.  The shooting action is certainly the star of the show with plenty of blood and dismemberment.  Especially the guys sporting wife beaters and welding helmets.  The story and side quests are fairly interesting.  The voice overs and facial animations look very dated, especially Murph with his helmet off.  His face looks like it was molded from play-doh. I don't feel as if the game is well optimised.  My rig is hardly old and more than capable yet I am seeing ridiculously high CPU usage with all other background junk turned off, set to Epic.  The game has a long startup similar to some Bethesda games and is glitchy up to the title screen but did I mention the shooting action.  Something quite satisfying about splitting noggins with your big fancy gun that really make me like this game far more than I did Terminator: Resistance.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nothing short of a miracle. Never would I dream of having a story-driven, RPG-lite, first person shooter based on Robocop. It is a bit glitchy, it is rough around the edges at some points, it doesn't have the best optimization... but man, it is worth it The game is just about remorselessly shooting gangs, but also about going around issuing parking tickets, solving local disputes and making choices between helping the public or the corporation. The tone is on point, it's as much of a dark comedy as it is a somber dystopia, as it is a touching story about humanity and trauma. The graphics are great, Robocop looks and moves like he should, all the recognizable characters from the movies look perfectly like the real thing. The voice acting is great too, specially nice to have the real actor from the 80's, Peter Weller, doing Robocop again.I greatly recommend the game, take it slow, explore around and try to immerse yourself on it, the devs clearly put a lot of effort and care into this, and it definitively shows... Just remember that it's a relatively lower budget AA game, not a Sony-caliber AAA cinematic experience. And I would also recommend watching Robocop 1 and 2, the movies, before playing this... But hey, you should just do that anyway, great movies
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Some minor performance issues and frequent texture loading in on an M.2 drive. Otherwise, the game it self ran very well. Game as such is a love letter to the first two movies. Witty remarks, over the top violence and Peter Weller giving his voice for Robocop, was a very welcoming addition. Sadly not every acting performance was solid, but passable at best.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story, super nostalgic experience! But I've got one problem: performance. I checked the games min specs before buying. I've got the exact minimum specs, but the only way I can play is at 1080p, dlss set to performance, and medium settings. The shadows are jagged and grainy, same with reflections, and I still experience frequent stutter while playing. More and more games are being released that require DLSS to run instead of being optimized. Can't recommend the game until I buy a better computer.Edit: In my frustration, I went and looked up how others were doing performance wise. Turns out, with the framerate set to limit to 60, the game runs horribly, but when I set it to unlimited, suddenly I can turn the settings up and hover around 70fps. this is silly, but at least I can enjoy the game now!
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: The shooting and aesthetic keeps me hooked longer than, for example, Trepang2, which also had good shooting but failed in a cinematic experience. This game got a lot of inspiration from the first 2 Max Payne games.It's really weaksauce how you can't look down to see your robo feet.I hear there is no new game plus, so you will always have inadequate detection skills for investigating the levels. So... yeah, that's a bummer.Also, WHY WHY WHY does Robo hold the AK with two hands, AND WHY IS THERE RECOIL WHEN HE DOES?! Way too much recoil on the guns. The AUG IS UNUSABLE... WHY? He's a strong robot, there should not be recoil like that.There are some gamebreaking bugs where enemies get stuck off-map and you can't trigger progression. Fortunately, you can revert to a previous auto-save.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Robocop movies, this game is for you. It's that simple. It captures the essence of those films excellently, and I'm honestly shocked how well this turned out. It's violent, gory, funny, epic, and just all around a great time. The fact that the developers pulled this off without the game coming across as a cheap knock off or an insult to the movies is impressive. After completing the game once, I am still astonished that we got a game like this in 2023. Robocop fans need to check this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: RoboCop: Rogue City

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:* No manual saving - game uses automatic save checkpoints. * Game isn't auto-detecting my monitor's base refresh rate of 120hz - has options to use 30fps and 60fps framerate locks but not 120hz. * Game doesn't do a very good job of presenting side missions in some circumstances - I have had multiple levels where I completed them and didn't even know there were certain side missions / tasks available until afterward as they were never presented in any noticeable way so I wouldn't find out until my after-action report and find out several side opportunities were completely missed. * Likely due to a lower-budget game, there isn't a lot of music in the game; some good music during roaming & combat can add quite a bit to the experience. There's a little bit of it toward the end which was good, but I think the right roaming and combat music in the right situations adds a lot of feeling to the game. * I did not enjoy the bomb disarm mini-game at all - thankfully it's only used in the game a couple of times. Pros:* Excellent graphics. I was pleasantly surprised by just how good they are in a AA title like this with a limited budget. Devs did a good job with this. * Controls are very simple and straight-forward for the shooting / combat aspect of the game. Very easy to get into the game. * Good solid narrative story and side quests that were fun to follow throughout the game. * Good environmental opportunities for throwing explodable objects at the enemies. * Game runs pretty well in terms of performance - I've seen quite a few mentions of hitching by other people but I have seen none of that, myself; game runs pretty darn smooth the majority of the time in 4K @ 60fps (this is on an RTX 3090 and 11900K). Game is pretty demanding, so just be reasonable with your graphics & framerates selections and the game should run fairly well for you. I'm running the game on a standard SATA drive (not an NVME drive) and no issues at all with stuttering or hitching. * Many different types of enemies during the combat so things stay interesting and not boring or too repetitive as you have to deal with the enemy types differently.  * I've seen some folks in the forums talk about stability issues with the game and a lot of crashes, but I had exactly zero crashes in ~16 hours of playing it. * Game has good, enjoyable mechanics in terms of the combat - good upgrade system so you can tailor RoboCop's abilities and enhancements to your play-style. RoboCop has some special abilities that you can unlock with them - for example he has a shield mode and a slow-mo mode that remind me of armor mode in Crysis & Slow-Mo from Fear / Trepang2 that are fun to use. * Zero wokeness in the game which was incredibly welcome. * No Epic Online Services.* No Denuvo.* No extra DRM or additional launchers needed. Game Length: ~16-17 hours. Final Rating: 8/10. With the AAA games industry in such shambles today with the ESG / DEI / Woke-Mind-Virus seeming to infect almost everything at the AAA level, it's A and AA games like this one that are having their time to shine and gaining support from gamers. I find myself buying more of these types of games than I ever have and I strongly recommend this game to others. I love supporting studios that make good content that gamers want without any of the nonsense.

_childDocuments_.review:
Become the iconic part man, part machine, all cop hero as you attempt to bring justice to the dangerous, crime-ridden streets of Old Detroit. 

Armed with your trusty Auto-9, factory-built strength, years of experience on the force and a variety of tools at your disposal, you will fight forces seeking to destroy the city you call home in an all new first-person, explosive hunt for the truth. You have the power to decide how to fulfil prime directives in your own way, but as the story unfolds proceed with caution because corruption and greed know no limits.

Prepare yourself to... PROTECT THE INNOCENT AND UPHOLD THE LAW.

name: Ultra Age
detailed_description: Slash your way through a futuristic Earth overrun with ruthless mutants and powerful robots as Age, a young soldier sent on a mission to prevent the destruction of humankind. Now including ‘Rebirth Project,’ the all-new rogue-lite side mission that can be accessed from the main menu! (DLC installation is required.) Far in the future, the resources of Earth have become insufficient, its ecosystem long ago changed irrevocably by a passing meteor. Humankind has divided into two: the people who have escaped Earth and relocated to the space colony, 'Orbital Arc,' and those who have remained on Earth in a facility called ‘The Shelter.’ Humanity vanished from earth after civilians from The Shelter failed on the experiment that was meant to be the last hope for humanity, while people from the Orbital Arc sent expeditions to earth in search for resources . Failing to find any signs of life, A young sword-wielding warrior named Age falls down from orbit to Earth. Accompanied by his floating android, Helvis, he must find the indispensable key to the survival of humankind... Slash through foes with a variety of blades in high-speed, stylish action! Change blades on the fly into powerful moves to create linkage and run combos. Different attributes and varied actions call for strategy against different types of foes. Launch the wire skill to pull smaller enemies toward you, or Quantum Warp to get instant access to larger foes! Use the wire to strategically overcome crowds, traverse gaps on land and quickly grab items. Gather elements to enhance your blades, expand your skills, and learn new combos. Install modules and power gear to level up Age and increase your arsenal of blades to take down the toughest of enemies. Use Helvis to burst into Critical Rage, cast Healing Pocket to recover, or Time Shift to loot more items. Follow Age on his journey in the year 3174. Experience cutscenes that tell the story of Age’s mission across futuristic mecha, forests and deserts developed with Unreal Engine. Encounter mysterious characters and overcome menacing bosses to uncover the story behind the fate of humankind. Fight through a series of hexagonal zones spanning 30 Floors as a reincarnate construct of Age. Consisting of battle zones with increasing difficulty and rewards, new monsters and bosses not seen in the main game, an enhanced upgrade system, and new blade affinities, ‘Rebirth Project’ adds a completely separate game experience providing hours and hours of gameplay to Ultra Age.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Finished the game on Normal within 6 hours.Game is quite good, it was developed by 6-9 people, you can definitely feel it, but it is still great Indie level of game. Story is quite interesting, gameplay is fun, game ends before you get bored. Try the demo and if you like that you will like the full game. Some elements in game felt bit unfinished (see below).Combat is good and swift, dodge mechanic feels very natural it does use some DMC/Bayonetta elements, and sometimes camera is clunky and every time your enemy goes off screen you lose lock on, but so far it was minor inconvinience, You can chain combos, switch weapon on the run to do combos. If you like the demo, you would like final game.If you want to know how does combat/gameplay feel:Take speed of nier combatSword switch similar to DMC, + Nero armAnd now put these 2 elements in X-Men origins wolverine quality of game. Thats what you can expect, nice mechanics but not polished to the level of DMC5/Bayonetta.Game is sort of a crossover between Nier and DMC/Bayonetta.Pros:+each boss is unique, there is a lot of them+weaponswitch for impressive combos+story+dodge mechanism+interesting enemies+no need to grind, you can find plenty of crystals by fighting and if you want to get more crystals you can press time capsule and all enemies will respawn - Ideally in the "maze" sections.Cons:-no new game plus/post game content (like arenas with bosses or replay a level)-You cannot max out "parts" as I was expecting or I must have missed 10 cores-for some reason when you max healing you can store up to 200 energy, but container still replenish only 100 points (not 100%). Kinda sucks when you die at boss and can only recover 50% of health recovery nearby or backtrack to other energy box.-from mid game you end up using only 2 weapons out of all 6 (to be fair 2 basically are upgraded version of original swords-parry mechanic on Claymore is somehow late and clumsy, hard to time properly on regular mobs.-camera is to close for my liking most of the time, sometimes its super annoying as you canot see ♥♥♥♥, specially against balls throwing offscreen beams at youo-lock-on enemies is lost if the enemy goes offscreen (minor annoyance),-forwarding time is not utilized in the game or required for progress. I never had to forward time to replenish swords. The lowest I got was to 8 Claymore charges, when fighing only robotic enemies with it. So there is no need to save on time capsules. Basically it is better to use Time manipulation to get new respawns when you are in the maze sections or when you cleared multiple spawns and need to return back.  You can get better drops and grind crystals.-I have died like 5 times in this game; 3 times because of camera, 2 times because I was rushing boss.Still fun game and worth the 30% of AAA game pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultra Age is definitely a fun game and it's an ideal entry point for people who want to get to know the hack 'n slash genre.For the veterans of the genre, it's a fun, short and not too expensive experience, but one that won't surprise you because of a bit of monotonous gameplay.It's not the graphical splendor, the high-quality story or the great dialogues that will convince you, but rather the fluid combat and the fun boss fights.Check out gameplay of the game here: Ultra Age is set in the distant future. You play a young warrior named Age, who must ensure the survival of humanity.Earth's ecosystems have been irrevocably changed and you, Age, are sent out with your floating friend Helvis as the last hope of finding a solution for humanity.In the game you will be equipped with a standard steel sword and you will also receive regular help from Helvis, so together you will have to save humanity from its destruction.The game also has good support for ultra-wide resolutions, check out an example of the game at 3840*1080 here:

_childDocuments_.review: It's really not that bad, and I knew not to expect the world with a small team's love letter to DMC. In a lot of ways they got the feeling and the ability to go CUHRAYZEEE right, giving you 4 equippable weapons that let you offensively swap between them with seemless combo potential.Thing is, the game is AGGRESSIVELY middling in presentation. Music doesn't pump you at all, enemies aren't too interesting, and the dime store Nero you play as doesn't have the charisma that makes you want to stick with him for the journey.I haven't finished it, but apparently there's no kind of mission replay, so you can't expect to take all of your tricks you've gained from the journey back to the start for a good power trip.I know it's a small crew that put this together, and what they made IS impressive considering. I just can't find the motivation to keep with this and not just turn on something else.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend Ultra Age overall, but it does have some significant flaws with it. On a fair numerical scale, where the line for an average game is 5 instead of 7, I would rate this game 6.5/10. It's a fair effort for the first game from a new studio, and I hope that they learn from the experience and their next game will be even better.Speaking of the positives of the game, the combat overall feels good. All the attacks feel fluid and the dodge is responsive. Attack animations are done well for the most parts and the hit effects and light trails from the weapon attacks look good without becoming overly flashy and distracting. There is a hookshot that either lets you drag small enemies towards you or teleport towards the target, which smooths out the friction of running towards enemies in a big arena and keeps the action moving. There is a cool weapon-swapping attack gives you i-frames and a weapon-specific attack, like a launcher, a dash attack or a counter, which encourages you to swap weapons mid-combo. All these things are cool and important for the hard to pin down "feel" of the game, and it's encouraging for a new studio to be able to nail down these intangibles in their first game.However, there are also a fair few problems with the game, both in the combat system and just in general. Starting with the non-combat issues, the story and music are pretty lackluster, which dampen the overall mood of the game. There is a weapon durability mechanic where you can unleash a super-attack when your weapon is about to break, which is cool in the heat of combat but leads to you having to keep on the lookout for crystal vein pickups which turn into weapons in between combat encounters to ensure that you don't run out of the weapons that you need. There is also a weird time advancing mechanic that will speed up the regeneration of crystal veins, which is basically an overly-complicated way of letting you mine more crystals. It's baffling that in a character action game with a time manipulation mechanic, that mechanic manifests itself in farming loot and not in slowing down time after a perfect dodge like you see in Bayonetta or Nier Automata.Now for my gripes with the combat mechanics, which hurt more for me to say. Firstly, although there are 6 weapons for you to collect in total, all of them are just different variations of swords. You basically have short swords and heavy swords, with some minor moveset differences between them. They don't really play very differently. On top of that, two of the weapons deal bonus damage against certain enemy types: the katana against biological monsters, and the claymore against robots, which are the only 2 types of enemies in the game. This leads to a situation when you play on hard difficulty where enemies become so bullet-spongy that it's not worth using anything else besides the katana and claymore. Furthermore, if you're at a boss that is robot type for example and you're stuck and need many attempts, you will eventually run out of claymores and need to backtrack through the level to farm more of them, which drags the pace of the game to a halt.Finally, we come to my biggest gripe with the game, which is an obvious padding of game length through scarce checkpoints. Basically, your level progress is only saved at checkpoints and you will be sent all the way back to the last checkpoint when you die. This wouldn't be too bad on its own, except that just before most bosses there is a random maze section. You have to go through a set of corridors and rooms arranged in a random configuration and fight groups of enemies before you even get into the boss arena. There is no checkpoint at the end of the maze just before the boss, so every time you die to the boss you get sent all the way back to the beginning and have to do the whole maze again. The maze is randomised each time so you can't memorise the quickest way to get to the boss, which means that essentially the maze becomes a randomised resource tax for your heals and weapons before every boss attempt. The game autosaves when you use your heals and when your weapons break so you can't even save scum to conserve your resources. There is no good reason to have this except to artificially pad out the playtime, and I hope that the developers don't repeat this again with their future games.Overall, even with all that criticism, I want to reiterate that I like the game overall and I want to see the developer improve with their next game. Fans of character action games know that a lot of bad game design elements can and will be forgiven as long as the combat itself feels good. Just look at Bayonetta with its many instakill QTEs, and the forced Space Harrier minigame section just before one of its most fun and challenging boss fights that you have to play over and over again every time you die to that boss. I will criticise those game elements to the day I die, but Bayonetta is still one of my favourite character action games. Likewise, Ultra Age is still a fun, compact game with stylish combat that you should give a proper chance to.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a decent hack and slash action game, This should keep you busy for a few hours. 5 hours in so far, not quite sure how deep in I am but it feels like around 75%?The general consensus some of us had while I was playing was that it seems like in general gameplay it plays like a slightly less polished Nier Replicant. I feel like as long as you know what you're getting into, you'll enjoy your time with this game.Performance. This game runs BEAUTIFULLY and supports high refresh rates.Nice combo systemPlenty of weaponsUpgrade paths for both character and weaponsSatisfying "Finisher" attacksMost boss fightsThe music. Some of it's nice but certainly wont end up on a playlistThe voice acting. English is fine, not as bad as many make it out to be.Weapon upgrade cost. Scales too high too fast.The story: It's just kind of there? Not too involvedLevel Design. Lots of wide empty areas and empty hallwaysMap. Rotating minimap and full maps make finding the right path annoying.Some boss fights. A couple were downright unfair.Stat upgrades: Pure RNG about whether you find a pickup that's better.Weapon Variety. Many share move sets and could have been consolidated into a fewer amount.The camera: It tries to be too clever with camera angles and makes fights harder than they need to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely on the fence on this one but leaning more on the negative side. Too many unfocused elements along with a bloated level design (looking at you desert area) that just feels wrong in a game that's clearly made with combat as the selling point. I really do applaud the effort as (so I've heard) this game was developed by a few students but it just feels more frustrating than fun at times. Maybe get it on discount but temper your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: SHADES OF TAN, THE GAME!Is it 2005 again?Ah yes, Ultra Age, the poor mans version of DMC.After playing the game, the best way I can describe this game is that it has the resource management aspects and checkpoint system of Dark Souls, with the combat and style of something like DMC5 or Nier Automata, and a progression system that takes cues from both styles of game while also being it's own thing. Which is to say that the game is very good!Ultra Age I still think is more of a rough gem for action game freaks and I absolutely loved it. I’m on my 3rd play though and it has gotten better each time through. The combat is fun and feels really well weighted. There is good sense of progression in the game in terms of unlocking new blades/ abilities and upgrading them that makes it really fun to play again and again. You never feel too weak or too overpowered.The combat is the bread and butter of this game.  It is not a very original system by any means and could probably use another mechanic or 2 but it is still fun and satisfying.  The game is so fluid in its combat and  like I said every move feels weighty and satisfying to pull off. It's honestly such a great experience and the last time I had this much fun with an action RPG was NieR Automata. Not only that but the performance on the Steam Deck is great.But it’s the voice acting that’s down right terrible. Somehow the main character sounds more robotic than his actual robot companion. It's actually down right embarrassing, but it's such a fun experience due to the solid gameplay. Honestly, the only thing is that you can never take the story (which handles some pretty intense themes) seriously because the voice actor seems like they used the bot from google translate to voice all of his lines. It's NakeyJakey bad voice acting level tier. Although I guess FF7 Remake had some of the worst conversation interactions of the modern era too and I survived that, so if you did as well I'm sure you’ll be able to handle Ultra Age.Despite having the worst voice acting l've ever heard in a modern video game, the gameplay is fun. It's just a mindless tear down of enemies. A good game to play when you just wanna kill stuff with a big sword. The game looks good and the fact it was made by 4 friends just sells it for me. I love buying and supporting these kind of passion projects.If you are a fan of action games then this is a hidden gem that should be added to your collection. It is nothing crazy special, but nevertheless it is a requisite purchase if some of your favorite games are Darksiders, Devil May Cry and Ninja Gaiden, just to name a few, and if you would consider anything that fits into the same league as those games in any way shape or form to be a must buy.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game sacrificed everything to make up for a great hack n slash game. Turned out the gameplay mechanics are rather dated. Enemy AI behavior can be weird. Basically, the entire game wants you to wield particular blades for enemies. For example, the katana is vulnerable for bio-organic/living things while the Claymore does massive chunk of damage to humanoids and robots. Although you are allowed to change between 4 blades, having to play with enemy vulnerabilities in mind limits creativity. This is especially during boss fights. Its a slug fest and takes forever to defeat bosses if you don't use certain blades. Also durability is tied to your blades which forces you to go out for a rage move every time your time your blade is on the point of breaking. Even air time isn't safe. Mashing the right trigger is what the game demands when you are horded by enemies. The creativity for combos is there but these restrictions put you to play without creativity. Furthermore, some robots aren't balanced and can be, at times, tougher than bosses.For a game which sacrificed visual fidelity, voice acting, poor animation, the only redeeming aspect was the gameplay. But alas! Gameplay felt sub-par. The developers have surely run out of ideas when they put the same 2 bossess at the latter part of the game. And what was the night and day cycle even for? Barren wasteland, empty forests as far as much eyes can stretch but once you venture, there is nothing there. Not even a power core cleverly stacked somewhere. Every thing is in plain sight. I gave this game an overall rating of 5/10 cuz I finished it. Played 5 mins of the DLC Project Rebirth but couldn't tolerate it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours straight in and the game STILL gets me invested to a degree. This is the kinda game that you would play as a kid and then become a part of your childhood games like GTA, Splinter Cell, Wolverine Origins etc. By all means I'm not saying the game is a masterpiece or anything, but this game's the kind of game that belongs in the old era of games when everyone created something original and was trying to see what works, all the while taking a close look at their peers and taking notes of what was done right.The story is engaging, and the way the game tells it just proves again the quality of linear styled games when done right. While the characters aren't really memorable, they're not dislikable. The only problem is the game doesn't really tell you much about who these people are. But the interaction between these characters do show that they're not one-dimensional, and the voice acting in this is very decent.The combat took what was done right from games like DMC 3/5, MGR, and made them more easier pick up, as in a lot more easier to get used to without losing much of what makes it feel good. For example combos are a lot more easier to remember and it takes only a bit of time to get used to them until you seamlessly transition between weapons; also weapon switching. Each weapon swap is an attack, a movement, and a block; the attack also differs depending on if you're in the air or on the ground.The level design is perfect for a linear game like this, there's never a moment where you feel lost but also never a moment where you feel underwhelmed or lose the feeling of exploration. It's ALMOST half as comparable to DMC 1's with how it takes you from place to place but still make the old levels accessible. Aesthetic-wise it looks gorgeous, the animations are really good for an indie game and the sound design is well-done. While the music is up to standard it does leave a little bit to be desired; nonetheless, it has it moments in where it matters like the boss fights (which are pretty good also) and ambiance.Overall, this tickles my monkey brain, me me like and happy.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game looking for a lightweight action title to tide me over until some other large releases came down the pipeline. Fortunately, that's exactly what this product is. This title clearly takes inspiration from some of the action combat genre's heavy hitters like the Bayonetta and Devil May Cry franchises, and while it adds some unique elements, its rough edges are noticeable enough that it tarnishes the experience.The game performs well, with no crashes or major bugs to speak of. There are some frame drops in certain areas, which may also be an intentional, dramatic slowdown by the developers, but they never got in the way of the combat. Surprisingly, the combat felt good. Weapons have weight behind them, and the game gives you several options when it comes to combo routes. Furthermore, there are mechanics that are inspired by other games, like the grappling hook, which emulates the warp function from Final Fantasy XV. Because of this, there is a lot of player freedom, but that's about where the positives end.There are some design choices that feel a little undercooked. The enemies look and feel like asset rips from the Unity store, in the sense that they don't feel unique, and much of the animation work and fight design make the enemies tedious to challenge. Health bars are often very large, and even when I had maxed out every single option on the skill tree, fights still felt like they dragged on well past their welcome. Half the time, if you take damage, it's because an attack is poorly telegraphed, or because the hitbox lasts too long, or because an enemy hit you from off screen and there was no way you could react. Some enemies just baffle me; their entire kit is unfun to play against, and I wonder how some of them made it in to the final game. Despite these problems though, the developers give you a broken tool in claymore weapons, which have a defensive counter ability which makes you completely invincible from all sides. The window for this counter is extremely long, and completely trivialises most fights if you have a general inkling of when enemies may attack. You can also equip two of these claymores, so while a weapon durability mechanic does exist, the game never punishes you for using the most broken weapons in the game. Not that this durability mechanic is anything to write home about regardless, because both this and the 'time passing' mechanic don't impact the game in any meaningful way. Couple this with a camera that often is too close to the player, and you've got a recipe for a lazy way to finish the game. I feel like this game could have been more unique. With enemies and locales that felt generic, an extremely generic player character model, and no distinct types of weapons or mechanics, at times Ultra Age feels like a combination of assets that the developers twisted into a functional product. Sure, the combat is good, but I'd really only recommend this title if you've played all the other big hitters and are just looking for something to tide you over until something bigger and more polished comes along.

_childDocuments_.review: A MUST HAVE for any action game fan.In short: -the gameplay is the star of the show here, it's the reason to buy the game. It is a very well done mix of Devilmaycry and Nier, with simple combos for all the swords that can be used in different situations (aoe, focus attack, leaps etc). Also all the swords are good against certain enemy types and have a switch attack (for instance the greatsword has a block mechanic for it's switch attack) that makes it so you always want to use everything in your arsenal. The enemies are pretty brutal at times and you must use your dodge/block and your attacks to keep on the pressure, or you can get killed very fast when surrounded, even on normal difficulty. You also have a pseudo-graplinghook that adds a lot of mobility in fights.-honestly it's pointless to go over anything else the game offers since every other aspect (sound, exploration, story, graphics, lvl up mechanics) are all just...decent, nothing to write home about. But I really think the gameplay carries the game on it's back.-one other note is that even tho you can't rebind keys, the default setup is actually really good for mouse&keyboard; it's rare to find a game where I don't want to tweak any keybindings.-I've also found no bugs of any nature in my time with it and the game runs really smooth.Highly recommended for some good old DMC fun, aka comboing enemies to death. Hope to see more from these devs, they did really well IMO with this game, especially for the price. So many garbage games out there for 30 40 bucks and this one (on sale right now for 12 euro!!??) just offers SO much enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultra Age is a action game that unfortunately falls short in several areas. _childDocuments_.review: I beat Ultra Age on Hard mode. On an indie level this game is decent at best, but it is not great by any means of a character action game. Nonetheless, I appreciate the effort and hope to see these devs try hard to refine their craft more, create more games of this type, and do better in aspects I believe that Ultra Age did not do so good at. Details will be farther below with what I think they could do instead in the particular aspects. In short this game is a painfully mid Nier Automata + MGRR combination that has ideas and questionable design decisions alongside a lackluster story and soundtrack that make the experience fall flat compared to what it is attempting to be.Details as to what I think sucks about Ultra Age and how to change them:-There is no system that provides an incentive for the player to use multiple weapons and to be stylish in combat. Instead, make me have to use all of my weapons so I get bonus currency or specifics unlocks for long-term good performance in combat encounters. -The damage types system pushes the player not to experiment with any possible depth to the combat. Instead this leads to players wanting to spam only 1 weapon that does the best damage to the enemy type they are fighting, the only two types being robotic or organic enemies. It is because of this damage type system that only 2 weapons in the game (the Claymore, and the Katana) are worth upgrading while the others (the Steel Blade, Lightning Blade, Gunblade, and Charge Claymore) suck in comparison because they do not deal full damage or are as effective at killing your enemies as the best two weapons are. Get rid of the damage types, get rid of the irrelevant environmental battling from the Charge Claymore, and make all weapons do full damage to enemies and each weapon is just a different moveset with its own benefits that all perform well in combat so that the player will want to use and experiment with each weapon in the game at some point aside from the ones that fit their particular playstyle.-The modules system and Power Gears is a neat idea that is held back by the irregularity at which the module types are dropped from enemies, not being able to equip more than one module of each singular type, and different gear upgrades just being plain better than others (Critical and Blade Modules outperform the Boosters and Wire by a landslide after the first level). There is no customization with the modules, it is only a system that "upgrades" the player by checking off boxes rather than being something to customize your character's effectiveness in combat as you see fit if there were any flexibility in the effectiveness of combat to begin with. Get rid of the lack of customization in the modules system, and instead of Power Gears just allow the player to upgrade by spending crystals and any other basic currency from combat to upgrade their character.-Time Shift and numbered weapon uses, useless mechanics that do nothing but attempt to trick the player to make more mistakes and waste time in a terrible way. Instead of these gameplay methods, I recommend that Time Shift instead becomes an ability that allows the player to switch the level they are in to either day or night in order to fight optional bosses and find upgrades or collectibles that they would not be able to find without using this ability, and also this could be neat as it would allow the devs to make each single level be as if you are playing 2 levels in one. Get rid of the weapon uses and instead provide a meter that fills up as you use each of the weapon to then overcharge the weapon like you do with a break attack, this will allow that system to exist without having to make the player be punished with not possibly being able to use a weapon mid-combat because of something having too much health or the weapon they needed didn't drop another use in multiple previous combat encounters.-A lot of the levels have big open hallways and spaces that exist for no reason, and the train level in particular has a questionable design decision to move the train to get to a stairway that was clearly accessible by just jumping down from the railing above it the entire time. Make each level have true obstacles in the level that aren't just keycards, and make each level a hallway that has the player making use of your jumping, dashing, and wire system to acquire collectibles or find secrets to then go to open combat rooms with maybe some neat environmental objects or interactable things in them that allow the player and enemies to use their surroundings to their own advantages.-The story had me rolling my eyes and uninterested the entire time as Age, Helvis, Medea, Deucalion, and Atlas were nowhere near interesting of characters to make a good gateway to the attempts of depth to the setting that is as bare bones as can be, the humor is dry and boring, and any lore is just non-existent or dumped on you in dialogue out of nowhere. Make the basics of the story as good as possible, make the lore optional to the player, make your characters have a presence to the player even when they aren't on screen, make your protagonist, their allies, and enemies more captivating and likeable through giving them each a unique style of some sort and allowing them to shine in different, and exciting ways.-The roguelike delving idea is pretty neat but this needs some work, we need more level and room variations in it. More enemies and mixing of them to vary it up. More modifiers on the enemies and give some to the player to make things interesting for them as well. Optional bosses, collectibles, or bonuses of some sort that can in these.-Don't re-use bosses if you aren't going to give them new attacks, new movesets, or anything at all different about them. Also, make the arenas for bosses just as epic and interesting as the bosses themselves.-The soundtrack needs a lot more excitement in it to fit with the high-speed, tons of action mood that combat is meant to have. Use more rock and metal style instrumentals to kick things up a notch in combat, and make your non-combat tracks as grand as possible depending on the mood of the situation more often.I do not believe I am truly unfair with what I have stated here. I only pose these with the intent that improvement can be done. With these changes that I believe the devs are quite capable of doing, they'd have an action-indie gold mine to release to players that love action games, and character action games like myself and many others.
