_childDocuments_.review: They say imitation is the highest form of flattery, and while the character action game genre in general were an inspiration for Ultra Age, the similarities to Nier Automata border on plagiarism. To be fair though, it is one of my favorite game of all time, so not the worst game to copy homework from.It's an indie creation from the land of worse sushi called kimbab and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ kpop culture, despite being indie the presentation is surprisingly decent. Visuals are a big potential draw, but somehow the game remained very niche at the time of writing this review. The optimization, particle effects and animations are surprisingly top notch, what is pretty apparent however is the unimaginative environment design, I'm not even talking about drawing similarities from environments and camera shifts of automata, more so how dull a lot of the corridors and arenas are (especially in the bloody palace mode HOLY F***), the more you look around the more the cracks start to show, the feeling that it's a rushjob of copy pasted assets and clutter, plastered around a unity map, never quite goes away. The enemy visual design is not too exciting, the robots share very similar visuals, and biological enemies are a few repeated crystal animals, then some variants are just recolors. All in all, it's a very competent looking game at first glance, with low budget starting to show only once you start playing it.However we all know the visuals are not the most important, and gameplay wise it's a decent game, they have neat mechanics of their own, and some borrowed from the genre classics. Different timed combos, several weapon types, light air juggling, invincibility dodge, enhanced combos through leveling, enemy weaknesses to certain weapon types, Nero grapple, "devil trigger", and most uniquely weapon durability, with special attacks when you break them. There is not a style meter to keep you switching the weapons around, but both enemy weakness and durability heavily incentivize it regardless. You'd think that with the weapon amount there is going to be huge overlap in weakness exploiting, when enemy types are only 2 - biological and mechanical, but some weapons have special effects of their own that are handy to keep around, most notably gun sword to apply bleed, and lightning sword to apply shock. I'd say the enemy encounters are somewhat hit or miss, at times it feels like there is not enough time to ever do a combo without getting hit, so you might resort to safe attacks like parry-riposte, or invincibility triggering weapon breaks, at times there is also too many projectiles around, and unlike Automata - your little pod (yes, I'm not joking, you get a pod in this game too) cannot shoot these projectiles down.There are also some weirder mechanics, like a time of day skip, changing the day-night cycle, as well as refreshing enemies and loot pickups (those are of course the weapons and healing charges), or upgrades so dumb they feel borderline useless - like the looting with your grapple, when you still need to be somewhat close to loot anyway, so that's several upgrade points wasted, for a potential 1-2 seconds save sometimes, said upgrade also doesn't work on loot crates that contain "modules", which are just randomize stat upgrades.Story is surprisingly, not a 1 to 1 copy of automata, though it does borrow a bit from it, I didn't pay a lot of attention to it as writing was extremely unengaging, I recall the main character being a clone that wants a power of immortaility, which is probably gathered through unethical means, and you discover some ruins of ancient civilization with rogue AI around, as well as those crystal corruptions spread around the place. Your pod is also a mcguffin of some sort, I'd guess it makes immortality gathering process more efficient and even more unethical and genocidal, there is like 3-4 characters in the whole game, so it's not like there is much to work with.Lastly the audio, combat audio is nice, some action sequence music is decent rock stuff, volume mixing is not AS f***ed as I'd expect from a small indie project, that said, I do wish some attacks would have better audio tells before you get hit, some of them feel unsynced, some get drowned out etc., and with how many enemies they like to throw in the arena, surrounding you from all sides at times, it makes it a rough time, with how much camera turning you need to do, it might unironically be one of the few char action games that are easier to play on KB+M instead of a pad.Overall, it's a decent 6 hour action game, I didn't like it as much as Assault Spy, but I don't regret buying and playing it, you can probably pick it up at decent sales too. And there is a free dlc included now, that's just a bloody palace with some rogue-lite elements, it's a tad unbalanced, and feels like some HP upgrades have been cut from the mode, but it's not "unbeatable" or anything, just takes a tad to practice. Still, don't let the runtime fool you, I had the game running idle, I'd say I've played main game for like 6 hours and bloody palace for probably 10-12, so if you don't vibe with second mode, you get 1/3rd of total potential playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game in all honesty.To get the story out of the way first..... well, it could be better but it's mostly passable. It has some standard anime tropes and bits you can see coming from a mile away.I played the game with Japanese voice acting and that was fine! There is a few minor moments where the voice acting doesn't quite deliver but i'd say it's a 99% positive experience. Good job on the Japanese voice actors!But what we really play these games for is the combat and I can say that the combat although a little bit basic is really really solid. It feels smooth, responsive, swapping between weapons is easy and has that same smooth feeling. If I had to give it 1 gripe is that it doesn't reward you enough to swap weapons around. Match the weapon with what the enemy is weak to and you basically have the winning combo.An example of this is the claymore vs the katana, the katana is strong vs biological enemies but weak vs mechanical, this makes it so the katana basically does like 10% of the dmg the claymore would do vs the mechanical enemies. So you just spam the same attack with the claymore to win easily. And this is another small issue, or big depending how you look at it, the movesets across all weapons are basically the same. Atk > heavy, Atk atk > heavy, etc etc. So it makes every weapon feel a bit samey. But because the combat feel so smooth and responsive this isn't too much of an issue but your mileage may vary.This issue of the weapon damage penalty is resolved in the free roguelite mode DLC a bit cause the extreme penalty is removed. You just get 100% of base dmg and a strong weapon get's the damage bonus (Example: Katana does 100 dmg vs a mechanical enemy but the claymore does 130, in the story mode this was more like the katana does 10 dmg the claymore does 200). This makes it so it isn't a heavy punishment to swap weapons around and it feels good putting your blades on almost breaking and just swapping between them dishing out multiple break blade attacks which do a lot of damage.But generally the combat just feels really really good. Could I recommend it for $21? No. The story is way too short for that at only ~5 hours including watching all cutscenes and the roguelite mode can be cleared in about another 3-5 hours and doesn't really require any of that typical roguelite grinding. But on a sale? Most definitely! If this dev team had some more budget and maybe time for an ultra age 2 or another game, adding more weapons, a broader moveset they would have an absolute winner on their hands. As it sits right now if I had to give the game a grade I would say a solid 7/10 leaning towards a 7.5 simply because the combat system feels so smooth and responsive.

_childDocuments_.review: I played an indie spectacle fighter, Assault Spy, and really enjoyed it. Ever since then, I've tried various indie games that LOOK like spectacle fighters, hoping that I'll find the same enjoyment. Unfortunately, most of those games play more like God of War 3 (or worse), and I end up disappointed.Enter Ultra Age. It LOOKS like it should play like Devil May Cry. You can switch between 4 weapons on the fly, you can cancel your attacks to do combos, it looks really cool, etc… However, because of fundamental design flaws, it doesn't play like Devil May Cry at all. Let's take for example combos. In Ultra Age, you can do various pre-determined combos (e.g. light attack + heavy attack will do one combo, light attack + light attack + heavy attack will do a different combo, etc…). However, you're not incentivized to do any combos that take too long since the enemy will start attacking you before you can complete it. Furthermore, you can straight up do more damage by doing 2 small combos (i.e. light attack + heavy attack) instead of doing 1 long combo (e.g. light attack + light attack + light attack + heavy attack). This means that instead of playing the game by trying out various different combos as you progress through the game, you quickly learn the optimal combos for each weapon:	• Katana: Heavy attack + change blade attack, heavy attack + change blade attack, repeat…	• Claymore: Light attack + heavy attack, light attack + heavy attack, repeat…	• Lightning Blade:  Light attack + heavy attack + heavy attack, light attack + heavy attack + heavy attack, repeat…Doing the same combos over and over again isn't fun. While you can choose to try other attacks, there's little incentive and you're going to quickly get bored since despite the game having 6 different weapons, they fundamentally play the exact same as each other (hell, two of them are basically copies with one being the "Claymore" and another being the "Charge Claymore"). They're all swords, and a lot of their attacks do the exact same thing (e.g. Light attack + light attack + light attack + heavy attack is the same for all of the weapons). So there's no incentive to create crazy combos, combining different weapons since the weapons are so similar to each other. Instead of creating crazy combos, the game allows you to press one button to do a cool looking attack that does a lot of damage AND you're invincible for the entire attack animation. This is balanced by the fact that you can only do this when the durability of your weapons gets low (weapons can break in this game, but it's not a big deal since you can equip like 15 of each weapon). However, while this LOOKS cool, it doesn't provide any sense of achievement since all you did is press a button to use the attack.Even if you felt like trying to use different weapons in your combos, the game discourages you from doing so. This is because different weapons are effective against different types of enemies. The Katana is effective against biological enemies whereas the claymore and lightning blade are effective against mechanical enemies. When I say "effective" I mean doing like…… 75% more damage than a weapon that is "ineffective". This means that you will always be using the same weapons over and over again.It also doesn't help that there's very limited enemy variety, and that you'll be facing the same enemies over and over again. There are like 2 biological enemies (a bird and a jaguar) and like 4 mechanical enemies (a robot, a ranged robot, a flying ranged robot, and a "heavy" robot). In regards to your defensive options, while the game is competent, it's nothing special. You have a dodge and a parry (in the form of the change blade attack on your claymore). It's pretty easy to both dodge and parry enemy attacks (both have pretty generous windows). You also have an energy bar that fills up as you defeat enemies. You can use 25% of your energy to basically recover 25% of your health. So you're typically not that afraid of dying.One good thing about the game are the bosses. They look really cool and are pretty decent to fight. I just wish they were more challenging, since I beat most bosses on the first try. At max it took me like 3 tries to beat a boss.The progression system is very…..strange. You have a classic skill tree where you can get passive benefits such as increased damage, new moves, etc… However, there's also a "module" system in that you can equip up to 6 modules to get various stat benefits (i.e. higher health, damage, critical rate, critical damage, armor, and a "master" module that increases all stats). What's weird about this system is that it's very restrictive, in that you can't equip more than 1 "type" of module at the same time (i.e. you can't have 2 damage modules, only one). What this means is that after getting a good type of the module (e.g. a rare damage module), you'll never be excited to find another damage module again. For like 90% of the modules that dropped from enemies or that I encountered out in the wild, I never cared about them since my current modules were better.There's a story, but it's pretty barebones. There's absolutely no world/lore building done and you're simply thrown into the world with little to no explanation. There's the main characters, Age and Helvis, who are apparently really good friends. There's Medea, who's apparently supposed to be some badass that you should be scared of. There's Deucalion, who's some super smart leader or something. But just because the game SAYS these things, doesn't mean I accept it/understand the significance of it. For example, in like the tutorial level Helvis "dies" and Age is really upset about this and swears revenge. Welp, just because the character is really upset by it doesn't mean the audience is since I only spent like 20 minutes with Helvis so who cares if he "died". ♥♥♥♥ like that happens a lot where something happens and the characters seem to care a lot, but I simply didn't since the game does a very poor job of making me invested in the world.Overall, Ultra Age was pretty repetitive. While the game looks great, the fundamental gameplay is pretty flawed.

_childDocuments_.review: t's the year 3XXX, and humanity isn't doing too good. The planet that appears to be Earth is inhabited by robots, mutated animals and colour-coded crystals. The remaining humanity seems to exist as part of [ORBIT], while the last people on Earth were part of [FRONTIER]. The story is pretty cryptic, and the game could've used a Codex. You play as Age, a member of [ORBIT]'s Exploration Division, tasked with recovering a piece of technology referred to as [FRONTIER] relic. Along with your companion AI, Helvis you collect the relic, which makes you a target of the [ORBIT] Combat Division. What ensues is a journey for Age and Helvis to find a ship and get back to [ORBIT], killing loads of things in the process The game is mostly linear hack and slash action-adventure. The game's main mechanic revolves around Age's nano-blade, which can take different forms, based on the kinds of crystals he picks up. Different blades are effective against different enemy types, and each blade has a durability limit. Once the weapon gets close to breaking, you have the option to shatter it, dealing increased damage, before re-fashioning the blade (as long as you have enough crystals to do so). Each blade has its own skill tree, but I found that towards the end of the game I had excessive currency to upgrade everything I wanted—although the game features the “enemies respawn whenever you do” mechanic, there's no penalty on death and no corpse runs, so currency stacks infinitely. Each weapon has same basic combos from chaining light and heavy attacks, with additional effects being available via the skill tree. One weapon does bonus damage to animals, and another to robots, so you'll constantly have those 2 in your 4 weapon slots, most likely. There's 2 basic enemy types- animals and robots. Robots have different attack patterns, but they tended to blend together. There's no parrying so dash-dodge is critical. In some areas, it's possible to get caught in a corner, where the camera goes haywire, and a few enemies finish you off “off-screen”. However, I didn't find this particularly annoying, and that's something that can happen in any 3rd person hack'n'slash. Oh, there's also a grappling hook, so you can pull weak enemies towards yourself, or propel yourself towards the bigger foes. The game's highlight are the bosses. There's a fair amount of variety here (although a few get reused at one point). Still, considering the game only has 4 main levels (plus intro and final boss arena), I was pleasantly surprised. Getting to credits took about 11 hours- and there's a roguelike tower maze DLC that lets you fight different enemy combos, which I haven't tried. The game's levels are linear, but occasionally you have to go into randomly generated mazes to fight in a bunch of arenas until you find a miniboss that drops a key item so you can move on with the main game. Overall, a fairly simple game, with some memorable boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: As a side note before the review, I played the demo for hours and hours maxing out the starting weapons. It was that fun.As a fan of DMC, MGR, Nier, and Bayonetta, this is a very fun one to add to that list. It combines elements of these games into a steaming hot pot of action. Nero's grapple arm from DMCV comes with the added function of being able to pull yourself to enemies on command. The dodge mechanic is very similar to Nier Automata. - Pros -Combat is fluid and rewarding. Attacks are flashy and appealing to the eye. I even found an odd technique where I switch weapons and dodge at the same time, letting me switch while dodging instead of using the weapons switch attack.The wire move is great for pulling enemies and for getting pulled TO them. Great ability for keeping the flow of combat fast.The Katana and Gunblade are my favorite weapons.Enemies doing a red blink when attacking is a nice help in the middle of all the flashy moves.- Cons -The story is a little lacking, but it sets the tone and gives context to the fighting.Weapon variety is a little odd, two weapons share core movesets of others which is a little disappointing. You also pretty much don't use the Katana for the last half of the game which is a shame, I like it's moveset. My favorite so far is the Gunblade, very fun weapon. Weapon durability is kind of a non-issue, so I don't see a reason for it.One ability that makes me scratch my head is the time travel mechanic which fast forwards time by 12 hours. I literally never used it. It does have some cool features on one level where certain times of the day spawned different enemies. Perhaps this ability could have been used to slow down time in combat.The ability that grabs crystals in area also seems like an afterthought created to make more uses for the crystals, it doesn't even grab the weapon crystals and power gear upgrades at max level. Not sure what do do about this feature.Some bosses and enemies should have "launchable" states after a certain point, it just makes the combat feel weak when fighting certain foes that never stagger and being limited in what moves you can do. ESPECIALLY humanoid ones. It's not always clear who you can launch into the air for more combos. Keep unlaunchable foes to only bigger enemies like DMC. Even Vergil can be launched in that series.Also enemies are just relentless sometimes, I'm so used to DMCV when enemies who are off screen don't attack.- Conclusion -Overall, this is a solid game for the price it is. I know I gave a lot of cons but thats because I know this game has potential.One feature that would help replay value is an update containing some sort of arena where enemies spawn wave after wave until you die. ( And a new game plus please )[]Other than that, I would welcome DLC or a Sequel in the future for this game improving on this core gameplay and not changing too much. You guys have a solid foundation and I would hate to see it step in the wrong direction.

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran of the hack-and-slash genre, I saw this game on Steam, saw the generally positive reviews, and thought to myself, "yea this might be pretty good." So I downloaded it, and after having my computer crash because every game on my PC defaults to the highest settings, here's my consensus:If you're just getting into the hack-and-slash scene, this might be one of the best games to start with. It doesn't do anything necessarily groundbreaking (obviously, I don't expect much from (what I've heard is) an indie project made by a small team), but it does all of these existing concepts well. It does introduce some relatively "new" gameplay mechanics, like having different weapons serve different purposes. For example, the katana is best used against beasts and animals, the claymore is best used against robotics, and the lightning blade is very effective against robotic shields. It also incorporates the skill tree, a mechanic seen in every ARPG ever made, but I have no complaints, there's really nothing it does  wrong. If you do want some games to directly compare this to, I'd say it shares the combat of , and the UI and upgrade mechanics of , although loosely.I do, however, have a small amount of complaints. My biggest issue is how the lock-on won't automatically swap to another enemy upon killing the enemy I was already locked onto. It can be detrimental to have to press R3 during a fight to lock onto another enemy, especially if there are a lot of enemies in a single area. Another small nitpick is how the time mechanic the game has seems to be a small gimmick that you rarely have a reason to use, so it kind of feels like a waste of code. Another is how the the story doesn't feel very well-presented during cutscenes and dialogue, but I don't play most hack-and-slashes for groundbreaking storytelling, I'll leave that to the  series.Overall, I do recommend this game. Again, if you're looking for a game to get the feel of what the hack-and-slash genre entails, but also don't want to play a AAA title like the ones mentioned, this is a good place to start. For people, like me, who play action games for a living, this won't be a "new" experience for us, but it's still guaranteed to give you a good time. I'd recommend picking it up during a sale, I got it for $15 during the Steam Summer Sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fun, fun. Double jump, grappling hook to either jump towards big enemies or pull small ones to you (both of which are upgradeable), upgradeble weapons that are weak or strong against enemy types, upgradeable attacks, flashy finishers, engaging boss fights. The mechanics aren't anything you haven't seen before but there's lots of variety. In the very beginning the enemy types seemed samey but every time I started to get bored with the enemies the game introduces new ones.Very reasonable price. Japanese voice acting is very good. The game is very conscientious of your time. Cutscenes are skippable, approaching a save point saves the game without having to do it manually, you are given shortcuts to loop back etc. Aside from having to long press to interact with certain things it implements basically all quality of life features other games sometimes lack. No nuisances, no tutorial hell, pick it up and play.Characterization for Eiji and his companion robot was achieved through a couple funny lines early on so I felt connected with him from the get go. The shadows make the graphics a bit muddy at some points. Wish there were more secrets but at least there are upgrade parts in not so obvious places. With a bigger dev team this would have been an instant hit. A total hidden gem considering I had never heard of this game before.

However it wasn't the best game as you would expect.During the playtime of this, I was first amused by all the great content and good core fundamental of being an action game, having really compact and smooth fighting system. Despite that, I almost wanted to quit mid-game due to its extremely sky-high difficulties. Which often you will found yourself without healing or beaten to death countless time. Unless you know how spam parry with Claymore, you got no chance beating Altas and Deucalion ( The last two bosses in the game ).Ultra Age will often feels like a game puzzled with many different mechanics, simply to test it out for a better  sequel. Like procedural generations, Break Sword, Rope, or perspective changing in battle. There are no clear instruction or waypoints to guide your journey, nor it will try to tell you to get all Power Core before getting to the next map. ( you will miss the achievement and most of the upgrades if you don't )However when I finally beat the game and get the ending song, I strangely felt the 8 hours of me playing this game is finally worth something. I BEAT THE FXXKING GAME! This game is really rewarding for £15. However if you hates souls like game or hard difficulties, please avoid it and buy something else. ( I REALLY MEAN IT )

_childDocuments_.review: This game clearly takes inspiration from Nier Automata, and on my book this is a great pro, but you can see some sprinkles of Devil May Cry and Phantasy Star Universe, at least on the weapon design.Good and fast paced hack 'n slash combat, satisfying combos, above average voice acting and all of that made by such a small team makes this game one of my favorite here on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultra Age

_childDocuments_.review: While it's a relatively short game (I beat it in about 6.5h with all achievements which are fairly easy to get in a single playthrough), it's actually decent. There are maybe some minor balancing issues (IMO the final boss dragged on for too long). I'm not a fan of boss re-fights, but there were actually only 2 so it wasn't too long (and it was a good way to grind some crystals). The writing wasn't bad or anything, but I wish Age was less whiny. Maybe it was the voice acting. It's a bit hard to hype yourself for a game if the main character himself doesn't want to be there.The graphics are decent. Music is alright, but at some places (like the desert) I think more could have been done to nail the atmosphere. The story isn't anything special, but it's not supposed to be. I was just a bit confused at the end

You get to upgrade each of the weapons individually and also you get to upgrade yourself as well.I'm playing it on hard difficulty which if you're not careful you can get killed pretty fast. _childDocuments_.review: Ultra age is an enjoyable 3rd person action game, developed by a small Korean studio.However, there are a few flaws, which prevent me from wholeheartedly recommending it. Most notably, that there are . I think it's fair to say, that they should be added, even though the standard button configuration is acceptable, even on a mouse and keyboard, which this game supports. Otherwise the PC port is OK and runs decently well.Now onto what I thought were flaws with the game's design:Firstly, I think some of the lite RPG elements actually work against the game and limit combo potential. Certain enemies are vulnerable to specific weapons, which means that if you switch to the incorrect weapon, you will severely hamper yourself. As such, I didn't really switch weapons during combat encounters.Second, you can't really do air juggling, which might be a design choice, but I do think it's disappointing. The reason I say this, it's because if you use your wire ability while in the air on an airborne enemy, you can actually reset your enemy's position, preventing it from falling. But, you can't reset your attack chain. So once you attacked 2-3 times in the air, you are going down. The areas you visit are also just...empty. You do a lot of running back and forth, often hitting dead ends, that sometimes don't even reward you with anything.Finally, there is no replayability. You beat the game, and that's it. The developers have, however promised a DLC, which will expand on the game. They said it should be releasing sometime in the summer of this year (2022, in case you are reading this far in the future).None of this means that the game is bad. On the contrary. Very nice and fluid animations, satisfying enemy hit reactions, and a combat system that is fun and responsive. Great variety of bosses too!It's a commendable effort for a new studio, and I am happy to support them, because I think there is potential here for greatness.For 20 EUR you could do a lot worse!
_childDocuments_.name: Ultra Age

_childDocuments_.review:
Change Your Blade, Change Your Destiny. Ultra Age is a high-speed, sword-swinging action game set in the far future that follows the story of young warrior Age, who embarks on a mission to save humankind from extinction. Use your blades to cut through robotic and mutant foes, explore futuristic locales, and unravel a vast conspiracy concerning the fate of the planet. Far in the future, the resources of Earth have become insufficient, its ecosystem long ago changed irrevocably by a passing meteor. Humankind has divided into two: the people who have escaped Earth and relocated to the space colony, 'Orbital Arc,' and the others who have remained on Earth in a facility called ‘The Shelter.’

Humanity vanished from Earth after civilians from The Shelter failed an experiment that was meant to be the last hope for humanity, while people from Orbital Arc sent expeditions to Earth in search of resources. Failing to find any signs of life, a young sword-wielding warrior named ‘Age’ falls down from orbit to Earth. Accompanied by his floating android, Helvis, he must find the indispensable key to the survival of humankind.

-Unleash Combos with Blade-Changing Action-
Slash through foes with a variety of blades in high-speed, stylish action! Change blades on the fly with powerful moves to create linkage and run devastating combos. Different attributes and varied actions call for unique strategy against different types of foes.

-Narrow Gaps Using the Wire-
Launch the wire skill to pull smaller enemies toward you, or Quantum Warp to get instant access to larger foes! Use the wire to strategically overcome numerical inferiority, traverse gaps on land and quickly grab items.

-Get the Edge with Skills-
Gather elements to enhance your blades, expand your skills, and learn new combos. Install modules and power gear to level up Age and increase your arsenal of blades to take down the toughest of enemies. Use Helvis to burst into Critical Rage, cast Healing Pocket to recover, or Time Shift to loot more items.

-Experience a Post-Apocalyptic Earth-
Follow Age on his journey in the year 3174. Experience cutscenes that tell the story of Age’s mission across futuristic mecha, forests and deserts developed with Unreal Engine. Encounter mysterious characters and overcome menacing bosses to uncover the story behind the fate of humankind.

name: Kayak VR: Mirage
detailed_description: Feedback, ideas or issues? Let us know through our Discord! About the Game Kayak VR: Mirage is a jaw-dropping and exhilarating journey through beautiful and unique locations, tailor-made for Virtual Reality. Maneuver our fully physically accurate kayak around checkpoints and crown yourself the fastest, or take it easy and use the free roam mode for a leisurely trip and enjoy the scenery. Features Realtime multiplayer for two players. (NEW!) Beautiful and varied locations to explore or race through, featuring multiple times of day and weather conditions. Cutting-edge graphics that push the limits of what VR is capable of. Fully physics-based kayaking for an authentic experience that really makes you feel like you're on the water. Free roam mode for a more serene experience through the levels. Sit back and relax in our controller-free tour mode where the kayak moves for you. A variety of sea and wildlife that brings every environment to life. Time attack with a checkpoint course on all levels for racing fanatics who want a real workout. Play asynchronously against other players on the global leaderboards or your friends. Customize your kayak, paddle and headwear with a wide range of unlockable options. Optionally transform your controllers into a paddle by attaching them to a stick or mount and take the immersion to the next level. Comfort settings that make sure people without sea legs can enjoy it all the same. A music selection that always fits with the environment and mode you're playing in. Optimized to run well across a range of PC's, enabling a high-fidelity experience on high-end rigs while maintaining good performance on lower-end rigs. Support for FidelityFX. Support for DLSS (compatible with NVIDIA RTX Cards only).

_childDocuments_.review: This has been on my wish-list for ages so it was an immediate purchase on release.One of the reasons it was on my wish-list is that I look after a girl who has Cerebral Palsy and who's movement is extremely limited (wheelchair bound, limited use of arms). She also has learning difficulties and is non-verbal and has no concept of language whatsoever.She loves the sea so I thought this may appeal to her and give her an experience it would otherwise be impossible for her to have.She was totally mesmerized and spellbound by the water and on seeing penguins and an Orca as she floated in her own little world with a huge smile on her face. I got an almighty growl when I took off the VR headset. I think visiting the worlds in this game has (already) become a thing now. :-)Thanks to the developers, you have allowed her to get away from her disabilities and see the world in a brand new way that otherwise would have been denied her.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: My First Time Kayaking in 10 Years! IT WAS AWESOME.*See my updated video review after 40 hours of play! *Spoiler Alert* It's STILL AWESOME!So, this is an incredible and very convincing kayak simulator with great graphics and realistic physics. It runs flawlessly @ nearly max settings on my i7/RXT 3070 system.  If you like kayaking, get it! Due to a spinal cord injury I can't kayak in real life anymore, but I can do this in safety and comfort. For accessibility, the Devs have stated that they plan to implement a sort of "touring mode" that would allow people who can't paddle to experience the environments too. This is great! However, I'd like to suggest also adding  XBox controller support as well. For those who may not be aware, there are adaptive xbox controllers that allow people with physical disabilities to play games. There are many people with disabilities, like me,  who love VR because it gives them the chance to do and experience things that they can't do in real life.   Simply adding xbox controller support to the game would make it much more accessible to all kinds of people with all kinds of disabilities!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a godsend for me & I love love this game!!!! Due to health issues I can't kayak anymore & had to sell my Seda Glider (19 1/2') kayak. Arcade mode's physics has very much the same movement as my Glider with wing paddles. In speed & acceleration. My right stroke is stronger so I would veer right without a rudder & the game does the same thing!!!! Once again I really really LOVE this game. In simulation mode the physics are like a flat bottom river kayak. Slow & quick turning. But I was a sea kayaker so arcade mode is a dream for me. The only thing I would like the devs to add would be a Rudder mode. Maybe have a simple on & off mode so you can hammer when going at speed & turn it off when turning is needed. For me that would awesome. I have been fortunate enough to kayak in Draco Bay Costa Rica & in the north between Vancouver Island & the mainland & in this game both Cosat Rica & Norway have the same feeling. Once again I REALLY REALLY LOVE this game!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Kayak VR is by far one of the best kayak games I've ever played. The graphics are beautiful and I love the ability to choose between racing, free roaming, and touring modes. The controls also mimic kayaking better than any other game I've played, although the overall realism puts it in that uncanny valley-like space where it feels so close to real that I get frustrated by small stuff I would otherwise overlook. The comments below are from the perspective of an experienced kayaker (ocean and whitewater), and should be taken as constructive criticism and are in no way meant to detract from an amazing game or steer people away from it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not "just a tech demo" as some reviews state - it's Kayaking. If you want guns or something more "exciting" go to Phantom: Covert Ops instead. Kayak VR: Mirage to me is more of a relaxing, exploratory experience. I love each map and there are little paths you can find and unlockables if you look close enough. Each location also has a day/night version with unique random encounters that can happen. I use Kayak VR as an active meditation session where I can just zone out from the world but also do something a little physically active. The sounds, music, and of course the visuals all really add to this title. You can tell a lot of work was put into this and it really shows. I look forward to even more locations!

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my review after 4 hours of play: tl;dr game is very  good!If you have a VR headset and a decent PC then you should definitely buy this game, even in this fairly limited release incarnation it is still very much worth the asking price. - : it's a game about Kayaking, you spend ALL of the time on the surface of the water, so the water is very important... fortunately the developers clearly realised this and must have put an extreme amount of effort into the water simulation. It looks, and reacts just like real water! The water physics, caustics, waves, transparency etc. and just the overall art style and look is super realistic… easily the best I have ever seen. Almost photo realistic… and all this in VR! What higher praise is there? - : also really great, the rock formations are incredibly realistic. They look unique and do not repeat. Textures look photo realistic from middle/far distance. Only when you get up quite close do they appear a little muddy/low res. - : are great, it feels good to paddle, which is important as you spend most of your time doing this currently. You can use the paddle to push yourself away from river banks, rocks, shallows etc. All works great. Most foliage is interactive and will react very realistically to your paddle, for example if you brush against a fern or some reeds they will bend and move out of the way accordingly. -  is very well done, each level has it's own music which fits the feel of the environment well. Wave sounds and paddle sounds are good too. -  is good. I have a decent spec PC (9900k, RTX 3090) and I can max out the settings in this game, and set the in game render resolution to 1.7x and it never drops a frame, silky smooth. This is more than I can say for most VR games I have played. -  so far. There are 4 environments but you will very quickly come to know them all very well. I hope more variety will be added in future. For a launch state it is fine, especially at this price but it would be great to have some new levels added at some point. - : basically here you can kayak, but nothing else. For a launch state that is fine but I think the developers will need to diversify the in game activities a little to hold players attention and round out the experience. They have this stunningly beautiful world with not a lot to do in it outside of just paddling around. - : very basic and functional at best, essentially just floating white text :) This is one area that does need improvement. Personally I feel that made for VR titles with physicalized menus (ie. actually part of the world geometry) work best. Leave 2D menus for flat screen games.- : textures can look a little blurry/low res when you get up close to the surface of a rocks/tree etc. From far/middle distance they look amazing, but not up very close. Overall, a very good VR experience and a worthy purchase. I wish the devs all the best for their future plans for this game and I shall be keeping a close eye on how it evolves over time.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR experiences! Amazing graphics. Love the animals, dont miss the turtle on the beach in costa rica, diving penguins in antarctica. Thoroughly enjoying so far. The races will give you a workout! Overall 10/10! Of note, felt some motion sickness after an hour of play, given the waves, so for those prone to motion sickness be mindful of that.

_childDocuments_.review: ONLY BUY ON SALEIt's visually stunning, and the physics are good, it's certainly a VR showcase piece to show off VR, but really that's about it.There isn't much content sadly. You will be in awe as you paddle around the scenes, that's it really, nothing to hold you or bring you back.More content has supposedly been on the way for a while now, but nothing has arrived or even been teased. At Xmas they reused the previous years scene. They have a "roadmap", but I don't have any reason to believe it's anything other than wishful thinking.If you can attach you controllers to a pole it's a better experience and more realistic/immersive, you can rotate the paddle then too.  This is better with Lighthouse tracking though as of course controllers can go out of view of your HMD with this method.TLDR: Beautiful with good physics. Buy on sale, play a few times then use it as a VR showcase piece. Don't expect more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Kayak VR: Mirage is a very beautiful, if not the most beautiful VR game to date. The environments look so good that it was a jaw-dropping moment the first time I saw it, even when I played a ♥♥♥♥ ton of VR games before. Content-wise you get a total of four different environments where you can play race mode (basically time trial) or free roam. There is a total of 11 race tracks across those four environments. Most of those take you 1-3 minutes to complete, but there are also two longer ones which take more like 5-12 minutes, depending on the player. There is NO multiplayer at the moment, don't get confused by the screenshots on the store page. You can turn on ghosts of other players (nearby players, friends, your own best) if you'd like. An actual multiplayer is still planned by the devs, but they have yet to announce any details or a release window. On all maps you can select daytime and night which is a nice addition. The most fun thing has been the thunderstorm though, which is only available in one environment, sadly. It looks incredible and also impacts the gameplay because of higher waves and faster flow of the water. It would be nice to see this for other maps too.Considering the visual quality of the game, it also performs pretty good and has a lot of options, also including Fidelity FX, DLSS and optional anti aliaising (MSAA or TAA).While the gameplay is a lot of fun, I only played some short sessions because it can get exhausting pretty quickly, at least in race mode. For more immersion and better/ easier gameplay, it would probably be best to play this with a broomstick or something where you can attach your controllers to. I didn't have the chance to try this though.The current price seems fair for what you get, even if the replay value might be limited. If you only want to play multiplayer, you might wanna wait until they actually add it to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: As the screenshots or trailer of the game will reveal, Kayak VR Mirage has irresistibly beautiful visuals worthy of being called eye candy,when you see the vr perspective you will be speechless and find that everything meets your expectations.Watch gameplay from the different locations here: Besides the visuals, the physics to control the kayak are very good, to put it even better it almost feels natural!Without the resistance of the water weight, but you will feel drops of sweat.the game starts in an indoor pool where you can make yourself comfortable with the controls of the kayak, or you can use the pool to fine-tune maneuvers in compact places.In the pool you will also find an inflatable ball and an inflatable flamingo. The only bad thing about the pool is that you can't mess around with another player and play a game of 'Kayak water polo tennis'.In the different locations you will be able to choose either an exploration mode or a race mode, in addition if you look closely when spawning in some locations during an exploration session you might find the inflatable flamingo and you should then have to go to the other side of the route to get.I suspect that by doing this you also unlock certain options in which you can upgrade or adjust your kayak gear and equipment.The race mode offers a number of different race routes per location and you will also be able to challenge yourself against ghost players of previous players who have completed the race,these ghosts are chosen based on the time you had when you crossed the finish line on your previous attempt.The different locations are also very varied, sub-tropical, an ice environment, desert and the wild rocks, and when you explore you can also spot things that you are less likely to see while racing, such as animals and specific places worth seeing.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: So much better than I expected! I went into this game with a moderate expectation of graphics, environmental manipulation, and only a basic understanding of what I was in for. The graphics are so crisp, I kept expecting to be able to feel the water when I put my hand outside the kayak, the breeze on my skin, and the sun on my face! Each map has multiple modes for both slalom style racing, and free roam, in addition to Day, Night and a Storm map (quite spooky). There are a handful of discoveries to look for such as submarines, and creatures, and a bunch of floaties from each map. You can interact with the wildlife to some degree, my kayak was knocked sideways by a baby orca (AMAZING!). In another map, I chased the whale (must be the size of 5 cars end to end), and when it first emerged to flop it's tale above water, I got hit pretty hard. I raced with two different schools of dolphins in one of the maps. Highly recommend you sit in a chair with lower or no arms and elevate your feet and keep stationary for the full experience. This will also make it easier to submerge your headset under the water to get a new perspective, as you will be properly calibrated to change to sitting on the floor momentarily. The music soundtrack is pretty chill, and you can earn enough nautical miles to upgrade your gear skins. Racing mode is one heck of a full upper body workout. Let yourself fully immerse, take it all in, both above and below the water. I absolutely love this whole experience, and hope they come up with more content!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: The game has now been updated with a toggle for showing/hiding the player body, and patch notes were included with a promise of more transparency in future updates. I really appreciate that response and don't have any reason not to recommend this game now, so I have revised my review accordingly. This game is a really cool, serene experience, especially if you already enjoy kayaking, just be aware that it's not a very long game, with only 4 levels to play through at the moment, with the 5th being paid DLC. I don't mind paying for new content at all, but just consider the extra DLC cost if you want to get the most out of this game. I think its also worth mentioning that the game is not very easy to run. You'll notice most of the Youtube reviewers who try out the game are running pretty high-end GPU's, and if you turn the graphics settings too low it does look pretty bad. Despite these drawbacks, I still find the game enjoyable and may buy the DLC at some point since it looks pretty decent. Apparently we are even getting 2-player multiplayer soon, which is pretty exciting! This game is really cool and pretty, but I'm finding it tough to recommend spending money on it with the recent DLC release and update. I'm not a guy who will complain about the price of a game really, especially if it's a VR game, and especially if it's GOOD. VR dev's deserve the money for their hard work and this game is gorgeous, but the lack of patch notes and overall communication is concerning. The latest update had no patch notes whatsoever as far as I can tell, but there were a fair bit of changes done to the game, as noted by one of the devs themselves in their discord server. One of these changes was adding player IK, arms, and body, WHICH YOU CANNOT TOGGLE OFF OR HIDE. In other words, the trailer and pictures you see on the steam page now do not even reflect what the actual game looks like. I would love to buy the new DLC but I am not going to do so if I have to play the game with hands which don't even match my skin color and detract from my immersion. I know immersion is somewhat subjective, but I even hide player arms and sometimes the steering wheel in racing games, because seeing fake arms and a steering wheel when I can already feel my own arms and wheel just makes the experience feel fake. And it's the same deal here. Just please give us an option in settings to hide the player model. Thanks
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an usual review. Let me go straight to the point. I would like to share the deep emotions and sensations aroused by the experience. It’s very personal, but I think it gives an idea of the value of this app in relation to the technical evolution of the new VR medium. For months I tried the public playtest of Kayak VR on Steam and gave developers some suggestions to make it better; the title says it all, it’s a Kayak simulator in VR, the kind of sim where you are meant to move the controllers as if you were actually paddling. The Australian Canyon was the only location available, but it was enough to sense the great potential of the experience; very immersive and capable of enchanting our senses thanks to the great graphic fidelity and the incredibile rendering of light, especially for what concerns simulation of water. At the time, I wrote that it promised to be a milestone in VR gaming. Well, now I played the complete experience and I can say it goes way beyond my expectations! I never buy games at day one, it’s a bad habit as consumer; however what I experienced in the playtest was so convincing that this time I broke the rule and bought Kayak VR at day one for supporting such passionate and competent developers.I must warn you that the quality of my experience is highly dependent on the quality of my headset and VR rig. I play with the HP Reverb G2; each LCD has a resolution of 2160×2160 on 2,89″, that means1058 PPI, with very good brightness, contrast, colors and blacks; horizontal FoV is around 98°, so it has a definition around 24 PPD. If this numbers sound weird to you, no worry. I make it easy. The visual quality inside the G2 is the same as you get when looking at high quality monitor FullHD 24″ from a distance of 32 cm. In comparison to the today state of VR tech, it’s insanely good and eye candy! Obviously to manage such beefy headset and take the best out of VR games and apps, you need a beefy PC, not less than a RTX3080. Ok, it was important to understand my personal experience, let’s go on.I bought Kayak VR on day one as promised, but I was on my summer holidays far from my VR rig, so I played the complete experience just yesterday! I lost the sense of time, I spent the whole afternoon glued to the G2 without realizing it! OMG! Let me tell you my experience. First of all I focused on the relax mode. Kayak VR comes with two modes: the race mode and the relax mode. The first mode is a kayak race simulator where you challenge other users; paddling mechanics are very good and as consequence very tiring, all in all it’s an exer-game. Don’t misunderstand me, I tried also the race mode, and it’s good, but I played few races. I didn’t buy Kayak VR for the race mode, but for the relax mode. In this mode, you’re alone with your Kayak, immersed in the silence and calm of a wonderful Nature. Definitely a contemplative experience for sensitive romantic people! You know, I’m Video Games Art, that’s my mode! I already knew the Australian Canyon, so I started with the Antarctica location. It was a pleasure to paddle in the charming iced water surrounded by penguins, and explore the suggestive ice caves where the blow of the wind and the dripping of melting ice are amplified. It confirmed my first impressions, very relaxing and immersive. Then I explored the Costa Rica. Gee! Please, let me live forever in the clear fresh water of this sunny warm tropical island! OMG, the reflection and transparence of water, the poetic encounters with exotic marine fauna, the turtle, the manta ray, the dolphins; and most of all the intriguing foray into a jungle ravine hidden by vegetation on the surface of the water! Wow! I slipped stealthily through the shadows of the narrow passage surrounded by vegetation, as if I were the first man to step, or better, to paddle in that hidden paradise. I could not believe the realism of the vegetation on my G2! For at least 5 minutes I was no longer on this earth. I was truly in that paradise, all my senses focused on exploration and contemplation, my brain completely fooled. It’s a great achievement for a still immature tech like VR. Don’t forget that you have just 100° of horizontal FoV and 90° of vertical FoV; you have no eye accomodation, your eyes are always focusing on the panels at fixed distance; definition of real images is at least 60 PPD, not 24 PPD; and so on. Nevertheless, Kayak VR made the magic! It is certainly thanks to passionate and competent developers that are better than big studios! And we’re not done yet! Now it comes the best part of the experience...Continue here:

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks absolutely stunning, but you better have a great graphics card if you want the highest fidelity. I was using a 2080 Ti with 64GB of RAM and my GPU fans were roaring at times.. but the graphics are literally like you're there (no attention to detail was spared).Absolutely love exploring and relaxing in this experience... it's what i got into VR in the first place! 2 MAJOR RECOMMENDATIONS for the devs:1) please allow use of thumbsticks to simulate paddling and steering/movement, not everyone is using this for exercise or racing or simulation of kayaking, it would make it way more relaxing for those who just want to explore the environment (like just relaxing/meditation) 2) i've shown this experience to at least 5 people and every single one had issues with VR sickness... this was never a problem when i showed them the National Geographic Antartica kayak experience, please look into how they avoided that and try to implement it into the settings.I totally understand this is a kayaking simulator and you've nailed it IMO, but to make this more marketable and accessible i would recommend the changes above. Thank you for putting the love and attention to detail to this water experience, it's amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so since getting into VR I've been trying to find some kind of release that manages to capture something of a 'real life' experience. Wearing a headset and limited resolution obviously makes this something of a fantasy. Some releases have been nice but ultimately boring with visuals not nearly good enough to hold my interest for long. Lots with potential but never realised. But Kayak VR may be something different. I've tried 'River Relaxation' by another developer. Kinda bland and basically just a mechanism to transport you along a river with no real 'sense' of anything. But Kayak VR gives an incredible sense of motion. Bobbing on a very impressive sea, every motion is truly plausible. The rise of the sea, the dipping of the kayak. All incredible. The water is the best I've ever seen. And the scenery is very, very good. Fixing the controllers to any kind of stick adds to the immersion. Way more than it has any right to! And, of course, it is this aspect that makes this 'game' so good. If you want to get a very good sense of kayaking then this achieves that task. If you want something that succeeds in what it sets out to do, then this is it. The environments are a little limited. Not necessarily each particular environment, but more the number of them. But I honestly don't think anyone could criticise the experience. I think the developers have nailed the mechanism and only very minor tweaking may be needed. But I hope and pray they use their talents to expand the scope of the experience. Lots more content please!If there's one thing I personally want it's to gently kayak down a river for an hour or so. We don't need to interact with anything, just a pleasant environment to enjoy. Please don't get caught up in unnecessary complexity. More wildlife, and more time-of-day and weather options would also be amazing. But the most important thing is hour long rivers!!!The developers have really done an amazing job. If you don't want this kind of experience don't buy it and don't criticise it for what it doesn't claim to be. But, if you are like me and want a perfectly implemented experience, then I wholeheartedly recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: This is the best kayaking / rowing experience in VR. I think it's a great game and I highly recommend it for not just for those new to VR, but also to VR veterans. However, Kayak VR Mirage is not perfect and it isn't the best looking experience in VR (there are more realistic looking experiences like VR Japan).  There are currently only 4 maps and 3 of them do have invisible barriers (the other is a loop around). There are day and night scenes, but no real-time day-night cycle or random weather (the Norway storm scene is probably the best looking map in the game though).  You do have asynchronous racing, but no real-time multiplayer racing or even coop. However, the game does have both simulation rowing or arcade rowing. I highly recommend the arcade as a beginner kayaker to this game. It is much easier and you'll have more fun rowing around the maps & races. You can also change hand positions or enable twisting of the paddle. You do not have avatar hands or body.Game is running on the Unreal Engine 4. On my RTX 3080, I was getting steady 90 fps on epic quality graphics and with DLSS on at medium quality with super sampling set to 1.4 pixel density. I did not experience any serious issues or bugs. There is no smooth or snap turning. You can play comfortable seated & it is recommended as long as you can comfortably row around. There are no options to traverse the world without physically rowing though.The game does look gorgeous. It is pure eye candy. The rowing physics is great as well. The main competition would be Downstream: VR Whitewater Kayaking and Kayak VR Mirage blows it out of the water. However, there is one area where Downstream is better, the currents for the water make it a more challenging experience. There just really aren't currents here at all. The water can get a bit choppy in the storm, but that's about it. The water is usually not deep at all, for some strange reason. I do wish I could listen to my own music. I do wish it had real multiplayer. I do wish I could see my avatar hands and body and that I could hold the paddle any way that I wanted. I do wish it had more maps. Still, despite all those criticisms, this game is awesome and a must buy for VR.

_childDocuments_.review: Just downloaded this (the min it became available) and i must say the visuals have absolutely exceeded my expectations.... just stunning !  All the youtubers saying how amazing the visuals are..... well i can see what they mean !  From the little i played so far no bugs although weirdly steering doesn't seem possible by simply rowing with 1 oar, you have to instead "brake" with 1 oar to steer, not a big deal it just seemed unusual. _childDocuments_.review: Played for about an hour. Game has great visuals, but that's all. In its current state the game feels very unpolished and needs more content, structure and things to keep you occupied. After 30 minutes or so of paddling around it began to get boring. As someone who has kayaked many times, the movement and force when you paddle did not match anything at all in real life. I've read some people say that they would use this game to show first time vr players. I would disagree, there is very limited interaction on what you can do in this game, no hands or body so you don't truly feel you are there. You can slightly interact with the fish in the water with your paddle, or by shoving off the shore with the paddle but it leaves a lot to be desired. Not a good game for first time VRs if you want to fully show off what is capable. It would  be a good game to just sit and look around and relax.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got to try the game, and I was blown away - that does not happen often. Graphics are Alyx class, and that says a lot. It's not strictly a game, but more a kayak sim. Feels like using a real kayak - or "better than life" as the devs call their company.  Using RTX 3090 I could do res 250% with all settings maxed out (but antialiasing set to on, not MSAA), and using highest quality of DLSS. I left the in-game pixel density slider at 1 and used SteamVR to set the res at 250%. Using lcd, DLSS creates a blurry image, but it's fine in res 250% in 90 fps. Disabling DLSS and using MSAA provided non-blurry image quality, but jaggies appeared. I ended up liking DLSS the most. I found performance to be best with motion smoothing disabled. I took a few shots:Water and cliffs look beyond amazing - and all in solid 90 fpsLooks like tessellation, but I don't think it is, and tons of polygons make this game/sim look real There are for now 4 different locations - this is AntarcticaFound a turtle on the beach - note the nice textures and dynamic shadowsSee the small ripples/waves in the water - it looks amazingKayak VR is a 15/10 - it transcends the normal scale like Alyx and Lone Echo 1-2.  For those caring about VR, Kayak VR should be in their collection.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't figure out what makes this game and other vehicular-based games induce severe motion sickness. I've had similar motion sickness with Star Wars Rogue Squadron and another jet-based fighter. However, Pavlov VR/Contractors and any other FPS humanoid games do not induce this for me oddly enough. I maxed out the various accessibility options and the nausea just wouldn't go away.Paddling mechanics/physics made sense in both "Arcade" and "simulation" control modes, though I couldn't help but question whether constantly moving your arms in a "Kayek" fashion would make for good gameplay despite how "realistic" it is. I grew tired AND nauseous at some point and alt+f4'd. If I didn't get nauseous, this would have made for a good exercise-y game.Execution of gameplay elements from graphics to sound were optimal and does what it advertizes. VR games are a different breed of games. A game like this could benefit from a demo, just so people can see if they get sick.Objectively speaking, while I cannot physically play this without getting sick, those who can will probably enjoy it for what it is. It might be worth introducing the accessibility options on startup.For now, I think I'll stay away from boats, cars, and airplanes when it comes to VR.Played on Valve IndexGIGABYTE RTX 3080i7-8700k @ 5.0ghz32GB RAMWin10 21H2

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are amazing! I really didn't expect them to be that good. The number 1 thing I would say this game needs to make it another VR masterpiece to show off to friends/family is custom animal interactions. When I would come across the animals, I was really hoping for interactions. To see the dolphins jump out of the water, come up to my kayak. The penguins to act like they knew I was there. I also couldn't help but want to get out of the kayak as well. Not sure if maybe some form of mini crafting could be implemented. Maybe even as easy as a preset camping area that you could just interact with, relax in a hammock, start a fire, etc. Very awesome though. Great job! Can't wait to see what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my new meditation app. Graphics and environments are amazing. I own a kayak, and the interaction with the controls and objects in the environment with respect to the paddles is an example for all other VR programmers to follow. The storm in Norway is my new goto "show a friend" VR demo, as after being on the water is a similar situation in a small craft myself, the swells and dips that push against the kayak's movement is next-level.I've played on an Index and Quest 2 over Airlink and performance is great overall on an RTX 3070. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly Steam hasn't got my playtime right at time of this review. I've played about 2.5 hours. That's actually how long it takes, at a leisurely pace to explore everything. Sure it's very pretty and has that 20 min wow factor however, beyond that there is nothing else to do. It's been dormant in my steam library since December 22 and has no update worthy of returning to play it. It's been nearly a year since release so I worry with the PSVR2 release, those reviews will go the same way and the devs will cash in and leave. I hope not but seen it too often, and this game has that vibe to me. I will say if the situation improves, the roadmap is followed, and suggestions are listened to, I'll update this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Is Kayak VR a good game? No. It is freaking brilliant.The package may offer ridiculously little content in the sense of a flat game, but it delivers what is possibly the best "look and feel" of a VR title in 2023. Of course, that verdict is purely subjective - and driven by my odd preference to chill in beautiful, watery environments. And in this case, these environments do not only work as crisp showcases for VR tech, but they are actually designed with great attention to detail, such that the mood and uniqueness of each scenery is credibly captured. The intuitive and seemingly simple controls allow a surprising variety of tricks and techniques, sometimes weird and whacky, but mostly fun and challenging to master. I felt like a lame opossum while struggling even with bronze times, until I started experimenting with some unorthodox movement options. Completing all achievements was a jolly joyful ride. And the hunt for more gold times and better spots in the top 100 ladder boards will probably keep me returning for quite a while. Allow me to close this review with a small anecdote: On the day I purchased Kayak VR, my headset broke - oof. I decided against a refund and sent the device for repair under warranty. It took a while, but boy was that the right choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals! I have a rowing machine and put the game on tour and just lose myself in VR world.  Can be a bit difficult to use controls and row but doable. Race physics seem like you can get away with just spinning your wrists and controllers but for the most part, if you act like you are in an actual kayak then it will respond very realistically.  Want: Canoe setting.           White Water.           More Maps. (sign of a good game if you just want more right?)Haven't played enough to see any glitches or problems in the game. Will update.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game as soon as I upgraded to a new PC for VR gaming at the end of 2022.I was blown away by the graphics, and the overall experience was good... but there just wasn't enough to it. Very tech demo-ish. I was told to keep a watch on the Trello roadmap, and hardly anything has been accomplished  since 2022! I realize they put a lot of time and effort into porting this to the PSVR2, but in the meantime, we early supporters on the PC version have been shafted of content bc of this.Edit - I originally gave this a thumbs down for poor support, promises that haven't been fulfilled. However, after some reconsideration I must confess that it IS good, even if a very small experience. If I could put a half-way thumbs up, I would. I'd say, ONLY buy this on sale, or, if you see the Devs have actually shown a preview of new content in development. That would make me really happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Got this on sale in the steam VR fest for £17 and I can say that's really the limit for what I would pay though there are some MAJOR issues with the game for me. I won't be refunding it as I intend to upgrade my PC in the near future and I have hope that the game will ultimately turn out to be quite fun. Now to the issues I have with the game, ultimately it just doesn't work. I load into the pool/main menu area just fine and my framerate there is fine also however when I try to load ANY of the worlds the game just crashes. After turning down literally every available graphical setting including all the resolution based ones I was finally able to load into the Australia world. At this point it looks like I'm playing an N64 game in VR but at least it works. The funny part is once I loaded in to the world I was able to put all the graphical settings back up to what they were on (epic) and the game worked perfectly fine. In terms of gameplay it's a fun game, I have never been kayaking in my life and never will (I'm disabled making it impossible) so this is a nice way to get to experience it to some extent. the mechanics feel good to me and personally I found controlling the kayak rather intuitive and fun. In conclusion I am willing to overlook the issues the game has right now since it is new and I do have hope that the game will turn into something that can be a lot of fun to play with friends. If the issues are ignored or brushed off as "you just need a better PC" then the game is going to be a complete non starter for far more people than just me.EDIT February 2023: I responded to the dev and we emailed back and forth but they were unable to fix my issue and just stopped responding after a while which was rather annoying. I have however upgraded my PC since my initial review (I now have a 3080ti instead of a 1080) and the game now works flawlessly for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: What is this sorcery?!This is so incredibely beautiful, better than real water!The races are fun, I am bad but that doesn't matter and it runs smooth as butter with everything at EPOS quality, 1,3 ingame upscaling with a RTX 3070, i7 10700 and 32 GB RAM.For racing and getting achievements while roaming you can buy visual upgrades and toys.The long wait was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Love, love, love this game! I zip-tied my controllers to a pole and sat on a padded bar stool with another one on my feet and consistently forgot I was in VR. It really is kinda that good. Like I would see a bird or a stingray or something and marvel at the natural wonder of it all. But my arms are very tired now.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be honest...I bought this game just to look at the photo realistic graphics for 2 hours and then refund it. Instead, I ended up playing it for 4 and a half hours straight and got addicted to Kayaking.The maps are beautiful. There are 4 different maps (currently) each with 2-3 courses each. (I think 11 courses total) You can race your friends highscores (no live MP yet, but it's on the roadmap) or just random people. That or you can go around each map in a free play mode. The entire game is just breathtakingly beautiful. You can competitively race each track, or you can just chill and explore. Both are really fun.The kayaking physics are great. They function exactly how you expect them to. There are arcade and a simulation physics models that you can swap between depending on your preference.The one problem I have with this game is performance. It's weird because when I joined the discord to see if this was just a me problem, everyone said that the game ran very well for them. For reference I have a R5 3600, 16gb 3200, 3060ti, and the game is installed on an SSD. But for some reason I have to drop the SteamVR render resolution to 50% and the graphics down. While others with similar rigs said they run the game fine maxed out. Anyways its a good game and easily worth $20. It's fun to kayak around and its a great to put VR first timers into.

_childDocuments_.review: game looks good and the devs have an actual roadmap to update the game with various new features over the year, but.....1) the clips and images look more like it would have long  tracks you can paddle along, but it only has 4 I guess, different regions and relatively small "race" tracks that go in a circle.2) theres not much content other than doing free roam mode or timed races with asyncronized multiplayer, which means you see a few recorded races of random players within your time spectrum. so its no multiplayer yet, but they wanna add it in future.3) somehow this game gives me extreme headaches and playing this for 15minutes is the limit.4) the few animals you can see are cool at first, but if you sit there watching them for 5 minutes you'll notice their messed up behavior and scripts

_childDocuments_.review: the default control setting works well enough with index knuckles, but being able to make your own peripheral with little to no added cost kicks the whole thing up a notch. i ended up using a shower curtain rod and some adhesive-less medical cloth tape called 'sports wrap' to fashion an oddly realistic feeling oar. even the haptic still works, as the vibrations reverb through the pole you can still feel it without directly holding the controllers themselves lolfantastic environment design, great ui, and realistic rowing feel come together to make what is now one of my favorite VR experiences currently available. plenty of settings for graphics and controls allow for a cohesive, immersive meditative workout that sneaks up on you as you gaze up at the stars. or down, to see lively ocean creatures going about their lives underneath the waves. the refraction shader (?) seems to be a bit lacking, and there doesn't really seem to be much in the way in terms of realistic wake physics (like when something big lands in the water off in the distance) but the performance trade off means that the relaxation may give way to a surprisingly potent horror experience frantically navigating a stormy shoreline in rough seas. the asynchronous multiplayer isn't something i entirely care for; i would rather be able lazily explore around w/ some homies instead of getting my ass handed to me around a surprisingly large number of race courses to choose from. but again, it might be a performance trade off and the implemented ghost-based races run seamlessly. i'd like to have an option to adjust oar length so i can sit higher up in the kayak and not have to dig into the water so much, not sure if that'd be a good option for the competitive side but my arms would appreciate the relative ease. cant wait to see what it looks like with a few patches of polish/bugfixes!!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: BUYER BEWARE, This is NOT a game, this is just another VR Techdemo that was put together in a haste and then abandoned. The developer promised Multiplayer and it never happened, the trailer is misleading because you think it has Multiplayer but it's just some disembodied Kayaks that follow a path trough some goals and they call this "racing". It only has like 4-5 maps and except one, they're all an open area for you to paddle around. I'm really disappointed this is not a Game, I was expecting paddling down a river rapids and maybe getting some Multiplayer, but this is not it.Note: This is why VR failed, there's a few gems worth playing but most of the "Games" are just abandoned concepts and tech demos that go nowhere.

Imagine a 2D game that has very few maps, even less content and a pricetag of 20 euro's... it would probably have no more than 20% positive reviews. Apparently you can get away with that on VR, but for me it isn't enough. Maybe I'll try again in a few years from now, after many content upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the prettiest VR game I've EVER seen.The gameplay is simple, relaxing and satisfying.The sound design is perfect, with a solid sense of depth and brilliant music direction.The controls are intuitive and immersiveThe physics feel satisfying - the water looks great.The game performs excellently at 90hz and with some tweaking it can really maximize your GPUs potential.This game has the looks of Chris Hemsworth, but the soft velvety touch of Hugh Jackman

_childDocuments_.review: What I like the most is doing a smooth and efficient run. It's (not that) easy to learn, but hard to master. So I expect to spend quite some time on each track.The kayaking sensation is great and quite a workout for the upper body, as far as it's possible in VR. And of course the environments quality is a huge cherry on the top.I played the demo for a couple of hours (on one track) and the complete game is what I hoped for, more content and varied conditions.Didn't explore it fully yet, had to refrain my perfectionist side to have a taste of everything. So far it's great, I'll confirm it after having played for 10 hours or so.It's funny to see ghosts struggling wildly in the rocks and stuff like that. Though when I was the one in the rocks, I had to restart as soon as I passed the finish line to overwrite the evidence :D Then sometimes admiring my own ghost messing-up, but hopefully I'm in front.
