_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quickly becoming my favorite VR game. I absolutely love kayaking and paddleboarding (hint hint, devs?) irl, so when my friend told me about this it was an instant buy. The racing is fun, the game is really immersive, and it's cool being able to have fun kayaking even if it's storming outside, and going out in conditions I wouldn't even consider braving in the real world.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Never had any interest in kayaking, but absolutely loved this game for its beautiful visuals and realistic physics. The only current downside is lack of content - just 4 maps, although some of them are quite big. Plus the game is still being actively developed so there is a real chance for additional content in the future.Controls are very responsive and intuitive. I use workout bench to sit in a similar pose that you would in kayak, and it is very immersive even without tying controllers to a stick:) Interactions between paddle, boat, water and terrain are physics based and yet somehow there is no jank, everything works smooth even when you swim in a shallow waters and grind the seabed.The game looks great and performs pretty well thanks to native FidelityFX/DLSS support.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to do a review when I saw this game also has negative reviews... If I had to give up all the games in my library and keep only one, this would be it.Other people have done a better job than me describing it. It's all they said - realistic, breath-taking, beautiful. I have been waiting for a game like this since I first bought my VR headset. There's no way to say what this game is until you have tried it. I wish all the best to the people who made this game possible and may your inspiration continue to guide you in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, probably the most realistic looking VR game I've played to date. It might seem like a boring idea, but it's actually really fun to race and even just paddling around on free roam can be relaxing. This is VR done right. I think it's safe to say this is one of those 'must have' games if you have a VR setup. (Devs are very responsive to issues which is nice as well)
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute gem of a game this is! At first I thought that it might not have a lot of replay value but it absolutely does. As a workout routine this thing is fantastic with the incentive to beat your previous times being an ever present driving force. Control of the kayak is very realistic and it’s gratifying to see your skill level improve to the point where every stroke contributes to your next record breaking time. I feel comfortable in recommending this game to anyone who is even the least bit curious about the unique game play and utterly beautiful vistas :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best VR experiences.  Is it a 10/10 game?  No, but it will come very close I think as these devs work on it more.  It is probably the prettiest VR game I've ever seen for sure.  My jaw hit the floor as soon as I loaded into the pool.  The physics are really good.  Exploration in free roam is great with some interesting things to find.  Hopefully they add more as updates come.  Is it worth your time and the money they are asking for it?  In my opinion, absolutely.  It is an enjoyable, relaxing experience if you want it to be or a great arm workout in race mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game! The most realistic VR game yet! Great for a sweaty workouts that don't seem like a workout. Arms so sore today,Only two complaints: 1 the controllers constantly vibrate with no options to disable that in game. Seems to eat controller battery.2 when just sitting and enjoying the scene the "press B to..." Message overlay appears ruining the view.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Came across this game on 7-27-22 bought it the next day after some reviews on youtube would i recommend this game yes 100 % I did the Costa Rica map in free mode and just amazed by the scenery and controls. I have kayaked before and own 2 kayaks this is a great item to get the motion down to build stamina or just waste time I lost track on that free run for almost a hour .
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I have been gaming in VR since 2014 and the rift DK2. it has been probably 5 years since I was as floored by a vr title as much as this.I Bought and tried the Kayak Mirage VR "game" last night.In some ways it goes back to the early VR stuff... as a game it is pretty light on content  So if you want games then this does not offer much.But as a tech demo to show what is possible, and possibly to show none gamers what potential VR has, as well as just a place to chill out it is incredible. For me it was £17 well spent, i am more than happy just splashing about and exploring the areas. Visually there is nothing else like it, not quite photo realistic but it is as close as it gets. (my RTX3090 had to really stretch it's legs on full bubble with my reverb G2)I am not sure the paddling is that accurate, though there are 2 modes arcade and simulation. it's good enough for me.I put my chiller fan on blowing on me as i played it and it definitely did what it set out to do. it has been a long time since i have been on a holiday you would consider a tropical paradise and will likely be a long time before i go again, but this was a nice reminder of what i am missing. It also is the perfect app to show off my Reverb G2 headset, hiding its main weakness (controller tracking at extremes) but really showing off its high resolution display.I also tried very briefly the storm in ............ Norway i think it is ..... around a lighthouse ..... that seemed good too but i think the limits to the water physics are on show a little. The LED displays held up well - its not really that dark. i havent done a night scene to check, that will be a real test for that.if anything the only problem is it is easy to let your imagination run away with what could be in this.... stuff which would probably take a lot of Dev time and is completely unrealistic.. I do hope we get more content however, perhaps a few surprise animals injected in (there are some already)  without being told , as well as the obvious stuff like fishing or white water rafting etc.Next job is to fashion a paddle.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Played on a Vive Pro with Wireless attachment and Index Knuckles controllers. 2080TI/9900k/32GB 3000 RAM/SSD.I was not expecting to enjoy this as much as I actually do. All the reviews talk about the gorgeous graphics and everyone is right, this game is probably the most graphically beautiful VR game I've ever seen. The water reacts realistically as well. I'm not sure what black magic the devs pulled to make this game run so well either, after just a bit of tweaking I got it running smoothly while keeping the settings high. Aside from graphics, I am blown away by the attention to details. Stuck my head under water to get a closer look at a fish and the game changed the view as if I was actually looking underwater, the audio changed with it. When you run up on land and use the paddle to push yourself away, the sound will change depending on the surface that the paddle makes contact with. Ice will let you slide off it easily instead of being stuck like rocks. The racing is ok, I'm not a huge fan of competition in a game like this but it does have leaderboards and medals to earn if you want. It has neat unlockables and secrets to find while free roaming which is always nice.I would like too see more unlockables and weather scenarios. I love the stormy map but would also like a more calming storm to paddle about in. 100% worth the purchase for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It came up in my recommended so I thought, why not? And wow. It blew me away. The game looks so well done, and looks so crisp. My jaw dropped on almost all the maps. I really hope to see a lot more with this game in the future. Would also love the ability to invite friends to a free roam so you can relax and kayak together (:Honestly though, 10/10 game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect this. I purchased it out of curiosity, expecting to refund it after trying it for a few minutes. I only tried free roam on a single map, but I've already decided that I'm keeping this game.The graphics are amazing, even on my old GTX 1660ti. The water is just mesmerizing. The environments are more carefully crafted than any I've seen in any VR game.The only small negative feedback I have is that with a WMR (so controller tracking by cameras on the headset) and my slightly awkward seating position, I felt that the game did not always managed to infer correctly where my hand was when it was out of sight of the headset, something that for example Beatsaber manages to do with almost magical accuracy. I will try to craft a stick on which to mount my controllers and activate the special setting for that mode, to see if it improves things! I'll be spending many, many hours in this game.Edit: OH MY GOD I WHACKED A PENGUIN WITH MY PADDLE AND IT FELL OVER. GAME OF THE YEAR 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This games graphics dont really look 1:1 when in vr (maybe they do if you have a 4k vr) but they are still very amazing.On max settings games preforms smoothly even an a little bit worse pc than recommended.Although i feel like the simulation mode isnt really that realistic (its still the most realistic for a kayaking game)I give the game a 9/10!(This game is so calming, i feel like i could just stay there!)
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure if it's better than life, but the graphics and controls are pretty good.I like how audio changes if you stick your head underwater, but found that things are sparse down there.Definitely not something to complain for the price or game-wise, but it would be nicer if there was official mod support options.Not that my lazy ass would actually make any mods...By the way default settings are kinda fuzzy and does not show the true graphical power of this game. For those with higher end hardware, or in need of a room heater, remember to tweek them up.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: In the 27 minutes which I have played this game it deserves a 15/10.It is the most calming game where you can explore and enjoy the subtle changes in the environment. It is a game in which I could fall asleep to if I really was about it. The graphics are impeccable and the white noise music in the background brings seals the deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game and highly recommended. The graphics are the best in VR after Alyx. The physics are great and the water and the enviroment almost looks like real life, you feel as if you are actually there in the sea. A new bar has been set for VR graphics with this game, highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I like this but I want it to be more. But that may just be me. I had an overwhelming desire to get out of the kayak and go explore the light house. I remember Nat Geo's kayaking VR game and was pleased that there was a feeling of freedom built into it. It wasn't much, but you could (in fact, had to) get out of your kayak to continue an exploration story.So, yes, this is a great little kayak racing game / escape experience. The atmosphere is soothing! If those things are all you want, then this is worth the price. But yet in my dreamiest of dreams, I want there to be a story mode add-on. Or at least some dynamic that let's you get out of the kayak and stretch your legs and rest your tired shoulders with perhaps some simple mini puzzles on dry land. That dog needs to fetch tennis balls out of the water or something. :)Thanks for a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally another kayak game besides Phantom Covert Ops. This game is too nice looking to be a VR game, but good lord it looks so good. I was doing a quick row through Costa Rica and I had to stop to write this. Buy it. This game is a must buy. The kayak physics are superb and the locales stunningly details. I can't wait to see what comes next for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely insane.  I have no words for this and its not just about the visuals (although they clearly play a part) but its the mechanics, the movement, lighting and most important for a VR game, the sensation of truly being there.  Pure immersion.  I swear, put anyone in the game who is seriously angry about something and put them in Antarctica at night and bingo, instant therapy!  Its a beautiful thorough experience.  I've been on each location at least 6 times and i keep finding new things every time!  I didn't even find the sharks until last night!  Then the plane and atom bomb....what else is hidden under the waters?!   This whole experience is an important step for PC VR and everyone who enters my house from now on in will be experiencing this.  My good friend who is not good using VR was absolutely blown away with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: 10 minutes in and this is fun. The controls are intuitive if you understand the basics of paddling. The game is beautiful and simple. It'll give you a low intensity workout too. Toss some weights on your wrists and I bet you'll be toned up in a month or two.I haven't played multiplayer yet. But I could see games of hide and seek, or tag being a thing. Looking forward to what this game brings in the future.Hopefully they allow modding. I would love to see levels put together by the community!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty well made, from the graphics to the physics. This makes for an very enjoyable kayak experience. There's a racing mode where you compete against the ghosts of other players over the world, but what I far enjoyed the most was just paddeling around and exploring the water and landscapes. My far greatest experience was the storm. The rain pooring down, the big waves bouncing the boat up and down, the lighting and thunder lighting up the cliff sides in the dark... it was pretty a awesome experience.The price is pretty high though, because apart from 4 maps (not including the pool) where you can paddle or race around, there's not anything to do. So if you have the money to spare and want a couple of hours of roaming around in a kayak with amazing graphics, sound and physics, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Free roam is the most transcendent meditative experience I've ever had in VR... simply perfect. And it's a pretty decent upper body workout if you let yourself really role play the paddle motions and not resort to wimpy wrist flips.I'm running a higher-end machine with a 3080TI, i9-10850K, and Vive Cosmos Elite with Index controllers. Mirage runs flawlessly (not a stutter) using DLSS with all options set to Cinematic/Ultra, double pixel density, and dynamic shadows... basically everything running full tilt. It's the closest I've ever felt to actually being "in" a real-world environment in VR. The water simulation is some of the best I've ever experienced in any game, including desktop fare.I'm not much of a boater, so I can't really speak to the accuracy of the paddle physics, but everything else feels perfect. It's almost a little disturbing how satisfying it was the first time I pushed off a rock with the paddle. Everything is just right... the sound (be sure to paddle through a cave), the controller vibrations (drag a paddle through some bottom gravel), environment reactions (everything I've poked at reacts appropriately), and the environment simulation is 2nd to none.This is a steal at anything less than $40 and pure developer insanity at its full $22.99 price. Really hoping this dev continues to release add-on content... my wallet is yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I keep veering off to the left. I close my eyes and I've done a 180°. Can push myself off of rocks, sand and walls with my oar. I feel like Indiana Jones when looking up at the trees and vines in the jungle area (Costa Rica level). Worked up a real sweat when trying to paddle out to a distant island (which was inaccessible). Got the Thalassophobia achievement. 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Quite nice. Areas very beautiful. Not too many so far but setting it to night or storm (not all have) adds a bit more variety. All looks very nice, Reallly cool underwater effectsas well. And nowhere near as nauseating as you would expect (and some reviews claim). If anything you feel a bit too static in your moving Kayak. In the lowest possible VR help options as far as i can tell.The controls work as expected. For insurance reasons i haven't tried the broomstick option yet. But there are some fun, more realistic(?) control options for that mode.Well worth the price even now and hopefull  more to come. For free roaming the more open areas could be a bit bigger. Off the race track part you hit the boundaries pretty quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: If you buy 2 games  get Alyx and this, this is what vr on pc can be. Its breathtaking, relaxing and amazing.  Top of all time. now you have to like amazing graphics and kayaking,   just buy it   thank you so much devs for bringing this  gem to us when it seems everyone is going mobile route.  I love my Q2 but this is a masterpiece on pcvr
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: All of the Features they promote on the store page are realized. This game is beautiful nature meditation and low-mild exercise.IDK about the racing element, that aspect doesn't appeal to me.The entire aesthetic of the game is super tranquillo; the stunning environments and rhythmic ambient music work extremely well together. It's got an overall calming effect (on me, anyway) even though it can begin to feel like exercise if you lose your enchantment with the environment.I hope to see in the future:1)More environments. (I will gladly pay for DLC if it is of the same or higher quality as the original content.)1a)Generic Isla Nublar. Throw some dinosaurs out there.2)Three modes of play2a)As it is. Calm and beautiful and serene and your day/night/storm options.2b)Realism Mode. Damaging your kayak or paddle on rocks and such could eventually end your run. Maybe hostile animal life that you need to outrun.2c)Horror Mode. Same as 2a until you get a heart attack inducing jump scare moment and are destroyed in some way inevitably and entirely by some horrific thing or circumstance. (My first play I paused for five minutes to search with certainty that I wasn't going to be eaten by a giant shark if I went into the deep water, as I was fairly certain I'd have a heart attack if that happened.)3)A compass on the fore area of the kayak that pointed the direction to follow a route or tour you pre-selected before your session. A race without the competitive aspect, just enjoying the visuals.4)Maybe fishing could be fun? That might just be a whole different game, though.10/10. If you need a break and want to take a six thousand dollar trip for twenty bucks, get your flipflops and some back support and row your way to calmate.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Just bought this, and I am blown away. The graphics are some of the best that I have ever seen in VR, and you feel like you can reach out and 'feel' the water. I never thought that I would try my hand at kayaking, but this has piqued my interest. If this does not win any awards for best game in VR, then there is something seriously wrong. I would have paid more than the asking price for this little gem, so don't procrastinate...just buy it, and enjoy the peace and tranquility it will bring to your life.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This VR game is just the thing I've been waiting for. Very immersive, I get totally lost in the realism, have just paddled my kayak around a tropical island and am amazed with the graphics and beautiful tropical clear waters with turtles and fish. KAYAK VR is now my number one game, VR fishing is up there with it. I hope these guys come up with some new maps soon ? such as the Lake District ? Cornish coast ? Scotland ? West coast of USA ? great potential for new adventures and locations, even fishing ?  Well done to the developers, this is a huge step forward in VR. Update 03.01.2023 this game/simulation still fascinates me, am eagerly waiting for additions such as new maps, new kayaks? sea kayaks? more choice with weather and sea states? great game, well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Kayak VR is beautiful and incredibly immersive. My wife doesn't care for VR at all, but even she spent half an hour paddling along Kings Canyon today. There are many settings for quality/performance and motion sickness. You'll be either working on your speed in a race course or exploring the environment (many animals and Easter eggs to find). For what it is, it is exceptional. Do keep in mind that it is highly specialized - you don't get out of the kayak, and your hands never leave the paddle.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin...   The game is BEAUTIFUL.  Easily the best looking title I've seen in VR.The paddling is modelled accurately - or at least as accurately as possible considering we don't have force-feedback rigs.It feels so nice to just go out on the water and chill.And then you also have the chance to put your skills to the test in the races, and boy do you build up a sweat.Definitely worth the price tag, 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a "game" - it's more of a relaxation simulator - and a really good one! The graphics were flawless and beautiful, the physics accurate and smooth. I've yet to try attaching my controllers to a pole yet, but I feel like it would be worth it. It's an embodiment of what the metaverse should be - an experience delivery app - being from Australia, I felt that the Kings Canyon map is very authentic. Well done to the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending assuming there will be more added later. For now, it's a nice experience but not something I'm likely to come back to often. Relatively small areas in each map to explore and no visual indication when you are about to go out of bounds so you can avoid a reset. The map load times are long enough to think it might not be loading, and no "loading" animation or word to tell you it's working on it. The graphics are good but not Alex quality (I'm using Oculus Link with cable on a high end PC - GTX 2080). Just not enough things to do other than race and explore a relatively small area in each map. It's fine but I need more to do to keep me coming back.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Good tech demo for sure. I'd recommend it as exactly that. It's not really a game and none of the whale or things shown in the trailer happened on any of the freeroams for some reason?Was hoping to have about 25 levels more than 4 for this price as even the levels are tiny and the Costa level takes about 5 minutes to get from start to finish.What would really make this game next level is having waterfalls to kayak off, really really high ones and extreme levels, fast rapids to go down etc. It's absolutely perfect genre for it in every way and I'd love to lose my stomach flying off a waterfall, birds going past n all that stuff.The levels are nicely rendered, but they aren't really much more exciting than the swimming pool to be fair. Still recommended for the experience and hope the team make an extreme version of this sim with hundreds more levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Recording of my first dip into the game: I've had this on my wishlist for ages, since the moment I knew that it was going to be a thing, and buying it the moment it was released was absolutely the right choice. This is just as immersive as I'd hoped, and just as rewarding to play as I'd hoped. My first 50 minutes or so in the game have me totally sold and it's easily one I'm going to be revisiting in VR on a regular basis.It looks great (albeit an Oculus link and a Quest 2 don't do it full justice). It feels great. It makes sense. While I do have some experience of kayaks in RL, I feel the available lessons in the game are easy to follow and should get anyone up and running in no time.This is, without a doubt, a huge recommend from me. It's such a good use of VR, and makes for really rewarding use of VR. You know how some games get to you and make you think about how good they feel and make you want to get back in them? Not to compete, but to just enjoy the feel and the experience. this is one of them for me.It does, however, have some small issues. While it runs very smoothly for the most part (on my setup anyway) there does appear to be the odd very jarring pause during races, from time to time (always seemed to be in the same spot too). On occasion I was also finding that the direction of the turn of the kayak didn't seem to match how I was paddling (it remains to be seen if this is a game issue, a general VR issue or just a Quest 2 tracking issue). I'm also slightly concerned that there isn't quite enough content to *really* last. The maps that exist look good and deserve some chilled exploring, but I do worry a little that I'll get a little too used to them eventually.On the other hand... with global leader boards for all the races on all the maps there's a definite dose of "just one more try I think I can get a bit higher in the ranking" to be had here.As I say, big recommend. I feel given the current content £20 is pushing the limit of what I'd be happy to pay, but I was happy to pay for what I've seen and enjoyed so far (albeit I got it for £17 due to the launch discount).
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Come On A Leisurely Kayaking TripKayak VR: Mirage is an amazing kayaking experience. From the breath taking visuals, the life like sounds and the physics of the water and kayak will draw you into one of the greatest VR experiences.This has to be one of the most breath taking games I have ever played. The game just feels so good, you will be immersed into the kayak and be sitting on the water. The only thing missing is water splashing you time to time.The game has two play styles. Racing which is more arcade play style and free roam where its heavy on the life like physics. I have only played free mode. Let me tell you, nothing comes as close to real kayaking as this. I live on the coast and have access to the water all year round to do things like kayak and spending time on the water. What I don't have access to, is the beautiful places the game takes you to kayak. There are four wonderful stages to pick from, each with a daytime or nigh time  run. Some levels also have weather conditions you can turn on.  All of this adds to the amazing worlds you will be immersed into.The game is not all just great looks and sounds. It also has one of the best simulations I have ever experienced  in VR. Moving around in the kayak just feels so real. The physics of the paddle and kayak feel so real. Specially if you attach your VR controllers to a pole to use as a paddle.I use meditation and other apps to relax on tough days, this game is one of the best relaxation VR experiences I have had. Just taking your time kayaking around, stopping to see the sights and sounds, will put you into the most peaceful world. One thing I would like to see in the game is a camera option, to snap pics of those special moments you will have.If you are looking for a true VR experience I can not recommended this game enough. It has just blown my mind. Do not pass on this experience, its one you do not want to miss.Watch my preview here,
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Only have 0.3hrs on the official version but have logged a lot more on the pre-release version.First thing to say is that I with I had an option to pay full price instead of the discounted. This was made for people with kayaking experience but at the same time for people who don't have experience it's super easy to pick up the skills and motions with the swimming pool lessons.There's so much adjusting you can do in this game in the settings, visually it's absolutely STUNNING! Playing it with both a Rift S and a Quest 2 the performance with the Quest 2 is outstanding, DLSS on, graphics set to the max and away you go. This truly is one of those games I think everyone who has a VR headset should get first, there's no way you'll be disappointed with this.Looking forward to all future updates and dev support as they've been great so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: TAKE MY MONEY!for real.  Abnsolutely stunning graphics, true to life movement style and physics, and just...wow... so much wow here.   i don't know what i feel more, the strain from working up a sweat in this, or my jaw being on my chest in a permanent "wow" from the scenery and water and .. man not gonn alie, i have a bit of a fewer of open dark water and kayaking the open waters in antarctica in possibly what in real life would be some of the most remote things a human can do....the heart got going, this.,..somehow helped a bit...  even the orca being there. I knew it was safe, but dang... that's an orca... somewhere under me...    I know it is harmless but this is such an awe inspiring view that instinct kicked in and i felt hunted lol.10/10 for the wow factor alone, VR needs more of this.EDIT: also had to add, racing a humpback whale.....epic.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning graphics, physics, environments! Such a gem for VR, loved it from the first second.edit (more details):What's is great about the game?- breathtaking detailed, very good textured, animated and lighted environments to explore in free roam with different day times- the physics with kayak, paddle and the water feel very credible- easy to play, hard to master (for best times in time race) - challenging online leaderboard with racing against ghosts of other players- technically astonishing high framerates with so much detail- maybe the VR game with the most advanced graphic settings to dateWhere are the great potentials for the future?- additional (arcade)l game modes in the gorgeous looking environments like a cup vs. NPC, fun obstacle races, checkpoint races with time limit, mini games like water polo with goals against other players, NPC or time,.. just a few ideas- fun tracks which are using the realistic environments and turning them into something different, e. g.  with purple water, crocodiles, wild water and other crazy stuff ^^- more achievements, secrets to find and unlockMany ideas are already listed in the roadmap:to make that all happen, I recommend buying the game to support the cool developers and to enjoy one of the greatest looking VR games of all time!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Does not work on the G2 gets stuck at the menu stage at the pool. At the refund point i decided to give it a go on the Quest 2 and OMG WOW.  The graphics are the closest to real life I have seen in VR.  I cannot wait for the issue with the G2 to be resolved as it will be even more amazing. Great work by the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, is you are into casual, exploring games with amazing graphics, this is for you. I spent quite a bit of time with the demo and the full version is just light years more than what the demo experience was. It runs great on my mid level rig with a 2080ti and is probably one of the best looking VR experiences i have tried. Your upper body will also get a workout for sure with all the paddling. The price is also a good deal, I would have paid double for this experience. Definitely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning graphics and a nice little workout as well. You can relax and check out the environments or head down for race on one of the many courses available. Here you can race against other players but not in real time which is supposedly coming in a future release I'll be looking forward to that. Lots of amazing things on their road map this one is definitely worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been impressed with a VR game like this since 2016, when I got the original Vive. Playing this on an Index is absolutely mindblowing. This is the first game in 6 years that I feel necessary to show to friends and family visiting. The nighttime at Antarctica brought tears to my eyes. My significant other says it's the best thing she's ever done in VR.Incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Kayak VR: Mirage is amazing. The graphics are some of the best, if not the best, that I have witnessed in VR. I am always looking for more relaxing VR titles and titles that transport me to beautiful locations that I will probably never visit otherwise. This one checks off both of those criteria.I can't comment on the racing as I have little interest in it, nor can I discuss the simulation aspects of actual kayaking. What I can say is that it is exactly the type of VR title that I love.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Only played an hour but it's great experience and a great add to a VR collection Runs great on Quest 2 Air link on a 3080 setup even on max graphics! I have never done kayaking before but I am very happy with the level of simulation/physics in this game.What I would link to see:Higher graphics settings on the background environment even on max settings my games runs smooth as hell so I would like the background to look a bit better still looks great thoMore tracksBigger pool area with more fun stuff in thereAn option to put a speed dial on just for fun to see how fast your going but i understand  if that's not realistic
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: What you see on the showcase video is DEFINITELY what you will see when you buy this game.Beautiful scenery, amazing water physics, interactive nature. I was amazed my pc can handle this game on max graphics, that's how optimized this game is,If you see this, dev. I'm very looking forward for future updates including multiplayer!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Breathtaking beautiful! I didn't try any of the racing modes yet, but the free roam mode in these beautiful environments is very relaxing! The four different locations offer a lot of things to discover and enjoy. I have to admit that I am a huge fan of VR relaxation environments and thus tried a lot of those, but Kayak VR is simply the best looking simulation currently available![my system's specs: Valve Index, AMD Ryzen 5800X, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 TI]
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I have only been on it a few short minutes, but quickly Free Roamed all the maps at full speed and was just astonished.  I really like that it keeps track of the distance you pedal, 2.5 km today and my arms ache and I am sweating a bit.  Great workout for the arms! The scenery is beautiful in all the maps, with natural wildlife, and great sounds. Amazing graphics.  I am running cinematic mode with my Valve Index and RTX3090.   The water gorgeous and I love that you can stick your head in it for a refreshing underwater view.  I will definitely be enjoy this more when I have less work to do :D   A couple of wishes for the future: 1. More animal life, dolphins in CR, Leopard Seals in Antartica, maybe a croc in Aus :D  2. Would eventually love a map with some rapids to navigate, even a waterfall to drop from, or surfing ocean waves. Keep up the nice work devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The physics are pretty good- that being said, the kayak itself is not one i would take on an ocean...it's a river kayak. the seascapes are lovely. -More animal life ( perhaps seals?)  would make it really fun. ( i see at least one if not more seal nearly every time i am in the sound) I am making a paddle for my controllers (HTC vive)  so that should help with immersion. My wish is for them to do a sea kayak model and a slightly more accurate paddle model. I could do without the ridiculous hats and love to see more realistic hats people do wear..gloves would be another thing to add in for points, but first they have to put in hands. What you don't get is a pivot on the paddle, so rotating it doesn't seem to do anything. Multiplayer freeroam would make it perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I am so impressed!  The environments are incredible.  It redefines what I expect in video game textures.  I could spend 100 hours in each map, and still want to hang out there longer.  I've got a better paddling resume than most, and this game really does the sport justice.  There's still room to improve, like the fact that your blade angle doesn't really matter, but for a beginner to intermediate boater, this is probably going to feel 100% accurate.  Also crazy how it works the same muscles as actual paddling.  Just shell out the cash; you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: The game has no campaign, no story, no NPCs, no survival element.....it looks good but the content is not there. As it currently stands, it's just a tech demo. Once you've seen the couple map variations which are very small, there's no reason to come back.The motion controls are very repetitive and get tiring very fast.The racing against ghosts is boring.The game misses the fun factor. Multiplayer is not what this game needs. It needs a campaign, a story, a survival element. Something to break up the monotony of just purely rowing all the time. Imagine if HL:Alyx had a kayaking side mission or two. Remember Phantom: Covert Ops?
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap!Photorealistic graphics, smooth and satisfying paddle physics, and performance is not hindered! I've only just started, but this is sure to be a great title to show off to non-frequent VR users!Only 4 locations are available, and I'm not sure if there is anything else to do besides racing and free roam. Regardless, the free roam experience is worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Only played for a short period but i love it. I'm afraid of a lack of content but those gold ranks for the races... wow are you gonna need ot practice for them. At the time of this I got a rank 3 and that's probably as good as i'll ever get... because i'm cheating as there's no one playing yet!If you don't have motion sickness and can love relaxing... this is the game for you
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics.  I don't have the newest rig, 2080 rtx and i7 7700k, 16gb ram.  It defaulted to epic and is performing well.  One of the most beautiful vr games/experiences so far.  I've been wanting something like this ever since I got vr.  I hope they add other areas to explore, but as is it is very much worth the price of admission.  I turned off the sound track and used free roam to explore.  It feels like you are really in the kayak.  The Norway storm environment was incredible.  Rain and lightning and thunder and the waves tossing you up and down, while in the distance the lighthouse.  It's very immersive.  I did start to feel a touch of motion sickness at this point, even though I do have pretty good vr legs.  Try keeping your eyes on the horizon.  I would go back to experience that scene though.  This game is kind of meditative.  You could just listen to your music and float around, watch the fish swim beneath you and the birds fly overhead.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: A near perfect, visually stunning and serene experience.  The environments are gorgeous with some pleasant surprises.I hope to see more environments, maybe rivers in the future.  Some flowing water would be nice maybe with some foliage overhanging the water.  I also wish this had drier regions like Africa where rivers could flow into small lakes with wild life teeming at the banks risking a drink with crocodiles in the water.  White water could be fun, but maybe distracting as the splashing can break the immersion if not done just right.Costa Rica is my favorite environment and I searched for a way to get into narrower water ways so I could be surrounded by that jungle.  The graphics are great and the lighting just about sells the environment as almost photorealistic.  Which makes me wonder what this game could do with photogrammetry.  Day and night cycles could be hard to do.I tried racing but that doesn't interest me as much as the free roam.  Racing IMHO distracts from the environment.  I would have liked to have more quests, like finding a piece of a treasure, taking a photo of particular rare wildlife, or a vista, anything that encourages looking at the beautiful environment.Besides the pipe dreams for more content, I have one gripe:  Having played Phantom: Covert Ops and enjoyed that rowing experience, Kayak VR does a better job at the simulation.  However, when you stop rowing, you stop drifting unusually quickly.  I have limited experience kayaking, but enough to know it feels off.  I wish that forward momentum was maintained just a little longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Mindblowingly beautiful and wonderful to play, this is very obviously a passion project. The amount of care and detail put into it is amazing. I cant actually believe it looks so good and runs so well! Highly recommended if only as a way to visit a beautiful place and explore. The concept of a kayak is, in retrospect, perfect for seated VR- if you have ever been on a kayak before its exactly the same, and if you haven't ever its fine because you dont have to worry about capsizing. Just be careful when using a broom handle to simulate a paddle that you dont smash something valuable...
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Plenty of positive reviews up already about the graphics and physics.  My favorite part is just casually paddling or sitting in the kayak and soaking in the atmosphere.  There's a roadmap for the game to to continue yet right now it feels a bit empty and small.  I'm hopeful there will be some rivers to explore or lakes, maybe some rapids who knows. The bones of the game are solid, so time will tell how amazing this can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible, the thunderstorm it's so stressful and frightening, i felt that i could get hit by a lightning!, also being able to get so close to penguins made me emotional, just one thing to improve is to have more wildlife, like having seals, whales jumping around, orcas, dolphins, etc. but after all, it's a perfect experience
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: A good while ago I tried the demo and was blown away. I really like exploration aspects and being able to just hop into a kayak in a photorealistic environment in a split second is... something else! Its also not just the environments, the water behaves like water and the kayak behaves like a kayak would. It is SO good at what it does. I had and still have zero doubts about buying this game right on launch and the short time I had today (launch day) had me quite impressed with the other 3 levels as well! I will also be keeping a close eye on the roadmap and future updates and possible future releases of this studio. Gefeliciteerd met de succesvolle launch, lekker bezig! (Congratulations with the succesful launch, way to go!)
_childDocuments_.name: Kayak VR: Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. The physics work really well, the visuals are incredible, the soundtrack is great. This is my new daily. Combine this with a rower and you got an awesome workout experience. I am using the index and index controllers combined with a WaterRower. The index controllers slip on and tighten to the rower handle easily. They can be either pushed all the way to the center of the handle with your hands on the outer portion of the handle, or the other way around with your hands closer to the center of the handle and the controllers near the ends of the handle. Either way seems to work just fine. I played around with the settings a little but only after 10 to 15 minutes, it worked really well unchanged. The only setting that is important to not enable is rotate paddles due to the way the controllers tighten to the rower handle.The kayak doesn't utilize the leg movements of the rower, but the side to side of the kayak adds some oblique utilization that I tend to ignore while rowing normally. I am very excited to explore all the maps and I hope the developer continues this project.  10/10 would recommend.

And we all know it's pretty easy to scare someone in VR!How did the devs do this? How have they made this look so much better than every other VR game? Maneuver our fully physically accurate kayak around checkpoints and crown yourself the fastest, or take it easy and use the free roam mode and enjoy the scenery.

name: The Thaumaturge
detailed_description: The Thaumaturge is an isometric, story-rich RPG with a unique take on turn-based combat, character development features, and investigation mechanics , facing you with morally ambiguous choices – set in a world teeming with mysterious powers and strange ethereal beings called salutors . The year is 1905. Warsaw lives under the yoke of imperial Russian tsardom. Its inhabitants constitute a diverse group of different ancestries, views, and beliefs with often conflicting interests: Russian soldiers, Jewish merchants, Polish townspeople, and more. Despite the circumstances, the city is a buzzing metropolis, where one can attend a breathtaking party with the high society, and later get robbed in one of the dark alleys of the Praga district. A city of great hopes and dreams on one hand and dark desires on the other. A thaumaturge bears both a gift and a burden at the same time. This parallel holds true for Wiktor Szulski , the game’s titular protagonist, who is drawn back to the tumultuous streets of 20th-century Warsaw by family matters. The gift of thaumaturgy is intertwined with family legacy, passed down through one's ancestors. This mystical inheritance significantly shapes Wiktor’s life journey tied around a pursuit of unearthly entities and their hosts. As only a thaumaturge can tame these ethereal entities - known to a select few as salutors - utilizing their mystical abilities to discover secrets hidden within the human soul and speak to the Darkness, no one understands quite like Wiktor how everyone suffers their own demons. Features: Shape your story – as a full-fledged RPG, it allows you to alternate your choices and make you deal with the aftermath. Develop your character – creating your own version of the thaumaturge will allow you to approach situations in different ways. Experience unique turn-based combat and defeat your foes using human attacks and skills as well as psychic strikes delivered by salutors. Influence and manipulate the temperaments of other characters to bend their will to your liking. Tame the power of salutors – use the unique set of their skills to gain an advantage while exploring the world and when bringing your adversaries to their knees. See the world that’s inevitably gone – explore the uncommon, heavily researched historic period of the early 20th-century Warsaw, where crime and luxury are often two sides of the same coin. Meet historical figures and learn about their involvement in the story. Created in Unreal Engine 5 to deliver a detailed & beautifully crafted world.

_childDocuments_.review: I admit, you have to be up to listening to lots of dialogue, but it is worth it and conversations are interesting most of the time.The turn based combat also feels like you have multiple viable playstyles that you can choose from. Also almost all Salutors seem to have a purpose in fights and you will find yourself using some of them every fight, while using others only if you design your strategy around using them.I hope there will be a dlc or a part 2 in the future :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: This was a marvelous, fresh experience. The Thaumaturge is a fascinating game.It reminds me a lot of The Witcher 1, even though on the surface they are completely different games. They both have that slightly janky European style, a fascinating main character with a brilliant voice, a quasi-realistic setting with a mysterious, magical flavor, more morally ambiguous characters than you can count and clunky combat (each in their own way, of course). But most importantly, they both have an atmosphere and story in both main and side quests that motivated me to search every nook and cranny to find all about it. Is it coincidence that both stories come from Poland? Maybe, maybe not. All I know is that I am really glad that stories like these are being told and I can experience them.The game is not without its minor flaws. While voice acting is generally superb, the spoken text sometimes does not match the subtitles, especially in the latter half of the game. Combat is a change of pace at best and a distraction at worst and feels unnecessary. Finding and taming salutors has not much other purpose than to improve combat option variety and open some dialogue options, but I feel they could have done more to make them feel more special and not like creepy pokemon. And finally, the game performance can be sporadically abysmal even on very high end hardware and the reason is unclear: I will a few more patches would do the game good and ensure that the legacy of  will be of a cult classic.The best moments of the game are its story and its fantastic characters and it is in the dialogue scenes where everything comes together almost perfectly. The music also improves the mysterious and creepy undertones of many conversations in "thaumaturgy dark land". There were a lot of great moments in this.In summary, I very strongly recommend this game if you are interested in the premise and love a dark, mysterious atmosphere in your stories. Be warned that combat is not the main point of the game and that there is "Euro jank", but in a good way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Thaumaturge, made by 11 bit studios, is an amazing game that really caught my attention. As someone who loved Frostpunk, I was curious to see how the developers would do with a detective RPG. The game reminded me a lot of Disco Elysium, but with a cool magic twist that made it really fun to play. The story kept me hooked, and even though the fighting was pretty straightforward at first, it got more challenging and enjoyable as I played. I'd rate Thaumaturge a 9.5/10 for being such an engaging and well-made game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed the refreshingly new story told by this game and would highly recommend it. The biggest disappointment I had was a certain lack of challenge. The combat is generally perfunctory requiring little care to successfully make it though, with minor exceptions for significant moments and the quests have a lot of hand holding - though this might simply be an old man's complaint about how all games are now compared to those of 20+ years ago.But those issues were clear early on and did not deter me from playing through to completion, which is quire unusual for me, to see the entire story through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Pros:-Absolutely captivating story, occult mystery and historical fiction blended perfectly.-Gameplay is somewhat unique, doesn't feel boring or tedious.-Combat is really engaging, requiring some strategy and knowledge of your Salutor arsenal.-The Salutor's designs are incredible and their animations are extremely well done.-Very detailed environments that actually feel alive.- Cons:-A few technical glitches and funny errors, but nothing gamebreaking.-Animations and facial expressions are a bit stiff, to be expected from a small studio but still very enjoyable and also very promising for future projects.-Combat can be somewhat confusing but will get way easier after a couple times.Overall great game, Looking forward to a sequel already and I haven't even finished the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Hate to say it, but the game is... dull. The writing is bland and sometimes just absurd, some plot points seem to come out of nowhere, and the village is just a bad tutorial area showing the bland empty world and not actually explaining half the interactions.One would hope that it would get better once you hit Warsaw, but there is no improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare to be whisked away into a world where magic reigns supreme and mysteries abound with "The Thaumaturge". As an avid gamer and fantasy enthusiast, I can confidently say that this game exceeded all my expectations.From the moment I launched "The Thaumaturge", I was captivated by its stunning visuals and immersive soundtrack. The attention to detail in every aspect of the game world is truly commendable, from the intricate spellcasting animations to the lush landscapes teeming with fantastical creatures.But what truly sets "The Thaumaturge" apart is its spellbinding gameplay. As a budding mage, players are thrust into a rich narrative filled with intriguing characters and intricate puzzles to solve. The spellcasting mechanics are both intuitive and incredibly satisfying, allowing for endless experimentation as you harness the elements to overcome obstacles and foes alike.The game strikes a perfect balance between challenge and accessibility, ensuring that both seasoned wizards and newcomers to the genre can find enjoyment. The pacing is spot-on, with each new discovery and revelation propelling the story forward at a tantalizing pace.Beyond its captivating gameplay, "The Thaumaturge" also boasts a wealth of content to explore. From hidden secrets tucked away in every corner of the map to side quests that offer unique rewards, there's always something new to discover, making each playthrough feel fresh and exciting.In addition, the developers have shown a genuine commitment to their community, regularly releasing updates and patches to address player feedback and improve the overall experience. It's clear that they have poured their hearts and souls into crafting a game that not only entertains but also resonates with players on a deeper level.In conclusion, "The Thaumaturge" is a must-play for anyone who has ever dreamed of wielding magic in a fantastical world. With its breathtaking visuals, engaging gameplay, and rich lore, it stands as a shining example of what a modern fantasy adventure should be. So don your robes, sharpen your wands, and embark on an unforgettable journey into the realm of "The Thaumaturge". You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I was sceptical about this game at the beggining, but I decided to give it a shot regardless.Not disappointed. The story is amazing, visuals are stunning and all these collectibles and secrets to uncover - fantastic.What caught me off guard is that actual Polish names in this game were spelled correctly, same as some of the districts. That's just some of the crème de la crème of this game, honestly.If you really enjoy uncovering secrets, interesting dialogues and many, many different options of doing things, you won't regret buying The Thaumaturge.Personally, 9/10 - spent most of my nights playing this game, I got even jump-scared once, lol.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Within 25 hours , I was able to do most of the content. It never outstayed its welcome, the pacing was good.Thaumaturge is set in 1905 Warsaw , within the Russian empire , it succeeds in depicting the struggles of the Polish revolutionaries in fighting for their independence and also their conflict with the Russian Military Police and the brutal ongoing fighting.From a lore and setting perspective, the devs managed to make a rich city , meeting actual historical figures at the time, adding to that I played in Polish dub which made the whole experience even more immersive.The story does have its twist and allows the players freedom of choice and even different paths to the endings.This game does have specific issues though:- The turn based combat is limited and rather boring, in a lot of fights, it felt forced. The game is rather easy in normal difficulty.- The exploration is not so rewarding, the player will keep clicking on "witcher sense" button to show where to go next, it doesn't allow the player to actually think deeply on how to find clues.- Music is overall grim and not rich , there's barely any soundtracks.This is was still an enjoyable experience.

In game you will find post card called "Viev from Łódź" - and you will see some tropical or sunny paradise...... Only city Łódź was super industrial, dark and dirty place in 19 hundreds. Was it AI made? Since this moment im just sick of this thing

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the game.I really like the setting and the story.I played on normal difficulty and I am kind of a lazy gamer but I felt combat was a bit too easy.I enjoyed doing the city secrets quests. They give experience which is valuable for upping your skills but in some ways there is not a whole lot to them and I can understand why some people didn't like them.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game sits in a space that's near Disco Elysium, where it's a fun game, it's educational, and it's art all at once. It very much causes me to become interested to look up more things about Polish history and Slavic supernatural while also having me think about various plot points as if I'm detective to try and figure out what's going on. Choices also actually matter in this game, as your Pride level can influence what options you can take (or not take) so replayability is big in this. Fully recommend this game
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. My biggest flaw with the game is the combat. Not the system itself but rather the enemies themselves. You are fighting the same type of enemies the entire game. Even when you fight demons, they don't fight themselves but with human figments. That and some crashes are my only real complaints. The best part about the game are the demon themselves and system around them. They look amazing and are pretty well balance toward any play style. While I do overall like the game. I do not recommend the current price. The best opinion is wait for it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I will say that the gameplay itself is great as well as the story. Fighting groups of enemies is a great mix of cool ability animations between you and your salutors. The lore woven into the story is quite interesting and the random funny bits are welcome.The game does itself a bit of a disservice with the cut scenes. Lots of popping clothes and jerky animations when the camera cuts to/from characters. Aside from that, I don't really have anything negative to say about the game but I do wish they would fix it. The game has a heavy amount of cut scenes and the beginning is incredibly heavy with it. It's worth cleaning up.Leveling brings a lot of variety to the gameplay. I wasn't expecting being able to add the perk of your choosing to your attacks. Building your attacks out differently and choosing which salutor to attack and swapping between them is a lot of fun.But please fix the animations.

_childDocuments_.review: So the combat is unfortunately for me personal not very fun, complicated and repetative, and I really, really wish there would have been more conflicts that doesn´t force you to fight your way out to finish a quest, or runing into people who gets ticked off for something minor and starts shooting at you med day in the streets of Warsaw.BUT omg if you can get through that, It´s an amazing game! The way it ties into history and themes are a delight, and I have no idea where where the story is going. All in all very worth it IF you don´t come for the combat.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a good story and a lot of reading, then this is the game for you.I like the setting and the atmosphere. And the soundtracks are pretty good too.Now let's talk about the bad stuff:- The combat is very boring and barebone- Where you find the clues make no sense at all a lot of the times. feels like a collecting sim more than investigating.- Not a fan of time limited quests. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very nice, including mechanics, characters and plot. You can see straight away it is made with love to Poland and it´s complicated history.* fun fact: there was moment in history, when Poland did not exist as a country at all.But. What is with the graphics sometimes? I play on a highest resolution and still some of the scenes look weird. Plus, some tiny visual bugs in a core fight mechanics. Other than that it is made creatively. With the romantic vibe of Russian "Master and Margarita" atmosphere. I love the game a lot.I would recommend it for sure, it is original, beautiful and helps your curiosity about Polish and Russian history.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid A tier game with good environments, great writing, acceptable voice acting... and a lot of bugs. Like hoo boy are there a lot of bugs. Crashes too. Every 10 minutes at the least. The prologue was good, but ever since I got to the main Warsaw area, it's been non stop memory leaks and C+ runtime errors. I can't recommend this game to anyone before they fix such basic things.Setting: The setting is interesting and it's a fresh take on the occult horror mystery genre. The environments work as you might expect and the graphics are decent. Don't expect to be wowed by anything outside the beutiful sketches and photos your character can collect during the game. The game has a disclaimer at the start that ruffled some feathers, but it boils down to the devs saying "we are very diverse, but wanted to make a mostly historically accurate game set in the break of the 20th century so don't get your knickers in a bunch over modern day political issues" which I think both libs and cons took to be aimed at just them, so do be civil about it. From what I've seen it really strives for historical accuracy as well as possible... though the electric trams of Warsova are three years too early!Writing: The writing style is interesting and doesn't hold your hand too much. Characters might intentionally leave things unsaid or avoid subjects. Some dialogue doesn't flow well into the next line and the character might go from one end of the emotional spectrum to the other between lines, which shows some late editing of dialogue, but it's not too jarring. Sometimes the characters are a bit superficial and wear their hearts on their sleeves which isn't quite typical of slavic people, who are usually far more restrained (when they don't get vodka at least). I would have preferred an even more mature approach where you have to work harder to unravel the Flaws of people, now it's just basically clicking on a few glowy bits on the ground and then using the dialogue that's clearly marked as "this moves the story forward". Maybe it'll get more complicated later on.VA: Like I said, it is acceptable. There are some really bad deliveries (young Wiktor is atrocious) but for a small indie team I didn't expect anything more. People speak english everywhere and drop random russian/polish words now and then, which is an okay compromise between full english or full polish/russian dub which would have been very problematic for, again, politics. I just really wish people would understand that it's a small indie company and people are complaining about not having their localized subtitles for this and that language, the devs can't do everything and for the time being I'd rather they use their time on fixing bugs than making subtitles in italian, brazilian portuguese or laplandish samic.Bugs: The game is both buggy and crashy, and that's the reason why my upvote turned into a downvote. Constant crashes and ubiquitous bugs makes this game difficult to play. I'm forced to stop playing until the game gets some patches. There are also a LOT of visual glitches, clothes billowing this way and that, texture pop-in, especially when loading the game. It's not a light game despite being an Indie title as it uses the UE5 engine and needs a better PC than you might expect, so do check the requirements.

_childDocuments_.review: The thaumaturge is a RT button simulator. It's also an rpg, with turn based combat where choices matter. You play as vladimir the machinist more correctly a deus ex machinist. who being abandoned by his father decided one day to find rasputin; yes that Rasputin and take him back to Poland to Varšava. Now the game makes sense like this review so far. But even tho i have a feeling that every quest has cut content that dissapeared sometimes in development, what this game has and what is special to my heart is slavic mythology. For example did you know that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Bukavac is from Srijem from Croatia. Me neither. We did it, we are special. ♥♥♥♥ you Luka Modrić. But no honestly the story in the game is so confusing its like everybody has their own agenda and practicly 2 hours before you finish you still don't know the ♥♥♥♥ you are doing here. Actually even when you finish the game you are still confused. I heard there is an ending where you are like ♥♥♥♥ this I'm out of Varšava and honestly i think its the best ending. Combat is trash, and no way in hell can somebody call it interesting. There is a reason Disco Elysium doesn't have combat, it's not necesary. Voice actors are, eh, contact Don't Nod guys and ask them for guidance. 75/100
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The story is pretty neat and they really now how to give that 1900 Poland feels and vibes.The combat is mid, and mostly uninteresting (accept than 1 combat which I believe may be optional)Writing quality has its hiccups but is mostly is OK.8/10DO NOT play this game if you expect to do detective work! You are really more for the ride when Wiktor does the investigation for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: 32 hours in and I am still absolutely loving this game. The story-line is very engaging: much more fun than sitting in 3rd year history ever was! It is also good seeing the history told from the Polish perspective as every country's history books record events differently, or ignore those which do not affect them directly. Characters are well thought out, no-one is wholly 'good' or 'bad' and I do like that my decisions actually change the direction of the narrative. My husband and I are both playing at the moment, and regularly pause to compare notes, so we are very aware of the consequences of all of our decisions.Graphically, it's beautiful. I want to visit Warsaw.As a casual gamer much more used to MMORPGs I am finding the controls (keyboard & mouse) very pleasant to use. In fact being able to mostly just use the mouse is great. The turn and turn about combat suits me fine as it allows me to fight tactically, and actually learn how to use abilities rather than just button mashing. If you're looking for a story based game, like history, and have a sense of humour, I would highly recommend The Thaumaturge. I am playing on Story Mode and loving every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Half way through the game so far, but this has been an awesome experience. The story and characters are well developed, and I've become attached to WS in a way I wouldn't have expected from the get-go. Poland looks so amazing and lively, which I think it is a real nod to the amount of time and work the devs put into the game. Sure, there are some repetitive moments in the game -- battle sequences make me crave something new in some sort of way, but as you start collecting more Salutors you'll start changing how you approach each fight, and it does keep you actively thinking about your next move. Overall, I highly recommend this for anyone who prefers a good story, great characters, and a bit of strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a unique atmosphere, interesting plot and well written characters (especially the protagonist Wiktor). Main points for me:- 1905 Warsaw feels real and full of life, you can see the devs poured a lot of love into it. - Exploration and gathering clues is a big part of the game, but it never felt tedious. Character interactions and vignettes open up while exploring the city. Combat is fairly simple but enjoyable - There are multiple ways of completing quests and developing Wiktor's personality, goals and relationships with other characters during the course of the story.- Gorgeous art direction (soundtrack, city map, Wiktor's sketches, clothes, salutor designs)
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is pretty fun and the visuals are nice but the voice acting is sub-par (To the point where I tried to change the language to polish so I could just read the subtitles) and the writing is also pretty awful. A hell of a lot of the side quests are just travelling from place to place which is tiresome.I'd say wait for a sale
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge may be an interesting game for you, if you like story based RPGs in a quite linear storyline. It has besides the main questline some sidequests and a lot to discover and is mainly set in the pre-revolutionary Warsaw in 1905, when the Polish were fighting for an on state, being devided between the Austrian, the German and the Russian Empire (though the Austrians and Germans only play a side role in this adventure). It is centered about occult folk lore about Demons and Ghosts, that can be seen and used by the Thaumaturge and therefore has some horror elements which makes it a game for adults. Even more, a Thaumaturge is a kind of wizard, that is able to see traces of persons that stick to certain objects. This ability is for others unsettling and even fearful.You take over the charakter of Wiktor Szulski who returns to Warsaw in 1905 and can enjoy a well written story with some twists and turns, sometimes surprises. Though the story is mainly linear and brings you to certain places in Warsaw, the sidequests and discoveries can be done more freely. There are some decisions to make that seem to be meaningful in the end; I can't judge the real impact of theses decisions though, that only would tell more playthroughs. You don't have the option to create your own character. Besides the option to alter hair, beard and clothing, you can pick and change skills.I really enjoyed the story on two days in which I immersed for about 25 hours in the World of the Thaumaturge. The main characters are interesting and each with talents and flaws, the complicated historical, social and religious background was reduced, but still rich enough to get an idea of how it could have been to live in 1905 Warsaw, though the story is purely fictional, even if it sometimes relates to historical persons.. I enjoyed the story, liked the round-based fighting system and the skill development throughout the game, though the fighting became a bit repetitive in the end. Although I found the story interesting, I don't think that the Thaumature has a great replay value, since the main story is too linear to make interesting enough Options to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: An okay game with interesting themes held back by below average execution.  The idea of playing an occultist in turn of the century Warsaw, investigating your surroundings through psychometric traces, is immediately intriguing.  Unfortunately the core elements are frustrating to engage with. Dialogue is stilted and plagued by non sequiturs, while pacing is awkward with scenarios starting and ending abruptly.  Combat is a chore that intrudes on the investigative gameplay.  Overall I was left more aware of missed potential than enjoying the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game, and it has some good ideas and a wonderfully unique setting. However, the writing feels... dull, and the dialogue is uninspired. A dialogue-heavy game like this really needs a certain spark and solid lines for the voice actors to deliver.No, they can't all be Disco Elysium, but this one still missed the mark for me. I wish there was something between "yes" and "no" for "do you recommend this game" because I'm sure it has plenty of appeal for a lot of people, and I thought it was just okay, but not okay enough to keep.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game so far and I'm even addicted to it, the atmosphere is similar to the first Witcher.For such a small studio (apparently 60 people), the game is impressive. The game is more for those who like history and slavic atmosphere, then you can appreciate its charm more, the only thing missing is the Polish dubbing
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: This game is special, and it was an absolutely amazing experience to play. It reminded me of the Witcher 3 (a lot), Disco Elysium, and Divinity: Original Sin. Anyone who claims to be bored during this game has to be suffering from TikTok brain rot because the story is captivating, characters are memorable, combat is fun, and the fantasy of being a Thaumaturge is almost exactly like the fantasy of being a Witcher. If you are on the fence, just bite the bullet and buy this awesome game!You play as a Thaumaturge, basically a warlock that can use demons (Salutors) like goth pokemon. There was even a "I wanna be the very best, like no one ever was" dialogue option so that is S+ automatically. You have the ability to absolve people of flaws that draw these demons to them and influence them to commit heinous acts. In this game you will dive into that fantasy, dense historical intrigue with Rasputin, Tsar Nicholas, and many time period relevant factions. You will piece together the mystery of your estranged father's death and chart your own path through the political and occult circles in early 1900s Warsaw. I will be singing the praises of this game for a long time.
