_childDocuments_.review: Trying to play  around its release earlier this year was difficult. From a misguided English dub to distracting performance issues, the game undermined itself at every turn. Had I stubbornly stuck with it, this review would have been much more negative. Thankfully, life finds a way. The powers that be thought it fitting I trade all my free time over the past couple of months for a chance to experience  in a much more presentable state—patches and a new Polish voiceover firmly in tow. While all the improvements and the universe at my side made me stick with the game until the end, they revealed that its finer points still require effort to enjoy. Gone are the NPCs with frequently mismatched voices to their models, the Polish voice actors who sound rather unconvincing speaking English and the non-Polish cast members who stick out like a sore thumb. Following an update back in May, you are no longer forced to use an inconsistent and rather unnatural-sounding English dub. However, while the Polish VO is the better way to experience the game, excruciating pacing issues and a combat system that goes nowhere cast doubt over the whole thing.Through fervorous attention to detail and an authentic historical setting,  wears its inspirations on its sleeve. Developed by Polish studio Fool’s Theory (the same one in charge of the  remake), it takes place in early twentieth-century Warsaw, following protagonist Wiktor Szulski as he returns to his birth city to attend his father’s funeral. Mixed in with—you guessed it—fantasy elements, it makes for a fresh take on an RPG dominantly based on Slavic folklore; something we've been getting plenty of in recent years.As the opening text so handily explains, thaumaturges are miracle workers able to perceive and manipulate emotions in the world around them; effectively being able to read and influence people’s minds. That alone would be a straightforward set of powers, if not for salutors—spiritual entities drawn to powerful human Flaws, who thaumaturges can team up with to further exercise their abilities. Szulski is a thaumaturge, though not a particularly good one, as he is nearly driven insane by a failed attempt to capture his second salutor prior to the events of the game. Thankfully, before he completely loses his mind, he manages to track down a certain Ra-Ra-Russian mystic to help him out and reinvigorate his search for power.All healed up and buddy-buddy, the two set off for Warsaw, a city Szulski barely recognizes after being away for fifteen years. An outcast and further shunned for being a thaumaturge, he’s forced to navigate family matters, the rising tensions between Polish citizens and the Russian Empire ruling over the country, and the unfulfilled expectations his late father had for him.  is built upon some great character drama with Szulski as one of the best protagonists in recent memory. How these characters are humanized, without the writing shying away one bit from the less flattering aspects of their personalities, is executed flawlessly. Whether you decide to play up that humanity or feed into Szulski's Flaw of Pride through choices that selfishly grow his power, the story doesn’t lose any depth and reacts to your decisions with surprising nuance. Not many characters will be outright kind, so you’ll come across plenty of situations where the latter makes sense. I swear, never has an evil playthrough felt so motivated.The same can't be said of the game's plot. It's not that it doesn't make sense, but rather that it lacks urgency and investment. You're supposed to think where Szulski’s allegiance and place in Warsaw lie, whether he’ll side with a political faction first, his family and friends, or perhaps turn it all around for personal gain. Yet, the conflict between the Russian Empire and the subjugated Polish people isn't that prevalent and doesn’t do much to get you personally attached. Every time you’re swept up in these circumstances, it’s at the behest of someone else, which makes it easy to remain indifferent and solely focused on helping out whoever it is you’re helping out. Szulski is primarily written as a self-centred character whom I could buy doing things for himself or those close to him, but not to achieve the goals of a group. Even the choices you have for the ending are mostly written around specific characters, rather than an ideology you can get behind.Looking at its gameplay,  functions as somewhat of a point-and-click with turn-based combat. Interacting with objects lets Szulski read the emotions imprinted on them, which leads to deductions that advance quests and award experience. With him being a bit of a glutton for knowledge and since manipulating emotions makes up the crux of his thaumaturgic powers, it's a great way of tying progression to the narrative.This carries over into all exploration, as collectables like photographs, sketches, music records, or newspapers and posters with absorbing worldbuilding can be found throughout Warsaw. Levelling up lets you place points into any of the four dimensions of thaumaturgy that each unlock different dialogue options as well as new abilities for their respective salutors, provided you managed to capture one as part of a sidequest.As thematically thought out as the gameplay is, however, it ends up feeling flat across the board and does little to make the game’s narrative shortcomings easier to stomach. While Warsaw looks great from a technical standpoint and the character models are sharp and detailed, it’s all so very lifeless; partly due to the drab colour palette, a criminally underused soundtrack that leaves many scenes void of atmosphere and blends together otherwise, and the blatantly poor animation. The characters in  look too good for how little they’re animated, which never lets you get fully immersed and, at worst, threatens to harshly dump you in the middle of uncanny valley on a rainy day. The isometric view as well doesn't do the game any favours.Both the combat and the search for clues turn into a chore due to a complete lack of challenge. What passes off for enemy variety is laughable and the whole schtick of reading your enemies' actions in advance makes for the easiest turn-based system I've encountered. The salutors' abilities and the different upgrades they provide to Szulski's own moveset, all freely available in any encounter, allow for lots of buildcrafting, yet there's no need to experiment past understanding the basics as you'll brute-force your way through anything that isn't a boss fight. While Fool’s Theory tied all the aspects of their game together and made serious strides in some rather expertly, the matter of the overall experience not being that compelling remains. I hope this isn’t the last we see of Szulski, though. If we don’t, I’ll at least take solace in knowing that all those little idiosyncrasies I love about the first  are probably in safe hands.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since the success of Disco Elysium there has been a small resurgence in more story focused RPGs, the Thaumaturge is another game in that style. Set primarily in Warsaw during the late Congress Poland era, when the city was a part of an ailing Russian Empire, The Thaumaturge tells the story of Wiktor Szulski, a Polish expatriate gifted with extraordinary powers who returns to the city of his birth to settle family matters. As a fan of RPGs, good stories and history in general, this was a game I could not possibly resist playing. So I did play it and now, a few dozen hours later, it's time to write down a few thoughts.The game's setting is largely historical but there are twists. In the game's world demons, called Salutors, exist. Drawn to people's flaws and influencing their behaviour. Superstitions and legends are explained as often being the work of those Salutors. There is also people that can perceive and form bonds with them, called Thaumaturges, which gives them incredible powers of perception and awareness. The idea may not be too original, but it's clever enough and well-executed. The historical aspect is also quite intriguing. The setting is not one often explored, though with the recent rise of the Polish gaming industry, I do expect that to change. Either way, the setting is well presented and fairly rich. A lot of time can be spent enjoying the sights and taking in life in early 20th century Warsaw.The game is heavily story focused. Following the death of his influential father and while trying to reclaim his legacy and repair his relationship with his sister, the protagonist finds himself at the epicenter of a struggle for the future of Warsaw. All that in the shadow of the teetering Russian empire and the plots of its would-be saviour, the charismatic Grigori Rasputin. Yes, that Rasputin, whom somehow Wiktor befriends. This mix of historical events with fiction works well and keeps the tension high. The player has many choices to make and things can often take unexpected turns. Most of the principal characters are well developed and complex. The various factions are often given ambivalent and conflicting appraisals.Combat is the other main aspect of the game. It has a turn based battle system where actions are queued and happen one after the other. The player character can use his Salutors and their various abilities to gain an advantage in combat, summoning them to do his bidding. Combat is not particularly complex, but it does have a fair amount of variety. There are negative effects that can be applied, a focus system which allows for special powerful attacks when the enemy's focus gets broken and so on. I did like the combat, but not overly so. The various animations can get repetitive after a while and there really is a lot of fighting. Surprisingly, the options provided to avoid fighting via dialogue are often quite ineffective. Rather uncharacteristic for a story-focused RPG. Negatively so.Focusing a bit more on the negatives, the game does come with a number of issues. The quest trackers for example are not always particularly helpful, some questlines don't follow organically and parts can be missed. Sometimes you just have to guess where to go next, when the game doesn't really cultivate a guessing style of gameplay. The obtuse map system is also partly to blame for this. The repetitiveness of battles was mentioned earlier, but the same can be said for general exploration. The game expects you to right-click both for tracking and to uncover hidden elements using the protagonist's powers. After a while that does reach a few clicks too many. Finally, on the story-side some choices feel somewhat railroaded and, particularly on minor encounters, rather illusory.All in all, the Thaumaturge is a nice package alright. Flaws and all. The setting, story and characters deliver and despite some mostly minor issues the game stays entertaining throughout. It is quite obvious that whoever created this game cared a great deal for Warsaw and its history, though I rather doubt they were big fans of tsarist Russia. Whatever the case, I do recommend this game to all fans of story-driven RPGs, fans of history and anyone who has an interest in this not often explorer era.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is done and dusted. I’m not certain how many endings there are in the game, but I qualified for four based on my choices and skills, so I saw those four. You play as , who is the titular Thaumaturge.The game itself takes many twists and turns, but much of the game focuses on your friendship with Rasputin, and your relationship with your twin sister Ligia, as you try to figure out how and why your father, also a Thaumaturge, was killed; while navigating the politics and general social climate of 1905 Warsaw.The story was very detailed and intricate, with a ton of lore and interesting branching paths that will, as mentioned above, ultimately dictate which of the game’s endings you can enjoy. Very well written and although the story itself is fiction, the backdrop of 1905 Poland and specifically Warsaw was, so far as I can tell, quite historically accurate. This game was highly enjoyable from a story perspective. And the progression of Rasputin from the beginning to the end was particularly compelling and noteworthy.Along the way, you will also seek to defeat and tame salutors, which are spirits who attach themselves to people who have a strong personality flaw (such as anger, fear, and so on). Additionally, you as a Thaumaturge already have a companion salutor who chose you based on your own flaw (pride in Wiktor’s case). A Thaumaturge can see these spirits, and thus try to separate them from their host and add them to your collection. Which in turn offer you special insight and abilities when dealing with other people, and new combat abilities as well.Combat is turn based and resolved using Wiktor’s fighting abilities and those of his salutors, along with upgrades and buffs earned along the way. These are purchased via skill points and are presented as four skill trees based on the type of salutor you are upgrading. Combat was fun and prevalent, but not specifically the game’s focus.The game’s focus is really investigation and dialogue. You, using your heightened senses as a Thaumaturge, will find many, many secrets in Warsaw, mostly taking the form of side quests. Some are story related, most are world building instead. Designed to help you get to know turn of the 20th century Warsaw. You of course will also use your investigative skills to further the main story quests.Gameplay is isometric, although cutscenes are 3-d. There is thankfully fast travel, and objectives are clearly marked. The world crafting was very well done. Everything looked very believable, and the developers clearly put a lot of time into the graphics, really making Warsaw a living breathing city.Additionally, every interaction is fully voice acted, and I thought it was quite well done. The team did a good job of getting a solid effort from the voice actors. The music in the game was quite enchanting, and the sounds of the city itself were omnipresent and ideal for the places they were representing.I played this on the Steam Deck, and I would consider it to be Verified despite not having that status. There were some issues with the game, but none seemed to be Deck specific.Rather, the issues with this game were very much general optimization issues. The game did struggle with framerate drops under certain circumstances. Specifically when it rained, when you were running through certain areas where it seemed like it struggled to keep up with the game’s rendering, and occasionally during conversations. Additionally, the game would sometimes freeze during the transitions between the end of combat and the ensuing cutscenes. These freezes required restarting the Deck and then continuing the game. None of these specific crashes repeated themselves. Meaning, upon restarting the game, the game functioned as it should after said battle(s).Anyway, I very much enjoyed my time in the game. Special shoutout again to the devs for how they handled Rasputin. That was immaculate. And I wonder if  will be a future expansion or another game in the IP. I guess we shall see. Although I received this game as a gift, it definitely earns its asking price. Give this game a look.

Highly recommended. However, before buying you should know this is a heavy narrative-driven RPG (or JRPG, really). Most of the gameplay is walking around, talking to people, finding clues and putting them together into conclusions. The order in which you do certain things, or if you've missed a clue or not, can have great impact on the outcome of a quest. There isn't too much combat and while I found it interesting (the summoning mechanic), it isn't exactly life changing. If you don't like to read, don't like games with a slower pace, don't like to explore cities and see a thousand little stories and interactions with little or no plot impact, then I'd consider skipping this (or buying, playing for under 2 hours, and then deciding).If you like narrative driven games, enjoy a great story and can appreciate amazing atmosphere and ``feel", then The Thaumaturge is a definte buy.

_childDocuments_.review: after completing my first playthrough i gotta say this game is pretty damn good, sure it has some flaws (funny i know) but overall it's a really fun and engaging experience. the story telling is great, and the world is amazing, a really cool concept executed in a really good way, the characters are great and likeable, even the "bad" characters still seem human, the voice acting is pretty good, not 10/10 but at least a 7 most of the time, sometimes a 5 or 6 but never below average. i personally really like the combat, it's turn based and focused on strategy which i like, the game provides you with a whole heap of cool and fun abilities with the different upgrades for your skills and the different salutors you unlock through the game, it's slightly repetetive in some sections, one specific one you have to fight 3 seperate fights right in a row which by the end was getting a little monotonous but other than that it's fun and somewhat challenging on the high difficulty (if you aren't a fan of the combat and just want the story/investigative elements of the game there is an easy mode)the design of the salutors is impeccable, both in lore and visually, each one is implemented in a way that suits the lore without compromising fun.still there is a lot more to say but it's not needed, overall i'd rate the game a solid 8.5/10, there's a few very minor things that could be improved upon but overall it's pretty amazing though it's also not for everyone

_childDocuments_.review: At times The Thaumaturge felt like an isometric walking simulator with clues spread out in levels, so I just have to follow the thread to find them. The investigation sometimes felt less like putting together clues and more like collectathons. There are so many conclusions that they end up feeling underwhelming. The writing in all these conclusions often seemed more urgent than the quests were.The endgame had a few surprises in terms of player choice and its consequences. My character was greedy for all the salutors he could get, and there was a very real consequence for his greed. It added enough to the story to make me want to play it through once again and make a different choice. This is what I felt after my first playthrough of The Witcher 1: the urge to go back and reconsider the moral dilemmas.That said, The Thaumaturge is not The Witcher; it’s not designed to take you on the lonely path so you can hunt monsters for challenge and alchemy ingredients. Instead, it’s an urban, sophisticated take on the monster hunter who is able to absorb the monsters and their flaws; what players do with those monsters and flaws is up to them. I enjoyed it for what it is: a psychological and political thriller adventure with RPG elements, steeped in Polish and Slavic folklore.

_childDocuments_.review: "- Your husband's last thought remained where he had died. I managed to read it.- Tell me, please. I'm sure it was something about putting Poland back on the map of Europe, right?- No, I don't know where the boat he'd been thinking of was, but he mentioned a summer afternoon by a peaceful lake and a wreath of marigolds.- Oh, God...- " ... and she was there - beautiful, magnificent, the only one "" Really loved the atmosphere and   designs. Overall, its an interesting setting; kudos to developers for coming up with something fresh in our world of remakes and remasters. You are playing as a polish nobleman in 1905 who has certain paranormal powers, which allow him to sense memories and emotions connected with various personal items plus allowing you to influence peoples' decisions. It makes you a paranormal detective of sorts, which basically describes a huge chunk of the game. You are searching for items, tying them together into conclusions and confront people about their secrets. Also, you're gonna do a lot of fighting. One of the things I learnt from this game is that everyone in Poland wants to beat you, mog you or both :P Dont worry, remember   I mentioned before? Those are the "demons" who are attracted by humans' flaws, which you can tame and use for your own benefit (both in fights and exploration )with a little help from a "certain man, who lived in Russia long ago". Fights are pretty straightforward, there are few tactics to pick from, some are easier than the others. If you'd pick a high difficulty you may struggle in the beginning but it will pass when you'll have more   at your disposal. Still, similar to other reviewers I found the fighting rather repetitive by the end of the game, although I was not really bothered since it was simple. There are few memorable characters and quite some interesting stories and sidequests, although sometimes it feels like the storytelling is a bit rushed and dialogues become rather flat, uninspired and linear. Luckily, the game is rather short, so you won't get bored, especially if you are not looking all over the place for collectibles. I can strongly recommend looking for sketches though, because these miniquests are rather interesting in terms of world building and its nice to see the effort developers put into crafting alternative Warsaw of early 20th century. Fair warning though, the game is rather heavy on the politics and some things that are included there might be debatable in terms of historical accuracy. I would suggest you to enjoy the personal stories of the characters and their relationships, because some of them are quite touching and heartwarming. Overall Score: 5.5/10. Didnt really like the endings of the main quest, felt like it was not very well thought through. Otherwise game is worth playing imo. I would recommend taking it during discounts and finishing it once.

There were tons of side quests . i did them all before i would exit the areas and it was alot of fun. Soundtrack was also very nice and i absolutely loved the boss fights . I'm calling this my favorite game this year so far. It might be short to some but its also only $40 . Personally i kinda dread when a game is 100+ hours now cause i got too many games to play as it is so i like these 25-50 hour playthroughs . I value the quality over the total time. If i still think about it afterwards then it was totally worth my money . i bought this one on a whim. Judged it by the cool cover and it was a successful purchase Overall Rating : 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Generally the game and the story are good, and the setting it all takes place in is very unique. Visually the game looks nice, however the game's performance is pretty bad at times.This game was a lot longer than I expected it to be, it took me 33 hours to complete the main story and all of the side quests (which are worth doing, as they are just as high quality as the main quest and often times directly affect the story's outcome), and there are many other endings which I haven't seen yet. I was pretty disappointed with the ending though, at least the one I got, as it wasn't really all that satisfying for the path I chose and it felt very hastily wrapped up.The gameplay is pretty good, though it is kind of a walking simulator. Most of the detective-esque stuff is right clicking to reveal hidden information in an area, and then clicking on it, which reveals some information, and if you've collected enough of it you will be able to come to a conclusion which will often unlock some kind of dialog with a character. Not extremely exciting, but I did enjoy it. The combat is pretty basic and never felt challenging or like it required much thought, except for the final boss fight. Another thing I was a bit disappointed with was the lack of interactivity. At most, you can look at photos which then unlock an "admire the view" prompt near the location, panning the camera away from the regular view and showing the map from a different perspective. There's occasionally stuff that you can interact with, like "buy doughnuts" or "drink cocoa" which play a sound and show a sketch alongside some text plus give some XP, but these aren't all that interesting. There's also several times in the story where characters might try and ask for money or ask for a bribe, but this has no impact as there is no actual money in the game, which I thought was a bit strange. I would've liked if there were shops you could visit with actual products to buy from the time period that maybe grant some XP and/or give a temporary boost to a stat. I also would've liked if there were some minigames that could be played.Overall though, I enjoyed my time with the game. I would recommend playing the game completely blind and not looking up any guides as the game is best enjoyed when you don't know what's going to happen next. I would also recommend playing the game with Polish audio and English subtitles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I can assure everyone that this is a game with a lot of love put into it. It has a heavy focus on narrative and investigation, almost like a dark fantasy Sherlock Holmes. Lots to read (not mandatory but advisable) but incredibly relaxing. The music and flow of the game makes it play out like a movie. Combat could be more expansive but it fits the game, no problem. It is not a traditional RPG in the sense that you don't search for better equipment, for instance. But what it lacks in systems and resource gathering, it delivers in charm and presentation. Performance is good, albeit not perfect, and there are some places where collision wasn't figured out properly. Borderless apparently works with your monitor's resolution so pick that in case you use super resolution. Though it still shows the incorrect resolution under it, it is running at whatever resolution your monitor is set at.I hope more people try this so Fools Theory gets encouraged to do more of what this game does well!I'd love to see an action orientated game like the Witcher but in this style/world/setting. P.S. The salutors look awesome!Very happy with it! Try it out!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not far into the story yet but it's already obvious to me that a lot of love and care was put into crafting this world; it's beautiful and the attention to small details is impressive. The music is gorgeous and absolutely haunting, and I often find myself wondering what they used to create some of those sounds. Every little while I stop for a bit just to listen to it. Very atmospheric.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: In Act 3, you will be locked out of many converstations / content based on attribute points. This is weird, because in Act 1 and Act 2 you will be maxed out. Then, Act 3 begins, and you will get 0 extra points and all of the sudden you will not be able to pick most options in conversation. In other words, saving up a bunch of attribute points (i.e. not playing the game as intended, based on information you do not have yet) would have been the correct play. It's pretty annoying to just throw away 20+ hours like this, but I hate games where options are locked based on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Yes its janky, yes the animations look kinda scuffed, yes i ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love it. the setting, the whole detective system, the flaws, it seems llike they had a crackhead idea and decided to actually do something with it and the result is Thaumathurge, a lovely, decently voice acted RPG. Its 30 bucks, if you have them spare, you will not waste them on this game
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: This game is legit so good. Thaumaturge aims for an atmosphere, story and dialogues and man, all of them are 10/10. However it must be said that the *weakness* of Thaumaturge is it's technical execution. Cutscenes are sometimes laggy, textures are visibly rendering in the middle of a cutscene or while walking around the map. It slightly worsens the immersion, but not so much. I mean, considering it was just released the state is actually pretty good, much better than Witcher 3 and Skyrim during release lol. If you're looking for a game which is like Disco Elysium but with old-slavic planting, original combat system and less boring reading, this is it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty enjoyable game. i ran the graphics on medium settings and didnt experience many issues. The game play can become a little repetitive once you are in late game but the story is pretty cool. I found it pretty easy to level up as soon as i made it out of the starting area just by doing side quest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Disco Elysium it did my heart a lot of good to see an isometric choice-based RPG with political and psychological elements. That said, this doesn't come as close to Disco as I wish it did in terms of handling any of that. My biggest criticism is that the games 3rd act comes out of (almost) nowhere and feels very rushed, but overall I enjoyed the gameplay, VO, graphics, and unique setting muchly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like the Council ,if you like to experience incredible atmosphere of Warsaw, if you like the song Ra-Ra-Rasputin Russian sex machine - this game is for you .Great design , interesting quests , memorable npcs. And what is the most important nowadays : no grind , no micro transactions , no 100000 collectablesOf course there is some minuses: - some bugs here and there, but nothing critical - choices and dimension points not really matter . If you are not rushing the main quest , but doing sides and exploration , in the end of act 1 you can easily have all dimensions by 6 points , so nothing can hide from you .Nevertheless the Thaumaturge totally worth its price and will not let you go for couple of days . 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: History meets occultism.First off, this is to 90% a pure story-game. Anyone who likes to rush through games and doesn't care much about story, side-quests and reading should stay far away. This is not for you.Everyone who likes a good story, great world building and the bleakness of eastern-european storytelling and mysticism will feel at home here.Really I love this kind of story but it also always leaves me kind of depressed and feeling like the story shouldn't be over yet. I didn't quite understand the ending I got. Went really quick and politcal and then I got the boss-fight and the epilogue didn't really explain much more either. So that would kind of be a critique of me, but it also fits the afforementioned bleakness of eastern-european stories. Go look for a happy ending somewhere else.On other point: I liked that I kind of had to look for XP and they weren't just thrown at me. Discovering the game really was rewarded all the way around.The fighting system is really simple but also fun. Got a little bit hard halfway through the game for a few hours but towards the end it almost was a bit to easy sometimes. I only had to fight the end-boss several times because I was being stubborn.The graphics still has A LOT of issues, but this is a small studio and I could really look past that. But yeah towards the end there was a lot of, I don't know. tearing? Especially hair seems to be a big issue for the game. But as I said, for the price and what else I got out of the game, that really wasn't so bad.I might consider playing it again at some point and going for other decisions.Will definitely check out other games buy the devs if they make more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Ra-Ra-Rasputin, Pokemon Catching Machine Thaumaturge is a cool, atmospheric RPG. It doesn't babysit you, letting you make your own choices and mistakes. The story is great, you play as Wiktor, a thaumaturge with daddy issues. You explore the city, uncover secrets, and team up with your smelly friend Rasputin to catch esoteric beings.What makes it stand out is that it doesn't hand-hold you; you have to figure things out. The game's world is full of mysteries, and as you follow hints, you learn more about the city and its hidden stories.Thaumaturge isn't just about the story; the game's creators put a lot of effort into building an interesting world. The visuals and atmosphere draw you in, making the whole experience feel rich and exciting.In a nutshell, Thaumaturge is a game worth playing for anyone who loves a unique and immersive RPG adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Had eyes on it quite a while, unfortunately It's a disappointment for me. World has great potential, the graphics is good but the gameplay is boring. The game doesn't have any real dialogue choices or different ways to solve quests, the "investigation" part just horrendously boring, just follow the red line, click on the clickable, pick all dialogue, goes into combat, win and thats it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Quite liking it so far. I agree with some of the criticisms that have been thrown at it, namely the combat. However I haven't experienced any of the instability others have apparently had to deal with, no crashes at all for me thus far. Overall, I think it's worth the money and I'd recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is, without a doubt, one of the best games I’ve had the chance to play this year. It masterfully combines a mysterious, well-thought-out, and captivating narrative with meaningful choices and branching paths that keep you engaged throughout.The character development is both deep and rewarding, offering a unique approach through the concept of Salutors, which adds an intriguing layer to the gameplay. Every decision you make feels impactful, making replayability a highly enjoyable experience.The voice acting (Polish dubbing as well :)) is another standout feature, delivered at an exceptionally high level, enhancing the overall immersion and emotional connection to the story.With all my heart I recommend The Thaumaturge to anyone looking for a rich, story-driven experience with compelling mechanics. This game is a true gem that deserves recognition!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions are good. If you are a fan of Disco Elysium or Spiders games, this feels like a cross between the two. The graphics are solid, and the writing is EXCELLENT. Control support is well done, and besides the UI being slightly small, it plays great on a TV. The game splits its focus into two pieces; investigation and combat. While neither are particularly complex, they aren't too simple either. Investigation may feel thin at first, but the dialogue and writing are very enjoyable. Combat, too, is very fast to understand the mechanics but there is enough variation that unlocks as you play to maintain interest. (Obviously after my low play time I can't fully estimate the game length, but it seems perhaps the short side for the price.) If you like historical fantasy and RPGs, this is a great one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with surprisingly deep story and and choices which will change direction of your story. I was great surprise when i try it and was catch by it till the end. Recommending people which likes more adult story, lots of side stories (big and small ones) and to everyone who like to uncovering little secrets of normal people.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game if this is the type of game you are looking for. It's basically like reading a book with some turn based combat and light skill tree development thrown in. I thought the story was well done and touched on themes you don't see very often in a video game. I liked playing as Wiktor and directing his journey.On the downside, the game is overly padded with collectibles and made it just a bit too long. You will be constantly snapping your fingers to look for crap on the ground. You need the crap on the ground because it gives you XP leading to better stats, skills and modifiers. Crap on the ground does have written lore around it and adds to the atmosphere. Eventually though, I stopped picking up crap on the ground and visiting their associated quest destinations, and never made it to the end of the skill tree as a result. Some of the skills looked pretty cool, but I don't feel I missed out too much. I could have easily reached 30+ hours had I finished all those XP filler quests, but this game was wearing out it's welcome around the 20 hour mark and I beelined the mainquest from there.Also there was a horrible stutter throughout my playthrough. Assets seem to be constantly loading and unloading. My brain got used to it after a while but it needs to be fixed.Overall, cool game that I recommend if you like this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a turn based RPG in a while. But The Thaumaturge was a pleasant surprise.+Phenomenal voice cast.+Incredible art design, from the Salutors, to the buildings and environments. And overall just a pretty game to look at.+Musical score was lovely, from classical pieces, to wide array of instruments in the OST. It just fits the theme perfectly.+Side quests were plentiful, I think I finished a good amount if not all of them. +Multiple endings, choices made through dialogue trees throughout the game will either seal off different options, and while there is no new game plus. Multiple play-throughs can definitely bring different results.+Performance was great, had some minor stutters here and there. But beyond that no complaints.+Picking your Salutors in a battle and speccing your abilities will be crucial in many fights. Lots of planning in some cases.+Doing side content helps with XP and can level up all the varied skill trees.Overall if you're looking to play a story driven, turn based RPG that is situated in early 1900s Poland, with an interesting cast of characters, a decent battle system, give this one a try. Lots of value for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting hybrid between an RPG and an adventure. Amazing graphics music and soothing picture and color combinations. Interesting story. And very nice gameplay in the sense that you always know where you need to go and what you need to do next. It's not like other adventures that at some point you might get stuck and not knowing where to go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Look, all I'm saying is that the game has absolutely sucked me in. I watched a friend play a little bit of it and not two days later, I had to buy it for myself impulsively and now I'm utterly enamored. The minor characters are all fleshed out and the main ones are absolutely distinct from one another in terms of individuality. And the salutors? Each design is unique and different and I'm completely riveted by them. Get this game if supernatural detective work is up your alley. Get it even if it's not. I absolutely love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far, I am enjoying it the more I play. I disliked the combat system at first playing on "medium" difficulty, but when the first boss fight prompted me with the difficulty screen, I chose the hardest setting, and oh boy did I start loosing constantly. That's when I got the hang of the combat system and realized that I'm having way too much fun with it (that's my first time playing a game with this kind of a combat system).I am loving the story and the setting so far, mixing history with magic (fantasy I guess?) is a cool and an intriguing touch, especially in setting that I haven't seen in other games before, Russian-controlled Congress  of Poland, just before the "Russian Revolution of 1905". The story, lore (newspapers, letters, npc conversations and etc.) do make the setting more convincing, immersive and fun to play.Negatives:There are some bugs and crushes here in there, but nothing game-breaking. I do think that leveling up is too fast, I currently have 7 unspent points before catching the third salutor. I don't like that when roaming the world the NPC's just have subtitles on top of their head. For me, the world would be just a bit more immersive if they had voice acing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere with a classic feel to it.So far so good, the game is pretty inmersive and allows you to shape your own character through ingame decisions, plus you can max your character stats as you prefer.The game looks amazing, the characters are intriguing and Upyr remains the best boy while I would not trust Rasputin with my life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and I can absolutely recommend it. If you liked Vampyr and Black Book this game is for you. Pros:-The atmosphere of old occupied Warsaw-Salutors! (their designs are purely awesome) -Great voice acting, especially the main character -The whole plot with Rasputin-Engaging quests and stories-Nice graphics -I loved Wiktor's monologues, his inner thoughts and dialogues with Upyr Cons:-voice acting for children was meh-too short :< only +/- 20 hours of fun-some small side quests are boring and unnecessary IMO -REAL romantic side quest for Wiktor - there isn't one in the game and I was counting on itJust play it, you won't regret it. I will play it in the future again to make different choices and see what other endings I could get.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Its sad I have to honestly put a thumbs down. Obviously, the team had a creative vision, some good ideas for the atmosphere and setting, but did not have neither talent nor resources to create something interesting in a story-driven RPG genre. The story is boring. Its not AWFUL or IDIOTIC but you can just see the low writing and directing skill. Noir detective style stories are a trap - they have to be really captivating, smart and stylish to avoid boredom, detachment and walls of dull text. The "detective" part is trivial - you just click on an object of interest and solve all the mysteries. Hell, even old-school puzzles with levers and buttons are more engaging and actually require player attention. The RPG system is simplistic and barebones. The gameplay is painfully average, combat system is weak and reminds me of the tainted grail a little - even though there was a lot of emphasis on difficulty spikes, experimentation and deckbuilding, here we have like 1\5 of good old rusty tainted grail in terms of tactical combat and builds.Overall, its like... 5\10 just for the effort of a small team, maybe? Honestly after a couple of hours feels like even 4. Sorry guys, you tried!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the experience overall, but I can't recommend others play it if they're looking for a game that you're truly interacting with. The story, setting, and reactiveness of the world are all very nice and kept me engrossed enough to finish it, but the vast majority of the game play is nonexistent. If the investigative aspect of piecing together the snippets and cluse you stumble across was a more interactive experience rather than a passive point and click gather or otherwise expanded upon it would leed to this being an actual game, rather than more of a long interactive cut scene.I will add that while I don't believe that the combat system is bad overall, I do believe it could do with a bit more expansion in general. For the game length it was just a little too light when it was the vast majority of the actual gameplay in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I've been waiting for more updates, but nothing has ironed out the freezing issues I have on desktop. I eventually decided to play the game on my Steam Deck, as that did not have the stuttering or freezing issues. I was able to play for about 2hrs before one fight just crashed my Steam Deck, requiring I do a hard reboot. This is one of the most disappointing "Not Recommended"s I've ever had to make. No matter how I try to play the game, it just doesn't want me to finish it. There's so much to love here, but it's just not playable on any hardware I have.I had a big plan to write a review a few weeks ago for this when I finished. I absolutely loved what I've played of this game so far. The investigation stuff is a bit on rails, so it's more of an investigatory "experience" than puzzles of any kind, but the overall vibe and subject matter is real satisfying and feels very unique. I'm in love with just about every part of the game, despite its roughness around the edges.However, after reaching Chapter 3 (after the docks), my game just constantly freezes at random, and if it freezes during dialogue (which is a HUGE portion of the game), the audio cuts out until you restart the game. Unfortunately, this has made the game unfinishable for me. I've tried to push through because I love everything else about it, but even with patches and turning off scaling tech and capping frames to 75fps (all recommendations from the dev to cut down on rashes and freezes), my game is still freezing and killing my experience.This game is absolutely worth playing, but considering that there does not seem to be any fixes in sight yet, I cannot recommend it for fear that you may encounter similar issues as I have and not be able to play/finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic setting. Character models are beautiful. I'm inspired to play Wiktor as a Pathfinder character. These are all the good things about this game.Historical people's names are pronounced 3 different ways across as many sentences. Combat is dull, none challenge even on hardest difficulty. Dialog in English is jarring at best. I feel like I'm spending more time snapping my fingers and running around then I am actually investigating.I won't refund because I wanna support small studios. Hopefully if they get a chance to make another game in the setting they'll get the time to clean up and release a full product as opposed to crunch making something unfinished
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game. However, there is wasted potential. Because all the information you gather is automatically assembled, it takes away the intellectual puzzle. The combat is complex in theory, but most of the time it does not pay to pursue involved strategies. The game also crashed 4 times on me, forcing me to replay some sections.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: + Revolutionary Warsaw (1905)+ Mystical Slavic follkore+ Story richThaumaturge is detective game where you play as Wiktor Szulski, a Thaumaturge. Person with ability to perceive human emotions by touching their personal items. Set in historical period of 1905 Warsaw, when part of Poland was under Russian rule.The story is rich and morally complex, with a focus on player choices. The main character's ability to control magical entities, called Salutors, adds to mysticism and perfectly blends historical setting with Slavic folklore.Gameplay is pretty linear. Focused on exploring districts of Warsaw, searching for quest clues and ocassionaly fight. Combat is turn-based where you need to strategically plan your moves and utilize Salutors correctly. You improve your attributes and abilites which help you both in combat and conversations.What I enjoyed the most was immersive historical setting with occult vibe and ability to make impactful story choices which lead to different endings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you want a good narrative experience, and aren't super squeezed for time. If you are really busy and require something truly exceptional, I would take your picky demands elsewhere!WHAT IT'S LIKE PLAYING THIS GAME-(YOU CAN'T ROLEPLAY A CHUBBY TIEFLING PALADIN.) You play as WIKTOR SZULSKI, and only WIKTOR SZULSKI. Your WIKTOR SZULSKI might be different than my WIKTOR SZULSKI, but he is still WIKTOR SZULSKI. He is a quite-literally flawed aristocrat with a definite history. How you move forward with that history depends on the choices you make in the game. But you are very much inhabiting a specific role.-(It's in the ISOMETRIC STYLE.)But that is more of an aesthetic choice. The isometric style is more of a camera angle thing. There's no party to manage, or an inventory really, or even a shop. It's not that crunchy kind of game with lots of stats. You don't pick up metal boots that grant you .000003% more resistance to stuns. Your "inventory" is basically a really detailed journal where you store character biographies, quest goals, drawings, item descriptions, and blurbs from newspapers you can pick up and skim. -(It's WHACKIER than you probably think.)I don't know why, but I expected the game to be kind of grim and self-serious and sort of faux-philosophical and heavy with the Nietzsche quotes. And it's not like super cheery or anything--sad things happen; it takes place in 1905, which is 10 years before the apocalypse in European history. But there's kind of this zany undercurrent of humor throughout this whole thing. Nobody farts or anything. And nobody gets whacked in the nuts. But it's the sort of thing where you'll suddenly be in a fisticuffs with some big-nosed boozer, and you'll be all like, "Wait. Who the f#%$ is this guy????"-(YOU FOLLOW A RED TRAIL A LOT. You click on lots of items and read lots of short snippets.)There's a map and you travel around different sections of the city via old-timey horse and carriage. But you basically run around the streets of Warsaw in the isometric style and click on things to read. The things you click on can be hard to spot if you don't constantly use your Thaumaturge thumb-snap thing that makes sparkly red lights appear. -(THE COMBAT IS BIZARRE, IN GOOD AND BAD WAYS.)You'll be walking around and you'll see a posh lady sitting on a bench. You start talking to her, when out of no where, some Russian or Polish dwarf will intrude and start besmirching you. And suddenly you'll find yourself in a turn-based fistfight with like a triplet set of these Polish bums. One guy will smash you in the nose with his elbow and you'll lose like 11 health points. The next guy will shoot your guts out, but you'll only lose 2 health points from it.Unfortunately, the combat encounters can be pretty repetitive. There's a puzzle-like element to it where you have to plan ahead. But each encounter feels pretty much the same, except the major boss fights. But the major boss fights are not radically different from each other, and aren't that radically different from the usual encounters. Very pretty art with the boss battles, though.Once I adjusted the combat animations to "very fast," I enjoyed them and found them amusing.DID I EVER WANT TO QUIT THIS GAME?No. This game didn't have some long sewer level or underwater thing where I had to grit my teeth to just get through.WHY I THINK OTHERS MIGHT CLICK ON THE RED THUMB-They are very short on time and demand something absolutely exceptional. "Good" is not good enough for them.-They hate, hate, hate the combat and can't get past it.-It's a narrative adventure. It felt like I was reading a neat novella, and the world and gameplay brought it all more vividly to life. However, someone else might want to flip that balance between story and gameplay. They might be seeking great gameplay with a sprinkle of story to bring it more vividly to life. If you don't like the story, I don't think the gameplay is engrossing enough to keep you around. It's not one of those games where you can ignore the story just to mess around and engage with the mechanics.-If you play this on Steam Deck, the game might initially launch in Polish. You just gotta be patient and fiddle around in the settings until you find the language option for English or whatever.WHY I CLICKED ON THE BLUE THUMB-I didn't always understand what was going on. But I was intrigued by the story and legitimately wanted to see how it all played out at the end.-Great art all around.-I'm a goofy person, and I greatly appreciated the bizarre humor.-The setting is very unique and beautiful. I kind of felt like a time-traveling tourist. I don't think I've ever played a game in this setting before. As an American, it felt very foreign, and I loved that.-The quest for unlocking the sad mermaid Salutor lady was really awesome. The setting felt different than the other parts of Warsaw, and there was lots of rain and bizarre characters. It left a long impression. When I think back on this game, I'll definitely remember that whole section.-I loved the characters and felt like Wiktor Szulski was a real person. I purposely played this game as an arrogant jerk my first time around. And I'm bummed by the ending I got. I care enough about the characters to eventually do another more ideal run where I give everyone better endings.-I feel like I've gained something by having these characters and this world floating around in my imagination. It feels more like I've gained something neat, rather than that I've lost time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised with this game. At the moment, FPS drops horribly when you get into cutscenes and fight scenes. So, disable motion blur, and volumetric lighting, and it should do the trick. If I remember what I changed correctly. Firstly, the story is excellent. The voice acting isn't the greatest but it is certainly made up for in the story. Side quests are not over abundant but that is alright for this top down RPG. Based in Russia in the late 1800s, you play as a begotten son come home to discover some things have gone wrong. Not getting into the story, the combat can be challenging but it also gets heavily annoying which seems intentionally to delay the story line from progressing. You also cannot seemingly talk your way out of most of these fights. It seems no matter what you select, you will end up in a fight. There are not really a whole lot of in game mechanics that will leave you wondering, "what's next". The ones that are displayed in the prologue are pretty much the only mechanics available. You'd think that you'd get to manipulate more people based on the beginning, but that is not the case. There are a few ways to go about the ending, I won't spoil it. Regardless, I enjoyed the game and fully recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its many, many shortcomings the game has an atmosphere. The music score and the visuals are beautiful and well executed. Dark, sordid yet pleasantly calming somehow. That is the best and the only plus so far. Everything else is not so good. But atmosphere is a redeeming quality, so I'd give this game a  thumbs up.Major problem, however, the game keeps crashing. And crashing. And crashing. Making the game borderline unplayable and certainly disrupting the atmosphere.Dialogs are stuporous and mechanical. Though voice acting is not too bad, the texts themselves are lifeless. _childDocuments_.review: This one kinda crept up on me but I'm really glad I picked it up.A beautiful game packed full of detail for people willing to read. My first playthrough took me 19 hours. It's a game with a story to tell. That story is mixed in between the cutscenes and all the clues you'll gather. I should point out the word "clues" should be used loosely, you'll spend most of your time right clicking, following the red trail and looking for stuff to read; be it newspapers or letters that will add to the world building or items for you to pick up impressions from related to whatever quest you're on, which will open up conversation options and possible solutions to your current problem. I will say the game doesn't do a great job at quest order; you'll often find yourself hitting a wall with being able to interact with items because your level is too low and you'll need to progress in some side quests to unlock the ability to level further. Combat is fun and can be a challenge if you aren't prepared. Turn based with all kinds of options for you to work with. As you level you'll gain "upgrades" to place into your combat skills, i.e: You can add a %50 chance that your quick attack interrupts your targets turn, or adds a debuff.Your Salutors also have a vital role in combat; some enemies have traits that can do things like heal them every turn, or prevent any status effect from effecting them. To get rid of this you'll need to attack them with a specific Salutor. Once you've progressed along the story there are some crazy fighting styles you can pull off with the different Salutors. It was a lot of fun experimenting!tl;dr - You'll want to read everything you pick up to get the most out of the game. SAVE before combat. Don't ignore timed quests. Enjoy a great story.

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews There are various time machines, such as books, plays/TV shows, and as in this case, video games, that enable audiences to immerse themselves in historical moments in human history.. The Thaumaturge serves as a gateway to a turbulent period in an Eastern country that unfortunately brings to mind very present-day territory invasion events. While not its central theme, the narrative provides glimpses into life in Warsaw, Poland during the 20th century.In the first-person narrative of “The Thaumaturge,” we follow Wiktor Szulski, a man ensnared by the grip of pride, as he grapples with supernatural elements. These less positive characteristics of personal traits are classified as “Flaws” that draw the attention of supernatural entities known as “Salutors,” who seek to amplify negative traits to dangerous levels. Hailing from a lineage of thaumaturges, individuals with the ability to perceive and banish these entities from human hosts, Wiktor navigates the legacy of his family’s unique gift.Our protagonist, grappling with a troubled past marred by a fractured relationship with his father, who forced him to leave home at a tender age, embarks on a journey of self-discovery. He retraces his childhood roots, revisiting the very place where he came of age amidst the pages of his life story. Throughout the narrative, his brash demeanor finds explanation and validation in his exceptional abilities, setting him apart from his peers. Each Thaumaturge is only capable of wielding the presence of a single Salutor, with the risk of losing their grip on sanity. Yet, Wiktor stands as a remarkable exception, capable of wielding control over multiple entities that aid him, even amidst the tumult of combat scenarios within the storyline. Moreover, given the interactive nature of the title, various responses are tailored to accommodate the player’s individual perceptions to a certain extent.As the story unfolds, the opportunity arises to reconnect with past acquaintances of Wiktor, who have undergone notable changes over the years since their last encounter. Despite his reserved nature, it’s evident the warmth he holds for his sister and the bond he shares with Gregori Rasputin, the self-proclaimed holy man and influential political figure from the twilight of the imperial era. Employing his healing gift of hypnosis, Rasputin aids Wiktor in navigating the influx of new entities, thereby establishing himself as a crucial ally within the plot.The ambiance of “The Thaumaturge” masterfully encapsulates the era it depicts, capitalizing on an atmosphere thick with suspense and the anticipated tension of supernatural encounters. Indeed, it’s this immersive quality that held my interest not only in the conclusion of the main storyline but also in its secondary missions. Despite the abundance of text, some of which may seem tangential to the primary objective, players are tasked with gathering clues, reminiscent of the investigative prowess of Sherlock Holmes, to uncover the truth behind the unfolding events. Whether probing a murder, unraveling the schemes of nefarious groups, or delving into the “flaws” and correlating personality traits that attract the attention of “Salutors,” players are armed with the necessary information to choose their preferred course of action at any given moment. While the narrative remains linear, devoid of multiple outcomes as seen in titles like Sherlock Holmes, players must comb through the map for clues aided by Wiktor’s unique abilities, though the game itself ultimately guides the resolution of presented challenges. Thus, it falls solely upon the player to respond according to their inclinations, armed with foreknowledge of the case’s conclusion.Regarding combat mechanics, it offers a relatively straightforward turn-based system complemented by its striking graphical design, featuring nightmarish renditions of both enemy models and attack styles of each “Salutor.” Certain enemies may exhibit buffs that can be countered with specific attacks from various “Salutors.” Generally, the gameplay doesn’t pose significant challenges, even on higher difficulty settings. However, there are instances where the difficulty spikes considerably, particularly during encounters with bosses, creating disproportionate challenges.It’s noteworthy that the significance of “Salutors” extends beyond combat to map exploration. Players may encounter clues inaccessible without reaching a certain level of Thaumaturgy dimension. The skill tree, categorized into four distinct paths—”Heart,” “Mind,” “Deed,” and “Word”—is intricately connected to each Salutor. To enhance abilities and elevate the level of one’s specific dimension, players must allocate experience points acquired from both combat and exploration of the map.The Thaumaturge adeptly presents a captivating narrative that unfolds gradually, offering rich historical context complemented by striking graphics. However, occasional performance and graphical issues, including NPCs overlapping and repetitive face and model designs, can occasionally detract from the immersion. Despite these shortcomings, addressing these rough edges could transform this title into a significant milestone within its genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, The Thaumaturge has some performance jank. The animations can be a little stiff and there are some visual bugs at times. So far, I've only had one actual crash, though. And at the time of writing this review, I've played for 35 hours. Some people have said this is a point and click walking simulator or even a pixel hunting kind of game. Which, I don't understand where that's coming from. But, I will say that if you're struggling to see the "Hey, look at this!" visual, then you may be somewhat colorblind. I don't mean that as a slight. The sparkly effect is mostly red. But it is noticeable and gets moreso when you snap and/or get closer to where the object is. Maybe tweak the colorblind mode and see if that helps. This game is an RPG with turn-based combat. You don't change your stats via equipment as in some RPGs, but you do change your attack effects via your choice in salutor actions and adjusting things that modify the attack chains you have access to. An attack could inflict max damage every time. Or double damage (or more) based on other factors. Or, maybe an attack will have a chance to negate an enemy action when a status is applied. There is a LOT of customization in how you set up your combat flow. So the reviews saying the combat is simple are apparently playing a different game. Or maybe they stopped before the more difficult effects and combat modifiers were introduced. As for the flavor and story, this game has it in spades. This alternate 1905 Warsaw is rich in life. It feels very lived-in: with all the beauty and misery that comes with it. It is nearly equal parts lush and gritty. The textures in this game are just so good. The high-class areas feel like appropriately posh, with an edge of tension with the occupying Russian guards watching from a distance. And, the down and dirty poverty-stricken areas feel outright squelchy and you can almost smell them. It may not feel like it as much early on, but your actions absolutely do have weight. There are several with potentially devastating outcomes. Allies may be made or lost depending on your choices. And, of course, how much Pride you cultivate throughout will also affect the story. You may get beat up a lot more if you're a smarmy, uh, jerk. While I understand that this game won't sit well with everyone, I do think that its current "Mostly Positive" is a bit unfair. This game has a lot of charm and I definitely recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is an RPG set in Warsaw in the early 20th century while it's under Russian occupation and with elements of otherworldly beings and paranormal added in. We play as Wiktor Szulski, who is a thaumaturge, that is since childhood he had special powers involving otherworldly perception of places and objects and ability to interact with otherworldly beings known as Salutors. After his father passes away, Wiktor has to delve both into the criminal underworld and the high society of Warsaw in order to uncover what his father was planning and how it's tied to the political situation in the city.I think a setting such as this (early 20th century Eastern Europe) is rare to see in games, and so it's quite refreshing and unique. The game uses events and characters from history and adds some of its own elements to develop its plot and characters. Wiktor is an interesting character to play as, because he isn't exactly a hero who strives to do the right thing. Most times he's in it just for himself, and depending on our decisions, we can be either just a mild annoyance to others or a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Usually dialogue choices where we act arrogantly or inflame the situation are associated with the Flaw of Pride which Wiktor is carrying, and developing our pride can unlock new dialogue options later on, turning Wiktor into a different kind of person.The plot tries to take us into multiple directions at once, which I felt made it seem a bit all over the place. Of course the setting is highly interesting, with the Russian empire pursuing its own interests, Polish nationalists and insurgents seeking to fight back, criminal gangs trying to profit from chaos and uncertainty, and also other thaumaturges having their own personal stake in the situation. Then there's also Rasputin, a well-known historical figure who was said to possess otherworldly powers. There are many interesting factions and characters at play here, but I feel that the plot sometimes bounced back and forth between them too abruptly and chaotically, and I thought some of those needed more time to cook and develop. Some parts of the story, particularly the parts near the end, felt a bit too rushed and anticlimactic. I suppose in some sense, the game is more mature in its story and not everything is solved through violence and big battles, and that you can conclude your story and get the ending through dialogue alone, but in another sense, it seems to lack that feeling of high stakes and adrenaline.The gameplay consists of several aspects that you'd expect in an RPG. There's exploration of environments and detective work, there are dialogues with choices, there are skill trees, and there is combat. The combat is entirely turn-based, and I personally enjoyed it. It's not a super sophisticated battle system, and most fights aren't hard, but it is fun and allows for plenty of experimentation as we get to unlock many bonuses which we can apply to our attacks. When in combat, we usually have the Salutors assist us, so it's not just Wiktor alone fighting. We can only have one Salutor helping us at any one time, but we can swap between them at will. This is important because enemies often have buffs and bonuses, and using specific Salutors against them can remove those bonuses and make the enemy weaker. Each Salutor also has unique attacks, so swapping between them is useful depending on the situation. This is especially true for when we need to self-heal or cleanse ourselves off negative states, because there are no potions or other items to use. We can only rely on our Salutors for everything!The combat is plentiful and often unavoidable when it occurs, but the game is by far not riddled with it every minute. There are many slower-going parts in the game where we have to partake more in detective work by scanning the environment for clues and making conclusions, and also dialogues with characters and make decisions on what to say and how to come across. Often we can even use our mystical powers to manipulate people too to get things our way. Availability of these depend on how we level up the skill trees.For most of the game we can also explore parts of Warsaw city, find things in the environment that give us experience points, such as newspapers, letters, posters, etc. At times we can uncover sidequests. These can help us not only in gaining extra experience points, but also in developing trust with certain characters and even finding some of the Salutors (some of these we get through story missions, while others are optional and are gained only through sidequests). It can be tricky to find some of the sidequests though. I missed two Salutors in my playthrough and only in the ending narration realised that there were two sidequests that I somehow missed and didn't know about. Wish it wasn't so obscure to find some of them.The music is generally nice. I particularly enjoyed the battle theme and found it to be quite catchy. The game is fully voice-acted and the voice acting is pretty great for all characters, even the minor ones. The visuals of the places we visit are well-crafted and atmospheric. The characters visuals are also decent enough, and the UI and menus are great. The only issue I have though is that the game seems to be pretty graphically demanding, even though it doesn't look like it should be. Even with a good graphics card, you can expect your PC to start heating up and making jet engine noises after just half an hour of playing. At first I thought maybe I misjudged my PC's ability to play this game, but seems there are other people who have had this issue too. So be aware that the game can be more demanding on your PC than what you might expect from isometric or top down games.Generally, I think The Thaumaturge is a decent RPG with a very interesting historical setting and characters, and a plot that can feel a bit rushed and underdeveloped in places, but generally good and worth experiencing. It offers a varied gameplay experience and isn't focused solely on combat and solving things with violence, although that is a necessary aspect in many parts of the game. I'd recommend the game on a discount, especially if you're unsure and on the fence about it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is a captivating RPG set in early 20th-century Warsaw under Russian occupation, blending historical intrigue with supernatural elements. You play as Wiktor Szulski, a thaumaturge with extraordinary abilities to perceive and interact with otherworldly beings known as Salutors. Following his father’s death, Wiktor delves into both the criminal underworld and high society of Warsaw, seeking to unravel his father's plans and their connection to the city's political turmoil.The game shines in its unique setting—a rare and refreshing backdrop that vividly depicts the complexities of Warsaw during a tumultuous period. The fusion of historical events with the fictional elements of Salutors and Thaumaturges adds depth and intrigue. The plot, though rich in potential, can sometimes feel chaotic and rushed, with abrupt transitions between various factions and storylines. Despite this, the narrative offers a mature approach to storytelling, where dialogue and decisions can shape outcomes, often eschewing straightforward violence for a more nuanced resolution.Gameplay in The Thaumaturge includes exploration, detective work, dialogue choices, and turn-based combat. The combat system is enjoyable, if not highly sophisticated, allowing players to experiment with different Salutors and their abilities. The use of Salutors in battle—along with their unique attacks and the ability to swap between them—adds a strategic layer to encounters. However, combat can become repetitive, and the dialogue options to avoid fights often feel ineffective.Exploration is a significant part of the game, with opportunities to uncover sidequests and gather experience points from the environment. Although the setting is well-crafted, some sidequests and Salutors can be elusive, making them difficult to find without thorough investigation. The game's music is engaging, particularly the catchy battle theme, and the voice acting is commendable across all characters.Visually, the game is atmospheric with well-designed environments and decent character visuals. However, it can be graphically demanding, even for well-equipped PCs, leading to potential performance issues.Overall, The Thaumaturge offers a compelling experience with its intriguing setting and varied gameplay. While it has its flaws, including a sometimes disjointed plot and a demanding graphical performance, it’s a worthwhile RPG for fans of story-driven games and historical settings. If you’re on the fence, waiting for a discount might be a good idea, but the game’s unique qualities make it worth considering.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Outstanding historical fiction plot- Well-blended crime, horror, fantasy, and occult aspects- The setting's moral ambiguity gives players a lot of freedom to immerse in and define the protagonist- Impressive multi-cultural and multi-linguistic character writing- Fantastic dialogue, with a few funny contemporary references here and there- Sweet detective mechanics, SO much flavor text everywhere- The visuals are all-around nice- The collectibles felt worth gathering (mostly for the clothes)*Felt like Persona 3-5 or Pokemon Colosseum & XD: Gale of Darkness mixed w the dark, gritty, mature ambiance of Assassin's Creed and Metro*Cons:- Isometric camera turns a beautiful setting into staring at cobblestones and dirt- Repetitive combat, and the boss battles are just waves of grunts where the bad healing mechanics are the biggest threat- There's no loot / gear to justify grinding all the grunts, just EXP, and I don't think I needed many of the levels I gained from Acts 2 or 3 to comfortably beat the game- Open world gets exhausting, lots of running back and forth, Wiktor could use a horse or a bike for sure- Not enough Salutors? Or too many w no customization options? They are given more narrative weight, like catching only legendary Pokemon, but their move-sets are all double-edged swords and constantly swapping between them to use the decent moves is annoying- Lots of hidden values for an RPG. This was especially worrisome for me with the Pride dialogue mechanic- Seemingly minor choices will ruin the protagonist's life (but that's realistic af and replay value too tbh)*Better writing than Vampyr, and better game mechanics than Greedfall, but reminded me of both at points; and a few things towards the ending reminded me of Call of Cthulhu*Overall:I'd replay it, and happily play a sequel in the same universe. But right now it's a solid 7 or 8, and I want to see it at 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It was a lot of fun. i beat it last night and stayed up way too late to do it. The story was very interesting. The characters were amazingly wrote. I enjoyed every tidbit of information i read, it was really immersive. It was exciting finding all the clues and exploring the areas. Each area having its own unique feel and charm alongside the people who inhabited them. I found all 8 salutors... do your sidequests ;). I had favorite moves for each. The turn based fights never got repetitive. I enjoyed the puzzleness to them and the animations that followed. Wiktor had a lot of funny one liners and you just wanted to keep stroking his pride to hear them. I enjoyed the dialogue and its interesting as an English speaker to hear different terms and ways of saying things. It kept the feel of it being in the past. There were a lot of tough choices to pick through, some minor that you learned later on had consequences. The end fight was really fun and challenging. It definitely felt like the main boss fight.This leads the game to be replayed to see it all especially with multiple endings. If you want a secret... you cant get every single thaum skill which i enjoyed learning a little too late. This isnt to say there arent bugs.. there are but they are no big deal... some subtitles are off from whats being said, some animation issues like a weird head shake in cut scenes that goes away quickly, & props sometimes clipping... it happens. There was only one fight i couldnt do because it wouldnt transition from the conversation to the fight.. i just got a black screen (fight with some sailors that had ladies with them). That's really the only thing i couldnt do.I would love to see the other flaws you take on have their own dialogue options. That would be really neat and immersive. It felt like they really had no consequences or meaning to them. Some gave you stat bonuses or buffs but they were just kinda there no matter how many you took on.. only your main one really mattered. I did enjoy the main flaw having its own invisible meter which locked out or made available dialogue options. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game, and big surprise. I was initially interested when the game was first announced but didn’t follow it too closely until it came out. Between the setting, the characters and the gameplay focus in finding hints and deductions, I kept thinking of it as “Sherlock’s Creed”, reminding me both of AC Syndicate and the Sherlock Holmes games from Frogware which I love. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game so badly. If it were a novel or a TV series, it might be one of my favorites. But it just isn't much of a game. Most of the game is detective work, but there's no thought required at all. Every quest points you directly to where you need to go and tells you exactly what you need to do. Wiktor solves mysteries--the player does not solve mysteries *as* Wiktor. NPCs pick fights with you for the most minor of things, and the combat is unstimulating and ultimately sort of a chore outside of boss fights. The salutors and combat upgrade system are interesting, but ultimately combat is easy enough that you don't really need to put much care into your build.The concept is interesting. The detail in newspapers, posters, idle chatter, etc. are very well done. Pre-WW1 Poland is an wonderful and engrossing setting. The game just isn't interactive enough for me. I'll probably finish it at this point, but if I could go back in time I probably wouldn't buy it in the first place.
