_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed this game more than I'd anticipated, it was quite a surprise from a title that had so little publicity or word of mouth after it.The setting of the The Thaumaturge is one of its best qualities, unique in the sea of fantasy and sci-fi themed CRPGs; I don't think I'll find another game set in early 20th century Poland any time soon.At its core it's a story about political intrigue and family issues, shrouded in occultism and slavic folklore. It's a more down to earth and personal affair compared to the world-ending scenarios that mire the genre.The graphics are better than most top-down RPGs, and there was a good amout of care put into translating this version of Poland faithfully.It plays like your standard turn-based JRPGs, think a streamlined and westernised version of SMT, and while the system isn't complex several fights kept me on my toes before I eventually mastered the quirks of its rules. Thankfully, no random encounters this time.The game, surprisingly enough, is fully voice-acted. I didn't think it would be at first, even so I still can't quite grasp if Wiktor is meant to sound tired or simply detached from his surroundings most of the time.The rest of the cast is mostly adequate, I especially liked the bombastic theatrics of his childhood friend; a stark contrast to the mostly dour and belligerent common folk and police of Warsaw.Recommended if you're looking for an RPG that is willing to explore a different setting and cast than your usual RPGs do, I will also add that it feels replayable and reactive to your choices, at least on a surface level.I hope for more from this universe now, even outside of a direct sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute joy to play, the gameplay is delightful, I love running around and solving mysteries. I really like the story as well, it's intriguing and sucked me right in. My favourite part is absolutely the setting. It genuinely feels like I'm transported to early 20th century Warsaw every time I boot up this game, showing its beauty as well as its grimness and grittiness. The realities of the time period are excellently presented. I've wanted a game to dive into the city of Warsaw for ages, and The Thaumaturge delivers that in style.The only negative thing I could say about the game is the lack of a Polish voice-over option, but according to the developers' answers to similar questions, it may be an option in the future, so I will gladly look forward to that possibility .

_childDocuments_.review: This easily becomes one of my GOTY contenders. Very atmospherically set in the turmoil of Russian and Polish history, in a rather sinister re-model of Warsaw city in 1905, The Thaumaturge scratches many itches for me. I like the tingling remembrance of reading Kafka or E.A. Poe's short stories, or even Proust and E.T.A Hoffmann of that era, when diving into this game’s version of central European age of industrial revolution. What the Thaumaturge maybe lacks in character models, animation and maybe some AAA deluxe treatment, it generously makes up with its superb overall art Style, its interiors and overall atmosphere. I really enjoyed the writing, the story and side missions and the great characters. There is some stellar monster design to be found here and a really deep and enjoyable mythological horror rpg experience.I also want to recommend the playful and surreal Soundtrack from Agnieszka Wlazły and Sebastian Syczyński. It's marvellous.

_childDocuments_.review: This year started off like this - games I had high hopes for disappointed me, while those I approached with caution turned out to be pleasant surprises. From the latter category emerged "The Thaumaturge," created by just five people.To explain what the game is about... um...Imagine Poland in 1905. Pressured by the Russian Empire, torn apart by socialist uprisings, and plagued by thriving criminal gangs. Poverty, misery, violence, corruption.Now, add a dash of magic in the form of thaumaturges - people with the ability to read the thoughts and emotions of others, and to control spiritual beings called "salutors," whose powers they can influence others with through tricks, quite reminiscent of Jedi. And of course, these thaumaturges don't live in peace with each other. Oh, and there's also a proto-Nazi organization that wants to exterminate them.So in this world, you seek your place under the sun - Victor (with a double W) Zshulski, heir to a financial empire, a man with a dark past and an unclear future, and yes - a thaumaturge from a family with centuries-old traditions in magic.Your job (aside from, well, surviving) is... um... complicated.Overall, the fate of Warsaw, all of Poland, and perhaps the entire world depend on you, but while you deal with global problems, you still have time for smaller ones. Like catching a serial killer, stopping a sadistic usurer, saving the lover of the Russian czar fleeing from authorities, and finding out where exactly they sell that notorious American drink, Coca-Cola.Seriously though, the game is cool. The mix of criminal investigations, "choices matter" storytelling, and (don't laugh) Pokémon is entertaining. For at least 30 hours, which is how long it took me to reach one of the few possible endings.It's not perfect.The graphics are slightly rough, some of the voice actors sound like they've had 1-2 extra shots of vodka before recording, and besides, even on the highest difficulty, the battles are too easy.But it's worth it. Definitely a chance to play it again, as well as to buy the (very likely) sequel.Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Good game, not perfect, doesn't need to be. I am having a great time, but I would like to see a little bit more done with it.While only about 12 hours in, and not sure how far into the main story I am, I do want to say that I think this game is great. Making a new IP is difficult, especially in our current age of sequelitis and reboots out the ass, and making something like this is no small feat. Games are hard, who knew?Fool's Theory have done a really solid job making this city feel lived in. It's no Night City, but maybe that's for the best. All the little Points of Interest, the sketches and fashion magazines and incidental moments (like being ogled by women on the street), framed against this deeply intriguing story that blends history with fantasy, makes The Thaumaturge's depiction of Warsaw feel very much alive.The detective mechanics, while simple and not exactly rewarding for the exceptional snoop (all the clues and conclusions being drawn for you), do provide meaningful interaction and the simple fact the game TELLS YOU when you have locked yourself out of certain choices makes it narratively satisfying, even if it's a little repetitive in execution. On that point, one thing I would've loved to see is more use of the Visions Upyr bestows upon you, perhaps featuring the other wild Salutors; giving us greater immersive context into the people we are investigating. Someone like Abaurycy or Vesna would have been perfectly used for this.I think Rasputin's presence in the game, while entertaining and welcome, is a little shoehorned in. If he was a persistent accompaniment to Wiktor, instead of another location on the map of Warsaw, with more input on the story, i think I would buy his presence in the game much more. But again, I'm only 12 hours in and I've been distractedly running around looking for fashion magazines and laughing that the game has no clean-shaven options at the barber.As far as combat, it's perfectly serviceable. I do think, however, that the thaumaturgy points are awarded MUCH too freely; even reading repeated advertisements or articles that do not provide anything for quest objectives give experience; I have maxed out my Heart and Deed trees (up until the second Salutor) and I only just acquired the third Salutor in the entire game. Given that there appears to only be a total of 8 Salutors, and I still feel rather early in the story, I find myself rather worried I will max out my skill tree and have nothing to try out next time I play this game. Plus, playing on the hardest difficulty I still find myself steamrolling most enemies simply through abusing Suffering and interruptions; enemies simply don't deal enough damage to be threatening enough, and certain combinations of attacks are simply far too powerful. I would like a future update that expands combat a little more, especially since the majority of the actual fight seems-- unwieldy. Mostly fisticuffs with the occasional revolver shot against people with knives, guns, and even full-ass swords.Most of the music also feels relatively unremarkable as well; not that it doesn't serve it's purpose, it's very immersive, but even the main menu theme doesn't have anything that makes me want to whistle or hum with it. It's rather tragic because I think a game like this could really shine with a strong soundtrack. You have things like the Hurdy-Gurdy, the Balalaika, the fiddle, all featured in the game, I think using instruments like that more prominently for the music would do wonders.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A capitvating take on creature-capture games in a wonderful setting.Since I'm both Polish and a Warsaw enthusiast this game sprang onto my wishlist immediately after playing the demo last fall. Got it a couple of days after release to see how the launch went and hopped in. The setting is wonderful. 1905* Warsaw in all it's glory. Despite liberties and abstractions made for gameplay every single district is recognizable. There's also some tasty lore and easter eggs for those in-the-know which I appreciated greatly. The setting is wonderful and dips heavily into beasts from folklore not unlike the Witcher. The only thing I can complain about is that Warsaw wouldn't get electric trams until 1908 in the real world but since everyone loves trams I'll let it slide. The setting literally made me buy this game and I got my money's worth.Gameplay is solid though nothing to write home about. The main char uses his powers to unveil secrets and solve mysteries thugh the player is being led by hand too much. Wiktor always draws conclusions himself and only a couple of quests allow you to interpret things your way.I played on normal and combat has this weird curve where I enjoyed in the beginning and end but had a lull in the midgame where you're not that powerful nor do you have many options among your salutors to torment your enemies and it boggles down to doing the exact same sequence in every encounter. Encounters are also, unfortunately, very repeatable outside of boss fights.Main storyline is interesting but a lot of the side-content fell flat. Two "freeroam" chapters include about 2-3 real sidequests of varying but never exceptional quality and the most interesting part are the salutor captures.I finished the game at close to 30h of usually good fun. Probably did too much collectibles unitl I realized getting sketches boils down to a boring right-click spam for clues and then going to a locations where the screen turns black and you see a sketch. This I felt was unnecessary and leaned heavily on my enjoyment of the game until the end of chapter 2. All in all a solid 8/10 for me. Would recommend even without a sale as the game is fairly priced for what you get out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: This is clearly a story-telling game with a rather slow pace. If you are into these, you can experience an interesting, mildly scary story in a "historicized" setting. You even may learn a thing or two about the time, i.e. early 20th century, and Poland.Dialogues are really good and the music perfectly supports all the scenes. The turn-based fights are mostly easy, once you get the hang of it. Overall, a cool concept.As a welcome distraction from other, more flashy (action) games, I very much enjoyed playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game-design, story set in Warsaw 1905. Narrative, plot, and setting are so well done that it actually made me interested in the political and cultural history of this period. Somewhat buggy, for me the sound of speech disappeared a few times. Had to restart the game to get it back. Eventually, it worked just fine. I definitely recommend following a guide for collectibles achievement wise, because two play-throughs are more than enough. Otherwise, you’ll get pretty tired of endlessly clicking on objects and all the reoccurring fights (learned this the hard way). Nevertheless, I did appreciate the originality of the game-design. Recommended to buy and play but as always it’s not for everyone; some patience is needed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game a positive review : I love the setting and the core idea, but the pacing is a disaster. It's definitily one of the most boring experience I ever had in a RPG.The gameplay loop is awful : you run around, spamming the button to snap your fingers, reading an absurdingly high amount of random boring documents to get XP. Then, to resolve quests and investigations, you run around snaping your fingers looking for clues, then the investigation is automatically solved and that's it.Here is another shining example of a game that thinks that gathering clues is the fun part of an investigation. It's not. At all. Deduction is.Story may be interesting but it is drowned under thousands and thousands of useless lore documents. After 1 hour in the game, all the excitement is gone when you find something. After 2 hours, all the excitement is gone. Period.I didn't like the combat as well, it's pretty dull for turn based combat... The add-ons management is also really annoying... So many useless work for so little...
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Game has it's flaws. It crashes, has graphical artifacts and issues. May seem confined at times. But it is incredible atmospheric and unique. You are drowned in early XX century Poland, at the edge of incredible political and historical changes (Prior to WW I and partitioned between Russia, Austo-Hungarian empire and Germany). Beautiful work was done to depict the time, social complexity, many cultures and nationalities in one spot fighting for their influence, and Warsaw in its unique style specific for that time period. You can believe this was "The Paris of the eastern Europe". Nicely rooted in Slavic mythology and spirituality which makes it unique gem among other games of this kind. To be fair it is a detective story with magical arch and mechanic comparable to games like Disco Elysium in game play mechanics. I pity that there is no Polish audio in the game as this would add to the game style and feel especially that dialog written in Polish use specific for 1900's Warsaw street slang called 'gwara'. Story is very nice and engaging. Based on family secrets in historical perspective. For interested parties (Works well on SteamDeck - could be optimized better. Around solid 30 FPS) + Incredible feel of the period+ Storytelling that is complex and not dumbed down.+ Good mechanic+ Rooted in Slavic mythos+ Great choice of historic period which is not often depicted+ Price to content ratio+ Good flow with focus on story. Not too difficult making it easy to immerse yourself.+ No woke BS overflowing even though respectful for all kinds of views and perspectives. - Graphical glitches- Crashes (3 in 6 hours of gameplay, hope to be solved after patches)- Pity you have fixed camera angle and can't turn it around (it is 3D space after all)- Graphic is nice but not stunning. - May be too historically complex for people used to simple stories and good-bad narratives.Not a masterpiece, but a nice little gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid 7/10. Really loved the unique setting, both in the historical sense with pre-war Poland with all of its players and the magic system. I also loved the monster designs and the idea of the protag being a demonhunting detective. The game is very pretty even tho the animations can be a bit janky.I was a bit stressed by the timegating the quests, its very frustrating to see I just missed a quest (even tho the game says when a quest is about to run out). The side quests, esp the Warsaw stories were a bit eh, I really wished there were more of real side quests like the "Real Fireworks" one.Plus the detective stuff is very hand-holdy, pls let me figure it out by myself maybe with the help of the salutors, but that would be a very cool core for the next iteration of this game!I would really love to see a sequel were the devs can improve on the game and push the 7 to a 9:)
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoy the storyline there is WAY  too much point and click going on.  The quests tend to all end abruptly and are not that enjoyable.  They basically end with you going to the end of the quest and looking at a sketch......Art work is good though so if you can plow through the quests and make it to the end great.  Lots of achievements to get so I am working on those but the desire to finish quests diminishes quite quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game for those looking for a meaty story, a large cast of interesting characters, and some RPG-related battles thrown in. The story and your choices to affect the story are key here, make no mistake, and if you are expecting numerous customizable options like a Balder's Gate you will be disappointed. But that is not what this game's goal is. This is a meaty story for adults, plain and simple - it is thought provoking, challenging, and dark in relation to its themes. It is a real historical world, yet not, and yet it feels as if you are creating a world in that time period. There are, however, very funny moments and moments you will cry- a testament to the writing in this game.The visual style is one of my favourite things about this game which kept me coming back for more. The detail is amazing and I love the top down approach. It's a bit Disco Elysium and that's a good thing to keep your perspective on the city you are running through. The gameplay is very balanced throughout, only a couple of battles I had to redo 10 times to get through but with practice it is satisyfing to push through and win. The detective/search scenes are fairly straightforward, and some people have critisised as maybe too easy but for the length of the game and the pacing I had no problem with this.Overall, this is a gem of a game - great story, hard achivements (to get them all on one go), beautiful artwork and great characterisation. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game! its got a few rough edges but nothing i would call a flaw or that detracts from the game, more that i can see the potential of this dev team. im only in act 2 but im starving or more content, i want to know and do everything in this rich and beautiful world. the voice acting occasionally isnt great but hey thats what the skip button is for. i went in on easy mode, timid of the combat system, but the rhythm feels great and has me eager to get into the meat of the mechanics. i love the characters, and can tell that all of the modeling and environments were done with such love! my only wishes are, in order of easiness of achievement, to someday get more varied cosmetics, maaaaybe to patch out the jarring american accents on background characters, and for more and more games in this world!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: 35bucks is too much for this... at its core, this game is an isometric point-&-click game with turn-based combat. It's like Slay the Spire's combat, with a collectathon game's gameplay. You spend 80% of the time running around using your 'scan' ability just clicking on various pages/books/items until you've collected them all, and then you get a turn-based battle... then you rinse and repeat ad nauseam. The game is narrative-focused and has lots of voiced cutscenes (with above-average voice acting), which breaks the monotony of running around clicking on collectables, but asking 35bucks for this is crazy. The game runs like trash, and you can't change the resolution of the game when playing on borderless fullscreen, plus there is no resolution scaling options AND you can't set the framerate either. This isn't a bad game, but it's crazy asking $35 for a game that is this basic. If you want a good isometric turn-based game, then instead look at something like Disco Elysium, Wasteland 3, or DOS2 which you can get on sale for less than $15.My first 150minutes with the game: For more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: A very climatic adventure game with tons of collectibles about historical Warsaw. The environment and storyline are pushing the overall score to 10/10, while character progress and fighting are dragging it down to 7/10. Side-quests were my favorite part of the game - nice writing there, mates!Graphic is just enough. Nothing too bad, nothing too good. It's unique, which makes you forget about issues here and there....Some notes after finishing the first playthrough:- Please rework the character skill-tree to be more meaningful to the story and distinctive. Right now, I just dump my exp into some characteristics, which do not really impact anything. Having a high Heart gives access to better skills and some dialogue options, but so do others. Give me a real choice that describe my character's progress. Disco Elysium might be a good inspiration on how to make interesting character development even in a completely non-fighting game.- Please, remove 90% of unnecessary fights. Even though they are dynamic, they are boring. This game looks like it is advertising a punch in the face as the best option to resolve any situation. I get the idea, but sometimes less is better.- Majority of quests are tagged as time-limited, which makes the unnecessary feel of urgency. Please tone it down, or explain better how the time passes.- Some QoL around finding clues on the streets, that not require using the 6th sense constantly?- Do I really have to collect everything? Exp is necessary to get skills and then salutors, which are needed to get better salutors and some advantages during dialogues. It's the GET THAT DAMN POSTCARD all the way, isn't it?Overall, the game lacks depth in its current state, but it is a perfect ground for improvement. I expect more from this world. DLC's with new engaging stories or new iterations of thaumaturges. Let me pick myself a salutor and a flaw, and put me in the middle of some interesting drama.Thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Recommended for RPG fans who like lots of dialogue and reading.Advantages:Good story and an interesting setup.Interesting turn-based combat.Cool audio design - very immersive and atmospheric.Fine writing.Nice art.Flaws:Combat starts being challenging after a few hours of gameplay. Earlier it's a little bit boring.Lack of gameplay in isometric exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, I love any creature collector and went in for the game to collect some demons, ended up learning a little bit of history. The setting is very interesting and I find the character very engaging. I did see a few graphical bugs, but not too distracting. There are multiple ways to solve a problem and I definitely plan on returning to see a different ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: First impression: It is great. Interesting characters, fine environment and to put an "modern" witcher into the 1900s is a dope idea. The Storytelling reminds me of Vampyr (which was also great) and the combat reminds me of Ruined King: A League of Legends Story. I experienced minor bugs, but one of them had me to restart the game. Sounds annoying but it isnt, cause the autosaving in this game is S tier. For the first hour it seems like a good buy and I cannot wait to see what will happen in the next chapter. (Go buy it now)
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Thaumaturge offers a rich world and engaging characters, with excellent acting that enhances the experience. However, the combat can feel tedious and repetitive. Despite this flaw, I still recommend the game, especially if you can snag it at a discount. RPG enthusiasts will find much to enjoy, though additional endings and a New Game Plus feature could enhance replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: It’s janky, sometimes the textures feel off, and the bug where you’re stuck in your menu but can hear your character moving around is fun.That being said it’s very fun, the detective aspects are a joy and the combat is definitely some of the more fun in a turn based I’ve experienced. Definitely recommend this one
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually the sort of person who pushes through buggy/janky games hoping they will get better.  I just couldn't with this.The only positive thing I can say is the graphics are quite nice.  I actually spent about an hour or so trying to play this but the screen shaking in cut scenes and the game just locking up every 5-10 minutes killed it for me.When it wasn't doing this the gameplay is the most simplistic and unsatisfying you can imagine, it felt like little more than clicking on obvious things.  The story is very dry and lacks personality and the voice acting feels like everyone just recorded their scripts without ever interacting with each other.With all that said i didn't see much of it, it might get better but other reviews suggest it doesn't and for a game that is this simple, and has been a few months now to be so horrendously buggy when it doesn't even look that interesting, I couldn't be bothered to spend any more time on it.I attempted a refund.  It was refused, but that's my fault I should have tried it within 14 days of buying it especially as I was a bit sceptical about it.  Lesson learned.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The game was like being a magical detective. I enjoyed the exploration aspect of the game. I enjoyed the characters and the fact that I could choose dialog and how things were determined by the dialog choices I made. I liked the way he was able to perceive secrets. The game was different than other games I have played. It was similar to Disco Elysium in play style. I did like that the battles were turn-based. I really did enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, the game started out strong with some beautiful graphics provided by the Unreal Engine. The story itself begins with an intriguing setting and characters, accompanied by a turn-based combat system that promises depth as you progress further into the game.However, this promise fails to materialize. The combat never delves deeper, and encounters with enemies become repetitive, offering little variation. After a while, players may find themselves questioning whether they could simply skip the fights, due to them feeling as a chore. While the game seeks to offer a "detective experience," it primarily involves wandering the city, searching for red dots that trigger dialogue options previously unavailable. The voice acting and facial animations leave much to be desired, feeling like an afterthought (though there may be improvements in the polished voice acting). Many characters come across as lackluster, with motivations that seem stereotypical and comical, such as "the unruly drunk" or "the religious priest."Overall, the game lacks challenging gameplay elements, which is why i can't recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Actually really enjoyed the game, combat is fairly simple with only the last boss actually causing me any problems. Voice acting is amazing for the most part, was a couple of lines that felt like they didn't match the energy of the moment/maybe recorded on their own rather than in relation to anything. Threw me off hearing so many different accents but I'm not sure what the locale would be in Poland in those times so gave it a pass. by far a very enjoyable game. Can recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: 4 hours in and off to a pretty great start. Love the detective aspect of the game. The combat is actually pretty fun and involves a bit more than I actually thought. The whole 1905 early Warsaw and fantasy aspect is really intriguing and like nothing else before. Graphics are really nice and the sound is spot on for this time period. I will say I wish there was a lot more interaction with objects in the world as the devs have created this amazing set to play in but beyond the stories there's really not a lot you can do in this world. No barrels or boxes to find loot in. No people to talk to. No homes you can peruse and maybe stumble upon a side quest or something. Not that I've found anyway. May change in the future. Still, a pretty great entry into the rpg world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Great AA/Indie CRPG. Fun adjustable Battle system similar to Shin Megami Tensei but not as punishing due to the mechanics. Choices matter and are reflected in the story. Interesting world that gives you insight into the machinations and politics of early 20th century Poland. Being able to interact with so many different strata of the populace between Trade Unionists/Capitalists, Whorerers/Officials and Religious groups really enrich the existing world. Thaumaturgy abilities as pseudo science taken seriously made for a compelling power system.
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is  an interesting combination of an early 1900s Polish supernatural mystery RPG in an isometric point and click narrative game with turn based card combat that involves a pokemon style collection of demons!It feels like the manatees at fox studios randomly collected the bits to go into this game, but shockingly ... it all kind of works!!The story is quite entertaining, the music is great and fits the aesthetic the devs are aiming for, and the combat is satisfying with a good amount of customisation and depth.Its also graphically quite a pretty game, with the odd bit of "eurojank" (i hate that term) but rather than frustrating, i found this pretty charming.Good times at retail price, but even better if you can snag it on sale.Full review...
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: It's very difficult to not recommend this game.I like the idea, I like the theme, the ambiance... but I feel like it's missing stuff.The game has a very casual feel to it, you can play with just the mouse.Also, nice graphics, nice storyline, multiple endings...At some point it's kind of repetitive even - you look around, pickup "loot", clicky-clicky all the way.If the fights weren't turn-based, they would've been very annoying, but this way they are more of puzzle.The thing I missed the most and find to be a giant hole in this game: conclusion/decisions that the player should make, and not to be provided straight up by the game.So, yes, very sad to give this a "no"...
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game with only a few weird things, like once i saw a characters head flicker almost like the game was choosing the correct animation file for the dialogue response and needed to "load" it... but it was like a 1 frame flicker, jsut enough to be "huh weird" and then back to the story.other than that, i have been having a really fun time trying to predict where the story is going, making choices, and then being hoisted upon my own pitard for my hubris. Fun to have a character with the flaw of pride.Been playing the game as "me" the first time through, but i am excited to replay it with a No Pride and a Full pride playthrough!
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: Love it! This game has amazing style! The art direction is going so hard!!! Love the 1905 Polish setting! The voice acting is so charming and the writing really makes these charactersn shine as unique and alive. Praise be to everyone who worked on this to make it look and sound so pretty. _childDocuments_.review: I will always love a game that lets you know it's been made with love and care when you play it. _childDocuments_.review: Mixed Cons -The game is ..good, but it has some problems with performance despite being a top down game that's not graphically heavy which is odd. -Slow load times -Scenes where half a sentence is cut off cause it auto progresses to the next spoken line or scene almost as if the game speed and dialog sections are running at two different rates?-The dialog can come off as unnatural a lot of the time, or feels rushed in the production, -Poor translation from another language to English??? Pros The city is well designed and set up Plot is original and unique Combat isn't bad but is confusing at times
_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good RPG with a lot of choices whose impact can be seen and felt during the game, and tries something new with the genre by avoiding having hundreds of numbers and stats and calculations. It's very easy to learn and requires some skill to master.My biggest gripe: Lots and lots of running around. The areas are not too big but you'll still feel like you spend more time walking from place to place than you do actually doing stuff.Also, personal opinion but the XP progression is badly skewed so it's too fast initially and slows to an almost total stop in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: slow-burn atmospheric story-telling with some turn-based mini-game elements (i would almost call it a puzzle of chaining abilities). not super hard, even on the hardest difficulty. can be a little indie jank at times, but not game breaking.the overall setting of 1900s poland is a vibe and the concept of a thaumaturge feels unique/cool. nice dark/gritty feel.would generally recommend this if the art style seems to be your thing and you are looking for a slowburn lore dump type story. kind of a niche game.edit: the combat mini game definitely gets old after a while. you end up doing the same thing over and over again, not a lot of variation really.

_childDocuments_.name: The Thaumaturge

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. However, it has a whole lot of things that are questionable at best and outright horrible at worst. The choices the game gives you are generally varied and interesting. You get to really shape your relationships with the characters in any way you want. Being rude and confrontational will get you in a fight, while trying to stay humble will make others enjoy your company a bit more, though it depends on the person. However, with that said, you really barely use your powers in this game. Very rarely do you get to actually influence people with your magical powers, something which I personally wasn't particularly disappointed by. Mostly you will be gathering evidence and looking for clues, which will help you in conversation. I enjoy this way more than just doing a skill check. The characters in this game are all interesting and acted really nicely, I played the game in english, despite being russian. My biggest complaint on that front is that some of them really don't feel particularly fleshed out, which is fine, to be honest, not every single person needs to have a lot depth, but I think some of them could have a bit more of that. I wish the PPS was more involved with the story, considering how much they are teased in the game. It seems to me that they're included simply by virtue of being a part of history at that point, rather than to be a genuinely interesting faction. This is a shame and I think the game's biggest wasted opportunity.The combat in this game is atrocious, which is a shame, if you consider how much of it is in the game. I played the game on the hardest difficulty and I think, before the final boss, I died maybe 2 times. I also really felt like I wasn't ready for the final boss, I simply lacked the levels necessary in the combat abilities, which would be my fault, but I won every single fight before it using the stuff I got from the prologue. It is extremely easy right up until the literal last fight. If I ever do replay this game, I'm doing so on the lowest difficulty. It feels like the authors played Disco Elysium, thought about the things which make it good, took some of them for their game, but forgot about the others. There is a lot of reasons why DE didn't have combat, and it feels like this game doesn't really understand them. On the topic of DE, the game world in here is way too large, most of the time you will just be walking from place to place spamming right click. There is a reason why in DE the world wasn't really large. I suppose the city in this game does feel like a city, but you aren't building a city, are you? You're making a game world for your video game about various characters and the story, you're not supposed to make a realistic depiction of Warsaw from 1905, it just has to be believable enough for me to believe that that's where I am.The side content in this game ranges from "go to x and interact with thing to get some xp" to really good side quests. If you don't feel like walking a whole bunch with no real reason, feel free to just ignore the "city secrets" quests, that's what I did after like 10 hours in. The actual side quests are all very good, at least the ones I did. The game makes them hard to miss, which is really good. Most of the side quests could very well have been a part of the main quests.So, in short, if you are looking for a very solid 15-20 hour RPG with great story and characters, this one here will be perfect for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Great unique game.  My first play through clocked in at roughly 35 hours, so plenty of content here, and I consider it to be a steal at the current price point.  For games like this, if done right, the story is the reward, and I think that applies here.  Top notch characters, quests, writing, and lore.  I wanted to soak in all the details of Thaumaturgy as well as the historical setting of 19 aught 5 Poland.  As for the turn based combat, my advice is to approach it like a puzzle.  What works on one difficulty will work on the others, so don't be afraid to crank it above what you normally would.  When you get into a fight that seems insurmountable (typically the salutor acquiring ones), take a step back for a moment, consider the mechanics available to you (and used against you), tweak your build out, and experiment with different approaches. So great game, highly recommended, and well worth the asking price.  I hope to see more of Wiktor Szulski in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is an ambitious AA narrative-driven RPG with many things going on in various directions. Unfortunately, at times, it may be too ambitious for its own good, as not every segment of the game is properly fleshed out, and many ideas seem undercooked. As a result, the game has many highs and lows. However, ultimately, it is a good game, which I recommend to people who like atmospheric RPGs focused on personal journeys and characters.Exploring Warsaw at the beginning of the 20th century and its many political and social topics is a fantastic experience. Expect intriguing characters, mature themes, enjoyable exploration and plenty of narrative role-play options. Pros:- Warsaw, at the onset of the 20th century, is an absolutely perfect setting for the game. The developers, who are Polish, took great care to represent their capital city properly. It is rich with details, imbued with little stories at every corner, which give the city life and soul. It is muddy, gloomy, rainy, and cloudy, but in a charming and atmospheric way. You will enjoy exploring every street and alley, learning about Wiktor’s history with the city, and learning about many new trends of the era.- The game's overarching lore explores many real-life social and political issues of the era, including women’s struggle for emancipation, social injustice, workers' struggle for better pay and conditions, the corruption of Polish and Russian bureaucrats and capitalists… All these are interesting and well-thought-out topics, with a balanced approach to these mature themes.- The fantastic soundtrack, which combines dark and mystic tones with nostalgic sounds of a bygone era of Polish history, perfectly adds to the immersion and atmosphere of Warsaw.- Numerous small side missions and collectables add to the lore and character development of both Victor and other characters.- Wiktor Szulski is a fantastically written main character, as well as many other principal characters.- The game’s many avenues for role-playing (in a narrative sense) allow you to build on these foundations further and create a version of Wiktor based on your choices, decisions, and actions. What you do matters in this game, and there will be consequences and repercussions.- The Salutors, demons you collect to fight alongside you and mess with people’s minds, are exceptionally well designed, both visually and in terms of their combat abilities. In addition, the animations for their combat abilities are very creative and original. Watching them execute their actions with unique animations is a pure joy.Neutral:- Voice acting is definitely a mixed bag. Wiktor and some other characters are perfectly voiced, but some less important characters feel rather amateurish and flat in their delivery. However, the biggest issue is the inconsistency in terms of accents. Some actors have a posh British accent, and some have a typical American accent. Others are clearly Eastern Europeans with a heavy Slavic accent. It can break immersion, but nothing too problematic.- Some character models don’t look particularly good, and faces can look especially uncanny. This is in sharp contrast to to the environments, which are rather rich in detail.- The game’s investigative gameplay, in which Wiktor collects evidence in the style of Sherlock Holmes games, is rather shallow and straightforward. You only need a couple of items for each investigation (which are only interactable items at any particular moment), and the game will make the conclusion for you; there’s no actual gameplay here. This is mostly fine with me, but don't expect puzzles and real detective work here.- I absolutely love that the game has a very elaborate codex/journal system where every piece of information about locations, characters, organisations, missions, clues, etc., is carefully stored. However, the UI should have been better. It often felt chaotic and challenging to navigate.Cons:- Combat is definitely the biggest issue I have with this game. The mechanics are shallow, and the gameplay is simply not fun. It quickly becomes repetitive, and I roll my eyes whenever there is a combat section. This is especially so because the game often throws random fights at you towards the end just for the sake of having those fights. It’s a nuisance rather than an enjoyable part of the experience.- Just like combat, the RPG system, in terms of your builds for combat, is also quite basic, and there are few options for customisation and strategising prior to battles.- The facial animations are subpar, which is not good for a game that focuses on its characters and their emotions. Whenever there is dialogue, the camera switches to face-to-face mode, and most characters have a very limited range of animations that ultimately fail to convey their emotions.- During my playthrough, I encountered numerous technical issues, including crashing, freezing, restarting my PC, and textures failing to load. Admittedly, the developers are working hard on fixing these, but I find it essential to note this.- The main story is intriguing until the very end, but the third act seems rushed and is kinda anticlimactic. It’s not bad, but there were no big “wow” moments, revelations, or anything similar. This is a kind of game where you will love the journey but be just “okay” with the final destination.

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge is a story-driven RPG that takes place in Warsaw, Poland, during 1905, a time when the city was under the Imperial Russian tsardom, facing complex political conflicts and ideas between Russian soldiers, Polish citizens and Jewish merchants. You play as a thaumaturge, Wiktor Szulsky, who returns to his home place due to urgent family matters. Thaumaturges are those capable of using magical powers and doing miracles. They are able to investigate people’s souls and learn their secrets by inspecting the items they touched to read their emotions and thoughts. Sometimes people like this have flaws, imperfections or weaknesses that are able to attract Salutors, supernatural demons who belong to the local folklore and that can only be seen by thaumaturges. Throughout the journey, Wiktor will find and tame many of these salutors, but most importantly, he will learn the secrets about his family and confront the people who rule the city in the shadows.The quest system is very interesting and, along with the unusual setting, it partially reminded me of The Witcher. Fool’s Theory is a team made of ex-CD Projekt Red developers as well others who have previously worked on Divinity: Original Sin 2 and Baldur’s Gate 3, so it’s not surprising that the quality of writing is fantastic, like there is barely any distinction between main and secondary quests because they are both equally intriguing. Some of the secondary quests are also tied to characters important for the story, so you can see there is often a connection with the main events. Many quests also include multiple objectives (some even optional) that can unlock new ways for completing them. A few are also marked as time-sensitive, so you can only complete them for a limited amount of time, which in my experience is very generous.Most of the quests require you to obtain information about the characters you meet. You can acquire “observations” by talking to them, but also from interacting with the items they touched. Once you have gathered enough observations, you will come up to a conclusion, which will unlock unique dialogue choices and sometimes allow you to manipulate people by using your Salutors (it works exactly like the Axii sign from The Witcher). Unfortunately, all of this is pretty much passive on your side. The game doesn’t ask you to interpret clues and solve investigations with your brain (like in the Sherlock Holmes games). You simply go around using your perception to detect items that are important for quests, pick them up, read the observation and once you have enough of them, your character will automatically come up with a conclusion. The good news is that your actions really matter and may have long-term consequences; for example, depending on your dialogue choice, a message will appear saying that X character will remember that (like in Telltale games).Like some people, Wiktor also has his own Flaw, Pride, and some dialogue options are directly connected to it. These choices can get you into trouble but they can also be a way to solve quests differently. Sometimes they are only available if you have enough Pride, so you must decide if you want to use it often and potentially impact the course of events, or ignore it completely. Upyr is your first Salutor and he follows your Flaw, but through the main quest you will be able to collect more Salutors that are extremely important for finding more clues and for fighting. That’s why I would recommend completing the first three main quests in Warsaw before following secondary quests, because battles are hard, if not impossible, to win without using other salutors and you will also miss some clues during investigations.Sometimes the game omits what you can do. For example, during one side quest, I had to talk to a serial killer who was holding a hostage. The quest details on the upper left corner only showed me what to do, but didn’t tell me that I could go to the police commissioner and ask for backup before dealing with the killer. This could lead to slightly different endings for the characters involved, depending on my dialogue choices. I still don’t understand if it’s intentional quest design or just a flaw in the quest instructions, either way the game encourages you to explore, talk and find clues even when they are not clearly marked on the quest’s list of things to do. Exploration is also important because some events only take place at a certain time, but you can change the time of day (morning, noon, afternoon and evening) by using benches. Exploring the same locations at different times of day can make you find new events, characters, quests and collectables. Combat is turn-based and you are often facing multiple enemies alone or occasionally with a companion. To win the fight, you must lower enemies’ health points by using a variety of skills and your salutor powers. You can only summon one Salutor at a time, but swapping between them is important because enemies have unique traits that can be disabled only by attacking with certain salutors. After fights, but also after completing quests, you receive experience and points that you can use on a skill tree to purchase upgrades and improve your attributes. The combat system works decently, but there is a lot of fighting (maybe too much) and it eventually becomes repetitive. Games like Disco Elysium and (partially) Baldur’s Gate 3 have proved that you don’t really need combat to succeed with your game, as long as you have a great story to tell, well-written characters and gameplay mechanics such as skill checks, attributes and some RPG elements. That’s why I think this game could have benefited from less combat, or none at all, as the better parts are exploration, story, choices and consequences.Another great aspect is the beauty of environments. You can fast-travel between different districts in the city of Warsaw, each one showing the social status of the people who live there. Locations are greatly detailed and look very real, despite the isometric view. The game is also filled with cinematic cutscenes and while characters are often well-voiced, their facial expressions are not very well portrayed. The performance on PC is great though, I didn’t experience any issues other than small bugs or glitches, but fortunately nothing quest-breaking. The Thaumaturge offers an impressive story that will be greatly enjoyed by those who loved The Witcher’s complexity of quests, as well isometric games like Disco Elysium. The Polish/Russian historical setting is very unusual for videogames, yet it is always believable despite the presence of supernatural powers and demons. Even if the turn-based combat lacks depth and becomes repetitive in the long run, this is a game you must play primarily for the quality of story and the satisfaction of seeing the consequences of your actions in the real world.

_childDocuments_.review: While I didn’t have high hopes for The Thaumaturge, it seemed potentially interesting. The setting, the time period, the topics and how mystical dark fantasy story could be integrated in all of that was promising. And the mix of story driven adventuring with turn based battles had a lot of cool ideas about them. But, unfortunately, the end result is quite underwhelming for the most part and outright bad in a few spots.As mentioned, the concept is strong. 1905, Warsaw under Russian Empire control, rise of the Rasputin cult presented on the edge of history and dark fantasy. With everything being dramatic and also veiled in the mysticism of “thaumaturgy” and people who practice this magic. As a result you get a cool mix of historic drama, Witcher-like demon hunting and Sherlock Holmes-like case solving. It’s all played from the top down perspective, controlled similarly to a point and click adventure or RPG in the vein of classic Infinity Engine titles or the far more recent Disco Elysium.You spend most of the time running around huge maps that represent different districts of Warsaw, finding people to talk to, items and collectibles. You’re also constantly clicking the right mouse to reveal the elements in the locations that have strong emotional traces that are usually tied to either minor collectible quests or to main or side quests, where they provide you with additional information and alternative means of dealing with obstacles, usually in the form of unlocking new dialogue options. To give the developers credit – they put quite a lot of big and small variations in their quests that lead to unique consequences and callbacks later on. Which mostly works fine, with only some “seams” being quite obvious.Sadly, in practice all of this is quite uninteresting. For example, the game often provides you the connections and conclusions for finding different items and traces and it really tries to emulate an almost investigation/detective game feel. But everything is so streamlined and automatic, that it’s faster and sometimes outright more beneficial, to just click past all of that until the game gives you a new trail to follow. For one, despite the overwhelming amount of the conclusions and items, it always boils down to 1-3 simple choices they unlock. For two, even then the game gives you a name or an address to follow there’s nothing on the map to use this information on, so you still have to follow the objective marker instead of using your head. And for three, clue items and collectibles simply do not exist until the game brings them into existence somewhere in their gigantic maps, leading to pure pixel hunting. The more I played, the more similarities I saw to Sherlock Holmes: Chapter One, a game I worked on. One that, I think, turned out quite well, but also one that could be improved in a number of ways. Yet everything The Thaumaturge borrows, it does much worse…At least the combat seems very promising in the beginning. The idea here is that of turn based combat where each action has a certain time for activation and may have additional effects of delaying or outright cancelling turns for the target. There are no items, no equipment and health is always reset to full at the start of the fight, so everything is always decided via smart usage of said actions. And as you get stronger and get more salutors, your abilities increase, leading to different strategies for battle – focusing on damage over time, making enemies scared, dealing pure damage, varying types of actions or building combos. Combat system is pretty cool on its own, but a lot of the time battles seem to exist just to “spice up the story”. And in those cases, combat is rather tedious, while the only narrative reasoning for it is that some random people come up to you and say that they don’t like your face.Biggest disappointment, however, is the story. For how cool the premise is, for how interesting the setting is, the resulting tale is just a messy “nothing” in the end. It does have highlights and better written characters, some moments and scenes are genuinely well delivered. It’s just that most of the time you go through the game, both gameplay-wise and story-wise, on complete auto-pilot and it’s hard to care about what’s going on. It does look nice and the music is quite pleasant. At the same time, however, the usage of Unreal Engine 5 here is quite unrefined and even ignoring that, the game can be quite buggy. I got stuck a few times, requiring a reload and crashes are also a possibility.While there’s nothing outright bad with The Thaumaturge, there’s very little genuinely good about it either. Almost every cool idea that the game has, remains undeveloped or taken in a direction that feels unsatisfying. While the ending of the story is presented as if there could be a sequel, I just don’t see why anyone would want it. That said, a new take on this idea could be interesting – one that could be more refined, even if that would require the game to be slightly less ambitious.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in the middle of Act II after about ten hours. I'm not sure I can recommend this game for a few reasons. Firstly, the story isn't terribly interesting, it isn't well told (bad voice acting, annoying dialogue), I don't really care about any of the characters, and there are just too many proper nouns (Thaumaturge, Salutor, etc). It's based in an interesting time period - 1905 Poland - but I'm not sure they do much with it. It seems like a pretty typical city with seedy elements, corrupt officials...it could be turn of the century New York. The combat is somewhat interesting, but it never evolves, either through enemy types, mechanisms, or interesting powers for the player that vary choices. The game also struggles with communicating game state (who has a debuff, how that matters), which is somewhat grating as the difficulty increases. Finally, the detective element is just roaming around a room or environment and clicking on every glowing spot. It's tedious and there is a lot of text that is too vague to be useful, but not clever enough to be engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are just interested in point and click adventures go here: A historical JRPG, which transports us to historical Warsaw and lets us fight against our own demons as well as the Russian occupiers. Are we looking at a new masterpiece here? The story gets off to a very interesting start. We arrive, close to madness, by train in a remote little village in Georgia. Here we are looking for a healer who can supposedly treat hopeless cases. The year is 1905, and the healer is Rasputin. The very Rasputin who allegedly got so close to the Tsarina and other ladies at court that he was later dubbed "Russia's greatest love machine" by ABBA. We get to know Rasputin better and he helps us to tame our salutor and also to capture a second salutor. We are a thaumaturge, and they normally have a Salutor, a creature from the shadow world that only we can see, communicate with and which also supports us in battle. Only very few thaumaturges have been able to bind two (or even more) of these beings to themselves, most have died in the attempt. We can do that, and together with Rasputin we travel back to Warsaw for family reasons. There we are drawn into various events and have to decide which side we want to be on. Freedom fighters, Russians, Jewish merchants, street gangs...We play Wiktor Szulski, a Warsaw-born thaumaturge. In theology, thaumatology is the study of miracles; great thaumaturges were Jesus and Francis of Assisi. Thaumaturges in the game also have special abilities. They can track down hidden things and recognize what has happened to them if it has to do with strong human emotions. This is more or less a trace of another person's personality. They therefore always need personal objects from other people in order to find out more about them. Thaumaturges also sense the feelings, thoughts and emotions of other people through personal contact. In battle, this enables them to anticipate the attacks of their enemies. We can further improve all these mental abilities in the course of the game in a skill tree with four strands (heart, hand, mouth and brain).When we explore the game world, we keep making observations, so we learn things after examining objects that remain hidden to the normal eye. We walk through the area and press RT/RMB to scan the immediate surroundings for anomalies. This also shows us the way to the next location in order to advance the plot. However, if we blindly follow this route display, we will miss out on all the hotspots we can investigate and thus all the experience points and information we can gain. The Unreal 5 graphics in the game are pretty good and varied, albeit a little gloomy and grey. The controls with the gamepad are also excellent. When we have made enough observations on a topic, we automatically draw conclusions. This is reminiscent of classic detective work, except that our gift as a thaumaturge allows us to discover many things very quickly without the use of modern tools or a laboratory. As a thaumaturge, we can also manipulate people as soon as we have learned enough about them. This is indicated to us by extended options in the conversations and works in a similar way to Star Wars - "These are not the druids you're looking for". This is how we convince NPCs to do things they didn't actually want to do.The game progresses by completing quests. These are displayed in a quest log and there are various ways to complete them. Some quests do not have to be completed, but we miss out on information or upgrades as a result. We spend most of our time in the game searching the rather large maps and talking to all the NPCs as well as taking a closer look at hotspots. The conversations (fully dubbed) are multiple-choice, whereby it is not possible to select all options, as selecting one option often steers the conversation or the story in a certain direction. During the conversations, we are usually shown our conversation partner in detail. Many conversations also run automatically as cutscenes. Very often we find texts to read in the game world, such as posters, newspapers, letters or flyers, which give us information (and experience points). All in all, the exploration part is extensive and quite talk- and text-heavy.But The Thaumaturge is also a JRPG. Battles are an essential part of the game, and if we lose a battle, it means "game over". The battles are classic. We choose an attack (or another action) from various options on a turn-by-turn basis. Sometimes we are also assisted by NPCs. We don't fight against the usual fantasy creatures such as rats, blobs or goblins, but against human opponents. Deserters from the Tsar's army, policemen, village proles or secret service agents have to be put down by us. We are supported by our salutors, who also attack our opponents under our control. Three difficulty levels allow us to adapt the challenge of the battles to our taste.The Thaumaturge is an exploration and text-heavy JRPG (Japanese role-playing game) in a historical (European) setting. We play a thaumaturge with special mental abilities who puzzles and fights his way through Russian-occupied Warsaw in 1905. By taming creatures from the shadow world, we improve our character while advancing our character's dark story through a variety of smaller quests in various historically well-researched and graphically impressive locations.

_childDocuments_.review: As of 09/04/2024 I have completed a playthrough of the game on patch 1.0.3. I think this game is a good fit for people that like the setting and story driven RPG's and point-and-click adventure games. The combat gameplay is average, and the investigative/detective aspects are not great. The story and characters  great. The love for Poland and gaming is clear and is really heartwarming to see. All in all the game was very enjoyable for me, and I would highly recommend it and rate it an 8/10. I look forward to this studios next game.The game is heavily influenced by Disco Elysium, but still has an identity of its own in both good and bad ways. The combat is not the deepest but is fun, the difficulty ranges from easy to slightly more challenging depending on your settings. The investigation parts do not feel satisfying, it feels like being spoon fed information. The choices in both combat and dialogue feel impactful and are plentiful. The game is beautiful. The writing and interpersonal relationships are one of the strongest parts of the game, as the world and characters feel alive. The voice acting is not great. There are no microtransactions. The rest of this spoiler free review has been shortened due to the character limit. The "investigations" are one of the less well executed parts of the game, and where I think taking more inspiration from Disco Elysium would have helped improve the game the most. The gameplay for solving investigations mostly revolves around pressing a "look for clues" button, once you gather a couple clues by pressing the interact button at the clue locations, the game spells out the answer, and when concluding an investigation most of the time it is not possible to draw an incorrect conclusion. It would have been more interesting and felt more rewarding if the player had to find clues themselves, put them together, and could draw incorrect conclusions. If the investigations and "detective" aspects are very important to you this aspect of the game is not recommended.The turn-based combat is average. The game did not feel challenging enough. The game was mostly played on Balanced, with small parts on Challenging, mostly because the difficulty kept reverting to Balanced, possibly due to switching between PC and Steam Deck. While I did die a couple times, optimal gameplay or strategies are not needed to finish the game.There are a lot of collectibles in this game, but finding them makes use of the "look for clues" button. This marks all the collectibles in a small area around you. Everything is pretty small and there is not a clear in-world separation of "clue" items and normal items in the background. This almost necessitates the use of the find clue button when trying to find collectibles, which means you will hear the sound effect very often. It also does not feel very rewarding, as it does not really feel like you found it. It would be nice if there were more . A lot of the  would have been interesting as small quests. A gallery in the main menu would have also been nice.The voice acting is inconsistent, both accent  quality wise. Even lines from the same actor are not always consistent. I did also not see any option for the language other than English, a Polish or "original" language option would really add to the immersion, and might sound more consistent accent wise. Line reads are often a bit awkward, to the point where it was sometimes a bit distracting. There are some better voice actors and line reads in there too though.The music is really good and adds to the setting and atmosphere. The sounds all sound nice, the mixing is pretty good, there are ample sound settings too.The game goes for a gorgeous, realistic looking art style, which is quite demanding. On lower settings a lot of the details are gone, but the world still looks nice. Especially the textures on the lowest settings did not look great on a bigger screen, but on a smaller screen like the steam deck most of the details are wasted anyways. The performance gain going from higher settings to lower settings were small, and older PC's might struggle running this game at anything more than 30fps even on the lowest settings. Texture quality felt very impactful on the visuals. The rest of the settings did not feel nearly as important visually. The ingame frame rate limit options are quite limited, as I saw no 30 and 60fps options. Different graphical options during overworld traversal, combat, and dialogue could also help, since the graphical needs vary wildly under these scenarios.Playing on the steam deck really highlighted the issue of having no real low end options. I played in bed on the lowest ingame settings, steam deck limit of 30 fps, 10W, XeSS upscaling on performance mode. The game is nice to play in bursts of about an hour on the deck. After this cutscenes would start stuttering, and after about 2 hours it would sometimes shut down the steam deck during cutscenes. The experience felt fine.The game was played on a 5700XT with an R5 5600 on a 1440p 144Hz monitor. Loading times were short and infrequent. The game was played on low and medium settings. The performance did not seem majorly impacted and a stable FPS was NOT reached under any combination of settings. FSR 3.0 performance mode was not enough for a stable 75 FPS during cutscenes and dialogue. The performance did not feel that bad, and it did not impact the gameplay or have any major stutters. I still recommend to keep textures as high as your PC can handle. This game would really benefit from lower end graphical options and fps limits.Attention to detail could be improved in some areas, particularly subtitles and general writing. Not a major problem, but it is sometimes confusing. Some of the geometry of the game also feels rough. This did not pose a problem for gameplay. I never got stuck, softlocked, or out of bounds.As this is a spoiler-free review, the plot and setting will not be a major point of discussion. I liked the story over all.Most of the choices in this game feel impactful. Some interactions seem to only have a slight change in dialogue, especially in the earlier sections of the game, but in the later stages the choices feel very impactful, and some of the choices made in the early game come back. This is one of the best parts of the game. The pacing as a completionist did not feel the greatest as it was kind of unclear when side-content would permanently lock. I do not think I got locked out of any quests, but it did alter the way I approached the game, prioritising side content over main story content. As the amount of side content between main quests varied greatly, it felt as if some parts of the main quest dragged, but the content I was doing intead of the main story was quite fun.I loved all of the characters in this game. It is fun to see them interact on screen. The characters and interactions feel fleshed out. The relationships between Wiktor and the people in his life are one of the best parts of the game. The main quest told a pretty interesting story. It felt very unique as it was heavily impacted by the setting of the game. Overall it was very fun.The bigger side quests were some of the best content in the game. There is ample choice and they feel replayable. The characters featured in these conflicts are memorable, fleshed out, and unique.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an instant favorite, easily making its way into my top 10 of all time—in the same category but better than Disco Elysium. It’s visually stunning, with a story that’s not only engaging but also very important in the current political situation with the new rise of fascist/bigoted ideologies. The narrative is historically grounded, with a fascinating twist through the inclusion of thaumaturgy.One of the game’s strongest points is its focus on meaningful choices that impact the storyline, making a playthrough feel unique and personal. The combat system is equally compelling; it combines tactical depth with a fun, familiar feel that reminds me of Pokémon in the best way. Overall, it’s a rare gem that seamlessly blends storytelling, fun, and style.

_childDocuments_.review: A well-made isometric RPG. Other than that I have little to complain about, I have a positive aftertaste and I'm looking forward to do a new run where I try to do things differently.Choices felt meaningful, I really enjoyed how giving in to your Pride  I've only experienced two of the different endings, but it was great to see how the different character relationships blossom, or fall apart.Much recommended, you should try it out!

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game so so much and despite that, still went in without any high expectations but even those got disappointed.The Gameplay of walking around and spamming right click just to then find a point of interest and get a handrawn picture seems fun at first but become so much of a boring chore if you are like me and want to complete whatever quest you can find.Alright, I thought the side quest (despite the boss fights these are quite cool) are not great... maybe the story will get me more engaged.. and I was wrong.The main character is not unlikeable and so is the surface scratched plot of the Story there is nothing more to say about it.Now by any means this is not a bad game the visuals of the areas are nice and I think they put all they could into this game yet the Persoanlity is still missing.If you don´t mind doing the same thing over and over again and just like the Atmopshere and some turn based combat here and there go for it. BUT if you look for a at least a little bit of an engaging or interesting story with nice characters that don´t seem like empty shells then you may look elsewhere or wait for a sale ( even tho the price is already quite fair)I hope this Studio keeps working hard and think outside the Box in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: YES but NoThis is what I would call a Point and click plus.The story is very rich and there's plenty of missions with multiple endings (12).Story, Lore is what makes the game great.What falls short is the combat. and how you get into them sometimes. they are a bit boring to be honest. You fight idle rpg style with a time bar that makes certain action activate faster or later. same for the enemies. I found dome fight to be too long (normal difficulty). One of the main issue is that sometimes just speaking to a NPC standing in the middle of the street will trigger a fight with them without us knowing who they are at first. It's a bit annoying in a game that relies on you clicking everything you encounter to make XP and progress the game. without a Diplomacy or escape option I found it irritating. In order to make fight easier you have to unlock Salutors and max your stats which forces you to do a lot of side missions. I mean a lot.Overall not a bad game, with a ton of reading to do, but the fighting feels out of place.

_childDocuments_.review: The Thaumaturge may lack the technical polish of bigger, higher-budgeted games, and it does suffer from pesky bugs and semi-frequent crashes, but such issues pale in comparison to just how gripping and enthralling I found its early 20th century world filled with dashing European demon-wizards and scheming, morally ambiguous historical figures. It’s a well-written, atmospheric journey where fact and fiction mingle boldly, supported by interesting side characters, political intrigue, and just the right amount of tactical, turn-based combat with a satisfying amount of customization. The Thaumaturge doesn’t shoot for the stars, but it doesn’t have to – even with its flaws, it’s got plenty of merits to make it stand out from the crowd and so, it gets a very strong recommendation from me.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a bit of Disco Elysium, a bit of The Witcher, - and a bit of The Darkest Dungeon when it comes to the turn based combat. Taking place in early 20th century Warsaw, during one of the most interesting time periods of the last century, - shortly before WW1 and with a sense of revolution and the collapse of the Russian Empire in the air, - this game, along with games like The Last Train Home, helps to put a spotlight on a truly fascinating time period that has been neglected far too long.

And even if the game is short, it has its replay value cuz you may choose completely different option and lead your story in a completely different way. _childDocuments_.review: I've had this game in my wishlist for some time, forgot where it came from.It was on sale, I got it.Damn, what a hidden treasure! It's somber game inspired by slavic folkore. The music is splendid and the city is a beauty. Despite the Thaumaturgic stuff and the monsters, it takes place in a realistic 1905 Warsaw, and it's really nice to see all the little details from that era when strolling the streets.I'm also in love with the story already, even if I'm only at the beginning. The characters are really interesting and *real*, you have a certain freedom of choice despite the protagonist having flaws, a past and relatives. There is a political agenda, but it's actually one from that very century, and it's very interesting to immerse yourself in the political and societal struggles of that time.The combat is not the most important part I think, but it's interesting enough and fun to watch.I really recommend it, on sale or not! _childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review. In this episode I check out a game ive been eagerly anticipating, The Thaumaturge. This game was released by Fool's Theory, who also created the stealth based RPG Seven and was published by 11 Bit Studios, the creators of Frostpunk, one of the best games ive ever reviewed. The Thaumaturge takes place in an Alternate version of Poland in the 19th century. Wictor is a Thaumaturge, a rare group of practitioners of Thaumaturgy, which allows them to sense and manipulate emotions in order to hunt and capture creatures called Salutors, who are drawn to negative emotions. After an attempt to capture a Salutor goes wrong and Wictors ability to sense emotions is compromised, he goes on a quest to find the infamous Rasputin, in an attempt to restore his abilities. His quest for healing will become a hunt for a host of Salutors decimating the populace.The Thaumaturge is a perfect mix of classic Turn Based RPG and Detective games. Youll need to combine Wictor's Thaumaturgy abilities along with your own detective skills in order to locate the Salutors, whilst navigating the complex politics of a war torn Poland and interacting with several famous historical figues. This game is a breath of fresh air in a market where quality RPGs are becoming more and more rare and is a must buy for fans of classic RPGs like Dragon Age. 11 Bit Studios are moving from strength to strength as a publisher and i cannot wait to see their future titles like Frostpunk 2.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. Game was provided by the developer for review purposes================================================Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Bitchute: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Twitch: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Odysee: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Rumble: Twitter: Facebook: Email Enquiries: The Thaumaturge on Steam: The Thaumaturge - First Impressions: ================================================
