_childDocuments_.review: I guess overall I liked it, the game-play was simple but engaging (think tell tales the walking dead) the story quite poignant and although it was a bit unpolished at times, as a film school production its fairly impressive.Pros- Art-style was fairly pretty. Sort of a comic book meets painterly kind of aesthetic. Some textures could have been better but there were some beautiful scenes with some nice lighting effects- Voice acting mostly excellent with a few exceptions.- Music was pleasant enough.- Story was interesting enough for me to practically play the whole game in one sitting; it was quite an adventure. Ultimately it was pretty sad in the end which I don't think is really a spoiler since you get bad news in the very first chapter.- Replay-ability to get different endings (up to nine different ones) if that's your thing.Cons- Controls weren't the best. navigation could be finicky; a lot of the time the character didn't go where I intended. Some times the character refused to move entirely (especially frustrating during the timed sequences) and some hot-spots had to be clicked a few times to trigger. There is also a need sometimes to use WASD and the arrow keys when they could have easily implemented a mouse drag binding for this.- A couple of the voices didn't seem to fit the characters age or background.- Very short for the asking price if you don't have the patience to replay the whole game to see different endings.- The on screen UI could have been a bit bigger. There are 3 metrics which are tracked in the top left corner and were quite hard to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Best Month Ever!

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice story from what I have played so far. This game is a visual novel which has point and click portions.  The developers should have left out the point and click portions and just made this a visual novel in my humble opinion.  But it is what it is, and it's very engaging and you can feel the love put into this project. The stylish graphic and audio elements to make you want to work through it and it's very easy to connect with the main characters.  There's a nice disclaimer at the start of the game to warn you of foul language and racial situations, because the setting of this game is in the middle of the 20th century and to give it realism, the characters needed to have various racial biases and sensitivities to social situations (ooh I feel so smart making this sentence) to really give you a taste of what it was like to live in those times.  For whatever flaws I see in the point and click areas of the game - which is just that everytime the game pauses to wait for you to figure out where to click on the screen to continue the narrative - the story is very captivating and I want to see this through to the end.  Like any good visual novel, I could see this game being made into a TV series or movie.  The point of playing this game is that it captures the lives of people in a specific time of American history, so you can experience something similar to watching a good movie.  If you love story-rich games, check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Best Month Ever!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has one of the most heartfelt stories I have ever played. It made me joyously happy and also extremely sad at the same time. There is some heavy subject matter in this game but it is handled very well and proper warnings are given. I would definitely recommend this game to anyone that is remotely interested. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER HEAVY. You have been warned. The first paragraph is safe, everything beyond that is enter at your own risk. So for a long while I wasn't going to review this game, it feels like it's someone's passion project and I hate crapping on people's babies, especially when it's a small team. And a lot of stuff seems pretty innocent - the writing's silted sometimes, certain events are incredibly unrealistic, the pacing is painfully slow (so slow that often I'll leave it running in the background and listen for some kind of indication that I have to come back and do something) and it has all the engagement of a free idle game. But these are all things that I thought, okay, it's got some issues, but that's not worth a bad review. And it has some upsides as well - the music, whilst painfully repetitive, is at least inoffensive, and the art is beautiful. Here's where the spoiler free warning ends, I'm about to deep dive into the story, though I won't touch on the ending. My biggest issue for the duration of the game was simply that the story itself is pretty bad. We already know the premise from the promo material, and there's no development of that, no plot twists, etc. It's just a series of events that the MCs experience as they're travelling around looking for a home for the little boy, and that format is fine but there really does need to be some kind of over-arching development of the characters at the very least, especially considering the whole premise of the story is "one character faces their imminent death whilst preparing their child for life alone." The character development should be the crux of the story, and there's just... none. Which is extra frustrating because both characters are so very flat. Louise (mum) contributes nothing but apathy and some vague one-liners with a hint of a fiery personality on occasion, when you allow it, whilst Mitch (the boy) has only a smidge more, showing himself to be a generic good child who loves his mother. There's also a system that develops Mitch's personality throughout the game (even when the "choices" you make are ones he doesn't see or hear, which is interesting), defining his ability to relate to others, his confidence, and his respect for law and order. None of these things will have any kind of impact on any aspect of the game, as far as I can tell, and virtually all choices are simply dialogue options, with the game frequently punishing you for attempts to be honest, diplomatic, or empathetic by lowering your confidence (because I guess being a heartless ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and being confident are the same thing). There's no nuance to it and very little sense, though at least relationships and law and order are a bit more developed. And a lot of the lack of development seems to be by choice? Like, there are plenty of times when realistically a mother would sit down with her son and talk about what just happened, but all we get are a couple of bumper stickers and "I'll tell you off-screen" comments. It's like the developers had a cool idea for a game but didn't realize what that game would actually entail, or maybe they were scared that their vision of the game - which would be mostly a mother and son talking about life and racism and such - would be boring. Like, I don't think any of us bought this game for the QTEs and action, but that's what they seem to have put most of the work into. As for the other characters you come across come in two flavours: completely flat with no personality what-so-ever, or a personality comprised entirely of tropes and stereotypes, and honestly that's what pushed me over from "just leave it alone" to a bad review. I appreciate that not everyone will care about this, but the cast of characters includes:  - Almost all women (except the FMC) is a victim  - Virtually every straight white man is a rapist, pervert, or violent racist  - The queer character is a manipulative pervert  - The black characters are meek and mild mannered victims to the white characters  - There's a couple of cliched Native Americans who only exist to aid and die for the MCs  - I literally don't think there's a single child in the game except the MMC who isn't abused by their parents What I'm getting at is that it's a game that prides itself on the diverse cast of characters, but it reads like it was written by someone who's never met another person in their lives, and it's handled with all the sensitivity of a tooth extraction with a rock. Honestly in places it feels mean-spirited, it's so bad. Combine that with a character development system that does nothing for characters who don't develop, a game that's so slow it's basically an interactive lullaby, and a story that doesn't exist, and you have a pretty but genuinely crap experience that I honestly have to avoid staying away from. And in response to the idea that life just sucks for some people - yeah, no ♥♥♥♥, I love those stories, give me all the grimdark, that's literally why I bought this game, I wanted to be heartbroken. That's why I'm made - I wasn't heartbroken, I wasn't even moved, I was *bored.* Comparably my dislike of the victims/abusers thing from the rant about the cast of characters - my problem isn't that victims and abusers exist, it's that EVERYONE is a victim or abuser, and their role is defined primarily by their gender and secondarily by their ethnicity and age (with the exception being Kiki the queer pervert exploiting barely legal girls for sex work who's heralded as a saviour). If they'd thrown in a male victim of domestic violence, made Kiki a woman, or ♥♥♥♥ even just show us someone getting smacked around by someone other than Louise, I'd have been happy, but nope, any badassery is done by the incredibly bland FMC in dialogue that sounds like a 10 year old wrote it after too many Sunday morning specials. In conclusion the game has very little to offer, including the premise it sells itself on. It's a really long and boring interactive road trip with two character you'll struggle to care about, doing things you'll struggle to care about, until nothing happens or something happens off-screen. Nothing's fleshed out enough to be significant, nothing's developed enough to be impressive (except the art, IDK if I'd call it impressive but it's pretty, at least), and the characters and assets in the game are neutral at best and annoying or offensive at worst, depending on your tolerance for harmful stereotypes and buggy point and click. If it's developed further and gets better I'll come back and update, but I'm not holding out hopes at this stage.

name: CULTIC
detailed_description: Rise up. Fight back. Gear up to fight your way through the ranks of an insidious cult. Their wretched minds twisted by the will of an unseen entity, you'll find just as much lead flying back as you dish out, so you'll have to run, slide, dodge, and make use of your environment to survive in this old-school-inspired shooter. CULTIC: Chapter One includes 10 maps full of blood, grit, and of course, cultists. After completing the story, you can test your skills in the wave-based Survival Mode, also included with Chapter One. Get a taste of Chapter Two with the newly added Interlude story map! Chapter Two will be available as paid DLC at a future date, and will continue the story of CULTIC! CULTIC gives you the freedom to approach combat your way. You can run in guns blazing, running, jumping, sliding, and dodging to keep out of harms way. If you prefer a slower approach, you can lay traps, let your enemies come to you, and pick them off from the safety of cover. Maybe you prefer to weave in between your foes, leading their attacks towards each other, and turning them against one another. With a full arsenal of mid-century firearms and explosives, you'll be well equipped to slaughter everything in your path - provided you don't get slaughtered first. Combat in CULTIC is fast and deadly. Well-placed shots can take your enemies - and yourself - out of the game quickly. Keep on the move or stick to cover, and use your arsenal wisely to stay alive as you fight your way through cult territory. CULTIC was styled to feel like a throwback to the shooters of yore, but with the advantages of a modern engine, such as physics, lighting, and a fully 3D game world. The gameplay, audio design, and art are all stylized to create a unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: After doing every achievement and completed the game in Easy, Hard and Extreme, I can say that this is one of the best "Old school FPS" i've ever played.Every level is intense and when you think you're about to get to the final chapter, it surprises you again with another frenetic level full of action and a new type of enemy that will try to annihilate you.I really recommend doing the Achievements because it adds a lot of replayability to the game and it makes you think of new ways to play it.Overall I recommend any fan of the old Doom to play this and for the people that never played something like this, this is a good game to start in the "Genre"Looking forward to chapter 2, good job Devs!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's an actual Blood 2. 10/10Longer review, Cultic is exactly what you'd hope for out of a boomer shooter made in 2022. Tight responsive gameplay with plenty of upgrades, quality of life changes and improvements since the genre peaked in the late 90's. The level and sound design is top notch, chocked full of secrets and the game itself is well worth the asking price. Coming from a Monolith industry veteran, it's no surprise Cultic totally and completely delivers on what the store page promises.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. If you loved Blood you will absolutely love this game. Even non-retro FPS respecters should like it. It is the best nu-retro shooter I have played (Wrath is second best) so far - and also one of the best shooters I've played in the last year.Lots of action along with a bit of a story-line to keep it interesting. Level design is brilliant and the maps are large enough to be able to take them in a variety of ways (so it is not so linear as actual classic FPS'). Lots of unique enemies. Fantastic range of weapons to use and upgrade. Amazing atmosphere.It's $15 well worth spent. It took me 9 hours to complete playing casual on normal difficulty.It's a real work of art and I'm looking forward to the next chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim wanting to do a small Indie game play-through, and it was a great choice. The graphics, game play, shooting-style, and everything is super fun if you like the classic video game style. The story line is enticing and finding how to move to the next step isn't very difficult. I did a full play-through on casual and quickly found myself needing a larger challenge. I'm excited to do another run on a more difficult mode, and even more excited for future updates / DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game yesterday and haven't even finished it but I can well enough say this was worth price of entry. CULTIC is absolutely stellar.AESTHETICS-Very distinct art direction that is perfectly nailed. The game is stylized in a very distinct way that can best be described as a foggy PS1 port of Blood with brown replaced with green and dithering cranked up to 11.WEAPONS-On the mention of Blood, combat feels like a very natural evolution of Blood mixed with light resource management. You have a very small collection of weaponry but they all feel refined and tweaked to perfection. COMBAT AND ENEMIES-And what are weapons wiithout baddies to use em' on. The enemy and encounter design is amazing. A very bad pitfall games like this fall into, going as far back as Blood, is having tons and tons of hitscan enemies that turn you into a bloody spongebob in a matter of seconds. It tends to feel cheap in most cases. Jasozz works around this by having bullet based attack be projectile-based; even yours. An excellent decision that lead to my deaths feeling much more fair.LORE-I won't get into the lore but it's scattered through readables like journals, diaries, and posted notes that are unobtrusive but very interesting to read.LEVEL DESIGN-Levels feel very intuitive to naviagate. Not once did I ever get lost which is a feat considering these stages have all taken me over 20 minutes to complete.HORROR-This ties into the art direction, the horror chops on display are among the best I've ever seen. I cannot describe how good Jasozz is at creating a tense atmosphere, building dread, and scaring the player. I really want to see Jasozz make a Silent Hill type horror game where he goes all out in this field.MUSIC-Before getting into the music, I must digress for moment about the modern day boomer shooter and its music. Skip to the stars if you don't care. A very controvertial opinion I have is that I very much dislike the fact that Andrew Hulshult is making music for a large chunk of boomer shooters. I'm glad Andrew Hulshult has found great success even going as far as the big boys with ID but by having one person make music for a bunch of games (especially if they're in the same genre) begins to strip away the identity of the game. The tracks he made for Dusk are great, especially the ambient tracks but have the same djent sound over and over, makes them start to blend together. I cannot tell the difference between the music in Dusk, Nightmare Reaper, and Wrath apart. This is all to say I'm glad Andrew Hulshult hasn't composed the music for CULTIC. ☆☆☆The music that Jasozz has composed fits the game like a glove, perfectly weaving together bitcrushed drums and synths with a powerful guitar that leads every big encounter that really sells the idea of one man taking down an entire death cult. (Note: Astounding that he made it considering his DAW looked like this; CONCLUSION-CULTIC is a phenomenal game that takes it's inspirations and runs so far beyond them it laps. I genuinely cannot think of a flaw or nitpick. If you're a fan of boomer-shooters, horror games, and especially Blood, absolutely buy this game. This is the Blood 3 we deserve.EXTRA-For the Blood 2 we deserve, checkout Blood: Death Wish, a modded campaign by Bloatoid. It has more varied encounters and vistas, authentically continues the story of Blood without being the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that Blood 2 The Chosen was. Very creative use of the base games voice clips and is even better than the original Blood, a good sequel should be.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. Absolutely one of the best in this genre. Definitely worth picking up. It's one chapter so far, but it's super high quality, lengthy,  and well worth the cost. Atmosphere and level design are top notch. Weapon feel/feedback is excellent. I think this model of releasing a singular (but extremely cohesive and polished) chapter at a lower cost, then later releasing additional chapters as DLC is much better than the Early Access model that a lot of indie developers opt for.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I usually don't get my money's worth on games under 10$, where to start...- Intricate level design with full-featured set pieces, linear maps broken up by expansive hubs to explore- STUFFED. WITH. SECRETS.- Diversity of enemy design, hitscanners, ghouls, and others balanced out with eldritch horrors. You will usually always know if an encounter is oncoming if you're careful- Full Arsenal of weapons each of which can be upgraded for differing play styles run-by-run; moreso you can just main one or two weapons (short and a long range, or even the hatchet and TNT if you like)- The shotgun is good (at close range)- The jump is REALLY good (vastly underappreciated)My only cons? They're not cons they're actually pros I just hate horror:- Heavily atmospheric, the dev really knew what he was doing going for the dithering style and combining in a lot of well-paced BGM and haunting sounds backed up with environmental cues and lore that makes the setting cause the hairs to stand up on the back of your neck- Occasional jumpscares that will make you lose your ♥♥♥♥ the first playthrough, these are easily remedied with explosives and FIRE FIRE FIRE on the next ones- two or three enemy types that are completely, pissantly annoying but you'll get good at peering through the darkness and atomizing them with time and experience.Either way if this was 40$ I'd suggest waiting for a sale, solid buy at 25$, but this is an ABSOLUTE BUY for 10$.

I was stoked when Blood: Fresh supply was released after having not played the original for 15 years or so; but this game is a huge step-up from that. Physics, pacing, level-design; they all feel like a well-made, modern FPS with the aesthetic of its inspiration. Nice!!

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is a worthy successor to Blood. It's a very solid retro fps game with excellent mechanics, striking levels and fun gameplay supported by a highly original arsenal.For me, the game's greatest strength lies in its nostalgic and sublime art direction, which creates an oppressive, unsettling atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: A classic First Person Shooter game that ticks all the boxes.  + Gameplay+ Soundtrack+ Feel of nostalgia+ Graphic style  CULTIC is a fantastic game that brings back memories of classic first person shooters like Duke Nukem 3D and DOOM. The gameplay is smooth and satisfying, with a wide variety of weapons and enemies to keep things interesting. The soundtrack is also excellent, with a catchy, old-school inspired score that really adds to the atmosphere of the game.One of the standout features of CULTIC is its graphic style, which combines retro-inspired pixel art with modern lighting and particle effects. The result is a game that looks and feels like a classic shooter, but with a level of polish and detail that you don't often see in games of this type.In terms of playtime, CULTIC offers around 2-3 hours of gameplay, with 10 maps that take around 20 minutes each to complete. There are also a number of achievements to unlock, including an extreme difficulty setting that will challenge even the most skilled players. Thankfully, the game allows you to save and load your progress, which makes it easier to tackle the more difficult achievements.Overall, I would highly recommend CULTIC to any fan of classic first person shooters. It's a simple, yet highly entertaining game that will appeal to fans of the genre, and is definitely worth checking out if you're looking for something fun and nostalgic to play. 2 - 3 hours  Just great (Can be done in a single playthrough, if you follow a guide)  Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried the demo a few weeks ago and it was so good that I voluntarily forced myself to stop playing so I could enjoy the full game on release date. And it was very much worth it! The game seems even more polished now and the flow of this game is incredible. I play it on Very Hard currently, and it feels a bit like a tactical shooter, no joking. You kill quickly but so do the enemies. Guns are all very satisfying. There is bullet time every so often when you land a headshot on the last enemy in the room. The levels are not too big and I find them easier to navigate than DUSK's maps and certainly easier than the horrific maps in Project Warlock II. The look is, of course, very reminiscent of Blood, from the animation of burning enemies to the cultist enemies with their brown hoodies, and in fact I love Cultic for the possbility to finally play Blood with a modern engine behind it. But don't get fooled by the looks! The game is nowhere near as unfair as Blood, you don't have to cheese and savescum. When I think of it, it is in fact way more like Brutal Wolfenstein. The flow, the movement, the type of WW2 guns feel way more like you are in an old game from id Software. The graphics though are much, much better in Cultic and at times actually impressive. Strangely enough, the music reminds me of yet another game, namely Grim Dawn and it suits the setting very well! But enough with all the comparisons! It is the curse of every pioneer's child to get compared to their ancestors. But let me assure you that Cultic is still very much its own game. Just try the demo and see for yourself. I, personally, was ultimately sold on the game when I heard the UI sound and how it crescends slightly whenever you hover over another option, and when you finally click on it, there is this culminating and yet somehow funnily disappointing climax. I almost had a sonic orgasm. They usually just don't make games like this anymore. Just imagine how I can be more satisfied by the UI sound of a menu than by a full blown Ubisoft game with 13 different DLCs! So do yourself a favour, buy the game already! Buy it! It's a tenner for Pete's sake!

_childDocuments_.review: Relatively short boomer shooter, though I'll have to say it stays exactly as long as it is welcome. This is good.The game is fun especially because the dumb enemies with their short aggro range let you approach enemy encampments and pick them apart at your leisure. It mixes this in with close-in combat where there are mobs who rush you, or mobs who ambush you. The game definitely convinces you that accuracy is key and you should conserve your ammo and then you do so good at it you have enough grenade launcher ammo to wipe the boss no sweat.I think the best part is the level design. It'll have you going back to places for reasons you never expected or in ways you didn't think you could. That said, it isn't using clever tricks from old game engines in new ways; this is a modern engine with a retro skin. Because of that, there's no map as I imagine there are no sectors from which to build an automap with.The only small critic of the level design is that I could tell that in the latter half of the game, the dev spent less time on secrets. I could only guess that's because you've been showered with items at that point anyway.Another great part of the game is that the guns sound really good to shoot and have really fun animations for both shooting and reloading them. A real work of art there.The goons you fight are mostly fairly samey, with some horrors thrown into the mix for good measure. But the price and the length of the game are an excellent match; you should play it if you like boomer shooters, authentic or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is an outstanding endeavour in old school FPS design and implementation, which is particularly impressive as it was a solo project. I've read opinions it's a (spiritual) sequel to Blood and I can certainly see the connection; but the game also has its own ideas, making it something more than straight up Blood worship (not that it would necessarily be a bad thing). It's great, probably one of the best retro shooters available now - can't wait for second part, which has already been confirmed a DLC/expansionGood stuff:+ Combat will feel familiar to fans of Build engine games, but particularly Blood, with its slightly floaty movement and similarity in the weapons department. There's a decent enemy variety and unlike in Blood, they're all fun to fight.+ I really like the art style. It mixes old school FPS nostalgia with its own take on retro visuals, without blatantly copying other titles.+ Amazing horror-inspired atmosphere; new levels will often start off slowly to build up an oppressive mood before unleashing hordes on the player. Scripting to build tension is used sparingly and intelligently, without becoming bothersome. Certain section of the game reminded me of RTCW's crypt section, while another one gave off strong Stalker vibes - good stuff.+ Level design is also superb; while the setting doesn't stray too far from horror classics (spooky forest, mine, mental asylum, etc.) each map feels different enough to not be boring. You'll get a claustrophobically tiny crypt level, followed by a really expansive foresty one, and then a semi-cramped mine map. That's just smart design. Plus, you get a fair bit of verticality and multiple approach options in some of the maps.+ While the game is fairly short - I finished the currently available part one in a little less than 6h on Very Hard difficulty and some secret hunting - there are absolutely no fillers here, it's a banger from start to finish. Plus, it's only 9 quid for this kind of superb experience. It remains to be seen if part two will be an equally good back for the buck, but right now, you can't go wrong with Cultic.Bad stuff:- No major issues I could find. Sure, the performance could dip to 50 fps occasionally, some textures were misaligned, enemies sometimes got stuck on props, but nothing that noticeably hindered my enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: A retro-style FPS that honestly surprised me of how good it is. I started gaming a bit late, so I didn't have any fond memory of retro FPS games with this style. At first I was skeptical that I'd enjoy this the way other people do. But damn, from the very first level, it hooked me in. The gunplay and combat sandbox especially sold this game for me. Despite using 2D sprites for enemies and your weapons, the animation and weapon recoil make the combat weighty, punchy and satisfying. Nailing a headshot with the repeater feels so good in this game.The enemies are also well done. Each of them serves a purpose in pressuring the player to use the right tool and keep them on their toes. As the game progresses, you get to upgrade your weapons and become stronger, but more supernatural enemies join the fight to keep up the pace. It's the mix of challenge and power fantasy all the way through.Each map has well crafted layouts with decently paced combat, exploration, cool set pieces and atmospheric horror. Experiencing this blind (not literally, just not looking up walkthroughs) with my headphones on was one of the few games that made me sit and finish the game from start to finish.But it's not really finished since this only has the first chapter. And honestly, the first chapter being 4 hours long, brimming with content, secrets, and variety of each level, is already more than worthy of the price. I'm eagerly looking forward to see what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr; It's a good shooter, it's a fun shooter even if you're not into "boomer shooters", AI has some flaws, but the game really ramps up in quality as you progress through it.I'm a fan of "Boomer Shooters" but I find most of them to be pretty stale or boring as they rarely try to do anything that improves upon the Boomer Shooter™ approved formula, CULTIC however, leans pretty hard on trying to provide the player with a fresh and interesting experience.The movement and shooting feel responsive and meaty, navigating the maps feels good and every gun packs a punch in its own way. The guns themselves are also pretty good, with a really good selection of weapons, and there's very little redundancy between them, the balance with ammo availability is well done as there was just enough ammo for me per map as long as I put some thought into managing how I'd spend it.The music is good, sometimes really good, in the sense that the tracks were really fun to listen to and they made every scene better by having their respective tracks, however the later portion of the game contains a lot of really long sections where the music loops non-stop until you leave them, these sections are worsened by this since the tracks have somewhat repetitive rhythms and dynamic changes that make the looping and the repetition of the rhythm stick out really hard. Enemies are also hit or miss in a similar way, every design is fun and "charming", in a weird satanist cult sort of way. It's very easy to read each enemy sprite despite the game's colour scheme, they fit in nicely with the theme of the game and are used well in each level they're in, and ranged enemies are projectile-based rather than hitscanners like in BLOOD, so your dynamite can be used in more elegant ways than just for cheesing around every single corner a level features. However the AI on certain locations acts irrationally by charging you when it would have the advantage holding its ground to be able to shoot you, larger enemies can be easily cheesed because they don't back away when you go inside a crawl space or a room they can't get through, and even though there's an achievement to kill an enemy while it is holding an explosive barrel, I only saw said enemy ever grab an object and throw it at me twice in a playthrough, and it missed both times while I was walking at a normal pace. There is a single instance of what I'd call "reskinning" enemies, and even though usually this is seen as a bad thing, I thought it was pretty fun due to the context of the level.Now where the game truly shines is its level design and pacing. The game starts in a pretty simplistic manner, just about what you'd expect from this sort of game. But over time it really picks up, each level feels pretty unique and sticks out in its own way, the action in each level was well paced out and I never really felt like encounters were repetitive. What surprised me in a good way, was finding myself in really tense situations, CULTIC has genuine horror segments at time and that's pretty great, they serve to slow down the pace of the level at the right time, and are the proof that the game's atmosphere is executed excellently. Overall I feel like CULTIC's an excellent game, it's a really fun shooter that I think even people who aren't into "boomer shooters" would enjoy if they're up for some horror-themed action.  It's definitely worth playing if you want a game that actually does something with the "boomer shooter" trend rather than just going with the flow,

_childDocuments_.review: Blood's cooler younger brother.CULTIC is a magnificent solo project where you play as a detective investigating a mining community in the mountains to discover it has been taken over by a mad cult devoted to a force known only as "The Will". The cultist swell their ranks with devoted robed lunatics, combat specialists equipped with special weapons, as well as hulking monsters and other shambling things. Very large enemy variety that you don't really see until a few levels in. Speaking of, the levels are surprisingly large and varied, with towns, rocky forests, mines, crypts, even one that takes place on a cargo ship. The game is pretty linear, though with side paths and secret areas to reward explorers. They're well designed, with several memorable set pieces and little moments that will incorporate key hunts (though not as tedious as the retro games that inspired it), switch pressing, or light puzzle elements (usually just putting a thing in another thing).Weapons are a selection of retro designes from the Mauser (obv inspired by RE4's Red9), a mare's leg, sawn-off shotgun, Sten smg, FG42 paratrooper rifle, & China Lake. All are satisfying and upgradeable (though the shotgun seems a bit weak starting off). My only non-complaint about this entire fantastic game is that the first person sprites don't change with certain upgrades that you'd think would make them look different, like the pistol stock or smg increased magazine.If you're a fan of retro shooters or are looking for a game with a unique "spooky" tone, don't miss CULTIC.

_childDocuments_.review: I was utterly captivated by CULTIC, a retro-inspired horror-themed FPS that shines brightly in the recent resurgence of the genre. Drawing inspiration from classic games like RE4 and DOOM '93, as well as other shooters of that era, CULTIC may not be as lengthy or complex as a modern full-budget title, but it throws its punches where it matters.The exceptional sound design truly elevates the experience. Each weapon boasts a distinct sound, and the auditory feedback from headshots, exploding cultists, and environmental events masterfully informs the player without the need for visual cues. The mechanical clatter of weapons and the visceral, guttural sounds of enemies disintegrating into gibs make the entire experience intensel satisfying.CULTIC's level design is superb and engaging, offering a consistent variety of level types that create unique arenas for gunplay. The atmospheric, sprawling environments encourage exploration, while the smaller, more compact areas are intricately detailed and immersive. Although the sprite-based visuals can occasionally make it difficult to spot distant enemies, this minor issue doesn't detract from the overall quality. Each level is distinct and inventive while maintaining the game's cohesive theme.The movement mechanics are swift yet versatile, allowing for fast-paced action or more strategic, measured gameplay.Your arsenal functions as a versatile toolbox, with specific weapons and equipment tailored for different situations. The real fun is in adapting your tactics and weapon choice to each encounter. I dont want to spoil any specific details, but I will say that CULTIC offers a unique and interesting loadout.The story is simple yet intriguing. A game like this doesnt need a good story but its a pleasant surprise to find one. I'm not typically one to read every note and letter in games, but CULTIC held my attention with its environmental storytelling and supplementary notes. I couldnt wait to discover every bit of exposition and world-building the game had to offer.The visuals pay homage to the sprite era of FPS games while incorporating modern, stylized flair that sets CULTIC apart from the rest.It may seem odd to say, but CULTIC doesn't necessarily break new ground in gameplay. Instead, it builds upon a tried-and-true formula, what it takes from its inspirations it executes flawlessly. I was surprised when the credits rolled and I learned that this game was made by one guy. You can tell that this is a passion project with a ton of talent behind it and I can't wait for the next chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: One solo developer has created one of the best first-person shooters ever made.Whether screwing around and enjoying the atmosphere and acrobatic flow of combat, playing with the many fun toys in your arsenal at a low difficulty, or sprinting, leaping and crawling from desperate moment to moment at the highest difficulty, 'Extreme', in which each enemy is a potentially lethal threat... It simply has a sense of flow and good balance and sheer *fun* I haven't seen achieved so well since FEAR, while evoking rich atmosphere, tension and excitement with low-detail but beautifully lit environments as well as anything has since the original Unreal.Cultic feels as much a Survival Horror as Resident Evil 1 and as much of a horror adventure as Resident Evil 4.The levels are varied in mood and core gameplay while retaining a perfectly consistent aesthetic and atmosphere throughout, all the more remarkable for choosing a bizarre fusion of true 3d gaming, 2.5d style sprites, and voxel-sculpted environmental props. The balance of action and horror, tension and catharsis was excellent. The freedom granted by the level design to sneak, ambush, lure enemies, rain down explosives from afar, leap in for melee, and mix up all of the above as you struggle through each battle was so much fun!If I were to criticise any quality of the game it would be the use of low-detail sprites for the enemies, with a weak rotation and a lack of rotated views - hitting enemies, reading the damage you're achieving, and recognising their animations for imminent attack can be slightly unclear for someone used to the richer sprite animations of Project Brutality/Brutal Doom, or for someone not used to sprite-based enemies in 3D/2.5d shooters at all.This is all I can find, the only criticism I can muster. The game was smooth, 99% bug-free, completely stable. It didn't annoy me, ever - it didn't bore me, ever. I was eager to go back each day for a few levels at a time until I finished it, something I experience a few times in a decade due to mental health struggles that make concentration and commitment to a game, book or series exceptionally difficult.You should buy this at a high price. Don't wait for a sale, get it now.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Cultic is a *phenomenal* game from one-man developer Jason Smith. Don't be fooled by its retro, OG Doom-like graphics; the gunplay here is as tight and satisfying as any modern shooter. Every aspect of Cultic succeeds: The atmosphere, the visual design, the lore, and most importantly, the gameplay. Cultic is a Doom-like in the sense that you go through the levels and shoot the enemies. The objectives generally never get more complicated than "find the locked door, find the key, go back to the locked door." Each of these steps involves getting past waves of enemies, usually robed cultists bearing everything from hatchets to machine guns, and a few more surprises that I wouldn't dream of spoiling.The guns, enemies, and environments are so tightly designed that I found myself grinning as I picked up a key and heard the grumbles of cultists flooding the room above me. I never got tired of nailing a fast headshot with the level-action rifle, using the slow motion that sometimes triggers on kills to swing my aim and pop another head, and then pull out my shotgun to blast away the enemies rounding a corner to try and surround me. 10/10. If you have ever enjoyed a shooter, you owe it to yourself to play Cultic.

_childDocuments_.review: If I were to describe this game in one sentence it'd be this: Cultic is kind of like Blood... if Blood was made by sane people.Now, if you're anything like me then you probably like a lot of things about Blood. Except the difficulty. Yeah, yeah, I'm sure Blood superfans will come to its rescue claiming that it's all fair and balanced but to me it's just a slog. Cultic gives off similiar vibes as that game: it's cult-themed, visuals and locations are similiar, weapons and enemies are obviously inspired by it. Except that Cultic is actually enjoyable for a normal person. So in short: if you ever wanted something like Blood except - you know - fun... well, this is it.Cultic is a retro shooter with really great oldschool aesthetics and a B-movie horror atmosphere. Chapter One offers 10 levels, all of which are enjoyable and fun to play. You'll be blasting your way through old, rundown buildings, industrial environments, wilderness, caves and all sorts of similiar locales. Lots of shooting, lots of slicing, lots of secrets and explosions - you know the drill. In terms of the setting this game nails it. You really feel like you're infiltrating the hideouts of some crazy cultists and the oldschool graphics add to the charm. The outdoor environments in particular are very, very nice looking. I'm always impressed when a game with retro visuals manages to make me stop and admire the scenery, even in the age of photorealistic AAA graphics.The movement is a bit of a mixed bag. Jumping is great - it's nice to have a game where the protagonist can actually make a high jump by default and get to various secret areas with ease. Movement on ledges and stairs is a bit wonky - very easy to fall long ways down. You cannot change the altitude when swimming by simply looking up or down which is weird.The most puzzling addition is the dash. Ah yes. Of course. DOOM Eternal has dash so now every shooter needs a dash, amarite? Here's the problem: dash only makes sense if it's limited. In Cultic it's not, so you can just dash all the time. What that means is that it's just an annoying version of sprinting. I'd much rather have regular sprint instead of this because crossing large distances is just mashing the dash button over and over. Why?The game has a bunch of features that to me seem like gimmicks that don't really help with anything. You can slide - ok... does it help with anything? I don't know. You can hold Crouch to roll when you fall down to minimize the damage. Cool, but why isn't this automatic? You can unwrap the dynamite bundle and spread it out. I've beaten the game on Extreme with just a few deaths and it never felt necessary so there's that.Dynamite in itself is rather curious. In order to throw it you have to (i) select it, (ii) light it and (iii) throw it. That's three button presses for what could have been just one. Why can't I just press one button that selects, lights and throws / "cooks" the bundle - like most shooters do with grenades - then goes back to the previous weapon? It just feels unnecessary. For the record, yes, I know you have a quick-dynamite button but it doesn't light it up and you still have to shoot it. It's not a big deal, just something that I would classify as a weird design decision.Honestly some gameplay features in Cultic seem to exist just so that the game looks "cooler" in trailers but they don't actually have much of a use in the game itself. Thankfully they're optional so it's not like DOOM Eternal that forces every system down your throat.What else... oh yeah, I don't like the music. At all. It has this low quality thing going on and the tracks themselves sound like they do not really work with the visuals and the gameplay style. It's a polar opposite of something like Incision where the soundscapes literally feel like they're part of the gameworld.Other than that there's not much else to say. The graphical style is great, the gameplay is enjoyable, the environments are fantastic. It's just a really cool game and I'm sure every retro shooter enjoyer will like this one. Great job! Looking forward to Chapter II.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo on a whim, then immediately bought the game and played it through in one sitting. It's that engaging.The combat is a nice mix of frenetic and tactical, rewarding thinking on your feet and using your environment. The art and sound design are top-notch. _childDocuments_.review: If you grew up playing Doom, Duke Nukem, Quake, Heretic and similar games... you don't have a choice: You were born to play this game. It's $10. _childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game! Cultic knows exaclty what a good FPS needs and it goes even beyond that. The weapons all pack a good punch and you have a great feel wehenver your shots land or not. Levels are open enough to offer you some freedom to explore but not too open to make you constantly get lost looking for keys. Also the firefights offer everything, from brief stealth sections, to fast paced twitchy encounters filled with explosions but also slower cover based fights in which precision is the key to win.As for the inspirations the game takes, a lot of people compare this game to blood. While I don't deny that it probably had some impact on the development of this game it reminded me more of resident evil 4, although a lot more fast paced. The only real critisism i can hold against cultic is that even though it offers only 10 levels, the game felt the need of throwing in a survival arena level. Kind of feels like stalling for content even though i feel like the game really doesn't need to do that as it has enough to offer for it's 10€ price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC is a retro-style shooter that that absolutely nails everything it goes for. The soundtrack is fantastic, the visuals are a joy to see in and out of combat, and the gunplay is superb. I played on Extreme for my first playthrough, and I can't imagine playing it any other way. The high damage output from enemies is mitigated by the fact that, with skill, the starting pistol can clear most enemies with 4 headshots (3 when upgraded). This will last you far beyond the point where you find and begin using other weapons. The spritework for the guns, as well as their animations, are just gorgeous.  Every gun feels great to explode, ignite, or pop heads with. The game is really good at building suspense when there's a lull in the action, too. There were even points where I was startled by a few encounters! The secrets in each area aren't too hidden or too numerous, so you won't need to search for a dozen hidden walls in each of the ten levels, and if you get yourself into a situation where you can't backtrack (which is incredibly rare, only happened once for me), you may even be able to grab and stack objects to jump onto to get back to earlier parts of the map!Overall, the game is a massive achievement from a solo dev, and I can't wait for more. I couldn't recommend this enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Very short but very sweet. Is very obvious with the inspiration from Blood, it plays a lot like that game. I played on second highest difficulty, there was plenty of ammo to go around, so pick your favourite tool of destruction and have some fun. My favourites were the lever-action and the good old sticks of boom.There are some nice quality of life features, like being able to to turn off the colour filter. I personally prefer the more colourful levels, but it is great you get the choice.What stands out is the really great level design and how responsive the weapons are. The bosses don't drag on, enemy variety is good, you are lethal but so are they. On the levels, not only is the map layout great, but the subtle approach to storytelling works in the game's favour. There is great music too, in some levels you have tunes reminding me of Hotline Miami.In the end, the flamethrower weapon trivialises some of the tankier enemies which is a shame, but there is also a nice variety of long range and short range engagements. Since the cultist enemies are hitscan, you cannot let yourself stay in the open for too long. Keep moving and they'll miss most of their shots though. And I wish the weapon upgrades were a little more impactful, but otherwise there is little to complain about.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is centered around very grounded classical gameplay and features, but the presentation and design are overwhelmingly unique, straying from the established norms for shooters, with more bold and risky decisions. It offers more. It has hooks beyond the gameplay. The art direction, setting, atmosphere, palette, setpieces and interplay of horror elements are stunning. The developer's keen understanding of outdoor spaces should also be mentioned, harking back to Half-Life's 'Surface Tension' chapter, and arguably surpassing the experience. You rarely feel boxed in unless the developer wants you to. Cultic eschews 'corridor gameplay' for very immersive well-designed theater. It's an incredible package, looks beautiful. A must-play, revives and expands upon the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: "Many barrels! Many new friends!"I guess I'm not the only person who thought Blood was a pretty neat old-timey shooter. Cultic takes a ton of cues from the Build engine classic, thought we have to make do without cheesy one liners this time around, as our protagonist is quite silent.While I'll obviously recommend Cultic, since I quite enjoyed my time with it, I'll have to provide a warning to start off: at the time of writing the game isn't quite completed. Cultic appears to be the first episode, with at least one more coming later down the line, paid for separately. In the time of Early Access games this can feel a bit shady, but for this project I felt the risk worth taking and the price worth paying, even if I can't know what the 'full' game will be like.Oh, and it's a solo developer project, which will always earn an extra point from me!The game takes place in a remote community haunted by missing persons cases. A shady cult has taken root and it is up to you to go in and figure things out. The start of your journey might be rough, but rising from a cold grave is par for the course in these games!The first things to catch the eye in Cultic is the visual style. The game merges old with new, using limited colour palettes and chunky 3D assets together with voxels and 2D sprites to create a look that's just modern enough to function on a technical and gameplay level while retaining the charm of retro games. Cultists, zombies, skeletons and even a damn tank will try to prevent your progress, but copious use of explosives, molotov cocktails and a nice little assortment of classic video game firearms should see you through.The game doesn't do anything groundbreaking with its design, though. Puzzles are simple affairs, exploration and navigation are straightforward enough to ensure you're not getting stuck and enemy encounters come at a steady pace, keeping the player on their toes and providing ample opportunity for blood, gore and guts to spill.All the while the game serves up a buffet of meaty weapon and impact sounds and a nice soundtrack to boot, building tension and promoting the sense of action as appropriate. I do have to point out, though, that Blood cultists had a much better scream when lit on fire, so I'm ducking a point out of the audio score for that.All in all, Cultic is a solid six-hour romp of nostalgia, violence, horror and gore. If you enjoyed Blood back in its day or just want something that looks retro but playes really well, Cultic is a fine purchase to make!Playtime: 6+ hours (Full playthrough)Ratings (1-10)Visual: 9Audio: 7Story: 5Gameplay: 8Overall: 8Posted 28 July.

_childDocuments_.review: Both a superb love letter to the original Blood FPS and a solid game in it's own right, Cultic was 5 hours of classic shooter delight:- taking the classic "exploding DOOM barrel" mechanic and enhancing it with physics and manipulation makes for some wonderfully dynamic combat encounters- each weapon feels distinct and useful while the weapons mod mechanic makes tangible feeling upgrades rather than just boosting stats- a seemingly rare instance of a Lovecraftian horror shooter which, while not a story rich as say 'Call of Cthlulu: Dark Corners of the Earth', still manages to capture both a noire feel and grounded yet grotesque setting through discovered notes and level aesthetics.- the gore is on point...  only thing missing is kicking decapitated headsBasically Cultic is the triumph of one developer, Jason Smith, and I am already looking fwd to Chapter Two whenever he is ready to release it.  While DUSK may be "Blood meets Quake" Cultic was, for me, a more immersive yet still frantic romp in Lovecraftian mayhem both familiar and fresh."Caecux infirmux!" ;)

_childDocuments_.review: It's unbelievable that this masterpiece was made by a single person! It is a bit too samey through out.-Kind of wish there were more variety of enemies, more so visually.-levels can lack a bit of variety as well, though that could be due to the very specific color choice.Boomer shooters are probably my favourite FPS' and this is a legit, top tier one. _childDocuments_.review: I want to take a bite out of this game like its a giant cartoon haunch of meat.The presentation is amazing, it looks good, it feels good, it plays good. Visually, it has a pleasing palette, and a great artstyle, while keeping everything readable. The areas have a continuity and clear progression to them that I like a lot, and I think it’s really neat that you get to return to the area shown in the main menu and opening cutscene.Levels are pretty long, but you can save and come back at any point without issue. There's a mix between more open areas and tighter corridors, and sometimes multiple routes you can take. Exploration is rewarding, there's plenty of secrets, and you'll never be short on ammo as long as you don't rush through everything. When going at my own pace and trying to be mostly thorough I found about half of the secrets.You can approach combat in a more methodical way, or much faster if you know what you're doing. Either way, you can't play like an idiot and expect to get away with it for long. Situational awareness is vital. Take stock of your enemies, use what’s available to you, and aim for the head. Headshots in this game are some of the meatiest, most gratifying ones out there. It's got some fun movement tech as well, but I think it’s better to get the hang of things first before looking that up.The weapons are all really fun and satisfying to use. They're upgradeable, and you'll find the weapon parts necessary for that in the normal environment and secrets. None of the weapons become obsolete later on, your pistol will be as reliable a tool as everything else, no need for it to waste inventory space like some other games. The hatchet in particular is one of my favorite melee options in an fps, not only because it can be thrown (and you can hold 10 at a time), but because you can use it to headshot close enemies if you charge a strike and aim just a bit up. This is a beautiful thing and I’m angry that more games don’t do things like this. I'm a hatchet fan until the day I die.Sometimes the enemy AI can be a bit dumb, especially around doors. Also, molotovs can feel like they can end fights too easily, but they do come with the very real risk of setting your own self on fire if you aren't careful and/or you’re in a tight space, so I wouldn’t call it a free win by any means.The threat from the two bossfights mainly comes from normal enemies spawning in the arena, while you try to manage both them and the bosses themselves. I don't think they're done poorly, but mechanics wise they don't stand out much from the rest of the fps genre. They do have good buildup leading from the preceding levels, and fun presentation.None of the negatives are significant enough to really hamper my experience, and the positives come together in a way that makes this an incredibly solid game. One of the best of the recent retro fps revival, in my opinion. There's a demo to try if you're on the fence, it's what pushed me over the edge to buy it. I got about 3 ½ hours on my first playthrough, and 14 after spending time in the endless mode and achievement hunting. Considering the quality of the game, I think it's well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: An all-around excellent FPS game. CULTIC has the distinction of being one of the few games that has perfectly predicted me as a player.For context, when I started this game, I did so while streaming, so a friend could watch. During our discussion, I would note things like, "The level design here is excellent" or "hey, this is a cool area." Within moments, CULTIC would have me swearing in panic as I realized I'd been pulled into yet another trap, my friend all the while doubled over with glee. The music is incredible. The visuals are haunting, sinister, and detailed in a way that only games with a low-res sensibility can be without alienating modern-day players. The weapons are punchy and fun to use, the sound design is excellent, killing people with dining room furniture is satisfying, and the level design is  good. Insanely good. I can't express to you enough how intuitive and well thought-out the levels are in terms of design. I've spent an awful lot of time crawling around several of these levels and still managed to not see or find everything.I heavily recommend this game if you're into DOOM-esque shooters, action-horror shooters like Blood, or just plain challenging shooter games with a retro aesthetic. This is A-level indie dev work, which is especially surprising given the size of the developer team: one guy.Do yourself a favor and give at least the demo a shot. You'll very likely want to come back for the whole thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful shooter. The guns all feel heavy and powerful. The environments are rich in detail, but you don't need a top of the line PC to play it. Every aspect is so polished, so professional, so damn good.And that soundtrack! It sets the mood so well! Gracefully dancing between bombastic heroics and genuine horror. It's a steal at two bucks, and deserves a place in your next Call of Cthulhu campaign.And hey, if your looking at the screenshots and you don't like the color filtering, you can just turn it off and get more naturalistic color in it's place.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey you… you like first-person shooters? Can’t get past the glory days of the janky 90’s? Oh boy, do 3D Realms and Jason Smith have a treat for you.Cultic is a classic shooter to the core that leans so heavily into its Blood influences I’m shocked Tchurnabog wasn’t the final boss. I can’t remember the last time I was as impressed with a shooter as I was with this one. But I love Blood, so maybe I’m being biased.GAMEPLAY & MECHANICSYou need to be a bit strategic, this game punishes mistakes, but in a way that always seems fair.It is responsive as hell, and when things die there is this really satisfying feeling you get from the shear gore, mixed with the sound that just makes it feel impactful.Enemies are nicely designed, heavily old-school horror film inspired, and make for a pretty good challenge. They can be a little dumb sometimes, but those moments often feel like you got lucky.Level design is impressive, even if some of the levels feel long-winded, and there seem to be entirely too many mines in this game (like goldmines, not explosive ones... but there are bear traps, so watch out for those).The weapons are what you’d expect from a shooter like this, pistol, fast-firing assault rifle, a precision rifle for some accuracy, lots of dynamite, so much dynamite, use the dynamite.Aside from the fairly lengthy 1 chapter campaign, there is also an endlessly enjoyable hoard mode.The environments are very interactable, its impressive how creatively you can make your way through levels.There are tons of secrets to find, and they always feel worth it.PRESENTATIONThe graphics are suitably chunky, meaty, but it works well with the setting, the art style is gloomy, tense, and filled with a sense of mystery and dread.The gore and blood are extremely satisfying. When you kill something, you don’t need to check, you know.Sound design is excellent. It’s not only really good at informing you about what’s happening around you, but it is oppressive, makes the gunfights satisfying, and works to polish off the 90’s shooter feel.The music is also quite good, the perfect addition to the scenes these tracks set.It's just so damn focused, nothing is out of place. Generally when a game is developed by a single person it takes some of the quality out of the game; but not with this one. It gives you a single, honed-in, tightly optimised and balanced little masterpiece. Good show Jason Smith, thank you for this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best damn games I've ever played. I'm actually not that into pure FPS games, for the most part but, this game really does it for me. I love the weapons, especially the feel of them. Between the sound, the feedback, the visuals and the use, the guns are some of the best done in any game I've played. Very little is as satisfying as blowing off cultist heads with the double barrel. Speaking of cultists, they make fantastic enemies. Each of them is different, posing a different kind of threat that keeps you on your toes. You don't get overwhelmed by the many types either. They're introduced incrementally, giving you just enough time to get used to the ones presented before another joins the menagerie. Each type is fun and interesting and provides a decent challenge on their own. The level design is just as excellent. They're sprawling affairs that wind and loop back on themselves at times, but never so much that you can't get a handle on the layouts. They're also interesting, aesthetically. They look great, feel great (not to mention menacing and atmospheric) and each are memorable for their own reasons. The hidden secrets in each level are damn satisfying to find too. Some are fairly obvious and others are much more challenging to find. I, most certainly, have not found all. I spent time in each level hunting them down but, those secrets are tucked away nicely. It'll be fun to go through and search again. The story is told largely by notes you find and environmental storytelling. Really nice stuff. It doesn't shove exposition down your throat. It's just around for you to see, if you pay attention. I really can't get over how damn good this game is. As far as replayability goes. It has it. No secret endings, different choices, or rpg elements. Nothing like that. It's just so damn fun you'll want to do it again. Now that's replayability. Get this game. You will not regret it. Not by half. I can't wait until chapter two comes out. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have go fantasize on the edge of my seat.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW FOR CHAPTER ONE (16/10/2022)SHORT REVIEWCULTIC is a first-person shooter. You play as a detective who travels to the wilderness after numerous people and an investigator go missing. The detective themselves get jumped and murdered, before waking up in a pile of bodies with renewed energy. If you ever played a Build game then you'll be right at home. Plenty of weapons, tons of enemies, locations are big and wide and the difficulty spike is smooth.LONG REVIEWSTORYIn 1963 several people have gone missing in the New Grandwell wilderness, and when an Investigator has gone missing a Detective is sent out to find out what is happening. But the moment the Detective arrives, they are ambushed by Cultists and murdered, thrown into a pile of dead bodies. Miraculously, the Detective is brought back to life and sets off to stop these cultists with renewed energy.Each level has notes and readables that provide little bits of world building information specific to each level, as well as notes left by the missing Investigator who explains what had been happening.GAMEPLAYWEAPONSCULTIC has plenty of weapons the Detective can use against the Cultists. You have the traditional Pistols, Double Barrel and Rifles along with some unique ones like the Lever-Action and Grenade Launcher to name a few. These weapons can be upgraded at Workbenches to increase certain stats and provide new features to use.ENEMIESAs the Detective moves further into the wilderness more and more enemies begin to appear. At first it'll be just Cultists wielding firearms but slowly more and more horrific, undead creatures begin to take stage. Each enemy has a unique style and a weapon to counter them.LEVEL LAYOUTOne spot that CULTIC shines (for me at least) is the level designs. The majority of levels are vast and open, with plenty of spaces to explore as well as small linear sections to help guide you on the right track.OVERALLIf you're a fan of boomer shooters and want to add some horror to your usual run-and-gun fun then I highly recommend CULTIC.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this one blew me away. I played the Demo for CULTIC before release and thoroughly enjoyed my time with the first stage. The full release (at least, chapter one) does not disappoint. The level design here is fantastic. You'll want to take your time to uncover all the secrets, which are sometimes tricky to locate but never frustratingly so. Gunplay and movement is suitably responsive, chunky, impactful, and just plain satisfying. But by far the best part of CULTIC is its aesthetics and inspirations. Cultists wield strangely familiar shields, (like the castle ganados in RE4), areas are appropriately gloomy and atmospheric, and the storyline conveyed by notes and journals is simple but full of campy fun. I also feel that the upgrade mechanics provide a bit of replayability (apart from replaying stages) providing for specialization in different weapons. My only serious con is that by the end of chapter one some of the surroundings begin to feel a bit samey: similar color palates of earthy browns, green, and grey muddle things a bit. But it isn't so bad as to kill my enjoyment of the stellar gameplay and environment. If you enjoy games like DUSK, DOOM, and, of course, Blood, you will enjoy CULTIC. You might also see shades of Bioshock here with the mixture of linear and open level design, weapon handling, and a sense of being in an otherworldly place. The price point is just right--what are you waiting for.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This is well worth your time if you like horror and boomshoots, especially if you feel that most modern games just don't give you enough explosives. At times I've had nearly 50 sticks of TNT in my pocket in this game and I've had a wonderful time using them. Maintaining a spooky atmosphere is difficult when you're carrying such a huge and effective arsenal, but Cultic somehow pulls it off: the sudden appearance of a ghost or harvester can invoke genuine panic as you frantically backpedal and fumble with your weapons. Combat is pretty deadly - just standing out in the open will get you cut to pieces quickly - but a well-placed headshot will put most foes down immediately, so there's a good balance of lethality between player and enemy. Unusually for this genre there's actually a good variety of ranges to combat, from mazelike hallways to big open areas, so weapon choice is key to success. It's fortunate, then, that your toolkit is wide, interesting, and upgradeable, with each gun suited to different situations. All of them feel great to fire too - enemies gib into bloody chunks, heads explode, burning cultists scream and run around the room, and there's a little bit of bullet time at moments of peak carnage so you can enjoy the spectacle fully. You can even hurl furniture at enemies if you get desperate! I'd advise not to forget to play through the Interlude when you finish the story: it adds a new level, a new perspective, and some new guns, and hints at what's to come. Completing the package is a fun and customizable Survival mode, so once you find all the secrets in the main game there's still plenty to keep you occupied. I was shocked to discover after playing that this was the work of a solo dev - congratulations to him for such an achievement. At only £8.50 it's a steal; I'll look forward to the next chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: Written from a perspective of a fellow FPS gamedev.short version: It is an absolute must playThe game was recommended to me by a friend, and at first glance, I was reluctant to pick it up because of sprite weapons and enemies. I'm biased toward full 3d games of the bygone era: Quake, Unreal, Half-Life, Return to Castle Wolfenstein, Soldier of Fortune, etc.However after giving it a fair fighting chance I fell in love with it, and totally forgot about my initial reservations. This game takes cues from all the great FPS-es of yesteryear, mixes it up and builds upon the industrial knowledge with immaculate taste and restraint. Playing through the game, I couldn't help, but to get reminded of all the games I played back then, plus many more, seeing their design spirit and philosophies implemented once more.This game is one of the best solo-dev games I had a pleasure of playing. All of the technical and design elements keep a rock steady, high quality bar, and I haven't encounter even one element, that would stuck out from this excellence.The storyline is a classic throwback to the occult themes of games like blood, doom, quake, or wolfenstein. The lovecraftian deep dive from harmless cultists through possessed metal patients, finishing up on demonic beasts from horror worlds. I just keeps getting more and more twisted and hellish.Wrapping up, I want to give a big hearty thanks for including my all time favorite: the FG42 (which I fell in love with long ago by playing Return To Castle Wolfenstein), and making it such a satisfyingly powerful battle implement.From one dev to another: Hats off. Games like these is why I wanted to work in this industry in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering CULTIC was made by just one guy, it's probably the most impressive game I've ever played. Movement and combat is so smooth and responsive, and the rush you get from blowing an enemy's head off never gets old. The level design is on point and meshes well with gunplay. A wide variety of different enemy types and arena layouts make every fight unique, and more importantly fun as hell. The story was understandably not the main focus here, but the gritty 1960s gumshoe aesthetic captured my interest. The art style is seriously impressive given the nature of boomer shooter graphics. Jasozz Games knows their colour theory.  The game managed to instil dread in me without it ever feeling cheap or undeserved. And for those like me who can't handle jumpscares, I only remember one or two minor ones. I also seriously appreciate some of the quality of life settings included here, such as being able to centre the UI for ultrawide players, and a speedrun timer. With the level of polish and attention to detail CULTIC boasts, it's almost hard to believe everything was built by one person. This is an S tier Boomer Shooter, go play it!

_childDocuments_.review: An exemplary boomer shooter. I picture this like a cross between Blood and Prodeus. If you like shooters you will like this. Only chapter 1 is available so far and it took me about 5-6 hours to get through and that was with taking my time to look for secrets. More chapters are surely forthcoming so I'm sure I'll get my money's worth.It's always very satisfying to bean a cultist with a bundle of dynamite. One thing I wish was changed? The animation on your lighter when you switch to dynamite or molotovs feels just a hair too long - there is a small but awkward dead zone between when you have the lighter out and when you can actually light the thing and I wish this were faster. That small difference could mean the difference of throwing a molotov at the perfect moment to burn up a chokepoint or doorway and all the enemies getting through said blockage before the fire is down.The sprite work and their hitboxes could use a bit of polish. I saw plenty of cases where an enemy got stuck in a door or on a corner because the very edge of their sprite was blocked. Feels a little bit janky at times.But don't take these comments as nitpicks. You see the Overwhelmingly Positive reviews. This is a good game, no doubt about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to write a review for this so bad, but I have to first get over my physical and mental trauma I got from playing the game, maybe I´ll force myself to finish the review this year...Edit 07.01.2023: Working on a video review about the game now, I don´t think I can put all this in textOk, so I recently played the game a bit more and I can now confidently explain my problems: -The biggest issue is that the game takes inspiration from games like Blood or Dusk but fails to execute what these games did, both of those games manage to get the spooky atmosphere down better than cultic and also have more enjoyable gameplay-I think the game plays too slow. It is trying to go for that spooky atmosphere by being a slower shooter but both Blood and Dusk got a good atmosphere despite being more fast paced-Combat doesn´t feel good. Ok, let me elaborate my problems here: First of all you are basically forced to headshot or you wont deal any damage, I tested it and on Very hard you need about 9 shots from your pistol to the body to kill an enemy and 4 to the head... This is just way too much in my opinion. Enemys are way too tanky making combat boring, because you are very squishy. If you run out of armor you are basically dead in 3 or 4 hits. Enemys also seem to have unlimed precision even at the greatest of ranges making long range fights undesirable. Secondly enemys should be easily recognised, just like in blood they wear different coloured robes so they can be distinguished. Or so you would think... The grey robed cultists either hold a relatively harmless pistol or an absolutely devastating Sten submaschinegun that will annihilate you as soon as you are in their line of sight. And then the brown robed guys. They are either comepletly harmless and just throw hatches at you or they  are armed with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grenade launcher that almost kills you with the first shot. And lastly I think the enemy roster is too small, but not in the way that it needs more enemys but rather there is a specific type of enemy missing. So in the game you either have enmys that are killed in like 5 bullets or less or you have enemys that were boss encounters and take like 90 bullets. That is just really annoying as there are no enemys in between, so you either fight bullet sponges or cannonfodder. -Headshot mechanic: I really like the headshots in the game, they feel good. It´s a bit boring you are forced to do them to deal serious damage to your enemys but it´s ok. But now to my problem: sometimes randomly when you gib an enemy or their head, a slowmo will play. This is either annoying, when the enemy is far away and you can´t really see the head exploding or when the enemy is the last one standing after a big fight and you just want to move on. Sometimes this also gives you time to react to a situation but that´s the exception in my experience. It just feels weird to have this feature just randomly implemented, I don´t see a reason to have it, especially since explosions also sometimes trigger this and it´s just even weirder when you can´t even see the viscera of the exploded enemy but still there is a slowmo. I would´ve really liked it, if this was a feature of the game that you sort of get this slowmotion bonus for every headshot and it plays similar to superhot, with the difference that you don´t have to stand still but play well and headshot cultists.So TL;DR: The game tries to be a spiritual successor to games like Blood or Dusk, but can´t hold up to those games and has very boring combat due to enemys either dying too quick or taking way too long to kill and then there is the sometimes annoying headshot mechanic that just gets in the way of the player and is only sometimes cool. I can see the good game, it just has too many flaws for me. Feel free to disagree and state your own opinion in the comments, maybe I will update the list in case there is something else I want to get off my chest. I will be checking out chapter 2 to see if the game improved.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into retro shooters of any kind, like Blood, Duke Nukem, Classic Doom or the more recent games like DUSK, Cultic fits right in with the best of them.Here's some gameplay if you wanna skip in, but the DEMO should sell you on it There are some levels that stand out as my favorites, and some that are almost too accurate to the classic games Cultic is trying to replicate (some levels are like a maze), but I never found myself fully lost which is a testament to the level design.Gameplay is solid with gun sound effects really adding some weight to the gunplay, but for me the star of the show is the OST.. this soundtrack SLAPS.Some levels have sections that adopt a sort of horror element, which was surprisingly refreshing, but most of the gameplay is just shooting dudes across the map.Overall, I recommend Cultic.
