_childDocuments_.review: Brutal, crunchy and inventive. Cultic really captures the feel of old-school FPS games with a simple but visceral core game loop, but manages to feel unique by adding a whole bunch of unique gameplay elements and small touches that just show how much thought has gone into everything on display. If you use the level-action rifle while you're holding your lighter, the character will reloading by spinning the gun around his hand, Terminator 2-style. You can slit a bundle of dynamite to throw a cluster that has a much wider range. You can kick enemies projectiles back at them!Even with the gameplay, the environments are the star of the show. Each level is absolutely enormous, but still has lots of small touches that make the world feel like it has a history. Tonnes of well-hidden secrets as well, which are actually worth finding due to the weapon upgrade mechanic that uses special hidden pickups. There's also a lot of variation to the locales, creating unique and memorable set-pieces rather than the ubiquitous corridor-room-corridor-room design that's common with a lot of throwback shooters.If you like 80s horror and 90s shooters, I absolutely cannot recommend this enough!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. If you have even a cursory interest in throwback shooters, Cultic is a treat. While it could have very easily been a (great) Blood clone, Jasozz managed to out do Blood in many ways. A few updates since launch has added some nice features like mission replay and an enemy randomizer (in beta).Cultic Episode 2 is gonna be fantastic

Atmosphere is off the charts, but don't think this is a horror game, you're the monster here.I kept putting this off, stupidly thinking it's a blood ripoff/clone - there are clear homages, sure, but gameplay-wise, CULTIC does its own thing, and it does it so f**kin well - it doesn't play it safe, it's not some other 'generic boomer shooter'.

_childDocuments_.review: Another fantastic addition to the boomer shooter genreControls are really tight, gunplay is fun and rewarding and the map design is *chefs kiss* with it both looking believable and lived in while also giving you great places to maneuver in both combat and in map progression. Only one map gave me a sense of "I have no idea where I'm going" but I feel that was the purpose of the design. A little on the easy side for veteran boomer shooter players, but still definitely something to experience with the environmental story telling being interesting enough to have me reading diary logs.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Up until now, BLOOD has sadly been excluded from the boomer shooter revival scene. CULTIC is a spiritual successor that, while being drenched in BLOOD, manages to have its own style and bring something new to the table. Also I don't see anything in CULTIC's story that conflicts with BLOOD's, they're also both in the hands of 3D Realms, so I'm choosing to believe they are canon to each other. Enough said, it's good, buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Balls what a good game, like jesus you would not think this was made by one person. It has just enough old school game mechanics mixed with new game mechanics and tech to keep you having fun the entire time, the running slide and jump kicking makes you feel like an action hero and the game rewards you for precision aiming. That and there are plenty of easter eggs scattered around giving references to classic media.

_childDocuments_.review: If Dusk = Quake + Blood, and Hrot = Chasm: The Rift + Quake, then CULTIC = Blood + Unreal.May be a bit short for 10 bucks (It took me about 3 and a half hours to beat), but it's a love letter to the sub-genre that I cannot recommend enough.Everything just feels right - the levels are interesting and have their own set pieces and gimmicks. The soundtrack is great, the graphics capture the feel of the era. All of the weapons feel good to use (although some are hilariously OP compared to others), and none of them ever feel useless (but some, like the molotovs, can be highly situational).Nothing feels unfair, and most of the secrets don't take psychic powers to find (although a lot are easily missed).I look forward to Chapter Two :)

_childDocuments_.review: A 2D stylized boom shooter following the styles of DOOM, Quake, and other such run-n-gun style titles. Players take control of a nameless cop who wakes up in a mass grave, as a conspiracy involving an ominous demonic cult begins to take control of the surrounding woodland. You can dash, slide, kick, explode, and headshot streak your way through each level in a variety of ways. Guns are varied and there is one for each niche of playstyle, intended to complement player movement and aligned targets (rifles, shotguns, pistols, explosives, etc). I particularly enjoy the art style, which is a grimy pixel nightmare filled with grotesque monsters and creepy cultists. The level layouts are fun and exciting, prompting players to find secret areas filled with helpful boons along the way. As the game currently is, its well worth the price, having some extra replayability for those looking to stretch their speed running and parkour skills.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I played Blood it has kept its spot as my favorite classic shooter of all time. Since then, however, I've yet to find something that could be considered a spiritual successor of sorts to Blood, but, thanks to CULTIC, I can say that search has finally come to an end. The artstyle and atmosphere blend together perfectly to create a sense of horror and dread not found too often in many games nowadays. The pixel graphics are a personal favorite of mine, somehow amplifying the violence of blowing someone's head to smithereens and having their eyes pop out whole. For the price, too (as of writing this review it is 9.99 USD) it is quite a steal. It is currently 10 levels as of me writing this and each one is quite lengthy. On my first play through I combed every inch of every map and my total playtime came out to about 9 and a half hours. For 10 dollars that is insane. And the best part is this is only Chapter 1. I cannot wait to see what they have in store for future chapters. All I know, though, is I will be buying them on launch.Even if you've never played Blood, you'd be foolish to not pick this game up if you consider yourself a fan of shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Retro-esque shooter with some of the best fast movement ability and skill based flick-shooting around.  Seriously it's like taking a base around Doom but stylizing it with Counter-Strike gunplay mixed with Mirror's Edge speed boosting tactics.  Amazing speed run game, can't wait for chapter 2.  Overall it takes about 3 hours for a playthrough but it's fun enough for multiple runs.

_childDocuments_.review: MAJOR SPOILERS BELOWRelevant Insights to my Cultic Exp: - Played on Hard Difficulty- Did not try to find every secret but found most of them- Already have a sense for these kind of games- Used most weapons, but the STEN was used the least. Focused upgrades: Pistol, Lever Action, Double Barrel, Grenade Launcher, Sniper.- Biggest surprise: can get through most of beginning of the game with charged-up Axe melee with no problem, and also witnessing enemies kick away my TNT. That interaction was cool. Set piece setups are great, and no limitations to how far you can engage the enemies were a great breath of fresh air (and you CAN stealth things if you are able to, believe or not). Deciding whether or not to use a molotov/flamethrower/lantern vs dynamite/barrel changed up certain parts dramatically.I like this game a lot. I think the dynamics of the game play are cool, the level designs are great albeit I am not sure why spiral stairs are such a headache for me in this game, the atmosphere is awesome especially the first time boxes thrown at you in the ship at you don't know why it's happening, music is spooky and sound design is great, the interlude is awesome and I wish there was some more of that, the puzzles are interesting, etc...; In regards to the stairs, I think it's an FOV distortion problem that I have but not sure if other players have. The graphics are great and the color palette is very unique if you take it all in. I love that each level is a giant sandbox with double-backing and looping that is on purpose! Great callback for me personally to games like Quake, Duke, and Doom.It's definitely a 3D Realms game (which is good!) with the level exploration, traversal, and non-hindered use of the entire accessible environment pieces. The AI is definitely your typical AI with some of them being particularly fun to deal with whether it's the snipers laying down in some cases (although I didn't see it that much after the first official encounter with them), the Ghost Cultist throwing things at you and the panic that settles in when it starts like crushing your head or something with it's telekinetic powers, the shield cultists actually using the shield and being a nuisance, the chainsaw cultists second stage of rage, and just the overall aggressiveness of each AI works great for the levels that range from claustrophobic hallways to arena churches. I really appreciated that the monsters and undead were not part of this larger enemy spectrum - they were an opposing force to the cultists and you find them many times either at odds or separated with the cultists fortifying their locations to "defend" their selves from the undead onslaught. Nice touch. I love finding the notes and reading up on stuff. The fact I can pick up stuff to throw barrels and lanterns is great, and hands down one of THE most satisfying things was throwing an explosive barrel and timing shooting it right and watching it work. I just got a few gripes: the interlude was VERY interesting and a great intro, and sometimes I feel that level of contrast isn't met by the end of the game. The sheer "♥♥♥♥ you" of cultists pretending to be officers was so good. I am glad the creepy factor stayed throughout and wasn't just blown on the intro. Something else that bothered me is the Sten is clearly better in the enemy's hands than mine. The church hold-out fight with the Cultists and Tank was very interesting and cool, until I realized the tank wasn't a real threat as long as I had the dynamite and grenade launcher handy which is only underwhelming in retrospect. However that boss fight was DOO DOO. The only reason I had to restart a few times was because of the cultists! That boss needs to hit the gym or something... or perhaps we'll see in Part 2 what's really the big bad? That's probably where the epicenter and culmination of this goes. After all, isn't the entire fight sequence of the game getting us ready for the finale anyway? Like Rocky training for the big night.Closing: Great Game. I can't say I am used to needing to pay for a part 2 of this, but I think a part 1 with interlude on Hard Difficulty or more is where you're going to get the best experience out of this. I got 7.5 hours out of this which is longer than some other "boomer shooters" so it's still a good value. I think paying for a Part 2 is not bad especially if you want to support the efforts of 3D Realms; clearly there's a lot of love put into this game! If you're chasing times, achievements, and secrets then that's where your replay-ability is going to be along with the survival modes. I love that this feels like a voxel spiritual homage to Blood. I loved blowing things up and killing enemies in funny ways, and there's definitely a lot of Easter eggs in this game that you'll find. Yes, I did spend at least 30 minutes of my total play time scouring bathrooms to find the pissing cultist and I found him. Appropriately, I threw TNT at him.

_childDocuments_.review: The , which blossomed in the wake of David Szymanski's 2018 breakout hit , has now been well underway for nearly half a decade. Currently, the genre appears to be teetering between receding back into the pixelated fog of 90's nostalgia, or remaining, as a niche, but well supported haven for wonky doors, questionably balanced weaponry and edgy Satanism.Jason Smith's  manages to make a strong case for the longevity of the , without reinventing the wheel – like, at all. Hell, you begin the game by crawling out of a shallow grave, ala the opening moments of Monolith Productions's 1997 classic . Devotee's of  will immediately recognize the brown robes of the hatchet-wielding Cultist's you encounter only moments later, after entering the . Said devotees are likely to go from bemused to ecstatic, after being reunited with a very dear old friend:  I paid $11.49 for my copy of . The TNT in this game was easily worth $5 of that entry price. It's just, so good. The ability to independently light, drop and/or throw the TNT, while initially a little cumbersome, enables a tremendous amount of problem solving mid-combat. Sense an ambush waiting around the next corner? Huck a stick of TNT, and if your hunch was correct, then prepare for a shower of bloody gibblets to come bouncing around that corner. Being chased by a chainsaw maniac? Drop a lit stick between your feet, as you frantically sprint away, likely while bunny-hopping over several bear-traps in the process.I could go on about how tactile each weapon from ’s diverse arsenal feels to use at great length – especially that bolt-action rifle, which gave me flashbacks to using the  from  – but, I’ll refrain. I will, however, take a moment to note the role ’s exquisite weapon design plays in the moment-to-moment gameplay loop, which often has you charging at the enemy, closing in the distance, then dealing damage and immediately collecting a small amount of health as your reward, before retreating, reloading and finding a new cluster of targets. It feels like a balanced mix of ’s , made famous by Bungie’s Jaime Griesemer, and 2016’s , which incentivized risky behaviour (in this case, melee combat) by rewarding it with health.In addition to designing a fantastic game, Jason Smith has also crafted a rather gorgeous one. ’s distinct palette provides a back-alley miasma of colour: filthy browns, the tainted pinks and purples of a week-old gasoline shimmer, all with the occasional highlight of a piss yellow. It’s an aesthetic that could only be described as a gamble – doubly so, given the addition of voxels, which blend rather seamlessly with the flat, Build Engine-esque sprites. Yet somehow,  manages to make its ugliness compelling, creating an atmosphere that’s far greater than the mere sum of its parts. Oh, and the sky-boxes are genuinely striking at times, which is a Hell of a thing to say about a .This relentless sense of style elevates the traditional, but imaginatively designed levels, giving them a powerful sense of place, the kind that would usually come at the cost of playability. In , however, the arenas are just as engaging to explore after the carnage as they were to strafe around in circles, spewing hot lead and being showered with gibs. I don’t think secret-hunting in a  has ever felt this organic to me, in large part due to that consistency of the level-design, which is maintained through-out, despite each room feeling unique and bespoke.The sole exception to this level-design excellence comes at the early-to-middle-point of the game, when you'll find yourself hopelessly lost in these pitch-black woods, exploring an atrociously recursive space. Maybe my brightness settings are just too low, but searching for those three pieces of that bloody bridge mechanism was beyond frustrating. Funny enough, the sequence much later on, when the player is  trapped in a  maze, was shockingly fun in contrast. It's hard to believe that the same designer who managed to make navigating a honest-to-God hedge-maze interesting also made... . The sequence in the woods reminded me of 's two worst levels, combined:  and ". Thankfully, it doesn't last for very long. And that sequence does end with a very memorable ambush, which almost made the preceding frustration worth it.I eagerly await  of . I'm sure I'll have more to say then.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is yet another entry in this apparent, welcome retro/boomer shooter renaissance. Done in the classic style established by Doom and Wolfenstein back in the 90s, Cultic will definitely scratch that frantic run and gun itch those who grew up during the evolution of gaming seen back in the 90s. However, this time with a welcome horror aesthetic that slightly resembles the themes of Resident Evil 4. When you merge the chaos of Doom with the atmosphere of RE4, you get a tense venture into dark, decrepit villages and dank, foreboding caverns. The narrative isn't all that impressive. It's a game which prioritizes action, so it has a story that definitely carries an intrigue with it, but without overtaking the main objective of fighting to survive. Still it is a story of uncovering the mystery of a cult and various disappearances, and little bits are unveiled as you uncover notes laying around. These notes are scribed as men people fearing for their lives, usually leading to their demise. They are well composed and usually escalate in distress the closer you get to the end, leading you to want to see the fates of these nameless people. As well as trying to understand just how serious all this is as you realize whatever kind of group this is, has some grand plan of potential Armageddon. There isn't much to discuss here, especially not without spoiling the notes, but what is here serves its purpose without being intrusive or necessitated. The visual flair of this game is very distinct, with a retro filtering, displayed with pixelated baddies and weapons and voxelized environments that work in tandem to craft a morbid, yet enticing world to traverse and conquer. There is such a visceral tone, engrossing the haunting lands that are inhabited by insane cultists and mutated beasts that resemble watered down, but inherently disturbing Lovecraftian monstrosities. Trekking through the villages is mortifying on its own, but when accompanied by the atmospheric soundtrack, everything comes alive, either incentivising you to withdraw and heed the imposing warnings of the pure ambiance within the droning, distressing tracks, or a drive to push hard and fast into the intense combat with the energizing metal or operatic pieces.All these details make the gameplay feel more engaging and dynamic. Within the gameplay of Cultic, there isn't a lot of complexity to the overall structure, however, the simple run and gun is tied together immaculately via a diverse array of methods to aid in your survival. You of course have the conventional tool at your disposal. beginning with but a rudimentary, albeit effective ax. It's your conventional melee weapon with a couple of functions. A lackluster swing that can be comboed a couple of times, a heavy swing requires some charge time to enact it, but having a great damage output that can be used to instantly decapitate your opponent, sometimes multiple; as well as when you have multiple on hand, you can throw it. Yes this one can be a bit difficult to land, however, once it's done it's oh so satisfying when you see their heads pop or land on the floor. However, be it through natural progression or secret hunting, this arsenal becomes a little more impressive ranging from a weak pistol, to an empowering shotgun or grenade launcher. Each weapon can be useful in varying scenarios, however, being honest, I found myself using the shotgun, Sten, Lever Action, and the sniper, leaving the pistol by the wayside, and the final grenade launcher as a useful but definite last resort. That isn't to say these are ever to be slept on as I love the pistol, at least when damage boosted.  Especially in the end game, I found myself becoming down on my luck and missing shots with my more powerful weapons (My own flailing) and resorting to my vastly accumulated handgun ammunition and coming out on top all thanks to this little fella I kept stuffed in my pocket for most of the journey. No matter where I stood in the game, every weapon, reluctant though I may have been, got a chance to shine. And with the crunchy, guttural sounds of each and every shot, it provides you an immense sense of power, overwhelming the parading hoards. However, these guns, satisfying as they may be are but a single means of slaying lunatics and savage monsters. You're afforded dynamite and molotovs to provide crowd control. I have to say while I appreciate the molotovs and know for sure they are incredibly useful as they were a Godsend for larger beasts such as the mutations or the shielded cultists as they allowed me to focus on other, less cumbersome foes as their health was either chipped away or they outright demolished their comrades by running through their ranks. Even so, I adored the dynamite so much. I never entered a battle without flinging some boom candles to obliterate the unsuspecting loons. It was great for taking out the grouped goons who were in a tidy circle and just generally for erasing any kind of nuisance who may be hiding behind some cover. Not to mention there were countless moments where my health was super low and rather than risking my head, I just lobbed a bundle randomly towards oncoming enemies to mitigate damage before moving in to collect health and generally regain my bearings. And in the moments where I see no point in wasting precious resources or where I was placed in dire straits, there is always the option of flinging lanterns that serve as makeshift molotovs, or maybe even and explosive barrel to mimic dynamite, but larger. Push comes to shove... throw a chair or candelabra. I played this on Hard and was well equipped most of the time, but I did come into some desperate times. These mechanics, while not the prime technique definitely kept me alive in several moments. This gameplay loop is almost like a dance, much like Doom or any other Doom inspired shooter. It requires you to manage your movements, dodging bullets, priming your shots, or thinking up alternatives when things become concerning. The constant bobbing and weaving, ammo management, and quick reflex driven action makes for always engaging gameplay. When you aren't busy shooting, there are also some secrets to find. Usually it's something fairly superfluous like a bit of ammo; other times it's a weapon or a small bit of lore. These secrets are almost always hidden well, as well as telegraphed so you can see them when entering a room, enticing you to seek it out, giving you a serotonin for actually uncovering it. Others are just kind of plopped under a conspicuous stairwell which leaves a lot to be desired.  This is just the first chapter of a series, so there is a lot to see down the road, but what's here is well worth the price. For me it was a five hour journey, which I know doesn't seem like much, but given this is a one man team, it has a lot to offer. Not to mention with the secret hunting and escalating difficulty, if you're into masochism, there is much in the way of replay value; including the Survival mode which is exactly as it sounds, but on a timer so it acts more as a time challenge. It's really frantic and demands you to hone your skills and understanding of the game's mechanics, but is well worth it as it is good training for the higher difficulties.All in all this beginning is an incredible one. With the gorgeously, grim aesthetic, fast paced gameplay, and servicably simple story, Cultic Chapter One is a shooter for both horror and action fans. If you grew up with DOOM or RE4 I highly advise you look into this as for better or for worse, it's nothing if not a wonderfully chaotic distraction.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game! I don't think I have ever been this excited to share a review of a game and I rarely ever do. From a lifelong gamer and a person spoiled with many options to play whatever game or platform I choose, this game really resonated with me and has landed a special place in my heart. I don't know if it is cause I am older now or because maybe I am over saturated with too many games that sometimes the joy of gaming gets diminished. How is it that I can play an Indie game made by one person and enjoy so much easier than some triple A title like gta or assassins creed? I don't know what it was about the retro style and the music (childhood, 80-90's nostalgia?) that drew me into it? Usually I would be looking for something with more modern graphics and realism.  It was so easy and enjoyable to just pick up this game and play for a session and get into this flow state. Thanks Jason for making this masterpiece! I think is a great example of how an individuals creativity and inspiration can make something so genuine and atmospheric. Opposed to something that already has this cookie cutter mold that corporations endlessly pump out.  Best $10 on gaming I have ever spent.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say its FPS Boomer masterpiece.  Just say it loud and proud.  Coming from you live form 3D Realms a game made by Jasozz Games.  You play detective John Doe (I honestly don't know the man's name) as he trails a cult in the mountain town of New Grandewel. Until he is killed by the cult itself and SOMEHOW comes back to life.  Now filled with anger, he plans on taking revenge by killing the cult and all of its members.  The action is fast, furious, and tough, expect tough fights and enemies you'll never see coming from through your bullet riddle journey.  The weapon controls are on point and the mark.  Everything from a hatchet to your shotgun, you have enough weapons to take down the cult and its members, just keep your eyes out for any secrets.  The best part is that the weapon does have upgrades, everything from faster shots, to alternate fire moods you have enough power to take down the masses, especially when you shoot someone's head off and in slow-mo watch the carnage unfold and seeing their eyeballs left behind.  If there is a complaint, there is one at the challenge level, be prepared to get killed several times from increasing forces from the cult.  Not to say that challenge is a great thing, I am just saying prepared for the tough big fights.  All in all, this is a great game, fun for all ages. 5/5.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true tour-de-force of the new Boomer-Shooter subgenre. I was not expecting to get this level of quality for what I paid.PROS:Engaging gameplay! The guns feel great, the movement speed and controls are just right, and I found it very difficult to not know where I was supposed to go apart from getting stuck for a while in a couple of spots. You can also choose your own playstyle just thru how you engage in combat. You can pick off from afar or barge right in, and the game will not strongly suggest one or the other to you; In fact it seems to accomodate both. Enemies are fairly dumb (which can be forgiven for zombie-type enemies I guess), but not so dumb that it's not a challenge. Excellent sound design!! The game has a very unique collection of SFX that have just the right amount of bitcrushing on them to give them that beloved "crunchy" tone. The gun SFX are especially outstanding in my opinion, they all have just the right amount of weight and it adds a lot to the experience.No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cutscenes!! If I want a movie, I'll go watch one. I'm always chuffed when a developer knows you don't need cutscenes in this kind of FPS. The story is kept nicely out of the way via notes you pick up a la Resident Evil 4, one of two influences this game wears on its sleeve (the other being Blood, as Civvie before me has pointed out).Not unlike DUSK, you can set the graphics to whatever era's style you're into, with plenty of interchangeable retro or modern options in the video settings. If you want just a tad spiky-looking, you can do that. If you want it to look full-on 1996 VGA quality, you can do that too (you sick bastard).CONS:Fairly short experience, though part 2 is in the works (can't wait!)Harder difficulties are devastatingly BRUTAL in this game. But maybe you're into that...The graphics are a bit overly mottled-brown, which isn't something I miss about shooters from the eras this game takes influence from, and I think it could've been left in the past. Really struggling to come up with any more!! Maybe a bit more enemy variety would have been nice.Other than that, I can't think of the last time I was this satisfied by a game I bought. Bigass thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr: Action FPS where the player fights an evil cult with some of the most visceral feeling weapons I've ever experienced.Amazing game heavily inspired by Blood. I also see elements of RE4 and some things that remind me of Return to castle wolfenstein. The player fights their way through an evil cult using a variety of awesome weapons. Literally every weapon is good and feels amazing to use, this game even gives games like dusk a run for their money in terms of game feel. The TNT is peak content, delivering that rare satisfaction of gibbing groups of cultists not felt since Blood itself. The shotgun is literally Blood's shotgun back and better than ever, decapitating any poor SoB that gets your way. Surprise, surprise, a good flamethrower in this game as well.There are many other weapons I will leave unnamed for you to experience yourself.The Graphics are in a strange place for me, some of the areas seem uninspired with reused assets, but the game overall is very nice looking with an excellent style. I know this is an indie game in its purest form so it deserves some slack with some of the arenas feeling samey. For every area that looks similar there is another that is awesome though, there are some amazing set pieces here and there. I get the feeling that this game will get much more impressive visually as the dev gains more experience and begins to really go wild.The music is top tier, the sound design is excellent. The popping of cultist heads never stops being satisfying, the weapons sound as meaty as they should.Honestly the biggest downside at the moment, is the lack of content, the game clocked in about 3 hours for me to complete the first and only chapter. If you want an amazing top tier 3 hour experience and want to help support the dev, buy it now. This is a game to keep an eye on, I think it will be an instant classic similar to Dusk.

_childDocuments_.review: I've talked about in the past how the Boomer Shooter market is full of Quantity over Quality products, with many of them having poor difficulty balance, lack of ammo, bad level design, guns that feel like plastic toys and overall a huge lack of originality throughout the genre. CULTIC however, is not one of them. It's a one man team who has seen many of the best Boomer Shooters and knows what he's doing. I will admit though, CULTIC does start out rough and without any knowledge of how to survive in the first few levels, it can be annoying.My biggest complaint at first was how easy it was to burn through your ammo. You only get three guns at this point in the game so you'll have to switch between a Luger, a Rifle and a Shotgun. But once you realise that your hatchet is your best friend, you'll be saving ammo constantly by using it. It's a beast in the beginning of the game and once you use it for the majority of the first three/four levels, you'll have tons of ammo to get you through the game. Thankfully, this rewards you later as in further levels throughout, the game gives you tons of ammo at the beginning of some missions with a lot of ballistic armour. Another problem I had initially as well was the graphics. They look(ed) extremely ugly for a Boomer Shooter and it was giving me an eye sore. Thankfully, you can make them better by turning off most of the fancy graphics options in video menu. Now the game actually looked great! The game has some really interesting levels and that's where my praises of the game start to coming in. First off, the level design is great! I always love a shooter that dares to be adventurous with it's level design. If you feel like you're on an epic journey, that makes it all the more better and CULTIC has some awesome levels, from a Chapel, to a Mining Town, to the Cult's main base, it's all excellent and makes for some great fun to explore.CULTIC also has some fantastic gunplay once you get into the swing of things. The game has a great variety of weapons that are all effective and sound awesome. Weapon management throughout felt great and I continued to use different weapons in different situations and for some difficult enemies. The game also felt challenging enough while mostly not being annoying. Despite some grievances I have with a couple of annoying enemies, once you get who they are down, you'll be smooth sailing on defeating them quickly.Another great aspect of this game is the music. There are some really great tunes here throughout the game and they really get you excited during many of the gunfights throughout the game. The final moment during the ending got me so pumped up for more, which leads me to probably my biggest praise of the entire game. CULTIC feels complete. If this was just the entire game, I would be sold immediately. But considering there is more episodes coming, I'm excited to see what the developer brings to the table. I can already imagine how good the next few episodes are going to be. But it's amazing how fully fleshed this game is. I beat the game around 2.5/3 Hours, but I cannot wait to play more and come back to this again and again!Overall, CULTIC is a pretty sweet Boomer Shooter that doesn't fall into the Quantity over Quality syndrome this genre has had since DUSK blew up in popularity. Jason Smith, the developer of the game gets what makes this genre work and I am excited to see what comes next for CULTIC. I cannot recommend this game enough. I became enthralled once I nearly reached the halfway point and I feel fans of the genre, who love games like DUSK, AMID EVIL, Ion Fury and Prodeus will love this. A very promising, very awesome game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is a Doom like fast-paced fps that nails a retro aesthetic with modern gameplay mechanics. The game is beautiful and surprisingly visually varied in its 10 levels. In these levels, you will encounter mansions, caves, and enemy bases to raid. Each level complements this truly unique artstyle. The blood, lava, water, and guts/eyeballs scattered around the map all add to the atmosphere. The artstyle is complemented by a great soundtrack that meets every tense moment with a sense of urgency. The shooting is quite simple, but paired with the well designed levels and quick movement, it comes across as really enjoyable. The game can be frustrating at times with stairs being stiff to climb and bullets not going exactly where you want them to, but these moments don’t detract from the game in any meaningful way. The game rewards a run and gun playstyle, especially given the fact that none of the guns are particularly accurate except in close range. I like how it dissuades camping for the most part. On top of the aiming being rather ineffective, enemies drop health when you kill them so it encourages you to go at fights gun blazing knowing you’ll get health if you kill enemies. Unfortunately, the enemy AI intelligence varies. There are some bosses where you can just hide in an unreachable area and shoot pot shots until they're dead. Granted I played on hard difficulty which was the 4th highest, so there is definitely plenty more challenge to be had. At the hard difficulty, the game never felt unfair. There were moments of frustration, but they were self induced and not really the fault of the game. There was enemy variety, but you mostly just ended up shooting at the same enemies with different weapons. The biggest downside is the story. It is essentially a nonfactor and can be largely ignored. You are tasked with uncovering the mystery of a secret cult that leads you deeper into their lair. As you go deeper, the story doesn’t really get any more compelling. There is a cop who went undercover before you and you uncover his field notes. The only thing is you never actually see or meet him, but this could change in the second chapter. Overall, the game works best when you’re just trying to tune out and enjoy some run and gun fps gameplay. The story is nonexistent, so you can just throw on music or listen to the in game music and just have fun. It’s not trying to be anything other than that and I can respect that. It is also made from a  single developer which is an amazing accomplishment. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC's deliberately crunchy aesthetics might be too much for some, enemy AI is easy to exploit, and is short when it comes to story or length. But CULTIC's level design, great soundtrack, and surprisingly deep combat system that rewards experimentation make it more than the sum of its parts, trading in the irreverent tone and quippy protagonist of Blood to channel Resident Evil 4 and mid-90's Lucasarts shooters. CULTIC is extremely impressive for being the work of a lone developer, and Chapter Two will hopefully make this the fully fleshed-out experience it deserves to be.

_childDocuments_.review: A retro-style FPS done right. CULTIC draws heavily from Blood for its weapons, enemies and environments, thought it does so without outright ripping the 1997 classic off. Granted, you'll spend the majority of the game blasting your way through hooded cultists, zombies and other monstrosities with shotguns, submachine guns and dynamite, but in between firefights the game likes to focus on the horror angle, serving quiet moments of palpable tension, usually leading up to the introduction of a brand new type of abominable adversary. The tone of the game is generally more subdued as well, with more down-to-earth creepy locales (don't expect a carnival or a mad scientist's lab) and a silent hero.  The weapon selection is fairly standard, focusing on practicality rather than uniqueness, which is fine by me. The workhorse weapons of Blood are still there, and I never really liked the flare gun or life leech anyway. The guns all feel and perform very well, and their functionality can additionally be upgraded with weapon parts hidden throughout the level which serve as a good incentive for secret hunting. What else can I say, it's insanely impressive that one guy made this game all by himself, and for the price it's at it should be a no brainer for any retro FPS fan.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic boomer shooter. Not quite as hectic as some other titles in this vein, I find that it often encourages more methodical gameplay. The gunplay is very satisfying (headshots remind me of Brutal Doom, which is always a good thing). There are also some customization options for your weapons which become unlocked as the player finds weapon parts in the game world.The sound and visual design are top-notch. All the weapons sound great, even the basic pistol.The story is presented mostly through the environment and through written notes. It is fairly standard (the title of the game pretty much says it all), but is perfectly serviceable as a way to make the world feel more grounded.One small complaint I do have is that the larger enemies sometimes cannot navigate the geometry very competently, resulting in situations in which the player has to go out of their way not to cheese certain encounters. But this is rather infrequent and doesn't really affect anything.In summary, give Jasozz Games your money, they deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this since the first demo, and I really have to say that it is incredible value for money. The passion that has gone into this very clear, and I definitely would like to highlight the most special achievement this game has pulled off: inspiration/homage without being stale or reductive.The game is very clearly influenced by the 90s FPS Blood (with hints of Return To Castle Wolfenstein in the weapon selection and level design), but has managed to be open with these inspirations while carving out its own identity. It is familiar without being a rip off.One of the ways in which the game achieves this is through its unique colour palette. While I was initially turned off by the strange filtering and off-putting colours, over time I grew to appreciate the strength of the design. The deep earth and rust tones, combined with the chunky (for lack of a better word) art style, made the world seem quite grim and oppressive, especially when combined with some of the more gross and sinister character designs (though there is one monster which is meant to be scary but just comes off as goofy due to its animation and behaviours).The combat is visceral and satisfying, with gory headshots and explosions occasionally causing you to go into slo-mo, which really helps you savour the moment. Objects in the world can be used as makeshift weapons and traps, which can really make you feel like an Indiana Jones-esque combat pragmatist at times.The level design is dense and full of exploration opportunities. There is linearity but there are so many rewards for finding secrets that you dont feel too confined to the main path. The highlight for me was probably the path leading to the Asylum level, as there was a good mixture between open arenas and tight encounters.Story-wise, things are pretty threadbare. There are documents scattered around the levels which provide some background lore, but I didn't find them particularly compelling. Luckily, it is not a plot-focused game, so the documents are there mainly to provide flavour as  opposed to deepening the plot.My only real critique is that the music does not match the tone of the game; the grim body horror and evil cult plot elements do not mesh with the melancholic, mournful nature of the music. I would also say that the final boss wasn't a particularly interesting fight, but some of the encounters preceding it were fantastic.Performance wise, my piece of ♥♥♥♥ laptop struggled with the higher settings, but things were fine when i turned stuff down. No real loss as it is a retro-inspired game without a huge level of graphical fidelity. I didn't seem to experience any bugs, but I suppose things could have been better optimised.Overall, I absolutely recommend this. Extremely satisfied with my day 1 purchase, and I am hyped for chapter 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this. Had a great soundtrack, some really cool moments like the open survival shootout at the church, and kicking doors in at the mental health facility clearing out the cult. Its balanced really well too and feels like all the guns have their place in the game and it never felt like i had too much ammo. The game does look and feel like a shooter from the 90's and its cool. I don't feel like any of the modern elements thrown in were useful. The melee kick is a bit pointless and the hatchet could've done with some cool upgrades or swapped out later on for a sword or axe or something. For the next game i'd want to see 3D models for enemies though. i know its meant to mimic games like DOOM but with the amount of verticality in the levels, you often see them from angles that destroy the illusion so they look like they're from paper mario a lot of the time and it does ruin the aesthetic a bit. i'd have preferred Quake style models.The game seems to run fine, but i feel like performance should be better considering what the game looks and plays like, so not really sure what the deal is there.Loads of cool throwbacks and easter eggs to survival horrors ( like resident evil 4 which this game does feel like sometimes)

_childDocuments_.review: Blood influence ? No doubt. No; Its not a spiritual successor but It is really good and as close as we will ever get to a proper successor so far anyway.... Great nostalgia trip.It checks all the right boxes.Dark Atmosphere Original Story (If youre into it; youll have to read by way of picking up notes but not required) Great GameplayGreat Level DesignGreat Gunplay Great Soundtrack.   Guns have 3 to 5 upgrades by collecting parts and using them in on a workbench. Not overboard. Gunplay itself combined with the upgrades does provide a little bit of depth to the combat. Guns feel punchy for the most part and does great at making you feel like you can handle whats ahead...if just so slightly. See the thing here is ammo conservation ; game does not give you ammo generously throughout, sometime you get a bunch at one time but mostly You'll be scrounging for it a lot of the time.  Game does a great job of giving you just enough ammo to make you feel "Oh I got this" and 2 engagements later ; "nope; I need more ammo"  So you're on the edge if things dont go right and then ammo is dripped to you through out each level afterwards. . I had to resort to the axe multiple times on many levels. It balances the line of just enough and not enough ammo most of the time.  Worst sections I think is the maze (youll know it when you come to it) it just kinda slows the pace down for no real reason other than to do it and you forced to figure it out to progress by fining key items within it. Pro tip: throw unlit dynamite to mark where youve been ;)    The graphics ....you know; I get that its a artistic choice and it does work for its intended feel but man; they do give you a headache after a bit. the 8 or 16 bit color scheme on textures really just make you want some more options like scan-lines or something else idk... it did give me a headache after awhile. All in all this a great game. If you're into old school shooters; this one is unique and is excellent from start to finish. Hope Chapter 2 continues with greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best retro indie boomer shooters you can currently buy. Cultic takes all of the good parts of Blood and blends them with a lot of great ideas from its contemporaries, consolidated into a nice, tight package with fantastic level and enemy design, and brutally fun combat. _childDocuments_.review: While  might not be as well known as  or , if you ask serious shooter fans what the absolute best sprite-based shooter of the 90's was, there's a good chance  will be the answer, so it's fitting then that one of the best shooters of the retro FPS revival is the one heavily inspired by .If I could describe  in one word, it would be "thoughtful". It has the usual systems you'd expect for a game like this, but lots of little extra details that just show you how much care was put into the game, and while any one of them would be neat on their own, seeing it all add up really makes a difference. Things like, "you actually have to light the dynamite before throwing it but you can also throw it unlit and shoot it" or "you can combine dynamite  a molotov" are great additions to the combat loop and really emphasize how much freedom you have, and there are lots of emergent ways to mess with environmental props and use them to your advantage which you wouldn't really get in a 90's shooter. Then you've got small details like "if you press keys on the typewriter, there's a bunch of gibberish letters at the bottom when you go to read the paper on it" which aren't really  but they're fun to mess with and the first time I noticed it I thought "oh, that's cool".Every weapon has a place, but the combat isn't so rigid you're locked to one weapon for one specific scenario (*cough*  *cough*) and the game isn't so generous with ammo that you can just go wild without having to strategize. Early on it's imperative to conserve ammo and while you do get pretty strapped as things go on, the basic melee is fantastic. The axe has to be one of, if not the most enjoyable weapon in a 2.5D shooter, you can charge it and basically get a one-shot headshot on standard humanoid enemies, and if there's multiple enemies nearby they'll also be decapitated.  also has some of the best headshots in general in a 2.5D game and each one feels like you really earned it. Later on you get a sniper rifle which sounds like anathema for a retro shooter, but it works beautifully in context. Once you start getting mroe ammo and not having to rely as much on the axe, you'll rarely have your full arsenal loaded up, so there's a strategic game of "do I want to use this weapon up  or use something weaker for the time being so I can save this for later?" which I enjoyed, and sometimes I just had to stop and look at my inventory to think, "okay what do I actually  and how can I use it to get out of this[/i]". It's a bit thinkier than the usual boomer shooter combat loop and that really tickled the  enjoyer in me.While there's currently only one episode with more planned out, the game feels like a full game with a start and end. Each level is  fairly unique in terms of theme and layout, and the flow is cream of the crop. The few boss fights the game offers are all pretty exciting and take some skill while still being fair, and I felt like the game was always a good challenge without veering into the realm of frustrating-for-the-sake-of-it. There's a pretty wide selection of enemies with a good mix of standard foot soldiers and tankier heavies, but even the regular humanoid types put up a good challenge. One thing I really appreciated is that the shooting enemies  hitscanners, and you actually can dodge their bullets, but you still have to be on top of things and can't rush into a crowd of even low-level bad guys. One guy shooting at you is fine, but several shooting at you is gonna require some footwork. I liked too that the game is confident enough in it's standard enemies to use them most of the time, because they really are compelling to fight. Every now and then they're a bit lacking in awareness (sometimes I'd headshot a guy and his friend right next to him wouldn't react), but they do have a surprising amount of agility. The heavier enemies are all a good challenge and take some thinking to find the best way to deal with them, but the game uses them sparingly which was refreshing as some recent retro shooters have had a tendency to spam them nonstop as part of the standard gameplay loop (again, ).The game's visuals are great, but they are probably the one place I did have a bit of an issue. By default the game has a particular color filter enabled that basically tries to emulate the low color-limits of old shooter games and while it  look cool and atmospheric, it also makes it so hard to tell what you're doing at points that I was legitimately starting to get eye strain with it on. It cranks the contrast so things are extra dark and there were times I really couldn't tell what I was looking at and having trouble seeing important things with how crunched the black levels are. The filter is so intense that you're lighter (which takes the place of a flashlight early on) barely does anything. I'm usually an extreme stickler for playing a game with the settings it was "meant" to be played with by the developer, like I  at the  mod that removed the green filter, but the filter in  was too much for me and I had to turn it off (and even then I still needed to bump the brightness up by about 10). For comparison, I never had an issue with how dark  was, but I  have an issue with how dark  was.Thankfully the filter can be disabled, and while I did feel a bit guilty for not experiencing the developers vision 100%, it's a lot more bearable and the graphics still look great and still have loads of atmosphere. If anything the color palette with the filter actually looks a lot more like the original  so in a way it's more retro with it off (and even the DOS version of  wasn't nearly as crunchy as the filter makes ). There's really a ton of effort put not only into the environments, but also the environmental storytelling and effects. Just simple things like "your hand light up if there's a light source behind you" really make a difference and the visual signposting is superb. I'd be really interested in learning how the dev made the enemies because there's times where it almost looks stop-motion in the way some of the 90's shooters actually were. Enemies have well-defined colors and silhouettes, so you always know what you're up against even at a distance, and all the animations for shooting  are punchy and satisfying.While the game ends at chapter 1 and there is more to be told, I felt satisfied with the story up to this point, and the one-level interlude taking place 2 months after chapter 1 has some really juicy differences that get me pumped to see what's next. You don't usually think of this subgenre as being particularly story driven and even here it's more in the background, but I was surprised how invested I got in the little logs, and the Intermission level seems to hint there's going to be more in-the-moment setpieces and story moments as the ramifications of episode one spread out into the broader world. is a stellar game and one of the best retro-shooters of the 90's FPS revival movement, and that's all the more impressive by the fact that it's all basically made by one dude. Even though it's not technically "complete", don't hesitate to play it now, because what's here feels like a satisfying full course meal, and I do feel like I'll mess around with the survival mode at least a bit since I enjoyed the combat and weapons so much. I don't doubt at all that chapter 2 will be amazing as well.

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid and fun first person shooter, riddled with references and throwbacks to just about every formative FPS released during the 90’s. I’m having a hard time finding unique descriptors for Cultic on its own however. At least without just listing older, similar games. But I think that’s sort of my conclusion here: It’s an amalgam. _childDocuments_.review: Cultic is great, but it's not BLOOD. I'm sorry but I have to make the comparison because playing Cultic and facing my own expectations made me realise one aspect that made Blood so unique.This isn't as much criticism towards Cultic per se, but just some thoughts I had , when I wanted to vocalise what it is that made Blood my favourite FPS ever - and what it makes it different to modern games. Please don't misinterpret this comment as me dissing Cultic, as I said, I think it's great but I have a really special place in my gaming history for Blood and hence I just wanted to write this.And yes- I will be talking more about Blood in this review than I will talk about Cultic. I don't need to say anything about Cultic because you already know it's a great game so just buy it - I'm here to talk about how I'm really hard to please because I love Blood and I don't think I'll ever get an FPS  that would be as special for me and playing Cultic helped me to understand the difference with old build engine games and modern ones-  but especially Blood. So this is my recommendation to buy not only Cultic but DEFINITELY also Blood: Fresh Supply! Just do it.What Blood gets right is that it's not afraid of being more goofy, more old school game where unrealistic physics aren't a problem.Well, it is OLD. But what I mean is that Blood has insanely fun dynamite -lobbing and rag doll mechanics. I feel that this is something many reviewer's and critics seem to miss about Blood. Point being, Blood was the most fun Build engine game thanks to the fact that it didn't try to hide the fact that it's a video game and concentrated on the fun game play loop. Modern games seem to miss this. I don't understand why game maker's don't try to replicate more of the completely outrageous physics of Blood. It's unrealistic to make a zombie or cultist to fly across the screen with gore chunks with crazy speed, but that is FUN. I like Cultic but it's not fast, floaty and outrageous like that.I admit that Cultic has the unenviable position to be compared to Blood, mostly due to the references it wears on it's sleeve itself. Blood was fun, probably the most fun I've had with an old school FPS. It's more tongue in cheek but not only that - the physics are much more floaty and comical. But that makes the dynamite lobbing and destruction also more entertaining. This is one thing that Resident Evil 4 also understood - it's a game that it isn't afraid of being a "video game". Many modern games seem to fall into this trap that they try to bit too much go for some level of higher so-called "realism" but sometimes the old school games captured something special just because they seemed to have more justification of being a GAME. Goofy, unrealistic and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good inspired old-school shooter somewhat weighed down by the fact it is an inspired old-school shooter. The palette/shading is certainly evocative and moody but all that brown and blue and rust are sort of an... 1 + 1 + 1 = 1 situation. The environments of the 10 maps are indeed rather varied even though there's a thick blanket of that old school palette. No fault to the game though because  and it executes it well.The weapons and damage profile is the highlight here for me; everything feels beefy and full of impact (except perhaps the STEN SMG which feels... pretty meh all around). The bosses  were mostly (all?) damage sponges which... eh, fine, whatever. That's old-school, right?There's a story that's played through with sparse notes you can optionally read. I found them fine, even somewhat comical, but you aren't really here for a story, right?Some really nice set pieces in here, too! Some might classify a few as jump scares - I don't feel they were that "cheap" as most were highly telegraphed/foreshadowed. Some of the mob rushes got me and I lost a bit of progress due to not quicksaving (minor new-school complaint: I feel like auto checkpoints could've been a bit more generous, but "that's a skill issue" I suppose).Sound was good, music was... fine? Maybe a bit out of its element here and there; I did appreciate the . I encountered no bugs or slowdowns; you can probably finish this in 4 hours or less if you play more fast paced like a boomer shooter. If anyone wanted to argue I'd say this is not a boomer shooter as the way I played felt like I was being rewarded for being somewhat strategic in nature. There's a sniper rifle, might as well use it, right?Pick this up if you want a sepia-rust-toned shooter to work through in a day or across a few nights. You'll have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly such an amazing and well-crafted callback to the old-school single-player FPS genre. Cultic is very reminiscent of Blood (1997), and honestly it's what Blood could have been if it didn't face the tech limitations of the 90's, but still maintained it's 2-and-a-half-D style and built upon it aesthetically. The addition of new, creative, and transformative mechanics really fill in the gaps of what would usually feel empty otherwise, topped off with beautiful and gameplay-friendly art direction, really makes Cultic worth the 10 bucks. Can't wait for Chapter 2.

_childDocuments_.review: a boomer shooter that absolutely totally gives a ♥♥♥♥.cohesive, thoughtful system design:- throwables heavily leveraged in both enemy & player directions- kick adds even more to this- fire feels great, you want to use it- environmental elements that make you care how to approach encounters but not too much to slow the pace- movement is extremely fun and stops at just complex/tonally reasonable enoughconsistent, top tier art direction:- thorough understanding of how to use old & new- great mix of beautiful billboarded sprites and voxel models where appropriate- high quality first person animations that add weight and feel to every gun- color filtering for darkness & underwater adds a ton of atmosphereextras:- just enough narrative for you to dig into if you care, and to give you a seamless experience otherwise- levels don't stop impressing in how they balance openness of approach and the desired impact of the guided pathonly standout bad was the clunk of weapon swapping in late game. numbers are great n all but the wheel is an only ok attempt to alleviate some of the pain of both remembering all your slots and scroll abusedo also wish the weapon upgrades were fewer and more impactful, little tacked on feeling

_childDocuments_.review: Could not recommend this game enough, it was a true joy to play through. It is very much boomer shooter, feeling more like the build engine end of that spectrum, but more modern than you would expect. It vaguely reminds of me of Resident Evil 4 in the best possible way, as it does feel deadly and ammo isn't so prolific that you can just waste it on your favorite guns. _childDocuments_.review: CULTIC is an amazing game. If you enjoy boomer shooters, or hell just shooters in general, I'd highly recommend picking this up. The movement feels great, the visuals are unique (though I understand why they may be a turn off for some), good variety of weapons, great level design with none of them feeling dragged out, copious amount or secrets. I could go on but the two things I love most about this game are the headshots and the music. This has some of the most satisfying headshots of ANY FPS game I've played, not just from the recent wave of indie boomer shooters. It just feels so good whether you're close range with the pistol or even with the lever action rifle popping a melon from halfway across the map. I feel like the music may get overlooked in the long run but the variety of tunes you'll hear in this title, and with the way it changes dynamically as you go through a level is just so damn good. Can't recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Blood..Lives..Again..First impression is pretty damn solid, good secrets that reward exploration, Enemy variety in the early levels is a bit meh with it just being different colours of cultist, but it tells you what the enemies are about at a glance so no points lost. Normal difficulty is a bit too easy but as is standard for the genre, enemies can knock off your health frighteningly quickly so don't get too comfortable.There's a quick grenade button that lobs a unlit bundle of TNT but whenever I tried to set something up or use it in combat it always resulted in me getting blown up by my own bundle cause the enemies can shoot it mid air and detonate it or throw it back just like you can.Weapon Selection is top tier, first three weapons you get are a broom-handle Mauser, a lever action rifle, and a double barrel shotgun. Yes. All of them are punchy, satisfying and impactful. All of this is topped off by probably one of the most satisfying headshot animations in gaming.£10 for a really good 6 hour Campaign is an excellent deal.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest criticism that I can think of when it comes to CULTIC: Chapter One is that it's a bit short. Which you won't mind considering the price and that Chapter Two is in development. CULTIC takes inspiration from the best of the 90s FPS genre and modernises it in certain ways and stays true to other older design philosophies. The fact that everything in this game is made by just one person is very impressive. Jason Smith is a blessing for the game dev world and an inspiration.So what makes this game so good? As a shooter fan, you might think it's a downright clone of Blood, but don't be fooled. Your character moves very different and so do the enemies and the handling of your weapons. Not in a bad way, just in a bit of a different way. I love the artstyle, the music and the big levels. They are of a very ambitious scale, but somehow they flow really nicely. It's one of those games that's great to start at a medium difficulty, but requires you to master it's mechanics for the harder ones. I love that aspect. There are so many little features that make it very replayable. So if you are a single player first person shooter fan, you owe it to yourself to play this!Wait... you don't like a lot of positivity? Alright let me think of something to critique.....alright, I didn't really like the survival mode. I found the difficulty curve to move up way too fast. But that could be personal preference and honestly, I've had so much fun playing the campaign. This is one of those games that I will replay a lot of times in my life.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the price fool you, 'cuz this ain't no bargain-bin, throwaway boomshoot. This is premium quality FPS gameplay with a compelling enough story to keep one interested for the duration of the 4-6 hour long campaign. Which, I don't need to tell you, at $10 is a steal in 2022. But the highest praise I can give it: after beating the campaign, I immediately felt compelled to start it up again on "Extreme" difficulty.Stop thinking, skip your next trip to McDonald's, and use a fraction of that money to buy this instead.EDIT: CAN'T STOP REPLAYING!!!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended.The combat feels very good and the overall aesthetic had me hooked from the start.I think the game would be slightly better if it leaned further into the survival horror aspect a bit more.The only bug I encountered was an issue where sometimes I would dash in a direction while already running but my camera would lag behind for a few frames.Some other small changes that I think would be good include:- Infinite sliding while going downhill.- The ability to dash while in the air for a few extra frames after jumping.- Crouch jumping allowing you to get slightly higher.- Some sort of directional indicator for the floating telepathic enemies (whether that is directional audio cue or a light source.- The ability to block/reduce damage for a single bullet when holding enemy heads/bodies (like a one time use meat shield).For the sequel, I would love to get some sort of Bioshock-esque plasmid power system after being infected with the parasite.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent retro-inspired shooter for the modern age.Combat is fun, with many encounters perfectly riding the line between "no sweat" and "oh sh**!" when playing on hard or higher difficulties. Weapons feel and sound hefty, with the somewhat lo-fi sound adding even more satisfying crunch. Levels are surprisingly large and varied, and full of secrets, some of which are hard to find without feeling unfairly hidden.Performance can occasionally be lower than expected, and can occasionally vary substantially in scenes with long draw distances. This can happen even when rendering at low resolutions, perhaps indicating that the bottleneck is not the GPU, but elsewhere. That said most of the game still runs flat out, and the overall experience is one of a snappy, responsive shooter.Stylistically, the game makes use of a "dithering" post-processing filter that may or may not appeal to everyone. It can be easily turned off in-game however, and looks just fine without it.The game looks great on an ultrawide monitor,  however the default FOV setting is ludicrously fish-eyed at such aspect ratios. This too is easily adjustable, but perhaps the game would benefit from a way of automatically setting the FOV based on aspect ratio.In-game menu help is present—barely—but would benefit from a more detailed indication of performance impact (for applicable settings). The help text for the "doodad count" setting also appears to be incorrect, showing instead help for the screen shake option.The ability to toggle display of in-game FPS is a nice option in theory, but in practice is totally unusable. There doesn't appear to be any averaging, reducing the displayed FPS value to a flickering blur that seems to update on every rendered frame. It'd be nice to see this fixed.For the most part, the games few issues are non-intrusive, and don't meaningfully detract from the experience. The big exception to this is the game's highly variable performance, with frame rate drops being especially jarring given the overall simpler, retro aesthetic. Jumping from 120+ FPS to below 60 FPS does hurt the presentation of scenes with long draw distances, and as it doesn't seem to be a function of GPU horsepower, changing the game's few settings helps little. All that said the drop are infrequent, likely due to the design of most levels, and are likely even less visible when running the game at a lower overall refresh rate (as the drop in frame rate is relatively much smaller).This is a great game, and absolutely recommended for those who enjoy a meaty throwback shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great example of how passion, understanding of gamemechanics and the mind of a gamer will at the end of the day give you a great game.There is some blood here, there is some rott, there is some doom 1-2 and mixed that with some Duke nukem 3d.And this game mixes those games into a new game and it is glorious!If you are looking for a single player FPS game with great gameplay with just a hint of new in it get this.Its a absurdly good game.Im just waiting for chapter 2 now.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC is very much one of the best boomer shooters out on the market. While the game overall isn't necessarily groundbreaking in a lot of mechanics it certainly does nail everything that makes these type of games great: Gun Variety, Gun-play, Movement, Level Design, and Slaughtering Enemies. In addition it takes heavy inspiration from RE4 and honestly it does so very well. I can definitely recommend this game if you are a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: My gateway into boomer shooters. Really excellently-designed game, satisfying shooting and movement, well-paced levels, lots of variety in weapons and combat approaches, and just terrifically excessive gore. Beautiful retro art style and sound design that makes the enemies and atmosphere feel genuinely creepy (before you obliterate 'em, anyway). Jam-packed with personality and polished to a sheen. Not a long game but well worth the $10 price tag, especially when it goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: What's there to say that probably hasn't been said already about this absolute gem? I've dropped 60 bucks on games that don't hold a candle to this. From the art design to the gameplay (and holy sh*t the music!), this game has brought me more honest to God entertainment than most triple A titles these days.  The fact that it was all done by one person just blows my mind. This is the kind of game that hooked me on gaming in the first place and I hate to sound like an old man (I am) but they really "don't make games like this anymore". Actually, I take that back, Jason Smith does, and the gaming world is a better place for it! Believe the hype, it's a retro masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. If you're looking at it, you're most likely a fan of the genre -- this scratches every boomer shooter itch I've had. Coming from Duke Nukem, Blood, Shadow Warrior, and Ion Fury this game stands shoulder to shoulder with giants for me.I love the mechanics, they're all very fun and clever. The gameplay is fast-paced and fluid. The graphics are incredible. I love what the dev did with the palette, and it's dripping with style.All in all, I'm barely an hour in and I love this so far. I completed the first level, and took my time to take everything in and look for the secrets, which there were several! I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the philistines parroting each other in the reviews with "LOL Blood 2". CULTIC is Like blood on a very surface level, that being: both games have cultists as enemies and dynamite as a weapon. The game, while has certain callbacks to it, plays nothing like Blood. However, it is a VERY good old school shooter and you should definetely play it. Because everyone have already fellated it enough in the reviews, I'll add some nitpicky complaints to the mix. Firstly. I didn't like the redisigned first map compared to the early demo; it feels very flat now, that can be said about most of the maps in CULTIC that have big open spaces, actually. The game is way too generous with ammo for my tastes as well, ironically, at times it feels a lot like cryptic passage add-on for Blood. So maybe in this sense CULTIC is like Blood 2, lol. Secondly. The game has kind of a weird weapon balancing. Lever action rifle is just straight up better than sniper rifle for sniping purposes most of the time. Fully upgraded handgun is a beast of a weapon that's better than shotgun and machine gun in most cases where these two weapons would be useful. Incinerator, that you'll get in the last 4 levels , is ridiculously overpowered, it's primary fire pumps out what feels like Satan's own ♥♥♥, that one shots most enemies including some of the mini bosses, the range of this thing is terrific, it shoots in an arc, so it can go over the cover, the ammo is aplenty and as a cherry on top it doesn't need to be reloaded, needless to say, the last boss doesn't have a chance against it. The only bad weapon in the game is the grenade launcher, it'is a joke even with all the upgrades, it's splash radius is pathetic, and it's damage output is not that good for how little ammo for it the game gives you.And finally. For some strange reason the item "blast armor" gives you health, which is probably a bug.Highly recommended. Go play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Coolest shooter I've played since Titanfall 2. A love letter to all shooters, integrating elements from Doom, Deus Ex, and Call of Duty, to Silent Hill, Resident Evil 4, and the Last of Us. It's rad af and I'm so glad there's a dev out there innovating on shooters in general, rather than acting like a reactionary vanguard of the old. There's so much fun to be had pick n mixing across gaming history. Fun little hatchets one hitting enemies like in Black Ops. Crouch and slide speed glitching like in Warframe. Shield enemies from Resident Evil 4, which you can then equip like the riot shields from Modern Warfare. Silent Hill and Stalker-esque grotesque and supernatural enemies. Deux Ex and Duke Nukem 3D sandboxes with secret areas that are contextualised as part of the world. Doom-style taunting, where you can get enemies to attack each other. Dark Messiah environmental hazards, combined with kicking and throwing. Heck, even Last of Us style weapon upgrades, built from parts you scavenge from the environment. None of it feels gimmicky. It's all integrated so well. Thanks Jasozz!

_childDocuments_.review: This may be a short game, but the amount of polish and passion that Cultic has is on display from the moment you crawl out of the burial pit to the final showdown with the big bad. From the expansive level design to the interactive objects to throw at your enemies (You can do a lot with a lit lantern and a gaggle of cultists). And the weapons... Oh man.You like the Red 9 from RE4? It's the first firearm you can pick up. You like upgrading your guns? This game has that and more, giving you incentives to search the map for secrets hiding weapon parts, along with some story notes unraveling the nefarious doings of a mad cult. Do you like to wrap dynamite with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Molotov? If yes, then this is your game.My words can't do this game justice. For just ten dollars, you are getting one of the best shooter on the market. If your still on the fence, the demo is still up for you to try, but for me, It is an easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Before we start, this game is definitely a big recommend. It's also made by one guy, which is pretty impressive. Currently it feels like a full enough game with one chapter, but there's intention to add a second one later down the line with the developer in question even mentioning a non-fleshed out third chapter.If you've played a lot of "Boomer Shooters" such as Doom, Blood, Duke Nukem and so on, this game fits that style and taste pretty well. The dev appreciates the aforementioned games as well, and obviously inspired by some other titles as well, such as RE4.Music is great, level design is also good, a bit of world building and story telling, secrets dotted throughout the stage that give you goodies to help you make it through, ammo, health, armor, the usual, but additionally you can retrieve "Weapon Parts" that feed into the game's upgrade system. You can upgrade your various found weaponry to get a variable to damage or accuracy, but some equally have some pretty unique upgrades to make them a little more enjoyable as well.This man has done a great job with this game, I give it a pretty glowing 10/10. I legitimately hope to see more from him in the future. Also, the game is ten bucks, what's not to love about quality like this for a price like that?

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, satisfying. This game's combat is crunchy and exciting, with plenty of interesting systems at play to keep it interesting over the course of the short campaign. i appreciate the fact that  many of the achievements are various skillshots, as this adds an extra layer to the combat.one criticism i will make is the persistent, drab environment that the entirety of chapter 1 takes place over. you'll go from wooded forests, to cramped indoor areas, to mines, back to the woods for a bit, back to the mines, then deeper into the mines, then back to the woods... you see where I'm going with this. understandably, this is only chapter 1 and a short interlude. i'm just hoping the following chapters will feature more variety in their level design. TL;DR, crunchy old-school fps with great combat and persistent (if repetitive) level design. definitely worthy the $10 price of admission.
