_childDocuments_.review: Have you played Blood (1997)? No? Then play it because CULTIC is just a Blood 2.0, everything CULTIC did was a blast of awesomeness and I deeply loved that feeling of being a kid playing Blood again, that nostalgia that went beyond a great experience.CULTIC is a retro-shooter that will test your skills and patience when it comes to deal with masses of cultists and abominations. Admittedly one of the reasons I also wanted to do this review was when I threw a dynamite bundle at a bunch of cultists and one of them ran right toward the bundle and kicked it back at me, that precious moment of "Oh F***" made me laugh so much because it was new, it was something I wasn't expecting, the AI will do some crazy things to test you, so yes you can expect some nasty stuff when it comes to the combat, either cultists throwing axes at you or opening a door and getting you off-guard (Yes, really, keep your guns loaded).The weapons feel unique and you'll learn what each one of them do at a particular case-scenario, you can blast away a group of cultists with a dynamite bundle or throw a molotov at them, fire damage works wonders against flesh. You can keep your shotgun ready to blast some enemies in half or just snipe them down at a distance with the FG-42, you can use your lever action rifle to explode some heads or use the Sten to mown down the opposition, really there is an weapon for what you need, even your pistol is useful, just don't try to take down the big ones with it only. And if you are wondering if bullets explodes dynamites sticks/bundles, yes, it does, throw a bundle near someone and then shoot it down when many more go toward you, the best "improvised landmine" you'll make.There is secrets, there is a story behind, there is an upcoming episode as well, yes this is the first episode only so be aware that the next episode will also be paid (from what I got, if I'm wrong about that then I'll edit this review). If you want a game that plays really well and give you that "old-school" feeling then CULTIC is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is getting a ton of credit as a kind of spiritual successor to Blood, and it really earns that comparison, but that isn't all that the game does. I felt the DNA of the past thirty years of shooters wrapped up into this thing, taking something and learning from every major leap that the FPS has gone through to create a real love letter to the genre. It's got Doom and Blood and Unreal and Half Life all over its level design, but also the whip fast speed of a more modern shooter and the intensity and rhythm of the 2016 Doom and Eternal. I even found myself regularly thinking about Alexander Brandon's work on the original Deus Ex while bouncing my head along to the excellent score. I almost can't believe that this whole game came from one dude, and I can't wait to see where Jason Smith goes next. An absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. Hugely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: What an exceptional title!The amount of bang for your buck on display here - literally - is well ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ worth it if you're even remotely interested in Boomer Shooters, most especially if you have penchant for id Software and 3D Realms titles of old; I was particularly reminded of the best parts of Doom and Blood.Unlike other run-and-gun Boomer Shooters, though, here you need to apply more strategy and be more cautious, especially on higher difficulty levels: players who bring good habits from Doom Eternal - i.e. dodging and fast weapon switching - will fare well here.Finally, the fact that this is very much the work of a solo developer is in its own right astounding: the amount of creativity on display, not to mention tonal consistency and sparse (which is perfect for the genre) yet intriguing narrative, make this a must-play for genre aficionados. _childDocuments_.review: An absolutely tremendous accomplishment. Cultic is a singular game that does everything phenomenally well. Lets start with gunplay: clean and every weapon feels excellent. Not a tremendous amount of variety in terms of weapons; however, this isn't a bad thing at all. In fact I think it's a good thing. The guns feel purposeful, designed with intent. And they are a joy to use, landing headshots with the long rifle is as satisfying the 1st time as it is the 51st. I rarely find myself getting excited with retroshooters, like I'm talking about edge of my chair excitment, but with Cultic I got excited. Probably the third map is where I really started to vibe with the game, everything opens up and it's unbelievable how massive these maps are. I'm actually pretty shocked with the maps in general, these feel like the best map design I've seen in a very significant amount of time. They're complex and detailed, but still expertly designed. I feel like the game has an amazing scope. I'm thinking of it in comparison to DOOM Eternal right, a modern AAA title with massive teams behind it, and even still Cultic feels like its a larger game. I don't really know how it accomplishes this? Maybe its because of the incredible variety in maps? It really feels like a world that's lived in, things lead into eachother in believable ways, whereas DE is sort of fractured in its map design and never really expands beyond increasing enemies, interactive movement items and corridors (not that this is bad at all, I am of the opinion that DE is THE shooter to beat for any modern fps, and Cultic honstely proves itself as a worthy game because it outdoes DE in a lot of significant ways). It's unbelievable that this is just made by one dude, the skill and passion in Clutic is clear and it BEGS for a replay. Can't wait for Cultic 2!

_childDocuments_.review: This will get long,  So il break it down in to segments.   "Playing on Extreme for reference""Game play"  Very solid,  Everything feels really nice and responsive,  The combat loop is really satisfying in the more hectic times,   Outside of a single bug that happened once that i can't replicate willingly,  i don't feel i have ever died for any reason other than my own.  Levels are long but the check points are well implemented.   If you know how to play these kinds of games, hard mode might be a little too easy.  There are some really clever secrets.  Some less than clever secrets. but everything feels rewarding for the most part.  "Enemies" I honestly feel there could be a bigger variety of enemies.  There is 1 specific enemy that i feel is a little redundant due to it's relatively slow speed and poor path finding and it's mostly easier to ignore it instead of wasting the ammo.      other than that the enemies can prove to be difficult sometimes. I don't believe there are any hit scanners in this game, but on harder modes you will feel their accuracy.  Depending on the situation you are in you will want to deal with priority targets first.  When you get used to the movement  you will be capable of dealing with a mass amount of enemies inside a complicated lay out, with no problem.  The game very much provides you with the opportunity to play well and feel really good.Weapons.   This is one of the most well balanced weapon set's since the original doom.   "Not quite there" but i personally feel that it's closer than most have gotten.   I will be going through the weapons.  Fists, Actually have never used. Hatchet.  The reason i have never used the fist.   Easily decapitates basic enemies while unaware, has a decent amount of strength behind them at full charge to be a good way of saving ammo.  can be thrown.  I have killed people with this before,  However, it does not feel impactful so i usually don't throw it. Pistol. 10 shot clip,  Decently accurate, decent damage..... is technically fully auto, as you can just hold down fire.. Because of that, I personally feel the burst fire upgrade is moot.  Pistol is a good all rounder even outside of the upgrades.The Lever Action Rifle. Like a shotgun. if that shotgun was a sniper rifle  that shot slugs at about 98% accuracy.  It's a fantastic long range weapon.  Not so much close range.  it is usable, but there are much better options close range.    I feel that for the job you will be using it for,  None of the upgrades are specifically worth prioritising over other weapons.   Ammo somewhat on the rarer side, but for the job you are using it for, it's enough.Shotgun.The boomstick. the choice of one barrel or two.  Absolutely brutal makes really easy work of pretty much everything close range.   All of the upgrades are well worth prioritising over every other weapon.  If you are going to max a weapon first.  This one is the one to focus.The Sten.This is your standard issue machine gun.   50 Rounds at base. It's an okay tool to use when there are a decent amount of enemies.  really needs the accuracy upgrade to bring up to adequate level. however it does have it's own place.The FG42If the Lever action rifle. Had a scope.  It's powerful.  The scope upgrade is an absolute must So much so id say that the upgrade should just be default. It's more for dealing with the things that the lever action is less effective against.  I have not found myself using the other upgrades, mostly as i feel it starts leaning in to the territory of other weapons that handle what they handle adequately.The Grenade Launcher.This weapon is a god. which sadly means the ammo does not exist for it Which sadly means that the absolutely phenomenal upgrades. are moot.  Even without the upgrades this weapon is very strong,  It does have it's uses, it's just those uses are very limited.  The incinerator. Might be one of the best flame throwers in any game. Kills basically everything. Alt fire kills everything else.  The arc can be a little awkward, a really good weapon if you really getting sick of a specific room. TNT.You might get a little too much of this but i'm not complaining. it's powerful it feels good. Molotovs. equally as fantastic as the TNT.  Doubly fantastic when you alt fire. "music"  I do enjoy the music.  you can tell when you are about to reload a few times when the music properly kicks in.  It's mostly designed in a way that it matches the action and it does a superb job of it "overall"   An absolute solid 4.5 out of 5. For me it never really does anything that drops it down an entire point.  it is very masterfully done.  And i am looking forward to the next instalment of the game

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is like an exhumed VHS tape of an action-horror flick by John Carpenter that was buried in the 80s.The gunplay is fantastic, and the atmosphere is great. The color palette, which looks great at first, quickly becomes boring and unfortunately, the maps themselves are not very varied, at least in terms of the environment. Since this is only the first chapter, I guess this ♥♥♥♥♥ will be ground out and each chapter will have a slightly different tone, environment, and color scheme. The level design is mostly great, by the way. There are claustrophobic parts, but most of the time it's just as open as it needs to be. There are one or two really memorable levels, but for the most part, it all blends together into a coherent, professional, and very atmospheric whole. That it's all one man's work - even the great soundtrack - is just icing on the cake. Cultic is a must-buy and another jewel in the retro-fps renaissance.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this expecting blood, its not blood. This doesn't mean the game isn't good and in fact I think its really good, you shouldn't expect blood's gameplay, but instead a more generic (not in a bad way) and chunky experience. It took me 2 or 3 levels to get accustomed to it but after that point I had a blast.Weapon upgrading is a welcome feature in this game and incentivizes secret hunting, which I found to be a perfect medium of difficulty to find. The weapons themselves all have super nice feedback, and contribute their own use case in combat.The music and visuals are both great. I like how the cracked walls are actual holes in the wall instead of a cracked looking texture, because other games I often confuse rock textures for having cracks when they just look like that.I do think a message when you die telling you what you died from could be a good edition.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Oozing with atmosphere and excellent level design / gun play. Definitely worth the asking price.I really have to say, CULTIC has completely blown away my expectations. I'm usually pretty critical of nu-boomer-shooters, lots of them really just lack any soul. This game does not have this problem. I sat down and played through the entire campaign without any breaks or pauses. It was genuinely gripping, and a masterclass in environmental storytelling (with notes to make things more clear). The level design was incredibly well done, pushing the player in one direction clearly while also enabling more open exploration on some levels, I didn't get lost once.You can tell that a lot of care went into making each encounter. You're always given just enough enemies to make a given fight a challenge but never unfairly so. Any point where I got stuck in the game really came down to approaching a problem from a different angle. There's about 4 enemies in the game that I think are somewhat tanky, but it's not just for the sake of making a sponge, it always serves a purpose. Even then, 2 of the 4 have an explicit weakness that makes fighting them way more manageable. The only section I struggled with was in a mid-game map, and that was because I failed to use my resources effectively and ran out of ammo. In a sea of very same-y boomer shooters I really think CULTIC stands out, and deserves recognition for its application of the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the game Blood 2 wishes it was.The game from start to finish is a spooky, action-packed thrill ride filled with blasting possessed cultists and creepy eldritch abominations for added bonus as you progress deeper into its macabre story. Unlike what you'd expect, the game doesn't have just one pace. It's interesting how often you'll be stuck in quiet, eerie scenes rather than action-oriented set pieces, which you wouldn't normally expect from an FPS game like this, but boy can this game get downright scary. There are some atmospheric set pieces that really instill terror and dread, which is kind of like Dusk's later levels. I'd keep your boom stick close in those moments if I were you.The music was my favorite part of this game, as well as the overall sound design. Both are absolutely top-notch and better than they have a right to be, honestly. Right out of the gate in the first level, I was head bopping along to the very well done soundtrack that's both adrenaline pumping and fear inducing sometimes. E1M1 and E1M3's combat music are just some of my personal favorites and good examples of this game's awesome soundtrack. Combined with really cool graphical (giblets and blood decals are hilariously gruesome) and lighting effects that set a dark, unnerving tone that in my opinion, manages to fill the void the original Blood left behind while also bringing some of its own creativity and ideas to the FPS genre. I cannot emphasize enough how well-made and fun this game was for such a small (basically one-man team) developer.Episode one is 10 levels with episode 2 coming out at a later date (for 10 more bucks I assume) so the story doesn't end after the climatic boss fight. Definitely worth the asking price if you're craving a really solid, fun retro throwback shooter that oozes atmosphere and creative charm.Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: A superb shooter that wears its inspirations on its sleeve while dancing to its own tune. With an earthy colour palette, cartoony gore, environmental interaction, grim atmosphere and emphasis on realistic locations with a fantastical and gothic twist, CULTIC pays clear homage to BLOOD.The same floaty jump, almost prone crouch height, dynamite chucking and fast, violent combat is present and correct, but the pacing and atmosphere is a lot more deliberate and down-to-earth than BLOOD's comical monster-mash pastiche. It's an interesting approach that works well, though initial impressions may seem strange if you're comparing the two too closely. There's a ton to love about CULTIC, and its dark vibe combined with much more emphasis on horror and deliberate scares mixed in with explosive action allows it to stand out from the boomer shooter crowd.

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt, one of the best if not THE BEST "retro" shooters you can buy right now. Everything about this game is top notch and it stands head and shoulders and eyeballs above the rest in a crowded field. Let's check why:- Graphics are a perfect mix of 2D and 3D/voxels that threads the needle perfectly as far as style goes allowing the game to keep a retro vibe while enjoying all the benefits that modern advancements can provide without turning it into a pixel pastiche or Unreal/Unity asset nightmare- Art style is a gritty, washed out style that again, perfectly threads the needle of old-school and new. Blood meets Redneck Rampage meets Chasm meets Quake. The weapon sprites and animations are gorgeous. If there was a single negative I could conjure, it's that because everything is so brown and grey, sometimes it's easy to miss things if you're not looking a little more carefully. Luckily items all have a nice golden glow to them.- Sound design is nearly perfect. Weapons are loud and punchy, enemies scream at you and splatter into lovely gibs with blood dripping around you. Dynamite and Molotovs explode satisfyingly. The shotgun was done by right and when you double barrel you can almost hear Caleb's maniacal approving laughter. Holding down the trigger on the machine gun is next to godliness. The music switches between spooky ambient and pulsing tracks (sometimes slightly jarringly) appropriate to the situation, and is a great mix of tracks that wouldn't be out of place in an 80's horror flick scored by Carpenter.- Level design is very very good. Some early spots can feel a bit too open and loose but as the maps go on you can tell that the designers are getting a better handle on it and tightening their grip. Locations are build engine style recreations of real life areas and places that lack some of the detail that made those games so popular but makes up for in atmosphere and its own form of verisimilitude. I would love to see a level editor or mod support.- Gameplay is tremendous. Fast. Bloody. Deadly(ish). You can go as fast as you like or take your time. The game rewards twitchy trigger fingers just as much as it does creeping around and headshotting cultists from across the map with your rifle. Lovely variety of enemies ranging in difficulty and threat keep you on your toes. Only criticism here is that some of the cultists don't stand out as much as they could with regard to their robe colour (I have been shot in a variety of horrible ways by cultists in grey that I swore were simply packing pistols). Health and ammunition are plentiful but not enough that you feel like you're doing too well. Game is a bit easy in this regard and I'm playing on Hard. Maybe extreme is closer to Blood levels of pain that I'm accustomed to. Also, thanks to a fun little physics engine you can pick up, drop, and toss most objects you'd expect to be able to allowing... immersive-sim elements of environment manipulation! Feel free to chuck those red barrels around and set up traps. Throw that lamp in the window down into that crowed room. Build a ladder out of barrels to get somewhere you shouldn't go normally. Awesome. ALSO, there is a weapon upgrade system that lets you find weapon parts (XP, cyber modules WHATEVER) around and use them to give yourself powerful permanent boosts to your favourite firearms. Most of these parts are found in the various secrets hidden across the levels, secrets that are going to make you work a bit to find. There are some in the first map that broke my brain trying to find.What are you waiting for? This game is way too cheap for what you're getting. It's wildly underpriced and hurts me that the designer doesn't feel more confident in what he's created to sell it higher. His loss should be YOUR GAIN. And I haven't even touched the survival mode. Try the demo if you're not convinced but come on, just look at it and the price and do the right thing.tl;dr - Blood meets Redneck Rampage meets Warlock meets Resident Evil 4. Best shooter to come out in a long, long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I got super interested in this game two years ago because of its art style and the fact that its like a mix between Blood and RE4, both games that I absolutely love.The weapons, enemies and sandbox of the game are incredible, straight up. All the weapons are crunchy are extremely satisfying to use, all holding a very important purpose within the sandbox of the game. The physics with throwable objects also are so fun and satisfyingly.The best way to describe this game in general is that its just meaty. There's so many little mechanics within major mechanics such as the dynamite in the game seemingly working like Blood's dynamite but you're also able to throw an unlit TNT and shoot it like a remote explosion or unwrap a bundle, separating each TNT into separate explosives.The level design overall is very well thought out and solid but there are some parts in levels, specifically in the first half of the game where I feel some parts could be condensed or the game doesn't do a great job directly the average player into the next area they need to go in order to progress the game. Every level after The Crypts (E1M5) is incredible though. Thee second half of the game is pure insanity and its fun as hell.I love almost everything about this game but like I've said, the level design could use a bit of work with enemies getting stuck pathing on the environment sometimes and some areas having weird pacing.The other thing is I feel like the music for some levels really doesn't match the vibes of the atmosphere at all. Like on The Mines, you have this only 80's-esque synth track that sounds almost upbeat in this super gritty and spooky section of the game.This game is still great though and I wish it got more attention, looking forward to the second chapter. The second half of the game for me especially started to hook me and I had so much fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, even with zero considerations, but when you factor in that every texture, model, script and song was made by one guy it's really an incredible testament to what can be accomplished when someone that is highly skilled executes on a creative vision. I really enjoyed the pacing of Chapter 1, starting off with a strong Resident Evil 4 vibe with slow and methodical combat encounters that becomes more fast paced and traditionally boomer-shooter-esque as the player's arsenal expands enabling them to rip and tear through enemies that were previously threats that needed to be approached carefully. I played through the game on the "Very Hard" difficulty and I found it appropriately challenging, often having to savescum through some harder encounters, but rarely to the point of frustration. The only thing I do not like about this game is the stylized color palette and sparse lighting can make identifying your enemies very difficult sometimes. This creative decision occasionally puts you in the scenario where you walk into a new dark area, and the enemies get the opportunity to attack you before you can even know they're there, as they're only visible by their muzzle flashes. This forces you to resort to blindly returning fire into the darkness hoping to hit your attacker. The sharpshooter enemies that hitscan from very far and do a large chunk of damage (24 points on very hard if Im not mistaken, making it narrowly NOT an instakill from the regenerating health threshold, which I think is a great design decision) are particularly annoying because of this. Keep in mind that is my one real nitpick with this game. Otherwise it's excellent. There's really a totally different game-feel from the archetypal boomer shooter and I would have a hard time even putting the "boomer shooter" label on it since it's influences are clearly drawn from genres other than classic FPS. It has horror encounters that I think work much better than they do in Dusk and Hrot since you really have to learn how to deal with new enemies as you encounter them for the first time. It's never as simple as pull out your shotgun and start blasting. Okay, sometimes it is. But sometimes getting up close to an enemy is a death with, and you need to use fire. Other times, they're totally immune to fire. There's a lot of tactical variation keeping you on your toes.  Highly recommended to anyone who enjoys a good FPS single player experience.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: To summarize, Cultic is a first person shooter game that plays much like older shooters like Duke Nukem and such, sprinkled with a few modern touches. You play as a disgraced detective, who decided to take matters into his own hand in order to solve a case of missing people, only to end up knee deep into trouble and cultists.While the game sadly feels short, it is very impressive, especially since it is a one-man project. Visually it has its own style, mostly using sprites for the enemies and the character's equipped weapon, and voxels for everything else. The colour pattern is unique too, which can be changed in the options should it not suit your taste.Gameplay is pretty fluid. Apart from the obvious running and shooting, you can crouch, sprint, jump and slide to any reachable place. The weapons work well with each fulfilling their intended role, and can be upgraded with weapon parts found in most secrets. Fans of Blood will find the use of dynamite very familiar.There is a good amount of enemy variety. Most you encounter are the robed cultist. They are encountered wielding a variety of weapons (they are colour coded to the specific weapon they wield, making them easier to identify in the heat of battle), while having a few more powerful variants to spice it up. Next to that you have a few monsters and freaks that may take you by surprise if unprepared.The levels are well made, leaving enough room for exploration, combat, even tension building for the occasional horror moment.Fans of old shooters will definitely love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is another retro-throwback FPS, most reminiscent of the similarly-excellent DUSK, with a bit of Resident Evil 4 thrown in the mix.You play as a rogue detective investigating a mysterious cult. And by "investigate" I mean "completely annihilate with an assortment of ballistic, explosive and flammable tools of destruction".You blast your way through a series of creepy rural locations, all of which are deceptively huge and detailed, considering the game's pixelly aesthetic. While the game my look old-school, the scope and interactivity is very modern.Every weapon feels unique and good to use, and each has its own set of strategic uses, as well as four optional upgrades, that you can unlock by finding the classic FPS secret areas. Enemies are also memorable and distinctive. Every encounter feels pretty unique. Cultic is all killer, no filler. While the game itself is quite short ( I beat it in about 6 hours), it has a ton of replay value in the form of extra difficulty options, secrets to find and different upgrades to choose. I'll definitely replay it at least once.All the bloodshed and action is scored with a genuinely very good soundtrack that reliably gets the heart pounding.I am not a huge fan of the FPS genre (as evidenced by the fact that I played this with a controller. It works great by the way), but Cultic can join DUSK and Half-Life 2 as games that really won me over. It's crazy good!

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a fan of generating difficulty through ammo scarcity. And this is that in the first hour.I am confident it would iron itself out a little as games that are poorly designed on this front cant help themselves once they had you more than 4 guns and feed you a supply of bullets for each, but i was not really enjoying the experience as a whole.The washed out world in a similar tone in such a low resolution and poly environment with this application did not come through for adding to my enjoyment of the environment, but rather made everything feel the same; with everything that needs your attention sticking out like a sore thumb or straight up glowing.Everything felt not quite balanced for fun. Throws of items were to slow and to short to be used for all the long shooting auto aim AI.The AI was to dumb to be challenging and was easily baited into firing their pattern, at which point you could step out and freely execute them. Or to easily baited to step into situations that would get them killed, like crowding active dynamite in a hall.It felt like i was plying the mechanics not a game., Could not play in the illusion or enjoy the game but rather just played the weak mechanics.The writing seemed excellent though from what i read across the machines. But the text is really only going to make up less than a percent of your game experience by time. What is there is good.There is nothing completely game breaking or a fall flat fail in this. I simply don't recommend it, as i have seen many other games come out in the last three years alone that have the same with better and more at a comparable price point.

_childDocuments_.review: There have been a resurgence in retro-styled FPS in the vein of mid-to late 90s games, many of these are not just enjoyable but recommended playing for not just FPS enthusiasts but all PC gamers. I cannot think of a title more deserving of that moniker than this game. When playing the demo the theme encapsulated me, and as a whole I was impressed.Still somehow Cultic manages to superseed these high expectations to create one of the best experiences since the recent retro-fps renaissance rivaling titles like Dusk and Ion Fury. A considerable feat considering it is only 10 levels long, has a small $10 launch price, and is made by one person. Cultics shooting feels good using mostly bullet projectiles making combat lack the cheapness of most hitscan games. Enemies are designed to have a good amount of telegraphing in order to combat them, off the top of my head the audible racking of sniper enemies makes engaging with them a lot more understandable than the "shot from nowhere" angle most other games with this enemy take.If I had a gun to my head critique of this game at all is that enemies can very rarely get stuck/confused, and the game has sections where it spawns them too liberally.Is it short: Yes, it makes no effort on hiding this. In this short "episodes" length though it does more with its gameplay and setting than most do with entire level sets. Cultic is easily the most sane $10 purchase to any first person shooter enthusiasts

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful marriage of inspiration and iteration, CULTIC wears it's BLOOD and Resident Evil influences on its sleeve without stopping at simple rehashes of game mechanics and atmosphere. Those that have played classic FPS and horror titles will feel right at home upon first launch, with the game quickly adding its own flair to keep things novel and interesting. The art style is the highlight of the experience, and that's not to take away from the great gunplay or environmental story telling. I can see how the music removal trope could get predictable but it never lost impact for my personally and the eerie, quiet moments are some of my favorites in the entire campaign.The only misstep I can think of would be the weapon upgrade system, but that's probably down to personal preference. Ignoring it doesn't put you at any real disadvantage any way so this nitpick could be ignored altogether.I play  of retro FPS and this is the first one in a long time to have that "spark." At $10 it's a no brainer.

We have physics, slo-mo, headshots, upgrades, movement tech, a superb soundtrack, and dense, secret rich levels. My only qualm with this game is the way it's being released, I don't think that it should be advertised as full release when an entire second half of the story is missing. It's planned to be released as a free DLC for chapter 1 owners, which I think is fair monetarily. CULTIC is great because it's not just content making nods to Blood and Resident Evil; it wants to do its own thing, and that thing is great.This game oozes atmosphere, the graphics are fantastic, sound design is great, and even the weapon selection is cool (seeing a Sten mk. _childDocuments_.review: This game is GREAT. I was hesitant as I hadn't seen much non promotional gameplay so I wasn't sure what to expect, but man did it click. Every single sound in this game is perfect, from the gunshots, ambient sounds, and ESPECIALLY the lighter. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who was born in the late 80s and grew up on FPS games, I've experienced the genre as it, too, grew. This game is clearly inspired a lot by those early games and builds upon them brilliantly.The use of sprites, low res textures, voxel-style 3d models, along with low polygon style 3d environments and color filters makes this game look and feel nostalgic for that simpler time in game history.  However, the game's mechanics add a clever bit of modernity to the mix.  The upgrades can unlock new attacks for weapons, increase damage accuracy and fire rate.  By the end of the game, you will feel like a walking arsenal.  And that's a feeling many modern games are missing.The pacing and immersion this game offers is wonderful.  One moment you'll be fighting enemies while the game's excellent soundtrack drives you forward, the next you'll find yourself tense... where are the enemies? Why is there no soundtrack? Why is it so quiet here?  Suddenly, you find yourself pumping out more lead.My words aren't really doing this game justice.  Try try the demo, get this game, and its soundtrack.

It functions like a mini sniper rifle excellent for short and long range combat.I've noticed this game is very similar to blood in a'lot of ways weather it be intentional or not I don't mind as blood is one of my top three fps games ever made but I just kept being reminded of it all the way through. The shotgun might as well be exactly the same as bloods with the primary and secondary fire being exactly the same as in blood but with just a slower reload and the enemies don't go flying backwards but still a very useful weapon in both games.The TNT I didn't really like at first but it grew on me. At first I was going to try and avoid using it as much as possible but when I found it easier to just throw it at full force every time it got easier for me to use and I got used to it though I think it's unnecessary to have a'lot of actions tied to it and I know there's some things you can do but I preferred the simplicity of bloods TNT where the primary and secondary fire felt more natural and flowed better with the game and there was two other TNT weapons with different functions. I still find the TNT in blood to work perfectly and sometimes close but not perfect and satisfying in other games besides bloods regardless if it's an fps or not.The sten I never used besides when I first got it for a second because the pistol does it's job but better and is more accurate and I don't like how it share's the same ammo with the pistol. _childDocuments_.review: Note: This game is a SOLO project.  Keep that in mind.CULTIC is a masterpiece of which many of us were not aware or expecting: its legacy will be that of a solo project which, seemingly out of nowhere, took the "boomer shooter" market by storm, and will henceforth serve as the standard to which new retro FPS titles are compared. It is undeniably the best retro-styled FPS I have ever played, which inevitably rules it as one of the best FPS I have ever played, which is all the more impressive that it was created by one man.  Whether it's the soundtrack, atmosphere, story-telling, or gameplay, I must say that CULTIC has been even more of an enjoyable experience than the original Doom or Quake games, and surpasses even Amid Evil, Dusk, Nightmare Reaper, and Prodeus.  Priced at only $9.99 and with a run time of 4.5 hours (and don't let that playtime fool you: it's packed with action), this game is a must-buy, discounted or not.It's difficult to say exactly what the narrative is behind the protagonist, but you play as a man who finds himself delving deeper and deeper into a Lovecraftian cult hidden in the dark crevices of somewhere in northern North America.  The story is simple, and is presented to the player through journal entries which can be found scattered across the maps.  The further you progress, the more you will learn of how regular men became entangled in a cult promising them wealth and power, and what ultimately The Will is.CULTIC is a retro-style FPS.  This means that while it appears like a proper retro-FPS, it contains modern FPS features which set it apart.  There are crosshairs, headshots, charged melee attacks, throw-able objects, and weapon upgrades, as well as dodging, sliding, kicking, and reloading.  Many of the weapons have alt-fire modes, which allow for flexible gameplay.  At your side you can keep a backup medical kit to restore any health lost, and the pack can be refilled with smaller medical kits if your health is already full.  You can pick off distant enemies with your FG42 or lever-action rifle, slide in with your double-barreled shotgun, incinerate hordes with your flamethrower, or lead cultists into a dynamite trap.  It sounds rather simple but try out the demo and you'll see how well-paced and addicting the gameplay is.  Oh, and there's slow-motion following gory final kills.  Yes please.Enemies range from your generic cultists armed with pistols and hatchets to zombies, poltergeists, and even greater monstrosities that I won't spoil.  They are fairly accurate and will try to pick you off from a distance if they spot you, or blow you out of cover with explosives, but the game still feels like the most fair FPS I've played.  I died a few times, but never did I feel even slightly cheated like in Quake or any other game with those "gotcha" moments with demons appearing out of nowhere once I picked up a key: the enemies are in set locations, and for those few that ambush you, your gut will be expecting it anyway (those of you who faced those bony and "Medieval" foes already know what I mean).The maps, like most retro FPS games, are generally open-ended, with objectives being locked behind doors; other maps are more linear and progression is dictated by finding levers to activate lifts or destroy rubble blockages.  Games are saved through checkpoints and manual saves, with no limit on the latter with the exception that the game will not save during combat.  For a retro-styled FPS, this game looks amazing, but this is not due to its graphical fidelity (as in Amid Evil or the redone Quake), but its style.  My first impression from the screenshots was that this game looked rusty.  I wasn't entirely wrong, but once you play the game the rendering will put the screenshots to shame, and you will learn that this rusty, incandescent color scheme is perfectly fitting for the atmosphere and setting.  This game has its own visual appeal that many will find similar to Blood, and that includes the glorious gibs.  I would say the only shortcoming of the visuals is that the sprites of fallen enemies turn with the player, which can look rather goofy, unlike in, say, Prodeus, where there are several angles for enemy sprites.For those who have played the game already, many will agree that they instantly fell in love with the game's atmosphere when they fell down the pit in the first mission, and it's this consistent atmosphere in CULTIC that is rarely paralleled in most FPS games.  There's something about CULTIC's Lovecraftian themes which aren't forced or over-done like in most games of the same persuasion.  There's no otherworldly dimensions or over-the-top and extravagant, abstract atmospheres; rather, this game takes a laconic approach and makes familiar sights home to horror.  This game is honest about what it presents, which makes it all the more authentic, believable, and confident.Whether it's the crunching of boots in the forest, the splashing of brains from a lever-action headshot, the unintelligible invocations of cultists, the explosion of dynamite, the chopping of wooden crates with a hatchet, or the boom of your shotgun, the sound effects are brilliant, especially considering this was one man who made the game.  Better yet is the soundtrack, which ranges from creepy, pulsating dark ambient (I'm looking at you, flesh pit in mission 1) to memorable synth tracks (the best track in the game is arguably when the player first beholds the demonic rift in the sky).  The developer didn't need Andrew Hulshult for this retro FPS game: he alone made a soundtrack that fits perfectly with his game's atmosphere, and is easily one of the best soundtracks in an FPS game ever made.Like most retro-styled FPS games, the controls are simple.  You can remap all keys, which is basically a necessity.  You can access weapons through shortcuts or a weapon wheel which slows time down.  There are also separate keys for sliding and crouching, which some will find refreshing given how many games will tie these two commands to the same key.  Running an Intel Core i7 10th Gen and NVIDIA RTX2070 Super, the game ran smoothly for me at max settings, and I have a hard time imagining it would run poorly on most systems.  The only glitch I experienced was having my character get stuck in a wall during the mission with the tank boss (until getting nudged out by an enemy).  I experienced no crashes or freezes.  The game is stable.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic horror take on the doomlike genre that's full of surprises, at least on hard. Idk about easier difficulties. It liberally borrows from other FPS subgenres, with headshots being crucial to the gameplay, but not to the point that it leaves the doomlike tradition behind. I love the 60s vibe that it has going, which is quite refreshing after playing some more generic and/or crappy shooters. Ammo is not given to you on a plate - you absolutely *need* to manage your resources. The gunplay is wonderful, with the opportunity to upgrade most of your weapons via a very simple system of finding parts (usually in secrets) to use at workbenches that you will find throughout the game. Ace music. The level design can *occasionally* be a bit confusing, however, this should be an instant buy for anyone after a doomlike that leans more into horror rather than straight up action. That being said, the action is definitely still there.Performance is a little bit questionable when one considers how it looks and plays. It definitely needs some optimisation. It recommends a friggin' GTX 1070. Why? If I didn't know better, I'd be asking if it's running a crypto miner in the background lol. This isn't really a problem for me at 1440p with a Ryzen 5800x and a 2070 Super, mostly staying above 120fps, (edit: locked 120 with my 4080 16GB) but there's millions of computers out there that should be able to run this properly but can't.There's a story, if you give a ****. Entirely skippable, as it's mainly told through notes that you find.Also, voxels. 9/10, one of the best shooters of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Only Episode One is out as of writing this, might update in the future.The only way I can think to describe this game is simple yet satisfying. I can't think of anything that Cultic tries to do that it doesn't succeed at. Exploration is fun, combat is engaging and satisfying, the horror is incredibly effective. I think if I had to say anything negative about it, I'd say the soundtrack can get repetitive and the final boss is too chaotic for my tastes and makes it hard to really know what's going on without some trial and error. But this game is an excellent blend of action and horror, with some crunchy and visceral sound design, punchy weapons, satisfying enemy variety and more. I've never been a fan of fire-based weapons in shooters before, but Cultic makes them some of the most fun. If an action-horror FPS game sounds like something you're interested in, pick this up. You won't be disappointed.

and better with each stage but it did leave me wanting more, especially when it ended when I was getting really really good, it's definitely worth the money it's like a fine meal, but if you wanna keep the playtime in mind when looking at the price there you go.Now to talk about the actual game.I'll be honest I was definitely kinda dissapointed with DUSK because people kept hailing it as the sequel to blood we never got but it really never clicked with me, something about the weapons or the progression I don't know I just kept wanting it to just be over, it's because of that that I went into CULTIC with such a skeptical mindset I wanted it to be Blood 2 (but not actually Blood 2) but I didn't want to get "wronged" again.That said, wow does this game deliver, it's a short one but damn is it fun, there's so much good about this game, pacing is absolutely perfect, the gunplay and all the immersive systems are awesome and make combat really feel like you get rewarded for thinking quick on your feet, the music was insanely good, I was really impressed by it it's this mix of synth with old-horror movie music somehow just it worked so well and the monster designs combined with the atmosphere ended up making something truly unique.There were some things I didn't like though, mostly the graphics, sometimes things just felt off, the mixture of some things being voxels but then other things not being voxels, the animations felt something to be desired (but to be fair this problem got mostly fixed when you got some upgrades for your guns that sped them up), the physics can be really annoying to plan around, sometimes objects go too far other times not far enough, sometimes stuff just falls through the floor when you're trying to place it somewhere it was just weird oh and lastly the ghost enemies can ♥♥♥♥ off.This game was really damn good and that's the problem with it, I just wanted more, more weapons, more cool stages, more enemies, more stuff to do (I will definitely go into survival at some point though just wanted to get my thoughts out) and that's CULTIC's biggest problem, I'm really excited for chapter 2 now but I don't know if I'll be when it Still, with all that said, if you're like me and you've wanted a game to be BLOOD's successor for a really long time, this one is the closest we've ever gotten, highly recommended.Edit: Voted for Best Music on the steam awards.

_childDocuments_.review: My first review went over Steam's anemic character limit, so I had to rewrite it to condense my points.This game is absolutely baller, everything about it is punching way above its weight, especially for a solo dev project. If you are even a little bit interested in this game, stop reading reviews and just play it! Huge props to 3D Realms for funding this absolutely insane man. I'll put everything in bullet points because Steam's text limit is really stingy.1. Movement.The building blocks of any good shooter, the movement in this game feels fantastic. It's hard to describe in detail, but it's super fluid, and the jumping has a sort of bouncy/spongey feeling that's just hard to put into words. It feels great, man. There are a lot of fun little tricks you can do to bypass sections of levels, bruteforce your way into secrets that were intended to be accessed another way, and just go really bloody fast. 2. Gunplay/WeaponsGunplay feels great. The handgun is awesome out of the box, has a very chunky, metallic, authoritative sound. The lever-action is damn near perfection, sounds excellent, hits like a truck, served as my workhorse in the later stages of the game, popping heads with ease. I didn't "get" the shotgun at first, you do have to be really in the enemy's face, but you can upgrade it and it becomes a powerhouse. Getting the extended choke (improved pellet spread) makes it feel like a totally different weapon in the best way possible. SMG is pretty good, standard boomer shooter machine gun. Sounds good, hits pretty hard, has enough ammo to clear more than one room without reloading. Only complaint here is that the game can sometimes be a little too generous with ammo, especially in the latter half of the game, SPOILER: 3. Enemies.Enemies are good. Their AI could stand to be touched up in any followups but the level design does a lot of the heavy lifting in that regard, which I'll get into next. Variety is excellent, lots of different enemy types to deal with, many of which are genuinely frightening the first time you encounter them. There are also some reskins thrown in during some sections to spice things up on top of the already wide rogues gallery. Everything is balanced and feels fun to fight, just perfection. 4. Environment and level design.Level design is top notch. Everywhere you go feels like it could be a real place, every arena you fight in feels meticulously planned out. You feel like you're genuinely fighting through ambushes and patrols that real people would set up. They're cleverly laid out so that most of the time, you can get eyes on a few of the threats, but never all of them. Sometimes the game will pull the rug out from under you and drop you into an ambush. The game likes to  play tricks on you like spawning a closed container by a locked exit that you have to walk past to find the switch that opens it, but when you come back, there are shotgunners waiting for you in the now very open container, all while you're getting pressured from an enemy up on a hill.  The levels have an atmosphere so thick you could cut it with an axe. There were a lot of levels that made me un-glue my finger from the sprint key just so I could slow down and absorb the ambience, or because I was genuinely uneasy. It goes from shooter to survival horror seamlessly, then transitions back like it's nothing. I would genuinely adore seeing a survival horror title come from this developer, especially if it had guns and melee that felt as satisfying as these.You also have a lot of fun things to interact with in the environment. The secrets are super intuitively placed, and I was able to find a majority of them just by being vigilant and poking around. As far as I can tell there's nothing super abstract or frustrating to find, they're all perfectly placed, give you a fair reward for the effort put in to finding them, and really spice up the game's already superb levels. You can pick up lanterns and use them as bootleg molotov cocktails, which is especially useful before you get your hands on a real one, you can pick up objects and use them as shields or throw them at enemies, you get lots of fun little notes and blurbs to read when interacting with some objects. You can pick up shields from enemies you kill that hold them, so long as you don't smash it, which restricts use of 2-handed weapons and your alt-fire, but lets you tank bullets so that you can get your bearings and get to cover if need be, or just allow you to push through some sections where you're getting shot at from afar unscathed.5. StoryStory's good, not much to say since there isn't a ton and it's not completed. The notes I did find were well written and engaging, feel pretty authentic, and I did get invested in the story of one unnamed reporter you find the field journals of laying around. Conceptually, the setting, the way the shield cultists look and behave, and some of the locations make me think that the story and setting took some inspiration from Resident Evil 4, but it definitely took a lot of inspiration from BLOOD.. It's tough to really rank this one without the full picture from the potential following chapters, but so far I really dig it. I want to know more, and that's rare for a shooter to pull off!6. DifficultyI don't know what changes between difficulty levels, honestly. I went in on Very Hard, and boy howdy does this game hold up its end of the bargain. I spent the 60% of the game constantly sitting at 25 HP (the HP you regen to automatically when you get knocked below it). Once you get the hang of the weapons, enemy timings, movement, and how the game expects you to use tools like dynamite, it gets a lot easier, but it was kinda rough for me at the start. At the beginning of one level I loaded a save probably 20 times or more. If you're not super well versed in boomer shooters that don't mind shafting you, I'd say go for Hard or Normal difficulties, I'm just a masochist and force myself to play on hard difficulties.Overall, I'd say the game is hard but plenty fair. Never at any point did I feel like I was thrown into an impossible or excessively difficult situation, even at 25HP it was just harder but doable. I imagine on lower difficulty settings it's way more forgiving. In general, the cultists don't mess around.7. Misc/closing thoughts.Game runs great for me. Never once had a technical hitch or any kind of stuttering. I hear that some people have issues with native fullscreen not running well on 4k monitors, though I wouldn't know as I don't have one. As I said, my only 3 nitpicks are that ammo drops are a little too generous at times, though it seems most of the challenge comes from the encounters rather than the need to conserve ammo. Sometimes enemies can blend in with the background, and the pixelated artstyle, while very charming and I wouldn't dream of changing it, can facilitate that. Maybe some kind of slight outline shine to make them stand out and make it a little more readable could help, but honestly I don't think anything necessarily needs to change. Viewing enemies from above can be problematic since everything is 2D sprites, but you'll never run into a situation where you just can't see them, only where it's a little hard to hit them because of the angle you're looking at the enemy from. Last nitpick is that a couple sections are confusing, or don't really make it clear what the game wants you to do to progress. This was a very small minority of my playtime, so I don't think it's really worth docking points for.9/10, awesome game

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. I caught wind of the title via Civvie11 and Skillup in some of their demo roundup videos. I played the demo about 5 times before the drop of the main game. With one playthrough complete I'll go ahead and drop my recommendation. For a price tag of 9.99USD and a single playthrough runtime of 4 hours for myself (on Hard with most secrets found in each level. About half all secrets found) it's a pretty solid bundle of fun. If you are intimate with shooters then I would recommend Hard as the difficulty to attempt your first playthrough on. If you are intimate with retro shooters specifically then perhaps a bump up might help. I don't play many and only found myself dying a few times over the entire 4 hours. Though I was on the brink a good handful of times after a fight. With that out of the way I'll try to simplify the into of my biggest points into a more readable pro's and con's moving forward.PROS-Wonderful level design. Secrets galore and some must be pretty well hidden since I scanned over things pretty hard. The flow and chance to tackle a lot of encounters in at least a couple different ways was welcome too. -Retro Look. Despite the simple looking style the game has it rocks it super well. A great balance of old school looks with more modern touches like the lighting really gives the game a great feel and ambiance. It also maintains fairly good clarity in hectic combat. Though the shields later enemies get can hide their robe color and make it harder to identify them until they let you know what kind of weapon they have via using it on you.-Tight gameplay. Headshots and they feel good. The game doesn't reward you with health or anything crazy for them but the pleasure of popping cultists grapes and how much more effective it is takes care of that for you. You naturally learn very quickly how much easier encounters can go by making it a focus to land shots accurately. The armament of weapons feel great, sound good, and maintain the style the game is after.CONS-Ledges seem...Rounded? This one  is a bit hard to explain. Overall the movement is great for about 95% of the stuff you are doing. However there's a few times you are having to balance on small ledges or are trying to make a difficult jump for a secret you can see and it just feels..Off. When you feel like you should be just on the edge of what is under you it can be easy to just sort of slide off until you are completely off and fall. It's a strange bit of wonkyness but of my four hours this maybe only accounted for 10 minutes or so of playtime total between 3-4 different situations. -You'll have to wait for more. This isn't really any fault of the Dev. (One? Crazy, I know.) Despite the wonderful package this game is I just can't wait until I get to dive into the next chapter. I thought the wait for a few months after the demo was hard.... Time for playthrough #2Overall 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best retro styled FPS games I have ever played. Cultic brings a great combination of gameplay, atmosphere, and story to the table. Visually it limits itself because of its retro style, yet these are some of the most beautiful visuals in a retro styled game I've ever played. While the game starts out slow, with the game giving you the most boring weapons first, a few levels in and you will love it! The combat is as smooth as slicing through butter or eating a very juicy peach. It's very fast-paced and feels perfect with the combat. There are (SEVERAL) really smooth and perfect combat sections throughout the game that feel so smooth, so fun, and the music makes it even more badass. And I'm talking even more badass than doomguy, because that's how well designed the combat is of this game. You are gifted a useful arsenal where every weapon can be useful in many scenarios, (even in late-game.) The story is more in depth than a lot of other games. You can read notes that inform you about many story related topics and also some filler. These notes are a little useful to the gameplay, (or at least in one scenario) where you have to read or skim a note to help you find a key. The main story is quite interesting and while it's not one of the main things that keeps you playing, it does add one to the fun and the theme. (I think story might be a lot more important in the next chapter, judging by how there's more story in the Interlude.) The game is one of few, that actually has the environments tell a story by themselves. In many other games, the environment gives a basic idea, but in Cultic the environments have every single detail in every single note.The music is great and makes a lot of moments, (like combat) so much more enjoyable and kick-ass. But it also does a GREAT job at adding onto the atmosphere of an area. Seriously, the music in Clutic is severely underrated!I would say the game is around 95% good, and the other 5% for a few smaller issues, but again, these are really small issues. In the ship level, I must've wasted over 30 minutes trying to find where to get a key, and they hid it in a hard to find spot. But if you run into the same problem, pay attention to the floor ;), but everything else is fine, if not awesome!Cultic is an awesome game inspired by retro graphics and older games, (like Blood, Doom, etc.) Cultic doesn't try to hide its inspirations, but Cultic itself is too good and too unique to call it a copy or anything like that. Cultic is an awesome game, and It's quite cheap! Seriously, if you have the money, go ahead and play it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. Buy it now. If you are at all a fan of retro shooters, this is a must-buy.However, I have multiple minor points of criticism that are aimed at helping the dev while this game is still in early access. If you have not played the game yet, do not read further. Just buy the damn game, you won't regret it.1. The model of the lever action. This isn't necessarily a *flaw*, but more so a grievance. The barrel is WAY too short when you're holding the gun, it looks ridiculous. If I'm not mistaken, this is by design, as the lever action appears to be a Mare's Leg, which is an actual, real life gun. However, that doesn't stop it from looking ludicrous. The barrel of the sprite is so small that it looks like a pistol, and it throws off the whole look. What makes this worse is that I love Lever Action rifles! And more specifically, the lever action is my favorite weapon! I want to feel like a Cowboy, and the ugly midget barrel takes me out of my Clit Eastwood RP. Please devs, add in an option to increase the barrel length of the lever action. I know this is a small grievance, but it legitimately upset me while playing. (And if you're reading this devs, please also add an option to play The Good, Bad, and the Ugly theme whenever I start popping heads with the alt fire, I will pay more weapon parts for this feature.)Speaking on weapon parts (fastest segue in the west), they feel a little mishandled. Simply put, most of them are boring. Although objectively helpful, increasing the magazine size is so generic and underwhelming that I literally didn't do it a single time. The only gun that would be useful on, the Shotgun, doesn't have it. But perhaps the worst part is that none of the upgrades are actually interesting. The only ones that is genuinely interesting (imo) is the Lever Action upgrade that gives you slow motion with every alt-fire headshot, and the Grenade Launcher upgrade that gives you fragmentation. They're great! More like those please. But almost every upgrade is some generic improvement on a slightly pertinent stat. Here's a good rule of thumb; If your weapon upgrade boils down to the same function as a weapon attachment from Call of Duty, it's probably not very good.For example, the pistol is totally and completely outclassed by the Sten, so why not give it the option to convert it into a revolver? Or even better yet, to stick with the makeshift, old-timey weapon aesthetic, why not have the switch from the Luger to a Revolver be a homemade, makeshift conversion to a higher caliber round? It dynamically shows that the protagonist has to scrounge around for anything he can use, and be crafty. It would also just look super cool to see a revolver cartridge stuffed into the body of a Luger, held together with duct tape and steadfast prayer. Or how about going crazy with this idea? The protagonist gets carried away with his DIY gun improvements, and turns the double barrel shotgun into this 8-barreled monstrosity that takes can hold 3 rounds in each barrel and takes 10 full seconds to reload, but possesses enough firepower to blow away a house. Adding onto the theme of sacrificing reliability for raw power, you could make the shotgun occasionally fire two barrels with one trigger pull, wasting a little bit of ammo. To subvert expectations a little bit, instead of having the alt-fire unleash all chambers at once, throw in a curve ball. Once you press alt-fire, the barrels start spinning like a chain gun, and you hear the protagonist's maniacal laughter as he unleashes a storm of buckshot into Hell's spawn.Especially since it appears like we're going to hell in the next chapter, wacky ideas like this are both appropriate to the setting and add to the charm of the game. I could keep coming up with ideas for Gun modifications and upgrades all day (I'm available for hire, just saying. Ah, who am I kidding, I do this ♥♥♥♥ for free), but I think we've gotten a little off track in my gun-related fantasies. Point of the story is; the weapon upgrade system is underwhelming. A flat damage increase and extra mag size is undoubtedly useful, but they're so uninteresting and yawn-inducing that you feel cheated, despite their objective utility. Please, in whatever way you see fit, spice up the weapon upgrade system. It's promising, but needs some... spizzaz... to reach it's full potential. (This is kind of a tangent aimed almost solely at the dev, so sorry about that, but I have to get it off my chest.)Speaking broader, WW2 weapons are perfectly serviceable, but I feel like it could be so much more interesting. Sure, it's more accurate to real life for the weapon upgrades to be a shoulder sling, or a better lever, or a higher capacity magazine. Yet those are all BORING. Not only are they conceptually uninteresting, they are mechanically pointless. All they do is allow the gun to be slightly better at what it already does. With or without higher damage rounds, the Sten performs exactly the same function, the only alteration is how long it takes to perform the function. Weapon upgrades or modifications don't have to be nearly as crazy as the two that I've suggested so far, it could be something the Sten stacking damage of the next mag based on how many enemies were killed in the previous 50 rounds, or the shotgun stacking overkill damage to your next shot, leading to you exponentially building up damage until you miss or unload all that built up damage into a single enemy. Those upgrades wouldn't change the primary role of the weapon, but they would change how you use them. They reward you for skillful, efficient play with those weapons by scaling your effectiveness directly with your competence in using them. It adds a level of depth that gives the game longevity that many other great FPS games simply lack. That's why Overkill is so beloved. To close up my senile, tedious ramblings, don't feel afraid to experiment. We don't just want Blood 2: For Real This Time, we want Cultic. Also, feel free to shamelessly steal any of my ideas if you feel so inclined, I doubt they're worth a damn, but you never know. (Except that Cowboy option, that's an invaluable suggestion right there.)

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped from the moment I played the first demo of this game.  Blood by Monolith is one of my all-time favorite FPS games (mainly due to its level design and the majestic immortal voice of Stephan Weyte) and although I was late to the Blood party, it quickly rose to my upper echelon of FPS titles.  I wish there was a proper sequel done.  People said there was a Blood II, but I don't believe them, just like how I don't believe it when people say there was a POSTAL III.  Much like Dusk before it, CULTIC is the product of one developer, Jason Smith.  However, Jason takes it a bit further by not just designing and programming the weapons, art, levels, characters, and gameplay, but by composing the music as well.  It is clear that a lot of inspiration came from Blood, such as the hooded cultist enemies whose robe color indicates what weapon they are using, impactful weaponry that includes a powerful double-barrel shotgun, different armor types that protect against specific damage sources, and even the beginnings of their first levels, which involve the protagonists rising from their graves.  CULTIC differs from Blood in many other respects.  CULTIC has a stylistic limited color palette that may initially seem off-putting, but given the setting and theme, fits the game very well and Jason is to be commended for it.  Along with the palette is a low-fi and "crispy" assortment of sound effects that are satisfying to me, especially when running through grassy and gravel-paved areas.  CULTIC has headshots, and they are some of the most satisfying headshots I have ever seen in a videogame.  The dopamine rush from popping a line of zombie heads with a single well-placed Lever-Action Rifle shot rivals that of mowing down a group of Zombiemen in classic DOOM with a Super Shotgun blast.  Getting a headshot or explosive kill has a chance to trigger a short period of slow-motion like in Killing Floor.  I think this is helpful in heavy combat and for punctuating a big kill with a well-thrown bundle of TNT, but I can see how this could be a negative to other players.  The levels are excellently crafted and are aesthetically pleasing. Jason has designed expansive areas such as the Shipyard in level 2, the Asylum Grounds, and the Mining Town.  The game also has many creepy and unsettling areas, such as the beginning of the Mining Town level, the Crypts, and the interior of the Asylum (to me, asylums are perfect settings for horror media).  Most of the levels are fairly linear, but are designed in such a way to encourage and reward exploration through secrets and to just admire the scenery.CULTIC's weapons can be upgraded with Weapon Parts that are scattered around the levels.  Most upgrades are standard, such as increased damage, better accuracy, and increased fire rate, but there are a few unconventional upgrades, such as guaranteed slow motion for headshots with the Lever-Action Rifle's alt-fire and increased knockback with the Shotgun that can boost the player while jumping.  I think an alt-fire for the Grenade Launcher that shoots electric grenades that don't do as much damage as primary fire but stun enemies would have been a neat addition.  The traditional nature of most of the upgrades is not a major complaint, however.Besides the robed cultists, the game's enemy roster includes eldritch monsters like a fast, brutish behemoth and what can be best described as a fat gray creature with a vertical mouth that takes up its entire torso and long, sharp teeth that devastates your health if it gets too close.  To me, the most annoying enemy is the Ghost, a flying cultist covered in a white sheet with two eye holes who attacks by tekekinetically throwing objects at you, even if the Ghost is out of sight.  However, if the Ghost looks at you, it turns your screen red, shakes your view, and greatly slows you down while doing damage over time until you break line of sight or kill them.  The Ghost is not annoying in a bad way in that it serves as an effective horror enemy in cramped interior locations and as a dangerous support unit in large battles.  Just like in Blood, each enemy has a burning death animation in which they flail about screaming.  The screams the cultists make are not as iconic as Blood's "IT BURNS IT BURNS AGHAHAGHHAGH" but fire kills are still fun to execute.As if the main campaign, which spans 10 huge levels, is not enough, CULTIC offers a Survival Mode that is best described as single player Killing Floor done better.  You fight waves of enemies that increase in number with each wave.  Each kill earns the player money that can be spent on weapons, ammo, and other supplies at a shop between waves.  Survival Mode pushes the player's skills to their limits and rewards ammo efficiency and movement techniques.  Much like Dusk and Ultrakill, CULTIC has its own movement tech that greatly increases the player's movement speed through jump kicking.  I have put as much, if not more, time into Survival Mode as the main campaign.  Special mention has to go to how the game approaches its difficulty settings.  Jason has done an excellent job designing the skill levels, much like how id Software crafted the Ultra-Violence difficulty in classic DOOM.  Not only does enemy damage increase at higher difficulties, but enemy counts do as well.  This leads to a high-risk/high-reward approach to the game on higher difficulty settings, such as greater counts of enemies wielding shotguns, who hit very hard but have a chance of dropping shotgun ammo on death.  Another special mention goes toward the better-balanced cultists of CULTIC.  Although I like Blood, one aspect I think is BS is how its cultists, the most common enemy type in the game, have instant reaction times and can mow you down in seconds if you don't deal with them ASAP.  CULTIC's cultists (heh) attacks can be baited by darting in and out of cover and dodged in open levels by bunny hopping and sliding.  I cannot forget the soundtrack either.  It's very well done with heavy combat-appropriate rock songs, atmospheric pieces that go well with exploration, and creepy ambient songs that can fit right in a Halloween or Friday the 13th style horror movie.As if all the positives already mentioned are not good enough, CULTIC has a low price tag of $10 USD.  Jason could have charged twice as much and I would have no problem with it.  This ranks it among the best deals in gaming along with Vampire Survivors and The Orange Box.  This is only chapter 1, also.  If Chapter 2 turns out to be a separate purchase, I would have no problem with it as well.  Chalk up another excellent title in the retro FPS renaissance.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really good old school-styled shooter. The combat and gunplay here is super satisfying, its surpisingly easy to pick off the many long-range enemies you'll be facing despite the pixel aesthetic. The game definitely puts a major emphasis on much more methodical and tactical gameplay than most older shooters, it reminded me of half-life a lot in its gameplay actually. You're constantly switching weapons and adapting, trying to predict the enemies and outsmart them, which makes for the long-drawn out battles with the cultists in huge open arenas being the best parts of the game, when in a lot of other games that'd just quickly turn frustrating. This balance is fine-tuned enough that you're always able to approach a situation in so many different ways, catered to whatever your playstyle and favored weapons may be. The combat may be slower and more tactical overall, but you absolutely can crank up the speed to your advantage too by utilizing movement tech like using the kicks for a sort of b-hop, or the shotgun upgrade to gain some vertical mobility. It makes for a style of game where you both need to be careful and slow but also act and move fast, it's a delicate balance that comes together perfectly.The game isn't without flaws however, the bigger supposedly more threatening enemies are an absolute joke. Their placement is questionable as they'll nearly always be in environments where they can easily get themselves stuck and just make them an ammo sponge and nothing more. Either their AI needs to be improved or they need to be better placed and incorporated into the levels. The other enemies also could use a bit more detection range, as in certain maps, it can be easy to pick them off from a distance without being noticed which just feels a bit too powerful sometimes, some more risk to that interaction would make it more engaging.The game also just kinda... ends. It is just chapter one at the time of this writing, and there's quite a good campaign here, but I do question releasing it in this style. Due to the gameplay first focus here, all it really will do is hamper the overall flow of the game. I'd be perfectly fine waiting for both chapters to be out rather than this splitting up of the full product.Those are really all nitpicks though, this was still an absolutely incredible game that I'm eager to do another playthrough of soon on a higher difficulty. (I played on Hard for my first playthrough.) Check it out if you're a fan of old school shooters!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent single player action/horror game. Although at first glance it may seem like one of those "new retro shooters" (it is to some extent, it shares some similarities with games like Blood), Cultic is actually closer to survival horror action games like Resident Evil 4 or Evil Within.Cultic has great atmosphere and level design. The weapons feel great and are very different from each other. Also, you can upgrade them using a specific item that you can find in the environments, so trying to find the secrets inside the levels is recommended, luckily their locations are not very cryptic.Unaware enemies are weaker, and although the game doesn't have an explicit stealth mecanic, you should try to make a silent approach every time you see an enemy or group of them that have not detected you yet. You can throw them axes of TNT bundles.There are different difficulty levels, and the way you play this game changes a lot between them. The gameplay that the low/medium difficulties allow is very different from the way you will have to play on the higher ones. So even though the game isn't very long, you'll definitely want to play it again to see those changes.My only complaints are the music, which is great but in my opinion it doesn't fit very well with the tone of the game, maybe a more atmospheric soundscape would work better I think.... My other complaint is the enemy AI, which is a bit inconsistent: sometimes enemies exhibit interesting behaviors like kicking TNT bundles you throw at them or successfully flanking you even in the larger and complex areas, but other times they get stuck in the level without a reason or fall off ledges even when you are not near of them...Anyway, this is just the first chapter and maybe these issues will be fixed in future episodes. This one is excelent and you should give it a change.

_childDocuments_.review: Great stuff. The gunplay is exactly what you would expect from a retro-style boomer-shooter, and the mobility, while also reminiscent of it's ancestors, is much tighter (less floaty/icey). The weapon upgrade system is simple, and doesn't force itself on you. The story and discover-able documents/artifacts reveal themselves naturally, and lend a wonderful element of exploration to a genre that is usually pretty lacking story-wise. The game itself heavily encourages exploration as well, rewarding you with tons of secrets to find. You can interact with much of the environment - many of the items lying around be used strategically in combat, like lanterns that burst into flames when thrown. The music is great, and the quality is much higher than what you would normally expect from an indie game? Maybe not even that, more like, these feels like fully developed tracks, that were very deliberately chosen to set the mood continually, tied in with the plot. They aren't just basic loops. It feels like so much was added since the demo. I've only played two levels so far, but I was very pleasantly surprised by a game whose demo I was already quite into, and had to come comment. Well done, Jasozz Games.
