_childDocuments_.review: While short (3-5 hours), Cultic brings sleek, fast gameplay for you to enjoy, plenty of secrets for you to explore, and an incredible soundtrack that helps to draw you in.Through the aesthetic presented and the simplicity of gameplay, Cultic is a fantastic experience and wonderful homage to a bygone era of PC gaming. Many compare it to "Blood" from decades ago.  I had never experienced "Blood", so for me this has been more reminiscent gameplay wise of Duke Nukem 3d (though Cultic is much more refined).  A decent selection of weapons is at your disposal, though they don't have a ton of variety (axes, dynamite, pistol, lever action rifle, shotgun, etc). There is a weapon upgrade system available to add some variety as you play and gather weapon parts (which you can often find in secret areas).Beyond the core story gameplay, there is a survival mode available to help with the replayability aspect of the game.  There are also several difficultly modes available to choose from, so Cultic can be an enjoyable experience or challenge for whoever wishes to give it a go.At times surprising in how creepy the game can get, Cultic maintains an overall dark tone with little humor, but oozing with atmosphere.   I will be updating this as I play more, but from the time spent before release and now, Cultic is a surprise hit this year. Do yourself a favor and pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing shooters for almost three decades, and this is one of my favorites in recent memory.  First of all, let me address the game's look and feel, probably its most salient aspect.The art style is unique, weirdly beautiful, and fits the game's tone perfectly.  I have never seen a game that looks like this before, and I can only guess how much effort went into getting it to have this look without making everything an ugly, pixelated mess.  Yes, you really can see an enemy across even the game's largest maps well enough to no-scope headshot them, and you'll be doing a lot of that if you want to stay alive.  That brings me to combat:This game does long range combat remarkably well, something I have rarely seen done with any real level of effectiveness in a "boomer shooter."  You can fight an enemy hundreds of meters away, and both you and that enemy will pose a serious threat to one another, requiring use of cover and quick aiming to come out on top.  However, the game gives you the precision to do this very effectively with a little practice, mostly by means of the lever action rifle or scoped FG 42.  That's not to say long range combat is the only way to handle things.  Close range combat is just as good, with a very cool retro weapon set that offers up a Mauser C96, double barrel shotgun, and a Sten MkIV, among other weapons that can be highly effective up close.  There are literally no bad weapons in this game.  I have played through it several times now, upgrading different weapons in different ways, and I can't find a way to break my build.  Upgrades will definitely affect how you play, but they never govern it entirely.Explosives and incendiaries are plentiful, and hilariously fun, as they should be.Enemy variety is much better than middling for the genre, with a good selection of baddies on tap to blast.  No complaints in that regard.Controls are simple, old-school WASD, but done right, with good responsiveness.The level design really feels like a natural progression of old Build Engine games.  Environments range from claustrophobic to enormous, and present a wide variety of combat challenges.  Environments manage to feel fairly real and immersive despite the graphical style, and I think that owes much to the developer embracing the limitations of the low-polygon, sprite-based retro shooter by way of the game's artistic rendering.As far as negatives go, the game is fairly short.  With only 26 hours, I'm almost through my third run, this time on Extreme, having beaten Hard and Very Hard.  That said, this game was essentially made by one individual, so there's only so much  length and content to be reasonably expected.  Another issue is that there is some platforming (mostly to get to secrets) that doesn't feel quite right in a few places.  There are also some combat scenarios that at first feel grossly unfair -- like "Blood" unfair.  However, I've always managed to find a way through them with some work.  Really, none of that is unusual for the genre, and it never really feels in any way crippling.Simply put: if you like retro shooters, you'll probably like this game.  Highly Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short, but oh so sweet FPS. I have to say that out of the recent crop of "boomer shooters" I think I love this game's aesthetic the most. It's grungy, dirty, and spooky. It doesn't feel like it looks the way it does just for nostalgia's sake. Oh yeah, it plays like a dream: lots of dashing, lots of headshots, lots of explosions. Don't pass on this if you love FPS games, and horror themed action games in general. One of my favorite games this year.I guess I'll be playing the survival mode until we get Chapter 2.A few notes / criticisms:- A lot of people say this game is short, citing a 4/5h playtime. This is accurate, but only if you play through in a straight shot on the easier difficulties and don't bother with exploring levels for the hidden secrets. If you play on the hardest settings and secret/achievement hunt you could see yourself spending a good 6-8h on a first time playthrough.- I see some people complaining about ammo scarcity. I personally think it's part of the challenge, this is a horror game after all. This game doesn't have anywhere near the same the ammo management difficulty of Blood.- Enemy AI: Overall it's good. The only issue I have is that in the larger areas it's a little too easy to pick off enemies in the distance who are just standing still waiting for you to make yourself known.- Difficulty: Overall a great range of options like any classic shooter should, but I don't think there was too much of a difference between Hardest and Extreme. Basically I'm saying extreme should be maybe a bit more extreme considering you can cheese some enemies in a some encounters (like when you can snipe idle enemies).

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favourite of the classic shooter revivals. It goes way beyond just paying tribute and really brings a fresh feeling to the genre through stellar art direction, modern controls and maybe the best level design I've seen in a modern fps. It is a linear classic shooter, but you can really feel elements of survival horror and immersive sim in here too which make it just so much more grabbing and atmospheric.It is a testament to what a one-man development team can achieve. There's a kind of consistent vision that makes this game incredibly magical. From the music to the gameplay, from the lore to the level design, everything just works so well together. The gunplay is unmatched. So crisp, so clean and with such a good arsenal of guns and movements, all of which really have their role. The gameplay feels very modern, and you really feel like it is a step up from the games that inspired it. The most magical part of this game though, is the level design. It is ridiculously good, with locations that feel real and grounded. Moving along is so intuitive, and figuring out which way to go is never a case of just walking till you're shot at. Instead, the game is full of environmental storytelling, blending together found notes and details in the environment to direct you. Every stage naturally connects to each other and yet feels varied. It's so good that it causes a sort of immersive state, where everything about the world feels real, and the (seemingly simple) story nevertheless grabs you. It took me about 6 hours (runtime 3:52 but had some restarts) to beat Chapter 1 and Interlude on Very Hard, and I just can't wait to see what's next. The recently added interlude really doubles down on the environmental storytelling, providing enough clues about the surrounding world to make you feel like Chapter 2 might very well take the storytelling and immersive elements to the next level.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is a premium experience for those of us who grew up with Doom, Duke Nukem 3D, Quake and Blood. It definitely wears its influences on its sleeves, but make no mistake this game has a ton of modern features. From fully interactive physics objects to a simple but effective weapon upgrade system, Cultic is a perfect blend of old and new. The game just oozes atmosphere, and the soundtrack is stellar. I find myself replaying certain sections just for the music. The fact that a single developer put all this together is a real testament to their dedication, artistry and technical acumen. I haven't even talked about the combat. Where to even begin? You can approach combat situations in so many different ways. Go in guns blazing, dodging around corners and swapping between weapons, or take a slower, more deliberate approach by setting traps and sniping targets. Use the environment to your advantage. There's just an unparalleled, satisfying crunchiness to it all.My only regret is not being able to play this one for the first time again. Eagerly await Chapter 2!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast through this 5 hour campaign. This game has an awesome roster of weapons, a killer soundtrack, and great level design. _childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually too big on retro FPS but Cultic blew me away and stands on its own amidst the comparisons to Blood. It facilitates slower, strategic play, and really encourages switching through weapons to play to their strengths. The level design is top notch and never overstays its welcome. After warming up to the mechanics, you can continue playing slow and deliberate, or you have the freedom to go full Doom Eternal, strafing through the levels to a gorgeous soundtrack while being encouraged to flip through  your diverse arsenal, all while accompanied by the screams of burning robed cultists left behind in your wake. The controls are tight, and enemy targeting isn't hitscan, which really encourages you to take advantage of the fluid movement baked into the game. It really is whatever you want to make of it, but it's always at the very least badass and great to look at.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to have negative feelings about Cultic. I'm a Blood evangelist, and seeing a new game aiming for that aesthetic immediately piqued my interest. However, in practice, Cultic just isn't a very good boomer shooter. The player's run speed isn't high enough for a retro experience, and making strafe slower than moving forward is a ghastly failure of mechanical design. The entire point of this style of game is strafe and kite, over and over - and you can't do that in Cultic, or at the very least you can't do it well.Another immediate bugbear is the aiming. No matter how much I tweak the sensitivity slider, it feels floaty and imprecise - almost like there's some kind of mouse acceleration. It's jarring compared to the lightning-precise accuracy of games like Dread Templar, Ion Maiden, and Amid Evil. I understand this is a one man project, but I definitely expected better - especially with the 3D Realms name attached.Dusk is a far superior tribute to Blood. Cultic has sublime visual design, but wrapped in a game that's just mediocre.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review just after finishing the game, and I must say that it's quality it's mind blowing considering how cheap it is. _childDocuments_.review: I have many issues with this game, but it's a great deal for 10 dollars. I'll start with the good: Great, memorable art style that looks not quite like any actual retro game. Massive, beautiful, intricate levels that feel open enough without ever causing you to become lost. Punchy, crunchy sound combined with satisfying gore/effects.The problems with the game are entirely located in the combat design. Cultic makes Blood (its biggest inspiration) seem fair and measured by comparison. Enemies have perfect vision, perfect aim and perfect reaction time. The biggest (and most easily fixed) issue is view kicking when hit, because you're going to be getting hit all the time regardless of what you do. Once you start getting hit, you're never going to stop until you take cover, because enemy firerates are high enough to where your screen never stops jerking around, making return fire impossible. The stylized low fidelity also means you're often being sniped by 5 squirming grey pixels from across the map.Speaking of maps, they're all vast, open expanses which harms the combat in several ways. Enemy vision and accuracy has no limit, unlike the player's. You're always being spotted before you can reasonably spot your enemies, so it becomes a game of following the directional damage indicator and discerning which grey clump is lighting you up. With no hyperbole, 90% of the game is going to be lining up your crosshairs on things you assume are enemies and spamming your pistol in their vague head area. So much of the mechanics are designed for close encounters (like sliding, kicking, shotgunning, throwing objects, etc) but they go mostly ignored because this is a backdoor sniping game.When the combat does get closer, other issues rear their head. Weapon swapping is locked for full seconds if you take any action, which makes it feel clunky when you're trying to be tactical. Enemies spamming fire 100% of the time means any attempt to throw an explosive at them (literally) blows up in your face as they manage to ignite the object mid-air. There's a dodge button, but it doesn't affect enemy accuracy. I guess it's for avoiding the rare melee enemies of the game? There's a quick dynamite toss button, which is a great idea but it always seems to backfire. You can shoot it mid-air but it'll always hit you, or you can wait for it to slide, in which case the enemies will either walk past it and block it or... kick it back at you. They love doing that last one.Don't even get me started on the psychic enemies that slow you to a crawl while draining your life any time they gain line-of-sight. It's emblematic of the general combat design of the game right now being all reaction, no proaction (that should be a word.)
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is a retro styled FPS, most akin to Blood. It's short but every level is memorable. While you can easily see the Blood influence, it doesn't aim to remake the game under a new name. Cultic has a unique color scheme similar to a sepia filter (which can be turned off if you desire, but in my opinion that ruins the aesthetic it's going for) and the combat on the whole feels different but still challenging and very snappy. The level design is superb, managing to mix elements of horror games with some very atmospheric and sometimes dark (literally) sections that could get a scare out of you. I already mentioned this but it can't be stated enough just how good the level design is, they're all very intricate, full of secrets, and are incredibly varied. Each level manages to somehow be distinct and very memorable, with the Asylum Grounds being my absolute favorite. All the weapons feel distinct and with a function, and there are secret parts crates you can find that you can use to upgrade your weapons to make them even better. Enemy design is very good and diverse for a game of this length. I remember in the very first demo the different kinds of cultists were very hard to differentiate because of the sepia tone, but in this final release they're all distinct and it's easy to tell which one is what kind of threat. The final boss was also a nice spectacle to battle even though he wasn't too difficult on hard.And the most impressive part is this game has been made by one person, Jason Smith (with support of course). And it really does feel like this singular vision passion project, which I absolutely adore in Indie games, and it's a quality that's incredibly hard to find elsewhere in gaming. Seriously enough of me singing Cultic's praises it's very cheap and it's a fantastic game. Not to mention Chapter Two will be releasing later on as DLC and it will be discounted for owners of Chapter One. GO PLAY CULTIC! P.S. Theres a survival mode if you want more content for your dollar.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent boomer shooter revival here. The secrets are not cryptic or boring and keep up with the pace of the game. The game tells you the story as fast as possible and its optional to even read it! No stupid lore ruining the momentum of the game. It even has a survival mode and the upgrade mechanics of the game's weapons fit perfectly into both modes. Secrets are very rewarding. The game's movement feels modernized which may be good for people that are new to the old style. Please turn off the double tap to dodge it will get you killed. I finished the game on the second to the last difficulty. It's also not too long of a game as well which is great because you can improve your times if you are interested so it does have some replay value. It is priced very fair for how much it offers. This game continues in the tradition of "game play before lore" which is part of why boomer shooters are great, the game also has some great creepy atmosphere going for it. Love the ambient music when I heard it but I didn't hear enough. If you change your controls you can abuse the slide mechanic for some fast level clears. If you are still looking for more reviews to help you decide allow me to help. If you see "game too hard" "ran out of ammo" "bad story" "game is too short"simply move on to the next review.Again I played on the second to last difficulty my 1st play-through and only ran out of certain ammo near the end. It might not have happened if I used more explosives in the right places. It took me a little over 6 hours and I looked up about 4 secrets because the pace of the game was fast and fun, I found the rest on my own!If you don't like a feature there is probably a check box to turn it off! I disabled the slow mo kills, I am not a fan of newer game mechanics in my boomer shooters. Excellent features for controller as well for even more old school feel. Final boss is lame af, (but very fast killable). The game designer must think bed of chaos is good game design... (its not). Also the music goes silent a lot when you are not in battle so it makes looking for that last secret very quiet. I was expecting more enemies but I haven't tried the final difficulty. A job well done, congraturation!!! This story is hapy end!!

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic old school shooter, obviously heavily inspired by blood and you could drop this in front of me and say it was blood 3 and id believe you fully. It was incredibly reminiscent of Return to Castle Wolfenstein and Wolf 09' actually. with the environments, weapon upgrading and general feel of being deep behind enemy lines and only going in deeper. The weapon upgrades system particularly reminded me of '09. Even some of the enemy designs are similar like the dual shotgun guys and the flamethrower guys, looked exactly like RTCW enemies, I mean ♥♥♥♥ it has the FG42 and the Flamethrower. Maybe I'm making connections that aren't there. Anyway, the gunplay feels amazing, nothing isn't useful, the enemies and their placements are varied, secrets prod at your imagination and never feel stupid not too easy. The game had a great sense of atmosphere to the point where certain set pieces genuinely creeped me out. The music is just phenomenal, one of the few soundtracks i bought. There is not a genuine criticism I can make of this game, other than that I died because the reload animation for the shotgun in the interlude map kept obscuring my vision. Also I had no idea there was a kick till I was done with the game and that makes me really sad. I think this type of game, like Blood before it, is best played on the second hardest difficulty in this case very hard. It allows for a great balance of measured tactical play, throwing dynamite aroudn corners and picking off distant enemies with your rifles; and expressing how much of a ♥♥♥♥-hot bombista you are, sprinting and jumping and sliding around weapon switching and firing off both shotgun barrels right into some dudes ♥♥♥♥♥♥ brain. Anything easier only warrants the super aggressive style and extreme does the opposite. Anyway good game with more to come get it on sale now or wait because the dev deserves more of your money.

_childDocuments_.review: an awesome and cleverly designed boomer shooter with minor horror elements would highly recommend my only gripe with it is that the play time is extremely short and leaves me wanting much more.makes excellent use of self set early 90's limitations sticking to a two tone approach using a muted brown and blue colour palette, that cleverly tie its small range of enemies into the environment making it easier for them to ambush or surprise you and also differentiates enemies by type of equipment they use. has very well thought out map design with a fair amount of branching paths that all end up leading to map progression and many a make shift jump scare as well as very awesome set dressing / lore that really create a great atmosphere.  the weapon variety all be it limited is very fun to use and feel amazingly responsive especially when paired up with the ultra gore the game provides my only minor complaint about them would be that a lot of the guns sort-of fill the same roll in combat and don't feel distinct enough from a game-play perspective. but overall impressions this game is really well crafted and well worth the money i can only hope that they continue to pump more content into it so i can play it even more!

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10What if Blood wasn't only a good game, but a great game as well? You get Cultic. Let's live again, again.+ Dismemberment+ Good level design.+ Good replay value.+ Good enemy variety.+ Good weapon variety.+ Weapons have great impact.+ Good aesthetics and graphics.+ Great soundtrack. _childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic (Episode 1) is a beast, kicking ass and taking names on its own (good) way. It scratched the itch of wanting to so-called "boomer shooter", with its own style.Although the comparison with Blood would be tiresome to many at this point, I personally felt that the similarity between the both is limited to their appearances and perhaps some of the theme(hoodie-upholstered fanatics shooting guns and plotting something sinister). On that note, you will end up being surprised if you were expecting Blood sequel, for they play rather different. As for how they differ, you will have to experience by yourself and draw your own conclusion!As for what are the strong points of this game, well... Just about everything was TASTY.- Guns pack pretty hefty punches, and sound cool. One thing I found interesting was that even though the game appeared to be set in the 1950s, the arsenal were from the early- to mid-WW2 days (I'm looking at you, Mauser C96). Still, they add characters to this game. And by the way, you are going to fall in love those dynamites.- Headshots are crunchy, and will make you endlessly satisfied. Bullet-times are bonus!- Soundtracks are golden, since they really set the mood: early on, the tunes make you feel dread itself with their eerie and haunting atmospheric sound; toward the end of your journey, however, you feel like a veteran action hero in Hollywood blockbusters.- Enemies: Chunky, gritty boys starting from humanoids to abominations. One thing I was having reservation was that their movements were, for some reason, jittery. But you get used to it soon enough, and it also adds to the character.- As for the lore, the player has to rake in notes and documents here and there. When I first noticed that that was the case, I was rather skeptical whether or not that approach would work. But it works, and works like wonder; what seemed like a series of disjointed text helps you draw the big picture in the end, which I really liked.Kudos to the developer, who chose to go one man army route and nailed it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a passable boomer shooter and impressive feat for a one-man band that will tide us boomers over until Boltgun drops.That said, I'm still forced to recommend other offerings from 3D Realms like Ion Fury and Wrath over it. I'd say play those first and then get this. Maybe wait until chapter 2 is out, but I'd not count on it ever happening. They still haven't finished Wrath or Ion Fury: Aftershock nearly 5 years since those games came out, and those games have entire teams of people.The game seems to have some performance issues; freezing up and crashing from time to time and odd framerate dips that I can't pinpoint the cause of, but nothing that rendered it totally unplayable. The art direction is rather drab, a bit too "subterranean" and too much brown. It also can at times be difficult to spot enemies due to the colors and art style. Most of the enemies in the game are kinda boring and the weapons are very basic shooter type guns. Not as fun as the stuff that was in say Duke3D or Ion Fury.I would say my biggest gripe with the game though is that it features too much modern shooter elements; the weapon select and reload is annoying, as is the slowed vinyl affect on the music when you gib someone. Much of the music really doesn't fit the vibe, but I'm not going to expect a one-man show to also be a master composer.The game is sort of how I imagine Clive Barker's Undying, or maybe those call of Cthulhu games would've been had they been build engine titles. If you like boomer shooters, you'll like this, but probably not as much as other titles in the boomer shooter renaissance.

_childDocuments_.review: DUSK blew my mind back when I first played it around 2017. My first shooter was Doom in 1994 and from that point forward, I lived and breathed FPS in my teenage years; but somewhere they lost the plot. DUSK brought it all back and got me excited about the genre all over again. At this point, five years later, we have a glut of these "Boomer Shooters" and frankly, most of them are just kind of bland and not very fun. I'll grant that I haven't played all of them, but CULTIC immediately grabbed my eye; Blood was a favorite of mine back in the day, so something styled after it had my attention. CULTIC lives up to the promise that DUSK made and far surpasses it at that. I don't have any details for you, just that CULTIC is fantastic. I'm old now, with a family and I don't game as much as I used to, but CULTIC wouldn't leave my brain and kept calling me back. I'd play it in maybe half an hour chunks, finishing a level here and there, as I had time, but I was constantly thinking about it, constantly wanting to go back to it. CULTIC broke my addiction to my Steam Deck, encouraged me to pick-up my old friends, Keyboard and Mouse and just have my way with some cultists. I am thankful for its existence.

_childDocuments_.review: Prefacing with: I finished the entire first chapter on Extreme within about 7 hours, found all but two secrets, and haven't played survival yet.Another preface: if you like fast-paced FPS games, do not read this review or any other. These games are best experienced blind, and there's basically nothing wrong with Cultic. It is perfection. It's everything you want in the type of game you're looking for. I am the foremost expert on boomer shooters so you can trust me.=====So this is basically peak boomer shooter. If you lived through the 90's-00's era of FPS, you know what 'boomer shooter' is really talking about. It's not a reference to 'old' shooters, it's a reference to a particular category of shooter. The kind where you move fast, you shoot fast, and there's as little talking as possible. Often none at all. No complicated backstory, no overdone cinematics, no exhausting exposition. These games are all about fast-paced, visceral, satisfying combat from start to finish - with a SMIDGE of rewarding exploration via 'secrets' - and Cultic has those things in spades.Every weapon feels satisfying to shoot. The satisfaction increases manifold when the shots connect with an enemy and make them dead, exploding them into a fest of blood and gore. We've got shotties, we've got bolties, we've got flamies and boomies, and brrrrrrrrap zoomies. Also: DYNAMITE STICKS, MOLOTOVS. YES.Work benches let you top up the functionality for things like rate of fire and reload speed, or you can just make everything hit harder! And to top it all off you get a slow-motion weapon wheel mechanic so you can change to a new weapon after every single shot because you're not really sure this is the weapon you want to use to rip apart the next group of enemies, hold on, let me try something else. These guns are too fun and I'm having a hard time choosing...The environments are what you'd expect when delving into the dark side of a minor, unassuming religious group that actually has some weight to its underside. You explore dense forests in the middle of nowhere, dilapidated mines, gut-wrenching crypts and some other interesting places, while being set upon by the psychotic zealots of the cult wielding many of their own weapons, bolstered by some more... unearthly forces. The enemies are surprisingly varied for being only the first chapter, suffice to say. And as the game progresses, it does a good job of making the fights feel like it's the hunter becoming the hunted; the difficulty ramp is fair, but not always predictable, and it has a way of getting you to think: damn, they almost got me, but not today.I think what really gets me about this game is that it manages to make you feel like you're doing well, when you're doing well, and really gets across the fact that your losses are your losses, not the game's. The enemies can absolutely dunk on you at any time if you're not careful; they hit really hard. But every single one of them, even the rapid-fire machinegunners and the long-range snipers, give you a clear and fair shot at avoiding the damage. There's always a bit of cover nearby, or an opening to exploit, or hey, if you're good enough; get that A/D skill going cuz these ain't hitscan!My deaths never felt like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥; I always knew it was me playing poorly. Even the ambushes were great at making you feel like you just got thrown in the deep end, but ensuring you had a reasonable way to avoid drowning. Maybe it ties one of your hands behind your back sometimes...So this is all well and good, but is there a 'story' of any kind? What's the purpose of all this? How do I 'immerth mythelf in the game'?Alright, alright. There's a BIT of story, and it's capped off by various bits of writing you can find throughout the game. Thankfully it's entirely self-serving and there's no functional advantage to finding the little pieces of paper, so everybody wins!Here's the summary, though:In Cultic, you are a detective investigating some concerning events-... oh, wait, that's the background from the opening video. Hold on a second...You were recently made into a memory and buried in the backyard of a particularly intense group of individuals. When you wake up, you decide you are not very happy about this, and looking to get a little payback. To top things off, this 'cult' seems to be getting up to some suspicious shenanigans that may or may not be chill for the rest of humanity. Combining these two points, it becomes clear you have one job, and one job only: to be as annoying and inconvenient to the cult as humanly possible. Your primary mode of doing so?Sprinting through the gritty environments while murdering everything that moves.Have fun out there, kids.

_childDocuments_.review: Ehh, ok, look. The 1st chapter is 10 bucks, and will last around 4 hours. Sure it's the best 4 hours you're gonna have in an fps, since it's an extremely refined and thought-out fps, but it's also ONLY 4 hours long, with chapter 2 coming in the future as... Paid DLC instead of a normal update like every other game that's not complete yet. Hrmmnhh...You really can approach the combat situations freely here, that much is actually true.... to a point. There are very clearly some sections where certain weapons are needed and others aren't, but then again, sometimes there are multiple roads or an expansive area where you could probably do some weird stuff with the tnt and grenade launcher and clear entire areas early, or slowly pick everything off with the rifle, pistol, and shotgun like ye old times.That doesn't apply to the bosses, though, who are bullet sponges with added annoyances that spawn in during the fight, though at least the ones for the first one do run out so you don't just waste all your ammo and time killing them for 20 minutes. If that happens on the second one, I don't know, cause that second boss happened right at the end of the game, and I already upgraded my guns and just wanted to get out of the damn catacombs already, so I practically spedrun it......Oh yeah. The upgrades. The parts for them are mostly in secrets, which irks me a little bit considering what fps secrets usually consist of, but, you get enough on the main path to get a few improvements, but not all of them, though that actually seems intentional, so points for that.The part that actually worries me, though, is that the dev's already gone and sold plushies with free copies of the game attached, and spammed his twitter with the fact that he really wants you to buy them, and put two "product update" posts in steam for it. I get it man, you want us to give you our money, but calm down, you haven't even finished your game yet, and the second chapter's not even going to be a free update. If ch2's not as good as ch1, people are going to get upset over that dlc fact, and the plushie, but if it is as good, or, god forbid it actually surpasses ch1, then it's not gonna matter and I'm just gonna look a little silly- gonna need to edit this review if that happens... Just don't up the price, cause, again, ch 1 is only 4 hours long for 10 bucks.Overall, if you're used to shooters and want to feel what a really damn good version of what you've replayed about a hundred times now in different forms is, go ahead and buy/play it, just keep in mind that it's really short and that the second chapter is going to be paid dlc, so, also stay a little skeptical about what that second chapter might be, both in quality and story wise. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to point out a bunch of annoying little problems, so let me just preface by saying the game is genuinely good.  And I don't say that lightly.  Games like Ultrakill and DUSK that people fawn over, their action just felt like endless circle strafing to me, not like the dance of Blood and Doom and some others.  CULTIC nails this though.  Combat is crunchy and rhythmic.It is in fact similar to Blood in almost every way, except the levels are bigger, there are light RPG elements which help the sense of progress, and there are more weapons, particularly conventional bullet-based weapons (which I'm partial to).So here's everything I  like:• All the way up to the chappel with the tank, the game gets off to a slow first half.  The weapons come slow, and more ammo and more enemies would have been appreciated.• There's too many levels that take place underground, or with an underground appearance.  Underground levels are always relatively simple and ugly.• Because of the larger, open levels, often the most effective way to play is the least fun way.  i.e. You can usually just pop heads from a large distance until the whole area is clear.• Every time you rebind a key, the list jumps back up to the top.  Definitely irritating.• I don't think hatchets should glow on the ground like ammo, etc.  They're just not valuable.  But when you see the glow you'll go over there thinking it is.• The game doesn't handle key binding conflicts in an ideal way.• The music track restarts when you quickload.  If it just continued, unbroken, every load would feel less jarring.• The quickloads take a little too long.  I know it's only like 5 seconds, but still, 1-2 seconds like every other game would be better.• The controls for lighting throwing dynamite/molotovs, is a little unintuitive.  The light throw is almost useless, so shouldn't left-click be the long throw?• The shotgun's reload goes quicker if you mash fire.  I'd rather it just go the fastest possible speed by itself.• When upgrading a weapon, you have the 4 possible upgrades in front of you, but there's no indication whatsoever on the UI of which weapon you're upgrading.  Since most wepons are conventional, their upgrades often look indistinguishable.• As it is, there's aboslutely nothing besides a pile of handwritten notes in each level.  Blood had a small cutscene per chapter, and little quips from Caleb during combat.  Slightly more in the way of story or even characters would go a long way for player investment.• An option for toggle (as opposed to hold) for scoped weapons would be appreciated.And things which are probably bugs:• I'm still getting “Gib Time” activating in certain levels, even with it turned off.• You can't quickload when you're dead.• If an enemy is standing behind a window, and you fire at their head, no matter how powerful the weapon, the first shot will *only* break the window; not damage the enemy.• The very first instance of the incinerator enemy disappeared after a quickload. (He had been alive and chasing me.)• When you quickload, your flashlight is off, regardless of its state before.• Just an idea, but using voxels for the corpses of enemies you've killed would look a lot better than sprites which spin around like crazy as you move past them.OK I think that's it for now.  Good game though, all things considered.

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I can describe this is simply this.Take the concept of Blood (which funnily enough WAS developed by 3D realms for a while before they sold it to Monolith Productions) and give it more of a VERY light noir kind of feel to it. This comes into context that you play as a (to my knowledge) unamed and undead detective who was killed by a cult but then wants to get revenge on them while ALSO still finishing his last case. You could say it's almost as if Caleb decided to join the police before he passed away instead (jokingly speaking of course)Now DON'T get me wrong, there are NOT any detective searching areas akin to Heavy Rain or L.A. Noire here. But what there IS is an emphasis on a grim take of mystery and the darker sides to investigating things. This is told through lore pickups you find in levels and as well as some of the settings where levels take place (such as an abandoned sheriffs office/jail and an asylum)I guess another comparison that can be lightly made here is Outlast but with a small bit of grim detective-esque flair to it.But none of that wouldn't mean a thing if the levels were badly, the guns didn't feel good or if the  enemies were pushovers right?Well thank God that this isn't the case and Cultic checks all these boxes.From an old repeater that can take down cannon foder quickly with one well placed shot to a double barreled shotgun that can blast heavier units to a variety of dynamite traps. You can even fall back on weaponizing your fists and legs or a hatchet or even the environment if ammo is low. But trust me, this is  a LAST RESORT because you'll quickly get your ass handed to you and end up back in your grave if not careful.As an added bonus, you can find secrets and collectible weapon parts where you can find hidden weapon benches and upgrade and or change your weapons between levels and carry them through the remainder of the campaign. From decreasing reload speed for the rifle to lower ammo capacity for the pistol but making up for this by increasing the damage. Despite being basic and obviously done in other games in regards to the upgrade system. It's not often that an upgrade system like this is integrated into a modern-retro type of indie FPS that aims for a 90s esque design approach. Top this off with every upgrade having a benefit and drawback (to be honest I just cant remember them all) and you have a nice sprinkle of strategy that not only makes you think but also can cater to your playstyle and what weapons you perfer, and as mentioned before, its good incentive for any completionist or person that tries to go for 100% considering most of these are found via secret areas.All of this thrown into CULTIC and a mix of dark/gothic atmosphere with a "detective biting off more than he could chew, but now is back from the grave" tale of revenge and this scratches that Blood/Horror FPS itch that me and many other games have been having.I can't WAIT for chapter 2 and I'm eager to solve the next part of this morbid detective's case of revenge, cultists, and chaos!Get this game if you want a unique throwback that is well crafted and does 90s grim FPS nostalgia done right while bringing its own twists and turns to the table
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only on the third level and this is already scratching every possible boomer-shooter itch you could have. Forgive Me Father was fine, and HROT set the bar pretty high, but this is currently my favorite of a genre I'm so happy to see being revived. Mechanics, level design, atmosphere, and scoring are all superb. The blending of voxel art and sprites enables the game to feel the way memories of a classic shooter play out. On the higher difficulties, it is damn hard. You might get stuck looking for a key. You might get your ass handed to you by a room full of cultists 20 times before you find the right combination of dynamite, hatchets, and shotgunning. You will quicksave like you're about to murder all of Whiterun frequently. And you will love every minute of it. One of the most exciting releases I've played in a hot minute.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic might just be my new favorite "new-wave-boom-shoot" (trademark pending) game. Everything about it just oozes Blood, however, it does manage to carve its own identity with memorable setpieces, the tasteful soundtrack, and the orgasmic gunplay's marriage to the high-octane action. I had a blast trying to Matrix my way through the game on extreme (which I would say compares to Blood on Well-done difficulty), but the game's quieter, more atmospheric moments are also to die for. Highly recommended to everyone, even if chapter one only comes with 10 levels.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: If this is what Chapter 1 is like, then I can't wait for Chapter 2. Snappy gameplay, weapon diversity without bogging down inventory with the introduction of the lighter, the challenging but not unfair difficulty, movement that doesn't cause motion sickness (at least for me)... Bravo, team. Well done. All I can really recommend is a bit more color variation, since the cultists blend into the background a bit too easily.P.S. Civvie sent me.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Boomer shooters are coming around again, and Cultic is easily the best example I've seen so far. With an arsenal of guns, explosives and handy hatchets at your disposal the endless hordes of cultists and eldritch monstrosities are great fun to fight. Cultic has atmosphere in spades, and more than a few moments that are genuinely creepy and tense. At under a tenner it's a steal, and there's more content on the way.If at first you don't succeed, try again with dynamite!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: A great boomer-shooter that combines elements from Blood and Resident Evil 4: from Blood it takes the horror/occult themes, ridiculous gibby gore and the tactical yet fast-paced combat of using cover, peeking, and clearing rooms with dynamite before entry to deal with deadly hitscanners, and from RE4 it takes the weapon upgrading system and campaign pacing where every level is something fresh and provides so much spectacle.Even after beating it, I was raring to get right back to replaying it on Extreme difficulty: the game's just that satisfying to play in general. Speaking of, the game's also ridiculously cheap for the amount of content you get: the campaign already would've been enough, but with a bonus interlude level and a survival arena, it's a steal!If I had to find something bad, I will say that my first impression of it wasn't the greatest: for example, the choppy animation for enemies can make it awkward to anticipate their movements and aim precisely, and in particular, dealing with hitscanners at extreme long ranges in open areas who react to you immediately made the game feel like such a pixel-hunt snipefest. However, once you get used to the combat design (which can be awkward if you have come from more run-n-gun shooters, as I did) and get better tools to deal with engagements, it grabbed me and wouldn't let go.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: ❤️❤️❤️❤️🤍I hope the developers out there are taking notes, because THIS is how you make a boomer shooter. The first time I saw this I was like, oh cool, someone made a spiritual successor to . I was wrong. This is so much better than that. I can’t get over how good this game is. The creepy atmosphere, the gunplay, and the music… everything comes together so nicely. It’s even more impressive that this was made by one dude. I don't like how dynamite and molotovs work in this game - you have to light them manually before throwing them so most of the time I accidentally threw them at the enemies without lighting them. I also had some minor problems with enemy pathing where they got stuck on things, which did ruin some of the immersion, took away some of the challenge, and ultimately robbed me of a few monster encounters that would have been incredible had the AI not gotten itself stuck on level geometry. The game is also very short, with only ten levels to beat. Still, this is more than worth the asking price.Warmly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid gunplay, pretty big maps, secrets to find are all pro's. Also alot of interaction with the environment. You can kick and throw just about everything, even eyeballs :p Also you can upgrade your weapons to make them better.People say that the game is shor,(3 to 5 hours for fast players), but there are achievements and other things to do. So, it will keep you busy if you go for extra challenges like survival.The game looks very retro, mind that this is by design choice. And turn down the brightness.The game is a bit like Blood(Cultists and all), and actually has a story you can read in different notes and at type-writers. This is chapter one and has 10 levels, chapter two will probably be released as a DLC.Recommended, especially if you are into retro FPS games.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is the best Retro FPS I've ever played. I played the original demo, and it was amazing back then. It's even better now.Something I never expected when I first played the demo was how much upgrading your character would be a factor. Not only can you upgrade your guns at workbenches using weapon parts, but you can permanently increase your maximum health by finding "imbued remains" throughout the game.If you don't care for the upgrades and want to rely only on your mechanical skill, you can just ignore them. Don't pick up any imbued remains, don't use workbenches. It's not like they're remotely required, each piece of imbued remains only increases your max HP by 5. On my first playthrough on the Hard difficulty, I only found 3 to bump by health to 115.Cultic's guns are masterfully crafted, each one remains useful throughout the entire game (and not just because of the upgrades).The hatchet is good for low-level cultists, especially opposing hatchet-wielders.The handgun can be used to effectively take out enemies from long range AND deal decent damage at close range.The lever-action rifle acts as the game's revolver, having a much slower firing speed than the handgun but with much more power and perfect accuracy, though also with scarcer ammo.The shotgun is absolutely insane at close range, and can reduce an enemy to a fountain of blood if you discharge both barrels at once.The STEN has less accuracy than the handgun, but much higher DPS, making it a better use of your ammo when it comes to crowds.The grenade launcher is probably the least useful gun, but only because you already have more than enough explosive power with the TNT and molotov cocktails.The FG42 is like the lever-action rifle, but with a scope and a different ammo type. If you are low on ammo for one, you can rely on the other.The incinerator is a flamethrower, and Jesus Christ is it powerful. It can immediately dispatch a low-level cultist using a single point of ammo (of which you can hold several hundred). Even the toughest enemies can go down in 5-10 points of ammo. The alt-fire is powerful too, but the the primary fire can get infinitely more use out of the same amount of ammo the alt-fire consumes.Each gun gets 4 upgrades (except the incinerator because it's already powerful enough). The first one always costs 4 weapon parts, and in every case it's a simple damage boost (except with the Grenade Launcher, where it's an increase in explosion size). The second one always costs 2 parts and in every case is a higher magazine/clip/tube/whatever capacity (except with the Shotgun where it's a faster reload). The third and fourth are weapon-specific and are usually 2 weapon parts, but are occasionally 1, 3, or 4. Some examples are better accuracy for the Handgun and STEN, tighter spread for the Shotgun, and a full-auto mode for the FG42.(I actually have a nitpick with one upgrade, the Lever-Action's "Deadeye." I think it's practically useless, especially for 3 weapon parts, which could be spend on something infinitely better like a faster fire rate for the STEN or a burst-fire mode for the Handgun. Deadeye just grants a small amount of slow-motion on a successful headshot with the lever-action's alt-fire, which barely helps, and also there's already a chance of it happening on a kill. I have two ideas: 1. reduce the weapon part cost to one, or 2. remove the Lever-Action's alt-fire by default, and have the upgrade actually be what allows you to use it, along with the slow-mo thing.)
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: So, I bought this game with people saying that this is the true sequel to my favorite boomer shooter, Blood. Now, this game ain't Blood, but it was not trying to be Blood. It took some notes from it for sure, in terms of weapons, game mechanics, and some tonal elements, but it is more of its own thing. This game has elements of Half-Life 2, Doom 3, and Blood, and a few other games I am sure, but it is done so well that you can't help but think that the developer learned the right lessons from all of these games, Doom 3 especially since that game had "tech demo" written all over it. This game is also not as difficult as Blood, but hard for sure provided a good challenge for me on a first play through. The visuals are striking, but I had to turn the limited pallet off. My eyes were straining from the default limited color pallet. A shame too, as it adds to the overall vibe, but the game still looks good even with it turned off.My one issue with this game, and a lot of other games have the same issue is weapon upgrades. I do not like these as all it does for most games is hamstring the weapons from being their most fun. I hate when games give you a cool new thing, but you can't use it because all of your other weapons are better because you upgraded them to be useful. Cultic is not too bad about this, but there are some weapon upgrades that are vital for them to be useful. The upgrade to tighten the spread of your sawed-off is a good example of this. This then runs into the other end of annoyances of upgrades that are either subjective in usefulness or flat-out useless. As I said, Cultic is one of the lesser offenders in this area, unpopular opinion, Doom Eternal is the worst recent example, but it still annoys me that the sawed-off is way more frustrating to use until that one upgrade. I would rather have fewer opportunities and upgrades to have, but have them be really useful or changing, like incendiary rounds, more considerable damage increases, or other things which could be considered spoiler-y in nature, but you will figure it out pretty quickly. It to me is Cultic's one weak spot, which is amazing. This game has so many cool mechanics to figure out, and I loved doing it. I loved scouring everywhere for secrets, and more of the game's rather unique, but comfortably familiar weapon set. I think the best example of how weapon upgrades hurts a game's feel, dynamite is from the word go, one of the game's best mechanics and is vital for higher level play. This is also the first game I have played that made Molotov cocktails feel really good to use. I can't think of a game since, well, Blood that got throw-able weapons like dynamite so good feeling to use.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect from the visuals, gun, sound design, level design and story i love it. The aesthetics/visuals are very unique compared to some of the other boomer shooters i've played (dusk really and doom 64 not well versed in this genre). Guns feel so good like there is real weight with each shot, however i did wish we got more lore i loved reading the notes and i wanted to learn more. Also i want to take about the explosives i was kind of puzzled why youd want to manual light it then it hit me, laying down traps and the ability to unwrap the dynamite so it spreads very cool. I can see the love that was put into this game and i really appreciate it. There is a lot of things id want to talk about and i dont want this to be too long. All im saying is this is the first review i have ever done with 8 years on steam this is a damn good game and worth every dollar and every minute of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: The Blood influence is obvious, but the open-ended combat design reminds me of something more like Crysis of all things. You often get overviews of large combat encounters and can take a lot of different approaches, including with various types of environment interactivity, to get through them. Few retro FPS styled games have attempted this kind of planning aspect and pace. I'm having a lot of fun, and it's the type of game I can see myself replaying due to the variety in approaches you can take to encounters, much like with the Crysis games.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: If you come here expecting BLOOD you better reconsider, it is inspired in some aspects but not much on the gameplay side, here it's more slow and methodical if you don't wanna get killed all the time.Personally I find the graphical style leans a bit too much into pixel vomit territory, it's hard to decipher what you're even looking at on a regular basis and that's not good in a game where headshots are your primary goal for survival.Still it's a great game, once you get into it the game feels great at every point and there's very few encounters that are particularly annoying or bad to deal with, ammo is plentiful though not overabundant and the two boss encounters are challenging in a fun way.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: I thought it was gonna be a decent boomer shooter emulating Blood.I was wrong, it is so much more than that. This game totally blew my expectations, The game is totally action packed, shooting feels awesome, the guns are great. the levels are great and theres even an upgrade system for guns so searching for secret is even more satisfying.If I had to pick something bad, maybe it would had to be that theres too many Mine levels, the lighting effect is too much even if this was the intent (I beleive its called dithering) and  two particular weapons feel clunky to use on the go (which I hope gets improved on a patch)Definitely get this game. _childDocuments_.review: After a first few levels i was expecting a little more, some of the mid-game levels i felt were maybe just a little too short, and some were just very wide open which gets a bit boring because i just shot everyone from distance. Weapons are great, but it feels weird to have 2 long range rifles, i was expecting to get something more like plasma canon or some other wunderwaffe to pair up with incinerator. Dynamite and molotovs are amazing though. Enemy variety is fine, but again, towards mid-late game i was expecting something more out of left field. AI is pretty dumb, often gets stuck or just walks into fire and dies, but that's rarely becomes an actual issue. Really enjoyed all the horror moments and atmosphere, that and the music are really good.The game is great though, and i think i'm more dealing with my own expectations and a style of gameplay i'm not the biggest fan of, rather than actual flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down my favorite FPS to have come out since Dusk caused a resurgence in retro FPS. The fact it was made by one person is staggering. The atmosphere is great, weapon feedback like nothing else on the market, music is both pumping and somber, and did I mention the amazing atmosphere? Every corner of this game, from the rendering style to the easter eggs, drips with effort and passion. Absolutely buying and playing chapter 2 the moment it releases. I'd pre-order if I could! It's that good!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic: Chapter One is good. People should know Chapter Two will be paid DLC, so you are not guaranteed both chapters with this one purchase. That's fine. This was worth the $10. It's got some unique qualities, but it's more or less another boomer shooter. Fans of Blood will enjoy this one especially after the lackluster sequel. I'll list the pros and cons below.Pros:-Solid gunplay with alt-fire options-Very bloody and very gory-Great soundtrack-Dark atmosphere-Beautiful well-animated retro graphics-Good enemy variety-High challenge-TNT/Molotovs are extremely fun to use-RE: Mercenaries-style survival mode-Well priced-Non-linear level design full of secrets-Worldbuilding through in-game notes is a nice touch-Color filter option-Weapon upgrade system-Environmental interaction adds immersive sim elementsCons:-No input buffering (pressing a number key mid-animation to switch weapons doesn't interrupt animation or queue the input for when the animation completes)-Final boss is an easy stationary target that can be killed in less than a minute-The few platforming sections are dreadful-Only a few weapons and they're not very unique. It's a standard arsenal (handgun, shotgun, rifle, grenade launcher)-Cheap enemy spawns and enemies often shoot you immediately upon showing yourself leaving little time to react (To be fair, Blood was like this as well)-Dodging is mostly useless (I don't even think the game tells you how to dodge)-Armor value isn't shown. It's just a meter that fills up/goes down.-Pretty slow load timeIt's a solid shooter for fans of the classic Build engine games. I wouldn't say it's all that innovative, but it's a fun, challenging, creepy ride. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a neutral review I would, but I liked it more than I didn't and the price point is fair, so I'll give it a positive. It's also impressive that this is a one-person endeavor. TL;DR; It's a good Unity-Engine FPS shooter, but it still feels like every other Unity-Engine FPS shooter.The game is fun, and it really has the heart of a 90s shooter. If you liked Blood back in the day, you will be happy about a lot of this game.Most of the maps are well designed, though (like many games in this genre) the later maps are smaller, feel rushed, and are not as thought out as the earlier maps. The first maps take 20-40 minutes to beat, while the later maps take around 10-15. Weapons are fun, not a lot of them, but the ones it gives you work well. Though I'm not really sure why they decided to feature Nazi weapons without context, but whatever. The sound design is great. The music is decent though some of the tracks are a little grating. So my main complaint about the game is by halfway through the first level you realize, "Oh I'm playing another 'retro-FPS' game made in Unity". While this is definitely a solid iteration, there is nothing that really makes the game-play unique, and almost ironically (as this was a common complaint about later games made in the BUILD engine) it feels like more of the same.  Even the slow-down mechanic (which has been done to death) feels tacked on and doesn't really add anything to the game. The game is also very short and ends abruptly, I was able to beat it in 2 and a half hours when usually games like this I expect to spend 9-12 hours, but, for 10 bucks, it's fine.Overall, if you like these types of games as I do, it will be a satisfying experience. Just don't expect anything groundbreaking here. I'd give it a 6/10 closer to a 5 than a 7.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic 2.5D retro FPS. Everything about this game is so well thought out.+ The weapons feel great, each serving it's own purpose. The explosive weapons are strong but balanced by how clunky they are. When in doubt: TNT...+ Enemies are fun, from how they attack you to the way they blow themselves up with their own dynamite.+ The level design in combination with spooky sound track creates an atmosphere that is absolutely stellar. Secrets that are cleverly hidden, notes scattered here and there, the lighting, the voxel assets that have just enough detail to look convincing, it's all very well done.- The weapon upgrade menu could have better UX, but that's nitpicking...The only real complaint I have is that there is only one chapter of it.There aren't many boomer shooters that manage to achieve this level of fun and quality, bravo.

_childDocuments_.review: There's one minor detail that speaks about the design philosophy behind this game; the doors.If you hit the use key on a door it opens slowly, giving you time to peer in and snipe anyone you see inside. Alternatively, you can kick the door open instantly and go full aggression mode, if you're lacking in patience.This reinforces the core idea of "play your way", with both slower and methodical play and fast-paced blitzkrieg action being entirely viable, as long as you have the ammo for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly amazing game with terrific atmosphere, jumpscares a horror. Takes a lot of inspiration from classic FPS games. The graphics or rather the art design is amazing. It feels like a classic game with lot of modern stuff. Doesn't get boring in the slightest. Soundtrack is very fitting, modern sounding yet midi sounding. Epic game.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so here's the deal:You're gonna fork over $10 for this gem.I want you to think about what $10 dollars means to you. Is it a dumbass fast-food meal that you're gonna eat and then "git rid" of later? Is it gas money? A gram? Look...the thing is...I don't want to hear it, and I know damned well that Jason Smith, the SOLO developer for this masterpiece, doesn't want to hear it either. He busted his ass to deliver the best boomer-shooter I've ever played; and I've played them all. Those $10 give you access to a Blood-inspired, cultist slaying, romp through the most open-ended levels I've ever seen in a boomer-shooter. The attention to detail is great too. He really nails the whole vibe of every level in the game. The way that levels loop back onto themselves is really awesome too. I was always amazed when I'd note a locked door early on in the level, and then end up using that door as an exit after obtaining the key needed for it. The first level alone kept me occupied for about 40 minutes on very hard difficulty. The sheer amount of interactability and complexity in the levels astounded me. It's just nothing that games that inspired it ever achieved. The soundtrack is really good too. It also helps nail the atmosphere that Jason was going for. Always fast when the action is good, and always quiet and eerie when it need to set a more sp00ky tone. I could say more but I won't. That's it. You'll get paid again. If you are a kid, and don't have a job, then do what you gotta do for that $10. You're welcome. Personal rating: 9.5/10Difficulty: 4.5/10 (very hard)
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is an old school FPS that can easily be mistaken for a 1997 release, unlike many "boomer shooters", a term which has been used way too liberally recently in my opinion, the game echoes many aspects that made the FPS classics stick out in our memory. At its core, it is a traditional FPS game, you start out with a simple melee weapon and progress to pick up an expanding arsenal that checks every box, trusty shotgun, explosives launcher, sniper rifle, automatic gun with high rate of fire etc. The level progression is linear, just like in the classics of the genre, you move through levels, picking up  keys and learning about the story through optional journals. The enemies also vary from simple grunts, to high HP powerhouses, as well as ones with magical abilities and long range attacks. Every staple of the classic FPS is here, as if someone was checking off a list.What makes Cultic work so well, as opposed to many contemporaries, is the atmosphere. From the very first moment in the game, you are dropped into a world of horror, the game maintains a grimy, dirty and dark tone throughout the entire playthrough. The setting is very similar to one of my favorites classic shooters, Blood, which was the main reason I picked it up. The influences of Blood are very clear, cultists, darkness, dynamite...If I had to pick a single developer to make an actual sequel to Blood, the developer of Cultic would be my first choice. The only negatives I can report is that the game is pretty short and I am not a fan of the upgrade mechanic, although it is well done and not absolutely necessary for progression, I've barely used it in my playthrough. If you are a fan of classics like Blood, Heretic, etc, I would highly advise picking Cultic up at it's extremely modest $9.99 price tag. You're going to have a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Right away, to those of you who just need to decide what difficulty to pick and quickly dive in, go for Extreme if you feel ballsy. It won't be too insane of you. Other than a couple of spikes that made me curse my arrogance, and one of them has been fixed by this point,  it's surprisingly manageable. The resulting hassle is a tactical feast rather than a frustrating mess. CULTIC borrows many things from Blood, yet leaves most of its relentless bullsh*t in the past. I'm saying it lovingly, of course (). For one, hitscan cultists here give you plenty of time to react to their presence, that being a saving grace when making higher difficulties viable. Now, for those in need of convincing.CULTIC celebrates its roots. I love the playfully macabre vibes it excretes, invoking memories of RE4, Blood, and Splatterhouse. Speaking of references, the game allows itself just the right amount of relevant nods while not offsetting the grimness of its world with some current out-of-character gags to please the crowd. Many things you'll find in it are hilarious and there's a ton of camp smeared about, although, for the majority of the time, the tone is appropriately morbid and the humour is pitch-dark, which I find extremely immersive. This game is going to age gracefully in every aspect of its presentation.If I remember correctly, the overlay filter used to be more aggressive before the release. Or maybe it only seemed that way? Somehow, CULTIC looks significantly better in action than on screenshots or in trailers. The visuals have been beaten into a pulp, coated in all shades of a bruise, and tastefully so. I can't get enough of these classy colours, they're extremely effective at painting the overall mood and tone. The skybox is beyond gorgeous and, even just by looking at the main menu, one can tell the artistry is pure grunge. Not to mention the stellar HUD, boasting fancy yet perfectly readable fonts. I'm a sucker for those.Local highly-detailed scenery is complemented with voxels for pickups and props. They're on the money, and not just visually, adding to the environmental interactivity. You can shatter a toilet or grab a chair and break someone's back with it. Oil lamps spill, furniture crumbles, barrels explode, and the explosions are fierily massive, facilitating gorgeous fire effects. Ah, screaming people running around on fire! It takes me home. The gore parade gets magnified by the dynamic and manually placed lighting, which gets reflected on your guns and enemy sprites. Also, I adore it when I can see my character's feet in a shooter. Not a kink, I swear.Map design is one, though. While CULTIC's isn't as intricate or varied as that of Blood, there are plenty of expansive maps for one chapter. I'm a slow player, so you can probably subtract several hours from my playtime, but these 10 appropriately grimy places are a bang for your buck either way. You get your caves and mines, docks, canyons, asylum, village, crypt, mansion, caves and mines again... maybe slightly too many of the latter for my taste. There's nothing you haven't seen before, yet every classic location is done competently. They neatly loop around and facilitate amazing encounter design that makes you expect death around every corner and use your booby-trapped surroundings to dispose of enemy hordes effectively.When stuffing said surroundings with secrets, CULTIC comes the closest to Blood by making you pay attention to environmental cues like cracks in the walls, vents, hidden buttons, or platforming opportunities. Besides, finding at least a few nooks per level is almost necessary because of the stern ammo distribution and the fact no one likes to miss out on upgrades, permanent health buffs, sometimes whole new weapons. The maps are interesting structurally rather than visually. Still, these tight haunted corridors, stuffy cellars, or your good old bodies piling in the middle of a room possess a strong atmosphere, drenched in rich ambience and pleasant music. Sometimes interspersed with moments of eerie silence.However brief. I’m not sure if “shooting shouting cultists with a Mauser” was the intended predominant impression to take away from the experience, but it felt better than it sounds. RE4 designs are evidently the strongest influence in this field. You'll see cultists wielding everything from axes and shields to grenade launchers, and they'll constitute the majority of your kills. Despite that theoretical monotony, they were fun to deal with. I had to seize advantageous positions to ambush them, hide for a breather, crouch and scamper like a rat, use everything in my arsenal, which was highly satisfying. Said monotony simply didn't get the chance to set in.To boot, every so often, you'll encounter monsters like ghosts, instakill chainsaw maniacs, savage long-jumping zombies, gargantuan skull-headed feral brutes, skeletons, and something my Steam friend accurately described as a "p*ssy monster from Michigan: Report from Hell". I particularly appreciated the tightly-tailored encounters where you, for example, get to fight a chainsaw maniac while manoeuvring around bear traps or when two of them chase you in a narrow hedge maze. That was exciting! Most of this game's encounters are extremely well-designed, it's full of such Panic Horror surprises. As a matter of fact, however, the real horror is you.These cultists messed with the wrong person who has the means to take them to school. Starting with all the ways to get out of trouble like fluid movement, including slides, dodges, and double-jumping. Local gunplay is smooth and snappy, with guns ringing, clicking, and clacking as they should. Shrilling gunshots lead to delightful headsplosions, making splurts of blood spray around the place. Punctuating the weight behind random moments of badassery, slow motion triggers sparingly on headshots and multikills. The overall game feel is enhanced by the combat awareness provided. Since finetuned feedback lets you know when you hit, kill or receive damage, violence here feels impactful and visceral.Harvesting it to the fullest is your arsenal. An insanely potent Mauser, a double-barrel that gets passable after a few upgrades, an enjoyable lever-action rifle capable of popping multiple heads when the cultists are lined up, a grenade launcher that is vital for your survival, and a surprisingly great flamethrower for a genre that loves to f*ck them up. There are 10 or so pieces altogether, but these are the ones I typically had ammo for. CULTIC is stingy like that, making up for it with tons of dynamite and Molotovs for all occasions. And don't forget you have a secondary fire for every gun and a cathartic tertiary fire for the explosives. It would be obscene to ask for more... but I'd love to see a working chainsaw in the next chapter, please.This review is glowing for a reason. At this point, it should be evident that CULTIC has class. The developer approached it with all seriousness and it could be seen long before the job was finished. Now, looking at how fast the game gets fixed and updated, how much people love it, I'm just glad to see the result corresponding to the efforts invested. To top it off, the polish is superb. I only had one random crash that I consider acceptable. All in all, between the timeless style, killer gunplay, and 10 saturated levels, even the worst of which never drag thanks to the great encounter design, CULTIC is a riveting joyride. Don't wait for a discount, it's a steal at full price.My curator

_childDocuments_.review: Cultic is the best old school fps in modern era. Unique gameplay, weapon upgrades, brutal combat, crunchy weapons and pixelated dark atmosphere. To top it off, is an excellent soundtrack.Each map has a unique layout and there's great amount of variety with different heights, vertical gameplay. Cramped hallways to sniper shoot outs. Some levels are creepy and horror comes into play which I liked quite a bit. The story itself is presented through visual storytelling and some text documents which are thrilling to read. Every map is filled with secrets to the brim and finding those out is really fun.Completed on Extreme and I recommend it to anyone who likes some challenge, it's pretty doable.Cultic is a really fun shooter to spend time on. Do not hesitate to go in and look for yourself. But, most importantly,you can see your legs. 666/10

_childDocuments_.review: Got bored one day, bought this game, booted it up...INSTANT 10/10Dear lord this game is amazing AND IT IS DONE BY ONE GUY?! WHAAAAAAAAA?So what are you expecting from this game?It's a Retro FPS, you boot it up, start a new game, pick up the weapon in front of you and shoot your way through enemies...simple as that.- There is a story, simple but effective: it's the 1960, you're a detective investigating on a case of people dissapearing, for one reason or another you're taken off the case but that ain't enough to stop you so you picked up a gun and your car to put the word end to the case...turns out it's cultist and they ain't happy to see ya. The lore is told through files; but of course the real star of the show is the gameplay.- The gameplay rocks: The arsenal is perfect and each gun feels chunky, meaty, powerful; Headshots are satisfying and play a big role much like explosions and fire, most of the environment is interactive and there's stuff to YEET at the enemies, the movement is perfect, quick enough to feel like you're in an action movie, the dodge, the kick boosting and the slide compliment the movement; much like a pizza with a good beer.- The enemies are varied: Cultist armed with various weapons, Armored, Zombies, ABOMINATIONS FROM ANOTHER DIMENTIONS... they have a simple AI (Find player, kill player, HOOGA BOOGA) and yet they can surprise you, also they all hurt like hell.- The OST surprised me, i was expecting creepy tunes and chanting ( I got that), i wasn't expecting an action movie OST, it's good.- The atmosphere of this game is another highlight, it can go from: Feeling like Ash Williams, killing cultist, spouting one liners ( Yourself of course, the character is silent) and then all of a sudden it's: "Why is the music gone? Why is everything gone quiet? Why do i have a bad fee...AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA"- The game has 10 levels but they're well designed and long just the right amount of time.If you're a fan of FUN FPS games then...BUY THIS GAME! Even at full price it's worth every cent!
