_childDocuments_.review: I love this new wave of retro-inspired shooters and Cultic is my second favourite of the bunch right after the tremendous Amid Evil. Calling this just another “boomer-shooter” doesn’t do the game justice though. While the first impression from trailers and screenshots might lead to the conclusion that Cultic is just Blood 3 under another name, it is a lot more. It certainly takes a lot of inspiration from the 1997 classic, but it adds survival horror elements to it and makes it play more like a modern game. And it nails almost every aspect of it. The graphics are gorgeous with a highly stylized and filtered look, adding a very dark and gloomy atmosphere to the experience. The amazing soundtrack ranges from pushing tracks to eerie background music. The gunplay is fast, frantic and precise. Blowing up enemies or dealing out headshots rarely felt so satisfying. Various, upgradable weapons give the player the right tools for every situation with enough room for a personal playstyle. Go in machine guns blazing, blow up everything with dynamite, grenade launchers and Molotov cocktails or pick one enemy after another from a safe distance. There is also a hopelessly overpowered flamethrower later in the game. Enemy variety and placement is great and there are even two fun boss fights - something most FPS do not get right. The level design is fantastic as well with wide open levels but also tight corridors and claustrophobic crypts. Small puzzles and tons of secrets keep the progression and exploration motivating without becoming another annoying "hidden keys and switches collectathon". Something that should be ironed out in the sequel is the enemy AI which gets stuck in level architecture quite often and could act a bit more aggressively against the player in general. Picking one enemy after another from a distance is often too easy. I honestly can't complain over the short campaign duration of only 4-5 hours when the quality is that high, there is no dull moment and the game is only 10$. A must buy for everyone slightly interested and of the best games of 2022.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: this game is really up there on the most satisfying boomer shooters i've personally played. there's lots of weapons and combat mechanics that really make you feel like a badass and none of them feel weak or out of place. no moment feels better than when you decapitate an enemy with a thrown axe from 100 yards away.the story, levels, graphics and music are great in design and thematics, and puts you right into that intense gritty horror space. there's also lore notes all over the place if that's your kind of thingprobably my favorite detail is when there's locked off areas with loot that rewards you when you use outside the box ways to get to them via parkour or stacking prop items to get over a wall, etc.all in all, game is definitely worth it's price and isn't super easy either!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly good game. Everything from the spritework, the music down to the gunplay and levels is absolutely phenomenal. It's baffling how something like this could have been made by one person. This is up there with the other "greats" of the boomer-shooter reemergence such as Dusk and Amid Evil, well, at least in my books! Gameplay is like someone mixed Brutal Doom with the aesthetics of Blood. Popping Cultist faces with the lever-action or sniper and watching their head give way to a fountain of blood is incredibly satisfying. There's just something about the enemies being sprites instead of 3D models that makes everything feel very crunchy, fast and responsive. 10/10. Hope we get more episodes!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of these retro-style "boomer shooters", and I find they can be very hit or miss; there's a real alchemy to putting together a game that can capture the essence of what made classic 90's FPSes fun while also refining it with the benefits of modern technology. Cultic is that rare game that can thread that needle perfectly, that plays the way you picture those old games playing in your head, and it may have just become my new favorite of this boomer shooter revival.The most obvious influence is Blood, and like Blood, Cultic has an incredible sense of tension in its gameplay (at least on hard, which I played on). Your character is well equipped to take out your enemies, but is at the same time still extremely vulnerable, providing that same mix of methodical caution and desperate, high-octane action that Blood did at its best. However, in Blood that could often feel like the result of primitive design, of filling a room with hitscanners that could mow you down in seconds, where the later levels with fewer hitscan enemies often felt easier, difficulty curve be damned. Cultic achieves its tension without any such cheapness; every enemy in the game telegraphs their attacks, those attacks can all be avoided, but they are still deadly if they hit, so what this leads to is often a more proactive playstyle, which is also encouraged by the phenomenal level design. The levels do a great job at forcing you into fighting different enemies at different ranges in different situations often enough to keep you on your toes, so you never really end up defaulting to a single approach, instead having to strategize, while being given *just* enough ammo for your best weapons to get through. And speaking of weapons, they're excellent as well, nothing too crazy, mostly your standard pistol, shotgun, machine gun etc, but all very effective and satisfying to use, with the weapon upgrade system enhancing weapons without changing their basic use or role in the arsenal.Ultimately, Cultic is exactly what a retro boomer shooter should be; classic design principles filtered through modern design philosophies, giving us the best of both worlds. It's tense, it's satisfying, it's gory, it's gorgeous to look at, and it's a ton of fun. I'm eagerly awaiting the next chapter, but don't misunderstand, it's well worth the asking price even just for chapter 1.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a great little game. Very nice and atmospheric, some good solid gameplay, nice and fast paced but also with some flexibility in how to approach fights if you want. Lots of little hidden secrets like an old school game, and while the art feels kind of like them it's done with much more modern back end methods that make it it all, thanks to good skill on the creators part, feel old school, yet still play smooth and with many of the more modern polishes and conveniences of modern engines.Pros-Gameplay, biggest pro.-Story/world, nice and interesting and largely handled through environmental stuff.-music and auidio, all great to listen to while playing, everything sounds good when fighting, and music is nice and energizing.-Art, very nicely done old pseudo pixel/old 3d style art and environments.-Pacing, nice variety of things and levels to keep it feeling different and fresh as you play,Cons-Length, it's quite short, just 5 or 6 hours even if you spend a lot of time exploring in the main story, a very enjoyable few hours those were mind you, but still short. And this is after the added interlude story update, only 4-5 without it. There is also survival mode that's decent, though definitely not for everybody. Given the price I'd say it's a great game still, but for those short on money wanting something to last awhile... depending on how much you like replaying stuff or working for high scores, this may or may not be for you. Hopefully new updates might add to this, but again even as is I'd say it's worth it.-Performance, a very minor con. It still ran good solid frame rate at all times but I got a higher/mid end system, but cranked my graphics card a lot more than I'd expect, even in menu/paused to go do other things. So it's more taxing than you might think, and have hoped if you have a really simple computer. So double check the requirements, sadly not much in the zone of graphical options or fps capping in case it was trying to render more fps than needed, but oh well. Still did at least play ok for me.Though on that note of the requirements, the current 3gb it says is inaccurate, it's closer to 6gb now with updates, not a huge deal just something they might want to change, and you be aware of if that matters till they do.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, this game is great. The original demo was very good, the re-done second demo was even better, and full release is even better than that plus all the added content of being a full game. It's very well tuned, very fun to play, and incredibly stylish. It works great playing more strategically, but this game really starts to sing when you get some of the (slightly) advanced movement tech down and start dancing around firefights like nothing can touch you. The enemy design is great, every enemy has strengths and counterplays and mix together in interesting ways, and the environments are really atmospheric while providing interesting and fresh arenas for fighting in.Also as a very specific kind of huge nerd, I absolutely love the weapons chosen to be in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Engaging solo project is a rare cream of the crop.Audio design is textually palpable, visuals are akin to the horror classics, story is sparse but involving (with a genuinely disturbing moment), and the gameplay is crunchy and snappy. Unforgettable level design, too. Superb difficulty scaling. Awesome weapons. Great replay value. This game's got it all, folks. Last time I enjoyed a shooter so much was  back in the '90s. is the BEST of the modern boomer shooters and easily the best FPS of the past decade.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: It's all the best parts of all the classics blended into one. Other Modern-Retro-Shooters peril to this absolute masterpiece. This is in my view is the very best one, hands down.It's not Blood, it's not Dusk, it's CULTIC.From a Build Engine fanatic perspective:Cultic seems to be everything Blood wishes it could be, while having some Redneck Rampage esq art. CULTIC (in my opinion) exceeds Ion Fury by a mile as far as compelling gameplay and story. The art is a dark, grimy, unsettling masterpiece that clearly shows you don't need a lot of visual polish to make a good game. The loadout is as crispy as it gets and every weapon feels powerful. Even though it's not Build Engine, it checks every single box, and does so effortlessly. 11/10. We need more. I nominated the ♥♥♥♥ out of this for 'Labor Of Love' & you should too.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the most fun games I've played this year. Solid gameplay. Beautiful visuals and music (honestly, a combination of forward facing sprites and voxel objects make the game a pleasure to look at, especially given the way AAA games look these days. And the music genuinely blew me away, brilliant music). Mega RE4 vibes (yipee!). Absolutely fantastic. The story is fun and interesting. Brilliant use of quiet moments to make things eerier (is that even a word?). Highly recommend playing on Hard mode. Great enemy variety always keeps you on your toes and keeps things interesting. _childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: CULTIC (2022) represents a retro-inspired first-person shooter (FPS) game, developed by the company Jasozz Games and published by the company 3D Realms.++ Exploding bodies, fountains of blood, and severed limbs are the trademarks of this high-paced, gritty spectacle. It features excellent gun gameplay around an upgradable weaponry, and provides a master lesson in sound design enhancing its horror atmosphere; both create an amazing level of immersion. Even Caleb would be proud!++ I consider the overall style of the game a nod to the original Blood (1997). And the different versions of hit scanners are responsible for some serious PTSD attacks I have suffered so far. A beautifully brutal experience on the Extreme difficulty, highly recommended. - Unfortunately, the protagonist lacks any characterization, and the role of a silent hero does not fit his… let’s say agenda. Hell, just give this absolute unit of a man some memorable one-liners and badass cutscenes.A solid first chapter full of high-octane FPS action, which impresses me with its atmosphere and gun gameplay. Quite a remarkable debut for Jasozz Games, and I am already looking forward to the continuation of this saga.Recommended for the risen, willing and able to slaughter through the ranks of an insidious cult.Estimated time for 100% completion: +10 hoursSingleplayer achievements: 22Multiplayer achievements: none
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: BA-BA-BA-BANGERRR! Chunky, crunchy horror shooting. The game could get my heartbeat to a cool 120 by either being in the perfect action-zone, mowing down enemies, or by cutting all music, and leaving me in the dark, fully recontextualizing all it's nasty creatures and horrific environmental storytelling so I fully sh*t my pants. I've found myself thinking "Oh wow, what an amazing final level" several times pre-empting the actual finale, which tells me that CULTIC doesn't save its best for last, its best is the whole g**damn thing.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: While Cultic is an extremely impressive product from a solo developer, it's merely competent in a genre of fantastically designed games.-The level quality runs from basic to bad. There's a surplus of dark levels, sewers, mazes, and drab caves.-The enemies and level design encourage slow plodding play, which is not to my taste. You'd better bust out your magnifying glass because about a fifth of the enemies that are dangerous to you will be shooting you when they're merely the size of your crosshair.Enemies are pretty much either pursuers or hitscan shooters, the same thing you've probably seen a hundred times. The ones that shoot dodgeable projectiles or explosives are far superior, but they don't mesh well with the hit scanners.-The music is very grating to me, and is very strange for the tone of the rest of the game. Again, I want to emphasize it's impressive a solo developer made it all, but it's triumphant tone and weak development is very strange when I'm plodding around in sewers.-The weapons and movement is simply not that interesting. You'll be humping cover dinging enemies with your good weapons from a distance or ambushing them as they stupidly walk around corners with the shotgun for pretty much the whole game. If it had one thing that it innovated in an interesting way, that probably would have tipped the scale for me.
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Sure to appeal to fans of Blood who like the cultist enemies but don't like being ripped to shreds by torrents of gunfire in seconds for the unforgivable sin of entering a roomIn all seriousness, though, this game's a lot of fun, the guns are satisfyingly punchy, and the level designs are solid, so if you're a fan of classic FPS games, give it a shot
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion this is probably the best retro revival FPS game. In all honesty I have not been very impressed with a lot of the early ones that birthed this revival like Dusk, Amid Evil and Ion Fury. They have all ranged from eeehh to good enough.Unlike those this game actually has incredibly satisfying combat with surprisingly multifaceted mechanics. It feels like there's endless ways to experiment with the mechanics and discover something new. I feel like this gives the combat a depth that was missing from a lot of the other neo-boomer shooters. But that's not the only thing that makes this game exceptional the combat just feels viscerally good, it doesn't have that awful stilted feel that games like Dusk and HROT had where shooting enemies feels like shooting at bags of sand, in this game shooting enemies actually feels satisfying. It comes from excellent sound design and gibbing that makes it feel like your shooting things made of actual flesh and blood. Not to mention I love the slow-motion mechanic that activates sometimes when you get a head shot.The level design was also excellent! A lot of the other boomer shooters have sort of monotone levels which is of course directly lifted from the actual shooters from the 90s. But that was born out of limitation and today we have much more freedom to actually have some variety in the level design which this game thankfully does. It's not just a constant bloodbath there are also these great little quiet horror moments that break up the action.Overall I'd say that this is my favourite neo-boomer shooter and I can't wait for Cultic: Chapter Two!
_childDocuments_.name: CULTIC

_childDocuments_.review: Death is only the beginning. Crawl from your grave and gear up to fight your way through the ranks of a mysterious and twisted cult. You, your guns, and your dynamite will have to shoot, slide, blast, duck, dodge, and maybe throw a gib or two to survive in this old-school-inspired shooter.

name: A-Train: All Aboard! Tourism
detailed_description: Step into the Role of a Railroad Company President with A-Train: All Aboard! Tourism Embark on a strategic journey in A-Train: All Aboard! Tourism , a business simulation game where you wield the power of the railroad to shape the future of towns. In the A-Train universe, stations are the lifeblood of communities, serving as catalysts for local development. As the president of a burgeoning railroad company, you have the freedom to design stations and lay out rail lines according to your vision. Will you build a sprawling network of efficient trains, or focus on optimizing the existing lines? Make sure to decorate your town by establishing subsidiaries and advertise your company to increase your brand power. The destiny of the town—and your company—lies in your hands. Tourism-based urban planning Each town boasts a unique array of tourist attractions—from tranquil hot spring districts to awe-inspiring historical castles. It's your task to unlock these destinations' full potential. If a tourist spot is hard to access, it will attract fewer visitors, no matter how incredible the view. Use your transportation network, which can include railroads, bus lines, and even ferries, to craft accessible and enticing vacation experiences. With each new surge of tourists to your attraction, you can be assured that your strategies are working! All aboard! Tourism is a one-way ticket to urban planning! Whether you envision a thriving metropolis, a peaceful town nestled next to natural wonders, or a bustling hub with a top-tier transportation network, the canvas is yours to paint. A unique story of your own, told with the help of your friends and associates. Now, it's time to seize this opportunity to dive into the world of tourism planning and take the first steps toward constructing your ideal city!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the Nintendo Switch version for 200 hours and getting used to slow, laggy menus and overall poor performance, starting to play the game again on my PC was extremely enjoyable. But you have to keep an eye on the recommended requirements, they are high for a game with relatively simple graphics.The only problem I have found is that the controls are not perfect. The main control is still the joystick, with the mouse+keyboard being a bit of an improvisation. For those who are used to PC games of this style, mouse+kb will seem pretty bad at first. It took me 2 hours to adapt and now I feel that playing with mouse+kb is the best way by far, but the gameplay could be much better if the game was totally designed for these devices. I foresee some players, for example, not understanding how to build a station because you have to use WASD for it to appear on the map, or having a hard time laying down tracks... There is, as yet, no option to configure the keys.The game itself is an extremely detailed sim, where you manage a Japanese train company that partners with the government to achieve goals related to urbanization of areas. The business management part is quite complex and encompasses things like payments of different taxes, buying and selling land, trades, subsidiaries, dividend payments, stock investments, etc. The urban planning part is focused on railroads, which make the city grow in an indirect way. Instead of building the city like a god (Sim City, Cities Skylines, etc), you build the infrastructure that will mobilize passengers and cargo and this will indirectly affect the growth of the city. It is a different and very interesting formula.Although the game is quite complex and gives people room to sink for dozens of hours carefully managing timetables of your trains, building complex infrastructure, etc, the scenarios are relatively easy (except on the "expert" difficulty) and it is perfectly possible to play more casually without worrying too much about micromanagement, advanced strategies or complex train lines, and still have a good time because the game is extremely addictive and fun.Note: It is highly recommended to play both tutorials first and follow exaclty what the characters suggest. Several important game functions will be blocked during the tutorial, including basic things like changing game speed, pausing simulation, changing shadow/texture quality, advanced options, etc. It is only after the tutorials, which can last for several hours, that the game will open up to its full potential. You can start directly in the third scenario if you want to access everything right away, however, which is not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a new entry in the series coming to PC, and overall it's my favorite. I already put over 100 hours into the Switch version, but here I am sitting at almost 90 hours on Steam, just over a week after release. It's fundamentally an evolution of A-Train PC Classic that is better in most ways. For those not already familiar, A-Train is a series all about Transport Management and Urban Development. It sits somewhere inbetween Transport Tycoon, Industry Giant and city builders like Cities Skylines and offers a rather unique take on these genres. Like TTD, your main activity is building railways and roads and manage various vehicles ferrying things around on them. Unlike TTD, it generally operates on a "higher" level of management. Instead of managing switches, you manage schedules, and the production chains are much simpler (there are only 6 types of goods, and none of their chains go deeper than 2 steps). It also has a bigger focus on the business side of things, even including aspects like paying taxes, stock trading, government subsidies, the option of becoming a publicly traded company yourself, and you'll be thinking a lot about taking out loans to make good investments and increasing your net assets (to further increase your loan limit and repeat the process). It also features a full calendar cycle with changing seasons, times of day and even holidays, which will all affect ridership in various ways.The main drive for all this transportation are the urban development aspects. Ridership at stations will drive growth, which will lead to various kinds of buildings being built near them. The game features a concept of zoning, which will influence what kinds of buildings can be built where and how well they can operate, as well as synergies between different buildings. The player can also build almost any kind of building in the game himself, which ultimately is the biggest way of making a profit. With enough effort, this can also steer the development process in certain ways and even lead to rezoning of districts. Real estate is another important aspect in all of this, since all land has to be bought to construct on it, so planning developments and buying land ahead of time before its value goes through the roof is essential.The result is a very neat machine of synergies that can be influenced by the player to lead to emergent development of cities in a relatively hands-off way, which I haven't seen to this extent in other games. Another important aspect is that, unless you want it to, A-Train is mission-based and not a sandbox game. And trust me, especially on the higher difficulties, these missions are hard! They are also accompanied by a cast of characters that interact with the player through VN-like dialogue sequences, and each scenario has optional slice of life storylines popping up every now and then. All text can be skipped quickly, so it should not be a big bother for people who don't care, but it adds a lot of character to everything.Now, lets get to the specifics of this version.There are lots more little things, but I think that covers the main points. In general it just feels more polished and feature-rich than PC Classic to me (aside from some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about the UI and controls, which were also not perfect in PC Classic). If you're a fan of the series and can afford it, you'll most likely love this one as well. If you are new but are interested, it's not a bad choice either, but PC Classic is cheaper and also a good entry point, while arguably inferior in many ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Me: This looks like an  cute and easygoing train business sim. Sure, I'll give it a shot.This game: I hope you like earnings reports, charts, taxes, stock trading, speculative land purchasing, trade contracts, employee morale, company reputation, property deterioration, subsidiary purchasing, and city management elements to go with your trains.Me: *plays for many hours straight, until 4 am on a weekday* Oops. Funny anecdotes aside, I'm seriously liking this game way more than I ever could have realistically expected. The AAA price tag can certainly be daunting, even more so if you think this is just going to be an easygoing, casual, business sim. It's not though. It's actually thoroughly convoluted (and underexplained, despite me just getting around to finishing up the tutorial levels some 18 hours in).I haven't even gotten into the morale, reputation, and deterioration aspects of the game yet, because the tutorials are locked into easy mode, where those things are turned off (or rather, locked at perfect condition).The real downsides to this game is that it's missing some  quality of life features (like being able to copy the route of buses and trucks, but easily shift which parking spaces are assigned to them, rather than having to go through menus on each vehicle). For a few vehicles that's fine, but when you have literally dozens of vehicles to manage, it's a real pain. The game's actually a port form Switch, so it's not surprising that it has such a menu-heavy structure, but it that doesn't really make the menus structure any better, it just tells you why it's not good. The controls can also be a little finicky as well, but they're mostly fine.Otherwise there's the fact that it will beat you over the head with  more complexity than you would expect by just looking at the store page, so if you don't want that, that could be. Then there's also the fact that the graphics (as you can see on the store page) aren't good. Still, this game is way more fun to me than it had any right to be. I didn't actually go in with high expectations, just sort of a "that looks cute". My expectations were totally blown out of the water.

_childDocuments_.review: Like others I have played this originally on Switch.I was unsure if I was going to get the PC version but my love of the franchise got the better of me.The graphics have had an upgrade from the switch version and are activated within the options menu, like the Switch version all the features are introduced to you through the two tutorials I strongly suggest playing through those first before you move on to other scenarios or creating your own. The tutorials do hold your hand quite a bit but they also explain the game mechanics quite well as long as you read all the help as its displayed, A-train has always had a hard learning curve as it doesn't quite work like a western transport sim or a western city builder but something else entirely.Now for me with this version of the A-train franchise its all about the scenario creating and creating Vehicles (Trains/Busses) you can create your own designs.Now scenario creating you have a lot of options and can even create your own stories to go with them. again it does take some getting used to as the controls and menu system is a bit cumbersome.Overall this is a good entry into the A-train franchise you just need to have the patience and give it time to learn the controls and the game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAY BASICSFirst and foremost, this game is a heavily Japanese-centric transportation tycoon. The forte of the game is its economy management. The game provides you with extensive financial numbers, and allows you to buy stocks and subsidiaries to supplant your transportation-related income. Subsidiaries are simply commercial, residential, industrial and recreational establishments the player can either build or buy to generate income. Players also have the option to buy and sell land plots. Finally, players can build decorative and region enhancing buildings, like parks, shrines, temples, and sports facilities. Maps are divided into cities, towns and villages. Development is static until a transit line is built, upon which the region around the areas served by the stations will start to develop rapidly, unless you happen to own the land around it. If you do not build them yourself, the game will randomly build assorted buildings from all the above categories, around the areas served.On the subject of transportation and vehicles, players can develop and buy a variety of generic trains and trucks. Most interesting are time tables - which relatively few games of the genre have - that allow players to meticulously control vehicle arrival and departure arrival times at specific stations or stops. Players can also build roads and highways. Combined with the above, this game could double for a rather simple but visually aesthetically pleasing city builder, at least a Japanese centric one.There are both a day and night and a seasonal cycle in the game. Passenger traffic will fluctuate depending on the time of the day, the day of the week, and even the season or specific holidays of the year. Similar fluctuations are seen for cargo resources depending on season. Adapting your vehicles and lines to operate the most efficiently according to these different time-related events is one of the most enticing aspects of the game, and is one that no other transportation-related game can compete with.Airports and Shinkansen tracks can be built to attract more tourists to the region, though the player has no control over the lines that operate out of such establishments.GAMEPLAY MODESWhile there is not a proper campaign, there are a number of different available scenarios that together can be thought as one. Unlike your average transportation-related game, scenarios/campaign are well designed, entertaining, and have different difficulty choices that can make them either a walk in the park or very hard to complete.There is a map and scenario editor that can be used if a sandbox experience is desired. The map editor will generate a random map based on some parameters, and players can then specify victory conditions. Unfortunately, no height map importing, and the terraforming tools themselves are relatively clunky to use.On either official or player made scenarios, once the game is "won", players can keep playing indefinitely. On the other hand, they can lose if they go bankrupt, which is easy to do if you do not watch your financial statements and spending.MAJOR GAMEPLAY ISSUESThere are some glaring issues, however. The UI leaves a lot to be desired, even when its Nintendo Switch origins are taken into consideration. For example, there is no single bulldoze button - you have to go to one of the many submenus and then either use the demolish tool in such submenu or locate a specific subsidiary or station, and demolish it. Many options that should come in the game by default are hidden as "advanced options" that have to be toggled on. Setting up lines can be quite a tricky and time-consuming task, especially for road-based vehicles. Most importantly, however, is the absence of train signalling. This can easily result in train blockages in tracks that share multiple lines, unless you either are comfortable micromanaging timetables, and/or use specific or avoid track setups to prevent this. Almost unforgiveable, especially considering this is a game focused on train operation.Other things of note is no proper terraforming (and even in the map editor the tools were nothing to write about) and building underground tunnels and stations is a major pain in the back.GRAPHICS and ARTWORKClean, simple and cute though not cutting edge. The game is isometrical 3D, remininscent and not much different from games such as OpenTTD or Simcity 3000 or 4. While it has that retro feel, and the game series itself is very old - dating from the 1980s - I do believe it would benefit from an eventual conversion to full 3D such as Transport Fever, or a simplified but still 3D version like in Railway Empire.Architecture and vehicles are, of course, your typical stereotypical generic Japanese building. The official scenarios have characters, drawn anime-style, fit well with the graphical style of the game, and add a further charm to the game.MUSIC AND SOUND EFFECTSThere is a wide range of sound tracks that fit well with the gameplay and the different seasons. Personally I think it has one of the best and most relaxing soundtracks of any related sandbox-related games.The game is, however, very bland on the sound effect department, with even train sound effects such as horns and Japanese train crossings lacking. At least station melodies - something very typical of Japanese stations - are included, but the lack of modding support precludes setting up additional or different sound effects or melodies.MODDABILITYUnfortunately, the game does not have mods. nor, AFAIK no official support for them, which is a real shame, as it would benefit from the inclusion of more buildings and vehicles.PERFORMANCEGiven the relatively simple graphics, this game is very demanding on the PC. There are some performance issues in highly developed maps that are present even in high-end computers. In particular, fast-forwarding becomes very laggy at times on such maps. On regions with extremely large economies (not required for your average playthrough, but required for some of the game achievements) the game may often crash, especially on fast-forward mode.VALUEAs much as I love the game, I do believe the current non-discounted price is too steep given the current problems and restrictions of the game. I would wait for a sale.SUMMARYA very deep and entertaining game that is held back by horrendous UI and the lack of signalling, and its steep price. Highly recommended if you are into micromanaging things in general, and/or want a highly specialized business tycoon focusing on Japan. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a real fan of the first 2 A-Trains some 20 years ago.  But every new version they come up with gets worse and worse.  This Tourism one is the worst.First off, the camera is too difficult and cumbersome to move around. They have 2 different camera views. One view helps you see more of the map, but you are limited as to what you can do. The other view that allows you to do things is too narrow. It was built for a controller, not a computer and mouse, which is what I have. Way too cumbersome to look around and move around.Also, when you lay down track, the track laying menu remains open and takes up 1/3 of the screen. Again, it was built for a controller, not a mouse. So you run out of room when you try laying down track. You then try to grab the map with your mouse to move the map so you can continue laying down track, but when you grab the map, it thinks you want to lay down track there, so it draws this long windy track where you did not want it to go; you're just trying to move the map.Also, in the very first tutorial, it asks you to connect to the next town by laying down track through a specific border tile. But there is a road in that tile already. And you can't buy that tile, so you can't remove that road. How can you build a track there? You can't, but you are expected to do that.Also, the dialogue with all this characters is way too off topic. You are trying to find your instructions in that dialogue, but they bombard you will endless chatter over mundane things like how bad the weather is or how excited they are to have you as their president. You have to click through 7 or 8 off-topic comments just to find the next instruction. But you end up clicking past your instruction which is buried somewhere in those mindless comments they make. So you have to sit there and read through all that nonsense chatter just so you don't miss your next instruction. It's torture!The menus are poorly organized. You have to search and search to find what you are looking for, because the font is so huge that they can't list very much on one page, because it was built for a console not a computer. There should be a short demo version of every single game available, so we can try it for a few minutes before buying it. Just 1 hour of gameplay would avoid many poor choices.  5 hours of gameplay was enough for me to give up on it and request a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not too knowledgeable about the venerable A-train franchise but I'm happy to say that this entry has nearly everything I look for in a transport tycoon style game. My biggest gripe is that the controls are a little finicky on PC since it's a port of a console game but there are options to make this smoother.As a fan of games like OpenTTD I was thrown a bit when I saw there weren't signalling options but you do quickly get used to time-tabling your trains appropriately.  This has been patched, huzzah!Most importantly, A-train all aboard tourism feels like an actual GAME with a challenge. You're not just making the pretty city of your dreams, you're actively building an economically viable business that helps the local cities expand. Some of the scenarios are tough and really make you use the game's systems to their fullest. That being said, when you want to unwind, it's pleasant to use the free-camera to ride with along your train network and take in the gorgeous scenery. All in all I'm really happy this was brought to PC, it has gorgeous art, music, and the characters are well written and funny - it's just a treat all around.The threat of taxes in A-train is scarier than any horror game I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, on sale, for enthusiasts who want to try something different from OpenTTD/Transport Fever.A little gem in the train tycoon field. The UI and the Timetable systems are a bit hard to get used to, but nothing insurmontable. First thing to do is to head to options and activate all advanced options and fine tune additional ones to your liking.Scenarios are interesting, the cities grow in an interesting manner, and the tycoon side is really developped (balance sheets, public offering, city zoning, subsidiaries...). The fast forward is also really usefull and efficient, making days and years pass by quickly so you can build up a bit of capital for your next build.Compared to other train tycoons/builders, I really liked the maps, the connections with bordering cities, and the way time is handled: day by day, with rush hours, nights, seasons, holidays. The buildings are also very varied, and with a very Japaneese style of build, resulting in an interesting scenery and very "organic" cities (as much as a grid based game allows). It probably is the most immersive train tycoon game I've played so far, and I really appreciated my time with it.On the other hand, the UI is terrible (designed for consoles) and lacks many information that could be useful, to keep it simple, probably. Because of this, creating timetables is a pain. Also, goods transportation is unsatisfactory most of the time.Overall, this could be a superb transport tycoon game, but it is let down by it's interface.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t often review things, but there’s a lot worth saying here.I’d like to qualify this review with the fact I’ve put hundreds of hours into Cities Skylines, OpenTTD, Cities in Motion 1/2, Transport Fever 1/2, Train Fever, Railway Empire, and Transport Tycoon. They don’t really hold a candle to this in a number of different ways.First, though, to address the issues many people  have raised in the reviews and other discussion.Price:The price is on the high side. Is it worth it? I’d say so. If you like this type of game, there’s a lot here, and more if you also like scenario building.Graphics:Don’t let the cute graphics fool you. This is about as hardcore as transport management games get. It occasionally looks great as your city grows too.Controls/UI:DON’T play with a mouse and keyboard. You’ll thank me later. This is a direct port of a Switch game, and it shows. But play with a controller, and it’s not the worst UI or control scheme.Learning Curve/Tutorials:This is a contentious one. The tutorials aren’t terrible, but they do throw a lot at you in one go, and they don’t always make you do the thing you just learned, so it’s easy to miss or forget things. I think a bit more handholding or guided play as you handle things like timetabling or goods production. I had to play both the tutorial levels twice to pick up on things I’d missed, and there’s still gaps.On the other hand, the tutorial introduces features, buttons, capabilities etc. VERY slowly. And normally this would be great, but it makes the game seem super shallow at first glance (e.g. even some essential track building features don’t appear til near the end of the first tutorial). More experienced transport management players will likely scoff at the early phases.Signalling/Timetabling:This might be hard for some to swallow, but this game relies on in-cab signalling and basic block signalling, not traffic-light style signalling you’ll see in other games. In the majority of games we use signals a crutch.This way is actually MORE realistic than most other games of this type, because having a train stopped anywhere but a depot is not efficient. And this game is all about efficiency. There’s a lot of math involved, but there’s nothing more satisfying than nailing it, zooming out, and seeing a symphony of transport hum along in front of you as you rake in the cash.You need to timetable your entire fleet and network to maximise efficiency, and this is one of the hardest (and most satisfying parts of the game).This or A-Train PC Classic?:You can’t go wrong with either, but I’d avoid A-Train 9 v4.0, especially the western release. Don’t let the graphics or higher number fool you, it’s an inferior game in most respects, and is plagued with game-breaking bugs.All Aboard! Tourism feels like an expansion of A-Train PC Classic, a lot like those themed expansions to the likes of Roller Coaster Tycoon. It adds a few extra features, modernises some of the graphics, but is largely the same game. If you prefer mouse and keyboard, PC Classic is likely the one for you, but I’d give this a fair chance - you could always get your money back.The A-Train series is way more deep and complex than the majority of its competitors, and it’s only the lack of western coverage that really causes it to have limited exposure.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game. It is an urban development simulator focused on a private company developing railroads, resource sales, and building subsidiaries. This game has a decent learning curve where the player needs to figure out what all the inputs are and what they do. Once you learn those inputs, the game provides very deep game play. Fortunately the developer has provided two tutorial levels and lots of supporting documentation. In addition, the difficulty level ramps appropriately.This game's roots go back to the 80's. The way it plays feels very old. Games like this one are not really made anymore. This game is extremely detail oriented and can be unforgiving if you have not internalized the structure. Drama from this game will often come from whether a station or building should be placed in one spot, or one square over. The gameplay is challenging and much more compelling than that may sound. All of the included scenarios are good and provide good replay value. There are many player-created scenarios, and a few rival the factory ones in quality. The scenario creation tool is pretty robust, and this can add many more hours of game play for those who finish the scenarios and want more. This is a Japanese game, popular in Japan, and most of the player base is in Japan. You will find most player-made scenarios are in Japanese. They are playable and winnable in the steam version, but the story will not be able to be translated. The various characters in the game discuss urban planning concepts in reasonable depth for a PC game. The characters are memorable, well-written, often fun, and add a nice flavor to the game. This game has a sunnier outlook on public transit than exists in the United States. If you work on urban planing in the USA, playing this game will be cathartic and reaffirming.  I have found this game very satisfying, and I have purchased it for both PC and the Switch. The Switch version has a better interface, but the PC version is much, much faster. Other reviewers have cited the high hardware requirements. This game has a RAM bus bottleneck. If you're speccing a system for this game, you will need very fast RAM (16GB recommended), a high clock CPU, and a midlevel GPU, in that order.This game will run well on the M1 Max in Crossover. I have put hundreds of hours into this game, and feel it is well worth the price. If you've played Civ 5 & 6, and wished the game play was deeper; or you're looking for the game SimCity 2000 aspired to be; or you're an urban planning professional looking to have some more fun than your workday usually allows: this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mix of train simulator and city building. At first it may appear that this is a train sim title but it's only the backdrop for basically being "JR" in that you are a transportation company but you are really about putting your finger in as many pies as possible to accumulate mass amount of wealth, taking your company on the stock market if you want to. This is a pretty educational game to learn or expand your knowledge of economics. This is game is also pretty cool if you want to recreate a specific area of Japan using the map editor. You can add dialogue that triggers under certain conditions and it would be cool to have scripts modify the game on the fly but the game doesn't go that far. If you like Japanese aesthetics in your skyline/sim city you should check out this game. This is your chance to visit Japan during travel lockdowns. The game gradually introduces more complex systems as you complete the first 2 tutorial maps. A lot of the things you might think "I wish I could do this" that are not introduced in the first 2 scenarios are actually advanced options. Advanced options includes more complex customization as well as "must haves" like the ability to rename your bus and create color coded trade routes. When you have 40 buses that all have the same name based on their model number you will want to use this for sure. Patience is required to learn this game, much like paradox titles. You will restart a lot as you make mistakes that range from jamming railways or roads by poor planning or putting stations in bad areas or wasting a ton of money in R&D without the backup funds to actually do your project. _childDocuments_.review: The basic idea of a city builder / transport tycoon type game is there - but it does feel like it has a almost vertical learning curve when it comes to figuring out the mechanics of this specific game. _childDocuments_.review: It's much better than the switch version, the performance is pretty good and there are options for resizing the UI. The mouse controls are generally good, I just wish I had some more keyboard shortcuts. This game is centered around setting up routes from the borders of the map ( neighboring towns ) to various tourist sites in the city.  Generally the goals of the scenarios is to put yourself in the black and hit some tourism target.One thing to note, is that there is a variety of ways to make money / profit other than just moving people and things around. People can buy tickets for your commuter trains. You can sell goods in your warehouse to neighboring towns. You can buy goods from local producers/your own business/or outside towns. Building materials can be sold to internal towns to fund city development. You can buy and sell land. You can buy and sell stocks. You can setup subsidiary businesses like shopping malls/ department stores etc. You can sell those business and the land they sit on. You can get government subsidies for doing the above.  The ways you lose money are in the fairly obvious things. Buying high and selling low, constantly redeveloping a plot of land, paying taxes, having trains and not using them.This is a train business simulation game. You can micro-manage the trains and bus routes to make more profit, but it's not totally necessary. The management/scheduling for trains/buses is pretty hellish and not fun. I think I'll need some proper spreadsheets to visualize the schedulliing because it's pretty difficult in game. I've been able to get by doing some basic stuff at the cost of inefficiency in my land / resource usage.Anyway, the game is kind of expensive at $60 for anyone that's not into a business spreadsheet simulator, but I generally learned a lot from this game and I've bought it at full price twice...

_childDocuments_.review: I started  as an absolute A-Train beginner. After 100 hours, I can safely say that this is one of the best railroad company and city development simulations that I have ever played.The depth of the simulation, the attention to detail, the wonderfully crafted scenarios, a manageable learning curve, the comforting old-school city builder graphics, the rewarding train rides through the city, the cute little stories that are told throughout the game, the engaging and challenging gameplay that requires you to constantly weigh your options, figure out the best angle of attack, and optimize your network, ... I could go on and on.It's fair to say that I've become a fan of the franchise.My advice:Get it if you are looking for a compelling business and city development simulation, that also has trains. If you are looking for a model train and railroad sandbox game, this is not it.Let me preface this review by saying that I'm new to this franchise. But I'm not new to this genre, I love OpenTTD.I was interested in A-Train for the last couple of years. I tried A-Train 8, A-Train 9, and A-Train PC Classic. They always had a steep learning curve. But there was never enough motivation to push through that rough start for me. I probably played each of them for 4-5 hours and gave up.With  it is different. From the start you get the feeling that you are doing something useful. And as you are learning the different elements of the game, you start to explore other options for yourself. It's then easy to find interesting things to do in each scenario on your own, with the knowledge that you have acquired.With its simplified visuals, the different orthogonal views, and all the lovely details in the colorful cities and surroundings, to me this is one of the best looking A-Train games! This is one of the key points for me: You build like in an old-school city builder, and you have the option to change the camera and explore the city freely, if you like.I'm looking forward to playing this game for many many hours.
_childDocuments_.name: A-Train: All Aboard! Tourism

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very different type of game if you're comparing it to other city builders like Sim City or Skylines. It's more story  objective based and the end goal isn't just to make as much money as possible. There's a visual novel aspect injected into the game. It has a learning curve and requires a bit of time to learn how to play, but it's rewarding when you succeed. I recommend playing on Easy difficulty at first.Pros: The character art and writing is super cute and the story-lines are great. I really like what they've done with mixing genres in this title. There are so many features, the game is very deep and well thought-out.Cons: I wish the main title screen had an options section though. You currently have to start a game to change the sound and video game options. Overall, this is a good game that I can safely recommend. If you like sim games and also cute anime characters you should give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: The 205 series was designed in 1982 as a cheap-to-produce train that could complement the 201 series sets which were considered to be expensive to produce due to the latter's thyristor chopper-controlled traction systems. The first set entered service on the Yamanote Line on 1985, and has remained a staple of the JR fleet network ever since. It was originally built with the low-end resistor-controlled traction systems, as they were cheaper to produce than the typical thyristor chopper-controlled motors or something similar to that, but this was somewhat dated technology due to the advent of the high-end variable frequency drive which had just started being used around this time. It uses a traditional design with an unpainted stainless steel body very much like most trains of the period. Each set has a different color scheme to indicate which area the sets serve.The 205 series is currently used on both JR East and JR West lines, and the 205–0 series will be finally ending operation in JR East on 2020. Filling their retirement from JR, 524 205–0 series vehicles have been shipped to Jakarta, Indonesia from 2013 to 2020 to continue their operation overseas replacing aging commuter trains and mass improvement of public transportation in Greater Jakarta by train, while there are still 205–0 series operational in JR West lines.It was manufactured from 1984 to 1991 and initially built 10-car trainsets for test-run conducted in 1984 for JNR Yamanote Line. It was manufactured by Tokyu Car Corporation, Hitachi for technical components, Nippon Sharyo, Kinki Sharyo, and Kawasaki Heavy Industries. The basic structure is similar to that of the subsequently manufactured vehicles like the 201 series & the 203 series, but the difference is that the window shape is a two-pane window panels with the upper stage descending and the lower stage rising. All four manufacturers were introduced to the Yamanote line in March 1985, and in 1991, like the other trains, the Saha 204-0 was introduced as a 6-door intermediate carriage for Yamanote Line to be assigned as new Car No. 10 to be coupled and form 11-car Yamanote Line trainsets from December 1991.In 2005, the Saha 204 intermediate carriages, were also transferred to the Saikyo line upon retirement from Yamanote Line, and also some of the existing Yamanote Line 205 series were transferred to the Keiyo line to continue their train operation until they ended on 2011. The trip number indicator of each leading car was initially introduced as a traditional roller-binding display as commonly used by other JNR rolling stocks, but in 1985, it was newly installed for the first time with the LCD type trip number indicator display and also later replaced along with the 0-subseries mass-produced vehicles.JR East uses cars with six doors on each side to cope with rush hour congestion. The cars have folding seats to increase the number of standing spaces, increasing capacity in the morning when the busiest time is reached. The seats can be locked automatically by the train driver. The time when seats are available varies depending on the line section. On the Yamanote Line, Saikyo Line, and Rinkai Line, they are unlocked at 10:00. On the Yokohama Line the seats are unlocked at 9:00. In the same line area, the conductor unlocks at the same time. When the lock is released, a lamp installed at the end of the seat is turned on, and passengers can manually pull the seats out to use them (this is a manual type for safety). As for storage, it is automatically stored (using springs and gas dampers) at the push of a button after entering the depot without passengers. There is a sticker inside the car to indicate that you cannot use your seat until the cancellation time. Therefore, depending on the train, there were those that could be used near the unloading station and those that had seats that passengers did not pull out. Also, to prevent tampering, the seat once pulled out by the passenger, is locked and cannot be manually stored.The body uses a panel structure developed by Kinki Vehicle to reduce costs and improve performance. This is a panel made of a reinforcing material called dimple board.The specifications were reviewed, and the height of each entrance was increased from 1,800 mm (71 in) to 1,850 mm (73 in), one vertical window was placed between the doors, and the side windows were increased from the vertical dimension of 880 mm (35 in) to 1,050 mm (41 in). This is also for the purpose of improving the physique of modern people and reducing the feeling of pressure in the car during rush hours. In addition to the panel-type structure, the gas damper-type balancer mechanism unit-type descending window to the side window and the customer door using Honeycomb structure have been a motivation to incorporate the technologies unique to Kinki Sharyo vehicles.Unlike the conventional conical laminated rubber type, the bogie uses the roll rubber type axle box support type TR241B adopted in 651 series. In addition, the towing device has been changed from the link type to the Z link type (this cart system is only in the 900s and 0s).Due to the structure of the seat, the heating device cannot be installed under the seat as in the past, so floor heating, which is rarely used in railway cars, is adopted. In addition, a small sheathed heater is installed under the seat as before. This is an ancillary, the heater only works when the seat is occupied.The air conditioner uses the AU717 type (50,000 kcal/h・58.0 kW), which has a capacity of about 20% compared to the conventional model because the door opening is large. The control method is an inverter method that uses 600 V DC as the power source (conventionally, an operation rate control method that uses a three-phase AC source. The 100 series will be described later). On the ceiling, auxiliary blowers (line delia) are added from 4 to 6, and circulator is installed at the top of each door (12 places).In the car, the number of grab handles has been significantly increased from 98 (4 door intermediate car before expansion) to 150, and 5 stanchion poles with a protector wound in the central passageway. The installed position is not in the center of the former entrance plaza, but in front (between) of the storage seats. It was installed because the seats were retractable and there was no place to grab near the door. Since there are six doors in the car, the number of seats is 30, which is less than the number of ordinary 4-door vehicles (54 seats). However, the seat width for one person has been expanded to 450 mm (18 in). In addition, due to the peculiarity of the auxiliary seat that cannot be used due to the above time period, the 205 series does not have a priority seat. On the other hand, it is compatible with barrier-free by installing wheelchair space here by utilizing the end of the vehicle.The emergency door opener of each door is installed on the top of the door covered with glass, and the 0.900 series says "How to use, you can open the door by pulling the handle in this glass toward you" It is written as ".", but since the 100s are in the same style as 209 series, "The door can be opened by hand by pulling the handle inside." Has been done.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong. Artdink had a good idea with the moe anime npcs and tutors. I like that. It's a slimmer A-train, so it's easier to approach than previous A-train games. I like that too!I really want to like this game. I really do. The majority of us who played it have. But the UI is cluttered and train pathfinding is not easy to understand or solve either without a developed signal system. Big red flags for me. I played almost 3000 hours between OpenTTD, Train Fever, and Transport Fever 1 & 2, so I know when a game has proper rail signaling. In All About Tourism, if you remove a train, it doesn't keep its original route, immediately randomizing it for some unholy awful reason. As a result, I spent at least 3 hours of the last five hours playing trying to salvage train route that were constantly stopped by another. I won't tell you not to play this game. I hope you had a better time than me. I was looking for a game that was able to fill that anime, city builder, and rail simulator niche. It fills that, but what costs? Cluttery UI? Odd game mechanics? No proper signaling. Even the camera is unfriendly. Sorry Artdink, gotta ask for my money back on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game, and pretty much have only one major complaint; the bus routing. To be blunt, it sucks. Forming loop lines but not amazing. However, trying to make point-to-point lines with multiple stops along the way is maddening. The route pathfinding once you have your stops selected can be problematic (and sometimes just completely broken, AVOID the "Basic Bus Stop" and "Basic B St 2" for this reason, as I have had the most issues when using them). The game also sometimes orders your selected stops in weird ways, occasionally outright ignoring the order in which you selected them. Placing new stops for a new line along will also sometimes insert those stops into the routes of other already existing and operating bus lines if they are along the routes of those lines. Other than and perhaps even in spite of that, this game is incredible. It has charm out the wazoo, but is also a fully-featured transportation  management game. Compared to, for example Transport Fever 2, it also has a much more robust and capable system for how your cities grow, not only upwards but also outwards. As you play through a scenario, your city will gradually spread its paved roots outwards and sprout its buildings further and further upwards, so long as you provide it with a healthy economy and robust transportation network for its citizens. To briefly summarise; This game is a fun blend of the less tedious aspects of Cities: Skylines and Transport Fever 2, cast into a surprisingly in-depth business management mold, with a fresh coat of Japanese charm interlaced into the very identity of the game. The game is tile-based, so setting up rail lines is simpler and more approachable than in Transport Fever 2, and the same applies to roads. Your city will also grow itself according to the zoning of each district instead of needing manual expansion as in Cities: Skylines. However, it makes up for a "lack of depth" in these areas with a fully-featured business management platform from which you operate the aforementioned transportation and city management features.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play SimCity 3000 as well as the next installment back when I was younger and none of the city builder games I've tried ever since really managed to capture the same essence or imagination than those two games which is why I still play SC after all those years from time to time. Well I think my search for the next big thing is now over, because even though this game is not a city-builder in the strictest sense of the word, it evokes the same feelings as SC. It's not really surprising as SimCity was heavily inspired by A-Train, with Maxis even having edited the series in the West. It feels nice turning small villages into megacities, albeit indirectly (you don't zone neighborhoods in this game) and taking in the sights when boarding the train. I had some issues with signaling but nothing you can't fix with some short term planning (i.e. not placing tracks at random). The UI also took some time to adapt to, but since I'm not an adderall-riddled game "journalist" I took my time and learned how to navigate it efficiently and now I don't have any issues anymore.Game may be pricey when there's no sale (depending on who you ask) but there's a lot of content in this game. I don't regret my purchase. Sucks about the DLC though looks like it won't be available outside of Japan.

_childDocuments_.review:
All aboard! Tourism is a one-way ticket to urban planning. A-Train, the classic urban development simulation game that allows you to create the city of your dreams, is now available on the Nintendo Switch. Become the president of your very own railroad company, laying tracks and running your trains as you see fit. However, you will be responsible for more than the railroad. You'll also be tasked with managing subsidiaries, playing the stock market, and participating in urban planning, in order to develop and expand your town.

This latest installment in the A-Train series introduces the element of tourism to the urban planning formula, and focuses on building up towns into bustling tourism capitals. Providing realistic business management simulations of financing, investing, and more, as well as a wide variety of customizable options for all your vehicles, A-Train: All Aboard! Tourism is packed full of features for you to explore. But don't be overwhelmed—players old and new alike will be able to jump right into the series thanks to the fun and practical tutorials provided in the early stages.

So why not hop aboard the A-Train with your trusted team of advisors, and start crafting a bright future for your town?

name: Capcom Fighting Collection
detailed_description: Ten of Capcom's most popular arcade games in one epic collection! A wide variety of titles are included from iconic series such as Street Fighter and Darkstalkers, Cyberbots, and the first home console port of Red Earth! And of course, all titles support online play! This is the perfect collection for both arcade veterans who remember the titles, and those who want to get into them for the first time! ■ Fully-featured online modes Players can aim to top the global leaderboards in ranked matches, or create a lobby with friends for casual games or just spectate some exciting matches. Supported with a robust Rollback netcode which offers a stable and smooth online experience. ■ First-timers welcome Beginner-friendly features such as training mode and one-button special move control options are included. You can also save and load any time for a quick do-over! ■ Additional content: The Museum This archive features more than 500 illustrations and development materials across the 10 included titles. It also includes concept art that has never been shown to the public before, and behind-the-scenes materials that give a glimpse into the development process. Not only that, you can listen to over 400 music tracks recorded from the arcade versions of each title.　 Included game titles (Japanese and English versions selectable for most titles *1) Darkstalkers: The Night Warriors Night Warriors: Darkstalkers’ Revenge Vampire Savior: The Lord of Vampire Vampire Hunter 2: Darkstalkers’ Revenge Vampire Savior 2: The Lord of Vampire Hyper Street Fighter II: The Anniversary Edition Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo Super Gem Fighter Mini Mix Cyberbots: Full Metal Madness Red Earth (*1 Vampire Hunter 2: Darkstalkers’ Revenge and Vampire Savior 2: The Lord of Vampire are Japanese versions only)

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get this out of the way. Yes, all of the games in this collection are easily playable through Fightcade. But let's be honest, a lot of people aren’t prepared to set up Fightcade because… oh no, you might have to download an exe file, open it, and click the OK button twice, and… oh, heaven forbid… download a ROM file that you yourself didn’t rip! A SWAT team will definitely kick your door in and raid your home once they find out you’ve done that!Here’s the thing though, Fightcade is honestly only good if you are looking to play King of Fighters, JoJo: Heritage for the Future, or Third Strike. Good luck on anything else. The main game I got this collection for was Vampire Savior (Darkstalkers 3), and can you guess how many people were playing it on Fightcade only a few weeks ago when I last checked?Six people. That’s six people across the entire world. So surely whatever playerbase is playing this official rerelease of all these classic fighting games would be better than that right?Apparently not because this game’s all-time player peak was a whopping 828 players. Currently, not even 48 hours after release, the playerbase is hovering at around 400 players. Combine that with the fact that this collection has 10 games in it, no cross-platform support, and player-selected region lockout, and you have a very fragmented playerbase, and that only accounts for people that are actually trying to play this online.It’s often said that fighting games lose a lot of players after the first 2 weeks as initial hype dies down and people give up on the game and move on to something else. This game never even had that grace period of hype because even mere hours after this game was released I was waiting several minutes to play a single match. It’s clear that buying this game at release was a huge miscalculation on my part and I fully expect it to be 50% off in sales by the end of the year. If you have some friends that you can play this with you’ll have a lot of fun, but if you’re just looking to play against randoms it’ll be a rough time, especially as the months go by and the playerbase dwindles even further. If you are interested in some of the games in this collection but have no interest in playing online, and emulators are, for some reason, a big no-no for you, then it might be worth checking out the Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium instead as some of the games included in this collection are also in that one, there’s just no online play. Whether they work out to be cheaper or not I don’t know as 2nd Stadium isn’t out yet.Despite everything I just said I do feel that this is a well-made, albeit overpriced, collection. Menus are quick and easy to navigate, there’s lots of bonus content to enjoy in the form of music and art, and online, when you can find a game, runs great thanks to well implemented rollback netcode. Naturally the 10 games included in this collection are all good fun and run with no issues. There are no tutorials for any of the games, but they’ve been around for years so I’m sure anything you want to know can be easily found on a fanmade wiki.And hey, it’s a good way for people to get into Darkstalkers, right? Lord knows they've slobbered over lewd fan art and cosplay of Morrigan for years, so now’s their chance to actually play the games she originated from… right?In closing;Great games, great collection, too expensive, dead online that runs really well.BUY IT AT A STEEP DISCOUNT.Also Capcom, Darkstalkers 4 plz?

_childDocuments_.review: Being able to play the Darkstalkers games, both online and offline, without going through the usual rigmarole of finding an emulator, hoping that it's not malware, finding a ROM, playing Russian roulette that it's not a virus, setting up the controls, hoping it detects your third party controller, hoping the game even works, and hoping it isn't going sixteen times the speed it was meant to... is just magical. I wanna try the other games in this collection, since they're part of fighting game history that I was alive for but sadly just never got exposed to at the time.But I specifically got this collection for the Darkstalkers entries. And in the short time I've had to just see if everything works, they're a blast to play again already. Sure, it's still hard. I suck as much at them now with proper controls on an official release than I ever did playing them via emulators. But they're just as fun. I'm not even gonna do my usual thing of waiting til I get tens, maybe hundreds of hours with this game to recommend it. Apart from two of the entries not having the option to swap to the English version, this still has EXACTLY what I wanted out of it.~~~~~Capcom, please understand, the best way to see if people are interested in a new Darkstalkers game is not to release the old ones again, but to, y'know, actually make a new one and see if it captures the attention of old and new audiences. Of course, considering SF6, your hands are tied, and let it never be said that people don't appreciate being able to play these classics with this collection now. I certainly do. This was most definitely a great release. I just hope you're not basing whether or not folks are interested in a new entry based on the success of these re-release collections. Because whether or not this or any of the other compilations in other platforms came out, folks have been wanting a new Darkstalkers game for over TWO DECADES.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Denuvo is no longer a backend to this game, so the Denuvo explaination segment is removed.Street Fighter has already had a collection rerelease called Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection. This includes every mainline Street Fighter and their iterations before Street Fighter 4. This includes all 5 arcade versions of Street Fighter II (yes there were 5 of them), all Street Fighter Alphas (arcade versions), and the golden gem that is Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike. This is currently availible on the Steam store page.The Capcom Fighting Collection includes tons of fighting games that have yet to be rereleased as well as ones in high demand. Darkstalkers is one such game that hasn't seen a rerelase since the PS2. Cyberbots, a fighting game where you play as ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechs, has not seen a US console release at all. Other games include Red Earth, a Japanese-only arcade fighter set in a fantasy world where you fight dinosaurs and wizards and other such warriors. Even Hyper Street Fighter II makes an appearance, a modified console-version of SF2 that includes whatever version of an SFII character you wish to play as. The collection comes with training modes for each game as well as single-button commands (if you wish), savestates/rewind, and tons of behind-the-scenes art. Really cool game if you're a fighting fantatic. Or even need some practice.One of the main negatives is the lack of players in the online mode. However, the online function itself great: you can select however many games you wish to play online, then play in-game (in training mode or arcade) as you wait for an opponent. The game also has rollback netcode, which allows both players smooth and uninterrupted peer-to-peer gameplay. This would all be fantastic, but unfortunately most players will play these games on Fightcade, a free online matchmaking system which allows players tons of options to play tons of fighters.However, a big plus for this game from me is the convenience. No hassle trying to find roms or setup controls, it's all right there ready to go. It's also a very lab-friendly game: while I'm out there playing matches in Fightcade, I'm here in training mode looking at the movelists and hitboxes. Not only that, but it's especially great for local multiplayer. If you have a laptop or Steam Deck, it's especially fun. It doesn't even take much to run, the thing can run on a Chromebook. Just plug in the HDMI cable to your TV, grab some some friends/controllers, and you have yourself a Friday Night Fisticuff.I would not recommend it at it's current price, though. $40 is a bit steep, especially since it's been 2 years and there's very little games on it. Wishlist and wait for a sale. The game has gone as low as $16, which I feel is more than fair.
