_childDocuments_.review: Everything that can be said to praise this game has already been said over the past 6 years. Instead, I'm going to rate the port itself in comparison to the previous releases.This port of Persona 5 Royal is easily the ultimate edition coming with all past DLC for both the original release, and the Royal release on PS4 (except one which has been removed for political reasons). This is strangely both a positive and a negative, as the DLC content is accessible from very early game and is quite unbalanced. That being said, if you truly don't want to use that content, you are not forced to interact with it. There are a few strange censorship issues with this release however. The symbol for Almighty damage has been altered, as well as a some "Feudal Japan" imagery. I use the quotes as some of the removed assets are only loosely associated with it, while others such as the removed DLC are more literal. None of this censorship has had any major impact on my gameplay experience however. This port has been done wonderfully. Everything flows smoothly with no stutters or lag. The removal I'll miss the most will be the "Take your time" logo used on the loading screens as they simply no longer exist. Loading screens and saving the game takes mere moments, to the point where I didn't even realize it finished the first time I saved the game. You can dip into a safe room, save and leave the safe room in the matter of 2-3 seconds depending on your input speed. It's incredible. Visual upgrades are top notch. While there's few customization settings, the settings it have are more than enough to justify the upgrade. While ultrawide support would have been nice, it does come with an impressive 4k scale with supersampling, as well as a 120fps option that makes the game look better than ever before. The only issue I have with the new visuals is a strange red filter over most of the All-Out-Attack animation, that fades near the end. This might have something to do with the game loading much faster, and I hope it gets removed with an update. For now, mods fix this issue. The keyboard controls are a bit strange but totally usable. Certainly not ideal, but you can configure them however you like. That being said, this is for sure a game built around having a controller to play with, and it takes controller support to whole new levels. It supports all modern game controllers including the Switch Pro controller, including interface icons in game, as well as the coveted Switch Pro Controller rumble, which few games support. You know, I didn't really expect Persona 5 royal to have as many extensive mods as it has, but it does. I've personally taken to a few mods that simply give me the "correct" dialogue choices in game to avoid alt tabbing for them, which is nice. I've also added a visual mod to remove the above mentioned red filter on AOA animations. That being said, this is merely a week after release and there's already model swaps and even an enemy randomizer. I cannot wait to see how extensive this modding community becomes. Overall, I don't think it's a secret that I have extremely high praises for this game, and this port is a fantastic edition to the release lineup. I've heard a few people say they don't think the game is worth $60 as a re-release, but I'd have to disagree. with the given improvements, along with all past DLC, a story with 130+ hours of gameplay, and even more if you are going for all steam achievements, it's a fantastic value, both for people who already own the game on a console, and especially for people who want to get into the game for the first time. I'd go as far as to call this THE definitive version of Persona 5.

It does everything the original P5 did, but it streamlines it and makes it SO much better! The battle system feels just a touch more fluid than base P5, the music is just as amazing as ever, the story and characters are written well. I'm basically a broken record since these are the exact same things I said with Persona 4 Golden.The new showtime attacks that were included add an extra bit of flair that I quite like, the new characters, new scenes and interactions, three new confidants, even the new third semester! This game is essentially an already amazing game, made even better!I personally only really have one issue with the game. The all out attack fade-in for people who have seizures. I love the idea, but there's no toggle to turn it off, which is quite annoying. Thankfully you can just download a mod to remove it, so that pretty much fixes my problem. Aside from that, the game runs super well! It's definitely worth the money! Especially since the base game  comes with most of the originally released DLC content! (There's like one outfit missing, but again, that can be added back with mods.) There's really not much I can say without repeating things I said in my persona 4 golden review. Go buy and play it! Either on your PS4, Xbox, Switch, or PC! It's a wonderful time!This game is easily in my top 3 favorite games of all time, and it deserves the praise and love it gets! 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal is an enhanced re-release of Persona 5 featuring a multitude of improvements, changes and new content.The core of Persona 5 Royal's story is mostly unchanged from that of the original release, with the majority of changes being subtle rewrites and translation improvements. Persona 5 Royal does introduce a couple entirely new scenes to the original story, but these mostly serve as a way to introduce characters and set up events for Royal's third semester. These new story scenes overall feel cohesive with the original story, however, the placement of some of the new story scenes can feel a little jarring - primarily due to them being added into an already jam-packed schedule.The bulk of the new content added in Persona 5 Royal takes place after the main events of Persona 5's story wrap up, with the introduction of the game's third semester. Introducing a new (mostly) self-contained story-arc and new dungeon, the gameplay of the third semester is exactly what you will have come to expect up to this point.The story of Royal's third semester is well written and provides an interesting experience that feels both familiar yet fresh. The story takes steps away from the main game's story to stand on its own yet remains close enough that it never feels as if it shouldn't belong. While the story is well written, one downside to the third semester is its length. The story features some interesting concepts not present in the main game, but due to the third semester only lasting for approximately one month in game, I don't feel as if they are explored to the fullest of their potential.Persona 5 Royal also introduces a multitude of gameplay changes:Confidants have been re-balanced, with availability, point distribution and skill ranks being adjusted for certain confidants. Confidants now also typically feature an additional "follow-up" scene that takes place as a phone call after returning home, giving you an additional chance to gain points towards a confidant. Along with the changes to confidants, the amount of free time you get has been adjusted with Royal giving you significantly more free time at night. These changes come together to make the daily life segments of the game flow more smoothly.The battle system has also seen some changes, most notably, baton passes no longer need to be unlocked for each character. The baton pass system has also been greatly expanded, now allowing you to chain together passes, granting you more options when formulating a strategy during battles.Mementoes has also had various changes made to it, with new music and collectables you can exchange for items present throughout. However, the biggest change is the addition of stamps, these are found scattered randomly through each of the blocks and can be exchanged to enable buffs within mementoes such as granting increased exp or money. The addition of stamps also gives you much more reason to actually explore mementoes outside of completing requests. However, attempting to collect every stamp can become a little monotonous as, just like with mementoes itself, the placement of many of the stamps is entirely random meaning you will often find yourself running up and down a block repeatedly hoping that you find a floor layout that actually contains a stamp.The palaces also see changes in Royal. While not being entirely different, many of the palaces feature layout changes that allow for them to flow a little smoother. Royal also introduces a grappling hook which is integrated into the palaces typically as a way to access hidden areas, introducing a little more variation to how secrets are hidden. Another addition in Royal is the introduction of Will Seeds, a new type of collectable found within palaces. Will Seeds serve to restore your SP, helping to make clearing a palace in one go a little more feasible, and upon collecting them all reward you with a trinket. One other change seen in the majority of palaces are the boss fights, many of which now feature entirely new phases or mechanics, these changes serve to both re-balance the fights but also help them to feel fresh to anyone who already played the original release.Overall, Persona 5 Royal is the definitive way to experience Persona 5. With its multitude of changes that serve to streamline the experience, it offers improved gameplay, a more strategic battle system, and a reduction of annoyances that all come together to make the game much more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played Persona 5 many years ago on PS4, enjoyed it very much and came close to finishing it, but unfortunately I had a lot of things going on at the time, so I had to put it aside. Alas, the console broke down before I could return to it, and I had moved away from PlayStation hardware in favor of PC gaming. Fortunately, the improved Persona 5 Royal version eventually went multiplatform, thus enabling me to play the very best version on the most powerful hardware available.Being originally developed for the PlayStation 3 hardware, Persona 5 was never a game which featured cutting-edge visuals, but nevertheless the game's stylized artistic direction manages to make Persona 5 a visually interesting game. Persona 5 features colorful graphics set in the distinctive style of Japanese Anime with a combination of fully animated 3D models as well as 2D animated portraits for each of the major characters, complete with both in-game rendered 3D and 2D anime cutscenes. As a result, P5R looks like a combination of a Visual Novel and a 3D Japanese Role-playing Game, which is likewise reflected in the gameplay, but we'll get more into that later.Persona 5 Royal features multiple musical tracks, consisting of both orchestral melodies as well as complete songs, each with English language lyrics. The music sounds good and the songs are extremely catchy, provided that you can appreciate Jazzy tunes, lounge music, and Japanese Pop. The in-game dialog is available in your choice of either Japanese or English, with all critical, plot-significant dialog and story sequences featuring full voice acting. The English Dub is best described as adequate, the performances aren't outstanding, but they suit the characters well and the lines are well spoken. I haven't sampled the Japanese Dub, but I'm unqualified to comment on it regardless because I don't speak the language.Persona 5 Royal is a combination of a traditional Turn-based JRPG, Dungeon Crawler, and a Life Sim/Visual Novel in which you must balance a daily schedule of attending High School, spending time speaking with friends to strengthen your bonds with them, exploring dungeons and engaging in traditional turn based combat with enemies. As you would expect from the aforementioned combination of genres, the game is extremely dialog heavy, including sequences in which you must answer questions in class, engage in conversation with friends, and carefully choose your responses from a multiple choice dialog tree in order to answer questions correctly as well as get closer to your friends. You also have a variety of stats directly associated with social interaction — Knowledge, Guts, Proficiency, Kindness, Charm — which directly effect your ability to express yourself. These stats are increased by engaging in various daily activities as well as interacting with particular individuals, and are fortunately in most cases gained passively from average everyday activities, so you don't have to invest too much time into increasing them. Interacting with your friends increases the Rank of your bond with them granting various perks in combat and allows you to fuse more powerful Personas to equip yourself with.The JRPG portion of the game is likewise exactly what you would expect from the genre. You explore dungeons, (Palaces) engage in turn-based combat with enemies (Shadows) with a variety of techniques at your disposal, earn Experience Points to Level Up along with money to buy equipment, and open treasure chests to gain loot in the form of various items. The only variation to the standard JRPG formula lies in the eponymous Personas, Mythological Entities which are equipped to you and your party similarly to weapons, granting magical abilities. Personas level up passively along with you when equipped, but have their own separate stats. Those who have played various Monster Taming RPGs will be familiar with the basics here, but it isn't difficult for newcomers to learn through progression.Altogether, the combination of genres compliment each other and makes for an engaging, multifaceted gameplay experience which can seem deceptively overwhelming at first but quickly becomes second nature in practice.In Persona 5 Royal you take on the role of a teenage boy who has been moved away from his home out in the country to live with a family friend in the city after he became involved in a confrontation with a drunken man who was attempting to force a young woman into his car, with the man injuring himself in the process and the boy arrested then charged with assault. The boy arrives in the city only to find that his undeserved reputation as a juvenile delinquent has followed him there, with his new guardian addressing him as an unwelcome guest, his teachers at school likewise dismissing him as a delinquent, and his classmates avoiding him while exchanging rumors regarding the details of his arrest.Shortly after his arrival, he discovers a mysterious App has appeared on his Phone which seems to restore itself no matter how many times he deletes it. One day on his way to school the App is inadvertently activated during a conversation with another ostracized student, transporting them into another world in which the School has been replaced by a Palace ruled by the School's abusive P.E. Instructor, with the two being locked up in the dungeon by the guards. They escape their cells with the help of a mysterious feline creature named Morgana, but are quickly caught by the guards on their way out of the palace, leading to the boy awakening to his Persona — his "other self" — granting him the power to defeat the palace guards and escape. The next day they return to the Palace where they are informed by Morgana that it exists within the mind of its ruler as a cognitive manifestation of his distorted desires, and that by stealing his treasure they can change his heart, thus putting an end to his abusive behavior. From there the trio forms a team known as The Phantom Thieves of Hearts, setting out to use their powers to reform society by changing the hearts of various corrupt authority figures, recruiting new allies along the way as they are drawn ever deeper into an insidious plot to seize control of Japan by manipulating the masses.Being a port of a game which was originally developed for the PlayStation 3, Persona 5 Royal doesn't require a particularly powerful PC to run. I encountered no performance issues whatsoever over the course of my 171 hour long playthrough and the game ran flawlessly at Max Settings on my PC. Your experience may vary based on the specs of your PC, but I can safely say that there are no bugs, glitches, or performance issues to speak of regardless.Persona 5 Royal is an excellent game featuring many hours of content between the deep, engrossing story and entertaining assortment of gameplay mechanics. I came just short of a 100% run, missing only a single Confidant, yet completing the story and side quests in their entirety, closing out the game by earning 100% of the Achievements. My playthrough lasted 171 hours, thus making it by far the longest of any single player game I have ever played in 35 years of gaming. I enjoyed the game thoroughly and am left with nothing bad to say about it whatsoever. I highly recommend it to anyone seeking an immersive JRPG to occupy their time.

_childDocuments_.review: I named my character Not Sure and am playing with Japanese voices this time around. I've played Persona 5 twice (NG and NG+) and Royal once - both on the PS4 Slim aka the formerly "Persona-God-of-War-Spider-Man"-station. I highly recommend the PC port here, even if you've already played the original Persona 5. It runs buttery smooth and the game itself has a ton of quality-of-life improvements and new content that make it well worth playing. It's the definitive edition of the game through and through.It runs well on Steam Deck.For playing on my desktop, I had to install Flawless Widescreen as a separate mod, since the game only supports 16:9. Currently, the UI is a little goofy  and there's minor pop-in problems, but I'm playing on 32:9 which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid so don't worry about it if you're just doing 21:9. I'm sure any kinks in the UI will be fixed down the road, since the fanbase is very passionate in the modding community.I also went ahead and installed SpecialK to disable the "Pause on Focus Loss" functionality, since there's no setting for that in-game to enable/disable. If you're alt-tabbing to check  confidant, fusion, or other misc guides, it'd be ideal for not hearing the music suddenly stop, since it's a turn-based game where you don't gain much by pausing.The DLC personas bundled with Royal break the game, especially Kaguya/Kaguya Picaro - so feel free to use those if you want to focus on the Story without turning it down to Safe/Easy mode. I'm playing on Hard difficulty.  I like the idea of Merciless difficulty, but it becomes more troublesome and annoying than "difficult" when you need to initiate demon negotiations, since you'll often kill things outright when landing a critical/weakpoint/technical hit. Save it for NG+ if you do that, since you're not gathering Personas at that point. Maybe, down the road, there will be mods with better combat difficulty tweaks.5/5 weeb game

The game feels very repetitive afterwards. The only thing that is interesting about this game is the bonding events, world-building and storyline, and that's all there is to it to Persona 5.Let me state a few positives about this game first. For once, the game has a very unique gameplay mechanics and the character/enemy/world designs are amazing. The story and bonding events are also very engaging and definitely intrigue you as a player. Despite its unique gameplay mechanics, it feels a bit too shallow compared to many other JRPGs I've played before. It feels like the game really wants you to explore the bonding event and nothing else, making this game feels more like an over-glorified yapping simulator (visual novel) than an actual game.Of course, some people might enjoy this type of game, but this is just a warning to some of you who are planning to play this game: if you really don't like visual novel or games that are filled with tons of dialogue, definitely stay away from this game. Don't let the Overwhelmingly Positive review scores fool you.

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for the right price to dive into this one and after spending 60+ hours with it, I think it's safe to say it's something I enjoy. But I do want to talk about some of my gripes with it. I think this formula, while obviously successful, is slightly stale; 3 games later and it feels a bit predictable, landing on similar beats to the previous games in ways that affect impact. This is a big reason why I think there is an important place for other games and gameplay in the Megami Tensei continuity to make their debut here on Steam, especially new and old entries in the mainline franchise as well as its spinoffs.Persona 5 has this almost constant problem of contradiction for me in which it attempts to address several societal problems but ultimately walks back its potency as a discussion; one example is the game's first antagonist, Kanoshida, whose abuse of female students is called into question with a nuanced take on dynamics of power in hierarchical systems. That brilliance is immediately upended by Ann's introduction as a Phantom Thief, which only worsens as tropes like jiggle physics and frustrating hypersexual comments by Ryuji and other characters appear, cementing her sexualization as a character despite attempting to call that into question. Similarly, the subtext of the protagonist's interaction is often designed to support such behavior, and even though it can be relatively easy to romance a number of people in the game before crucial arcs in the plot, the narrative itself fails to acknowledge the possibility that the player might not want to partake in such activities. If the player enters a relationship, the world is not impacted in any meaningful way; the game's systems restrict the player's ability to avoid behaviors of infidelity/misogyny and provides no means to contest those behaviors in the characters around them. In contrast but not too dissimilar from that problem, the game reminds you constantly of your responsibility to the game's conflict, which at times feels less like a critique of heroism as a cultural phenomenon as intended and more like a reinforcement of recognizable flaws in that narrative. The themes of rehabilitation, delinquency and redemption are perfect places for a broader conversation about society, but sadly, they never reach that level and I find that disappointing.Despite that, the characters are still quite engaging and its Jungian themes are fascinating in their depiction. I think it's worth braving some predictability, at times comically anime-esque objectification and occasionally monotonous dungeon design for such philosophical ideas as uncommon as they are in RPGs, and in doing so, you'll be rewarded with some of the best UI in gaming as well as addictive turn-based combat, strong and varied social interactions, and diverse interactivity with entities from cultures around the world.

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell this is a turn-based combat RPG with a deep social simulation twist. It features a well-developed combat system alongside a relationship simulator with social stats that influence gameplay. Your choices throughout the game impact how things develop, adding a layer of replayability and consequence. The game shines in how its charming world context ties these systems together. Managing your time wisely, with attention to the day and available options, adds a satisfying layer of accomplishment.The story boasts excellent character development and well-paced transitions. While some relationships might feel a bit formulaic, the overall narrative delivers a satisfying conclusion. The Royal version integrates new characters seamlessly throughout the story, avoiding the feeling of them being tacked on. This enhances the investment in the story's twists and character growth.While the raw graphical power might not be top-of-the-line, Persona 5 Royal's true visual strength lies in its style and UI. The attention to detail in character portraits, menus, and the overall stylistic coherence throughout the game is impressive. The UI design stands out as a particular highlight, offering an exceptional level of clarity and visual appeal. This is one of the facets that I love most about the game.The second thing I love most about this game is the sound-work. The soundtrack is fantastic, featuring catchy and memorable tunes that elevate the experience. The voice acting is superb in both quality and volume, adding significant depth to the lengthy story.Persona 5 Royal offers a truly exceptional gaming experience. It's a fulfilling journey that encourages players to explore and complete as much as possible. The game's length is substantial, but the content is consistently engaging, avoiding the pitfalls of repetitive filler quests found in other titles. All the elements come together in perfect harmony, making this a game highly deserving of recommendation at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Slight Edit : the game play time isn't correct. For some reason my SteamDeck didn't update the store, but I have around 20h on the deck First of all, this isn't *exactly* a negative review, but, as always, given only the choice between positive and negative I had to chose one that would level off the general rating.P5 Royal isn't a bad product, and if you are into dialogue/cutscene heavy "games" (games being used here in the loftiest, vaguest way possible), I assume you'll love it. I'm also aware that most JRPGs fall into that category ... I was just expecting a tad bit more from a 60€ game.My problem with it is that it's much less a game than a slightly interactive anime. The combat is rather pathetically simple and repetitive, the dialogue options do *sometimes* actually make a difference, but that's rather rare, as most options in dialogue all express the same, just with other words (this might be a shortcoming of the English translation though!), and, in the big picture, meaningless. The worst part of the game design though is the save-point system, which forces you to keep playing until you reach one of the rare save-enabled scenes or lose all your "progress" (which, in this case, means mostly rewatching fast forwarded version of the dialogue, enjoy the 'complex' "press continue button" game loop, and redo repetitive combat). Pro tip: Play it on a Steam Deck. At least you can pause anytime you want (Albeit you can't start another game). Visually it's nothing really to hoot about, but it's functional. You can get a steady 50fps with everything maxxed on the Steam Deck (whilst it still looks rather dated). I'm pretty sure you can also get a steady 60fps on it, but 50 is my usual battery saving refresh rate.Acoustically it's nice, with some okay jpop and good voice overs (english in my case). Again, nothing really popping out but it's functional.The story is your standard Teens going against the system/adults fare, with some added levity via darker topics like depression and suicide, and here, again, it's functional and actually fun, though, again, not stellar.All in all, you're probably not missing much if you just head over to youtube and watch a "let's play" session, unless you are REALLY into JPRGs .. then go ahead, knock yourself out. You'll probably love it.

_childDocuments_.review: In the ever-evolving landscape of video games, certain titles stand out as exceptional pieces of art, combining gripping narratives, innovative gameplay mechanics, and stunning visuals to create an immersive experience. Among these, Persona 5 Royal unquestionably claims its spot as one of the best video games of all time. Released as an enhanced version of the critically acclaimed Persona 5, this game transcends its genre and captivates players with its compelling story, intricate characters, and refined gameplay mechanics.At the core of Persona 5 Royal's excellence lies its narrative brilliance. The game takes players on a rollercoaster ride through the vibrant streets of Tokyo, intertwining the supernatural with the mundane aspects of daily life. The protagonist, a high school student codenamed Joker, becomes entangled in a web of corruption and conspiracy as he and his group of Persona users, the Phantom Thieves, strive to reform society by 'stealing the hearts' of the corrupt evildoers in the world. The story unfolds in a series of meticulously crafted arcs, each delving into the lives of the main characters and exposing the dark secrets that bind them.One of the standout features of Persona 5 Royal (and the Persona franchise in general) is its ability to address complex and relevant social issues. The game fearlessly tackles topics such as societal expectations and pressure, corruption, the impact of technology on personal relationships/the world around us, and even heavier themes such as mental health issues, sexual assault, suicide, and more. This narrative depth elevates Persona 5 Royal beyond a mere gaming experience, turning it into a thought-provoking exploration of contemporary societal challenges and social commentary.Persona 5 Royal boasts a cast of very memorable characters, each with their own unique personalities, backgrounds, and struggles. The game successfully establishes a deep connection between players and the characters, as their growth and development are intricately woven into the overarching narrative. The 'Confidant system' (a.k.a The Social Link system), a mechanic that popuralized the Persona franchise and that has been everpresent since Persona 3, allows players to build relationships with these characters; providing emotional depth, personal memories with said characters, and tangible gameplay benefits, up to a maximum "Confidant Rank' of 10. It also happens to be the case that 10 different unique Romance paths can be unlocked and explored, even simultaneously (although this can get messy, and I would not recommend it, especially so to the faint of heart and those with a good conscience).Another selling point for this game is that the characters and cast feel very believable and 'alive', making for a that much more immersive experience. The top shelf, high quality, and realistic voice acting (both available in Japanese or English, although I recommend playing with English dub to any non-native-level-Japanese speaking player) sells these characters so extremely well and really makes you forget that you are playing a game or even looking at a piece of fiction in the first place. Because of this you're *right there* with these characters in the present moment, and you unavoidably grow fond of them the more personally you get to know them; and the more endeavours you undertake and overcome together.The enhanced Royal version of Persona 5 also brings with it the inclusion of new characters, such as Kasumi Yoshizawa and Takuto Maruki, who add further layers to the narrative, introducing fresh perspectives and dynamics to the already established cast of characters, and besides this other characters were given additional screentime in this version of the game as well. The well-crafted character arcs, the humor that every character brings in their own way, and the emotional impact of their personal stories contribute significantly to the game's universal acclaim.Persona 5 Royal is a visual feast that combines a distinct art style with a vibrant color palette. The game's unique blend of Anime, cel-shaded graphics and stylish character designs creates a visually stunning world that sets it apart from other videogame titles. The attention to detail in the level design; which is based on real-life locations in Japan that have been recreated in-game in an almost 1:1 fashion, the beautiful and lively Anime cutscenes, the designs of the Personas -  the manifestation of characters' inner selves - are also a treat to the eyes, and above all the imaginative settings of the 'Palaces' that you and your crew have to traverse through all contribute to the game's aesthetic appeal.Moreover, the game is accompanied by a phenomenal soundtrack composed by the fantastic composer and music artist Shoji Meguro. The game's music and Original Soundtrack do not only enhance the atmosphere, but also becomes an integral part of the overall experience. The jazzy tunes and energetic beats, and above all the lead singer Lyn's super unique and smooth voice perfectly complement the game's stylish aesthetic; creating a synergy that further immerses players in the captivating world of this unforgettable masterpiece.The addition of new personas, confidants, game(play) mechanics, and locations expands the game's scope; providing players with even more content to explore than ever before. The revamped dungeons, known as Palaces, offer improved mechanics and challenges, keeping the gameplay engaging and dynamic for returning players and newcomers alike.The inclusion of the Thieves' Den, a customizable hub for players to showcase their achievements and interact with the game's lore, adds a layer of personalization to the experience. These enhancements demonstrate the developers' commitment to delivering a polished and well-rounded fresh gaming experience for both returning players and new players alike.Most of all, the game simply has an astounding amount of (gameplay) mechanics. When you're not saving the world, you can do things like read a book, hit a few homeruns in baseball, study, go out on a date, do fitness, go shopping, fishing, go to the arcade, watch a movie with someone, etc. But in the palaces, you're busy with stealth, planning, item management, and strategic turn-based combat. You feel like you're truly transported into the game's world because of the sheer amount of things you can do in it.I absolutely recommend this game to anybody who can appreciate a videogame that has a fantastic memorable cast of characters, doesn't mind tons of dialogue to read/listen through, loves snappy, stylish and strategic turn-based combat, can really appreciate a good original soundtrack to listen to for days on end, loves an emphasis on a truly marvelously stylish artstyle, likes Anime, and can tolerate a game with extremely hype moments that are offset and juxtaposed with many moments of slow burn/some grinding here and there.Persona 5 Royal stands as a testament to the potential of video games as an art form. Its narrative depth, well-developed characters, stunning design, and extensive gameplay mechanics collectively contribute to its status as one of the best video games of all time. The game's ability to tackle relevant social issues while providing an immersive and enjoyable experience cements its place in the pantheon of gaming masterpieces. Persona 5 Royal is not merely a game; it is a work of art that transcends the boundaries of its medium, leaving a truly indelible mark on the hearts of players worldwide. P.S Thanks for reading my review.-lustY

_childDocuments_.review: I would have left a neutral review if possible. The two main downsides were Mementos (a randomly generated dungeon, which I found a tedious slog) and the combat in general, which feels very static. I like turn based combat, but I enjoy when that feels like a game of chess, with the ability to move characters around, take actions in any order within the team and work with a small amount of information that leads to lots of combinations and flexibility. P5R is the opposite of this. Combat is just a cycle of selecting an attack (or using a buff/debuff or healing) from huge lists of powers and items and slowing chipping away at HP. This makes lengthy boss fights very tedious.  The process of fusing personas is another complicated set of menus of combinations, stats and powers, which I found boring. I also found the game unnecessarily long and repetitive.On the positive side, the story is strong and the characters are engaging (despite being largely high school tropes). The cut scenes are fantastic, and the soundtrack and animations fun and immersive throughout. I loved daily life and building relationships (though I was disappointed that forming a romance had very little impact on character interactions). The palaces and their puzzles are mostly fun to explore and solve.Tonal missteps tipped my review into the negative. The male gaze makes a regular appearance and is unbalanced by any female equivalent (the guys get to gawk at the girls in their swimwear but not vice versa). The game is obsessed with how thin and sexy Ann is, which felt gross, and there’s a scene in which  It also felt gross that I could  Perhaps worst of all, there’s blatant homophobia. There is only negative representation, of the most stereotypical caricatures of gay guys, who don't respect boundaries. No Atlas, gay people are not looking to foist gayness onto your children. This all felt deeply uncomfortable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game became my favorite game of all time.I have finished Persona 3 Portable, Persona 4 (PS2 version) and Persona 5 Royal. Each game is dear to my heart for different reasons. The reason I found Persona 5 Royal superior to other games, well obviously, because of gameplay. It feels so refined and satisfying. Also one of the unexpected plus points for me is inclusion of earlier titles' battle themes. Fighting while listening Mass Destruction with Persona 5 Royal's combat was a blast. But for me, what makes this games special isn't combat at all. It's your bonds with your friends and memories you make along the game. Eventhough it's just a video game, and they are bunch of jpegs and lines of code, spending time with them feels like spending time with your best friends. While playing it I always said ''I wish I had friends like them.'' but then I realised that my friends like that (and much better :)) and I was neglecting them this whole time because of school or some other excuses. This is weird because social simulator feature of Persona games mainly focuses on managing your time. Yet I was unable to do it in my real life. So after saying goodbye to every confidant that I had maxed out in the game, I decided that I want to change my life for the better and organise my life for the better. For that reason, after finishing the game I haven't felt Post-Persona Depression like other entries. I felt hope for the future eventhough I am still a little bit sad about finishing the game.I want to thank everyone who spent time making this game, this was a beautiful journey from start to the finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Having grown up on Persona and other Atlus games (SMT series..etc) as a child, P5R is the ideal persona game you could realistically ever ask for. While there is no doubt that Persona 3's story is a god given classic, P5R took what the original Persona 5 game set down and amped it up by a hundred - the story, the characters, the revamping of personalities and artwork, and overall the flow of the game itself has become more engaging than ever before. This review will contain SPOILERS. You have been warned.The PROS of the game:+ Psy/Nuke/TechnicalCombat is fluid now, there is never an instance where I view a skill as "man this is kind of useless huh..." like I have before in the previous P1-P4 games. I can always find a way to make a skill work if I genuinely try, and building your Persona with the network functionality allows for more adaptability at an early game experience. One of the biggest differences to me was the innovative ways you could implement physical attacks with your debuffs more alongside Psy and Nuke no longer being utterly useless (they were new (if you don't count P2's nuke), but effectively brought next to nothing with them). P5R changes the way this is handled in combat compared to its vanilla counterpart and brings a more enjoyable factor to ramping up how much damage you could output. Baton pass is no longer attached to your confidants, technical damage can be scaled up, and you can spend many rounds of the game building and building and building for your team and your own Persona. (For instance, if you learn a skill in the Jazz club and then go to the church, your team will be able to remember the skill in NG+. This is amazing for allowing multiple members of your party to gain Arms Master/Spell Master).Overall, the combat and gameplay enhancements with ambushing, new confidant skills for exploring and fighting, and so on and so forth made my playthrough ten times more enjoyable than the vanilla game (considering the fact that I actually WANTED to NG+ it....yeah). It breathed a new life into factors like Crit/Technical/Damage altogether.+ Akechi is no longer a storybook cartoon villain. One of my biggest gripes about P5 original was how cartoonish Akechi really truly was, he was always there twirling his little villainous mustache while also being one of the biggest clowns in the book. A detective prince that did absolutely zero detective work, and only showcased how "cunning" and "manipulative" he was after we wiped the floor with him in Shido's palace. Not to mention trying to engage in the way where the player should feel sorry for him just for the sole fact that you had a few drinks with him at Le Blanc or on an outing or two. The vanilla game not showcasing how he really is, nor letting him behave in an honest manner true to himself really cut the some proper interactions out of the game HOWEVER P5R COOOOOMPLETELY fixes this issue. I did not mind Akechi in the vanilla game despite my gripes with his writing, but he is fully fleshed out and actually given real depth in Royal. It was probably one of the biggest boons of the game to me to see how his storyline got switched and getting to actually use him beyond one dungeon (lol) was great. My only wish was that I wanted him to stay navigator longer in Maruki's palace (one day is just not enough for all his snarky commentary).In Royal, he really acts like the mess he truly is, and you actually see how he showcases his detective work. I won't spoil everything, but it really saved his character for me. 10/10 for his pure bitchiness and pettiness, gaslight gatekeep girlboss.+ MarukiI personally, will actually say nothing about Maruki. Please play the game and get to know him yourself, he is probably one of the most engaging characters we have witnessed thus far. A lot of people I fear have misunderstood the themes of a certain area, and why he provides the choices that he does - I have seen a lot of criticisms that he contradicts himself both as a Counselor and a Cognitive Psientist. He really doesn't, though I will say this comes from my own understanding as someone with a psychological research background through my field studies... it's important to understand where his inherent bias begins to take play with his character and how it effects the world around him.Give him a chance, he brings some of the best OST P5R has. There is a part near the ending of the game where he interacts with the protagonist in a way no other Persona game has ever done before, and frankly I love it. It's nothing but pure feelings on display between two individuals that got to know one another over the course of the game.+ / - KasumiI loved and hated Kasumi.Kasumi was a character I genuinely enjoyed the dynamic of in the beginning, I found that her character was pretty likeable despite how shoehorned in she was. As long as it wasn't another Marie, (and THANKFULLY it wasn't) I was more than grateful to accept and additional character like herself... my only gripe however is how forced the romance is. It becomes unbearable, and the extreme swap to dynamic but suddenly bringing the original dynamic back in tow was a bit hard to stomach if only because Atlus wrote it in one of the poorest ways they could have.I think if her character were more polished and they weren't pushing her to be your TRUE ROMANCE GIRL XOXOXO 10/10 CALL ME BACK BABEY, I would have been more keen toward her. Still not Marie, so still good. Also she gives boosts to your critical hit rate in end-game, we TAKE those.+ SoundtrackIt's an Atlus game let alone an addition to one of the most outstanding Persona game soundtracks to date, of course the soundtrack is good. You don't even have to ASK if the soundtrack is good - just wait until true ending.+ Visuals / ArtFinally, no more one sprite circus show with the way most facial expressions were slipping off of every character's face. Sprites are on-point, the art in the cutscenes are pretty on-point, and yeah. Frankly, it's a lot better to look at now.+ DungeonsMan, the dungeon design... I don't think I'll ever be able to play the older games the same ever again. Royal blew it out of the water with the dungeon design alongside how Mementos was played. Mementos being akin to that of Persona 3's Tartarus, while the Palaces were like those of the dungeons from Persona 4 in design but MUCH MUCH BETTER. My biggest and most fatal criticism about Persona 4 is that the dungeons are an absolute slog to get through. Persona 5 Vanilla brought out these outstanding maps and dungeon designs too, but they were also pretty sloggish themselves. Royal however, brings a new feel to the dungeons. You can actually progress without feeling like you're looking at the same thing ten times over or going down yet another stupid hallway (I will never forgive Persona 4 for it's "GAME" dungeon and the onslaught to both my eyes, ears, and brain). The combat is good, exploring the dungeons is good, Mementos is good. Thank god.Now onto my CONS which I will keep relatively short:- The grind is kind of meaningless.- The reaper's fight is not as engaging as it used to be. - The introduction to passive skills both through the confidants, your Persona, and otherwise really made the gameplay far more easier than ever. This isn't inherently a BAD thing (I enjoyed it!), but after getting used to how this game worked and as a previously experienced fan I can 100% say you will pick up on what this game does in combat FAST. - If you're an experienced veteran, playing on Normal is NOT enough. Go hardest difficulty from the start.- Ambush has 1 theme only.- Your choices as a Protagonist beyond Akechi and Maruki are irrelevant. Dialogue options are pretty redundant, I felt they didn't hold too much weight. I did however, love the protagonist's personality and aesthetic.- The fanservice is over the top at times, but it's Atlus.Overall, my favorite in the series thus far. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Gustavo Fring, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn.Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Fring flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Fring was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my criminal activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to discuss Persona 5 Royal. Instead, I will discuss its impact on me as a person:This game carried me through 4 consecutive months of escapism I put myself through in order to spice up my weekly routine of Work, Gym, Martial Arts, and coming home alone to my parents and sister. Being a 24 year old can be tough, but being a single 24 year old introvert with no relationship prospects is brutal.Funnily enough, Persona 5 Royal taught me to face reality head on rather than make excuses and use games to cope. I want to work hard to better myself while maintaining hope for a better future no matter what curve balls life throws at me. While I'm no social butterfly, I'm now starting to develop the confidence to talk to a pretty woman or try new things that are outside my rigid routine. At the end of the day, life goes on irregardless of my circumstances. It's up to me to decide if I am going to sink into the mud and whine about how life isn't fair and the odds are stacked against me or if I'm going to make the most of the hand I've been dealt and take advantage of the opportunities around me.Finally, I fully intend for Persona 5 Royal to be the last game I play for a long time. Gone are the days of coming home from work or the gym and locking myself away in my office while I mindlessly grind away. I want to rediscover my passions and find fulfillment in the things and people around me. I call on you to do the same.Once you finish Persona 5 Royal of course. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave the game a good try, but the small frustrations mounted to the point I can't be bothered to try any more.  The limited time for activities like raising stats or bonds and the looming knowledge that if I don't get certain things done within a time limit I would be permanently locked out and have to play through the entire game again just for the "true" ending is very discouraging.  I don't want to put in a hundred hours just to find out I don't have enough intelligence because I missed a crossword puzzle or a test answer.  Following that, the characters just weren't engaging, the main character is the blankest blank slate of a protagonist since I last played pokemon, Ryuji repeats the same line ad nauseam, Morgana mostly shouts exposition and obsesses over Ann.  Speaking of Ann, I have scarcely seen a character so jarring in execution.  In the first arc, she fights to not be seen as an object to obsess over, but the game tries to make us see her that way.  The fact that, in order to progress the 2nd palace, she had to strip for a future party member, while the scene is played for laughs with Morgana opening a door, is just really uncomfortable.  Furthermore, Ann's phantom thieves outfit is covered in zippers, and her persona is based on a seductress who used her body to manipulate men.  It is such a gross case of having your cake and eating it too after spending so long learning about Ann's trauma and abuser.I am sure people can enjoy playing Persona 5, of that I have no doubt, but I cannot get pass these issues which are so heavily placed in the beginning of the game.  The music is good, the designs are good, but the execution of everything is so all over the place.

_childDocuments_.review: It just feels like P5R improved every superficial element that was subpar in P4G (mainly in the presentation department) at the cost of elements that made P4G special. Yes, the dungeons are hand crafted set pieces now instead of P4G's corridor marathon, but they're still the same repetitive game-play loop of ambushing shadows and opening doors. The trivial puzzles that are occasionally sprinkled in hardly breakup the monotony. And in any case, P4G's corridors make a return in Mementos, only now longer and more monotonous than before. Yes, the combat and interfaces look flashier but the game is even more shy about presenting any kind of challenge than P4G. Yes, your new gang has some interesting moments but there are much less special events with them than in P4G, and there are so many monotonous dialogues about the rotten adults in charge that would surprise even the Kids Next Door. It doesn't help that most boss fights consist of equally monotonous monologues about how rotten they are. There's more problematic elements I could gripe on & on about: Yusuke's creepiness ("Pose nude for me or I'm calling the cops"), Haru coming in too late in the plot, Makoto & Futaba dominating the party too much, the fortune teller that predicts what your friends want to hear in exchange for money, etc. etc. Finally, P5R adds a third semester & while the main story of this extra leg is fairly compelling, there is almost nothing new to do here. It's "Go to the Gym or Jazz Club until the timer runs out" semester, because none of the other daily activities are worth doing at this point. Overall, it just feels like I spent 150 hours on an experience that would have been better if it lasted 40 hours. I don't doubt the skill & commitment dedicated to make this game, I'm just skeptical that the end result is still slight downgrade from Persona 4.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to preface this by saying I've played the original PS4 version and the PS4 Royal release so my review will be mostly based on those. Yes, this is the third time I've purchased Persona 5.Persona 5 Royal is one of the greatest JRPGs to release from the last generation. It has an absolutely amazing soundtrack, flashy animations, great battle mechanics, fun and likeable characters, and a fun plot. This was the first Persona game I've played and it hooked me on the series as a whole. While this one deviates quite a bit  from the previous entries, with uniquely designed dungeons instead of randomly generated dungeons, it still holds a lot of what makes a Persona game "Persona". The unique dungeons are great set-pieces for their respective owners, and have a lot of good (yet usually simple) puzzles to break up the battles. Outside of dungeon crawling, the game features a lot of slice-of-life mechanics like hanging out with characters, attending school, and various other mini-activities. It's something that breaks up the constant fighting and dungeon crawling, which is nice in my opinion. Doing activities and hanging out with friends uses up a portion of your day, so planning and making smart choices for your playthrough is a must.Royal introduces a whole ton of additional content and changes over the original release. A whole new semester and dungeon, new characters, more fantastic music including a new battle theme, affinity changes to enemies and bosses, new boss mechanics, and a ton of QoL changes that make this the definitive P5 experience. The game, with the new content, clocks in at around 120-150 hours, depending on if you're looking to get all the achievements or not.If you're a fan of turn-based JRPGs, and like (or don't mind) slice-of-life content, you're sure to love Persona 5 Royal.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was my first entry into the Persona/Shin Megami series and I couldn't be more thrilled about it! Sometimes I'll occasionally just start getting lost to the good vibes while getting ready to plan my next move. The combat and gameplay really have to be special or just really have a good flow to it in order to keep me invested and Persona 5 Royal does exactly that and more. I'm constantly caught off guard by how many ways you can approach enemies in combat in this game and each method has been really exciting to use when unlocked.I may write more down the line when I'm done with my first playthrough, but I do have one issue with this version of the game being, Denuvo. It's an anti-piracy thing that's been put into several games I've purchased in the past including this one. While I don't have any issues with Atlus trying to protect their games from piracy, Denuvo in particular has the capability to cause the game to lag every so often which kinda sucks. Unlike my time with Resident Evil: Village, where I couldn't go 5 seconds with lagging, this case weirdly enough is decently more tolerable and not completely game disrupting. I with there was an alternative, but it's the only drawback I have about this specific port of the game. I love Persona 5 Royal regardless.

This problem actually exists in all Persona games, but it is so blatant here that I have to mention it:Persona 5 is an open rejection of the Christian God of the Bible, and glorification of others gods (including lucifer). The games have Gnostic themes to them, such as tarot cards, praying to various gods and fortune readings. I wasn't too disturbed by this in Persona 4: Golden where the strongest Persona you could fuse was lucifer after "discovering" the truth. However, this game takes it to a whole another level toward the end. Some spoilers follow:Truly brazen how far they took their outright rejection, and even hatred, of the Christian God of the Bible.What I am trying to say here is that the game itself is good, but the story could be better, and the game even has downright demonic themes attached to it. They're not ashamed of who they support, and they are doing so openly; in your face. Buyer beware.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal is an engaging game that boasts captivating characters and a well-crafted storyline, making it one of the best I've encountered recently. However, it does suffer from some notable flaws. The combat, unfortunately, falls flat and lacks depth. While I initially had a decent amount of fun with it during the first 20 hours or so, it eventually became monotonous and dragged on. As I progressed further into the game, I found myself actively avoiding combat whenever possible, as it simply stopped to be enjoyable. Adding to the frustration, many of the bosses had an unnecessary amount of health and dealt overwhelming damage. To make matters worse, most of them lacked weaknesses or could be affected by status ailments, essentially rendering the core mechanics of exploiting weaknesses and ailments ineffective. The 5th boss, in particular, proved to be the low point of the game, imposing a tight time limit and throwing wave after wave of enemies at me while constantly debuffing me and buffing itself. Another bothersome aspect was the sporadic absence of voice-acted lines. Understandably, given the sheer volume of dialogue in the game, fully voicing everything would have been impractical, but it was jarring when the voice acting abruptly stopped for several sentences during crucial story missions only to resume as normal after a few sentences.However, if you can look beyond these flaws, you'll discover a truly captivating story and a cast of well-written characters who are a joy to interact with. Spending time with the confidants and delving into their personal stories proved to be an immensely enjoyable experience. Additionally, the chemistry among the main characters during combat is remarkable. Furthermore, the art direction in Persona 5 Royal is visually stunning. The entire game radiates pure style, and even a quick look at a few images is enough to appreciate its aesthetic. Notably, the game's music is a standout feature, characterized by gripping jazz-like compositions that will stay in your mind for days. Certain musical pieces have become personal favorites, surpassing those found in most other games. In conclusion, despite the aforementioned drawbacks, I recommend Persona 5 Royal to anyone wanting to experience a great story. Roughly 60% of the game remains unaffected by these issues, allowing you to relish your time spent interacting with confidants, reveling in the game's stylish direction, or simply immersing yourself in its captivating music.

Surviving the ups and downs of school life, choosing your daily actitivies wisely, strengthening the bonds with your confidants, finding new Persona users, working out at the gym, keeping the interest of your divine collaborators, planning and carrying out your infiltrations while staying hidden - P5R is a game that has you realize the importance of proper time management, to the point where you end up feeling motivated to implement a thing or two into your own life experience. As a Persona veteran who has played the P5 vanilla version, P5R on the PS4 console, and who could not resist the pull of a Steam release, I can assure newcomers to the series that you will not regret spending your money (OR TIME lol) on this masterpiece of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 is definitely one of the games of all time. I remember hearing about it all the time back in 2016 but I never really cared enough to play it until now, that I got into the series as a whole.After being absolutely blown away and in love with Persona 3 FES and Persona 4 Golden, I was really excited to finally boot up Persona 5 Royal. Did it meet all of my expectations and blow me away even more to the point where I'd call it the best game in the series, as many others claimed all these years?I'll start with the overwhelming positives. The game looks fantastic, the music (as usual) is stellar and the world truly feels more alive than ever, considering P5 has more places to go to than 3 and 4 combined. The utilization of newer generation consoles and their power really helped push this series in a direction that has rendered its aesthetics and looks to be absolutely stunning. The story too was incredible but I can't say it was perfect. The words "Phantom Thieves" really start living in your head rent free after playing this game. The characters in this game are ones to remember; I can easily say that I enjoyed mostly everyone that joins the party, as well as the misc. social links. Wait, my bad, confidants. The changes to how your confidants give you abilities that influence the gameplay is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GOOD of a feature. And speaking of gameplay, the game is overloaded with quality of life options compared to its predecessors, which might make it too easy at times, but in all honesty helps take Persona turn based combat to a new level.. For example, while I do believe the story of P5 is awesome, there are some really low lows for all the really high highs. The beginning of the game grabs you by the balls and drags you through the best pieces of narrative seen in gaming history, only to later get a little annoying and obnoxious in the middle and occasionally drop some f-you bombs towards anyone who dislikes cringy clichès to finally become reach an incredible climax right at the end.I used to think that Persona 5 had a bad habbit of never ending and feeling EXTREMELY padded. Royal did not do this gripe of mine any favors and if anything, it only reinforced the feeling that the game overstayed it's welcome. Now it wasn't my first rhodeo as I had played Persona 4 Golden prior and done the extra content in that game, but it just felt a lot more naturally done than the way P5 went about it. Now having played the game a second time, I'm more open to it and and have come to terms with most things but it still doesn't really get as good as it did in 4.Now for my last, biggest complaint of all.There is nothing new to be said here. Morgana is an extremely divisive character and it's extremely easy to hate him. Personally, I really hate him. I cannot stand his head-over-heels attitude for Ann and the fact he has to come explain every minute detail about your daily/upcoming activities like the exposition horse that he is. Having now played the game for longer, I still can't get over just how much annoyance he adds to the game's social sim elements. Even though I know it will never happen, now seeing that even Metaphor will have a mascot-esque character, I sincerely hope Atlus does away with these annoying characters. (future me's edit: gallica is an amazing character and I love her) They add nothing to the game even if their Japanese audience tries to say otherwise.So to summarize, I definitely don't think that Persona 5 is overhyped or overrated or anything of the sort. It definitely met most of my expectations and I'm very glad I played it. This is a humongous game and it's truly hard to express every feeling without forgetting details and it's a game that everyone has to go through. I really hope that if one day we see a Persona 6, it takes the scale and improvements made in 5 and really puts them to good use.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal, an enhanced version of the critically acclaimed Persona 5, is a tour de force in the realm of JRPGs that seamlessly combines a gripping narrative with stylish presentation, complex gameplay mechanics, and an unforgettable cast of characters. Atlus has taken an already outstanding game and elevated it to new heights, delivering an experience that is nothing short of extraordinary.From the moment you step into the shoes of the Phantom Thieves, a group of high school students turned supernatural vigilantes, Persona 5 Royal immerses you in its world of societal rebellion, psychological exploration, and the duality of the human psyche. The game's narrative is a masterful blend of teenage drama, intrigue, and supernatural elements, exploring themes of identity, freedom, and the power of friendship. It delves into the struggles of its characters with a depth that is both relatable and thought-provoking, offering a level of storytelling rarely seen in video games.One of the game's standout features is its unique mix of turn-based combat, social simulation, and dungeon crawling. As you juggle your life as a high school student by day and a phantom thief by night, you'll forge relationships, improve your skills, and explore the Metaverse, a cognitive realm shaped by human desires. Battles are not just about brute force but also exploiting enemy weaknesses, negotiating with demons, and recruiting Personas – manifestations of your inner self. The strategic depth and variety in combat keep it engaging throughout the lengthy adventure.Persona 5 Royal is a visual masterpiece. Its distinctive art style, vibrant colors, and jaw-dropping animations create a visual feast for the eyes. Every environment, character, and Persona is exquisitely designed, each contributing to the game's immersive world. The dungeons, known as Palaces, are a testament to the game's creativity, with each Palace representing the distorted desires of a particular antagonist. This artistic prowess extends to the game's UI design, menu system, and the jaw-dropping All-Out Attacks, which are as visually satisfying as they are satisfyingly powerful.The expanded content in Persona 5 Royal adds even more value to an already substantial experience. New characters, including the enigmatic Kasumi Yoshizawa, bring fresh dynamics to the story, while additional events and confidant (social link) interactions deepen your connections with your teammates and other characters. The new semester in the game's calendar serves as an epilogue, offering a satisfying and emotional conclusion to the Phantom Thieves' journey.The jazz-infused soundtrack of Persona 5 Royal is a masterpiece in its own right. Each track enhances the game's atmosphere and emotional resonance, elevating every moment, whether it's an intense battle or a quiet character interaction. The music perfectly complements the game's stylish aesthetic, leaving an indelible mark on the overall experience.While Persona 5 Royal is a near-flawless experience, its only drawback lies in its time investment. The game's intricate mechanics and extensive dialogue can be overwhelming for newcomers, and its length may prove daunting for those with limited playtime. However, for those willing to invest the time, the rewards are immeasurable.In conclusion, Persona 5 Royal is a triumph of game design, storytelling, and artistic expression. Its rich tapestry of gameplay mechanics, engaging narrative, and stunning visuals create an experience that lingers in the mind long after the credits roll. Whether you're a veteran of the Persona series or a newcomer, Persona 5 Royal is a must-play masterpiece that sets a new standard for JRPG excellence. Step into the Metaverse, and let the Phantom Thieves steal your heart.

As much as I tried, I could only one shot basically all creatures for the first 3/4 of the first palace. The one exception being Pixie since it was weak to gun fire. Even how hard enemies hit is an issue, I'm currently half way through the second palace with everyone in the basic starter armor and it's only now that the mini-boss is hitting hard enough to be an issue.My one other relatively minor complaint is that the DLC box is an all or nothing deal. I opened it for the outfits and had a load of medicines thrown on me, as well as 100,000 Yen, making having to save to unlock the fortune arcana not really a thing anymore. It should also be noted that there's a bunch of super strong (between lv11-80ish) shadows you can just summon for free once you unlock fusion/summon. _childDocuments_.review: I always tried to play games like Final Fantasy or Dragon Quest, but I was constantly bored by the overall turn based mechanics. As you can see, I’m not a turn based RPG guy, but the Persona series made me think otherwise. Persona 4 Gold was my first game of the series and I became a fan after experiencing the World created by the game. I was concerned about the battles and dungeons, but I ended up loving it. The Weakness system is super intuitive and really fun to play. After finishing it, I started to experience different turn based RPGs that I always wanted to play. Persona 5 Royal is in many ways a natural evolution of the previous games. The game screams aesthetics, its art direction is something that was never seen before in a Persona game. The combat is great, the dungeons are no longer randomized and the music is outstanding. The tracks don’t get annoying and there are multiple variations of the same song. The first time you listen to “Last Surprise” you WILL jam with the music. I only have 1 issue with the game and it’s something that can be quite disappointing: the events aren’t bad, but they are forgettable. Persona 4 does much better in that part: the characters are better developed and the events are mostly fun and wholesome. In Persona 5 the events are always the same, and even when it’s different, it’s short and always something to do with the Metaverse (with little development of the characters lives outside of the Phantom Thieves). That rule doesn’t necessarily apply to the Confidant Events, but the other ones that happen during the main story aren’t the best in the series. All of this can be explained by the game tone in comparison with the 4th game: while in Persona 4 there’s this upbeat feeling, Persona 5 keeps the things more grounded. Overall I think this one problem doesn’t affect the experience that much and it’s still a great (and maybe the best) Persona game. If you want to start playing the series I highly recommend Persona 5 Royal.

_childDocuments_.review: Note from someone who's played SMT lll: Nocturne; Don't punch the cyclops elephant.This game is my favorite game of all time. The game's visual elements also have an impact in gameplay; the UI effect for when you hit a Technical in battle, or the splash screens when you do something cool; they're all really good ways of telling the player, "Yo, you just did some REALLY cool ♥♥♥♥!"Persona's also known for its deeper-than-average plotline, where once again, P5R delivers. While some of the characters' writing and dialogue can get bland and a bit off-taste, the overall narrative is awesome. There's a lot of twists and shocking moments that'll catch someone off guard the first time they play it; it definitely caught me off guard.I wish I could say more, but TL;DR, it's an amazing JRPG with a lively and memorable cast, excellent visuals and gameplay, and above all else, Joker Persona 5. _childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal, the enhanced version of the popular game Persona 5, is widely considered to be one of the best games of recent times, and for good reason. The game offers an immersive and captivating experience that is both enjoyable and thought-provoking. The following are some of the key reasons why Persona 5 Royal is a good game.First and foremost, Persona 5 Royal has a rich and engaging storyline. The player takes on the role of a high school student who gains the power to enter a mysterious realm known as the Metaverse. In this realm, the player must navigate through a series of interconnected dungeons and fight against corrupted individuals known as Shadows. The story is well-written, with complex and well-developed characters, and it also explores various social and political issues such as corruption, freedom of speech, and mental health.Another reason why Persona 5 Royal is a good game is its gameplay. The game is a mixture of turn-based combat and life simulation, allowing players to build relationships with characters, attend school, and engage in other activities outside of the Metaverse. The combat system is challenging, but also rewarding, with a variety of skills and abilities available to the player. The life simulation aspect of the game is also enjoyable, as players get to experience the daily life of a high school student and interact with a diverse cast of characters.In addition to its gameplay, Persona 5 Royal also has exceptional graphics and music. The graphics are colorful and vibrant, with detailed character designs and beautifully rendered environments. The music is equally impressive, with a fantastic soundtrack that perfectly fits the tone of the game.Finally, Persona 5 Royal is a game that encourages players to think critically about the world around them. Through its story and characters, the game explores complex issues and encourages players to question the status quo. This not only makes the game more engaging, but it also inspires players to think about the world in a new light.In conclusion, Persona 5 Royal is a game that offers a rich and immersive experience, with a captivating storyline, enjoyable gameplay, exceptional graphics and music, and thought-provoking themes. _childDocuments_.review: Game is mid at best, if I'm being entirely honest.That being said, TL;DR, if you enjoy anime stuff and have enjoyed previous installments of the series or just like mechanically basic JRPG's, you'll probably enjoy this game.Now to get into the bulk of my issues with this game:There are some frustrating aspects of the main story line and some of the side quests, particularly the dark themes combined with the annoyingly naive disposition of the main cast. Some villainous characters in the game also never get their just dues. Minor spoiler: the fact that we couldn't send the couple making essentially CP to jail is a travesty.Also, I seriously doubt the general public would give a ♥♥♥♥ if some unethical rich dude died of a heart attack. I, in fact, think that a huge chunk of the population would enjoy it and most of the rest couldn't care less.Some anime tropes that are insufferable and unfunny are also squished into this game and I find that to be pretty annoying, like casual sexual harassment from the main male cast. An anime staple, I know, but come on, that stuffs never been funny. However, Persona's strong points are still strong in this game. Most of the social links and side story development are satisfactory, this is also probably most of the reason why people play these games. I know that's why I kept playing it.The bulk of the non-combat gameplay is basically a hold over from the previous games, which is fine, cause there wasn't anything really wrong with the daily activities your character did between dungeons. This is also where a bulk of the side character developments happen and therefor, are the best parts of the game.The dungeon crawling and exploration is also largely a hold over from the previous games, which is a shame cause that was always Persona's weak point. They added some minor problem solving and platforming/exploration aspects to the game, but they're so easy that they're a minor distraction at best. Dungeon design varies from bland to extremely poor, with no outstanding levels that are fun to play, with the later dungeons being full of back tracking, looping rooms and basic puzzle solving in same-y looking corridors and rooms full of the same enemies.Combat is also mostly similar to the previous games except they've added a bunch of mechanics to make it even easier like the sneaking mechanic which makes ambushes trivial. This only gets easier the further the story progresses. They did add a few new elements and status effects along with tech skills and such to spice it up but the mid-late game will still revolve around your OP MC one shotting mobs and nuking bosses as quickly as possible using overpowered Persona's and builds. This of course is only applicable if you know how to use the fusion system, but that's not difficult to learn and fusion guides are plentiful on the internet if, like me, you just want to smash through the dungeon segments as quickly as possible so you can do more side character development. The art direction of this game, like the other games in the series, is stellar and in fact might be the best yet. I'm also certain this is a huge chunk of the reason why the game scores so highly despite is numerous flaws.Anyways. that's all I can think to say about this game. By no means is it perfect in my opinion, and I did find a big chunk of it to be pretty frustrating, but I did enjoy my time with the rest of it that didn't annoy me and I don't regret purchasing or playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game after seeing the reviews were all through the roof, praising it for story, combat, gameplay, ETC. The story seemed compelling.Unfortunately, the game falls short in multiple areas.The combat starts with a degree of strategy required, but as you progress it goes from "Find weakness and exploit" to "just spam abilities because nothing has a weakness."The social simulator is cumbersome, tiresome, and drags on. Few of the side characters actually have interesting story arcs, and I found myself not caring about the girl who is too self conscious to be good at modeling or the like.I played this originally on the switch, got about 1/4 of the way through, then couldn't find the interest to finish it.
