There is so much fluff that just adds delay that you end up losing an enormous amount of time to just waiting. I don't even mean dialogue or story exposition - I just mean moving from point A to point B, or an animation that you'll end up seeing so often that it just gets old and tiresome. The final fight even has a timesink that adds nothing to the story.And in traditional fashion, you can't skip the credits.The main story line was pretty good, I had some laughs along the way, but this game was a rough slog of timesinks and busy work. I only finished it because I'm stubborn.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, P5 is a game of two halves. The first, is a fairly standard JRPG where you go through dungeons, engaging in turn-based battles as you grind your way to the boss to claim the MacGuffin. This is enhanced by some clever twist such a simplified stealth mechanic that allows you ambush enemies to gain an advantage in battles and a complex system of elemental attacks and weaknesses/resistances. That last part may sound pretty standard, but even that was given some added tactical depth since hitting an enemy's weakness doesn't just do extra damage, it knocks them down, and if you manage to knock down all of the enemies on the field, that opens up other options. This leads to a combat system where you're encouraged to use every tool available and think tactically about how to make the best use of your limited resources rather than simply mindlessly mashing your default attack and only busting out the big guns for boss fights. (Final Fantasy, I'm looking at you!)The other half is a life sim that plays out more like a visual novel. While not as immediately engaging, this is where you get to really know the people around you, both your party members and others who cross your path over the course of the game. Every one of them has their own stories as you follow along and grow closer to them. This isn't purely for lore purposes, though. The closer you grow to your confidants, the more benefits you receive. Some will help in the dungeons, while others will help you make more efficient use of your time in your day-to-day life, but all of them are useful. Yes, more efficient use of your time... as that's the core pressure in this half of the game. You only have so many slots available each day, and every major action uses one up. Invariably, you find yourself having to weigh the pros and cons of spending time with one person to grow closer to them, working a part-time job to earn some quick cash, or studying so you can pass your midterms. There are almost always a half-dozen things you could be doing that would all help in some way, but you can only do one of them before time marches on and you need to move on to the next slot (or get swept up in the next bit of the story).The two halves aren't quite as tightly interwoven as something like XCOM (where you'd go on battles to retrieve equipment that could then be studied back at your base to better equip your troops for the next battle, and so on). The dungeons, for example, are far and away your best source of income, but while there are definitely places where it can help in your everyday affairs, most of it will likely be sent on upgraded equipment and supplies to assist in your next dungeon run. The personas you can acquire in the dungeons (the source of your more mystical abilities) can provide a slight boost to your relationships if they happen to match up with the person you're trying to grow closer to, but otherwise the dungeon delving  does precious little to help as you go about the daily routines of a high school student. Even so, there is enough interplay between the two (in addition to simply breaking up the gameplay so no, one style overstays its welcome), so that the overall experience of each would be greatly diminished without the other. In short: it may have taken forever to come to PC, but it was totally worth the wait! P5 is easily one of the best JRPGs. It still borrows from many of the same tropes (teenage protagonists banding together to save the world), even if the high school setting is somewhat unique (though typical for the franchise). If you can't deal with those quirks, this may not turn everything around for you, but if you've ever enjoyed a game in the genre, this is a must-own!

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal is in my opinion the perfection of turn based combat as well as an excellent social sim. It has a huge cast of unforgettable and well realized characters (and the SIU director), some incredible dungeon designs (visually and gameplay wise), the best video game soundtrack of all time, and a story that even with its 100+ hour runtime leaves you wanting to do it all over again. You will laugh, you will cry, you will probably cringe at some point (just being honest). Most importantly though, the game will assuredly leave an impression on you if you reach either the game's original ending or the "new" Royal ending. The story of Persona 5 is expertly crafted. The game starts in medias res, showing our protagonist, Joker, escaping from a casino while guided by his teammates. Joker is captured while escaping, and brought to an interrogation with prosecutor Sae Niijima. She proceeds to ask him questions that we as players don’t know the answers to yet, but those questions peak the player’s interest. She talks of stealing hearts and another world as though we should be aware of the meaning behind her words. Then we are thrust back in time to April of the same year. What then follows is 100 hours of riveting story arcs, with incredible party members, interesting supporting characters, and immoral villains. You discover another world called the Metaverse and learn that you have the power to change society by infiltrating palaces (a.k.a. RPG dungeons) and stealing the treasure of the ruler. Without spoilers I will just say that the game just gets better and better as it goes, culminating in a final act that is my favorite ending to any game. You will know all of these characters as people by the end of the story, and you will feel both extreme satisfaction and a bitter hollowness knowing that your time with them is at an end. Combat in Persona 5 is a very fluid affair. Rather than navigate menus and sub menus constantly. Most basic actions are just bound to single keys or face buttons on a controller. This makes the pace of battle incredibly quick, as by the end of the first palace you will likely have a handle on which button does what and never need to think about it again. Grinding is not really required at all, it is possible to beat the game without doing any (I know, I've done it). However, there is an instakill ability unlocked by progressing through the game that makes you instantly win battles with enemies far below your level and you still gain the experience and money from the fight. This makes leveling incredibly quick in the late game so no need for hours upon hours of mashing the attack button on stuff that poses no threat to you.The major mechanic that differentiates the combat from other JRPGs is the "one more" system. Hitting enemy weaknesses causes them to be knocked down and triggers a "one more" allowing you to take a second turn or hand that turn off to another member of the party for increased damage. These can be chained together through your entire four person party, culminating in your final party member doing massive damage for 0 cost. These mechanics and controls culminate in the best feeling turn based battle system I have ever used. Nothing I have played before or since has felt as good as this system has to control. Whether against common enemies roaming the palaces or the corrupted rulers of those spaces the game feels fun to play from beginning to end, which is incredibly important in a game of this length.An important aspect to mention when talking about how the game plays is the dungeon design. In game the dungeons are referred to as palaces, and without spoiling things I will say that they are all ruled by the villain of their respective story arcs. These are not randomly generated hallways and rooms that you will see repeated ad nauseum. Each palace is hand crafted and they are all visually distinct from one another. You’ll solve puzzles, sneak around, and do some minor platforming between the various bits of combat. No two palaces feel the same, which is impressive considering that they are at minimum around 4-5 hours to complete each on a first playthrough, with some being considerably longer. The combat isn’t the only gameplay however. Many of the ingame days have Joker just living out his life as a high school student. You do various activities like work out, study, eat, read, watch movies, etc. These activities raise Joker’s social stats, which in turn allows him to do more activities. Talking with your confidants (major NPCs that Joker has a meaningful connection to) will level them up, unlocking new abilities for Joker and his party to use while in the game’s palaces. Some have more use than others, but in the Royal version of the game, rarely is there an ability that is not useful in some way. Some of these confidants are locked behind social stat requirements. Making raising them important to making sure that you are as powerful as you can be.Throughout the game you unlock more and more places to explore outside of the palaces. These new places in turn open up new opportunities to raise social stats, provide new vendors for items, or serve as hangout spots for Joker and his confidants. The last thing to talk about regarding the game itself is the presentation. Everybody on the internet has heard people talk to death about how good Persona 5 looks. Unfortunately for everybody, I’m about to jump on that bandwagon as well. The art style on display here ensures that the game will never age. I’m not an art or graphic design major by any means so I don’t properly have the words to describe it, but just seeing the game in motion will convince anybody that art style is more important than raw graphical power.Likewise I’m not a music major either, so I can’t dive into the technical reasons behind why the music is so good. The soundtrack runs the gamut from slow somber tracks for the nights spent exploring Yongen-Jaya, to intense boss themes, and jazzy battle tunes. There are some true standouts that still hit me hard to this day after hearing them in their original context. I can listen to almost any song off this soundtrack anytime and never get bored of it. Everything stated above is just my opinion. I know over the years it has become trendy to hate Persona 5 and the Royal version for various reasons. However for me, this game hit at just the right time in my life and it hit me hard. I flat out hated JRPGs and Anime before playing this game, I thought of them as just “weeb ♥♥♥♥” and said that they “weren’t for me”. I only tried Persona because I had friends tell me that they loved it and that I would probably love it too. I went in with lower than zero expectations and came away not only willing to play more JRPGs, but also to watch anime that I had never given the chance before. For all the reasons that I have tried to list in this review, I was left completely floored by an experience I thought I was going to hate. I ended up loving the characters, the world, the gameplay, the music, the art, everything about it. It was the best possible experience to have as an introduction to the genre. I think a lesser game would have repelled me off and I would have kept believing that games like this just “weren’t for me”.I started writing this review intending to just say “game good”. I didn’t post that though. I wanted to make sure that for a game that had such a profound impact on me, I had a review that could possibly convince somebody to play it. I don’t have any delusions that this will be the top rated review on the steam page. It is more than likely that nobody will ever read this. If by some chance you do see this though, and you haven’t given this game a shot, I implore you to please give it a shot. If you don’t have friends like mine who pushed me into playing the game, let me be that for you. This game is worth taking a chance on.

_childDocuments_.review: : I had the game on xbox gamepass and recently Bought the game on steam thanks to the spring sales and managed to move my save files (so steam total hour does't reflect my full playtime of around 133 hours)and ooooh boy best decision i ever did!Persona 5 Royal is the game that made me enter the Persona Franchise and it never left, Everything from the Artstyle, The Story, The Characters and Especially the Music(composed by Shōji Meguro alongside the Beautiful Voice of Lyn) makes you immerse in a Beautiful depiction of Tokyo and it's Districts, Spanning from Shibuya to Akihabara to the new addition Kichijoji and more.The Artsyle oozes with originality, I have never seen such a Unique Player Menu in my life, the sharp contrasts between red and Black is dominant (especially in the menu) with the unique blend of anime and comic style. The persona design are awesome and the characters outfits fits their theme beautifully. The Music arrangements are perfect, The Acid Jazz genre fits perfectly with the story of the Phantom Thieves and The royal music additions are the best. My favorite ones are; "Beneath the mask" "I believe" "Rivers of the Desert" "Last Surprise" "Whims of fate" "Butterfly Kiss" and "life goes on"The Story talks about Rebellion against society that has been distorted by desires, and those who have the biggest distortion they have their own "palaces" (a unique take on dungeons)and as the job of us Phantom thieves we need to steal their heart that is formed like a treasure in the palaces and let them confess their sins. All palaces  have their distinct artstyle and I never found them boring thanks to the nice addition of puzzles that makes it more enganging. Also you have "Mementos" which is a more classic take of dungeons and it manifests the distorted desires of the Public.The Characters are very well written all with their unique backstory and especially they feel so close and real that you can't believe they don't exist, maybe that was the intention for Atlus after all, the MC can be our self projecting he doesn't talk much and we do the dialogue choices, The Major strength of Persona is the Social Link system and this one is the best, especially with the additional 3 social links for royal. The game heavily emphasize to do social links and that's really important, especially if you want to unlock the new Third Semester, Also gives to your party members new Upgrades and Abilities and "Awakenings" that will strengthen their persona. Plus you have other confidants that give you passive boosts for your Party. Oh and if you want "more" than a simple friendship for a female confidant you can! on my first playthrough I chose  without cheating because she is my ideal type and the ideal Fit for Joker IMO, but you can choose whatever you want to see fit.(On a side note about romances: you can also do Harem but you are in for a treat in the end so I won't suggest :P)There are 2 characters that made me Cry a Lot. Especially one that felt so close to me, because it resembled that type of friend that you really want to save but he refuses and wants to carve his own path alone selfishly.... if you want to know the name for me it was  A character so well written and characterized with a tragic backstory.Persona 5 Royal is one of those experiences that pushes the video games as a work of art and it really made me change how I am living my life, It helped me change my fashion style, how I approach people and removed a big part of my shyness.It made me really appreciate the friendships I have made along my lifetime and pushes me to strengthen their bonds with the one you are closer, because in the end of the day they will be there for you always, like you were always there for them and that I am really grateful.10/10 Kasumi Best Girl

_childDocuments_.review: I've already beaten the original on PS3 and 4, as well as Royal on PS4, so I will mainly be critiquing this based on the quality of the port and other changes made to the original. If it's not already evident, I like the game quite a lot.The port overall runs fine overall, with some odd dips in areas with lots of NPCs like Shibuya (and I'm assuming Kichijoji later on in the game is the same), that seem to be CPU related as changing the graphical changes doesn't affect performance what so ever. I would've expected slightly better performance on a system with a 5600x, RTX 3070, and an NVMe m.2 SSD. But hey, at least in less densely packed areas I can manage 4k 120fps just fine on my 3070!The textures appear to be AI upscaled, which does help with sharpness in some regards, like with the bustup images for characters heads, etc, but also has some side effects like weird color banding issues in some scenes. I think it would've been better to go with a more selective approach rather than just upscaling all the textures, as it negatively affects some of them.However, I think this is overall a decently competent port that delivers a version of the game that's improved over the PS4 version. The new console versions seem fairly decent as well, but I think the PC version is definitely the superior version of the game.Given the games overall reputation I think it's good to go in with your expectations in check, the beginning is a bit of a drag and it takes a while for the game to get going, but it's absolutely worth giving a shot at least.also yoshizawa a best, anyone who disagrees is wrong :^)

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing entry in the JRPG landscape, blending story telling, time management, and turn-based gameplay beautifully. This is definitely my 2nd favorite entry in the series after Persona 3. However, the balancing leaves something to be desired.The early games is well managed, giving all difficulties a separate and defined experience. As you progress you may notice that encounters just don't gain strength even close to what you do. By late game, having both boost and amp skills is enough to one shot most enemies, even when hitting their resistances. Both hard and merciful feel no different to normal, and with the damage buffs in on merciful it can feel like engaging with the games systems is more of a punishment than a reward.What this game pulls me back with is its real world section. The gameplay here is the series best, while having the best overall cast of character, outside of just the main party. The abilities gained from confidants gives even more to the system, I just wish they were in a game that could handle them without becoming a cake walk.Overall and amazing game with a lot of content. I look forward to 100% completion.

_childDocuments_.review: The consensus I see in the reviews of this game is that it positively affects your life outside of the game as well, and I wholeheartedly agree. Somehow, a game like this has given me motivation that I have never experienced elsewhere. One of the big ways it does this is with the use of time. The most free time you can get allows you to do two things per day, and early on the game warns you to make good use of your time. At the end of my first play through, I hadn't yet managed to max out my friendship with all the people you can meet, I only barely maxed out my social stats, it left me with so much more to see. But even if I couldn't do everything I wanted to with the time they gave me, I wouldn't have done nearly as much as if I slept through the free time in the evenings.Not only does this game visually demonstrate why you should use your time, but many of the songs heavily encourage you to chase something. Follow your dreams, you can make an effect on others' lives, don't give up. A large message of this game is that the goal is to "Help people in need," and it feels almost as if players are the ones in need, even if they don't realise it.And honestly, I'm not gonna tell you to get this game, get it if you think you might like it. But even if you don't get it, or maybe can't get it, I think listening to the OST is also an experience in itself. During quarantine on an average day of online schooling, I decided to start the P5 OST in its entirety, including the P5R songs, and I was crying by the end, despite not knowing a damn thing about how the story goes. This game truly does feel life changing. It absorbs you until you finish it, and leaves you with a fresh new perspective on life. I started it early January, and only finished it early July. In this time it has become my favorite game, and I will be playing others in the series shortly. I hope you can get as much out of this game as I did :)

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off by saying that if you are not a fan of really long game's that are 80% text then I CANNOT recommend this game. But if you are by some chance a masochist who loves to spend more than 80+ hours on a game which more than half of the game is about reading then oooh booyy this game is for you.The Visuals are really stylish and every moment you spent looking at the game you would constantly think "Daaamn that looks good" or "I should totally start dressing like this character". There are a few animated scenes which are also really nicely done. The Design in regards to the enemies and bosses is really badass and it especially shows the twisted and wicked side of the so called villain character which you are supposed to change their heart.The Story is the so called meaty part of the game and it starts off way differently than Persona 4 (In 4 pretty much everyone was pretty neutral or nice to our MC and it was the basic trope of the new kid coming to town). Persona 5 flips that ♥♥♥♥ over and starts you off by literally making you live in an attic while your guardian is constantly nagging you not to do stupid ♥♥♥♥ or he will kick you out (and treating you like the criminal bastard that you are). The class and teachers themselves also treat you like trash and no one wants to befriend you or anything like that.The themes are also very adult this time around (exploitation, status abuse, sexual deviants, etc) which is very welcomed for the series and I truly am glad that Atlus started throwing more adult themes into their games.Gameplay wise this is a pretty standard JPRG with a lot of dungeon crawling and puzzle segments (they threw in some stealth mechanics which were too overpowered in my opinion OR entirely useless).The so called Palaces of the bad guys are pretty distinct and you can navigate pretty easily in them without any trouble or too much backtracking.The part that I did not like was the Mementos. That ♥♥♥♥ was visually almost the same and the navigation was incredibly annoying.It even becomes worse by the end game due to the fact that if you did not spend a lot of time in mementos before (doing side quests ,etc) then you will have to WASTE(YES  WASTE) a lot of your time reaching the end of that ♥♥♥♥ (which can be incredibly long and tedious and you gotta do it in 1 go). The mementos ♥♥♥♥ really pissed me off (even if you literally can just run over the easier bosses if you are a higher level than starting a battle phase).Creating new Persona's was also pretty fun and you get to experiment mixing and mashing them with a guillotine lmao (but not at the start since you will be a low level scrub who does not have the required level to make a Persona).The Soundtrack be boopin and moopin and foopin(younger generation is this how you become cool?).The music is pretty great and when there are fights it gives you a pretty good rush and pumps you up to kick the enemies asses.The calm and chill moments with your buddies are also nicely done but my only regret is that the soundtrack is not that long and  for the 80+ hours it becomes wayyy to repetitive until you start playing songs from youtube.Finally, this game in my opinion is really too bloody long for it's own good. While the Phantom Thieves could have been written much better, this game has some of the most interesting side characters in the franchise imo. Characters like Iwai, Sojiro, Kawakami, and Maruki honestly carry the game. The soundtrack slaps, the UI and art style is beautiful, voice acting is perfect, and the gameplay is objectively the best in the franchise. Palaces are a massive improvement over P4 dungeons, and there are way more side activities you can do than in any other Persona game. Not only is this my favourite Persona game, it is my favourite game of all time. Even though it's flawed, I'm sure you'll still have a very good time with it on your first playthrough. If you would want to replay it numerous times, I recommend you do so with mods, at least the ones that completely rework the difficulty. Either way, if you're at least a tiny bit interested in P5R, then go for it and buy the game now. I 100% recommend it and honestly, most of the problems this game has are only really noticeable if you are mentally deranged just like me and put over 1K hours into this damn singleplayer game lol.tl;dr game so good I haven't touched grass in months 👍

_childDocuments_.review: As cliche as it sounds this game changed me as a person.I first played the original game on RPCS3 back in August of 2020 a little over 3 years ago. I didn't know anything about the game other than Joker was in Smash and one of the characters looked like an Inkling from Splatoon. 2 weeks and 100 hours later it took its place as my second favorite game of all time. This game sucked me in with its unique half life sim, half dungeon crawler gameplay. What made it so good was each part interacted with each other. You build relationships with people to game abilities in the meta verse and complete missions in mementos to continue confidants. At the time turn based combat wasn't really my thing. I found it boring a lot of the time. But this game somehow made me enjoy it. The one more system is what made it so fun for me.The art style was nothing like I've ever seen before with everything so flashy, stylized and quipy.Up until this game I didn't care for stories in video games but somehow this game pulled me in like no other. I was invested in the first arc in the game and after it (and every subsequent one) I kept asking myself: "what happens next?" The Third Semester was easily the best part of the whole game. It has the best story arc and dungeon in the whole game. It's writing even made me go through a mild existential crisis. I won't spoil it, but just know; this was the only game to have a boss fight make me cry.After beating this game, like many others I felt hollow. All those friends I made, lives I've changed and the world I lived in and the story I was apart, it was all gone. I've had a few games leak a few years from my eyes before, but this game had me sobbing. Both from sadness and happiness of just how good this game was. Every time I hear the credits theme I remember those feelings and get goosebumps.As mentioned at the beginning this game changed me as a person. I got to live a life as a good friend, someone who was nice, people liked, was good at things and made an impact and led others. I wanted to live that life too. Without getting into detail, I wasn't a great person when I first played Persona 5. Not a terrible person, but there was lots of room for improvement for myself. I reflected on how I acted throughout my life and made sure that I would actually become a better person. And I'd like to believe I've succeeded in that part.For as much as this game gets a bad reputation from some of its fans I truly believe it's best to ignore that and just play the game. This game is one of the best and probably one of the most important games ever made. So if it wasn't obvious by now: PLAY. THIS. GAME! I don't care that it's upwards of 100 hours because every damn one is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Its finally here,after 6 years of begging, disappointment and vain this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game finally release on PC.. if you like JRPG or Persona 4 Golden then this basically an evolution of that, more stuff to do, more engaging gameplay, stylish visual,  and this also the Royal version which basically the "Golden" version of Persona 5 with all the DLC and more!.The port is great so far although i saw some weird animation bug where character transition between animation change abruptly, FPS locked to 120 but thats more than enough in my book at least more than what i got played the old one in the ehem "alternative" method long time ago if you catch my drift, you can play with keyboard and mouse quite well but controller is always recommended.For those who don't know. Persona 5 Royal is basically a mix up between the sims and RPG where you need to have a school life like studying, taking exams, making friends, getting part time jobs while also conquering dungeons, fighting enemies, leveling up your level,  beating bosses and all that RPG jazz, it sound weird but it coexist nicely in the games.The battle system is turn-based but with a twist where you can exploit enemies weaknesses or getting critical hits to get one more turn and you can do this until all the enemies are down and you can perform so called "all out attack" that basically wreck havoc on the enemies so any Battles basically revolve around identifying weaknesses and exploiting it or debuffing enemies to then inflict Technical damage which basically the same as weakness but with a chance to trigger one more turn, and Persona's is basically your Pokemon where you can use their abilities in battle and so on, you can get them by either recruit them in dungeons or by fusing them together.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the WORK OF ART which has been polished to the very last detail.As an old-time Persona fan such as myself, I absolutely can't RECOMMEND this enough!It's beginner friendly and especially an ideal choice if you're planning to get into the franchise.Not often are there RPGs which deviate from old-era styles to a real, city life experience. From train transits, street walkways to underground stores, not to mention the jazzy-vibe of the cafe; really capturing the essence of how city life should feel like!The best thing the game offers is its broad spectrum of things to do! I find myself being indecisive of whether I want to continue bonding with different characters (considering they're all pretty well written and their social progression is what makes you want to spend more time with each character!), talking to different NPCs to discover more about the world of this game, enhancing different stats that allow you to unlock different aspects of the game with each rank (yes, you need a higher level of "GUTS" to talk to that pretty girl you had your eyes on.)or just the JOY of being able to interact with almost everything! Each option bringing a new surprise and never the "last".If you're an old persona fan like me, I'd suggest not comparing this game with the older titles and letting it be its own independent masterpiece. - The battle mechanics follow the same format as before except they are aesthetically fluid with more battle options that make it quite entertaining!- AHH the SOUNDTRACK, MY BELOVED. if there's a game with the name "SHOJI MEGURO", you bet your arse it's going to BOMB! heck, if nothing else appeals to you, trust me, the soundtrack will, because you'll NEVER SEE IT COMING!- Like I said earlier, this game offers a wide variety of things to do, you can enjoy the city life experience both during the day and night which HUGELY improves how many areas you can interact with. It's indescribable how much comfort this game brings to me by enabling me to do things in game which normally aren't possible in real life AND you get to play as the transfer student and experience school life once more; even though that trend never left Persona games, it never got any less entertaining either! ( would be interested to play as a student in university next..)If you've read thus far, I'd be baffled if you haven't already bought this game.This game may not be 100% perfect but trust me, it's quite hard to overlookthe fact that with every BRUSH STROKE, DESIGN, CODE and SCRIPT, this game was made with absolute passion, It's an honor to even be able to experience this game. A MAJOR thanks to Atlus for continuing to make these brilliant games!Lastly, don't be an idiot like me and be so mesmerized by visuals and artworks that you neglect the strain in your eyes from glaring at the screen ;D

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite game now. I didn't even realize that I had missed the bonus content though, in retrospective it would have been easy to do , so I reccomend looking that up to go sure. It was the best game even without the bonus royal content anyway.Everything about this game is a 10 if you ask me. I have never in my life seen a game with such an astounding visual style as this, even the menu has more soul put into it than most triple a games nowadays. The game is beautiful while retaining its characteristic "stylish" style. That's kinda the only way to describe it.  I do have to say that the real world looks a lot better than the "metaverse" parts of the game, although there are certainly exceptions to that as well.It runs amazingly too. In my 80 or so hours I never once even noticed a slight drop in an area or so, and I was running it at 120fps on highest quality settings, with a 2060 super. This just proves how astounding the visual style is, for it to look that good while also being not too graphically demanding.Man, the story. I loved everything about it, I always wanted to come back to it after stopping for a day, and I always was excited about what would happen next. I love every one of them, they are all amazingly written, which says a lot, because in a lot of media I see there are some really annoying characters, which luckily isn't the case here. There's not much I can say without spoiling here, so go play the game yourself.The music absolutely stunning. But this game somehow even tops that game. Seriously, the music is so good. Every soundtrack is a jam, I found myself randomly feeling the music all thoughout the game. I'm sure you've heard this game's soundtrack somewhere before already.All in all, this is an absolute must play for everyone who is even remotely interested in anime or RPGs. Sell your grandma's fridge if you don't have enough money.

_childDocuments_.review: Adult themed Pokemon featuring teenage protagonists who rip their face off to summon an manifestation of rebellion against the mask forced upon you by society to delve into awful peoples minds, rip their metaphorical yet real in an alternate dimension, heart out and force them to change. All in the style of a Gentleman Thieves.You enter an alternate dimension which generates as a dungeon of the awful persons mind. Four person party turn based combat. Each party member has a 'Persona', the manifestation mentioned earlier, which they can use the abilities of, or attack directly themselves (Melee AND Guns!). Your main character has the ability to take on masks of other distorted souls they find, allowing for hot swapping your team of summons for the flow of combat. Lots of smaller build up over time for combat for smaller features like passing an extra turn to another party member, however the big mechanic is the Press Turn system Shin Megami Tensei is known for - Hitting a weak point, get an extra turn. This applies to your enemy as well.The other half of the game is a life sim. Do different teenage activities to build personality stats: Guts, Kindness, Knowledge... ect. This is also where you mingle and form relationship bonds with others through a lot of small side stories while you are in the human world. These stories level up as bonds and grant you benefits. Each bond has different traits, but all of them give you extra experience for each level when fusing your summons together. Which is also a thing. If you like JRPGs, you'll love it. This game absolutely oozes style and that style will hold up well into the future. If you like Pokemon, hopefully you're able to handle adult themes. Abuse and suicide are topics in the very first part of the game. Also you execute your pokemon to make them into other pokemon. This is creature fighting and collection, not raising (outside of the grinding sense). A majority of your Persona power will come from fusing them, so your party changes often.I'm a Persona 4 stan all the way, but I can't deny P5 has gone well beyond my expectations for the original release on consoles, P5R only adds more cherries on top.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, Persona 5 is a great game with charming characters, varied gameplay and an awesome soundtrack. However, this truly recommendable game is buried in another game - a hulking behemoth of pointless mechanics, bloated dialogue, and baffling design decisions:- While I do like the premise of being a Thief of Hearts, the execution of the main storyline isn't quite up my alley. The game isn't as eerie as Persona 3, neither as much fun and shenanigans as Persona 4, nor a romantic take on villany as the original Arsene novels. Instead, Persona 5 is a story about rebels - not the dangerous kind, mind you, but the kind of rebels that decide not to eat their veggies at dinner.- There are too many characters, each with too little time in the limelight. It doesn't help that the initial characters, those with the most screentime, aren't exactly the most interesting ones of the bunch. There's hardly any personal relations or team-building between characters either, so it feels like you end up with a group of acquaintances rather than close-knit friends.- The dialogue is shallow and repetitive. At times, you get textual recaps of recap dialogues, both right after the recapped event. Other times, there's half a dozen me-too lines, one from each person in a scene, without any relevant contribution.- The confidant dialogues have always been more of a guessing game, but it is particularly bad this time around. The dialogue regularly doesn't even hint at which answer might be right at any time. I think the fallacy here is the idea that answers must fundamentally be "right" or "wrong". Why not have different answers steer confidants into different directions, instead?- Persona 5 takes weirdly specific inspiration from earlier installments, right up to individual jokes and certain plot points.- Balancing is completely broken. You overlevel quickly, even without grinding, by just killing enemies you come upon. In turn, combat becomes easier and easier towards the end, which makes the final fights just feel hollow. And that is even without using the overpowered skills of former DLC personas to one-shot everything.- A lot of mechanics are useless or redundant. For example, many pass-times have so little benefit (meditating, laundry, training) that they just aren't worth spending your limited time on. In the same vein, skill cards are a low-effort replacement for persona fusion and SP-restoring skills and accessories work around the need to conserve energy in palaces.- Naming your character was supposed to help immersiveness back in the day. With ever more voice-overs, this just doesn't work out. When everyone refers to you but by "he" or "him", this feels weird and forced. It's not as if your every decisions had any major impact on the story, anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: 25+ hours in, Persona 5 Royal is truly a good entry point for someone just starting in the Persona/Shin Megami Tensei series. Here's why:(review coming from someone who has grinded both Persona 3 and Persona 4 on old platforms such as PSP, Playstation 2, and Playstation 3)- There is no direct correlation between each series. You can literally play which number you prefer but my recommendation would be Persona 5 > 4 > 3- Gone are the days where there's a need to emulate this game in order to be played. It's almost a dream come true to experience this game in 120 hz in PC.- The game (Persona 5 Royal) is much much much much more forgiving than its predecessors. You start off with a lot of money, items, even OP high-level Persona, and costumes which normally you don't get. There was a time that MC can get one-shotted by a normal floor monster which would lead to a Game Over unlike in P5R that you can just restart the battle/go back to the Safe Room. Oh, and no frequent SP regen/save point if there's a nearby floor boss/mini-boss. - This is the least grind-[iest] among the three in terms of Safe Room and save points where Persona 3 is the most grindy.- Persona 3, for me, gives a lot more challenge, complexity, and RNG compared to the other 2. It would go down for me as one of the greatest JRPG games I've ever played in my life.At this point, I'm just here to enjoy the story and the gameplay of P5R but for someone that is just starting with P5R, the other 2 is sure to delight you as well and even more than this one.All hail Persona and Shin Megami Tensei!

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal builds off the original game's core and makes reasonable changes to present new challenges to the player while attempting to interweave a new narrative into the plot with the introduction of two new characters. For the most part, one of the two new characters was integrated into the plot much more profoundly and reasonably than the other, who felt like they were adjacent to other characters and only seemed to be a character that existed when interacting with the protagonist of the game. There may be reason for that but it despite the efforts, it only alienated the character and made them feel more slapped onto the story rather than emotionally significant to the game. Gameplay wise, this is one of the most stylistically creative turn-based games I've played. Even if I already played the original Persona 5, I can't help but admire the work put in by the artists and graphics team to make a JRPG look so uniquely sound. Adding on the funky jazz-inspired music that plays during the game and a generally compelling story, it's easy to understand why the original game was so popular and how this new version really does improve upon it.I will say that at times the game does feel strangely dissonant in its themes, particularly with the handling of the character of Ann. I don't want to go into more detail given important plot points that may be spoiling early game story, but I will say the presentation of her character in the remainder of the game from her costume to the behavior of other "good" characters seems to pretty tone deaf to her role in the initial chapters of the story.The characters overall really do sell the game's story in a fairly convincing manner, with each bringing their own sense of heart, humor, and tragedy to the story. I do recommend the game for others to play, and it's a game that can be platinumed in a single playthrough if you follow a tight schedule, or simply explored enjoyed for what it does offer players. That tight schedule can be off-putting for players who are seeking a more combat-flavored experience rather than slice-of-life simulator combined with a JRPG game.

But I say this with temperance due to how I disagree with some of the philosophical conclusions the developers seem to want you to "get" (especially at the end). Those of you reading this in posterity and aspiring to be civil servants will understand why I say this, those who don't most likely won't. Nevertheless, this is a game absolutely worth spending your time on (not to mention the non-trivial trivia you garner). I now even know where the Japanese term "Baozi" originated from, though I'm not quite sure where I'm going to use such knowledge yet!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Best game of all time 10/10 just buy it. They somehow made the perfect game even better. Do NOT skip any dialogue on your first play through. It is insanely worth the price at around 100 hours per play through.Probably one of my favorite games of all time. I only have 57 hours on steam and have probably around 400 more on PS4. I try-harded and got all of the achievements on my first go. The royal edition adds so much to the game and I would definitely recommend this version to all new-comers. I would however also warn people who want to play the rest of the persona series to start with different games as none of them will feel as clean as this one. Story: The story of this game is set in Japan and is so fantastic that I wont even say a thing about it. Just do not skip any dialogue, look at youtube videos about it or spoil yourself. You will hate it. The character development for most characters is really nice to see and is usually very natural. Gameplay: The game is an RPG where you take control of personas which are basically like pokemon. You go through a story dungeon experience some story and go through the next story dungeon. Each of the dungeons are extremely memorable and do not overstay their welcome. There are some changes the royal version made that made previously very boring and unfun dungeons extremely cool. At the end of each dungeon there is a boss which in the royal edition also get a new phase when compared to the original persona 5. There are a bunch of elements which different personas can be weak to and the point of combat is to buff yourself up, hit weaknesses and either befriend or defeat the enemies. Since it is a JRPG there is a twist to the game. The twist being that the other half of the game is a social simulator where you forge bonds with your friends and teammates and others in the real world to assist your escapades in the dungeons. You also have to manage social stats which allow you to progress the social bonds with characters and do things in the world. The game starts off kind of slow. The tutorial ends on the 2nd of may where the first dungeon is used as a tutorial for everything. I PROMISE IT GETS GOOD.Music: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Atlas sound team is just crazy. I would highly recommend the soundtrack on spotify as you can kind of get the vibe of the game. I have nothing more to say than that some of the tracks are really upbeat, moving and some just out of this world. The music is used very well in game too and it never feels like your are forced to listen to the same song over and over and over again. I think 3 of my 100 hours on my first play through were just listening to the music in the background. Design: The game is stylish as hell. Every single menu, piece of UI, character, attack, area, city, dungeon and persona is designed extremely well. Each of the dungeons are visually different and explore really unique themes. There are a couple of completly animated cut scenes and attack moves which are really cool. Negatives: When you finish the game, depending on how invested you get, it will really be OVER.To conclude, get it. Do yourself a favor and get this game. It was the sort of experience where after the credits I thought, "Wow, its over.... Now what?" I will probably never forget this game and some of the soundtracks still give me goosebumps when I hear them. 10/10 TO GET TO THE TRUE ENDING YOU HAVE TO Even after 500 hours I still cant find the Ginza line ;-;

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much hype when it first came out in 2016.  Plenty of people wouldn't stop talking about it, and it's pretty clear that quite a few gacha games featured a crossover with this game in an attempt to make bank.  Clearly, the game did well enough for people to think milking it for nostalgia would print moneyPersona 4 was pretty cool, I guess, but it did get pretty annoying when some enemies showed up that were immune to everything.  Persona 5's combat is better at least.  Even if you hit an enemy that resists that element, you get the typical RPG "less damage and they won't get knockdown or anything like that."  Not "the game proceeds to punish you for your stupidity."  Yeah, that might seem easier to some, but to me it makes the game much more enjoyable.I also really enjoyed the demon negotiation part of this game.  Like Shin Megami Tensei, if you have the persona already in your party, the others will give you items, or improve your persona's exp and so forth.  You can also sort of talk your way out of continuing fights that way.But after 39 hours of playtime, I'm not particularly enamored with this game.  Don't get me wrong, it is not a bad JRPG, but it seems to lack the narrative heart and soul that Persona 4 did.  And Persona 4 was kind of annoying.  I'm also the kind of person who dislikes raising sims with a passion, especially when they are vague, and I hear Persona 3 is better about that but I'm not biting into that game for a while lolzIf you love a soundtrack that oozes style, this one's decent.  If you love themes, plot and the like, get Persona 4.  This one's gameplay is better than 4 but not "unique" enough to me.  All depends on how you feel I guess.  After playing a bit of Reload, I've slowly soured on Royal, and thus I feel others need to be warned too.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the original Persona 5 on the PlayStation 3 and it truly was an incredible game, easily top 3 my favorite games ever. However, after revisiting the series with Persona 5 Strikers in 2021 and this year with Persona 5 Royal... I cannot say how much a anime-style JRPG has changed my life. Sounds stupid, but this very series of games made me hold on to my real life friends even more. I couldn't wait to play this game, especially because I was busy with final exams when it released. But now I coudl play it freely.Game-wise, I loved every single second of it. Even though it's the third time I did the story (P5 normal playthrough and NG+, alongside this one), I am not bored. Insane. The story is truly immersive, long, perfectly-paced and just overall a treat. The characters just seem so real to me, it truly felt I made some amazing friends, which made our departure in the end the more painful, but you know, don't be sad because it ended, be happy because it happened. P5R adds some spice to the bosses and combat, disabling the Reaper Flu Season glitch from the original, adding Jose in the Mementos for more rewarding grinding and also the third semester, the last chance to finish up some remaining confidants, as it's customary for remastered versions of Persona games.I adore this game.Oh and also Futaba Sakura is THE best girl, she's literally me.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Royal stands as an enhanced version of the critically acclaimed Persona 5, developed by Atlus. Released in 2020, it redefines the boundaries of what a "director's cut" of a game can achieve. With its expanded storyline, additional characters, refined gameplay mechanics, and stunning visual enhancements, Persona 5 Royal offers both familiar comforts and exciting novelties to both newcomers and returning players alike.Storyline and Narrative Depth:At its core, Persona 5 Royal maintains the gripping narrative that made its predecessor a standout title in the RPG genre. Set in modern-day Tokyo, players assume the role of a silent protagonist codenamed Joker, a high school student who becomes embroiled in a clandestine world of supernatural phenomena. The game masterfully blends elements of high school drama, supernatural mystery, and social commentary, creating a rich and immersive narrative experience.Royal introduces a substantial amount of new content, including an entirely new story arc centered around the enigmatic character, Kasumi Yoshizawa. This addition not only deepens the lore of the Persona universe but also provides fresh perspectives on existing characters and events. Moreover, Royal expands upon the original's endings, offering players more choices and consequences that significantly impact the overall narrative trajectory.Character Development and Relationships:Persona 5 Royal excels in its portrayal of characters, each with their own intricate backstories, motivations, and arcs. From the charismatic leader, Joker, to the charming but complex confidants, every character feels well-developed and essential to the overarching narrative. The game delves into themes of identity, justice, and redemption, exploring the personal struggles and growth of its diverse cast.One of the game's standout features is its Social Link system, renamed Confidants in Persona 5 Royal. These relationships not only provide gameplay benefits but also offer deep insights into the lives of NPCs and the protagonist's own journey. Royal introduces several new Confidants, including Kasumi Yoshizawa and Takuto Maruki, each contributing to the game's themes and character dynamics in meaningful ways.Gameplay and Mechanics:Building upon the solid foundation of Persona 5, Royal introduces various gameplay enhancements and quality-of-life improvements. Combat remains turn-based, with players summoning and commanding Personas—manifestations of their inner psyche—to battle enemies. The addition of new Personas, skills, and combat mechanics adds depth and strategy to the already engaging gameplay loop.One of the most significant additions is the inclusion of the Thieves Den, a customizable hub where players can interact with characters, view artwork, and listen to music from the game. This feature provides a welcome break from the main storyline while offering additional rewards and content for completionists.Visuals and Presentation:Persona 5 Royal retains the distinctive art style that has become synonymous with the Persona series. The game's vibrant colors, stylish character designs, and visually stunning environments are further enhanced by improved graphics and animations. From the bustling streets of Tokyo to the surreal dungeons known as Palaces, every aspect of the game is meticulously crafted to create a visually captivating experience.Furthermore, Royal boasts an exceptional soundtrack composed by Shoji Meguro, featuring a mix of catchy pop tunes, atmospheric melodies, and intense battle themes. The music not only complements the game's aesthetic but also enhances its emotional impact, drawing players further into its world.Conclusion:Persona 5 Royal stands as a shining example of how to enhance an already stellar game. With its expanded storyline, deep character development, refined gameplay mechanics, and stunning presentation, it surpasses its predecessor in nearly every aspect. Whether you're a longtime fan of the series or a newcomer looking for an unforgettable RPG experience, Persona 5 Royal is an absolute must-play title that sets a new standard for the genre.

The game does have a slow start but getting through it isnt really that hard and once you finally start playing a part through the story the game holds on and never lets go until the end.

The only thing it really had going for it was Akechi and the Rival archetype, but most of that comes from Royal.  Then again he just felt like Adachi Junior. The main cast excluding Sumire was just so forgettable or made me want to pound my head against the wall.  First of why was Ann, a victim of grooming/Sexual assault confined to just jokes about her body or her being the dumb headed blonde. Even in her social link it does not do her any justice. Just horrible, now I know why people ♥♥♥♥ on the writing of women in persona games. Makoto and Haru, are just there, so forgettable. I even forgot about them once in the later game. Especially Haru, she has like zero screen time half time and felt like a rushed last minute decision in the development of the game.  Ryuji was okay, honestly just felt like a flatter mix of Kanji and Junpei. Yusuke, I enjoyed him he felt fun and was a breath of fresh air in the cast. Morgana, I absolutely adore morgana. Overall the first 100 hours of the game before you hit royal are actually so laughable, forgettable and boring.  I didn't feel amazing or invincible during any of the game unlike P4 and P3R. I just felt so bored and I wanted the base game to end. Royal:Royal is an attempt to make the game better, keyword an ATTEMPT. I see what they were trying with Maruki. They were trying to make a social link to go along with the main antagonist. The problem is I did not care for him at all. The game really forces you to care about him. I didn't see him as Joker's main antagonist. He's just there whinning and complaining running away from pain, which sounds good on paper. He wants to escape pain and wants to make a reality away from pain, but He has no meat to this, he's so flat and one dimensional nothing really attracts me to him. Probably because he wasn't in the original game and so they had to find ways to put him in the game. Sumire is actually pretty good! I enjoyed her social link and actually wanted to see more of her! Honestly though the main part of royal felt more like P4, but backwards. Instead of the massive edgelord Adachi, we get a ♥♥♥♥♥ aka Maruki. Maybe if they made this the original game with more time to flesh out everything, it could of done so much better. They just really throw out the games inital themes of rebellion with some half assed "you need to face real life, even if it's painful."If you want better themes go play P3R and If you want to have an enjoyable cast play P4. The glazing on this game is insane, The palaces sucks, the palace rulers are so forgettable, the cast is whatever. The half baked puzzles are just annoying and the boss fights are just frustrating. I can't believe P5 and Joker are the face of Atlus now when Chad Narukami and The goat Makoto exist.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this game... I am in awe.Persona 5 Royal is incredible in so many ways. Stylistically, musically, and narratively, it is top notch. I can't really understate how incredible this game is. Perhaps some people might find the combat lacking, but truthfully the combat is just a part of the gameplay of Persona 5 Royal. The real meat of the game is the time management/visual novel gameplay, which involves maxing out your "social links," which, while they do give you bonuses which help with combat and progression, also allow you to better get to know the characters of the story. I could sit here and talk about all the amazing things in Persona 5: the unique and varied designs of the characters, shadows, and persona; the many different narrative themes of Persona 5's 100 hour long plot; the satisfaction that comes from late game Persona crafting when you have essentially unlimited resources to try and build the best Persona you can. I mean, it says a lot about this game that the biggest criticisms I can come up with are things like: 1. The game arguably has too much content, I 100% it in 150 hours and there are still many challenges for me to complete. 2. There are so many different forms of progression that on normal the game becomes too easy too soon due to lack of balance (advice: if you are enjoying Persona's combat, wait to get Ryuji's social link to Rank 7 and don't grind too much; also, if you are a JRPG vet who wants a legit challenging experience on your first playthrough, I would set the difficulty to Hard as soon as you feel you'e learned the ropes). Around halfway through you pretty much have to actively avoid breaking the game balance. So yeah, absolutely incredible game, 10/10, don't spoil it for yourself. If you love JRPGs, and maybe even if you don't, you're gonna love this.

_childDocuments_.review: First review ever:  Really good game and it's going to be one that sticks with me. Please bear in mind a "10" for me is an all-time favourite game and I'm a harsh marker, so I cannot emphasize what a good time P5R was. For some context: First time Persona player, completely new to the series I picked up P5R on sale as it's something I had my eye on for years. Big spoilers ahead in the writing section as I have to talk about story a bit, so do avoid if you are thinking of playing.Let's start with the best bits - the music is FANTASTIC and dare I say carries the game a little. There's so much personality behind each track and even the admittedly insanely repetitive combat music is still good enough not to get tiring. I showed great restraint only adding about 5 tracks to my favourites list. Funky, rocky, instrumental goodness with a few excellent vocal tracks. The visuals also make it to the top of the best bits, as P5R REEKS of style and flair and is overwhelmingly crafted in the visual department. Everything looks seamless, smooth and polished. Brilliant.The characters are probably the next best part - each seem fleshed out, diverse and have their own repertoire of motivations and desires. When something happens, they are written consistently in how you'd expect them to react. This is surprisingly difficult to pull off and most games ♥♥♥♥ it up, but P5R does it really well. Hanging out with each character is fun and building up confidant ranks with your chosen favourites is a good time. Nice one.The gameplay is solid - combat is really well-designed and feels a bit like Pokémon crossed with any other JRPG turn-based battle system. Focusing on finding enemies' weaknesses is pretty fun, critical hits are satisfying and the variety of spells and abilities is refreshing. The (early game spoiler:)  adds a great collection mechanic which could be fun for certain completionist-type gamers. I would say the best bit of combat is in the "showtime" mechanics and joint attacks, which are consistently a blast to unlock and use - they also appear rarely enough to keep them fun and interesting. I have SOME gripes about the game allowing the unlocking of extremely powerful DLC personas for free, as I feel that may ruin the experience for some people. I made an effort not to use them until late-game, where I felt their inclusion was warranted.This is where I docked a point, because overall the story is "pretty good" but not as standout as the other elements above. I think my overall thoughts were some of the writing choices were VERY questionable, and here is the big spoilers so please avoid if you haven't played: Also:. These points definitely aren't dealbreakers, just perhaps the story could have been managed a little more succinctly. I also felt the story was a little juvenile for me at points.Consider buying this game if you like JRPGs, particularly those with social mechanics (such as Fire Emblem) - it is a long game and will keep you busy for a while. The experience is well worth it and I have a great time. That said, I wouldn't pick it up for full price and would wait for a half-off sale or something. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 is a role-playing video game where the player takes on the role of a male high school student, codenamed Joker, who lives out a single year while attending school in modern-day Tokyo. It was released for PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4 in Japan in September 2016 and worldwide in April 2017. It was published by Atlus in Japan and North America, and by Deep Silver in PAL territories. An enhanced version featuring new content, Persona 5 Royal, was released for PlayStation 4 in Japan in October 2019 and worldwide in March 2020. It was published by Atlus in Japan and worldwide by its parent company Sega. Persona 5 Royal was later released for Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S in October 2022. This game is visually attractive and stunning, the interactions between characters are mostly goofy and have a good sense of humor, nothing felt too out of place. The music (as with all persona games) is just an absolute pleasure to listen to and I thoroughly enjoy it while playing. The addition of the "Thieve's Den" in the Royal version of the game I really loved, getting to play the funny little card game with the characters I know and love has brought me a good amount of joy. The customization of it is also a big plus.Furthermore, the character design is phenomenal, it truly encapsulated the character that it's presenting even at a quick glance (which is what good character design is). I genuinely love everyone's **spoilers read to next paragraph to not get spoiled** Metaverse outfits and I recently purchased one of the outfits for myself to cosplay as.I have had MANY bugs happen to me throughout the game, including but not limited to; the insides of masks Z-Fighting when I look at the character, horrible horrible horrible lag when I even dare to think about tabbing out. The port to the PC is lackluster to say the least.Aside from the bugs I faced and the small gripes I have with this game I still consider it one of the best games I have played. The characters are charming and the character design is stunning. The stunning style of this game never ceases to charm me.After (Finally) finishing this game I have to say that, the story is genuinely moving and inspiring the ending really moved me especially and if you have any doubts about purchasing this game... Be shaken free of those doubts and commit, although the game is not perfect it is more than worth your time and hard earned money.

_childDocuments_.review: Four hours in. This isn't a game. It's a manga. And a tedious one, at that. In the four hours of playtime, 3 and a half were just clicking passively through a never ending story. Very, VERY Japanese. Kid smokes a cigarette and brings disgrace upon himself and all his ancestors.  zzzzzzz....  The characters are very unlikable. The female teacher who won't stop whining about her life... The schizophrenic sidekick who is screaming in rage in sentence 1 and laughing in sentence 2... This "manga" isn't redeemed by it's gameplay, either. The game is full of loading screens, that go on forever, until you press a button. Except it never tells you that it's waiting for that. You just have to find it out for yourself... eventually. The color palette is really obnoxious. Like an antacid commercial threw up all over your screen. Lots of neon purples and blues and reds. Combat is complicated and largely unexplained. And in the first 4 hours, dead easy. Almost no enemy survived the first round.This one was a disappointment, to be honest. I guess if you are determined to get it, I'd advise waiting for a deep-deep sale. It will lessen the pain 4 hours later when you get tired of waiting for it to get fun, and quit.Uninstall this one and don't look back.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love jrpg and anime it's an amazing entry point into SMT/Persona franchise. I have played many hours on PS3 back in the day, it was my first Persona game ever. I like the cast/story of P4 more (maybe cus I watched P4 anime before P5 came out), but graphics, UI and accessibility wise P5R wins by a long shot.The good: * Awesome Jazzy soundtrack with loads of bangers* Interesting cast of troubled teens and adults* Story is intriguing and did hook me in well when I first played it (my save on PS3 clocked around 50+ hours before my ps3 up and died)*The fact it came out for PC at all, getting Atlus to actually port it felt like a dream can true since I can finally get to where I was.* Awesome Monster/Shadow designs, they are one of the main appeals of the game to me.*Royal added lots of new content compared to original P5 for PS3 & 4. It's basically Persona 5 GOTY edition.* Cool anime inserts in key story moments.The bad:* Some writing feels very bad and not thought through. It's mostly great but there are times when I roll my eyes at the anime logic or jokes.* Serious mental health problems of some side characters don't get proper closure or the characters just don't mention them much after the story arc closes (is Shiho okay?).* The tone tries to go for a gritty serious story, but feels like a lot of big problems just go away through power of being special friend team or brushed aside. The way some scenes are written gave me whiplash due to how different in tone it felt to initial crime drama feel.The ugly (things which are a turn off for me and might be a tough sell to certain players):*Some female Phantom suits feel way too skimpy, but I get why they design them like that (sex sells or whatever)*Similar to big jrpgs, it can fee exhausting to play due to requiring lots of time to get through the story and grind. Since I lost my save I've restarted it a few times but it felt tedious to replay.*You're kind of railroaded into dating your teacher, or at least have options of getting close with adult women (might be a touch disturbing for people sensitive to that). The whole Takemi situation screamed sus to me, but good Doc herself is a decent woman I guess. The things you do for the team  just because your talking cat forces you to.Still, if you are okay with fanservice, anime tropes and somewhat clumsy handling of certain topics it's a great time it's great value for money.. You can potentially get 100+ hours in completionist run.Despite eveything I still can't wait to go on dates with Makoto, chill at LeBlanc with Sakura family and finally meeting Haru. My old ps3 save cut short just before getting her playable. Oh, and there's new stuff/semester and all new characters to meet too, if you're coming in as somebody who played the original version.Solid Persona series entry, even though I like their earlier Persona games more. Now will you please port your older psp/PS1-2 games too, Atlus! People will love it guaranteed, I know I will since I'm fan of your franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game for people that aren't into RPGs. It catches you with a pretty interesting story and introduces you to the gameplay in a really nice way that is well paced. I don't usually finish RPG games, but I have replayed the original (non "Royal") Persona 5 multiple times, and now gone through this one. In general I would say Persona 5 has been one of my personal favorite experiences with games, and Royal is just a generally enhanced version of the original.This game paces itself by going between the story, daily life and battle portion in chunks. Not only are battles intuitive for new players, it has some unique twists (e.g. "Baton Pass") compared to other RPGs, which make it more fun. The daily life part provides a good break from the main story and battle allowing you to explore the city and improve your stats and relationships to help with battling later. The soundtrack and the general art style of the game is also great.From the point of view of someone coming from the original, I generally like what they added to Royal. The additional content is nice and more time is given to interact with things in daily life. One highlight for me is how Mementos is less boring with its new mechanics. There's a new semester, which provides some interesting additional story. While I was playing it I found it nice, but I have no strong opinions to share here, I may wanna go through it again to better understand how I feel about this part of the game. Either way it's more Persona 5 to play, and I like Persona 5.As far as the PC port is concerned, I have no complaints aside from the existence of Denuvo DRM, which I hope it gets removed as soon as it's cracked just out of principle. That said, I did not observe major performance issues. The ability to play at 120 FPS is good and the game looks pretty sharp after tweaking the settings.With all that out of the way, as much as I like this game, I personally dislike a few things, most of which comes from the original game and is still present on Royal. Some opinions I would highlight are:- The reliance on googling and the network feature to experience the whole game is probably one of its major downsides to me. This was especially an issue on the original game with the laughably low amount of time you actually had to do things, and it's good for new players that Royal actually gives more time to players in daily life and more opportunity for earning 'points'. However it still doesn't solve the root issue, where the dialogue choices you need to make make seemingly no sense most of the time and random trivia questions that you couldn't possibly know most of the time leave important point progression up to chance. I'm very conflicted about this because I do not know what a solution if any would be applicable to this issue.- The writing of this game is both its pro and con. I'll not go into detail as to avoid spoilers, but the characters here start really strong, there's some really heavy plot with emotion, like the stuff going on with Ann for example. But when their major plot is done and they've been fully introduced, these characters go downhill and become a bit of a joke, like their whole story is dismissed. There are really cringe points in this game, like what happens with Morgana well later on in the game. Somehow, the story still works and still has impact, but it's far from perfect.- Fusing personas is an interesting mechanic, but one that you'll either like or hate doing as a beginner. It's something I personally somewhat avoided on my first playthrough, and the thing is that for better or worse, this game is just about easy enough on normal that it won't punish you for not taking advantage of it often. I was hoping for quality of life improvements on Royal like showing all registered personas in the Fuse by Result section, or showing duplicate skills existent in other Personas, but neither of those exist in this game.- Some of the bonus content that was previously DLC in the vanilla game can be way too OP. The bonus Personas for instance, you can already summon a level 90 Persona at the very start of the game, which makes no sense. You'll need to personally avoid using these to not break the game balance further.To end, just some thoughts on the difficulty, or rather the lack thereof I had while progressing through this playthrough as a returning player. On Royal, 'Merciless' is still a messy difficulty that ends up easier than its supposedly easier counterpart 'Hard', so I chose to personally stick to 'Hard' on my playthrough. I think that Royal has added things that benefit the experience of new players, but they have in the process made the game easier for returning players seeking challenge. Some confidant abilities () are especially unbalanced and will help with that. I personally wish there was a proper step above Hard, one where I would not have to add restrictions on my own to make the game more challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: At least it's finally over. This game targets a very specific audience and I'm not part of it. I think the appeal must be the repeating patterns and casual, predictable interactions with random people. I believe there's a big nostalgia market for people who want to re-live the structured school period of their life where they had time to kill, future held promise, and life didn't entirely go to ♥♥♥♥ yet. In that way, if you did like P4 and want another 150 hours of more or less the same thing, it might be right down your alley. Skip the rest if you don't want to get upset.The protagonist has zero personality and acts as a blank slate for the player. If conversation choices between "I'll be counting on you" and "You can do it" actually mattered for the story, this would almost qualify as a visual novel. There's probably 15 hours of an alright A plot in the entire thing, but it's buried in 150 hours of filler where you need to allocate your time to dull social interactions and lame activities. The characters have little personality or real, human emotion outside the three bullet points used to describe their role in the game. The game attempts to tackle complex social issues like domestic abuse and suicide in an almost insultingly simple "cheer up" fashion. If that doesn't work, ask magic people to beat the bad guy up in the magic land and the issue is resolved.The combat is a glorified Rock, Paper, Scissors interpretation and barely evolves throughout the game. The best thing about it is if you're higher level than your enemy, you can spring at them for an instant kill without the actual combat. This also lets you quickly ramp up levels, loot and infinite money.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 bursts onto the scene with a unique blend of rebellion and style.  You take on the role of a high school student by day, navigating the complexities of social life and academics in a fictionalized Tokyo. But beneath this seemingly ordinary facade lies a secret identity: a Phantom Thief.  Donning a mask and a swagger, you and your crew infiltrate the twisted mental palaces of corrupt individuals, aiming to steal their distorted desires and force them to confront their wrongdoings.The narrative in Persona 5 is nothing short of captivating. It tackles mature themes of corruption, societal injustice, and personal growth, all woven into a story with high stakes and memorable characters.  The turn-based combat is polished and strategic, letting you unleash powerful Persona attacks alongside your teammates in dynamic battles.  But Persona 5 is more than just combat.  In your free time, you can explore the vibrant Tokyo districts, soaking up the atmosphere, forging bonds with your confidantes, and engaging in a surprising variety of activities – from working part-time jobs to batting cages and catching the latest movie.  These social elements aren't just fluff; they strengthen your Persona abilities and unlock new options in battle and story events.The presentation is phenomenal.  The game boasts a striking visual style that blends sharp anime aesthetics with a rebellious flair.  The soundtrack is a masterpiece, pulsating with energy during battles and dripping with atmosphere during exploration.  The characters are a stellar cast, each with their own quirks, struggles, and motivations that make them feel real and relatable.Persona 5 is a lengthy experience, but the world is so engrossing and the gameplay so addictive that the hours melt away.  It's a game that will stay with you long after the credits roll, a testament to its exceptional storytelling, stylish presentation, and innovative social sim elements.  If you're looking for a deep and rewarding RPG with a unique identity,  Persona 5 is an absolute must-play.
