_childDocuments_.review: Hooooo BooooiAfter over 100 hours of game play and finally finishing the third semester i can actually join the overall discussion around this game, and i gotta say...I love itStarting off with the game play aspect, as someone whose experience with turn based combat is essentially just Persona 4&5 so far, the combat here is pretty good. Animations are fast but flashy enough to not get stale after seeing on repeat for 100 hours, and mapping the controls to each individual button on a controller (or keys if your on MnKB) makes fights faster in comparison to Persona 4's approach on scrolling through them with the D-Pad. The 'one more' mechanic not only helps these encounters feel fast, but encourages the player to use different personas in their arsenal as well as their other party members. Theres also the 'baton pass' mechanic, this is such a fun tool use and fits right in with the Persona franchises love with striking weaknesses that its a surprise that none of the other games had it. While the turn based combat is fun and easy to learn, Persona 5 runs into the same issue I had with Persona 4's combat, in fact its even worse in this case, in that the game is just way too damn easy after the first 2 dungeons. After beating the first 2 dungeons in Persona 5 most of these poor shadows just couldn't even touch me, a big reason for that is partly due to most of the personas that I levelled up and unlocked at the time having abilities that wiped the floor with these losers, and also in part to my boi Ryuji. Its already well known at this point but unlocking Ryujis rank 7 insta kill ability essentially just makes grinding a breeze. Not only do you get to just ram through low levelled shadows, but also get full exp and yen for doing so with no loss. Whilst I appreciated this at first for making grinding manageable, the monkey paw effect of having the difficulty take a nosedive made me question whether the trade off was worth it. Honestly, besides over-levelling issue, there's also the fact that Physical damage is just wayy too good, it practically wipes through shadows that don't have resistances to it and its also the only skill type in the game to have a colossal rank which emphasises just how much more powerful it is compared to the others. The bosses in this are a mixed issue as well, on one hand they have some fun gimmicks and attacks they can throw at you, but they're also far too humble when it comes to dishing out damage numbers (and i played the whole game on Hard). Bosses here fall victim to the ever so powerful physical skills and either needed bigger health pools (not to the extent of P4) or more powerful attacks to really pressure players. As it stands right now they're unfortunately fun but easy to breeze through (with the exception of Okumara). In terms of the social aspect of this game, there's not really much i can add onto that hasn't already been said before. The day to day activities of living as a high school student and bonding with your confidants as well levelling up your social stats is ridiculously addicting and embarrassingly enough I think I spent more time getting stressed out over deciding which which activity i was to spend on each day than each all the bosses combined. Getting into the flow of managing your social schedule and seeing which days you have free to spend on Mementos & Palaces (combat stuff) and which ones to focus on confidants or part time jobs is the best part of the game and makes up for the lack of challenge through the 1st quarter of the game.This game also has the best UI I have ever seen like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ why does it looks so good, seriously more Western devs need to take notes from this game because we need to break out of this 'less is more' mentality with how a lot of their UI's tend to look. The comic book aesthetic combined with the bold red and black colours make opening and looking at menus so satisfying, which is a plus considering menus are most of the combat anyway. It isn't just the UI, the entire game just oozes with style with the way that the characters and world are cell shaded, to the point where at some point I didn't even think this was a JRPG. Overall, this game was an absolute blast to play through, apart from my critiques on the lack of difficulty I would easily replay this game again on NewGame+.(also, whoever at Atlus thought it was a good idea for the extremely OP DLC persona's to be free in the persona compendium needs to be fired, like come on this game is already too easy as it i)

_childDocuments_.review: I'll probably end up writing a lot about this game, so if you want a quick review, here it is: This game was an incredible experience. Although I'm not in the same age group as the characters, I ended up identifying with them. The story is deep, heavy, but at the same time light and full of twists and turns. I was so immersed in the story that I reached a point where I’d wake up early just to play. The characters are extremely charismatic, and the story is impeccable. The game has a mind-blowing plot (especially in the true ending). And about the turn-based combat, which I thought would be a weak point—it was quite the opposite. The system is fluid and became one of the most fun parts of the game.The truth is, the first time I heard about this game, I had no interest in playing it because it was turn-based, a style I don’t usually enjoy. But, after some recommendations from friends, I decided to give it a shot. I downloaded the pirated version, ran it on a PS3 emulator, and immediately hit my first obstacle: the game didn't have a translation in my language. It might seem like a minor detail, but at the time, I had never studied another language, so even English was hard for me.Still, I pressed on, with a dusty dictionary I had at home and a translator on my phone (couldn’t use it on the computer because an alt + tab might crash the emulator), i was determined to understand what made this game so special. At first, it was quite challenging; I can say the first 30 hours were a struggle to understand what was going on in the story, but gradually, I got the hang of it, and my dictionary lookups became less and less frequent. Honestly, that alone made the game worth it for me, as it turned out to be the spark that got me interested in learning a new language, which I think is priceless.Even with poor performance and frequent crashes on the emulator (this was my second obstacle, my PC was like a potato), I played for about 90 hours and got completely immersed in the story. But when the Royal version of the game was announced for PC, I dropped everything I had done in the game so far (I was practically at the last palace) and decided to wait to play an original copy, thinking I owed it to Atlus.I couldn't really afford the game at launch, so I waited for a sale that fit my budget, but it never came. Until a friend decided to gift it to me for my birthday (if you're reading this, thank you so much, you have no idea how happy I was to receive this gift). And from then on, it was pure joy! This time, language was no longer a barrier, and the performance of this PC port was impeccable.In the end, I got all the achievements in the game, explored every detail, and enjoyed everything the game has to offer (for the second time, but now in the Royal version). Honestly, I love Persona 5, and though it’s not a perfect game, it’s definitely one of my favorites.

_childDocuments_.review: Here we go Persona 5 Royal is on PC and it didn't disappoint, one of the best rpg's released in the past few years.So what is this game? It's a unique jRPG with high emphasis on story. It has no relation to other games but shares similar lore (what you see in Final Fantasy games) so it's a great starting point for new players.This is royal version which comes with additional content which adds more hours of gameplay after finishing the main story. It incorporates additional content into the game and story very well so it doesn't feel out of place by any means. It feels like the additional content was there from the beginning.While I prefer the story of Persona 4 Golden (which was more serious in my opinion and even philosophical), I prefer the dungeons or palaces of this game, it's like day and night. Although Royal story makes up for it.You play as Joker, a teenage boy who arrives into a new town and goes to a new school where he meets new friends and discovers the metaverse. Soon Joker meets a talking cat, witnesses some shocking events at the school and the journey begins.Game consists of two different worlds – real world set in Shibuya and metaverse. In the real world you have to go to school, you increase your stats, build relationaships with friends and do other stuff which includes growing plants, fishing, playing games, watching movies, reading books, studying, making coffee and more. Every action cost time, basically you can do two thing per day.Metaverse is where you steal hearts. After you identify the person you can go to their palace to steal their heart which changes that person in real world. Each palace is entirely different both in visuals and gameplay. Exploring palaces takes time, each one of them has its quirks, some have puzzles or additional requirements and each main boss offers a unique experience and forces you to use different tactics.There are several playable characters although you can only take three of them with you into combat besides Joker. You can switch them mid-combat or at the entrance so if you see that you need to change the composition of the party, it's easy to do.Each character has their persona in metaverse and have their own costumes. While Joker can use multiple personas.Velvet room is the place where you can fuse personas to make new ones, rearrange your personas, buy new ones etc. In general it's a place where you manage your personas.While in combat, if you critically injure the monster (except bosses and tough enemies) they speak to you and you can demand three things – joining you which means that monster becomes one of your personas with its own skills, ask for money or ask for an item. You can of course just kill them.There's also mementos, it's like a common palace of all the aociety instead of one person. Mementos has many floors but in general it's just a generic dungeon and place where you go to do side requests and farm.Real world time management can be tricky when you don't know what to do. Increasing social stats is important but also increasing friendship rank with your friends opens up their side-stories and gives you abilities in metaverse. You can meet and interact with non-playable characters so you'll need to manage who to dedicate your time to well.Eventually if you rank up a girl to max rank you can become a couple or decide to friendzone her. You can go into relatioship with multiple girls both your age and older, like your teacher.You get to buy your gear (you can find some), buy/make items which heals of buffs you or debuff/damages the enemies.Combat is turn based and often requires some planning and knowledge of the game to exploit all the weaknesses of the enemies. I played on easy because i wanted story and still managed to die few times. You take turns and you have few choices each turn. Physical attack, guns, persona or item. Each enemy has its weakness to certain attack or element (some have no weakness) and it's up to you to discover them.So in short gameplay consists of real life activities and dialogues and metaverse. Don't forget that you can spend as much time in metaverse once you're there as you like and it will count as one activity.Graphically the game is quite unique. It's Atlus game, the only other similar looking game is Catherine made by the same developers. The graphics look great, amazing art-style which stands out of any other game. Palaces especially look great and it's a great leap from Persona 4 Golden where you only had mazes with identical textures everywhere.Performance isn't the greatest, especially if you turn up rendering scale. But this game is fine even at 30fps.Played on 5800x, rtx 3080/4080, 32gb @3440x1440. I had render scale on 150%, game looked amazing and very crisp although I was getting some fps drops which was weird since the game isn't a technical marvel. There's lack of graphics options.No ultrawide support obviously because there's lots of 2D images. Partially works with flawless widescreen. 2D images are stretched and you can see the void where 2D background boundaries end. Anime cut-scenes are stretched, use reshade and bind a button to quickly change the aspect ratio when cut-scenes play.Sound design is absolutely outstanding. This game deserves the best soundtrack of the year. Really it has one of the best soundtracks in the industry. After playing this you'll either go to youtube or spotify to listen to those songs.Voice acting was good too, each character sounded nice even though it's not always the case with niche japanese games.It's a wonderful game filled with 100+ hours of pure content, worth any price and is close to being a masterpiece. The story could be better and it has some weird minor performance issues but it's a must have for any rpg fan.

The competition is not even close. This is not a very well known series in the west, which is really a shame. The game has a 96 on metacritic which is incredible as an example. Seriously, I don't think I'm biased toward particularly liking persona either. The story rivals books and movies/TV shows, the music can seriously compete with things you've heard on the radio, the characters are to-die-for. The gameplay is super fun and unique. The game is super long as well (which I suppose can be a negative) so you're getting your money's worth. (as someone who doesn't like to fork out money on a game) My PS4 playthrough took 113 hours. I was playing on the easiest difficulty and trying to get through the game as quick as possible. If you took your time to really 100% the game, I can see it being 200-300 hours. If this doesn't look like your cup of tea, PLEASE give it a chance. I can not recommend this game enough. I have had 6 friends try it and they all loved it and it is their favorite game too. Please give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: My first Persona/Megami Tensei game. Heard lots of good things and I really tried to like it and it actually was enjoyable at times (first 10 hours or so?), and the OST is a banger! But the main story isn't great, and there are a lot of weird stuff in this game like a 40 year old teacher grooming a 16-17 year old into a sexual relationship. Or how the game hypersexualizes a 16-17 year old girl. Or how a 30 year old drunk also grooms the first mentioned 16-17 year old.Aside from lackluster main story and some super weird and creepy things like that, the game isn't that much fun. It's LONG. It's repetitive. There's an extreme amount of explaining everything to you as the player, over and over and over just in case you missed it the first 19 times. The combat and story isn't good enough to support it being this long and repetitive. The different characters aren't interesting enough to support it either. If you don't mind the pervy creepiness that is included in a lot of Japanese mangas/animes, and all the usual tropes and clichés from that genre, and you want to spend like 100hrs to finish the game once (a lot of players recommend multiple playthroughs...) then sure go ahead. But if you struggle with the sexualization of minors, don't like the typical manga/anime stuff, want fun gameplay and a really solid story, and don't want to spend 100hrs of repetitive gameplay just to finish the game, then you should look elsewhere.What also makes the creepy perv stuff extra disturbing is the fact that the rest of the writing is quite juvenile as if they are trying to appeal to a teenage audience... while including grooming and hypersexualization of minors. Just felt really icky and weird to me.Finally, without spoiling it, the final boss fight was hilarious (in a bad way).

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 is a critically acclaimed role-playing video game developed by Atlus that tells the story of a group of high school students in Tokyo who, as members of a secret society known as the Phantom Thieves, use their alter-egos known as Personas to battle supernatural enemies and change the hearts of corrupt adults. The game is the fifth entry in the popular Persona series and is widely regarded as one of the best RPGs of all time.One of the standout features of Persona 5 is its unique blend of traditional turn-based combat and social simulation gameplay. In addition to battling supernatural enemies, players must also manage their time and build relationships with other characters, which affects the strength of their Personas and the options available to them in battle.The game is also notable for its stylish art design and memorable soundtrack, which help to create a distinctive and immersive atmosphere. The story is engaging and emotionally resonant, touching on themes of social justice, identity, and personal growth.Persona 5 is a game that rewards players who are willing to invest time and effort into its world and characters. The game's mechanics are deep and nuanced, and there is always something new to discover, whether it's a new Persona to collect or a new character to get to know. With its engaging story, memorable characters, and addictive gameplay, Persona 5 is a must-play for RPG fans and a standout entry in the long-running Persona series.

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone tells you to try Persona 5 even if you don’t like JRPGs because it’s not like other JRPGs, they are wrong. They are wrong and you should trust their opinion less. Persona 5 has all of the things I hate about JRPGs in spades. Flavorless numerical progression that just makes numbers get bigger, hours of grinding through hordes of pointless random enemies just to make your numbers big enough to beat the boss’s numbers, mindlessly selecting the same options from a drop down list to select the same option 500,000 times, the list goes on. This is a JRPG through and through and as much as I dislike the tropes of the genera that’s not this game’s fault. It made no effort to hide what it is and it’s not the developers’ fault that some game reviewers led me astray. What this game is, is an excellent JRPG. The characters are charming and I found it easy to get emotionally invested in their personal stories. The main storyline seems simple on its face but has some serious depth in the themes it explores and real surprising cleverness at some points. The artwork is beautiful and the aspects it has borrowed from collect-a-thon games and applied to its level up system adds a visual variety to progression that a lot of JRPGs sorely lack. While certainly not a cerebral game, its combat system has enough complexity to it to allow for a little cleverness in tactical approaches to enemies. Whose number it bigger still reigns supreme, but it lets the player punch a *little* bit above their weight if they’re smart about it. If I have any complaints against this game that are not complaints against the genera as a whole, it’s that I feel like they didn’t do a good job scaling progression, especially toward the later half of the game. The bosses of each level are significantly more powerful than the mobs of the next, so once I was strong enough to deal with them I was too strong for anything to give me a challenge until the next boss. Similarly, some of the late game abilities given by characters toward the end of their individual storylines feel kind of useless once I’d progressed the game far enough to unlock them.Overall, if you don’t like JRPGs, nothing about this game transcends its genera, it readily embraces the mechanics and tropes of the genera. If you like JRPGs then I think you will find this to be one of the finest examples of the genera.

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare that I actually finish a game, never mind one that can chalk up over 100 hours in a playthrough. It's considerably more rare that I finish a game twice, especially one of this length. As I dig in to my third playthrough of Persona 5 - Second playthrough of Royal, with the intent of completing it and then beginning my second play through of Persona 5 Strikers, I still feel the same excitement as I did the first time I got invested in the world. This is my favorite game of all time; the cohesion of theme, music, gameplay, story and art direction is perfect, and each of those is spectacular in its own right. It is not a perfect game - the story can be cringe, the characters and dialogue are typical juvenile anime tropes, there can be a lot of grinding on the harder difficulties, etc. But it's about as close as I've seen, and I hope in a year or two I'll be making a fourth playthrough when I purchase the game again on the Switch. This is the quintessential, long-form, turn-based JRPG experience.

Break free from the chains of modern society and stage grand heists to infiltrate the minds of the corrupt and make them change their ways! name: Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp
detailed_description: DANGANRONPA S: ULTIMATE SUMMER CAMP is now on Steam! Summary Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is a massively enhanced version of Ultimate Talent Development Plan, the boardgame from Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony. The stage is set at the tropical resort of Jabberwock Island, and players improve their characters via the 'Development (Boardgame),' 'Battle,' and so on. Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is the dream crossover of Danganronpa characters with over 1,000 event scenes, and offers new swimsuit outfits for all characters. Also, players can now collect collab illustrations drawn for merchandise in the Mono Mono Machine! ・Game features Development (Boardgame) The main part of the game in which players will develop their character over 50 days (50 turns) of summer camp on Jabberwock Island. Roll a die to determine how many spaces to move. An event will be triggered depending on which square the character lands on. Each character has various stats, including level. Character stats improve by leveling up, stopping on a Growth Square, or interacting with other characters on Event Squares. Bosses placed by Monokuma and monster battles triggered by Battle Squares will impede the player's path along the way. Talent Squares grant Talent Fragments, which grant characters new skills. Players will also need to acquire weapons and armor at shops and treasure chests as well as utilize cards featuring useful effects to their advantage. Battle A Battle Mode can be played separately from the Battle Squares found in the boardgame. Develop characters and form a party of up to four members and take on the 200-floor Tower of Despair where Monokuma-type monsters await. In the Tower of Despair, enemies attack in waves, and the player is rewarded with Monokuma Medals upon victory. Players need to increase their characters' levels while learning skills and gearing up their characters in order to emerge victorious. School Store In the School Store, players can spend Monokuma Medals and Monocoins they've obtained in battle to gain new characters and support items using the MonoMono Machine. Each character has different rarities, and the higher the rarity, the faster they will grow in Development mode.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a conditional recommendation; if you answer NO to any of the questions, DO NOT BUY!Have you played Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc?Have you played Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair?Have you played Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls?Have you played Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony?Have you cleared all of them?Did you go beyond clearing the games to experience character lore (free time events; minigames; etc)?Did you... at least not dislike... the Ultimate Talent Development Plan in V3?Are you willing to play V3's UTDPlan but bigger and better?Are you okay with gacha to collect cards (playable characters AND hundreds of permanent microbuff cards)?Do you love the characters of Danganronpa?Do you wish you could see more free time events between them all?Now this one's important...Is this game on SALE?!Remember, if you answered NO to anything, then absolutely do not buy under any circumstance.Also, a warning. The overarching story of this game doesn't seem to be replayable, and once experienced... it's gone. People have been known to have trouble resetting progress... reset may be intentionally especially difficult since there is a monetised option for collecting the cards... y'know, with real money (please don't actually use that thing, lol, you can get them all for free... eventually).But the lack of replay/review function for the overall story is concerning. It was actually kind'a neat...Basically, this is for hardcore Danganronpa lovers who didn't mind the UTDP in V3 (and maybe even liked it).It's a'ight and I like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Regrettably, I have been a fan of the Danganronpa series since a bunch of my friends got super into it during high school. I’ve played all of the games but never watched the anime series. Needless to say, I like the high points of Danganronpa. It’s got some really bad parts, but I’m mostly able to look over them. Hearing news about another Danganronpa entry had me excited and I half expected it to get ported to Steam eventually despite launching on the Switch initially. Since it was advertised as an expansion for the postgame dungeon crawler/board game found in Danganronpa V3, I knew what to expect going in. But what I didn’t expect was for a complete game to be inferior to what was once a bonus mode. Also spoilers ahead for the whole franchise.As previously mentioned, if you played V3, it’s Ultimate Talent Development Plan. If you need an explanation, the focus of the game is a pseudo-make-your-own RPG party member on a board game where your decisions impact your character’s level, stats, and skills. Some of the board spaces and specific turns show off visual novel-style character interactions with everyone from all 3 entries, but besides that, there’s no gameplay similarity between this and the mainline games. In the original, after making a party of characters you’d enter an RPG dungeon crawler with random encounters, boss fights, and little areas you could explore for loot, you would cycle between the two modes, making stronger characters from your progress in both the dungeon and the board game. Repeat indefinitely until you either see all the character interactions or beat the final boss in the RPG section. It wasn’t much on its own, but as post-game content it was huge. I loved wandering around in an old-school dungeon crawler with characters I liked and the unique dialogue I sometimes got was a cherry on top. I had a fair share of fun because it was a nice bonus for what was already a complete game.So how did Danganronpa S handle making what was originally side-content its own thing? The marketing entirely focused on making it a bigger experience, and it’s precisely that. But bigger doesn’t always mean better. What was once a short 15-minute experience with the board game is now a 40-minute endeavor. The only small addition is that the bosses are now also on the board. Otherwise, the drastic increase in time investment required was a major detriment to my enjoyment of the game. Also unlike V3, the game heavily encourages doing the board game with every character for both story progression and to get better characters for the dungeon. Speaking of the dungeon crawler elements, they’ve been entirely stripped away. What took its place is just a gauntlet of enemy encounters that I had the auto-battle feature plow through for the whole 100 floors. Danganronpa S rips away elements from the V3 version just to elongate the less interesting part of the game. My time with the board game segments was a never-ending grind that I was only able to get through because of how little effort it actually required. I highly doubt that most people who pick this up will want to finish it. I hated the board game so much. I would toggle my brain off frequently until I stopped on an event space that wasn’t something I’ve already seen.That leaves us with the other selling point: interactions between characters across different entries in the series. Again, this is something V3 already did but S brings in Ultra Despair Girls characters. However, I honestly don’t even think these half of these characters are interesting enough to warrant considering their interactions. Except maybe Monaca but that’s because she was a way more interesting and threatening villain than Junko was. Otherwise, I just really don’t care for the kids, bears, or Hiro’s mom. The most compelling events usually involve characters that didn’t get much screen time or some characters catching onto a detail that would be a major plot point naturally. For example, seeing that Tenko actually admires Chihiro despite their gender or seeing Korekiyo catch onto Mikan’s more controlling side. I think my favorite scenes were seeing a bunch of characters cluing into Monaca faking her handicap status. There’s minor stuff like seeing Gonta and Gundham getting along due to their shared love of animals. Besides that, there’s a complete lack of any story. What little remains is cut into tiny segments separated by hours of repeated interactions. It’s a complete tonal shift and expects you to take the plot really seriously in the final hour after playing as every character too.Also, a complaint of mine is that all of the art and music are recycled from past entries! The only new art pieces are 3 full illustrations, the cover art, and swimsuit sprites for everyone. The music is entirely unoriginal though. This is really disheartening since Masafumi Takada’s music was one of the highlights for me. I know that cutting corners by reusing content is a very common practice in game development, but when your game is almost fully composed of it is when it starts to bother me.I want to go over who this game is for in the first place. This game is for the extreme hardcore Danganronpa fans. It’s impossible to enjoy this without any familiarity because of the massive spoilers for every plot point. That’s why this game is monetized with microtransactions! Wanna play with the best possible Celeste character immediately? Fork over 100 yen and you can! It’s not actually on the Steam page, but you can go to a vending machine in-game that wants your money. I personally did not get to play as my favorite characters throughout the battle gauntlet. I never got to play as Himiko or Celeste until the very end. I could definitely see Spike Chunsoft pinching a few pennies off the impatient bunch. The sluggish nature I mentioned is likely entirely intentional in an attempt to push people towards it. Microtransactions in visual novels aren’t something I’m looking forward to seeing replicated.Danganronpa S is ultimately a time waster for the most devoted Danganronpa fans. And as someone who enjoyed all 3 mainline games, it apparently seems like I’m not a part of that group. And even to that crowd, I wouldn’t recommend picking this up. Unless you’re so desperate to see your waifu in any official capacity, you’re better off spending your time elsewhere.  If you’re hoping for more Danganronpa, go look at fan-made content. Honestly I feel as though I’d enjoy actual fanfiction more than what was passed off as official.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most bottom of the barrel, blatant cash grab I've seen in a long time, and I knew this going in, but still left disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: **Before reading this review, please keep in mind that this is MY opinion and shouldn't affect how other people view this game**Alright, so before I begin this review, I would like to say that I am a HUGE Danganronpa Fan. I've seen my boyfriend play the main 3 games and Ultra Despair girls for me. This is the reason I bought this game in the first place. Because I thought "Hey, it's a Danganronpa game and a gacha (which I also happen to enjoy)! It could be fun to see how this turns out." Even through seeing the mixed feelings about this game, I remained optimistic, and decided that I wanted to go through the entire main story before I gave my review. Here is what I thought was good, mixed, and bad with it. Good things:-New interactions with characters: As a fan of Danganronpa, I thought it was nice to see the characters in a new enviroment where they could interact, regardless of what game they were in.-Easy to pull on the gacha: If you do regular runs with the characters and do the occasional tower run, then I believe it is very generous when it comes to the gacha, which is something that not all gacha games give.-Bathing suit skins: Alright alright, of course I can't mention this game without mentioning the fact that one can see the characters in bathing suits, and as somebody who definitely likes the eye candy, I can definitely say that it was a definite plus of the game. Mixed Things:-It can get a bit too easy once you unlock the scrolls: Now I wasn't really sure whether this is good or bad, so I decided to create a mixed category just for this. So once one gets to level 20 (and every 20 tier until 100) one can obtain a scroll which makes the game a bit easier as you don't need to go to every single Mini boss to get said scroll. Now, while I do believe that it is nice so one can actually progress in the runs faster, when you get all of those scrolls, it almost feels a little too easy. Like there were runs I was done before day 20 and then had nothing to do for the rest except interact with friend tiles, and that wasn't nice. Bad Things:-Easily Repetitive: So as somebody who did every single character run in the game, I can say this with certainty. This game becomes SO repetitive after a while. You do the exact same thing just with different character. You beat all the bosses, try to beat the main (secret) boss, and get to lvl 100. You have no idea how many of my characters I got the same skills with since I knew it would work, regardless of their type. And this repetitiveness made the game so tedious to deal with.  -Only one map: This leads to my first point here which is that it is repetitive, but I believe that having one map doesn't help. Like sure, if there were different maps (or at least routes) for every character, then maybe that could help it not be so repetitive, but I feel like it could have helped. But nope. -Predictible story: Sure, maybe the ending of the story was a bit different than what I had imagined, but the overall predictability on what would happen in the story, was just too much of a bad sign for me. -Tedious tower levels: While i will say that some of the tower levels were pretty easy and a good way of getting coins, I feel like some of them just had objectives that were just...so tedious that I didn't even bother completing them. -Limited classes: There are only 3 different classes of characters, and while they do focus on different things, I feel like there should have been more, since again, it lead to a feeling of repetitiveness while playing the game.Overall, would I recommend this game? I am not sure, I don't think I could especially with how I felt towards it in the end. And the price doesn't help. I feel this could have been more of like a free game (as most gachas are), but just the fact that it costs so much for a game that after a while becomes repetitive, no. I wish there was a mixed opinion button, but hey. For now I'll just have to leave my review to help, but I will still say that I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved the Danganronpa series since I first got introduced to the insanity with Trigger Happy Havoc, and since then I've platinumed 1, 2 and V3, while also watching the anime series and OVA. I was happy to hear about another game in the series (I'm aware of Ultimate Despair Girls but never picked it up as it didn't seem to offer enough gameplay or story wise), but the store page made me hesitant - so I checked out some reviews, and one person online mentioned that it was a bit of a love letter to the series. So with that, I decided to pick it up.The game is basically the worst aspect of V3 (Ultimate Development Plan + Monokuma's Test), as the whole gameplay loop. That's the stick, but the carrot is nice and cute cut scenes of characters from all over the series interacting with each other. So essentially, you have your love of the characters and series competing with the grossness of a very grindy and not very fun gameplay loop.Not only that, but there's a shop in the main menu. While the currency for this shop can be obtained within the game, it's in pretty short supply - but never fear! There are microtransactions that allow you to get around this. >.> So that's also gross.So for all this, why am I giving the game a thumbs up? 3 reasons:1. To let Spike Chunsoft know that there's enough love for Danganronpa that we'd appreciate more games. Maybe just a bit more fun next time - more carrot, less stick.2. Even if there's way too much grind for the events you get, seeing all these awesome characters again is nice.3. This is the main reason, and why I feel like this game may be some sort of secret masterpiece. Firstly, following the ending and twist of V3, having this as the next entry - V4 as it were - is just so damn appropriate in the context of the twist. Beyond that, this is a series where despair is one of the main themes. Having our beloved series release a game that's grindy, unfun, is selling a lot of itself on fan service, and has gacha mechanics and microtransactions - is that not just the epitome of despair?

_childDocuments_.review: Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is a game for fan service and an extension of V3's Talent minigame. This is similar to Animal Crossing Amibo Festival without the toys. With a battle gauntlet RPG design. This mean there's no exploration or dungeon crawling at all in the Battle Tower section. Every Danganronpa cast is here except for the Danganronpa 3 anime. Story is about the Danganronpa cast go in Jabberock Island from the 2nd game for a summer camp trip, but Monokuma wants to spread despair. By doing so, the cast must gather Hope Fragments by completing 50 days (50 turns) on every single character. Thats all to the story. The player must collect character cards by completing tasks from both the Talent Development and Battle Tower. It is very grindy and boring. Luckily the Battle Tower mode does have a auto battle feature. There is an option to buy these cards, but its a greedy tactic for micro-transaction. I don't recommend this game.This game does support the PS4 controller and Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically a fanfiction come to life. "What if everybody lived, and they all went to Summer Camp in the Matrix together? And also Monokuma was there, and summoned wacky digital monsters to have an excuse for combat?" That's the whole premise. Either you like that idea on sight, or you hate it on sight. Playing the game will not change your view either way.Two kinds of people will like this game - If you've seen or played all 3 main games and UDG, and really absorbed the lore and the character dynamics, you'll feel rewarded by various blink-and-you'll-miss-it references to small details in those games. Or, if you WISH you could get into the DR games, but they're too gory for you to handle - you're in luck! This is truly a "everybody lives AU" where characters mention plotting bad things, and past suffering, but it's like one-tenth as traumatizing as UDG, which is, imo, as dark as the series gets in terms of on-screen dark content.A third type of person who loooooves grinding and pixel-retro dungeon-crawling and turn-based combat, and doesn't mind swimsuit models of anime characters, will also find this game worth their money if it's on sale.There's a lot left to be desired in the explanations of stats and skills. If you get impatient with the slow pace of combat progression in the Battle Mode, you'll have to look up online guides on sites other than Steam. The whole shape of this game is based fully on the V3 post-game mode "talent development" so much so that V3's character's stats are directly copied from there. There are a few typos and confusing word choices that seem to stem from the translation choice to hew closer to the JP original text of THIS game, than the English translations of the OTHER games. Unfortunately, they still make Gonta talk like a caveman. He can TOO read! :(The game DOES have a gacha system, but it is 100% possible to unlock everything with in-game battles and grinding, there is NO pay-to-win here. There's no online multiplayer at all, so if you choose to pay any more than the sale-price into the "School Store Vending Machine" you're just choosing to spend money instead of time on unlocking the content of the game. This is a feel-good "power of friendship" visual novel that touches on some dark themes, and has some light Dragon-Quest-ish combat slapped on top. It's not a mystery-solving or combat-focused experience. Uber-fans could justifiably accuse this game of blaspheming against the series' central themes. But if you're able to ignore that part, and just want to learn more about the characters and their alternate-universe friendships, and just have some fun? This might be a good time for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp is a game that almost tries to be good, but, for the most part, isn't. Let's explore the ups and downs of the game (+, +/-, -, ?):+ I love seeing all these Danganronpa characters together! I need more Akane, Aoi, Miu and so forth in my life! For reasons!+ The game board is interesting.* There are many possibilities, many variables to take into account when improving your characters**+ The game looks and sounds nice, as Danganronpa always does.+ The turn-based RPG approach is interesting at first...+/- ... but then it's always the same thing. This game is extremely repetitive.+/- * The board never changes.- Acquiring skills is painful and very limited.- **Once your run is done, it's done. You can't continue leveling up your character after your run is over.- You need to get lucky in order to be strong AND fast enough to win the fights. Oh, and bosses are usually easier to beat than the normal enemies.- Unlocking everything would take forever. So, why would I try when nothing ever changes in the game anyway? If you really want to unlock everything, enjoy the random mono machines! Grinding! Grinding everywhere!- Everything comes and goes so fast, there's barely any time to get anything meaningful out of anything in the game.-- There's no story here, which is very, very fatal. _childDocuments_.review: It's ironic that so many people trash on the game for not being good, while for me it's the only Danganronpa game that feels like a game, rather than a visual novel with mini-games, with decent replay value. But I'm just part of the minority, who love the game as it is, and that's fine.I'll keep it brief. The game is designed to be a grindy fan-service board game rpg gacha. There is no actual plot to speak of, you can expect plenty of character interactions from across all 4 games, including Ultra Despair Girls, although there won't be any character development to take note of. You basically level up your characters individually by playing the development mode, or in other words, the board game where you roll a dice and land on panels, like in Mario Party games. The main goal is to level up your characters as much as you can, so they can be used as a traditional turn-based rpg 4-man party in the Tower Climb Battle Mode, in which your goal is to beat the waves of enemies, so you can advance further in the tower, until you reach the boss of the stage.There are 3 different types of vending machines, like in the previous Danganronpa games, from where you can unlock different characters in the exchange of in-game currency. This is the part which many people trash the game for, because it has an integrated microtransaction system in place, from where you can get X currency at the exchange of real life money. I need to note that unlike Freeware games, you can unlock everything there is to unlock in this game without paying for any microtransactions. There is no content locked behind paywalls. But the grinding can become excessive and tedious for some people.To conclude, I mainly play this game when I want to relax, unwind and turn my brain off, while vibing to music or podcasts. I love the game for what it is and do not regret my purchase at all. I'd only recommend you to get this game if you are looking for a:1. Happy world Danganronpa setting where all characters interact with each other.2. You like, or at the very least won't mind, grinding in video games. 3. You are looking for a simple, colorful game to unwind to.

Despite this tepid attempt to ruin it, I don't think it sustained any meaningful damage.Game shouldn't exist/10

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I played through UTDP in danganronpa v3, beat the entire thing and even grinded for extra couple hours to develop all the characters in the game for a little bonus dialogue. In this game, I can't really fathom the amount of grind compared to the UTDP mode. You have 68 characters, each one takes 15-20 minutes to develop, there's a high chance you roll garbage even if you have U-cards, so the development doesn't guarantee further tower progression, the amount of pulls you get is minuscule with how many hours you have to put in, I just have massive hoyoverse games Vietnam flashbacks in this one and it's sickening. And the few fun interactions in each 15-20 minute run don't make up for the soul-draining non-stop grind. Too long, very boring, filled with frustrating RNG and insanely slow progression which is already driving me crazy 20 hours in (I spent approximately 40-50 hours in Ultra Talent Development Plan and only started losing my mind after clearing the final boss, where I decided I'd develop all the remaining characters for the achievement).

_childDocuments_.review: (Link to my Youtube play-through at the end of the review for anyone wanting to see a sample of gameplay before buying)Might as well post a review for Danganronpa S: Ultimate Summer Camp, since I've currently sunk 9 hours or so into this game and am pleasantly enjoying it for what it is. First thing you need to understand: this is a spin-off AU, and as such it has no relation (as far as I'm aware) to the actual story of the Danganronpa games. It's basically Danganronpa V3's Ultimate Talent Development Plan board game mode, except greatly extended and set on Jabberwock Island (Danganronpa 2's setting).Second thing you need to understand: this is a very grind-y sort of game. In essence, you pick a character from Trigger Happy Havoc, Goodbye Despair, Ultra Despair Girls or V3; you take them into Development Mode (the board game), where you level them up and develop their skills; then you can use your developed characters as party members in the Battle Mode, which is like an old-school turn-based RPG. All throughout this, you earn special Monocoins which can be used to unlock other characters or gain useful items/hype cards (which boost certain characters) from the various different MonoMono gacha Machines available in the Store mode. Rinse and repeat...So far, I've only managed to get to the fourth island in Development Mode and haven't even yet got to floor 10 in Battle Mode, so even after 9 hours of play there's still more for me to get my teeth into. The key point being: if you're not into games that do require you to grind a fair bit, then Danganronpa S may not be to your tastes. In essence, you have to develop your characters, get Monocoins, unlock more characters plus items and hype cards to improve their stats, develop more characters, redo characters you've already developed from scratch in order to make them even better, then push a bit further in Battle Mode, and so on and so forth.Personally, I've been enjoying it. Even if you're not into grind-y games, you might still like Danganronpa S just to do the friendly events in Development Mode, where you can get to see some of your favourite characters interacting with one another.There are only several other minor points worth noting:-If only the Ultra Despair Girls cast line-up for this game had also included Yuta Asahina and Fujisaki's dad, right? On the plus side though, thank god Haiji Towa wasn't included.-Everyone gets swimsuit sprites! Unfortunately, I feel like the designers got a bit bored once they reached V3's cast, as some of the Killing Harmony crew have the blandest swimwear of all time...-Mukuro is still disguised as Junko. She doesn't get sprites of her own self. Feels bad, man.-If only we could also have had some of the Danganronpa 3 anime characters starring in this too, right?But with all that said and done, I do recommend Danganronpa S - particularly if you enjoy the franchise. It's worth a shot, even just to see all your favourite characters having a nice, fun time and not having to worry about them trying to murder one another...

_childDocuments_.review: Overview:My relationship experiences have been puzzling and frustrating. While I am genuinely interested in women and open to emotional and sexual connections, my responses when approached or proposed to seem contradictory. Despite my longing for a committed relationship, I often find myself sabotaging potential connections over seemingly minor details.Self-Gaslighting:The term "gaslighting" traditionally refers to manipulating someone into questioning their reality. In my case, it’s an internal process where I convince myself that I don't like someone based on small, often insignificant factors. This self-sabotage feels like a defense mechanism, although it’s not clear what it’s defending me from.Patterns and Triggers:The triggers for my self-gaslighting vary but are typically minor and somewhat superficial, like the person's age or a small habit. Once triggered, I start rationalizing reasons to reject the person, convincing myself that the relationship wouldn't work out, even if I initially felt interested or attracted to them.Possible Reasons:Perfectionism: I might have an unrealistic ideal of what a partner should be, leading to rejection of anyone who doesn't fit this mold perfectly.Fear of Vulnerability: Despite not fearing commitment consciously, there might be an underlying fear of emotional vulnerability or intimacy that causes me to push people away.Self-Protection: I might be protecting myself from potential hurt or disappointment by ending things before they start, using minor flaws as justification.Overthinking: A tendency to overanalyze and overthink minor details might be causing unnecessary doubts and leading to self-sabotage.Past Experiences: Previous relationships or emotional experiences might be influencing my current behavior, leading to a pattern of rejection as a coping mechanism.Seeking Solutions:Understanding this pattern is the first step toward breaking it. Here are some potential ways to address the issue:Self-Reflection: Spending time reflecting on past relationships and my reactions to them can help identify underlying fears or unrealistic expectations.Therapy: Professional help from a therapist can provide insight into why I self-sabotage and offer strategies to change this behavior.Mindfulness: Practicing mindfulness and staying present can help reduce overthinking and allow me to appreciate potential partners for who they are, rather than focusing on minor flaws.Communication: Being open with potential partners about my tendencies can foster understanding and patience, allowing for a more honest connection.Conclusion:While my tendency to gaslight myself into rejecting potential partners is frustrating, understanding the possible reasons behind it is crucial. By addressing these underlying issues and working on self-improvement, I can move towards forming the meaningful and committed relationship I desire.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a rocky start, but the biggest issue regarding long loading times on launch has been resolved via an update.  There still exists some bugs and annoyances particularly during the first hour or so of gameplay, but at this point I can officially change my rating to a "Recommend" with some caveats:Game initially launches in 720p Window mode.  Alt-enter puts the game in full screen mode, but with black bars on the top and bottom and bezel-like art on the sides due to my display being 1080p.Graphical and other "System" options not available to change until after the approximately 30-40 minute intro/tutorial sequence (about 8-10 minutes if you fast skip).No easy way to replay the intro/tutorial if you skip so that you can set your graphics options properly.Xbox Controllers (wired or wireless) don't appear to be auto-detected by the game in regards to on-screen prompts.  An option exists in the "System" menu to change to the desired controller prompts.  Unfortunately, the selection does not save after the game is exited and option defaults back to "Keyboard" on the next run.  On a positive note, the Steam Deck properly sets this option to "Steam Controller" automatically and the prompts match with no further configuration required.Once I got past these issues and into the game proper, I've found that Danganronpa S is both playable and enjoyable.  This is especially true for fans of the series that can embrace the "what if" scenario and appreciate character interactions that couldn't have happened previously for various reasons.I do hope that Spike Chunsoft will issue further updates that address the minor bugs and annoyances that still remain.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a recycled version of the Talent Development Program from DRV3. It's not as high quality, but it is definitely easier to get through than DRV3's, so I can at least appreciate that. I guess my disappointment stems from me thinking it would have leaned more VN than the regular bonus mode. (Hell. I would've even been fine if they just did another version of the bonus modes from DR1 or DR2. Actually, why DIDN'T they just make it a huge Love Across the Universe??? That would've been  ). I wasn't a fan of it the first time, and I'm still not. I mean, the reason I love the games so much is because of its original gameplay and story, NOT the bonus mode gameplays (who the hell is raving about that...) The only fun thing about those is the bonus content and/ or the possibility of romancing a couple of your favs.As for the bonus interactions themselves... the writing is so  ... OFF. It's like they got someone who had a general idea of what the character's shtick is and ran with it, so you just get a lot of one-note dialogue. (This is especially true for Tenko). Of course, it's not all bad, but it just makes you wonder why they would release such a half-assed game. In the beginning, I was actually super hyped, even more so when I was seeing new CGs and sprites of the characters, but that was short-lived.A thing it does right that I wish they had done for the DRV3's Talent Development Program was that you could actually go back and look at the interactions you were able to get through development.Now, imagine my disdain when they brought back Monokuma's Dungeon 2.0 😌.. I was not happy to see this again, but I was elated to see it wasn't the same time-consuming BS as DRV3's. The only thing you have to worry about is pulling U versions of the characters and maxing them out. I'm not well-versed in these types of games, as I'm not at all interested in them, so I can't say for certain if I'm just really bad at them, but from what I experienced: It's still quite time-consuming and you have to be extremely lucky in a playthrough to complete each goal within the 50 days. Numerous times, I have played with the intention of maxing out the character and completing the goals, but because of a series of bad rolls and luck, I'm wasting my days on lowly Monobeasts and am hardly getting any progress on my stats, hence barely even reaching the 3rd island by day 45.Dear lord and DON'T get me started on when the Monkubs show up throughout my playthroughs. Tell me, why in the hell they made it so that the Monokubs--who are there to provide support and NOT be evil--are able to  impede on my progress????? Imagine my horror and  when Monosuke and Monokid show up and take a portion of my Monocoins when it's already hard enough to get a good roll to land on a shop or even earn a Shop Card; or, how about when Monodam shows up to forge my equipment and somehow he instead greatly decreases my stats when I just bought an upgrade with my dwindling Monocoins??? Are you kidding me?! I must be missing something, but I would think this game would have put a focus on fun and interactions with characters rather than making that incredibly difficult to do. Speaking of rolls, when I want to focus on landing on friendship squares, jfc I'm left wondering why they didn't separate it like they did in DRV3? 1 for Talent and another for Friendship, at the very least. It would make it so much less of a headache if I was able to land on more Strength or Talent Fragment squares, but of course that would be too easy... and why would it be easy? 🫠 It's not like this was supposed to be a celebration of DR's 10th anniversary and a gift for the fans..... Oh wait.But, at least if it gets too hard collecting all the presents, art, interactions, Ns Rs Ss Us, you can just buy 'em ! 🤪  🤠 Let's make an in-game purchase, shall we? 🤡 (Can you tell this game's made me insane in the membrane?)Overall, because I have an unhealthy obsession with Kokichi and an undying love for Danganronpa, I continue to play the game. However, if you're not the biggest fan and/ or Tobyn Jacobs when it comes to their favorite Danganronpa character, I suggest pretending this game doesn't exist AT ALL. _childDocuments_.review: This game is based on the Ultimate Talent Development Plan from Danganronpa V3. For the most part, it is about the same game. detailed_description: Dead Space Digital Deluxe Edition The Dead Space Digital Deluxe Edition includes the base game and 5 exclusive cosmetics (3 Unique Suits and 2 Suit Textures). It’s everything you need to look your best while surviving the horrors aboard the USG Ishimura. About the Game The sci-fi survival-horror classic Dead Space™ returns, completely rebuilt from the ground up to offer a deeper, more immersive experience. This remake brings jaw-dropping visual fidelity, suspenseful atmospheric audio, and improvements to gameplay while staying faithful to the original game’s thrilling vision. Isaac Clarke is an everyman engineer on a mission to repair a vast mining ship, the USG Ishimura, only to discover something has gone horribly wrong. The ship's crew has been slaughtered and Isaac’s beloved partner, Nicole, is lost somewhere on board. Now alone and armed with only his engineering tools and skills, Isaac races to find Nicole as the nightmarish mystery of what happened aboard the Ishimura unravels around him. Trapped with hostile creatures called Necromorphs, Isaac faces a battle for survival, not only against the escalating terrors of the ship but against his own crumbling sanity. IMMERSE YOURSELF IN NEXT-GEN SCI-FI HORROR A sci-fi horror classic returns fully rebuilt from the ground up with elevated visual fidelity and 3D atmospheric audio. From the frighteningly detailed rooms and workspaces of a slaughtered crew to the eerie atmospheric sounds of a desolate spaceship, you’ll explore a stunning sci-fi setting full of unpredictable and tense moments without interruption. UNRAVEL THE MYSTERY ABOARD THE USG ISHIMURA What starts as a routine repair mission for engineer Isaac Clarke and the crew of the USG Kellion quickly turns into a battle for survival as the truth behind the horrors onboard begins to unravel. Following an expanded narrative experience, uncover the dark secrets behind the events aboard the USG Ishimura through the final logs of the ill-fated crew and your encounters with the few survivors that remain. IMPROVISE TO SURVIVE Confront the nightmare aboard the USG Ishimura with genre-defining strategic gameplay. Repurpose and upgrade Isaac’s engineering tools to creatively defeat enemies with precision.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to review. Ill start off by saying I never played any of the past dead spaces, but maybe now ill give them a try since they are on gamepass. The environment is gives off a good sense of fear, with its dark atmosphere and great sound design, especially when using the 3D audio option and atmos. The story seems to run in "cliche" territory, but still pretty interesting, and graphically it looks nice. However, the performance  is very poor. There are frequent microstutters and freezes, even right when you 1st get into the main menu, and the framerate is all over the place. I will go from anywhere from 45-100+fps, but nothing is steady or constant. It just bounces all over. This is running on the settings it defaulted to, which was everything medium with fsr2 turned on, at 1440 native resolution, so what resolution its actually running at idk. This is running on a r5 3600x and rx6600 with 64GB ram, installed on an nvme drive. The constant framedrops and stutters really take you out of the immersion that they clearly put alot of effort into, which kind of ruins the experience. Its hard to really say if I recommend this game or not considering the performance issues. On one hand it seems like it would be a good playthrough, and its got me interested in going back and playing the originals. However on the other hand, the issues it has literally cant be ignored when your freezing for 2 to 3 seconds at a time frequently. You could have the greatest game made, but if it dont run, or run properly, then that really dont matter, does it? Just look at what happened with the last of us. Maybe if you had a beefy, overkill pc and can get a stable framerate, youll have a better experience. I know what I have dont compare to some rich boy build, but ive had no issues running anything else I play and I would say I have a fairly decent pc thats comparable to what the average person is going to be running on. Best I can say is check it out during the trial and see for yourself.

It'd be fine fighting a room full of necromorphs then somehow picking up kinesis or going through a door into a narrow hallway with nothing can almost crash my game.-------------I have now finished my first playthrough and the stutter in the last few chapters was even worse. The stutter would start and restarting the game fixes the issue in the same areas so it's not like a particular area is too graphically demanding. _childDocuments_.review: Motive did me proud with this remake. An amazing remake of the original game, fixing core issues that plagued the original Dead Space while adding some new twists and changes on story and gameplay in awesome ways. .The new "Flesh and Bone" system that was introduced now makes each weapon in your arsenal much more deadly and useful - now you may want to use your Flamethrower/Force Gun to strip away the flesh quickly and then swap to your Plasma Cutter/Line Gun to snap those bones with a shot or two - instead of 7 or 8 shots. Now the game also rewards you with better ammo economy (and more health kits if they die before getting to you) if you use the system properly to your advantage - this also means you can sell off the ammo you may not need and use the credits to buy more Power Nodes.The Bench upgrade system has also been improved -  now you no longer have to spend Power Nodes on useless nodes that don't give any benefits like in the original game for your upgrade path - now it feels meaningful and awesome to spend your Power Nodes as each node now will give an upgrade in some sort of way.Some parts of the story and characters has been changed but I can say they still fit in very well in this remake - and some parts actually surpassed the original writing. A solid recommendation for the OG Dead Space fans and any newcomers to the series!

_childDocuments_.review: Terror Factor: 10/10 - Dead Space is a testament to the survival horror genre. Its ability to instill a profound sense of terror through its claustrophobic environment, spine-chilling enemy design, and unpredictable jump scares is unparalleled. It's not just a game; it's an ordeal that tests your courage in the face of unimaginable horrors.Overall: Dead Space is not for the faint of heart. It masterfully blends science fiction with survival horror, creating an experience that is as terrifying as it is unforgettable. The game pushes the boundaries of fear, making you dread every step, yet compelling you to push forward. If you’re a fan of horror games, Dead Space is a must-play title that will haunt your nightmares for years to come

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space Remake is a reimagining of the iconic survival horror game that terrified players when it first launched. Set aboard the derelict mining spaceship Ishimura, players once again step into the shoes of engineer Isaac Clarke as he battles grotesque creatures known as Necromorphs while uncovering the dark secrets of the ship. With updated graphics, enhanced gameplay mechanics, and modernized controls, the remake aims to deliver an even more immersive and terrifying experience for both newcomers and fans of the original game.Pros:Updated graphics and visuals that breathe new life into the haunting atmosphere of the Ishimura.Modernized controls and gameplay mechanics that improve the overall experience while retaining the essence of the original.Enhanced audio design and soundtrack that heighten the tension and horror of the game.Faithful recreation of the original storyline with added depth and nuance, including potential new story elements.Potential for additional content and features to surprise both new and veteran players alike.Cons:♥♥♥♥♥♥ Map, these days we are used to fast travel and + a map that you can not add a waypoint to i miss fast travel other than that it's ok, Possibility of technical issues or performance problems, especially on certain platforms or hardware configurations. Necromorphs does not feel as threatning as they did in the original they do not run like crazy at you comes up to you like resident evil zombies in remake can be improvedGraphics:Dead Space Remake boasts updated graphics and visuals, with detailed character models, realistic environments, and improved lighting effects that bring the terrifying world of the Ishimura to life like never before. From the dimly lit corridors to the blood-soaked rooms, the remake aims to capture the eerie atmosphere and chilling aesthetic of the original game while leveraging the power of modern hardware.Gameplay:The gameplay in Dead Space Remake is modernized controls and mechanics, offering a smoother and more intuitive experience for players. From dismembering Necromorphs with strategic limb targeting to solving environmental puzzles and managing resources, every aspect of the gameplay is carefully crafted to balance nostalgia with innovation.Story:the storyline of Dead Space Remake is expected to closely follow the events of the original game,  With updated character models and voice acting, the remake deliver a more immersive and chilling storytelling experience for both new and returning players.Audio:The audio design in Dead Space Remake is enhanced, with atmospheric sound effects and a haunting soundtrack that complement the horror and tension of the gameplay. From the eerie whispers of the Necromorphs to the unsettling creaks and groans of the Ishimura, the remake deliver an immersive audio experience that adds to the overall atmosphere of the game.Replay Value:Dead Space Remake offer significant replay value, with multiple difficulty levels, unlockable content, and potential new features to keep players coming back for more. Whether you're a veteran of the original game or experiencing it for the first time, the remake aims to offer a compelling and terrifying experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat.Final Verdict: the most iconic survival horror games of all time. With updated graphics, enhanced gameplay mechanics, and a faithful recreation of the original experience, the remake satisfy both longtime fans and newcomers alike. EA Motive's dedication to preserving the spirit of Dead Space inspires confidence that Dead Space Remake will deliver a worthy successor to the classic horror title.

_childDocuments_.review: After the initial "performance fixes" I've beaten this game multiple times. Had around a 50-80 fps experience with no crashes. Problem is, those "performance fixes" only partially fixed the problem. The game still suffers from immense stuttering, fps drops, horrible screen tears if you have v-sync off, and now with the newest driver updates, CONSTANT crashes. The solutions I've seen from the community have temporary fixes such as deleting your cache in the game files, and although it does help, it doesn't fix the issue (at least not for me). After around 30 min of game time it still hard crashes. One crash made me restart my whole computer. The fact that the devs and EA haven't offered an update or comment to address these issues yet is honestly baffling and quite frankly worrying if they want this game to stand the test of time like the original did. If it weren't for the performance issues this would be a damn near perfect game. However, as long as these issues persist, I can't in good conscience recommend this game to ANYONE with a Mid-Tier PC build or lower. I'm on an RTX 4080 with 32GB and I still get stuttering and frame drops when going to a new area of the map. Until then, it'll just stay as yet another reminder as to why EA and anything affiliated with them is terrible in one form or another.Update : the Driver Latest updates have apparently fixed the crashing for most players. However, there are still players in the community who still have issues with regular crashes or fps drops. Until EA/ Motive themselves come up with an update or fix, I will still keep my negative review for this game due to the horrible communication or lack thereof from the people who made the game. They took their money and ran, and until they themselves update it, my points in my review still stand. Don't get me wrong, it's a great game but the stability really needs to be worked on.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't stop thinking about the way Isaac looks at where I point camera at. I know, bog standard third person video game features, seemingly every game has it these days. But, something about his high-tech welder mask that emits horizontal cold light dangles on the line between appearing human and alien. Or, maybe it's the robotic, heavy steps with dirty metal slabs on his shoulders reflecting the light bleeding in motion. It's easy to forget that Isaac Clarke - our avatar - is a human, until he grunts, cuss and stomp the pain away.(this is the part where I must clarify that while I did play the original Dead Space, I ultimately left half way through feeling somewhat unfulfilled, a very technically advanced experience and tremendous atmosphere that never managed to make me feel like I was in grave danger).-----------------------------------------------------------------------Playing Dead Space 2023 made me realize that AAA gaming hasn't progressed as much as I expected in the last 15 years. The whole "cutting limbs off" shebang remains Dead Space's most talked subject which over a decade later, only got iterated further instead of being pushed forward. At the same time, the idea of a remake that keeps "just enough" from the original is worth a debate point. After all, if we are all whole then what's the point of remaking us whole?The changes are visually visceral, the improvements are on paper, spectacular and clever. Weapons' alternative fire modes are more fun and balanced and useful. The metroidvania-lite structure introduces thrilling risk to the core loop. The changes to structure and level design make things flow better and give the Ishimura a more concrete identity gameplay-wise. The AI director is introduced to keep you on edge, create excitement through unpredictability. Enemies are tweaked and reworked to better complement the intensity and combat pacing. The "pick your poison" element built into specific rooms gives player more agency. On paper, Dead Space 2023 is a "perfect game".But that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, there's no such things as "perfect" games. You can nitpick that the base necromorphs move slower and the final boss fight is trite and easy, but got'cha like those never take away from complete packages. I don't think Dead Space is a perfect game, and it doesn't need to be so.But the thing about the game that cemented my love for it, is the contrast between Isaac in a soulless engineering suit, moving at the pace of a bulldozer, violently mowing down gratuitous creatures with coldness in his "eyes", while muttering "♥♥♥♥ this ship". This is a controversial change, giving Isaac Clarke a voice that is, from the same actor in the sequels no less. It's arguable that the lack of voice for Isaac Clarke added to the sinister beckoning atmosphere of Ishimura's stranded status, as "in space, nobody can hear you tearing apart flesh" remains constrained within these corporate backed space stations. What dirty job happened in the Ishimura stays in Ishimura. "Capitalism is a ♥♥♥♥♥", Dead Space broadly announces through various wall graffiti and text logs, even more so through Isaac's gestures of violence, which, towards the end, get even more exhausting.I think horror, at their most fullest, showcases human killing off their own self, both literally and figuratively. Like the slow descend to madness of Dani from Midsommar, the audience might not need to impose judgment onto character to feel their pain from dying, or actually, killing themselves from the inside. While Isaac used to be interpreted by his expressive movement and action, that Isaac before was a cog in the machine and just like puzzle design in an average Uncharted game, cogs are often conveniently thrown away in a corner so the machinist can come later and put it where it belongs. The new Isaac is the architect of death, one that has full agency of his action, the air that keeps the machine cooled and uninterrupted. The horror comes when this architect - us, realising his human part is slowly decaying. Are we more used to Isaac's real lavishly animated eyes full of humanity and hope, or the back of his head and his "health bar" visualized by his backbone which lights him up like a beacon in every single corner on this ship? The cruelty of futuristic industrialism renders us wholly alienated, where the only human trait left is the vaguely oval-shaped head animating above the vaguely backbone-shaped body clumsily twist and turn, mimicking real human movement. Human's worth as much as their head and body, until the voice comes up, blood drips down, and then the pain makes us whole.I strongly believe that remakes don't hold the duty to keep the spirit of the original alive. Souls can be reborn but never replicated. If anything, for me Dead Space did above and beyond what it was meant to be, to give an aging soul a new voice. This might not have been an original piece created entirely through new ideas, but it dares to speak up, loud and clearly, through fierce tone and end in powerful silence.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering EA's track record I was really worried about this game and wasnt expecting much effort to be put into this but after finishing the game I have never been happier to be so wrong. This is easily one of the best remakes I have ever played and I think all companies that are looking to do something like this in the future should use Dead Space as a blueprint for how to remake a game the right way. I have played and beaten Dead Space 1, 2, and even 3 multiple times and I am a big fan of the franchise but I would be lying if I said Dead Space 3 and then the lack of Dead Space games after that didnt have me feeling  like the Dead Space I knew and loved was gone. With the Dead Space remake however, not only was the original games atmosphere and charm beautifully replicated, but it was taken a step further to keep things fresh for veterans of the series like myself. Everything was familiar but at the same time it had all changed enough to keep me on the edge of my seat the whole way through. As a remake this game is honestly up there with Resident Evil 2 for me as one of my absolute favorites. Both games managed to take a beloved game that has been played to death by its many fans, and refurbish it to bring it up to date while still keeping all the things that made us fall in love with the originals. Dead Space exceeded all of my expectations and I highly encourage everyone, new or returning, to give it a shot. Heres hoping that Dead Space 2 gets the same treatment in the near future. 10/10

I was one of the DS fans that thought the remake was unnecessary, but now I want DS2 to be remade and DS3 to be remade with this quality from the ground up. This has to be the best remake ever made. It made an absolute amazing game so much better. There is no reason to go back to the original after this. The games EA dev teams can make when they are passionate and aren't completely under the dictatorship of their executives. This remake shows passion! You can tell these devs loved the original as much as we did. I hope EA keeps it up with how their single player games have been doing. What an experience Dead Space is. I can't stop but be happy we have this. I'll say it over and over. Dead Space is amazing and this remake is amazing. Do yourself a favor if you haven't played Dead Space before and play DS Remake and DS2. It is the best horror out there. I promise you a great experience that you will remember for a really long time. It's been over 10 years since 1 and 2 released and it's still so great playing these games. A true 10/10 in its genre. PS: To all non-headphone users. Get some headphones for this one and turn on 3d audio. You won't regret it.
