_childDocuments_.review: Played the original all the way through for the first time back in 2019 I believe. It was clunky, outdated, but definitely still playable and absolutely still scary (I have always preferred Dead Space 2 to the first one, but always recognized that the first was the scariest). This is an extremely authentic remake so far with some great additions. While I am only on Chapter 3 while writing this, almost everything is exactly like how I remember it. Anything that is a bit different is honestly better than the original, or at the very least as good as it. Graphics are beautiful, and the game runs very well. When the game wants to be dark, it is DARK (visually, not tonally (well, both actually)). The amount of detail Motive has added is extremely impressive. I'll change or rewrite this review if I see fit later, but I wanted to share my early thoughts and say this is definitely worth the buy if you're a fan, or want to become one. Support the devs by buying this full price so it increases our chances at a Dead Space 4, or a Dead Space 2 remake (which I want a lot more than a 4th game personally). Motive has been extremely transparent in how much love and care they put into this project, and we can truly see that now that it's in our hands. Thank you Motive :) <3EDIT: I don't normally 100% achievements with games. It was a blast doing it with this one. When I played Dead Space (2008) in 2019 like I said above, I did it only with the Plasma Cutter, and it was cool having an achievement with it in this one. Impossible mode, Plasma Cutter only run, the alternate ending, man this game was a blast to go through .Got all the achievements with 3 runs (needed to start a 4th run to get all the upgrades for the last achievement). Wish there was more to do because I would've liked to go through it again for something. One of my favorite games of 2023. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: So yes, it's a remake. I know some people hate the remakes trend, but having missed that game when it released, i'm glad i'm being able to experience it in a modernized version. Overall, i really enjoyed it. Of course as you probably guessed, it's not for you if don't like scary games. Being used to them, i didn't find it terrifying but there are definitely some tense moments and a few good jumpscares. Everything in the game's atmosphere screams Alien: from the eerie sounds and music to the story, even if the creatures obviously aren't the same. The story is solid and even if it's nothing revolutionnary, it definitely kept me wanting to know more and surprised me a few times.The visuals are nice, the game probably has the best looking explosions and flame effects i've seen in quite some time. The character feels a bit 'heavy'. At times it's good because it allows you to really feel through its moves and the controller rumbles the violence and impacts from the fights, but i gotta say i sometimes wished that the controls were a bit more responsive. Overall, it's still good in that department.I put 20 hours to finish in difficult mode and while it might sound on the short side, content is dense enough that i didn't feel the game would have needed more. Plus, it has some replay value through NG+ and achievement hunting if you're into this.Recommended, too bad EA hasn't been happy with the sales, because i would have loved episodes 2 and 3 remakes.

_childDocuments_.review: First off before review, if you get any softlocks like I did once at the start of chapter 5 and are in impossible mode with no backup saves. Go here. Follow the directions and back up your regular saves if you have any first, just to another folder or something, then use these backups for impossible mode.   You can grab a backup this great guy uploaded there. Saved me from losing 7 hours of gameplay, gamestate was mostly the same. Big fan of the Dead Space Franchise, got this remake as a gift and love it so far. I don't know if it was because I had game saves in older Dead Space games or if it was because my buddy got it for me early and that unlocked it, but I had impossible mode open from the start and went straight for that. This remake is not just a graphic refresh, it is a new game that follows the main overall story of the original game with some changes. Some soft locks are very annoying, so if not on impossible I would keep backups at least a chapter behind. For impossible, back up all of your saves to another folder, then set up one of those impossible save backups. Get your impossible run done and then restore your other playthroughs if you have any. They put in backtracking and some sidequests for some extra gear and items. But areas you've been through can always have new enemy encounters. The weapons have mostly been updated, as far as I can tell everything, save one gun, has the same primary fire. But alt fire on most guns has been changed. The story beats aren't the same but they rhyme if that makes sense. You don't follow the same path and setup to get to certain parts of the game. WIl update the review to be more final and less messy once I've finished the game.

Not to mention the sound design adds so much - from the intimidating loud thump of Isaac's boots hitting the metal floors of the ship to distant echoes of screams masked by the heavy machinery and groans of the ship. If you're a survival horror fan. the dead space series will not disappoint. This new remake really shows that good games can never die.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a remake that not only does justice to the original, but improves on it in almost every conceivable way. I remember first playing through Dead Space back on the 360 during high school and feeling moments of pure terror, and some fourteen-odd years later feeling many of the same feelings washing over me like a tidal wave. The nostalgia hit is very real.The changes made to the story were often subtle, yet felt organic and well thought out. Instead of simply ham-fisting a voice actor into the game and calling it a day, Isaac's updated role has been accounted for brilliantly, with character dialogue and scenes being totally redone to fit the changes. Several major story scenes were updated, some redone entirely, but in a way that pays homage to the original while still maintaining an identity of its own.The Necromorphs new visuals were striking, often stunning, but never boring! I found myself able to distinguish between them with greater ease and prioritise threats during combat. Additionally, weapons felt like they did serious damage, with flesh and viscera sloughing off still-living enemies in a truly disgusting, amazing way. Every weapon felt like it served a purpose in the toolkit, though as a creature of habit, the Plasma Cutter became a fast favourite.Even the ill-fated Ishimura was given extensive work, looking far more like a ship lost to its doomed fate. Exploring around and taking in the scene was an absolute marvel. When I first heard about the Authorization system, I had trepidations it would turn into some miserable system a-la Other M, but instead it felt equally organic, unlocking new areas to explore and incentivised backtracking. Nice touch!Maybe it's luck, but I encountered very few bugs or issues throughout my playthrough, If anything, my only technical complaints revolve around a sometimes laggy interface, with save stations being notably irritating. I hope these are things that can be addressed in a future patch.Otherwise, EA Motive, thank you. This was absolutely f*cking amazing. I only hope the Sprawl gets the same treatment one day~10/10, will gleefully blast Necromorphs again.

_childDocuments_.review: Surpasses all expectations. Better than the original in nearly every conceivable way. This is the way you do remakes. NO cut content, only enhancing what existed before and adding additional content on top of it. The graphics are fantastic, the game-play loop feels fun and engaging, much more similar to Dead Space 2 in that everything feels more fluid and smooth, kinesis is much more effective with ripping off limbs and pinning enemies to walls, just like DS2. The story feels way more fleshed out with a lot of additional dialogue and exposition surrounding the lore, about what the marker is doing to people, unitology, etc. The story just feels more complete and immersive than in the original game. It's more up front and center, versus just in the background. The new inter-connectivity of the Ishimura makes the ship feel tangible and massive in size and scope. There's more incentive to backtrack and revisit previously explored areas now due to the security clearance system(sort of similar to how the Power Node doors worked in the old games). I just can't stop glowing about this game.It DOES have some performance issues right now, but I expect these to be patched sooner rather than later. There is some stuttering, and it's my belief this is due to shader loading but I could be wrong. The game pre-loads shaders, but I don't think it's preloading ALL of them. The game also utilizes inherent Variable Rate Shading, and there's no way to turn it off. This is causing some issues with aliasing and muddier than usual textures when utilizing DLSS. It becomes more obvious the lower the internal res gets. There's also some weird "ghosting" like effect on Issac's character model with DLSS on. It's more obvious in brighter lit environments, but when strafing back and forth with Issac, you notice a trailing/ghosting effect on the model. If you turn DLSS off, it solves this about 90% of the way I'd say. The problem is, turning DLSS off is a major performance hit, and depending on your hardware, it may not be worth it to you to do so. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A superb game I for once enjoyed playing again for a bit because usually I'm not very attracted by remakes unless they could provide a decent new content.Callisto Protocol comparison for people who want honest point of view is quite simple:- Visuals & textures are incomparable. Callisto feels like a generic UE game while it's all the opposite for Dead Space. The textures are well-chosen, they are even organic like the ones you could have seen in the "Event Horizon" movie.- The game was not stuttering with RT that much compared to Callisto. In Callisto I had to tweak the UE settings on RT properly to get rid of the stutters. And it's not tied to AMD at all.- User interface is THE one in Dead Space. OK, I will be straight to the point here: it's an iconic one. Callisto tried to mimic it but failed badly, you can't even move around with it.- Progression is good in Dead Space and you are granted much-much more tools, armors, and weapons than in Callisto.- Each and any weapon in Dead Space is giving you a full tree to unlock and use it the way you want - and it's an enjoyment to progress through it.- Map design in Dead Space is much better and encourages exploration with a bit of new goals introduced by the remake.- Dead Space combat system is providing you a lot of ways to deal with enemies compared to Callisto BUT to be honest here, Callisto does offer something in the ways of melee combat and it's the ONLY good feature in "devenir" to me. A very good one at its base, it's something to scratch and it's probably the first iteration of a system that needs to be developed further for future games. The evade move is just what we need in nowadays games instead of that decades old roll.- Traversal system is way better in Dead Space with the ZERO-G suit jetpack. Callisto is about tunnel crawling with no interactions at all and that EVER OVERUSED sliding inside a tiny space in between two walls.- Callisto Protocol has pretty good animations, vaulting over crates, climbing down stairs and so on. Dead Space could maybe benefit on new ones not going away, however, from proper armor weight.- General content which seems to be several times longer than Callisto (to me it's like at least x2 times).To conclude: Dead Space is far superior to Callisto Protocol.The only drawback of Dead Space 2023? The price. Not corresponding at all to what it is (refunded for that reason). It should have been halved. And I do hope they will also do a remake of the second episode and above all a remake of the third one in CO-OP taking that into account.

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is quite possibly one of the best remakes ever made. And honestly just a good game too.This game took the original and made it 10x better. Graphics are most obvious, the gameplay with the intensity director and peel system. As well as that fear system that keeps Isaac on edge. The necromorphs all look horrific and disgusting. Especially the brutes and the hunter (who got expanded lore). The narrative got a big upgrade this time around due to some rewriting they did (the personalities of Hammond and Kendra) which mainly consists of various audio logs or entire side quests. Some of the chapters in the game have some objectives swapped around or completely changed which is mostly caused by writing differences (won't get into for spoiler reasons). The new story in general is much less linear and engaging for 2 reasons. It's engaging because Isaac can now speak and has his own thoughts and contributes to the conversation at hand rather than being ordered around and listening to his colleagues bicker amongst each other. And it's less linear because you can pursue objectives out of orders and go anywhere in the ship whenever you desire.The atmosphere and soundtrack generally keep up the tension and further expands on that "not knowing what's out there" feeling in the original. technically speaking, with a 10980xe and a 2080ti (high end parts but a little dated now), running this game at 1080p ultra was very easy due to the native DLSS support. Game isn't buggy like some of us might have expected, and is also very well optimized. All in all, this remake does what it set out to do extremely well and is definitely worth imo. Kudos to EA motive for finally giving us a decent AAA game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Space

_childDocuments_.review: This Dead Space remake is, in my opinion, the epitome of what a remake should be: Honoring the original vision of the game while improving upon what was there to begin with. In other words, if the original team of Dead Space created this game today, I imagine it may not be far off from what we have received with this game. There are many positives to have with this remake with few negatives, so let's go through it quickly.Improvements:- Isaac Clarke is no longer a silent protagonist- Graphics and lighting- Greater Exploration- Interesting Side Stories- Necromorph dismemberment- AI Director which makes exploration more tense- Added Dead Space 2 Zero GPositives:- Story is interesting and compelling- Gameplay is intense and very fun- No HUD which gives a more immersive horror experience- Foam HandDrawbacks:- Replaying the game can be annoying due to security clearance not carrying over and unskippable in-game cutscenes (luckily cutscenes are not common and generally short)- Impossible mode does not increase difficulty, or at least very little, and instead turns the game game into a 'Die and Restart' mode which I am not the biggest fan of- Stuttering when entering areas that require a new load in- One feature that I wish got a little more love is the "Limited Power System." Essentially, when some system needs power in order to advance, sometimes you may need to turn off power to the lights or even life support. I wish there were more areas that required you to make a decision between these options or even add more to the mix like Zero G and maybe even something like "Ventilation" which would cause more necromorphs to spawn.Overall, it's not a perfect game of course, but it is an especially fun game that does way more right than wrong that it gets a 10/10 score from me and a definite recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play the original Dead Space forwards and backwards. Played it so hard that I memorized every audio log and lore bits, even decoded some of the scrawlings on the walls. You know, all the good stuff.Let me tell you, the only thing that I can say is a disappointment in this remake is that I can't snap my Plasma cutter back and forth as fast as I used to, Issac needs to be stressed to make that iconic stomp grunt (but does it more often the further you get into the game), and the gators (Leapers) don't crawl over the hull when the Kellion is attacked. That's it, and that's nitpicking HARD.The ambiance is amazing, the sounds are nearly identical, and better than that: The Ishimura is more cohesive. All the locations are pretty much the same in style and layout, except for some notoriously tedious and arduous ones that sometimes made the game drag back in the day. The ship is still HUGE, and you actively get a sense of where everything is as you're traveling through it. Not to mention that its really easy to double back to nearly everywhere in the ship. Monsters? They actually imported some monsters that originally were in Dead Space 2 and 3, but they work. Again, I feel like the Leapers didn't get their time to shine, but they're still scary as heck! And the story has changed, but not so significantly that it's a different game. It incorporates some further lore, and some things that weren't mentioned in the games proper. If anything it builds things up better and creates a new sense of mystery for people like me who played the games to death. If anything this game is showcasing itself as a REBOOT rather than an honest to goodness ReMake, and I am here for it! Maybe we'll get the whole series again, the second game will make more sense while still being absolutely fun as heck AND.... well, let's just say that they can't do anything worse with the third game. So. Definitely worth the money, and worth the play through.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Sincerely near-perfect remaster of one of the best 3rd person horror games of all time.  Difficult to put down.Pros:- Faithful recreation of the old game with plenty of new things to explore- Added content feels like it was 'always meant to be there'.  This remaster successfully bridges many plot holes between the original Dead Space and Dead Space 2.  - World-class sound design and the upgraded graphics are stunning.- Still a genuinely frightening experience.  Jump scares will 'get you' half a dozen times and the overall story/art-design is horrifying.- Like the original, the 2023 remaster features a core gameplay loop that makes the game addicting.  Upgrading weapons/equipment and scrounging for materials is a fun experience.  - Giving Isaac a voice was the right decision.  The 'silent protagonist' feature of the original felt out of place.The Bad:- They leaned into 'ugly Nicole' and even made Isaac uglier... No idea why they felt the need to redo Isaac's face.- Some of the new story-scenes felt a BIT forced...as in, the characters are spewing disposition for a half a minute.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing remake that keeps everything that worked in the original and fixes what didn't. Gameplay, Graphics, Story, Atmosphere- all phenomenal. Gunplay/ combat is very satisfying and never gets old.My only two complaints are performance and replayability.Performance---------------Performance ♥♥♥♥ itself every once in a while- screen freezes when there are a lot of enemies in a room and buffering when loading the next area. On two occasions, characters didn't spawn in during cutscenes, so Isaac is just talking to nothing. Encountered a couple minor bugs like doors and items not spawning in for a few seconds.Only major bug was during a scripted shooting sequence. Isaac's aim was locked to the ground and I couldn't shoot, causing me to die but then still being able to roam the camera around the room with enemies ignoring me. (Manually reloading fixed this.)Replayability------------------There are new enemies, story details, and an ending on New Game Plus. However, there is no skip button for anything. If you want to replay the game for achievements, you are forced to replay the slow opening, relisten to the same voice calls, and rewatch every single cutscene. Even if you just want to check out items you unlocked, you have to replay through the entire opening just to look at them.In all, I'd recommend. Despite performance issues here and there, and tedious replaying, it never got in the way of my fun for the game. If you are a fan of survival horror, this is a MUST.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be talking about the game in very broad strokes so don't worry about spoilers. I'm bananas about the Dead Space series. The experience of playing the original in 2009 or so left a massive impression on me and I think this is overall a pretty fantastic update. I've played the original  duology to death on every system, listened to stuff, looked at stuff, everything. So as someone who has Nicole's monologue burnt into the back of my eyelids, I was pretty sceptical Motive would be able to win me over with Dead Space 23. I was very pleasantly surprised, though. It's clear a lot of love and care went into refining Dead Space for the remake and in many ways I find these refinements make the setting, characters, and mysteries all a lot more compelling. On the lead up to release there was an IGN series of short interviews with developers, artists, writers, etc working on the remake. It was really fascinating hearing about how they were approaching different aspects of the project, there's a lot of interesting insights about the aesthetic and thematic goals of the game in there that get me really craving a Dead Space 23 art book. If you're sceptical about Dead Space 23, I think they're worth a watch. It's really striking how thoughtful they've been in creating their take on Dead Space and I don't think their efforts deserve to go so easily overlooked. If you're really interested in the artistry of the series I'd also highly recommend The Art of Dead Space, it's a great book and an amazing collection of art that really lays bare the core identity of the series. It's been a great companion piece to Dead Space 23.  I think a lot of people have been comparing the choices and artistic aims of the original team and the new devs in bad faith, I really can't see anything but reverence for the source material here. I'd also say that the differences that are there are interesting and well worth exploring!I'm also glad Dead Space has room to breathe again, EA really pushed the extended universe the first time around and I'm glad to see that mistake hasn't been repeated. I'm not someone who's super into lore, I like finding extra information that re-contextualises things in cool ways but this extended universe stuff can get pretty silly. There were animated movies, books, tie-in games, a Wii rail shooter (which I enjoyed) and most of it just served to undermine the setting and the horror for me. That isn't to say the remake shies away from its roots because it absolutely doesn't, there's an entire New Game+ path that I think incorporates a direct reference to one of the extended universe novels. If you're a lorehead you'll definitely recognise familiar names in text logs, even very forgettable characters get some mentions in. I really love this about the remake, it reincorporates a lot of this disparate stuff into more of a coherent whole. I think my favourite addition is the AI director that manages encounters and atmospheric effects. Dead Space is a game that invokes hypervigilance, I think that's part of what makes the series so compelling. You're always alert, always listening and watching, always looking over your shoulder. It has an intensity that I feel is absolutely unmatched. With the AI director in the mix that feeling is sharper than ever. You can't rely on memory alone to get you through now. Yeah, you can still memorise spawns and there are still an abundance of scripted encounters but you can never safely bet you know what's coming and when. Sometimes the lights will flicker and steam will hiss from the pipes- nothing. But sometimes a pregnant and most of a divider will be waiting for you right by the shop. You can truly never assume you're safe, that feeling is no longer illusory as it was in Dead Space 2008. I think that's great. I also found that the director would spawn interesting combinations of enemy types which is cool, it went a long way to making the threat more unpredictable. I never really experienced any of the performance issues everyone else is talking about so I think my main issue with the game is very petty. I flat out do not like the redesign of the Soldier rig. They look like those guys who're really into Mandalorian themed tactical gear and Punisher stuff. So, yeah, not sure if that's an intentional update to reflect reality but, aesthetically speaking, I found it very jarring. I think this is a very solid foundation to build on to bring back the Dead Space series. I hope in the future there might be more challenge modes, higher difficulties, more unlockable suits. Most of all though I hope Motive, like their predecessors, take some pointers from the Resident Evil games. I'm a big fan of the records system in the recent Resident Evil titles. It contributes enormously to replayability and it's neat getting to examine all the models, animations, concept art, all the good stuff. As someone who likes crafts and fan projects, something like that would be indispensable. it's all work that very much deserves to be admired, too. Some of the detail on the necromorphs is ludicrous. A records system would also be a great excuse to do wild runs like beating the game without healing or opening the shop. Just give me a reason, Motive.There are thousands of things about this remake that I could just keep gushing about. Maybe I'll update this review over time and do just that (I have). But I hope for now this review has gone some way to convincing you to try out Dead Space. Tanya Clarke killed it as Nicole, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a HUGE fan of the original game, it being one of my all-time favourites.I really think that the remake is absolutely worth it, somehow making an already terrifying game into a truly crap-your-pants experience. Something like updated graphics and lighting wouldn't usually tickle my fancy but with Dead Space, it takes atmospheric to a whole other level. On top of that, it makes the game feel so much more realistic (e.g.: The Kellion is actually damaged from the crash).Isaac also has dialogue which initially I thought might take away from the game, being a fan of the whole 'silent protagonist' thing, but to be completely honest, I think it adds a really needed layer of depth to it. He's actually thinking like an engineer and I don't have to try and fathom why the hell I'm bumbling about in the dark collecting certain things. _childDocuments_.review: What I liked about your game, Motive, was the transparent communication with the players throughout your production period. Not a lot of developers have the guts to show the WIP of their works, but you did, and kept impressing us even more with each video uploaded on YouTube platform.Yeah, this isn't a review anymore, but a love letter. Thank you for putting all the effort to remake this game. While it stays true to the original, it's also different. Dejavu hits sometimes, but you guys have twisted it so good I feel like I'm being gaslighted.Even though you guys were completely transparent with the Sound Design aspect of this game, it still keeps catching me offguard. I really hope it wins the Sound Design award, you guys more than deserve it. Okay, back to review. Sound Design of this game is the second best I've seen (first is Hunt: Showdown). With every step you take in a dark hall, you can hear a Necromorph stalking you, ready to jump on you at any time. And don't let me get started about the whispers you keep hearing. Sounds of monsters are so well done I had to pause the game and scream as a mofo sneaked up on me in the dark.Many of the sounds are from the original, but effects have been added to them that make them completely new. For example, when you use a Health Pack, depending on the severity of your injuries, Isaac breaths a fresh air with various intensities. Also his voice changes depending on his injuries, makes you feel it when you're running around with RED hp.About the music, in an instance, I heard an out of tune plucked string instrument, it was wild af. Also it seems that every type of Necromorph have their own type of "music" attached to them. For example, those mimic-like skin tissue enemies that crawl on you have a very distinct fast and high pitch violin plays in a very chaotic and, again, distinct staccato fashion. It was beautiful, which lead me to quit and write this review.__________It stays true to "cutting off limbs," and honestly, it feels way harder than other Dead Space games. Or maybe I'm getting old. I had no problem aiming at the tail of a Leaper in the past, but here these guys are so agile with their tails, it feels like they hide them behind their bodies. Stasis isn't as op as it used to be.I've been playing on Hard difficulty, and had my ass handed back to me in a few instances. Enemies, however, feel a little bullet spongy. It's not easy to stun theme, and melee attacks are even less effective than the other games. However, it allows you to do a very quick melee attack after aiming, which helps when enemies get unexpectedly close.I love the new "Pick your poison" sections. Sometimes you have to divert power from one of your two options to a new section to progress... which leads to interesting choices. You want to venture in the dark? Or do you want to have the life support cut off from the area and rely on your Oxygen supply to carry you through? Both choices are equally thrilling and fun.Zero Gravity sections have been changed to what Dead Space 2 did: once you disengage your gravity boots, you have to rely on the installed Thrusters of your suit to orient yourself and find your way to the objective.Speaking of objectives, the Objective Finder (known as the Locator) is a bit annoying. Instead of being on-hold, it's now a single time use. If you didn't get it the first time, you have to use it again. Sometimes I have to check 5 times because the signal goes through the ground to show that you have to descend, but it's a bit difficult to follow when you're in a hurry.In addition to the main objective, which progresses the story, there are now optional objectives you can follow. Can't spoil much, but they are intertwined with the main objective. However, how it works and switching between main and optional objectives are a bit annoying. If you complete an optional objective, and it leads to another optional objective, game automatically switches to main objective, which means you have to manually change to the optional objective if you want to follow it.Upgrading your weapons and suit is a bit more complex than before: in addition to Power Nodes, you now require Upgrade Parts to further upgrade your equipment. This disallows you to break the early game balance by putting all your Nodes in, let's say, Plasma Cutter and wreck havoc on your enemies. This was annoying at first, but a welcome change, since it keeps the challenge throughout the entire playthrough.New weapons, instead of bought, are now acquired throughout the game. Also another way of keeping the balance in your fresh playthrough. In the previous games (Especially Dead Space 2) you could just buy a Linegun as soon as possible, and go through 4/5 of the game without much of a hassle. No more of that here.However, on higher difficulty settings, you realize that some weapons are simply outclassed completely by other weapons.__________Isaac now talks, and he's modeled after the voice actor, Gunner Wright! I love this guy's voice and it really brought Isaac to life in Dead Space 2. The voice acting of other characters are decent, but it lacks the depth that the original game had.The characters in the Remake feel like they've already been through this ♥♥♥♥ for some time. Kendra's "I don't know, something's in the room with us!" or Zach Hammond's "THEN REROUTE THE DAMN POWER!" from the original still haunt me to this day. They felt authentic and real. I finished the remake and I barely remember a line that was said.Some parts of the story have been changed to connect this game to the rest of the series, which was a welcome change.__________Graphics have improved a lot. There are godrays that really capture the feel of a foggy full of smoke area. Your flashlight also interacts with the fogs and smokes, which makes it interesting while engaging the enemies. There's also the screenshot on the Store Page, where godrays are going through the fog from behind a hanging tram system. It looks as beautiful in game as it looks there. There are also more stunning visuals like that later on.On the otherhand, for reflections, the game uses Screen Space effects intensively. In some instances, for example the beginning where the big screen is showing the progress of CEC, if you don't look at the screen, there will be no reflections on the ground. Immersion breaking.For enemies, the more you damage a limb, the more damaged the tissue becomes, eventually leaving nothing but bones, which you can shoot to cut. This also indicates how much damage an enemy has received to their limbs. You have to see their limbs after a non-lethal explosion. It looks and feels good.I can't really say much about the character faces. They look good enough :DThere are also small details such as the ignition torch on Flamethrower emitting light on objects.__________Throughout the game, I'm encountering severe stutters. I thought maybe it's because I'm playing on a 12100 and 6700 XT, but people with better systems are also reporting similar issues. This thing really hurts the overall smoothness of the game, and honestly shouldn't be ignored in a review.__________ I highly recommend this game. If you're new to the series, it's a great game. It's thrilling, scary, and puts you on your toes. Good headset is extremely recommended. Don't be like me and play it with earplugs. Get a proper sound system.If you're a veteran, I have to say the game has been in good hands. Definitely give it a try. I highly believe you'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Jason,I must admit, my dear slasher counterpart, that Dead Space has crawled its way into my cold, dark heart. As the embodiment of nightmares, I am no stranger to the macabre and the horrifying, but this interactive horror masterpiece has left me positively gleeful with sadistic delight.Dead Space is a testament to the sinister creativity that lurks within the darkest recesses of the human mind. From the moment I stepped foot onto the doomed USG Ishimura, I felt an electric surge of anticipation, relishing in the claustrophobic atmosphere and the palpable sense of impending doom. The game's expertly crafted narrative ensnares players in a web of cosmic horror, each step leading them closer to the brink of insanity.The attention to detail in Dead Space is exquisite, my dear Jason. The grotesque and visceral creature designs, with their twisted limbs and gnashing teeth, are a sight to behold. The meticulous dismemberment mechanics, allowing players to strategically sever limbs from these abominations, is a stroke of genius, catering to our shared penchant for bloody carnage. The haunting sound design further amplifies the sense of dread, every creak and whisper conspiring to send shivers down one's spine.Ah, the gameplay, my dear silent friend, is a symphony of terror. The strategic dissection of necromorphs with the Plasma Cutter, the harrowing encounters in zero-gravity environments, and the heart-pounding moments of desperate survival against overwhelming odds all weave together to create a chillingly addictive experience. The scarcity of resources adds an extra layer of tension, as each decision must be calculated and every shot fired counts.But it is the psychological horror that truly sets Dead Space apart, my hockey-masked comrade. The relentless whispers of madness, the hallucinations that taunt the protagonist's fragile sanity, and the eerie silence broken only by the distant scuttling of necromorphs serve to burrow deep into the player's subconscious. The game expertly manipulates fears and phobias, leaving players in a perpetual state of anxiety and unease.my dear Jason, Dead Space is a morbid masterpiece, a sinister symphony that dances upon the jagged edges of terror and madness. It indulges our shared appetite for horror and offers a chilling reminder of the boundless possibilities of interactive nightmares. I implore you, my hockey-masked friend, to embrace the horrors of Dead Space, for it embodies the very essence of our eternal existence—feeding on fear, reveling in darkness, and etching nightmares into the hearts of all who dare to play.With wicked glee,Freddy Krueger

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I'm enthusiastic about remakes but this is a great one.  It's very faithful to the original and since it's new it runs a lot better on current operating systems.  It hasn't been that long since I played the original, but honestly I couldn't really differentiate between the new and old.  Sure, there were no side quests in the original so that's new but the story is pretty much the same as the original. Combat is similar to the later Dead Space games, which means it's a lot smoother.  Isaac moves much faster and it's easier to dodge enemy attacks.  The weapons are much more balanced too.  In the original game I stuck primarily with the plasma cutter but in this game there is more of a reason to switch so I also used the Force Gun, Ripper and Contact Beam. Creature behavior is more interesting.  You could usually tell in the original when you were about to get attacked but I felt like this version surpised you more.  Also there are layers to the enemies' flesh so you get to see it peel away as you cut them up.  Isaac talks now and he says a lot of funny and appropriate things for his character so this was a good edition to the game.  I'd say this is the best you can hope for with a remake since it does the original justice and the enhanced graphics and additional content keeps the game interesting so I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space Remake is a remake of the iconic game from 2008, which for many was the revitalization of survival horror. Personally my favorite horror game of all time so when i heard this was getting remade i got excited, the question is, did Dead Space Remake deliver?Not exactly.To begin with, this has nothing do with the bathroom signs, weird looking models/faces, odd dialogue changes, race swapping, cringe graffitis whatever, if anything people ignore the real problems of this game for these little things.First of all i finished the game two times, getting all of the weapons, suits, and upgrades along with the secret ending so i have pretty much squeeze all this remake had to offer. The game stays most of the time faithful to the original storywise, the kelion crew gets sent to a repair mission to the Ishimura, something is off about it, they get attacked by the necromorphs, etc. However the changes this remake makes to the story are half assed or straight up bad, needless to say there will be spoilers.-The Chen Change: This change is just bad, in the remake chen and hammond were best buddies a long time, however chen gets killed and turned into a necromorph, eventually this gets to hammond, starts to hallucinate about him being alive and feel sorry about him, which eventually this would lead up to his death. This change is just made for cheap emotional value and holds no weight whatsoever, we know little to nothing about chen and the game tries to make the hammond death emotional since he was killed by his best buddy and in an effort to avenge his buddy and to put an end his misery, he kills himself along with chen with the singularity core. This was really lame and felt off since chen was just alive for like 10 minutes and barely talked to hammond and suddenly they were best buddies? it was not developed at all and it was just pushed down our throats since now chen is "relevant". Take in mind the original hammond death was not emotional, but it was iconic because he gets brutally torn to pieces by a brute.-Worse lighting, sound design, and animations: Dead Space had a beautiful sound design and lightning for it's enemies, atmosphere, and guns; This is straight up downgraded massively in the remake, recurring to cheap tactics like darker rooms, fog hallways, and flickering every then and now. Not only that but now almost every room in the Ishimura looks the same, this affects the USM Valor as well. I think the best example of this is in the final level where you fight the hive mind, where the lightning makes the whole scenario way worse than the original, people will say it's realistic, but that doesn't equal better and in this case it was an artistic decision to highlight the hive mind, which is completely butchered in the remake. The sound in the remake also lacks weight and intensity compared to the original, guns sound toned down and generic compared, and the atmosphere now has been replaced for either lackluster sounds or generic horror music, a clear example of this is the lurker reveal, which pales in comparison to the original. This of course also affects the necromorph sounds making them sound really generic or straight up lame(just listen to that necromoprh elevator scene) The ones that were affected the most were: The lurkers, slashers, leapers, exploders, guardians, the leviathan, twitchers, and of course the hive mind. Finally some animations just look bad like walking/running animations. ripper reloading animation, some characters death, and the death animations for Isaac now look awful with the new models(looking at you head transplant death).-Poor voice acting: I have no idea why nobody mentions this but i'll say it; The voice acting in this game sucks, no disrespect to the motion capture actors since direction also matters but many of the new voices are just way too underwhelming, they sound way too quiet, way too calm in the intense scenes, and some of them just straight up don't fit their characters at all, dr kyne is the clear example of this as his voice now sounds generic and doesn't fit at all, butchering his character in the process. The only exception of this is Gunner Wright and Tanya Clarke since they are playing their respecting characters and know them well, but other than that the cast is lackluster. Some scenes that are notable for this are: The USM Valor ship crash, hammonds death, kendras death, any time dr kyne speaks, kendras betrayal, mercer's death, and the crew talking about getting the tram back on.-Enemy design: You can call this a nitpick, however i think it's worth mentioning it. The remake changed the aspect the necromoprhs, whereas now they tried to make them look more monstrous rather than human looking, the original design had this uncanny look where they somehow looked like something that is human but at the same time isn't, with the stretched faces and pink looking skin. The necromorphs now are just pale looking and completely deformed, some of them actually look more alien than actual humans.Lackluster OST: Small complain, the remake mixes tracks from the original game while also using the remake ones in other parts, however the parts where the remake ones play sound pretty generic like the leviathan boss fight which is also now the hive mind boss fight (unless this a glitch), and the zero g remake now sounds bland instead of tense like the original.Now, the remake actually improves in a few things like guns balancing like the flamethrower and the ripper, the new secondary fire weapon abilities which i'll admit are really fun to use and make the gameplay more fun and chaotic. The gameplay is also faster now and roughly plays now like dead space 2, but the core gameplay wasn't changed that much since well the original already played well and it aged like a fine wine. The zero g sections are definitely a good improvement, however i feel like they relied a bit too much on this change, changing some parts that use this new zero g mechanic just for the sake of it, the only thing where i didn't like this change was the leviathan boss fight, which is now way less intense and much more easier, and it's not like the boss fight was hard to begin with in the original so yeah. The graphics are nice too, but they are not that impressive either. Overall, this remake is disappointing to say the least, i can tell Motive wanted to truly tribute the original dead space, but either because of budget restraint, lack of creativity, or close deadline made this remake fell flat. Another thing that also seems to be the issue is that they tried to make changes while being as faithful as possible to the original, however these ideas eventually contract themselves making them feel short, underwhelming, or straight up pointless(Liz cross plot twist, chen, isaac talking, backtracking, dead space 2 zero g gravity, etc.) I would not recommend this over the original and unless you're solely interested in the gameplay i'd get this on a good Christmas sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Dead Space again after so many years feels so damn good. This is a proper remake, not one of those scams that simply brush the textures a little bit and call it a "remaster". This game is a completely redone Dead Space 1. It keeps the core aspect of the game intact but enhances the game in multiple ways.The story is mostly the same, you are Isaac Clarke, an engineer on his way to the Ishimura, a giant mining ship which suddenly went completely silent. You and your team are tasked to find out what happened and repair any potential damage. It is assumed that the comms system broke down but when you arrive you find out that there is something much more sinister at play. The crew of the ship is mostly dead and the corpses are turned into undead mutants, called Necromorphs. The only way to deal with those creatures is to tear them apart since even a badly damaged necromorph will hunt you down.The gameplay is almost the same as the original game, you walk around the ship and can have different weapons, starting with the plasma cutter. Weapons can deal damage to different body parts and eventually tear the limbs off, which does massive damage to the main HP of the enemy. Necromorphs are designed in a way that they have multiple limbs and depending on what you destroy, you might take their ability to attack, to walk or other stuff. Taking enough limbs from an enemy will kill it faster than just doing damage normally, so you have to aim carefully if you don't want to waste ammo. Killed enemies can be further destroyed by stomping on them, which will release additional loot but will also make sure that they don't just pretend to be dead (which they can do). New here is that the enemies are now designed in layers, you can peel skin, tissue, muscle and finally bone from them untl the limb finally snaps. This gives the already detailed amputation system much more depth and makes the game even more eerie to look at. This can happen to you too if you die, making death scenes quite disturbing. Weapons have been rebalanced, I found myself rarely using any other weapon than the standard Plasma Cutter, your starting weapon. The cutter was already so powerful and perfect to cut off limbs, other weapons felt so weak in comparison. In the remake they have buffed the weapons, so now everything feels more viable, they also limited the amount of upgrades that you can put into a weapon at the beginning. You now need schematics to unlock more of the upgrade grid for a weapon so you won't max the Plasma Cutter before anything else.  You also don't have to buy the other weapons anymore int he shop, this time you get them while you progress through the game which encourages you even more to use them.They changed a bit of the story, overall it still is the same but Isaac is not silent anymore and takes part in conversations, comments on events that happen in the game and you have the feeling he is more part of the overall story instead of just being a silent stand-in for the player. This is more reminiscent of DS2 and 3 than the first one but it's not a bad change to be honest. Isaac was never a "Gordon Freeman" and that's okay. The game menu, as usual, is the RIG system, which is an immersive Ui that is a direct part of the game world itself. When opening the menu, ISaac simply activates a holographic display and browses his inventory or checks the map. You can also, just like before, place a hologrpahic line that helps you to find your next objective in the ship. This is a really helpful tool and I still cannot believe that no other game tried to recreate this concept. Whzile you can just follow straight the objective, you can and you should check other paths and rooms because they can contain additional loot, even if you have a high risk in finding more enemies.The combat is very solid, gunplay feels great. Each weapon has a primary and secondary firing mode and you can have 4 weapons equipped and switch between them on the go. Additionally you have stasis and kinesis, two extra modules that are similiar to "spells" in fantasy games. Stasis slows enemies down to a crawl, which makes it easy to hit them or to evade an attack, kinesis allows you to pick up objects or even dead bodies and throw them around. This can be used to solve puzzles but also to jurt enemies. Kinesis is much stronger than it was in the original game, which makes this a welcome change.And of course, the atmosphere of the game is fantastic. Seeing the game in modern graphics adds much more to the scare factor. The lighting is briliant, the new sound system makes you much more paranoid. There is nothing more unnerving like walking down a dark hallway with nothing but the shine of your flashlight while you hear some sounds int he distance. And suddenly a necromorph jumps out right behind you. The game does know how it can get you and I love it.If you are looking for a great survival horror game, look no furthe, this is as good as it can get. And since Dead Space got a remake, there is now a good chance that we can get one for DS 2 and 3 as well, we might even finally get DS4 if we are lucky. I'm glad they decided to revive the series and I'm even more happy that this isn't the usual cash grab that you normally see in this business, especially since EA is the publisher.

Isaac now has a voice and actually meaningfully contributes to the plot. The visuals are absolutely incredible. The game is filled to the brim with small details, and the developers did an excellent job recreating the Ishimura in a way that was faithful while still being an improvement over the original in every regard. It runs fairly well, too. My 3050ti managed a mostly stable 60FPS on medium-high settings with RTAO and DLSS on quality. I did get infrequent crashes, especially when messing with the graphics settings, but they weren't frequent enough to be a dealbreaker.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Probably the best remake everA remake done right. The original holds up pretty well in my opinion, so a remake wasn't necessary. But, boy am I glad they did it anyway. Many remakes make the mistake of deviating from the original in a bad way, or just too much to give that feeling of nostalgia. That's not the case here. It holds true enough to the original to make me forget it's a remake at times. It feels exactly the same as the original but manages to incorporate major quality of life improvements. They seem to have managed to cut out a bunch of fluff that wasn't necessary while adding in new optional content that is worth exploring. Obviously the visuals have been overhauled and it looks fantastic. But more importantly, they redone a majority of the dialogue that is far more believable and flows better than it did in the original. A part of this is the added depth to a lot of the side characters. They each have a more flushed out story that fits perfectly into the narrative. The sound design is impeccable. The ambiance holds a tense atmosphere and the soundtrack adds to this tenfold. Weapons have far better mechanics, specifically the alternative fire modes, which all are useful in this game. The upgrades are better mapped out and combining kinesis and stasis upgrades with the suit upgrade tree was an excellent choice. The flesh rending mechanic is satisfying and adds to the immersion rather than being a needless gimmick. I can only hope for the team to continue the story, either remaking the rest of the series or skipping straight to Dead Space 4. Although personally would love to play through a new and improved Dead Space 2, as it was my favorite in the series. Again, doesn't need a remake\remaster but I'll take it if they give it. If it leads to a better Dead Space 3, I'm all in. That one needs a bit of rewriting and return to the series' core concepts.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what a remake of a game should be like; it takes everything from the original game and gives it new life. I enjoyed the additions of the side missions, and the more fleshed out story line. Since Isaac can talk in this game like he does in Dead Space 2, it makes it seem like he isn't just a flesh suit for the player and with the ability to actually look for Nicole in this game, it actually feels like Isaac is worried about Nicole (In the first game she is brought up a handful of times, and since Isaac is mute and has the emotiveness of a plank of wood, he kinda just seems like he doesn't actually care that much). Daniels is more likeable because of her added dialogue (I actually felt like she wasn't just being a ♥♥♥♥ for no reason in this game, unlike the original). Honestly, all characters seem better than their original counterparts with the help of the new dialogue. The alternate ending is a fun addition to this game as well, although honestly I didn't have the patience to go around rummaging for 12 Marker fragments without the help of a guide.I also really liked how they made the Ishimura a ship you can fully explore whenever you want, not regulated to having to do certain sections in certain chapters, and I enjoyed being able to enter a room and recognise it from the first game, yet because the devs reworked it, it is more fun to traverse and feels better thought out.My one complaint is that you cannot skip cutscenes or character dialogue. By the time I got to my third playthrough of the game I did not want to sit waiting for the doors to unlock because I was forced to focus my whole attention on watching Kendra and Hammond bicker with eachother, I just wanted to progress to the next section. Maybe a future patch can add this feature.Personally I haven't had any issues with any bugs, or troubles with the UI, so I can't comment on that.TL;DR: Great game; one of the best remakes out there, Definitely worth your while to buy :)

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal upgrade to a beloved classic, this remake takes what made the original good and elevates it on every level. Let's look at some of the changes. First, utilizing the zero-G controls of the later games made zero-G sections in this game far more fun than flinging yourself wall-to-wall with no control once you make the jump. It also makes sections like the basketball court a lot more fun. Opening the map up to be fully explored at any point in the game is another masterful choice, especially with the addition of security doors that encourage backtracking to get better gear and more loot. Speaking of gear, how they retooled upgrading makes it so much better than the original as well. Rather than waste nodes on empty slots, every node slot upgrades your weapon in some way. Not to mention the addition of unique weapon upgrades that add more firepower to each weapon, like damage over time for the plasma cutter. Back to the map itself, while many key areas play out the same, there are many changes in how you go from area to area, and certain areas are fully retooled to be unique from the original (thank you no more turret section). And also, the overall look and design of the game is beautiful. Like, when I'm not getting chased down by man-made horrors beyond my comprehension, I can stare out the windows of the bridge to Aegis-VII and get such a breathtaking view. The game looks just as good as it plays. Overall, if you love the original, this will blow your mind, and is a must-buy at any price. I sincerely hope EA plans to put out more Dead Space content, because Titan Station deserves to be given the same remake treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of the franchise, seeing the first game return and revamped, it's an early birthday gift to me! The environment is still terrifying, the gore is still disturbing, and the revamped 3D assets are simply amazing! Hearing Issac speak more, reading environmental tidbits through text/audio logs, seeing everything be knit together beautifully is well worth the price.And EA said single-player games are dead. PSHAW!I am hoping that the success of this revamp means we can see a revamp DS2 (though that game STILL stands up on its own just fine to this day), and a PROPER ending to the franchise with a non-crap DS3.The only negative things I have to say are about how the game runs on my PC. I don't have the beefiest PC, it handles most games just fine, but I do have the occasional frame drop and audio crackling/or audio cut off. When the live video calls happen, the audio is either ahead of the visuals, or it train wrecks together. Tried running the game on low settings on my 4K monitor, and yeesh the game did not like that. It runs semi-fine on medium on my HD monitor though, but that's where I encounter the hiccups I mentioned.My specs are as follows:OS: Windows 10Processor: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700K CPU @ 4.00GHz   4.01 GHzRAM: 32.0 GBGraphics: GTX 1650Direct Version: DirectX 12Other than the hiccups I experience, the game is f***ing P E R F E C T! A 10/10! Nay, a 100000000000/10!!! I hope to see more from Motive and their handling of the franchise. Whether EA ordered this revamp directly, or Motive just said: "Hey, let us work on this project.", I'm glad to return to the horror soaked halls of the USG Ishimura.LATER EDIT:Despite the performance issues, even having to re-load a save to get some assets in place for cut scenes at times, I finished the game with its short comings in the performance department. I truly love this game and can see the work/dedication Motive put into their work, and hope they revisit the performance side of things.The voice acting, phenomenal. The assets, phenomenal. The environment, phenomenal. The slight changes to the story/events and the inclusion of side quests, all handled perfectly. Everything is just perfect!And to those who say the game is 'woke', go touch literal grass. I'm not kidding. Get up and go touch grass, now. It's not a suggestion anymore, it's a demand. _childDocuments_.review: DSR Is Horrific...ly Amazing10/10The original was one of my top 3 games ever and this did not disappoint; though its basically a 1:1 remake of the game.I needed a game like this so bad cuz I've been overwhelming disappointed with most of the games I've played recently. _childDocuments_.review: As you reminisce about the game Dead Space, a flood of memories washes over you. You recall the countless hours spent immersed in its dark, atmospheric world, where every corner held danger and every step could be your last. But amidst the adrenaline-fueled gameplay, there's a lingering sadness, a tale that touches the deepest recesses of your heart.It all began on a rainy evening, the perfect setting for delving into the eerie corridors of the USG Ishimura. As you navigated the desolate ship, you couldn't shake the feeling of isolation and dread. But amidst the chaos, you found solace in the bond you formed with your companion, a loyal friend who shared your passion for gaming.Together, you braved the horrors of the necromorphs, facing each challenge head-on with unwavering determination. But as the story unfolded, tragedy struck in the most unexpected of ways. In a heart-wrenching twist, your companion, your confidant through countless battles, met their demise in a gut-wrenching sacrifice to save your character.The loss was profound, leaving a void that no amount of gameplay could fill. Every subsequent playthrough served as a painful reminder of their absence, a haunting echo of what once was. And as you reached the game's conclusion, a bittersweet realization washed over you: though they may have perished within the confines of a virtual world, their memory would forever be etched in your heart.As you set down the controller, tears welled in your eyes, not just for the loss within the game, but for the cherished moments shared with your departed friend, both in the virtual realm and in the real world. Dead Space had become more than just a game; it had become a poignant reminder of the fragility of life and the enduring power of friendship.

There are enough praises already so I'm just gonna address a few critical opinions (SPOILER ALERT).(Most of the thumbs-down complains about the stuttering issues, so I'm going to address problems beyond performance)- The new Zero Gravity system sucks - annoying and hard to control.- Some of the game's deaths and personalities are underwhelming. Mercer and Hammond's deaths are way less cool than in the original game.- Ending feels rushed. Many details from the final boss fight were removed (like how the Hive Mind grabs your feet, pulls you up in the air, and makes you shoot it while hanging upside down). The whole acid tentacle routine feels extremely predictable.- I kinda like the old Isaac as a silent protagonist. Silent protagonists lead to better immersion. Tthe game creators probably make the new Isaac more talkative because they want to create a sense of continuity into a Dead Space 2 remake.- Not sure how I feel about the new Cross/Isaac hallucination thing. It feels like the creators tried to create something new, but it didn't feel impactful enough for me.All in all it's still a thumbs up for me as EA didn't completely destroy the game - they turned it into something a bit different, striking a balance between old and new audience. It's a 8.5/10 remake for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I should not have to rely on DLSS to have a playable framerate with a 3090. This game is extremely poorly optimized and my thermals are through the roof when I do play. Yes its a visually impressive game but at the very least I should be able to get 60 fps on native. Even with the DLSS I still get occasional stutters and fps drops. That is unacceptable and there is no solution. No mods.Moving past the performance of this game it's a solid remake in the sense that it kept basically everything kosher and improved nearly on everything. The atmosphere is not as daunting and intimidating and that vibe just isn't the same. I will say I do wish they kept Isaac's silence or just really restrict his speaking as I like that it took a whole game for him to finally speak. Also wished they kept his design from the original games and just made him look younger instead of drastically changing his appearance.Overall its not a bad game but the poor optimization really held back my ability to enjoy this title. Get on a deep sale and play during the winter because boy does it burn hott. Not the worse remake but not the best very far from it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should be put on a pedestal as an example of everything that's wrong with modern AAA games.First thing, they didn't improve the gameplay at all. It's the same janky movement from the original, which wasn't that bad back then but should have got an improvement more than a decade later. Funny how this game, which was based on the original RE 4, still don't have quick turn or even a run option that isn't jamming your finger on the analog button. This game fails in everything CAPCOM succeeded with RE4 remake.Graphically the games looks fine considering the technical improvements and artstyle but they failed at the lighting department. The game is supposed to be dark but not like this game, where everything must be lit with a flashlit or otherwise it's just pitch black. It doesn't help the immersion, doesn't make it more scary, it just makes the game ten times more frustrating and harder to navigate.The design of the zombies also got a downgrade, it's one of those cases where you stuff something with a lot of detail and it ruins the semblance of the monster. Apparently they don't twich that much anymore and moves in a more generic way.They also made Isaac insufferable. I wasn't fond of him having voice lines in DS2 but this time it just turned him into some edgyboy, so out of place for an engineer that is supposed to be immersed deep into the most horrific thing someone could experience in their life. He talks more like your generic combat marine pissed off than anything.And last, there's the "updated for modern audiences", with characters that don't look or act like the originals at all, with Nicole being the biggest letdown of them all. Isaac got changed to for whatever reason and looks completely uninteresting and generic.And yeah, couldn't miss how this game runs terribly and stutters a lot.So in the end, this is a pointless and creatively bankrupt remake from your truly EA, who killed and butchered this franchised back with DS 3 and now with this game that should've been just a simple remaster. Which is funny though, it would've been the cheapest options. But who knows what is inside souless corporate CEOs heads. The company even went into anti-consumer practices, like keeping the OG game buried and out from sales.Just play the original game, it still runs fine.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible remake all around. Having been a fan of the franchise since 2008, the amout of attention to detail and care Motive evidently took to emulate the atmosphere and feel of the original game is staggering. Overall, I'd say they took quite a bit of tonal inspiration from Dead Space 2, which is seen and felt in setpieces and in the overall pacing, while maintaining the isolation and claustrophobia that defined the original Dead Space. In terms of plot, the overarching story is the same as in the original but with subtle connections to other Dead Space media (2, 3, Extraction and even books and movies) as well as explanations that flesh out and expand on aspects of the original's narrative that weren't as well explained as they could've been. A particular reveal at the end is especially clever, I won't spoil it here but it improves on the original and shows genuine care on Motive's part.The gameplay is familiar to anyone who's played these games, with DS2's zero-g traversal and expanded kinesis making an appearance as well as the addition of side-quests and a freely explorable Ishimura. It's a winning combination.The only nitpick I could think of is that some of the original VAs fit their characters better, particularly Hammond's and Kyne's, but they still did a great job. Overall then, this is a great title, I hope its success paves the way for new Dead Space games.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5 / 10I never played the original so my review is absent of any nostalgia. I grew up on survival horror like Resident Evil and Silent Hill but somehow never got around to playing these games. I loved this game. Playing this remake was extremely fun. I thought the combat was great. The weapon variety, the enemy variety, the balance of figuring out which weapons work best on which enemies was challenging to master.The graphics are amazing as well as the level design. I was constantly stopping throughout the game to admire the level of detail that was put into the environments. My jaw dropped when I first entered the bridge. It was so cool to see!The game performed extremely well for a brand new AAA release. We've all seen many new, big budget releases drop with numerous bugs and issues. However, I ran into very few hitches. Maybe the occasional hiccup but nothing to take away from my enjoyment.The story was interesting as well. I took my time to read and listen to the lore in the game and found it all very interesting. The missions felt diverse and very practical given the setting and story.The only complaints I have for this game are: 1) the menu was not very user friendly. Trying to swap weapons in your inventory was frustrating while under duress, and trying to shift things around in a specific order was cumbersome. 2) The game did start off a little slow imo. Didn't do much to move the story forward or give you any lore in the first couple hours. The combat difficult was very trivial in those first couple hours. It didn't exactly hook me right away but once it did it never let go. Overall, I loved it and can't recommend it enough. Please buy this game so we can convince EA to fund remakes of the other Dead Space games. I would love to try out those too!

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this good game to everyone. Overall gameplay experience was good even though it was not totally perfect. The problem with the flawed melee combat system of The Callisto Protocol game is gone since there is only shooting in Dead Space. The story is as great as the original. The only problems I have with this game and it is very annoying most of the time is switching between weapons in the inventory and weapon slots. The weapon interface is not that great. It must be a joke for anyone to think that it is ok for players to manage items or weapons in inventory while monsters or enemies are right in front. This tends to happen when 2-3 weapons ran out of ammo within weapon slots so players are forced to choose other weapons from the inventory list during combat which is silly. There are only 4 weapon slots while there were more than 4 weapons that Isaac can use. This is stupid, very annoying and I don't see the point of this. This  makes it difficult to switch between weapons because there aren't enough slots for them. In other games I played, we can press 1 to 8 and select any weapons available but in this game we can only select 1 to 4 weapons in the slots and the only way to select 5th and 6th weapon is to access inventory which is absolute joke especially when we were in a combat. But who has plenty of time to manage items or weapons in inventory when there are monsters in front of them ready to rip them apart into pieces? This worsens the weapon interface. For instance, there are times that I do not even know what kind of weapon that I had just selected after so many re-shuffle of weapons between weapon slots and inventory and there was no indication on the corner of the screen to tell player what type of weapon they selected and how many ammo are left. This is very inconvenience. This also leads to one incident that had me killed after switching weapons from inventory like the shooting against tentacle of leviathan in the corridor. I thought that I was still using laser like gun which requires holding mouse button longer to fire but I had line gun instead so I failed to pull the trigger and even worse is that the ammo were not enough and I did not have enough time to switch to other weapons so Isaac died. Most of the deaths were all cheap deaths due to stupid reasons in this game. Also, sometimes running does not work while pressing shift after releasing the aim button which can lead to Isaac's death since Isaac cannot dodge from any attacks.The fight against Leviathan did not impress me much because it reminds me of the concept from Resident Evil in which the monster is very big but we have to shoot very tiny weak spots which are difficult. My mistake was to shoot at the tentacles too early in the fight which had wasted my ammo that lead to my death. It is normal for most players to shoot when they see a monster regardless of their size so it is our instinct to shoot but it turns out that I was suppose to save ammo and shoot at the weak points of the tentacles which was impossible to see until it launch an attack towards Isaac. I wish that there is more freedom for players to shoot anywhere at the monster just like with the regular monsters and make the monster break it into smaller pieces which would also improve the damage physics caused by shooting but this concept from RE would never allow this so it looks unrealistic. It seemed like the developers had rush and did it in a lazy manner to design the boss fight. The only time that I would accept shooting specific tiny weak points is to liberate passages blocked by monster's blobs but for a boss fight is not really a good concept and does not improve damage physics. Basically there was no freedom to shoot anywhere at the giant monster like leviathan.The good part of the story is that this game gives me a creepy feelings about Nicole. I feel that she's been dead before Isaac arrive to Ishimura spaceship and this is why the mad villain doctor was using her 3d holograph to bait Isaac but after hearing her creepy voice from Isaac's radio that sounded almost like paranormal EVP of ghost then that's when I feel that there is something creepy about this. Either she needs to be rescued from that mad doctor or she is already dead and as a ghost. The original game also gave me a hint that Nicole did not make it at the end even if she was still alive during Isaac's visit to Ishimura so I was wondering if they had made a bit of changes to the story that Nicole could have been dead earlier. I was a bit confuse when I saw Nicole at the mining area as a living physical person but the way she talked on the shuttle still gave me a creepiness feeling that this might not really be her and I was right. This is also because I had played the original game and I know that she became a ghost later therefore, it is possible that she might be a ghost earlier in this remake. In fact, the only difference is that Nicole died before Isaac arrives to Ishimura in this remake version, unlike the original game.  It was Elisabeth Cross who pretended to be Nicole with the power of the Marker. Even if the story is a bit different but I don't have a problem with this. However, I still recommend people to play the original game before playing this remake version. This concept of a protagonist with a creepy weird lady who is either a stranger or a known person whom he or she loves but this creepy lady never makes it at the end looks very familiar to Silent Hill 2 concept and Silent Hill 4 like between Henry and a Cinthia in the subway station which gives me a creepy and uneasy feeling which is a good concept in a horror video game but at the same time it gives a sad vibe to the story as well. Anyway, I think that Nicole looks a bit older in this remake than in original game. I think that she looks prettier in the original game even though she looks more realistic in this remake maybe due to improved graphics and textures.For the audio, I think that some of the original game's audio or sounds were better but at the same time there are some sound or audio effects of the environment that is better in this remake. I missed the screaming sound of the monster from the original game when it came out from ventilator's shaft like "ARRR!!!!!!" because it sounded more scary and it was more intense. Originally it sound like half human and half monster so it was creepy but in this remake they sounded more like the growling of the beast which is not as menacing and not as creepy as the original sound for monster. Also when the monsters was dying in the original game, they sounded better and creepier than in this remake like "Akk! Arr!" or like as if they were choking in their own blood which makes it more realistic and creepier. I think that the original game also had a female sound version of a dying monster especially if the monster is a mutated female which was very creepy and realistic if I remember and this is because not all staffs are males of course so it would make sense to also make some mutated monsters as females like the female nurses at the medical area. If they also add mutated female monsters then this could have been more scarier. I don't know why they removed these good audio or sounds of the original game but I think that it was a mistake. However, the noises coming from the ceiling and other sounds in the environment are more scary and better in this remake. The crawling sound in the ceiling reminds me of Amnesia The Bunker and also Alien Isolation game. It gave me goosebumps because I know that the monster was very close but I don't know where it will come out. I also wish that they could have add more types of monster which would increase intensity of fear and horror atmosphere otherwise it might still not look very realistic and it would be kinda boring.Above all, this is a good game and again I still recommend this game to all players even at this price.

_childDocuments_.review: In the eerie corridors of the Ishimura, Dead Space Remake delivers an immersive horror-shooter experience that grips you from start to finish. With every step, tension mounts as you navigate the derelict spacecraft, never knowing what grotesque monstrosity lurks just beyond the next turn. The game excels at keeping you on the edge of your seat, constantly challenging your nerve as you fight for survival against the relentless Necromorph threat.What truly sets Dead Space Remake apart is its attention to detail in world-building. The environment of the Ishimura feels hauntingly real, with its darkened halls and flickering lights adding to the sense of dread. Each area you explore is meticulously crafted, offering both a sense of awe and terror as you uncover the ship's dark secrets.Combat is where Dead Space Remake truly shines. The strategic dismemberment system adds depth to every encounter, forcing you to carefully target limbs to dispatch enemies efficiently. Whether you're facing off against hordes of smaller Necromorphs or engaging in intense boss battles, the combat remains satisfyingly challenging throughout.However, as much as Dead Space Remake excels in its gameplay and atmosphere, it's not without its flaws. The ending, while unexpected, may leave some players feeling unsatisfied. Without giving too much away, it diverges from the expected conclusion, offering a twist that may divide opinions among fans of the original game.Despite this minor setback, Dead Space Remake remains a thrilling experience from start to finish. With its immersive atmosphere, strategic combat, and unforgettable setting, it's a must-play for fans of the horror genre. So, grab your plasma cutter and prepare to face your fears aboard the Ishimura—it's an unforgettable journey into terror that you won't soon forget.
