_childDocuments_.review: It's beautifully Done. An ode to the original. This feels more like a Remaster than a remake. By combing elements (both game play and story) of the first two Dead Space games, we are given this renewed version of the original. Enemies drop ammo when stomped; Isaac has spoken dialog; and there are added holographic interactions that add new depth to the original story. While keeping the atmosphere of the first game, this remaster makes use of the Zero-G movement from the second. The weapon and armor upgrades have also been updated. Each weapon has 1-2 additional upgrade pieces that can be found or bought to add new tiers to it's upgrade tree. These trees come with special features, some of which have not seen in either game. I personally had an issue with my Game pad (Razor Tartarus V2) not working with the game. However, when I switched to a basic keyboard it controlled just fine. With a boosted set of graphics, a fairly up-to-date computer may be needed to avoid some screen lag between menus and at start-up.Over all, 9/10. Highly Recommend, Especially if you love the Dead Space games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Space

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S HERE!!! And it did not disappoint (unlike a previous knock-off). Issac is back in all his glory and the undead stand no chance. This revamped classic still hits home like it did 2008. With more areas to explore and more weapon to try out, this game keeps you on your toes and whispers "Twinkle-Twinkle Little Stars" in your ear. Man does this game look and feel like the old days. Character models could have used a bit more touch ups (Hammond and Issac look like plastic dolls). Performance is crisp and steady. FPS never dipped. Had one hard crash, but a blessing in disguise since I was near death and the necromorph's surrounded me. Overall, 10/10 game. Staring off strong with this classic and developers really delivered on this remake.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all is this a good remake of the old game?      Yes, for sure!     This game instills the same loneliness and horror that the original did with a new coat of paint, excellent new methods of story telling through more conversations that happen as well as audio logs found throughout the Ishimura.  Gun upgrades still feel as rewarding as ever as the player collects power nodes throughout the ship they can upgrade various stats on their tools as well as their suit to improve survivability.  If you like the Resident Evil franchise before they went First Person I can strongly recommend this game.  Maybe not the remake as of yet but if you are interested in checking out the world maybe grab the original, as its still playable and fully complete.      However I will say that within the remake there are a few things that the team did to make the game feel a lot more smooth and less annoying.  The meteor segment that you had to laser focus on in the original title got redone so you don't feel like you have to lean forward and enter gamer stance to accomplish, as well as a few other redesigns that I would rather not spoil.  However a few things to make note, ensure you are installing this game on an SSD not an HDD otherwise some pretty odd things may occur like the following:    When progressing through the initial part of the story one of my favorite weapons in the game was unfortunately missing, The Ripper, a tool that essentially shoots chainsaw blades into your enemies.  Pretty great for dismembering limbs if you ask me, so it was a bummer that it wasn't present where everyone online stated where it would be.  No big deal though I moved on and just decided to use some of the other tools I usually don't use in my playthroughs I have used in the past.       Another thing that came up was that there was supposed to be a big cutscene where the villain, Mercer, explains his evil plans and why he thinks they aren't so evil to Isaac while they are face to face through a panel of glass.  When I ran into this scene it was just Isaac standing there talking to himself.  At the end of the scene an invisible monster broke through the glass and lucky enough since I was using the flamethrower as one of my weapons it wasn't too big of a problem.       Now for the big issue and the primary reason I am even writing this and why I can't justify anyone buying this or maybe I am extremely unlucky... I just got into Chapter 12, the last mission, and I was tasked to put 3 power cells back into a generator to essentially get the main story moving again.  I slowly descend into a pit where they're supposed to be located and to my surprise I could not find them.  Reloaded the game, went back down, no power cells.   Closed the game, checked file integrity through Steam, reopened it, descended into madness and still no power cells.  Now I am stuck waiting for EA to get back to me on a possible fix for this which could be who knows how long.  Further proving that games should NOT be purchased at launch, which is unfortunate because this is one of my favorite franchises.    TL;DR:                   Would I buy it now?  Yes, but only if you are a die hard fan of the franchise or something to scratch that Resident Evil itch.Edit:For some reason when I created another file and ran to the point where the Ripper spawns it was there.  I closed the game, and checked my other file to see if the power cells were there.  The only thing I changed was the game from being on an HDD to a SSD if this is really what caused the issue that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Game is still great but that's an awful bug.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it and at full price too. The atmosphere alone is unparalleled, graphical updates and slight story structure changes only make it better. If they happen near the unskippable cutscenes at all, guess whether they're before or after...As said above, Kinesis while useful is very unreliable. In combat, it's a toss up whether it'll prioritise grabbing A: a spiky thing, B: a coffee cup near the spiky thing, C: a text log off in the distance somewhere.Occasionally the controls can be sluggish, most notably getting Isaac to run in combat.Misc technical issues: enemy pop-in, sound died once, room didn't load when door opened.All else is quality work. The Ishimura still sits proud alongside Citadel Station, the Von Braun and Sevastopol Station as the kings of sci-fi horror settings.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally fell in love with the original game and series, regardless of the short comings those original titles had. This to me is worth the extra money even though I already own the originals on console. On launch week I had almost no issues with game performance. With better graphic and audio fidelity on PC there is almost no competition with the original title on console. I havent played the original on PC so I cant speak on that too much, but with this remastered version I've had minimal frame drops and stuttering and averaged around 100ish fps on a GTX 1660 Super, 64GB 3600MHz of RAM, and a AMD Ryzen 7 3700X. Considering my experiences on other games with lesser graphical settings, I think this game benchmarked pretty well on my PC. My gameplay experience was as smooth as butter even while streaming on Twitch and basically pushing my entry level PC to the limit. I was very impressed with the quality of my experience on launch week. I'm comparing this to my experience on launch week of The Callisto Protocol (which was developed by people who developed DeadSpace originally). This remastered version can be argued as being "just a face lift for the original", but it's not. It performs better than most recent games and does it all while telling the same epic tale that I remember growing up, which also is where I found my love for the sifi-horror genre in video games and even film. I bought the deluxe edition and I would certainly buy it again, even if I only get cosmetic items in game for now. There were a few visual bugs I noticed in game, like the interaction button would stay on an item even if you walk away from it or some bodies would rag doll uncontrollably when you would hit them. And in once instance I had an audio bug where a sound would play repeatedly, I just quit to main menu and came back and it was fine. It's not a deal breaker at all considering those same issues exist in many other games and really dont occur all that often in this title. Also something I noticed in this game that I dont remember being in the original... there are almost no, like literally no loading screens or loading sequences. Even when at the main menu while selecting one of your saved game files, you instantly jump into your saved game from the load menu. That caught me off guard at first and I havent seen many games do that so well. Maybe that's in the original game as well but I cant recall. Kudos to whoever worked on that, it's flawless in my humble opinion. That alone allows a player to stay immersed in the experience and stay in the action as much as possible and I freakin love that!. But yeah I have very little to complain about with this game so far and love that it still has New Game Plus as a feature so I can endlessly enjoy playing the game. Highly recommend to everyone to at least try it out, even if you hated the original game for whatever reason. People are going on about this game being politicized or has some sort of political agenda, bro stop. People these days will complain about anything and everything. If you want a game that crosses the line and is a trash game on principle, go talk to Neil Druckmann about The Last of Us Part 2. You'll get your fix there, not here. DeadSpace is a masterpiece that deserves it's recognition. I would rate it a 10/10 but I'm sentimental towards the original title so take my rating as you will. Stay safe out there!

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just finished my first play through, and I am definitely going back in for the new game+ later. This game is absolutely an improvement on the original Dead Space, and that is a very, very difficult thing to accomplish. The atmosphere has been pretty much better all around. There were a few things from the original game that I wish were in this one, but that pretty much adds up to maybe 4 to 6 specific sound effects that I prefer the original versions of. Other than that, the sound design was all around just better, and the graphical enhancements (particularly lighting improvements) just kicked the atmosphere into the next gear pretty consistently. This game looks and sounds amazing, and it is somehow significantly more immersive than the original. However, the atmosphere is the smallest improvement that was made in this humble gamer's opinion.The most significant improvements come in the gameplay. This game is just ridiculously fun to play. The guns have been drastically improved from the original. Most of the alternate fire modes were change and made infinitely more useful. So I found myself running a loadout that I would not have been caught dead with in the original game. The damage system on enemies and corpses is just objectively better, with the pealing system being used to deliver even more diagetic combat information to the player like which limbs are the weakest on the player's target. The progression system was also improved. There are a lot more upgrades for the guns and no empty nodes. the only barrier to weapon progression is finding upgrades in the game that expand the gun's upgrade tree.The story has also been greatly improved. While I think it comes at the cost of one of the character's personality, the overall narrative along with the writing for each other character is just a lot more cohesive and enjoyable than the original. There are even some characters that you kinda only saw through longs in the original that have their own stories sort of brought to life in this one. I definitely hold this version of the game as my personal head cannon for the series, and I enjoyed the changes to the story so much that I want Motive Studios to make a DS2 and 3 that follow their version of the story instead of the original. Because Motive revitalizes some sub plot threads that came from my favorite logs in the original game, and Motive has opened the door for those threads to be further explored and fulfilled where the original trilogy just kinda forgot those parts of the Dead Space universe. Obviously won't say what any of these things entail. I don't want to spoil this.Last but not least is the Ishimura itself. Along with the stellar atmosphere that both improves and respects the legacy of the original, the completely seamless experience of the Ishimura pushes the entire game an extra mile. There's no loading screens. The tram system is (as far as I could tell) an actual functioning tram system, and exploring the bowls of the massive industry defining planet cracker is as intuitive and terrifying as it ever has been. Seriously, play this game. Then, play the new game+. Then, play it again, and for Pete's sake buy the 70 dollar version. We need to show EA that projects like this are worth the funding. It's been a long time since I played a newly released feature complete single player game that was anywhere near this good. We really need more of these, and we need EA to fund more Motive Studio Dead Space projects.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 is my personal score for this game but it's a must-play horror game among the others like: Resident Evil, Metro, Outlast, S.T.A.L.K.E.R. It's a game everybody needs to experience at least once in their lifetime because it perfectly captures that feeling of ultimate dread and loneliness in space. I became so connected to the characters and to the Ishimura itself (the place where the game takes place).Now why is it not a 10/10? Well, I haven't played the original and I don't know how optimised that game is, but this (the remake) runs fine on maxed out settings on my setup, BUT, and this is a huge "but", it does suffer from many frame-rate cuts and micro-freezes. It's not game breaking but it's annoying from time to time. _childDocuments_.review: If they can/have fixed all the tech issues from release, it's BRILLIANTI have a very special place for this game in my heart as my number 1 favourite horror game to date, so it means a lot to me that it got a remake especially since the base steam version in perma-bugged. This is hands down the game that has restored my faith for horror games coming this year, it has flaws but they're not really with the gameplay or the design of the campaign or the graphics, it's more technical stuff that unfortunately comes with a lot of releases in recent years, that granted can be fixed. The cons immediately i'd say is the performance, on release it had a LOT of bugs, a mix of stuff that ruins the atmosphere, and stuff that can stop your game in it's tracks by softlocking you. My game never crashed but it may as well have done, it would occaisionally go to black screen, 'load shaders' then throw me back in somewhere that i can't get out, i got thrown into the abyss with one white tile beneath me when as i walked into the leviathan room lmao. When trying to NG+ sometimes it wouldn't load anything and it would just go silent and i thought it was corrupted. There was one part in chapter 12 that nearly caused me to start the entire game again because the battery boxes wouldn't load in the room past the 2 guardians, fortunately i had a save, and there was a way to do it that meant touching absolutely no pickups and walking all the way there instead of running, which was dumb. apart from that it's just little things that don't break the game but ruin atmosphere in a game that HEAVILY relies on atmosphere, enemies that just pop into reality or spawn invisible and attack you then become visible, doors and rooms that still need to load as you approach them, just little things like that could be improved so that it feels like a smooth, immersive horror experience.THE PROS ARE SO COOL, the rework on weapons bar the pulse rifle are so good, new guns have different functions and secondary fires now that have new uses, the graphics help MASSIVELY with atmosphere since they did a brilliant job with lighting, the quality and look of people and surfaces is beautiful, the rework of stasis and kinesis in this game is perfect, it just overall feels smoother and more fun. The exploration is better and the world is one place now instead of individual levels and it has some replay value, not much but it's there and the fact that they've made enemies random as you work your way back keeps the tension high. Live gameplay animations was a nice touch, makes it feel like the world is still moving around you and your'e still part of it, doesn't take you out of it with cutscenes like most other games. Weapon upgrades need to be found now so you can unlock more of the node slots on your guns to stop you from becoming OP early, keeping the game interesting and forcing you to think carefully about your resources and options, and the fact that node doors have been removed from the world is great for this and means you don't have to hold onto them, keep upgrading whenever you can.This is a really well done and faithful remake to the best Dead Space game in the franchise and i'd happily put it at 8/10, if they fix the tech issues completely in the future to the point where they are barely noticable it would be a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to turn the spooky bois into a lovely garlic butter steak and potatoes skillet, follow the steps below:INGREDIENTS LIST FOR THE STEAK AND POTATOES1 1/2 lb (650g) flank steak, sliced against grain (if you squish the scary bois you can take some chunks from them. You can use organs as well, but they have a weird squishy taste to them)1 1/2 lb (650g) baby yellow potatoes, quartered1 tablespoon olive oil3 tablespoons butter, divided5 garlic cloves, minced1 teaspoon fresh thyme, chopped1 teaspoon fresh rosemary, chopped1 teaspoon fresh oregano, choppedSalt and fresh cracked pepperCrushed red chili pepper flakes, optionalThe marinade1/3 cup soy sauce (or coconut amino for paleo and gluten-free)1 tablespoon olive oil1 tablespoon hot sauce (we used Sriracha)Fresh cracked pepperDIRECTIONS1. To prepare the garlic butter steak recipe with potatoes wedges: In a large bowl, combine the steak (spooky boi chunks) with soy sauce, olive oil, pepper, and hot sauce. Set aside and allow steak (spooky boi chunks) to marinate while you cook potatoes. (be warned that other spooky bois may try to eat this while marinating)2. In a large skillet over medium-high heat (you can go into the engine maintenance room, very big fire above you), mix 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter. When butter is melted, add potatoes wedges. Cook for about 4 minutes, stir and cook an additional 4-5 minutes until potatoes wedges are golden and fork-tender. Transfer sauteed potatoes to a plate and set aside. (be careful for the babies, they will attempt to yoink the potatoes)3. Keep the same skillet over medium heat and add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, garlic, red chili pepper flakes, and fresh herbs. Lay the steak (spooky boi chunks) in one layer in the skillet, keeping the drained steak marinade for later. Cook the steak (spooky boi chunks) on each side for 1 minute each, until nicely browned – adjust timing depending on how you like your steak.4. Right before the Garlic Butter steak (cooked spooky boi chunks) is done, you can stir in the reserved marinade if you like, and cook for one minute. Add the potatoes wedges back to the garlic butter steak pan and heat through. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if necessary.5. Remove from heat and serve immediately your steak (cooked spooky boi chunks) and potatoes, garnished with more crushed chili pepper, fresh herbs, and a sprinkle of parmesan cheese over the potatoes if you like. Enjoy!I am not liable for any death or injuries as a result of one attempting this recipe.

_childDocuments_.review: Being of an age where i can remember buying the original Dead Space on the first day it was released, i was both excited and nervous to play the remake. We have all played remakes where they heart, soul and meat of what made the original such a great game has been watered down, removed, or diluted to a point where playing the remake damages your fond memories and nostalgia for the original. Thankfully this is not the case for the Dead Space remake. Hand on my heart I loved every minute of the remake. It genuinely felt like I was playing Dead Space, albeit a smoother, better rendered version. I felt they hadn’t lost the visceral, atmospheric, brutal and stunning visuals, sounds and feel that made the original one of the best sci-fi horror games I have played. The story has a few tweaks and alterations that I feel don’t detract from the story, in fact I felt some enhanced the story. _childDocuments_.review: This is unexpectedly an amazingly good game. I've never been a fan of the Dead Space franchise (didn't play the first three games), so this marks my entry into the whole shabang and what an entry it is!This game shows polish, it has a lot of complex gameplay systems and mechanics that greatly help with feeling immersed. Things that other games *coughcough*Starcitizen*cough* promise for years - that when you open a door to open space, all other open nearby rooms and corridors vent their atmosphere - are implemented here. Among a long list of other sensible, functional systems. Sound design is very high quality and the difficulty also seems fair. Also can we talk about just how properly 2023 this game looks? REALLY good. Awesome volumetric light effects, very crisp tonemapping and bloom and the various holo UI screens are also nicely made. This is what I expect a modern game to look like.Also very little if any bugs. Thoroughly impressed.This goes onto my alltime favorite list and I look forward to the NewGame+.

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought it was possible for EA to make a good, fully complete game in the current decade, but EA Motive outdid themselves with this one. It's very rare that a remake/reboot actually stands up to the original, especially for something so genre defining as Dead Space, but this game surpasses the original in every way possible, and is genuinely one of the best experiences I've had in games in quite some time.

_childDocuments_.review: I cant overstate the replayability of this game.  I'm several runs in and i am still planning on another run.There are a good variety of weapons.  All with alternate fire modes.   All with individual skill trees.  Each of the weapons feels truly different, like a new character build.The environments just feel good.   Sounds, random voices, etc.   Really suggest playing at at least a decent volume.  So much detail as well.   Notes and random things on walls.I made the mistake of ditching my first weapon early on my first run.   For some reason though the game decided to not drop me ammo, just little 100 cred chips.   By chapter 7 i had to revert the game from medium to easy.   So word to the wise... keep your first weapon.  Its a beast anyways.My only real gripe, and its minor, is that they left the ability to recover ammo from the rifle.   Creates quite the in game cheat.  Resetting weapon skill trees for near endless ammo in general makes even harder difficulties trivial.    Disabling the ability to reset the trees in hard mode + would have been ideal.Still need a to try a fresh hardmode run with no tree resets.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10This is how a remake should be. It grabs the original, enhances the amazing aspects, changes or improves the ones that weren’t well-received, and then adds better things. 8/10Simply fantastic. The music, sound effects, and everything really contribute to the feelings of being trapped in a spaceship filled with monsters.The VA is the best element here, specifically Isaac having a voice. The first game was kind of weird for having Isaac be that stoic or calm. However, now we can experience how his character evolves and reacts to the world from being surprised and scared about everything going on, to finally going all out and having nothing to lose at the end. 9/10Amazing upgrade. The Ishimura feels even more terrific than before, the lighting is right where it should be. Weapon effects work great, and the Necromorphs are even more nightmarish than before.  9/10Better in every sense, and the best and most claustrophobic moments come courtesy of Zero-G and losing your orientation.  9.5/10The story follows, roughly, the same path as the original one with some significant changes regarding a couple of characters. I believe these changes are really for the best and help paint a more tragic picture of everything that happened and how the Markers warp your mind.Unfortunately, it also changed a minor detail from the original one  but it also adds make those characters more proactive, which is good.

_childDocuments_.review: So I remember playing this game when it first came out when I was much younger. It absolutely terrified me. Hands down one of the scariest games I ever recall playing and it has always held a fond place in my heart and memory. So the remake had a lot to love up to. It has not disappointed. The visuals are absolutely stunning and it has recreated the heart pounding moments I remember so fondly from all those years ago. The immersion, the visuals, the audio and the tension are all worthy of the £50 price tag that some would argue is too high for a remastered games. It does have some teething issues. I run everything maxed out with an R7 5800x and a 4080 and I experience a little stutter from time to time, that being said my frames never drop below 80 in upscaled 4K with DLSS quality enabled. DLSS balanced offers over 100fps and native 1440p offers me well above 120fps. The game does feel less scary than it was all those years ago, but that has nothing to do with the game itself and everything to do with my age. Dead space remastered is, to me, a reminder of what the Callisto protocol could have been. The Callisto protocol was an enjoyable game but it failed spectacularly and creating heart pounding moments and the spine tingling fear that dead space creates. Download and enjoy.*Edit*  They've released a patch and my stutter is now far more frequent.

There's even small tidbits floating around that tieback in to the old graphic novels released alongside the original game.If you loved the original series, this game is a MUST.  If you're a fan of survival horror, this game is a MUST.

_childDocuments_.review: EA takes a leaf out of Capcom's book with the remake of , because not only is this is a remake done right, it's a hugely enjoyable experience from start to finish that enhances the property in all the right areas. This 2023 remake honours the source game in all aspects, even ironing out the original games rough edges and expanding nicely upon the games lore so purists of the original should fret not.  now looks and sounds terrific by modern day gaming standards (just listening to the ship creak and groan is enough to induce pant-soiling in those first few hours without the demonic howls of the creatures on board that will eventually pummel towards you), but they have taken core concepts and game mechanics from the original and modernised them for the better making playing this version of the game far more enjoyable to play.  Now not only do a handful of the mining weapons you encounter offer actual usefulness to the player, each and every tool is useful in this remake and if upgraded correctly can provide a devastating attack that works to the players advantage. I also like how they have integrated the weapons into the game now having the player find them dotted around the ship rather than purchasing them from a store. It's a small change but it adds to the immersion factor greatly.Lore has also been expanded upon,  with new side quests and characters that delve into the motivations of key characters in the game giving it a lot more depth than the original. Many of the big boss fights, while still similar in nature to the original, have been tweaked and changed for the better making the grotesque encounters with them even more terrifying.One major change is the way the game handles zero gravity, which to be honest was a bit messy in the original game. I don’t think the technology was quite there for it when the original made its debut as I generally found these sections in the original frustrating to move through. With this remake they are exhilarating sections to navigate through (one can quickly lose their bearings if not paying attention which will often have fatal consequences for the player) and I regularly found myself drawing deep breaths just like Isaac himself while moving through these sections. I can't stress enough how good they are now. These sections are like chalk and cheese when comparing them to the original.  Another major change is that the main protagonist now also has a voice, but thankfully he only speaks when spoken too so unlike other third person adventures you don't have to listen to the character natter away to themselves constantly (aka Nathan Drake or Aloy) which is an annoying feature in most modern games today. My only gripes is that the game can't sustain the tension of the first few hours due to its lengthy running time so the scares and frights eventually give way to some slight annoyance, especially since the game likes to continuously throw you into rooms with increasing number of Necromorphs. Also enemy variety is a bit limited.  From around the four/five hours mark the player would have encountered almost all varieties of enemies the game throws at you so the surprise factor diminishes somewhat, especially given that the player becomes more of a force to be reckoned with as  the game progresses and you upgrade your weapons.Performance is good for the most part but there are traversal stutters (movement between two different areas) that slightly hamper the game performance. In my eyes these are small gripes though because when eveything is said and done, Motive have provided gamer's with an outstanding single player experience from top to bottom that I can't recommend enough. I am comfortable EA hand over the license to Motive now because they have proven they clearly understand the assignment.Bring on the remake of the second game!
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Space

_childDocuments_.review: The Dead Space (2023) is a stellar re-imagining of the classic that redefines survival horror while staying faithful to the original’s core. As a fan of the genre, I couldn’t be happier with how this game balances tense, atmospheric horror with survival gameplay.The story kept me engrossed from start to finish, and I managed to complete the main campaign in just over 9 hours. It felt streamlined and efficient, with minimal backtracking, which is a refreshing change compared to many games in the genre. Despite its brevity, the pacing felt perfect, and every moment was packed with tension and purpose.The visuals are absolutely stunning, breathing new life into the USG Ishimura. The lighting and sound design create an oppressive and immersive atmosphere that constantly kept me on edge. The Necromorphs are more terrifying than ever, with grotesque detail and clever AI making every encounter a fight-to-survive experience.The gameplay improvements are subtle yet impactful. The addition of zero-gravity traversal and revamped weapon mechanics makes combat and exploration smoother while still maintaining the resource scarcity and dread that define survival horror.Whether you're a returning fan or new to the series, this remake is a must-play. It's a shining example of how to respect the source material while modernising it for a new generation. Dead Space (2023) is a chilling, gorgeously remade survival horror masterpiece. Tense, immersive, and beautifully paced with just the right amount of modernisation. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and faithful remake that takes some missteps in its execution.  As someone that played the original almost ten times, this game feels intimately familiar, but better in almost every way.  Aside from the obvious (visuals and audio), the expanded level design, refined enemy encounters (a certain recurring enemy is now much less annoying), better balanced weapons, and expanded story are all great.  It is a great game, but a few things stood out for me that I feel should have been different.The three side quests should've just been integrated into the story.  They provide good backstory and are more or less along the way of the main path anyway.  As is, they're hard to keep track of due to the game's very limited HUD.  This disrupts the otherwise excellent pacing and flow of the game.There is still a limit of four equipped weapons.  Being able to use all weapons easily in battle would’ve been great fun.  It's a cumbersome limitation that didn’t need to exist.The boss fights are awful.  The boss fights were a weak point in the original, but they were not annoying.  Here, they are.  The changes made have you clumsily fighting for control instead of fighting the boss.

_childDocuments_.review: To describe this product I would sayholy crap im playing a VIDEO GAME from 2023. This is the first "game" in a long time to actually feel like a video game. Controlling Isaac feels really nice and feels like I have control of him. This is the first third person game from a triple A studio in a long time that made controlling the character and fighting not animation based. So everything is very responsive and very much skill based. Speaking of video games and skill, this game will test your survivability repeatedly. I got through maybe half the game before I had my first death. And let me tell you it ramped up slowly in difficulty. Really testing what you as the player had to do in order to survive. At one point I found myself only able to use the objects around me to fight off the onslaught of enemies.So as much as I hate EA, ill vote with my dollars and say this is how it's done. I fear how ever Motive will only be stressed further when it comes to making games and I really hope EA lets this team take their time to make games like this one.Remember, not every game needs to be open world 1 billion dollar budget, to be successful. Motive understood the scope of the project before starting and everything feels so polished because of it.Of bugs I encountered, only 1 and it was easily repeatable where I could fall through the map when jumping off the ledge after hitting the gondola button. But who knows it could be a feature.I still would love to see a Dead Space game where we get to play as a different protagonist...

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space Remake is a new standard in not just remakes, but in survival horror. This game did the impossible, it somehow is BETTER then the original game its remaking. Dead Space Original is no where near a bad game, in fact, if you can't play this game I highly suggest you play the original, as it is still a amazing experience and plays excellently on everything. But if you can, play this version, even if its your first ever Dead Space game, and if you have played the original, this game feels like a love letter to it. Ill break down the parts of the game I like, don't like, and what honestly blew me away.What I like:-The story: It is Dead Space Original... BUT MORE! The main events of the original game are all still in place, The flow of the story still feels exactly like the original. However, the moment to moment events have taken interesting and sometimes completely surprising turns. It honestly feels like they took the story and just added more to it, making things clearer and raising questions that could only really be seen if you dived deep into text and voice logs. (Great example is how Hammond in the early part of the game warns Issac to cut off the limbs, and then wonders if they are actually dead, or if they simply stopped moving. This is an excellent hint to whats really going on, and puts the fear that you can never truely kill these monsters). Issacs new speaking role is a bit of a toss up depending on who you ask, but for me, he never said anything goofy or action heroy, not even when scarey stuff happens. Infact, the only real time he talks is when someone is talking to him, while you wonder alone through the Ishimura, Isaac never butts in with any sort of dialog, which in my opinion was the right call.-The level of detail:The only words that adequately describe the amount of little details in this game is "Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥". The gore is beyond anything I have ever seen in a videogame, period. from muscle tearing off, to limbs going limp in their sockets before falling off the necromorph, to the random corpses all around the Ishimura having extremely detailed peel systems all on their own! (I was messing around and shot this corpse in the face, and his face came off, but still left his hair, making who it was recognizable. Even when the head was severed, it kept its model and damage.). Isaacs stomp becomes more vocally and physically aggressive as the game goes on, and he can deliver his dialog in different tones depending on his health state. Lets not mention the blood detail in the game, from the blood that slashes onto isaac, to the slow drip of it off walls and issacs visor. The facial Animations and character movements are almost uncanny, but still visually pleasing and feel natural, honestly there are so many little details I literally cannot list or even remember all of them here, there is so so much.-The Scares:I thought going in this game wouldn't scare or startle me, as I've played the original Dead Space and Dead Space 2 what feels like hundreds of times on my Xbox. However, this game has genuinely scared me, due to the seemingly random nature of the Nekromorphs.(While playing I was ambushed by a nekromorph, but because of how the game set me on edge, a moving light tricked my brain into thinking I was being attacked from the side, only to be slashed while I was distracted by the first Nekromorph. It was a genuinely fun scene and I really felt got in a good way). The Ai of the Nekromorphs aren't Einsteins, but they feel like a genuine threat with their habit of pincering you from front to back, and on one occasion I had a nekromorph I was running from disappear, only to find it hiding in an alcove waiting to strike when I went back, genuinely good ai that make combat really fun and ususally, frantic.The Visuals: The requires a beefy system but not because its un-optimized, but because there is genuinely just stupid amounts of detail. It genuinely looks better then the Callisto Protocol while performing 5 times better. (BIG NOTE: CURRENTLY THIS GAME DOES NOT WORK WELL ON THE STEAM DECK). It does drop frames during really big events in the game, or randomly while it seems to be loading parts of the map, but they are few and far between enough not to bother me too badly, but its important to keep it in mind. There is one suit in the game that looks... awful, but that's on purpose since its the unaltered suit from the original game! The things I found troublesome or didn't like(Nick pick) Isaacs Appearance: I don't prefer the new look, but I understand why they changed him. It doesn't really affect my gameplay so its fine.Frame Drops: This is a medium issue for me, but it happens enough that it can be a little urksome. I think its likely a shader issue.That's it.What Blew me Away:The amount of detail, to commitment to the original games feel, and the genuine actual fact this game is a complete package right out the gate. The game even has a secret ending and a New Game Plus, it reminds me of the days where games were passion projects and the people behind the software loved and cared for the game in all its aspects. From the Optimization (which still needs a little work) to the details with blood and gore, to animations to movement, to the voice acting to the natural flow from one area to another. It is to Dead Space as Black Mesa was to the original Half Life, a fantastic recreation worthy of all the praise it is collecting. If you love Dead Space, buy this game. If you love Survival Horror, Buy this game. If you want a polished, complete experience beginning to end, get. This. Game.Go on... Make. Us. Whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the original, this game is an improvement in just about every way and looks absolutely gorgeous. If you're looking for a sci-fi horror game where you get to actually kick some ass, then you have come to the right place. Combat is very fun once you get the hang of it, but the game still manages to keep you on edge, as any good horror game should. My one major complaint is character writing, which I find to be extremely basic and rather uninteresting. By giving him a voice, EA has made Isaac into pretty much the only interesting character, which honestly isn't as bad as it sounds. The actual lore and universe of Dead Space are excellent, so you will still be plenty engaged in the world and story. Just don't expect any of the characters to act in a particularly intelligent manner. Now I'm just wondering if I should play DS2 or wait for them to remake that one as well...

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to love with the changes added in the remake without losing the feel that the original Dead Space had. Isaac talks but not too much, no node doors, and clearer targeting lasers are a huge plus. Graphics look great and the lighting is by and large much improved. Side quests are fun and new game+ provides a good challenge increase in some parts if you aren't already way over-geared. Secret ending does leave a little to be desired and could've been more impactful but I don't think it fell completely flat. The zero-g moving can get really disorienting with it following the mouse directly and I muss having separate objective tracking for stores and other small things but I had as much fun if not more with the remake than I did with the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space Remake is a masterful reimagining of the 2008 classic, taking everything that made the original great and enhancing it for modern audiences. The atmospheric tension is palpable, with the haunting corridors of the USG Ishimura brought to life with stunning visuals and a deeply immersive sound design. The upgraded graphics, along with detailed textures and lighting effects, make every shadow and grotesque necromorph even more terrifying. The gameplay has been refined, maintaining the perfect blend of action and survival horror, while the improved mechanics and voice acting breathe new life into the story. The game captures the essence of isolation and dread, making every encounter feel intense and unpredictable. Dead Space Remake is a must-play for both newcomers and fans of the original, delivering a terrifying, unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dead Space remake is a great game. If you've never played the series before, you'll have a great time. If you have played it before, you'll have a great time too but there are some MASSIVE differences. For everyone saying it's a step above in every regard, I strongly disagree. Some (mostly minor) gripes:-The devs saying they took minor liberties with the story aren't being truthful. This game is not subtle. It assumes you've played the series already or are incredibly stupid. The mystery from the original game is gone, in its place plot points from DS2 and DS3 (please, don't make us do this again...) are front and center / being shoved down your throat. The pacing is out the window and all the quiet parts are being yelled into a megaphone.-The cutscenes grind the game to a halt. You routinely just stand in place and wait for things to resolve around you. Please let us skip cutscenes if we want to - especially on the final boss!-They reworked all the weapons, which is a bit of a mixed bag. Most of my old faithfuls feel nerfed, which is upsetting. Some seem built as explicit hard-counters to certain enemies. Hopefully we'll get lucky and they drop classic versions of the weapons in an update.-The loot table / ammo drops in this game appear to be bugged. Turns what should be a survival horror affair into a frustrating mess at times. Please fix this or change the name to 100 Credits Space.-The game looks gorgeous, but GOOD GOD is it dark. I cranked the brightness up and there were still areas where I couldn't see an object literally in front of Isaac. That's neither moody nor scary - it's just frustrating.-Similar to the lighting, the enemies have been reworked. While not inherently bad, the original's enemies were very easy to decipher based on sight/sound and some of the remake's blend in to each other. Given the hard counters, the darkness of the game overall and the fact some have more health due to nerfed weapons, it can get wonky at times.-The map is a nightmare. For a game that built in backtracking, good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ luck navigating your way around the ship. Please update to drop pins for navigation help. Even with all the above, though, I still easily recommend this game to anybody. The story is the most glaring part to me but only because I LOVE the Dead Space series - 1 and 2 are perfect games to me and I've beaten them over and over. Time to jump into New Game +!

_childDocuments_.review: The good:  This game pulls you in from the beginning and is awesome from start to finish.  It’s a masterpiece.  The gameplay, graphics, atmosphere, and story are all amazing.  JUST PLAY IT.The bad:  This game is BUGGY.  This is the buggiest game I’ve played in over 10 years.  For a game released in 2023 by a major studio… this is bizarre.  Did they play test this at all?  It was launched a year ago, and the bugs happened in January 2024.  WTF!!!Installed on SSD.  16 GB ram.  RTX2070 SUPER.  Core i5-4690K. High settings at 3440x1440.  My specs aren't amazing, but 95% of the time the game ran flawlessly.Be prepared to go to End Process for Dead Space in Task Manager after every crash, which is usually at least once per play session.Some of those common bugs are:Using menus… super slow frame rate, sometimes the game crashes.Exit the game… crash.Start the game… crash (sometimes)Load last save after you die… crash.Changing video settings… crash (and doesn’t save your changes)Enter random small hallway… game crawls to super low frame rates (but other huge areas with a million little objects runs smooth)Alt-tab… crashIn addition to the common bugs, I encountered 3 possible game breaking bugs (spoiler alert)

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think that the original Dead Space needed to be remade. I thought it was perfectly fine, an amazing product of its time and also still amazing still to this day. My mind has not changed on that matter upon finishing this remake since I still think the original stands perfectly on its own and didn't need to be remade. However I cannot lie and say that the remake isn't a great game. In fact, it's actually insanely good, incredibly well made and polished.There isn't much that has changed from the original, but where changes were made, it was mostly for the better. The graphics, sound, enemy design, environmental design, the zero-G segments, the combat - basicly everything feels like it's state of the art, up to date and the game simply is a pleasure to play. HOWEVER. That's not to say that some changes weren't for the worse. Even though all of the voice acting has been re-recorded and Isaac has been given a voice like in Dead Space 2 and 3, all of the characters feel completely lifeless, emotionless, muted and overall just utterly fake when compared to the original's equivalents. Sure, I appreciated the way Hammond's story was handled and the way it ended was in my opinion even better than the original, but it doesn't feel nearly as impactful as in the original just because all the conversations felt fake.The combat had also undergone a huge change but here, the result was clearly for the better in every way. The original's combat feels like a point and click adventure in comparison to the new mechanics introduced in the remake. No longer do you just shoot at the limbs, now you have to take into consideration the individual layers necromorphs are made of. The creators describe it as a peeling system of sorts where you first have to expose the deeper layers of the necromorphs body/limb to then eventualy dismember it and it is so good, you wont believe me unless you try it for yourself. Thanks to this addition some previously garbage weapons were made incredibly useful such as the flamehrower,  however for some reason the plasma cutter still remains to be the most powerful and reliable weapon in the game. Also the upgrade system got remade for the better. No longer do you have to put power nodes into empty slots that do nothing, every upgrade feels like it makes you more powerful.As with any other remake or remaster it's quite hard to simply reccomend the game, even though it's clearly a more pleasant and up to date experience than the original (though admittedly worse in some aspects). The truth is, if you've played the original, aside from the secret ending, which doesn't really change anything all that much, there is nothing new that awaits you in this game. If you've never played the original I think it's a great way to get introduced to the Dead Space series and in that case it's an easy recommend. For some, experiencing dead space again in a fresh new coat of paint could be exactly what they want if they are big fans and want to reexperience their favourite game. In that case a recommendation is also warranted. But for most that have already played the original, I don't really think it's a great investment. Dead Space is a horror game and most of its appeal is lost upon finishing its first playthrough. You already know every section and the horror is simply no longer effective. If you don't mind, sure go ahead and buy it but don't be surprised when you'll feel like it's not nearly as scary or fun as the original. The truth is, you've most likely already had fun and there is only a little more to be had. Climbing the same hill can be fun even on repeat trips, it just tends to be nearly not as fun as or as impactful as it was the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it. The paranoia and dread is still there. You don't know what to expect around the next corner. I just couldn't help myself and HAD to explore the Ishimura as much as I could. Isaac talks, and he's got great dialogue with the rest of the cast. He feels more like a person, rather than a robotic zombie slaying machine. The story is enhanced. There are optional side missions and additional text/audio logs that help you piece together the greater mystery of what exactly went down on the Ishimura and what the deal is with Unitology. I can't say it enough. As far as remakes go; this is absolutely perfect. Music, Visuals, Gameplay and Story are all 10/10.You wont regret picking this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space Remake exceeded all of the expectations. It feels like the original one but better in all possible aspects.1)Ishimura is almost exactly the same as it was back in 2008, but with some major improvements(more places to explore, more ways to travel through ship, feels like actually whole ship). 2)Necromorphs are one of the best twists on zombie genre that I can remember, and here they were improved ever so slightly with new graphics and animations. 3)Addition of side quest doesn't feel forced and actually expands on the original story.4) I've played Callisto Protocol from the day 1, and one thing that was lacking from "spiritual successor" was the atmosphere of fear and hopelessness. Here in Dead Space I got just that. I thought that there was no way I could be scared again after playing the whole trilogy multiple times. But this game manage to recreate those feelings that I had more than 10 years ago. It all boils down to how Motive handled those small details like necromorph sounds, lightning, sudden necromorph appearances, Isaacs heartbeat and many other tiny details. Everything that Motive made screams competence and complete feel for what the audience wants form the game. 5) Characters. They are the same as they were, but expanded on.If you're the fan of the original one, you will have the absolute best time of your life with this one.If you're new to the series, you will get the absolute best experience in horror game genre.Make Us Whole.

_childDocuments_.review: All around this is an easy recommend. If you never played Dead Space you definitely absolutely should. If you DID play DS1 this has enough differences to sometimes be annoying and sometimes be a breath of fresh air. They made a bunch of weird changes to the tram system and progression - there are chapters roughly where they  used to be but not exactly, the chapter isn't a hard break anymore (i.e. no save and break at the chapter, you have to find a terminal), you always end around the tram but sometimes the actual progression is through some new side doors, etc. This is all really Chapter stuff, eliminating the hard breaks. Probably so you can chase down side missions out of order, which are now explicitly listed in the objective tracker.So far I've done the side missions, skipping one on accident, but I couldn't say if it's more story or just busy work.The rest of the game is mostly like you remember it but with a few weird hiccups.  I remember using telekinesis to grab a newly chopped off limb and always getting what I wanted. If you were fighting and used TK pointed at an enemy, you usually got a claw off the floor. Now it grabs anything but. I've pointed it directly at a plot element (battery I think) only to have telekinesis completely miss and grab a corpse instead. Not a claw either, just a big wet corpse.A few changes just feel like they had to explain away Video Game choices. Lockers are locked in one chapter, then suddenly unlocked the next - no no, that doesn't make sense, let's wedge in a "Security Level" that puts a big yellow badge on everything and gives you an extra button press to open something because you have to unlock it first.  It's very likely this was a change made to make it more of an open game instead of a strict chapter game. No chapter breaks mean no magic unlocking.These are all just nit picking though. Like I said in the first line, this is an easy recommend. If you're truly a purist then figure out how to get DS1 2008 running properly and you'll be set. If you can stand a few weird changes but mostly a very direct remake of the game then get this.

_childDocuments_.review: As you may have noticed, there are occasional negative reviews on this game citing bad performance, and I am one of those people. My current specs are as follows:Ryzen 5 5600XRX 6800 XT (16gb of VRAM)32gb of 3600mhz low latency RAM1TB NVME SSD Running at 1080pSo as you can see, I am meeting and sometimes exceeding the recommended requirements of this game, I've tried adjusting settings accordingly, and don't have any other programs open, made sure the drivers are installed correctly, etc you know the drill. Yet, I am getting persistent frame drops, and freezes, making it really frustrating to play since this is, ya know, a survival horror game where things jump out at you, and when the game freezes when a new sudden thing happens on screen it makes it difficult to react. I made the mistake of holding onto this game beyond the 2 week period that you are able to refund the game, which I get is a me problem, but I had hoped it was some sort of bug that they would eventually fix. Nearly 5 months later, I can't say I'm holding my breath anymore as the game still has these issues. I don't always buy games brand new, I'm not exactly a pre-order collectors edition type of guy, but I was excited for this and wanted to join in with everyone else in the community who were experiencing the game. While I'm glad everyone else enjoyed playing this game when it first came out with no issues, and I am able to see its a smaller group of people that has had these performance issues, however I so painfully wish that I didn't spend the money on this.I can't say everyone is going to have the same issues as I did, but I wouldn't take the risk if I were you.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommendation is no but it's more of "yes, but there's a glaring issue which is likely to ruin the fun".I enjoyed the original dead space back in the day, and this remaster has for the most part done a good job of, well, taking the original experience and making it run well and look good. Unfortunately, notable parts of the gameplay are dated; the enemies stop being "scary" after a while and having them pop out right next to you, behind you, etc. is more frustrating than anything. Rooms that lock up and make X numbers of monsters come out of the closets become repetitive. This is understandable though, since it's an older game being remastered, not re-imagined.However, what kind of kills it for me is the rebalancing and "dynamic loot" systems... that is to say, the "dynamic loot" ensures there's no loot most of the time. You'll be out of healing items with only one magazine of ammo in your different guns and... the game will just throw you 100 credits as loot. And again. And again. And again. oh, you're almost out of ammo entirely, half health and no healing items? You're still not getting squat.It's basically a (very bad) RNG modifier to difficulty; i'm playing on normal but that doesn't really matter much when the game will deny me the ability to SHOOT the enemy and melee is suicide. I even went so far as to look things up, found an "exploit" for multiplying pulse rounds (which was tedious) and stocked up a bit on extra ammo and upgrades... then an hour later was running out of ammo again because there's exactly 0 drops of either ammo or usable amounts of credits. Looking it up, this has been a recurring issue... for some people and not others. The game can just decide to lock out drops and if it does you're just kinda SOL.The constant having to scrounge just kills the enjoyment. i can understand such a thing on high difficulties; not on normal. "dynamic loot" that almost removes the loot entirely so you keep running out of ammo constantly is just dumb.

_childDocuments_.review: Though there are certain stylistic trade-offs going from the original to the remake, Dead Space '23 is an exceptional remake that maintains the expected qualities of the series while taking the liberty to add and improve in small but substantial ways. There are certain narrative changes I don't care for, and the game manages to be more brutalistic and unnerving than the original in some points while oddly toned down in others. What can't be disputed is that the gameplay experience has been massively improved from the '08 title- a fully connected Ishimura and the addition of Dead Space 2 mechanics help bring it up to snuff and make it about as replayable as the sequel. Regrettably, however, there are a number of ways in which it still doesn't quite reach the same level of polish and excellence of 2- there are buffers on weapon switch/alt-fire in certain scenarios, and movement, zero-g navigation, UI usage, and kinesis are all notably clunkier than their counterparts in Dead Space 2. If Motive intends to remake 2, they will have a lot of cleaning up to do on the mechanics side of things. Optimally, I'd like to see them work on Dead Space 4 instead, as I'm more curious to see them take us somewhere fresh and new within the Dead Space world rather than fully retread the trilogy.This review was half complaining but it's only because this remake is excellent, and its flaws should be acknowledged so as to help make a future installment as great as it can possibly be. I love the changes to the upgrade bench, the reimagined spaces, and the massively upped replay value. A solid 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel obligated to let the people know that EA has done the best they could've with this remake. Honestly one of the best remakes I've ever played. The amount of small details blew me away, for example, if you are dangerously low health Issac starts to talk more quieter and sounds injured, meaning if you had low health the entire game, you would essentially have alternate dialog because the devs had the voice actor for Issac do different lines for a "healthy Issac" and a "injured Issac". Another example would be Issac in a vacuum (room with no air) you have a timer on your suit that gradually goes down unless you find a air tank to get more air. If you wait till the last 10 seconds Issac starts to struggle breathing and begins to panic almost, but if you find a air tank just in time you can hear him begin gasping for air up until hes regained his normal breathing pattern. Its as if most games nowadays don't care about the little details and just push for getting a game out there as soon as possible to get a mediocre experience overall. This game proved to me that there are still game developers out there willing to go the extra mile and produce a great game. There are many other great things I could list about this game but the review is already long enough and im just doing this because I felt obliged to leave a review. I rate this game a  and  recommend it to anyone who is contemplating spending the $64 dollars for it.

_childDocuments_.review: While not as impressive now as the original was in 2008, it's still a great game. The biggest problem with this remake is how buggy it is. I lost a one gun/impossible run halfway through to massive shader stuttering. I've done 2.5 playthroughs and had a huge amount of stuttering but it is mostly done during chapter 1 and then maybe once or twice per chapter and not usually in combat. When it does happen in combat you can be killed almost immediately upon recovery. I thought I was going to have to refund the game because the stuttering was so bad that I spent most of the opening scene looking at a series of still images. The stuttering doesn't seem related to performance otherwise, I can run the game at max settings at 70+fps but use reduced settings for 144fps and the stuttering wasn't noticeably improved or worsened by changing graphics settings.The kinesis targeting is horrendous, trying to pick up the claws off a dead necromorph is just as likely to bring the entire arm or even the entire necromorph over as it is the damaging projectile which makes kinesis unreliable during fights, which is a huge disappointment because the remake bringing the DS2 style kinesis onto the Ishimura was one of the most exciting parts of the remake for me. The targeting for throwing is significantly better than for picking up but still not what I would call great. The aiming on controller is also weird in a way I don't experience in the original Dead Space, like the projectiles are smaller than the aiming reticle (. I did my first playthrough without auto-aim and was trying it out on my impossible run but it has it's own problems, like locking onto the air next to a limb and being difficult to refocus it back onto the enemy.If you've beaten Resident Evil 4 Remake on normal difficulty or harder I would recommend playing this game on Hard. Dead Space Remake's hard difficulty is easier than RE4R's normal difficulty, mostly because Dead Space never throws the number of enemies at you that RE4R does. The difficulty seems mostly on par with the original Dead Space, though some sections and enemies are easier or more difficult than before (wall guardians are significantly harder in the remake but the hunter seems easier for example).

_childDocuments_.review: I am at a loss of words.They took a very solid game and turned it into a masterpiece.Easily one of the best survival horrors titles to be ever released, and that's counting the original Dead Space games.It's not just the amazing and faihtful (but cleverly updated and redesigned) visuals and audio.It's the revamped story, expanded levels, updated mechanics, reworked weapons, AI Director (which is one of the best things to happen in survival horror, ever), added side content, sidequests, full backtracking through the entire ship, overhauled (or changed completely) bossfights - There are so many changes and improvements this feels more like a soft reboot than just a "remake".Most amazingly of all, almost every change is for the better. I thought I know what to expect, but this plays *significantly* different compared to the OG, and with the dynamic AI Director pulling the strings I quickly succumbed to the insane, unpredictable tension I rarely, if ever, witnessed in a video game before. _childDocuments_.review: I'll be the first to admit. I expected this game to crash and burn. To make fun of people that bought what I assumed would be another EA dumpster fire. I was salty over what happened to visceral games and what they did to the series at the very end. When I heard that the original game was being remastered, one of my favorite games ever made that spawned a spectacular sequel , some fun and interesting spinoffs and books, and a deeply disappointing  final mainline entry. I fully expected it to devolve into a ♥♥♥♥ show that I wanted no part of. Eventually game play came out and while I thought it looked clunky and soulless with a new coat of paint. Eventually I could see the old game I deeply adored buried deep in there and it started to bring me hope for the game that truly brought me into my love of horror games. As of writing I have completed the game and I am about to start my NG+ playthrough. I couldn't have been happier with this game. In my opinion it is a remake in the same vein as the Resident Evil 2 remake. Everything old is new again. The Necromorphs look amazingly detailed and grizzly looking and the peeling system they added that originally thought would be unnoticeable in the heat of combat was a fantastic feature and helped me track which enemies were battle damaged in the thick of combat so I could prioritize better ammo on healthy enemies in order to save ammo and be efficient. Its incredible to watch the clothing, armor and even skin get scorched, severed and even blasted off by the weapons in game. For instant gratification, use the force gun on them. The new "open world" layout for the Ishimura is also a feature that I was skeptical of at first, but as the ship opened up more and more , the more I came to appreciate it. Gone is the old system of locked power node rooms and having to always keep a spare node in your inventory to open the rooms when you came to them. Instead these locked areas are opened up with the new security rating mechanic which greatly improved the feeling of progression for me personally as I would excitedly back track to these areas when ever my clearance increased and I felt the contents of these rooms was almost always worth the trek, more so I would imagine on hard or impossible compared to the lower difficulty where you are just showered in health and ammo. My one gripe with it is why is the Captain's clearance only level one. I guess it could be justified in some way in lore given how things go down but it still seemed weird.Weapons, my god the weapons. Every thing sounds fantastic and really show you how dangerous these engineering tools can be in the hands of an untrained person swinging them around or a engineer hell bent on finding his girlfriend thanks to the peeling mechanic again on the Necromorphs. Everything sounds like it packs a punch and it shows on their corpses after the fight ends. One thing that bothered me at first was some of weapons had their alternate fire modes changed. For example, the Line gun used to have a timed mine that would demolish anything that was near it after its small timer was up. Now its more of a trip laser that does continuous high damage along its path once placed on any surface, perfect for setting up a kill zone when you knew Necromorphs would start spawning in. I ended up loving the new alternate fire modes in the remake and had a blast trying to figure out how to best use them in each scenario, really made the game play feel that much deeper. Hands down, they are all better than the original game's version.The new story is also really good, they made several changes to audio and text logs to really flesh out the lore of the setting. Answering some questions and setting up a few more. I didn't like how somethings were completely spelled out for the player, but its probably for the best as before some of them are only answered in the sequels and kinda messily too. The game also has side objectives Isaac can do on the ship now as well that further flesh out some characters and their motivations. All the characters in my opinion were changed for the better and in some instances much more sympathetic and relatable instead of being just one note bad guys.All in all, playing the game was an amazing experience and it took me a little more than fourteen hours to beat the game and it's side missions and I still feel like I accidentally missed out on a few things at the end, some thing I am quickly going to correct on NG+.It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ what EA did and what happened to Visceral Games, but that wasn't Motives fault. I sincerely hope that doesn't stop people form giving the game a chance. If it helps, then just pretend a different publisher funded it, but in an age where gaming seems to have devolved into terrible copy and paste game design, mediocre combat and truly awful writing. Its honestly refreshing to see a remaster that was more than just a cash grab and it honestly felt like every step of its development was filled with actual passion from some very talented people. As you could tell from my long winded review, I highly recommend fans of the original 08 release to give this game a try and for newer players to try out easily the best 3rd person shooter/horror game on the market. In my opinion nothing even comes remotely close for what the game is trying to do,

_childDocuments_.review: Or Dead Space is a remake of the classic Dead Space from 2008. Dead Space is a third person shooter.You play as Isaac Clarke. Your girlfriend is a doctor aboard the USG Ishimura, a position you advised her to take. You are an engineer and are headed out to repair the Ishimura. When you arrive on station the damage is much worse than you thought. On your way in the auto docking system crashes your ship.The graphics are greatly improved, but the controls seem worse that the original. I last played the original about three years ago, but don't recall so much accidental resource use. I believe this is in part because Dead Space 2023 is also playable on a console. Some items require you to be aiming, others require that you not be aiming. This also happens when you are in Zero G, space. You need to collect oxygen using the E key, the same key that is used to rotate you.You can't jump. I could make a reason why you can jump, like your boots hold you on the deck. But, when you're running in the dark you frequently get stuck because of something on the ground that you can't see because you're either busy running or gunning to stay alive.Saves are at save stations. There are also auto saves, normally before a fight where you are very likely to die a few times until you figure out what you need to do in the fight.There are a lot of jump scares, initially causing you to waste ammo. Ammo and healing are very limited. I tended to use a specific weapon until I ran low on ammo and then switched to one with plenty of ammo, rinse and repeat. Some mobs are best dealt with a specific weapon. You'll notice when you enter an area that you tend to keep getting ammo for a specific weapon, that's your clue that is probably the weapon you want to be using. There are a variety of weapons and you can upgrade them. You can select up to four weapons to fit your combat style. Most of the weapons have a secondary fire function that is a more powerful attack and uses more ammo.The story is very dark, mental health issues, suicide, murder, hallucinations, and much more. This isn't a story for the faint of heart.I had a few times where the game wouldn't close out when I exited and one crash when I was trying to load a saved game. Most of these occurred after hours of game play.A graphically improved version of Dead Space, but the controls seem a little clunkier than the original. There are some fights where you will die multiple times until you figure out what you need to do.CPU: AMD Ryzen™ 9 7950X3DMotherboard: Gigabyte X670E AORUS EXTREME (rev. 1x)RAM: G.SKILL Trident Z5 Neo Series (AMD Expo) DDR5 RAM 64GB (2x32GB)Video: ASUS TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 4080Or

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this hurts more than you might think, giving this game a Neg- review. Dead Space is in my top 10 fav games of all time, likely in the top 5. Back when the original launched, I ordered the best collector's edition you could get, an EA<dot-com> exclusive that included a card that was actually autographed by the dev team, and I still have it. I can't tell you how many times I have played the original game through, but I for sure have beaten it on every platform it was released on, and multiple times on each. I was never a big survival horror fan, I think I have only beaten one Resident Evil game, though I own them all, but something about this game just clicked with me. So, I was extremely happy when I heard they were releasing a remaster of Dead Space, and that Glen Schofield was involved (his is one of those autographs).I installed the game immediately, and have played off and on since, though, admittedly, I expected to have spent a lot more time playing the game by this juncture. The game looks incredible, it looks just like I had envisioned it might, certainly no disappointment in that area. My biggest issue, and I will continue to hold out hope it gets resolved, is the repeated massive frame drops, in the teens and lower, and once the drops happen the game will often linger in those ranges for extended periods. This is literally game breaking, especially in a game that can be rather fast paced at times, and require split second reflexes. Some of the areas with these drops have been puzzling, as there is literally nothing else on the screen other than Isaac, no creatures or movement of any sort.I have installed the game on two systems, a dual RTX2080TI liquid cooled system (yes, I have tried with SLI enabled and disabled, the issues remain in both scenarios, though there is an increase in frame rates with SLI enabled when the latency is not present), and a Steam Deck. On my PC it is installed to an internal Samsung NVMe M.2 970 SSD, and on the Steam Deck it is installed to an external USB SSD drive. Oddly, the Steam Deck suffers from slow downs less frequently than my PC, though they do still occur, with the graphics settings set to the default settings, which I believe are essentially low. I have also tried turning down the settings on my PC, including trying to set them to "optimal" with Geforce Experience, and the issues remain. Another strange finding, is my PC CPU (i9-7940x) has seen temperature spikes, 83C, that are the highest I have ever seen it reach, but my GPUs both are riding between 35-38C for their highest readings. I do not recall my CPU every spiking much over 60C before. I do hope, PLEASE Motive, that they get this resolved soon, because at this point I have no wish to refund this game. Nothing would make me happier, gaming wise, than to play through this game with the incredible graphics, and the new additional content. I will update my review the moment this issue is resolved, which I hope is sooner rather than later.

_childDocuments_.review: Read my extremely detailed review here:TLDR;Remaking a modern classic like Dead Space was always going to be a gamble. With Dead Space (2023), Motive and EA tried to pull off a bold and risky move to bring the series to a new audience, while remaining respectful to the series’ origins. They have largely succeeded in breathing new life into the long-dormant IP with such a quality remake. Sure, it’s not a 1:1 remake like most purists wanted but, Dead Space will surely impress newcomers and fans (at least most of them anyway) with excellent audiovisual design, an even brutal combat system, expanded lore and an immersive campaign that’ll last you anywhere from 12 to 14 hoursWhether you’re a fan of the OG or a newcomer, Dead Space is the first great AAA offering of this year. Hopefully it means more great things in the pipeline for the series. Maybe we’ll finally get the definitive Dead Space 3 experience at the hands of Massive. But that’s food for thought.
