_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great step forward for remakes and how they should be done, for once I find myself, for the most part at least, saying wow well done EA, Good Job! Something I usually only say sarcastically.The game has been masterfully remade whilst staying true and faithful to the horrifying original.A hot topic of discussion has been the visual redesigning of the main character, Isaac. There have been some pretty significant changes to his appearance of which I fall on the side of agreeing with. In previous instalments of Dead Space, Isaac looks like a battle-hardened war criminal who who completely expect to be an absolute apex predator on the USG Ishimura within 35 minutes of landing on the condemned vessel.The new, soft-faced Isaac however, looks like an Engineer. He looks like Isaac Clarke, engineer by day, engineer by night. He looks like he does Sudoku on his break, he looks like he would be a great dad, if your daughter brought him home one day you be relieved! And its this soft shelled engineer appearance that makes your stay on the planet-cracker much more terrifying.The characters are quite well written, they quite believably know what they're talking about without through out too many sci-fi buzz words and I felt decently immersed in the world of Dead Space. I would argue that if anything, Isaac talks too little. You never really get his opinion on many of the events of the game unless he has someone to talk about it too which I thought is something they could've utilised a bit better!The systems of the game such as weapons and upgrades aren't necessarily anything ground breaking which is neither a good nor bad thing, they use tried and true progression systems which never seem to get too stale but also don't leave too much to be excited about. The weapons do however, look and sound amazing, especially some of the heavy duty ones like the Contact Beam!Now for the bad...Hello Denuvo, we meet again, you salty sea-dog. Whilst arguably a game of this profile perhaps needs anti-piracy measures included, it's once again at the expense of those who choose to fund it. The game runs reasonably well with a surprisingly high frame rate when the settings are maxed out (12900k, 3080ti) especially with how breath taking the game looks. However, if anything stuttered that much at a secondary school it would get severely bullied. The 1% and 0.1% lows are horrendous and for almost no reason other than Denuvo cranking CPU usage. It's something you get used to after 6 or 7 hours but something that you ultimately shouldn't have to and if you take a break to play something else and then return to this title, it's just as horrendous as the first few hours.After playing this title for almost 25 hours over the course of two play throughs, my once young and optimistic PC is now a shadow of a machine which I have no enrolled in weekly therapy.All of my other issues with the game are rather insignificant, especially as they had a previous title they had to stay faithful to. Some of the weapons like the rifle feel really underwhelming, especially when playing on higher difficulties or even at lower difficulties before a significant amount of upgrades are pushed into it. It would've been nice to see some alternate skins that weren't locked behind a paywall, but hey, it EA, baby steps right? I was also quite aggravated to be stuck with the LVL 6 suit skin once I purchased it as it bares no resemblance to the engineer suit Isaac iconically dons throughout the campaign. The only other suits being the legacy suit and an award received for completing the game on impossible, though personally once I achieve this I can't see myself playing too much more!Overall, I dig it, I want more.Perhaps some of the more technical, performance related criticisms will be buffed out in the future, Denuvo usually doesn't stick around forever and after a little polish in that regard it might be a near perfect remake!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic remake, and an incredible way to experience Dead Space.The new updated layout of the USG Ishimura does an incredible job of making the world feel real, immersive, and interconnected. You are given multiple reasons to explore and backtrack to discover areas or items. Being able to explore the entire ship once you've discovered the areas feels great, even when knowing a Necromorph could be around any corner.Side missions have been introduced that give you more lore for the world, and expand on the backstories of characters that were only minor in the original.Issac Clarke being voiced is a great positive, allowing him to feel like an actual character with agency, responding to other characters and contributing suggestions to conversations, making certain plot points feel far more impactful and believable.Another improvement on the original is the adjustment and re-balancing to weapons. Weapons like the Flamethrower and Pulse Rifle now actually feel useful, especially once upgraded compared to the original counterparts where they often were only used if my Plasma Cutter ran low on ammo.My only real negatives are- The games performance feels very inconsistent, FPS can vary from a steady 80-90 in one area suddenly down to 35-40 sustained in another.- It should not be verified for Steam Deck at all, for the same reason as above, its performance just isn't good enough, especially as there are areas (like the bridge when multiple enemies spawn) that tank the frame-rate to around 20 FPS and stays there, which just isn't playable.- There are quite a few glitches, some which can soft lock you and be game-breaking, though these will likely be patched pretty quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Dead Space Remake is Dead Space but better. It's a very faithful remake of a classic horror game, and if you enjoyed Dead Space, this remake is the perfect opportunity to revisit a classic. Get it and play it. It's still the Dead Space you know and love, but made bigger and better for modern gamers. However, I'd also like to take the opportunity to review Dead Space as a whole. Now that I am revisiting this classic as an older, more experienced gamer, some of the magic has worn off from when I first played it in 2008. Is it still a good game? Yes, but not as good as I remember it. This is mostly because I played System Shock 2 and the game ended up being one of my favorite games of all time. Since Dead Space was intended to be a spiritual successor to System Shock, I couldn't help but compare it constantly to System Shock, and it came up a bit short in my eyes. That is what this review will be all about. + The limb-based combat system is fun and unique. It rewards good aim and reflexes. If you can aim on a mouse and keyboard, the difficulty becomes trivial. However, if you can't aim, or are on controller, then it'll be a bit rough for you. Dead Space takes the win over System Shock 2 on this one. While I greatly enjoy SS2's RPG combat, it oftentimes felt more stat-based than skill-based. In contrast, everything about Dead Space's combat is skill-based. If you know your enemy's weaknesses, learn quickly, have good situational awareness, and can aim, etc..., the game greatly rewards you for it.+ The story is much improved over the original. Isaac Clarke has escaped from the Silent Protagonist Realm and is now much more proactive and sympathetic. Hammond and Daniels are also much more likable characters and have a constant presence throughout the story. + The game has a more heavy-handed horror atmosphere than System Shock 2. It just gives off a different vibe overall that horror fans may like more than SS2. You constantly feel like you're stuck in some dark, twisted hellhole where the walls are covered in layers and layers of ass cancer and everything around you has more limbs than teeth. Things are constantly bursting out of the walls and crawling down from the ceiling, etc... It's that kind of horror. While I did like this style of horror at first, it did get old very quick, and that leads us to the cons.- Dead Space is extremely unsubtle. It's good at startling me, but not good at making me feel scared, if that makes sense. I'd say the difference is in the enemy presentation and sound design. In System Shock 2, the sound design is more understated. Most of the time all you hear is the ambient noise of space, your ship, and your footsteps. You listen in silence to audio logs scattered throughout the ship, piecing together what happened in complete solitude. Then, slowly, you hear other footsteps that are not your own. You hear indistinct mumbling - voices that are intelligible, but devoid of all humanity, uttered through synthetic vocal chords and mangled windpipes. You are no longer alone, but are among The Many. You can distinctly hear a Hybrid and a Cyborg Midwife, with their characteristic mumbling and robotic screeches, just around the corner. You pull out your shotgun and get ready for a fight. In contrast, the monsters in Dead Space tend to drop into the room with a loud explosion, then scream and squeal as they shamble towards you slowly while the game plays these cheesy horror stings in the background like you're supposed to be scared. When you're about to get into a fight, the game always plays this horror track to tell you all about it. After the 10th time this happened, it was just ridiculous. By the end, I got pretty good at anticipating when the game was gonna pull these cheesy scares on you and was always prepared for it. Maybe they were deliberately going for some kind of horror B-movie vibe? Dead Space definitely takes itself a bit too seriously for that, though. Resident Evil 4 could pass for a campy horror B-movie, but not Dead Space. - The story, while better, is still not that good. The evil space cult trope is even more tired now in the year 2023 than when this game released in 2008. There is also no single clear, charismatic villain that you can really latch onto like in SS2. People on the ship went crazy because the McGuffin artifact is making them crazy, and the space cult is helping the aliens take over. Does this sound dumb to you? Well, it is. SS2 follows a somewhat similar story, but it is much better written and more subtle. There is no space cult, and the backstory of the UNN Von Braun from SS2 is told entirely through audio logs. The writing and acting is so good and you come to care about many of the crew members on this ship through just the audio logs they leave behind. They tell a story of a desperate struggle for survival, of people fighting against something they don't fully understand, and that are manipulating them into doing things they normally wouldn't. If you were to ask me about the story of what went down on the Von Braun, including the who pushed things over the edge, who fought back, who was caught in the middle, etc... I would be able to tell you, but if you were to ask me to do the same for the ISG Ishimura, I wouldn't be able to it. The inclusion of the space cult just prevented me from taking anything seriously. The storytelling of Dead Space just felt unfocused and cliched, which is unfortunate, because the story definitely had all of the pieces that made System Shock 2's story great, but it didn't put them together correctly. - The characters of Dead Space also pale in comparison to SS2. Shodan and The Many individually are a thousand times more interesting than every single character in Dead Space combined. I'm sorry, but Dead Space Remake, even with its improved characters, still do not hold a single candle to the eloquent, chilling, and charismatic villains of System Shock 2. In SS2, your """""ally""""", aka Shodan, is constantly taunting and belittling you. Your enemy, The Many, makes a genuine attempt to try to understand you and make you sympathize with their cause. They are both intelligent and charismatic, and you feel like you are caught up in a war between two beings you couldn't even comprehend. The voices of the crew members in the audio logs that you hear also contain a lot more personality than the crew in Dead Space. You get a glimpse into how they think, feel, and lived on this ship before things went to ♥♥♥♥. System Shock just had strong, stellar characters that you could follow throughout the whole story, which is something that Dead Space struggled with, as Isaac, Hammond, and Daniels don't have any meaningful chemistry or interactions with one another beyond just being a bunch of co-workers working together to survive.- Finally, Dead Space, in its attempt to have a more gritty, realistic artstyle and sound profile to suit its horror vibe, lost a lot of the visual and audio clarity that SS2 had. Environments and enemies in SS2 looked extremely distinct. I could tell hydroponics apart from cargo apart from the bridge and apart from engineering. In Dead Space, everything is just brown and dark. As for the enemies, I can tell a Cyborg Midwife apart from a Hybrid apart from a Psi Reaver simply from their silhouettes alone. Their sound profiles were also extremely distinct. You will recognize enemies by sound before you ever see them in System Shock. in Dead Space, however, I can barely tell the necromorphs apart by their appearances, let alone how they sound. They have bits and pieces poking out everywhere and are all colored like ass. Of course, this is also a deliberate design choice and make them more effective at creating a "horror" vibe, but I simply prefer the enemies of SS2 more.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: great details, low quality animations, horrible and useless backtracking. 8/10 for now.Can't believe i only played for 3 hours so far. I'm of course a fan of the original trilogy, and i enjoy my annual replay. This remake is...well, quite different from what i expected. The atmosphere on the Ishimura will give you chills. In the original game you could hear some distant noises and scraping at the walls, but here it's all over the top: you're gonna look behind you at every whisper and low growl. They really nailed this part. The details are amazing, the ship looks alive (no pun intended) and semi-working. Maybe even too much.I found myself squinting hard to discern drops and ammo on the levels, since they manage to camuflage pretty well among the rubble. Perhaps intensifying the light they emit might do the trick? Voiced Isaac is a surprise and a welcome one. Pretty good voice, rarely pleonastic, goes to the point. I enjoyed Hammond and Kendra too, even if a lot of people seem to criticize them. I dunno, perhaps i'm too used to the superior italian voicing.Now for the gameplay. I'm sure the devs wanted to give us the feeling of controlling a REAL human being instead of a badass gun-toting engineer, but they jumped to the opposite side: Isaac moves in such an awkward and clumsy way that it left me speechless. Do they actually think humans run like that? Also, aiming with weapons is all wrong: there's almost no recoil, the arm is bent in a strange way. Isaac barely moves his body when shifting sideways. This needs some prime work. Take a look at DS2 for reference.Last but not least, including backtracking has to be the worst choice ever made by any dev ever. Considering Isaac's strafe speed, the ungodly amount of doors that open up completely in 2 full seconds, the enemies respawning after you cleaned up a whole sector...it just seems stupid and untested. Locking certain upgrades behind security locked doors is even worse. All thing considered a pretty good start, at least from what i saw in three quality hours. You can tell they put all their love for this series. Give it a try, mods are coming.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe this game is just not for me.I've tried playing the original twice (or maybe even thrice), and did not get that far, and now I've tried the remake twice, too, and I still have the same complaints: it's just not that atmospheric or interesting. I know, sounds strange, when people are praising it for the atmosphere. But it does make sense if you think about it just a little bit.If you do that, you may realize, that the atmosphere is achieved here with just 2 tools: lighting and "jump scares" done by monsters. And within the first hour of the game you already get a situation where you are forced to lose the light for the sake of progression (literally, there are no alternative routes here), and soon after that a "jump scare". Just 1, but you disabled light specifically for it, and nothing else, really. Because if I was an engineer like Isaac, I probably would be going to a fuse box (with just 3 fuses, duh) to open an electric door, but would rather try to override its controls, which are definitely near that door itself. I mean, I have a source of energy with me (plasma cutter), so jump-starting a door should be easy.And yes, I know this is part of simplification of reality for the sake of the game overall, but it just does not work for me in this case. Resident Evil games a notorious for puzzles that often make little sense, but there you are put into a completely unknown and mysterious environment or into one which is somewhat familiar, but clearly had "dark secrets". You buy into the weirdness, because you expect a mystery and a secret. But Isaac has been to Ishimura before, if I am not mistaken, and if her has not, it's a man-made ship in a highly volatile environment (space), so it would be done with proper logic applied to it for the sake of safety and resiliency. So to me, an engineer albeit software one, such "puzzles" just ruin the immersion.Even if I do close my eyes on these nuances, apply "it's just a game" mentality, I still can't get immersed, because there is nothing else, that works towards the atmosphere. Think about it: literally like 5 minutes into the game, when Isaac is closed in a room, with his colleagues on the other side of the glass and monsters suddenly appear, what is Isaac doing? Nothing. Well, ok, he does say like 1 short phrase with almost no emotions, but that's it. Control of the character is not taken away from you even for a moment, even though it would have made sense to do that and show him... Dunno running for the exit or banging on the glass. Really, anything at all, that would show at least a semblance of panic or concern for his colleagues. This might have been ok in 2008, but since remake was being done, why not adjust it? Mafia did work on that, even though the original was already good, why not here?The dismembering mechanic is also kind of... Well, not "boring" per say, but firstly it also does not make much sense (although maybe it is explained later in the game), and it soon becomes somewhat tedious, the novelty goes away. Does it make the game more difficult? Probably. Does it make it more engaging? Maybe. Does it really feel unique? In the end - no. I would much rather prefer the dismembering mechanic be applied only to bosses (which are in the game), specifically so that the encounters felt more personal, even intimate. But when you are doing it on regular basis with regular monsters it just gets too old. Especially since often there is no real dismemberment even: I saw multiple times, how a limb was not severed, even after multiple shots at the same place, but the monster still died. It contradicted the "lore" even.Again, maybe this is just not a game for me. I prefer more personal and, possibly, cinematic horror games. If you are like me in that regard, you probably won't like it either. But if you are looking for a "meaty" shooter with some puzzles and jump scares?.. Maybe that's a game for you, indeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Space

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake of the 2008 original game of the same name. This review will assume you've either played the original or are unbothered by minor mechanical and story spoilers. - Improved visuals - Issac now has a voice, the character did not speak at all in the first game. Dead Space 2 was when he got a voice.- The limb system is improved, flesh will tear off the bone before more force is required to maim a necromorph.- Upgrades are slightly different, arguably improved- Some of the puzzles are different, for instance that horrible sequence where the ADS cannons are offline in the original is dramatically improved.On the following specs I was able to run the game at the high preset at 1440p around 50-90FPS. However, I ended up enabling V-sync to lock it at 60 because the fluctuation became too much.Ryzen 5 5600XRTX307032GB DDR4 @ 3600MhzIn addition to the visuals, the game does a much better job at conveying what is actually going on while still being vaguely mysterious. Of course this is difficult to achieve having played the other two games numerous times.The one improvement I wished was in the remake is the ability to alter what the locator is looking for. Such that you're able to find benches, stores or save stations easier.There are other differences as well such as needing security clearance to open certain lockers or storage units. You won't miss them, it's part of the story. Previously, you would have needed to use a power node to open [optional] doors. A resource used otherwise to upgrade weapons or your suit. Kind of like using a shiv in the Last of Us to open doors.This is a great remake, if it doesn't inspire Dead Space 2 and 3 to also get remade I hope at the very least in reignites interest in the franchise and Dead Space 4 gets made.There are many people that describe this series as “Survival Horror”. And they also say that Dead Space 3 specifically strays from this path becoming an “action” game. Well, I've got news for those people, Dead Space was always an action game — just set with a horror aesthetic and theme. What I believe people intend on conveying when they say “survival horror” is that there is resource scarcity that requires management that makes combat more difficult. Which is not untrue of Dead Space, but on the medium difficulty there's nearly no place where you won't have health packs or ammo. In my understanding, the term “survival” — at least in regards to genre tags — implies there is something akin to tending to needs like hunger, thirst, sleep, etc. But for whatever reason, the survival part of “survival horror” seems to only be used in the more traditional sense. The sense where you are trying to not die. Which can be applied to a considerably large number of games. In any case, I consider the Dead Space series, or games like Resident Evil 4 and older to be action games set in a horror theme. The original 3 Resident Evil games, not the remakes, are what I truly think of when the term Survival Horror is used — 'tank' controls, inability to aim precisely and fixed cameras. But that's just my two cents.

It looks and plays great for the most part. I played w/ all graphics settings set as high as they would go at 1440p w/ AMD FSR 2.0 set to Quality and RTAO enabled. _childDocuments_.review: Disappointment is the emotion I felt after finishing Dead Space Remake. TL;DR: it barely qualifies as a remake, not enough additions and changes. An expanded remaster would have been better. It's still 90% DS1 so it's enjoyable nonetheless, thus the recommendation.Audio design is not as good as in the original: They didn't even properly update the mechanics to Dead Space 2 level:On the other hand plot holes are solved. Isaac's backstory is expanded upon through a text log. Nicole has a series of side quests to flesh her out much more via side missions. References to characters from the prequel comics and Downfall animated movie. A neat detail is that Isaac has slightly different dialogue lines when he's low on health or winded.They added optional side rooms with mechanics to open them like Security Clearance, or switching a Circuit Breaker to choose what receives power and what doesn't. Redesigned the asteroid turret sequence to a more reasonable one. Weapons are better balanced, though the Pulse Rifle is still garbage.Not all changes are for the better, however:These additions are not enough to warrant a remake. The core game is still 2008 with a few QoL improvements and better balance. It had so many opportunities for good ideas, e.g. why didn't they make the Hunter like Mr. X in RE2R which would roam around the Ishimura?DS1 required only a remaster. It holds up really well today. I'm still recommending Dead Space Remake since it's good, but only because it's 90% original Dead Space. If you already own DS1 and don't have enough money for the Remake, either skip it, or wait for a deep, deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I left this review not long after launch and hoped it would be fixed. Changed to negative now as almost a year later and they have still not fixed the vast majority of issues this port has. Awesome remake stifled by an abysmal  PC port.ORIGINAL REVIEW:It's an excellent remake so far! Stays faithful to the original while taking some upgrades from the 2nd one and adding some extras to keep long time fans on their toes. Overall the visual presentation is outstanding! There are some muddy textures when seen up close in the light, but most of the game is dark and looks really stunning. Audio work is some of the best that has ever been done! Positional audio reminds me of the old Thief games but with the added benefit of modern acoustics/reverb. Everything sounds crisp and weighty. For the most part it plays great too for me. Shaders are pre-compiled (hopefully this is redone if drivers are updated too). There are definitely a fair few stutters around still tho. Nothing too bad for me yet, especially after I disabled dynamic res. But this seems to be an issue for most people so hopefully it can be resolved in a future patch.Frustrating to find out Denuvo is in this game too and not listed on the store page. I wouldn't have bought the game until that was removed if I was aware before. There's a good chance that is the cause of the stutters and the sooner they get rid of it the better.Edit: Anyone else noticing the muddy textures should disable DLSS and FSR and just go for TAA. Apparently something to do with variable rate shading is causing the textures to look worse since it's  sampling from the lower upscaled res. Roughness maps look crisp on TAA and I hope they can fix that too.

_childDocuments_.review: Motive follows up their excellent Star Wars Squadrons with an even more excellent remake of Dead Space. While it still stings that EA killed the IP and developer Visceral in the 2010s, it's great to see the love and care Motive has put into this remake. If you've played the original countless times you'll find this release nostalgic yet novel. The devs found a perfect balance between honouring the original and making good quality of life changes. Rather than split the game into distinct levels, the Ishimura is now fully explorable. Paths are still blocked off and only open as you progress the story, but the ability to traverse the ship (with the tram acting as fast travel) to complete newly introduced side quests, or collect upgrades is wonderful. It brings the game closer to titles like Prey (2017) and Resident Evil 2 (2019). There's also the addition of mechanics from the sequels, as well as a suite of accessibility options for those that need them.Two things worth acknowledging: Dead Space doesn't require EA App installation which is always welcome. Additionally, EA hasn't removed the original from sale. So if you don't like this version for whatever reason, the old one's still available!I couldn't be happier with this release, and I hope Motive has more Dead Space in their future!

In my eyes this remake is good enough to flat out replace the original for anyone looking to get into the franchise.I'll keep this review short and to the point. I loved this game. I dumped about 17 hours into my first run and loved every second of it. Well worth the price for me. Amazing visuals and art direction. From what I can tell the game is faithful to the original where it counts and innovates and improves everywhere else. NG+ also seems to add enough to keep me engaged for another run out the gate but I do wish they did a little more. Maybe NG+ exclusive side quests, boss changes, weapons and random encounters. Not a complaint I'm just greedy for more content.The only other thing I'd like to note is the optimization and DLSS implementation are kind of bad at launch. Wasn't enough to detract from the experience but maybe hold off until those are addressed. Lots of hitches and DLSS artifacts pretty bad on some surfaces. Otherwise it's a hard recommend for survival horror fans or fans of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Dead Space by Visceral set a very high bar for what is to be achieved in the framework of whats possible. Dead Space 1 was a masterpiece (ofc only my subjective opinion) and I admit, I was quite sceptical but also hopeful when I heard of the "reboot" announcement.After now some 6 hours and halfway into the game I think I can somewhat judge what I saw so far and what is to come. If anything changes in the later chapters I will ofc edit my review if I see necessary.1. the atmosphere of the first Dead Space has been kept and in some ways even enhanced. The addition of mechanics like the intensity director gives the game a whole new environmental feel. Nailed it.2. The graphics from 2008 look quite dated by now and I am happy to see that the remake has been very faithful to the overall texture design and enhanced it as well to look more modern but also more worn. The new graphics are very neat most times and stunning in some point. 3. Gameplay has been already rather exceptional with the birth of the Dead Space series due to the strategic dismemberment. The Remake improved with the peel system/mechanic an already quite solid system. It also balanced out weapon power quite well because ngl the og Plasma Cutter with full upgrades almost one shots every necromorph. Now I at least need 2. Also the new upgrade paths gate you a bit from over-investing into one weapon/system head on which adds so more interesting progression and also again balances things out a little.4. The story of Dead Space was never exceptional. Fun concept of weirdo artefact go brrrr and cause zombie apocalypse. With the addition of more voice actors and Gunner Wright now completely voicing Isaac the whole game feels more alive (and dead) however sometimes I referred the more silent sections. Also there were some minor changes to story progression which are no problem imo because they tie more into how the characters would act, instead of Isaac being the mindless "Yes Sir, I will do that" guy.For me personally this is a worthy successor to the original and in some ways it is even better (e.g. gameplay). If you liked the OG Dead Space 1, well you will probably like this one. Play on Hard for a nice challenge tho.If you are new: Strap in and fasten your seat belts because you are in for a ride.Always keep in mind what I am saying is in the end only the babbling of a guy who wished to see this game succeed and is happy to go back to one of the adventures of his childhood. Thank you for reading :)EDIT: I had some minor performance issues which I so far could not trace to any hardware component. Likely there are some things that are not optimised perfectly but overall the performance is fine. I had one sever frame drop which fixed itself on the fly.My System:CPU: Ryzen 7 2700XGPU: Asus TUF RTX 3070ti 8GBRAM: 16 GB Corsair Vengeance 3200MHzSSD: Samsung Evo 970 Plus 1TBMB: Asus ROG B450 F V2EDIT 2: When terrain loads in (like after opening a door or elevator) there are some more stutters later on in the game. Nothing to write home about but a lil nuisance none the less. Hope there will be a fix for that. Original evaluation does not change, still a blast to play.Final Edit: *Disclaimer* this includes spoilers:Overall I loved it. The graphical fidelity and the atmospheric pressure on the player are phenomenal. I encountered more performance issues like lag spikes to the end which did not coincide with any of my hardware spiking so I assume it is still a software related issue or rather optimising issue. The end was mostly like I remember it although I must say the bait and switch at the end got me off guard. I stick to what I said at the start: Highly recommend it.As for the performance issues, I hope they will be addressed in future updates and I also hope a better protection software than Denuvo (although I do not know if that is rumors or not) will be used.Anyways I love the original dead space! There is no doubt about it. I have very fond memories of DS1 when I played it as a 15 year old boy. the remake gave me this feeling back. Exploring the known unknown. It gives me back the difficulty of the first playthrough. The remake is how I remember the original to be. Not better nor worse but the same game in a new age. With more nuances and improved gameplay which made me feel like that 15 year old boy again. And for this experience im truely thankful to Motive Studios for giving us this absolute gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Too stingy on ammo:    After getting more guns, the game keeps giving me ammo for guns I don't use, like I've got tons of ammo for gravity gun and flamethrower but no ammo for plasma cutter and pulse rifle.     Poor autosave system:     I ran out of ammo after killing the hunter. Right after that I was dragged by a tentacle and I needed to shoot but I have no ammo, had no choice but to rewind to lose 15 minutes of progress.    In the room with nuclear warhead and two exploding necromorphs, I thought I must not kill necromorphs but slow them down with stasis. It happens I ran out of stasis so I flew back to ishimura and bought one pack then returned then died. When I got revived and went inside again, I discovered I had no stasis. If it wasn't for I found out you can kill exploding necromorphs without them exploding, I would fly back to ishimura again. REALLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FRUSTRATING.     ♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss fight:    No idea how to dodge attack of the hive mind so I just kept running randomly. dying many times because I don't have more health packs.     Leviathan fight was equally ♥♥♥♥♥♥.    Didn't make the fact that you need to kill hunter with something else. In the second encounter it says "kill the hunter", so I thought I need to spend all my bullets on it but it turns out I need to kill it with engine fire? what?    Control:    When you are low on health and spam F key, it doesn't all register, annoying. When you want to freeze enemy with C while shooting, it usually doesn't work and I misused quite a few stasis packs due to this. I was spamming C key and then I let go of mouse2.    Looting is so bad. The animation is slow. You need to press two even three times to loot a box. And it usually misses for some reason. You just can't pick it up. There are many rooms in the game with 5 to 10 boxes to loot. It is so annoying that I just spam E key nonstop.   Puzzle:   The puzzle generally lacks hints. I can remember several times where there is a battery missing and I can't find one anywhere near.   The one where you reroute power in zero-g is horrible. I lose my bearing in zero-g and I need to get close to "the thing" to move it into place. Just horrible experience.   Pathfinding:   Press X to show where to go is great since I get lost all the time. The path it shows is mostly good but sometimes confusing. This is not good experience. I hate open world games that reveal path with a keypress. It ruins the game, you only look at the line, not the world. In a linear experience, it is not that bad but I still prefer figuring out the way myself.    Performance Issue:     I am running this game on a Ryzen 5600 + RTX 4070ti rig at 2k ultra quality with dlss quality. Getting about 110fps on average. Not very optimized compared to re4 which I am getting 170fps almost all the time without dlss. In the last few chapters, my CPU refuse to boost higher and the framerate dips to about 80fps. Not too low but makes me sick because there is A LOT OF STUTTER, whose severity is between minor and gamebreaking. Luckily, it doens't stutter when I am shooting but almost exclusively when I am moving to another room, which you do all the time in the game.    Conclusion:    First few chapters are enjoyable and sometimes spooky but it drags on. At the end I just want to finish this game asap so much that I turned down difficulty for the hive mind boss fight. It is not easy for me to finish a game but not every game finish is good. I have a mixed feeling about this game. It is certainly not bad, but not as good as games I really like, for example, darks souls 3, elden ring and metro exodus either. Maybe I am just really picky and really bad at solving puzzles. I would reluctantly recommend this game since games I can finish is already rare.

The only real complaint I have with the remake is the animations on Isaac feel a bit janky at times, controls can feel awkward at times due to how they changed the health and stasis restore commands, and some the voice acting feels worse than the original, Hammond especially. Overall though it's a fantastic game I can highly recommend both to old fans and newcomers. Easily a 9/10.

Great remake.There is some stuttering as many other users have pointed out even at medium settings but my case was minor and somewhat rare, dynamic spawns weren't Left 4 Dead Director levels of competent despite ambushes being common as Necromorph AI don't seem to dynamically coordinate attacks as a group, the backtracking to open security doors gets a bit dull, the shooting range changes set me up for an expectation that failed to be lived up to when I got to zero-G basketball, using junction boxes really wasn't much of a game changer, sometimes looking for clusters to shoot is a bit of a pain as some areas read a bit poorly at first glance when looking for objectives. _childDocuments_.review: I'm hesitant to call this better than the original in every way, but I also don't understand why there are people calling it just a reshade/retexture when that very much is not what this is. Unlike the original, I actually found this version kind of scary, instead of just having its tense moments. Maybe I like this as much as I do because I've always seen the Dead Space games as virtual haunted houses instead of actual because of how over the top they are. It really is more of a horror themed action series than scary survival horror, and this game managed to capture that perfectly while managing to use it's increased fidelity to amplify the most unsettling parts of the atmosphere, rather than taking away from it. I admit there are parts of this game that do feel less passionate that the original, particularly when it comes to the voice acting, but sub par voice acting is something that rarely takes away from a game unless it's particularly bad, and I otherwise actually kind of like it in horror games as a fan of older survival horror. Parts of the game feeling kind of cheap or even bad on purpose is a trope of the genera at this point, maybe not a good one, but it's one I would say this game does not take to far.  Over all, I am impressed with this remake and also very upset that this IP is still owned by EA.I just saw the reviews for the DLC and felt the need to add that you definitely shouldn't buy that unless you actually want it. EA doesn't need your $10 and they aren't going to use it to fund a Dead Space 2 remake. It's depressing to see that people actually think that's going to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space is a survival horror game that was first released in 2008. The 2023 remake features updated graphics, changes to scenes, and improved gameplay mechanics. In this review, I will be covering my thoughts on the updated version of the game. Dead Space's gameplay mechanics are a mix of survival horror and action-packed combat. The controls are responsive and intuitive, making it easy to navigate through the game's environments and combat scenarios. The game's unique "strategic dismemberment" mechanic, which requires players to strategically target specific limbs of enemies to defeat them, is still present in the remake and remains one of the standout features of the game. I encountered a few bugs during my playthrough, but they were minor and didn't greatly impact my experience. The story of Dead Space follows Isaac Clarke, an engineer who is sent to the USG Ishimura to investigate a distress signal. When he arrives, he finds that the crew has been infected with a strange alien virus, turning them into horrific monsters. The pacing of the story is well-done, with a mix of tense and suspenseful moments, as well as action-packed sequences. The characters, including Isaac, are well-developed and their motivations are clear.  The graphics in the Dead Space remake are a huge improvement over the original release. The environments are detailed and atmospheric, and the character models and animations are well-done. The sound design is also excellent, with tense and suspenseful music that amplifies the tension of the game's horror elements. The voice acting is top-notch, bringing the characters to life in a believable and convincing way. Dead Space has limited replay value, with no major unlockable content or different endings. However, the game is still enjoyable to play through multiple times, and the improved gameplay mechanics make it a more enjoyable experience. Overall, Dead Space is a solid remake that improves upon the original in many ways. The updated graphics and improved gameplay mechanics make the game more enjoyable to play, while the well-done story and characters keep it engaging. I would recommend this game to fans of survival horror and action games.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely sensational remake. No bugs or performance issues with the game fully maxed out. The game looks beautiful while remaining very very faithful to the original art direction. Same applies to the story and game play. The changes to game play are a welcome change, its so fun to be able to go wherever you want during zero gravity instead of how it was done in the original. I was sceptical about them changing how Isaac looks and the fact that he talk but I'm pleased to say they did a fantastic job, him talking feels natural and its nice to see him talking to the other characters unlike the first game. My one gripe with his talking however is that I wish he was a bit more scared. It'd be nice since this is his first experience with the necromorphs and the fact he is an engineer not some sort of soldier. Isaac's new face looks great and when he talks with his helmet off his facial movements and expressions look natural. The enemy design is as great as it was in the originals, just better quality models. The sound design is great as always, however I wish the stomp sounded a bit more impactful, there's nothing better than curb stomping a mf. I am doing my first play through on medium and the enemies do feel a bit tankier than usual. I also think its a joke that you can pay an extra £10 for 5 suit skins that honestly aren't that good. Whether you're new to Dead Space or a returning fan, you wont be disappointed by this remake, its clear a lot of love went into it. Great job Motive.P.S. I hope this game sells well enough that somewhere down the line we finally get a Dead Space 4Edit: Just finished the new game plus mode and achieved the secret ending. Well worth it imo. Now all that's left is an impossible run which will be as much pain as it was in the first game. My opinion on the game has not changed, this is still the best way to experience the start of the dead space story.

Definitely worth experiencing if you like horror games and find the premise interesting.I never played the original and clearly the original was 10/10 for its time. But today, there are a lot of things about it that make it a solid but not great game. The combat and controls are clunky. Enemies mob you and it doesn't feel satisfying to take them down. You can't dodge or dive out of the way so trying to move around enemies just feels awful. You're constantly swapping between weapons just to find one with any ammo.I'm taking some big points off for one horrible boss that can only be damaged with certain weapons but you have no ammo for those weapons so you're just sitting there like a fool trying to figure out what actually can hurt it. And you're running out of oxygen but you can't actually pick up any of the tanks because the boss keeps pushing you away. It's probably the worst boss design of any game I've played and I'm a souls vet.10 hours in and I've barely gotten any interesting upgrades since the upgrade trees unlock so incredibly slowly. I ended up switching to Easy difficulty just to enjoy the story because I didn't find the actual combat or dying repeatedly to be fun at all. There are no interesting secrets, just some new doors that unlock periodically, so you don't feel rewarded for exploring and the progression-based elements like security levels just feel like thinly veiled linear story progression tools. All in all, I'm going to try to finish it but it hasn't blown me away and the combat and controls are so bad that I've switched into just trying to experience the story as quickly as possible and then put this game down

You navigation system is entirely useless and does not make sense.  I mean, you are given access to all of this super high tech stuff AND YET your ability and means to 'navigate' to your objectives is purposefully made over the top confusing, if not totally needlessly yet PURPOSEFULLY super confusing.  So this became so tiresome to me that I started to just lose interest in playing further.  In addition, the character cannot seem to even 'walk' properly, his ability to walk or move at anywhere NEAR a 'brisk' pace, LET ALONE 'run', is entirely STUPID.  As in, VERY STUPID.  I mean, come on now, when a man is in a position where his LIFE is about to end, I am CERTAIN that he can somehow 'must up' the energy and adrenaline to MOVE.  In THiS game, it is obvious that the character is purposefully 'gimped out'.  As if he has been smoking 12 packs of cigarettes his whole life, and is 'missing' one lung.  Thus the game very soon begins to feel 'totally' FAKE.  I want a game that feels REALISTIC, not FAKE.  They did this in order to 'inflate' the difficulty, but I tell you the truth : To DO this ends up producing a game that just feels AnOYING instead of FUN.  There is NO ...SUCH...  THING as 'stealh' in this game either.  You are NEVER 'able' to make ANY kind of 'slow' and stealthy approach to ANY area. _childDocuments_.review: You are sent as a rescue team to help a troubled mining ship, like it's another monday morning. But after setting foot on the USG Ishimura itself, you will soon realize that you too, will wish for a rescue.A classic survival-horror game that still hold up 15 years later. The Remake is definitely one of those modern remakes that don't smell the quickly done work; Graphics are cranked up to modern standard, but some entire areas have been remade. In both cases, old and new rooms will feel just like what you remembered, but in 2023. Isaac is much more relatable as he is talking now, a few dialogues have been updated following this upgrade.The instinctive and original gameplay has been preserved, with a small update given to the weapon upgrade systems, to match the more recent Dead Space 2.Thanks to modern computers, the Ishimura itself is now one giant level that you will explore, sometimes with back-track to precedent areas; some of them will be altered and every room you enter, wheter it is for the first or seventh time, will never feel safe.Necromorphs are an almost constant threat that will keep you on the edge of insanity.Sometimes it feels like a tabletop rpg where you can immerse yourself in the horror of the ship, exploring it the way you want, fighting the way you prefer with the monsters that roam the ship.9/10, superbe atmosphere to look at and play in, good gameplay and instant-classic narrative inspired by movies like Alien and The Thing.I removed one point because 60€ is a bit much for a game you've already played 15 years ago, even tho the amount of work put in it simply transpires.Better than Callisto Protocol

_childDocuments_.review: Why does this get a thumbs down from me?Well, I am a long time player of the House of the Dead series, it is literally a childhood classic for me, so when I saw this remake of the first game, I was excited about it. However, instead of bringing me joy, the game turned around and stuck a middle finger in my face and was horrible compared to the original. Sure, its got nicer graphics, but thats about all I am willing to say about this game that is good. Everything feels too beefy, especially on easy and normal mode, along with incredibly tight frames where enemies can just hit you and ruin your no-hit runs because they simply just got close to you out of camera frame which makes it impossible to shoot them until they just get a free hit off of you. Sometimes, an enemy will also hit you, even if you kill them before they finish their attack animation, which feels wrong. Somehow the original arcade cabinet wasnt *THAT* bad, y'know for being made in 1996. This game was made in 2022 using not only UNITY but a better coding engine, yet it has more bugs and flaws than a 1996 game. On top of that, the game sometimes just breaks on the title screen. and this is a ***2022 game*** you could atleast make the game work on atleast the title screen.I wouldn't call this a reliable remake even from a new player experience.

_childDocuments_.review: What the original does better:-fairness of mechanics. Even though the arcade version still has a bit of jank like getting jumped quickly, most of the enemies are actually pretty easy to kill as long as you understand how they work: shoot the weaker zombies in the head to kill them fast, shoot the stronger enemies in the arms to buy yourself time and expose the head. Some of the really tough and annoying enemies can be dealt with easily if you know how they work. The remake sort of does that, but it's less consistent in that sometimes you'll decapitate a zombie and they'll still be charging at you for one of your hitpoints.-An absolute banger of a soundtrack. The remake doesn't have the original soundtrack, let alone a remastered version of it, probably for copyright reasons. That's understandable and respectable, but if you've ever listened to Chapter 2's "revenge" for the original arcade version, you can understand why I don't want to settle for less.-Bullets actually do real damage. With the remake, it feels like you have to shoot incredibly fast at everything and  you won't get hit. This is especially apparent with certain moments where you can't start dealing damage to certain enemies until an animation is completed, and is even more so obvious with the last two bosses. A full playthrough in the remake is liable to make your trigger finger sore, if the arcade version didn't do that badly enough.-There will never be a situation where an enemy offscreen deals damage to you. This isn't the case with the remake, especially in horde mode. The remake also likes to center the camera to whatever monster you/the game wants to target, making aiming a little difficult at times. To my knowledge, the original doesn't have that.What the remake does better than the original:-you don't have to spend 500 hours learning about PC emulators and sacrifice your firstborn child to get the original House of the Dead running on your computer.

_childDocuments_.review: Me, in 2007: "Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles is pretty great, and probably the closest thing to a House of the Dead 1 remake we'll ever get."Me, in 2022: "The House of the Dead: Remake is pretty great, and probably the closest thing to a Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles remake we'll ever get."Life is wild sometimes. The House of the Dead was one of my favorite arcade games as a kid, one that also provided amusement in college when Typing of the Dead was one of the few games I had on my laptop. As of this writing, having beaten the game to see how faithful it is, I can safely say that it is  faithful, having closely recreated the original level design, enemy placement and event branching while updating the visuals with a modern polish that nevertheless adheres to the original art direction and atmosphere. Similar to the justly well regarded Resident Evil 2 remake, it gave me a sensation like I was seeing on-screen today what my adolescent imagination parsed from the blocky polygons of the late 90s. It also adds a lot of tasteful extra touches, like dramatic lighting in areas that were very flatly lit in the original, unique designs for all scientists that you save, enemies ragdoll on death in a satisfying way and can still be shot post-post-mortem, and so on. The visuals combine reverence for the source material with smart use of modern tech to make for a way better visual experience than I ever figured we'd see in an update for this game. Sound design is also pretty good, and the new voice acting even somehow manages to capture the same weird energy as the original without coming across as tongue-in-cheek or self-aware. I felt very satisfied with the presentation overall. The one minor nitpick that stood out was the use of 30fps video clips for things like the tutorial attract demo and the menu background, which originally confused and alarmed me on start up.As for gameplay, every zombie, scientist, item and branching path flag is exactly where it was in the original game, at least from what I could tell from my first playthrough. This degree of faithfulness did lend itself to feeling a bit easy on the default difficulty, so if you are a veteran of the original you might want to consider bumping it up if you want to break a sweat. I have yet to dive into the game's original modes, but seeing as my primary motivation for buying this was the hope for a faithful and good looking remake, and that's what I got, I felt comfortable making the recommendation even without having thoroughly weighed every hour of game time available. One minor change that I've seen lamented in a review or two is that the game dropped the original's "backtrack through the game" sequence during the credits, but I suspect that might be a technical thing as the remade levels might be too large and detailed to be easily snipped together in real-time, and I do not feel consternation about the developer's decision to spare us more 30fps recorded video in place of live gameplay.If you're a fan of the OG HOTD games, a fan of arcade rail shooters in general, or even someone who just likes zombies and/or spooky houses, I'd say you can definitely find $20 worth of entertainment here. If you desire a more modern style of game, maybe it's not for you, but the clearly advertised fact that it's a remake of a 90s arcade game should have informed your decision even before you reached the review section. If nothing else, buy this so we can get a House of the Dead 2 remake in a similar fashion and then I think I'm that much closer to checking off every item on my list of dream remakes of games from my childhood. I'd appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: The House of the Dead: Remake is a remake of the game of the same name, first released in 1996. It's a light gun, rail shooter game, the type you usually find at arcades. You cannot move the character besides shooting and reloading. You play as agents Thomas Rogan and/or his partner G, as they try to rescue fellow agent Sophie from the mansion of mad scientist Dr. Curien. The mansion is overrun with monstrous creatures, with different shapes and sizes. Some are weak and some others powerful, they serve as bosses.As a remake, this game is near-identical to the original. It's almost a 1:1 remake with better graphics. The original game is known for its corny lines, and this remake still retains that. At least the voice acting and quality is a bit better. The enemy placement and alternate pathways seem to be identical as well, or even if it’s not the change is minor. There are no new story moments, new levels, or anything. If you played with the original game, you will be very familiar with the levels and enemy placement.There are, however, some new features. Like you can play the campaign in Horde Mode, where a lot more zombies appear. But the most welcome change for me is the ability to switch weapons anytime. To unlock this, first you must complete the game saving all scientists, and its not that hard. Then secret chests with alternate weapons will start appearing in your next run. Some weapons are like a powerful crossbow for example, great for killing bosses. Or an assault rifle, for peppering whatever's in front of you with bullets. You don't have to keep using the basic pistol.Length-wise, this game is like what you'll expect, very short. You can finish it like under an hour. But if that's your only purpose, then I don't recommend buying this game, watch a playthrough instead. To fully enjoy it, I recommend trying out different weapons and pathways, as well as hunting for the achievements. Or when you're bored one evening and just want to shoot some zombies. Its not a multiple-hour-long zombie horror adventure like Resident Evil.There is a problem for this game at my end, where it would either blackscreen, freeze, or just downright crashes my computer at a load screen. Even a fresh reinstall didn't fix it. I managed to get it fixed by deleting all files named MegaPixel Studio SA at C: -> Users -> (your name) -> AppData -> LocalLow and verifying the game files. Then start the game and use the Exclusive Fullscreen mode at Options. It works perfectly for now, and I don't want to tamper with it anymore in fear of breaking it again. If you can analyze more, I'd love to hear about it.As someone who played the original game since I was a kid up until a few months ago, I'd definitely recommend The House of the Dead: Remake. Some people say it's nostalgia bait, as its almost the same game just with better graphics and some new features. And while that might be true, it's still worth a try, especially if you love achievement hunting. Go play the original games, and I do hope we get the others released for PC, and maybe some remade as well. Fans of zombie shooter games will definitely love the HotD franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a child, there were three games that pretty much any other kid you met was guaranteed to have played: Tekken 3, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, and The House of the Dead. While the latter did not have the staying power of the other two, particularly after the rail shooter genre died out, HOTD was very impactful in its time. Alongside Resident Evil, it revived zombies in the public imagination - going so far as to inspire the likes of George A. Romero. So when I heard the news that one of my most beloved childhood games was getting a remake, I was ecstatic.Until I watched some gameplay footage, anyway. But I believe watching a game and playing it are often two very different experiences, so here we are: I've finally played through House of the Dead Remake.It's a pile of crap. This has to be one of the worst remakes I've ever played. Given Sega's lack of interest in reanimating this old zombie, I feel like developer MegaPixel and publisher Forever Entertainment's main interests lay in wresting some nostalgia dollars from people who grew up playing the original, because this is clearly not an attempt to introduce a classic to a new generation of fans. There simply isn't enough effort put in. Gone are the iconic character designs, the vibrant and striking colour palette, the campy fun, the well-animated violence, the punchy sound effects and the incredible soundtrack.Instead, what we've got here is a washed-out blob of mediocrity. Everything is functional, and nothing more. The art design is hideous, with only the Hermit boss looking decent, and it's hard to even tell things apart. The fluid effects - blood, slime, water, lava - are distractingly bad and feel like they come from a pre-alpha version of the game. The guns sound like toys. They feel weak too, because the ragdoll physics are so limp compared to the hand-animated reactions of enemies in the 1996 game. I could go on and on.The original House of the Dead had a distinct corny charm born from its lack of self-awareness. House of the Dead Remake feels like it's trying to border on parody, but it doesn't even accomplish that. For whatever odd reason, the serious parts have been made more serious and the comic parts more comic, and the end result doesn't mesh well.The most heinous crime of all is the soundtrack. The original House of the Dead boasts some of the best arcade music in history. House of the Dead Remake's OST sounds like a YouTube musician making HOTD-inspired music, and you know how YouTube musicians are. Everything has been douched up with excessive synths and shred-metal wankery. No sense of proportion. I know, I know, Forever Entertainment didn't license the original's soundtrack and the composer's Twinkies were too soggy and bla bla bla. I also don't give a ♥♥♥♥; I have my own problems. This soundtrack isn't bad just compared to the original, it's bad by itself. It sounds like circus music, and strengthens my feeling that no one making this remake was interested in the cohesive whole as much as their own contribution.This is a very harsh assessment, but I feel MegaPixel's dev team were simply too immature. Talented people who are probably big fans of the original game, but have neither honed their craft nor learned about subtlety enough to have a project like this outsourced to them. The emojis in the loading screens contributed to this conclusion. [¬º-°]¬Playing House of the Dead Remake is like drinking a soda after it's gone flat. It wears the skin of the original, but lacks the heart. 'Soul vs soulless remake' is a bit of a meme, but I feel it really applies here. The original game managed to do more with technology 25 years in the past. Go play that.

_childDocuments_.review: I desperately want to recommend this game, I really do. I WANT to love it. I build arcades and my own light guns, so this game seemed like it was made for me, but I'm gobsmacked that it was released without a shred of light gun support. Even now, well over a year and a half after it's release, playing it on my arcade with my light gun (where it should really shine) is damn near impossible. Even after spending time trying to fine tune the mouse speed to be reasonably close to 1:1 with my gun movements, the game insists on moving my crosshair around for me every time I hit reload or continue. Every time it jumps, my gun's aim is now offset by a random amount. One moment my cursor will be slightly off my gun aim to the left, then it'll be 5 inches to the right, then it'll be stuck to the side of the screen. Please, just give me an option to use absolute mouse coordinates! There's also no multimouse support, so anybody with 2 guns like me is SOL. Honestly, I really wanted to like this game. It does so many things right, but it's impossible to play on proper hardware.

_childDocuments_.review: This remake does capture the feel of the OG pretty well. The game play is fun, rewarding quick reflexes and accuracy.Their are branching paths, different weapons to find, shootable items, secrets and in-game achievements. Would like to emphasise the game is good fun to play.( I have been a bit critical in some of my review) Graphics are good in 4k and run smoothly which is important. Using GSYNC and borderless window mode works a treat. This game does seem to push the PC pretty hard. Reading the comments that some are having crashes. I haven't had any stability issues which makes me think for those with stability issues overclocking may be the issue. This is the type of game that will push a system so if hardware isn't dialed in it may be a potential cause. Sound and music is ok. The audio quality is average. Nothing to write home about but serviceable.I do kinda feel that the audio lets the experience down a bit. The game has branching paths to find and three endings.  As the campaign is short, maybe 15-20 minutes give or take the replay ability comes from getting the unlockables, earning achievements, seeing the different endings etc. I think the campaign could be a bit bigger even with the branching paths. Either that or more game modes, maybe a survival game mode for example. As it is the content is limited.Something I think could be done better is how the combat feels and the general feedback when you shoot something. The combat is ok but I don't quite get the sense of holding a powerful firearm and doing serious damage with it. I'm not sure exactly what it is that feels a bit underwhelming. Also shootable items need to give more feedback when destroyed visually or with better sound effects or be more obvious or something I'm not sure. Shooting bonus items is a big part of the OG as is the branching paths. Making this feel rewarding is important.Overall the game comes recommended if you understand that it's designed for multiple play throughs to see all the endings, unlock all the weapons, earn all achievements etc. The shortness of the campaign, the lack of varied game modes as well as the 'not quite as satisfying combat as it could be' hold it back a little but it's still a good game and worth a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: is a reimagining of the classic game with the same name from 1996. While we will never get a PC release of the original game due to  losing the code, this is possibly the best way for everyone to experience the game. Unless you emulate it, are lucky enough for your arcade to have it, or you can spend thousands of dollars to get a cabinet to go and play the game.I myself have never played the original but there was a cabinet that was at the arcade where I live. To this day, it’s one of the biggest regrets in my life for not experiencing the classic - I did watch a few lets plays on the game, however. One thing I should note is that while I do like some of the changes present in the remake, I do have a few issues with them that I will explain later on in the review.Also, this is the only  title in the mainline games to actually take place in a house rather than a city. has gone into insanity in his pursuit of life and death and unleashes biologically engineered creatures on his staff at the . Two days later, after getting a distress call from ,  decides to go to the creature-infested mansion. The story is rather simple and straightforward, nothing has changed from the 1996 version, and everything remains the same. There is nothing to really talk about in terms of story as it’s quite short, fitting for an arcade release. The cheesy voice acting is there, although while they are still good I am a bit more used to  and  voices from the original. is an on-rail shooter, you follow a straight path where you will have to shoot zombies and save scientists. Saving scientists will reward you with points and sometimes a health kit, be careful however, if shot, your health will go down by one tick. Your score will determine the ending you get after a run, with a total of three endings to get. At the end of each level, you will fight a boss, each having a weak point that the game will show you, with the exception of the final boss won't show you its weak point.There are a ton of collectibles for you to find throughout the levels that will help increase your score. If you save all of the scientists in a level, you can unlock a different weapon to use, however, you must find these weapons in the levels, which require you to replay the game. Although in my opinion, I go the classic route and only use the pistol to fight my way through the mansion.There is also a  mode that you can play which will increase the number of enemies that you will encounter. There are a few different difficulty options you can choose, such as playing the game on the original arcade difficulty.There are multiple paths that you can take throughout the game, these will have different enemies for you to face and different scientists for you to save. The story does not change when taking these different routes, but they have their own interesting ways of going through it all.The original  had one of the best soundtracks that I have heard in gaming history, and I was hoping to get something that was just as good and updated. However, that was not the case here. We got entirely new music for the levels that do make nods to the original in a few ways. Although I can’t fault the devs on this one with the little research I did, it turns out the reason the original soundtrack was not included appears to be unknown but I assume it was due to legal issues.My overall thoughts on the whole soundtrack are that it’s ok for the most part. It will never beat the original and I do wish that it was included but oh well.The  has a very beautiful aesthetic capturing the gothic horror theme very well. Although I should note that the game had a much better graphical feel in the arcade version than what we get here. This also applies to some of the enemy models that simply had better designs. With this said, the designs provided here do have charm and still look good. The game ran fine for me, but I did hear of some performance issues that others have experienced. I may have come across something when I recorded my video on it but I have yet to confirm this.I am not going to lie here, I had low exceptions on this remake, as the original did a great job at what it accomplished. However, I am glad that I am wrong, somewhat. While I do have a few issues with this remake, it’s not entirely the game's fault or even the dev team's. I do recommend buying this game but maybe wait for a sale. While the nostalgia factor is there, you only get about 30 mins of gameplay out of this title. To me, that’s not worth the asking price of 29.99 CDN, a 50% off sale would be perfect for the game to go and pick it up though.I have heard that the sequel The  will also be remastered as well and by the time of my writing, it’s apparently halfway done. I’ll definitely try that game out when it releases.If you want to see a look into how the game is played, then check out the video I made, note that there may be some performance issues from the game in my video.

_childDocuments_.review: The House of the Death: Remake is, as the name implies, a remake of Sega's classic on rails shooter.The graphics and gameplay have been overhauled.The game also features two-player local co-op, multiple endings, and a photo mode.Watch a snippet of gameplay here: In addition to improved graphics and performance, House of the Dead: Remake features new audio, updated controls, a horde mode, leaderboards, a photo mode, achievements, and a gallery.In addition, the remake can be started with 2 players via the local cooperative multiplayer as mentioned earlier.While there are four levels in total, each instance has several routes that in turn put other threats in the way, as long as you are aware of the various criteria. Some paths require shooting a specific element in a room, while another path only opens after you fail to eliminate an exact opponent. Walking these paths is not just for fun or variety, as route A, for example, contains a chance to score a higher number of points, while route B can offer something helpful such as a hidden medkit in a destructible barrel or crateThe game also works great on the Steam Deck: The enemies blow apart nicely and it really matters where you shoot.If you shoot at a hand or arm, you can really see it flying off in pieces, if you shoot in his stomach, you can really see the ribcage.Shoot him in the leg and he'll fall over. Those small details are nicely done and as a fan of the original game I can appreciate this.The story is a little bit different and the level bosses have also been given a new look.Unfortunately, some bosses have received a little less attention than the others, so you sometimes have a whole new enemy and sometimes recognize him one on one from the original, but I don't see anything wrong with that.

_childDocuments_.review: IMPORTANT NOTE: other users in the reviews have reported that this wouldn't load past the main menu. This also happened to me at first on its initial launch as well; after selecting my mode, only the audio was working; shutting it down via CTRL-ALT-DEL and re-starting the game fixed it. This is NOT the first time that's happened with a Steam game on its inaugural start-up, so I won't hold that against it and neither should you. In fact, having used Steam since 2004 (Half-Life 2's digital launch) across 3 very different systems, I recommend that for most games you should get your options configured, then exit-and-restart it, then actually begin playing. OK, on to why this gets the recommendation!I had this in my wishlist for a while but never bothered because the reviews were mixed and my rig is a decade old at this point and has a GPU that doesn't meet the minimum requirements. My system:CPU : Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4770 CPU @ 3.40GHzNVIDIA GeForce GTX 760 w/ VRAM of 1024 MBRAM: 16267 MbWindows 10 (64 bit)But today I got it in a Humble bundle, so why not fire it up instead of waiting for my next build? Well, I'm impressed  I'm giving it a thumbs-up for a few reasons:1) It's giving you exactly what it says it will. I played the original arcade HOTD to completion a few times back when it was a staple of the waning years of arcades, and even a quick amount of time with this revealed that it hits the beats like a good cover should. And since the original source code for HOTD is still lost at this point - as is the code for the original PC port it got from Sega in the late '90s - this remade version is the next best thing.2) It ran just fine after lowering the resolution from 1080 to 720, with all the graphic options turned to maximum. This old workhorse can't do 4k at 30 fps unless it's a sprite-based game, but after the initial launch hiccup this ran without issues. I didn't notice any frame-rate drops either until various parts of Stage 3, and even then it was perfectly playable. Can't ask for more than that. 3) The classic replay options get complimented with your modern trimmings: monster gallery, horde mode, credits system, achievements, stats, unlockables, controller vibration, positional surround sound (nothing like hearing an off-screen chainsaw rev up or a monster moan in your rear speakers!) and so on. HOTD was well-regarded for being an arcade rail shooter, a genre as linear as it gets, to also feature with branching paths and multiple endings, encouraging you even in single-player to spend more tokens on extra replays. This keeps it up.  4) Solid implementation of the controller option. I was born in late '82 and anyone who played light-gun games on an NES controller without the Zapper knows that always hindered the fun. The SNES and Genesis controllers weren't much better. D-pads and face buttons were just the way it was, and ports of coin-op games were...well, the only way to experience Operation Wolf and Terminator 2 etc. outside of an arcade. Thumbsticks, triggers, and sensitivity adjustments go a long way in improving things, and barring a VR port or mod, this is it. (I own the Wii and PS3 ports of HOTD 3&4 and Overkill, along with PS Move and a Sharp Shooter. I assure you, the controls here are fine and beat not having this game at all.) 5) IT'S FUN. Really, I spent enough time with the original cabinet to assure you that this is worthy and worthwhile in and of itself. For those who crave nostalgia and want the exact same low-poly experience from close to 30 years ago (!), nothing else will satisfy. For everybody else, this is just fine and worth the time.As for value? Well, whether or not you buy this at its regular price, you'll get better value for your money than you would have from loading however many tokens you put into the cabinet for a play-through! ;)
