_childDocuments_.review: God game if you like metroidvanias. Though I must say it seriously needs to improve the clues and guides it gives you to complete quests. Other than that, the game is very fun. Good combat, good map, good leveling, ok weapons, very entertaining bosses. Play it on hard and you'll have about 40-50 hours of entertainment. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who got all the achievements in this game, I can say I very much enjoyed it. I originally played the game, got frustrated with the difficulty spikes and quit altogether. Six months later I returned to give the game another chance, and I'm so glad I did. You'll hear a lot of negative reviews complaining about things like no minimap or the stiff combat, which I can totally agree with. But this game also shines in other places, to the point I think the positives easily outshine the negatives.The map in this game is HUGE, literally one of the largest metroidvania maps I've seen which is great, I thought each area really varied in enemy types and visuals. The game is not linear, and it's not always clear where you are suppose to go, but I say this in a good way. The game gives you plenty of freedom to venture off but will warn you when you find enemies that are way above your level.  However, it's very easy to get lost and having to pull up your map every time can be annoying. Yes the combat can be a bit stiff, but I still found it quite enjoyable. Your dodge does not have i-frames till much later, and there is almost no knock back from both you and the enemies. However the skill tree unlocks plenty of unique abilities which had me changing weapons types continuously through the game, and variety is nice. The difficulty scaling could also be improved. At times it can jump so high that you think you are too under leveled for that area, but nope that's where you go next. And the boss fights are mostly good. There were definitely a few where it felt better to just tank hits to get in damage, but there were plenty that had a solid and easy to understand attack pattern that would test your reflexes. And again, the enemy variety type is great with no reskinned enemies that I can remember.And my only other complaint would be the story. It's so chaotic and all the characters are using so many terms from the game's universe that it sounds almost like gibberish at points. I liked where it was going, but all the game's vocabulary had me lost as to what was happening.Beyond that I loved my time with Afterimage. The music was beautiful, the locations were fascinating to explore, and I very much enjoyed the progression of abilities and upgrades. The amount of weapons, armor, and accessories is plentiful, and the platforming and movement was very smooth. I definitely will say if you are looking for a very solid metroidvania, definitely give Afterimage a chance.P.S.- Kudos to the devs, there were a lot of complaints originally with the game and upon returning I noticed many changes that addressed those complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is an enigma to me. The combat and map design are god-tier, with lots to see and lots to do. You have many options for weapons, spells, and armor, allowing for a variety of builds. The combat is fast and fluid, tough but fair, and overall fun and engaging.  Additionally, the game looks gorgeous. While the art style is generic anime fare, but its good generic anime fare. On paper, these qualities would make it one of the best metroidvanias I've ever played.However, Afterimage suffers from two dire flaws that bring the experience down. Firstly, the game crashes frequently. At its worst, it would crash every 90 minutes. I have no idea why this was happening, but at least the generous auto-save system let me keep any items I found ( those from chests at least ). The second, and more problematic issue with the game is how it scales its enemies, Basically, every enemy in any given area is certain level, and if you are more than 10 levels beneath them, they one shot you while you do no damage to them. This on its own wouldn't be a big deal, and it isn't a problem early on when your path through the game is fairly obvious. However, a little over half way through the game, you have a lot of areas open to you, and no clear direction to go. in any other metroidvania, this wouldn't be a concern, since every area would have roughly the same level of difficulty. In Afterimage, all of these areas have wildly different enemy levels, and if you want a smooth difficulty curve ( and enemies you can actually fight ), it has you ping-ponging throughout the world in a non-intuitive way. There is no indicator of enemy level other than a skull over their head if they are too strong for you, and no way to check an enemy's level until you beat them once, so you won't know if an area is too tough for you until you visit it. This adds an incredibly frustrating element to the exploration that almost killed the game for me. I only continued after deciding to consult a guide on where to go, something I have never done for any other metroidvania. This is why the game is so strange to me. There are elements that make it one of the best metroidvanias I've played, and other elements that make it one of the worst. Despite this duality, I still recommend this game for anyone who likes metroidvanias, as long as they use a guide to tell them which order to explore the late game areas. Using a guide mitigates the leveling issue, and saves you from the most frustrating aspects of the game. Overall, its an incredible game with incredible flaws, but those flaws can be managedAlso, the story is incomprehensible, but thankfully, you don't need to know what's going on to enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the demo, you probably mostly know how you'll feel about the game. It's very colorful and you find weapons of different types as you explore. You start with just a sword, but also find great swords, scythes, whips, and at least one other type of sword. There's a ton of space and the level design isn't extremely memorable, but it's memorable enough for you to recognize certain spots. The map also lets you place up to 200 reminders with various icons, which is nice.Combat feels pretty good to me, as it's similar to a lot of classic games in the subgenre. You can have two weapons equipped at once and most weapon hits will keep the majority of enemies from attacking. You can dash forward or backward, which I think works quite well, but you don't get I-frames, so don't be expect to constantly dash through enemy attacks. A lot of enemy projectile attacks can be knocked back to enemies and you can equip a tome to use elemental magic spells. Weapons can be improved with a consumable you'll find on occasion, but you absolutely won't want to use these all the time, as you consistently find better weapons. Afterimage is an action-RPG, of course, and the main character, Renee, levels up upon accruing sufficient experience, which grants you talent points that can be spent on a skill tree. You'll also find talent points whilst exploring. These will give your stats a buff, as well as teach you new abilities for specific weapons. I'm fairly satisfied with all of this. The exploration is similar, as I really feel like the game does a fantastic job of incentivizing you to look in every nook and cranny, as there's a lot of great stuff to find. You'll naturally also be able to backtrack and find new stuff with your movement abilities.Now for the stuff I'm not crazy about. When you die, you lose all of the experience you have on you since the last time you level up. This obviously isn't a giant deal and you'll get it all back by touching it at the spot you perished. Afterimage also makes use of a bonfire equivalent, so you'll respawn at these, as well as heal. Resting will bring back any defeated enemies and refill your healing charges too. The game isn't all that difficult, though, and there's no stamina management or anything of that sort, although your MP will recover over time. The bonfire equivalents are quite far from one another, though. The map also doesn't fill in automatically, and it only fills in the places you've been upon using a bonfire equivalent, which I don't mind so much.As for another thing I don't care for, you can only fast travel by using a consumable (at least, so far). This obviously puts a major damper on going back and exploring, but these consumable might be easy to come by later. Early on, I only found a single one of these, so don't expect to find them all the time in your first few hours. Overall, I'm enjoying the game and it offers most of what I like to see in a Metroidvania. It also appears to be fairly lengthy.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Solidly fun metroidvania. I've been having a blast playing it. The graphics are pretty, gameplay seems challenging at times but fair. Movement and combat feels pretty fluid, especially once you unlock a few skills for your chosen weapons. I appreciate the ability to have two weapons equipped at once and to attack with either based on the situation.To clarify some points from other reviews I have seen:--There is a free fast travel option that unlocks partway through the game, though you do have to go a bit off the beaten path to find it. This allows free, unlimited, transport between any of the major confluxes (ones that appear with green icons on the minimap). There are a limited number of consumable potions available from the start of the game that allow access from anywhere on the map to any major or minor conflux.--I have found the controls to be fairly tight. My only complaint in this regard is that customization does not go super in depth. In particular I found myself wanting to slightly increase my controller's deadzones to avoid accidentally turning around when I release the joystick a little too forcefully.All in all, I think it's definitely worth a playthrough if you like the genre. I am a little bit miffed at the high amount of negative feedback it seems to be getting and wanted to say I have found it to be a very enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: --DISAPPOINTED--The developers really aimed low with this one. Here are the main points that caused me to apply for a refund:1 - COMBAT: My main issue with the game is the combat, it feels too simple, slow and unimaginative. Which makes it hastily repetitive even with the optional weapons, it doesn't have any I-frame, perfect dodge, combos, parry etc that could've made it engaging and fun to master. Combat against enemies and bosses is as follows: dash > poke > poke > dash/jump > poke  > repeat.The  weapon balancing is a bit odd. It's clear that some weapons are better than others so there's no use to diversify. I think they should've stayed with the sword only and add like 20 different fancy move sets.2 - PROGRESSION: For me what really makes it really  BAFFLING -not only in here but in other metroidvanias- is how basic movement like double jump, dash and down-slide is something you need to unlock as you progress, it feels cheap. Some early bosses would've been more fun if these were available from the beginning. Even in the tutorial is somewhat bizarre that you need to pull that jump + release + attack for the slight hover effect trick to get to a ledge, I thought at that point "wow this game must have a lot of micro and deep mechanics that are necessary to learn, nice!" but no, it's  because you unlock dash 20 minutes later. Like WTF. lol3 - OVERALL EXPERIENCE: What everyone is saying about traveling, checkpoints, enemy AI, etc. I also agree with those arguments so I will not rehash those points.4 - VISUALS:  I don't like the aspect ratio/size of the game. Everything feels too small it's hard to appreciate details. I would've preferred if everything was like 20% larger. The rest of the game *feels* beautiful. But the art direction is a bit "safe"; it doesn't have a memorable rendering technique in my opinion. Overall, the game feels like an "ok" game but that it's a bit shallow with the mechanics the developer put on the table. They had a good foundation but the execution was simply, utterly and appallingly featureless.If you are like me that puts gameplay as the most important tenet; I recommend to you the following games:- Eastern Exorcist- Blasphemous- Nine Sols (still in EA but keep an eye on this one)- Awaken Astral Blade (Q4 Release but sometimes they have demos available)
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very large metroidvania, so big that shrinking the maps down a bit wouldn't take anything away from the game.The map marking tools are excellent and very very necessary. Being able to mark the things you'll want to come back for later because you can't reach them now is going to save a massive amount of time.Probably the only major criticism I have is that the story is too sparse. The world building and lore that have gone into it are actually really good, and it would improve the game a lot if there were *more* time spent telling the story, and especially connecting many of the elements. I can certainly see how easy it might be for someone to play this and simply not be able to follow why things are happening, you need to read the souls around the map, do the side quests, etc to have any clue.And it's actually a very nicely imagined world, so it deserves more depth to the story.It's still a great game and I played it all the way to 100% all achievements.

_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this game a lukewarm recommendation.When it's firing on all cylinders, it's pretty solid. The combat feels fluid, and the platforming is fun.The problem is... actually kind of the opposite problem I usually have with games. Most of the time, I play a metroidvania, and it ends and I wish there was more of it.Afterimage is the inverse. The game world is massive, to a mind-numbing degree. That SOUNDS like a good thing, but the problem is that the game doesn't really have enough meaningful collectibles to fill out that map, and it only has about as many abilities as an average metroidvania-- actually, fewer than some.The result is that you spend hours wandering, trying to figure out where on earth you should go next. You'll find dozens of secret corridors in every area, but virtually none of them have anything meaningful-- best case scenario is a small weapon or armor upgrade, but there's so many different weapon types that it's probably one for a type that you don't use.And there's no hints to where you unlock new abilities. After I got the double jump, I wandered for about three hours before I finally googled a map of the game and spent about twenty minutes zooming in and squinting to figure out where the remaining six-ish abilities even were, let alone which ones I could get to.I also feel like the boss fights are... mostly not that great. They tend to have pretty fast attack animations, making it extremely difficult to dodge. They're still not necessarily that HARD, since you can tank most of their hits and heal up in between, and just outrace them, but it means that beating a boss doesn't feel like you learned the fight, just that you cheesed it.I know I just said a lot of negative things, but for what it's worth, I did still enjoy the game. I didn't finish it, because I reached a point where I just got tired, but it was still a fair number of hours of enjoyment. I would probably recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania! No iFrames, who cares, there are _tons_ that don't use iframes; furthermore, the bosses or enemies don't require them. For those who complain about the warp potion.. they're cheap as all heck, I just stocked up and I'm warping all over the place. Overall a very enjoyable experience thus far. Solid recommendation.This game is bad-ass.  I don't know why it gets a lot of hate.  "Can't dash through enemies". Well, if you play the game long enough you can.  100% worth it, one of the best metroidvanias of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game i can say that i loved it and for me is one of the best Metroidvania experiences i have had ever, but also some of the reasons i love the game are some of the reasons why some people will hate the game.The most similar game to it is Hollow Knight a Metroidvania with RPG Souls Like elements and lots of plataforming, that description would be a buy for a lot people but i need to give some warnings and explain why even if you love Hollow Knight you may dislike Afterimage.First and one of the most important reasons is the map, is not that it bad designed, on the contrary the map is well designed and intuitive i just got lost once in the whole game  so what's the problem?, it's the sheer size of it, the map is ridiculously big i don't lie by telling you that is around 5 or 6 times bigger than Hollow Knight's map, one area of the map is around 1/3 of the size of the whole map of Hollow Knight, the areas are massive, which depending on the person for some this would be the best or the worst.Adding to the size of the map, the games has no minimap so you will need to constantly open your map to move around, and even if Fast Travel is a thing in the game free fast travel is only available in the main saving points of the game, if you want to fast travel to secondary saving point you will need to use an item which is scarce until close to the end game and you find the merchant that sell them which fortunately are cheap.About exploration depending on the person it would be good or bad, the game never tells you where to go, the biggest hint you would get is the name of the specific area you need to go, but that's it, there's no markers, no signals, no arrows, absolutely nothing to guide you, which i believe is the intention, because the first quarter of the game the progression trough the areas is semi linear, but once you get a certain item the map opens and you can just go to any of the next areas with almost 0 restriction, your biggest roadblock would be the lack of certain abilities that are needed to keep going, but also most of the time those roadblocks are positioned on a way that you could explore the majority of the area before you need to back track to find some ability you need to keep exploring, is not uncommon for you to ended up wandering on a late game area and managing to explore a really good portion of it even end up getting end game gear when you are supposed to be on early game, so like i said at the beginning some people will love this and some will hate it.About combat is good but nothing super complex, you have 2 weapons your main and your sub weapon, a third weapon which is your magic attack, the weapons are divided in types, it comes from the most common like swords and daggers, to whips and scythes, magic scrolls and staffs, every weapon plays really different from each other so just use every weapon and find what you like, also every weapon has different skills which are unlocked through your talent tree, a problem that i saw with the skills is that i believe that all the weapons are balanced if the skills are not taken into account, but once they are there some really big unbalance, there's a particular skill combo with the daggers and the scythe that is busted and melts everything in the game, also some weapons skills are not particulary good, i believe the Greatsword and the Whip are the most affected by that. Something important you have a dash and a dodge, but bot have 0 invencibility frames until certain ability is acquired so that's a problem for a lot of people, also leveling in the game and the talent tree outside of the weapons skills is only stat boost, so the progression there is really lineal, also the difficulty is not high, i would not say is easy but is not hard either.So about the plot, i actually don't know what the game is about, like it starts as a revenge plot of you avenging your village and your master, but then the stakes became bigger for some reason and it seems you are the chosen one  but also you aren't....., in the end i didn't understood the plot, the lore works really similar to the Souls games which NPC , weapons, items and journal entries have most of the lore, but i would say that in the end the Souls games do a better job of at least giving you hints of what are you doing and what is the purpose of the whole thing even if you don't read any of the lore, Afterimage doesn't do that.About technical stuff, first and the most obvious is that the game looks gorgeous everything is drawn and animated by hand, the areas, enemies, backgrounds, npc everything looks beautiful there's 0 criticism on that area this is one of those games that will look good forever, the sound design serviceable nothing bad but nothing great either it just works and does the job, the ost is good i would say that the songs from the areas are really good and complement the areas wonderfully but some songs in some areas have the problem that don't loop correctly, like the song just ends there's no music for a few seconds and then starts again, there's a particularly noticeable one in one of the early areas, and the music for the bosses is just forgettable i only remember one particular song and that's it, is not that it's bad but there's noting noticeable about those songs.The game runs well i didn't have any problems with it i have a 3060 and i played in 4K on Ultra with no issue whatsoever also outside of render scale, resolution and screen setting, the only other setting the game has is graphics quality which goes from Low to Ultra and i didn't see how it look on low so i can't say if the difference is noticeable or not, i didn't found any noticeable bug nor glitch, nor the game crashed on me and the load times are almost non existent.In conclusion i gave a recommended because i loved the game, but also based on the way the game is designed i can't just go and bluntly say to everyone to buy it, i didn't list anything as a pro or a con because and the end the quirks of this game are the reason why some people will love it and some will hate it, so if what you read is of your liking then go for it you will enjoy it a lot, if you art divided wait for a big discount maybe for you the quirks become more pros than cons or maybe is the contrary just don't buy it at full price if you are divided, and if what you read is not of your liking then just don't even try it you will hate the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely an underrated Metroidvania.Solid combat, tons of exploration, tons of weapons, tons of skills, spells, etc, make it a really compelling game to play.Especially its map, which is HUMONGOUS, even by modern standards, definitely stands out. Gives out strong Hollow Knight vibes.Some really nice quality of life features too: you don't lose health when navigating environmental puzzles with spikes, so you can try to beat them to your heart's content . Fast travel that is not intrusive and requires a semi-rare resource. Skills don't cost mana (spells do), which makes total sense. Dash and air dash available from the start.That being said, some may find its cryptic progression system downright bad. The endings are a mixed bag too, especially if you're not a fan of .All in all, I maxed it out, got all achievements and not once had a feeling the game is a chore, which to me is all that matters. As a father of a little kid I don't have much time for gaming, so if it can keep me in for almost 60 hours it means I find it good. Would definitely buy a sequel, if it ever comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a game this satisfying since Dust an Elysian Tail. The combat feels sharp and responsive, the art is nothing short of gorgeous and stunning and the gameplay feels extremely balanced with every weapon style having their uniqueness. Finding secret feels rewarding and while the combat could benefit from a bit more variety in enemies selection. I haven't felt like it's too shallow of an experience. The various terrain always keeps you on your toe.There's a marking system! Which is always awesome to have in Metroidvania but often feels like developers refuse to give you the tool to mark stuff up and expects you to remember every nooks and cranny on your way. So far the game is everything I love out of a Metroidvania, don't believe the mixed review, this game is worth every cents. Whole-heartedly recommend, can not wait to play more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: GOTY for me so far. Absolutely brilliant. Every area brings more stunning visuals, to the point I was excited to see new areas just so I could discover more enemies and scenery. You feel bad killing some enemies cause they're so pretty! Beautiful, relaxing soundtrack. Fun combat and the weapons are all so great you want to use most of them throughout the game. I've never upgraded so many different weapons except in souls games.Excellent exploration and an outstanding amount of content/map size. Being able to do all endings on one save by just reloading the game is an achievement hunter's dream! I am really terrible at platforming and what I loved about this game is if a section was really hard, a new ability made it possible for me to achieve it later. I REALLY love that. It was like making it accessible without adding accessibility options. The game only had 2 very minor flaws. The resting potions you need to teleport between smaller trees and not being able to sell excess weapons/armour/accessories. Only one major flaw is I am locked out of getting 2 achievements due  but I am hoping they patch that.Despite those things, I 100% recommend this phenomenal game. I hope this game gets dlc and a sequel. It may be my favourite metroidvania ever. It's really up there for me with Ender Lilies and Blasphemous.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth it.  I wasn't expecting to get 40 hours of this game when I bought it.It has a really large map to explore and plenty of secrets to uncover once you unlock (many) new abilities.Combat is quite good with six types of weapon besides spells, so you have plenty of options on how you can play. Only downside I would say is some of the weapon skills that need movement input end up not being satisfying to use (at least on my experience). Bosses can be quite challenging but not one was too extreme to deal with.Lastly, you can 100% this on a single playthough and there are no missables in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the kind of gamer who judges a game's worth by hours played, Afterimage is sure to get you your money's worth. Not since Hollow Knight has an MV been so large, expansive, open ended, and chalk full of secrets that even many veterans will miss. This game's exploration is as deep as the visuals are breathtaking. Just when you think you've seen it all, you find 3 more areas filled to bursting with content. Enemies and bosses are a mixed bag; either being so easy you question why they exist, or so annoying you just avoid them until you can clobber them like the others. But combat is saved by the game's wide selection of weapons, moves, and abilities you can customize as you see fit. Platforming is the perfect blend of tough but fair that makes you want to master the game's movement. And music is just as stunning as the visuals with a soundtrack that always adds to the atmosphere. All in all, a new great addition to the ever expanding metroidvania genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Afterimage for its exploration. The map is huge, in a way that I found enjoyable. The explorable levels are massive and beautifully made. The music is very solid. The story is also solid for a metroidvania. Combat is fun and reminds me a bit of Megaman Zero (not as hard tho). You have a lot of freedom with your character's build, too (different weapons and stats).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a solid A-tier metroidvania being held back by a few weaknesses.  Here is a general categorical breakdown and some thoughts after hitting 100%:The world of Engardin is absolutely massive and arguably has one of the biggest interconnected maps in the genre.  The exploration quickly becomes extremely non-linear after the first few hours of the game.  You’ll come across many moments where it is possible to wander into much more dangerous later game areas.  At the same time, you’ll run into many ability-gated paths that you’ll need to return to (there is a marker system for the map to make this easier).  There is also a town that serves as a main hub which is decent overall, but missing a bit of value in the late game.Each area strongly has its own unique vibe with distinct themes, different monsters, hazards, and bosses.  Within all of them there are countless secrets and treasures, some that are pretty well hidden. One major strength in the game is not just how much loot there is, but the variety of the loot itself.  You can find new weapons, armor, currency, upgrades, abilities, etc all just from exploring.  It helps keep things fresh overall.Pretty decent for the most part.  The XP-based leveling system serves as a core foundation and grants skillpoints for misc. upgrades.  There is a bit of depth in terms of buildcrafting, which incorporates multiple weapon equips (two melee and one spell) along with 3 armor & accessory slots which increase or decrease a variety of stats.  If you’re into min-maxing, there is plenty of opportunity.  This all combines with a skilltree which is.. not the best but could be worse.  You get a lot of freedom with what to use your skillpoints on, but it is mostly just passive stat bonus upgrades and a confusing format.  However, the fun weapon skills make up for this.  The combat itself became really enjoyable as the game progressed.  It doesn’t stray far from the familiar health & mana bar system along with an allotted number of heals that recharge at a checkpoint (some soulslike influence sprinkled into parts this game).  There are five different weapon types, two of which can be equipped at once.  Each weapon type has a variety of attacks that can be done with it, which allows for a ton of possibilities for creating combos.  In some moments it honestly felt like playing Smash Bros, in a good way.  The monsters and bosses all had a unique variety of movesets as well up until the endgame, and there were a ton of them overall.  If I had a main complaint with combat would be that some boss hitboxes and animations were a bit questionable/annoying. While the graphics themselves aren’t revolutionary, the art direction is what shined, especially within the presentation of each of the areas.  The sheer number of different themes is impressive, especially when most of them have beautiful vistas.  I felt the animations were hit or miss, but in most cases were pretty solid. One specific thing I personally felt was strong was the visual transition between some of the areas in the game.  In many cases there was a distinct “blending” effect as you go from one to the other (there are no loading screens except when fast traveling). The music was pleasant all throughout, with mostly orchestral vibes that appropriately matched the area or event.  There are plenty of catchy tracks, although the boss music could’ve been more hype.  The in-game sounds I felt were pretty average.Afterimage isn’t too difficult for a majority of the game as long as you’re killing enemies to level up as you progress.  Toward the end things ramp up a bit and there are definitely some challenging bosses.  But the flexibility with how to tackle them really comes in handy and changing my build is what got me through the tougher bosses.  Platforming was never really too difficult, and most of the slightly challenging platforming sections are optional side paths that lead to treasure.The story was a bit of a mess, to say the least.  Some elements were easy to understand while other parts didn’t make much sense at all.  The bulk of the story comes in lore fragments and toward the end where there are multiple endings and special chapter-based post story (which is improperly referred to as NG+).  Vague storytelling can be good in some cases, but I feel the execution here was not great.  Another recurring issue was the English localization, which contributed to making the story even harder to grasp.  However, the localization problems were most noticeable in quite a few instances where certain descriptions of items and skills were either misleading, or completely inaccurate.  By no means is this game breaking, but it was definitely an annoying hindrance from time to time.Branching off this, one thing Afterimage needs to improve on are the quests and giving the player some sense of goal or direction in general.  By no means do I think it should have hand-holding levels of guidance, but there should have at least been some type of vague hints or clues on the general objectives for quests.  While the non-linear exploration was still superb, everything felt disjointed in terms of figuring out the overall goals during quests.  It mostly comes down to hoping you are heading in the right direction. The remaining flaws in Afterimage mostly come in the form of minor quality of life issues and occasional lack of polish.  The main example of this I can give is the UI/UX which sometimes lacks sensible descriptions and layouts.  This is especially noticeable within the skilltree, which could use a major organizational overhaul.There is probably plenty more I could add, but this review is getting pretty lengthy now (if I think of anything significant I forgot to mention, I will add it in).  The pros outweigh the cons in this game by far.  If you’re seeking a longer, cozy metroidvania to escape into, Afterimage is a great option.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally getting all achievements and full map completion, I guess it's time to leave a review. It's a really nice and really huge Metroidvania, you can tell that the devs put a lot of effort into it. It reminds me a bit of Vigil: The Longest Night in a couple of ways, but that game is a Souls-like where as Afterimage is pure Metroidvania.It's difficult as well (at least on advanced difficulty, dunno about normal), don't be fooled by the easygoing earlygame, things will get a lot tougher as you progress. I think the game expects you to do some level grinding, which I didn't do at all, so at some point I was basically underleveled for every boss I encountered. It got better later in the game though, when you have so many areas to explore that you'll naturally level up a lot. While I kinda wish enemies simply scaled with your level, being underleveled is still better than being overleveled, which happens in some other games of the genre and makes things too boring. Anyway, the boss fights, and there are a lot of them, all felt unique and a good chunk of them very challenging too. Maybe 2-3 of them were cheap/unfair (which could simply be because I was underleveled, or because I didn't realize "subweapon damage" was for magic, not for melee, and my build was completely wrong lol), but the majority of them were cool. There's also a boss rush mode (except it's not a rush, you can select any boss you want to fight) and 3 playable characters which you can use in it.The overall combat and movement feels really tight and fast paced, which I like. You can choose between 6 main weapon types (sword, greatsword, dual swords, scythe, whip & katana) and various subweapons (magic). There's a skill tree that'll allow you to improve your stats or unlock new weapon skills as you progress. Each main weapon type has a unique moveset which will be expanded on with these skills. Some weapons even come with innate skills unique to them. There are a lot of weapons, with different elements, different special effects and sometimes bonus stats.Like I said, the game is very huge and there is a ton to explore. The level design (maybe aside from some very obnoxious parkour puzzles) is fantastic. So many secrets everywhere, tiny nooks and crannies you can fit and find items in. And gameplay aside, just atmospherically the game is amazing. Everything is very detailed and pretty, it's pleasant on the eyes. Only downside is that in order to fast travel to any location of your choice, you need a consumable, which will cost you money in the long run. I'll get to why that's a huge problem later.Something I often see people criticizing about the game is the story and lore, which is a bit confusing. I think it's alright personally, nothing amazing, but gets the job done. What I gathered is that  There are also some translation errors here and there, unfortunately, but it shouldn't get in the way of understanding what anyone is saying in-game. And even though I wouldn't say any of the main characters really grew on me, one of the bad endings was so heartbreaking that it actually made me sad. lolNow lastly, what I have to criticize about the game: the way money works. Farming money in this game is pretty much impossible, at least not efficiently. The most efficient way will still take you for ever, I think I spent 2-3 hours just farming money towards the end. The intended way of getting money is to break these containers that are spread out throughout the map. But once you have discovered all of them, that's it, they don't come back. The game has an achievement that requires you to buy every single shop item from every single vendor in the entire game. Because I obviously didn't know I'd need a crap ton of money at the end, I always spent the money I gathered throughout my playthrough by buying potions, the aforementioned fast travel consumables and upgrading various weapons I wanted to try out. Don't do this. The fast travel stuff is kinda unavoidable if you don't want to spend a lot of time running around, but you don't really need that many potions. I basically never used potions outside of boss fights and even then I tried my best to avoid using them because it felt a bit cheap (still did it a couple of times). Upgrading weapons should be fine if you don't overdo it like I probably did. God forbid I wanted to have multiple options for every weapon type... Just stick to 2-3 you like and ignore the others, I guess. Anyway, with all that being said, my conclusion is that it's a really solid game and I hope we get a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 7/10. The movement is crisp and responsive and the attacks feel good to use. The 6 weapon types and their skills provide a good variety of options, although I wasn't a fan of the inputs for some of the skills. Some of them require street fighter style inputs like quarter circle and double tab forward, which made them annoying to use in my opinion. I didn't use the spells much, so I can't say if they feel good to use. On their end, the platforming puzzles were very fun, they really felt like Hollow Knight platforming. Overall, while the gameplay is good, I'd say that it is missing a little something to elevate it to a really great level.Art and music: 9.5/10. I'm by no means knowledgeable in arts and music, but I think most will agree that this is the strongest point of this game. The world is absolutely gorgeous and the music is fantastic.The world: 7/10. Enemy variety is mostly good, the different zones feel distinct and the map is absolutely huge with over a dozen different zones. Although it is easy to both find high level areas early and to not know where you're supposed to go next, which mixed together caused me to spend too much time early trying to progress in zones I had no business being in. Fast travel depends on a currency that is somewhat rare early on but that you can buy for cheap later on, so it was never bothersome for me travelling across the map.Progression systems: 7/10. Finding and upgrading gear and getting new talent points felt good for most of the game, but it never felt terribly impactful. I wish that there was a way to quickly see what newly acquired items are, late game it was a bit annoying to scour my inventory to see the charm or weapon that I just got. Story: -/10. I didn't really care or pay attention to the story so I won' rate it. While the vibe of the story isn't really my cup of tea (cute magical girl and her funny sidekick go on an adventure), I gotta admit that the dialogue could be charming. Also, the amount of lore from item descriptions and memories (?) that you find all over the map is absolutely huge, so if you're into that you're gonna have a good time.Overall: 8/10. Afterimage is, in my opinion, a very good game definitely worth its 30$ price tag. A single somewhat completionist playthrough took me around 20 hours, which could easily climb to 30-35 hours if I wanted to get all of the achievements and even more if I wanted to complete the trial of souls (boss rush mode). It's not perfect, but it is a must play for any metroidvania enjoyer.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eyes on Afterimage for a while now.It is one of the best metroidvania experiences I found in a while.Positives:Negatives:The only thing I'm neutral on is the story.It is there, and is interesting at some points, but it did not get my full attention, and felt like an afterthought.To be honest, it might need some polish but it's a great game, up with the top metroidvanias.Also I'd recommend this earlier to your average gamer than something like Hollow Knight as it feels a lot more accessible, even with is faults.

_childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania game that seems made my people who never played metroidvanias. There are several things that this game just doesn't deliver that honestly makes the whole experience almost not worth. You can sequence skip and get soft locked in places, there's no minimap forcing you to keep opening map, there are several mechanics that are not explained, the skill tree is generic with some interesting points, and you can "rebuy" some skill points at different levels but to know that you need to keep moving by the skill tree node by node. Quests are poorly written as most text in the game, you have bad indicators on what to do overall. The map markers you can use are very limited, and having several map markers that are too similar serves no purpose. There are several metroidvanias that are far better, even more so considering the steep price of this one, mostly for the anime art and voice acting. Skip this one, even at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a nice metroidvania with some difficulty not being absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everywhere on any fights (there are still some fights which you won't clean on first try and may lose some part of sanity if you don't take a little bit of seriousness). As is it a metroivania exploration is important, with of course some areas or shortcuts to unlock as you play, the map is really big (you may find out after twenty of gameplay) there are loads of areas with various enemies more or less strong, explore as you wish and you may find some bosses that will wipe you out, but that's the key of exploration, try to beat it regardless of keep it for later (exception for some bosses or certain enemies that will absolutely destroy you no matter when you try them if you don't learn to dodge almost perfectly).Killed enemies respawn only if you either die or rests at TP points. While the map seems really large, I don't feel like some areas are designed for filling purposes only and to make the whole world bigger. The game possesses a fast travel system that'll let you teleport from one big TP to another (requiring the main TP of the zone is unlocked), and an instant teleportation to any TP you have unlocked for the cost of a returning potion (you can collect them by exploring for items in hidden places, or simply buy them later in the game).As for the mains abilities for progressing throughout the game, depending on how you explore areas, you may find yourself with only one ability unlocked after thirty hours of playtime without being able to progress, and mostly without knowing what you may have missed. You will be playing as Renee, a young girl who lost memories from her past and is willing to regain them as well as having the ability to return upon death, which is explained in game why she cans, you'll also be accompanied by Ifree, a little floating creature. There are a lot of weapons with some different stats from some to others, regrouped into six different groups, as well as some secondary weapons, accessory slots and armour of course, almost of all this will be upgradable. And there is a skill-tree that divides into different branches for weapons categories and explorations enhancements, as well as some stats buff, play enough to level-up and have the amount of essence crystals for maxing the whole skill-tree (no choice to make here except the order you want to go). Second to last there will be some NPCs offering side quests which can be either really simple, or long enough to hardly end it yourself if you don't do in one go, and some cooking that'll give you permanent boost upon first use plus regular boosts for consumption (some are really good for completing some boss fights !). And lastly the game contains some ten endings, some are considered as new game+, which is not exactly true as new game+ is an option unlocked by doing some precise endings that unlocks a second character for a separated gameplay where you play ten chapters apart from the main story (you can choose them on your save file after unlocking it in the menus). But the most important thing to me is that you can complete all ending in one save file without restarting your run from zero multiple times, with some prerequisites you can complete all ending in any order without preventing any from being doable. Overall, the game was really good and fun to play and had a much higher playtime that I expected (whether for the main story of for the 100% the playtime will differ naturally), the musics are pretty good for the different game zones and enhance the ambiance really nicely. The relation between Ifree and everyone, and mostly with food also is super amusing. The only downside could be the mains afterimages for progressing in the game that can be completely missed by accident if you didn't go one way or another or simply forgot a boss. It was still a good experience that I'd recommend to anyone willing to play a metroivania with some difficulty, especially for near endgame zones, where you really need to learn to dodge and be patient in boss fights (especially for ending 3 which is mandatory for unlocking newgame+). Side note, if you use the ability to parry hits with the swordfish, you will still take little damage, even if you perfectly parried.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a beautiful Metrodvania-style platformer that is too big for its own good. After, if you can overlook its flaws, it is still enjoyable. The game have some lovely art and character designs. They are consistent throughout and most importantly for me, easy to read. You can see clearly where threats are, and some tight controls help too. I was also quite fond of the music, though I have heard others describe it as bland, so YMMV. The main flaw is the game is so large; too large, I feel. While some maps are well designed, a lot of it is quite repetitive and simply a chore to traverse. I enjoyed the open nature of the exploration but feel if they just halved the scale and went for tighter design, it would have served the game better. Some of the secrets that require difficult jump/dash challenges were particularly frustrating, especially when you start running into multiple iterations of them. The combat balance is... okay. Most bosses hold up and do some interesting and different things, but towards the end there was a very sudden lurch in difficulty. Most of the time though you may find an area or a boss that is too high level but there are two other maps you can go visit instead. Regardless, it is fun because the different weapons essentially give you entirely different movesets. This would be the best part of the game if not for how weapons and spells are gear that gets outlevelled, forcing to you swap. It would be better if they are fixed and you upgrade the character only.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't finish the game because it's way too large - unironcally.Way too much bloat, minor upgrades like 2% move speed, which is worthless to put into your game in my opinion and then lore as well as the world doesn't feel properly connected.Also, why are there so many materials and cooking related drops that are not only difficult to pick up due to small hitbox, but also feel like even more bloat? Compress it down, focus on a few ingridients.  On top of that, an awful map and quest system. You can not mark things on the map manually, which I don't prefer anyhow, but it also doesn't mark important spots for you when you visited it. Nor are for the most part, any major quests that drive the plot forward mentioned on the map. 11.7 hours in, level 70+ bunch of hecking items and I'm truly lost.That just shows a lack of a proper quest system. Best example is Hollow Knight and how it had symbols of the 3 dreamers you have to kill. Anything along those lines to pull the player along through this insanely large interconnected world would be very helpful!Also, movement boils down to dashing a million times in quick succession to move through the massive world, which I think is just large to show how cool stuff can look.I see the large amount of work that artists put into everything, but, gameplay is key and that is missing here.I can not recommend this for this price tag and the lack of features explained above.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, solid metroidvania. Not without minor flaws, but I enjoyed my initial playthrough (I still have NG+ to go through) a lot and I think the game is worth its price and player's time. Starting from the positives. You get access to map immediately with 500(!) marks with many different kinds to your disposal. It's amazing. You can regularly put it on your map whenever you find sth of interest. It helps with backtracking A LOT. Combat is fun. There are 6 weapons + magic weapon of choice. Every weapon has a few combos that are unlocked through exploration and executing them during combat is extremely satisfying. I played mostly with katana and whip myself. Those gave me the most fun out of all. Locations are beautiful and are quite distinctive from one another. Also this game runs so SMOOTHLY. I have quite an old laptop which I wish I would replace in the near future. Most of my games have issues with lags and loss of FPS. I believe I have never had any that kind of issues when playing this game. Music is very good and complementary to the whole game. Side quests were quite good and got me interested in finding and talking to NPCs.This game achieved sth that i longed for for a long time. I got lost in this world for a few hours (in a good way). There's one boss in overleveled area that I thought I am supposed to fight it later. It turned out that I was on the right track. Nevertheless I liked the way devs constructed levels and paths of exploration.The last thing. Nearly right from the start i got so engrossed in the game that I lost track of time for the most part of my playthrough. I had sessions lasting 4-5 hours when I felt like max 2 had passed. It's surprising for me because after playing Aeterna Noctis I was so exhausted and lost my passion for this genre of games. Afterimage ignited my love for metroidvania action platformers again, for which I'm extremely thankful to the creators of Afterimage.Cons/minor problems/feedback for devs for potenial DLC or their next game: Main story is a bit wonky and I'm not sure if I understood it all. It's not bad, but a bit complicated and there happened many absurd things along the way. Hope NG+ will let me understand it more. So many marks/pins available to a player is an awesome choice from devs, but why is there a requirement to have specific potion to teleport between safe spots? Also there aren't many given through exploration. It's okay at the first half but during second one it becomes inconvenient. When pins and accessible map that are given to player from the start (without need to buy it from some vendor) gives player extreme feeling of freedom, those potions make one feel caged and stopped from exploring points of interest previously marked on the map. Also the fact that they are sold from cooking merchant and not from one selling general stuff. It's a bit weird choice, but ok.Locations of NPCs during side quests sometimes are completely random without a single hint. I wish they were visible on map or there was a hint about their location in quest log. After spending 30+ hours exploring it's a bit too much to expect player to go through the world again to find NPC on some random platform.Aerial combos would be a great add to the game. There are a few bosses that fly so high that it's nearly impossible to hit them with other combos than attack in the air and you can't use magic (your only ranged option) in the air. It's just a suggestion to better the experience.I had a bug that a bit disappointed me. In game you obtain glyphs that during exploration and fights you use to heal yourself. After one fight and the last boss after another boss player is supposed to get one of them. Game freezes instead. It pissed me a bit, especially in the latter case (which made it impossible to achieve the last ending of normal game). With the help of one of the devs on their discord I manged to complete it. I believe it will be patched sooner than later.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VERY mild yes, almost borderline.This game has the many-endings and secret-ish items and routes and such, plus a pseudo NG+ that is really an alt-character path to the "true" ending.All that can be great but, unfortunately, the writing/translation in this game is fairly bad. There's typos and lost of awkward phrasing and jilted sentences, combined with a general sense of what I assume was a desire to be pretty secretive and subtle. Unfortunately that doesn't combine well with a lackluster translation/writing.Gameplay wise it's a decent metroidvania anyhow - though my biggest complaint is touching an enemy damages you with quite a knockback and even a screen freeze, which interrupts a lot of platforming/attacks/etc., and your dash doesn't go through enemies, meaning that bosses are pretty jump over/dive under and not much else.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Very snappy controls and movement, pretty art, decent music and voice acting, lots of weapons and traversal powers that feel rewarding, a lot of content and a good map.-Cons:On the other hand, even after what looks like significant updates from reading older reviews, this is plagued with a lot of basic quality of life failings that could have easily been remedied.I said the map was decent, and it is, but there is very limited automatic marking of points of interest/quests/obstacles (There's no indication that something is a body of water you need the swimming power to access, for example, meaning you need to manually mark every single pool you find or it looks like an unexplored hallway you missed). You can place map markers (Good!), but there are no icons for basic things and several similar redundant ones. Continuing the example there's no good icon for 'water here, come back with swimming later', so you end up reusing else like the cooking pot... and then the UX for selecting the icons that do exist is terrible, making you scroll through the entire list in one direction by mashing the right trigger a dozen times every time you want to select a given icon.Why is there no option for a minimap?Area level ranges are completely hidden from you for no discernible reason (seems like this was an intentional change made in an update?), the only hint you get is a marker over enemies that they are far above your level.So this creates the awful situation where you end up backtracking multiple times to areas every few levelups to see if you are now the correct level to explore them. Even then this seems inconsistent, as multiple times I pushed past a few high level enemies at a border only to encounter a boss that wasn't above my level in the same area and was able to clear it out.Fast Travel is a mess. Why does this use a consumable, with how much the game wants you to backtrack across large maps? Even with the update that adds it to an early vendor, it's too expensive early game to buy. Why can you only fast travel to one point in each area that's often out of the way or not near where you'd want to reach when backtracking, instead of all of the available save points? Why is the free fast travel so limited in where you can do it from and to? Why does the menu for it not include the location on the map, and only an unhelpful screenshot of the save point? Why are major area names obscured until you find a random lore pickup? This creates a lot of frustration and wasted time when backtracking where you spend half your time traveling to travel points and going back and forth to the map rather than actually exploring the new areas.The separate water/boat map is a neat idea, but it is completely disconnected from the main map and some of the areas there don't seem to appear on the main map... so it just ends up being needlessly confusing to navigate.Every time you pick up a new weapon, armor, accessory, costume, item, etc. you receive no information on it or what type of item it is. You have to open the menu, scroll to find the proper section, scroll to the proper slot, and scroll through your whole inventory until you find it to figure out what you just picked up. Even then descriptions can be unhelpful, giving you flavor text while not actually telling you what a spell does for example.The majority of the talent points are extremely underwhelming, things like multiple ranks of '+0.5% spell damage on a specific element' are a waste of space on the menu and really should be removed or condensed. The fact that you have to go back through most of the tree again at higher levels without a good indication of what nodes have multiple points or unlocks also feels annoying rather than rewarding. Things that should probably be talents or a permanent unlock are instead given as afterimages that you have limited slots to equip and can only be changed at a save point. It feels terrible to reach a new area, realize you needed to have the 'fog reveal' afterimage equipped to progress, and then have to backtrack across the entire zone to equip it and then back before continuing just because you wanted a basic convenience power like money pickup range equipped while you were exploring.Enemy balance and positioning can seem all over the place at times. Some normal enemies are completely helpless even at higher levels, while others will have fast homing attacks that instantly 180 in midair to follow you multiple times, will instantly flip to face you mid attack, have badly telegraphed AOEs that spam out in front of them or in multiple directions at a large distance without a good indication of where will be safe, or they will instantly charge at you on sight extremely quickly.Enemies will occasionally spot you and shoot at you from offscreen, or be positioned directly inside a hidden area you can't see into until you've run into them, or are right next to the edge of a ledge mid-jumping puzzle or crawlspace and feel like taking damage from them was unavoidable. It's not a big deal, but it can make exploration more annoying than it should be and makes items like the early health regen amulet feel essential to wear all the time.Several bosses were completely trivial while others took forever to kill as they had patterns or positions that prevented attacks for long periods of time or had what felt like several times the health of others (I'm sure this isn't helped by the hidden level ranges). Many bosses have multiple attacks that you need to see (and usually get hit by) before you understand what they were trying to telegraph, leading to a lot of facetanking instead of interacting with them properly. Decorative foreground objects can completely hide enemy attacks or entire enemies from you, even during some boss fights.Some of the core systems are badly explained to the player. For example, I was completely unaware of the death penalty for the majority of the playthrough. I had only died in overleved boss rooms which I had no reason to return to immediately and assumed the vague map icon was just the one for an unkilled 'boss' and not to recover the XP the game hadn't told me I'd lost.Some of the final 100% achievements could use rework (Ex: The 666 damage one)-In addition, maybe it is a translation issue, but the story has been incomprehensible. I really tried to pay attention but quickly lost track of what was going on. There is a lot of vague mysterious talk about proper noun individuals/groups/entities/areas to keep track of, often while the main character is being kept intentionally in the dark on half the details by the speaker. Events that you don't know about but characters do are constantly referred to without being explained, important item descriptions are often completely meaningless, quests are difficult to follow and usually have nothing in game to remind you to follow up on them unless you go through and read the menu regularly. The main character seems to have no idea what or who her partner and best friend, who is there for the whole game and in every conversation, actually is most of the time.-Conclusion:Overall, I definitely had fun but the quick gameplay and nice aesthetics really carried the overall experience. I liked it enough to fully 100% it, and I would recommend it to any metroidvania genre fan and think it is worth buying for sure... I just hope the developer can clean up all of the rough edges a bit more (they do seem to be making positive post-launch changes, which is good) to bring it from a solid game to a really excellent one.I'd also say don't be intimidated by all the 'biggest metroidvania ever' comments... I'm not sure where HTLB is getting 50% more playtime than I had for a normal completion and 100% completion. Maybe the balance changes and system updates cut down on a lot of padding/deaths for me, but outside of the final running around to 100% everything the length felt totally normal to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I actually worried about background and environment that it would be too flat and lack of details based on what I saw on trailer. But when it got on handed, I founded out that it's pretty neat and gorgeous. I've played a couple of Chinese games before (ANNO: Mutationem, Eastern Exorcist) and those games really have a problems with details and animation. Not like Afterimage, I can feel that developers really put an afford to this point. You can see waving clothes, fancy wings affect, various weapons animation, etc.Controls is very responsive. I'm not a fan with collision damage, it can be annoying some times but it still fun to play and I having no problems with it. I really like how each weapons feel in this game, board sword is heavy but also feeling a hard hit, blade with unique timing and style, sickle that feels very badass in every swing. Boss fights are amazing and very intense, except most of mini bosses are quite boring.....I kinda impressed that they put voice over in every dialogue. But NPC dialogues have a length between 1 sentence to 1 paragraph so it's just very boring and with bad pacing, it makes things even worse. The last time I got something actually useful from bosses and exploration are about 4-5 hours ago, which is a really long time and can be grounds to frustrated feeling, lost motivation, etc. Finally, it came to this state, "I can't go to this area because I don't have wall jump.", "I can't go to that area because I can't swim.",  "I can't go to those areas because my level is too low." It's like they have some restrictions every where I go. Maybe they're trying to keep their game balanced and having back track like other metriod vania games? But why would they make fast travel a rare thing to do because you need an item in order to use it and it also very finite and hard to find. It's like developers can't find the middle ground between "freedom" and "restriction". So, the result is you may feel overwhelm by the enormous map at first, but when the time goes on you will feel stuck like you can't go anywhere else. Then you find the way and got overwhelmed again by even larger area. This may seems like a good thing but in fact it doesn't, at least for me.It's basically very confusing especially in Talent Tree and Inventory. You can barely distinguish between non and upgrade able because the restrictions they have, when you spent your skill point, you will found out that it requires level 45-60 to upgrade to next level.Menu itself is just too much things going on. You have to watch some sort of transition between one and another menu like if I want to open my Talent Tree, I have to press options menu on my controller then R1 a couple times and in the meantime I have to watch a fancy animation of every page I pass on the way to my Skill Tree. So my opinions is just makes it a wheel menu like Genshin or weapons wheel in Farcry but if you ran out of buttons in the controller just make it simple and go back to the regular form just wiped or faded transition, that's pretty enough.I'm not finished yet, the next thing is Inventory. Why in the world would you put non consumable items appear in the inventory with use button?? Not just that but you also wrote the description like it's usable. For example, Secret Art an item that you will get after defeated the first boss. Just picked it up and you will automatically be able to learn that skill in Skill Tree. But it's also appear in your inventory with the description and use button like you can press and learned that skill, but you can't because you've already learned that before you even know. The problems is it requires level 40 50 or 60 I forgot but it's a really high. In the conclusion, you just defeated a boss and also got a useless thing that will be useful in the next 15 hours.Achievement Progression is also not working properly. I defeated Loss, the Broken Wings but still haven't got any achievement. I saw someone that got like 15 hours in game but still have only 4 out of 46 achievements.Obviously not a big deal but it make me feels like I haven't accomplished any goals in game.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels all over the place, no clear direction as to what you have to do, some bosses have undodgable attacks and a lot of places are accessible right from the start unlike other metroidvania games. So its hard to recommend it.They could also make an improvement in how we meet the bosses. Sometimes you end up being underlevelled for them and sometimes the opposite if you meet them too late.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, if somewhat difficult to follow, MV game.  Art, sound, and gameplay are excellent.Fully voiced which is uncommon for the genre.I advise looking up a map of what to do but otherwise no caveats to recommending this game. Biggest downside is really the fast travel system being item based without clear "go here" quest objectives, for the most part, but like I said, if you look up a map of where to go it's a non issue but the map is BIG and without a guide you'll likely miss a lot.  A lot of complaints are about lack of i-frames in dash/collision damage, that's one of the games mechanics and you do get i-frame dash later, you adapt to the combat style and it works really well. 8/10, with better quest direction and an at-will fast travel system would be an easy 10/10 recommendation.
