_childDocuments_.review: If you are a metroidvania fan, then you will find Afterimage to be a solid installment. Its not the strongest, but it is a solid game. Its graphics are beautiful, absolutely gorgeous, but they are marred by somewhat clunky animations. This is especially felt with the main character.The music is simply good. There's some tropes with it like a middle eastern themes song for the desert, but that seems par for course. Like most metroidvania games, you will spend a lot of time running about exploring, even backtracking over previous levels to visit previously inaccessible areas. However, where most metroidvanias are tight enough that you can look at your map and discern where to go next, Afterimage is sprawling with little to no direction. That is not hyperbole; the map is crazy big. Originally the zones had suggested levels to help give some guidance, but even that disappeared in the first patch. Where you might think that the addition of quests would give you some direction, it does not. Just keep running around and, if you can't figure out where to use that whistle, just keep going east over the very large bridge. You don't normally play metroidvanias for their writing. You only need enough to give basic motivation and context before you charge on in. Still, Afterimage tries to pack in a story, which I deeply appreciate. The writing starts out as dazed and confused as your character, but by the midgame it has developed solidly. The voice acting vacillates between wonderful and stilted, the latter of which can be jarring when it happens given the juxtaposition. Overall, the voice is pretty on par with JRPGs.If there was one truly annoying thing in this game, it is that it is still working out the bugs. For instance, as of the time of this writing, the jump button will occasionally just stop working, affecting both keyboard and controller, and the whip's jump attack sometimes simply passes through enemies without dealing damage.Despite its few flaws, Afterimage is a good deal of fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful 40 hour magical girl adventure with a vast world, plenty of treasure, challenging platforming and bosses, and multiple endings which make the good ones feel satisfying to reach. Probably too long and bloated for a Metroidvania at times, and so many things are hard to figure out without a guide, but for a mere $30 CDN it's fantastic value especially if you plan on committing to a single game for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Highly rated metroidvania in my book......I like a lot of them but I'd put it up there with GRIME, ORI, Aeterna Noctis, Hollow Knight, Phoenotopia Awakening. If you are a fan of metroidvanias, this is a MUST play. If you are new to the genre, give it a go to get a sense of what "getting lost in a massive map" feels like. You may like it, you may not. The platforming of this game is accessible so it makes for a great testing grounds to see if you want to play some of the bigger map MVs.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very beautiful, and very fun. I don't play a lot of Metroidvania style games, but I ended up getting hooked on this. It's very satisfying to unlock a new ability, and to go back and collect things or explore areas you couldn't access before.The translation is a bit wonky at times, which leads to some of the voice acting to be a bit off and the story itself can be a bit hard to follow as a result, but if you're just looking for an action platformer, it was a lot of fun. The game encourages you to try different weapon types, as you generally will find better weapons than what you currently have before upgrading them feels worth it. There's a LOT of secret collectibles and whatnot, so you'll change loadouts frequently, and the skill tree is set up to encourage you to diversify what you put your talent points into, as you'll probably reach level gates with extra TP to spare.The art is beautiful, and the soundtrack is nice, though not particularly amazing (it's hard to stand out these days, as many games tend to have great soundtracks). The map is MASSIVE and you will need to backtrack to get things. If you like to just explore, you're generally rewarded with weapons and abilities. It can be hard to find everything without a guide, but I didn't need a guide to complete the main story, and the side-stories you can usually find by wandering around and checking out the map to look for NPC markers.In all, it was worth the time spent on it, I got the game on sale, but I'd say it's worth the base price if you enjoy this type of game. I've 100%'d the main game and "new game +" in about 36 hours, and there's still the boss-fight Trial of Soul if I want to revisit the game some more, but that's a bit excessive for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: One of the longer Metroidvanias that I've played. Lots of endings too. And they're at different points, needing different things so you can't just sit in one spot and go through all of them.Artwork is really good.Combat is... alright. The fact the dash through enemies was held for an ability later on was annoying.Once you get around level 80 pretty much everything is a cakewalk.I dunno how to really say it. But this was good.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I waited until I finished the game to write a review on it. This game is not perfect, but it is a wonderful game. It takes a little bit to get going with your mobility and such, but once you get rolling, it's addicting. The combat is fantastic. There is an unbelievable amount of content in this game if you want to 100% it, and it has a story that is not bad at all. Yes, it might be a little generic with the whole super-powered girl with amnesia bit, but it's done well, and the game itself is gorgeous. There are a lot of different zones that are all memorable and very fun boss fights. I feel it's a very good balance of not sadistic hard but not easy for the average player to make it through with some effort. All in all, this game made me feel things I have not felt since I played Hollow Knight, and that is always a feeling that I strive to find again in games. If you are on the fence and you like Metroidvania games at all, I strongly recommend giving it a shot. It's very worth the time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely scratched that itch I've been having since I completed Bloodstained Ritual of the Night. I haven't completed the game, I'd say I'm about a third, or maybe even close to half way done with the game and so far it's an APRG Metroidvania in the spirit of Symphony of the Night/RotN, you get gear, you have a talent tree, you gain levels, etc. There's plenty of side quests to do, and there's a multitude of endings to obtain. The platforming isn't challenging, you don't get hurt if you land on spikes or jump into water (before you get the ability to swim), and death isn't as "scary" as in Hollow Knight since you get a fairly big health pool, and a multitude of ways to heal yourself--so if anyone is worried that this game might be "souls-like," it's really not, when you die, you lose the experience you accumulated since your last level up, but once you retrieve your spirit or whatever you get it all back. The bosses are fairly simple once you figure out their shtick, the only thing that would make the bosses challenging is being under leveled, but if you follow a map like the one I'm using that gives you a list of all the areas and what levels you should be in that area, those instances of finding bosses that woefully out level you are few and far between. Now, I won't say the game is perfect; it's not. The biggest gripe I have is how vague this game is when it comes to figuring out where to go next. Now I don't mind exploring, finding stuff, killing stuff, etc. but I'd like to know where I'm at, or what direction I should be heading in. I downloaded a map of the game to get a good idea of what level each area is to kind of gauge where I should be going, but I shouldn't have to do that--the game should at least give some direction that I should be going in, not just give me some story bits with vague wording and setting me loose to go and figure it out. All in all this is a game in the truest sense--what I mean by that is there aren't any real cut scenes (at least I haven't run across any yet), the graphics are hand drawn and animated, the story is fairly vague requiring you to piece things together, and the overall feel of the game is it's just simple and fun, like a game is supposed to be. All in all, despite by gripe, I think this game is easily worth the price of entry--you'll get a good 40-50 hours of solid game play from the game, and with a NG+ and finding all the endings, collectables, etc. you get a very meaty game for $25.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a decent little game, the price is fine for 20+ hours of content.It's your typical Metroidvania, it doesn't really take any risks, the story is "so-so", you either like it or you just skip it. It did lose me a bit towards the end. Just like the entire game did. The "last" 2 zones in particular just stretch the game out. And the story kinda falls a bit flat there. Up until that point the game wasn't really super linear, but you had more or less a clear sense of where you were going ... then suddenly I felt a bit "lost". Not like "where should I go?", but more "why should I go?". The game didn't seem to want to tell me that in relatively clear terms, so I just went from zone to zone, defeated boss after boss, watched some cutscenes, but never had a clear goal in mind. It could do a bit better with guiding the player in that regard.The zones themselves are all pretty much great, each and every one has a different vibe to it and unique enemies and music as well. Traversal is slow-ish at first, but at the end you barely need to touch ground anymore, which is good, because there is a moderate amount of backtracking involved, especially if you really want to get the endings, yes, plural. These are another point of contention for me, because they just feel a bit shallow and without finality. After an ending the game just quits to the title screen and you can load back in as if nothing happened. Which ending you've chosen basically doesn't matter, you can unlock them all in 1 playthrough anyway. Finding them all is, I suppose, the big deal. More on that later.Like I mentioned earlier, the game overall is relatively "basic". There's nothing "wild" here, nothing that would really set it apart from other, more accomplished Metroidvanias... BUT what it does it does competently. The map is useful for once, you can set your own markers (and you should), fast travel isn't too problematic, unless you've spent all your money on crap. Combat consists of using 6 different weapon classes, each with their own unique move sets and findable weapons, you can have 2 equipped at any time, as well as a support item which let's you cast a variety of spells.There's 3 armor lots, as well as 3 ring slots as well.My biggest complaint here is that these mostly felt like an afterthought. Early game weapons and armor are useless later on and can't be upgraded to be on par or at least close to late game weapons. They simply lack damage. Some weapons have unique skills or talents as well, and it would have been nice to keep a favorite and just upgrade it or switch it out vs. different enemies.The way stats are handled, is rather poor, because I never found an actual overview of how much "pyro resistance" for example I got (maybe I didn't find it) ... or whether it even mattered? It's not super clear what the different damage types do, and some weapons are just superior to others (like the whip being able to attack multiple times in mid-air, while not falling is almost a requirement I feel like). Dodging, unfortunately, doesn't exist, until the very end of the game, so the only way to avoid damage for 15+ hours is to jump over or duck under it, or back off, basically. Enemy patterns on the other hand become rather elaborate later on, and boss patterns as well, giving you a sense of basically "having to take" some punishment. You can heal and you do have health potions on top of that as well, so for me, personally, I didn't really have much of an issue on the regular difficulty. Even beat some bosses I sure as hell shouldn't have at that point. But I'd say the boss fights are actually quite good here.After you've beaten the game, you unlock a "NG+" mode, which is a bit of a misnomer. It's basically 10 short chapters with a different character before you can return to the main game, and do some more boss fights and quests to get the true ending. I'm currently on chapter 3, and I don't know whether I'll be able to beat those bosses, but for 25 bucks Afterimage actually provides more than enough if you just want to scratch that Metroidvania itch and don't want to feel frustrated with some of the less stellar examples in this genre.Solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game, I feel like it's a weak metroidvania, weak on the metroid part, leans more castlevania but is also sort of weak there, but it also feels good to play... so I recommend itThe weapon damage system and stats, the talent system, it's all confusing and seems more complicated than it offers anything to the game, weapon damage and skill damage don't make sense and seem to be primarily useful for cheesing, but there's till some fun attacks that existFast travel are very spread out but you get a limited consumable to teleport to any shrine, so it feels more like a tool for speedrun routing rather than QOL for normal playInventory is unclear, things exist in various places but when you loot something, no clarity as what kind of item it is and finding it can be difficult, it's unclear if items should be sold or serve a purpose so you're likely to hoard them until you get some kind of proof or really need moneyBut it's still fun?  I'm just perpetually confused by various aspects of the design while having fun.The only best clearly good one is that while it uses a Dark Soulsian system of Estus and Souls.... "Souls" are EXP only, and you just level up automatically and get a point to spend.  Money is not tied to souls, so while it rides the bandwagon of that system it is smart enough not to marry itself to the idea over smooth gameplayThat said, if you die on a boss, exp sits in the boss room.... but also that said, since you level up instead of having to find a bonfire/NPC, you aren't punished for over extending

_childDocuments_.review: Unclear of where to go with both sidequests and mainline. The map is huge and it's easy to miss a lot of secrets, passages and power-ups. The hitboxes can be janky at times and IMO the voiceacting isn't to my liking. However with that said, there's a lot of content, challenging platforming bosses and it isn't too punishing for dying. The flow of combat could do with some changes since a lot of times it can just turn into a slugfest. But the soundtrack is nice, the design is beautiful, power-ups are fun (albeit sometimes a bit lackluster/OP), there's a lot of backtracking as well. But for the amount of time that I've put it in comparison to what I paid for this game, I'd say it's worth it if you're looking for a challenging platformer. Not as brutal as Hollow Knight, but close to it, and not as casual as certain others. Not bad, not bad at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: A hard no, the game is big and the static images and backgrounds look nice but that's about it.The animations are stiff, the story is complete nonsense, enemies are braindead and a lot of the world feels slapped together more than actually designed. It's an absolute pain to get from point A to point B even once you have all the traversal upgrades. Not that you'd really want to, this has been by far the least rewarding Metroidvania I've played my entire life. Most chests have absolutely nothing of value or gear that can randomly drop from enemies but they still require skills from 2/3+ zones further ahead by which point you've already gotten a better weapon. Backtracking is just not rewarding.Enemies as mentioned above are completely braindead and that works in their favor as this game has both contact damage and ridiculous damage buffs to enemies who are higher level than you which you have no way of knowing without getting hit and watching your healthbar disappear. There's something fundamentally wrong when I'd rather take a boss' death laser than touch his pinky.The skill tree is mostly static buffs like the .5 and 1.5% damage or defense you'd see in a Ubisoft game. There are 2 skills for each weapon but some of them are so useless they're downright a debuff. They usually lock you in an animation you can't get out of for a good second or two after the skill stops dealing damage but some of them such as the parry/perfect parry on the greatsword actually still make you take damage even if used correctly. And then there's the daggers which just melt entire bosses in 5 seconds.....Overall I'd recommend avoiding even on sale, the devs need to hire a designer who's actually played a decent metroidvania and reword most of their systems before this game should be considered.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so, this is a sidescrolling Metroidvania with some notable Hollow Knight and Souls influences.In the gameplay department, yeah, this is pretty OK. There's some neat custom attacks, and a pretty broad range of weapon types to choose from, some which have their own unique attacks.It's a huge world to explore, bigger than it initially appears.In terms of storytelling ... oof. The English writing is terrible, the English voice acting is terrible, the story is at best incoherent. It tries to do the Souls thing of explaining very little and putting lots of item descriptions around for Lore, andI think it probably worked better in the native language? But it very much did not translate well.Overall, thumbs up because it's a fun Metroidvania. Just not for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: A clean and beautifully animated metroid-vania  side-scroller.  It doesn't break any new ground, but don't let that take away from the experience.  If you like the style of game, you will love the classic game pay and rich visuals this game has to offer.  So far I have really enjoyed it and seems to have a really decent size and scope with a lot of content; especially if you aren't cheating and using guides.  Lots of variety in skills, weapons, and items keep things interesting and a moderately well written story.  Definitely pick this one up, and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: The world is pretty, the characters are very anime like in terms of their voice acting. I can't say too much yet since it's the beginning, but it has a pretty slowish start.The gameplay is a bit slow and the movement runs into the issue of pausing when doing different attack animations, making the gameplay less fluid.The enemies at least in the beginning are quite boring to fight, they have cute designs and some gimmicks, but the actual combat is pretty limited, despite having an arsenal of different weapons, could just be an early game issue, but the gameplay is a bit dull.There is a ton of segments when you're exploring where you see something on the other side of a wall and have to make your way around to get there and break it, or get the loot.I'd say get the game if you enjoy the discovery aspect of these platformers, because there will be a bit of back and forth.the boss fights in the trailers do seem promising, so I will look forward to continuing sometime.I'll recommend this game with a caution, I'd compare it to Ori but with less movement options. There is a fast travel mechanic that does get introduced, but I've yet to use it, because the backtracking/finding another way around is contained to the area itself.At the very least, I'll continue to see where the story leads.5/10 for now.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best and largest metrovanias I've ever played. As a huge castlevania and ori fan I would say this is up there in quality and "just another 10 mins (which turns into 2 hrs btw) gameplay.Amazing flow, combat, choices and exploration.The map just keeps going, seemingly never ending of nature, but each zone is interesting, full of secrets, back track unlockables and fun.Quests are vast and span multiple locations.   My only gripe is that sole of these are very obscure, so requires a good or two.Multiple endings which don't require and game restart.And did I mention new game plus which is a game in itself. Plugging the gaps in the main story and unlocking further content in the main save... 10 times triple AAA content for half the price.Plays like a dream on the steam deck too...

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I would love to give this a positive review, I can't. The game's artwork is absolutely fantastic and many of the enemies are well detailed, fluid, and interesting... initially... However, this game serves as a reminder of many of the things NOT to do when designing a Metroidvania game world.The biggest fundamental issue with this game is the game world. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ criminy. The game world feels artificial... constructed... It's really hard to explain it in words, but each section in a "room" in an area feels like the world designers wanted to maintain their ability to be random so as to try to be interesting and just came up with all different sorts of navigation paths and used them almost as brushes and painted them into the maps. There's so many different types, of those patterns, that it doesn't feel like they templatized them (fortunately!). However, the game world still feels constructed and inorganic. An organic feel can be hard, I get it -- I'm making my own Metroidvania and have been working on it for years, and making a game world organic AND interesting can be one of the most difficult challenges, especially in a Metroidvania where the game world is so integrated into what makes an MV an MV. But the answer isn't to methodically and functionally develop your game world. The reason it's taking me so long to make my game is because the standards Iv'e set for myself is to ensure that the game world is enjoyable to navigate through. That means enemy placement must make sense. The terrain and everything about it must feel organic. Elements that provide challenges to navigate through or past must make sense as to why they would be there (if the world were actually real) and not feel like they were put there just to provide a challenge. In Afterimage, the game world seems designed to be as large as it is just for the sake of having a large world, almost as if the developers thought that giving the players a large world is all of, or the most important aspect, to what would make players like the game.  A large game world is  of other factors,  the motivating design factor itself! There's no concept of rooms since it's all one room in a way (there's no loading unless you're fast-traveling somewhere). There are areas (I guess you could call them biomes, but there's so many areas, that the color palettes feel like other areas, and thus not actually distinct biomes). However, there are way way way too many of them given how large and pointless each one actually is. If you take these areas and break them down, just visually looking at the map, into reasonable chunks, the rooms are MASSIVE and most of the rooms just feel like they're there for the sake of just being there. to pad the game world size because of the belief that the bigger the game world the more the player will like the game.Compounding the problems, mentioned in the previous paragraphs, are the fact that there are, I dunno... 14? 18? however many areas (I haven't counted but it's a metric ♥♥♥♥ ton and these areas are MASSIVE. This means that most of the rooms (filled with these "constructed"-feeling sections) in these areas feel this way and if that is the case for most of the rooms in the areas individually, and most of the areas feel that way, then most of the game world feels that way. There's an inkling of confirmation on my thoughts on this that I've picked up while playing the game. Through these areas a a crazy amount of little secret areas where you can slide under some wall, or jump through some wall, or destroy some block and these secrets lead to some sort of reward. I personally believe they did this because they looked back at their game world and realized just how empty the game felt due to the size and the rooms don't really serve much purpose and so they may have felt that by adding in hidden chests it would help soften the feeling of boredom. However, many of these rooms are guarded by some absolutely insane jump, dash, bounce, dash, thread the needle, bounce, double-jump, dash kind of traversal path where you are constantly threading the needle the entire time because the walls, ceiling, and floor are covered in spikes that if you touch them, warp you back to the beginning of that section to try again. (The only saving grace here is that it doesn't damage you). This would be understandable if the reward was worth the effort. Most times it's some potion that you use as currency (a consumable item) when fast-traveling (yep, no free fast-traveling here in this game lol), or a single item of a set of three that'll increase your hp or mana... Seriously? You need 3 divine leaves or 3 divine petals (or whatever they're both called) to increase your hp or mana just a tiny little bit and you hide them behind those kinds of sections? Outrageous. Just reward the player for checking every nook and cranny for hidden pathways, no need to make them work as hard as they are for it after they already discovered a hidden location. FFS. It's like diminutizing their endorphine of reward for finding the secret because that wasn't enough, now they have to navigate the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and that's only for a single leaf or petal, you only get a benefit after getting 3 of that kind!The rooms themselves have multiple branching intricate pathways to navigate but only serve to get to the next room that feels the exact same way as described in previous paragraphs. And that's a big problem because it feels tedious to navigate each of these sections when the rooms feel as though they serve no purpose. Let me elaborate on that a bit with a more concrete example. In Symphony of the Night, for example, on the two ends of the castle are giant elevator shafts. Those sections are incredibly tall because they HAVE to be. The elevator serves to connect to different floors that are laid out, in general, horizontally. Those elevator shaft areas not there simply just to make tall rooms. There's a functional purpose and reason for their presence. It's even grounded in reality where you have skyscrapers and an elevator provides access to horizontally laid out floors. Additionally, much of the content (platforms, landings, walls, enemy layout, etc.) inside of the sections of SotN are where they are because, again, purpose and function. It just happens to be that the purpose and function throughout that game make the game feel really nice to navigate through. Navigating through Afterimage just constantly feels like an immense slog (to be fair, calling it an immense slog, I feel would be being generous).There are a CRAZY number of "boss" fights. Many of these boss fights aren't even true boss fights, they're just a wave of all of the enemy types in that area that spawn in that you defeat. In any case, whether it's an actual boss, or a wave of the area's enemy types, the rewards are often a kick in the nuts. Some weapon that you're probably not going to use, or 1 or two talent points that'll barely make a difference, or some other trash pulled out from the garbage can. You'll constantly be asking yourself, when the ♥♥♥♥ do I get the ability to do X when there are so many damn places requiring that?! And each time you come across a "boss" fight, you won't be able to help yourself thinking, "great, another ♥♥♥♥♥♥ item. A wasted opportunity for them to give me something I actually NEED."The game wears out its welcome after a few hours of playing and as a result, it's only good to keep play-sessions fairly short.

The gameplay is pretty linear and customization is a joke because "new is better" all the time. _childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is a hearty meal of a Metroidvania, offering hours upon hours of enjoyable gameplay. The controls and combat are tight, with later enemies and bosses presenting a fair challenge to experienced gamers. The bright colour pallet and varied environments provides a welcome change from the muted tones that are often used in this genre. I had a lot of fun exploring the incredibly vast 2D world.The narrative and character dialogue would benefit from a revised English translation, by a native English speaker. I recall that all of the characters were fond of using the word "mayhaps", which is an archaic version of "perhaps". I found it was difficult to grasp the storyline, until all of the loose ends were tied up in the game's epilogue.The difficulties with the storyline did *not* land up detracting from my overall enjoyment of the game, which was blast to play through the majority of its 40 hour runtime. Afterimage is arguably the best (and definitely the largest) Metroidvanias release since Hollow Knight. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best game I've played in years. I love the metroidvaina genre and this was a breath of fresh air. The combat is great and varied with lots of weapons and armor sets to play with. The zones are stunning, the bosses challenging, and the story actually held my attention and made me want to know what was going on. The new game plus that they made was different than anything I had seen before and really did a great job at telling the rest of the story. I would give this game a solid 8 or 9 out of 10 it was just so enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals and fun game play. Quite a big game, surprised me how much content there was. Similar to other contemporary metroidvanias, it incorporates multiple endings and obscured progression with a healthy amount of ability to sequence break based on either A) your ability to fight strong bosses early or B) your ability to abuse the down kick bounce on flying enemies. The way they handle NG+ was interesting (spoiler warning) . . . . . you unlock a separate game mode where you play in highly curated quest line as an overpowered character. Would be cool if 100% unlocked the ability to play as that character in the base game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is an amazing metroidvania that kept me playing to full completion. The combat was amazing, with six different weapons to choose from. I only tried 4 of them in the scythe, whip, greatsword, and katana so I can't speak to the last two but each weapon felt unique and you unlock new moves with special inputs as you level up your skill tree. Movement felt nice and snappy, I especially loved the downwards dash which I haven't seen too much in other games and it made evading bosses a lot more fun and fast paced. Exploration is really fun too; the areas are all pretty unique and there are lots of items scattered around the map for you to find. I also enjoyed the NG+ which consists of ten chapters from the perspective of a different character which clarifies a lot of what happened in the game and really enhances the story. The art is great and I enjoyed the music. Overall, I highly recommend this game
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage is one of the strangest metroidvanias I've ever played, and extremely half baked. I'd only recommend this if you're a *serious* passionate fan of the genre, and even then you have to be really excited more by the exploration than combat or gameplay. The combat of this game is just boring, plain and simple. The boss fights are way too easy and can all be trivialized by the game's "leveling" system (why does this even exist?). Basically every boss in the game besides the final bosses I first tried and it wasn't even close, simply because I was just exploring a lot, killing everything on the way and leveling up a bunch.The game's map is absolutely massive, bigger than I've ever seen in a metroidvania - but this works to its detriment. There's just no real reason for it, and it takes away from the games charm overall. There's a lot of great ideas here but most of them aren't done well. It really seems like the devs put almost all of the effort into the art (which is incredible, for what it's worth) and everything else was an afterthought. The biggest problem with the scale of everything is that the game ends up overstaying its welcome and you get pretty bored halfway through.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, 24 hours review hereThere art is well-polished here, but in term of game design and character movement flow, it lacks a lot compared to typical platformer like Megaman X/ Donkey Kong/ Ori.1. Let's start with the BIGGEST difference: DASH- Dash has fixed distance traversal and doesn't go along the slope if the slope is downward (upward slope is okay)- There's no transfer of momentum from dash to jump. Basically: you can't "dash jump" in this game. "Dash jump" is the technique that get 'abused' a lot by platformer players to get away from enemies quickly, get further distance when jumping, etc.- Because there's no concept of "dash jump", the "dash cancellable by jump" also doesn't exist. This contributes a lot in rigidity of the game.- Due to dash is not cancellable to jump, you often get contact damage with the enemies. Which I'll talk on the second point2. Contact damageOh boy, this game does punish you a lot with from contact damage. You lose TONS of HP and iframe blinks only last like 1 second or less (other games has 2-4 seconds). In case of spiky ground, you got teleported back to starting point, nullifying your efforts when you need to reach certain chest/items3. Rigid combatThe bad dash contributed a lot to this. Since you can't easily adjust your horizontal movement while jumping, tons of combat (at least in the first 24 hours) is done via positioning, and luring the enemies so that you have low risk on getting hit by them.A lot of skills in the game doesn't give the character iframe. Like many downward, dashing, or jumping skills for many weapons are still iframe-less. There's little to no incentive for the player using them because it makes your character get closer to enemies and be dealt with contact damage (since they have no iframe)4. Unlocking important skill for explorationOnly after 24 hours of play time I can finally get ~80% the necessary skills for exploration. Double jump took more than 10 hours to get, wall climb probably obtained around 18 hours mark and ground smash at 22 hours mark. If only they were to appear sooner (at least give some general direction from the quests on where the players should go), the gameplay shouldn't be so painful.Overall, it's playable game. I definitely going to continue to play. But I just felt that all this painful experience could be removed if they can get better character controls/skill design.In short: Better Dash, more iframes will make the game more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with Castlevania & Metroid. Absolutely preferred Castlevania. Absolutely detest the term 'Metroidvania'.Anyway - I generally find these games to be very dull & return them very quickly. I just feel I am often retreading old ground, but have been hoping one will actually make me CARE and WANT to explore. None of them have - and I really mean none of them - until this.That sense of wanting to explore every nook & cranny, like I did in the original Turrican on the Commodore 64 around 30 years ago is often well rewarded - the world is absolutely gorgeous & ever changing, the difficulty is absolutely fine for a casual player & I love the weapon variety.Personally - it's the most fun I have had in an action platformer with exploitation elements in a very, very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started the game, I was pretty sure I was going to make this a "no" recommendation.  I am still a little torn there, but in the end I think I had enough fun to switch it to a "yes".That being said, I have to say that this is a real mixed bag here.  For one thing, it's huge; that means there's a lot to explore and discover, but at the same time it means it's kind of a slog to get through.  There is a strong art style here with a lot of different biomes, which I love; there are also a ton of different pieces of equipment to change up your playstyle.  For some reason, though, the two never meet; the only cosmetics you get are changing the color of your outfit and the weapon you swing.Put on top of this the innumerable typos, the incomprehensible story, the large amounts of backtracking, the poor signposting for quests, and you get something that won't be for everyone.  If you want something that feels kind of like Symphony of the Night in its gameplay but is much more obtuse, you'll like this.  If you want something where you can poke around in the map for hours looking for secrets and finding hidden bosses, you'll enjoy this.  If you want to grind and get overpowered and eventually just swamp even the secret bosses, this might be for you.  Honestly, if you want emotional character beats, you may be happy with this, just don't expect to understand the story those beats are set in.Don't go into this expecting anything other than a mechanical triumph, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Well If you have enjoyed playing hollow knight then you should try this game as well. Althought there were many times in this game that made me search the entire map for clues on how to advance to other parts of the map, I liked a lot of boss fights and enemy unique behavors, the animation are a bit wonky but you will get used to it. And you should pay close attention to the background most of the time, cuz most of it is breath- taking. Btw you will struggle a lot on bosses as you progress, but once you learn their attacks it is very fun fighting them, just like in hollow knightGood Luck & Have Fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Big map to explore, and you're given a lot of free reign in terms of where you can go at any time.  The downside of that is that while you can stumble on certain strong items earlier than you might otherwise, you may also miss a power-up that helps you get to a lot of treasures, and not even know you missed it.  The combat is sufficiently enjoyable - not the best in the genre, but above average. Can't say I was particularly drawn in by the story, which is a shame because there is a ton of expository dialogue. There were also quite a few typos - not a big deal but something which ought be easy to spot and fix.Biggest complaint is that the quests don't do that best job at guiding you from point to point at all times - but even more so, there was more than one quest I because I didn't retread the same ground at the right time to find the right NPC to even get it started.  So it got to the point where I'd pretty much been everywhere, and seen everything, but couldn't progress because I had to randomly stumble on a couple NPCs who had moved. Had I not resorted to looking things up online that is. Nothing is missable though, so that almost makes up for it - but it did make the end game a bit anticlimactic in that I'd felt like I finished it, but still had to zoom around the map to a bunch of locations I'd already been to a dozen times to talk to NPCs over and over again.One suggestion I have is to not be afraid to upgrade a weapon the first tier or two if it has a special property that seems interesting.  Even the third and final tier you can buy more if need be, but you'll get dozens of the first two tiers.  The descriptions for a lot of weapons and spells are not very well explained so you pretty much have to unlock the ability and try it out to see if its any good. And there aren't any visual indicators or icons for temporary buffs.Although I spent much of this review nitpicking the game, I did enjoy it.  It just didn't stand out in any particular way.  Due to its size and reasonably polished combat I'd recommend to fans of the MV genre looking to scratch that itch.  I played on Advanced, which I'd definitely recommend for veterans of the MV genre because it wasn't overly difficult.  There were a few bosses that took a few attempts because I was fighting them perhaps out of optimal order and am very stingy with consumables, but I prefer when it isn't just a walk in the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very good, challenging, but not extremely difficult, at least for me. Most of the bosses were easy enough to survive with the healing and learning the attacks. Others were more difficult, and required more learning. But still not very difficult for me.There are a lot of healing potions in addition to prayer healing. But maybe that was because I needed very few of them.There are a lot of hidden loot, and places. The progression is non linear, and often predetermined by the level of the character (enemy level), or some movement abilities. There are some pin types which can be put on the map, but not many. They seem however to be enough, at least if you can remember what is the meaning of the pin.The areas, and rooms have beautiful backgrounds, and the story is pretty interesting.There are a lot of weapons, but they would be you get a better weapon type, and switch to it, until some of them get interesting bonuses.There is a way to upgrade the weapons, but I found it not very useful until the endgame. There are some weapons with special bonuses wich only unlock after 2 "cheap" upgrades.The map has completion % but in a very bad way, where every part of the map is counted as a % completion, so if there is a dark non explored area of a room, it will be reduced from the %. For example if there is a big room, and so tall that it wasn't possible to "explore" the ceiling of it, it will be reduced from the % completion. this prevents to know if every item has been collected or not in a certain area.I found the lack of beeing able to move the camera up and down, not very problematic, but still lacking, and in some places it could have been useful.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand the reviewers praising this game, or the reviewers saying "it is this close to being good". It is not. Aside from the art, everything is bad.Music is boring. Story (at least english translation) is terrible. Started skipping cut scenes after the first; nothing makes any sense. The controls feel off. The dodge button is not really for dodging, it is for movement. So when an enemy charges you and you press dodge, you either  dash into him, where YOU receive stun and damage, or you step back, but since the enemies charges in your direction he will hit you regardless. Vertical dodging is not an option as controls feel off. Enemies do not properly telegraph their attacks. The map desgin is bad; no sense of direction. Open world does not mean "make it big and empty and have dozen paths that lead nowhere and make traversing as time consuming and mind numbing as possible". Good Map desgin is hard, and these devs are inept. There are no options for graphics; I had visual tearing and could not activate vsync ingame. Enemies start being spongie WAY to early.There is so much that made me upset in less than one hour. Stay away from it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily my favorite game from the first half of 2023. The movement, combat, art, and music are all exceptional standouts that make it a fantastic experience. The story was definitely a stumbling point, with a poor translation making it even less intelligible, but it wasn't enough to take me out of the game. It's also unreal just how massive this game is, making it an incredible value as well as a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: A mechanically solid, beautifully drawn metroidvania with some real nice animations on our main character, Renee, both for her movement and combat.What stood out to me was the general flow of combat from the get go. Having good movement especially thanks to the dash/backstep right from the start was key to that fluid flow. Combat has a solid amount of depth with the number of weapon types like the katana or dual blades, with one weapon that can even be improved depending on the 2nd weapon you equip. The tech tree looked complicated at first, but really, you will fill it out by the time you're done with the game, so "builds" aren't really a thing. But speaking of the tree, you can unlock weapon-specific skills which after performed by command-inputs much like a fighting game. If metroidvania game devs take any lesson from Afterimage, please let it be this. Such a cool idea that adds a ton of combat depth.Then add to that our standard metroidvania traversal skills and it makes exploring much more fun, and boy is that important because there is SOO much to exploreJust when I thought I had explored a solid handful of areas they throw another 10 more in your face. However, I will say, even though something like Aeterna Noctis is also vast and complicated (although perhaps smaller than Afterimage) the pacing in Afterimage did not feel as good. I would attribute that to the quest journal being very vague and cryptic. Some may like that, where they can rack their brains with the quest puzzles, but if I were to compare it to AN where it would have a marker to the next plot point, Afterimage felt like I was travelling the world for the sake of travelling without much purpose. Sure, I could read each lore bubble that comes my way, or read each item description like its a Souls game to figure it out, but it would feel nice to have at least the mainstory quest have a guiding marker.Speaking of map markers, USE THEM! Open the map, and slap all the stickers down, because you ain't gonna remember that chest or shiny object that needed the double jump from 5 maps ago, or pathways that are blocked because you have to approach from the other direction, so you return to an open path on the map thinking, "oh I haven't explored there yet, lemme take 10 mins to travel there. Oh yeah, it's a blocked wall..." (and yes, there is fast travel between save points but they're consumables so I felt reluctant to use them early on)And make a note of the NPCs for that same reason. The journal mentions to return to quest-givers after collecting items for them, you best have left a marker or note for yourself, because that quest log ain't gonna tell youLastly, the story while giving us lots of questions, could still be followed for the most part and was serviceable. I feel like the game would benefit from a journal log that will expand as you hit major plot points, because like a soulsborne, I forget a lot of stuff and need to read up on some ♥♥♥♥ to remind myself of things and piece the puzzle together. The true ending path did feel a little bit tacked on, but not unwelcome. Definitely an interesting way to deliver it though through their version of New Game+In the end, I did enjoy my time with Afterimage. It has its shortcomings, but I do recommend this beautiful game for those metroidvania lovers out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed Afterimage on Kickstarter and I’m glad I did. I’ve throughly enjoyed playing this fully on the Steam Deck. It runs incredible and is optimized very well. Little to no bugs or lags/stutters. Platforming, movement and combat is great overall.My biggest two complaints:- NPC quests are difficult to keep track of and do not have that much reward for how lengthy/confusing some of them are- the overall story is confusing and I wish was more cohesive and easier to follow. I really enjoy the story of video games, so this was a bummer, but not game breakingThere could definitely be more improvements with future patch updates and I hope there will be, but I overall it’s incredible and I highly recommend this game if you enjoy metroidvania’s

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very decent metroidvania. The world is huge, there's a lot of enemy types and abilities. Whole game took huge inspiration from Hollow Knight, but it's not a bad thing. All weapon types are fun to use once you unlock some of their skills, soundtrack isn't anything special, but it was pleasant. Story can be a tiny bit confusing, might be a translation issue. It's extremely easy at the beginning, but gets a bit of challenge late game. Highly recommend advanced difficulty, since "normal" one is more of an easy choice and makes the game have completely no challenge at all. Tho take this with a grain of salt, since I have some experience with other metroidvanias and for me this one was probably the easiest I've played up to date.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous!You see the price and compare it to other metroidvanias out there and think "Man, maybe there isn't as much content" but then you boot up the game and you play and play and play and the map just doesn't seem to stop because it's gigantic and there is so much exploration you could do with a little backtracking after you complete certain tasks. Also the quests take hours to complete because there is no such thing as "Get me X items and I give you X gold" boom, achievement, no no no. Quests take hours because they also tell a story and make you explore.Gameplay - At first it's easy, you jump, attack blah blah then it turns into dark souls because your dash doesn't have an i-frame until later on in the game, you can't double jump yet and such. Overall there are a variety of upgrades for your character like a talent tree, 6 types of weapons, spells and trinkets.Music - Nothing very fantastic, your typical fantasy OST. Story - You play as Renee, a young amnesiac girl and student of Aros, that is the lone survivor of the attack on her village.The game excels in being hard until you learn basic mechanics, I love every single aspect about this game and if I could forget everything that was in it just so I could replay it again, I would.Verdict - GET. IT.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost didn't buy this game because of some of the reviews I read... That's frustrating, because this a fantastic game. If you like Metroidvanias, give this game a chance. The art style is truly beautiful. The world is absolutely enormous and there's so much to explore. The combat is tight and fluid, however, the one thing a lot of people criticized are the hit boxes and I agree with that. Sometimes things hit you when they clearly didn't touch you, and occasionally your attack will just whiff, it's annoying but far from a deal breaker, 98% of the time it's great. Another criticism is of the music, and I don't get it, the music is atmospheric and fits the locations really well, Town of the Exiled comes to mind. As the story begins we aren't given a whole lot of context or exposition, it can feel underdeveloped at points, but it comes together as you progress. But strong storytelling isn't the selling point of the genre, look at SOTN, it's about the world and how much fun it is to explore and level up, in that respect Afterimage delivers. I will give it a mention that there are several nods to SOTN in this game, some just aesthetic but there was a point late in the game when in order to progress you have to equip a certain item or two, and if I had never played SOTN I don't think I would have figured it out. Another criticism I have is of the auto-save system. There are many times when I'd like to say, fully upgrade a weapon just to see the perks, or use a specific consumable and reload the game if I don't like it, but you can't do that. It auto-saves upon exit, so it kind of eliminates the ability to experiment with certain items. That's more a subjective gripe and for some I'm sure it's not a problem. The only other criticism I have is there's no stats screen for your character.  There's a basic Max HP, DEF, STR, etc. in the skill tree window, and every one of those stats that is tied to your gear is reflected there. The problem is that the majority of your gear has other stat bonuses, i.e. EXP %, Elemental DEF, HP Absorb, and so many others. Obviously you see the buff in the gear description, but that's it, so if you want to stack buffs a certain type and care to see what the cumulative number is, better get out your calculator. A main stat page would also define your EXP as a number, or at least ___ to your next level, and your current HP, xxx/yyy, but those values are only shown in the gauges during gameplay, these basic things are just bizarrely absent. Those small UI issues aside, I really like this game, and I definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania. Map is huge, which means lots of explore (fun) and lots to traverse (not fun for backtracking). Fast travel is OK, only one per zone, and convenient fast travel (multiple points per zone) is restricted to a limited item (late game opens this up). Combat felt good, lots of weapon types (only ever used one, honestly) and gear. Story is convoluted, primarily due to special terms used in this game. Dialogue is not great, but voice acting was pretty good. I didn't love the overall art style of the game, and the game has little animation (it uses a lot of static assets slightly rotated back and forth for movement), but individually the art was nice and clearly had effort spent on it.Exploration and progress is generally non-linear, which is fun and also can be easy to get lost, as you will get a feel of what skill you need but don't know where to go to get it, and the huge map can lengthen that search. But there is so much to explore that the journey feels exquisite.Depth is deep. Lots of quests, figuring out how to finish the quests, how to unlock certain areas, discovering a lot of areas are actually optional when completing the basic endings, discovering all the endings (like 10? had to read a guide), and wrapping your head around a lot of small secrets.A few notes:1. Inventory handling is kind of weird. It will keep an icon for items you do or don't have (it'll show 0), which really fluffs up your view. Plus you cannot sell the last copy of any weapon or outfit, which means that items that you ever get one of (like a special chest) will stay in your inventory forever. The only items of that kind that gets sold will be rare equipment drops from common enemies. So I never bothered trying to sell anything, basically.2. The game will show a completion percentage (0 to 100%) per zone and is based on map uncovered, and NOT based on items obtained. You can obtain an afterimage late game that shows the actual number of items obtained vs available, which is what's actually helpful.Anyway, this is a great game for MV fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and absolutely GIGANTIC Castlevania-style metroidvania game. Every time you think "oh, I guess that's probably the end of this direction of the map" it surprises you with more. Just do not expect too much of a story that makes terribly much sense. It is not as though there was no story, it is just told rather poorly, leaving pretty much everything to interpretation. The quality of the English translation did not help, although the Japanese voice acting did not seem terribly much better.I guess it is worth noting that when the English text says "Beings", capitalised, the Japanese text literally says "Humans" ("ningen"), thus shifting the meaning of a central object in the game from "source of all life" towards "source of human life specifically". Which kind of makes sense, all things considered.The controls are pretty good, my main complaints would be that most weapon skills are not great or hard to use and execute properly and that magic cannot be cast mid-air. Further, there are several areas that do not show up on your world map at all, making exploration annoying and difficult. These areas are mostly either pretty small or part of the post-game/true end, however - that means, the majority of the gameplay is not affected.Other points I can state that may be viewed as more positive or negative:- The game will not hold your hand much, it will let you explore just about anywhere, there are sequence breaks available and it handles them like a champ. The downside to that is that it also does not really tell you where to go.- While you should focus speccing into only 1-2 weapon types that you like and actively use early on, later on you can easily 100% the Talent tree, enabling you to use any weapon with proficiency. Some people have complained about the lack of necessity to specialise, I like that you can change your mind without having to respec late in the game. My favoured weapons were the greatsword as main and the whip as secondary weapons, for their sheer power and range, and the amazing aerial attack, respectively. Until near the end of the game, I decided to use blades as my main weapon instead.- One weird thing, though: the achievement acquisition is weirdly off-balance. I got the first 2-3 achievements near the beginning rather quickly, but then it took me several days until i finally got another (and that one was the most random achievement, for dealing exactly 666 damage...). But then, near the end of the game, I got about 20 of the remaining achievements back to back.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by stating that I have now fully completed and explored the game with 100% achievements. This is more or less your usual metroidvania in terms of map/mechanics and is very enjoyable - definitely worth the asking price. - Gameplay is responsive and fun. The different weapons offer enough variety. You unlock additional passive effects as you progress (including invincibility frames for the dash). - The world and music are beautiful and a joy to explore and experience. The map is much bigger than you think. - The story unique and engaging (I had a lot of fun with the true ending). Both the Main and Side quests give you general directions (not always enough but overall decent). NPCs are displayed on your map so that you can more easily find them (Some side quests require you to find NPCs in various locations as they move around). Overall, a great game that is definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could offer a more neutral review of this game. While it functions well as a metroidvania game, the combat can become repetitive. The variety of weapons does help to alleviate this issue. However, the game requires a lot of grinding. After 11 hours of gameplay, I am only at level 45, and some areas I've encountered are meant for players at level 75. Unlike most metroidvania games, this game does not challenge the player through abilities and mechanical skill but instead through equipment and numbers. Additionally, it's easy to miss important abilities or upgrades while playing.The story of the game is probably its biggest downfall. It's quite incomprehensible. Although the introduction sets up a premise of souls not returning to the world as they should, which has resulted in a wasteland, none of the NPCs, including the main character, refer to it. Instead, players are thrown into the middle of a story without any explanation, making it difficult to follow. I've stopped reading the text because it just adds to my confusion.If you don't mind a lot of grinding and want to play a side-scrolling action RPG metroidvania with fluid combat and movement, you could consider buying this game at a deep discount. However, if you're looking for a more engaging experience, it might be better to wait for upcoming releases like Silksong or other highly-anticipated metroidvania games.Given my current backlog, I am not entirely sure why I keep coming back to this game... Oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Afterimage

_childDocuments_.review: Finished with all 10 endings.Beautiful art style, enormous areas to explore and good combat. Movement also feels really good. Music was servicable to good. There are a few things that were a bit irritating:Item descriptions often mention buffs / debuffs or skills / spells but don't explain what they actually mean or do. There is no proper explanation for your different stats. Some are easy to understand but something like the difference between "Normal Attack Damage" and "Main Weapon Damage" isn't.The skill tree was a bit annoying to navigate. You shouldn't have to go through each ability every time you open the menu.The story is completely incomprehensible with a lot of terminology thrown around. I suppose they couldn't really find a good way to translate from Chinese to English while still having the story make sense. The quest log suffers from that too. Quite a few typos in there as well. It's very unfortunate because a comprehensible story would elevate this game a lot. I still really enjoyed my time with the game and would rate it 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Afterimage started out beautifully - the gameplay is fun, the scenery is gorgeous, and the world is intriguing. I loved exploring the environment, getting upgrades, and growing exponentially stronger throughout the journey. Everything from the beginning to the mid-game was incredible.Unfortunately, my enthusiasm slowed down during the end-game. There are more than 5 endings, with non-obvious clues to get the required items for them; and the epilogue content is almost exclusively story. The post-game content was enjoyable again, after the story had run it's course, but that may also be because I started using a guide to alleviate the tedium.Nevertheless, the majority of the game remains fantastic. I loved my adventure with it, and only wish that I put it down after the final boss - but for a completionist, there is a lot of tedium at the very end.

_childDocuments_.review: love the game! it was a refreshing 2d metroidvania games. you may call it a rip off and whatnot but to me its successful in delivering that nostalgia that you got from playing SOTN years ago (which many other recent games attempted but failed in doing so). The exploration (how its expand as you acquire more exploration skills), the battle + skill system, difficulty level to me is satisfying and rewarding at the same time. my rant in the battle system will only be in the lack of explanation on subweapon capabilities (thus I finished the entire game without ever using it). The story can get confusing (i think because of a translation issue). but apart from it, the game is amazing! Give it a try especially if you are a fan of 2d metroidvania type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: In my personal opinion, the main storyline of "Afterimage" isn't quite as strong as it could be. It tends to lean towards drama and dark fantasies, but doesn't fully explore its potential. The narrative revolves around the legend of the god who created the world, as well as the tale of Goliath and the ambitions of humans.The protagonist, Renee, starts the game with amnesia, accompanied by a partner or friend named Ifree who stays with her throughout her journey. In the world created by the god Luca, Renee sets out to uncover the mysteries behind the world's curse, her lost memories, and to aid new friends she encounters along the way.Surprisingly, the most intriguing aspects of the story come from the NPCs who provide side quests. Their stories are so engaging that sometimes you'll find yourself reluctant to finish all the quests too quickly.Overall, while the main storyline may not be the game's strongest suit, the depth and richness of the side quests more than make up for it, providing an immersive and captivating experience.The evocative soundtrack of Afterimage enhances the game's atmosphere, immersing players in its richly detailed world. Each track is meticulously crafted to evoke emotion and set the tone for various gameplay moments. From stirring battle themes to tranquil exploration melodies, the soundtrack elevates the overall gaming experience.My favorite theme:

_childDocuments_.review: + art direction and graphics generally are excellent+ music is great- story is nonsense, mostly because of bad writing or voicework- progression system doesn't allow you to make builds- UI needed a few more months in the ovenWhat Afterimage does well is the general look and feel of the gameplay. As something that plays like Castlevania, it really does it justice for the most part. Some antiquated design ideas like contact damage I don't personally care for, but the gameplay feels solid. It also looks fantastic while you're playing: some animations might not chain together well (for example, running from a standstill looks awkward) but generally the artwork and level art design are excellent.I wish the game world was a little denser, or at least was condensed. There's a lot of beautiful areas, but they could have been shrunk down 1/4 and the world would still feel empty. There's so many long stretches of nothing of interest or note, it's a shame because a world denser with content or NPCs or anything, really, would have been preferable.Enemies, despite looking nice, feel braindead. For the most part, they run or fly at you, sometimes using weapons but most of the enemies I saw so far don't. It's uninteresting to play because there's no nuance in their behavior. Bosses, too, where they have a rotation of moves that don't "wow" you like bosses in another game would be. It's also trivially easy: you can tank hits all day, it kind of doesn't matter. Even very early on I felt like I was way too resilient for these kind of games.Writing and voice acting when taken together feels like it was AI generated. VA delivery is hit and miss but it's not helped by the sloppy writing. There's so much word soup early on, I'd hesitate to call it lore dumps because the game will spring a new term on you and it's not written well enough that you can infer from context, but it's also never explained what many of these words mean. The story is made out to be some grand affair but the writing just doesn't support it. I never felt invested in the characters or the world, unfortunately.The talent tree is poorly planned: very early on you'll realize that you can't really specialize in one area because besides the initial talent unlock, upgrading talents beyond the base level requires you to be a much higher level. You'll need to scan the tree just to find  to unlock, and often that something is unrelated to your "build", in quotes because to get the talents you want for a specific playstyle often requires you to spend numerous other points in unrelated playstyles. You're forced into one build, a jack-of-all-trades which makes potential future runs a harder bargain.UI in general is a sore spot. Frequently when gameplay transitions to dialog boxes, the camera might go off in the distance to look at nothing, or an empty dialog box appears and nothing happens. In fact, the  didn't even load properly for me, I only saw it for a couple of frames because the cutscene preceding it bugged. Navigating menus, how slow it feels to find an item or navigate the map, I have to wonder why they didn't put more time into that. Games like these benefit immensely from speed and everything becomes a standstill the moment you open a menu or dialog.I put it down after only a few bosses because I've seen enough. There just wasn't something there to immediately hook me, and in fact, there was little to keep me entertained in the few hours I spent. Put plain, Afterimage is boring but also frustrating: boring with its massive empty world and uninteresting enemies/bosses, frustrating in its lack of polish and UI design. The gameplay feels nice but gameplay alone hasn't justified a game since the 90s, and it's in the "everything else" that I cannot recommend Afterimage.At 10w max TDP, at least however far I got, was consistently 60fps. Render scale set to 100%, highest graphic setting. Text can be difficult to read, in general the game could have used a zoom-in feature as even your character roaming around can be hard to see. Controls well on Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it in the beginning and I still do 12 hours later, but I got to a point where the difficulty ramped up like crazy. Went from destroying everything with rarely having to heal to now getting 2-3 shot by normal enemies and 1-2 shot by bosses.It was so abrupt that I feel like I'm missing something.They also went way too hard on the inaccessible areas where every 2 min I find a new spot I need to fly, swim, break the floor or get through a barrier which I can't do at the moment while the last big ability I got was 6 hours ago.I still recommend it, but only if you like metroidvania games. Combat is smooth and responsive and the game looks great but it has a lot of pacing issues for me.Edit: I was actually missing not one but a few areas which explains the difficulty increase, but it's still strange how out of your way you have to go to find these level appropriate areas.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to finish the game, but it became so frustrating that I gave up. At first, I was enjoying it, but the more I played, the more boring and frustrating it got. The developers tried to include too many features without making sure they all worked well together and felt satisfying. The story is uninteresting, the gameplay lacks polish, the map is too large, and there are other significant flaws.With so many issues, I'll focus on the two most frustrating things: the gameplay and the map.GameplayThe gameplay is simple, which isn't necessarily bad. Many games with simple gameplay are incredibly fun. The problem is a lot of things just doesn't work. Skills are often frustrating to use, with most being ineffective and some skills making you taking damage and cancel the skill. Aerial combat is the most frustrating things, you have almost nothing to do with flying enemies and for some resson you can't use your magic in the air (or the dumb name they use, the subweapon). In early game the gameplay works fine but the enemies have simple attacks layout. However, in the late game, they spam attacks, some are in area and you have two options to deal with it, use one of two wepon that have a parry skill (that doesn't work becouse you end inside de enemy most of the times and take damage ) or you can dash back to evade the attack and dash to the enemy to attack again, but the enemy is starting a new attack because f*** you. The lack of more defensive options like a guard or evade make the late game a pain to play. With enemies with ranged attacks, a lot of projectiles that came so fast you can't even react and to help make things worse, some areas the background makes very hard to impossible to see what is coming. The hitbox and hurtbox of all is just a mess, I tooked a lot of hits that you can clearly see how bad the shape of the hitbox and to finish, attacks sometimes just pass through enemies (most in aerial combat).MapThe map is extremely unnessecery big. It doesn't make sense make a map to big and implement such a bad fast travel system. Each area contains a large teleport tree, but it's often necessary to walk long distances to reach items that were previously inaccessible. There are small trees that you can fast travel but require potions so is limeted to use and are equally problematic due to the map's size.I like exploring but I like to know where I need to go too, and most of the time you don't have idea where to go and with a such big map makes more confusing. The map to use in the menu is terrible too, I think needed more information like plataforms, a not terrible zoom out to see the things better and a mini map could really help explore more enfficiently and make me stop open to menu to see where tf I am going.ConclusionIn the end it's sad to me that I couldn't finish the game. There were some aspects that I really enjoy, like soundtrack, the itens system, some RPG elements, the skills that work is fun to use, voice acting and other small things. However, when considering the overall experience, the game fail in the most important aspect for me: fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Trust me, i really want to recommend this game.Everything about this game SCREAMED passion and style. From the art direction, the combat style, the very image of the world (no pun intended)But, as it stands right now, this game is... very rough. Especially when you compare it to a vastly better counterpart, or its inspiration even, which is VERY clearly Hollow Knight.The combat is very rough. And it is not in a fun-hard kinda way like HK or similar metroidvania either. The map layout is... kinda ♥♥♥♥ most of the time, at least in my experience playing through the early sections of the game world. Backtracking is HELL with this kind of map layout, and the sheer fact that you have to backtrack the entire f-ing way just to get to a particular ledge again because an enemy that spawn RIGHT AT THE EDGE of the other section decided to snipe you across the map. Speaking of enemies - the enemy design is so awful. Either they bumrush you and leave no room for staggering, or they decide to stun every single hit you make. It is... very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird. And a mechanic that i think is very neat with this type of game - the ability to deflect projectiles - is fun at first with a couple first enemies which, arguably, best design for this type of ♥♥♥♥, when you clearly have to deflect their own attack back at them in a creative way in order to get past them. But later enemies... they just eat up too much projectiles. To the point that despite harder to kill them by melee attacks, you would rather just do that anyway because it took too long for them to die to their own bullets. And the game kinda KNOWS this, so they force you to fight those types of enemy SEVERAL times throughout the game in situations that you have to deflect their own attacks on ledges that once you dropped, you have to backtrack like half the game to get there once again. You tried to dash in and melee, they just knock you down to backtrack; but if you decided to deflect their attacks, IT TOOK FOREVER JUST TO KILL ONE ENEMY."But there is talent tree where you can increase your stats!!!" That's another gripe i have with the game. _childDocuments_.review: It's got some good, but not enough. First, some pros: the game looks good. Pretty art, pretty environments all over, feels pretty good to move around. It sounds pretty good. Decent music, effects, etc. Neutral stuff: It's got combat. It's got combos for your weapons (neat). It's also got leveling and a huge skill tree that is 95% "do 2% extra damage in this specific scenario". One weapon attack, one weapon type, etc. It functions, and it technically makes for some customization, but could have been good if it was like, 1/5 the nodes and have each one be more significant. Abilities I got before I stopped were bog standard too. Dash, air dash, double jump. Nothing bad, nothing that made me go "Oh, fun new idea, neat." Bad stuff: It's huge. Like the map should be, like the skill tree, 1/5 of it's size. So much walking for the sake of it. Not enough interesting to do, just... more.... walking and some jumping. They have hidden little upgrades and items and things, but like the skill tree, that also amounts to a lot of tiny incremental damage upgrades on a specific item type, so most of it feels next to useless. The story is nonsense, or if it made sense in the original Chinese, the translation is so rough I don't really know or care what's going on. It's pretty bad. Directions of where to go are nonexistent, which can be a fantastic thing in a Metroidvania if done right. In this I just got bored walking around for 20+ minutes unable to find where the game wanted me to go next. Even map markers for when I ran into a dead end would be fantastic, but it just gives you one goal and has 7 maps in between you and that spot, so... good luck. All in all I can see the effort and love from the devs, but I'm sorry, there needed to be a few more people involved in translation, talks about purposes for upgrades, items, and locations, and some more intentional map design that points you in the right direction or an optional help system. Something. Too many games in this genre do all of these things better to spend the time with this one.
