_childDocuments_.review: Leaving an early review to help with discoverability, but unless something dramatically changes later on, this is one of the best controlling 3D platformers I've played in recent memory.The controls are snappy, the camera is fluid, the level design is smart, and the overall design is laser-focused. This game knows exactly what it aims to be, and achieves its goals with precision. The mix of 3D and precision platforming feels great, and there's something for many people to enjoy: cruising through levels with a lovely faux-retro aesthetic, collecting all hidden objects, or speedrunning for best times and scores.If you have any love for 3D platforming at all, be sure to check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun if your trying to casually play it but for me I wanted to 100% the game so I almost did 100% the first character (hana) but why is it not that fun to 100% the game? cause you cant die on every lvl which gets easy over time which makes it more harder for you so I would say if you want a hard platformer get this also to the creator of this game if your seeing I got the true ending and saw the msg at the end your mom would be very proud of what you have done
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little game. Simple but very tight controls, hella charming old school graphics, and fun level design. The game is fairly relaxing and not too punishing, except for the baking world that made me rage with much vigor. (in a fun way. mostly.)By default you have kind of a wide turning radius, but there's an option in settings that makes movement feel much better. Its called quick turning or something like that. With overwhelmingly positive reviews I cant exactly call Lunistice underrated, however it does seem fairly little known. It deserves a strong recommendation for anyone with an interest in the genre, and for everyone else it's cheap, short and accessible enough to be an easy yes as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and fun platformer!List of things I liked:- Very well designed platformer- Very simple character easy to use- Controls are straightforward (easy to learn)- Variety of mechanics added in every level as you advance on the game- Good price for the content it gives- Small (with small I mean small) background story that may encourage you to finish the game.List of things I found boring:- Very slow phased on the first 3 levels of the game (very easy platforming)- The character you control has a great speed but I sometimes wished you could make it faster even if there are mechanics that take care of that.- I didn't get the story that much, maybe by replaying it and reading carefully I will understand it. (Maybe just skill issue of reading)And I think nothing else is on my mind, the game is great and I loved every part of it.Btw there is a mechanic in game that may make it easier ingame, just press space bar and the attack button instantly after space to make a super jump (you need to hold the space bar for maximum height too)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game and story line, We get to follow this well built story while playing a character we slowly learn about as you progress farther in the game. It's so rewarding staying behind and taking the extra minute to collect everything just for the additional story as well. This game gives endless hours of lore and entertainment. Also Love Toree so seeing the lil duck felt amazing. Please keep up the amazing work. Love your games, glad to know you and Siactro are friends cause both of your guys games are absolutely stunning!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: - This is pure fast-paced precision 3D platforming. All you do is run and jump from platform to platform while avoiding hazards and not falling into the abyss- With Hana (the main character), movement feels slippery and some times makes it hard to realize where you'll land, especially when first starting out. The negative user reviews are fair in this regard, try out the demo if that worries you- Hana's attack gives her small upwards boost, essentially allowing you to triple jump, which feels satisfying- Upon beating the game for the first time, it unlocks 2 other slightly different characters:- Toree is faster than Hana, but dies in one hit and has no attack, so it can only double jump. Maybe I just got better, but it feels less slippery and easier to control- Toukie has small jump height, but can flap its wings 3 times to go higher and attack to stall falling - that's a quintuple jump and, yes, it feels good too- I kinda recommend against going for 100% with Hana right away just so you unlock the other characters faster and can decide which one you prefer before getting tired of playing the same levels- The camera follows you around and changes on its own, so it can be janky- I found Lunistice a joy to play, well worth my time
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the biggest fan of platformers, though it isn't to say I dislike them. I usually feel more neutral of them overall, but when one I play one that clicks, I treasure it. Needless to say, Lunistice is just that. This game is an absolute treasure, putting a smile on my face from beginning to end. The price is perfect and, while a very quick game (about 90ish minutes), the replay factor is extraordinary.The music is just lovely; nothing out of the blue or in your face. It's a nice bgm which accents the levels quite nicely. In addition, the visual style is a cute homage to the playstation 1's overall look. Hana is the cutest tanuki and, after finishing the game, a few other members are playable which change some gameplay elements.I will say the gameplay is the weakest part, if you're looking for a title with a little more depth. But the feel of the game, the movement, is fluid and superb. I personally prefer my games in the genre to nail movement above all else. You can build after, but sometimes, simple is truly for the best.The game is 5 dollars which makes this an easy decision if you're looking for a new game to play through. It's an absolute delight from start to finish!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to be mean to this game, because it's clearly had a lot of time and love put into it. But man the core design of the thing just isn't very good. It's essentially structured like a fully open Crash Bandicoot game, "linear" levels that are very open and require thorough exploration to 100% complete. Unfortunately, because Hana feels so weightless to control- bolting from 0 to 100 the second you touch the stick and having very simple animations- exploration isn't very satisfying at the best, and "swearing-at-the-game-with-the-cookie-platforms" frustrating at the worst. Add to that HOW stages branch off to hide extras, and how it encourages you to get every crane in a stage to 100% it [which is far more like getting every coin in a Mario 64 stage than getting every crate in a Crash stage], and the game is VERY stop and go. Even if you're not going for 100%, the problem of "wait which of these paths should I take?" is consistently there, because it's not obvious when you get to a fork in the road which path leads to a collectible and which leads to progression in the stage.Lastly- and this is just a personal gripe- Lunistice does that thing where the cute video game has a dark sad backstory told through lore logs you find in "glitchy" parts of the stages. I'm so damn sick of that cliche man, creepypastas and their consequences have been nothing but a disaster for cute indie games.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A great fun platformer, with plenty of content to keep you replaying if you enjoy it enough:- 2 different types of collectables throughout each level- 3 types of S-rankings per level to try to achieve- 2 extra unlocked characters with gameplay differencesThe graphics are cute, each world with its own distinct theme and gimmicks.The music is fun and very catchy.And overall the movement feels good, but personally, brought the experience down a bit sometimes... The game starts to require quite some precision which is difficult on its own, but as with many 3D platformers, depth perception became a frequent problem.To help with the depth perception, you have a very visible shadow below you from any height, but the game often gets quite fast, and some of the platforms quite tight, not giving you much time to make sure you're lined up.Luckily there are plenty of checkpoints, and no lives to worry about, but it destroyed any desire I had to go for the S-Ranks for 0 retries and the time limits.But other than the depth perception, any 3D platformer fan should enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A bang for your buck 3D platformer at an inexpensive price. The gameplay reminds me of Sonic and Mario Galaxy with how the environments are and how the stages are paced. It was a bit frustrating at first but enabling shadows and messing with the smooth turning option helped out a lot for the rest of the game, especially in those tight turns and platforms. What killed me the most was overshooting jumps and falling off slippery ledges. The momentum could be better but you get used to it as you play.The enemies are cute but they do have the same designs per stage except at the end. They're pretty simple, you pretty much just run at them then press attack. It has collect-a-thon mechanics in cranes and letter blocks which help make the stages more engaging but some cranes are only present in branching paths where the letter blocks are. The stages also have hidden stuff which contribute to the later half of the game too, without getting into much spoilers.Otherwise, it's a quick game to finish. I believe my first playthrough ended around the 2 hour mark with the rest being the other characters and just completing the collectibles. It's a great game in short bursts and the replay value is definitely present here. My only gripes are some branching paths which can be difficult to spot at first unless you look for them and the Autumn stage which hurts my eyes when I look at the skybox.Rounding it out at quite a low price tag, keep this game on your radar if you're a fan of 3D platformers in general. If you're looking to kick back and relax, pick it up! It won't hurt your wallet and its definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Quirky platformer with a neat little story in the background charming PS1 graphics and a lot of Sonic Adventure style gameplay with really smooth platforming and neat environments. Soundtrack is also a banger. Worst thing I can say about this game is I wish it could last a little longer, maybe one more world? But at 5 bucks it's an awesome grab to play through an evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, the first three worlds are great: great music, great flow, bright and colourful aesthetics. Then World four with the disappearing platforms comes around and goes "slow down, this is a rhythm game now" except your character falls too slowly for the fast-changing platforms. This is where I started just speeding towards the end as fast as possible, whereas before I was enjoying exploring and collecting all the cranes+letters. Then there's world five, with a neat autumn aesthetic (in the background at least, the vines and platforms were a sort of pixelated vomit colour, for lack of a better description), but the layout was confusing and frustrating. I realised I wasn't really having fun anymore and decided to put the game down.I do also wish the game gave you a letter score based on your speed (maybe there's an achievement? Idk), since there's a timer and there's so many mechanics that get you moving faster, but it appears to be more of a "take your time collectathon and don't die" game. If that's your thing, and you enjoy a challenge, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully charming Sega Saturn inspired platformer that is equally simple and challenging. Lunistice offers 17 brisk, action-packed levels across 9 uniquely themed worlds. These levels are largely liner challenges that combine tight platforming with fast moving theme-based gimmicks and a dash of simple combat that keeps a healthy dose of excitement and flow. Hidden collectibles, a challenging but rewarding ranking system and unlockable extra characters with unique playstyles wrings out a lot of playtime for an otherwise quick journey. This genius design allows for quick replay sessions or more casual play while offering plenty of challenges for players wanting more. A cryptic (if very low profile) narrative, gorgeous 32-bit inspired visuals, and a mix of energetic and relaxing music makes for an exceptionally well-priced experience. The game seems to have a fetish for levels over bottomless bits, which along with some occasional weird platform detection are the only major criticisms. If you like 3D platformers this is an easy buy for all ages and skill levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I barely ever play 3D platformers, so no idea how much weight my opinion has here, but I thought the difficulty curve was really solid, and the gameplay was overall really fun (especially after I realized you can get the S-Ranks achievement by doing both parts separately -- meant the last run in each stage was just speeeeeeeed)! Relatively simple gameplay loop, but it gets pretty much everything right besides the odd annoying section or two.Definitely recommend, even if you aren't usually a 3D platformer enjoyer. Simple, but it's got lots of love behind it!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent homage to PS1/Sega Saturn platformers. The movement feels excellent and there was never a moment where I blamed the controls for my deaths. The game looks spot on for the time, which can be a pro or con depending on who you are, but for me the nostalgia hit hard the whole time.In regards to completion, It will take about 10/12 hours to 100% the game and overall it felt like just the right amount of time. I didn't get bored and when I finished I felt satisfied.The music in this game slaps. I regularly mute games and play with something else off to the side. This game I never muted and went so gar as to recommend not only the game but the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: So close to being a great game. Music is a jam and a half. Art style is fantastic. Great level design. The main issue I have with it is how it controls. There's some fundamental issues I have with it that makes me hate playing it, and it's mostly camera stuff that could be fixed.When it comes to camera's in third-person games there are a lot of settings that have been used to get a good feel. Personally, I'm against pretty much all of them. I want full agency of where I'm looking, and I will move the camera where and when I feel the need to. This game will shift your camera left and right if you are just moving in that direction, very similar to Splatoon, with no option to turn it off. As for mouse options, the resolution of the game is low (for aesthetic reasons, it's not a bad thing) so all mouse movements are exaggerated. There's options to tunr down the sensitivity, but the lower limit is 50% depending on the setting and it's still too high. There's also some deceleration to mouse movements, causing it to feel like it's slides a little more after you've stopped moving your mouse. Again, no option to turn it off. There's also a minor thing of some areas not having good depth perception, but there's an option to unlock the vertical cap on the camera to help remedy that.I really wish I could play this game. It looks really fun, but the camera is such an important aspect to platformers, and getting it wrong can make it unplayable for some people, especially those who are sensitive to excessive camera movements. In my opinion, if a dev is going to add extra camera functions, please add a setting to turn it off. There are people who don't want any setting for their camera in third-person. A Hat in Time did an amazing job with their camera, including many functions that help people, but a setting for just about every single way the camera works. While not every game has to be as in depth as AHiT, just having a toggle can go a long way for many players.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a really fun 3D platformer that's really simple to pick up and play but very difficult to master. The controls are tight and responsive while also having a good sense of flow and forward momentum, and the levels are cleverly built to take full advantage of that. It's almost like if a 3D Sonic game was made for the Saturn back in the day.Gameplay wise, it never holds your hand, but at no point does it feel cryptic as to what you're supposed to do or how everything works. There's a tutorial you can play from the main menu if you need to know how the game works, whereas the actual game itself assumes you know how to play making it good for both newcomers and experienced players. It's also pure 3D platforming the entire way through - no forced combat arenas, no stealth segments, no mini-games and no bosses to break the pace. There are also no 2D sections which is a huge plus.Each level feels expertly crafted and built for all kinds of platforming players from casuals to speedrunners. One of my favourite levels is the food themed levels where coloured biscuit platforms change from outlined to solid in time to the beat of the music, requiring players to keep a good rhythm if they wish to make those jumps.Levels are fairly linear and only require players to reach the end of the level. While you have infinite lives and checkpoints are well spread out so you never have to redo too much progress, the number of resets per level are tracked and you're ranked based on how many resets you've made. Each level also has cranes to collect along the way, along with a ranking system that grades you at the end based on how many cranes you collect and the number of resets, so there's plenty of replay value that encourage coming back to levels you already beat.Unlike other platformers that typically have a run button that makes you move faster when held down, Lunistice has a walk button that allows you to walk slower which is useful for those very narrow walkways or small platforms that require extra precision. You can invert this in the options if you prefer it the other way around. Also, if you're having a hard time landing on platforms due to the depth perception that comes with the third dimension, you can turn on drop shadows in the options so you can get a good idea at to where you're going to land.I love having PS1/Saturn style pixelated 3D graphics in my games, and Lunistice more than delivers on that. In addition to feeling like a throwback to the mid-late 90's era of 3D graphics, this game also has a strong visual style of its own that sets it apart from others in the genre. There are also options for a CRT filter and 20FPS modes to make it feel even more retro, though I chose to play with those off.The music is also fantastic and each track fits the theme of the levels really well in addition to providing memorable tunes that stay in your head even after you're done playing. Stage 5-2 takes place in a gigantic tree that has had its music completely drained, requiring players to go through each of the different areas of the level to gradually restore the music before finishing the level with the music fully restored to how it was in 5-1. The food themed levels also include the neat touch of having some of the scenery dance in time to the beat of the music which I thought was really cool.Honestly, for its asking price, this game is a steal! I would've paid double the asking price and I'd still find it good value for my money. It's a really fun 2-3 hour game that is a must-buy for those that love the 3D platformer genre like I do and it's a shame we don't see enough games like this nowadays. It also brings me back to a time where games were designed with fun in mind first and foremost.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: If you're being recommended Lunistice for any reason whatsoever: Pick it up. It's an incredible value for 5 dollars.When it comes to 3D platformers, very few control as well as Lunistice. There's so much responsiveness, and just the right amount of restriction... It's hard to explain, but no matter what you're trying to do, 99.99% of the time, your character will do that thing, and it will have the results you wanted. That may seem vague, but if you've played enough 3D platformers, you know exactly what I mean.The level design is wonderful as well, and frankly this is what 3D Sonic should have been from the beginning. The sense of speed and control is phenomenal, and it's only complemented by the wonderful level designs, visuals, and music.I really only have two nitpicks, and these are extremely minor, and definitely understandable considering the small scope of this project. I should note, before jumping into those, that this game does reuse a lot of assets, but in very clever ways that you won't notice at first. Anyway, the nitpicks:There are only really 4 enemy types, and maybe 2 of them are a threat. They also don't change their appearance to match their setting (with a few notable exceptions). Really though, these simple enemies do well with the simplicity of the combat, and defeating them always feels great, It's not really that big a deal, all things considered.The other thing that jumped out at me was a bit more jarring. The next to last world, which I won't spoil anything about, except that some of the grinding segments can be a bit persnickety about when you need to jump, leading to some deaths that will set you back a ways, as the last checkpoint was quite some time ago. Again though, this is offset by the brevity and quality of the other aspects of the levels. I just wanted to be thorough and collect all my thoughts here.Like I said at first, if you've been recommended this for any reason; aesthetics, music, gameplay, whatever, just do yourself a favor and pick it up. If I could force more game devs to make their platformers control more like Lunistice, I would in a heartbeat.Oh, and the dev for Lunistice is really cool and takes player feedback very seriously. Shoutouts to them!!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet and slightly challenging (at parts) game for fans of the 3D Platformer genre.100%ed Hana's levels in about 3 hours, and it was a great time! The music absolutely bangs, especially Stage 3 & 4.Stage 4 Act 2 is anxiety incarnate if you're going for the S rank. (Not a bad thing though, and after 100%ing the rest of the game it became my favorite level!)Stage 6 Act 2 is the only level in the game I genuinely think is poorly designed. There's a point-of-no-return jump after a rail where you can miss cranes if you don't time the jump perfectly, which led to a few annoying resets on an otherwise easy level. There's also a part at the end which reminds me of a badly designed Mario Maker level where if you pick the wrong hoop you miss cranes (and can't go back) and have to reset, felt a bit cheap.Outside of those tiny blemishes in what is otherwise a really great 3D Platformer, the entire rest of the game is very solid. Judging it by what it is, an indie platformer, I'd lean towards saying it's one of the best ones I've played. Big recommend!Small edit: I'd personally recommend going into the Gameplay settings and turning off smooth turning (makes the game much more responsive, at least on controller) and turning the drop shadow on. I'm not sure why the latter isn't on by default, since it can help a lot if you're struggling with bouncy objects like balloons!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: There is just something about Lunistice's gameplay that is magical. The whole game just brims with the genuinity of the OG 3D platformers; the purpose-driven but goofy vibes, it brings joy even if you fail at a section. Some moments you feel like you're playing Croc on your Sega Saturn again.Oh yeah, also #LunisticeSweep
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a small scope throwback 3D platformer with gorgeous art direction. While short, running under 2 hours, the game introduces an impressive number of concepts in that time. Each stage is unique and focused.However, for me, Lunistice feels too Super Meat Boy to capture the essence of Sonic the Hedgehog. I really wished for more time spent doing relatively casual platforming, with challenging routes for faster times. Once you get past the second world there's very little margin for error. It seems backwards to me that the generation who grew up with these games are getting older, with little free time and poorer reflexes by the year, yet we're marketed games with a higher mechanical skill floor than the classics.All the same, this is a loving and heartfelt tribute to some great games - and it's easily worth checking out for $5. There's even a demo if you're on the fence.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Great platformer. Reminded me of the Dreamcast era, specifically Super Magentic Neo. Really fun and great tactical feel to the movement. The vibes are immaculate and the story was nicely understated but evocative, and leaves me interested in learning more. What happened before? What will happen after? Hopefully we'll see more in the series before too long!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun 3D Platformer. I honestly don't really have much else to say in regards to my simplified thoughts, I could go into the story but quite frankly I was enjoying the gameplay too much to take the time to see what was going on story wise, so... sorry about that. All I know is that the movement is good, the music is good, and the stages are good (even the ones that I had some troubles on). *I almost finished with this review without mentioning the graphics. They're good I guess, I don't really care too much about how a game looks as long as it's confident in its presentation. Also I don't really have much strong affinity towards the 32-bit era of games or their graphics. But I do feel that the game is confident in its presentation, so I think it looks good.I do have some very slight gripes but most of them are nit-picky. So for everything past this sentence until the line I would suggest anyone who hasn't played the game or even the demo yet not even worry about.For one, I wish the player could have more control over the smooth turning. Like being able to set smooth turning on/off for when you're in the air or for when you're on the ground, also different intensities of smooth turning. Another option which would be nice is being able to go into borderless window if that happens to be possible. Options wise that's about it. Like I could say something like: mappable controls, but you can just do that through steam so I really don't see much point in it. Characters and movement wise, I don't really have too much to say either. Although I do wish Toree maybe had it where after running at top speed for a few seconds created the flame barrier thing that does damage when riding on a rail (or stuff along those lines) so that you could plow through enemies while still not having a proper attack. Although I don't know how accurate that would be to the character's original games. And of all three of the characters I would say that Toukie was probably my least favorite their movement was a little odd to get used to at first and even when I did it never felt great all of the time. Their attack was also the same way for me, putting yourself in a position to get the most out of your attack took a little time to get used to, and I heavily suggest anyone using smooth turning to just not when using this character. It makes taking encounters with two enemies much easier and faster. Keep in mind that even with them being my least favorite they're still far from bad.For stages all of them were great, even though I had a hard time with Stage 4's gimmick at first (especially 4-2) they were all well made and fun. Although I found two stages in particular I'm a bit more iffy about, that being stages 5-2 and  which I feel ran a little too long which while fine casually, makes them not very enjoyable for completion since dying right at the end of a stage 5 to 6 minutes in in the case of 5-2 is a little infuriating since now you have to through all of that again and hope you don't mess it up again. This isn't as bad when it comes to getting all collectibles since checkpoints exist but it still is annoying at times.  On the subject of completion however, it's fine. Difficult enough to be a good challenge without feeling impossible. Making it where you don't have to get all collectible and no resets in a single run helps a lot with that and I'm really glad that the game doesn't make you do so. All of the achievements are good, although I found the one where you go through an entire stage breaking all of the crystals to be a little strange since it's the only instance where you're asked to do that and its not like you get anything for it outside of the achievement so it was just weird to me. Maybe its another inside joke or something idk. Generally unless you really care about full completion with achievements included I would recommend most players just get all S with Hana for the cool reward and enjoy playing through the game as the characters without bothering with getting S on everything.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Overall a very great game with some very specific things that I personally found some troubles with but I feel for anyone who's just looking for a good game to play especially a 3D platformer this is probably one of the best options out there, especially with how much of the game you can experience through the demo alone and how much more you get out of the surprisingly low price of admission. I would probably put it among my top 5 suggestions for people looking to play the genre. It's a solid 8.5/10 for me. Likely to go higher with the  fact that the devs are planning to release more content, which I cannot wait to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I tried out the demo for about 10 minutes, and that was all I needed to fall in love and purchase it. Honestly some of the most instant fun I've had playing a singleplayer game in awhile, enjoyed every second of it. Visually charming, controls well, soundtrack bops, level designs are super cute. Easy recommend at this price for anyone who loves platformers. Also should be Steam Deck verified, because it was perfect on there.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I only needed to play through the first two levels to know this game is absolutely charming and fun! And although its Steam Deck verification is listed as "unknown" it works great on it. The gameplay is fluid and the aesthetic is very Sega Saturn-esque, I love it!Update: 12/3/2022: After clearing quite a bit more of the game, I'm even more confident in my recommendation of this game. Also, I absolutely LOVE the visuals of the final stages.💜
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic game, especially for the price. Having followed the game ever since the first public demos came out, I can say it's been an amazing ride watching this quick 30-day project become something so much bigger.Between the really charming use of the early 3D console platformer style, the really fun and fluid gameplay, the fantastic soundtrack and the great replayability, I can definitely give Lunistice a huge recommendation for anyone looking for a really great platformer to sink their teeth into.(Also it has a tanuki, how can you go wrong with that?)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fantastic 3D platformer taking it's inspirations from early 3D platformers such as sonic adventures but with a refined gameplay that make it a more welcoming experience for peoples who din't mastered 3D platformer yet.visually it's look like a Sega Saturn game with maybe a bit more details , it's nice , the controls respond well and the checkpoints are well placed , there is replayability as the game seem to have a true ending and there you can play to try to get the best score possible in each level too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Goodness, what an absolute treat this game is! Played through the entirety of just Hana's story, took about 4 hours, including all collectibles (but not all S ranks). Will definitely be going back to play as the other two characters in full to round off the game in the future.It's rare to play a game that just feels so , so absolutely tight and focused, like a person wrote out their specification, picked up their tools and set to work, and not only crafted exactly what they had outlined, but that what they ended up with translated so unbelievably well from paper to product. There's not a foot out of step, every aspect of the game feeling so carefully considered and constructed, a really impressive passion project! The core of the experience truly has to be the incredibly tight control system, Hana feeling like an absolute dream to control from the moment you start playing, and only feeling better and better as you master the tiny intricacies of the system; I find myself not playing a lot of 3D platformers, and I've no idea why that is, but  instantly hooked me with its great movement and sensible controls (if putting Jump on one of your shoulder buttons becomes an industry norm, I will be  pleased).Each world beyond the first one introduces some new mechanic which changes the way you interact with the levels, but crucially, your core set of skills remains the same throughout, which results in a really nice organic increase in challenge as you go through - a particular favourite of mine is the dessert-themed world which uses music and rhythm for environmental challenge - it might lack the sort of replayability that comes with taking new skills back to old stages like an  or  but it makes for a compelling first-time run (and, additionally, there are other characters who bring that sort of challenge if you like, which I think is a nice way to diversify the game!) With each new world comes a new theme, both visual and musical, and I'd like to highlight the soundtrack in this regard; nicely crafted tunes for each world and, really, just a wonderful soundtrack all over! I love the different visual styles of all the worlds and, in general, the game, too - it's clearly meant to be played on a CRT, but there's a filter for that if you need it - an appropriately dream-like landscape with random elements jutting out of the clouds, it's really beautiful, and really capitalises on both the limitations of a small development team and captures the spirit of the era of games it tries to evoke.There's a nice little bit of narrative going on, which is dished out to you as a reward for exploring the levels fully and finding all the collectibles; its a nice incentive to dig through the game proper if the intrinsic satisfaction of fully exploring the levels didn't work for you, and I have to say, there's some really interesting ludonarrative stuff going on that I don't want to spoil. I'd say run through without worrying about collectibles, then go back through and go for 100% for maximum satisfaction.Honestly, this might be a boring review, I just can barely think of any criticisms of this game - Hana's footstep sounds get a bit annoying, there you go - it's just been an absolute delight to play through. This is a proper little bitesize treat of a game and I can't wait to see more from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely incredible. I was having such a bad day, and I picked up this game after browsing Steam. I had already been kinda interested in Sonic-likes, but I'm really bad at platformers so I thought this would be frustrating.Not the case! This game doesn't exactly hold your hand, but it's so fluid and controls so well that I feel amazing speeding through the stages. The story is also incredibly interesting, though I wish we got a bit more at the end; I still have so many questions. But it does its job of making you want to keep playing and playing so that you can reach the end and get as much info as possible.I could go on and on, but I'll keep it at this: for the price tag, this game is incredibly worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a nice 3D platformer with a retro art style, I got lots of nostalgia for other titles in the genre from the level designs and colour pallets (Sonic Adventure, Banjo, etc.).  Not a lot for me to say other than Lunistice is a short, well rounded game, and is easy for me to recommend to anyone who likes games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice takes heavy inspiration from Sonic the Hedgehog, and other influences from Crash Bandicoot, Donkey Kong, and Mario. The character you start with is pretty fun to control and the opening levels are great, but it doesn't last.The game is split up into worlds with two levels each. In a sense, the first world teaches you to crawl, world 2 teaches you to walk, world 3 teaches you to run, but then world 4 pushes you out of the nest and expects you to fly. Yes, the difficulty spike of world 4 is mountainous. If you remember Beep Block Skyway from Super Mario 3D World (and I know you do ), this game borrows the disappearing platforms timed to the beat of the music, but makes them phenomenally more frustrating. You would think that your ability to double-jump and hover would make it easy to deal with these platforms, but you are wrong. They switch too fast and your character falls too slowly. Eventually you run into a stretch that requires speedrunner-esque perfection. It feels as though they ran out of fun ideas at this point and resorted to making troll levels. This is where I quit, sadly. To the game's credit, it is very well put together. It looks great, sounds great, and the controls are great (I love using the shoulder buttons to jump and attack). It doesn't have lives, stupid cutscenes, cringey voices, or long loading screens. However, the difficulty will wreck anyone but the thickest of brick wall head-slammers. If you're reading this and didn't have any problems with world 4, congraturations. You're winner. I simply do not have the right neurological state to keep playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fun short little platformer. It does have a story, but most of that it told through notes as well as the game's intro. Other than that, you play a character by the name of Hana and go through a set of levels that are based off her memories. Complete with fun music to listen to, and a few tight platforming sequences.Where the game shines is obviously the platforming.  The game has a lot of room to find skips and everything else, while still moving pretty fast despite Hana's movement speed not being the fastest out there, she's still decently quick. For speedy boys out there some of the skips are a lot of fun too. My personal favorite to do runs of is 6-1.The music itself is also incredibly good. A lot of fun to listen to. If you can buy the soundtrack off the composer on bandcamp: . Or buy it on Steam, either or works.In the end, this game is a steal at $5. A solid experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is totally delightful, and I feel like I'm robbing the devs by only paying 5 dollars for this much fun. Granted it's pretty short. Absolutely oozes style and whimsy, the visual style of the levels reminds me slightly of genesis-era sonic without feeling derivative and the music is absolutely catchy. Controls are airtight and smooth, jumps only occasionally felt frustrating due to small depth-perception issues but nothing that actually takes away from enjoyment of the game. The character snaps wonderfully to 99% of the wonkier, tilted platforms and the game as a whole really lets you cut loose and just soar through levels. My only real complaint (read: Nitpick) is the ranking system. While you're ranked for overall performance at the end of each level, this doesn't seem to be tracked anywhere, while your best-of for collectibles and deaths are tracked, but separately. So S-ranking stages can come from 2 separate, fairly easy runs, especially since time isn't considered for ranks anyways (though it is tracked, which is still wonderful). I think a slightly robust ranking system would REALLY go a long way to making this game so much more replayable, but otherwise this game is pretty much perfect, especially for the criminally low pricepoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Right from the getgo you can tell that this game is a love letter to PlayStation 1 inspired games. The colourful graphics and creative level design mixed with the guest appearances of Toree and Toukie make for a wonderful and well paced formula that can give you hours of joy to sink your teeth into. With the new Accel Coda DLC releasing for FREE in the future, this is a must play!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game. The game does run into a few snags near the end when it comes to 100% completion it's still an incredibly fun game.The whole point of the game is that you run and jump through a series of levels. You're free to get some collectibles along the way if you want to get the true ending, but really there's nothing that outright forces you to get them if you don't want to which is nice. Though it does lead to the game feeling a little hollow if you go that route. As far as total playtime the main campaign will last you about 3 hours even going for everything. But then you'll unlock two new characters to the roster which can extend playtime since they also have their own 100% completion rating.Moving away from the gameplay I wanna talk about the OST and the graphics. The OST is wonderful and never misses a beat in my opinion. It's wonderful to listen to all day long. And as far as the graphics my god they're wonderful, possibly the best part of the game. It truly feels like a Sega Saturn game plucked straight out of that era.Buy this game. Buy it twice even. It's such a good game that's also only $5 which is criminally undervalued.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: + Gorgeous presentation (art style, colour palette, character design & UI)+ Fun, varied level themes+ Great OST+ Multiple characters each with their own small twists on the gameplay+ Extremely fluid & satisfying controls (once smooth turning is disabled in the options)+ No hamfisted bossfights+ Good length+ Jump being bound to the right bumper by default- Cranes can be easy to miss in some areas with a lot of visual noise- Baubles being multicoloured inevitably leads to some blending in with the environment- Big jump arc out of transportation bubbles feels tedious- Some collectable layouts break flow- No way to backtrack on grind rails (not a big issue but came up atleast twice for me)- Platforming difficulty a bit too easy in general- Smooth Turning being ON by defaultIn regards to the smooth turning, I think the game should explain both options to the player before it starts & make them choose, or atleast have it off by default. Having it on feels pretty bad compared to having it off & I feel like most players won't bother looking through the options so they'll go through the entire game not knowing a better control option is available. Overall I really enjoyed it. Played through the whole thing in one sitting, getting S ranks with all 3 characters. I highly recommend it to 3D platformer enjoyers (especially Toree fans).
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Controls really well, level design is generally excellent, looks good, sounds good. Other players have already sung Lunistice's praises more eloquently than I ever could.The one caveat i haven't seen addressed by other reviewers would be that the game marries 3D Sonic-style "go fast and platform accurately" stage design with collectathon game design, which doesn't always work in the game's favor I believe. I enjoyed Lunistice the most when I was just moving smoothly from section to section, but the crane tracker means you're always conscious of leaving them behind, which tended to slow me down and shift my focus towards "collect everything" as opposed to "whooo, go fast!". The goals feel diametrically opposed and I almost feel like there's two games here: one where you just zip through the levels in a few minutes and one where you scrape each stage for 12-15 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game that harkens back to the platformers of the past with a bit of a twist. The feeling of speed mixed with platforming can feel so good at times. The soundtrack is very catchy and the controls are great. The game is not without its faults. Mainly the camera movement. This has been pretty much fixed with the updates released. Also while the extra stuff you get after completing the game is very nice, one did annoy me for being a huge area and it wasting lots of time if you're trying to get an S and you mess up once, having to try again.  Still though, get the game if you're a fan of platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute platformer, with somewhat fast movement and flows well, for the most part. I've S Ranked all characters and done almost all achievements in about 7 hours, and had fun during 90% of it.There's however just two hiccups: the final Hana stage, Infinite, which requires absurdly precise jumps for how long the stage takes. So if you're going to S Rank everything, this stage is going to murder you. A LOT.And getting to the "bonus content" (which is unfortunately very minor as it is just 2 stages) requires you to replay through the entirety of the game TWICE. A bit of a shame as it just felt like padding all over to get a bit more time into the game, which dampered the fun when I finally got to the good part.Other than that, it's definitely fun to play. Go and try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid little 3d platformer game with cute graphics and a compelling soundtrack.The movement isn't particularly deep, but it satisfies for a dozen hours of platforming and collecting. This type of game is hard to come by nowadays, so if youre interested in the genre at all, its worth a purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fast paced platformer with a retro vibe that hits the spot juuuuust right for me. It has somewhat of a Sonic vibe in the gameplay if you ask me, or at least what Sonic could be if done right. You can play the level with speedrun or scoring in mind, eitheir by goind darude sandstorm on the level and getting to the end as quickly as you can OR you can choose the collectathon-enthousiast way and take your time to collect all the cranes and other things in the level by going a bit off road. If you're looking for a shot of nostalgia and simple yet refreshing level design no doubt you'll find it here. If you're not sure about the game I strongly encourage you to try the free demo for yourself; and heck the game is 5 bucks in my book it's pratictally free for this quality content.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent and excels in what it's goal is. Simple 3D platformer with lots of great platform design. If you are tired of grinding in a game for 40 hours to feel satisfied and just want something to pick up and play, then this is it. To the creator(s) of this game, thank you very much for the fun! Can't wait to see what you come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: First of: Dont let my play time fool you, i played it on Switch first and bought it again becouse i liked it :3If you love the 3D Platform Games from a time that were better (in your mind) its a solid game for you. It made by one Person from the ground in round about a year. So if you want to have a good platformer and support a indie devs first commercial release, its the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game! ...but it can be a little cumbersome if you are trying to get S ranks on all the levels. Love the way the platforming feels, and how much you can get out of the relatively simple mechanics. This kind of feels like a mix of 3d and 2d Sonic, if that makes any sense. From what I have seen so far, the level design is really good, and generally leads you to where you need to go extremely well.However, there are a few problems that kind of hinder the game for me. The levels can be quite cumbersome to S rank, for one. The levels can take minutes to finish, which would be fine if falling off the edge at any point didn't mean losing your ability to S rank. Doing a level near perfectly only to fail a tricky jump at the end REALLY takes its toll and makes me put the game down after a few times. The other main issue I hold is that it can be tricky to know where the cranes are that you missed. Again, these are minutes long levels, and getting to the end only to find you've missed one single crane is.. not a super fun experience.That being said, if you don't need to S rank every level to enjoy a game, it's fantastic! And even if you DO need to S rank every level to enjoy a game, it is still really good! It can just be a little cumbersome sometimes. Still a great game though.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I was convinced to buy it based on the demo. And yeah.Played through once so far. IAlthough I have gotten all the "Unlock Final Level" collectables, I am going to be doing so, and motivated enough to try S-Ranking the stages as well.This is an engaging little game with what i can only describe as a banging OST, interesting and cute visuals but most importantly:I think the actual gameplay is just, super-super smooth, and its worth playing for that alone.It's not particularly long but it is one of those games you'll want to just come back to in a few years to replay, and for £5 that's a pretty decent deal.The additional playable characters look like they'll extend replay value.Cute, cosy little game, recommended.Update: Having now beaten the game and on the way to 100% completion, still maintains its recommendation. The final stage is a bit weird though.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very little experience with 3d platforming games, but this made me crave more. the game is simple, it's fun, it's fast paced and controls very, very well (once you turn off smooth turning in the settings). Oh, and the music is really good too c: The only real critique I have of the game is that the difficulty curve was a little strange, there is one level in particular that was like four times as hard as any of the other levels, and I died a LOT while trying to get double S rank on it. _childDocuments_.review: Glorious freedom of movement!This is a simple platformer/collectathon that I consider worth every penny. _childDocuments_.review: A very nice and relatively short 3D platformer that reminds me of early 3D platformers on the N64, Playstation, etc, but for good reasons. _childDocuments_.review: Fun 3d plataformer, the moveset feels hella good to control and master.Levels are nice to explore aswell as they are moderately challenging.Soundtrack is a blast, and make every level feel unique in its own way.Overall a short game with replayability mostly being "get all X" + a few other thingsbut for its price I think its worth checking it out

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fun platformer that waves the flag for nineties retro-styling; it stays comfortably in its lane just long enough to wring all of the possible enjoyment out of  a simple formula before it can become repetitive. With intentionally blocky visuals but surprisingly crisp controls, Lunistice is an enjoyable experience that doesn’t set out to do too much, and in doing so achieves an awful lot. Despite some issues with depth perception, I had a good time with Lunistice while it lasted, and perfectionists and speedrunners will get more from this Sonic Adventure 2 X Sega Saturn-inspired runner than perhaps they expected.Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10Lunistice was an interesting game for me, as while I am not the biggest fan of platformer, and the focus of this platform game was to be a nostalgia trip for ps1 style platformer games, I still found a ton of enjoyment from this game than I thought I would. While it does have the flaws that I normally dislike from some platformers like lack of technical movement and momentum lack, The story was a surprising but tiny positive for me.StoryThe most you get for the story of this game will be the beginning voiced cutscene when you boot the game, and then the rest of the story is only if you get the secret notes and finish the true ending, where it talks about a cycle formed by an organization, and with letters sent by the main character to their parents as they go through the experiment of destroying the moon. However destroying the moon only causes the game to loop, but the glitches it causes is how the notes were formed to begin with due to being a glitch in the system, and with those notes is how you are able to finally break the cycle and become free. While the story is basically 5-10 minutes worth of content in this game, it was still pretty well done and I applaud the dev for that.GameplayIt has the mix of a sonic game but with the movements of Super Mario Galaxy, and while I did enjoy it overall, I really did wish there were more technical movements as it did become a bit stale due to lack of progression with how good I got with the movement. The level designs in the later levels were really good, but replaying them was not that interesting due to the linear design apart from 1 level in the game. Turning off smooth turning made the movement much much better though, as it removes that slow turn around speed and makes the game feel much snappier. In the end though it was a bit too easy for my liking, but the deaths were punishing depending on what checkpoint you last got, which would only really set you back at most a minute or 2. If there ever was a sequel, I think an additional movement option that allows for more freedom in movement and expression would go a long way, even though I didn't play the other 2 characters in the game.MusicPretty good overall. I do think there was some issue with repeating songs, or especially songs that sounded too similar, cause it would get repetitive as the game went on. The music rhythm and the last level were highlights easily for me, and I did enjoy the main theme that played throughout the game, but I did feel tiring of the music as I went on and on, and eventually did play youtube songs in the background when I was replaying the game, but for an indie dev it was really good still.ConclusionThis game is easily worth the buy, as with all the issues I have with the game, it only costs $5 which is a STEAL for the content and enjoyment you get from the game. I don't think personally that it is one of my favorite platformers, and there are others that do better in certain aspects of this game, but I still think it is worth picking up this game especially if you like old school 3d platformers.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This 5€ treat has no right to be one of the best games I've played this year, yet it is.The OST is chill and fits the vibe of the game; it has that wonderful PS1 nostalgic look; the environments look great and the characters are adorable; the level design makes the most out of the simple move-set you are given and the main course, as it should be, is the gameplay: The gameplay is some of the smoothest platforming I've experienced, probably the best since I first played Celeste back in 2018. You can tell it was made with love and care, and that the developers tested the hell out of it because Hana, Toree and Toukie feel wonderful to control in every single level. I feel like I could have fun just moving around in an empty room with how satisfying everything is. It feels like what you remember old platformers playing like, meaning all the good bits without the jankiness behind them. I'm beyond impressed.My only "complaint" is that I finished the game with all 3 characters and got all the achievements in about an afternoon's time, but that's absolutely okay because, once again, it only costs 5€. FIVE EURO.It's a gem, one I hope doesn't stay hidden, and it's absolutely worth your money.I hope this isn't the last we see of Lunistice 'cause I could keep eating this gameplay by the spoonful!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: As far as precision platformers go, Lunistice does things very well, it's cute and feature nice retro graphics, movement is enjoyable and precise, like, the simple fact that you can do a spin attack and a double jump in any order makes everything very fluid ! I liked the music too !Really fun if you're into that kind of things, and on top of that, it's cheap, give it a go :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: So, going off what I have learnt from inside the game only, this game was made by a twitch streamer with help from several other people, & the goal originally was to make a game in about 30 days, but then decided to continue improving and adding to it.I didn't realise this when I bought it, my brain was just like Now that I'm aware of this, I have a much better idea of what I think of the game.I... don't like this game.That's not to say it's bad! considering the development of the game and its pricing, I would bet many people would be happy enough with the quality they are getting from this game, just not me.Minor spoilers, & I'll cover the parts I consider big spoilers.So, brief overview:This is a retro-style 3D platformer where you play as some tanuki named Hana. You go though many differently styled levels, with 2 stages each, and attempt to collect paper cranes, avoid weird creatures & get to the end, in order to get a higher score. The game is fairly quick to complete, taking me 2.5 hours to get through.The level designs are very cutesy & retro-looking, though can appear very scrambled if you look at certain sections of them, which may lead to some people getting lost or confused. With how fast-paced the game can be at times however, you may not notice this as much.The platforming, depending on the stage, can be very fun & unique. As you enter different level designs, more small mechanics are introduced, like beach balls to bounce on, or geysers that shoot you across the map. Despite appearing unimportant, they help diversify the stages, giving players more to focus on & preventing them from tiring from the game.One of the best things I think the game introduces is mechanics that change the entire rhythm of the platforming.However, this game does not keep up this diversity and begins to become somewhat repetitive.For one, you will only ever see 4 types of enemies on all the stages. They will be the only other obstacle in your way, other than the platforming. They do not change the way they move or interact with the environment in any way.I would've liked to have seen some change in what I faced as I was platforming to give me a bit more of a challenge as I went on, though I did not see this.Two, many types of platforming mechanics are reused (which is understandable & OK if implemented right), such as the grinding on rails mechanic, speed up runway, or random purple boosters.This is an issue, as most stages are provided only a couple additional mechanics to make up for this reuse. leading to them suffering from repetition. Additionally, these assets may not fit the design/feel of the stage. Random purple boosters in the sky can be odd to look at & use in any level.You play as the character in 3rd person, with a camera that has the vertical axis partially locked. Immediately this is annoying, as it can be hard to identify where you're going if you are going up a vertical climb.This can be fixed (slightly) in the camera options by turning off the vertical lock setting, though you are still partially restricted from looking up, but not so much when looking down.You have the ability to attack, jump twice, & attack in the air to gain a small amount of height. Other than that... you can hit a button to walk slowly. This works completely fine with how the platforming levels are designed, I never had a single issue with these mechanics when used in the game's levels.You have 3 hit bars, which go down when hit by the enemies or some world hazards. I believe this is unnecessarily big, as the enemies you face are not strong enough to be able to hit you 3 times before you defeat them. I've only ever died once from losing health this way. Implementing a way to reduce ( or maybe even increase) this would've been a nice addition.When you lose all your health, you restart at these gateways that act as respawn points throughout the stage. you don't run out of lives, but you do lose your score at the end of the stage. I would say that this is for the best. I would probably lose my mind if I only had, like, 5 lives.I would describe the music as upbeat & dreamy, which slowly becomes more action-packed as you go up the levels. I would consider the music one of the game's biggest strong suits, each piece of music fits its stage perfectly. It complements what the game is trying to achieve very well.Big spoiler ahead, be warned.So... why do I recommend this game?Well, this isn't EA, It's a very small group of indie creators who work an additional job. All of what I have criticized, although relevant (according to me), is expected from the group type that made it. They should be proud of what they have created & have encouragement & help to be able to continue making new & improved games.Ok, out of text. Thanks for reading all my bullsh-

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little platformer. Some of the S ranks were rough, but there was a huge difficulty spike in 4-2. Worlds 1, 2, and 3 had their moments, but nothing like world 4. _childDocuments_.review: Absolute sweetheart of a game. Adorable main character, excellent leveraging of crunchy PS1-ish graphics, superb level design, atmosphere, soundtrack...everything about Lunistice just oozes charm and personality and is executed with mastery and grace. The platforming is mega smooth, speed and momentum feel clean and very much in-control, no issues whatsoever with the camera - this is a title that modern 3D Sonic installments could seriously take a few fundamental lessons from.There's a secret ending you can unlock by nabbing a handful of collectibles in each stage (check a guide for details), and it's worth doing that anyway, because the alternate paths they're located on are immaculately designed, really fun to traverse, and pretty simple to spot while you're cruising by. I fully played through the game twice in a row, once just casually finishing levels and enjoying the ride, and then again to hunt for collectibles and play the secret final stage. Both approaches were entirely enjoyable; choose whatever works for you.Lunistice is super cheap, it's like 2 hours long, it's an absolute darling, buy this game and enjoy it on a cozy Friday night in.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that since I own it I don't know what to think about it. At least now it should be easy for me to write some words about the game.Lunistice is a platformer that I hadn't played in a long time. It is something different from platformers I have come to know, play, love and hate. Its visuals quickly imprint themselves in the mind and the very simple gameplay knows how to motivate through the collectible cranes, letters and other items. At least I always felt good only when I had everything at 100%.It falls into the "easy to learn, hard to master" category of a game that, with its simple gameplay, nevertheless demands maximum focus from the player and I often failed to complete a level 100% due to unfocused moments.The only thing I have to criticize are a few things: The camera made it difficult for me to assess where my character actually was even with the drop shadow, the disappearing platforms in the moon levels disappear much earlier while you can still stay on them for about half a second, and the acceleration and weighty movement often invites frustration.All in all, though, a nice little game that I just put almost 7 hours into...More than Singularity which wanted to be more ambitious. _childDocuments_.review: Having 100% completion on this game, I have to say it really is excellent, especially for the price. The music is excellent, all characters feel unique, not much to complain about. If story is your thing, however, this game doesn't have much of it in its current state. That isnt to say there is none at all, but what little there is is presented through an opening and closing cutscene, and a page of lore per world you complete.If i had to give criticism, during repeat playthroughs on other characters, the bonus levels can feel tedious to reach as you're just replaying the the original levels with a slightly different moveset. However, each bonus level has something great to offer. Toree's bonus level takes full advantage of his mobility, and Toukee's bonus level is a sprawling level with a non-linear element that had only been explored to a much lesser extent previously. These are both excellent levels, but it feels like Toukee's level is almost wasted on being a bonus level that requires a repeat playthrough, as it is by far the most impressive in the game in scale (and arguably visuals). I would absolutely recommend this game for the price and for the quality, and look forward to seeing what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good but it's not great. There's a lot of competency on display here and the influence from both modern Sonic The Hedgehog and Super Mario Galaxy are on full display but there's still a little something lacking. There's a lack of boss fights, the musical level has super strict timing, I never really felt 100% in control of my character (until I tried the bonus characters who clicked with me more) and there's just the air of a game that's 90% of the way there. The camera sometimes gave me issues, it never spun as fast as I wanted it to and doesn't allow you to rotate it up or down very much so the times I wanted a good look at the scenery I got very little. There's a narrative here but I kind of checked out, the storytelling is very exposition heavy and I think here the rule of "show, don't tell" has been thrown by the wayside a lot. Going for 100% is also very annoying.That said, the music and visuals are gorgeous. Zero duds on a stellar soundtrack, truly excellent, and visually it all pops. The creativity within the level design displays a mind who understands what makes a good 3D platformer and there's just a lot of very neat touches. I especially enjoyed the rail grinding sections. Adding a secondary mapping to for jump and attack to the shoulder buttons of the controller was to me when I knew this game was special because I saw the developer understand that you can move and use the camera simultaneously when you don't have to use the face buttons, chef's kiss.This review has me listing a lot of negatives but only because the flaws are glaring in the face of the massive amounts of competence on display. I want another one, but give me some bosses, give me a couple more enemy types, tighten the movement and camera up a bit. It scratched an itch for me and left me wanting more. It's a fun game... But it is also a compromised one.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a great little 3D platformer. The art style perfectly captures the feeling of ps1 games while improving on how games actually looked like on the original playstation. At first the controls felt a little off and I had some difficulties landing on small platforms, but I got used to the crontrols and achieved a great amout of precision after not to long. This combined with a solid difficulty curve ment that I never had too many problems crusing through the levels and everything felt just hard enough. After replaying the game I realised how much better I became over the course of the first playthough by how easy the early levels suddenly felt.The game is not very long, but thanks to it's low price I think you're already getting your money's worth after the first playthrough, especially if you try to S rank every stage.But after finishing the game for the first time you unlock two more characters to play with. Each of which has a bonus stage aswell. These characters have unique enough playstyles that I had a lot of fun playing through the entire game with them as well. The additional jumps of the bird made me aproach levels in a different way and not being able to attack combined with only having 1hp made playing with the duckling a nice challenge.There where only a few small sections of the game that I didn't like,(edit: all of them have been changed for the better in a recent patch :P) most of the time I had a blast. So I would say for the small price of 5€ this is a no-brainer if you are looking for a 3D platformer. Big thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice demonstrates such a keen awareness of the full history of its genre and aesthetic that I think I have to acknowledge it as the most technically competent 3D platformer ever made. It calls its shot and then hits it dead center 17 times in a row. It is an absolute joy to play in every way that you can play a platformer: casual exploration, focused collectathon, technical speedrun gauntlet. And Toree is in it!The difficulty is refreshing but surmountable. The physics are crisp and tight. The camera is responsive and predictable and tasteful. The level designs are simple but striking and creative. The lore is a little cheesy but still fun. Almost every technical detail has been polished to a mirror shine---I found exactly one bug (pausing desyncs the audio in 5-2) and it is at worst a minor annoyance. The asking price is about four times smaller than what I would expect, and eight times smaller than I would be willing to pay. If you have liked any 3D platformer ever made, you'll probably find something to like in Lunistice.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is an indie 3D platformer with mostly linear stages, very refined game design, very tight controls, a respectable amount of replayability, and a pleasing low-poly aesthetic. I highly recommend it, it's entirely worth the 5$ asking price. Full Review Below.In Lunistice, you play as a tanuki named Hana, traveling through stages in a world of dreams (or something like that).Hana moves with the complete 360° of the analog movement both on the ground and in the air. She can jump, double jump, and perform a spinning attack. She can also spin attack once after leaving the ground, either after or during jumps. Spinning at the same time as starting one of her jumps makes you perform an extra high jump. This is best used in mid-air with her double jump, generally, but in truth, there's a sort of proportion to how the jump arc works based on the amount of time between the jump, her direction and velocity that results, and when you execute your spin. Spinning and jumping at the same time will maximize immediate height in the jump. However, spinning in mid air further out from the last jump will typically just slow Hana's fall slightly, allowing you to gain a bit more distance sometimes, or give you some hang time to move above a platform while in the air. The full 360° analog movement and complex air movement are the bread and butter of this game's mechanics, and make controlling Hana an absolute blast, and it opens the levels up to some very creative shortcuts.Every stage has two acts, and in each act you have 3 main objectives. Firstly, you can collect all of the floating Origami Cranes, of which there is usually 100 or more of. Second, you want to beat the stage with as few deaths/resets as possible. At the end of a level, you are given a rank on both of those based on how well you did, which are averaged together to give you a rank for the level overall. S being the best, and D being the worst. If you want S ranks, you need all of the cranes and 0 deaths. That's right, you'd better get good. Luckily, for the not yet so good, every act has plenty of checkpoints and you can pause and return to the last one you touched anytime you want. Lastly, in every act there's also 4 letters you can find that spell out "HANA", found on hidden or slightly out of the way paths. After collecting them, an extra section at the end of the level beyond the goal area will appear, allowing you to collect either a Key in Act 1 or a Note in Act 2. Doing this is not part of your rank, but completing these does offer some insight into the game's plot in the form of readable email logs.In addition, every stage tracks your best completion time, meaning- for replayability, you can challenge yourself to beating your own best times, something every Sonic fan probably is familiar with. Also, on replayability, the game also features two additional playable characters, each with quirks and unique mechanics, I won't go into details here, but this is another boon for repeat playthroughs.Moving on from gameplay, Lunistice deliberately has a very low poly, low resolution look- emulating something you'd expect from a Sega Saturn, PlayStation, or Nintendo DS. Unlike those systems, however, it targets widescreen at a rock solid 60FPS, even on the Nintendo Switch port, and this buttery smooth framerate contributes a lot to game feel here. It also has a pretty solid, albeit, not super memorable soundtrack. I wouldn't call it a weak point exactly, on the contrary in fact, it fits the game very well- I just don't think I'll be listening to any of these tracks outside of the game. So, musically, it's pretty good, but not outstanding. The game does have a story- but I've been deliberately not talking about it. It's very minimal, and it's best left unspoiled I feel.Overall, I love Lunistice. The game is fast paced, mechanically rock solid, and incredibly fun. As a veteran to 3D platformers in general, I can definitely see influences of a multitude of other mascot platforming games in this game's design, but this exact blend isn't something I've ever quite experienced before, and it really leaves quite an impression. I really hope to see more 3D platformers from this developer in the future, and I'll no doubt be revisiting this game many times. Both on PC and on Nintendo Switch.I can't recommend it enough, it's absolutely worth the full asking price of 5$. Frankly, it's so good, it could cost twice or even thrice that and it would still be getting a glowing recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: about 12h but it is heavily dependent on skill level 6/10 3, but with 3 different characters that play a little different Not really, but on the steam forum you can find info about a lot of achievements and  No No No No No No No No difficulty option NoLunistice is an awesome platformer. It isn't a cakewalk, it is a very challenging game and the achievements make it even more challenging. It has the looks of games around the Nintendo64/PlayStation 1 era. Back then I couldn't appreciate the art style that much, I mostly remember frustration with it but looking back now it gives a feeling of nostalgia. It took a bit of time to get a feeling of how far and high the main character jumped, and it can be made a bit easier by turning "shadow on" in the settings to see a clear circle on the area under you to know when you're at when in the air. Also the "slow walk" took some practice and mostly was learning just very gently pushing my thumbstick forward. After learning that I enjoyed the game a lot. It all works fine, it looks nice, what do you want more from a platformer? I wasn't able to complete the game myself because in later levels (starting from world 3) the game had a lot of "on rails" sections and those gave me quite some motion sickness. I tried to play more levels by taking breaks in between, I wanted to keep playing because I had a lot of fun, but I found myself struggling because I just felt sick. I don't have much motion sickness, but this is one of the few that triggered it for me, which felt weird as it hasn't the first-person view. For the time to 100% this game I mostly looked at tracking websites how long others needed to complete the game. The game has achievements for getting an S rank on every level, for this, you have to find all the collectibles and to have not died while playing through that level. What is very nice is that you don't have to do those 2 things in the same run, so you can first try to get all the collectibles and then try to get through the level without dying. You need to do this with all 3 characters if you want to 100% the game. There are a few other achievements for which you need to do something specific on a specific level, most of those you'll be able to do without even looking up what to do. I would recommend combining finding all collectibles and destroying all crystals on level 3-1, as for both you'll have to go to each area in that specific level.
