_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice is a fast paced 3d Platformer which is simple on the surface but does everything all around really well,The stages all introduce a new gimmick which makes them feel unique from each other  and follow a general difficulty curve that might not be easy to get into for beginners, but it does never feel like it gets too impossibly hard.with an average length of about 3-4 hours for the 100% ending it might not seem like a lot, but the game offers tons of replayability in the form of achieving S ranks,additional characters and speedrunning.The soundtrack produced by Knasibas is perfectly fitting for the game and deserves it's own attention from an already really good game.10/10 would recommend spinning tanukis again
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Also im just a nerd I never write reviews unless I really like the game and Lunistice hitLunstice was first showcased as a 30-day Unity project for SAGE '21 as EVERSLEEP: LunisticeGaiden, for those who may not know the name, SAGE is an online game exhibition event with a focus on Sonic-style games, but that lately has also shown many incredible gems that attempt to replicate substance rather than merely gameplay or art-direction.Earlier this year the Demo was released, and 3 days ago the full game came out. My review is solely of the full game, as I bought it during its launch sale, which also coincides with the time I first learned of it (learning a bit of a games history never hurts though, does it?)Alright so, the sonic “substance” is somewhat renowned, Fast gameplay, cute animal characters and BANGER music. Lunistice delivers in each an every one of these points (god Hana is so CUTE.)The gameplay of Lunistice itself itself harkens back to the games from the Dreamcast and PSX platforms, but with a shakeup of introducing more focus on collectathon aspects whilst retaining the straightforward level design, of particular note  is that the game has an alternative path (imagine the secret paths of the early crash bandicoot games) that you can take at no cost aside from encountering it in-game and generally is more difficult  than the main path with the reward of a special collectible and more cranes (the main item you pick up). Level format is 7 Stages split in different parts, generally 2, the levels are generally long, taking up to 10 minutes in some cases of later worlds, however checkpoints are very generous and are given before any part that requires more concentration or precision from the player. The stages themselves allow you to “sink” into the gameplay loop, with very easy to understand Although I found some sections that were a bit unfair, the game did provide a shadow option to ease some of the jumping challenges, and the 1.02 update now includes an alternate physics option that is more similar to the SAGE ‘21 demo.Here is where I say some of the stages had some pretty annoying sections with precision platforming, particularly Stage 4 where I constantly tripped with the temp, although that may be more because of muscle memory from another game with the same mechanic, there were also some choices such as rails dropping you into bottomless pits with a very tight window to jump off from (not helped by the camera) and some platforms being surprisingly tight with the leeway they give you to jump to and off them later on the game.Scoring is based on how many Cranes you collected and how many deaths you had in a stage, with time not being graded or recorded, but shown at the end of a stage alongside a final grade, I am not sure if time does affect the score, but the level design very much shows potential for speedrunning, and its not gonna surprise me if categories for 100% collectibles, fastest time or more show up.Combat however is a simple one button affair with one-hit enemies that come in three varieties (plus some breakables) but the big deal of this move is that it serves as a jump extender that can be performed before or after a second jump, the game plays quite a bit with the mix-and match nature of Hana’s move-set through the stages.Graphics and Sound wise, the game has an aesthetic similar to what you would find in a Y2K but with more modern sensibilities, in my opinion I would call it a “modern anime from a 90’s series”, Graphics are generally pixel-art and with low-poly models, definitely retro! The music is also incredible, composed by Knasibas, who definitely knocked the ball out of the park with the OST, matching each stage perfectly and hyping you to go through each stage. Story wise, I will be honest and say I am mad that it’s so INTERESTING yet put to the wayside as secrets, while It works fine as is, the only cut-scenes are at the start and end of the game, and only one of the three is voiced! (although the performance is very good!). While I know that the story is not the main focus, I definitely would love to see more exploration of the events and aftermath of the story after this, like seriously I would buy a comic or anthology or something of the sort. And yes, I did not clarify anything about said story, It’s better off that you simply read the store description and go in blind. Trust me.Honestly this game is illegally good for its price, Short, but with such an effort put into it that it would put many, more expensive games to shame, regardless of price its a must buy if you love speedy platformers with high replayability, and if you enjoy mysterious stories you might enjoy this one (and again please make more in this setting, absolutely ripe for potential!!)-revoblam.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and high quality platformer. Gameplay is fun and fluent, deaths usually feel like it's your own fault and the game looks gorgeous. _childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be relaxing, fast paced, atmospheric and challanging all in one, depending on what kind of way you choose to play. That is pretty great In my opinion.For example: after finishing the main story I chose to go for 100%, which invites you to paly play in a much more slow and careful style as it involves finishing stages deathless as well as finding all the collectibles.I'm also quite sure that this game lends it self for a good short speedrun pretty well if that's more you jam.And even without any of that just finishing the 2 to 5 hour long main story is already great fun.The only thing you shouldn't hope for is a grand narrative experience. Even though I like the narrative aspects of the game, they very much take the backseat and are more something to make you curious about any possible future titles.To conclude:Overall: Good game.When also considering cost: Exrtemely good value game!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal 3D platformer that knows how to use all the tools in its belt to let the player succeed in: 1. Collecting things and exploring cool environments2. Speedrunning levels that are fun to traverse with a simple double jump + spin3. Enjoying the banger soundtrackHonestly, I have no complaints. The game has everything I want in a strong platformer. It's got tight controls, varied level mechanics, fun secret paths, and the aforementioned excellent tunes. The story is a little weak, but I don't really mind. 9.5/10, you can't go wrong with the cheap price, either. This is a must-buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: This game is criminally under priced. For $5, I thought I was playing a game worth $15-20 given the quality of it.The graphics for this game is quite retro-themed and tries to copy a similar style from games like Sonic, which I found to be really nice. It also has a CRT option to give you that more authentic feel if you so desire it.The music in this game is spot on and each zone having a pretty distinct theme really drew me into anticipating each new zone I was going to reach. The level designs themselves are solid with each area having a new mechanic that is introduced whether it be the water, 'crypt of the necrodancer-esque' platforms, the sliding on platforms, it all combines itself to make each proceeding level more challenging than the last. Once you complete the game, there's still collectibles to obtain as well as 'reset' runs where you try to complete the level without failing, for certain characters, this involves a no hit run where you can't take any damage from the environment or enemies. This adds a nice layer of replayability to the game. Speaking of characters, you will unlock two additional characters once you complete the game for the first time, both with their own unique ending. The game does introduce a little bit of lore via completionist content, incentivizing you to fully complete each world as the main character. Again, more reasons to play through the game after your first play through.If you do plan to purchase the game, I highly recommend using a controller. I never tried the game with M+KB, but I felt that a controller was best suited for the gameTo get S-tier on everything and 100% all achievements, the game took roughly 13hrs to complete. For $5, it's hard to argue how this game isn't worth the value you get out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I am too young to know the PS1/Sega-era that have inspired this game. Maybe that's why it's a bit difficult for me, but I still loved every second of it.Apart from the awesome soundtrack and the polished visuals, it also has secret lore hidden that makes wanting to know more of this world!I've watched the developement streams on twitch so I know how much effort went into tiny details and also things like accessibility options.So far I have only comppleted Hana's route with Toree and Toukee still open, so I will probably spend some more hours in this lovely game.Also this game is optimized with respect to speedrunning and I really want to try that one out too! (it will be my first time ever :'D)I can really recommend and it and if you're not sure, try out the demo :D
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little 3D plattformer with beautiful levels, fast gameplay and secrets to collect. For anyone like me who doesn't like the PS1 era aesthetics too much and has seen some screenshots or videos of the game, the game definitely looks a lot better, when you play it yourself (esp. the giant tree level). Looking forward of what the speerun community will do with the game.  :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play that many platformer games but right after starting this game I felt like I have played this game for years already in terms of controls. It took me quite a while to get used to the rythm platforms but even with that I enjoyed the entire game very much. The exclusion of time for S ranks really makes me enjoy the game so much more than other games where I struggle to beat even A ranks because I'm too slow but there still is a timer for anyone who likes to go as fast as possible.Anyone who is decent at platformers should be able to enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: After following the development of Lunistice (and the several iterations it went through) for a few years, I'm happy to say that it turned out pretty great. You can quickly tell that it was made not only with heart, but also competence; by someone who loves (3D) platformers and understands how they should be designed to create a smooth, satisfying game flow. As such the controls are tight and responsive, the visuals accompanied by equally charming sound effects and an upbeat, catchy OST. The levels all bring in their own unique elements and have clearly been designed with speed and fluidity in mind. Speedrunning through them or taking it a bit slower and going for 100% collectibles (as I did) feel equally fun, especially since completion time isn't factored into the ranking. Checkpoints are mostly well-placed with just one or two exceptions at certain particularly tricky optional segments. Overall I'd say there's some decent challenge to be had without things ever feeling unfair.My only criticism would be about the minimalistic story, which starts off with a pretty cool voiced intro cutscene that immediately peaked my curiosity, but then (as far as I could tell at least) does basically nothing with that setup until the very last level. As fun as the game was, I actually felt a bit disappointed by the end because in my opinion there was quite a bit of unused potential there.(Edit: Well, I have to partially take that back, because I'm blind and only just noticed that you can read lore texts in the level select screen. I WAS wondering what some of the collectibles were supposed to be, lol. Still would've loved to experience more of it during the actual gameplay though.)Putting that aside though, I highly recommend Lunistice to anyone looking for a polished, short and sweet indie gem. Absolutely worth its money.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Charming retro platformer with excellent controls and challenging (at times as a casual gamer even borderline frustrating) level design. But the longer you play the better you get.Has some decent replay value due to collectibles and additional characters with different movesets.Definitely recommended and worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Lunistice reaches into my childhood and pulls out a vibrant, fun and challenging PlayStation game from half-remembered bits of classic platformers. It perfectly embodies how I remember these games looking and feeling, yet manages to dodge their shortcomings. It’s a joyful, nostalgic experience.I’d say more- but that would just waste time you could be spending playing it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Wow does this ever remind me of old school PS1 platforming. If you weren't around for that age you'll have to excuse the very particular controls and camera. If you dropped in hours back in the 90's with games like Crash Bandicoot or Spyro you're in for a rare time traveling treat. Music and SFX are good, the graphics are spot on. Enjoy some platforming goodness.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: A great little Platformer. The controls are tight, even if you need to get used to some peculiarities of them. Even when you misjudge a jump, you never get the feeling that it was the fault of the game.The graphics are a delightful throwback to the classic platformers of the N64 and PS1 era of Video Games, charming and bright.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: I usually hate 3D Platformers, and Ive never liked any sonic games I've played, so you'd think a sonic inspired 3D platformer wouldn't be my thing but I found it surprisingly enjoyable.I got quite heated at times when the precision platforming got a bit too annoying and especially that rhythm section caused my blood pressure to spike a bit. I'm also generally quite ♥♥♥♥ at 3D platformers, on account of playing very few. I am thankful this game avoided the major pitfall of having a time limit, cause being sent to the beginning at that last level would have made me snap my controller in half.Other than that though, the levels are cool, the artstyle is nice and music works well so consider it a recommendation I guess. Its fairly short which I think is entirely to the games' benefit and I dont mean that as an insult
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Did you always want to be hungry, have music stuck in your head and play a fox dressed as a tanuki? Then this game is for you!I had a lot of fun playing this 3D platformer. The visuals are extremely charming, as are the characters. The music is catchy and the controls are great. Playing through all the levels with the main character took me about 4.5 hours, and there's still stuff left to collect. So you'll definitely get your money's worth!
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: 3D platforming with an amazing game flow.The controls are tight, visuals are nicely styled after PS1 graphics (including CRT and 20fps emulation), the music is absolutely AMAZING  it's only 5 bucks.I strongly recommend buying this if you are looking for the warm, fuzzy feeling of playing a really good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: After replaying this game with their new camera options enabled I can now fully recommend this game. Its a short platformer/collectathon hybrid game with insanely cute visuals, and added repeatability with 2 additional characters, each with their own mechanics. If you're struggling with motion sickness like I was I highly recommend you turn off the pixelation as that seemed to really help with my issue.ORIGINAL REVIEW:Really fun game with fantastic visuals, its just whatever they did with the camera made me extremely motion sick. Still gonna give it a positive review for the time being but if this was a one off issue or something gets changed Ill rewrite my review
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Wow just wow! I've been wanting a good platformer like this for a long time.The game not only convinces with its incredibly good controls, but also offers you seven chapters full of varied and fun levels. In these you can collect collectables and try to break your high score, which gives you even more incentive to explore the levels. These are linear in design, but still offer plenty of room to find new paths, shortcuts and secrets. The game grabs you right at the beginning so that I played through it in two sessions, for example. For the story you need about 3-4 hours which are really worth it and afterwards you even have a few bonus tasks to do.For me the game is a real insider tip and I still have to force some friends of mine to buy this masterpiece :D"Rating: 10/10(voted for game of the year)
_childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: The crystals add so much pop to the color schemes and even running in circles is fun, because the footsteps and jumps sound so cute. _childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun, if you like solid 3D playformers that isnt just running forward and jumping then this is perfect for you.You'll jumping, turning, going in spirals upwards. no straight lines here just fun platforming. _childDocuments_.name: Lunistice

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased this after seeing a Rock Paper Shotgun article about it and could not be happier with my decision.Finished the base game without getting every collectible in under 3 hours. The music is atmospheric, the graphics reminiscent of another era (with framerates to match, should you choose), and the experience short, but sweet.I'm incredibly impressed and hope devs look to this game as a model for nostalgia hits done right. _childDocuments_.review: Overall: 8/10Excellent music, nice graphics, pleasant game to play. I like short games too, so its a huge boon to effectively finish everything (Minus beating the game again with the new characters) In around 2.5 hours. The game falls short with the Camera & Repetitiveness, which honestly is not too bad considering the pace & length of the game. But the camera is a big stickler for me;Pros:• Fast paced platforming, rewards speed & precision• Infinite retries, only losing a letter grade for subsequent deaths• Platforming in general feels really good• Easily recognizable-repeatable entities (Grind rails, bounce pads, launch rings, disappearing platforms, etc)• Fun to collect the HANA letters on each stageCons:• The Camera.Which is obviously designed for speed, as it sits behind Hana at a fixed angle, pointing forward. Tilting the camera (right stick) backward zooms it out a bit, and tilts it down a tad. I want to be able to point it further down, so I can land these jumps. I lost count on how many times I died just to not being able to tell what Hana was above or not above something. (I do know about the options menu -> Player Shadow option. While nice, its not effective because of the camera restriction)• Repetitive levelsOnce you've seen the third level, you will have encountered nearly all types of platforming element the game has to offer. Its the same enemies all the way through, the same types of platforms, and the same grind rails. I do wish we were introduced to more stuff as the levels carried on.Summary:I unlocked the real ending (Collecting all the HANA letters on every level) and completed every stage. I started a play through with the other characters, but I'm not sure i'll beat the game again.Totally worth the some ~5 dollars USD its selling for right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a simple but fun moveset and gorgeous low poly graphics. For ~5$ USD this game is an excellent scratch if you have a 3D platformer itch, definitely worth picking up. Oh also the music is insane, every track slaps

_childDocuments_.review: First found out about this game due to SAGE 2022 (look it up if you don't know), which featured the demo of this game. And because so many Sonic games during that event were pretty lame, figured I'd give some other ones a shot, and this happened to be one of them. Turned out to be my favourite game of the event and came to be one of my most anticipated games for the remainder of the year (I was literally gushing over the demo over how fun it was). Fast forward to when I finish Sonic Frontiers and transition into this game... My hype was just kinda gone, and idk why really. Might be because I played the demo already so I'd basically already played (which is why I should stop playing demos tbh, takes away from that epic "first time feel"). The controls are also not really as good as Frontiers imo (even the Cyber Space levels). Feels like you go in directions randomly sometimes (adjusting sensitiviy doesn't really help much) and the jump ESPECIALLY can be annoying sometimes when it either overshoots or undershoots, and is really hard to land on small or narrow platforms sometimes due to how floaty it can feel (which is one of the reasons I don't really care about going for all S-ranks tbh, since you can't die whilst going for them). Other things about the game imo:- OST is good, but nothing really that I'd listen to outside of playing the game. - Speaking of OST, level 5 BGM is completely silent until midway through the level (which I think is a super odd design choice tbh). And I don't really like that level in general personally, feels way too big.- Level design is OK at best. Do really like speed up platforms, rail grinding and water slides tho. - Really wish there was actually a final boss tied into that final level ngl. - Story is essentially non-existent lol, even though there's meant to be one. That all said though, it's still a fun game, just not the "top 5 games of the year" material I was expecting it to be really, had my hopes up too high. Do recommend you give this a shot though, it does have a ton of charm.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, Lunistice is fantastic. The controls and platforming are very tight, the level design is fun and the environments are very well put together, the soundtrack is great to listen to from beginning to end, and the story, while simple, is told very well. Thoroughness in exploration leads to finding optional collectibles, which provide a good challenge without making things harder. If you're looking for secrets, you most likely won't need to repeat any stage more than once to find everything in it. Even though the game is short, there is a surprising amount of replayability. You can replay all the levels if you want to get all the collectibles, earn the highest stage rank, or you can even play as different characters, who each have their own mechanics and movement abilities. All of these aspects come together to make an utterly amazing game, that is incredibly worth its low price of admission and more.

_childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory is Harvest Moon if it was a JRPG taken to the extreme. Don't try and think about the game like you would Stardew Valley. Think about making big numbers even bigger. Your soil has stats. Your plant seeds have levels. Items have stats and levels. Items that go into equipment apply unique stats and also increase hidden level values that make stats bigger than you could imagine, with even more crazy crafting potential when you start getting into negating negative penalties and adding multipliers and all sorts of black magic. Your character has stats on stats on stats. Your character has both regular levels from killing monsters and also skill levels from performing actions, no matter how mundane. Sleeping? There's a skill for that. Bathing? Yup. Walking? You bet.If what you want is a casual farming simulator, this may or may not be the game for you. Just be aware that Rune Factory wears its JRPG influences on its sleeves, and there are a whole lot of mechanics that are bubbling underneath the surface if you're willing to indulge them.
_childDocuments_.name: Rune Factory 5

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Harvest Moon game with a 25-35 hour RPG sidequest.For newcomers, this is a great game if you can get it at a bit cheaper of a price. If you like Stardew Valley and wish there was a more compelling story, then this is a series you should check it out. That's about all I have to say for you.For Rune Factory fans, this is not Rune Factory 4: The Sequel.This is Rune Factory 5. The first hour of the game had me feeling like this game was going to be an objective step down. Everything felt off, and I couldn't quite put my finger on it. You have these cutscenes with their forced pacing on dialogue and such, which was pretty minimal in RF4. You are forced to greet everyone on the first day, and there is no timer counting down while you do so. The music isn't as vibrant as RF4. Plus, you're subjected to some really long opening cutscenes introducing characters you haven't been sold on yet. The start just doesn't hit as hard; RF4 paid a lot of attention to getting all of the systems' down to a science, and the quality of life/ergonomics were pretty incredible overall.However, the first hour is not the rest of the game. The game really picks up and I felt at home. I got used to the music and the town really grew on me. Personally, I really enjoy the character designs, much more than RF4. Everyone felt unique and I wish everyone was as thoroughly explored as all the bachelors/bachelorettes. The story was serviceable, it wasn't great but it wasn't awful. Doesn't hold a candle to RF4, but that's not the point here.The story progression is probably the starkest departure of this game, and no doubt what spawns a lot of the ire from hardcore RF fans. I played on hard difficulty.  The game does not limit you on how many requests you can do per day, or how many of the "Wanted Monsters" you can do. Going blind, I was able to complete the entire story by Summer 3. The last 1.5 dungeons took those 3 days of Summer. Every single day had major story progression. Throughout this, I barely had to engage with any of the crafting system after getting silver equipment - and that was only for farming. I never once used a handmade crafted piece of armor or weapon beyond a pair of boots I crafted because you can't unequip the squeaky shoes unless you have something to put over it.This choice to enable the player to ignore the mechanical depth is not a flat-out downside, it is a difference, and I believe this is the achille's heel of the game for the fans. I'm pretty certain you can beat the story part of this game without even farming once - I'm excited to go back and replay it like that, to see if it's even possible. It might be tangentially possible in RF4, but I really don't think it would be fun. It'd be like doing True NeverClick in cookie clicker - waiting 30 minutes to an hour before you finally get the right things to line up. My play experience by refusing to engage with the crafting systems in depth was not as pleasant as it could have been otherwise, but that's what I enjoy about the series. I died many, many times to Faint moves, and if I engaged with the system properly I would have been prepared to upgrade my equipment to resist it, or preferred food to do so. But now I can say I beat a game within a season and some change, and that's what makes me happy. You can get away with the first 3 fields and have a very pleasant experience. Hell, you may even be able to get away with just the first one and be just fine. It also doesn't help there really isn't much of a prescribed post game. You can do a 20 floor dungeon, that's about it. No dungeon seeds or anything. However, you CAN bump the levels of the enemies up pretty high, which I guess is what the devs were thinking when they added those systems.This newfound freedom in terms of how the player can approach the game - fast paced and bum rushing the story, or taking the time to really take in the town and the systems - both really helps and hurts the game. There's no mandatory downtime, you don't have to wait for anything. But then, why do I need to wait for my crops to grow? I finished the game and then did a victory lap the day after harvesting all my leeks I planted, but now none of that million+ gold I have is going to do anything to help me progress the already finished story. Also, why the hell am I getting access to flowers about 75% through the story? Did the devs want the "Raise everyone's friendship to 5" request to be an arduous challenge or something? I realize that the game encourages you to give people homemade items, but I've grown up playing since the series on the SNES Harvest Moon on Wii VC. Old habits die hard, and I want my flowers dammit.If you go into RF5 comparing it to RF4 the whole time, you're going to hamper a good experience. It's flawed, but I think it really works well if you view it as its own entity. It's a bit disappointing the story doesn't really cover the game anywhere even close to long enough for progressing everything. But there's a LOT of upgrade possibility, and it's very easy and accessible for understanding how to trigger the heart/friendship events. To me, this is peak Harvest Moon. Sure, you don't really NEED to get that mountain house, but you can if you want to grind for it. It seems like they designed a Harvest Moon game for the town, and then the dungeon and combat completely separately, then merged the two and called it a day. This is where I realized what felt off about the game at the start. It was starting off like Harvest Moon. Stupid cutscenes and manual forced greetings before you can even play the game to give you that country side living vibe for whatever reason. Then, Rune Factory takes the wheel for the next 25-35 hours while it gives you stories and dungeons to go through. After that, though, you're kicked back to a Harvest Moon town that you can go through and unlock a whole bunch of upgrades, veggies, fruits, and flowers in a really casual, laidback manner. The idea is pretty cool in my opinion - having a short main game with a lot of side content. I just wish doing that grind ended up having more bonus dungeons or a cute little scene here and there. I feel like that was where they were headed with this, but they decided to just wrap it up, and the game suffers. In the end, Rune Factory 5 is a lateral move for the franchise overall. Instead of having a prescribed pacing to events, RF5 essentially lets you go as hard and fast as you want. There are bits and pieces of the previous Rune Factory games and their stories, and it's an incredibly familiar experience on the surface. However, the main story goes by fast if you let it, and there's not much "Rune Factory" side content with dungeons or bosses that will block you. Instead, you get a lot of casual content for you to explore and go through. RF5 at the very least lays a good groundwork for an RF6 to take over and flesh out a more thorough story and world, if it ever happens. I just hope it's more Rune Factory and much less Harvest Moon.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so happy that I purchased this game. I waited because of the reviews but it's definitely not as bad as I was anticipating. It is very much a Runefactory game in 3D and actually reminds of a nice looking Gamecube or Wii game graphics wise. I really like the characters. They aren't as colorful as Runefactory 4 characters but it definitely still feels like I'm living in an anime world. This is largely due to the dialog. In Runefactory 4, everyone had something new to say pretty much everyday for a year. For this game, the new dialog comes with an increase in friendship and even then, there's not as much. So it's more varied than your basic people interactions in Harvest moon/Stardew Valley but not as curated as Runefactory 4. I'm a woman and play as the female character and this time around, I'm much happier with the Bachelors as most of them look like they're over 18 (save for Cecil). The Amber, Xiao Pais and Kiels are thankfully gone though Cecil and ♥♥♥♥♥ could have been made a bit less childish (not as bad as the aforementioned people of the previous game but still...). I'd rather they have adult looking characters with childish mannerisms than child looking characters who they are trying to sell to me as adults (a problem in anime in general).  The farming mechanics are fun. The main character is definitely more vocal than necessary in their farming activities but I find it more humorous than annoying. They could have done more to explain the Farm Dragon mechanic. They were just kind of there all of sudden but I'm a hands on learner so maybe it's better that they didn't and you can just figure it out as you go. The music is just as beautiful as the previous games (1 and 4 is what played the most. I only played 2 briefly and can't remember it to save my life). No complaints there.What brings this game down the most is the performance. I've run into a really annoying glitch where the farm tool sound effects can end up looping.so I have to save and reload the game. On top of that the camera shakes. These are amateur mistakes and I can understand why people are turned off by the lack of finesse. It's a modern day gaming issue where games just seem unfinished and this game is no exception. Some cut scenes even have a rushed quality to them and the dialog can seem a bit off... I wish these game designers would focus on making complete, finished products that function well. Ocarina of Time on the N64 has better camera movement than this game. There's no excuse.Overall, RF4 was 10/10. This game is 8.5/10. Still very good but a whole point comes off for performance issues. Don't think of it as"The sequel to Runefactory 4". If you're still on the fence like I was, think of it as it's own unique entry to the RuneFactory series. If you like Runefactory games, you'll probably like this one.Update 1/28/2024So I beat the game and during the final boss fight, the boss got stuck on a glitch. I was attacking it and noticed that nothing was happening. I had to LEAVE the final boss fight and come back just to beat the game. Inexcusable. I've spent at least 2-3 years of my life gaming. I've never come in contact with such a glitch at a final boss fight. I was left with a bad taste in my mouth at the end. 'Embarathy' really. The end cut-scenes felt cheap. I had tears of joy and sadness at the end of RF4. For RF5, I just cringed.I would put this game closer to a 7.5-8 now. They took what could have been a phenomenal game and created it half-halfheartedly. So many game designers (and movie directors) do that these days. They know we love the series and play on  that, figuring we'll eat mediocrity right up. It sucks. And no fix has come out to address performance issues. I went back to fight the last boss again later on and still got the same glitch. I think after that I felt like I was just done with the game. *Sigh*

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would absolutely recommend this game to both Rune Factory enjoyers and people who have not yet played a game in the series. There are some downsides to the game compared to previous titles, but I really adore it.Regarding glitches, I have not experienced any (aside from a very minor UI bug that fixed itself when I loaded a new area) nor have I encountered a single crash. Quick rundown for people who have never played a Rune Factory game. It's Harvest Moon except you get the RPG mechanics of having a million skills for literally everything and a lot of combat - walking, eating, bathing, you name it, it's a skill. The story is always a little dramatic, but the characters are memorable, charming, and quite goofy. Even the farming is a little extra, and not so slow-paced (in terms of quantity grown and speed grown at). By nature, RPGs can get a little grindy and RF isn't really an exception here.Pros:- The game runs without hitching or lagging on my PC.- I enjoy the keyboard and mouse controls (you can also fully change them on the launcher - not from in game).- QoL changes from previous titles: seeing where cutscenes are/who they are for, auto pickup items, mass deposit lumber/stone/grass, switching between storage bin/fridge/tool bin/etc from one screen.- I really find the 3D style charming and for the monsters that are new, they all have really fantastic designs. The colors in the 3D world are really vibrant (compared to portraits).- The crafting/forging system is just as complex as previous titles, and I love it.- The character dynamics are really fun and I'm glad to see that a character's event also incorporates other townsfolk.- Fishing feels easier this time around, which is a good thing because it was impossible for me to catch the rarer fish in previous games.- It's a lot easier to stockpile lumber and material stone as well.Cons:- The voice lines for common actions are way too repetitive (watering at the beginning of the game, picking up any items, brushing monsters).- The world feels very empty.- You cannot place furniture very close to anything at all. (There is a mod on Nexus to fix this, I really recommend it).- Boss fights feel like they take ages because there are long pauses while you wait for them to be vulnerable again after a phase change roar.- Cutscenes will, without warning, skip through parts of the day or even to entirely new days - this is not a glitch. I recommend saving before doing cutscenes for this reason. It's not so bad, but skipping from 11am to 5pm on a festival day without warning is tragic.- Murakumo and Heinz feel like they're never in their shops when I want them to be there.- It feels like it takes ages to get from bronze to silver tools.- I hate that you can die from using a skill when you're out of RP and low on health. I would rather prefer to be unable to use my skills in these cases. An accidental slipup and I cast my spell seal, also killing me.- The flower shop takes WAY too long to unlock, with no indication that there even is one or will be one util it's unlocked.I personally don't think the cons outweigh the pros here, some of them are very small gripes or easy to get used to. RF5 is just a fun farming life-sim with combat and dating.  If you're looking for a Switch game like this, get Rune Factory 4 Special or wait for Rune Factory 3 to be released on the Switch. I own RF5 for the Switch and I bounced off it so hard, it's tragic.

_childDocuments_.review: I rewrote this review. My original review did not sit well with me. It failed to effectively communicate feelings I have about the series and the direction they chose with this entry. Harvest Moon and Rune Factory are a series I have enjoyed for the better part of two decades. These games mean quite a bit to me.If you enjoyed the core systems in previous games, you will enjoy them in Rune Factory 5. Farming, taming, crafting, magic staff intricacies, etc. Those things are still here and I think they're some of the best iterations yet. The quality of life improvements on top those core systems just make it even better. It is nice to start a new day and teleport  to a boss I'm farming for drops. It's also wonderful to access any storage and instantly swap to other storage mediums. Having town events clearly market on the map and allowing you to trigger them when you want is another welcome boon. Accidentally selected short sword instead of long sword? Now you can just swap to the correct weapon type you want to craft from any like-type crafting menu!This is the first Rune Factory core game that is making the jump to 3D from the handheld. It is rough around the edges and you will have to be willing to forgive some aspects of their design to enjoy the game. For some reason, even on a solid state drive the game lags horrendously on the first run each time I boot my PC. It only lasts for the first few minutes and then doesn't happen again, but it is annoying when other more intense games do not. By default, the game uses a “farming camera” when you move onto farm plots. Do yourself a favor and shut it off in the options menu because it is horrible and jarring. Side stories sometimes share the same start locations for events and the events can stack over one another. You'll finish one event only to immediately trigger the next and these cannot be canceled. You'll have to see the entire event through before going to the one you wanted to do next.Targeting in combat can be iffy at times when it randomly switches and faces you in a direction you don't want to. This can also happen when simply trying to chop wood or break stone. You will swing the hammer and miss by a pixel or the game will fail to line you up properly. Final note: some battles will throw out a monster that has an instant kill attack. These are few and far between, but sometimes you don't know they are in a particular spawn group. Their attack will just tag you randomly and you'll be looking at a hefty revive fee.Taming is once again partially RNG hell. Despite my best efforts, I failed taming my fourth chicken over and over again despite having level 10 eggs, brushing 15 times, and having a level 20 or so skill in taming. They have instituted a 10 item limit as well where if you don't get the tame within 10 tries, you'll have to start all over again. Expect to reload frequently on particular bosses.Finally, the final boss fight ran into a bug where they completely locked up at 70% of their HP. Reloading the auto-save fixed it but this handily destroyed the pacing of the entire end sequence.When the game first explains taming in Rune Factory 5, it talks about a new mechanic and ties it together with taming. However, you don't actually need to use it for taming. The wording of this tutorial was a bit confusing and mislead me for two-thirds of the entire main story.These characters are vapid. I attribute this to a lack of time and money for the developers since they had to claw the series out of bankruptcy. Not enough time is spent on the cast to really bring them all to life in the ways they deserve to be. The love interests are one dimensional tropes for the most part and the rest of the town is not much better. The world lacks the cohesion of feeling lived in. In Rune Factory 4, you could run into people having discussions about various things. It felt like they had their own goals for the day. You could inspect things inside their homes and they would comment on them. They were also unique, even if they were based on a trope.The main story is severely lacking. They tried rehashing certain aspects of Rune Factory 4 but with a minor spin. However, since the characters are so empty there's just no connection to be had with them. The villain only shows up briefly at one point and then not again until the very end. There's a two minute redemption arc that I can't even care about since I know nothing of his background or story. There are other emotions you're supposed to have with the villain, but you just can't have them because you never take the time to build on it. The worst part is they lock out marriage, some quests, and other parts behind story progression or clearing the main story completely.I know this is going to be a contentious opinion, but I dislike the fan service. Previous games have had their fan service but this time feels different. It feels more up front and one sided to favor a male demographic with the designs. How up front this game is about it was very apparent when you are introduced to the combo doctor-mayor and her underwear being above her short-line. Wolf-girl and Ludmila in particular feel as if they are created more for the feeling in your pants than for storytelling or character building – which is an absolute shame as I would love to know more about the beast race and how succubi fit into the world of Rune Factory. Another example is Misasagi and whatever those “shorts” are. Additionally, if Misasagi were to move any faster than a brisk jog, her wardrobe would malfunction.Let me clarify, I do not hate these characters. I just feel like they're underutilized and missed opportunities. Ludmila does not explain enough as to why she dresses that way or how succubi are in the rest of the world. Are they all like her? Are there incubi too? Do they get along? No idea, we don't talk about it. How about Wolf-girl – Why do the other Beast villagers rarely talk about her? How is her tribe different from other Beast tribes? Finally, Misasagi herself is a completely missed opportunity. If Misasagi were a romance option – It opens an entirely new avenue for storytelling. Now you have a single mother who also has a child. Instead of just having your own kid eventually, now your first child would be her child. How well does Hina integrate with that change? What about future siblings? Would Hina feel like she's being replaced? Would she get along with them? What if she didn't?You can have your fan service characters. Just make them characters and not some teenager's wet dream. I'd rather have six well developed characters over 12 trope-y romance options. More world building and interpersonal connections, please.If you're a fan of the series, you'll enjoy it. On the fence? -- Buy when discounted. New to the series? -- Look into Rune Factory 4 Special. It's a better entry into the series with a stronger story and characters. Play with a controller -- for both games!Edit: Wolf-girl is F u u k a since it auto censored. Spelling/grammar

_childDocuments_.review: If you own this on the Switch or thinking of getting it on the Switch, this review is for you. I've owned RF5 for the Switch on release, and had I known it was coming to PC I would have waited. The Switch version only has the advantage of being portable. It claims 30 FPS on Switch, but is more likely 30 FPS and below even when docked... which is absolutely pathetic in modern gaming, especially since the Switch claims to be a console that's supposed to compete with whatever Xbox and PS they have out these days. About 10 hours in to the game on the Switch it was obvious that Rune Factory 5 was being dragged down by the Switch's lack of graphical power and buttons. The game's open world (which is absolutely beautiful on PC, something you cant really appreciate on the Switch) would reduce frames by a lot, the graphics looked like something out of the Nintendo 64, buttons and menus are stuffed with the lack of buttons, and it was clear the devs had to remove a lot to make it run 'just enough' for the switch. On PC everything is, obviously, smooth. I have the frames locked at 120 and they never drop. The game is incredibly well optimized graphically and the keyboard+mouse controls make the game much more fast paced in every aspect, including combat, as it should be. I have the graphics set to MAX, making it look like a modern JRPG should.  I set the graphics to the lowest out of curiosity, and not even the Switch could reach that quality. Farming and fighting are made smooth with keyboard+mouse, resulting in a fast game play that was really difficult to achieve on the Switch with it's button layouts. I also tried it with the good ol Logitech controller, and even that makes it better than the switch's controls. It really is a shame the Switch players dont get to see and play the game as it should be. Rune Factory 5 is probably one of many video games that are being held back by the need to optimize for the Switch.

_childDocuments_.review: Jumping straight to it with this one, Rune Factory 5 is a good game but not one without faults. This game feels rushed, missing features and lacks some polish and QoL but overall, it's still a good game IMO. In short, RF5 is the most accessible of all RF games. The game's story can be done as fast or as slow as you wish. Aside from the main story, the game acts a lot more like a Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons game compared to previous titles. There's a bit more hand holding in the first hour compared to the rest of the series but after that the game opens up a lot. The farming portion is more similar to HM/SoS where you just do what you want to do at your own pace. Talk to the villagers, do requests, manage your farm, etc. This alongside the typical Rune Factory activities like crafting, fighting and taming monsters.Oh and I recommend installing RF5Fix (there's a guide in steam guides) in order to fix all of the minor bugs the game has (aside from the music glitch).Rune Factory is a farming game where you can farm, tame monsters, dungeon crawl and get married. Everything in RF has a skill associated to it which increases your stats, even the SOIL has stats! These stats help with tons of things and allow you to feel like you're making significant growth just by doing things you want to do.Most monsters and bosses can be tamed some monsters drop daily and other monsters are great in combat and can be brought alongside the villagers to the dungeons and hang out with. All monsters and villagers have levels and friendship levels to level up to gain perks such as extra stats or higher level produce.And finally this game has crafting. You can try crafting at a basic level without adding tons of upgrades or special effects or go full crazy and combine multiple accessories into a single slot.TL;DR RF has a lot of mechanical depth that can be explored in your own time as there are many helpful guides online that explains how to do so, while also being a fun time waster as its farming sim aspect is very solid and can also be very in-depth if you wish to explore it. Make tons new friends, decorate your house, etc. Less refined compared to 4S. It's still decent but not much has been improved aside from the shift of perspective. The dash is also kind of slow, though not useless as the game includes a perfect dash mechanic. Not sure why the combat from Tides didn't make it in as this was definitely not the first foray into 3rd person the series has had but what we got is serviceable. Farming is the same as 4S, tho there are no longer seasonal fields which are a massive pain and annoyance as the lack of seasonal fields means plants that don't grow well in the current season are debuffed in growth like in 4S. Farm Dragons are the farm expansions this time round but don't have fixed seasons, tho you can feed them crystals for various effects. Nothing special, it was really nice and gave me the feels by the end but it's not as long as 4S or as good as 3's (which has the best story IMO). A nice way to tie the player with an objective and aim like every other game in the franchise. Probably the most important part of a game that's half life simulation. In short, I love the cast, better than 4S IMO. All of the love interests are appealing and super cute. The town as a whole are also super nice though I do wish they had a bit more development like the love interests. There's a decent bit of nice QoL, including but not limited to: multiple warp points within the town, being able to warp in and out of specific parts of dungeons and to your other farm fields, etc. The new "Catch" mechanic is a bit iffy but really useful when you're grinding items. Mostly the same as 4S but with some minor adjustments, you can find these by looking up guides online on what exactly they are. In the end it's just as in-depth as the previous games though you won't ever be forced to actually learn to use it past the basics in this one. It's easy, probably the easiest RF title to date. While I personally prefer a challenge, this is mostly good for accessibility purposes though I wished hard mode would've actually posed a challenge or we had a 4th difficulty option as abusing the crafting system can make the game way past easy.Overall the game is fine, it's not worse or better than 4S. For what this game provides there are both ups and downs to what it changes and what it kept. Overall this is a really good spot to start the franchise as it eases newer players that may not be very well versed in RPG mechanics like combat and in-depth crafting into the series much easier than the other games. I only encountered some but the ones I did encounter were a bit annoying. Music sometimes cuts out only in the town, forcing you to reload your save to fix it. The camera sometimes stutters (varies). Final boss can get stuck, if it does just warp out. Not very fluid for a 3rd person game, it's not bad but it could be better. Step down from 4S. Should've made each dragon have their own season, their aesthetics are just for looks and they're pretty much nothing more than extra space for farming and barns. You can only have one side event up at any time, this means that until you complete the current event you can't progress romance stories or confess to your love interest. The side story objectives are also usually rather vague and don't tell you when you can progress aside from a marker on the map that appears if it's able to be progressed, this can result in multiple days of being unable to progress a story cuz you don't know when or where to continue. Some main story quests also prevent them from progressing and it's never made clear when it does. It's too big, getting everywhere is a schlog and there's a bunch of empty areas on certain maps making it feel too big. HOLY CRAP WHAT IS THIS SPAWN RATE. You can literally stand on your field and see the debris spawn in 5, this is WAY too frequent. Various things that don't affect most people but affect certain crowds can be improved such as buying and moving furniture etc. They even removed some things like hiding headwear (using invisible stones). Saving should stop being at save points only and be doable anywhere, the game would benefit from it a ton and it won't break anything. Furniture placement has always been iffy but it's at its worst here. Somehow there's less mechanics explained to you in 5 than 4S. At least in 4S some villagers may hint at them but you only get the basics here.Game good, some flaws but overall very good entry to start with if you're new to RF.Is it worth $60? Depends on you, I'm done with the postgame and mostly clearing up the extra stuff land I'm at like 80+ hours. The game's not for everyone but personally I enjoyed 5 more than 4S. The main story can be beaten within a single season if you want to rush it or be done as slow as you want. Sadly the game's postgame is rather lacking as there are no dungeon seeds so if you prefer the dungeon crawling this game's going to be pretty short.RF5 combines the best elements of HM/SoS's slower paced relaxed farming sim elements with RF's crafting, taming and combat which makes it a nice change of pace if you prefer doing things slower and feel overwhelmed by the mechanical depth some of the RPG elements of this game has.If you like HM/SoS or are already a RF fan who wants to play a new game... buy it, it's worth the price. Otherwise maybe wait for a sale (30-40%?).

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Rune Factory 3 and 4, which I really, REALLY enjoyed, this game feels like a slap in the face.I wanted to give it a fair chance after hearing all the mixed opinions, but I just can't anymore.With each passing hour I wanted more and more to just play Rune Factory 4 again.The Town and environments are way too big, have no charm and look empty. The way the NPCs behave is also very stiff and lifeless. An Example: During a festival, everyone goes 2 mph to the plaza and then they'll just stand there doing nothing. They don't interact with eachother at all. Not even simple hand gesture or talking animations... they're just standing there like robots and stare off into the distance for the whole festival. Outside of story events It's like they are oblivious to the existance of eachother.I also encountered multiple repeated dialogues within the first week. In previous games you could go a month or two without seeing any repeated dialogues. Like seriously, what happened here? The NPCs are supposed to be the highlight of Rune Factory!Days are way too long. I have everything done for the whole day when it hits 1 or 2pm.The rest of the day just drags on and I just want to go to the next day.Combat and Farmwork feels very unresponsive and janky. It seems like it buffers previous inputs for way to long.The game just feels unpolished and unfishined.It's also not enough that the graphics looks like one of those bad licensed Wii games, but it also suffers from performance, pop-in and several other issues that where and will never be fixed by the devs.I can understand that a transition to 3D and creating all the new assets can be difficult (they re-used a lot of assets going from RF3 to RF4 for example), but they could at least have committed to fix the issues that the community has with the game and not just abandon it after release...Edit: Typos

It just disappears out of existence, with no sound or anything, where in older game it was like, nomnom sound effects, with few eating particle specs here and there, as the item like got smaller and smaller as it was eaten. Had a lil animation to it. Everything is kinda like this. Those small extra layers of polish around the whole game is just... missing... Break a mineral, and the big ol model just... disappears out of existence in the blink of an eye. No death animation or anything. The sound effects of the menu is not satisfying or wet at all in it's quality, but feels like an annoying chunky dry chirp beep that grains my ears after listening to it for too long. The music... is like... dude... there's 1 track?? And it sucks lmao. You will hear the dang town music on repeat and loop forever, and it will drive you insane. Every event cutscene, starts with a jarring transition screen through a black screen as you enter the designated event point. They don't really occur naturally, or the characters are at the places the events take place. They kinda just... teleport there magically as you enter the zones. The cutscene always starts with this weird one specific camera shot of your character walking up and going, heya guys, huehuehue, wassup? And like... I seen that same thing play out a billion times lol.Where in older games, every NPC would kinda have at least 2 unique dialogues for every day of the year, here, they feel like they have 2-3 lines of dialogue in total that they might repeat if you talk to them. You will already start seeing repeats on the second day lol.I could go on, but I'm lazy and tired. Last main thing is just... _childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played Rune Factory before, go with 4 instead. If you have, only buy if you're just desperately thirsty for a RF fix. The story and gameplay are fine, but it just completely drops off after you beat the main story. It me took until the beginning of Fall to get that far. _childDocuments_.review: A game so nice I bought it twice for Switch and PC.  The PC version plays far smoother (up to 120/unlmited FPS) where the Switch version was so choppy I had to pan the camera to stare at the ground almost all the time.  On the PC, everything looks much sharper, but the sharpness also betrays the limits of the Switch-targeting textures and polygon counts.  If you're willing to forgive that, Rune Factory 5 is a charming farming/life simulator game with atypical depth.What's Rune Factory?  The Rune Factory series started back in 2006 on the Nintendo DS, adding RPG battling to Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons farming when Stardew Valley was just a twinkle in ConcernedApe's eye.  Rune Factory 5 is the seventh game in the series if you count the two spin-offs.  As is Rune Factory tradition, expect to be an amnesiac meeting a town of friendly people including lots of bachelors and bachelorettes that wouldn't be out of place on the set of the Dog Days anime.  Yeah, it's quite weeby, with visual novel JRPG elements.  But also very sweet and wholesome (even the resident succubus).Rune Factory 5 stands apart from the rest of the Rune Factory series by going fully 3D, but it was somewhat awkwardly realized.  (I find the PC version with mouse and keyboard helps with the awkwardness due to the added precision.)  For the first time in the series, all the marriage candidates are available to either gender of protagonist (but there's only two genders in the game).  This latest iteration of the crafting and combat mechanics are very well refined and streamlined with use-based progression and robust party support that can include townspeople and tamed monsters.From my experiences in Rune Factory 5 PC so far, it seems to be a very effective port of the Switch version.  But the distant texture and poly counts are a bit Switch-hardware-limited, so don't go in expecting PC tech demo graphics.  Also beware that there is a bit of a learning curve to get a handle on the JRPG consolitus interface.  However, if you like life simulator/farming games with RPG mechanics and anime aesthetics, I can easily recommend Rune Factory 5.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Rune Factory. 4 is one of my favorite games ever, period. I tried this game on switch at release and the performance killed it for me, so I thought this port on a deep sale would maybe change my mind over a year later. Spoiler alert, it did not. At first I was enjoying it, until I started realizing that it wasn't just performance that killed the game, it was the actual content of the game. I beat this game before even getting a single typhoon, being able to date a single character, growing anything higher tier than a sweet potato, or getting any decent equipment. I basically didn't need to seriously engage with any of the aspects of the game outside of the story, for the most part unlike 4 where I not only felt it was important but enjoyed doing it. This is not a good video game and I hope and PRAY that the devs have learned from this fiasco and will do much better in 6 and the spinoff because Rune Factory is a series that deserves the kind of love that similar games of the genre get.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I love the Rune Factory series and enjoyed this game, I simply can't recommend it due to the lack of replayability and endgame. When you compare this title to a 3DS title such as RF4 or 3, the lack of content after the story ends is quite disheartening. The games dialogue is also extremely repetitive and characters lack a lot of relationship connection with the MC. Even after marriage some of the generic language with the MC isn't changed and is awkward as they still refer to you simply as "Friend" rather than "Lover" at times. There's no sense of accomplishment in getting the best in class gear and weapons just to steamroll one dungeon in 30 minutes-2 hours (Level and skill dependant). I understand you can raise the levels of all monsters via orders, but even then it seems pointless when there isn't much accomplishment out of it. This game also has a lot of random bugs/graphical bugs that are unpleasant. The audio bug is one that comes to mind that made it difficult using certain boss monsters as companions without being earfudged to the tenth degree.The REALLY bad - Character events being spread out amongst SEVERAL days and time in this game running really slow is a killer. There isn't much exploring and daily boss runs does get boring but only waste 2-3 hours at end game. The clock is simply just too slow and with the way events are randomly spread amongst late hours - early hours its a bit of a slogfest waiting for things. For the impatient gamer and people wanting to experience side story, it can be gruelling. Waiting 10 minutes to run to one location for 30 seconds of dialogue and then having to wait again is a bit much isn't it? This really wouldn't have been a problem if they  added more things to do with some worth to your actions. The Good - Character designs are very nice and they never fail to please in this aspect. Beatrice and Ludmila are the biggest gems. The story was a very unique experience and I had a very enjoyable time reading through it, although it did feel like it was rushed (Note I did speedrun the story for the most part before getting into relationships. I did give gifts but was not actively seeking events/dates daily). The "Special" dates we're a treat and I did enjoy quite a few of them outside of a few characters having bland romance and dialogue. They also stay true to being a partial farming and crafting sim and is still enjoyable after so many years. There isn't a lack of recipes anywhere and the new addition of "Starfall" fruits/vegi's makes it unique (Although I would reference back to the fact that often times the recipes dont have a lot of use and/or are overkill when you get it)My word of advice is if you plan on getting this game, come into it with a clean slate and not with an RF4 mentality of endless things to do. This game was certainly rushed in a lot of aspects and deserved to be held back for another few months/ a year to polish & add truly heart capturing content/dialogue. It is a shame that game developers nowadays wont take the time to add small things like the hug/kiss animations RF4 did to make MC feel more in-touch with the other characters/your lover of choice. There is a lot to enjoy, but there certainly is a lot to nitpick and be unhappy about. I chose not to add the more nitpicky bits as there is... A LOT...

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed with this game. It's a bit grindy but it's absolutely one of the best farming games on the market right now especially if you have ADHD or its cousins and can't focus to save your life. That's okay here, because in Rune Factory 5 you're always accomplishing something! Whether getting lost in the forest or forgetting what you're doing halfway through a task, that's okay because you're still leveling up your walking skill! There's a skill for everything - walking, bathing, sleeping, eating, oh and of course fire and water and earth and farming I guess as well. There's a skill for every weapon type such as axes and swords and lances, and there's a skill for love. If you like seeing numbers go up, you like leveling up, or you like constant reinforcement, you're going to like this game a lot. Because there's plenty of that and it's fun.There's not just farming you can do - there's an entire combat system that's pretty robust and enough moves and weapons to keep you from getting bored long. I struggled with the camera at times but it's generally pretty intuitive with the lock-on system and enemies spawning in front of you on the field so there's no surprises and you can usually just run away. The main story of the game is basically dungeon diving and doing that to push the main narrative forward in between letting your plants grow. Unfortunately, most of the dialogue made me laugh in an unintentional way and the story is not great. The characters are really sweet and pretty likable though even if they don't have a huge amount of depth to them.If you get sick of fighting yourself, you can actually capture monsters and let them fight alongside you. Or, you can let them stay in their barn and receive brushes and gifts from you on a daily basis. If you grow friendly enough, they will perform some farm work for you in the game's additional farm plots not connected to the main one. I enjoyed this a lot and there's plenty of enemy variety to capture that each give their own animal products (e.g. fleece or milk) and have their own combat moves and stats. One of my favorite features, however, is that you can take up to three townsfolk with you and they will follow you around town and fight for you whilst gaining relationship points though. Eventually I had a legion of ladies with matching bows and shields I crafted myself to vanquish enemies for me.If you get bored of all that, it's recommended you give gifts to townsfolk and converse with them often. I found this part of the game frustratingly a bit of Guide Dang It material because there's so many characters and each villager has their own gift likes/dislikes and they're generally more expensive to have in the early-mid game. There's not a huge indication as to whether you gave a villager a liked/loved gift (though there is one) so one must be exceptionally good at note taking and paying attention to pick up on the villagers' hints about their favorite gifts and remember it all, including whether or not you gave a villager a gift that day or not. (Though there is a mod for that, I have yet to get it working for myself.) While villagers do mention their favorites when you gift items usually, they have an extensive list of items they will also accept. If you hate looking stuff up be wary of that - however I ended up happily playing the game with a handy visual guide I found on reddit because the community is pretty awesome.I haven't played other games in the series so take this with a grain of salt. My understanding is that most long-time fans favor earlier entries, especially 4, over this game and I can't comment on that at this time but as a new fan of the series I am having a great time. I may update my review later because this game made me want to play the others in the series when I am done with it, which is a high compliment from me.This game is a "just one more day" type of game where you will find yourself awake in the middle of the night with bleary red eyes wanting to keep going. There are some weird quirks about the game, though, such as furniture placement sucking and the furniture having to be placed like 3 feet from the wall for some reason. Luckily, there are mods to fix this and I hope the mod scene for it grows. A recommended mod is  which is a pretty simple mod that fixes a lot of small things including adding ultrawide and 16:9 support and a nice intro/logo skip. Once you've seen the intro a few times, install this and the game will look and run better.This is not a cheap game but if you enjoy progression you will certainly get your money's worth of hours out of it. It does go on sale sometimes though, so if you're paying $30-40 (USD) for it I'd say that's an exceptional value which is about what I paid and I don't regret it because I'm looking forward to the next festival minigame right now, among the dozens of other things I could be doing.If you have a moment, check out my curator  (formerly known as CheapEasyGood100) for more recommendations of cute games like this!

_childDocuments_.review: After being put off by the abysmal performance issues in the switch release (a great sign for the series' "breath of fresh air" installation), I finally mustered up the willpower to try out the Steam release. I wish I hadn't. I wish I'd stayed blissfully unaware. I love Rune Factory, and I wish this game was better. Every single aspect of this game feels like it was handcrafted to make gameplay as slow, sloppy, and bland as possible. The player character never comes to a clean stop, pitching and sliding across the ground as they switch from, say, running to filling up the watering can. At the same line, the removal of the jump mechanic from previous 3D installations adds a strange heaviness and restriction to movement (want to take a shortcut from one building to another? Well if those two buildings are separated by too steep of a hill, you can ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ forget it!). The game clock has been slowed down for the first time in the series, which I was willing to forgive at first as a concession to the world's grand new scope- expect you're still waiting around for the slow-ass characters to meander to their desks so you can get literally anything done. Hell, even the dash mechanic is slow, moving the player character an almost comical 3 inches forward while frozen a static crouch pose. Not that this mechanic needs to cover much ground anymore, anyway: early game combat is pathetically easy, with monsters that just kinda stand around and look at you until they decide, oh yeah, they're actually supposed to attack.What I've seen of the new mechanic(s) is just... yeesh. The new monster taming system, clearly intended to add more dynamic action or charm to the "brush and dodge" rhythm of the prior installations, is agonizingly boring. Monsters shuffle periodically from side to side until the recharge meter mercifully fills up, and you can fling a beam of light that will net you the failure reaction a few dozen times before the game shows you pity. And yet, the fact that the capture spell need to recharge at all is, I'm sure, another desperate attempt of the developers to prevent you from burning through the bare bones objectives of the early game, lest you realize that all of your work will be done by 2pm every in-game day. Rather than actually enjoying the experience of living in Whatever The Town's Name Was, I frequently found myself bumming around SEED headquarters, plants watered, quests completed, and daily convos exhausted, trying to fight the urge just to accept defeat and skip to the next day."Maybe I'll go fishing or grind some weapon skills to pass the time." 'To pass the time'? I'm playing a video game! This *is* the time waster!!!!The character animations themselves are... just awful. The choreography of the events are so stilted and strange, where models spin and wobble on a dime as they turn about to look maybe not "at" each other, but in the approximate direction of the other party's face. All movement from walking to running is janky and slow, showing a lack of polish that's almost insulting. If someone with the technical knowledge were able to even out the graphical details of two cutscenes from RF5 and, say, Tides of Destiny, and show them to a stranger who had never seen either game before, there is *no* way that person would be able to accurately guess which game released over a decade prior. (And the *walking*. Gah, what the hell is up with the walking? I have never seen such deliberate, high-knee, janky robot steps in a game before. It's awful! We've already figured out walking in 3D games! What happened!!!!)I'm realizing that I haven't even talked about the townspeople themselves... the worst part is that I actually kinda liked them! RF5 has clearly repeated the dating roster quality of 4, with a decent selection of interesting guys and gals for you to get along with (minus one glaring exception for each game). Even before I knew just how much of a slog this experience would be, I was already looking froward to romancing a few different options in separate saves.... ahh well. Fat chance of me getting through this game more than once.And the story itself is downright aggressive in how little it wants to build. With all the preamble of a flash flood, you wake up with amnesia, and save a girl. Now you live in Rune Factory Town! I've never felt less endeared to an entry to this series. I've never felt less interested in learning more. I've said it a million times in this review, but it's just. so. *Sad*.After *checks notes* 9 agonizing hours, I'm throwing in the towel. With wonky controls, a play system that is both insultingly easy and mindnumbingly dull, and a lingering feeling that I was still waiting for the game to start, even after I had long since left the prologue, RF5 simply is not delivering the quality of its predecessors, both direct (with 4), and in spirit (with 3D Oceans/Tides of Destiny). Since I let my hopes blind my common sense, I won't be getting a refund on this particular bad investment. But know this: I continue to slog through this experience with a heavy heart for what could've been... and an open eye on the game's modding community.The absolute best part of Rune Factory 5 is that it gives us a glimmer of hope for RF6. Reviews seem to be high, and other people are having fun. So, even though I stand by my opinion that this is a disappointing mess of wasted potential... maybe it'll do something good for me in the long run.(But even if you disregard this one review, please promise me this: do not buy this game at full price. It is, and the high of it's enjoyment levels, a $20 game at best. Good luck!)

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some serious problems that need to be addressed first. 1) It has difficulties detecting the resolutions available if you have more than one monitors that support different resolutions. In my case I have a 1440p and a 1080p monitor connected. For some reason it will default to my lower spec monitor and will not let me select resolutions that should be available for my main one. I had to resort to some shenanigans to fix that.2) It has problems with many controllers. Personally I use a PS4 controller with only the steam drivers. It gave me some serious trouble to have the game recognize it while every other game I have of the last 5 years have no problems at all with it.3) Many people have reported they have problems with in game menus or cinematics not displaying correctly. Personally I did not face this problem though.4) The game often crashes at loading screens. The game remains responsive during that time, with music playing and you can push buttons and see the tips on screen changing. but it never leaves the loading screen. Your only option is to close the game and restart. This means that if you haven't saved recently you lose all progress. This is a problem that existed in the switch version as well. 5) The game screams from miles away that it is a sloppy mess. I do not expect a triple A game from this company but for 60 euroes I would certainly expect these issues to have been resolved before becoming available for sale.At the moment of my review I have about 11 hours on it. A big chunk of that time was wasted redoing things and reclaiming progress I lost after I had the game crash at a loading screen and this is driving me insane. Unfortunately I am well beyond the 2 hour limit in playing time I had in order to ask for a refund since I was hoping that they would do something about it. Instead there is no feedback at all from the developers. To make the long story short my main complaints have to do with technical problems and the stupidly high price tag it has for what it offers. It might be worth your time if they fix those bugs and make it available at a better price but as it is right now you 'd better stay away.Edit 21/07/2022: It appears that the crashes at loading screen are related to the "Shadows Distance" and "Drawing Distance" settings. In my case I had those set at the "Long" setting. Reverting them back to "Default" fixed the crashes for some reason. Admittedly I did a reinstall of the game so that might also be related. Still given the overall condition and quality of the game I do believe that asking 60€ for it is too much. Hence I will maintain my "Not recommended" stance. Should the price change to something more reasonable though I would probably reconsider it.
