_childDocuments_.review: A very good solid entrance for rune factory. I only have a few nit picky problems. The story and pacing are garbage. And by the time you get to endgame, you'll get into more high tier crafting but it utterly destorys the balance. My character is about level 200~, and I used the extra directives to increase the levels of the enemies to the point that the end game dungeon has about lvl 800 enemies. They don't do damage to me but now require a decent amount of swings to kill. So it kinda makes the ultimate crafts and ultimate tier upgrading as completely useless. There's no point to it.And then the pacing of the story is far too quick with a rather simple and unforfilling story that doesn't even answer everything. And unless you pace yourself and make the dungeons and story a backburner effort, you will certainly find yourself finishing the game before you can even date someone. I put in about 180 hours according to steam and I havn't gotten to year 2 even. I have finished the game, utterly destroyed the postgame dungeon, maxed out forging, crafting, cooking, and chemistry to 99. And I finally got married after grinding that out. Now, the romantic option I went with was the last one to be introduced so it was going to take longer but I pretty much got everything out of this game to a satisfactory point and I still havn't gotten children yet. So that is my complaint with pacing, in that friendships and romance/marriage is really long to do and I had plowed through everyone thing easily in the meantime.And it really does suck that the game makes your 'home' the second floor bunking area of SEED. You get to expand it and all but you can't move the beds and its just so restricting. The placement of furniture is HORRIBLE. (Thankfully, there are mods on the PC that can fix this for you).But I do recommend this game so let's talk about the good. It's rune factory. The farming is good. It's awesome to figure out cash crops and go out and adventure for items to upgrade your gear with. You will work on leveling up your crops so you can make more money. And then when you get farm dungeons you can use the crystals to get more space to farm and even raise the quality of crops, health of the soil, etc. Capture monsters, befriend them, get their products while they help you water and harvest the crops on the farm. Level them up if you want adventuring buddies.Leveling up your skills rewards you with better gear and better ways to upgrade stuff. If you ever have an issue or a problem with an aspect, you can always upgrade your gear to deal with it. And even cook food that'll give you a buff to deal with it. Chemistry basically superpowers your farm once you learn how to craft chemicals and revitalize and keep your farm and crops healthy.The characters are interesting. Though I feel a good number of the male romance options are boring, imo. (Maybe cause I'm a guy. Eh.) The town and character events are interesting and provide alot of character and depth to most of the characters.It's a good game besides the nitpicky problems with the game's pacing and story, it's a solid entry. and certainly worth the 60$ for the 180 hours I spent on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 5, by developer Marvelous Inc. and publisher XSEED Games, is a farming-dating-fighting simulation. Initially released for Nintendo Switch in 2021, it is now available for download for PC via Steam.TutorialsThis was my first foray into the Rune Factory universe, which was perfect because it meant I had a lot in common with the main protagonist, a mysterious amnesiac hero-type who appears in the woods outside of Rigbarth just in time to save a local girl from some fuzzy sheep monsters.Thankfully, the game is set up for first-timers and amnesiacs and features an extensive tutorial at the beginning of the game. And when I say extensive, I mean extensive. Organized as “missions” for the local townsfolk, the tutorial takes between 3-5 hours of gameplay. That is 3-5 hours just to open up the early areas of the world and start dungeon crawling. Even the first fighting adventure the player goes on is still part of the tutorial since it focuses on teaching the player how to fight using the “dash” feature. The tutorial can feel like dragging the player along, for example, when you get asked to buy a bowl of rice to familiarize yourself with the different shop features.Still, the truth is, there is a ton for the player to do, and having the tutorial to hold your hand when you’re learning the system is really helpful for a first-timer. I think anyone already familiar with the Rune Factory franchise might find it a little tiresome. Also, since the tutorial is built into the game plot, there is no way to skip it. Personally, I think a gamer would have to absolutely love this game to want to do a second playthrough and go through the opening sequences again.Even with the extensive tutorial, players will still need to consult online resources to figure some things out. For example, after learning how to schedule a Cooking Festival with strange talking head Eliza, I could not figure out how to cook anything until I looked outside the game for an answer. I learned that my level was too low to have learned any recipes, but there were still ways for me to continue participating in the festival. There is a huge fan following for this series, so if you ever get stuck, there are plenty of tutorials to help players get unstuck. (Like the fact you have to talk to the shopkeeper Terry THREE times before his shop menu comes up!)FarmingThis game is definitely farming-forward. The player learns how to hoe and plant a field from the beginning. Farming can be as straightforward or complicated as a player chooses to make it. I could just do the basics, or I could track weather, analyze soil composition and make elaborate spreadsheets about the best times in the game to plant turnips or toyherbs. While farming is the most detailed aspect of Rune Factory 5, I really liked that the game allows the player to choose how much energy to invest in the farming systems.FightingFighting almost feels like an afterthought for this game, especially when compared to farming.The controls are basic but a little clunky. Players should rely on the “lock-on” feature, or an attack can miss an enemy. Interestingly the game forces the player to put equal time into grinding levels as into forging new weapons/armor. I got to a point where it didn’t matter how strong my attack was; if I got hit by an enemy, it would hurt. Same with weapons. If I didn’t keep my weapons updated, then it didn’t really matter how strong I was, my attack damage would be less, and I would find myself in trouble.Rather than being frustrating, I found this really enjoyable. It forced me to put all that tutorial knowledge to good use. I never found myself seriously struggling to finish a dungeon or fight a boss. DatingDating in the game is pretty straightforward. There are characters the player can build up a relationship with to act as a companion to dungeon crawl with (my favorite kind of date) or to even marry. I was delighted to see that RF5 had the same relationship options whether you played as the boy hero or the female hero. This is a better show of support for LGBTQAI+ than slapping a rainbow on a backpack.I didn’t put much effort into the dating system, mostly because I was too busy farming. Still, I have my eye on Murakumo, and I will continue my slow seduction of him by giving him some grass every day.ControlsProbably the worst thing about this game is the controls. It’s evident from the start that this was made to be played on a console. Button mapping seems a little haphazard and redundant. There are different buttons to hold a farm tool/gift/weapon than there are to equip it, and there are two buttons a player can push to stash items in their bag. (Why not one button to equip and one button to stash?!) Thankfully, the game continually prompts players with the button they need to press, so I didn’t need to really memorize how to open up the three different menus.For some reason, the developers included two cursors…but only on some screens…and only one of them is needed to click. I don’t know why, but it’s weird.ConclusionOverall, I had a lot of fun playing this game. Its slow pace and opportunities to obsess make it a lovely place to escape when the real world gets a little too real.And I’m going to call it a day.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game. Some 'clean up'/polish I think the developers could have done but overall a decent story and no one dies that you really love / care about which is an improvement to RF4.Note to Developers: Don't only let players access + bread post game and if you do then do not make the post game bread + crap worse than the previous version / chest version of the items. (Ie the farm tools....). It is disappointing to unlock new farm tool recipes post game and then find out they are worse than the ones you got near end game. I get people can cheat and look up the recipes ahead of time and craft them but that shouldn't be the intention of the game right? Another quality of life element is to make the furniture actually be able to be lined up to the wall and other furniture. Additionally; allow some more customization of the character and clothes options. And allow people to deselect what clothes your party wears and choose the armor and such. NPC kept changing to previously given armor back and forth (especially the headgear). So I had a character I liked kept going back to being pumpkin head because that was a good armor piece early game. I know late game you get the option to take back all headgear given but it'd be a nice quality of life just being able to change their armor in the menu screen yourself. Finally: the drop rates S U C K in this game for item stuff. I am not trying to make the bestest of best stuff (though I think theres too many options) but I got to a point end game where I can't make annnything and of course it isn't purchasable because Heinz just has a tiny rotational stock where something 'might' be there or not and its really not. I can't tell you how many times I sat there trying to kill something over and over and over again. I am not even trying to 100% make everything. Just needed a decent weapon to get to floor 10 in the endgame dungeon but me and party doing crap damage because our weapons are too low. And those 1 -shotting ghosts on floor 9... could have been explained how to avoid that. I read online about the feint stuff but some helpful hints by the floor door or something but it probably would have required another rare drop. I like game grinds dont get me wrong but you overdid it. Looking forward to Rune Factory 6!

My original review did not sit well with me.At first I wasn´t sure if I should buy Rune Factory 5.I am a fan of this series but... the video´s I saw in youtube and the comments here made it hart for me to make a decision.But I read that Mister Yoshifumi Hashimoto and X-Seed etc worked on the game, so I gave it a try.You have to empty yourself from the impression of Rune factory 4 special.Why because the animation here is completly different and you have to get used to this new style.Just like in Rune factory 4 you can do everything on your own personal feelings and speed.There a "turtorials" that explain things to you and you can read more on signboards.And yes there a things like (for me) "dating how to do it" that is not explained like in rune factory 4 too laugh.It took me 4 years (gametime) to find it out myself^^ but I find it good that there a things you yourself have to find out on your own^^There are some ppl who wish it would have looked like "Harvestella", I can understand it but those two games have different styles. So to say this game is not worth buying is a bit over reacting?You have to find out it yourself^^ We all have a different taste and understand the word "animation" different too and that is good!Let me tell you what I mean with "animation" here in rune factory 5 it is like you open an colorfull manga.There are so many details in so many different way´s that I am often not sure if I overlooked it the last time or did it change because a year was over. Or did this building change it appearance after I invested in it or is it me who overlooked some details. Hope you can find the love that was puted in this game too^^.Of course if you are not used to: "me free decision, oh god what to do... what to do!" and react in: "running around in circles" than this game will be bored and frustrating. But if you can overcome it and give the relaxing village a chance who is almost forgotten^^ you can find a gameplay that is almost same as in rune factory 4 with more details a bigger barn for boss monster (me happy).Only difference is, that it seems the dev had a time limit and couldn´t do everything they wanted.Gameplay: You play a male or girl in an open rpg world, tame monsters, do farming, crafting, find love (this time you don´t have to beat the game bevore you can marry as a girl a girl etc.), friends and protect what is dear to you. Find some secrets the villager have soon or later after you make your own cute kids.^^Extra: There a lots of clothings if you buy the dlc and later to buy from npc´s too, if you played rune factory 4 special there is a special costume for you!The Intro has a little suprise for you after you played to a certain point in the story line.Some conservation are voiced its cute^^I am happy that it is only a part voiced moment because I like to read and you should really read the explanation.^^ Will make it easier to catch crystals and objects in the trees^^New funktion: The day is longer than in rune factory 4 that is a bliss for me.^^who else hand up^^And there is a how do you call it... you can pick up stuff more easily almost like automatic pick up.Its a bit hard to benefit from it as a keyboard player but if you are like me you will find a way, wink.There are tons of adjustment you can do when you first start the game and later on over the save book.For your own pc you can make the decision for all settings!You can play with controller and keyboard too and german language is there (jahhuuu)Now try it out yourself and if you like search for some pictures.One thing is bothering me and other player ist... arranging the furniture you get... in rune factory 4 I could put them on the wall (almost) here... lets say I can play hide and seek^^but you can turn the furniture in every position that wasn´t possible in rune factory 4. I had the idea with open kitchen and putting some on my land is has style too^^ Thx for this nice game, I am curious how it will unfold and thx for all the dlc´s.Greetings a fan

_childDocuments_.review: Rune Factory 5 does hold most of the same mechanics as rune Factory 4 - and is complete with the usual amnesiac character waking up outside of a town.The transition from 2D to 3D isn't exactly the smoothest; the environments are a little bit too flat, and the performance suffers at points - but I think ultimately it's still a very good farming Sim. If you can get past the 3D portrayal, you're effectively looking at more of the same fun stuff from Rune Factory 4, though now with the addition of same-sex relationships.If you liked Rune Factory 4, you'll like 5 - it just takes a little bit of getting into.They also finally added a proper event tracker, which was my only complaint with Rune Factory 4, so it has iterated in some ways!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for 60 dollars at launch on the switch but I thought that it was so violently awful that I had to get it on steam just to write this review. I will be asking for a refund promptly after submitting this review.I would not pay money for this game, ever. Compared to its predecessor, RF4, which is one of my favorite games, RF5 is the very definition of "one step forward, two steps back" (but it should really be "five steps back" in this case). What I mean to say is that although there are many small QoL improvements they are vastly overshadowed by significant flaws in graphics, gameplay, and overall feel.Let's examine some of these claims in more detail. For one of the small improvements, we can note that switching items is significantly easier on controller/console due to certain macros they added, which helps the flow of the game a bit. But as stated before, this comes with many steps back. There is a significant amount of lag when pulling out or switching items that just makes it feel sluggish to move around. This problem with flow is exacerbated by the load times and bloated town. One of the best things about RF4 is how compact the town was and how lightning quick the load times were. It was easy as pie to walk through Selphia, check all the shops, and talk to all the villagers to see their dialogue in 4 because you could walk from one corner of the town to the other in less than 30 seconds, load times included, and check everything out lightning fast. Compare to RF5, which despite being a graphical downgrade (more on that later) has incredibly bloated load times (esp on console) and a town which is incredibly empty and spread out for no reason. Not only does this make the town just look worse (Selphia is a very quaint little dense village, as opposed to the sparse, empty collage of stock houses in RF5), but it makes it annoying and time consuming to traverse the main area of the game. The load times are made even worse by the game's use of separate farming expansions on the backs of the dragons, which force you to sit through even more load times when going through and watering your crops for the day. Think of how different this is than RF4. In that game, it was fast to go through and water all your crops, which made sense because the genre is built around doing repetitive but quick tasks every day. RF5 requires you to sit through multiple long loading screens as you travel from farm to farm, and in between you get to use the incredibly clunky watering can to waste even more of your time.But before we get even more negative let's touch on what I would consider to be the only clear improvement that RF5 introduced. This is the addition of same-sex marriage in the western ports of the game, which I think was a long overdue feature that was sadly lacking in RF4S. I do not personally use this feature but I know that it meant a lot to many of the fans and am glad that this was added to them. One of the most annoying pieces of rhetoric surrounding this addition was from gamergate losers on the internet complaining about "oh what if the male candidates try to hit on me", completely ignoring that RF4 had an oversight wherein this actually happens despite same-sex marriage not existing in that game. Usually I would write this complaint up as nonsense, but the poor implementation of RF5's event system means that this complaint actually has some merit.Specifically, one of the bigger "steps forward" in RF5 was the improvements to the random event system, especially as it pertains to the romance events (which are mandatory prerequisites to marriage). IMO what was clearly the biggest flaw in RF4 was all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ soft resets you had to do to get the important events (i.e. the one that triggers act 3 and the romance events for your chosen partner). RF4S fixed the bigger issue with the act 3 event but still left the issues with the romance events in. Of course, despite the issues with random events, I would still be opposed to completely removing them because they add a lot of freshness to subsequent playthroughs (I know if I ever boot up RF4 again there will be some events I've never seen waiting to be triggered). This is why I really appreciated the attempt of RF5 to create a middle ground between preserving the freshness of random events while removing the frustration of attempting romance events. The way the system worked (at least at launch) is that once a romance event was available to be triggered, a heart icon appears on the map with the face of the character who the event is for below it. Moving within a certain radius of the character will then automatically trigger the romance event. The devs needed to go a step further and make it so the event only triggers when talking to the character in question or even explicitly having the choice to trigger the event or talk to them like normal when interacting with that character. There is a common issue where a romance event trigger point will be placed in an important spot, such as in the store where you buy seeds, so that you CANNOT enter that area without going into the event trigger radius, unless you trigger another one before entering (because two events cannot be active at once).Thus, players (myself included) are often basically forced to trigger romance events for characters they have no interest in due to them "blocking" points of interest. This is what I mean by the poor implementation of same-sex marriage; due to this, there are not 6 but 12 characters who trigger romance events! I was forced to activate a romance event for a male character who I naturally did not give a ♥♥♥♥ about. Not only was it frustrating to skip through all the dialogue for the event, but because the game was so unfinished at launch, I encountered a glitch that made it impossible to complete this event, which hard locked my save file into a scenario where I could not progress any of the romance lines and was the final thing that made me quit playing.I hate to bring this idea up again, but I think that this example is the strongest evidence of the "one step forward, two steps back" concept here -- the implementation of same-sex marriage should be an unambiguously good addition to the game, but the event system is so sloppy that it leads it to trip over itself and cause some issues.I'm pretty much done with my praise of this game for now so let's pick apart some more of the flaws. The graphics in this game look like ♥♥♥♥. RF4 was not particularly fancy with its graphics but there was a charming feel to its look that made it feel comfy and lived-in. Contrast to RF5 which has atrocious color design (everything is way way too saturated) and feels graphically empty, stale, and lifeless. The landscapes are just full of textures which look ripped from stock assets plastered over a mostly bare open world. There was really no reason to make the jump to 3d here considering that RF5 looks, handles, and performs worse than RF4 for the change.The combat system is also borderline unplayable. RF4 never had amazing combat by any means but it is fun enough that engaging with the amazing crafting system becomes fun. RF5 combat is so janky, slow, and clunky that I never felt motivated to play it which in turn harms the rest of the systems which are supposed to feed into it. The devs evidently realized how broken the spells were and tried to nerf them by giving them an unreasonable amount of endlag, but this is a poor balancing choice because it makes the game feel bad to play.It seems like most want to pretend that this game is not that bad but again I would NEVER spend money to play this game. RF5 should have never been released in the ugly, unoptimized, clunky, and unfinished state that it was. RF4 still exists as do many other games with more quality content than their dollar price. There is no reason to reward publishers for putting out this inferior, unfinished garbage when more worthy purchases exist.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely unpolished game. Crashed my system while playing for the brief period that I have played so far. Textures are of varying quality and makes the art style of the game very jarring. Autosaving happens too infrequently for game that is basically a time dump, so if the game does crash, you will potentially lose hours of progress because you can only save at specific locations. Combat feels okay, but the movement mechanics are awkward in general. Hair physics option causes awkward clipping and shaking that is also distracting. This game seems to have a lot of potential, so I might try to play at some other time, but I would definitely not recommend this game to anyone at its full purchase price. Very disappointed because I was hoping that the game would have evolved at least a little bit since the hiatus, but that does not appear to be the case.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is the first Rune Factory game I have played. After 12 hours into the game, this is why I give this game 1/5. First of all, THE BACHELORETTES.... They all look like still developing young teen girls, like maybe 14 or 15. When I first met Misasagi, the wolf milf, I was like, "Okay, now this is the type of wife I want". NOPE. No woman you meet in this game that is actually developed and looks old enough to marry and have kids with, is date-able or available to marry. You can only be friends with them, THE DEVELOPERS HAVE FRIEND ZONED ME. I think the developers purposely did this too, because Misasagi will say "Hey you should come get drinks with me and 2 of the hottest chicks in the game that can't be dated".... When compared to the bachelors in the game, its a complete joke. Pretty much all of the bachelors I have met (Except Cecil who looks like a literal kid) are developed and even look older then my main male character. So because of the poor choices of females for straight players, I am already taking 3 stars out, heck I'm just give it a straight 0 just because I can't date Misasagi. The GAMEPLAY: So this is one of the good things about the game. The game play is good, I like the hack and slash combat for adventuring and the farming. BUT there are some major annoyances, such as there being no alert sound or "flashy red health bar" mechanic to let you know you are about to die. There has been so many times I just die and I had no idea my health bar was low. What makes this worse, is that the enemies have no labels as to what level they are. In the first area in the woods, I went up the hill to the left which had high level enemies and killed me quickly. LABELS WOULD BE NICE. Like maybe label the areas to let the player know what has higher leveled enemies and what doesn't. Like the first wanted monster you have to kill at the beginning of the game, is pretty much un-killable until you get better weapons. Does the game tell you this? No.  In fact, the game pretty much never tells you anything. No sign or label when crops are done, just the same "inspect" arrow as everything else in the game. Doesn't tell you where ingredients or items needed for recipes drop. Doesn't tell you that some events only happen at a certain time of day. I have had to search online of what to do, many times so far... P.S. The main character will just SPAM you with voice lines while farming and when shopping at stores the character who is selling will just say "Take your time" every 5 seconds....The GRAPHICS: The terrain looks like as if they let the intern make it, LEGIT. The terrain looks AWFUL. 60$ game for terrain that looks like it was made by someone who is just learning Unity and I am playing on MAX GRAPHICS. The town is boring, pretty much no scenary except for trees that look like they are from a old 2000's anime mmorpg. The art for the characters and the 3D models of the characters are pretty much the only thing they focused on it seems. The BUGS: Yeah, I saw reviews saying this was a good port for steam, HA. I have many times where my camera is on crack just fidgeting up and down for no reason at all. My tools or weapons while running the animation will glitch. The characters of the game don't even know what is happening in the game half the time. One of the quests of the main story is to wait for a character to wake up because she is in bed from being injured. I go outside and she is WALKING AROUND. I talk to other characters and they all talk about how they can't wait for the WALKING AROUND character to wake up from being injured in bed. So things like this really destroy immersion. But you know, as mad as I am that I can't date misasagi or just have a wife who doesn't look like a developing 14 year old, I still am enjoying the gameplay aspect of the game. Hopefully they add some patches to fix some of the bugs in the game. Hopefully the developers don't screw over the straight weebs next time in their next game, can I please just have an attractive developed wife at least without feeling like a pedo? Thanks.UPDATE: I have poured more hours into the game, and have unlocked the final bachelorette Ludmila, she is the only date-able female in this game that looks developed, so shes the only reason I am still playing now. Also I have noticed the AI in this game is terrible, characters will just repeat the same stuff over and over to you. _childDocuments_.review: as someone who played a lot of rune factory 1, i was excited to get my hands on this, but the balancing is a joke.i was confused to find a random mix of extremely high level enemies and extremely low level enemies in the open fields, monsters who hit for 0 barely 10 meters away from monsters that can kill you instantly, and the low level monsters dropping stupidly high level items that makes farming obsolete in terms of food and profit. why spend days farming for a few thousand gold when you could go out there and one shot something that drops food that restores 40k health and 10k stamina, and sells for nearly 8k, with a fairly high drop rate?when you fight (or avoid) your way through a massive army of high level monsters to reach a dungeon, you find the monsters in the dungeon are only the weakest enemies in the region, making the only threat in the dungeon traps, which are easily avoided with your dodge which has invincibility frames that can actually destroy some traps, and most monsters can easily be stunlocked with the basic combo of any melee weapon, so even something extremely dangerous becomes harmless if you can fight it 1 on 1. the only thing you cant stunlock is the dungeon bosses, which are so slow and telegraphed, you can easily avoid their attacks without the dodge invincibility.the overall story progression seems to be based on time, with each new dungeon/quest being unlocked a week or so after the last, leaving you with very little to do as far as story/quests go. even relationship quests seem to have a cooldown, so you cant even hang out with people during your down time outside of saying hi and getting a generic response in return.the wanted monsters are kind of a joke, being just an ordinary monster with increased stats. using the throw attack of gloves i was able to get past the insanely high defense and capture all 4 star wanted monsters shortly after the third dungeon opened.crafting seems fairly awkward, to learn a recipe you either craft it through either blind luck or knowing the recipe by heart (ie pickled turnip and all sashimi are only 1 ingredient) or learn it randomly by eating magical recipe bread, assuming you already have the tool/craft skill needed to craft it, so you cant learn anything to look forward to crafting later on. you can only buy 2 recipe bread per day at the bakery, and an extra cooking recipe bread at the restaurant if you dont mind paying extra, adding extra limits to crafting, in addition to needing to take a quiz on crafting before you're allowed to buy each crafting stations.taming is a really awkward process. for the most part i forgot that throwing items was a thing, i accidentally picked up a rock, so i threw it at a high level panther, instead of damaging the monster, it tamed it, and for a while i had a powerful ally who slaughtered most of the monsters i encountered, until its health finally dropped to 0. after some struggling i managed to figure out how to banish it back to the first forest, as i felt it inhumane to keep a dying pet i could not feed. while its nothing major, i do find it awkward throwing a rock at something's head is the key to taming it, and far too easy when you could accidentally tame something several levels higher than you, where the first game taming was a risk, getting in close with a glove to pet the monster repeatedly as it tries to bite your face off, and being rewarded with a weak pet that grows along side you.i do like the characters, despite how cliche or predictable they are. it brings a smile seeing the children having their fights, the buff wolf who forgets his own strength, the dog always questing for the shiniest sparkly treasure, or the boy detective always on the lookout for the next big case. its a shame you cant spend more time watching their stories play out.overall, i find myself having too much time on my hands while waiting for quests and social interactions, with no motivation to invest extra time into farming or crafting, as im already looting items that restore over 100 times my stats and equipment that far outweigh what i can make after eating all the bread i can find, and im barely able to find enough fertilizer to maintain my farm.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so this is my first entry in the series, and i cant rate it well, if i could rate it as a mixed experience that would be ideal, I dont fault the game for the things i dont personally like, but rather, the things that make it less accessible to people who dont get on well with video games, even though they want to play them.I probably barely scratched the surface on 5 but giving it a good shot for a few hours and always at the point of "what now" constantly thinking loads of small life improvement things could be better, I understand the inventory system, most the farming system, but from the start its never the clearest thing as a new player, everything seems like an extra step, and that extra step diverts your attention not keeping you in the zone so to speak, take care of plants one day and then quest the next, you can get into a routine, but still it just seems to not be an inviting game.Overall i think my main issue is it does not know how to pace itself, go sleep wake up see what x and y is doing then probably improve your relationship with others, but it all seems a bit too slow and dragged on a bit too much, gift things to x y or z every day and try and get a friendship level that whilst not difficult, again just seems like an extra step more than it should be.If that does not seem to bother you, its okay, a bit too simple in some regards, but in my experience never a relaxing one, just a forgettable one where i can do things, but it does not feel like i have had an impact.I dont regret my purchase, as i did get it on sale and hey, if you just want the switch game without the bugs then at least it works on the deck, and ill likely come back to it when brain empty, but as it stands, It just does not pull me in as i would like it to.

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much a Rune Factory game. The characters are delightfully wacky. I would like to like it. While the port isn't awful, it also isn't great. The controls are iffy. The auto-targetting function has a tendency to pick the wrong thing. While there is a system to manually select your target, it is only slightly less annoying to use than the bad auto-targeting since it takes camera control and limits movement. Throwing has a tendency to sail over whatever you are throwing at (due to 3d object tracking) unless you explicitely lock on to it and give up camera control.I've yet to find any good way to quickly get stuff out of inventory to give as gifts, which is a real problem in a game where you usually give half a dozen or more gifts to villagers a day. Trying to scroll left/right for any distance in the "quick" inventory select screen tends to result in scrolling up/down instead and losing your place. The previous game avoided this by putting up/down and left/right on different gamepad elements and it's a real shame that behavior was not kept.

I wish you could at least set your preferences for the characters (female/male MC, straight/bi/gay, gender neutral), as the forced gender-neutral responses make the romances very forced and the characters fall for you no matter what you do. Plot was overall fine, but I was able to beat the game by mid-autumn on the first year while RF4 took me 3 in game years. Story was fine, but you honestly don't learn anything  It makes the game plot feel incomplete and unfulfilling. Guess you just live out your days farming away and maybe getting married with a character that treats you like a friend after marriage.The game is very bland in terms of looks, it's as if you imported it straight from the Wii era, which is disappointing for a game that came out in 2022. This probably looks great on the Switch, but definitely not PC.Obviously I played it for over 100 hours, but I would only get an RF6 (if RF3 Special gets enough attention, which it probably won't due to there being only a male MC and only bachelorette options) if it actually had the same level of charm and soul as RF4.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the worst PC port for a game I've ever seen, and I'm usually quite lenient on ports. The struggles are so bad, I'm giving it a rare review of NOT RECOMMENDED (unless you want to use keyboard and mouse). IF YOU WANT TO USE A CONTROLLER, use a switch pro controller. Others likely will not work. Whether by the "native" support it claims to have or by Steam input, an xbox controller will not function. It either doesn't register any input at all, or it has a blank mapping for controls and will not accept any modification. Using many different workarounds, I managed to make my xbox elite controller work one time. The next time I booted the game, it didn't function at all. No settings changes in any fashion. I even had to use third party fixes to make it show controller buttons on the screen since the option to show controller buttons still showed keyboard controls.IT WORKS ON STEAM DECK, after some modding. Quite well actually! I did have to follow the guide to add ProtonGE and make it use that, otherwise the visuals wouldn't show. And again, I had to use the third party fix for it to display buttons instead of keyboard controls. (These fixes still don't allow a bluetooth controller to work, so playing it on the dock is not an option.) The game does run well otherwise, and the controls with the Steam Deck after modification are rather nice and smooth.AS FOR THE GAME ITSELF, it is honestly pretty fun once you can play it. The RP (energy/mana) system is a little clunky and annoying in how limiting it is. Money is decently easy to obtain and the game gives you all of the starting tools via requests/quests. The monster taming is fun, though I don't fully understand it quite yet. The barn system for taming feels a little limiting, but i'm not too far into the game.

The sell/buy prices need to be better balanced, some sell prices are so low for what the buy price is that it makes starting the game AND starting the game with no knowledge extremely difficult. At least the sell prices should be raised to around half the buy price in MOST instances some items sell-buy price ratio is fine.2. the player should not get stunned for 3 seconds they SHOULD stumble (about .33 seconds of stun, though near or below .5 seconds should be far better) as the player should not be punished for something they can not control. There should also be stunning immunity so the player can't get stunned then stunned again immediately. For clarity the "stumble" should be equal to or less than .5 seconds and the fall should be near or under 1 full second.3. the stack size is too small (9) it should be raised to either 18 or 27, of course it will need to be properly play tested to tell if 18 is perfect or if it should be raised higher.\4. TREES, specifically their leafs. Trees like the center plaza tree type should have loose blobs or groupings of leafs to look more pleasing to the eye not the panels they have at time of writing. The way the spruce-like tree leafs look is fine as is.5.The player should be told that the rocks, twigs and such CAN destroy crops. The voice acting not being done for the full text line always, is very odd as having full voice acting is expensive but brings more life to the characters were no voice acting can allow a game designer to put more money into making a better feeling better looking game.7. _childDocuments_.review: RF5 is another entry in the Rune Factory series. If you've played one before and liked it this one will do, if you didn't then I don't think they did anything here to move the needle for you. If you haven't played a Rune Factory but have liked other farming RPGs like Story of Seasons (called Harvest Moon in the West before 2013), or Stardew Valley and wanted one with more RPG mechanics (dungeon crawling, leveling crafting skills, etc) then this is the series for you.I've devoured RFs 2-4 on the DS and 3DS respectively and overall I feel like RF5 is just.. fine? It fixes a lot of the issues I had with RF4 (so much progression tied to RNG , less miserable post-game dungeon) but it really feels like the first numbered entry to be using the behind-the-back 3D perspective in a lot of other ways. So many of the scenes happening are still primarily shown through the 2D portraits while the 3D models get extremely limited motion (ie, calling someone out for their legs shaking because they are scared but their model is perfectly still, faces being expressionless while the portraits emote, some animations don't properly loop such as running with a long sword out you can see the animation screw up and move the sword around weirdly, etc).I'm hopeful for RF6 and the Project Dragon spinoff because there is so much room to grow here. I like the idea of 3D RF and the basic combat still works well here, but there are a lot of little annoyances that should really get sanded off. Bosses shouldn't suddenly stop taking damage with no visual cues for when they stop taking damage and when they are hittable again (and honestly just get rid of that mechanic) for example. I like how they seemed to learn that making the post-credits dungeon as much of a slog as RF4s was a bad idea, but they also gave you 0 payoff for making it through it here. Having so many of the only events to hang out with people and learn more about them and the town be "romance events" is a bad idea and is probably part of why the marriage and dating events are so rare of achievements on Steam, you don't really want to block off the other events because they are where most of the interactions actually are. I'd love to see a follow up where the visuals don't break (the shadows are really something else), locking up your character isn't as easy as changing what spell you have equipped mid-cast animation, and you can't ruin a run by accidentally slamming an enemy you need to kill out of bounds.For me, RF5 doesn't dethrone RF2 at the top of the series but it's just fine along the others, flawed but enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I am having a hard time understanding the positive reviews. This game is extremely clunky with unintuitive controls. I last played Rune Factory 3 so I'm not new to the overall game or its offshoots but I'm somehow at a loss of what to do each day. Picking up items requires repetitive key mashing, placing furniture is willynilly with no grid, in order to shop you have to go through a conversation dialogue, farming feels awkward because of the UI, controls, and camera angle. I do one task and then save and quit. Where as usually in a farming sim there's so much to do the first time you pick it up you'll finish a week plus of game days, I've had this for a week and played 2 game days. I'm crawling through, trying to get my money's worth, but I would strongly suggest not buying this.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. I'm at the start of summer and apparently I'm almost finished with the story. The combat is easy, but I'm having difficulty keeping my crafting skills up in accordance with the story progression. So by the start of summer when I have gold and other materials I'm still using only the 2nd tier of farming materials. The pacing of this feels very off.The characters themselves are, mostly likeable. Although there are some individuals where you go "I can't date them really?"Honestly after playing RF4 and then this one I kind of think this game pails in most comparisons. I would not pay full price for this, maybe $20-$30.Update 8/9/2022: Put an extra 10 hours in this game, on Summer 12 and I'm at the final dungeon and I can't bring myself to care about this game. I could have finished the story within the first 10 days of Summer in Year 1. Considering how easy this is in comparison to how grindy it is to increase your crafting levels, unless you find or are gifted items you likely will not be updating your equipment in comparison to your progression. I haven't even unlocked most of the seeds because they are hidden behind requests and I don't get them fast enough in comparison to how far I am in the game. Flower seeds have to be found via hidden locations that you need a crest for, or a companion creature who can search, and you need to ship those seeds once before you unlock them in the shop. So it's not guaranteed that you will find these seeds and flowers to unlock them.I still can't recommend this game for it's full price. I'd say max I'd spend is still $25 on this. This is one of the biggest disappointments I've had when it comes to a farm sim in some time. I wanted to like this game like I did Rune Factory 4.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Rune Factory game and I had higher expectations for the 5th game in the series, and sadly these expectations are not met.  Both the farm simulation and battle system feel like amateur attempts to imitate something better than what they are, while the quality of the story and cutscenes utterly fall flat what I consider a professional product.  Lastly, the control scheme is rather horrendous where it took way too many button presses to do anything other than moving around your character.
_childDocuments_.name: Rune Factory 5

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated game. Contrary to some other reviews I would say this is a GOOD game to play if you've never played Rune Factory before. It seems that most people who are dissatisfied with it are fans of the series. This is my first time playing a Rune Factory game and I'm really enjoying it.It takes a few hours to get into, but once you start doing missions and dungeons and getting into the swing of things, the gameplay loop is addictive. There are tons of quests, events, dungeons, and a basic story to follow. I haven't had any performance issues... No crashes and high FPS the whole time. The graphics are hit or miss, and the animations are glitchy at times. Combat is basic but fun. There's no character customization unfortunately, which is a negative. The voice acting is there and good, but it's only for a handful of dialogue lines. Also the music is good but way too repetitive, so it's best to get the item that lets you change the music in town. Overall this is like a mix between Harvest Moon and Ys, if you've played those. For me it was definitely worth the $30 on sale, I'm not sure if I would pay $50 for it. I'll probably end up with 100 hours in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have and always will love the RF series. I got RF5 on my switch. I could never get used to the camera angle. So, I stopped playing. I also didn't like the new 3D art style Marvelous decided to go with. It was off putting and made the game harder to digest as opposed to its usual AND nostalgic RF counterparts. And given the gap between RF4 and RF5, I'm more upset with how they chose to have more "underage" looking characters instead of having the bachelors/bachelorettes age with their audience. Safe to say I had high expectations for that alone because I was in a freshman in highschool when RF4 was released. I was disappointed back in 2022 during RF5's release because of how young the bachelors/bachelorettes looked. And the one they tried to look aged up, still had a baby face. Murakuma was an attempt! The camera angle, 3D artstyle, and young looking counterparts is why I stopped. However, this steam port has its own issues. The graphics are actually really bad. The blending wasn't there in full screen and it looked like there were moving waves and distorted colors every time and any time there was movement on the screen. (This doesn't happen on the steam deck). Another thing is the steam deck compatibility. Safe to say, it is "playable" as it says for the steam deck. Graphics will be considerably better, but the control are janky. The amount of times, I opened the map instead of inventory because those controls are what I'm used to was insane. Also the use of touchpads was not included. It's all joystick and control pad which is a shame because I find myself more apt to using the touch pad over reaching for the control pad on steamdeck as I have small hands. A small thiing to complain about, but it has to do with comfortability in terms of hand movements. I think string instrument players would understand what I mean by that LOLAs it stands, I don't think RF5 was a good port and as much as I want to look forward to RF6 and its spin off, I have low expectations. For me, a lot of a game has to do with art, but if the art isn't there, I tend to get bored easily. If you want a game with more mature bachelors/bachelorettes, look into Palia. Currently on switch and free. You can marry a widowed father aka DILF. Favorite bachelorettes are Kenyatta and Tamala. The one downside would be microtransactions for cute skins but they keep the skin shop out of mind out of site tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: It is an entertaining game and for that I would recommend this game, specially for fans of the previous game.For those people that are not fans, this is a monster catching game, where you can raise monsters and use them as battle companions. You also work in a farm for various reasons like creating recipes, potions and use as crafting items. Like Harvest Moon games, you can also marry one of many candidates if this floats your boat. The game has a mission objective, with simple dungeon crawling and bosses in order to beat the story. You have can customize your character with weapons, clothing and magic you can buy. It is an action RPG, first and foremost, but it's not as deep as your traditional JRPGs.The setting is pretty basic too. The houses in the town are too far apart for some reasons, and the design of everything is like it was made by a rookie designer. It just looks empty. Characters dialogue is basically unchanging and after the first two or three times reading the same thing you will just skip it. There are character events that happens sometimes, and these are enjoyable to witness, but they are very few. If not for the story and the other types of gameplay, this would make this game very boring (kinda reminds me of those Harvest Moon games released for the 3DS).Graphics are PS2 tier, and this is no joke, it's like this was a game developed for the 3DS and not PC or the Nintendo Switch (which this game is probably a port of). They characters are cel shaded but the environments looks from the PS2 era. I think this is like their second or third game in 3D, so I would expect a better work in their next iteration. Their 2D games were amazing when they were released.I don't remember lag on this game, which is something the Nintendo Switch was suffering from in some parts of the game.Something to point out, it that for some reason when playing this game with a controller, you won't be able to see the icons pertaining to the controller, but the keyboard. I don't know why that happens, but it is something to note. There's a mod for this, so just do a web search on this if you're interested. The mouse+keyboard combo works fine too.There's always discounts for this game, so I would wait for one. I bought the normal version, since as the posting date all of the DLCs are cosmetic. Between this game, Harvest Moon: Wind of Anthos and Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life (I think this is the latest and is the one I last played) I would recommend this game over the other two.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have never played Rune Factory before, what is wrong with you? I'm kidding. But seriously this has a little of everything. Instead of pixel graphics and chibi characters, you get a full character and a very pretty world to explore and run around. Not too far into the story yet, but for 30 hours of just doing as I do (farming and trying to get Murokumo to like me) it plays exactly how I expect it to. Steam Deck- This game plays just fine on the deck. I have had no issues playing on the system and actually prefer to play this way than on pc. My only grump are the pro buttons. I'm sure there is a way to remap this but I haven't bothered with it yet as its not much of an issue until I need to scratch my nose and end up yanking my fishing line out the water by accident.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good Rune factory game well deserve for a sequel.It's got a better or more easier farming mechanic from 4, at least that's how it felt when I played.When you shipped a crop you can buy it with the same stats from the shop.Battle's a bit clunky, but you'll get used to it. Not that this aims towards a hard core RPG anyway.Difficulty may not be much since its 3D and all, cause I just used Gatling comet to breeze through the game.If not GC i just used Earth spike for hit and run.The most major part in a rune factory game is your daily life.Honestly it was weird since everything was in 3D. Movements, Animations, attacks even farming were a fresh feeling.Never shy away in a life simulator game. New is always a great spice in your daily life.And finally we have the People in Rigbarth.I'll be honest, the people of Rigbarth takes a bit of time in getting them all.I mean look at the last person to join the town, she's basically past the second arc.Well in a relationship sense they are all nice but only a few maybe unique. Well if you compare them to 3 and that's too over the top.Likewise building a fresh event after event to your daily life in Rigbarth was handled pretty well.One of the major things unnoticeable for me was the tree system. Orange and apples are in trees(Duh, of course they are.).I meant they are hidden so well, It was at a later point did I even get to find out where they are.My last advice: Play while enjoying their company and have a heart full of patience.Whether it's a chore they give you or you need to stalk them until midnight.Even if the story is on a slow progress, Or the events won't pop out.Have the patience to blend into the game. If you play while giving everything a comparison, It won't be fun.Trust me, I did that too, since I compared it a lot from 4.

_childDocuments_.review: In the past I've always had a hard time getting into Rune Factory titles because they seemed so difficult to me. This game has fixed all of that in my opinion. The barrier of entry is much lower, making it friendlier to new players. It has the pretty art style and interesting storytelling that I was sorely missing in the newest Story of Seasons game, and the combat isn't too prohibitive even for someone like me, that generally plays more cozy games with little combat. The game still has a decent amount of complexity with crafting, upgrading, min maxing your equipment, etc, for those that like more of a challenge. Or if you want to focus more heavily on farming and just make weapons to ship for money, you can do that too. 50 hours in I've barely made it halfway through summer, there is tons of content in this game. An instant recommendation for fans of farming sims and RPGs alike! The main issues I have are these:The MC talks WAY too much. Every time you use a tool she has something to say about it.Upgrading the hammer to hit multiple rocks feels almost pointless when clearing around your fields, since if you use the charge you will probably destroy crops along with the rocks.Whoever decided it was a good idea for the game to rain confetti for 12 straight hours on festival days, really needs therapy. Luckily its only when you're in town and doesn't happen in dungeons but it still feels highly unnecessary, a small blurb that it's a festival day should suffice.

_childDocuments_.review: Took about 3 days of constant playing to beat the main story utilizing a Bug, an incredibly over powered spell that carried me through 70% of the game all the way to the end, And a bunch of OP food that I got from who knows where. I had 2 complains though. 1. I experienced a bug at the very end of the game where the final boss glitched into the ground, Wouldn't move, and wouldn't go below 70% hp. The 2nd complaint is a mob type that inflicts fatigue damage that 1 hit KO's you. I kept getting 1 shot and had absolutely no idea why, only that a certain mob would do it, and not how to counter it. I had to look up a solution on google which was making food that increases fatigue resistance. I could of probably figured this out myself but once again, I used an OP spell that got me to the end of the game within 3 days so I didnt even have access to the recipe or components to make said food. Good game though aside from those few complains. Would recommend for anyone who is looking for a casual time sink farming sim, to sit back and relax while playing. Just because its a farming sim doesnt mean it doesnt have combat, and the combat was responsive and not half bad. Lastly and probably the most important thing in the whole game, you can marry your waifu ;) that alone makes it a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hoped I'd like this game because I'm a fan of the genre, but I just didn't. It's incredibly janky, and feels horrifically outdated. I'd equate this to a a Nintendo DS game circa 2008 with upscaled graphics. The inventory management is absolutely atrocious, and frankly I found very nearly every character introduced in the 70 or so minutes that I played to be annoying, creepy, or a combination of the two. There's also the fact that there's no character customization, just a pre-generated male and female model, which I was aware of going into the game, but for me is still a negative on the whole.I was also hopeful for the combat, but from the small amount of it in the tutorial it's seemingly just target lock > press left click until target is dead, which was disappointing as well, but in fairness seeing as after 70 minutes in I still hadn't been allowed to try any further combat I'd take this with a grain of salt, perhaps it gets better later on, but I never reached that point. I really truly wanted to like this game, and was hopeful from the reviews that I'd enjoy it, but based on my experience, everyone here posting positive reviews is either riding on nostalgia from previous entries in the series and have turned a blind eye to any flaws or problems with the game, is recommending it ironically or jokingly because haha waifu good, or has never actually played a good game before and doesn't know any better.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm that one weirdo who's bought this game like 5 different times on multiple platforms and since you can't review stuff on Switch I'll just air my grievances in this review.TLDR: It's a enjoyable game if you like farming sims mixed with a JRPG but it's not the best the series can offer. For the same price you could get Rune Factory 4 Special which is the pinnacle for RF games imo. The company that made this game went bankrupt (possibly during the development of 5) and as such there is a lot of areas such as combat, exploration and story that needs to be fleshed out a lot more for it to be a great game. If you do intend to play it, get it on sale. That said I am recommending it because personally, I love the game despite all of its flaws. You can easily be sucked into spending hours perfecting every aspect of your vegetable farm and minmaxing your gear feels very rewarding when you smash that final boss with 2 hits. The character designs appeal to me a lot and there's plenty of quirky guys and gals that you can romance. There's just a lot of elements core to the series that hits my brain just right that a lot of the gripes I do have can be ignored (or modded lol) to still make it an enjoyable experience.For the people who want to hear me complain in detail lmao:- Story holds on its own for most of act 1 but act 2-3 are kinda just a mess with weird pacing and uninteresting villains.- Fun and engaging farming mechanics with a variety of crops and the fact that you can tame any monster as a farm animal is a series staple that I love.- Combat that feels a bit floatly at times, 90% of enemies are just exp/material fodder and bosses pretty much use the same attack patterns.- The town itself is alright, not much to write home about except it being a small seaside village.- There are open world sections but they're pretty empty and honestly not worth exploring.- Dungeons are ok but get repetitive during late game.- Endgame not having the procedural generated dungeons RF4 had  (bring back dungeon seeds and Sharance Maze ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥).- NPC characters are fine, if not a bit lacking compared to RF4's cast. - Most marriage candidates have some interesting aspects and I do think the character designs are this series' strong point (3D models are carrying ngl, the some of the png sprites are kinda weird).- The festivals are actually really fun, I enjoy doing the minigames.- Really intricate crafting system (grinding mats are kinda annoying tho)

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, first off, I was biased toward Rune Factory 5 from the start, mainly because I thought this game would never happen after Neverland's bankruptcy. But they have since come back, ported (albeit a bit lazily) Rune Factory 4 Special from the Switch to PC, and released a game that I really, REALLY want to recommend to everyone. Alas, I lean towards recommended here even though I'm mixed on this game.Rune Factory 5 is a JRPG meets light farming sim. You should know the drill by now. Farming, dungeon dwelving, romance, marriage, the whole nine yards.I will start with the story, while pretty much ticking every anime trope under the sun, it's pretty good, if a bit nonsensical by the end.The characters I am absolutely in love with, with Heinz in particular being my favourite due to my penchant for puns. Ryker and Lucy are my favourite bachelor and bachelorette respectively as well. Speaking of which:In a series first, you can have same-sex relationships. That is all I'll say on this front, because I'm a straight male so I feel that it's not my place to comment more on this aspect.Combat is still good with a lock on system now that the series has dropped the top-down angle from the handheld games to the 3D camera that Tides of Destiny had. Hell Ghosts can suck it, though. Be warned of enemies one-shotting you near the end.While it sounds like I recommend this, I am still mixed on doing so due to one teeny tiny bugbear: and no, it isn't that the graphics are quite basic. It is that the port is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TERRIBLE.Okay, not as bad as I made it sound, Arkham Knight it ain't. But when your game looks like it could run on a toaster from 2014 (or hardware even worse; like a Wii U) it had better run well. It doesn't. Instead, the game stutters quite a bit. The camera is clunky and at times it is so choppy it might as well run at sub-30fps.So once again a terrific Rune Factory game is let down by another lazy port. Thankfully, because of course, there is already a mod that fixes the performance quite a bit as well as implements other QOL stuff, which I won't link because I am not sure if Steam allows links to Github. Google RF5fix. That should point you in the right direction.In summary: A good game, nice if tropey story, interesting and engaging characters, inclusive relationships, good combat, bad graphics, lazy port.9/10 if the port weren't rubbish, 7.5/10 otherwise. If installing RF5Fix it's the former score.Also Lucy is best waifu don't @ me

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game because i have played Rune Factory 3/4 and like those games a lot. They were some of the most fun games I have played because of their addictive and unique style. But this game feels like a generic 3D game that would have been released for PS2 in 2003 that people would look at the cover art and then not even think twice about buying it. This game has some major issues that i wish didn't exist due to the jump from topdown to 3D.I'll list these problems because i really hope they get patched or something because it would be unacceptable for these same things to appear in Rune Factory 6.1. This game jumps to 3D from topdown pov but it doesn't add anything new. There is potential for new things to be added but they just copy and paste everything from the previous installment and dont use the 3D element well enough to justify the change.2. The 3D Targeting in this game is bad. Not just for combat, but for everything. You have to do everything so slowly and accurately so you don't mess anything up that it becomes tedious. Wanna capture a targeted monster? Hope you don't accidentally move the camera so it targets something else. This is worse when there are multiple monsters while locked on.Wanna cut this crop with the scythe? Looks like you moved a tiny bit at the last second and cut the wrong one.Wanna place furniture so that it lines up? Well you cant because the indicator is broken and it won't align unless go farther than it should. Even then furniture placing doesn't look good.Wanna Target this really specific and tiny item. Good luck because moving even a little bit will cause the target indicator to fidget everywhere.Picking up and throwing stuff feels really bad in this game to the point where it should either not exist or should have been improved.3. For a 3D game the map feels extremely bland, empty and disconnected. The town feels big, but empty and a lot of the areas are unused except for specific events. The outer areas feel half baked and look like they were just mashed together as fast as possible. They could have added more just to make it look more alive.4. Npcs don't feel as lively as previous games. One thing i like to do in the these games is talk to everyone and use the "hello" spell when walking past them. This game was the worst when doing that stuff. The npcs don't even respond to you when you just say a simple hello to them except for maybe one of them. The rest of them just repeat the same boring 1 line over and over again every time. How did they not add this simple thing correctly from the previous games? 5. Events being static on the map felt out of place and didn't make sense. In this game events will trigger if you walk into them on the map, but sometimes you don't want to do the event until you are ready or you want to do something else instead. The only thing you can do to stop them from happening is to walk away from them unless they are at a spot that you want to go to but not do the event. This gets extremely annoying if you want to go to the shops but an important event will happen there that you don't want to do yet.6.The game feels too easy at times because they copy and paste the top down combat without accounting for the 3D element. A lot of enemies attack and then pause for insane amounts of time making them all easy to kill. Even bosses do this. Also monsters do really slow telegraphed attacks that are predictable. This would be harder in a top down view because you wouldn't have as much room to move around, but in this game you can run around your enemies without ever fearing to get hit at all. 7. This one is more personal, but not being able to romance Terry, Elsje, Misa or Simone is really disappointing. Elsje not being an option feels out of place because she is just kinda there compared the others.8. This game lacks something to drive the player forward or maybe its just me. Combat is too easy and money/points is never really an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Stardew Valley, you'll enjoy the deeper farming system and addition of crafting, with a lot of unlockable festivals and friendships.If you're a fan of Harvest Moon / Story of Seasons, you may be thrilled by the addition of combat and magic (and not having to make lots and lots of the same crafting machine).If you're a long-standing Rune Factory fan, you'll notice that RF5 is retreading similar ground as RF4, but with several twists to increase your quality of life. It may still be worth it to you!Rune Factory 5, to me, is a "transition" game in the franchise - with most of the development time and effort needed to support the transition to 3D with new models in a new engine. It feels like a game made by an experienced studio in a new, less familiar development environment (Unity Engine). This has lead to a little jank and a few areas that could be more optimised, but no dealbreakers.If you've played Rune Factory 4 Special, you won't find anything massively new here - There are several Quality of Live improvements (some listed below), and you can now have a same sex marriage without needing to use the in-game model swap. As a fan, I'm happy to accept RF5's shortcomings to support the series and its creators. If your money is tight, however, I would not recommend 5 over 4 Special, unless one of the bachelorettes *really* excites you. Rune Factory 5 is the first full-3D title in the Rune Factory series since 2011's Rune Factory: Tides Of Destiny. Soon after Rune Factory 4 was released in 2012, Rune Factory developer Neverland Studio declared bankruptcy. Seven years later, Rune Factory 5 was announced in 2019 as being developed by Hakama Inc., a new subsidiary of Rune Factory publisher Marvelous AQL. Hakama is headed by Story of Seasons and Rune Factory producer Yoshifumi Hashimoto. (Seasoned farming game veterans may recall that "Story of Seasons" is the team behind the original "Harvest Moon" (Bokujō Monogatari) games, which due to licensing issues can no longer be called "Harvest Moon" overseas.) Most of the effort between Rune Factory 4 and 5 likely went into the change from 2D to 3D - new engine, new models, new challenges to deal with. 3D assets take a *lot* of time, effort and money to develop - that's why the Persona games often recycle their demon/persona models from game to game). Even if the team had access to Tides of Destiny's assets, they would no longer cut it on modern hardware, or weren't compatible with Unity.  Rune Factory 5 has a couple of small but noticeable quality of life increases over its predecessor, Rune Factory 4 Special. These include:* You can be queer; all dateable people are available for everyone. No more waiting for post-game model swaps and squinting away the pronouns.* Skill growth seems faster than in Rune Factory 4 Special, and Runes spawn more frequently - making the early and mid game less grind-y.* Similarly, the new Spell Seal feature allows you to get monster drops more easily. Less drop farming, more actual farming.* Town events are now clearly indicated on the Map via a pink marker with the character's portrait in them - no more hunting for triggers* Stumps and rocks spawn in- and outside your farmland, making it easier to get building materials up. There are still quarries and logging camps on the overworld map, too.* Instead of needing a save point to access fast travel (chaining Escape until you get to one), you can now freely warp to unlocked points using the map menu.* When forging weapons, you can now switch recipe categories (Short sword, long sword, spear, etc.) using the LB/RB buttons. No more menu-hunting (though the long menus are still there). - Items and Recipes seem to have been copied wholesale from RF4 with only a few new additions.- The characters are as fun and vibrant as always.- RF5's story has less of an overall arc. RF4's arcs gave you a distinct sense of where to go; RF5 might leave you waiting for the plot to come get you sometimes.- The graphics are... fine. They were likely designed for hand held consoles, so they're a little underwhelming on a modern, powerful PC. The style is different from past 3D Rune Factory titles with more dynamic blurs and motion. There's a good number of effects that add magic to the game world; the only issues I've noticed were small issues with floating animations and a little bit of clipping, but nothing actually bad.- There don't appear to be "season fields" (fields where it's always spring / summer / autumn / winter). However, crops do not wither "out of season" so you'll still get your Emery Flowers.- Rune Factory 5 runs much smoother on PC than on Switch, as the Switch allegedly isn't optimal for Unity Engine games. Loading times are fast (~2-3 seconds on map change)

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Uninspired, careless gameplay with many annoyances -- but if you can look past them, you may still have a positive experience.---If you are a fan of the series, then no bad review is going to deter you from playing it, and probably enjoying it, but for anyone else, I cannot recommend this game.First of all, why, in 2022, are you still not able to save your game from anywhere? There is no technical excuse for it, and it just makes it an annoying experience ESPECIALLY when the game will occasionally crash, often forcing you to replay the VERY LONG day (relative to most games of the genre).Another MASSIVE problem, especially since you can't save on demand, is how easy it is with the wonky controls to completely screw up your farm. If you are repeatedly pressing the action button to say, mine a rock, it will queue an extra hammer action before the last one finished, which if you happen to be next to an important plant of yours, may result in a permanent loss of that plant -- which is indicative of the overall problem with this game.The combat is okay at first, but the more you play, the more you realize how flawed and uninspired it is. Not to mention the lack of care or detail that went into many of the monsters and mechanics resulting in poor hit detection, unavoidable death from stuns, or accidentally wandering 10 steps from monsters who do 0 damage to you, and that you can one-hit kill, into monsters you do 0 damage to and 1 hit kill you without warning (there goes all your money!).There are a few minor bugs and workarounds, such as the game exclusively allowing the first controller it detects as your input device, which means if you're streaming it with a remote controller, you either can't -- or you are forced to see keyboard/mouse hints for controls and have to discover the key button mapping on your own. In about 50 hours of play, the game has only abruptly closed while I was playing twice. Overall, I wouldn't say that the game is .I would say, however, that . Very little thought went into protecting the game play experience, or the obvious player frustration of losing progress. So many unnecessary actions and time wasting because the devs either didn't know how to or didn't care to improve the overall experience. Why would a rock spawn colliding with a well, so that when you miss with your hammer (which you can miss even though the correct world tile is highlighted) you permanently destroy the structure, because you have already queued an additional hammer action by the time you realize you missed the rock? Why is it so easy to do things like destroy furniture, things that most people won't ever do in their play through, and so time consuming to do things like buy multiple pieces of furniture at once? Why is there a loader every time you go to craft something, when you are just allowed to skip it?I may be more critical than most, as a software developer, because I know how easy it would have been for the devs to find better solutions to greatly improve the QOL of this game --
