_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed the 2013 release of The Stanley Parable, and so it is with a heavy heart that I say I can't recommend this game given the state it is in. There are numerous bugs that should have been noticed and squashed way before release, especially seeing as how delayed the release was. The game constantly cuts the last second off of dialogue, features sound clips that fail to loop correctly, lurches whenever new dialogue is spoken, and after a certain point in the game a specific achievement is impossible to get.Feels rushed. Glad others are enjoying it though.

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe, now with more Stanley, brooms and buckets.Let's not forget that the original was an exceptional piece that dealt with the concept of choices in games and the absurdity that entails. Having said that, we need to also acknowledge that Ultra Deluxe is not the same as 2, 3, epilogue or prologue, and as long as you don't treat it as such, you'll surely enjoy the paths this one will take you on.With that said, we need to address a few more things:-TSP:UD includes the entire content from the original.-It also acts as a self critique of the previous and itself.-It reuses nearly every asset from the original game, while also modifying pretty much every ending.-It adds a few more endings and twists.When it comes down to what made the original Stanley Parable, THE Stanley Parable, the humour was mainly what drove it forward, pushed by the player trying (or not) to follow directions.Ultra Deluxe mainly adds a variable or two to it, adding to the absurdity of it all but really following on the footsteps of Stanley, only to get the same (in general) ending, with a slight, round, handle-y twist. Given the excellent not-so-hidden meaning of the original, I did my best to look for one other than "This is not a sequel", because it isn't.Alas, I didn't find anything else.At one point I even felt bored, expecting more out of it.Then again, this isn't a sequel.If you've never played the original, by all means get this one and play it.If you have, then don't expect to be blown away, but I'm sure you'll get some enjoyment out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, how much the spirit of this game has fallen from grace. I used to feel so empowered by this once impeccable work's presentation of choice in video games. But the narrator has fallen low (too low I would say) when he introduced the dreaded skip button. And all to try to get some uncultured swine to change their Steam review. This was the impetus- the resonance cascade leading to the game's further detraction from its once perfect and wholesome meaning. The corruption could only escalate as other gimmicks were introduced: some pithy bucket (which strangely makes me feel reassured about the unethical business practices of The Stanley Parable 2), an infinite hole that has the gall to be finite in length, and a mechanic that demands I imagine myself as the founder of Jonestown. Such depravity cannot even be rivaled by the loot box or microtransaction mechanics of your typical triple-A video game company. I hope you know what you've done, Cookie9. You made the developers take a perfectly functioning and thought-provoking game and sullied its artistic merit in some half-baked effort to please the masses. If only I was given the chance to reset the game so I could forget this was even possible. Oh, if only.Alright. I'm doney with the funny.

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, It is this: What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience, it leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world - there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so... The Stanley Parable.This is gonna be a long one:The Stanley Parable is a meta game, and that's almost an understatement. It's a game largely about games, and spends much of its time philosophising about freedom and choice and will and how that all relates to narrative tropes in video games, and it's not shy about doing so. It's extremely dense, and requires a lot of unpacking to appreciate in entirety. That being said, it's pretty great; if you don't want any spoilers then I would recommend you stop reading here, and buy it, especially if it sounds like your type of thing. Outside of saying something generic (albeit true) like: "it is funny" or "The Narrator is very well voiced", unfortunately I can't tell you  it's great without analysing it a little, and to do that, I'm going to have to spoil it somewhat, so here goes:    Look at me; I'm rambling. The fact I can ramble about it for so long is a testament to it's quality and density. Pretentious fools like me are toyed with by the game, too, you know. It satirises lengthy self-important rambles like this. Not even by analysing it do I escape its trap.It's a damn enjoyable trap though.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like all previous versions, The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe is an incredible game in terms of storytelling, atmosphere, comedy, and usage of doors. If you've played any other version of this game, get this as soon as you can't. If you've never played a Stanley Parable game before, don't look up anything more about it and experience it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: This game is buckets of fun. I think compared to the original this version of the story holds more water. Honestly I think the original pails in comparison. I've been waiting for this game for a long time and man am I happy with the results. I laughed and laughed at a lot of parts in this game and enjoyed it immensely. Thank you guys for creating such a wonderful experience that was both fun and thought engaging. It was on my bucket list so I am so glad that I got to play it before I kicked the bucket.But honestly guys this game is great and I'd recommend playing it a lot even if you've played the original. Both are fantastic games that have brought much fun to my life. Thank you Crows Crows Crows.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the original, but better! If you played the original on release and haven't replayed it since then, it'll be a fun time to come back to. _childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe is a mysterious, ominous, multiplex of conundrums that really make you think about the perspectives of the reality around us. The intrinsic desire to find every ending, toggle every button and door knob, while our beloved narrator guides Stanley to a higher plane of existence. It also questions our profound understanding of inanimate objects and their importance to society. Thus, we must evolve to be at peace and harmony with said inanimate object and accept our dismal fates in whatever this short, quaint and mysterious life we live. For the affordable price of 35 dollars from Hobbington, one can experience not just a game, but a work of art.

_childDocuments_.review: Stanley arrived at his office building as usual, but to his surprise, the doors were unlocked, and no one was inside. He wandered through the empty cubicles and offices, looking for any sign of his co-workers, but it seemed that he was completely alone.At first, Stanley was confused and a bit worried. He wondered if there was a memo or email that he had missed, announcing a company holiday or closure. But as he searched through his emails and checked his phone, he found no messages or notifications.Feeling a bit lonely and uncertain, Stanley decided to take a break and grab a cup of coffee from the break room. As he entered the room, he saw his best friend waiting for him on the counter - the bucket he used for cleaning coffee he spilled on his desk.Stanley smiled, feeling a bit relieved to have some company, even if it was just a shiny metal bucket. He sat down at the table, sipping his coffee and chatting with the bucket about the strange situation."I don't know what's going on," Stanley said, shaking his head. "It's like everyone disappeared."The bucket remained silent, but Stanley felt comforted by its presence nonetheless. He decided to make the best of the situation and explore the empty office building, with the bucket as his trusty sidekick.Together, they wandered through the hallways and explored the various floors of the building. They found some interesting things - a stash of office supplies in a storage closet, a collection of funny photos on a co-worker's desk, and even an old dartboard in the break room.As the day wore on, Stanley began to feel more and more at ease with his new situation. He realized that he was enjoying the peace and quiet, and the chance to explore the office building without any interruptions or distractions.And through it all, the bucket remained by his side, a constant companion in an otherwise strange and empty world. In the end, Stanley decided that he and the bucket could handle anything, as long as they had each other.

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe is a game that no review could ever fully do justice. It's a smart, witty and funny game, with lots of different endings and easter eggs that will end with you questioning if you have really, truly seen everything the game has to offer or if there's even more waiting for you to find. You won't regret it. And whatever you do, get the broom closet ending. The broom closet ending is the best ending.

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable's remake is, to put it lightly, incomprehensible at times, but that's just part of the charm. For a choice driven game, it sure has a lot of endings to get, too. You can annoy the narrator, create a custom sequel to the game every time you boot it up, and it also has an achievement that requires its' players to touch grass (which, given the amount of people who have 100%'d this game, nobody has done as of yet). 10/10, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: The entirety of the 2013 commercial release, plus a plethora of new things to explore, a very solid discussion and analysis of game design mixed in with making sure the word "bucket" no longer means anything to my brain. Absolutely worth a play if you liked The Stanley Parable as a mod or Source game, or just want to hear a dignified British narrator yell at you about the concept of choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, as someone who played and loved the original, This review was on point. Overwhelmingly Positive is for those who haven't played it yet."Back when this was announced at The Game Awards in 2018, I was hyped.The game experienced a lot of delays since then, but recently it finally released in 2022.And I am severely disappointed.The original game is almost unchanged besides graphical tweaks and new effects here and there.The original game now has two new endings and one that has been changed, presumably for copyright reasons.I assume the door that leads to the actual new content unlocks after doing some of the original endings.And this is where it goes downhill. The game tries to be self-aware and ironic about itself, jokes about it being a expansion or even jokes about a sequel!But here's the thing: That's the only gag. That the game got new content. It grows stale after a while, and are probably more true to the actual experience than the writers might have intended.The new content of Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe is lacking, and it doesn't help that the game was joking about it early in the path of the new content.After going through some areas that can't be accessed again until "completing" the game, the narrator makes some tweaks to the original game and we are send to: Stanley Parable 2!Except it's just the regular office with some balloons and figurines you can find here and there. But what about the new endings? As already mentioned, there are two new endings to the main route of the game. After being send back to the office in Stanley Parable 2, you will see a bucket on a pedestal on your way through.And that's how you get the new endings. You pick up this bucket, and go about the original game's endings with almost the exact same condition. Every mian game ending has a bucket-variant, except for two, which in turn have been replaced with one bucket centered one.Yes, the glorious new endings revolve around a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bucket. It was funny at first, I'll admit, but it grew stale after the second Bucket-ending.But at least the whole Stanley Parable being recreated is correct, right? Well, yes and no. It's complicated:As also mentioned before, the original game is barely changed. It doesn't look any better than it did in my memory. But it was recreated: In Unity, which might explain the fact this is a standalone title and it took so long to come out.Wait, standalone title? That's right!For the cheap price of 21,99€ (10€ more than the original) or the bargain price of... 14,66€, if you already own the original game.What?The majority of this game is just the original game from 2013, except you have to rebuy it + increased price if you already ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ owned it.This should've been either a free update or a 5€ to 10€ DLC for the original title, not this lackluster 15 bucks expansion pack.Conclusion:Buy the original. A large part of it is identical to the fancy new Ultra Deluxe version, and it sure is a whole lot cheaper and more worth the price.If you already own the original, don't buy it either. Pass it up. If you really wanna experience Stanley Parable again, just download the OG-version and play that." - MissCassidy
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: There are games, and then there are art pieces.If "The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe" was a movie, it'd get a bunch of Oscars.If it was a book, it would get a Pulitzer prize.It is a game, so all it gets is this review.I am a big fan of the original game, so I was hoping for the best, but fearing the worst when launching the Ultra Deluxe edition.I was hoping to find the same humor and playfulness of the first part, but discovered a postmodern masterpiece, which uses the same old engine of humor to achieve transcendence.Take the bucket gag for example! I first took it for one of the many stupid jokes, but quickly realized: this is actually a profound philosophical concept. Is a bucket  just a bucket? Well, maybe  bucket is. But THE bucket most definitely is not. THE bucket really deserves all the praise it is given. It might  like a bucket, but it is nothing else but the life force itself!
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Listen, if you like this game, that's fine. Don't let my dumb opinion ruin your day.For me, I thought this game would have way more content. new places, routes, and just other fun things. But instead, I was given 1 big message about how "sequel bad". Games can be more about messages then being a game. Example, Undertale, while the gameplay is pretty crap, the message it sends is really good. What makes it different then TSPUD, It's not $25. Stanely Parable was a really good analysis on giving the player freedom. While the idea of looking at why sequels can ruin games is cool. I felt that they just took TSP, and made it have a bucket, and a new message.I get that it's the "point" That the narrator is just ruining his own work trying to make it better.  But I felt like this idea could've been expanded on. Since the game now runs on Unity, (please do correct me if I'm wrong!) it could've been the narrator turning TSP into other genres of games. Trying to appease different audiences, only to push away the people who loved his work. But instead, it's just TSP, but better graphics, and you have a bucket.For me, the biggest problem is the price. I know that making a game is hard. Adding all the new lines, and endings for the bucket was not easy to make. But as a player, I felt like I was just playing a joke. They advertised it as this big expansion to the game. Then make fun of the idea, and just reskin the base game.Like I said, if you love this game, keeping doing it! I can't stop you! But for me, this game was really disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Hey I've just barely started playing this game, but I gotta let you knowI love youThis bit of game inside the larger category of art games makes me very happy to just know it exists and is thriving.Thank you so much for your continued development and support (of yourself, because you deserve it!!!)-cloudself/Bailey
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: At this point I have finished this game. There is still much to enjoy but I have found most of the endings/ content. The experience is unlike any other and I would say it is worth the price I paid for it (18 bucks on sale). The amount of content in the game has essentially doubled so it is worth purchasing again for those that already own it. It also offers some good and insightful commentary on gaming as a whole.All the negative reviews about the new content being underwhelming are missing the point about sequels that the game is trying to make.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable is a story about Stanley and his missing co-workers.To speak at great lengths about this "game" would be a disservice to it. This is a hilarious, downright genius execution of a "game" that takes a simple story and turns it into a yarn ball of tales, whether its through the expert narration by Kevan Brighting, making a generic location actually feel vibrant with stories to tell and having fun little details in each location and anticipates your thoughts and moves in a mocking-like manner (which also carries over to the achievements).With the Presentation, story and "gameplay" all on point, The Stanley Parable is an excellent showcase in creating a masterpiece, with a hefty amount of replayability, out of something so little. Something many AAA games could take a lesson from.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: This is the story of a man named Stanley. Stanley worked for a company in a big building where he was employee # 427. Employee # 427’s job was simple: he sat at his desk in room 427 and he pushed buttons on a keyboard. Orders came to him through a monitor on his desk, telling him what buttons to push, how long to push them, and in what order. This is what employee 427 did every day of every month of every year, and although others might have considered it soul rending, Stanley relished every moment that the orders came in, as though he had been made exactly for this job. And Stanley was happy. And then one day, something very peculiar happened, something that would forever change Stanley, something he would never quite forget. He had been at his desk for nearly an hour when he realized that not one, single order had arrived on the monitor for him to follow. No one had shown up to give him instructions, call a meeting, or even say hi. Never in all his years at the company had this happened, this complete isolation. Something was very clearly wrong. Shocked, frozen solid, Stanley found himself unable to move for the longest time, but as he came to his wits and regained his senses, he got up from his desk and stepped out of his office.

_childDocuments_.review: If you somehow don't know what this is: It's a meta-narrative focused walking sim with a funny narrator. Only you know if that kind of thing sounds like a good time to you.Subtract about 26 hours from my playtime because I'm a lunatic who left the game running for a whole day to get a silly achievement.I loved the HD remix (never played the og mod), and I really liked this one too, but I will say that a lot of the commentary the original offered doesn't hit as hard or hold up as well almost a decade later, just because the narrative structure and how narrative is tied to gameplay of many story-driven games has changed in that time (because of course it has), as well as the mindset of a lot of players being different. So I think that it's worth keeping in mind the cultural moment the original was made during... if you're the thinky type who likes to overthink things. You massive nerd.Still, it felt nice to jump back in and spend a little more time with the narrator, and there were some legitimately striking moments in the new content that I found to be quite powerful and engaging. Overall, though, having played the original, getting all the new stuff (and revisiting the old) felt a lot more like checking off a to-do list than active exploration teasing at the boundaries of the game and it's layout than the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: A novelty and a work of art, but you can burn through the content pretty quickly. Once the narrative paths are over, as funny as it can genuinely be at times, that's...it. There's not much else to it. I don't recommend watching any YouTube videos before playing it, as it will honestly spoil everything the game has to offer. It is, at best, perhaps worth a few dollars. It will last you longer than a theatrical experience, but admittedly I got tired of The Narrator at times, especially when all I wanted to do was to get to a particular branch. Again, let's make it clear: it's a clever experience, but just not worth what they're asking.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the story of a man named Stanley. Stanley worked for a company in a big building where he was employee number 427. Employee number 427’s job was simple: he sat at his desk in room 427 and he pushed buttons on a keyboard. Orders came to him through a monitor on his desk, telling him what buttons to push, how long to push them, and in what order. This is what employee 427 did every day of every month of every year, and although others might have considered it soul rending, Stanley relished every moment that the orders came in, as though he had been made exactly for this job. And Stanley was happy. And then one day, something very peculiar happened, something that would forever change Stanley, something he would never quite forget. He had been at his desk for nearly an hour when he realized that not one, single order had arrived on the monitor for him to follow. No one had shown up to give him instructions, call a meeting, or even say hi. Never in all his years at the company had this happened, this complete isolation. Something was very clearly wrong. Shocked, frozen solid, Stanley found himself unable to move for the longest time, but as he came to his wits and regained his senses, he got up from his desk and stepped out of his office.

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe is one of very few newly released games in recent times which I've genuinely felt a great deal of anticipation for before buying. I quite thoroughly enjoyed the original, and while this version is absolutely a lot "more of the same" it definitely didn't disappoint (and there's certainly enough satisfying twists to keep things interesting). I won't go into any detail about the gameplay or story elements as I feel even minor spoilers would simply detract from the experience - it's really something best enjoyed by going in without any predetermined expectations other than those based on the original game (which is does help to have played to fully appreciate Ultra Deluxe, but is not at all a requirement as all of the base content is included anyway).Upon first playing it's not exactly clear where or how Ultra Deluxe would change/expand upon the base game, but soon enough the new content presents itself and the story begins to unfold.Kevan Brighting (the voice actor of The Narrator) is of course back and his performances are absolutely impeccable just as before, his work on both games has truly been a work of excellence. The writing to support this brilliant dialogue holds up just as strongly too, and on several occasions I did find myself bursting out with genuine laughter - the extent to which I had to close my windows to avoid becoming a nuisance to my neighbours.I played the new content for about 4 hours (and saw practically all of the newly added content), which as far as games these days go isn't particularly a lot and, however, I found the whole experience to be thoroughly satisfying and certainly worth the price. And for what it's worth, virtually the whole 4 hours contained new content and didn't have any of the filler or fluff that so many games get bogged down with just to add playtime. It's for sure a case of quality over quantity here.If I had to point out any negatives from the game it would be things got a little bit samey towards the end of the new content, and it did almost feel like the game was running out of steam at this point, I was able to feel the point where the content was beginning to run out. Another reviewer compared the endings in The Stanley Parable to a flowchart, where Ultra Deluxe simply adds on some extras and also includes a *modifier* that provides alternative dialogue/environments to the endings in the base game. I would agree this is an accurate description of Ultra Deluxe, and by the end I did find myself at the point of simply going through all of the base game endings  with the *modifier* because that's the only content I had left to see. It wasn't necessarily a bad thing, but it was starting to get predictable when it got to the point of "The Broom Closet ending  this time with a ******."There's so much more I could say about the game but to summarise and wrap things up:Absolutely excellent game and was definitely worth the wait for release. Very reasonable price all things considered especially with the discount for owning the original. Biggest criticism is that there was less new branching storyline and new endings than I was hoping for and things did get a bit "linear alternate versions of the original endings" in some places. But absolutely not enough to ruin the experience.If you enjoyed the original or think you would have enjoyed the original, you'll almost certainly enjoy this and would be better off diving in to give it a go than reading reviews. Overall very fun and I have no regrets for picking it up, supporting some very talented devs, and spending my time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe "The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe"? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone, for the stone into which the Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted, offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more, so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from "The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe", it is this... what a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience it leaves me hopeful that as a community — as a world, there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: I debated myself whether to recommend this game expansion or not. Ultimately, if you have played the original, I don't think you are missing out NOT buying this.Yes, there are new content, but they are heavily tied to the original content such that much is expected and grows tedious. Remember when you played the original game, everything is unexpected and new, at least not until later when you try to hunt down some sub-paths you didn't try. Now the Ultra Deluxe is like putting more fat on the original body of story, it's the same but with added self-reflecting flourishes, hence the annoyance grew as the novelty is not there. Actually there are few times that the game felt new - new mechanics and environment. But after discounting those self-actualising scenes that are not really entertaining, there's not much.I haven't explored everything, but I badly need a mental break from the game from being overloaded with dry monologue. Meanwhile, I can't help but think that the devs spent time and effort into the wrong aspects and direction, perhaps in name of convenience and familiarity, instead of building a 2nd gen experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game filled with all different kinds of emotion, sadness, anger, hapiness, and nostalgia.This game teaches us players such a great lesson about the importance of just simply enjoy what you have at the moment, enjoy it for long before it turns into an ancient, well beloved, old game hidden in the depths of great games to always remember the great times you had. This game teaches us to always enjoy the memories we have, cherish them and keep them hidden away in our memories and hearts forever, but never to try to enjoy it once-more by begging the developers to the point where they make a game just like this, but with new 'fun' gags that are only enjoyable for a brief moment. This game teaches us that once we have experienced something, we can never experience it the exact same way you want to again.Yes, I do indeed really miss the Stanley Parable, but that's okay! Because I already had fun, I experienced a part of my life that will for ever be remembered and cherish.I like to remember that if we ever experience the same thing over and over again, it becomes boring and dull, meaningless.This game does such a good job of reviving the experience, reviving what it feels like to wonder "what's going to happen this time, what is the narrator going to say? Oh, I cannot wait to find out!" I cried of happiness, remembering it all, I laughed in joy as I experienced the wacky gags that the game has, I got annoyed when I had to, once again, wait for dialogue to happen at moments I wanted to wait for it. I experienced such a roller coaster of emotions throughout this game, and I only wished I experience it again one more time. But, as I said, we cannot as we should always cherish these moments, like a fine, classic wine.

I'll give some examples for easter eggs/new endings for you guys to potentially add:(1) A way to deactivate the self-destruct systems in the countdown endingSo this is an obvious one, maybe, as I assume everyone has wanted this after seeing the countdown ending. But I have a particular idea as to how you could do this. What if there was some secret interaction with the slider character where he could  activate the buttons in the countdown ending? It has already been shown he has more power than the narrator, and is discreet, based on how the Narrator doesn't know the test achievement machine was fixed until Stanley pulls the lever. It could help further establish the powers at play, and possibly lead to another special ending.(2) Narrator vs. Slider Entity.Maybe if there could be several situations where the slider man changes something, the Narrator could confront Stanley as to how he is doing this, maybe result in some big fight.(3) Bottom of the Disco Control Facility EndingBasically, imagine if the disco easter egg impacted the B.O.T.M.C.F ending. Judging by the Bucket Variation, you can put stuff down there, so maybe it could spawn a disco floor and/or even lead you to a special room. It would be pretty tight to hear the narrator get down, maybe see Stanley's other friends boogeyThere's definitely more options ofc, just some suggestions, assuming you even read these reviews. _childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the original game.  It was innovative, interesting, and had a great sense of humour.  The meta-narrative was interesting and unlike anything I'd seen in gaming before.  It was truly something different.The "Ultra Deluxe" version is... more of the same.  The same game with a handful of extra stuff tacked on.  Which itself wouldn't necessarily be so bad, but the extra content really doesn't break any new ground.  Where the original Stanley Parable was cleverly self-aware, Ultra Deluxe is irritatingly self-indulgent at times.  Where the original was short, quick, and never worse out its welcome (except maybe for the baby game); the update is uneven and at times even tedious.  It's telling that the overwhelming majority of the positive comments so far are essentially just memes and quotes, not saying anything of substance about the game itself.The bulk of the "New Content" part of the game purports to comment on the changing world of gaming, criticisms of the original game, and the predictable nature and desires of gamers -- as exemplified by its new collection quest.  But rather than providing any real insightful commentary, it comes off as merely encouraging and exploiting them.The absolute worst part is the interminable diatribe against the previous games' critics.  Rather than addressing the criticism in good faith, it ends up merely creating a straw-man version of said criticism, and then going on an interminable tirade, utterly lacking in humour and bordering on on mean-spirited at times.  I nearly quit the game at that point, but wanted to give it a fair shake and evaluate everything available, so I could ensure that I didn't miss something that really set the new version apart from the original.  So I completed every pathway and got every ending (again, except the baby game, because I was not about to sit through it for four hours, and didn't feel like looking up the cheats), including all the new versions of the original endings (not going to say what these are or how to get them, to avoid spoilers).Aside from the protracted whinging about fans and fan-demands, there wasn't anything here that stood out as significantly different, thematically or philosophically, from the original game.  It felt less like an extended exploration of the themes and topics of the first game, and more like a cynical cash-grab pandering to the sorts of gamers who want to play the same game over and over and over, instead of exploring anything truly new and innovative.If you haven't played the original Stanley Parable, then a lot of the "new content" in this one isn't going to make much sense, since it's mostly meta-references to the original game; but it's still worth playing if you can sit through (or skip through, since that option is now available) the tirade in the middle.  If you have played the original, then you're not really going to find anything particularly ground-breaking here.  If you're the sort of person who enjoys games that are little more than re-hashes of games you've already played... well this is the game for you, I guess.  Either way, if you do plan on playing it, do yourself a favour and wait for it to go on sale at a deep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe the Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted, offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more, so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe it is this... "What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience it leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future."

_childDocuments_.review: I must say, contrary to most players, I am quite disappointed with the new version of this game. This ultra deluxe version features "new content". Unfortunately this "new content" is pretty bad. First of all it takes a while to even unlock any of the new content. When you first boot up the game, after having to complete a bunch of tedious tasks which have no effect on the game whatsoever, you are essentially playing the original game, with nothing really different at all. The game asks you in the beginning if you have played the original, which I have. Even so, you're still forced to play through the old content a couple of times before the new content is accessible. The new content is essentially just the original game being discussed with a few cheap, uninteresting gimmicks here and there. The new content is so focused on talking about itself, that it failed to provide anything at all. After a long time of the narrator talking about the game (and restarting it), you are finally led to a big expo which contains the uninteresting gimmicks I mentioned. These gimmicks do not fit into the story or the narrative of the game whatsoever.The new narration that was added on to this game was advertised as being longer than the entire old narration. Unfortunately most of this new narration is either endless rambling that serves no purpose whatsoever or the narrator just talking about the game itself.What this game is all about is an object that provides slight modifications to original endings, which is what makes up most of this new content. So in short all that you're getting with this game is the original game, along with a few modifications to the original endings and some pointless gimmicks. There is no continuation or elaboration of the original story which is what disappointed me most as a returning player.This game might be nice for someone who's never played the original, but for a returning player, it is quite disappointing and a waste of money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: For someone who hasn't played or heard about this game prior to Ultra Deluxe, the game isn't what I was looking for.The game is a walking simulator, with multiple short endings; that much was clear. However, to avoid spoilers - what the game is about is barely described anywhere.I expected it to be a game about games that talks about phenomena we don't notice, while playing games - to stay more aware of how we are being manipulated. However, this is a narrative about the characters in the game; nothing more. The endings are not woven into a single narrative (or at least that what I concluded thus far), so the repeated backtracking to change a single decision with mechanics that do not innovate in any way can become tedious.The game lacks novelty and polished, possibly-also-innovative controls. Might be worth playing on a subscription service rather than worth paying for.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the original Stanley Parable quite a bit, so my time played doesn't really count here. This is definitely the better version, especially if you haven't played it before. The only thing that does make me a little sad is they couldn't use the Portal and Minecraft references in this edition, but it's not exactly a deal breaker....as this is only one of the dozens of endings. Yes, there are TONS of endings for this game. There's so much to explore and see and do in this game, you almost never know whats going to happen. You might think you can do something but you actually cant, you might think the game glitched out but it's actually part of the story. This is the Backrooms before the Backrooms were a thing. You'll be outside the world, go into different games, laugh and cry (mostly laugh). Heck, there's endings where you literally have to perform certain actions for HOURS straight (which were designed so you can't use an automatic method to cheese it). The writing is clever, the narrator is amazing, and the game is entertaining for everyone watching. My kids love watching me play and helping figure out what to try out next. I recommend this game for people with quirky senses of humor, and if you like exploring weird liminal spaces (even if that's not technically what you're doing).

_childDocuments_.review: A great game made even better by the expanded content and there's a considerable amount of it. The various scenes/scenarios in Ultra Deluxe probe even deeper into the heart of the human condition in ingenious ways. Kevan Brighting gives another brilliant performance as the Narrator and was downright hilarious. Easily one of the funniest games I've ever played. I hesitate to say this because assessments like these will always vary from gamer to gamer, but 2022 has seemed pretty quiet so far in terms of new releases. IMHO, the two best games I've played this year are Aperture Desk Job and this one. Aperture Desk Job is essentially a Portal 2 modification and SP Ultra Deluxe, as everyone knows, originally began as a Half Life 2 mod back in 2011. Valve should start making more games is what I'm saying, lol. Although it looks as though Somerville and Scorn are set to release later this year, as well as Entropy: Zero 2. I hope so, at any rate.

_childDocuments_.review: Performance review for Bucket:Aiming for a top job in the organization. They set very high standards, aware that this will bring attention and promotion. Reaches a decision rapidly after taking account of all likely outcomes and estimating the route most likely to bring success. The decisions almost always turn out to be good ones. Always succeeds in explaining ideas clearly. Others find Bucket easy to understand. They also have the ability to listen carefully to what others are saying, to understand and then to respond appropriately. Conversations with Bucket are two-way. Bucket has a powerful physique, suited for heavyweight jobs, or situations when it’s an advantage to appear strong. When dressed for the job, personal appearance and dress immediately impress. Distinctive, perhaps distinguished. Bucket enjoys public speaking, and is very well received by audiences. Eloquent, clear, persuasive, interesting, always captures the interest and fires the imagination of listeners. Comfortable in any situation, even when speaking unprepared and without notes. Intellectually versatile. When a topic is unfamiliar or new concepts are put forward, Bucket listens, learns and adjusts quickly, and is soon making a full and useful contribution to the conversation. Meticulous in keeping the workplace clean and tidy. Bucket makes a habit of keeping own area clean and hazard-free and also assists and encourages others to do the same. A pleasant, outgoing personality who always gets on well with others. Bucket will always be noticed and popular in a group. When working to a firm but realistic deadline, Bucket always completes tasks to a high standard. Care and accuracy is obvious even when put under pressure of time. Prepared to work all the extra hours it takes to meet the deadline. Always contributes vigorously to the efforts of the team, whether as a leader or a team member. Understands own weaknesses and others’ strengths and goes to the right people for help. Sympathetically helps others to address their weaknesses. Responds to setbacks or adversity with redoubled vigor and enthusiasm. Will never accept that defeat is a foregone conclusion, and inspires others to stay positive and fight on.

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone, for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted, offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more, so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, it is this... What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience. It leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world - there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: The new content basically consists of- One long and linear ending that can be summarised as "what if the new stanley parable was all marketing and no content...? haha just kidding... unless?" - two new short to very short endings- bucket funnyAfter many years of development and and a 3 year delay this feels pretty underwhelming. Imo the game would've been better with more story branches and areas to explore, rather than one very long, very meta new ending.Only thing I thoroughly enjoyed was the infinite hole.

With this new iteration, I wanted to make sure I didn't make that same mistake again. And GOD I am so glad I did. GET THIS GAME AND PLAY IT  Doesn't matter if you've already spoiled yourself for the first game, Doesn't matter if you've already played the first game yourself regardless. Hell, this is probably the best 8 or so hours I have (and will) spend this year period. If or once you have the money, get this game. It's one hell of a trip.P.S. Even if this wasn't a good entry, I'd still have given this game a good review because the textures in the Unity asset files told me to : )

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another hilarious commentary on the state of video games:I played the original a long time ago, and I really appreciated it's snarky take on storytelling issues in games. This rerelease adds a whole bunch of new endings, and even new content to pre-existing endings, and a whole new narrative that comments on nostalgia, responding to feedback, and all sorts of other issues in gaming. Its worth the money. Also, narrator, I see you.

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone for the stone in which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may be more, so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe it is this... What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience, it leave me hopeful that as a community - as a world there is time for us to become our greatest selves as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the original game, that came out in 2013 and all of the additional content: Demo versions, Rafael version... When I got the news that this game is going to come out I was extatic. I think I wasn't the only person salivating in the waiting for the Stanley Parable ULTRA DELUXE: The Hidden Octopus 5, Pocket Full of Content. But here it is.Aaannnd... There could be more to it, I'd say. More WaCkY endings, more references, more gags and jokes. It could become a real Stanley Parable 2 even. But on the other hand -- it's great as is. It's liminal, sad, it literally the First Game with more CONTENT on top of it. I got the bucket and I was happy. Can't ask for more, really even though I kind of wanted to. I think I went through all of the content in 14 hours and several times too. Too bad the Confusion route doesn't allow you to take the Bucket with you to supress the confusion. Some things are very subtle. Some thoughts and moments are touching. Most jokes land greatly with precise comedic timing (!) and I appreciate that. The work done by Kevin Bright and devs is very well done and the Narrator is as always in my heart, even though, it may have become less sensitive over the last 9 years. Thank you. 9 buckets out of 10 Endings.

_childDocuments_.review: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe amazes me. It stays true to the original game, yet adds in so much more. It is incredibly funny, bends your mind (especially in some parts of the Confusion Ending), and is overall one of the greatest games ever made. Even if you haven't played the original game, I still recommend giving this game a go. Trust me, it is brilliant. Why is it brilliant? You'll just have to play it...
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: To sum it up: I was not ready.So many aspects of the original game made me absolutely adore it. I've always loved interactive fictions - especially those that break the fourth wall (which this one does a LOT) - but The Stanley Parable was unlike any I had ever played before. With its excellent, intelligent writing, attention to detail, subtle commentary supplemented with engaging humour, I fell in love. Kevan Brighting brings the Narrator to life, making him a human in his own right rather than a disembodied voice. The Narrator's wide array of emotions play hand-in-hand with his sarcastic and witty remarks and the dialogue never feels forced.Discovering easter eggs, trying different pathways, altering my actions ever so slightly just to see what will happen - this is what The Stanley Parable is about. "The end is never the end", as it says. And it does not disappoint. I was so intrigued by the little details. A small dialogue change in the employee lounge, or a flabbergasted reaction from the Narrator when entering a passcode too quickly. The work the developers put into these small little features shows just how much they went the extra mile to make the game as entertaining as possible. Everything comes together, everything connects, everything interlaces and intertwines to make something truly, truly spectacular.My favourite end in the first game was the Zending, in which you choose the red door. The developers went out of their way to help you relate and feel for the Narrator, who is simply trying to find some peace in the stories he fabricates. In this ending, those same developers exploit that sympathy and twist it into the profound reality of guilt. It was heartwrenching, yet beautiful. Bittersweet.Then came The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe.The new content did not just live up to my expectations. It exceeded them. It blew them out of the water by telling a story that I never thought it would tell. The original game was a commentary on the way humans make choices. That was the center idea - choice. But alongside choice, there's an underlying theme of loneliness throughout the games. Stanley finds all his coworkers gone - that's the inciting incident. The Narrator tricks him into thinking he has a wife, or that he has a life outside work. The loneliness of Stanley is thoroughly explored in the original game, but the Narrator's reality is not brought up often (only in the  endings). Despite how meta the game is, it does little to explore the Narrator himself. One of the endings in Ultra Deluxe took a step back from Stanley and gave the true main character the spotlight he never had, telling a relatable, emotional, powerful, and heartbreaking story.The Skip Button ending. In this storyline, the witty jokes and the absurdity of The Stanley Parable take a backseat to allow new themes to shine - that longing for the past, to undo the mistakes you've made; that feeling that you're never good enough; the fear that you will die alone... and the guilt that you, the player, are forced to experience.It made me cry.I was not ready.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Stanley finds this game a bit hard to describe, as this game is unlike anything else. Stanley spent most of his time walking and listening to the narrator, but although this may sound boring, Stanley found the humour and the creativity to be top notch. Although Stanley did find the game to be a little bit short, Stanley did discover many different endings, and there are many that Stanley noted were not found in the original  (nearly  twice as many), so it was definitely worth playing for Stanley even though he had already played the original. Stanley likely wouldn't have found some of the endings without outside help, and would recommend looking up endings once it feels like you've found them all, as you'll likely find that you missed some like Stanley did, and all of them are worth reaching. There isn't much replayability unfortunately, as Stanley now knows all the possible endings, but Stanley still wholeheartedly recommends the game, as it's a great laugh and features creative storytelling that is unlike anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: Narrator,I ADORE the game, it brings me so much joy. And to be honest, I've learned from it. There's endless hours on entertainment, and if you rush through it, you miss so much dialogue. If you just take a few minutes to wait and listen to the Narrator's soothing voice, there's so much interesting and funny dialogue you'd have missed if you were just rushing through the story, trying to get achievements and trying to find different endings. I sat in that door-less, window-less room with the skip button for ages, just listening to the Narrator talk, until the script looped. Sometimes I'd listen to it once or twice more, because it'd change a little.So much love, time, effort, and work has gone into this expansion, and its amazing.

The creation of The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe after so many yesterday of youth spending their days crafting C# code and witches farming optic fibre for the distribution of this wonderous game has paid off, as I am delighted with reliving and experiencing the new, impressive features combined with the original release. It has taken courage, sacrifice, and exactly 2 tonnes and 53 pounds of absestos, the miracle fiber of nature, to reinvigorate the failure that was the original release of The Stanley Parable. Should this exemplary game be an example to any developer that desires to deliver a comforting, fulfilling and heart-felt experience that only a healthy and daily dose of The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe can provide,

_childDocuments_.review: From (from) the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved video game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made.It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone, for the stone into which The Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted, offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change and you may become more; so much more than you were before.If there is any message to be taken from The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, it is this:"What a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience! It leaves me hopeful that as a community - as a world, there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future."
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the hell outta the original Stanley Parable back when it was new, I went into this with hopes of a ton of new content. Though I did really try to temper my realistic expectations to maybe only a handful of new endings so I wouldn't be disappointed.The first few playthroughs I enjoyed the small tweaks on a few of my favourite endings from the original SP, but was feeling a bit bummed that it just seemed to be basically the same game. Then, around playthrough  4, I spotted a doorway labelled 'new content'. Of course I went straight through the doorway.The hours that followed were full of some of the most thought provoking, philosophical and darkly hilarious interactive content I've experienced in my 30-odd years as a gamer. Though I will say the narrator does ramble on sometimes, so kudos to the devs for developing the groundbreaking skip button feature.For anyone who enjoyed the OG SP but is wondering if Ultra Deluxe brings enough to the table to warrant buying it again, I'd say emphatically yes. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me be clear: This is not a cash-grab re-release of the original game with just a few more endings, it really is a re-imagining. I own the original game, and I am very happy with my purchase of this one.Like the original, this is a game best played with no spoilers, so I won't give any here. I just invite you to remember how you felt the first time you played the original - unable to fully grasp the game's fleeting narrative structure, trying to find footing within the story, surprised and delighted by the subversion of expectation. If you're anything like me, this version of the game will reignite the same sense of wonder that captured you nearly a decade ago.They really explored every possible narrative theme in this, so I couldn't imagine them making another follow-up. With this version, the series now feels satisfyingly complete.The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe manages to take the original Stanley Parable, a game about nothing, and flesh it out into a much richer, much more ambitious game about nothing. And the Narrator is with you for every step of this terrible, beautiful, dumb, excellent non-journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I could not be bothered to play this game to full completion. The narrator is obnoxious and unfunny, with his humor and dialog proving to be more irritating than entertaining. The individual paths themselves are also not very fun, not offering much to do throughout each path, and requiring some rather tedious nonsense to get certain endings. I cannot reccomend this game to anyone, even as a "so bad it's good" game, as you'll more than likely wind up bored by your third or fourth play through.- buglivia, 2018

_childDocuments_.review: Was it good: Yes. The narrator is what made the game for me, and the developers obviously have an incredible sense of taste and humor. It was very funny.Worth $25 bucks: No. Try $15-$20? I played it for 4 hours, without looking anything up, and completed nearly 98% of the game. After I was sure that I did most of the stuff, I browsed the internet for the endings and - yeah, I missed only 2, and that was that.Worth re-playing: Well... there's not much to do anymore... So that's 4 hours for $25 bucks, or, you could take your bro/mate out for a movie date. Your choice.It's funny, and good... but I do have a bit of buyers remorse over $25 for 4 hours of game play. I don't even worry about spending money usually! I do make a very good income as a traveling Healthcare Worker. But I'm just a bit surprised that it was only 4 hours of game play, and I did stretch it out as much as I could.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly funny, creative, satirical and overpriced. The first game was already a little gem but this deluxe edition includes more to see and find while having a lot to add to it’s original themes. People who played the original should wait for a sale as I don’t think it’s ENOUGH to justify it, but for newcomers it’s absolutely worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I think as a concept there are many things to be taken from The Stanley Parable: ULTRA DELUXE. Many of those things are are concepts, such as the concept of choice, as it rightly points out. There is an idea that choice, where is does or does not exist in the fathomless depths of Stanley's imagination. The Stanley Parable: ULTRA DELUXE expands this idea by infusing a philosophical treatise with a pseudo-quantum parabola masquerading as a conceptualization of Schrodinger's cat. Which is to say that you cannot know outcome of choice without not making the not-choice as the choice of not making choices is choice in of itself, as you may well know, that brings you no closer to equating the size of a non-existent non-cat with a shape of an inverse-U, ect. In The Stanley Parable: ULTRA DELUXE, you control an entity colloquially identified as "Stanley", or perhaps the narrator, in their effort to either make or not make choices. _childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead– murdered by my brother-in-law, Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now, and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, he asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded. I... I always thought Hank was a very moral man, and I was particularly vulnerable at the time – something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me in on a ride-along and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin, so I agreed. Hank had a partner, a businessman named Gustavo Fring. Hank sold me into servitude to this man. And when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling-out. Things escalated. Fring was able to arrange – uh, I guess... I guess you call it a "hit" – on Hank, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured. And I wound up paying his medical bills, which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge. Working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring. The bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA. To keep me in line, he took my children. For three months, he kept them. My wife had no idea of my criminal activities, and was horrified to learn what I had done. I was in hell. I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, and in response, he gave me this. [Walt points to the bruise on his face left by Hank in "Blood Money."] I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. All I could think to do was to make this video and hope that the world will finally see this man for what he really is.

_childDocuments_.review: From the ashes of depravity rises the phoenix of quality. How else to describe "The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe"? Such a revolutionary step forward in the lineage of one of the most beloved game properties of all time! The additions and changes made to this expansion will surely resonate in the annals of the history of all media ever made. It is perhaps true to say that no mistakes are forever etched in stone, for the stone into which the Stanley Parable was carved has itself been transmuted, offering a message of hope to those who have ever erred in their judgement. You are not beyond redemption. You may change, and you may become more, so much more than you were before. If there is any message to be taken from "The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe", it is this... what a fortune, a privilege, a joy it is to have had such an experience it leaves me hopeful that as a community — as a world, there is time for us to become our greatest selves, as great as we ever could dream of in our wildest, most ambitious visions for a brighter future.

The jokes and references still hold to this day and the whole feeling that game gave seems to have been ahead of its time in terms of the ‘liminal space’ trend.This game however, reminded me that games are art. If you want more laughs then this game has you covered in new jokes and references to the original, but it also emotionally engaged me in a way that only a few games do.This game is visibly overflowing with the effort put behind it and I believe it’s best for you to experience it blind like I have.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first game not so long ago and I wanted to check out this one that came out last year. From the start, you can tell its just an HD remake of the beloved Stanley Parable from 2013 that everyone has grown to know and love. I played through it normally the first few times and then the extra content kicked in. Immediately, I was overwhelmed with all of the new things to see and do, new buttons to push, more little clues to seek out and more dialogue from the wonderful Narrator. My first thoughts were wonder, this was definitely a step up from the original but not in a bad way. From being self aware from reviews and trying to give the game more charm than the original, it felt more like it's own game other than a sequel to the main Stanley Parable. I do tend to hyper fixate and dive too deep into what a game may be about. I did this for the first game as well. Having all of these silly characters in a game that follows a story, it makes you think of the reflections of the real world. I think that could be one of the main messages it wants you to follow but then again, that couldn't be the case. It's a long trip of self discovery. It's similar to the game made after the original Stanley Parable, The Beginners Guide. Each ending, each path, each decision the player makes for Stanley, it's a reflection of the choices that you, yes, you, yourself are making in your everyday life. This does depend on the life you lead but how these decisions can affect yourself and the people around you are for your choosing. Having little details for the players and much more was such a joy to discover. Playing a game that makes you think deep about life are hidden under some of the places you would never think to look, I surely did. Life is certainly a blessing isn't it? It's amazing what a simple game can teach you about things that you've been searching for your entire life. Bravo to the team that have made this game to really make me reflect more about myself and the paths, friends and choices I will make in my future. Hopefully, someone else out there will think that too, I really hope they do :)

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm.... I actually didn't play the original game, I've been hearing about this game but only managed to try it after watching a bit of Slay The Princess (which I'm excited to get later) and heard it's inspired by this. I was excited to see what it's all about!Generally, I find the humor kind of juvenile and dated. Well, it was from 2011 I think? And irony was In in those days I suppose, and adding that there wasn't many games poking at the nature of choices in narrative-based games back then... I can see how this got a huge following. I don't mind goofy jokes mixed in if there were something genuine in there but I don't think there's any... in fact, the game seems to be mocking me for trying to look for one? For trying to take it seriously as a narrative?Which is like, one thing. But the newer stuffs are worse because they're like.... new? They got developed in, what, 2019? 2020? And the tone remains the same level of juvenile? Worse still, they're mocking long-time fans(!) who want new stuffs in a game they're paying real money for? They're putting in real negative Steam reviews on blast to everyone playing this game? I got reminded of a local film which reviewers said "love letter to the cinema" but keep doing ♥♥♥♥ like talking about 'cliched' shots filmmakers do on climax scene, while the movie did each shot one by one, all while the supposed climax scene (where I'm supposed to be feeling about the, you know, plot) is happening. And how 90% of it is a 'fake' movie that uses every 'tired' romcom trope and the 10% is the characters talking about how stupid the movie is. Stop talking 10 paragraphs about the empty joy of collecting or whatever, I love clicking at figurines because I paid money to play games and everyone knows it is the nature of games that people will try to be complete it! Don't make people go through 'empty' new contents because it's a 'commentary' on how games like to make sequels with 'empty' new contents??I do have to say though, I'm genuinely impressed with such annoying attitude of writing narratives they somehow managed to keep the narrator charming. The idea of narrator weaving a story to 'free' Stanley from his lethargic way of living, but that story and Stanley's existence are also what keeps narrator alive and they're desperate in keeping the story going is very fun. Narrator having the capability of cruelty to the point of killing Stanley if he rebels against them but is crying and throwing up when Stanley *actively* kills himself or throws the narrator away, narrator being sick of Stanley keeping himself in a cubicle jail while also losing their mind at the idea of open world game.... the desire of control and codependency wrestling against each other.... *chef's kiss*The juxtaposition of neurotic narrator who's obsessed to make better and better 'eternal' story with Settings who's content with having passive relationship in the darkness within never-changing games is also an interesting concept I wish were written in a less.... this *hand gestures* way. But yeah, I do still like the characters despite being very annoyed at the attitude of the writing as a whole. I let narrator rambled way longer than normal people do in Skip ending and was excited to meet Settings every restart, that's how much I like them.I think if you're interested in this game with the same reasons as me, it's still worth to play if not to see the roots because I do enjoy looking through my favourite works' references. Else, I think there's a lot of medias playing with the concept of free will and choices in more interesting ways nowadays...

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to understand why anyone would dislike The Stanley Parable. It's a classic, a humourous exploration of the concept of free will vs determinism correlated against the concept of video game design. Did it need an ultra deluxe edition? Probably not. It does at least allow the game to transition to consoles so the plebs can enjoy what we master race played almost a decade ago. Do you need to buy it again? Nah. But you can... if you want to... if you think you actually have a choice... Maybe, Stanley, your mind is already made up. Personally, I'm enjoying it, though it definitely felt a little smoother in source than unity, the new content is as drily amusing as expected.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. It does a really great job of not only replicating, but adding on to the mind-blowing feel of playing The Stanley Parable for the first time. It does a great job developing characters (surprisingly), has a lot of very humorous moments, and has some really deep moments that made me pause the game and think about what just happened. The only downside of this game is that now I experience all that again. I am really going to miss the feelings this brought me as I played it. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Very funny, all StanleyI thoroughly enjoyed the original and this felt like a great mix of funny new material with some nice call backs thrown in. That being said, while I enjoyed the new content I don't feel like every returning player will think this game is worth the price. It's tricky because I don't want to spoil the game, but it's worth putting that out there. Maybe consider doing some research at your own risk, though if you're on the fence I say just take the plunge and pick it up on sale. For any new players though, I whole heartedly recommend this game. Same great base game that provides a unique and humorous interactive-narrative based experience now with added fun to enjoy, but zero the futile longing for more Stanley Parable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite simple: if you liked the original, you'll almost certainly like "The Stanley Parable Ultra Deluxe". The game builds on the original, but there's more than enough new content and there are several new endings. It is important to know that the new content is not thrown at you, but that you have to actively discover it. That's probably why there are so many negative reviews with playing times of two to three hours. The developers constantly poke fun at themselves for just selling a new rehash, but for me there was more than enough to discover. Like the original, you're basically playing the same map over and over to discover new areas or new endings. What is really entertaining are the narrator's wonderful comments, which are sometimes full of black humour, sometimes full of self-mockery and sometimes full of self-pity. Not to forget: There is now a bucket. Praise the bucket!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story, about a man named Stanley, that you may have heard before.If I had the choice to spend my £13 on a Domino's pizza with extra trimmings to enjoy for less than an hour and increase my waistline for until I burned it off, or The Stanley Parable Ultimate Deluxe to enjoy for at least 6 hours, and replay however I want, and share with friends. I would choose the Stanley Parable Ultimate Deluxe every time.And frankly, as entertainment mediums go, that's the kind of decision you're making, £13 was the reduced rate since I already owned The Stanley Parable and it seems to equate about 6 hours of additional gameplay on top of the original game which is also in there.The Stanley Parable Ultimate Deluxe is satire.The game has moved from the Source engine, to the Unity engine, and with that comes a problem that the 2D interface is not designed for ultrawide, but that problem aside, it has allowed the developer to create a game which feels like it's what the creator wanted to make in the first place, it finally gives the developer creative freedom outside of the game engine, because they have control over the entire thing.If you're new to the Stanley Parable, you're in for a treat. There's a lot of replayability here as you find every nook and cranny in the game.If you're not new to the Stanley Parable, and you liked the dry humour of the first, you're going to enjoy this game. Especially if you are also share the mindset of being somewhat tired of typical gaming and game development tropes as the developer also is. It's somewhat of a more mature humour for those who have probably grown up with gaming for a long time.As I said, it's satire.I enjoyed the game, I laughed, and I haven't laughed at a game in a long time. Thank you for that, after 9 years from when the original came out, and I'd sunk a good number of hours into that before it was on Steam, where I then played it for an additional 3.Maybe I'll order a domino's next month.

This isn't a game with much replay value once you're done, but you're unlikely to regret the experience.

name: The Expanse: A Telltale Series
detailed_description: Experience the exciting universe of The Expanse like never before in Telltale’s latest adventure, The Expanse: A Telltale Series. Take on the role of Camina Drummer and explore the dangerous and uncharted edges of the Belt aboard the Artemis. From scavenging wrecked ships in a zero-g environment, to surviving a mutiny, to combating fearsome pirates, you make the difficult choices and reveal Camina Drummer’s resolve in this latest Telltale adventure. A TELLTALE STORY LIKE NO OTHER Immerse yourself in the role of Camina Drummer, the Executive Officer aboard the Artemis, a scavenging ship hunting for a big score in the outer regions of the Belt. You must corral a crew rife with tense relationships and powerful personalities, and make tough decisions that will decide everyone’s fate. EXPLORE THE BELT IN ZERO-G Scour shipwrecks, use mag boots to walk on walls and ceilings, and utilize zero-g thrusters to float through the void. As you fly through sections of ships and the open expanse of space, interact with objects in the world and converse with members of the crew in the largest and most immersive exploration of any Telltale game to date. DIFFICULT CHOICES, GRAVE CONSEQUENCES Contend with the unforgiving brutality of space, the politics of a corrupt solar system, the animosities of your crew, and Drummer’s own conflicting responsibilities to the people she cares about and the Belt she has sworn to protect. There is no right or wrong path - only your choices and the consequences they unleash. INCLUDES ALL 5 EPISODES Episode 1: Archer's Paradox Episode 2: Hunting Grounds Episode 3: First Ones Episode 4: Impossible Objects Episode 5: Europa's Folly

_childDocuments_.review: The Expanse Telltales is a very good narrative game. It's a prequel to one of the characters (Camina Drummer) from the TV show of the same name. If you like the series (or the books) you'll love this game, as you'll be immersed in the universe from the moment you arrive at the menu.
