_childDocuments_.review: This is proving to be a pretty difficult game to review.  On the one hand, I enjoyed myself, and that's enough for a positive review.  The character designs are visually fantastic and consistently-written, the soundtrack is great, and the vibes of the game are nice.  With that said, though, I do have some complaints.First, I encountered some bugs in the game, some merely visual (art assets appearing on the wrong layer), while others affected the gameplay.  It was uncommon, but you should prepare to miss a small number of lines of dialogue, have minigame issues (the heart monitor minigame is especially prone to fail to recognize inputs), and sometimes require a forced game close in the middle of a scene because the controls froze.  Annoying, but you can play past it.  There are additionally issues with the English localization, but more a word repeat/misssing/strange turn of phrase, and those were very rare and not especially distracting.The final issue for me was the writing, and this was a little more of a pervasive issue.  On the one hand, the characters are interesting, believable, and consistent, which is what you'd want in a story like this.  On the other hand, there are severe issues with pacing, made all the worse by large empty areas of the map and frequent path blocking that puts more time between you and your next snippet of dialogue.  Well, I shouldn't say the areas are "empty", there are wonderful art assets everywhere, but I prefer to also have more things to do during my cross-town excursions, and this game doesn't have quite as much to offer in that regard.  On the other hand, there is a very sudden and severe ramp of stakes towards the end of the game, with little in the way of a conclusion for most arcs.  I'm talking like, almost zero falling action or resolution.  Some of the events of the climax could also have used more in the way of foreshadowing, though there were elements scattered here and there for some points.  Was it still good?  Yes, absolutely.  Again, I had fun.  Did it need some editing passes and maybe more time to help the game shine a little brighter?  You betcha.One thing I'll say, regarding a thread of comparison running through many other reviews, is that this is not just Second Night In The Woods.  The tone, plot, characters, and themes are all dramatically different, and one should not base their desire to purchase this game on whether or not they liked that one.  The trailer for the game is a good representation of what you'll find.  If you like what you see, go for it.  Just don't expect all 2D sidescrolling games with animal characters to be the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really like Fall of Porcupine. It's a lot of fun, the characters are nice and interesting, the story and plot that's set up has me engaged, and the world they built is fun to see and feels like a great town. Unfortunately this game is also a buggy mess and it's just not something I can recommend in this state. I hope it gets fixed because what I've seen is a genuinely good story that I do recommend, it's just part of a game that's really unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Lots of bugs, a very long beginning before the story gets good, and the mechanics of some of the minigames in the hospital lead me to not recommend this game.I finished the whole game wanting to give it a chance and I liked the storyline of the game, but here's why I wouldn't recommend playing: - It has far too many bugs: characters will walk away while in conversation with you and their dialogue will move offscreen to be unreadable, some minigames wouldn't work correctly. It seemed like it needed more time in beta testing for them to work out all of the bugs, they don't make the game unplayable but they are very frustrating. There were also issues with the dialogue itself, there were many missed or misspelled words and some sentences I struggled to make sense of, this impacted the experience and the overall message when you don't know what a character is trying to say. - The main cast of three characters that we see the most of (Finley, Mia, and Karl) feel very one-dimensional. They don't really feel like a friend group all together and I found myself not very attached to Finley as a main character.- The hospital minigames got old very fast and the difficulty scale was not very consistent, at first they were easy, then it seemed the next time they became very difficult, and then the next time were a medium difficulty. I suppose you could justify that as commentary but it was very frustrating for the gameplay.- The play time is very long and the story takes a while to get interesting. It does become an interesting story, but the beginning of the game could have cut down SEVERELY and it would make it much more enjoyable, as it is now I wouldn't recommend getting through the beginning to get to the good parts at the very end of the story. Overall, it has the bones of a game good game, I love the setting and the character design and like I said it has a good story and a good message it just takes too long to get there.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: To be perfectly honest, I wasn't familiar with Fall of Porcupine until very recently. I saw the trailer for the game at one of the summer conferences and was immediately interested in the art style and the premise. A lot of people seem to compare it to Night in The Woods, but I believe this is a little bit disingenuous because, while maybe the devs took some inspiration from NITW, Fall of Porcupine has a lot to offer as its own product.The game was a welcoming surprise that kept me invested from start to finish. The narrative actively explores themes of freedom, loss, sacrifice, and the never ending resilience of the human spirit. You're a young doctor that just moved into a new city and started taking first steps by working in the local hospital. During the daytime, you will be tasked with numerous hospital chores in the form of mini-games and I felt that there was enough variety there to keep you engaged as your progress through the story. The main theme of the game is to show that working in a hospital is not an easy task, and you can't expect to be able to save everyone.In your downtime, you'll be able to socialize with the local crowd, plus you can hang out and explore deeper relationships with your friends. There is a city to explore, but there are not a lot of side activities to be done, there is some roof climbing and the odd tidbit in your apartment with which you can interact, but most of the interactions with the environment are tied to story stuff.In my playthrough, I noticed some bugs. Some of the button prompts didn't work, and the notes app on your phone wasn't showing, until you started the app again. Part of the dialogue was repeating or wasn't showing it all and there were some grammatical errors, but mostly it was nothing that affected my enjoyment of the game.I truly believe that this title deserves more attention, there is a demo you can try so if you like story-driven games with some fun mini-games and interesting characters, give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you a little story.I'm roughly 2/3 through the game, coming off of a very emotional scene where our main character is confronted with the inevitability of death. In the moments immediately afterward, other characters reel from the impact of this death in the community and grieve together. As I go around back of the local bar, I encounter another of the hospital staff, wracked with survivors guilt, and help him come to terms with the fact that there are things we can't control, actions can have unknowable consequences, and we have to move on regardless.Tragically, while entering this part of the game, the main character's torso despawned, meaning that this lovely dialogue was coming out of a raymanesque pile of floating limbs.Fall of Porcupine, frankly, is riddled to the gills with bugs. Some are serious enough to require a restart (talking to a certain NPC after a cutscene disables your movement controls, pressing the wrong button when starting the dancing minigame changed my game language to French, etc.), but even the purely cosmetic ones are a hammerblow to the immersion and atmosphere. This is a 2D talk-'em-up, and is somehow as broken as a modern AAA release.It's a shame, because I really enjoyed most of my time with Fall of Porcupine. The story was quite touching up until it abruptly stopped, and the art design, obviously, is excellent. There's a lovely game in here, but I can't in good conscience recommend it until it's fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game and it pains me to leave a negative review but I honestly just can't recommend it. There are lots of things some big and some small that bring this game down and it could've been such a great experience.I picked up this game mostly because I was interested in the story. I feel like topics around healthcare aren't explored nearly enough so I was extremely interested in how they handle representing underfunded hospitals and overworked staff but I'm really sorry to say I was disappointed at best and I felt kind of insulted at worst. The healthcare system isn't perfect. I feel like everyone has been critical of it at least once whether you complain about high prices or long wait times. These topics are tackled in the story as a passing mention but the people that are most vocal about these issues are portrayed as a couple of angry idiots and the game makes it very clear that you should see them as such. Very disappointing to see a portrayal like that especially because a lot of the criticism for the healthcare system has a lot of nuance to it. I do not need this game to hold a really deep philosophical conversation about healthcare but I was really hoping for a story that's grounded a little more reality especially how I saw it mention that they interviewed healthcare workers when writing the story. The story also feels kind of slow. I get that you'd want to develop the characters before the drama to make the player care about them more, but for how abruptly this game ends, the time spent outside the hospital feels disproportionate. And this feeling is only made worse by the lack of animations, music and weird sound mixing. The characters regardless of situations rarely change their expressions and don't even look at each other while talking. All of them have maybe one idle and one talking animation and this coupled with almost non-existent talking sound effects made the conversations really static and quiet regardless of what was actually being said. The music was very nice when it was there but the majority of the game is spent in complete silence or just ambient sound effects of wind or crickets that are sometimes so loud that they drown out the already quiet music. The game also has some weird tonal shifts kicking off loud and bright minigames in the middle of a quiet and dark moment. There's one pretty serious event in the game that pretty much starts most of the drama of this story and has major consequences later but while you're doing it it's just a funny rpg-like minigame with funny music and goofy attacks! I just couldn't take that moment seriously because of it. Again I wanted to love this game! The art style is cute and nostalgic, the lore that they came up with for the town of Porcupine is cool, and the characters all felt distinct, but the issues I mentioned above dragged it down too much :(
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I was so hoping to write a positive review for this game! Right up until the end I was going to. So many typos and grammar issues in the dialogue, and could be a bit clunky at times (glitches and mini games not working correctly) but the story and atmosphere and characters were well done so I was enjoying it anyways. BUT THE ENDING!!!! SO SO SO SO LAME. SO DISAPPOINTING!! Without giving spoilers let's just say, there was sooooooooo much left unsaid and so much left unresolved. What a sad and lame ending to an otherwise not perfect, but lovely game. If the developers were to add more to the ending, actually resolve things- then I will gladly come back and recommend this game, but I am honestly just so sad right now at the lame ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a happy ending... this isn't the game for you. That being said... if you want a game that gives you insight into the healthcare system? This is a definite. You want to feel things? This game does that.As a healthcare employee the story of this game resonated strongly with what I've experienced over the last decade. It hits hard regardless of where you live (devs are from Germany, I live in the US).I enjoyed the game. The art style is wonderful. I love the little details like when you float as Finley your 'wings' and tail get a bit floofier. Most the characters feel really solid.The things I didn't enjoy... the mini puzzles were meh. They weren't difficult but they also weren't overly exciting. They were such a small part compared to the story that it didn't matter as much to me.  The other thing was the leading and spacing of the text in the speech bubbles in English. Seemed everywhere an 's was used there was a space between the word and the 's. Example: It 's, we 'll, etc. And there were some areas where I think the translating went bad, extra words that made things sound wrong. A few times all the text didn't fit in the speech bubble. But if you are used to reading auto-corrected text to speech from friends and family, you'll figure it out easily enough.But these 'bad' things are things didn't really affect how the game played or the message it was giving. The game overall is rather solid and was enjoyable to play, despite the heaviness of the story. Prepare yourself for an emotional journey and you may want to keep a box of tissues nearby.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so initially I had a meme review, but now I need to be serious.This is a fantastic spiritual successor to NITW. But it is unfortunately marred by game breaking bugs. During my time I experienced two.1. Pina (a character in game) ceased to exist after a cutscene during the festival. This softlocked the game as you must talk to her to progress forward during this portion. Fortunately I found that letting her remain close before initiating dialog that caused the cutscene would prevent the glitch.2. The button prompts during one of the doctor minigames refused to appear, thus softlocking the game. I haven't actually found any solution, and I am currently stuck here. Unable to progress. Ironically this softlock takes place roughly 15-30 minutes after my previously listed one.I'm leaving my review as positive for now, as I do overall enjoy the game. And the game has been receiving frequent patches. So I'll remain hopeful for now. Expect an edit soon if this is / isn't fixed in the near future.UPDATE: A recent patch fixed it and I was finally able to progress. _childDocuments_.review: The only good things this game really has going for it is that the art and characterization were solid.No real story, no real character progress, definitely no ending. Plus all the bugs (one of them actually game-breaking - the snowball fight), the terrible mini-games with terrible instructions...A game of great promise that sadly falls short of that promise in nearly every category.

_childDocuments_.review: fall of porcupine, a night in the woods like adventure with stunning art, sweet ambient music and incredible characters. the town itself is simply a work of art, the way it changes with the weather is breathtaking and makes the world feel alive, which makes up for the fact that you have to spend a lot of time walking across the town if you want to interact with everything and talk to everyone - i spent a lot of time just walking and praying i wouldn't be locked out of exploring the other part of time before finley's workday starts. the music was an incredible bonus and didn't get on my nerves even after spending at least an hour real time going through the town, which says a lot about how great it is in my opinion.the characters are amazing and it definitely pays off to spend time with them and talk to them as much as you can. finley is a quirky protagonist who admittedly talks a bit too much sometimes, mainly when you interact with objects in the town (mostly the statues.) the other big characters are wondeful and it pays off to play the game twice to see all the hang out options between the two main friends. the story is heavy, real and incredible. i laughed, i cried, i cried some more and then the big shock came and i prayed it wasn't the end only to be hit with the ending titles. the story will leave you feeling vulnerable, shocked, nostalgic, everything and nothing at once. it is raw and bittersweet and so worth it. my only issue is the occasional bug here and there - sometimes when a character follows finley they start sort of flying in the background or get stuck somewhere. my other main issue was with the stethoscope minigame - it felt a bit laggy but admittedly i do suck at it so it might just be me. i also want to quickly highlight the accessibility (that i use every time i have to do the stethoscope minigame and somehow still fail, who knows if it's me at this point.)all in all, i recommend this game - the story, art, characters, music; the emotions you get out of it, all of it is worth a few bugs that i hope will be fixed in an update. i give it 8.5/10 and will definitely play again (i really want that last achievement hehe)

_childDocuments_.review: This one is tough. I played the demo for Fall of Porcupine during the Steam Next Fest and was really looking forward to the full release. I love the premise of what it's like working in a little hospital for a little isolated town, the artwork is great, and I enjoyed talking to and getting to know the characters, but after finally getting the time to sit down with it (about 5-6 hours, some offline), I just felt like I was pushing myself to make any progress. The story wasn't exciting enough to keep me interested, the mini-games offered no challenge, a LOT of time spent walking from A-B, and the constant bugs and visual issues I ran into were frustrating. I think I understand what the writers were going for, but everything felt just a bit too mundane. I think what this game is trying to say could have been accomplished in half the time, or less, with more respect for the player's time. For example, fast-travel exists (kinda) but only for one specific thing and you still need to walk a lot to and from the fast travel location. If you're not going to that same spot per the plot, fast travel was unavailable and you had to spend 5 min walking to a place you've already been to before. Eventually, it just didn't feel worth it to continue playing. Secondly, the bugs. Oh gosh. I played on Steam Deck and I struggle to see how this game is 'verified' on deck. I constantly ran into things like: Text cut off the screen, the aspect ratio incorrect and cut off during conversation/mini games, characters getting stuck on walking paths while following, text overflowing the speech bubbles, text auto-skipping when pressing a button to load the chat bubble but other times it wouldn't skip, audio cutting out oddly, etc. Maybe it was just the platform I played on wasn't tested, but the game felt unpolished and like it wasn't thoroughly play-tested. This feels a little harsh, I know a lot of work went into the game, but when text is cut off or overflowing in a visual novel it's very obvious. This game is lovely, it has a lot of things going for it that it does very well, but as a fully packaged game it just didn't work for me. Additionally, I think the comparisons to Night in the Woods will leave folks disappointed. If I were to recommend this game it would be to someone who really loves visual novels and have some personal connection to the medical industry, but only after it's been patched.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{Gameplay}---☐ Replayability t ☐ Hours upon hours of fun! ☐ Good at parts. ☑ Nothing to remember. ☐ Ping Pong is better. Very simple gameplay, a few mini-games are thrown in, some are fine, others are a bit broken or hard to understand. ---{Story}---☐ It will change your life forever! ☐ You'll stay up all night thinking about it! ☑ Just enough to not skip the cutscene. ☐ Glimpses of good writing. ☐ Monkeys on typewriters could do better. The plot is slice of life until near the end, most of the game you're waiting for something to happen. There are small hints of a bigger thing at play, but they too don't add up enough to get the mystery rolling until the ending happens. The story itself is quite standard, but it has some cute and cozy parts to it. I think if they were to revamp some of the game, they should add more clues to the big surprise. And most importantly add an epilogue!---{Characters}---☐  deep investment into memorable characters! ☐ Well written and have lots of depth! ☑ Enjoyable to watch and interact with! ☐ They do their job well enough. ☐ Unlikable, and not in the good way. Most of the residents of Porcupine have their own charm to them, which is a little sad because they get very little screen-time. Some characters have 4 or 5 conversations through out the game, others have only a few lines of dialogue.'Main' characters have enough screen time to start having a connection with, but they don't really grow. The protagonist Finley doesn't have much of an arc through out the game. Sure, he gets better caring for patients and grows closer to his friends, but that's what most people would do anyway given enough time.One event in the game could be considered a growing moment for him, but it's not like he changes as a character after. He just goes through the moment and the game carries on. Any time for growth at the end is put to the side for the finale. And then the game just ends. I like Finley and the other characters, i'd loved to see a more fulfilling conclusion for them.---{Did I Cry?}---☐ It emotionally scarred me, for better or for worse. ☐ Yes, tears were had... ☐ My eyes got a bit teary. ☑ No crying, but it it still impacted me. ☐ My eyes have never been drier. Despite a lot of problems I did enjoy the story, more than I thought I would. Many of the characters were nice, maybe too many, but they were fun to watch. Sadly though with the ending being quite sudden, not being attached to most of the characters, and the lack of an epilogue, it wasn't enough for even a single tear. This isn't a sad game though, so that's to be expected.---{Graphics}---☐ Beautiful art style, unforgettable. ☑ Uniqe and gorgeous! ☐ Your standard nice looking graphics. ☐ A bit ugly or hard on the eyes. ☐ You call these graphics? The style of the characters are simple yet pleasant, and the art design of the Porcupine is cozy.---{Soundtrack}---☐ One in a billion, a must listen! ☑ They knew what they were doing! ☐ Pretty good! ☐ Eeeeehhh. ☐ Just mute it in options. Most of your time spent is in the hospital or walking around the streets, and the music accompanies that well. It's not stand-out like some other games, but it's still really nice.---{Audio}---☐ More enjoyable than actual music! ☐ Your ears will enjoy it! ☐ Better then most games! ☑ About average. ☐ As bad as nails against a chalk board. Mostly footsteps with a few ambient noises. I did notice some audio levels being louder than others.---{Atmosphere}---☐ It's so dense you could cut it with a knife! ☐ I take a moment to appreciate it every now and then! ☑ Quite likeable! ☐ It works well enough. ☐ Welp... they tried. Porcupine is a pretty big town, a lot of running is needed to get from one end to the other. After a dozen or so trips it can get tedious, but they did a good job making it interesting enough for the first playthrough. The vibe of the town is very connected, it really does feel like everyone you see lives there together, each person knowing the other.---{Bugs}---☐ Not one. Not a single one! ☐ Noticed a few ☑ Can happen often. ☐ Persistent in the game. ☐  The worst part of the game, softlocks, UI bugs, overlapping issues, dialogue repeating or showing up in the wrong place. Over time I hope these are fixed, because this game deserves better.---{Price}---☐ It's free to play!☐ Full price!☑ Wait for a sale.☐ Wait for a  sale.☐ Save your money for anything else.For $20 this is a fine game, if you're looking for another NITW you won't get the same experience. But if you're okay with a simple game with a simple story, this is far from the worst you could choose. Get on sale if you're unsure though. Or try the demo! Apparently it takes place before the start of this game, so it might be a good idea to try it either way.---{Ranking}---☐ G.O.T.Y!☐ 8/10!☑ Better then average!☐ It was OK.☐ Eh, not for me.☐ Don't bother even looking at it.Fall of Porcupine left a soft spot in my heart, it has a nice story with good characters. Honestly most of it's issues could be solved, or at least alleviated, with the addition of an epilogue. I really hope the best for the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: However the game aspect leaves more to be desired. I spent too long running around the town trying to find something interesting when there wasn't much. I played the game 100% on the steam deck and I learned quick that some of the mini-games were not designed for it like the bandage wrapping part. After beating the game I went back in with simple mini-games turned on and it still has deck users trying to hit and hold directional and other buttons that's just nearly impossible to do. Playing with a keyboard was the intended way.  I also noticed that the stethoscope mini-game just doesn't register some of the inputs neither, so be okay with not being able to A grade the harder versions of that mini-game. There were a few other minor bugs like the dance animations not being displayed when hanging out with Karl. I want to emphasize, the draw for Fall of Porcupine is the story, characters, art, and some of the music pieces. Fall of Porcupine is an interesting experience with heartfelt moments. The visuals drew me in and I did feel good about most of my time spent with it. Tips I have are: hold X (or whatever equivalent on the keyboard) to get through speech bubbles instantly instead of having the unfolding type-writer effect; and don't wander around too much in town there isn't much to do—sorry to Frauke and homeless walrus guy and comic book kid; it wasn't that interesting of my time spent, lol. The town center location, Pina, a friend to Finley, and the hospital is where the good stuff happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Kaaaaarl!... ahem.Fall of Porcupine leaves me really torn. The story and characters felt great, and while the town could've been more dense, it was at least sufficiently filled with life (given that you technically aren't supposed to spend a lot of your time exploring).But. Bugs! So many of them! (I played this game on Steam Deck, so YMMV on PC, but in any case this is not how "Deck verified" is supposed to look like.)And not just the occasional visual glitch or clunky movement that could be overlooked when it comes to indie titles, but the softlocking sort (e.g. ) that forced me to close and reopen the game a dozen or so times - meaning a return to the most recent one of the way-too-sparse auto-save points, every time.Add to that certain minigames where inputs don't properly register or the timing is significantly off - this sluggishness being blatantly noticeable when activating the minigame accessibility option - and you're in for a frustrating gameplay experience.As such I really can't recommend this game, as much as I want to for its narrative aspects; not in the broken state it's in. Maybe that'll change if the devs should decide to return to releasing patches at some point, instead of leaving this as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really hard review to write because I really wanted to enjoy playing this game because the demo was really good and I enjoyed interacting with all of the characters.Long story short:- Fall of Porcupine takes place after the demo, if you haven't played the demo, you won't understand what is going on. Why the progress from the demo wasn't carried over to the main game baffles me...- This game needs a map, it takes too long for Finley to travel to each destination. Why is the hospital so far away from everything?- The pacing of this game is completely off. The first chapter is very well paced. You get to know, understand the characters. _childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine uses one of the most beautiful art styles and heartfelt, philosophical narratives and dialogue with all the characters (even and especially some around town who you aren't required to talk to like Fauke at the fishing spot in the far left), however, the game could really use some additional polish. While it's nice that the bus stop and elevator can save time, they also cut out much of the potential narratives with residence that are required in order to build a stronger connection to everyone and the story itself. Fall of Porcupine is similar to Night in the Woods (the games are even structured the same where you have to choose between hanging out with either Mia or Karl), but where Night in the Woods spends more time building those solid connections and focusing on how things have changed dynamically between Gregg, Angus, Bea, Mae, and the other residence of Possum Springs as Mae finds herself, this isn't as fleshed out with Mia, Karl, Pina, and Finley and loses a lot of depth and charm as a result. There's so much to work with (at times almost too much where a lot could be stripped away), yet somehow leaves you wanting more simultaneously. That being said, there's charm in the narrative being based around real stories from those who work in healthcare, especially following COVID and is a delight visually. At the hospital there are a number of tasks: shots (one of the most boring of the hospital mini games requiring that you just release the required amount of medication in the red zone), diagnosis (an image based game similar to Wordle or Mastermind), EKG (somewhat similar to your standard Guitar Hero style rhythm game}, pill prescription (a somewhat math based logic puzzle of the fewest pills to prescribe and combine to get the desired result) and changing bedsheets (pressing and releasing buttons under time constraints). Some tasks are genuinely enjoyable while others do get a bit monotonous and tedious (and don't truly have an impact on the story regardless of whether you pass or "fail" (get a C). Overall, it's still a gorgeous narrative driven game that's cozy, especially for the fall season. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Note before reading this review: If there would be an option to give this review a neutral rating, I would have done that. As the story is awesome but the game is unnecessarily long and can feel like a slog to get through. Around the end, the story gets way more interesting and that feeling of it being a slog faded away.  16h? 2/10 2 No, not yet No Yes, many missable achievements No No No No No No you can use the accessibility settings and still unlock the achievements Maybe the one about wirting the comic? Read more around the end of this review for more info.Fall of Porcupine is a story-driven adventure game. You play as Finley, a junior doctor that recently moved to a small town called Porcupine for his new job. You'll meet the people that live in Porcupine, make friends, and work in the hospital. Treating your patients and some of the sidequests requires you to complete some mini-games. Most of them are fine and can be made easier through the accessibility setting in the menu... however, I have no idea how to get a good score in the mini-game for listening to someone's heart/longs. I sucked so so bad at those already at the beginning, let alone later on in the game when it gets harder. The game will warn you at the start of a new game that it deals with heavy subjects. This is very true and if you're sensible about those things, you might want to play this game later or decide it is not for you. As the story is very touching and emotional. It gives a look inside the life of somebody who is working in a hospital, bringing their best A game, but still failing from time to time. Especially around the end of the game, it made me think of healthcare workers during the pandemic. The game had a few bugs while I played through it, nothing really game-breaking but sometimes I could talk to people and then the conversation didn't start. Or was working on a quest but something else was listed at the top as a quest I should be working on. Having objectives at the top of the screen is also an accessibility option, but sometimes it was not accurate of what I should be doing. Another thing that brings the fun of playing Fall of Porcupine down a bit is that a lot of things feel long and slowed down. Rooms are long and most of the time patients lay at the end of the room, streets are long with not much to do in them, which makes them feel long. And since you move a lot through rooms/corridors and streets, it feels like this endless slug that becomes boring very soon. It ramps up the game time while not adding much to the game or the story. The surroundings are beautiful, but not when seeing them for the 5th time. Then the achievements... normally I make sure I can tell you all about them and have unlocked everything myself. However, in this case, I have only unlocked a little over 60%. I haven't unlocked everything as there are key moments in the story where you have to choose between option A and option B and both are tied to achievements, so you have to play at least twice through the game.  There is one achievement about writing a comic with one of the characters but maybe I didn't visit him enough, but randomly in the story he started talking again about wanting to write a story and started the questline from the start, which didn't give me enough time to get through it before the ending, not sure if I would have otherwise. There are also achievements that I have no idea how to unlock, as Emma never talked about a book and I have no clue where I should have heard the mysterious voices. Not having a clue about those 2 achievements and encountering a bug with the comic book storyline made that I didn't play through the game a second time.I did enjoy Fall of Porcupine, and I highly recommend it for the story. As it was so touching and emotional.

_childDocuments_.review: High hopes but no satisfying game.I have played the predecessor Night in the Woods before and I still love it to this day, for anyone reading this and considering this game, go buy Night in the Woods instead, but to anyone still reading I will summarize the goods and the bads in the following section.I will not focus on what the game is or its story for the most part.The good: - The Art stylesFall of Porcupine has a distinct visual art style best resembled by the game "Night in the Woods" and this was the main reason for me to buy it as I hoped for it to be a worthy sequel.-The main storyIt is of a doctor in his residency years. The idea is catchy and not seen often in games before. It is interesting to show the different parts of the medical sector working together. The Bad:- The interactions with the characters:There are not many dialogue choices and later in the game there are even viewers or none.Most of the game is a story that you progress through without shaping the main character’s personality.- The atmosphereThe game does not feel populated by people going on their daily routine and shops to visit and places to see. Most of the time you will travel from on location (most often your home) to another location ( most often the Hospital) but on your way only a hand full of NPC's will have dialogue options and nearly none of them will have you to decide what to say. Thos travel times feel long and take up a good chunk of the game, just walking.  There are only view times where locations are harder to reach that will yield a benefit (having to climb a house to reach a Head or an NPC) but these events are always visible to the player and easy to reach making them nearly impossible to miss. - The ConsequencesNo matter what you do or don't do, the story will progress at one pace and you cannot influence that or your relation to any of the NPC's. No minigame you fail or succeed in will have a lasting effect, not visiting locations daily will have just a bit of an impact on the small progression with the NPCs there.- The BugsI encountered several game breaking bugs: - the fuse box that you had to activate was not interactable, some dialogue did not progress, the phone did not open, NPC'S having the same dialogue or non and several minor visual glitches.- The MusicThe music has a small but not interesting set of pieces, with the title screen music being the most prominent. I would have liked a whider variety of soundtracks.-  The EndThe ending comes to shot and sudden and you are left with a feel of disbelief, you were not able to say goodbye to the characters you have meet and see the locations once again in a different light but a hart cut and a unscippable credit scene makes it really unpleasantThe game felt more like a stretched piece of gum that loses its flavor with each hour you play than the exiting story it could have been. I felt a lot of NPCs were not fully written out like the paramedics with whom you will have only really limited interaction possibilities. I want to make a view comparison of the (NITW) Night in the Woods and explain what is missing in this game.NITW had a lively city with lots of locations that you could visit and a lot of NPC'S at those locations. Each day their dialogue changed in a meaningful way and reflected your actions towards them, there were poems, story’s and friendships to be had, none of those are seen here (FOP). There were special cutsceens that you earn from having interacted often enough with on NPC and there where special events trigged by your action. Often these events were interactive and fun and so different. And don't forget about Deamon Tower.The Soundtrack was amazing, and you can listen to it even when not playing NITW. Fall of porcupine should have been the perfect sequel to NITW as previously you played a collage dropout dealing with the problems of going back to your hometown and in FOP you play a collage graduate who must deal with a bad life as well even though he reaches everything May (NITW min character) did not. All of that is missing in Fall of porcupine and so much more. I am disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to state this game is very pretty and the first half of the game is very enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: When I first stumbled upon "Fall of Porcupine," it immediately reminded me of the indie gem "Night in the Woods." Maybe it's the charming autumnal setting or the anthropomorphic animal characters that do the trick. Regardless, this PlayStation 5 adventure has a cozy feel with a unique twist—it delves into the life of a healthcare worker.Welcome to the snug town of Porcupine, where you step into the feathers of Finley, a bird who's now a doctor at the local hospital. Days here are spent juggling hospital shifts and exploring the town's nooks and crannies, engaging with its colorful residents.The game kicks off with Finley facing a patient crisis that leaves him temporarily out of work due to an injury. After his recovery, it's back to the hospital grind, and here's where you'll receive your tasks. Each workday involves caring for three patients, which essentially translates to playing some mini-games. These tasks, like needle injections and stethoscope use, are alright but can be somewhat frustrating and poorly explained. Your performance, whether stellar or subpar, doesn't seem to affect the patient's outcome, making it hard to invest in your minigame scores.However, the heart of this game lies in the interactions with its eclectic characters. The residents of Porcupine are bursting with personality and fascinating stories. Whether chatting with patients in the hospital or bonding with townsfolk, every conversation is a delight. But it's not all sunshine and rainbows. "Fall of Porcupine" tackles real healthcare issues like stress, and there are intriguing mysteries to uncover, both within the hospital and the town's history. While the story is engaging, it does suffer from pacing problems and a rushed conclusion.Visually, the game shines with detailed characters and a palette that exudes relaxation as you explore the town. However, there are performance hiccups and minor bugs, including frame rate drops and characters talking off-screen. The audio, on the other hand, is a perfect match for the small-town atmosphere."Fall of Porcupine" takes players on an emotional journey, shedding light on critical healthcare issues. It's not without its flaws, as the story can get tangled and rushed in places, and technical issues need addressing. Yet, these hitches don't overshadow the joy of living in this world and connecting with its captivating characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale, and I think the sale price is absolutely worth it. Full price, maybe not so much, ONLY for the ending of the game (and some of the "mini-game" mechanics being wonky on a controller).The game had so much character and so much to explore and find. Slightly disappointed in some of the world being unused... (What was up with the weird cult people in the tunnel? Why introduce the mopey fox kid and then suddenly have someone just mention that he moved away?) and the whole third act felt SO rushed. It felt entirely unfinished! One of the characters (your boss) at the ends even says "Hey, come here, I need your help with something quickly!" and you run outside to help her and it's just over, credits roll???I ADORED this game and played it pretty much non stop of two days haha. But the end felt unsatisfying and really, really disappointing...But, if it's on sale, I think it's worth it for the story alone, and getting to know all the cute characters. Talk to EVERYONE. Explore. Explore the playground, the shopping area, the town square, the river--everything you can before you go to the hospital everyday. There are so many stories to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros : + Artstyle - Amazing and fits the theme very well+ Music - Beautifully crafted Calm and relaxing+ Story - Engaging characterization and surprisingly immersive experience of being on the healthcare industry (feel wise of course)Cons :- Bugs - Still quite a lot of them while encountering. Some lead to game locks sadly or some immersion breaking.- Save Functionality - It doesn't have cloud save currently and you can really move it manually as well. Also the game feels like i would benefit with save files.- Story - Both a pro and con, as if the characterization and experience is amazing, the ending does leave a lot of unanswered plot lines.I had a beautiful time playing this game. With its amazing art style and music, the music really makes you care about the world and interested to poke around. First few hours of the game engaged me with unique characters and a quite gripping story. The characters and the patients that you encounter feel real. The mini games are cute as well.But the best part in my opinion of the game is how, at least for me, feels it simulates the experience of being a doctor very well. I do mean this emotionally of course. The way you want to treat and interact with your patients, the way the make you feel attached to some of them, the little annoyances that some patients also have, all makes them feel so real. Not only that but that also helps sets the pressure when the story picks up.--- Spoiler warning ish ----Now sadly the downfall is this game is in my opinion not the bugs, but the story. As much as it does immerse me on the feel of being a doctor, the story and the characters plot progression feels unfinished after the credits roll. Although emotionally it did capture what i thought what the game was trying to potray, it still doesnt really feel accurate to have some plot lines too open ended and up to interpretation. But with all that being said, I still recommend playing the game if you don want to tolerate some of the bugs. I feel the game can give you more empathy and understanding to the message that its trying to convey, even if the story is a bit unsatisfactory.Tl:dr - Game good, makes me feel emphaty, story is a bit lacking in the ending, buy if you can tolerate a lil bit of bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: IMPORTANT: I haven't finished the game. I left it the halfway point or so. If that changes I'll make sure to update the review.Fall of Porcupine was easily my most waited game for... Ever since it was announced. To the point of checking the Steam page on release to check how many hours were left to be able to play it, get it on release day and so on. But I just... Don't really enjoy it much?Let's get the obvious elephant in the room out of the way first: Night in the woods. FOP wears its NITW inspiration on its sleeve. It's OBVIOUS. And with NITW being one of my favourite games ever, obviously that was one very big reason why I ended up anticipating this game so much. Problem is, seeing it now in hindsight, being so obvious with the inspiration was a bold move that can be equally good and terrible.As I said, one of the good parts is obvious: You're instantly gonna catch the attention of the fanbase of a very very beloved game, and interest will spike almost instantly.But the bad part came when I started playing: This just looks like Night in the woods aesthetically. Nothing is really even close to NITW. And I know I should be judging Fall of Porcupine for being Fall of Porcupine and not Night in the Woods 2, but I feel this reaction is normal precisely because of the very conscious choice of making it look so similar.The first thing that had my alarms ringing was the soundtrack. It's... Charming I guess, but for the most part, it's almost like it isn't even there. It's SO subtle, and simple, that at some points you don't even notice it. There's a lot of parts in the hospital where you're practically in silence. There's this scene with Mia where you're both running to see who makes it first to a basketball court. And I caught myself thinking, in the middle of it, "If this had a good, emotional song in the background, this scene would hit A LOT and would be something people remember". Because, again... That's what NITW would've done. And what made it be so beloved. So it was bold to kinda create some of your game so much after it, making people's expectations go a certain way, and then have them find out it was just the very outer layer that looks similar to it.I loved the demo, because it had what I expected: Main character introduction, then you go to the hospital, the day ends and you hang out with new friends and learn more of their backstories, and then the whole thing ends up with a mystery to hopefully unravel in the back through all the game.But then the full game is just... Very repetitive and samey. You go to the hospital. Have conversations that feel like they go nowhere and feel repetitive and the work consist of sequentally completing a few minigames that go from "Oh, this is entertaining and makes sense contextually" to "I don't know why this is representing doing this thing/I hope I don't have to do many more of these". There's practically no mentions about the mystery, practically no hangouts, practically no mention of anyone's personal lives... It's just "Go to the hospital, do the same three things, go back home, repeat". And sometimes you see Finley making comments and remarks that look like they were actively trying to emulate something that would've come out from NITW... And it just doesn't work. You feel a whiplash. Because it's disconnected. What happened before and what happens later doesn't really fit with that moment. I don't know... I feel like they had the tools to make a GOOD game and a GOOD memorable story, but the choice to work between the margins someone else laid before made some things just not work and feel out of place, disconnected, slow... I can see the love behind it. That's why I'm sad. Because I know they could've made a VERY good game. But I ended up being in a situation of "I really really really want to like this game but I keep getting distracted every 30 minutes because nothing is grabbing my attention". But I'll try and finish it and see if I can end up with a better taste...

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, I am really having a hard time with this game, but I feel ultimately I cannot recommend it.The issue is that I liked the game; I don't mind that it was slow paced and more down to earth, I enjoy smaller stories and seeing the daily life of characters, on a strange way, the game was relaxing for me (Even if I felt pretty stressed trying to impress my boss and get on time to work, not that I had control over either thing.) I did enjoy story, and the characters for the most part.So, if I think all of this, why I can't recommend it?Well...neither of this aspects is strong enough, or good enough, for me to justify the rest.I am not a gamer, and I am not one to talk about the technical aspects of a game, but there were way too many times when the game just, got buggy enough that I needed to take it out and start (the phone not downloading the tasks, my character getting stuck in between places, a characters needed to progress somehow missing from the scene) and this wouldn't be as annoying, if it wasn't because you cannot manually save.The game saves for you, when it does that? You aren't sure, is there any way you can check the last time you saved? Not that I had seen; it was EXTREMELY frustrating for the game to break, and me to re-do everything that I just did. There are other types of bugs; like the HELP option in your phone not working, characters who say you can talk to but then don't, some visual bugs (example, a character has a ribbon, you get in front of said character, and the ribbon is on top of you know) The latter one weren't too distracting or an issue, but worth mentioning. Options in accessibility, like turning off the mini games, were also not working.Perhaps is because I am autistic, so take this with a grain of salt: But the explanation for the mini games multiple times didn't make sense to me, I would read the instruction, have an idea of what I need to do, and then turns out I completely misinterpreted. You can complete the game in around 8 hours, which, for the price I paid, I didn't mind (However, I got the game at half price,) I know technically, I could do other events if I reply the game, but I didn't enjoy this game enough in order to do so.I liked the story and the characters, but not enough to replay it again. Look, a story doesn't have crazy twist and turns in order to be interesting, you can have a simple story and still enjoy to replay, but for that, you need to have strong, charismatic characters, and this game doesn't have them. I enjoy them, and I can't say they were strictly one dimensional, but they weren't anything special either, even when I dedicated my time to one specific character, I didn't felt I got to know him or anything.To top it all off, the story doesn't offer enough variation for me to warrant another replay; the chances to choose where to go and see what someone else is going are few and far between, and wouldn't change the outcome of the story overall. The ending...oh boy; without spoilers, things pick up around the end, where it goes nuts with the amount of escalations, revelations, and such, and while all tied together, it does felt like were on a steady, slow pace, and then suddenly we are going down faster and faster without a stop, and then...is the ending, which is so short, and we see so little, is like you did get that stop, but now is just over. I get, that is suppose to be like a love letter to all those health workers who need to tolerate way too much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, due to a lack of funds, staff, and so forth, and having it end there rather than getting a super sacharine ending or a super depressing one (I really can't see it going on a middle with this one,) makes the experience more realistic, but damn, it still feels abrupt. Even if I enjoyed the game, I can't recommend it because I don't find it enjoyable enough for me to justify all the issues.If I had one recommendation to the devs, is that even if you cannot completely fix the bugs, at least give people the chance to save on their own; I feel it would really alleviate a lot of the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up Fall of Porcupine during a Steam sale. While I initially enjoyed the game, it slowly got more and more frustrating to actually play the game. The text bubbles had frequent typos, the mini game controls lagged, and there was no way to know when the game had last saved. The only saving grace was that you can turn on a setting to make the mini games easier. If I hadn't used that feature, I wouldn't have finished the game.The story itself is heartfelt and hard hitting. I found myself tearing up several times, but a few tears doesn't make up for the bugs and other frustrations. Sometimes the pacing was so slow it was unbearable. Other times, you felt pressured to move forward that you didn't feel like you had the opportunity to explore the world at all. When the character is concerned about getting to work on time, I am too, but by going straight to work, you can miss parts of the world building.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a hard time deciding whether or not I liked this game enough to recommend it. Overall, I believe it has a lot of potential, but there are a few issues that I had a problem with throughout the story. First, there are definitely some bugs in the game, but it seems that developers are working really hard to fix those issues. There was a point in the game where following a very goofy scene, I wanted to return to my apartment, but was unable to enter. At this point, I was more than halfway through the game and no suggestions fixed the issue. A couple days later, the devs made an update and I was able to continue the story. Secondly, the pacing of the story seems so slow at the beginning, then following an emotional plot point, the game seems to hit you with everything all at once. At the end of the game, there seemed to be all of the major drama and height of the plot, and then the game just... abruptly ends. I didn't believe it was the end. Not only did there seem to be no resolution after building up the story for so long, but I was left with A LOT of questions regarding those hard hitting plot points. Third, while the mini games were enjoyable, there was no direct impact on the story, and there almost felt like there was no point to doing well or doing poorly if you were just going to get the same story regardless. Your patients don't react different, and Dr. K seems to treat you the same regardless of how well you scored.Finally, and I think this might be one of the more important points, is that there were a ton of medical inaccuracies in the game. I streamed this game and had several medical professionals in my chat point out flaws ranging from the medical diagnoses & jargon to the hospital layout/structure. I understand that the game devs likely don't have a medical background, but I think it's really important that if the game is going to feature the medical industry that it be represented in the best, most accurate way possible.Of course, there were several things I liked about the game as well. The soundtrack of this game is so lovely, and definitely deserves a lot more recognition. I'm also a big fan of the art style of this game - I mean, who doesn't love these adorably drawn characters? In addition, while the technical aspects of the healthcare industry were off, the healthcare professionals that watched me play agreed that this game hits the nail on the head in regards to the emotional and mental impact that the industry can have. You'll definitely see the toll that working long hours, getting berated by colleagues and outsiders, and trying to balance a social life outside of work can have on anyone who works in healthcare. All in all, I think Fall of Porcupine is worth a play through. Looking past my dislikes of the game, I think everyone should educate themselves on the trials & hardships that people in the healthcare industry face. This game does a great job showcasing exactly that, and I hope that this game helps spark the conversation of improving the industry as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game for a while. it's very cute, it follows the Night in the Woods style very well, but it can't quite pull off the same charm and wonder that it's inspiration had. The characters are likable, the setting is quaint (though there's probably a couple too many scenes where 'go to point A' has you run through too many empty screens) The plot is very serviceable up until the final act when all hell breaks loose.The final act isn't bad, but it has -way- too much going on. For one, Finley's accident was supposed to have a mystery attached to it? It's barely mentioned except for people heckling him about the accident but then suddenly it's Important. it leads into an interesting plot reveal, but it feels like it's out of left field. And then there's the riot. And the mysterious plague. And then the fire. I liked the feel of the climax's circumstances, where you're forced to deal with patients in a crisis, but the set up and resolution don't really work. The last scene before the credits roll is nice but.. again it feels unearned and sudden and like there should've been more to the game for some proper resolution. The photographs in the credits offer a tiny bit as does the post credit scene but it... yeah just all feels unearned. Would've liked either expanding the chapter, let it breathe a little more so things can resolve properly, also maybe tease things a bit better (Like, plot reveal -makes sense- with other implications in the game, but it feels like it's underused/underdiscussed, it's just revealed in the middle of a crisis and is revolved during the credits). Just a very messy ending that really does put a crimp on the whole game. If you -really- like Night in the Woods style games and the art style is attractive, it's worth a look, but honestly it's probably more enjoyable as just watching someone else play it on a Let's Play run. I can't say i'll be re-playing it to do the other character scenes (like Night in the woods you have multiple points to pick between 2 characters, however, unlike night in the woods, seeing the storylines to completion by picking the same friend every time doesn't earn you any resolution) Kudos to the team, I'd love to see more from them but with lessons learned from this one. The english dialogue needs another pass, still a lot of errors, and the minigames are still a bit buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, this game has pretty obvious bugs. I played it through twice to finish all the achievements, so on the second play through I could adjust positioning so dialogue wasn't cut off where I had apparently gone too far in my first go, but both plays the game sound cut out (at different points) and eventually the game crashed. There were also some grammatical errors in the dialogue but not enough that I was put off.Despite this, I really loved this game. The art and music were breathtaking. It felt so perfectly "fall," somehow cozy but a bit bleak all at once. I do not work in healthcare, I don't know if I could even play this game if I did because some parts were honestly so emotional to me. Did I love all the mini games? No, but I really enjoyed some and I felt like they did a good job of breaking it up so it was more than just a visual novel.You have to play twice to get every achievement. I don't recommend doing this back to back like I did. Play it, and revisit in the winter, or next fall.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of The Porcupine is an intriguing game that captures attention with its atmospheric setting and impressive art style. The gameplay elements are enjoyable, and the music enhances the overall experience. However, there are a few noticeable drawbacks that prevent it from reaching its full potential. One of the main disappointments is the story. Similar to Firewatch, I had high expectations for the narrative, but I found myself let down when the credits rolled. It feels like the game falls short in delivering a satisfying conclusion. Additionally, there are moments where the pacing becomes monotonous, resulting in a rather boring middle section. While the game showcases creativity in certain sections, it feels rushed overall, which is surprising considering the effort put into other aspects. There are missed opportunities to explore these creative elements more extensively, leaving the impression of unfinished potential. I didn't love the ending, but I enjoyed to journey to get there. On another note this games needs Steam Cloud saves!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to leave a negative review but I had high hopes...Visual styleAtmosphereSound (when it exists)Everything else.This game has a lot of potential, and I've been anticipating it for a long time, but seems... something went wrong. Unfortunately, I can't review the story because I lack the motivation to complete the game. However, regarding the other aspects...The game feels tight and uncomfortable. I play a lot of games, but I've never seen a situation where I couldn't exit the menu by pressing B (on the Xbox controller), and this thing is driving me insane.I can't avoid those pauses during the dialogues that I can't force or skip, those moments when  Finley gets stuck after the loading screen when he is running through the locations.I can't relax while playing it because I keep stumbling over gameplay flaws. It's particularly frustrating that there's no option to "save and quit" the game in the current position or at least provide manual save options. Due to several bugs I've encountered during approximately 3h of gameplay, I've been forced to restart the game, setting me back to a spot I was at 20-30 minutes ago. It's quite annoying.Bugs: Sometimes Finley gets stuck, and sometimes there's no sound at all, not even the sound of 'typing' in dialogues.I'm really disappointed because I expected a lot from Fall of Porcupine. I waited for it, hoping to spend time enjoying this game. The only thing that prevented me from quitting the game earlier are the mini games. They are amazing and fascinating. Perhaps I'll give a second chance to this game if the devs release several fixes because I genuinely want to learn the story's end.

_childDocuments_.review: This story will stick with me for a while.The fact that this was dedicated to healthcare workers makes it even more wonderful and also sad. Sad but true.It is a good story to tell, in a wonderful way.The ending might seem sudden, but I feel it was exactly how it was supposed to be.As a healthcare worker you run around all day, helping everyone and it can feel like a thankless job. And you cannot save or help everyone. Which can be demoralizing and heartbreaking.This game tells that story, in what I feel, was a wonderful way.I played this for 10 hours while streaming, but I could have gone twice that long. I didn't talk to everyone in game, because I read everything out loud on stream and needed to save my voice. If I played this privately I would take more time to explore and get to know every single person.The mini-games were fun (I think I had the easy ones turned on), I liked the characters, the music and the experience as a whole.Do stick around for the credits if you finish the game ;)Thank you devs for the tears and the fun.I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine is a beautiful story about the state of the healthcare system in general. It delved deep into the dirt, scandals, and manipulation behind it all.. but as well as the little good things such as the doctors and nurses who are passionate about their career and genuinely care for their patients. Some critiques I have for the game:- The stethoscope minigame sometimes doesn't detect when I press the corresponding buttons. Sometimes I have to double tap it for it to register and at best my usual results for that game are a B because of it.- The surgery minigame is difficult for no apparent reason. It's like your fingers are playing twister when you go through this minigame.- When I go off the game to go to the menu then back the sounds except for the background ambiance completely disappear. I have to close the game completely to fix it.- There are times when I don't know I'm still in a cutscene and by instincts I move around then the game stops me and the scene plays out, after the scene finishes I get completely soft-locked because I made the unfortunate decision to move mid-cutscene.Some bugs I noticed:- Finley's body sometimes overlaps with his clothesBut overall I recommend this game for it's beautiful atmosphere, characters, storytelling, and moral lessons that it has in store. I love Fall of Porcupine.

_childDocuments_.review: "Fall of Porcupine" by Critical Rabbit is a heartwarming and poignant narrative adventure that delves into the complexities of small-town life and the healthcare system. Set in the picturesque town of Porcupine, players follow Finley, a young doctor, as he navigates the challenges of his new career and builds relationships with the town's residents. Here's a detailed review of the game based on various online sources.Pros:- Engaging Storytelling: The game's narrative is its strongest asset, offering an honest and emotionally resonant depiction of life in the healthcare system. The story tackles heavy themes like stress and mental health with sensitivity and depth, making it a standout in the genre​.- Charming Art Style: The hand-drawn, cartoony visuals are both charming and vibrant, adding a cozy yet melancholic atmosphere to the game. The anthropomorphic characters are full of life and personality, which enhances the overall immersion and emotional connection​​.- Varied Gameplay Mechanics: Fall of Porcupine features a mix of mini-games and puzzles that are well-integrated into the storyline. These range from medical tasks like prescribing medication to leisure activities like basketball and bar brawls. This variety keeps the gameplay engaging and fun​​.Cons:- Lack of Polish in Certain Areas: While the game is generally well-received, some areas feel underdeveloped or rough around the edges. For instance, certain interactions and dialogue sequences can feel slightly off, and some gameplay mechanics could use more refinement to reach their full potential​​.- Underused Features: The messenger function on Finley's phone and other minor features could have been more developed to enhance the interactive experience. This minor shortcoming indicates that there was room for more in-depth interactions​​.- Emotional Weight: While the story is a significant strength, its heavy themes might not appeal to everyone. The game deals with real-life issues that can be emotionally taxing, so players should be prepared for a mix of heartwarming and heart-wrenching moments​​.Conclusion:Fall of Porcupine is a beautifully crafted game that excels in storytelling and character development. Its combination of heartfelt narrative, charming art style, and engaging gameplay makes it a must-play for fans of story-rich games. Despite some lack of polish and underused features, the game's emotional depth and relatable characters make it a memorable experience. Rating: I’d give it a "porcupine-perfect" 9/10 Bird of a feather.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really weird game. It looks cute and it is, but also... it isn't. +- everyone should know what you learn about working in the health system in this game- exciting story (after a while), close to reality- very cute design and sidestories- made me very emotional (happy, proud, sad, disturbed)- the music is unobtrusive but follows you after you finish the game-- for a while you really do what an assistant doctor does: sleep, go to work, work, go home, sleep; honestly it feels as if most of the time you walk; that's necessary for meeting people, but it's still a bit boring- there are a few bugs that forced me to play some scenes twice or even three times, as the scenes are long and involve a lot of talking, this was kind of annoyingPlay it! _childDocuments_.review: This is a cozy and charming game where you take on the role of a junior doctor in a quaint town. The game features a variety of mini-games that simulate the process of treating patients.The game shares some definite similarities with Night in the Woods, particularly in its narrative style and the way it encourages exploration and interaction. The atmosphere is similarly warm and inviting, making it a perfect choice for fans of that genre.However, there are a few drawbacks worth mentioning. Firstly, there is a significant amount of walking, which can become tedious over time, especially if you're trying to explore every nook and cranny of the town. Additionally, the game has some buggy elements that need addressing, which can occasionally disrupt the otherwise smooth gameplay. Lastly, the German to English translation is incomplete in places, which can lead to some confusion and detract from the overall experience.Despite these issues, the game’s charm and engaging mechanics make it a delightful addition to the cozy game genre.

_childDocuments_.review: After some playtime in game became active bus stops, which allow Finley to go directly to the St. Ursula and move plot forward, skipping travel through the town. My first thought was . Sadly, then come the second one, with understanding that there isn't much to look at. Or anything, besides great artstyle of backgrounds or a little extra minutes of ambient soundtrack.The plot, or, at least, the message of the plot, is fine. Hardships of work of medical stuff is a good base for the story - it's something we all experienced in our lives, can relate to or at least understand. But the thing is - it's stays like that for the good portion of the game, and even "crysis" at the end doesn't changes much. Like a river - a favorite subject of a boar-lady character in game - it's stays calm, then meets a huge step down, and... doesn't even return back, because game has no ending. It just stops at some point. There is so much going on a second ago - a riot, a fraud, fire, plague! And boom - that's all, folks. I believe you have to see some sacral meaning in the "fall" of St. Ursula, and I wish I could, if all the previous narrative wasn't a simple slice of life.Even worse, there is no "slice" in this "life", because it's empty. I've ran to and fro through town whole game, waiting to hit some side activity or event, or start a quest, but never found one, except a brief conversation with some characters, getting a hat back to a hobo, or making up a story with a yak-girl. And it's not a good reward for all the running.Finley have whole phone with contacts of his frineds and family, but can't do anything with that(messages from brother and mom here for... reasons?). There is notes about other characters Finley meets, but it has no purpose - like, why write about fox-kid, if he disappears completely after two days and never comes back?Main hero doesn't changes thought story. He spends time with friends(tho, why are we even friends with Karl? Just because?) and other stuff, but stays the same aguish pigeon like he was from the start. He's insecure, can't stand for himself nor his friends, and at the same time spits out lifes wisdom out of blue for Mia. He has a "mysterious accident" at the start that leads to nothing. A story with a flower that leads to nothing. A funerals tragedy that leads to nothing.Well, maybe his job is entertaining? You go to other floors - most of the time they're closed, except moments when you have to move the plot on them. There is a whole woodpecker-surgeon, and you see him twice for the whole game! TWICE! You go to the cafeteria - and swine boos you away. Basement mole never shows up. Minigames? Broken(thank to bugs) or unfun(because, again, your performance leads to nothing, good or bad).Of course, there is some good parts - brother-rivalry between two retarded deer-twins, whole plotline of Finley first dead patient, memory figurines in the woods, festival. Those small moments framed with great art design and music. And I wish developers the best in their next games because throught those moments I see great potential in their work.But "Fall of Porcupine" is like a rusty bike near Finleys home - it's here from the start of the game, and stays like that to the end. Even Finley doesn't want to take it to himself, as he planned.Also, you can't romance nor Mia, nor Dr Krokowski. Huge L for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with lovable characters and an important story about the current situation of our health care system. This game is mostly story driven with some minigames here and there. You play as Finley in his first days at St. Ursula Hospital. After a couple shifts you start to realise that your job as a medical assistant is way more difficult than you thought. I loved the combination of funny and emotional dialogues which always keeps in balance. After some hours you start to feel home in Porcupine and you fall in love with its inhabitants. There are some little bugs and glitches but Critial Rabbit is very eager to fix them asap. Thank you very much for this gem of a game. I cried once during my twitch livestream which says a lot about the story. :D

_childDocuments_.review: [small update after finishing the story, please see at the bottom of the text]Like some others have already said, I wanted to like this game sooo bad and it breaks my heart to rate it like that, but with the brutal "recommended, yes or no?" truth Steam is giving me... I have to admit I don't recommend the game :(You are the doctor in the hospital of a small rural village and you face some truths about exhausing work in the medical sector, finding your place, making friends as an adult, and balancing taking care of others and you.The artstyle, the idea, the characters are lovely and got me looking forward to the release very much after playing the demo. But the game has two main issues that can't be overlooked:- Bugs: The obvious one is that the game has been released with several bugs. Mine weren't game breaking fortunately (other players have not been this lucky). Some minigames didn't work well, but that only gives you a bad medical rating and does not affect the story. A few dialogues were mixed up, I couldn't read ingame messages from time to time (only lore), and visuals overlapped or disappear. I see that there have been many bugfixes already tho.- Slow paced, empty world: The sidescrolling town and hospital in the game consist of several screens, but they are so insanely empty of... anything. Why do I have to walk past approx. 10 screens on my way to work if several of them don't have a single dialogue option (don't even get started on real exploring options)? Why is the hospital five stories high if all I need except for floor 3 are like 4 other rooms during the whole game? The beauty of the world does fade after a few hours because there is almost NOTHING to freaking do, except for linearly following the story. And walking... and walking... almost no platforming unfortunately either, despite being a sidescroller.To wrap up, please note that the game isn't a complete failure. Maybe a 3.8 out of 10.I have about 1-2 hours to play left as far as I know and I will finish the story.But I have no intention to running another 8-10 hours in a new game set just to complete the achievements (sometimes you have to choose between activity option A or B).Make a dense story game in a small world - or make a sidescroller with puzzles, platforming and exploring options. But this... is just not it.Sad face :(UPDATE:Unfortunately I have to agree with the critics of the last story arc, because wtf is this? Did the devs run out of money?It seems as if they squished 50% of all plot ideas into the last 2 days, which therefore turn out very clumsyly executed and rushed. This is so unsatisfying (for a game which is 80% about the story and dialogue!) and not fair to the good intentions they had for heath care representation.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, with reservations. This is an imperfect game, and I'm not just talking about the bugs, of which there are many. It's also got some structural and storytelling problems, and the game play can feel samey. The overall message of the game is incredibly unsubtle, though I don't know if that's a problem in and of itself. This game clearly owes a lot to Night in the Woods but isn't as ambitious or strange or touching. Not that it's not touching at all, because it is. But cutesy art and a lot of mini-games aren't what made NITW special. Not those things alone, at least. I wish there'd been more mystery (and mystery solving), more diversity in the mini-games, more characters with unique interactions, just a bit more depth. That said, as someone who worked in a hospital during the first two years of the pandemic, Fall of Porcupine hit in a very particular way that I appreciated very much. The final chapter of the game felt very real, capturing the "it's all falling apart at the seams" feeling that those in healthcare experience all too often, especially when hospitals are having budgets and staff cuts so that executives can line their pockets. And while the game's message is delivered clumsily and maybe too forcefully, it is an important one. I would say that on the whole, I enjoyed this game, imperfections and all, and do have to hand it to the developers for using the medium in a unique way to explore the types of things that aren't typically explored in video games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super promising. Beautiful art, full of character. I love what they're trying to do. But it is not a finished game. The game is riddled with game breaking bugs that make it frustrating to play. As a player that wants to get more or less every challenge correct, being stifled by mini games either being super poorly explained or no back button option, it makes it no fun at all. Also the accessibility settings to have a guiding prompt is only offered in German, which is completely unusable to anyone who doesn't speak German. Once this game has had proper playtesting, I'd love to give it another go because I know for sure it's something I want to properly play. It's just not worth the time right now.
