_childDocuments_.review: After having finished the game, I can rightfully say I enjoyed it.The music was great, the art direction was fun, and the story was very engaging.The mini games could use a bit of work and there are still bugs to squash (I know the development team is working on them diligently) so, I'm going to say it was worth my time and money and I hope this studio learns some lessons and I'll be looking for their next release.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: It is a lovely little game that has a lot of heart. I think it could have benefited from a few more writers, and more consultation with medical/industry experts. The message it sends about the hardships in healthcare, while apt and true, doesn't dive into deeper root issues. The characterization was great and memorable; a real highlight of this game. Although the narrative could have been more solid, especially at the end. A few weird bugs but nothing game breaking.Definitely Worth a play through. especially if you like cartoon animal people.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a thumbs up, although my feelings towards it are more neutral.I enjoyed my time playing this game, as I am a pretty big fan of it's inspiration, Night in the Woods. Also I love pigeons, sue me. However, right now the game is extremely flawed, and I can't really fault the people that gave this game a negative review.- The artstyle is gorgeous. Just like NITW it follows the aesthetic of picture books and it makes for a visually appealing experience. The character designs are extremely cute, you can immediately recognize everyone's personalities from the way they're designed.- Most of the story and characterization is solid. There's some hiccups here and there (and we'll get to the biggest one, don't you worry), but for the most part the game genuinely made me get attached to a bunch of characters. A certain character passes away and I was holding back tears.- The music, when it's present, does a pretty good job at setting the mood.- There's certain long periods of time where nothing but ambient noise is present, even though everything else indicates there should be music playing. Certain scenes deliberately have no music and very little ambient noise to sell a dramatic moment, but there's others where it's clear the point of the scene is NOT to be tense/emotional, and have the exact same lack of audio.- THE ENDING. I had read a bunch of reviews that mentioned the game ends abruptly and in a non-satifying manner, and they are absolutely correct. - The bugs in the game can and will break the immersion of the game. Things like Finley and other characters floating in the air for a split second as a room loads, background objects being in front of characters you can talk with, characters standing up when they should be lying down, Finley's torso disappearing at a very emotional scene, continuity errors where characters either don't know me despite talking to them earlier or do somehow know me despite never interacting with them until that moment, so on and so forth. I thankfully never stumbled upon any game-breaking glitch, but the ones I did experience hampered the immersion I experienced.- The minigames are varied and fun, but most of them are by far the buggiest part of the game. The stethoscope and snowball fight minigame are the two that were the most broken in my experience. I had to turn on the easy minigames accessibility feature just to make the experience more bearable.All in all, the game right now is in dire need of more bug fixes, as apparently other people have had it worse than I did. Later on, I'd argue this game, WAY more than Night in the Woods, is in dire need of its own Weird Autumn Update, in order to flesh out the characters and the story more. Despite my overall negativity I recognize this game is a work of passion and I overall had a decent time with it. I hope in the future I can revisit it and have all of my concerns blown away.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Fall of Porcupine. It’s a journey that still has me thinking a day after I finished it. It may be far from perfect, but it’s an experience that I won’t soon forget.The game draws clear inspiration from Night In The Woods, one of my all time favorites. It doesn’t live up to NITW’s legendary status, but it doesn’t need to, in my opinion. Fall of Porcupine delivers its own unique twist on the formula of cute animals going through harrowing life stuff.The story is the main draw of this game. It’s a heartfelt tale about the hardships of healthcare workers. The writing is witty, and the characters are engaging and feel real. It takes a while for things to get going, but I actually enjoyed the slower pacing at the start. The ending was a bit abrupt as well, though this only made it more impactful for me personally.Another strength is the game’s presentation. It looks beautiful, almost like a children’s book. The characters are cute and the colors are vibrant. The music provided some nice ambient background tunes—nothing too special, but it was fine overall.When it comes to gameplay, there isn’t too much of it. You walk around, talk to characters, do some occasional platforming, and treat patients. These treatments take the form of minigames that can get a little tedious sometimes, but I feel this was a good way to translate the difficulty of healthcare workers’ day-to-day tasks, so it didn’t bother me. There were a couple of small bugs here and there, but nothing was bad enough to take me out of the experience, and the team has been releasing quite a few patches since the game released.In conclusion, I really liked Fall of Porcupine. It’s certainly not for everyone, but its characters, story, and beautiful visuals will stick with me for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, I wish I could give this a neutral review. For some reason, I choose  to recommend for all my "neutrals". It's not a bad game, it was just average in my opinion. Especially after playing Night in the Woods. I thought Finley was an adorable character, and I loved his gliding jump. I missed being able to jump on and interact with things like you could in Night in the Woods. I didn't care for really any side characters for this one. I just feel like there wasn't as much to do. The story, while good and relevant just didn't hit me the same either. So overall, it's not a bad game; I just didn't think it was anything special.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed this game! Unfortunately I really couldn't connect with it, the character development was so slow and never really deep, the bugs broke certain areas of the game making it super unenjoyable. The worst part was the ending,,, it felt so rushed and unfinished. I'm super sad, I wanted to connect with the game and enjoy it but it really was disappointing and empty. I know the devs worked hard on this game and I worry they felt rushed to finish it to keep the hype. A great concept but a poor execution.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: This truly is a good game. I honestly, like many others, had several issues with the ending and many unanswered questions. For example,  I did enjoy this game a lot though. The characters were personable, there was a fleshed out story line, and the game play was interesting enough to keep me playing the game. It tugs at your heartstrings in certain parts.  I would recommend this game, but I really would like resolution for the third act. Too many loose strings that I really want to see tied. If those strings are ever tied, I'll be first in line to replay this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game, despite of the rushed ending. The art, the story, the minigames and the music (even though sometimes I missed sounds in the game). I love that you can put the minigames on a easier setting. Sometimes things were a bit slow except for the ending (third act). That went super fast, a bit too fast in comparison to the other acts. It feels really rushed and unfinished. I'm left with quite a lot of questions. Sadly you can't seem to get 100% completion in one playthrough. I don't really feel like I want to play through the whole game again but I also want the 100% completion. It's a shame you can't revisit parts of the story. Would recommend the game though if you love story rich games with a minigame element to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: story-rich, fantastic characters and gorgeous scenery, fall of porcupine was an amazing game i think everyone, especially NITW fans such as myself, would love. this game was dedicated to the hardworking people who work in healthcare, and i believe it portrayed really well how hard a job like that is, and just how more difficult it can be under stressful and difficult circumstances, and how much of a toll it can take on your mental health.although, i would heavily recommend maybe waiting to play this game until alot of the bugs and glitches gets solved, as i had to restart chapters and even completely quit the game on many occasions. SPOILER BELOW!!!.....the ending left me a bit dissatisfied, cause it happened kinda out of nowhere, and i felt it could go on for just a little longer, purely to show the aftermath of it all. ending the game without letting us talk to everyone or see how it affected porcupine was pretty disappointing...otherwise, the story and the characters left me entranced to not be able to stop playing the game, and the music was gorgeous too.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: So many glitches. The NPC's have no life or personality to them and while the text conversations are very well written and sometimes very deep they lead basically nowhere. Its missing the mystery and pull that I expected initially (especially after playing Night In The Woods).  Please let this be the beta version and improve it somehow because the premise is so good and so heartfelt.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would recommend this game. The writing and art style heavily carried the game for me. Writing was well done, but I feel like the story as a whole could have been better, particularly at the end. The mini games were fine, except for the one where you have to press multiple buttons at once. On controller, it was nearly impossible to press all of them at once for the harder difficulty ones. I feel like there could have been more music in general. There were many times where the game felt unnecessarily quiet. Complaints aside, I did enjoy playing the game and felt like it was worth my time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks beautiful, the characters have a lot of potential. The mini games are nice. I love the theme of it (very heavily NitW inspired aesthetics, which I can say nothing bad about).Narrative games is really "my" genre. I wanted to like this game a lot and really tried to. But.Sadly, the pacing just wasn't for me. 6 hours in (I am one of the "talk to everyone each day" kind of player), the story didn't really developed enough to hook me up. Plus dialogs themselves just feel like they're dragging way too slow and long. Seldom do I get impatient with game characters talking too much, but here it was way almost all the time (maybe slow text bubbles are part of the problem, but the bigger culprit is probably writing).I did not finish the game, mind you. If there's a twist further down the line, I did not witness it.This game is not bad, it still has a lot of great stuff in it - but, in my opinion, it's for more patient players than me.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Night in the Woods, and this game scratched that itch and I could feel the influence of that game on this one in the writing, music, characters, etc. There were a few bugs, but not enough to ruin the experience. All in all, not a bad first game by the studio. I would love to play a sequel or a similar type of game but only more refined.If you enjoyed Night in the Woods, this is great. If you're interested in this type of game, maybe start with Night in the Woods. Otherwise, I recommend getting it when on sale. I look forward to see what other games this studio makes in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: It would be a neutral for me. The story was nice and some parts got to me, but I feel that there was not a clear conclusion and the problems that were presented were not fully resolved. From what I've seen before buying it, it had some nitw vibes and certainly, it hit some points, but again I feel like  THE BUGS THO! I had to restart the game multiple times cause my minigames bugged or I got stuck in some of them. I think they can be easily resolved, but it made me finish the game slower.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I have to give this game only a reluctant recommendation. However, there are things that i need potential buyers to know right off the bat.This game suffers, and i mean truly suffers from bugs. Bugs i havent seen before in other games. I played Cyberpunk 2077 and let its story run on rails, and suffered less bugs there than i did in Fall of Porcupine. However, out of the ones ive experienced here, none were game breaking. But they certainly were more than a little annoying.Though there certainly are bugs and poor translations and spelling errors, i think the most disappointing part of this game is the amount of open ended story lines. Places the game not only could have gone, but wanted to go. So many details were left out that i would have loved to see, that were never developed. Unfortunately even the ending suffered from what i feel was budget cuts and time constraints.Regardless. I did enjoy my time playing Fall of Porcupine. I intentionally tried to let the game speak for itself, letting it be what it is rather than what it isnt, hence why i set aside my NITW hype. Fall of Porcupine tries to deliver a message, and to that end it did deliver. And for that reason, ill recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting story with cute and relatable characters in a beautifully illustrated world.Fall Of Porcupine succeeds at raising awareness for the problems and shortcomings of our modern healthcare systems without going overboard. The story and characters therein feel real and beleivable up to a certain point.Unfortunately, toward the end of the game the story became what felt very "rushed" to me.The overarching plot point of "What is really going on at St. Ursula's?" is unceremoniously resolved in an exposition dump between two NPCs that the player just kind of stumbles into. Not much actual investigation needed, which is sad, because I was looking forward to "resolving the mysteries".Several plot points throughout the game never get resolved, and certain questions never answered. It feels like about a third of the story is just missing at the end. Some of the characters kind of just dump exposition on the PC, instead of naturally developing a relationship with them. One notable exception to this was a character named Frauke, which was written very well and shows that Critical Rabbit have the ability to do this.During my playthrough, I did encounter a few technical bugs as well, which will hopefully get resolved in a future update, such as the phone not always scrolling correctly or getting stuck, audio becoming stuttery and the game freezing a few times.Overall, this game was a beautiful experience though and I shed more than a few tears during the sadder parts of the story, but unfortunately that story, which has a lot more potential, falls flat at the end.I hope to see more from Critical Rabbit in the future. This stuido clearly has a lot of potential.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: very very good game. loved the characters, loved the art, and loved the music. the only few gripes i have with the game is that it did have a number of glitches such as not allowing you to finish certain tasks, repeating dialog, characters phasing through other characters, and sometimes the game would freeze at a certain point and i would have to restart the day. the other issues i had was that it felt a little short coming to the end, and that some characters didn't have enough content or screen time and if more characters had more content, dialog, and screen time (such as antanin who we barely got to see at all)  i feel like this would have made the game stretch more while still having its original main story. but i do feel that overall this game is worth it and i would defiantly recommend it if you are looking for a very emotional story driven game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this by saying my appreciation towards this game is going to be biased as I have worked in settings involving patient care and am in school getting a degree in a healthcare related field. I'm also going to avoid comparing this to Night in the Woods because while they may feel similar, especially in an aesthetic sense, it's probably best to view this as its own separate piece of media (and multiple people have already written comparisons)First, this game is gorgeous and I can tell a lot of work went into crafting everything; I especially love how the camera will pull back to show off environments for emphasis.This game does tackle some interesting topics and certain societal and healthcare infrastructure problems are universal no matter what country you find yourself in; I think the writers were very thoughtful in the ways they decided to portray these issues and I honestly admire that.My main criticism is in regards towards pacing and the ending. Spoilers incoming.My other complaint is that this game is a bit buggy, but I'm gonna give this a half pass since its a new game from a smaller team. I did get softlocked at one point and dialogue bugs can sort of ruin the flow. If these are turnoffs, I'd recommend waiting a bit until some things get ironed out.I want to thank the team for making a narrative that did connect with me, and I look forward to replaying this game to get some achievements I missed after it gets tightened a bit. I hope this team moves on to make new games because I feel like they'll be able to make even better ones in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoilers* An immediate favourite game of mine! I absolutely loved the prologue and the game itself did not disappoint - couple of issues with the mini games not working properly, but I loved the narrative and general vibe of the game, super cosy and easy to chill out to and enjoy! Recommend it to anyone - and already have been doing! Characters, storyline, plot - all FAB! However, the ending felt super rushed and unfortunately tainted the whole experience by the end. I was expecting the Dr to have a longer chat with me, it was like one sentence? You then don't even say anything to Mia or Karl... felt very abrupt. Disappointing to become so invested in a narrative that doesn't really tie up, other than a few pictures at the end - whilst the sickness gets hinted too, presumably via the water, it's never really specified and it felt like I ended up with more questions than answers which was a shame as it made the game come to a disappointed end that I was otherwise really enjoying! I also wanted to see how things ended with my friends, Mia, Pina, Karl, whether Alfio came back (also were we supposed to find his hat at some point!?) The story was well fleshed out at the beginning, so it's a shame it didn't continue towards the end. Otherwise, really enjoyed the game! Just disappointed by the sudden end after being so invested in Finley's story.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Such a sweet game. I haven't finished it at the time of writing, but I've already fallen in love with the characters and story it tells. If you like Night In the Woods I cannot recommend this game enough to you. The town is fun to explore and has me going out of my way to check in with characters every day to continue their story. I'm not very good at the mini games but I enjoy them none the less. Most of the game breaking glitches happened at the hibernation festival. I had to restart twice and then quiet entirely at the end. First round, Pina got stuck and didn't show up for the riddle section and the second time around, the section didn't end after I got the pickleweed. Finally at the end, the audio was sputtering so hard it lagged out entirely, thankfully I got to a save point but three restarts for one section is unfortunate.I want to tote all the positives this game has, I really REALLY do, just... The frustration I have with it is getting to me.If you can handle the glitches, it's worth it. Until then, hold out for a few patches.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Good sweet relaxing story. A few bugs, but hopefully they're fixed within a month or so.The story is overall very relaxing with the mixture of various mini games keeping things fresh. The soundtrack was also wonderful and helped add to the relaxing atmosphere of the game to reinforce the mood. Seeing Finley go from complaining about long hours to then experiencing all the other challenges that healthcare workers face was quite eye opening. As a healer main in mmorpgs, I sympathize with a few of the points, heh.My only main problems with some of the mini games included the injection mini game where it's not exactly sure what you're supposed to do and the bandage change mini game which prompts some really difficult and awkward input combinations requiring the use of the claw grip to do the basic ones. There is the simple mini games setting, but I have yet to try it.At the time of writing this review, there are still quite a few bugs in the game. Nothing game ending, but enough that it's a bit of an annoyance. Layers showing up wrong, text prompts that don't do anything besides making Finley stand for 5 seconds, characters talking out of frame, etc. Hopefully these all get fixed soon. There's an achievement that no one has gotten yet and reading forums, I think it may be because it's bugged.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the game, which according to Steam took me 8 hours. In those 8 hours, I have learned many things, most importantly the hardships of medical workers. This game paints a clear picture of how medical workers are treated in our society, and how much they put into their job to receive little back. Sure, the game is buggy, and some fixes must be implemented in the future, but afterwards, this experience absolutely changed me.EDIT: The game is receiving tons of updates! Always great to see work being done to fix some bugs and complaints!
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good, it has a few (especially visual) bugs here and there, for me it repeated some dialogue I already read instead of showing the one that was supposed to show, also ending in me missing out on an achievement, bummer, but I can ignore that since you have to replay to get all of them anyway.Generally it has a lot of potential, the characters are great but it could be so much more, the first two acts are amazing and then the third just doesn't deliver as much as it should have, more explanations, character development, a satisfying resolution.I still enjoyed my time, story and game play wise, it looks adorable and I cried a few times, so I still recommend playing it!
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a beautiful art style and as far as I can tell the story is really well made. I have only gotten to the third act and plan on finishing it. The problem however is that the bugs start appearing once you have hit the second act. I have no idea how long this game has been in the making but I think the game should have more work done to it. The only frustration I have had that has almost made me quit is the glitching while doing the dance mini-game. I never like to complain about the games I buy especially when buying them right when they come out but since I had and still have high hopes for the game, I hope the problems are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: The art style has a nice charm to it, the sound design is solid, animations work well, and it does have that kinda laid back Night in the Woods style gameplay, but it seems like this was rushed. I encountered numerous benign graphical bugs, but also a couple annoying UI glitches. There are also occasional typos. I do see that bug fixes are being pushed, but I doubt the content of the game will be updated, which is mainly where I find things lacking.I just played to the end of the story, having gone around hitting every interaction I could find, and the plot feels incomplete. The beginning was a compelling plot hook, but the sudden climax leading up to an abrupt end offered little closure. There are a few times where big events just... happen, seemingly for the convenience of the plot, and I'm wondering if I missed something.Feels like some gameplay mechanics were thought up and then forgotten during development. Perhaps it was intended to be there only for flavor, but the phone seemed underutilized with the notes and messaging app being barely relevant. Finley is able to glide, yet there are few platforming opportunities to use it on. These things could've been used to add more content to the game.Can't say I hate this game, can't say I love this game. I will upvote but say I can't fully recommend it. Give it a try if you're really interested in these types of games, but maybe after some more updates. The developers definitely have potential for future titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun cute game - there's a little polishing that's needed here and there (some grammar with the English localization, getting stuck in certain mini-games or dialogues with no way out but to close the game and start over, NPCs getting stuck in one area but their dialogue still triggering off-screen, etc.), BUT considering it's the debut release, not everyone can get it right the first time. I stayed because of the characters. Underneath all of the bugs and occasional hiccups, I stuck around and got to the dawn. Doesn't advertise itself as more or less than what you see- can't wait to see what else they can do!
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: Fall of Porcupine is a colorful vision of a town of anthropomorphic animals. You play Finley, a resident doctor new to the region and hospital of the town. The village and its inhabitants feel realistic and have a fair level of depth to them. Similarly, those who work in the hospital have lives and personalities as well, which adds to the charm and immersion.Mechanically, your work in the hospital is depicted by minigames: a pseudo rhythm game for stethoscope use, a math puzzle for medication, a logic puzzle for diagnosis, and a sort of timed event for injection. The stethoscope mini-game is very difficult, and is programmed poorly; however the remaining games are actually quite fun and I felt accomplished after each one. Similarly, life in town have occasional events where you play minigames to do various activities such as dancing, snowball fights, playing basketball, etc.Without spoilers, the story is a relatively realistic view of the healthcare system, and what life is like for those who work in it. The stress of not only the workload, but the consequences of your actions, is not overlooked by the game. You deal with the loss of a patient, which all surgeons inevitably will face, and the mental and social ramifications of it. It also depicts the public perception of healthcare, the agony of medical bills and insurance claims, and the anger family members can feel at the loss of a loved one, even if at no true fault of the medical professional.While I was very impressed with the bulk of the game, the ending of the game was very disappointing. I don't know if it was the artistic intention, to depict how "the work is never done" or "there is no good ending" for healthcare workers, but it felt very abrupt, and very dissatisfying.  I also don't know if there was something mechanically I did to get a "bad ending", but it doesn't feel like I did.Many people will compare this game to Night in the Woods, not only for its visual style, but its narrative exploration of a story, and its focus on character relationships. Night in the Woods also had a somewhat lackluster ending, but it is miles above this game's ending, unfortunately.I believe Fall of Porcupine is the first game of Critical Rabbit, and for that, I forgive a lot of the smaller issues. The story told is very good, and I commend the group for their accomplishment. The game plays well, but have many bugs; however none broke the game for me. Some bugs include objects appearing on the wrong layer, animations not stopping, dialogue repeating, prompts not disappearing, NPC characters getting stuck, speech bubbles in wrong locations or of wrong sizes, cameras not focusing on the correct location, etc. None of these were game-breaking in any way, and can be forgiven in a studio's first game, immediately after release. The only bug I had that was intrusive was that sometimes pressing I to open the phone (the only way to get your tasks for the day) would not open the phone, and I would need to quit and load again. This occurred more than once. There were also several audio issues where the music would stutter or freeze all together, but even with that, the game was playable to the end. Additionally, this game was made by a European company, and a few localization issues are present. A few grammatical issues, idioms/phrasing oddities, and an issue with deciding how to number the floors. Yet again, none of this overtly took away the immersion, and the story was still delivered beautifully.This was a great first game, and I'm looking forward to this studio's next game. I hope they use this release as inspiration to do a bit more QA testing before their next release though. Also, if the studio releases a patch for the bugs, or even an addition to the ending, I will update my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I was hooked after I had played the demo: Reminding me of Scrubs with its setting, atmosphere and humor, Fall of Porcupine makes me really nostaligc. <3 The game itself runs smoothly, I have no tecnhical issues so far with a mediocre notebook. The tasks are neither too hard nor too easy, I enjoy them. The cute animations and the very well chosen music make this game a really nice experience to forget about your day. I'm excited to play it through!
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: It gets the points it's trying to make across well, there are countless problems in our society, not just in the healthcare sector, which this game is dedicated for. I understand why a game like this exists and I welcome it as more people might wake up as a result, to realize what everyone is dealing with, what problems our society has, etc.But it is still a game, and therefor I have to rate it as such. This game was made by a German development team, so I expected quality, and was disappointed. The Beta Testers let problems slip past that were very easy to notice during normal play, such as but not limited to: background art not updating with , the English localization containing countless grammar and spelling errors.. The game even got hard-stuck for me towards the ending, which forced me to restart it and pray that it saved before.. which it did, luckily. NPCs tend to get stuck, but they just teleport if they're supposed to follow the player. Overall, it made it hard to immerse myself as a result.According to the credits, a single person was handling the coding during development, so that may have played a huge factor in that. The game is poorly optimized for what it is, but it should still run just fine on old machines. Most of the issues the game currently has can easily be patched within a few hours. Unless the code is beyond jank, but how would I know?Overall, I give this game a positive rating. While it does suffer from quite a few bugs here and there which do affect gameplay, it still manages to get its point across which is the main purpose of this game, that and all the issues can easily be resolved, the game was just released, so I'm expecting a patch soon.If you're thinking about picking up this game, be aware that it is not your usual game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: A nice made game but so many bugs. If you feel like you want to do a good job the 3 different key hitting cutting job is sometimes just not working and you'll only be able to get the worst rating. For the rest it seems all fine other than the stetoscope job which is just not balanced at all. Sometimes chat bubbles are cut out or the phone app won't show everything as expected. Such a shame. I hope in a little later state of the game this will be fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, but I would wait a little before purchasing since it has quite a few bugs (understandably, as it was just released).I experienced a lot of character clipping (of myself and other NPCs), missing dialogue, reset of story dialogue (I was not able to finish one of the character arcs due to this), long pauses between dialogue (looked like the game was going to crash), and achievements not being given despite finishing character arcs.I must say, I was also a little disappointed by the third act. While there was a lot of action, the story did not really resolve and left at a climax, and one part of it was exceedingly tedious.The story was otherwise fun and I would like to revisit the game again once these bugs are resolved.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I vastly enjoyed this game in the 11 or so hours it took me to complete my first playthrough. It's well written, has a great story, and a great theme. There are a few bugs I experienced as I went, but they were more minor inconveniences than anything else 99% of the time. Overall I think this is one of the best games I've played in many years. The developers are even after release at work fixing bugs and adding new languages
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've been looking forward to this game for a long time. I played the demo about six months ago, and I found it to be a charming game filled with promise. I work in healthcare as well, so it was a bit a personal torch for me.I do like a lot of aspects of the game, but it is a first effort for the studio and it frankly shows. There were several game-effecting bugs, aspects of gameplay that did not account for ghosting on keyboards, and the pace of the story is wildly uneven. It seems to me that, much like the hospital in the game, this studio simply ran out of funding and did the best it could to deliver. I liked it, but if you expect a clean and finished product you will be disappointed. The arcs for the characters were there, and the stakes of the story escalated beat by beat but it is clear several key scenes were cut. The etiology of aspects of the crisis towards the end were never explicitly addressed (but were clearly tied to a water-borne illness) and several character arcs felt unearned. I hesitate to recommend it, but I still do. Because it's a labor of love by a first time studio that does somewhat adequately represent the struggles of being a junior doctor in a rural town. I'm also keenly aware that I'm playing it in a language that it was not written in. That said, if you were expecting something along the lines of the polish of Night in the Woods, you will be disappointed.If several patches address some of the bugs I experienced, and maybe a few scenes were added to flesh out some of the characters (with some editing of the wordy scenes that are already there) there is an excellent game in here.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: How good this game? I installed it thinking I'll play it for just a short while then continue with my work... I've only just stopped playing after 3 hours. Overall, Fall of the Porcupine is a delightful and immersive gaming experience. It combines charming visuals, captivating storytelling, and enjoyable gameplay elements. Just be warned: it can be highly addictive and might derail your productivity. But trust me, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I give this a recommendation with a warning, because even though I find the game to be interesting, fun, and honestly quite sad at times, the game has a real issue with bugs as of the time this was written. I have not encountered any that severely hamper the experience, but there exist a lot of visual bugs and some auditory ones at the moment (primarily having parts of characters clip behind other characters/objects while others do not), and they do have the ability to throw one out of the experience. Also, while the English translation of the game has been mostly accurate with grammar, there are still several moments where dialogue either uses the wrong word (like your instead of you're), two words are smashed together with no space, or a misplaced apostrophe. I am able to ignore them personally and I've really been enjoying my experience, but if you're not one who can ignore such issues I would recommend buying the game after a patch releases to fix some of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: I was able to meet the German developers from North Rhine-Westphalia in person at Gamescom in Cologne in 2023. As someone who works at a university hospital and sees terrible things every day and feels completely powerless, this game left me emotionally and emphatically charged and shaken up. In these few hours, you can see in a nutshell what the German hospital system is like. Lack of funds, power-hungry individuals who act as if the patients are important when only the turnover is important. Doctors who at first seem very grim and bitter, but who have been working in this system for so long to help people and see no way out except to carry on or change professions..Apart from a few bugs, some of which are more funny than annoying, this is a very good game IF you don't compare it with other similar games. In the early stages, I often compared the game to Night in the Woods. Although both games pursue completely different interests and stories. So I gave the game another chance a year later and I'm glad I did. It's true, it's difficult to get into the game, to get interested in “most” of the characters. The only ones I really cared about were the old turtle lady, Mia, Karl and the doctor on our ward. Nevertheless, I really enjoyed the game with its 6-10 hours of playtime and often had to think about how and whether it could go on like this. Similar to the aforementioned Night in the Woods, after playing the game you feel like a grain of sand in the universe and question your decisions in life.In my opinion a very deep game for a team that has developed their FIRST GAME. Congratulations to my fellow countrymen.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun game! I'm really enjoying it so far and it definitely gives me some Night in the Woods vibes. Took me a minute to figure out one of the mini games. I also really love the characters!I did have a little trouble trying to launch it on steam deck at first and saw that someone had mentioned trying experimental proton on it and then it launched perfectly ♡
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

_childDocuments_.review:
FALL OF PORCUPINE is a unique story adventure. The collision of work and daily life - an exciting reflection of an unhealthy healthcare-system.

You don't even have time to look at the clock because your patients are waiting! Investigate what's wrong with them through your conversations and treat them in different minigames that challenge you in logic, speed, and skill. And most importantly, withstand the stress when the strict head doctor questions your knowledge yet again.
_childDocuments_.name: Fall of Porcupine

name: Riven
detailed_description: “I know what he’s doing… He’s watching you.” Travel to Riven , a beautiful and mysterious world on the verge of collapse. Explore this mysterious place, solve its puzzles, reveal its mysteries, make a daring rescue, and escape. VISIT A MYSTERIOUS WORLD “I am Gehn. I assume you’ve heard of me.” Riven takes you on a journey through dense jungles, awe-inspiring caverns, and monolithic structures. Explore a world bent to the whims of a man who sees himself as a god and where every corner will immerse you in an otherworldly adventure. IMMERSE YOURSELF IN A SURREAL LANDSCAPE “There’s a great deal of history that you should know…” Riven rewards careful observation. Challenge Riven’s cunning puzzles, deftly woven throughout its narrative. The environment of Riven will reveal the story of this world as you make meaning from seemingly disparate bits of information and learn everything you need to know about this world. UNRAVEL RIVEN’S SECRETS “...it may be time to give this inexplicable mystery a second look.” Who are the mysterious island dwellers you encounter during your exploration? What purpose does the giant golden dome serve? Why is this world on the verge of collapse? Play Riven and discover the answers to these mysteries- and more. ABOUT THIS REMAKE Created by the legendary indie developer Cyan Worlds and based on the smash-hit original released in 1997, Riven has been lovingly revisited by its key original visionaries to expand the epic narrative of the Myst universe. Experience Riven like never before - with free movement through a real-time 3D environment. This brand-new, re-imagined, and expanded version of Riven offers a deeper story, new captivating visuals, and a journey that stays true to the original release while also expanding on Riven’s breathtaking world.

I assume you’ve heard of me.” Riven takes you on a journey through dense jungles, awe-inspiring caverns, and monolithic structures. Explore a world bent to the whims of a man who sees himself as a god and where every corner will immerse you in an otherworldly adventure. IMMERSE YOURSELF IN A SURREAL LANDSCAPE “There’s a great deal of history that you should know…” Riven rewards careful observation. Challenge Riven’s cunning puzzles, deftly woven throughout its narrative. The environment of Riven will reveal the story of this world as you make meaning from seemingly disparate bits of information and learn everything you need to know about this world. UNRAVEL RIVEN’S SECRETS “...it may be time to give this inexplicable mystery a second look.” Who are the mysterious island dwellers you encounter during your exploration? What purpose does the giant golden dome serve? Why is this world on the verge of collapse? Play Riven and discover the answers to these mysteries- and more. ABOUT THIS REMAKE Created by the legendary indie developer Cyan Worlds and based on the smash-hit original released in 1997, Riven has been lovingly revisited by its key original visionaries to expand the epic narrative of the Myst universe. Experience Riven like never before - with free movement through a real-time 3D environment. This brand-new, re-imagined, and expanded version of Riven offers a deeper story, new captivating visuals, and a journey that stays true to the original release while also expanding on Riven’s breathtaking world.
short_description: Uncover a story of intrigue, betrayal, and a civilization teetering on the brink of collapse as you solve intricate puzzles to unlock the secrets of Riven. Built from the ground-up and expanded from the award-winning original game released in 1997.

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised at how much the game had been developed.  Really enjoyed it.Not only was the sound and the graphics enhanced, but the whole game play too.  From the interactions to the puzzles being revamped to randomised outcomes and endings - which took a bit of time to sort out and understand.The price, though helps with the developer is considered OK, I didn't feel like my eight hours was justified,  That said, I'm happy to pay for it , to help them and maybe give them funding to develop other Myst games.Well done, I'd expect a lot of positive reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played Myst or Riven. There is no way this slog is worth 30+ € without some hardcore nostalgia to keep you going.The main problem is that the game does not respect your time. Think you missed something in a place you visited previously? Good luck hiking for 10 minutes through various "quick travel" systems to get there. Wait 30 seconds for a cart to come to you after calling it with a button. Wait 10 seconds for a door to close while you can't even see it, because you're control-locked staring forward at something you can't interact with yet. Oh, there wasn't anything to that hunch of yours after all? Well, time to hold down shift (because of course there is no toggle for running) for another 10 min wading through the world and staring at the same unskippable animations! This is not immersion, it's boredom.The puzzles aren't that good in and of themselves anyway, but their cryptic and sometimes pixel-hunting nature combined with the absolute drudgery of getting around the world ruin what satisfaction solving them could have brought.Unless you are in it for the nostalgia, don't play this. There are better (equally obscure and cryptic) puzzle games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is magnificent. For those who played the previous game, it is a dream come true, that of being able to move within these mysterious islands. Everything is reproduced with coherence, but many "licenses" of structuring the environment have been corrected due to the fact that immersion in a 3D world (and no longer point and click) requires greater coherence and precision in the terraforming of spaces.Level design-wise, it is truly a gem. Playing in VR, the spaces are balanced to move with the right sense of freedom, while being guided to follow specific pre-established paths. It is clear that this choice is the best to return the same experiential response of the point and click game.The biomes, the non-dispersion of the spaces, the artistic choice of colors and lighting sources, the composition of each glimpse (always studied in detail to evoke the maximum WOW effect. It seems like you are there, and you would like to live there, it is so beautiful.Great Cyan, for me your most successful product ever
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Wholeheartedly recommended. I played Riven when it was first released. (I was an adult. Yes, I'm that old.) This remake's quality is actually higher quality than my memories, and nostalgic memories have a way of being better than the original. The visual design is stunning. The audio, both soundtrack and ambient are outstanding. Cyan, you've outdone yourselves. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic update to an already great game! Proof that games don't need to be 90 hours to be worthwhile. The adjustments to the puzzles to make them more replayable is a welcome addition. Distance on the interactables got me a few times though, so if something looks like you should be able to move it, but the hand isn't showing up, just move closer. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Coming back to Riven on Steam Deck while traveling overseas, and then again in Steam VR after I got home, I can say that it has exceeded my expectations. The environments are immersive and captivating. The experience of exploring the ages again, this time with my young niece by my side was a wonderful time. The rides are so much fun. Getting to look around on the rides in VR is the best part. Definitely use a good chair for a proper experience. Loved all the small minutia and grand events and sights that make the world feel lived in and hint at its rich history. Riven is definitely worth exploring again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan, you’ve nailed it. Riven is my favorite game of all time and this is truly lives up to this fan’s expectations. Riven was clearly remade with intention and passion and it shows. For those who are new to Riven and the Myst series, give the game a shot and truly take your time exploring. Yes it can be an occasionally challenging game, but if you take notice of the environmental cues and learn how the world of Riven operates, the answers will come.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan has done something magical with Riven. Riven is an excellent sequel to 2020's remake of Myst and a perfectly fine starting point of its own. The game's world and puzzles have been updated to reflect modern game design sensibilities, while also being a love letter to fans coming from the 1997 original.If this is your first time playing Riven, grab a notepad and pencil, dim the lights, and prepare to fall in love with a world you'll get lost in.If you're returning from 1997, put aside your preconceived notions and enjoy discovering Riven for the first time again.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A someone who played this in the 90s, I love how they've reimagined the game. It may disappoint some die-hards hoping for a faithful remake. But, if they had done that, I don't think I would have played it through again. The old puzzles wouldn't have held up. I would have still bought it, walked around a bit for a nostalgia hit and closed it without finishing it. Thankfully they didn't do that, I'm playing it through for the new experience after the nostalgia wear off.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Having just played the original Riven a few months ago for the first time, this was, of course, a must buy. What a remarkable remake. I thought I'd blaze through it, and yet it took me a good 10 hours to finish it and get all the remaining achievements. There are some things in here even for the veterans.A puzzle & storytelling masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A True Gem in the (re)MakingThis is one of those rare cases where the sequel surpasses the original in almost every category, and mind you, the original on its own is a legendary title. It's the same with this remastered/slightly remade version of the '97 classic. Myst was amazing, Riven twice that much. Bigger, better, baddasser.The story expands so much in Riven that it is a joy to unravel, the world-building and the amount of lore infused in it is brilliant, and you are constantly rewarded for your efforts, every step of the journey. Your keen eyes, ears and touch will be your guiding stars, and your brain will love you for it. Yes, it gets hard, but never to the point where nonsense, plot armor, or deus ex machina, for that matter, take hold. Instead, just like Myst before it, every piece folds PERFECTLY into the puzzle that is Riven, no pun intended. Oh, and by the way, the game looks absolutely stunning on every front, and the audio design is right there to follow. A sheer joy to play, especially in an age where we are left starving for the genre that has long been forgotten, but hopefully not lost. Minor drawbacks go to technicalities such as the mysterious absence of your notebook hotkey (I'm looking at you devs, and at your letter "P", Myst), some strange optimizations I've noticed beyond 60fps (e.g. 120 with VSync felt like limitless and uncapped, my rig started roaring), and a few glitches that occurred (not gamebreaking, just weird OOB/no clip moments at one specific ingame cutscene), and the lack of polish for the UI, with a particularly ugly and unimaginative main/options screen menu, just like in the Myst remaster.All in all, games don't get better than this, go get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves the Myst series, I loved this remake/remaster. It is so invigorating to be able to freely walk everywhere in these Myst games and even more so in Riven. The ability to walk and see everything instead of "still" images is so much more immersive even if just to look behind rocks. They changed a bit of things with still keeping the original feel of everything making the story and puzzles more in depth. It also makes revisiting Riven even more fun as its like playing for the first time in some cases. The only downside I've ever had with these remakes is the lack of FMVs but it comes with updating everything else so I'll take what we can get. Definitely pick it up if you were ever curious of playing the first two of the Myst series.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I am mildly recommending this.I played the original version roughly 25 years ago. There's changes, and QOL improvements. I don't remember the puzzles being this frustrating. They've changed through.But the thing I was looking forward to the most was the VR experience, like with the Myst remake. Riven and VR seemed like a match made in heaven. Once again, the VR experience seems to be an afterthought.I play this with my Quest 2, over air link, through to Steam where I bought the game. It plays well enough, but it very consistently crashes every single time the little sub/tank thing in the village arrives at a destination. So I have to keep switching to "regular" mode just to navigate through there. I cannot count how many times I've seen the startup screen for this game.Like Myst VR, there is a "note taking" feature, which consists of simply taking screenshots which go into a gallery "notebook". At least it didn't take 1.5 years for them to implement it this time.... Not that it does a lot of good, because so much of the puzzles just can't be screenshot. Sure, it helps, but you will inevitably be resorting to pen and paper. An example - the little hangman game that give you a glyph count... can't capture that information. It'll just see what's presented on the gadget without the animation that you had to count in your head.You practically need a spreadsheet to help cross-reference the 800 million different kinds of symbols/glyphs/lettering/colors/quantum spins/etc. So if you're looking for a good VR experience... it's mostly fine, but just be ready for pain. I do not grasp why they thought the screenshot approach was going to suffice for people wearing headsets.Oh right - that "notebook" is excruciatingly slow and clunky to get into, navigate, enlarge, go back, resume game... every single time you need to look at something - one thing - at a time. On a few occasions, I accidentally quit the game instead of resuming, as I have to carefully aim my laser pointer hand at the "Resume" button in the menu.I'm sure in 15-37 months, this will be polished and worked out.I'm largely ranting out of frustration, as I really wanted to enjoy this, but find myself ripping off the headset in frustration more often than not.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: For a moment I was a bit set back when I went to find old places where I knew puzzle pieces for later were. Then I found out how they implemented the newer puzzle element and they are a BLAST even more so in VR.  Also its absolute surreal to stand in The Temple of Gehn and get a scale of how huge the ego of this guy is. There are a few things in there also from the Book of Atrus and I am super happy. Very well made so far, cant wait to beat it fully in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The islands look great and the puzzles are very interesting. After playing Myst I always wanted to play Riften, but there was no modern version available, so this is a nice gift from Cyan. Before playing this game, definitely play Myst first, I personally played RealMyst Remastered. The biggest gripe with this game is that it is unstable, with nearly every session ending in a crash. Hopefully Cyan can fix that going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven. Without the ball/eye/animal sound puzzle = heaven. I first played Riven with my dad when I was barely old enough to read. I have played it since it's steam release, but could never quite capture that feeling again. this time i could! and this time I could actually solve all the puzzles myself. I looked at a guide to tell me 2 things. simply telling me the islands i needed to visit was enough. the marble puzzle, super hard, but doable without a guide. and learning 2 different numeral systems in one game. priceless. i did finish it a bit quick. even finished most of the alternate endings. but worth it. and i didn't even use VR.TL;DR if you want a puzzle game, or want to relive riven buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game holds up way better than I hoped for. The puzzles feel more grounded and less surreal than many of Myst's puzzles. This new edition looks just how I remembered the original looking though of course now it's fully 3d rendered in much higher resolution. The move to first person shooter controls feels natural and doesn't detract in the slightest. The puzzles themselves felt good for the most part--not too difficult and not to easy. There are some journals in the game that feature a lot of writing but I found the writing to be engaging--the entries were well written enough to easily hold my interest despite being fairly long.The game has a very neat built-in screenshot library, which make 99% of the puzzles solvable without having to take notes. Unfortunately when I played there was some sort of bug which caused screenshots to blur with previously taken ones which made them blurry. One puzzle in particular was annoying when I noticed that a bunch of glyphs I took screenshots of were unreadably blurry. I had to go back and take multiple screenshots of each one until I got a non-blurry result.The fast travel system that you eventually unlock is fairly cumbersome. It's still faster when you're island hopping but there are a lot of slow animations to sit through. It can be frustrating when you want to pop over to one part of the world to check something and then pop back.Still these complaints are rather minor. If you liked Myst or other puzzle games, you'll probably like this one. I sure did!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: In the 90's I was obsessed with the original Myst and Riven. I wanted nothing more than to visit them for real. This is as close as I am going to get to that, and I am very grateful for it.I have now finished the game (without using any hints apart from one accidental minor puzzle spoiler I stumbled upon) so I am updating my review to reflect this.The graphics are incredible and look great on Steam Deck, although I am sure they are the best on a max-spec PC/PCVR rig.I am loving that the game is both such a familiar and nostalgic recreation of one of my favorite games of all time, but also has many bold changes from the original. Some are necessary to adapt the game to realtime 3D/VR, while others I've seen look like they have been made to flesh out the world and the story and provide a sense of wonder, mystery, and discovery for seasoned fans. It's kind of like playing the game for the first time again, which is an incredible gift. I’m sure this was a difficult tightrope to walk, but I think they’ve done an admirable job and managed to stick the landing.I am so happy that they got the original creative leads back together for the remake (Rand Miller, Robyn Miller, and Richard Vander Wende.) I think they have been able to make the new content fit well into the original vision for the game because of this, and the respect that newer Cyantists have for this game as well.The VR controls work well for the most part. I have had a few issues such as a particular puzzle involving sliding tiles being difficult to control, and the hotspots for book pages being a bit difficult to grab, but I managed. I have been playing in both VR (Quest 3 standalone) and flatscreen on deck, so I am assuming the controls for the PCVR version are the same. The flatscreen controls are quite smooth and intuitive and work great on deck also.Also as an aside, the new screenshot and note system they added is quite nice, but to solve the core puzzles in the game I’d still recommend using pen and paper to solve the core puzzles like in the old days, it really is just so much more intuitive. This is why I switched from VR to flatscreen about halfway through the game.I do have a few relatively minor nitpicks. I think the CG humans are much improved over Myst (2021), they still look a bit videogame-y but so far have been good enough. It's a shame, but necessary, to lose the original FMV performances, and I think the new actors and mocap performance matching to original audio has worked pretty well.But these criticisms don’t do much to sully the experience for me. All in all, I loved this game. Thank you so much, Cyan, for making my childhood dream a reality - I've been waiting for this totally immersive experience of Riven for almost 30 years!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: nice to be able to immerse yourself in a whole world without any distractions. really rewards players who enjoy exploring and clicking on little things, and putting them together until it creates a result. it might benefit from some more story integration, especially to provide context around what's happening.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing retelling of the classic puzzle/narrative game. The Myst remake a couple years ago was beautiful and wonderful to re-experience, and the new randomized puzzle solutions feature was a welcome addition giving a bit more replay value than the original had. But what Riven 2024 does is far beyond that. Not only are there additions, but there are also changes to some of the puzzles, lore, narrative, and clues. Many elements are really fleshed out and it also allows you to explore further in some areas that longtime fans have always wanted to poke around in. Think of it like an Extended Director's Cut. It's almost like an alternate universe Riven where the story is more or less the same, but it's been somewhat remixed in that you cannot simply play through Riven 2024 with knowledge of how to beat Riven 1997 and expect to finish it easily. It's a retelling of the same game, but it's like a game you've never played before at the same time with new puzzles that you can solve all over again! And it does this rather well and with care for those who are very familiar with the original.You'll find new areas to explore, new puzzles to solve, new dialogue, and new music. It's often been said that Riven has all of two puzzles and the whole game is more about exploring and discovering the information and clues you need to tie it all together and unraveling the compelling plot at the same time. All you're missing is the information. The remake is no different, but there are new elements to discover as well. We also used to get the pen and paper out to make notes on our discoveries. You can still do this, but the game also graciously offers a Notebook feature that allows you to take screenshots and add notes to them allowing you to reference them at any time during the game. Sometimes drawing is easier (and more fun) to really work out the details, but you can absolutely get by with just the Notebook feature. A very welcome addition!And then there's the graphics. Ever since the first realMyst (3D remake of Myst) by Sunsoft in 2000, I've longed to play Riven in full 3D as well. But as time went on and graphics capabilities improved, I more and more wanted to see Riven given the quality it was due. The Starry Expanse fan project sought to remake Riven in full 3D and put a ton of work and effort into it over the course of the past two decades and even released a small demo of one section of the game. The feeling was amazing. But I really was hoping that the graphics quality would improve. Then Cyan created Obduction and we got to see what a full 3D adventure game by the creators of Myst could look like. It was very nice, but didn't quite reach my standards for what a Riven game should be. Then they remade Myst. Wow! In my opinion it was a few steps above in quality of what they did for Obduction. But now with Riven 2024.....well, it's everything I could have hoped for. The photorealism in full 3D I always dreamt of. The graphics are absolutely stellar. If you poke hard enough you'll find things that look a bit off, but I'd say 98% of everything is about as photo-realistic as you can get with an excellent graphics quality to performance ratio with a system with decent specs. I'm running on somewhat medium setting graphics with an RTX 2060 at 4k and I'm quite happy with the results. I don't always get a full 60 fps, but it is certainly satisfying enough.My next playthrough will be in VR and I can't wait to experience it. I HIGHLY recommend this game for old fans and newcomers alike! The puzzles themselves, as I said, deviate quite a bit from the original but they're also a lot more fair I feel. I love the original Riven experience and I wouldn't change a thing, but all those little sore spots that people have had with the original for all these years I can safely say have been very competently dealt with and made more fair with all the clues you'd need to notice things. No more "how could I have known that??" moments. But it really gives return players like me a new reason to enjoy the game. It's not something I can beat in 25 minutes, like the original, and I really appreciated it allowing me a real reason to spend more time in the game and discover all the new areas. Maybe some return players might not appreciate this, but I certainly did. The original is always there and this remake is not SO different that it disappointed me. It gave me a GAME to play and not just run through the motions with. I loved it and I expect/hope you will too.So support Cyan's amazing effort, buy Riven, and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is incredible. The world of Riven looks absolutely stunning and being able to move around and look freely is an amazing experience. I was able to appreciate the environment so much more and it made some of the puzzles I ended up stuck on years ago seem much easier to wrap my head around. The setting reminds me a ton of Dune and I probably spent a couple hours doing nothing but admiring the environments I remembered from the past. The world is incredibly well-realized. The sounds are perfect. I only needed to look up a few hints. One, I had missed an important item and the other two I just didn't see a tiny switch. Every pipe, switch, etc has meaning (except for some fun red herrings/environmental "toys"). My one gripe is I wish the characters were still live action, but it doesn't really take away from the experience.10/10. Best puzzle game of all time, with an amazing story and setting to back it up
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 15 years ago, I played Riven for the first time, and it still remains one of my favorite gaming experiences. It's not possible to experience it for the first time again, but Cyan just gave us the next best thing. Remaking it in UE5 with modern rendering and VR support. It's not just HD textures though, some parts of the game has been redesigned. The puzzles are different too, so there will be new stuff to figure out. If you've been waiting to replay Riven again, now is a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent update of the classic into full realtime 3D. Cannot recommend highly enough! Finally fans of the original who always wanted to see what was just out of shot of the fixed renderings can turn their heads.For players of the original there are enough changes and new puzzles to make it worth a replay. No game before or since has done as well making the puzzles seem part of the world as Riven, and that continues in this version.The only ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the replacement of FMV filmed characters with kinda-ok-but-not-great 3D models. I can see why they had to do this as it's now a real 3D environment, not a 2D rendering of one.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to say no to but it’s just not very good in 2024.  I remember playing the original.  Vaguely.  The representation is faithful enough, I think.  But now it’s just a tedious easy puzzle game with a lot of invisible walls as well as endless backtracking with slow unskippable animations (just let me climb a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ladder, why does that have to be on rails?!).  Of course, in the mid-90s, riven was a super impressive game for many reasons.  It looked crazy good.  It was imaginative.  It evoked 3d convincingly enough while actually being a series of stills.  The sound design was amazing.  Myst was more impressive in my opinion but this was a good sequel.  The flip side of the faithful representation in 3D is that while in the 90s there were just no options to go in certain directions depicted convincingly enough by not being able to click on them, recreating it faithfully now means invisible walls.  While in the 90s the animations of stuff moving were impressively blended into the stills (also padded the play time, let's be honest), now, they’re nothing special and take so long that I’ve honestly walked away from switches thinking they did nothing only to then figure out that the animation that you’re now not forced to look at is just very long.  While the vistas and land still lives without people or animals helped not break immersion in the original, now it makes they make the game feel lifeless.  The now version is also much more pixel hunt heavy.  In the original, you’d be face to face with a thing and it’d be clear that it has to do something.  Maybe you don’t have the info or some doodad yet but it was clearly a point of interest.  Now, it’s easy to miss interact-able objects  because they have to be looked at from a relatively narrow range of angles (sometimes... sometimes clicking anywhere within a cubic meter zooms you on an object), the hitboxes are usually tiny, and you’re surrounded by thousands of beautifully rendered objects that do nothing.  While it was fun deciphering the languages, it turned out that I was nowhere near needing to do that and actually I had just missed a rusty valve on a rusty pipe a couple hours previous.  Not failed to see the logic or couldn’t figure out a puzzle, no, missed a brown thing against a brown background, at the edge of the screen.  And don’t get me started on the reading.  So much reading.  Like, worry about oled burn in amount of reading…It's also important to point out that while some of the things that are annoying now were annoying in the 90s, the games in this series were so different than anything else out there, it was worth it.  Now, any recent shooter looks better and has have worlds that feel more alive.This game occupies a weird netherworld for me.  It wasn’t as memorable as Myst so I’m not basking in nostalgia and, while pretty enough, it’s no longer impressive audio-visually and is quite is quite frankly so-so puzzle-wise; I guess the latter was always true but it stood out against its contemporary point and clicks.  I’m inclined to say that if you’d like to experience this piece of video game history, find the original on cd and jump through the no doubt numerous hoops in order to get it to run.Or get this.  Preferably at a deep discount.  But know that you might feel more annoyed than challenged.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: In general, a gorgeous remake. However here is a list of the few issues I had with the game:- Quite a lot of traversal stutter. Especially when running.- Character models are of quite poor quality. Animation is also stuttery.- Inconsistent visually. Some areas are beautiful while some look a little underdeveloped visually.- Not crazy about the new gimmick with the lens. I suppose It was put into place to rework one of the more notorious puzzles in the original game. However I personally feel that the original puzzle could have worked fine with some tweaking. - The grand puzzle of the five islands has been simplified quite a bit. Probably to make it more approachable to a new generation of players. This is not a dealbreaker, as the main idea of the puzzle is still intact. Although I feel the old version was more satisfying to solve.Overall I really liked it despite these inconsistencies.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you so much for this amazing remake, Cyan! I hadn't thought a true 3D Riven would ever be realised, so the announcement came as a big surprise and now I can say you surpassed all my expectations!What I love is that it's really the Riven we know. It looks just like you would expect it to look like. Yet at the same time, there are changes and new areas... but it almost feels like they were always there! It has truly received the love and attention for detail that one would hope for. I don't think it could be any better... it feels like this is Riven as it should be!Thank you so much!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really have any hours on record for the game as I played it together with a friend on his setup, however, I have to say, this remake of the 90s classic is absolutely above and beyond what I expected.Everything from the meticulous reproduction of the original environments, the puzzles, either being the same or improved upon, and numerous incredibly smart alterations and additions lead me to say that this is absolutely the definitive version of the game, and a true must-play for fans, players of the original, and newcomers alike.Now while I do praise the game highly, and the experience of stepping into this world all over again was an incredible experience, I will say I find the biggest caveat to both this and the Myst remake is that the characters have been moved to 3D models from FMV. I fully understand and sympathise with the reasons why it has to be this way, and I can't envision anything but the most difficult of ways to attempt to implement a solution that bleeds upscaled or re-shot FMVs of the characters into a fully 3D real-time environment, however, there is a certain magic and immersion I had in the original games due to this marrying of these elements, and the overall experience is lesser for their omission.That is the only possible complaint I can fire at the game though, it stands as a true modern marvel, I would never have expected to experience Riven again in such splendour, and I can't thank the original Starry Expanse team and Cyan for making this happen. Cyan, you were an indelible part of my formative years, and you continue to be a source of joy to this day, keep doing what you're doing ❤️Everyone reading this: Play. This. Game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, this is riven. It's good, and if you haven't played it buy either this one or the original and start exploring. It's one of those rare games where the world itself is the puzzle to be solved. Though there are a few caveats for this release:As a big fan of the original I was at first disappointed to discover quite a few differences as I explored. If you've played the game there's a good chance you'll b-line to the nearest familiar machine only to discover it's mechanics have been changed. I soon discovered that it was changed just enough to give me a new challenge and kept me busy for a good 8 hours. I originally purchased it to explore riven Island again and support the awesome fan team that led the project for 10 years only to discover there's a game there (albeit short) for returning fans as well.Changes come in three categories: 1. Lore fixes, there are a few changes that just make sense lore wise and mostly all harmless. with one major exception that will probably surprise every returning player. 2. Simplifications, there are some changes that seem to have the purpose of making things easier to understand or accessible to vr players, all but one of these are good. 3. New Puzzles, they clearly wanted to give new players a treat and replaced a bunch of puzzle elements, all of it leads to the same place but it has different solutions and even mechanics. I'm of two minds about this, One one hand it was awesome to actually have to play this version of the game and it's the closest i'll ever get to playing it for the first time again, on the other hand Riven relies so heavily on it's world building for puzzles that any change to puzzle elements is also a change to it's world, to put it simply this is not the same Riven... But for the most part it's an equally good Riven with enough meat for new players to keep you busy for a while. Good luck!
