_childDocuments_.review: The 1997 version of Riven is one of my favourite games of all time. I remember I'd sit with my Dad as a small child and watch him play Myst and Riven. Along with my sister we all played and solved Myst 3 and 4 together, gathered round a laptop taking hand-drawn notes and sharing observations and ideas. I've gone back and reinstalled Riven more times than I can count just to wander around and take in the atmosphere. I've finished the game many times over the course of my life, just to re-experience the same magic. Hell, back in college I even figured out how to run it on my old Android phone through ScummVM on a tiny 3.5" screen!I've been wishing for a 3D version of Riven (Just like the many iterations of realMyst) for longer than I can remember. I kept an eye on the Starry Expanse project blog page for updates for years until the project was shut down and taken over by Cyan, but even then I was excited to see what would happen with official support and Cyan's increased budget and creativity.And I hate to say it, but this isn't a 3D version of that game. It's a wholly different game wearing Riven's face.Many of the same locations and landmarks remain, but it's an entirely linear experience now with simplified puzzles that are less naturally integrated into the world (I think as an attempt to appeal to a wider audience). As a result it loses a lot of the feeling of freely exploring a real, lived in world, and slowly discovering its secrets at your own leisure, even despite the enormous graphical upgrade and full VR support.And speaking of VR, the game has been redesigned to prioritise VR users comfort. Many switches and levers in the world have been moved to a more central location at waist height instead of having little interactable things around the environment encouraging looking around every nook and cranny. Every door now slides smoothly to the side instead of swinging open, just so VR players can't get caught by them or disoriented if they somehow clip through the camera. Instead of climbing under locked gates or through ventilation pipes, those parts have just been removed or redesigned, so now you just walk everywhere. The maglev rides and minecart have also been motion smoothed, and feel less exciting and dangerous. All of this on its own is great for accessibility in VR, but there's no unfortunately way to turn it off in flatscreen mode...I feel like they've systematically stripped away every little detail that made the original game such a masterpiece, and all of those changes are touted as "fixes" - Like *this* is supposed to be how the game was all along if the original devs weren't constrained by technology or budget or deadlines.As someone who just wanted to explore the original game in full 3D and VR, and maybe share that same experience with others (Who never played the original, and never could be convinced to play an ancient pre-2000s slideshow game), the way the remake is being talked about as the truest version of Riven immediately crushed those hopes and dreams. At this point I very much doubt that we'll ever get the faithful recreation the Starry Expanse project might have given us.New players will likely love the new version. As much as this is a big step down from the original, it's still a great game by today's standards. Old players might welcome the changes and the novelty of new puzzles. I unfortunately can't say the same. It's both too different in terms of gameplay, and too similar in terms of aesthetic, for me to truly appreciate the game as its own separate entity. If we'd had both the linear "easy mode" re-imagining alongside a faithful Starry Expanse type remake with randomised puzzles like Myst VR had, I would have played both and probably loved both. But the fact we have this and only this is honestly soul-crushing.I can't play this. It's such a disappointment. I'm actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ heartbroken.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A great puzzle game, technically a sequel but you can get away without playing the first game. The environment is beautiful, but character models are a little lackluster. Luckily, it's mostly a solitary game so you don't see them much.Riven is the sequel to Myst, but you can get away without playing it first. It'll just provide what's essentially an extra paragraph or two unless you really dig deep into some in-game and meta lore. I highly recommend Myst: Masterpiece Edition for the point-and-click fans and realMyst: M.E. for the free-roam fans. Myst (2020) is fine as well, I just prefer the older games' FMV cutscenes + graphics.I've played Riven (1997) previously. A good few times now, and about a year or two ago most recently. It took me around 12 hours to 100% this version, alongside finding most of the non-achievement alternate endings.If you're new to the series expect a base completion to take a fair bit longer (maybe 20-30 hours depending on your puzzle solving skills). I'm tempted to say the original game is harder, but this one had a new system that I'm not entirely sure I figured out. The new music tracks are great, and I'll always be a fan of the old ones. While environmental detail is utterly beautiful most of the time, it falls short very rarely (the LOD for the massive leaves on Jungle Island from Temple is not very good). Sadly, a lot of the character animations are a bit clunky: although 3d models for characters are improved compared to Myst (2020), they still run at a lower fps than the rest of the game and their animations aren't always aligned with in-game objects.I experienced one or two funky bugs with interactive objects, but it really wasn't a common occurrence. Riven (1997) is a decently different experience than this one, and I'd recommend having a look at it alongside Exile (the sequel) if you enjoyed this. You could likely play both Rivens in either order without losing out on much from either, but I couldn't say for sure.One desire I had that I saw someone else mention in the reviews:    I was a bit disappointed that the  didn't retain its complexity. I was very excited to go into it after having completely forgotten how it worked. It still isn't a bad puzzle  by any means, but it'd be amazing for some form of original puzzles to return.Also, the

_childDocuments_.review: NUMBER 5NUMBER 5NUMBER 5NUMBER 5...no wait, that's the wrong number. Sorry Yoko.Either way by the time you are done Riven the Fifth Age of the Mysthology will be embedded in your brain thoroughly.This is going to sound extremely hyperbolic, but I truly believe this is the greatest PC game ever created. Now, much is owed to the original of course - but this is not an exact replica of the original. Some things have been changed. Some have been improved. But despite this, Riven is NO LESS diabolical than it ever was. It's the greatest puzzle of all time in digital form, which is an impressive feat considering how FEW puzzles its world actually contains.Sure, there is learning the mechanical flow of how things operate. There is experimentation with switches and valves, staples of Myst echoing Channelwood mainly. There is the necessity to build a deep, comprehensive knowledge of the culture of the Moiety, the world itself, and it's various trappings, right down to the fauna that inhabit it. But the actual "sit there and hammer away to figure out a puzzle" parts of RIven are far less in their distribution than Myst, far more sensible, and FAR FAR more gratifying to the point where it is sometimes difficult to even see that these two games are from the same series since the philosophy behind them seems to vastly, vastly different. Riven is such an unmistakably large leap ahead of Myst in every possible way that its surprising to hear it only came out a mere few years after Myst. It feels like the natural progression of a series that was around for twenty years before it eventually was refined to where it was now. I am gushing, but this is the point - I've never played a game like Riven, and I know I never will again. Cyan has done interesting work over the years, but Riven is their absolute masterpiece, and this remake is such a massive leap forward in so many ways that it really is hard to believe. Visually its absolutely stunning. It captures the look and feel of the pre-rendered world of the original to the nines. It's easily the most glorious and breathtaking game world I have ever seen. The one negative here, the sole thing holding this back is that the character models in Cyan games are still incredibly weak in comparison to their contemporaries. Better than the Myst remake, yes. On par with more recent Cyan affairs, perhaps, but nothing beyond that. It's just very hard to reconcile a game world that is absolutely unmatched in its art direction and execution with the decidedly far, far lower fidelity of the character models. The game world itself looks like it would be a far better math with character models, say, on the level of a Larian Studios game such as Baldur's Gate 3. But games cost money. They take time. They take tools, they take, and take, and take, and at some point, SOMETHING has to give. I think the character models are a fair trade for a world that looks this beautiful, and the only reason its even worth nitpicking is because it is the ONE flaw in an otherwise completely immaculate visual experience.It's really hard to not gush on and on here because this is just such an incredible remake. I never thought I'd see Riven remade in such a triumphant and celebratory way while actually improving on the old game (in my opinion) but not replacing it. That is one of the things that was so smart here - to give even existing Riven fans a new experience by changing just enough that their memory wouldn't be able to fill in all the blanks. The inherent issue with Myst is that you fundamentally understand, as a Myst fan, what needs to be done immediately. You can just never go back to not knowing, to that original discovery. RIven fixes that in every regard. Riven for a time was the best PC game ever made. The remake extends and improves upon it, and is the new reigning king.The king is dead.Long live the king.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler-free review.What an amazing experience. Riven is a glorious sequel to Myst, and both these games will make you feel smart like no other game can. In both games you arrive into a place full of mystery. You get bits and pieces of information, and at first everything will be very confusing, and you will have no idea where you are, where you must go and what you should do. But eventually you start piecing everything together, solving puzzles, and the world will unravel before you. Stumbling around for hours like a blind kitten until everything clicks together and you figure out a way to move forward is extremely gratifying. The in-game screenshot & notes feature is a brilliant quality of life addition, but expect to still be required to take notes and make some napkin drawings to keep track of tips you discover. The visuals are stunning, the world and locations are gorgeous, and a pleasure to marvel at. Sound design and music are also on point.That's the good parts so far. Unfortunately, there are some downsides. The game's stability, particularly in VR mode, leaves something to be desired. I bought Riven on release and tried using it in VR right away, and the game would crash the moment I'd try moving around. Perhaps the issue was patched out since then, I haven't checked.In normal mode tha game would sometimes crash as well, but the auto save does a good job, and I never lost any progress. Performance ins't amazing either, moving around some locations caused hitches and frame drops, despite me having a *very* powerful gaming PC. On several occasions, my progress was stumped purely because some tips / interactable objects were not highlighted clearly enough. You can blame this on haste and lack of attentiveness, but I still think it's a legitimate problem. Probably caused by transitioning from the original frame-by-frame design of the game into a realtime 3d space.Another annoyance is traversal. Vast majority of playtime in this game is spent on moving around and between locations, and often the path between where you are and where you must go is convoluted, and requires multiple loading screens and waiting for painfully slow animations of interactable objects. If you enjoy puzzle games at all, I cannot recommend Riven enough, despite the technical issues and small gameplay annoyances.And do yourself a favor, and avoid cheating by looking at walkthroughs. Even if you're stumped and roam aimlessly for hours. Trust me, all of the game's puzzles can be figured out if you pay attention and think, with no need to look into outside sources. I cheated only once, and I regret it endlessly, because the answer was right before me, but I was impatient.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven was one of those games that I loved and hated back in the day, because even though I was completely immersed in its world, the puzzles were too difficult for a kid like me (or maybe I was just too stupid, who knows). I gave up on finishing the game at the time, but the whole experience was memorable and even a little surreal due to the live-action clips and the real actors talking and looking at the camera. For those who are too young to know, Riven is the direct sequel to , two ‘90s games that are considered some of the most important puzzle games of all time. The latter has already had a successful remake in 2021, so now it’s time for its sequel to shine with a complete overhaul.Playing Myst is obviously recommended for many reasons, but you can prepare for Riven simply with a quick story recap. In short and without major spoilers, you play as a nameless stranger who is tasked by a man called Atrus to rescue his wife, Catherine, from his dangerous father, Gehn. Atrus is a descendant of the D’ni civilization, capable of writing worlds and traveling between them using some sort of magical books. Riven is one of these worlds (which are actually called “Ages”) and the place where Catherine and Gehn are imprisoned. Your objective is to free the woman and capture the evil father following Atrus’ plan, but nothing goes as planned in videogames and you will have to rely on your brain cells to make sense of everything. The story also includes multiple endings, so there is definitely some replayability if you feel like speed running through all the puzzles again.While there aren't any major changes from a story perspective compared to the original, there are certainly many visible differences in the gameplay and graphics. The game has been entirely rebuilt with the Unreal Engine 5 and looks simply fabulous. I had to watch a video comparison with the old one not only to see the insane graphical leap, but also the faithfulness of the developers in recreating the same feeling and atmosphere, which was perhaps the most difficult thing to achieve. Each location is gorgeous, and the level design is intricate and well-connected through puzzles. The old technical limitations have been removed (you had to move through different static images in the original game) and now you can move freely through the beautiful 3D environments. This really enhances exploration, offering a greater level of immersion and expanding the ways you can solve puzzles. The characters that were once played by real actors have now been replaced by 3D models that aren’t as expressive, but the voice acting and performance capture are still quite convincing.A few minutes into the game and I remembered why I didn’t finish Riven before. The game doesn’t hold your hand, it doesn’t tell you where to go or what to do. It’s your job to understand everything and you must figure out how to solve puzzles on your own. Instead of common puzzle mechanics (explore a location, solve the puzzle to remove the obstacle, proceed to the next location and repeat), Riven offers an open world structure where each puzzle is multi-layered and interconnected. Think of it as something more like  (which obviously took its inspiration from Cyan). Some puzzles will require you to learn different languages and number systems, while others will remain unsolvable until much later when you gain more knowledge or new items. I won’t give you any spoilers because this is the central part of the gameplay, but know that sometimes you will have to test your luck by randomly interacting with objects hoping to figure out how to progress. Between puzzles, you will explore, read, learn and be fascinated by the deep universe that Cyan Worlds has created. I’m not gonna lie, I smashed my head during the first hour trying to solve puzzles, but then something clicked in me as I was fully immersed in the world of Riven and I started to think with the game’s logic. Solving puzzles became more intuitive, still very challenging, but also rewarding because there is nothing better than feeling smart (or powerful). Some puzzles can be very difficult even for veterans of the genre and I won’t hide the fact that being unable to solve them and progress (without using external guides) will likely cause players to feel confused, frustrated or bored (perhaps all three at the same time). Riven is not a game for the average casual player who just wants to walk through beautiful, peaceful locations, but you know what? I love it! Even though it’s a remake, you finally get a real puzzle game that makes no compromises and doesn’t align with the general idea that all games should be easy and accessible to all players. I recently read a quote from the director of  saying “a game for everyone is a game for no one” and I was thinking “wow, this applies perfectly to Riven”.While the original Riven will always retain its charm, this is probably the best version to date and the one that most people should play, including those who own a VR headset. It is a spectacular remake, incredibly faithful but also enhanced in many aspects, starting with the transition from static backgrounds to 3D environments and free exploration. I think that even in modern days there still isn’t a puzzle game as difficult and complex as Riven, maybe because it wouldn’t be mainstream or maybe because players have been used to a certain level of ease and guidance in videogames that prevents them from enjoying games that test their intelligence rather than their manual skills.

_childDocuments_.review: Riven will always hold a special place in my heart... of all the Myst games, no game makes you feel like you've traveled to another world that's unique and distinct on it's own as much as Riven does. Hell, I might even say no other video game in existence does this as well as Riven...It's odd, as the story tells us that Gehn, the author of Riven and main antagonist, cannot write Ages that are stable and everything he touches is doomed to collapse on itself, yet somehow Riven stands as the most unique and wondrous Age out of all the Myst games and I can't help but feel that removing Gehn as the main antagonist was a mistake in the later games. Maybe it's because I'm older now, or maybe the world has changed, but after playing this game again in this new format I can't help but feel Gehn was more correct then not to demand the people of Riven view him as a God. It ended up creating a unique culture and setting that I felt was never replicated in any of the other games and it's something I long for Cyan to recreate once more in a proper sequel.As such this game is truly a breath of fresh air in the current landscape of gaming. Outside of the clunky character animations (The only downgrade), everything about this game feels like a faithful reinterpretation of the orginal, with better puzzle design that I'm sure will create less confusing and a graphics fidelity (on Epic settings) that not only match the original's pre-rendered magic, but makes everything feel even more real and alive.I really can't express how much you need to play this game. This game is absolutely necessity for any game developer to play as it will inspire you in ways no other game can. $35 is a steal... get it now, don't wait. Your life will be better for it!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know how I feel about this game. Its not the original, but is very closely based on it. Its a Remake, not a remaster. To me, the story is weak, and does not really work. They left it and most of the puzzles mostly the same. They did change the world. That I could tell, they didn't do this with Myst. They left it all the same, just linked it in a first person mode. They didn't do that here. If your going to update the game, update the story.The story is weak. Poorly written. Outdated. This is a big deal because you have to read through it to get the answers. This makes playing the game tiresome. Thinks click, but are not always pointed out. I did a lot of guessing and got pretty far. I had to backtrack to try to remember how I would have figured out to get to point. I got really far without an effort. Then I needed to know what it all was that I did to solve a bigger puzzle that used a lot of the information I never picked up on.To be honest, unless you are vested in this game, it doesn't keep me focused in the game. Many of the mechanics are broken in the game. at times the cursor pops up to tell you to interact, and at times it won't. I found Myself going on a click hunt. to see if I could click the right thing. Its not a game for me. I think if they MMO this title. Maybe gave it a chat. Maybe played with others. It might work. As the way this game is, its just too out dated. I know this sounds dumb, but make it like a kids Roblox puzzle title. I see kids play them and It keeps them in the game. They don't see the answers to the puzzles, but can work through them with there friends or the community.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A much-needed update to a classic, fantastic game. Of all the Myst series, this one has the most interesting story.  You find out about the characters' motivations and you are rewarded for your puzzle-solving with new areas & new revelations about the characters and what's going on. Even though I'd played the 1997 one a couple of times, I still struggled with some of the puzzles here, in a good way. I love a game that has me taking notes and struggling to see patterns or figure out codes. The Myst series really did pioneer logical puzzles that made sense--not only in terms of the puzzle itself, but also the story. If there's a puzzle, there's a reason why it's there--every machine has a thought-out purpose in the world you're exploring. I have to admit, though, I do miss the old FMV video--the characters aren't quite as lifelike or relatable when rendered with graphics, and while the facial mapping is getting much better, they still don't look like real people, the way video does.  I'm sure it was too complicated/impossible to update in that way, so not a criticism to the devs. Overall, I can tell this update was made with serious love & effort, and it shows major respect for the spirit of the original. And the new areas and fully-fleshed-out graphics were very cool.

Falling out of the map didn't reset me and the last autosave was out of bounds with no way back in. _childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly strange remake. At times extremely loyal to the original, at other times equally willing to tear things out and creatively redesign from scratch. Being that open to experimentation with what many consider one of the best games of all time was a risky move.The end result is, thankfully, very good. The changes feel for the most part well considered, and for those with lots of time with the original, they made the experience feel fresh and unpredictable. Most of the puzzles are redesigned or replaced. The new ones follow similar structures but with entirely different execution.The main event of a remake of Riven is obviously the realtime 3D, high fidelity environment. And they really knocked that part out of the park. Many areas were striking in their visual execution, with nicely detailed scenery and lighting that always felt like it correctly echoed the original look. I know the original Riven better than most places I've lived, so of course there are a few changes I disagreed with and missing details I would have liked to see. But these didn't sour the experience at all.Overall I'm happy and a little surprised with how well this has turned out. I'd recommend it to anyone who played the original or is new to the series with these recent remakes.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely Fantastic! this game is so incredibly optimised and put together, that even though the minimum requirements state that you should have a Ryzen 7 2700x, it runs perfectly fine on a Ryzen 5 5600x, with no issues at all.MYST and RIVEN have been two titles from my childhood that I still regularly revisit for Nostalgia sake, and now that RIVEN has been re-imagined for the modern era, a new generation of folks can experience storytelling and amazing puzzles; sharing in the experiences we had decades before them.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece. What I love most about Riven is that it's not just some puzzles sitting disconnected and half-motivated in an environment, It's this whole world that is coherent and makes sense and motivates the things you can solve and interact with. Very little suspension of disbelief needed (with very few exceptions. looking at you, ). Never seen the world-building and the mechanics so close together in any game of this kind. AAA quality from a true indie studio. Sound design and visual aesthetics are just so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven (2024) is an absolutely incredible remake of the 1997 original. It perfectly captures the artstyle and tone, while managing to remove some of the original's annoyances.I would argue that the only downgrade is the character animations. The original's FMVs using actors still hold up great, whereas the remake's rendered characters and their somewhat choppy animations stick out among an otherwise unfathomably beautiful game.What is Riven? Simply put: A point and click adventure from a first-person view. You do not collect a lot of items, instead you are expected to pay attention to the environment and the lore scattered within. You are expected to keep your own notes and learn the systems of Riven's world.If you like adventure games and you are interested in Cyan's works, this version is a great introduction.Riven is not as cryptic as Myst and the fully 3d environments make navigating the world considerably easier than clicking through the static images of the original.As someone who originally played Riven in 1998, I cannot recommend this game highly enough. The original is still a beautiful game in its own right (and holds up surprisingly well), however the ammenities of the remake granted by 25 years of technological advances make it a much more accessable game for players today.This game is a true labour of love by Starry Expanse/Cyan.Again: Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the original classic in nearly every way. The detailed visuals, the haunting sound track and the layered world-building all come together so well. If you've never played the original and you like puzzle or exploration games at all, you should really experience this masterpiece. If you have played the original, there are enough surprises to make it feel nearly like a new game. The only minor gripe is with the animated characters replacing the captured performances - but it is minor. This remains one of my top 10 games of all time and this remake only cements that standing.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the 1997 original. I loved the remake, especially the new and remixed puzzles!I consider this game (original and as remade) to be a signifcant improvement over Myst because there is always an in-game significance for the various puzzles. Nothing is arbitrary or out of place. The remake definifely stays true to this.If you enjoyed the original or any other games in the Myst series, I definitely recommend. They did great at making the game fresh and exciting again even if you do remember the original puzzles.Reviewed on non-VR.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the original and I've found this remake really refreshing. It's nice to have more active characters in the game but the FMV was just so charming. Edit: I have since replayed the original and though I know 90s FMV has a bad rap, the stuff in Riven was so top quality it really is a shame to loose it, though I understand why they would do it.A gripe I have is that I used the screenshot option quite a bit, along with notes, but I wish the notebook was accessible though the bag as an actual notebook and not exclusively though the menu. _childDocuments_.review: Desktop: Definitely the way to go. You can take notes (and you should). The landscape is gorgeous. The character models look a little simple and out of place in contrast with the extra detailed environments... but you don't interact with people often, so I didn't mind that too much. Overall, wonderful experience.VR Experience: A beautiful game to explore, but the puzzles are not friendly with my Steam Index considering how many notes you need to take. I had some areas that crashed frequently (moving through the marbles occasionally made me crash, and the submarine always made me crash). There were some very difficult to activate levers throughout the game that were made worse by the VR experience. The screenshot "notes" are extremely cumbersome to reference, so it's probably best just to lift up the headset and take notes manually. Except if you walk through a wall, the game crashes. I really struggled to read the cursive through my headset.

_childDocuments_.review: I lack the words to adequately express my abiding love for Cyan Games reviving this beloved entry in the MYST series. I recently left a crestfallen review of Firmament, expressing my disappointment that both as a narrative and a puzzle game, it fell short of even boring for me. I specifically completed every one of it's achievements to exhaust its potential, hoping I had simply missed something. I concluded after doing so that I had not. That Firmament was simply an unrefined vision whose realization failed to meet with its own self-imposed expectations. I expressed my heartbreak at how far the publisher had seemed to have fallen in making masterpieces and how desperately I hoped it wasn't true.Riven as a game did more than just restore my faith in Cyan to publish high quality games that reach into the beauty of aesthetic. It nailed the elements that made Riven special as a game in its time. The photo realistic design language presents a unique fusion of a quasi-historical-true-to-industrial-steam-and-aether-punk fantasy setting. Every element is like walking into a living history museum of a truly fantastic universe where the magic of leather-bound journals, stoppered vials, and alien astrolabes comes alive everywhere you look.And if all of that sounds too esoteric for you, I would humbly ask that you package that feeling and stow it somewhere to be forgotten. Because of all the things which Cyan does best, it is giving the player the opportunity to truly and personally learn to appreciate the world you find yourself dumped into with each successive game. Relish the beauty of the mystery, indulge in the wonder and prospect of unraveling the hidden things and appreciating the sublime connections between.Now before you buy this game, I would make a recommendation. Go out and buy yourself a beautifully embossed or decorated leather-bound journal to take notes in. And use that book to muddle through every puzzle you work through as you play this and every MYST series game you play. Participate in the game with your own journal entries as you untangle the myriad of puzzle elements. From counting systems to mechanical troubleshooting and rudimentary mapping, truly let yourself sink into the sloppy yet elegant messy work of taking your own notes, wrestling with ideas, and jotting your own theories and suppositions to amend with later entries. Do the things which characters throughout this game do and you will come to a deeper appreciation of the characters and your combined investment in their well-being. I whole-heatedly believe you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven. The fifth age. The sequel to Myst. The original Riven is a game that I've carried with me for most of my life. I got a copy on DVD as part of the Myst Trilogy box set, and I was hooked. Everything about it was entrancing, and I kept coming back to it even after I finished it solely to admire the beautiful world. Riven, the remake, is like being able to come back to the world you remembered, but with things being ever so slightly different. Some of the puzzles in this version are slightly different, including the infamous Fire Marble puzzle. This gives the world both a sense of familiarity and a sense of newness as you learn the things that have changed, and get to appreciate the gorgeous visuals with a fully unlocked camera. And that right there is the main thing that this Riven remake does the best. If Riven 1997 let you see into a world, Riven 2024 lets you ENTER that world. When URU was once described as "D'ni In Real Time," THIS is what I had envisioned. It's Riven, rendered in real time, looking just like it did as a point-and-click game. There are a few weaknesses the game has. Namely, the people are a little...off. As a result of supporting VR and having a fully controllable camera, the live-action video has been replaced with 3D modeled people, and the result can be a little bit unsettling. Ultimately it's not a huge problem, because you can easily suspend disbelief for most of the game, but the people have a bit of an uncanny valley effect going on, and not just with their looks. The animations are just a little too jerky and robotic at times, but you ultimately can get used to it, especially since people are a relatively rare sight in this game. The only other potential weakness is the notebook system. The game has a notebook, allowing you to take screenshots and make notes about the screenshots from inside the game. This is a great feature! However, I wish there was a way to access the notebook without having to press the escape key a few times to get to the menu. It would be great if a key, say N, could take you directly to the notebook. In short, Riven is a fantastic experience that I strongly advise adventure game fans play. If you loved the original Riven, you'll still find lots to love here. If you've never played it before, then this is a fantastic way to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun experience that holds up to the original, with better graphics and welcome additions.  The new notebook, while it doesn't have a much-needed keybind to open, is a good addition.  The puzzles have been improved to make answers easier to recall, such as if you have to input some values, you'll be inputting it into something that very clearly resembles something you've already seen before.  But that doesn't make it too easy, you'll still need to put in some thought and maybe revisit areas.  At no point will you feel completely lost, you'll always have just enough to go on to make it to the next step.What to expect: Expect to take notes beyond the in-game notebook.  Paper and pen, draw some images, do some math, and interpolate some numbers.  Some of the puzzle is learning how fictional numbers work and making some assumptions on the way.  Expect to think about more than what is currently on the screen in these puzzles.  The whole world you are in has answers. You don't need knowledge from the first game in the series, Myst, to play this game.I would recommend this to anyone who likes puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others playing the first-person version of Riven, I also played the original on its first time around. And loved it. This is a puzzle + ambiance game. It's decidedly not about shooting, or reaction time. It's about lateral thinking and linear problem-solving and ordering your thoughts. It's about a design perspective on the world. The underlying question is so often: how does this work?! What does it do?Clearly, someone built this thing for a reason: what was that reason? Is there a way around the obstacle?And all of that is set in a context of spiritual - if often slightly disquieting - solitude. It's a digital product that effects a decidedly more mindful state than most digital products.Even the frequent references to writing with a nib pen - a very deliberate process of recording thoughts and ideas. There is a marked difference between the experience of writing slowly versus writing so much closer to the speed of thought when using a keyboard.The medium is the message indeed... This game will not give you the experience you get from a first-person shooter. The feeling is much more like trying to solve a wooden jigsaw puzzle in an empty onsen after a particularly relaxing massage. In fact, one of the more unique facets of the game shows up when you are stumped - you are given the opportunity to sit with your frustration and boredom and the absolute knowledge that there MUST be something you haven't seen or haven't thought of - but your very boredom and frustration get in the way of seeing or thinking of anything new.What I'm trying to say is that this is not a game for everyone. If you're looking for bright lights, loud noises, and fast action, this is not for you. If you want the rare experience of being invited to slow down and turn inwards - while immersed in a richly textured and beautiful world - then please come in, stay a while.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my most anticipated game of 2024, and after finishing it (on GOG, hence my short play time on Steam) I can confirm it's more than lived up to my expectations. And those were surely high, because Riven is on of my two favorite games of all time. For newcomers, this is the version you'll want to play if you want to experience this masterpiece. You are very welcome to also try the 1997 one, but if you have to play only one, it's this remake. If you have played Outer Wilds, it has a lot in common with it, although it is quite harder and will require you to be fully invested in the world and pay attention to every detail if you want to make your way to the end of the adventure (grab a pen and paper!). I do suggest playing the Myst remake before. While it is not strictly necessary, the beginning and end of Riven are directly tied to Myst and won't make much sense if you haven't played it (it can be finished in about 6-8 hours).For longtime fans like myself, it's a delight. Like so many have said : it feels like the Riven you remember, but also a fresh new game, so you'll have the double benefit of reliving a classic in full 3D with the joy of discovering new details, puzzles, and stories.Riven is one of the best puzzle game of all time, and it is so because it is in essence so much more that a puzzle game. Most of those (even Myst) are structured like a series of solid puzzles on top of which there is a good story.In Riven the frontier between story and puzzles is much more fuzzy. The game is full of details and every one of them has been placed here for a reason. But that reason may have nothing to do with any puzzle! Most of them are meant to flesh out the world and enrich a story you'll have to uncover by yourself through exploration, careful observation, hypothesis and deduction. This is a game that elevates its environmental storytelling to a art form. Everything in the world makes sense, from an in-universe perspective. And your relationship with this world is going to be very different than with most games. The obstacles don't feel like puzzles that have been placed specifically for you to resolve them as a player. You are in a foreign world you know nothing about, you don't belong here and while your main objectives are made clear from the beginning  you are going to achieve them is left for you to figure out.So understanding the world of Riven, its history, its main characters and their motivations are all very important to progress. The puzzles all have a reason for being here, and understanding that reason will help you a lot in resolving them. But it's not just about the puzzles, all the details are interesting to examine. That's where the game is fantastic at being immersive. You don't have to ask yourself: "Why did the devs put that here, what am I supposed to do with it as a player to beat the puzzles?". One important note if you want to discover everything by yourself (which I recommend): . Some of them tells you things before you have a chance to figure them out. Not much, it's mostly things like the name of the islands and such but it can take you out of the game a little.For the more "technical" aspects:This is a very beautiful game, and it ran very smoothly at 60fps on Epic settings on my 3080 with 16GB of RAM. The water is especially striking, and the game has some great visual tricks with it that are more than just "it looks cool". The original art direction is perfectly rendered and makes it a really timeless experience.The biggest point of contention is about the characters. While the original 1997 game used FMV that were perfectly integrated in the world, this version used 3D-modeled characters. Don't worry they look waaaay better than the Myst remake. While the rest of the game feels like it could have been produced by a AAA studio, this is where it's useful to remember that Cyan is an indie studio with a fraction of that budget and has one(!) person fully dedicated to the characters. They have been unevenly polished: while most of them look quite good, one encouter especially seems to have recieved much less polish, while a couple of others are just stunning. Don't expect AAA quality from them, but it's overall pretty good and a great achievement for a studio of this size. They also took this opportunity to adapt some dialogue, movements, and add new characters a a lore treat for the fans (the are )And no, it's unrealistic to expect them to integrate the original FMVs. It was possible in Myst because most of the characters spoke through a little screen but the Riven FMVs are low-res and adapted to a fixed shot, not a free-look 3D game. They would just look like out-of-place 2D sprites moving arounf.Not to mention the problem of Gehn, whose monologue spans on several different shots. In 3D you can keep your eyes on him at all times so he would just snap into a different posture 3-4 times during his speech.(they actually made a nice little addition in the remake, not in his lines but in the way he moves, that makes his speech even better, by making use of the free 3D environment. It's subtle but very interesting)I also have to talk about the changes and additions from the original !For the most part they are great. A couple of details that can be debated, but this remakes adds infinitly more than it loses. The additional details and adaptations have been very well-thought-out. Some inconsistensies have been corrected, some areas expanded, the Rivenese culture is much more present and interesting, the Age of Riven really  like it's decaying (instead of the game just telling you this though journal entries)...The two main puzzles have also been touched. While the structure remains the same, they have been made more accessible. I don't feel for a second that they have been "dumbed down".The totem puzzle does lose a little of its organic feeling (from a narrative perspective it was really elegant but I never figured it out on my own when I was young), but it was a really obscure one and impossible to adapt 1:1 on a free-roaming 3D game. Some of the difficulty has been instead moved to a different structure, one that is in itself a new puzzle for those who aleready played Riven 1997, and is much more narratively coherent and interesting.Same goes for the marble puzzle. While it appears much simple on the surface, it requires you to figure out a couple more things than the original did. They will be very easy for a returning fan, but for a new player, it's not that much simpler, just less frustrating. And it also helps to strenghten the narrative.There is one small puzzle ( on Survey Island) that I feel is out-of-place in a game like Riven. And the mechanisms inside the  are a bit obscure for the player, a thought that someone has developed .There is also a couple of things that can be improved I'd like to adress the developers:- As a non-english player, the ability to remap the controls is absent and the game does not automatically detect my AZERTY layout, which forces me to change my input settings in Windows. It's not much, but it does make the game feel less professional.- The subtitles could use more options to make them more visible (font size, background color, etc.).- I looooove that the journals are handwritten and it's a wonderful touch.  some people may undersandably benefit from a overlay with a more legible typewritten font that you could toggle.

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps the greatest microcosm of the loss of uniquely spiritual, eerie quality of Riven 1997 that I fell in love with in favor of dull light fantasy rationalism in Riven 2024 is how animal life and natural formations, previously intertwined with the fate of Moiety, now stay firmly outside the text. With changes to puzzles and visuals, the Sunner's belch, along with the rock they lounge on, cease to be means by which you immerse yourself in the world and culture of Riven, becoming simply window dressing, temporary distractions that ring hollow. None escape this fate. Look at le epic fish! Isn't it kewl :OKeeping them as aesthetic background of the age and pasting right over with a more grounded, technology-first solution (even if there's something intriguing about literally viewing the world through the lens of oppressed), resembles a palimpsest. In it, we see a fundamental shift that Cyan began with Myst remakes come to fruition. Through this choice, and indeed many similar smaller choices, Riven 2024 conveys a different message than the original 1997 version and ironically could be seen as Gehn's preferred take on Riven - logic and technology not only first, but uber alles. To me, as much as I enjoyed my time revisiting familiar places with improved graphics, this alone warrants a negative review. VR-first nature of remake's design doesn't do it any favors either. Between fervent adherence to sliding doors, numerous puzzle simplifications with strictly chest-high interactions, various cool levers homogenized into VR-friendly buttons, weird blink-alike blackening of the screen at key moments where your character has to be repositioned even with accessibility turned off... You have to wonder whether collapse of the bridge between boiler and temple was staged so as to prevent VR players from having a tedious long walk and further commit to a more instant, less delayed gratification philosophy of jingling keys in front of their faces. An irony second only to "Gehn's Riven" is how putting supposedly immersive technology forward actually reduces variety in interactions and progression.VR necessitating use of 3d models over live actors further undermines the magic - clearly the developers are more skilled at environment design than modelling humans. Poor likenesses, stilted animations, HORRENDOUS lip sync that made me double-triple check whether I'm hallucinating. This cheapens every moment of character interaction, but none as much as your first impression of Rivenese village, now seemingly bereft of life. Barely noticeable 3d models run out of the frame before you can spot them, as if ashamed of their ugliness being recorded next to numbers in my notebook.I suppose it's inevitable that as creators age, their perspective changes and so does their output. This is an eternal curse of the remake - you only have to peek at now seemingly so dated Star Wars discourse to see how much grief there's been over various modifications Lucas committed to over the years. Parting one world (of the original) from another (of the remake) is something I therefore encourage and hope that this remake will not come to be seen as the "definitive version" in the future.Here's to hoping Cyan turns the page on remakes and produces more new, original games to find themselves again - though if firmament is any indication, the studio seems to be running out of juice. Still, one must imagine the ending has not yet been written!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's amazing. But it also has many very annoying flaws that they should have improved prior to releasing it, and that I still hope they will improve.For the most part, the visuals feel both beautiful and realistic at the same time. However, I am very frustrated by the comparatively poor quality of the people. It's very sad that the very first thing you experience in this game is seeing a very cartoony looking Atrus. It feels like you are just watching some stupid kids cartoon. The movement of his mouth doesn't even match the words coming out! I don't get it, did they not play their own game before releasing it? If so, it should have been obvious that the character models are terrible and they needed to have an FMV video footage option, at least for non-VR users, as many people are not playing this game in VR. Or just make the 3D models more realistic somehow, but this is just terrible, and I doubt they could have ever gotten any 3D models to look nearly as good as FMV could have.The way you enable HDR is stupid and confusing. Figuring out how to enable HDR is not supposed to be one of the puzzles in Riven! They couldn't just include it with the other graphic settings? Anyway, once you do figure out how to turn it on, even if you have an HDR display with HDR enabled, it actually looks worse not better. What I mean is, the game looks the best if you have HDR disabled for both your monitor and in the game settings, enabling it in the game does make it look better than having HDR enabled on the monitor but not in the game settings. Anyway, with HDR fully enabled for both the monitor/system and in the game settings, when you are looking at something very bright and shiny, like the sun or the outside of the temple, yes it pops much more and looks way more amazing. But normal scenes look washed out, and the game is a lot less beautiful overall.I haven't finished the entire game yet, but so far the puzzles are nice and different enough from the original that I can enjoy playing the game. They fit well into the world, they make sense, and are fun to solve. I will update this section after completing the game.I don't really remember what was in the original game's journals, but this time around, reading them really helps you to understand what this world is about, and the characters and story around what is happening. It's not a ton of reading, and it doesn't have to read like a well written novel, you are just reading people's journals and it helps you to fill in what they are like, and what has been and is happening.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Be aware, this is not a straight remake of the original. It's mostly the same, but if you played the original then early on you will notice some things have changed. Mostly for the better, there's some amazing additions. The 3d character models aren't as expressive as the FMV of the original and some of those moments are absent in this version, but that's just the nature of the new format. On the whole, I'd say it's worth experiencing at the asking price. I tried it out the VR mode on a Rift S, it was decent. It's clearly a non-VR game adapted to VR, so it's a little awkward, but not unplayable. I had a bit of texture twitching here and there, nothing too bad. I'd say if you can, it's worth trying just to stand in these incredible environments.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's fantastic. A wonderful remake in every way. It's beautiful, runs well (3080, 5800X3D, 4K), and remixes things in great ways to make it so you cannot simply rely on your memory from years ago. The music is a wonderful ambient backing track that is eery & incredibly memorable - it really plucks the nostalgia strings well.The major puzzles have their answers re-generated each run, so you need to learn the systems & actually have an answer. Only complaints is some things not well optimized for controller (like twisting wheels, which happens often).
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't think I've ever played a game like Riven.  I played and got stuck on the original way back in 1997, and even back then I felt like it was something wholly unique.  Its predecessor, Myst, while certainly somewhat dense in the way its puzzles were presented, played mostly like vignette of challenges that helped you progress through its various Ages, and that's essentially how most puzzle games I've played have felt.  Riven is... different.  It seems to have more in common with "walking simulators".  Rather than a series of mostly disparate puzzles, the player's focus is on immersing yourself in the art, culture, and science of an unfamiliar world and its inhabitants.  There are a few minor, quick puzzles throughout the story, but the game as a whole is about using the knowledge you gain to complete what amounts to a single, "final" puzzle that both literally and figuratively connects everything you've seen.  (Incidentally, that puzzle is what I got stuck on back in 1997.)  That Riven does this in a way that feels so natural and intuitive - while still taxing your brain - makes completing it feel rewarding in a way that I have never experienced in a puzzle game.  Add to that the fascinating premise of Ages and Linking Books that Cyan Worlds put so much thought and creativity into all those years ago, and I can't help but think that this remake has taken the spot as my favorite puzzle game of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know more I can add to the conversation, other than I freaking love the Riven remake. The graphics, environments, sound, lighting, music.. All 10 out of 10. The original 1997 game is one of my favorite all time games ever since it first released. It's my favorite of the Myst series and my favorite out of all Cyan's games. One of the best surprises about this remake, for me, is how they reworked some of the puzzles. It made this game feel both old & familiar and new & refreshing. I've played a ton of remasters/remakes over the years but never anything quite like this. It feels and sounds exactly like I remember the original game. The new puzzles add a newness to the experience that made playing it more interesting that I anticipated.Riven is a game rich in ambiance and environmental story telling that draws you in. It's the kind of game I like to play with the lights down and a good headset or sound system. The puzzles never feel arbitrary. From start to finish it is a very rich and rewarding experience.If you're a fan of Myst you owe it to yourself to play this. If you love first-person adventure/puzzle games, I heartily recommend it. Riven was a masterpiece when it came out, and this remake is equally masterful. Thank you, Cyan! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remake of one of the most organically designed and critically received puzzle computer games of all time. Whatever small critiques I may have (Some of the 3D performances are rough; the new music is not very thematic) are quickly lost in just how faithfully and creatively renewed this game is. The changes made, both to the benefit of VR players, the puzzles and the areas themselves, fit seamlessly into the old gameplay, as if this was always how Riven was meant to be played; Indeed, this may just become the defining way to play Riven here on out. Greatly looking forward to Cyan's continued work remaking or creating new works in the Myst series.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake! It changes way more than I expected, and all of it just adds to the experience and immersion. You can tell Rand kept a notebook of little things he always wished he could go back and improve. This is a must play, even better than the Myst remake, since it had so much more to update and yet kept the tone and style more intact.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I simply HAD to write a quick "review", even though I've just made it to the Jungle Island with the plesiosaurs sunning on the rock (chapter 2 if you're counting). Coming upon these beasts was one of my favorites moment playing the original Riven 27 years ago. Sneaking up on them then watching them lumber away into the water was so fulfilling with the visual remake of Riven I almost yelled.THIS is how you remake a game! Other companies take note:CYAN did this masterfully in all respects. I loved the Myst remakes and of course all the original Myst games, but seeing RIven in all it's visual splendor, even though I haven't even really explored the jungle island area yet? Jaw dropping visuals, beautiful score bringing back such good memories. The satisfaction of solving puzzles is so fulfilling, still, as it was with the original Riven. (Note: I purchased the "Companion" DLC, which I know will help at some point. It's very well-composed and offers small clues, as well as full solutions. I'm so glad it's also in PDF form, so I can copy it from the game's files to my desktop and alt-tab back and forth from the game if and when I need help)Back to the game: as noted, stunning (and I mean STUNNING) visuals, beautiful audio score that touches on so many aural memories of the game, gorgeous animations abound everywhere. Photorealistic water/ocean effects. THe character animations are very well done in 3D (I don't mind the lack of the FMV videos from the original; no way to implement those without degrading the "look" of the game, plus taking up a LOT more install space). Some of the puzzle solving (so far) isn't exactly the same  as in the original but the basics appear to still be there, and I don't mind that. I'm treating this as a new game.Important: the RIVEN re-creation is optimized wonderfully, even on my 5-year old Dell desktop PC that, while still robust, certainly isn't top of the line anymore. And that's with ALL visual settings cranked up to EPIC. Amazing. I mean, I've got a little fan-noise, but not much. If this runs on MY PC, it'll run on yours :-)OK, back to the game. I haven't been as happy to play a computer game in quite a while, and I've played TONS of PC games. Oh, wait....did I mention MULTIPLE SAVE SLOTS (I've used 4 so far, I'd venture there are more than that)? Us older adventure gamers sure appreciate that, Cyan teams. Thank you! Very few games have that feature anymore.For me, so far? 10/10. I can't wait to progress further. Damn, this game is so gorgeous. Glad I'm retired. More time to play Riven :-)Thanks for creating this masterpiece, Cyan. Again.*****NOTE: I am NOT playing the VR version, so I cannot speak to anything VR-related. Just the non-VR version.***********Two notes now that I've been playing for several hours:1) There are 10 manual save slots, which is great.2)Do NOT waste your money on the companion guide, as i did. Many of the "solutions" are obtuse and are in little way actual solutions. There is a good video walkthrough in the "guides" here on Steam and also a decent walkthrough online on one of the gaming sites. The five (I've been counting) times I've needed the "companion guide", it has been an actual help only two of those times. Waste of money.Loving the game, though!

_childDocuments_.review: It’s possible this is the greatest remake of all time.I used to think remakes were just easy money grabs. Then recently we started getting stuff like resident evil 2 and FF7R, lovingly crafted remakes of classics. And Riven might just beat all of them. It is a perfect remake and a perfect game and it improves on every good part of the original and smooths out every overly difficult part. I always liked Myst a lot more than Riven and I LOVED the Myst remake….. but now I dunno. This might be my fave it is just so absolutely brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven ("The Sequel to Myst") was a true masterpiece, helping to define what a point-and-click puzzle adventure game could be and *should* be. This remake preserves the same degree of immersive environmental storytelling and gorgeously-rendered worlds, while also expanding and modifying the gameplay to keep veteran players on their toes. Truly a delightful experience. If you have never played a Myst game before, please try the original Myst game or the Myst remake (both on Steam). Myst 1 has some story and lore elements that could help your experience with Riven. Otherwise, watch some Myst 1 YouTube videos and just dive straight into Riven (which IMHO is a better game anyway).I did not get a chance to play this in VR, but I will at my first opportunity. It doesn't seem like the VR market is quite there for content vs affordability, but Cyan keeps releasing VR-compatible games which, collectively, give me some hope that VR technology could become more accessible.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Recreating the experience of first playing this game with friends, all huddled around the same screen, has been a joy! Now, we can cast one of us playing but still made sure to bring out the notepad and bounce ideas off of one another. Puzzles have been revamped and new elements added, meaning there is even more reason to return to the Fifth Age. Cyan has done an incredible job. As my friend and I both said, this is how the game looked in our memories of the original. One more room to explore and one more lever to pull.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, beautiful, and immersive, just as the original was.  Would highly recommend to anyone who loves puzzle games and especially those who've played the original.  Cyan again brings puzzles that are wonderfully integrated into the world building and storytelling of the game!  I have been really enjoying so far and am excited to be solving brand new puzzles and hearing the new music added!Was a huge fan of the original and so I was incredibly excited for the new release.  It was a nice surprise to find new puzzles that I could solve from scratch instead of just slowly remembering how I solved the original.  Almost every change is justified, as the original game was largely unbeatable by the general public and most people who played the original would be lying if they said they didn't need to look up at least one of the puzzles solutions.  From rearranging locations, to streamlining your path through the world, the changes are designed to better guide you through the more difficult puzzles.There is of course a bit of sadness, when finding some of the locations changed more than expected, but overall I think the changes are good, making the game more appealing to new players.  It's important to remember the goal is to solve every puzzle in the game ,  looking at a guide or cheat-list.I'm so happy this game was made, and I'm always happy to support Cyan so they can continue to make great games with beautiful worlds and storytelling.  Can't wait to see what they'll put out next!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is an example of what a modern remake should truly be. A modern update to the game that fixes what didn't work in the original and upgrades what did work. There are various remakes that are designed to show what the game would be if the tech we have now was what we had back then, and Riven is one of those. It takes the locations, and imagery of the original 1997 game and gives them a major glow up. It fixes some of the more tedious puzzles from the original (the fire marble puzzle from the end of the game for example). The music that is has really emphasizes the ambient atmosphere more that the original, thanks to its use of real instruments. Add VR compatibility to the mix, and you have a remake that is a brilliant love letter to the fans of the MYST franchise. This really makes me excited to see if Cyan Worlds Inc. are going to remake MYST III and IV.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Myst games, and Riven was without a doubt my favourite of the series when I was younger. I have replayed Riven again in recent years and when I saw this version with updated graphics and some new puzzles you bet I added it to my cart immediately. My issue is that this game as it exists is unplayable for me. The motion sickness I experience on it is insane - even with all the recommended setting adjustments, after 5 minutes of playing I would have to go lie down. This isn't exclusive to me either, the top thread on the discussions page are from people complaining about the same thing. I hope that the devs are able to make some adjustments or somehow create a click-to-move option like the OG version to help with this issue. Unfortunately I had to refund, but would happily repurchase in future if this issue is fixed because I really do love these games.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended (with a few caveats)The flatscreen experience is fairly polished and the game itself is great with a super unique approach to puzzle design. However, there seem to be a lot of issues running the game in VR at the moment. I finished this game with a mix of both flatscreen and VR  modes and really enjoyed my time with it for the most part and it seemed to played well in both modes. However, I've had to start the game twice over due to save file corruption and redo several sections for the same reason. I think this might have been the result of jumping between VR and flatscreen modes. I also had several UE5 crashes while only using the flatscreen mode. Which may have been caused by continuing the game from a VR save. For VR players, it might be worth waiting until a few more patches have been released before purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: I only just played a few hours, Did the old Riven somewhere in 1997, so much memories come up now, the sounds, the music, it was such a great game back then.  I am so glad they did a remake on this game, It is really fantastic. It is so totally worth to buy it. Cyan Worlds, thank you, you did a great job.By the way, it works perfectly on linux (mint) and on a Ryzen 3 5600 16 gb
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan changed a few things around but the things they added or changed make sense lore-wise and add greater context to the world. It's all around very faithful to the original and only has a few minor bugs I am sure will get patched out. Be careful on the sub though, I got soft locked in a perma-loop once.I definitely recommend this game to seasoned fans or just fans of puzzle games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. I was never able to get into the original title (I'm not fond of pixelated point-and-click's, sue me!), but always loved the atmosphere and storytelling in the Myst series. This remake, for me at least, finally marries solid graphics and movement/navigation with the always great story. The impressive visual fidelity and remastered audio tracks really bring the vision and world to life in a way that the original just couldn't at the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Great trip down memory lane - but with a significant amount of new features to make it all seem fresh and new again -- bravo!My only complaints are trivial: I occasionally had trouble with the dual joysticks (I played using an Xbox controller), and sometimes "landing" on the "hot spots" was problematic.For example, I wanted to click on a doorknob, to open a door, but the pointer cursor went just a little bit too far to the right, so I scooted it back towards the left, but it went past the doorknob, and I had to scoot it back right again, etc....I would REALLY have liked a "snap to hot spot when close enough" feature, to avoid just a little bit of frustration.Also, while not absolutely necessary, I think a little compass icon - even just a little circle in one of the corners that indicates which way is North, would have been helpful while traversing all the twisting passages and pathways.  Some people may say that would be cheating, or making things too easy, but there were several times I would have liked to know exactly which way I was facing.However, these trivial complaints only detracted slightly from the beauty, the exploration, the head-scratching, and the "A-HA!" moments when I finally figured things out.   Mild spoiler ahead:By far my favorite of the entire Myst series (all of the other games left me either mildly or HUGEly disappointed), I am glad they really did this one right!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game, and certainly a contender for best adventure game of the year.Still, I prefer the original, which I played back in 1998, and then again a couple of weeks ago, in anticipation for the remake.Here's why :- In the old game, puzzles felt like they were part of the world. "Solving" them was really about immersing yourself into the world. They were replaced with new puzzles, which, while really good on their own, don't reach that same level of seamless integration. I can only guess as to why the designers made that decision, but the probable reason is that, in the old game, you could literally walk through hints without ever noticing them. This is why people felt the game was hard at the time...possibly too hard?- In the old game, moving around was super fast. You had the zip mode, and could skip any transition with the ESC button. In the remake, and even with the option to skip most transitions, I felt that moving around was more cumbersome. It might not seem much, but when you're stuck, the last thing you want is go through an unskippable animation for the 100th time (I'm thinking about you, domes).- The old game had real actors. While the new 3D models are ok, I don't think the new sections carry the same level of emotional intensity.Overall, my recommendation is to play this game, but if you're not too put off by the graphics, I would highly encourage you to play the old version, first. It's still possibly the best adventure game, ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I can't describe how incredible it is to see one of the very first stories I ever explored on my own as a child brought back to life with such love and care. Other than some minor adjustments to puzzles and a few new areas, it feels like not a single pebble is out of place in this world.Two critiques: this version seems to take just as long to load new areas as it did to change discs in the original. Recommend installing on solid state! Also, I couldn't get VR working, waited 30 minutes for the first scene to load after the intro and gave up.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's great that everyone else seems to be enjoying the game, but I was looking forward to replaying a game I had trouble with in my childhood so  I could solve it now that I am better at such things.Seeing all the radical changes they made for the sake of making the game easier really made me not want to play it. Familiar places are now entirely different. The creators really don't seem to understand their own source material and what made it great. Instead of updating a classic they made a new game. I don't understand why they did this, Myst was remade much better than this.Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I never really had the chance to do a true play through of the original Riven. I'd watched a let's play of it well before I ever had an opportunity to play, because I wanted to know the stories. This rebuilt Riven feels like it was purpose built just for me and that situation. I knew bits of pieces of what I was doing which helped steer me on a forward course but otherwise I had to take my own notes for the brand new puzzles, while exploring new areas. I loved every minute of it.The world felt rich and fleshed out, even more so than before, and getting to walk in these locations in VR was especially fun though I did switch to normal play near the end for convenience for note taking.My one complaint is the lack of transitions. If this is a graphical thing then I take it back since my computer isn't really up to snuff for this, but every transition movie was made into a black load screen. Every elevator, mine cart, maglev train, ladder, and even just turning the maglev around spawns a black screen and very brief load. This felt really disappointing as it removed some of the most breath taking moments from Riven, the mine cart ride in particular. I hold some hope that maybe a future patch or mod might put these sequences back in, but given the rest of the world's face lift, I was willing to forgive this draw back.At the end of the day I played this to get lost in a world and be part of a story that wasn't interested in holding my hand. I got both of these in spades and loved it dearly. But I swear to Yeesha if you remake Myst 3 and don't include the marble ride I'm burning Cyan to the ground.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic re-make of one of the best puzzle games of all time. This is a spell-binding game : the graphics are superb, the music is excellent, the puzzles are great, the sound design is super-immersive.It feels so good to return to this world so many years after playing the original, and being able to freely roam around. The changes from the original make sense and are totally in line with the spirit of the original, while making things a bit more accessible and keeping things fresh.If I must nitpick, I encountered a few minor glitches, such as clipping through geometry on one occasion in the jungle, and also a book that was hard to click. Also, comparing to the original, I do admit that I had a soft spot for the original FMV as the new character models, while good, feel a bit more game-y. But I understand the why and it's truly no big deal.What truly sets this game apart as a classic, for me, is how much it doesn't feel like game. It feels like I'm visiting a real place. Very, very few games ever achieve that. This world has a rarely paralleled mood and feeling to it. And the remake has perfectly recaptured the unique feeling that the original had. An absolute must-play for puzzle game fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Like it's predecessor Myst, this game originally set a pattern that others copied on and improved. Now it's time for the update to take a quality of life leaf or two out of the playbook of those that came after. With new as well as changed puzzles for the originals, it means that us Old Timers can't just rock up and flex our knowledge of the local counting system, or remember what fire marble goes where - anyone who says they can do that from memory anyway is lying through their teeth!! - so this has been a pleasing blend of "I remember how to do this" and "Huh , WTF happened to the <insert favourite environmental puzzle of your choice>"I can't comment on the VR aspect - my playtime was solidly 2D, but this game is a solid 10/10 on both puzzles and visuals - there are plenty screenshots now lined up to be my new desktop wallpaper...
