_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great puzzle game. It's been adapted from the original point and click game to a 3D experience, and done very well. The puzzles are very satisfying to work out, and notes are absolutely necessary when playing through the game. As someone who had seen the original played through as a kid, coming back so many years later and refreshing those memories with a modern take was a blast. My only complaint would be some animations taking a while to complete. Especially climbing ladders. I can forgive the animations that are just some mechanical component taking time to move, but in some cases having to wait for 3 10 second ladder climbing animations in a row gets tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Played original Riven many Ages ago... this new version is so incredibly immersive. You can spend ages (no pun intended) each island, drawn in by the unique beauty, the immersive colours, textures and sounds, and forget what you were hoping to achieve. The best just got better, but I sense a rift in the game like the original...
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings on this game are very mixed. I should probably start by saying I never played the original Riven, so I'm coming at it from a new player's perspective.On the one hand, it's a very immersive experience, with beautiful visuals, a genuinely interesting setting and a compelling story. All the puzzles feel naturally integrated into the world, and it has one of the coolest/most unique fast-travel features I've seen in a game. However, as many others have already pointed out, the way the game is structured means you will likely need backtrack a lot, which results in most of the game time being getting from point A to B. I didn't mind it too much just because the animations are engaging enough, but I can definitely see it being a turn-off for other people. My other main issue is just how short the game is. There are really only 2 main puzzles, with lots of little mini-puzzles in between, and I was really hoping for some more.If there was a bit more content this would be an easy recommendation, but as it is, it depends on how much you're willing to pay for a ~10-12 hour experience. A memorable and unique experience, no doubt, but a short one. Though I do think if you have VR it definitely adds more value to the offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is fantastic. Riven is one of my favorite games of all time, and this remake does not disappoint. The additional puzzles and changes to the original puzzles keep it fresh even if you already know the core goals or mechanics. I often find myself delighted by what *isn't* there from the original, because it means there's something new to solve. It's awesome actually feeling the islands and landscapes connect. That first maglev ride is ::chefs-kiss::.Pros: No switching CDs every time you change islandsCons: You still have to wait for maglev door to close every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Completely blown away by this version of the game.I just wanted to run the game for five minutes to see what the developers could do with one of my favorite video games before playing it in more depth.I was stuck for an hour and a half rediscovering a world I thought I knew.I'll update this review later, but I just wanted to give the game a thumbs-up to support it and say that this is perhaps the most beautifully crafted world you can explore in a video game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the original a few years ago for maybe about 10 minutes, but couldn't really get used to the slideshow-style navigation, so I decided to hold out for the inevitable remake. I can finally see why the game is considered to be such a classic; it has the same mysterious feel and practical puzzle design sensibilities as Myst, but it took the integration with the environment and lore and pushed it to the next level. It's such an old game, but I haven't seen another that does cryptic environmental storytelling this well.There were a few puzzles that felt a bit cheap (find the inconspicuous collection of pixels to click on), but in the grand scheme of things those few moments felt pretty forgivable - or even refreshing, in a weird way. I've played a lot of games lately where I can feel the designer's hand guiding me almost every step of the way, where every little potential frustration or inconvenience has been sanded off. The result is often something hollow and inoffensive where I'm just guessing the designer's intentions, being right most of the time, and going through the motions instead of playing the game in an organic way. Riven was a breath of fresh air in that regard. I never once thought about what the game wanted in a meta sense, I was just immersed in an interesting world that had left me to my own devices.As I understand it, they've redesigned a lot of the original game's puzzles, so I'm curious what the differences are. I'd guess that some fans with heavy nostalgia for the original might be upset with some of the changes. They could be right, maybe the original game's puzzle design was more interesting; I wouldn't know. But as someone who came in with no prior opinion, I thought it was a fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: My dad first plopped me down in front of Riven when I was about 7. Since then I've played almost every re-release of it. This has been the best by far. Honestly it looks as good as I remember it, but obviously it looks leagues better than the original. I just kept stopping in wonder at how amazing everything looked. On top of that, they actually changed parts of the original game, modernizing and streamlining puzzles to better work with today's playstyles. I liked that I actually had to learn some new things to complete the game, rather than blasting through the puzzles I've solved dozens of times. I do think that this has to be the last time I buy the game...right?
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The feeling of stepping back in to Riven was as good in 2024 as it was when I first did all those years back. The changes to puzzles were amazing as it allowed me to experience that thrill of figuring out a complex puzzle all over again. I felt like a kid again. I wish there would be more games made like Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A solid puzzle game where the culture and art of the worlds you discover all feels thought-through and interconnected in a masterful way. I love this remake of the original classic and the ability to soak in the environment at all angles. You slowly peel away layers and understand more about how the world and its puzzles work. Just wish there were ray-traced reflections, as the screen space reflections can get a little glitchy in parts. Other than that, this is a beautifully-detailed world.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: So far my experience with the game has been overall positive! Visually the game is stunning; its amazing to see this game fully-realized in 3D after so many years. The revamped puzzles and overall simplification are honestly a welcome change, esp since the original could be a bit obtuse/tedious at times with its puzzle design.However, there are also several bugs I've encountered, ranging from visual to game-breaking. At one point my FOV dropped into the single digits after interacting with an object, and was only able to fix it by relaunching the game. So, in its current state I would still recommend the game, but hopefully the bugs get fixed in a future update.8/10  (10/10 if the bugs are fixed)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm...I would give a mixed review if I could. A lot of love went into this, and - for the most part - it brings back amazing childhood memories. However it also deviates from the original in some significant ways that are difficult to accept. I'm also very sad to see that the real life acting scenes have been replaced with subpar 3d ones. I think part of what made the original Riven so iconic and part of what really drew you into the story, was the delivery of the actors which just sadly doesn't come through with the 3d character models.Would I recommend it? Yea sure. It retains a lot of the atmosphere. But I don't think I would recommend it to someone over the original unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Whoa. I beat Riven? I beat Riven!Gorgeous world. Genuinely some of my favorite fictional architecture. There is joy in simply inhabiting this game.Moderate puzzle difficulty that maybe feels artificially enhanced by how much tenacity is required to comb these labyrinthine islands for every last necessary detail, to say nothing of how leisurely a pace the game forces you to move via its decrepit transportation machinery. I loved hating these machines. They encouraged me to think hard about where I actually wanted to go next, instead of simply idly wandering when I wasn't sure.As a "Myst" game, it is leaner and more focused than others in its genre. It feels smaller than Myst. But it wields its restraint exceedingly well. What's there is awesome. Riven even has a bona fide plot of sorts. I liked every second of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is one of the greatest video game sequels ever made. Made by Cyan Worlds back in 1997, Riven absolutely blew Myst out of the water. Why is that, you may ask? Well, because while Myst had clear objectives you had to do, Riven was all about  In the opening of the game, you are given 3 clear objectives to do when you partake on your quest. Those objectives being: "Find and capture Gehn", "Find and free Catherine", and then "Find a way to signal Atrus". But, oh no! You are immediately locked in jail, your book is stolen from you, the only way you can capture Gehn, and the person who captures you dies shortly after, leaving you with no other option but to explore the vast landscape of Riven. The reason Riven is so complex is because of the lack of direction that is given to you. You just need to use your wits and explore, finding and completing its various puzzles. Myst was a lot more strict during its production since Cyan Worlds had to abide by strict guidelines with the game, making them unable to see the game's true scope. Riven's production was a lot less strict, and Cyan Worlds was allowed to literally go nuts and make one of the most beautiful and complex adventure puzzle games to come out of the 90's. This remake further expands on what made Riven so good as there are entirely new challenges for you to face, and entire sections from the original game are even cut, but technically not at the same time, like, for example, the bridge leading to Crater Island. Interacting with the lever that would bring the bridge down and make it become usable in the original Riven now causes the bridge to collapse, and now you'll have to find another way to cross over to Crater Island entirely. But, the true and definitive way to experience the Riven remake is, of course, in Virtual Reality (VR). I don't think the Cyan Worlds developers really realized how much they have made one of the most beautiful VR experiences to come out of the modern age. And just like the original Riven, Myst's VR remake was more of a test of what was possible, and Riven, once again, blew Myst out of the water. This is truly one of the greatest video game remasters of all time, and barely anything comes close. Riven is truly the definitive VR benchmark.Go buy it. Seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: it only took 27 years for graphics technology to be able to do Riven in real time. seriously, though, this is an excellent remake, a remake done right. every change feels like it fits, and makes the experience better. i can't wait to someday play this in VR, too, once i can afford the setup for that. if you like the original Riven, any version of Myst, Cyan's other games, or are just an adventure game fan in general, this is a must-get!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is the sequel to Myst, picking up right where the previous game left off. If you've not played Myst yet, I recommend playing that game first. There are many different versions of Myst, and I have a review on the Steam page for the most recent version (simply titled Myst) that should help you decide which version is right for you.Unlike Myst, which has three different remakes, this is the first time that Riven has been remade. As such, playing this version - with updated graphics, free-roam movement, VR support, extra content - seems like a no-brainer. Unfortunately, the situation is far more complicated than that. Calling this a "remake" isn't the most accurate description. This game is a dramatically different take on the source material. Though the broad strokes of the original story of Riven are still there, the details have been changed, and the gameplay is almost unrecognizable.Reworking this game so thoroughly was a bold choice. I had always been a fan of the original Riven because it was one of the only puzzle games I've ever seen to create puzzles that integrated perfectly with the environment. Nothing in the world of Riven is an explicit puzzle, rather the puzzles are derived from your lack of knowledge about the cohesive, coherent world that you have invaded. There are no purpose-built test chambers or arbitrary locking systems, rather there are practical mechanisms that aren't documented because you were never supposed to be the one using them. There is a culture that you don't understand because you were never supposed to be visiting them. The game is coherent in a way that almost no other game I have ever played has been. To fundamentally rework Riven without upsetting that intricate weaving of narrative and world-building and gameplay would take some significant effort. I am a firm believer that with enough dedication to that goal someone could make another game like Riven, but it would be no easy task.What did Cyan do to maintain that cohesion in this game? Effectively, they didn't even try, and the result has left me with mixed feelings. The new Riven is far closer to Myst in structure, with a world that is physically believable, visually intriguing, but functionally ridiculous. In that regard, I suppose it resembles most puzzle games. While the puzzles may be somewhat more narratively justified here than they were in Myst, they are nowhere near as perfectly integrated as they were in the original Riven. There are puzzles for puzzles' sake. There are character behaviors that don't make logical sense. There are unconvincing environmental behaviors. All of these in the name of explicit puzzles.For me, this destroys a fundamental appeal of Riven, but what it *doesn't* do is make this game a bad experience. Riven had always been a unique case, and I have enjoyed plenty of puzzle games that had more direct approaches to their puzzles. When taken for what it is, this version of Riven is just that: a very good but fairly standard puzzle game. In my opinion, that's a step back from the incredible work of art that the original game was, but it's not a bad place to be in a vacuum. If you didn't know this was a remake, you'd probably have a good time here.That said, as someone who has played both versions of the game, I see this release somewhat differently.  I have watched many people play through the original game, and often those who stopped before reaching the end did so because they found it too difficult. This is a common sentiment. Riven is generally considered to be an incredibly difficult game. That difficulty largely arises from the indirect nature of its puzzles. Seasoned gamers will come into Riven looking for more traditional puzzles and won't find them. Piecing together the components of the world that will help you do what you're trying to do is exponentially more difficult if you're thinking of that original Riven as a game and not as a world.  game doesn't require that mental shift. This game presents the player with a far more guided path through far more explicit puzzles. As such, I see it as a welcome alternative for those who enjoyed Myst but couldn't make it through Riven on account of the difficulty. You'll get the broad story arc and be set up to play the later games, but the experience will be far more Myst-like.For returning players, the recommendation is more difficult. Part of me is disappointed in this game. It is a clear downgrade from the original product, and the fact it bears the Riven name and is sold as a remake will undoubtedly cause many people to play this version instead without knowing any better. Given the number of Myst remakes that have happened over the years, perhaps the work put into this product will result in a more faithful remake of Riven at some point in the future, though I wouldn't hold my breath for it. I would love to see such a product. It deserves to exist.Still, another part of me is happy that I have something to point to for those who struggled with that original game. If this is the gateway that gets more people to play Myst III, perhaps it was worth it after all. And of course, I did have a good time with it. If these puzzles comprised Myst VI, I wouldn't be feeling as confused as I do right now. I would be singing the praises of another solid puzzle game in the Myst universe that lives up to the original Myst's standards. The only reason this elicits negative feelings is the fact that it doesn't live up to Riven, the title it bears.If I could rate "mixed" here on Steam, I would. Since I can't, I think "not recommended" is the better option. If I'm recommending against this game for first-time players, I think that's the recommendation that ought to take precedent in my selection.

_childDocuments_.review: I had several crashes on my Valve Index, particularly around the domes, also shadows looked really strange, semi-transparent, and would appear and disappear as I moved my head. When I started playing on my desktop, for some reason the VR 'comfort' setting was still enabled, which removes transport sequences, once I found the setting I was able to view them again, but for a while thought they didn't exist in the game. I'm sure there are a few bugs to work out, but overall it's a great recreation.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me wish I had a VR setup. Gorgeous visuals, so many little things to interact with, and amazing puzzles that will require some note-taking in order to fully grasp.I definitely recommend playing either realMyst: Masterpiece Edition or the 2020 remake of Myst before diving into this one, as there are a few story elements that might not entirely make sense without the knowledge from that game. But Riven takes the foundation that Myst made and built upon it in extremely unique ways. It has a better narrative, better puzzles, better environments, and it all seamlessly blends together to create a puzzle-driven narrative that feels more like you're discovering the world and its culture rather than just pulling levers and pressing buttons.Unfortunately, there is no option to substitute the 3D models with the original FMV actors, but at least the models look a lot better in this game than the 2020 Myst remake. Some of the animations have a tendency to desync with props and such (the prop will be floating on its own, following the character's animation a half-second behind or so), and that's a bit of a bummer, but far from a deal breaker with how few NPCs you'll be running into, let alone ones utilizing props.All in all, it's a fantastic and unique experience for fans of puzzle games, or players who love to immerse themselves in detailed worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Here are my initial VR impressions of this game 2hrs in: For comfort (latency) requires high end PC such as RTX 4080 or 4090 with decent CPU. If you have, then I'd highly recommend buying. Graphics and sound are stunning. Did encounter a few bugs where I needed to restart game. Thank goodness for the auto save points. This game uses Unreal Engine 5 graphics and with a Quest 3 the immersion is incredible. You will be transported into this world and its a great experience. I only bought this for the VR and I wasn't disappointed. Oh, its got some basic VR comfort options such as snap turn and teleportation locomotion.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing in VR and have been enjoying it without major issues. Overall it looks fantastic and even if it isn't a true VR title, it still has a good implementation. The first thing I would mention is that if you are playing VR, be aware that you might have a better experience if you change the comfort settings in the menu to your liking. I have had some visual issues with the shadows/lighting when in certain areas like a cave, where the left and right eyes are rendered significantly different enough that it looks bad. I had to turn the "shadows" graphical setting down all the way to prevent this. I hope they can improve this issue because having higher quality lighting improves immersion, but it may just be a limitation with the Unreal engine.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely masterful and well overdue remake of one of the greatest adventure games from the 90's.  The visuals are beautiful, the puzzles, though redone, will still require a lot of thought and attention to detail, and they've managed to make a game that both feels nostalgic and fresh.  I'd even argue this turned out better than the Myst remakes.  I cannot recommend this more highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is impeccable. The puzzles are (mostly) enjoyable. The music is beautiful.The travel cutscenes are lovely and the animations are fantastic. But after the 30th time travelling back and forth on a mine cart, or a jet-rail train, or waiting for spinning orbs to come to a stop, open, close, load and open... it grows tedious, time-consuming and eventually straight-up frustrating.Forgot one small clue on another island? There goes 10 minutes of nothing but travel and backtracking.I appreciate the artists desire to show off all their amazing animation work. But at some point you have to understand that we've seen it, and we'd like to skip it. Same with the credits.I can't in good conscience recommend this game when so much of it is padded with forced travel tedium.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As far as a remake goes, this was probably the best way they could have done it. It's a good blend of new puzzles with rewritten story elements that added really well to the experience and finally allowed us to have a good look at the inside of Tay and outside Gehn's second lab/house.All said and done, the environment that Riven '97 released in was a very different one from today and I think they adapted well. I hope Myst 3 and 4 get the same treatment.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a first time player of Riven, it was strangely also the only game in the Myst series I had not played yet. With this remake, it felt like the right time. I have not played it in VR, only on PC.In relation to the other Myst games, Riven is a treasure trove of good puzzles and a great story. The remake makes the world more easily accessible and feels immersive. There were a couple bugs, most graphical related, but after fixing those the game ran smoothly from beginning to end.If you like the Myst series, this is definitely a recommendation! If you are new to the Myst series, or have not played point-and-click puzzle games before, this is a very good one to start with.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that can appeal to both players who have never played riven and players who have played the original version. The game largely has its original puzzles but with some small changes and twists that makes it exiting for everyone. I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves puzzle games but are okay with being frustrated with hard puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A great remake of an old favourite.    Whilst I miss the old FMV, the new CGI character models are ok, and in line with the recent Myst remake.  The puzzles remain difficult, although its nice to see Cyan have clearly taken feedback on board with respect of some of the fiendishly difficult puzzles of the original game, and have considered this in redesigning and updated for this new release.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I could dive in and play after getting past the 14th-gen Intel shenanigans (solved by installing the latest BIOS version)."Wow!" is a word that quickly comes to mind. Just walking around, I am in awe of how realistic everything looks. Things like "gold bricks" look like gold, and the water looks real; natural elements look photorealistic. Riven is an excellent demonstration for Unreal Engine 5 but in the form of a complete, feature-rich product.Beyond the engine's technical prowess, the gameplay and story are excellent (so far). I am okay with 3D characters replacing the FMV actors (but Cyan kept their voice dialog, which has been great). So far, this is a fantastic experience. My only warning is that if you have a 13th or 14th-gen Intel CPU, update your motherboard's BIOS to resolve issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original in 1998, this remake was 15 hours of intense dopamine rush - completing the multiple endings and hunting down all of the side achievements. It would have been an extra bonus if they could have somehow preserved the original video capture versions of the characters, since the 3D animated versions were a bit... awkward. But this is a very small gripe. This game is a real gem in a sea of crap.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This remake of Riven brings the 1997 classic into a real-time 3D environment. With enhanced visuals and an expanded story, it stays true to the original while offering new experiences. Experience Riven like never before and uncover its secrets.Riven 2024 Ultimate Walkthrough Guide: All Endings, Puzzles, and Cutscenes
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: OK, so a few points (in no particular order): - Wonderful graphics! The environments are gorgeous and everything just looks SO good! - They did change some of the puzzles to make them easier (though I don't think it would be too easy for first time Riven players), though the way they did it was REALLY FREAKIN AWESOME! - Some of the environment is changed around. There was a few times I said "wait, I thought this was over there?". Nothing major, but it's not 1:1. - There are some graphical bugs. Especially when traveling between the islands, sometimes a chunk takes a bit to load in, but nothing game breaking. - That being said, there was one time where I soft-locked when trying to view my satchel. I clicked twice in a row and it went away, but thought it was still there. A reload fixed it and no real progress lost, fortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Returning to one of my favorite worlds in VG history in this stunning remake using Unreal Engine 5.Riven pushes you to open your mind and think creatively about your surroundings. It's not just about figuring out , but also  — like an explorer and engineer.The puzzles are organic in that way. They integrate seamlessly into the universe, which feels like a real, dynamic world with a deep backstory. It doesn't hold your hand or set you on a linear path so remember to use the in-game notebook/screencaps frequently because you have to deduce the story and solutions on your own. It's never tedious however as the resulting escapism is unparalleled, you genuinely feel like you've transported into a new world.27 years after its release, it's safe to say that no puzzle game has matched Riven's depth and quality. This remake is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A really awesome remake of a beautiful classic game. While the 3d character replacements are no match for full motion video... its understandable why they had to do it, and not 'so terrible' it ruined the game. Loved the changes to some puzzles, and the re-imagining of some spaces.I am not disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a die-hard Riven fan, I think I own like 7 copies of the original game, and easily rank it in my top 10 games. I have played all the Myst games to some extent, and a bunch of Myst-likes, but I can't think of anything that comes close to Riven as a whole package. Needless to say, I was anticipating this release.This is a great remake, and a fascinating sidestep from what they did with the Myst one. In Myst 2021, every puzzle, as far as I can recall, was exactly the same as in the original release. The main differences were alterations to the machinery, art, and how you interfaced with certain elements, like the removal of the dentist chair. It was a pretty standard remake, but it definitely felt off, knowing the art direction of the original release.Riven did the complete opposite. Instead, if you looked at the screenshots here and weren't intimately familiar with the original, then you'd think you're looking at a 1:1 remake. This gave a false sense of familiarity as a returning player, and it was endlessly fascinating to see every change they made, while being so incredibly respectful to the original art. It gave me the sense that I returned to this place after a long time, and things had changed. I can't speak to how a first time player will feel, but actually exploring these environments seamlessly, with alterations, felt like playing a new Myst game.I have my gripes, but they're minor. 1. There's a screenshot function that you are encouraged to use in place of taking physical notes, which I usually avoid using because I'm a weirdo who likes busting out graph paper and jotting down a bunch of symbols, but they let you append notes to screenshots and it seemed fine, so I used it throughout the game. In late game though, I noticed that a few of the screenshots of notes I had taken were just slightly blurry or low resolution, and you couldn't even differentiate the symbols because the lines were too thin. So I then had to backtrack, just to take the physical notes that I normally would have, had there not been a screenshot function.2. This isn't exactly the same game as the original. The art direction is spot on, the atmosphere is perfect, the areas are always familiar, but with all the minor changes in between, it feels like a very different experience. It's hard to explain how it feels to love the original, and play this version. Every change feels thoughtful, though. The broad strokes are there. This is Riven, but it's also a companion piece to Riven.3. Character models4. You cannot skip animations like you could when an FMV activated in the original. This makes backtracking significantly slower now, as you're forced to wait for every animation in the game.I don't know which version I prefer. This is a very good remake, but it's a different game. I honestly think most of the changes in the remake are an improvement, especially in relation to the world-building and feeling of presence, but your mileage will vary based on how much that matters to you. Personally, I've never felt more engrossed in the world of Riven. The expanded areas, the sound design, the respect to the lore, and the love and care put into the simplest things like some barnacles on a structure that dips into the sea, make this impossible not to recommend to returning Riven fans. I also recommend it to newcomers who understand that this is effectively a walking simulator with a bunch of obtuse puzzles, and are on board with that.Thank you, Cyan, for delivering on something that could have easily never been fully realized. You allowed me to experience Riven fresh again.

_childDocuments_.review: ( Non-VR Review )tl;dr: If you've played Riven 1997 before, this one is different than what you remember, but it is my opinion that all the changes are enhancements, and you will enjoy your new trip through Riven with some new mysteries and questions to answer. If you haven't played the 1997 one before, then you should know that this is one of the finest worlds ever created, stuffed full of environmental storytelling, puzzles, art, mechanisms, and mechanics. If you're into that sort of thing, try it!---I'm a big, big, big fan of the Myst series. I played Myst pretty young, 6 or 7 or so, initially with my dad helping me click around, but he got frustrated with it and left it to me. It took me a really, really long time, but I figured it all out and beat the game... by trial and error if anything, honestly. My house didn't have Internet back then, so it's not like I could look up answers. I had my notebook and the game and time and that's about it.Not long after, Riven released in 1997 and I begged my parents for a copy and received about a year later. This game took me a really long time, too, but not as long as it should have if I hadn't improved from my time with Myst at all - eventually, I learned how the world of Myst connected and why, and the world-consistent puzzles helped a lot. I could never go back to other adventure games that have disjointed, out-of-place, or nonsensical puzzle elements - the puzzles in these games are much more connected to the world. There is some justification for their existence. Myst was a bit looser with this, but Riven is strict. This sense helped me with Riven (1997) a lot, but the original release was nonetheless quite difficult. My struggle understanding and exploring the world, I feel, set me up to be good at creative problem solving for the rest of my life - I don't think I'd have the things I have now or enjoy the things I now enjoy if not for the lessons and patience I learned from those 5 noisy CD-ROMs in a cardboard box.This 2024 remake of Riven made me nervous when I was going into it, before I had seen it. I knew that it was partially the fruits of the labor of the Starry Expanse project, which began remaking (and re-remaking, and re-re-remaking, as I recall) Riven in full 3D quite some time ago and formed the basis for this project which the original Riven (1997) developers Cyan then continued and completed. I was worried that I would find that the world didn't land the same way as it did before, or that the world would have been changed, or that somehow the nature of full 3D exploration would somehow diminish the value I used to receive from every still frame of image from the original. Not so.At first, I was just thoroughly pleased to walk around and see the game from new perspectives. It's quite pretty. I wasn't disappointed. Then, I realized a bit too late that it seemed like I was somewhere that I ought not to have been so early in the game, and I realized something has been changed... several things, in fact. When I discovered the nature of one of the larger changes concerning the multitude of domes scattered around the islands, I was uncertain how to really feel until I realized that I felt the same brand of wonder that I remember feeling from the 1997 release, way back when. And just like that, I was sold.Every change that's been made, I feel, has strictly been an enhancement. There's not a moment where I thought "Darn, I miss how it used to be." There were times I was surprised something wasn't where it was supposed to be, or surprised something didn't exist at all - but after a few moments of thought, I almost universally returned to "You know... that might be for the better." Some weird lore loose ends from the original now have justification. Some weird idiosyncratic elements of the original are now either replaced or contextualized enough that they blend in. I think it's all good. That's just personal opinion, though.I'm exceptionally pleased by this remake.A tiny spark of hope is now lit within me for a full 3D remake of this caliber of Myst III: Exile, someday. Am I being greedy?Performance/Stability: Good. Played on Linux via Proton, zero issues. My rig is quite capable and was able to play on high settings with no trouble, hitches, stutters, or slowdowns.Music and Audio: Excellent. Played with headphones. Robyn Miller's music is beautiful, haunting, and evocative. The sounds of the mechanisms and machines are all so satisfying.Visuals: Great! I was worried they would be inferior to the pre-rendered stills of the original, but technology has advanced so far...Story: Fantastic. I've played every Myst game and read every Myst book. I'm not objective.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the original game of Cyan. I could see that most of the other fans were quite excited by this remake and were saying very good things about it even before the release. Were they just hyped? I was quite worried and a little reluctant at the idea of Riven, a real gem, being remade in a 3d engine. As an example, I'm also a fan of Final Fantasy 7-9 on the PS1, and when I see the result of Final Fantasy VII Remake, even though it has many qualities, I started to think that it might not be such a good idea to remake those good old prerendered games from the 1990s. So I jumped into Riven Remake with apprehension. I have motion sickness, so I cannot play a lot without feeling nauseous, but it's ok in Riven. My computer is old (2013) so in addition I cannot set the graphic settings at a elevated level. In fact, I couldn't even launch the game initially, black screen, because my GPU wasn't happy with a DX12 feature. In the end I could start playing it with the -dx11 option and it plays nice. First steps in Riven... As I feared, I'm not very fond of the 3d characters, but I anticipated it, so that's fine. And they're not so bad, could have been worst. I prefer Atrus in the original intro, but he's quite convincing in 3d too. Then I'm teleported to Riven in the jail at the beginning, and after the short scene, I can make my first steps. Wow the graphics are somptuous! Even with low quality settings, it's amazing. The feeling of freedom in exploring the islands is just beathetaking when you knew the first game. There are small animations here and there, trees, sea waves, insects... The world is familiar yet different, I'm visiting it for real! I quickly get used to the changes and take my old habits, and I know what to do and where to go. Ah, I quickly notice that various things have changed. At first I'm not very happy with these changes. The armchair room is not where it used to be and so I can't climb in the maglev as quickly as I wanted to. Mmmh, a little disappointed. But then I start to play with the rotating room and I find what I know, more or less. Except that the full 3d makes it much easier to understand what we are doing, and this is a very good point! So I rotate the rooms, open several doors, go here and there and finall fnd the armchair that I was looking for, at last. Not bad. I open the door to the maglev and go back on my steps, taking notes and screen captures on my way. I take the maglev, there is still the "wow" effect inside. I visit the 2nd island, enjoy the sea creatures. I go look for one of the Riven balls that, I know, is located near them on a rock. But it's not there anymore, things have changed. That makes me a little grumpy because I liked to search for those wooden balls in the past, enjoying the sound effect associated with each of them. Maybe they're still somewhere else, but instead I have found a strange magnifying glass with invisible paiting. Reminds a bit of The Room. I don't like a lot the idea of having to wear that glass to not miss hidden clues, but well, why not. I continue, visit the forest, take more screen captures and notes on my paper. Then go back on my steps and climb in the small wagon. I reach the 3rd island and the ride was cool like before. I find my marks quickly on this island, it hasn't changed a very lot at the beginning. Quickly I reach Ghen's lab and there are many changes inside that I like and find logical. More and more, all of the changes make sense to me, and I start to really like it. I'm curious about the stone orbs.I continue, open the doors, take captures, etc. Finally I arrive on the 4th island and visit it. I love the environment of this island, it's so unique, almost like a fantasy world with all those rocks. I play with the device and quickly find the code to the hidden level with the lift. I reach the cave where we can see the Wharck, a very rivenesque sea creature, that I wouldn't like to meet for real. The place is beautiful with that gigantic blue circle. I take some more notes and leave, back to a previous island, and now I can use the submarine, which lead me to having fully access to the small village. I'm visiting, I'm now fully immersed in the game and I love it, I can't stop despite the motion sickness. I'm at 3 hours of games and I have made a lot of progress, but at the same time there is still so much to do! I left plenty of devices and clues on my way that I will have to check again, and understand how they work. Riven Remake worried me, now I am reassured and I can say that it is a masterpiece. I'm glad I jumped into the adventure despite my firt idea of a remake, despite having an old pc, and despite loving the old version. I'm not one of those fans who thought it would be great even before I started playing it. I had to really dive into it to enjoy this creation. And I can tell that it's incredible. Of course it might still be too difficult for many young players, particularly novices who never played an adventure game, or for less patient players. The game is sometimes slow and takes it time. Some will not like it, personally I find it relaxing. There are no enemies, you can't die, there's no TPS view, no battles. It's pure exploration, joy for the eyes and the ears, joy also when you solve a challenging thing and get that "ahah!" moment, and you can continue your exploration when you were stuck. It's a very very beautiful world, very similar to the original version but better with the UE engine, and yet different enough from the old game to justify buying it again. Am I in love with this remake? Maybe not totally yet, I still haven't finished it and I know that I still have a long way. But from what I saw it's a new masterpiece and I hope that the flame of Riven will continue to burn for many many years in the hearts of many people! At least, Cyan did something really cool here, that must be awesome to play it in VR. I recommend this game, definitely!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally played this for the first time. Not only is the remaster beautiful but its design holds up to this day in a way that feels like nothing like it has since been created. I've played a lot of puzzle games, especially ones which advertise themselves as narratively-driven or thematically deep in some sense, and there really is no compare to the time the developers must have spent unifying every aspect of these worlds' history, language, technology, culture, and the looming catastrophe they face into something "game-ifiable" (game-ificated?).Where the smallest bits necessary of a hero's journey combined with neverending curiosity are the only extrinsic rewards to be found, this game has some of if not the most natural, realistic sense of exploration I've ever experienced. Combine that with very well explored, unique science-fiction elements, each puzzle becomes something with perfect sense of reason to exist and be solved. Each clue collected like a book well-read and the implementation bringing you closer to the characters who's footsteps you follow. I have never felt like such a scientist, archaeologist, historian, linguist, and engineer. Because of this, Riven is immersive in a way I'm not sure I've ever experienced before, and at some points, transcends into heights which makes it feel much like the Lord of the Rings did for world development in literature. MYST was my favorite game for almost all my life. For similar reasons actually - as a kid, MYST exposed me for the first time to the idea that you could be wrong about what a game is telling you to do, or perhaps that it can be abstract at all. That there can be multiple endings and the game doesn't exactly tell you which one is good or bad, allowing you to comprehend that yourself (not to say it's ambiguous). In that way, MYST married story and parts of its gameplay, the choices, together perfectly to me. Now I see that RIVEN went and put that into every element of itself, until what was left feels like much more than a game. An experience that will stay with me all my life, a story that could only be told with an interactive medium.I had never played RIVEN as I struggled with it as a kid - it was difficult to tell signal from noise in regards to puzzles but ultimately I'm particularly glad to visit it all this time later. Having the context of all the games I've played since it's release, makes me realize what's so special about this game that is missing from many modern puzzle games. It seems silly that few games are like it when it is approaching 30 years old. I'm still reeling from the experience but it's probably the best thing I've ever played.If you haven't played it, do so. If you have, play Outer Wilds. ::)

_childDocuments_.review: The game is buggy in some ways—it crashes all the time. The UI is clunky in a lot of ways: going out of bounds (i.e. moving around naturally in VR) leaves you not knowing where to stand for getting back in-bounds, and holding open a book for an extended period of time *really* starts to hurt your wrist, and going into the menu sometimes forces you to use your non-dominant hand until you go back into the game and physically handle an interactable object with your dominant hand. I've had similar problems with Cyan's other VR titles—they really need a UI/UX guy who knows what they're doing.All that said, it's still an amazing experience, and I'd still recommend it for people who have enough technical savvy and cool enough heads to work through the very obvious, actually very bad problems. If I were a professional reviewer, I'd obligate myself with a negative review, but the truth is I personally am really enjoying the game (after an initial period of being very angry with it).

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the original Riven, so I can't compare this game with the old one, but my exposure to a similar game was the remake of Myst, which I enjoyed and which led me to buy Riven.I have mixed feelings about the game. Overall, I like how things are tied together and enjoyed the overall story and world. I cannot highlight specifics without spoiling the game. Sadly, there were a couple of things that I disliked and that made my experience worse.For my liking, there is too much traveling, considering how things are spread out. It's fine the first time, maybe the second time. But when you're stuck and looking for solutions, it becomes tedious. Taking almost 10 minutes to return to a specific place is just too much. That feels like a bad design to me.I also checked how puzzles were done in the original Riven (1997) by watching some playthroughs, and I feel the Jungle Island puzzles were done better due to more obvious visual clues. The same goes for a few other places.One thing that initially surprised me was the option to take screenshots and save them in a notebook. Sadly, the execution is very poor, and it's better to take notes outside of the game. The biggest problem is the resolution: the in-game screenshots are not taken at the same resolution you see while playing. Additionally, the navigation is frustrating. When you view a screenshot and then return to your list, it throws you back to the beginning instead of where you left off.Having said that, I would still recommend the game, but there are better puzzle games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I played realMYST: Masterpiece Edition in 2015, and that was my introduction to the series. (Thank you, brutalmoose!)Not long after that, I played and loved the rest of the series after they came to steam (back in 2018-ish) using  of hints along the way - a habit from trying to solve the first Myst.Then, barely a year ago I marathoned through the entire pentalogy using no hints, just pen and paper as well as a familiarity with what I'm  to find and  to find it. And that was great! Definitively enjoyed them all more the second time around.So tl;dr, I consider myself a pretty big Myst fan!And as all Myst fans knew of course, there was a fan-effort to build a realtime 3D version of 'The Sequel to Myst'. Eventually, that fan-effort transformed into an official remake announcement, and I've been even more hyped for realRiven ever since 2022. With how good Myst (2021) turned out, I knew that Cyan could tweak and improve upon the foundations of the 1997 masterpiece, with modern graphical fidelity, lore updates and so on. But best of all; let Riven be played and solved in that oh-so liberating real-time 3D and free mouse look!So after playing it, I think this remake turned out amazing! I had a fantastic time playing through it all-- pen and paper in hand, as well as its new built-in screenshot/journal function --where every update and change was a welcome surprise and a remix of the original. Though it's not exactly "improving upon perfection", I'm glad Riven (2024) forged its own identity which now usurps the old Riven journey for me with the expanded areas added. Those remixed elements in this new version therefore cause this (more well-balanced difficulty-wise) replacement to the original to not be a replacement for it - which I'd say every remake and re-release of Myst has attempted to be.But yeah, this game hits it out of the park in the ways that matter; audio, graphics, , impact, immersion, discovery, and a Tolkien-level of worldbuidling.Even with the solutions to the original fresh in my mind, I managed to get lost at least once when looking for an important (but skippable) marker, and I'm split on whether I should be thrilled at the game letting me got lost before arriving at the solution myself, or disgruntled at how that particular part, , was intended to be solved.I can only hope that realEXILE is next - my favorite of the entire series.

_childDocuments_.review: A Timeless MasterpieceFew games can claim the timeless brilliance of Riven, and even in 2024, it stands as one of the most breathtaking achievements in interactive storytelling and world-building. As the sequel to the legendary Myst, Riven took everything the original did well and elevated it to an entirely new level, creating a gaming experience that remains unparalleled decades later.Visuals That Transcend TimeEven by today's standards, Riven's pre-rendered environments are nothing short of stunning. The artistry and detail poured into every inch of this world make it feel alive, mysterious, and eerily real. The intricate design of the islands, the beautifully woven cultural elements, and the subtle animations breathe life into Gehn's fractured domain. Its ability to immerse players in an alien yet familiar world feels as fresh today as it did in 1997.A Puzzle Design MasterclassWhat makes Riven truly timeless is its brilliant puzzle design. The challenges are deeply integrated into the narrative and the environment, requiring players to truly understand the world rather than brute-forcing solutions. Every puzzle feels meaningful, serving as a piece of the grand narrative puzzle that slowly unravels as you explore. It’s the kind of game where solving a challenge delivers not just satisfaction but also a deeper appreciation for the care and thought that went into the design.Narrative Depth and ImmersionIn 2024, storytelling in games has evolved immensely, but Riven's narrative structure remains a benchmark for excellence. The game tells its story primarily through exploration, environmental clues, and cryptic details, allowing players to piece together the lore at their own pace. It’s an experience that rewards curiosity and critical thinking, making every revelation feel personal and earned.Why It Still MattersIn an age dominated by fast-paced games and instant gratification, Riven stands as a reminder of the power of patience, observation, and slow-burning mystery. Its influence can still be seen in modern narrative-driven titles, and its atmosphere, music, and puzzles continue to inspire awe in new generations of players.ConclusionWhether you’re revisiting Riven for nostalgia or experiencing it for the first time, the game remains a shining example of what the medium can achieve. In 2024, Riven is not just a classic—it’s an essential gaming experience that feels as magical and rewarding as it did when it first captured imaginations.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm extremely glad Cyan was able to recreate this! While somethings are different like movement, some puzzle changes, etc, I was able to recreate some awesome childhood memories of watching my dad struggle with the puzzles! A very welcome change was not requiring to switch one of the, what seemed like 8, disks every time you went to a new age/island haha! While I'm not a fan of the CGI/cartoony characters, I kinda understand it.  Awesome game, especially for the nostalgia. I really hope they reskin Myst 3, 4, and 5!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is what my 12 year old brain thought Riven looked like when it released all those years ago. Camera controls are fantastic. Visuals and sound design are super immersive, as I hoped it would be!Running the game on a fairly powerful computer, I experienced no bugs other than a few difficulties using an XBOX controller for certain puzzles, in which case I just switched to a mouse for finer control. Framerate never dropped to where I noticed it, and while there were a few texture pop ins on the tram rides, they were so quick that I barely noticed.Absolutely loved the reimagining of certain crucial puzzles, and was very happy that someone who has replayed the original many times could still struggle a bit, be surprised, and have that same awesome feeling when a puzzle was solved.To the devs: Thank you for listing the Starry Expanse team in the credits, as well as the original team. And thanks for making this an amazing experience I'll definitely share with others.PS: Did you really have to

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is awesome! It doesn´t matter if you played the original one from old times or not - this is a jewel. But if you played the original one back in the 90´s you get "that feeling", and this time luckily without changing 5 CD-ROMs throughout the entire game. ;) The graphics are so realistic that one wishes to be there, at the beach and the sea, in these caves... _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is mysterious, treacherous, yet beautiful. A world and civilization on the brink of collapse, torn apart by family conflict and a madman intent on making himself into a god.Picks up right where the first game in the series, Myst, left off, but if you'd like to start here, then the brief journal Atrus gives you at the beginning will explain everything you need to know. There is a prequel novel, Myst: The Book of Atrus, that I greatly enjoyed as a Myst fan but is optional for playing Riven, and arguably might be more enjoyable after playing both games.This is a remake of the 1997 game by the same designers, expanding on it in thoughtful ways but maintaining the strange yet familiar atmosphere that made the original so unforgettable. It is difficult but satisfying to puzzle your way through the islands of Riven, where an understanding of the world, factions, and characters is your greatest tool in making progress.A masterpiece, and the best game I've played all year.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A missed opportunity for greatness. It nails the visual and auditory feel or the original. Phenomenal graphics. Being able to freely explore the world, and view spacial relations realistically is amazing. The subtle expansions to the areas you can explore are a nice touch.A few of the changes  are welcome. Most, unfortunately, are not. They follow a general pattern: They remove one aspect of what made Riven great and unique, which is the holistic design of the world and the main two puzzles. (The other aspect: The beautiful world and graphics, remains intact!) The new gameplay is comparatively linear and piecemeal, instead of integrated. This is in some cases acute , and in some cases subtle: The navigation , the replacement for the  etc.I feel like the redesigned puzzles are inferior to the original; my suspicion: it's to make game time more predictable, and to prevent players from getting stuck.An advantage of a gameplay redesign is fresh exploration for those who already know the original. For this selfish reason, I had a better time with it than I might have had with the original, since it introduced new elements. Because of the specifics of the redesign, I would recommend the original to someone who hasn't played Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's that good old Riven but now you can move everywhere you want and watch all your environment 360 degrees.  The islands have been partly redesigned and the puzzle are at least a bit different or completely new though they roughly serve the same purpose.  You should find enough new features for you to revisit that great old game and still have fun.  Of course, if you once played the old game, it will give a great edge to play this renewed version. And for those who never played that game you will have a real challenge to finish this one without any help of any kind like I did in 1998.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I loved it in 97 and I love it today. The VR is pretty crashy on my Valve Index, but I suspect that will be patched out soon.Some of the new puzzles were great. One of them was frustrating to the point that I looked up cheats and STILL don't understand it.The game is stunningly gorgeous. We thought it looked good in 1997, but this absolutely takes the cake.Everything that is animated, however, looks stilted and bad. The character animations look like chuck-e-cheese animatronics. The big falling events, like the bridge, look like they're divorced from the gravity of the world they're in. The bugs and birds look better by comparison, but the animation of when they're moving is very immersion-breaking.In spite of that, Riven is a monumental work of art and you should play it right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished the game yet, but this is the right way to do a remake. True to the feel of the original. Runs just fine on my potato. Looks great at 1440p running on lowest graphics settings (textures set to High, Super Sampling set to Quality)  my 4k 65" TV.One complaint/bug is the very first viewfinder that points at a spinning dome wasn't rendering any animation right away. Walked to another location related to the "puzzle" and when I came back, it worked fine. Not sure if it was my graphics settings or an actual bug in the game. If Cyan plans on remaking Myst 3: Exlie, I'm buying it on release date. 11 out of 10Edit : Finished the game. Some of the puzzles were frustrating, but it brings back memories of how frustrated the puzzles were in the original Riven. Still happy to play this game on release date and glad to support Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's Riven, it's beautiful, it's immersive. Makes me want to get a VR set to experience it. One minor letdown is the character models vs. the original full motion video. I get why they did it since you have full movement, but it was jarring since I vividly remember the original. Still, I can overlook that because the rest of it is so amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely faithful remake of the original. Having played Riven since the mid 90's, I know many of these places from memory. Even though ive been to them before, the visuals leave me with a sense of awe and wonder seeing them in HD. The puzzles have been redone to be a little less tedious, but still leave plenty of challenge for you to consider bringing out the notebook to write stuff down. My only complaint is some of the animations can be a little jank and a few minor bugs, but these are not a huge hindrance and are being worked on.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A well-crafted reimagining of the original Riven, this remake maintains the layout of the world but offers completely new puzzle solutions, making it feel fresh even to seasoned players. Unlike the original, where you might solve a series of intricate steps only to realize your progress much later, the remake is more rewarding in how it clearly shows when you've made a breakthrough—keeping you engaged and aware of each accomplishment along the way.However, one significant difference is in character presentation: Gehn, one of the most compelling figures in the original, loses some of his impact due to the remake’s animated character models. The uncanny valley effect here can be quite distracting, especially when compared to the full-motion video in the 1997 version, which gave the characters a uniquely realistic presence.This remake offers a new take on a beloved classic and may appeal to newcomers with its accessibility, though fans of the original may find the changes a mixed experience. So, if you really want the original feel with the mystery and obscure puzzle design you must buy the 1997 original. I honestly recommend buying both versions as they are truly different games.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful update to a point-and-click legend. The puzzles have been modified and adjusted to both make more sense for world building, and to fit into a modern 3D game format (if you know, you know). Since it's not just a 1:1 recreation, there's a lot of new stuff to explore, so if you're a fan of the series it's a guaranteed good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven... I can't believe it. Myst, sure, remake that it's the most famous, but this one. Wow. I played Myst as a kid with my dad. It was an awesome adventure, even if I didn't understand it all. But Riven was what really shaped my kid mind, the first time I was really able to understand a complex story. Wow and what a story. 5 disks for 5 islands - explore thoroughly, because switching them is a pain! I never forgot it, never gave up hope that I would be able to really explore it, like I could Myst.It was an awesome game, and this is a great remake. Hear and seeing Atrus, Gehn, Catherine, even that guard at the beginning again after all these years... If you ever wanted to really explore the awesome environment and story that Cyan made in this game, this is how you do it! The only thing I miss is seeing the real people.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game I've been waiting for ever since real Myst came out. (~23 years ago)  The changes to the game, one in particular, really came unexpectedly and had me in a state of giddy-shock.  The effects and soundtrack are great as always.  This game always had that one unique visual look that I loved.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful recreation of the classic game, with many new very welcome additions and changes that further expand upon the games design, art and feel. The changes from the original seem to all be things that "just make sense," and create a more fleshed out and intentional atmosphere, which is hard to do considering the art and design of the original being as phenomenal and immersive as it is. The visual style and graphics are incredible, the colors and ambiance is pure fantasy. The sound design and music is very similar to the original with wonderful additions and re-imaginings. It feels like the game I remember through the ever present "nostalgia-glasses" that are hard to take off, plus the awe of discovering many new things and places to explore. I applaud the studio Cyan for this release, reigniting the magic I felt playing Riven all those years ago, truly re-imagining the experience for today's hardware and graphics.Overall, 9/10.An absolute must play for Riven fans and newcomers alike. Please play this game, there is so much to take in, you won't regret any of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy remake of a wonderful game.For fans of the Myst series, there is nothing better than finally being able to explore more of the enigmatic worlds that made the series so successful. This is the game we imagined back in the day when it came on 5 cds.If you're unfamiliar with the series, you do not need to play Myst first, though doing so will enhance your experience. The puzzles are challenging, though slightly easier than the original. Because the game is now 3d, they can't reuse the old FMVs from the original, and they've been replaced with passable 3d models. The voice acting is still intact.Fans of Myst and Riven will be happy with this. First time players may experience a little bit of confusion, but that's almost the signature of narrative puzzle games. Especially Myst games...it's the experience falling into a starry expanse...

_childDocuments_.review: Good graphics, VR worked well. This is my first time playing Riven and from my understanding they made some of the puzzles a bit easier. However they still kept me very busy!The only real issue I ran into was that you can't really take notes without taking off the VR headset, which is immersion-breaking. Yes, you can take screenshots, but the screenshots are a bit dim in the menus. It took putting multiple screenshots together and being able to write on something to figure out the number systems. Yes, they're simple enough once you have figured out they are base 5 and base 3, and after that point, I didn't have to take off the headset again,. _childDocuments_.review: I played Myst and Riven back when they were originally released.  I finished Myst but never finished Riven, though I enjoyed it and always intended to.  Well a year or so ago I played (and completed) Myst VR on my Vive Pro 2 and really enjoyed it.  Walking through those worlds I could only experience as a slideshow back in the day (or in flatscreen2D in RealMyst), just added immensely to the experience.  That is why Riven has surprised me so much.  I expected my Myst VR experience to be repeated here but, I don't know if it is more because I'm now on a Pimax Crystal or because the worlds are just so much more immersive and interesting, but at about 10 hours in, I'm finding Riven to be just stunning. I have a huge VR library, but unlike any other game, I've never found myself repeatedly voicing out loud, "this is SO cool" so many times.  This, along with the fact that the puzzles make more sense to me and seem more tied to the world elements rather than the more abstract ones common in Myst (not that there aren't abstract puzzles).  Anyway, I just wanted to gush a little since I think Riven is just this incredibly good and so happy Cyan decided to port it.  I should note that I also played through most of Obduction (which I found to be only ok), and returned Firmament as I just couldn't get into it.  But Riven is just so much more.  Magnum opus stuff.  Gotta love it.With that said, there are a few relatively minor technical nits that's I'd love for Cyan to address someday. One is that even on my 13900K/RTX4090 performance could definitely be better (I find myself wishing the detail could be cranked to the levels of, say, Kayak VR and still be playable rock-solid at 90fps); and there are some issues with shadows that are a bit annoying (Firmament had this issue too).  Also, for motion sickness reasons which I'm very sensitive to, I tend to prefer teleport.  In Myst VR I played the entire game using teleport and found it to work just fine, but in Riven I can't.  They do include it as an option, but I'm not sure if its just a poor implementation of it or because of the nature of the more complex environments, but I just find teleport to not work effectively in this game.  So I have to resort to smooth motion and just take more frequent breaks lest nausea set in. So if you are also sensitive to smooth motion, that might be one word of warning.  Otherwise, I don't regard any of these as show-stoppers at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a surprise to see but I am up in bounds happy to see this game finally get a remake. It was far over due since Myst got ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3. _childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the Myst series, and have many fond memories of them.  I have bought the various remastered and improved versions of Myst over the years, and while I enjoyed playing them, I have always considered Riven to be the highlight of the series, and always wondered if they would ever remaster it.  In some ways I didn't care too much, because the original game was great to play and its graphics aged surprisingly well.  But when I saw that this was coming out, I got it as soon as I could, and I was not disappointed.  The improved graphics and ability to freely walk around is certainly nice, but it was the little touches that I appreciated.  For one, they improved the depth of the island, by which I mean they added various things to show how Gehn and the Rivenese lived there.  But they also worked to address potential plot holes from the original game, so that there was a more logical backstory and how some of the puzzles were set-up made more sense.  I won't say more as that might give away some plot points, but if you played the original and remember it well, you will enjoy this game. _childDocuments_.review: As an adult I cried three times in my life. Once when I got married, once when my kids were born, and once when I stood on the cliff of Temple Island on Riven in VR. This game is an absolute masterpiece. The amount of love that was poured into it's creation in 1997 and again in 2024 is unmeasurable. The Myst franchise is much MUCH MUCH more than 6 video games. It is an experience. The beauty and depth of the series is unparalleled. The attention to detail is remarkable. The lore........... oh gosh the lore, is a masterful rabbit hole you will willingly hurl yourself into. Every game in the franchise brings its own depth to the story. But Riven....... Riven is the heart and soul of Myst. It's characters are timeless, it's vision is supurb, it's story is rock solid. The sound and visuals are carefully in harmony with each other. Riven was the first video game to rival a Holywood Blockbuster. (as far as I know) it was the first video game to have a tv commercial. Myst was the best selling PC CD-ROM game of the 20th century.1 game, 4 sequels, 1 spin-off, 3 novels, a comic book series, a GAP ad, a real linking book. No other game franchise has ever risen to the heights of Myst. Cyan does NOT make games, they engineer masterpieces, they create worlds.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I'm impressed! I was expecting a basic remake exactly the same as the original, but Cyan really went out of their way to change things up and add new content. Not to mention the world looks STUNNING and so immersive.• New or revamped puzzles means some of the original ones have changed or parts are missing, this might disappoint a small subset of original fans and cause them confusion while playing but I think it's an improvement.• The video actors have been replaced by 3D characters. Although it was done better than the cartoony style in the recent Myst remake, it might still be a negative for some people since it's not as hyper-realistic.• New or revamped puzzles to keep the original fans busy, I was very excited by the changes.• Beautiful graphics,  a huge upgrade from the original 1997 Riven.• New elements in the environment that help backup the lore more.• As always, fantastic music and sound design, Cyan is known for this.• The game feels immersive, it's easy to forget how long you've been playing.• A lot of depth to the lore, much can be discerned within game but some of it might need to be discovered in the other games in the series and the trilogy of books.All-in-all, whether you're an old fan or new to Cyan games, I highly recommend this game. You can't miss this one if you enjoy puzzle, narrative, or detective games. Hope you enjoy your adventure as much as I did!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzle games, this one may be for you. I thought I would like a good puzzle game, but discovered that it is not for me. Nevertheless, I think I can recommend this game for puzzle lovers.Puzzles are well thought out in general. There are many things to discover, and many tiny details have a meaning somewhere else in the game. Sometimes you need to find that one piece at one end of the Riven world to accomplish something at the other end of the world.  Most puzzles are still solvable without all the details. Graphics are quite good, that helps a lot for the immersion. _childDocuments_.review: If Myst was the influential yet forgotten game, marrying cutting edge visuals with clever puzzles, then Riven was the hidden masterpiece showcasing the Platonic ideal of environmental storytelling (despite selling millions of copies). Now, in 2024, Riven has returned for a modern audience to show the world that it is still an unparalleled achievement.In the remake, you now walk (instead of click) through the broken islands of Riven, making your way through the dense environments while figuring out how everything on the island works and eventually how to defeat the megalomaniacal Gehn. If in 1997, the pre-rendered visuals were absolutely beautiful and (sur)realistic, here in the real-time remake they are equally so. You can look everywhere in this world and be rewarded by beautiful vistas, of oceans crashing down the shorelines, buildings and structures hanging on rocks and trees, and steampunk gizmos shining and steaming away. Looking everywhere is in fact key, as hidden pathways and secrets dot the landscape, the finding of which are necessary to progress. In contrast to this beautiful world however, the world is not peaceful and cozy. For a developer who has espoused non-violent gameplay, the atmosphere of Riven is cutting and hostile. The Rivenese, the indigenous population of the game world, are hiding from you. Gehn’s colonialist influence is felt everywhere, from him fashioning himself as a godlike being, to his D’ni culture and architecture imposed everywhere on the island, down to the D’ni numbering system barging on the Rivenese numbering system. Even in 2024, the marriage of gameplay and storytelling in Riven is so effortless it still feels like the entire gaming industry isn’t just catching up, it has actively put up its ears in dismissal. You aren’t merely exploring the island and solving puzzles. You are actively engaging and learning about the cultures of the colonizer and the colonized on the island. You are solving genuine secrets the two cultures are keeping from each other. The remake puts this in sharper focus thanks to retooled puzzles, which smooth out the more oblique tendencies of the original game. The old (and quite frankly inaccessible) Moiety animal sound puzzle has been replaced with a new visual Lens of Truth-esque puzzle. The animals are now signified with the Rivenese numbers rather than the D’ni numbers, showing a stronger cultural resistance from the Moiety. Walking through Riven 2024 shows how far we’ve come, but also how embarrassingly little we have progressed. In 1997, Cyan showed how you can use cutting edge graphics to tell novel and challenging stories, unlike anywhere else in any other medium. Circa 2024, most trrrriple-Ayyy video game companies have merely used cutting edge graphics to tell safe, Hollywood-cosplaying with gameplay that at best has to actively circumvent the cutting edge graphics with yellow paint in order to be readable and playable and at worst feels significantly lessened in comparison. Considering that Cyan itself isn’t even the economic juggernaut is once was, but now a relatively small indie developer which still managed to pull this off with Unreal Engine 4, Riven dares everyone to take a leap of faith in the starry expanse.
