Look, you can't even see in the game because the extremely heavy anti aliasing they force on you and cannot be turned off makes everything more than 5 feet away a blurry mess even on a machine with an rtx 4080.That's unacceptable for me and on top of that it performs like crap and you can't actually grab anything with your hands without being in very specific and nonsensical spot. Doing something as simple as reading a book in game is a nightmare.The game itself seems really interesting but this is unplayable.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven from 1997 is one of my favorite games of all time, and it is extremely exciting to finally be able to play it again with modern fully 3d graphics, and in VR!I feel like this remake strikes the perfect balance that a modern remake should strive for: Keep the spirit of the original intact while changing enough to make it feel justified, rather than simply uncritically retreading old ground. Even if you played the original, you will get stuck again and have to re-evaluate what you know. This really is the closest thing you can get to the feeling of playing the game for the first time. However, it's not so different that it is unrecognizable as the same game. Again, I think they threaded this needle extremely well.The things that make this game great are the same that made the original great. Beautiful, scenic and artistically crafted graphics accompany a compelling backstory and narrative. You won't find a game that does environmental storytelling better: Literally everything has a justified purpose of some kind. This blends into the puzzles. At it's best, Riven's puzzles don't feel like puzzles, they feel more like a test of how well you understand this world and its culture. As with anything that changes a beloved classic, the original fans (like myself) will always have some nitpicks. However, for me personally, for every change that might not be to my taste, there is another change that I really like that actually fixes a pertinent issue from the original. And at the end of the day, I am just extremely grateful that this game finally has a lovingly crafted remake from the original developers. (After the 5th Myst remake, it was about time! :P )
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Riven something like 25 years ago. This put me in the odd position of mostly remembering the puzzles and world layout, but not specifics. Plus, things changed with the remake.I don't remember the original well enough to give any detailed feedback on the remake. Some things are obviously new, others clearly streamlined. The most infamous puzzle of the original is definitely easier (or maybe I was just a dumb kid - I couldn't even understand it after reading the solution in a guide). One of the changes (a new number system) seems to make more sense from a worldbuilding perspective, but I can't remember if it was explained away in the original or not. On the whole, if you have fond memories of the original Riven, you will like this. If you tried Riven decades after it was released and couldn't stand the technical limitations, you should give this remake a try. For the most part, this is "the original game but prettier, with free movement". Some things are different, but at worst they're merely "fine" and there is absolutely nothing detrimental added.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake. I was concerned my nostalgia for my original playthrough in the 90s was rose-tinted, but no, this is the real deal. Buy if you enjoy adventure puzzles held up by lore and logic rather than the all-too-common strange combinations of meaningless objects.All that said, I still highly recommend the original as well. This game is a significant technical redesign, making both '97 and '24 versions worth trying for their own reasons. Lots of little callbacks to the original elements are a nice touch, but this is *not* the same game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Riven growing up, and returning to the islands felt magical. I especially loved the changes and added content that made it feel new and exciting—they simplified a few things, resolved some weird inconsistencies, and expanded on the lore. Loved it! An absolute must-buy for any fan of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Original "review" below.Im so incredibly torn on this remake.For one, what it caused emotionally is absolut worth every penny I paid.Yet some aspects are so disheartning Im at a loss.Just purely the Game itself:Looks amazing if you can run it on high settings.That hardware needs to be damn beefy/new.The 3D modells of the characters are an absolut downgrade. I would have prefered pixalated video files of the old 1997 versions.Performance:I realized way to late into the game that my system didnt reach the minimum requierments just yet.Which causes an extreme buzzkill for me initially due to bad performance and absolut emersion breaking stuff happening.I still finished the Game on the lowest settings but man this REALLY kills the 3D Character Models...If I could I would give it a neutral review, 3.5/5.It scratched an itch but it also let me hanging slightly unsatisfied.Im still gonna change my review to positive as t feels slightly more right that way.Its been a journey for sure----------------------------Initial Review/Reactions:Make sure to check the Systems minimum Requierment! They mean it!Performance is absolut terrible for me with slightly below minimum System specs.Stutters, insane loading times, sound completely out of sync.Ghen had no head first time seeing him in the classroom. Sadly it killed my nostalgia by hour 2.Its great when its running I guess.It never even occured to me that I would need to check my System for this game of all games.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven lives up to the hype! I'm blown away by how good it is.The three pillars of Cyan's games, the environment, puzzles, and narrative, have all been improved while staying true to the essence of the original. The visuals are stunning and filled with detail. I like the zoom feature that lets you see details up close or observe far away objects more clearly. Logical inconsistencies from the original have also been corrected. Additionally, the remake gives us new lore to dive into, which is the first in a long time in the Myst/D'ni universe. The original directors all returned in some capacity for the remake, and it shows. The whole team clearly has a lot of talent and passion for Riven. Thank you for creating this masterpiece for us!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this and I think I can still recommend it because it's a gorgeous setting and the puzzles seem well done and not too overwrought, but beware - playing this (standard version, not VR) gave me pretty bad motion sickness. So bad that I unfortunately had to refund the game altogether. I've had the same thing happen in other first person games with slower motions like this one, such as Power Washing Simulator and House Flipper. So just a heads up, if you're like me: this game might make you motion sick. Decreasing FOV and fiddling with the control settings might mitigate this for some people, but it didn't for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Like many on here who have played the original Riven. This is exceptionally well done. There are a some new twists that are refreshing. The use of the Unreal engine is awesome. Even if you have not played the original I highly recommend this game. Visually stunning, game play is smooth, puzzles are just right. Hoping there is more to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A stunning remake, the original stands as one of the most engaging worlds I have ever visited and this version of it is even more beautiful, dynamic and vibrant. If you have any interest in slow intricate puzzles this is one of the best of all times, and this version is by far the most accessible.While some puzzles are easy to miss, all are signposted in some way and once you understand that even the more convoluted ones start to open up. Everything was placed deliberately and taking notes is vital, you never what information will be needed later to solve a puzzle but this leads to my one gripe: Flicking to and from your journal is a little clunky particularly in VR. This is a major missed opportunity and I found myself using a physical pen and paper more than the in-game systems.There are some legitimate concerns I have seen raised around some of the new puzzles, and they do give a different vibe to the original. But they fit so seamlessly into the world that they feel like they could have been in the original game. They are not worse just different. While I have not played since I was a kid, I was surprised by how many puzzles I remembered how to solve, so everything new that I had not experienced was a refreshing surprise that I adored.TLDR: One of the best ways to enjoy one of the best puzzle games of all time. If you hate puzzle games give it a skip, but otherwise you owe it to yourself to experience the world of Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan worlds are the GOAT's of old school, intelligent puzzle games - creating some of the most awe inspiring environments to grace a screen across so many of their games (personal favs being Myst, Myst 5 & Obduction).  In remaking Riven, this has solidified this fantastic games' place in the 21st century and this is a brilliant example of how to bring a game nearly 30 years forward in time.  Amazing job guys, keep it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent modern adaptation of the classic!  The world felt completely familiar, with many nods to the original (and at least one other work), yet different enough to be new and challenging once again, and with expanded areas of Riven not previously accessible to explore.  A thoroughly enjoyable experience for this long-time fan!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This world feels just as surreal, beautiful, haunting, creepy, and threatening as the original Riven did.  It's one of very, very few fictional places that I've been able to fully lose myself in.  While the geometry of the world is fairly simplistic, the texture work in this remake is absolutely gorgeous, and I'm so glad they included a zoom feature so I can marvel at the fine details.  Materials have multiple layers of ware and many tiny ornamental details.  As beautiful as the game is, it's the sound design (much of which seems to have been preserved from the original) that makes this place real.  Everything you interact with has weight to it, takes time, and sounds distinct from everything else.  The haunting music in this game makes me feel a very specific sort of fear and awe, which fits the game's plot perfectly.Some of the larger and more iconic puzzles have been simplified, but that didn't detract from the experience for me.  I love being able to write notes on screenshots.  I still had to use a little physical paper to solve a few puzzles.  If you enjoyed the original or have any interest in puzzle games this is a must play.  I would recommend playing Myst first if you haven't already, since it will make the story easier to interpret and will show the huge leap in progress Cyan made with world building between the two games.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is the sequel to Myst and the story picks up right where the original left off. Atrus needs your help to free Catherine from Gehn, Atrus' estranged father.  When you arrive on Riven you are instantly captured, but you are freed a very short time later by a mysterious benefactor. You come to realize that there are two factions fighting for control of Riven, those who are loyal to Gehn and those who want to be free from Gehn's tyranny. It's up to you to find Gehn and trap him in a one man prison that looks like a linking book. But making your way through this world is not as straight forward as you hoped. You must overcome numerous obstacle in order to proceed.Pros:Superb GraphicsSimple ControlsNon-linearOpen World MapMultiple EndingsMany puzzles to solveCons:Some of the mechanics are painfully slowOne puzzle was misleadingI absolutely loved the 1997 version of Riven and the remake is nothing short of a masterpiece. Some of the puzzles have changed from the original and each time you play the remake, the game is slightly different because the order for some of the puzzles are random. Best of all, for the first time, you can see Riven in 3-D and go where ever you wish.The only two things I didn't like about the remake. The way the machines work on Riven tend to work very slowly especially domes that lead to the Starry Expanse. They could have been sped up a bit. The other problem I had was with one of the puzzles. Unless I missed something, it was intentionally misleading making it illogical but it's the only one.At the time of this review, Riven 2024 was selling 34.99.  I love the Myst worlds and I this remake is well worth the price. Bring on Myst III: Exile.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This was definitely a day one purchase for me since the original Riven is one of my most memorable gaming experiences. Now I've bought both on release!With only an hour of playtime I have already had multiple jaw dropping experiences and while I was skeptical about changing up the game with new and altered content, I am now pretty much all steam ahead enjoying this experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible remake that balances the old with the new. It is very familiar for veterans of the original but with enough changes to make the experience fresh. If you are a fan of puzzle games, you owe it to yourself to pick up an excellent remake of one of the best puzzle games ever made.Only thing I can say as a small knock against this remake is that we don't have the charming live action people imposed into the game for cut-scenes. The models they use here are fine and look great but there's a charm to using live action people that is a little bit missed lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A classic and worthy successor to Myst; great visuals, great puzzles, great lore. I will say there are some issues; objects that are not clearly interactable unless you're reaaallly close to them, some very easily missed paths, clipping and animation issues (I was softlocked a couple of times which required a reboot), but this is a very adept remake! Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is a gorgeous remake of a beloved classic - and I say beloved, even though I had no concept that the game even existed before I played Myst (2021) last week, and grew immediately hungry for more. I can say definitively, without the rosy glasses of nostalgia, that this game was a fantastic experience and stands up to today's exploration-puzzler titans entirely on its own merits. Riven picks up right where Myst left off, though newcomers joining the series here would not feel like they had missed much by not playing the first entry. While Myst is a great game that I also recommend playing, Riven's greater focus on characters and story means that it's much easier to get invested in the stakes of the game right away.Riven is not a direct one-to-one remaster of the original title; instead, some mindful additions have been made, and the flow of the game has been altered slightly to enhance the experience and ensure that even veterans of the title have a few surprises waiting for them along their journey. Myst (2021) launched with a Photo Album, allowing you to take pictures of the game world for later reference, in case it was needed. Riven enhances this feature, calling it Notebook, by allowing you to type notes alongside any images you capture. In my playthrough, I used this feature not just for picture references, but as a journal to record my experience. Anything that interested me, I took pictures of and scribbled down a few lines. By the end of the game, I had a robust journal that documented my entire journey, and I took some great joy in reliving it, even just hours later, as new revelations recontextualized things I had seen earlier.I highly recommend Riven to anyone who likes exploration puzzlers, but especially to those who might be interested in the lore and history of the world it presents - a world where writers, using an ancient formula of written language, create books that transport the user to distant and fantastical Ages, and how the civilization that produced these writers spread their imperfections into the worlds that they would come to inhabit.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original 1997 release of Riven was one of my favourite games of all time, so I was very excited to hear about and play this remake. Having finished the game just a few minutes ago, I have almost nothing but praise. It was like playing it for the first time all over again, because this isn't a 1:1 translation from the original. Most of the puzzles (and even a few minor elements of the lore) have been almost completely rebuilt and remastered, and the care and attention that has gone into this work is on full display. Even if you're someone like me who has played the original enough times to have it memorised start to finish, while you won't be knocked quite back to square one, you'll have hours of fun figuring out how everything works again. As I've said to a few friends when discussing the game, it's like learning new lyrics to a familiar tune, and I enjoyed every minute of it.To be balanced, the game does have a few flaws, as not everything perfectly translates from the original 2D point-and-click game to the modern 3D-rendered, VR-experience I played through. Some of the VR controls are a little clunky at times, and I think I still prefer the original live-action actors to their 3D counterparts. But on the whole, this new version of Riven retains the soul of the original, with outstanding puzzles and an immersive world. Whether you're an old veteran or a first time visitor, I couldn't recommend this game highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This Is A Challenging Puzzle Game. I love it, and the riddles either are about doing the same thing over and over again (One Puzzle Got Me Stuck For 15 minutes when all I had to do was press the button one more time) or they were a nice challenge. Bring some paper and a pen though, as writing stuff down helps with certain puzzles (and your memory).Also Don't Touch Strange Books
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "No, but..."  reviewRiven 2024 keeps the content fundamentals - the look, the plot, the iconic puzzle  - but like most abridged editions, loses some of the specific tone and design voice that lived in the less approachable elements and stylistic details.So despite this version's stellar environments and more modern navigation, And those were the chief reasons I loved it when I finally truly played it in 2019; and why it's still worth playing 25+ years after its launch. There are a added touches here and there that feel at home with the original design sensibility  but the changes in flow, puzzles and the new areas take away from how integrated, consistent, justified but incidental everything was in the 1997 version.It sadly feels more inline with what Firmament offered: the new elements are more than often mechanical, repetitive and fairly arbitrary to the point of feeling gamey ... an approach that doesn't live up to the design of Riven '97. But a lot of it is still very good, albeit, in a fragmented, incomplete  way... like in an abridged version.So here's my suggestion:   - using Riven Universal Hint System page where necessary.If, after that, you still  bounce hard off its navigation scheme or low resolution or no hand-holding integrated puzzles, but want to explore more of its world, come here and buy this one to play; you'll have a very decent time. a team seemingly punching above its weight with fascinating new hires; and thus potentially very cool projects on the horizon.And go play Obduction, it's almost as good as Riven 97.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Man am I happy I played Myst first, this game is about 5 times as difficult and obscure.Good:- Graphically stunning.- Great VR mode, with a ton of comfort options.- Great performance, average ~100 fps in 1440p on an rtx 3060, on high settings (dlss quality)Kinda eh:- VR is difficult to run well, average ~40 fps on an rtx 3060 on low settings (dlss performance, playable but not great)- Puzzles are much harder than those in Myst, sometimes a bit unfair imo.- Oddly enough, no height adjustment in VR. This was present in Myst.There's a guide you can buy, but you can also use the internet to help you out, no shame in it lol.The guide gives you a guarantee that you can at least try it with a vague hint first, and not accidentally read the answers on a search engine result. But it's a bit steep, for something that you might only refer to twice.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool to get back into the world of Riven.  As a remake there are a few puzzles that have changed, and the in-game characters are now 3D instead of the live actors, but otherwise a really good remake with the ability to free-move around the islands.  Great job Cyan Games and looking forward to finishing Riven!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: VAGUE SPOILERSI was nervous that I would be disappointed by the changes made to the remake. After playing the demo and seeing big differences, I actually got excited to see what else was new. Aside from a couple bugs (fingers crossed they get patched out), this is the most fun VR game I've played since Half-Life: Alyx. It's also a visually beautiful game, in and out of VR. I played the original Riven dozens of times. I'm looking forward to replaying this one and finding anything I might have missed the first time around.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: That's the way a remake of an amazing classic should be done! I absolutely loved it! I had some of the best surprises playing this game, from the newly added features (which offer a better and a more in-depth experience of Riven, further creating the impression of a real, inhabited and hostile place) to the modified structure of already existing features (which was simply jaw-dropping). This is THE single game during which I was in a constant state of excitement and enthusiasm from start to finish. I loved the way some aspects of the old Riven were much better explained in the new version (most of these were part of the jaw-dropping surprises and, believe me, I have had quite a few of those). I loved the amazing attention to detail and, as always, how some of it was "hidden" (i.e. things you have to rush in order to catch a glimpse of or stuff you have to wander even in the tightest places to discover). Thank you and please keep creating such amazing worlds!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what a remake should be. Able to capture the feeling of the original game but with enough thoughtful changes to make it feel like a new experience.  I played original Riven when it was released in 1997 and never thought I'd be playing it again feeling just as immersed as I did 28 years ago, truly a surreal experience. Thank you so much to the teams at Cyan behind this.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's Riven! What more do you want? But, no, really, the magic of Cyan Worlds' early games is that they manage to capture the feeling of decoding and interpreting the environment--a detective game sans detectives. It's a feat that contemporary adventure games still rarely pull off. This update preserves what made the original good and when it makes changes to the puzzles, its largely for the better. The fact that players can walk through a 3D space is a huge quality of life improvement in itself, as this makes it easier to understand the world of Riven as a space. Any puzzles with pipes, darkness, or general navigation feel much more fair in full 3D.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: My name might give it away that I grew up to be a Myst fan. Riven was, in fact, my "first video game" that my dad played with me when I was 4. The entire series including original Riven has seen multiple replays and I was more than excited for a 3D remake.What surprised me immensely is that my expectations were exceeded by Cyan not just doing a raw remake but also having the courage to make changes that streamline the puzzles, storytelling, and progression of the game. Not only did that flow feel better - it also allowed me to feel almost like I'm playing this for the first time again. Some new puzzles and elements were added as well.Overall I had a very enjoyable time with the game and am very excited that this beauty has finally seen the light of day.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven is one of my top 5 favorite games of all time.  I love Cyan, and have followed the company nearly my entire life - since I first played Myst as a 9 year old kid.  This game originated out of a fan organized remake project called "The Starry Expanse" project - where some intrepid and highly skilled fans slowly and incredibly meticulously were trying to convert the images from the old Riven into high quality 3D maps, and ultimately fully and painstakingly recreate the game in every detail in full 3D.  I anxiously read every development blog update and donated money to the project.  You could tell it was a grueling and difficult endeavor, which went slowly.  Ultimately they made some sort of partnership with Cyan, who hired some of the team, and I think absorbed their work into this.What BLEW MY ABSOLUTE MIND - is that I thought this would be pretty much an inch by inch remake just as the "Starry Expanse" project was doing.  NOPE.  There are some HUGE changes.  No spoilers, but oh my lord.  Also - each time I saw something different early on, my initial fanboy response was disappointment.  Disappointment that it was different from my nostalgia.  But after I thought about the change and the decision behind that change, one by one by one - I agree with every single one of them.  The have truly gone through every tiny part of this game, and made changes that make it feel like a more cohesive, sensible, and story rich world.  The changes they made are incredible.  This is no MACLUNKY!Graphics:  Absolutely stunning.  They are taking advantage of Unreal Engine 5 and oh my GOD the lighting, and the texture / geometry detail is stunning.  I am not sure if they are using nanite and lumen but it looks like they are.  There are some scenes that truly are difficult to distinguish from a photo of a real place.  My only gripe here is the characters.  I do not think they are using metahuman.  The characters are ROUGH.  I really miss the videos of the real live actors.  They previously were so integrated into the CGI world, that it was better matching to the scenery than a lot of blockbuster movies today.  But these characters - the detail is low, the textures are rough, and the lighting is very flat.  Granted I'm on a M2 Max MacBook Pro - but this is with every graphical detail setting set to "Epic."  I wish they could find a way to rotoscope in videos of the actors into a 3D space / VR capable world, but maybe that will become a possibility in the future.Audio:AMAZING as ever.  Robyn Miller's original soundtrack is here, intact, and with all the right gameplay cues.  This is the ONLY video game soundtrack I keep coming back to again and again through the years.  The mood and the atmosphere is unlike any other sound experience.  AND - there is new stuff! That's all I'll say! :-DGameplay:All I can say is there is a MAJOR change in the way the environments and puzzles are laid out.  I love it.  It truly is a whole new game with new things to explore.  If you are upset that it is not an exact match to the "old Riven" then I would just suggest playing the old Riven.  I did leading up to this game and had an absolute blast.  I think they can both stand on their own.Story:I am nowhere close to finishing but I just had to get something down - I will be back here to update later. . . . . Overall rating pending, but this is quickly becoming my game of the year
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original, oh man, this is so good. SO good. The changes and additions to the game are absolutely an enhancement, and I'm so happy to be back. This is what happens when people who designed the original get to design the remake. I am not disappointed in the least!If you haven't played Riven before, it's one of the best exploration/ knowledge based puzzle games of all time. It's beautiful, engaging, and (let's be real) a masterpiece. Many of us have known this for decades, but it's really great to be able to share this with new players!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good faithful remake of the original. Some have claimed the puzzles are not as well integrated and lying everywhere. Not entirely true. The puzzles for the 'mild spoiler' rebels are actually more lore friendly than the original as they are supposed to be secretive and good and going undetected by the antagonists of the story. Making them more hidden and using more native symbology was a much needed improvement over the original. The thing I wish had been added into the puzzles a little and a way to learn it was the language. It is present, but there is not a way to learn it. Also there is not a way  to learn how combinations of higher numbers work without using an outside of the game source. It would have been nice to have been in game. A little bit more exploration for some of us that like more of a challenge than others. Also the final puzzle was harder in the original. This point I agree with many others. It is too simplified in the remake. If this had to be done for some players then a harder mode should have been made for others. Other than these points and the fact that the original video could not have been upscaled with AI and reused in the remake, the remake is pretty good. Worth it for new players. Old players will enjoy the new graphics, but miss certain things that the original had and maybe did better in some areas of the game. With this game I would suggest playing both versions. I guess the old version will run on windows 10 or 11 like  the new. If it doesn't it will with a program called SCUMVM. It is a VR machine that does a near perfect run of the old version of Riven. You only need Windows 10/11 to run the new version. I did notice it had a bug that made it crash once though partway through. This only happened once and didn't occur again. Also beware of 'spoiler' walking in a certain area with the walkways upside down as you can get stuck. This fix is exit the game and go back in on the autosave when reloading the game. Do not try to save first if you are stuck here. This bug can happen elsewhere, but mainly in the area I mentioned. For those of us that played the original, don't expect things to be in the same places or work in the same way. Some puzzles and locations have  changed or been expanded and work differently now. Better I think too. One bugged area that was in the original is now fixed in the remake. The biggest thing for players of the original; you will get to go in new areas that you could not go in before, and this alone makes the remake worth playing. For all players the story is the best in the series and very engaging. Without it all the rest would be pointless. For this alone I would strongly recommend this game to play and consider the graphics, new areas to explore, and puzzle revision to be the icing on the cake. If you like puzzles and a good story this is not one to miss out on.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Game looks fantastic with an art style that oozes charm and feels very polished. The world building, story and lore really do wonders investing you in the world of Riven and its many secrets.The puzzles are incredibly well built, offering a solid challenge while also feeling like they have purpose for existing instead of just being there for the sake of gameplay.Being able to take screenshots is a welcome bonus though I still had a pen and paper to hand for when I needed to cross-reference the pictures.Multiple endings are pretty fun also.Cons (Might not be a con for you) Puzzles, while well designed, sometimes wont give their payout straight away and will combine with others later on. Sure the payoff then is absolutely euphoric but you may leave many areas feeling like you've missed something when you haven't and that can sour the victory a little.Backtracking downright sucks. It'll take you an age waiting for the train system to arrive, turn around and take you to the next island (can be sped up by setting vehicle comfort to comfortable in the options) only to repeat the process again because you need to get on a different train from that island to reach your destination. There's a fast travel machine that'll take you directly to your island of choice but even that takes a while with its two load zones and two minor puzzles you need to complete each time you want to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun puzzle game, I had to get a few hints because I was oblivious to certain things that are supposed to be easy to find and would have taken me hours otherwise. The puzzles are very in depth and often layer over each other. If I didn't get tiny hints every once in a while though there could have easily been 5-10 more hours added onto my playtime
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: From a purely graphical and immersive experience standpoint it's great. Between the free roam and updated graphics, it's fun to see.However, if you care about the puzzles more, this game is a massive downgrade from the original. They massively simplified most of the puzzles, they changed most areas of the game in more ways than just graphics and walking around, so purists that liked the original are going to be mad. They also gave Riven the "yellow paint" treatment in some regards where they removed a lot of "extra" stuff and highlighting important things or making things like buttons much more noticeable.Walking everywhere takes forever, There is no Zip Mode, Most animations can't be skipped and loading in new areas can take several seconds and isn't done in parallel with the animations.Also, it's 2024 and we are still releasing games with controls you can't configure? Isn't that functionality BUILT IN to Unreal? You just have to implement it?
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The reworking of many of the puzzles was a smart choice. I narratively knew how to beat the game, but I still had to take notes to solve the new-ish puzzles. It really made the remake feel just fresh enough to warrant the cost of admission. Thanks Cyan for finally finishing this 3D remake over a decade in the making. Now please make Myst VI or something... or at least another novel. Finish the Book of Marrim pretty please!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe this is real. I'm so immersed I struggle to remember what was in the original game or not. I'm glad they changed some things because the most difficult puzzles are the one I remember, and the most evil doors. Nice to see the doors are intact lolIf you have a 13/14th gen intel cpu, you might run into crashes when trying to launch the game. Your mileage may vary, but whenever a game gives me this crash I just need to turn down the Performance core ration in Intel Xtreme tuning utility. I switch it from x57 to x56, and then it doesn't crash
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Very accurate recreation of how the original 'felt' to play and explore. Lack of forced perspectives made it easy to get lost in the world again, as much now from taking in the scenery as from missing 'that one item or button', a liveable trade. Main hiccups are mostly technical issues, like lighting and rendering bugs/pop-in at the edges of the screen. Also, the 'internal' screenshot resolutions can frequently render them useless for visual information, *cough* comparing lights to corresponding symbols on a stone wheel *cough*.The 3d renders of characters are often uncanny, but generally understandable alternatives to locking down movement for cutscenes, though the one 'fleeing' character did demonstrate that they were still 'forced' to stop you at least once. Really, the biggest thing that stuck out to me was how neatly trimmed Atrus was, when his journal reads more as a man buried in his work, using your help as a trump card only after months of all-consuming writing and formulating.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited since Riven's original release for this retelling and it is worth it.I was an avid Myst fan when it first came to Windows in the 90's, but my computer couldn't run Riven then, so I missed it on release. I read the books, I saw the box, but I never took the leap. I played later installments, I early beta tested Uru! But I never went back for Riven.Playing this version of Riven took me back to a place I'd only ever been next to and it felt familiar and fresh. I've since played the original Riven and I appreciate the reworking of some puzzles, refinement really, and the little visual touches and changes that take advantage of a fully-3d engine. Playing this game has made me want to revisit the books, the later installments, and the community I'd spent so much time with. This is a worthy and level-setting recreation of a great game and I hope the team has it in them to continue to explore the many worlds of the D'Ni with fresh games and retelling of the originals.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's practically lived inside the original 1997 game, I was anxious to see how the remake would work out. After finishing it, I can say it lives up to its potential. There were several points in the game where I had a flashback to how photorealistic I remember the original to be. Everything's been lovingly recreated and some puzzles have been updated (for the better!). My only gripe is that it's now somewhat slower to get around, as you can speedclick through the different screens and there's no zip mode. But that's only minor and didn't detract from my enjoyment of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The game does a great job making the puzzles feel like extensions of the world rather than arbitrary obstacles (with a couple of exceptions).  It constantly feels like you're learning about a new world, culture, and technologies.There were 2 main downsides.  The first was a couple of puzzles, my difficulty was with finding what I was meant to interact with, rather than what the solution was.The other is the slow animations of travel between islands.  It feels thematic, but also when you need to reread something on another island, the only 2 methods of travel are very very slow.  I'd estimate 40% or more of my playtime was backtracking.Overall, this might be my favorite puzzle game.  Highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is overall enjoyable, a lot of quality from it comes from the 1997 Riven (such as the story, puzzles etc) but this is well recreated.Some puzzles and layouts were changed, and I think it's fine overall, it's the kind of stuff that would fit in the universe and the original game.However there are some important flaws to note : The game clearly lacks optimization, there are some glitches, some crashes, overall it's a bit rough on the edges even though it doesn't ruins too much the experience, it would just be nice to have some more polishing.Also, I don't really see what's the point of VR, this is clearly not optimized enough for it and there's nothing really interesting that VR brings to the table.Also, I lost 5 years of my lifespan on that unskippable rotating room animation on the temple island, as well as the starry expanse domes transitions.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this entire game in VR and let me just get this out of the way: This game in VR, right now, is a hot mess. It is extremely resource intensive, very often struggling to maintain 90 fps on my setup (RTX4090 + 13900k) WITH DLSS quality on. It supports both Steam and openxr runtimes so you CAN use steam overlay, but for some reason, the game turns into a jumbling mess while the overlay is open, to the point where everything would shake uncontrollably while the achievement window popped up. And, by far the worst part: Out of the 3 or 4 fast travel methods the game has, it consistently crashed to desktop when using 2 of them. By consistently, I mean about 60% at first, and that rate just went up as my game progressed. One of the fast travel methods isn't even optional, but mandatory for completing the game, so whenever I had to use it and it crashed, I just opened the game in flat mode while in VR, fast travelled, saved, closed the game, and resumed it in VR. That experience is exactly as miserable as it sounds.And yet, I'm giving it a positive review. The reason for that is that this is an absolute gem of a game. Having never played Myst or Riven before, I went into these 2 games completely blind, and played both of them in VR. While Myst felt like a fun interesting little adventure, Riven was absolutely breath taking. The VR mode makes you work for it, but it's absolutely worth it. The feeling of being in a beautiful and unknown world full of secrets to be unlocked and a mission is only amplified by the VR experience. The writing pulls you into its world and characters, and somehow, the remake of a 1997 game feels more modern and sophisticated than most of the contemporary stuff I play. I finished this game over a week ago and I still think about it every day, whether it is a puzzle, a line of text, a specific place in its world, or just about the sense of wonder and discovery it made me feel as I slowly peeled each layer of mystery away from its onion.Bottomline is, the VR iteration of this game is frustrating, but be patient with it. It's well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original was one of my favourite games, and at first I must admit I wasn't too keen on there being changes between this and the original. It didn't take me long to overcome this feeling and fall in love with the world all over again. I think most of the differences either made the game tighter or else added interesting new areas to explore, and in at least one case both. The new puzzles were fun to solve - something I was unable to do the first time around without a walkthrough. Whether that means they are easier or I'm simply more accustomed to the world and the type of puzzles it can throw at you I'm not sure, though I suspect a bit of both. Either way it was a lovely experience which I definitely recommend to anyone who is a fan of deeply immersive worlds.

_childDocuments_.review: Once I stopped trying to play it based on my memory of the original, it became fun again. This game is significantly different from the original. _childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong fan of Riven, this remake was an absolute thrill to soak up.Almost every moment of my playthrough was spent giddily gazing at everything with child-like wonder.It's amazing how when you play the original game, your mind fills in the gaps for all the content between the images; it turns static images into spaces. In this remake, you'll feel that sense of space and wonder, but your eyes and ears will just present it to you, rather than your mind attempting to read between the lines.The changes to the game and world are well thought out. Bringing a sense of accessibility to newcomers, while adding moments of pure joy and wonder for veterans. The changes also serve to take a few layers of difficulty off some of the most brutal puzzles in gaming history. Personally I think this is great, as it still challenges people without making most of them get over frustrated and move on, or just simply use a walkthrough and blast through it.We additionally get more lore in the journals, more areas to explore and expanded areas that were once brilliant but small. The sort of places you longed to see more of, but never could.Of course, this is still a game - it's imperfect, made by a much smaller team on a much smaller budget. At the time of writing, the character animations are a little rough, but still very much a step in the right direction for Cyan. I encountered a few little visual glitches here and there, but nothing game ruining or overly third-wall breaking. Also sometimes the lipsync felt a little off, but that may have been a bug or something on my end.All of Robyn Miller's fantastic original soundtrack makes a return as well, a soundtrack I haven't stopped listening to since 1997. He also injected a couple of new tracks into newer sections of the game as well, and while they are lovely on their own, I couldn't help but feel like they felt a bit out of place. They sounded very much like a modern Robyn Miller track, rather than a Riven / 90's Robyn Miller track, which can be a little jarring if you're a huge fan of the soundtrack like I am. It's certainly not game breaking though. Personally I'm surprised he didn't use the original synths that were so pivotal to the Riven sound, but I'll respect his intentions here.Overall though, this game is phenomenal. As a lifelong fan returning home, or a newcomer wanting to see something amazing, this game really delivers. No game really does environmental storytelling and puzzles that are totally grounded in the world like Riven - and I'm happy to report that the remake lovingly carries on this legacy.If you love Riven, and don't mind a bit of a mix up to keep things fresh, this one's for you.If you never played it originally but enjoy exploration, lore, world-building and puzzles, I know you'll love it as well.It's a solid 9/10 for me, and I want to give Cyan my absolute heartfelt gratitude for this labour of love.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: In a word: Awesome.  I had played Myst and Myst III: Exile up to this point, skipped Riven.  My roommates and I all played this together, bouncing ideas off of each other and worked through it... Just like how me and my parents played Myst in the 90s.  Awesome time, reminded me of a formative memory.  Graphics are great, puzzles are logical, world is captivating.  If you're on the fence, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have a ton of hope for Yet Another Myst Remake, but this one is head and shoulders over the others.It doesn't open especially well, because the (necessary) change to 3D modelled actors is... clunky, but once the actors get off the screen and you're left in the world proper, it's absolutely stunning.  Riven looks almost as good as it did in 1996, but now with free movement!  The world feels bigger, more concrete.So the basic execution is good, that doesn't justify a purchase.  What DOES, however, is the changes made.The two uber-puzzles have been modified heavily, as have a few locations and the domes, and every change is the correct one.  I always thought the animal-eyes security in the first game just made Gehn look silly for not figuring it out for months, but the totem alternative version in this version not only makes it easier to overlook the clues, but it adds depth to the Rivenese rebellion and their cultural outlook.  The Fire Marble puzzle has been significantly improved, and the changes made to the domes actually made me stop and gawp in awe when I got inside them.Further, the changes made to the map are also all correct.  No more weird and twisty paths for sake of paths - the village island now feels smaller and more claustrophobic, and the weirder rooms have been relocated out of reach of the villagers - Gehn's illusory projection chair to the temple altar is now tucked into the cliffside in a harder-to-find location instead of literally down the hall from the temple room where anyone can see it.  The map is neater, perfectly sensible, and no longer has Myst's infamous "random unknown machine" aesthetic.Also, they went wild with the decay aesthetic.  While the only real glimpse into the islands' rotting state in the original was the interconnected maglevs and the sealed fissure, the remake makes it much clearer.  Bridges collapse, the ocean is full of holes that spew mist, literal rifts in reality float quietly in the air, destroyed machinery lays at the foot of cliffs.  The sense of urgency that was quietly there in the original is dialled much higher this time around.On the whole, I think I would put this as my hands-down favourite remake ever.  The added puzzles are great, the changes made all serve the worldbuilding, and the visuals and sounds are knock-down gorgeous.  I'll miss the FMV actors, but seeing how little people are onscreen, it's a tiny sacrifice for all the excellence on display here.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: And they say time travel is impossible. When I started the game, I was back in good ol' 1997. _childDocuments_.review: So far so good.  I've played it for about 6 hours on my M2 Pro MacBook Pro, all graphics settings on "High," and I've had zero issues. Man, they're *amazing!!*I didn't start to play this game until after the first patch was released, so I can't speak to any bugs that existed prior to that, but I have yet to experience any fatal flaws.  Minor graphical glitches are all I've ever experienced, thus far, and even those have been very few and far between.If you like the Myst series, and you want to experience Riven on a modern computer with modern graphics, I 100% recommend this.  Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the original Riven. As far back as I can remember using a computer, I have memories of the game. As a kid I was just exploring, pretending I lived there with a strategy guide at my side to ensure I could see every nook and cranny of the world. As I got older I started to appreciate the aspects of the game I had overlooked as a kid; the incredible world building, puzzle design, sound design, music... I could go on. These things are the reason the game had so greatly captured my imagination as a kid, I just hadn't taken notice of them until I was older. While I have no regrets experiencing the game this way, as it has been hugely influential in my life and my career (I'm a game dev), I have always wished I could experience Riven blind and see if I could solve all of its puzzles myself.This remake has not only allowed me to immerse myself in a world that I've been wanting to visit in VR for a very long time, it also gave me a taste of solving Riven myself without a walkthrough thanks to the changes that have been made. I say "taste" as, even though some puzzles have been changed quite drastically, they still remain very similar in spirit. The changes are all well thought out and tend to make a bit more world building sense than the original's puzzles, though I also think they've been made a tad easier and in so doing, some of the elegant subtlety of the original's puzzles has been lost. It's hard for me to judge the difficulty of the changed puzzles though as, again, being as familiar with the OG as I am I was pretty quickly able to pick up on how the clues were to be applied to the puzzles. There is one major change to how a clue is derived that I really do not like () as the mechanism just doesn't make much world sense to me, but otherwise I am extremely satisfied with how the game design has been tweaked.Aside from puzzle changes, there are also several changes and additions to the world, all of which have clearly been thought through thoroughly. One new area in particular had my jaw drop the first time I entered it. There are also new areas that were previously only teased in the original game, and new details and sequences that wouldn't have been feasible with the pre-rendered nature of the OG, making it feel like these things were always meant to be here and now can be thanks to there being fewer technical limitations. Whether new or old, all the areas and set pieces in the game are wonderful to explore.Of course all these changes and the ability to move freely would be moot if the game didn't look good, but it is as beautiful as ever, if not more-so in some cases. Even in VR, though some graphical fidelity is scaled back, the game looks fantastic. The striking art direction of the OG is all intact. Visually I would say my only complaint is a handful of rather janky animations sprinkled through the game. Some are fantastic - animals in particular seem to have gotten special attention - but there are others that immediately made me remember I was in a video game. Some weird physics moments, a handful of awkward character animations, and unnaturally abrupt elevators were some of the more noticeable ones. This is a pretty minor complaint, but it's one of those areas that the original technically did better.Before moving on from visuals, I'll also say that the character models and animations are quite good all things considered. Some seem to have gotten more care than others but all in all this is Cyan's best attempt at realtime 3D characters.The sound design here is wonderful. I greatly admire the soundscapes created for the original game and was very happy that almost all of the original sounds were reused here where appropriate. While in recent memory Cyan's sound design has been adequate, it's lacked the level of detail in Riven's that conveys mechanisms far more complex or aged than what you'd expect just by looking at them. My only complaint is that there does not seem to be, to my ear, any spatial or binaural audio tech in the game, which is *very* important for creating an immersive VR experience IMHO. Sounds don't quite pan and bounce naturally as a result. I really wish Cyan would invest in this technology in the future, but that aside the sounds themselves truly make Riven feel alive.The original soundtrack was fantastic back when it first released and is still amazing today. It aids greatly in setting the tone and telling the story. My only complaint in regards to the OST is that the handful of new tracks, composed by the original game's composer, do not fit into the existing OST and do not reach the same level of production quality. I'm not sure why but it doesn't seem like any attempt was made to utilize the same synthesizers as the OG OST did and so the new tracks stick out a lot, and not in a good way. The production also seems very dry overall to my ears. I can't complain too much as the original is still here in its entirety, but it would have been great to get new tracks of the same style and quality.Lastly, playing this game in VR was mostly great, thought there are a few things that could be improved. For one, I have been experiencing a nasty crash bug playing in VR, often when the game tries to adjust/unlock my position due to a loading zone or due to some mechanism moving me around. Hoping this can be fixed soon. I also think the screenshot system, while sufficient thanks to the pause menu opening and closing quite quickly, could be improved. Mainly saving the scroll bar position when opening and closing screenshots and adding next/previous buttons when viewing a screenshot would make things a bit more convenient when trying to jump between several different ones. I also wish there was a better way to read journals in VR. I had to hold them at a pretty awkward angle with my Index controllers and ended up just switching to desktop mode to read them as holding them got tiring fast. Overall though the VR interactions seem pretty solid. There are a handful that express weightiness by lagging behind your hand position which I really appreciate. None of the issues I have with the VR implementation outweigh the experience of exploring this world in VR. Anyone with a headset who has been hankering for an amazing world to explore should be getting this game immediately.Conclusion: The original Riven is one of the greatest games ever made, and this remake does it justice. In fact, in some ways, it improves upon the original. While you can't go wrong with either version, this one is absolutely worth playing and will likely be more accessible to modern audiences without losing much of what made the original so great without replacing it with something equally so. VR support is solid, and makes this a must buy game for anyone looking for VR games to get lost in. This is a world I think everyone should explore at least once, even if you don't ever finish the game. If anything about this game intrigues you - a screenshot, the premise, a recommendation - don't hesitate and jump in.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy "Myst like" adventure games, then this is  game you should not miss.RIVEN is, quite simply put, the greatest game that has ever been made. Full stop.Now, thanks to Cyan and The Starry Expanse Project, I get to relive this game anew after over 20 years.I've only just begun this remake, and have been impressed with it even more than I thought I would be. That is quite a feat considering my bias in feeling that this is, once again, the greatest game of all time. I've played every Myst game and read all the novels (many times), and deeply adore this franchise.I was concerned about the switch to 3D rendered characters in place of the old FMV sequences, but the team's care and attention to detail has laid my concerns to rest. The level of expression and detail in the character models absolutely fits the game's style, and look great.I look forward to experiencing the changes, a couple of which I've already noticed just in the first half hour of game-play, and exploring this delightfully well crafted world in full 3D.Thank you to the teams at Cyan and The Starry Expanse. A special thank you to Rand and Robyn Miller.Edit: Completed my first playthrough in ~9 hours. I maintain my opinion that this is a very well-crafted remake that is not only respectful of it's source, it enhances it.If you aren't familiar with RIVEN then it could easily (and likely will) take you longer to complete. I would have easily completed it in far less time had I not been taking my time to look at all the beautiful scenery, as well as the changes/additions to the puzzles. I don't even know how long I walked through and watched the butterflies on Jungle Island.I knew I was going to love this remake, but I am so grateful that it is even better than I anticipated.Potential Spoiler (Story not Puzzle spoiler): RIVEN (1997) was my favorite game of all time. How fitting that it took RIVEN (2024) to overtake it. My new favorite game, is a remake of the original. I couldn't have wished for more.Thank you again to everyone at Cyan and Starry Expanse.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a review before on steam or played the original Riven or Myst before my purchase of the combo pack with both games. I got the games because i'm new to VR and wanted a more relaxing game to play between the more intense racing games I normally play. Myst VR was cool and interesting but Riven remake is a whole "nother" level! i'm totally shocked at the level of attention to detail that was lovingly crafted into this game. i want to commend the DEVS! you guys are AWESOME! please make more VR titles!  the immersion, the lore and mystery behind the world the cool mixture of primitive technology/cultures and advanced wizard like contraptions you get to mess with and how the story unfolds is great. for all of you who may have played the original Myst but never tried Riven give yourself a gift and try it!

_childDocuments_.review: A true masterpiece, as a remake and as an original game.As a huge fan of he series I loved it so much- Fans of the original will get their magnificent full 3D 4K remake, that is incredibly beautiful and smooth in regular 3D, and the VR is marvelous, and if you dreamed of being on Riven there you have it nowThe modification / additions are well balanced, with some new/modified parts and puzzle while keeping the original very well preserved. So it's enough to be surprised if you know it, and amazedRand of course, but also Robyn Miller for the music and especially Richard Vander Wende came back to capture the same magic that happened in 1997, but even better. The orignal voices are kept as well, which is great particularly for Gehn voiced by John Keston, and of course Rand as Atrus.- Newcomers will discover the best puzzle game of all time, with welcomed tweaks for the most difficult puzzles of the orginal, making them more accessible without changing their essence. To me, it's the smartest world building and puzzle game ever made, because it works as actually one meta-puzzle that you have to reconstruct piece by piece, gradually understanding the world as a whole.SLIGHT SPOILER : The only small regret I have are the 3D characters, I would have loved to have the original live actors like the most recent version of Myst but it's understandable that it just wasn't doable technically, as they move around and the footage from 1997 would probably wouldn't have worked out.TLDRIt's a wonder and a classic for any puzzle and worl building games fan, and a marvel in every aspect, new and preserved, for the fans of the original. _childDocuments_.review: When I heard that there was going to be a 3D remaster of Riven I was incredibly excited. Riven is a game that brings me right back to my childhood, gazing at the mesmerizing stained glass style art on the cardboard box and sleeves that contained it's 5 disks. I remember spending weeks stumped and roaming around the amazing world that Cyan had created, the deep and immersive lore is some of the most formative mythology of my childhood. I expected to load up this new remastered version and gawk at the stunning graphics, reminisce with my favorite objects and environments, breeze through the main puzzles (as I have essentially committed them all to memory and that which is not memorizable I could find very quickly), get goosebumps as the final cutscene plays, and call it a night. Seriously, I thought I could cruise through in one night. Boy was I wrong, and in the most amazing way.I had read that there would be extra puzzles, and I thought, "great!" What I had imagined was an extra switch on boiler island, a new path to go down to find some familiar clue, and the like. Well, I got that, and so much more. It is a really daunting task to take a game that is so beloved by so many, and is so furiously nostalgic to it's player base, and just change a whole bunch of it. The fact that it was such a massive success and provided hours of enjoyable gameplay to even a seasoned veteran Myst player is a true testament to the passion and care that was taken by the development team. The people who worked on this game love Riven, and that love saturates every pixel you encounter. This was not a cash grab, this was not a vanity project. This is what a remake should be. The core puzzles of the game have been reimagined and reimplemented so that the game is fun for both new and returning players. They fit seamlessly into the world, to the point where if you were playing it for the first time, you probably couldn't tell what was old and what was new. The new puzzles utilize the environment and lore with such masterful grace that has become the hallmark of Cyan games. They don't feel like cheap rip-offs of the original puzzles, and hit the sweet spot of challenging but not impenetrable. Many of the areas of the game are expanded and fleshed out. Previously inaccessible areas are opened up to the player for exploration. I was almost giddy when I, just for laughs, clicked on a door I knew could not be opened and it swung open. "Wait, I can walk around out here?!" It was so cool and so well done, it truly is like a love letter to the fans. Both the visual and sound design is stunning, just like the original. Words can barely describe the pure dopamine given by being able to experience one of your most cherished childhood fantasy worlds in full HD 3D environments. Some voice parts are re-done and others are preserved from the original (RIP John Keston) and both are fantastic. The music hits at the pit of your being like no other soundtrack can, "atmospheric" doesn't even come close to describing the level to which the music elevates this game. Again, pure gold.All together the remastered content is a tribute to the blood sweat and tears that were obviously poured into this game and the original. Alas, nothing is perfect. The flaws in this game are far below the threshold of significantly taking away from the experience. The live action FMV videos of the old game are replaced with CGI models which works.... about as well as could be expected. They don't quite succeed in climbing out of the uncanny valley, but it's understandable, the team really didn't have any other options and did the best with what they had. You spend very little of the game interacting with other people so it's only a footnote. Something that could be addressed is the occasional de-sync between the voices and the actors which is just a tad more distracting than is necessary. I saw a handful of rocks and set pieces just pop into existence, particularly while using the public transit available on Riven, and also had one or two crashes to desktop. That being said, warts and all, this is one of the best remastered games I've ever played.95/100Would link again.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a big fan of the original Riven so I jumped on this new edition the moment it came out. It’s a lovingly made new version this time in three dimensions. I greatly enjoyed my time with it.However I don’t think every aspect of this new edition is a straight up improvement from the original. A lot of work has gone into streamlining the puzzles and while that make it more welcoming to new players I do think some important aspects have been lost.For example there is a new inventory item that is introduced early in the game that takes something away from the game only being about observation. Some hints have been made more explicit and no longer require some essential deductions. Finally the newly introduced number system wasn’t used to its full extend in my playthrough. I could get away with only understanding parts of how it worked and the game never pushed me to understand all of it.This version has some additional story bits and I think I really enjoyed the additional detail. The way Riven combines the lore and puzzles remains unparalleled and I really do hope Cyan decides to continue developing new material in the Myst universe again.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven was one of the games that brought me and my best friend together as kids, 2 decades ago. We would spend hours poring over every inch of the game, trying to squeeze as much info out of the journals, taking notes on printer paper, and really pushing the tiny gears in our heads to try to figure out the solutions to what are truthfully some of the most difficult puzzles in the series.Last night, my friend and I finished playing the Riven remake together :) I can truthfully say that it is perhaps one of my happiest moments in gaming, and that's in no small part due to the love and care that Cyan has put into this remake.I still love the original Riven, but I will be the first to admit that it has some very rough edges. At times, its puzzles and solutions seem overly obtuse and contrived. It's a highly ambitious game held back by the technical constraints and design limitations of the time.The remake addresses all of that. The original locations and puzzles are all here, but have been much more fully realized. In many cases, small alterations have been made for better pacing. In other cases, entirely new mechanics, items, and points-of-interest have been added to more logically lead you towards the solutions of the game's most notorious puzzles. Locations that were under-utilized in the original have newfound purpose. None of it compromises the integrity of the original's vision, and all of it is tied together by an absolutely gorgeous graphical upgrade.Every change combines to create the definitive version of Riven. It feels like the game that Cyan always intended for us to have. It's a love letter to everybody who played the original, and a gift to anybody who never had the chance. This is, officially, my favourite in the Myst series, and it makes me dream of what would be possible if Exile, Revelations, or End of Ages were to receive a similar treatment.If I had to nitpick, my friend and I were ever so slightly disappointed in the quality of the character models and animations. They just don't quite manage to match the charm of the original's FMV scenes. The remake also maintains some of the "hidden in plain sight" puzzle solutions from the original that largely just rely on you being very attentive and thinking a bit outside the box, which at least to me have always been more frustrating than satisfying to figure out. But I would be lying if I said that these minor gripes really had any measurable impact on our enjoyment of this incredible game. It was a pleasure from start to finish, and I'm so glad my friend and I got to experience it all these years later. Thank you from the bottom of my heart to everybody who made this possible <3

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece of puzzles and art when it first released in 1997, and remains a masterpiece of puzzles and art in the remastered version. There have been welcomed changes to the more obtuse puzzles of the original, and they have served to expand the cultural artifacts of its deceptively lore-rich world. This is a remaster for the Ages.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr It's a pretty great remake of, arguably, the best puzzle game ever made. So yeah, buy it.This review contains no spoilers.I'm gonna open this review by disclosing that Riven (1997) has remained my #1 game of all time for most of my time on this planet, so this review is probably a little biased both in my praise and my criticism. But that also means i know this game like the back of my hand and I noticed every single change and put a lot of thought into my conclusions here. With that said:Riven (1997) is the best game ever made, and Riven (2024) is also pretty damn good for a lot of the same reasons. They are, however, not the same game. Besides the obvious technical advantage of making a game for hardware 25 years newer, Riven (2024) has a good number of things that are outright alterations or additions to the old game. Unlike the many Myst remakes over the years, Riven (2024) does  attempt to just be Riven (1997) in 3D. Instead, there are new areas added, new lore, and virtually  of the puzzles have been replaced with new puzzles. But, also very importantly, Riven (1997)'s fantastic visuals and music still remain, even prettier (in most aspects) now that the technology is 25 years newer. The final result is an updated and slightly expanded version of an already amazing game, which gives you... an amazing game.But Riven (2024) is not flawless. Riven (1997) suffers some downsides both because the game's technology is old and the game's puzzle design philosophy is old. Riven (2024), meanwhile, suffers a little because the game's technology and design philosophies are too . Riven (1997) was also a highly funded and published game, while Riven (2024) was done by an 100% indie Cyan (woo!) and some amazing work by the volunteers in the  team, but the budget was almost certainly smaller.On the technical side: Riven (1997) was highly limited by what home computers were capable of doing in 1997. The actual core artwork of Riven is practically flawless: Riven (1997)'s renders were made by a large team of well-funded artists using extremely powerful hardware and software to make cutting edge computer graphics. And then those absolutely spectacular renders were compressed down into 608x392 dithered images and some little quicktime videos (running  in rectangles above the still images) with a bitrate that might  a meg a second. And those tiny little pictures still managed to fill 5 CD-ROMs to bursting. Riven (1997) is an absolutely gorgeous achievement in computer art, and you gotta watch it through a little grimy window.So, how did they get around that in Riven (2024)? Now we're in Unreal Engine 5, an engine I don't like very much, but benefits from 25 years of advancements in computing. Both Talos Principle 2 and Riven (2024) suffer from a lot of the same UE5 problems, including framerates lower than what they really should be, really aggressive asset streaming that often breaks the immersion, and movement physics that are really not great. (If you've played a UE5 game you probably know what I mean, but you've almost certainly played a UE4 game, and UE4 had a similar but milder stink of its own.) However, UE5  looks pretty damn good, and you can bulldoze over any unoptimized software by just dumping more watts through your big green space heater. The result is a game that  has more visual fidelity with the same brilliant art direction, plus more freedom of movement than Riven (1997) could ever hope to achieve at the time. Now, instead of clicking through little pictures, you're walking around a pretty gorgeous island that looks a whole lot like the one you remember. But there were still things that prerendered graphics could do that you can't do by strapping a facebook phone to your skull, so some things have been lost, too. Some other subtle but noticeable downgrades and/or alterations have been made for the sake of VR compatibility and motion sickness prevention. There have also been a couple of small areas that are completely new, but only one of them has any sort of gameplay in it whatsoever, while the rest are pure (and very pretty) eye candy that you simply walk through once and then you're done. The good news is that virtually all of the problems I just mentioned are now patchable and may simply disappear by the time you read this review (I'm on day 1 patch right now), and you still end up with something that's pretty damn good.On the design side: Riven (1997) was /hard/. The puzzles were fantastic, but they pulled no punches. Riven (2024) has replaced all but a few minor puzzles with new ones that slot pretty seamlessly into the world and incorporate new content that expands the lore and the game itself. But they're easier puzzles for sure. And I don't have a problem with that at all: the old puzzles are still there to go play on the old game, which runs just fine on the current steam/gog version or through scummvm. I do, however, think the new puzzles don't integrate into the world quite as seamlessly as the old ones did. The new music /mostly/ fits in pretty well and is all pretty great, but there's one new song that doesn't quite fit the rest of the soundtrack. The new 3d animated characters are, naturally, worse actors than the literal amazing actors that did the 1997 FMVs, though the new voices are superb and John Keston remains a perfectly voice Gehn. The writing that has been replaced, both in journals and in dialogue, seems a little bit worse as well, but I find that a little harder for me to be objective about, so that point might just be my grumpy old man bias talking. But, still, you end up with something that's pretty damn good.(If anyone wants to talk specifics about any of the above points, that would require spoilers, but get in touch and I'll talk about Myst stuff all day any day)In the end, we have two versions of Riven, neither of which are perfect, but both of which are very very very good. And, importantly, Riven (2024) is far more accessible, both in its technology and its difficulty. Both games are definitely worth playing, but if you're reading this review because you're thinking about buying Riven (2024), do it. Buy it for your best friend too. You probably ought to play  or  first, but it's not a strict requirement.Cyan's still here and still producing gold, and Riven is a masterpiece that everyone should experience.
