_childDocuments_.review: I’m giving this a thumbs up but with some big caveats:It’s Riven, so I would guess that the biggest demographic of buyers are people who already experienced this game (people like me). The base flatscreen game is good, it’s mostly on rails with branching paths which may be weird for the younger folks just now getting into it but it should make perfect sense based on the source material and I’m fine with that. This is still Riven; it’s a good game with a really fascinating universe which expands the lore of Myst pretty significantly. I haven’t played either in a while and I never finished Riven before; the visuals and the beauty of the game remain outstanding.The biggest gripe I have is that there are a lot of UI nitpicks: there should be a quick save key, the screenshot notebook should be accessible with a single step: you access the starting journal by bringing up your satchel so this seemed like an obvious move (I might have missed it if it’s there though?). Also, screenshots don’t sync across devices but your cloud saves do, which I suppose is the best outcome if you have to choose but still…The controls really need to be rebindable. I played a little on my Steam Deck and it actually runs pretty well but the preset controller settings are baffling (left bumper for screenshot? What exactly is the right trigger doing?). Currently there’s no changing it in game, so Deck users can fiddle with a custom configuration but I didn’t want to do all that.Ok. That’s the flatscreen situation, I think we’re talking about a C+ or even a B- on execution since the base game is still good and the 3D remake is pretty faithful to the visuals.The VR is at least a solid D, maybe worse. I’m not convince anyone playtested this for more than 15 minutes. The graphics are still good, I’m actually pleasantly surprised it runs on my laptop (beefy legion laptop, but still!). No. This is more about the thoughtlessness of the UI but now the ramifications are infinitely worse.Managing the 3D satchel is pretty cool, but working with the items is a nightmare: the starting journal (or other journals you may find) are atrocious since the programming wants you to turn a page at least 90% before it fully turns which means you keep trying to turn the same page over and over again. This would be easier if you didn’t have to keep your other hand gripping the book and there’s no way to change grips from continual to toggle. Opening doors sometimes works like this too. There’s a lot of accessibility settings which is great but also strange that they didn’t also add the standard VR controller settings as well.Speaking of controllers, I’m also at a loss to explain their approach. Screenshots are able to be taken in the pause menu, the menu itself is accessible (on the Q3) by holding both the X and Y buttons. The Y button brings up the satchel. You interact with grippable stuff with the middle finger grips. You move and look with the joysticks, clicking in to run. So what do the forefinger triggers and the other three buttons do? Mostly nothing? So no screenshot button? Huh?It feels like they had 30 seconds to assign controls and then never went back.So yeah, VR looks cool, it’s why I picked this up. But I’m definitely finishing this in flatscreen.

_childDocuments_.review: I play Riven in VR, revisiting it after playing it first in 1998 when I bought my first PC. The Myst series absolutely lend themselves to VR where you really are exploring the world. Hopefully the rest of the series will appear in the future. I confess to having bought into the series many years ago, so there is a degree of preaching to the converted.This is not a game for those who require constant action: there is a lot of thought, backtracking and note taking involved. You need to take your time and properly explore. I admit to consulting a crib sheet occasionally! The reward is that the gorgeous graphics allow me to enter a world that, certainly in VR, is as immersive as any I have come across, as near to 'being there' as you can get. The rides on the Riven transportation systems are fantastic! One proviso is that you need a reasonably powerful PC and high resolution headset. (I use Ryzen 9 5900x and Nvidia 4080 super with Vive Pro 2). Being able to easily play seated is a bonus for me due to arthritis and general back trouble. I hope others will get as much enjoyment out of the game as I am doing so at the moment. I do not know if Cyan representatives read these reviews, but I will make a couple of what I hope are constructive criticisms for future games of this type.  These specifically apply to VR which, unfortunately, much as I would wish otherwise, a niche market. The photo note system is not as good as that in 'Obduction'. Some form of easily accessible virtual keyboard note system would be welcome, after all, it rather spoils things to have to take off your headset to check clues. This, of course does not apply to playing in flat screen. Also, perhaps some further thought into optimising frame rate with high quality graphics: this was well managed with 'Half Life: Alyx'. I leave this to the coders.As stated, these are meant as constructive criticisms. If you enjoy the adventure game genre, then you must try this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute masterpiece (pun intended) and I hope that everyone had as much fun as I did with this.I had played Riven The Sequel to Myst years ago on my PS3 using the PS1 disc back in 2012 since I had discovered Myst and was absolutely obsessed with it. I bought every game in the series on disc at the time.I even had them sent to my home under the name "The Stranger." XDI love the series and I hope we get a remake of III, IV, and V at some point, but I only want that to happen if they have the passion to do so. If they don't feel like it, that that makes sense.This game put into Real-Time graphics what I imagined it would look like with those pre-rendered pictures and FMV sequences. It is so detailed and runs very well on my computer.I think the eye/head tracking for the NPCs is especially astonishingly intimate and immersive. I personally don't mind the 3D NPCs because the look good to me.The ones in the newest iteration of Myst look very off, but these look totally fine to me.I love the environments and I believe the changes made here and there to the locales and puzzles alike are not just understandable, but welcome. It breathes fresh air into the remake while keeping enough of the old game to appease fans of the 1997 release.Please do yourself a favor and buy this game. I was lucky enough to get it for a discount upon a discount since I already owned the most recent Myst remake.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven was the first game I'd ever bought and it fostered a life-long love of puzzle games. The audio track still fills me with nostalgia and the steampunk / mechanical puzzle aesthetic is right up my alley. The Good:- Amazing graphics- The same atmospheric soundtrack- A fascinating world filled with puzzles and exploration.The Bad:- Game breaking VR bugs, I quickly had to switch to pancake as the VR is unplayable.- Poor optimisation leading to numerous stutters and texture popping. - I was sad that the characters had been replaced with CGI, I understand why it was done but it robbed the game of some of it's original charm.

_childDocuments_.review: "Riven" used to be my favourite game when I played it over 20 years ago and it has never given up that status. But also, since that very first day I wandered through the world (well "clicking through" really), I was hoping that one day I could explore the islands walking around. Over the last decade, I've been occasionally following the Starry Expanse project, who had the aim of creating a sort of "Real Riven", always hoping it would one day bring me that possibility. And so I was over the moon when the original developer, Cyan, joined to finish this project.To be honest, I would have been fine with a 1-to-1 remake of the original, but what Cyan have done here has exceeded my expectations. I have to admit that I haven't finished it yet, but every change I encountered so far has been interesting in a good way. And it is strangely satisfying to stand in front of a door I've easily opened about a hundred times before, only to find myself being stuck now due to a different puzzle setup.Most importantly, back before the year 2000 while playing the original game, I got this unbelievable feeling of immersion in a computer game world, something I have never experienced that much since then. "Myst III" and "Myst IV", as well as "Obduction" had some very good moments, "Schizm" as well despite some subpar live acting videos and animations, and I also enjoyed games like "The Witness" or "Quern" or the "Portal" or "Talos Principle" series, but nothing came even close to the atmosphere and world building of "Riven". Today, I finally got that feeling back and that was extremely cool!There is one negative point that I should mention and that is the character animations. I know they are pretty decent, but nothing replaces the real video footage of the orginal game for me. Especially the intro to the game is missing some "punch" or urgency that the original had. But that's really just a minor issue.All in all, thank you Cyan for giving me back this amazing feeling of being there. It was worth the wait and I'm excited to see what you do next!EDIT: I have now finished the game, so I thought I could update my review as well. I am still extremely happy with the new version of the game. The graphics, sounds and immersion have set a very high bar for other games. I want to slightly take back my criticism of the character animations. I got more into them as the game went on and they are pretty acceptable. Still not as good as live action footage, but ok. Unfortunately, they do lack a bit of punch and urgency not only at the beginning but also at the end and that's a shame. Maybe an update could fix that slightly. But as an unexpected further plus point, there are new areas that you weren't able to access in the old version of the game, and being allowed to experiencing them now was such a nice treat! Obviously, I wish the world was five times the size, I could wander around for many more hours just getting lost in the world.Without spoilering too much (so I'll stay vague), I briefly want to have a look at the two major puzzles in the game and assess their significantly reworked versions.1) "Animal" puzzle: I was a huge fan of the old version. I have to say, though, that the reworked version is the new standard for me here. The way it is presented makes so much more sense now with the backstory of the Moiety. It made me appreciate their entire lore so much more. And that's all done without sacrificing complexity while staying fair. Big thumbs up!2) "Marble" puzzle: There were aspects of the old version I liked, but some bits felt slightly obscure for the sake of making it harder. Like the other puzzle, the reworked version lets some aspects make more sense with the backstory. But the aspect of placing the marbles could have been kept closer to the previous version. I find this too easy and fast, leading to the slightly dissapointing fact that one spends relatively little time on one of the islands because there is no need to.But all negative sounding points I raised are so small in comparison to the positive outcomes out of this reworked version. All in all, in a game that values the story of the world probably higher than just presenting puzzles, the changes for me made me fall in love with the whole world even more. If I hadn't given a thumbs up to this during my first review after only an hour of play time, I would do so now!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I never expected to see a fully-3D Riven remake, not just because the game is massive compared to Myst, but because the original 1997 Riven is still possibly the best-looking pre-rendered adventure game of all time, outdoing even its own sequels for just how believable each of its scenes look. The first thing I did when I booted up this remake in VR was let my jaw hang in awe at just how perfectly the very first area matched the original Riven's opening image 1:1 while giving me the ability to fully explore it.I'm not exaggerating when I say Riven may be the most important VR game since HL: Alyx. You can play this flatly, but it feels like VR was made for Riven, and vice versa. Either way, the only thing you're missing out on by playing the remake over the original are the (IMO) stellar live-action performances by Rand Miller and the late John Keston. What you get instead is a chance to experience a dark, diabolical narrative set in an expertly-crafted world in a whole new light.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was obsessed with this game when it came out in the late 90s, this is a very worthy remake! It captures all of the world-building and realism of the original, but sands down some of its more maddening elements - as a result, the sequel is not necessarily easier than the original, but it's much less likely to trip you up for unnecessary reasons such as some tiny clue that you overlooked hours ago. I think it's the rare remake that can be considered superior to the original, not only in terms of visuals (of course), but also playability - and I hope it can inspire other future games in the genre of story-heavy puzzle adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a kid when I first played Riven. I was hooked for a long time, and the music stayed with me since then. I am now a father of 4, and when I started Riven remaster, it was the most beautiful slap in the face. So many memories came back at once. _childDocuments_.review: Visually gorgeous, fairly faithful to the vision of the original, I'd say most of the changes are for the better, not all, but mostly. _childDocuments_.review: It's undeniably wonderful to see one of the greatest puzzle games ever made get a modern update, but this version has a great many issues that would need to be resolved before I could recommend it without reservations. The first and most glaring issue is that almost nothing in the game is skippable, which is particularly bizarre when you consider that the original game, 27 years ago, allowed you to skip almost any animation, as the creators undoubtedly understood that even the most beautiful animation can be tedious after you've been forced to watch it 50 times. While there are specific settings that allow you to always skip ladder and vehicle animations, they don't cover the dozen other repetitive animations in the game, particularly anything involving the domes or the rotating room on Temple Island. This is even more annoying for the end credits, as if you get one of the "bad" endings and wish to restart, you're better off just hitting alt-F4, as pressing escape does nothing. Turning on ladder skips also always black-screens as it skips the animation, which I personally find kind of jarring.The game also just feels generally unfinished and lacking in polish, which is a bummer for such an incredibly gorgeous piece of art as Riven. A lot of the transition animations either prevent the camera from moving or move it in sudden and jarring ways, and the character animations feel particularly janky—doubly so for anything involving the characters' hands or facial animations, whether it's pages flapping around as Gehn flips through a book, or his glasses clipping through his hands as he sets them down on the table. The character models also feel weirdly low in detail compared to the rest of the world, especially for a modern game on a modern engine. The lack of polish in these areas really hurts the immersion, which I'd argue is an important element of the experience for a game like Riven. Despite running in a modern build of the Unreal Engine (which the game's marketing materials can't wait to remind you), you can't rebind the keys from the in-game menu, which as a left-handed person is just obnoxious. Engine performance is also inconsistent, often microstuttering at weird times. That would be a bigger issue if this were an action game, but it's still annoying.While I'm ultimately glad this remake got released, I really hope that it gets some patches to improve general polish and performance. It's a less consistent outing than I would expect from a legendary studio like Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I remember not playing Riven until after having finished Exile. I had played MYST endlessly through several platforms: PC, Sega Saturn, etc. And I knew there was a sequel, but for some reason, I assumed it was just a cash grabbing, bad sequel, since in my head, nothing could top the first one. So, I never gave it a chance. I remember almost buying it for the Playstation, but even then, I didn't. So, after having been floored by Exile, and buying a brand new PC to be able to run it, I decided to go out and get a copy of RIVEN, and so it began...how one game became my favorite of all time, in over 4 decades of playing video games. I've played it all. Throughout my time picking up every console, and trying out every kind of game, I always came back to the bright and sunny world of the Fifth age. And of course, having seen MYST get a "Masterpiece Edition", and a realMYST, and a realMYST Masterpiece edition...those of us who were fans of Cyan worlds waited patiently for a RIVEN remaster of some sort. But it never came. And then the people at the Starry Expanse gave a glimmer of hope, but without much official word that it might be completed, or that it might get "picked up" by Cyan. All hope was not lost, but it was also not confirmed. But it's finally here. So, as a long time MYST fan, what is my final word?: 1. It is NOT a 1:1 recreation of RIVEN, so don't expect that. It's not a "remaster", but it's also not a remake. Probably what you'll hear a lot is the comparison of Resident Evil and their remakes. It is essentially the same game, but almost as if it's an alternate version of it. This is a great thing, because it gives not only a fresh coat of high resolution paint to our beloved game, but it's also a horrible thing because it adds and subtracts things that we were expecting, that were familiar to us, that we wanted. It's almost exaclty equally a good and a bad thing.2. Puzzles are slightly reworked...for some reason. I guess to keep the theme of "not just a fresh coat of paint" going. At times though, I felt this was unnecessary. Sure, some changes are welcome, because of modern gaming standards, and because of the "friendliness" to VR that it has to have. But again, for those veterans like us, there's almost no way to see it as "contrived" at times. 3. Some puzzles are entirely different. Again, I appreciate the effort of introducing brand new things. But again, it made me have a feeling of unfamiliarity that was unwelcome. It felt like coming home, to what you thought was a remodeling of your home, but there's a couple of important things missing, and there's something things and objects that weren't yours and were just added to your house, and you have to keep them and live with it. It feels "intrusive". 4. I do appreciate them winking at us Veteran MYST players a lot, with some puzzles, with some trophies, with some "occurrences" in the game. There's some specific nods that only "we" will get. It's nice to know that this is not just a game for new people, but that those of us who have stuck around for 26 years waiting for a remaster/remake are being acknowledged.I have 2 "uglies": - The endless glitches. Sure, these will be patched, as so far at the time of this writing, I believe we're on patch #2. But man, at times it feels so rushed. Especially if you think about the timeline from when we heard from Starry Expanse that they might be headed in that direction, and now it's only been a couple of years. Makes you think that we'd rather have had more time polishing it, than rushing it out the door.- Going full cg rendering for the characters, instead of reworking, reutilizing the old live action. This is a straight up "no" for me. It did not land AT ALL for me. It gave me trauma from the MYST V days, and I was hoping never to feel that way again. It looks SO OUTDATED - I'm not exagerrating, it looks like from the mid 2000's kind of graphics - except with 2023 resolution. So, pretty much MYST V, played on a high end PC with max settings. Sure, I appreciate keeping a lot of the voice acting from the late John Keston and Sheila Gould. And while I do see it as a nice way to pay homage, I couldn't help but think that to some, the thought "they did them dirty" might come to mind. I didn't think it was disrespectful, but I thought they could have done something else. Maybe AI upscaled the old footage, I don't know - something. Something ELSE other than going full CG. But I'm not surprised that CYAN went in that direction. It's just disappointing. I thought there was a little hope, with OBDUCTION. but FIRMAMENT cemented that they'll probably never give us live action again. So, is this what we've all been waiting for? For the most part, "sure". I don't think anyone will come out actually disappointed in it. I know some of us were JUST expecting a remaster/rework of the old one since, especially going back to play it on a big, modern screen - we can definitely tell that the graphics, and the resolution does NOT hold up after all this time. So, while this is not our "chance" to play the old RIVEN but with a brand new 4K fresh coast of paint, it is a good re-imagining that preserves MOST of what we loved about it.I AM glad they didn't just "reboot" it, and completely changed everything about to make it unrecognizable. I have RIVEN on my computer, on my phone, on my tablet. And I play it every now and then and have been for 26 years. I show it to new people, and enjoy seeing them experience it for the first time. But it's such a deep foundation of my time spent with games, that it begs the question: Will this game replace my playing of the old game?Street Fighter II CE completely replaced playing World Warrior. UMK3 completely replaced playing MK3. Sonic 3&K completely replaced playing Sonic 3. While this game is beautiful for the most part, and gives us things we never saw before (like finally going inside of Tay, something we were never able to do, until that one guy made the interior of it on Dreams, in that video on youtube). For me, I will never get rid of RIVEN (97) and will go back and visit it at some point in the future.But there's no denying that this is great accomplishment in its own right.

_childDocuments_.review: I played myst and riven as a kid, and without internet it was one of the coolest games I've ever played.  I was probably 8 or 9.  I "beat them" using strategy guides back then.  Now I'm 37, and nostalgia is heavy for Riven, which was my favorite out of the two (it looked so real back then!). _childDocuments_.review: Following Myst (2021) i now also played through Riven for the first time. Again great story and visuals. Even a bit better than Myst imho. The world is beautiful. The game certainly bigger and longer. Somewhat harder puzzles. Partially. More polished, but still not perfect in controls and menues. You still have to do quite some backtracking and traversal is also still very slow. You wait a lot for animations to finish. To be honest i used a guide to point me into the right direction here and there to avoid running around for too long. Again there is quite some text to read and it would have been much less painful for me if it was not all in hard to read handwriting font.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I first played the original in 1997, and it immediately left a great impression on me. We now live in a time where a lot of people have a short attention span, and if you're one of them, this game may not for you. The world of Riven, a set of tropical islands with strange buildings and alien technologies, demands to be observed calmly to be understood, for its mysteries and puzzles to be solved. The goal? Save your friend's imprisoned wife from the evil clutches of an evil megalomaniac. No, there are no guns you can use. Your weapon? A book!This remake is simply wonderful, and I really hope that new players will give this a go! Yes, some of the puzzles may leave you confused at first, though they're all based in logic, and with such a loving community out there, all you need to do is ask for a hint, or get the guide book. Just try to allow yourself to be immersed in the world, and challenge yourself to figure it out for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's Riven. It's familiar yet some things are different. There is one change that I'm a bit unsure of given the implications on the lore. I had thought it different prior to playing the remake which has shown me something else on what the...thing...actually is and what it means.Still, it's worth a play for both those that have played Riven '97 before or are just jumping in fresh. For those that have played it before it does take rewiring your brain a bit. A few times I've got stuck on a puzzle to later find out I was doing things the old way from muscle memory. The remake shakes things up enough that old players will trip over themselves.In all, I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A reasonably faithful remaster of the original world, with enough changes to make it a new puzzle experience. The 3D actor replacements are good enough for VR at least, though the animation is a bit rough. Having played the original, the new puzzles slowed me down enough to get around 8 hours of play time, and I only got stuck once.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is a great game.This is not only from the game looking absolutely AMAZING but also how the world feels like it could be real. From the people (NOT the C.G.I ones) to the architecture and the world as a whole.Riven is also fun to just walk around and look at things, and maybe actually trying to Finnish the game every once in a while.Plus with the remaster some of the old puzzles were either moved, changed ,or in some cases I believe cut altogether. (But I could be wrong about that last bit.)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Looks fantastic!, plays very smooth and well optimized.What memories of my youth. Always checking with Dad to see what exciting and mysterious locations he came to. (Ohh dad a cable car, a mine cart that we can ride in) Wonderful memories :DNow let's see if I can complete it myself without hints and internet.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An utterly gorgeous recreation of a foundational classic - and one of my favourite games from my childhood! I still have my notebook from working through the original~ (Haven't had to use it yet!) >_> The remake offers a lot of quality of life improvements simply by its nature - smooth graphics and free movement are both more immersive and huge time-savers! I do miss the FMV, although the 3D recreations of the characters are quite well done. There seems to be a whole host of elements I don't remember - some of these are certainly new revisions, others I might just have forgotten about. (I did remember the place on Boiler Island (I guess they have names now?) where I was stuck forever originally though! Tricky door! >_<)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An ABSOLUTE TRIUMPH!!! The level of care and attention to detail put into this game is incredible--I am so grateful and relieved the team approached the redesign with the respect and care this sacred experience deserves. The original is an incredible achievement in of itself, and has a serious tone, but this redesign makes the game more colorful and fun.  It clarified and developed the larger concepts, but also smoothes out smaller experiences that were confusing or ambiguous in the original.  I loved learning more about the Rivenese culture in particular and also captures the spirit and visuals of the original. The main puzzles are a good mental exercise, but they are fair and quite fun.  I bought copies for friends.  THANK YOU THANK YOU CYAN!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Faithful, gorgeous, real-time 3D remake of Riven with some interesting twists added in. The culmination of everything The Starry Expanse Project hoped to achieve.Cons: There are several typos and a few bugs that currently still need to be worked out.EDIT: Since I wrote the interview, the DLC PDF typos I noticed have been corrected.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan really managed to re-capture the look and atmosphere of the original game, the textures look great, most of the sounds and music are identical, but that is certainly not a bad thing. Cyan, however, has chosen to make many changes to the game, and they end up as a bit of a mixed bag. I really appreciated them changing up the puzzles, even if some were a bit streamlined, but the addition of yet another number system feels like old hat at this point, they did it in the original game as well as Obduction, so I suppose it has become their gimmick. I also enjoyed the extra lore additions, like harvesting a fire marble, showing how Gehn went about making them for his own uses, and some other stuff I won't spoil here.The FMVs have been replaced with 3D actors which is of course understandable, and they look much, much better than what they did for the Myst remake which ultimately added an option to restore the old FMVs for that. The issue with the 3D models is the animation quality is not terrible, but also just not great, but at the end of the day this is a minor nitpick in a game where you interact with other characters only a select few times. Sadly, Cyan has repeated another shortcoming and left the keybinds unable to be rebound, also there's no indication in the default keys that pressing R is a very handy shortcut to bring up the Moiety lens, a tool you will often use, I happened to read that elsewhere. I was happy to see that you can set the cursor to automatically disappear when you're exploring and only appear when you want it to for interacting with things. All in all, it's a solid remake, it looks  great, but you may or may not like the changes they made if you're a big fan of the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A modern remake of a point-and-click adventure game close to my heart, it's faithful to the original from 1997, but with enough changes to keep it fresh and interesting (although whether it was  with a game that old, I'm not sure).The game looks as beautiful as it did back in the day, except this time it's not pre-rendered and runs in real-time. Unfortunately, I don't have the space for a VR setup, because I can only imagine what that would be like. By the time they remake Myst III: Exile, I should get that figured out. The Amateria ball puzzle would be amazing to see in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was and is a huge fan of the original Myst games, I can safely say that this remake is both true to the original and confidently unique from it. The two central puzzles (finding the Moiety, reaching the 233rd Age) are brilliantly reimagined while retaining the soul of the original puzzles. The art direction is remarkably faithful to the original; I frequently found myself experiencing deja vu. Occasionally there would be some distracting pop-in and weird animation issues, especially clipping and jerkiness with the human characters. But in the face of everything this game does well, these are minor complaints.I can't help but think this remake is the true realization of the creators' original vision. The 1997 version is undoubtedly a triumph in its own right, but this version is proof that the substance of the game is timeless. And it really is timeless; with its rich lore, challenging puzzles, delightful visuals and stellar sound design, Riven reasserts itself as a paragon of the puzzle game genre.Wow this reads like a game journalist review lol i just really love this game
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, good remake, they changed A LOT of things, new rooms, new puzzles (some good, some awful), new musics BUT you need a good gaming PC for the game.I can run the new 2021 MYST game perfectly on my couple of years old PC but not this one, it loads for around 1 min, sometimes I got to a area and watched many different “layers” load for 7+ seconds ruining the “feel” of the game, I had to refund, sorry I’ll play the 1997 version.Biggest gripe is some of the new puzzle, (the "space" linking dome) new puzzle breaks any "suspension of disbelief" of a possible real world from before strait into fantasy, and adding the new number "language puzzle" (yes a second one) is beyond ridiculous, and breaks the tone previously achieved.While other updated puzzle was nice, the throne room projector controls relocation, the fixed "under the door fiasco" and the contained new "space breach" where all very nice additions.It did not need to be so high in requirements for "top of the line graphics", leaving your older family PC out.  Command and Conquer Remastered made it work perfectly for everyone on any mid machine.I'll might give it a new try in many years, but for now I cannot give a positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who got deeeeeeply engrossed into the Myst universe in the late 90s, Riven was and remains one of my favourite video games of all time, CD-ROM swapping and all. More than just taking Myst and making it bigger/prettier, Riven had a uniquely anthropological element to it's storytelling and puzzle design that has made it stand out not just among the Myst games but within the genre as a whole - there's a wonderful immersive elegance to the idea that a major obstacle to your progress could be solved by a 5-year-old who lives in this world you've been dropped into.  Really my only knock against it was that it's postage stamp-sized resolution has done it's world building and its puzzle design poor justice as monitors have become ever larger and more pixel dense. Suffice to say, I've been dying for a remastered version for decades at this point - this remake was a day-one buy for me and I dived head-first into it. This is a heavy remix of the original's structure - the gorgeous locations all feel highly familiar and the story plays out in a near-identical way, but the puzzle alterations are substantial and will both keep you from speedrunning through based on your memories and completely alter your way of navigating the islands - entering the spinning domes for the first time was an especially big unexpected surprise. One thing I especially appreciate is how the Age of Riven now legitimately feels like it's falling apart - while in the original it's decay always seemed more like it was being told rather than shown, now you get to witness (or cause!) collapsing infrastructure and seismic activity that makes the whole experience feel substantially more precarious.The biggest complaint people have has generally been the CGI actors replacing the FMV. The models are... okay. They're not fantastic, but they're supposedly better than those in the Myst remake (which I've never played) and the complaints some have that they look PS2-quality are hyperbolic. The realities of a freeroaming world and up-to-4k resolutions unfortunately just make FMV impractical. An unfortunate change but the acting scenes in Riven are so infrequent it honestly doesn't bother me too much. Completing the game is also relatively quick, especially if you're familiar with the base structures of the original. Your old notes on Dni numbers and indigenous animals will still be vitally useful here, and while the puzzles are considerably different they're also IMO a bit easier. Altogether I was able to get one achievement short of platinum within about 10 hours. Nevertheless, it's absolutely wonderful to simply revisit this world 25+ years later with the expansive visual perspective the art design truly deserved from the beginning, so much so that the lack of a quick-travel zip mode barely even registers for me. For that alone it was well worth the purchase, and it's enough to make me want to dig up my copes of the extended-universe books again.Riven runs very well on the Deck and is perfectly playable, though it is sometimes a touch slow for textures to fully render in certain visually-dense areas. Some of the video effects for the Linking Book visuals also don't load.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Just binged the whole game. Had a big, stupid grin on my face the whole time. Loved all the changes they made to the puzzles; it felt like playing a whole new game in a deeply familiar setting. The new narrative, content, and extra areas they added all made it feel fresh and exciting to explore as well. Can not recommend this game enough to both fans of the original and the uninitiated alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This remake perfectly captures the feeling of playing the original Riven back in the 90s - both the joys and the frustrations. Playing the original now is rough because games have developed so much over the years, and that old interface (and the graphics which were once astonishing for the time) just haven't aged well. The remake is beautiful, controls well for the most part, and provides the same joy of discovery without the need to swap CDs every five minutes.One important tip: DO NOT RELY ON THE IN-GAME SCREENSHOTS TO TAKE YOUR NOTES. The screenshots are not of good enough quality and sometimes the information you need is not visible in them! I learned this the hard way at one of the final puzzles in the game. I'd taken screenshots of several things I knew for sure would be important, only to discover that the symbols I needed to see where not visible at all. I then had to spend ten minutes traveling back to the location I'd screenshotted to check the clues again. If you think something is important, WRITE IT DOWN IN A NOTEBOOK. It was disappointing to realize this potentially helpful feature wasn't really functional.The puzzles are for the most part not too difficult if you pay close attention and note down details in the environment. I'm not sure if this one is easier than the original or if I've just gotten a bit cleverer as I've aged, but I didn't need to consult any walkthroughs to get the best ending (whereas I relied on walkthroughs for pretty much the whole original game back when I was a teenager).Be prepared to be patient, however. Where the transport between areas was once a point to swap discs, now they are long cutscenes which I presume are used as fancy loading screens for each area. Riven is made to feel like a world you're actually inhabiting, which means there is no fast travel. If you forgot to write something down on the other end of the map, you'll just have to travel back there (although there are some settings which can reduce some of the animations, at least). Players used to modern games streamlining the process of getting around might be frustrated by this, so go into the game prepared for it.The only other disappointment I felt was in the character animations. I understand that using FMV wouldn't be an option for a remake of this style, and so 3D models were probably their only feasible option, but the animations for the characters are just awful, and not nearly as realistic as the environment surrounding them. Still, these are a very small part of the game, and hardly a deal breaker.Congratulations to the team who remade this classic game. I was ready to be disappointed, but you really nailed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Myst or any other other like games, Rivan doesn't disappoint. It is classic Cyan style game and for me, this is my jam. I love the mind bending puzzles, decoding languages, using inference and deduction to solve problems, having to stay on my toes to notice everything, document a scene, keep notes, dang! I love this cerebral kind of gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This remake completely exceeded my expectations of what a real-time remake of Riven could be.  Having waited decades for this day, it not only looks absolutely incredible, but plays better (and differently) than I expected.  The alterations to the flow and layout of the world are well considered and go a long way to providing a fresh experience for veteran players. I played through this game with my 11 year old niece and she was completely taken by the world, the puzzles, and the amazing attention to detail-- and I am grateful that this remake gave me an opportunity to share with her one of my favorite games in a cutting edge way.If there is a way to incorporate a "fast forward" function, similar to modern re-releases of classic RPG games, it would go a long way toward addressing my only minor frustration with the game-- the time waiting for some of the longer scene transitions, elevator rides, room rotations, etc to resolve.  They are incredibly well executed from an audio visual stand-point, but the 10th time you've seen it, you will be wishing for something like "zip mode" from the classic games or the aforementioned fast forward functionality.  To the team at Cyan-- absolutely incredible work.  It was worth the wait, more so than I could have anticipated.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Dream come true, as someone who's been into the Myst series ever since I was a kid.The thing with this game is I would've been completely content with a 1:1 remake of Riven, if it meant I could play it in VR. Not only do I get to play Riven in VR, but they went above and beyond with the changes and new content they've added.Kudos to The Starry Expanse Project and Cyan themselves for a decade's worth of dedication and effort in making this possible. This is now my favorite VR title.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely beautiful game. It has such an atmosphere that's hard to describe but so wonderfully present everywhere in the game. I love that the game is very deliberately paced. And the architecture is so intriguing and upfront! 9/10.My only gripe is a functional one - you can't rebind keys, and I'm a WERD player instead of WASD. It's very easily fixed by using the Keyboard Manager in Microsoft's PowerToys, so you can hard-rebind keys while playing the game.Once again, a masterpiece. I'm thankful for Cyan's revival.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The team somehow managed to capture the feeling of playing it again for the first time. What an amazing job they did on this remake. The lore feels rich and immersive, and the puzzles are fresh and exciting. If you played the original, there are little easter eggs all over for you to appreciate, but the game stands well alone by itself as well so if you have never played a Myst game before, you can still jump in and enjoy all Riven has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful in VR, if very demanding. Turn off DLSS (or it will be blurry) and check the comfort settings before you start.I've replayed MYST too often, but never Riven. I remember so little of it. It's wonderful to experience the world as a real space. Everything makes a lot more sense. Controls are a little fussy, like grabbing and turning things, turning book pages. Books: Hold it with one hand. With the other hand, point at the edge of the open book - right at the stacked pages - until that hand turns red, then grab and drag all the way to the other side of the book.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Cyan or have never heard of Myst or any of the titles Cyan has created, the Riven remake is wonderful. There are things that have been expounded on that make the game that much sweeter from it's original in 97. I look to see Cyan address some of the graphic issues as they always have to polish Riven to a high gloss. Relax and play within worlds you can never quite forget. The sun always shines in Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan did it! They made a remake of the best puzzle game ever and one of my favourite games of all time, and made it even better. Riven remake is a perfect example of how to improve on an already great original, staying true to old fans while capturing new ones. Since I've played through the original several times I thought this was going to be a great nostalgic time experiencing the world in 3D, otherwise just running through the puzzles, but what a pleasant surprise I was in for. Do yourself a favour and get lost in one of the most captivating game worlds there ever was.Thank you Cyan!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I'm biased. The original Riven is my favorite game of all time and I am a huge fan of Myst to an arguably unhealthy degree. That being said, this remake is so good. I'll not pretend it's perfect, but I must say the original isn't perfect either, and without nitpicking small problems I'd say this is overall a very faithful, and very well done remake of the 1997 original.The rest of the review I'm going to focus on the technical parts of this game, particularly some issues I had, but suffice it to say that I think Riven continues to have one of the best stories in gaming, and I think the modifications they made to the story and puzzles were exciting and generally well done. I would have liked even more expansions in certain areas, but I suppose I musn't be greedy.Now, I just finished my first playthrough, which I did in VR using a Valve Index and I do feel it's important to mention a few issues. First off, this is an Unreal Engine game, which if you've had the experiences I've had should be sounding alarm bells and, sadly yes, there are numerous visual glitches in VR that seem to be unfixable. Thankfully there are relatively few effects and random objects that render differently in each eye, but this game is rather plagued by LOD pop-in and shadows shimmering in and out of existence (and do yourself a favor and put shadows to low in VR, since any higher the shadows get REALLY glitchy), as well as stuttery animations. I don't blame Cyan for this since it's very rare that I've played an Unreal Engine VR game that didn't have major problems, so I assume it to be largely a problem with the engine (and I much rather prefer UE in general to Unity). VR performance is also pretty terrible, again I blame this more on Unreal.Outside of VR issues I'm sad to say Cyan is still making heavy use of screenspace effects, and so far I don't think there's any confirmation it will be getting an RTX patch like the recent Myst remake did. From what I've played of the flatscreen version it doesn't seem as bad as, say, Obduction's implementation, but it's still a notable rough spot on an otherwise amazing looking game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven 2024 is somehow just as incredible and engaging as it was 27 years ago. The things that are new and different almost universally fit as if they had been there all these years, while making it a fresh experience for someone like me who already remembers the puzzle solutions from the original. It looks amazing, it  right, and it all comes together to make an incredibly exciting game to play. If you loved the original, this will be as close as you could ever get to getting to re-experience it for the first time.The only thing that doesn't quite compare to the original is the character art and animation, but you're kind of in an impossible situation there. The FMV from the original game can't just be brought over, but you also can't get the kind of fidelity you'd need to rival FMV from 3D characters without an obscene budget and an army of people.My one and only actual complaint, which is present in the original game as well, is story-related. I have loved Riven for most of my life. It made a huge impact on me growing up, and stands out to me as the best of the Myst series. Riven 2024 lives up to that, and in my view stands side by side with the original as two of the best adventure games ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven is probably my number one game of all time. It impacted me greatly as a teen back in the late 90s and is one of the biggest influences on my entering the game development field myself. To have Myst and now Riven, both so influential memories of my childhood, be remade so excellently has been a dream come true. I've had so much fun playing both Myst and now Riven with my children, going back through memory lane but also giddy in excitement at the changes that have been made and the new puzzles and clues to discover!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The original Riven was *not* a short game for me, and I have put off replaying it for many years. This masterful remake not only brings the Fifth Age to life with modern graphics, it also ties the islands together in a way that provides a sense of spacing and scale that the 2D renderings of the original release could never quite convey. I'm actually exploring -- not getting lost, not clicking randomly hoping to find a path or stumble on a clue. As frustrating as it was, I remember my first playthrough fondly: this release has made my second playthrough perhaps just as memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Lousy remakes that overpromise and underdeliver are a dime a dozen these days. Unlike those, *this* is how you remake your game. Bluntly speaking, other than one or two nitpicks about the intro, this is an upgrade to every part of the game in nearly every way. Moving through Riven had me asking myself if it was a fever dream, so many areas are the spitting image of the 2D slides of the original, and clearly much thought and effort went into translating everything into a real 3D space. Not to mention the sheer number of revisions for lore accuracy and realism/immersion, and the expansion of underdeveloped parts of the story.And it released stable and mostly bug free, not to mention decently well optimized. I've played nearly every game Cyan has put out and own multiple copies of several, including physicals from decades ago, and this one is a big winner. You guys improved the masterpiece, and it was probably the closest I'll ever get to playing Riven again for the first time. Thank you for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: What a treat to get to play Riven again! I think I bought my first computer to play that game in 1998! And, in 3D! I would rate Riven as one of the best video game stories ever written. And I've beat hundreds of games. Here's my list of best stories ever: Batman Arkam Knight, Outer Wilds, Riven, Planescape Torment,  Tides of Numenera, Myst 4, Mass Effect 2, LA Noire, Portal 2.  In this remake I really missed the live action though, but it'll keep me buying the next version in 2050 lol (fingers crossed). I liked the new puzzles a lot, and they sorted out some loose ends in the story that I had trouble with understanding. Hard to believe that the graphics in this new version are even better than the images in the original game. Time heals all video game limitations :) Thanks Rand, Robyn, and team!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a new game, not just Riven with a fresh coat of paint. The puzzles are different, with old ones now offering interesting new solutions. Entire areas have been moved and redesigned with completely new architecture. It's more complicated and complex than before, featuring entirely new mechanics and mind-blowing areas never seen before.This is a remake of the 1997 PC game, Riven, now made in the Unreal engine. The characters are now 3D modeled instead of live-action cutscenes. While the performances are a little flatter than the original, the overall experience is incredibly immersive. It is very much in spirit the old Riven we were all captivated by.It took me three years of playing off and on without a walkthrough to finally beat it, and I can proudly say I did it without any help. Now, I'm ready to tackle it again. Get this game only if you enjoy exploring and solving puzzles. There are no monsters to slay—just you, a dark room, and a notepad. Prepare yourself, For this game is much deeper than it appears,To the developers: Thank you so much for all your hard work. This game is my favorite puzzle game ever made, and you all did it justice.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful to the source while still feeling fresh. I was worried at first this would be a tedious retread of what I already knew, but things have changed in this Riven, and discovering its secrets was genuinely thrilling at every breakthrough. It's like revisiting a place in your dreams, knowing it's different to the last time. I thought Myst III was my favourite in the series, and Riven would remain that haunting, elusive, 5-CD labyrinth from my childhood. The deeper into this Riven I have gone though, the more I'm convinced it hasn't been topped, much as I still love Myst III. The aesthetics of the design, the music, and the gorgeous visuals are absolutely iconic, and unravelling mystery upon mystery is immensely satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible remake. Expands on the original in thoughtful and surprising ways while always respecting the tone and authenticity of the world. The puzzles are cleverly changed and all the additions and alterations work together to improve the game and flesh out the lore.The animated characters and some visual areas of the game are not executed as well as the original, but these are minor shortcomings in what is one of the best remakes I've ever played. If you love the original you'll love this, and if you're new, you're in for an amazing journey through one of the most compelling and well crafted game worlds ever created.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It is a master piece in environmental puzzle.  Played the original when I was younger a long time ago and it still hold up to the memory.  Puzzle have a different solution and some puzzle have been greatly improve.  The notebook is a great addition in those kind of game put accessing it via the pause menu takes time. I would suggest playing with a pen and paper along side. It is not mandatory to have played the original Myst but I would strongly suggest playing it before.   It gives explanation and is a good introduction to the kind of puzzle.  I would strongly recommend.  Be patient with it and don't fear to  look at hint or the original but try to avoid spoiling yourself the solution to puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I was curious to see how much better Riven could be with a powerful PC driving it (13900 and RTX4080).  Since it was already attached, I first tried Riven with my Oculus Rift S, and while it was certainly better than the Quest version it was still lacking that “knockout punch” to set itself apart from recent competition in the VR space.  Most of the technical issues were eliminated or reduced playing with the SteamVR version, but I had forgotten about the Rift’s screen door effect that was blatantly obvious given the generally flat shaded nature of Riven’s art in VR.  Switching back to my Quest 3 and using Steam Link to wirelessly connect to my PC offered me the best possible results of all my VR solutions, giving me stable technical performance and the best color and visual clarity.  I was shocked at just how different the same game looked and played on the same headset based on which version/store it was purchased.Unknowingly, throughout all my testing I had been slowly getting better and better quality, but when I stowed the goggles and sat back to enjoy the game on a 77” OLED in full 4K it was like stepping into a new world.  As transformative as experiencing Riven in VR can be, playing it on a high-end PC at full Epic settings in 4K is often beyond words and even screenshots.  What we all thought was photo-real back in 1997 was just a hint at the expansive 3D island chain Cyan Worlds has created today using Unreal 5; while not even tapping into the advanced feature set you would expect for an outdoorsy game such as this.  Seeing Riven running all-out can easily bring tears to your eyes – or maybe that’s me just not blinking – but rest assured this is not your dad’s (or granddad’s) Riven.Read full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake of the original, keeps the aesthetic and feeling of the original intact whilst altering some of the more tedious puzzles. You can argue that it has become too easy in some places, but as someone who got stuck on the original for years before completing it I found the changes acceptable. Not too much in terms of new lore or events, all the story beats are the same with little additions and side areas to expanded their environments out a bit more. Overall I highly recommend it if you like the original or even if you just like how it looks
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Still the same great story as when I played though the original way back when. If you like puzzle games with a bit of mystery and stunning visuals, you'll love this remake. If you played the original this will still offer some challenge as many of the puzzles have been changed/reworked. It's good to be back!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Riven on launch in 1997. Like Myst, the world built by the team at Cyan has always stayed with me. A fantastical and tangible place that no game has really managed to create since. Both Myst and Riven truly are masterpieces, a word that is now sadly over used.At the time my friends and I dreamed of being able to actually walk around the world of Riven in real-time. Just imagine if this incredible world could be explored like other 3D games?Well here we are, 27 years later, and it has absolutely been worth every year I've had to wait.This Riven remaster has absolutely shattered, and I mean SHATTERED, my expectations. It's utterly captivating and mesmerising. The puzzles are more accessible and I just love being in the world.I hope the team at Cyan get the opportunity to release Myst again using all the UE5 technology on display in Riven. I also hope that Exile gets this treatment as well. I feel so fortunate to be able to explore this world with the graphics I always imagined would be impossible. It's truly wonderful to be alive and to be a gamer right now. THANK YOU Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2:  The crash in the submarine when playing VR seems to be fixed!EDIT 1:  Looks like a lot of heart is going into the updates and there may be a fix in the latest patch for the VR crashes I was experiencing.  I haven't had a chance to review it yet, but will change this to positive with the hope that it is indeed fixed.===== ORIGINAL POST ====My time is precious.  In fact, everyone's is.  That's why when I sit down for an hour or two to play a game on the weekend, it needs to just work.THIS game crashes in VR a lot.  Especially when using the submarine, but it has happened to me in other places as well.  It's just super reproducible in the submarine.  What do you have to do a lot when a game is crashing?  Re-load the game.  That brings me to my second point... the load time is way too long.  Probably 50% of that is just sitting and waiting for the Cyan logo / animation to finish.  How is that not skippable?  Any time that is not spent loading should be skippable!Aside from crashes, the VR performance is a C+ at best.  Lots of stutter, pop-in, and weird shadow effects.  I'm on a 3080 with 64 gigs of ram, Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700K CPU @ 4.00GHz  ....  Should be fine.Other than that my other gripes are that this is mostly just a port.  There's none of the things you expect in VR like hand interactions (they just move through everything)... no full body support ... no physics interactions etc.Lastly, from a perspective there are a lot of rough edges.  Music transitions are abrupt.  Not enough music and ambient noise to build atmosphere.  On the plus side the graphics are good, the puzzles are fun, and of course the story is interesting.I should add that I fully understand that this is a small team and frankly, this would be a positive review if it weren't for the crashes.  It's just that even with a positive review, there would be some negatives that I listed above.  All in all, I appreciate that the game was made and will change this to a positive review if the VR crashes are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This has been an amazing remake, and one that definitely encapsulates what I imagined Riven to look like in the 90s. They didn't forget their original fans either, as puzzles solutions are randomized for each playthrough.The only downside is that, like the Myst remake, 3D characters aren't quite "there" yet. Compared to the real-life acting of the original FMVs, the 3D counterparts are stiff and jerky, like a first-pass motion capture, with very little facial expression. But don't let that subtract from the absolutely beautiful scenery, literal world-encompassing puzzles, and mountains of lore.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: While the overall experience is certainly different and less difficult than the original, a lot of these changes are welcome for folks who may just want to enjoy a game rather than spend hundreds of hours blocked due to one missed detail. When I originally played Riven, I got completely stuck for years due to not knowing that the lights could be turned on in the cave on your way to Tay, I don't think most other folks would be patient enough to work through that or the incredibly difficult animal sound puzzle that was in the original. Both have been made far easier to deal with.There's still a lot of instability on this release, assets not loading in on time and crashes were abundant, but autosave was effective and I didn't lose any progress due to those issues. I'd really hope they resolve these problems in a few patches over the next couple of months.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: 'Riven has seen Cyan Worlds use what is possible with current day tech to give their classic title from 1997 a new lease of life, and they have done this successfully again following the same treatment being given to Myst in 2021. Bringing it with it some of the most challenging puzzles I have ever faced, which are designed perfectly for both flastscreen and Virtual Reality. With the world of Riven looking truly stunning and a pleasure to explore as you work out the puzzles. Cyan Worlds are doing great with bringing the best and most taxing puzzle games to VR. Where the puzzles do get difficult, when you solve them you see how fantastically they are designed, for this reason any puzzle game fans should add Riven to their library as soon as possible.'Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: Astonishing remake - unfortunately my exploratory needs have not yet been satisfied - I need more!!!The music is awesome and sucks you right into the game, same goes for the 3D graphics that look amazing, especially the water, plants and insects. You really feel like you have been transported into the game. I loved every minute of it.The puzzles are solvable without help, although I had to use some time of thinking in between and some solutions or progressions didn't come to my mind easily, but thats just how it should be!Also the 3D Models look much better than in the Myst Remake. What I didn't like so much are the Domes that take a long time to  each time. Other than that everything was bug free and a real Masterpiece once again. I made a terrible mistake at the last big puzzle that had me go a little crazy looking for hidden levers here and there, until I figured out that my notes haven't been correct at some point earlier, but as in every Cyan Game: Don't give up guys. The ending is worth it! I loved the Looking forward for the next VR Remake or maybe even a new Age..? ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: i played Riven when it first came out, so of course I thought I knew how to solve this version.  Wrong!  This game is enough like the original to be warmly familiar, but the differences are quite welcome.  I played  without any glitches and only saw a few graphic artifacts.  I don't ever expect a game to be perfect, but I do expect the immersion to be maintained.  I really enjoyed this game, I want to spend more time there.  Well done Cyan.  Thank you for having such integrity.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing but improvements over the original; the only gripe I have is sometimes unreal will fail to load something like an onclick event (ladder near the town dock being the biggest problem) or inventory item (frequently prison book, infrequently moiety lens), and if you pass up the first "you first" prison book encounter and go back for the second, the window / click event is misaligned. Otherwise, fantastic job modernizing; I look forward to seeing what modders do to tighten up the character models a hair over the next couple years.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but I wouldn't buy it for the VR. They use the continuous smooth movement technique that makes it prime for VR sickness and some of the VR controls are clunky. I still can't figure out how to turn pages in the book in my satchel.With a keyboard and mouse its great. Visuals are very good, and its Riven so its fun
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing Riven as a kid and be absolutely mesmerized by the travel cut scenes between islands. Nothing came close to that back then. This new version is a great trip down memory lane, but felt a lot easier and shorter. Maybe it's because I did not know English at all back then and could not read anything? Still, I am very happy to have experienced this masterpiece one more time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

It's perfectly playable, but there are some frame rate issues. This has the same weird shadow issue as Firmament. It looked blurry at first, but setting AA to low and DLSS off made it better. People say you can turn off AA with a file edit that I haven't tried. About the game, it's like Myst. Pretty cryptic, and you'll get stuck sometimes.
