_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake of the original game from 1997. This isn't a 1 to 1 remaster, but rather Cyan decided to go full 3D and include a decent VR mode as well. Additionally they decided to replace or reconfigure puzzles so even for old fans there will be surprises. Also randomization is built in so there is replay value.Difficult puzzle game especially if you haven't tried anything in the Myst series before. It is ok to look for hints, I know I did.Some tips: Use ingame screenshots for note taking (press X on keyboard), and if you're on keyboard pressing R will bring the most recent inventory item back to your hands. I wish I knew that during my first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible remake for new and old fans alike. The refactored puzzles were an absolute thrill to work through, journal and pen in hands, just like the original. The best part is (minor) lore changes and additions which makes the islands feel more lived in and practical. And then there's the new fanservice for die-hard Myst fans. I wish series like Zelda could pay off like Myst has over the years.10/10 and I haven't even tried VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A mesmerizing and beautiful game. More of an adventure than a puzzle game but the way it culminates at the end is a fantastic puzzle. The way they translated the prerendered and 90's art aesthetic to Unreal 5 is fantastic. The art is quite timeless and imo much more interesting and unique than what we have seen recently from Cyan and other modern games.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having an absolute blast, but I took a break to come and report that Riven is great in VR on the Valve Index. I have wanted to play a Cyan game in VR for a long time, but the last few VR games they released had critical, game breaking flaws on the Index. I haven't been able to find any here, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I deliberated a lot before choosing 'no'. In the end, I decided that what I have to say would be more useful to someone checking why they might NOT enjoy it.Riven, even in its 2024 incarnation, is like a really old, really good, really old movie. Something with Gene Hackman and lots of saxophone and brushed hi-hats. The kind of movie where maybe three things happen over the course of two and a half hours. It's been remastered in 4K Dolby Atmos, but at the end of the day it's still two and a half hours of Gene Hackman.Aesthetically, it's delicious. It has that balmy Mediterranean ambience that I loved in AC: Odyssey and ICO, and it's a really nice place to spend time. The writing and story is excellent, it's woven into the world and presented from different perspectives most effectively. If you're here for the story and want to pore over journals and really look at the world and think about what it's telling you about that story, you're going to love it. I should imagine it's also a wonderful VR experience if you are so equipped.On the other hand, if you're looking for another Talos Principle or The Witness - if you're looking for an actual puzzle game - maybe wait until there's a sale. There are relatively few true puzzles in Riven; often the 'puzzle' is realising that there's another way you can exit an area, or looking around for the one button/lever/wheel to progress. There are only two puzzles worthy of the name, and they're so much more spread out and difficult than the rest that it can feel like hitting a wall. Compared to the best examples of, say, web-based point-and-click adventures over the last decade, Riven felt a bit thin.Also - guys, we're nearly a quarter of the way through the century, and I'm not getting any less left-handed as time passes. Where the hell is my key rebinding screen?Minor gripes: while there's superb art direction and the expected Unreal Engine prettiness, and movement is probably as free as one could hope for a game gated behind interaction animations, the interface is distractingly janky. You'll often find yourself having to move in order to access your satchel inventory without it clipping into scenery, and your Notebook (where screenshots are kept) is inexplicably relegated to the system menu rather than being present in game.In conclusion: I did enjoy Riven, at full price - but as a very pretty narrative walking simulator with extra steps. If that sounds good to you, and you don't mind arthritis if you're left-handed, you'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I feel I need to leave a comment or two. This was gorgeous, it was as thrilling as the OG hardcore forebear. I decided to play through in desktop mode first to feel the vibe. I had taken extensive notes on the first one, and they came in somewhat handy overall. But things are randomized in this one with each play through and slightly different, so it takes as much exploration and observation as before. The previous lore helps for sure, but this seems so much more immersive. I looked forward to the casual reading and note taking (mostly screenshots via X key which are super duper useful and save so much note paper lol). It's so smoothly usable, as to almost not require many notes at all, just a good memory. It ran flawlessly for me in 4k with zero hitching, everything set to epic. My next quest will be playing through again in VR. If you have an attention span, and like a mental challenge get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this by saying that this game is not for everybody. It's incredibly difficult and takes a lot of patience. I got stuck tons of times, many of which had the solution right under my nose. That being said, this game is one of my favorites of all time. The world-building and artistic style of this game is one of the best i've ever seen, the puzzles are incredibly satisfying to solve, and, while i found the ending a little lackluster, the story is overall really engaging. By the end of this game, I had multiple pages of notes in an actual notebook written down, and that type of engagement in a puzzle game is not something I've experienced since playing the original MYST. This remake makes a lot of changes to the original, and every single one is for the better.TLDR: If you think you're up to the challenge, you should absolutely play this game, it's worth all the time it takes.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be honest - this game needed more time in the oven. Why it didn't get it is beyond my understanding. Riven was fine. Some fans wanted to do their own remake. Then Cyan swooped in, announced an official remake, and it was out within a year. For VR, even!So positives first, the puzzle and level redesigns are mostly great. Some even lend more context to the story. I love that! And of course the environment is beautiful. I absolutely love the quality put into the journals, though a few of the rewrites and additions are a bit silly to me and use phrases I'm not sure these characters should be familiar with.There are a lot of little things that are distracting. Goofy animations in places, weird timing. Pop-in. Bad looking character shadows. Robotic faces at times, and glowing white eyes on the characters. The huts seem really tiny now.Which brings us to VR. It's clear that a few things have been redesigned to accomodate VR, which is fine, but they didn't even implement it well. None of the VR interactions give any sense of the friction or weight of the levers and buttons. Everything in VR feels really small too, like they need to scale it up and run a separate iteration of the game FOR VR instead of plopping a camera into the 2D one and giving you hands that are about as functional as a regular mouse cursor. It was immediately disappointing to me. That, and it performed so poorly on Quest 3 (where I originally purchased it) that I refunded the game and had to switch to the flat version on PC.All gripes aside, I'm glad they took another pass over Riven and found some new inspiration for it. I hope they make more games in this universe, honestly, and take more risks. But I want higher quality out the gate. Make us wait. Take your time. And consider re-approaching FMV again. Myst V and 7th Guest VR are good examples of what I'd prefer to see. Even Obduction was preferable to the jank on display here (honors to the work on Gehn, though. Well done there.)At the end of the day, I had to fill a full page of a physical notebook with diagrams and symbols and backtrack a bunch to beat a video game in 2024, and that's a damn good feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As an absolute die-hard Riven (1997) fan, I was equal parts thrilled and skeptical of a remake, but Cyan absolutely delivered. They managed to take a remarkably believable (albeit fantastical) puzzle world and make it somehow even more grounded in its own lore, adding attention to details and fixing inconsistencies that I hadn't even considered before. Fans of Riven absolutely owe it to themselves to check out this version. Even if you have the original entirely committed to memory, you will very quickly find that there is more to dig into here.For new players... I suspect it's probably a touch easier than the original? I think there are accidental shortcuts to solving a couple mysteries thanks to some interface changes, and some of the altered puzzles seem a bit more straightforward. But considering that the original was among the hardest games in its genre, that's perhaps for the best. The essence of Riven is still alive and well as ever--there are really only about two real puzzles in the game, but understanding what they are, where they are, and how to solve them requires piecing together information from across the entire game world. Not many games have even tried a design like that, let alone succeeded so well.Sorry about the bridge, I didn't know that would happen. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: "I wanted a life full of magic, full of books that bridged worlds, that lit up the darkness like stars." As someone who has a lot of very fond memories of playing the original Riven, I admit was a bit sceptical when I heard that a remake was in the works. This was completely unwarranted - I had a wonderful time playing this new version. <3It made me feel both nostalgic through the beautiful reimagining of the old and excited and happy about the discoveries of the new. The only thing I missed a little were the awesome FMV performances from the original, but I realize that they would not have been possible to integrate seamlessly into this version. To the team at Cyan - thank you so much for all the good times, then and now.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a newcomer to the Myst series or a returning veteran, this remake is 100% worth your time and money.I have seen many reviews and comments saying that it does not have the same vibe as the OG Riven, or that the puzzles are easier.  I really disagree and I will explain why.After beating this remake, I went back and played through the original. I beat both without any hints or guides.It is my honest opinion, after having played through both within the past 2 days, that the Remake is the superior version.The OG Riven has its charm of course, but the remake allows you to see the world in a whole new way.  For one, the remake is clearly very good looking.  The graphics are crisp and nice to look at. The original environment has been recreated wonderfully with some interesting changes that you might not even really notice at first until you go back and play the original.I disagree that the puzzles are easier.  This is simply not true in my opinion.There are new and remixed puzzles to be found, and I think they provide more gameplay opportunities and provoke more thought, whereas, the original Riven has less of these factors and you really spend most of your time trying to figure out a couple of the games biggest puzzles/mystery's. While this is also true for the remake, there are more working parts contributing to the bigger puzzle, in a way that is more interactive for the player.In both versions, you must use acute observation and thinking outside the box to reach the answer, but it is done in a more interactive way in the remake, which I really liked.They have added   I believe the addition of this actually makes this puzzle on par in difficulty, if not more difficult than the same puzzle from the OG game.There is also The  is similar but it has also been changed up a bit to keep you on your toes.  You will have to think outside the box, just like the OG version. I thought I had this easily figured out and then got stumped for a bit, had to backtrack and re observe older areas, to figure it out.All in all, as far as puzzles go, they did a really good job here keeping the original ones as well as spicing them up, and adding new ones to keep returning players still wondering exactly what to do. I didnt find them to be easy at all.  I think people forget that the first time they played Riven, they were a little kid, and now they are adults, and their observational and critical thinking skills are undoubtedly superior now compared to when they played the game the first time. Lastly,  they have added some new areas, you can see and explore the Island of Riven in a new way and see some different areas and angles that you never got to see before.  Most importantly, you can now explore more of the They also still have the hallmark of a lot of the things you loved about Riven originally, such as the music and dialogue, the animals and creatures, etc.  You will feel at home. Give this remake a chance.  This is truly a wonderful remake and I recommend it to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful to the original while still feeling fresh at the same time. Beautiful game, stunning visuals and brilliant music and sound, it's a wonderful experience, in my opinion only improving on the original, not taking away from it in any way. I will always still love the original game but this is now the best way to experience Riven by far. Simply beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cons: 1. The 3D models are better than Myst (2021), but still take away from the experience.2. Concessions made for VR makes some areas feel flat/odd. (Tram rides)3. Optimization needed to smooth out some stuttering, but this will likely be fixed in updates4. Some achievements seem to be bugged. Again, will be fixed in an update.5. New music from Robyn Miller is good, but feels out of place. Pros:1. Faithful recreation of the original game’s art that is mind blowing.2. Music and voice direction still incredible.3. Any changes to the game are all well thought out and make for a surprising and engaging experience even for someone who has played the old game every year since 1997.Riven is my favorite game of all time. I played Myst at the age of 5 and followed it up with Riven when I was 8. No other piece of media has shaped who I am so completely than Riven. The prospects of a remake had been very interesting to me for over a decade but ultimately I viewed as an inevitable disappointment.I stand corrected. Riven (2024) is the modern (pre/post-Obduction) Cyan Worlds magnum opus. Not only is it a faithful recreation of the spirit of Riven, but also changes the game to always be surprising for the seasoned player and ever engaging for the transition to 3D.Is it perfect? No. But after the disappointment of Firmament (the gameplay, not the art or story) I was ready to also be dissatisfied in this. The first images of the new 3D models were disheartening, and in the final game they still aren’t great, but far better than the similar attempt for Myst (2021). Other downsides are some of the new compositions by the great Robyn Miller which is great music, but sounds more like cut tracks from Obduction rather than for Riven.Riven (2024) is a triumph. It might not hold a candle to original which is still so very special to me, it displays that Cyan has what it takes to navigate into the future. Possibly with new Myst games as teased years prior.Final Thoughts: would like to see the lighting “unlocked” or something to see some of these areas at night or at afternoon. The decision to bake in the lighting makes sense to keep the Riven vibe, but it would be cool have like a “sandbox” version of the Riven environment to play with lighting and potentially weather. I know it isn’t “realRiven” but could be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Coherent story line which encourages one to move on and adventure - the story line occupies the mind and draws you into the story as you observe and solve puzzles.Good nonlinear game play.Similar to but different from the previous Riven - greatly enjoyed both.Not a great fan of using plural pronouns when the singular is meant.Waiting for the next in the series ........
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: horrific quest 3 implementation:-each eye has a different lighting / scene, resulting in a dizzying display of two images trying to display at once...motion sickness extreme.-incredibly low resolution graphics. i am running a 4090, and cannot look at anything more than 5ft away, resulting in 90s level renderings-abysmal frameratesi keep waiting for the community to mod / patch this, because the developer obviously could not be bothered to support the most basic and common PCVR HMD in 2024
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible re-imagining of a classic game. This game came out the year I was born, so it's safe to say that I knew exactly how long we've been waiting to see it come back again. Cyan, you've knocked it out of the park. Not only did you remake the game, you changed the way some things are done in order to subvert the expectations of those who are veterans to the experience. It didn't take me as long as I figured it'll take most, but I will say that is in large part to having recently played the original experience and carrying over knowledge. I had such a blast playing this, and my favorite part still remains the tram rides. Looking forward to whatever comes next from your team.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. I'm a huge fan of escape rooms in real life, and this game is essentially several immersive digital escape rooms tied together, with deep lore and much exploring/learning required!I haven't played Myst (yet), so I came in with zero context for the lore/game mechanics. It was NOT easy, which is honestly exactly what I was hoping for!  There's zero tutorial, zero explanation of how things work, and zero apologies for being so difficult. This makes solving puzzles that much more exciting and satisfying. It also makes getting stumped that much more frustrating... but worth it in the end! If you're like me, you want to do the entire thing with absolutely zero walkthrough support. I made it through 96% of the game without looking anything up, but there were 2 things that had me genuinely confused... which I won't spoil... but both were near the end, and I was glad to find out I was actually on the right track anyway! I finished in about 22 hours, and I honestly feel quite proud of myself!All that to say, this is definitely "Type 2 Fun." Not a casual game, and not stimulating in the typical flashing-lights-moving-pictures type of way, but deeply fascinating and intriguing for curious and determined minds. And loads of "fun" in that sense! Don't give up! And good luck :)
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely wonderful. Changes plenty of puzzles yet still keeps the core intact, this reads as an alternate universe version of Riven, and it's most welcome. Before I get into anything, I highly recommend this game, I had a fantastic time unlocking this puzzle box and seeing where the unique concepts of Myst were expanded.There are some problems sadly. The game hitches in a handful of sections on my very high end rig, and it's always the same locations. Pop in on the trams is pretty rough. most times an animated character interacts with an object, it visually breaks in some pretty rough ways. Lip sync is non existent and the 3d characters look so utterly uncanny I deeply wish they kept cutscene control out of the player's hands just so we could have an option to reinsert the original live action performances cut out and put into the game, even at a low res. I had a couple moments where the main menu completely locked up because i used a controller at some points. I had an unfixable glitch where I paused and opened the satchel at the same time, causing the animation to freeze me in place permanently until a reload.I do also want to add that this along with Myst both desperately need a point and click mode. There is a lot of gorgeous visual direction lost, along with some puzzles becoming so wildly obscured by unlocking the player's vision that I wish there was an optional mode.These are issues that need fixed, adjusted, or tweaked for sure. however, none of them kept the core of this game from blasting through brighter than one would ever expect.The music, PEAK. The visual design, PEAK. The puzzles, PEAK. every other facet of this title is rendered with such masterful precision that I still hope the rest of the Myst series is remade, despite my sickness of remakes.If you want to take some time to exercise your brain with music that goes OFF paired with gorgeous and striking visuals, play this, no questions asked. After Myst of course.And if you want an EVEN BETTER time, play the original. This acts as a nice refresh of the classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Not just a remake, but a re-imagining.As someone who read the prequel books before diving into the original Riven on release (back in my Uni days... damn I'm old), this 2024 version hits all the right notes. It's faithful to the original without slavishly holding on to its more frustrating qualities, and it even elevates the game in some aspects.My only complaint is that I miss the original FMV performances, but I can see how there'd have been no way to integrate them into the 3D format.Word of warning: Some of the puzzle solutions are randomised on a per-player basis, so you can't just look up the solutions in a newsgroup like some of us did in the 90s...
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a magnificent reimagining of Riven. If you've never played it, buy it now! If you played Riven back in the '90s, buy it now! :) What can I say without spoilers? It's stunningly beautiful, deeply thought out, and filled with more story, worldbuilding, and puzzles than before. As fantastical and strange as it may get, Riven always feels like a deeply real place, and the new version is quite likely the greatest game Cyan has ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the original Riven I can say that the remake is well worth picking up. It is incredibly well made and while there are some very minor visual shake ups, this feels like I'm walking through the prerendered pictures of the original. I was very surprised to see that many of the puzzles were remixed slightly, it still feels like Riven but changed enough to feel like a new experience. If you love Myst, buy it. If you're new to Myst, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Still as outstandingly great as it was in the 90s.All the conceptual changes made to the original actually serve to better present the Riven's backstory, or make the it clearer why a puzzle works the way it does.By that I mean the puzzles are a bit less "tacked on" than they were in the original. They are not puzzles for the sake of there being puzzles, like some in Myst and later titles in the series. For every clue you have to find, there is a very good in game reason, why that clue was left and why it was left in that particular way.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventure / puzzle games of all time. A lovingly crafted remaster and remake that fully recaptures the spirit of the 1997 classic while adding some great quality of life features. Play without a guide if possible for one of the most immersive and rewarding puzzle experiences in gaming.Pros:- A masterful puzzle game that is genuinely clever, intricately designed, immaculate- Score worth playing on repeat, sound work is phenomenal, the best creaky board sounds in the business- Gorgeous art direction- In-game notebook so you can take a million pictures and forget everything anyway- Some randomized puzzle elements make brute-forcing impossible (brainlets in SHAMBLES)- No guidance, forcing you to think and make connections between areas that can be stimulating and full of brain expansion momentsCons:- No guidance, forcing you to think and make connections to a point that can sometimes feel punishing to the point of brain implosion moments- Navigation is slow, sprint toggle please, making the mandatory backtracking such a chore I wish to throw myself into the Starry Expanse- Confusing ending structure, easy to get a doo doo ending and have to replay a lot, good option would be to have a "point of no return" notice- One cutscene feels longer than church, skip please- Crusty FMV characters removed in favor of, let's just say, very not great looking CG models.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the best puzzle game ever made in VR was a treat.  There are some changes from the original version, but for the most part I liked the changes.  You need a very good gaming pc to run Riven in VR with the highest quality graphic settings.  I have a 3080 TI and a 9700K cpu and I was just able to run it on the high settings with a 72 hz refresh rate.All though I do love playing this game in VR, I think Cyan is falling behind other companies who make VR games.  For example, in games like Half Life Alyx, you have realistic physics so you can pull or push open a standard door.  Cyan's solution to this is having these sliding doors and when they tried to have a swinging door, they were a bit clumsy.  I feel sliding doors is a lazy solution.  Also, instead of the simple solution of having a crouch button for puzzles that are low to the ground, Cyan chose to change those puzzles so they are at standing height.  If pressing a crouch button is too complicated for your player base, they are too dumb to be playing your puzzle game.  In the latest version of Myst, there is a glaring example of this in the channel wood age, where they had these insanely long levers (which looked ugly to me) to divert the water.  I would have rather just had the lever closer to the ground and I would press a crouch button to get low to the floor so I could manipulate the lever.  Or another solution could be the lever is close to the floor but I could manipulate it from a standing position by pointing at the handle and the lever is highlighted and then I can press the grab button and then when I move my arm it moves the lever.There are some things I did like which Cyan did in VR, like fast travel for ladders and having a seated mode.  I particularly like having a seated mode, because you can sit and be the height in the game that you would be if you were standing, this is important for puzzle games as sometimes you are standing in one place for awhile trying to solve a puzzle.  There is a strange group of people who think VR must always be a complete simulation and if you are pressing a button, you might as well play the game flat, but that is just silly.  These same people used to think if you're not physically walking in your play space, your immersion is ruined, but logic prevailed and people now use an analog stick to move around in VR.  Same thing goes with a crouch button, I don't want to bend down a million times in real life, but I also don't want everything to be be designed at waist height because of that.I hate to nitpick but I love Cyan games and I love playing VR.  This game is awesome and you should play it.  My nitpicks are just to highlight where I see room for improvement.  I give it a 9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game that I would recommend to everyone, there really aren't many like it. Maybe there are none exactly like it. Walking around this mysterious world feels amazing, it feels like a visually stunning almost real place.There are "puzzles" to solve, but they're not really puzzly-puzzles. It's more like you're discovering a world that is the way it is for good reason, with a rich history and story, and you're a visitor trying to figure out how it all works. It's actually genius. The story isn't super in your face, it's told through careful observation of the environment, but when things click, it's the best feeling in the world.It's a little tough, but not SUPER hard, I managed to beat it with only 2 small nudges in the right direction.Begging the developer for more games, no one does it like them!

_childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERS REVIEWTL:DRFor me, a 10 out of 10 experience. Genuinely loved everything they did in the game, this maintains everything you loved about the original Riven while adding enough new areas and puzzles to make this adventure feel fresh and exciting. Plays brilliantly, runs smoothly, visually stunning, original OST is present and correct. Myst and Riven fans will love this masterpiece all over again.FULL REVIEW:This is a stunning remake of Riven. A game that looks almost exactly like the original game but adds enough new areas and new puzzles to make the experience feel fresh, new and just as interesting as if you had picked it up for the very first time all over again.Visually it's amazing, especially if you have a good 4K TV or monitor. Crank it up to 4K and prepare for your jaw to drop at each and every location. The soundtrack from the original is present and correct in each area, untouched, exactly as you remember it. A really nice touch. Gameplay wise, it plays like a modern adventure game. It's fully free roam, there's no point and click option in here. You can explore every inch of this amazing world in full free roaming and beautiful 3D. It supports VR too, though I do not have a headset so I cannot say anything as regards playing the game that way.I'm happy to say that the voice acting is as excellent as it always was. Atrus lines appear to have been re-recorded, as have Catherines but Gehns original voice acting (by the late, great John Keston) is present and correct, which is a really nice touch. His original performance was amazing in the original Riven so it's great to see that they haven't changed that.There are a few faults in here, though they're all minor nitpicks. There are some huge stutters as the game physically pauses (albeit very briefly) and loads in the section ahead of you, especially noticeable in the domes and on entering new areas. Also the 3D character models are a bit weak, albeit they are a lot stronger than the models used in the Myst remake. Atrus and Gehn do genuinely look quite good and move pretty well but the other character models in the game look a bit awkward at times. There is no option (at the time of writing this review) to revert to the FMV actors of old so just make note of that if that's an option that you would prefer.As I said, minor nitpicks overall.I very highly recommend this game to adventure game fans and especially to Myst series fans and fans of the original Riven alike. This is everything you will want it to be and more. A brilliant achievement.

Definitely a nice little nostalgia trip, but definitely a different game. Felt more like taking a tour of riven instead of playing riven at times. Definitely recommend anyone who hasn't played the original and still would, though less so, to those who have played the original and wants to see what a updated graphical version of the age would look like..khapo rezunuh rildolgelenij gath

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I grew up with the original Myst and Riven and loved Riven so much I played it 4+ times in the row as a kid. The world was beautiful, and it felt lived in. However, the game, while difficult, was nowhere near as difficult and time-consuming as the remake. The remake is a whole other beast, and I must admit, I found it infuriatingly confusing at times, partially due to UI-related bugs which broke the game temporarily (until a reload/restart).Here's the breakdown:+ ~8 hours to complete one story from beginning to end with as little guidance as possible.+ ~14 hours to 100% all achievements without a guide, though I sought out hints from time to time and utilized my existing knowledge of Riven from over 2 decades ago.+ Beautiful environments to explore! Walk around in familiar but somewhat refreshed environments with WASD and FPS style camera movement. Beware: some puzzles are harder to figure out because of the new control scheme but not a ton.+ Some randomization occurs with the puzzles, making this somewhat replayable.+/- OG Riven's puzzles and world are way different, so your past knowledge may be more of a hindrance than a boon, making this a mostly new experience for all players but also making it much harder to figure out, with or without a guide.- FMV sequences were replaced by impressive but ultimately inferior 3D models.- Some levels and gameplay mechanics of the original Riven were completely removed or dumbed down in the remake.- Interactive elements are somewhat limited. I expected more physics objects in this remake, but for the most part, items were static and had scripted movements.- VR is supported but only barely. I recommend just playing this game in flat, non-VR mode. It's simply more enjoyable that way in my opinion. Your mileage may vary with different headset and controller combos. You may have some trouble with Index controllers when paired with certain headsets. I noticed problems with mine in a brief test but after a PC restart, they randomly worked.Overall, it's a great remake, but it messed with the formula that made the original Riven beloved too much. After playing this remake, I went back to the original and realized I would have enjoyed a remaster of the original more. Oh well. Still a great experience. Well worth the asking price if you're a long time fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake that captures the feel of the original game perfectly.  Best installment in the franchise.Pros:  Graphics are great.  Still not a fan of the 3D people but they did a better job than the last Myst.  I really like how they kept the feel and the theme and story the same, but rearranged enough of the paths and locations to make exploring rewarding even if you know the game really well.  I miss rolling wooden balls but the new puzzles are SUCH an improvement.  The main antagonist seems much more competent and threatening in this version. Really enjoyed my first playthrough.Cons:  Not as many run ins with the locals as the original.  Made the island seem much more empty.  Despite being an all new 2024 remake, it still falls prey to the have to stand in one spot and click this one spot to activate something.  If I click on a device, I shouldn't have it not work unless I am standing in an exact orientation to the device.  It should just work if I'm close enough and click on it.  I would also like more randomization of the puzzles on subsequent playthroughs.  The only randomization is the very very easy things, so not much at all.Loved it and can't wait for the next one, whether Exile (pleeeeease) or a new sequel (shut up and take my money.gif), I will for sure be buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Riven, the remaster of the 1997 best selling game, is a nostalgic walk down memory lane for those of us who played the original when it was released. The 1997 original featured some of the best looking scenery and incredible world building that has ever been made in video game history. While the original game was made from pre-rendered images and video in low resolutions by today's standards, this remaster brings the game into the Unreal engine, accomplishing in real-time what we could only ever dream of or hope for 27 years ago. Cyan's treatment of the setting has always been one of verisimilitude, forsaking the spectacular in order to try to maintain a grounded sense of reality, encouraging the player to inhabit the role of the "stranger".Not only has this remake captured the heart and soul of the original, in my opinion it elevates the experience. Some of the original puzzles were overly complex have now been simplified. Some have been removed and replaced. Old players will find the experience comfortably familiar, yet be sufficiently different to make the purchase worthwhile. New players can sink themselves into the world of Myst and discover a beautiful and compelling world and story.Advice for new players: you will be tempted to look up walk-throughs and guides. Don't. The biggest joy in these games is figuring out the puzzles for yourself. Take your time. Look everywhere. Read everything. Yes, read.I hope Cyan will consider making more games in the universe of Myst, if not the series. There is much still to explore about the D'ni and the ages they learned how to link to.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original version as a teenager and fell in love with the game/series. As a young man, I was interested in solving the puzzles. I didn't care much about the story. As I aged I started to prefer the story and the journals in the original game. No matter how many hours I spent playing the original, I never finished the game (solved all the puzzles).  I got stuck on the Moiety Pillar Puzzle and the final marble puzzle. Those two I looked up online maybe a decade ago during my last play through. I was excited when I learned about this new and improved game, which I was given as gift. This time the hard puzzles that stumped me as a kid and a decade ago was made more accessible. Especially, since you don't have to enter disks (which a patch had been released years ago to eliminate that hassle) when you entered the islands. The most important difference between this version and the original is that this version is more complete.  I mean you can tell if you played the original that this version was what the creators wanted to do, but technology of the time hindered them.  The vent going into Gehn's lab on Boiler Island in the original version seemed more of a quick fix to what really the creators wanted to do due to time constrains.  This time the creators had all the time to get things right and build the puzzles that they really wanted. Every single puzzle or obstacle made sense in this version based on the story and character of the game. Not every puzzle or solution in the original made sense in this way. Thus, this version is more polished than the original just like the sphere in Gehn's lab.  The visuals were spot on even if there is an error in the rendering, which happen only 2 times during my play through. A reload of a save fixed the error.  Therefore, if you love stories and puzzles...this game is must have.  Thank-you Cyan for redoing one of the greatest games I have ever played.  I complete enjoyed all the new elements that had been added. I really didn't miss the ones that were removed. Now that I finished this game, I will wait in utter anticipation of what will come next in the updating or new additions to the sage of the Myst series.

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is a first person point and click adventure where we solve puzzles and decipher cryptic codes across volcanic islands, each strewn with steam powered machinery and ancient artefacts. Set against the backdrop of a collapsing world held in the grip of Gehn, the game unfolds through a series of quests to free our protagonist, Catherine, from captivity. The narrative deepens as we interact with characters like Atrus and the rebellious Moeity faction, ultimately influencing multiple endings based on our choices. The scenery throughout is just mesmerising - from the metallic, polished domes to the rusted machinery and lush, verdant landscapes - every environment in Riven is crafted to evoke a sense of surreal, otherworldly beauty. The sky's vivid azure hue contrasts with the subtly artificial glow of warm interior lighting, creating a visual atmosphere that feels both familiar and completely unreal. Riven invites us to solve its mysteries at our own pace, immersing us in a world where every click is a step towards understanding.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this.The original Riven was one of the very first games I played. I replayed it two years ago and I can confidently say that - besides the abysmally low resolution - it has held up well both graphically and in terms of gameplay, given its age. This remake is, unfortunately, a disappointment both in comparison to the original and as a stand-alone game in my opinion.Before I get into why that is, I want to applaud Cyan for this remake because it is clear that a lot of effort went into this game. The graphics are stunning and are a faithful and genuine improvement over the original graphics. The water and animal animations are great. Some aspects of the game were reworked due to the nature of the original being a point and click game and while I am not a huge fan of most of the solutions (see below), it is undeniable that a lot of creativity has been employed to come up with them.All that being said, here is why I think this game falls short:The linearity in this game is crushing. One of the key factors to Riven's success was how most of the game was accessible right from the start and the game put very little effort into putting you on the right track. The remake is the polar opposite: Most of the hints needed to solve a puzzle are collocated and fairly on the nose. I imagine some of this was done to save some backtracking, which takes a lot longer in this iteration (clicking through islands was extremely quick in the original). I can appreciate the idea here, but it takes away a lot of immersion and realism. To further illustrate this point, let's examine the game's two main puzzles and compare them to their original versions:Another aspect of the game I disliked was the constant locking of your character and camera. The immersion that a true 3d game brings is dependent on your character actually being able to use all degrees of freedom. A lot of clickable interfaces in this game violate this idea by zooming themselves into view and stopping you from moving your camera or character at all. In doing this, the remake degenerates to a point and click game with slightly better graphics. Some of these locked angles are supposed to help the player better understand cause and effect of the machinery they are manipulating. I found this to be further unnecessary hand holding for the most part. I would have much preferred if the puzzles, wherever possible, let you click buttons, push levers etc while still allowing you to move your character and camera. The rather slow animations when zooming in certainly didn't help here either.All in all, I would love a more faithful remake that keeps most of the puzzles as is or at least keeps them within the spirit of Riven and seamlessly integrates the puzzles into the world rather than making them stick out like a sore thumb.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven remains the single best adventure game ever made, and it's not close. 2024 is the year that real-time 3D graphics can finally live up to the promise of photorealistic pre-rendered scenes from 1997; the game is so gorgeous is hurts a bit. The puzzles and the way the game progresses have been made more accessible at the cost of a little bit of the brilliantly organic verisimilitude of the original game, but I can forgive the game for that. Riven deserved a full 3D remake, and this game absolutely does the original justice. I am blown away. It was like I was a kid again playing with my mom and my sister, except I'm older so I had more of an idea of what I was doing and was better equipped to fully appreciate and enjoy it. I really just can't speak highly enough of the remake, as someone for whom the original is one of THE three games that got me into game development.

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is like the most lore centric game in Myst series, theres soo much to do in this game but it gives you a clear indication of what you need unlike exile or revelations. I've meet couple of bugs in this game, one that was with the notebook, where you delete something yet afterwards it kinda messes up the thumbnails for some reason so you have to navigate back to the menu and enter again, i tore my hair out soo much when i found out that i deleted something that wasnt supposed to be deleted, and the second bug is regarding the inventory and the mirror, theres a case where you would press R and open up inventory at the same time it would get stuck and you have to restart the whole game because of that. But nevertheless its an amazing puzzle game where you have to pay attention to every single little detail.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the original Myst, Riven, and Exile. They're three of the only games I care about, quite frankly, and Riven was my favorite of the three, for its spooky environment, and amazing plot. I also happened to enjoy the 2021 Myst remake, if you select "classic" video mode, and get rid of the CG characters. So what went wrong with the Riven remake?As you can probably already guess, I am not a fan of the CG characters. They're the number one thing that ruins the realism of the game. I tried out the game on two different computers, and there was a lot of fine-tuning required at the beginning to get Atrus and Cho looking halfway decent. Yet their hair had a fuzzy-yet-transculent quality that bothered me. Was there really no way to get video footage of human beings into the game? If the resolution of the original footage was too low to work in the new game, I'd much rather Cyan use footage with new actors.The game has substantial issues, however, which extend beyond the use of CG characters. It's been revamped to such an extent that it feels like a re-interpretation rather than a remake. Some of the changes make sense plot-wise (such as the Moiety using the Rivenese numbering system, rather than the D'Ni one), but most are completely arbitrary and needless. Plateau Island has been completely gutted and dumbed-down. I'll leave it at that. I'm also puzzled by Atrus linking to Myst during the opening cutscene, rather than continuing with his writing, so he can stabilize Riven. Has the purpose of this ever been addressed by the developers?Most surprisingly to me, the new game is a lot more linear than the old one. You have a few randomized puzzles, but other than that, there's a singular line you need to follow if you want to win. In the original, you had a lot of leeway in choosing which order to the solve the puzzles. Case in point, once you got to Jungle Island, you either had a choice of staying there and solving some puzzles, going to Crater Island, or going to Plateau Island (if you knew about the trick with the Wahrk Elevator). In the new game,  - at least as far as I can tell.While the visuals in the Riven Remake are cool at times, it is still a vastly inferior game to the original. While the original may have a low resolution, it looks amazingly organic and real, compared to Riven in the "Unreal" engine. The use of real human actors was the icing on the cake. What I could see happening is someone devising an AI-upscaled version of the original Riven which ends up being superior to the remake. I know there is already an AI-upscaled version of Exile that looks OK.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really comment for new players of Riven, as I know the original game inside and out so I already knew what to do and how to think in most cases. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish Steam had a third option to the question "Do you recommend this game?" and that third option would be "Maybe". And this game is a big maybe to me.As the sequel to Myst, I was very excited to try the Riven remake out, as I had loved the Myst remake Cyan Worlds had previously made. I could never get into the original game, as it was far too outdated by the time I wanted to try it. Same went for Riven, where I tried to play the original, but I just couldn't get past the horrible controls and the graphics. I was happy to see a remake of Riven was in the works and wish listed it immediately. Now it's here and I can't exactly say I love this game, but I don't exactly hate it either.The game itself is gorgeous. The graphics and details are quite impressive for a world that is largely lifeless. You see some animals here and there, with some other humans sprinkled in at a handful for times throughout the game, but for the most part it's just you and the scenery. And the scenery is quite beautiful. I found Riven to be a very quiet game. It felt like there was a lack of ambient sound in many areas and some sound effects were either delayed or nonexistent. You will click buttons or pull levers only to hear silence. The cut scene audio sounds like it was ripped right out of the original game, which would explain its poor quality. There isn't very many cutscenes or spoken dialogue, so it wouldn't have hurt to have hired voice actors to redo the lines.The puzzles themselves are just like Myst, where they are solved by interacting with the environment and not having to carry items around or combine items. The puzzles are mainly based around interacting with the environment and numbers and symbols. As you progress through the world of Riven you'll have to call back upon many details you came across during your travels. And that is where this game drove me nuts. Having to recall minor details in an area you haven't visited in hours. There is a journal, where you can take a screenshot and make notes on it. I appreciate the notebook, but that isn't the problem here. You need to collect screenshots of EVERYTHING in order to understand the later puzzles, but you won't know this until it's too late because for most of the game you can easily progress without utilizing the journal for anything. Then all of a sudden the game turns around and drops multiple puzzles with code combinations that require you to decipher a made up language and number system that up until this point was hardly used. Now you have the fun task of traveling back to multiple areas of the game to collect clues, which require you to go through the longest traveling animations I have seen in a game in a long time. I hate having to consult online guides for hints or an outright answer, but I was forced to several times towards the end of the game where I was just so damn sick of numbers and symbols. I enjoy difficult puzzles, but I absolutely despise having to backtrack for them and this game makes you do a ton of it, even beyond just the puzzles. I hinted at it in the paragraph above, but traveling between islands and even in some parts of the islands themselves can be a massive pain. There are two main ways to travel between islands and they involve a trolley system and . Both of the these methods have long animations and aren't fast in any way imaginable. You'll have to utilize both of these methods frequently and by the end you'll be glad to never use them again. Oh and how can I forget the damn rotating room on the first island. There is this rotating room with five different doors, but you can only use two doors at once. As you rotate the room with a button from the outside you'll need to wait until the doors line up with where you are standing and then with another door. To get from one specific door to another, you need to go through the painfully long animation of the entire room rotating multiple times until you can walk through, but then it might require you to do this whole process over again at another door to get somewhere else. If you want to see first hand how stupid this puzzle is just go on YouTube and see for yourself. The game makes you go through this area many times later in the game, but requires you to do the rotating puzzle each time you pass through and need to access a slightly different door. In the end, I am going to recommend this game, but barely. I love puzzle games and I have to support them, especially with remakes like this one. However, they need to be better than this. That's not to say I didn't like the game. I did, but the negative aspects of it just drove me nuts. It's never a good sign when you're playing a game and are trying to finish it because you just want it to be over. That's what happened in the last three hours of Riven for me. I wanted to be done with this game and uninstall it, so I can move onto something better.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually stunning and the atmosphere is quite incredible at times. A really wonderful use of lighting, colors and a very good composition in every environment. I know they mostly reproduced the prerendered images and cutscenes from the original in full 3D, so this game is so beautiful for the most part thanks to the original's art direction but this is an impressive and faithful modernization.The small critters and various animals that make the world feels more alive are really nice too. The CG characters are obviously less impressive but they're miles better than those from Myst(2021). They're good enough that they don't take you out of the experience. To me FMVs will always be the superior choice in a Myst game, in the 90s they gave those first games in the series that eerie 'real' feel. But it's easy to understand why this wouldn't work well in modern games.For the rest, it's mostly Riven, one of the best adventure/puzzle games ever made if not the best, with several changes that makes this new version feels like its own thing, a re-interpretation of Riven that doesn't completely replace the original. Playing this game was a great mix of nostalgia and new discoveries. I got a bit stuck two or three times and I liked it!I know that this will be entirely subjective and I'm sure some people would have preferred a 100% accurate remake but I think the changes they made in the puzzles and the flow of the adventure are all good changes. It's obvious they were thought out by people who understand their game and the lore. Everything new is included in the game world in a lore-friendly way and some changes are arguably better than what was in the original. In any case there's nothing that feels out of place, too 'modern' or too 'gamey'.It's hard to talk about the difficulty because there must be a big difference between someone who played the original and someone who's new to the series, but it doesn't feel like the game was made to be 'more accessible' at all, in a pejorative way I mean. This is still Riven with its Riven-like puzzles and Riven-like difficulty.I didn't play it in VR because I wanted the comfiness of taking physical notes like I did with the original but I did a quick tour of the islands in VR after finishing the game just to see what it feels like. If you're ok with taking notes in the virtual notebook inside the game and playing it like that isn't too physically uncomfortable for you, this is definitely worth it for the added immersion.There is really nothing to complain about. I'd say that in regards to everything they did to refresh the experience of exploring Riven in general, I felt a few missed opportunities of adding more stuff to look at or interact with, like in the Moeity Age for example, but even as it is, they did something new there and it was nice. This is just a case of wanting more of everything as a fan so it's really not a criticism. And Riven was always more about Riven itself.I really hope we'll see more games like this in the Myst universe. I have nothing against new IPs but there's just something fascinating about those Ages, linking books and ancient civilisations. This really brought me back to what I enjoyed in video games in the 90s/early 2000s, the kind of experience that seem increasingly few and far between nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a wonderful game, still as good as it was when it first came out 27 (!) years ago. Back then it was a behemoth of a game, way ahead of its time, and today… I've still never played a puzzle game that has managed to weave together its puzzles, story and environment as well as Riven. It feels like it hasn't aged.And for old farts like me, this remake has been smart enough to change things around so it feels fresh even after several playthoughs of the original. Books have been rewritten, puzzles have been modified or replaced, areas moved or added to force you to take different paths from before. It almost felt like playing for the first time again. I was giddy with excitement every time I started it up.This was finally the game that made me like VR, too. Bought a headset just for this, and I'm glad I did. Though, to be honest, when you need to write notes occasionally, VR is still kind of a pain. Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exquisite imagining of the original Riven in a modern engine and interaction framework. It's very rare for claims of "better realizing the original vision" to ring true at all, but in this case, I think they might. The fluid movement and visual presentation do change the tactile sense of some of the puzzles, but overall I think it's a positive change. The music and ambient sound design remains happily faithful to the original, which I think is essential to the world this remaster has brought back to life.I do have one complaint, which will be vague in an effort to be spoiler-free: There is one significant puzzle that has been altered (substantially, from memory), and the new version seems to deliberately mislead the player in one of its clues. There is enough information in-game to move past this, but for how and where it occurs, it's an odd choice that I felt made for the only blemish in this otherwise outstanding game.This is probably the best way to experience the game now, for new or returning players.

_childDocuments_.review: - all about point and click adventuresIs this game a masterpiece? 27 years after the release of the best-selling game of 1997, a complete remaster has now been released. Is it a cheap re-release or a contemporary renovation?Riven (by brothers Robyn and Rand Miller) is the direct successor to Myst. Myst was released back in 1993 and took the world by storm at the time. It became the best-selling game ever and defended this position for several years until it was replaced by The Sims 10 years later. The reason for its resounding success at the time was probably its excellent graphics (as one of the first good PC games to use the CD-ROM as a medium - along with classics such as Rebel Assault or The 7th Guest). In addition, it was also a game that was extremely well received by female gamers. Myst has been re-released several times over the years in an improved version, and finally underwent an excellent complete remaster in 2021.But what about Riven? With Riven, the developers at Cyan have continued the success story of Myst, but this time they had a slightly bigger budget. When it was released in 1997, it was already common practice (and technically no longer completely new territory) to publish new PC games on CD-ROM. Riven took up five CDs back then. Although it no longer set any new sales records, it still sold extremely well. In contrast to Myst, however, there were no new versions of Riven in the following years (apart from a DVD-ROM version, console and cell phone ports). So if you wanted to play Riven until now, you could either try to somehow get your old original to run on new PC hardware (difficult), install it via ScummVM, play it on your cell phone or play a console version (PlayStation, Saturn). The edition available on Steam was also just the old original without any improvements and with ScummVM as an emulator. So it really was time for a new version - and it has finally been released!Riven throws us straight into the story. If you haven't played Myst before, you won't understand much of the story, at least at first. We continue to play a dimensional traveler who is transported to the world of Riven by Atrus in order to find and rescue his wife Catherine. Riven is ruled by his evil father Gehn and is slowly being destroyed. Arthur makes it clear that we can't leave Riven the same way we traveled there, but hopefully he'll bring us back once we find his wife and Gehn is neutralized. And what's more, he may have found a way to bring us back to the world we originally came from...Once we arrive in Riven, one of our books is stolen, but the thief can't enjoy his booty for very long. After this introduction, the game begins - and it is structured very similarly to its predecessor. We are in a world that is sparsely populated by other creatures, but is full of strange buildings and other constructs. We have no idea what the various devices are for or how they work. The gameplay consists of exploring the world and solving various puzzles, which are usually related to the machines in the environment. Press switches and buttons, flip levers, move things around, always with the aim of opening up new paths and making progress. There are a total of five large islands to explore. Some puzzles also use musical clues. We have to use our intellect and intuition to discover the truth about Riven and its inhabitants. Riven has several possible endings - from a positive ending to the absolute failure of the player.The new version of Riven, like the remaster of Myst before it, has been completely reprogrammed. In contrast to the original, we now move completely freely in a 3D environment developed with the Unreal Engine, and can no longer just travel from point to point. In addition, the story has been expanded at some points and new graphics have been added. Some puzzles have been adapted to our new movement options. However, if you already know the original, you will recognize most of the locations and puzzles without any problems. The graphics also look excellent in high resolutions, and the many small movie sequences in the game are now of a much higher quality than before.This is what a lavish new edition should look like. With the new version of Riven, the old classic from 1997 has been perfectly reworked and adapted for the current generation of players. Riven is of course of particular interest to players who have already played Myst and now want more of the same - without any major changes to the game mechanics. Many puzzles, the solution to which is only revealed by attentively observing the surroundings, lead through a leisurely developing adventure - without time pressure and skill interludes. You'll have to decide for yourself whether you still find this type of gameplay contemporary.Finally a lovingly revised new version of this all-time classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. I have the fondest memories of playing the original back in the late nineties with my dad and brother, and can happily say that they've recaptured the magic here perfectly. I haven't played it in VR yet but intend to once I get the opportunity. Honestly, nostalgia glasses aside, I really can't think of any serious criticisms of this game - most of the puzzles are, at their core, the same puzzles from the original, with some QoL changes here and there and some new puzzles thrown in. The atmosphere and immersion are just as good, if not better, as the original game, to the point that I was never unhappy having to backtrack or wander around or simply be patient while I worked out what to do next. I sincerely hope Cyan continues working on the Myst series and pray that this game does well enough to convince them to keep at it.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played  as a kid.  I was aware of its existence for sure, but I didn't play the game proper until I was in my twenties.  So I didn't have much of an attachment to the game, at least not to the same level as I did with .  When I heard that Cyan Worlds was making a re-make of , my reaction was essentially a "huh that's neat" before moving on.  Fast forward to June 2024, and I notice there's demo for  as part of the Steam Next Fest.  So on a whim, I decided to install it and fire it up.My jaw dropped.The modern remake of  is utterly gorgeous.  To be able to experience it in 3D with high-quality, photorealistic graphics is something that could only have been dreamed of back in 1997.  I can't quite put my finger on what makes this one in particular stand out to me.   has gone through so many remakes and revisions, yet none of them wowed me the way  did.  Perhaps it's because  was left untouched for decades.  There was a team working on a fan-remake (they ended up being picked up by Cyan Worlds to help with the remake, which is really cool), but aside from that  never got the same love as its predecessor.  Maybe that made the jump from the original graphics to the new that much more stunning.Or maybe it's just me.  Maybe my lack of expectations made it much more spectacular for me.For the uninitiated,  is an adventure game.  You walk around the environments, picking up pieces of the story as you go, and solving puzzles.  Even back in the day,  was unique in that its puzzles would often require you to have an understanding of the world around you.  In particular, some of the late game puzzles will test you to make sure you've been paying attention and not just brute forcing your way through everything.Some of the puzzles in the remake have been drastically changed from the original game (the animal totems one comes to mind).  These puzzles, from what I can remember, are definitely an improvement from the original.  They're more clear about what you need to do while still retaining that key aspect of being integrated into the world's lore.  Some more avid  fans may have a different perspective on that, but for my part they were a good change.  There are other changes as well (including an entirely new area that wasn't in the original game).The story will be a bit confusing for those who maybe haven't played  before.  Some of that confusion is intentional, but considering  is a direct sequel some of the concepts will be difficult to untangle for those unfamiliar.  It's not impossible to come to grips with it, but you'll be playing a bit of catch-up if you jump in unaware.The one major issue I have with this remake is the cartoon-y character models.  The lip syncing on them is very off at times, and they don't always fit in quite right with the environment.  They're a massive improvement over the terrifying 3D abominations they had in the 2021 remake of , but they still feel out of place compared to the world around them.The only other complaint I can think of at the moment is one I had with the original: occasionally the story will just drop a twenty page journal in your lap and expect you to read it.  And you'll have to, because the journal could contain a necessary clue for progression.  It's nothing major, but it is a bit irritating to have your exploration interrupted because you suddenly need to read an entire short story.But aside from these complaints, the  is a fantastic achievement.  So whether you're an old fan looking to re-experience a classic, or someone who was just too young or never played the game growing up, this 2024 version of  is hands down the best way to experience it.  Just be prepared to challenge yourself, and plunge into a fantastical world of puzzles and secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful beyond belief. It's fascinating how they were able to translate the still visuals of the original game into a modern first-person perspective with free movement.Some of the puzzles and enigmas you have to solve require a lot of attention to the environment and quite a bit of back and forth, but the sheer beauty of the scenery made every moment a joy.Another thing that I loved was the way the game tells its story although this should be credited to the design of the original game. The story is not handed to you, it is given in small bits of dialogue, writings and environmental detail. As you progress you realize that small details in the environment that seemed purely cosmetic at first actually tell part of the story. It's up to you to connect the dots and many details are left for your interpretation.This game as become one of my favorite games of all time. Thank you, Cyan!

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of people here, Riven is one of my very first memories. For years, I've been watching The Starry Expanse Project, just hoping that one day I could see Riven again with fresh eyes, where it looked as real as it felt all those years ago.I wasn't sold in the beginning. Right away I noticed some subtle changes that threw me off. I was expecting an exact remake, with no changes aside from what was absolutely necessary. Some puzzles were changed, or removed entirely, and I just about threw my hands up and gave it up. It wasn't my Riven.I'm glad I finished it. One thing I love about Cyan games is feeling like they know me, that their games are for people like me, who have been here for decades. And I had a moment with a puzzle where I knew the change was made for people like me, to make me slow down and enjoy the game instead of blitzing through with solutions I memorized 15 years ago. I already knew how solve the  puzzle, I've solved it a hundred times, and they know I know how to , so HA! Now the puzzle makes you ! This is a Cyan game, and you will not leave without . I felt like I was being punked. I couldn't believe it. I felt like Rand was sitting on the other side of my screen laughing, because there was no brute forcing my way through. I had to solve it myself.So what it really comes down to, is I didn't love all the changes in the beginning (but in hindsight most of them made sense, either from a story perspective or a flow/sequence perspective). Most of all though, I came to appreciate what a gift it was. Riven (1997) is as familiar to me as my own house. Cyan gave me the gift of seeing it again with for the first time. I got just a little bit of that excitement back that comes from discovering something new, and solving a puzzle for the first time, experiences I thought I would never have again in a game so important to me.If you want this to be a shot for shot remake with not a single pixel out of place, you will be disappointed. If you meet it where it is, you can play Riven for the very first time, again.

Modern tech is insane man, that I can run an Unreal 5 game at near high/epic settings with a resolution this good.

_childDocuments_.review: great semi-remake, some puzzles have changed or are missing but there is a whole new set that have replaced them. this is nearly how i imagined the world of riven from the original 2d frame by frame moving game. world building is beautiful, runs pretty smoothly, not perfect (day 1 no updates yet) but very good. some small bugs. still have not completed the remake with about 5-6 hours so far, im expecting at least another 2-4 hours until finished, and was told some of the puzzles are randomized every play-through for repeatability. if you like puzzle games that can be a bit convoluted or sometimes just no sense of direction, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: So excited that a game I played as a kid could come back in such a brilliant and vivid way. Not only was it nostalgic, but the changes to the layout and puzzles were thoroughly enticing and welcome. My only critique was that the character models felt clunky and uncanny at times, but apart from that the world is beautiful and vibrant with a lot more to explore and generous storytelling through the environment. _childDocuments_.review: Although there are a lot of pros and cons for me, I recommend this remake - simply because it's stunningly beautiful. I loved every second of the visuals. I don't liked the heavy changes that were made to the puzzles - especially the biggest one. Instead of a more modern version that is a bit less unfair, it got replaced by an equally other weird puzzle. _childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this puzzle adventure! I had no nostalgia for this game, so this was a new game for me and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The environments looked amazing and the environmental storytelling was good. Took me around 8 hours to beat and the puzzles were just the right difficulty for me, who doesn't play too many puzzle games. Would highly recommend!I only have 2 major complaints:1: I had my character freeze completely 3 times during my playtime, had to fully restart the game to fix it. Luckily there's good autosave so I lost no progress or had to redo any puzzles.2. No option for plain text. The game has all its notes and diaries in handwritten cursive, which at points is extremely hard to read to the point I had to start guessing words and sentences. By the midpoint i just gave up reading them since there was so much to read and it became tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed re-playing this game after playing it many years ago with the fresh changes.  Great Art and Story.One of the aspects I like about riven is there is no overdone "rule of three" patterns (or similar) (something that I think obduction and firmament had in those worlds).  Every island seems different and patterns are not overdone and over pushed.  The a-symetric linking to worlds is nice and feels more real / natural to me where the linking of worlds can go anywhere.Cant wait to play the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to have to give this a guarded yes,  for a stand alone remake of the classic Riven game it is still very enjoyable and I am happy that so many new players get to experience a bit of the wonder the original game has.     Graphics are crisp, its a beautiful world to explore.  Lots of nostalgia as you wander around familiar yet changed worlds.   The soundtrack is the same, with most of the ambiance of the original.   Its a seamless play, no gltches.  Playing on epic settings and there is no lag, though start up loading screen and some transitions are long.    Its nice to plug and play, no fiddling with workarounds with the original to get around the old programming   I really enjoyed the new areas, puzzles and exploration, it felt like a new game at times.Now for the bad.  Its not Riven.  They took out alot of the exploration, all the tiny and huge flavor sounds, beeps, boops, doo daws, thingamijiggies and animations that made each world a wonder to explore, charming and at times horrifying with realization of what went on.   it was maddening in that you just knew the tiniest detail was vital for solving those infamous puzzles.  Notes were mandatory.   They took away the huge reward for solving those world puzzles, the linking books that took you to a whole new world with new sound tracks, exploration.   Each world was a stand alone environment, felt natural.    This Riven is a shell.   a beautiful one, still wondrous to explore, but empty.   The separate worlds are crammed into the main one and seem incongruous to the environment.the incredibly bad.  the in game characters.  their rendering is atrocious, they interrupt flow and pacing.  really ruined the lonely desolation of the worlds.  too busy and unnecessary.   old riven it was such a shock to see another soul, it was very eerie and alarming.  here they just plunk em down. its still a good adventure game.   I would highly recommend players also buy a copy of original Riven on GOG and give it a try.   you will need a walkthru but its worth it.  (the gog version works, im afraid the steam versions of myst and riven were not working last time i tried, they may have gotten them working by now as its been years, but i doubt it.)
