_childDocuments_.review: An absolute triumph. Nearly every decision that went into this remake was the right one. The team realized that capturing the feel of the original game meant re-imagining some aspects while meticulously replicating others. The end result is something that feels just as magical in 2024 as it did in 1997 -- not an easy feat. Riven was never a mere puzzle game -- it was an experience that bathed the player in the wonder of its sights, sounds, and mystical world. And I'm happy to say that is still the case.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing the OG Myst and Riven alongside my family, trying to work out the puzzles as a team. Especially Riven stood out as a very special game with its worldbuilding, and visually made a huge impression on me as a kid. The one caveat of the original was that it was borderline too difficult for us to complete even working through it together. With this new remake, to me it feels more intuitive, immersive, and just the right amount of challenge, and amazingly extremely accurate to the original (it looks absolutely stunning), the exception being the puzzles which have been changed up in some surprising ways (personally, in a good way).I followed this project over the years eagerly waiting any news and updates from the Starry Expanse team, and now seeing it finished feels totally unreal (no pun intended) and like a dream come true. From the music and visuals to the lore and story, it is everything I was imagining it would be. I did encounter a few bugs playing on Steam Deck, but nothing major that prevented progression.Thanks Cyan and the Starry Expanse team for reviving my childhood nostalgia and fulfilling their dream to become fully immersed in this beautiful world!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: My father came home with the original Riven when I was 4 years old, and I've played it throughout my life. This remake is incredible. Here are a few thoughts in case you need a nudge in the right direction:Pros:1) The Age of Riven is falling apart and completely unstable. You see and feel this constantly throughout the game. It almost made me feel that I was playing too slowly and needed to hurry up.2) The puzzles are close to the original but different enough to give even the most devoted fans a challenge without feeling like you're playing a different Riven.3) There are changes, and yet all of them are really well thought-out, from the Moiety puzzle, to how the doors automatically close in the Maglevs when you sit down (something that always irked me as a kid). The fact that the RIvenese can now access the schoolroom directly makes much more sense, and perhaps my favourite change is the redesign (or perhaps repurposing) of the submarine for Gehn's direct and complete use, which is more in line with how I find Gehn would think. I questioned each change, even subtle ones, and found that they added more to the world. Truly, well done team. 4) The exploration of some previously off-limit ages. I nearly shrieked for joy. The fulfilment of my childish curiousness. 5) Perhaps my favourite were the domes. I sat there with my jaw hanging open, looking like a fool. Cons:1) The Temple Island fire marble puzzle broke my brain. For those of you who are Myst franchise fans, this is where you prove to yourself after all these years that you have earned your Myst Black Belt. Don't cheat, you can do this people.2) A small one maybe, and just my humble opinion, but I don't understand why the opening Atrus dialogue was changed. It's literally the first thing you hear when you play and I'm sure many of us can say it off-by-heart. To me, it's a hallmark of Riven. When Atrus spoke about his "one person prison" I rolled my eyes. 3) The animation of the characters could have been a little sharper, given that Riven at times feels more realistic than reality. (Perhaps I was just spoilt with seeing the likes of John Keston and Sheila Goold in the original?)Small issues aside, this is an incredible remake. I had an absolute blast playing it, and without question my 4 year old self would have enjoyed it, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's Riven 2024, a very hard, (you've ben warned) puzzle game. It's different than the original in certain details and puzzles, and it looks a lot better. It has some pretty nice puzzles. The series has a story, some of which is rather original, but unfortunately the characters are not well written. Many character decisions and motivations (including the players) are a case of "What? Really? Why?". So I'd say it's neither good nor bad, but a tiny bit more on the bad side.Why?: 1. If you kind of know what you're doing, you can play through in less than 14 hours and I remembered no details from the old version and took my time (apart from looking up 2-3 details; you can easily miss certain objects as some areas are very dark or you're looking at things from the wrong angle).  You can definitely play this a lot faster. And the reason it takes so long is that you're travelling back and forth between places which takes a lot of time. So the "fun" is over rather soon. 2. SPOILER ALERT....Even the good ending sucks. The guy you did all of this hard work for including saving his wife, has nothing better to do than leaving you to die and does so for no apparent reason. He could have just offered the player to touch his book just as his wife did seconds earlier and everything would have been fine. Terrible terrible writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely insane remake. Loved every second of what I've seen so far. A few puzzles have changed, but given the fact that its changed to full 3d/VR from point and click, I think the changes are more than welcome. The detail, the design, and the thought that went into this is absolutely astounding, Highest of recommendations if you're a fan of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the very definition of "it's exactly how I remember it" - truly incredible to move around in the fully realized 3D world. And I appreciate that they changed a bunch of puzzles, added more lore and areas etc. Keeps the game feeling fresh for "veterans" like myself who skipped school to play this back in 1997!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is not just a remake of Riven with a fresh coat of paint. I mean: it IS a photorealistic recreation of the 90s game in Unreal Engine, but it ALSO changes up SO MANY puzzle elements of the game that it feels more like a sequel to the classic. Those familiar with Riven's OG puzzles will immediately notice something is ... different as they begin their exploration. New challenges and game dynamics give this towering cultural icon of a game a whole new level of depth and interest.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven 2024 is vastly different than the game I am so used to. A lot of things have changed, including expected pathways are gone or blocked. It is a totally new and fresh experience. I'm running the game on PC, a lot of the scenes don't load right away, NPC's appear headless for a few moments, animated vehicles lag quite a bit the first time you ride them. It is something I hope will improve in time. The CGI characters, honestly, look like something from 12 years ago. I understand why they went with CGI, a lot of the actors are much older or dead. I remember getting to the sub was fairly easy, now it's hidden away and I cannot imagine how to get to it now. I'm 5 hours in, only 1 crash, and 1 place I got trapped by unrezzed statues lol So all in all not bad for a new game! I will write a more detailed review once I finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original Riven, but this is fantastic. It could do with an option to skip or speed up travel scenes, because these take pretty long, and are common, because it's not always clear where you're supposed to go. But my god, the puzzles in this game are simply spectacular. They are some of the most elegant and interesting puzzles I've ever come across in a game. The story is hard to follow at times, especially if you haven't played the first game. But it's kind of told in an "after the fact" manner - a bunch of things happen, and later you find a journal explaining what you saw. It's difficult to keep up with all the details sometimes, but it's a cool story. It's really beautiful as well, with gorgeous graphics and lifelike environments. Highly recommended overall!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent. A very faithful remaster and still an enjoyable experience after all these years. It's a little rough around the edges in some places but there are no obvious deal breakers that would stop me from recommending the game.The performance is a little iffy, mostly due to stuttering which happens whenever you enter a new area. A lot of the easter eggs from the original appear to be missing, and the overall vibe of the game is a little different. The puzzles are still quite difficult and I feel like a hint system would be been a great edition to the game, but old walkthroughs and hint guides are still valid here.All in all though, it's a fantastic remake of one of the greatest point and click adventure games of all time. If you're a fan of puzzle games it really doesn't get much better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven has always been one of those games I wish I could experience for the first time again, and Cyan have done exactly that!  It looks like how I imagined it looked as a kid, but actually hi-def this time.  The sounds and music (and even the color of the rocks and sky) immediately brought me back to playing the original Riven.This new Riven captures the feel and sense of the original Riven, but includes some updates to keep it fresh.  Some puzzles are tweaked, and others are completely new.  The original will always be there for those who want it, and I love this new version!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Riven is... honestly a bad game. Full of back-tracking, with most of the puzzles boiling down to finding that one hidden button that you missed.I also tried playing it in VR, but the experience was not very good. - Shadows only render if they are visible from the left eye, makes everything weird to look at- The screen goes black if you move close to a wall while in some cutscenes, like at the start, even with the camera being visibly away from the actual wall!- Some menus render in front of your hands and the aim lineIt's a product of its time, with a mediocre story, and mechanics that are a fun gimmick at first, but quickly become repetitive when you have to wait for the same animation to play for the 100th time as you back-track once again because you missed something.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: About as perfect of a remake as you can get. The puzzles and a few other things have been reworked, keeping the game fresh for both veterans like myself of the original 1997 game, and new players alike. I would highly recommend getting The Riven Companion Guide with the game if you're not used to these kinds of puzzle solving games, just in case you get stuck and need a small hint here or there. As a veteran myself, I needed to briefly use it for one small part.Cyan Worlds has truly knocked it out of the park with this remake. From both the quality of the worlds, to the quality of the new character models for everyone, faithful to the original games in both visuals and audio (they carried over the original game's music, along with new tracks), I really can't think of a single flaw without nitpicking.I'd give it a full 5/5. Would highly recommend picking this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The remake of this classic has taken my breath away. The detail of the original, six disc CD-ROM game from 1997, and all its nostalgia is here. But even more than that, now its in Ultra HD, where i can let my eyes take in every corner of the world, as if I were standing right in the middle of it.  The entire time of my play through felt as though I was walking through a dream of time long ago, when I was in high school trying to be the first one in my friends group to beat the game. However around every corner, everything in the world felt different, a good different, Game developers take note, This team knows how to do a proper remake. This is truly a masterpiece for the ages and Cyan has accomplished it twice in my lifetime!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games ever and the remake doesn't disappoint.  Really it's more of a reimagining in some ways and even experienced players will find new and unexpected things.  All of the changes felt like they were made for internal logic and consistency in the world and not arbitrarily.  The only thing that's a downgrade are the 3D character models replacing live actors but that's pretty much an unavoidable compromise to make this VR compatible and free-roam.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A rare experience that fully invites one into another world — an anthropologically rich fictive culture, a society torn apart on a crumbling reality in thrall to an ersatz God. There are additions here that expand and fortify the 1997 masterpiece including some breathtaking moments that produce both awe and sorrow. For someone whose childhood was indelibly stamped those decades ago, this was like tying a tourniquet around the arm and mainlining pure nostalgia. I can't quite imagine what this must be like for a complete newcomer but this represents a unique game whose holistic puzzle design will leave one seeing connections between seemingly discrete challenges and I would argue, is far more intuitive and surmountable than the abstractions of its predecessor, .A stunning achievement but one that requires patience and scrutiny.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It is the same but different from the original. The islands are the same(ish), but the feel is the same. The puzzles were a tiny bit new. We older players have the Dni math memorized but this one brings in some complexity. I said "Thank god" once or twice but cursed my screen when (as is tradition) I marched back and island or two. Some of out tricks from the original still work. That actually saved me quite a bit of time. New players will have a harder time. But the sights are worth it. Especially near the end,
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I liked that this was an updated version of a classic puzzle game, the first I had ever played. Im not sure how it fits into the overall Myst franchise, story-wise, but for the most part it looked and progressed as I remembered. So if you had played to original, this is a must-have experience. Game play is updated enough to not frustrate those expecting modern puzzle games yet it stays true to its original intent. I highly recommend this game if you are a fan of the franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The remake is just brilliant. The puzzles are masterfully executed and perfectly integrated into the lore and environment, the feeling you get when you piece everything together is priceless. Visually this game is stunning, definitely one of the best looking game of the year. More than a few places have left me in awe, the level of details and environmental story telling is just insane. Some of the new places have gotten my heart race of excitement...Definitely one of the best game of the genre, in line wild Outer Wilds. I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing remaster in terms of graphic upgrades and full 3D world. Unfortunately the puzzles have changed, and are somewhat easier, but still the essence of what they did was kept. Would love a version with the original content in tact, but I can't really complain since this comes with an amazing VR version too. Stuttering is present in both versions, but they are working on it and since its slow paced, it doesn't detract too much. Overall it was an amazing nostalgia trip that made me smile many times over, thanks for making it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: 9.8/10I was giddy about the original game when I got it for Christmas as a kid. Let me simply say this - this is how you do a remake. A few clunky animations and glitches aside, which I am sure will get patched, this is a masterpiece that improves on a masterpiece. I truly appreciate the fidelity to the original while still updating and modernizing it, while also remixing most of the puzzles to be new and fresh while still feeling like they belong in the universe of the D'ni.They don't make games like this anymore, which is truly a shame. If you're on the fence, just buy it. Do it. It's worth the adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This new remake + reimagining of RIVEN is hands-down my Game of the Year. I was completely blown away. Cyan Worlds somehow improved an experience I didn't think could be improved. It's like stepping inside the best speculative fiction you've ever read and becoming a protagonist.1997's Riven was already the most compelling fictional world I'd ever explored, but there are some changes and expansions that the marketing for the new version hasn't even hinted at. I gasped. I laughed. At one point I cried. At one point I almost jumped out of my chair. Five stars out of five.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.I was 3 years old when the first Riven released, I still remember watching my brother and dad figure out this puzzle of a game. Some of my earliest childhood memories are getting lost in this world. I personally had no idea what I was doing, it was just incredible being able to point and click and adventure.Revisiting it in 2024 is just pure nostalgic bliss. And it feels amazing being able to solve this on my own. It's incredible how well Riven stands up after all these years.The visual storytelling is second to none.Tips for newcomers to this age: bring a pen and pencil, avoid hitting the 'sprint' button, take your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It's a surreal experience seeing it all in moving 3D, even after playing through the Myst remake. I haven't really noticed the changes but I played it quite young, I kind of miss the real actors in it but then seeing how that looked in Obduction I can see why they are going this way. Will be nice if one day video actors can be incorporated in 3D environments well. The game overall is beautiful and not having the images cut away makes it all make more sense spatially and I am understanding it all a lot more than I did as a child. I feel like a tourist in this game it pops up with achievement like a tour guide and i immediately start snapping away screenshots. It's nice to get lost in the world of it, I can't wait to get to the beehive, I could never get that far as a kid.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I realize this isn't going to be a very popular opinion, but unless you get this game in a great sale, I would take a pass.  By the way, this will be the first game I've ever reviewed that I didn't recommend.1. It's esoteric to the point of frustration.  I've watched multiple people play this and the reactions are all the same - basically what the heck is going on?  That should be the feeling during the first minutes of a new game, not the entire game.2. For those of us who loved Myst, this is NOT Myst.  Not that it needed to be, but you can play and enjoy Myst and still dislike Riven.  I loved Myst, including on VR.3. I enjoy exploring a virtual world - every nook and cranny.  But the game areas were difficult to move back and forth between, and the fast travel mechanism was incredibly annoying.4. VR - I bought this because it had VR support.  I played a majority of the game in VR, and found the control interaction to be hit and miss.  Maybe it was just that I was already frustrated, but when I finally ended up going back to the PC screen to play, I wasn't much happier.  I can usually tell ahead of time the games that I will return to in a couple years and replay - and there have been bunches.  Sadly, this isn't one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful. Thank you to all who made this happen. I played the original on windows 98 when I was a just a lad and loved it, this, this is great! The nostalgia is delightful and quality impeccable and the vr amazing. If you've read a negative reviews please be skeptical, so many people are so full of hate these days and should appreciate an actual good game that isn't price gouging micro-transactional shallow-plot garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Some thirty years ago, my brother and I were two little kids that hopped on our family's humble Macintosh IIci and became enamored and awestruck by an immersive 3D-rendered world that was Myst and then later Riven. It was very different from any of the sprite-filled 16 or 32-bit games at the time and seemingly beyond the scope of what two tiny grade schoolers would comprehend.We'd confuse our teachers as to why we would go to school drawing black triangles on the corners of our composition notebooks, complemented by a rune on front and square drawing on the first page, and then treating them as mystical teleportation books (and yes, with the added sound effects). Or bewilder our family by walking around the house with our hands stretched outright, "clicking" our way across the house. There was also never a shortage of Myst or Riven island drawings, or increasingly ornate Linking Books, strewn about our family and friends homes and classrooms. My brother even created an Atrus outfit for Halloween once. Eventually, my interests turned elsewhere in games, but Riven always maintained an impact on my brother. He even promised me that he would one day work for Cyan. At the time, I kind of shrugged it off as a cute but unrealistic dream.Riven had inspired my brother so much that for Christmas one year he didn't ask for toys or video games like a typical kid would, but instead a complicated 3D modeling software called StrataVision 3D, the very same software used to render scenes in the original Myst. I had no idea what my Dad was thinking to get his grade-school child an expensive piece of software that he may have no idea how to use, let alone for however long, but he did. With only the paperback manual, my brother went on to teach himself how to craft an impressive 3D island-world directly inspired by Temple Island in Riven and navigate it using HyperCard. And throughout his school years he continued to model and draw art for many of his projects because of this. Eventually, as an adult, he finally broke into the gaming industry and I figured that was the end of it.Much more recently, I returned home after living ten years abroad as an expat. I came home to find his computer on and that some kind of game was running on it. I was shocked to find out that he created a welcome home game in Unreal Engine to greet me. And woe and behold, the first thing I'm greeted by is the very island-world that he created as a kid. It was instantly recognizable and only something that we would understand, as we shared it together so many years ago. Somehow he was able to painstakingly port it over from that old 3D software and turned it into a playable adventure world. It was a small game to play through, but it was chock-full of inside jokes and childhood references to Macintosh games or pop culture we once used to enjoy as kids.I was also surprised when he told me that he got into the Starry Expanse Project, who were working on the remake of his favorite childhood game, Riven. Little did I realize that some thirty years later my brother would come full circle from the dreams and imaginations of his childhood self to end up contributing to the development of the very game that inspired him to break into the gaming industry in the first place. The fact that he achieved his childhood dream and pursued his inspiration due to this game has left me incredibly astonished and proud. Truly, there is no one in life that you will know longer than your own sibling and I only have one. I love him very much and this accomplishment is a memory I will treasure.I am buying this game once more to show how grateful and supportive I am to Starry Expanse and Cyan in remaking such a fantastic world and story to get lost in once again. Thank you for the impact and inspiration you've had on our lives.Edit: Clarifying that he was involved with Starry Expanse not Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning, and runs like a dream on my mid-level gaming laptop. The game's auto detected graphics settings were medium - high and I bumped it up to epic mode and it still runs nearly seamlessly. The changes to the puzzles are great, there are enough changes to keep old fans interested in the replay but it still feels like Riven in the atmosphere and story. I literally gasped when I saw some of the changes, in a good way. The textures, the water effects, unbelievably realistic. Having steam achievements is fun, too. i wish I had more thumbs so i could give it more than two thumbs up lol
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Brings back memories! The bundle finally compelled me to replay these classics. Absolute gems and very nice remakes. The only thing I’d wish for is for this game to do well enough to get some sort of post launch updates adding in support for advanced UE5 features and ray tracing. Incredible work from a truly passionate team/company. Please never change.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like Cyan did everything right, here.They made no compromise in remaking the original world from 97 into one that feels real and compelling to walk through in the 3rd dimension. The attention to detail, both in the recreation of the original environments and sets, as well as bringing those environments into a modern graphical context is clearly visible. There was a lot of care put into this project, and I am happy to see that.The puzzles differ slightly from the original, in some ways for the better (better integrating puzzles into the world, having them make more sense in context, etc.), but they are still pretty rewarding to solve. I think between Cyan's current track of modern remakes, Riven far outshines the 2020 Myst remake in just about every way. There is a lot more integrity preserved this time around, and while my current recommendation for playing Myst in the modern day still teeters between the 2020 remake and realMyst, I have basically 0 issue recommending the 2024 Riven remake to anyone interested in pursuing the Myst series.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this expecting yet another ...After not personally connecting with Obduction or Firmament, if you'd pitched me on the idea of modern Cyan doing a full-on Riven  with changes to puzzles and additional content, given how much the game means to me, I'd have urged them to play it safer...Thankfully, I dove right in without reading anything about it, so the changes were a complete surprise!I'm delighted to have been preemptively proved WRONG, and have been enjoying the heck out of this version. Some of the puzzles have been tweaked to be a bit more intuitive, others have been replaced entirely with new puzzles and mechanics that are more accessible, (especially for the hearing impaired) and what I've seen of the new content has intriguing world-building implications that don't really feel like they retcon or go against the spirit of the original.That said, the old game is still well worth playing, because it feels darker, dirtier, and scarier; (I don't have a VR headset but assume that the increased visibility and cleaner textures here and there were necessary visual comfort changes)It's probable that making small tweaks to a masterpiece is much easier than creating from scratch, however... , but if design changes are on the table, and THIS is what Cyan is now capable of, part of me hopes they remake Myst 3, 4, and 5 at this quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth buying and supporting the developers if your an old school fan or have never played it before. The game is the byproduct of developers who care. It holds up after all these years, so to speak. Thank you for your hard work and dedication in developing this perfect remake! And most importantly, making me feel like I actually am revisiting Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I will never forget begging the game shop clerk to let me try out this mysterious game I had found while browsing the PlayStation section: It had what looked like an alien knob celery on the cover and appeared enticing. The clerk begrudgingly put  in the demo unit, which was meant for adult paying customers, not 11 year old kids with no money. Instantly I was taken to a world unlike anything else I had ever seen. I didn't know about , or -likes. After five minutes of walking around Temple Island my demo session was over and I had learned: Games could be more than virtual playgrounds for kids. Many years later I tried to get into  for real, bought the version on Steam, the one on iOS, but never got very far, to be honest. Now, in 2024, I'm playing this stunning Unreal Engine showcase and I'm in awe. Getting to walk ALL AROUND all this puzzle machinery in full 3D helps so much with actually understanding what is expected from me. Currently I'm switching between the 2D and VR versions, and both have their advantages: The 2D version runs like a dream, in luxurious high definition, not an ounce of jank to be found. VR is a different story. While there are plenty of comfort features – I can actually use smooth locomotion without getting sick thanks to the vignette feature – the shadows look all wrong and flickery, you easily clip into objects and the resolution obviously is limited to what your kit delivers (I'm using a Quest 2), taking away some of the visual sheen. I probably won't play the whole game in VR, but getting to see what different islands look like in stereoscopic 3D is such a privilege, I imagine telling that to 11 year old me, that one day in the future I would explore theses places with a computer strapped to my face, amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I like puzzle games & VR but I don't recommend Riven in its current implementation.Graphically its really well presented, the art style/originality and quality are very good my principal issue with Riven is pacing and gameplay. The main issue is that once you are well into the game there is no way you can progress unless you start making handwritten notes about things that you learn... how the hell do you do that in VR? You can't you are forced to remove the headset or go back into the game in monitor mode.The second issue is its very easy to miss something in VR that would otherwise be much clearer or obvious to monitor mode, which then makes the game difficult to work with... its not a puzzle at that point its just frustration having to retrace your steps looking for some detail you may or may not have missed or retry interaction objects that should just work.Finally I get the need to not spoon feed players, but in Riven knowledge is given to you in such a poorly thought out way its almost as if they assume you've played Riven before and come to the game with outside knowledge. For the most part things just don't make any kind of sense, you move through the islands completely unaware of what is going on around you with no real purpose other than to find things to do. When you are given some knowledge its dumped on you, who wants to read a huge hand written journal in VR or notes that you can't carry around with you or maybe you can but you can't get it to work...In summary its not been properly play tested in VR imho, you have to rely on external information to make sense of what is happening making the experience needlessly frustrating. Yes its hard but hard in the wrong way imho because things are too easily missed and not explained well if at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely yes I would recommend this game!  Riven was originally one of my favorite games and it's now become even more so.  I've played the 2024 Riven in both the PC and VR versions.  The PC version is terrific but the VR version is .....just ....WOW!  Cyan is amazing with graphics, and they're devious in the way they develop puzzles!  So much fun.   Like many of the others, I would have preferred to see Rand/Atrus but this works too.Looking forward to more Cyan games - new or remakes.  Keep it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The Myst series has always been a favorite of mine. What they've done with this game is nothing short of amazing.  If you haven't played through these games at least once in your lifetime, you should definitely give them a shot.  The story gets progressively better and better with each new game.  Good job with this remake and freshening up the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Its a awesome game but parts of the VR version are hard to use. Still good and worth a positive reviewIn order to read the books, you have to turn your wrists in un natural ways and it can be painful. Taking a screenshot of the book does not show the regular print in the screenshot section like the flat screen version does.So any in game hints that you need to read and you are stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original, this ended up being more than I hoped for. There's a bit more to it than a simple remake. The environments are absolutely beautiful and superbly detailed. The puzzles are challenging, with some changes from the original that you might not anticipate. It really is an expansion on the original Riven in all the ways that matter.There are a few issues that stick out to me:1. The animation on the characters is pretty lackluster; it appears they animate at a lower frequency than the game's refresh rate; there's some unnatural clipping/sliding when characters are manipulating objects2. The inventory system is pretty jank; if you open the satchel when close to objects or walls, the contents will be behind the obstruction and won't be clickable3. The built-in screenshot system is too inconvenient; you might as well use the Steam screenshots feature so you don't have to go through multiple menus to get to it; I also noticed that some of the earlier screenshots I took had become somewhat illegible vs what I saw in the game when I took them, not sure if that's a bug or not4. Waiting for unskippable animations gets old and tiresome quickly, especially when you are jumping around different islands searching for clues; this remains an issue with the fast travel system5. I only found out after a game update that I missed a clue due to a bug that has since been fixed (the steam switch); thankfully I had enough other information that it didn't prevent me from completing the gameThe game is very much worth your time, even with these small blemishes. This is particularly true if you're coming from the original and crave an even deeper exploration of the world than the original offered.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of the original games (yes, even End of Ages) and the books. I'd been looking forward to playing this since I heard about the Starry Expanse Project years ago. I enjoyed the Myst remake a couple years ago and this hit about the same. It's somewhere between a remake and a re-imagining. The new things that were added didn't feel out of place. I think the weakest parts of the game were the character animations, as well as the tram and cart rides. They didn't quite feel as exhilarating as the original. Maybe it was the jittering, maybe it was the sound quality. It just wasn't as much fun to ride from island to island.If you were a fan of the original, I think you'd enjoy this as well, but go in with the understanding that it isn't the original Riven.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of Cyan games for a long time. I personally enjoy playing Riven, and it is one of those memorable games from my childhood. I was super excited to hear and eventually buy the new game. This remake is truly what most remakes wish they could be, a faithful update and improvement to the game. Cyan went beyond simply remaking the game in a 3D environment. Puzzles that needed better explanations and more logical solutions were improved. All in all, Riven easily knocked it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: THE best puzzle-adventure game ever. You need to pay attention to the world and understand it... and take your time. You'll be greatly rewarded. Since playing the original Riven in the '90s, I wished I could find another game that gave me that same sense of immersion and that same rush when figuring out how it all made sense. This remake manages to provide the same experience in a more polished game where all details have been carefully considered and tuned to make it an even better experience. And it's gorgeous!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. They changed enough to make it meaningfully different but it's still recognizably Riven.And I really really really like the change to how the domes work; it's such a better narrative justification for what's going on. And the interaction is so satisfying. They also removed most of the "hope you realized that was clickable while you go in circles for hours" puzzles or made them substantially more obvious, such as the open/close door trick on Boiler Island.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake of a landmark title. Some differences are in place but the original 1997 release still exists and does run well on modern hardware for purists. Most impressive to me is how well the game communicates the feeling of the original prerendered 3D art. For those new to the game, in terms of modern titles Riven is closest to the Outer Wilds or Return of the Obra Dinn in its world and puzzle design. Gaining an understanding of the world is how one progresses, and there isn't anything quite like the way things 'click' in this game. One complaint I do have is that the achievements take some of the mystique out of the game, specifically by naming locations/providing more detail on art and objects you find in the world. Personally I prefer drawing my own conclusions on things in the world without the pop-ups butting in. The in-game notebook is also a bit underbaked, although a great idea. Taking notes on a pen and paper is still the ideal way (and you will need to take notes).I recommend disabling the steam overlay for your first time through.Bring a notebook, try not to look up any hints, and enjoy your first experience on Riven. You only get one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a much better game than the original, if you liked the original, you'll be so pleased with the things that have been added and upgraded. Also the graphics are amazing! Yes, it's a slightly difficult puzzle type game, if you aren't in to taking notes / photos of stuff to figure out clues then maybe it's not for you. However, if you enjoy a unique challenge that has only gotten better in this remake, then it's a great game! Would also HIGHLY recommend picking up Myst as well, this really IS a sequel and although not necessary, it is just fun to know the story. :)

_childDocuments_.review: breathtakingly beautiful, with many of the sharp edges sanded off or replaced.the new puzzles and updates to existing puzzles all play really nicely and still present an engaging and sprawling challenge- even for those of us that are returning for the second or third time. In many ways the new puzzles make more sense as part off the world. I understand that designing engaging puzzles is incredibly challenging, but this team has absolutely nailed it.Visually, this is the best the game has ever looked, the textures are fantastic and combined with the sound design create an incredibly believable world. so many moments in this game you are confronted by some strange unknown object that is simultaneously completely believable- you know exactly what it would sound and feel like to tap on that giant rusted steel plate, and you feel that you could. this has always been Riven's greatest strength. if you love the original- buy this and play it, the updates are well done and make the game feel fresh. If you have never played- buy this version and play it, it will surely be the definitive version of a  wonderful game

_childDocuments_.review: Liked it a lot. I did not play original and game structure reminded me of Outer Wilds. There are some occasional stutters, but overall it works fine.The only issue is that game ruined marble puzzle for me. Gehn's journal contains picture of directions and shapes which points to the dome and exactly matches dome structure. But if you try to match shapes using this information, you fail. It does not help that puzzle has no feedback loop: solution either works or not. I do not understand why that piece of incorrect information was added to the game, as puzzle can be solved without it.

_childDocuments_.review: man this game occupied such a large space in my early years. being just a kid transported to this place was great. a lot of this made this play-through, of course, nostalgia-driven. however the twists to the puzzles made this play-through just as rewarding. this is a game that grabs attention and demands you to keep a close eye on details. my head start returning to this game made my play time rather short. but it is a world one easily can get lost in for hours on end, scouring through journals and notes and random scribbles to make sense of it all. highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved the game since I played Myst when it first came out (but never Riven).  I did get some hints when I was really stuck but this game reminds me of an intricate puzzle box cube.  You don't want too many spoilers to kill the value of the puzzles, but I forgot how unforgiving 90's game puzzles can be.  I was lazy and found all the totems but never wrote down the symbols or order thinking "oh I'm DOING it, but when it comes to the end I'll just key in the guide's solution"... NOPE it's random.  So DON'T take any shortcuts, take lots of notes and remember - nothing's going to pop up saying "do you want a hint?" no matter how long you stare at a puzzle.  Just remember with the hints - it's hard to appreciate this absolute work of art if you don't give it a good try before you get hints.Also the SCREENSHOT function is AWESOME and remember - use the NOTES feature to add in important details that go with your screenshots of things and places.  It makes it SO MUCH EASIER than little scribbled drawings on paper.

_childDocuments_.review: It's easy to see where all the love for this series comes from now.I played the original Riven and then this more or less back to back and can say this game is a treat for new and returning players. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remake of the 1997 classic with a couple changes here and there, though in my opinion they're certainly not bad ones. Except for the fact that all the standard doors now slide to accommodate VR folks, eugh.The only glaringly obvious issue I have with it otherwise are the character models. I recall seeing better back in Far Cry 3 and that was 12 years ago. But given you don't see them very often, this isn't the biggest issue, especially because the environment design and texturing is top-notch. The golden dome especially just looks real, I can't believe how good the texture work on that is specifically, and the whole of the game looks absolutely stunning besides which.If you're a fan of the original game or even if you've never played it, this is an easy recommendation. It's faithful enough that even a new player should have no problems jumping in and getting a similar experience.Edit: Looking at this again with a like-for-like comparison of the original, I'm surprised how much was changed and cut. There are many paths which no longer exist, and comparing screenshots to screenshots from the same locations, some areas feel very much smaller and likewise the distance between areas seems to have been shortened in some cases (albeit not too dramatically). If you're a fan of the genre you'll definitely need to play the original still for the authentic experience, but this remake is still fine all the same.

_childDocuments_.review: The terms "remake" or "reimagining" often provoke skepticism, frequently perceived as mere commercial ventures exploiting a fanbase's nostalgia. These projects might showcase enhanced aesthetics, higher resolutions, and better compatibility with modern hardware, yet they rarely offer substantial innovations to the original game. Therefore, when news of Riven's remake emerged, I was initially apprehensive.In 1997, Riven was celebrated as a masterpiece of environmental storytelling. Its visuals, narrative, and puzzles were pivotal in cementing the success of Myst. The question persisted: why revisit the islands of Riven after so many years? However, this new rendition of Riven is not merely a nostalgic journey but an entirely reimagined experience. The puzzles have been meticulously redesigned, the storyline has been expanded, and the previously subtle lore has been elaborated upon, rewarding those who delve deep into its intricacies.The visuals are nothing short of stunning, a testament to Cyan, the small yet talented development team based in Spokane. Their dedication and craftsmanship have once again brought this immersive world to life. This remake is not just a game to be played; it is an experience to be fully embraced and lived. Although it is indeed a remake, it has been reconstructed from the ground up, surpassing its distinguished predecessor in every conceivable way.

_childDocuments_.review: Had the original on my dads computer never finished it This one is a substantial upgrade along with VR the puzzles have been redone and I think they are far better than the original as they aren't as cryptic. My only complaint is the original cut scenes had much more drama and weight than the remake does with its frankly not very impressive character models, they get the job done but Alex Vance from Half Life 2 looks way better and that was near 20 years ago. I see why they changed them as it would be weird in VR.Many consider this game to be one of the best point and clicks of all time mostly cause of how immersive and realised the world is, this world wasn't slap dashed Cyan put a lot of effort into everything from the culture and how the people of Riven live, to how water, food, and traversing the islands work. You can lose hours of time reading up the lore and wikis for this game if your into that sort of thing. Myst separated its puzzles in different worlds Riven has two big puzzles with hints scattered throughout the islands as well as unlocking travel to the islands. Myst is very linear there are worlds you travel to and you only have to do a puzzle in a certain world. Riven by contrast has clues to its two main puzzles everywhere to the devs credit there are hints to them but they're easy to miss. The game is slow paced for a reason and expect to do a lot of back tracking, you have to be on the look out constantly and you will need a sheet of paper or the note system in the game for this one. I confess I needed a walk through to finish it some puzzle elements were hidden so well that I was left scratching my head it was only upon watching a lets play that I saw there were hints I just didn't notice. Did I mention the puzzles are perfectly integrated into the world.I overall enjoyed this game it can be short at 10 to 12 hours(less if you use a walk through) story is great though I was invested and the game is really worth playing especially in VR I hear. Also as someone who recently beat the original this one is no where near as cryptic with bs puzzle solutions as the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun to explore and open immersive world, with clever puzzles weaved into things. It does a great job (especially compared to Myst) of making the puzzles feel involved as part of the world rather than arbitrary. The remake is very pretty and being able to explore the world freely is great. Unlike the one-to-one Myst remake, many puzzles have been slightly changed, massively reworked, or added, often to help incorporate the free movement into the world, reduce the amount of unnecessary obtuseness, or flesh things out a bit more. I never played the original but the consensus amongst older fans does seem to be that generally the changes are positive and also allow for a new experience for them. Personally I felt the puzzles were all really engaging and felt natural (i.e. nothing felt obviously like it stuck out as having been added to a pre-existing game), and having gone and watched a playthrough/explanation of the original and its puzzles I definitely understand and agree with the major puzzle changes. The only issue here is that, occasionally, an interactable object isn't entirely obvious like it would be on fixed screens. I definitely missed a switch or two because it blended into the background a bit too much. Overall it was fun! I enjoyed taking notes as I unpicked the codes in the world and put together connections between the lands, which was somewhat necessary to avoid excessive backtracking of the open world.

_childDocuments_.review: New Riven is everything the original was, but immensely more enjoyable due to the improved navigation and modern technology. It is just fresh enough too that there is still a good deal of problem solving, exploration, and discovery to be made for veterans of the original.Riven is a a beautiful game even on lower end hardware, and audio is absolutely part of the experience. Remember, audio was one of the few things that helped you feel the world was alive in the original game and not just a series of still photos. Be sure to play this game with good headphones or speakers!The character animation is pretty dang good, but not flawless. There are some awkward movements and clipping issues, but we aren't talking about an expensive AAA game here and I think we can easily forgive the rough edges. It's certainly an improvement over the previous Myst title.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most formative games of my youth and one I return to quite regularly, even if it's just to listen to the still incredible soundtrack by Robyn Miller. Riven is an absolute standout in the annals of gaming history as the overachieving if somewhat overlooked younger brother to Myst. It is exactly what the Empire Strikes back is to Star Wars or the Godfather II to the original. The superior sequel. It also has that unique bittersweet quality that some of the best things in life have: You can truly only experience them once. In trying to remake a classic, I think Cyan has made something special here. The people who developed this remake knew exactly what they were doing and who was going to buy this game. This IS Riven but it's a more self aware Riven that knows that some changes had to be made but they serve a dual purpose 1. to be more inviting to new players but 2. to change it up and surprise and delight returning players. No easy feat. They also absolutely NAILED the look of the original game. There are parts that look to my eyes like a cleaned up SGI render as if they brought back all the original models or uprezed original renders. It's just that good. They also kept much if not all of the original sound work which is absolutely iconic. While the music is much ballyhooed the sound design for Riven was pivotal in it's presentation.Praise be said, I do have some negatives:I had my doubts after playing the 3d remakes of Myst. Maybe its that you take your time a bit more to scan the information presented in each frame. Maybe its that your mind fills in the blanks with the limited information you're given forcing a more grandiose sense of the world. Maybe the faster pace of full traversal makes the world you're in feel a bit smaller. Or maybe it's some combination of all of these but something is lost in the jump to 3d and that feeling is definitely present here in this remake. It's something that I can't place my finger on but it's a definitely a sense I have. There's less atmosphere. Less of a feeling of solitude, or that you're being watched. Something feels missing.  Something inside me thinks "That's it?"Another bit of charm lost in the transition to realtime 3d is the character models. Seemingly seemingly a necessary evil the replacements are stiff and stilted. Worse, they have none of the charm of a Cyan hallmark that was even brought back for Obduction. Worse yet, in some instances they actively change the tone and pacing. A perfect highlight is the introduction sequence with Atrus, one I consider one of the best introductions to any piece of media, ever. The new version lacks the pacing and gravitas of the original and even comes off as somewhat jovial which is just the wrong tone. Here's a video that illustrates what I'm talking about so you can see for yourself: Lastly, some of the changes. I understand why some of the changes are there and in some areas they absolutely add to and deepen the experience. But in others, they feel like additions for the sake of additions. Change for changes sake. A perfect example of this is the area with the frog trap with the vent passage above on Boiler Island. I don't want to spoil anything and I know exactly why they changed that section but the new bit doesn't really much at all. It's essentially just a longer hall way. Granted, it's a very pretty hallway with a couple distractions. But it still serves exactly the same function. There's a ton more I can rant on but and I don't want to elaborate too much on the negatives because so much here is positive. It's amazing that they could get so close, or even nail something I think many have wanted for decades. The artists and game designers should be commended on their work. I hope they decide to make a brand new entry in the Myst series. One that picks up where Riven leaves off. If they can keep up the quality like they do here, I think it would be something special too.

_childDocuments_.review: This ain't your granddad's Riven!  It's better! :)  It's familiar enough to clearly be recognizable as Riven, but enough changes that it's like playing it for the first time - a fantastic accomplishment in my opinion.  Normally a "reimagining" is a red flag to me, but with the dev team Cyan has put together, full of like-minded nerds who love the franchise, I have been having an absolute BLAST exploring and taking  in the new lore.  They said the changes made were to make the story more consistent and fill in gaps among other thing - they're not messing around!!!  I've been giddy waiting for this ever since Cyan announced they were working on it (a couple of other Discord servers can attest to this ;) ). _childDocuments_.review: One of the strengths of many Cyan games is the feeling that you're a visitor dropped into a very real place that is simply unfamiliar to you. Riven is that, and more beautiful than ever, but also if you've played the original, it's also a homecoming. Everything's been cleaned up, some things rearranged and some lovely new additions, but it is still very much . It's an amazing sense somewhere between deja vu and nostalgia when you turn a corner and get that pure joy of "I've been here, I know this place!" (And the sounds! I laughed in delight the first time I got on the mag-lev and it made the EXACT noise I remembered.)If you've never played Riven, but like any kind of puzzle or exploration games, this is a must. It's a gorgeous, rich world, teeming with fascinating details in every corner. I highly recommend grabbing a notebook and penciling in a few leisurely days to get lost in a beautiful world.Having watched the Mysterium presentation: if you're all still reading comments, thank you so, so much. Riven was magical when I was twelve and I'm blown away that you've given us something that provokes the same joy and wonder almost thirty years later. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This remake manages to capture the feeling of mystery that the original game inspired. _childDocuments_.review: Riven '97 is my favorite game of all time, so this release has been the most hyped game release for me since the original. From the Cyan logo to the end credits, the goosebumps were back in full force, and I cannot express enough how faithful and thoughtful the remake has been to the original game. Having finished it, I can say that this  Riven, and not  a remake, and that is the biggest compliment I feel I can give it. The puzzles were thoughtfully reconsidered, and the world expanded upon in small ways that are both a love letter to Myst fans and a means of tying up the original's loose ends to create a more streamlined and complete experience. Some of the original's puzzles were fairly punishing when you solved them incorrectly but with the correct logic, but the new Riven's notebook system and careful puzzle re-imaginings allow for you to have all the tools you need to make connections and progress while being fully immersed. I do wish the notebook was a little easier to open and navigate, but this is a minor inconvenience for a massive step forward in the game's accessibility.The visuals are often so faithful to the original that, after the initial rush of seeing those landmarks in such high resolution, I was quickly transported back to the feeling of immersion and familiarity. Walking the world's paths in real-time creates a more connected labyrinthine experience. Part of me does miss the still images -- their compositional framing and subtle visual clues -- but I believe the conversion was worth it to create a truly immersive world.I also want to give a shout-out for the many accessibility options included to fine-tune the experience, especially for folks sensitive to motion sickness and in need of context captioning.Honestly, kudos, Cyan. Simply magical.
