_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a treat this was. It isn't just a Riven 3D remake - it's a complete re-imagining of Riven. This game gaslights you in the best way possible. You go from doubting your own memories, "I know in my heart of hearts that I used to go under this door... right? Right? Maybe I just forgot about this hinge pin?" to "Okay, now I know this is different, this 100% wasn't here before, they definitely changed stuff." Many puzzles have been altered, some puzzles have been removed, and other puzzles are completely new altogether. Even though the overall forms of Riven are the same -- the same islands, the same objects -- it's like a different meal with the same ingredients, but elevated and modernized.:1. It's about as close as you'll get to playing Riven again for the first time even if you already know the original game front to back, which is by far the best part about this remake.2. Do you miss those old feelings of "What on earth is this for?" or "Where do I go from here?" or "What am I missing?!" Well, you're in luck!3. The new puzzles exhibit a lot of good judgment overall. To change so much is a bold decision, but it's done really well here. The new puzzles feel right at home.4. Riven looks amazing, and it's a lot of fun to explore in 3D. There are lots of new details to discover as well. For instance being able to step outside in Gehn's 233rd Age made me audibly gasp. It always bugged me that you couldn't do that in the original. Lots of little improvements like this are scattered throughout the remake.5. The spinning domes overhaul... WHAT. Was not expecting that at all, but what a great surprise and cool mechanic.6. Lore accuracy improvements - you'll only notice this if you got into the original story of Riven, but the updated details are now a lot more consistent and make way more sense.:1. Some people may not like the lens item. While the original game did have an inventory system, it sort of evolved naturally with the story and was mainly just books. This time around, there is a lens item you'll need to find in order to progress, as it'll let you see things that are otherwise not visible. I just imagine someone getting stuck, and not realizing they actually don't have all the information available to them from the environment alone, unlike the original game. At the same time... when you're stuck, you explore. And someone who is exploring everything will stumble upon the lens eventually. But in my opinion this is the riskiest change to the game.2. While I personally enjoyed the addition of a second number system, I wonder if a new player would find it overwhelming. As a little kid, figuring out the existence of just one number system and how it worked (without using any guides) was already a tricky enough task for me back in the day. :1. Probably the only serious con on the list, but you can't skip stuff. In the original, you could skip FMV animations you've already seen such as the rotating room animations, or dialogue sequences, etc. You can't skip any of that now. Even the end credits are unskippable and come with each ending of the game - at which point it's faster to just Alt+F4 and re-launch.2. The CG human models... I mean, I get why they had to go this route, but I think the game does lose a bit of its charm not using real actors.3. If you're a die-hard Riven purist, you will find this remake to be a letdown if you were expecting exactly the same puzzles from before. 4. At least as of the launch date, there are intermittent stuttering issues with the game, at least on max settings. It's not a serious issue, but it's occasionally noticeable. My hardware is strong and often has no issue maxing out most games, so I don't think it's a performance thing. There seems to be some kind of issue with how assets are loaded in that block the UI thread or something. Considering the kinds of bugs that other people are reporting regarding load-in, I think there is probably room for improvement here.:I had a lot of fun with this remake. Both old and new players alike will get a fresh experience. It's quite an awesome and surreal feeling to revisit familiar territory after so many years and still get stuck -- I love it. I hope other studios take note, because this is how you remake a game. My thanks go out to Cyan and the Starry Expanse teams for making this happen!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only an hour in and I am blown away by how Cyan has not only given a timeless classic a gorgeous 3D makeover, but has also managed to add content in a way that feels perfectly natural and seamless. I have dreamed of this remake becoming a reality for *years* and it looks like it has been well worth the wait!!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Cyan has shown again why they are truly Grand Masters of "The Art". No game (or series) has explored such a rich depth of story-telling, world crafting and atmosphere quite like Myst (and Riven). When the remake was announced, I could not contain my excitement to FINALLY be able to revisit the amazing world of Riven again in full 3D. Add to that the ability to finally visit Riven in VR, a dream I've had ever since experiencing Myst in VR.Well done Cyan! I have been singing Riven's praises since it released in 1997 when I was just a child, and I will continue to do so for many years! Thank you so much for the amazing love and care you've poured into this remake!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: So far I love it! I'm impressed that Cyan has done such a good job recreating the look and feel of classic Riven. I've been playing in VR (Valve Index), and am almost at the end.I have encountered some small glitches, mostly shadows in one eye that don't show up in the other. I've also encountered regular crashes if I try to use the submarine in VR, it will crash when it arrives at the next stop. So I had to use the submarine in flat screen. Also, the same day I am writing this review, I liked to age 233, and experienced a crash while waiting for Gehn in the cage (In VR). I repeated it a couple times and got the same result, but was able reload and play flat screen till I got Gehn trapped in the prison book. I will come back later and continue in VR. . . . I assume these are problems that will be fixed in time.Anyway, I am loving it! Good job Cyan.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the story and the graphics of the game, they are both so intricate and consume you from the moment you begin playing. The puzzles were hard and I won't lie, I had to get some help online a few times toward the end but they were really enjoyable regardless. I think it's worth the time it took to play and its price. So if you're interested, I would tell you to just go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake and not a remaster, but it's still Riven. The worst part of the game is not being able to click super fast to zoom around. PC mode is beautiful even if it turns my machine into a furnace. VR needs control improvements, it's not consistent in how you can interact with ladders, and some of the puzzles are restrictive in how you have to interact with them.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A great (but rough) reimagination of the original game, a lot of the world has been reworked with new puzzles and things to see while staying true to the original.The roughness really comes down to the characters being out of place, the models aren't bad per se, but they just don't fit the artstyle of the game. You've got this beautiful photorealistic world with weirdly cartoony smoothed out characters that stick out like a sore thumb.The animations are just unpolished and break quite often, the props used don't follow the characters animations well. It's honestly quite disappointing after hyping the new animation system up.If you can look past this, it's a really fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10-Quick Summary-While missing puzzles, the old live action sequences, and being an easy mode version of the original. I believe this still holds up as rendition of Riven for those who may not have the same patience as you needed for the original game.I hope Cyan, will finish up the rest of the puzzles missing from Riven. Then go on to create more games. The Age's are so beautifully crafted, most games today can't capture that same magic or intrigue.As a fan of this series and playing all of the myst games (except the MMO), i was very much excited to get this.This is an easy mode version of Riven, and while not missing much of the Awe that was in the Original, it is MUCH shorter and less exploration of the world.While i wish they added a few more options for color blind people (The Marbles still were a challenge i had to look up), the rest of the game scratched that itch that only so few games even get close to.A lack of the old integrated videos were also something to be missed. The acting of the old games still holds up, and wished there was an option to show them, EVEN if they broke immersion just because they added such a feel that even today games have yet to capture with 3d Animated characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: grew up with myst III, since myst and riven came out a bit before my time and as a kid and i don't think we owned it. played through myst once, but never tried riven. friend mentioned this came out and took a look and im seriously impressed. love the worldbuilding, the puzzles actually make sense in the context of the world, and it doesn't answer Every Single Question which is something that bugs me about modern material. leave me some mystery damnit. from what i can tell it's a fairly faithful adaptation of the original, with some adjustments to architecture or puzzles with a few callbacks.tiny bit of jank in places but nothing that took me out of it; textures taking a second to load in on one or two items, loading times being a little goofy, animations not quite snapping perfectly etc - minor in the grand scheme i suppose.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! Just Wow! I Played Myst and Riven when they originally came out. I had a coffee cup, hat, posters,tshirt, the novels, and the Myst to Riven coffee table book. I even got my "Book of Atrus" signed by Rand Miller. I'm such a huge Myst/Riven fan. I've been following the Starry Expanse project for the last few years and was thrilled when Cyan took over. And today I began playing the game and I'm overwhelmed by the graphics, smoothness, and new twists. Absolutely fantastic remake and way more than I even expected. Great job to all involved!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of puzzle games, I cannot seriously recommend this one. I think most people that have enjoyed this game must have enjoyed it purely on a nostalgic basis. The pacing of the open world puzzle game is very poor. There is an incredible amount of running back and forth that becomes increasingly painful as you wait for 15-20 second long animations for things to open or move you around. The puzzles themselves didn't quite feel like real puzzles and were mostly unrewarding to solve. Overall, it was a disappointing experience after reading many of the reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: While familiar with the original, I'd never played it, so I came into this version completely green. First and foremost, the puzzles are not nearly as convoluted and nonsensical as the masses would have you believe. Having cleared the game with no outside assistance, the greatest challenge I faced was missing an essential interactable and wandering around aimlessly for a few hours, which highlights how tedious all the traveling apparatuses can be. I'd like if the world felt more alive and not just waiting for the fabled "Protagonist" to come and explore all its mysteries. The environments look very nice; people and things, fantastical. Animations are kinda janky. I really appreciate the (perhaps comically) extensive options.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I love Riven and bought this to support Cyan, and will not be refunding it. But this game STUTTERS. Reproducible consistently in certain areas like something is loading and blocking the render thread. This completely ruins immersion, and I can't imagine what it's like in VR. I'm just having a normal walk and then LURCH. Will be hitting 150-200FPS then all of the sudden "oopsie!" and the engine is having a fit leaving a freeze frame motion blur imprinted on my retinas. And always in the same spot so you know it's coming and just sort of cringe as you try and climb a flight of stairs  where you know this is about to occur but don't know on exactly what step it triggers. I can't imagine what that's like in VR, but I imagine not good. As an example, just walking up and down the stairs on the first island I can trigger this with 100% consistentcy.I can accept a bit of jank and engine chug here and there --  but it's frankly too frequent and too apparent for me to be able to tune it out and have a good time.If this gets fixed/patched I will update my review, but i was SO HYPE for this and now I'm kinda glum. This may seem petty, but too many games these days seem to be content launching with a performance profile like this. It really feels to me like some additional tuning or finesse around when assets are streaming in could go a long way.FWIW - despite being able to hit a consistent 150+ on high/epic settings, in an attempt to reduce this I've turned on DLSS in ultra performance mode and dropped everything down just to ensure that things aren't thermally throttling or smth. The stuttering, it does persist. In the same spots. Every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is coming from someone who has only played through the Myst 1 remakes and not touched any other games in the series)I have not finished the game yet but a few hours in at the time of writing this review, having worked through a few of the islands z but I've seen enough to know that this is one of the most beautiful games I've ever seen. The art style and fidelity genuinely makes you feel as if you're walking around in 90's cgi in real time, something that I wish other games tried to do (the latest remake of Myst 1 did NOT do this which I found somewhat disappointing however realmyst masterpiece edition actually does and is my preferred version of the original). Each island manages to be pretty unique and there are some really really cool locations to visit which really can fuel the motivation to work out the puzzles.As I've said I'm only a few hours in atm but I find the puzzles in this game to be some of the most fair puzzles ive played in a game, because alot of the puzzles aren't really typicql puzzles but more about learning the logic of a dreamy yet intuitively familiar world. The puzzles don't feel like puzzles designed to be puzzles for the sake of gameplay but rather something someone in the world would actually create to serve a practical function. Myst 1 hinted at this sort of puzzle design with ages like channel wood for example but riven greatly improved its execution and scope of that philosophy. It probably isn't for everyone but if you actually are patient with it you will start to understand it's far less arbitrary than other typical point and click adventure games (like Sierra's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moon logic puzzles). Just go at it from the perspective of learning a new place rather than typical adventure game puzzles. All in all this pretty much turned into an instant classic and I don't have any complaints whatsoever, especially for the extremely generous price it's being offered for
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic re-envisioning of Riven from what feels like the ground up, done by the original creative minds behind the original Riven from 97! Puzzles are new and different- but also the same in intent. Playing the game felt like hearing the true story of Riven after hearing a slightly miss-translated version for years. So very close, but the changed details just *make so much more sense* than they did in the original, which I still love to this day.Cyan did the right thing by making the changes they did, and the environment is *fantasticly* recreated in the visual department. It feels like the original Riven in all the ways that matter while still being *just different enough* to not be a total 1 to 1 remake. If I had to recommend a version of Riven to play, i'd be hard pressed to chose one over the other, but as far as execution of the environment and aesthetics and puzzles go- this is the version to go with.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: The Myst Series will always hold a special place in my heart for many reasons.  One thing i really love about it is it doesnt portray itself as a normal puzzle where the puzzle is straight forward.  Instead it presents it self as a living world you happened to discover where through attention to detail and other means you can truly feel as if you are solving puzzles but exploring a world built on the logic of if it really existed.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed it. I remembered almost none of the solutions for the original Riven so I am not sure how similar they are. But I can tell you moving around is 1000x better. Game ran beautifully for me. I really appreciated the instant screenshots, cuts down on backtracking dramatically. I feel like it's a bit shorter than the original game but I enjoyed it too much to care, worth the purchase to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: For those who have played and loved the Riven of old, this version is a great update.   However, it is more than just "realRiven", the puzzles have been completely reworked (and in many cases, completely changed) so that it is a whole new experience.  The use of the Unreal Engine makes for an overall gorgeous experience that you'd expect from Cyan.   PROS:  Beautiful graphics, smooth UI, new/re-imagined puzzles.CONS:  The human character modelling and animations are almost embarrassingly bad and jarring in contrast to the fine detail of everything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Fasten your seat belts for the maglev trip, folks, because... this is not the Riven you might remember. And I think this is a good thing - Cyan no doubt gambled on the idea that players of the original game would get it, remember how everything worked, and then go, "Whoa, wait a minute, what's THIS?" when certain things turn out very differently. I know I certainly did. (There is in fact an achievement for relying on the familiar solution to a certain puzzle. The solution in question no longer works, but they're glad you remember!)The chief gripe people are going to have, of course, are the character models, particularly given how appallingly bad the models were in the remake for Myst. My own fear regarded how they would handle Gehn, portrayed by the late great John Keston, who died in 2022. (I had hoped he would make 100 - he would have, if he had lived to December of this year - but 97 was a good age. Especially for a guy running MARATHONS at that age!) I will confess that I found the models a little... off in some respects, but certainly less jarring than the remake for Myst. Then again, to be honest, except for perhaps the lore involved, I did not play this game - or Myst for that matter - for the characters (except perhaps for Gehn, as previously mentioned)... I played it for the scenery. And HOO BOY, does this game deliver on that score. I must have taken maybe two dozen screenshots from various angles of the dome alone.Without giving too much away, certain elements of this new Riven are a LOT more open than the original, with a lot more room to explore. If you're like me and you're a sucker for screenshots - as well as wondering just what lay beyond some of those doors (and other things as well) - this will be right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely incredible remake. Exceeded my expectations many times over.If you're a fan of the original, you'll love it. The game is visually impressive. Exploring the world of Riven freely in 3d makes it feel more real than before. I would have been fine if that was the only change, but the puzzles have received an update, as well. I won't say too much in a review, but your first peak inside one of the spinning domes will leave you stunned.For those that are new to the series, I'd still recommend it. The Riven remake is not merely playing with nostalgia. But get it with the Myst remake if you haven't played the prequel already.My only real complaint is that some of the animations are clunky. I understand why why the developers can't use FMV in an environment the player can walk around in, but at the same time, the lack of quality in character movement leaves me feeling like something was lost in the upgrade.Suffice to say, the Riven remake that us fans have been wishing for all these years has finally arrived, and it is more satisfying than we could have anticipated.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous re-imagining of one of my favorite games of all time. I feel like it's not nearly as difficult, and by extension, you don't have as much opportunity to engage with the lore and the world, which is a real shame. Arm yourself with patience and a notebook, play the original, and then return to the remake to revisit those places you fell in love with!
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I have the original game, so my opinions are based on the previous game and my expectations for a modern remake. I absolutely love that Riven is now in HD with 360-degree vision; experiencing it is almost like playing Riven again for the first time. However, there are a few things that I could be more satisfied with.  I'm a bit on the fence about changing the puzzles, however, I understand that with the new system/game engine, the old puzzles may be a bit too simple and would be completed too quickly; the previous game took longer to complete because of the need to repeatedly click through a series of images, but with the new game engine, you can analyze and move through areas much more quickly.  I'm not a massive fan of the new "Starry Expanse" area: moving between Ages was accomplished by "linking books," which was part of the original Myst/Riven lore; substituting the linking books with the Starry Expanse changes canon, so I don't like it very much. I'm also on the fence about the bridge being destroyed, but I understand the bridge might make moving between islands too quickly and possibly affect the order in which the player is intended to visit them; it also reinforces in the player's mind the understanding that the world is falling apart. Sound and ambient music are still atmospheric, which is excellent, and subtle additions like the destroyed tram are also nice additions that breathe a bit of new life into the game. Lighting and texturing are great, but even with textures set to the max, textures should be higher resolution. What I feel ruins the game's atmosphere and immersion are the animals and characters; they don't look realistic! Please, Cyan! take a look at photorealistic characters of games like Call of Duty MW I-III as a reference to improve your characters, and if you can't improve the character models on your own, outsource help; but from observing the character models from both Myst and Riven remakes, it seems like your 3D modelers aren't very good at creating character models, and may need a bit of outside help to polish things up - I say this without malice, only love for your creation (original and remake) and hope that you'll make Riven even greater.Thank you, Rand, Robyn, and Cyan, for creating a fantasy world I could lose myself in as a kid and an adult.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: I started this right after I finished Myst. As I mentioned in my review for Myst I had never played these before but I always wanted to when I was a kid. To play these in VR was quite a treat. There are some big differences between Riven and Myst. The graphics, visuals, and atmosphere of Riven is miles above Myst. Not that Myst is bad by any means. I was just super impressed with Riven's world. I also felt the puzzles had a lot more depth. You could tell the developers wanted to make it better in almost all aspects. On the other hand, I did run into a lot more bugs with Riven (playing in VR anyways). I had almost zero issues in Myst. However in Riven sometimes the game would let me walk partially through a wall, my vision would go black but I could still hear things. however I was stuck and would be forced to reset. Also in some vehicle transitions the game would crash. I could remedy this by turning off the vehicle transitions but that's one of the coolest part about playing the game in VR. It didn't damper the experience and I've read they're working on a patch for this issue. Overall awesome game highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong fan of the original game (quite literally, I remember sitting in my father's lap as a small child playing through it together!) this remake is absolutely breathtaking. The visuals are beautiful, and exploring this world again, one that I spent so much time in as a kid, is absolutely heartwarming. I have monumental praise for the team behind this game.However. As others have pointed out, and as I came to notice quite quickly, things HAVE changed. Change is not always bad. Change can be quite good. It's bringing me new joy to explore this world again and find that the puzzles I once knew have been changed, and seeing that I would have to figure it out all over again. However... it seems that many of the new or remade puzzles are simpler than their old counterparts? Maybe that's just me. And if not, maybe that's a good thing? Some of the original puzzles were very obscure. Perhaps a more approachable game is better. But still, I can't help but feel a twinge of sadness and disappointment when coming upon some of my favorite parts and seeing that they'd been drastically altered or removed altogether. Rest in peace to the old entrance to Ghen's lab. You ate so many hours of my life for a red herring.All in all, I still recommend this game, both to newcomers and fans of the original such as myself! As much as I wish I could have seen the full original game in all its glory, I think what we've gotten is more than enough to satisfy most people. I know that I for one am happy to just see this beautiful, magical place brought to a new era, where I can enjoy each and every inch of this world once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake. I do wish they had added some kind of indication of where to find  i spent far too much time struggling before i discovered it. It was def my bad for assuming the area was unexplorable but with how much they definitely catered to returning obsessive players i think ti could have been done better maybe by simply . Otherwise i loved it, even with the frustration of the new stuff :D
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: This reimagined Riven is absolutely beautiful. My PC is somewhat below the minimum requirements, but nonetheless, when using the graphics settings recommended automatically, it is playable. There are times when I come to an area I haven't recently visited, and have to wait while the visuals are rebuilt. Perhaps this is due to lack of RAM?It's a great pleasure to explore the world of Riven with more freedom than the original version allowed. And the changes to the game offer intriguing new challenges to old hands.System: Core2 Quad, 8 GB RAM, Gigabyte RTX 3050 with 6GB VRAM
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original game I have to say, it's a great game and a great remake (coming with some slight changes)The graphics are beautiful, it recreates the locations of the original faithfully and  makes them come to life.I really love the worldbuilding and storybuilding, have been for the original and do for this remake.It's a testimony to the original pre-rendered graphics that we only now get an accurate representation of a real-time rendered riven but oh does it look beautiful.Yes it changes details and puzzles from the original but at least for me those changes all seemed to serve to make the game more cohesive.The few puzzles I felt were a bit too much of a stretch in the original became easier while still retaining their character. One problem I have to talk about is that there are stutters (probably when either new parts of locations are loaded in or shaders are loaded). Maybe it was fixed now (I played the game at the time of release) but it was definitely a conspicuous issue when I played a few months ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

_childDocuments_.review: Uncover a story of intrigue, betrayal, and a civilization teetering on the brink of collapse as you solve intricate puzzles to unlock the secrets of Riven. Built from the ground-up and expanded from the award-winning original game released in 1997.
_childDocuments_.name: Riven

name: Breakout: Recharged
detailed_description: The grandfather of brick-breaking games is back with some of the toughest challenges yet! Breakout: Recharged steps up the excitement with a fresh coat of paint, exciting power-ups, and another original soundtrack from award-winning video game composer Megan McDuffee. Breakout: Recharged will forever change what you expect from a brick-breaking title. The endless arcade mode and 50 challenge levels will push you to the limit of your skills. Don’t fret, however, as this wouldn’t be a Recharged title without game-changing powerups. Expect the aid of rail guns, homing missiles, and explosives to join the traditional multi-ball. You’ll need every tool in the arsenal and razor-sharp reflexes to climb the global leaderboards. Key Features: Old Meets New: Classic Breakout gameplay updated with refined control, and modern visual flourishes Power Up: Blast special bricks to pick up paddle-transforming power-ups a rail gun, explosive balls, missile launchers, and more Challenge: Compete in a series of 50 challenges designed to put even the most seasoned players to the test Compete: Reach the top of global leaderboards for arcade and individual challenge modes Bring a Friend: Play local co-op in every mode - breaking bricks is better together! Get in the Groove: Rock out to an original score by Megan McDuffee

short_description: The original brick breaker returns with its toughest challenge yet. Survive as long as you can in arcade or take on one of 50 challenges picking up game-changing power-ups along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: A blast from the past! Breakout: Recharged is a major update to a classic Atari 2600/80's arcade game. Featuring time limited upgrades to your player paddle (such as explosive shot, slow-mo, additional firing, etc). You have the option of the standard game, classic, and classic recharged. Each offering their own unique perspective on gameplay.Graphics are simple to nice. Complimentary to modern times. Sound and music are very good, apropos to the genre and update.As a side note, it is best played with the mouse as this mimics the classic roller seen in the arcade. One can use a controller but it is not as fine tuned in my opinion and subject to error.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Ill be honest, i've become quite addicted to these Recharged series of games. They are a lot of fun to play and unlock the achievements along the way. Breakout was one of the first games I played as a kid on My humble Commodore 64, and was in fact called Krakout! I absolutely loved it back then. Breakout games are essentially hitting bricks with a bat, along with multiple different power ups and in this version you only get one life as well so mistakes are very costly, which is where the skill comes in. Its high score based and there are online leader boards.I find it best using a mouse as you get much better precision with the bat but you can use a controller if you want.One of the best things is that the developer is responding and fixing issues, which in prev games was non existent so i want to give acknowledgement to that and long may it continue. There was an issue with the achievements unlocking but it has now been fixed via a patch which is great.Its worth picking up for the price if you love your Breakout games/clones.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: OK so this is an interesting game. I loved the original Breakout and this does not replace it but does offer a nice alternative.What I likeThe design is nice and the variety of challenges is great. The leader boards are also a good incentive to improve your game.What I dislikeThe BAT control can be to fast using  Mouse which in my view is the most accurate control method. The Ball dynamics do not seem to fit the angle of the bat and even though you hit the ball to the correct path a block can send the ball on an endless side to side motion. This is infuriating as the blocks are moving down the screen.What I would like to see* BAT Speed Adjustment (Remember not all Mouses are equal)* More accurate ball control from the BAT* Computer Generated Daily Challenges with a leader-board* And most of all a central Scoreboard that covers all the Recharged Games with challengesOverall a great yet somewhat frustrating version that I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: They fixed the mouse controls, finally. And now it's an amazing game. Games like this were meant to be played with a mouse/trackball/dial, not a joystick. So, finally seeing the analog controls fixed is great, and a reason to finally play this game. Several modes and challenges with global leaderboards keeps an eternal reason to keep coming back to this very fun take on a classic. Great to finally see Atari do as much with the breakout genre as Arkanoid, Wizorb, Shatter and others have done, since they invented the thing. Nice comeback, reminiscent of Space Invaders Extreme or Pac-Mac CE, delicious modern crack made of nostalgia.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: This is for me, the absolute best of the recharged series. The attention to details in the levelsand the variety of game play is fantastic. The walls in this game feel as though they have a life of their own. They advance, they shoot back, they explode. You really get the feel of an old school shooter, vibes of Arkanoid, Breakout, Warlords and Space Invaders all come to mind. The power-ups are great fun, rapid-fire, slow-down warp, extended paddles and path finders, all a welcome addition in times of crisis. There is the standard recharged game, 1 life, an extended version with 3 life's, a version with no power-ups and a ton of challenge levels which have been an absolute blast to play. Some of the levels are amazingly hard, but no matter how many times you die, you'll keep coming back, and I might add, it never loses it's charm or makes you want to quit in frustration. Graphics and sound, top notch, absolutely no complaints, and the mouse control is spot on. I'd absolutely recommend this game for retro and breakout fans, easy 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game really suffers from sticking too close to its source material. There's a lot of design flaws here that you don't see even on older games of the genre. The biggest flaw by far is the inability to manipulate the ball by means other than the paddle. This is important because the ball can end up bouncing around a mostly empty field near-horizontally (making you wait for no good reason), or you might not be able to bounce it without getting hit by an enemy bullet. This is not an issue in games like DX-Ball, where you can manipulate the ball through a magnetic force on the paddle. There's a lot more jank beyond that, like buggy menus, lengthy game over screen, buggy bullets, bad power-ups, etc, but suffice to say that the game is not nearly as polished as I expected it to be. It's also painfully obvious the co-op challenge mode was a complete afterthought, yet you are required to beat it to 100% the game. This is made worse by the fact that the stages are the exact same as the solo challenges. Talk about padding out a game...Honestly, just go play DX-Ball instead. It might be super old, but it gets a lot right that this doesn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Arkanoid and Super Breakout and was skeptical at first, because I really like a challenging game and almost all modern games are really easy. Well, this one doesn't hold back! It's a real pleasure to play and Atari really did an amazing job of modernizing Breakout without dumbing it down.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Its breakout. You've played breakout before, so you know if you'll like it before you play this version. The missions are great fun with some being quite challenging.Controlling your paddle with the mouse feels much better than with keys.Co-op mode provides a nice challenge for someone playing alone, but is very doable. One achievement requires co-op play.Overall 8/10, will likely grind single player for a good score.

_childDocuments_.review: Some good ideas here.  But only having one life and start all over again?  And the menu system is very bad to navigate.  Wasn't able to pick classic mode or quit the game.  There was no way for me to select those options using the controller.  Had to press ALT+F4 to quit.  Practically any other breakout or Arkanoid clone is better than this shovelware disguised as a good looking game.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: This is good fun and the local co-op, where two people have half the screen each, is really neat. I've played a few of the challenges, too, which were fun. I was a bit surprised there wasn't a mode (that I could find, anyway) that was actually like old-school breakout. The two things that nearly made me give it a "did not recommend", though, are:1) No Steam Cloud saves, so switching between PC and Steam Deck means you don't have your completed challenges etc.2) It doesn't seem that the saved game path/profile includes the Steam user ID, so opening this game on the Steam Deck with a second user meant they instantly had all my challenges etc completed.Those were pretty disappointing to me, especially given the game is Steam Deck Verified.

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to the Classic Breakout game but each round has only 1 ball.  Challenges make up a majority of the fun.  some creative one some just lucky. Power ups were interesting and added flavor to the game. Would have liked a version like the original and super versions to be included and to have more colorful bricks but if you like breakout/Arkanoid type games you will enjoy this one. If not this one won't change you mind.  Achievements are fairly easy to meet.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun modernized  game.  They managed to bolster the play mechanics with upgrades, but not turn it into  (not that  is a bad thing).  It helps to retain more of it's original  identity.In , you pick up upgrades that let your paddle shoot the blocks.  In , it has shooting upgrades (several of them), but you do not get to click to fire, it fires automatically.  This means you have to hover your paddle beneath the desired target until it gets destroyed while making sure the ball stays in play.  The game is controlled entirely by moving a single axis of control; just like the original .In my opinion, the funnest part of the game are the challenges.  It has online leaderboards so you can keep trying the challenge until you shave enough time to reach #1 on the list.   is a combination of skill and luck so it gives just enough challenge and frustration to keep you grinding your way up the high score list.I hear  for the  comes with extra challenges.  If this is true, I would really love to be able to purchase these extra challenges as an inexpensive DLC.  This would give Atari their exclusive bragging rights, but still allow other players to get to the same content for a small fee.  Everyone would win.The menu system in the game is clunky.  As far as I can tell there is no way to scroll through the list of challenges.  You have to click on one near the edge of the screen to reveal a few more.  Achievement notifications appear in the lower-right corner of your screen; perfect for blocking your view of the action.  You quit the game by going into the game settings menu.  That's weird, man.  Stop that. comes with local multiplayer where you have two paddles on screen at once, each sharing one half of the screen.  It sounds fun, but I haven't tried it yet.  Online multiplayer would have been a nice addition.Atari has really stepped up their game since the first Recharged game of .  How about a  to bring it up to the level of these newer games?In the original , you can press your paddle up against one side of the screen, and keep twisting the knob in the direction of the side of the screen.  The moment you turn your knob in the opposite direction, the paddle moves in the opposite direction.  In , when playing with a mouse, the paddle behaves like it is following an invisible mouse pointer.  If you move the paddle to one side of the screen and keep moving your mouse, the paddle stays locked against the wall but the mouse pointer that you do not see keeps moving.  Then you must move your stray invisible mouse pointer back into the active play area before the game paddle once again responds.  It is a minor issue, but if you are familiar with the original game it is something you will notice.  This might be more of an issue if you have multiple monitors; turning them off before launching the game might reduce help this issue.  I've seen a mouse pointer briefly appear in my adjacent monitor now and then.The music is nice.  The graphics do not have the glorious vector look that some of the other Recharged games have.  It is not a huge issue as the original  was not a vector game; but neither was .   looks very sexy in vector graphics. Very good aside from a minor mouse control issue Very good Upper side of adequate It has it where it counts Clunky Very happy with my purchase.  The  Exclusive challenges would be nice to get.  If you find it on sale it is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review, The game is good and fun but i have some issues about the game. I have played most of the recharged games, they are fun but for me breakout gets boring faster than the others. One thing I don't like about the game is that bricks spawn in the same spot every time you restart the game, and that decreases replay value more than the other games in my opinion. Shooting bricks are so annoying that sometimes I even get mad when you play the game and you will find out how annoying they are, trust me, especially when you have the bigger platform power up. Power ups can be crazy and some can distract you to make you lose the ball easily. I play it with my mom and it's fun to play. My favorite Atari recharged game is Centipede which is an amazing game. _childDocuments_.review: Sheesh! Sometimes it was more frustrating trying to complete Co-op challenge than Solo one. _childDocuments_.review: Breakout: Recharged is an officially licensed, console ported remaster/remake of the old Breakout game... which, in case you've been living under a rock since the 1970's, is a twist on Pong where instead of battling another player, the ball breaks various "bricks" floating in space.  Eliminate all the bricks without missing the bouncing ball, and you move up to the next level.  I shouldn't really have had to explain what Breakout is. Ultimately the problem here is that this is pretty shallow by todays standards, and there are many Breakout ripoffs that exceed the original game far better than this official remake does.  Dreamstone being an example, although it has terrible graphics, it's got advancement and progression systems that add a lot of value to the experience... there's nothing like that here, but the price is still eye-watering (considering you can play Breakout clones for free in a web browser). On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic low quality vector art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the mediocre 2D visuals.The game features extremely lazy, minimalist "art", of the type you normally expect to see in low effort Flash/browser games and mobile apps.  Considering this is being evaluated as a PC game, having the graphics phoned in like this isn't going to result in a high quality, visually impressive game that PC gamers are used to seeing.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 12 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 50,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.Breakout: Recharged has the ridiculous, laughable price of around $9 USD, it's not worth it given the defects and shortcomings with the product, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.  For comparison, the $9 asking price for this game could get you games like "DOOM", "Rainbow 6 Siege" or "The Forest".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  There's also thousands of free, superior quality games on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW #82Breakout: Recharged----------This will be the third entry that I've reviewed in Atari's Recharged series, and I'm pleasantly surprised at how much I like playing this one. The main reason for this is that the original Breakout game, in my opinion, had a formula that has been reworked to death in only a couple of ways over the decades, those ways being the addition of enemies and/or new block types and the addition of power-ups and/or weapons. For this reason, I normally shy away from "Breakout clones", because I've felt for years like if I've played one then I've played them all. Very few ever feel to me like little more than another tired retread down the same path, so to speak. Breakout: Recharged surprised me at being an exception.One thing that was definitely done right with Breakout: Recharged is its pacing. Bricks are always periodically appearing on screen and dropping down towards the player. This means that things are screen are routinely changing, and as a byproduct, there's never a point where you're frustratingly burning 15-30 seconds in an attempt to angle the ball just right so that the annoying, single remaining brick can be broken in order for you to progress. In fact, very quickly, you will find that the game's action picks up a heck of a lot within a minute or so of play. Cannon blocks and bullet bricks fire shells that are instant death should a player be unlucky enough to touch one, and power-ups occasionally rain down in groupings that can be almost overwhelming in number and density. (Note that most power-ups do not "stack".) The overall feeling of B:R is very fast-paced and sometimes chaotic, which I feel is a smart way of honoring Breakout's arcade roots. The feeling of the game's pace is reinforced with urgent-sounding electronic background music, moving visuals displayed behind the gameplay, and the slick and smooth way that the player's paddle moves along the bottom of the playfield.With this said, I found that the Classic game mode heavily subdued the game's action-oriented vibe and was actually boring to play, feeling more like a slog to get through than a game that I wanted to keep going for as long as possible. Additionally, in all game modes, the colors of the animated backgrounds felt muddy to me and not as vibrant as maybe they should. I checked to see if the brightness was set too high, but I didn't find a way to adjust it.All in all, though, I'm pleased with my purchase of Breakout: Recharged. As someone who was assuming before giving the game a try that it would be just another boring clone of classic Breakout, I happily give this title a confident recommendation. The developers did a really good job at making this a fun experience that harkens back to the golden age of arcade games and yet feels refreshed and not stale in any way. Co-op and challenge modes definitely help sweeten the deal.(NOTE: Co-op mode was not evaluated for this review.)

They didn't make the mistake made in Arkanoid Eternal Battle.Even the (basic) arrangement of the bricks and paddle lengt helps the game with the mouse (a spinner is not strictly necessary, but it is still recommended for higher difficulties).Arkanoid coin-op remains unbeatable. _childDocuments_.review: It's like if the devs of Tetris Effect and Lumines made a Breakout/Arkanoid game. I got this on sale for $5 and it was well worth the fun that I had, even $10 is a decent price for how much content this game has. The challenge mode is lengthy and has plenty of fun objectives and maps to do. If you're wanting more than what arkanoid has done in the past you're not exactly going to find it here. There are definitely innovations in the visuals. Seeing the sparks fly from the explosions and land on surrounding blocks brought me joy. The odd outrun 80's aesthetic mixed with a bit of psychedelic geometric visuals really makes playing this game a fun time no matter what. Also check out their Centipede Recharged game if you like this oneUpdate!Just finished the Co-Op mode. I had a lot of fun completing the challenges with my partner. My only gripe is that the control options kind of suck. I was only able to find a way to play with one player using the mouse while the other used the arrow keys. I wish this game had more controls customization. Also odd thing to notice but the Back and Retry buttons would randomly swap throughout our playthrough. Not a major bug but holy crap did it get annoying when I would hit the key to exit the stage only for it to switch on me and retry it instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, and is definitely an homage to the Atari VCS/2600 console game Breakout from the 1970s, I love the art style. My only real complaint is that the arc used to calculate how much the ball deflects when hitting the paddle isn't clear or may be too big. I would definitely give the paddle some curve to show what that arc is, and maybe back off. It just seems that unless you're really dead on center when hitting the ball with the paddle, the ball wants to go flying sideways. It should be a much smother transition.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I have an arcade cabinet and have played this using an iPac2 interface with a spinner and it works flawless. There is no custom binding for other keys (navigate menus etc) but it works great with a spinner. I do not understand why all these ATARI "Recharged" titles do not allow any custom key-bindings. Surely they must have anticipated people have arcade cabinets and would like to re-live their child hood in that format? If you want to play this on your Arcade cabinet with a spinner, I can recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: As far as Atari Recharged titles go, this is the pinnacle. It took a few games to perfect the concept. With really lackluster Missile Command, just decent Asteroids.. now with gems like Gravitar and Breakout!Breakout seems really simplistic as a game, but devs really keep it alive. Firstly, there’s Arcade mode done right. One life/three life, power ups/no power ups - that customisation was so hard to implement in the earlier games? Secondly, challenges - damn hard ones. This mode seemed like a afterthought in previous recharged titles. Now, it’s the meat of the game. This will make your blood boil… and it’s glorious! Breakout Recharged is a fantastic reanimation of a classic… and you can play it as you would on your Atari 2600 or with modern twist and power-ups. It’s just done tastefully, always retaining the spirit of the original title, even in flashy Recharged mode.Great, challenging - worth every penny. Also, Megan Mcduffee with another killer soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Great upgrade from the orig Breakout and Super Breakout games as those were slower and if you had one brick left it could take forever to get it. This version the trajectory works as intended. The orig super breakout did not. There is a new wrinkle here and i dont like it. Its shoots bullets at you. In no other brealout/Arkanoid game did they have this. The problem here is the computer can cheat and time the bullets to coincide with your paddle placement. thats  a SUCK FACTOR, as the new mode is only one ball. Overall a very fun game if you get it on sale. Dont pay $9.99 tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to Breakout, the gameplay will always be timeless. This recharged version makes the game more accessible to younger players who may not be interested in the original, sans power ups or music.For myself, it's not a game I'd binge long hours playing, but to come back every now and then to beat my previous high score or the scores of others. I recommend Breakout if you're looking for classic arcade gameplay with modern elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Breakout: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review:
The original brick breaker returns with its toughest challenge yet. Survive as long as you can in arcade or take on one of 50 challenges picking up game-changing power-ups along the way. The grandfather of brick-breaking games is back with some of the toughest challenges yet! Breakout: Recharged steps up the excitement with a fresh coat of paint, exciting power-ups, and another original soundtrack from award-winning video game composer Megan McDuffee.

Breakout: Recharged will forever change what you expect from a brick-breaking title. The endless arcade mode and 50 challenge levels will push you to the limit of your skills. Don’t fret, however, as this wouldn’t be a Recharged title without game-changing powerups. Expect the aid of rail guns, homing missiles, and explosives to join the traditional multi-ball. You’ll need every tool in the arsenal and razor-sharp reflexes to climb the global leaderboards.

Key Features:

Old Meets New: Classic Breakout gameplay updated with refined control, and modern visual flourishes

Power Up: Blast special bricks to pick up paddle-transforming power-ups a rail gun, explosive balls, missile launchers, and more

Challenge: Compete in a series of 50 challenges designed to put even the most seasoned players to the test

Compete: Reach the top of global leaderboards for arcade and individual challenge modes

Bring a Friend: Play local co-op in every mode - breaking bricks is better together!

Get in the Groove: Rock out to an original score by Megan McDuffee

name: moon: Remix RPG Adventure
detailed_description: Many moons ago In 1997, the now legendary anti-RPG “moon” launched in Japan. Now, under the watchful eye of its original creators, it's finally on Steam, in English! Have you ever felt it odd that the heroes of RPGs go around opening villagers' closets and stealing from them? Or that they travel the world indiscriminately killing all monsters they meet? This game looks at the RPGs we all know and love from a new perspective. Story One moon-lit night, a young boy is sucked into the depths of his television set whilst playing a video game. He falls into a place called 'Moon World', and thus begins a search for love in order to recover the lost moonlight. Here, the mighty hero of Moon World murders innocent animals for experience, but the boy's growth comes from saving the souls of the animals and gathering the love in the world. Yes, in this game, you level up by loving, not fighting. The inhabitants of this world are all unique. Observe their daily lives and learn where they hide their secret love. 'Now, please, open the door!' An RPG without battles - Save the monster's souls - All the monsters killed by the 'hero' are actually just innocent animals. As you explore the game, you will encounter the bodies of these pitiful creatures. But, if the boy can catch their souls, they can be saved. A living, breathing world! - Peek into the secret lives of the NPCs - Moon World's residents go about their routine lives, depending on the time and day. The florist goes to work in the morning, and the castle guards arrive at their posts. Some folks have secret midnight hobbies, and others just spend their days fishing. MD System - Choose your own soundtrack - In moon, you can choose your own music. By using the special music playing Moon Disc (MD) function which appears in the game, you can walk around the map listening to the tracks you like in the order you set them.

short_description: Don't be a hero. Experience the love. Experience moon. moon is an anti-RPG steeped in story and character, mood and music.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone. That said, it's worth a try by just about anyone. To define it in terms of genre, moon is like an adventure game with life sim and puzzle elements, all applied to the overall context of an RPG world.I'll just throw some quick advice here for anyone new to the game in rough order of importance.0) Read the manual here  . It actually has really important information about how the gameplay loop works. One of the biggest takeaways is that you have daily time limits that slowly increase as you generate more love. Hitting the time limit is a game over and has you reload your last save. Again, though, read the manual for more info. (Apparently you can also check part of the manual by pressing Tab ingame, but I've not tested this myself.)1) Keep a notebook or something of the sort to jot down info you might forget later. This can range from mysterious messages and numbers to what days/times characters say they do things, or even just to what the days of the week are called. There are some parts where you may need to draw a little diagram or something to work as a reminder. If you keep notes, not only will the playthrough be smoother but you'll likely not need a guide of any sort.2) Save often by going to bed. You will collapse and lose unsaved progress if you stay up for too long, but the game only has a time limit per day rather than having some overall maximum number of days you can play. As a side note, stock up on your daily free cookie given to you by Gramby whenever you can in the early to midgame.3) Relax and take things in. When I played this game for the first time I was used to blasting/pushing through every game I played for full completion in as little time as possible. moon, though... it's a game that you pace yourself in, doing little tasks and accumulating love until you reach the endgame. It does have an actual ending (two, really), so keep that in mind. You do indeed have a goal, but take your time. 4) The fishing contest is almost entirely RNG if you choose to do it. It's not fun. if you go to a restaurant before you do it you can improve your chances. Just make a save before doing all that so you don't have to wait another week ingame.5) The game's music is great, but a few of my favorite tracks are THE OTHER JET, POP MAY DAY, Heads in Clouds, and I'm waiting for the night. Still, you can't go wrong with pretty much any of the MDs in the game. Try out whatever ones you can!moon's world is beautiful and soft in a way I'd call reminiscent of a fairytale you read from your primary school's library or some old fantasy film on VHS you found at a video rental or thrift store as a child. Some kind of weird edutainment game you played in preschool, or maybe even just a strange commercial you saw on TV a few times on a kids channel. It's not a typical post-2010 saccharine 'soft relaxing cute' game, instead having an older and less bubbly style of immersion and dialogue. You might not feel that everyone in the game loves you the same way you have to accomplish loving tasks for them, but such is the way of the world. In Moon World, people are as people are in the outside world. As long as you're both genuinely willing to talk things through and try to understand each other, it's possible to help each other have a better existence. Doing good is often an end in and of itself.When I first played moon I felt something I really needed: a sense of wonder that let me be a kid for a while again and a sense of peace in not being a hero. It gave me a breath of fresh air playing a game that's got a mix of different species to care for, not just humans. moon is a special game. I'm so so glad it's finally gotten a wider release. It's lovely, and I hope that if you play it you'll have a good time as well.... That is love.... This is love.(Edit: I'm seeing a lot of people mentioning a certain major 2015 indie RPG as a basis for recommending this game. That's great for getting a wider amount of new people into this, but I'd like to note that moon is still a great one to try even for people who aren't really fans of that other game. I personally don't like that other game at all! Yet I still found moon awesome. So if you also aren't too big into that smash hit indie game, I still recommend giving this one a shot. You might find it more to your tastes as I did. Cheers!)

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually insane this game wasn't available in English until last year.I've bought this game twice (earlier this year for the Switch). Great game and way before its time capturing stuff Majora's Mask and Undertale did before they existed. It's a fun adventure game that is all about smelling the roses. If you liked any of the previous two games for what they uniquely offer or like Disco Elysium, Monkey Island and Super Mario RPG there's a lot in this for you. Fun jabs towards Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy too.

_childDocuments_.review: Moon first released in 1997 for the original Playstation but unfortunately never made its way outside Japan and never got officially located until 2020 when a worldwide Switch re-release of this lovely game happened, it wouldn’t be until 2021 when this adventure would arrive to PC but here we are, let me go straight to the point, Moon was a very special, weird and lovely adventure and while I will recommend it for everyone, I know for sure not everyone will enjoy this game due to its weirdness and perhaps structure but if you are a bit interested, I invite you to keep reading this review and find out if it’s the game you want to play or, more importantly, the game you need to play right now.We are a kid who’s playing his RPG “Moon” on the Gamestation when all the sudden gets transported into the game’s world, Love-de-Gard, as a nameless entity referred as kid or your nickname, sooner rather than later you will realise that you are inside the game and you will follow the storyline but with a catch, instead of the merciless Hero you came here to spread love among all living things and change the destiny of the creatures of this world. Saving the strange animals of this world, helping their inhabitants and most importantly, changing the fate of this world by spreading love, not violence.As you can see, the story of this game seems to be very RPG standard, you know, be the hero, save the kidnapped princess, slay the dragon and while that’s true, that’s NOT our story, we follow the same path as the hero but our objective is completely different, our presence in this world brings joy and hope for those who get slayed and kicked by the hero, who is a dumbass and a merciless vile character, in this world our objective won’t be kill the monsters but help them, chat and learn about the people who live in this world, explore the different places of this lovely place and of course, end the story in a different way.You will find this place both interesting and eccentric at times, there are countless references to the real world of the late 90’s - very early 00’s (trends that peaked in this era that started in the 90’s) and even some philosophy and metacommentary about you and the meaning of what you are doing, the further you go into this adventure, the clearer the picture becomes, this was a very special journey in which you will be able to see through the eyes of different inhabitants and that’s really special, in general I thought this approach of getting love by doing good actions for others was probably what I needed the most at the moment of this review after all what’s happening and happened to the world in the last few years, who would have guessed an old classic could give me a positivity boost just by giving me the option of making love and not war.Let’s talk about this world, Love-de-Gard is similar to an island in which all biomes fuse to create a colourful and varied place to explore and live, world is size limited though but please remember this is a 1997 game so it’s completely normal and yet, it feels big, condensed and deep.Castle Town, Mushroom forest, Technopolis or the Tropical fields are just a few examples of places you will find and explore during the adventure and you will see how each place feels different from others, every place has a distinctive style, type of characters and most importantly, new ways of getting love and spreading your good actions.Even though the game’s world is not really big, there a one-direction fast travel to a few locations of the map that will make your walks shorter, however, you won’t be able to return via the same method, you will have to go back in a normal way but the way is integrated it makes complete sense why and it’s very…. “Moon-y” hehe.When it comes to visuals, you can expect a PSX game with sharper details given the different panels we have nowadays but overall the visual aspect hasn’t been changed and, to be honest, I don’t think it needs to change anything, it’s a product of its moment, game is 25 years old and as so it’s being shown, however, the art style and the imaginary put in this game is lovely and mind blowing.Animals, characters and locations do have a peculiar and distinctive aspect, I think they even used real clay models for the monsters back in the day and you can see how they look in here, a real world touch in a game that talks about the thin boundary of reality and fakeness? Amazing touch here.What you can see in the screenshots it’s what you will find in the game, I found it to be very pleasant and I enjoyed the visual style of the game.Sound and music is another aspect I liked, character voices are non-real language gibberish, quite common in RPGs as you know, and that was fun but the cool aspect of this segment is music, all music was composed back in the day by independent musicians and you can see the vast variety of styles and themes, I think they nailed it, if I had to name my favourite track right now, I think I would go with “Kera Ma-Go” which is very cheerful.Gameplay has a few things to keep in mind, first of all, even though it’s called Moon RPG it’s NOT a JRPG, it is an adventure that refers to itself as RPG as a metacommentary from what happens inside the game, so if you came here expecting levelling up by fighting and getting new gear, forget about it, you level up by completing tasks and saving animals.Saving animal souls is easy, read the description of each body you find (some are really hidden, in case you want to complete all of them) and learn what are the requirements to make the souls appear, once the animal soul is accessible, just hug it, easy, right? One button. Completing tasks is something a bit more tricky, it requires objects, reading the details of the conversations and thinking a bit about the clues, but they are quite simple mechanically speaking, it’s always hugging, getting an object, stocking an object or using music, simple as that.The clock, you must keep in consideration the red arrow as it marks the moment you won’t be able to continue if you don’t sleep to change the day,  as you will be really tired, or by eating to extend the limit a bit to reach your bed on time before you collapse and game over reaches you.As I mentioned before, there’s also a fast travel option that works in one direction, you see those spiral roots? Well, keep those in mind.Gameplay loop is simple but there are tons of hidden interactions that you will appreciate and of course I didn’t mention a few things.When it comes to performance I played this game on Steam Deck and it’s officially “unsupported” . How so? Well, let me tell you that, like Valve said, Unsupported doesn’t mean the game doesn’t run on Deck, it means it might have a problem or two and well, they are right, it took me 15 hours to reach the ending and I only got 1 problem, on a very specific cinematic event game crashed but once I re-entered the game this didn’t happen and I continued perfectly fine.Playing process was painless and the experience was console-like, I installed it, the controller profile got configured automatically and deck did some background translation for some Windows processes, once the first boot was done, everything ran perfectly fine with no errors at all aside from that specific one, which I think might have to do with some codec translation in the background but I can’t be sure, this problem is likely not present on the regular windows version so rest assured this game will run well on your machine, it doesn’t consume that many resources.And that’s about it, Moon was exactly the game I needed right now and it delivered a wholesome experience that I won’t forget, I can’t recommend it enough to all of you even though I know this game is not for some of you, the very least I can do is to encourage you to play it and see if you like it, a timeless classic.Great job, Onion Games, you made it.

_childDocuments_.review: To even attempt to describe just how wonderful and culturally important this game is would be a waste of my time and a waste of the time you could be spent playing it. Instead, one should go in completely blind EXCEPT for the official translated guide that Team Onion so lovingly (heh) put together for players to use. It explains basic functions for the player that would be hard to understand in-game AND it feels so nice to read. Is it a perfect game? No, far from it. But it is a game made by a team that truly loves video games and loves the player to bits. So please, don't be a hero.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can often be very confusing and frustrating, and even the most dedicated fans will agree it's a bit of an acquired taste. The main gameplay is solving puzzles, most of which are less about finding a clever solution and more about figuring out the meaning behind vague and often really obtuse hints. It's absolutely okay to not enjoy this game, however widely praised it is by everyone.But moon is worth experiencing just for its cultural significance alone. It's a game you have to try out regardless whether you think you'll like it or not. And it's interesting not just in the historical context, but also as a work of art of sorts. The game has an extremely strange and fascinating surreal style that you won't find in any other media, which for many will outweigh its weaknesses.Note that this is a game where you need to be VERY attentive to all the hints and dialogue, explore every corner of the game world, and take notes for pretty much everything you see on screen, otherwise you will likely not get full enjoyment out of it.If you play for a couple of hours and it doesn't connect, feel free to stop, it's a long game and you don't have to torture yourself. But do at least give it a try. I assure you that no matter how much time you spend on it you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by stating  is not a perfect game. Just like Chulip, translation inaccuracies often turn somewhat vague puzzles into challenges much harder than they should be and end up hurting the experience. Furthermore, as seen on the , the originally planned ending was quite different from what we got, which clarifies why some things are left partially unexplained.Still, from the way the plot is conducted to the gameplay mechanics themselves, there's so much inspiring stuff to see here that telling anyone not to give it a try would be a crime. Stuff that any RPG would do well to take inspiration from, yet only Undertale did (and honestly, not as well as it could). If you're a fan of adventure and RPGs in general, I'd already list this as a must-play.Also, I'm not sure how different this version is from the previously released Switch version (the one I've played before), but it's a good sign that they've made the most relevant parts of the game's manual available if you press Tab. Maybe we can expect new easter eggs and mistranslation corrections?One way or another, be sure to give Moon a chance if you're looking for something different and oozing creativity. And if you like it, do consider trying out Chulip next. The setting is just as great, and if you had enough patience to reach Moon's ending, you already have what it takes.: Since I've mentioned this version could have extra stuff, I think it might be a good idea to add this piece of info from :"

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest up front: I didn't finish this game. I played for quite a bit, and then I got to a point where I figured out what the main objective of the game was, then realised in order to get to the end, I'd have to deal with RNG, time-of-day sensitive events, and most importantly, one of the worst fishing minigames I've ever seen.But still, it's overall pretty interesting. I especially like how everything is a neat puzzle, how you have to pay attention to context cues, your environment, put multiple things together. It made my brain feel big. I like the world, the characters, and how both unhinged and grounded everything is. It's weird, but in a way that makes sense.In short, I really like the premise, the themes, and the overall ideas on display here. It's just the actual execution I have problems with. But then again, this game is over 25 years old, so I won't hold it too much against it. Games were literally built different back then.It is a recommendation because what it does, it does very well, and as a historical artifact, it is very compelling. I would definitely play a modern reinterpretation of this formula, with better controls, quality of life improvements, an in-game calendar, and less punishing timings. Oh, and a better fishing minigame. Or no fishing at all, that'd be good too.Although at that point I could just be playing Undertale again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny and strange and full of creativity.  It's clear how this inspired Undertale, Majora's Mask, Dropsy, Petscop, etc.  It's a commentary on RPGs, made by former SquareSoft employees.  Experience an RPG from an outside perspective.  Time passes and characters have daily schedules which makes things feel more alive.  It plays a bit like a point-and-click adventure, though it's suitably non-linear, and if you ever get stuck, there's a wiki you can consult that will give you gentle hints in the right direction.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe i haven't written a review for this game yet despite it now being one of my fav games of all time. wonderful little adventure across a silly world with silly characters, with a deeper message about love and storytelling if you look for it. by modern standards, the slow burn pacing is a bit of an acquired taste. it has a day/night cycle and a weekly calendar, with some events only happening on very specific times that you'll have to figure it out from obtuse hints. its best to keep a guide on hand for whenever you feel stuck. despite that, everything about moon's presentation is designed to be best played at your own leisurely pace, and i rarely ever felt bored even when i was just walking from place to place.i highly recommend everyone giving this game a try even if it doesnt seem like something you'd be into! don't be a hero, experience the love :)
