_childDocuments_.review: I have played Crysis on release day and cleared it dozens of times and a dozen ways.  The spawning system an open maps (very large open maps, but not true open world) make it so every single playthrough is different past the first few kills in the first village area you approach, but that is the tutorial.It is the BEST first person shooter ever created in my opinion for 2 reasons.  It was a decade ahead of its time and it needed the best pc at the time, but that is not why.  Its innovation, which the series itself dropped in the sequels has still not been rivaled in any game I have seen.  In the field as bullets are flying modification of any weapon you pick up is one thing but a physics sandbox on top of it makes it special, Chop down trees, blow em up, use your super suit to punch down most walls except reinforced concrete and so on.Open world, every fight based on the spawn system is different in every playthrough and the modification system was great and I was hoping that they would take this awesome baseline and innovate but they didn't.  They regressed making a Crysis 2 and 3 a corridor shooter.I hope Warhawk gets remade as well, unless somehow I missed that it was part of the remaster as it is the same game from a 2nd character's point of view and different missions.They had basic vehicle combat and you could tell they planned on flight combat in future release, especially with the surprise enemy at the end 1/3rd of the game, but nope.  Bow and Arrow, different character and boring storyline about the suit rather than the secret enemy hit the sequels.I will be playing the sequels for my 2nd time since i got them in this package but probably that 2nd time only.  However every year or so I will pop in Crysis and play through it with a different style that time.  As with release there are a few times you crash but luckily it is right at a checkpoint.  They never fixed the save system.Besides that one problem, you should try it.  Especially now that it is cheaper and remade with modern graphics.Crysis should have been the template for all FPS shooters going forward.  Realistic, Sci-Fi, modern, etc...  all could have been improved with the systems in Crysis but for some reason or another they made the sequels for a more casual audience that did not want to approach a KPA group will crab crawling prone to sneak in, map the enemy's location (which differs based on several factors beside random, like if you went loud in a close by place or enemy, they are already on the mounted guns and patrolling with intent or took out everything quietly or completely stealthed, with no kills except the tranquilizer (tactical attachment) dart.If you like Military Shooters and Sci-Fi and prefer gameplay over graphics then you will dig this.  It was praised for its graphics at the time but its systems were what makes it a non-stop fun lifetime game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much new that can be said about Crysis that hasn't already been said over the last 17 years since the original was released. Performance wise this remaster is playable on a lot wider range of hardware than the original ever was and that's a good thing, as the game is still snappy and fun to play. Wide corridors give you quite a bit of flexibility in how you approach an objective, no excess secrets or hidden objectives to distract you and good voice acting mean that you are drawn into the game and can progress quite quickly through the game. _childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered is, after all the updates, a solid remaster but one that could be more too.Some things I noticed right off the bat:- No more quicksaves and only checkpoints- Performance is better compared to the original version but this is mostly due to DLSS- AI is still rather dumb at times but I think its a little better- Some minor graphic effects from the original are absent- Loading screens and binoculars are still not ultrawide optimized and glitch- In many aspects the game looks better but the coloring feels off and too bright- Some bugs have been fixed but others are still an issue (Such as broken parallax occlusion mapping effects)- The Ascension level is missing all music- There is no crouch toggle key and using the classic nanosuit controls makes you stand up- Something seems wrong with the music transitions- Warhead expansion is missingI guess Saber tried their best but ultimately its not a definitive remaster for me. The games performance without DLSS is actually quite similar to the original 2007 version including some real performance dips at random parts of the game such as the end boss fight. DLSS kinda rectified this but it feels more like a workaround than anything else. You also need to disable your inbuilt GPU because if not the game thinks you do not have a raytracing capable GPU. The new raytracing effects do look nice though but I think they also generally change the tone too much at times like everything is brighter than in the original game. DLSS is a game changer though not only because of the improved performance but also crystal clear non aliased picture.AI is not really better and often just completely stops working with the enemies looking in one direction and not reacting to anything anymore. Quicksaves are also gone and it just seems like a downgrade. Aside of that some GUI elements are not ultrawide optimized such as loading screens and the binocular and that especially seems like a weird thing to miss for a notorious PC game like Crysis.Luckily they brought back classic nanosuit controls and other old PC input controls which was definitely missing in the beginning. Another thing I noticed is, that for whatever reason there are some dialogue lines in the campaign I have NEVER heard in the original game. Thats really obscure and maybe means the original 2007 version had a bug where some radio chatter never triggered but no idea. Should note though that I play in German. Also I have played the game like 10 times over the years ever since 2007 and let me tell you, it was quite a flashback playing the remastered version with maximum "But Can It Run Crysis?" settings and full raytracing. It did at least manage to make me feel nostalgic for 2007 when you tried running ultra settings with a 8800GT but you ended up having 30FPS at best. Just that now the FPS are more along the line of 60-120. Damn how times change.But the most disappointing thing of all is that Crysis Warhead has been completely ignored to this date. But thats probably because they never had a CryEngine 3 port of it to begin with but even the original Crysis CryEngine 3 Xbox 360 port was lazy as hell. Probably one of the reasons the remastered version turned out as it did.The game deserved better and I bet some studios like Nightdive would have done a better job but maybe it was also due to the lack of budget. Crysis 2 and 3 remastered turned out a lot better but that might be due to them not needing many upgrades to begin with.Achievements are easy peasy to get. Well at least for someone like me who finished the game countless times on delta difficulty. Took me 8 hours to get all of them and finish the game.Maybe give the game a Warhead DLC and some additional budget. Would love to see Crysis Warhead remastered campaign in the game together with some further general updates. Fix the things I and many fans pointed out and maybe even add DLSS 3.0 and Frame Generation. Currently the game is slightly better than the 2007 version but there is still room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy the remastered trilogy on a Steam sale and revisit a classic. _childDocuments_.review: Even though the abovementioned quote might be a bit cheesy, I could not help myself because of how ironic it is. As a fan of the original  from 2007, I was sceptical about this new version, especially after I heard numerous complaints when it was released a year ago on a different platform. I wanted to try it out nonetheless, though. Perhaps it got better after a few updates?Well, that certainly did not happen, hence the FUBAR quote. is not a step forward, nor it does not at the very least stagnates like other remasters. Instead, it manages to be worse than the original game, indolently ruining already existing aspects rather than making them better or bringing some modern quality of life improvements.Thus, it was a bit hard for me to write this critique of mine. While the core of this first-person shooter remains the same, the said aspects are subpar, making my experience tiresome. Due to that, I was forcing myself to finish it, as that was not  lovely  anymore but rather its butchered version. And that is not a moaning of a nostalgic guy with so-called pink glasses because I have replayed and even  the original a year ago, so it is still fresh in my mind.Let us get to the game itself, though. The premise of its narrative is not extraordinary nor a reason why you should play , but it is serviceable for what it is. You are supposed to rescue a bunch of scientists from North Korean claws on the Lingshan Islands. To achieve that, you have a powerful Nanosuit that enhances your combat possibilities by increasing your strength, speed or even making you invisible for a while. However, you will find out soon enough that there are some strange alien beings on this very island, and they are not exactly happy with your presence. Despite these aliens and futuristic equipment, I still find the fact that North Koreans successfully conquered a foreign piece of land as the most unrealistic one.Nevertheless,  excels with its simple yet engaging gameplay loop, which could be the remaster’s case, too, if it was not for several shortcomings. The freedom in how to approach each situation, whether by going all-in with a minigun and grenades, armoured vehicles or by silently killing enemies one by one, is still present. You can even customize the weapons by adding various attachments, such as scopes or different ammo types. However, artificial intelligence seems to be even dumber than before, as I witnessed it demonstrate brilliant tactics like observing the nearest wall or walking in circles. Moreover, it felt as if there were fewer foes, as several patrols I expected to encounter were missing during my playthrough; it seems as if they did not spawn at all. Lastly, there are some unnecessary changes, such as providing players with infinite ammunition when controlling a tank—this allows you to obliterate everything from a distance, destroying the original’s purpose of being careful and scavenging for supplies. Due to all of that, it felt significantly easier to play this remastered version even on the highest difficulty setting.What made my experience even worse were the weird controls, as the mouse movement is not as smooth as I am used to and meddling with its settings did not solve this issue; it felt as if it was constantly fighting with me, so I could not relax and enjoy my time with it. Another problem is that some actions, like reloading and changing fire mode, are set to a single key, due to which neither of them works, and you have to rebind them from scratch to be able to use actually use them. Additionally, changing the colour of the interface swaps it only in the main menu but not in the game itself. Ah, I almost forgot… both manual and quicksaves are not implemented to this very day either. I would guess that all of these oversights happened because of porting it from an old engine used for consoles rather than using the original one.Then, there is an aspect that is completely missing—the multiplayer part. I have adored playing it years ago, as it had a bit unique take on large-scale battles, with capturing crucial points and using vehicles as the  series presents nowadays. Its inclusion could make  worthy, as it would revive its community; alas, that did not happen.As for audiovisuals, there is a massive issue with the imbalance of audio, which is mainly noticeable when firing from weapons. For example, a regular handgun’s sound almost blew off my eardrums, while a fully automatic assault rifle is barely hearable. I could forgive such inconsistencies in a small indie title but in a remastered version of a triple-A game? That is both sad and laughable; mainly, when you consider the fact that this has not been fixed for over a year by now. I guess some of the updated visuals deserve a bit of praise, but the original already looked amazing; I mean, it is  after all, which started the infamous  meme.Honestly, I do not see a single reason for which I should recommend buying . The audacity to ask the owners of the original title to pay for this subpar, butchered version is beyond me. For a long-time fan of the series, it feels like a slap in the face. I would not suggest this even to newcomers, as  from 2007 is much cheaper. A counter-argument could be that some people have problems with launching the original, but that only underlines my point! If someone did not bother to fix these issues over the years, they should not tell their customers: . Disgusting. There are already many questionable remasters with performance problems, such as  or , but even those were at the very least provided for free—that does not mean we cannot criticize them, but at the very least they do not present themselves as the second coming of Jesus when their state is worse than his during the crucifixion.

_childDocuments_.review: Its been about 5 years since I first played crysis so I cant really say theres a massive difference with the remastering. I was on a 1650 system on the original game and it struggled. Now im on a 3070 system playing 1440p at ultra settings with performance raytracing. What I do remember is several spots losing fps like crazy. Still the same no doubt the engine's fault. It was still a fun game to play. If youre to play these games it probably is best to buy this version if you ever upgrade to a better pc. I got it as a bundle for under $20. All the hours combined of the three games is about 27 hours. So in my eyes it was worth buying. I would attempt to play the crysis trilogy with a 4gb card. Having a smooth experience is out the question even 1080. The story is still great. Though I really wish they would have redone the in game cinematic cutscenes better. They still look like 2010 cutscences (Not gameplay ones). But the FREAKING TRANSPORT MISSION WITH THE TORNADOES. STILL ABSOLUTE CRAP. They couldnt have put a little effort in making the controls better. It is still one of the worst missions I have ever played in a game. Because its never your controllers fault. Through my playthrough my controller worked fine but the game bugged out to where it wouldn't register my thrust. Had to restart the game. There were a total of 4 moments where I had to either restart the game entirely multiple times, last checkpoint load, or restart entire mission multiple times. This game still is buggy like the original. Which is a shame because this is supposed to be the best version. Overall crysis is still a good game but what was the point of remastering when they still havent solved the original issues over a decade later. Wont matter which version you buy original or remastered, both have their issues. Though I less in this version. Gameplay is fun and enjoyable. Nomad is definitely my favorite character in the entire trilogy. Worth a play if your pc can run crysis.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:* Has a field of view slider but it can only go up to a max of 80Cons:* The multiplayer gamemode was not included in Crysis Remastered when it was available in the original game* I have a 5950x and a RTX 4090 yet my game sometimes will drop below 60 FPS at 4k with all settings, included ray tracing, maxed out* The AI is dumb to where it can bug out* Game pauses and mutes itself when it's alt-tabbedOther thoughts:* The game does start off pretty slow* A recent patch restored back the campaign level called "Ascension" along with a few control options* Not much replayability due to the lack of multiplayer and mods compared to the original game* I enjoyed the lore since I find an alien invasion to be fascinating* I recommend in trying it out when it's on sale; otherwise don't bother. _childDocuments_.review: Once hailed as a technical marvel, Crysis 1 really shows its age and no amount of so-called remastering - reskinning in essence - would bring it back to its 'glory' today. The enemy AI, the gun animations and gunplay, the level design and storytelling and performance are either showing their ages or simply bad. For instance, the game is remembered as an open-world shooter while its openness is limited to the first several sections and most of the time you proceed in a linear manner with NPC(mostly Prophet) warning you about the enemy activities up ahead. And players can't really tell whether they are using the gun or underbarrel attachment from the way the protagonist holds the gun, and switching between rifles and underbarrel attachments always show the animation of protagonist adjusting fire mode selector. It's not even fit for being a benchmarking tool either, since its graphics isn't good enough to justify its poor performance on the highest settings or higher settings.

I'm looking forward to the remaster of Crysis 2 and 3 but their original versions still hold up so it isn't a high priority. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of this game since I tried it in 2010. It was she who made me leave PS2 for PC. So I played the 2007 original (luckily I have it) to be as objective as possible. I played both games on "SWAT" difficulty in hopes of fixing the problems that the original 2007 version had.    It's cool to go back in time. Such familiar cards, as if they had never left them and the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥ balance of opponents (the enemy in the cap can withstand 5 blows to the head or dies immediately) Eh... MEMORIES!!!   Controlling the suit from part 2 is very inconvenient (for the reason that the developers didn’t just cut out one mechanic and replace it with another, but put two on top of each other (they conflict with each other), so I returned the controls to the completely original ones (although I think the controls are the second part is the best). The problem of the original with the strange use of processor cores has been solved, but added “probably for balance” optimization problems have been . Played on graphics settings (CAN IT RUN CRYSIS?) with Ray tracing and immediately my video card (2060 super) transferred me from the native resolution (4K) to FullHD. On FullHD, stays around 57-53 FPS. In a battle and with high dynamics, it drops to 47-44 FPS. You can turn off “Rays”, then you will get +10 fps, but the shadows and lighting greatly lose their beauty, and sometimes even the shadows of the guys, which hurts the eyes. You can also turn on "DLSS", you will also get an increase of +30-40 FPS, but the picture loses a lot in detail and smoothing. I played with on "Rays" and "DLSS" are disabled. So the minimum optimization requirements are still lacking. The enemies hit much harder than in the original, it feels like I'm going against them with my bare ass, and not in an armored suit. Also, the suit’s energy is consumed faster, so you have to sit out more often to charge (a little annoying).   As expected, I beat a game from my childhood that isn't as amazing as it used to be. A very strangely made remaster. Updated textures and shadows were added only to certain elements (vegetation, ground, water, rocks, lighting and costume), and everything else was forgotten. And it looks strange when there is a cool detailed costume on which shadows and lighting play, and the face of the Prophet or Psycho is the same as in the original (was it really difficult to add details). For my personal taste, the picture is also very oversaturated and the atmosphere of some locations is lost. Everything else is the same as before.   A remaster of a game that many wanted but ended up underwhelming. I would advise you to play the 2007 version (if you can find it) and experience more sensations from childhood, and modern builds will already give more fps than before (I got 85 in 4K with a drop to 72 FPS). I expected more from this game, but unfortunately it disappointed me. So I cannot advise an ordinary person (not familiar with the series) to buy it, and to an ardent fan of the original I can only say that it is at your own peril and risk.If you got here, then know that you are the BEST!!! _childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original, so I don't know how the remastered version holds up to it. But this game is a very unique fps. It is very linear, but gives the player a feeling of agency I've never encountered in other 'linear' fps games. It reminds me of the Military Base level in IGI, but on steroids. You can opt for stealth and use distractions, or dive out of a car and watch it blast into a camp, go the human shield route and opt for an all-guns-blazing playthrough. All this, with seemingly full availability of the map. Even vehicles are available to you, with surprisingly good handling. The story was simple and crunchy. No nonsense, well-paced with sufficiently good characters. Better than most military fps games. And it works well with the game at hand. A very, very well-crafted game.Mild spoiler:The only mildly icky parts were the alien ship level and the final level in the jet.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an updated review from my initial one. I have now finished the game on the hardest difficulty and earned all achievements. The core game is perfectly fine. However, there is just so many things missing from a remaster. I never played the original, but there's a bunch of things missing that I learned was in the original. Quicksaves, which would have made my delta difficulty run much more bearable and less annoying. Not to mention things could have improved, such as the difficulty descriptions in menus. Delta difficulty was described as having less modifiers than there actually are. For example, enemies recieve aimbot and can notice you from across the map. The player has reduced health and the game is much more unforgiving. However, the game gives no indication of this, which led me to play quite a bit of the game under the impression this just is how the game was. The game just has so many inconsistences that may have been understandable for the first release, but not for a remaster. Just don't buy the remaster, buy the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis with a new coat of paint, kind of. There are a number of features that are straight up missing that makes the first game more fun, biggest offenders being modding support and quicksaves. No leaning is not gone, it's just set to a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bind by default. Outside that, the game's art style has also changed to something a lot more vibrant (). The game also seems to nerf strength mode and speed mode even in classic mode. Only real improvements made to the game are optimization (though it doesn't feel like it once you set everything to very high), and the removal of SecuRom. Honestly I'd prefer if Crytek changed the Steam client of Crysis to the one they sell on GOG instead of spending all this time on an inferior port. Overall, I'd only recommend this game if you're a die hard Crysis fan that wants to see some extra eye candy. $15 isn't too bad of a price for this game, but I personally would not pay a penny more than that. If you don't have the first game, I highly recommend it still, just get it from GOG instead and play with mods.Honestly I'm open to changing this review but only if strength and speed mode are reverted, gameplay changes like trees not breaking from punches are fixed, color settings and times of day are reverted to what they were in the first game, modding support is added, Warhead is included in the game, and further optimizations are made for multithreaded cpus. So yeah, just buy the GOG version and mod it.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are ridiculously good for it's time -- and the small features like vegetation toppling over, buildings exploding in gameplay, and picking up wildlife really are impressive for a game nearing 2 decades old. Lots of vehicles to control, AA turrets, and a super badass suit with cloaking, fast running, high jump, and an armored mode. Weapons can be mildly upgraded with attachments. A bit of stealth, lots and lots of action, some cool moments and a whole lot of cheesy ones. The korean island setting is pretty cool with super open areas despite the game being linear -- you can tackle things in different ways. It's pretty janky here n there -- I didn't experience much jank until later on in the game. Dialogue can get cut off, AI can get pretty stupid, I see the potential for getting stuck in props, etc. The general gameplay and setting are definitely the shining parts of this game. Everything else wasn't too good to me (some of the characters -- mostly your commanders and other nanosuit friends I found enjoyable). Regardless it got me interested in the series and I'm looking forward to Warhead, 2, and 3.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the worst remasters I have ever payed. The original game is much more stable and doesn't have so many glitches and bugs as this. I have played it through two times, one time on Normal and the second time on Delta. In both playthroughs I had a gamebreaker glitch on the same spot (Bulldog ride in the mission Exodus). At the first time it was enough to delete my saves and restart the mission from the beginning (from the mission select menü), but the second time on Delta difficulty it dowsn't wanted to work at any way. I spent a haf day to resolve the problem, but at the end it resolved itself randomly. Sometimes trigger elements are also not workind and you need to reload the last ceckpoint or restart the level. I really don't know how Crytek allows such issues to exist even after two years of the release.The graphical improvements are actually not bad, but the game doesn't look so much better as you would expect to it's system requirements. Some high resolution textures are actually worse than the originals as they make really visible patterns. You cannot move every physical object as in the original and also the music is somewhat altered during the game.With all it's issues, I absolutely cannot recomnend this version of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis: Remastered is a sci-fi futuristic first-person shooter developed and published by Crytek and released on Steam in September 2021. I will note I finished Crysis: Remastered last weekend, before Patch 3 was released this week.If you find this review to be helpful, please leave a thumbs-up. I also have a review page here: I originally played and reviewed Crysis in 2016, on some PC that included a GTX 560 Ti. For those interested, the link to the original is here: For the time, I thought Crysis was an enjoyable experience but could not play it on Ultra without performance issues. Have a look at my (back in the day) rating system, below.These ratings were based on a couple of key things from my original play, including:The above is still fairly accurate, noting in the Remastered version that:That said, Crysis: Remastered is sold on updated visuals and technological features and is optimised to current hardware. Playing on a PC with a i5-6600k, GTX 1070, and 16GB ram, I found the Remastered was optimised extremely well and I did not experience any framerate or stability (e.g., crashes) issues. The overall graphical fidelity is a broad improvement on the original and the Lingshan Island is still a beautiful sight, credited to an updated lighting system. While the graphics are broadly improved, the Remastered did not update all assets and objects (i.e., bag in opening scene, some characters), and therefore, the textures on these are disappointingly low-resolution and blurry. I am also surprised to find a number of bugs throughout my experience, including, but not limited to, the aforementioned AI scripting, as well as constant sound drop-outs during missions and the AI boss fight not triggering in the final mission, requiring a level restart(!).I commend the legacy of Crysis I, and Crysis: Remastered is a nice trip down to memory lane, particularly in a nice campaign. But I am conflicted because the Remastered version was not overly a good experience. It adds a nice overall graphical upgrade and performance optimisation is fantastic (and I will note Patch 3 further optimises it), but it falls in several areas. First, it does not address issues from the original game such as AI scripting and if that is not fixable, I appreciate that. It is also unfortunate that the visual improvement does not impact all assets, resulting in a number of low-resolution characters and objects, and there are a high number of bugs and glitches throughout the game. On this basis, I do not recommend Crysis: Remastered.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have been great for its time, but it doesn't seem to hold up too well in the modern day.Personally, I would recommend starting with Crysis 2 if you are interested in the series and if you want to know about the story, either look up a playthrough or spend an hour on the wiki reading up on the story.My reasons for this conclusion: -  (it took me a bit under 8 hours to beat) - . There were quite a few times where I was looking at a situation and asking myself, "Why, why would you do that?!" or "How did I get here again?" -  The game ends rather suddenly and at a weird time with no true resolution to the plot. To further add to the confusion, when moving onto the next game, it is as if the characters of this game (Nomad, The doctor, Psycho) never existed -  At the start of each boss fight, I found myself thinking, "Is this a boss fight? Why are we fighting? What just happened to 'x'?". And the fights themselves were of the type where you didn't know what was actually going on and after shooting at the boss a bunch you start wondering if there is a weak-spot or something that you need to hit to deal damage. A good example is the answer to the 2nd boss is to shoot it with ~4500 minigun rounds. (Because after shooting the boss with the first 1000 rounds and seeing nothing happen you are likely to consider shooting at it more with the same weapon). After every boss fight I just found myself thinking,  -  This game if full of elements that directly contradict each other's purpose. A good example of this would be the stealth feature in the game, you are incentivised to use stealth in the game, problem being that enemies can frequently spot you at points where you still can barely make out the enemy with a 4x scope. Enemies spotting you is also instant or close to it. Additionally, if you fire when cloaked, your energy is instantly set to 0 (even with a suppressor) meaning you can only fire out of cloak (this does get addressed in later games) this also applies to all weapons, so a shotgun is just as valid as a pistol in terms of energy conservation. Human enemies also only die in 1 hit to headshots and can take 3+ hits to die to body shots. So, if you shoot and miss the head, you have alerted the entire enemy force to your presence. You also have your energy instantly get set to 0 if you get shot so using cloak so using it in a dangerous situation is likely to just leave you without energy and still in danger. All these factors made it so that it was far easier, less time consuming and less risky to just sprint past all the enemies you see -  Despite wearing the most advanced suit of armor in the world, you still go down to a second of sustained fire from any weapon. Even if you use armor mode, it will only block maybe 4 bullets and leave you with no energy and no health -  There wasn't a second I fought the Ceph that I enjoyed. They are tanky, there is a lot of them, they are fast, and they can fly. I would find myself constantly looking into the sky wondering where I was being attacked from while being shot at from 3 different directions all while every enemy takes 2-3 shots from even the strongest weapons in the game. The only saving grace was that they dealt rather low damage. (again they are much more pleasant to fight in the later games)In all, this game's primary effect on me was making me appreciate the other games more for their improvements to the formula

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis remastered is one of the best shooters out there. A badass game about a couple of veritable 100 % Giga-Chads: United States Army Delta Force Operators(Nomad, Prophet, Psycho) equipped with highly advanced cool nanosuits who are sent to uncover the mystery behind the discovery of an ancient built structure that has been found buried inside a mountain in the fictional Lingshan Islands, which turns to be of alien origin. You(Nomad) and your team end up fighting North Koreans and aliens: the Ceph in an attempt to try to stop an alien invasion.This game will increase your testosterone unlike the woke puke we are presently fed on a monthly basis. I never got sick of hearing"Cloaked engaged", "Maximum armor" "Maximum speed". Words said in the most manly way possible. The game offers some nice gameplay elements in an open-world map. You have the stealth approach where one can use the nanosuit powers(cloak) and silencers to silently infiltrate an enemy base/get past a jungle patrol and fulfill the objective. If you do not like the silent, more passive approach you can opt for the obvious head on approach where you attack directly an enemy base/jungle patrol killing anyone in sight-using your suit armor power for protection.There are some additional elements to the combat gameplay that makes things more fun if you find your self in a pickle-low on ammo. Firstly you can use environmental objects to throw at the enemies to incapacitate them/kill them. Secondly you can grab the enemies by neck and throw them like nothing using your powerful grip. The game has also some additional vehicular/aircraft gameplay which is a nice break from the normal shooting mechanics. Makes the experience more whole with this added variety. The weapons variety and customization is nice. It allow players to find their own style and quickly adapt to new challenges by being able to modify them in real time. Turn a weapon to a silent one by putting a silencer or reverse it back. Put a sight scope for close range fights or a sniper scope for a long distance target and vice versa changing it as your needs change. Put a flashlight or a laser sight or maybe a grenade launcher for increase damage. You have the SCAR the primary assault rifle, XM2014 the a military-grade combat shotgun, FY71 Assault Rifle capable of both fully-automatic and semi-automatic fire, the dual wielding Pistols, the powerful Hurricane Minigun, The Molecular Accelerator-Ceph weapon, The sniper-DSG-1, the LAW-disposable compact missile launcher and the TAC Gun which is a prototype hand-held nuclear weapon. You also have your fists, grenades, C4 and the weapons from the tanks, patrol boats, military jeeps.  The game physics is one of the best putting to shame most games from today. Most parts of the environment can be subject to manipulation. There is a nice destruction system where you can have fun with the environment: mow down trees with your Minigun, collapse a building on top of enemies, blow entire bases to smithereens. The game story is good enough for a shooter and the characters are memorable and likeable enough. Mostly Nomad, Prophet and Psycho. Prophet voice is one of the coolest voice I have heard in all my years of gaming. It is so memorable and will stick in your memory. The graphics is another aspect where the game excels. The remaster comes with real-time voxel traced global illumination, extremely high resolution textures. The lush jungle, the water, the bases and the weapons looked very good on my 50" TV on 4k Very High on my RTX 4080. Made some nice screenshots.  The combat and AI is pretty challenging and fun especially on higher difficulty but even on normal difficulty. The enemies are pretty relentless and will spot you from a distance, hear you if you run-make noise and get alerted, they will even call for reinforcements. You will need to use your suit powers, quick reflexes, a bit of strategic planning(use things from environment: destruction, distractions) to defeat them.Overall Crysis remastered is a very good game with open world design, good graphics, nice weapon variety and customization, memorable characters, one of the best game physics, good fighting mechanics. The games deserves every dollar it asks for.I would rate the game a 8.5 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? The original was a masterpiece when it was released in 2007 - it had jaw-dropping visuals and was a good shooter, too. This remastered version makes the game playable on Windows 10, with new resolutions (ultrawidescreen worked fine), and adds raytracing if you are one of the few owners of a supported GPU. It also removes the quicksave option of the original and does not include multiplayer or the Warhead expansion. I finished the campaign without problems, but it had a few visual glitches now and then. I would not really call it a masterpiece today anymore - but it was still great fun to fight as a US commando soldier with an overpowered suit and kill North Korean soldiers and then aliens. And yes, I did enjoy the fight against the aliens, too, even if this part of the game plays completely different from the first few hours. The tropical island still looks awesome, some of the levels are really big and you can explore them freely, using different vehicles. The story is absolutely stupid, but who cares - at least it has a story to follow. There may be better FPS out there today, but I still had my fun up to the last fight with the alien mothership. They don't make shooters like this today anymore!FPS for nostalgic fans who want to re-experience the classic, or gamers who want to know if their rig can run Crysis.

(Spoilers after this point, if you would even call them that) In one of the missions, you needed to fly a VTOL aircraft and transport a civilian and such, that was probably one of the worst experinces of a flying a vehicle I have ever had. I used a game pad instead of keyboard and mouse, and I had to use my thumb on the D-Pad (To go up and down) my pointer finger on my left joystick (To move) and the aircraft wouldn't just stay in the air you had to keep elevating it up or it would come crashing down. Also, it probably took me at least a half a hour alone to get through the tornadoes. ANYWAYS, good game if you are playing it for the story/plot (Like me, I have the other two games), but if you are trying to buy this game for its stealth, FPS, or to fly an aircraft? I would just say skip this one and go on the Crysis 2 or 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the sloppiest 'remaster' design choices I've ever experienced; but still one of the best games ever made.Pros:- Plays almost identically to the original.  A successful port of the maps and combat.- New Ray-Tracing looks stunning and adds much more realism and depth to the environment.  - I didn't have a crash throughout my entire playthrough.  The original never ran stably for me; on 5 different systems....Cons:- Many cutscenes have been worsened by goofy lighting, animation glitches, and the occasional audio glitch (late music, missing lipsyncing for 1 line of dialogue etc)- QuickSaving requires a MOD.  I realize the other Crysis games were Auto-Save only, but the more linear gameplay allows for that.  Experimenting with the AI, physics, and combat mechanics were part of what made the original Crysis so replayable and it's an essential part of the experience!- The game has been 'reshaded' with too much saturation for my taste.  The game feels much more 'cheerful' than the original.  The aliens are less scary as a result, too.Recommend only on deep sale or if you've never experienced the original.

This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.

It used to take quite an effort to demolish a building but now one power fist is all it takes. However, once you get used to it, you'll just go on.For this price point, I can certainly say that this game is worth it. If you've never played Crysis before or get used to triple A games in 2023, it will certainly feel clunky. Crysis was always a janky but beautiful tech demo. The remastered is the same mess but with one huge change of adapting the more intuitive suit controls from Crysis 2 and 3. _childDocuments_.review: Playing Crysis now in 2021 is a surreal experience and also an extremely enjoyable one. I can only imagine how awesome this game was back in the day (if you had the hardware to run it). Sadly, I didn’t and I never played it back then, even though I would have loved to. Playing this game now for the first time puts the rest of the series into context for me. I understand the other games better and the series, as a whole, makes more sense. I like the visuals in this remaster and I love how surreal it feels to play an old game that's been cleaned up a bit. The game looks great to me and I think it’s a fantastic mix between old and new aesthetics. I tried to play OG Crysis here on Steam a while ago but I couldn’t enjoy it. I did manage to get it working to some degree on Windows 10 but there was no proper controller support. The performance of this remaster is totally fine and the proper controller support is really what made the game accessible for me... finally. I also got it for a great price because I already owned the original here on Steam, so what is there to complain about?Crysis is a lot of fun to play, it’s like a military sandbox simulator with crazy Koreans and science fiction elements. I always liked the idea in the Crysis sequels, of fighting the soldiers first and then changing things up, to fight the aliens for the second half of the game. Playing through the remaster let me experience that idea in it’s first iteration. Which in-turn made me appreciate the sequels even more and what they were trying to achieve. The hardest difficulty setting (Delta) is great because it makes the game more immersive, without becoming annoying (except for the final boss). It’s really cool to actually need to use the suit powers and environmental cover while taking head-shots and feeling like a bad-ass ninja. There are some cool details on the hardest difficulty too like having to listen for grenades without HUD markers. While the human enemies only speak Korean which makes it harder to determine what they are doing.Where as the rest of the game is totally fine, the final boss is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pain in the ass, on the hardest difficulty setting. Crysis is a lot of fun, just like the sequels and on the harder difficulty settings it’s even more fun, with the only exception to this being the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ final boss. Which required me to die a lot and come up with a crazy trial and error strategy. There is also a fairly crappy level where you have to fly an aircraft and the controls are pretty bad but it’s actually not too difficult, once you get used to it. Crysis Remastered is also a relatively easy and fun game to get 100% achievements on (again with the exception of the final boss). A couple of the more advanced achievements are fairly bugged though, such as the ones for completing the game on the harder difficulties. It’s do-able but they are a bit janky and you need to work around this. Anyway.. this remaster made this fantastic game accessible to me, playing with a controller on Windows 10, for a very low price. I really enjoyed it and I highly recommend that you play it too!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really sure what the point of this remaster is. If it's to make Crysis run on newer operating systems and with newer hardware, then it could have been a patch to the original Crysis. But I didn't really notice any positive gameplay changes.Quicksaving was removed, which is the worst change in my opinion.The walking speeds were changed for the worse, even with "classic nanosuit mode". It feels slower now. (But the cost for powered jumps is reduced.)In old Crysis, left-clicking the big circles with the numbers in the weapon configuration switched through the options. I'm used to doing it this way. In the remastered version, this doesn't work anymore.There were some weird bugs with sound effects being unexpectedly cut off, where I don't remember it being this way in the old version. And the end credits start with cool music that quickly fades away to some calm background trumpet-y music, just to start again like 30 seconds later.There seems to be a bug in the first mission, where enemies on the beach after the three logs that you can roll on two enemies, can see you even though you are cloaked. (Thankfully it only affects this area.) I can't reproduce this bug in old Crysis.So yeah, I can't really recommend the remastered version over the original one. I bought it on sale in a bundle along with Crysis 2 and 3 remastered, so it's fine overall, but if you want to play Crysis 1, I recommend getting the original one.Edit:I forgot to mention: The game handles aspect rations wider than 16:9 very poorly. I played on a 3440x1440 screen (21.5:9). Overlays like the binoculars, sniper scope, etc. are cut on the left and right. Loading screens have similar pillar-boxes on the left and right, and those tend to flicker very intensely. Like, I know that I don't have epilepsy, because if I did, the loading screens would have triggered seizures.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Ultrawide supported just fineYoung people coming up can play and enjoy a legendary shooter that I loved so much back in college...that's about itCons:The manual save system is completely removed. It has checkpoint saves only and you can't choose to go back to specific checkpoints either...your only options are the most recent checkpoint or the beginning of the level and that's it.Every time I start the game back up, that dastardly motion blur setting is back on again no matter how many times I turn it off.While some of the sound effects have been improved (starting rifle and the pistol for example), some are just as bad as they were before (the fictional AK sounds unchanged) however some are significantly worse...the footsteps, even when walking on grass or sand sound like you have giant metal boots and are moving on a metal floor...even when sneaking softly.To use the suit quickwheel menu like the old game, you enable this in the gameplay settings. When you are crouching down and access this wheel, it causes you to stand up for no reason. So hiding behind something and accessing this wheel to cloak means standing up and being seen, defeating the purpose of cloaking because now you need armor mode and are in a fire fight. If you disable this classic wheel mode, you are either in armor or strength mode and just manually enable cloak when needed. However, when you run, it auto uses speed mode! What, why!? I don't want to use speed mode every single time. That should be its own separate setting in my opinion.I think the stealth is off...I used to be able to crouch and hide in bushes/shrubs or prone crawl in high grass until fairly close to an enemy, causing them to get surprised. Now I can sit perfectly still in some bushes and the enemies see me from a pretty good distance away. Crysis 2 and 3 had that issue where stealth was REALLY bad so I'm guessing they maybe used a newer Crytek engine from one of those games to make this one and weren't able to replicate the awesome quality stealth that the original had.The game is horribly optimized.Optimization deserves its own section:I'm no fool, I get that the highest settings are often designed for screenshots and to attract gamers. It gives us something to upgrade for, gives us something to compare to, gives us something to benchmark etc. So typically if I can't max a game I lower stuff one setting at a time as needed and eventually play it smoothly. My system currently is an i9-12900k, 3090ti and 32GBs of DDR5 running windows 10 on a gen 5 (EDIT: oops gen 4 not 5) PCIe NVMe. Theoretically it should be strong enough for everything I can throw at it since I am only running a 1440p ultrawide, not a 4K but still, the max settings were aimed at being future proof such as with the original game so I began tweaking the usual suspects like ray tracing and shadows etc without being annoyed. I got to the coastal house of level 1 (when the sun is up and the jet flies by) and disabled v-sync so I could begin troubleshooting. I ended up basically lowering EVERYTHING to low and it still didn't feel smooth and playable. There is one setting however (Objects Quality) that can't be changed in game so I went back to the main menu to change it. After it lagged on 'Can it Run Crysis' I tried 'Very High' and then 'High.' It started to feel better on 'Medium' but didn't feel smooth until 'Low.' You have got to be kidding me. It seriously either lagged hardcore or felt like my walk speed was varying in speed as I moved along with anything above 'Low.' Never seen a single setting so badly optimized. Isn't a dealbreaker by itself but really odd.Long story short - I think this was a huge disappointment and can't recommend it to anyone that played the original.If you did NOT play the original then this one is probably a better choice since the original is also horribly optimized but also struggles in other ways on modern systems.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous graphics ahead of its time. In this remastered version it has become even better with high resolution textures and revised atmospheric lighting.- Great physics that were innovative for back then. You can interact, shoot, throw or shatter almost everything in a very convincing way. After a battle has finished, the landscape will be absolutely destroyed. A feature that even new games miss.- Well paced battles with many things happening simultaneously. Good immersion level at a war situation.- Gameplay allows you to choose between various approaches, either more tactical or entirely destructive. Cloak and shield powers of nanosuit are good additions that give the gameplay extra depth.- Awesome survival atmosphere. Some parts have a weird dark, terrifying feeling. After a certain point it gets surreal and artistic.- Fantastic sound design. Both environmental and battles' design feels natural and rich of sounds. Surround is well implemented and helps you understand enemies' direction.- Interesting music that fits perfectly in each situation and gives an extra boost to the atmosphere.- Nice animations especially at enemy creatures and at the protagonist's hands.- It is very cinematic for its age. Great direction and camera movement with some nice timed events and special effects. Cool cut scenes too.- You can drive a boat, a hummer, a tank and even fly an airplane.- The story has a cliché beginning but after the middle it offers some interesting twists. It is still simplistic but descent enough for this king of shooter.- It is well balanced. Normal difficulty will challenge you without being too hard.The bad- Navigation mechanics and interaction commands are not very responsive. Constant small glitches here and there (e.g. when crouching) will sometimes ruin the pace and the vibe you are into.- Big loading screens and bad optimization for a game that old. You have to enable vsynch, otherwise the game will roast your cpu.- Mediocre enemies' AI. Sometimes they react very slowly and others they run towards you instead of covering.- Small variety of weapons and even fewer weapons' upgrades.- You cannot save whenever you want. Sometimes there is a long distance to cover between two autosave points.- The map is bad and most things on it are indistinguishable.- The control mechanics of the airplane part are poorly implemented. Frustrating.- It has small duration and abrupt ending. In fact there is no ending. I didn't like this weird final boss battle too.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis was my favorite video game franchise as a teenager, yet I was lukewarm at Crysis 1 for a few things – balance, level design and AI, but this remastered version turns out to be more likeable thanks to rebalance.The original is not an easy game and the high-tech nanosuit always feels like it is no thicker than a piece of paper, especially for my younger self who was a much less experienced gamer. Some weapons are difficult to work with because of the range and recoil, and damage seems wildly inconsistent, like a helicopter could eat 3 shots of RPG like nothing.With the rebalance in remaster, nonsense like that no longer happens and all weapons are more manageable and fun to use with consistent damage. Difficulty and playtime drop as a result (15 vs 7 hours for the first playthrough), but it is a major step up for the experience. On the flip side, the necessity of stealth largely decreases, and I find myself always in favor of direct combat with the game becoming easier, so I say the remaster is less strategic and more simple shooting fun, though higher difficulty should revert that.Perhaps because of the rebalance and the lower difficulty, or the developer made some changes in levels (I am not sure if there are any), or just me became a better gamer, the remaster doesn’t have a lot of frustration the original has, which is why back then, I was not a fan of the more open level design of Crysis 1.With the frustration gone, I started to appreciate the more open level design allowing more freedom to decide how to approach objectives. I also become appreciative of the level variety that has car, ship, tank and aircraft levels arranged in an organized manner like Halo, which the second and third Crysis no longer have. That said, it is still confusing AF on how to kill the first boss in the final level as the game still doesn’t give clear instructions.It is disappointing that the remaster doesn’t fix the biggest issue - AI. They are still dumb AF and they still have hypersensitive detection as the original - the lush vegetation makes it difficult for players to spot enemies, but they have no trouble seeing through, reminding me why the OG is so frustrating.The OG has great graphics for its time but is not comparable to modern games. The remaster updated but didn’t overhaul graphics, and what really noticeable changes are clearer water, bluer sky, greener vegetation and more saturated color tones, which make it less photorealistic than the original. While doing so, the game introduces a contrast issue causing dark areas to be very hard to see, but without offering a proper tool to calibrate.In conclusion, the remaster indeed is a better version of the game, but I don’t think the improvements are substantial enough to warrant a re-release (an rebalance update to the OG is probably enough). It is more of an eye-grabber for Cry Engine and future sequel. But if you have the original, you can get the remaster dirt cheap now, so why not?

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be as honest as I can with this Crysis 1 "Remaster"I'm brand new to Crysis, never having had the ability to run these games when they were in their prime, back circa 2007 or whatever. I've since bought the original Crysis 1 after this remaster made me puke blood.So naturally, anyone new to the series who's buying this version of Crysis 1 for the first time would probably think: "Well, I've never played the original so I might like the remaster purely for what it is, despite it's many claimed differences".Wrong.You're going to shoot yourself in the foot if you approach this Remaster with that attitude, and you ain't going to have no nanosuit to protect those toes either. Allow me to begin:(1) The "volumetric clouds" look like silly bubbles.(2) The sky is so blue that it makes me feel like I'm in Bikini Bottom from Spongebob.(3) The grass is a saturated cartoon green that makes me feel as if someone tried to put me in a jar with a leaf so that they could attempt to mimic my human environment for me.(4) My "3080Ti Mobile" flings the fps counter from 90 down to 45 in two person gun fights, showing some very poor optimization that shouldn't be evident in a game this old. The pain doesn't stop there, I promise. This version is essentially the pc version, ported to console with downgrades, then ported back again from console back to PC with "enhancements". Lies, all lies.The old version of Crysis 1, which has since been removed from Steam, never really was the way to go either. Steam's original version was 32bit only, making it a avoidable version at best.Just avoid this, unless you like Fortnite or something.

Although this seems like a replacement its actually not because both games feel different and do offer different experiences so I would still recommend both versions including warhead to anyone who enjoys this. Delta difficulty feels like what It should have been and that's what brings out the nano-suit's game-play potential. @Crytek My only comment is a big wish to have some enemies spawn in different locations when you re-spawn, replay a map or start a new game all together, so that it would maintain suspense in replays, because it is ultimately those situations when you go in blind which require you to make the right choices with the nano-suit, whether you should play it slow or not, so on and so forth - it makes for epic immersive game-play and helps bring all the environment around you to life.  I still see much potential for this title regardless of newer installments. Reflecting on your pre-alpha/alpha development builds - that simple military style of the game HUD had/has a special impact on my perception and perspective of the game; that version of the HUD gives it a raw military systems feel of IRL modern combat and It changes how the nano-suit feels. I also always wondered why the dive mechanic was removed - t's very easy to see dynamic spawns and a dive mechanic to work very well together. Immersion is important.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a remaster. It's not even a compatibility update for new hardware. _childDocuments_.review: Buggier, looks worse, has features removed, gameplay tweaks make it worse, performance is worse. Everything about this game is worse; it's the opposite of a remaster. - Some bugs make the game outright unplayable, like losing the ability to perform any actions like switching weapons or picking up items midway through the game. The game also frequently hangs when a level has loaded 100%. Mouse movement also doesn't work for the VTOL mission, meaning you literally cannot play the game pass the VTOL mission if you don't have a controller, and even then, the controls on the gamepad are horrible, and even still bug out sometimes, where the left stick would stop working altogether. This is after the patch that was said to fix most of the issues. - It looks worse despite using the improved engine with a bunch of new graphical features, looking over-saturated and contrasty. - They removed the ability to save manually, so you'll have to rely on autosaves. - Ammo in your gun counts towards your total ammo, which didn't happen before. This doesn't make sense, the magazine in the gun isn't in my pocket, so why the change? In fact, if you empty your magazine by 1 round, you can pick up 1 additional round. This makes zero sense. - The new suit mode sucks, but at least they let you switch back to the old mode. - I can't figure out what is causing my performance to drop so badly despite the settings being similar to the old Crysis. If all this game did was add higher res textures, SMAA, TAA, DLSS, and Raytracing, that would have been at least a half-decent 'enhanced' edition, which when combined with the discount for existing Crysis owners would be fine. Then they could have thought of extras like recorded playback, crosshair customization, an FOV slider, and maybe even co-op campaign, and that would have been a good remaster. It's amazing how they instead managed to make the game worse. I literally have never had such a frustration experience trying to play a game in my life. This is such a disservice to the original Crysis which is a legendary game. Whoever is thinking of playing the game, just get the original, it's way better than this piece of crap and is even available DRM free on GOG.

_childDocuments_.review: Transport yourself back to the scorching summer of 2008, a time when gaming was forever altered by the arrival of Crysis. I vividly recall being a wide-eyed 9-year-old, eagerly exploring the realms of PC gaming for the first time. With my father's purchase of our inaugural computer and my uncle's installation of Crysis, I was thrust into a world of unparalleled excitement and challenge.In those early days, the term "but can it run Crysis?" hadn't yet become ubiquitous, but the impact of Crytek's masterpiece was palpable from the get-go. As I delved into the game, I was immediately captivated by its stunning graphics and immersive gameplay. Every pixel seemed to pulsate with life, drawing me deeper into the lush jungles and sprawling landscapes of the game's setting.But Crysis was more than just a visual spectacle; it was a true test of skill and perseverance. As a young player, navigating the game's challenges was no easy feat. From tactical encounters with enemy soldiers to heart-pounding battles against otherworldly foes, every moment was a thrilling adventure filled with triumphs and setbacks.Yet, despite the difficulty, I found myself utterly engrossed in Crysis, spending countless hours honing my skills and pushing the limits of what I thought was possible. The sense of accomplishment that came with overcoming each obstacle was unlike anything I had experienced before in a game.Looking back now, it's clear that Crysis set a revolutionary standard in gaming. Its groundbreaking graphics and innovative gameplay mechanics pushed the boundaries of what was possible in the medium, paving the way for future generations of titles to follow.As the years have passed, my admiration for Crysis has only grown stronger. And with the recent announcement of Crysis 4, I find myself eagerly anticipating the next chapter in this iconic franchise. If Crytek can capture even a fraction of the magic that made the original Crysis so special, then we're in for a truly unforgettable gaming experience.In conclusion, Crysis remains a timeless masterpiece that continues to captivate players young and old. Its stunning graphics, challenging gameplay, and enduring legacy make it a must-play for anyone with a love for gaming. So here's to Crysis, a game that will forever hold a special place in my heart and the hearts of gamers around the world.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered brings the classic shooter into the modern era with significant graphical updates and support for the latest display technologies, including HDR. The game's innovative suit powers and diverse combat scenarios remain as engaging as ever, providing a gameplay experience that is both challenging and rewarding.The remaster enhances the iconic storyline and setting, allowing both new and returning players to experience the game's narrative in a visually stunning manner. The addition of modern resolutions support ensures that Crysis Remastered looks its best on contemporary hardware.However, the game's transition to the modern era is not without its flaws. Notably, the VTOL mission presents a significant challenge for PC players due to control issues when using a mouse, necessitating the use of a controller for an optimal experience. Additionally, the game suffers from a variety of bugs, including sound issues that detract from the immersive experience. Sound effects may get stuck or disappear entirely, and invisibility glitches can break the gameplay flow.Performance-wise, Crysis Remastered demands more from systems than expected, considering the technological advancements in gaming hardware. Players with high-end PCs may find the game running poorly, even when other graphically intense games perform flawlessly on the same setup.In conclusion, while Crysis Remastered successfully revives a beloved classic with stunning graphical enhancements and maintains the core gameplay elements that made the original game a landmark in the FPS genre, it is hampered by technical issues. These include control problems, bugs, and unexpected performance requirements. Despite these setbacks, for fans of the series and newcomers alike, the game offers a worthwhile experience, albeit with some caveats.

_childDocuments_.review: Its fun, yes. It was a milestone when it was initially released, and while its a super linear story shooter, it still manages to suck you in. A lot of the features of this engine was soon to be the standard in later released games.However, strictly talking about the first Crysis Remastered Game, I cannot advise you to buy it.What is the problem?The Crysis 1 Remaster is based on the Xbox 360 Release Code, and therefore is heavily downgraded in a lot of areas. (e.g. Vegetation doesnt even react to your explosions anymore.)It also just runs bad. Lets face it, its not a debate. The game has no noteworthy upgrades besides a very basic raytracing implementation and some lighting upgrades. Playing the original game heavily modded with similar upgrades, is still running - twice - as good as this remaster. How can such an old game only run on 70 fps on a modern mid-end machine? (RTX 3080, 5600x) I used to play the original game on a 7800 GT with an Athlon XP 3200+, just think about this for a moment. Im not even talking about the "Can it run Crysis?"-Meme Graphic-Mode, that has practically no noteworthy difference then just running the game in a slideshow.While not so important for me personally, as I dont think a lot of people would still play it today, its also missing the multiplayer part of the original game. Something that should be mentioned.It also doesnt come with the standalone addon Crysis Warhead, and there is also no Remaster-Version in general for Crysis Warhead. Something I think is needed, considering the price-tag for this remaster.So as long as you are not buying it for the integrated nanosuit-hotkey mode (Introduced in Crysis 2 and 3), or the achievements, you are better off with the original game. You can get the original game on origin for like 2 dollars, or on GOG for like 5 dollars. Also buy the original Crysis Warhead.Only ever buy this remaster when the whole Trilogy is heavily discounted and you already know you want to play the sequels.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never got to play the original, this was an interesting play. The gameplay is stiff and clunky, the stealth system is pretty awfull (enemies spot you through objects at any range as long as they have line of sight) and the story and lore is barebones.I did enjoy most of the first half of the game once I got used to the clunkyness and learned to weave in and out of combat rather than go full stealth, but the second half diminished that enjoyment. It is one of those game where I wish Steam had a "netutral" option, but I choose to recommend it due to it's legacy, and the fact that it is, except for some slight visual polish, a 16 year old game which has held up pretty well.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I bought it a few years after its release, I enjoyed the original. I also wish they had upgraded the game mechanics/controls/gameplay so all match. This version is really, mostly, just the original with a new set of textures and, maybe, some raytracing thrown in.I will say that there are a couple things that were in at least one of the original Crysis (first game) that weren't in this one.  I seem to remember that there was a defense at the mineshaft (after the small encampment fight that included the (second) tank) and inside that shaft, clearing it.Also, with what I consider to be a huge gameplay omission, you can no longer press <Shift> and W while prone to move in the prone mode at a higher speed than regular crawling.  Now, when you are prone, have pressed W, and then <Shift>, you STAND UP and start running.  A really bad situation when you are surrounded by enemies!  There were a number of times that I REALLY wish I could still do this.Anyway, if you either have never played the game or its been a couple years, then I think y'all will enjoy this version.  But don't expect more than (mostly) a new coat of paint over the same old vehicle.Do I recommend it?  Yes.  Could it have been better if some of the "under the covers" had been improved?  Also, yes.Oh, and only worth buying at a 50%+ sale...AMD Ryzen 9 3950x64GB RAM (WAY overkill for gaming, I do video editing)Nvidia RTX 4080 (150+ fps)2x Alienware 1440p 160hz monitors (SUPER color accurate, once calibrated, avg DE <0.30, NOT a typo!)

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, horrible remaster.This is a game that I’ve played since 2007, I still have my physical copy of it on my shelf and I’ve played it many times with many hardware configurations, so without a shadow of a doubt, I kinda have a feeling when a scene is rendered correctly or not.I played this remaster from start to finish with Ray Tracing  and it sure does look absolutely beautiful, one of the best looking games of 2007 is still one of the best looking games in 2023, no question about it. But it only looks great in very specific circumstances, for example, in bright daylight the RT technology shines (no pun intended), but in the second half of the game which involves a lot of dark areas and a lot of snow, you’d be hard pressed to tell if RT is still being used if it wasn’t for the performance hit.The last level was particularly painful for how darn DARK it gets, there’s a certain lab scene that makes it unreasonably dark when there’s like 5 people in the same room, it sure as heck should be a lot brighter with that many people in it. Not only the dark scenes get comically dark, but I’ve also found plenty of gameplay bugs, especially in the second half, like rocks that sway back and forth like leaves, soldiers getting stuck in important doorways, dialogues that trigger a second time in a row after going back to where the trigger was, music cutting in and out… I understand this is an old game with very different tech than what is considered standard nowadays, but it sure as heck didn’t feel like it was falling apart like a house made out of sticks and glue with a shiny polish.And that’s without mentioning how bad they screwed with the controls, Saber Interactive, in their infinite wisdom, wanted the controls to feel closer to it’s sequels, but it only feels like a forced, dumbed down version of the original without the tight feel of the sequels, fortunately you can go back to the original controls, but ALSO they took away the quick save feature in place of a crappy checkpoint system without letting you pick from earlier saves if you somehow get screwed by said system.I’m in a sort of predicament with this review, I do not recommend this remaster because of how buggy it felt throughout my playthrough, but I also hesitate to recommend the original release instead because of how hard it is to make it run at reasonable framerates on modern computers. Don't buy the original on Steam, instead I’d recommend the GOG release of the original Crysis along with Warhead, you can get both for dirt cheap and they both already have most fixes applied, namely without DRM --which was a big issue with both games back in the day.Game is still worth playing, but stay away from this remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Go as part of an elite squad to Lingshan Island to rescue a group of scientists from captivity.Take advantage of a special nanosuit that gives a person abilities that exceed those of an ordinary person! Jump several meters high, disappear - to get close to enemies from any direction, destroy buildings and objects around you, run like lightning! And all this in an updated graphics!With the release of Crysis in 2007, Crytek raised the bar on graphics to heights that many other titles could not. The game (for that time) could boast not only excellent graphics, but also destructible environments, good voice acting and immersiveness. The player immersed himself in the game and, together with the hero, thought out his way to the point of the task - through the Jungle filled with Koreans.In 2020, Crytek decided to play on the feelings of the players and just released the same game again. Only slightly improving the graphics in some places - adding a newfangled rtx. Which, instead of making an already great game even more colorful, did the opposite.With the advent of rtx in the world of Crysis, the surrounding space became bright, pale and lost most of the shadows. In addition, Crytek has significantly degraded most of the textures. Because of what it is already impossible to look at the faces of the heroes without a shudder.I sincerely believe that Crytek wanted to make the game better - but simply loading the game with new technologies is not the same as improving it. Due to the changes, the game has become hundreds of times easier, losing the former challenge that the original threw.I do not recommend this game. Especially if you have not played the original, then I advise you to buy it easier than this remaster.

As for the actual game, it depends, do you like gunplay against smart ai in tight scenarios? You won't get that, however, if you enjoy driving like a madman away from enemies as they try desperately to kill you while you dodge trees, jump hills, etc. you'll love this game, or atleast the first half, the second half starts with a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ zero-g segment that i got lost in for a decent amount of time, and the enemies are boring af to fight. Seriously just look up a guide when you enter the mountain until you're out. After you leave the mountain, vehicles are less common but the gunplay becomes much more enjoyable partly because you get OP guns and enemies are a lot more versatile. Along with these the Michael Bay level of explosions and spectacle helps to compensate for any boredom. Finally the game ends with a fairly intense boss fight and a cliffhanger.
