_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played Crysis before, I think I would still recommend starting with the original version, but if you're a longtime fan this remaster offers an interesting new lens to play the game through and it never hurts to play Crysis again. I would probably give the game a sideways thumb if I could, since there are aspects both better and worse than the original, but considering owners of the original can get a pretty good discount it's worthwhile if you can get it cheap.There are definitely some visual aspects that look a bit nicer. It's not revelatory but the new reflection effects to make certain things pop a bit better and I've always been of the opinion some of the original game's textures looked a bit over-sharpened, which the new volumetric fog smooths over nicely. The raytracing is pretty tasteful and in-line with the original art direction without being overdone, and there's some cool uses of it, such as being able to see your own reflection when you pick up a CRT Television. Character models seem largely the same but again, the facial textures don't seem as overdone on the sharpness filter and faces are a bit nicer to look at in general. For some reason the original Crysis didn't have anti-aliasing which struck me as odd even at the time given the game's intent of having every graphical technology under the sun. The blues and greens of the island seem to pop more as well, which is very pretty to look at and the water in particular looks great.What is disappointing is that the Godrays seem toned down compared to the original. The scene in the first part where you finally step out onto the beach at sunrise was not only an iconic moment of the game, but a historic moment in game history itself that said "This is what games are gonna look like in 5 years" and the lighting just felt toned down here compared to the original which made that bit lose some of its edge. So while I do like a lot of what the remaster does, it's not a complete upgrade. Performance seems fine, but admittedly I'm running the game on the deliberately absurd "Can it Run Crysis?" mode, which on my 3090 tends to hover around 50fps which is pretty playable. I'm sure if I dialed it down to something more normal I would get a great framerate but my Tim Allen-like desire for MORE POWER UGH UGH UGH prevents me from setting my games to anything less than the maximum, and frankly if the newest edition of Crysis runs smoothly on Max it means that either it's time for a new Crysis or that society has come too far.The default control scheme in this remastered edition is also . Thankfully you can more or less set everything to how it was in the original but the default setting makes the game way more awkward to play. They tried to streamline the suit controls by basically having the powers activate when you do an action that can use that particular power. So for example, if you hold the jump or throw buttons you can do a "strength jump" or "strength throw". It works fine for the suit and cloaking (which is just the e key), but every time you sprint the suit goes into speedmode which wastes precious suit energy and it doesn't seem to let you just do a normal sprint. The streamlined controls worked in  and 3 because the whole game design was pared down for a more consolized experience, but trying to put a consolized control scheme in what is otherwise an unchanged full-fledged tactical PC shooter is just a mess of a default to ship the game with.The placement of the hotkeys also means that the lean keys are mapped to T and H by default which is wildly inconvenient and I personally feel that making the deliberate choice of suit mode before jumping into combat was a deliberate part of the tactical considerations the original game wanted you to make rather than being able to just have everything at the press of a button. Again, you can set things back to how they originally were, and I get the feeling the streamlined setup was meant for the console ports then somehow got backported onto PC, but the default binds make the game significantly more clunky for no reason and deeply uncomfortable to try and use in combat. There's a weird weapon select menu if you press the 6 key which is absolutely  but thankfully the original weapon switch keys are normal by default as well. That said though, the quick tips never change based on what your key setting are, so you might have the game telling you to press a button you mapped to something else, which feels unpolished.Once you get over the jank of trying to remap the controls though,  is still as fun as ever. The game was derided by some at the time as a mere tech demo, but I find myself coming back to it again and again over the years even after the visuals begin to look dated in spots (and the original still mostly looks amazing). It's a true tactical sandbox, and while the game isn't "open world", each level is wide enough that you can approach from any direction and really get creative with how you want to handle a scenario. See a vehicle you like? Jump in and rampage through town. While there have been other sandbox shooters since, like the various  sequels (and keep in mind  was the follow-up to  1, before Ubisoft took that series in a different direction),  and the  series are the only big ones that really do it this well. Your suit is powerful, but it won't compensate for bad decisions and the level design is just great. I do agree with the general consensus that the last quarter of the game isn't as good as the first due to a shift in the enemies you fight, but it's still fun. The gameplay feels pretty much the same, one or two weapons seem to have a punchier sound effect, but it's still the same old  and you don't have to twist my arm to much to get me on a new playthrough.While  isn't perfect, it certainly isn't a  either. The visual refreshes are interesting enough to be worth going through again and I wouldn't be surprised if someone either mods the remaster to have the better aspects of the original, or ports stuff from the remaster into the original. It is a pretty glaring omission that they left out the  expansion which is fantastic in its own right, but it's nice to see  being done with the series.  If you've never played the original, I'd again recommenced the original, but if you're already a fan and looking for something new, it's not a bad way to kill a few days.

There are multiple paths and tactical methods one can take and deploy to approach each level which is really appreciated and rare in FPS games.  The remaster is relatively well executed and again makes testing new systems fun.  Early in the original's release people would use Tri-SLI 8800 GTX geforce Nvidia cards to try to  run the game at 30 FPS at 1080p! It's one of the only FPS that still is fun to play in 2023 and will always be one of my favorite FPS games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was the pinnacle of graphics back in the day. I remember buying a new graphic card twice plus a fresh set of RAM to max out all the details and it looked incredible - still with 30frames max but as long it looked great who cared :) The remaster had a rough start at release, right now in its current state it plays nice, but there are still some bugs around. Some of them you may know from the original game, most of them are new, at least for myself. Especially at the end of the game they where quite some of them around, but nothing game breaking. Sometimes the frames dropped for a few seconds for whatever reason, sometimes there's no muzzle flash, invisible walls or rubber banding. Also I had a weird facial animation bug one time. When having the "reduced movement" bug just change weapons and you're good. In its core its still Crysis of course, it will always be one of my fav games, but besides the updated graphics (raytracing looks great) I'd still prefer the original, maybe with some mods. Textures where updated and looked nice in 4K, but they forgot soem spot here and there.Achievment wise its very easy, got all of them in one run under 10 hours. Delta difficulty is pretty easy, thanks to your suit. I recommend to start "Marathon man" early on so you dont have to power-sprint around at the end of the game to pop the achievment. Also look out for the yellow markers for side objectives, but they are very easy to spot, plus the game tells you every time.Final verdict: If you loved the first one its cool to come back after all these years, if you got the hardware. In 4K it still takes a lot of ressources. There are bugs, but nothing game breaking. Plus, should you be a  completionist like me, its a very easy 100% game when it comes to achievments.

_childDocuments_.review: A classic reborn with some tweaksPeople often think of Crysis as a shallow tech demo game versus an actual fully formed open world romp. You are on an island, you get objectives, now go explore and find ways to complete those objectives. Its a semi-linear branching path where you can do all sorts of mayhem in the destructible game world. Its a simple plot, nothing too deep here, but enjoyable all the same.Its a short romp, only about 6-7 hours, probably about 15 if you wanna replay on the Delta difficulty and go for all the achievements. But it doesnt really overstay its welcome. The remaster of the game has some simplified control options (and the ability to go back to classic) but it can feel a bit clunky at times, especially picking up ammo and weapons can feel very..well.. frustrating at times, not helped by them sometimes clipping through terrain. The big highlight on the remaster is the RT reflections, which are really cool and add a lot to the game, in fact the RT and SVOGI implementation makes the game look absolutely stunning if you have the hardware to run it, but it is an older game and there are limits to it compared to more modern titlesWould I recommend it? Yes I think I would to anyone just getting into PC gaming, Its a classic and a game that crushed PC hardware 15 years ago and with RT, manages to strain it today. Just remember its a 15 year old game and it has its quirks.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game and the remaster is... fine. It's absolutely unnecessary if you already own it, but the controller support is nice. It runs worse and doesn't look that much better for it. There's also quite a few glitches, especially on the flying VTOL level that required multiple restarts just to scrape through the level without the ship spinning wildly through the scenery but not actually crashing on almost every attempt.The biggest problem isn't with the remaster but with the game itself. It's a lot of fun, right up until about the final third of the game. It's been said before, but it's absolutely true. Once the aliens arrive, the fun just drops out of the game. Fighting human enemies in the nanosuit is amazing, but these enemies from the zero gravity level onwards are tedious and annoying and that continues for the rest of the game. Just endless fire from above from floating enemies, but they also often hove directly above you and the game doesn't actually let you aim directly up for some stupid reason, so there are levels where they will occasionally shoot you from a position you cannot fire back from. It doesn't seem intentional, but it happened enough to make it annoying.So get the game, play it up until the aliens, and then honestly just quit right there. It's actively anti-fun from that point onwards and it doesn't get better.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to be honest, my heart has always leaned more towards "Crysis 2." Maybe it's the nostalgia of that urban battleground or the more polished feel. But that doesn't mean the original "Crysis" doesn't pack a punch.Set in a lush, tropical paradise, the game is a beautiful mix of stealth and chaos. The suit's capabilities, switching between armor, speed, and stealth, are a game-changer (quite literally). Each encounter feels like a sandbox where strategies can be mixed and matched. And then there's that iconic tagline: "But can it run Crysis?" This game was, and still is, the benchmark for graphical prowess.The remastered version? It does justice to the original, amplifying what was already a graphical marvel. The sun filtering through the dense foliage, the ripples in the water, the detailed textures — it's all enhanced and feels more alive.For all its worth, while "Crysis 2" might have stolen my heart, the original "Crysis" laid the foundation. It set the stage for what was to come, introducing us to the Nanosuit, the alien threat, and a world where strategy and raw firepower go hand in hand.So, if you're curious about the Crysis universe and wondering where to start, "Crysis Remastered" is the gateway. It's the genesis of the series, and it provides context to the sequels. While it might not be my top pick of the franchise, it's undeniably essential. Strap on that Nanosuit and dive in; the jungle awaits.

_childDocuments_.review: + No Denuvo DRM. + Support for Achievements.+ DLSS Support for Nvidia RTX Cards.+ Still plays like Crysis (2007) overall, despite the negatives I’m about to list from what I’ve experienced and read from other people.- No Cloud Saving Support. - No Multiplayer and Crysis Warhead is still treated like the red-headed stepchild of the Crysis Family.- It’s based off the PS3/XBOX 360 version which means the benefits of being able to quicksave are completely gone and now, the nanosuit powers have been nerfed both in effectiveness and how they control/feel.- Apart from SVOGI and Ray Tracing, the “remastered” graphics artistically look much worse and uglier overall than the original PC version. Said Ray Tracing isn't worth the hit to performance since it only focuses on reflections.- Optimisation on PC is still busted thanks to Cryengine still only using single threaded performance from the CPU. This results in constant stuttering even at the lowest settings while using v-sync. - Lingering bugs that aren’t fixed in the Epic Games version still persist in the Steam version.- Now uses EOS (Epic Online Services) despite strictly being a single player experience.- Casts doubt that the remastering efforts for Crysis 2 and 3 won’t be a disaster, since both of them will be still Epic Games Store exclusives for a year.  - All of these negative aspects, combined with no actual improvements equate to making the 20% discount at launch and an extra 30% for those who own the original PC version, still a complete rip-off for what you’re paying for vs what you get.

_childDocuments_.review: Experience – First TimeWorld/Setting – 7/10Story – 6/10Music – 5.5/10Gameplay – 6/10Overall Review – 6/10One Line Review – Game of Two HalvesReviewWorld/SettingThe World of Crysis is gorgeous to look at. From the moment you parachute in to the world, you are amazed by it. The vegetation, environment, water etc. everything impresses you about the world, considering the game came out in 2007. But once you get used to it, it becomes boring pretty quickly. And the reason for that is simple: repetition. For the first half of the game, you are only exposed to the jungle. It is only in the second half that you experience the real reason for this game’s existence: aliens. After that, the second half of the game becomes much more interesting! The environment constantly changes. One level you are inside an alien ship and in the next level you are struck by blizzard. The variation in the levels makes the second half of the game ‘the better half’.StoryThe story of Crysis is good, but pretty predictable. The reason for that is: We have been exposed to these kinds of stories for a long time, from transformers to AvP etc. The difference comes because this is a game, which means interaction. You discover everything by your own. The first half of the story is, you fight North Koreans who have captured a research team along with the entire archipelago. The second half: you fight aliens! That is all I am going to say.MusicThe music was good. If you can call a single track playing again and again ‘good’.GameplayThe gameplay was pretty lackluster, apart from nano suit feature, which was great! The guns were good to handle, at least some of them were. The nano suit features were great! But were limited in its scope. It did not help that the ‘power bar’ drained so quickly that you could not really experiment with your nano suit features at all.

_childDocuments_.review: While crysis is a good game this just isn't worth it. Visuals:  It looks better than the original but the performance you get doesn't match the quality of the visuals.   It is also very inconsistent, some things look great while others look like they reused original textures.   It creates this unbalance that looks worse than either would on their own.   Like the way things are destroyed looks really really bad and cheesy.     On top of that even with a top of the line graphics card there is a good amount of studdering.  Gameplay:The gunplay itself is excellent and the guns are fun to use.    The enemies in general are fairly tough although that is one of my major complaints is when the enemies literally take more shots to kill than they can kill you in when your the one wearing the high tech nanosuit.  Balance is all over the place for the most part, some things were stupidly easy and others ended up overly difficult.    There isn't a good difficulty curve to the game it just randomly spikes and dips.  You get sections that are a joke followed by an overly difficult part and then another overly easy section.      Balance is utterly broken at times and some things are just flat out bugged.   For example, on the final fight it is possible to get chain frozen until you die which is just annoying and makes the fight a chore instead of being fun.       Enemies seem to sometimes just know your location and will just look straight at you if you get too close even with stealth and crouched and the lack of a takedown makes actual stealth gameplay suck since you can't really misdirect enemies or take down enemies without alerting everyone around.  The strength options are completely useless in the game and honestly even the defensive shield gets chewed through so quickly by the more dangerous enemies that it is borderline useless.   On the other hand you can completely cheese the stealth mechanic and enemy AI with a bit of range by shooting from stealth hiding behind a tree and stealthing again.     It made the gameplay balance just feel terrible and should have been something you would have expected to be fixed in the remaster.  Sound: the sound is pretty much the same as the original and not that good.  There is nothing to say here, it sounds like a 15 year old game.  It honestly didn't seem like they did anything with the remake in that department.    Pretty much if you never have played the original it is worth buying because the game is still fun and the price isn't bad for the 6-10 hours your going to get out of the game at 25 dollars.  Honestly though that is the most I would say it has in value.   It has very little replay value, no multiplayer and isn't very long.  Ideally I would recommend wait for a sale to be honest.   The game definately isn't worth the price if you already own the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but only as part of the Crysis Remastered Trilogy bundle. Note that it doesn't feature multiplayer, and there are no cloud saves at time of writing.The Remaster:- This is an interesting remaster since it's not built on the original engine of the PC version of Crysis, resulting in some gameplay differences, notably AI not behaving quite the same. It's not a big deal if you've never played the game before since the general gameplay features are still there, but if you've played the original on PC the experience is a bit different. There is also a revised set of Nanosuit controls, which I think is designed to function more like Crysis 2 and 3, but I never actually tested them and instead used the classic Nanosuit controls that behave like the original Crysis.- Performance wise things aren't too bad if you change a few settings to avoid CPU problems: if you put objects to high, vegetation and shadows to medium / high, you get a level of detail and draw distance that's similar or better than the original game for increased performance, and most other settings (apart from ray tracing) can be turned up to maximum without much impact. Another advantage of the remaster is that it works out of the box on Windows 10, whereas the original game requires user fixes to launch at all.- In terms of graphics, it's a bit of a mixed bag. The updated assets generally look quite nice, but compared to the original the colour tone is a bit over-saturated during the day, yet the dawn and dusk sequences have less atmosphere. There are ray traced reflections too which are nice to have if you've got the hardware, though the number of reflective surfaces is a bit limited in many areas.- Unfortunately there are a few annoying problems with the remaster. I had to use console commands to set additional min and max sensitivity values, as the menu slider didn't give me a low enough value, but then the tank had a ridiculously low sensitivity so I had to change them during gameplay too. There are also some audio problems, such as shooting an enemy from long distance and his shouts from being hit are like he's right in front of your face, and there are other similar imbalances which don't help with positional audio and dialogue during gameplay either.Conclusion:- Overall it's not a terrible remaster, but I feel like the lack of polish and some of the visual changes hamper it a bit, and given how iconic the original was for PC gaming at the time, I recommend playing the original first if you can just for the classic experience. That said, the remaster is worth a play if you get it as part of the Crysis Remastered Trilogy bundle, and if you've never played the original the remaster will still give you the general gameplay feel so you're not missing out, without any fixes required to get it running either.The Game:- The first half of the game features sandbox levels where you fight the Korean army using your Nanosuit features for temporary increases in speed, strength, or a cloak for near invisibility. You can interact with just about anything; picking up objects and throwing them, shooting down small trees, destroying buildings, and driving around in vehicles. You can acquire shotguns, assault rifles, a sniper rifle and more, picking up attachments along the way such as lasers, scopes and grenade launchers. This gives a good variety of options for traversing the tropical island and completing objectives - you can go in guns blazing or sneak around with the cloak etc.- The second half of the game is where most people's complaints come from. It becomes increasingly linear, and you start fighting aliens instead with a reduced amount of combat options. I personally don't mind it that much, but the first half of the game is definitely where things shines and why (in combination with the visuals) it was so iconic back in the day.

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster is a pretty mixed bag but generally I'd recommend it over the original. First, let me get a big thing out of the way. This version is based on the Xbox 360/Playstation 3 port of Crysis. This was likely done as those ports were done on CryEngine 3, while the PC original runs on CryEngine 2. Unfortunately, this brings some sacrifices. The enemy placement and number in levels is different from the PC release. and the AI also behaves slightly differently. Certain visual features are missing or replaced with more performance-friendly and in some cases less impressive looking counterparts. The infamous "Ascension" mission was missing at launch, and was only added in a patch later down the line, and there's a widespread bug in that said mission that prevents mouse input, requiring use of a controller or a program to map mouse input to controller input. In terms of general visual quality and design, it's a real mixed bag. Some stuff looks really good like the overall lighting composition, water looks great, it's not a bad-looking game by any means, but then there's some iffy stuff. Most, if not all. of the geometry and meshes, are exactly the same. This means many objects are still very obviously jagged and low-detail. The colors in the Remaster are also far more saturated, most notably in the missions taking place in forests and jungles, the grass and leaves on the trees are a richer, brighter green, which gives the game a less photorealistic look. I definitely wish there was a mod that changed said foliage assets to a more natural hue. (This is more of a personal nitpick rather than an objective criticism, however) Performance and tech-wise this remaster is actually a pretty dramatic step up. Anti-Aliasing looks far better than the 2007 game's primitive MSAA solution, leading to far less flickering on stuff like foliage or distant detailed objects and textures. You can push out the game's rendering and draw-distance a lot more, at the incredibly demanding "Can it Run Crysis?" setting, the game's LOD and Foliage rendering are pushed out to the max level and every object is always rendered at full detail, no matter how far away it is. Unless you have a super-beefy PC this option isn't really practical and is mostly meant for future-proofing the game. In terms of performance, the remaster is just better than the original game. Just the fact that it partially takes advantage of multiple cores and threads is huge, and for anyone with an RTX card, DLSS is also an option, so you get much better performance at very near to native image quality, and sometimes even better. All-in-all, there's a lot that's been improved in this remastered version but there's also a lot that's disappointing. This means that there's no real ideal version of Crysis. If you go with the original you miss out on the improved performance, AA, and lighting. If you choose the Remaster you lose out on the arguably better artistic design in many areas and missing or worse-looking effects. Because of this I can't really give a recommendation on which is better. I played the Remaster first and had a great time but after also playing the original for a bit some of the features that version has are sorely missed in the Remaster. I'd say if you want the extra performance and ease of use play this version, but if you have a really beefy CPU and don't mind some framerate dips then go for the 2007 original.

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember the first time I played Crysis Remastered, and it was like stepping back into a game that defined a generation. The moment I entered the lush, tropical island filled with breathtaking visuals, I was immediately struck by how stunning the graphics were. Every detail—from the leaves swaying in the wind to the sunlight shimmering on the water—made the world feel incredibly immersive.The gameplay is just as exhilarating as I remember. The freedom to approach each mission in multiple ways is what makes Crysis stand out. Whether I wanted to go in guns blazing or take a stealthy approach, the nanosuit gave me a thrilling range of abilities. I felt like a super-soldier, seamlessly blending speed, strength, and cloaking to outsmart my enemies.The storyline, with its mix of sci-fi elements and military action, pulls you in and keeps you engaged. I loved the way the game escalates, introducing new challenges and enemies that kept me on my toes. Each encounter felt intense, especially when the AI would adapt to my tactics, forcing me to think on my feet.The remaster also did an excellent job of updating the graphics without losing the essence of the original. The enhanced textures and improved lighting really brought the game into the modern era, making it look and feel fresh. I found myself stopping just to admire the scenery—something I never thought I’d do in a first-person shooter!However, I did encounter a few bugs along the way, which is expected with remasters. Some glitches occasionally disrupted the flow of gameplay, but they didn’t take away from the overall experience.In summary, Crysis Remastered is a fantastic trip down memory lane that still delivers an exhilarating experience. The stunning visuals, versatile gameplay, and engaging story make it a must-play for both newcomers and fans of the original. It’s a reminder of how groundbreaking Crysis was, and it still holds up remarkably well in today’s gaming landscape.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis is a fun, pretty game that ultimately doesn't deliver on the initial promise of its first levels. It's still worth playing, even if it's just to experience the entertaining nanosuit abilities and marvel at what was, and is, a very good-looking game.The first few levels are these big open environments that give you freedom in how you approach their objectives. But this is only true in the most literal sense; you can approach the objectives from any direction, because you aren't boxed into a linear path. But that's where that freedom ends; there aren't any options in terms of how you actually complete the tasks set for you, or any "immersive sim" style gameplay choices.After these early levels, the game becomes much more of a linear shooter. It's still entertaining, but it's probably not what you came for, or expected.Playing on the hardest mode, the game is mostly weirdly easy, with very generous health and shield recovery and plenty of ammo available. The nanosuit's ability to make you super strong, invisible, or really fast mean you can easily out manoeuvre enemies and any challenge really just comes from making sure you get the first shot on any enemy you encounter.The biggest disappointment I have with Crysis is that most of the weapons are boring to shoot. There's this great system where you can modify weapon attachments on the fly, but you never really get a truly exciting weapon, with the possible exception of the missile launcher (when is a missile launcher ever not fun?)This remaster is mostly fine, though there are some pretty severe audio balancing issues, and moments where sound effects or music aren't audible when they should be. Vehicles that are hundreds of metres away sound like they're right on top of you, weird stuff like that. This version of the game also uses a checkpoint system with no manual saving, which is a really poor substitute.It's a recommend with several caveats, but I did have a good time for the most part. Something about the suit announcing "Cloak. Engaged." triggers a dopamine release for me, so that alone was worth the price of admission!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying That Crysis is a very special game to me. No lie I've probably played this campaign about 25 times. Back in the day when I built my first computer with the phenom 9950 and a GTS 250 I was looking at benchmarks and I discovered this game. I got the demo and played it so many times. Then I got the game, and I loved every part of it: the human conflict, the aliens, the story, everything. Original Crysis wasn't the most optimized game out there and I saw a cry engine showcase with a part that looks just like the island from the first mission of the game then I heard a remaster was inbound, so I was expecting the quality from that showcase to be the entire game and boy was I wrong.I'll start at the beginning. Crytek sold their souls to the devil and released Crysis remastered on the piece of ♥♥♥♥ epic game store as an exclusive for an entire year. I know they are starving for money, but this still stings. Anyways about a year later I got the entire trilogy for 70% off and today, I finally got around to playing it.Some minor Spoilers I guess…..And man, this game has issues. From visual minor to severe visual glitches that never existed in the first game to mechanics changes such as in that boss fight against that one guy in the nanosuit when you hit him, he has an EMP blast that completely stuns you and you can't do anything when you're stunned, that was not in the original game nor a feature of the nanosuit. That part made me mad as hell lol. That was a big change instead of a 1 vs 1 duel to the death everything is slowed down massively because you can no longer attack him immediately you have to run around and hunt for a weapon and then attack him while the doctor keeps yelling stop him the whole time which she says a lot due to how drawn out this fight is now and he seems to be made of titanium because he's a super bullet sponge now even just in strength mode.Other changes include at the end when the big Ceph Walker thing grabs you can no longer face it to attack it to go free you're just kind of screwed if you get thrown too far and you die.Also, when you're on the vehicle turret even if you turn off hold mouse to aim down sights you still must hold mouse to aim down the side of the turret it's quite stupid.Regarding all these mechanical changes: a remaster is supposed to preserve everything, just improve visuals and optimizations and not reinvent the wheel by changing gameplay mechanics.One surprising thing is this game preserved the VTOL mission which honestly, I was not expecting because that was cut from the original game that this is based off which is the Crysis version released for the PS3 and Xbox 360 so in short, we're basically playing a port of a PS3 and Xbox 360 game with some extra additional things bolted on.This remaster was probably the most important remaster to me, and they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up which is well known at this point. The only thing honestly that was improved was the 8K textures they used for the game, but you can fix that by playing the original with just a HD texture pack and done. Also, I was able to play the game from start to finish without a single crash so that's also a positive because their original game if you play about three missions straight, you're going to crash it's weird. There are all kinds of other examples of visual downgrades but a few I can think of is 1) at the starting of the first mission prophets face in the first mission intro had a lot more detail in the original. in the “Remake/Remaster” all the detail his face is just flat and 2) per object motion blur being completely removed that's something else you can see at the intro to the first level. This reviews all over the place, but I had to write what I'm feeling right after I finished it. I'm going to uninstall this crap and stick with the original which is far better. They shoehorned in cry engine 3 or whatever version they're using into this game, and it shows. This port/half assed remaster is trash I'm very disappointed. This is also much harder to run, and I don't see much visually to warrant that. The difference between Ray tracing on and off is next to none.TLDR:  Sadly, I cannot recommend this at all. What I can recommend is that you go either on EA Origin or GOG and get the original Crysis and Crysis warhead they are both amazing open ended sandbox games.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it, tried it and refunded it.It looks better  but plays worse. My recommendation is to simply play the originial instead. You get better gameplay for less money and on maxed settings it's still pretty solid visually.Starting with the positives: - The game now looks like how I remember it. Visually it's been brought to the 2020s and my nostalgia is happy about that.Sadly thats it. End of the positives. (comparing to the orignal of course, not making a review about Crysis as a game. Love this game)The negatives:- The mouse sensitivity is insane. Even on the absolute lowest setting its still twice as high as what I play normally, and I know a lot of FPS gamers who play significantly lower sense than me. I was struggling more with controling my character than I was with the actual enemies. - Which brings up the second point: the AI is terrible. Seemingly completely unchanged from the original, but in the mean time us gamers have all gotten used to for more responsive and interesting enemies.- Movement feels sluggish and unresponsive. Its like moving through syrup. I don't recall the original feeling like it was constanly holding me back. Even with speed mode enabled I don't feel like a fast and deadly super soldier, instead I feel I'm obese and cannot run properly.- Various performance issues. Poor optimisation on some features, frame drops and the likes. I didn't play long enough to really give detailed feedback here.- A big one. Audio. WHY, just why, do they put all this effort into visual improvements but apparently haven't put a single minute of effort into actual audio improvements. These are the same gunshot sounds, impact sounds and explosions from 15 years ago and many of them sounded unimersive and unrealistic even then. Even the most beautiful environment won't feel immersive if it sounds 20 years dated.- Not so important for me personally but still relevant: the multiplayer content was cut out entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: Great example of an earlier FPS with open ended gameplay. Constant stealth feels like the wrong way to play. The real enjoyment comes from playing with the AI and some of the physics. This is also a perfect setup for the story of Prophet and the rest of Raptor Team.While I would recommend this to any fans of shooters, I should warn that we employ a stableboy named Caleb who struggled with this game. We hired him because he's slow and can't really work anywhere else. He thinks our cows are called dogs and also thinks our goats are called dogs. Actually, he believes most things are dogs. I saw him looking at the table salt at lunch one day and he asked, "Can you pass the dog?" Anyway, I recommended this game to him and he couldn't work for a week because he was convinced there were aliens in his clothes.

_childDocuments_.review: A different take for the original Nanosuit system. It's good fun. A little overpriced I feel, but I do recommend getting it on discount. Differences (aside from graphics, obv): 1. The biggest difference is there's no manual save, only checkpoints. I'm playing on delta and hardly noticed any difference, honestly, not a lot of difficulty increase. 2. Nanosuit. You CAN switch back to the original, but if you played the original, the new system offers some different experiences.     2.1: Your energy regens A LOT faster. This makes the "cloak - regen - cloak" loop a lot faster.     2.2: Sprinting in speed mode costs MUCH LESS energy.     2.3: Jumping in strength mode costs less energy.     2.4: Armor mode is completely useless. Not only does it bleeds energy, it costs pretty much the same amount of energy as the original when shot, which was the default mode in the original... So in total it tanks LESS shots cuz of the bleeding.     2.5: Your default mode is strength, meaning you don't get the passive protection like in the original, and might get one-shotted more often.     2.6: The new strength mode doesn't seem to suppress gun recoil. I really like that you activate modes with one button instead of the wheel. I just hope armor mode was still the default mode, unlike the garbage it is now. But oh well, it's still fun. Other than that, gameplay wise it's pretty much the same as the original, crouching around in cloak and shooting stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: BEST ON DECK: 6 - 7 hours battery, 60 FPS, No Setting Changes NeededA simple rescue mission goes haywire in the worst way possible in the remaster for the classic FPS game that defined the benchmark question: "Can it Run Crysis?". In Crysis Remastered, you are armed with your nanosuit and swap between super speed, strength, armor, and cloaking to tackle your enemies in a constantly changing environment. Using your suit and tools, you will need to tackle threats beyond this world and figure out just what the hell is going on.Crysis Remastered has gotten mixed ratings due to a couple reasons. These include bugs, some graphical downgrades from the original, and it being a port from the console releases. Unfortunately, this is the only way to play the original Crysis unless you owned the original before it was delisted from Steam. The good news is, it plays quite well!I started off at the medium settings and was pleasantly surprised how well it ran. For the most part, it could stick to 45 FPS without any caps, but the battery would drain a bit more than I would like during some high octane parts of gameplay like driving into an explosion, tons of enemies on screen shooting, and sprinting across the world. I decided for a recommended initial build to stick to 40 FPS with some settings lowered to "low" for stability purposes. I also lowered resolution to 1152x720 as this drastically helped during those intense moments.Crysis Remastered also supports simultaneous KB+M and Gamepad inputs at the same time, which means enabling gyro controls through Steam Input will work well! I have found setting the gyro behavior to mouse feels a bit better, but setting to joystick works too.For the full review, I will provide 2 other builds that will make improvements to battery and a higher framerate, but due to Crysis Remastered being a large game, I want to test more before making those recommendations. I didn't encounter any major bugs that were specifically due to the Steam Deck and overall I felt the game ran without a hitch. I did blow up many houses and tried to instigate a lot of physics movements, but it held strong. I have been pleasantly surprised so far how well it is running and feeling, especially coming from how hard it was to run the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I've said "Yes" to whether I would recommend it, this review should be taken as a criticism rather than praise towards the game. Let's start with some gameplay views: The nanosuit now functions a lot like the way it does in 2 and 3. Default is Strength mode and the suit regenerates energy only in this mode. Armor mode passively drains energy aside from taking hits. The good news is, this can all be reverted by heading to Options --> Game Settings --> check mark Classic Nanosuit. Suit shortcuts is also something you may want to look at, as enabling Classic Nanosuit mode makes you unable to use the toggle keys to quickly switch modes. A mixed bag, but my preference is using the Classic Nanosuit.As for the rest of the game. Quite a few graphics glitches are noticeable in many environments. A.I. behavior is not as refined as before and can end up behaving very strangely at times, or stuck in a spot especially if you reload a checkpoint near a patrol.One pain point for me is that the game does not play all the dialogues properly. Like the in the final part on the aircraft carrier and in the mines there are missing some dialogues. Technically they are there in the game but the game proceeds too quickly before they can play. Can be rectified somewhat with some xml edits but we shouldn't have had to.Biggest owie for me is during the final fight on the carrier deck against the mothership. Very often one of two things or both will occur: 1. Psycho and Helena don't disable the shields even if all hostiles have been cleared, and this can happen for either of the "arm" shields. 2. The boss will be stuck continuously using its freezing beam for several minutes non-stop leaving you on a constant loop of being frozen, unfrozen and refrozen even on the easiest difficulty. Eitherways you have no choice but to reload the checkpoint.So, if given a choice, I'd recommend you get the original Crysis from GOG which incorporates a fix for the executable.I will say this much for the game though: the looks have definitely been touched up and a lot of places and objects are certainly more detailed and more beautiful. VFX also improved. But yes, buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: All this game did was make me appreciate the original from 2007 more. For a remaster released in 2020+, this version is a little underwhelming. Textures, water effects, particle effects, depth of field -- sure, all of these things have improvements for the most part. But when you compare side by side, the improvements feel kind of minor, which only speaks to just how good the original already looked to begin with.To ensure I was getting the most out of this, I enabled the "Can It Run Crysis?" mode with the raytracing enabled, which cranks everything to the max. On my watercooled rig (5950x CPU + 3090 GPU + 64 GB RAM), in 1440p mode with VSync enabled, on a 144 Hz monitor -- framerates usually hovered in the 120 FPS range with some dips going under 100 during heavier scenes, and otherwise capping at 144 when not much was happening. It also pushed my coolant temps to 37C, which is the highest I've ever seen it go (for context, most games barely push it north of 30-31C. Harsher games might put it to 33C or even 35C).Still very playable, but it's strange to see a remastered version of Crysis that 1. still looks dated by today's standards with little improvement over the original, even with maxed settings, and 2. is way harder on my machine than several modern titles that look better and perform more efficiently.I enjoyed the game, but mainly the first half where stealth and infiltration were more viable strategies. Once things go all alien on you, I feel like the nanosuit starts to lose its edge and things devolve into braindead shooter territory. The whole game is over in 6-8 hours, even if you are going for all the achievements and playing on the hardest difficulty mode. Once it's over, there's not much in the way of replayability. There's no multiplayer mode in this version, so I'm not sure what more there is to do. I bought this game on sale for $4.49, mainly to get the achievements. Had I paid the full $29.99, I would have probably felt really dissatisfied with how little this remaster offers over the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Released in 2014, this review of Crysis Remastered takes into account the criteria and standards of that era.(̿▀̿ ̿Ĺ̯̿̿▀̿ ̿)̄ 👍TLDR: Crysis Remastered impresses with breathtaking visuals and retains the beloved game play mechanics of the original. However, the game is marred by occasional bugs and glitches, while the traversal system and final map could use further polishing. AI improvements are also desired. Despite its flaws, Crysis Remastered offers an immersive experience for fans seeking nostalgia.With all the said.. Still recommend.Pros:Breathtaking Visuals : Crysis Remastered stuns with its meticulously redesigned environments, impressive lighting effects, and attention to detail. The game takes full advantage of modern hardware capabilities, creating a visually immersive experience.Refined Game play Mechanics: The remastered edition retains the beloved core gameplay mechanics, such as the versatile Nanosuit and open-ended level design. Players have the freedom to approach combat in various ways, adding depth to the game play experience.Engaging Nostalgia: Crysis Remastered successfully captures the essence of the original game, offering a nostalgic journey that fans will appreciate. The updated visuals and refined controls breathe new life into the classic game play.Cons:Bugs/Glitches: Crysis Remastered is not without its share of bugs and glitches, as has been commented on by many players. While my play through was relatively smooth, I did encounter one level-breaking bug that forced me to restart the final level.Polishing Travel Mechanics: The traversal system in Crysis Remastered could benefit from further polishing. Walking across terrain feels less smooth than expected, with abrupt level changes that disrupt the fluidity of sprinting.Frustrating Final Map: The final map proves to be a source of frustration. Navigating through small hallways and doors is acceptable, but encountering issues with passing through NPCs or NPC bodies necessitates reloading checkpoints to progress.AI Improvements Needed: Although the AI has been enhanced, some players may find that it could have been further improved in terms of enemy behaviour and tactical decision-making.Conclusion:Despite its captivating visuals and enjoyable game play, Crysis Remastered falls short in a few areas. The presence of bugs and glitches, although not pervasive, can disrupt the overall experience. Additionally, improvements are needed in the game's travel mechanics to ensure smoother movement and eliminate abrupt level changes. Lastly, the frustrating aspects of the final map, particularly the issues with interacting with NPCs, can hamper immersion and progress.

_childDocuments_.review: As a tool to fry... I mean, I mean to test capabilities of your hardware Crysis Remastered is good, as good as it was the original back in its days. As a game though, Crysis Remastered sucks. Shortly after starting the game I began to encounter various bugs, such as enemy AI going nuts sometimes (they tend to drive on rocks while they are on vehicles, when they spot you after you unclock they start to move chaotically for some reason while shooting me with precision of a marksman), falling off the map (happened only once, but it was weird one cause i tired to lay down under stairs and seems those stairs pushed me out of map boundaries), enemies getting stuck inside the objects when you power throw them and so on. The other reason why Crysis sucks as a game is its implementation on Nanosuit - this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ energy bar feels much worse than stamina bar in soulslike games. This ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ energy bar just takes all the fun you could possibly have messing around switching modes and throws it out of the window. It gets even worse on max Delta difficulty where "Armor" mode of the suit is basically useless, enemies pierce through it in 3-4 shots. The only viable suit mode is Clock that drains the faster you move resulting in, you guessed it, constant actions of "clock, move a bit, unclock, regen energy, clock again and repeat until you get spotted and start they mayhem". Limited amount of guns makes the game even more boring. Once you get your hands on AK (the most customizable gun in the game) you basically set up for whole game untill the final fights with aliens where you switch to Gauss Rifle with some RPG and finish the game.Terrain looks good, water without any doubts looks AMAZING. But looks can't save boring, limited and clunky gameplay. Crysis 1 doesn't work properly as a shooter, it doesn't work as a proper open world game (Far Cry 1 with its jungles did it better) and it doesn't work as a storyteller type of games because it got basic story (which i hope evolves and goes deeper in Crysis 2 and 3). It is simply a tool to push your hardware to its limits if you are bored of launching Furmark stresstest.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a great nostalgia trip that I really enjoyed. It clocked in at about 9 hours for me to do a complete play through of the storyline. Open world is fun to screw around in, but guided missions are much better for story telling.The story itself was a pretty decent sci-fi, there is no forced romance or crappy plot written in. _childDocuments_.review: You can still buy the original Crysis by searching for , then selecting . You can also buy it from , if Crytek decide to pull it from Steam completely. If you're keen on the remaster's visual improvements there's a  that improves the original's visual fidelity beyond those of the remaster, giving it 4K textures, global illumination, screen-space ambient occlusion, real-time reflections, tessellation, volumetric clouds, and so on.As many of you know, Crysis Remastered is a PC port of a console port of the original Crysis. Destructibility has been scaled down. Physics are worse. Performance is worse. Quick saves have been removed. Difficulty is lower; enemies do less damage and hit less frequently. The most damning thing about the remaster is that the gameplay has been changed significantly from the original game. Certain suit modes have become tied to actions, such as speed with sprint and jump with strength. Furthermore, you suit mode can't be changed while in vehicles (I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved ghosting past enemies—they'd know I was there, but they wouldn't know  in the vehicle I was).The original Crysis was hard by design. By making  select suit modes on the fly, you had to think when planning out and enacting combat situations. The remaster takes away a lot of this and Crysis plays more like an action game rather than an immersive sim. I died a lot going through the same levels in the original Crysis, but those deaths made me consider the inadequacies of my play style. I breezed through the first thirty minutes of Crysis Remastered without a sweat. This is not necessarily a bad thing, because it  still enjoyable, and there's no fault in enjoying a breezy game. What's unforgivable, however, is that Crytek has tried to hide the original game as much as possible, rewriting the experience of Crysis to conform more with its successors, Crysis 2 and 3. As I said earlier, the first felt like an immersive sim, where you  had to discover new ways of playing the game through experimentation. Mapping suit functions to actions streamlines this process of experimentation, and I think it's an incredibly sad thing to do. The richness of the original game is lost.You can read more about my thoughts on the original Crysis , as well as ways to make it perform well on modern PCs.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of the Crysis series. I played all 3 originally on the Xbox 360, and with the remastered versions of the trilogy now released, I wanted to replay it to hopefully recapture some of that FPS nostalgia. I remember enjoying the original, with the 3rd one being the best, and I am happy to say that this game scratched my FPS campaign itch, even with all of it's flaws. The remaster is a decent upgrade in frame rate and graphics, but there's not much more than that. It does suffer from bad visuals and bugs at times, but I was able to get past them when they appeared. It does feel outdated, like you'll know immediately it's a game that plays like it was made in 2007, but as a fan of those kind of FPS games then and now - this one was worth another play-through, especially at a cheap price tag of $5-$10. It's a nice 8 hour campaign if you're tight on time. You aren't really shown where to go and can get lost at times, but I was able to find my way to progress without looking up a guide, which is a huge plus for me. In fact, you can even blow by some areas to advance quicker. It makes it less fun, but it's nice to hop in a vehicle to pass an enemy base to hit the checkpoint, but if you needed to stretch it out a bit more, there are some secondary missions to do while embarking on the main quest.The game reminds me a lot of Halo: Combat Evolved's campaign. Is it a bit outdated? For sure, yes. (original released in 2007 and I reviewed this in 2024). _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to break this game down into three parts. There will be spoilers ahead but this game has been out since the early 2000's so most people should know what the story is by this point. The Good:- This game functions as a perfectly fine FPS. It does exactly what it says on the tin. The integration of the nano suit makes combat with the game varied enough so that it doesn't feel like your typical Modern Warfare/Battlefield game play loop. - The environments and the design of the game from a visual stance is nice to see. The jungles feel very dense with different areas that can be used for tactical use such as hiding or cover when needed. The way that enemy strong points gave access to different approaches of combat was also refreshing. The visuals themselves, while I don't have a rig that can run the game at maximum settings, was very pretty and you could tell why this game pushed graphical boundaries to not only their limit but even made new ones. - The difficulties paired with enemy A.I. felt reasonable. I played the game at medium difficulty because if I wanted to play a difficult game, I would go play Dark Souls. This I wanted to be more of a fun and relaxing, unwinding experience. - Weapon variety is nice and there are certain combinations for almost every player type. If you want to go stealth or extremely aggressive or something in between there are plenty of options to choose from. The Bad:- The story and the characters are a mayonnaise sandwich. While the nano suit is a very nice addition to the game, the actual game play loop is uninspiring and lacks a lot of creative impact or direction. This game feels like it's selling points was the nano suit and how amazing the graphics could look if you had the insane hardware requirements needed in order to do so. - While the environment is nice to look at and game in, it does get repetitive after a while. I really wish there were more areas to use and plan your mode of attack through instead of just a enemy encampment or dense jungle. There are a few select areas that do change it up slightly, one being in the alien ship where you had to align yourself correctly while floating in zero gravity and enemies could come from any angle. but other than that, attention to include environmental combat and having a wider ecosystem to fight in would have been fantastic to see. - Maybe it was just my experience, but there were times I would pick up a weapon that had it's flashlight on or there was mention that I had the option to use different ammo types or an under-slung weapon system. It didn't matter what I pressed there was no way to use any of these options or turn the flashlight off. - The inclusion of the nano suit was nice, but a lot of the times I just opted to use one feature of the suit for a huge chunk of my play-through. The sprinting feature was the only other option I used. I think if the game had been designed around the suit and the features it included would have brought the game head and shoulders where it is now. The Ugly- This game is horrifically buggy. The A.I. would act up and not function properly. There were swathes of the game that I couldn't interact with anything or a prompt wouldn't appear and I would wonder around gormless until I had to look up what I was supposed to do next. Events that characters in the game would exclaim and point out never actually appeared on screen and I just had to use my imagination of what could or might have happened.  - There is no reason to use any of the features the nano suit provides instead of its invisibility feature. Pair that with any weapon with a sight and you can breeze through most if not all of the game in no time. Paired with the buggy A.I. and it makes the game play even less interesting. - I had to stop playing the game because the second part of the final boss fight I could not get through. Not because it was difficult, but because I was caught in an endless loop of the alien mother ship freezing me over and over, which you have to spend time breaking out of, while the smaller alien ships around it would endlessly hit me and I would just die with no way out of it. I tried every tactic I could think of and nothing worked. - There are plenty of times where whatever I was shooting at, the bullets would just phase through the target. This is especially frustrating during the final boss fight where you need to hit certain points on the mother ship and your bullets would just go right through it and cause absolutely no damage. - The story and the characters bore me to tears. You're not invested in anything that happens on the island because everything has the same impact and depth as rice paper. Enemy units start employing their own type of nano suits? No further investigation into that, it just gets brought up once and never mentioned again. You discover alien life and that the strange structures around the island belong to an advance alien race and the island is sheltering a huge alien ship? Your character barely comments on any of this. The game put all of it's eggs into the graphics and hoped you didn't pay attention to anything else. - I would not buy this game and because of the experience I had I will not be buying any of its future installments either.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis Remastered Review: A Masterpiece RebornGraphics: A Visual FeastCrysis Remastered is a visual marvel that redefines the limits of gaming graphics. Leveraging the power of modern hardware, this remaster breathes new life into the lush jungles and detailed environments of the original game. The enhanced textures, improved lighting, and ray tracing support create an immersive and breathtaking experience. Every leaf, shadow, and water ripple looks stunningly realistic, setting a new benchmark for graphical fidelity in the gaming industry.Gameplay: Classic Excellence RefinedAt its core, Crysis Remastered retains the groundbreaking gameplay that made the original a legend. The sandbox-style gameplay, which offers multiple approaches to combat and mission objectives, remains as engaging as ever. The Nanosuit, with its superhuman abilities, provides a unique layer of strategy and freedom. Whether you're cloaking to stealthily bypass enemies or using maximum strength to engage in explosive firefights, the gameplay is fluid and exhilarating.Performance: Smooth and OptimizedOne of the standout achievements of Crysis Remastered is its optimization. Unlike its predecessor, which was infamous for its demanding system requirements, this remaster runs smoothly on a wide range of hardware. The developers have done an impressive job ensuring that the game scales well, delivering a solid performance even on mid-tier systems. For those with high-end rigs, the game provides an unparalleled showcase of what their hardware can achieve.Sound and Music: Immersive Audio ExperienceThe audio in Crysis Remastered complements its visual splendor perfectly. The remastered sound effects are crisp and realistic, enhancing the immersion. The game’s soundtrack, a mix of tense, atmospheric music, and adrenaline-pumping combat tracks, adds depth to the overall experience. The voice acting remains top-notch, with well-delivered lines that add to the narrative's intensity.Story: Engaging and IntenseCrysis Remastered brings back the gripping story of the original, blending sci-fi elements with military action. The plot, centered around a mysterious alien threat on a tropical island, is engaging and well-paced. The narrative unfolds through well-crafted cutscenes and in-game dialogues, keeping players invested in the unfolding drama. The remaster also includes subtle improvements in character models and animations, making the story even more compelling.Additional Features: Modern EnhancementsCrysis Remastered isn't just a graphical overhaul; it also includes several quality-of-life improvements. The updated user interface is more intuitive, and the addition of modern control options makes the game more accessible to new players. The inclusion of new graphical settings and customization options allows players to tailor their experience to their preferences, whether they prioritize performance or visual fidelity.Conclusion: A Timeless Classic PerfectedCrysis Remastered is a triumph that pays homage to the original while elevating it to new heights. It combines cutting-edge visuals, refined gameplay, and a compelling story to deliver an unforgettable gaming experience. For both veterans of the original game and newcomers, Crysis Remastered offers an opportunity to experience a piece of gaming history, now more beautiful and accessible than ever. It's a must-play for any fan of first-person shooters and a testament to the enduring legacy of the Crysis franchise.Final Score: 9.5/10Crysis Remastered stands as a shining example of how to properly remaster a beloved classic. It's not just a game; it's an experience that every gamer should witness. Prepare to be amazed—Crysis is back, and it’s better than ever.

Controls feels out of whack, I think there was a weapon wheel but the key to pull it out was so inconvenient that I was using scroll to swap weapons and I know that you can change key bindings, but I refused because this is how authors wanted it to be played. Flying VTOL? You better be joking. Thank god there was only one point that required flying, because generally speaking the controls are so botched, I might as well fly with display off using floor rag as input device and achieve the same result. Right from get-go the game misleads you to thinking that you can play each mission quietly by adding suppressors to almost any weapon and hinting that there is alert meter. Better ignore that crap because enemies spots you from kilometers sometimes even without even looking at your direction while crawling inside bushes. They'll raise the alarm and you're cooked. You can wait for it to go down a bit, but that unnecessary extends the time spend playing it plus on other difficulty levels than easy you die easier than in Souls franchise. I finished the game under 8h [and spent like 1h afk] including completing all extra tasks, but some sections you just gotta sprint and forget about enemies. About sprinting, idk who's idea that was to stick sprinting, jumping and melee under "power" meter, but it's more than annoying and again extends playtime without adding much in return. There was mentioned at the beginning, that the map can be destroyed, but it's super limited to certain tree types and constructions, most of objects still remain indestructible, which I don't see the main reason why remaster couldn't bring those too. My tip for you: find sniper rifle, use it whenever you can because it's honestly one of the better weapons due to low recoil and huge damage. Plus you can take out enemies from longer range from which they can't hit you.

I guess that's the reason why they removed quicksaves, call it balance. The remaster looks great and I don't have any technical problems running it with most settings maxed out with my Radeon RX 580, Ryzen 5 2600 3.40 Ghz and 16 Gb RAM. Some people say they don't like the new terrain re-color or the new water looks, but I actually do.As for downsides, I've spotted some eye-catching ugly textures and models, 2007 style, which I think might have gotten into the remaster version straight from the original, with no work done over them whatsover. Overall, they aren't many and mostly start showing up in the second half of the game. But I feel like crytek gave up remastering the final levels, the latter the worse looking they are. As for the bugged AI that so many complain about, I've seen it a couple of times, can't say it was a game-breaking experience. In total, this is a nice version of Crysis to grab in 2021, regarding it's on steam and even cheaper than the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis was loved by PC fans and hated by those who only had one PC fan.Sometimes I still think "will it run Crysis?" when thinking about a pc, not realizing it was released over 15 years ago.Crysis 1 on Delta with Advanced A.I Mod and a graphic config used to be one of my favorite FPS experiences and I’ve played FPS games for 20 Years. And to this day it’s in my Top 5 FPS Games of all time. Its not perfect, like no game really is, but it did so much right and did not dumb down the whole game to be a multiplattform game, which sadly will never happen again.The first Crysis remaster is a bit spotty and deviates more towards “looking pretty” than it does “looking realistic” and removed things like manual saving. It's a mostly-better version of the original, but it's not a 1:1 comparison due to certain physics and shading features breaking in the Remaster, like vegetation reacting to explosives, or SVOGI drastically changing the Cutscenes in a decidedly worse way at times. Overall though? It's a smoother package, more widely accessible, and the RT is damn good.I would personally recommend this remaster. I think it's overall, especially with the fan patch, a solid experience that runs well, looks pretty nice, and has friendlier balancing and pacing, and who doesn’t love screwing with Koreans?The modern nanosuit controls are more intuitive to a lot of players, and the game's AI isn't as aim-bot-like anymore. And unless you're really familiar with Crysis, a number of the bugs won't be noticable.If you don't enjoy this Crysis 1 remaster though, don't let that dissuade you from trying Crysis 2. Crysis 1 is an interesting game, and well worth playing, but it's kind of a mess, and it's not uncommon for newcomers to be like, "It has interesting ideas, but I don't see what the fuss is about."7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Memes of poor optimization aside, the game does run fine in modern computers. The devs were going for "breakable objects" and were willing to sacrifice plenty in order to do it, among a few other decisions that made running this game during its release quite a bit of a hassle.Graphics look fine today. Not great, but fine. The game is surprisingly short. Even messing around a lot and taking your time, expect the campaign to be over before the 10 hour mark.I appreciate the game changes its thematic constantly and keeps you on your toes as to what to expect. It starts as a stealth jungle shooter, lightly morphs into attacking military bases into a more active one, quickly shifts tone into a vehicle driver in the middle of of a war with plenty to choose from, makes an unexpected twist into a sort of semi-horror game with space mechanics, switches again into airplanes, and then the final boss hits.Weapon selection is fair. Balance is... a mixed bag. On one side, your health regenerates, you have shields, and rechargable invisibility. On the other? For the first half of the game, your enemies can spot you from half a mile away and accurately hit you with a SMG from that distance, too. Not to say the game is hard, but you do need to abuse the hell out of your stealth suit. I don't know about others, but the enemy jungle camouflage is REALLY good. Sometimes, I can't spot them until my radar says I'm standing right above them.Story is actually pretty good. It's intriguing, well-paced, and well-told through the first person perspective without ever feeling exposition is being dumped on you or feeling forced. Characters are varied and likable, if a little cliche.Last boss is bugged - sometimes. How to find out? Ah, you'll love this. Sometimes, it's invulnerable and you can shoot it until you run out of all the ammo in the arena, after half an hour, and you have to keep shooting because, even if it's not bugged, it has a ridiculous amount of health. If it IS bugged, all you can do is restart the level. Not the checkpoint, the level. Yeah, really fun to find out the hard way. It was a well-known bug and it hasn't been repaired for the remaster.The game is cheap on sale, as if they know this is not that great of a start, but let's see where the franchise goes. Maybe it will get redeemed down the road. It's not a bad game, but the negatives outweigh the positives so far. As a stand-alone, don't think it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Crysis is utterly beautiful; be it in its original form or this 2020 remaster. The game offers genuine technological prowess in its gorgeous outdoor jungles and industrial indoor bases. It has some truly jaw-dropping vistas, and it serves as a perfect benchmark for those who bought a new, more powerful graphics card and/or processor.Also, as a game, it slaps; It's a pretty solid shooter built around non-linearity in a linear framework, courtesy of the Nanosuit, the game's main gimmick. Cloak gives you the advantage to begin a quiet assault, Armour gives you protection if you want to go in guns-a-blazin', Speed gives you a powerful sprint for hit and run attacks, and Strength allows you to jump further and throw farther, whilst giving you a powerful punch. Coupled with some [mostly] solid AI, the end result is some truly fun gunfights and engagements.However, it's not for me. The gameplay, despite doubling as a power fantasy, has an odd quirk where enemies take less damage from bullets... but neither do you. You take as much as you deliver, and because of this the game is far more tactical than other futuristic power fantasy games about taking control of the battlefield and emerging victorious I.E. Halo, F.E.A.R., and Doom. Don't get me wrong, it still holds up, but for me it's not my cuppa tea.So yes. I'd happily recommend it but players more familiar with an arcade-style of shooter should be aware of what they're getting into: This is a thinking man's game, and if your reflexes aren't up to snuff, you will be punished. Otherwise, if you have new hardware in your computer (or a new computer period), Crysis Remastered is basically a must.

(check out current Intel CPU performance 'jumps' last years and don't even start on dimnishing returns, they can do better but why should they?)Fastforward to 2024 and Crysis Remastered is not that much better looking, AI is dumber than it was, game has more bugs and overall it is a worse product - like almost all games in the past 5 years, making good business hurts the industry.If you're in for a quick nostalgia trip and want to see how much power can your GPU draw under max load this game is for You, otherwise skip.PS This one can not run on 3x3.2Ghz CPU paired with 512 DDR3 RAM shared with GPU peaking at 0,24 TFLOP like Crysis 1,2 and 3 did back on Xbox 360, RTX 4090 is over 400x faster...

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I played this for about 2 hours and couldn't understand why I wasn't having fun. Crysis 1 is a fantastic game, that is not in question. I was enchanted as a kid by the physics engine and the very small detailed interactions with things like palm trees, bushes, and foliage. But...- The suit is, by default, the Crysis 2/3 suit and for a game that's designed with the Crysis 1 suit in mind, this decision baffles me. There's a toggle to force it into the Crysis 1 suit but that should be the default IMHO as the game was designed for it.- The hotkeys for the suit do not work or at least don't change from the Crysis 2 hotkeys.- They removed manual saves and quick save/load. I lost about 5 minutes of gameplay because I had to get up and go to work. I was in a safe place with no enemies around (because I had dealt with them) and I didn't have enough time to push forward to the next checkpoint.- You can't skip splash animations. Yes it's a nitpick, but I don't need to be told who made the game every single time I boot it up. Yeah I get it, can I play now?- The game is three times the size of the original. And speaking as an inexperienced loser nerd, yeah the game's graphics are better so I understand high-resolution textures add on a gig or two. But the graphics aren't that much better to warrant the size of the remastered version.For all these problems, the fundamental game has been, to my knowledge, untouched. Go find the original. Buy it on GOG or something, find one of the fan patches that allows the game to run, and play the original.You'll save a couple bucks, the game will run better, it'll only take up a third of the drive space, and the game will be a better experience for it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played the game, or even heard directly of it, if you're a gamer,, chances are you know of it through the question pros tend to sometimes ask people about their gaming hardware, "Can it run Crisis?". If that question wasn't enough to hint at the graphics of Crisis, allow me to confirm that Crisis has some of the most demanding graphic needs that a game can have. That being said, the end result is nothing short of breathtaking. In this game, you'll play as Special Ops Raptor Team Member Jake "Nomad" Dunn as you're sent to the Lingshan Islands in the Philippines on a rescue op to extract Scientists from a military coup. But the further you make your way into the jungle of the island, it quickly becomes clear that there's a lot more going on this island than what meets the eyes. One might even ask if you'll be able to believe your eyes when you behold the secrets of Lingshan. Armed with the state of the art technology of your Nano suit and allied by American Marines, fight to protect the scientists and your team. Perhaps you might even survive to get to the bottom of the mysteries inherent in this first person shooter.

My only real complaint is that the last quarter of the game becomes just a alien shooting gallery and really loses what made the last 3/4's so good. Campaign is about 5-6 hours long and has replay value to go through again and experiment with the games mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I was fooled by misleading reviews for Crysis Remastered and Crysis 2 Remastered. TL;DR: Crysis Remastered is the best Crysis game (even better than the original) and Crysis 2 Remastered is the worst of all three remasters.Disclaimer: I am a PC player and I never play action games on consoles. For me its blasphemous to even think of playing games like Crysis on a console.Important Note: I have seen some reviews mention that they have changed the gameplay aspect of using the nanosuite. While this is true, for those of us who liked the original behaviour, they have provided an option in the gameplay menu to switch back to  the classic mode.Suggestion to players: Play on Hard difficulty (even if you are playing it for the first time).Longer version: Crysis Remastered genuinely feels like a remaster unlike Crysis 2 which even after remaster looks like trash. The visual upgrades in Crysis Remastered are evident and they are not just some subtle changes over the original. The game looks like those upcoming photorealistic UE5 games that we see in YouTube videos. And I am saying this based on the gameplay without ray tracing turned on. This reminds me of just one con this game has- on some AMD GPUs you cannot turn on the ray tracing. I surfed internet for some workarounds but none of them actually worked. Other than that this game is a masterpiece. When I say this, just know that this is coming from a long time fan of Metro and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series. One of the most difficult thing in video games is handling AI especially AI of human enemies/NPCs. Crysis put many modern games to shame in this department. BGM and SFX is spot on in this game. And the setting of tropical island perfectly handled. Plot is engaging and keeps you intrigued till the very end.Ratings:Graphics: 9/10Aesthetics: 10/10BGM: 10/10SFX/Sound effects: 7/10Story/Plot: 7/10Gameplay: 9/10Performance - No ray tracing (PC: i5 13600k + RX 6700xt): 10/10
