_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh one of my personal favorite game! Was pleasantly surprised that it was ported to the PC out of the blue. Monster Rancher and Digimon are my 2 fav franchises for the PS1 days, I still have them on all my devices to play with emulators today.Concept of the game is pretty simple, take care, train and raise your monster, compete in tournaments for cash and glory, go on expeditions when it comes up, send your monster to errantry to gain bonus stats, learn new skills and even encounter wild monsters of varying strengths.What makes the game unique is the ability to summon new monsters using CDs if you are playing with the PS1 version, this port changes that mechanic to search for songs online instead and uses the songs to generate the monsters. You could also combine 2 monsters into a new monster or even use the disk items in combination to set them to become a specific monster.There are also a number of improvements made to the port like far shorter loading times, better music quality (i think?), part-time job and I think they improved some of the sprites.All in all, I just love MR1, 2 and the card battle game. Very happy to see it ported officially to PC, hoping to see more ports and hopefully more improvements and addons to them in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Rancher 2 is an absolute classic, one that I've been playing regularly for 20 years, and this new port to PC with Monster Rancher 1&2 DX is solid overall. The bug fixes and small mechanical improvements present are very much welcome, though some of the minor technical details of the PC port are questionable (like the buttons intended for the mobile version being visible when they are not needed for controller users). For full details check out my video review for Niche Gamer (pre-release copy was provided by Koei Tecmo.)
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: These games are pure nostalgia for me, so my review may be biased. I played both these games for hours and hours as a kid, and remember battling my mom and my sister locally on my playstation. If you have played these in the past, definitely worth every penny. If you haven't I would suggest giving it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for a game that is equal to this to hit Steam for a solid decade. I absolutely love Monster Rancher and legit screamed when they announced we'd be getting the ports over here in the West.Without a doubt the best monster raising sim ever, it's so full of charm and super well-polished for having originally come out in 97. My only issue is that there's no way to control the volume inside the game itself, but that is such a minor nitpick because guys it's here and it's good and it's everything I've been hoping for these past ten years ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ <3

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the magical world of Monster Rancher! The beloved series makes its triumphant return with Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX, bringing together the wildly popular simulation games – Monster Rancher and Monster Rancher 2 – all in one amazing collection. Raise your own monsters and train them to compete against other eccentric creatures in combat and tournaments. With hundreds of different monster types, each with their own skills and abilities, every Rancher will be able to raise and train a monster that's a perfect fit for their personality and play style. Returning fans and newcomers alike can enjoy the timeless monster training and battling experience in Monster Rancher 1 & 2 DX!

name: Starfield
detailed_description: STARFIELD DIGITAL PREMIUM EDITION Premium Edition includes: Starfield Base Game Shattered Space Story Expansion (upon release) 1,000 Creation Credits Constellation Skin Pack: Equinox Laser Rifle, Spacesuit, Helmet and Boost Pack Access to Starfield Digital Artbook & Original Soundtrack Buzz About the Game Starfield is the first new universe in over 25 years from Bethesda Game Studios, the award-winning creators of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Fallout 4. In this next generation role-playing game set amongst the stars, create any character you want and explore with unparalleled freedom as you embark on an epic journey to answer humanity’s greatest mystery. In the year 2330, humanity has ventured beyond our solar system, settling new planets, and living as a spacefaring people. You will join Constellation – the last group of space explorers seeking rare artifacts throughout the galaxy – and navigate the vast expanse of space in Bethesda Game Studios’ biggest and most ambitious game. Tell Your story In Starfield the most important story is the one you tell with your character. Start your journey by customizing your appearance and deciding your Background and Traits. Will you be an experienced explorer, a charming diplomat, a stealthy cyber runner, or something else entirely? The choice is yours. Decide who you will be and what you will become. Explore Outer Space Venture through the stars and explore more than 1000 planets. Navigate bustling cities, explore dangerous bases, and traverse wild landscapes. Meet and recruit a memorable cast of characters, join in the adventures of various factions, and embark on quests across the Settled Systems. A new story or experience is always waiting to be discovered. Captain the Ship Of Your Dreams Pilot and command the ship of your dreams. Personalize the look of your ship, modify critical systems including weapons and shields, and assign crew members to provide unique bonuses. In deep space you will engage in high-stakes dogfights, encounter random missions, dock at star stations, and even board and commandeer enemy ships to add to your collection. Discover, Collect, Build Explore planets and discover the fauna, flora, and resources needed to craft everything from medicine and food to equipment and weapons. Build outposts and hire a crew to passively extract materials and establish cargo links to transfer resources between them. Invest these raw materials into research projects to unlock unique crafting recipes. Lock and Load Space can be a dangerous place. A refined combat system gives you the tools to deal with any situation. Whether you prefer long-range rifles, laser weapons, or demolitions, each weapon type can be modified to complement your playstyle. Zero G environments add a chaotic spectacle to combat, while boost packs give players freedom to maneuver like never before.

_childDocuments_.review: This would best be described as "Chinese Balder's Gate". It's a western style RPG created by Chinese Devs set in the warring states period. Despite having no childhood memories I'm having a blast, and it's killing me to give this a thumbs down.The problem is that to there are both graphical issues and performance issues that need to be solved. While you can find the solutions on the forums, it took me a full hour of tweaking to get it playable. Even now, there's alot of jank that is just frustrating enough to detract from the experience. Unless you are willing to put in the time to fix it and deal with minor continued tech problems...  it's not even worth a deep discount sale.Past that, the translation is pretty bad along with distractedly awful Voice Overs. That said, it's generally playable and you can generally tell where to go, what to do and what you need to know. There's just a few questions such as "Is Shoot Rate your accuracy for melee weapons?" or chuckles like "Are you sure you want to overlay your save file". From here, this it's all uphill. From here, I'd genuinely say that this is a fantastic game and if the first issues don't scare you away you have amazing game here.The plot is about a prince who was ordered to kill himself for crimes against his father. He decides to ignore the order until he has confronted his father only to find himself in the middle of a conspiracy to eliminate all the heirs to the throne. You travel the land trying to punish those responsible, evade the law and protect the innocent people caught in the middle.There are tons of quests to complete, many with multiple paths or at least results. You'll be able to recruit several heroes, collect unique equipment and treasures, and decide what kind of a ruler you want to become. This game also features a crafting system that would still be considered innovative today. The materials that you collect can have their level of quality and special bonuses that they offer. The items you craft are a direct result of the ingredients that you use. If you want to build a fire sword, collect ingredients that offer bonuses to FIRE and hopefully also are high enough quality for strong base stats. The crafting is more than a raw numbers game and leads to a really cool system that I haven't seen before.Combat falls somewhere directly between Diablo and Balder's Gate. It feels faster and less RNG than a traditional Tabletop RPG but still has just enough stats and skills to make you feel unique. Enemy actions tend to be more interesting than D&D also as wolves will howl to alert nearby allies or lunge at you to move out position and dodge your attacks. They revolve around a much more action game style than traditional RPG.This does lead to some frustrations as some enemies don't stay still long enough for your characters to hit them or enemies running away leading to long boring chases.  The ideas are fantastic and absolutely add to the game, but aren't perfect. Overall, I played this odd-looking game on a whim and I'm glad I did. Of all the western RPGs I'd played, I'd put this near the top in terms of raw enjoyment. But the hoops you have to jump through are enough trouble that 9/10 players won't enjoy the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to recommend this game generally, but it's a good nostalgia tour if you happened to get to play this game around the era it was released in. I want to say this game came with a random bundle pack my mom picked up somewhere not knowing what made for a good PC game, and as much as my modern tastes here have let me down, the game is better than you might guess. That said, modern tastes have spoiled me and the game mechanics are not great for the single player campaign at least. It's playable, and the historical fiction set in Fantasy china is cool, but like Kong Gang the muscleman, that concept does a disproportionate amount of the weight carrying. If I'm being honest, this game would probably play a lot better if it were a tactical turn based battle, like XCOM, since a lot of the clunkiness is just from clicking around and your party walking to an enemy then doing a few laps around them before doing anything useful. I find I often have to pause, select each character individually and queue up actions and then unpause and let things run for a few seconds. The astute among you will recognize this is turn based battle with extra steps - but your mileage my vary.The dialog options are full of cultural stuff that I think gets lost in translation, so you might struggle playing through the game without a walkthrough on a second screen to refer to when the morality checks don't make much sense to westerners, and to be honest I don't actually mind this. It would have been a disservice to localize it, and for better or worse, we're getting a better approximation of someone's interpretation of period specific Chinese culture.If you've played this game decades ago, grab it and play it until you can't be bothered to finish. If you're a big fan of ARPGs and don't mind fighting the UI and can get this on a decent sale, try it out. Otherwise, maybe if you're interested, watch a play through online somewhere and be like "oh wow, that was a neat little project that someone made over 20 years ago".

_childDocuments_.review: Works fine on Linux. I use startup options found on protondb, as they helped a bit with mouse cursor being inaccurate.gamescope -w 1920 -h 1080 -f -- %command%As for game itself, it's the same thing I played years ago on my winxp box, but sadly not the best version of it. As from what I could read up there is China only version that has the widescreen support patch and couple other fixes (I think you can buy it on steam for like $1 by searching 秦殇 steam on google).  As for the game itself, it's Diablo 2 with a twist that you can have multiple characters that will vanish on their demise, so you will play it safer for a while and grind up some "lower level" mobs to just be that bit stronger. Story is a okay, there are some twists and turns, but for the time it's a good one. Controls tend to be a bit clunky, like main character moving somehow way faster than everyone else, mobs glitching in a weird way, or PC's moving around and taking a ton of damage to just try and hit that one enemy. Ye it takes a patience and a guide to get some things in Story Mode, but I would rather take a friend and play MP so you can create your own character and not be forced to play the main character. If you like older diablo clones, it's a fine one, and if you are looking for another "asian based arpg" blade and sword is one I played as a kid and is fine too.

_childDocuments_.review: Prince Of Qin is an action role-playing game, which takes place around 2,200 years ago during the last 20 years of the Qin Dynasty. Players can play as Fu Su, the Crown Prince of Qin. According to history, the Prince committed suicide in obedience to an imperial decree that was forged by his younger brother Hu Hai, who went on to become the Second Emperor of Qin. In this game Prince Fu Su does not die, but strives to take revenge on his enemies and becomes the Emperor of Qin in accordance with his birthright. [Strategy First Inc.]

name: ASTLIBRA Revision
detailed_description: If you haven't purchased ASTLIBRA Revision yet ASTLIBRA Revision is a quite an unique game. We recommend you play the public demo first (it is just above the Add to Cart button) before deciding whether to purchase it. The demo provides full Prologue and Chapter One content, as well as a demostration of late-game battle systems. It takes 1-2 hours to complete. Have fun! About the Game Join our Discord Server Travel Through Unfamiliar WorldsExplore a vast, dangerous, yet beautiful world. Broken up through multiple chapters, join the protagonist and Karon, his talking bird companion, as they confront time and fate. Back to The Golden Age Of JRPGs, with Side-scrolling Action Slashing, Smashing, thrusting countless enemies while building up stamina for powerful Possession Skills, which are enough to melt away anything that blocks your way, including huge bosses that could take half, or even more of the screen. Fight aggressively while thinking strategically, always pick up the most trust worthy equipment, and select the best suited skills to deal with ever changing circumstances. Fight God-Like Boss Battles Battle ferocious bosses throughout the story, each with their own set of attacks and challenges. Upgrading abilities and acquiring new skills are vital to finishing each battle and progressing through the protagonist’s story. Multiple Ways to Build Your Character A warrior mastered ranged combat with bows and throwing knives? A mage smashing enemies with staffs and cast magic at the same time? Play it in your way. Gathering experience to level up, collecting force to grow up, forging and mastering equipment to open up more tactical options. Combat and Story, Why Choose When You Can Enjoy Both 14 years in development and more than 1 year for revision, award-winning indie developer KEIZO gave his all into this work. The plot keeps twisting as characters growing in an ever expanding world; Classic themes like time travel and tons of spoilers are all custom-made with the developer's own style. In ASTLIBRA, Story elements are often made into game mechanics, for example, your soul-mate Karon is not just a sidekick to talk with. Fruitful Endgame with Even More Challenges With 6 difficulty options, all kinds of players can enjoy the combat system at their own pace, but no one can finish all those contents casually - even after you 'beat' the game, the Postscript after Final Chapter will provide extra story, new adventure and fresh system, tapping the potential of skills, equipment, as well as your imagination.

_childDocuments_.review: Great action RPG!!!But level and (mostly) puzzle design is the most obnoxious and dubious that I have seen in years (every other aspect of this game is fantastic). Seriously, why do I need to use google a couple times at any chapter to progress the story...Most puzzles could be solved with attention to every detail and some trial and error. But it will take a lot of time and I want to play in action RPG, not in puzzle solver.If you like old school charm of "what the heck should I do next to progress" - go for it, you will get that feeling a lot for better or worse.Otherwise save your nerves and play something else.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: Just got all the achievements (minus DLC) and I can confidently say that this is one of the best games I've played in recent years. Got the game because of the reviews and it looked like a grindy satisfying side scroller. That gif in the description where you kill a bunch of enemies and they explode into gems and coins is very accurate.The gameplay is fun and the amount of grinding is perfect. Just enough to not become boring.What I was not expecting is for the story to be SO good. Couldn't stop playing until the very end primarily because of the story. This is definitely one of those game that I wish I could forget just to experience it again.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: A game made with passion.I can feel the love and polish the maker give to this game.Enjoyed the gameplay and the story, and now that I finished the game, I wish there would be more of it.Story: Is great, not an award-winning, but definitely one that will stay in my memories.Pacing and character development are perfectly executed. The plot twist are interesting.Funny and heartwarming moments in-between.Both adventures and emotions are delivered.The story kept me interested till the end.Gameplay: Combat is simple but engaging and deep at certain times. The hard and above difficulties are challenging. It is somewhat grindy, which might be a + or - for some.Some fetch quest, but not spammed to annoying level.Art: Reminds me of 90's design and mix of modern style. Which is good for the game. Sound: Soundtracks are well picked, it matches the game and delivers. Stage design: Stages are very simple, but enough to get the jobs done.GametimeL 40~70 hours, depends on difficulties and if the player aim for 100% clear or not.My nitpick:The revision story seems like something that suddenly pops out of nowhere.Equipment is power leveled, no point to revisit your old gear (until postscript).Progression and character growth are a bit out of line at certain points of the game.Not much replay value (After full completion), unless one wants to enjoy the story again, or challenge higher difficulties.TLDR,It got the story, the gameplay, the soundtracks, and the gameplay time.Worth every $.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a newly-huge fan of metroidvania games, and came here from recommendations based on Bloodstained: Symphony Of The Night and Timespinner. Was playing Afterimage, tried this one out on a whim, and stopped Afterimage completely to do this instead.It's a beautiful game, way too fun. Have close to 100%'d it at eighty-one hours, at least as close as I'm willing to get. The conclusion of the game and its final chapter were so satisfying that it'd feel weird to fire it back up just to check some boxes. Aside from some uncomfortably-outdated tongue-in-cheek perversion, I found the story and its characters genuinely charming and engaging. Twist after twist, especially late-game, with what felt to me like few plot holes. Fun game mechanics, responsive controls, satisfying empowerment and a decent amount of customization. Actually laughed out loud a few times, even with a culture barrier.If you like metroidvanias at all, I think you'll love this game, and the demo's a great way to find out. In the demo, there's a showcase version that lets you try out some of the early-game gameplay, and you can start a new game which transfers over seamlessly if (when) you purchase the full thing.

_childDocuments_.review: MASTERPIECE!! This game keeps on giving. I would recommend that you play it on impossible difficulty if you like soulslike games, it works very well. (It can be grindy at the start on impossible difficulty but it gets hella good and it is a decent challenge.) The backgrounds are AWESOME. Music is good. There is a good of variety of ways to fight and there is no copypasta monsters. Every zone comes with brand new mobs. It plays a bit like a metroidvania/Megaman X. Literally one of the best games I've played in a while. Anyways, if you're thinking about it, go for it!!Edit: I forgot about the story, the story is well made and is about time travelling. Main characters are all interesting and have good personalities. TLDR: Press buttons, unreal fun happens. 11/10 GOTY not even kidding.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie games out there.  Fun and satisfying ARPG gameplay, great plot, well paced progression systems.  Despite dozens of hours of gameplay, you keep getting new abilities, and it never feels like you plateau.The translation is decent, but could be better, and there are random horny sections that I think are meant to be comic relief but just end up jarring, but these are minor criticisms.  Overall highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra Revision is a masterful blend of innovation, narrative depth, and breathtaking visuals, but Astlibra Revision is more than just a pretty face; it's a game with substance. The storyline is engaging and thought-provoking, weaving together elements of science fiction, philosophy, and existentialism into a tapestry of epic proportions. As you delve deeper into the narrative, you find yourself pondering the nature of existence and the mysteries of the universe, all while embarking on an unforgettable adventure.

There is a lot of it and Its just not for me.  You feel right away that its filler.  I don't want to have to keep clearing the same places over and over on the whim of a pet dog.(seriously).  Clear an area to reach the end just to have a "sorry.  Come back later when you have Item A and I will let you pass."  It's just too late 80's ,early 90's level design to me.  Reminds me of Zelda 2.  6/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun; I think it took me around 70 hours to almost 100% it, and for only $25, that's a lot of value.  The graphics and music are very nice, and the gameplay is pretty smooth with a controller.  It also has a lot of quality of life improvements over the typical Action RPG formula, such as being able to easily redistribute all your level-up points to try out different build focuses.  Story-wise, I found the plot interesting throughout, but there are a few instances where I think the English translation might have struggled to convey some points clearly.  All in all, though, it kept me wanting to see what direction things would go next, and typically defied my predictions in a satisfying way.So basically, go ahead and buy it, thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really glad that this game appeared in my feed. For the price and the fact that it had one main developer is incredible. One of the reviews I read that really caused me to check this game out said, "Don't let the graphics, game play footage, or demo throw you off. Play the game and you will love it." So I did. The trailers and footage didn't really grab my attention, but I'm glad I dove in.The music Keizo chose is perfect for each setting. I never got tired of listening to the tracks as I played through the stages. The sound effects are also very nice. Except that the penguin has the same FX as a laser. :-pThe graphics polished for this 2D side scroller. Each character, monster, and environment are very detailed. Not to mention the amount of equipment! I was initially overwhelmed by the amount of stuff, but the progression is quite nice and made grinding tolerable/enjoyable.The game play and mechanics were great. It felt so great beating the crap out of everything once I got the hang of everything. Customizing the protagonist to be a non-stop demon killing machine was very satisfying.This game is a great hybrid of retro style and modern mechanics. The controls are responsive (turn off Shield Charge), the customization is fun, and the story is even deep and thought out.Give Astlibra a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing RPG platformer that I can't recommend enough. It's a sidescrolling 2D RPG (Think Metroidvania with less focus on exploration) with a very cool skill and combat system. Using your partner to use "possession skills" you can summon or transform into various spirits of different elements using a very intuitive casting system (almost like fighting game inputs rather than menu navigation), in addition to your weapons, armors, and shields teaching you passive skills (similar to Final Fantasy IX) and a MASSIVE skill tree to increase your stats and learn new spells. It's also quite long, often with a "just when you think you're done, there's a new arc of the story" factor that feels great. Playing on Hard is a good balance of difficulty, and it's not particularly grindy. With optional bosses, lots of completionist achievements, and postgame methods of improving your character and gear, you'll be fully occupied all the way to the end.The story is actually pretty good too. A lot of twists, turns, drama, and comic relief, none of which overstays its welcome. There is some time travel in the plot so as you can expect things get pretty crazy, but it's never convoluted or hard to follow. The only cons I can really give are bugs so minor as to be negligible (a certain achievement not unlocking until a complete game restart for instance) some translational errors (to instead of too) and in my opinion some of the terrain construction looks a bit odd with how tiles match up. None of this is so obvious or egregious as to be distracting from the overall quality but I would be remiss in not mentioning it. Despite these cons, I can only recommend it. An absolutely masterful RPG and an independent one no less. Not perfect, but just about as close as you can get.

_childDocuments_.review: I am the type of person that normally does not write a review of the game. But after 67 hours and reaching the true end, All I have to say is, wow, what a journey. Not once have I felt bored throughout the playtime of this game.In the interest of not spoiling the game, I will not be discussing any story elements. To put it in vague terms, the story is constantly able to keep me on the edge and give me surprises. There are a few other comments that mentions some occasional juvenile humor that really troubles them. However, it hardly bothers me and gave me a few good chuckles on occasion. But I will mention it just in case you are sensitive regarding this type of humor. The combat of this game is also great! I never knew that having multi hit per weapon attack will feel SO GOOD. This is something that more 2D side-scrolling action combat game needs to take note. The music is freeware music that is available on the internet. But not only does it not diminish the experience, it just highlights that the freeware Japanese music creation community are masters of their craft. Every important moment is accentuated so well by the music, and quite frankly, I prefer this style of music of the vast 99% of AAA game that I have played. Many of those musics are now on my regular playlist.Thank you Keizo, for spending 15 years giving us this amazing experience. And thank you to all the others who help make the Revision version possible. I will now pledge my thumbs up to the sea of positive reviews. Astlibra Revision is now one of my favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra was an absolutely amazing game, and I loved every second of time I played through. Initially I was a little hesitant to start the game, but I regret not starting sooner. The story was amazingly well written and thought out, and even though it can feel confusing due to the many twists in it. There were also a ton of moments that had me giggling like crazy as well.  I found that overall there were very few plot holes or things left out. The characters were all extremely well written and none of the dialogue felt forced or artificial. The artwork was gorgeous beyond belief in my eyes and I always made sure to stop and appreciate the scenery. Even though the game play loop was simple and basic spam attack I always had fun just plowing through mobs, especially in the end game where you can make yourself infinitely more powerful. The music was spot on and Astlibra had many straight bangers. My favorite part was definitely the weapons mastery system because It forces you to use and learn the different weapon types. Enemy designs were also stellar and I love the way they all look. Even though some achievements got extremely grindy it did not take too much time to achieve everything after I finished the end game. Astlibra immediately became one of my most favorite games of all time and I fully support buying this game at full price. Honestly I think this game even at full price is cheap for how amazing it is.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

With all my playtime, i haven't managed to 100% the game, nor do i want to, but that's entirely fine for me, i had an extremely enjoyable time playing this and would recommend to anyone they at least try the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: Only nine hours in, and boy does this game scratch an itch. I like grinding, finding rare items, combat doesn't seem super complex and deep yet, but it is getting there. I've read that the game keeps adding layers and choices as it goes, and since I am only in the 3rd chapter of the game, I am guessing it's gonna get more in depth as I go. Plenty of customization options, the game looks gorgeous, altho some enemies animations can look a little wonky. I have felt rewarded for my experimentation, and I look forward to continuing to play the game.The story is a little trite, anime inspired, and the dialogue is classis JRPG, full of ellipses and melodrama. I don't mind it, altho so far this isn't gonna blow me away with the story. The gameplay and depth of customization so far have. I don't know if this game qualifies as a metroidvania, but I wish there were more metroidvanias like this, leveling and combat wise. The map so far isn't like a metroidvania, but some of it would fit right in.Edit: Story got better. Still kinda cliche JRPG stuff, but I loved it. I believe I am in the post-game/endgame stuff, and it's amazing. Easily worth the pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: This game captivated be for the better part of a whole week. Playing it alternately on my PC and Steam Deck throughout the whole week on Hard difficulty it took about 60 hours to 100% the game, without really being stuck anywhere.It's not perfect, far from it. But it was so entertaining and fun to play, I just have to recommend it.Game ran absolutely flawlessly on Deck and hardly drained the Battery.Only flaw in that regard is, that as of now the Deck automatically sets the resolution to 1280x720 and saves the resolution for when it is next started on PC, and to change it on PC the game has to be opened, resolution changed and restarted again. Little tedious.The Story was the biggest surprise. No matter how you guess the Story continues, the game throws a curveball and something completely unexpected happens. And that exact scenario happened like 15 times; just when I thought I knew what would happen the game did a sharp turn and shattered my guesses.The Combat is simple, but very fun nonetheless. You mash a lot, try to jump and dash around to avoid being hit while occasionally using items. Simple stuff, but executed very well.There are a couple flaws I want to point out though.First of all, as many said before, translations are a little weird at times. It's not unintelligible, but it's just... off at times. You will notice the weirdness here and there in the translations, but that won't stop you from understanding the Story. If you don't understand the Story, that's just because the Story is absolutely convoluted and insane (but still great), not because of any errors in translation.Also, the game feels a little stretched with a lot enemies being recycled throughout the end (last chapter).But that's it already, there isn't much else for me to negatively point out.I had a ton of fun, more fun than I had with some Triple-A Games.It certainly could profit from some improvements to the UI and its navigation as well as improved translations, but it's perfectly fun as is. If you enjoy some mild grinding and 2D Rpgs, this is probably gonna bring you some fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite an interesting game.  Don't expect cutting edge controls or platforming.  However, it has a great story (including a lot of post-game content which extends the original story significantly).  It has a ton of RPG like elements and in many ways a "classic" RPG feel.  It's not exactly a metroidvania, though you DO get new abilities and DO backtrack to certain areas, but not in the same way as you would with a metroidvania, so don't expect the same type of experience.The combat is pretty fun, but not overly complicated either.  There are a plethora of progression systems to upgrade your character.Ultimately, it comes down to the story though.  Any time I play a game or watch a movie, I'm trying to piece together what's going to happen in advance so I can predict all the twists.  I thought I had this game all figured out from the beginning.  Boy, was I wrong!  There are so many crazy twists and turns that keeps the game fresh, and in the end, the story actually made sense, despite being a such a twisting journey along the way.  It's funny, fresh, and has a ton of ups and downs.As long as you're not expecting cutting edge, AAA features or a typical metroidvania experience, and you like RPGs and an old-school feel, then this game is a good fit for you.  I'm definitely glad I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game hampered by some odd platforming and obscure puzzles. I know this was a huge labor of love for the developer and it's a very impressive piece of work. I think when I saw all the reviews were overwhelmingly positive I was expecting a masterpiece, however the game would be about a 7ish out of 10 for me personally. I'm sure it's a 10/10 for many people, which is great for them and I'm glad they enjoyed it. I just wanted to add another perspective that will help evaluate whether to spend the money on it or not.Personally I don't think this game is like Castlevania SotN or Bloodstained, more of a linear RPG with similar combat. ====Amazingly beautiful character and sprite artwork (REALLY really nice)Tons of content and optional bosses that can be tricky to beatKaron and Gau have amusing personalitiesIncredibly wide weapon, armor, and accessory options that all look fantasticLots of ability to modify your character build and min/max Earning special attributes from the weapons is a fantastic idea and was well implementedSpectacular looking and very useful spells that are easy to use on the flyThe story premise is interesting and more introspective than mostYou can easily dodge the enemies if you don't feel like fighting themSave points are well spaced and restore lifeDifferent difficulty options make the game accessible to all skill levelsFinding the hidden targets and arrows is entertainingController support is excellentFun achievements to unlock in Steam====The largest issue by far is that It can be very difficult to know what is foreground and background. This complicates progression as it can be difficult to know what to do next... platform assets are not obvious, hidden entrances can only be found by throwing yourself at walls, it would be nice if the background was blurred, had less contrast, was darker, etc.  Music during fighting is frenetic rapid tempo electronica or synth rap that is irritating. This is my second least favorite part of the game. More approachable music would have been preferable. Tons of travelling back and forth solely for the sake of increasing game timeCut scenes with the dialog feel long because of the constant ellipsis and pauses. While I normally love puzzles, many in this game seem obtuse and will require you to consult the web. Dialog has tropey anime stuff baked in  I personally don't like the silent protagonist, but I realize it's an artistic choice. The decision to replay the intro after every chapter is strange, but at least can be skippedSome artwork is taken from photos and is sometimes a 3D view which clashes with the 2D sprites, and the bridges that are a black silhouette are odd. Getting the ingredients you need for crafting can require plenty of mindless grinding until end game when your luck is much higher.Ultimately at the end of the day I feel like the amount of content and effort easily justify the price, I find myself getting a little bored with the slow pacing, running back and forth over the same areas, grinding for drops, not being able to figure out what to do next, and rapid pressing the button to get through slow dialog scenes. I wasn't sure if I would finish the game but it gets better after Chapter 5 and is more enjoyable. My ideal version of this game would make the platforming surfaces more contrasting and obvious and make the background look like the background, add a couple more clues on what the character needs to do next, eliminate the fetch quests back and forth, allow the user to skip the dialog bubbles and pauses with a button press, and include some music that's not high tempo. If you have the patience to deal with the issues listed above, there is much fun and tons of content to be had.

It doesn't do anything in my opinion that deserves an overall negative review. The flaws of the game are present, tangible and valid, but don't do enough to ruin the game.All in all I will say it again, if you think it looks cool then pick it up. _childDocuments_.review: This game may not look the best but don't let that discourage you from trying it. I was skeptical when i first saw this game. Yet 30+ hours later I can say that Astlibra was worth every penny. I haven't finished the game yet but that's because there are things I want to accomplish. The game play was smooth and leveling up was very satisfying. I'm not usually one to get engrossed in the story of a game but I found myself actually reading the dialogue and trying my best to keep up with all the twists and turns. There isn't any voice acting but the writing does a great job portraying each character. As much as I love this game, there were a couple moments where I almost quit playing. A few of the puzzles can be pretty frustrating and one battle in particular almost made me break my steam deck (but that's what the internet is for). What made those puzzles frustrating was the amount of back tracking. But thank god this game is a 2D side scroller so it's more tedious than long. If you decide to get it I want to leave a some tips:- Don't sell ANY weapons, armor, or shields. If you need money just grind it out.- There are hidden items in each area. Some will be skills that really help in battle. - Spend some time in each area to grind out resources. There are some rare resources that will come in handy later.- Use your save files. The game gives a lot and some decisions will affect how the story goes. - Min/max stats help a lotEdit: I finished to main game. I love this game

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my top 10 favorite games of all time, perhaps even tipping the scales in favor of my absolute top 5.After finishing all of the Ys games, my soul felt hollow and begged for more ARPGs similar to Ys. That series holds a special place in my heart and I wanted to relive that magical experience once more. Sadly, no other developers out there are able to deliver that special Falcom touch. Years of searching, yet no avail.That was, until I happened to stumble upon Astlibra. At long last, someone besides Falcom was able to pull it off. Astlibra is basically 2D Ys with god-tier gameplay, god-tier soundtrack, and god-tier storytelling almost on the same level as the Trails series. This game manages to check nearly all of my favorite boxes for what I want to see in a perfect ARPG.Thank you KEIZO for helping me relive the Ys experience all over again, and then some! For those of you who are also in the same boat as I am and love Falcom games, please buy this game right now and play it! Even at full price, it's 100% worth it.Astlibra is an experience you will cherish and reminisce until the end of time.

_childDocuments_.review: "The fruit of 15 years of development and love."I'm not a big fan of 2D sidescrollers. While I appreciate the genre, for some reason, games like Hollow Knight or Dust tend to bore me after a few hours. The only other 2D game of this type that I enjoyed till the end was Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, a game that, till the end, I felt I really didn't want to end. Astlibra was the same for me.There is much I could say about the very interesting progression mechanics, the fun and challenging combat on higher difficulties, and the unique and interesting art style that fits the game perfectly. Above all, I'd like to compliment the story. While the twists and revelations of many stories across all media became predictable to me after many years, Astlebra kept me guessing until the end. I don't want to spoil anything, so I will keep it short and simple. The characters are great, the backstory is well developed and introduced at a great pace for the player, and the twists and turns are surprising but not in an unbearable way with the related elements of the story already introduced. There are also many side details that you can piece together from clues found around the world through exploration.It's not really a complaint; it doesn't bother me, but I know there are people who are bothered by some innuendos and sexualization. I wouldn't say there is a lot of it in the game, and for me, it was in no way a distraction from the story, but it is there. Some of it could be said to fit with the themes of the story, as gods and goddesses of old religions were heavily sexualized. (I think there could be a big debate about what sexual stuff is natural for us since we are beings born of desire, but well, I don't think review is the place for this.) Aside from that, I think it could do without, but it does help to develop the characters' relationship in some ways. Anyway, just be mindful of it if it's something that bothers you.Well? What are you waiting for? Go and experience this unique game!

Wake up now or I'll put my sweaty feet on your face!"), it really just feels out of place and weird. Also, playing off a lesbian relationship as goofy and non-serious in the face of demise left a bad taste in my mouth. _childDocuments_.review: ASTLIBRA ～生きた証～ Revision ReviewThe best and the weirdest thing about Astlibra is that it feels, looks, and sounds like an artifact from the past; like a forgotten PS1/PS2 game. And in some sense, it really is — being mostly made by a single person over 15 years. It is one of the comfiest games I've played, with difficulty tuned to be just right (I beat the game on Hard), the grind being just long enough not to become dull, the progression giving you new things to look up to and think about often enough to keep the combat from turning stale, and the story always throwing curveballs to keep you on your toes and prevent you from guessing what's going to happen next.In terms of gameplay, the closest comparisons I can draw are Dust: An Elysian Tail, and the Ys series. The former being a straightforward action platformer with a robust combat system. The linear structure and the fast-paced, action-oriented gameplay are rather refreshing in this age of endless roguelites and metroidvanias. The latter having a classic JRPG story about fighting against seemingly insurmountable odds to save your loved ones. After falling out of touch with modern JRPGs that either overload you with a dozen of proper nouns in the first hour and try to involve you in some political conflict; or simply being about a bunch of whiny school children (and often being very problematic about it) doing stupid things but still coming on top of incredibly incompetent adults this game's story is anime, but in a good way — in the same way as TTGL or DBZ is.Astlibra starts slow in every sense of the word. The game begins with a lengthy cutscene (the textbox even warns you that the intro is long and absent of action), slow and simple combat, and a bare minimum of RPG progression. But over the course of 60-80h, it really ramps up, only dropping the tempo a handful of times, but never entirely stopping until the very end of the 3rd ending. What initially began as a search for your childhood friend turns into a time-travel adventure involving gods of inner and outer realms, multiple intertwined storylines, and a sizeable cast of major and episodic characters. A relatively slow and simplistic attack-and-block combat turns into an air-juggling and spell-slinging visual feast.A basic STR/DEF/MAG RPG system expands multiple times, unlocking more and more ways to affect your character stats and abilities, including, but not limited to systems similar to NieR: Automata's Plug-in Chips, FF X Sphere Grid, and FF Tactics' Equipment abilities.PS: I almost forgot to mention an absolute banger of a soundtrack, consisting primarily of a Vocaloid-infused drum and bass EDM tracks straight from '00-'10, with an occasional brostep thrown into the mix. While it might not be everybody's cup of tea, it definitely works well for the action and the story that it frames and deserves to be called one of the most daring soundtrack choices in my recent memory.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are willing to put up typical Anime shenanigans (mildly lewd) its a great game with a lot of heart and soul poured into it from its mostly solo dev. I recommend playing it on at least Hard for a first play through to encourage using more of its systems, Hell if you really want a challenge. One complaint is if you miss a key item/ability you can only backtrack to previous chapters while in between chapters, so if you start the next one under powered it can be difficult. You also don't know you missed something important until you get a checklist treasure book so for a first playthrough you must be thorough. One key ability that is absolutely required: Energy Drain, from the Rare chest armor Nexagram in Chapter 4. The game makes so much more sense after acquiring it, healing you when you use possession skill i-frames for a portion of the damage. People who complain about difficulty are not using this ability. Many ability's are super niche and can make it seem unnecessary to collect them all, then you lose out on the occasional required ability.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not play enough of this game to say much, I appreciated it comes with a demo mode though, it allowed me to experiment with some systems of the game upfront.I found the combat system to be "weightless", as in everybody kinda flies around with lack of gravity and slow. I had a huge hammer but initially I used a sword and a shield, in both cases the weapon felt like having the same weight and speed.The magic system really didn't feel like magics, more like a "limit break" kind of attack.The sound effects, or the lack of good quality ones, takes away a lot from the gameplay, hits don't deliver. I didn't find a dash button, which contributed to the slowness.This game seems to be story based but I couldn't see anything that would appeal me story-wise given that the narrative medium is interrupted wall of texts. This would have worked 20 years ago, but not anymore.Overall, I can't recommend it, I was considering keeping it at $5, but at $20 I asked for a refund.There is an enormous depth between magic and equipment, but I didn't explore it further.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this right after I beat the main storyThis game is absolutely insane. The art is good, the combat feels fluid,  the art is great, and the story is really something to behold. I want whatever the dev was smoking when they made this plotline because it's fantastic but makes no sense if you try to describe it to someone. Just when you think you're finally going to get to the conclusion, it goes insane-o mode and really sucks you in (spent like 3 straight nights playing it trying to finish only to find out there's still more story).I think the endgame is where this stuff really shines. You feel as powerful as the game says you are at that point, and the big completionist style rewards are surprisingly achievable. Sure there's some tough spots at the end, but beating a boss is less about "git gud" and more playing around their patterns and knowing your toolkit. If something feels too hard, chances are there's some skill/item you've overlooked or haven't unlocked that'll put the boss to bed.The progression system is also really nice. You've got your classic level up and allocate stat points, but there's an expansive stat tree maze, and all of the weapons and armor you come across can gain XP and level up to give skills or an item and enhanced stats. There are very few points where you've maxed out everything you can, and at that point it's best to chokeslam whatever big bad is causing trouble and move onto the fresh new stuff.Probably the first time in years a game has dragged me this deep into its mechanics/story, and I loved the ride. Not for everyone, but if this seems up your alley get the demo and then get the game.

_childDocuments_.review: ++: Gameplay is so much fun! It's addictive and rewarding. The game pushes you to experiment with fighting styles, and as you constantly change your habits, dispatching enemies keeps feeling great. Levelling up your attributes, choosing gear is a mini-game of its own. Playing with a controller with rumble support provides great haptic feedback, it just feels good! The plot is also cool, with unexpected twists and turns, but there's an issue with it, more on it below.--: A lot of cringe-y sexual innuendos, and I mean, A LOT. Imagine every sex-related trope of Japanese games (female underwear, enormous breasts, awkward compliments from total strangers, sharing the bed with a friend of an opposite gender HINT HINT), and it's there. Almost every dialogue revolves around this or that. Who said we need to save the world? Forget it, we are going to enjoy watching a cute girl undressing because she misunderstood what was asked of her! No, seriously, it often seems the game was written by a horny teenager. The plot suffers from that greatly, it kills mood and involvement. But if you're only there for the combat, it should be ok.

_childDocuments_.review: HOW is this game "Overwhelmingly Positive"?I just played through the "DEMO". I mean, it's okay - but I cannot see how so many people recommend it.The combat is both slow and confusing; I'm not sure if it is my effects flashing around the screen or that of the enemy. Can't figure out if you can aim it or you have to somehow time it right and it isn't FUN enough to try to figure it out.In short, this game is kind of... underwhelming. _childDocuments_.review: Picked this up because the demo was a lot of fun and it seemed narratively interesting, but I was not prepared for just how invested I'd end up by the time the credits rolled. 75 hours and all achievements later and I can pretty confidently say that it's my game of the year by a significant margin.In the simplest terms, Astlibra is a side-scrolling action RPG with a focus on combat, exploration and light puzzling. Its simple visual style belies the care that went into every aspect of its design, with mechanics, game feel and scenario writing which are evocative of Falcom's work on what I'd consider to be the strongest entries in the Ys series (The Oath in Felghana, Origin). Astlibra's quality is all the more impressive given that the bulk of its production was handled by a solo developer over the course of 14 years. Every part of the game oozes the sheer charm and passion that went into its development, and I'm hard pressed to come up with any significant complaints at all.Don't read or look up anything about it prior to playing. Just jump straight into the demo and give it a shot. Progress carries over to the full game if you end up deciding to buy it. I promise you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very very very good. It definitely has some rough edges but the overall product is worth your time.The gameplay is complex and addicting with a huge variety and moddability in your toolset, allowing great player expression. There is a minimum amount of necessary grinding even in normal difficulty but because the gameplay itself is so damn fun it doesn't feel forced or annoying.The story itself does suffer from some plotholes and anime tropes that will probably rub some people the wrong way but it manages to stay charming enough for the most part and does its job of convincing you to disintegrate the villain of each chapter.I also personally found the contrast between the interactable environment and the photorealistic background a great choice that adds a lot to the game's charm artistically. _childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is kinda like if you took Symphony of the Night and made it into a JRPG about time travel instead of a metroidvania.The plot is absolutely BONKERS in the standard JRPG ways, and the characters are fun and likable and interesting. It drags a little towards the end, where you are so powerful nothing challenges you anymore but you still have like 8 hours of game left. I played on Hard and I would say that is a good balance of not too hard but mostly not trivial. The combat is fun if kinda simple, but it's just deep enough to be enjoyable throughout most of the game.This game feels like they squeezed every last drop of potential from it. Every character, every location, every idea is explored to the fullest extent with the resources available, which is admittedly not a bunch, but oh man Keizo does not let that stop him from creating the 40 hour epic he dreamed of. This game is the maximal exploration of what is possible in this particular genre fusion, and I felt compelled to collect and do as much as possible, and that is usually pretty rare for me nowadays, and says a lot about my enjoyment of the game.All in all if you are someone who likes JRPG stories and SotN/Bloodstained gameplay and don't mind some questionable/actually wrong translations occasionally I would easily recommend Astlibra for the full $25, even moreso if it ever goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty amazing side-scrolling RPG (especially considering small dev team) with reasonably complex combat and thoroughly complex plot. The fighting is similar to Dust: An Elysian Tale, or a Tales series game so far as attacks hitting multiple enemies multiple times per swing, with a millisecond pause per hit and pretty open movement.I will note that the game is clearly anime-inspired: obfuscated plot, teenagers killing gods, and immature male fantasy depictions of women (afaik, the artwork was censored from the original version). Thankfully, it never goes full stereotypical anime with squeaky voices, exaggerated expressions, or vocalizations for every single action or special ability.+Some legitimately impressive artwork+Every NPC has unique portrait and sprite+Every item has detailed inventory art+Equipped gear shows on your character+Plenty of equipment and build options+Pretty fluid combat once you unlock some abilities+Bosses can require some strategy and even bullet hell management+Re-spec nearly anywhere+Infinite inventory (Hint: Don't sell anything! You'll regret it later.)+Varied music of decent quality+All  music tracks playable from main menu+Frequent save points and almost 200 save slots+Multiple difficulties, and can switch during play+An unending amount of things to level up+Nearly every item you master provides a worthwhile bonus+Optional/hidden areas+Game warns you before high-difficulty areas and final bosses+Game notifies you when conditions for true ending met+Arena usually requires clever use of equipment and skills+Fast travel, including to old areas+Can't miss any content (despite what it sometimes seems)+Items and skills to help find missing collectibles+Can skip dialog and cutscenes+Mild puzzle elements, requiring some thought+Enemy abilities telegraphed by sight, sound or nameplates+English translation cleaned up in May of 2023+Can download old translation if you prefer Engrish nostalgia+Can re-bind controls, decent number of options+Perfectly stable for me+A number of unique mechanics+Generally likable characters, with some humor+Time travel taken casually. No headache-inducing cause-and-effect.+Game just doesn't end. Post game and another post-post game and another.+The final post-game adds a bunch of new mechanics+Story, twists, & lore being revealed through credits fadeout+Between 40-100 hours of play, depending on thoroughness and difficulty (took me 74 casual hours for nearly 100% normal)~Story can be confusing at times. Reveals may take tens of hours.~A few plot holes and unresolved minor items~Seriously, how did she provide those panties?~Couple of typos/misspellings and very minor bugs~Combat is largely a button mashing scrum on lower difficulties~Combat effects can obscure detailed bosses or enemy attacks~Some doors have enemies behind them that instantly hit you~Can immediately re-try failed bosses at cost of items you used~Grindy, but rewarding. Not too hard to get OP.~A couple of brief difficulty spikes, even on lower difficulties~Final dungeon can be a bit RNG if you're going for true ending~Doing arenas early can lightly spoil some content~You're going to need a guide to understand a few mechanics~Animations can be hit or miss~Minor swearing, sexual themes and all-but-nudity~Portrayal of women's art and personalities is a little immature-Chests, coins, and force can occasionally get stuck in walls-Some non-critical enemies can get stuck off screen-Final weapon is given too late in the game to be usefulPlayed on:i7-12700, RTX3060, 16GB DDR4-3200 @ 1920x1080Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|SNormal Difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Good music, extremely engaging and fun game-play, and an interesting story. So much playtime and such a bargain, I'm so glad I found this.However, : There are many translations that are misleading or wrong for skills and stats. Look things up if they seem wrong, or look them up anyway. As an example, a core stat (Adaptability) apparently increases resistance to abnormal status ailments - this is not mentioned anywhere; going by the description it only improves your attacks while underwater. Another example, an ability is described as "+10 against all status ailments, 1.5x damage taken". It was previously translated even worse, to make players believe they would deal more damage under certain circumstances. But it is still wrong, and is actually +100 against all status ailments which is a huge difference. These issues are not nearly enough for me to recommend against the game, just enough for me to warn people to look things up if they sound weird.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a clear recommend. The game is very long (60+ hours), and while I had a good time with it, I'd give it an overall rating of 7/10. Was it worth the time commitment for the content? I lean towards yes, but am on the edge.Pros- Decent plot that has good pacing with gradually escalating stakes from start to finish. - Solid music, solid art direction- The game could have ended at several points and been good enough, but the developer has a clear obsession w/ this game and would not let it end until he was finished. - Fun allusions to other doujin games and somewhat obscure Japanese franchises. If you're this deep into doujin games, you probably were hyped to see Shade in the music credits. Keizo gets it.Cons:- There is nothing truly new here. The game is high quality from start to finish, but there wasn't anything mind blowing. This is why the game is hard to recommend, it's requires such a commitment, and while it has several high points, there was nothing euphoric in here for me.- There's varying opinions on the story. For me personally, it was whatever, although I think the way it was presented was fantastic. I will not remember most of the characters names in a week or two.- Combat gets stale around the midpoint, full completion is a boring grind. Part of this was brought upon myself by playing on a high difficulty (see footnote)- All females in the game are overly sexualized to a degree that it distracts from the plot. Boss characters have massive breasts with hand crafted jiggle animations. I couldn't take these characters seriously.One note, I played the game on hell mode, and I absolutely do not recommend it. Enemies kill you so quickly on hell mode, compelling you to grind right before major story beats until you find breaking combos towards the second half. End game bosses have so much health that you're compelled to go for a full completion playthrough. I don't know how difficult hard mode is compared to hell mode, but I imagine that lower difficulties would have given me more flexibility to rush through the early game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be using a template and try to highlight separately from both the main game and the DLC.ASTLIBRA Revision is a side-scrolling game that revolves around a young man looking for his friend after his hometown was attacked by demons. The gameplay is simple yet complex, the RPG elements are very thought of, everything was superb.ASTLIBRA Revision (Gaiden: Cave of Phantom Mist) is a separate DLC with the same gameplay mechanics but with an added feature of roguelite elements, the story tells of a baker's daughter and takes place in parallel with the main game, so it's best to completely finish the main game first.Strongly Recommended - ✔✔☐ Very Difficult☐ Difficult☐ Moderate☐ Easy☑ Very EasyFor both the MG (Main game) and DLC, the controls are pretty much the same. I didn't do too many changes but the controls feels very fluid.☐ Poorly Balanced☐ Somewhat Balanced☐ Moderately Balanced☐ Well Balanced☑ Perfectly BalancedDifficulty in this game actually affects the mechanics of the game, where for the 2 hardest difficulties, the game won't pause when you are casting magic and using item from the quick slot. I'd say these changes are what makes the game veerryy smooth in terms of gameplay.I did a blind Hell (2nd hardest) difficulty playthrough for the MG, and Impossible (Hardest) for the DLC. The difficulty spikes are well balanced as long as you properly equip yourself. Increase in difficulty typically just raises the enemy's damage and health points, the AI itself doesn't seem to change. I rarely encounter a case of damage sponge bosses. The attack patterns of the enemies are beautifully telegraphed and designed, especially the bosses and they are enough to keep you on your toes but still mesmerized by the effects!☐ Not at all☐ Slightly☐ Moderately☐ Very☑ ExtremelyI got 100 hours in just a week with a 100% achievement. Need I say more?Jokes aside, I never feel bored even when grinding, everything feels very rewarding. The game also has SKIP feature so it doesn't make repeating story tedious after you die, or when you want to try another choice regarding the story.☐ Meaningless☐ Not Meaningful☐ Somewhat Meaningful☑ Quite Meaningful☐ Highly MeaningfulAfter a certain chapter, you will encounter some cases of Choices Matter that affects endings and how the rest of the chapter plays. So it's best to have multiple saves. The aftermath itself isn't too game-breaking accept for one, I'll let you figure that out yourself!☐ Very Unsatisfying☐ Unsatisfying☐ Neutral☐ Satisfying☑ Very SatisfyingGrinding feels very rewarding where each and every weapons, shield, armor you unlock have a Mastery gauge where once maxed will give you a reward. Exploring the map, finding out hidden treasures and bosses, grinding for materials, all of them will reward you and it doesn't feel like looking for every detail is useless. Post-game also has mechanics where you will be able to crank up early game gears and make it viable for end-game dungeons and FASHION.☐ Not Interesting☐ Slightly Interesting☐ Moderately Interesting☐ Very Interesting☑ Extremely InterestingOh boy.Main game story, as I said, revolves around a boy looking for his friend after his hometown was attacked by demons. Story was really captivating and beautiful, no cliches no niches, LOTS of plot twists and things that will leave your mouth hanging and wanting for more. The story involves eradicating demons and time traveling, with every side characters perfectly impacting the story. Keizo did a very amazing job for this.DLC story takes place at least after the 2nd chapter of the main game (I think?), with more plot twists. It's shorter than the main game but it has the perfect length for the DLC, the narration itself is still beautiful.☐ Not Immersive☐ Slightly Immersive☐ Moderately Immersive☐ Very Immersive☑ Completely ImmersiveThe world building is beautiful, the backdrop for most areas gave me a wide-eye as I am awed by the design. It may not use unreal engine and all that stuff but, man, even my girlfriend was captivated when she watched me play this game.☐ Not Appealing☐ Slightly Appealing☐ Moderately Appealing☐ Very Appealing☑ Extremely AppealingSometimes you'll feel familiar with the visuals. Some will make you feel nostalgic, stunned, and wondering... "Have I seen something like this before?"Well it's none other than  from VanillaWare! Beautiful character designs, character portraits, everything feels like it's from Odin's Sphere. The particle effects of magic, weapon swing animation, skills, they feel very impactful added with a really good SFX.☐ Very Unfriendly☐ Unfriendly☐ Neutral☑ Friendly☐ Very FriendlyPretty easy to navigate, inventory sorts by itself and cannot be sorted manually. Most of the time I feel like it should have been able to be manually sorted by quantity, type or weight.☐ Poorly Designed☐ Somewhat Designed☐ Moderately Designed☐ Well Designed☑ Excellently DesignedBattle mechanics wise, from normal attacks, skills, magic and item usage, you'll feel like everything will come together smoothly especially with Hell / Impossible difficulty where the game doesn't pause when you're doing magic or using item.RPG elements of this game are one of the best I have ever seen. You have stat points (or in this case it's called Magic Stones) that you can allocate to your desired stat. The MG will acquire 5 Magic Stones every level up, but DLC will require you to find or farm the Magic Stones since it's roguelite elements will reset you to level 1 everytime you quit the the dungeon. Some of the unique stats are AGI (this gives you combo bonuses and weight reduction of your weapon and shield, which in turn will give you more attack speed) Luck and Adaptability (ADA). now ADA is a unique stat where I most of the time...don't care. It will increase the time you can stay underwater and reduce movement speed obstruction debuffs from water and snow.Aside from the magic stones, you will have Force, a currency to use on skill trees that unlocks magic and stat boosts and a unique scale system where you put items on the scale, try to balance it and the more balanced it is, the better the stats given by the items.☐ Poor Content☐ Limited Content☐ Moderate Content☑ Extensive Content☐ Abundant ContentYou have main story, hidden dungeons and an arena. It's simple but it works wonders to boost my gameplay hours.☐ Very Dissatisfied☐ Dissatisfied☐ Neutral☐ Satisfied☑ Very Satisfied☐ No☑ YesBuy the game, it's OVERWHELMINGLY POSITIVE for a reason.

_childDocuments_.review: "Castlevania meets Chrono Trigger"That's an apt way of describing this game in a nutshell. Gameplay-wise, I feel it shares the most in common with Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow and Dawn of Sorrow. But even though I can compare it to those two, ASTLIBRA Revision manages to be it's own thing.That being said, go into this game anticipating a lengthy story -- it is an Action RPG, and it very much keeps true to the "RPG" aspect. Personally, I think the story is excellent even though I've yet to finish the game. It starts off a bit slow, but after a certain point everything just clicks, and before you know it you're flying through the game eager to see what happens next.But hey, you don't have to take my word for it: This game has a demo! You can experience the entire First Chapter for free, and your saved game(s) will be carried over into the full game. Try it out for yourself. It may only take 1~2 hours to get through if you're playing it casually, but if you decide to complete absolutely everything? Well, that took me ten hours.And all that effort gave me a running start into the rest of the game. It's worth the price tag, but you don't have to rely on my word on that. All in all, I absolutely recommend this game. It has been a 10/10 experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply one of the best games I've ever played. The narrative kept me on the edge of my seat constantly, while nailing the balance between emotional moments and comedic relief. As soon as you think you might have an idea what's happening in the story, you're thrown for a loop in the best way possible. The combat flows smoothly, and the various methods of stat upgrades and such are in-depth, yet easy to grasp. But perhaps what is most impressive of all is the music selections - despite, from what I understand, being all royalty-free tracks, they feel crafted for each moment and area. I cannot even put into words how incredible some parts were because of the music alone. Play Astlibra.

_childDocuments_.review: HOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOLY,I did not have high expectations for this game at all. I don't usually do "side-scrollers", but after reading the comments, I tried the demo. The demo was interesting/fun enough to get me to commit to buying the game and it absolutely was worth the $25 price tag.This game apparently took 14 years to finish and that adds to the charm of it. It ramps up the nostalgia to a 100 with the old fashioned menu, text dialogue sequences, etc.I just finished the game as of this review and I am very emotional and sad that it is over so here are reasons why this is probably one of the top 5 games I've ever played- Story was absolutely insane with an amazing cast of main characters - There's a post main game story that is EVEN MORE INSANE with new game mechanics that absolutely makes the game even more fun- Soundtrack is nothing but bangers- The game feels like, dare I say, an anime. Felt like I was playing a "show"- Combat is stupid fun once you really understand it- Art style really grew on me However:- There are sparse translations errors; nowhere near enough to be annoying, but it happens once in awhile- I'm so used to hand-holding to progress stories.. Astlibra makes you actually think think to progress the plot starting from the 1st chapter. It's very refreshing, it just can catch you off guard because you do have to think outside the box sometimes.- It is a little bit grindy to get the build/items you want, but Astlibra rewards you very well for grinding with 2 separate leveling systems and a weapon mastery systemok gonna go cry now

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant at first, especially at the opening video and the seemingly low end graphics of the game. However I downloaded the demo and played it to the end and had to immediately buy it. The gameplay more than makes up for the mediocre but passable graphics, as well as a killer soundtrack that you can play from the title screen with each track you 'unlock' as you play the game.PROS:- JRPG Story base and in depth character development (though it may take a few chapters for this to set in)- Metroidvania Goodness, hack and slash -esque combat with a diverse way to customize your character to handle any challenge the game puts forth.- Summons! Six different elements you can assign a summon to, and each category has a slew of different summons you can unlock and customize a loadout with- Massive and extensive skill web (Reminiscent of FF10 or Path of Exile, Salt & Sanctuary, etc.)- Equipment learning system: Mastering Weapons/Shields/Armor will grant you perk points or perk skills allowing you to customize yourself with unique and powerful passive abilities, like double jump, treasure finding, and the like- Item Crafting System: Large and extensive crafting recipe system to create items that will help in your progression through the game- Item Stat Gains: A system allowing you to set certain items in special slots that give permanent bonuses while equipped and can save multiple different sets allowing for different loadouts, such as farming or debuff resistant builds- Free Respec: At any time (at certain locations) you can alter your stats from your level ups, adjusting as necessary to the challenges presented in the game- Combat system that is in depth and grows as you learn more skills throughout the game, such as perfect guarding, parrying, shield bashing, etc.- Bosses, bosses FEEL like bosses, always an amazing boss battle music accompaniment and amazing artwork for the bosses you encounter, and use of mechanics to win later encounters. You can't just roll face across the keyboard to win depending on the difficulty you play at, but normal and above you can only get away with that for the first one or two 'intro' bosses.- Replayability! You always have the option and opportunity to return to locations you've been before even if it doesn't feel like it, so if you've missed something you can always come back, as there are rewards for full completion.- Length: The game is long, from start to finish and including the post game (yes there's actually a section the game itself refers to post game that is required to 'finish' the game) As of the time of writing I think I'm within the last two chapters and I've put 40 hours into it. So its well worth the money for a Metroidvania RPGCONS:- Story is very much in JRPG style, so with the pros that brings there are also cons, there are some cringe-y tropes that are associated with that that pop up here and there. If you can get past that, its not really that big of a con but some can take away from the seriousness presented in the story.- Puzzles, story progression does require some puzzles to be solved to advance, and while NPC placement allows to offer hints to push you in the right direction some puzzles will make you question your existence, and there's not a huge online support for guides or reference to this game other than youtube playthroughs (at the time of writing this review)- After a while the game encourages grinding like a typical JRPG would warrant, but in a metroidvania setting that's not difficult to do, but at the same time monotonous and sometimes tedious, not that grinding in any game is fun or fulfilling but it is a boring point of the game unless you mix things up and use it to try new builds and equipment loadouts or try to master equipment.- Arena Missions: There is an arena that poses 5 challenges per chapter of the game and offers almost necessary rewards to progress through the game and most have timed challenges or 'don't get hit' requirements that make them difficult and sometimes grueling. I personally don't like arena type challenges in games unless they are truly optional or the reward is just a really good item that isn't entirely necessary. Not in this case. Thus it is listed as a con for me, but I know some people actually like challenges such as these.Takeaway:If you like having full control over stat and character progression this game gives you that control, and even manipulation over it, as well as passives and active skills alongside actual equipment loadouts. And there's so much progression you don't get to feel like you're capped out or you're done, as there is always more. The game is always kind and gives you a heads up when you'll be going away from the 'hub' and be locked into an area until its completed so that way you can prepare accordingly and even after transitioning there will be shops available for continuing access to supplies so you're not left high and dry. Even with the cons and complaints I have with the game the Pros greatly exceed them, and I would list this in my top 5 metroidvania games.
