_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It's very apparent that the Dev was very passionate about this game.Story: 9/10I enjoyed the characters, can't say much about the plot without spoiling. It's not too long or too short. There's a couple of sidequests, but they don't really feel like sidequests, Idk if I should call them that. One of them is a guy giving you a reward for getting all the weapons,shields and armor in the game. 99% of the game is Linear main story stuff. There are no missables, the game has a system where you can go back to any location, sometimes the story will lock this functionality for a bit, but it unlocks right after that specific story segment anyway. You can go back to all previous areas in between main story chapters.Some part of the true/alternate ending is locked behind a little bit of grinding. This is the reason why it's not a 10/10 for me. It should be lower, but I enjoy the combat enough to not hate the grind enough to lower the score more.Gameplay: 9/10Combat feels nice and impactful, Items feel varied enough, weapons with the same type feel similar to play but they have different skills attached to them so I guess it's okay if you think of them as something to use until you master the skill. The spell variety is nice, and you can change their effects later in the game via item customization with boards. Overall it didn't get boring to play for the 60 hours I put into it.The scales mechanic is unique and interesting for me. You can use basically any non-equippable item to give you passive stat boost, the stat depends on the item, and it depends on how you balance the "weight" of the items on a scale.Soundtrack: 9/10Purely subjective, but I think some songs were pretty memorable enough. After A play session, I would randomly remember some of the songs in the game playing in my head.Some Negatives:It's a bit grindy, but not really required. I did end up unintentionally grinding for a while because I wanted to get some weapon skills so I can't really say how the game would be like if you did zero grinding. I can imagine the bosses might feel a bit bullet spongey if you have low stats or something. But Since I did grind some, I didn't personally experience this, on average I had high enough stats to not have any problems with bosses, I did use a lot of consumables though.I personally didn't mind the grind because I was having fun with the combat, but I can see people being put off by the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was almost exactly what I needed when I needed it--during a frustrating quarantine over the holidays. The gameplay scratches an itch like few games do, with a progression system that is multifaceted, meaningfully impacts your success, and feels nigh endless. Enemies hit hard, but you have good defensive options between your shield, Castlevania backstep, and i-frames on your summons. New abilities come from weapons and armor, which all require certain enemy drops. The game can absolutely be grindy, but I happen to be someone who enjoys a grind that feels rewarding! It also doesn't hurt that most of the area music is fantastic, and the soundtrack is varied in a way that not many games are willing to commit to.As for the story, there's a lot to praise! I think a lot of the appeal is in the storytelling, as the chapters like to play with your expectations. Most chapters are only at their halfway point when you'd traditionally expect them to end. It feels inspired by the tone of games like Nier, taking a mostly straightforward fantasy setting and storyline before throwing in a bunch of twists that cause you to reflect and recognize the horror of the situation. Things gradually unveil themselves as you go on, but not without a number of curveballs and emotional gut punches. While I think the structure and plotline are pretty strong, the characters leave a little more to be desired. In particular, Astlibra Revision has a serious issue with its treatment of female characters. Frankly, the oversexualization and abuse of women in this game would have been outdated 15 years ago when this game was first being written. There are plenty of mentions in the comments about chapter 4 (which is painful to play through at times), but parts like chapter 5's treatment of Shiro are just as bad. Its a distracting and obnoxious feature of a game that otherwise has a lot of merit. I think that Astlibra Revision is best enjoyed by those with nostalgia for action rpgs of the late 90s and early 2000s, who are willing to delve into a darker tone and look past some of the more dated parts of the game. I do like this game quite a bit, but my enjoyment is muddied by the fact that I can't wholeheartedly recommend it to friends who might otherwise be interested if not for the rampant misogyny.

_childDocuments_.review: Whew, well.  Like I always tell people. I rarely write reviews, and when I do its either for a game that deserves it meaning mostly its positive, or a short one which I will remove later being negative, like I did for RCG2 due to its release state.  Considering I been playing video games longer than most steam users have been alive, I pretty much seen it all.  Well thats enough intro  lets get down to it. Astlibra, a hidden gem of a game, coming out of nowhere.  Quite honestly in my opinion, could be a Indie nominee for the VGAs *I feel sorry for the VGA host, he almost, almost got to have one go without incident, just right there at the end, poor guy* And I say this due to how well created the game is, harking back to the old era of video games.  I see alot of primary influences in it, particularly the old Y's games, and a little bit of Drakken 2 Dragon View.  What influences you may ask?  Oh I can name quite a few, even seen references to them.  Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, Zelda, Chrono Trigger, heck even Metroid for a particular area.  The developers  who seemingly spent 15+ years creating this have obviously been playing video games for a long time, and are all what the Japanese term calls them "Your everyday Salaryman"  thus why it took them so long to create this.The basic plot of a very, very long story, which, heavily influenced by both Chrono Trigger, and a very, specific game for a twist over midway thru,  is that you are a Silent Protagonist orphan who as a boy was attacked by Demons invading your village and tried to run away with your childhood sweetheart.  You both got surrounded, and then you lost consciousness as you got attacked by a giant powerful demon, only to wake up in a cabin in the middle of absolute nowhere with a talking Raven.  You realize you are far, far from human civilization, so far that their are not even any demons around since they tend to stay near human settlements only for some reason.  You and the raven who seems to act as your surrogate father, tries to live life in this cabin, but your urge and desire to go back to your village and find the girl you have feelings for is too much, and you keep attempting to leave, only to realize the forest surrounding your cabin goes on seemingly forever. The raven then relents and decides to go with you and guide you.  The two spends eight, entire years, walking thru the frontier with no demons or humans in sight until finally you do come across civilization at last, and you are now a fully grown man.  Thus the adventure truly begins. The game uses some very beautiful background images, similar to how the SNES days have done it, with excellent character and monster animations with some enemies looking like they been hand drawn.  Its a action RPG combat system with near infinite stat growth, you can constantly keep getting stronger but to a certain extent.  You can gain levels, get these monster essences called Force, to boost your stats in a sort of stat board placement system similar to what FF 10 uses.  However to keep you from getting too overpowered, their is a maximum you can go on this Placement System which is defined by locks you cannot open until you reach the next chapter.  You also have a skill system that uses Magic Crystals that you collect via various means.  You gain these skills by mastering the massive assortments of weapons, shields and armor.  Most of these will have a skill attached that once mastered, you can either use the skill for free long as you use that piece of equipment, or assign Magic Crystals to that skill to have it on permanently for as long as you have crystals assigned.  This allows you to customize your character to your play style.  All this allows you to do basically three different types of builds I primarily see.  Want to be fast and defensive? Use a one hand weapon with shield,  with a shield you can block most attacks so long as they dont break your block gauge.   Spec to skills and stats that favors this.  Want to use a two handed weapon or thrusting weapon?  Spec for agility, use skills that boosts the range or speed of these weapons.  Want to use a magic staff and throw out fireballs and lightning like a wizard?  Spec for Magic over ATK and select skills that compliments Staff usage.  You also have a summon system called Possession, which uses button inputs to dictate what you summon.  You earn these summons via the Stat board and they are categorized in six different elements. Fire, Water, Earth, Wind, Dark and Light.  You can set these summons however your play style or need is and they use a gauge called ST or Stamina which you regain simply from attacking.  Standard play loop is, attack until bar fills up, then use possession, then repeat.   Possessions are a way to cause massive damage all over, or to get yourself out of a bad situation.  I personally like using possession skills where you become the Summon for a fixed period of time allowing me to consume healing items in safety if needed.  Due to near infinite stat growth, and of two, new mechanics that comes up post game, I wont spoil those, but I do wonder why the developer did not put those at the start.  I highly recommend to play the game on either Hell or Impossible difficulty, since the game seems balanced around those two difficulties.  You can change difficulties at will at any point until chapter 2.  Once you go past chapter 2, you can only go down in difficulty and cannot go up again.  Which is a weird design decision, I played the game on Hell and often wished I could put it up to Impossible since I am a completionist and I often will find ways to circumvent or cheese anything difficult.  I still had quite a challenge on Hell mode, but most bosses just seemed too easy due to the amount of grind I would put in and simply due to collecting all the weapons and armor to gain more skills or Magic Crystals.  In short, if you want to be lightly challenged, play it on Hell, otherwise, I recommend Impossible if you want to at least 90 percent the game.  Many enemies and bosses can become bullet hells where dodging or blocking is needed depending on your playstyle.  Difficulty will determine how much you need to grind or simply be patient and dodge and block as much as possible. Just keep in mind the game has Near, infinite, stat growth.  You CAN with enough grinding, be so overpowered that even the true final boss, or the optional final arena boss, will be as weak as kittens to you, even on impossible, but that would take a tremendous amount of grind, and you would have gone and collected and done everything long before then either way, unless you get unlucky collecting....Hearts, at the near end. Wont spoil that. Now, the soundtrack.  Honestly again, I see influences from past games on this, particularly Y's.  Now most JRPG fans would have played a Y's title or two, and would know the awesome high energy soundtracks that tends to come from that franchise.  They did pretty well with this in Astlibra,  using the same high energy seen in Y's.  The first area, Volcano area, and Demon Castle being very notable.  Sounds fantastic and makes you pumped to play which is what I believe the developers were intending.  Overall and I will say this, I have over 200+ games in my backlog.  Many on steam, many physical.  I have in my immediate concern to play and finish right now, Harvestella, Dragon Quest Treasures, Star Ocean Divine Force, Made in Abyss Binary star, Strangers of Paradise Final Fantasy Origins, and Sword and Fairy 7.  FF and DQ being in my top 5 franchises to complete start to finish. Yet, I chose to play this over them. Give it a shot. It well deserves your attention.

There's a good variety of different progression mechanics that have kept me hooked; maxing out the XP bar for each weapon, shield, and armor piece to either unlock new skills or more capacity to equip skills has been especially compelling. _childDocuments_.review: Okay so this 2D action-JRPG is absolutely amazing but it certainly has its fair share of flaws. There's too much pointless backtracking, quests and puzzles aren't explained properly leaving you to aimlessly wander until you figure out what to do, enemy attacks are poorly telegraphed (it gets worse when you're fighting many enemies at once), pushing down to block is an absolutely terrible design choice, the writing (translation) isn't the best but it has its high points and fun twists, and the characters are mostly bland stereotypical templates.However, the combat, leveling, and the satisfying feel of unlocking new gear and upgrades feels absolutely amazing, it's very satisfying. If you love to level up a ton of skills/weapons/stats or to grind then this is the game is certainly for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is something that hardly any other game is these days. It's a finished and incredibly polished. Astlibra can easily take its place among the JRPG behemoths of the 16 bit era, and it may well be one of the best -if not THE best- JRPG ever made. The fact that this was created by a single person is simply mind blowing.Although you can still clearly feel the indie jankiness in the game, it has been polished to the degree where it just becomes its art style. At times you feel like you're playing a mid-2000s flash game that has been iterated on a million times until it was effectively a AAA release. It borrows stylistic elements from at least a dozen other successful IPs yet manages to outshine most of them in execution.While I could go on endlessly about the things Astlibra does well, let me critique the few things that it didn't. - The music is sometimes a bit of off. While overall the soundtrack has been very good, it does have weak points.- The translation work is occasionally lacking. It's not nearly as bad as it could be, but you can tell it's a game made primarily for a Japanese audience.- There is a strong focus on grinding for power. This is perfectly fine and expected in the genre, but especially towards the level 40-50 areas you are no longer expected to grind where the story takes you. If you fail to figure that out, it can feel like you're running into a brick wall.- The hardest challenges in the game effectively turn into bullet hell gameplay. That's also fine, but at times the visual clarity is severely lacking which can make the challenge feel artificially difficult.- There are some random pop-ups of out of place sexually suggestive art that can at best be explained by "Japanese game". They are very few though.- The optional content (i.e. arena challenges) are not very optional at all and yield de-facto required items.To recapitulate: 10/10, amazing game, would recommend to anyone even remotely into JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very addictive and compelling structure if you are the type of player who likes to explore thoroughly and grind a bit to stay ahead of the curve in your RPGs. Basically, most gear in the game is constructed from materials dropped by enemies, and repeatedly using said gear unlocks most of your important magical abilities. There are two separate systems for gaining better stats by killing enemies: from gaining experience and leveling up, and from collecting colored orbs and using them on a Final Fantasy X type grid, where the latter system also unlocks some magical abilities and some items/gear. Additionally, stats are also modified by placing items on the pans of a magical scale, where you have to balance item specific bonuses and getting the weight balance right. There is also a crafting system where you can create a variety of items from several magical recipe books. The 8 hour postgame/postscript adds additional systems that are beyond the scope of this review. The character progression systems are wonderfully complex and interlocking, but still easy to grasp early in the game. The game makes great use of an act system and restrictions on how far you can progress on the grid to restrict the current possibility space to make short term goals achievable and clear. When I got to a new act, I could not wait to grind the new enemy types for the materials/items, build all available gear, get the corresponding magical abilities and advancing on the grid system until the next hard lock.The game has a quite convoluted story focused on time travel. I personally liked most of it, but at times I mashed the progress button hoping to get along to the next farming spot ... The quality of the story varies a lot between different segments. Looking back at the game, the best and worst segments were sometimes contained in the same act.The graphics seemed off-putting at first, like a botched up-resing job of a game that may have looked better with a more pixelated look, but I got used to the visual style. The 2d traversal and combat feel great and contribute to how addictive it is to collect materials/items for the character progression systems.In conclusion, this is a well structured and frankly pretty addictive action RPG. The game is great for people who have a hard time getting into games and remaining interested in them, where the clarity of the game's structure and your short term goals are a big part of this.

_childDocuments_.review: When I beat this game, I had two reactions. My first reaction was WOW, this is seriously impressive and quite inspiring for a solo dev. One man over the course of 15 years slowly perfected the game. The combat is fun and satisfying, as well as quite simplistic (you just mash attack and sometimes cast spells by holding a button and inputting 1 or 2 directions). There is some depth to the combat, such as backsteps with I-frames and perfect blocks, but really nothing beats mashing square at a ridiculous attack per minute rate. Can induce carpal tunnel, but it's very fun. Over the course of 50 hours not once did I get bored or tired of the combat. I went out of my way to fight enemies to grind for resources, and I loved every minute of grinding in this game. I would compare the combat to something like Symphony of The Night or Aria of Sorrow, except with a few extra moves tacked on, and spells don't require as many inputs to cast and are actually pretty much all worth using. However, don't be fooled - this isn't a metroidvania, you don't backtrack to previous areas once you acquire some form of power up to progress through the game. This is just a 2D side-scroller jRPG, and it's linear.Progression is tied to resources and can be easily described as "number go up". When you kill an enemy, they drop money, "force" (a resource spent leveling up stats by small increments, acquiring new spells and some other goodies in a special menu board), experience points, chests and crafting materials. Chests can contain recipes for particularly powerful items for the chapter you're in, and crafting felt rewarding because equipment stats are palpable. Additionally, each piece of equipment, excluding accessories, has an XP bar you can fill up. Once you do, you either upgrade its stats or receive a skill which you can slot in using crystals you can acquire throughout the game. This system gives the player a wide array of customizable options to choose from, allowing the player to min-max their equipment (as is suitable for a jRPG game). The soundtrack is fantastic. The surprising part is, as far as I know, it's nearly entirely royalty free music. The tracks vary in genre, and you never really know what you're gonna hear this chapter. The music might be grating to some people, and I'd understand if that were the case, but I loved all of it.The writing is insane. The less you know about it, the better. It's unpredictable and unironically has a "twist-per-hour" rate that keeps the game going that kept me interested and invested. I've seen some people say the game doesn't know when to end, and to an extent that is true, but I never once felt like the game was padding itself. It doesn't need to. The writing isn't perfect, though, and specifically characters suffer from this. They can be somewhat inconsistent as well as very, very, VERY trope-y. Treat the characters as if they're from an anime from, like, 2009 or earlier. There were moments where I shook my head, mumbling "this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game" to myself, but I still loved every character in the game. Nobody really outstays their welcome, and the sheer magnitude of the plot absolutely eclipses any issues I had with any particular character's scene. Seriously, the plot is a wild ride. Then, once you beat the game, there is a new game plus - a "postscript" - and it's probably one of the coolest iterations of a new game plus I've ever seen in a game. The new game plus is also more plot and the fact that it's a new game plus is part of the plot. It also adds new mechanics, though mostly just for extra stats so you can power yourself up into outer space. That was my first reaction. My second reaction was what the ♥♥♥♥? Hey, KEIZO? WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥?I loved every hour of this game, money well spent, and I highly recommend it to anyone who wants a more classic jRPG approach to gameplay with the writing of early Final Fantasy entries and Chrono Trigger mushed together. There's genuinely few games with a story like this out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on calling this game underrated because it really isn't for everybody. It's grindy, the combat doesn't evolve all that much especially with how much the game makes you do it, and a lot of the interactions can skeeve some people out. However, if this game strikes a chord with you, then it is legitimately one of the most amazing games ever made.The combat, while simple, has a lot of underlying interactions that makes deeper than what makes it initially seem. None of the weapons have any special unique animations, but weapons such as knives are faster and can charge your magic bar better, staves have a total of 1 attack power but have strong secondary effects such as shooting fireballs, and heavy swords have great range and power at the cost of speed and weight, which you will immediately and intuitively feel out as you play the game. Yes, the game has a lot of grinding, but it also keeps rewarding you for all the small actions you do. Of course you can level up like in all RPGs, but Monsters also drop "force" which you can use to permanently upgrade your stats or even unlock new spells and weapons/armor/accessories. Monsters also drop chests with a whole host of loot that will make grinding actually exciting to engage in, from new equipment recipes, to straight up new equipment, to resources you can use in your adventures such as healing items. All these are not carrots-at-the-end-of-the-stick that other grindy rpgs have to force you into grinding, but fun rewards the game constantly throws at you. Not to mention the sound design and all the little visual flourishes that attacks do make the simple act of actually just fighting monsters all that much more fun to do.The music, while not wholly original, fit the tone of each stage all the tracks are placed in, which really transcend the experience. Stand out tracks for me include the boss theme of Act 3 and the stage theme of act 7, which you wouldn't even know weren't actually originally made for this game unless you looked it up or someone told it to you with how well they were implemented into the game.The story is the biggest pain point for any players who enjoy games such as these. It attempts to explore a lot of weighty subjects such as fate, death, loss, all wrapped around a time travel mechanic, which has historically not worked out well for stories that use them, while also having very "anime" interactions, an example being, one of the female characters repeatedly misunderstanding that they are being sexually propositioned by a merchant when it was actually a wholesome interaction all along. There's also a secret boss in chapter 5 that will be very offputting for a lot of players that aren't used to, let's just say. very very "anime" media. Don't take this part as a condemnation from me though, as you can really feel the love from the dev weaved through every bit of every interaction you have with all the characters. Once you realize the stakes of the story, you really feel this sense of unease and dread at what might happen when you go along because you really grow attached to these characters. TLDR, it's not for everybody, but if you let your guard down or if you already enjoy games and stories like these, it is a magnificent experience that will stick with you for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best Action RPGs ever made. And don’t get me started on all the RPG systems that are put into this game. It can sound overwhelming when reading about all the systems before starting the game, but Astlibra manages to introduce the systems step by step over dozens of hours of gameplay. The player character can level up, distribute attribute points, learn magic, add items to a magic Libra to improve all kind of stats, distribute points on a giant Sphere Grid, find and craft dozens and dozens of weapons, shields, armors and accessories and unlock boards for every single weapon, armor and accessories to improve them even more. Seriously, if you like to become the baddest of badass RPG characters with fun grinding, optimization and build options, this is your game. But it is also your game if you like crazy anime stories. Or just a laid back, relaxed Hack’n’Slay with nice graphics. You know what? If you like videogames even a bit, you have to get this game. Period. It’s a masterpiece. Some of the best 20€ you can spend on Steam. Get it and spread the gospel. Don’t believe me? Try the demo. And oh, this is the PERFECT Steam Deck game as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I came to Astlibra Revision like many folks, due to word-of-mouth from online communities and friends. It's not the kind of game I'd usually find myself digging into - I'm not big into Metroidvanias or more action-y RPGs. But I gave it a chance and found myself really, really enjoying it, I played on Easy mode (which I'm sure is anathema to many), but as a 40 year old with heavy work and family commitments, I just don't find the joy in "gitting gud" that many do. But even on Easy, I found it appropriately challenging for a relative newcomer to the genre. The way the game expands systems and options over time felt really thoughtful, and the story is weird but a lot of fun. Some of the quirky, very JRPG-ish sexuality is juvenile and embarrassing, but nothing worse than you'd find in games of the era it's celebrating. I finished the main game and did quite a bit of the new game plus and heartily recommend it. Considering the size of the development staff involved, this game is genuinely a wonder and provided me way more enjoyment than many, many games with hundreds of devs and unbelievable budgets. Highly recommended, and I expect if you're looking to for the mastery angle, cranking the difficulty will certainly deliver, but other reviewers' experience will be more relevant there. Thanks to everyone who recommended this game to me - I would never have found it or picked it up otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was ever a textbook example of "don't judge a book by it's cover" in videogame format it would be this game. Because while screenshots make it look like some sort of cheap mobile game using mismatched bought assets, it is actually one of the best indie games I have played in my life, if not one of the best games in general ever.I don't even know where should I ever start with praises for this game. The gameplay is addicting, the graphics - while on screenshots looks cheap - in the game work very well, the music is fantastic, the story is gripping, you really feel for the protagonist, you want him to succeed, his absolute unwavering conviction to help people he loves makes him extremely likeable, and all that while still staying silent.The rest of the NPC's are all fleshed out and likeable so when they struggle you really want to help them and it feels good when you manage to do so.Also big props to devs for not bowing down to modern day beauty erasure standards, as there are lots of stunning spritework of female characters with huuuuuuuuuuge plots of land in this game, like hot damn.If I really had to criticize this game at all I guess I would say there are some plotpoints that feel a bit tropy or are straight copies from other pieces of media, or the game might feel a bit grindy at times but those would be a tiny insignificant scratches on a surface of this beautiful diamond of a game.Bottom line is: 11 out of 10, took me about 72 hours to 100% and it was probably one of the most fun games to get a hundo completion. In fact I'm sad that I'm already done, I want more of this world, more of this characters, more of this game. And if that is not a recommendation for you than I don't know what is.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good. Played on normal and wasn't too hard though starting from normal you could always turn the difficultly to easy. Total game time to complete is 30ish hrs(from what a dev had said), but I've grinded for nearly every possible item to acquire and master. Try out the demo first I implore you as it gives a rough grasp on the combat.  The story is based around the Libra scales of time and fate which are the manifestation of the Goddess Astraea's powers. It's interesting, thought invoking, and largely linear .  Only gripes with the story are that in two chapters there was an annoying amount of abrupt "oh you thought" moments where you think the chapter is over and you're leaving the zone only to be halted and told to go back up to three times before the chapter decides it's over. In the other chapter you think you're going to catch up to your friend as he's always just out of eyesight before you suddenly and coincidentally start having abrupt visions repeatedly as you chase throughout the zone like the developer is having fun teasing you with "but wait, there's more!" The last gripe is that after conclusion of every chapter you'll be re-watching the same cutscene over and over same as when you have to watch the Libra sending you back in time. These cutscenes are skippable, but I watch them the first 5-6 times as a brief intermission just to appreciate the journey so far and to collect your thoughts about whats happening in the story.    The gameplay is fantastical with combat based around techniques(combos), utilizing shields to bash(group them up for aoe) or parrying, dodges, magic skills, making use of I-frames, using weapons your enemy is weak against, putting items on the Libra scale and balancing them to gain their effects, making use of two-handers for their range advantage and bigger hitboxes if you can keep your agility high enough. A gross weight of 80 or higher is a no no akin to the dark souls "fat roll", so to avoid this either choose a lighter weapon/shield or give yourself higher agility to wield it effectively. Fire is weak against water, Earth is weak against Wind, Darkness(lightning) is weak against Holy and vice versa for a total of 6 elements, you can also see this by how the game has the magic skills ordered in the skill menu.  Progression in this game is looking for treasure chests that contain very useful items. gathering materials and monster drops that're unique to each monster in a zone and purchasing every weapon, armor, shield, and accessories in the store then mastering them to either get a magic crystal or a Karon skill(passives). As well as gathering "force" from defeated enemies in order to spend in the Grow menu to grow your attributes, obtain weapons unobtainable elsewhere, and new magic skills. I highly recommend you master the tree branch at least by chapter 3 as it gives a Karon skill that improves the rate at which you master weapons. An example of how powerful your character could get by the end of the game is that your agility is high enough to have a gross weight of zero, having the "full burst" Karon skill that consumes your full ST bar to increase the power of your next magic skill in proportion to the amount consumed(there's two other variants of this skill) then casting the magic skill that increases your movement and swing speed. You'll be swinging so fast that the swing animation has to cancel itself for the next swing which is funny to look at and amazing to hear how fast you're landing hits on an enemy melting through them.  I've haven't played anything quite like this before excluding the samey side-scroller rouge-likes that pad the game time by having you die a lot and starting over from the beginning. Definitively worth a play.

_childDocuments_.review: After a hundred hours of playing, I have finally finished this game, beaten the final boss, and borne witness to a beautiful ending. I am actually baffled that an indie RPG of this depth and quality exists; no matter how much I played, it always had something else up its sleeve to surprise me with. This is nothing short of a passion project with emphasis on the passion; I am actually moved to tears by having played something that is like... this. I haven't felt this way since . I feel invigorated and purposeful for playing this game. I am actually angry at having played other indie games that aren't this deep, this full of content, this .I do have a couple of issues, though. I'm going to forgive the choppy translation and the hideous mishmash of textures and graphics; this is a passion project by someone in their basement, after all, and I expect it would be tremendously rough.What I do take issue with is our hero having no name and no voice. The silent protagonist is a trend that I really wish would die in video games already as technology's evolved past the need to keep text boxes sparse in order to preserve disk space. Same goes for not having a name. It just feels weird and strange for everyone to call you "dear hero" or "this guy", and it's  weird when it is outright stated that your name is written somewhere in game but no one ever refers to you by it.A character having no name and no voice is meant to allow the player to project onto them but that simply doesn't work here: our hero is indeed a character with driving motivations that characterise him, the search for Anulis. We should be drawn deeply into our hero's passionate and lifelong search for his beloved childhood friend but the lack of actual characterisation on display feels like a wall of jelly that I can't get through. What's more, the hero does talk to other people a lot and express himself but, without words, all you get are people constantly repeating everything you say like Solid Snake. "What's that, dear hero? You want to buck common sense and leap into danger to save them?"A lot of scenes in the story are diminished by the hero's inability to speak but none more so than one specific moment near the very end. The knees of that scene absolutely buckle as it tries to convey what  be a moment of such heartwarming sincerity and fulfillment but only has one half of it.I stress that our hero is very much a character and so the typical strengths of a silent protagonist, however meager, do not apply here. If the protagonist spoke, the game would be so much better for it.But this most certainly does not impede the quality of . Play it. Play it play it play it play it play it. Play the demo. Be made curious by the demo so that you buy and play the whole thing. If you're a fan of , this game will exceed every expectation you have and more. _childDocuments_.review: Conditional thumbs up. _childDocuments_.review: Only in the very early going but the title seems promising. Attractive art style that shines through in the sprite work. Fun hack and slash combat that already shows some promise with a few different learned abilities accessible.Update: Just wanted to add to my impressions after playing a couple more hours. While I have only progressed a tiny bit further into the game, I've learned a bit more about the leveling and "grow" system. The game has regular exp. that you collect from defeating enemies, but also gives you different color gems. You can then turn these in for various stat buffs and even new abilities. It feels like a slightly more free form sphere grid from Final Fantasy X.I've also just unlocked the second "summon" ability. I am blanking on the proper name, but you gain "ST" via attacking enemies. This in turn fills up a gauge from which you draw upon to perform special attacks with the aid of your quasi "familiar" avian ally. This adds a nice wrinkle to the already enjoyable hack and slash combat.You also have character passive and active skills you must manually activate from it's own menu. You must have the required amount of magic crystals for the given skill you wish to require. These range from things such as displaying enemy health values, showing you how much damage you're dealing, as well as more active abilities such as being able to guard in mid air or dash/sprint with the press of a button (or double tap of a direction) .I already managed to write quite a bit, and from the slight bit I've read online (I'm trying to avoid spoiling too much as I get the feeling the game could get pretty wild) I'm barely scratching the surface of what the game has to offer both mechanically and from a narrative perspective. I look forward into delving further into the adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it a 6/10. Still worth playing if you like this Metroidvanias. But not a particularly good one. The fighting mechanics has that thing where the game pauses for a split second whenever your attack connects. This is a combo-heavy game. In addition, one attack hitting multiple enemies freezes the screen for each enemy hit. Really annoying. You do get used to it.The magic system is interesting. You can equip 8 different magic attacks/summons and you have use them through a button combination. It's quick and easy to use. The magic/summons have situational uses, so you still use different ones every now and then, even if one of them is overwhelmingly the best for enemy swarms. To build up magic meter, you need to do physical attacks. It goes down over time if you are not attacking.The passive bonus system is a little too much. Leveling up grants you stat points that you can allocate and respec whenever you want. A "growth" screen has a skill-tree looking thing that lets you buy stat points and sometimes new magic skills. The amount of stat points you get from this screen overshadows anything you get from leveling up.Lastly, you get to pick items that give passive bonuses. This part is cool. You get scales that need an equal amount of "karma" from items on the left and right sides. You mix and match items (consumables, crafting ingredients) of different karma values and different passive bonuses to get the two sides as equal as possible. If they are not equal, you still get the bonuses, but the values are diminished. Again, the "growth" screen provides so many stat points that the bonuses from the scales are not as big a deal.The weapons aren't very varied. You have a few magic staves that give mostly useless magic attacks. Can't really aim them right. 1-handed swords / hammers and some two handed weapons. The attacks though are pretty much identical. Spear and rapier are different, but everything else has the same animations/attacks.There is also the passive magic bonus system. You equip magic passives such as double jump, swing heavy weapons faster, auto-guard, etc. Utility skills mainly. So far the gameplay is:1. Start in town. Arena in town has challenges where you can win extra items. Some shops, but you have everything after the first visit.2. Go to the guild to get a new mission. You get transported to a new area.3. You leave town and can't come back until you finish the mission. Every mission so far has had a shop in the mission area itself so this isn't a big deal. It does mean that you can't just go to the arena whenever you want. The new area contains all of the ingredients for the new items you can buy from the new shop.  Each area is only a few different screens. No real exploration.4. Back in town. You can go back to old areas through a portal once in town again.It's a pretty grindy game. I am playing on Hard and it takes forever to master the weapons you get. Mastering equipment through use grants you new magic passives I mentioned earlier, so you want to master all of them in case you get a good utility skill.But the biggest problem is there is nothing to discover. Metroidvanias are about exploration and getting skills that allow you to explore old areas you couldn't reach before. None of that here.  There is ONE area so far in Chapter 4 (I think) that has a secret entrance to some secret area with super strong enemies. One-hit kills at the time you first get there. Maybe later the game has more of this stuff, but I'm a solid 16 hours in the game and that's the only thing so far.So yeah, the issues are that it's a bit too straightforward, too many mechanics that have overlapping effects (leveling up, growth screen, and scale system all add passive stat bonuses), and the fighting is a bit clunky, though not as bad as Salt and Sanctuary or Blasphemous.

_childDocuments_.review: Old school hack and slash that perfectly blends:* Combo smashing: Combo goes brrr, yet you don't even have to spam since there is a skill that let you hold a button and your character will just execute the combo automatically. What matter is timing and mixing up your attack.* Timed blocking: You have a shield, use it. Even bosses' attacks can be blocked perfectly. But being passive and hiding behind your shield means becoming a sitting duck. Your stamina is limited. You can't keep blocking indefinitely.* Special attack: Normal attack fills up a gauge that can be used for a wide range of special attacks with devastating damage.   It starts with holding a button, inputting a fighting game style sequence of directional keys (e.g: down up) and releasing the previous button.   You would summon and sometimes transform into Final Fantasy style GF spirits.   They also grant you a short period of invincibility.   The best defense is a well timed offense.   You can negate a bunch of hard to dodge, costly to block attacks by a timely special.   Which brings us to:* Counter attack. Block an attack and immediately counter also grant you invincibility frames.   This is a key to get through some seemingly impenetrable defenses.   It feels amazing to execute that perfect sequence of blocking, counter attack then special, throwing a bunch of numbers up while dashing through a flurry of threats being thrown at you.Not only that, the battle system is supported by:* A host of varied craftable weapons and equipment each with their own play style.* Weapon mastery can give you a bunch of useful passive skills.* A skill tree system that looks more like a skill maze.It may sound like there is a lot of grinding but there isn't.Even on hell difficulty (the second highest), I never had to grind.Just exploring, walking from one objective point to other, killing everything on the way is enough to get through the game.Not just that, before boss fights, the game always let you respec your stats for **free** so you can tinker with your build to find the best way to tackle a boss battle.You are never trapped in an invalid build, making you grind to make up for it.There are respec potions but I never had to use them since the game is so generous with respec points.Also, the mixtape (music) is fire. Even in the beginning when you only have a tree branch to hit some slime, the music goes hard.It makes me want to be a JRPG heroes and save them waifus.Cons:* The dialogue is kinda silly. Jokes are sometimes made in serious scenes that just breaks the mood and then characters went serious again.* The story is pretty cliched so far. A do gooder, self sacrificing hero with insane strength (you) trying to save everyone with the power of friendship.If you do play, I recommend starting with Hell and lower it to Hard if it's too challenging or your progression is too slow.At certain point in the game, you can't raise it up to Hell again.On hard, the game is moderately challenging, you do die often if you are careless.In difficulty below Hell (second highest), the game pauses when you are inputting your fighting game style button sequence for your special attack. It makes timing a lot easier and forgiving.In Hell and above, there are no more pauses. You have to perfectly master those timings. It feels good to do the same damage cancelling sequence said above in real time, dodging death by a hairline.However, I admit I'm getting old and my progression in Hell is too slow since I have to keep retrying the same path and bosses.I dropped to Hard later and the game is enjoyable so far.

_childDocuments_.review: "Wanderers of Ys,Simon's Quest,and Cadash had a class reunion with their old chum Chrono-trigger!" ~Game-Sport"When you think it's over it's not. You'll get your money's worth!" ~Ferbes"If Square made a Final Fantasy into a side scrolling action rpg it would play out something like this!" ~Electronic Mayhem"Will take you Nier and far. Has fangs like Symphony Of The Night whilst being much broader in scope. Astlibra is not afraid to get deeper and darker yet also retains the nostalgia of being a fun high fantasy romp. Its' scales are perfectly balanced!"" ~ Independent Gamers Anonymous "Remember how Zelda II The Adventure Of Link was a good but very flawed game? Imagine a similar idea constructed with better parts and a more adept engineer. All whilst throwing in some existentialism and science fiction into the fantasy rpg cauldron!" ~RPG-ArgonautsAstlibra is simultaneously a game and an experience. Around 10 or so hours in isn't even the tip of the iceberg but consider the fact in those 10 hours I could hardly put it down and I stopped only to say that yes,while it is on sale you should consider picking it up! If you were on the fence before it's a good excuse to dive on in! There is no secondary launchers,no season passes,and no current year politics. Just a really good side scrolling action rpg involving time travel,past lives,altering fate,spooky eldritch mysteries,and becoming as gods. Somehow manages to line up in the vicinity of Final Fantasy,Ys,and Iga-era Castlevanias on the pie chart! English translation is superb and the story-telling is based. I haven't been on this many emotional roller-coasters for quite awhile if I'm to be bluntly candid.Ditto for the soundtrack,art assets,and overall presentation. All this put together by "one guy" whom got a bit more help by equally passionate animators,illustrators,and composers down the road. Astute creative pioneers whom obviously saw the true value in this project and the potential it held.You can only get something like this naturally. It requires raw no-holds-barred imagination. No trust and safety committees. No sensitivity squads. No share holders. No mega corps. Just individuals passionate about the craft that is game design. It's too bad the AAA industry has become out of touch with the wild-west that was once game development. When passionate programmers made masterpieces in their basements on their spare time on the weekends! It was a different time and I would argue a better time.Anyway,that's all I gotta say. If this was the last game I ever got to play I'd be content with that. I'd feel as if I was going out on a high note as they certainly do not make em like this anymore.Pros+Presentation is retro yet simultaneously jaw dropping!+ The soundtrack is on a whole other level. I don't have the words....+The game's systems are varied yet accessible.+The story-line really is like binge-ing thru a superbly written manga or a really good episodic anime!+Excellent crafting system!+Boss fights have just the right balance of spectacle and challenge.+Loot is everywhere and in everything! +Puzzles so far have been fun and fair! If you pay attention you will rarely get stuck.+Armor pieces and weapons look different from each other when you equip them on the protagonist. + Refreshing fan service and even some playful adult innuendos. I appreciate that because in current year including those things denotes conviction and courage!+The combo system that mixes in additional inputs to summon final-fantasy-like guardian spirits as you are simultaneously hacking and slashing away is poetry in motion!Neutral+/- Rpgs in the late 90's surprised gamers with what I call "climatic continuations". By that I mean you think the game is leading you to the last battle when in truth you are just at the midway mark. One door closes as another door opens. You get the gist! In FF6 this counted as the 'Land Of Ruin Arc" after Kefka messed with the magic statues and rained down his wrath upon the world. In Chrono Trigger there was a hidden quest to recruit Magus and the game even continued on after Crono died as all his friends had to once again travel through time to bring him back. You could even fight Lavos in the past,present,or future to trigger different outcomes. Astlibra does something similar and even introduces brand new systems to upgrade your gear. Excessive? Repetitive? Unnecessary? Certain people might think so but if you enjoy grinding for that true ending whilst attaching ridiculous deity-tier attributes and super charged abilities to your collective armory and arsenal then Astlibra's penultimate chapter will be a nostalgic time-warp back to those golden days of gaming! It feels akin to that fond memory of renting a hidden gem from block buster,convincing your parents to eventually buy it for you,and then having all summer to gleefully unravel its' mysteries! Cons-There is very little in the way of hand holding. You are given the basics in an isolated tutorial section then dropped into the world proper like a baby being delivered by the stork!-No voice acting. You are going to have to read a lot. I don't personally consider this a sore-spot but I know certain folks are used to even their computers and their i-phones talking back to them!-End game is "brutal". Even on a lower difficulty the fates will chew you up and spit you out! While it doesn't entirely undermine the whole experience it goes from "Challenging but reasonable" to "Welp,guess I'm gonna have to excessively grind and find those hidden god-artifacts!" in the blink of an eye once you cross a certain threshold.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good action game, a little rough in spots, like areas where the BGM doesn't loop cleanly, but it's all minor nuisances really.It consists of a simple gameplay-loop, you go into a location, which will consist of some 5 to 10 screens, you fight your way through some 4 or 5 different enemies (unique to said area), you unlock all the items available in that area, there's a boss fight, the story progresses, and then you go into a new location.Combat is very fast and responsive,  not so intricate, you have a few different moves, but you couple regular melee attacks with powerful magical attacks/buffs  (that are activated by entering directional commands, kinda like a fighting game but not quite)Progression is multi-faceted:- you have your regular leveling system, just gaining exp from defeating  enemies, then distributing your points in different stats- there's what the game calls the "grow system" which is this huge tree of, mostly, minor stat bonuses, that you get by spending a type of energy you get from defeating enemies, there are 6 different types of said energy, and you'll need a balance of them all (different enemies give off different types) to complete the whole tree, you can also get new magic skills and improve said skills in this same tree- The game has MANY pieces of equipment, and each  has it's own progression of sorts, in which, while wearing/wielding an item, all experience you gain by killing enemies goes towards said item "mastery", when mastering an item you gain a new ability OR a crystal used to activate said abilities (it's a basic balancing system, for example, you have 8 crystals, and 10 abilities to chose from, some abilities need 3 crystals, some 4, some 1, and you have to decide which ones to enable)And it's all very satisfyingI also like how the game respects the player's time, for instance you can respec every time you level up, or at any time in specific locations, plus you don't have to worry about missing any content since, after a certain point in the story progression, you can revisit any previous area to get anything you might have missed.The story is your usual anime-grade nonsensical stuff, but it's alright

_childDocuments_.review: ✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨☑️Reasonable price tag.☑️Delivers a unique RPG experience.☑️Great story.☑️Great character personalities.☑️Great music / boss music.☑️Addicting as hell combat.☑️Menu sound effects are great.☑️Incentive to farm mats for new weapons.☑️A system to grow your character.☑️Build the way you want.☑️Weapons respond well to their WEIGHT.❌A few minor translation errors. ❌Boss HP scaling is absurd. Astlibra is a unique experience. I went in expecting the game to be mediocre due to the trailers showing overly complex designs for the characters and back grounds. But putting that aside, I decided to give it a honest try.It felt like I was a kid again as silly as that sounds, playing games like Maplestory, running around mindlessly mowing down hoards of monsters for the sake of wanting to level up and farm materials for quests / weapon crafting. The story is pretty predictable, as in if you know something the characters do not you have to force them to do what you know you shouldn't, if that makes sense. The story is good regardless, but the desire to want to actually go out and farm materials from monsters and minerals is just as good. I spent 2 hours in the demo area alone just unlocking everything and having fun and another 4+ hours in the lava cave, once again farming. The proficiency system as well gives you a lot of reason to want to keep mowing down enemy after enemy along with the very fair growth system which is kind of similar to Final Fantasy XII with it's "Zodiac" system. Granting you new skills and bonuses in your overall character stats at the cost of grains from your enemies. If you can't afford lets say 5 green, you can use 15 of another colour to grow without having to search for those specific types of monster drops. The issue with Boss HP scaling comes with the difficulty setting. Monsters will gain a lot more damage to you, while also having a lot more health. Easy mode has most bosses and the very first boss you encounter at level 7-9 (unless you power farm) with about 9k health which takes forever, but it's fine cause you take like no damage, however, the harder boss fights have over 20k while being able to one shot you if you haven't been power-leveling or doing proper hit and run tactics.I rarely get this attached to video games, the last time I was this invested in a story was when I was playing through Divinity Original Sin II. Lost in thought and the world I was exploring. Try the Demo. It's very short and doesn't offer to much, but it will at the very least help you understand what the game is all about. It can be a little bit confusing at first, but it's honestly really fun. The combat isn't perfect, but it's a Hack & Slash! Run in, mow down enemies and bosses, farm the materials and get some new gear, unlock new skills and weapons to take on bigger foes and challenges. The game was developed by a solo Japanese developer for over 14 years. KEIZO has a daily job and only worked on the game after he got back home. You know it's not easily to develop a video game on your own especially over 14 years of development. However, with the help of prolific artist Shigatake (Dragon’s Crown) and Haku Tatsufuchi (Magic: The Gathering), and Publisher WhisperGames, the game has got a "Revision" upgrade, which you see here today. Stay and pay attention to the story, it might have it's translation errors here and there, but outside of that, it's pretty solid. It definitely makes me want to play it, not for any other reason than it's good and nostalgic.EDIT:It keeps getting BETTER and BETTER the more I play this game. The time travel, the plot, the story, the characters. My god.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly a masterpiece. KEIZO's 15 years of work really paid off, he made something truly special here. It's been awhile since I couldn't put down a singleplayer game, and since I played something where the pure passion of the developer was tangible while playing. Story is excellent (though I'm a sucker for time travel and the butterfly effect, and we ignore how cringe chapter 4 was) but more than that I just love the compelling sense of adventure it provides, and just how ridiculous the scale of it gets. Gameplay is fantastic and incredibly addictive, I never got tired of experimenting with new builds. There's tons of ways to consistently get a bit more powerful, and there's a lot of incentive to collect all of the weapons and gear and level them up - they're always useful since you unlock skills that can be used with any build. Also this game is BEEFY. Every time you think the story is coming to and end it just keeps going, and going...but at the same time it doesn't outstay its welcome. Just the main story took me almost 70 hours to complete (though I really took my time grinding and making sure I didn't miss any secrets because I was having a ton of fun). Postscript really took me by surprise, because I wasn't expecting it to introduce new mechanics. Also while the DLC doesn't add too much to the story - if you enjoyed the combat you'll have a lot of fun with it, and I wasn't ready for it to be over, so I was happy to have it. Very highly recommend playing it on at least hard mode, because while the game isn't afraid to kick you in the ♥♥♥♥ -  it's SO rewarding when things click for you and you finally beat that bastard boss that was giving you trouble. Absolute must play for any lovers of oldschool JRPGs and well worth 2x the price. While I certainly wasn't expecting it, it very quickly snuck into my top 10 favourite games of all time. Actual 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I didn't think I would summons and fights big tiddies anime girls. Literally one of my favorite games right after NieR:Automata including the musics which is a really high praise because I  NieR OST and I swear I heard vocaloid in at least one of the songs and damn it was good. You have to play this game to experience the story yourself, I think this game is best play on hard.When I first saw this game on release I thought it was weird base on the gameplay trailer, enemy movements kinda stiff like papercut animations, the game seem to have microstutters or pause for a bit when you hits your enemies, I thought it was a low quality product but trust me it's not, I was dead wrong, those things are crucial to the gameplay. This game may look like a metroidvania but it's not, it's more like a liner game where each chapter take place in an area that you can come back later, there's no one big map with many zonesI highly recommend trying the combat demo, if you like the basic combats you gonna loves this game. I played on Hell and only just finished like half postscript. This game is the definition of underrated, it has no reason to be this good for this price, normally I don't even like JRPG (mostly anime games not Janpanese games) or side scroller.The combat actually has a lot of depth in it, at first I thought it would just be stand in one place spamming attack button to build up ST to use possession skills but the more you play the better the combat gets. You can do melee attack, range magic attack, guard, perfect guard, back step, double jumps, air dash, upper cut, downward slash, guard counter, shield bash, shield charge, you can also change how some of your attack works later on.There are many weapon types and each has different basic attacks moveset, swords have medium range and speed, daggers are short but really fast, hammers are really good at breaking enemy poise/posture which will stun them for awhile, magic wands are crazy good at ST build up but need to be used at melee range, spear has long range and medium speed but need to be two handed, big swords/hammers are slow but have highest damage per hit. This is not a game where you pick a weapon you like and stick with it, expect to change weapons a lot depend on what you're fighting, there's a very early weapon you can get that will help you cheese most of the arena challengesThere are 6 elements in the game, each has 5 possession skills that you will slowly unlocks. They are really fun to use and you will be using them a lot as they are your best damage source, they also provide iframes, you can get healed if you're attacked during possesion skills later on so they are very important.Boss fights are awesome, it's like a dance where you have to learn the boss movesets, some boss are just bullets hell though. There's only one boss that I despite in this game even in postscript, it's literally just a bad boss design that is unfun and unfair to fight on high difficulty, even in the lowest difficulty this boss is still a menace. It's chapter 3 boss which is like a breaking point for this game, the story will only get better after chapter 3 but it is also the worst boss fight I've ever experienced in any video games, I swear killing Sword Saint Isshin in Sekiro is less frustrating than this stupid boss. The boss is At one point the game turned into a which is nicheI do have some minor nitpicking: There's absolutely no  what so ever, even after a long boss fight or a long cutscene, you literally have to manually save at a checkpoint.If you die in a boss fight you'll have the option to restart the fight but that doesn't mean the game will load previous save because there's no auto save in this game, any consumable items you used will be gone.Later on there will be moments where so many things are happening on the screen you can't see the enemy animations so you don't know when to guard or dodge so you just take damage for no reason.Relic soldier's attack hitbox is bigger than what the animation shows.Chapter 7 by far is the worst (it's only like 30m or the first half of the chapter but still), no karon, can't walk without dying in 3-4 hits at level 50, shield can only block so many hits before it break, long walks without save spot, not even after a CUTSCENE, you have to fight 2 BOSSES without karon, I know there's a rare item that you can use to destroy mobs and probably intended to be used for this chapter but I don't like using items, it isn't fun but neither do stripping the player's abilities.There should be a setting to adjust brightness and contrast, the map sometime too dark so you can't appreciate the detailsSome attacks will just blend in with bright background and you can't see anything.This is probably the longest review I've ever written and that's how much I like this game, one of the must play game just like Nier:Automata.Edit: Finished the postscript. Wow, what a journey, I've played nearly 100 games, 10 000 hours on steam and this has to be one the most amazing story in gaming I've ever experienced, my second favorite story ever after One Piece which I still love after probably over 10 years. Thank you for creating this masterpiece KEIZO-san.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gift that just keeps on giving! I've got a ton to say, but all you need to do is read the header and the bold bits to know whether or not this game is worth your time.  Look, when I first saw this game, I told myself, "damn, this looks a bit dated. I haven't played a game like this in a long while, I'll probably not like it." I proceeded to try the free demo, went absolutely wild with all the fun equipment, magic, and tools you're given to play with, and got extremely interested in the brief bit of story that was teased. It was a little overwhelming at first due to how much stuff you're given to test out, but I bit the bullet, bought the game, and went on an emotional roller coaster that kept me invested every step of the way! My god, where to begin? You're an orphan who got separated from your childhood friend, and you set out on a quest to find her. A simple enough premise, but add a talking crow, some magic scales that give you the ability to travel through space and time, and you've got yourself a recipe for a plot that will keep you guessing up to the very end! You'll meet so many wonderful, memorable characters that will win your heart and make you want to do everything in your power to help them, even if that means making some very difficult decisions. In the end, you'll grow to love your companions, especially your talking crow, and you'll come to appreciate how much you've accomplished together.Time and fate are, of course, key themes of this story, and you'll leave every session thinking about how the story relates to your own life, and be inspired to take your precious time on this earth more seriously. I can not emphasize enough how much this story will stick with you as you slowly but surely make your way through every chapter.... it's a masterpiece. Did I mention that a single dude poured his heart and soul into this game? Every played Stardew Valley? That game had a similar development cycle, and it was friggen AMAZING - same holds true here - Keizo has truly perfected his vision for the experience he wants players to feel as they progress through this game, and I can 100% attest to that. I'm not ashamed to admit I wanted to cry a few times through the story. Ok, let's say you don't care much for story - that's ok, you're gonna love this game's combat. Swords, hammers, maces, axes, magic staves/wands, bows, crossbows, guns, and much, much more are available for you to use and abuse on your enemies. You've got an extremely rewarded leveling system that makes you really feel like you're growing in strength from your battles, and it's extremely fun being able to harvest materials and craft new equipment for yourself as you progress through the map. Friends, when you boot up that demo and start fighting a few demons, the very first song you hear is going to give your ears an orgasm. I kid you not, the official game has the most BADASS music to go along with you fighting beginner enemies! Keizo didn't need to go that hard, but that's just an appetizer for what you're going to be enjoying as you play. The music, like the story and combat, gets better, and better, AND BETTER, AND BETTER. Every single stage of this game kept blowing me away with how great the soundtrack is!I'm a guy who likes to exercise to kickass tunes, and I can tell you now, Astlibra Revision's soundtrack has been added to my lifting and cardio playlists. Simply put: this is the greatest JRPG music I've heard in a LONG while, and I've played a lot of fantastic JRPGs with banger soundtracks... this is in a league of its own... similar yet arguably better than the music you'd hear in the YS series. Look, I don't write reviews often. See that giant wall of text up there? It means: THIS GAME IS AMAZING! BUY IT RIGHT NOW! You could wait for a sale if you like, but I guarantee that this is one of those rare gems that's worth every single penny. You're going to remember this game for the rest of your life.Thank you, Keizo, for sharing your passion and vision with the world. Your game has truly touched my heart and I've a greater appreciation for life and the journey I've taken to reach this point. We can't go back in time IRL, but you've taught me that we can always fight for a better future. Truly, this game is a masterpiece in every sense of the word...

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and well-designed action adventure game similar to the Ys games on the SNES or Zelda 2. The gameplay is action-based combat with RPG elements in a sidescrolling format. The gameplay is tight and reactive, it's very easy to fumble your movement options if you get sloppy, but the default difficulty is forgiving enough to generally let you recover from mistakes. The difficulty curve is gentle until about Chapter 6, where the game spikes hard and basically tells you to get ready to rumble for the rest of the game. The system mechanics are extremely robust, with tons of options to make your numbers go up and to get stronger. And you need all of them, because if you don't you're going to get chewed up and spat out. DO NOT ignore the Grow board, it is a bigger source of stats than actually levelling up and your actual main stat progression method. There are a couple puzzles that are a little frustrating in the way the game signposts the answers, but there are answers to them here and there if you want to look for them and can't get the answers on your own. The translation is a little stiff in the beginning, but don't let it put you off. The plot develops steadily and goes from a charming 80s style 7 to 11. I found the plot compelling and interesting, and they eventually wrap up all the core questions of the game. The game apparently had been in development a long, long, time, and the breadth of content is actually quite staggering once you've broken past the surface layers. The game is absolutely worth your time and money. If you like this kind of thing, get it!

_childDocuments_.review: If you really like old school Ys games specifically the sidescroller RPG Ys III: Wanderers from Ys then you'll probably love Astlibra.There are a number of sore spots like the Aguni boss fight in the lava area and a number of really frustrating bosses in the post-game story where they'll throw multiple 150k HP bosses with 1 hit kill lasers but despite all that I ultimately enjoyed the 60+ hours I spent with this game and would highly recommend it to anyone with:1. Someone who enjoys the difficulty of the Ys series2. Someone with a lot of patienceThe post game is excellent btw: it kind of turns into a diablo-like loot game where enemies start to drop Weapon/Armor/Accessory boards which basically makes all equipment viable at the end game by letting you slot in extra bonus stats or skills into everything.Theres one other thing I should mention: I feel like this game is weirdly balanced around an ability in the game called "Berserk" which basically gives you 3x damage but also makes it so if you're hit once you die. And if you do end up using healing items in boss fights, they don't reset if you end up having to restart the fight from a death. So, if you end up playing the game I would suggest going into the game knowing that you're probably going to have to use this ability.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great and its gameplay loop scratches a lot of itches for me. I won't discuss the story as part of this review, but suffice to say it's compelling enough and has a number of interesting twists to it.The bulk of the game is a side-scrolling action RPG, with the combat and enemies giving me strong Castlevania: Symphony of the Night vibes. You're going to amass an arsenal of weaponry, and at a surface level combat is going to devolve into running at the enemies and spamming your attack button while occasionally busting out a special move. That said, there's nuance in the details and in the optimizations, and boss fights will also require at least some adjustment to your strategy if only because of the sheer numbers behind their attacks.The game encourages and rewards exploration. Some very powerful equipment and upgrades are hidden behind a gacha machine that requires "small metals" hidden in chests throughout the game world in order to access. Despite the name, the machine is not random at all, however it always dispenses items in the same order. Your fifth metal will always get you the same item whether that was the fifth metal it was possible to get, or whether it was the 20th you could have possibly gotten. So getting the rewards from it on-pace requires careful exploration of each area. Fortunately, the game is organized into chapters, and between chapters there will be a point where you can backtrack to previously explored areas to find what you missed, so you can always just breeze through the story and come back later if you'd prefer.The game also encourages and rewards grinding, on several fronts. Each chapter has a blacksmith with an assortment of weapons, armor, and shields you can forge. Forging these requires money, but it also requires items that are dropped by enemies in that chapter. So you're encouraged to grind on the associated enemies, get their item drops, come back, and forge the equipment. What do you gain from this aside from stats? Well every weapon has an EXP bar that gradually fills up as you kill enemies with it equipped. Once it fills, you will either unlock a Karon Skill, a special ability that modifies the gameplay in some fashion, or a Magic Crystal, a currency that allows you to equip Karon Skills. Additionally, if the equipment granted a skill, you can equip that skill for free while the item is equipped, and if it gave a crystal, its stats will be enhanced going forward.So you're encouraged to get into this loop of forging equipment, grinding on enemies to master that equipment, going back with your new loot to forge more items, and repeat the cycle until you've mastered all of the available equipment. While doing this you'll also gain EXP for your character which earns level ups which allow you to buff your base stats, as well as "Force", another currency that can be spent on the Growth Board, a system reminiscent of the FFX Sphere Grid where you can spend force to unlock nodes which grant stat boosts and unlock further nodes, with some special nodes even giving you bonus equipment and new special moves to use in combat.Overall, the combat feels satisfying to execute, especially at the endgame, and the gameplay loop and progression systems kept me very engaged for the entire play time. If any of the above sounds fun, you should grab this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Having beaten both the main game and the postgame, I can safely say:  This is the best 2D RPG I've ever played in my life, no contest.  Minus a small stumble with an early boss and chapter 8 stumbling a bit heavily on mechanics and frustration factor, there's so much incredible good packed everywhere around it that it's beyond easy to just say "Yeah that's just That One Level and That One Boss." and leave it at that, and honestly, it comes right before the introduction of one of my favorite mechanics in the game.The game's a great riot, Hard is genuinely challenging, and there are difficulties beyond for those who truly like to push themselves.  Fun, steady gameplay progression, pretty fluid controls, a very fun fighting system, a unique and fun to play around with magic system, a whole grid of powering up to do, a skill system based on mastering weapons...there's genuinely not a single part of this game I don't like.If I had to pick one nitpick...some of the skills are bound to inconvenient buttons, IE float and block both being holding Down on input, and some attacks can get lost in the utter kerfuffle that is mid to late game magic spam with screen spanning attacks from you and the boss alike, making you suddenly die to something you never even saw.  Though, fairly, that's also your fault for filling the screen with clutter before you knew what was coming~.You're doing yourself a favor by picking it up and playing it.  I got it in a bundle with Chained Echoes, and I originally wanted Chained Echoes, knowing nothing about this game.I didn't stop playing it on my Deck until I'd beaten the whole thing.  Genuinely, I love this little game.  Thanks Keizo, looking forward to seeing what's next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid 4 in many ways. The gameplay is quite decent and the story even if it has big lows (Hotel room chapter... xD) ends in a high note in many ways. Some of the mechanics are unexpectedly deep, the soundtrack is quite varied (and has a couple of fully voiced JPOP songs in case that's your preference), the struggle throughout the story is consistent and even if there are difficulty spikes (Was playing on hard, all said), the game can get quite easy if treated as a classic JRPG.Some of the negative points are unclear or weirdly thought puzzles, some maps are unnecessary convoluted, some chapters are quite off-putting, has a lot of forced anime tropes (YMMV), the chest rarity is mostly worthless (Gold chests can have basic items in them), and keys are too expensive in general.This is a love project by someone that really enjoyed the game and were able to release their vision, and it shows in many areas (combat, major plot points, some branching of dialogues and actions are quite impressive, equipment and level system have several rare and even unique approaches). And to the creators I just want to say, thanks for making this game. It was enjoyable and fun.Post DLC: The DLC is fun, an other than a misseable achievement (easy to miss if you are not aware), it has nice content in a Rogue-lite environment going throught the maps of the original game and fighting monsters as the Baker's daughter you heard so much about on the original story.The DLC in general is enjoyable, even if the story is a bit lacking. Being able to use "classes for the character", dressing up the character is fun for a bit, and you can save the world looking like several characters in the story (girls/only... wouldn't have minded dressing up as some guys as well). Boss fights in the arena are challenging but usually you will be able to destroy the strat bosses (unless you avoid exploting magic-caster invulnerability).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing experience. I honestly stumbled across it randomly through the story-rich tag, and damn does it have a story. The gameplay is really fun, the story is well structured and well told, even though you wouldn't think a sidescroller like this would be story heavy, it absolutely is. The game is also HUGE, like 50-80 hours huge depending on how much you want to go for all the armors and weapons. The puzzle interactions are a love letter to old-school RPGs, and the fact that every item is it's own thing (not just a reskin) just adds to the already impressive charm. The character art and level design are beautiful, the music is not only amazing but does a perfect job complementing the different scenes, you'll want to listen to the music both for itself and then again for the nostalgia of the memory of the part in the story that it evokes.If you really want a challenge, play this at the higher difficulty sets, if you just want a great story with tons of attention to detail, play this at a lower difficulty setting.
