_childDocuments_.review: I haven't quite played a game like this since "Death's Gambit" (now "Death's Gambit: Afterlife"), ENDER LILIES, or NieR/NieR:Automata. It seems that the "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews and the absurdly high number (~33%) of all players that got the "True Ending" are for a reason, after all.When I first saw the game, I thought it looked ugly and that the gameplay looked boring. I could not be happier to have been wrong, as it ended up being a fantastic game. The story was great - full of twists and turns, insanely increasing stakes and comedic relief. The gameplay was surprisingly fun - fluid and responsive with lots of different abilities to master and press. There is a giant skill grid called "Grow" in addition to a traditional leveling system and an armor/weapon/shield mastery system that also unlocks various skills ("KARON"). There is blocking, and i-frame dodging ("Backstep") and i-frame magic to avoid damage or even heal.As it turns out, the reason for both the initial off-putting impression and it actually being really good is that it was made by a single developer over the course of 15 years; a mixture of extremely limited resources/budget and it apparently being something he really wanted to make; something he himself wanted to play -- a rarity in a world where games are made by a boardroom decreeing they want yet another seven Assassin's Creed games being made simultaneously.I would not really advise playing on the highest difficulty as all it really does is extend grinding periods, but you can freely change it for the duration of the first chapter so you can easily see for yourself. Hard difficulty is probably the best balance between grinding and being a completionist.An amazing one-man accomplishment, for sure. ありがとうKEIZOさま。本当に。

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing old-school adventure game / RPG's when they were new. Your Final Fantasys, Secret of Mana, Castlevania, Act raiser, Valkyrie Profile etc. There's been a drought of JRPG's lately, and I sorted Steam by the JRPG tag to see what was up. Most of the games were fine, but nothing really piqued my interest or my eye. Then I saw a game with a funny name, terrible graphics and "overwhelmingly positive" for the reviews. I scanned the page, watched the trailer and checked out some images. The old-school progression and side-scrolling combat looked fun, but even an older dude like myself was completely turned off by the graphics.I am so glad that I gave it a chance despite my first impressions. This is one of the best games I have played in the past decade, perhaps even in my lifetime. I put this game up there with other genre-defining titles such as Final Fantasy VII/IX/X, Nier, Nier Automata, Legend of Dragoon and the likes of Squaresoft/Enix's blockbusters. If you are anything like myself and are interested in this game but turned off by the graphics, please give this game a chance. With this out of the way, I'll get into the review proper, taking the most time with the gameplay systems and tackling graphics last.: Gameplay is a 2D side scrolling action game like Castlevania is. The thing here is the game has MANY avenues for character progression, with some of the options being incredibly interesting and different from what the industry has done previously. These features heavily influence the aforementioned 2D side scrolling action combat. You have an equipment system where nearly every piece of equipment in the game has a skill which you need to earn enough EXP to unlock (Think Final Fantasy IX). These range from simple stat boosts to straight-up entirely new mechanics that you will weave into your gameplay loop.You have a "scale" system, where you have to put in items you collect on your adventure (Potions, food items, materials, monster drops, etc) to gain bonus stats. Each item has a weight value attached to it, and your goal is to balance these sets of scales according to the benefits the item in question brings and the weight it has attached to it. This causes a lot of thought based on what stats you value and how to make them work in the confines of the weight attached to them.And finally you have "possession" skills that rely on a meter you fill up with active combat attacks. These skills are varied, you can swap them out for other skills, and using them makes you invincible for a short period upon activation. These skills range from buffs, to attacks, to utility and more.What makes this game such a masterpiece is how all of these systems work together to form such a fluid combat system that has an immense amount of depth and fluidity. You learn the basics in the first 5-10 hours of gameplay, and you're constantly having new tools available to the player as you progress but nothing makes anything else obsolete. They just give you more options and more tools to mix up the flow of combat by weaving these options together. Most of these tools have either cool downs/resource bar requirements to work and how you play the game will drastically change depending on how aggressive you want to be in encounters. You COULD run it, hit the boss a few times and run out and block, or you could mix up Possession skills for invincibility to block a huge boss attack, be aggressive, block a few attacks with your shield - but now your block gauge is gone and you have no meter for Posession skills, so you backslide for the iframes THROUGH a boss attack to get enough meter and shield gauge to continue the flow of combat.I could honestly go on and on about simple things, such as how the hitstop slows combat down enough so that you can see the insane amount of action on the screen at once so you can make a decision that would not be afforded to you if you were playing passive and NOT slowing down the combat with the hitstop. It is so fluid and masterfully executed that I'm beyond impressed that a single guy managed to pull off what I consider to be one of the best combat systems I have ever played in a game. The combat is as intricate as you want it to be. The better you, as the player, will determine how aggressive and relentless you will be. - The story is excellent. I wasn't expecting much, but I was honestly really impressed with what I got. It started out as a simple story with some intrigue, light-hearted themes with some melancholy thrown in. As you continue to play the game the world, its characters and its plot opens up and becomes more and more intriguing with the stakes being raised through your action. I can't go too in depth without spoiling the game, but I will say that this game can blend future-dystopian themes with gods, folklore, demons and mechs. What's amazing here is how Mr Keizo has let these themes be disjointing when they need to be to suit the story, and seamless and fluid when that is important to the story. Nothing touched on in this story is pretentious, and the story itself is pretty simple as far as a story involving time travel can go. But it's humbling, it's comforting and while it doesn't reach the insane heights' something like NIER does, it's a competent and compelling story in its own right. You end up caring for the characters, the world and the story. The only issue is some rough translation work that can make some of the script come across as a little "stiff" at times, but it's not too intrusive to take away from the experience. - The music is fantastic. There's your standard fantasy violin tracks, piano pieces and it all is really competent and makes the world feel alive. When the story needs it, it even has modern tracks like some electronic with vocals that honestly sounds wonderful. I felt like each piece fit the location really well, with the exception to a couple tracks that honestly really did not fit their encounters. JRock when fighting a fiery demon god? I can dig it but it just didn't really fit and kind of took me out of that fight. - And here's what I saved for last, and with good reason. Out of all the cons I have for the game (Some area design from a gameplay standpoint, enemy placement, enemy design from a gameplay standpoint) graphics are objectively pretty poor. The developer, Mr Kezio, was virtually a one-man team and did what he could with what he had. The terrain is especially jarring, but when you take into account the fact it was one man working on this I feel like it's forgivable. I would argue that perhaps due to the limitations on the graphics that the other systems were allowed to be so fleshed-out and shine like they do. The graphics ended up appealing to me after a while, perhaps Stockholm syndrome. The quality improved a lot as the game went on, which I have to assume was due to the game being a 14-year passion project by a lone guy. If anybody is going to be turned off from the game, I have to imagine this is where it will be. I hope you will overlook them, as the game itself is a complete masterpiece, but I understand if you cannot. - This is perhaps one of the best, most fluid and cohesive games I have ever played in my life. The gameplay is unbelievably well executed and imagined, and the story and the supporting systems add a level of depth and versatility that is refreshing and honestly startling given how this was made by one guy. This game is a masterpiece and deserves your attention. I could go on, but character limits and all.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute masterpiece of an experience. One of the rare times where the phrase "greater than the sum of its parts" is not only applicable, but is a gross understatement. I completed all achievements in 65 hours and I was very surprised at how much content this unassuming indie title has for you. The basic premise is that it is a 2D JRPG "Metroidvania" with fast and smooth combat. When I say "Metroidvania", I don't mean Symphony of the Night, where it is one (two) giant map. This is more like Order of Ecclesia, where there are several smaller maps that aren't physically connected. The visuals are both great and also lacking. The sprites are all wonderful, though I wish the animations had more frames. In the middle of combat you don't notice the frames of animation that the sprites have in the slightest and everything moves fluidly as the actual FPS is stable. The biggest complaint I have visually are some of the background and foreground environment sprites have clear lines so you can tell exactly how it is all tiled together. Again, in the heat of combat you will not notice it at all. That being said, everything looks cohesive and nothing ever seems like it was designed and created for another project and just pasted into the game without care. The combat is awesome. It is fast and simple on the surface but also has depth to it. You will have a bad time if you are just mashing the attack button and not much else. You must utilize the offensive and defensive skills you learn along the way. Possession skills are great and eventually become very overpowered once you master how to fight. It becomes so fun once you get into the groove of it all that you will want to take the time to max out the exp on all of the weapons, shields, and armor... and it won't feel like a chore at all. The RPG mechanics for leveling stats, crafting, weapons, armor, shields, Karon magic, the Force board, Possession skills, Libra system, Item boards, and enhancing your equipment keeps you busy and you always feel like you're making progress and improving. Each aspect is straightforward on its own and in conjunction with the other systems forms a tight web of character progression not seen often enough. This game respects your time in ways most others in the JRPG/RPG realm fail to by having several ways to respec almost at any time. There are tons of free places to do it in town or at mokyun shops. From shops you can buy respec potions so you can do it anywhere. It is a nice touch. The story is very JRPG but man did I care about it. I didn't really expect that going into it based on the demo and screenshots of the game, as well as other reviews that suggested it was all over the place and what not. I didn't think so at all. I don't normally care about story too much as a lot of times it appears to be just a means to an end, kind of thought up on the spot to justify mechanics of the game, but that isn't the case here. I was very invested in the goings on of everyone. Almost brought to tears, empty pit in my chest levels of invested in the story. The music is done by a bunch of different artists and it is basically all wonderful. There was some random rap song in one optional room I didn't care for. On the other hand, the third area music was done by the legendary S.S.H. and it shreds. Other styles are present as well and it really fits so much better than you would think. I'm going to be listening to a few of these tracks for a very long time down the road. Some things that you need to do to progress the game aren't totally communicated well to you, though that is most likely due to the translation. If you pay attention and don't skip cutscenes or conversation, you'll probably be able to figure out what you need to do 90% of the time. There were a couple spots where what was needed seemed sort of obtuse and I didn't really seem to understand how I was supposed to glean what to do from the story or conversations with NPCs or environmental clues. Though when you bring up the menu it will give you direction on what you're supposed to be doing overall, but again, a couple times that wasn't any help at all. Trust me when i say this game is great. I don't ever write reviews. I am sacrificing sleep to write this because I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. This is much better than so many AAA big budget RPGs and it was just a labor of love from one guy. That passion is palpable through out the entirety of this game. This is a steal at full price, if it ever goes on sale, do no hesitate to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: "Do not forget.You are taking another's treasure when protecting your own.If the scale of destiny favors a soul, it destroys the fate of another.Will you change this balance, or cast your eyes aside?Is it true that your choices bore no responsibility?Is it true that you committed no crimes?"Genuinely the only game akin to Castlevania: Symphony of the Night to ever capture my lasting interest the way that SotN did, thus far.It's a lot of elements from SotN and Aria of Sorrow, as well as Odin Sphere ad Dungeon Fighter Online, with a lot of very old Final Fantasy classic story vibes for the early stretch. That is, before it takes a turn into some surprisingly good stuff - dialogue can be a bit much tonally at times, a misplaced horny joke here and there, but the story's actually gripped me and kept me attentive even after 20 hours which is a feat for a game like this!PLEASE support this game. _childDocuments_.review: If you like simple side-scrolling action RPGs like the older Ys titles or Metroidvanias this will be worth playing.  But the more important dive begins with the following questions: Do you like systems in your game?  How about systems within your systems?  How about external systems that allocate into the previous systems, but then allow you to unlock additional systems?!  This game is like a Billy Mays ad where every time you think you figured it out, there's a NEW system that only ADDS to the old, without taking anything away.  This game can be as simple or complicated as you desire, but the complexity is a dream for players who enjoy that kinda' thing.  The story is great, and Nier fans will appreciate some of the seemingly convoluted aspects contained.  Are their flaws?  Plenty.  But when you scroll through the credits in under two minutes you know each of those people put a great deal of care into how the game was delivered.  At worst, you discount the game because "there's other games like it" out there, other 2D Metroidvania-esque whatevers and they might play better.  But at best, you will play the game and enjoy it for what it is.  It was a 110 hour journey for me on the "Hell" difficulty to 100% (I go slow).  I hope others can get a fraction of that time to just give it a try.

The story is fairly minimal (at least as far as chapter 4, where I'm currently at), but it is getting somewhat interesting. For anyone who is looking for a game with great combat/upgrade mechanics, but hates the 'slog' of typical JRPG stories, you can completely skip all dialogue as far as I'm aware and just keeping going with the bits you enjoy. I booted it up out of boredom a few days after getting it and didn't put it down for 9 hours in my first session. I got this game on sale, but I do believe it actually is worth it at full price.

It felt a bit grindy on Hard (like, run through the areas a couple extra times killing enemies to max out equipment you found, since they level up too) but probably less so on Normal and below, but I liked grinding to see what every maxed out ability or item does. _childDocuments_.review: Well, I write this review 125 hrs. into the game, this is certainly a hidden gem, you can tell by looking up info about it, there´s barely anything. It fully reminded me of Symphony of the Night, (if you needed some reference).Collect weapons, armor, accessories, unlock skills, try different builds with the Karon system; melee, "range", magic builds, it´s also really easy to respec your character (and free). _childDocuments_.review: Play on "Difficult"Aslibra's heavy usage of stock assets and sprite tweening make it one of the ugliest games I've set my eyes upon, and yet, Keizo's choice of music as well as great gameplay make it a must buy, the moment to moment action and customization makes it one of the most engaging games I've played in a while.Now, the game is difficult and expects you to learn all of it's mechanics (which are not made entirely clear thanks to the translation) as you advance, chapter after chapter you'll stumble upon a new wall that may make you rage quit, and the schizophrenic usage of save points will make you curse the developer's lineage each time you die after a bossfight. That being said, not once did I feel that my situation was hopeless, Astlibra lets you respec your character freely and experimenting with builds is heavily encouraged and necessary for unlocking new abilities, however, this makes the game a grind if you have no idea what to look for.It's kino, get it now

_childDocuments_.review: ASTLIBRA is an absolute gem of a game. Its an action JRPG/platformer with all of its standard fare, but with the added bonus of everything being really well done, having good gameplay mechanics, an amazing soundtrack, and a fantastic story to keep you immersed in the game.The game is an action JRPG, so nothing turn-based about the gameplay. The action is smooth and really fine-tuned, at least in my opinion, and that becomes especially apparent as you grind and raise your stats. One part of the game has some elements in it that are added to the existing game later on and it opens up the possibilities for all manner of grinding and stat min-maxing. The weapons handle different and weight will determine how fast or slow you go with a weapon based on what type of weapon it is (some weapons are slower than others, and some are really fast). Weapon range and handling also play a factor in how well a fight goes. On top of this, there is a growth tree that can up you stats and give you summoning skills that are really helpful through out the game (and some are so helpful that they are on par with the most powerful summons you can obtain). On top of all of that, there is the Libra system where you can put items on a scale that gives you even more stats or resistances and even allow for more money/force (used in the growth tree)/experience gain. Balancing it perfectly allows you to get the stat boosts and such from both sides of the scale without them being diminished on one side versus the other. The weapons, armors, and shields are all items that you can play with and level which will net you either some new abilities that you can select later or magic crystals that will allow you to equip said abilities if you are not using the item in question. If you equip the item with an ability, you can choose to equip that ability with no extra cost to your magic crystal pool, which is a great way to maximize your usage of abilities to their fullest. Accessories do not come with any leveling mechanic so they are static (at least until the latter half of the game). There is also a new customization mechanic later in the game that will enhance weapons, armors, shields, and accessories that can not only up the stats of everything, but allow for changes to abilities or adding new stats, which was a interesting answer to the usual "I've grinded all the stuff, now what?" question and even attachments that can be added to them (although most of it comes with RNG, so there is a reason to continue grinding to get the best stuff). The story itself is absolutely wonderful, well written, and executed so well done that it ties up all manner of loop-holes very well, including ones that you didn't even know it had (or forgot about which is a phenomenal surprise when you realize some things later on or remember certain characters). It has its tense moments, which are assisted by the gameplay obviously, its funny moments, its sad moments, and some of the twists you don't completely see coming either. It does well in foreshadowing some events and even some inconsequential story pieces end up showing up when you least expect it, There are some things that are predictable and, again, this is a JRPG so it has many of the staples embedded in the story, but it works in its favor rather than to its determent, or at least I think so. Its been a while since I've played another game as enjoyable as this one. I absolutely recommend this game to anyone looking for a good JRPG to enjoy your time with that has the right amount of gameplay mechanics, story, and overall enjoyment that can be found in ASTLIBRA. I hope to see more games from this developer that are as fun and enjoyable as this game was.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra's odd, but I'll say that it never once bored me.Its controls are pretty nice, its music is great, its progression is surprisingly fantastic with all the systems it uses, it has a large amount of content that only get better the further in I got, and despite a bit of messiness I think a lot of people can find worth in the narrative.All of these things alone are enough for me to recommend the game but let's get a bit more detailed.The combat's pretty simple but man is it fun, there's a real nice amount of enemy variety, a lot of the larger bosses are pretty fun to get through, and honestly my biggest complaints would be that you can become too powerful for your own good.On top of this is the magic system, full of legitimately useful and powerful spells for all kinds of occasions, and the way magic works is great.MP or as it's known as ST, builds up as you hit targets, so it promotes aggression instead of just sitting in the backline.There's tons of spells to unlock as you go through the game, and while I may have been basic with what I actually used, there's a lot of really cool ones to use.There's tons of worthwhile progression, from a basic level up system where you individually increase your stats, equipment to provide new passives that you can learn and use permanently so long as you have the resource to equip it.A MASSIVE growth tree that lets you get loot, character upgrades and additional permenant stats via a secondary form of EXP, and even more progression in the post-game, which lets you become stupidly overpowered.The best part about these systems is that it's all very easy to respec into whatever you want, as the game will allow you to mix and match whatever passives you want, when you want, and also change your level up stat allocations at several points, including when you level up.It also incentivises grabbing every single piece of equipment you can get your hands on, to learn even more abilities that'll make you even more busted, it's just a brilliantly crafted system.The game also never lets you miss out on content, while this isn't a metroidvania, it is possible to gloss over nice pieces of equipment/upgrades here and there, not to mention superbosses, so being given to option to go back to prior areas in-between chapters is legitimately appreciated.Let me be clear and say that the game will NEVER, let you miss out of items, with there being a few exceptions to gain an item that'll help stop a certain optional grind much, MUCH later into the game.To be a bit more negative, the quality of the game is a bit, "uneven", not bad, just off.Graphically I think it's apparent that Astlibra is probably a tier below most games you'll play, and to go along with that its art can be a bit inconsistent, using a mix of custom artwork of varying artstyles and slightly animated jpegs.It's iffy, and when it comes to enemy design I feel it can be problematic, as some telegraphs can feel a bit cheap with how poorly animated/displayed things can get.To its credit though, I feel the game despite how graphically poor it might be, never wanted to be a bore, as the backgrounds are decently layered, bigger entities are given the graphical quality they should receive and there is genuine effort put into trying to make the background/world feel less still than it could've been.Regarding the level design, it's kinda bad.It feels very "game-y", with tons of wall clipping, tiny blocks for platforms, weird scrolling for some areas, I wouldn't call it too well designed.What really doesn't help is how backtracky the game can become at points in the main story, as sometimes it just feels like it's wasting your time.But it's also not the biggest selling point here, as for the most part you're just going to be mowing down enemies as you get from point A to point B.Commenting further on these negative aspects, I will say that it feels like KEIZO did a better job designing the later areas in the game instead of the early ones, maybe it's just due to a lack of experience at the time of developing some of these levels, but it's most notable during the early parts of the game, which I feel can help sour expectations.One thing I won't necessarily defend though is an optional grind at the end of the game, as while there are methods to skip it throughout the game, if you miss these items, you may just find yourself mindlessly grinding enemies until you get the drops you need for some additional content, just a very odd choice.As advertised, it's a sidestory. While it does hint at more content to come, its story is pretty basic and non-essential, and it's gameplay is still as good as it ever was.The new progression systems work well, death has some fun consequences instead of just sending you back to your last save, but its biggest problem is that as a roguelite, it just doesn't have enough variety. You see all there is to see on the first layer and from there you just kinda go through the motions. The new bosses aren't interesting enough, especially with how strong you can get, and there's no new enemies at all.Perfectly harmless if you really want more once you finish the game but easily skipped if you're satisfied with what you got or didn't like the few rogue parts the game had in the base game.I think a second pair of eyes during development could've fixed a lot of my issues, but man this was still so much fun to play through, it feels nice playing something that feels like someone knew what players actually wanted.Very easy to recommend, with or without a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game expecting a solid indie RPG, got a 60-100 hour game with a great story, characters, OST, and several neat ways of leveling and improving your character. Gameplay is solid, and feels great after you get used to it and pick up some upgrades.Play on Impossible difficulty if you hate yourself but also want pure satisfaction. Was 100hrs for me since I died a lot and had to retry boss fights plenty of times, but easier difficulties should give you at minimum 50 hrs. Playtime in the in-game save file doesn't keep the time if you died and didn't save, and my final time in-game was about 45 hours. There's a mild amount of jank, and some things like enemy projectile visibility could be better, but I also played on the mode where literally everything kills you in 1-2 hits, so might not be as problematic on lower difficulties. If you do play on Impossible:  the Berserk and Cicada Shell Karon Skills are your friends.Seriously, this game was not even on my radar and is now my biggest candidate for GOTY 2022. The game might not look like it, but $25 is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ STEAL for how much content you get. One of the biggest, most impressive indies I've ever played, and you can really tell this was KEIZO's dream game with the amount of passion put into it. Play this game ASAP, you will not regret it.Also, when the credits roll:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. I've spent over a 100 hours playing this.... so this should be a good indicator of how much I like this. The combat is great and I love how every weapon gets to be useful. Some may not fit your play style, but there are plenty to choose from. Daggers, clubs, swords, shields, great swords, spears, mage staffs, bows, crossbows, etc. Some weapons have different element types, some are faster, so the weapon with the highest attack power is not always the best.There are lots of different skills to find which basically work as passives, about 10-12 different special moves, and a bunch of magic spells. Late game you unlock additional gems that can completely modify the original skills and magic spells. The game has a system which allows you to combine items into new items. The ingredients are mostly drops from monsters, which makes for a far better system than endlessly grinding for more money to get better equipment. The boss fights are large and enjoyable. Killing one of the major bosses actually feels meaningful here and serves to move the story along. If you want to find every item in the game, some back tracking will be needed but you can do so at any point in the game. Nothing that you can miss and lose out on permanently. A few minor things aren't translated too well, but its pretty much limited to the skill descriptions and it looks like the developers are patching it. You shouldn't let that stop you from enjoying an otherwise great game. I consider it to be a bargain at the $25 asking price, especially considering the amount of enjoyment I got from it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best RPGs I've played in a long time. The animation is charming (if you grew up with 16-32 bit sprites), some catchy songs, engaging game play loop and likeable characters. Game plays a lot like Castlevania Aria/Dawn of Sorrow but instead of farming for souls, you will be grinding for monster parts and to level up your gear; thankfully the drop rates are quite generous. People have mentioned translation issues, I did not encounter any (played in 2024). Purchased on sale but would have happily paid full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Very frantic and engaging combat. Only on the 3rd chapter but it's pretty good.Edit: Holy &^$#... _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; This game has a fake level up system. Nuff said.First 20 hours are alright, then the game takes a HUGE dive downwards in quality. Also QA is blatantly missing in some sections.Hard to recommend, not worth the price tag as the game is weighed down by insanely bad game design decisions. Off-screen enemies with a map-wide full heal or an attack that sets you at 1 hp every 3 seconds, bosses with instakill attacks you can't see coming until you read a guide, RNG based drops that took me literally 5 hours to drop with cheated max luck stat, after which you of course get pushed out of the screen boundaries and all the drops despawn, so you have to do it all over again, Don't know what plot twists the others are talking about, I'm afraid if you've read a book before you won't get surprised by anything, the writing is decent yet predictable. Game is kinda fun but incredibly frustratingly so and not because of good game design or difficulty balancing.P.S.: Yeah, there are caps on the effectiveness of your statpoints per level. You can allocate 1 point per level into each stat, that gives you +5 to that stat. The next gives you +3, then +1, then 0. That is absolutely insane design. Square peg goes into square hole.

_childDocuments_.review: Well this was something else.- The graphics look generally terrible, barring a few exceptions like the beautiful plains area.- The translation of some stuff is at once hilarious and hopelessly confusing. You'll have no choice but to test out or look up what some abilities or perks do to because many descriptions make no sense- It's got its good moments but overall the story is convoluted, anime trope-filled nonsense - complete with the weird pervy sexual innuendos and physics-defying bitties. I burst out laughing the first time i met a certain godess with her melons individually flopping around in every direction.So why the positive review? - The combat is oh so satisfying. Hits have a short pause to them so you have that comfortable microsecond to plan your next attack, most weapons feel nice, and there's many options for solid builds. - There is a TON of content. I put 70 hours into with a "try to be decently thorough" approach, without overdoing it. There's a ton of secrets to find, megabosses, that kind of thing.- The difficulty felt just right. I did a spot of light grinding here and there to top off some weapon masteries but that was it. I minimised fast travel so that the grinding felt organic.  - The progress feels great. Lots of secrets to find, weapons to unlock, and skills to master. There's many ways you can tweak your character and by the end I felt deliciously powerful without it being too easy. In the end if you want a fun side-scroller RPG with outstanding gameplay, this is it. Show this solo dev some support; I look forward to their next project
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the Flash-era graphics fool you, this is one solid game. I've put 100+ hours into it and there's still a little bit more to go. One could call this "The Return of the King Endings: The Game," with all the psych-out conclusions. Just when you think you're done, BAM, more to do. Action is fast-paced and responsive, with satisfying melee and magic combat. Ranged combat is lacking, but still works for what it is. Story starts out convoluted, gradually clearing up, only for it to get wacky by the end, like any good anime series. Overall, if you like action RPG's with a deep story, even deeper play mechanics, don't mind the perviness that comes from some anime, I assure you this game is totally worth your time. I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: You start with a stick, beating slimes and soon are fighting dragons and other epic creatures, a slow and intense, not really boring grind to reach godhood levels, seeing big numbers popping over and over as you slash or explode your enemies.Developed by a single person in the span of about 15 years, Astlibra Revision is an enhanced version of Astlibra proof of life. It adds a new chapter - and has new art by Shigatake, making it closer to almost being a Vanillaware title.The plot is as heavy as any RPGs and visual novels, making it an interesting and important point. Hell, so many good time travel stories spawned since its initial development that I feel a little burnt out by them, but it's always cool and exciting to see.Finding hidden equipment, learning new mechanics and plot details, challenging bosses you missed before, having a huge variety of equipment and customization that make progression extremely fun.And the soundtrack is really cool as well, mixing many genres and a lot of good and memorable Vocaloid songs. They are memorable, and I still listen to them from time to time.Chapter four was the lowest point for me, mostly due to story-related reasons. Chapter 3 and everything else gets better as you go, plus the post-game teaches you new mechanics with a lot of content, making it worth your time with a rewarding and fulfilling new ending.This game is an inspiring indie achievement and I'm glad to have played it. Might play the DLC someday.Pumpkin Hill Part II -
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels amazing to play, like a true spiritual successor to Vanillaware's sidescroller action RPGs (particularly Muramasa Rebirth and Odin Sphere Leifthrasir). Videos don't capture how good the combat feels when you're actually playing it, but the demo gives you a sample of midgame-level combat so you can try for yourself. Progression is on point - the game does a great job of gradually doling out new abilities and mechanics over the course of the game.It also has a really good soundtrack that goes hard right from the start, when you're whacking slimes with a literal stick and don't have any magical abilities (yet, you get your first one almost immediately which lets you summon a small fire-breathing dragon).Even at full price, this game is honestly a steal for the quality and quantity of content that you get. It took me ~50 hours to 100% the game on Hard difficulty, and unlike most JRPGs I didn't feel like there was much padding. The later parts of the story start reusing some content, but it's done in a way that doesn't feel lazy.The biggest downside is that the graphics and animations can look kind of janky, but you get used to it pretty quickly, and some locales and enemy designs do look legitimately good.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: I am very picky about games under the "metroidvania" genre and the "JRPG" genre. Both, if done well, are some of my favorite types of games. When I saw this, I figured I had to give it a try. This has turned out to be the biggest hidden gem I have ever found, and may in fact be my favorite indie game that I have ever found on Steam. The battle mechanics, the story the style, the bosses, the spells, the skills...all of these were done so well and were so well-polished. There is no doubt that this was not a typical cookie-cutter indie game release. This was a passion project. 10/10. It has tons of gameplay, with a length that well exceeds 70 hours (if you want it to with post script) and will have you hooked. Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a pleasant surprise. I tried the demo on a whim, and enjoyed it so much I bought the full game as soon as it released. The game was much lengthier than I expected it to be, and I spent a lot of time playing it; I initially bought it to tide me over until Persona 5 Royal hit Steam, but I ended up wanting to completely finishing the game even after it released. I obtained all of the achievements in around 80 hours, playing in Hard (or Difficult) mode, and even want to go through the game again on Hell mode.There are some flaws, and the game could use a touch-up and polishing on the clarity of the translations, but the overall experience is great. The main story is interesting enough and will keep you wanting to progress more. The combat is addicting enough to just blast enemies to level up and/or farm materials and not feel like a chore most of the time. Boss fights can get pretty tense and even some normal enemies will keep you on your toes since there are a few jank hitboxes. There's a wide variety of equipment and skills to extract from said equipment to equip. The music is top-notch in most sections, even if a bit odd sometimes. There's even Vocaloid songs, surprisingly. I wish there was a way to get the OST or listen to it outside of the game somehow.Highly recommend this game if you are interested in 2D side-scrolling Action RPGs similar to Castlevania and others of the same vein. The current asking price of $25 feels like a great deal, although I got it for 10% off from the launch discount. Heck, just try the demo. You can play the entirety of the first chapter and a small sample of mid-game combat which will help you decide.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite the surprise for a metroidvania type.  Very well crafted and you can tell the developers put in a lot of time into this game.  The music is fantastic and really brings in the atmosphere.  The subtle sound effects are placed in both the background and in conversations which is a nice touch.  Graphics are collages and conglomerates of realistic photos.  Most of the time they work beautifully but there are times where the transitions are rough around the edges.  The combat is smooth and gives much freedom for personal player style.  The only down side really is the game starts a little slow in story but every chapter really draws in an immersive hook.  Overall, there are very few metroidvania's out there that can compete with this one.  Astlibra is definitively worth buying even without a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I have little experience in the Metriodvania category, the 2.5D sidescroller action rpg niche thing. The only other game that I've play similar is Symphony of the Night, which I played until the disc cracked. And even still, I played this game for days straight, got 100%, and am already waiting on the sequel. It brought me back to the younger days, on summer break, pushing Alucard to beat "luck-mode" with my younger brother on the sofa beside.To start, the game is as hard or as easy as you want it to be, with 6 (I think) different difficulties. I played through on "hard" - once I got to about 75% completion though I wish I had selected one difficulty higher. The story was solid. It did get somewhat convoluted, but that happens with JRPGS, some of the translations could be better, but the majority of the dialogue was good. The combat is fast paced and fun. The skills and magic system are easy to use and critical in your success. Master weapons to learn new skills, unlock new magic through growth. There is a great selection of weapon types and styles, and in the back third or so of the game you can make even your starter gear as strong as the end game stuff. What I miss in the newer RPGs I play is farming - THE GRIND. Astlibra doesn't require you to dump HOURS into powering up your character, but if there's an empty bar that needs to be filled.... I'm gonna fill it. A huge plus for me was the multi-layered leveling system: You earn experience, you earn a spendable growth currency, and even weapon exp. In the back half of the game you can also find supplements to your gear that further enhance your stats and skills. I will eventually replay this. I will need to be in the mood to invest the time though, like SoTN it is an investment to clear completely.I thoroughly enjoyed the time I spent on Astlibra Revision. I would recommend this game to any who are a fan of the genre, and even to those that haven't dip their toes in the water since Konami was king. These are the games the AAA studios should be pushing.
_childDocuments_.name: ASTLIBRA Revision

_childDocuments_.review: This game may look janky and ugly on paper, but its true potential is unlocked once you actually start playing. _childDocuments_.review: Wow!!! Amazing! Spectacular! Beautiful! Those are the words that comes through my mind while and after playing this great game! _childDocuments_.review: An indie masterpiece that blew my mind and transported me to another world. Not since the likes of Cave Story and Soul Blazer has a game surprised me by its depth of story and mechanics. This is one of the only games I have ever 100%ed and it's due to the innate urge to see everything Astlibra Revision has to offer. The creator, KEIZO, has created a side scrolling action RPG that expands its mechanics throughout its episodic structure. Many reviews I read and watched before playing sounded opaque about details, but were lavish with general praise, and this review will be no different. Astlibra's story structure reminds me of Yoko Taro titles, where the overall objective and even plot of the game may shift several times during the story through a variety of viewpoints and "endings".  This game has a plot that kept me guessing and continually thrown off by where it goes. Astlibra, enters the same level of game plot pantheon as: Chrono Trigger, 13 Sentinels, and Nier Automata.

_childDocuments_.review: Good story. Bad gameplay.  That sums up Astlibra Revision.  I wish I could give a neutral score.The combat is slow and clunky and is more an exercise in patience than skill.  The enemies have so much health that it just takes forever to kill them and damage you take is most likely to happen due to lack of focus during the repetitive slashing at them rather than any challenge avoiding their highly telegraphed attacks.On the plus side, the story's creative and engrossing.  I don't want to give anything away, but I do ultimately think this game is worth playing but do it on easy mode.  Hard mode doesn't make it any harder, really.  Just tedious beyond belief.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the entire game(+dlc) with achivements i think this game deserves a review.The gameplay is fun from fighting enemies melee or with magic  to getting stronger in many different ways likelvl up, the grow board, stat cards etc.The music fits pretty much every time so i didn´t even know that most of it is free music.The graphics are quite beautiful from the background to the enemy disigns. The enemies moving around somewhat reminded me of that one lovecraftian roguelike game where every part of the monsters kept moving on its own which i found funny.The story surprised me a lot. Sometimes i was already expecting something which was mostly correct and sometimes it took a turn i didn´t see comming. After talking about the good things of the game it´s now time to talk about the bad ones with some spoilers in it.Since i played on hell until act 5 and then replayed on impossible until the end i can say if you just want to enjoy the game play hard max and if you want a challenge hell. Impossible is for people that really know the skills necessary to survive or in my case find a way.The first boss that was just unfair was meldine in act4. She shoots earth spikes at you which can be blocked no problem BUT if the spikes hit the ground next to you( because that magic is sprayed around) it creates earth magic that cannot be blocked.Unless you invest some points in healt and def you will insta die. The same boss fight becomes easy in the postscript because you can stay in the air where it doesn´t matter if it hits the ground. The second boss that is the reason you could never no death speedrun this game is the fake demon lord(demon summoner or something). He summons two enemies after some time up to six i think which includes bosses. And they are not just as strong as they were in the act you played in nooooo they have hitpoints like act 5.Just evil and i didn´t know you can buy the mokyu dolls postscript so i wanted to save all of them. Luckily he teleported into the ground/stairs where he did nothing and i just crossbowed him to death.Overall if you can´t defeat a boss just put all points into magic and use double crossbow unless its a 3:1 bossfight which happens in act8 and post act 8 twice(and the greater demon when you don´t have karons skills). One thing that felt like a missed opportunity was the secret marionette boss and the postscript marionette fight where if you fought it before Karon and Gau could make remarks on Shiro getting almost naked again. Since Shiro is the only character that  in postscript never regains her past memories for some reason it would make sense that it surprises her again.Another problem that i had with the game is that once you got all the loot out of gold and silver chests they only drop keymould B. Why? I can get stat cards out of the cheapest chests but the rare chests only drop moulds? That took all the excitement out whenever i saw them. Now in postscript the crossbow exploit and magic overall becomes almost negligent since you can buff weapons and armor but weapons only give atk not mag dmg.So i have a 30+weapon with over 2000atk(4000+ with everything) but only 1500 magic. All the skills in the maingame look cool but are really weak unless its a situation where it really hits like a truck.(phoenix for dmg and sylph and berserk for melee buff)The enemies that get controled by geas get a slightly different attack pattern which i found cool. Sadly after act 4 post they don´t have any new attacks which i found dissapointing.Last the achivements:the only two achivements that are pure evil and kaizo should be ashamed of it is the hit 200000 times and walk 50000 steps. When i finished the game i was at around 31k steps and 141k hits. So i had to put a fork in my keyboard to walk against a wall for 45min and spend another hour on the training stones. That was zero fun in a game that entertained me the entire time. Just reduce it by 50000hits and if possible it should be distance instead of steps since most people would move with air dash.Now to Gaiden(dlc)Gameplay wise it does so much better than the main game. The magic is strong, you can get stat cards out of all chests, the growth at the end where you can spend infinitly gives five times more statpoints etc. One of the biggest problems why i didn´t play with the berserk skill was the fact that enemies can spawn right at the door instakilling you. Why not make every a spawnfree zone of 1 1/2 character sprites to the left and right of the entrance?Also even in the last stratum no new enemy got introduced (the final boss not included in this) which i think is a lost opportunity. Another point i just remember is how after every run the game reminds you how you can spend force to grow....i got the message the first time why does it appear over and over again? Same goes for the Arena after every stratum that gets finished. The story in Gaiden makes no real sence in the main timeline as far as i can see. Maybe the first gameplayloop where you´re a ghost could be when the demons attacked the city but the hero was never trapped in the cave of mist(which kai apparently did to stop him from using the scales but in the main story he helps the hero getting into the future at that time sooo not really?).Also when you kill the hero becoming the new master of the scales looking at the main story where kuro kept ownership of the shield of laia after time rewinding and so on  it makes no sense in the timeline. The timeline when the goddess Lieselotte appears can be considered after the main game since the entire idea is to help Al Khasim revive Astarea but again at this point the Hero and Karon should freak out that the scales are just gone.The ending itself gives me mixed feelings kind of negating the sacrifice that Astarea made and not really making sence why the God of Life and Death calls the Bakers daughter the secret weapon that the gods planned for all along but at the same time giving a happy ending( For the end scene kaizo could have made a sleeping astarea dragon animation but whatever).Overall it´s a must play for fans of this genre and i hope the sequel baiting at the end of Gaiden will result in another dlc at least and a new game with a more planned out story than gaiden at best.Edit:Just remembered a few things. Shiro staying alive after chapter 5 is optional so i guess it makes sense that she never remembered her past life.

_childDocuments_.review: Completely blown away by this game. Utterly enraptured. I didn't want it to end. Combat was always an absolute blast. Well-tuned difficulty aligned perfectly with an expected and gratifying grind. Constant twists in the story to match equally compelling character growth systems. I want to call this _THE_ sidescroller RPG experience. Thank you KEIZO for a game I'll never forget. ---Getting into this game was so fascinating for me. ASTLIBRA evokes an air of nostalgia surrounding perhaps a respected sleeper PC-98 game, one that you've only ever seen on the periphery of game lists. A game always just out of reach but always lauded whenever mentioned... a remake of a game for another day, maybe. The art, animation, and overall design experience lend themselves  well to this feeling, as if you're playing something utterly classic and uncannily familiar. This makes ASTLIBRA feel like a triumphal love-letter to the genre, obfuscating itself as a hidden lodestone. As you play you'll learn it sets a new mark, surpassing expectations set by its forebears.  Gameplay was consistently engaging and rewarding. Always new techniques to try out after grinding for mastery and equips through each new zone, culminating in zany, creative abilities and combos that allow for a surprising range of builds. I recommend playing on at least Hard, since the grind makes itself worthwhile without becoming overbearing. There are some difficulty spikes around bosses-- some early ones being absolute HP sponges-- but as you experiment with your various options and find patterns you start to see how the game is really played. Hint: Possession skills give i-frames. I said earlier that the story is compelling- and it is, if you have a ounce of soul- but take this with a grain of salt... as seasoning, rather than skepticism. The translation  pretty hard, yeah, especially at first. The vast majority of the game is extremely well translated at this point, but there are still some moments with typos, syntax, or strange idioms that stand out. Personally, this is a pinch of that aforementioned salt: just part of the experience of doujin/fan translated media, lending strongly to ASTLIBRA's authentic feeling. The charming episodic openers make it clear that this game was formed chapter by chapter in its original doujin publishing online and make for excellent stylistic bookends. ASTLIBRA retains a lot of sentiment this same way through its storytelling: narratives and plot spectacle shenanigans that wouldn't be out of place in a LN or anime, moments of sudden levity that strike from nowhere, and an ambient level of horniness (providing much of said levity) that matches any given classic shounen. "Forgivably horny" is the term I've been throwing around. Wrap your expectations within this package and you'll be a very happy camper. The music selection and placement throughout the story are top-tier, and it makes me wince that we probably won't get a compilation for easy direct access. "Wintering Ezo Red Fox," "Go When," "Black Tears and Lives to Protect," and especially "Relic of Agunamonita" are all living rent-free between my ears now and forever.The heart, dedication, and compassion put into this game by its developer are entirely evident, and he deserves every last ounce of praise we can give. KEIZO, you can have my "Love," specifically the one Porin found on the ground for me. That one was cool.

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE BUY THIS GAME!!!!!!!! ALSO PROBABLY DON'T PLAY THE DEMO MODE IN THE DEMO BECAUSE I DID AT FIRST AND DIDN'T THINK I'D LIKE IT!!!!!!!!!!!! IF YOU PLAY THE DEMO START A NEW GAME!!!!!!!!!Now with the formalities out of the way, Astlibra Revision is one of the absolute greatest games I have ever had the pleasure of playing in my entire life. I will admit, it probably isn't for everyone, but I highly recommend buying it if it seems even a little bit up your alley, since if you don't care for it you'll still be helping to support an incredible developer. This game excels extraordinarily on every front imaginable. So lets go through those fronts, shall we?VISUALSThis is definitely the most debatable point. From an objective perspective, I'd say the visuals in this game aren't great. There are various mismatched artstyles all over the place, and a lot of things seem to just be stock assets. However, this strange artstyle gives the game such a unique feeling that very few other games capture. It makes the game stand out among all its contemporaries for being so unusual. For me, the visuals evoke a very strong sense of nostalgia. As to whether it's the early 2000s, late 2000s, or early 2010s, I have no clue. It just captures that vibe, whatever it may be, and just makes me feel at home, reminding me of the good old days, whatever days those were. Plus, when this game wants to do spectacle, it definitely does some great spectacle.SOUNDTRACKThis game's soundtrack is mostly, if not entirely, made up of stock and copyright free music. However, the song choices that were included go so unbelievably hard. The very first level theme is one of the most motivating and awesome songs I have ever heard for a first level, and all you're doing it hitting slimes with a stick. If you want good examples of tracks from this game, listen to Enter Velocity by Shimajiro and Lava Belt by TAZ. Both are absolutely amazing. Also there are even a few songs in here by Sakuzyo (for my fellow rhythm game fans), who always makes excellent songs.STORYNow we get into the really incredible stuff. Astlibra's story is completely unhunged, utterly nonsensical, and frankly deranged. It is also one of the best stories I have ever seen in a video game. It isn't quite to the level of the NieR games or Omori, but I'd place it as a solid 3rd place. Nothing ever makes any sense, every twist is insane, and the game outright lies to you on multiple occasions. And yet, it's told beautifully, everything is foreshadowed very well without being predictable, and the feels hit so hard so many times they'd be convicted of murder. This story is one-of-a-kind, and I wouldn't wish spoilers for it upon my worst enemy. If the game itself isn't to your liking, at least watch a playthrough just so you can experience the incredible narrative it has to tell.GAMEPLAYOh yes. This game is pure and utter chaos in the absolute best way possible. Early on it plays fairly basically while managing to not feel boring or like a slog. However, as the game goes on, it slowly becomes more and more apparent that battles are not just enemies to fight. The combat system in this game is a lock, and you have been given a keyring so full you could never manage to count all the keys it holds. By the endgame, battles feel less like planned and crafted encounters and more like "how much insanity can we theoretically throw at the player? Oh that much? Ok cool do three times that." And somehow, it never feels unfair. Except Beatrice, she's kinda annoying. But one slightly annoying boss out of a 50+ hour game is such a small issue I wouldn't even bother saying it is one. And on top of all of that, there are the system mechanics and upgrades.Karon skills are a very neat addition. Every single weapon, shield, and piece of armor in the game can be leveled up, and will give you either a new ability or an extra resource for assigning those abilities when mastered. This sounds like it would involve a lot of grinding to get everything, but I spent very little time overall grinding for anything, and I never felt particularly bored while I did so. I say this as someone who hates grinding in games with every fiber of my being. The abilities you can get are also all very interesting and fun, leading to all sorts of potential builds and shenanigans.The Grow system, however, is where things get insane. From the outside it seems like a basic skill tree. Gather different colored Force from enemies and spend it to unlock stat boosts. However, this skill tree is essentially its own entire dungeon. There are chests to find, special items, locked doors and keys, all sorts of crazy things. And the sheer size of it is unbelievable. It is likely the largest skill tree in any game ever made. And yet, you'll likely fill out almost the entire thing by the time you beat the game, and likely not feel any real need to finish it unless you really, really want to. There are more very cool and interesting mechanics on top of those, but I think I've gone on for long enough.CONCLUSIONPlease play Astlibra. It is one of the greatest pieces of media I have ever experienced and the fact that it was mostly made by a single person is utterly insane. The fact that this game is so obscure is devastating to me, because I want as many people as possible to experience this game's perfection of its craft. Play it. Tell your friends to play it. Tell random strangers on the street to play it. Because with the massive amount of work that went into this game over its 15 year development, it's earned it.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my favorite games of all time.  It reminds me of both Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night (though no necessary backtracking typical of Metroidvanias) and the couple Ys games I've played.The game's story is compelling and the English localization is really good.  Every time I asked myself about some implication of an event - how or why did this happen? what will result from it? - the game dev proceeds to answer or at least acknowledge it.  It shows a lot of thought went into the story which tackles a topic that so often creates plot holes.The gameplay is very fun and is what mostly reminds me of Bloodstained.  Each "chapter" provides opportunities to grind - there are a multitude of progression elements to grind for - and I was always excited to do so.  This was helped by the fact that there is a pretty clear-cut way to determine if you're done grinding for a given chapter - it made it feel like an optional goal to hit each time.  And no problem if you don't hit that goal, you don't have to backtrack but you certainly can!I'll stop myself from going on and wrap up with a testament:  Every time I turned the game off late at night, I always literally said out loud "my god this is such a good game".  The fact that it was largely created by a single individual, KEIZO, over the course of 15 years is an inspiring display of the capacity of a person to produce something incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches an Ys sort of mashy action-RPG itch, but I'm not sure why so many refer to it as a masterpiece or say it does things narratively that have never been done in games before.  I was entertained throughout, though it does err on the long side and I would imagine a good number of people would find it repetitive by the end.And also, sorry to the devs, but it's gotta be said- one of the ugliest games you'll ever play.  A perfect 90-degree sideview with no sense of depth or placement, and ultra-detailed textures that scream "N64 4K texture pack" and all look like they were lifted from photographs as-is.If you did enjoy this game's story, go play 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim instead for what I would consider a much more impactful and surprising time-travel story.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I finished ASTLIBRA Revision. On the timer 16.5 hours (Proton does not count playing time offline). In-game time is as follows: about 70 hours on "Normal" difficulty, and about 17 hours on "Hard" difficulty. Had to go through the game twice, as I wanted to collect all the achievements. It was two completely different experiences. On the subject of time, to confirm my words left only one word: . If you know, you know.So, review. Saw a lot of good reviews of the game, decided to try it. I can say with confidence - it was one of the best gaming experiences.What I liked:-The story is strong, and it really is very good. The story leaves a nice aftertaste, it is completely finished and leaves no blank spots behind;-Music accompaniment fits the game perfectly, the combination of multiple genres sets the pace of the game. It's a subjective feeling, but through the music you can somewhat predict which way the story might move;-Various bosses, especially it feels that way on difficulty "Hard" and above;-Was pleasantly surprised that some bosses can make a real bullet hell, it was a very pleasant experience since the days when I played Rabi-Ribi. It's not often you see a 2d side-scroller project with bullet hell mechanics;-One of the best endgame content, with new mechanics and a big part of the story (no spoilers, it's just worth it);-The game is well balanced on "Normal" difficulty, and some will find it challenging on "Hard". I can't speak for the other difficulties.-Responsive controls, the character always does what you want to do;-A lot of RPG mechanics, some mechanics show themselves very well in the endgame;-Many options for enhancing a character's power, their combination makes the game very entertaining;-Well-hidden secrets and puzzles that are fun to solve;-The ability to quickly skip dialogues, which saved a lot of time on a second quick playthrough.Neutral points:-Although the secrets are hidden very well, there are some secrets that can be found either by accident or by digging every stone. Although I only had a few of these moments, -Maybe not everyone may like the graphics, but the game manages to pleasantly surprise with stunning views, especially in the second half of the game.Controversial points:-If you properly level up your character, the endgame part may be too easy for both "Normal" and "Hard". On the other hand, the balance of the endgame will depend entirely on the player.I could not identify obvious disadvantages in the game. It completely fulfills its functions.Bottom line: a great game, with good mechanics, bosses and a good story. ASTLIBRA Revision deserves to go into my box of awesome unique projects.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, Astlibra, is a true hidden gem. Never played any version other than this Revision, but if this is the best version there is, I'm thankful for all the bells and whistles.You play a young man whose childhood friend goes missing after a demon attack, accompanied only by a talking crow. Between your swordplay and the crow's magic, you fight through demons to find other human settlers and hopefully what happened to your old hometown.The graphics are very basic that feel like they were from an RPG maker built, and yet are used so vibrantly and creatively they appear almost high-end, much nicer than most AAA games. Which is good because with how you fight waves of waves of monsters and how one swing of a sword can hit multiple demons at once, there will be a lot of numbers flying around your screen. Battles are also a joy, as they are like a blend of metroidvanias (especially Castlevania Symphony of the Night) with their traversal maps and enemy fighting, with older Ys games and/or Trails games in both the rocking music for each area and how many ways you can get stronger. There are weapons and armor you can craft through enemy parts you get from drops. The weapons have experience bars where mastering them gives you either new skills or points to use said skills. There's a growth map that gives you bonus stats, and even some rare bonuses like equipment and new magic spells, based on mana points you also get from each kill. And of course the basic level up system where you can put points into stats on each level, and total freedom to rearrange them later.Best of all is the story, that hits closer to home than one might expect. Sure it's a tried-and-true metroidvania hack-and-slash singleplayer game where you guide your hero on a journey to slay demons. The dialogue is rather witty about the character's actions, and has some nice levity moments where the hero's androgenous looks gets him mistaken for girl more often than not, or how your crow companion, Kanon, brags they can protect themselves in a bubble when entering water but the hero sheepishly admits that he can't swim. But this is also a story where the core theme is about what it means to live, and how some people would sacrifice everything for others. The first two chapters hit me so emotionally because of how chilling and real it reminds you that it is a world where there are so few people left, making the ones that the hero and Kanon find after eight years of solitude all the more impactful. As well as all the more tragic when some of them are gone, even long before you realize. Special mention goes to Chapter 2, which stars an old couple living in a swamp with a guardian dog. The dog was not initially friendly and even bit the man's fingers off when trying to feed him. But the old man insisted to help the dog to eat and live, as dying is easy but living is worth something. It turns out the dog, Polin, is more than meets the eye since he has a nearby goblin tribe out to get him, but the ending is just beautifully tragic that it got me teary eyed just remembering it. Astlibra is an amazing game that has everything one could ask for: beautifully detailed world, intense and rewarding gameplay with even scaling difficulty levels from kid-friendly to hardcore, killer soundtrack that would make you think Falcom had a hand in it, and a story that just moves you. I regret not playing this sooner, and strongly urge others to give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10. If you like games like SOTN, you'll probably like Astlibra. WARNING: there's some seriously cringy pervy content.Astlibra does a solid job with the fundamentals: combat mechanics, equipment balancing, the UI, mob design. In other respects, like overall visuals and music, it's passable. There's not a lot of recycled content, which is a plus. Even NG+ isn't just hardmode, but a whole extension of the storyline with various new mechanics. All things considered, Astlibra is pretty good, but outclassed by other recent additions to the genre.Cons:- Minor bugs. Just save often in case you get stuck (that only happened to me once).- Confusing instructions. The explanations of some mechanics are ambiguous. I had to use a combination of the internet and trial & error. Also props to the dev for participating in online discussions to help clarify things.- Cringy pervy content. Sexy stuff in games is great. This is something else.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has many issues, it is far more than the sum of its parts. I was absolutely entranced by it; the story is fascinating, the gameplay is phenomenal, the various systems that unlock as you go are mostly well thought out and very fun, and the sense of growth is almost unmatched. There are just SO MANY things to do and ways to power up your character, and you'll need all of them to succeed. I'm afraid to say much more without spoiling things, almost everything is tied to the story so well that describing most of them in detail would rob you of the moment of discovery.A relatively minor, lategame-only system is actually one of my favorites, and non-spoilerey, so I can talk about it a bit: Boards. They serve many purposes, but chief among them is the ability to make ANY weapon or armor good with enough work. Just getting a board takes all equipment up to *rough* parity, but with enough work you can almost completely customize them. Want your claws to deal all 6 elements of damage? Sure, go grind for a few hours. Want your starting wooden branch to be better than most postgame weapons? Not even that hard tbh, just get the board and toss on the accessory that focuses Board drops on equipped gear and it'll catch up in no time. Between Boards and skills, you can make basically any playstyle work by the end, regardless of how good or bad they are baseline.I will, however, note that there are many, many, *many* issues with the game that may lessen the experience. There are a few absolutely awful bosses (ex. chapter 3) and two chapters (7 and 8) that have genuinely some of the worst video game design I have ever experienced in 30 years of gaming. There's also a *lot* of 2000s Japanese flavor, both for good and bad - I hope you like puerile jokes about boobs, cross-dressing, and some absolutely nonsensical puzzles without even a single meaningful hint. Consider using a spoiler-free guide if desired.The overall experience was absolutely worth it in my eyes, and unless the above is a total dealbreaker for you I highly recommend giving it a shot. This game is really something special. It won't change your life, but it's an experience that you won't soon forget.Just don't get the DLC, lol.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Astlibra Revision on Twitch and posted on YouTube. Went through the main game and post game story. TLDR: Good game, alright story, lots of fun mechanics, really fun but challenging in a technical way on Difficult / Hell difficulty. Expanded thoughts below: - Plays similarly to some side-scrolling action platformers, thinking Castlevania series. Character has a bit finer motion control, several fun movement and attack abilities, etc. Magic feels varied and presents unique attack / defense opportunities, especially combined with Karon's skills that can totally change mechanics. There are tons of items to collect, lots of mix and match stats, and the different weapon classes feel unique. Bosses are fun, trash mobs have varied looks and basic attacks, and the levels are passable. I did have some frustration on some sections (the hopping enemies that attach to you and make you bleed... I love those @_@). Overall, very fun game. - Decent visuals. Reminiscent of flash gameplay, but it's a little more polished. Most big boss sprites look great. Enemies have decent enough palettes and silhouettes to be recognizable and fun. But yeah, the bug bosses and effects are where the game shines. My only minor complaint, especially in the postgame bosses, is there would be enough going on I would sometimes lose track of my nameless hero. Or the attack particles / sprites would get hidden by flashes and other effects. Not terrible, but playing on Hell with the Berserk skill active... left me ripping a few blue hairs out of my gorgeous locks.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is a fantastic 2D action RPG. It may look like it's a Metroidvania, but there are little to no powers or unlocks that provide access to new areas. Each area is mostly self-contained per chapter of the game's story. And this game's story...I wish I could play this game again blind.The main character starts out as a young boy who befriends a girl about his age. Their village is attacked by demons and he attempts to save her only to be killed. Or does he?This game has so many twists and turns, and every time you think you know what's going on, you're wrong. It seems like it's going to be formulaic and follow established tropes, but then pulls the rug out from underneath you. Straight up to the very end, I could never have guessed where the story was going, and it was all excellent.If I had to make any complaint, it's that the when the story switches to moments of levity, they are usually a bit on the pervy side, such as borrowing one of the girls outfits to masquerade the main character as a woman and having the aforementioned girl follow behind in provocative attire, or having a main plot point kick out with one of the male characters leading the player character to watch the female characters in a hot spring. Additionally, a few of the bosses are women with huge breasts that range is level of provocative appearance. While I didn't have any problems with these things, and they didn't happen too often, I'd be remiss in not mentioning them.Finally, regarding the depth of game mechanics:There's a plethora of weapons, with different stats, swing speeds, etc., but they also unlock different abilities once you max out their proficiency meter, so you'll want to seek out, buy and craft all that you can to unlock them.There's a huge grid of stat-ups, spells, and other goodies that you can unlock with elemental crystals you get from killing different types of enemies. And if you can't find the exact color you need, you can buy it with a different one, albeit at 3x the cost.There's a system where you put different items on a set of scales. Each item has it's own passive effects, and the closer you can balance the scales the bigger percentage of the effect you can get.I can talk about how great the game is forever, but if you dig 2d combat, like what you'd find in a Metroidvania, but not necessarily the exploration aspect, this game should not be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Action-focused sidescroller that features an engaging fantasy story featuring an MC searching for their lost friend with some interesting twists. It has an engaging story making you wonder more about why the events that happen occurred.  Soundtrack isn't bad either despite being a mixture of different sources that somehow work really well with the game's aesthetics and atmosphere.There are passive abilities that can be slotted in order to adjust combat abilities, make grinding easier, and add additional UI features which each take up a magic crystal capacity that can be expanded . Combat features button mashing which differ in moveset for sword/2h-sword/lance/wand/hammer/etc., directional attacks which tend to be the same for every weapon, and skills that vary from summons, support, and active attacks which each provide some level of invulnerability time. All of these are not gate-kept behind going to specific areas to swap out when you really need specific builds during boss fights. Want to focus on two handing and then swap to sword-shield in the middle of battle because bullet hell? Open the menu, navigate to the equipment/skills/abilities, swap out, done and no additional futzing. However, the game does force you to be on the lookout for hidden treasure in the clunky map designs since the way you unlock more moves is via treasure chests in the world. This involves searching for tiny directional arrows, mini-bullseye, and obscure hidden paths. Some of these can only be reached once the appropriate skills and combat maneuvers are acquired to combo together. Puzzles are relatively easy and obscure since sometimes the game provides prompts noting an interactable and other times they're just obstacles that you mash buttons and/or use random baubles you find to interact with it.The game is fast and doesn't futz around with handlholding so much meaning combat, puzzle solving, and story keep the momentum going. Absolutely recommend this game. Also, I will never forgive KEIZO for Chapter 5. Both for the questionable "correct" choice and the aftermath of the "wrong".
