_childDocuments_.review: This has been one of the most enjoyable Action/RPG I think I've ever played; almost up there with Nier:Automata. 2D side-scroller combat with tons of gear to craft. A lot of the weapons are basic stat upgrades with a choice between preferring Range, Speed, or sheer Power. Good range of evasive/defensive options (an evade/dash with invincibility frames, a shield to block with its own health bar; can unlock abilities for "perfect block" that if timed correctly can restore health or prevent shield HP from going down). Plenty of "special attacks" (summons) that continue to unlock throughout the game, and even into the "post-game". Combat always felt fun, unlike some other action RPGs where the combat gets old after a few hours.  Replaying in 2024 with the new English translation - it's much better now, very good overall. Only noticed some rare minor issues. A few puzzles mid-game were a bit confusing, and I had to resort to using Google Translate on the Japanese Wiki to get solutions. This may have been partially due to the rough translation, or with not understanding an expected mechanic. [spoiiler](I couldn't knock the "Green Orb" lose with a sword or club; why would a Bow + Arrow work???). [/spoiler]  - game is well worth full price, I have no regrets and I'm a cheap bastard. :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Hack and Slash games, and JRPGS, please stop reading reviews and actually play the game. It's shockingly good. This game plays more linearly than a few other Metroidvanias, but I never felt like this detracted from the game at all. Combat is relatively simple but the content the game has allows you to create a few cool strategies that can give the game a lot more depth. I did initially play the game as a "just keep whacking the enemy before they die" sort of playstyle, as I did for most Metroidvanias, but this game genuinely allowed the option for a fun playstyle where I had to think about when to utilize i-frames while performing magic that took HP away to stay net neutral with costs while outputting significant damage. Honestly? Not many games tend to have that sort of freedom which is really cool.Also, I have to say that I also thought that both the OST and the story kicks ass. The story can be a bit zany so for people looking for a more grounded and realistic story for one setting, it's sort of understandable, but even then, I still think it's really cool. The fact that the game's able to introduce details, and somehow make them all relevant at some point of the story is really admirable.I really enjoyed this game, the 74.4 hours of playtime are all part of one save file, with me playing on the "Hard" or "Difficult" setting. It's just that particularly long of a game, with it never really feeling like it falters, and even delivering during post-game, which is fantastic. Please play the game, especially if you're into Hack and Slash or JRPG's.

_childDocuments_.review: Global Achievements don't lie: Over a quarter of all players have reached the true end.  Even absolutely top tier games rarely boast more than 10% finishing the game - let alone massive long RPGs like this; Divinity Original Sin 2 has about 12% game completion rate, for example, and is one of the top RPGs of all time by basically every measure - and ASTLIBRA has twice the percentage of people who stuck with it all the way to the very end.  It's not just a good bit of a game - it's amazing start to finish.I didn't know if Symphony of the Night would ever be dethroned, but in spite of a little bit of map jank here and there, the weirdness with overlays and mining, and the fact that the first two boss fights in chapter five felt over tuned, this is my new top metroidvania.  The weapon mastery system ensures that you're always trying out new gear so the combat never stagnates, the magic, growth, and spell systems are very well done, and the post game equipment boards and weapon upgrade systems add everything you need to keep the game feeling fresh from the very first level to the true final boss mechanically, and the story has plenty of turns to keep you engaged the whole time.Normally I'm a bit more reserved in my reviews, but honestly?  Buy and play ASTLIBRA Revision right now.  Don't wait for a sale.  Right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt an amazing JRPG. Taking nods from gaming classics such as Chrono Trigger and Castlevania, and combining them into a perfect blend of exactly everything I miss from the 90s/early 2000s of gaming. Mechanically the game constantly adds new features and abilities all the way up to its very finish. This keeps the gameplay fresh and does a very good job of gating power so you do not become too easily overpowered on higher difficulties. While a bit grindy at times to unlock new abilities on gear or get enemies to drop specific materials, most of this can be lightened with abilities or increasing luck. The story does a good job of keeping you wondering what is going to happen, and has a hell of a payoff at the end. It took me around 110 hours to fully 100 percent the game on the second highest difficulty. And that was with me being a bit slow because I loved playing so much. With all those glowing points, I cannot stress enough that this game may not be for everyone. There is VERY Japanesey writing and characters that unless you enjoy the tropes and the goofiness I can see why someone may be put off. On the other hand, if you enjoy these things pick it up immediately because the game is brilliant.For a one guy love project that took 15 years and is easily better than the AAAA standard nowadays, its an easy sell. I love this game, and I hope more people get a chance to experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my playtime, I played through the entire game on a friend's account, but I ended up loving it so much that I bought it to support Keizo and leave a review. I don't want to spoil anything, but the story is phenomenally good. It's a real emotional rollercoaster with lots of unpredictable twists and turns, and even a few gut punches, but there's always a light at the end of the tunnel. It reminded me a lot of Gurren Lagann, which is my most loved story of all time. Just like Gurren Lagann, it can be a little corny, silly, or bawdy at times, but that's part of its charm, and it rarely loses sight of the overarching themes of humanity, love, and hope, even when faced with overwhelming despair. It's very much a story about "the indomitable human spirit". Beyond that, the world-building is surprisingly good, and it plays around with a lot of tropes that you wouldn't initially expect. There's lots of mysteries to uncover, and the game loves to drop hints about things so you can feel smart for correctly guessing before the answer is outright revealed.As far as the gameplay goes, it's solid. It won't blow you away, but it's entertaining enough for the game's run-time. There are lots of progression systems, so you always have this sense of growing and getting stronger. Some people might be turned-off by important items being hidden, but I liked it, because it meant exploration and curiosity felt genuinely rewarding. I've seen some complaints of too much grind, to which I'd say, turn the difficulty down and ignore the progression systems. Though as a grind hater myself, I rarely was bothered by it.Lastly, while I can't credit Keizo for the soundtrack, as it's entirely freeware, I *can* commend him for his choice of songs. There's a wonderful variety here, and a lot of really energetic, catchy songs. Some of the more emotional tunes were absolutely mesmerizing when I first heard them in-game as well. They definitely amplify and enhance the impact of the story beats.In all, I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game and the story is going to hold a special place in my heart for a long time to come.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique title with a unique look, Astlibra is a blend of JRPG mechanics with Metroidvania-style combat (though it is not a Metroidvania) that tells a story spanning across time. While naive at times, the writing is fun and tackles a number of unique, thought-provoking situations.Final Fantasy players from the Playstation era will notice heavy inspiration from FFIX's Ability system and FFX's Sphere Grid, and a "Possession" system that treats summon monsters as single-fire spells. Oldschool RPG players know the drill. At the same time, and much unlike an oldschool RPG, the combat system encourages quick reflexes through the use of Fighting-game combo inputs to pull off a variety of dazzling moves. Throw in the readily-available respec system, multiple RPG-style leveling paths, dozens of arena challenges, and a simple crafting system, and Astlibra becomes a surprisingly fun take on a variety of well-known mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you ever know from the very moment a title screen hits you're about to play an all-time great? The PC-98 music hits, the moonlit background descends, and I knew instantly Astlibra was about to become one of my favorite games.There's something to be said for the sheer freedom of expression allowed when one has absolute authority over their creative expression, especially in a culture like Japan routinely producing off-kilter ideas. Keizo is, like any good Japanese artist, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horny. You thought Takahashi was horny while directing Xenoblade 2? Nah, fam. Astlibra is plagued with scantily clad titty beasts. Plant monsters whose only censorship is her vines, floating bodies without appendages but no deficit of cleavage, goddesses whose battle armor is lingerie, , and a year's supply of juvenile sex humor you've seen in literally every ecchi you've ever watched. To really round off the sentiment, there's a traditionally JRPG colosseum-like arena with individual matches and one of those matches is titled "Harem" in which you have to slay every degenerate demon the game has ever thrown at you. Keizo is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horny.Keizo is also, like any good Japanese artist, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ . This man has read his fair share of visual novels, clearly loves time travel, and probably threw every idea he ever had over its development time at the wall and performed mad science to fuse it all together. This design philosophy extends to the gameplay for sure, but I'll come back to that later, because there's a phenomenal story here if you can make sense of it all.Time travel is fascinating; even when it's riddled with plot holes it's gotta be one of my favorite genres. There's not a lot of "meaningful" choices in Astlibra, but there are choices, you can make the wrong ones, and you will feel the weight of them. There's VN-style epilogue-like "dead ends" (not always bad endings, necessarily). But most importantly, Astlibra's central theme is its opening tagline: life is a series of choices, and every time you make a choice to help someone, to save someone, you hurt or lose someone else. You could have the literal tools of God in your hands with the ability to correct any history you saw fit, but the butterfly effect unfolds -- what will you lose in the process?Chapter 7 really struck an emotional chord with me, one that all-time greats like Fullmetal Alchemist (2003) and Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica have, when the price of obsession was made manifest. What are you willing to sacrifice for your obsession? I watched a dry comedy-drama called Russian Doll last year, also a time travel story, and a certain character described something they termed a "Coney Island moment": your one past decision where everything went to hell. You made one catastrophic decision, however inconsequential it seemed at the time, tugging the lynchpin that kept your entire life together, and the butterfly effect surely unfolds. Astlibra's thesis is thus: if you could reverse time and undo the "Coney Island moment," sacrificing all the bonds and memories you made in the process, would you, and could you live with the consequences afterward? So many ideas are thrown into the story & lore it can be difficult to untangle, and yeah, I'm pretty sure it's riddled with plot holes (although I'll note that by the end it *felt* like every loose end was resolved), but if you can untangle the mess and bask in the distinctly Japanese zaniness, it packs some serious emotional weight.The over-the-top design philosophy is infused into the gameplay as much as the narrative. By the postgame there are four different progression systems, a wide variety of techs with near-infinite build options and the ability to respec whenever you want.  I finished the game on hard, and it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard. My final clock time -- getting 100%, including achievements -- was 61.5 hours, and Steam registers a playtime of 95 hours. There's idle time in there for sure, but that demonstrates well over a dozen hours of lost progress because there is no autosave and trash mobs can ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rip you a new one. By chapter 5 or so, it's entirely practical to be dying within 3 hits.Combat is visceral and the gameplay loop is crack. You will be  by fields of mobs as you hack 'n' slash your way through them, manipulating your iframes, guard gauge, cleverly hidden techniques, and Karon build to steamroll them as efficiently as possible, the gamepad rumbling in your hands with every slash, the frustration of playing what often feels like a 2D soulslike where every input matters, dying, dying dying to trash. Every chapter has its own equipment section with materials dropped by mobs only found in that chapter, accompanied by a super streamlined and super rewarding crafting system, making it sinfully easy to blow 5 minutes grinding for a few more mats to purchase that next available weapon. The game rewards grinding almost  well.The game's biggest flaw is how it reeks of early-to-mid 00s development. The gameplay loop is simple. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ESL translation steals heavily from American idioms, like "using the John," in ways that just make zero sense within the setting's context, yet it's nonetheless nostalgic to a time of mediocre VN translations (Tohsaka's anus is defenseless), ♥♥♥♥♥♥ anime subs, and downloading new episodes on BitTorrent then burning them to your DVD while posting screenshots of your ripped DVD collections on fan forums. The puzzles and platforming are excruciatingly retro; satisfying in their own way, but to solve them you have to think about them from a design perspective of a different era. You literally walk through glitches in the scenery to solve puzzles. Secret treasures in the game are well hidden in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pixel-sized green arrows, in the late game behind scenery, obstacles, and other hurdles making them, frankly, impossible to find unless you have a treasure guide up, and I absolutely recommend one to the side while playing. It's borderline cozy how there are virtually zero guides available online because it's so niche and playing it draws you into a real community; but there is a treasure guide, you should use it, and expect that otherwise, you will probably have to figure ♥♥♥♥ out on your own.Everything comes into harmony to produce a grossly addictive game as I was propelled from literally the first 30 minutes to see the plot unfold, yearning to see the story's earliest and most harrowing mysteries resolved -- in most cases, far differently than I could have ever imagined.It's rare these days I can play a game and not levy a dumptruck load's complaints at it; I'm aging and I have a lot to ♥♥♥♥♥ about it. A game's worth isn't so much defined by its flaws as it is how much its draws transcend those flaws. Astlibra is a gem. It's uniquely its own, there's so much to digest, and its creative expression is something you can really only get out of a game developed by one KEIZO for 16 years. The sort of poetic beauty to it all: the slice-of-life adventure of handling a new town's dilemmas every chapter; your guild master opening each chapter with a spine-tingling, heartrending summary of whose woes you must resolve; to see a VN-style opening theme at the end of EVERY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CHAPTER; all in a spacetime transcending romantic epic in pursuit of your first love. It's quirky, it's convoluted in a way only a JRPG could be, and it's beautiful. Go, my minions!

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a great game. If you like long action JRPGs and collecting equipment you will love this game.Pros:- story- tons of equipment and skills to collect- a lot of enemy variety and plenty of bosses- music is really exceptional- long (70h+)- plenty of options for builds and variables to play with- only 1 missable achievement (play the game on hard or higher)- arena challenges (mostly normal battles but there are some dps checks and a bit of a puzzle fights too)- you can skip cutscenes- bossfight checkpoints between boss phases (with 1 exception for some unknown reason, maybe an oversight)- situational humor, no modern day politics or meme/celebrity references- over 100 save slots for your game saving needsNeutral:- if you are underleveled you will be 1 shot, if you are overfarmed you will just steamroll. I played the game on Hell difficulty which is next to last and honestly it wasn't so bad. Last difficulty makes the enemies too spongy for my taste for most of the game and Hell was perfect for me (there are like 3 or 4 lower difficulties too and you can always go lower but not higher)- ability scrolls are hidden in the world (there are some ESSENTIAL combat skills that make this game so much better, hiding them isn't the best idea imo)- a lot of cutscenes and reading (no voiceovers)- a lot of time in the menus- nostalgic feel, it plays like an "old" game so you have to think like you are playing an "old" game. For example, if you want to use an item on an object in the wold like a key on a locked gate you have to go into your inventory, select the key and use it.- backstep instead of dodge forward but on the other hand shields are very strong in this game + you can always quickly turn around and "backstep forward", it just needs getting used to (there is a skill to make it into a forward dodge but you get this skill mod in postgame so it is waaaay to late for that)- when you die you have to load your last save so you know, you lose everything you gathered up and done to the point of your demise (which is a great incentive to not die)Cons:- the further you progress the more flashy abilities you have, same goes for enemies and sometimes it is impossible to tell what the hell is going on during those massive bossfights because it's all overlapping- solutions to some problems the game presents are mostly reasonable and were in one way or another mentioned along the way but this one part where you have to fill a huge jug with water so the STONE would float up to the surface is so mind boggling I would have never guessed wth I was supposed to do- berserk skill breaks the game (3x damage but 1 hp), you can just turn skills on and off without any consequences and it seems to be a solution to many difficulty related problems people have, just turn berserk on when boss is "broken" or when  the window is open and turn it off the second you feel threatened, repeat to win ez. In other words, there is easily available cheese in the game.- when you restart a boss fight from the "bossfight checkpoint" it doesn't give you back your consumables that you have used so better stock up before bosses

_childDocuments_.review: Very great game and obviously a passion project of the developer. Lots of attention to detail and many cool small touches such as all of the equipment changing your appearance (sometimes pretty dramatically).Essentially this game is a metroidvania that leans very heavily into JRPG game-play influences (as opposed to the more "souls-like" metroidvanias that have become more popular recently). Lots of equipment, stats (all sorts of "numbers go up" to play with) but also a really neat system that lets you kit out your character with different abilities to suit how you would like to handle combat and exploration. I'm also a big fan of the magic/summon system that takes some ques from Symphony of the Night but handles it much better since you have to build up a charge, the press a button which stops the action while you input a two button combo to trigger the spell/summon you want. That probably doesn't entirely do it justice but it works very well in practice. I'm not sure I've seen an action RPG or metroidvania use quite the same system.The basic loop is that you enter an area, explore it, harvest materials from the enemies in an area and then use that to upgrade your equipment at a shop. You learn abilities from said equipment so it is worth your while to collect and use as much as possible. The equipment also lends itself to very different fighting styles depending on your kit.The game-play loop is occasionally broken up a bit by some light puzzle and problem solving that is just interesting enough to keep things fresh and keep the main game-play loop from getting monotonous.I haven't finished the story yet but so far it is extremely enjoyable with a nice balance of exposition and game-play. Also some nice comic relief thrown in. From what I can tell based on where I am in the game and what I've seen about the game it is clear that this is going to be a lot longer than the typical 15 to 20 hours that this style of game usually clocks in at. And given the great story I think the increased length is a major plus. I am at 24 hours at the time of this review and I am nowhere near done.One of the biggest standout areas of the game is the banging soundtrack. Seriously, there are some killer dungeon themes in particular. I am going to be on the lookout for the soundtrack for this one.If I must list a complaint about the game it would be that it is just a touch grindy if you want to fill out all of the available equipment for each area. It isn't anything game breaking but it wouldn't bother me if the drop rates for material were just a touch higher.Overall though this game is worth the very modest asking price and a real steal if on sale. If you at all enjoy metroidvania style games and/or JPRGs playing this one is a must.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished spending 57 hours being completely absorbed and compelled by a game of which I had understandably low expectations. And man was I blown away. I do not usually review games - I just play them and move on - but man this is different. The screenshots, previews, and the demo that comes with the game understandably temper your expectations. The backgrounds and environments are off-putting the first time you see them. And the combat feels stiff. And the story line in the opening few chapters feels a bit aimless and stock-standard (you have amnesia and are trying to find your hometown - this feels like it has been done quite a few times). But the strength of this game is that it grows on you and continually develops. The action gets more and more fast paced and satisfying. I can't emphasize enough how good the combat gets and feels. I had more fun with the combat in this game than other Action RPGs like Nier Automata. With a lot of those games, you just mash the dodge button over and over again. With Astlibra, you charge into the fray of battle, execute combos, and devastate your opponents with combos and magic. It's all so satisfying. And the graphics grow on you. They mesh perfectly with the combat and magic graphics. Some of the animations for the gods and mechs look surreal. The design Keizo implemented into the game encourages grinding and fighting. He wants you to battle and enjoy yourself. And you are rewarded for it!  You get crafting items, and a multitude of other types of experience to grow and power up your character - and it all feels so intuitive.  Nothing is hidden, and you always feel rewarded for your time commitment. The storyline is probably the most unique narrative I have come across in a long time. it starts our so simple, so that you (the player) are not expecting much. But layers and layers keep getting added on, and when they all come  together, you are taken aback - you simply are not expecting the plot twists. And the ending ties up all the loose ends perfectly. Others have mentioned that you can't go into the storyline much without giving too much away, and i agree. You should experience it for yourself. I will say this, though, that crow is my ultimate bro. If you are a fan of action RPGs, or RPGs in general, or if you grew up during the 90s and 2000s with RPGs like Chrono Trigger, Xenogears, or maybe even Ragnarok Online, play this game. You will have a blast. Keizo, if you are reading this, you are the man. This man spent a decade creating a game that feels so good to play - a game that looks and feels like it knows exactly what it wants to be. I definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: it nails the retro JRPG vibe and provides a smooth combat experience along with a wild story that blends sci-fi and fantasy.The combat system feels like a mix of elements from a variety of different JRPGs. As a non-exhaustive list of examples: a standard level up system, stat and skill trees, weapon leveling to learn skills, crafting, a permanent item buff system, and much more. The game does a great job of blending all the different systems and encouraging you to tweak and experiment (you can freely re-spec as much as you want) which makes for a really fun experience.The story goes through a ton of twists and turns that make for an interesting ride from start to finish. However, I will throw the caveat that the lighthearted moments tend to use a lot of JRPG/anime/manga/LN tropes. Given the game is a JRPG, that shouldn't be a shock or anything. I thought it was worth pointing out though because the game really doubles down on it in certain parts despite the overarching narrative being much more grounded and serious.The artwork was solid all around. I would not say the graphics overall would win any awards by modern standards, but they perfectly fit the retro style of the game. The boss designs were all quite unique and there were also not many reskinned enemies that I can recall.The music is all over the place. What I mean by that is that there is no consistent theme across the music, so you get a wide variety of genres and styles. I didn't outright hate any of the tracks, but I definitely enjoyed some much more than others; and there is large variance in how well certain pieces fit certain parts.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic RPG. The world is starved for side-scrolling RPGs that go beyond Metroid, Castlevania, or Dark Souls. Even with all its obvious Falcom influences, Astlibra is a unique game balancing arcadey combat, hardcore RPG grit, and abundant quality of life features without any sense of compromise.You gotta love the pick-and-mix of proven RPG mechanics here: mastering equipment to learn new abilities, use-times for healing items to keep 'em from trivializing combat, MP that regenerates quickly from melee attacks to promote a spellblade playstyle... Wonderful. There's some grind for crafting materials, but it's a joy to scan back and forth across save points, see the fireworks go off, and snag loot.And the doujin visuals! All the strange detailed textures and lumpy tilesets... Painterly paper-doll goblins fighting alongside squash-and-stretch photo manipulations of snapping turtles... *chef's kiss*Its weakest point is its story. It's not bad, exactly; it gets you from point A to point B, and it takes place in a charmingly cliche JRPG world. But there are long stretches of time where you, the player, sit with two-dimensional dramatic ironies or obviously suspicious characters while the mains blabber on and on in confused exclamations and redundant questions. It's like, "Hey guys, I figured out the whole mystery behind this town an hour and a half ago!" Few of the games' premises require extended dialogues,  yet here they are in abundance.There's also a moderate amount of pervy comedy, like sexually appraising a girl's fat ass as she's on her deathbed. I'm not a prude, but I do think it's tonally weird to sexually appraise a girl's fat ass as she's on her deathbed. Better have a tolerance for this stuff coming in.Also, the translation is bad. It's charming and you can get the gist if you're familiar with amateur Japanese-to-English translations, but woof.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time RPG fan, but I have recently had a hard time getting into most JRPGs. Long, convoluted stories, annoying characters and slow, repetitive combat saw my interest wane as I felt my time was being wasted. Well...this exceptional game grabbed my attention and saw me playing it to nearly 100% completion in a week and a half, and I don't feel i wasted any of that. The story is good, if a bit long, the music is awesome and the combat is phenomenal. I would recommend this to any RPG fan in a heartbeat, if only for the incredible combat and amazing craft that went into this. It has a charm that only a passion project can have, and I hope I don't need to wait 15 years to see KEIZO's next work.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game two weeks ago, finished it with the DLC in about 9 days on hard difficulty after 75 hours of hyperfixation. I recommend it. TL;DR at the end. While good, the gameplay is nothing new, so I'd recommend it more if you're in there for the full experience rather than just the 'pushing buttons' part of the game. Astlibra's a weird game to evaluate, it has things it does extremely well and its good at selling it to the player, and there's some other things that vary between mildly annoying to very bad.First off, the game feels extremely satisfying to play, you can feel the extreme attention to detail in just about everything. The action pacing is nothing short of exceptionnal, everything feels good. One thing I like is that there is a lot of freedom when customizing your build. However the game is very grindy, and you're going to have to suck it up if you're going for the higher difficulties (which you have to for one achievement if you're a completionnist). Fortunately one of the last stage is designed for grinding and it has super cool music to keep you entertained so it wasn't such a bad experience, but still it was a bit much. Speaking of which, the ost is also hard to evaluate. I might be wrong about that but there is no original song and even if there is, the vast majority of the soundtrack come from copyright free libraries. That being said, the ost is nothing short of absolute perfection.Every music that you are going to hear, and I mean EVERY. SINGLE. MUSIC. blend perfectly with whatever is happening. It's never boring, every track that is playing at some point fit like nothing else can. I still remember how great and hyped up I felt at the beginning of the game when you get your first weapon and the 1st zone track starts playing, there could have never been a better fit, and I have plenty of other such anecdote on how the music made me feel at different point of the game. Seriously, it's memorable.A review of Astlibra wouldn't be properly done if I didn't talk about the story, which is also hard to evaluate. I've been thinking about it a lot and my opinion might be unpopular but... I don't think it's as good as other who like the game will tell you.Don't get me wrong, I liked it. Like everything else in Astlibra there is a lot of stuff that was done right. I liked how dramatic it felt. I liked how everything is tied together. I liked the themes the dev was going for. I liked how much efforts were put into world building. I liked how every character's actions are driven by their own motivation instead of plot convenience, which is always appreciated in that kind of stories. And while this last point is a major strength of the story it's also one of its weakness. You see, other than exactly three characters (Gau, Karon and the great sage), everyone is one-dimensionnal, characters in this world don't have a lot of depth to them so I don't feel much attachment to them when something happen. Overall the story felt very predictable, I won't spoil it for you, but every plot twist can be smelled miles away. Some subtle story elements were pleasant surprises but those were minor things that are barely relevant (like why a certain someone stopped showing up at the inn). In addition to that, there's a metric ton of plot holes in there, they don't really get you out of the action but I strongly advise you not to stop in order to think about anything related to the power of the scales, just accept things as they are presented to you. Does all of that make the story bad ? No. It's good, it really is and it's definitely a unique experience. But don't buy Astlibra expecting perfection, time-travel stories are hard, alright ?TL;DR : Overall, Astlibra is a very unique blend. It's done well, has a lot of toughts put into it on nearly every part. It deserves every single bit of praise it received, and the story is good but flawed in a way that doesn't take from its uniqueness. Also, I'm definitely buying anything the dev make from now on.Free tip : The game gives you a lot of save slots to work with. This is done purposefully. Use them. Also expect 70h to 120h of gameplay if you're a completionnist.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra is a fantastic Metroidvania with surprisingly good combat mechanics. This game is absolutely what you're looking for if you want to play something like Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. The story can get surprisingly dark and mysterious which makes it very compelling.The game also features a game mechanic where your companion learns passive skills from the equipment that you find from your journey (Weapons, Shields, and Armor). Enemies drop elemental "force" that you can use to give stat buffs to your character, unlock new offensive magical spells, and treasures to gain more power for your character (advancement of this mechanic is restricted at certain points until you further advance the story).There is also a passive system that uses the items that you find and craft on your adventure to empower your character and offer unique benefits to your character such as increased resistance to all manner of status effects, increased exp, increased coins from enemies, and even passive Health recovery.Many treasures are well hidden, and side content like the Arena offer fantastic rewards. The story is linear, but at certain points you are able to backtrack to seek missing treasure or additional force to power up your character. There is content in the game that you can miss depending on your decisions at certain points in the story.I spent quite a bit of time on this game and it was very enjoyable. I honestly did a bit more grinding than I needed to when I could have just used a different setup to defeat a certain boss. Mix up your tactics and try different weapons as wildly swinging your weapon may not be enough to overcome your enemies.The sound quality can be off at times as some enemies make strange sounds, but this game's soundtrack is quite fantastic. Visual quality is also very good overall. Be wary that some bosses fire many projectiles and you can lose track of what's going on if you have additional characters on screen when using your character's abilities. I would also strongly advise that you reduce the screen flashing in the options menu.Overall this game is easy to recommend for anyone wanting a Metroidvania with a lot of content. It will keep you busy for quite some time and challenge you as much as you wish.

_childDocuments_.review: After fully beating this game, I can certainly say Astlibra is a masterpiece of the action JRPG genre. The gameplay is extremely fun, with a good mixture of button mashing while still retaining a need for situational awareness or tactics. The weapon experience system unlocking new abilities was always a treat, even if the weapons more or less played the same and having a shield was almost always better. I really enjoyed the designs despite that and working on a build that felt good for me to play. The summoning skills really add more depth to the gameplay as well, and I always found it fun to mess around with them and figure out which ones I liked or didn't like using for different encounters or areas. Just moving around in the game feels great, and everything is very responsive. That said, puzzles can sometimes be obtuse or confusing, and the EN translation isn't always consistent, but I can give it a pass.The overall story was so much better than I expected, even if it does follow many JRPG tropes, which you may love or hate. It continued to surprise me up to the very end. Some things seemed like they were obvious only for the scene to be turned upside down onto its head as the story unfolded. My biggest complaints about the story were the silent and unnamed protagonist, even though multiple times he "talks" in a small wordless speech bubble and people say "this has your name on it" a few times, and the weirdly perverted moments that can be very typical of Japanese fiction. I was able to look past those moments for the rest of this beautiful gem, however, and I think if you can as well, you'll really like this game.I would suggest this game to anyone who enjoys side-scrolling Castlevania games, DMC, Chrono Trigger, or the Final Fantasy series. It's not the type of game for everyone, but if you enjoy action RPGs and the JRPG genre I think this is absolutely worth your time and money. It hit almost all of the right buttons for me at the right time, and I basically played this game nonstop from start to finish. Absolutely incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: If there’s anything at all that catches your attention in the first couple hours, then PLEASE see this game through. I know first-hand the game can be damn annoying, plain frustrating at points in the early chapters.However, the combat, the gameplay loop, the intrigue of the cast, the world-building, the dopamine rush of pressing attack to see numbers go up, the sense of wonder finding new legendary gear, the scale of boss fights… if you enjoy JRPGs I’m pretty confident there will be something to grab your attention here. After all, ASTLIBRA is a love letter from KEIZO to JRPGs and its fans.If you are curious then please try the demo. It is 1–2 hours long, and it will be representative of the combat system with some decent upgrades and gear available. It will definitely feel weird in terms of the pacing but that’s for the sake of putting the player in a position where they can experience a well-equipped Hero and some story beats in a condensed experience.I’m taking a break from the game before playing the roguelite DLC, but this game is still very much living rent free in my head. If you enjoy (J)RPGs then I sincerely hope you get to play this game and see it through yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Astlibra has it all. Flashy and fun combat with tons of new skills and abilities to unlock. A story about friendship, family, romance, the dark side of humanity, and fighting against corrupted deities. Graphics which likely utilized assets from every royalty free source imaginable along with monster and character designs from the guy that did a lot of the art for Dragon's Crown. Initially I was lukewarm towards the visuals but they started to grow on me and now I find them quite appealing. Then there's the soundtrack which just kind of pops off for most of the game injecting banger after banger into your eardrums. It's an all around fantastic time and a definite recommendation from me if side scrolling JRPGs, anime, and doujin games are your jam. This is honestly one of my personal favorite games I've played in years and I hope many more can discover it. This game deserves all the love it's been getting and so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's good and probably better in Japanese/Chinese - this is a public warning that you may not experience the 'overwhelmingly positive' vibes the other reviews give off. I'll chuck another 20 hours into it and we will see if the game re-defines my life, gives me a 6-pack and causes me to reach spiritual enlightenment like every other reviewer.Vibe check follows: The systems in this game are incredibly deep and provide an incredible amount of customisation and depth which is a real shame because the weapons all feel very same-y. Heavy weapons feel exactly like magic weapons which feel exactly like shortswords. Combat appears flashy but is pretty shallow when you get into it. It boils down to find the summon with iFrames and abuse it while you spam whatever attack most efficiently builds up the summon gauge. The game feels like it's running at a lower FPS than it is because of all the slowdown when you hit an enemy with a weapon. Combat is like a vintage car, very pretty but you wouldn't want to drive it to work. Art wise, in screenshots it looks incredible - but the animations don't feel fluid. Most enemies and characters feel like cardboard cutouts stuck on ice-cream sticks. Character animations look like they were created with motion tween, 10 000 layers in Photoshop and blutac. Personal taste though - your mileage may vary.People are really hype on the story - leading me to assume they played the game in Japanese or Chinese because some translations to English feel, for lack of a better term, constipated? (Like they're nearly right but still not quite there and it's really difficult to squeak it out and get a good flow going). The developers seem very active and responsive to issues with translation/community though so credit for that.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and enjoyed it overall, but it's hard to recommend generally and I think a lot of issues are being overlooked in the positive reviews I've seen.Pros:* Gameplay is surprisingly fun and in-depth, lots of progression systems - by far the best part of the game* Best battery life I've ever gotten on my Steam Deck, even compared to other 2D games* Funky world setup with an interesting premise* Postgame (avoiding details for spoiler reasons)Cons:* Great concepts, but the writing is a bit of a mess and character writing in general is weak/inconsistent* Some really awful and horribly out-of-character anime cringe especially in Chapters 4-6 that nearly killed the game for me* The game is pretty grindy in the mid-section, and features some obtuse/confusing puzzle design especially in Chapter 6. Expect lots of backtracking and repeated environmentsThe gameplay is a lot of fun, and the game pulls a fakeout that I think is pretty novel. But the overall writing execution just isn't that good - characters constantly make baffling choices to advance the plot, details get overlooked everywhere for convenience, etc. Most of the characters are very inconsistently written (the worst being turning characters into sex offenders as a joke out of nowhere), which made it much harder to get invested in them.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I (largely) absolutely love this game. But, there are some parts that are so bad it could deter people from playing this game. But I think I've got a succinct reason, and that's because every single mobility or function (back dash, double jump, **invulnerability for a brief moment after taking damage**, etc) is locked/hidden. The most important one being the ever so brief period of invulnerability after taking a hit. Without that, you can and most likely will be killed by an attack you get caught in, forcing you to start back at the beginning of a gauntlet. My only other gripe about this game that some of you may not mind, is the random barely story related busty babes with jigglies in battle with me, all but hitting me with their cleavage as an attack. For me that was my initial experience. HOWEVER!! When you get those abilities, and youre more mobile, you truly start to love this game. Every weapon, every armor, every shield (and some accessories), all show up on your character. Each piece must be crafted, and actually used in battle to get its benefit and it makes you experience weapons you wouldnt normally use. The areas are fairly huge and have such incredible detail. Every creature is unique. There are so many ways to play the game and alter your character. But as a true metroidvania lover, you ask "What about the secrets?" This game has so many damn secrets and things that are hidden that when you discover them, it kind of gives you a sense of wonder. Highly recommend this game to anyone who loves metroidvania style games with exploration!

_childDocuments_.review: 17.3 hours - initial review:It looks weird, the grinding is heavy, The dialogue is difficult to read sometimes (Slight leniency for it needing to be translated) and the inventory/crafting is kinda rough.... but I can't stop playing this game.For some reason fighting is addicting. I can't explain why it is, it just is. The heavy grinding is slightly redeemed due to how addicting and satisfying it is to mash the attack button and whip out different spells.There is an absurd abundance to collect. You get skills, and you get weapons that you need to use to get more skills, and then you level up to get more skills, and you level up to get points, and you collect gems to get stats that also give you more skills and it just keeps going, and normally I hate it, but for some reason it's fun here, I really don't know why.I give it a recommend if you want a game with an absurd amount of content and some addicting hack and slash game play. I don't think I'm far enough into the story to know if I can recommend that yet, but I'm definitely wondering what's gonna happen next.Edit @ 30.9 hours in: The  dialogue is still really rough to get through some times. It's hard to write good RPG dialogue, but when it's read out one line at a time which is sometimes just 2 words and a bunch of ellipses, it really gets rough. However, the story has really taken shape pretty well in my opinion, and the gameplay loop is still fun.One thing I will say is that I widely underestimated the importance of Defense and HP. All the way through , I had no HP, and just max Speed and Attack.  hit me like a truck, and I basically just switched all my level up points into Defense and HP and my damage really didn't suffer that much, but my survivability went wayyy up. Still having a good time, looking forward to the rest of the story.Final Edit 37 hours: The story ended up being a lot more interesting than I thought it would be. , however, is BRUTAL. There's one enemy in particular that kind of ruined this section for me, and I knew I was close to the end, so was more just looking to get through the game which made it more annoying. I was wrong however that I was close to the end! Seriously the amount of content this game has is ridiculous, if you enjoy hacking and slashing and grinding, this game is pretty great.

_childDocuments_.review: This thing is bizarre, I haven't even finished it at ~65 hours and it's so much fun I haven't even registered the fact that I've already spent a AAA RPG amount of time with it, with the ending not even being in sightHow does this game have zero visibility while simultaneously having one of the best review ratings on Steam I've ever encountered, as well as (going by the % of people completing certain achievements) about a quarter of anyone who's purchased this has played the game to full completion (which again is a time investment of ~80 hours)?!If you like at least a few of the following:- Platformers- Action RPGs- JRPGs- Very blatantly Japanese game design- Mysterious juego aesthetics- Involved narrative- Consistent presentation- Item management- Obscure secrets and hidden content- Character builds- FFX Sphere grid / FF12 License boardyou're guaranteed to enjoy yourself with this.It's obvious that this was created by a person who had their taste shaped by predominately Japanese games, wouldn't be surprised if a whole slew Falcom games provided inspiration for this (old school PC-88 Xanadu comes to mind a lot), especially also when some of the background tracks are absolute bangers which sound like they were workshopped by Falcom Sound Team JDK and provided royalty free or something.The game just keeps throwing more content at you. I genuinely thought I'd reached the end about two times and still got blindsided when it occurred for a third time.The only thing I can knock on a bit is the sporadically horny writing which sometimes comes out of nowhere, but this game is otherwise such a beautiful work of passion I can forgive it a few negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat's got that addictive mix of simple yet satisfying. Weapon skills are especially fun to grind out and the merching/crafting system adds a lot of playtime to the areas without making it feel like a pointless level grind. Story's not the most original or anything, but I'd put it a bit above serviceable. There's been a few points where I've been legitimately interested in what's going on. All that aside, this game gets weird/gross horny almost out of nowhere around the 10-15 hour point. I can put up with my fair share of anime cringe, Neon White was unironically GOTY, but there's a line man. Once you get to chapter... I believe it's 5, the game just starts getting overtly sexual in a way that's more than a bit uncomfortable. The big tiddy anime girl goddess(es) were one thing, the wink-wink-nudge-nudge 'one bed' bit was pushing it, the lesbians who are only lesbian to talk about ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was a bit much for my taste, forcing the sorceress character to parade around in lingerie (something she explicitly doesn't want to do) is where it started to feel unforgivably gross, and following up by having her be told by the leads that she got blackout drunk and started stripping for the town is where I decided I wasn't recommending this game to human people. The worst of it is that it comes (almost, there had been a few sex jokes before that) out of nowhere so far into the game. If this is where you're going, you've gotta frontload it a bit so people aren't getting to that point then being annoyed with the content. If all that had happened in chapter 1/2, it still wouldn't've been my cup of tea, but I at least wouldn't feel like the game tricked me into getting invested in the combat systems before dropping the bomb.

_childDocuments_.review: 60 hours of pure gameplay bliss and my personal favorite game of the year. I BEG the developer to implement some sort of NG+ system down the line. I just want a reason to keep playing the game over and over again.The combat system starts off very basic, and as you go along it starts to become insanely fast-paced by the end of the game when you’re practically lawn-mowering enemies (unless you’re playing at Hell or higher diff).The mechanics of strengthening your character are diverse, yet not confusing at all. You have a few routes to go about it: 1) Leveling up, 2) Karon skills (which are essentially combat mechanic modifiers), and 3) Ability tree (FFX/PoE style grid-like stat tree). Much later on in the game you will unlock additional systems that make progression a bit more refreshing.As for the story, I happened to enjoy most of it a lot, although it may be hit-or-miss for people. If you don’t like the stereotypical anime tropes of JRPGs, you won’t like the story or dialogue in this game, either. However, if that’s your thing as it is with me, you might really be intrigued with the story. I found the characters to be quite charming and lively, and the protagonist, although silent, manages to display a broad range of characteristics in spite of it. You really get the sense that the protagonist has his own clear-cut personality and identity despite being silent (though  at that point, why even make him a silent protagonist to begin with?)9.5/10 gameplay, 7/10 story, 6.5/10 visuals, 8/10 music, and overall a 9/10 experience. It really does give the impression that one person put their heart and soul into this project.I thoroughly enjoyed staying up all night playing this game during my work week.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITED REVIEW: Well, I suppose this is one instance where I have to eat crow (heh, apologies to the little buddy in this game). To use the Shaq meme, "I have to apologize, I wasn't really familiar with your game."Have I changed my mind about the critiques I mentioned? No, the translation still hurts the game and the graphics are still somewhat underwhelming. However, after finishing it and experiencing it firsthand, I can say without reservation that the story is SO good that even despite the terrible translation it carries the game and makes it a must-play. I don't want to spoil anyone but it really is the sort of thing you have to experience for yourself, just hearing about it doesn't do it justice. It's been a long time since I actually felt emotionally attached to a game's characters, but this one actually did it, and I got tears in my eyes during one of the climactic fights (you guys will know the one). So yeah, I'm turning this review from negative to positive and encouraging everyone who reads it to forget my earlier churlishness and buy this game. Just try to ignore the bad translation (so far, hopefully they'll patch it soon).A couple other reasons for a positive revision. First, when you get a wider variety of combat skills, it really does become pretty satisfying and engaging. The fact that there are so many mistranslations (for instance, the description for one crucial skill says it recovers ST when it actually recovers HP) hurts it, but like I said above, they should fix it with a new translation soon. Second, while it's still not genuine Vanillaware quality, some of the boss sprites, especially near the end, do look super cool. Third, the music is MUCH better than I gave it credit for at first. Most of it is taken from free stuff, but by the end you can tell the dev became an expert at choosing good songs, as a lot of the themes and event music are absolutely perfect and wonderful to listen to, I especially love the Belkade late-game themes.Finally, more than anything else, there's one primary reason I revised my review to a positive one: One of the devs themselves (specifically the publisher) took my concerns to heart. In general, I'll almost always support a dev if they acknowledge my suggestions and make changes even if I'm dissatisfied with a game at first. I did this with They Must Be Billions, didn't like it at first but changed my negative review to positive after they released a patch making the game less annoying and adding more content. The publisher, WhisperQ, acknowledged my complaints with the translation and has mentioned there'll be a patch to fix it soon! So I'm definitely all about supporting folks who want to improve even if they've made a mistake, and I can't wait for the revamped translation so I can enjoy the game as it was really meant to be played. I now encourage all of you to buy it, support the devs, and join me!(OLD REVIEW)First solidly negative review I've written in a while, but while I really tried to give this game a fair shot, it has too many problems for me to recommend it. Despite some extremely good points--15 years of effort, an absolutely massive, in-depth combat system and art from Shigatake, one of the Vanillaware guys--the flaws of this game make it impossible for me to recommend or even justify paying 20 dollars for. Specifically, like I said, it has one of the most in-depth combat systems you can find anywhere, but the atrocious translation hurts it severely. There's a huge amount of skills to unlock, many of which are absolutely crucial, but mistranslations or outrightly incorrect translations make it very difficult to tell which skills you actually need--you need to use some of the guides friendly people on Steam have provided, which isn't acceptable for a professionally produced game. The control mapping is also absolutely terrible. Thankfully, you can change some of the more annoying button mapping, like the dash and enter room buttons being the same, but there's a shield bash move that makes some of the platforming segments nearly impossible when it activates when you don't want it to, and you can't disable that without either not using shields at all (locking yourself out of a pretty significant number of abilities and gameplay choices) or going through a bizarrely arcane method, one again described by some good steam folks. Like I also mentioned, the art from Shigatake is very nice, but unfortunately you won't find the delightful backgrounds of Odin Sphere or 13 Sentinels in this game, because the great artist just did character portraits--the backgrounds, terrain, etc. looks like cheap freeware fare. The plot, from what I've gathered, is actually relatively compelling despite how it starts off as not a basic riff off an old-school Ys style platformer, but again, the poor translation cripples its impact. As much as I wanted to love this game I cannot in good conscience recommend it, though if my refund request doesn't go through since I've beaten the first chapter, I might play through it some more if I'm stuck with it after this. We'll see if I change this review.

_childDocuments_.review: A Diamond in the rough. It's all here, though. Better than decent story, fantastic music, great combat. Expect a lot of grinding if you're a completionist like me, but the rewards have so far been 100% worth the effort.If I have a single gripe, it's this: While the game keeps the fanservice and horniness to a pretty low level for the most part, when it does come up, it's the kind of writing that you'd expect from a 14 year old. I've seen worse in AAA titles, but I feel like it doesn't add anything to the story or characters when it happens, and takes away from the experience. Thankfully, they've been pretty short, so easy to get through and forget.Don't let my above statement prevent you from giving the game a shot. Edit, now that I've Finished the game. It's a solid 9.6/10. IT would have been my easiest recommendation for a game, and a nearly perfect score, but DEAR LORD, the unnecessary horny dialogue, boss models and cutscenes. If I could, I'd cut all of them out completely, and nothing of value would be lost. It really is what drags down what should be a shining example of an indie action RPG. Those instances alone make it hard to recommend without a huge warning.

_childDocuments_.review: A game comes to mind when I think of Astlibra. Infinite Space. A game that I'm sure only a very select few people would even know. It was a game that really brought home what it's like to go on an adventure, think to yourself "well what could possibly top what I just experienced?", and proceed to answer that question with something even crazier and more exciting, constantly, in that same game. Likewise in Astlibra, the game kept going, and I fell deeper and deeper into its story and world. There's very few games that do this. Other examples are games from the Ys series, Labyrinth of Refrain, Octopath Traveler. It's the escalation of problems that really drives it home for me, and I've always held Infinite Space as King when it comes to that. Astlibra however almost gives it a run for its money. The story gets crazier and stranger, but it stays true to its rules and you really just want to keep playing to see what on earth happens next.On top of all that, the gameplay loop and progression is pure crack. The various mechanics to strengthen your character is very well done, and with its real-time combat, really just makes you want to keep killing ♥♥♥♥.I really can't sing many more praises than this. Astlibra will have a permanent home in my heart as one of the greatest RPGs I've ever played of all time, and I think it's the games that take up real estate in your memories that are exceptional.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 8.5/10ASTLIBRA Revision is a delightful blend of retro RPG nostalgia and modern gameplay innovations. It captivates with its engaging story, deep mechanics, and charming pixel art, making it a must-play for fans of classic role-playing games.- Engaging Storyline: ASTLIBRA Revision boasts a rich narrative that draws players into a world filled with mystery, magic, and memorable characters. The story is well-crafted, with twists and turns that keep players invested from start to finish.- Deep Combat System: The game features a robust combat system that combines strategic planning with real-time action. Players can customize their character's abilities and equipment to suit their playstyle, adding layers of depth and complexity to each encounter.- Stunning Pixel Art: ASTLIBRA Revision's pixel art is a feast for the eyes, capturing the essence of classic RPGs while incorporating modern touches. The detailed environments, character designs, and animations create a visually enchanting experience.- Atmospheric Soundtrack: The game's soundtrack perfectly complements its nostalgic aesthetic, with a mix of melodic tunes and ambient sounds that enhance the overall atmosphere. Each track is crafted to evoke emotion and immerse players in the game's world.- Extensive Content: With numerous quests, side missions, and hidden secrets, ASTLIBRA Revision offers a wealth of content to explore. The game encourages exploration and rewards players with valuable items, lore, and character development opportunities.- Steep Learning Curve: ASTLIBRA Revision can be challenging for newcomers, with complex mechanics and a high difficulty level. The game requires patience and strategic thinking, which may deter players looking for a more casual experience.- Occasional Pacing Issues: Some parts of the game may feel slow or drawn out, particularly during extensive dialogue sequences or repetitive side quests. These pacing issues can interrupt the flow of the game and test players' patience.- Minor Technical Glitches: While generally well-polished, ASTLIBRA Revision does have occasional technical glitches, such as minor bugs or performance hitches. These issues are not game-breaking but can be a slight annoyance.Overall, ASTLIBRA Revision is a fantastic tribute to the golden age of RPGs, offering a compelling mix of classic charm and modern gameplay. Its engaging storyline, deep combat system, and beautiful pixel art make it a standout title for RPG enthusiasts. _childDocuments_.review: There are a few things to note about Astlibra before I get into the positives about this game and why you should play it, as they could turn you off from playing it. However, I will say that if you don't mind anime, have enjoyed hacks and slashes, and don't mind a bit of a grind, you will really like this game. However, if these things turn you off, don't bother; otherwise, go and buy it. This game can be very easily ruined by spoilers, as the story is a big selling point.With that out of the way, the games are amazing, and if you have ever enjoyed games like Kingdom Hearts, youll also like this, though unlike KH, this game is entirely in 2D, which I think doesn't work too well with a hack and slash, but I think the game does well regardless. Only towards the end and EX maps do the bosses and enemies get too tanky, and you have to start grinding if you really want to start doing damage again.Now what I think is its best selling point is its story. I'll try to avoid spoiling anything, but let's just say that not only is it compelling, all of the twists and turns are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wild that the game at a few points of the story tries to lull you into a false sense of security only to pull the rug out of under you the whole time. Don't get me wrong, towards the end it starts to feel a little annoying, but most of the time at the end youll feel satisfied with where the story ended up.Now its not all sunshine and rainbows, however, as mentioned before, this game not only has a bit of a grind, but unless you follow a walkthrough, not only will you miss things that can be important to the story, you may also miss items that make the game 10 times easier (make sure to 100% the arena). Also, having to level up every piece of equipment is annoying, and I wish you had the option of just skipping leveling some items as all weapons and armor are worth leveling up either for the karon crytal or the special passive.All in all, it was a great experience that I won't forget anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Come for the gameplay, stay for the sweet tunes. Reminded me a lot of Wanderers from Ys (Ys III.)The Good:- Gameplay is pretty snappy and there's a ton of options to tweak things how you like. Even a few accessibility ones! (My poor thumb after not using the 'hold to continuously attack' one for most of the game.)- Most of the music is great and can live rent free in my head for a bit.- The story has a bunch of good twists and turns and it goes some interesting places with it, even if it takes a bit to get there.- The skip functionality works and is very good.The Bad:-If you don't trim some of your combat options it's pretty easy to end up fuddling about a bit. Hovering in midair instead of downstabbing a fool happened to me a lot.- Difficulty is a bit wonky. For me the toughest boss that I died the most at was the Chapter 6 mid-boss. Also some of the enemies there caused plenty of game overs for me. Very much a bell curve with dips and peaks.- The story leans a bit too much on telling rather than showing. Lots of places that could be improved with visual aids or animations instead of text boxes. (Really wish there was a world map.)- Similarly the formatting of the intro movie between each chapter like a book/episode would have been much better if it actually changed as the game went along. It does not. I guess it could be handy as a reminder? But really it mostly reminded me of the skip function.- One character has a whole extra pile of misery to go on top of the misery they already have and it's just too much misery man. You don't need to escalate with that! It's counterproductive!The Annoying:- Heavy use of already-overused tropes. Oh there's a pervert, oh there's mention of a hot springs, time until pervert peeps at the hot spring t-minus 10 minutes. It feels obligatory and low effort.- One song for an encounter in the postscript. The first time it's neat and spooky and weird and then the other five or so times it's just annoying. Much like that encounter really, so at least it's fitting! Bad earworm though.- There's one side-quest that requires you to collect every weapon, armor and shield in the game. There's an item that tells you what gear recipes you've gotten and another that tells you what inventory items you've collected, but nothing for gear. It was rather annoying, not challenging old man.

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, good visuals, and fun gameplay. By chapter 7 the combat does start to feel a bit tedious but the story will help you push through.The puzzles in chapter 6 are all horrible and should be reworked, redone, or removed. (One of them requires lighting wood on fire. Torches? Don't work. Fire breathing spell? Nope. You need pine resin + a flame arrow.)Playing on the easiest difficulty will be easy until chapter 5. Chapter 6 and 7 get very very very difficult, even on the easiest difficulty. Playing on anything above Normal difficulty means you will die in one or two hits. Not fun.I suggest playing the game for the story rather than the gameplay itself. Other games do this type of combat far better (Bloodstained for example, Rogue Legacy 2, etc). The combat isn't bad but it just isn't unique nor is it as fun as other titles. It is also frustratingly difficult. [Not to mention that underwater cave section where you have to travel through three different rooms, while underwater. Only to find out you can't get air unless you used a bomb on a specific spot. The last save area was several rooms away - meaning you would have to redo this room several times. That is just bad game design.]

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly enjoying this game so far. It's a really interesting and slightly complex story but I've been interested the entire time, even enough to read additional in game lore books and the like. For a JRPG the grind doesn't feel all too bad, but I also haven't done any end game stuff yet, so I could be very wrong about this soon, so far though resources/money/experience and equipment mastery have been easy to gain and have consistently grown in proportion to the difficulty. This game is an action JRPG, and a unique one at that. While the animations look a bit choppy, the game play is quite smooth, and it encourages the use of all skills at your disposal, the controls are very polished in this regard as well, the game feels fun and intuitive to play. This game is either a collectathon enjoyer's worst nightmare or dream game. There is a ton of things to collect whether it be magic abilities, weapons and materials, equipment skills, filling out the "growth" map., etc. A ton to do, however it's made more rewarding due to the fact that you can easily plan out very efficient farming routes for both enemies and resources all while swapping in and out weapons/shields and armor to max out equipment skills or get an item for 'mastering' the particular weapon or armor all at once. Also by equipment skills I mean abilities like passive upgrades to attack speed, or elemental damage, or even item magnet abilities. You can use them for free if you have the weapon or armor equipped, or you also have a growing ability to use unequipped but mastered skills which grows over time. The actual combat itself, while it feels nice does get a bit mundane as eventually when you get good at it, it's quite easy at normal difficulty. There is a variety of things you can do combat wise, and it grows over time as you collect combat abilities. Though these you usually get from chests it seems. Blocking is valuable as well, it's great for projectiles and protects against status ailments. You also can utilize the invincibility frames you get when you use the magic in this game, and you use both ranged and melee abilities along with magic as sort of a catch all Gary Stu type. On top of this you also have a variety of items you can use to fit any situation, from all enemies in a room being heavily damaged, to throwing an arrow by hand which is surprisingly powerful early on. The game also utilizes a delayed item use system. So you use a healing item, a progress bar appears, and then the item is used. If you are struck/leave that zone etc it will cancel it. It hasn't been difficult to break away from fights to heal/shoot a bow at a distance as well. No autosave system, save often, and when you interact with a save point all enemies not in that zone are resurrected. If you leave your zone and come back those enemies do respawn as well.There is a lot of depth to this game too. An arena with multiple and varied "cups" ranging from platforming  and combat challenges to speed challenges. You are able to backtrack after you've progressed to a certain point in the story, so don't overly stress on leaving things behind. Though the catch is you have to complete the chapter again. Makes the game ideal for speed runners I guess. You even get your own house and back yard. Unknown if any visual or functional customization is possible. There is a lot of freedom in character customization as well. You can allocate 5 points to attributes every level, but you can reallocate them as you see fit at specific points scattered throughout the game, and there is some strategy to this, even terrain dependent strategy. You're well served just bumping attack, defense, and health too, at least as far as I've gotten in the game.There are many puzzles, and a lot of context clues as you watch cutscenes. This game is cutscene heavy, so for those of you who may remember that boss fight with Riku during the old PS2 KH1 days you can rejoice, for this game features a skip button.It's a semi silent protagonist. I think it's deliberate, as the character will talk in game, but you can't see his words. There is always context that let's you know what he's talking about, but let's you sort of fill in the blanks of how he communicates it with your own imagination.This game plays excellently on Steam Deck. There's some choppy audio, but I've not been bothered enough to try and fix it, so there may be a workaround for it I just haven't utilized. It's also really good with the battery life. Like you're hitting the top end of the "possible hours" of a single charge. Though that may be obvious as its not that graphics intensive. Overall I definitely recommend this game, there's a lot to do and it's very approachable but if you want to can turn the difficulty up to 11. I haven't tried that yet so I don't know how the challenge is balanced, I would say it's likely a damage sponge method given the health pools of some bosses. This is speculation though, and it could be user error with regards to my damage output, so your milage may vary. Lastly, it's pretty clear a lot of love and care went into this game, and I think the developer nailed something really cool, unique and fun to play here. There's even a demo if you really need to see for yourself. I believe that this game is definitely worth picking up.*Edit: I am incorrect about having to complete whole chapters over if you go back to them.Game finished edit: I can honestly say this is a must buy for me. Probably if not definitely my GOTY. I literally played non-stop until I finished it, and I didn't feel like any part of it was a chore except one specific thing at the absolute very last part of the game, but even then the methodology is interesting and fun for the most part. You're doing yourself a disservice if you like anything that you see on this page and don't pick it up in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I've written a whole thesis on this game over the course of playing it, but at this moment, I have a short way to figure out if this game is for you.Do you like Grinding, Interesting Gameplay, Carrots On Sticks That Incentivize Collecting And Levelling Every Weapon, Shield, And Armor in the Game?If so, regardless of any negatives, you'll probably enjoy the game. The Core Gameplay was very fun for me, playing on Hell Difficulty, it was challenging, and figuring out strategies I enjoyed was fun. Certain areas were harder than others, but I was adamant on buying and levelling every new weapon, shield, and armor in each chapter, to stay on top of what new abilities I could use. Genuinely, the gameplay is the Shining Star that is this incredibly unique video game. Notice how I (and probably others) haven't once mentioned that this game looks like a Bitcoin Miner Fever Dream, with all of it's stock photos, fighting PNGs of Flowers and ♥♥♥♥. That's because by the 20th hour, you'll be used to it. It's incredible what the human mind can adapt to.The negatives for me are: The story is ALMOST good, it's interesting enough to keep me reading it, but good god this game was so clearly written by one person who shoves as much horny, fetishistic, 14 year old humor in it it's insufferable. The first few times I wasn't sure if he was just trying to write some fan fiction or not, by the end of the game, (with a very specific "If you don't wake up, I'm going to sit on your face and fart" moment) I knew he wasn't even writing the fan service for the fans, but for himself. Dialogue is basically Horrible to Insufferable whenever you hear that Goofy Music that is always playing right before one of the characters completely ruins the tone and mood that the overarching story has been setting up just to make a "WOAH SHE'S GOT FAT BOOZOONKOOS" joke. Now I obviously want to and AM faulting the game for these moments, but I have to give credit where it's due, you can simply press Start and Skip literally ANY dialogue in the game, even if it's one single message box. And it skips Very Fast. Big ups for that, but the story was just interesting enough to make me read it, and also hate the game for ruining what it was setting up.Another negative that really depends on your Taste and Preference, the music. Some of the music is good, some of it is laughably out of place. I couldn't help but burst out laughing every single time I heard a Monstercat-esque copyright free dubstep song just start blaring over what would otherwise be a somewhat interesting or important moment. It completely kills the vibe sometimes. You don't get used to it, at least I didn't. An important thing to note about all of these faults is that this was originally a browser game, when you learn that, and learn that it was put online in about 2011, a lot of these choices make much more sense. The dubstep, the horny fanservice, the Stock Photo Trees and Clouds, the RPGMaker lookin Characters, the general way the plot goes in general I've seen like 20 times at least in these types of browser / flash games tbh. Just thought I'd mention that as well.The game genuinely adds 3 or 4 new mechanics to the Post Game Chapter (After the Final Chapter), which is awesome, because they're good mechanics that spice up the Core Gameplay, and the Core Gameplay is the only thing that kept me playing, but I wish they had been added in far earlier than Post-Script. Mostly because, in general Post-Script feels like it overstays it's welcome. I got to Post-Script 60 hours in. I have 80 hours now completing the game, and I intentionally didn't do the "Good Ending" yet because that would be another 2 hours of grinding (not complaining about the grinding, I was just ready to be Finished with this game 10 hours ago).I hate giving number ratings because they're arbitrary as hell, I very much enjoyed my time actually playing the game, theorycrafting, doing fake math with the Libra Scale Balancing, optimizing my Berserk Usage, etc. Reading the story and dialogue, horrible, it might be for you, it certainly was NOT for me. Take that as you will, have a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall rating for me: 9.5/10This game looks great, the controls are tight, the music does a great job at being interesting and appropriate for the locations, environments are highly varied, enemy design is top-notch, combat is fast-paced and frenetic, and the story is absolutely incredible.  But none of these things compare to how interesting the progression systems in this game are.  You will be given a huge variety of methods to increase your character's abilities, with new systems appearing throughout your journey even into the endgame.  The epilogue alone introduces multiple new systems that completely redefine every aspect of the game if you delve into it.  In short: There's plenty here to keep min-maxers busy.  These systems are accompanied by some great QoL features (such as being able to freely reallocate skill points as needed) that make grinding optional but still quite rewarding.  Each piece of equipment feels unique when you get it, and EVERYTHING is useful in the endgame, so you have a ton of freedom to play how you like.  The only criticism I have of the game is that difficulty settings have no impact other than boosting/nerfing enemy stats, which means the highest difficulty is just smacking around slimes for 3 hours while trying not to get hit more than once or twice.  Higher difficulties slow the game down without making enemies more interesting to deal with, but given that this is the industry standard anyway it's more of a nitpick than a real complaint. For its price this game is an absolute must buy imo.  Don't sleep on this title!
