_childDocuments_.review: Good story,great visuals,amazing music and some very challenging puzzles (I dont usually play puzzle games so I had to look for a video guide for a few puzzles),funnily enough the Ina Jones achievement (complete all the rope/chain sequences without falling) took me longer than The Watchful eye achievement (dont die during the last boss),because I skipped one of the 2 ropes next to each other during the first few chapters,and you need to have it fall to the ground for the achievement. Overall this is a great game and I definitely recommend it,even to those who don't usually play this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Aspire: Ina’s Tale is a surprisingly nice puzzle platformer game. The game looks beautiful and together with the lovely music it creates a nice, tranquil vibe. Ina’s story is abstract and inspirational, which I really like. The characters you meet along the way all have their own personality and I really liked that. Even though you don’t see them for very long, I feel like I know them. There’s one gameplay issue I encountered: I had difficulty picking up some of the small moveable blocks, especially in the dungeon area. Next to that, I would have liked the game to be a bit longer, since it’s so good. I would have loved to see more areas of the tower, since we only really got to see three. The puzzle elements were very nice, though, and I liked the various crystals needed to progress through the puzzles. Overall Aspire is a very enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Aspire: Ina's Tale is a platforming side-scrolling game where we play as a princess who has the power to control spirit to move, extend or light up platforms to escape from a Tower that is stealing the dreams from people within. For me, this game was a lot of fun to traverse to fix the Tower by solving some interesting puzzles that get progressively harder and a little bit more complex as we get closer to the end. The boss chase was also intense, it really put your knowledge of the mechanics to the test, even though, (at least for me) my frame rate dropped during the chase it was still a decent one, not as fast pace as Ori and the blind forest first chase of course (mostly due to the music), but still up there with how they incorporated the mechanic in it.For me, this game was a nice, colourful invention with unique crystallize patterns design and a variety of dungeon creations, if anyone is curious about getting this game, maybe wishlist it and wait for the discount along with the artbook as it seems a few people completed it around the 2 hours mark, ignoring my playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: is a “cinematic” platformer with light puzzles and a few chase sequences. The story follows the titular character, Ina, who is trying to escape from the crumbling sci-fi-esque magical Tower. The story is linear, the dialogue options do not affect anything, and there is no exploration. The non-playable characters appear once to say a few lines and to be shown again only during the credits. The story significance of the spirits goes against their gameplay usage - they are energy sources to activate platforms and to be left in those platforms or at the barriers between the puzzles, which is deeply ironic, considering that the main character is a priestess who spends a few minutes narrating that she is going to save them. The platforming part clashes with the cinematic animations - the character is slow, clunky, and uncomfortable to control. While the controls are partially rebindable (can’t rebind the movement keys), some actions use the same key with the difference being tapping and holding it. The graphics, while very lovely, also prevent from seeing clearly whether a platform has been activated or not or whether something is an obstacle or a part of the scenery. The few early-game chase sequences are very easy and require only holding the movement key away from the foe. The actual issue is the timed puzzles which, as mentioned, do not work well with the character controls. During one of them, I struggled to determine if I got the logic wrong or just could not perform the actions quick enough (it was the latter). The music became rather annoying at that point, so I turned it off. The final boss, on the other hand, was generally fine - it did not kill instantly and there was enough time to pull/push/climb all the blocks. The game saves the progress on the generously-placed checkpoints and it is possible to roll back to any of the previous ones. While the game itself is rather short, about 2-3 hours, the quality of the gameplay and the story makes it a positive quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing experience, Halfway through my playthrough I felt compelled to write a review for this game, but I held off until I experienced everything this game had to offer. I went in with a pretty open mind, expecting a simple puzzle game with some gimmicky mechanics or graphics, but this game far exceeded my expectations. I've never been so invested into a game on my first playthrough, I'm extremely happy I decided to play this.The gameplay is fairly surface level, I can definitely tell this game isn't really focused on the gameplay elements more than the story and environments. It was still enjoyable but there wasn't really anything challenging and I never found myself getting stuck anywhere.The graphics, wow. Absolutely stunning, and one of the greatest looking games I've ever played. The massive almost otherworldly looking structures and objects paired with the music creates a sense of scale with just how big the tower really is. I found myself stopping multiple times just to admire the backgrounds and scenery. This artstyle is beautiful, and I hope to see more games like this in the future.The music, oh my god. This has one of the most beautiful soundtracks. Each song has such an impact that it will really resonate with you after your playthrough. The music is incredible. It compliments everything going on in the game perfectly. The sense of curiosity, fear, hope, feeling overwhelmed, the music portrays all of these emotions at the perfect moments in the game, especially during the last part, I was really feeling the panic and stress there.I haven't felt a special feeling of immersion in a while, this game brought that feeling back to me. Do not play this game for just the gameplay, play it for the experience, letting yourself follow the story, admire the scenery, talk to each character and listen to how they express themselves and the stories they have to tell. I cannot recommend this game enough, and it is well worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Aspire: Ina's Tale is a mellow, thoughtful little puzzle platformer, which brings some interesting philosophical writing, that all too often veers into quasi-intellectual wank.Positives:  -Music-  It won't win any awards but it wins over your ears by virtue of being meditative and subtle, without huge theatrical swells.  Again, nothing really special, but it accentuates the gameplay without getting in the way.-Graphics-  Not fancy at all, but highly evocative and with some occasional flourishes and effects that don't come across as gilding the lily but rather as genuinely special touches.  These are stylized by the way, not photo-realistic, but if that's your jam you'll really enjoy the visual palette.-Gameplay-  Some may lambaste it as being too samey and too easy.....but I just had a really good time, even if I was only occasionally "challenged".  Not everything has to be a white-knuckle battle between you and the  a quiet, story-based platformer, non-stop action and rapidly escalating skill requirements would seriously detract from the enjoyment.Meh:-Plot-  It doesn't really get much past the surface of the storyline and it is just a bit too vague and up its own rear-end (it seems to think it's deeper and more intellectual/philosophical than it actually is) to be 100% enjoyable.-Controls-  For the most part tight as a drum, which sure is what you want in a platformer....but occasionally it's a little too floaty, especially in the last "battle", where some heretofore unseen mechanics and gameplay themes come into play.All in all, it's very enjoyable, but it's a little bit less than the sum of its parts.  Recommended with minor reservations.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, beautiful levels that are pleasing on the eye. Game itself is not too difficult but offers enough of a challenge to keep it interesting from beginning to end. It won't take up too much of your time and is definitely worth a purchase to waste away a quiet afternoon. Definitely recommend! 👍

It only takes like 2-3 hours to complete and I think it's worth a playthrough. It might not knock your socks off but it definitely was an enjoyable time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great art style and good music.  Short but sweet game.  Story is somewhat vague, and the gameplay is solid for the most part.  Could use a bit of polish, but perfectly acceptable for an indie game.  Had a difficult time with the final boss, because I kept dying faster than I could deduce where I was supposed to go.  Kinda wish the path was more apparent, because the environment often blends together.  That being said, definitely pick this game up for the Autumn or Winter Sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of have mixed feelings about this game. First of all, it was really short. I love puzzles and this game had quite a few of them, though they seemed pretty easy to me and I got the hang of them very early on. I would've liked it more if there were more complex or tricky puzzles (like the ones we had toward the end) and if it wasn't so short.The next thing that makes me so unsure of my feeling toward Aspire is the story. I kind of expected it to be deep or at least emotional, but it didn't leave me with such impressions at the end. I liked the characters and conversations they had with Ina, and I liked the world too, but I feel the story and the message it tried to convey weren't as polished as it should've been.But I gotta say the art was beautiful and the soundtracks were amazing. There were also lots of save points that made backtracking super easy. Overall, I enjoyed it and had fun working on the puzzles and meeting the characters. So, yeah. I recommend it but treat it as something casual, or you might feel a bit disappointed at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: While this is by no means the best puzzle platformer ever conceived it is still one worth playing, because even though there's some shortcomings in terms of gameplay & technicalities, there's still a work of art underneath. Let us dissect.Just one glance at the trailers or screenshots should be enough to convince you wether or not to pick up this game, as visuals really are the main appeal here. I for one found them to be absolutely gorgeous from start to finish, especially in the more verdant midgame area. Every screen has something nice to look at, wether it's odd geometric shapes, gorgeous godrays or just nice compositions. The artists really knocked it out of the park here. It really reminded me of Gris at times, which is a testament to how good the game looks. However not only the visuals but the designs of the characters and environments are awesome as well. With the architect and guiding light designs being my favorite. In terms of music; the score, while not as memorable as something like gris or inmost, is still beautiful and fitting. I'm going through loss currently so the soothing soundtrack helped me relax and find some peace in a time where i'm needing it most. These are the game's biggest positives, and in my opinion, reason enough to pick up the game.However there's also some issues that plague the game, mainly gameplay. This game's main puzzle mechanics are really basic and as a result so are the puzzles. I wasn't really engaged or challenged solving the puzzles because of this, and if you don't care about visuals but do about good puzzles then this may not be for you. The story was also not as engaging as some others gems found within the genre.Lastly there's polish and while the game was bug free for me the loading times were, for such a simple game, really long. Failing a jump or anything else that would reset you made you go through a 5-10 seconds loading screen. I know that's still pretty short but most puzzle platformers have near instant respawns. In the end this isn't a dealbreaker as the game has different strenghts and is short enough to keep you engaged without the load times ever getting too much to bear. It's a nice, beautiful and short game that's decently priced for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my praise is directed to the game's aesthetics. It's just so gorgeous! On par with Gris, methinks. But unlike Gris, this game has actual gameplay.Most of the puzzles are enjoyable, with a frustrating few. For a puzzler that involves timing, the controls shouldn't be this finicky and there could've been more wiggle room for some of the timed puzzles. Doable, but still. The story was a little meh too.All in all still enjoyable, but walk away if you don't want timed puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: In my review of Aspire: Ina’s Tale I won’t be revealing any plot spoilers. I’ll only provide a brief synopsis of the story and I’ll discuss the plot and characters featured in the first half hour of the game. I’ll also explain game mechanics introduced later in the game, but I won’t be spoiling how the protagonist obtains these powers.In Aspire: Ina’s Tale you control Ina, a young woman who needs to escape a mysterious area known as the Tower. Her goal is to get back home, to a town called Kamiura, where she lives with her father. Ina is a priestess and she learned the profession from her father. She had a lot of responsibility in her hometown, from performing prayers, conducting ceremonies in front of people, and even fasting all day.As she journeys through the Tower she meets a wide variety of characters. You can talk to these NPCs as you travel through different areas, and there are branching dialog options that allow you to respond positively or negatively. Your dialog choices don’t change the story, but it is certainly interesting to see different kinds of responses.One of the earliest encounters you’ll have in the game are with two NPCs named Thief and Joker, who help explain more about what the Tower is exactly and how Ina can escape it.Two of the earliest characters you’ll meet are Thief and Joker, who each have their mannerisms and quirks.. These NPCs have a lot of personality, from their artwork to their animations. For example, the Joker acts as flamboyantly as possible and his artwork and animations reflects this. On the other hand, the Thief is extremely reserved. The Thief prefers hiding and not giving away any unnecessary details. As you interact with them more and more, they both slowly open up more to you. There are many other characters you meet along the way, but I’ll leave them all as a surprise for you to meet.Where the game really shines is in its artwork. All of the characters have very colorful 2D designs. The 2D animations are also very well-made, and you can feel the weight when Ina swings on a rope, as well as when she jumps and lands. You need to take your time when swinging on a rope because you need to build up momentum to jump and land on the next platform. In fact, you need to be careful when jumping from tall heights, otherwise Ina will take extra time to recover which can be dangerous if an enemy is chasing you.The game is not trying to have the latest graphics of course, it’s just a small indie title. For the scope of what the game is trying to achieve it has a surprising amount of details. One small detail I really liked was how Ina has a reflection off of many kinds of surfaces. There’s areas with dozens of crystals, and as you walk or jump by them you can see Ina’s reflection off of each crystal.The game has very beautiful backgrounds. As you progress through the game, there are three major areas: the starting area which looks like a utopia that was destroyed, a beautiful garden area which is now unkempt, and a mechanical area meant to feel very cold and industrial. Each of these different settings have their own hazards to watch out for too.The soundtrack of this game is also very well done. The main theme of the game feels very mysterious, but also relaxing at the same time. The soundtrack really reflects the atmosphere and mood of the game and it kept drawing me in more and more. Many of the tracks in the game feature Asian instruments as well which go well with the cherry blossom garden environment.Don’t mistake this game’s colorful appearance and fun soundtrack with only happiness though. The game features a lot of lore and backstory, and the game does have many serious plot events and somber moments.Underneath this game’s colorful artwork there is a lot of sadness to uncover.Both Ina and the NPCs have a lot of internal conflict that they need to overcome and you’ll actually get a great plot out of this game.The gameplay is very addicting, and is also easy for newcomers. Aspire features no combat at all. It’s a 2D puzzle platformer, so a lot of the gameplay involves avoiding obstacles and enemies. You can move around and jump like any other platformer. Sometimes Ina will need to swing on a rope to jump across platforms and Ina can also climb up ladders.What makes Aspire unique is that you can absorb blue energy to deactivate machines, and you can give the energy back to reactivate them. Many of the puzzles involve finding energy and giving it to a particular door.Although Ina starts out using blue energy, she will be able to use green and purple energy later in the game which allows her to do different actions. Ina can give energy to certain platforms, which can either increase the size of the object (green energy) or move it vertically or horizontally (purple energy). When you put all of these elements together, the result is very fun puzzles that you need to solve to get through the game.The game starts off with easy puzzles to get your feet wet, and they get harder as you progress through the story. Even so, the puzzles near the climax of the game don’t get too hard at all. Even the worst puzzle would only take me 5-10 minutes of thinking, and the puzzles in this game are easier than similar indie platformer titles. The puzzles are made in a way such that you can’t permanently mess them up and there are only so many things you can do. It really is meant to be a relaxing game most of the time with a few sections in-between that’ll make you scratch your head.In one of the earliest puzzles, Ina has to push a crate with a rope attached so that she can swing across the rope to get to the energy source. You can’t jump over the box at first due to a low ceiling, so you’ll need to move it to on of the ends, jump over it, and then pull the box back towards you.The game also features plenty of checkpoints that you return to if you die. I’d typically see a checkpoint every 5 minutes or so which was very reasonable. You’ll likely die many times from just exploring, be it from pitfalls or enemies attacking Ina, but it’s easy to try again using the nearby checkpoint.My only criticism with this game is that it’s a tad short. My playthrough of the game took only three hours and it certainly is possible to beat the game in one sitting. There are a few optional memories of the NPCs you can find throughout the levels (referred to as Stone of Memories) which also contain information regarding lore of the world, but otherwise there aren’t really any collectibles or optional content in the game. Although all of the NPCs were extremely well-made and nuanced, there are only one or two NPCs per region which some people may find to be underwhelming.As well, the route through the game is very straightforward, with only one branching path per region to collect the optional memories. I do like that the game has a small scope and that it features tightly-woven gameplay, but at the same time there is a lack of substance and there isn’t any reason to go through the game again except to experience the plot again.Although my criticisms may sound harsh, don’t take it to heart because the game is very charming and fun. I’d say to definitely give this game a try if you like other 2D indie puzzle platformers. Aspire: Ina’s Tale definitely stands tall among other similar games such as Limbo, Inside, or Little Nightmares. If you enjoyed any of those titles I can guarantee you’d enjoy Aspire as well. Aspire is brimming with great artwork and animations, and is really worth a playthrough despite having a few shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my preferred genre. I love non-combat, linear 2D puzzle games. This one is really beautiful with excellent music and a nice, heartfelt story. There are few small annoyances here and there. I'm only 1/3 through the game. I'll update the review once I've finished the game.Edit: I completed the game in one sitting after 2.8 hours. I honestly love short games, but this one felt a bit lite. The puzzles rely less on logic and more on trial and error. Some puzzles were great, but others were just weird and I figured out the solution almost instantly. Overall, I felt while playing this game that is was not coherent as a linear experience, but looking back after completing it, I think it was a good little game with a good little story.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The art and aesthetics of this game are amazing and the puzzles are challenging enough without being frustratingly difficult.  The only downsides to this game are that it is very short and the world-building never quite gives you enough information to understand what's going on.  It doesn't take anything away from the game necessarily but it could have added to it with a few more levels to really dig deeper into what the mysterious Tower is and who Ina is meant to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The game does nothing new but what it does it does very well. It is very heavily influenced by Gris, with the gameplay being a mix of Gris and Limbo/Inside, and the soundtrack and artwork sharing a similar feel though stylistically different. If you like very pretty puzzle platformers this is well worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: What is Aspire: Ina's Tale?It's a short, colorful, 2D platformer with a strong puzzle emphasis with some platforming thrown in. Created by Wondernaut Studio and published by Untold Tales, Aspire: Ina's Tale was released last year, on September 30th. For the Switch, Xbox One, and for Windows.-=-=-=-While it took me only a handful of hours to beat, it is a mostly well crafted experience with few, if any, gameplay-related problems. Those, primarily devolving down to nitpicks. I.E. The interaction with ropes feels very stiff and unnatural. -=-=-=-Story wise, Aspire starts out strong and continues to provide intrigue into the world without revealing too much. At times, it makes Aspire feel more like it's a prologue or an introduction, rather than a full game on it's own.For what there is, the characters are vibrant, the environments are colorful and interesting to look at. The puzzles are smart, but not too challenging, and progression through it will only end up taking the average person a handful of hours at most.-=-=-=-While I can't say there's much replay value (unless you want all the achievements), Aspire left me with the desire for wanting more from this Universe, and I hope Wondernaut get's the chance to do more with it.With it's short run time, it's value to you will be whether or not you can justify the pricetag vs how brief it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A good 2D puzzle platformer.The gampleay is pretty simple: the casual walking and jumping is complemented by some rope swinging and crate pushing. The logical puzzles are mostly easy, although a few are harder nuts to crack. The use of the spirits is a nice addition but they do not provide a significant complexity.The visuals are beautiful, the whole game looks amazing. The background music and the overall ambience is generally calming with the exception of a few action scenes so it is a great game for relaxation.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The game is short, has it's very beautiful moments, great music, but the story dropped me midway.The beginning of the story was intruiging, but as I was reaching the end, I felt the dialogue become more and more boring right until the end.Still the characters were interestingly designed (inspired for some fanart) and the 2d puzzle platforming was a lot of fun.I would recommend playing it for a light, but fun story and gameplay.---Guide tip!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful with great character designs. Although the game mechanics are not the most fluid you will ever experience, they were definitely better than I expected. I found that loading up chapters one after the other ended up causing major lag, but once I exited and logged back onto the game, the lag went away. The puzzles will definitely make you rack your brains a bit and the platforming is pretty good, too. It took me 8-9 hours to 100% the game. I really recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a fabulous experience, that I really really enjoyed playing through. The art style is one not seen often in games! The game play overall was smooth up until the very last part. I also enjoyed the way it encouraged you to explore and look around your world.However there is one thing that I have to raise as the only negative. That at the there was a lot of 'frameyness' in the game, which was making it harder to get timing right when needed
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This generally is a good game. It's interesting on the side of puzzles, details to complete all the achievements, dialogues with NPCs and generally what would be the message to the player. The environment is...well, it's not my favourite kind of design or style, but nonetheless it's good, well done. Also the music does its part, really! I really enjoyed this game............here comes the problem.Generally when you buy a videogame, you'd expect to be able to replay it anytime. This I cannot do. The game has some bugs, it seems, and these bugs (or bad event handling) are stored in the save data, which is shared among all Steam accounts, so if some data is badly stored in your save data you just cannot solve the problem restarting the game (I changed account, resinstalled the game and selected New game, so yeah, I tested already what could be tested). This is even harder to solve since it is not so clear which files contain the save data and could just be deleted to start a brand new game. Also, the game was quite short to me, considering I bought it in sales period and normally its cost is higher. The problem to me would be the price rather than the duration.I repeat I actually liked it, but spending that money to properly play a game for 2-3 hours and JUST ONCE is unconceivable.I'm writing this on January 17, perhaps the game will be fixed in the future (or maybe not?). As things are now, this is pretty much I can say. Try it, but knowing you possibly will be able to play it properly just once.
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely charming little game! If you like platformers with a bit of a puzzle twist then you will love this. The graphics are absolutely stunning, the soundtrack is phenomenal and there's a depth that you wouldn't expect from most short platform/puzzle games.I would argue that it's at least somewhat like Little Nightmares in parts, although not as dark, it has the same feeling of "what on earth is going on" with similar gameplay. I also streamed the game, my little community loved it as well and commented on it saying it was charming, beautiful, tricky at parts and made you think. For anyone interested on seeing what it's like, I have posted the video here although I would recommend just going in without any prior knowledge! ->
_childDocuments_.name: Aspire: Ina's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Aspire: Ina's Tale is a game that does what it does exceptionally well.Is it a sprawling world full of complex mechanics and endless collectables? No - and it doesn't need to be because of the deep and reflective narrative given by the story, the stunning visuals in every area and beautiful scores which fit perfectly to accompany it all.The game is not very long but certainly shows it's strengths. I would recommend it for anybody wanting a gorgeous casual game to play through with some light puzzling elements.

name: Cursed to Golf
detailed_description: THE PRESS ABOUT CURSED TO GOLF: 'The Dark Souls of side-scrolling golf roguelikes is quite the pitch, but Cursed to Golf looks like it’ll pull that premise off.' Polygon - 50 most anticipated games of 2022 'Golf in a series of platforming dungeons? As you battle to escape the underworld? (Or Golf Purgatory, which sounds just as bad.) Power-ups and weird obstacles and a never-ending series of neat gimmicks? Lovely pixelart? Cursed to Golf sounds absolutely wonderful.' Eurogamer - The games we're looking forward to in 2022 'In Cursed to Golf you take on the role of a Golf Champion, trapped in Golf Purgatory after a lightning strike stops you dead in your tracks. To ascend back to the land of the living, you’ll need to play through 18 dungeon-like holes.' Nintendo Life - 33 Indie Games We're Excited About On Switch In 2022 About the Game Play as The Cursed Golfer, trapped in Golf Purgatory after a freak accident takes you out as you’re about to take the winning shot of an international tournament! Legend says that playing through the devious courses across Golf Purgatory will get you back to the land of the living and, more importantly, to the trophy you were about to win. Each course is governed by a ghostly Legendary Caddie, who will tutor you in the mystical ways of golf to aid you on your quest for redemption and revival. Cursed to Golf offers a fresh take on the golfing and roguelike subgenres. Make your way through a hole within the PAR Count or your curse will take you back to the beginning of the course! To add to the challenge, these courses don’t just have bunkers and rough spots but are also chock full of mad obstacles like high powered fans, spikes, TNT boxes, teleporters and a whole load more. It’s all par for the course in this twisted take on the classic game! Being cursed to play golf forever in the eternity of Golf Purgatory has its benefits, too! Use Birdie-Eye to catch a view of the whole course and see what trials lie ahead. Par count running low? Luckily, gold and silver Shot Idols are peppered throughout the holes, smashing through them with a cinematic flourish will replenish your shots. Ace Cards will turn the odds back in your favour, channeling your otherworldly powers to manipulate the game in incredible ways. Scattershot, U-Turn, Rocketball, Mulligans are just some of 20+ cards you have up your sleeve to turn the tide back in your favour! Every shot counts! Explore the golf-themed world and characters of Golf Purgatory Precise “Golf-Like” gameplay across a randomly-ordered course in 4 biomes Navigate tough dungeon-like holes filled with wacky hazards Golf in style using over 20 unique Ace Card power-ups Challenge the world in online leaderboards 70+ holes to experience will keep you swinging for eternity

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game and I definitely had fun, but I have a lot of thoughts about it.The game's shortcoming is that while gameplay is fun, trying to marry it with roguelike mechanics can make the game too frustrating for most players to even finish. I personally feel like I wouldn't want to run through another game after beating it. I felt like I've experienced everything it had to offer. Most of the time roguelikes are about changing your tactics, trying new things, and making choices in between your challenges. I don't think the game hit the mark on these 3 points.Allowing shorter full runs and less constraints on players may have been the secret sauce to entice players like me to keep coming back. Maybe even different clubs that would remove your spin and add a different type of ability. I just don't want to stray too far from the safest path, because I know if I fail I have a very long run to get back to where I was. The action cards allow some flavor, but if you experiment too much you will most definitely fail. There are boss powers that give you extra bonuses like bringing cards to new runs, having +5 more strokes for each hole, or allowing the player to set a checkpoint along the run, but I personally feel like these are band-aids for the fact that an entire run takes so long as well as the difficulty on each hole. They feel like they were put there to ensure players will eventually win.Another possible solution is to start with shorter courses that have less hazards to encourage experimentation and have a gradual difficulty rise with each passing hole. Between each hole a player could choose to lengthen a course or add more hazards, then the next hole would generate. Some sort of risk reward choice. I applaud the devs for attempting something new like this, it's hard to mesh genres. It was a great shot. The theme and style are amazing. The gameplay had some faults.I would still recommend this game, but I think players should definitely know what it is before going in.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Before you buy, you need to know 2 things: 1. This is a super fun golf game2. This is a terrible "rogue-like" (there is a trick to circumvent that element completely)The game misses its genre entirely. Why this needed the coat of a rogue-like without meta progression when a run easily takes 4-7h is just beyond me. This is flat out one of the biggest genre-mismatches I have ever seen. However, Instead of starting over from the beginning after you fail a single hole, you can just ALT+F4 the game any time during a hole and you will reset at the beginning of that hole. This trick alone is the saving grace, why I can give it a thumps up in the end.The actual golfing is actually really fun and mostly fair. The card & accessory system is fun, but can be hard to manage. There is an accessory that gives you 3 random card each shot INSTEAD of your usual card deck (that has limited quantity) and that was sooo much more fun to play, I wonder why they didn't make it the default mode and remove the buying of cards entirely. This game could easily live up to its potential by removing the awful perma deatrh mechanism and making this pin permanent. Handcrafted levels would be a plus, but it was fun regardless.So if you use ALT+F4, it's a recommend. If you don't, stay away.PS: I hope there will be a 2nd entry, but please be a puzzle / golfing game and not a rogue-like.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Cursed to Golf is a action adventure golflike game that has some roguelike elements in it. You travel through 18 holes in golf purgatory to reach ascension after your character dies by getting struck by lightning. You meet other golfers stuck in golf purgatory through the run and each of them act as a boss level towards the end where you have to get to the hole before them on a long course. The game has over 70 courses all with different hazards and shortcuts to help keep the golfing as fresh as ever. On the courses you can use Ace Cards that positively effect your shot, or add extra shots to your par meter. The game has 20 or so ace cards total. The par meter starts at 5 for each hole and if it goes down to 0 the run is over and you have to start back at the beginning. After each hole you gain money that can be spent in a shop to buy ace cards and outside of shops you can also collect ace cards between holes.PROS---------- Fun, simple and addicting golfing with tons of unique courses to help keep it fresh- The game is hard, but in a good way. You'll fail a lot but it always makes you wanna keep playing and telling yourself "1 more try"- Lots of variety with ace cards that help enhance the courses and allow for a lot of fun shortcuts to be discovered- Cute 2D pixelated graphics with great music and animations- Good price for what you get- Addicting gameplay if you're a golf fanCONS-----------Unsure with how much replay value there is after clearing the game once (I have yet to clear)-Some text on screen I can see little specs that make it look unfinished. Should be an easy fixReally there isn't many negative things about the game besides bugs so I'm going to list some bugs I had while playing- Game freezing. Once or twice in my ten hours the game randomly froze and wouldn't let me shoot. Made me restart the game which ended up with me restarting the hole- Boss glitched out of a tight corner once to win the hole. Lame- Two times the game allowed me to skip every hole and just go straight to the boss- Inconsistent money made after each hole. Unsure how they determine how much money you get after a hole. Is it based on how many shots it took? Or how many shots I have left?Really that's a quick review, but it's a good bang for your buck for sure and I'd highly suggest it. You can watch a full YouTube review Happy Golfing!
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Just not for me. The design feels too focused on finding the "intended" solution to a given hole rather than figuring things out as you go and the par mechanic can just put you in unwinnable situations because of a move you made 4 shots ago. Was honestly pretty excited for this but it just didn't quite deliver the experience I wanted.The soundtrack is absolutely amazing, though, I have to give that a shout-out.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Could be a fun game if they fix the annoyances I had with it. Here's my list of improvements:1: Each club should have it's own zoom. Not being able to see where my drive would land was incredibly frustrating. Never felt like skill if I landed the ball outside of my visible range, it just felt like gambling.2. The levels are WAY WAY too long. Especially in the last couple stages. Some levels took me 30 strokes which was a real trudge. A round of golf should never take more than 30-40 mins. My first run through the game took me almost 3 hours. 3. Organize the ace cards or show all the ones we have and let us pick one. Really annoying to spin through the list and try to find the one you want. 4. Some of the ace cards feel sloppy. If I use the rocket, it would be nice to know how long I have to use it. Same goes for the phase card and drill card. I would have saved so many strokes just knowing to not try to go over a little gap because I was running out of fuel on my rocket.5. Some way to know where teleporters go. Like an ace card or something would be fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy and cheap. The early game is fun and carefree with fun holes and pleasant visuals. The end is a miserable poorly coded slog. I had multiple cards not work as intended and I died because the game refused to acknowledge my "gimme 5". Hard is one thing, unfair is another, and poorly designed is too much. Ultimately this game is more frustrating then it should be with the late game holes 15 on being absurdly cheap to almost being broken. I cannot recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cursed to Golf

_childDocuments_.review: It's like one of those old browser mini-golf game that's extremely flashy and polished, and hopped up on caffeine. Game looks and sounds so damn good, pixel art is top notch! So bouncy and full of life. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this game, it looks like a lot of fun. The beginning of the game is really enjoyable too but as you get further into the game, it becomes more and more frustrating. The actual golf mechanics are rather frustrating and feels inconsistent. The arc moves too quickly back and forth so it's hard to make your shots. You also can't zoom out enough to see where your further hits are going. You have to guess bounces. The edges of platforms have a visual overhang but the ball will bounce through it completely which gets very frustrating at times. There are bonus cards to make your shots have variables like a rocket ball that you can control or portals just to name a few but you really can't use them in the first half of the game and then in the second half, you have to hope you have the right ones for the level lay out. It can also feel like a chore at times. There's a fast forward button but it still doesn't feel fast enough. For the start of holes it says press escape to skip the opening cinematic which is a flat out lie because it never works. Sometimes pressing left click on the mouse will work, other times it won't. It's really bizarre how inconsistent it is. Then when you play against a boss, you have to wait for the boss to take their shot and it just makes the whole experience feel quite slow. The roguelike elements are interesting but the holes are just too overwhelming. Later holes end up requiring you to be practically perfect, especially the end game. It's fun at first, seriously frustrating later on. I enjoyed the first few hours and wanted to finish a run and couldn't be bothered with how little fun I was having after the first few hours. I would recommend skipping this one. Kind of sucks that it's fun pretty much up until you get past the 2 hour mark where the refund window closes but what are you gonna do.

_childDocuments_.review: The music isn't anything amazing or mind blowing but it is pretty catchy and enjoyable. It gives off a good feel for the game.The controls are nice and simple which help with the flow of the game while also giving a lot of tools to assist the player with their shots and planned pathing. Funny enough even though this is a golf roguelike this somewhat feels more like a precision platformer with how the controls and gameplay feel but that's not a bad thing.Ace cards are cards you can buy or collect during your run to improve your chances on holes. They can give you more strokes, give you better positioning, take shortcuts. There are a lot of them but they improve the game a lot because it creates a whole new area of strategy on when to use them and how. You can use them to save you from bad situations or take big risks by making crazy plays/ shortcuts. There's even pins which are basically expensive permanent upgrades for the rest of the run. They are additions that really make this stand out as a golf game.Unlike other roguelikes that are fast paced or you have to dodge a hundred threats from multiple directions in quick succession this is thankfully a roguelike where you can take your time and focus on your strategy and enjoy a slow paced game because its golf. It's a nice way this game stands out. It's strangely a game that is very relaxing but also very stressful due the severe punishment this game gives out.I can't believe I'm saying this but this might be THE hardest roguelike I've played. Harder than Dead Cells, Hades, Slay the Spire, Binding of Isaac, FTL. The reason why is because the game is super punishing for any mistakes. Instead of traditional golf where you try to score below par, you have to reach the hole in a limited number of strokes or you lose. You'll have to destroy statues along the way to refresh your strokes. The problem is that the statues are pretty far apart from each other so by the time you reach the next you'll barely have enough strokes remaining so if you make any mistakes (land in a bunker, water, right next to a wall you need to shoot over, miss a statue) you'll probably run out of strokes you need to reach the next statue. Then there's the punishment for failing a run, in other roguelikes runs usually take 30 minutes - an hour to complete so failing does not feel terrible, but in this game runs take so long it will take multiple sessions to make decent progress and will probably take multiple hours to finally reach the end so if you run out of strokes, you are going all the way back to hole 1 when it takes about 10 - 20 strokes just to complete each hole! Some people may like the length of the game because theres more content and thats fine but if you are the kind of person that would rather have 1 quick run, this game is not that.Some of the Ace Cards effect the ball very differently to assist you but it would be nice if I could be given a quick chance to practice them to understand how they feel before I do my actual shot because too often I have to learn how they work in the middle of flight and I end up wasting them. Since there are so many cards that change the controls or feeling of the ball it feels like a lot of times you have to learn how they function quickly before you waste them and again since this game can feel so punishing it often feels like they are not worth the risk of experimenting with or learning. Also with all roguelikes when you reach the late game there are usually new enemies, mechanics, or obstacles that will kick your butt the first time you experience them and that is fine for a roguelike. But other roguelikes focus on quick runs, because runs here are extremely long, it can feel super frustrating if you don't understand them in time a lose just because you couldn't figure out how they work. Like the unique Ace Cards, there should either be a quick cutscene to explain how they work or a quick tutorial to explain them with the way the game is designed. Trying to learn these things in the middle of a run is just too risky to try with when the punishment for failing is so extreme.When you are preparing your shot, you'll have a tracer to show you where your ball will go when you hit which is great. However the problem shows up when one of your main objectives is to keep hitting statues to continue your runs. Way too often I'll hit the statues but then hit a hazard because I don't know where it will land because the tracer gets blocked by the statues. It has cost me too many runs because of it. It would be nice if the tracer would go through the statue or the ball stops after hitting one.While the levels are nice and have multiple different paths to reach the end with different amounts of risk vs reward which is good design it also unfortunately makes levels appear confusing and hard to tell which way to go to reach the end. Levels look like mazes which means you'll spend a lot of time on the free cam trying to figure out the way to go. Hopefully they add an option to turn on something that shows you the main path to the end so I don't have to spend so much time on the free cam just to understand the pathing and directions.A quickplay mode would be nice as a simple option if I just wanna do a quick run of the game. No limited strokes or statues, just traditional style golf of trying to get as few strokes as possible. Being able to choose how many holes you wanna play or how long the holes are would create more variety in how people can play the game.This feels like a great game to challenge your friends in as everyone would have different plans on their pathing and Ace Card usage. Maybe it would be nice if there was an option between least strokes or whoever survives the longest. Still this feels like a game that would benefit a lot from a versus mode.I know this part will be controversial but I do think games are better when they have multiple difficulty options and this is a game that would benefit a lot from having one. Something as simple as easier holes, more statues, or increased number of strokes per hole. Other roguelikes like Hades and Dead Cells have one to make their games more appealing to a larger audience and having one for a simple game like golf would surely bring in a bigger audience without scaring them away.Despite me giving this game more cons than pros I still do think the pros outweigh the cons. It's a good game that is very enjoyable but doesn't really feel designed for a casual audience. It's a game that involves a lot more time and investment than I expected and that's not a bad thing. It's still a new game that could use some improvements but the general direction and ideas of the game are still very enjoyable. It's fun, unique, and challenging and yet a relaxing game with a lot of replayability. If you are a golf fan who wants a game with lots of replay value and diversity, this game is great for you but doesn't really appeal to people who want a simple basic golf game. It's basically a randomly generated golf game with unique mechanics and strategy that turns into a game that feels like a precision platformer challenging dedicated players asking them to plan ahead each move carefully.

_childDocuments_.review: game was fun, i really love how all of the cards that i found felt useful, on top of all 3 clubs being useful too. the mechanical gameplay of golf is so expertly crafted in this game, and if this game was given time to have a fleshed out normal adventure mode it would be absolutely perfect and easier to recommend.i love roguelike games, but this is one of the rare cases where I wish this game *wasn't* exclusively one, the levels are long and fun (and since they're random theres endless situations for the player to need to solve with what they're given), but this also hurts when the desire to jump into a run from the very beginning is very low. i might come back to it and give it another try to see if i can make it to the very end.speaking of the very end, the end of my run was pretty buggy actually, the game's boss fights seem to not be completely bug free, speeding up the gameplay causes some visual bugs, and I actually got completely softlocked on the 2nd boss. I don't think I was going to win anyway, so i didn't feel too bad about it, but I ended up freezing a lake near a teleporter with the freeze ball, and then on my next turn my character just stood in place and I couldn't make them do anything. But overall the game seemed pretty solid without running into any gamebreaking bugs besides that. overall, i love the idea here and the game is hella fun, i just wish i could enjoy it more casually without fear of having to restart from the beginning. (If there happens to be a mode where I can freely play through the entire story without having to restart if i lose, or lose my cards if i exit and rejoin, then I severely apologize and i will edit my review.)

_childDocuments_.review: Played it quite a bit and loved it at first, but I'm hitting a series of walls in where the repetition (not the same holes, but they come up in a sort of - rotation so to speak), from each run start really wearing on my patience and make the early sections of this golf game a tedious chore the dozenth time you've cleared the same holes - which also effectively siphons off content and experiences from players who cannot regularly clear stages - or are patient enough to do so - over and over. I'm a bit of a stubborn mule, so I've gotten deep into the game, and think the content/cards/courses later are are WAY more interesting - but the unforgiving nature of the game when it comes to making errors, especially in boss encounters, many won't get to even see it.This wall I'm encountering may not be encountered by all players, and you may have a blast, but there is a very real barrier that others may encounter and is worth considering prior to purchasing, as this game does require a significant mastery of the game's mechanics (and a ton of patience to blow throw less interesting holes you've done many times before) in order to progress at all - given this does not have any carried over progress per run aside from assists/checkpoints from bosses you beat - if you've managed it.Maybe the game was designed with dedication and skill in mind, and alright sure - but as a new game series people should know that it will not be for everyone and will be demanding for the player.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah I'm impatient, but this game really needs to figure out an auto-fast-forward feature. Holding spacebar every time I'm not  actively playing the game is incredibly tedious. The game's pixel art, design, and soundtrack are all great, but it pulls way too much focus to that when I just want to play the game. I don't want to watch every animation for every action every time anything happens.The game introduces some frustrating mechanics seemingly at random, it might be buried in the never-ending dialogue that seems to last forever and also can be accidentally skipped very easily with clicking. Couple of issues: Bosses bypass par limits, the entire screen is occasionally clickable despite there being a designated button (Choosing wrong paths), and powers have a time limit on them. If you try to U-Turn a ball but want to wait for it to fall into the position to redirect, it can time out and your ball just falls to the ground.The difficulty is made painful with these functions, and walls being an unrealistic dead-stop to the ball is hard to explain. The ball bounces off of floors with ease, but loses almost all momentum at hitting a wall.Love the idea of this game but pretty weak execution outside of its aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: Its an interesting idea however done poorly.Providing additional feedback for Dev :)Im gonna start with the worst thing in the game, the camera system. The camera being this zoomed in makes the game feel claustrophobic, and spending time in the free cam trying to figure out the routes around the level, as well as the teleporter layout bloats the gameplay loop. If the teleporters had some indicator of their exit that would be nice. Being able to 'nudge' the camera is great, however it being bound to the same buttons as controlling looking left and right is awful and makes certain shots more annoying than needed (i.e bank shots off a wall). I don't think that blind shots, especially with the margins you have in holes 15-18 are fun.The hitboxes for hazards are very finnicky, and honestly, the fact that touching the slight base bit of the land next to a spike kills you hurts when you are trying to land precise shots. I have fallen through terrain, especially near the edges of ledges and ended up in unwinnable positions. The arrow on bounce-pad aiming is also significantly off from my mouse, making aiming less natural than it should be.And really, the par system amplifies these shortcomings. Janky hitboxes and terrain collision hurt when you lose an hour of watching animations to it.Not gonna lie, if the game just let you flounder and get as many shots as you need to beat the holes, and just didn't give you the 'good ending' if you were above par I would enjoy the time more. There are interesting maps later on, but why would I try to do the hard shots when I could loop a few times and stack up ace cards to just brute force it. This is obviously just what I would do, shifting more towards score attack and optimization than ending runs because you fell through a ledge into a zombie pit.Also having the exit to the shop be on the left when all other forward navigation is to the right is annoying.Also keys should be able to be rebound.TL:DR It feels like a 2010 mobile game port and has the same issues as most of them. It's very pretty though and has some bangin music.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally "hold developers hostage" by "leaving a negative review while asking for a feature", but at the same time... I have to. I feel like this one thing I want and the fact that it's not here is holding this game back. This game doesn't feel like it quite has the oomph of replayability that some other roguelites do. That's it. That's all I want.The main gameplay loop is decent enough in most regards, (although I'm not in the mood to elaborate on this) and I think my money was well spent. But I'm just saying, this isn't a roguelite that quite gives you 100 hours of fun. The "room variance" or amount of handcrafted parts of a level, also leaves much to be desired. I often spot almost-exactly same hallways, especially in the desert biome. It would be nice if it had workshop support so players could make more chunks, but that's also not here.So this is both a cautionary review and a feature request at the same time.I know, I might be a hypocrite when I say this doesn't give me enough hours and yet constantly preach games don't always need to last 50+ hours, but at the same time, it's a roguelite, and it should be the main selling point of these.

_childDocuments_.review: First run was super fun, second less so, third even less so. It's great to start with, but it just keeps getting blander and blander. The upgrades don't help, they just make things ridiculously easy, to the point that I stopped really caring to try. And screw the final world btw. Spending more time looking at the level and it's animations than playing the entire game.Edit: This game has a lot of things that shouldn't be in a game that isn't intended to be a rage game. Which, to the best of my knowledge, it's not intended to be. To give credit where credit is due, this game has a nice and cute story that does feel surprisingly good to complete. Not that I think completing it was worth it, but it did feel good to win, and the final level was actually some good fun. _childDocuments_.review: 1st of i want to say,yes, the game is fun. it been a fun little game to play.BUT and a massive BUT. it has far too many glaring issues.mainly bugs that ruin the experience.were these bugs fixed, i'm sure it would be decent.so lets get to it shall we.the courses are quite limited in design, only 5 or so playthroughs done and i think i seen every course pop up multiple times. the abilities aren't randomized, so you're not getting area 2 or 3 abilities in area 1. vice versa u won't get area 1 abilities in area 2 or 3. which is kind of silly.the last 3 holes are always the same. if anything, the game doesn't recognize you ever beating the game. the cut scenes and dialog will remain the same after beating it 4 times already.the levels are ok, the pipes and teleporters don't tell you where they go. so it's a matter of deduction and chance.some stages require far too much effort to get through without perks or abilities.some require 30 some hits to clear. when u could use an ability to cut through half the stage..speaking of perks and abilities.they are pretty much a must have to clear the end game. the stage design is stupidly bad at that point and you're not given enough strokes to clear it without help.the store sells you "pins and cards" that will help with that, but again, due to zone limitations you're not getting the ones you need or want.the toggle pins are a 100% must. some of them completely break the game.the random chests are pretty pointless. the amount of gold you get out of them is neglect-able at best. 250g or so, not much honestly as a single card pack costs upwards of 1.2k and a single stage grands 1k.then we get too the big problems,the bugs.the very 1st run i did, we could have cleared the game.but the game is full with bugs, the ui doesn't line up with what you're doing and softlocks parts of the ui. preventing you from doing what u wanted to do.several of these bugs are, UI bugs - the ability cards won't trigger, or appear to trigger when they don't Shop UI bug - shop screen not displaying any items Screen stuck - After using an ability and then go through a teleporter during the same stroke, it freezes the UI. preventing the player from turning. Game wipes - reloading the game can make you lose all your progress. this can include the things you have during that run.  Collection losses - at the store is a collection book for cards. so u can save them for future runs. but this too can get wiped out at complete random.honestly, i enjoyed the game despite its bugs. but it ruins the experience quite abit when ur far into a run and then have to reset because the UI bugs out. or the game prevents you from doing anything.the lack of veriety in some of those stages is also a hamper. it's not enjoyable seeing the same stages over and over without any changes. this especially on the last 3 courses where they are always identical. and instead of it being a skill check, it's an ability check. "do you have the abilities/cards to clear this"honestly there is no reason for hole 16 to 19 to exist after clearing it the 1st time.specially after clearing each boss stage. those aren't repeatable. so why are those holes?all in all, it's an ok game. but it needed more to keep me playing at least.

_childDocuments_.review: In Cursed to Golf, you play as the GGOAT (Greatest Golfer of All Times) or at least you were about to be if it wasn’t for the lightning bolt that struck you on the last hit of the most incredible shot in your career. In death, you end up in Golf purgatory, but fret not, wee one, for you can escape it by successfully doing the afterlife 18 holes.In Cursed to Golf, you play as the GGOAT (Greatest Golfer of All Times) or at least you were about to be if it wasn’t for the lightning bolt that struck you on the last hit of the most incredible shot in your career. In death, you end up in Golf purgatory, but fret not, wee one, for you can escape it by successfully doing the afterlife 18 holes.Cursed to Golf is a 2D golf roguelike with deckbuilding mechanics, and quite frankly, it’s a strike of genius.To advance through the different levels of the tournament, you will need to get under par every time, and it’s quite a challenging ordeal. Indeed, not only will you have a minimal number of shots to succeed, but the levels are filled with obstacles and traps. It also keeps changing between tries (or sometimes even during the level itself)!To help you in your adventure, you will have at your disposal a few different clubs to make your shots: a driver, an iron and a wedge. Each comes with another way of attacking the ball. After deciding on your club, you will need to gauge the power of your shot and confirm it on the power meter, then comes the trickiest of it all: the angle you wish for and this one requires quite the timing. It is also possible to add spin to your ball, which could very well be the deciding factor of your last shot.Cursed to Golf also includes some subtle but well-made deck-building elements. Cards are available in the game and can be bought in the store (Eterni-tee) or found between levels. To help your shots, you get to draw cards from booster packs that are there to help when you activate them. These will modify how you will shoot the ball or how it’ll act while in the air, and so on.  For instance, you could transform the ball into a mini-rocket, give it the power of the elements or why not just do U-turn mid-air? It is effectively adding different ways and possibilities of completing each level. You can afford these cards by completing levels that will net you some money. Furthermore, you can also break some silver and gold statues present throughout each level to net you some extra shots and help finish the level.Not straying away from its core, Cursed to Golf is quite challenging. Should you fail during the course, you will fail and need to restart with nothing. After defeating bosses, you will be granted a few extra perks, such as the capacity to place a checkpoint. The smartest of us will also save cards in a binder to save them for future runs.Simply put, the only way to progress is for your skills to improve and improve at the game.Graphically speaking, the game has lovely pixel graphics and a retro ambience that will fill you with nostalgia.Sadly, the boss fights can feel highly unfair and almost frustrating. I saw myself at one shot from winning a boss fight and having a boss extremely far behind me, but that somehow managed to cross a massive chunk of the map in one hit, along with the map conveniently changing form and shape to facilitate the boss’ hit. I couldn’t plan for it, but it’s part of the game. That said, they’re possible to beat; you will need some skill and a good deck of cards! You can also stun them by destroying boss-fight specific statues, but I found these statues to be placed so far away that I would waste too many shots going for those.That being said, the game was recently patched, and quite a few bugs I experienced are now gone. But not all, sadly. During many runs, I play and lose all my money, achievement completion or even recorded progress, so I have to restart, which is frustrating when you’re far enough. Finally, Cursed to Golf is a highly original take on Roguelikes by using a brilliant idea for a genre that could always use some innovation. But it also has a great ambience, music and charming graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: I keep flip flopping while writing this review but eventually decided to not recommend this game. I simply did not enjoy the game and was just pushing my short 7.5 hours of my time on this game to finish it. I played this game after the "pins" update which made the game significantly easier. I would probably just raged quit if I played this before the update.It is a mini-golf roguelike with power up cards you collect along the way. It is a roguelike because once you fail a boss fight OR failed to get to the hole before the par score, you go back to hole 1.I think the reason I don't enjoy this game compared to other golf games is I prefer all the setups and planning to be before the shot. But I don't like that a lot of the powerups require you to activate it mid-flight. There's also a persistent UI bug with it displaying the wrong club after every shot. Right clicks (cancel) that failed to register making me do a shot I don't intend. And I got 2 softlocks on a boss fight where I was toggling the fast forward but the game went giga slo-mo and it would take hours to probably finish the boss' turn and I just restarted the game.Finally, as a roguelike, there's a lack of power improvements after doing it over and over. I would rate this 6/10. Good game, but just boring for me

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty rad! I really like the feeling of nailing a power-up to make a tricky shot, and the generated holes are pretty fun.Unfortunately, I kept having a bug where I would be stuck between shots sometimes (especially on a boss level), and when loading the game up it loads back to the prior spot but with items and strokes used up from the lost shot. I couldn't figure out a solution and didn't hear back from the devs. Just something to be aware of, but maybe it'll work differently on your machine! I'd definitely recommend otherwise.Edit: I haven't hit that softlock again, so that's good! I still find the power-ups extremely *swingy*, and especially the later holes seem to generate as though a specific power-up is required to finish them at all. This is compounded by some of the power-ups not communicating clearly how they work, so it's easy to completely waste multiple of them just trying to *pin* down how they function.That said, it's still pretty neat. The holes are sprawling in a fun way, and the controls for taking shots are fairly forgiving. I still recommend it, but it might be worth a burner run just to try power-ups out.

_childDocuments_.review: Great at being a pixel art golf game, decent at being a roguelike. Pros: 1) Beautiful art style, with quirky and interesting characters, 2) cool, simple story 3) great golfing gameplay with very interesting "Ace Cards" that can change how each shot works (rocket ball, multi-balls, ice balls that freeze water, etc), 4) overall very fun and addicting.Cons: 1) the game throws 3 seriously overpowered permanent "upgrades" at you as you progress through towards your first win/clear. These are the only upgrades you get in the game, but they are so powerful that they kinda trivialize the game thereafter. 2) the game has 4 "bosses" but after youve beaten them ONCE they are never fought again, replaced on the map simply with a normal hole. the bosses are great, so only having to beat them once in a roguelike is a strange choice that makes subsequent runs less fun. 3) the holes are a little long, making a full run 3-5 hours depending on your speed. 4) the postgame is nearly non-exisitent. For a rogue-like, i wouldve liked more difficulties, more modifiers to unlock after wins ( like slay the spire's ascension system) or..... anything really. The only thing to push you to play more after the first win is getting better scores on the leaderboard. This is the ONE thing i would like to see in future content updates, it's my biggest gripe with the game, and IF it got any kind of post-game system like i mentioned above, i would give it a much higher score as a roguelike.Final Score: As an indie Golfer: 9/10.                    As a roguelike: 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Each playthrough is a set of golf courses chosen randomly from over 70 courses. Unlocks come in the way of "Ace" cards during each run, which aid you during play by affecting your shots in numerous fun ways or providing additional bonuses to help you from losing.No permanent progression that I can see, unfortunately, It's not like your typical roguelite, but it is fun (and hard) as heck!Think of this game as a fusion of 2D golf and precision platformer with a little roguelite spice.EDIT: Correction, there is a form of permanent progression, but it's minimal? You do unlock permanent upgrades after defeating bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential, but at the end of the day it heaps too much on you and isn't that fun.I really love the core mechanics of using cards and golfing to traverse the levels.What brings the game down is a ton of quality of life issues:1. After i hit the ball, I have to wait for the same stupid animation over and over again. This is my number one issue. It takes forever.2. The default perspective is way too close. I have to re-unzoom at the start of every level.3. The boss levels are THE WORST. Watching the boss have to swing his club and wait for that whole thing to happen brings the game to a screeching halt.4. No warp to later levels is pretty brutal. The first zone takes a long time to get through.5. Remembering how the cards work and how to activate them causes me a lot of mistakes that feel cheap.6. There isn't quite enough variety in the core game look to keep me hooked.7. The golf cart is cute, but at the end of the day feels like another slow 'watch this animation!' cut scene. Speed it up!Overall I was really digging the game. I could totally see some additional support bringing this game back into positive territory because it is so close to a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, I am still gonna give the game a good grade, but dude. There are SO many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ problems in this game, that I can totally understand all of the negative reviews. This has some of the worst replay-ability for a rougelike and some of the worst balancing I have seen in on too. Is bad balancing a bad thing fun wise? Nah, I enjoy plenty of broken things. The problem is though that some cards do practically ♥♥♥♥ all or are totally redundant.The fire ball and ice ball are beyond useless before the caverns.The time stop does not INSTANTLY stop you, you get a lil nudge that still goes on a bit that is JUST noticeable enough that it messes with your timing over those teeny tiny holes.The portals half the time just totally break out on me. I can't get inside of them, maybe my game is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ who knows. The pins are psychotically broken. Honestly, you can keep half of them in the game for all I care. I think they are totally fine, maybe make them more expensive? Idk. But the other half of those pins? The ones like have every idol in the map broken upon entering? 50% PERCENT OFF ALL STORE PRODUCTS? Starting every single shot with ♥♥♥♥ like multi-ball, rocket, or timestop? Jesus christ. Dude just take all of the permanent powerup pins, the break every idol on the map (the one for just the silvers is fine I guess), and take out the 50% discount pin, make the remaining "pretty good ones" just more expensive or harder to get, then boom. I'm not gonna say it fixes all of the problems with the balancing, but it puts the game back to a point where the difficulty is cruel, but tightly knit together. Crap like permanent rocket  and whatnot just busted the game wide open.WHY CAN YOU NOT REFIGHT THE BOSSES, THOSE WERE ALL COOL AS ♥♥♥♥?!Those are the complaints off the top of my head, I can't really remember much else, except that the hole in one achievement is total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.To briefly cover the good, the ost ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bangs, the art style is extremely strong, the story is very simple but the characters are cute, the physics are looser than a tiger ♥♥♥♥♥, but I personally find it fun. The cards that actually matter let you adapt just a bit better, and honestly, most holes can be completed with minimal card usage if you just git gud. I won't pretend that's anywhere NEAR easy, but I was able to go a couple of endgame holes without substantial card usage. I would totally kill if in the future, there was added replayability where you could PLAY 3 campaigns as the other golfers, each with their own buffs but they have a debilitating weakness, a challenge run unique to them. The new true ending would thus require beating the game 4 times in order for them all to ascend. Wouldn't that be awesome?This game is like losing your virginity to a ♥♥♥♥♥. It's not oiled up in the right places, and certain parts of the experience feel like its giving you a disease, but it was still pretty fun and an experience I won't be forgetting soon, even if there are grasses greener than this games ♥♥♥♥♥ pubes.

_childDocuments_.review: The most crushingly difficult 18 holes of golf you will ever try to play. It's entirely possible that you will face an unwinnable situation after struggling through 9+ holes and you just have to suck it up and come to terms with starting over again. You will be replaying the first few holes over and over and over again. Even though the course is randomly generated, you'll still see the same stuff over and over again in the first areas due to how often you need to replay them. The design on some of the holes is very obtuse and difficult to figure out the right path.There is some variety in the ace cards and curses, but not all that much. It's a simple game, you just need everything to go right over the course of all 18 holes and any mistake has you start over again. I'm writing this after a very frustrating 4 hours so it comes off negative, but I did really enjoy a lot about the game. The music and pixel art is really cool and it has a nice pick up and play ability, so it's easy to keep on the back burner while you play other games when you get too frustrated by this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Cursed to Golf is a very unique and fun game. I've run into a handful of issues that have detracted from my enjoyment. There are a few hazards located around fast travel points that punish you for going into these fast travel points. It doesn't feel good and really ruins the mood. I tried going through a pipe twice and lost a ball for each attempt. Kinda sucks. I can't complain about the difficulty provided; it feels good making godlike shots and doing risky plays that could make me lose. I do dislike some of the extreme difficulty focused in Hell. Spoilers: Birdie's danger zones are way too oppressive. The danger zones in Hell are wider than they actually appear. If you land on the outskirts of Birdie's zone you will be grabbed. This is kind of hard to avoid if you're trying to maneuver through the very tight and spike littered land that is H E L L.Though I have these couple issues, I really love this game. It's so much fun and it has so much style and charm. Kinda feels like a blend of Worms Armageddon and Golf. You have so many tools in your inventory besides the club. You can shape the field and 'cheat' your way through it with Ace moves. It's lit.I originally tried playing this with an arcade stick and that was no good. Best with a controller. Or anything with a right stick.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:-Fun mechanics & gameplay-Unique gameplay-Great art, design, animation, & soundtrack-very challenging-Inexpensive for the quality and contentNegatives:-No PERMANENT progression i.e. skill tree. You really just have to save ace cards that you can buy by grinding money in early levels before making a serious run. Even then, they're expendable and you can only save up to 40 cards (they don't stack), and have to be at an item shop to withdraw them.-The card album only shows 4 cards at a time, you can't auto-sort them, and they don't stack in the album. Please make this more user friendly, devs.-No tutorial for how to use some abilities and how some traps work. I didn't realize the tombstones were "-1 penalty" hazards - I thought they might be a helpful thing? It is the underworld after all.-Some controls are unintuitive (some ace card abilities activate with left click, some with right click, and it seems kinda arbitrary. This might be so you can stack abilities but I might be wrong)-No way to know where a teleporter will take you. The "birdie eye" view really ought to show you a dotted line or something so you can see where a teleporter will take you, as some just dunk you straight into a hazard and that feels super unfair.-Really difficult, and frustrating at times when you get handed an unwinnable situation.To the devs: The ace cards and new 'meta' abilities (Like a 1 time checkpoint after you lose once per round) that you get from bosses don't feel enough like a permanent progression. Give me a skill tree! Let me get OP so I can breeze past the first several holes, and feel the challenge of later holes! That's the point of a rogue-like. I don't wanna have to grind, save money, buy a bunch of upgrade packs, put them all in my album, rinse and repeat, just to feel like I have enough resources to make it further in the game. This is a great game, but PERMANENT progression would take this from a 7/10 to a 10/10 for me.
