_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game? It wears its inspiration on its sleeve. The developer was very clearly intending to put their own spin on Portal. From the gun that manipulates your environment, to the interactables that are used to facilitate the puzzles, to the snarky AI companion. Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery, but a poor imitation is what I found this game to be.The first and most egregious thing that took away from the experience for me was Astra. Whichever millennial wrote the dialogue for Astra did not have the comedic timing or wit to compete with what was written for  GLaDOS or Wheatley. I found myself dreading every line of dialogue delivered for Astra. I genuinely did not laugh once. I am not one to use the term "cringe", but it's the best word I can think of to describe how this felt.  Had the game not had this talking gun AI companion I don't think it would have been any worse off for it. There are elements to the level design of this game that at times can be wildly frustrating. Having to redo the launches of blocks off of the springboard platforms over and over due to the random nature of the launches definitely got old after blocks would take a trajectory with just enough momentum to barely roll off of the moving small platform you have to land them on. There are also sections where conveyor belts are meant to deliver you from one platform to the next, but they are ever so slightly raised above the level of the platform you are on so you must jump to get on them. The issue is that the jump the game was designed with either is not high enough or the belt has a collision model that finds you jumping and getting stuck right at the edge over and over again. Completely unnecessary. Give the player enough of a jump that they can reliably get onto a belt that is connected to a platform they are already on, or lower the belt.The game is not necessarily a very difficult game. The only real difficulty comes as a bit of a cheap shot, where you are forced to start your puzzles over multiple times as a function of the games main mechanic: Rewinding. Often times you will only be able to figure out the first few steps needed to progress forward. As you do so, you realize that in order to have your blocks do what you need them to do, you have to situate them at the very beginning of your run in a different way because this game is all about rewinding. Once you figure out you need your block doing a certain thing for you later on, it means you have to restart it's rewind so that action is the first thing you do in order to have it be rewound to the spot as you move forward in real time. This is forced trial and error. It feels like artificial difficulty and artificial padding of game length. The game is graphically nice enough to look at. I would certainly not call it ugly by any means. There are a handful of scenes I would even call "striking". It would be nice if there was a bit more artistic variety, but obviously this falls prey to the same constraints Portal had because you are in a facility. Even still, there is a scant bit of environmental shakeup throughout the game. The industrial feeling of The Entropy Centre was a bit tiresome for the length of the game.A very peculiar inclusion to The Entropy Centre is combat. I find myself scratching my head as to the decision process behind surmising that this would be a net positive for the game's design. As it's implemented, the combat feels very unsatisfying and much like an afterthought. I can see the reasoning behind including it in some instances, where the idea is to induce pressure on the player, but with how janky this feels I can't help but believe that perhaps environmental hazards would've been a more immersive route.The Entropy Centre as a concept is not bad. It's an idea with potential, however the execution really fell short for me. I pushed through to the end not out of enjoyment, but out of a completionist personality trait that can work to my detriment. I am not one to be negative like this but I just did not come away from this experience with a smile on my face and positive memories.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: "Entropy Centre" is a Sci-fi puzzle game that at first glance is a clone of the portal games but manages to distinguish itself in several ways. The core mechanic of the game revolves around a gun that allows you to rewind objects, similar to the iconic portal gun. While the puzzles can be challenging, the concept becomes clearer as you progress. The game atmosphere is great and the storyline is engaging, although I found myself somewhat confused by the end. Overall i enjoy playing the game.Since Valve is not gonna make portal 3,  having these indie puzzle games is the next best thing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: There is very obvious inspiration from the Portal series, which is hard to avoid in puzzle games these days, but I am all for it. This is the first game I have played that captured how incredible portal was, but this did it in a much more modern style and it worked really well. I enjoyed every second. The humor, the puzzles, the story, were all so captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, I am absolutely astonished at how great this game is. I saw this game on the "coming soon" page 3 days before it came out, bought it on the day of and played it for a bit the following day, I knew nothing about the game except it looked like a fun new spin on the portal series, and that's exactly what it felt like through the first half of the game. Very simple story shown at the beginning with a very simple way to complete it, complete puzzles. *SPOILERS*But... Something felt off with how long the game was when I checked the achievements and how quiet and still everything was, then the "ghost" is introduced, and me being who I am got a little scared because I hate horror, but also calming myself down thinking "ah, it's just good ol Biggles" and not thinking to much on it. The puzzles keep getting better and better as each chapter goes by with fun new interactive ways to complete each level with just a cube or two. Just like portal 2 when entering the old aperture science laboratories, you enter this endless office that keeps progressively changing, now something definitely feels off. Then that ghost appears again except this time there's more than one and there's also writing on the wall warning you of "rewinding the cataclysmic event" and you soon realize this is your office, and your email, and that you stayed here when everyone else left. This is right about where I lost it and had to finish the game this night because I was expecting some awesome looking 8/10 puzzle game but to be treated with a plot twist to make an actual story, 10/10. I am very grateful I came across this game when it came out, and if I'm gonna be honest I thought the price was a bit much for just a puzzle game, but now I realize the length and the effort that was put into the making of this game. Honestly a lot cheaper for something I would enjoy this much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This was quite the journey, I have to say. First off, the graphics and music are both great, and from the get go the atmosphere feels awesome, so that is a good start.The characters are quite likeable, not that there are many (main ones at least), and the dialogue and interactions between Aria and Astra are especially nice, but for the side characters you see in the terminal messages, well, they're as good as characters like that can be for the most part, but that's fine as they aren't the focus.The world building is interesting; the architecture of the buildings themselves feels mostly basic on the outside (Not all of them, just some, probably because of seeing mostly grey), with some interesting design choices, but the general area and the story it contains are quite something. I found exploring when I had the chance with a bridge cube to be quite good. For example, in the beach area, I used the bridge cube to meet a little bot out in a boat in the distance. I didn't even notice he was there until I got closer, so that was a cool find.The story is bittersweet, I think, especially the ending, if, well, I really hope for the best outcome. I'm not going to comment too much on it because it'd be a spoiler, but it is a good story. I liked it, and it certainly shows determination.The puzzles for me weren't too difficult, only towards the end were, I think, 2 or 3 that were somewhat difficult, but your experience may certainly differ. Personally, though I had a blast doing them, it felt great doing them.The game also feels greatly optimised, I had everything on ultra and for the most part it was completely fine, only the rare stutter here and there when I was loading a new big area, or when something HUGE was breaking down.For the bad, I'd say it's rough around the edges there were times I could see into places I probably shouldn't, and invisible wells blocking you from walking to the toilet but not blocking you from walking around to the side of the bathroom stalls, and the music cutting out if you opened the menu and stayed there for too long, for example.The UI for the main menu is bland and basic but that's not too much of a problem since it's just the menu.Other than that, I don't really have many complaints about it. They could have probably used a water splash sound effect for when walking on wet areas, that certainly felt missing. Oh and also Overall, it was a very fun puzzle game with great graphics and music and a nice and bittersweet story. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Really a fantastic spiritual successor to the Portal games. Not only is this a thrilling action puzzle game, but its also a sci-fi mystery with lots of little pieces to uncover as you gradually discover the true nature of where you are and how everything has come to be. The hidden bits of lore that you uncover really add to the atmosphere.The game takes about 8-9 hours to complete and also has a built in custom level designer and custom level browser. Bottom line: If you enjoyed Portal 1 and 2, you will enjoy The Entropy Centre.

_childDocuments_.review: So, first off, this was a gift that came out of the blue in December of 2023.  My thanks to that individual, whose privacy I'll respect.  I was touched then, and remain so now.But how about the game?  It was a journey, let me start with that.  Strip out the plot, and it's a game about solving puzzles.  There's an in-game reason for solving the puzzles which is, bluntly, very silly.  But the puzzles themselves were kind of fun and made me work a bit; I stopped partway through a few of them for dinner and such, so let's say... 12 hours.  And I really enjoyed myself for 11 of them.That remaining 1 hour made me take pause a bit, moan privately to my wife a few times, but I stuck it out, and I was rewarded.  And I really want to explain all of this to you so it makes sense, but if you want an elevator pitch, I quite liked the puzzles themselves and I warmed up to much of the game, the plot especially.  The "combat" still felt like padding.  So there you go.  If you want more details, stick around, there's a fair bit I want to unpack for you.First, the gameplay.  The core of it is that you have a device that lets you undo 30-ish seconds of an object's movement.  You don't have to do it all at once, you can undo it in bits and pieces.  The objects in question are clear:  basic crates, portable jump pads, portable bridges, etc. so a very limited, obvious selection.  Crates need to go into certain positions to interact with other items, or just hold down pressure plates that activate other things in the puzzle room.The problem is that there are way more pressure plates (etc.) then you have items you can fool with.  So you need to work out the sequence of steps you need to do to solve the puzzle and where each of your items ought to be for each step.  Then you move the items through those steps , and then as you do your various steps, you can  those objects as required.  So it means you have to conceptualize the solution, and then work it out in reverse besides.  It's a bit like programming:  do these steps, in this sequence, to get these results.Some puzzles aren't immediately obvious and require some exploration. While most puzzles have an obvious flow to them, a few (mostly near the end) try to fool you with superfluous steps.  This is important, as your ability to rewind objects is limited, so efficiency is important.  Don't dawdle and second-guess yourself, go drag your crate around its steps promptly.Loved all that.I compared this to Portal, but there's one really key difference:  Very little in this game required much in the way of reflexes at all.  The trickiest part is making sure you landed on jump pads you placed, as you fell from some height.  Portal, on the other hand, had a few things requiring good timing and reflexes.  If you're not the fastest gun in the Wild West, you'll still do fine here, and that's even with what fightin' there is.So yes, there's some combat-ish sequences.  Fighting is mostly catching enemy plasma bullets (which move at a sedate rate) and rewinding them.  Sometimes you also have to find switches to flip in a room at the same time.  These seem like filler, mostly; a sort of where's waldo but your life on the line.  Fortunately, even if you whiff it, your character can take a hit every ten seconds or so; it's forgiving in a way.  I just didn't find it compelling.There are also a couple action sequences where you need to rush through an area while selectively rewinding collapsing scaffolds.  That's got a bit of spectacle to it, and they're pretty linear so it's just a matter of getting through it and not dawdling.  The plot at first starts off very... jokey.  At first I thought it was trying to bite on Portal's style a bit, a sort of "ha ha dystopia" thing going on.  You are accompanied by a jokey-goofy AI device trying for oblivious humour instead of Portal's style of a kind of menacing AI trying for oblivious humour.  I don't want to write a whole essay describing it here, but you can buy me a pint and I'll talk your ear off.  This game leans towards the zanier style of humour, which I'm admittedly less fond of when it's overdone.  All the same, it does set a goofy tone.As you go along in the game, though, you see (and can read) various terminals.  These give you little tidbits about the other people that used to be here, and what they were doing.  The mood of these terminals changes over the game's progress.  There's a bit of a... well, I don't want to call it a "grimmer" undercurrent, per se, but it becomes apparent that others in that facility are faced with some difficult decisions to make. That stands in sharp contrast to the AI device, which... well, for me, it did add a bit of weight to the whole game.  I might have done the AI a little differently, perhaps, but that'd take a lot of thinking and a pint.The ending of the game... well, some people called it dark.  I thought it revealed the sheer, dogged determination of the protagonist.  Get me another pint, and we can get into a heated chat about this in a pub if you want.  I'm cheap. Anyway, I had a good time on the whole.  I'm grateful I was given this game, even though it took me like nine months to get around to playing it.  I should have done that sooner.A bit of an obligatory thing:  I hate advertisement, and advertising myself is awkward, so I'll put it down here.  If all this rambling mess of words didn't give you the hives, I do some streaming on a very regular schedule, and I'm partially there just to talk to people who show up.  If you're here, you're my kind of people.   - there's a schedule which I stick closely to, even.Oh yeah.  And I'll get the sequel to this if ever they make one.  No complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better Portal-like games. Decent sense of humour. The setting and characters are maybe a little too derivative of Portal 2, but that's standard and inescapable for this genre of first person puzzler.The game's main strengths are the puzzle and exploration sides of things. The puzzles aren't super-hard but aren't all completely trivial. The mechanics have some new twists on them, and fit together well. A few things are hidden in the environment for you to find, or find out how to reach, which makes looking around worthwhile.Graphics are very nice. Voice acting is good, too. Story is interesting enough that you want to keep going.Runs great on Steam Deck.If you like the genre then you should like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: [game purchased as part of a charity bundle, designating 'received for free' just in case. It's a bit of a grey area]I wanted to like this game so bad, I really did. Portal 2 is one of my favorite games of all time, so maybe I can't offer the most objective of reviews on this game- but it just never does enough to call itself anything other than "we have portal at home".Mechanically, the physics are just too jank. All of the puzzle elements are slightly smaller than they should be, and your jump is miserably short, which combine to make everything extremely fiddly. And because all of the puzzles involve long rewind chains, you'll often have to redo entire puzzles from the beginning because of a missed jump. The cherry on top of this jank sundae is the 30 second rewind limit. It sucks. I hate it.Story and atmosphere wise, I like what it's going for but I just don't think it sticks the landing. A huge minus for me is the extremely limited soundtrack. It's hard to feel any sense of rising tension when you're puzzling to the same music in act 15 as you did in act 3. I'd say pacing is also an issue here: there's too many long and tedious puzzles towards the end, draining any sense of urgency. I'd say the best section of the game is   Honestly I wish they'd committed to the vibes of that area for the whole thing. TLDR: There's a lot to like about this game, but unfortunately it's all covered in a film of jank. I'd say give it a try, but only if it's on sale for cheaper than portal 2.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game, it's very portal-esque but manages to be innovative with the time rewinding mechanic. It's a refreshing take on portal and it's visuals.Solving the puzzle and then having to solve it backwards to get the elements into the right place is creative.Unfortunately this game doesn't feel polished. Some places the background structures feel"off" and unfinished. I found a missing texture which let me stare into the void.The company's logo is just an 'E', would have been nice to have something more unique and recognizable.And the puzzle mechanics are... finicky. Hitting a jump pad could be a lot more forgivingand trying to stay on one of those collapsible structures with another cube feels very cramped.This in general makes it kinda easy to die and some of the checkpoints are very unforgiving.All-in-all, I still recommend it and wish the developers could fix these issues in an update.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre was a portal inspired game filled with a rich story that encapsulates the flow of time. The game is great for beginners, as the puzzles were easy enough for me to complete them in under 10 minutes. I will give the Entropy Centre 6/10, because I felt the puzzles were too easy and repetitive. I believe that they extended the story too much for the . Lastly the  were the worst part to my opinion, as they were just run to a button and to the the next one and maybe get killed along the way and start all over again.The Entropy Centre 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, nice soundtrack. Jump platforms are extremely annoying. Some puzzles are "keep trying until the physics cooperates enough for you to succeed." My longest puzzle took half an hour of trying to execute the solution after I figured it out. The ending was very unsatisfying. If that bothers you, skip it. Otherwise it's worth a run.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! The puzzles feels fresh and innovative. Very portal-esque gameplay.A few areas are rush-events but most are very relaxed puzzles.The controls are great and the game looks really good on a Steam Deck, though some text is a bit hard to read on such a small screen.If you like 3d puzzlers like portal this is a solid choice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I really enoyed the game, it was a fun story and i figured it out about half way through and found out about the "ghosts" half way as well, spooky and interesting for sure! i cant help but think my ability to "double jump" with the pads by letting it drop and landing on it mid air was apart of the puzzles but it helped out in the long run XD 10/10 good game for sure, just wish it had a happy ending :P
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: As a similar-to-but-legally-distinct-from Portal style puzzle game, it's fantastic. Maybe a little on the easy side in the first half, but there were some real headscratchers later on, and getting through the whole thing without a guide was extremely satisfying. There's a wide variety of doodads to work with - boring cubes, laser cubes, bridge cubes, jump pads, three different "change-your-thing-into-another-thing "fields, fans, conveyor belts, and more. And every time Astra said  "New puzzle element!", initially I would groan because it felt like it was becoming too much, but when I actually got to puzzling, it never felt like too much. So if you're looking for this style of puzzler, The Entropy Centre is a sure bet.My gripes mainly revolve around the story. 1. A good 80% of the game is "Get to the reactor." I'm pretty sure that starts in Chapter 3 and ends in Chapter 11, or something like that. It's a whole lot of stalling, with no interesting narrative or character threads filling in the huge gap.2. As soon as you learn what the game is about, your brain is going to say "Hrm, I wonder if this will happen," or "I wonder if the game will end this way." There's a very good chance you are right. There's so much potential for mind-bending weirdness in here, yet the story is as straight as an arrow. Don't play for the story, but  play for the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Center feels very much like Portal. I mean that in a good way, in case you were wondering.While a lot of aspects of the game feel extremely similar to the mechanics of Portal, the fundamental design of the game makes it feel new, and different, almost like what Portal could have been if it had another sequel years down the line.The storytelling... well, let's just say that even though I'd already pieced together the ending well before it happened, the ending sequence still sent shivers throughout my body.Never have I wanted a game to have less levels (so I could see the ending I was anticipating sooner) while at the same time, wanting more and more of them.The game's mechanics were unique and enjoyable, the puzzles were challenging, but solvable with enough time and thought, the story was top-notch, especially all the bits of lore scattered throughout that give a feeling of unease, and inevitability, with some humour sprinkled in.I got this game during a sale, but I would have bought it at full price and enjoyed it all the same. I only have just under 8 hours of play time, but it feels like much, much longer than that, and is of course, still worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game only because of its excellent puzzle mechanics and a couple of superbly designed levels which will make your head hurt until you solve them. If you like Portal-like games, you will absolutely enjoy the puzzle-solving gameplay of The Entropy Centre.With that said, here's what I don't like:- The world-building and story are really poor and uninspired. There's almost nothing to immerse me in the world of the game properly, and the writing is awful. - The game's world design and visuals are washed out, repetitive and boring. The game looks ugly and outdated but not in a retro way, it simply doesn't have good-quality visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Wait wait wait, a game where you wake up as the sole occupant of a facility and your memory is a little fuzzy, and you have a gun that breaks the laws of physics and the gun has an AI in it that compels you to complete test chambers using the gun to solve puzzles and cubes to trigger switches, and there are bots that try to kill you along the way, the moon is involved somehow, and you’re not entirely certain of the AI’s intentions? SWEET! I love that game! 🤣All joking aside, it's a great game. Yes, it sounds a bit like Portal 2 if you're *trying* to make it sound that way, but the game mechanics work very differently from Portal, so it's a satisfying puzzler experience that is different enough to be its own thing. It has its own distinct personality/atmosphere, so doesn't feel like an imitation of the other.I'm working my way through some other "Portal like" or "1st person platforming puzzler" games, but The Entropy Centre stood out and is the first of the lot I completed.Why do I like it? The story is interesting, I like the dialog, the voice acting is great, and love the humor. I like the music. I love the "aha!" moment when I figure out how to solve a puzzle. Even though the puzzles are relatively easy, and usually simple to execute once you know the solution, I do appreciate that the solution is mainly based on figuring it out, and generally not based on tedious timing.So far, this is my third favorite "Portal like" game, only behind The Talos Principle and of course the Portal series itself. All of which are highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game fun, if occasionally tedious when I messed up some of the platforming jumps and had to start a puzzle over again, and is worth a try if you liked Portal 1&2.It is however not as good as the games that inspired it, with the way the story is told in particular lacking the same kind of impact that you see in Portal. Which is a shame because the premise of the game lends itself to some very interesting story beats that are sadly relegated to optional text files that you can miss if you're not deliberately looking for them.Overall I'd say around an 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games.Some gameplay spoilers ahead. The Entropy Centre is a first person physics puzzle game, with some simple platforming gameplay in some chapters. The puzzles revolve around using objects and switches, while using your “gun” that can control the flow of time in specific objects and small structures.I won’t spoil the story, so I’ll just say that I enjoyed it very much and found it very interesting and engaging. It has a very elaborate and well written world and time, with its specific lore and scientific (as in science fiction) explanations for the events taking place. The interactions between the main character and her partner are also entertaining, with some jokes and funny conversations between the two.The graphics are very good (4K ultra settings), especially the environments and backgrounds, like when you look outside the window and see Earth, as well as the particle and light effects you see within the game. Only up close, some of the textures used seem to have a lower resolution, but it’s not very noticeable. The OST helps set the tone of the game, with abstract and ominous futuristic sounds that you hear in the puzzle areas, but changes to a more exhilarating rhythm in some parts of the game. The voice narration is also very well done, for both the main character and the robotic companion, and, as mentioned, the conversations between them are interesting and fun to listen to.The puzzles start very simple, mostly on the first levels and later in the first puzzle of the chapters where new objects are introduced, and there are a lot of them, but not all are used at the same time. Only later on, the puzzle start getting more complex, with a lot of different steps to do and objects to place, but you just need to remember to . It took me some time, but I managed to solve all the puzzles on my own without any help.Unfortunately, there are some bugs regarding the achievements, I got one on chapter 7 and a friend got another on chapter 1. The chapters were concluded but the achievement didn’t pop… it might be related to the connection between Steam and the same itself, maybe not saving on the cloud might prevent this.  27 Achievements. Around 10 hours, without any help. Easy, it might take time and a few tries but most players will be able to solve most puzzles without help, just look well at your surroundings. Easy, but a bit time consuming without a guide for the collectibles: most are easy to spot but a few are very well hidden. Most of the other achievements are unmissable and only a few others require doing something special in specific locations that can be revisited after you finish the game. The Entropy Centre is a physics puzzle game with very good ambience and fun and accessible puzzle solving. The world, story and the characters are also well written and interesting and you’ll be eager to find out how it will all end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable Portal clone, runs well on an updated system on max settings, mild stutter here or there, but nothing game breaking.  Puzzles are simple at first but then get more complex as I progress, wish there was more stuff to interact with like in portal, but its a minor gripe.  Guessing I'm about half way though based on achievements so it may be a bit on the short side.  Hope they add a workshop mode or more story later on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: In the 15 years since  first appeared in the Orange Box bundle there have been many clones and homages of varying quality and degrees of originality. How does this one fair? Well, despite shamelessly ripping off 's story and level structure, tone, and even humor,  does so with considerable heart and delightful detail. If you loved  you'll likely love this. I had a great time with it.As with  your task is to solve a series of puzzles using buttons and cubes for a convoluted scientific reason. As with  something has gone wrong with the science and the facility is falling apart. As with  you have a wacky sidekick to provide hints and comic relief. And there are even cute robots. Really, the only significant difference is in your primary puzzle-solving gun-tool: here you "rewind" time on objects, requiring you to think temporally as well as spatially.And yet  is good at all the above. The excellent story has a classic sci-fi premise that fits well enough with the puzzle mechanic. The characters are charming and hilarious. And there's a nice addition of non-puzzle adventure areas to provide a change of pace. As for the puzzles, they are generally satisfying. The increase in difficulty is quite gentle and I found the first half of the game, perhaps even more than half, to be a bit too easy. My patience was rewarded with some juicy challenges later on.I must mention that the initial release was a bit buggy with some wonky physics here and there and a broken achievement. Since then it has been patched and feels more polished.All in all,  is the opposite of groundbreaking. It wants to achieve exactly what another game did and, well, it does.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Had a pretty fun time with The Entropy Centre. Conceptually, the whole mechanic of rewinding objects forces you to rewire your brain which does set it apart from most other games in the genre. Unfortunately, you learn to think in this way extremely early on and then the whole rest of the game is a total breeze. Not a single puzzle except for the very, very last one in the game ever really stumped me and even that one was solved in about 25 minutes. I appreciate the lengths they've gone to in stretching the rewind mechanic as far as possible but its interactions with the rest of the puzzle pieces sprinkled throughout the game are not very innovative and we've seen them in countless other first person puzzlers.This game can be comfortably beaten with all achievements (using a guide for collectibles) in 6-7 hours making it a short and concise experience. The writing and voice acting never overstay their welcome and successfully manage to examine some pertinent questions to our time. The Entropy Centre is not something I'd recommend to people looking to get into the genre as there are so many others who've come before and done it better, but to veterans looking for some more first person puzzle action, this is certainly worthy of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Don't normally make reviews, but this was such an exceptional game I felt like I needed to. The gameplay is very inspired by Portal, which isn't a bad thing by any means, however where the game stands out from Portal is through it's exceptional and fun characters and it's interesting story. Easily a 9.5/10. Only reason I wouldn't give it a 10/10 is I ran into a few bugs, non game breaking though, and they could easily be fixed in a few patches.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game. Nice spiritual successor to Portal. 2 things that stood out to me:- lack of centering. I can only explain this by... you know how Portal pulled you to the center of your portals from jumping? TEC doesn't do that, leading to some jumps you can miss by centimeters. And if you've set up a 30 second route using the games mechanic, it can get a bit annoying. Be aware.- grabbing objects seems a little off. Like, if you're close enough to a block to grab it, it's finicky.I liked the concept, and liked the companion. I didn't finish it because I got tried of setting up puzzles just to fall off s platform I needed to be on. That and I reached the point in the game where I was looking up solutions, and knew I would've never considered the way to go about it.Still, recommended. Solid 7/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-The Entropy Centre is a first person logic puzzle game that takes a good amount of inspiration from Portal but is able to carve out a strong identity of it's own.  This genre is dominated by the Portal series and the Talos Principle series, making it extremely difficult for aspiring dev's to achieve success.  While I don't think this game is good as either series, I do think it's hands down the next best first person puzzler.  I really enjoyed my time w/ this mind bending beast of a game.  The entire game revolvs around rewinding time and new mechanics are added consistently throughout the roughly 10-15 hr campaign.  It took me just over 12 hrs to reach the finish line and I enjoyed close to every minute.Consenus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  This game is really fun, but it's not perfect.  Since the key mechanic is time reversal, you have to constantly think steps out backwards.  Typically, it's only 2-3 steps per device that you are rewinding, but it will start to get tough to keep everything together in your head as you are rewinding multiple devices 3 or even 4 times in the later puzzles.  This game is going to get compared to Portal 2 a lot but I don't think that's a bad thing.  I actually think that there is a lot of room for this game to grow if the dev did want to make a sequel in the future.  If you love Portal or the Talos Principle, The Entropy Centre may just be the next best first person puzzler on the market right now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of meaty, fun and challenging puzzles to solve with no true hints of any kind. Lots and lots and lots and lots....lots and lots and lots...okay cool it with the puzzles guys. this game took 3 or 4 sessions because of my lack of desire to open a door and see another flipping puzzle with something slightly different than before. I'm not saying the story was bad or the puzzles weren't GOOD, but it certainly was not engaging enough to play so many puzzles to beat the game, because only a few puzzles were truly satisfying to figure out.  and the good feeling of realizing how to solve most the others was curbed because you had already figured out how to solve them, but now you have to wait for the cubes to rewind all the way through the cube changer and then on the laser button and off the laser button and on the elevator button and the door button to another cube and then back and then--Oh $H!%& I forgot the put the cube on the final button so I have to jump down and setup the whole thing again. NOW I can go through the exit! One of the times I quit was when I had to set up 5 times because my brain solved the puzzle 10 minutes before my hands figured out how to control in midair, causing me to miss the bridge and fall, meaning the 2 minutes of setting up and rewinding cubes was to be done all over again. Good Night. I didn't feel smart--I felt like the clumsiest circus trapeze clown in the tent with only myself to blame. In conclusion, if you like lots of challenging puzzles, you may like this game. Lord knows it took me a while. I sure hope some of my 19 hour playtime is me leaving the game on overnight or something because yikes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing world building, characters, story and voice acting. Not a bad looking game either.But the puzzles are either too easy or more often, too repetitive.And after placing another block on yet another square for the hundredth time, I just couldn't go on.That's every puzzle in a nutshell. Find the block and rewind time until the block is on the square that opens the door to the next puzzle. Time manipulation has the potential for so many innovative puzzle ideas. But after 2+ hours the game rarely ever shifts from moving blocks around.Maybe the puzzles get more creative as the game goes on. I only made it to ACT 6.But I wasn't having enough fun to continue. Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: 10 / 10This game is incredible. The moment you step out of the first room in the game, you can feel that there is Portal 2 D.N.A. in every bit of code.The puzzles are simple, but pretty mind twisting in the later chapters. Combat is minimal, but challenging enough without being overly frustrating. And the story is witty and fun.If I didn't know any better, I would think this was made by Valve themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Portal without portals. Aside from the blatant ripoff of the appearance and puzzle elements, it is a (usually) fun and challenging puzzler. All the puzzles had fair solutions and do not require cheesing, but figuring out the solution can really test your logic skills. Being able to think in reverse is a must throughout, as is three dimensional thinking. Just like the game series this was inspired from, it feels so rewarding when you have that a-ha! moment and figure out a tricky part that was causing a mental block. But I had these gripes with the game:Constant music gets annoying during puzzles.It ripped off Portal too much unnecessarily with the appearance. They could have used their imagination more and made the Entropy Centre look much different than Aperture Science.No indication of when checkpoint/save occurs.Too much pointless repeated clutter. Seriously, you see the same cleaning cart in every room and puzzle area.Jumping often sucks. Jump cubes require more precision than seems necessary.But if  you have the itch to play a good puzzle game and you also were a fan of the Portal games, then yes you will enjoy this game. As long  as you can forgive how much it copies from those games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game lives and breathes the DNA of Portal 1 and 2 and that is a good thing! The story is very intriguing and I just wanted to push forward and play more to find out more. The puzzles are a lot of fun and I found them a bit harder than the ones found in the Portal games, but nothing impossible to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game is TEDIOUS.The Puzzles are okay, some quite good, but executing them takes too long.Especially, if you make  one mistake, often you need to start from the very beginning.Also, if you die in a scripted sequence, then again from the top.It's even more painful, when you realize that in this game about rewinding time, you cannot rewind yourself.That would guarantee much smoother experience - I missed way too many jumps in this game.Doing the puzzle is very often a chore.The rest of the game, graphics, stability etc is fine, and I'm enjoying the story so far. I finished about 85%of the game when writing this.But  I cannot recommend a puzzle game in which puzzles don't bring joy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must play for fans of the genre. The central time-rewind mechanic is innovative and makes for those euphoric epiphanic moments when a puzzle comes together. And it is also used in surprisingly well done action sequences to break up the puzzles resulting in a remarkably well paced experience. The game's difficulty scales very nicely, where by the end, you are using everything you have learned about how to think about this particular style of 'order of operations' puzzle to solve very complex rooms.There is the perfect amount of story (both in the global narrative sense (including very nice worldbuilding) and in the local character sense) to push you along without getting in the way - and it is all really compelling. And the overall narrative sticks the landing for a very satisfying ending.It can be frustrating to have the solution to a puzzle in your head, but just failing to execute it (either because you used your 30 seconds on rewind not quite efficiently enough to get everything back where it needs to be, or because you miss a blue bounce box and have start again) but you will also get better at executing the puzzles as well as solving them as the game goes on. The game took me around 10 hours to beat without a guide, which I expect would be around average for players who have played first person puzzle games before. If you enjoy these type of isolated, test-chamber style puzzle games, this is a excellent one of those.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: OK, first of all, like many reviewers have said: Yes, this is basically a clone of Portal/Portal 2 but without the portals, you're accompanied by a talking gun instead of a sentient potato, and you're trying to stop Earth from exploding instead of a giant underground laboratory controlled by a maniac. Basically, if you enjoyed Portal 2 and wanted more, this is the game for you.It's a beautiful game, the puzzles are moderately hard, it feels like you're actually working towards an overarching goal rather than racing to the end of a level.I feel like a lot of the negative reviews are kind of deterring people from buying this game. Yes, the story is kind of a basic "save the world" plot. Yes, . Yes, the levels make you think. Yes, it's harder than Portal. The game was made by , cut him some slack.But if you've finished Portal and/or Portal 2 recently or several years ago and wanted more, this is the closest you're gonna get to a new Portal game without Valve finishing grade school and counting to three.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are way too easy, many times it takes me more time to sit through the dialogue while I wait for the next door to be opened than it does for me to solve the actual puzzles. Was expecting puzzle difficulty equal to that of Portal 2 but the puzzles are honestly easier than the ones I've encountered in Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. I managed to get up to act 4 in under 30 minutes. I'm not saying the game is bad in anyway it's just too easy for me personally and that's why I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10, amazing game amazing graphics, amazing story, amazing soundtrack, great ending and amazing npcs (im honestly attached and need merch) the only complaint i have is that theres no running option when some parts of the game feel like i should be sprinting, and that i couldnt find that cat the emails in the game were talking about p.s some of the puzzles felt a little easy but that very well could be because i play allot of puzzle games and just finished a different time based puzzle game not long ago
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the opportunity to play The Entropy Centre, and I have to say, it was absolutely amazing. A friend of mine recommended it to me because of my love for Portal. Starting the game I saw some similarities between The Entropy Centre and Portal but The Entropy Centre was unique and creative in its own ways. To start, the storyline of The Entropy Centre was fascinating, with a well-crafted plot that kept me looking for lore. I like the ideas they explored and felt rewarded when I went out of my way to look for more information. I loved the writing, characters and the voice acting was great! One of the things that really impressed me about The Entropy Centre was the level design. I found that the puzzles were challenging but not frustrating. The level design pushed users to think outside of the box to solve puzzles. Puzzle solving always felt good and I loved the way the game pushed me out of my comfort zone of thinking. I do not recommend beating the game in one sitting as you may rush and ruin the experience for yourself. You also might get frustrated, so try to take breaks! Overall, I highly recommend The Entropy Centre to anyone looking for a fun, engaging puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fantastic experience so a solo dev this is an absolute triumph Well done!Graphics are great (asset reuse was a little tiring towards the end)Puzzles were great (a few exploits here and there)The Combat was not neededSounds we amazing!Could do with less hand holding (the coloured squares on the ground)The Ending is amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game inspired by Portal, as one can likely assume. It's mechanics are well designed, and intuitive, and the story, while convoluted, does make sense. It does have some minor issues with how objects are placed in the environment, floating grass, corners where you can see outside the map, and similar things. They are however, as previously stated, minor, and only noticeable when paying close attention. Something which is somewhat necessary if you want to find all secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy games like Portal, and this one is really close near it. However, as much as I enjoy the mechanics and the actual level design, the gameplay however is kinda tedious. There is a nice story to discover and lots of interesting conversation mails to be found, however, it feels like they added a bit too many puzzles and not enough story to enjoy. Puzzle after puzzle after puzzle, a lil bit story, a lil bit run away from the cute killerbots and then puzzle puzzle puzzle puzzlesss, it keeps on going and they keep on going with more new "features". And again, all mechanics are great, it's getting a chore to complete them. It's a great game to enjoy who loves puzzling like games such as portal, but for those who enjoy a tad more story, feels a bit lacking. The cute conversations between your weapon and the hero you're playing, its all nice and well, not enough imo. I think i'm about halfway through and it's feeling like a chore to complete the puzzles, rather enjoy the mechanics, story and level design. Unlike the portal games, it feels like the puzzles have been injected into the gameplay instead of building around it. I will recommend this game, but I do have mixed feelings about this. Great voice acting, interesting story to discover, great portalesque gameplay mechanics, but tedious puzzles and there is no real joy to get after finishing the puzzles. Because the puzzling never ends and sure it might be nice for those who really enjoy solving these puzzles, but for the casual player, it will not lol.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING. Its a perfect combination of casual (slightly difficult) game play with spectacular story telling with everything coming together in the end. Side characters were few but more than enough. You will feel very invested on playing the game. Visuals and scenery of the game blew my mind and gave me goosebumps. If you played portal, this gives the same vibes but will still be on another level. Trust me bro. Dude. Damn. GYAT DAMN
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Refunding mostly due to very poor performance, game running at 90fps but stuttering constantly no matter the settings.Game is  just trying way too hard to just be knock-off portal, and it is very off-putting. Some bad voice acting also.Main mechanic is not interesting enough for me to want to bother any further with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A good game if you loved the Portal series of games. Less emphasis on physics based puzzles and more emphasis on sequence and object placement. Allot of the puzzles will involve using parts in the correct sequence (using the entropy gun) and there are allot of different blocks and functions. The atmosphere is very ominous and creepy and there is a surprisingly grim story at the center of the game. Highly recommend for anyone that likes puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Must try for every Portal and puzzle fan. Gorgeous setting and graphics, well fitting soundtrack, engaging story with "collectible" tidbits filling the mystery along the way. Good voice acting.Puzzles have plenty of fun mechanics to play with and all of them are introduced well, maybe even too well. Even though the puzzles are all fairly easy to solve, after getting hang of the rewinding and freezing time, it is still  every time from taking a look what needs to happen to proceeding to arranging the elements in correct order (needing to think in reverse!) and positions to executing the sequence.Few small gripes:   - Puzzles are fairly easy (hardest ones took less than 10 minutes for me to figure out the solution)   - Maybe bit too many introductory puzzles to new elements, one per element would be enough   - Water causing cubes to shoot in the air when trying to grab them is frustrating on the rewind-time limited solutions   - Solutions involving jump boxes are at times incredibly fiddly to execute, those things are darn easy to miss   - Some puzzles can be cheesed with chain jumping the same jump box by rewinding it while you are in airAll in all very worth the asking price, completed the game with almost all of the collectible story bits in 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game a lot! They had a lot of fun messages stored away that helped you piece together the world and the puzzle mechanics were interesting. I don't play many puzzle games so maybe that's why it was a nice challenge but I enjoyed the characters, the personality and style of the game, and the small bits of humor they placed into it. The team put a lot of effort into it and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Could be better. Graphics are great, OST and voice acting are pretty good. The time rewind mechanic is very interesting, but the puzzles are too easy (ignore steam played time, I've actually completed all 15 stages). I had more fun with harder puzzles in other games such as The Spectrum Retreat, Relicta, etc. Also, the robots are obnoxious and unnecessary, the game would be better off without them; in escape sequences they're alright, but in lockdown/regular puzzle stages they're just annoying.Finally, the plot concept is interesting, but the delivery falls flat in terms of atmosphere/environmental storytelling. Endless scribbles on walls and whiteboards with dumbed-down sentences like "Rewind earth??", or "Solve puzzles"... like, no ♥♥♥♥. It's like visiting a game studio and seeing a whiteboard with "Make game??". Also, the emails are pretty uninteresting too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a well-rounded, excellent, puzzle game. I really enjoyed playing it.The puzzles are about moderate in difficulty. I generally finished each puzzle in 7 minutes or less. I prefer that. A variety of new puzzles with new elements is more fun to me than working on the same complex puzzle for an hour. The speed with which I completed each puzzle felt on pace with the urgency of the story. It is well balanced for my tastes.As each mechanic is introduced, the game subtly guides you on how to solve the puzzle. The game does a fantastic job showing you what you  do (I put a lot of weight on this because it lets me quickly filter out bad ideas and "interesting techniques" so I can solve the puzzle correctly). While there is one  correct way to solve the puzzle, I always felt free to step through it the way I wanted.If you know what it's like to set up a complex solution only to fail at the last step and have to set up everything again, then you know it gets old quick. That thought never crossed my mind while playing this game. The rare times when I did have to set up again, it wasn't a chore. The mechanics of the game are well implemented.Somewhat unrelated side note: this game lets you jump whenever you want! I know it's a weird thing to point out but I always feel choked when games don't have or disable jumping. Thank you, Entropy Centre, for letting me jump!The story ties directly in with the main mechanic in the game. The story is unique and it explained  you're solving the puzzles. It's a "Sci-Fi" explanation, but it works perfectly; it doesn't feel like a cheesy justification.There are three voices in the game's story: the player character, a companion, and a facility narrator (I guess you could call him a narrator? He gives status reports/updates as you progress). All three play well off of each other. The voice tone is lighthearted and witty, which generally compliments the game. However, it can feel a little calm during the action sequences. The voice lines fit with each other but don't necessarily portray what's actually on-screen. You could be in a fight for your life and your character sounds like 4% more afraid. This is honestly my only gripe with the game. It doesn't pull your focus away but it also doesn't draw you in as much as it could.It's clear that this game took heavy inspiration from the Portal series. However, the "entropy" mechanic is executed so well that it doesn't feel like a Portal clone. It feels more like a successor.The magic that made Portal fantastic is in The Entropy Centre: a fun and dynamic core mechanic, a story to drive progression, and some witty commentary.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoyed this.It's a great looking game with a time-reversing mechanic, but you already know this before even seeing this review. I reckon it works really well. There were definitely a few where I had to pause for thought and one that got me very frustrated, but it'd be wrong for a game of this genre to not get me like that once or twice.Here's something I'll say in challenge of those reviews that are "it's all the same puzzle". Most of the puzzle chambers are similar in nature. But then so were Portal's.What it *also* does like portal and it's sequel is use the time-reverse mechanic in non-puzzle-chamber settings such as residential areas, museums, control centres which offer that world building side of the game that immerses you in the story.I've played through to the end once. I'm not sure if there are any additional endings (nothing in the discussions, perhaps a dev could reply and tell me :D ) but I'm definitely going to play through again anyway to get the "hat" soon!I got about 10 hours out of this and I feel like I got my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun if you like puzzles. The game feels very much like a mix between The Turing Test and Qube 2, which are both great games. I've player for about 5 hours so far and still have some mechanics that haven't been introduced yet which is a good since since most puzzle games tend to be short.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, I fully recommend it if you love puzzles. As people say, it's Portal's worthy spiritual successor. But I have to give it a No for two very painful reasons:- Bad platforming. Please, Devs, implement automatic fall correction so that you always land on the jump cube if you'd fall near it. All good platforming games implement generous invisible landing surfaces to avoid frustration.- The ending. It looks like the protagonist is dumb or just ignoring all the clues she's seeing about what's about to come. Even if she keeps her final decision, some more elaboration on the dilemma would have been appreciated. It looks like she is completely blind to what the player is seeing from chapters 12 to 15.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: So this game looks like it might be a portal style game and while I really REALLY love the new tools you get to use and their use throughout is really cool BUT BUT, unfortunately that's killed by the way you have to interact with some of these later in the higher level puzzles. UNLESS YOU LAND EXACTLY AND I MEAN LIKE EXACTLY ON THE SWEET SPOT YOUR NOT GOING TO INTERACT WITH THE DAMN TOOL!! WHAT IN THE HECK??? I mean this game has sooo much potential to take it to the next level but it falls flatter than a crepe. I can't give it a good rating because this is such an integral part of the game. At least in portal and its successors your given a bit of lea-way and don't have to be mid exact center to use its tools and thats what makes it fun. Also some tools come and are incredibly useful but you never see them again. I hope the devs see this and maybe expand out those contact area's a little so the puzzles arent impossible because you were 1 mmm off the center of that tool.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game will be a smooth play thru but underwhelming for anyone that has played a good share of fps puzzle games. The puzzles are pretty straight forward and require little skill with platforming and timing. It's more about understanding how to reverse order of operations and standard problem solving. What really impressed me about this games was the environment, characters and way the story was told. Everything was well paced and had plenty of variety. But on the story I will say that you pretty much guess the whole thing in the interlude, which really sucks because they do have a cool delivery of key information throughout the game but the climatic moments are kinda lost because you knew all along and it's just confirming what you thought. They missed an opportunity to deliver something new after you thought you knew the whole story.All that said, small dev team delivers a game well worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Having previously been frustrated by time mechanics in games like The Talos Principle I was concerned when going in blind to this game that it might be a slog but it quickly grew on me and became a really fun sequential puzzler.Voice acting is decent, Aria especially is charming.I love E's chirps.The music suited very well and graphically it was genuinely impressive, not just because it was performant on my relatively old hardware (1080ti) but it is gorgeous!I can't recommend this enough to any fellow puzzle enjoyer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;Dr: Great game 8.5-9/10, rough around the edges but nowhere enough to affect how I feel about the game. Pick it up if you want a game that scratches the same itch as Portal or The Talos Principle. While the inspiration is obvious in both theme and the way the story is expressed, The Entropy Centre exceeds expectations of being just "another Portal like puzzler." The primary concept/gameplay mechanic explored in this game is incredibly unique, and adds a new, interesting layer to the puzzle box design. The mechanics are explored to a satisfying depth, and the increase in difficulty is steady, without any jarring jumps or unengaging lulls. There are some slight rough patches, primarily in regards to design language, with a couple puzzles being difficult to read due to being "busy" in design and having important features hidden or obscured, however this is something that can easily be overcome by the developers with further experience. The story is intrinsically tied to the primary mechanic, and while it's nothing to write home about with the entire plot (including "twist") able to be pieced together rather early with no real subversion of expectations, there are certain sequences that highlight the potential the developers have to tell a truly great story, in narrative, experience, and environment. I wish I had picked this game up earlier honestly, as it was a great experience, absolutely worth the cost of entry even at the original asking price of $20 upon writing this review. Genuinely, if you enjoy Portal, The Talos Principle, or any of the cerebral, puzzle box type of games, do yourself a favor and pick this game up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kind of a slog. While some puzzles are very well desinged, this is only true for about a fifth of them. most of them are either way too easy or the solution is very fiddly, causing you to spend considerably more time on the execution than figuring out the solution. Also oftentimes, due to the nature of the rewinding mechanic, you can softlock yourself in puzzle chambers, and you have to kill yourself to restart the puzzle.Adding to this is a frustrating saving system, that doesn't let you save manually and frequently restarts you 1 minute of walking away from the puzzle chamber. Also the puzzle quality drops dramatically towards the end. After a while I was only playing the game to see the story finished. Needless to say, i was disappointed as well. Despite taking so many influences from portal, that it could be considered plagiarism, the developer didn't seem to think story was one of the elements people liked about portal, because there barely is any. The Hook is alright and by the 3 act a big development happens that really makes you interested how the story will progress. This however is the highpoint of Entropy centre's Story, as there is literally NOTHING happening up until the end in act 15. And the ending is really the most unsatisfying opvious ending that could have possibly been chosen. The story is really nothing to write home about. Also a puzzle game doesn't need action sequences. Why the core gameplay is constantyl interrupted for mediocre action sequences is beyond me.TLDR: The game is basically a glorifed portal 2 mod. The story is bad, the new mechanic is interesting but fiddly and annoying, there are constant physics bugs that can completly screw your sollutions up, and for a puzzle game there are too many action and story sequences.  There are better portal 2 mods for free, this one is only for people who REALLY need another Portal-like game
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good game with puzzle design that immediately reminded me of Portal.  The puzzles were challenging enough without getting too difficult, and some of the mechanics were pretty cool.How the story would be playing out became pretty obvious fairly early on, but it wasn't bad and I enjoyed the banter between the characters.Overall a great game, and I would love to see additional content either DLC or community created.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, Cool story and Characters, Sadly though It can kind of start to feel a bit endless and repetitive after a while. Also (Spoilers) when you eventually get to the levels with the conveyors and jump pads the physics get really messy. I ended up checking videos after a while to see if i was doing the level correctly because physics kept breaking.  BUT overall id recommend the game, mainly for the story but also if you like lots of puzzles this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are good. The game has Janky platforming controls. It could've used some type of shortcut-unlocking to reduce the frustration of re-doing the sections that you already solved, but have to do again, due to falling off a platform at later sections of the puzzle.The visuals and writing are good, The music is average and felt repetitive during the "tense" sections.Overall, recommended for puzzle games enthusiasts
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game, some of the later puzzles can be broken (just 2 or 3) but besides that i gotta say this finally scratched the portal itch for me, and wonderfully so, i do hope the developer finishes the story because i kinda get what he was going for but still feels empty and that's not a good feeling to end your game with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: If you like portal or time travel stories play this game.  Puzzles have a great balance between easy, and satisfyingly difficult.  Lot's of fun easter eggs, and notes throughout the game hiding in every level.  Love the story.  The way the game works made it easy for the gameplay and story to interact nicely without distracting from the other.E.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very intriguing puzzle mechanics that build and build throughout the many acts of puzzles, however the story felt a bit lacking to me, and I was left unsatisfied by the end. The little bits of backstory and lore you pick up can sometimes be funny and interesting, but don't really resolve at the end of the story, and left me wanting a more fleshed out epilogue. Still the puzzles were good and tough, just wish there was less of "try again, oops screwed up one little thing in the sequence, try again, etc..."
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: It's no secret that this game is heavily inspired by Portal 2, but since that is one of my all-time favorite games, this ticks every box for me, and more. The puzzles are never *too* complicated, the story is incredibly captivating and the ending is insane. Although somewhat predictably, it feels really cool to unravel the story throughout the game as you start to realise what's really going on. All in all, this is one of my favorite games of 2022, and I can see myself replaying it multiple times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: It started off giving very strong Portal vibes, which the game obviously draws from. During the first hour I fully expected it to fall flat and just be remembered as a Portal Knockoff, however after completing the campaign I'm happy to say that I feel like the game stands on its own, thanks to solid storytelling and voice acting and interesting puzzles. The game ran approximately  9 hours for me, which is just about right I feel, because although the storytelling is great, the game did start to feel repetitive by the end.I'm giving The Entropy Centre a thumbs up: cool brain teaser with compelling storytelling
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A strange beast among puzzle games. They are a very specific type of games that usually seem to think that all the mental effort you have to put into playing them deserves an appropriate and immediate reward, that they are going out of their way to offer to you promptly, making you feel like a proper hero at the end and showering you with endless love and reverent affection for being so smart and doing your job so outstandingly. , though, is, oddly enough, a puzzle game with a grim and rather depressing story, there is no reward for saving the world to be had here, because there is literally no saving the world to be done in this game. The game also doesn’t care much about your ego and has no one singing you praises or cool songs (remember “Still Alive”?) at the end. Nevertheless, it seems to be very aware of the genre’s latest conventions and is telling said story with lots of charm, cuteness and lightheartedness, Portal-style (the many Steam reviews lovingly mentioning The Weighted Companion Cube eloquently attest to that), which only makes the carefully foreshadowed conclusion all the punchier.Furthermore, not only is the game aware of the genre’s conventions, but it plays expertly with them and isn’t afraid to tell you early on exactly how it will end, knowing perfectly well that you won’t believe it and will still push forward, ever confident in your resolve and happily transported by the vision of glory that’s already beginning to take form inside your head. “Yeah, sure, game, do your thing, raise the stakes all you want, I’m sure I’ll overcome everything you throw at me in the end.” Will you?... Well, I’d like to tell you how it all plays out, it would make a fine ending for this review, but it could be considered spoilers, and I’ve been recently reprimanded for writing spoilery reviews, so allow me to end it by saying that Aria Adams, ’s puzzle-solving protagonist might be the most deserving of a hug character I’ve ever encountered in a video game.
