_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a charming and funny game. While it at times reminds me of Portal, it definitely brings its own style of humor to the table.The puzzles stay rather simple for a while, and at first that worried me, but now I realize that the purpose of those simple levels is to acclimatize the player to the rather counter-intuitive approach to puzzle solving that the Entropy Centre asks of you. Fear not, the Entropy Centre *does* get more difficult later on, but it never becomes unapproachable. Never did I encounter a puzzle that made me confused as to where to even start. Solving the more challenging puzzles is very satisfying, and several mechanics are introduced throughout to spice things up.In terms of story, without spoilers, the Entropy Centre is intriguing and mind-bending at the best of times, and a bit silly at the worst. It's lowest points are never very low, and it's highest points had me shouting to my friend (who I was in a discord call with at the time). Rest assured, the ending of the Entropy Centre is well worth the journey (and its fun and charming writing style will keep you entertained along the way).There's only two real characters in the Entropy Centre, but they're both handled quite well. While the character you play as is a little shallow and generic feeling at first, she does get fleshed out later on. Your companion, meanwhile, starts off a little quirky and cold feeling, but she will quickly draw you in and make you invested in her.If you do decide to play the game, I encourage you to search out the optional readables. Some of them are hidden behind optional challenges, which can be quite fun to solve on their own, but the readables really add to the mystery and buildup of the story, and can make some revelations even more impactful. You don't need to exhaustively find every single one, but even just a few could make the whole experience stronger.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: After 8.7 hours of gameplay, I've finally finished The Entropy Center. A spiritual successor to the Portal series, The Entropy Center aims to give us that Portal 3 experience we so deeply desire. Not only does The Entropy Center fill my "Companion cube shaped hole", it does so much more, truly making it a game of its own. I'm astounded that it was put together by such a small team, and I look forwards to future releases from Stubby Games.  This game is one of the best I have ever player, competing with the likes of Portal 2 on my list of favorites. The Entropy Center builds on the mind bending puzzles of Portal, creates a realistic and believable atmosphere, and has an intricate story that truly makes you feel like part of another world.I've mentioned Portal too many times already in this review, but this game is NOT Portal, its a game that does the same thing with a different core mechanic. The Entropy Center swaps your portal gun for an entropy gun, completely changing the concept. The game does however, use many of the same concepts elsewhere, like with the cube, laser (thermal discouragement beams), and bridge cubes. These cubes all employ mechanics seen in Portal, but rather than using portals to change their locations, you must put them in their locations first then rewind them back to where you need them. This concept allows for many new kinds of puzzles where you bring one cube and then the other, or where you use two cubes together to bring them both over a gap, the game may take from Portal, but it also builds on the mechanics. The Entropy Center doesn't just learn from Portal, it also adds its own content with things like the tall cube. This is an example of entirely new concept that melds with the time rewinding mechanic of your gun, the tall cube doesn't have its position rewound, rather its sate, going from large to small. The tall cube isn't the only new idea, there are fans, conveyor belts, and transformers that are all completely original and innovative ideas, bringing the game away from being 'Portal 3', and closer to being 'The Entropy Center'. Although there is a clear inspiration behind The Entropy Center, it truly is a game on its own, not just a Portal replica.The Entropy Center successfully creates an interesting an believable atmosphere. The game knows what it is and how it does it. There are only a few titles within the video game industry that excel at keeping the player's disbelief at bay, my favorites being Bioshock and Metro Exodus, like those, nothing feels out of place in The Entropy Center. The are explanations behind everything, the computers containing lore-emails are all in offices (or whats left of them), the break rooms between puzzles, even the puzzles themselves have a purpose (something I struggle to find in the Portal series, "testing" what kind of excuse is that). The game doesn't just focus on what the puzzles are for, but also life outside of the puzzles, with the lore emails, and relaxation areas. Showing life outside of puzzle solving fleshes out the game's atmosphere and makes the player feel like they are in a functioning environment. A functioning environment tells a story, and answers many of the players questions about the world, creating a more realistic feel. The Entropy Center gives every object a purpose and creates a believable environment that I enjoyed exploring.The narrative in this game is controversial, though it moves incredibly slowly, it manages to keep the player somewhat captivates throughout the entire game. I was always looking for that next computer, searching for the next bit of lore I could find to flesh out the story all while solving puzzles. This captivation shows how good this game is at keeping the player enthralled in its story. The game doesn't have all that many story beats, I found this to be the biggest downside. The player has to keep looking for that next bit of hidden story to keep them engaged. If you aren't one to look around and would rather focus on gameplay, The Entropy Center might become a bit repetitive for you. This game is lacking in narrative beats considering its duration, but it you're willing to look, the game will keep you engaged start to end.Overall I found The Entropy Center to be one of the most enjoyable video games I have ever played. It's definitely on my favorites list. A must play for any Portal fan, or any video game fan for that matter.

I have anxiety when I have to jump on it. I wasted way too much time than necessary having to start over only because I did not hit teeny-tiny jumppad collider.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie I'd say this is simple math: If you like Portal, buy it. If you don't like Portal don't buy it. In all seriousness I already heard and read in advance that The Entropy Center will remind you on Portal, but after playing it I would say  like Portal, just with another gun mechanic: Level like game construction like Portal, similiar block mechanics and a companion who talks funny all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Center is a puzzle platformer in first person perspective, staring Aria and her rewind device Astra, as they try to prevent a cataclysmic event happening on earth, through the use of Entropy Energy generated from solving puzzles.The game is a bit Portal x Braid, as it has a somewhat dystopian setting with quirky chippy dialog as backdrop for the puzzles, puzzles which utilize a rewind feature. That means you have to essentially solve the puzzles backwards and work your way back to the beginning, which probably is also the theme of the games plot. Although when time parallels and time rewind mechanics are involved, you never know.The puzzles themselves aren't overly involved, and the game would rather push new and different puzzle cubes at you, but ever so seldom make you utilize multiple of them in a given chapter, at least not until towards the end. At the same time the difficulty of the puzzles doesn't really evolve either, despite new puzzle cubes being introduced, ultimately in the end it's about rewinding the cubes back to their respective triggers to open a door.There's a couple of segments throughout the game that involves dexterity, especially involving the conveyor belts, that the game could have been without. Similarly there are a couple of segments with simple puzzles that also has repeatedly spawning enemies that are just a nuisance and in the way of the puzzle element of the game.Overall a solid production for an indie title, although the environments does get a bit bland and repetitive. The music is fitting and dramatic at times,Technically the game could have been better, developers should have learnt by now that, if they intent on forcing film grain, motion blur, mouse acceleration (what year is this even?) and all other nonsense elements, that they at least make it possible to turn those off in the games settings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the puzzles, the story and the humor and changes of gameplay. This game is really well done, i have no complaints as of now but i didn't complete the game yet so if i notice anything bad i will update the review. So, this game reminds me a lot of portal but it doesn't feel like a knock-off or anything like that. It has it's own puzzles, characters and form of gameplay and scenery which i all really like. The puzzles feel fresh and i really like how the story is told. Some people have complained about performance but my game runs at over 144 fps on ultra and i only have a 3050ti. If you like puzzle games like portal, you will like this
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend? "Yes, but...".The world design is gorgeous, the puzzles and the story are good in general, but there's a point where the puzzles - rather than introducing new obstacles/elements, or making you feel excited about having mastered the mechanics to proceed faster - just become "same old, same old" tedious.OK, at this point you're probably 3/4 through the game and you might just want to hang on, to see how it ends, but it's just a shame, the game lacks a little bit of "breath", to make the whole game as interesting as the first half.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and interesting, the lore is not too deep, no need to look too much into it, and the ending is a bit underwhelming, I mean of course it's all very exciting in the moment but it's bittersweet.All in all I would definitely recommend this, it's fun, not too hard, challenging, funny at times, spectacular, a bit moving and the whole mystery can be very entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty well polished, runs great, but the puzzles just aren't very interesting. The puzzles deal with setting up puzzle pieces and then you can rewind them along the path that they moved. Easily half of the puzzles have essentially the same solution where you move the single puzzle piece from position to position, in reverse order, and then rewind that puzzle piece step by step as you use it to get through the puzzle. I kept waiting for some ability or puzzle piece to be introduced that makes the game interesting, but it never happened.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥, buy it, no questions askedThe Entropy Centre is a puzzle game where your main interaction with the world is by reversing objects in time. You play as Aria, a woman who wakes up in a science organization with little recollection (sound familiar?) and you are accompanied by Astra, the assistant in your gun-like tool that reverses time. Although it has little direct offensive capabilities, there is actual combat in the game, and some options open up to you with how you can fight back - the mainstay being reversing the enemy's projectiles in time and guiding them right back to them.If you think this game sounds like Portal, then you're somewhat right. There are story beats that feel right at home, some of the puzzle elements, the dry, witty banter between Aria and Astra, the Entropy Centre collapsing in a dilapidated state - but it has more than enough to stand on its own. Particularly, the lore and worldbuilding and how it ties into the current story is extremely fascinating, and I adored the ending.This game was made mostly by a solo developer, and with that in mind, the production quality is insane. This game barely has any bugs or glaring issues. It's not perfect, mind you, I found a few tiny things here and there - but by and large the game does an extremely good job of making sure that everything is as it should be. I brought a jump cube from a previous puzzle into the next puzzle and it got fizzled before I could bring it in - it was made sure that I couldn't cheat in any obvious way.Overall: great story, fun characters, nice music, mind-bending puzzles. Absolutely worth it
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Takes a lot of pages out of Portal 2's book, but I ain't mad at that. I enjoyed the story, the puzzle mechanics that got increasingly more challenging, the dopamine hit I got when I'd solve a real head-scratcher. If, like me, you've given up on there ever being a Portal 3, this will scratch the itch!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-nice art direction-decent characters-passable story (although predictable)Cons:-rewinding doesn't add to the puzzles. it only makes things unnecessarily confusing and convoluted-later puzzles are overly complex-making minor mistakes forces you to set up the entire solution again, which can take a few minutes
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Fun-to-solve puzzles with an intriguing story, quirky humor, impressive visuals and effects, great sound design, great music, and attractive lore scattered throughout the campaign. The only negatives are the clunky movement of your character, and I also have mixed feelings about the ending. Overall, it is worth getting if you are a lover of puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a decent experience, especially when considering the game has been done by a single person.It takes inspiration from portal, i personally find it a bit repetitive : the rewind gun seems like a fun idea in the first place, but it quickly feels like you are solving puzzle the same way.I would have put a neutral recommendation, not great but not bad either.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: To think that such a unsettling Story could be packaged into such an amazing Puzzle Game.The Entropy Centre is a game where you attempt to rewind a cataclysmic Event that happened on Earth by completing Puzzles in order to generate Entropy Energy.Throughout the game you will discover more and more and more about The Entropy Centre and it's employees by reading E-Mails on Computers that are scattered in the facility.Without spoiling, the ending isn't very surprising but also extremely messed up in it's own right.This game really draws a lot of inspiration from the Portal-Series in many areas like the abandoned Facility that apparently used to operate with "questionable ethics" or the AI-Companion that follows you wherever you go but the most important one is the excellent Puzzle-Design.The Puzzles in The Entropy Centre start of simple with just a couple buttons, pressure plates and cubes but quickly rise in complexity with new Puzzle-Elements varying problems to conquer. The puzzles can be solved pretty quickly but are never too simple or too difficult and feel very satisfying to get through.The game can be finished in about 10 hours which is a good length for a puzzle game and especially for this price.If you like Portal and Portal 2, you'll like this game as well
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: i just beat the game a few minutes ago. without spoiling anything i'd say i have a mixed opinion on this game. on one hand, it strongly (and i mean STRONGLY) reminds me of several game dev ideas ive had previously; but executed better than i was able to in my attempts...it truly is the game i tried to make on multiple occasions but failed. It also has a really gripping story, absolutely beautiful art direction, and mostly good gameplay...but thats when there are some problems. there were a few sequences that felt hair-rippingly difficult for no reason and out of place for a puzzle game which i feel could have been avoided entirely; and there are a couple puzzles where i admittedly had to exploit bugs to get past (though i am sure there was a more legit way, i couldnt find it.) in regards to bugs, there were a couple that also prevented further progress but the game fixed itself after quitting to the main menu and re-entering. its also extremely frustrating in a few places where i kept dying or otherwise failing and the checkpoints were sometimes pretty lousy, meaning i had to redo stuff i had already struggled through just to get back to where i died.Story wise, i was dissapointed at the end to find that i had already theorized correctly what it was going to be from a very early point in the game; though that does tend to happen with me because i am very good at inferring stuff from subtle clues. the final issue is that there was one story sequence in the game that kindof bothered me.. ive never been somebody who likes horror and it got a little too horror-esque for my comfort in one part, so new players should be cautious if they are sensitive to certain topics, such as .overall however, i still recommend this game simply because of my aforementioned point that it reminds me a lot of my own work. even if im a bit sad i didnt execute the idea first, im still glad it exists and sombody else made it happen in this case. i will certainly be making fan tributes in some form soon!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles are really great. The main issue is that a lot of time in some of the longer ones is just spent waiting for the cubes to rewind, and a couple solutions feel ... almost hacky? but they really do make you think and are very satisfying to complete.The "action" sections all go on too long, and dont work for me. they might be better if you could sprint, or if they had very generous checkpointing. I died a view times just because the game didnt give me enough time to figure out which way to go or it wasnt clear and had to replay a full minute of initial cutscene and then running, multiple times. You also cant sprint in these sections which takes some of the tension out. like the clock is running down, move faster lady.Very fun and satisfying puzzle game though adn well worth the price of admission. If you like Portal youll find a lot to like here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't really recommend this game. It is not a bad game, but it feels a little monotonous.There are many similar, more detailed and better written reviews than mine, but I just wanted to add mine.As a fan of portal I realize that the game is similar, but I also tried too look at it and review it without comparing the two games too much.TL;DR:+ it's own mechanic for puzzles,+ interesting story (although it may leave you a little disappointed),+ cool soundtrack and nice graphics,- becomes monotonous and the puzzles may feel repetitive,- the world feels empty, very little interaction with it and the game doesn't reward exploration,- little sense of achievement from solving the puzzles,Review:The game has it's positives: the game has great graphics, enjoyable soundtrack and it's portal like in some aspects (which we all know is why people are interested in it). It has it's own mechanic for puzzles which has great potential and (at least at first) is quite interesting.The story is interesting, but unusual for the game. You learn most of it from the dialogue which is interesting and fun to listen to but sometimes underwhelming. I can't really say that the plot is good because you might feel a little disappointed after you "beat" the game.  Nevertheless, the story was what kept me playing.The puzzles are fun at first when the concept of rewinding time is new and you get new toys, after that they get kind of repetitive and somewhat tiresome. You run around the room, figure out where are the boxes and how to get to the exit. Then figure out the order, reverse it (try not to ♥♥♥♥ up because then it becomes tedious) and go to the next puzzle. That's about it. Obviously there are some differences in every puzzle but the process is pretty much the same, so the puzzles soon become repetitive. Additionally, as I was playing through the game I slowly lost the sense of fulfilment/achievement after I solved the puzzles. It did not feel like I beat the puzzle/obstacle. It seemed like I just walked on the path prepared for me and figured out what steps I had to take to progress through the game.The game doesn't really reward exploration. You may find lore info on PC's but that's about it. Because of that I find the world a little lacking, at least compared to what it could be. The environment was interesting but it all felt empty and dead.At the early stages you can pick up some balls and throw them or rewind time on an apple, later in the game you may stumble upon a slideshow and scroll through it for some information, but that's about it. You can't pick up anything from the ground/tables/benches, however you can interact with vending machines to spit out some of it's content, but like with the rest of the stuff, you can't pick it up or interact with it.The environment and all of those things are pretty much the same thing throughout the game, no matter if you are in the offices, "outside" or under the facility.The content of the areas, how they are connected and how it would work as a facility in which people live and work does not make sense. There are elements that seem to be there just because they are needed for a puzzle, there is very little sense and no explanation as to why the area looks like it's "glued" together from elements of environment and offices (which are very often in strange places in a middle of a "puzzle").Overall the game draws you in with it's interesting concept, cool soundtrack and graphics, and maybe some similarity to portal, but after playing it for some time, it feels monotonous and leaves you a little disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: First up, it looks fantastic. I think it was developed by one person, so big props.Its WAY to easy tho, nearly every puzzle can be solved in 30 seconds and on the first try. The story is kinda predictable but still good. I would not recommend buying it for the full price, its just not worth it. If you want hard puzzles like portal, this is not the game for you. If you want the same feeling of story telling like in portal, then this is the game for you.Also, no easter eggs, so dont even search for any.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: So I normally don't write any reviews, which is actually a shame and I should start to write more, but this time I really wanted to write one.The Entropy Centre is a puzzle solving game inspired by Portal which is a really really great thing. Even though it is inspired by Portal it has it's  completely own charm and Story.The puzzles were very great, the time mechanic is really really thought out and is fun to use. Puzzle elements get introduced in a very easy to understand way. I never was really stuck in a puzzle, though this could also be because I already have experience in puzzle games and harder ones, but this doesn't mean that I didn't have fun solving the puzzles. It was a very relaxing experience and the story is really really great. I wanted to read all the terminal messages because of how funny and informative they were! The Game has a really great setting and throws some hints here and there for the player to make him/her think about the story.All in all I can really recommend this one for people looking for a game like portal, people who want to experience a nice puzzle game with a good story. PS: I love E.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another game that starts you off by letting you solve interesting puzzles, then forces you into a jump-and-shoot test of your speed, agility, and reflexes. After, of course, it is too late to return it. (No, we did not play for 48 hours. Some kind of bug in Steam had it keep the game open after there were no visible Steam windows on my Windows 11 desktop.)Buy this if you like running and jumping, not if you were looking for more Portal.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is incredible. It takes clear inspiration from Portal, but with higher stakes, more devious puzzles, and a slight bit less character development. I found it to have a lot of excitement and mystery, with an unsettling atmosphere and a bit of existential dread.Loading sections could have been masked a bit better as they often cause a stall in performance. I encountered a few bugs, annoying but all minor. Sometimes I'd die from rewinding a platform I was standing on. A few times I experienced an object falling through a lift platform. Twice my rewind effect got stuck on a non-existent/offscreen object and I couldn't continue without reloading. Overall quite respectable even with the minor glitches.If you're a fan of Portal, don't miss this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Portal you're gonna love this game.If you're experienced with puzzle games the puzzles themselves aren't very challenging (so far) but the characters and world building are great and I am really enjoying the story.I have one gripe though,  I don't know if this was intentional or an oversight but it's such a downer for me. The lack of sprinting option is annoying in most parts, and is absolutely critical at the more dramatic parts, when you're supposed to feel urgency and would probably run if you had the option, but instead just walk at a leisurely pace.This lack of sprinting was also my downfall at in the  which would've been much easier if I could just walk a little faster.Edit after completion: Towards the end of the game it got a bit boring, the puzzles don't get much harder it was never hard to figure out what I needed to do, it just became more tedious. All in all very nice game, could've been shorter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very nice and quite fresh throwback to the days of Portal. It has many references to it, some more subtle, others are not. If you've played Portal and/or Portal 2, you will definitely know your way in this one. It also involves manipulating object through time, just like in the game Singularity, which was one of my favorites... so it's not quite Portal, though. Don't think it is, because here you have to think with doing things in reverse natural order in time, instead of thinking with portals.Honestly, there really should be more games like this. Puzzles or not, I really love the concept.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like at first, but it improves a lot during the campaign. - brutalist architecture is amazing on this game- i thought that the robot companion was going to be annoying, but i ended up liking her.- the sci-fi plot is really cool and makes you think- combat/action sequences are just bad and frustrating. - it starts too easy- some puzzles are too long andd sometimes you already know the answer, but it takes too long to execute
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I came here to edit a review that I thought I'd written after my first playthrough two years ago - but I turns out I didn't write that oneIf I had, I would have overall recommended The Entropy Centre, alongside some stern words about how it was frustrating to get stuck after I'd discovered the solution to some of the later puzzles in the game because of the physics engine jank. It was particularly annoying because it dampened the narrative urgency that the story was trying to create.I don't know if it was me or the game that has changed, but on a second look it was a lot smoother than it was previously, though there were still the occasional incident.Regardless, at its worst it wasn't a dealbreaker for me - I really enjoyed the story and characters, and in particular the ending struck me as quite moving. The puzzles had some interesting ideas and I found it enjoyable to navigate the environments they were set in. Veterans of other puzzle games are unlikely to find the puzzles particularly challenging, so keep in mind what you're looking for. Overall - quite nice, worth a look
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I normally don't write game reviews so the fact I am speaks volumes.Where do I even start with this game? I absolutely loved playing this in terms of both gameplay and story.Gameplay was challenging, sometimes frustrating, but it felt soo good once you had an idea of the solution. I played through Portal 2 and the mechanics are similar enough to pick up, but still distinct to make you think through things in a different way. Also like Portal 2, there were sequences where the facility just started crumbling apart around you and you had to use it to your advantage or react in time to save your skin, which I really loved seeing in another game. Only issues I really had was that the physics would sometimes wonk out and mess me up, even if I had the exact right solution, and sometimes the entropy device took a few tries or some readjusting to actually be able to shoot what I was looking at.Story-wise, I fell hard for this. Normally, I get fed up with time-travel because of all the paradoxes and what-not, but the Entropy Center seems to take this into account not just in your main storyline, but in the worldbuilding done around the facility through the intel. Speaking of, I love the way the worldbuilding was executed. Majority comes from various emails and messages you'll find on computers around the facility, but you also run into presentations and whiteboards showing off the major plot for those that don't want to inspect every computer they come across. The emails though were very realistic so to speak, like you had some of people discussing their issues with work and going through crises over some of the consequences of that work and you also had a chain of people replying "Cat." to a serious work email involving a cat. Aside from that, once the story starting approaching the Big Reveal, it felt like a payoff. It wasn't exactly an obvious twist, but one you could logically come to given the mechanics of the game and it just felt like all the little unexplained pieces so far just clicked as you got up to it.Overall, new fave for me and if you like puzzle games or especially if you liked Portal 2, I highly recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I'd love to avoid comparisons to Portal because it's unfair on any game, so I only really use it here as a spoiler-free way of giving you an idea of exactly what you're in for.  It's incredibly close in experience to Portal 2.  Valve could have bought it up, rebranded, called it Portal 3, and no one would have questioned. Visually it holds up, aesthetically it's wonderful, the dynamic set pieces are jaw dropping, and it's a ton of fun.Obviously it is it's own thing, and I'm happy for that, the temptation to 3D print my own TIME GUN is rising rapidly.It's longer than expected, it's more gorgeous than expected, and I was far more invested than I expected too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I have a headcanon that the titular facility in this game is an alternate-universe counterpart to Aperture Science, in a world where they delved into time travel rather than portals. They're uncannily similar, right down to the overgrowth and destruction, backstage areas full of catwalks and conveyor belts, extensive integration of AI into their operations, and even a two-handed tool known as the "Handheld _____ Device" (Entropy Device in this case). It's so similar, and I love it.The puzzles can get a little stale early on since you can only do so much with "use box to open doors in reverse order, then rewind it while walking through doors in sequence," but it starts picking up a little ways in with new and interesting puzzle elements. Each of the (very short) chapters introduces a new element which is often then not seen in later chapters, which gives each chapter a unique feel but also feels like the moment you get used to a new element, another one is introduced and the previous one is cast aside. It keeps puzzles fairly fresh in the late game but also can feel a little overwhelming having to start from scratch with a new element every 5-ish puzzles.The writing is similarly witty to Portal as well, with an AI in your gun that occasionally converses with your character. The conversations vary in quality, but on the whole I like having the little voice in my weapon. The story, while simple, is also quite interesting and kept me going with wanting to find out how the overarching conflict will resolve.Definitely give this one a go if you've been craving more Portal-like puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratched the same itch that Portal 2 scratched. A worthy competitor in both story and gameplay mechanics without being too similar to the Portal franchise in story or gameplay.The puzzle mechanics are varied and interesting, with my only gripes being the solutions to the puzzles get quite samey by the end of it, and some of the tight, platforming jumps were genuinely frustrating at times. The story was *really* well done, though the game seemed to dump most of the story on you at once, rather than spreading it evenly throughout the game like Portal 2 did. Late game environments sent chills down my spine, and were some of the coolest environments I've every played in in a game.All in all, this was worth the money, and I'm more than happy to throw my wallet at any game that harkens back to one of the greatest games of all time (Portal 2). Thank you for making this devs! This was phenomenally well-done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished it yet, but so far:It's basically Portal 3. Don't get me wrong; It's definitely worse. The puzzles are much simpler, the connecting parts are very repetitive so far, and the story while intriguing is quite sparse (You *can* get some more extra story bits in computer logs)Despite all that, I love it.First off it looks great.Second of all the puzzles; while kinda simple are still quite clever. They give a lot of 'ooooh' moments which are fun. I also find it not as frustrating as a lot of puzzle games. So far, whenever I got stuck on some part, I would just exit the game and the next time I played would complete it instantly.Lastly, Your AI companion is super cute. It started off kind of stiff but I think 'she' gets way better the more you know her and interact with her.Anyway if you want Portal 3 this is a pretty safe choice IMO. Scratches very similar itches.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game when it was released, played until chapter 8 where I got stuck with the lockdown and some mobile, off-brand turrets (bots). My first thought when seeing the scenario was "not again". I just hate having to avoid missiles while trying to solve a puzzle. So I didn't bother trying to proceed. However, I liked the story, so now I started a new game as I'd like to see where it goes. Things are going better this time, and I have passed the part where I got stuck. Didn't even need a guide, just a bit of hide and seek to figure out where everything was. The puzzles are getting trickier, which is great, although I suspect I will be needing a guide soon. To summarize: like the story and puzzles, could do without the bots.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Liked: interesting concept for the puzzle to rewing time, good intro to new elements. Nice story and a bit of funny lore to discover, nice graphics, a few "action" scenes. Disappointing: too much walking in very repetitive rooms. At chapter 12, I still don't understand why garbage is lying everywhere... The puzzle difficulty is not very high or at least not increasing fast enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: theres potential for a good game here, but it feels like the developers just kinda ran out of ideas when making this game. in case you dont know, entropy center is a portal-esque puzzle game where youre given a device that rewinds time for dynamic objects the player interacts with. you can move a cube around and then rewind it in the path you moved it back to its starting location. now theres am IDEA for some interesting puzzles here, but the problem is that the developers just keep reusing the exact same puzzle over and over and over with it. its just "button 1 opens door 1, button 2 opens door 2. place cube on button 2, then button 1, walk through door 1, rewind cube back to button 2 and walk through door 2." thats it. thats literally every puzzle in the game. it just repetitive and predictable. it gets tiring after a while when youre presented with the exact same puzzle for every single level. the game also has a mechanic where if you press the R key youll delete an objects rewind data, and it was never used once. granted i only played through maybe half of the game before i gave up but still, i seriously doubt that mechanic can be used for anything other than a hindrance. the game also has a robot character in your entropy gun who talks to you throughout the course of the game. now theres a possibility here to have an interesting character dynamic between the main character and the AI and have insightful conversations and eventually form a bond with throughout the course of the game, but instead its just an annoying tagalong who explains new puzzle elements and spouts expositionnow to be fair, the game does have its positives. it has a pretty good story conveyed to the player through voice overs and email logs sprinkled throughout the game world. it has good voice acting, good environmental design... and thats pretty much it honestly. it just gets stale after a while
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet puzzle game that's probably 5-8 hours normally (ignore my padded numbers as I was idle a lot). Definitely scratches an itch if you're looking for a puzzles game. I had fun with it, the story is pretty decent if not a little predictable. Altogether it mostly felt worth my money and time though hopefully some patches will make it even better. Biggest complaints I hope they fix to make it truly great: Save points are arbitrarily weird and some deaths require a lot of back tracking and seeking out intel multiple times. Pair this with the amount of times I got stuck randomly or the game crashed and this feels mildly frustrating. Intel tracking seems straight up broken. I observed it incrementing incorrectly multiple times in a repeatable way due to deaths resetting their progress. Don't bother with that one achievement hunters unless there's patch mentioning a fix.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A very good "Portal" clone with interesting puzzles based around time manipulation. The game is thoroughly enjoyable and the story was really engaging and made me want to find out what was going on.The only negative point worth mentioning is that movement, especially jumping, could feel a bit janky at times, but it wasn't too often or bad.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I finished my first play-through, and boy is the story worth it. While the game unfolded it kept me wondering what was going on until the very end and even then I had questions to ponder over. The graphics are beautiful and the sound effects are well placed, the puzzles you complete are really intricately made and very well put together, the dialogue is humorous and works well, and finally every time you think you break it or get around something, it rewards you by making you feeling smart when you actually find something that was intended for you to find. My only criticism of it is just simply a result of how small the team was that made it, which is that your path forward feels too convenient for it's setting, and that exploration and incentive to look around isn't rewarded often. It feels very linear, one way, and generally with a set cut out path in most areas. It's small world building stuff but the game play is still challenging and fun. Overall to sum it up quickly, it feels inspired by Portal with the puzzle aspects, and navigating it is like going through Portal without a portal gun, but instead a time reversal gun. It's a really interesting way of navigating puzzles and I had a lot of fun unraveling all of them. Definitely worth buying for the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Entropy centre is a  first-person puzzle game where you are a survivor who has to work their way through puzzles made by an artificial intelligence using just your mind and a gun which can rewind objects back in time. Graphics- GoodSoundtrack- DescentAudience- TeenagersDifficulty- Decent difficultyStory- descent storyGame time- good lengthPrice- Its not too expensive, but it's always on sale7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing puzzle game worth every dollar. The story is engaging, the way the world works is interesting, and the puzzles are even better. The way you have to think in reverse at all times is a really fun challenge, and while I wouldn't say any of the puzzles really fried my brain or anything, every one of them was fun and gratifying to solve. If your a fan of Portal or games like it, this is a great one to pick up. I genuinely hope the dev makes DLC or updates with steam workshop support, I would jump at the opportunity to solve more of these puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Decent puzzle game with flawsIt runs flawlessly on steam deck The story is captivating at first but fizzles quickly. The initial few hours are story heavy and then about halfway through the game the story just kinda disappears and you're left solving puzzles in silence I found the puzzles to be moderately challenging but the ones that required precision platforming were more frustrating then fun Certainly worth a play for portal-esque type game fans but tempter your expectations. Entropy Center reminded me a lot of The Turing Test, a game I found to be a much more engaging portal type experience
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game with some real brainsqueezing puzzles. Very satisfying to get through, but I wish the pacing of the story was better. It kinda comes in big lumps aside from the terminal hunting, and it would have been a nice reward after each puzzle to have a little bit of dialogue and background story. Instead you can complete several puzzles without any story whatsoever and suddenly you get a whole blob of it in one go. Which is frustrating when the story is so good too...Still, that is the only minor fault I cound find in the game, the rest is brilliant!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal. Would go back in time to play it all over again (wink wink). Puzzles are well made and depending of the difficulty, shouldn't take you too long to figure out. The story is incredibly interesting with all the logs scattered around the game, and Astra is a really fun companion to have. My favorite game has always been Portal 2, and i can say with certainty that this is a very close second.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: While it is a shameless rip-off of Portal in almost every way, it's still a lot of fun and has it's own, slightly friendlier vibe compared to Portal. And since the replay value of puzzle games is somewhat limited, fans of portal will probably be happy to find a little bit "more of the same".It's an easy recommendation for anyone who likes Portal, and anyone who wants to see just how far you can take copying almost every single idea from another game. If you have no shame.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is . The writing (and voice acting) is very well done. The core game mechanic is well thought-out and has some surprisingly complex effects; while there's only a handful of basic puzzle elements, the developers made excellent use of them, especially in the latter half of the game. Strongly recommended, especially if you enjoyed Portal.If you're thinking "this looks like another Portal knockoff", you're not exactly wrong; it borrows heavily from Portal:- You wake up to a robotic-sounding man telling you it's time to do puzzles- Nobody else is around and it is obvious that it's been that way for *years*- So the facility is completely falling apart- Sci-fi gun with magical powers- A talking AI who provides commentary and whose primary goal is to get you to solve puzzles- About 95% of the puzzles involve dropping cubes onto floor buttons to unlock doors- Floor plates that throw you through the air- "Hard Light" bridges that you can walk on- Laser walls that destroy carried objects and reset the effects of your gun- Dark tones in much of the humor- Killer robotsAdditionally, the eponymous Entropy Centre was clearly designed by the same architect responsible for The Oldest House ().  The devs did a really great job with that, actually.However, while there's a long list of  that were borrowed from Portal, this game definitely adds its own twist to each.The "Entropy Gun" that you receive at the start of the game has the ability to "rewind time" for objects.  This basically grants you a limited ability to move objects without directly touching them.As a result, while Portal would have (say) 3 floor buttons and you had to figure out how to get your hands on 3 cubes, The Entropy Centre will give you 3 floor buttons and 1 cube, and you'd have to manipulate that one cube to hit the 3 buttons in the right order to let you clear the puzzle.The first third or so the game is relatively boring, because the only two elements you have to work with are ordinary boxes and portable springboards, so each puzzle boils down to "okay, in which order do I need to press these floor buttons? okay, drop the box on those buttons in reverse" so you can ride the lift/pass through the door/whatever to get to the end.However, the game eventually introduces more complex mechanics, and that's when things get really interesting.  The latter third of the game starts to get quite challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really not sure what I was expecting from this game when I started it, aside from puzzles, I mean, kind of the selling point, but I still somehow got more than I was expecting. To get it out of the way,  Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal Portal PORTAL. That's a selling point for me on games like this, but this game honestly feels like more of a cross between not just Portal, but the Turing Test as well, and manages to do things arguably better than both of them; in terms of narrative, at least. Doing these tests have a clear cut purpose. You're not just trying to escape or survive while being vaguely led on by a disembodied computer voice, you have an objective, and even though you're working out what happened at the Entropy Centre with context clues and long forgotten emails, you have a goal, and it's pretty interesting one at that.That out of the way, it's not a Portal clone. Puzzles in a room isn't a Portal exclusive idea, and because of the narrative behind the game it never feels like I'm playing Portal. It always feels like I'm playing the Entropy Centre, despite me constantly referring to things by Portal names, like Fizzlers and Faith Plates. Point is, it's not worth writing off as another Portal clone, it's doing its own thing. There's clear inspirations from it, but doesn't feel like it needs to fall back on familiarity to get people invested.The puzzles themselves never felt overwhelmingly difficult, even when Astra stated that the next few courses would be, or when an email said that the upcoming test was SUPER HARD, I ended up completing most of them in under 5 minutes, and there are monitors that'll tell you how fast you completed each test after completion. Weird way to help me keep up the pace, but it worked. Each course consisted of about 5 tests, and each course introduced some new test element. There are a lot of them, but the main ones are the different cube types, which never really felt overwhelming.Aside from that, the Entropy Device is a really interesting gimmick to get behind. Rewinding things opens the door for a lot of critical thinking, and once you figure out not only how to solve each test, but the order you need to solve it in so rewinding works, it's super enjoyable. A few small cons, though. The physics is a bit jank. I found myself having issues going from a conveyor belt to a jump cube in one test despite following the guidelines on the floor, and aiming a jump so you land on the jump cube can be difficult at times, and frustrating if it's like, step 5 in your rewind so you need to redo your steps so they rewind properly. The last con is that some test elements blend in with the environment too much, namely the launchpads, catapults, Aerial Faith Plates, whatever you want to call them. They're floor colored. It took me 30 minutes to complete a test chamber because I couldn't see one of the Faith Plates huddled in a corner because it was floor colored.Aside from those things, good game. Not worth sleeping on if you like puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good portal-type puzzler game. The puzzles were pretty good, the atmosphere was well-executed, and the writing kept me interested enough. While it's a pretty fun game, it's still not as good as Portal 2, although I'd say it's about 80-85% as good. Considering Portal 2 is often regarded as the best puzzle game of all time, I'd say that's pretty high praise, and definitely a worthwhile game to play for those who have had their fill of Valve's masterpiece but want to experience more things like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: An unpolished game that doesn't trust you to be smart enough to play it.Every puzzle is introduced with a tutorial explaining what it is and how to solve it. No thought requiredAny deviation to that is not allowed, even to the extent where it will introduce mechanics and teach you them, just to remove them later if they would allow you to solve a puzzle in a way they don't want. For example, early on you are taught you can launch objects. Later, when you need to get an object through a barrier the you are not longer able to launch objects over it, seemingly for no reason.Voice acting is very good, but there's so much clipping in the environmental objects that it becomes distractingA game that looks the part, but folds under close inspection
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game, but after finishing it, I'm just disappointed. Perhaps the sunk cost fallacy entropy is the real entropy after all.It is very similar game to portal, but without the extreme polish that comes from a major studio release (though they did release on schedule, not on valve time)I really liked the environment design, some areas are gorgeous. The theming of everything is spot on, and I enjoyed the voice acting. The characters dialogue could be a shade dense at times. There's a point where something obvious is written on a wall and your character reads it then says "What could it mean?".You have essentially 3 puzzle elements. Cubes which press buttons/Cubes which press buttons and also provide additional movement options.Buttons which come in either the pressure plate variety that the player can stand on or place a cube on, or the laser "button" which are activated by the laser cube or static lasers in the environment.Jump cubes can be a little irritating to land on at times. You can hit the edge and stop dead, requiring the whole solution to be rebuilt.Minor irritations:I don't like the lack of a crouch button. I see why it was excluded (so you cant go in the bot/cube holes but it doesn't make sense in the fiction.I'm not keen that your character is water soluble, sometimes going ankle deep with instantly kill you. Some of the checkpoints are a bit distant too, requiring several minutes of puzzle to be completed again because you slipped when exploring.I don't know if I'm jaded by playing a lot of this type of game, but I did find the puzzles to be extremely repetitive. There are several puzzles which require the same actions in the same order, but the layout is different. Same solution though.All puzzles are solved using the exact same formula: by placing all cubes where you need them last, then where you need them second to last, etc then rewinding them as required. Most puzzles I solved in 2-3 minutes, except the really long ones. A couple made me think, but not enough of the 50-ish this game contains.I also found that the middle part of the game was really tedious because of this. Mid game high level detail, not really a spoiler:Late game continuation spoilers:Ending spoilers:All considered, I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed. I probably would have been happier overall if I'd never bought this game, or at least stopped about a third of the way in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game is trying really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard to be portal. And man is it close, but in playing this game you see how much of Valve's game design and general quality comes down to polish. And holy jesus ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ christ, does this game lack polish. This game is a 7 or 8 out of 10, that would be a perfect 10 if only they could put some time into it.

_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, just often boring.I am at the end of act 6 and so far there've benn 5 boring puzzles for every intertesting one.I am afraid the core mechanic seems to have only very limited design space.I'd rather play a much shorter game with only the interesting/new puzzles, since every puzzle is work, insofar that every puzzle requires some amount of backtracing.Beautiful story and especially sound design though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are relatively trivial, at least up to the 6th act (over 15?). As time puzzle go, Braid was way better. And as for the genre, Portal was more interesting.The main  letdown is that every puzzle feels exactly the same. Even trying to access the out-of-the-box areas is way too easy and doesn't really happen often. The only difficulty one may find is the inaccurate physics/collisions that may force you to redo a setup and move a piece a few centimeters away because a jump made you stick on a wall or something. It's not something that I find enjoyable.I don't plan wasting more time on this anytime soon but it still may be nice for new players.It's not bad, but I wouldn't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing!TL;DRIf this game is on sale, buy it immediately!if you really like Portal, buy it immediately!So good, i couldnt stop playing, finished the whole game in one sitting in about 9 hours.Im not done, since im still missing 4 achievements, so if youre going for 100% id guess this game offers up to around 10 hours of gameplay, depending on how smart you are :')  Some things that kind of bugged me while playing:some issues with shaders/effects overlapping, e.g. when a laser is drawn on top of outerspace, it gets distorted, making the entire laserbeam look jagged in some places. the maps have some minor issues, e.g. in the staff area, theres a hole in the wall next to a pile of rubble, where you can quite easily look out of boundsApart form these smaller issues i have, i still recommend this game. it definetely has that portal feeling to it, but it doesnt feel copied at any point. all the puzzles are very much solvable without a guide, yet still make you use your noggin (i DID have to look up 1 puzzle tho=P.S. -1000000 points for not being able to crouchlol
