_childDocuments_.review: While this game is HEAVILY inspired/a copy of portal without portals, I still think this game can be overhated. There's plenty of reused things from portal they copied over here, but that doesn't make this game inherently bad. The puzzles are well thought out, and the overall feel of the game is fun to play. Just because this game ripped assets from portal, doesn't make it a bad one. There's a few things I don't like such as how the throw mechanic is introduced early but you can't use it until way later in the game, and I wish instead of reusing portal objects in their own name they'd stick with more original things to use, though, it doesn't take away much from the experience. I'd say to buy this game once it's on sale, It's got hours worth of gameplay, and a good story to boot. It's 100% overhated for being classed as a portal copy, even if it reuses assets.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, enjoyed it a lot.If judging it as a standalone game (not comparing it to Portal. or similar experiences), it's really cool, not sure how much time or money it took to develop it, but it's a solid 8-9 hours for one play through.Puzzles are enjoyable, although maybe racking up in difficulty a bit too slow, since you really start to turn gears in your head more in about last third of the game. The variety of mechanics for puzzles was really appreciated and it didn't feel stale, with few somewhat original ideas (at least for me, but I didn't personally play a lot of puzzle games).Story is fine, nothing too exciting, but I guess enough to justify the stuff happening in the game, although I didn't like ending too much, it was sort of underwhelming and predictable, and didn't really lead to anything.Visuals are great in quality, but a bit lacking in visual style and design I'd say, and seems to be all over the places on some occasions.If comparing it to Portal, I'd say it'd still hold up pretty good, but I feel like level storytelling, as well as narrative through visual design in general is lackluster. Almost everything has this overgrown post-apocalyptic look to it, as if it was untouched for hundreds of years, and it stays like that through whole game, with very little changes and mix-ups (the most notably probably being )On technical side, had 1 crash and 1 game freeze (when I was switching windows) through whole playthrough so I'd say it's stable.On R5 5600X, RX 6900XT, 16 GB of 3200MHz RAM and PCIe gen 4 SSD, game was running good, in 1440p had 120FPS locked on Ultra settings everything, only there were couple of stutters every time there was (I assume) level streaming, especially in the very beginning of the game, before any loading screens, but it wasn't anything game-breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Good game!(Though landing on the jump boxes from a high spot has been a pain like 90% of the tries)(Really, you finally have the solution of the puzzle, execute it, and then yo have to repeat because your invisible feet didn't touch the damn box for less than a meter)(By the way, what worked for me was to aim (totally) down while falling and make the circle at the center of the screen to "touch" the box)(And still managed to miss a couple of times)
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Entropy Centre was an enjoyable experience to play through, for the most part. The things that really sold me on the concept was the idea of temporal puzzle solving, and clear portal inspiration. However, Portal this isn't...The puzzles, as mention by other reviewers, are generally all samey and quite simple; Not really taking full advantage of most puzzle elements (Which might be a benefit for the god awful water physics). Say for some of the later puzzles, they really just equate to doing the solution in reverse to solve it. Also, for me at least, I found most of the puzzle rooms unintuitive as puzzle elements like cubes and the springboards were usually hard to spot among the scenery (More so the springboards, as a faffed about in a room until I eventually notice a springboard a couple minutes in my confusion).Physics were janky at worse (Water physics were awful), but still worked. Those 'combat' encounters were too frequent and tedious And those sudden deaths thanks to rewinding structures and objects awkwardly were infuriating.However, aside from that I found the story interesting, the environment and music great, and the whole entropy gun the best part of the game. If you can power through some low points, its a definite recommend but for the others just play the demo and see if you like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game does enough to differentiate itself from Portal in concept, yet it provides the feeling of a "sequel in spirit".The story is compelling enough and the puzzles in the later levels left me scratching my head.My only complaint is that I can't play it for too much more than an hour without feeling motion sick.EDIT: I'm pretty sure that the motion sickness came from either the FOV setting or the first hour of the game. Either way it wasn't a problem for most of my playthrough. Although the game feels story-light and repetitive from the halfway point to near the end, I still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: An okay game. Visually feels like an asset flip with the same bush and vine copy pasted a million times. Portal and it's followers had a feeling of starting in a clean research center and later breaking into a backstage with creepy corridors. Here you start in a backstage, killing the vibe of breaking the rules and exploring something you shouldn't. Base mechanic is boring - it's not about actual time rewind - it's about rewinding certain objects on their path... until it's not. 90% of the puzzle rooms are: place the box on plates in reverse order, then fire your gun. Puzzles are extremely, like 1 y.o. toddler level easy - every new room takes you 15 seconds to figure out which cubes do you have, then 15 seconds to solve the puzzle in your mind, and another 3 minutes to actually do it because the rewind function is so slow, The gun really needs an option to hold another button to speed up the process to at least x3 speed. Also after the introduction of bridge cube you can skip about 70% of the remaining puzzles just by placing it on some slope and building yourself a staircase to the exit. And I'm not like a speedrunner or bug hunter, these game breaking moments are obvious and so easy to do. This is just bad level design. And for some reason there are so much action sequences which are, again, boring and slow.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is a great first person puzzle game that involves spacial and temporal awareness, lateral thinking, and a lot of logic. It is right there on the sweet spot of games I like most, such as Portal 2, The Talos Principle, QUBE 2, etc. But ultimately, it lacked some polish and playtesting that would have placed it in the same category as those. This review might contain some small spoilers, but anything significant will be spoiler-tagged.: The gameplay is fluid and easy to get, and the controls are intuitive, and everything runs smoothly. I did miss a crouch feature, but that's mainly from me being used to it. The jump specifically felt rather short (I can't get on top of regular cubes, for example), but that might've been due to puzzle limitations. One thing that severely bothered me, however, was how often I'd get stuck on weird geometry, or how some boxes would clip through platforms, etc. Some more intensive work on playtesting would've been nice on that front, especially in areas where I could get physically stuck, or have a difficult time moving around in. I have also managed to very trivially access some areas the game clearly didn't want me getting close to, such as dead end corridors and little crevices in natural landscape. One other thing that became apparent as the game progressed was how often the game would use broken catwalks for navigation, to the point where any time the room would shake, I'd immediately go scavenge-hunting for the next catwalk to rewind.: On the visuals side of the game, everything looked spectacular! Given the small team and budget, the game looks very polished and well thought out, with high quality assets and interesting level geometry and decoration. Some assets could have used some subtle texture variation, just so they wouldn't look so obviously copy-pasted (like all the lockers in the game being labeled "C4"). The early areas of the game look very believable and lived in, but as you progress through the campaign, you start to see more places where the visuals and level design were cut short. Near the end of the game, there were several, easily accessible offices (so not those far away ones you can barely see) that were completely empty, just a box with lights on the ceiling. There were also bizarre choices for prop placements at times, such as having those bulky tube monitors with logs sitting on top of a very modern flatscreen control panel (with a perfectly good office desk nearby where it could've been). Some puzzles had very, very extreme lighting and fog, to the point where everything looked white and opaque and difficult to comprehend and navigate.: The puzzles were amazing! Many of them had me thinking and planning for several minutes at a time, and the puzzle elements were very inventive! I especially like the departure from Portal 2 in that puzzle elements are primarily attached to puzzles, which meshes really well with the game's mechanic. Unlike in Portal 2, where you bend space to access fixed elements, in here you bend time to access mobile elements. Brilliant! Most of the puzzles were also very logical and easy to execute. As a puzzle designer and level designer myself, however, the main issue I had was readability. The early puzzles were fine in that regard, but late puzzles had the exit tucked away in hidden corners, had (mild spoiler for a late puzzle element) completely invisible in the equally grayscale floor surrounded by foliage, and later yet puzzles completely forewent having tracks for moving platforms to ride on (they would just float from point A to point B, clipping through anything in the path). Another major gripe for me was the time limit in the gun's time recording ability. A lot of puzzles - especially the late ones - involved a lot of steps, and having only 38.1 seconds at our disposal meant that, in some puzzles, I had to be extremely efficient with how I handled objects. I'd reset them at the start of their path, then make the most straightforward and linear moves towards their next destination, and would rewind them to correct for any idling in-between. And even then, in one particular puzzle, I had to solve it all over again twice because, despite all the optimization in timing, I still lost time!: This is where I'll probably disagree with most players. I'm already pretty accustomed to first person puzzle games, so the game was probably overall significantly easier for me than it was for most players. Especially up to chapter 6, I genuinely felt like I was solving the same puzzle over and over, with some very small variations. Once you inherently understand the way the time mechanic works, you can easily figure out those puzzles by playing them in reverse in your head. And since most of them are just about the order of execution, then the challenge became less about finding the catch and more about memorizing the actions you gotta do. I wish there were more elements like (mild spoiler for a late puzzle element). The late late puzzles, especially past chapter 10, significantly improved the challenge of the puzzles, and some of them really had me stumped for a while, but still, some of them just felt like "advanced" versions of the early puzzles, in that it was easy to solve but difficult to execute. I was also not very fond of the (mild story spoiler for late game) sections, as I felt like they completely detracted from puzzle solving and didn't fit the gameplay style at all.: I will be frank, the story isn't the strong suit of this game. It's an interesting premise, and has some compelling characters, but it overall wasn't too inventive or captivating. There wasn't much of a deeper meaning, or theme to explore, outside of the superficial ramifications of the setting itself. But, in all honesty, that didn't matter too much to me, since the story didn't really seem to be intended to be the main focus, but rather served as a platform to keep the game going and to justify the puzzles. I encountered several seeming loopholes and contradictions in the narrative - but I guess that's what happens when time travel shenanigans are involved - and at times it felt like the game tried to overexplain some details to its detriment (for example, when one email chain tried to explain déjà-vus with technobabble, when it could've given it an air of mystery and given more room for the player's imagination to fill in the blanks). But by far, the thing that bothered me the most was the way that reading emails and logs didn't really mean anything in the game. It just served as a "collectible" of sort, and while it did provide some funny jokes and gags, the exposition it gave didn't really seem to influence the gameplay. For example, prior to getting the entropy gun, I read an email that described it (even explaining what the "PEA" acronym meant). But when I did get the gun, my player character still questioned it like I hadn't literally just read about it less than a minute prior. I also wished that more of the story was told via audio logs, paper logs or just environmental storytelling. I don't want to just read about The Entropy Centre, show me more about it! Immerse me in the story!In summary, my rating for this game would be a 7.5/10. Solid puzzle game, really enjoyable for the most part, and excellent overall production quality! Could have used some more playtesting and feedback. I would really like to be able to make puzzles for it myself, there is a lot of untapped potential here! I still recommend this game because, despite the nitpicks and issues, it's still a very enjoyable, very fun puzzling experience. If you can, buy it on a sale. Lengthier review:

_childDocuments_.review: Overall It's really good, however;The game never gets 'hard' it's always pretty straight forward to get to the solutions of the puzzles, so much so that the first third of the game were an absolute chore to play because of how easy and repetitive the puzzles were.I'm not that keen on a voiced protagonist, she doesn't add much besides trying to put thoughts and feelings into your head...it's a show don't tell kinda thing.Finally the ending is nice, if predictable but the lack of agency in the outcome is disappointing even if that is half the point8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I was going to like this game at first honestly. Decent graphics, solid easy to understand mechanics and concept, and and somewhat interesting plot. And for a while it went pretty smoothly.But then the game makes the same exact mistake that every other game attempting to rip off portal does: It doesn't know when to STOP. There is no getting around the fact that if you keep trying to pad out the gameplay too long the puzzles get repetitive, then boring, then outright frustrating. I've only gotten through level 7 so far, I'm sick of the puzzles now and I want the plot to make some bloody progress...and apparently this isn't even the halfway point for the game.And while the narrative isn't bad... we've all seen this kind of writing before. Sci-fi that messes with time loops and attempts to "think outside the box, you know like every other sci-fi puzzle game" and in doing so does exactly what you expect it to do as a result, with pretty predictable plot twists, etc.I don't want to keep playing anymore. That's the review.

_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I have never been so wrong about a game before in my life. I was reluctant to buy what appeared to be a Portal copy with cheesy smiling robots. And for the first two hours of gameplay, that's what it seemed to be, just a literal attempt to copy the opening of Portal 2 with ugly lighting, walls that looked prefabbed from the level editor, jumps that were easy to miss, bad checkpoints, and the same puzzle over and over....But then I got to chapter 4. I don't want to spoil anything. But nearly everything after that point was excellent. Gameplay. Story. Visuals. Length. No bad language anywhere. Only I wish you could interact with a few more objects.If it weren't for the opening chapters, I would give this game a perfect 10/10 score. This is the best puzzle-platformer that I have ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game, I feel.. mixed about positive or negative review. Game looks and runs great on PC. But from the beginning I expected the game to be more "open world" puzzles, not like Portal and test rooms.  By that I mean it felt like lab (and yes, story explains why..) but  enviromental puzzles would be great. Also got bad feeling when 3/4 of the game and yet another game mechanic is introduced and started to feel overwhelmed. Or that the game is puzzle after puzzle with little breathing room. More story breaks or shortening puzzle chapters would be enough (since last chapter and charging entropy energy to 100% felt neverending) On the other hand, characters were great, voice acting same and I would love to see sequel (even tho review seems to be negative).

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, look... I really like the general setting of the game and the core concept as well. But solving puzzles in this game feels like doing chores. _childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this type of game, its like the people said, the game is Portal puzzle-like but without the portal and you're trying to messing with time here, the idea is not that new but its certainly delight to see this idea was executed well and feels fresh, certainly worth the time and price if you like Portal!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice puzzle game in the veins of Portal/Portal 2. The difficulty is significantly higher than in both Portal games, at least starting from Act 7 (out of ~15).You will be rewinding objects in time, in order to reach the exit from each room. These objects all have other properties that provide many combinations.There are occasional glitches which may ruin something that should have been a valid solution, but most of the time, it works very well.From time to time, there is an action / combat interlude, but these are not too difficult or scary, just require you to think on your feet.The humor is different from Portal's, but still very enjoyable, at least on first play.Seems it will take about 10-15 hours to complete (progress has slowed for me now in Act 11, after 7 hours), which is a solid length for a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my most anticipated games of 2022 after seeing it in the Playstation Showcase in June. It looked like it had the spirit of Portal with an abandoned facility, mysterious premise and cute robots. I enjoyed the Demo and decided to get the full game on release date. I enjoyed the whole experience, I would often smile at some of the writing and loved Astra the robot companion. The mechanic of rewind objects is a very cool concept and gives me vibes of the FStop footage from the scrapped sequel of Portal that would eventually become Portal 2. The presentation was very good and was well optimized from the Demo. The Demo had severe lag spikes when loading different puzzle rooms and that was rectified in the final game. I only had a few bugs, nothing game breaking, but sometimes cubes would clip or I would get stuck, but perfectly playable. The puzzles are challenging sometimes, but nothing stumped me. It’s a lot of cubes which is to be expected since you need to rewind an object. There are a lot of systems you would expect and are slowly introduced and there’s always something to look forward to. I normally get disappointed by the story in these games, but I was pleasantly surprised. The reveals while exploring the facility are exciting and made solving the puzzles have a definitive end goal. The final nail was that this was written and developed by one guy. This blew me away cause this is a content rich indie game that feels high quality and provided me with 10 hours of gameplay for only $20. I would recommend this to any Portal fan and puzzle fan it was quite the treat.Edit: I forgot to mention, but the music was fantastic. Please put it on Spotify!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: At about 10 hours I've just about finished my experience with the Entropy Centre. I've found the journey pleasant but now I have reached the point where I just want to wrap things up. I've reached my patience level with the main mechanics and feel as though the difficulty curve only goes up after you get about halfway through the game, and then remains up. That itself is fine but makes my play sessions shorter and shorter.-The puzzles as a whole are very clever and use lots of creative tools to jostle your brain into thinking about reverse engineering every aspect. -The dialogue between Aria & Astra can be cringe and feels outdated. But it's limited and some charming moments occur. I guess I prefer a silent protagonist.-Great environmental design and I wish I could explore more of the visible areas around the 'office.' -I've enjoyed reading the messages left behind on the computer terminals.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed with this game, to put it lightly. I won't mention other games made by the owners of Steam because it's already been said, but even people I streamed this game to made the comparison off-hand. It's rather blatant at times; one or two superficial similarities (like a science-based setting where you complete puzzles for some end there) is fine. The overlap is when it becomes eyebrow-raising.The gameplay itself is fine but it's got the problem some object-based puzzle games do where if you mess up even ONE step, you have to start the whole thing over. Even if it's an error that's not your fault like the physics glitching out (Objects moving on conveyors). The glitching didn't happen too often, and if you're not opposed to this aspect of object-based puzzlers you'll be fine.The most disappointing aspect is the story, lore, and message. First, the message is forced and silly, frankly. And it wouldn't be so bad if the story wasn't pointless. But it is. You can guess fairly early on what's happening, the game reinforces it, and the lore you have to go out of your way to find leads to the said forced message. It's frustrating because they put so much effort into voice-acting and everything, and there's a point where there's obviously meant to be some sort of, like, emotional connection or understanding. But I just felt nothing. Basically, if you want rewind-based puzzles, go for it. I'd even say it might be worth $20! But no matter what, I'm just disappointed with what the game gave me versus the potential it had with such a story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent portal-style game. The dialogue is cheeky, the puzzles are nice and tight, and the adventure is definitely worth it. The game's main mechanic is a rewind mechanic that can rewind the path of an object. It is important to note that it does not take account the time it took to travel that path. If you have played games like The Talos Principle or Hourglass, this subtle difference is a huge departure of the rewind gimmick. Now your planning does not rely on waiting, but creating the correct path to solve a puzzle. There are a few other subtleties that make this rewind mechanic super dynamic, but I won't spoil them here. The game adds many mechanics to it, and I mean many, such as time gates or jump cubes (basically portable springs), which all add a new level of complexity to the puzzles. There is one level early on where you have to figure out how to bring 2 jump cubes 2 floors up, but your only way to move upwards is with the jump cubes. It's an interesting problem with an even more interesting solution. That is just one example of the many different clever puzzles that are in this game. At about an hour and a half, I reached Act 5, and I was worried the game was going to be way too short. The rest of the game took about 6 extra hours, so it wasn't actually a problem. The levels get far more complex once you reach Act 6 and onward. At this point, the game trusts you understand how to play and throws the training wheels off. If I had one gripe, it's that the first few acts had a few repeat puzzles, and you can see this in the demo. It got better as time went on, but it was definitely something worth pointing out. Overall, the game's clever take on a rewind mechanic removes any annoying waiting and adds a more dynamic tool that is far more interesting to play around with. Even with my gripe with the beginning levels, this game is a 10/10 for me. What a fantastic experience this was!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: One of my most anticipated indies of the year and what an amazing experience it was.This game has so much charm, such a thought provoking story, and fantastic gameplay.Calling this game a ‘Portal-like’ doesn’t do it justice in my opinion. It really expands on that idea and adds so much of a cohesive story around it including lots of lore to be missed within the world itself if you’re not looking hard enough. It reminds me a lot of Control in that way.The characters are relatable and super charming, the sound design and score are great, the visuals are immaculate as well.It’s so impressive that the entire game was made by essentially one person!At times I did feel as if there were a few too many puzzles. Yes it’s a puzzle game, but I feel they had something really special with the few action sequences in the game between the movement and rewind systems and wish they used it more!Overall I had an incredible time with The Entropy Centre. One of my personal games of the year and really think it’s worth checking out for anyone into solo adventure or puzzle games.I can’t wait to see what the developer does next 🙌
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a Portal-like, I can't recommend this game highly enough. The puzzle difficulty hits the perfect sweet spot where they aren't too easy or too hard, and solving each one feels incredibly rewarding. I also found myself surprised by how much I enjoyed the story and the characters. My only complaint is that the physics and jumping can be a bit wonky at times, making a few puzzles harder than they need to be. Despite that, this was some of the most fun I've had in a puzzle game in a long time. I'm gonna remember this one for quite a while.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre might be a bit of an acquired taste, but overall I'm going to have to give it a solid thumbs up.Things it has going for it:1. Incredible style and atmosphere, absolutely visionary design that clearly draws on such greats as Portal( 2), and yet brings something fresh, unique and clearly its very own to the table. It's also really quite pretty effects-wise, and also feels quite well performance-optimised!2. Tight voicework by an AMAZING cast (really gets you attached to the characters), and how did one person write all of this?? **AND** also develop the whole rest of the game????3. Novel gameplay!Things it has going for it....BUT:1. Novel gameplay!....but it doesn't quite toe the complexity vs complication, simple but difficult line quite as well as other puzzle games I've seen. Some of the environments allowed a few too many ways to fudge solutions using level geometry, and a number of others had "steps" that were a little too long for my taste. I think a great goal would be to reduce the rewind time on the device and make the levels clearer *and* more possible to accomplish with that.2. Delightlyfully creative and inspired story, perfectly nailing the satire-but-the-fate-of-the-universe-is-at-stake....but (and it's hard to do this without spoilers, I'll just say:) there was so much more potential in the story for what could be done, how it could have been resolved.3. There's a little bit of bugginess with clipping and collision, especially when carrying objects, and the controls aren't quite perfect for navigating air gaps and hitting precise targets, as the player is required to do a number of times.How did mostly one person produce this amazing work? I don't know. But call me when there's more!PS please also tell me where else the members of the voice cast have featured
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Sufficiently similar to portal to scratch that itch, sufficiently different from portal to not feel like a rehash. Enjoyable little time-bending puzzle mechanic w/an interesting story to boot. Couple annoyances in some of the later puzzles (one of them I'm pretty sure I solved out-of-band) but all in all fun game from a small studio. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: It's Portal in a parallel universe where the mad scientists invented a gun that messes with time, instead of a gun that messes with space. Kind of.The idea in itself is brilliant.The physical paradoxes of time travel are much more obvious than the physical paradoxes of portals, though, and I think that limited the devs a bit in terms of gameplay possibilities. Nevertheless, they found a combination that is fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at this game, it's hard not to see all the similarities with Portal, which it clearly draws inspiration from. Overall the game is quite good, it looks good, it plays good, no major bugs, and the premise is interesting. But there's one glaring fault which they miscalculated which Portal got perfectly, and that is level length and how much time you waste when you have to restart a level. In short, the game is hard, it is too difficult for a player whose only other experience with this genre of puzzle games is Portal.If you have played many of these sorts of games and are okay with hard puzzles and starting a level over after spending 5 minutes getting all the cubes in the correct positioning and then having to do it all over again, then this game is for you.But if you've only played Portal and or Portal 2, then know that this game is much harder and is likely not going to be fun for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Difficulty : 1.5/5 (Easy)Global : 4/5 (Great)Curator page : There's a certain number of pure Portal-like games out there (Lightmatter, Relicta, Turing Test, QUBE, Magnetic etc) but The Entropy Centre has to be the best I've played.I usually don't like these games a lot because they often fail to reproduce what makes the Portal series such a masterpiece, leaving only easy and not really interesting puzzles.So why isn't The Entropy Centre like them? Well, it is puzzle-wise unfortunately. Especially if you're already familiar with the time rewind mechanic, you won't have any trouble at all.Every puzzle is solved rather quickly and only doing the solution takes time. If you've played some Portal 2 workshop maps, the puzzles of the Entropy Centre are very similar to all those easy maps with a bunch of things scattered that you have to activate in the correct order. Except you have to record the solution this time.The problem with the time rewind mechanic is that creating hard puzzles means creating tedious ones, the game trapped itself with this core mechanic. That's why I don't really mind and understand the puzzles being a bit too easy.I'll skip the other mechanics, everything in Portal 2 is in there. I'll just talk about the jump pad, the hitbox could be better because sometimes you hit the edge and it doesn't count. And missing a jump pad jump means restarting the solution so it can be annoying.Where The Entropy Centre actually shines is on every other aspect :- Let's start with the best, the story. The Entropy Centre is a moon base where people solve puzzles to gather entropy energy in order to rewind the Earth when a cataclysmic event happens. You are Aria and you wake up alone in the devastated centre and the Earth is exploding, so your goal is to rewind it yourself.That's the sort of story I really like and it was well done, including the ending (though I think the story has even more potential). There's also a lot of lore to find in the mails of certain computers.- As you probably guessed from the story, the atmosphere is unreal. The destroyed Earth in the background unleashes shockwaves on the centre, destroying parts of it and allowing you to create paths by rewinding the debris. The walking sections outside of the puzzles aren't boring at all, that's for sure.- The game runs very smoothly, that's clearly something to praise. Most games nowadays are optimized like sh*t.The visuals are also stunning, seriously. And that's why I think exploration could've been made more important. There are sections of the game in which you can explore a bit, but there's usually nothing to find and that's a shame.- The characters are very cool with very good voice acting, dialogues and humor. - The sound design is top notch.The Entropy Centre isn't perfect and doesn't reach the greatness of its inspiration, but it's an extremely good tribute. Especially when you know it has mostly been developped by one person, that's just outstanding.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming game with a creative main puzzle mechanic. I've seen plenty of puzzle games that I'd call "Portal clones", but this is one of the first I've seen of what I'd call a "Portal 2 clone". This game has a very similar tone and replicates a lot of the things Portal 2 did to really up the quality from the first one, in that it's got interesting lore, humorous character conversations, more intense plot, etc and in my opinion that's very much a good thing!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know man. If I could, I'd give this a "meh" rating. The puzzles never really evolve much beyond what you have in the first few levels. It's always "position everything in reverse order from how you need it, then rewind everything one step at a time to get a little bit further until you're at the end". It took the game several hours to even introduce mechanics besides the time reversal (the crimpling box, object transformer and conveyor belts) that do not take very close inspiration from Portal. The puzzles were always so straightforward that I rarely had the same feeling of satisfaction of "wow, how the ♥♥♥♥ did I figure that out?" that I get from other puzzle games. There are basically never "think arond a couple of corners" solutions, it's almost always straightforward. This game had a ton of potential, but the mechanics are somehow... not complicated enough?The way the story could end becomes fairly obvious after just an hour if you read the message logs. There are so many chapters in this, and yet in most of them just about nothing of significance happens. The story is way too predictable. And yet, I still at least somewhat enjoyed it. The voice acting is great (although the writing is a bit corny at times), the scenery is amazing and the graphics are very pleasant to look at. The message logs, info videos and slideshows do a decent job at world building, although, IMO they give away too much too quickly, without much mystery left for the player to figure out. The music is also pretty nice. Overall though, this game never even comes close to living up to giants like Portal 1/2 and Talos Principle. Since it's not particularly long and surprisingly cheap, I would still say you can give it a shot if you're into puzzle games. Just expect it to be a bit mediocre.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute fantastic puzzle platformer that is quite impressive from an Indie team! If you enjoyed any of the Portal games or spin-offs, this is a sure-fire recommend from me. There’s plenty of familiar mechanics in this game and it’s also surprisingly long at around 7 hours of first-time gameplay.The gameplay itself borrows a lot from the Portal series; there’s the bridges in the form of bridge cubes, lasers in the form of laser cubes, spring boards, cube-button-pressing puzzle solving and of course, your trusty gun - in this case, the “entropy” gun. The Entropy gun reverses time, allowing you to rewind an object’s previous timeline to perform actions a second time or in the reverse order. This mechanic is really well done and all of the puzzles do a good job of showcasing how it works. In terms of the puzzles, personally, the entropy mechanic was easy to understand for me and I didn’t feel too challenged (only one or two puzzles out the whole game had me stumped for more then 10 minutes). If you are struggling, all you have to remember is to do the steps in the reverse order – if you know what the last thing a cube needs to do, then it’s actually the first thing it has to do. One thing that I give a big thumbs up to is how it introduces some very useful quirks with the gun in a non hand-holdy way. One puzzle in particular shows how you can freeze objects in time, which becomes heavily utilised in the later levels, but it’s introduced in a way that makes you feel like you discovered it and not the game railroading you to do so. I also enjoyed the interludes between puzzle sections, where there are detours around the centre which often involves using the entropy gun on now broken scenery to act as a make-shift lift when rewinding time.The graphics are quite frankly beautiful. The scenery to all of the puzzle rooms tends to be very well crafted and constantly seeing the Earth destroyed reminds you of what’s a stake for the character. I liked the little detail of the further you got into the game the closer the Earth was and the more destroyed it was. Something which I think is done much better than in Portal 2 is that you truly get a sense of destruction. One of the only things I disliked about Portal 2 is that you never really saw the destruction happening to the facility, but in this game, the scenery illustrates this perfectly – there’s overgrown plants growing in crack in the walls, entire ceilings and walls crumbled, puzzle rooms that are tilted in which you have to work at an angle – it feels much more immersive and it’s just so well executed to make it feel like you’re walking through an abandoned facility that’s been bombarded with planetary shock-waves.In terms of the story, I won’t spoil much, but I think it’s good and enjoyable. The premise is that humans have built a Moon base called the Entropy Centre which can use Entropy energy to reverse the Earth back in time; thereby undoing bad decisions that caused cataclysmic events so as to prevent the end of the world (if you’ve seen the TV series “The Lazarus Project” then it’s similar to that). You play as a character who is the only one left onboard the Entropy Centre with only your Entropy Gun which has a friendly AI to talk to. At the start of the game, I found the conversations between your character that the AI a bit obnoxious and why a mute protagonist worked so well in Portal, but I must say, the writing in the latter stages of the game definitely gelled better and the jokes and wittiness won me over in the end. The cute little “Entropy Bots” act as the turrets from Portal and I must say they are quite adorable, even when trying to kill you! Also, the fact you can boop the nose of the ‘E’ Entropy Bot is the cutest thing ever.The music for me was a little bit of a let down I must say. I think it’s fine from an objective point of view and in isolation, but when it’s compared to the likes of Portal 2 or Portal Stories: Mel, it just isn’t quite on the same level. A couple of tracks I quite liked and I’m glad they stuck with more “ambient” style tracks that don’t distract you from thinking of solutions to puzzles, similar to Portal’s approach.Overall, I highly recommended this game to anyone who likes puzzle platformers and even if not, I recommend you give the demo a go anyway, and as an aside I would also give this game an extra point for even having a demo in the first place (which I wish more games did).

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely an interesting game with interesting concept, unfortunately the execution of it is slightly lacking.First few puzzles were great, introducing mechanics.  Puzzles in this game require to reprogram your brain to think differently I managed to think "in reverse" pretty quickly.  After you rewire your brain to think like this game want puzzles are more or less trivia.  If I remember correctly the longest a puzzle took to solve me was ~10min and even that was only because the platforming is off in this game.This platforming is not done well.    Did you know that in PORTAL 2 the game cheats and nudges you to help with precise platforming for it not to be annoying?  Well even you did not know it, after this game you will notice it as this game does not help you a bit .I think, If this game was half as long with half its price it would be perfect.  At least for me the second half of the game was tedious as the game did not show you the whole puzzle and you had to start solving the puzzle with half knowledge and than discover that you had to change something slightly at complete begging, this would not be a problem but this game lacks a quick way to reset a puzzle, additionally HOW DO I RUN?  This game has enough walking; running would definitely help.  Also surprisingly this game has some "fight" scenes that don't fit in very well and are even not explained why are they there, apart from  The story.  The story was surprisingly great and was I think the main reason I finished this game.  The story ties all lose ends , and leaves you to think about implications of thinks that happened. Is this game worth 20e maybe, for sale @ 8e  definitelyI hope steam would have neutral rating but I have to go for recommend as story pushed this game more to that side.

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply charming and visually impressive game whose puzzle mechanics ensured I felt less like of an idiot when playing Tears of the Kingdom. Having to do all your steps once and then rewinding them again is occasionally frustrating, but the charming characters and lovable dialogue made the experience worth it. The dilapidated corridors and cosmic horror of your situation pairs well with this rogue's gallery of snarky goofballs.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the fence with this one.The game itself is very fun and the mechanics of time travel are interesting.  The thing that makes this not as fun are that some of the voicelines and cut scenes are not skippable.  And for a game which allows you to try out and explore some things that might cause you to die, to give up exploring because you don't want to hear the 1 minute long elevator cut scene or the beach voicelines means that I'm just going to be disappointed.Also, I know the mechanic.  You rewind time to fix certain things that are broken.  I don't need to be reminded of this every so often between stages.  Unless it's unique or has a way of helping me explore something, random rocks falling or random ceilings falling in the later parts of the game are more annoying.  Overall a great game with some annoying gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: So imagine Portal except the writing is cringe, the levels are poorly designed, the puzzles are almost all identical and uninspired, and the music is annoying. This may be the most creatively bankrupt, uninspired game I have ever played. Anything it has that's good is ripped for Portal (they literally have certain puzzles and even jokes ripped straight from portal) and everything else is garbage. Almost every puzzle is 'put box on Pad A, then Pad B, then reverse box to Pad A' it's abysmal. It's humor is stolen, its mechanics are stolen, and it's all thrown together in an uncreative fashion by a passionless team. I mean, the developers couldn't even be bothered to change the color scheme from Portal - these people do not deserve your money. I wanted a Portal-like game, not a bad Portal ripoff.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good Portal-esque game. (mild spoilers marked in this review: an enemy name, number of chapters, stories unrelated to progression)The puzzles range from trivial to head scratching, nothing too difficult to understand, but sometimes the execution gets frustrating.- Unlike Portal there are no invisible funnels guiding you during jumps, so restarting the whole puzzle cause I missed the last jump was a fairly frequent occurrence. - The 38 seconds rewind limit does become a problem towards the end, I had to restart the first half of a puzzle because I took about 39 seconds to do a sequence of actions with a cube. - I also really disliked the lockdown sections where you get attacked from all directions by 6+  that keep respawning and you can only defend effectively from one at a time.Those 3 things I found frustrating made some small parts of the game feel like a chore, but the rest was really good.I kept playing for the fun puzzles and funny dialogue, very much worth it.There are  chapters including the final story only chapter, the game lasts about 7-8 hours at a leisurely pace. Most of the story is found by exploring and reading text on the various terminals, but the game can be played without engaging much with it if that's what you prefer, there are also some funny random parallel stories sprinkled throughout, like .

_childDocuments_.review: The good:+ Superb puzzle. I find it's well designed and also quite challenging (from middle to end of game), while rarely give me frustration where i solve 95%+ puzzle without guide.+ Somehow entertaining characters with great voice acting.+ Great visual, even though i find few parts looks generic/"stock asset" or could have better animation.+ Run well on Linux with default version of Proton.The bad:- Extra lore/story (in form of terminal message) must be located manually on computer which could be missed easily or require you to access location which is tricky to access. I went out looking for it, but only obtain about 70%.The ugly:* Premise and early part of the story are interesting, but my enjoyment ruined due to pacing problem. And personally i'm baffled to find .* Intriguing lore/world building, although it suffer from few technical error and inconsistency.* Some parts lack polish. For example, there's no option to restart from last checkpoint (especially useful if you stuck on odd location) and your jump need to be somehow precise (otherwise you're wasting time to retry the puzzle).Albert some flaws, The Entropy Centre is decent puzzle game and probably most similar game compared with Portal series. However, if you primarily interested with this game due to the story, maybe wait for big discount or seek for different game. And if you're looking for very difficult/challenging puzzle game, it's likely you'll find The Entropy Centre too easy for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, clever mechanics, beautiful visuals and a gorgeous soundtrack.Being compared to Portal is a massive compliment, but The Entropy Centre clearly defines itself with its quirky time rewind mechanic and interesting story. I would find myself thinking about the game at work and wanting to get home to play more! A brilliant first release from the solo developer at Stubby Games – cannot wait to see a sequel!!An absolute 10/10 must-have for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good puzzle game, if you like puzzles you will like this game. After a certain amount of time playing this game you start to think and solve the puzzles in a backwards order. The story also makes sense and is not to complicated with good looking graphics to go along with it. My main complaint is the vending machines; you can only activate them 6 times each and they dispense objects (mostly cans of beans) that do not correspond with the objects in the glass. This game is fun, short enough to not drive you crazy, and  has creative solutions that make me see patterns in puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game with a "*" At its core it is a fun twist on portal and my hats off to the developer. But I have been on the same "puzzle" for 30 minutes now. Not because I don't know what to do but because with the conveyor belt if the jump pad isn't in the pixel perfect spot you're not making the jump and you can't take your time aligning the pad as you need almost all your rewind time since you need to place the pad in 2 different pixel perfect spots. And there is nooooo way I'd pick doing this over replaying portal.I'm not writing this to deter anyone from buying this game, I just want those who decide to give this game a try to do so with realistic expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre is an excellent experience. .This game, however technically a Portal clone, has its own story and its own mechanic (sort of). Rewinding can be a lot of a mental headache (especially towards the end), and if you mess up on something in the beginning, YOU HAVE TO COMPLETELY RESTART, but that click feeling is ultimately very gratifying. The game's puzzles can be fairly broken, and in one case, a bug forced me to complete the level using a glitch I found. Those faith-plate thingies (along with the trampoline cubes) are now the bane of my mortal existence.The story is really interesting. However in puzzle-solving it IS Portal-reborn, the story is totally on its own. Me, I tried to get all the secret computer-thingamajigs, and I think that helped me understand the full scope of the narrative. This is one of those games where you're in the shower and thinking about it, then you randomly say, "OH!". Aria, Astra, and Tannoy are all very well-voiced. Their characters are (except for Aria; she's great), well, characters. I think there should have been a snarky antagonist like GLaDOS to freshen things up a bit, as honestly Astra is just a very predictable and common companion that is funny, just, you know, not GLaDOS. I love GLaDOS. Anyway, the end, however I won't spoil it, it (like the puzzles) is awesome when it clicks.It doesn't really need its own paragraph, but the little "combat" sections are fun, fast-paced, and honestly, a bit of easy-to-eat brain candy. They aren't really based in strategy, unlike the turrets, but are just easy (it's nice after some really tough tests).The price, well, yeah, it's plenty worth it. I got it during the winter sale at approximately $21, and I am quite satisfied with my purchase. I wouldn't wait for a sale for this buggy but beautiful game. As you can see, I put in about 14 hours at review time, and that was the only me playing the game.The fact that  is just nuts, and in that respect, Undertale, Donut County, and Stardew Valley could wet their pants. The quality in this game is really, truly, good, and It's... Nope, it's still no where close to Portal/Portal 2.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The core rewind idea is interesting and the writing is generally good, but the puzzles are far too repetitive. Nearly all of the puzzles I saw in 90 minutes of playtime were solved by putting two blocks on the same switch, bringing one of them across a hazard and back, then bringing the first block back and rewinding the second to catch up to me. It was very cool the first time I did it, but much less so after the sixth time in a row without substantial changes. Other reviews from people who played further suggest that this doesn't get better - I wasn't interested enough to let the refund window lapse in order to find out.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting gameplot and well designed and beautiful game. Reversed thinking to solve the puzzles is rather special i think. _childDocuments_.review: (insert the usual complaint about Steam not having a neutral option)It's a good premise, it's well made, but it's stretched way too thin. You're told to go to  in act 2 or 3 or something (I forgot) - you finally find it in act 12.The puzzles themselves are also stretched thin. _childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre fits firmly on a shelf between Portal and The Talos Principle. The roll-back-time mechanic is fun. The puzzles are clever. The characters are interesting with great voice acting. The story is solid, delivered via dialogue and by reading a lot of little bits hidden throughout. The environment does feel a little simple and repetitive at the start, but it significantly improves as the game ramps up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Copies a lot from Portal but mostly in a good way. Some of the platforming is a little meh.+++ Puzzle difficulty balance. Not too hard, not too easy+++ Cinematic story and the general underlying message of the game (except maybe the ending)+++ Great soundtrack and immersion--- Platforming segments can be frustrating--- Once you find the pattern of the game mechanics, you will have experienced all there is to see from chapter 7 (out of 15)--- Some puzzles require you to just follow the exit while others require you to think out of the box
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Very portal inspired game with a decent story.If you're avid about story and lore more than puzzles you will likely enjoy this game as you can read terminals for the lore and throughout the game a decent story narrative. On the other hand if you much prefer puzzles I would look somewhere else. This game doesn't have extremely difficult and challenging puzzles and they're not particularly unique from puzzle to puzzle.The game does have a demo (at the time of this writing if there is no longer one) so I would give it a shot as it does give you some story narrative and if your interest is piqued then I would get the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoyed this game! If you liked the Portal series, I think you'll like this one too and I very highly recommend it. The puzzles were really fun to solve and the voice acting is great!The only gripe I have is a very minimal QoL thing IMO.There's no manual save, but when you go to quit the game, it warns you that any unsaved progress will be lost. [Sweating.png] The problem is that it doesn't tell you when the last time the game saved and there's no indicator that the game is saving so you have no idea when it happens. After a tiny bit of searching the interwebnets, I learned that it saves at the start of each individual puzzle which is perfectly reasonable. It would just be nice to know you're not about to lose a bunch of progress...
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: I certainly understand some of the comments mentioning the lack of polish. Comparing it to portal, the tweaks making movement easier (scripted momentum, portal succ, portal magnet, etc) certainly make this game annoying if you compare it to portal, and i certainly get it. I rarely felt that annoyed at the lack of this polish though, move just "sucks i have to jump in the right place" but i got used to it quite quickly. The puzzles were quite easy i felt, only the last few got me a bit challenged, but that wasn't a terrible thing for me, just annoying how fast some of the puzzles felt. i only had to google one puzzle, and that was because the box kept falling in the wrong place, to the point i thought that can't be the intended solution if it wont fall in the way i want. The ending isn't that bad, i mean there isn't really a plot twist after the main big one, which happens a decent bit before the final ending, so it's kinda spoilt as to what will happen. I still really liked the game, certainly worth it especially on sale which it goes on often. sad they haven't updated this game in a while and feel they likely wont though. certainly has potential

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't even completely it tbh, but I just got bored. The puzzles all seemed really easy and very straightforward. _childDocuments_.review: I'm ich Chapter 10 and not going to finish it! large parts of the game are not about solving the puzzles but  testing your physical dexterity. if you're not 100% able-bodied (and maybe more suitable controls: stay away). the obvious game to compare this to here is Portal 2 which had a great accessibility. if you expect something similar: stay away! instead you have to millisecond-time actions, dodge enemies and move the character in time pressure situations. the exact thing I  don't want to do in a first person puzzler!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: 99.9% of the game's budget went into looking pretty. The puzzles from start to finish are an absolute joke. The puzzle designers were either not intelligent enough to design an actually challenging puzzle or they intentionally dumbed them down to kindergarten level to attempt to appeal to a wider audience. I had way more fun in this game just breaking its flimsy physics system and skipping half the puzzles with the bounce pads. Would not recommend if you're looking for a puzzle game, this felt more like an obstacle course.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: On God? Astra is the only reason I got out of bed today, wanting to hear her dialogue is the biggest highlight of this entire experience. Review: The game took about ~11 hours to finish while searching every nook and cranny for the intels. The puzzles were not insanely hard, but there is a HUGE opportunity for a level creator to take place here, I can see there are tons of assets in the game to make some truly mind stumping puzzles. There is a little bit of wonkiness with the physics and some testing boxes getting flung around or crushed rewinding debris, not too often however.As for the story, I figured I knew where it was going, but the journey was really what made the game worth playing, the environments are beautiful and the relationship between Aria and Astra is quite charming. Understanding truly what is going on and what has happened, I think is something only the creator himself through another media or DLC could state.Overall, worth the cost, if you're looking for something fun to do over the weekend, certainly give this game a try, if this review doesn't sell it. Try the Demo!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: If the game description wasn't enough to convince you, do yourself a favor and check a handful of (detailed) reviews first.Although that sounds like a bad thing, I absolutely recommend this game (and so do 90% of reviewers).I got this game at half price. But after completing it in about 10 hours, I would still not have a problem if I had gotten it at full price.    But some reviewers forget the fact that they didn't pay a "AAA price" or were bombarded with ads for this game everywhere, telling you how amazing it is and how you should preorder months in advance. That's because this isn't a AAA game.Yes this is heavily inspired in the Portal series, but Stubby Games (at the time of writing) has a total of 1 game on Steam...  During my playtime I only had one major annoyance: the jump cubes. It's the only thing that, considering how much this game "took" from Portal, I would expect  to be a problem. I am not a game developer, so I'm not gonna say game physics like these are trivial. But Portal did it 10+ years ago and their development, techniques and ingenuity has been documented in many ways.: they were both pretty fun and interesting, but of course have several things that could have been done better. Most puzzles are closer to easy than challenging, but to me that was not a bad thing.  Unfortunately, this part also contains some of the lackluster situations, where they were clearly trying to "change it up" or forcefully make you feel a certain way. Like with most "destructive" environments and shoehorned situations. For example, .The graphics are great and the design ideas (in general) are pretty identical to Portal. Lots of "lived in" and abandoned rooms mixed in with the "test chamber" look. But then also many common and outside areas that made me think of Prey (2017), basically showing you that it wasn't just about science .
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very enjoyable game. Immersive and well created environments with a compelling story.Puzzles are enjoyable whilst not being too difficult. You'll figure out the structure to solving the puzzles fairly quickly. It's also good to have the story play into the need to do the puzzles rather than them being in the way of travel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If half of the puzzles were cut (especially the early easy and samey ones) and an alternate ending was added (and/or more character introspection at the end), I would be able to recommend it.I wanted to like this game, and some parts are enjoyable, but I can't recommend it.  The rewind mechanic is cool at first, but it isn't enough to carry a game of this length.  Less is more.  Either another unique mechanic should be introduced, or half of the puzzles, "traversal challenges", and empty hallways should be cut.  The themes and story were very interesting until I hit a pacing wall early on and was drip fed redundant evidence for the rest of the game.  Then the ending disappointed even further and desperately needed either an alternate optional ending or at least some introspection on Aria's part. Spoiler: Some other things:-game is pretty-voice acting, environment, music, and vibes are great-interesting puzzles (to me) started popping up at around chapter 6, and there were some good ones after that-environment and puzzle blending is very contrived (not a dealbreaker, but there is very obviously just one convenient catwalk or crumbled ledge to get to where you need to go, and it breaks immersion a bit)-inconsistent physics while object is being rewound for obvious gameplay purposes breaks immersion a bit-combat is cool the first time, I would remove all but 2 additional encounters after that-bots will make noises while you are in a different room puzzling-collisions are a little wonky sometimes--give character a sprint button, higher jump, and another input for faster rewindThis all comes off as pretty negative, but I'm just focusing on the things that if improved upon would drastically enhance the experience for me.  The little frustrations and monotony just built up due to the frequency of easy, repetitive, and slow nature of many of the puzzles.  This is still a very impressive project, especially for a solo dev, and I would keep an eye on their future projects.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: My only main gripe is that there is a lot of waiting for things to move to their places and if you miss a jump you would have to redo most of the puzzle. Didn't happen too often and the puzzles are quite short so it's not the biggest deal but if there will be a sequel I'd love to see this addressed.The common comparison with portal is definitely earned.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: One trick pony. Every puzzle felt almost exactly like the last.There is a sequence of buttons/plates to push with a cube. Do the sequence in reverse order, then apply the time reversal beam to the cube so that the sequence is completed in the order needed to progress. Thats pretty much every puzzle, they eventually mix things up a bit with different kinds of cubes but its too little too late.Other aspects of the game arent great either. The sections between puzzles are also very samey and boring. A bridge collapses, reverse time on it (you do this 40 times throughout the game!). Reverse and enemy projectile back into them. Thats about it. Also you walk so damn slowly.Then there is your side kick. The joke is that its annoying in a corporate kind of way. Gets old real fast, feels like reddit tier humour half the time. its rather cringe.Not bad, just meh. Falls far short of its contemporaries like Portal, Talos Principle, Turing test & Qube
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: The Entropy Centre: The Best, Believe Me!Let me tell you folks, The Entropy Centre is tremendous. A game like you've never seen before, just tremendous. They say it's like that Portal thing, but let me tell you, it's even better. People are talking about it, believe me. I know games, I've played them all, and let me tell you, this one's a winner.You've got these puzzles, folks, these puzzles that are out of this world. They're saying it's about time and space, and let me tell you, I know all about time and space. These puzzles, they're smart, they're challenging, but you'll solve them, you will. And when you solve them, you'll feel like a winner, just like me.Now, I hear they've got this AI, Astra they call her. She's a talker, let me tell you. Reminds me of myself, always speaking my mind. But she's funny, too. I like funny, and I like winning. So, you've got these puzzles and you've got this AI, what's not to like? Nothing, folks, nothing.And the story, oh boy, the story is something else. World-saving, time-traveling, it's got it all. I've been there, I've done deals, and I know a good story when I see one. The Entropy Centre's got a story that'll make your head spin, and I promise you, it's worth it.Now, some people are saying it's like Portal, and you know what I say? I say, if you're gonna be influenced, be influenced by the best. I've influenced a lot of people, believe me, and this game, it's influenced by greatness. It's got that Portal vibe, but it's got its own thing going on, too. Originality, folks, that's what I'm all about.So, if you're looking for a game that's gonna challenge you, entertain you, and make you feel like a winner, then The Entropy Centre is the game for you. I've played it, I've seen it, and let me tell you, it's a winner. Get out there, grab it, and make gaming great again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: At its best, first-person sci-fi puzzle adventure game, The Entropy Centre, shines as brightly and mind-bendingly as did the original Portal, its phenomenal sequel, The Talos Principle, and other great puzzle-centric games of the last decade plus. At its worst, well... *insert clip of game-breaking bug* Let’s just say that The Entropy Centre likes to get in its own way, often undermining its intense, at-times fascinating plot with forced humor, or compromising its occasionally brilliant puzzle solutions with clunky platforming sections and poor optimization. It’s not all bad, but it’s certainly not all good.  Explanations in video: . Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler kind of) 100% recommend this to anyone that liked the Portal games. But it's also definitely not Portal. It was about a 11hr game for me (my playtime got reset after a patch). And very entertaining/engaging the entire time. The music is beautiful, the world design is perfect, the puzzles are fun and challenging without being over-the-top difficult, and the story and ASTRA are amazing. I sure hope there's an Entropy Center 2: Escape the Loop.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzle are actually really not that witty, they aren't challenging at all while unexciting in gameplay. And there is way too many invisible walls in this game. Even though it was apparently about creativity most puzzles had only 1 single solution. Making the laser align especially when you can't see it was a major pain.Would not recommend to buy at all.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing portal knockoffs I am almost annoyed by the fps puzzle genre but this is a portal-inspired game that has redeemed my faith and for me actually stands in the same tier as the portal games. It's not better than them, of course, but by copying the format and structure only and bringing in a unique but intuitive puzzle mechanic as well as one of the best story sequences in recent memory this is a game I will bring up whenever portal is being discussed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: We have Portal to thank for paving the way for first-person puzzler development (a genre that hadn’t seen a lot of movement before Portal’s release), and its phenomenally tight design showed that you could do a lot with a little. Several gems followed in Portal’s wake, and, even though you can see Portal’s influences in them, they all managed to do their own thing. Consequently, the genre’s been gifted with several entries that’re fantastic games in their own right (Antichamber, The Talos Principle, possibly The Witness depending on your feelings about it), but how would you feel if I told you someone has released a game that made absolutely no attempt to change anything about Portal’s formula? Enter The Entropy Center (TEC).For my first hour, I was ready to write TEC off as too much of a Portal imitator. Its blatant similarities grated on me, “oh look, a chirpy AI companion;” “a “gun” style tool that acts as the hinge for interactable puzzle elements;” “an abandoned and overgrown facility with only robots left to control it;” “employee participation in tes- I mean, ”. Of all the first-person puzzlers to come out since Portal, TEC’s the closest to straight up cloning it. However, the puzzles eventually hooked me in, and, at some point, I found myself pushing forward with genuine enthusiasm to uncover what came next in the story. Portal’s been out over 15 years now, and normally I’d want something that took its ideas to evolve the genre, which TEC never really does, but perhaps it’s been long enough that there’s room for a copycat that doesn’t push the envelope.With that said, it’s hard to say much more about TEC because everything about it is just a Portal redux. I could tell you that the time rewind mechanics and variety of puzzle objects to interact with are well-implemented and develop at a good pace, but, as with everything about TEC, that was the case in Portal and so it is in TEC. It’s impossible to overstate just how closely TEC follows in Portal’s footsteps, it practically lives in the skin of its ancestor. So if you liked Portal and want more then you can get TEC without a second thought. However, if you want a first-person puzzler that tries to have some semblance of its own identity then you’ll have to look elsewhere, but remember that Portal was good for a reason, and TEC shares its brilliance, so you’ll be doing yourself a disservice by skipping over it.Quick afterword: my review left out that TEC was predominantly designed by a single person, and, taking that it into account, it's astounding what they've achieved. The graphical detail, world-building, puzzle quality, audio, build stability, etc. are all phenomenal considering that it was mostly one individual. Perhaps the price of this is that there weren't the resources to differentiate the game more from Portal, but it's a tremendous achievement by itself considering how well put together the game is. Perhaps the fact it's so well put together on such a small team is the part that separates it from Portal, but it's a nuance you wouldn't notice if you went into the game blind, and that's a huge credit to the design as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Entropy Centre

_childDocuments_.review: This game really stretches your brain and is kinda stressful at parts. I really loved it and finished it in 9 and a half hours on my first play through, so that is about the low end I would say. I solved a lot of puzzles much quicker that other people I know.
