_childDocuments_.review: So, Asterigos is not a great game, sadly.  I had seen some trailers and liked the idea of souls-esque combat in an ancient roman setting.  Stylistically, that's very much my jam. Unfortunately, while the combat has some neat ideas with the dual weapons that you can combo between on the fly, hot-swappable elements to exploit enemy weaknesses, and of course big special moves to help you take down bigger baddies, it all just falls apart in the execution.The combat feels decent enough when you focus on your own moves, but enemies are kind of erratically aggressive. Hits deal a lot of damage when they connect, but so far into the game there's very little reason to be afraid. The game gives you more healing than you will ever need, and enemies often let you just stand and wail on them in-between their own attacks which come out haphazardly, and far too seldom.The first story-boss, Baraad, is no exception. While he does have a bevvy of moves to make the fight varied, and brings them out gradually to ramp up the challenge as the fight goes on, the whole thing just moves too slowly to be any fun. It's like a poorly rehearsed stage fight, where the actors have to constantly, and politely wait and check that their partner is ready for the next phrase of combat. Plus he's got stupid amounts of health that drag the fight out for far too long given how humdrum it feels.And as if that's not bad enough, the writing and acting are just a complete miss for me. The story is both simplistic nonsense and too convoluted for anyone's good, throwing new proper nouns at you without any context every few story beats, and the dialogue and voice acting are at best Saturday morning cartoon levels. Sometimes not even that.Sadly, this is not a game I recommend at all. It would need quite a lot of polish to be enjoyable in the long run

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a third person action game set in a fantasy themed world of magic and monsters. Player character Hilda has travelled to the city of Aphes in search of her father, the commander of a legion of soldiers who are on their own quest to find a cure for their cursed king.•	There are 6 weapons to choose from and you can have 2 equipped, which allows you to quickly swap between them during combat. I mostly used the staff to attack from long range, and the daggers so that I could quickly dodge enemy attacks. You could also use sword and shield, spear, hammer, and bracers.•	Weapons can be upgraded to perform special attacks, and you can also use fire, frost and lightning magic.•	Enemy variety is good. In addition to warriors equipped with sword and shield, spear, bow, or magic staff, you’ll have to fight against minotaurs, harpies, lions, bulls, giant insects, and rock monsters.•	There are also several massive bosses who are quite challenging. While their health bars are a mile long, you can quickly lose half of your own health in a single hit from their powerful attacks. These fights were the most enjoyable part of the game.•	I played on “adventure” (medium) difficulty, which is mostly well balanced. I died a few times, especially during boss fights, but still made consistent progress.•	Non-boss enemy AI can be easily exploited at times. It seems like they’ve been programmed to defend specific areas, so if you back off far enough they’ll just disengage and walk away, allowing you to get in several free hits. Its also possible to use ranged attacks to aggro individual enemies to take out groups one enemy at a time while the others stand around and watch.•	Completing side quests is more annoying than it should be because Asterigos lacks two features that most modern games provide. Firstly, the journal doesn’t list active quests so its hard to remember what you’ve been asked to do by some random NPC a few hours ago.•	There’s also no map, which sometimes leads to confusion when simply trying to figure out exactly where you need to go. While progress through the main story is mostly linear, each area contains several branching paths that loop back around and can occasionally feel like trying to navigate a maze. •	Overall story quality is average. Hilda’s relationship with her dad was the most interesting part, but unfortunately the story was more focused on the local politics of the city which I didn’t really care about.•	Voice acting is good. The dialogue/writing lacks quality, but I think the actors did the best they could with what they had to work with.•	Key story conversations are voiced, but any “ask for more details” dialogue options are text only.•	Conversations feel low budget because they aren’t shown through typical cutscenes, just the normal gameplay camera angles. Also characters’ mouths don’t move when they speak, and their body language animations look stiff.•	It took me 26 hours to finish the main story.•	I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes, or framerate.•	Controls are fully rebindable and work well with mouse and keyboard.•	I like the colourful art style.I would have given Asterigos: Curse of the Stars a neutral rating if Steam allowed it. While the boss fights are the highlight, everything else is pretty average. I’d suggest waiting for a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really unexpected gem. I played this on next fest and expected a basic little soulslike romp but ended up getting sucked into this world for 50 hours.I can tell a lot of heart went into this, its such a charming game world with a whole host of interesting characters. Some rambling thoughts on it all:The combat is fun and gives you some options right off the bat for weapon types, you can carry 2 at a time and each weapon has its own skill tree with some of the later skills feeling very powerful and fun to use. The only downside to this is the upgrade materials are expensive and fairly hard to come by so despite filling the skill trees out for my first weapon set around halfway through the game I didnt really have enough to switch over to a new set for variety sake. But theres ng+ for that. I enjoyed almost all of the bosses and enemies, I played on the hard setting and it was an enjoyable difficulty with no major wall points just a handfull of tries for each difficult part that never dipped into true frustration. The story is what surprised me the most. This game is absolutely loaded with lore, and to get the most out of the story (or really to get anything out of it at all) you do have to be willing to coax it out of optional dialogue options, side quests, and notes found in the world. Basically you are piecing together what happened a thousand years ago and the relationships between characters and how that all comes together to affect the present time. It was refreshing to play something without much handholding, theres a main quest tracker which i suggest disabling in the menus but aside from that theres no map or waymarkers, sidequests are kept in a journal with illustrations and notes instead of a "quest tracker" and there is a ton of missable content in the way of items and lore to pick up that then lead to further interactions and quests. I really do recommend playing this at a slow pace and soaking up the world.The game world is quite large with levels that are fairly porous and have shortcut connections within themselves and connections to neighboring areas, teleporting will have to be unlocked later in the game so its up to you to navigate and understand shortcuts for awhile. Some downsides:the 2 worst issues that affect the whole game are, it does that thing that ive seen some other games do where distant enemies will have reduced animation framerate, and then some sort of interpolate blur thing on top of that so they look really wacky from afar. But im not even talking cross map it can happen even within aggro tether range. Another issue is direction sound is really bad, enemies will often sound like they are behind you and you can clearly hear things even if they are behind multiple walls. Keybinds are not currently supported as of writing this but are planned to be added later. But as long as you are on a qwerty keyboard the default bindings are fine and I still prefer it over a controller. Those issues aside, a really nice game and I definitely got my money's worth. Its clear a lot of care went into the game and it has a sort of oldschool charm to it. I hope the devs continue to make more. There is a dlc coming out next year which I will check out for sure. These sort of AA indie titles are always such a good experience for me, I come in with no real expectations and less money on the line and walk away feeling really good about the experience. Hopefully you enjoy it too if you give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Nowadays, for whatever reason, I almost never end up staying invested in a game and sticking with it to the end. With Asterigos, I never felt like I had that problem. For perspective, I completed the game, did pretty much all the side quests, all the secret bosses, and (almost) got the secret ending in around 30 hours. I do think the story was genuinely interesting, and the game play was enjoyable as well. Yes, you have a limited set of weapons, but I used the daggers with the staff as a secondary, and the combat never got too dull. The art style is really charming and almost all of the characters have great voice actors and interesting stories. Yes, this is very much a AA game, you can tell they were working on a smaller scale, and if you go in expecting Elden Ring you'll be disappointed. But if you go in just wanting to run around a beautiful city, fight some dudes, do some side quests and look past some flaws, you'll come out the other end happy. I really hope this game does well enough to allow the developers to expand and make a sequel, I'd love to see what they could do with more time, more funding, and more people!

_childDocuments_.review: i was realy wrong about this gameinitialy i thought "just another souls-clone, mixed with greek mythology"both takes couldn't be more wrongAsterigos is probably one of the best (if not the best) 3rd person action-rpg i ever played.why?a nigh perfect core-gameplay, aka the combat, exploration and progressionan incredible deep, highly detailed and well thoughtout world and stunning audio-visual design (neither video nor screenshots do the actual game justice)the most important part about any and all action games is the combat. Asterigos nails this part like no other.you basicaly get all possible weapons (the new dlc apperently added more options) pretty much from the get go. you can equip 2 weapons at the same, but mix and match at all times via the ingame profile (inventory). each active weapon has one normal attack and one respective special.these attacks vary incredible. from heavy hitting aoe hammer bashes, to sword'n board stabs, pike pokes to magical balls of fire. the sword'n shield might allow you to block, while the staff offers as it's special a snipe shot. doesn't sound that great? how about mix and machtching attack chains between each equipped weapon?you combo staff ranged attacks with the possibility to weave in a sword'n shield block'n parry at any point of the staff chain. or you combo with sword'n shield but suddenly you need to get out of the way? weave in a staff attack and your character jumps back while leaving an elemental aoe attack behind. this goes for all weapons and all combinations. now mix in unlockable (talent-tree) ressource costing skills (like creating magical shields, aoe-buffs, damaging companions, large scale attacks), and the ability to switch your attack element via simpel button press (often enough changing each weapons effect significantly) and you get so many tools and options. it's snappy, meaty, responsive, and one of the best combat-systems i ever played in one of these games. then there's the progression.you earn exp by killing stuff, each level up offering you one attribute point (or two every two levels) and one talent point (large, hughe, talent tree) to shape your character. the talent tree is also very well done. it doesn't just offer both new active and passive abilites, or changes existing abilities completly (these changes can be turned on and off in the perk-menu), but furthermore it weaves in the usual % increases to stats with actual abilities...you get 2 for one. to use skills unlocked in the talent tree you also don't need to have the respective weapon equipped which offers just so much variety. similiar to soulslikes you also find materials (enemy drops, enviroment) to upgrade pretty much everything: weapons, elemental damage, etc. . and while there might not be a real armor-system (you unlock and get different cosmetic outfits), basicaly you get 4 permanent gear slots, to equip different "trinkets", offering everything from mitigation boni to changes to your loadoutsize. unlocking hidden chests doesn't just reward it's contents, but you also fill a sorta battlepass bar, which unlocks new stuff after certain keystones are met (like permanent increases to your "mana" or stamina, new outfits, etc.). the world might look like an oldschool disney movie ala Hercules come to live, and it's very pretty to look at, especialy in motion, but it's certainly not ment for children. the game gets dark very fast. adiction, heck even canibalism, sorrow and pain litter these streets. main and side quests are all part of a greater narrative so is the incredible amount of lore-material filling this world. names and some design aspects might look like greek mythology, but it's not. it's a sci-fi / fantasy world, build around seemingly mythological aesthetics. your character is part of a nordic-special task force, many of your allies could very well exist in the greek patheon. the voice over, writing and music are stellar. especialy the music is just incredible well done, often mixing arabic, greek, even modern influences while beeing very well produced and always fitting the enviroment you are currently traversing. what the game is not is a souls like. you can save at all time (hard save), which will save the general world state (dead enemies, looted stuff), but not your position, you will resapwn at the last checkpoint (well) upon loading. you also do not lose your exp-ressource upon death, just a little bit (standart 10%) of your currency (trading, upgrading) which is permanently lost, but easy to grind back. also there are difficulties.yes, checkpoints (well) do respawn enemies upon resting and thus restoring your health, etc. . yes, bosses can deal insane amounts of damage.but calling this a soulslike is a stretch. it's a masterfully crafted 3rd person action rpg. think Zelda, meets Metroid-vania, meets Fromgames. most of critic i saw on steam was down to a lack of handholding or direction. there's no questmarkers, no map. but the game is designed for exploration. each area is distinct, hidden loot or lore around every corner. exploration (and also backtracking) is part of the core game design and it's absolutly wonderfull.you should believe all these youtube videos claiming Asterigos is an overlook gem. it's hard to describe how well made this game is. i realy do hope a sequel is already in planning. great IP, wonderfull game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really torn on posting a review this early into the game, but it's got to be said that the narrative here is objectively bad. The gameplay is good, but not revolutionary. The story is interesting, even if it tries a little too hard to pull off the Dark Souls breadcrumb-style approach to lore. But if "Choices Matter" is a tag you care about, prepare to be disappointed. Instead of just letting itself be a linear Souls-like, Asterigos instead made the bizarre decision to give you no real choices, and then actively gaslight you into thinking there was a choice and that your decision was not just morally gray, but was actually the "evil" choice. And it's not just once, it's constantly, and the NPCs are all-in on shaming you for it. It's the weirdest narrative choice I've seen in a long time, and it makes an otherwise decent play experience feel really cumbersome.There is also a ton of time-inflation based on the lack fast travel between bonfires, you end up wasting a ton of hours traversing through completed areas trying to find the next one. I'm still going to try to finish it, but the second or third time the game artificially pulled the chair out from under me and tried to make it seem like I made a choice, I stopped pretending that this was a game you play for the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Well made souls-like with an interesting setting and fun combat. You can tell the writing was translated but it ended up having a much more interesting story than I expected. The setting is fantasy-Athens and they spend more time than you might think discussing the politics of freedom and related concepts. This does conceptually fight with the fact that you need to kill lots of semi-normal people to beat the game.For the combat, you actually start with 6 complete weapon styles and they're all pretty different, but some of the styles are clearly better than others. It's moderately difficult, I played most of the game on hard difficulty to get that true souls feel. _childDocuments_.review: My friend and I just had a new profound love for souls-like games and it is when she bought it for me. Thank you Maruh! <3Let me start off by saying that you need no soulslike experience to play this gem. You might get fooled by videos, thinking the movement and controls are stiff, but in fact when you actually play it yourself everything is so smooth and the combat is very abstract once you unlock some skills. You have a good choice of weapons to use and elements to it (like fire, magic, thunder and ice).My friend would ask me to stream my gameplay for her and we would sometimes laugh our asses off as I was playing on hard mode and struggling to kill mobs mostly and falling down the map :D It has a good amount of interesting side-quests and side-bosses that you can enjoy, in case you are an explorer. All the bosses have a unique design and set of attacks, so they are enjoyable both on easy and hard difficulty mode. The maps are prettily design and the mobs are so good to the point that they annoy the ♥♥♥♥ out of you :D but you end up making fun of them At the first stages, the game has no map so it was a struggle for me but then I found if you talk to NPCs, they will give you some directions - don't worry, at a later stage you can teleport at any check points and you get so hooked into exploring and getting all items/chests, that you don't even need a map.The game has two endings and if you are an achievement hunter, you might enjoy the 'better' ending as it requires you to complete a certain set of side-quests in order to get to that ending. There are some guides online if you struggle.All in all, this game is definitely worth the money as it is a good amount of hours playtime (mind you I spent 37 and I still did not complete all quests) and the graphics are just beautiful. :coolchick:

Simple and fun soulslike adventure, i enjoyed it greatly.Pros:No bloat, no filler contentVery light on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and frustrationAll weapons viable and require no stats to useResponsive combat with low commitment on attacks and generous i-framesStamina only used for dodges and specials, you can attack non-stopBig interconnected world DS1-style full of shortcuts and fun explorationEnemies telegraph attacks very clearlyActual story and actual ending that you cant understand without VaatiVidyaHard difficulty feels just right without farming expAlmost no penalty on deathLooks nice and have very cool fresh settingFinal boss is not a giant laser blob that spam projectiles and runs from you for 20 minutesCons:Some important upgrades hidden behind walls of fluff dialogueMost exploration rewards are upgrade mats, consumables and loreQuestionable balance of active skills and mana management in generalSome minor bugs

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I've played 20+ souls-like games at this point, I can confidently say this falls into the bottom 3 of the worst I've played. The game has a good looking world and decent combat mechanics, but beyond that the rest of the game is not well constructed at all. My biggest gripe is the story and text. God is it so overdone. You typically see in souls games the lore is very scarce and mysterious, this game took the opposite approach, which is totally doable, but this game just simply didn't do it right. The amount of reading you can do in this game is astronomical, and a LOT of it is forced. And it is VERY boring. Dialog where you cant move the character or play the game is constant. Very tedious. Even the end credit scene is not skippable and drawn out in text. My biggest gripe beyond all of that is the writing and the voice acting for the main character. She is ALWAYS surprised, by everything! Literally everything she says seems like she was just put into shock! Why????? Beyond all of that the game can be enjoyable to an extent, I started skipping the dialog that I was allowed to at some point and just forced myself to finish the game given I spent money on it. I usually play through all of my souls-like games several times, I uninstalled this one immediately after beating it and will never play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Pre-release review (Spoiler free)While it is tagged/advertised as a souls-like - this game really feels nothing like it. The combat is fun and diverse, the game gives you many different weapons to choose from right from the start so you can mix and match a build that you enjoy playing with. Whether that is a spear throwing mage, or a hammer wielder that switches to daggers to quickly finish off their enemies. The world is colorful and rich with details, and every location feels different from the other. Following the main objectives, there are also many side missions that can be done in all the different regions. At the end of each main mission, you will be facing a boss and I must say I actually really liked the boss designs in this game. Especially monsters from the animal kingdom.  The bosses in this game aren't ridiculously hard and the animations are good, and that is what really spiked my interest in playing this game. As this is a pre-release review I sadly can't share too much of the story and don't want to spoil anything but overall you are playing as Hilda, a warrior set out to save the world from the Asterigos curse that was brought upon the people by the evil aphenian Eumenidies. The story isn't dragged out and all cutscenes/dialogue has voice acting, which I really like, and there are lots of written lore that can be picked up and read from your journal. Overall, I really enjoyed my time with this game and I would definitely recommend this one!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's not good at Souls-like games, I can say that having difficulty options makes this game pretty much the perfect game for newcomers in terms of difficulty. Normal feels just as difficult as it should be for someone who doesn't care about dodging every attack at just the right time or parrying in a 0.1 seconds time. The game also does away with the "3 health potion charges" mechanic, opting for a whooping TWENTY potions (again, or normal difficulty). Meaning, you can take a whole bunch more damage and be just fine. With that out of the way, the world itself is nice, not the most varied one, but with a game that takes place mostly in a city, you can't really expect anything too crazy. The characters are pretty lame, with boring backstories and stories that might start interesting but ended up causing me to roll my eyes so far back that I could almost see the insides of my brain rotting....and the dialogue is really cringy at times...The combat isn't that great, it works really well against some smaller, humanoid enemies, but it becomes frustrating against other kinds that aren't so easy to read. Fortunately, you also have some magic at your side and the ability to fight from distance. There are only 4 item slots to mess with (not counting the weapons), and some of them are interesting, but they're given to you way too late into the game to make much of a difference.Some of the talents are nice, but some are just bad or boring,or just don't fit many playstyles. Like, if you go for a more damage focused character, you won't have as much "mana" and "mana generation", so having access to 10-20 spells doesn't help, since you're so limited in what you can do, and there are some that are clearly better than others in all but some very specific situations. Overall, a decent game to buy on a sale, and good for someone who wants to try a souls-like game that's on the "manageable" side, but a bad story and many lame characters make it impossible to recommend buying at a full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game made with love. I'm so chuffed I took a chance on it after coming across the title. It is a beautifully balanced action adventure with Dark Souls styling - a growing favourite genre of mine, the Souls-lite ;P Many aspects of it reminded me of 'Ashen', but the endearing character of Hilda as lead heroine (what a stellar protagonist) easily launched the story and the gameplay into it's own uniqueness. The combat is engaging and punchy; shield combat is particularly satisfying - I would recommend playing the game on Hard/Challenge difficulty to truly make it shine (I do hope in a sequel that the extra risk might yield greater rewards as well, instead of mere stat alterations).The world, which encourages environmental exploration and is a pleasure to discover, the lore, the narrative, the art, the design, ambience, these were all unexpected masterpieces presented in this game and of a calibre unexpected when first considering the title. The only little flaws for me were some odd bits of dialogue and a few exchanges that seemed out of place, or more precisely, out of character, and some pieces of lore (that went on for pages) broke the pace of exploration a bit too much. Otherwise, this game is a triumph of its genre and expresses an incredible talent of a passionate indie? development team. I hope Asterigos sells well. I hope the studio makes a sequel. I cannot wait to play their sequel! This has become one of my all-time favourite titles. Remarkable. Thank you for your art.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is like many say a not really a soulslike, I want to start with that. The game is good the story is quite more direct and the gameplay has many similarities with the genre but the game is far easier. Yes you can still die but the times I did was because I got thrown off a cliff in an already tight space.Performance is good, I played at 3440x1440 (21:9) all the way and while I had to make a quick fix for the fov, I played at 120 fps all the time. Yes I had some stutters when loading the game but it would recover a few seconds later and stay strong the rest of my play sessions.Now, gameplay. Yes it has soulslike elements but the game can be abused with the save system so the penalties are avoided but the penalties are usually so small that is not really an issue. I finished the game on easy and I still had a bit of challenge as I decided to finish the game not going above level 20 (you have to find an item hidden in a chest in the shelter for this to be an option). Most bosses are fairly easy at least the main ones, I only went for 1 optional and I didn't do it on purpose.The game has a pretty impressive skill tree that you can reset to work better with the weapons you like the most. I only used the shield sword as main and daggers as secondary. Both main and secondary can be used at the same time for combos and use special skills to unlock in the trees making your fighting style feel good although combos are pretty simple.Do I recommend it? yes. The story and the aesthetics made me stay, the dialogue is sometimes week but in general is a pretty good experience for the value. It has plenty of content and the difficulty can be increased for those more skilled in the genre. But please don't expect a full soulslike experience as is more of a hack n' slash game with soulslike elements.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a competently made souls-like clone that lacks some things to make it great. I had fun playing it but it could have been so much better. The exploration gameplay is great - the whole map is interconnected and is really interesting to explore and see different types of zones. No demerits here.The combat is a mixed bag. Out of the 6 available weapons, I used the Spear and the Staff, and they made combat a complete joke even on max difficulty. The only stuff I slightly struggled with were the optional 'endgame' bosses that spawn right before the end of the game. The staff lets you just artillery strike enemies from half a map away and they can barely do anything about it. It doesn't work well on bosses as they tend to have quick gap-closer abilities, but for bosses you have a spear, which has a parry ability, that lets you nullify any damage from an attack, gives you a very strong counter-attack and has a chance to stagger your target. And you're heavily incentivized to pick two weapons and stick with them to the end of the game, since you'll be putting your trait points into weapon abilties, and putting your crafting materials in improving those specific weapons. Sure there are options to re-spec and to farm more reagents, but they are time-consuming and annoying.That said, the combat is still pretty enjoyable. I would have preferred it leaned in more on using more than the two weapons you pick for variety's sake, but even just using the two, I was satisfied with it throughout.The story is ... eh. It is waaay, waaaay, waaaaay too wordy. There are dialogue trees inside dialogue trees inside dialogue trees for pretty much any major NPC about the most minute uninteresting unimportant crap. I wasn't intrigued, I wasn't hooked, I didn't care. There are a few interesting character designs, but they end up standing still and doing nothing the whole game.Overall, it's still more positives than negatives and the negatives are tolerable and didn't stop me enjoying my time with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is incredibly fun and really sucks you in. It is a Souls-Like for sure with the stamina meter, roll/dodge, dying and reviving at a "bonfire" while losing some currency. BUT it is way more forgiving, the level progression is not linked to the currency you collect and with the game providing all the weapons at the start for you to choose two to play with at anytime you don't need to worry about gearing out after halfway through the game for your play style. The Combat is really fun, as you level through different weapon trees it will unlock different attacks/patterns and abilities that change the flow of you attacks. Also, the different enemies and types of attack patterns between all the regions didn't leave me wanting anymore, I had fun fighting everything. The only draw back to the combat I have is there is not way to check the weaknesses (elemental) for each enemy, causing me to do a lot of attacking, run away, swap element, attacking and again and comparing the numbers. Other than that I had fun with the combat and enjoyed every special animation done. The story was really great as well, I enjoyed that certain outcomes and decisions made throughout the story that you may seem insignificant at the time really does change the outcome of certain situations. The main story will have you going through each of the area thoroughly as you progress, and there are several side mission you stumble upon across that way. My main gripe with the side mission is there is no way to track them so if you don't pay attention and do it right away you'll probably forget. Some of the side missions are story-line based as well to where instead of going and doing the boss of that region you have to back track to the beginning of the region to drop something off then go back through the whole region to fight the boss. Overall I give the game a 8/10, Solid combat, great story, forgiving enough to not make your blood boil, but hard enough to make you have to take a few of the bosses a couple tries. The main downside I had with this game is that you don't unlock the teleport feature between the "bonfires" early enough in my eyes. Forcing to run through so many different zones again and again to get back to where I left off for first 10 hours of the game was monotonous.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a review, these are my first impressions of the first 7 or so hours of the game plus additional time spent replaying older parts. I have a video talking about the game here for those who prefer the format: The game is estimated to be 30-40 hours in length. This is also based on a pre-release version of the game.You're probably looking at this game and thinking "oh Jesus, ANOTHER souls-like RPG with a unique setting?" but this one is good, quite good. In fact, there's a lot more to it than just that. While the pacing, enemy and level design, boss design, and world-building are very similar to a souls game, the game's combat attempts to be a much more fast-paced character-action affair.  Think Devil May Cry or Bayonetta but without the insane combos. Your attacks are fluid and fast so there's more focus on dodging and dancing around your target while constantly keeping up attacks. You have all kinds of special moves to use in combat that are flashy and fun to make up for the lack of a deeper combo system ala Dynasty Warriors or Senran Kagura. The one thing the developers really nailed here is execution. The controls are smooth, and the animations and transitions between attacks are slick. It genuinely feels like the developers had someone on their team who was some kind of character-action guru telling them what to do. It's as if Hideki Kamiya was staring right into the programmers' eyes, judgingly, making sure that everything was where it should be. I've seen AAA games screw this element up horrifically and yet this newer studio with a AA publisher does it perfectly.The question is does it hold up for the 30-40 hours you'll be playing? I have over 6 hours into a save (the rest was spent replaying older areas) and I will say that while I enjoy the combat, I am cautious about recommending it. The big fundamental problem with adding a fast-paced traditional character action game to a slower, more methodical souls-like RPG is that they kind of clash as you'd expect. You can't be styling on enemies and throwing them in the air to do a thousand combos on them in a game that is paced like souls. So instead, you have to remove those combos to make the game flow a bit better in terms of pacing since this is a non-linear game. The problem is that Asterigos can get weighed down by the need to grind as you'll only be given a small choice of weapons from the start of the game and you'll be carrying them (for me, 7 hours) for a while, possibly the entire game. This means you'll be using similar move sets most of the game and in the case of this game: you have to grind to keep more than two of them viable to use at once. There are affinities that give you magic damage but they don't change how the weapons work. For example, the fire weapon affinity doesn't let you drop flames as you roll-attack around with the spear. Once again, I need to draw your attention back to the controls. If this game didn't have excellent technical systems regarding the controls and general fluidity, I would not be talking this game up so well in that first paragraph.As for the other parts... The story is alright, the setting has Greek-Roman-inspired elements but it doesn't feel like that all the time, feels like a mix of other stuff. Would've liked them to stick to the Greek theme more. Some of the vistas and backgrounds look genuinely amazing. Performance is mixed. This game ran really well for me on an older 1070ti but after switching to a 6800xt I'm having some performance problems on the exact same settings, mainly due to a hitching related to when the game loads stuff in the background. The music is really pleasant to listen to at times, sometimes excellent. Sound mixing is good too on headphones. The story and voice acting are just sorta there. It's a bit of an info dump near the start of the game and the motivations are sound for the characters and there is a bit of a mystery to unravel I really like the narrative setup for each district you'll be killing stuff in. But overall, it's not why you play it and you'll only get invested because of your playtime, not the characters themselves. You play it for the level design and to fight enemies and thankfully, at least for the first 7 hours, that has been really fun. But if you're a souls veteran I do recommend you put the game at the highest difficulty. Medium/adventure difficulty I found to be almost boring. After 2 hours of play, I restarted the game and found even more secrets in the first area. You can change the difficulty at any time in the options menu within a loaded save though, which is nice. I wouldn't call it a "more accessible" souls game due to it being very different in many respects (mainly the combat) but if you don't like some of the more punishing parts of souls, such as the actual currency/experience system, you'll be happy to know that you don't lose potential experience points when you die, so your progress never feels wasted. You do lose 10 percent of your cash and you can't get that back after each death though.I do think this is a game to throw on your wish list at the very least or buy on sale or even buy right now if you're really aching for another souls game to play before we get more stuff from Elden Ring if the first 7 hours are anything to go by. This is one of those games where I feel the execution of the game is better than its own concept. Please read other write-ups on the game and reviews, don't just use mine though. _childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars - A Souls-lite with plenty Rough Edges that has its shining momentsIn Asterigos, the combat shines with a diverse range of skills and engaging fights against various enemies and bosses. Quest Log Issues: The journal lacks practicality, focusing more on miscellaneous thoughts.    Typos and Grammar: Numerous errors in dialogue and text. Inconsistent Difficulty: Boss fights vary widely in difficulty and not in the fun way and some enemy as well ( not sure how is on other difficulty finished the game on the hardest and felt very unbalanced)Conclusion:Asterigos offers an somehow enjoyable souls-like experience in a unique fantasy world. _childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the stars is an action-adventure soulslike with great resemblances to God of War, Hellblade & ofc Dark Souls. For an indie game it surely exceeds expectations with its beautiful graphics & animations, bonna fine cinematics, gorgeous combat & pacing,its mesmerizing neo-classical OST & generally great attention to small details.With all that being said, it still has a few issues, bugs & peculiar direction choices but nothing game breaking.It can feel both quite challenging & an easy going breeze & I shall explain further below why.Story follows Hilda, a ginger female warrior who's after finding her dad who went missing on one of his expeditions. Things get twisted when she reaches the city of Aspes, in which she learns about strange political schemes and that her dad has a part in all that.While generic it has a fine pace but it's definitely not its strongest points. The world is semi-open with few linear areas, but everything being quite explorable & interesting with a dozen of secrets areas. You collect a plethora of notes & lots of echoes, which are magical holograms of the past, to learn parts of it. There is voice acting which is mediocre imo & occasionally the dialogues are overwhelmingly long with not so much concept.Combat wise, it plays like a mixed soulslike hack'n'slasher. You start almost immediately with 6 different weapons, each having its own combo & one special ability & further down you choose between the 4 elements to magically boost your weapons. This is where the cheese strats start, and with few trial & error, you can find ways to progress the game while challenging yourself or easily destroy anything that stands your way. For example, while you have a dodge button, it's much better using the dagger weaponswhich have an invisible dash that covers triple the dodge distance and have better I-frames. One weird thing though that should be mentioned, is that running, dodging & using special abilities use your stamina bar, but attacking doesn't (!?) Which means you can spam endlessly while using the stamina required abilities quite often since it also regenerates while attacking. Trash mobs are easy to deal with & half of them being battle sponges. Bosses on the other hand are quite excellent, with great attack patterns & phases.There is also a noteworthy talent tree, which you can try various builds as you can re-spec with the use of a consumable item at any time.Now, regarding the cons, bugs & peculiar direction choices that I mentioned above. While a soulsike with the classic "bonfire" system, unlike in other similar games,on Asterigos you immediately lose a percentage of your collected "souls" each time you die. But... it has an manual save/load system,which you can cheese to not lose used items or souls on death, further talent point testing etc. Locking on enemies while outnumbered doesnt always feel good, since you get dead angles much more than you'd expect, getting in corner when fightingn gets you stucked & bodyblocked. Game has a jump button but it's the same key as the dodge one, with the difference beingthat you can jump while sprinting and dodge while not, making it hard to use if needed while in combat. Some platforms and areas that seem reachable ain't,you can jump and grab ledges but not ladders and you can get blocked by tiny object that you'd normally step over. Pressing escape to change options doesn't pause the gamebut it does when hitting tab to change your weapons, level up or read your Journal.Also collecting stuff while enemies are nearby, locks you into dialogue or whatever the collectible has to offer but the enemies are free to hit & kill youduring that time. In few occasions I also couldn't collect stuff for unknown reasons until I made a circle around doing nothing & returning to it.All in all, Asterigos might not be perfect but it's surely above decent, exploration is neat & rewarding, combat is fantastic, the overallfeel is cozy & it keeps you in its own way in wanting to play & progress further. For me it's a solid 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a great game.It excels in story, gameplay, and atmosphere, having a well-put together soundtrack, well-developed bosses, and enemies and skill trees that are constantly providing new mechanics to the game. Legitimately, almost every single skill point you use WILL meaningfully alter combat, providing new combos, charge attacks, and minor mechanics at every opportunity. The weapons are also varied, each with their own distinctive special abilities, and every enemy has different attacks and ways of dealing with them.I truly loved this game. The experience was slightly hampered by a few minor bugs, but I trust the devs will address them in the future. The game, coming from a Chinese studio, is also very well-translated. There are minor grammatical errors here and there, but the vast majority of the game's dialogue (which is well-voiced) and lore findings are well-written and completely understandable.It's very clear that the developers put a lot of passion into their game, ensuring the entirety of it was well-fleshed out. The design and stories of all the areas and characters are also well-developed, and they dont skimp out on giving backstory to even the bosses. In some spots the smaller AA budget is noticeable, such as some awkward animations for idle characters when they're talking and a lot of non-important dialogue being unvoiced, but the animations for all of the enemies and for combat sequences hold up, as well as the existing voice acting.Whatever the devs make next, I very much look forward to playing, and I'm glad we can still get nice, well-made AA games like this with plenty of heart put into them. The game pulled at my heartstrings, tested my skill, and wowed me with gameplay variety.

_childDocuments_.review: is done and dusted. This is a pretty honest Soulsborne experience, albeit a lot more colorful, with a lot more dialogue and a full story, and generally easier gameplay overall. In other words, Souls vets will enjoy it, but people new to the genre will also find it to be very approachable.Combat is quite fluid, with a fair amount of special moves and such. The areas can definitely be confusing and there is are no maps to consult, so you’ll be going off of memory, which is fine once you unlock fast travel. Until then, you’ll probably feel lost and wander for a bit. If there is a sequel, a map is thing I'd definitely include. The game does reward exploration. There is a bonfire system in the form of teleporters, and there is a central hub where you can upgrade gear, buy stuff, advance quests, get new missions, and so on. Actual leveling can be done anywhere, and includes an ability node system centered around your weapons.Speaking of weapons, you basically summon them from a magic bracer you wear, and although you can upgrade them in various ways, you get all the weapons in the tutorial section. What you can find or craft/buy are trinkets (buffs), materials and consumables. You also don’t leave “souls” on the ground when you die, although you do pay a souls penalty when you are resurrected.Anyway, I didn’t do all the side quests and it took me about 24 hours to do what side quests I did finish plus the main story. There are a lot of optional bosses as well. All in all, there is quite a bit of game here, and I expect you could easily add another 10-20 hours if you’re planning to do all the content. You will also have to play twice to get all the cheevos, and my recommendation would be to use a guide for your second run as the eight (out of ten possible) conditions you need to meet to get one of the endings are very specific and easy to mess up.Btw, I played this exclusively on the Steam Deck. It was a fantastic game for the system. Which reminds me: the graphics were stellar and the voice acting, of which there is a lot, was also very well done. The protagonist, although not voiced by Ashly Burch, sounds a lot like her, and if you’ve played either Horizon game, you could be forgiven for thinking of Aloy as you listen to the dialogue lol.*I did receive a review key from tinyBuild pre release. Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I Wanna See More of This PleaseIt’s been quite some time since I’ve been doodling around the Souls series. I’ve played a variety of games you could call the infamous “soulslike,” or games that have mechanics and elements inspired by the Souls series, though none from From Software actually. One such game is Asterigos: Curse of Stars.To me, Asterigos came at a time when Greek mythology was flourishing in pop culture, as it does every now and then. It released just a few years after Ubisoft made a fortune with Assassin’s Creed Odyssey and Immortals Fenyx Rising, the great yet often overlooked gem. I think this game rode that same wave of popularity. Without that push, maybe Asterigos wouldn’t even exist. But the thing is, I like Greek mythology. I’m interested in it. I played and enjoyed both of those earlier titles, so when I saw this, my interest lit up immediately.Asterigos has a lot of content to offer. Its story goes deep into its own web, and there’s plenty to uncover. Exploring the world and its secrets feels rewarding, and that’s one of the game’s strengths. Even though it’s set against the backdrop of Greek mythology, it’s surprisingly original—it avoids the usual tropes like gods constantly meddling in human affairs or overusing famous mythological creatures. Instead, it carves its own path, with an original story that stands apart from typical mythological renditions.There’s a certain charm to being a kind of hidden indie gem. Sure, it’s a bit underdeveloped in places—most of the text isn’t voice-acted, the cutscenes are few and far between, and lip-syncing is practically nonexistent. But all these things are forgivable here. That high-budget polish isn’t the point. Think of it as Assassin’s Creed Odyssey mixed with Dark Souls, with a dash of Breath of the Wild thrown in for good measure, all for a fraction of the cost.That said, there’s room for improvement. Hilda, the protagonist, is a bit of a disappointment. She’s the lead, but she feels more like a plot device than a fully realized character. Her actions, her attitude, and the way she views the world all serve to push the story forward, but she doesn’t feel like she’s growing or evolving in a meaningful way. Every other character in the game has a complex backstory or some depth to them, but hers? It’s the oldest cliché in the book: the perfect daughter seeking her father’s approval. She has no real flaws. I mean, is being too altruistic supposed to count as a flaw? It feels like the writing here, much like other parts of the game, is a bit underdeveloped.The visuals in Asterigos are very Disney-like—bright, colorful, and almost whimsical—which isn’t exactly my cup of tea, but I’ll admit it works here. There’s something welcoming about it. Despite the game being centered around fighting against authoritarianism, with gameplay focusing on tough, hard-hitting combat, the visuals are lighthearted and comforting. It kept me wanting to play more. If the game had gone for a darker fantasy atmosphere, maybe I would’ve had to step away from it more often. That’s just a guess, though.Now, let’s talk about combat. It’s fun, well-designed, and full of interesting mechanics, but here’s the thing: it lacks that “ahh” moment—that flash of brilliance that makes it truly stand out. It’s solid, but it’s missing that extra spark that would make it rise above the crowd of other soulslikes. It’s good, but not groundbreaking.As for my final thoughts: I like the game. I had fun, and I’d recommend it to anyone who’s looking for a solid action RPG with a unique take on Greek mythology. It may not be perfect, but it’s a charming, enjoyable experience. Asterigos: Curse of Stars gets a 7 out of 10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a phenomenal game, absolutely blew my expectations out of the water. For starters, and from the very get go, the combat is insanely good. Its super responsive, feels really impactful and is just a lot of fun. You start with a sword and shield during the "tutorial" phase of the game but after about 5 minutes you unlock the entire arsenal. You have two active slots that determine your left and right click attacks, you equip your weapon of choice in either slot and can create chaining combos between both weapons...for me, I played the entire game with spear and sword/shield but used the spear most of the time as the reach and its ability to parry was extremely satisfying. Each weapon has a special ability, such as the spears parry, shield block and so on, I dunno, I didn't really bother with the other weapons honestly so I can't say much about those. You don't collect new weapons as you play through the game but you can upgrade the ones you have and learn passive and active abilities that improve how the weapons work and increases their damage output.There are a few features in this that would probably have you consider it a 'Souls-lite', such as dying that causes everything to respawn, conduits (bonfires) that you can rest at and later on learn to teleport between, ambushes, secrets, hard hitting enemies, bosses, secret bosses, shortcuts and that all too familiar eerie sound you get while running around. There are also these sludge monsters that hide in certain chests that do insane damage to you, but are somewhat easier to deal with than your typical mimic. These are a few of the staple features, but honestly, it still feels like more of an adventure RPG that borrows said features due to how popular they seem to be...but don't let that stuff scare you off, it isn't anywhere near as hard as a souls type game and comes with a setting to change difficulty if its too hard and you just want to enjoy game at an easy pace, or focus more on the story.Speaking of story, there is a LOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOT of exposition in Asterigos, tonnes of readable lore and about a million dialogue options for just about everyone you meet, so if you're into reading lore or learning about ♥♥♥♥, then this is the game for you. For me, after about 3 or 4 hours, I got burnt out on reading the over 9000 lines of dialogue between the action and just started skipping huge chunks of it...sometimes I can get into it, other times I can't be too bothered. I was definitely playing it more for the action myself. I don't really feel like it detracted from the experience and most of the time I was still able to figure out what to do if I payed a little attention during gold text dialogue options, or just did a little googling since I was trying to do as many side quests as possible.Voice acting is pretty top notch, some really good work put in, though not everything is voice acted, only major plot points or gold dialogue options. Big props to the VA guys for this one!The world is one big seamless playground where all the areas are interconnected with no loading times or transitions, but you can only get to later areas after certain points and there's no way to skip areas, no hidden passageways, its all quite methodical in its execution. I have to say as well, the world is really well designed, super interesting to run around in and discover new stuff.In terms of the visuals, it follows a more 'cartoon-ish' art style but still looks fantastic, from the quality of the texture work, to the architecture and beyond. It's also worth noting that the animation work is top tier and only makes the things like running around and more importantly, the combat, so much more impactful and exciting. chaining combos between weapons looks amazing and the movements of active abilities are just...chefs kiss.100% worth a play through, and a lot longer than I thought it would be. I went in with a certain expectation and was given something even better. There's apparently DLC on the way too so i'm super happy i'll get to come back and play more in the future.

I didn't get attached to any of the characters, their motivation seemed kind of meh. Verdict - get it on Sale if you are looking for a souls-like game friendly to casual players (yes, Game Difficulty is adjustable and graphics is pretty cartoonish).

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a really charming game. The art direction for this game is really outstanding, and there's a level of attention to detail that you don't see too often in other games. All this while the game is very appealing to look at.The combat is fine, it's not anything groundbreaking but they let you pick two weapons that you can use at the same time out of a total of six. There's a skill tree where you can unlock skills for your weapons, and perks that give you bonuses whilst at the same time giving you a negative effect. There's also different elements for your weapons and they're supposedly more effective towards certains enemies, although the game never makes it clear which enemies are weak to what, and you have to guide yourself a bit through gut feelings. There's a fair amount of bosses, but they vary in difficulty and should be looked at as a way to finish you journey through an area. They're cool at least.The story is a highlight, but it can also be a turnoff. It's one of those stories where you're dropped in the middle of everything and only get fed droplets of information as you progress, and understand more as you get further into the game. It's a good story, but the problem is that it can be very confusing to follow because the details of the story are told through items that let you listen to conversations from the past, but they're just figures talking to each other, there's no cutscenes or anything to follow and the events you're seeing can be from 15 minutes or a 1000 years ago. This is all made worse by the fact that the game a lot times doesn't take into consideration what you know/ have seen and what you don't know. You can be saying you have no idea what something is in one dialogue, and explaining it thoroughly in the next. Sometimes characters will talk about something that you should've seen already but you're just left confused as to whether you've forgotten something or it really is just the game not knowing what you've seen (mostly the latter). This game is rather cutscene shy, they would've made this game a lot better, but I'm guessing that the lack of cutscenes were just a limitation. At least your character keeps track of what happens through her diary with cute drawings and short explanations. The lore of this game is quite rich, perhaps a bit too much, but you can tell that the developers wanted to create an expansive world, and in that they succeeded. There's tons of diaries/books/notes to read that all delve deeper into the details of the city you're in, and what motivated each character.The music also deserves some credit. It's really well done and the tracks are of good quality, they set the mood and are played at the right times so as to set the tone for some encounters.There's a lot of side missions in this game, and of good quality. The problem though is that keeping track of them isn't easy. The little journal you have keeps track of which side missions you have, but aside from some cryptic things your character may write, you better never stop playing this game or you'll forget what characters told you to do, because after they tell you once, they'll never say it again aside from a few instances. You also never get notified properly when you're finished with the side mission aside from getting an achievement for some missions, and when there's no more space to draw in your diary Despite being labelled a Soulslike, this game plays more like a Hack and Slash with Soulslike elements than a proper Souslike game. You still have stamina management, there's the equivalent of bonfires, you lose resources when you die, etc. One thing that is oddly Soulslike about this game that I noticed midway through and haven't really seen anyone comment about it, is that the game's structure is pratically identical to that of Dark Souls 1. Allow me to explain:This doesn't detract from the game in any way, but it's something that I couldn't help but notice.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale, my overall review is like 6/10.Good things are the art, ideas, certain story elements, and some designs. Honestly I have more bad things about the game to say than good. But that's because the good things are just normal average things. I can't justify saying the game is terrible though. First off this is not really a souls like. It's more like God of War, you have set weapons that determine your play-style. There are "bonfires" but they practically do nothing except act as checkpoints and you cant even fast travel with them until a certain point. I could not see why they decided on that. The combat is fine though a bit sticky at first. The real issue is the enemy AI is very bad. You almost never die because the enemies attack like once and then stare at you for 20 seconds. So if you die it's because the game baits you into being careless and just getting hit when the enemy actually does something. And there's some weird stunlock if you do get hit. Most stuff dies in about 3 hits though, and I played on the hardest difficulty. There are balancing issues in my opinion. Certain weapons are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in comparison to others. The staff is the only ranged weapon really and it's damage is massive. The bracelets are easily the worst weapon which sucks because i thought they were cool. You could make it work but it's way harder to use. Also you can stack multiple DOT skills and kill bosses in 5 seconds. The story should have been good but it just felt like something was missing. They introduce characters for the first time and pretend you know who it is already. This isn't a problem, however, I found myself more interested in the events that were not present in the game rather than the main plot. About halfway through I just started to skip all the dialogue because it was so boring. And most of the lore you have to read so I did not. The main character becomes very annoying the longer you play. It's like a ps2 game I would've had. Not great but fun enough. I hope the devs learn and improve on their next project.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an indie Souls-like/action RPG. Graphics are pretty basic but there are some great looking environments. There is some kind of story here but the dialog goes on for way too long and it's not particularly interesting.What it is good at is being a good entry point to the Souls-like genre. It has a difficulty setting. Attacks cost no stamina. You can hold up to 20 healing potions at a time and nearly every enemy drops one. You keep your stardust (souls) when you die and you don't have to worry about returning to your corpse. Enemies only respawn when you rest at a waypoint but to be honest there is no need to rest as it only fills your health bar. You could play the entire game without resting and respawning enemies. There are a lot of collectables and secrets here. A bunch of optional bosses with their own achievements. Overall, a lot of content if your looking to 100% a game. With that in mind, full price isn't too bad. It's well worth it on sale for a nice breezy run through for Souls veterans

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game! Story, lore, characters, environment and graphics are all beautifully done. There are incentives to play this game several times. Different weapons with their respective skills and perks offer so many possibilities. For example, I always like to play a mage character in these games, but there are no explicit spells here. However, one of the weapons is staff and using it feels like casting spells. Dodging feels incredibly satisfying and is spot on. Different elements further enhance combat. _childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for a while. And as as soulslike fan I really tried to enjoy it. But after only 3 hours playing on "epic" difficulty I find this game incredibly underwhelming.First thing you will notice when starting the game is the clunky controls. Man, this really feels like controlling a character from the N64 era. The default walking animation is so abysmally synced. While doing one step the character travels the distance of 3 steps for example making it just look really weird all the time.Followed by terrible hitboxes. Right in the tutorial area for example there is a small canyon with a tiny enemy blocking the way. Your character should be able to pass it on both sides easily, yet it blockes the whole passage.The most important thing in a soulslike is the enemy / camera lock mechanic - which basically does not work in this game. To make it work you have to perfectly aim on the enemy with your character, otherwise it won't lock on the enemy. In most souls like games when an enemy comes from behind, you just press the camera lock, to turn around and fight it. Here you click it 20 times while rotating the camera without being able to lock onto it. SO basically in 95% of all encounters you just attack enemies randomly without the camera lock. You can't even lock an enemy right in front of you just because it walks up the stairs. Terrible.Next terrible flaw is having to press the heal button for something like 0,5 - 1,5sec before triggering the heal. I don't know who thought of that but healing in a soulslike should be an easy task. Here you have to remove your finger from the trigger, and risk being hit by not being able to control your character, only to realize that the 3 or 4 attempts of hitting the heal button didn't work and you have to try again and again. Why?Not being able to hit multiple enemies which huge swings while they stand next to each other randomly, also confuses me.dashed into the quintus area with the 3 robbers... got killed by them during dialoque animation not being able to move... I found the storytelling so boring and forced that I started skipping dialogues right after the tutorial area.So yeah - finished 2 1/2 areas after 3 hours - which I did not enjoy exploring - like at all.By the way. In the windows task bar the game is misspelled "Asteriogos" while running.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the stars at first glance appears to be a game that would struggle to make its mark in the plethora of titles in the action RPG genre. However there are modest improvements over its peers that I think should be lauded in its genre and other story-linear games. Choices or lack thereof, matter. I am sure everyone has seen that near every story focused game has this claim, however Asterigos early on examines your willingness to follow the easy and direct solution without question as is usual in combat focused titles. Characters will criticise your willingness to blindly follow the most obvious path ahead. It's not entirely groundbreaking stuff, but it is presented in a way that you may scrutinise how you may or may not be accustomed to the typical questing system of go to area A, kill all enemies and return to quest giver B without regarding any consequence or purpose except to simply proceed. Again nothing crazy, it's a hack and slash game but it shows that the developers attempted for it to be more than just what its genre defines. The game's combat system is modestly expansive and designed so the player can choose early what weapons and set ups they prefer with a mix of skills that combine harmoniously. For example skills can combo with your basic move-set, weapon ability, a quick swap between two allocated weapons and everything in between. Ultimately you could spam the same same actions and make your way through the game, but ultimately the fun comes pulling off attack with varied move-sets, kinda like a fighting game. Again nothing super ground breaking but it (a smaller and focused title) does go beyond what most AAA games in the genre attempt. The game is stylised to where it can be compared to Fenyx Rising but that's not necessarily a bad thing, it's a very pretty game. The voice acting is not always present but it is excusable for a AA title, and what's there, is of a high standard. It won't win GOTY or compete with the big guns and could use some polish, but with what it attempts to accomplish, it (in my opinion) shows that it was made with more introspection than many other games with larger budgets and dev teams behind them.

_childDocuments_.review: Ape-like men and delicate women populate this Roman and Greek mythology inspired... wait that can't be right. Roman and Greek? That's what the tagline says... Maybe in the loosest of senses. It is more accurate to say that its a city of people cosplaying Roman elements who didn't look up what an archon is and then imported templars from the medieval period and... Look, if you're going to to publicly peg your setting to a particular inspiration, get it right. Otherwise, just let your setting be. The audience is smart enough to figure it out if or when it matters.Anyhow, your clearly Celtic inspired Murder Waif will somehow tote around six sets of weapons as she is rightfully called a child by everyone even as they rely on her martial prowess... even though most are immortals who apparently never bothered learning to use a sword in the last thousand years... *sigh* Embrace being an elite child soldier who was left behind by her father and whom complete strangers will use to further their agendas by sending you into danger!On this journey, you'll be aided by a fox smith with noodle arms named Vulcan, whose connection to Roman mythology is that vulpine and Vulcan have the same prefix. See? Totally related. What's that? The actual Latin roots are vulpes and vulcanus, two completely unrelated words? Don't tell the writers that! Also don't mention that this game includes Odysseus (Grecian hero) and Minerva (Roman name for Odysseus's patron), as that may cause them to actually give their source material more than a cursory look.As implied, the writing leaves much to be desired. It comes across as U.S. high school level at best, which is to say that it is loud and obvious. The biggest failing though is how characterizations can be inconsistent. In one area Murder Waif can scream about how she's fighting to help the people oppressed by a local gang. Then in another area she screams at smiths for not respecting a guard that was bullying them when it is clear they are prisoners forced to work. I get that she's a traumatized child soldier who has been resurrected a few times and is only valued in this game for her murdering, appearance, and gullibility, which is itself enough to cause a psychotic break, but I don't believe the writers considered that when then wrote this.The game is not without bugs: My UI vanished (it came back after save and reload), and I got stuck on a wall (also fixed by save and reload). Some of the controls are needlessly strange as well: you use one key to confirm attribute choices and another to confirm talent choices, and one's a tap, while the other's a hold for... reasons? Some animations also look a tad strange, like the copious shoulder movement when running, but they are mostly solid.If you read this far you're probably wondering how I could have possibly given it a thumbs up. Well, I must admit that no matter how dumb a game might be (or at least I haven't hit my limit), I do enjoy playing a Murder Waif. On top of that, the graphics are solid, especially the environment, and the gameplay is excellent. Where It is certainly not the advertised souls-like, but it is fun and engaging. It is clear that the designers are top notch - the web of quests, particularly how they interact with each other, is great, and the level design as fabulous, particularly Styx. There are definitely features I'd like to see, like putting voice to the rest of the dialog or more unlockable outfits (folks should know by now that end game = fashion) or having sword and shield about more than the shield or an automap, but what's there is still fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant souls-like that's not very challenging (even on Challenge difficulty) compared to more usual games in the genre.Main things that make the game easier1. The healing potions are just an item you can get as a drop or buy, all without the need to rest at the checkpoint.2. When you die, you only lose a portion of your money, the experience for leveling is a separate bar and is not reduced upon death.3. The dodge is very generous with invinsibility period, and you can do it a lot of times in succession before running out of stamina.4. Weapon attacks do not consume stamina (DLC can change that). So you don't need to manage stamina when it comes to combat, you can just dodge behind an enemy, land some attacks, dodge again, rinse and repeat.Good1. You can switch between different weapons, each of which has unique skill. This allows you to pick your preferred playstyle and experiment with different combinations. Later you also receive gems which apply elemental damage to weapons and allow for even more variety. You only have those 6 weapons that you start with which might seem restrictive but in practice I think it's just enough.2. The atmosphere is a mix of bright, colorful visuals and dark themes like slavery, human torture and experimentation, exploitation of desperate people, etc.3. The level design is alright. Maps are interconnected, so you have an incentive to look around and explore. You'll find shortcuts, treasure chests and other useful loot.What could be improved1. The game relies heavily on side quests, but there is no proper journal to keep track of their progress. You have notes with some scribbles which are not particularly helpful. Even if the game wants to be a proper souls-like, the quest log would be beneficial for experience. No need to follow Dark Souls' formula too closely.2. You get the ability to teleport around halfway through the game. It could be introduced a bit earlier to cut down on running around when exploring and completing quests. You do have consumables that teleport you to the shelter or to the last used checkpoint but they only work if you need to go to shelter and back, but if you want to go to other areas you still have to run on foot.3. The game has a lot of dialogues and reading. The lore is presented through notes. Some might find it irritating and not very "soulsy". I didn't mind it that much personally.DLCDLC adds new, more challenging, boss fights. You get rewarded with materials to modify your weapons (separate from weapon upgrades of base game). Considering that combat alone is not the strongest side of the game, it's weird that the developers decided to focus on that. The balance is all over the place, some fights are manageable, others can be quite brutal.I'd suggest getting the game if you want more relaxed souls-like. Even if you don't like souls-likes, you can still give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a very fun action game that suffers from an excessively bloated story and trying just a little too hard to be like Dark Souls. For me, this is a solid buy-on-sale chill weekend game.At it's core, the game features most of the standard souls elements, high damage enemies, a focus on i-frame dodging, losing currency on death, respawning at infrequent checkpoints, resting to restore potions and respawn enemies, hidden chests, mimic chests, interconnected levels full of unlockable shortcuts, no (useful) map, rare items found by hunting small enemies that run away, an animal that trades items for other random items, a story about the slow decay of a kingdom to a mysterious curse, obtuse questlines that require specific actions or dialogue choices to get right or fail, etc., etc. Sometimes you'll feel like they ripped a chunk of an area straight out of Yharnam or the ramparts of Boletaria, or the Tower of Latria, or the Crystal Cave. However, I found moment to moment gameplay to be much less like souls and more like classic action games. The difficulty is significantly lower than the standard soulslike, but if you're new to the format, the challenge is a decent balance. Most of the time you can just hack through enemies, occasionally dodging away during the infrequent "red glow" unstaggerable attacks. The weapon system involves equipping two weapons at a time out of six options with possible chain attacks. There is an upgrade tree for weapon skills but I rarely found it worth engaging with since the standard combos made short work of enemies anyway. There is no armor system and the item inventory is scarcely used except for healing items and the odd quest item. This means your starting sword and board basic combos will last you for the entirety of the game, and tbh, that's just fine. The game is also very colorful and vibrant, which is a nice change from the usual souls gloom. There are moments where it seems to get uncharacteristically dark though which stand out as strange, particularly the Tower of Latria equivalent which is caked in blood from torture victims. Though those moments might have been more impactful if I wasn't mashing through the endless dialogue to get to the next gameplay segment. The story is told in a method so overflowing with detail it puts the Silmarillion to shame. NPCs, the very frequent diary entries, the ghost flashbacks, the grave headstone inscriptions, the man behind the door with a candle near it, none of these people will EVER stop talking. As Willaim Shakesman once said, "brevity is the soul of wit." No wit was found this day. You might think I'm exaggerating. I enjoy fantasy stories with in-depth lore, and yes I HAVE read the Silmarillion. I found myself mashing through the endless dialogue before the end of the third area. There are 20-50 notes, headstone inscriptions, graffiti markings, loose pages, etc. to find in each area, often with full page or multi-page lore dumps. All of it is the bog standard "we tried to deal with the curse, we failed." I scraped areas as clean as I could and I was still missing many notes. There is a lot of voice acting in the game and it is used very poorly. The actors do a fine job with the material, but conversations just do not flow together. Sometimes a character will obviously have the wrong voice, like the seedy merchant/info broker (Greirat wannabe) who has the voice of a whimsical old man. Important npcs have voiced dialogue for story and quest lines, but not for incidental dialogue, which is fine. However, a lot of quests are secretly hidden behind npcs you can't see because you have to knock on a random door, to be greeted with pages upon pages of unvoiced dialogue that ends with a journal update signalling that you somehow started a quest. However, the journal will not summarize the important information for you and is thus useless. Additionally, while wandering areas you will occasionally encounter enemies which you can eavesdrop upon while they talk about the local situation. However, there is no voice acting for these goons and listening will not stop them from attacking you, so it is usually better to just kill them before they can finish talking. And perhaps worst of all, story progression is gated behind periodically returning to the hub area (on foot for the most part) and listening to yet another half-hour lecture from your boss before she opens a door at the end of the area you literally just cleared.I like this game a lot. I had a lot of fun with the relatively simple hack-and-slash combat. The story delivery is just so abysmal and the Dark Souls elements are just so forced. I'd love to see a sequel where this character/game come into their own and shed the shackles of mediocre imitation.
