_childDocuments_.review: I've beaten this game twice. i don't usually go for a second run so soon but I really enjoyed my time here.It is important to note this game is not AAA. It's a very well made game but it is clearly AA and there are minor ways this makes itself known. A lot of issues I had were fixed though and these were mostly quality of life in nature. The gameplay itself is very enjoyable. It is a tad souls like, but in a much more casual friendly way. Your weapons have many more options and there is some fun in tinkering with various builds. Gameplay is smooth and reactive. Enemy variety is decent enough. The game's length is great as it doesn't wear out its welcome. It has different endings depending on some rather obscure choices which could be better, but it's not the most impactful change so you will not miss much. Bosses are decent but could use a little more kick in some cases.What I really liked was the overall aesthetic and story of the game. It has likable characters and some actual character progression for many. The MC makes mistakes but grows and learns. Initially it can feel like some of the characters giving you jobs are too harsh on you, but it all makes sense as you progress. The world has established beliefs and a culture too. _childDocuments_.review: ====1/1/23 Update====A very promising combat system, for the most part, from a future AAA developer. Heck, you could say the game is already a AAA title, in some respects. The combat is great and reminds me of Fable meets Dark Souls, minus the cool assassination (back stab) moves of Dark Souls, or the ability to stab them when they're on the ground, though, I wish it had a clean parry/ counter-attack system. Hilda, with her sword and shield, has a neat shield bash counter-attack that is completely Spartan and I love it: She draws her shield back and drives/ slams the rim of her shield into the opponent. The only frustrating element there is that the enemy has time to hit her in the middle of countering, which is pointless as counter attacks go. If all counter-attack does is make you vulnerable? Why do it? Especially if they can also hit you before you've recovered from doing it! A counter-attack should work in a way that sets you up for a clean opportunity to stun/ jar them, while dealing notable bonus/ crit damage, and even possibly serving as a finisher. As is? It's just not feasible to use.The story is well done, but the voice acting suffers and so too does the in-game dialogue/ writing. Some of the responses are riddled with throwaway lines that the NPC doesn't even need to say, or responses that don't line up and because of that I just skip past most conversation. It makes me wonder if it's just poor translating to English. On the topic of writing? I think the person who wrote the story did not write the in-game dialogue because the bits of story that are narrated by Minerva sound well done. Graphics are well balanced an clean and the art style is gorgeous and reminds me a bit of something between Fenix Rising, Fable and World of Warcraft, but no ray tracing, no native HDR... It basically has the aesthetics of what a remastered Fable might look like i.e. it's definitely not pushing any present day FX... Not even real-time lighting. Should you remove the excessive fogging effect, using r.fog=0, within engine.ini, the lighting is jacked because it relies on the fog to mask the problem of lighting and shadows. With fog removed, it's just like someone painted black in the corners where shadows would be. You seen this technique, a lot, in games like 1995's Tomb Raider and Quake. Performance on a 6900 XT is actually kind of bad. I should be getting an easy 4K 120FPS, even on consoles, with what we're seeing onscreen. It shouldn't be that much more demanding than, say, Trine 4, to be honest and therefore should even be an 8K game, yet? I can't manage over 70FPS and can't figure out what's using that much GPU. I also receive slight stutters...even with VSYNC. This is while using the latest drivers. On my laptop, which uses a 3060TI, I run the game at 1080P and it has no issues meeting my monitor's 144Hz limit, ultra settings. Performance-wise I can run Assassin's Creed - Valhalla with 30% more frames at similar resolution, but AC Valhalla is doing ALOT more and in a much larger world with high res texture.  It's just a shame the game doesn't seem have true 4K or 8K texture assets, if DVD format were still a thing? This would be a DVD-9 install game, as weighs in at about 10GB. a small 4K game, these days? Should at least be over 20-30GB.Animations are a little stuttery, like when watching distant NPC/ enemy walk, it's like 15FPS. The animations are all together floaty, especially for Hilda. I'm an immersion player and prize being able to just walk in an analogue fashion, sometimes I walk slow and sometimes moderately fast, and I use gamepad for these sort of games for that reason, but sometimes PC games will let you control your walk speed, via, mouse wheel for this reason as well. Walking really slow (just a hair of thumbstick pressure) seems okay, in terms of animation, but it's so unnaturally slow that I don't think people walk like that, unless they're afraid of what's ahead or have a medical condition. Any additional pressure to move forward results in slow motion jogging, where HIlda's steps are too tall to be considered walking. It's like they took the running animation and just slowed it down and called it walking. Basically? The faster you walk, the more hideous it looks. In fact? Even running without sprint looks odd as well, but running with sprint looks more natural, but still floaty. When you walk down stairs Hilda is about 1 foot off of the ground and when she's standing out on the grass/ dirt her feet are under the soil a lot of the times.The game tends to get congested and uses the old school "follow the path" model, where you find yourself doubling back through the same areas, crossing over/ under previous areas and paralleling the same areas. It's fine because I grew up playing games like this, but nowadays? It's also nice to at least instill a sense of open-world, with some good open-world like areas. A game like this in a scaled down version of the Elden Ring map would be perfect, as it would combine a good balance between open-world and re-visiting old areas, in order to deeper explore places you didn't have access to prior. I did love, however, the labyrinth systems, like in the aqueduct and Stella Mines/ Glittering Mines, I felt like I was playing something between Ocarina of Time and a dungeon crawler at once. Audio is definitely not a problem. There are some sweet sound FX in this game, unlike others I have heard. Ambiance and mood is definitely not the game's problem. The music is very well composed.Side quests are lacking and lack direction. Half of them are obtained by knocking on doors of people you'll never see. I have some very cryptic quests in my journal that just say something like "Treachery! Enlisting the help of gangsters (or something to that effect)!" and I have no idea what it's alluding to, where I even got, nor where I am to go. Some of them just seem like vague statements or opinions than they do something more direct, like "Otto wants me to check the lab on the second floor of Styx" or "The stranger at Black Street asked me to collect 10 starite fragments..." Something we could all understand.The biggest crux?The game lacks CUSTOMIZATION!!! You can't have an RPG without this! I was excited to see there was a trinket system...none of the trinkets show up on Hilda! They're just passive stat increases. A major trick was lost. A deeper customization system is NEEDED! If you were not fortunate enough to catch the pre-order of this game because, like many, you had't heard about it until now, you've literally lost out on 1/3 of the customization options: there are only 3 possible outfits, including her starting gear. What's more? The devs don't seem keen to throw us any free content and add to the quality of life of the base game, instead? We have to wait to pay for DLC.Further more, on the topic of appearance, I feel like her sheath (more like luggage case) is way too big and distracting for her petite build and wish they'd have just gone with a minimalist approach and just show the two primary weapons you have selected...easy peasy. Her shield can go over her sword on her back, her staff/ spear/ hammer can co-exist with her hip/ lower back placed daggers, and her sword/ staff/ spear/ hammer can all be slung on her back, either in an X figure, or in parallel (Witcher style)...literally anything is better than a Death Stranding backpack. Add to this, no hair colors, no hair styles, no dyes for clothing...literally nothing to grind for but rocks and potions.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Just finished my first playthrough on Challenge Difficulty, and it was GREAT! Gotta give the Devs props for a great action RPG game, it was a blast and I'm already starting my NG+ which offers more items and better upgraded items so there's incentive to. Keep up the good work guys!If you like Action RPG's, then this one is a great one to go with and the price is very fair for what you are getting, definitely recommend as long as you can put up with a little "Indie" feel to some of the games elements and a tad buggy at times(enemies and yourself can get knocked up into the air on an invisible platform from time to time but you can get down so not a big deal)Not finished yet but close. Great little Indie ARPG, NOT a Souls-like as this game is much easier than what Dark Souls would be, that being said if you are familiar with Souls-like games then this one will come pretty naturally to you. The beginning first few zones can feel a bit tedious while you work towards unlocking fast travel, but due to the lack there-of early in the game it incentivizes you to explore, and you WILL miss stuff your first time through. 45 hours into my playthrough and I'm STILL finding stuff I missed even very early on that I totally could have gone to if I had kept lookin for it.The combat is very fluid, the bosses and their mechanics are fun, and the world looks great, very aesthetically pleasing from the bright forest areas to the dark dingy dungeons.I'm playing on "Challenge" which is he games Hard Mode and it has been a very fair challenge I feel, again if you are familiar with Souls games then this will feel just about right to you. One Note is that on Challenge all of your resistances (both physical and elemental) are heavily reduced, this is where Challenge mode enemies get their damage from, and even a trinket that reducces damage from a source from -65 to -45 will actually make enough of a difference in your survivability.LOTS or Lore to find/read if you are interested, I've read most I've come across but some stuff is just really extra to be extra and I still don't feel like I'm missing out on the main story/plot by skipping some of it.The Quest design is made to make you think and explore, as the joural really doesn't help, it basically tells you what's happened during a Main or Side quest but never tells you if it is complete or not, nor how many steps there are to completing it, and some have different outcomes based on your actions/choices, so good luck and I hope your memory is good!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Asterigos. Gameplay overall was solid with multiple viable options when it comes to combat. Since upgrading every weapon can definitely get grindy I would recommend testing all available weapons in the early game and focus your upgrades on 2-3 weapons to get the most out of them. I played on "challenging" so if you choose an easier difficulty you maybe able to use more weapons throughout your playthrough. The general progression felt good, level ups and trinket upgrades combined into a nice power curve over the whole experience. Graphics are good, the artstyle may not be everybody's cup of tea but I liked it. One gripe I have is that animations on enemies more than half their framerate when the player puts some distance between themselves and the enemy. Most of the time sightlines are not that far out though so its not a big issue. Sound design and music are great overall, lots of themes that I enjoyed a lot and I am very happy that the soundtrack is available for purchase. The story was good, I enjoyed all the characters although it took some time to get going and to hook me. I would say if you do not like reading in games this game has quiet a lot of it and I would argue it is almost necessary to read a lot of the documents one can find to get the bigger picture about this games story and world. Not an issue for me though, I like reading a lot in games :3So overall definitely an easy recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good. It's a souls-like but with it's own refreshing take and a much more obvious story. Bosses are fun - for the most part, some are hot garbage that aim to overwhelm you with either add control, extreme RNG (much more so that the souls games) or both. *Disclaimer* This statement is directed at the non-main story bosses, which should be challenging, but not all of these ones are designed very well.The quest system needs a rework. Like most souls-like games, there is no easy way to track what you are doing (which is fine), but they attempt to provide you journal here. The journal is confusing at best and would have been better if they left it out. If they reworked it to properly track quests - because lets be honest, this is souls-like but much more forgiving, then it would probably add a nice touch to the game.Difficulty is fairly easy. Challenging (the highest you are allowed to choose on your first play through) is still much easier than a normal souls-like play through, enemies just hit much harder and have a bit more HP. Overall its worth it, I look forward to what the DLC and further game updates fix/add to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little souls-like with a great main/player character, considered world-building, interesting characters with pretty good voice work on average, decent music, and competent combat though it could use a little tightening up (and probably another usable ranged weapon other than having the staff beam as the only option). Story is pretty good if a little verbose, and feels like it has a better balance of having sad outcomes for a lot of characters/questlines while not being as outright depressing as your usual soulslikes. Size, interconnectedness, and visual variety of the areas is pretty good, and exploration freedom is decent. Definitely worth the asking price, especially with the free content like outfits and such that they gave out after release. Really hoping this gets a sequel as this has a fantastic main character/side characters (timeskip older Hilda perhaps?) and world/setting that I would love to jump back into.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos curse of the stars is a 3rd person adventure RPG about a young woman named Hilda, who has found herself in a predicament with an unlikely ally.The story of this game is extremely long and filled with lots of lore. If you are not a fan of very long dialog you will not like this game. While the main story is fully voice acted, any of the optional dialog is text only. The combat consists of the use of multiple weapons the player can choose at will from swords, spears, daggers, magic, and melee.Combat itself can sometimes feel a little clunky and I wish it flowed faster. The magic however was really fun to use and a good way to keep back some of the mobs.I see a lot of reviews comparing this to dark souls. This is no where near a dark souls experience.  Sure it has some mechanics used by dark souls such as dodge rolling and respawning of all enemies should you heal at a save fountain. But that’s it. Nothing else in this game nor the difficulty is anything near as frustrating as dark souls.I thought this game was great and was filled with tons of things to go and places to explore. There is also no map in the game. I wish there was for easier navigation but I eventually learned the different location layouts as you visit them a few times.Overall this was an outstanding game 8.5/10

On top of this I unlocked the storage 25 hours in... not sure who thought that this would be a good idea.The game is made like a metroidvania where if you unlock certain stuff you can backtrack for loot but there's no map nor a radar to help you in that backtracking and there's not even a quest tracker in any way shape or form, the ingame journal just simply sucks and doesn't help you at all.The game is super obtuse because the devs tried to copy some stuff from Souls games or any From Software games like it has a souls lite combat, obtuse quests and map design but it simply doesn't work.If you think this is like Immortals Fenyx Rising like I did, it's not but I wish it would be because that's a damn good game!Just avoid this or wait for a massive sale.

So don't let that discourage you if you're thinking about trying the game.1. Honestly I think the biggest negative is the storyline and dialogues. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: updating after 100%, upticking to 7.5/10 (after reading all the lore this time, lots of interesting stuff in there, good world building bumps this up.  Also played with more classes this time through, spear stole my heart).This game's solid.  7/10. I recommend it, but it has its problems I'll vent about here,MINOR SPOILERS FOR WEAPON PROGRESSION, NOTHING ON STORY THOUGHIts a pseudo souls-like that works well enough.  The dialogue feels really poorly translated at first, but it improves somewhat as time goes on.  If you like reading texts, you'll get a lot out of this game - the quests are voiced, but every other dialogue is just text and there's 300 or so documents to read (which I liked but it can be a lot).  Also a whole lot of in-game cutscene style lore in the form of big blue glowy balls, which are fine, but its a lot.  There's a whole lot of lore that's a bit overwhelming and I found myself skipping through a lot.  I want to do a run where I watch it all, its just a bit too much all at once, and often I think that's because its incredibly vague and a bit all over the place as you piece things together; some of that is intentionally keeping your character in the dark, some of it is the mystery your character is actively trying to uncover, and the rest is a pretty confusing backstory... its a lot of intrigue and fogginess that comes from too many angles to hold my interest all at once.If you like achievements, you can one shot this game with a second save at a critical juncture.  But then you can't level past 20 and that's a bit of a bummer.  I did it in two, the level 20 first and then a difficulty uptick for the real thing.The maps are fun once you know them but so horribly confusing at first.  Only world map is in the hub, but its decently detailed.  It feels a bit like the surge in terms of mapping confusion if that helps at all, but the world map is much more usable, at least for the city area.Quest log is absolute dogwater.  Its the worst part of the game.  It tells you what happened and nothing about where to go for sidequests.  If you go back to the last character in the chain you get nothing. So you better remember everything. I get being a souls like you want to be minimalist in some ways, but if you have this many plotthreads, at least make it a bit more navigable. Gameplay stuff:I've had no responsive or visual issues playing this game thus far.  some ranged attacks hit walls I don't agree with but nothing more severe than that.  Hitboxes seem pretty on point (though splash damage goes a bit further than animated sometimes, so dodge a bit harder than you think), iframes work as expected. I've seen other reviews complain about this stuff and I don't really get it. Classes.  There are 6, each is good in its own right, but some have things that set me off.  Here's a pointless personal ranking (to clarify it, I used Sword&Sheild primary and Magic Gauntlets as my secondary on the lv20 run and on hard I ran Spear w/ Daggers alternating with Spear (though i dropped the daggers for the hammer at the halfway mark)1. Spear (parry), throwing a spear is great, which you could do a weaker one off mana though.  Dodge attack is an aoe (one of the only two and the more effective of them). Ult is a moonlight greatsword, gotta love it. 2. Sword & Shield (Block / Shield Bash), just solid standard stuff that works well.  Ult is a boomerang shield, you have abilities where you can toss your shield and keep swinging and recall it at will.  One really nice leg-cut dash that works well to set up anime finishes to a lot of boss fights3. Staff (ADS for beam attack).  Hear me out. This one is boring af at first with just a spam thing.  This scores up high entirely on the back of unique weapon animations per enhancement, particularly in the combo finishers (which you unlock in the tier - each weapon has one to unlock that way).  The ult lets you spam that (though for some reason doesn't let you swap enhancements during the ult, which is a shame and a half and drops this one down to 3)4. Magic Gauntlets (mines).  If it wasn't for the mines this weapon would be top tier for me, they're just uninteresting and take up so much of the tree its annoying.  You get some cool magic weapons on charge atks, which I wish were a bigger part of the kit over the mines.  The skills here are great, astral knockback and the ice wall thing in particular are great add ins for most builds I used which brings this one higher). Ult is just a range extender on the combo, animations for the weapon (and the magic melee charge things) are based on the enhancement, which makes the weapon feel more versatile than it is.  Makes for a good secondary weapon for the charge swings though and the roll is the second aoe and the combo has splash at parts. 5. Daggers (dash).  I love the daggers, lots of fun. Abilities are a bit all over the place and I only stud with the tele dash (the whirlwind sounds better on paper than it performs).  Ult is good though.  Biggest gripe is the dash being a second ability instead of a roll replacement, I get the stam cost weight, but its awkward if you like to swap weapons around.  Since I had to bench them over this (basically trying to dodge a lot when not having them equipped when I wanted to alter, it was ultimately best to retire them.  Damage isn't as aggressive as you'd like and not quite as fast to make up for that during strike moments in boss fights).6. Hammer (heavy swing). Don't at me.  its a fine weapon. The grav throw thing is great. The ult is just a boring slow earthshatter thing and i just got bored of it.  Its as traditionally played as the sword and shield, but with less innovation to make it stand out, basically.  But its good for what it is and I'd imagine its many people's favorite.Respeccing is available, first by a merchant with increasing prices for each go, then by another guy later that is more specific (talents or abilities) which is nice for weapon variability as I like to switch things up. Chests overall are poorly implemented.  Way too many mimics honestly. (EDIT: originally complained about needing to double roll, spear or staff solve that, but you can just throw a dagger, I didn't really touch throwables enough playthough 1).  Chests loot is really lackluster as you have to open several to get anything and they're just passive stat bonuses.  EDIT: you do in truth get upgrade mats as well, but they are largely the same stuff that's farmable, so its pretty meh to always be that.  I know it can't have weapons, which is usually the fun stuff, but even some fancy rare trinkets or weapon skins or something would've gone a long way to making them rewardable - or just make less if you have nothing too creative to put in em).  They also follow a clear path.  Would be more fun for replay if each chest did something specific so you could focus on a build. Enemy variability is decent for a souls-like.  Compared to the likes of surge, code vein, and steel rising, you'll have much more variability here.  Each zone is pretty unique.  Some reskins but the interactions are different enough that you don't notice it much. They do have elite variants of enemies too which I always like.  Boss variability stands out well until you get to the bonus bosses and they're just reskins thrown in for fun, which is fine, but a bit of a chore for achievement hunters.TLDR: biggest problems for me are the side quest log, way too many mysterious plot lines to follow at first, no bow class, basic magic options and you usually just have fire on, chests are not rewarding enough and almost feel like they shouldn't even be there.Biggest pros are replayability, weapon variations (though not as many as I'd like, each one is really thorough), clean solid play, fair hitboxes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was almost good. However there are so many small issues that build up to make the game lose its luster.Enemies are spongy and your attacks hold no real impact. The weapons are ok, but don't feel significant. The story starts off interesting but after about 2 hours in, it's just non stop exposition and the story becomes skippable and uninteresting. The camera is odd and often messes with your view. Also, there is no map, minimap, quest markers, or quest log. I am fine without quest markers, but no quest log or mini map seemed like a bad choice.

_childDocuments_.review: If I was going to give it any accolade it would be: The game with the most savage chest mimics award :')A very good game with a fully realised world, which includes heaps of flavour text embedded in notes etc throughout each of the areas. Was expecting a short and sweet 10 hours romp, but have been pleasantly surprised by the amount of content included without there being an excessive amount of backtracking, which becomes a non-issue about a quarter of the way in.  Doesn't break new ground as far as combat goes, does what it does competently and has a decent variety of weapons with their own skill trees. Had me at breaking point with one of the bosses and another that took a few attempts. Recommend playing on the hardest setting for the best experience as its quite well balanced and feel like how it is intended to be.    Seems to have done well with awards which are justly deserved, a solid and good-looking first entry for the studio.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some good things going, the art style is unique and cool. The presentation is nice, voice acting is good and it has some pretty good ideas for combat.So why a thumbs down?Because it's just not fun. The combat is clunky and just unpleasant to engage with. You basically have 2 choices when approaching combat, you can try and use precision and time your movements to the thousandth of a second.. or you can just mash the attack button as quick as you can until you either win or die. If you like Dark Souls games and find that type of combat fun then you might enjoy this one more then I did. The game market is just full of these watered down 'souls like' games. If you're into that, just buy the cheapest one, they're all basically the same. Tired and uninteresting, this one is more of the same. Thank god for refunds!

_childDocuments_.review: ☑️Visually okay.☑️Souls-Like.☑️Combat is fluid to a degree. ☑️A hot furry NPC.❌Pretty unlikable models. ❌Feels rather slow paced / boring. ❌Story is rather boring. ❌Can't hang out with the hot furry. People will often say, yeah this or that game is similar to this game, it's how life is now'a'days. However, once I got to base camp and saw the amount of DETAIL and animation they put into the blacksmith character, I lost all interest in the game, because of the lack of detail put into everything else, was this character one of the developers sona's? Is this where all their funding went into? Why can't the rest of the game be like this? Generic, putty looking humans. Frustrating game play. _childDocuments_.review: This is a long game. There is a teleport system like other soulslikes, but you'll be what feels like a long ways in before you unlock it. Don't worry about level grinding too much, you'll get a lot later in the game. I personally recommend the spear/javelin (whatever they call it) and magic staff for main weapons, but completely up to you. I also ran with all my points into ATK only, no HP or SP buffs, which is why I ran the spear for the parry ability. Overall I'm really en joying this game and would be satisfied with a AAA price tag, so even at retail price this is a steal. I'm not a huge Dark Souls fan simply because of the difficulty, but soulslikes with a solid story are always good imo. I give it a solid 4.8/5. Would be 5/5 but takes way too long to unlock teleport imo. I may update this later as I believe I'm not even halfway done based off the amount of achievements I have left for killing certain bosses, and i have not started the DLC yet.Edit: I was probably 3/5 of the way through at review time, but the teleportation made it way faster to get things done. Since I do so much damage the boss killing was relatively quick and easy. If you go for achievements, get to level 20 then lock your level with the trinkets it gives you. You can 100% the game with only one playthrough. Best advice I have is thoroughly explore, but don't waste time killing every single enemy, they aren't worth your time if you're going for quick playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, the combat is really fun. I can tell a lot of love went into this game and that's awesome. The Disney aesthetic was a bit off putting / out of place at points though and the game had 2 of my biggest pet peeves in gaming:1. Subtitles that can't be turned off.2. Cutscene audio that isn't music put through the music channel. This means if you turn off the music you lose most of your cutscene audio. Note that I only turned off the music because it got really loud during conversations, making them hard to hear. The music itself isn't bad at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game actually took longer than I expected from an indie dev.The different weapon types are which tailors the game to your suiting which is great and all but I just wish you could have acquired a few more after progressing the game as an incentive to keep more players playing. Same goes for cosmetics.I would say the strongest suit this game has which makes it stand out is how they present the story, the setting, characters in the game.The  seems basic at first but the more you dive deeper into the game, the more unfold. Theres even a deeper lore to go with it if you do the side quests. To add more detail to that, you have choices that go with some of the quests that can change how the quest ends.The  goes hard. They stuck well with the theme and did a great job enfusing the map layout to them. My only problem is that later into the game, some of the maps are unnecessarily spacious but I suppose it was a give and take since some of the architecture of the game is supposed to be huge.Each  in the game are unique and lovable. The level of design for characters is so well do  I found  cringe. The characters are that diverse. Youll want to keep playing the game as soon as you realize your actually populating the hub with each quest done.Just a note. In comparison to any game it would fall near Darksiders II with these similarities:- same style story telling - cut scenes- a select number of weapons with each a skill treeYes its still has the souls-like mix into it, but after finishing the game it I realized how nostalgic it plays rather than new.

_childDocuments_.review: A Soulslike where you play a young woman who journeys to a cursed city to find out what happened to her legion and her father. It has a web-based advancement system similar to something like Path of Exile (though not as elaborate), and a swappable armory of weapons you can choose from with different abilities - sword and shield, dual daggers, hammer, staff, etc. This is one of those games where after playing to the next bonfire over the course of a week, I didn't have any big problems with the game, but just found it kind of dull. In the end the reason I stopped playing is because I just couldn't find any reasons to keep playing. If you're a big fan of the genre maybe give it a look.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better Games I played this year!The world:The graphics are really nice, the world is beautiful and especially the different places you can visit are stunning. Big greek buildings, caves full of crystals or just the wild forrest, you really feel beeing in these areas. The main character is really cute, red hair and green eyes really suits the model and the weapons have really nice animations.The story:The story is alright to quite nice, depends if you try to get involved. Many informations are given by echos or papers so you can discover the story piece by piece. The greek setting and the fantasy aspects get along pretty well.The gameplay:If you like souls like games but you suck at Dark Souls, this game is for you. Quite challenging at some point, there were some bosses where i freaked out after 5 tries but it´s comepletely balanced and fair. The fighting aspect is really fun, you get 6 different weapons and can use 2 at the same time to find your own combat style. I went with daggers and magic staff and loved it. You can discover so many things by talking to strangers, finding hidden paces or just listen to some random enemies talking to each other.All in all i really enjoyed my time with it. For the first playthrough I needed nearly 30 hours but I didn´t discover everything (6 Treasure Chests were missing). So a big thanks to the gamemakers, I really loved it and recommend it to everybody who likes 3rd person games!

_childDocuments_.review: Great souls-ish type game, on the easier side for that kind of game which is a positive to me. Has a fairly interesting story with lots of good lore and worldbuilding, told in a much more direct way compared to the usual in its genre. My main annoyance with the game is a trend taking hold of gaming in general lately, boring rewards for exploration (it's pretty much always just upgrade materials since they give you all the weapons at the very beginning of the game and have a leveling system to acquire skills from) so I don't really hold it against the game too much. It's also a lot longer than I was expecting, and I didn't really find that to be in its favor, the second half of the game doesn't add much to mix things up gameplay-wise  and will probably be purely running on how much you enjoy the story at that point. Overall though, I enjoyed my time with the game and am excited for the expansion and whatever else comes out of this studio in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, often intense game that I genuinely enjoy, even if it's more of an on-rails experience than what I typically play. The combat feels fluid and while some of the controls aren't intuitive compared to certain other pc games, I haven't had any issues with picking them up. Also the maps often feel large and complex since they often have hidden nooks and paths to discover, some of which take a bit of inventive thinking to find, making exploring something fun to do in each district. My only pet peeve about it is how easily you can lose track of side quests (particularly where to go next or details of what to do for them) and the journal isn't as helpful as it could be in terms of letting you know which side quests are finished and which are in-progress.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly well crafted casual souls-like, if those words could ever appear together. The game is a lot more forgiving than Fromsoft's entries, with only 10% of your currency lost on death, and an arcadey, comically long distance roll. The combat appears very well polished and engaging, with a good variety of play style choices and abilities. I don't have any complaints in regards to combat but I have so many complaints in regards to player experience. This game is designed to inconvenience and annoy you. You have no fast travel until 20+ hours in, no map, no quest marker or even quest logs. Finding anything is up to pure luck. If you want to do a quest, you better memorize every line of dialogue from the quest NPC because he won't repeat it, and you won't have access to that information ever again.Final verdict: it's a fun game if you're willing to put up with the developers' ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I played on the highest difficulty and found it an okay challenge compared to other games of the genre. While it's certainly clunky at times, it mostly plays well enough. This is apparently the first game of the studio and it's a pretty good debut.The negatives? Combat gets repetitive because you have 6 weapons and that's it, little variation. Some skills are much better than others so you stick to that skill and that's it (whatever the dagger thingy is where you slice around like crazy). Sometimes the damage feels weird - like you get borderline oneshot at higher levels which is weird. Some enemies are also health sponges which is annoying. I think styx was the worst offender in that regard. Navigation was also hard at times because some of the scenery just looked the same and you can get turned around quickly that way.The positives? Really cool aesthetics, a neat story, variations in scenery throughout the levels and enemy variety - like every level offers up new enemy types and not mere reskins.Ultimately, this was solid fun for some 33 hours until the 2nd / true end given a rather low price at that. I enjoyed it. I probably won't replay it like I do some other games of the genre because the combat was rather one dimensional but as a one time adventure, it was certainly worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I followed this game since the announcement, since the gameplay and style looked awesome. It also reminded me on immortal fenix rising, which isnt available on steam. Since the game was develloped by a smaller studio and not EA or Blizzard, i decided to preorder. The communication of the dev team on the discord server was very good. In contrast to that, the treatment of pc players at launch is abysmal. Any console preorder could play 3 days earlier. In addition to that, the game went on sale on launch day. This screws over anybody who preordered, since they paid more. The preorder bonus is fairly small and not worth the 5 euros you would save when buying later. The gameplay and voice acting is quite good. Only main dialogue options are voice acted, while most other dialogue is done only in text form. This raises the question if costs were saved here (on the dialogue of the  character). Other key aspects for a souls game are missing as well. No real fast travel excist (except going back to the main hub) in this game, eventhough it is the end of 2022. The side quests are fetch quests where you need to run five different errands to get a small reward (ressources you can by later with your "souls"). These errands are just running there and back again.While the mission design is fairly similar to dark souls (no detailed information where you should go or map), the orientation and map design is inferior to fromsoftware. It kinda feels like the environment wasnt designed for this and the hud was cancelled as well. While i can forgive the bugs and gameplay issues, i cannot forgive the scummy behavior towards the pc playerbase. This behviour is the reason for me to request a refund.I hope you have nice day

_childDocuments_.review: Initially the “Souls-like” tag had put me off. I have absolutely no desire whatsoever to put myself through anything Souls-like. However, it came out that there is a difficulty setting and further reading online alleviated my fears and I went for it. And good news, I played on Story/Easy and it was a relaxing romp. I died twice (so far) in combat but that was due to my own sluggishness.PROThe difficulty setting. Main sell point for me.Combat feels quick and fluid. It doesn’t feel as slow and unresponsive as some of the Souls-like games do.You can switch and change your weapons quickly (primary and secondary weapons, and enchantments), but other load outs (trinkets and other weapons) you can also change but via the character menu.There is a LOT of lore, so the story is deep.CONTHERE’S NO MAP. This made exploring, especially in the beginning, really frustrating. I got lost so many times. So many times I did not know where to go or where to hand in a quest.THERE’S NO QUEST LIST. Only the "Main" quest shows, and that is on screen. You have a Journal that keeps track, like a diary, of people whom you’ve met or things that have happened, but like a diary, it does not tell you what you must do. “So this thing happened, this was interesting.” Yes, and? What must I do? Before the final showdown I tried to clean up side quests that I missed. I had to exclusively rely on online guides and it is then that you realise that there may have been a few quests that you may have broken by killing the wrong person or giving the wrong answer, because you had completely lost track of what was going on. The tidal wave of lore documents also does not help, because you miss so much.Anything else that could be wrong with this game does not even matter, it is so minor. But these two, the lack of a map and quest list, will be the major obstacles in preventing me from playing this game again (which I would like to do very much).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game so far.The only big issue is that it's being review-bombed by a bunch of literal cry babies.It sucks that the game doesn't let you rebind your keys, but all it takes is 10 minutes of getting used to the control scheme, and it's not like the default control scheme is horrible either..Also those who claim the devs screwed them over after pre-ordering the game, when will you ever learn common sense and stop pre-ordering games? However this game allowed for pre-ordering and you did pre-order it. One would assume that when you pre-order a game from a small team its because you would like to support them. But now you're literally crying over 3$...

_childDocuments_.review: 10 out of 10. I love this game. While I'm not a souls-like expert, I did pass Elden Ring and Kena. The atmosphere, art style, story and voice acting is top notch. I'm glad this had a strong story element, unlike most other souls games. Also, I don't think I would have played this if it didn't have difficulty settings. I played on Normal , but dropped it down for some of the bosses. I found this game extremely fun, it gave you that sense of exploration, especially since it didn't have a map. I was always looking down each pathway and behind each object looking for goodies. In the mines I was always on the lookout for explosives. Unlike other games where you don't really look at the game/graphics and are mostly looking at the map and question marks, I found myself really taking in the graphics and art style. This game also did a good job of not making backtracking a pain or boring. Just enough enemy variety and they are not all humanoids. I would often start up this game and later realize that I'd been playing for several hours at a time. Can't wait to see what this developer comes up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: is a story driven and dynamic combat based action Game in a Universe that leans a lot onto Greek mythology. As a very impatient young Hero, the Protagonist starts to follow the steps of the Northwind-Legion with the goal to not just follow a cursed Kings commands, but also to gain more Prestige in the Ranks of said Army and in the Protagonists Fathers Eyes.Various different Weapons are put into the Players hand to pick from and to allow different Playstiles to fight off the Enemies that populate the mystical Lands of Aphes. And not just Enemies are along the way. Also some NPCs in need for Help and for the Player to make decisions that can sometimes have a significant effect on further in the Story appearing Elements.The Games strength is definitely its Explorable Gameworld that leaves it mostly up to the Player in which direction to go next. Also the Combat is not to complicated and after a few attempts goes very smoothly, as special after unlocking new Skills in a large Tree of different abilities.The Story offers a lot to enjoy too and gives the different NPCs a lot of Character to be uncovered by Reading through Manuscripts written by those NPCs, by using new dialogue Options that pop up and by then accepting and finishing their personal Questlines.But also the weak Points need to be mentioned. And in Asterigo’s Case it is coming from the weird difference about the Voice-Over. While some Dialoques have a voice over, other have not. That may seem minor, but it destroys the Immersion everytime it shifts from voice over to not voice over.Also the Camera needs some updates, as specially on some big Bosses who are then almost off of the screen and, when locked on force the player to not been able to see the rest of the combat zone, or when not locked on are like invisible and hard to dodge when they do some major Attacks.Another thing that needs mentioning is also the missing Questlog. Its hard to tell which Quests are still followed, halfway finished or completely finished and so it would be nice to have a little overview on that.I recommend this Game to People who like dynamic action-based Combat Games, as specially those who like the Fantasy-Genre to fight various Bosses in a nice to explore designed world. ---------------------------------6,5 / 10 Grafics (They have their own Style on this one, but the Characters could still use a little bit more Details and Polys)7 / 10 Gameplay (Easy to manage the Weapon- and Skill-Menus and the Combat-Mechanics are not to complex to handle)6,2 / 10 Soundtrack (Interesting Soundtracks that support the Atmosphere in Locations and during Bossfights)8,2 / 10 Main-Story (The Main-Story is well implemented and leads the Player through the Game-World. Some Plots are sadly predictable tho.)6,4 / 10 Side-Story (Interesting Side-Stories from various NPCs, but sadly almost no Voice-Over like they did with the Main-Story.)7 / 10 Characters (Interesting set of Characters you can meet up with and uncovering their Background with lots of Dialoque Options)6,3 / 10 Enemies (Lots of Enemies, tho they start to feel repetitive after a while and only differ in which Element they are weak to rather then forcing Players to come up with new strategies)8,7 / 10 Boss-Fights (I totally like difficult Bossfights. Very challenging on the highest Difficulty-Setting where each could lead to Players having to make a new setup of Equipment and Skills to beat them. – Depending on the Players own Gaming-Skills :P)

_childDocuments_.review: They warn you in advance that this wasn't built for PC users, and they're right. Terrible UI/Controls. Game constantly takes control of your camera, as if you're an idiot without hands or a brain. Not just for cut scenes, even when simply walking down a hallway, it will start moving your camera against your will. Fighting the game for the camera is fantastically absurd. Save/load doesn't work as intended. It decides where you will spawn and saving does not mean you will load to that same position. Clicking with the mouse doesn't work as it should. Sometimes you have to click and hold, sometimes you use space bar. Whoever designed this game has acts like they've never used a mouse in their life. Are you a masochist, who enjoys self flagellating? Then this game control system is for you. There is no map = major failure. The story and combat are well enough to slog through the frustrations, but given how terribly the UI, controls, and camera works, it's only worth about 10 bucks. Wait for a sale. If you were raised on budget PCs (consoles and controllers), then the game is probably fine for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this was a very solid arpg. I recommend this and I look forward to the already planned DLC. My thoughts below.Story- Not bad, Greek mythology inspired but it's own thing. Dialogue can be pretty cheesy but I really warmed up to it after initially brushing it off. Only important bits are voice acted. There is a ton of written lore to find if you are into that.Combat- Decently fun. I didn't get bored with it despite using the same 2 weapons for my entire playthrough. You area offered 6 weapons within the first few minutes of the game and can use any 2 at once. Each weapon has up to a 4 hit combo and a special ability. You can finish a combo from one weapon with the final blow from the other. There is a skill tree that allows you to unlock passives and 5 (I think) unique skills and a stance for each weapon to further customize your playstyle.Quests- Only main quests are tracked. The only slightly negative that I have with this game is side quests aren't tracked and aren't always straight forward. I either forgot or didn't understand what I needed to do because I missed the dialogue due to real world distractions. I ended up not finishing several side quests due to this which also means I missed unlocking some secrets that were tied to those quests. There is a journal, but I didn't feel like it really helped with the way it was structured. Turning in quests isn't always straight forward as I always found myself just going through every dialogue option with all the NPC's until I found the correct option to turn the quest in.

_childDocuments_.review: This could be a good game, if it did the only gameplay it has right. Unfortunately, combat is subpar.Can't help but compare it to Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning. That game was an RPG with character development, somewhat interesting story and vast world to explore. Combat was dynamic albeit a bit basic. This game, Asterigos, feels as if you just took combat from KoA:R and called it a day.Locations are maze-like, empty maps with no clear path to goal. Dialogues are too long and boring, full of filler on boring events and characters. Talents are boring and don't influence the gameplay much. Weapon choice comes down to what can deal the most damage before having to dodge away. Enemies are too easy, bosses are damage sponges only waiting for you to slip or make a mistake to steamroll you.Couldn't name a single character that is likeable, including the protagonist.There are so many better ways to spend time instead of getting lost on uninspired maps or pressing hit-hit-hit-dodge over and over again.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected to have fun with Asterigos' decently executed combat and idly pay attention to the plot just to make it through the game; I was certainly not expecting my favorite part of the game to be the incredibly detailed and fleshed out world of Aphes, full of complex characters and motivations, intricate storylines and genuinely nuanced and deft writing. My progress through the game soon became one of searching out documents to learn more about the people and history and pushing storylines through to reveal dramatic plot points or further political intrigue.Hilda is a member of the Northwind Legion, this world's viking/Celt analogue who journeys to the mythical city of Asterigos to discover what happened to her father's company of soldiers. Their king has been cursed with an artifact from Aphes and sent the Legion to search for a cure, though Hilda was not yet experienced enough to join them. When she arrives, she finds a city in stasis for 1000 years due to the curse and becomes involved in all the problems that have arisen during that time.I honestly cannot heap enough praise on the writing. While it can sometimes be delivered clumsily or awkwardly, and the voice acting can be uneven, the writing is strong enough to shine through any flaws in delivery. Early on when Hilda goes off plan and does something most games would applaud you for, everyone in game reacts in a way that surprised me. Very few, if any of the characters are simply good or bad. It's hard to explain without spoilers, but every boss I took down had more to them than being an obstacle, every ally I made had mistakes and ugly parts of their past, all of them were linked with each other and the city. These were complicated people with millennia of history. Very rarely was anything I accomplished not tempered with some sort of consequence. And it's strengthened all the more because the city and world it takes place in is so strong and full, the developers really put in an impressive amount of effort to make a place that had such an enormous history. Documents abound everywhere, you'll read one that is simply poems that a famous playwright did, then one on laws regarding rationing and naming someone that appears in a later note about being jailed for breaking martial law curfew, or notes on experiments to solve the curse referencing a note you read hours ago that a scientist wrote about sabotaging something. The only glaring flaw that stuck out to me was honestly Hilda and her story mostly because in a game where it puts so much emphasis on how going off and doing what you want has consequences...she is still the primary mover of every event. Legendary monster? This teenager can kill it. Stalemate as a result of too many lightning dogs? Tiny girl will kill em all. It just felt really incongruous, but I also realize you can't have a game where the protagonist watches other more capable people solve everything. It just can sometimes feel weird to have Hilda be the one to solve an issue by throwing her face into it.The graphics aren't a AAA title, but the style and aesthetic are great. Honestly, picking ancient Greece/Rome as the inspiration for Aphes was great because it's a very underutilized style. And they did a lot of great work in giving the city it's own identity and keep it consistent with the setting. There are a very healthy amount of environments and the game does a very good job at weaving them through each other so you'll sometimes get that "Ah, this path leads back here!" that can be fun when exploring.I was expecting the game to have a smaller scope, but after 31 hours and hitting the credits this is actually a hefty game. There is quite a lot to do, many sidequests and optional activities/fights with even just the main storyline being a good time investment. I will give a small aside that despite doing all the sidequests, I apparently solved some of them 'wrong' and thus was locked out of one of the endings which only irked me because for most of them I wasn't sure exactly what I could have done differently or how I would know to do a certain step unless I looked it up. Small complaint though.The combat is good. It's...fine. I may be the wrong person to go in depth for this as I'm not exactly a wizard with action games. Though it says Soulslike on the tin, I'd liken this more to a character action game or simply action RPG. Rather than finding weapons and armor everywhere, you get all your weapons from the start and can equip two of them to use. I went with the hammer and daggers and even those were enough to make me feel overwhelmed with options. Someone better than me at these games would probably find a cornucopia of options to play with as you level up and get more options and special abilities. Meanwhile, I kinda soldiered through while upgrading only two weapons and rarely using more than 3 abilities or switching elemental weaknesses. As a result I found the difficulty decent, sometimes a bit...not jank but I'd wonder about a hitbox here or there or why I didn't hit with an attack. The aformentioned more talented gamer will probably find the game a tad easy, so a higher difficulty might be worthwhile for them.Even if sometimes the combat wasn't my favorite part of the game, I loved my time with it. There was just so much to like about it, so much more of the world I wanted to see and characters I wanted to learn about. Well worth the price, even when it was full price. There's a large amount of content, replayability to try different loadouts and get a different ending and a truly fantastic set of characters to follow to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a souls-like game for people who don't like souls-like games. Similar vibe, atmosphere, gameplay and story but lacks the punishing difficulty. The souls genre is one that is not for me. I find it grindy and replaying the same levels over and over again to memorize enemies, and boss movements is rewarding but it does not hold my attention. This game is a much lighter affair that is very beatable but still offering some challenge without being punishing or overly grindy before you make progress. It's a very aesthetically pleasing game but those hardcore souls fans should look elsewhere. The challenge you're craving you will find lacking here but for me that is exactly what I was looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to anyone who likes Action RPGs, but Nier fans in particular will appreciate its sense of world-building and lore. The graphics, music, and overall presentation are above average for a game like this. The greco-roman world sparkles (sometimes literally) with detail. The voice acting comes across believably and convincingly, especially emotional and important scenes. The main character Hilda is curious, driven, and capable, traits which I found endearing.Difficulty is fairly customize-able. There's an easy, normal, and hard mode. You take a lot of damage but trinkets and awareness help you reduce it. You can easily grind your level too high if you feel like it, but there are also trinkets you can equip which make you take more damage and earn no XP. Get ready to read and also get ready to lose your bearings. If these two things don't automatically disqualify the game for you, you'll find an enjoyable and replay-able experience here.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid indie souls-like that I enjoyed and I feel like we need more games like this in the genre. The only negatives I can think of are that the quests are too convoluted and that there is too much dialogue in the game. The way quests are designed in this game is confusing and lead me to look up some of them online. It is easy to get lost on what to do/where to go next. There's also a LOT of dialogue in the game - not a negative per se, but it was for me. There was too much reading in the game for my liking, but some gamers do enjoy extensive dialogue and lore. The last thing I'd mention is that the game feels "slower" in terms of its pacing, story and overall gameplay. Fast travel is not unlocked until a bit later and at the beginning you only have warp crystals, which are somewhat uncommon. That didn't bother me but I can see it annoying some people.Overall I'd definitely recommend the game for fans of the genre. If you're hesitant then pick it up when it goes on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: I highly enjoyed this game! I'd describe it as something of a souls-lite, in that it definitely has carry over's and design stylings of souls games, but, also a lot of just typical action-adventure RPG stylings. For those who are on the fence with soulslikes due to their generally very high difficulty, I found the medium setting to be a really fun experience, it had a few difficult moments, but, very casual compared to a souls game, more in line with what you'd probably expect from your typical RPG.The game is very story-centric and I'd say overall it's pretty solid on that front, there is a lot of dialogue and writing in the game so that might be hit-or-miss for people, but, I thought the dialogue was fairly well done with great voice acting particularly for the protagonist, and the lore dump writing while fairly dense at times was quite interesting and gave a lot of insight into the events and structure of the world and the people within it.The game definitely isn't perfect by any means, it sorely needs an update to its journal and general quest handling, as well as either needing more guiding indicators in-world for getting around when exploring or backtracking or a basic map, I mean look, your character is frequently writing down information and observations in their journal, it would only make sense for them to be keeping some sort of roughly drawn map for getting around, or even if the map is a no go, at least keeping track of quests and objectives better, I know the point is to focus more on the organic exploration and discovery, but, even from a lore and in-world perspective, it doesn't make sense to have so little info given the nature of the protagonist and the mission they are on.There's a lot I could say about the game because I truly did love my experience with it, but, I know it's also highly tailored to me in style and setting and thus I'm definitely more able to overlook faults that would otherwise be pretty frustrating. I certainly recommend the game, but, of course, I'd suggest reading a couple of reviews both good and bad, and watching some gameplay to get a better idea if it is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The full price of $34.99 is fair for what the game is -- it's clear that hard work was put into this -- and the full price is what I paid, but getting it on sale might make the the mediocrity hurt less. If I could give this a more middling review I would. It took me a very long time to finish the game because I lost interest and stopped playing for some months before returning, then took another break, before finally pushing myself to finish. I'm glad I did manage to see it through the end as the premise of the game was what drew me into it initially.The combat was pretty simple, but enjoyable with some fights being easy to cheese if you're having trouble. The music was fitting although forgettable and the characters were generally likable but only Hilda, Minerva, and Eumenides were memorable. The rest were okay, although I admittedly forgot how Shay and Hilda are connected other than Hilda was after him in the past for some shenanigans he got up to?, but I was quick to forget them. Roxane started interesting, but she was kicked to the wayside so early on that you forget she exists until the very end when there's a little blurb in the end cutscene about her.I wasn't a fan of the choice in art style, which reminded me of Pixar films, and while you heard the characters speaking their mouths didn't move unless it was part of a short animation that looped to convey an emotion. It made the characters feel rigid while the voiced lines were playing and detached from their own voices.My biggest gripe with the game was the lack of a minimap or even a larger area map that you could view from a menu. I'm the type of person that gets easily lost so I got lost often in the twisting and connecting pathways. This made navigating areas more frustrating than anything else.The story was solid -- nothing groundbreaking -- but still pretty good and the only reason I decided to finish the game. There were some sidequests but I didn't go out of my way to complete any as I didn't feel compelled to do so if they weren't a requirement. Any I did finish was by chance.The bosses never seem to get more difficult in terms of, well, difficulty so the final fight didn't exactly feel as rewarding as it was probably meant to. Perhaps this was because I used the daggers. Daggers are the dual-blade weapon option and it was easily the best weapon choice for me. Spamming blade dancer made every fight a breeze including the last two big boss fights. The speed of attacks made chipping away at health when I ran out of SP quickly depleted any enemy's HP to the point where it almost felt unfair to use them. Supposedly Round 2 (Asterigos's version of NG+) makes the enemies tougher, but I didn't bother with a replay.All in all the story was solid but nothing fascinating and the rest of the game was rather bland. The limited color palettes for most of the environments didn't help this either. While there were a few characters I enjoyed, most I could've done without or at least with less dialogue as there's a lot, but only the main dialogue paths are voiced the rest is text-only. The story was what carried the game and the combat was simple but fun albeit mindless. Without those two things I would've abandoned this game a long time ago and wouldn't have considered coming back. It was worth a playthrough, I didn't feel any of my money was wasted, but I don't have an interest to play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish steam had some mid ground for reviews.But I'm going to tilt to no for this one. You have these smooth moments that are just completely interrupted by nonsense like not being able to dodge out of a sprint sometimes so you have to stop sprinting in order to dodge. Only being able to jump while sprinting like this is some Dark Souls 1 wannabe or something. No input buffering so you cant press your heal button mid roll to have your character drink a potion right after ending a dodge. For an action combat game the enemies have strange attacks and hitboxes that dont do a good job of communicating to the player whats happening. The character has no minor stagger animation but getting hit makes you lose control of her.... but she just stands still doing nothing for half a second. I don't mind instances of losing character control as punishment for not avoiding certain attacks but something about this game just does an awful job of delivering it. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best souls-like games I've ever played, despite its cartoonish style and and relatively simplistic story.Pros:* no local map (only quite uselesss global Sekiro-like one);* no quest markers;* net-like locations will require you to memorise where you've been and where you haven't; intertwined by openable shortcuts;* different types of weapons with different animations and different skills;* good visual style, architecture, characters' and weapons' models;* good calming music (though, maybe, not a lot of it);* good optimization;* good price (12 USD is the full price in my country);Cons:* if the location is designed to be like I've described above ("will require you to memorise all the paths") it should be less monotonous, it should contain more noticeable and memorable objects, to spark the idea of the location-learning in the player (and simplify it, the learning);* if you don't have what interesting to show on the part of the location -- don't stretch it and inhabit by identical/similar enemies; better make it at least just a bit more compact, but instead more interesting, memorable, concentrated;* I may be blind. But if I'm not, and the game indeed somewhere in the first half of it(self) allows you to craft 4 mediocre trinkets and nothing new is being added till the end of the game (no new trinkets to craft and no upgrades to existing ones) -- I'm not sure why you've spend your time on that feature at all. This feels half baked;* I don't see a reason why healing potions aren't automatically replenished as soon as I return to the hub. Other consumables as well.* not required, but it would probably be nice if in the description of the quest at least a respawn point would be mentioned, like "blah-blah-blah, where you can get if you start from the A point and turn to the left". Then the player opens the "special" map finds a point A by its name, "goes" there and knows where to go next. But that's minor, I had problems with not knowing where to go, but rarely;* please don't disable "skip cutscene" button, ever, if possible;* a ton of collectible texts, which I have nothing against of, but since I'm not a big reader, I find them more redundant then useful (or at least interesting);* BUG: if you change the outfit of your character to the alternative one, come close to the ladder from the top (at least the stone wall, maybe other kinds of ladders too) and press "go down", the character will either try to do that but stay on the top, or try to do that and fall down; I don't remember when I've seen something like this the last time 😮Conclusion: recommended, even strongly, for its price. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a 10/10 for me.Combat is awesome. You get six weapons each with their own talent tree and a special skill. You always have two of these six equipped. Daggers have a dash, snb have a block, spear parries, bracers throw mines, staff fires a laser beam, hammer has well a hammer attack. I preferred daggers and staff (staves are long range). You can learn skills for each weapon (uses mana) and perks which can change how your weapons attacks and specials might operate. All weapons can be upgraded at a smith.You get four elements to imbue your weapons with on the fly and each of those can be upgraded. There are attribute points but only three stats so it's hard to screw up your build. Also respeccing is cheap.Combat is very fun. Fast paced. exploring is fun, ton of branching paths that can open up shortcuts. You do unlock fast travel eventually. There's a lotta like notes and letters and books you find that'll expand on the lore. Game is very dialogue heavy too, mostly in between boss fights though. Story is fine I guess. I'm playing on normal but considering a replay on hard. There is a story mode as well. A couple bosses are piss easy but a few of them took me more than one try (especially when rolling off a cliff is possible). You lose some currency on death but not xp. There are a lotta side quests but no real quest log or map, so best of luck completing all that stuff. At this price point it's a steal

_childDocuments_.review: A well optimized game, with a decent story, and actually good action combat. Large zones with no loading screens, sporting what I can only describe as Vindictus combat. Honestly their old trailers don't even do it justice, the hits definitely have some meaty impacts. I nearly 100%'d the game without realizing it, which is extremely rare for me. I might actually do it, and I hate collectathons.  Despite having a souls-like tag, it's not a souls-like at all. It has physical checkpoints and enemies reset on death/rest and that's it. It is some classic ps2-era action combat and it's actually refreshing to see some decent combat in an action game. None of that "oh their doing a special uninterruptable attack that you must parry" Simon Says ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you want to dodge all attacks you can, if you want to block all attacks you can(kinda), if you want to parry all attacks you can, if you just want to "face-tank-trade and see if you knock them down before they knock you down" you can. No electric slides, except for the enemy that actually has an electric slide. Clean hitboxes with the exception of enemies with mining picks that can wipe out entire continents with their downward swing. Even Cleaner numbers, this isn't maplestory where at endgame you deal billions of damage. At level 50 for example you might have 5-6x the hp of a level 1. Same goes for the raw damage. This allows for a decent player to take on mid-end-game enemies at level whatever, and that's pretty nice. At the time of playing and completing the game in 30ish hours on patch 1.04, I can say this was a surprisingly well made game. If I had to be nitpicky, could've used a personal map, especially in the city. The game has rather rewarding questlines that can open up sometimes downright absurd npc interactions, or apparently change the outcome of the game. However quests can sometimes be finicky on whether or not the game thinks you completed or failed a quest. For instance you can get the reward for a quest, and still get reprimanded for failing the quest because you didn't confirm the quest completion back at town. Audio can be a bit strange as the audio is centered on the character's position and facing, which can cause a little confusion. Also the enemy AI is very non-aggressive out of combat, removing a lot of the danger if you choose to use any sort of tactical approach, you can very easily separate large platoons with a few throwing knives. Wish the music that you can earn and have play in the hub would stay until changed. If I were forced to be objective, it's an easy 8/10 probably an 8.5/10. An action game that stands on it's own without the need of gimmicks, but more importantly it just works. Now if I didn't have to be objective 10/10 I'm actually already pre-ordering their next however many games.

_childDocuments_.review: I was thoroughly impressed with how much I came to enjoy this game.Footnote: I hate Souls games and the overwhelming majority of all Souls-likes. I hate the feeling of playing a game that hates you just for buying it; it's one thing to have a gradual difficulty curb, it's another to punish unfairly.
