_childDocuments_.review: in summary: I like this game. somehow, through all of it's flaws, it captured me. try it if you want to play an easy souls-like game in an interesting greco-roman fantasy setting.asterigos has good combat, a large variety of skills, weapon combinations, and spells at the player's disposal. it really feels like the combat is one of the most polished aspects of the experience. there is a lot of freedom afforded the player when it comes to choosing your fighting style. there's a large variety of enemies and bosses for you to combat, and the fighting never really gets stale.the cons...the game is extremely lore-heavy. characters you've never met before will tell you paragraphs of information about people and places and events you've never heard of. the world is clearly very complex, and the writers must have put in hundreds of hours constructing the history of the universe...but some things are better left a mystery. the pacing of the game often suffers from too much information being dumped on the player.aside from the hyper-verbosity of the storytelling, there are other issues with the writing. the story being told doesn't make particularly compelling reading. I mean, you don't have to sit down and write the next lord of the rings, but it certainly wouldn't hurt if the writing style was a bit more creative. the prose is dry: there is little humor, very little information is left to the imagination, and almost no plot detail isn't spelled out to the letter. I WISH the story was cut down to just the most interesting events, and the documents were fewer and a bit snappier. if you really like getting into the story of any game you play and you want to become an aphesian history professor, you're in luck!a nitpick about these documents: there are quite a few documents called things like "faded old document" or "document with lively handwriting" or "document with odd signature". they all use the same set of paper colors, and they ALL use the same exact font. video games are a visual medium, people. you can SHOW me handwriting on an old sheet of paper if a document is meant to be handwritten. you can SHOW me the odd signature on the dossier or what have you. show, don't tell applies to many arts, but the visual arts have the unique freedom to show almost anything you can imagine. just show it!hilda, our protagonist, is positioned awkwardly within the narrative as both the savior of aphes and also as a child who no-one respects...and at the same time, it's shown that hilda doesn't really respect herself, either. even by the end of the game, after becoming ostensibly the most powerful warrior of all time, her aspirations are modest and her plans for her future are dull and boring, if not bleak. the entire game, she seems to see herself as just a rank-and-file soldier, subservient to everyone and everything. it would have been a MUCH more interesting game if there was some form of character development beyond her stat numbers increasing.the "quest log", also known as the journal, is almost completely useless. unfortunately, when hilda is given a quest, she seems to not care about writing down what to actually *do* -- she seems to prefer writing down her miscellaneous, sometimes unrelated thoughts. this is just unmarked side quests with more steps. if you're going to have a character who actively journals during the game -- hell, you can SEE her literally pull out her little book and write stuff down -- let her write down a quest log! the things she writes down don't make sense. why wouldn't she, presumably a highly trained and disciplined soldier, make a log of her activities? skyrim did a similar thing, albeit with a much less diegetic "journal". to the game developers: you're not making dark souls. you don't have to copy *everything* they did.on top of that, all the text -- dialogue, item descriptions, scattered documents and the like -- is riddled with egregious typos and grammatical errors. without even that baseline level of writing polish, it's hard to care about what the game is trying to get you to read -- and again, there's a LOT of reading.the level design is fairly good...but it's intensely, noticeably barebones most of the time. the shelter is one of the areas that feels most "alive", due to items being scattered around, people lounging about, and npcs that you can talk to. hell, one of these npcs actually MOVES (vulcane the smith, who walks back and forth between her desk and anvil). imagine that. the rest of the world is mostly barren of all life save enemies to kill. if only there were a bit more decoration here and there, some lighting variation like the sun or moon's rays piercing through clouds, a person who doesn't just stand in one spot like a statue, a bit more color contrast in environments.... many of these levels feel dead and odd, like those false cities designed for military training.the mechanical issues are less noticeable during a regular playthrough, but they still exist. for context, I played my very first run on "challenge" difficulty. I figured there was *no way* this game is as hard as an actual souls game, so I played on the highest difficulty. one of the biggest effects of this mode is that your resistance to damage starts in the negatives; minus seventy per resistance type, to be exact. at the very late stages of the game, through careful gear selection, was actually able to get my resistance to either fire, magic, or ice all the way up to...zero. which is where it *starts* on the "adventure" difficulty.however, even on "challenge" difficulty -- in which you take almost double damage from nearly everything -- it's mostly an easy experience, especially if you've played the soulsborne games. but when it gets hard, it really gets pretty damned hard. however, I'm only referring to the optional paragon bosses that are accessed via the shrines throughout the game.some of these bosses, like , really feel like you'd need a doctorate in stamina management to effectively dodge every attack. some of them felt very unintuitive, with awkward movement required to beat them. some of them, like alkinoos (who's thankfully not very difficult), require performing some mind-numbingly repetitive event before getting to the actual boss fight.the difficulty of each boss is wildly inconsistent, both with the other paragon bosses and the rest of the game. I'd say both the  were MUCH more difficult than even the final boss of the game --  if you have multi-phase bosses and bosses that interact with the player before arriving at the "arena" proper, why in the name of heaven would you NOT use those mechanics for the ultimate enemy of the game?there seem to be a lot of audio bugs. even if you turn the volume down to the lowest setting on all the sliders, some sounds, such as lightning strikes from certain bosses, will still come through at full volume. it's odd how something like sound effects not responding to the volume slider didn't make it through testing.I really liked playing through this game. I'm currently trying to get all the achievements I accidentally locked myself out of via missing unmarked side quests, so I'm playing it again. I just wish it had a little more polish put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit bored as the game started, but it unravels to be quite entertaining as you go further into it. Overall, recommend playing if you want a light Dark Souls experience, but with far less annoying combat, more pleasing visuals and with concrete explanations to the lore (instead of making it as vague as possible and leaving stuff up to your imagination).Things I liked:- Engaging and atmospheric story about a viking in a cursed ancient Greek city;- Immersive lore, if you're able to get through walls of texts used to convey it;- Combat is dynamic and enjoyable. A bit repetitive, but at least it's not designed to be annoying;- You can parry , including non-humanoids, magic, lightnings and plunging attacks;- Dense world with shortcuts and side stuff to explore;- Quests are tracked in an imitated playing character notes - atmospheric;Things I didn't like:- Obscure and somewhat random criteria for good ending (e.g. not doing one NPC's quest to prevent him from dying);- Too much of text. A lot of interesting lore, but way too much of filler entries;- Most of skills/perks are combat style specific, and you can use up to 2 combat styles simultaneously (out of 6). There is no way to switch them outside of menu (like with quick access buttons), so you will likely spend most of the game only using and leveling up 2 of the styles, forgetting about the others;- In the academy, after completing the area boss 2 NPC quest givers suddenly die, making their quests incompletable;- Crafted trinkets seem to be completely useless;- Quests are tracked in an imitated playing character notes - confusing;- There are a lot of shrines in the game that you can pray at. When you do, you get the message "nothing happened". There doesn't seem to be anything else to them, so it looks like trolling and I don't enjoy being trolled >:(

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Re-reading this review I realize I sounded a bit harsher than this game deserves, it really was a fun playthrough!Its a good game, sort of an easy mode Dark Souls, but WOW is there a lot of exposition - if you want to read/listen to everything you are probably going to be spending just as much time doing that as actually playing.  The only parts that are really hard are the DLC "Paragon" bosses which introduce a crazy difficulty spike that really wasn't fun imo.  This was on the normal "Adventure" difficulty btw - I'm actually not sure if the difficulty level can be changed after starting...My main gripe is that it can be hard to figure out what you missed in your playthrough - the map tracks how many chests and weasels you missed in a zone, and the "archive" can help you track down missed documents and items at least.  There are *some* player created resources to help in this regard but they are scattered all over the place and not as easy to find as in more... well... popular games.I can't do NG+ in most games and this one is no exception, and they do have a fair amount of content locked behind NG+ mode, eg you only unlock the ability to craft quest reward trinkets in NG++I did encounter one major bug that almost prevented me from finishing my playthrough, but thankfully I was able to resolve it on my own.If you liked eg Immortals Fenyx Rising then I think it's worth a playthrough.

Disjointed, fleshed out by exposition 'echos'. No ones mouths move. You're introduced to teleportation in the first ~5 minutes of gameplay, but well into the main story your character is in awe of the concept being real. ...You've used it several times by then. The protagonist is amazed by what 'stardust' can do, but is a master of 6 *shape shifting* weapons powered by OP battle magic.Every NPC is demeaning to the protagonist. The subplots don't fit together. In combat she's far more powerful than her father, physically 5 times her size while the dude is insulting and dismissive. The side characters all share one of 4 enemy models making them instantly forgettable. The magic system is just anything and everything. Necklaces are the only consistent thematic piece. There's no guidance on which of the 3 quest threads to do in what order, even though you need elemental power-ups from one to complete the next, leaving you wandering for hours more. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid MEH. I don't think it deserves an outright negative review, but it needs a light discount at least to be worth it. However, there are many glaring problems.Pros:1) A charming art style and good character design.2) Decent controls and move-set. Being able to seamlessly switch between your two carried weapons is cool and the particle effects from the moves look pretty too.3) An okay story. Nothing phenomenal, a bit convoluted, but decent enough to keep your interest along your journey.Cons:1) Bosses simply do not feel rewarding in this game because you are rewarded with nothing other than trinkets and crafting materials upon defeating them. Getting great loot after a hard fought battle is one of the best parts of a souls-like and it is simply missing here.2) You are stuck with the weapons you get at the beginning of the game and simply upgrade them throughout. This would be perfectly fine if it was a linear game, but a game like this should have things for you to discover, cool outfits and hairstyles to unlock and so on in my opinion.3) The lack of a proper map to use for navigation is huge oversight. It is a tremendous quality of life upgrade as games such as Elden Ring have demonstrated. I hope the devs add this as a patch. On the topic of navigation, teleportation between conduits takes a little too long to unlock (about a third into the game) and should have been allowed much earlier.----P.S. : I genuinely hope that the game does well enough for the developers to be able to justify making an Asterigos 2. For a small studio, they have achieved quite a lot; if they take feedback and learn from their mistakes from the first title, I truly believe they could make a proper gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: A respectable action-adventure game.  While it shares some similarities to the "Souls-like" genre, I don't feel it quite earns that distinction.  There are plenty of opportunities to cheese fights with range/techniques and stamina rarely runs out when you need it most.  The dungeon designs were sprawling and memorable, but sometimes overstayed their welcome (looking at you, Styx).  Quests are "logged" in your journal but otherwise tracking them is a chore - there are several I left open, because I didn't feel the need to see them through to the end and backtrack through an area for the 20th time to get lackluster crafting loot as a reward.  Combat is enjoyable and responsive, with dodging being able to interrupt your attack combos quite quickly allowing for more risky and aggressive play style.  Each weapon set felt good to use, though I ended up settling for the Spear and Staff for the majority of my playthrough.  Each weapon has a "talent tree" that you will easily be able to spec into two of (accounting for the ability to quickly swap between two equipped weapons in combat with fluid transitions), which link to special skills(spells) for each weapon type.  Many of the actual skills seem gimmicky and not altogether useful considering how precious mana becomes in prolonged engagements, but there are several exceptions that upgrade the weapon's damage output or utility considerably.  The story I felt was the weakest link, and the ending itself seems to come abruptly and with little consequence to your actions as a player.  You can skip most dialogue, which I found myself doing on a few occasions when conversations were clearly trying to build the world's lore, but had constant interruptions with poorly timed "reactionary" comments from the main character.  All in all, this is worth a shot if you're looking for a 25-30 hour single player adventure with fun combat and a large world to explore.  Worth it at asking price and a steal on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to review. The game does things badly , does some things great and mostly is middling.There is no doubt in my mind that the developers of Asterigos have huge amounts of passion and talent. This looks to be the first game they have developed or at least the first to hit the western market and i have to say if this is true then im impressed. It's not often that eastern developed games outside of japan can hit the western market and appeal to many western gamers , however i think that this does a good enough job to warrant a purchase (on sale). With this being said however the game does fall flat in a few areas which bring it down into mediocrity. or Slightly above average.The good:I love the music , animation/art and world building. The game makes me want to explore it , the music is varied and fires on all cylinders , the animation is simply one of the best ive seen. The world building is almost in my top 5 of games.The average:The combat is pretty average , its more i-frame based than reaction , and if you get hit you stumble leaving a feeling of clunkiness which is often what reviewers dont quite understand in the feedback loop of gameplay , so instantly get turned off and refund. Other then that it plays more like kingdoms of amalur (combat wise) then say dark souls, although gameplay generally has a souls LITE feel to it.Difficulty could be ramped up a bit , so talents ,attributes and weapon choices feel more impactful , To increase difficulty i would make the ai more adaptable and harder to stun lock , also almost getting rid of the small aggro range and reset the mobs seem to have. The perfect difficulty to start would be that of the 10 secret bosses during the last part of the game , at the moment these are optional but i would say that they were probably of normal difficulty which would have been a good type for the start of the game.I actually like the talent tree , almost all of the skills in it changes your abilities and attacks in various ways and are not just stat boosts , i love this , but would like to see a larger tree with more neutral skills that are not just tied to certain weapons.I would also like to see more and different weapon types , and different looks to each weapon , i.e there could be multiple swords with different stats and bonuses (But i get this is usually the way eastern rpgs are made , in its current form) I would also like to see actual armour that can also be upgraded , not just trinkets. This would lead to bosses being more exciting , if for example they all dropped unique items , not just upgrade materials so you can upgrade your generic weapon to +2.I think if they worked on the ai , balancing , and game play progression systems , The next time around i can really see a good game forming. But as the product stands now i would give it an average 5/10 ,

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a "souls-like", it's a "dark souls clone", it's so utterly faithful to the original Dark Souls formula in every way. I could write a page straight just listing every single aspect of it that is lifted directly from the Fromsoft games. This includes combat, level structure, loot design, and so much more. They've laid over top a fairly boring plot and quest structure - but it is just about entirely skippable and optional: you can just kill your way to the next boss, skip some talking, and repeat until the game ends. This - like any souls clone - is about the moment to moment combat - and the combat is very good. It's not *quite* as tight as Fromsoft's own combat, but it's well beyond serviceable. Parrying and countering with the spear is an absolute delight. The rolls feel great, the bosses are fun and fair with plenty of character to each of them, the trash mobs are great fun to knock over with well-timed parries... if you're into the slow blow-trading combat of Dark Souls, you'll probably love this.Strict Fromsoft purists will surely find many slight nitpicks to complain about if they try, as they cannot help but do - but if you just want to do some Dark Souls style combat in a pretty game with a new, brighter setting, and some bosses you haven't fought before, hoo boy does this deliver. A lovely, lovely time. Polished, pretty, satisfying - it's Dark Souls with a Sekiro parry option and fresh aesthetics. What more can one ask for?

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is fun, similar to Dark Soul but easier. The i-frames on dodging seems to be much longer and outside of some bosses there are very few enemies that can one shot you or nearly one shot you. I use a 3-1-2 distribution for attack-health-ability levels.Performance/graphics is good for me at all max settings, but I'm also using a 3090 so your mileage may vary. Key binds cannot be changed, which is massive glaring issue. The developers have said that they are fixing this. The story is interesting enough, but there is way too much text. I mostly just skim through it.Ultrawide works but you need to edit an ini file otherwise it just shrinks your vertical fov to "zoom in". Character customization is very limited. No visual changes, you just pick 2 of 6 weapon types and use those for the entire game since the perk system is fully tied to each weapon. There is no map and I only unlocked fast travel 10 hours into the game. If you're not someone who can remember routes then you might have a frustrating experience of running in circles. The side quest system is absolutely abysmal. You've got a journal but it doesn't tell you what to do or where to go. It only lists what you've already done. So again you better have a good memory and be able to figure out where to go and what to do based on context clues.Overall the game is worth the $35 price point, but barely. It's good points are really good and it's bad points are really bad, so value will differ depending on the person. Check some gameplay videos out before you buy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, mostly. The combat's not incredibly nuanced, but you can dodge-cancel out of many attacks, which helps, because everything hits like a truck.Outside of the weapon mod system (unlocked in the expansion), your basic attacks don't consume stamina, just dodges, sprinting, and whatever alt-fire mode your weapons have. But stamina regens extremely fast, so it's not really worth worrying about except for some edge cases. One of the Expansion's challenges is one such case.There's a lotta dialog, there's a lot of documents... none of them matter all that much. And very little of it is going to stick with me, I'm afraid. The story is... there. The characters are what really shine. They do have nuances. Although I was getting *extremely* sick of the game insisting on moral relativism and you have to figure out your own answers about good and evil, but everyone clearly *has* thoughts about what's acceptable, and it comes across as extremely hollow.There's 2 endings, and the process for getting the better ending... there's some guide-dang-it bits, because it's about certain sidequests being resolved correctly, and I wouldn't have guessed the right responses, or even if a given quest could result in a point towards the good. BUT the war table does sprout a wee badge each time you get one right, so there's *some* way to track it.It's alright. I was rather surprised to find out that the recently added bonus stats from finding chests wants you to find more than all of the chests in the game. (NG+) And I was really irritated by a couple of the optional final-chapter bosses, and a couple of the expansion's arenas felt unfair. (A couple were really cool to solve though.)I waited for the DLC to drop, which turned out to be smart with how post-release patches added whole systems as well as polish. And as per usual, there was a sale to coincide with that.It kept me interested and entertained. And even the most frustrating bits only needed a handful of retries. (Though one, I only won due to a glitch in my favor.) So, it's a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay Video:  ✔️ ; your name is Hilda and you visit the city of Aphes to find and save your father, and figure out what the heck is going on in this city. You will find at least 250 documents and hidden notes in the world that either adds more to the lore, or some pointless and boring statements/stories that have nothing to do with it. There are tons of side quests that you can find and a lot of interesting characters to talk to❌ ; there are two endings (and side characters endings shown as a slideshow, similar to Fallout), but story is pretty linear; there are no branching paths or butterfly effect, you will fight the same bosses and take the same missions. That being said, for some reason the game shames you for killing a certain boss/doing a certain action, and I thought to myself that there had to be another way, so I loaded an old save and kept exploring the same areas multiple times, tried to find different paths and even avoided fights, but there wasn’t, and I wasted more than 3 hours of my time. However, picking certain choices and finishing specific side quests can unlock more dialogue and affect which ending you’ll get.❌ ; at a certain point, the game will give you three separate missions with their own substories to finish, and you can choose which one you want to begin with. However, each one stops halfway through (when the story starts to get good, the game gives you a poor excuse like “the door is closed, i’ll think of a way to open it later”), and in order to continue you must complete the other two (halfway though as well), then complete an entirely new quest, and then you will come back to them. Not to mention that the quests are heavily scripted and have to be done by the book or else you won't be able to progress. , there was one sidequest later in the game, I found most of the notes, I knew what was going on and where to go, I found the locked door that led to the next objective, and I had the key to open it, yet I couldn’t do so, why? Turns out I had to find one more hidden document first, and then I can open itThis is just me being nitpicky, but what makes a souls-like game awesome is the emphasis on environmental storytelling and lets the player connect the dots, and not constantly spoon-feeding it to us, which the game does constantly.✔️ ; staff, daggers, sword and shield, hammer, bracelets and spear, and you can only equip two weapons and four different abilities. You can upgrade weapons and unlock powerful abilities using stardust (aka points that you get from killing enemies) and materials that you find in the world. They are fun to use against enemies. If only they added more ranged weapons other than the staff (such as a crossbow).✔️ ; “story” aka easy mode, “adventure” which is the normal difficulty, and “challenge” which is the dark souls level of difficulty (and sometimes even harder). You won’t gain extra experience/stardust if you choose a higher difficulty, but enemies will do more damage to you. In addition, if you play on “adventure/challenge” diff. you will lose 20% of your stardust when you die, if you choose “story” difficulty then you'll lose only 10%.✔️ ; there are over 22 bosses (main, optional and endgame), and most of them have their own unique design, combat style and music theme. The endgame bosses are difficult so prepare yourself before facing them. I played it on the hardest difficulty and they were pretty challenging to the point that they can oneshot you if you aren’t careful.❌ ; for example:✔️ ; the game has a similar art style to Immortals Fenyx Rising. There are a lot of interesting locations to explore, tons of hidden passages and different regions to visit.❌ ; some doors look openable but they aren't, some platforms look reachable but actually aren't, and some buildings look accessible but they are actually out of bounds.✔️ ; butter-smooth 60 FPS.❌ ; unexpected camera movement, large enemies fit into tiny doors, game freezes when saving, character disappears when teleporting, odd hitboxes, getting stuck between objects and weird surround sound(?) (fighting an enemy in front of you but the sound comes from behind). All in all, the game took me about 25 hours to complete, and it’ll probably take 10 more hours if I want to find the rest of the endgame bosses and complete all the achievements. So many cons but I still recommend it; it is a decent game with fun combat, good story, great soundtrack and challenging bosses. As for the issues: yes, I know this is an indie game from a new indie studio, but coming from ex-"Blizzard, X-Legend, XPEC, and Runewaker '' developers, it is still a good game but it could’ve been better.

Definitely worth playing if you're into this sort of stuff.Now i'll rant about a few things that bugged me while playing:Slow. Elevators. Remember that elevator in Drangleic Castle? Well, all the elevators basically move at that speed.You know how straightforward Dark Souls quests are, right? Well now imagine the options to advance are 2 layers deep in a dialogue tree. Although you generally know where characters will be if you pay attention.Combo system is good, but a bit basic. (sequel pls)Early game spoiler: Too much dialogue, stuff gets repeated often, for instance a character gets mentioned. Later on you meet him, he introduces himself and Hilda (MC) is like "Who dis?"I played on Challenge difficulty, however i think, while in normal NG it was balanced how i like it, in NG+ the poor design difference for these modes starts to rear its head. This is because there are three difficulties, Casual, Adventure and Challenge. Casual gives you a ♥♥♥♥ ton of extra health, Adventure is just "normal" and Challenge gives you a -70 penalty in defense. So, you just take 70% extra damage, right? Seems ok for a hard mode? The thing is defense gear is borderline useless because of this. (Armor effectiveness is reduced by more than half, and that gap only grows as you get more armor)♥♥♥♥ Blood Vials.Anyways, a very solid start and i'm looking forward for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: makes a strong first impression but after half a dozen hours or so you'll quickly come to realize most of its mechanics and features are merely superfluous, hiding how shallow it all actually is. You gain access to all 6 weapons from the start but once you start leveling two of them there's no incentive to ever swap out the selection. Combat itself isn't bad per se but does feel like they've tried to disguise a hack-and-slash game as a Soulslike. Which, for obvious reasons, doesn't really work. Stamina isn't tied to combat and so you can basically just swing away endlessly without any major penalties. The difficulty while playing on Challenging is borderline unplayable at times as it suffers from huge spikes in difficulty and I quickly found myself sticking it on "Story" instead. Life's simply too short and this game, despite its best efforts, doesn't deserve my time what with all of the poorly designed boss fights and enemy attacks that can outright ignore geometry or reach you despite not being anywhere near the attack.The environments look nice and offer a nice change of pace from all of the dark and oppressive levels we've seen from other titles in the genre but unfortunately provide very shoddy signposting and can often become maze-like. When you are not trying to find your way around the place you'll often be stopped in your tracks by endless (and I mean ) amounts of dialogue, lore texts and other uninspired exposition dumps (have fun knocking on an inordinate amount of doors and read how "Character B" talks to "Character D" without any voice acting or flavour). For people who obsess over lore this game has you covered as there's entire novels around almost every corner and desk but for people who prefer to play a game instead of reading one at least know that you can thankfully skip most of it with the press of a button. I'm not sure what they were thinking including this many narrative elements though. I can enjoy a good story in a game as much as the next guy but the way its told in  borders on being obstructive. It's simply too much. Obviously it's a budget title and as such as can excuse some of the jankiness but even when looking past some of those issues  remains a mediocre Soulsite (I use that term loosely here) albeit with an inviting art style. It throws everything at the wall in hopes of something sticking and unfortunately most of it doesn't. It's an "okay" game at best but an incredibly frustrating one at worst. So I can only recommend this if you're somewhat new to the genre and when it's on sale at that. Otherwise you're better off playing something like  instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I am pretty surprised by this game. I picked it up at 30 dollars with the discount, and so far, I think it has been money well spent.It plays like a mix of a Souls-like and standard ARPG in the vein of God of War. The graphical fidelity is not top tier, but I find the visuals rather charming, and Hilda's model is a mix of cute (big green eyes, fiery red hair, freckles on her cheeks) and athletic, which fits the story nicely. Some environments are outstanding (outskirts, bazaar, etc) while others a little rougher, especially the Black Streets. Overall, the graphics are not a detriment to the game whatsoever.Asterigos is a Souls-like, and you'll recognize several mechanics if you're familiar with the genre, including upgrade materials, a bonfire system, verticality in location layout. However, the game is not nearly as difficult. I am playing on challenging and only died once so far to setting something on fire and not realizing it explodes. Haven't died to a boss yet. If you're looking for an Elden Ring or Sekiro difficulty, it is not Asterigos.The game rewards you for exploring with items, upgrade materials, and lore tidbits. I have to give a bonus here, as some lore tidbits also reference places where the player can find useful materials and salves (healing items). This is a great way to reward observant players. It also gives players access to places (like a rooftop or ledge) with seemingly nothing there, until you realize it gives a sight angle to see ambushes or dangerous enemies. Again, a bonus kudos for this design.The biggest negatives I've found so far is the camera controls, which on controller are a bit clunky. It is easy to get the camera facing the opposite direction the character is facing, such as when an enemy charges and you roll under him, and it can be clunky getting the camera around Hilda's back while turning. The attack, dodge, and special controls are responsive, and I've had no issues with them. The story is serviceable, though not world shattering, and the world building is done well. I find the Greek mythology inspiration interesting, and a lot of effort was put into world building. However, some of the dialogue is confusing or... odd. For example, a character early on refuses to tell Hilda about the city, because Hilda doesn't need to know, she is supposed to leave ASAP. Yet in the very same conversation the character tells Hilda that she will learn all about the city later. A small nitpick for me the names given to side NPCs, like Poor A and Poor B, or enemies named Ruffian A, Ruffian B, Ruffian C, etc. It harms immersion when you see actual generic names. Another nitpick is the tendency of characters to continually remark about Hilda's appearance. Due to lore reasons, the people in game changed, so when they see a normal human they know that human is an outsider. Despire other outsiders being in the city, everyone you talk to is surprised by it, and it gets annoying after awhile.Overall, I recommend Asterigos to fans of Souls-likes and/or ARPGs. The developers are a small indie studio, and it is clear they are talented. At 30-35 dollars (with current 10% sale) it is a solid game. I will be watching this studio, as I think they are really going places.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game, fun to play and interesting.  The animations are smooth and the weapon combos make the available move sets more expansive, especially with the small combos that involve switching weapons.There are a few minor issues, such as some missing sound effects.  Certain actions simply don't have the impact I feel the developers intended as there are no sounds or effects to augment the geometry and animations.  Don't be discouraged though if you were planning to try it; these are rare.If you go into it expecting full Dark Souls, you will be disappointed.  This game clearly had some inspiration from the series, but took several things in its own direction, and I applaud the innovation.  It's fun in its own way without needing to be a complete ripoff of Dark Souls, and if you're looking for a game in the same genre then this one is worth giving a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Twilight Princess and Dark Souls adopt Fenyx' little sister. Although the game shamelessly "borrows" many design choices and mechanics from games you know and love, the sum of its parts is definitely its own thing. Challenging but forgiving combat, with different weapon types that each comes with a skill tree. There's lots to explore in various biomes that all feel different. No quest markers, no (mini)maps, unlocking short cuts as you traverse. There's a fist full of bosses thrown at you during your adventure, with a whole set of extra optional bosses to boot. However, the storytelling is absolutely horrendous; the bare bones story is fleshed out out by a mountain of needless exposition and false drama.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played just under 8 hours of the game but there are a few things that stand out quite sharply to me. Instead of fetch and complete types of quests it allows you the ability to do quests in the order you prefer, it also has fun little side quests along the way that add to the history of the game. _childDocuments_.review: this game is a hidden gem indeed. it has many elements that makes it a good souls-like, but it also has flaws that might be the reason why this game is not popular. Let's get into it:Game Design 8/10The character design is similar to overwatch, like crossover between Disney and Japanese 3D anime. The characters are finely detailed, especially the weapons. There is this one character with over-engineered weapon that is similar to Cloud's weapon from final fantasy 7 that can morph into another forms, the problem is that this character has very short screen time lol. When you see it in action you'd wished the main character has it too. It incorporated greek-roman theme which brings you unique souls experience.Map Design 9/10Many people complain about how they can get lost easily in this game and there are no map feature to locate and mark something for you to revisit later. As souls veteran, I'm used to this and it's perfectly fine, in fact, I personally prefer it like this. There are lot of hidden places, shortcuts you can unlock later, and overall very good map design. They are detailed, make sense, and most importantly, interesting enough for you to explore. Though at the endgame section, the map design is too bland, spacious and tedious, the only place that I give thumbs down. Story and Lore 8.5/10The characters in this game are memorable because they have good writing on their dialogues and the overall plot is interesting to follow. The politics are complex, makes you have to think in different perspective to fully understand the motives of each characters. Even though the main quest is too cliche, the writing will keep you entertained. Characters also has more dialogues the more progress you made or if you have anything relevant to them.Music 7/10Music is decent. The music you can play via a certain character in the game later, are quite nice to hear. Some characters have the best VA I ever heard. Combat 6/10Enemies: Too predictable and cheese-able. Each area doesn't have a lot of enemy variations, but each enemy have several good movesets especially the bosses. The problem is, they are very predictable and combat AI is too simple to execute each moveset. For example, get closer and they do moveset A, get far away they do moveset B, drops below certain HP and they do moveset C. In dark souls, you get more variations and enemies do take side walk, keeping its distance, do simple attack before doing specific moveset, which harder to predict. Weapons: Janky, sometimes unresponsive and unbalanced.There are 6 weapons you can choose and their respective skill tree. Each weapon has unique play style and customizeable moveset depending which skill you activate. For example a twin dagger can unleash flurry of attacks and you can pick what kind of followup attack; Be it jumping slash or charged flurry, you can customize it. Some skills and weapons are just too OP that you don't need specific weapon to defeat specific enemies. You can just use that one OP weapon and skill to the endgame. You cannot change your weapon easily. You have to go to menu, select primary and secondary weapon, then go back to fight. In summary, this game has a lot combat potential but the execution is not good enough. For indie dev, it's quite decent. Gameplay 7/10You got no markers, no quest trackers, no map. It's all in the narrative and how well you remember what to do. You do have journal where the main character keep track about things she found along the road including side quests. Personally I love it, but I understand that some people will prefer the convenience of maps and trackers. The fast travel feature will be unlocked later in the game, until you have it, you got to navigate manually. Obstacles on the road prevents you from getting further but you will eventually find shortcuts, keys, or other items later to get over it. To be fair, most souls game also has no map and quest trackerWeapon upgrade, augments and "trinkets" are not that interesting. There are no poison, bleed, etc. Only poise and elements. Replayability 2/10Unfortunately, this game has bad replayability due to the broken combat and the RPG dialogues. There are lot of dialogues and cutscenes, even though you can skip most of them, they're really taking your time. Don't get me wrong, a good writing is enjoyable at the first time you see it, but become tedious on NG+. The combat is harder in NG+ but that just makes the enemy more spongy and will easily oneshot you. You can get all the achievements on single playthrough, if you're following the guide and very skilled in combat or use easiest difficulty (one of the achievement needs you to cap your level to 20).

_childDocuments_.review: This was rough but nice at the same time.Off the bat, graphics and music are pretty good, and voice acting is decent.The story is pretty nice, it has its sad moments, its ok moments, its dumb, smart, sweet moments, it had all of those, you know, in a way it's one of the more realistic stories I've played through in a game, from how characters were, their reactions, the story itself, all of it, much like how sometimes reality doesn't make sense or has it's many many different moments, or how people don't always act as they should. At least realistic in one variant of life, after all, not all lives go the same way, some go easier, others happy all the way, etc.Truly in a way it is quite praise worthy, anyway, quite an interesting ending too, although I felt like it was a bit bittersweet given what happens.For characters, I wanted to like a lot of them, but the only one I consistently liked throughout the whole game was Vulcane, truly, she was the best. Starlight and a few others were also cool. Everyone else had its annoying moments, heck, it almost felt like Hilda was becoming more annoying as the game went on (sometimes), with some things she said. However, Roxanne was by far the worst character, she single-handedly made me want to switch sides. Sheesh, she had her nice moments later in the game, but yeah, imo it's rare for her to be nice.Combat was pretty good, having 6 weapons to choose from so you can early on decide on your playstyle is fantastic. I pretty much liked all of them, although for me my favourites had to be the staff and the daggers. The enemy design was nice, but I think the boss design was better, especially with all those ones near the end of the game. One thing I gotta say though, although it's a souls-like game, it wasn't all that terribly difficult, this is from playing on normal, but, as long as you didn't mess up, even in bosses (sometimes), you'll be fine, maybe even able to finish this game deathless.There's stuff you have to learn on your own about this game, which is fair. The  caught me by surprise, not gonna lie. The crafting thing is neat, although for the most part, all those trinkets seem kinda useless because all they have is slightly higher stats, but the ones I find and get from quests and stuff have effects ON TOP of having some stats, so it's kinda meh., there were a few bugs I found besides typos here and there, for example, a visual bug is if you make Marissa play music and then go to Minerva to get the whole 'area cleared' thing, all the NPCs will then have something to say about it, however, if you talk to Marissa in this state, she won't stop playing the music, rather, she'll stand up and her lyre will start floating and moving slightly as Marissa moves.Another bug is in Laurel Craft. I'm unsure if this is how I did it, but I spotted the colossus, so I attacked him with Q and effectively killed it at a distance. Then I went closer and triggered the voiceline about the colossus, which caused me to be stuck via the gates wouldn't open. I fixed it by reloading, but it was still annoying as I didn't know I was stuck (I mean, I was literally stuck, but I didn't know that it was bugged). I respawned and kept killing the enemy, but only later, after checking gameplay, did I realize what was up.Climbing down cliffs is hard because half the time it will play the animation but not change my elevation to go down, so I'll just be momentarily floating until I fall, most often than not on the solid ground that I never left... Not to say that it wouldn't TP me to the air and just kill me other times via fall damage...In some voice lines, the mouths don't move, even in cutscenes.In the Sunken area past the Ponte Academy, after you battle that mini boss, there's an area you go down to. Well, if you go down there and choose to look up and shoot the wood to make rocks fall, if you then go to the way to climb back up but stay in the corner at the bottom, there will be a rock that lands on you, it won't kill you, you'll just be stuck inside it forever. This too gets fixed by reloading. After many of these, I sure was glad I could save anytime, and reloading it would just move me to the conduit and fully heal me.In the Glittering Deeps I assume the Turquoise Symbiosis Crystal is meant to be given to the physikoi in exchange for a trinket, like a blue starite brooch, perhaps? Well, that doesn't happen, instead, the white one is given, the same one you get at the start of the game, worse yet, you can keep giving him the crystals, ONLY after giving the normal ones can you then give the important quest item one, which gives no extra voice line, no item, nothing.Finally, the little orb that you can throw to mark places whenever is buggy, as in I can't get rid of it sometimes, I'll make it go away, but then if I ever tp to an area that had them, there's a chance that one of them will decide to be a bugged one and be there every time I appear close to it., it's a pretty nice game and can easily be an entry way to souls-like games for those that want to start on an easier one. Along with that, it has nice graphics and music, and the story is interesting with some cool characters. Do keep in mind it has some bugs though.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I'd like to say that I like the ideas and what developers at Acme wanted to do with Asterigos. Despite its very obvious and stylelized look, not very huge budged and feel to it, the game is very ambitious when it comes to lore and world building, which is a blessing and a curse at the same time, depending on peoples tastes, what they're looking for in games and what they like in this genre - which is character/story-driven dialogue heavy single player Action RPG.There's so much lore, so much dialogues, many characters to talk to for at least 10-15 min (if not more), so many various texts you can read etc., that it is owhervelming. And on top of that you can go to doors, overhear conversations and even partake in them if you want, which is a very strange design decision cuz you're basically talking with doors and not actuall characters you can see.I get that this is a way to make the game's world feel alive, but unfortunately it just doesn't work for me, it's not very interesting, ingaging or memorable, the ambition is there, but not the actual interesting part of it for you to see and experience, or at least I don't think that it was fully realized. Take A Plague Tale: Requiem for example, you can't talk for 99% of NPC's in cities and towns, but it wasn't NPC's purpouse, their purpouse was to make the world feel alive without ovhervelming you with not very needed or not interesting conversations and there was actual NPC's there, not locked doors with voices... oh, wait, I mean't texts.You see, only very few dialogues (and scattered throughout the world memories of the past) are voiced, everything else is text only. Now this is for sure related to the games budget and totally understandable. Cuz let's face it, if there's something else in the game that can be made better be it gameplay, combat, visuals and what have you... then to cut VA's budget is for sure the right thing to do in my eyes, especially since there's so much text and digalogues. Plus, the very best games of old didn't even had VA to begin with, relying on a huge amount of text instead (partly due to very small CD space budget of just 700MBs back when there was only CDs available), so... that's not a huge problem. As for the lore, billions of scrolls, text notes etc., well I'm sorry, but there's just way too much of them and I've stopped reading very lenghty ones with multiple pages. I mean, c'mon, I admire the world and lore building and it is very well written, but at one point in development you really need to make hard decisions and axe some stuff / scale it down and only leave the most important stuff for players to read. I can't say I know how it feels to not put something you worked hard on into the game you've been worked for years, but at some point you just have to make difficult decision and make your game better for it and not bloat it while chasing for ambitions.Now, let's talk about gameplay. I'm just gonna say it... I don't like combat in Astergos. It works for sure, there's multiple weapons you can use with their own playstyles so if you like it, you will have options. But in a world where Kena exists, which is a much less ambitious game overall and there's not that many weapons you can use in it, despite all that lack of variety in weapons and playstyles, it just feels better to play, more fluid visually, more polished and responsive. I can't say that combat in Asterigos is bad, far from it, I've played far, FAR worse games over the last 30 years than Asterigos, it's just to me the fact that it's just works is not enough to like it. I hoped that after the patch (which fixed and improved many things in the game) it'll be made more enjoyable, but it didn't happen.The actual design of the world is not very good also. I mean, visually it looks good and I like the art and modeling, but it's way too large, there's not such thing as easy navigation, no such thing as a map to let you explore the world and see where you've been or not yet etc. There's no way to track quests or any sort of clear, working and understandable system for this, there's a journal, but it's a mess. There's also very strange way for you to fast travel - you use scrolls to teleport to the game's main hub, but you can't teleport to places you've been already to finish side quests (which are not very good in terms of what you actually doing). You can only travel to the very last point on the map you have saved at and you can't travel freely between these points which is absolutely buffeling to me. The levels are HUGE in this game so you'll be walking and running A LOT, but to make it less boring and tedious... there's only half a solution in the game right now, while very obvious one is right there for everyone to see, which could've been less of a pain than what's in the game now. To be clear, I'm not talking about markers showing you were you need to go etc., no, the actuall world navigation and exploration of it needs to be enjoyable, but it isn't, not yet anyway.I guess to summ it all up... it's Acme's first game as a team, so I'm willing to close my eyes on a lot of things cuz let's face it, what developers strided to achieve is very, Very admiring. You can just see that there's a ton of work people put into this game, but sometimes it's not the ambitions you need to stride for, but to make the best possible game in every aspect which you can actually fully realize with what's possible looking at your budget. And with that, despite all of this criticizm, various flaws and very strange design decisions, I still think that it's a good game overall and I think there's an audience for it for sure, so it get's a Recommended rating from me.If developers are reading this - guys, I'm sure that after reading a ton of feedback you will make your next game better, it's just innevitable. _childDocuments_.review: Frankly, it started off well. Combat was slow and clunky, but the few abilities and the weapon variety seemed interesting. Unfortunately, problems just kept cropping up.Want to know where you are? Nope. Want to know how to get ANYWHERE? Nope. Want good level design that naturally leads you to objectives? Occasionally, but mostly you're just left there with literally no idea where to go and no map at all. Want an easy way to backtrack and check places? Nope, we'll only give you a 'teleport back to last bonfire-esque thing you used' and 'teleport back to hub, an area that seems to be designed to aggravate anyone that likes efficient and logical layouts. Want to upgrade your weapons? Yeah... If you randomly stumble on the furry blacksmith hidden in a corner, who easily blends in with the random background clutter in the mess of a hub. Want to not waste your time wandering down a massive pathway that makes you do a slow wading animation only to end in a gate without any prompt or hint as to how it should be opened? HAHA Nope, good one, right? Sure got me there, game! Nice one! Now I'd better teleport back to the hub and try again from the start, right? Cool!You could say 'git gud' to the above, and I did push through several zones despite the above. The issue I ran into is that I always felt like I was going the wrong way or doing the wrong thing, rather than naturally exploring. Rather than an interlocked design making the best of linear mixed with some exploration pathways, it just felt like they'd somehow done both of them, badly.I loved Elden Ring, and I enjoyed most of the Dark Souls-type games. This one is trying to borrow the general design, add in an anime-tier storyline about a girl searching for her 'papa', but it lacks most of the creative flair and intelligent design to not leave players frustrated. Unfortunate, as it started off well enough as a 'budget-ish' title. My suggestions to ease the above: Add in an optional waypoint / directional hint system (easier than redesigning the levels I imagine), add in a teleport to specific shines (or whatever they were called) with options for each one in an area, and at least TRY to hint that the random NPC in a corner behind the ten other NPCs is useful to you. Souls games are difficult and somewhat opaque, but they usually make sense once you break the surface, and usually offer you the tools to not waste hours of your time backtracking from the literal hub whenever you want to make any progress. This... Not so much.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but the similarities to the recently released Soulstice are striking - again we play a young girl who kills monsters in melee combat while exploring a city abandoned by god and the world. The city of Aphes was once the seat of an advanced civilization that researched and successfully used magic. Unfortunately, something went wrong in the process over time. Time to clear up the matter and rid the city of its problems. It's not exactly the first hack and slay action game on the market, but unlike very many competitors, it not only has the quality of graphics and animations right, but the playability fits as well. It's simply fun to move from battle to battle through the city, always getting new information about the background story. The battles aren't just against the same enemies over and over again, but against a variety of different enemies that always require new tactics to defeat.A city that has been suffering from a terrible curse for 1,000 years, full of horrible monsters and countless dangers... and a young girl is sent to sort out the situation. Typical computer game storyline, Shakespeare would turn in his grave at such a ridiculous premise, but we gamers can be glad to at least get some story. Actually, it's like that in most games anyway - we play a lonely hero who slashes his way through endless hordes of monsters in the fight against evil. And the story is actually not that bad, it is told in detail in many cutscenes, (magical) flashbacks and with the help of many written documents and contains quite a few more details than "evil wizard creates monster army and wants to conquer the world". Our decisions have an impact on the further course of the story.We play Hilda, a young warrior who is sent to investigate what happened to an expedition led by our father. Our father set out with some warriors to explore the city of Aphes - and has been missing ever since. So we'll explore Aphes, the fallen city of stars, and over the course of the game we'll try to solve its problems and restore the city to its former glory. To do this, we'll just have to destroy a few monsters. We can choose between several weapons, besides our short swords we also have a hammer, a spear and a wand (for ranged attacks) to choose from. With our shield we can block attacks. As a trained warrior, we can handle all of these things, though of course we'll get better and better as we progress through the game, focusing on specific weapons.We get to know Minerva, who has retreated with her faithful to an underground part of the city. This serves as our headquarters, where we can use the services of the blacksmith between missions or just relax. This is also where we receive new missions from Minerva. The city is influenced by Greek architecture and actually looks quite impressive... however, it is relatively empty. The interaction possibilities are limited. There are monsters hanging around every few meters, but little else is going on. A huge scenery with little content. Unfortunately, there is no overview map, and the individual sections are not that small.Using attribute points obtained in battle, certain characteristics of our heroine can be improved. Health points are increased, more damage is inflicted during attacks, and so on. Besides, there are also talent points to learn special abilities. For example, you can massively increase your efficiency with certain weapons - though of course you'll have to decide which weapon(s) you want Hilda to specialize in. Hilda can equip 2 weapons at the same time. Trinkets also improve hero attributes, while potions, salves or shards can be used for one-time bonus effects. Consumable items can of course be placed in fast access slots. Equipping two weapons at the same time and being able to quickly switch between them in combat, combined with the skills, talents and magic elements, leads - after a little practice - to incredibly fast-paced combat.A good-looking, challenging, yet accessible action-adventure game with many conversations, fast-paced combat but a relatively empty and repetitive game world.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a game made for those who want to explore and revisit areas, looking for documents and reading some lore. I enjoy those things so maybe that's why I really liked this game.After paying attention to the documents in the game and the dialogues, you can see the work that was put into making the city of Aphes was immense. It has a very intricate and solid lore. It took many aspects of the roman and greek civilizations to make a very unique magical setting. Definitely a nice work of art for me, even if the soul-like combat style isn't my preference.I got this game on sale (without DLCs) and enjoyed it a lot. Definitely recommended.WARNING: Devs state that this game pays importance to your decisions. That is true, but probably not how you would expect it to be. Decisions in this game are actually either of the following:1) Vaguely descriptive speech bubble choices during key dialogues.2) Whether or not you did a side quest. That's it. If you do a side quest it sometimes counts as a "decision". Also, to officially finish some quests, you might need to talk to an NPC even after you did everything that was relevant. Keep in mind that to get some quests/events, you might need to explore dialogue options on friendly NPCs.Another weak point on decisions is that it's not clear what you are exactly choosing most of the time. Whether doing a quest or choosing a dialogue option is going to have a positive or negative impact in the game is mostly unclear.Overall (my ranking is: 1 Awful - 2 Really bad - 3 Bad - 4 Kinda bad - 5 Mid - 6 Okay - 7 Good - 8 Pretty Good - 9 Great - 10 Amazing):Combat - Good: I'm not a fan of soul-like combat gameplay, but I still enjoyed it.Character progression - Mid: There are only 3 stats you can level up, which makes it very simple, not necessariliy a bad thing. The skill tree is nice, but equipable items are very plain and more flavor could have been easily added here.Exploration - Pretty good: Zones feel very big as you discover them, yet small once you revisit them. I think that's a really good point it its favor.Main story - Pretty good: The strongest points might be how emotions and motivations of the characters are very well portrayed in their dialogues and you can see how they struggle with their past and ideals.Side quests stories - Great: The narrative aspect can get really dark, even though the visuals are cute.Characters - Amazing: Characters have good reasons for the way they behave and the decisions they take. ThBackground lore - Amazing: Aphes is very well built, not just visually. The historical and social aspects of this city are greatly detailed.Visuals - Pretty good: Its notably weakest point is that the main character's animations are a bit bland. If it wasn't for that, the game would have great visuals.Sound - Great: The soundtracks are really good for the most part and there are some few ones that i really liked.Decisions - Bad: The decision system is just not well done. If you really care about this, please consider that it will very likely not be a satisfying point of the game.Rankings will obviously be different from person to person, so keep that in mind. I don't think this game is perfect, but also has very few remarkably weak points, and has some clear strong points. I'd recommend it if you like finding out about what's really going on in a story, beyond what is told in the main line's dialogues or if you like immersing yourself in the game's world with a beautifully detailed environment and fitting music.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is globally very good, with a lot of good ideas regarding the lore, the setting and the characters. The story is interesting and very well intertwined with the lore, and well written. Graphics are good, art style is nice, music is great, gameplay is good although pretty basic and not much varied (you learn most of the skills in the first half of the game), but the locations are all so diverse that you are never bored and are compelled to explore. It is somewhat "soul-likey" in that there are "bonfires", you lose 10% of your currency when you die, enemies respawn when you rest or die, and even critters can kill you in 4-5 hits if you are not careful, but the game is not "difficult", not even the boss fights, but it's not trivial either, at least on normal. Combat feels good even though it does not flow perfectly at all times, and the skills are cool (although you will end up using a very small subset of them). I wish that the fast travel was unlocked from the beginning, but it is enables soon enough, so no biggie. Please note that all of the "negatives" above are really minor remarks.  Now with some more substantial complaints: - some maps are a bit confusing due to the re-use of assets, which does not compromise the credibility of the locations (they are pretty well done) but it hurts navigation a lot, a map would have helped. Not necessarily and "automap" or one that you can consult from the menu, but at least a map in the environment itself, with some direction signs, or basic maps drawn on the walls, or something like that. - The thing that I liked the least (and I feel that this has made the game somewhat less enjoyable than it could have been) is quest management: the journal is a bit messy, it's hard to keep track of things because there is no outline of the active quests and sub-quests (they are only divided by locations) and at times it's difficult to understand if you are done or not because the steps appear as "comic bubbles" around pages, and the same goes with what to do next. Some activities that may impact the ending are also not tracked at all. Also, some pointers about where you can find some NPCs are very vague or are described too concisely, and this is made worse by the lack of a map. - Some choices have somewhat arbitrary consequences OR look equivalent at the moment, so at times you really feel like you don't have the elements to decide. None of these were deal-breakers for me, but they may be for someone. Anyway, aforementioned gripes aside, I really enjoyed the game and recommend it to most gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice RPG set in a somewhat northern/viking/greek/roman-inspired world. First playthrough took me about 50 hours, but that's for a rather completionist approach. Pros: World design (looks beautiful with lots of details and hidden stuff), spells & skills (choose 2 of 6 different weapons to be used for fights, each with specialized techniques), fighting system (has a really intuitive and fluent feeling to me), story (is quite elaborated and well thought through).Downsides: Quest log (there is none, you only have a diary which contains some basic information), map (there is none, but a map would make this game about 50% easier); protagonist skins (since we're talking about a very young woman / girl here, some skins are just a bit too much skin and insufficient clothing); naming of NPCs (for lack of creativity, villagers or brawlers are simply named "Villager A", "Villager B" and so forth), enemy balancing (enemies seem to be set to a certain level which doesn't change when you level up -> first bosses are really hard to fight whereas in the second playthrough you just kill them in the blink of an eye).Overall a good game, although you have to keep lots of stuff in mind (when to do what & where) since some basic tools like a quest handling system are missing, which makes it easy to miss some quests and therefor parts of the story. 7/10Note: If you like dogs, be rather careful if you want to play this one, since the developers are clearly NOT dog-persons.

_childDocuments_.review: I wholeheartedly recommend this game. The game borrows some names and the aesthetics of Greek mythology, but the story or the characters are far from just copies. The story and worldbuilding are really good. So do not worry that you will know what is going to happen if you played God of War or watched Hercules. I would say the gameplay and the story are the best parts. The quests can be confusing sometimes. There is a journal, but it does not help if you get lost, because it mainly contains the thoughts of the protagonist and not really any hints for the many quests. There is no map.Another aspect that can lead you astray, are the choices you make during the early quests. The first main quest you receive can not be done, like you are asked to. You have to keep a low profile, but you can not and even get told off by the quest giver because you had to do something you could not control. The first sidequest in the game gives you two times two different options how to proceed, but they do not change anything regarding the reward or the outcome of the quest. So naturally you would think the quest or your choices do not really matter, but a little spoiler here, the choices you make in the rest of the game matter a lot. So be careful. Maybe the point of designing the early quests this way, was to make you think about what you do onwards, but it can feel awkward in the late game, when you notice that your choices have an effect, after the game taught you they do not in the early stages. But the game was still so much fun, that I had to get all the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can see through the fact that your caracter looks like a Bratz doll from 20 years ago, this is actually a really good game, carried by the really, really good exploration. ( like REALLY good.) it will take alot of time to find all items, dokuments, chests etc.. Lots of doors that opens from the other side, ladders to kick down, mimics in chests, respawning enemies, ng+ and other soulslike elements. That being said, it has been critisized alot for having an "easy mode", but any dark-souler knows that just because theres candy infront of you, doesnt mean youll have to pick it up. So dont go easy mode, because even on hard mode its not really that hard if you are experienced in the world of souls-like games. You can however very early on put on an item (like agape ring in ds2) so you wont gain experience, meaning you can go through the game on lvl 7 or something, and also theres another item that will take 30 % of all your stats if you wear it. do that and your playthrough will be more challenging and alot more fun. As for the visual part i liked the atmosphere of the areas, but would have loved to be able to change the appearence of the "cartoonish" caracter, which just doesnt fit into the universe or the surrounding visuals Imo :) As for Controls and move-sets its pretty decent, and switching between your two carried weapons feels nice and fluid, like the game itself. Theres not any ground-breaking new mechanics you havent seen before, but If you like the exploration part of souls games, you will like this. If you however only are into the "Fighting challenge" part of soulslike games, you might get a bit dissapointed even on hard mode. For me the exploration kept me interested (still need a few chests) and ill def do annother run sometime soon, just for that "holy" achievement :)  7,5 /10

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is a fairly unusual duck in the pond of games, it's a Greek-inspired soulslike and -lite that does a lot of things right, even if its not a perfect game by any means. I definitely am curious to see what the dlc will be like and what more the team that made it can do in the future.The game takes place chiefly in the curséd city of Aphes and its surroundings where protagonist Hilda, a teen battlemaiden with magic weaponry has come to seek out the lost expedition led by her father. Aphens was once an advanced civilisation reliant heavily on magic and a rigid caste system where one man unleashed a catastrophe that turned all of the people living there into purple skinned near immortals who rely on stardust for their survival. Attempts to lift the curse have not been effective so far, in part due to there not being enough information, but also due to the martial law laid down and the inability of the noble caste to cast off their hubris.Hilda comes into contact with the Adherants, a rebel group led by Minerva who is trying to lift the curse despite being seen as criminals by the remaining archon Marble and his army and as heretics of the old faith by the Ethrus cult running amok. NVM as plain enemies by the actual criminal gangs and such. So prepare to die as you're tackling this game, though unlike in Dark Souls Hilda is merely whisked to safety on losing all hp.Something you do need to keep in mind while playing this game is that the inhabitants of Aphes have been bitterly enraged throughout the thousand years this curse has gone on. So don't expect them to be overly inclined to be reasonable or open to new ideas unless you insert them with a crowbar. You can only access portions of the city, many buildings and areas being inaccessible and a lot of in-area npc's being door-npc's (aka you talk through the door of their home). Somewhat of a pity, but understandable. There's not a ton of enemy variety but they make the most of what is there.From plumetailed critters with sickles to werewolves, minotaurs and harpies. From bandits, soldiers, elite soldiers to lions, bulls and colossi. Possessed miners to crystallised humanoids, geode monsters to hangers (snake-scorpion-bugs). There's a good selection of storyline bosses and a good few optional ones. The issue is though that the game's not very challenging on the first run, mostly relying on some cheap mobbing in places to up the difficulty as enemy AI is a bit simple.There's a lot of humor in the game as well, even if it does sometimes try a rug-pull on you. For example, when you make it to the shelter, one of the first things you'll notice is the red wolf lady working as a smith. It isn't until sometime later that you learn why a furry-like is in a game or why the explanation is in-game plausible. At least you do get a slightly oversized murderfloof to join you mid to late game who'll open up a trade shop... Khajit has wares if you have junk, neh?I have to say the big draw of the game, aside from its inspired setting, is its boss roster. The storyline ones get an introductory cutscene and do require you to think ahead. There's a few with a fair nod to Dark Souls and such, prime example being the academy boss fight. Starts off against Asterigos is a fun game, but you do need to slog through a cool to lukewarm start. Grinding for stardust is tedious, nvm fetchquests needing item x. You can mitigate it somewhat by ensuring you collect all of Quintus' lost stock so you're not entirely reliant on enemy drops. It's certainly not a perfect game, but in the end it is definitely one I'd recommend. Just be aware that there's a fair bit of uncanny valley and overly long death/revive animations.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 50 hours in game, completing most of the side quests and the first round of the game. I must say that this game gets a recommendation from me. The combat was slick with style, while not holding your hand you learn to use magic and all your weapons through the game. Learning not only monsters, but environment reactions to your weapons and element was a major factor for my enjoyment. The art style was enjoyable through out, the in game character models are distinct and memorable, while Hilda's journal held enough art to it that it felt like an entirely different game. I am looking forward to accomplishing more rounds to this game and exploring all of what I missed or could not cover in my first play through. I would recommend this whole heartily to those whom are fence on this game, it is well worth the price and I look forward to the DLC and future sequels to explore this world.

_childDocuments_.review: This game in its demo seemed very promising, but the story is so absolutely boring I found myself skipping through dialogue to just get to the next gameplay point. And that's where I find an issue. The gameplay is fun, and fast, but the number of times enemies just sit there in between animations  at you while you prep a charge attack is just very obvious. There's also moments where I've gotten hit at the end of an enemy combo, only for the character to just stand still "stunlocked" with no clear visual of why, and the enemy standing still as well. Combat itself at the core is just too easy, just spam your abilities, back off, and dodge constantly. This game is just too forgiving with its I-frames allowing for dodge roll spam, and unnecessarily punishing with AOE attacks (love a big dude falling on me 3 feet away somehow crushing me). That there is no true fast travel system except to "last point you traveled" and "hub that is way too empty early on with nothing to do", just makes this game feel hollow. I really tried to give this game a shot, but it does not scratch the itch I thought it would when I had played a demo.The walking speed in this is so slow. It feels like it was lowered so that it would take players longer to traverse maps that are fairly empty in some locations to draw out play time. I wish I had gone with my gut at just before the 2 hour mark because this is definitely a purchase I regret.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure I'd recommend it for its price, I got about 32 hours out of it and didn't do everything. It's a good game, but it's far, far from a great game. It's like baby's first souls-like adjacent game. It's got bonfires, and very light souls currency mechanic. That's about it. The pros:- Great visuals- Great music- Expansive world, like in true Dark Souls fashion, you can run from one point in the world to the other technically with never hitting a loading screen. It just makes uses of long ladders and elevators instead.The cons:- Way, way, way, way, way too much dialogue and reading!!! This game is overly story told, they just keep cramming dialogue and reading in where they can it certainly seems. It's so overdone that I actually lost interest in reading anymore, and just button mashed through dialogue not even halfway through the game. It's..ridiculous honestly. It's further insulting since there's copious amounts of flyers, posters, pages, and books to read all around the adventure that do a great job of world building on its own. You can infer just as much about the story and setting just by reading the materials instead of having a stupid amount of NPCs with overwhelming, mind-numbing dialogue. - Some hit boxes on somethings throughout the game are questionable.- Some typos here and there in dialogue, load screens, etc.- The Bracelets weapon was a disappointment. I was hyped going in expecting to have a souls-like brawler, but nope they just lock you into a slow, sluggish, very short ranged magic ball attack thing. It was very confusing, because there are brawler/monk enemies in the game who have unarmed fighting animations...is it that hard to give the main character the same thing?I may recommend it, but I'll be haunted for some time at how great this game could have been if it had just hard-line emulated Dark Souls 1 (To the creators' original artistic direction's dismay). If you played DS1 and play this, then you'll probably be disappointed and may understand where I'm coming from with this thought. It just would've been so much better with minimal dialogue & NPCs and no story direction other than what you can infer exploring and reading materials/flavor text.
