_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but nothing about it is worth recommending. I can think of many cons, but no legit pros. Here goes.CONS:- fortnite/valorant graphics, yet the game still doesnt run well compared to other games that look far better- gameplay is hella janky. Movement, hitboxes, abilities, none of it feels right- story is delivered through excessive amounts of dialogue. And I really mean excessive. These characters just wont shut up. Its like the polar opposite of Dark Souls storytelling...- audio is weird, especially water sounds. Fountains and checkpoints sound like flushing toilets- game is too easy even on the hardest difficulty, except you'll occasionally get 2-shot by bosses- you get all 6 of the weapons in the game right away. _childDocuments_.review: First of all - this game does everything correctly. It kept me hooked until I have beaten the third boss, then I suddenly lost interest. It simply felt like I had seen all aspects of the game already.Recommendation-wise: Asterigos has nice story and characters in the vein of JRPGs with its emotional and relational twists. Gameplay is mostly souls-like from the checkpoints that heal/save/respawn enemies, to the souls gathering (but used only as currency). Crafting/trading system is clearly taken from Dark Souls III, and movements/skills system from Nioh as well as potion mechanics. Sounds are great, and music is beautiful sometimes creating really nice atmosphere, and all that complemented with more than decent voice acting.All in all - I'm glad I've received a good 1 hour per euro paid here, might even finish the game in the future.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is a rather decent indie souls-like type of game with nice art direction and mostly responsive combat. Story is and characters aren't particularly memorable but they are good enough to create a believable setting. Gameplay-wise, Asterigos falls on the easier side of the genre (it is also closer to something like Kingdoms of Amalur than Dark Souls) as even on highest difficulty the timing windows for blocking and dodging are generous and enemies aren't particularly aggressive. The combat does become slightly repetitive after ~20 hours as there are only 6 weapons with limited move-sets. The game doesn't have a map which is normal for the genre yet here I wished it wasn't the case as some of the areas you're running through in early-mid section of the game are particularly similar looking (city corridors) and it might be confusing at first on where to go next and which alleyways are dead-ends you've been to before an hour ago.Overall the game is a 7/10 to me, I enjoyed it for most of the time but it would have been better if it had more variety in terms of weapons and character customisation, or if it ended few hours earlier.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually don't know why the game is not better known. It seems to be a bit of an underdog.It deserves more appreciation.The combat consists of combos with and between your two main weapons. I used sword+shield and spear most of the time and it was pretty solid. In addition you can use skills you need to unlock, like a spear thrust and so on.   Enemies don't really stand out too much and some are a bit boring. Others, also later in the game are better.Bosses were mostly not so much fun for me personally. Just a few were alright. But they are not the main driving factor of the game.The leveldesign is pretty solid as well. Some early areas look a bit empty but others are very well made and there are diffenrent areas with different main themes. Most of the are quite appealing and fun to travers and explore.The artstyle is gorgeous. Everything is well crafted and looks neat. Environment, weapons, characters, menu, items. Everything looks very appealing and was made with care and love.Story is very deep and there are alot of side quests that you can follow, if you want. I could not really get into the story tho. I didnt cared for it or the side quests but i feel if you take your time and dig into it, it would be pretty neat as well.Game still has its flaws. I would have liked a bit more customisation options, like and additional weapon slot or an actual utility belt for items. That would have made the combat more fun and fluid.Overall the game is very good for the pricetag and i would give it a solid 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Review so far, what makes me interested in this game is because it takes the concept of souls-like games. tps, exploration, hub, checkpoint such as bonfire/grace, enemies can spawn again if rest at the checkpoint, the use of stamina in combat and resources lost when die. because it's similar to souls-likes in general, so I like almost everything in this game. but no one is perfect. there are some things I like, and some things I don't like(+) difficulty option, when you die the resources not completely lost, great for people who want to try souls-like games (+) colorful visuals, beautiful (subjective)(+) combat system, I really like this one, 6 weapons and unique skill variations, the effect of the skill is very beautiful, parry is not so difficult, unlike Kena which is not clear timing parry(+) variety of enemies and boss(+) poor a, poor b, poor c. best NPC name ever!(-) cringe dialog, especially when in the mine when talking to one of the characters (don't remember what his name) (-) you can't feel character being hit by an attack, there is no effect, especially for long-range attacks, when you look at the health bar, you are already dying, unlike elden ring, sekiro, or dark souls which have details if we are hit by an opponent's attack(-) why is there no restock automated system? it's annoying to have to go back to the hub just to restock items, especially potions(-) exploration, it seems that there is no souls-like game whose exploration is as fun and satisfying, like sekiro and elden ring(-) no customization(-) elemental damage that doesn't really work significantly in combat and enemy, no effect on enemy, and no effect visually on enemy when player attackalthough there are some negative points, I still like this game. I can say this is souls-lite/souls light maybe, because it's much easier than other souls-like gameswhen you die the resources not completely lost, there is a difficulty option, you can save at any time and anywhere, and increase the attribute character by leveling up character, not by "souls"and for developer and publisherplease if you want to release a game again, don't discriminate between console and PC release time, if it's 1 or 2 years I understand, because it's a contract from the console. but if it's only for a few days, i don't know what it's for and why you distinguish the release time on console and pc

_childDocuments_.review: It's an entertaining game with a good combat system. My biggest issue is the map. Without a radar to help you navigate it, it's easy to get lost. Lots of corridors lead to dead ends. Searching for the quest location is sometimes really tough and it gets boring after a while. It's far too big for what it is, sometimes it just feels empty or repetitive.On an unrelated note, I find it a shame that a game with a Greek/antiquity theme (which is somewhat rare) has a nordic type main character (which is overused). Part of what made me buy the game was that for once we got to see something different to the many Skyrim theme copies out there, so I was a bit disappointed about that. Missed opportunity to fully get away from the omnipresent nordic theme in gaming. But this is minor.The story is great, and the combat and animations are amazing. The boss fights are difficult and really exciting, each different to one another. These are the things I really liked about the game. I'd recommend it despite the map issues mentioned earlier.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro: - Combat feels great - the world is beautiful and interesting with a surprisingly complex and compelling story - Traversing the world gave me the Souls feel of "oh! I'm here!" after exploring for a while - The map and eventual fast-travel mechanic work nicely togetherCons (ish): - Some dialogue implies there are multiple approaches to some boss fights, but there isn't,  which can be frustrating, but those fights are also fun, so I didn't fight that to be a big deal.  - The side quests can be a bit of a slog, but if you're coming from Souls then this won't be all that different - Weirdly distributed non-pre-order outfits. Only two in the base game (from what I can tell), and the rest are in NG+. Doesn't effect gameplay, it just seems weird. None of the cons were bad or annoying enough for me to stop playing, and the pros were enough that I wanted to do an NG+ run, especially since some things actually do change a bit in NG+. Very well done game for what seems like an indie developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost two hours in and I can tell it's going to be a nice game.  It's not dark souls, not sure why it's tagged "souls-like," the fight style reminds me a bit of JRPG/Nier although notes of Fromsoft are in there for sure.  The first bosses to get to the home base are a bit intimidating, especially for those who aren't used to fast combat.  Once you get to the second zone it does have a dreamy mythological feel to it which is very cool.  Good music and story as well.  But I can see the unfinished/unpolished parts mentioned in some of the comments.  I play KB&M, and have on all games unless they were uncontrollable (which I refund them if they can't).  So keep the below in context.Devs- constructive feedback:-The game seems well optimized.  I try to run my GPU on the cool side (a modest GT 1650).  Ultra high settings had it running at 96%, but toning down to just high and 60 fps cooled things down to 41%.  The game still looks gorgeous.  ADDED:  The academy section is huge and gorgeous, with good level design.-Keybinds are good, better than Elden Ring and Nier Automata, and on par with most other games.-As other players said, need a map.  If fast travel to the save spots is in there I haven't found it yet after two hours, which should tell you a lot.   It should be clear how you can travel to the home base and back to where you were without having to blink an eye, and with no map, that appears impossible.  ADDED:  I later discovered two types of scrolls that you can buy from a vendor.  One gets you to home base, the other gets you to last checkpoint machine.  But they are consumable, if you run out you're stuck.  Very awkward fast travel method.  Also, found a video that shows fast travel comes later in the game like DS1.  Considering this game was made in 2022, travel should be there from the start.-The tutorial in the journal literally has 10 sections filled in with "???" and I'm not kidding.  It's not just polish that's missing, it's pretty basic stuff.  -The descriptions in the help tutorial are way too short, basically saying nothing, and lack of tip text some pages makes the game an unknown.  For example, how you get a skill, and at what level it will unlock were/are a big mystery at the start.-This could be a really wide-open all-ages game if you'd increase the difficulty levels from 3 to 5.  Even story mode is a bit hard especially at first.-Quest markers (goes along with the map) would be really helpful.-A tutorial mode on/off would be very helpful as well especially if you want a broader audience.  In the first 10 minute there enemies and boss I faced felt like a tutorial, but it was not clear at all.  A very Fromsoft move, but please don't be FS if you want this game to reach a broad audience.  It will only result in many frustrated players and thumbs down reviews, hence ruining what could be a really wonderful game.Devs, if you actually finish this game, and add things that are customary in other games (you know, a map... and clear ways to fast travel) I think many people will love it.  Fingers crossed.All in all, it's worth playing, especially if you can get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's at least a polished and optimized game. But it completely fails to keep me interested.The art style isn't my cup of tea, with those self illuminated weapons and gadgets, as if everything is glass or plastic with built-in LED lights. The voice acting (especially one of the voices) is sometimes terrible, and sounds like your nerd friend trying to sound powerful during a live RPG.I've tried to force myself through this game. But dodging and killing monsters all the time is not what I consider fun - so I cheated with WeMod so I could focus on other things. It got a small tad funnier that way, since I could spend more time with exploration and story. But... Somewhere mid game you get some objectives in places NOT marked on your map. So you have no idea where to go. I suppose you are encouraged to explore. But that is only fun to the point where you believe you've covered every inch already, and can't figure out what spot you have missed. The levels are a maze after all, where every room looks the same as the other, and there's no map (not a useful one at least). So it gets difficult.At that point, I feel like I have milked every drop of fun there is out of this game. It wasn't much, so... Not recommended.

All enemys will respawn if you die or rest on a conduit (the eqivalent to the bonfires in the Souls games). But only if you rest. you can teleport around (later on int the game) or restock your consumables without a respawn.In the early game i got beaten down alot, till i got used to my weapons, enemys and learnd how to dodge propperly. _childDocuments_.review: This feels like a licensed PS2 game.Like a publisher saw God of War 2 and thought "wow we can make money with that" and used an available IP to make their own game. That's not what happened here obviously, but it gives me the same janky feel. Like Nightmare Before Christmas on PS2. A DMC-like that was juuuuuust a little step or two away from being amazing.It's not bad, but everything feels just slightly off.Attack animations from enemies are ambiguous, they don't have the kind of tells other games of this kind do with audio cues or visual cues, and often have lots of small follow-ups. it's really easy to get stun-locked by very quick attacks like this. The parry is completely unreliable for most attacks because of this animation issue, you can learn the moves but they don't have anything actionable you can associate with them like a Dark Souls or DMC enemy would, and on top of that, hitboxes seem to be all over the place especially with humanoids.The first real boss, a big crocodile, has a giant AoE beam that sweeps extremely fast and it's not really easily reactable, you gotta predict it and the stance he takes he also uses for a much weaker attack that you can punish for good damage. The following boss, which is a scripted fight granted, has lightning spells that will stunlock you very easily too, which he'll use to cover his other attacks, and that's fine, but it  off. It's hard to put into words what's wrong because it's just janky.I like it so far, I can deal with the jank and will likely get used to it, but it needs a lot of polish which the devs seem to be totally onboard for. I look forward to that, for now I'll just keep playing. It's a good game for what it is and if I'm totally honest I do dig the jank a bit, it's kinda nostalgic that way.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good game. Genuinely the most fun I've had with a Souls-like outside of Nioh 2. In short, it looks good given its very particular art direction, animations are smooth and solid, and combat ,while looking a bit clunky, is responsive and smooth. All the issues I have with most other souls-like games tend to be around terrible i-frame registration, stiff combat, no animation/dodge-canceling and cheap enemy tactics. In truth, there isn't a single Souls-like game I even enjoy outside of Nioh 2 which, to be fair, deserves to be in its own category and not viewed as a Souls-like. All that said, this game has none of those aforementioned issues. For being an indie-game (and it does feel like an indie game), it is very well done and polished. An easy 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very fun and well made. It feels more like a Darksiders-like than a Souls-like which is in the tags. Everything from the artstyle and gameplay, to the progression of the story and quests feels like it did in Darksiders 2. Which is a good thing. The animations are well done and combat flows really well, doesn't feel clunky at all. The world is interesting, based on Greek mythology. It's also very interconnected, you sometimes end up in a past area that you didn't think you were near. You find lots of shortcuts etc, Generally just good level design. The only thing that bugs me is that it feels like the game was made with gear and equipment drops in mind, but it was cut out last second or something. The systems are there but they aren't really used. You have slots for some trinkets, but thats it. You can make these at a smith but they don't appear on your character.And there are countless hidden areas and secrets with big shining treasure chests to loot, and in every one of them all you find is 1 or 2 upgrade materials. Which just feels kind of dissapointing after a while.It does make me think that the devs had intended to implement gear and drops but just couldn't finish that aspect up in time, or didn't have the budget.Either way very good for a new studio. Can recommend it for anyone, especially if you like Darksiders or action RPG's generally. Hoping this does well and they can make an even better sequel sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Started out slow, but once you get pass the first few bosses, the story gets intriguing. Some may dislike the Souls-like game's lack of hand-holding, but it will soon become part of the charm. Strangely enough, for an ARPG like this, the delicate intricacy of the story is what got me hooked.Looking forward to the next game this studio puts out.

However, I feel like much of it is overshadowed by the input delays. I believe they added so much delays on almost everything that the slow and unresponsive during combat. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved my time with Asterigos. The story is told well; the combat is fun with styles to play with; the graphics are really nice and the exploration is very satisfying. Giving people the option of multiple difficulties as well as NG+ is icing on the cake.I can sympathise with people who found that maybe there are too many items to read (there's a LOT) but you can simply just not read them too. Everything you really need to know is told to you by the characters you meet and the memories you find.Highly recommend this under-rated gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.Captures the worldspace inter-connectivity and pacing of DS1, with a smoother less jank combat system. It has deliberate pacing in combat (slow estus heals, attack commits, long skill casts, knockdowns, etc,) that mirrors true souls-likes yet has snappy moves, combos and general speed of something closer to elden ring or code vein. Very clean and rewarding combat; no input queuing issues or iframe jank at all.Generally great boss fights (especially towards the end of the game and in the DLC) with few long boss runs and quality design- they test the players spatial awareness and pattern recognition rather than quick twitch reactions, like a true souls-like should. Enemy movesets become increasingly diverse but always remain exceptionally readable and telegraphed, so they always seem fair (even one shots). I played primarily as a staff mage build and the enemy boss kiting felt fair; frenetic at times, most bosses had interesting gap closers and directional combos to keep a ranged combat difficult and satisfying (I played on challenge mode for reference).Story showed that you can weave a moderately complex narrative into a souls-like and enrich the game; the cutscenes and verbose dialog and notes engendered me to the story, rather than taking me out of it. Character customization felt meaningful and solid, playstyles felt diverse and unique depending on build.Can't say enough glowing remarks about this game. They took the souls-like formula and knocked it out the park. I especially like that they were able to develop a quality souls-like without any of the unfathomable genre-defining 'waste the players time as a meaningful failure consequence' design garbage that even Miyazaki has now abandoned.Don't let the unique aesthetic fool you; this is an exceptional game for souls fans, and considering its an indie title it deserves far for recognition.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very generic but I found it enjoyable for the time. When you have nothing else to play this game is a good soul like type game but more on the easier end. I felt like I used the same skills the entire game and used the same method of beating every boss. Dodge , use my ultimate ability and spam abilities. There is no boss or enemy that I though needed a different strategy. The art style is really nice and the main character is okay but the story is really boring, so if you do not like the gameplay you will hate this game. The levels are semi linear but you can go different paths that just end up to the same spot or nothing interesting besides npc dialogues. 6/10 but I recommend it for people wanting a soul type game that is not that hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Greece-themed manapunk. I love itDifficulty: Mediocre. I guess it can be a good introduction to souls-like genre. 1Gameplay: Dynamic and flashy. Six different types of weapons at your disposal with different utilization. But stances are just broken. 1Story: If Siddhartha Gautama was nurtured to help the poor, instead of becoming Buddha, he will become Uchiha Madara. There are also some speculations regading social class system, but i find them underdeveloped. 0World: Forget about the vagueness of souls-like, because you will be buried under the freakin library of internal documents what shed light on in-game events. 1Main bosses: They're distinctive and enjoyable. I would say they're all almost at they same level of difficulty. Except for Eulalia. You suck, Eulalia. 1Optional bosses: Cool creeps and they're more challenging than the main ones. But there is one but. In order to find them, you have to go to the same locations, and there is zero motivation to do so. 1Things that annoyed: - Hilda keeps her journal and, if you expect to find relevant information about quests, you're dead wrong. She almost NEVER writes down what exactly needs to be done and where to go. She just contemplates on a situation. If you postponed a quest, your only option is Google. -1- The customization of the main character is almost absent. You cannot change an apperance of your weapons. You have only one additional outfit for your first playthrough. That's it. -1- I wouldn't say that this one  annoyed me, I'm just dissapointed. Final boss is epic however extremely weak. I expected a proper challenge. -1 So, I give this game 2 bad endings out of 0. Nice game. Play it. But don't expect much. Just enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A game of constant highs and lows. At least it's not boring, but it definitely tests my patience at times. The art style and visuals are wonderfully varied and colorful with lots of dynamic, impactful animations. But the graphics can get buggy and choppy (i think it's the game reducing framerate of distant objects to save memory but doing it five feet from my face).The sound is distinct, crisp and unique with such detail and quality work that I can tell exactly what enemies are doing just from the audio. But the mixing is bugged and it always sounds like distant enemies are right next to me and the music will drown out conversations.The combat is varied, snappy, and challenging with lots of enemies that feel satisfying to fight without being too unfair. But the moveset and attacks have frustrating quirks that mean I die when it's not my fault (like the dagger dodge sometimes changing to an attack instead, thus killing you when you don't move like you expect to).There's lot's of lore, exposition and details to make for a very lived-in world that feels alive. But the character dialogue is stiff and a lot of "tell, don't show" meaning I didn't care about anyone except the blacksmith.For every point of praise, there's something that really bothers me. It's an interesting game and at least as fun as it looks. Pick it up and play, but be warned.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: LET ME SAY FIRST THAT YES, I WOULD BE UP FOR ASTERIGOS 2, BUT....It's a game of half and half, and I really wanted to wait to review this near the very end of the game. It's not a definite yes or no, but it's in the "maybe" pile. The concept is a very nice design. I want to be brutally harsh on this game on as much as possible, but before I plunge the knife, Acme did a good job. It's a learning curve to a good recipe. The edges on this first attempt are just..quite burnt. POSITIVES- Hilda. Great design, hope to see again and see more development as a person- Weapon choice. Got a little bit of freedom.- Voice acting from all is pretty good. Two thumbs up.-Elemental mechanics. Nice variation, stuff like ice putting out fire, lightning breaking goo, which also teaches you to stun mimics.-very good environmentally in terms of area design. -Butcher boss-Jumping is fluid and works quite wellNEGATIVES- Harold comes off as a..REALLY dislikable character. I feel like the game is too mean to Hilda too quickly, and a lot of characters you just won't like, and won't really grow to change that opinion. Harold's setup is worthy of a punch however. Definitely not a fault in the model design or the VA, but more a script issue? There's a lot of made-up terminology they have to make up and that'd take a lot of work, but just..yeah, the script doesn't flow for me. Could do with some polish.- Costumes are set as post-game rewards, and the preorder costume does NOT work. I don't really plan on doing multiple rounds, so this just feels like a slap in the face to miss this. It's not a core part of the game, but like, why make 3 costumes when 2 are locked, and the 3rd doesn't work? There's a lot of people complaining about this in general.- The shield mechanic within the sword+shield weapon is just not viable.- Grab attacks from mimics and centipedes deal overwhelmingly high damage, and feel a little visually uncomfortable. Would be nice to see it toned down, block some damage with a qte, or just like, something more vanilla? Have a guard throw binding bolas's or a grappler that throws you across the room or such.- The "Area-wide" blast from a certain gigantic boss is kinda poorly set, Needs a bit more, direction to guide the player close first BEFORE the callout. Chances are, if you're on the second floor still, you won't make it.-Certain quests are bugged or have poor timeframes for completion- Sword+Shield ankle slide. Great attack, but bugged if you slide into certain objects and get permanently stuck WITHIN the object.-Feather shots can pierce through certain coverIt's flawed, but good. Even with my criticism, i'd honestly say, people should buy it just to encourage Asterigos 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option.I really wanted to like Asterigos, after keeping tabs on it prior to release, but there were a few quirks with it that I struggled to get over, despite the overall game play being solid when it finally came up to play in my personal queue.The first of which was the menu/conversation navigation. You select most options with a tap of the button (A for my Xbox controller), but then the final option you have to hold it. Seems like a minor thing but it annoyed the crap out of me since there was no indication that it would be the final part of the sequence.The second is the lack of a map. This is definitely personal preference with the completionist/collector style that I play, but finding my way around to check every nook and cranny without a map - even just one on the pause screen, not necessarily a mini-map - was frustrating, especially in the early areas when I'm unfamiliar with it.Overall, I would probably recommend this for folks who like the souls-like genre, particularly if those two things don't bother you/you can ignore them. Those two personal issues aside, I enjoyed the game play itself, so I hope either A) they get tweaks or B) I can get over it to dive back in.

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite an ordinary action hack & slash game in the antique scenery.Mostly it feels like “Darksiders” but without complex 3D puzzles.The main character is a teenage girl - Hilda, who has outstanding skills in combat magic, which allows her to be considered as a full member of the elite warriors group - “Northwind Legion”. She ventures into the ancient cursed city of Aphes in order to find the missing expedition led by her father.The game has quite enjoyable styling: cartoon-like graphics with high digitalization. It pictures ancient Greece and Roman scenery: architecture, clothing, weaponry and so on. Overall visuals are very enjoyable. This is a living example which proves you do not need to create a realistic graphic to make a nice looking video game.There are many cute details. For example: there is an animation in which Hilda actually writes down an entry in her journal on the quest progress. And Vulcane can win a contest of being the cutest game character ever.However, many things are quite disappointing.There is no close camera for dialogs. All efforts put into dialog animations are almost wasted, which is a pity.Hilda can break through the stone walls, but is unable to overcome a wooden door. Sometimes she can break through the iron grid and sometimes she can not. There is no way to distinguish whether this particular one can be broken or not unless you give it a hit.The main story is trivial: beat the antagonist to control the ancient magic relic and lift the century-long curse.At some point it seems there is more in the telling. Once we kill a local gang leader, and Minerva lectures us for being careless as a new gang will definitely take his place, it seems the story-line can be more twisted. But alas, it is quite linear and bold. Why is Hilda so sure Minerva is the right person to trust? Why is Eumenides definitely a foe - after all he is trying to lift the curse as well, and her father is following him? It would be much more interesting if it was unclear which side is the correct one, or even better, if the game allowed us to choose one.There are some minor side quests, which are totally unremarkable: like “go there, bring this”. Mostly we get such quests by talking to people through the closed doors. We even give and receive objects from them without opening the doors. This looks like a cheap implementation for me.The game has a decent combat system, which is pretty standard: weapon attacks, rolls and special moves driven by astral energy. There are different types of common enemies: some are nimble, some use range attacks, some use gorilla strategy and so on. Bosses are quite unique and use a large variety of different attacks.There is no feeling of copy-paste here, which is good.There is a wide selection of weapons: sword & shield, hammer, daggers, spear, magic staff and magic bracelets. While, only two weapons can be equipped and once Hilda manages to switch between them instantly (just like “Darksiders”). You can pick the weapons pair to suit your battle style, however, in practice one of them almost always will be a staff, since it is the only ranged weapon available. Attacks can also be enhanced with elemental power: fire, ice, lightning or astral. Different enemies are resistant or vulnerable to different elements. This reminds me of “TES” series (“Skyrim” in particular). However it is far under the “Divinity: Original Sin”. Fire attacks can trigger flour dust to explode, but are unable to light a torch attached to the wall. We are unable to freeze the water or channel electricity through it.Special moves are a little disappointing. They consume astral points (AP) to be performed. These points are restored by hitting enemies with regular attacks (reminds me of the ichor from “CodeVein”). In practice you always save AP for the “special occasion” as they are depleting very quickly and restoring quite slowly. It would be much better if special moves were less powerful, but can be used more frequently.We can move the game world freely. But the locations beyond current main quest progress are always closed by obstacles: closed doors, magic barriers, poisonous vine and so on. We receive the means to bypass these obstacles only as we advance the main quest. Thus mostly the game is linear.Character development system is unremarkable. At each level up we have an attribute and skill points to spend. Most skills are linked to the particular weapon. Thus it is better to stick to the same weapon set at the beginning of the game.Sound is mostly unremarkable, but good enoughThe main disappointment is that only main quest dialogues are voiced. Despite there being tons of conversations - most of them are just text.Marissa’s songs bring some diversity into the game music, but mostly they are too short.Total rating 6-7/10. This is a decent enough action game, but it has nothing special, and many parts of it can be done much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this critique in the hopes that Acme Gamestudio (hereinafter referred to as "AGS") will read my feedback and take my suggestions for improvements into account. So far, as of my writing of this review (with the game being at patch 1.04), I would recommend Asterigos. However, I do so with caveats in my recommendation, as the moments of enjoyment I experienced while playing were interrupted by periods of  frustration that I feel didn't have to exist in this game and only were in the game because the developers mistakenly think certain frustrating elements make the game better or more satisfying to overcome. I wouldn't even be publishing this critique right now if the people working at AGS haven't clearly demonstrated their willingness to keep an open mind to constructive criticism, as is evidenced by the numerous quality-of-life improvements they introduced in patch 1.04, such as the ability to rebind controls and the removal of stamina depletion when running around without any enemies alerted to make exploration and backtracking enjoyable. With the "Asterigos: Call of the Paragons" expansion DLC scheduled to come out on February 24 next year, AGS has plenty of time to implement the suggestions I am about to offer. Most of my suggestions call for very simple changes that can probably be easily patched in a future version of the game. I hope they take my proposals to heart, because I really do think that this game needs them, especially since a lot of what I'm suggesting are things that a lot of other Asterigos players in forums have also suggested in the past.In short, the problems I have with this game can be divided into three main categories::: I thank any of the developers at AGS for taking the time to read this critique. My words may seem overly negative, but if I didn't actually enjoy the game and saw very easy and clear room for improvement, I wouldn't be writing any of this. I look forward to seeing future patches improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually a fan of the souls-like genre, but I found this game very enjoyable. I liked the Greek fantasy meets Norse fantasy aesthetic a lot, and the characters were very well managed. Many of the characters were very honor and duty driven, whether they were soldiers or aristocrats, while others were much more selfish and unscrupulous. These characteristics were present among both the 'good guys' as well as the 'bad guys'. The characters were the strong point for me, which enhanced the plot as well. The villain had a noble goal (equality) that was taken to a dangerous logical extreme (equity), which made him more interesting than a basic ♥♥♥♥♥ power monger.The voice acting was good, but there was a lot of dialogue. Too much at times, but my main issue was when new dialogue options would open up with characters you'd have to root through the dialogue trees to find them. Some games would put little icons next to dialogue options to entail that there were new options for the player to pursue, I wish Asterigos did something like that. Would've helped a lot, I was often paranoid I'd miss something so I'd just scour dialogue options just to be sure. Sometimes I ended up getting very valuable input as a result of this.Weapon balance could use some work. Daggers are probably the best, and paired with the staff you have great ranged options. Idk how you'd fix it though, as speed helps deal with many enemy attacks, but the spear had a counter attack that was a lot of fun. It's just not as reliable as dashing around with daggers, I personally would've liked a chime sound effect of some kind to accompany the spear to rely on audio cues to prompt counter opportunities rather than just try to memorize every mob's attack pattern and grunts. In the end, it was just too easy to rely on daggers to avoid damage altogether.I'd give the game a 7/10 but if I liked souls-like games more, I'd push it up. But, I enjoyed it more than I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very satisfying souls-like, probably one of the better ones made. Combat is very smooth and fluid. It does not suffer from the typical "eurojank" complaints (and yes, it is not european). There is a very heavy emphasis on story, so this is not one where you have to fill in the blanks. In addition all the NPCs are very well fleshed out with full story arcs. Great voice acting all around. Combat gives a fast dodge cancel, so that makes combat feel great. You get all weapons near the start, and playing through the game, seems you can max (+10) one weapon (possibly more?) and almost max others if you want to grind. Weapons have an attack and an alternate mode. Daggers give "dodge through" spears do parry, staff gives ranged attack. Probably staff should be mandatory as second weapon since the ranged attack is so good. You also have 4 elemental stones, which add bonus damage to attacks and can solve some environmental blockers. Each stone can be upgraded to +3, for more it is RNG with a trade partner to get materials.Crafting is used to upgrade weapons and elements and to make accessories, There are 4 accessories "slots" which can be mixed and matched at will. They may absorb certain damage types and also give some minor buffs. For players that want an absolutely brutal hardcore experience there are two early accessories to absorb all XP (no leveling) and to set all resistance types to -30. After the game is completed a NG+ mode is available.Probably my biggest complaint about the game has to do with the side quest mission structure. There are a lot of things to find and many of them relate to side quests. There are so many side quests and so many items it is hard to remember who needs what and where to find it and so on. You do have a journal and while that helps somewhat it is still difficult to figure out who needs what from where. Resolving side missions often means searching down character dialogue trees for "gold" dialogue options. That could be done better. Not getting all the items will mean some story arcs may not be completed. Which might be a minor thing unless you are a completionist.Anyway if you don't like hand holding, then this will be a game for you. Game length, probably 30-60 hours if you take your time and attempt to do all the side quests. The game is a soulslike but the difficulty is overall much easier than dark souls. Soulslike in this case means you lose some money on death, and regular monsters respawn, but not much else.

_childDocuments_.review: Still got a ways to go but I wanted to rate this while it was still on sale, I think it went a bit under the radar on release and seems to have gotten a few updates to address initial complaints.Asterigos is an action adventure game with an emphasis on combat and exploration. I think it's level design takes a few things from dark souls but if I'm being honest it doesn't actually mechanically resemble it too much. My expectation for that might come from reviews rather than the game itself, or maybe the UI. Even on hard the difficulty is much easier, it doesn't punish you past a small amount of money loss on death and you don't get a magic infinitely replenishing potion item (the one you have is something you find in the world and functions more like a slow heal over time.) On hard combat is intense enough where you need to pay attention, but moment to moment the character kind of plays like a... pretty good ps2 game. Outside of skills most weapons have 3-4 attacks and a single, permanent gimmick (bracelets make mines, spear has a parry) While a lot of the enemies are easily exploitable with -certain- attacks, I'm trying to stick with obvious intended attack use, and I think it all plays quite well. Also the hard mode, which is characteristically unbalanced in a good amount of games like this, feels pretty good. Enemies feel like they have the right amount of health so far, and my character seems to scale reliably to them.Visually the game looks great, it runs pretty good (loading map chug is apparent, might be an engine thing, idk I don't have that particular issue with most open world games) In lieu of grimdark they adopted a very cartoonish artstyle, and I think the characters are very cute. In addition to adding more variable scale to humans, I think it also makes some attack animations a little easier to read. I think the cartoony aesthetic at some points undermine story segments, where something serious will be happening or there's extremely morose or depressing dialogue, and Hilda does very exaggerated emoji expressions in response. On the note of dialogue, I don't think the "voice" is quite right. Characters like priests talk like teenagers, dialogue sometimes feels completely unnecessary and a good amount of the incidental questioning dialogue doesn't actually build up the bigger picture. It could be the prior expectation of a soulslike that's poisoning my perception of this, but I would have just liked more succinct world building dialogue.The story itself is fine. I like that it's not just a retelling of Greek myth but a genuine unique story world grounded in that mythology. There are surprisingly heavy implications for how your actions influence the world, sometimes a little forced, sometimes a little preachy, but definitely a lot more than I would have expected from a game like this. I think this game has a better establishment of moral grey area with minor couple-sentence npcs than most fantasy games do for their main stories. Technically, the game hasn't crashed for me or anything. There are a few weird collision things where I can sometimes climb up to something I'm not supposed to, but I think that's kind of fun. I like the fortnite season-esque sequential unlock of goodies from finding chests, I think that's a cute mechanic to add to a single player game, and a good motivator to search for something even if I'm certain it's another astral shard I don't need. I assume that was something added in post, since I think there were only a couple outfits on launch.Anyways, definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Asterigos is a very interesting and competent indie ""Souls-Like"" (as in "Combat is lethal, you respawn at bonfire equivalents and so do the enemies") with a very compelling setting and excellent replayability, thanks to its varied weapons and movesets : I completed the game with the Swords & Shield and the Spear (which allows Sekiro-esque parries), but you can mix & match just about any of the 6 weapons and end-up with something as outlandish as a spellcaster/bomberman hybrid with the Staff & Bracelets (but completely foregoing the blocking mechanics)Despite taking place in a single city, the locations are relatively varied with a decent level-design, even though they lack originality and can feel derivative at times : you have interesting and gorgeous locales such as an Acropolis or overgrown Greek ruins, alongside places you'd swear you've already played through, such as basically Demon's Souls' Asylum with Diablo's artstyle.The story is pretty classic, with serviceable characters ... but the setting, along with the artstyle, are pretty captivating : I loved the mix of Roman/Hellenic influences for the City and its inhabitants and Norse (for the main character) viewed through the lens of Taiwanese developers. It's full of neat and quirky ideas and reimagination of myths and concepts that I never thought I'd see, and left me longing for more of these kind of original settings for Action RPGs.I've rambled enough. Asterigos is a decent game well worth its price, especially for the first game of the studio ! I'm pretty interested in what Acme will be proposing next ! :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, it is at its core , a 3rd person action RPG. Some compare it to Fenyx Immortal Rising, which i have also played. In terms of look and theme, yes,  but Fenyx got a ton more stuff (typical of ubisoft open worlds).Eg:  There's no flying , no mounts, no real jumping and no puzzles.  Asterigos is a bit more focused, i did not find the world super open or super big, the story leads you down a fairly concentrated path with regions only opening up as you progress. Once you finish a region, you would find little reason to return other than some side-exploration. The game took way too long to open up teleporting/fast-travel, which also made the "back tracking" tedious, so i didn't do much of it until the end of the game , and by then i felt it was not particularly necessary.There's also a souls-like tag on this game, i got no idea why, this is not a souls-like. I did not find it punishingly difficult (and i do not like souls-likes for that reason ). The only souls-like thing here is how you die / resurrect at the last visited fountain (aka "save point") and enemies respawning upon death.  However, since there's a casual difficulty , i'd say the game is easy enough that this is not a major problem. These fountains are fairly well spread out and i did not feel like i ever had to backtrack too much . You can of course save anytime, but reloading will also place you at the fountain, but not always with the enemy respawned.The combat is fun, i felt there's a decent amount of styles to play. While you get all the weapons from the start, you can only use 2 weapons at a given time [no quick swapping] . The skill trees go down each weapon and can change their styles a bit. I used alot of re-spec potions [and later you can just pay a guy] to try the different styles. I did however feel the staff being the only ranged weapon made it overpowered and a requirement to be in my rotation , i would have liked more options or limits here, i felt at a disadvantage using 2 melee weapons.In terms movement/exploration the jumping and climbing in this game seems "scripted" and limited to very specific situations. Your character do not have a true jump button for example, the character will do a run-jump across gaps and can jump when there's an object it can jump over, otherwise it won't do anything. I found the story a little long winded, i did not really get into the story, i guess the presentation style did not work for me. The dialogs are often in-game and i felt would drag on too long. The end-of-chapter cinematics are just drawings on a book page and i felt like it was trying to be too poetic and not necessarily clearly telling me "this is where we are now with the story" . My biggest pet peeve is the journal / questing page . I could for the life of me, never figure out what is going on with the side quests . The whole journal page is by default written in greek

_childDocuments_.review: Well done!It's a good game with competent action combat and well-told story.Souls-like? Not really. A better description would be souls-lite. It's more dynamic and action-driven rather than methodical. Most of your actions can be cancelled at any time and dodge has wide iframes with full invulnerability. Attacking doesn't cost stamina and there is no attribute to scale it. Combat is fun and engaging.You also get all weapons from the very start and you can use two of them at the same time. There is no swap mechanics, so you can combine fast attacking daggers with shield blocking. This also adds to the fast paced, action oriented combat. I was really amazed by the animations, everything feels smooth.There are no drops and it was a good decision. You get all weapons from the very start, so you can try what combination you like. And when you start upgrading them you already know what you want to use, so there is no fomo.Armor is replaced by trinkets and they are all craftable. However, you need to find the blueprints first. It's not a very fleshed out system, but it's ok. There are also few consumables, besides HP/MP potions, but they're used for exploration purpose (or pure utility), not really as a fightning tool.The progression in every zone is linear, but the whole map is designed like Dark Souls 1 (the first half). You also don't get teleportation in the first half of the game. Generally it's very well done, but you need to pay attention and to remember where you are and where you should be going. There is no map to help you.Due to the level design, there is a lot of secrets, interconnections and hidden doors, so the exploration is a reward on its own. However, the only physical reward you get is a chest with a progression system, so every 5 or so chests you get some small reward like boots to your defenses etc.The story is surprisingly mature, despite all the cartoonish visuals and child looking main character and it's well told, for most parts. Moreover, all quests are handled in-game. There is no quest log, no arrow above your head pointing out the direction, no hand holding. Hints are given through dialogue or item description. This is how it should be done. However, it's not without a big flaw.And the big flaw is that there is too much dialogue. It's ok for character development or for the purpose of story telling, but there is also a lot of lore exposition handled through the dialog system. I believe this could have been handled better.The game is great, but it's not AAA production. Dialog outside the main story is not voiced, the cartoonish style is sometimes "too much" and it has the "off putting" feeling in it. Generally, I feel like the visuals don't match the game design.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good, story-rich action rpg, that no one noticed. The combat reminds me of Dark Souls, but feels better, especially good with keyboad and mouse, something that From can never achieve. It is done right. Not difficult, but can be challenging on hard. But there is a bigger focus on the story part of the game. Dialogues and notes, and more dialogues and notes, and more... Sadly, less important dialogues aren't voiced and it's the biggest downside of the game for me, really breaks the immersion. Lots of side quests are well hidden in those dialogues, sometimes too hidded, you need to speak with every NPC until you're sure they won't say anything new, then speak again just to be sure. The locations are well made, encouraging exploration and rewarding it. Many secrets are hidden here and there, they're also done right. Not always obvious, but nothing crazy. I had fun looking around for them. The performance is great, always stable fps on 1060 without a single frame drop or stutter. No crashes. No bugs that I could notice. it really is a big surprise during the times, when every game comes out as a broken buggy mess, that barely works. Good job devs. For me it's a solid game. I didn't expect it to be that good.

You can't even begin to form an emotional connection with anyone. You do the quest and think "Finally... ok, who's next?" Even with the main characters in the hideout, it just feels lifeless. Only transparent NPCs are shown that don't even move.-To much to read-Then a lot of text is thrown at you. Meanwhile I'm so annoyed by that, I don't care anymore and skip it.-No map yet-There is currently no map and this pisses me off. There are so many paths to explore. So many NPCs will give you quests or you will find locked chests/doors. You have to remember everything. _childDocuments_.review: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars is at times great, mostly good but on occasion bad, however, on the whole it has an impressive amount of quality content. It is good enough for me to keep an eye on the developers’ future projects. this review might be updated after the release of the DLC.The game takes place within the Cursed City of Aphes where you travel to re-establish contact with your father, the commander of an operation to cure your king from a curse. However, you quickly get involved in the matters of the city and the plots of the factions. The story feels well-paced without superfluous tangents and is broadly well told. However, there is some exceptions to this, particularly the overwhelming amount of dialogue when you first reach the . It slows the game down to a crawl and unfortunately the information you receive is not too interesting. Unless you enjoy reading about worldbuilding. These conversations are typically handled without any further player input which gives you some insight into the player character Hilda, but in certain cases you are given dialogue options. Since there are only a few of them they can have relatively large consequences such as affecting quest rewards or your progress towards a specific ending. Furthermore, this game has something called  that are recorded conversations from various points in the timeline, unfortunately they are visually completely static. Personally, these are some of the most intriguing conversations, as I love the way it lets me slowly uncover the history of Aphes and its inhabitants. There are also a number of side quests, and for the most part they could have been handled better. It is mostly fetching items or running between two characters so it can get pretty vague especially since no one repeats themselves. Yet there is a journal, surely it is of some help, right? No, the journal is mostly Hilda’s thought and reactions to the quests, which I do like, however, most people would have written down what they are supposed to be doing. As I have made clear there is a lot of reading, but there is also voice acting in this game, typically reserved for quests and . It is understandable why they limited the amount of voice acting, but what is here is not flawless either. For the most part its fine, and sometimes it gets really good, but when it is bad it is really bad and sometimes you cannot even hear them over the cacophony or music. Asterigos is obviously not a realistic game, which is good, it leans into its more fantastical aspects and gives you a lot of artistically different environments and enemies while they are still clearly of the same world. It also has a nice contrast between more vibrancy and colour versus foggy greys each making the other sections stand out more. The enemy designs are also quite cool especially some of the later enemies, such as the guards of Styx. It is quite clear what they drew influence from, and it works rather well. There is also the aforementioned journal, there are a number of things relating to it that I like. Firstly, they added the neat detail that Hilda actually writes in it when it gets updated. Secondly, and more importantly every page of it gets covered in her drawings that relate to the quests you are doing. I thought it was kind of cute. The fact that they also look good is just a bonus.Regarding the soundtrack, its great it has unique songs for bosses, areas and as rewards for completing certain quests. It knows when to be bombastic, but it also knows when more melancholic or sombre tracks suit something. It is probably the most consistently high-quality aspect of the game.   This is an Action-RPG therefore you get attribute points and talents both of which are rather self-explanatory. Naturally the talents are more interesting, you get various types that can be divided into augments which are passive, skills which you activate and perks that typically carry trade-offs, like changing a movesets. The inclusion of all of this is good particularly if you do a low-level playthrough and so can only select a limited number of talents. In such cases perks can change the way you approach an encounter while on a high-level playthrough you might mix and match perks to a greater degree.    Concerning the active skills, they are rather powerful and come in many different forms each requiring your AP resource. The quickest way to recover your AP is by drinking a potion but it also replenishes while you are fighting. I especially like the skills that includes dashes as they can be used to kite enemies while damaging them. It also synergises well since the game favours an offensive playstyle as it recovers AP more rapidly. However, the game is not difficult, enemies telegraph their attacks very clearly which makes for an easy dodge or an easier parry with the spear, as a result encounters are hardly ever a challenge, but they are fun due to the fast-paced combat and the way different weapons work together and mix their combos. One particular issue is the damage feedback when you are hit with projectiles. Sometimes Hilda does not react at all, and you might not even notice that you were hit, while in other cases you will get a devastating stun that seems to last an eternity. It is even more dangerous if you get stunned while near any lingering area of effect damage as those are atypically deadly. These things can make a few bosses a bit annoying, but it is easily surmountable as no boss is particularly complex, though a few of them are still spectacles, especially the last boss. The rest are a bit varied in quality, the worst of which being an early boss that forces you to wait for an extended amount of time, and one hours later that seemed to feature respawning enemies. As for the best it would probably be the aforementioned final boss, an optional boss that while featuring respawning enemies is an actual fight, and the three duel fights. On another note, it was rather disappointing to see that all but one of the optional bosses were locked behind an end-game event. Most of them are not even unique, as they are boss variants of enemies you have already fought against but with a few more attacks. It is fine to do it this way, but I find it a bit tragic too.   One of my favourite things about this game is the interconnectedness of the areas especially in the early game. There are shortcuts looping around within a region but there are also several unlockable paths that connect them to each other and back to the , however after unlocking teleportation the areas become more self-contained.Unfortunately, actually exploring the areas is less interesting, in general the only thing worth considering are the collectibles and the quest items, as the rest of it feels very unrewarding. Yes, there are items and chest to pick up but the only thing you receive are consumables or crafting material and in low numbers at that.What they could have done is reward you with e.g., trinkets, reusable consumables or parts of an unlockable outfit. Something like this would make certain chests stand out and the chance that you could get something special would elevate the rest of the experience Speaking of there are some chests that do stick out, because they are mimics. Outwardly I could never figure out if they have any special tells which is a problem since their grab can be lethal, but you can in fact tell them apart by striking them or by aiming at them. I dislike that that seems to be the only way as you feel foolish for attacking every chest, but the mimics are placed rather effectively, and I often found one just after letting my guard drop.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favorite soulslike - even better than Elden Ring (don't hate me for opions). The game is sort of a cross between Dark Souls and Kingdoms of Amalur (with a little Immortals: Fenyx Rising and Dragons Dogma flavor). As you would expect, there's shield-blocking, dodging, and parrying, but for some reason there's no backstabbing. I'm not sure if this was for game balance or if the devs just didn't have time to implement it. Also, parry doesn't stagger enemies so if they're in a middle of a combo, you still get hit even if you're successful and there isn't a clear sound like Dark Souls so you mainly just can tell by looking at your hp barThe combat feels less impactful than Dark Souls and maybe also Fenyx Rising - like the weapons don't feel like they have weight. It's feels more similar to Kingdoms of Amalur, but you have lock-on so that at least is better than KoA.The basic attributes don't seem to affect which weapons you can use so (love it or hate it), it's different than Dark Souls in that regard. The are special attacks to unlock so maybe stats affect which ones you can unlock idk.Also, it has an amazing OST and looks very good visually - I'm using a reshade setting that enhances it as well. The level design is hit and miss. They have the shortcuts that we all know and love from souls games, but they don't always seem necessary. They're also too big and it's easy to get lost. The enemy diversity is pretty good. They rarely ever have the same enemies from other areas.The first boss was relatively challenging on the hardest difficulty (harder than Asylum Demon, but around the first DS3 boss in difficulty). However, the 2nd boss was a lot harder. And the 3rd boss even harder. Definitely as hard as several bosses in Dark Souls. Several people in a forum thread are saying the hardest difficulty is significantly easier than Dark Souls and soulslikes, but I'm finding it almost as hard. Maybe a little easier, but not as much as some people claim.Edit: The bosses in the first half are relatively challenging and somewhat comparable to Dark Souls, but the areas are less punishing than Dark Souls. However, the normal enemies get a lot harder in the 2nd half of the game. SCREW ALL YOU SOULS HEADS FOR ACTING LIKE EVERYTHING IS EASY. YOU'RE THE REASON WHY ELDEN RING IS TRASH.I'm currently burnt out on Soulslike games and bought this because it sounded less punishing. I haven't played enough to give a final verdict (I'll change my review to negative if I change my mind later).Edit 2: I'm changing my review to negative (maybe it would be neutral if Steam had the option). This game is harder than the first 2 Dark Souls and maybe as hard as Dark Souls 3. I've beaten the game on the hardest difficulty, but some of the bosses are absolutely miserable to fight. They'll one-shot you if you don't put a bunch of points into health and they're HP sponges on top of that. It's like fighting Dark Soul bosses on New Game Plus. The last boss is the absolute worst. Full of projectile and AoE spam so you don't have a chance to get that many hits in or heal. The majority of the time you're just running around. He's what made me change my review to negative. And yes, I have beaten him on the hardest difficulty.There are a lot of little annoyances on top of that like how save games and potions work. Other things that I can't remember off the top of my head. I still stand by what I said about this being my favorite soulslike, but the problems just make me more angry every time I try to play.Below is my original positive review. Like I said at the end, I would revise my opinion once I had a better idea about the difficulty. Despite all my complaints, they at least have easier difficulty options. I just feel like I'm cheating if I lower the difficulty since I am able to beat it on Hard. I just don't feel like bashing my head against the wall for 30-60 minutes to beat a boss.Edit 3:I'm changing my review back to positive. I was salty over some of the more difficult bosses (and I still think some are poorly designed and/or too hard). Also, I found out you can change difficulty settings in the middle of the playthrough. I generally don't like doing that in games, but I can't really complain (as much) about the difficulty if I can just make it easier with in-game settings.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite Souls-like, although some would say that's not a proper comparison. I say it's similar enough that people who are into Souls-likes would like this game and thus calling this game that would only benefit more people. The changes this game makes from the typical Souls formula is only for the better in my opinion.+Melee combat with a bit of ranged and various skills.+You respawn at conduits "bonfires" where instead of losing all currency you only permanently lose like 10%.+Currency doesn't directly improve your stats but is instead used, in conjunction with rare items, to increase the stats of your weapons, elements, and to buy defensive trinkets.+The game is difficult but not unfairly so. Pay attention and use your skills and you will be good.+Selectable difficulties! And you can change them at any time. So if this style of game sounds fun you can enjoy it still on easy, unlike other Souls-likes. There's also a hard mode if you want it more difficult.+It does make a massive and positive change with the story presentation, where there is a lot of it and optional lore, making a stark contrast to Souls-likes whose stories are barebones and difficult and annoying to follow. On the one hand, you're back into the action in Souls-likes faster, but on the other if you care about such things you can learn a lot more about the world and characters here if you wish.+The side quests aren't mere fetch quests and are usually much more involved and interesting.+Side quests sometimes give you choices and these choices do have an impact on the conclusion of those characters later. The main quest will also give you choices too.+6 weapons, each completely viable to beat the game with. You can only have 2 equipped at a time, but if you desire you can swap them out with any of the other weapons at any time. Each weapon offers a completely different way to fight.+Skills add more depth to the game, where each weapon has its own skill tree and where perks will drastically change how you use that weapon, but can be disabled if you don't like the change it makes.+A lot of great and memorable characters.+The blacksmith is the cutest most kindest furry girl.+Some people say the combat doesn't feel right, I don't know what they're talking about. It feels great to me, very fluid and always does what I want it to do.+If you take your time and read every lore and exhaust all conversation options you can expect a ~40 hour game on your first playthrough. But even if you ignore that and just want to fight, it will still take you quite a bit of time. And then there's new game plus and beating the game with different weapons!+-A lot of side quests but some of them can be difficult to find. They usually aren't too hard to complete, but I had to look up a few.+-No real map. The game is huge and often interconnected and can get confusing, although that's a welcome staple of Souls-likes (learning and memorizing the layout is fun). However later in the game you do unlock the ability to fast travel between every conduit (bonfire) you've used.-Can't do the sublimation ritual and become a furry.Seriously I can't think of anything truly negative about this game. Worth the price even not on sale if you're into this type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd rather leave this one a neutral review, but since cons slightly outweigh the pros for me, negative then it shall be.So, everyone here is praising the game's story, combat, progression, etc, etc. And at the beginning, I thought the same - wow, this one's fresh, cool. What I didn't know when I started playing it was how damn boring it would become by mid-game and what a tedious chore it would end up by the grand finale. In a nutshell. + Fun and fluid combat system (that really has nothing to do with souls-like games)+ Nice story - pretty solid, albeit extremely simple+ Good progression until about mid-game+ Pleasant visuals+ Sometimes fun side quests+ Pretty interesting boss battles and boss lore (especially the endgame ones)+ Curious language/alphabet system - reading the journal, you can switch between the original text and its English translation, which, if you're inquisitive enough, can help you read all those writings on the walls in Aphes. This isn't in any way required gameplay-wise, but it sure adds to the atmosphere.+ A secret ending that you can only get if you fulfil a number of conditions (and the game won't tell you what they are, so figure it out on your own)- WAY TOO MUCH LORE. This game explains every single damn thing in its world in so much (unnecessary) detail that at some point you start thinking the writing part was given to some graphomaniac. As a person who read all the notes and item descriptions in Control and loved it, I can say Asterigos doesn't do even a lukewarm good job of its writing. It's teeming with dates, names, and events that you start forgetting as soon as you've stopped reading yet another proliferative note or plaque.- On the same note, a veritable TON of dialogues. You can chat with every meaningful character in the Shelter, and oh how much chatting it is. As soon as I saw the sheer number of dialogue options with Minerva, I realized I would never know what she has to say about many matters. And somehow I feel like I didn't lose much.- With the previous point in mind - side quest dialogue lines are hidden deep within those innumerable dialogue options, and a lot of the time the questions you need to ask to get there make no sense whatsoever. I was lucky to find that out at the beginning of the game, while I was still interested in reading and hearing every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ line of its lore. So I just skipped through entire portions of dialogue later to see if there was something related to the side quest I was trying to complete.- While NPCs are happy to chatter on for hours about trivialities and the history of Aphes, and while you're able to ask them to repeat this useless stuff any number of times, quest NPCs will  repeat what you need to do to complete their errands. So if you accidentally skipped that single line where they said what they wanted from you, or you missed the point because you were hypnotized by their ceaseless blabbering, you won't be able to ask them to repeat that one meaningful part. You're on your own now, cowboy.- Speaking of, side quest rewards are... nonexistent? Wherever I finished a side quest, the only thing I was rewarded with was a characteristic jingle. Or I might've missed something, can't say for sure. In any case, that felt pretty anti-cathartic.- Crazy amounts of backtracking. It gets much easier after a certain event mid-game, but until then you have to run back and forth with just a precious few shortcuts to help you out. Not fun.- Absolutely useless journal (apart from the language deciphering part I mentioned in the pros). Your character jots down stuff that doesn't say anything that you can use to navigate through quests, and sometimes it even leads you astray instead of giving you hints at what you should really do. - Some enemies and bosses are simple reskins of other enemies and bosses. Given that this game has a rather simplistic design to begin with, it feels like cheating on the part of devs.- You're given a choice of weapons to use, and you can switch them up all you want, as well as their respective skills, providing you with a rich variety of distinct fighting styles, but by mid-game it becomes old. Strange as it is, I was bored by all the options given me after about 25 hours in the game, and I only completed it because I thought it a waste not to after all these hours.- I'll put this one under a spoiler because it might contain some. All in all, it's not really a bad game, but it does get old after a dozen hours, and my advice would be to skip as much writing and dialogue as you can to keep your interest sparked all the way until the end titles. Otherwise, you just might drown in the swamp of empty chit-chat and feel frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game on the whole. Few flaws  Maybe 8/10. It really is trying to copy the Dark Souls game style, though it is far more upbeat.   In fact, almost everything wrong with the game is due to trying too hard to be like Dark Souls. The game on the whole is great, which I don't say often.But let's break it down a little: { PROS }+ : Nice art style.  Stylised but not too stylised.  The slightly cartoony look helps to empathise with the characters. + : Beautiful level design, at least in places. The Greek aesthetic works well.+ : Well-written story.  Lore seems decent.  And for all that it tries to be like Dark Souls, there is a lot more focus on plot.  I like that. + : Relatable characters.  Again, it deviates from Dark Souls here in the sense that the game mostly doesn't feel too lonely.  It is nice to actually chat with characters knowing that you aren't just leading them to their doom.  And they're well-written with believable personalities and motivations.  The characters are probably my favourite part of the game.+ : Weapon movesets are rather cool...  though there is an addendum I'll get to now...  { CONS }- : Lack of Customisation or Replay Value.  You play as Hilda.  No choice in that.  The alternate costumes are all garbage, so there is no point changing outfits.  The trinkets don't meaningfully change any aspects of gameplay, so there is no point changing them up.  There are two endings (one "Normal" and one "Good"), but you can get them both in one playthrough if you know what you're doing.  The only thing that changes is weapon build, but some are vastly more viable than others... so why bother changing?   The game simply has no replay value.  UNFORTUNATELY I went full hog with 100% completing the game to the point where I locked myself out of the Normal Ending... yeah....  Perfect or nothing. So I've got to replay just to get an ordinary ending. - : The game pushes the "Souls-Like" angle a bit too hard.  While it avoided the grimdark tone of FromSoft games, the whole immortality plot, campfire substitutes, respawning enemies, random platforming deaths, NG+ difficulty, and bugger knows what else just screams "Dark Souls ripoff".  I feel like the game was too constrained by rigid adherence to this formula, and could have done better by doing just about any of these things differently.  - : Labyrinthine 3D stage lay-out.  No compass.  No maps.  And in some stages, very poorly lit.  I prefer open-world games, but I don't mind linear games.  What I don't like is trying to navigate a maze where I can't work out which way I'm going except by trial and error.- : Really poor side-quest handling.  The "journal" is purely decorative.  While the only things that are truly missable are mostly inconsequential "e.g. trinkets", not even knowing whether or not you've completed a side-quest can be kinda damning sometimes. - : Collection Achievements.  It is a fact of life that in any game where there are achievements for  or whatever, 95% of my focus and energy is going to be sunk into the pointless scavenger hunt and not on the plot of the game.   At least these ones aren't missable. - : Weird lighting issues.  There is a range of artificial darkness around Hilda which is obvious by the way the distance looks brightly lit until you get close and it plunges into darkness. Much more apparent if you're using the little glowing light source, which doesn't really help with visibility most of the time but is necessary for finding chests.  - : The American dub is jarring.  The voice actors all have really strong Murican accents that sound completely out of place with the game setting. Sometimes it is hard to take the game seriously because I'm laughing at all the awful drawling.   Okay, to be fair, the voice-acting isn't "bad". It is actually pretty good, but it is also very very american. - : Not really a game fault, but since this game was never particularly popular, information on where to find things / how to complete quests / etc is kinda sparse in the community.  It HAS all been found, I believe, but I had to tap a lot of different discussions here, on Reddit and Youtube to get to the bottom of everything.Anyway...  it has been a fun time... which I expect will be considerably less so on the second playthrough I need for that last ending and the 2 achievements remaining...

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, especially for the price. I would define this as a souls-lite game, where there is obvious odes to souls games (some punishment for death, large areas with shortcuts/secrets, similar upgrade systems) but more streamlined with less to really customize. While there is skill customizations for each weapon type, this largely just replaces the fact there is six weapons and not dozens. The combat is very smooth and the dual-weapon equips really makes combat much more engaging and lets you cater the play-styles. The downside is the enemy AI is..... unbelievably basic?Lots of story, nice voice acting, way to much (but you can ignore it) exposition that is dumped. But the characters / voicing really carries it. The only two qualms I would add:1. is the world design, while nice aesthetically, is sort of poorly done in terms of exploration / pathing. Many shortcuts are borderline useless due to how frequent they are. They tend to cut very short amounts of time off running around, and they feel less like a reward for progressing than a normal souls-like game would.2. is the difficulty. currently on the hardest difficulty, the game has been incredibly easy with the sheer amount of healing mixed with a rather subpar AI. They can be slow, have super long attack tells and, with daggers or dodge rolling, super easy to avoid with i-frames.If you're looking for a hardcore experience and difficult game, this isn't it. But if you're fine relaxing to a souls-LITE game that has some excellent quality in almost every aspect, and is a super fun casual game to play, it's definitely worth it.
