_childDocuments_.review: My reaction to Asterigos was very high...and then kinda low...and then high again by the end. Allow me to explain.My first experience with the game was a bunch of youtube ads that made it seem like a AAA game and then the demo in Next Fest that sold me on the high production quality. Graphics are good, systems looked promising, world design was fantastic. I didn't have much time to play with the combat, given that you have six weapons to choose from and can use any two of them, but all things considered I figured this was a game to wishlist and wait for the price to come down since it was sure to be priced out of my cheap-ass range.And then someone bought it as a gift. So I started playing. First half hour matched the demo, and then I got to learn more about the actual story and start exploring new areas...and...I got lost. A lot. I'm fantastic at navigating 2-D spaces, but 3-D games can be tough sometimes, and Asterigos was especially tough for me. There's no map in this game, no fast travel (initially), and a decently large enough area to roam and explore and fight your way through that I enjoyed it but I knew I was fumbling my way through. And gradually I leveled up, unlocked abilities, etc. But the main NPC in the game gives you three quests out of the gate and I was stumped trying to complete them at several turns mostly just because I missed which way to turn. Plus a few other issues which were probably my own fault. But more than anything, in this phase of the game, everything felt much slower than it should have. I needed 13 hours to finish these first three quests -- I know because I made a post on the forums at the time -- and I was seriously considering bailing.Then I finished the third of those quests, unlocked an *actual* fast travel system, and the game opened way up. Following those three are four more quests in new sections of the map, and they all felt fresh and interesting and fluid. The game just absolutely took off for me at that point, and I think a big part of it was simply that I actually had some sense of geography. I also had maxed out everything I could train in my first weapon chosen and started working on a second, and being able to use the staff effectively as my second weapon choice really altered my gameplay as well. So basically I want to acknowledge that, at least for me, the game dipped initially despite many really great things going for it, but it also pulled back up and became very good by the end.So let me talk a little more specifically:Asterigos is the story of Hilda, a legionnaire from a town whose main detachment of special forces went into the legendary city of Aphes. Aphes has been essentially quarantined from the rest of the world due to a sort of curse of immortality called Asterigos. Nobody wants to go there and nobody from inside can really leave, until a mission prompts Hilda's Northwind Legion to stage operations there...without her. Three months later, she's sent to reinforce them or at least scout for their progress. She's also the legion commander's daughter, which had something to do with her being left behind, but now she's making some real waves in Aphes.Hilda fights with six different weapons -- sword, spear, 2H hammer, daggers, magic staff, and magic bracelets. You can equip any two of them and use them somewhat interchangeably. Each has a basic attack style, a special ability (like blocking, parrying, a charge attack, an aimed shot mode, a quick dash in) and each has an entire section of Hilda's talent tree dedicated to it, where you can learn several activated abilities and really specialize in that weapon. Combat will inevitably be compared to Dark Souls, which is slightly warranted, but not enough to call this a "souls-like."The art in Asterigos was one of the first draws. It's very vivid, stylized and fluid. At no point does the game ever really disappoint visually. The world and level design is fantastic (when I'm not getting lost in it) and there's great variety and a ton of work put into making Aphes feel alive. Many of the scenes in the game have full VA, with quality acting, but then the game supplements that with infodumps that are purely text. The characters in the game are generally charming and the game did have me guessing at a couple points who precisely would be the final villain. It's probably no surprise that you get to fight all the candidates for the title by the end. Hilda is very much the "hero" trope and the game even leans into this and calls her out on it at a couple points.There are a few negatives I should address. Beyond what I've already mentioned, fighting in enclosed spaces is sometimes difficult to manage in a game where you're sometimes expected to dodge-roll and counterattack because the enemy is now behind you and you can't see what they're doing. Or they're flying about you, out of reach. There is an auto-targeting mechanic, but there are times when it's better not to use it. The game is also *just* Dark Souls enough to sometimes lock you into attack animations when you aren't expecting it.However, I think the biggest thing that frustrated me with this game is falling. Asterigos has **ZERO** failsafes against falling off an edge. Most games have at least a little bit of guardrailing, but in Asterigos, you go from on the platform to off the platform and falling one pixel apart. Given that many of the battles take place around edges or while charging up ramps and stairs to hunt down archers, and it's not hard to see how you might roll defensively and find yourself flying over the edge. Or getting knocked back by an enemy and sent over the precipice. Or simply forgetting which button is your daggers' special move and suddenly lunging ahead off an elevator. That last part happened 4 or 5 times to me. (Oops.) But because of the lack of fast travel during the first half of the game, when I did this while trying to run out of an area that took a very long time to reach the end of, and then I got warped back to the bottom and had to run back out again, I got very irate at the game for wasting my time.So while this is a very quality game and you will come to appreciate it by the end, it does take a little bit of time to click -- time I almost didn't give it. You'll probably notice these things after the two-hour mark. Until then, it feels very immersive. And after the halfway point, it was very immersive. The 10-50% mark should have been, too. The bones were there. Just a few design choices and a lack of developing experience with the controls and navigating the map held it back in that interval. So not 10/10, but still very much deserves a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Another 26 hours and I still cannot suggest buying this game.I came back to it after a long break to see if it was just a mindset issue, no, its about as bad as I remember. The final bosses scripting is a bit of a joke, you are either running away forever due to stupid chasing tornado abilities, or just absolutely stomping his face into the ground.I want to go through and 100% this for my own sick twisted pleasure of owning 100% games, but this is terrible. If you play 3 hours of the game, stop there, you have played the entire game, thats it.ORIGINAL REVIEWI tried very hard to enjoy this game, and in parts I did.But there is so much pointless bloat and inconsistency in the gameplay. The combat itself is for the most part great, some bosses are a little repetitive and bland, but when 90% of the game can be mitigated by parrying with your spear which has a huge parry window, the challenge is lost.The story fell flat very very quickly to the point I just simply skipped dialogue so I could get back to the game itself, thinking I could rely on a journal or being able to talk to the character again when I missed information.Good. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Luck. While there is a journal, its a "this is how i felt about the situation" not "Damn, I really should take these supplies to everyone in the village, including in the houses, which is about as clear as mud through a telescope with no lenses.I wanted to give this game some love but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I was over it within the first few hours but wanted to give it a true shot.27 hours later and I just would rather not look at it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending only to the people who are desperately eager to play a game which includes:1. 3D close combat2. Nice looking female protagonist3. Attribute/Ability customization4. without any other additional requestsIn addition, recommending only to the people who are OK with:To be honest, the battle itself is challenging and acceptable. The attribute and ability systems are customizable and interesting. It's possible that you get killed by a mob while you are distracted. So, if you could continuously discover the joy of struggling, you could be happy/satisfied. The motivation is the problem though.As an ex-Sqaure Enix fan (I was born in 80s in Japan.) I thought for over 10 years: "Square Enix is still a good storyteller. Yet, their games often lack an integrity between story and gameplay. I'm not gonna watch movies."But ironically, Asterigos made me think the contrary. Yes, we need the both to play - A good story motivates you to move your character. A good gameplay motivates you to discover further episodes of the story. The each of them needs to be linked together well like a perpetual motion machine.Playing Asterigos gives you such a feeling like you are playing, just in 3D, a 1980s'/90s' game which no one of your school mates knew though it was allegedly not selling so bad.Personally, I am satisfied with the game because I wished the above mentioned 4 conditions anyway before the purchase and could buy it earlier for a huge discount price. However, if I had bought it for the full price, I definitely had blamed the game and myself for days.As a result, If the game costs less than 20 Euros/USD, 2000 JPY AND you are 100% sure about your wishes, then I can recommend you it. But if you pay more/have more expectations - No. I can't.Having all said, I actually have a positive feeling towards the development team since they are releasing bug fixes and improvements one after another. I don't hate the game, I think it's a pity that its story, text lines, heroine's voice and personality are so powerless in comparison to its combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this game. Bought it initially as a test for myself in the souls-like genre, but this game is so accessible for all styles of gameplay. You can have a story experience, a typical but harder than normal arpg experience, or a souls-like experience, its really up to you. Once i started playing, didn't really care about the souls-like tag, just loved the game as it is.Surprised that it was made by an indie dev then i realized it made sense, the level of polish and attention to detail has many AAA companies beat i think. I guess this is what happens when a company focuses on delivering an enjoyable product to players to gain profit, rather than a lackluster product peppered with micro-transactions and gutted content as dlc. This game gives you the whole package for the price you pay and its totally worth it.Points that i loved:Voice actingMusic [lovely]Level design, textures, detailsPerformance [no issues, smooth experience]Game play [loved parrying haha]Story line, writing, dialogueAccessibility Art [loved the journal art in particular]Points that i didn't like:Honestly i can't think of any, but many people didn't like that it doesn't have a map. I didn't like it too initially, but i got used to it after a couple of hours. Just used my memory.There's also mention of no proper quest tracking, but i didn't mind that too, since it made me listen to the dialogue and figure out where to go. Sometimes you'll just stumble on solutions in later levels haha. So yeah, I loved the game, loved the experience. I hope they'll make another in the future, there's still so much story to tell. There's characters to pursue and mysteries to explore. Really hope more people give the game a shot, You won't regret it! [well probably, depends on taste i guess haha].

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fun and satisfying, with just one or two nitpicks, like whether I stagger an enemy with my spear or not seeming to be entirely random, and which attacks I can parry and which leave me staggered also being unclear.The exploration is a bit... janky. It's got the proper "Oh god where am I going? Oh thank ♥♥♥♥ a dead end, now I know there's nothing here" kinda feel, but since it gives you all six weapon types right at the start all exploration can reward you with is upgrade materials, and that's just not terribly exciting. Useful! But not exciting.The upgrade system is also perfectly fine, I have one petty nitpick in that you can only upgrade at the home base, and depending on where you are, it can be one HELL of a walk back. This was especially annoying on the second real boss, who is miles harder than any other boss I've fought so far. Walking ALL the way back to the sanctuary just to get one more upgrade for my two main weapons was a major annoyance. It was enough of an upgrade to out DPS the boss, but I personally would prefer a fast travel system. But maybe I'm just spoiled from Dark Souls and BloodBourne letting me do that. All in all, it scratches the sould-like itch, and had some pretty cool art and designs; Solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this extremely negative review by saying this game is beautiful to look at, i really wanted to like it.  The environments were nice to look at and the art team did a great job. I even bought the deluxe edition and i will endure the game to the end regardless. That said - dark souls wannabe with 10x worse combat. There is 0 feedback when you get hit. Your character just blinks. There's no Estus, its a random healing item you pick up that cant be upgraded, slowly heals like 1/4 of your health over time and isn't renewed at the games bonfires.I'm fighting a boss where if you parry him, a secondary fire attack hits you that goes through the parry. They have designed the game to literally be at odds with how they designed it. Why make a weapons mechanic be to parry and then have the weapon mechanic be punished? 100000000000000000IQ guys well done. This game has 6 WEAPONS FOR THE ENTIRE GAME. You get all of them at the start and just upgrade them. While it seems like you can get other "outfits" it's not armour you can collect and upgrade or anything. I'm 13 hours in, not got a single new outfit yet,Now there's a boss you need to destroy crystals on 2 obelisks with waves of enemies for both, if you dont get back to the middle of the room insanely fast the boss insta kills you. This game is actually retarded. Bed of Chaos on steroidsSpeaking of upgrades, many of the upgrades are actually hidden behind character side quests. Think Dark Souls embers but much more obscure and you will likely never find them accidentally. Great, you hid a large part of the upgrade system, genius.I have memed every single boss and enemy but this one (warden), they were too easy. This boss just breaks the spear. _childDocuments_.review: A great little indie soulslike that has great style, an interesting story and a lot of love.This game is a great indie game that hits all the soulslike notes when it comes to gameplay with some unique twists of its own. For starters all the weapons you will ever need you get from the beginning of the game and you can pick any two to use at a given time with the rest easily swapped to in the pause menu. The upside to this is theres no need to run around the map collecting potentially useless weapons on the downside some of the weapons feel a lot less useful when compared to others. The other addition this game has done differently to other similar games is that this game features usable abilities that range from damaging to defensive you can have four of these active at a time and each one is not limited to using a specific weapon, although each one is linked to a specific weapon. These abilities are unlocked via skill trees, there is one skill tree per weapon. While an interesting idea some of these abilities allow you to cheese the game very easily removing a lot of the point to changing up play styles (i stuck with the same two weapons throughout the game).The games story starts off pretty similar to the souls games with the plague of undying that cant be cured type deal but the use of npcs to flesh out the relationships they have to one another, how they feel and how the class structure of the city works it does start to feel different from those games in areas. You play as a soldier called hilda whose father led the army to find the source of a curse that threatens their king, and you are trying to find them and check on their progress in the search.Visually the game is very pleasing the setting is styled after a mostly greek/ roman gods type setting with some norse thrown in with the main character. The theme mostly fits and despite a few uncanny valley feels from the protagonist it seemed to all mesh together very well.Theres some pretty good music for some of the bosses aswell as a lyre player that will play some nice instrumental tracks for you in the main hub but nothing stuck out a lot it was just pleasant and a welcome addition to the game.Overall a great game with some noticeable downsides, mainly the lack of tracking or even coherent notes for side quests and the combat could be cheesed very easily with certain abilities. Despite that I had a lot of fun with it so it deserves a 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT : After playing through the DLC i can no longer recommend this game. The DLC is EA level cash grab, maybe even worse. Stay away from this janky Dark Souls copycat You'll get your money's worth of entertainment, but at the same time this game definitely isn't a must-play. I'd say the 8/10 is a bit too high, but 6.5-7/10 would be fair.I'll split this review into two parts, there will be some spoilers about gameplay itself but not much about story, since i really didn't pay any attention to it after like first 6hours of gameplayPersonally i really like this cartoony graphics style and the game is, at times, really nice to look at.I also like the progression system of this game. Right at the begining, in like first 10minutes, the game gives you all the weapons and you are free to experiment with them all and choose the ones that suit you the best(you always have 2 weapons equipped and can use them at the same time, combine attack of both mid-combo etc..). The weapons are upgradable, but all the upgrades do is increase the dmg you deal with that particular weapon. Upgrades do cost some rescources, which are quiet easy to come by, but if you are completionst, and would aim to upgrade all of them, then some grind would be inevitable. I personally was using daggers/staff and managed to get them both within 1 playthrough to +10/+9(+10 is highest) without any grind, but with quiet throrough exploration of the maps themselves.Besides weapons and upgrades, you also gain talents and atribute points for our protagonist Hilda. Those are quiet straight forward, you get some passive buffs, you get some active abilities etc... and what is nice is that if you make mistake/want to respec for different weapon(the talent points unlock more skills for particular weapon) the you can easily do so with potion from Quintus, or later on from the Iraneous guy so thumbs up for not punishing people for bad choices and allowing players to experiment with builds.Map design, in terms of the layout, is quiet well done and if you've played the mighty Dark Souls, especially DS1, then you will immediately see a lot of similarities to that game. There is ton of shorcuts to open, maps are nicely interconnected and exploration feels rewarding in terms of loot.Game is also pretty solid on technical level. During my ~30h of gameplay i encoutered only few bugs and had to forcequit the game only once because Hilda got stuck on some box. Also ran the game on GTX970(6-7year old card) on 2nd highest settings 1920x1080 at around 60ish FPS so if your PC isn't an absolute potato you should be able to run it without much issues. Even though i've gotten my money's worth of entertainment out of this game, there definitely was quiet a few instances where i was considering to just quit and don't look back.Even though i like the graphics style, i have to leave thumbs down for the devs because of the locations they chose to put in the game. First map you start in is nice lushish forest and is really gorgeous, but then you go to village that is ran down and looks as if it was in the middle of the desert. Then you go to ugly mines, then you go even deeper into the mine,then later in game you go to Alcatraz-like looking prison, then there is the mandatory sewer level that at very first glance you are like "huh, this looks like New Londo, but worse",the shelter itself is like firelink shrine from Dark Souls 3, which i really didn't like, then you have a city that could look real nice, but doesn't because of the fog and color pallete of blue/white/grey. There is few maps i enjoyed being in, but those are definitely in minority. In future DLCs, if there will be any, i would appreciate if the devs chose more interesting, colorful maps to really make that graphics style shine, because in the base game the mark is, for the most part, missed.I praised the progression system in "The good" part of this review, but the combat itself was intetionally not mentioned there, because it doesn't deserve to be there. The combat is serviceable, but feels super clunky at times. Game does not allow for animation cancelling, which is really annoying. For example:Staff has this "fire breath" looking attack, that you have to charge(the charging part is possible to cancel) but once you release the attack, which lasts for around 3-5 seconds, you are locked in position and you  move. This is real pain and can easily cost you your life if you haven't noticed an enemy behind you. In short, please add the posibility for animation cancelling.Bosses. Some of the bosses are quiet well designed(the crocodile that you fight at the very start of the game, Twin colossi or the big bird), but some of them are downright frustrating and they feel as if they were designed for a different game. BOSS SPOILERS AHEAD.Magic enchantments-you have at your disposal 4 elements(astral, fire, ice and lightning), but they are nothing more than switches of "how much DPS am i gonna do to this enemy". One would expect that fire would, i don't know, set enemis on fire, but no. If you have fire resistant enemy, you will just do less damage, if the enemy is weak to fire you are gonna do more and same goes for all of the other elements. There are some instances where you have to use specific element , but other than that, it's just DPS switch. Story. I really wasn't paying much attention to it, which speaks for itself. One thing i will say is, that the ending cutscene feels as if it was written before the rest of the story was. I Would like to say more about this game, but sadly character limit exists so yeah, this would be it. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a very nice AA soulslike game with a bright colour palette with some dark areas and story beats. If you're looking to get into the story, side quests, characters and lore, there is a lot to chew on here and I'd highly recommend giving it a try. If you just want the combat and exploration, the game is nice but there are better alternatives out there.As someone who has never played (but knows some stuff about) Dark Souls, I feel like this game is baby's first soulslike. The combat and the level design/exploration seems very inspired by the former, although more forgiving in all fronts. The game has 2 possible endings, and most of the dialogue choices don't matter. The ones that do matter in regards to the Glory Ending (the alternate ending) can only be found out by paying a lot of attention to the lore and/or by playing more than once and paying attention to the special sound queue that plays after relevant choices are locked in. None of the choices truly alter the story in any big way, even if the narrative leads you to believe so in your first playthrough. Consider this a linear game with a normal and an alternate ending, not a choice-based game (regardless of the marketing might lead you to believe).

_childDocuments_.review: I'll update this review once I get further along, but after a few hours and taking down two bosses, I have some preliminary thoughts:1. Combat is fairly fun, although I'm not swapping around weapons as much as I thought I would be since you end up having to commit to specializing in one or two weapons. Don't get me wrong, I don't consider that to be a negative, but I was kind of expecting to be swapping weapons around to counter various enemy types based on the gameplay videos I had seen.  In the end, I decided on dagger/staff for fast attacks and ranged, and it's amazingly easy to cheese most fights with the staff since it has a sniper rifle mode. I actually stopped using that mode because it felt too powerful. Most smaller enemies fights pretty much involve rush up -> mash light attack -> enemy is stunned -> enemy dies. Larger enemies may require a bit more rolling during engagement, but so far the combat feels less risky than I was hoping on challenge difficulty.2. This is not a particularly Souls-like game. Yeah, it has a comparable bonfire mechanic and a dodge roll, but everything else plays more like an action RPG. Actually, it reminds me more of Kingdoms of Amalur that I played back in the day, with fairly smooth controls and motions. Some people have complained about control stiffness, but I haven't had any issues with a PS5 controller. Don't expect weapons and fighting to have the same weight as Dark Souls, you're going to be playing this more like Zelda (I haven't played an action RPG in awhile, so my references are a bit dated).3. I've seen a lot of complaints about the storyline and dialogue. Having gone in with zero expectations, I think it's fine. I'm not sure why people were either expecting the usual dark environmental Souls-like storytelling or a Mass Effect-level story, because you're probably not going to find too many indie games like that. It's fine for what it is, and it's been keeping me entertained.4. The sound effects are actually fairly solid, the voice acting has been tolerable, and the music is either pleasant to the ear or blends into the background. As long as the sounds/voice/music doesn't stick out badly, I'm fine with it, and that's what we have here.5. The greatest weakness of the game so far are the enemies, because there are several problems. The enemies don't engage very quickly, so it's easy to rush up and destroy them with daggers before they ever land a hit. They also have difficulty navigating around obstacles sometimes. Sometimes they don't really react much during combat, I'm not sure if they're being stunned by my flurry of attacks, or if something else is happening. Bumping up the enemy reaction speed and allowing them to block/parry/dodge me would help make combat feel a bit more engaging.6. The levels do have some Souls-like inspiration with a central hub and branching levels, but it doesn't have the same level of complexity with secret areas so far. You won't be crawling over every surface trying to find hidden areas, but there is some exploration to do. Items that you pick up won't be terribly varied, but they do serve useful purpose in upgrading weapons or creating trinkets.7. I've only run across two side quests. One had me run back and forth between two NPCs a few times, and the other was a typical fetch quest. Probably one of the weaker points of the game so far, but again, I've only played 3 hours and have only seen two quests. I'm probably not going to be expecting Witcher 3 or Greedfall level sidequests for this game, though, which wasn't really my initial expectation going in anyway.8. The only glitch I've seen so far is that sometimes the enemy model refresh rate is oddly low when sniping them from a distance. It's pretty jarring to see an enemy running at me with really low frame rate movement.In conclusion, I'd recommend this game as long as you have the right expectations going in. The thing that I think would benefit the game the most at this stage is either adding a higher difficulty level or tweaking the enemy AI to be more aggressive at the current highest difficulty level. If you're the type looking for high risk, high reward Souls-like combat, I'd go play something else. If you're fine with an action RPG that has embedded some Souls-like elements, you'll probably be happy here, especially if you're someone who usually plays on easy/normal difficulty modes.

_childDocuments_.review: For $35 game, this is a reasonable to good investment of time/money. Comparisons to AAA titles are unfair. The fact that they're being made at all is a testament to how good this game looks despite its modest polygon count. Combat feels a little clunky at first and there are certain awkward aspects that never go away. For example, you need to be standing completely still to use a potion. You can't queue a drink action during a role like you can in Dark Souls. However, once you lower your AAA expectations a little and earn enough perk points to get a build going, combat starts to feel fun and strategic. I believe there are certain exploits that might make the game too easy, but as a sword/shield and staff build, I didn't notice anything too cheesy.The lore is surprisingly good. There's a fun Greco-Roman motif with a mix of Sanderson-esque fantasy. As a connoisseur of classic literature and Brandon Sanderson, this was very satisfying. The story itself suffers a little from exposition dumps and a tell-don't-show philosophy, but most of it is skippable and the game's atmosphere is potent enough to make up for any missed exposition.I wish there was an easier way to keep track of side quest. Main quests are easy to keep track of, but for all the work that went into making the journal menu aesthetically pleasing, I wish a little more thought was given to it's functionality.Slight spoiler alert, but you eventually get the ability to teleport between waypoints. This should have been a thing from the very beginning because the world is surprisingly large and maze-like for a 10 GB game. While this fits perfectly with the whole Greek motif, it can make navigating a chore.There are occasionally odd difficulty spikes between areas, but nothing that can't be coped with a la older rpgs.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been fun, the combat is interesting and allows for several different styles. Personally I play aggressive and risky with daggers and bracelets for fast and slow attacks. There's 6 weapons in total: sword and shield, spear, staff, bracelets, daggers, and hammer. You can get damage upgrades to assign to your favorite weapons, blah blah, typical souls-like stuff here. however dying offers almost no punishment other than enemies respawning, it'd be nice if they had a soul system to buy levels and items but sadly exp is free. Personally I'm not that good at souls-like titles but I find this game to sort of be a breeze, I've counted every death in my play time and it totals to 6, 4 if you don't count falling into the endless void. So far I've beaten 3-4 bosses and haven't died to any of them. For people familiar with souls like games that want to give this a try, there's a pair of rings in the hub area that reduce all your stats by 30 and stop you from gaining exp, I recommend putting those on and playing on hard mode. YES, it has an easy mode. This would probably make for a good low-risk introduction to the genre for people that want to get an idea of what it's like. My biggest personal gripe with this game is getting from one zone to another. It's annoying and has probably taken me 45 total minutes to figure out how to get from one zone to the next so far. In the games defense, my navigation skills rival those of Roronoa Zoro.TLDR: fun but easy adventure that offers methods of boosting the challenge for veterans, somewhat unique combat system that *kinda* evolves as you get further in. The toughest challenge yet: finding the next area lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Super cool, especially for the price.Comparing it to Souls games isn't right, it's more like Nioh with a vastly simpler equipment system, though it does have some of those Soulslike influences.I think my favorite part of the game is the two weapon system, letting you kinda make up combos on the fly, and it's surprising that all six weapon types have their own switch attack that happens if you change weapons mid-combo.The characters are interesting (if really longwinded exposition-y), the setting is cool, and the combat is great.Anyway, complaints, since I don't like reviews that just list off the good stuff:1. The skill tree is kinda weak since there's six paths, one for each weapon, and that's it, unless the game unlocks something fancier later on, but I don't think it does. This means you're very unlikely to do anything more than just two paths and maybe some of the starter passives.2. You have three (3) stats to put points into. That's it.3. (Haven't gotten far enough in the game to really see it much, but) apparently the game's marketing has always been about it being some game with a bazillion choices that matter, but people have been saying there's really only like two or three situations where that's true. Also, the game tried giving me a serious choice to make, but then I looked it up later and found all three options result in the same thing, no changes.4. As much as I love it, the bracelet weapon is an abhorrent mishmash of random stuff all jammed together in one weapon, like they just couldn't decide.5. There's a whole "switch elements on the fly" system, but no way to tell what any enemy is weak to, so you're stuck randomly guessing and hopefully remembering what you find out, AND hoping you fight groups that are weak to the same things.6. Equipment is basically just "two weapons, plus four accessories" and I'm really hoping the accessories become more complex than just defensive stats later. Really hoped for something more complex than this.7. There's one of those battle pass things just randomly stapled onto the game. It's nothing bad and it's free, you just earn a point when you open a chest during your adventures and slowly unlock things as you go, but why is it even in the game?8. Jump and climb mechanics are weak. it's got that generic "climb what the devs manually marked as climbable" thing, where you'll never be sure if you're allowed to climb something or not, and you can't jump to grab onto the ledge unless they manually marked it as such too, which comes with silly moments like a rock that's a pixel higher than your jump preventing you from going up there, making you backtrack for the "proper" way.

_childDocuments_.review: Yup ! I would recommend if you like Souls games BUT don't expect super high challenges. On the ocntrary if you don't like Souls games it could fit because you can adjust the difficulty level and if you don't like horror / dark ambiences and, like me, if you enjoy more magic/mythology, Asterigos can be a good choice.Combats are nice and you have plenty tools for a flexible fighting style : 6 weapons, a good chunk of skills to unlock with points, elemental stances to change your attacks elements but also moves (depending of the weapon). Lore is pretty rich, nice variety of enemies, some bosses are neat (but overall a bit easy imo), hidden quests (you'll have to read a lot !). My only regret is not the fact you don't have a map/radar, it's the level design itself, it's a bit clunky.* Mythological vibes are great, and I enjoyed some NPC stories* Combat system, really nice and many possibilities* Weapons : the choice is large enough and interesting fighting styles* Enemies : some force you to adjust your weapons/skills. Some non-bosses are tricky* Hidden secondary quests (I like to read :P)* Different outcomes during some quests* The main character : she's neither bland nor only pretty, not even full of clichés, it's great* Most of important NPC : interesting backgrounds, no annoying ones. And kudos on Marissa's design* Music : I enjoyed Marissa's songs, I wish we could replace the default music in the basement. I should mention the participation of the talented Emi Evans (NieR !)* Starlight, I love that big boi <3* Level design is a bit off (environments but also the difficulty level)* Characters are not very properly introduced and it's often unclear, the story is sometimes confusing. Secondary characters stories are shattered and we easily lost interest or forget them* Very chatty. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:Damn. I was very pleasantly surprised by "Asterigos". I went in not expecting much really, but instead got delivered a high quality, challenging and detailed RPG with beautiful character models, exceptional boss fights, with very fluid and customizable combat system, and an engaging progression system that makes you want to explore and fight enemies. Also the game runs very smoothly and you can get super high frame rates even on maxed out settings. Cons:For all its pros listed above, there are cons, and one very major one. The worst offender is the sheer, staggering amount of expository dialogue in this game. Oh boy, it never ends. There is so much in fact, that about 60% of the total dialogue is not actually voice acted, which is extra jarring- people are talking to each other one second, and the next, complete silence for all the other dialogue choices. And when you add the document system into this, (story notes), at _MULTIPLE_ times the game slows down to an absolute CRAWL, where you are going nowhere for the next 50 minutes if you want to learn more about the cursed city of Aphes. Better click all those dialogue boxes and read all the notes. Yeah no, I gave up after like 10 hours in. Too much is too much. You will understand once you play it yourself.  The other significant one that will affect, and has affected many peoples playthroughs, is basically the complete lack of a mapping system of any kind. No large "M" button area map, or a minimap with markers. Nope. You get a dimly glowing throwable marker that will disappear into the background faster than you can take a sip of sparkling water and look back at the screen. Mostly, completely useless.  Those 2 cons are what I'd keep in mind when making the purchase- other than that, I give "Asterigos" a warm recommendation on behalf of the things the game does exceedingly well.

_childDocuments_.review: Thought it was a hidden gem.I nearly dropped it a few hours in, as I didn't get the combat at first. Turned out, I approached it as a typical hack-and-slash action, while it isn't - it's on the slower side and takes some time to understand how it works. It has its "rhythm", and it won't work if you simply mash it and hope for the best. Although the prologue can give you that impression ! Soon though, you will learn that knockdowns and parries and invulnerability animations are vital.Very solid and interesting story, although some characters feel kind of out of place the way they're written (Is Harold a Marine ?). There are choices in the story you have to make, but none are "good" or "bad" and the game will not flash a red warning sign telling you that you might regret it later. I liked the part that it's not advertised though.One of the best parts - lore, story and quests exposition is done masterfully and in a very immersive way. The journal looks like it's being written by Hilda for herself, not "the player". Same for the quest item descriptions - you have to pick up what they're for from subtle hints in the game-world. Can't think of a good term for this in videogames - but perhaps something akin to the fourth wall in theatre ?For that reason it can be sometimes difficult to say which stage of a given quest you're on - you sort of observe  as it unfolds while gathering more details - there's no checkmark to tell you "this is the last bit". There's no TL;DR - you really have to understand what's going on to proceed and I thought that was beautiful and enjoyed it thoroughly.It's open world. But an open world - without any fluff. There are chests scattered around but for every few you get a meaningful stat upgrade and valuable items. The world is up there with the ones I consider the best open world designs like Sekiro. Each zone flows seamlessly into another, sometimes intersecting - exploring it is pure fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an overall polished game with good combat and decent character and world design. It does not break any new ground as far as action RPGs go, but the parts involved are all serviceable at the very least. You can tell there was a loving craft and passion behind the project even when the game stumbles.Combat/Progression:You are given all weapons pretty much right at the start and will unlock skills that widen their movesets over time. You are encouraged to experiment a little bit towards the beginning but will most likely eventually end up with two main weapons since you can only equip two at a time. The game further ushers you in this direction through the skill tree, as you will only get enough skill points to solidly invest in two weapons. There is also an ability to change your element type on the fly, but this does not change the movesets much (staff excluded). As a result, element swap mostly amounts to just being a simple test of game knowledge.Stat investment is the other area you can customize your character, but it is extremely simple. You can only invest in damage, health, and ability point regen/damage. I found nearly no use in investing in anything but more damage and health. You can also gain trinkets that bolster your resistances, albeit only slightly. A few of them have other extra benefits, but they are all minor effects.Combat flows similarly to the newer Assassin's Creed games. You have a dodge roll, basic combos, charged attacks, blocks/parries, and magic/ranged options. You also have activated skills that are very powerful and even game breaking at times. The animations are very smooth and the controls feel very responsive leading to combat feeling satisfying and fluid. At its worst, it will seem too easy even on the harder difficulty setting. Enemy design and variety will keep things interesting enough until the end of the game, though the AI can feel janky at times.Level Design:Not too much to say here. It is fairly decent and features simpler levels that have a few branching paths and shortcuts that you can unlock creating loops. Secrets are hidden in the world here and there, but the rewards are never particularly interesting. I did find exploration fun enough on its own though to do so anyways. Story/Character/World Design:One of the weaker aspects of the game. There is some good here but the problem lies in the presentation and the volume. There are simply too many text and dialogue boxes in the game, and I say that as someone who grew up on JRPGs. It would be fine to have that much text if the writing were just of a higher quality and did more to keep you interested. This is sadly not the case but it's not all bad. I do like the characters overall and I think the voice actors are carrying a lot here too. You can tell they are really trying to do their best with the script they got. As a result, the most bearable parts of the story/dialogue are the parts that are voiced. I think the game would have actually functioned just fine if all text minus the voiced lines were cut. The voiced sections also just seem better written as well.Final Thoughts:I can definitely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys action RPGs where combat is the main draw. Expect the combat to carry the game, with serviceable parts all around otherwise. Don't expect a whole lot of innovation in its design and you will likely enjoy your time with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a proper action RPG with some familiar Soulsian tropes, like strategic bosses, emphasis on a stamina system, and the kinda-sorta bonfires that serve as save/respawn points for both yourself and enemies.Other than that, it plays more akin to classic Action RPG hack'n'slashers, like Fable or perhaps even Kingdoms of Amalur. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~I finally finished! At over 70hrs, and I'm sure I missed a few things since I didn't get the vaunted "Glory" ending, this was not a short game by any stretch of the imagination, but it was a bloody marvellous one! I had so much fun with this, the art style is lovely though the technical "quality" definitely feels date with low quality models, textures, and whatnot, but it still held together and looked quite delightful due to the colourful and slightly-less-realistic aesthetic. Music was melancholic and atmospheric, voice acting was above par, and the gameplay loop was genuinely enjoyable.Yeah, I enjoyed this immensely, and it ran *flawlessly* too, no performance issues at maximum settings and 1440p.

_childDocuments_.review: By the time i write this review, i'm currently into the third main area of the game.How is it possible that no one has ever talked or published this game before!? I actually found out about Asterigos thanks to the Souls like tag on Steam, else i would have skipped this masterpiece.This is really a AAA production masked as indie project with low budget, because the devs did wonders.Map design is great, it really feels like a true souls style quality shape. There are multiple hidden paths and treasures, verticality is very well rendered in creating the multi-path and shortcuts are tricky and smart, just like Bloodborne.The combat system is the true gem of the game. Asterigos provides a dual-weapon switch combat style, where the common "light" and "heavy" attacks are replaced by the "weapon 1" and "weapon 2" attack. Attack patterns, effects and animations depend on the combo, so mixing them is fundamental to pull out your true strength. Each weapon also has a special attack or move, which also replaces some canon souls mechanics. For example, the "parry" mechanic is bound to the Spear's special move, so if you're a veteran of the genre and you like parrying, this is the weapon for you.There are also many more combat features, such as sliding, charging and changing freely the elemental nature for your weapons, but i won't dig into them not to spoil everything!Lore wise the game is story-driven. There are many cutscenes and NPCs are not cryptic. Still, if you really want to know everything for real, you must read all the documents you find scattered in the world. There's also an Echo feature which reminds a lot of Code Vein, which recreates an event long-gone past since like a memory stored in magic.Characters are far away from being as complex as Dark Souls' ones, but they provide their fair share of progression. Politics reigns supreme in Asterigos, as it is the true engine that moves everything in the game. There are a few characters that, once met the first time, make you feel uncomfortable (they seem not convincing), but your POV will change as you progress with the lore and find out how they are like that (one example for this point is the blacksmith).Graphics are 3d styled-cartoonish, something calling out many references to the great Roman and Greek productions such as Hercules, the great Caesar and so on. And it's fine, since the game draws from that pool.The game is very well polished and optimised: in 13 hours I've never experienced a single drop of frames, stuttering or whatsoever - and i play on max settings with FSR2 on quality mode in 1440p resolution! (RTX 2070 Super)Longevity wise, the game feels way from being over on my playthrough. I'm definitely taking my time exploring every corner, every wall, every path, looking for breakable walls, mimics (♥♥♥♥ them!) and farming stardust (the "souls" currency) in order to upgrade my weapons, my elemental powers - but i'm already aware that after this area there shall be at least one more since i already have the main quest to go. Also, i already know there will be at least one more main quest later, since an entire region of the city is still locked from me.Where's the catch? Well, AI behaviour is not as smart as it should be on a souls game, they are pretty straight forward and bosses only are very fun to fight against. Also, i play on the highest difficulty and the game doesn't sound so much punishing. I've died some times, and i only lost some stardust from my count, instead of dropping them all and move back to retreive them (so you permanently lose some currency on each death, but you never drop it).I could talk a lot more about all the other mechanics, but i won't spoil anymore.This game is a masterpiece and the music is so great.Don't make my mistake, get this game now and but the Ultimate Edition. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had Asterigos on my wishlist for months before finally giving it a try (haven't played the DLC). I'm the kind of player who would become incredibly frustrated with Dark Souls and Bloodborne (I played some of the latter and quit early because of said frustration), but Asterigos offers me a similar kind, but easier, challenge, even on normal. This game feels ACCESSIBLE. I cannot overstate how overjoyed I am about this, too. I play on normal, so I can imagine easy will be even better for those who need more breathing room than I do when playing a game. That's not to say that it's dirt easy, though, I was left a little frustrated with some encounters, but not to the extent that made me quit Bloodborne before I'd even progressed past the first area.The story is amazing. If you're used to loads of hints on where to go next, it might be a bit challenging, but if you've the heart of an explorer like me, this won't be much of a problem - the game pretty much goes out of its way to reward exploration! If you like to delve into lore, there's a bunch of documents and dialogue (even if not fully voice-acted) that will paint a clear picture of Aphes and its history.If you're aesthetically inclined, Asterigos is also a clear winner. The character and environment design is just stunning. I'm a great fan of the effects, too.I know some feel that combat can become a bit repetitive, but I'm not sure I agree - the enemies are quite varied, and you need to learn how their attacks work to time your parries (I really love the spear) and dodges, as well as to effectively counter.TL;DR: This is a story-rich, accessible, semi-soulslike and beautiful game that I wholly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been one for Soulslike games, but this one is a lot of fun. I was initially drawn to the game by Malukah's cover of "Nostalgia," and the music in game did not disappoint.The story is fantastic, and malleable, story mode is wonderful for a casual or a newbie to Soulslike games, and the optional challenges are amazing. Collection logs, optional bosses, secret locations, there is so much to do and find.I very much enjoy the side stories you can choose to participate in, and how the smallest details can change the outcome of any event. Crafting & upgrades are simple, and the wide variety of traits allows for varied builds of all sorts.Some of the writing choices make me very angry, however. The player is considered a child, and no one lets that fact go. From everyone doubting the abilities of the individual who single handedly toppled three criminal organizations that the Legion couldn't handle, as well as assaulted the Legion fortress itself and came out on top, simply because you're a child, to being belittled by important allied individuals, many characters make my blood boil.Worse still is that not only does the main character accept this treatment, she eventually apologizes to the individuals belittling her and says they were right. When events actually proved the player right, somehow she sees it as her being wrong.Do I recommend the DLC? I purchased Paragon & the Northwind outfit on sale.The outfit was wonderful for just a few dollars, a small buff that's useful even into late game, and what I personally think is the best outfit in the game. Very fitting for the character. Most of the negative reviews on the outfit are from people angry that the preorder reward is available as a cheap DLC, and they're right to be angry about that. But that aside, it was worth getting (on sale).The Paragons DLC was also worth it, to me, on sale. The outfit that comes with it wasn't to my tastes, and I definitely don't see it as a plus. The weapon mods are interesting and useful, allowing for fun experimentation. The boss fights are more involved than the main game fights, and really turn up the challenge, even in story mode one mistake can be fatal in some of them. Buying it when I got the game was a good choice, as there is not a ton of content there. Buying it after having played would have felt less satisfying.Summary: A wonderful game, loads of fun, be prepared to be treated like you're simultaneously a heroic great warrior and a five year old throwing a tantrum because others don't think your accomplishments deserve any respect, the DLCs are worth buying, but only when on sale, and best bought when you start playing rather than later on.

_childDocuments_.review: Disney meets Dark Souls. No. Seriously, it feels like sometimes.You play as a stronger than hundred men teenager girl who is half the size of any adult and is constantly trying to prove herself.There is a lot of lore laying around the game like documents and images for you to waste time reading and collecting to probably forget a few minutes after. Believe me I've read everything I found in game and frankly there is sometimes too much, but you can just skip to the action anyway, every dialogue option and cutscene is skipable except end credits.The story itself is okay, you try to help some people to lift a curse that's so bad it makes everyone immortal to the point everyone just wishes to die.There are a lot of self righteous and whiny npcs that makes it feels like the world is so unfair and that anything you do trying to help them just makes them angrier and whinier and blame you for their lack of strength to make the world their utopic vision.The game itself is quite fun, I enjoyed the combat and it has some mechanics like dodge, limited potions each checkpoint, dodge, respawning enemies if you die or rest in checkpoints, newgame+, block with shield, parry with spear, weirdly spinning with a hammer and also a staff that can be used as if it was a longbow, you can aím it!What you see is what you get. The weapons you get in the early game are the same you gonna see the entire game, there are no finding cool weapons or shining armors around, but with a 6 weapon type variety in combat and they can combo together, they're also upgradeable and each weapon has its own talent tree with abilities and perks which makes things interesting. Perhaps adding new weapons and outfits would make things better.Difficult itself isn't that much even if you play in challenge mode, the bosses could be something more, they tend to be pretty friendly and allow you to heal up and giving you enough openings to destroy them with ease despite their fancy moveset but the game has its challenging moments.Graphics wise it's a really good looking game and has stuff like scaling fsr and the performance is good. I only encountered a bug that happens sometimes where the talent page font gets black making it hard to read them, but if you restart the game it fixes. Probably they gonna fix it soon in future updates.It's a good and entertaining with the combat and talents, there's a nice story and annoying npcs and dialogues. I can easily recommend though, but I think the upcoming dlc should be part of the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good Soulslike, albeit not the hardest, I still have a long way to go and so far it's been amazing. You can make the game harder by using optional accessories that can be obtained in the main hub area that prevent level-up and reduce defenses. You can cheese most enemies but for fun's sake I choose not to use cheese strats to make it funner. The world is huge and interesting to explore not to mention amazing art and OST to accompany explorations. Overall an amazing game, there are changes I would make (harder difficulty and some minor balance issues) definitely one of the funnest games I've played in recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good! The art style is very appealing, characteristic but not without details. Especially details in costumes and materials. Different zones have different environments and atmosphere, I had fun exploring around and enjoying the view.In my opinion, the combat part isn't as attractive as the graphic. I expected more dramatic moves in battle when I saw its art style. The attack moves aren't bad, they are smooth and solid, just not what I expected. The story obviously has an important role in this game, I can find many things to read or inspect everywhere. Puzzling pieces from different people or papers together brought so much fun to me! I'd try to find everything in a zone before moving on, that's probably why I'm still in early zones lol

_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah I was wrapped up in this game within the first 46 minutes. Couple hours in now and I have really been enjoying it! It plays amazingly smooth. Combat feels very fluid! How the weapons function change over time the more you delve into their respective skill trees. I can genuinely say that all 5 weapons are super interesting and I'm having a hard time deciding which ones I want to focus on! A fun problem to have. Only thing I haven't seen yet are different armors/outfits but there is clearly an indication for other options. We'll see.Update after finishing: The story was pretty whatever honestly, I could never really get engaged with it and you can only finally get a new armor once you beat the game. Once you max out your weapons, you're really just stuck with nothing to look forward except more bosses that don't actually reward you with anything except more currency to buy potion with, woohoo. Solid game just zero armors or weapon designs to look forward to. What you start with is all there isThe bosses themselves were cool tho and the areas were honestly pretty unique and fun to explore. Combat was good throughout the whole game and parrying with the shield was honestly TRULY enjoyable, I just loved doing it. Wish you could get cooler looking versions of your weapons..but oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: While I overall enjoyed this game, there are a few key criticisms that I have of it.- Hilda- Basically Dark Souls meets Immortals: Phoenix Rising- Some of the later levels, such as  and , were really fun to explore- I really enjoyed using the Daggers and the Staff (the two weapons types that I decided to focus on during my playthrough)- The game felt pretty polished, and I only encountered a few minor bugs during my playthrough.- Way too much dialogue- By the end of the game, I completely ran out of things that I wanted to spend my talent points on. I was focusing on Daggers and the Staff, but I reached a point where the only thing I could do was spec in other weapons that I wasn't planning on actually using.- Extremely lackluster post-boss cutscenes that don't really add anything of substance to the game- I personally just wasn't that interested in overarching story and the main antagonist- The quest journal is horrendously designed and has abysmal organization. There is currently no way to see if a quest is actually completed or not, and no way to track side quests.- Finally, there are an excessive amount of scripted events that temporarily take control of your character away from you

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like it could have been really fun if the interface and controls had been done competently. Unfortunately, they haven't.First off, I play on an AZERTY keyboard and those are not fully supported. It means I can't configure controls properly and had to switch to QWERTY layout. Whoever in this day and age designs their keyboard API to use actual inputs instad of key position needs to step up their game, this is not 2003. On an AZERTY keyboard, the keys that would be 1 2 3 4 on a QWERTY are accentuated characters. The game doesn't support those, so not only can I not bind anything there manually, but anything that would be triggered by 1 2 3 or 4 doesn't work either unless I change my layout.Then, movements are clunky AF. By default, jump is on... G ? At this point, don't bother including a jump. Items on W X and C (ZXC for QWERTY users) ? Sure, it can be rebinded, but see the above point.This could be somewhat forgiveable if combat was fun, but it's meh. Weapons are rather uninspired, special moves are kinda weird, and dodge... Well, it exists. And when you do dodge, you get hit anyway because of the huge hitbox of the enemy attack, and the camera which either won't let you face your enemy or won't let you see where you are going and might get you stuck into something.The game isn't terrible, but the amount of jank is just too damn high to bother with it. If you're looking for a greek myths inspired game, play Immortals Fenyx Rising instead, at least in that one you're fighting enemies, not the game itself.Refund requested.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I tried so hard to like Asterigos.The first five or so hours were very intriguing. I found myself going out of the way to look for and rifle through every piece of lore. I wanted to know more about this city, what happened to it, why so many character were at odds... Then at about the seven, or eight hour mark, I stopped caring. About the lore, characters, zones, etc. And after fifteen hours, I ran from objective to objective, not stopping to fight unless I absolutely had to, simply to be done with it all.The boring world and its bland characters would have been less of an issue had the gameplay been ever-changing. But it wasn't. It became stale fast. There is very little variety. Every weapon in-game is given to you from the jump and from there, you simply upgrade them to make them stronger while also distributing attribute and talent points in certain trees to cater to your "playstyle" (which is a term I use very loosely as, again, the lack of variety is mind-numbing). However, I will be honest: all of these upgrades did not matter. Once I learned the dagger spin-to-win move, I blasted through every enemy and boss with very little issue. And so that's what the game became: running through every area, using the same skill over and over and over again until the credits rolled.I have been told the End Game is pretty redeeming? But it took me 20 hours to finish the base game and I have zero interest in going back. I can appreciate what they were trying to do here, but almost everything fell flat. That said, I must give props to the composer. The music is gorgeous and was by far the best part of this otherwise very dull experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Asterigos: Curse of the Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Devs, sorry for a bad review. I see that you put a lot of work in this title, but if you don't know how to do a soulsborne mechanics right - just don't do it.Combat is a main break point - and this is a focus mechanic of the whole game. Unpleasantly slow, unresponsive, and sluggish. We are not wearing Havel's Set here, and look at Bloodborne or Nioh - she don't need to be so slow.A small tip for you:Reduce inactivity frames, speed up her attacks for 20% and general speed for at least 30%, make her rolls longer and faster - if it plays more fun this way - implement it.Enemies have a very badly telegraphed attacks. And with such unresponsive controls and wobbly camera this is a problem.Another tip:Make a small blink ( visual and sound ) when we need to parry/evade enemy's attacks - this way you don't need to rework all animations for better readability.And, to be honest, combat style like in Nier: Automata is a better fit for this title.And another tip:Don't waste player time on dialogs, stories, and don't take his controls!If heroine comments something - let me move freely.Less blah-blah - more action. This is a start of the game, I want to explore, learn combat and gain level ups. I don't want to stuck and listen a tone of graphomania lore and "how to play" on 3 pages. Also, there is to much "press and hold" stuff going on in UI.Also a question:Why you don't did a pause on ESC? This is a single player title and players can step away from the computer from time to time.I hope that you will follow a Thymesia devs example and listen what your player base says. Till then - refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game.  To see my point, here is my opinion in short sticking points:+ great and recognizable art design+ great environment and world design, done with many care+ big (linear) world with much to explore+ interesting story and well done character design+ good music, consistent with the environment+ crisp combat+ difficulty by settings and self set handicaps+ immense skill tree and other options to customize the play stile- teleport too late in the game(after about 25%)- no detailed map/mini map, might be hard for people with bad directional sense- no detailed quest lock(just mini lock for main quests) which tells you what to do next, diary instead which tells you what you have done lastThe bads where none in my opinion, I really liked the dev's decision to not implement a map that made me much more invested in the world which looks so beautiful and a very detailed. In the end I know every nook and cranny. Also, the decision prevents people from skipping anything interesting and checking the game off their checklist, which the game does not deserve it in the slightest. The late teleport initially made me worry that I would get story locked from the content,  but every time that might have happened, there was a prompt that prevented me from doing so. The game is perfectly polished, so no negatives on that side. I found my favorite game of 2022 in Asterigos and I'm hyped for Call of the Paragons in 2023.I totally recommend Asterigos, give the game a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Baby's first Souls-like. The demo of this game made such a strong impression I was so pumped for it but in the past two months I just cannot get myself to progress further than a little over 10 hours in. There is a full skill tree but it's amazingly shallow. The upgrade system exists but I'm not entirely sure why as the upgrades are so minuscule compared to the item investments. Graphics are decent, with Hilda being the highlight, but the environments are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring. The hardest games to talk about aren't those that are exceptional or awful but ones like this. Everything just feels so painfully average. I don't hate Asterigos by any means but compared to how much I want to like it I'm just disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being in souls-like genre, this game has a difficulty slider. An appreciated feature for those who are new to the genre and want to try it first without experiencing the trauma from difficulty (Thank you, Dark Souls!).Visuals is fantastic. Love the match-up of Pixar-looking graphics and the greek-mythology artstyle. Movements are flashy when they need to be and the game did not abuse particle effects, unlike other Triple-A games. I did not experience any visual issues the entire game.Soundtrack is also really good. It's so good that in some boss fight, I had to turn down the background music because it was hyping me too much.Storytelling is good and the game is rich in lore. They made an effort to really dig into the details of the main NPCs in the game in a way that their own side-quests reveal details about them.World-building is great. Lots of areas to explore and things to uncover. Each biome is unique on its own and at the same time coherent with one another (meaning you can go from one area to another without needing to fast travel) and it almost feels like open-world. Enemies did not feel repetitive at all. And there's very minimal boss-now-normal-mobs-later issue.After-input delays - my biggest gripe in this game. The developers implemented so much delay in between every action that combat can oftentimes feel clunky and slow. You're using potions and you want to dodge an incoming attack? Delay. You want to double-dodge? Delay. You dodged and now you want to aim your ranged weapon? Guess what, delay!TL:DRSupport good small indie devs! It's one of those underrated indie games. Games like these are like gems of our lifetime - very hard to find.

And some of the skills can gimp you in some ways while giving you a bones in others.  Im only 6h in but i can see that it can get really interesting with the builds! _childDocuments_.review: Hey, you guys made a wonderful game here. It's beautiful and fun and I'm excited to see all it has to offer. You have made some bizarre and annoying interface decisions that you really need to fix.>Why is there a half-second delay with the jump? Annoying. Make the response instant as expected in literally every game ever made.  >ELIMINATE THE PRESS AND HOLD SELECTION. Bad news: Nobody in the human race wants that or likes that. It's annoying. Get rid of it. >Forcing the user to press yet another button to transform the journal text from gibberish to readable is ridiculous. I get it, immersion. But in this case: NO. Make it a readable human language from the start. Very stupid.>The save screen should close immediately after a save. You are not a Japanese company. Be more modern. >And finally, a personal pet peeve: "Ask about herself." THIS IS INCORRECT ENGLISH. It's "Ask about her." You get it? Adding "-self" to a word does not make it a more formal version. There is a specific grammatical instance for "herself" "himself" and THIS IS NOT IT. These should all be easy fixes that will elevate this otherwise wonderful classic-feeling game out of the amateur space and into the pro space. USABILITY.

It was also just the second game with Soulslike mechanics I had ever played (the first being Elden Ring, which I hadn't even finished yet), so I was kind of a noob at the time. Upon returning to this game for a second playthrough a year and a half later with somewhat more experience, I found it to be a much more mixed bag than I remembered.(A quick note before I start parsing it out, though: throughout this review I'm going to be referring to this game as a Soulslike, which, I'm sure, is going to make some other people who have played this game roll their eyes. _childDocuments_.review: Love the game, the mechanic, world-building, story and characters are great!However, the side-quest is a bit hard because there was no tracker what-so-ever, so most of my time spent going around wondering where to go, or trying to figure out what's next on the side-quest. Spear counter-attack is very satisfying while dagger's skill is mostly to cheese your enemy if you plan to win the game under level (level 20 or below achievement). Sword and Gauntlet is okay..? then the rest I just dont find the charm in their 'special ability'. But all and all, really enjoy the game. And the lovely art ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really like the game. Combat had some promise in the beginning but at some point I just went the lazy route of mining everything instead of spamming attack. I also like the character growth our MC goes through after one event in the beginning, which causes her to be more critical of her actions. There were also some thought provoking topics happening in dialogues with the other npc's which I honestly love. I mean, Aphes is based on ancient Rome after all. _childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Aphes – a city-state full of magic and wonder inspired by ancient Rome and classical Greek designs. From the mist-covered bazaar streets to gloomy sewers, the enigmatic forests at the city’s outskirts to deep chasms full of glittering crystals, the landscapes of Aphes are full of beauty and dangers. Choose from a variety of ranged and melee weapons on the go and combine them as you wish! The talent system allows you to pick and expand your combat style by choosing two out of six completely different weapons: sword and shield, dual blades, spear, hammer, staff or even magic bracelets. Equip a magical staff to obliterate your foes from the distance or switch to a gigantic battle hammer to squish them in a close combat. Whilst Aphes might distract you with its breathtaking views, this city is not for the faint of heart. Fight your way through 60 different monsters and encounter 22 unique bosses – each with its own unique battle mechanics. Every choice and every decision you make matters. Your journey in Aphes will lead you to discover the truth behind the city’s curse, letting you piece together its history through conversations, discovered documents and cinematics, as well as Hilda’s own diary, which she’ll update with sketches and observations. The world of Asterigos is full of secrets and untold stories. Find over 100 collectibles, complete numerous side quests and build on your legacy in the New Game+ mode!

name: Phantom Fury
detailed_description: Shelly “Bombshell” Harrison is back in this highly interactive mix of first person action and road movie adventure. Embark on an adrenaline-fueled journey around the USA. Use an enormous arsenal of weapons and skills to battle treacherous soldiers and vile mutants, all while trying to save mankind. Taking place many years after her fight against Jadus Heskel, Shelly “Bombshell” Harrison awakes in a new world, pulled out of a coma at the behest of an old colleague, with a new bionic arm. Tasked with securing a highly dangerous artifact, the legendary Demon Core, Shelly embarks on an intense journey around the US, as she tries to overcome her own past to save mankind’s future. Key Features An intense mixture of bombastic action and road movie - Fight through seedy hotels in Albuquerque, explore abandoned facilities in Los Alamos, secure the streets of Chicago, and so much more! An insanely interactive world - An incredible amount of interactivity brings the environments to life. Fully usable computers, helicopter flights, playable arcade machines are only a few examples of what you can expect. A vast array of weapons - Over 20 unique weapons are at your disposal! Fan favorites like the Bowling Bombs are joined by brand-new equipment such as armor-piercing shotguns and electrified foam shooting devices. Unlockable weapon upgrades and mods with completely new fire functions will give you the necessary control needed to overcome any fight the way you want! A wide range of unlockable skills and upgrades - Weapons aren’t the only way to overcome the many challenges waiting along the way. Upgrade your bionic arm and suit with powerful new abilities, such as a punch attack or an electric shield. A terrifying number of enemies - Encounter vicious cyborgs, menacing soldiers and disgusting mutations, each with their own special skills. Push your skills to the limit in exhilarating boss battles.

_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a different format for reviewing games.  Titles like this straddle the line between "recommend" and "not recommend".  Phantom Fury is not done.  It has bugs, some levels (especially the open format ones) feel unfinished, the game is clearly lacking ambient sound, the AI is pretty bad, etc.However, I've had fun with it.  I'm on the 12th of 15 chapters, and not once have I thought the core gameplay is bad.  The weapons hit hard, the level design is good, and the enemies, while not varied, are fun to fight.  The game has had 2 patches since launch, and they have improved the game quite a bit in regards to the bugs and sometimes spotty performance.  I think this title is something that anyone who likes the type of FPS titles that were released in the late 90s to mid 2000s would enjoy.  It's no Half-Life 2 or Far Cry, but it's worth 10 bucks or so.  Wait for it to go on sale and scoop it then. It's not nearly as bad as forums and youtubers would have you believe.
