_childDocuments_.review: Also fire your audio director.With the discussions around the game being generally negative (and rightly so after that demo), I wanted to take a look at the gameplay to see if the negativity really is warranted. What follows below is  that caught my attention during the first level of the game.It starts with me realizing that 3DR really did pull down the demo after everyone rightly ♥♥♥♥ on it. They never put it back up, or updated it with the "fixes" that were "almost there but not ready for the demo's release". So thank god Steam support is very generous with refunds. That's definitely not the best start after all the demo drama.The first thing that catches my attention is the graphics, or just how mismatched it feels to be exact. The Colonel stares down at me with oddly smooth and , yet the rest of his textures are pixelated to fit the Ion Fury style. In fact, a lot of models are weirdly high-poly yet have texturing that would match a more low-poly model. This isn't as bad as it sounds, but it's just noticeable enough for you to pick up on it.The Colonel phases out of the room as you conveniently glance away, as you never hear the door open or close. I then go to punch my way out of the room and break the dash ability on the punch by using it on the slope . Another fun fact, if the game loads directly here skipping the cutscene, the door model doesn't even load at all but the collision remains.Some tutorial box with a missing keybind. Weird! This happens quite a lot, even with things I didn't rebind.Around this point I start throwing objects around, and it feels like . I don't want to say  did it better, but the standard for throwing stuff was set in 2004. When you throw things in this game, they just glide through the air as if moved by an invisible force. , which is something objects would actually do if someone ever threw them. It looks  bad and like it was quickly slapped in to the game. Also, objects that impact surfaces make almost no noise. Glass beakers and vials make the tiniest tinkle as they shatter, and even some larger objects just make a quiet "bump".After making my way through and finding the baton, I watch rubble from a falling ceiling rise up out of the floor before the debris from the ceiling even has time to hit the floor. Weird! There's a keypad here with a code you can physically input, which would be neat if the pad highlight followed your mouse input properly. Pressing a number causes it to delay with the tracking and freak out.Also vents display their broken graphic if hit by an explosion, but their collision isn't removed.Then I get the pistol. You use the pistol to shoot down a ladder, which you completely just noclip onto. Like, you don't holster your weapons, there's no camera bobble or anything, there's not even . You just float upwards and get spit out next to it. It feels extremely lazy.After a couple of melee swings to hit the electricity box in the same area, I noticed that Shelly wasn't making any sound at all. Like, not a peep out of her as she whips around slaming people with her arm (and baton). Not a grunt, yell, or even just a sharp exhale. This sounds trivial, but it's the little details like these that help to sell things like weight and impact. This even applies to things like climbing and sliding. The only noises Shelly makes are pain grunts. I am being dead serious, she has 20 lines for pain grunts, 1 line for eating, and a pant VO. I don't even know if this panting VO is used since I never heard it (like at low hp or sprinting).And I should probably mention Shelly's voice.  I can't tell if they recorded her lines in a cardboard box, or if this was a... "stylistic" choice. She is the  character to have a filter like this, excluding radio calls. Everyone else sounds perfectly fine. Why? Was the audio director trying to emulate the sound of retro voices? Why not for the rest of the characters then? Why not change any of the other sounds? WHAT IS GOING ON???Here's a direct comparison for your listening pleasure:While we're on the subject of audio, I'd like to mention the lackluster ambiance in this level. You hear:Where's the computer hums? Where's the hum and clicks of a server rack? The hum of the lights, hissing vents, or refrigeration units? Some of these things  have sounds, but are  you have to be on top of the object to hear anything. This level feels lifeless and dead because it's so damn QUIET. Drones you fight have this same issue. They explode after being killed, but the charge-up sound is so quiet that you can't even hear it unless you pick one up.I then get stuck trying to find a way to open a door. Turns out I need to interact with this PC to open the door. You wouldn't think to use the PC given that there's . The only difference is that this one has a faint green light on the front, which is very easy to miss in an already cluttered room. When the important objects get mixed in with the set dressing, better care needs to be taken to  important areas or objects.Shelly is fireproof.Generic statement about the bad AI.Nearing the end of the level, I find what could be some of the worst design choices I've seen in this level. After clearing a lab of two enemies, I see a big sign and arrow pointing up towards a waste disposal area. Ok, that's the way I guess I need to go. Following this path leads you to a dead end with a pickup box. To my left is a slightly open door with a visible weapon at the bottom. It's brightly lit and there are explosive barrels I can shoot. Ok, logic would dictate that there's some way to get down there. You wouldn't just highlight something so well to not make it obtainable, right?To your right is a vent trailing off, which looks like the same ones you crawl down. There's a red light and a "No Entry" label slapped above it. Try as you might, this vent will never open. It's at this point it hits me why that sign is there. The devs saw beta testers get stuck here trying to reach the weapon below, despite the weapon not being obtainable. They then slapped the no entry text above the vent and called it a day, instead of just designing the area better. Why not remove the weapon? Why not remove the interactable barrels? Why not just make it darker so you don't think to look down there? Why not change the vent so you don't think you can enter it? Instead, they took the laziest approach possible and threw some "nothing to see here" text up.And yes, that area is indeed inaccessible.This was . If that's the first level, the  your game gives to the player, then I don't want to stick around to see the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoo boy where do I begin!Imagine Half-Life, except it has zero flow and bad combat. That's this game!Every couple of minutes in, you will be faced with a dead end with little indication of where to go or what to do, and forced to backtrack a little (and sometimes a lot!) to progress to the next section.There's one bit where you blow up the door to a mine, but first you have to find some explosives. The explosives are in a shipping container behind you, with the door facing away from you so you have to comb the area a little, but in reality all you're doing is going LOCKED DOOR > CONTAINER THAT MIGHT AS WELL HAVE A KEY IN IT > BACK TO LOCKED DOOR > YOU WIN!What is with the level design throughout this game? It sucks. Nothing flows or is exciting. It's just irritating and poorly thought out. Shoot and destroy this bent grate! Yay you got through! Okay now this identical vent grate cannot be destroyed but it looks the same. Don't make players try vents on the off chance one of them will break like the first. What's wrong with you.So anyway, the level design isn't the only part that sucks the fun out of this game! The combat is bland as hell, reminds me of an early 2000s shooter that isn't one of the good ones. Enemies either run towards you or stand behind cover indefinitely. Zzzz. Guns suck, they have very little feedback and don't feel good to use. Even when you eventually get Loverboy (the revolver), it feels just as weak as the pistol. Christ.What's with the fist too? It just charges up, enemies shoot you, and then it might just zip you behind the enemy missing them entirely. Lmao.So we're in the home stretch of things bad about this game! Yippee!The environments, while filled with clutter and props, have very little interactivity beyond picking them up and throwing them. You see this pot of pencils? Throwing it shows they are completely static, nothing happens. You see this IV pouch? Throwing it... Is the same as the pencils. You have a handful of truly interactive things, such as the vending machines, paper towel dispensers and uhhhhhh...It's like they played a bit of Ion Fury, saw how interactive the environments were and the only thing they gleaned from that was "put lots of objects in". Dur.I found a spot where you can go fishing that plays 1 of 2 animations each time where you either hook a fish, or a PIZZA! LOL! A PIZZA! HAHAHAHA. No it doesn't do anything, other than BUST MY SIDES WIDE OPEN. BRAVO! No but really, it'd be fine if anything happened. Anything other than the same animation except it's a pizza and not a fish now.Game is weirdly quiet and empty feeling. The intro has a dude going QUICK WE MUST HURRY and then you kill like 10 guys and it ends. No sense of urgency, not only through sheer lack of set dressing, but audio design too. Remember the banging soundtrack from Ion Fury? Not sure these devs do.Shelly sounds depressed now. The voice actress did such a good job in the first game (pro women lover here, sorry incels), but I feel like the script in this game couldn't have managed to squeeze out a good performance from even the toppest of the top most expensive VAs.Upgrade system is fine. My boring pistol now shoots 3 boring bullets instead of 1 boring bullet. Cool. I can upgrade my useless punching arm! As if I'm ever gonna do that. You find these in the environment sometimes. Not hidden particularly well or anything, but they're there.Graphics are fine. Do the job but overall uninspired and kinda bland.I guess what I'm trying to say is this game is wack. Don't buy it. It's so wack.

_childDocuments_.review: When I sat down to try this game, I genuinely hoped to have a different experience than the one I had. I tried, I really did, to find reasons to give this a positive review. Unfortunately, there are far too many downsides to overlook.First, let's talk about the patches. The developers have rolled out several updates, and yet, the issues persist. It feels like little progress has been made towards improving the game, but that's still truly disappointing.One of my major grievances is the game's optimization. Running it on a system with a 4070 SUPER, i7-14700K, and 6000 MHz dual-channel DDR5 memory grants expectations of smooth sailing. Instead, I find myself sitting through frame drops below 90 fps during intense scenes. This level of performance on such a setup is unacceptable.The stuttering and microstuttering are particularly infuriating. My setup should handle this game with ease, yet these performance hitches are all too frequent. At times, it feels like the game is waging a war against my system.Moreover, there are frustrating moments when shots simply don't register. You line up your sights, take the shot, and nothing happens. It's infuriatingly common and detracts significantly from the overall experience.My personal gripe is how drastically the game has deviated from the original Ion Fury. As a fan of the older title, this departure feels unjustifiable and unwelcome. It lacks the charm and appeal that drew me in initially.The gameplay itself is tedious. Shooting, which is supposed to be the main attraction, feels poorly executed. It's bland and lacks the engagement and excitement that a player seeks in a game centered primarily around shooting mechanics.Lastly, let's discuss the elephant in the room: mouse smoothing and deceleration. Even after numerous patches, this issue still lingers. It's bewildering that a problem easily fixed through a few lines in the ini file remains unsolved by the developers.In conclusion, while I sincerely wanted to appreciate this game, the combination of unresolved technical issues and gameplay missteps makes it difficult to recommend. For those still interested, I've included a temporary fix for the mouse input issues below.4/10.Navigate through "%localappdata%\Phoenix\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor" and open "Input.ini" using your favorite text editor.Add the following entries below "[/script/engine.inputsettings]":Note: "bEnableMouseSmoothing=False" might already exist, in that case there's no need to add it again.Save the file and launch the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ion Fury felt good to play. This game does not. Even on normal enemies feel bullet-spongy and crack-shotty. Skill issue? Quite possibly but I never had this issue with Ion Fury.Game starts off very WTF'ey. Shelly wakes up to her commander talking to her about a mole in the organization and you're now on the run. Why? Don't know at the start and I didn't play very long so I never found out. Drones overall made me take an early break. Dodgy little f^&*ers that explode after you kill them. Not fun to fight against and they're QUITE numerous. Will pop out of boxes and vents too and immediately get free shots on you unless you already knew they were there so that's nice, innit?Hit feedback is very weak. In Ion Fury it was pretty obvious when and if you hit your targets but here you just gotta see your target ragdoll and even then you might have wasted more ammo trying to kill them. Fortunately, ammo is not very scarce so you will probably not run out of it because of that.Speaking of weak, the weapon-feel of the first two weapons  you pick up (EDIT: played long enough to get the loverboy. It doesn't do much more damage than the basic pistol and your max ammo is VERY limited); the plain-jane, not-the-loverboy pistol and the shotgun. Both feel very "nothing" to fire and some early enemies will even take three shotgun shots to kill. Shotgun is pretty nice for taking out the drones because even with as dodgy as they are the pellet spread of the shotgun will oftentimes take them out in a single shot. Just be sure to run from them because, like mentioned earlier, they explode some time after they die so if you're hunkered down against multiple crack-shot hit-scanners then you may be eating a ton of damage just trying to move to new cover. And hey, Slipgate? Why do I have to wait for that long to get the loverboy?Visuals. They look alright. Very "Slipgate Ironworksey". Not offensive.Not a terrible game by any stretch but not as good as Ion Fury. EDIT: Just played a bit more. Wasn't having very much fun with it. Ion Fury is much better. I recommend that one over this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this one blindly because I loved Ion Fury. From what I saw from the trailers I couldn't believe I could go wrong with this one. This game has so much potential, but it is made half-assed!!There are too many bugs and most of the game feels like it isn't done seriously;- I lost my upgrades after 3 hours. Upgrades also seem unneccasary in the game.- Levels are unintuitive. I have reloaded some checkpoints because I got stuck in places where I wasn't supposed to be. Sometimes there is no telling in where to go to. I don't mind having to look for the right way as in oldschool maze shooters, but sometimes the right way feels very off and not in line with the rest of the level.Heights in levels are also strange as you cannot die nor take damage when you fall in most cases. This gives me doubts on where to go sometimes. It has brought me back to the beginning of the level a couple of times and guess what....I had to reload the checkpoint and redo the same stuff.Level variation is okay, but some seem put in just because the developers thought they had to.- Enemies often respond late and pretty much just run towards you guns blazing. Sometimes you see them take cover and you get a glimpse of how it could have been done.- Weapons feel good, but are unbalanced. Ammo is not scarce and you can kill everyone easily with the Loverboy's alt fire. ALSO: some alt fires don't work (anymore) because of game bugs.- Difficulty is unbalanced; I play hard difficulty and I only die because of cheaply placed enemies. In these cases you might get some oldschool replays because it has a checkpoint system(!!??).- I am playing for 6 hours and upon until now you just hop from objective to objective and there is no real story developing. - The characters are empty and Shelly's lines are dull. In the beginning it felt like I was playing Half-Life again. Then it start to cumble more and more and you only get glimpes of what could have been. These glimpses are the reason I am still playing it. Oh man this could have been a masterpiece :(Hopefully the developers have the decency to give it a big update for the paying fans. But in the end even the biggest update isn't going to save this game I am afraid.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that it is worth stating beforehand that Ion Fury and its Aftershock expansion make up one of my favorite classic-style shooters that I've played in quite a while. That being said, before going into Phantom Fury, I was fully aware that this game wanted to go in a different direction from the controlled chaos of its predecessor, and I was completely willing to see what it had in store for me with the "Half-Like" sub-genre it had labeled itself with. What I was not prepared for upon booting up this piece of software was one of the most confusing, clunky, poorly signposted, empty-feeling, and unfinished first person shooters that I've had the displeasure of playing. Ai that has the mental fortitude of a mushroom as they constantly fall over each other and pose no threat by themselves as the level designers flood you with them in hopes to overwhelm you with gunfire, level design that is obtuse and seemingly designed to confuse the player for as long as possible with cryptic progression and in some instances outright bad design in terms of directing the player, weapons that have almost no feedback upon using them, and what makes the whole package such a sad sight is that a lot of love and effort clearly went into this title. The graphics, while not cutting-edge when compared to other modern shooters, have a very pleasing style clearly trying to ape off of Half Life 1's chunky and pixelated look, but with modern tweaks such as dynamic shadows and volumetric fog that all look great. The music was very well composed and full of high-quality ambient tracks and battle themes, however once the game is actually being played with your own two hands is where everything falls apart, as the underlying systems of the game were very clearly rushed to get the game out as soon as they possibly could.Playing this title was one of the most tiring slogs that I have ever had to endure in my almost 15 years of playing first person shooter games, and unless you're fond of that sort of experience, I would highly recommend staying away from this title unless it's on sale for a steep discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Fury

_childDocuments_.review: The amazing level design is about the most praise I can give the game. It's visually appealing, believable, and quite detailed.The weapon roster brings back a few familiar faces, but now with interesting upgrades.Then it just goes down hill from there.The AI is very basic to nearly brain-dead most of the time, even as bad as just standing still to let you shoot them.The end of the game feels unfinished, taking what I previously said about level design out the window and leaving a bland, uninteresting trek through a war-torn city.Then there's the bugs. Alt-fire doesn't work after a checkpoint reload, (which can be fixed by pressing M), and your ammo count sometimes just doesn't display.The version I played and livestreamed on had a softlock so bad, that I had to call it for the day. I was informed it would be fixed on release, but I am doubtful.To summarize: there is clearly some talent here in the art department, but Slipgate being Slipgate will just take that talent and churn out slop.This game is not ready; do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I am glad that I didn’t listen to the YouTube mob - yes there are a few bugs, but this is a very fun addition to the Ion Fury series.Conceptually the game is a sequel in the sense that this would have likely been the sequel that would have been made had Ion Fury come out circa 1996.The bugs I experienced were mainly polish related (physics get wonky on items like safety pylons, missing sound effect, little bit of level clipping). These in no way detracted to the experience for me - and certainly didn’t overshadow the excellent level design, chunky retro modern visuals, or really engaging gunplay with a pretty awesome weapon selection.It also has one of the best train levels in a FPS game ever. Seriously it is in the same league as Blood and No One Lives Forever in that respect.This is a very solid modern take on a specific time period for the FPS genre, and it really succeeds. Sure the narrative is very shallow (so was Ion Fury’s and like every game they are influenced by), but it is a fast paced sequence of levels that hit more times than it missed for me. I recommend this game if you have a slight tolerance for a little bit of jank, and enjoyed the classics like SiN, Half-Life, No One Lives Forever, etc. from the time period it is trying to reflect.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of "Ion Fury." In fact, it might be my favorite FPS game of all time. To me, that game is a solid 4 / 4 and half stars. I own it on both Steam and in physical form. THAT'S how much I love the game. I wanted two copies. If I were to rate this game, I'd give it a 3 and a half. It's GOOD. But is it GREAT? Not right now. I'll list the positives here. As I think some of the critics are a bit harsh on it honestly. POSITIVES: -Love the new graphics / character models. I feel I can get more immersed into Shelly's world. I love all the interactive prompts, which only add to the puzzle solving and keeps things fresh. I feel like I'm playing a PS2 game sometimes, which was my era of gaming. I'm 30 YO. So that was the big system of my day I feel. - I love the new puzzle solving. Instead of just key cards, you have to go through computers and find codes and clues. I love this. -The enemies are a lot of fun to fight, they remind me of the enemies in the first game honestly. Just soldiers who don't know how to react to kick ass woman killing them. lol. -Destructible environments are awesome. Reminds me of the old "Red Faction" game. -Playing it on Medium difficulty is a really good challenge for me personally. Things don't feel overly hard or easy. I felt like in the first game things were a bit TOO hard and puzzles a bit too tough to figure out.  The developers did a good job finding a good balance. -There's nothing like...BEYOND broken here. So far I've had a fun time. It's engaging. It's fast paced. I haven't run into game breaking things like some people are saying. It's all good as far as the overall presentation and gameplay. Just needs a bit of polish... MIXED: (I hope these are fixed at some point.)-The AI is mediocre. Some of the soldiers do what they should, but others just stand around and wait for me to kill them. Unlike the first game where I felt like I was in danger more. It doesn't break the game as normally it's good...but yeah it needs fixing. Not a complete mess, but I totally agree with the critics that it needs polishing. -Sound effects. Some of them are really good. While I think others are...meh. Specifically talking the bowling bombs. There's no sound when they're thrown or about to go off. In the first game it was very clear when one was thrown. Same goes for collecting bullets or other bombs. There should be a 'click' sound or something to indicate I've picked up more ammo and stuff.  -I think when you aim for a limb, the limb should be blown off and the enemy left writhing in pain. There's not enough differences in body shots. You can blow off a head. But I wanna blow off a leg or arm. Something like in "Soldier of Fortune." -More ambient noises. Sometimes levels feel super quiet. Especially the outdoors. Some extra distant sounds wouldn't hurt. Like cars driving by or birds. Just something to make it feel more outdoors-like. -Sometimes the bowling bombs don't go off when enemies are near. Not sure if this is an AI issue or UI. But it's just something I noticed when fighting a large group of guys. -Punchier sound effects. Sometimes gun shots feel  I loved the sound design of the first game. It felt crunchier, meatier.-There's missing sound effects. Doors opening, engines etc... -I wanna be able to adjust the saturation. I love that feature in games. So yeah, as said-I do recommend this game. There's a lot more good then bad in my opinion. I'm really glad to own it now and will continue the campaign for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could vote for a neutral "meh" option I would. I really really wanted to give this a very slight thumbs up but all things considered it's more on the bad side of meh.I finished the game and had fun with it for most of it, which is more than can be said for other Slipgate titles. I think part of my tolerance for its flaws is due to still having this idea of some mythical amazing Duke Nukem Forever 2001 version in my head, due to the trailer released for that game back then. As far as I know, the company behind Phantom Fury owns the assets for DNF 2001 and started developing this game inspired by it. Phantom Fury is likely to be the closest thing we'll get to some sort of a realization of that concept. But as it is, it has major flaws, and surely the bar must be set higher than that. The game starts off well enough with immediately flawed but serviceable gameplay, but gets progressively worse as you get into areas where the devs ran out of time to finish things up. The final levels especially are a slog.Aside from that just many elements about it are not good: AI, level design, sound issues, many many bugs, etcOh and of course no quicksaves which is a bit of a cardinal sin.In its defense, I guess I can say the environments can look great at times. And as said, I had fun with it, but it's possible part of that was due to me streaming the game to some friends and having a giggle at some of the jank together.Not terrible, not fantastic. People who don't have a high tolerance for bugs would do well to skip this, wait for patches or for a lower price. For everybody else, I think it's worth a playthrough, but don't expect anything amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: A very, very tentative recommendation - we're talking 6/10 here. I enjoyed it, but it's clearly rushed, unfinished, and shoved out the door. I didn't use half of the guns, most of the upgrades were unnecessary or worse than the default, and the much-hyped cameo by Blade from SiN was over in seconds. It's also extremely buggy and has some bad level design.That said... I did have fun with it. It's not a great FPS and was hyped up as something it could never be, but if you get it on sale and are forgiving of the flaws, you may have fun too.

_childDocuments_.review: So this feels like how back in the 90's when they would rush out a 3D engine sequel to popular game. First we got Blood/Ion Fury and now we get Blood 2: The Chosen/Phantom Fury. Its trying to max out its late 90's cred with overt SIN and Duke Nukem Forever (the original Quake engine one) references and DNA. However it falls flat by having some big very cool levels that just aren't that fun and lack hidden secrets or fun stuff. The first level actually has a back area where you can find a bunch of what appear to be references to other games including the goggles from indie game Fortunes Run and even glimpse a closed up hidden area with a gun that isn't in the game. Ladders up to boxes are cosmetic and you try to stack objects only to find you are supposed to shoot the items down to access them. An entire late stage section of the game has dozens of vertical areas and fire escapes but the whole area is unused, the second to last boss is ultra hard compared to the actual final boss and the whole thing feels like a rushed fever dream. Shelly's characterization feels flat and brusque compared to the first game and her cool bionic arm mechanic to push or break items seems mostly abandoned halfway through. Game however gets massive cred for having a protagonist who excels in melee and feels actually strong unlike Dukes last ride. Shelly would give the psycho ninja protagonist of FEAR a run for their money.  However her enemies are mostly meh and some like the mutants are laughably easy unless they have a barrel or other item to throw at her then they become an extreme threat, being able to shield up on the suicide explosive enemies feels very reactive and tactically unlike most games where you have to back off and panic fire rather than execute a smart combo play and keep forward momentum. In a post ironic world this title perfectly encapsulates that micro era right before Half-Life 2 released where 3D shooters were being released that while nostalgic had a lot of flaws and controversy like Kingpin, SIN and Blood 2 a little bit more spit and polish and we could have had a great Ion Fury + DNF sequel we should have gotten two decades ago. Instead we have a passable game that embodies all of the hubris and failed potential of 1999 gaming. A solid 6 out 10, playable and enjoyable but deeply flawed. If you want to experience all the heartbreak of SIN and DNF  not getting a proper sequel this game is a drop of bittersweet poison candy on the tongue. For those who didn't suffer the agony of Deus Ex: Invisible War on release/demo this one will fall flat and come off as an extremely obtuse boomer shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay when the devs described this game as a road movie adventure I was on board completely. What I was expecting was maybe Half-Life with some walking-sim elements with interesting story and character moments. While there is a decent variety of locations, there isn't really much story or characters at all. So you definitely shouldn't go into this game expecting something like that. But I think the game is still interesting enough to recommend.So what kind of game is it, in the end? Well, it kind of feels like something from the mid-2000s in an alternate timeline where DNF 2001 came out. That either sounds awesome or terrible depending on whether you're nostalgic for that period of gaming. I think this is probably worth it only for the kinds of people who played and enjoyed games like Unreal 2, Far Cry, RTCW or Tribes Vengeance (or even Pariah) back in the day, those sort of forgotten, mid-tier FPS games.Some positives: • The weapons are great, and all of them feel useful. I think maybe they could have combined weapons or reduced them, because by the end juggling between weapons in intense firefights can get hectic. The shotty is damn fun, and has a nice alt-fire that blinds enemies allowing you to rush in and take a bunch of enemies out in seconds. Almost feels OP.• I really like the clean art style they went for, this blend of unfiltered textures, but with modern lighting. Outdoor areas especially look really nice at times. Games just don't look like this anymore. Also when you look down you can see your feet!!Mixed:• Level design is mostly good, but it's a little inconsistent. There were like 10 level designers on this game according to the credits and it shows. The Grand Canyon Facility and The Phoenix Tower are the highlights where the arenas feel as good as anything from the recent Doom or Wolfenstein games, with a good readable geometry and verticality. Other times though you're just in these big open areas with very little cover and it feels messy. Again, I liked how varied the locations were, from underground labs, to big open vehicle levels.• AI is a bit of a mixed bag. Sometimes, mostly in indoor arenas it seems, they're pretty intelligent, hiding around walls and attempting to flank you, and tossing grenades if you stay in one place too long, while other times they sort of just stand in place and are really easy to take down.Negatives:• The music just kind of sucks. Sort of just bland, low-key techno that doesn't really match the gameplay. Like the whole soundtrack sounds like something out of a hacking minigame. I thought after Doom 2016 we'd have hype music in FPS games figured out.

_childDocuments_.review: The buzz around  had me expecting the retro FPS equivalent of Sonic 06, but while the game is unfinished, unpolished, janky and sometimes baffling, it also manages to be a pretty good time. There's a whole host of oddities in every level, from floating props to enemies that don't notice you and weirdly unfinished effects, but despite everything I was surprised how fun it was at face value and ended up enjoying myself for the majority of the game.Not helping is the fact that the game's jankiest and most rushed-feeling parts are all near the beginning. Everything before you get to White Sands (the game's ersatz Black Mesa) feels less like a proper FPS level and more like a 2 or 3 minute vignette meant to get a trailer shot and it's  how fast you blow through each segment. This is where the most references to the mythical 2001 build of  take place and I wonder if the opening act was crammed in last minute just to get that retro shooter cred. The most egregious of these is the GDF bar, which is an homage to DNF2001's Slick Willy nightclub, but the level is so abrupt and disconnected with anything going on that it's actually surreal. Your enemies for the entire game are the GDF soldiers, and at this point you've slaughtered several dozen of them. You go into this bar full of GDF and nobody bats an eye at the fact that the person they're trying to kill has entered the room. Nobody pulls a gun, nobody gives a "hey, how are ya" if you come near, and I cannot for the life of me figure out  unless they just take their break time  seriously. I thought maybe this was a friendly squad who hadn't been tricked by "the mole", but once you find the thing you're looking for, a bunch of zombies burst in and  the GDF who didn't mind you waltzing in on beer time start shooting at you. It feels like it was there to get the DNF reference without any thought to how it would make sense in context and a lot of moments in the opening are the same way.Surprisingly the game picks up a lot once you get to  and the level design from that point is pretty good and reasonably -esque. The pacing finally calms down and and it starts to feel like you're playing a proper FPS campaign instead of a disjointed series of scenes. I generally didn't have any issues figuring out where to go, though I started playing after the first patch, which did supposedly fix some signposting issues. The enemies are fascinating. I've heard that they don't react to being shot and I've heard rebuttals that they do, and both camps are right to an extent. It's more apparant in those awkward early levels where if you shoot someone from a certain angle, they might not react at all, and drones don't even notice you if you approach them from any direction other than the front, but if you shoot most enemies from the front you'll get a pretty reasonable flinch.The strangest thing I noticed was how the standard human enemies moved. During those opening levels, it felt like the animations for walking weren't even synced up with how they were actually moving, and soldiers had a strange tendency to suddenly zip around corners and obstacles at lightning speed, sometimes so blazing fast that they were actually sliding around which was certainly hilarious, but not a sign of polish.What surprised me though, is that once I got to White Sands and was in tighter, more linear interior environments rather than the opening's wide outdoor spaces, a lot of the behavioral quirks went away. Enemies stopped zipping and sliding, and soldiers looked and behaved much more naturally. I get the vibe the enemies were optimized for the tighter  style environments and that their AI wasn't meant to operate in open spaces, which makes me further suspect the opening levels were tacked on to fill their Duke Nukem reference quota.When the enemies are in their element, there's a lot worth praising. They're good at finding where you're hiding, their tendency to vault over things and take cover is impressive, and they know when to retreat. It's cool watching a group of humans fight a group of zombies, and the zombies themselves have a cool ability to walking over to physics objects and throw them at you. It takes timing to dodge and I was surprised how natural it looked for them to grab objects given how awkward some of the other enemy animations were. The enemies are all fun to fight and satisfying to gib and that's really what lets the game hold up even through all the jank on displayThe weapons are fun, but there's too many of them and several cover the same niche. All you need to get through 98% of the game is the Loverboy, the two shotguns, and the microstinger (rocket launcher) and you're pretty much set. The arsenal feels like they made the weapons first but didn't consider what scenarios they'd be used for or how to balance them, and some feel like a solution in search of a problem. As in , you've got the weak-but-precise pistol and the Loverboy revolver which still has the lock-on ability from . The lock-on is more reliable here, but despite being a fun feature it's massively OP and throws the arsenal off-balance. Against standard enemies you can lock-on and clear a room in seconds. 's revolver was powerful too, but its ammo was scarce which forced you to fall back on the glock.  is so generous with ammo that there's never a reason to switch things up once you have a superior weapon. The SMGs are usurped by two assault rifles pretty quickly, and the stun baton is basically useless for combat since your fist is a one-shot kill that you don't have to switch to. The circular saw has such rare ammo that I never bothered with it outside of the puzzles it's used in.The Ion Bow shows up mid-game as a dedicated sniper weapon, but the Loverboy's lock-on has infinite range which makes it a better sniper weapon than the actual sniper since it gives you automatic headshots. A couple weapons do chip damage over time, but they're so slow you're better off just shooting the enemy with a regular gun. At one point you get a boss's head as a weapon and couldn't even figure out what that does, it only seemed to evaporate one enemy and didn't do anything to anyone else. In the 11th hour you get  pistol, John Blade's Magnum, and while it one-shots most enemies with a bodyshot it's  not as good as the Loverboy since it doesn't have the lock-on. The game's Immersive Sim trappings are really just lip service which is disappointing. You know how everyone loves hacking turrets and turning them on the enemies? Well, you can hack turrets, but only to disable them, you can't flip them, and by the time you get to the terminal or battery controlling the turret there's a good chance you've already destroyed it anyway (and you might as well since you can't take them over). Two shots from the Microstinger and it's down.Despite everything, the combat loop is enjoyable, the grpahics are gorgeous (aside from the weird dithered transparency effect), and the level design is pretty good once you're over that initial hump. Unlike a lot of janky shooters, there wasn't a segment that made me want to ragequit (like 's The Room). It's obvious the devs weren't given enough time to do everything they wanted to or fix all the bugs, but even in a rough state it's still fun and I hope it will still usher in the Half-Like revival the same way the also-janky  ushered in the boomer shooter revival. While  is objectively the more polished of 3D Realms recent releases, this was a lot more fun and it didn't outstay its welcome like  did. I hope they keep patching it and that someday the game can reach its full potential, but it's still a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom Line: Not RecommendedIf you're looking for a great playing "boomer shooter" FPS featuring the same character, please look at Ion Fury and it's expansion content "Aftershock" and no further. These games are developed by Voidpoint, LLC. Slipgate Ironworks, the developer of this game, has received the earned reputation of releasing lackluster products in an unfinished state and Phantom Fury is no different. This game's initial trailer was exciting and conveyed the idea of what this game hoped to achieve. However, ideas and actual products are two separate things; One takes relatively no work at all. This needed more time to cook. Even then, the developers might just not have had the chops to create the vision they had. Either way, unless you're a really die hard FPS fan that likes to experience both the great and terrible, you should spend your hard earned money elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a hate/love feeling for this one. The homage to old school games is fun. The combat is fun but not complex like new games. Fun for a Boomer Shooter.But the level design and UI design. Seriously!? Just choosing a level in the menu interface is a hassle. How should I know what the first level and the last level is when the menu goes in circles. As a user I have no idea. Just add a step indicator or just print our "Chapter 1 2 3 4" etc...The same design mistakes goes in the overall game design. Hunting for keys is so annoying. Just one example of the puzzle design. You have a Brown Key attached to a Brown wall - HOW WILL I SEE IT? KEYS ARE NOT NORMALLY BROWN THEY ARE METAL.There are so many unessecary game design decisions like this. Another example - it seems you can push a button (in the Cabin) BUT NO you have to do something other before you even can use your finger. And the game gives no hints as to why you suddenly can not use your finger to push a button until much later.I think this is a case of a Programmer thinking they know how to design. They dont. They are so bad at it. I know I work as programmer myself - leave the design decisions to the professionals, please.But still as I said I have a a love/hate relationship towards this game. The combat is fun for a boomer shooter - but the design decisions - PLEASE LET A EXPERIENCED PERSON MAKE THOSE DECISIONS.The person doing the art design on this game is awesome however. Feel old and new at the same time in a really good way.I kind of recommend this game if you really like boomer shooter. But be prepared for confusing level design.

_childDocuments_.review: Ion Fury was such a great game, it was fun, great level design with hidden areas and secrets, great humour and being made in the Build Engine was also a little bonus for me. It felt like a real spiritual successor to Duke Nukem 3D for the modern age.This sequel however... felt like it was phoned in over a weekend. The level design was awful, half the time you couldn't tell where you were meant to be going. The story was boring and unimaginative. There are way too many guns, but then again, you'll need them because the only thing to do in this game is shoot endless waves of enemies. It's not fun or engaging, there are no hidden areas to explore, no real thought to the design or artwork.A true disappointment and I wish I hadn't spent so long finishing it so I could refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty excited for this game, I absolutely loved Ion Fury. However, Phantom Fury is extremely unpolished and also fails in several game design issues. Here's a list:- The game starts. Doesn't explain who you are, what is GDF, why you woke up, why you have a missing arm, what your goal is, why of anything. Straight into the action blindly.- The voice acting is bad. The phrases speak of urgency and dire circumstances, but the expression from the actors is neutrality. "Oh this is bad. Please help. Oh, be careful. This is a gun, use it."- Some tutorial panels quickly disappear, also no in game explanation of some basic mechanics.- The music is extremely bland. It has zero action feel to it. You're almost falling asleep while playing the game. The music from the first trailer was sick. The music in the first game was sick. What happened?- Your melee fist attack is janky. Among other bugs. Sometimes weapons don't fire. Weapons don't have an oomph to them, they feel light and have little impact.- Lastly, Shelly's character was absolutely destroyed. She's not the same person. She's just angry and sadistic. No wit at all, no innuendos, no jokes, nothing. Mostly quotes like: "Die" "You're pathetic" "Waste of ammo".The dev's PR handling and botting in social media also leaves a rather bad impression.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played Ion Fury, I was hoping for more of the same just a different art style. It wasn't quite that. It feels very of a time, specifically like Unreal 1. It does a great job sending me back to that time, good and bad. But I wish I had been told about the tone change, Ion Fury has Shelly act far more like Duke Nukem, smack talking bad ass, Phantom Fury tones that down and gets a little more somber and serious. There's still one liners, but fewer, and less revelry in the violence. Which fits, you spend the entire game fighting against rogue GDF forces, the "good guys" in universe. It just wasn't what I was expecting coming into this game, but grew to understand and like.Some levels are a little confusing to navigate, as if they purposefully made the choice not to use lighting or signage to always leads you through a level. It was a nice reminder of older times, a little frustrating, but not bad enough to impact my experience personally.I'm not sure if I didn't get it, or if the game was trying to be something else. I was expecting an arcade shooter, but got something that seemed to push you towards melee with the new Robo-Fist attack, but doesn't mechanically benefit you unless you get some upgrades far later in the game. Especially with the larger expansive environments, range really starts to hurt. I played on Normal, and got used to the moment I showed my face, an enemy would take a shot and shave some armor or health off. Which pushed me to explore levels more for upgrades, health, and armor. Enemies felt tanky, but later on I discovered that hit location greatly matters, so go for head shots since most enemies are bullet sponges.The writing and performance is a little flat, the energy from Ion Fury seems gone, Phantom Fury's Shelly seems angry and passionate, but some of that fire has simmered. Voice Lines lack a certain punch that Ion Fury had. Story is nothing to write home about, but it really doesn't need to be, is serviceable and gets you from interesting location to interesting location.From a tech standpoint, if this had come out around Half-Life and Unreal it would have blown people away with the physics and all the various mini-games you can play in game. There's a nice bit of variety to the game, but not quite enough of a break from the central gameplay loop for me personally. Eventually got tired of just shooting and going for headshots and wanted something to break it up, like another helicopter section, vehicle section, or even a turret section, but never got bad enough I put the game down because of that lack of diversity.I feel like there were less secrets or references compared to Ion Fury, again different game different vibe, but something I was hoping to see more of. A lot of the references came from locations and vibes, yeah that one level feels very Half-Life. That said,  was a highlight for me personally. Simple but seriously made me smile and gave me hope to see them again.Over all, I would recommend it to folks looking for a Classic Shooter (Late 90's early 2000's vibes), or if you enjoy Shelly or the greater Universe that seems to be forming around this. Otherwise it's a solid 7/10, which now a days is almost a death sentence critically, not good enough to be great on it's own, not bad enough to get a lot of press and maybe have interested people check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: A completely okay game that is at fault for being a subpar follow up to infinitely better game. Phantom Fury is the follow up game to the Retro FPS pioneer Ion Fury. Developed by Slipgate Ironworks and not the original developers following Shelley Harrison as she's back at it again. The game is most notable for being styled like the linear narrative FPS games of the late 90s and early 20s, such as Half Life. Much like how Ion Fury mirrors other Build engine FPS game. However it often feels like a imitation that references bits and pieces of those games rather than using it as a basis and expanding upon that already solid framework. Nevertheless the game functions and other than a few minor gameplay bugs is completely playable and fun in it's own way. But is still a subpar follow up to such a innovative first game, even it's Aftershock DLC. Gameplay of Phantom Fury is honestly really solid but needed more polish. As stated before it's in the more linear narrative style with games like Half Life, specifically the second is where the game is pulling it's inspiration but mixed in with mechanics from other games and of course drawing from the original Ion Fury. Gunplay is fairly standard you have a variety of weapons from pistols, shotguns, rifles, and unique weapons to play around with. Weapons carried over from Ion Fury work 1:1 with their Build counterparts like the Loverboy and it's incredibly useful Altfire. While the new weapons range from non-original but also very useful or weird and unusual. Shelley also has a brand new mechanical arm which allows her to punch really hard. Which is helpful occasionally in combat but I mostly found use of it since you can get some really good momentum off of it. This leads into the other notable part of the game, the upgrade system. Hidden throughout the game's level are these.... Nanoite? canisters that allow you to upgrade some of your weapons, arm, and your suit. They range from really useful like a stun flash for your basic Shotgun to completely useless like a projectile shield that prevents you from attack. Personally I was able to get enough canisters by playing normally and looking for secrets to get way more than enough to get all the upgrades I wanted. Enemy combat however is probably the most halfbaked, practically every enemy beelines to you like a moth to a light, like Half LIfe 2 Combine AI but even less sophisticated. Normally this isn't a issue since at the start a lot of the level design is hallway-like inside of buildings but once you get to the more open areas of the game it starts to crack. The drone enemies are simply annoying cause they're not that strong or deal that much damage but they almost always explode after a few seconds on death which got me a few times. Mutant enemies are okay with the right upgrades but seem to have a lack of polish, like how the zombie-esque mutants casually jog to run after you. Really as a whole is a bunch of familiar mechanics that feel like they're there just to be like "Hey remember that thing" rather than taking it and putting it's own spin on it to be unique. Style wise, Phantom Fury is back at it with that Slipgate Ironworks' artstyle that was also used in Graven. Lowpoly models with a high density of visible pixels but combined with modern aspects like a large level scope, physics engine, and lighting. For the most part the game is well detailed throughout it's various levels which span across a huge variety of locations. The only exception is the final act of the game where the level design a lot more open and plain. I think the reason why the other parts of the game were able to look pretty good for what this game is, is simply because of the smaller scope that's given with stuff like interior rooms and the sort. It's pretty evident when the Mall and the final area of the game has clearly more time and care put into them. Otherwise, game looks good, just wish the game was better. Overall, Phantom Fury simply exists. It's not a great sequel to Ion Fury and looking at it on it's own it doesn't do THAT much that other games released back then and very recently do better. However I would be lying if I didn't have fun with it. It thankfully holds together enough to be worth at least one playthough, if you can get it as cheap as possible cause 25$ could be spent on a better game, like Ion Fury. Since as this game didn't do well for obvious reasons, we're likely not getting any more "Fury" games unless a miracle happens. Heck I didn't even mention that John Blade from SiN shows up just because, considering his remaster of the first game is still in development limbo. As a whole treat this game like a Phantom it's up to you if you interact with it or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Subtracting the controversy surrounding this games launch; I think this a decent title, and a short romp into nostalgia for late 90s/early 2000s FPS games.I think this games biggest downfall is it's inspired by a host of great games, without quite understanding what made those games so great. The moments that it decides to execute on It's own original ideas is where the game shines, whereas the moments that are ripped wholesale from other titles of the era (On-Rail segments, Crate Stacking physics puzzles, etc) is where the pacing comes to a slog.Despite this, Shelly is still a fantastic protagonist that always makes me grin when she delivers her one-liners, the weapons arsenal is engaging and enemy health values aren't as monotonous as other typical Boomer Shooters.Overall 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I love retro shooters and I enjoyed Ion  Fury and I really want to like this game, but there is just so much wrong with this on a game design 101 level. One of my main problems with this game is that the selection of weapons is widely incompatible with the level design: most of the weapons are tailored for short-to-mid range combat, but roughly 95% of all enemy encounters happen in wide open areas and even the indoor areas are so large that many of the weapons are practically worthless -- I have spend the first 3 hours only using the pistol and the revolver, because you'll get to almost half the game's campaign before the game gives you an assault rifle; I would have given an arm (pun indented) and a leg for a proper sniper rifle in this game. The next point that annoys me is that enemy movement is extremely erratic and unpredictable, which makes aiming almost pointless. And even though most of the levels are mostly linear, a map would have been really helpful -- there have been several occations where I have been wandering around for fifteen minutes trying to figure out where the game wants me to go and what it wants me to do. Also, there are good reasons why auto-save and auto-heal were invented at the same time: the former one just doesn't really work without the latter one...But finally, what really disappoints me most is how forgettable und unremarkable this game is in absolutely every possible aspect: no oneliner made me laugh, no advertisement poster that had a clever punch, no remarkable weapons and no memorable enemy designs, no game mechanics that we haven't seen a hundred times before and last but not least a completely uninteresting and bland story line. Phantom Fury is not a terrible game -- it's just a really mediocre one that hasn't anything interesting to offer, sadly.@Slipgate: Please sell/donate this IP to voidpoint.-- Edit --I feel obliged to say that there is one thing that has suprised me positively and that is the level of detail in the level design with all the little objects that have been placed around the maps.

That's been it so far.  This game is not littered in bugs the way people have been saying.  The cinematic style is very Half-life - gameplay is very Half-life.  The guns pack a punch and have more weight to them than they did in the demo.  So, good job on Slipgate and 3D Realms for taking feedback. _childDocuments_.review: I wish that i could give this a neutral reccomendation, but i rather hope for a good ending to the development of this game and between the two available options go with a positive one.The game itself is really fun, i got what i was hoping with the feel of the combat being something similar to the feedback of Half Life with more spongy enemies and such instead of the immediate feedback of enemies melting of a boomer shooter, so i'm totally ok with this not being Ion Fury 2 but a new interpretation of the world and characters.Until now all the levels where really cool, the art style is awesome and i feel that's always something happening in the levels.What is unnaceptable is that i can't remember the last time that i had to deal with inability to keep playing a game due to bugs that straight up hard lock my progress.I have tried playing the 4th level multiple times but cant get a necessary item to progress to spawn (a floppy disk that should be next to a terminal).I understand a big open world game or a game with emergent gameplay having problems with progression triggers, but a linear first person shooter with such a problem can only mean two twings:1) There was no time dedicated to QA this game before its release.2) There was time to QA the game, but most of the problems where ignored and the game was released with full knowledge of its broken state.I hope for stupidity before malice but everyone knows the current state of the industry so its probably the second option. I dont like the idea of requesting refunds of games, i dont usually care if i dont like a game if i pay for the experience and i finish it i`m ok with it.But i never had to deal with simply not being able to progress a game due to a blocking bug and the frustration of not being able to do so for playing more than 2 hours.TL:DR: There is a good game here with a lot of heart and love, but the game is broken. Give it a few more months and hope for continued support with fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: I think that there's a decent game at hand here, and I actually think that it does not deserve all the hate it seems to get online.I'd like to start with the things that I actually liked and enjoyed while playing through the campaign.First and foremost, I think this game looks great. The art-style is spot-on for something that tries to mimic the graphics of the late 90s and early 2000s, with some modern lighting and effects-work on top. Levels are set in varied locations (e.g. canyon, laboratories, forest, destroyed city) so there is always something new to see for the player. Some levels feature some quite impressive vistas actually.I also quite liked the gameplay (although there are some issues; more on that later). Gunplay is snappy, movement works (mostly) great, and there's some good gameplay variety here consisting of combat, exploration, and some light "puzzling" (mostly key- and switch-hunting) sprinkled in between.Combat is generally good; there are a lot of fun weapons to choose from and lots of enemies that together make for some intense firefights. There's also the occasional bossfight, too (although these aren't great, but still mostly fun).Exploration also worked for me since there is an upgrade system for your character and weapons, so exploring the levels feels rewarding to get those precious upgrade points for your shiny new gun.So far so good then! But, as mentioned above, there are issues that are totally worth mentioning, but I don't think that those would make the game un-enjoyable for those that like these kind of old-school shooters.First, the story is just... bad? It's very predictable, and in general pretty flat. Characters are not really interesting, writing is kinda bland. No big deal for me though since it still is "engaging" enough to push forward through the campaign.Speaking of "pushing forward": There's one level in particular that's just super confusing regarding its layout. I understand what the devs were trying to do here (kinda copying that feel of the "old" shooters from the 90s where you're hunting for keycards in maze-like levels), but its just designed badly and drags on for what feels forever. Most of the other, more linear levels are very good though and navigation was only an issue for me in this one specific level. Other than that there are some vehicle levels that are mediocre at best, but those don't overstay there welcome I'd say.Moving on, the enemy variety feels kinda lacking the longer the game goes on. Don't get me wrong, there's actually quite a lot of different foes, but since they all behave kinda samey it gets repetitive after a while. Enemy AI also isn't great; most enemies simply rush towards you guns blazing (or trying to melee you), sometimes getting stuck on level geometry causing them to basically freeze in place and not attack anymore. Not a huge deal, but worth noting I think.As mentioned, there's a huge loadout of weapons to find, but for some of these I found the balancing just kinda off. No big deal since there are still more than enough viable options to choose from, but I feel like some of the guns need re-balancing to actually encourage using them. I did encounter a few issues throughout my playthrough. These can be summed up like this: In the end, I still enjoyed the game quite a bit and I do think there's a fun game here hat could need some additional polish regarding aspects like balancing and some minor technical issues (object collision, enemy AI). For me this sits somewhere in the 6.5 to 7.0 out of 10 range.

_childDocuments_.review: My first review here.Finished this game that was patched with Patch #2. Started a new game from the beginning and finished at the end of gameplay to make sure for writing my thoughts and experiences here.Ratings separated in sections:Graphics  - 10/10To be honest. I had a great feel for playing this game with the great looking graphics and arts that remind me of the older games Duke Nukem 3D/Shadow Warrior, Half-Life and Duke Nukem Forever.This kind of graphics and styles. So amazing.It's absolutely not needed to go with AAA graphics. This in-game graphics worked greatly.Level/ Leveldesigns  - 8/10Very well made levels with so much realism and immersion. In a good way. Nothing simplified, nothing extreme. Well balanced that came with different settings and environments where I was. Good weather in Texas? Great! Or the night? Or something creepy and dull somewhere else? Everything. Zero complain. I like it. They must have put so much work for designing levels...Weapons / Bionic Arm / Suit  - 8/10Good variety of weapons for different purposes and has upgrades. It come with pro and contra of their own. Like in other games. Plus it has a mod menu (default shortcut key: M) to configure the weapons for your own liking.It can be rather confusing from the beginning without any hints or the indication for how to use Loverboy revolver as example or other weapons. Though it's easy to use and easy to figure out for what these are for.I liked the upgrades for bionic arm and suit that's important for later gameplay. Very useful.I advice you to do not to rush through without reading upgrades properly. Take your time and decide which one to pick for your liking. Music - 8/10Fairly good.Savegame system  - 8/10It come with checkpoint save system only. It's more safe compared to the classical savegame system. Though, if I had progressed anything further than the last checkpoint saved and died somewhere... I had to redo everything again after loading the last checkpoint. I know it was frustrating but the more I getting used to it, the calmer and easier it will be in the end. Plus I knew for how it went previously before the death.My honest thoughts. It really couldn't hurt to add a classical savegame system but I don't think it's necessary as it come with its own pro and contra too depending on for how you use to them. Making a simple mistake or forgot to save it manually will loose your partial or full progress. For the last: Good luck to start over new. Playtime  - 7/10Done on Easy difficulty. Roughly 13 hours. I lost the overview for play time during the 2nd playthrough until the end of this game (Final Boss). AI  - 7/10Not too bad, not too good. I can give here a mixed result for experiencing the AIs behaviour inside and outside of combat and for how they dealt against me in many different situations. To be honest. It's nothing broken. Just slight pathfinding issues. Some odd AI behaviour that You don't see in other modern games. It's fairly okay. It was a thing back in the good ol' days of video games.It lacked the clipping as the enemy ran through me to the other side. Especially for walking through the opened door and suddenly the enemy left the room through me. I had no chance to block 'em that's pretty odd.Playability - 10/10This sections means if you struggle due of bugs or any things that breaks the game. Keep you away from playing this game.I can tell you safely: It's very playable after the Patch #2 was installed. I would like to thank the devs for their hard works for fixing numerous bugs, some critical bugs too. Be expected for some new unknown bugs. To be honest: Very playable. Get it. Play it.DopeFish - ??/10Why am I writing this?Story / Gameplay / Direction - 7 / 10It's not really Story heavy as expected but the fair amount as needed to know about for what's happening in the world of Phantom Fury. Blam blam through without having any Story is not my thing.The gameplay wise is very good and friendly to learn and play through several maps/levels. It come with three difficulty levels: Easy/Normal/Hard. You can find anything you can't miss, even for weapons and the upgrade currencies. But some may need your proper brain work to get it through. One map/level that really has a very proper brain to work it through. Nothing dramatic. You can spend some time to figure out and solve it without to hurry. No need to rush. And no need to curse about anything from time to time. Yes, it can be frustrating at the beginning but the more you getting used to it. It will be better and easier in the end.I'll give my personal assessment for this game:  80 - 81% of 100%Just good. Not perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out as Half Life 2 clone. You have an introductory level which teaches you how to walk, jump, crouch, go to the potty, and eventually how to shoot guns. Levels are filled with physical objects that can be picked up and thrown around; this doesn't serve any purpose, but you can do this and then advertise as a feature on Steam store page. Each drawer in any desk can be opened individually - not a single one has anything in them. Not an easter egg or consumable pickup, only the same lonely piece of paper.First levels of the game play like Half Life 2 with Douk Forever 2001 mixed in, subsequent levels become its own thing. Levels are different from each other to keep the game fresh, which I like. Level design is a mixed bag though, but it's a problem of enemy AI not working with it.Vehicle sections are also advertised on Steam store page. There are two levels with jeeps - they are not really fast and only have machineguns for weapons, playing on those is a slog. I almost forgot about underwater scooter segment, which is also a slog, but at least it's short. What I didn't forget is helicopter section. You may mistakenly get excited about this like we are playing Crysis again; how silly. It's rail shooter... Let's talk about something else.Phantom Fury doesn't want you to run fast. Peek from a corner and shoot kind of gameplay is encouraged in this "...adrenaline-fueled journey around the USA". There is sliding option, but enemies have 100% accuracy and Shelly can't slide several times in a row. What would have happened to the game if someone from 3D Realms told Slipgate to make all enemies shoot projectiles and increase running speed? Ion Fury clone would happen, which will be a better outcome to be honest.Weapons are servicable. Some weapons are good, some bad, and everything else is okay. Weapons, which return from Ion Fury, are less fun to use than in Ion Fury, but it's because of broken AI. I will talk about about this later. Back to the discussion at hand - weapon modifications; they are not good. Upgrades in general is what happens when developer is afraid of them becoming game breakingly strong - Slipgate made upgrades useless. A handful of useful upgrades, and everything else is disappointment. Disappointing - good way to describe the game. Shelly has a prosthetic arm - you can punch enemies, but it's a short, point hitscan with autoaim which doesn't even work half the time. It's not fun to use and it doesn't stun enemies if they survive, just staggers them; the shield is unlockable ability, which is the most useful out of all, even if it's situational; and the ability to carry heavy weapon is useless outside first boss fight because heavy weapons are terrible. The suit features such upgrades as "Chance to double health pickup" and "Slide can destroy crates". I don't usually condone plagiarism, but in this case I wish they copied Doom Eternal.If anything shows the absence of Slipgate Ironworks' understanding of basics behind game development, it will be enemy AI. Giving a simplified explanation of AI for your generic gunman: it has separate states of walking, shooting, stagger and death. Your gunman walks around; when time comes to shoot the player, the gunman stands in place and deals damage after some time, to give the player chance to shoot back; when shot, gunman gets staggered or dies. Doom, Duke 3d and Blood did that and it worked. Phantom Fury though... Enemies always move in erratic matter and don't stop when shooting. Doesn't matter in tight corridors, does matter when levels open up because the player gets shot from 3+ sides with no cover.So what I am trying to say in the end? This game is mediocre in a peculiar way. There are good ideas put into it, but they don't really work - weapons are unique, but not fun to use; level design is competent, but it isn't built with enemy AI in mind. All the merits Phantom Fury has feel like things being checked out in a to do list without any consideration for why those work in the first place. John Slipgate spent his weekend sitting in front of a computer watching popular FPS youtubers with a notebook in his hands, and now the very same people he looked up to will spit on his very creation. Truly a tragedy.Phantom Fury is flawed and Slipgate Studios don't know what they are doing. It's true that I'd had fun with the game, and perhaps I would have left a positive review if I were new to videogames, but I am not. There are better games to spend your time on than Phantom Fury. Don't bet on Slipgate Ironworks.

_childDocuments_.review: While I didn't feel the same elation playing this game that I did with Ion Fury, this is still a good retro-esqe game and I did enjoy playing it. The jump from Duke3D graphics to this newer style is nice, the combat is varied and the enemies are decent. The levels are decently made, and the keycard-hunting style of progression wasn't as tedious as some games in the genre. Now the gripes. The story was very predictable, I would say it's basically every cliche in the genre all wrapped up together. It was a real cheese-fest. I was also bothered by the checkpoint system with no manual save ability. Finally the performance. Even though it looks like an older game, it's way more demanding than I thought it really should be. Playing on a 7800X3D and 7900XTX, I should have had a locked 144FPS @4k, but even after lowering the settings from the Ultra to High preset, I would often see dips as low as the mid the 60s and major stuttering in large areas. No doubt this game could use with some optimizations. I did finish the game in a weekend, and while overall I would say that it was worth playing, I don't see myself doing any replay as I did with Ion Fury and I would really recommend to wait for a bit of a sale. $25 isn't bad for this game but under $20 would be easier to recommend.
