_childDocuments_.review: Sooooo.. Luminous Avenger iX 2.On one hand I really missed being able to bounce all around the place pretty much whenever I liked in ASG2 and iX 1, stringing combo upon combo and staying airborne as long as possible. On the other hand though, I understand having more than one bullit in one's disposal opens the door for breezing through every stage pretty much. Notably because of Prevasion and Flashfield, both of which were easy to take for granted (especially in iX 1). So to see that Inti Creates decided to scrap those two abilities entirely, while also changing Copen's move-set into a more melee-focused style isn't a shock to me at all, nor do I find it a valid reason to bash the game. If you can look past being limited to one bullit and take the time to get a good handle on how Copen plays this time around, the game flows  great. If you really want unlimited bullits however, you could always go for Overdrive which also provides some other nifty buffs if you buy those upgrades in the shop. Or die, get revived with Anthem, and have your score butchered. That too. My only gripe with this new form of combat is that the three hit combo  except for certain enemies and  as most of the time you'll put yourself in harm's way before getting to make the most of that Razor Wheel. As a result, you'll end up wanting to use the aerial attacks instead. I feel if there was an option to dash and then slice enemies like per-say, Zero's Z-Saber in the X or Zero series, then maybe I'd find myself using the chainsaw more often? It's not useless, far from it, but I hardly found any situations you'd want to use it over tagging the enemy and going to town.I myself am neutral on Prevasion and Flashfield being removed in favor of the new Heal Mode, same with changing how Kudos are handled (for the main game anyway). Also the music is a bop, as always. I ain't got much to say about the story, though the end-game is crazy as always with this series. At least the story doesn't depend on you having played iX 1 beforehand to fully enjoy this one, so that's a plus maybe?As for the stages themselves, they're all pretty well designed with this new play-style in mind. Each of the sectors you visit are all visually distinct from one another, both with their themes and gimmicks. The emblems weren't all that hard to find either, with only one or two genuinely making me scratch my head. Health pickups no longer can be found since we have a dedicated button to heal, so that's a given. The only stage in the whole game that made me feel confused was Autochrome's, as I remember being disoriented at least two times thinking I was going the right way..only to find myself at a dead end with goodies or I end up right back where I came.Easily one of my favorite parts of good Mega Man-like games are the boss encounters, and this game delivers some excellent bosses. I ended up loving every boss here, though they were a bit on the easy side for the most part. Not only are there plenty of openings, but certain weapons can benefit you during fights even if they're not exactly boss weaknesses. Like using Optic Barrier to destroy those ice turrets during Hail's boss encounter, or using Whirling Chopper to cancel Brigade's giant beam sword attack right before he uses it. And of course I must also mention some of the easter eggs (notably ones referencing the Mega Man Zero games) were fun to pick up on whether they were subtle or more blatant .As for the weapons you get for beating each of the Gravekeepers..they're all great! The only weapon I found somewhat lackluster was Doomsday Charge from Dacite, but it can be quite damaging if allowed to charge up fully. Sadly you're stuck with Anchor Nexus at the start which I found to be one of the weaker EX weapons in iX 1, but that's okay since it does help ensure you get those tags when you need them. Makes for a good introductory EX weapon at least? Even then, none of the weapons outshine each other significantly and they all have their uses.My more notable gripes with the game go into spoiler territory with the end-game (as well as the story stuff), so here's your warning before you open this rather lengthy spoiler tag:Overall I had a blast with this game, and I'd honestly recommend it to anyone who's remotely interested in what this game's going for. Even if the story's quite frankly the worst in the series. That said if you're not a big fan of how Copen plays after giving it a few hours, that's totally okay! Maybe next time we'd get the best of both play-styles in a possible iX 3?Another edit here: Since the time of this review, Inti Creates has updated the game allowing players to tackle Hard Mode with unlimited lives. There's also more boss DLCs too, which I've yet to get around to purchasing as of now. If I do get them, I'll make sure to write up a review for each of 'em. Though seeing some of them are $8 and others are $4, might be a while before I splurge on them.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I understand; the mixed reviews focus too much on comparing this game to the last few ones and what the game does wrong like changing Copen's playstyle, having the story feel like an excuse for this game's existence, locking the true ending behind hard mode, etc. The story and characters are pretty mid but the gameplay, stages, soundtracks and bosses (not including the dlc bosses) were enough for me to enjoy and play through the game. The change of Copen's playstyle wasn't necessary but it's something I liked. It definitely could've been done better by keeping him as the ranged character and having Blade from the previous game be close-ranged like how Copen is in this one rather than replacing his gun with a chainsaw.  I enjoy games that give the player a challenge in which it's up to them to learn the right patterns, learn from their mistakes and using the available resources to succeed and clear the level; this game does just that, especially in hard mode. Hard mode gives you only 2 lives per stage, locks you from healing manually and from using the suit mods you could buy in the normal mode to power up your gear (checkpoints in this game heal you to full hp and they don't disappear in hard mode). If it ends up being too hard, there's an assist mode you can activate when making a save file that gives you access to manual healing and 200 lives.My recommendation is if you're a Gunvolt fan or just care about the story, you're better off skipping this game or looking up a playthrough. If you're just looking for a somewhat challenging, fast-paced 2D platformer with pixel graphics and a bit of anime visual novel stuff on the side then give this game a try. I bought this game here when it was on sale and liked it enough to buy a physical copy on switch and play through the game there.

_childDocuments_.review: The main story is rather short, you can complete it in 2-3 hours. Easily one sitting. If you want to view the true ending, you'll have to either play through hard mode, which isn't available from the start, or via youtube if you don't care about getting it legit.This is a game that can be as easy or difficult as you want it to be. Right from the start you have access to an infinite supply of healing that you can use as often as you please. There is a downside however, which is that every time you use it you get a score penalty. If score and rank aren't things you care about and you aren't looking for a challenge, by all means abuse this as much as you see fit. If however you are looking to achieve high score or for the boss fights to feel like actual threats, heal yourself as little as possible. Not even using it a single time is ideal.Beyond that challenge lies hard mode, which I won't go into much detail on as I have not yet played it myself. However, I do have some details regarding it based on what I've been told: Healing is disabled, as are shop unlocks. You are limited to your base stats without upgrades. You have a limited number of lives in each stage. Boss weaknesses are scrambled.If you have played Gunvolt 2 and/or the first Luminous Avenger iX, you will notice early on that Copen controls a bit different this time around. At first, it might seem like he's been nerfed, however this isn't true. It would be more accurate to say he's been rebalanced. Here's some of the details regarding that:You can no longer fire your pistol on the ground, as Copen no longer has it. Instead, you have a new weapon reminiscent of the Z-Saber from the Mega Man X and Zero/ZX series. To help encourage this additional focus on melee combat, you'll notice that normally you can only dash once in the air per jump. You can no longer stomp, and reloading isn't a thing either. This will definitely be the thing that makes you feel nerfed the most at first, but don't fret. The multiple dash system hasn't been removed, and in fact got a rather significant buff when activated. Achieving 1000 kudos (score) from attacking/defeating enemies will activate Lola's song, which brings you into Awakening mode. While this is active, you are given infinite bullit dashes to make use of to play more similarly to in previous games, but you have to be quick. There's a meter under Copen that depletes with time after each dash. If it runs out, you won't be able to dash again until you touch the ground.Also returning from previous games is the chance for Lola to revive you with her song when you die, putting you into awakening state. Keep in mind that this is different from the one you earn through 1000 kudos. As long as this is active, you will be unable to earn kudos. I've found you can deactivate it by simply using the healing ability. This will of course have a score penalty, but it's better than not being able to earn kudos if score is what you are aiming for.I do have some negative criticism for this game as well. For starters, as someone who enjoys the story in games I play, this one is much too short for me. I'd have preferred it to be around 5 hours long, even if that meant simply padding it out with sidequests or something. And no, I don't count a slightly different ending scene for beating Hard Mode as the story being longer.Additionally, with this game being a sequel to iX 1 and me being a fan of that game, I was hoping Blade would be playable as an optional character. This even could have been a great way to pad out the story, as Copen and Blade could have gone their separate ways and progressed through the Tower in a different order, each revealing different plot details on their own unique paths. Instead, unlike the main Gunvolt sequel, we are left with only a single playable character to play as here, which feels like a missed opportunity.For English dub enthusiasts, I am happy to report that the English dub is actually quite well done. What I'm not so happy to report is that I've heard that apparently the dub is also the reason why the price is higher than previous games in the series. It makes sense, making a dub isn't free after all. But it is something to take into consideration. If you're the kind of person who doesn't prefer playing these games with English voices, the price increase might be especially annoying to you, and understandably so. You're paying extra for a feature you won't even use.Overall, while the new gameplay style isn't for everyone and the balance changes might be a bit much for some people's tastes, as well as other issues such as the game being fairly short, I'd definitely wholeheartedly recommend this to anyone who's a fan of the previous games, or other MMX-likes. I've had a ton of fun with it, even if most of that time has just been replaying stages to go for high ranks and unlock more of the shop upgrades. _childDocuments_.review: There is no doubt that Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 2 is an experimental game and thanks to this fact, it takes one step forward, but two steps back. The old Copen is no more. Bullit Dash gauges and reloading are gone due to your new weapon called the Razor Wheel. You also don't have Prevasion, instead you have infinite healing skill. You can get another version of Prevasion back by purchasing a skill called Hyper Guard which halves all damage you receive to 1 when standing still on ground, though. This version of Copen without purchasing any skills is very difficult to get used to. However, I'd suggest you to grind some EC and purchase every skill available if you want to enjoy this game to its fullest. If you don't want to do that, you need to start playing slow in Break-Shift mode and build your kudos until you get into the Overdrive, then you can start playing fast just like old Copen. In Break-Shift mode, your dash is limited to one. However, in Overdrive, you have unlimited dashes as long as you keep hitting enemies (this requirement can be disabled by purchasing a specific skill) which makes it easier to maintain the Bullit-Shift mode longer. In the beginning of every level, the enemy layout and level design are suitable for Break-Shift mode and they evolve into a more suitable one for Bullit-Shift since it is predicted that you'd hit Overdrive by the half of them.  Story is very different than the ones you've seen in any Gunvolt game, but it is not something unique. Having maintained a proper peace in his world by taking care of the berserk AI Demerzel, Copen dedicates himself to research. While looking into a blaster rifle that is presumed to be from another parallel world, Copen, Lola, and Kohaku gets isekai'd into another world where only robots exist and they try to find a way back into their own world with the help of a robot called Null. They eventually find a huge pillar that consist several micro-ecosystems within its walls and each ecosystem has a defender against intruders. They are called "Workers" and all of them were built by someone they call "The Creator" who was the last human of that world before they went extinct. This "Creator" and the supervisory AI called "The Mother" of that world are not random deities of course. The Mother's ultimate aim is to revive this Creator, and his identity is for you to find out. To get the true ending, you need to collect every collectible and conquer the "hard" mode. Now don't get fooled by the word "hard", the true definition of this mode should be "insanely hard" or something like that. Be prepared to suffer if you're after the true ending, that's all I got to say.To sum up, Luminous Avenger iX 2 is a different, but a good game overall if you can make peace with the changes. Visuals and sprites have a striking resemblance with ZX series, they're almost like their enhanced versions which shows that INTI CREATES still got what it takes to make a proper ZX game. I hope CAPCOM will come to their senses and make another collab with INTI CREATES and give their fans what they deserve. Before I forget, avoid buying any DLC for this game because they are overpriced and the rewards you get for them are worthless. Yes, even D Burst.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a mixed review, but there's something in this game that I really like...They took Copen's gameplay from iX, neutered it, and added via a weirdly unexplained saw-blade attack the vaguest possible hint of Megaman Zero (referenced explicitly in the bisection death animation when enemies are cut). Enemies are more interesting than in previous Gunvolt games, and it feels like some effort was put into making them fit with the gameplay mechanics... but not really. There are special enemies that you need to hit from the top and/or back with the dash, but the solution is always the same, and these enemies don't really allow for much interplay or anything else that could be interesting. When dealing with regular enemies, it feels too much like rote— dash at enemy, blast while hovering down, land, repeat. You do also have a melee attack, the aforementioned saw-blade, but it is ABSOLUTELY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ USELESS. I don't understand what they were thinking when they designed this, Bosses are more difficult than previous games. They straddle the line between reasonable and unreasonable, and some of them are more on one side than the other... truly though, I enjoyed a lot of them. A few are BS, and the worst are exacerbated by the amount of visual noise on the screen. That was a problem with Copen in previous games, too, but it sucks here because of how difficult the bosses are. One boss in particular has projectiles with colour-clash with Copen's projectiles and it makes the fight unbearable.The final boss is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful. It's not that difficult in general, but it's boring as hell and it has one attack that is literally impossible to predict or reliably dodge, at least as far as I can tell. It takes forever and just sucks ass.What do I like? Well first of all, the songs are real good in this one. Secondly, I sort of sympathise with their plight... Copen is pretty much just zooming a screen or two across and then bouncing off whatever enemies happen to be there, or else memorisation of enemy placement for a score run. They wanted to make a game where the dash was more limited and you would have to pay more attention to things on screen, enemy attacks, where you can land etc... a slower, more considered version of Copen's gameplay. At points it almost comes together, but it doesn't feel like they were able to really bring it together overall, and so you just have a gimped version of Copen with sort-of more interesting enemies and decent, challenging bosses. It's okay!

_childDocuments_.review: Now first to get it out of the way, yes I did enjoy this game to some extent. I've played majority of the games of the Gunvolt Series as a casual player. I came into this game blind and devoid of expectations. At first, I was frustrated with the game's change in controls, changing Copen's playstyle from shooting around like on loads of rocket fuel to a more clunkier close combat simulation that makes it difficult at times to keep a decent combo going.However, because of how the main campaign has made it almost brain dead easy to keep your combo because getting hit doesn't reduce it to zero, I found myself breaking the main campaign from the constant amount of upgrades I was able to purchase from a casual playthrough. Along with this was what I could assume was the infinite amount of healing, which, although appreciated at first to make the game bearable to get through while learning how to control Copen, also could break the game in half.So not only does the main campaign offer you infinite full heals, but also upgrades that can literally made you feel like god.The main problem I find with this game however, lies in the Hard Mode. It's basically a revisit to all of the stages, except you are back at level one with none of your upgrades, and one hit drains your Kudos back to zero. This makes the jump in difficulty from the main campaign into hard mode feel like you just got kicked in the gut and tossed off a cliff. As of me writing this review, I've only beat one the stages in hard mode. It made me feel like ripping hairs and it might have made me age 5 years. The two lives per stage fills me with pain as I keep dying at the bosses of each stage because I am that bad at doing such a simple concept as dodging.So how about that story? Well it's....kind of irrelevant? Copen, Lola, and Kohaku basically get isekai'd to another dimension and got to find their way back home. It's a very simple plot that can sort of be ignored concerning the main timeline of the series. The plot twist of  but the world itself isn't explained much, leaving lots of plot holes that need answering. So it kind of left me unsatisfied when thinking of the story but oh well, I play for gameplay.The songs added into the game are a bop and I find myself humming them a lot, probably because of how this game's main campaign made it super easy to listen to them. So you shall be tortured by Lola's singing unless you turn it off in the options' menu.The inclusion of English VA was a surprise for me when I heard about it. Everyone from what I could tell, portrayed their characters pretty well. However, because I am fond of the JP VA performance, I have played using that voice option throughout the majority of my playthrough. Shame they also couldn't make English versions of the songs, but that would have costed extra to do and a good coordinator to pull off to make them sound great. I'm probably asking too much from this.So why do I recommend this game despite having complaints about the main campaign? Because I found myself enjoying such a simple and ridiculous game at times. Breaking the game filled me with hysterical laughter and the game itself can be fun if you know what the heck you're doing with such a limited moveset. Would recommend more of the shenanigans you can pull off in the main campaign and recommend masochists for Hard Mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's see now I will say this much, despite me saying I dislike this game, it's not that it's bad exactly but...when compared to previous titles in the series and the first iX it's extremely poorly done, for starters they shoved in a sword, now granted it looks cool as heck but is it effective? by goodness it's not, not even remotely, in an attempt to either emulate zero in some way or test the waters for the new gal in gunvolt 3 before that is fully out there, they designed Copen infinitely weaker than his prior form (which should have been free, even if you had to earn it) using an incredibly weak melee that has 0 air option unless you like very very weak chip damage options, a single aerial boost in base form, melee's first hit doesn't stagger and you'll find enemies will stop you mid combo or just straight up won't die, all in all it ends up being a weaker Copen dood.Granted there are some things they do that fix things, score doesn't go down (in normal mode) for getting hit, something I admit I never understood being a thing in the gunvolt games for basically saying oh hey here's a game mechanic called prevasion! now neeeever ussse it evvverrrr, like uhhh yeaaah, so no score killing is nice, prevasion is replaced with a special defence that requires you aren't moving or shooting and will make you take a single point of damage which is a little annoying as you need to not be attacking for a good second for that but enemies will be on you in half a second so you have to play the long game there but it does make bosses a lot more interesting to fight, there's overdrive mode which basically turns you into old copen but still less good as you are forced to be quick with your multiple dashes or you'll just lose your meter entirely dood.Talking about OD although you have to grind out for them, it has a lot of super handy skills, such as regeneration, infinite dash meter, higher defence, less meter cost for you special weapons, there is a perk to up your sword damage but...it makes you lose kudos if you're hit, that's more like a punishment really than a perk, it was an interesting idea that ironically would have been better if they were cheaper, I mainly say that because I beat the game and basically barely bought anything, like at all, I went for the main skills I wanted and was 2000 short for the last one I wanted, of which was the third skill I wanted so there's that dood.The story is a little basic but interesting, there's apparently a true end but one I hate lives systems which they add along with the upped difficulty, there's no NG+ to keep at least the skills you bought in normal and quite frankly once was enough, it didn't have the flexibility to be played more than once, the game was kiiind of fun but also enough of a hassle at times that what fun there was to be had was kinda drowned faster than the fat kid in pre-school who belly flopped and forgot he didn't know how to swim dood. <-> To end it I just wanna say again it's an okay game, in fact it's not even that badly priced but if you're a prior fan of the games you may find yourself like me and that it was a major downgrade overall in the fun department I will give it "kudos" for giving them full voice acting and in English no less which these days is dreadfully underdone so it was pleasant to see, thank you for reading and if you do get the game I hope you enjoy it dood ^-^7Afterword to the devs: (not that they would see this) the sword/disc was a fun idea but if you ever do it again I will suggest that you drastically up the damage as the point of melee in games is to have a high rish, high reward as you need to get in close, usually against some rather nasty and damaging enemies, there was no reward, only risk, you also need to realise that taking away the movement options and linking them to score which if you lose by healing makes you weak again is a poor choice when Copen was always such a powerhouse in the movement department, remember when making games you build on what's there to not scrutinise your fanbase while still improving on the game style and it's formula, this here was what I like to call a megaman Z4 where you gave us a cool hand, the concept was great but ultimately it was useless and never used compared to all the other cool weapons and stuff the prior games had, looking forward to GV3 and hope ya'all keep making good games dood ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Ok I finished the game.This is the weakest game in the Gunvolt series :PC'mon Inti Creates... I loved Gunvolt 1 and 2 because of their nice and rather unique story, and the near mind blowing continuity... There's none of that here. This is more like a spin off.The characters don't even have much to offer here either. The only good elements are the graphics and gameplay. Some of the music was nice, but Gunvolt games have been weak with soundtracks since the beginning. Please, step it up...Also, Hard mode is unplayably hard.I recommend waiting for a Steam sale.------------ Original Review -------------------I'm not downvoting the game, but what's with the price? The first game is like $10 cheaper.From the moment the title screen appeared, I felt ripped off. The music is the same, the title screen itself is the same except for the 2 on the logo of course. That was a really bad first impression. Back in the NES, MegaMan games each had its own title screen image and music. We've literally gone below the expectations of an NES game.Then the game starts, and it is all done just exactly like the first game. Some images, some dialogue, and then gameplay. In fact it recycled 1 or 2 more songs that were in the first game for the dialogue scenes.... wait, is it expensive because of the English voices??I would have honestly preferred no dub. The voices are good though, in fact I didn't even notice at first because it sounds JUST like the Japanese voice acting I was used to, except somehow in English :P that's a good thing they keep the exact same feel and sound. But still, I wouldn't have paid $10 more for that.I played the first level, nothing wrong there, same as first game. Not just the static screen and selectable text. Think of the SNES games and how they opened, there were a LOT of cool things going on.- All-new soundtrack, 0 recycling, and music that's more memorable.- Different type of cutscenes. Instead of portraits talking to each other, I want to see it like how it is in-game, animated character sprites in the places they're supposed to be in.

_childDocuments_.review: I'mma keep it real with whoever may be reading this, this might be a bit lengthy so in a nutshell the game is good and I'd recommend it to anyone interested, albeit cautiously.The story is good, it's a Gunvolt game so what do you expect? Of course it's gonna be good! As is the gameplay, although I personally feel like it's a slight downgrade from the first Luminous Avenger iX with the almost complete removal of the Bullit Dash. It's fine, you just might take some time to adjust like I did.BUT! Getting the true ending is where my main issue lies. To get the true ending you need to find every bonus emblem and then beat the game on hard mode. That first part is fine, no problem, but you are NOT gonna be able to beat the game on hard mode if you're only a casual fan. I was able to do it, but I'm not exactly a casual fan of the series either. Meaning that some people are effectively locked out of seeing the game's true ending. I think that's kinda dumb as none of the other games in the series have done this. The closest to it is the original Azure Striker: Gunvolt with collecting all the jewels and beating the final stage a second time while wearing the handmade necklace. But this? I can't help but feel like it was used as padding to justify the slightly higher price...If you're a casual fan who also enjoys the story I'd just recommend playing the game as you normally would and looking up the hard mode cutscenes. (Of which there's only about 4 or 5, two of which that are actually of any importance, and they're all pretty short which adds to the feeling of hard mode feeling like it was used for padding) If you're a veteran fan, and I'm talkin' the kind that get the best rank in every stage, then it'll probably be tough at first but it's nothing you can't handle. Luminous Avenger iX2 is still a great game, and again, I'd recommend it to anyone if interested, just be aware of the requirements needed for the true ending if you care about that. If you do decide to go for it, I wish you luck when it comes to hard mode and encourage you not to give up. You'll get it with enough time and practice.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that's beaten this game last night, I have alot of gripes with this game being actually bad and felt like clearing the air on a few things, but I dont really feel doing this review to go about it but here we are anyway. I'll try my best not to make this too long cuz I feel the problems are rather simple and a bit obvious.Story:Inconsequential. Yes, you can skip this game with the knowledge of "Copen got warped out of a tower" and not miss anything. Not only that, but this story is such a miss. I dunno what they were thinking with this, but the tone feels off, like an even less mellow dramatic story than the X games, and the bummy acting doesnt help either. Copen's dub sounds highly under performed, even for an emotionally-removed character and has no undertones of an edgy murderous borderline anti-hero, but more like a bored businessman that rolled out of bed on a Monday; His voice doesnt match him either. Lola is passable but can get annoying at times, especially when you get the same comments on using the saw weapon. Everyone else would've been somewhat passable too if the sound mixing wasnt utter turd, even after adjusting sound settings. Like do I need to lower BGM to 10%?? Somehow this is worse than the sound mixing in SA2. It's especially bad for the Mother computer, with the worst echo filter in history. Anyways, to be more coherent, you basically start off in this tower, need to find keys off of Gravekeeper bosses, who I wouldnt care to know why they're called that. Why? Because this game repeats the issue of introducing boss as they come at the end of stages with flat characterization so it gives you little care about them before taking them out, but even Gunvolt 2 did this better by having at least a few fan favorites with funner and grounded characters. The only time game ""TRIES"" to be serious is when you get the keys (which doesnt take much time tbh), and Null, a new character sacrifices herself so you can teleport to the final boss. Yes, the story is this short to sum up. Not much at all happens between all this. Null's death was a poor fanfic writer's attempt at making her sacrifice matter and sting, only to be left with an itch. It made no sense, at least to me too, since....She gets impaled and ran through by a bunch of cables, for the teleporter to work?? They even gave her green blood, which I suppose is oil since 99.9999% of humans went extinct at this point (only one being Kohaku). Even with the narrative of her design as a Worker of the tower having no purpose (cuz defect??), where everything else has an order to follow, I still didnt care. The death would've been far more effective if you tried your best to save her multiple times, she had ties to Copen and Gunvolt, or knew where more humans were. But no, we get a forced, drawn-out death where she ends up arbitrarily losing her memory data to be of use. Garbage.After killing Momma's boy for getting in the way, the Mother computer itself is a bit convoluted too. If her directive was to bring back and ensure the survival of humanity, then why endanger Kohaku by possessing her? Which I have NO IDEA how a machine can do that to a human like it were a ghost, so this also made Zero sense. It's implied that this was due to it being corrupted, but still doesnt help the bad story execution. And yes, this turned to the two last boss fights, where the first one you'd only need the cheap weapon to quickly take her down. After all that, Copen and co I guess find the wormhole that Null could make for them to get out? (Apparently beating the Mother computer senseless made the whole tower blackout) Whatever, they're with Copen's boyfriend, Gunvolt (who got prettier with longer bangs), at this point aaaaaand THE END. Not even a secret ending, with the very last moment of the story coming back to Null who seems to congratulate the player. Thing is...NO ONE CARES. It feels like the writing staff got a bunch of nooby writers to put together this gutter trash of a story, thinking sacrifice and poor Waifu-baiting makes this even memorable. Need I say again you can skip this game?Gameplay:This is more than likely what ppl zipped to but I dunno how much I can expand on this....So remember how Copen's known for his high speed gameplay where bounces off of walls and enemies to get the job done? Gutted. No I'm serious. His bullet dash strings are practically nonexistent. It is only accessible when you're in Overdrive mode, but not even the stomp reload is back. Meaning...You get only ONE BULLET DASH by default...That also apparently means NO PREVASION!...WHO TF THOUGHT THIS WAS OK??? Maybe it's to address the lack of difficulty the Gunvolt games provide at times, but you cant even buy it back and there's no post-game to get it back. Even the characters are like "Yeah Copen. You're out of luck". Eat me. It would've been possibly forgivable if the game was designed around this.....But HAHA, nah they didnt even try. This has some of the worst levels in the series. So you'll be trying your best to manually falling after a dash-tag into something. ALSO let's not forget the new weapon. The buzzsaw gun, which sounds cool, but you end up doing alot of the same bs since it shoots projectiles at whatever it tags, with the promotion of using the saw on the ground for 3-hit combo. Which gets counter-intuitive cuz you CANT do the combo if something's tagged, and there isnt a button to take the tag off, with no combo attacks in the air to make this remotely ok, so obviously the design of this also wasn't thought through. It does jack all against bosses so what a way to give us such an ineffective weapon. As the MAIN weapon btw. Pretty sure no one likes using it on repeat.The EX Weapons aren't too good either, with the best ones being the one to stop time, and Quad-laser one. Maybe the boomerang one since it can hit a tagged target multiple times. Funnily enough, for as much as Lola calls out names of the weapons when switched to them, I still cant remember them by name. Oh well. Maybe quiz me on it next time.The Skills can def make the game easy, somewhat replacing Prevasion (especially with the upgrade where you take 1dmg for holding still upon hit, but still a poor man's replacement). Not sure how much you can do the screen-nuke Skill, but it seems you can do the healing one up to around 10 times, with a cooldown, but by the time you're low on health again, you can heal back up the same way. Once you learn this, most bosses are trivialized. The only ones I struggled on was GlideMan 2.0 (cuz pit and 2nd boss i fought), IceWoman (cuz WHY TF DOES MOST OF HER ATTACKS FREEZE ME?!! REALLY), and the final boss itself. Even then, I only needed to heal 2 or 3 times, and they're ded. What a joke. Oh and leveling up might as well not be implemented, cuz you dont even get new skills. Darkness mode doesnt come back (yet it does for the attack Skill?). It's like they want you to not have fun. Also that high-damage mini-boss where you have to destroy like 20 of it's turrets can burn in hell.Music:It's hard to put into words, but the instrumentation is just not nearly as memorable as the rest of the series' games. In fact, I kept thinking back to those game's OSTs over and over while playing. These tracks are just so laughably underwhelming to listen to. And sorry I'm not a weeb for not fangasming over the J-pop tracks.Conclusion:Shi ttee, convoluted yet skippable story, sh ittee, egregious gameplay, and disappointing music. I'm so tempted to give this a 1/10, but my series basis is telling me to sit with a 2.5/10 cuz it can only prevent me so far. They shouldnt have made this trash and Copen's first game should've been his last if things were gonna get this bad. Also why....On God's green Earth....IS THERE DLC FOR THIS!? NO ONE ASKED FOR OVER 30$'S WORTH OF THIS BS! Skip this and let me do yall a favor.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of basically everything else Inti Creates has made, including the previous Gunvolt games and the previous iX game, and honestly... this one's not great.  I don't think I'd call it , but it also isn't very good, and not worth the asking price for the amount of content.Copen's gameplay is significantly changed from his previous appearances.  I can understand why Inti Creates did this; in GV2 he was clearly a secondary character who was designed to just dash through stages as fast as possible.  He zips through the air from one enemy to the next, barely taking the time to even look at the stages.  This was made even more apparent in iX, where the stages were designed solely with him in mind, and thus they were all fairly unmemorable and boring.  To actually sustain a full game as the main character in his own right, he needed  mobility, so that players were forced to slow down and actually think about how they approached the stages.So, they did that.  Copen can now only do one air dash before has to touch the ground, he has no prevasion, and his ground attack is a melee attack that makes him stop moving.  The result is that stages are more interesting and you have to put more thought into how you're going to get through enemies, but also, it's just less .Copen also has a much wider variety of upgrades that he can buy, but you'll only ever get access to most of them if you play stages repeatedly to grind.  If you just play straight through to the end, you'll only be able to afford a couple of upgrades.  If you compare this to the older Mega Man X games, it really makes it apparent how much more interesting stages were when there were unique upgrades hidden throughout them and you had a reason to explore.Gameplay aside, it's short, and the plot is absolute throwaway filler.  Nothing interesting happens, everything is back to the status quo at the end.  If they make an iX 3, it's hard to imagine how they could even find a way to make this game relevant to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would really only recommend it if you like the Kudos system. Kudos make and break the game. Here's why. When you get 1000 Kudos, you get infinite dashes for a short time, until you touch the ground or bounce off an enemy, at which point the meter resets. Honestly, this is a good reward for maxing your kudos, and it was really fun. This is a good way to make casual players care more about the kudos system, but a major issue is the infinite healing. You can infinite heal, but it resets your Kudos, meaning you lose out on the dashes. This is an interesting system, but let's say you don't care about kudos (which is a valid way to play in my opinion). You can basically spam healing, leading to an easy game. So you're either forced to max out your kudos to enjoy the game (which will take many attempts as this game is decently difficult without healing), or don't care and get an, at best, okay, insultingly easy platforming game. I only died 5 times during the game, and 4 of those were pit falls (an instant kill) in a very short time period, which are annoying to avoid considering you have one air dash by default. The only other time I died was on the first boss as I was trying to max my kudos, and due to another issue.The main weapon in this game sucks. Your main weapon is so awkward to use, and it makes the intro stages a pain. Once you get used to it, the weapon is okay, but it doesn't beat Copen from the first game, not by a long shot. The other weapons are pretty good. I equipped the fireball most of the time as it's not only a long range shot, but you can charge it as well.The store is also a good aspect of the game and I enjoyed it. It made the game more fun, and overall the upgrades are great. Annoyingly, the grounded dash-tag doesn't work by default, but with a shop upgrade, it made the game more playable. Another thing I really like are the bosses. These are some of the hardest fights in the series without healing, but they're oh so satisfying to kill.The last thing I want to note is the amount of content. For $25, you get a 2 hour game that at the very best will probably take 4 hours to beat. It took me 2 hours on my first try, which isn't enough content, and unlike Gunvolt 1, 2, 3, or even LAiX1, there's barely a postgame. Sure, there's a hard mode (which leads to the true ending), but that's not enough to pull me back into an okay game. I should also note that there are DLC bosses, but those cost $30 total. When Gunvolt 3 gave us free post launch content, alongside $2 DLC, I don't see why this game couldn't, considering they came out in the same year. I didn't buy them, but all I can say is that they look cool, and that's really it.LAiX2 is really a weird game, and I can't recommend it to everyone. I'd say try the other Gunvolt games and see if you like the ranking system. If so, you should buy this game. Otherwise, I wouldn't get it. If you want this game but way better, play LAiX 1. Overall, I'd give it a 6/10.P.S. this game took the term 'mommy milkies' way too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the previous three Gunvolt games, and still love this one. iX 2 is a bit controversial with the fanbase of these games, but honestly I do not understand at all why. Yes, it plays differently. Yes, it's not the same Copen you're used to from GV2 or iX 1. But is it bad? Not at all.This game still has top notch level, enemy and boss design that create a highly addictive game for score running, having arguably the best bosses in the entire franchise so far. The Razor Wheel is a strange change to Copen's gameplay, but it works because the entire game is designed around it. The first half of most stages is well designed around that melee gameplay, being more linear with enemies paced nicely to allow you to get quick razor bonuses by quickly dashing around and meleeing them. When you hit 1000 kudos Copen regains (almost) all of his functionality from previous games. The second half of each stage, generally around when you would hit that 1000 kudo mark feels designed for that free-flying floor is lava gameplay that is unlocked once you enter overdrive, and it flows well from there too.I would understand people being annoyed by the Razor Wheel if this game still had the same kind of level design and structure as Copen's stages in GV2 and iX1, but it doesn't, the whole game is designed around the combination of the Razor Wheel melee and the old-style gameplay you unlock in overdrive, so I honestly cannot fathom why people hate it so much.Is this the best game in the series? No. But it's also not the worst (that title would go to ASG1). All four are incredible games and iX2 is no exception to that.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 2 is both a mouthful to say and also the second installment in Inti Creates' Azure Striker Gunvolt spinoff series that stars the titular Gunvolt's sour-faced and white-clad rival. Unlike the original iX, which decided to home in on and improve upon the gameplay that Gunvolt 2 introduced for our leading protagonist, iX2 instead dares to blaze a new trail for itself in order to separate the two series more drastically from each other by swapping out freeflowing, score-based action for more conventional melee-focused combat. Does this gamble pay off? Well, it's a give and take sort of situation for sure.Before this game, Copen's gameplay loop focused around his trademark "Bullit" dash, an aerial maneuver that would consume one bullet to fuel a dash that could be aimed in four potential directions. However, unlike your typical action hero, Copen's dash were not just for mobility, but also provided the key component which he relied on to start his offense. dashing into an enemy would initiate a lock-on state that would in turn allow Copen to easily dispatch of the enemy with a volley of homing shots. The more enemies you could chain together before landing, the greater the score multiplier, which would eventually enable you to enter a powered-up state provided you didn't get hit. Taking out enemies or dodging weren't the dash's only uses either, as ricocheting off of the environment would not only let you close the gap between far-off enemies, but would also refill the bullet you burned to initiate the dash in the first place, giving Copen the potential to virtually never land in a continuous dazzling display of aerial acrobatics that lasted from one edge of the stage to the other.As fun and unique as this concept was, it did have something of an adverse effect on the level design and challenge, as surfaces eventually stopped feeling like platforming-based obstacles and instead just became fuel for your never-ending flight. iX2 seemingly tries to correct this by grounding Copen through the enforcing of an absolute limit of one dash per jump that can only be regained by physically landing. In return, Copen has gained the Razor Wheel, a melee-oriented weapon that's closer in execution to Inti Creates' own Mega Man Zero series than anything previously seen in the Gunvolt franchise. Copen's old gameplay isn't entirely gone, however, as racking up points will eventually cause Copen to enter his overdrive state, much like in games prior. Unlike those titles, Overdrive has become far more than just a general stat boost, as entering the state restores the ability to Bullit dash repeatedly, just as you could in Copen's prior adventures.On first glance, this is a solid idea, as locking away the old Bullit dash behind a score requirement really gives the Overdrive state, as well as the hunt for points to reach said state, a lot more weight and a tangible sense of accomplishment that just weren't there before. Once you start trying to optimize your scoring to reach Overdrive, however, you realize one problem.... The Razor Wheel just isn't that interesting comparatively. All you need to do to maximize your scoring is to simply defeat enemies quickly once they appear, which is kind of just what you'd do in any other action platformer to begin with. Copen's Bullit dash is such a transformative mechanic that I had to devote an entire paragraph to cover how it functions, and Gunvolt himself likewise has a tagging mechanic that completely changes how you view the environment and enemies around you back in the main series. The Razor Wheel doesn't really have anything that really defines its utility as something new beyond being melee-oriented. It's sort of just a flavorless stopgap you have to deal with until you reach Overdrive and regain your old abilities.Luckily, iX2 does bring another new thing to the table, and that's a proper Hard Mode that, surprisingly enough, is actually integrated into the game's story. The normal mode is short and holds your hand so tightly that you even get access to infinite on-the-fly healing. At first, I were rather disappointed to see how you practically couldn't die unless you deliberately avoided healing to bank a higher score, but then you unlock the Hard Mode and realize that all of Normal Mode were just there to ensure that you knew the basics and had a baseline understanding of how each boss operates. Hard Mode, in true Inti Creates fashion, is no joke. You're stuck at level 1, you get no uprades aside from the Mega Man-styled EX-weapons you gain from bosses, said bosses come at you with their entire arsenal from the start and that arsenal is now enhanced through the roof with new follow-up attacks on top of the innate speed and defensive boosts handed out across the board. You also have to adhere to an old-school lives system and Healing is straight-up removed. Needless to say, this is where the real game begins, and, as someone who were raised on the Mega Man Zero series, I kind of really fell in love with it.The innate limitations that were imposed upon Copen in this game becomes a lot more enjoyable when providing a challenge is part of the game's mission statement. You don't have a lot of tricks up your sleeve, so making deliberate use of that gimped Bullit dash of yours becomes all the more important. Does the increased challenge from Normal Mode go a bit too far, especially since the mode is now integrated into the story itself as opposed to serving as an optional extra feature for advanced players? Absolutely. The rough transition between the modes is staggering to say the least and I definitely feel that revamping the bosses' attacks on top of the massive restrictions that the mode already imposes on you was probably a bad call, as the information you gained during your training run no longer fully applies. Still, once you hunker down and replay the boss missions in Normal Mode to study their patterns and the tells for each of their attacks, you'll gain enough baseline knowledge to adapt to the enhanced versions once you hop back into Hard Mode. It's a grind to be sure, but if you're the kind of person who finds enjoyment in studiously hacking away at a singular section of a game until your execution and pattern-recognition is spotless, then I'd wager chances are good that you'll enjoy this portion of the experience as much as I did. As it turns out, Inti did later offer up a post-release compromise for the less stubborn individuals who have better things to do than to grind away at a single small game for hours on end and introduced an Assist Mode that sands off some of the rougher edges by tweaking some of the restrictions that Hard Mode enforces upon you, though I have yet to play it for myself, so there's little for me to say on that front. Making the transition between modes go a bit smoother is certainly a good thing, though.In closing, Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 2 is certainly going to be divisive. Gunvolt fans will probably find the Razor Wheel to lack the pizzazz of prior scoring mechanics and those who prefer sticking with Normal Mode will find a short, overly lenient adventure where you literally have to decide to not heal to fail. However, if you're a glutton for punishment who don't mind the laborious process of replaying bosses over and over until you finally get every tell and attack pattern down to a science, then iX2 might very well scratch that itch in a way that Inti's games haven't quite done for me since the Mega Man Zero series' Hard Modes. You should probably approach with caution, but if you're looking for a tough, fast-paced and responsive action platformer to test your mettle against, then chances are good that this is going to hit that spot just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: After dedicating more time to getting good, and trying out hard mode, this is the bomb, actually. The whole "easy to pick up, hard to master" aspect of the Gunvolt series is in full force here, and hard mode makes every stage and boss fight a grueling yet satisfying ordeal to claw your way through. I thought I was going to hate it, but I love getting closer to a win every attempt. Based on the time I'm gonna be spending trying to get through hard mode, I might just be able to recommend it at full price, too.TL;DR. Get it on the sale, don't even look at the DLC prices, experimental and takes a bit of time getting used to, turns a little too wacky near the end. Not as "bad" as my friends made it out to be, honestly. Presentation is top-notch, story isn't important.Don't head into this game expecting the same gameplay as GV2 or LAiX 1, this game is trying something different by playing more emphasis on Copen's sawblade melee to build up Kudos with precise three-hit combos, holding your saw blade into a dash to do a quick double tap, or buffering the first hit of the three hit combo in the air to land a clean hit.With this game removing prevasion and losing Kudos on hit, it's definitely more casual, in a different fashion than other Gunvolt titles that let you prevade everything if you want to. I can get behind a more restrictive moveset when the level design compliments it, and working your way up to overdrive, removing the restrictions locking your "infinite" airdash is satisfying enough, too. So I enjoy the game when I'm in the stages.The bosses get kinda really stupid near the end though, there's no reason I should be facetanking the final boss' weak point for 5 minutes straight.Addendum: I looked more into the DLC, and while the boss fight themselves are pretty pricy, locking some game changing QoL abilities behind said bosses is a little, uhh... Bad? :S

_childDocuments_.review: Wasen't expecting Inti Creates to make a sequel of Luminos Avenger iX 1. This rather.. suprising, i have lots of things to say here.. At first, when i saw the gameplay i was like "man why they have to nerf Copen that hard? But damn his new suit looks absolutly cool asf!" So i bought the game on psn, Nintendo Switch and PC and guess what.. i end up enjoying it and turned out to be my GOTY despite the "many" flaws it has. -Gameplay wise: downgrape from the previous title since they nerf Copen's mobility, making him focusing more on ground base combat with the Razzor Whel. And.. prevasion has been removed but you can buy some upgrade like short time invicibility when you get hit, hyper armer wich reduce damage taked by 1 on the ground, icarus wing wich gave you "infinite" bullit dash and more. YOU have to work your way to earn 1k kudos by doing Areal ex kills, quick razzor kills and finding all four emblems wich gave you access to OverDrive. Also.. they don't give you the 1k bonus for completly assembling the emblem wich is sucks. I like how some levels have specific themes; Volcano, Jungle, Artic, Space and they have gimmicks wich you have to pay attention for. Each boss have weakness to exploit wich the right ex weapon. Also.. they gave you healing ability wich fully restored your Hp and stored your points. Hard mode make things worst because you CANNOT heal, boss patern has changed and weakness aswell, and you start with 2.. YES two lifes wich forced you to properly play the game with no upgrades and levels up. It make the game impossible to 100%. But thanks to the last uptade where they add Assist mode that allow players to have 200 lifes and healing unlock, you can just.. cheese Hard mode. The visual of the ranks is very flashy wich is another thing i like about the game, it gets more when you got a X ranks aka highest rank. I love how they put couple details in visual aspect, mostly how Copen's suit change between "Break Shift"(ground combat) and "Bullit Shift"(Areal combat) and how well animated his and others sp skills are.-Music: Nothing but amazing! Lola's song are banger asf and they also bring the songs from the previous title. It's also avaible to lisent in the official Inti Creates channel. They made a 3D Volcanoid model of Lola singing the new song to promote LAiX2 wich is absolutly genious. I keep watching over and over and admire how charming Lola is.. i seriously adore her so much!-Story wise: kinda.. straight foward and some kind of "isekai" where Copen randomly find a blaster rifle and get stucked into a different world full of robots. Him, Lola and Kohaku must fight their way to the Grave Pillar so they can return back home with the help of Null. Knowing the fact it's a sequel from LAiX1, there's some reference from Gunvolt 1 and 2. Then again.. this game required you to play the previous title and GV1 and 2 for better understanding. I hate how the rest of the story is locked behind Hard mode to get the true end.Overall, Luminos Avenger iX 2 is a great sequel despite the couple amount of dissapointment, DLC prices for collaboration boss battle is outragious.. all of them should be at least 5$. Kinda wish they add extra levels like.. adding stages from LAiX 1, GV1 and GV2 with one last uptade. Suprise the game runs on my potato laptop but there's some delay and lag who might be the cause of the spec of the laptop i use. I need a better one.. At first i was fustrated from how the level design are but not anymore since i learn how it works and i have lots of fun. I feel fresh to comback into the Gunvolt series for 10 years since i played the original GV1 on the 3ds.Rate: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: iX2 follows the Events of the previous game, but is disconnected enough that its story can be enjoyed as a standalone experience if you havent played the first game.Copens Moveset is toned down compared to the first game and the untargeted attack of the primary weapon is replaced with an energy saw, as well as the bullit mechanic being shelved entirely means that movement and attacks are a lot more deliberate and enemies can actually pose a threat, unlike the first game.Once again the bosses have great designed movesets - and this time you actually care - with weaknes reactions being a little less pronounced, the weapons all have unique roles in your arsenal, with seperate behaviours for locked and unlocked states, allthough the former are admittedly almost all some version of chucking a projectile at your target, but the tactical choice in most weapons having essentially two fire modes is greatly appreciated.Also worthy of praise, the game features a Hard Mode that is actually seriously threatening even for veterans in the genre, with limited HP, open stage selection, revamped boss weaknesses and the True Ending to the game.Lastly, while i personally stayed with Japanese Audio, this game also introduced a full english voice over for those that preffer it that way.

_childDocuments_.review: Story is about what you'd expect, it's an Inti-Creates title, the art is on point, as expected, and the music isn't as good as previous titles, but still good overall.So why rate it negative?That's because the gameplay kinda sucks.Copen now uses a chainsaw for melee combat. This could've been good, but they decided to make it relatively weak, extremely stubby, and painfully slow. At very least, you can still tag enemies and play a somewhat standard Copen. Except you can't. Copen's signature Bullit Dash got a hefty nerf, only sporting one charge this time around with the only way to recharge being touching the ground. But hey, once you get 1000 Kudos, you get a somewhat normal gameplay experience again. The level designs this time around feel very confused. It feels like they can't decide whether I should be playing Zero or Copen. I do like how the stages open up a bit around when your Kudos should be at 1000, but the previous issue somewhat persists. The bosses almost all have "Spark Mandrill Syndrome". Once you find their weakness, they really can't do anything to you.Apparently, there's a hard mode with limited lives and mixed up boss weaknesses. I think it's hidden behind the emblems, but for the first time, I really couldn't be bothered to care. I got the normal ending and that's where my playthrough ends.Just skip it. It really doesn't feel worth the price they're asking.

_childDocuments_.review: While I personally love this game, I don't necessarily disagree with lots of the Gunvolt Community's faults with this game. It's definitely not perfect and could've been much better and it feels like the fact that the game was essentially a sequel for sequel's sake really hindered it in the long run as this game was pretty much made in under a year to fill out space till Gunvolt 3's release.Sadly this game doesn't have Copen's trademark playstyle that many fans loved and wanted but it's not completely devoid of positives IMO. The game pretty much nerfed his playstyle but also gave him a decent amount of new toys to play with. The new buzzsaw melee weapon that Copen has is a really fun change of pace since it allows for more variety on how to tackle bosses and enemies, no longer is the only answer to an encounter "tag and shoot", some bosses can even be killed extremely quickly with the new buzzsaw combo than if he just had his typical peashooter and homing shots. Where the game honestly fails is the fact that they made Copen way more grounded, you just can't really fly much anymore and it's extremely jarring even if you've never played the other games where he's playable. It's not a change that you can't get used to but it's definitely not the best design choice.The game definitely feels like it was designed with the overdrive mechanic in mind this time round, get into overdrive and Copen pretty much becomes the same as his previous incarnations but the fact that it becomes a mandatory thing to abuse isn't the best design, especially in hard mode where you have to pretty much play perfectly or you get an overall worse character to play in terms of overall feel. I'd still defend that Copen's new moveset isn't bad, it's just honestly not perfect. IMO they should've made the bullit meter that you get in overdrive a part of his base moveset and made the overdrive version infinite (like the subroutine you can get later on). That way the changes can actually shine rather than be overshadowed by the overall nerfed feel of his playstyle. Really the sad part is, they have the gauge in normal mode mechanic implemented... as a DLC, the Yumo DLC boss gives you this passive. If this passive was part of the base game from the beginning as part of Copen's base moveset.... well I'm sure many people would like this game more.Core mechanics wise the game is pretty much the same as the previous iX game, you can find hidden kudos bonus medals around the map and the game focuses on clearing stages with a good score and good speed. Main difference this time round is the fact that Lola can now infinitely heal you at the cost of all your kudos. The visuals of iX2 are also just genuinely amazing, great aesthetics and visuals all round.Story this time is also pretty nonexistent, there's tons of small details that Inti honestly excel at, ranging from subtle character moments that showcase a lot of the bosses' personalities to small details in motion like Copen's armor changing when you're airborne or grounded. There isn't a "lack" of story per se but a lot of it takes a back seat till near the end, most of the conversations you'll have in this game are pretty much character banter and relations which isn't bad IMO. Where the story sucks however... is well... hard mode. They tied the true ending of the game to hard mode, which is honestly ruthless as hell. I will personally do it for completions sake at some point but the fact they locked crucial story elements to hard mode when hard mode used to be just some fun extra content for their generally short games is a bad change IMO as it inherently makes the game less accessible to most players. In fact hard mode was so bad that they had to patch in a mode where healing is unlocked from the start and you start with like 200? lives. Overall just a bad choice compared to even the first Gunvolt game's jewel hunting or even Gunvolt 2's secret epilogue where you have to clear 80% of the game's challenges on both GV and Copen to get the short scene.Overall... Is iX2 a bad game? Far from it, I honestly really loved my time with it. It wasn't the best in the franchise but I honestly loved the mechanics, after learning how to abuse some of the mechanics and how the buzzsaw works it genuinely does feel like a great addition, it just sucks that they had to nerf Copen to allow for these new mechanics to be added. If you have the money to buy this game AND the Yumo DLC then it's an amazing sequel that expands upon Copen's arsenal in pretty fun ways. Otherwise it's a solid game... just not an iX game. Copen is here but his moveset being nerfed really makes this game a hard recommend for those who want more of the original Copen playstyle.I still recommend this game as it's solid but if you're the kind of person who wants Copen to play the same as his other iterations... Well, I'm disappointed to say that I don't recommend this game. It took a while for me to truly appreciate the changes but it's a hard sell even for someone like me who likes the new playstyle and only wishes to have the ability to fly back.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I know what Inti was trying to do with this game. 	Copen (protagonist) was always busted, given that he could air-dash up to 5 times before needing a recharge. If he dashed into an enemy and tagged them, it restored an air-dash/'bullit'. This was all to the detriment of the platforming. Whilst exhilirating they could've limited him further.	The problem is that Inti's solution is such a drastic nerf of the character that it misses the point of his playstyle. Now Copen can only air-dash once, and his hover time is timed now.	A better solution would've been to simply reduce the bullit/air-dash count. 2 air dashes would've been sensible whilst still allowing you to refill one in mid-air if you tagged an enemy. Maybe reduce the distance travelled and require a wait period if all dashes are expended. This would've rightfully limited the character whilst allowing skilled players to play frantically.	Instead we get a game that misses the point of its protagonist's playstyle. They even ruined the scoring system. Previously, you chose a difficulty before each stage that affected how much damage you could take before kudos (the franchise scoring metric) resets: all the damage; 3 hits; no damage. Now they put it on easy mode and kudos will only reset if you hit a checkpoint or use one of your two abilities (healing or a screen clearing attack). 	This franchise scores you on clear time and kudos, so the idea is to play quickly but diligently. Getting up to 1k was a feat, and keeping it was a challenge. Now it's expected, and easy to maintain. It diminishes the scoring aspect of the franchise as it existed. And it doesn't replace it with anything better. 	I think the reason they almost guarantee 1k kudos now is because it unlocks Copen as he used to play, albeit with alterations. Once you reach 1k you can airdash multiple times, but I think you only have enough gauge for 3 dashes. Hovering uses the gauge as well, so you have to balance the two and dash into enemies to refill the bar. If he played like this all the time the game would've been fine. Maybe lock a longer bar and recharging mid-air behind 1k kudos to limit him further.	There's a 'hard mode' unlock that has the 'true' ending. I didn't bother, but from what I hear it's far more punishing and locks your health at a low amount. This game is full of contradictory decisions. 'Copen is busted' so they nerf him tremendously while giving him infinite healing. Main game too easy? Make ultra punishing hard mode with no in-between difficulty. Duh.	This game is good for a casual playthrough. Meaning a person that won't bother score attacking. And honestly, I think that's the majority of buyers, including me. But even I'm perplexed by Inti's blurry vision when it comes to their own product. Is it a fine platformer? Yes, and the levels are arguably better than iX1. Is it also at odds with its own game formula that incentivises score attacking? Undoubtedly. And I think your view on this game depends on whether you're comparing it to its predecessor or looking at in in a vacuum, because whilst I do think it's bad direction I also don't think it's a bad game.	Hopefully they have a clearer vision of what they want their game to be the next time. Because right now I'm wondering what the point of kudos and scores are when its impossible to not reach 1k. Why he needed a nerf if he was too powerful when they gave him infinite healing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of the gunvolt series, but man... it's hard to like this game. If you're expecting anything like the other games, don't. The best way to try like this game is to treat it as its own entity closer to a regular megaman game. The game is rushed and it shows, yet it also has all the telltale polish that could've made it a stellar game. If you're looking for the new apex of 3d action, go buy Gunvolt 3. That said, if you're a diehard who can take the game for what it is, need more Copen and Lola in your life, and can tolerate the ridiculous story and hard mode (with lives, for some reason?) then I think you'll at least  get your money's worth. Just... don't buy the dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: I love how Copen plays in IX1 and Gunvolt 2 but ultimately I think the changes to the gameplay in this title are for the worse. I understand why they had the idea to limit you to 1 bullit dash because a lot of sections in the previous games felt trivial and as a result the level design had to be simpler, however I feel like they took too much away and didn't give enough back. Much of Copen's score building used to be tied to chaining together air kills as high as possible but now thats not very possible until late into the stage on hard mode. Instead you're stuck with a pretty shallow 3 hit combo as your main way to build score up until overdrive. Overdrive itself has the opposite problem by giving you too many dashes to the point where it trivializes stages to a greater extent than even past titles and has upgrades on normal mode which make it nearly impossible to die. On hard I think the boss fights are pretty decent once you learn them but I can't really justify the decision to have a heavily limited live system at the same time. A lot of their attacks feel impossible to fairly judge on the first go at them and although that can be remedied with assist mode that feels like more of a bandage on a greater problem. You don't lose lives if you restart the whole level but the skill ceiling on some feels way too high to have that much downtime between attempts. Maybe I'm just ass tho. I still love the art, music, and overall style. Gunvolt series is so charming to me that I can't really call it a bad game; just maybe mechanically inferior to previous titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what you expect from Gunvolt/iX gameplay. Fast paced (if you want it to be) levels, with cool skills, and mobile character. You are pretty much immortal, although the system in this game just allows you to heal at any time, even during knockbacks(which are very short), when jumping or when being swallowed in poisonous acid. Falling into holes still instantly kills you, but as in previous games you might get an Anthem upon dying, which makes you even more powerful.Copen is controlling a bit different than in previous game, being more grounded. I've seen some people hate it a lot, but I found it made the gameplay more interesting than bullit hell from previous game. Your mileage may vary.The story is so basic and useless it could as well not exist. They wrote themselves in the corner in the previous game, and this one just feels like a filler episode of an anime. Happens in another world, and nothing that happens can have any impact on the "real world". I've finished the game yesterday and I already forgot what it was about. To see the true story you need to complete the base game, get all emblems hidden on the stages, and then complete the game on hard. Which I didn't, I just watched the cutscenes on the youtube, and it's still not good.The unlock system for all the modifiers is quite grindy, better items can cost 80k+ coins, and you get maybe about 5k per stage during your first attempt(where you won't get the best score, since you're looking for collectibles and learning the game). If you master the levels you get more. To maximize the score you basically you want to avoid all checkpoints, never use heal, get a lot of Kudos, and then finish the boss with your ultra to convert Kudos into the score. Not too different from previous games.The 6 special weapons which you get megaman style are very distinct and diverse. I liked 4 out of 6, other 2 I used only in the places they were supposed to be used to get a collectible. Most of them can be used in different ways, which is cool.If you liked previous Gunvolt games you'll like this, unless you just can't survive Copen control a bit different than in iX1. If you never played any of the Gunvolt games this is not the game to start with.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying, this game works very differently than the original.Basically the only thing I miss is the reload stomp.My only complaint is that there's a whole complex combo system to get enough points to activate diva mode, which is basically a super mode.  Get 1000 points and you're in it, but there's all sorts of modifiers.  HOWEVER, in practice it's just "get two emblems without using the healing skill or a checkpoint", since emblems are worth 500, and it's honestly hard to get 500 points from other things between two emblems.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 2

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the breakshift mode a lot, there's tons of satisfying hit feedback with the pizza cutter making your screen and controller shake, sending million sparks as I bisected some dude.Had tons of fun killing one dude, throwing the disc and had it quick break another enemy while I was dashing away at 300mph. Getting 1k kudos doesn't take that much time thanks to bonus emblems and big quick break numbers. There's tons of thought put into level design where you lock into an enemy while holding "the right direction"  getting catapulted away and by God's grace there was a ledge waiting for you so you can keep dashing. Or being forced to kill so fast or else you miss your timing on some stage hazards. (This is cool!)Bosses have EX Blade Tier fun movesets>Dacite throws grenades you have to lock on to create safe spots>Ninja guy having cool and long strings of moves you have to learn when to bounce into him because he barely gives you any openings.>Hail's shmup attack>Green soldier guy being my favorite... having a sick big robot fight where you can parry his energy blade with spin chopper and THEN he hops off the robot and you have to fight him as if it were Sekiro or MGR never stopping bouncing into him + his second version with the fire divekick is sick too.Don't even need to talk about not-copen, the airplane siblings and the last boss. They are all sick.However, HARD MODE is where most of this falls flat. >They lock you out of boomerazor so byebye bayblade shenanigans that made melee combat fun and gave it more tech>NO BONUS EMBLEMS. Bye bye Lola for 50% of the stage even with perfect scoring plus some sections look empty without them and there's no longer that fun need to do some sick calculated dash to catch one of those without touching 9999 lasers.The flow between Breakshift mode and Overdrive was so good on NORMAL story mode. You could see where the game expected you to be on Overdrive due to how the level design changed. But on hard... it's gone.Only cool thing you get off this slogfest "HARD MODE"  is some move variations on the EX Bosses and THAT'S IT. The stages are unchanged and scoring is awful because some stages branch in many sections and you are forced to WASTE your time to get X rank.Meanwhile on iX1 you had special stages that were more linear but with extra fun stage layout to bounce around compared to the story mode ON TOP of EX Bosses making it S+ rank in terms of replayability. tl:dr. Loved this game mechanics, level design (on Normal Mode only) and hit feedback (Controller, screen shake and explosions go brrrr).  but HARD MODE is just BORING, takes way too much time to get on Overdrive by deleting  Bonus Emblems from the game and literally locks you out of some melee tech even though it's more melee oriented that NORMAL MODE. Also less replayability than iX1 because of the lack of special Stages.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Too easy for vets, but could be a good starting point for people for whom Mega Man is too hard.Gameplay is fun but it doesn't really "sing," and the level design didn't seem "just right" until the Space level, which is one of the last 2-3 levels. The voice acting is also a bit much, and distracts from the game's strengths, although they DID add both English and JP voiceover, which is no small feat. Kudos for doing it, it just didn't really work for me.
