_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed the game.  As with most games, there are thing that could have been done better.  Most people I've talked to are upset about being forced to use the razor wheel rather than focus on the bullet dash, but I view it as a way to mix up the game play a bit.  There seems to be some indication that the older version of the bullet dash will be added later as DLC, so there is that.  I would say that it is definitely worth the price.  The normal play through is very casual and does not provide much challenge.  Hard mode is where the real fun is at in my opinion.  They increased the difficulty in all the right ways.  The only "down side" is that you have finite lives in HM and will have to restart the level when you die.  I imagine this was Inti Creates way of having players experience the level + the boss, rather than bash your head against a boss for the next few hrs.  Pros: - Character designs are amazing- Love the music/voice acting- Controls feel great/responsive- Boss designs are great and their move sets are slightly altered between normal and hard mode- Hard mode requires strategy and technique- There are good reasons to use weapons gained from bossesCons:- The story does not appear to progress Copen's character/world, and feels more like a side-quest from an MMO.- If you are a fan of Luminous Avenger 1 and are completely married to only using the bullet dash, then the first half of the level will seem slow (this just requires some creative movements in my opinion)- Unlocking hard mode is hidden in an area that is not obvious (I guess this is in line with the story, but I feel Lola could mention something when you are passing it.)- Combo system could be more robust. (Does not account for killing multiple enemies in quick succession, and gives no points for killing mobs with boss weapons)- Ways to get combos are unclear (Some times you get a quick kill with the razor wheel, some times you don't.  Also does not indicate that you can get some extra aerial points when using anchor nexus)
_childDocuments_.name: Gunvolt Chronicles: Luminous Avenger iX 2

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, a very solid and beautifully made game. I'm a little split on the changes they made to the gameplay. On one hand, limiting the boost makes you take more into consideration the platforming aspect of the level design, which in the first game was something that you could pretty much ignore. But on the other hand it makes the game slower, and I did miss the over-the-top combos you could do in the first one. But the game is still very good though. Bosses are fun, and I like that you can unlock costumes.One thing that does bug me though is Hard Mode. While I like the inclusion of it, I don't like that the ending of the game is locked behind it. It is a very brutal challenge that took me a few days to finish, and I don't like the idea of gatekeeping the real ending of the game, that a lot of casual players aren't going to be able to see. Another thing was the costumes. While I really love unlocking costumes, the ones in this game are questionable. I wasn't very comfortable with how lewd the costumes were for a girl who, in canon, is underage. I know that's like an anime thing, and there were some cool ones, like the Christmas one. But I personally just don't like that part.With all that said, the game is still very good, though a little short. The price is a bit high for what's available so maybe wait for a sale. But if you like Megaman style games, especially the Zero games, then definitely get this at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: First, the game is awesome. I get every achivement and almost 100% the game and that was really fun. Thank you Inti Creates!Compared to the previous game, you have no more bullet to air dash (you can just air dash once, to air dash more, Lola must sing). You have no more "Prevasion" too ( if you take damage, you lose some HP). In addition, you lose your gun for a kind of sword chainsaw. But, you can shoot with it if you lock an enemy. And it's working ! I don't have the impression of just flying above every enemy and bosses or just run into them and take no damage. Plus, you have a good basic attack ( because the gun without locking enemies in not very strong).The EX Weapons are great too! I used every one of them (except one) during all the game. In the previous one, I only use the half of them.But the game is not perfect. It's pretty short, even if gunvolt's games are short. I took my time and finish the main story in ~5 hours.I don't spoil more than that, but I was disappointed because there is a lot of "rematch bosses". In gunvolt iX 1 you have to fight blade 3 times (I think) and it's the same here.It's not a problem but wait. Blade it's the recurrent foe in G iX1. In this game you have also a "Blade like". Okay I accept.But, some "Rematch bosses" take the place of boss level. I'll explain.In G iX1, you have to enter into Sumeragi secret bunker 2. You have to fight :Rebellio, Stella, Crimm(old bosses) and a new boss : Butterfly Effect.Here you have to fight old bosses then... modified old bosses. It fun for one of them (ref to Megaman Zero 2 <3) but you don't fight more bosses than that.I hope it's clear.To conclude (before some spoilers) the game has new stuff and delete old stuff and it's working pretty good. The game is really cool, especially if you want to 100% it. If you just want to complete the main story, be careful because it's pretty short and you'll not fight true challenge :) The soundtrack is insane, new sprites too (even if skills animation reminds me mobile game like Langrisser Mobile, there are really damn good) !One advice, take your time and dont rush the game.Then...[Some Spoilers]No special missions after the final boss, you can just refight the bosses (same difficulty, it's not EX bosses) and the boss rush. And you unlock all of them directly after the final boss. So you can just rush the boss rushBut...You can unlock hard mode with medals. I First think : "f*ck the game is fun but short. And there are no EX Bosses" ( i love to try hard bosses)But there is a EX Mode !! Hard mode removes level up (you're block at 200 hp), you cant learn skills such as "more energy for ex weapon" etc...Bosses are insane !! You really need to learn patterns (Ace or the final boss for example) !!But levels are not very hard. As I said there is no level up, so you can just rush the boss.In G iX1 The level before EX bosses was challenging! Not here.The good point of hard mod is boss patterns (yes, I f*cking love that) and try hard again and again (because you havent infinite life in hard mode).There is a true ending too. (cool but i need the rewatch it again, i think)For me, the game is insane! Thank you again Inti Creates![End of Spoilers]Thanks ! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played that much of this game but completed the previous game in the franchise.And this is a downgrade in terms of mobility. Wich isn't good in a game that's based on mobility.Does it offer some change in comparison to the first game? Definitely. But I think there's just too much downgrades at this stage of the game alone (second batch of missions).Another thing is that they removed kudos mode wich means you won't be hearing the fun music unless you're really good at the game, wich I'm not, so yeah, no fun music for me. OR you have to skip every checkpoint during the missions which means that if you die, you get to start all over from the beginning of the mission, wich is sometimes quite infuriating and I definitively don't enjoy.In the previous installments you had the CHOICE to activate kudos mode or not. In this game that choice is taken away.I'll keep playing out of curiousity but I can't recommend this game sadly. Too much important downgrades.EDIT 1: Bosses are too unforgiving for casual players like myself. Just fought two that have attacks you can't counter so you're forced to tank them and face the death once again should you be too low on health.

_childDocuments_.review: It takes some times to get used to if you are used to the previous copen's mobility as this game heavily focuses on ground combat before you hit overdrive. Although to the people out there who just wants to play this game purely for the story, I highly recommend just watching it on youtube or something because an ending of the game is locked behind hard mode which is absolutely brutal, you will git gud whether you like it or not and your butt cheek will squeeze at every single boss fight (heck I'd even say harder than the hard mode of Mega Man Zero and Mega Man Zero 2). The soundtrack is decent as well, Ypsilon's battle theme totally slaps. Another downside is that the volume adjustment is pretty pointless since it barely made a difference when I adjust them, and pushing them all the way down doesn't even mute any one of them, so much for enjoying the music without all the cluster ♥♥♥♥ going on.Overall a solid 8/10 solely because of the ending being locked behind hard mode and the volume adjustment thing as mentioned above

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT-Lol. This review didnt age well at all, did it? Hey Inti, you imbeciles. Instead of putting that crutch in and ruining the point of Hard mode, why not add Darkness trigger from iX1 to it instead?Oh wait, because its paid DLC.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiots. 11/10 for making Prevasion-addicted scrubs cry.But seriously though. _childDocuments_.review: Dang good 2D side scroller action game, inti never fails to deliver! If you're a fan of their past games or any of the mega man zero games, you'll appreciate this! It's more of that same action fun, but with new fresh mechanics. They nerfed copen a little bit in this game, they removed 2 of his extra mid air dashes, but to me this is a good change and allows the creator to better make levels around it. Speaking of the levels! They're awesome this time around and are very dynamic environments with great mechanics and feature many usages of the weapons that copen obtains from defeating bosses.my only few small gripes are:-the upgrades you can buy are all mostly boring and straightforward, not enough cool combo changer, ability modifying upgrades like in zero 3. It kinda feels like they just did not have time to include more upgrades. Since there's only a small portion of them that are cool and show potential, but for some reason a lot more is missing.-the game's length is pretty short, I haven't finished it yet but I'm 3 hours in and close to being done I think. Duration will vary on if you make the game harder for yourself or not.-the lore is pretty much non existent, it's all mostly just a reason for Copen to go and fight some bad guys while not impacting the main plot of the games. Which is completely fine! until they try to force some moments are not earned at all. They attempt to have a sad heartfelt moment with one of the new characters in this game and it falls soooo flat. They expect you to care about this character you know practically nothing about, and have spent what feels like about 5 minutes with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the GunVolt series and Luminous Avenger iX.I am really happy that Inti Creates made another installment in the series! I did have an over all good time playing this, though I do have a critique.This games difficulty stems from the player wanting to get either high kudos or a high score, otherwise, the player has an infinite amount of heals (you can spam them endlessly and safely if you want). While I do like the player choice for difficulty, I do personally feel that infinite heals takes away from the stakes/difficulty of moment-to-moment game play. If the player had the choice to lock them self into a difficulty level, it would totally get rid of this critique.This is wishful thinking, but a difficulty level selection may be nice to either choose damage multipliers from enemies of limit heals a player has per life or maybe even a cool down time for healing.Just my 2¢Good game tho

_childDocuments_.review: If I could leave a Mixed review on Steam, I would. Might as well say this is LAiX1 but with a lot of design clutter and better graphics. I'm leaving this one as positive because I'm not feeling particular negative today.One of the most obvious things you’ll probably notice out of the gate, and maybe noticed in the previews as well, is that Copen has 1 dash that won’t be given back to you until you land. A lot of the aerial combat in this game is completely stripped away, until…Overdrive. It’s back again except you’re HEAVILY incentivized to use it. Remember that thing about 1 dash? When in Overdrive, your dash is on a meter instead, effectively locking your movement options behind it. You’re officially playing the game once in OD, now it’s time for you to not lose it.Right. There are two things that can reset kudos in this game (on Normal Mode). Using an SP skill (which 90% of the time is healing), and touching a checkpoint. Yeah, OD was so important that they removed kudos dropping on taking damage. A crying shame that they also tell you that your healing skill has no drawbacks right at the start. This game also has melee combat, allegedly. 3-hit combo that locks you in place when you use it. There’s not really any reason for you to use this except in one situation. Most of the bosses are designed with LAiX1 combat/movement in mind, meaning you’ll be right at home with them using OD. Unfortunately, they changed this at the very end and designed the final boss around LAiX2’s combat/movement. A real shame, since that means that 90% of the bosses don’t want you using your melee combos on them, while the final one EXPECTS it. And oh dear lord does it expect it.You want to have a much easier time (and more fun, might I add) with this game? Avoid checkpoints and never heal. Invest in OD Auto-Recover and OD Defense Up ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: Love it.You only get one air dash this time, but you can earn the old style multiple air dashes by going into overdrive with 1,000 kudos. Your non-lock-on attack is essentially a sword instead of the pistol, which is short range but does more damage.  There's also no Prevasion or Bullits, but you can heal as much as you want (though it zeroes your kudos when you do, so don't do it if you want to use overdrive).  It plays better than the first game because of these changes IMO.They also added sound and music volume sliders in the options (THANK YOU) though they don't go to zero for some reason, just very quiet?

_childDocuments_.review: Having a good time. Solid, fast-paced action plat-former that's great even if you're a newcomer to the series. Copen can't zip around the map like he used to but I think they make up for it with better boss/level design and fun abilities.Chunky buzz-saw > Laser tag pistolEdit: If ya'll are still iffy about the slower movement with the buzzsaw and all that, there is a movement cancel technique that circumvents the issue (it's not very hard to do either). Dunno if the developers put it in intentionally or not, but the gameplay's more satisfying for it. Give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: This one is... complicated. To rate as a standalone game, it's... alright. You can toggle some of the options which are otherwise busted. (Think like the Disney Rides from KH3 and such)Examples include: Standing still reduces all incoming damage to 1 (bosses signature moves no longer mean anything)Unlimited uses of healing (Nice QoL if you don't care about difficulty, but... weird)Other than that, the most dangerous thing in this game is that cliffs will instantly murderize you.You might be thinking, "Well, why positive then?" ...it's... complicated. Story wise, I am not a fan, mechanically I wish they didn't do Copen the way they did (bullit dashes are now limited to 1 before landing, you can't stomp land before like in 1 either. Instead, overdrive gives you unlimited dashes for a timer until coming into contact with a surface or enemy.)Similarly, on the subject of Overdrive, you no longer lose Kudos when hit.If you've played a single Copen game up until this point, know this: He is not the same, no matter what you do it's weird. He even has 7 powers instead of 8 like in most games.I played through the campaign only to learn that the thing that amps up the difficulty is unlocked only by completing the game and getting every single collectable and then you unlock Hard Mode.You could theoretically just handicap yourself for a similar experience, but you see...Hard mode has its own story beats and mechanics and is basically the actual difficulty spike of the game. No upgrades, no levels, just pain (if you're into that)What are the perks? An achievement and a special, albeit... kind of expected(?) ending. The story is... weird and I can't say I'm a fan. I would've loved it if I were 13, lemme tell you.But yeah. All in all, the game has potential and as a standalone... it's not *bad* perse.Would I recommend it to others? I guess so... barely. Only because of the fact that it does function as a game?Do I like it?...NO.

Besides, Lola songs are good but not as memorable as older ones, and the story is just ok.Overall enjoyable experience, but feels like an Inti experiment and filler game while we wait for GV3

_childDocuments_.review: The trailer pretty much told you what to expect: "Copen is the new Zero." If you are in for this, this game will not disappoint you.Aside from replacing the gun with a blade, the most noticeable change is that air-dashing into an enemy or a wall does not recharge your Bullit unless you are in overdrive mode. This means, before you can do a second air-dash, you have to land first, and this obviously encourages you to do more close combat on the ground.The change in the Bullit system also leads to the cancellation of Prevasion, so you can't avoid damage by keeping the Bullit gauge full anymore. (As a compensation, you now have the unlimited recovery skill, so you can still cheat the game.)So, the whole thing is really very Zero-ish.(I mean, if you want to do the Copen thing, you still can. However, you have to stay in overdrive mode, which means you cannot touch check points or use the recovery skill, then you can do consecutive air-dashes, shoot homing projectiles and stay in the air all the way to the boss.)I have just started playing, and am already having a lot of fun. I know the rest of the game will be great!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun I've had with Copen's gameplay.People are gonna be mixed with Copen's nerfs. My take; i welcome most of the nerfs. I do think that bullit dashes should be replenished off bouncing walls/enemies, and the breakshift style needs some buffs with the saw's damage/speed/knockback midair. Otherwise, this is imho the best Copen has been.The trade-off for the nerfs is better level design. As a fan of the previous titles, Copen needed to be toned down, as he practically cheats through the stages bu just zooming through them. iX one in particular was pretty bland in level design and emphasied Copen just tagging into things. That game is still very fun and recommended, but the levels in here actually feel like legit platforming levels. They are all beautifully made and have really fun stage gimmicks that make you wanna speedrun them again and again.Though the more busted OG version of Copen is locked at a 1000 point kudos wall, it isn't hard to achieve with the 'gutless' kudos mode being the default. You can easily rack up points and soon find yourself zipping through stages and enemies in no time. The shop upgrades are very easy to obtain as long as you first go for the credit gain upgrades, so Copen has plenty of customization to tweak the difficulty of the game. The presentation is very top notch. The english voice-acting is very well done, and the stages are beautiful, have some great tunes, and with kudos being easier to earn you get to hear Lola sing to you far more often than in previous titles. The bosses are a colorful cast and very fun to fight with slightly less bullet-hellish pattern thanks to the wider stage view and overall changes. Only thing is a lot of them tend to suffer from Spark Mandrill syndrome which can make certain fights too easy at times. For long time MMZ fans, there are so many nods to those games that you're sure to love. The story is meh, and fine for what it's doing, ending what seems to be a potential multiverse thing, but the GV games never really grabbed me as much in the story department. The best in narrative still hands down MMZ when it comes to their IPs, with BMZ coming close. I was at least a bit more engaged thanks to the top notch english voice acting.  My biggest gripe is that the game is too short, and I can only hope for an action/megaman style platformer that has at least more than 20 stages. So, whether the overall content is worth it really depends on how much you wish to replay, as these type of games are all about mastery instead of just 'beating it to beat it' anyway.I give at least an 8-8.5. I am very excited for GV3. This was a great game and worth my purchase. I've beaten it and already am down to rerun it again. Support Inti. These guys are great.

name: Crime O'Clock
detailed_description: ADD TO YOUR WISHLIST About the Game ALERT! ALERT! TIMESHIFT CONTINUUM AT RISK! Prevent crimes before they happen! It’s Crime O’Clock! Investigate cases through time and evolving maps by unveiling a multi-eras linked story. Will you be observant enough to solve the mysteries? Crime waits for no man! As a time detective, your job is to solve crimes through time that should never have happened! Each map has multiple time markers to visit and use to resolve different cases of hacking, murder, theft, and much more. But a common thread of strange events is developing over the centuries... Something or someone is trying to disturb time, find it! A HUGE zoomable map for each era is the playfield for the deductions and the search for clues. YOU must proceed with a deductive method to combine the missing pieces. By resolving cases the map changes and new adventures are unlocked. As you can see, it's a point&click game; the only skill you need is your fully functional brain to unplan crime! You will not be alone in your job: EVE, an advanced AI, will help you, providing guidance and tools. Using EVE’s system, you have new ways to find clues and evidence: deductive sessions alternate with action and puzzle mechanics for a complete user experience. During your adventure, EVE will upgrade its systems, unlocking new features... During the investigation, you will explore five different ages: Steam Age, with automata, crazy inventions, and gothic mysteries Atlantean Age, with its magic crystals and its peaceful and utopian civilization. Information Age, based on the real city of Milan in Italy, the developers’ hometown. It features some of the most iconic buildings such as Duomo di Milano, Castello Sforzesco, The Last Supper and many more! Lost Age - the sands of time hide mysteries and technological marvels Aeon Age - bright lights, ruthless corporations and underground struggles - all hi-tech! There's even more! The Fulcrum Stories mode introduces a new and different way to play Crime O'Clock. Move freely and try to reconstitute the journey of 30+ characters and across 10 times ticks. You might even recognized some of the characters...

name: Death of the Reprobate
detailed_description: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array. By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing; so on the seventh day he rested. “Did you have a nice week?” asked Mrs God. “No.” Replied God. “I have birthed another pitifully substandard world. Destined, no doubt, to spiral over millennia into a violent capitalist nightmare, just like all the rest of them.” “Never mind,” said Mrs God. “Chicken pie for dinner!” Story Immortal John is dying. As his last surviving heir, you have been summoned to hear his dying wish. Will he ask you to avenge his death!? To murder all those who have wronged him!!? To bring to fruition his life long plan to topple the ruling elite from within, shattering the balance of power, and ultimately saving the world!!!? Or will he simply ask you to stop being such a shit? Only time will tell. Or me, I can tell you – It's the last one. Death of the Reprobate is a gentle story about helping people and being a nice lad. Travel around a quiet, rural town - help the locals in their day to day tasks. Wander into the nearby woods - make idle chit-chit with a woman submerged neck-deep in a tiny pond. Climb to an idyllic viewpoint in the mountains, overlooking earth and sea and sky, the natural and the man-made, the eternal mystery held within the infinite depths of the distant horizon - help a man shoot some birds. This is a game full of slow burning simple pleasures... ...Until the Devil gets involved. Features Pointing and Clicking – A traditional point and click interface, with a 'verb coin' interaction menu and a simple inventory from which you can drag and drop your preciously hoarded items. Renaissance Artwork – Renaissance, Rococo and even a hint of Romanticism, to be a little more precise. Hundreds of paintings, spanning hundreds of years, are all brought together into one consistent world. Classical Music – Music by Eduardo Antonello. Period appropriate music that adapts as the story progresses, recorded using real medieval/renaissance instruments. Standalone Story – Death of the Reprobate is set in the same world as Four Last Things and The Procession to Calvary, and features some recurring characters/themes, but it can be played independently. Highbrow Buffoonery – Lofty subject matter is treated with gleeful flippancy. Gags about butts are taken very seriously. But rest assured, while some of the jokes may be ridiculous, the puzzles make perfect sense! (or at least adhere to a consistent internal logic)

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I guess we got another painting-based Terry Gilliam-like animation game from Joe Richardson. Seven years after the funny Four Last Things and four years after the incredibly inventive The Procession to Calvary. It’s still silly, funny, visually clever and kinda fun. But this time it also seems somewhat unnecessary, a fact that the game itself acknowledges.Just like with the previous titles (and the non-paintings-based titles from the developer), this is a point and click adventure game with mechanics reminiscent of the 1990s PC classics. You have a few screens to move between, a few tasks you can do in a somewhat non-linear order and you point and click on things to do stuff. All of the game’s art is based on classic paintings, that are remixed and reshuffled in crazy ways to tell an absurd and silly story that is an excuse to give the player some fun tasks, problems to solve and maybe comment on history. While this particular game is, probably, the most crass and vulgar of the three, it’s still very funny and with numerous moments where it’s hard not to laugh at the absurdity of things.Sadly, unlike The Procession to Calvary, that felt like a genuinely clever adventure game with a fun subversive gimmick, Death of the Reprobate has no mechanical surprises in store. And, in fact, this is the only game in this “trilogy” that I found solutions to problems being too bizarre and illogical to be fun. There is a built-in way to get hints on how to proceed, but a lot of the “puzzles” in the game are genuinely frustrating and unfun.Which seems almost to be the point. The tone of the game in general feels to be a “well, you wanted another game like this, so here it is”, rather than an active desire of the developer to do something interesting. I suppose, it’s good that what we got is still fun and funny for the most part, but I also don’t think this game really needed to exist or brings anything worthwhile that couldn’t have been experienced with the first two. If this game wasn’t so well written as a comedy, which is sadly rare, I feel like I would’ve not liked it at all and would have not recommended it. But as it is – yeah, it’s still alright. You should buy The Procession to Calvary instead, though, as that game is genuinely great.

_childDocuments_.review: Renaissance RevivalJoe Richardson brings his Immortal John trilogy to a dramatic conclusion with “Death of the Reprobate”. This point-and-click adventure, a whimsical masterpiece crafted from the canvas of Renaissance paintings, exudes a distinctly British humour that would not be amiss in a Monty Python sketch. But does this audacious blend of art and comedy ascend to the heights of a magnum opus, or is it just a bottle of piss?Paintings Come to LifeSticking to its iconic formula, this series masterfully blends the visual allure of Renaissance paintings with classical music, punctuated by timely sound effects that reflect in-game events. The artistry of incorporating scenes and characters from various works of art continues to astonish, even into the third instalment. The labour required to seamlessly fuse these elements to make them appear naturally part of the scene is truly overwhelming. The orchestral background music perfectly captures the period setting, and even those unfamiliar with classical music will recognize many of the tunes as they navigate through the game's diverse sections.One minor critique concerns the revamped dialogue display. While the improvement is mostly welcome, and the calligraphy-style text complements the game's aesthetic, the choice to present it in speech bubbles rather than on strips of paper feels out of place.A Good Deed Gone Wrong?Let us be honest, point-and-click adventures are not usually celebrated for their rich storytelling and deep character development. This is perfectly fine for the genre, as the narrative's primary role is to provide a starting point and a clear goal. It simply needs to be engaging enough to keep the player moving forward, with characters serving as puzzles to solve and move on from."Death of the Reprobate" follows this formula to a tee, clearly outlining the player's objectives and, upon completion, rewarding them with a brief, darkly surreal ending. Along the way, you encounter bizarre and quirky characters, each with their own problems to solve, serving their purpose adequately.However, it is worth noting that the plot echoes the first game, "Four Last Things." Instead of committing the seven deadly sins, this time you must complete seven virtuous deeds.Quick Trip Through the AbsurdThe short playtime kept the simple puzzles from becoming tedious in this entry. Interestingly, only one puzzle left me puzzled, though I found a workaround, I am still unsure if it was the intended solution or just an easy bypass. Compared to "Four Last Things" and "The Procession to Cavalry," I found the puzzles to be much easier this time, or I had simply become more attuned to Joe's unique and twisted thought process. Reflecting on my playtime of the previous two titles, it was evident that this one was slightly shorter.The Book of Quality AssuranceThose who know me well are aware that I have a knack for inadvertently uncovering bugs and glitches in video games. However, this time around, I did not encounter any game-breaking or significant issues. In fact, there was only one minor and inconsequential bug, if I clicked near a building's entrance, the protagonist would sometimes enter the building instead of moving to the desired spot. This was easily remedied by clicking a slightly different spot on the screen, so it is hardly worth addressing.Blasphemous Masterpiece?Did I enjoy it? Absolutely. Is it a stellar example of a point-and-click adventure? Without a doubt. Would I recommend it? Wholeheartedly. Should you play all three games in The Immortal John series? Definitely. Is there a “but” coming? Yes, and here is why.I adore the idiosyncratic and playful essence that harks back to the genre's classic roots. It is a must-buy for any point-and-click fan. Although it is a stand-alone game, I recommend playing all three to fully appreciate the developer’s story that spans seven years.So, what is the “but”? At its core, the formula has not evolved much across the titles. This leads to diminishing returns, not in quality, but in the novelty and impact of each release. With each iteration, the experience feels a bit less fresh. Consequently, I cannot rate “Death of the Reprobate” as highly as I would like.Pros•	Masterful Blend of Art & Music•	Humorous NarrativeCons•	Lack of EvolutionScore: 7/10 – Stays true to its iconic formula, though it lacks the fresh impact of its predecessors.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kinda disappointed in this final installment. Not much grinning or random snort laughing for me here. I don't mind that these are short.  and  were fun and funny (to me) and I was looking forward to playing the last game of the triptych. Where the previous titles blended social-political commentary of the middle ages and Renaissance art with a cheeky modern juxtaposition, crude and slightly juvenile humor,  feels more like my annoying freshman-in-college little brother went ham with tit, sex, poop, and body jokes after the first week of freedom on a liberal arts campus. It gives forced edgy in a cringe kind of way, the horniness is over the top, the sacrilege reads brittle alpha vandalism vs humorous or provocative... I just... I dunno... It's like I just watched some dude touch a boob for the first time the same day he realized homoeroticism exists throughout world history/culture. It tries too hard too much and goes for low hanging fruit instead of the witty, brash, and intelligent quips that were peppered throughout  previous titles. Every solution was basically handed to you,  The majority of  amounted to fetching things and running from one side of the play area to the next. Picking up every object you could and periodically visiting your inventory solved any momentary dev logic challenge. The areas overall felt boring, uninspired, samey, and small. It felt like Joe just wanted to get this done and out the door. Although it somewhat redeems itself towards the *very* end, I can't help but feel let down. The juice was definitely not worth the squeeze for me. Would not recommend full price, would only recommend on sale to fans wanting to see the end of the series. For newcomers I'd recommend either the bundle on sale or just the first two. 2.5/5 for me. Misaligned with the previous two titles.

_childDocuments_.review: finally, the conclusion to the epic if not that connected trilogy is here. more of the same pointing & clicking & slapping, now with flower-picking & bird-bothering action. a collaboration between a single developer and the greatest artists to have ever lived, it has top notch audiovisual presentation, and luckily silent text display without gibberish, but also has the always unnecessary typewriter effect, just about tolerable here.separate volume settings and manual saving anytime on top of an autosave, plus there's a hotspot indicator (shows them while the button is held, doesn't annoyingly time out after a few seconds), double-click to run, a few languages and a toggle for drag & drop controls, otherwise it's click to pick up, click to use.it's funny as hell, as usual, takes 3-4 hours (or a matter of minutes if you're a lazy bastard). the only things missing, on top of an instant text setting, are way more than 3 manual save slots (same as before, come on), resolution options and a windowed mode toggle (alt+enter only makes a non-resizable window, useless).I rarely buy (and even more rarely play) games on day 1, absolutely no need and very often foolish, but this, along with , was one of the few non-regrettable purchases. too bad the demo was only available during one of the fests, sad to see joe succumbing to steam's fomo ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ too.

_childDocuments_.review: Death of the Reprobate delivered exactly what I expected from it – nothing more, and nothing less. If you’ve played the demo and found yourself craving more, then do absolutely check out the full version as well, because that’s precisely what you’ll get: oodles of outrageously zany and occasionally vulgar dialogues, bizarre characters that never fail to shock and surprise, and a hilariously anachronistic presentation that combines classical art with modern, absurdist comedy. This is a farce through and through – deliciously outrageous and refreshingly hilarious. And I enjoyed every second of it.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: While definitely shorter and easier on the puzzles than its predecessors, Death of the Reprobate is still a fine conclusion to the triptych. To start off with a few gripes, it definitely had some more sexually explicit gags (which kind of threw me off guard), and in some places, the game feels a bit rushed. It's most noticable in the play time, but also with the puzzles - they are much easier to figure out, consist of less steps (you usually find the solution to a problem in the next scene, instead of going through several),  and overall there are fewer scenes, if I'm not mistaken. Makes the game world feel somewhat smaller than, Procession to Calvary, for example.But maybe it was my own impression.Gripes aside, the humor is as good as always, the level design and animations impeccable, and I have to applaud Richardson's creativity. It's difficult to stay inventive, funny, and versatile across three games sharing identical mechanics and themes, but he seems to succeed every time.Overall, I'd recommend Death of the Reprobate to anyone who had played and liked the first two games, but with a disclaimer that, personally, I find it to be the weakest of the three.Still, I don't regret the purchase, and am more than happy to throw money Joe Richardson's way :)

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but it's the weakest in the series. By this stage in the Immortal John Triptych, you know if you're the audience for this kind of game. Death of the Reprobate offers more of the beautiful artwork and cheeky humour that Joe Richardson's games are known for, but I couldn't help but feel that this game was missing the magic of its two predecessors.Four Last Things was groundbreaking on its release -- a modern point-and-click adventure game that eschewed VGA or EGA pixel art styles in favour of Python-esque animated paintings. The writing and religious theming were top-notch and unlike anything I had ever played before. Procession to Calvary went even further, expanding the game world and the choices available to players in dialogue, puzzles, and decapitations. If FLT was the prototype, PTC was the culmination of a creative vision. Against this backdrop, Death of the Reprobate is a bit of a letdown. The world is smaller than in PTC and no new mechanic or hook was introduced. While the game is competent in every way, I couldn't help but shake the feeling while playing it that Richardson didn't really want to make it. The spark just wasn't there. The only time that I sensed some real passion from the creator was at the end of the game [spoilers ahead] where he gleefully facilitates the destruction of his own world [end of spoilers]. If you only play one of the Immortal John Triptych games, play Procession to Calvary. That's Joe Richardson's magnum opus (not magnum o'piss, mind you). Death of the Reprobate is for completionists.

_childDocuments_.review: Another fine game by Joe Richardson, and a satisfying third game in the trilogy.  Unfortunately, the game makes it a little TOO clear that this particular series of games has come to a decisive end, but that's the biggest criticism to be had here!A little quicker to play through than the last one, but the sense of humor and excellent artistic choices we've come to know and love are back in full force!  Very much worth the price, and a solid gift idea for friends and family! Give it a go!

_childDocuments_.review: What a freaking masterpiece. One of my most sought-out qualities in games is a sense of wonder - never knowing what will come next. Every scene in this game is a new onslaught of Monty-pythonesque absurdities and unpredictable interactions. If you are willing to take a leap of faith, you will find something here. I can't promise you that it will appeal to you - but you will have an experience you won't have anywhere else. I loved the heck out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Just as ingeniously silly as its predecessors. Packed with blasphemous rabelaisian toilet humour and some witty puzzles of chaotic logic. As much as I understand, Joe Richardson wanting to leave this type of games behind, I sure hope someone will pick it up and keep feeding this niche. On the other hand, I really look forward to what Joe will grant humanity in the future.Although I initially was a bit let down of the short length of Four Last Things, I've replayed it twice already and know, I will again in the future. The look and dialogue of all three games is so on spot, it scratches an itch few artists can reach.
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Very good point-and-click game and a great ending to the trilogy! I really like the new text bubbles, they really fit the style. My biggest gripe with the last two games in the series was how the flashy text felt so out-of-place with the artstyle and this fixes it.If you liked the previous two games you'll certainly like this one too. As always it looks amazing and the dialogue is cleaver. It took me 3 hours to beat (without cheating, looking stuff up or using the in-game clue thing). For a short point-and-click game, $15CAD is a bit much, but considering it's one-of-a-kind I'd say it's worth it. It's the same price as a movie ticket.I must say however, my favourite of the trilogy is still The Procession To Cavalry. It had more interesting and grandiose environments and I preferred its story and quirky main character with the sword for interactions. The ending in that one was also more fluid / fitting / rewarding. Don't get me wrong though, this one also has a very epic ending, but the story overall feels more similar to the first game in the series than it should.

_childDocuments_.review: Death of the Reprobate is genuine highbrow buffoonery. With its biting satire, intuitive gameplay, and Renaissance style, Richardson has once again proven he can make profound statements about human nature while making us laugh at our own pettiness. _childDocuments_.review: The last of the adventure game trilogy features more interactions and tidbits than its predecessors. If you did enjoy Monty Python and Monkey Island (simultaneously), you'll enjoy this too.. _childDocuments_.review: Some compared it to Monty Python, while this being true to the idea of animation using historical art assets, the humour leaves a lot to be desired. _childDocuments_.review: I have to start by saying I enjoyed the game, it's only fair to say.The humour, the art, the music and the convoluted nature of the puzzle logic are all still something I enjoy, having played all the games by this dev before, however, it does feel like there was potentially a point where he just gave up and released the game?Having played the demo, I didn't realise that I'd already completed half of the game, which meant that when "The End" came up I was pretty surprised and assumed this must have been a fake-out. It turns out it was a fake-out, but only in the sense that a 5-10 minute long sequence with no further gameplay elements follows before the actual ending.My reluctance to recommend this title is based purely on price point to playtime though, so if you go in knowing that you're only going to get 3-ish hours and are happy to pay this price, then go right ahead, it's a fun little game. but if you've played the demo, don't be surprised that you're half done already.side note, i know my playtime says 4.6 hours, but that's because i left the game on while I went afk for a while
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Like previous two games, style and animations are very nice, and together with music they create a good ambiance. But the weakest part of the games is what author (and some fans) most probably thinks to be the strongest: "edgy, nihilistic" writing. Satiric paintings and surreal medieval themes give a very strong and tasteful base, but author just drown it all in his over-the-top wannabe acidic, but disappointingly bland sauce, mostly consisting of ground-level and very tired generalisations, like "love does not exist", "everything is only for money", "religion is stupid"... with new hits in this installment like "children are noisy, dirty and awful". It feels like taking a drunk angsty teenager to the museum: "all these men were stupid drunks, and all these women were wh*res! I would f*ck them and kill them and burn all these silly palaces to the ground!". In short, writing makes it a cringy cheap copy of Monty Python, whereas even the same game but without such comments and dialogs would be much better and deeper. For the next game, please hire a writer.
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Hilarious dialogue, excellent artwork (I mean they're museum pieces so it SHOULD be excellent by definition), puzzles are fun and not too challenging with only a modicum of moon logic.  The in-game hint system works great.  Only drawback is that I wish it were a little bit longer.  Definitely a recommended game.
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Joe Richardson makes really unique, hilarious games.  While I'm sad that this will be the last in the series, it is a perfect way to finish.  The puzzles can be tricky (solutions are available in game in case you get stuck).  I have played all three in this series and loved all of them.  Whatever you decide to make next, I'm interested in playing it!  Thanks for this game - it is truly a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Death of the Reprobate is another excellent point-and-click puzzle game following Four Last Things and The Procession to Calvary. The humour is just as strong as those previous games and the puzzles are now more polished than ever, thanks to some helpful guidance and structuring that makes it harder for players to get lost. This is a fantastic send-off to a fantastic trilogy of games!
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Joe Richardson’s spectacular Magnum-o-Piss.Death of the Reprobate is an unorthodox combination of snobby Renaissance art, high-brow classical music, religious satire and 21st-century humor. This game is full of personality, as it includes so many interactive things beyond the side quests and main objectives. You will want to scour every corner of every frame searching for bits of hilarious dialogue. Every single interaction is memorable and laughter inducing.I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of point-and-click adventures, art, music, religion, or humor.My very religious girlfriend and I have played and thoroughly enjoyed all parts of the trilogy, and this is easily our favorite.  What a swan song.
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasure it is to return to a Joe Richarson game!I loved Four Last Things and The Procession to Calvary for their burlesque and absurd sense of humour. _childDocuments_.review: Death of the Reprobate is a blasphemous bird bothering simulator for sex perverts and other degenerates. 5/5To elaborate, the game is VERY funny and well-written point & click adventure game with creative use of medieval paintings for graphics. It is amazing. Not wildly different from other Joe Richardson games, but that is never a bad thing. ALSO WORTH NOTING is that there is a dedicated bumblebee button, dedicated dog button and a dedicated button for sick back flips. Life can be joyful!The only negatives are that some of the puzzle solutions are kind of out there. But at this point that is an established part of the genre and an in-game hint system alleviates any frustrations. The game is also quite short. At the same time, it is one of the densest video games in terms of joke quantity and quality. Every interaction is funny and surprising.Absolute masterpiece of a video game. Worth the full price. 5/5

_childDocuments_.review: The third and final entry in Joe Richardson's iconic series, and very much in keeping with previous titles Four Last Things, and The Procession to Calvary (both of which are probably best played before this one, though you will be fine if you want to jump straight in here). Joe Richardson is a master of puerile humour (it's a compliment, honest!), deftly combining it with artfully cut-and-pasted classic imagery to create his unique style.Death of the Reprobate's fairly linear plot feels more similar to Four Last Things than the branching routes of Procession to Calvary. You're told to do seven good deeds, or you'll be omitted from your father's will. Cue lots of hilariously silly tasks to "help" people out. The gameplay feels a bit tighter and more refined than previous entries, with less wandering and pixel-hunting - both good things IMO. That said, I felt Death of the Reprobate's puzzles were simpler and more straight-forward to solve than the previous games (bar one riddle involving maths), and I found myself hugely overthinking some of the solutions. There is even a character that can provide solutions if you get stuck - a nice touch, but I imagine most players will find this much easier than Procession to Calvary, which had some fiendish puzzles by comparison. The end result is that the game felt much shorter than previous entries, only taking around 3 hours to complete with almost all achievements. I don't think this is the end of the world - and the way Richardson has chosen to wrap his trilogy up is well-worth experiencing, so I'd  definitely recommend this if you enjoyed the previous games!
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Death of the Reprobate is a satisfying finish to Joe Richardson's "Immortal John" trilogy, demonstrating what a delightfully unhinged mind can do with an art history and theology background. Your quest, given by the Actually-Quite-Mortal Immortal John on his deathbed, is to perform seven good deeds before the day is through (in an inversion of "Four Last Things" charging you with committing all seven of the Deadly Sins). In pursuit of this goal, you will do sensible things, you will do baffling things, and you will do things that are kind of awful.As with the previous games, each screen is packed with out-takes from over 500 years of European paintings, remixed in ways that hold together surprisingly well, and hilariously subvert the original intent of the art. The snark delivered at the artwork (especially when it appears in its unadulterated form) resonates with remarks I've made during many, many museum visits, some done while slightly tipsy.The puzzles are clever without resorting to moon-logic, for the most part. One will make you very mad. You'll know it when you see it.
_childDocuments_.name: Death of the Reprobate

_childDocuments_.review: Another classic to complete the Immortal John trilogy. _childDocuments_.review: I have been following the development of Death of the Reprobate for a while now, eager for more Renaissance silliness in my life. This could have easily been a disappointing game. After all, aren't the third games in a series infamous for being terrible? But, praise be it wasn't.Whilst I played through the game, my partner was sitting on his computer and would periodically look over bemused, as I sat at my PC snort laughing at something utterly ridiculous. Usually, this was due to a swear word in pretty script whilst a character was doing something equally vulgar. A true gift.So, what can I truly say to summarise the game? The storyline is funny. The art is pretty. The classic music is catchy. Altogether they create a juxtaposition of perfect absurdity.

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing a game by Joe. Absolutely love this. Genuinely extremely funny and charming. Immediately bought his other two games and am going to be finishing those off next. Only cons are its pretty short, I finished it in 2 1/2 hours, and that sometimes the "internet speaky-ness" of its writing, including the use of actual emojis, felt a little too out of place and took me out of its world just a bit more than I'd have liked. _childDocuments_.review: I've been eagerly awaiting this game after playing the first two, and it doesn't disappoint. Comedy is famously tough to pull off in games, but these are about the funniest I've ever played. The humor is delightfully crude, but whip-smart, and there's always some bit of pointed commentary among the butt jokes. (Procession to Calvary had a delightful dig at crowdfunding; this time, it's about AI art.) Great taste in source art and music--all of it put to great use and thoroughly credited so you can appreciate the craft. The design is tight and efficient. While I'm a little sad that this is the end of the series, it feels like the formula has been fully explored and it's a great way to go out.

_childDocuments_.review: Artistic, well written, funny, stylish, this game has it all. I have never laughed while playing a game as hard as I have with this game, the humor hits all the right spots in the best ways possible. The artwork that is used in this game is stunning to say the least and if you are an art buff will leave you wanting to know more about the various paintings displayed throughout the game. On a site full of indie games that pander and try needlessly to make you laugh with poorly written slop this game stands above them all with genuinely cunning dialogue with well prepared execution and timing to make sure the jokes hit you as hard as they can. As of writing this review I have only played around two and a half hours but I know without a doubt that this game will forever be not just one of my all time favorite point and clicks but one of my all time favorite games in general. I plan to purchase the rest of this developers catalog and try my best not to blow through them all too quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Death of the Reprobate' is the third and final part of the 'Immortal John Triptych' and it is a fantastic game. You take the role of Malcolm, the titular reprobate and dissolute son of Immortal John, who is tasked by his ailing father to complete a series of good deeds so that he may prove himself worthy of inheriting the throne. On his journey, Malcolm aids a variety of strange, yet hilarious characters in a variety of ways; from helping a tired father tend to his children, to finding a desperate woman a husband. With the typical Pythonesque and sometimes topical humor we've come to expect and love from Richardson, told against a backdrop taken from the gorgeous and bizarre art of the past centuries, 'Death of the Reprobate' is a gem that I absolutely recommend to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Blasphemy is a sin, but so is making me laugh this much in a game! Every scene in the game is gorgeous and stitched together with so much love. There are so many blink-and-you-miss-it interactions scattered throughout, and it's clear that a lot of attention to detail was given to the game! It's really fun watching all of these static paintings come to life, and to experience them through the hilarious contexts and personalities they've been given by the developer. I'd highly recommend this game to anyone who's an art nerd, a sado-masochist, or simply looking for a great time!

name: Have a Nice Death
detailed_description: Welcome to Have a Nice Death 1.0! Huge thank you to our community during our Early Access journey! You can now experience the eighth department - the Inevitable Time Department - with a new boss, mini-boss, enemies, the end of the storyline, 'quality of death' improvements and much more. Discover and explore the darkly-charming, procedurally-generated departments of Death Inc., where you’ll meet a diverse cast of memorable characters—like your affable pumpkin-headed assistant, Pump Quinn—who are always willing to share the latest office gossip Sharpen your skills (and scythe) through fast-paced hack n’ slash combat, utilizing over 70 unique weapons and spells you can find and upgrade to create devastating combinations Since Death can’t die, use what you’ve learned and earned to overcome the numerous minions and bosses in each department of Death Incorporated... over and over. A performance review after every run guarantees that you’ll unlock interesting items and upgrades that will help you progress on your journey Taking more power for yourself is a controversial move in Death Incorporated’s company culture. For instance, adopting a Curse upgrade for yourself might result in the Labor Inspector granting your subordinates enhanced powers, or worse, raising the cost of koffee and other items that are vital to your work output

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I will say this game overall is really good. Great animation, smooth combat, lots of new weapons/spells to choose from and can also unlock new items. However I will say there are a lot of bugs/over sights I have dealt with during my time playing in just 4 hours. First, the game has a bit of an issue with you putting a spell/weapon on your Y key instead of B (I use a PS4 controller). If you have an item on B and nothing on Y when you proceed down a floor it will automatically swap back to Y for some reason. I have had a few times where I had to keep going back to the menu to keep swapping back because I like spells on B. I've had two times so far where I loaded up the game and all my progress was lost and I had to start over. First time the game crashed, restarted it and boom, all gone. Not sure why but just be ready to lose progress if it crashes. Also, if you don't dash at an enemy CLOSE TO THEM you will not go through them and will be pushed back in front of them and get hit. I tried to dash through Grimes 4+ times but his thickness kept pushing me back and I would get punished. Now a few things I would suggest added is a parry. I know that isn't that WOW BIG DISCOVERY for games such as this but it does insentivize aggressive/risk taking game play rather than this hit and run scared game play. Gives more options and a feel of risk reward factor. Another recommendation is something I like from Dead Cells where it gave you rewards based on number of enemies killed without getting hit or beating a boss without getting hit. It felt more rewarding to me as the player to actually play better. Also, most of the time I ignore enemies unless I have to kill them because they barely give anything good other than a bit of money for re-filling HP but if I just ignore I won't even need to do that. So why even kill them? All in all, good game design/graphics, good animation, smooth combat but definitely some flaws.EDIT: Exited the game to put up this review and I lost my progress again. wtf I don't even want to play anymore because I keep losing my progress it's so frustrating

_childDocuments_.review: I'll confess that I'm not really a big fan of rogue-likes. There are a couple here and there I've enjoyed and fully completed, but I'm usually not that good at them and tend to get burnt out after a while.That being said, if you're like me or just new to the genre, this one might be worth picking up. There is a lot of personality crammed into every inch of this game, with the characters, setting and dialogue oozing with dark, meta humor. The characters will even reference previous runs you've done with Death himself seeming to remember exactly what killed him.I also like how the moveset customization is handled, with there not only being different types of scythes you can unlock and equip, which completely change up your basic attack combo, but there is also a large variety of extra weapons and spells you can use to augment your play-style.My only real complaint here is that due to its rogue-like nature, there are different currencies or mechanics that don't come up in runs nearly as often as others, making it difficult to fully explore every aspect of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand this game is in early access right now so any criticism should be taken with a grain of salt. I enjoy playing this game for it's humor, combat, and art style. It's fun to play like a hack and slash before your health is whittled down to nothing. One issue with this game is it is VERY punishing. Taking any form of damage will most likely result in a shorter run. The health recovery in this game is abysmal. It seems that when you kill enemies or break urns there is a chance they may drop anima (a healing orb). You may store up to three healing orbs and use them manually to recover health. Cool right? There are two problems with this. The drop rate for the anima is extremely low. Chances are you go through every floor up to a boss and never see any. If you do happen to receive anima they don't heal very much of your health bar. Combine that with the fact that you take a percent of damage as semi-permanent damage and your gameplay becomes a war of attrition.Another relevant, but smaller issue is room generation. When you go to the next floor you are given one to three choices of the next room type you go to. This will determine what rewards you will receive throughout that floor. The main problem is the amount of rooms before you reach the boss. Shops and The Forge become useless if you don't have enough currency. You will sometimes find yourself unable to purchase anything from the shop (heals included) simply because you didn't get enough soulary in previous rooms. Weapons and spells in the shop are expensive and are rarely worth it if you have your weapon slots already filled. Prismium floors may not show up in the random floor pool and only give one prismium. So being able to evolve your scythe is a coin flip. As bad as it seems, I think there need to be more floors before the boss. This would give the player more risk/reward. However, this would only be reasonable if the health issue was resolved.Don't think these things completely ruin the experience though. Have a nice death is a fun (and challenging) game. The weapons are cool, and the fury mechanic is amazing. The characters are charismatic and funny, and the art is top notch. I'm excited to see the future of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I've done upward of 50+ runs (?) and beaten the game about 15 times by the time of making this review, and I decided to go ahead and do a few runs on the newest update before tossing my thoughts in. First off, the movement feels AMAZING. They did a wonderful job of making your starter Scythe feel really good to use and depending on other weapons you find down the line your movement options can change. It was an actual struggle picking up Dead Cells again (which I logged 100+ hours in to) because after getting a feel for the movement in this game, it made that game feel so sluggish. The combo system is pretty cool too. Your scythe has a three-hit combo that can be dashed or immediately canceled into your other weapons. It takes a little getting used but man it feels good once you get going.The level design isn't much to write home about. The levels themselves look amazing, there's so much stuff in the background and foreground that change based on which department you're in and there's a lot of little touches that help bring it together. That said, progression in levels is pretty linear. save for the third department. You follow the path, you run into enemies, sometimes you find items/weapons, then you move to the next floor. I like it, but some will definitely find it repetitive. The enemies are great. They're all pretty unique and they all have their little quirks that you have to watch out for.. The little lore bits you get for all of them is cute too. That said, the diversity per department is pretty lacking. You'll typically run into the same 5-6 enemy types, and while their attacks are unique enough to keep you on your toes it may get stale to some after a while.The big one: Boss Fights. The boss and mini-boss fights in this are so well done! There's something engaging about walking into the boss room, hearing the music kick in, and then seeing Death and the boss start trashtalking eachother. It gives the game a lot of unique character, and the differing banter per each run helps to keep the game a little fresher every time. The fights themselves are also fun. Every boss has their own tells for what they're about to do, and even if you don't catch on in your first few fights its not that hard to pick up on. Every fight is pretty unique and you can't really treat any two fights the same. This goes for the mini-bosses too, who are plenty dangerous in their own right.On the miscellaneous, the soundtrack is great, the aesthetic and the animations are amazing. This game just oozes charm and personality. I got it for that alone and I don't regret it.I also want to mention a few gripes I have or had with the game. The big one that everyone talks about is the healing. When you get hit you can only earn a PORTION of that HP that you lost back with blue Animas, unless you find Pure Healing, either via Yellow Anima or Pure Coffee. Originally, it was complete RNG if you got Animas (the main source of healing) and you could go entire departments without seeing one. This made getting hit feel TERRIBLE. Not only that, but because of the gray health feature, it wasn't uncommon to have runs where you were stacked on Anima but couldn't use them because you needed Pure Healing and regular healing. Thankfully, the devs did exactly what I had hoped and made it so that if you're fully stacked on blue Animas and you find another blue Anima, it becomes a Yellow Anima. You can also now buy Animas between Departments. The other gripe I had is that for how big the levels feel, there really isn't much in them to occupy all that space. However, with this update the devs has begun adding secret rooms, and I think they've mentioned adding more secrets down the line. Thank you devs.Final Notes: This game is EARLY ACCESS. And we're talking EARLY early. This game was a buggy mess on release, you could clip through the floor, become invincible, do infinite damage, etc. If you're expecting it to be perfect you're silly. It's obvious the devs care and put a lot of heart into this game though, and I'm excited to see where they take it especially after their recent Infrastructure Update.

_childDocuments_.review: Began playing last week, and upon reading the reviews, it really seems like the Dev team took onboard the tips and ironed out a lot of bugs. These include having more bosses, level variety, an area to view all your past attempts, more curses/abilities, and enough choices when moving between levels to make them fun. Although the map layouts are repetitive, the weapon randomisation keeps things interesting. There's amusing employee characters; past reviews from others breathed life into the game. MY favourite part is the Hack n slash.My only gripe is not having many more opportunities to heal, meaning mistakes are costly as you ascend, (or rather descend) each level. But I don't care, I like respawning and having a choir sing: 'Welcome to the After Life~~~'. It never gets old. Unpopular opinion, I would place this game above Dead cells. Dead cells was very imbalanced with the sentry gun being the only overpowered tool out there to beat the game. I got bored with it very quickly, and the pixels obscures the game...making it messy. Have a Nice Death has very clean swipes and spell effects that doesn't overcrowd and leaves you in awe.GET . THE . GAME. . .

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of rouge-like games and this has easily become one of my instant favorites.  From the artwork, to the humor, to the overall types of abilities and combos, this game has it all.  I can't wait to see what else they bring to a really good foundation.That being said, this game doesn't do a great job at a few things:1. Explaining the floors - the first few runs you might have no idea what the floors are, and even after a dozen runs, I'm left scratching my head because the names are very misleading.  What I thought was supposed to be an anima deposit contained NO animas or healing whatsoever. I'm also not so sure why there are random minibosses mixed in the levels - they don't provide any special upgrades or curses.2. If you're using a controller, there is no vibration to let you know you've been hit.  Sometimes I'm dashing around and when I think I've made it out without a scratch, I see my HP and it looks like I've been hit by a bus.3. Point 2 also brings me to my last point - general HP and damage taken.  I get this is a rogue-like, I know it's supposed to be hard. What perplexes me is the damage numbers start scaling after level 2, and your damage won't go up unless you've randomly gotten to select a damage increase curse. Some of the smallest enemies also hit like a brick, and with no natural invulnerability after taking damage, you can be subject to 3/4 of your hp gone without a notice.  Again, I love this game, and I may have silly opinions, but I know addressing these three things would help me have a better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.Here's the deal:This game is fairly fun.It has charm, personality, an incredible soundtrack, beautiful environments, and a neat concept.But it lacks in a lot of areas.-A lot of dialogue feels half-finished and is filled with errors or nonsensical "jokes" (not to mention that a lot of the lines are accidentally assigned to the wrong person in certain conversations).-There are plenty of bugs.-A lot of the lore is kinda just word soup that doesn't make much sense even within the context of the game.-Narrative quests can very easily break and be unfinishable.-Half the weapons are not viable.-It just feels like a mess to play.Another thing this game struggles with is replayability, which is weird to say given it's rogue-like nature.Runs don't feel different enough to eachother.Most of the difference lies in what weapons you get.The enemies get boring after a while.The pre-built-but-randomly-arranged rooms get samey after your 50th run.And even the weapons start to lose their flair once you realize only about half of them are worth using in any capacity.What makes it worse is that this game is, at it's core, a series of boss fights.The actual departments themselves serve more to waste the player's time.The enemies are usually not too threatening. With a few  exceptions, every enemy is relatively easy to deal with.Even a mediocre build can sweep through most areas with ease.Sure, If you get a mix of tougher enemies, you can take a few hits, but overall it's not difficult at all.And then you get to the thanagers and sorrows.And then the game proceeds to completely change it's approach and amps the difficulty up a few dozen notches.You can take 9+ hits from a normal enemy, only for a boss/miniboss to kill you in 3.The game is a series of decently tough boss fights with semi-pointless filler between them.You spend your time between bosses going through floors, easily clearing them, and getting upgrades.The bosses are ACTUAL threats and can kill you with ease, while everything else is trivial, barely hurts, and is just plain boring....This game is an "art first, gameplay second" type of game.The visuals, the audio, the lore, it's all stunning.It's not without flaws, that's for sure, but almost all of those flaws are easily understandable and excusable.The team behind this game came together to create a work of art.I love the story being told. I love the environments.I love the music.I love the characters.It's a damn shame that all the beauty is bound together with mediocre, tedious, samey, and unrewarding gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Will be Updating this review after the promised changes and updates to the game have come.After playing for a good 4 hours, I have come up with a random review cause I decided to sit down and do this.Pros: -Music slaps harder than my father and makes repeating bosses not feel as bad as they do.-Art-style gives a great hollow knight like feel with the game-play being slightly similar to Dead Cells-Some Characters have good personality adding more depth and feel to the world.-Combat although can be clunky at times (Input lag seems to be an issue for me, don't know about others) feels fun to run around with all sorts of equipment. Whether you want the slow but big damage hammer, or throw out poison. The game allows for multiple ways of engagement.Cons:-The 2nd world is a strange jump after the first boss with rooms giving you 20 of the same enemy, if this is the case for the rest of the game it can get pretty annoying dying to the same enemy cause the game preferred to spawn them with 8 different cycles.-No other use for gold ingots besides adding more useless and sometimes decent weapon/food to the randomized loot generator.-You lose everything when you die, New weapon upgrade that you finally were able to get lucky enough to get? Gone because you made a simple mistake.-No permanent hp/mana upgrades making it an artificial difficulty solely based on luck-Healing items as scarce as they are only provide so little early game. Animas feel like trash when you can only heal like 5 hp and the golden ones only appear so rarely.- I dislike how prismium is handled, You can go an entire run without being given the option for a prismium department. THE ONE THING you need to get a better scythe or to get more than just 2 selections in the shop, and even if you spend that prismium, it is lost on death meaning always you will start with the basic scythe and 2 slots in the shop. Even if you upgrade the scythe, you still have the spend another one to upgrade it for that run. Even if you get one it may be a while before you can even spend it. -This is the worst offender and by far deserves to be at the bottom of this list, If this is a legitimate game mechanic it deserves the amount of hatred it receives from me. Loot not spawning in departments they should be, I've had in 10 separate cases now where I've selected whether it be Prismium Department or Soulary, or even Hr office to get a curse. Nothing would spawn but enemies. The loot room would have nothing spawn inside and nothing of the department would drop meaning you just wasted ur time going through that room for it to have nothing. It has killed a few runs for me especially when it comes to Vital-mana.All in All: This game is early access, Of course its going to have issues and sometimes lacking QOL but if you can get over the RNG determining a decent chunk of your fun then yeah It is a great game, but I wouldn't blame others for waiting as it does need some polishing.Have a nice death. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great style and humor. The problems i currently have however outweigh the good. The power curve in this game as is is wack. The things you unlock by playing is more random ♥♥♥♥ in the pool. So ironicly you would be better off NOT unlocking all of it if there are bad items. The randomness of healing is normal for a roguelike but this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. You can go from the 1 boss to the next and see nothing to heal with. The charges you MIGHT find don't heal more then the gray HP you have. The golden charges seem to heal more i only found the 1. The best way to play this game seems to be run by everything and rush the boss. Never found a real reason to fight anything that isn't locked in a room with you. For what more money? ♥♥♥♥♥ next to worthless since shops appear randomly. The enemies HP pool increases after every boss but it dosn't feel like there is a clear way to get more damage. The system for fighting seems to just be mash attack like a monkey. BTW you can use up and down to alter the attack string. I want to like this game but as is I really don't. Played Skull the hero slayer. And it does what this is trying to do better. It's like this started off not as a rougelike but was turned into one.Now with more hours in i can say for sure the combat is 1/2 finished. When you use a LT+(attack Button) it'll work like it should MAYBE. Facing left? It'll fire off right. The next time fires the way you are looking. It's also great that you can't do it mid air. Still can't see why. The basic attack is so unusable it's not funny. Why is the grim reapers scythe so bad at killing? Sure you can RNG hope into more damage for it. But the best way to play this game is to range gun down everything. The speech bubbles that show up when you talk to npcs go so fast that i can't read them and follow the conversation.  TLDR: Everything outside of the visuals feels like 1/2 of an idea. Come back in a year or 3 when they have the game finished and all the weird quirks, bugs, balance worked out.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: this review is based upon the Early Access version of the game.The game is pretty fun and I love the artwork and theme of the game. I will say that it was an enjoyable experience, but it feels like it needs a lot more content. Personally, I would not have released it as early access. Some of the translations seem to be a little off and certain dialogue points are still entirely in French. Some of the cloak/weapons you unlock take forever to find since it is basically random, and certain cloak/spells have a higher drop rate than others. This is pretty frustrating since you have to unlock those weapons ahead of time. There isn't an option to limit which weapons are in play, much like in early editions of Dead Cells. This makes it disadvantageous to unlock anything but the best cloak/spells for several runs. I have high hopes for this game and look forward to additional content down the road, but for now, I would wait to purchase it.
