_childDocuments_.review: I honestly love Roguelikes/Roguelites because of there replay-ability and creativity in game-play, but i'm sorry to say this game has neither for me. The game has massive flaws game play wise, and in other categories (but I will not talk about them because they are more nitpicks that don't effect the overall package, like how the boss dialog is not the greatest).The meta progression (which is cool on paper) can actually make the game harder for you which is completely backwards. All of the new foods are completely useless. "-10% prices for 10 minutes" does nothing for you. Getting a shop is randomized so even if you your able to find one before the time is up, you get what? to save an extra 10 soulary, sound pretty sweet to me. The main thing you want from the fridge is the one that gives you three healing orbs. but unlocking new fridge items make it rare to see it. And this goes for weapons to. Some are fantastic and fun to use like the Spiteful Chomper, others are just filler.The injures mechanic is very flawed but has a easy fix. It basically just makes it so that you can only heal the amount the you  have most recently been damaged, but it just roll a dice to decide how much it will actually heal. Just make it so that whenever you use a heal orb it heals the full injury, simplifies the whole thing into something responsible.On a positive note, the art has so much personality, brads and Will Hungs theme are absolute bangers. Characters like O'sha and Joe have some pretty fun dialog. While the secondary themes of the levels like Jungle and kitchen seen very random. The main ones like a garbage dump (level 2) and addiction (level 4) are very nice. While dark, the image of a a room full of people who hung themselves, and then Will Hung just coming back to life and goofily pin balling across the screen was so funny. Also having the same enemies from level 1 come back in level 4 is a bit lazy, but makes up for there slight design change being really fun.The game is not terrible by any means, but is lacking in any proper motive for me to continue playing, because both it's game-play flaws and how it handles rng.THOUGHTS AFTER UPDATE 1honestly didn't change much of the problems and only added new content, which is fine. It made the healing orbs and just items in general spawn more often. But just having the orbs is useless if you are not injured, BUT having the option to buy some at the end of every level now is a nice touch, lets you heal up after mostly likely using up all your orbs from the boss, but still getting hurt, and therefore having some injury, after you run out during the fight.

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game's writing, art, animation, music, and how it all comes together for the general presentation. The core gameplay is a bit harder to praise. This particular action roguelike leans towards the higher end of the difficulty scale. It's not so much that enemies are difficult to deal with as it is that mistakes are sometimes extremely punishing. It's not uncommon to go from full health to nearly dead after just a few hits later in a run, even if you stack your max health into the triple digits. The flow of combat is swift and the mechanics are simple, but these enemies don't wait long to swing after winding up to hit you and multiple enemies WILL attack at the same time if they're in the position to do so. If you don't stack defense buffs (either from items or mid-run skill trees), you're gonna lose some pretty big chunks of your health bar when you get hit. I've had quite a few amazing runs go down the drain in seconds just because I panicked while trying to dodge a sudden flurry of attacks, dodged into the wrong corner, and received a swift beatdown from some common enemies. It stings every time.I think the game is a fun challenge, but I can't recommend that you jump right in if you're interested. Instead, you should probably watch some (hopefully spoiler-free) gameplay of a run or two first to see if it's a challenge that you personally want to tackle. If you do try it, remember the premise of the game:Death just wants to take a break. You should try to take one too if you start feeling tilted.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea, concept and the design but after playing this game I don't really want to keep playing.Why?Combat feels good but little weird. Let me explain: It's a mix of hack and slash and soulslike, where player has quick executing fast attacks but you cannot cancel your animations. Attacks also cancel your movement and move you around themselves. I'd rather have more control on how I move all the time.Game mechanics are not well explained. I still have no idea what are the differences between different kind of floors maybe it's just the reward at the end but I can't really tell, maybe I have some idea depending on the icon and color but that's it. How do you get different kind of currencies to level up your character? How does leveling up work?Characters and story: I find it very boring and uninteresting. The motivation behind main character is little unclear, characters are always saying something random and uninteresting, I don't care about any character. I ended up skipping most dialogue after some point because of how long and useless most of them are. (Nothing is voice acted, which might have helped the game in this regard).Healing up: why can't I heal above some threshold? I don't understand the necessity of that mechanism. The gray bar that limits your hp gain unless you use golden regen. It's very useless mechanic in my opinion which is not even explained in game.Boss mechanics and difficulty: I find it bit too punishing sometimes, some boss mechanics are not intuitive, meaning that you cannot tell what the boss is going to do based on it's animation so you end up eventually dying because regaining health is not easy at all. What that means is that you need to remember all boss mechanics, which some bosses have quite a lot. If I compare this game to Hades for example, I have much easier time dealing with boss mechanics there because game is top down, I have more space to walk around and there is no gravity but in Have a Nice Death dodging some mechanics become little bit problematic because of soulslike no-animation cancelling playstyle and even if you dodge using special key attack can still hit you in the location where you end up after the dodge.  And then you start all over again.I had the most success with ranged and magic abilities that hone to targets automatically or have large AOE. I think those abilities were clearly superior to melle because of fast MP recovery during which I could just focus on dodging attacks. Oh, and some ultimate abilities are terrible compared to others.

_childDocuments_.review: Even very early on in Early Access, this has real potential to be my GOTY 2022. Right now, yes, healing is very difficult/rare to come across, so it's much less roguelike Hollow Knight and more like Dead Cells with boss cells turned on.That said, once you get a grip on the difficulty, you'll naturally start realizing attack patterns and general awareness are SUPER important, and once you're navigating patterns with ease, your need to heal will decline, allowing you to explore more offensive Curses (buffs that last for the run you're on), and you'll feel better about exploring different weapons you can pick up and weave them into combos and your broader gameplan on any given run.Once you get into that groove, it's super addicting - the first boss serves as a good wake up call to really make sure you understand HaND's fundamentals, and now I can routinely sleepwalk past him. It's the second boss that I'm starting to learn, and finally managed to beat him once as of this review. I look forward to the additional content!As far as personal gripes, the only real thing I can say this early on in development is to let the dash have a visual cue to let you know when it's ready to be used again - I've taken more damage trying to mash dash to i-frame out of danger more times than I'd like to admit.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been releasing gameplay for several weeks now. I have previously played the ORI games and this looked like something I could get into. _childDocuments_.review: "Have a Nice Death" is a captivating action game that blends fast-paced hack 'n' slash combat with a fascinating premise. In the game, the focus is on honing your skills and your scythe as you battle your way through various challenges. With over 70 unique weapons and spells that you can discover and upgrade, there are numerous opportunities to unleash devastating combinations and keep the gameplay exciting.The central idea that death cannot die adds a unique and engaging twist to the game. Players must utilize their experience and loot to repeatedly overcome various minions and bosses in different departments of Death Incorporated. The ability to receive a performance evaluation after each run ensures that players can unlock interesting items and enhancements to enrich and advance their journey.One particularly intriguing aspect of the game is the decision to gain more power, which is controversial within the corporate culture of Death Incorporated. This decision leads to curses that add a humorous and challenging dimension to the game. For example, curse enhancements for the player may result in the Work Inspector granting enhanced powers to the minions or increasing the costs of essential items like coffee.In "Have a Nice Death," players experience an exciting blend of action, challenge, and humorous elements that make the game a unique and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The issues of "Have A Nice Death" are as followed:1. The inability to heal yourself for most of the entire level. As you fight regular enemies up and to the point of the boss level one would have to rely on luck that there is enough health points for you to succeed depending on your skill level.2. There exists no chance for the beginning player the acquire a feel for all moves available to them after tutorial due to the fact that after the player dies they are forced to restart with new weapons and skills that are extremely unfamiliar to them. If by some chance a starting player were to become familiar with their weapon it is once again put up to pure luck that they would get the same weapon again after dying.3. While the introduction of curse/benefits and stores allow the player to gain a slight edge over their opponent it feels out of place for a 2D Roguelike game dependent on a player's success on that level and other levels to come. Since you do not keep anything once you die it feels pointless to have if the game is proving too difficult for the player already.Though I believe that many who have reviewed, played, and beaten the game have had a great experience they however are not reflective of the average gamer who play casually when they have free time. For a game to appeal the fanatics it adds unique art style, original gameplay, and detailed lore, but for a game to appeal to everyone it has to make some concessions in a way that draws in the casual player. Difficulty games can get the blood pumping but also turn away those who cannot get a solid footing in the first level. If someone plays a little bit at a time eventually within a few hours that player can get a feel of how to beat and win eventually rather than hit a brick wall over and over again hoping for a miracle. For this game to be more successful it has to let the more casual player be able to get stronger a tiny bit at time each time they play rather than tossing them into the fray. To put it simply crawl before you walk and walk before you run.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Good game mechanics foundation for a typical rogue-like.- Beautiful animations and artwork- Quirky characters, setting, etc.Cons:- This is definitely an "art" first kind of game, where it feels like a bunch of artists are making game design decisions that don't translate well and are awkwardly implemented.- Biggest issue by far is that most bosses have zero telegraphing of their attacks and do way too much damage, so there's just suddenly a massive attack hurtbox in your face doing anywhere from 1/3~1/5 of your HP. There's no real invincibility period after being hit, so you'll just get blasted by the over sized untelegraphed hurtboxes with some amateur-hour precise AI programming movement and tracking for homing attacks and get obliterated by something you've never seen before and learn nothing from the situation because its your only ****ing chance to play this boss. What an amazing design choice.- This game's 1st idea of progression is about running through a gauntlet of generated maps with pre-set bosses at checkpoints. The further you go, the more rewards you keep when you die or make it out. Pretty typical for rogue-likes but those games assumes that your second, third, and next consecutive runs are enjoyable enough to standout on their own and keep you engaged. There's zero real variance between runs other than the random pickups. The reward for this progression results in permanent unlocks to buff some aspect of the game.- This game's 2nd idea of progression is more about grinding kills on every type of enemy there is, with every weapon/side-arm/spell you pick up. This is tedious and lazy game design. The reward for this progression results in discounts to buy a chance to unlock new weapons/side-arms/spells in next playthroughs that are often worse than the base game weapons/side-arms/spells.- Killing regular enemies is mostly pointless, so you find yourself rushing to the exit of every level, leading up to bosses.- Tons of weapons/side-arms/spells are just completely weak so I find myself running with the same kit over and over again until curses (AKA boons) force you to play differently.This game is very close to being amazing. It just needs several improvements, namely for making boss fights more manageable, improving the enjoyment of the game loop, and making regular enemies more rewarding to kill.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a LOT of work still. The levels are TOO short, too few enemies, which in turn give very little drops,  the bosses seem TOO OP, and there seems to be no flow or direction. It's great that there is a choice of which floor to go to, but knowing the point of each floor escapes me. Half the time I can't even tell where TF the character is during fights, causing the player to take unnecessary damage. The health meter doesn't make much sense with the greyed out area and the health goes down WAY too easily even from minor enemies leaving you with very little health when it's needed most. Leveling up seems to take WAY TOO LONG to actually feel like you're getting anywhere. The secondary weapons do not seem to do much. How many F'IN TIMES do I have to fight Braaaaahd??????!!! After playing a little more I am noticing the awful attack animation during boss fights and how a boss can hit and kill you during the animation. TF is THAT about? Besides the aforementioned cons, the pros are great. The game LOOKS fantastic! The control of the character feels pretty tight, (with the exception of it moving so fast it's hard to keep track of where he is), the color palette is perfect, the music is BRILLIANT!, and the story line, so far, is most entertaining. (still not sure why Death's underlings would be so disrespectful towards him),... The only reasons I would not recommend this game have already been stated. It seems it is still a work in progress. It NEEDS a LOT of work. There seem to be a lot of places where there could be hidden items, and there is nothing. The levels seem very short and kind of make no sense in some places, as there are areas that a player can go to where there is no point of even going. (Hidden items throughout levels would be a SUPER upgrade for this game). I hope this critique causes inspiration rather than dislike. This game COULD be a masterpiece. For now, it should be FREE.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: Combat. The combat feels great (at least, the scythe does). Art style is amazing, especially at 4k/144hz. Movement feels really good, and the dash is great. However, outside of that - I can't recommend the game. It's a roguelike, but... in other roguelikes, you unlock things that make you stronger so the next run you go, you get a little further. This one has 0 permanent unlocks, upgrades, etc. The only progression is you RNG your way through rooms that give you the currency you need to upgrade weapons. The curse system is pointless as they offer very little in the way of making you stronger. Most of the curses require you to get hit to activate.... which makes no sense. Also, good luck healing. You can hold up to 3 healing Animas, but you might find 1 every 3 or 4 runs. The game has potential, and the artwork department did a killer job, but the gameplay department might wanna play a roguelike to see how they actually function.

_childDocuments_.review: So...I love rogue-lights (and roguelikes, but I like a Hades way more than a spelunky), they make up 90% of my steam playtime and I've logged 100s of hours into enter the gungeon, hades, Nuclear throne, isaac, and most relevant for this game: Dead Cells. Although the game is still in early access, after the latest big patch, I think Have a Nice Death has the bones (no pun intended) to become the next big contender to the rogue-light crown. A 2d fast paced action game hasn't felt this tight since Dead Cells, and you can tell that some (or all? not up on my game org charts) of that game's staff helped make this; and if you're a dead cell's fan; let's be honest, you've already bought this. that said, if you're at all a fan of the genre, It's still a hard recommend. Beyond how the game feels, The game is GORGEOUS like...cuphead gorgeous, with beautiful hand drawn art and some pretty crazy effects. That doesn't mean the game is perfect; it's unforgivingly difficult (as opposed to forgivingly difficult, like a dead cells, or a dark souls), and currently, a major aspect of in-run progression (the ability to level up your weapons) is entirely based on RNG, and could either never come, or come too early or too late to actually come in handy; and it's darn near required to advance past the 2nd biome. There's also next to no metaprogression; meaning there's nothing that you can do to improve your character run-to-run. The only thing you can unlock are more items...which never seem to spawn when you need them! However, the devs have heard these issues, and seem to be correcting them, but don't buy a game with the promise of future updates.Also, even now, the game is so hard, completing a 4 biome run might take you a REALLY long time, but the combat here is so fun, you won't mind!

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Have a Nice Death is a visually stunning action platformer roguelight w/ the emphasis placed on the action.  The expectations have been through the roof b/c of how dynamic and interesting the artistic design and animations are.  For an early access title, it's well polished.  However, as of right now, it's very limited on content, needs some balancing changes, and starts to feel tedious within the first few hrs.*Notes:-As of March 2022, I have played for just under 4 hrs of the early access version of HAND.  I plan to revisit in 9-12 months, when this project is closer to that 1.0 window.What's Good:-This game absolutely shines visually!  This is one of the better looking games out there.  The visual style is kind of a blend of Hollow Knight, The End is Nigh, and Grime.  The background environment is very cool looking, and the animations steal the show.  Bosses are very interesting visually, physically imposing, and all have a distinct style.  The art style gets an A from me!-The soundtrack although limited, is great.  It has kind of an upbeat Tim Burton feel, and fits the tempo of the game perfectly.  The entire audio design is rock solid even and will only get better as they add more variety to the final build.-HAND opts for a very interesting meta progression choice.  Basically, you will earn currency which allows you to purchase various weapons to be added to the weapon pool.  As you get closer to completing certain achievements, you will get a discount on these weapons.  This is a brilliant idea, b/c it motivates players to jump back in for a few more runs in order to save as much currency as possible.  If you ever feel like you aren't making any progress on a coveted item, you can just purchase it for full price.  This is a system I'd love to see implemented more frequently in this genre.-This is a fast paced, action focused game that trims the fat.  You won't ever get bogged down by too much narrative or filler.  This is an easy game to jump in and immediately start cutting up baddies.Could Use Some Changes:-After almost 4 hrs, I haven't found a single secret.  There are tons of places in the world that seem like they would perfect for a secret to be behind a wall, but as far as I'm aware, they don't exist.  This is a problem b/c it makes the world feel a bit bland.  The level layout starts to feel stale really quickly.-Platforming is almost non-existent.  You will jump, dash, and move around plenty.  However, it's so simple and predictable, that it feels like a missed opportunity.-There just isn't enough variety in the enemy types.  There are only about 4 enemy types per stage.  Since there are no secrets, close to no platforming, very predictable level layouts, and all of the enemies quickly blend together - this leads to the early parts of runs feeling extremely tedious.-There needs to be alternative bosses, more unlockable weapons, and more interesting synergies for the powerups.  This is an issue that almost every early access roguelight project faces, so I feel confident that this will be cleared up over the next year.Consensus:-Middle of the Road Game (Tier 4 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  HAND has so much potential, but as of now, it feels like it needs a bit more time in the oven.  It's only $15, so I don't think it's bad value at that price point.  However, there are also so many incredible games in this genre that are fully finished and offer tons of variety for basically the same price point.  I would moderate your expectations going in.  This is not the second coming of Hollow Knight and Dead Cells imo.  I do think the final product will be a really well rounded, unique, and dynamic experience.  It just may take some time to get there.  Pick it up when it's on sale and see what you think.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like combat platformers and you like roguelites, this one's a no brainer. But be warned: this game is really difficult. By far the hardest roguelite I've played. The bosses are extremely quick and kill you in a few hits. Healing doesn't do a whole lot when you can get 3 shot in the span of 2 seconds, so be ready to die many times.POSITIVES:- Tight, responsive controls (other than UP+attack seeming to not always work). Movement and combat feels very similar to Hollow Knight but even quicker.- Beautiful art and animations- Great sound and music- Wide variety of bosses that have interesting and unique movesets- Wide variety of weapons and power ups that make each run feel a little different- You get to choose rooms and even entire floors as you go which also gives each a run a little more variation- Enemies' bodies do not have hitboxes. You can only be damaged by their attacks. Furthermore, your dash has i-frames. This works really well for this game as it is fast paced and precise. Taking damage never feels cheap and you know you could have avoided it if you played better.- Tons of characters with their own dialogue and side stories if you're into that sort of thing. None of it seemed very important so I mostly skipped it.NEGATIVES:- Lack of regular enemy variety and difficulty. This game is actually surprisingly easy other than the bosses. You breeze through levels stunning every enemy in your way only to get obliterated by the boss.- Lack of clear explanation for a lot of game mechanics. This paired with the fact that there is almost no information about this game online means that you are often just taking wild guesses as to how some mechanics work.- Some weapons/spells just feel WAY more powerful than others which limits build potentialNEUTRAL:- Difficulty. This could be a positive or negative depending on how much of a masochist you are. The game has an "easy" mode. Don't be fooled, it's not even remotely easy. It's way harder than heat 10 in Hades. The regular game is near impossible without getting a busted build (or maybe I just suck at the game). I've only beaten the game a few times in the 50 runs I've done.Overall, I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes combat platformers and roguelites and wants a solid challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review in early September 2022 while the game is in early access so I expect I'll need to update the review later. OVERVIEW:This game has a LOT of potential. I think it could eventually stand with Hades and Hollow Knight. Unfortunately it's not there yet, which is unsurprising given it's early access. Right now players are essentially giving the devs data to improve the game and see what works and what doesn't. Gameplay itself is surprisingly un-buggy for early access. PROS:-Lovely aesthetic. Everything is nicely stylized, the animation is delightful and the whole atmosphere nails grim humour on the head. -I found the controls reasonably intuitive and nicely responsive. It took a few runs to get used to them of course, but I think there's potential for really great emergent gameplay as the game develops. Animations for actions are real clean and the i-frames in the dash/dodge had no problems that I experienced. -Great concept. The content that's there is fun, poignant and relatable. CONS:-My game keeps crashing! It crashes while I'm in an elevator between levels. Fortunately crashing doesn't lose all progress made that run, but it's frustrating having to re-do a level especially if I had a good run pre-crash and then a bad run post-crash. -Unforgiving: this could be a pro or a con depending on what you like. Right now, for me, it's a con because unlike other rogue-likes, there doesn't really seem to be a way to get permanently stronger in between runs. The resources you spend after dying and returning to the beginning go into buying a greater variety of weapons for RNG to give you during your playthrough. What I'd like to see are options to increase health pool permanently, or options to increase spawn rate of health items, weapon and curse drops etc. Spending options in between runs are limited. I didn't feel like I was making any sort of progress or had anything to work towards other than just getting to further levels over and over. -The mechanics and gameplay itself was great, but I got no overarching sense of plot beyond "get out there and kill as much as you can". I don't know if I've gotten far enough yet to find it, but even in the first couple hours of other similar games it felt like there was an overall plot developing and a lore-rich world to play in. This may be missing because it's early access or it may just not be coming. Obviously I'm hoping for the former. Overall, despite the cons, I'd recommend the game because it's early access and has incredible potential. From what I understand, the Devs are really paying attention to what players are saying. I hope this is true because the good aspects of the game are really really good. I just need *more*. More depth, more variety, more character ability development.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I would have loved this game to be good, having been in the discord server since the first trailer and always being blown away by the passion in both the art and witty corporate satire, it just doesn't hold up in gameplay.The movement is quite clunky, in that the character is very stiff with little air control and the dash seems to have a cooldown for no other reason than for there to be curses to make it feel nice to use. It's also extremely long, often leading to you dashing through something to avoid something, but resulting in you getting hit by another part of the same attack (very common in thanager and sorrow fights)The combat is only tactile and snappy for a few weapons, with the rest being simply too slow (e.g parasol or the buff cloak), too overpowered to care (e.g any busted curse synergy) or spawning so many particles that you easily get hit or the game crashes (e.g lyberis skulls) or something else which doesn't make you enjoy the experience.Speaking of combat, the balancing is not the best, especially when there's achievements for beating the game with ridiculous artificial difficulty modifiers. As you rampage through death inc. the enemies will accumulate a large amount of health, so unless you get a run with a stupid combination of curses, weapons or both your thumb is going to get really tired of mashing buttons. Having played through early access there has definitely been improvements to quality of life. I don't feel like run success is determined by anima luck anymore - just weapon and curse luck now. I think the tree is a bit redundant, with the most useful things being doors that make even more blatant the health balancing issues since you don't have curses.The game's level design is nearly non-existent save for some of the platforming in the intriguing floors and the final level. This is probably due to the heavy reliance on procedural generation but even in the cases previously mentioned the movement meant that these were notoriously unfun.Lastly the game is pretty badly optimised, having multiple consistent crashes even after early access due to the amount of particles on screen. Not even having an FPS limiter to cater in some way to this problem is downright ignorant.TLDR; art style and humour is phenomenal but the gameplay where most of the time is spent lets it down tremendously

_childDocuments_.review: So here is the thing... i like it, but i don't love it. I beat the game a little after 10 hours, and now other than unlocking the last weapon left i feel no compulsion to keep playing. Here is a short breakdown:Pro: gorgeous, smooth combat, and satisfying play. I love how tight the game is and the dash and movement is so fluid. The setup is nice, being able to choose floors lets you have a hand in your run and go in the direction you need most.Cons: the RNG is bad... like really bad. I got the same weapon on the same floor 3 times... then on the next floor same weapon twice. If you get an OP drop, boom... you win your run. It isn't as much skill based as lets say dead cells. I also have no incentive to continue to play after winning. Granted, it is still in early access so i anticipate the devs will add more. also... every floor feels exactly the same after the 8th hour... no mixup at all. i know exactly where enemies are and it gets bland very quickly.Overall: it is a 7.1 out of 10 for me. not a bad game, at all. But the shelf life appears to be about 20 hours and that is it. It doesn't have that dead cells factor, that keep playing and challenging yourself and get better to it. Not much to unlock after a short bit. BUT, it is early access. So i recommend it. There will be more to come and more added i am sure. it is a funny and fun little game you will enjoy.

Weapons and curses (which are buffs you can get for each run), those I can see being RNG-based in which ones you get each run. But it looks like the side quests are also kinda RNG based? I don't play rogue-lites that much, so this could 100% be me being out of the loop. But each run, you might get a character that has some dialogue to advance you along a side quest. But it's not guaranteed you'll get that character dialogue, even if you've done everything you're supposed to for that quest up to that point. Even after 159 hours of gameplay, I still have a quest or two that isn't finished. But that's not required to 100% the game, so it's not a huge deal. Just mildly annoying.Bottom line is, some tiny problems, but well worth your time regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm only 4 hours in, but those 4 hours have been great. Its kinda like Dead Cells, but kinda not. There aren't really any paths to take, thought it looks like they will be adding something like that. You are stuck with a scythe (though rarely in a run you can power it up to a slightly different version) and two abilities, either magic or cloak abilities. Magic uses mana (which recharges very fast, like a few seconds after spending it all) and cloak does not use mana. You also need to conserve your life beacause you CANNOT HEAL MISSING HEALTH only the most recent "injuries" which is a greyish part of the healthbar about equal to the last hit you took. So in order to regain HP once you lose it, you need to find an item that turns your entire bar into injury mode and then pop whatever heals you have available. This makes the game more difficult as you really need to focus on not getting hit and basically use your heals when you get hit by a big boss attack or something of the sort to get the most out of your heals.You will lose a lot and replay the exact same fights a lot, so its good that they have an absurd amount of dialog for the fights. Like some bosses I've done 10 times now and I haven't seen a repeat of dialog yet. Honestly, this game is fun right now and it has a ton of potential for the future. If you like action roguelikes then this is a game you will enjoy. If you are unsure then put it on your wishlist and wait 6 months to a year and check back. I'm sure its going to be considered one of the best games in the genre in a year or 2.Oh also, there is no upgrading outside of a run. You can unlock weapons which gives you the chance to find new things during future runs, but that's it. No stat upgrades or anything.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Magic Design Studio's really have a unique way of creating awesome atmosphere for all their games and this one is definitely a step up on Unruly Heroes in my opinion. I love the unlockable skills in this game and the boss encounters and the variety of bosses. As a roguelike every run is different to your last which keeps things interesting. My one complaint about the game is that nothing you achieve on a run carries over to your next run which essentially means that, depending on your playstyle, success in a run can be highly RNG dependent. I'm hopeful that this changes at some point and you can 'configure' your loadout a bit more before a run gets underway. Overall though, Have a Nice Death is an awesome game, loads of fun, and seriously well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10. Good. Not jaw-dropping, but good.Pros:Great visuals, sound, good music. Solid, smooth gameplay. Lots of fun builds. Very animated characters, occasionally with good humor. Amazingly convenient built-in way of reporting bugs.Cons1. The story and dialog don't make a lot of sense (and yes, I have a desk job). There are a few moments of good humor, but nothing beyond a mediocre sitcom. Often the dialog and story make absolutely no sense, like they were written by a bad AI. The humor and commentary should make this game stand out, but a lot of it is just disappointing.2. At this point, a game in this genre needs to bring something outstanding to the table. Have a Nice Death's visuals are exceptional, but that's it. It doesn't really set the bar, stand out, or bring anything new worth noting to the table.3. A couple of very minor bugs. Not worth avoiding the game over.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of good qualities, to name a few:- Characters are funny/quirky (the cast is unique and I've started to adore them and their interaction)- Story is in an interesting setting (I know that the death god theme has already been used in the roguelike game Hades but I still think this game has lots of potential using the Grimm Reaper take on this theme)- It looks cute in a creepy way (the art looks like a combination of the metroidvania Hollow Knight and the roguelike Dead Cells and it really attracted me to buying this game)However there are a few things that prevent this game from really shining, the biggest ones being:- Player character sometimes glitches and gets stuck in passable platforms when jumping through (this is also occasionally accompanied with the soundtrack temporarily breaking)- The spawn rate for healing items is very low (I have gone thru runs where none spawned in the first world, leaving me with barely any HP to fight the boss)- The rare/special currency and the upgrades you could buy with it are lost upon a run ending (you'll get extra points for having it but it still feels kind of useless to get/use sins it will ultimately make no difference to gameplay, admittedly I only managed to get past the first world boss)- The hit boxes are way to big (I can hit enemies that are about 2 player characters away from me and enemies can hit me even when I dodge)- The game doesn't feel rewarding on the long run (besides the glowing bubbles at the spawn room, the codex entries, and the dialogue from the NPC's there just aren't any other changes to the world which just doesn't make me feel like I'm progressing gameplay wise)In the end I really like this game, it's brimming with potential and I hope the developers can work out the few programming kinks and gameplay imbalances.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, very well done. Very good art and ambiance, however the one critical flaw is that this game NEEDS stronger healing. Nothing is more annoying then having two or even three animas with no injuries to heal. In my opinion, the injury system needs to be scrapped and animas heal their same values in health, up to full. While I get this game is supposed to be a challenge, it feels like the system is rigged against you when it was already pretty difficult to begin with. With that said, I would recommend, just don't expect much healing.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler warning ahead!!This game has a lot of amazing stuff going for it!! The gameplay feels fun and fluid, with each combination of spells and weapons you find feeling like there's a fair amount of mastery and strategic building when picking curses and upgrading items. Obviously it's early access and it shows at some points when you're playing, but there is a LOT of room for growth and potential here. I'm very excited to see where the game goes, I've had a blast getting some surprisingly powerful runs, and the game feels fun enough even with the base stats and no unique items, that says a lot for a rogue like.Specific things:- I REALLY like how all of the enemies are powerful but easy to deal with on their own, when there's a LOT of enemies in the same room it can get VERY difficult and it feels like the counterplay is based around smart and skillful play rather than trying to use cheesy strategies. It never feels unfair or like I didn't deserve to get hit by an enemy or even an enemy's projectile.- The control room upgrade system is really cool, I do hope to see more upgrades for the scythe in particular but even on it's own it allows for some really nice guaranteed damage with the first upgrade, and some interesting off build choices for the second upgrades, where you can pick a lower damage but multi-hit upgrade for infusion (On-hit effect) based builds, or a higher damage but lower range/slow attack speed upgrade for meaty damage builds. - Some spells/weapons feel very underwhelming, and some feel WAY too powerful. I wouldn't want to use some of them even if I had nothing else sometimes. Like the shuriken weapon, or the timed explosion spell. Some of them are explicitly common items and it's understandable they're not super strong in comparison to rarer items, but even as niche or early game items they still don't quite feel worth picking up. Not sure how to explain it exactly but they don't feel very good. Anyway I'm not really one for writing reviews but I'm very much enjoying my time with this game, really excited to see what the devs bring forth during early access. Will be keenly following updates!!
_childDocuments_.name: Have a Nice Death

_childDocuments_.review: I really, REALLY want to love this title and give it hours and hours of playtime. The art direction, character design, and animations are all absolutely top-notch, but...- health ("pure" health that heals you to your max hp cap, vs. animas that heal up to "damaged" soft cap hp) is excruciatingly hard to come by, meaning that by the time you get to mid/end-bosses, you're running on fumes- RNG feels very against you in terms of getting cloak actions, to the point where you can get to mid/endbosses with just your scythe- definitely a lot of "just don't get hit lol" vibes, but the dodge doesn't give nearly enough iframes, and scythe/cloak actions have way too many recovery frames, so you feel that you're not given a good toolkit to do well- gauge usage (L2/LT+scythe/cloak skills) have a wind-up that leaves you vulnerable until the animations start- curses feel pretty lackluster in terms of game balance, even the ones that have penalties assignedit feels that the game intent/design/execution all contradict each other at the moment. overall, the game feels "stingy". the game has a LOT of promise depending on where the devteam feels they are at in terms of a 1.0 release and i'm happy to change my recommendation with successive content updates

_childDocuments_.review: It plays well and is responsive and the enemy patterns are mostly fair. The weapons (apart from the basic weapon(s)) are largely interesting and runs don't feel repetitive in the first few hours.What keeps this game from being a full recommendation is the lack of  meaningful meta-progression. You can unlock new weapons, which sometimes are better, and sometimes are not, but they won't really help you to finish a run, unless the weapon is just strong by itself. That means the first run is almost hard/easy as the last one.You passively acquire XP which unlocks some minor helpful meta-progression (starting with a single charge heal-flask, unlocking life-leech in the random skill pool etc), but that doesn't feel rewarding nor is it truly on a run-by-run basis. No max HP/MANA/DAMAGE, no better starting gear, no starting skill choice etc.That makes every run basically the same "progression"-wise, which at the end, feels like you wasted your time if you died prematurely.There is an "easier" mode that has no penalty attached, which is the only help you can get to make runs truly easier.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the early build of this game long ago and been holding off on playing the game since then, till its official release drop but now the time is now ripe it would seem. Never seen a game look so stylish and visually stunning yet look so bleak at the same time, in a good way. The environment does an exceptional job at capsulizing how dreary and gloomy the cubical workspace is. Except now, you can finally say "we are living in hell"... literally. Charming narrative, lots of dark humor, smooth combat with a somewhat decent variety of builds to choose from. The game has a small arsenal of weapons but they offer a nice rage of move-sets in a form of ground/aerial directional input. Which is a big plus for a game (rouge-like) of this nature. When put into motion, everything feels very snappy and responsive (with really flashy animations to boot). Weapons and skills also have their own “EX” specials that can only be executed through the special gauge. Although, some skills/weapons are outright superior. Most of the time you probably don't even need to dodge, hell even early game you can pick up skills that can let you outright clear rooms while standing still. Some people will say the bosses can be unforgiving, but I dare say, due to how forgiving i-frame dash can be and how busted the RNG can work in your favor. The game can offer a decent challenge at times. If you are in need for another well polish action rouge-like, with beautiful hand drawn animations.Something that can go toe-to-toe with the likes of Dead cells, Hades or even Hollow Knight. Then definitely pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: As a newcomer to roguelike style games and sort of opposed to the idea of them foundationally, I actually like this. To be completely honest at this moment it's not worth 15$ as the lack of content is sort of big. Provided you're skilled enough you can get through all of the sorrows relatively quickly. Of course it provides enough challenge to make that process lengthy for me and likely most people. But the fact remains is that content is little.However, the art, fluidity of gameplay and the gameplay itself is outstanding. The theming is great. The audio is pretty good. I don't have too much to complain about. That being said my only real complaint is that the story sort of contradicts it's gameplay. Some roguelikes offer permanent progression and some have you start from scratch every time. That's fine. But the story of this game is that Death is super powerful but bored of reaping. So he takes a desk job and slowly loses his stature and strength. So why is it that through all of the killing and reaping I do, death never gets stronger? This is a major concern from a story/gameplay design for me. If you don't want any kind of progression, you shouldn't have made the story in such a way that regression is the initial problem. I think at the very least, there should be a permanent set of ability unlocks/upgrades to be had. I understand no damage bonuses and not coming back with new weapons or power ups. But why not keep the extended range scythe? Or the sickles? No matter how many times you play or how many people you kill, death never gets stronger. That's disappointing considering the funny intro to the game showing his regression.Anyways. All in all, as long as the game adds more content down the line, it's very fun to play and the artwork sells the game for me. I hope it's not too long for more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Have a Nice Death is an incredibly charming platformer/rogue-like game about toxic corporate culture and burnout.  You play as an overworked and burnt out Death whose company has been mismanaged to hell and back by his middle managers.  Your job is to whip them back into shape so that you can take a vacation.  The game plays more like Dead Cells than Hollow Knight in my opinion with some very precise and smooth movement.  It's also chock full of clever little references to workplace culture like flying books that are the physical manifestation of documentation that nobody ever bothers to read or ghosts that are created by frustrated employees forced to perform the same mundane tasks for eternity.The game has references to some pretty heavy topics and while they aren't ubiquitous, they do exist so please be aware, there is a disclaimer in the beginning that goes over more.  Otherwise this is a solid buy and a fun game that is especially vindicating if you're a heavily burnt out and overworked corporate employee such as our little friend Death here.  This game could also be considered a toxic boss simulator cause you're just going around beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of your employees instead of having an actual conversation though hmmm.

_childDocuments_.review: Played extensively (28 hours) to thoroughly examine the game before reviewing. Overall aesthetics and controls feel good when they work and curses add interesting twists. I know it's early access but at the very least in an early access game the basic controls ie; left, right, up, and down, should work. They don't break all the time but enough to get you killed and frustrated. The control's input lag sometimes doesn't allow you to turn so you are unable to attack the correct way, and that is how you stun enemies, so unexpected failure to turn and to stun leads to extra damage. Damage removes a portion of your max health unless you get one of several rare items to allow it. This means any inability to turn, such at to attack or fire your spells the right way, will just chip you down until you have 20 out of 100 max HP and get one shot.Will recommend this game once the basic control issue is fixed. Until then, even in an early access title, can't recommend this degree of input issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I had such high hopes for this game. I saw the ads, and I loved it immediatly. I was eager to try what looked like a fun, casual roguelike with a charming atmosphere and quick, responsive gameplay. And at first, that's what I got. The sound was great, the fighting felt punchy and fluid, and the animations were stunning. But as the hours set in and I started to realize just how aggravating this game is, my enjoyment was sapped away.  Besides the vary short tutorial, practically nothing was explained. The first boss was like a brick wall; no matter how many times I threw myself at him, I never felt as though I was making meaningful and satisfying progress. I found myself desperately hoping for useful spells and for enemies to drop heals. And all the while, the gameplay and music just got more and more monotonous. I shouldn't have to rely on RNG to even have a chance to beat a boss. I shouldn't have to grind for an hour to upgrade my scythe, and only find out after dying that it doesn't carry through runs. I shouldn't have to preform perfectly executed moves just to avoid taking damage on the third mini-boss arena in a row. I shouldn't have to wait a full year for the inclusion of difficulty settings. And most of all, I shouldn't have to write a three-paragraph rant about a game that had so much promise.

You get multiple cloaks / spells / buffs. The lore and stories between the employees are fantastic ( I think it is. Didnt bothered reading it ). It even has an ending. So why is it "weird".You start playing the game long enough that you kinda notice some stuffs. Understandably since its a rougelike, you are expecting it to have the "same" pattern of floor maps. Floor 1 has "two variant" of floor maps. The one in the garden and the one in the basement. This is nice. You then proceed to area 3 ( the physical / mental ) area. Yeah... that area is recycle with the same exact floor map. Maybe there is 1 change but after spending 20hrs in it, that map is the worst map overall. The tone of the music is really awful in those areas. I understand that its trying to take the area "seriously" but then you have the Waldo Burger area that has a banger OST. Also it doesnt help that choosing between physical / mental area for the buffs (red or green tree) because you can mostly just get it from the HR NPC so if anything, you want to pick the physical area as it is more safer + the boss is easier.Upgrades are a huge . In my 20 hrs run, I only manage to get ONCE a fully upgraded sword/spell/cloak together. Thats with the help of the RNG food buff. At most in a run, I only manage to usually get 4-6 upgrades because of how  difficult to get prism and money for it. .The funny thing about this game is how it looks easy and feel easy but then the enemies hit so hard like a truck that it feels like you cant really make any mistakes after area 3 onwards. Kinda ruin the enjoyment. Sure, I can lower the difficulty but if I want to fight the "secret" boss, it has to be breakdown 1 anyway so yea.So how would I rate this game? Its around a 7.5 I guess? Music is bland, art style is great, mechanics is great, balancing is bad. Bosses are great but then they hit so hard. Lore wise is great cause its comedic but its too much text. I think it all comes down to how much of a masochist you are to enjoy the punishment of the game. Again, one would say, "oh there are some spells that are super broken and makes the game easy". Sure but then its still all RNG on whether you can get those spells + buffs and I'm sure it will take multiple runs to get it which isnt that enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: The game appears to be made with a lot of love, and I really want to like it, but can not...The graphics, animations, and the overall atmosphere are just lovely, however:For an early access title, starting this game feels more like logging in to World of Warcraft after a 10 year break - you are bombarded with new systems, characters, dialogue, unlocks without any meaningful way to learn them or any motivation to care. There is a tediously long tutorial that overexplains the rudimentary basics, but fails to cover any of the important game systems. It would be great to have a better learning curve, where the game elements are introduced and explained as you progress and discover them. Some basic systems in the game are unnecessarily convoluted, and could benefit from being simplified. For example unlocks, curses or healing. After about 8 hours of playing, I still don't understand how the bizarre 2 tier health system works or what is the point of it. Standard things have unintuitive names, which creates a need for a lot of tooltips and makes already convoluted systems even harder to understand. Weapons are called cloaks? Health has wounds, vitam, anima, max HP?Curses and weapons appear to have some kind of rarity system to them. However, it is difficult to see or feel any power difference between an orange curse and a grey curse. Curses seem to somehow form a progressive tree, but the number of curses in the game seems to be much higher than what can be seen in the tree? Unlocking things between the runs doesn't feel meaningful. There is a bunch of new spells & weapons that can be unlocked for a chance to appear in the run, similar to Dead Cells. However, there are so few opportunities to find new spells and weapons during the run, it feels like investing in needles in a stack of hay. Combat is beautifully animated, however, the scythe combos can not be cancelled, which is very frustrating. Your character will be hitting the air for several seconds trying to complete the combo while the nearby minions are chomping at your health. There are not enough opportunities to heal, while some bosses and minions can kill you in few hits. I will keep an eye on this game and follow it's development, but playing it is just not enjoyable at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I've had it up to here with this player-base's lack of common sense, Just go to recent reviews and you'll immediately see my point. You'll notice most talk about things that can be solved with simple common sense, but instead choose to make mute points to make a marvelous game look like the hottest piece of trash on the market. So let me spin my review on why this game is amazing for first month release.  For the shortest answer If you're too busy with your day, its a 8/10 maybe 7 ATM. For the more dedicated or simply curious individuals, here's the more in depth review. :  Have a Nice Death is a 2D-platforming Rougelite in which you take control over Death himself in managing his own company in the afterlife, known as Death inc. The game-play loop revolves around you navigating these 2D environments via exploration, combat, and the occasional Mini-Boss/Thanagers and Area Bosses/Sorrows. To aid you in all of this your good friend T. O'Shah (not even Death himself can escape mandatory OSHA inspections), who provides you with curses which are buffs that assist you throughout your journey to beat your employees back into submission. There are several different departments you'll navigate as you venture out through the company, ranging from the damp and odorous Pollution Department, To greasy and savory Toxic Food-Processing Department; HAND is sure to deliver some creative and diverse set-pieces for your eyes to enjoy.     While most who have 'played the game' in the negative section would call it slow and clunky, this cannot be further from the truth. The game allows for diverse methods of movement, be it with your invincible Dash or even through more creative means with your Up-Slash with your Scythe allowing almost instantaneous upward momentum. The game revolves around you not taking damage and actively aids in helping you do this easier through the curses, though a good portion don't seem to understand this and chalk it up to either bad design or "difficulty". Besides your Scythe which comes equipped with several different variations you may have the chance of encountering at the very beginning of each run, Death inc. supplies you with other tools such as Cloak weapons and Spells. The key difference between the 2 being that Cloak weapons are bound by a cool-down, while Spells are dependent on Mana conservation. They are also buffed more by the red 'Attack' portion of the tree while spells have their own green 'Spell' tree, with Blue being largely for healing and defense. While minor ATM due to the games fresh release, there are some creative ways the moveset interacts with your environment, such as using your form of healing (Anima) to unlock secret rooms which house special goodies ranging from MORE healing, to temporary buffs, to even legendary spells and weapons! All of your arsenal would be arbitrary if you didn't have some good enemy archetypes to knock some sense back into, luckily you don't get skimped out there either. The game provides a wide cast of not so employee of the month co-workers for you to smack around, all fitting their environment beautifully. Reaching the end of each part of a department allows you to take an elevator through to different parts of said department, each room having its own rewards, such as Cloak Stores having one Cloak weapon by the end of that segment, Anima deposit having Anima, and so on and so forth. The ending floor for each department contains the boss or Foreman for their respective part of the company, which provide a nice challenge and are plenty fun to duke it out with. The runs end when you either reach the final boss or you perish due to being overwhelmed by the power of even later common threats.   This section will be kept very brief seeing as how it's not a MASSIVE part of the game. Now I will fully go on record and say in bias that..I love almost every character in the game. They're all so unique and identifiable with all their own quirks and kinks. I will fully admit however that some of the humor can be a little dry or can fall flat, but that rarely happens. The side quests are all cute and creative if you choose to read the dialogue which unfortunately I don't even see most content creators for the game do.   Unfortunately, I can't just be bias and say the game is perfect as it is admittedly riddled with problems. To start, lets start with the more tame issues, some achievements and Side-stories are bugged in which they will be soft-locked and inaccessible for the save file as of the most current patch. The more major changes that should definitely be looked at is how the game is balanced. The skill tree feels like there isn't too much variety in how it powers you up, though they do make you notice the difference they add to your build via the power higher tier curses gives your current run. The base game feels a tad too easy, keep in mind I am currently on breakdown 9; however I am aware that after 10 it becomes exceedingly unfair when it comes to the difficulty spike, but not impossible if you don't have an OP build. All these things I expect to be fixed though seeing as the game has only been out for little over one singular month, yet people expect the world from a new developing team not used to creating games. : Single-handedly the biggest issue is ironically enough the Devs. I don't want to give them too much hate nor unneeded critique when as a whole they did great for a first release; however their willingness to change their games vision just to appease angry "fans" needs to be looked at and addressed. I am more then glad that they are so responsive and willing to make needed changes, but when you start say lowering the skill ceiling as well as the skill floor, you start to get a game that ends up being way too easy. For a Rougelite/Rougelike, that's a pretty blatant flaw that could cause even players who sink several hours into the game, could cause them to grow disinterested.     :   There's so much more I could've gone on and on about, and arguably it could be for the better. But I simply wish to give you insight from someone who's played the game a good amount, and is looking from a perspective of a game in a very early stage of its life that can still change drastically if needed to. If I ever feel like making a follow up review or state of the game discussion, you will most likely find me in the game's Community Center. For potential buyers of the game, I must recommend it, it's cheap, fun, and a great game you can fit into your schedule with the shortest runs only lasting about half an hour. Finally to the people who have complaints like   I hope you enjoyed this albeit not very in depth review of the game, but hopefully it should suffice and lead to more conversation and thinking about what's actually good for the game vs people who deter new players when they cant even beat Brad. -Icedragon64302

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot write a real review with only nine hours of playtime. So far, I love the combat, I love how fast it can be, HOWEVER, the game crashes constantly on me. It runs perfectly well, without skipping frames or slowing down, until it suddenly dies. I would love to play for a good two hours per session, but it is quite frustrating.I like it so far, I enjoy mostly everything about it, although I cannot properly judge until I have at least beaten it once (and this is a game you want to beat many times).One other thing besides it crashing that I can mention, however, is that inputs on keyboard are not as responsive as they could be. For example, pressing "UP" then "ATTACK" launches you upwards, and pressing "DOWN" then "ATTACK" will do a down smash. However, the game doesn't register the last input you pressed, if you haven't let go of the first one. If you pressed "UP" then "ATTACK" and didn't let go of the "UP" button, then press "DOWN" then "ATTACK" the game will not input "DOWN," making you slash in the air and not come back down. That's an issue because this game is very fast paced. It's a minor issue which could be solved on the player's end, but it'd be a nice change if they tweaked that a bit. Sometimes you're just not fast enough to let go of the button, because of the game's nature. The same thing happens if, mid-air, you are pressing "LEFT" or "RIGHT," and try to smash down. If you haven't let go of "LEFT" or "RIGHT" before pressing "DOWN" then "ATTACK," you will slash mid-air.Great game so far, I hope to play more in the upcoming weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: The game is too unfair to you. When you die, you don't power up, you just rinse and repeat with a wider RNG pool of weapons. Whenever you lose health, it's nearly impossible to get back to MAX HP, literaly.I can't recomend the game on it's current form. I consider myself above the average gamer with quick reflexes, and for me it's basically a repetitive frustration, where getting to the end is mostly impossible. Let me elaborate... Whenever you die, you expect to come back stronger, but not here. You only unlock a currency to unlock more weapons that deal the same damage every round, opening even more the pool of weapons RNG that you can get. All runs are pure RNG.You have 3 types of health: 1- Your current Health; 2- The health you heal through blue orbs (they are rare); 3- The health you can heal until MAX Health.I'll explain... If you take damage, you lose current health and you lose a "pseudo" max health. If you pick blue orbs, you can't get over that threshold, only gold orbs will do it. So near the end, what has happened to me, is I have 140 Max HP, but can only heal 50 and I'm going against a boss with a current health of 20. It's impossible.Then you die, you come to the begining and you don't have anything to make you more powerful, you just have the chance to unlock more weapons to the RNG pool and there you go.You are heavily penalized each time you take any damage and the mobs after the first stage are brutal... They spit stuff from where your screen don't even show, below you or even above... So you are bound to take damage and never get it back.

_childDocuments_.review: I am seriously pissed that this somehow slipped through the cracks and I didn't play it when it fully released last year. I'd had my eye on it for a while.This game is epic. It is everything a Roguelike should be; it gives you the tools to create insane game-breaking builds, it's fast-paced and fun, the enemy variety is enough that it doesn't feel repetitive but not so overwhelming that you can't remember what each enemy does, and it has a wacky set of memorable characters and a hilarious sense of humor. Please add DLC where I can play as Pump Quinn. I will give you all my money and worldly possessions.Unfortunately, this game commits a roguelike cardinal sin by just being too darned short. It's clearly trying to do a Hades-style thing where every run you go through unlocks new dialogue and there's little narrative quests you can do by talking to people in order, but the dialogue gets exhausted pretty fast and some of the quests are bugged and straight up never initiate (I think). The thing that makes Hades so unique is that you can play it for dozens upon dozens of hours and still feel like you haven't found every conversation, which this game ends up failing to do even if the conversations it has are really funny and charming.It also expects you to play it a LOT. There are fifteen difficulty levels that can only be unlocked in ascending order by beating the game on the previous one, which is clearly meant to be the endgame "god gamer" achievement challenge that all roguelikes should have. Ok, nothing wrong with that. But there's definitely not enough content in the game to sustain playing for that long without it getting at least a little stale, even if the moment-to-moment stuff is still really fun.Overall, this is a perfect 30-hour-or-so Roguelike, a great 60-hour Roguelike and an ok 150-hour Roguelike. I still loved playing it and definitely expect to have fun doing the endgame stuff (unless it's bugged, in which case I'm outta here), but it's not going to give you Binding of Isaac levels of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of potential, but I just can't get myself to love this game.I like everything about it, except the Enemies and combat system.It's fast pace, but just feels too clunky to really have some sort of impact.Swinging the Scythe and practically becoming stationary makes the combat feel slow and leaves the player to make split second decisions to possibly dash or not before most likely being hit.The Boss battles left me finding the normal level enemies more dangerous just because they were harder to read, especially when you encounter the small closed off sections.The Spells were something I didn't really use, since they didn't feel useful, so I stuck with the Scythe almost all the time. The other weapons didn't feel any different and I couldn't find a situation where they were a better option.I ended up having issues with the movement when trying to dash and slash, but I'd end up canceling my attack or just not at all being able to have my input be registered. So I was just going in a loop trying to hit a couple enemies.I know it's in Early Access and is subject to change, but I just can't get into the flow this game provides currently. It looked amazing and felt nice, but the combat, being the biggest part of the game, doesn't feel right.It might to other players, but this threw me off too much to really find it enjoyable, outside of the visuals.I feel bad saying it, but personally it feels like the main features of the game were a little over looked, where as visuals seemed to be the priority.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a solid base and looks promising, but i feel is not quite ready yet for my tastes.Pros:Beautiful art styleFun story hookThe base makings of a great gameCons:Zones art and mob design is too repetitive, the procedural generation needs more chunks and allowed layouts to work with.Unlike many other reviews, i feel the movement is not as fluid as i would like it to be, particularly when it comes to dropping down through platforms.I really want to like this game and i expected to find it more fun than i did. With my limited gaming time, there are too many well polished games out there for me to justify being an early adopter here. I WILL keep returning to it every few months to see how it is progressing and hope to some day redo this review into a "100% definitely buy" recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot going for it in terms of art style and boss variety. Unfortunately the combat is quite spammy, with most enemies needing just a few hits to become stunned and you mash the attack button to finish them off. There is significant weapon variety but none of them change my play style at all. I don't play any differently if I am dual wielding fast scythes or have the slow windup staff, and that is a problem when it comes to the games longevity. The platforming/level layout is simple and boring. While traversing through the levels nothing is asked of you on the platforming front and you are not punished for being sloppy. Most levels are horizontal with large platforms and open spaces between combat encounters. Being a roguelite you are expected to play through the same levels over and over yet only after a few hours of play I started to become bored. Most of the damage I took was because I was rushing through everything as fast as possible so I could make it to the engaging boss battle asap. Once I realized this the game became ruined for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seriously needs some love, which it's getting, thankfully. Right now there are, as I see it, three huge issues: Healing, Upgrades and Abilities. There is not enough healing for the course of your run, however that could be ignored if the point is to not need to heal at all. But the dash, as it appears, is meant for quick movement and not actually dodging. The I-frames, or period of invincibility during/after the dodge, are abysmal. Okay, so you need to stay moving, got it. But almost all of the enemies are ranged, save for a couple. So you are mostly going to be flying around, never getting a chance to attack, and if you do, it does entirely too little. So you'll need to upgrade that, and you can. Once per run, if at all, and it isn't permanent. And it costs what you may not have. So, what abilities do you get. A lot actually! There are ranged, melee, utility, and none of them are entirely useless. You can unlock more between runs, using gold. So, I want to say one more time, nothing carries over. Every single bit of currency that you didn't spend, as well as some other stats, get turned into proportionate gold. This gold is used to unlock items that you can find during your run.That's it.That's all gold does.Which is cool, but some permanent upgrades could really help with making the game more bearableHowever, before I end, I do want to say that the devs are awesome, and have openly stated that all player concerns will be addressed when updating the game. So, All of these problems that I (And a few others) have, will likely be fixed in the future.So, yeah, TLDR: The game needs a couple huge fixes, but the devs are ready and willing. Kinda sucks as of right now though, which is understandable for early access

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review ever, just because I SO want to like and recommend this game but there really need to be some changes for it to reach it's full potential.The style and visuals are amazing, the controls feel good and reactive but oh lord does this game need some permanent upgrades. The minions you're fighting don't really feel like a challenge, but then you come up to the mini-bosses (thanagers) or bosses (sorrows) and most of the time you're just blown away. _childDocuments_.review: Have a Nice Death is a 2d action roguelite in which you play as an overworked Death suffering from burnout. Relatable, right? It has a company called Death Inc., which, you know, handles killing people and harvesting their souls on behalf of Death. Except since Death is suffering from burnout, things have gone a bit crazy in the company. After getting fed up with the dismal state of the place, it is decided: death will put the company in order again. You have basically three main attacks, which are your ever-present scythe and two special attacks using special weapons and spells you can collect. The controls are simple, with your movement, your i-frame dash, and your attacks, but that doesn’t mean you can’t do much with them. Depending on when and how you attack, you can perform all sorts of nice combos using your three weapons. You can even use a unique devastating attack with your special meter that charges as you hit enemies. I mean it,   though you won’t have access to all of them at the beginning of the game. Instead, you have to permanently unlock them between runs using ingots - a type of currency you can find - in your office. The buying system is actually pretty cool: everything has a set price but it gets progressively cheaper as you accomplish missions throughout your runs, like killing X boss 3 times or something. So if you really want something, you can unlock it as soon as you get enough ingots, but if you’re patient, you can eventually get it for a lot cheaper. You can also even change your own scythe’s attack patterns at the beginning of each run, allowing some customization for your otherwise static weapon. And if that’s all not enough, within each run you can also upgrade your weapons for the run using the temporary currency you can find, which are akin to souls.But your weapons are not the only things that offer lots of variety in the runs - far from it. If you meet up with your HR employee during your runs, you’ll  By themselves, the buffs you get are not too great, but the idea is to combine many of them to truly buff your character. You get stuff ranging from a flat defense increase all the way to infusing your attacks with different elements, adding crit chance, and others. There seem to be 3 types of curses, represented by the red, blue and green colours. While it may not look like it, and while this system might not offer as much variety as some other games in the genre, you can get some pretty crazy builds here. My first successful run had me stack up the blue defensive curses that made it so I basically took very little damage from trash mobs, and had a 30% chance to drop anima, which are healing items, upon getting hit. So what would often happen is I’d find an arena, get hit a ton because I suck, and still walk out with more health than I entered the arena with. It was absolutely insane.  I’ve seen, when doing research, plenty of reports of people getting stuck in floor 3 or such for quite some time, and I can absolutely see that happening. I managed to beat a run on my 7th or so attempt without any difficulty, but I’m pretty sure that’s just because of my busted defensive build that I was really lucky to stumble upon. This is not the norm. And if it is the norm for you, rejoice!  That’s right, everytime you get to the end, you can increase the difficulty by one level, which eventually changes attack patterns on trash mobs, thanagers and bosses.What? You have no idea what thanagers are? Well, each department has a number of floors you have to get through. At the end of all those floors, you find the department boss, which works as the main story boss for the zone you’re at, per say. However, as you clear each floor, you can choose amongst a few randomized options where you want to head to next. The name is usually a good hint of what awaits you: you have the HR floor which will certainly give you a new curse, anima floor which will definitely have an anima waiting for you at the end, etc. One of these floors, if you feel particularly daring, is the thanager floor, which has basically a miniboss waiting for you at the end, a thanager. Well, I say miniboss, but really, they even have a boss health bar. They’re just not story bosses. As I said though, the game is hard, and chances are said bosses will kill you many times.  Aside from the weapons I talked about, you can use ingots to buy decorations for several rooms in the company, and you can also level up using exp you gain at the end of each run. The levels take longer to gain, but they’re the ones that give you the best upgrades, like starting a run with one anima, out of three max, or even unlocking shortcuts that bypass entire departments and skip straight to their boss.But if you think leveling up and buying new stuff is all you’ll do between runs, you’re very mistaken.  Often, when you die, you can find new dialogue from several NPCs, usually progressing some sort of self contained story. I was privy to a strike, and I got to hold on to the edge of my seat as I saw an employee try to locate his missing shoe, just to mention a few. There’s always something going on. The dialogue is pretty funny at times, and always charming!If all you care about is the story, though, be warned that it won’t be over by the time you finish your first run. There will still be plenty for you to find before you truly get to the end, and you may, perhaps, even find a secret boss… You may also already have seen, but the game is super charming not only in its dialogue, but also in its visuals!  I mean, just look at death! Death is adorable!  I really enjoy this in a roguelite.Anyway, there’s more I can say about the game, but I’ll let you find the rest out by yourself. The basics have been covered, and that should be enough for you to decide if it is something you want to experience. As per usual, it’s not an experience for everyone, and some will not like the sometimes lackluster curses, or how hard the game can be. I’ve even seen complaints about the combos: they’re there, but if you hit enemies enough, you stun them, which makes it so you effectively don’t have to really take advantage of all your moves… at least in easier difficulties, since you can rush enemies and basic attack them a few times, stun and kill them. None of that bothered me, but it’s still worth a mention as I did see complaints. If you do pick up the game, I hope you enjoy it!
