_childDocuments_.review: This should be one of the action roguelike genre's staple. I had no major grievances apart from crashes here and there, and also the initial perceived difficulty from how fast bosses move. Tbh if you stay still and try to observe how they move, game gets a bit easier afterward. First 10 hour I got my crap kicked in, true. But you get quite a lot tools to deal with the game. Even though I win the last challenge(last boss) with so called overpowered weapons, I have to say it is not really a necessity to win. If you consider the visual and audial art. This game is quite charming. On par with the fan favourite ''Hades'' on my opinion. Animations are so slick, textures are so crispy. I really enjoyed how everything look, sound and move. As a genre hallmark, movement is very nice and comfortable. Unless I get frustrated or panicked somewhat, I get to move how I wanted %100 of the time. Lots of weapons have a good range to it, so I get to feel powerful usually. As a story and messages in dialogues, characters and enviroments there are a lot of things to unpack I think. But tbh I did not fully engage with it. Since it is a fast paced game, I didn't fully read everything. There were parodies and messages about workplace, life and the world in total all over the game. Without sounding dumber than I really am, I say they were very - in tune? -. So as a game, this is a total package. If it only crashed 1 or 2 times, I couldn't find a real con in the game. So in a perfect world, where this game does not crash; Have a Nice Death should be very much popular. The game does everything right.  Recommended to actiony platformy roguelikey game players.

_childDocuments_.review: Man. There's a lot of good decisions but some awful ones as well. I personally don't think a metroidvania style game with roguelike thrown in works. They just don't mesh to much in my opinion. I keep giving them a try though and some are fine but I never stick with them too much. Maybe when I get a steamdeck and have downtime at work or something.Anyway, this game is gorgeous. The sounds and animations are just top tier. The problem is the combat. Bosses aren't really challenging and the little enemies are...pointless. You don't have to fight them. You have a chance to get drops but the chance is so small it's more lucrative to just..run past them. Maybe make it where they're worth stuff 100% of the time, otherwise I"m spending like 1 minute or less on a level and just running through.UI is fine enough, you gotta learn what stuff is going to mean or do through some trial and error though. The descriptions could use work. Needs to be less like in binding of Isaac or more like in other roguelikes. This is probably a repurchase after it fully releases but for now this just isn't good enough. It's not bad, just not good enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game have a fantastic presentation in terms of animations and audio, however also has a fundamental issues with game mechanics that makes it extremely unfriendly to play, i can't recommend this to anyone but the most hardcore: if you beat "Enter the guneon" you might like this, if you like "Dead Cells" for it's polish and difficulty scaling, you will be left baffled by design choices,some of the issues:one: you can't cancel your input, if you invoke long heavy attack you can't dodge during it, this is quite an issue, since you are always surrounded by superior number of foes with quick attack patternstwo: whenever you take damage your max health pool is permanently lowered, there are some ways to mitigate this, but non are guaranteed, and as a result the more you play the less and less max health you have, it's like playing on Nightmare difficulty, but from the get go, when you don't even know the game yet.three: dash system have a delay that prevents you from dodging multiple times in the row, quite a problem since from very beginning you will be fighting enemies with very little "tell" but extremely fast projectiles, and often in the group

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but the difficulty balance is killing my mood for it.The health system is whack. Enemies hit like trucks while your healing is both very little and limited. Blue anima heals so little and heals to the injury threshold. Gold Anima gives around the same little heal as well and increase the threshold. Anima needs to heal WAY more especially when some Curses can give you penalties that buffs damage for enemies.There should be more indications of attacks or something. Each time I run into something new, I get killed cuz there's no indication of what kind of attack the enemy is gonna do. Then I have to start a entire new run and get all the back to where I was just to figure out what went wrong.Enemy damage and Hitboxes are the biggest problems. The first boss can kill you in like 3 hits, considering you haven't increased your starting low health pool. Once you enter area 2, the regular enemies hit just as strong as the bosses.I've lost so many runs to bad hitboxes. The Thanagers, Leon Clean & Candice have perfect examples of the bad hitboxes. All those runs lost to taking damage before the swing happens or the swing been finished but the weapon or attack hitboxes are still active. They even hit from beyond their animations.EDIT: Tried a couple more runs on the same patch above and the later enemies can destroy a third or fourth of your health bar. I even had a bunch of blue curses to increase defense and regenerate health but still getting nuked. Funny how enemies deal more damage than your anima heals even when buffed. The game is starting to feel like a "Nuke or get Nuked" type of game.EDIT 2: Did a run and got a run-ending bug. The Modern Warfare Department had a floor that didn't load the rest of the stage. That run was destroyed due to a bug.These issues are taking my "One more run" feel from this game.Hopefully it gets some more balance fixes and bug fixes soon...

_childDocuments_.review: Is it worth your money? Yes, please buy this game and support the devs. There are a few things that need polishing. But if like me your looking for that Hollow Knight fix this game will do it while very much having it's own personality. The animation is insane, there at least no more work needs to be done. The detail in the levels and all the enemies is as I said, insane. The sound is weirdly satisfying, and once you get the feel for the combat down it can be crazy fast. Here are the two bugs I ran into, the game froze once when I was selecting curses and I had to forcefully shut it down, and once a bosses health bar was gone but he didn't die. I saw a review saying that the controller support didn't work well, but I've been using a PS4 controller, and while I did reassign most of the buttons I never had any issues after that.VERY solid 8/10, when i finished probably a 10/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: After one successful run on the base normal difficulty I have to say this game is solid. The combat is fluid and fast paced, the game provides constant progression so that it does not feel stagnant even after failing again and again, and that isn't even mentioning the best part of the game, which is the animation and design department. My only complaint is that character dialogue for side quests can be a bit too wordy for such a fast paced game, but that is more than made up for by the boss dialogue, which has not had a repeated line in my 9 hours so far and seems to use your current run for a basis for what they say (for example: when I ran a build based around poison, Brad the first boss commented on how the toxic gas cloud I used was stinking up the place). Overall this game is just incredibly charming and fun and I would highly recommend it to anyone who has a liking for Rogue-Likes in general.

_childDocuments_.review: The characters and aesthetic are charming, and the music is quite good. If you really love roguelites, there's enough here that you will enjoy this game. However, as someone who is only kinda into roguelites, I found this game intensely frustrating. This game is long, trivially easy levels punctuated by very difficulty boss fights and some difficult arenas, so my experience was mostly being bored and then being frustrated as I was pitted against way too-difficult challenges. My main gripe though is the two-tier health/heals system: it is awful. Especially as a new player - you wind up with tons of the tier-1 heals that you can't use, and then you die to an especially hard arena. I could keep ranting for a while but... there's the core of a good game here. But the execution is just one disappointment after another.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the same game as the one from Early Access...This obviously goes without saying, but I feel like the game has changed drastically from what it used to be during it's development. The overload of content and update after update turned what was once a simple, quirky, yet appealing time killer into a generic try-hard. For a rogue-like, there is little freedom of choice in how to go about your next playthrough. Of the overwhelming amount of weapons and curses this game has, there are few that actually help you get through the game. Most of them will only help you through a little of the beginning while some are just useless, and the ones that are good are rare to come across. In other words, the game is luck-based. In all the hours I have put into this game, the only times I can remember beating the game were when I got lucky enough. On top of that, the game is horribly unbalanced. There are features not present before that make things too easy or too hard. You would think these two would balance each other out, but that could not be further from the truth. The "Contracts" for example. While they are a great idea on paper, and definitely fitting for this type of game, they are poorly done here. Once you progress to a certain point, you get to choose three contracts before starting a playthrough, and given the choice of four(?) random contracts to select for each of the three slots. A majority of them are terribly unbalanced to the player's favor, especially the "Take It or Leave It" contract, which basically just gives you a free item. You may also choose to change your selection of contracts at the cost of 50 gold, meaning you can basically just cycle through them and pick out the good ones to give yourself an advantage at the beginning of the game. And there is more stuff like this as you progress. Level up high enough and you can start the game with free curse re-rolls, animas, and soulary. On the first level you can choose one of three random scythes the use throughout the game, and gain elevator access to all the main bosses, allowing you to just skip through certain parts of the game entirely. Maybe these criticisms are invalid and I just don't understand rogue-likes (I don't...not entirely anyway), but I feel like being able to start the game with all this stuff right off the bat takes from the excitement of starting a game empty handed wondering what weapons and items you will collect for this playthrough. It also makes each playthrough a little less unique, I feel. Maybe I am just old fashioned, but I feel like this game was much better before all this new content. Sure it still had some problems with balance, as well as other problems of its own, but at least back then it had an excuse as, again, it was still in development. Also why did you change the soundtrack for the Physical Illness dept., Mental Illness dept., Maxxx, and Krank? The old soundtracks were much better, and I wish new players of the game could have heard it.Despite all this, and many more problems I have with the game, I still love the theme, visuals, and atmosphere of the game. The concept is neat and original, and playing as Death is a lot of fun. It is just a shame that it has all been kind of wasted by the overload of new content and the developer's "quantity over quality" mindset. The only way the game could be fixed now is with some sort of cut-back...if only the developers could go back the games roots during it's Early Access phase, and focus more on balancing it out and introducing more ways to beat the game, rather than dumping out more and more content for the game. And please bring back the old soundtrack...at least as an option. TL;DR: The game has changed. The difficulty, weapons, and curses are terribly balanced. It is mostly luck-based, with there being just about only one way to beat the game. Please bring back the old soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried to give this game a chance for 15 hours, but sadly, I can't recommend it. The art style, VFX and music are amazing, and the movement and fighting are very smooth, but the gameplay loop gets boring quite quickly, and it doesn't feel like a game has (or will have) much to offer in general, despite plenty of weapons and spells. I played it since it launched in Early Access in March 2022, and despite game receiving few content updates since then, it doesn't feel like anything was improved in terms of core gameplay and depth, and I doubt it will be improved at all.Some levels are too big without a reason - plenty of empty spaces, but not enough enemies, meaning you'll spend your time running, dashing and jumping to get to the section with enemies. The levels look really good, at least.There are 2 healing systems, which seem completely unnecessary and only create confusion.On a plus side, the game has a good sense of humour, with plenty of puns and jokes, so it will keep you entertained for a while. The music is pleasant to the ear and fits the atmosphere very well, and the elevator tune during a loading screen is a nice touch. The art style reminds of Rayman Legends, and is very strong aspect of the game, but is not enough to keep a player entertained.Would give it 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the trailer either a few months ago or a full year ago and then somehow never saw anything on it again, I'm glad steam had showed me the game on the front page of the store. It's not some hard ass game for dark souls players who have too much time to sweat off decades of their maximum lifetime to have perfect parries or dodges and scores, so if you're one of those people go back to your mother's basement.But if you like impressive visuals, vfx, comedy, and tight gameplay then this one is for you. It's not a game with extreme difficulty or even extreme RNG as I saw in someone else's review. The "rare" items appear just as much as any other item once they're unlocked. The rare part is just the time it takes to unlock them and the power they have. While getting used to mechanics and gameplay may take at least a few hours of playing it is fun and satisfying to feel invincible and fly through enemies with cool weapons and abilities. Even with the amount of times you will lose and as much I see just a few reviews saying it gets repetitive, it actually just doesn't, it gets more fun once you actually figure what you're supposed to do and can go through it with differing gameplay because of the random chance of various elements. The bosses work well and I'm impressed with the flow of the visuals and the gameplay working so well together, it just seems like that's either it's such a difficult thing to do with games, or a lot of games just don't try hard enough for such a thing. Well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true rogue-like which means when you die, you die. You start from scratch and the level layout changes a bit each time you do.  If you like these types of games you will enjoy it because hitting and dodging is very satisfying, there is a small to large learning curve, you might win due to god luck but to win consistently you will need some practice and understanding of the game. --------- *Problems* -------Moving through a level will have you fight in what becomes a closed off room, sometimes the fights are borderline impossible to get hit in, which quickly turn to impossible to not get hit in because enemies like to change direction and aim bot you. I enjoy the challenge but because of this glitch i feel scammed.--------- *Weapons* -------Unlike every rogue-like, all weapons are usable...BUT some suit a specific play style one which you might not like, this means when you buy other weapons which are less good for you, you are paying to doom your future runs.-------- *Curses* -------Curses exist to buff you unlike the name suggests. There are 3 small trees, so small that you can have almost 2 fully completed if you risk it and fight mini bosses. Now there are Good and Bad AND Completely useless, for example bleed gains 50 stacks, this buff is insane and can win you the run with good dodging skills. That buff, is USELESS if you do not have infused bleed curse, will you get it? Probably not, will Bleed, Poison and Burn related curses constantly pop up without those abilities being infused to your main weapon ever? OF COURSE THEY WILL.------- *Shop* -------Talking about useless the shop is the definition of useless and a waste of a room space. There is a penalty when taking good buffs one of which is to close the shop, always take that because that is the best part about the buff you just got!Overpriced and nothing of value, nothing that impacts a run almost in any way shape or form unless you upgrade it and lets just say in 36h of upgrading it, only ONCE did it pay off in a way because it did cost me everything i gathered that run.------- *Food* -------After a main boss is defeated you will go to a break room with a fridge that has food. This food ranges from Amazing to borderline questioning the mental capacity of developers who thought that a food that gives -10% to the shop for 2 MINUTES of game-play was good. So good in fact that this food has to be unlocked to be used and costs 5 COMPLETED  RUNS of the game meaning you need to beat the game 5 times to get enough currency, or grind 3 times that... Only 1 food is Amazing and only 3 foods are considered good one of which is the most expensive permanent item in the entire game.EDIT:I came back to the game, new content more floors more bosses more mini-bosses new items many (per the community) very broken but I did not have them. So I thought it will take me a while to beat it and was excited I streamed it to a couple of friends and found that it is far EASIER then before. I beat the game in that 1 run after a 3 month break. It was so easy that I had to stop attacking the enemies and bosses just to see what move sets and animation they had. Each time you beat it it gets "harder", the buffs the enemies get are laughable at best needing you to finish it multiple times before they can any meaningful buffs. At that point you will be warmed up so i doubt even then it will pose any kind of challenge.TL;TR (Too long to read)Good, fun game play, good learning curve very nice variety of play styles and enemies, cool boss design BUT ---> Game needs a rework of the shop and needs to tweak buffs that have affects on other buffs you might never get, needs to rework almost every food (this is done now) (buff you get after a boss battle) because the vast majority are useless. Needs to let players disable a few weapons they bought because some require a specific play style that might not be suitable to that player that bought the weapon to try it out. Needs overall AI aim bot removal (didn't care enough to look at projectiles because i was immortal) The game used to be easy to the point its boring or impossibly hard. Now it ranges from impossible to lose unless that is your goal, to waw this is how the game should feel. Opposite of what they should have done. Great for kids!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of great things about it; the art is phenomenal and the animation is smooth, the aesthetic and charm are abundantly clear, great sound design, serviceable story that only adds to the charm, funny little characters and last but not least good combat. Yes, there's a lot of good in this games if you enjoy games like deadcells or hollow knight I would definitely give it a try. It's also at a fair price point I'd say, the average roguelite enjoyer could easily spend a lot of hours in this game trying different weapons or aracana, for sure with the plan to add more content as the EA goes on.Having said all of that, it is still in EA and it is noticeable. For starters here's a couple of bugs that I have personally ran into and that are a tad annoying; 1) You can get stuck on little ledges where you have to jump to get out of being stuck, it's happened to me once during combat, I don't think I have to explain why this hampers the flow of combat/movement and is not desirable. 2) When you only have 1 cloak weapon/aracana and you switch it to the second position (I personally prefer having my arcana on B for Xbox controller), it automatically swaps back to the first position at the start of a new level. Of course this isn't a major issue but it is annoying to go to the menu and swap them around again. 3) Not really a bug, but sometimes when dashing it feels like you run into a forcefield and slowly get pushed back (happens most often with big enemies and sometimes walls) this has seriously messed with me on one of the bosses  causing me to get hit when i was trying to dash behind him to avoid his punch. 4) I think this is a bug but it could be an intentional feature, when I took the elevator to a prisium deposit I didn't find any prisium only a curse. In the same run when I went to HR to get a curse I only found a permanent health upgrade. I don't think I have to explain why this messes with trying to get the run you desire and can really hamper the experience. It could be a fun thing as a challenge mode, but in a normal run it's rather bothersome.Other than that there's some balancing issues I'd say with certain arcana/weapon cloaks dealing a lot of damage for a fraction of mana/time of other spells/weapons (looking at you boulder rain). I wouldn't suggest nerfing these as they're honestly a blast to play around with but maybe upping damage values or lowering mana values for other spells to balance it out a little. Lastly some personal nitpicks; 1) One of the curses in the red tree that you can get is more of a penalty than a bonus (talking about +15% damage cloak weapon/scythe damage for -25% damage in the one you didn't pick), this honestly is a curse that I refuse to pick up because there's almost no benefit to nerfing myself while all other curses I've found so far only gave a straight buff.2) The amount of times I find prisium deposits when leaving the control room is hurting me, I don't know if there's a way to make some sort of algorithm that checks if there will be a control room and prisium room and tries to make sure you get prisium first. This is incredibly minor but it does bother me sometimes.I know this review points out a lot of the things that are less than stellar at the moment but please don't let that dissuade you, there's a great game here that is honestly so fun to play for sure when you're in the flow of the combat, I just wish this game to get even better and for that purpose I want to highlight any and all bugs I have found and all things that personally kind of bother me. If you think this game looks fun give it a try, I don't think you'll regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I do hope this game gets better, but in it's current state I barely do not recommend this.Art and music are alright, but the graphics seem to be made for 1080p, as they feel very scuffed on a 2k display. FPS also seems to be locked at 60, though I'm not too sure that's much of a problem. Enemy projectiles have an issue of blending in with the backgrounds, which makes avoiding them a little annoying sometimes.The gameplay loop and style is very reminiscent of both Dead Cells and Hollow Knight, but falls short of what makes both masters in their category. You can get locked into attacks, unlike in other similar games where you can cancel an attack midway if you need to dodge, which feels extremely bad due to enemies being a majority ranged. It's like a bullet hell where you have to stand still to attack enemies and just watch as you tank a shot or two.Loadouts and build choices feel very... weak. Weapons/Spells other than your scythe almost always have a cooldown, mana cost, or ammo tied to them, sometimes multiple of those. This makes them feel like tools rather than alternate playstyles, and it really hinders the rougelike feel they are going for. You CAN upgrade your scythe into alternate versions, but the option to do so is entirely up to RNG via the handful of rooms you get to choose at the end of each level, and only occasionally comes up within the first set of levels. In Dead Cells, weapons feel like just that, WEAPONS. Each with their own attack pattern, strengths and weaknesses that you had to learn and master. Here they just feel like one-use damage bombs and that's it.The Curse system, their passive buff/debuff building system, really feels negligible. They have very weak effects and don't feel very useful. A lot of them seem to be "Retaliate" based, which means they activate when you get hit. That's the one thing you DON'T want to do.Healing is almost non-existent, and what is there feels really bad. The game utilizes a grey health system, where you can only restore a portion of your missing health rather than all of it. This can lead to situations where you have 3 charges of the built-in heal, but only a "max" recoverable health of say 25% your original max. The only way to regain health past this cap is to find RNG drops from enemies, shops and other sources which give "Pure Healing", and most of these options give you less than 25% health. This system feels like complete and utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It would serve the game better if the game were more fleshed out like Dead Cells, where you have a choice limited amount of health potions but have other means of gaining health through the build and weapons of your choice alongside the rng drops.Replayability, as far as I have discovered, is limited to just unlocking new weapons for new runs. No permanent buffs, no new inherent abilities, no feeling of getting stronger. You can use Souls gained throughout a run to upgrade your Scythe and additional weapons, but as soon as that run is over you lose all of those upgrades. It's hard to want to play a rougelike when they don't give the feeling of improvement with every run.

_childDocuments_.review: Managed to beat the game twice and it's a very good game overall but it has two major issues I see that are holding it back.Animations are beautiful, combat is satisfying, music is great and the game really pushes you with the variety of enemies and their attacks. It's a great game and if you don't have issues with what I'm about to mention then it's a good choice for a timesuck.My first issue is the weapon balance, and it's a joke. There are plenty of weapons that are just too weak to justify using when there are several options that you clearly lose out if you don't choose. There are interesting balance choices that I'd love to see spread out on all weapons, such as Bees' normal attack being meh while the Fury ability being a great choice to deal high and consistent damage for room clearing and bosses.My second issue is the Curses. They're great in concept, found at random in the various floors or being a reward for defeating a boss, giving it some risk and reward to gain more. However the upgrades are all tiered and will be given to you if you're high enough in the tree, kinda taking away the feeling that rougelike/lite games have of improvising a loadout on the move. The tier system is there to not give you anything overpowered when you start out, but the weapons are already ignoring that idea. It's a pretty simple fix, just increase the tier of perks with more visits to O'Shah. It plays into the reward system of giving you ingots with more stats in the run, and just makes the game more dynamic in each playthrough. Trust me if I have to win every run by just maxing out the Red curse tree which gives me lifesteal, crits on stunned, scythe damage, cape damage and infusions while using the other trees to just improve my infusions or gain termination abilities I'd rather go play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the only early access games and when you keep in mind the game is early access you are able to look past a few of it's shortcomings. There are so many things that are just fantastic about this game. To start the game is a mixture of Dead Cells and Hollow Knight and it was made directly with inspiration of Dead Cells and the devs even met with Sebastien Benard every so often to talk about the game and to ask for advice. It is somewhat similar to dead cells but it also has a lot of differences so I'll start by going through things in the game and what is amazing about them and even some negatives.The combat in this game is better than both Hollow Knight's and Dead Cells' it is insanely fast combat and has a ton of creativity with all the different scythe transformations and over 30 unique weapons. All of the bosses feel incredibly different to fight and the way the movement of the game ties into the combat is just amazing, the movement and feel of being able to attack and move is just fantastic. There are a few issues with some balance between the weapons and some weapons have bugs but these can be easily changed in future updates and more weapons will also be added in the future.An absolute bop that sells the fights and arenas incredibly well.It makes me really sad to see a negative review of this game, not because I disagree, but because it is Early Access and the author of the review most likely won't check back in and rereview the game and that is sad to me. A lot of reviews are also just flat our wrong and ignoring aspects about the game or calling it too difficult which is a common sentiment I hear from people. I personally don't think this game is very difficult at all, it is just punishing. While difficulty means it's easy to make mistakes, punishing means mistakes are more impactful.As of writing this, there is a major massive update coming May 10th and it will be adding a lot and if you want information about it ask the discord, look for the trailer, or watch the stream on their youtube which shows off a lot of the changes.  I will keep this incredibly brief because I don't have many negatives about the game at all and the ones I do can easily be patched out. There are bugs obviously, and a few weird factors like not being able to remove the cursor from the screen even though it does nothing. The infrastructure development update came out on May 11th so a lot of reviews before that are now inaccurate. I wanted to update mine with how much they have changed it. All I have to say is the game is so much more fun, this does come at the cost of some difficulty but they added so much and streamlined a lot of the boring bits of the game, particularly the start of a run. With this update I can firmly give this game a 9/10, and again I am totally willing to bump this up with future updates.Overall I absolutely love the game and what it has in it currently, it won't be for everyone but it has a ton of different aspects to love a ton more stuff is coming in the future. With how the game is now I would give it an 8.5/10, but with future updates I would probably increase that with how much they are planning to love. I highly recommend joining the discord if you want more people to talk to this game about or even comment on this review and we can discuss the game.

There is a lot to like here and not just the art style. The combat is fun and snappy, and the power-ups are interesting as well. Although, honestly, there were only a couple I really liked.This game is difficult, and I would even say more difficult than other similar games I've played. I am playing through Dead Cells atm too and had an easier time with BC4 last week than I have advancing in this one. Most of that is simply due to the RNG not really offering much. I would have entire runs with very little healing. I would sometimes make it to a boss without finding a weapon. Then I would have a run where there was a plethora of goods to be had. I usually expect some runs to be better than others, but here it just seemed to be skewed heavily in one direction or the other. An aspect it borrows from Dead Cells is that if you unlock too many weapons you will clutter the supply with a bunch of useless ones. I sort of hate this mechanic as it punishes progression. If I were to start another save I would choose more wisely. But, here I found that there was one weapon I really liked and I only found it twice in 50+ runs. But I ran into some common junk ones a lot. I could see me loving this game in the future. It really has some good bones and a solid foundation. I just don't think I want to play anymore until there have been some more updates. Do I recommend this game? Yes, sort of. You might very well love it. It is one thing to have healing e rare in rogue-lites but introducing a "wound" bar mechanic on top of limited healing is INFURIATING. Not only do you start with zero healing items, when you do find the very rare one, it only heals up to the maximum the "wound" bar will allow, and even then it doesn't even heal all the way to that most of the time. If you end up at low health at any point, chances are you are stuck therefor the entire rest of the run because there is no way to bring it back up besides with the very rare and nearly useless true healing dropped items. The devs NEED to figure something out with this by either removing the wound mechanic ENTIRELY and making healing animas do a set health percentage, or give out more pure healing items. Lastly, please for the love of god can we have a full heal after a main boss? three times in a row did I finish the second boss and walk into the third stage with almost no health and die within the first two floors.2. No real permanent progression: The only things that carry over for each run is the weapons you unlock to find throughout the run and food in the break room, that is it, nothing more. You can't increase maximum health or mana, you can't get upgrades to start with healing items, and remember upgrading your scythe with a prism? Well that's gone each run as well. I understand not wanting to hand players crutches to make the game incredibly easy, but it's another thing to feel like you are literally starting the game over from scratch each and every run with no help to get you back to where you died. there just needs to be a little more that stays persistent, look at Hades' mirror buffs, look at Dead Cells where your resource is for both unlocking weapons AND things like healing portion maximum.3. Levels are extremely small: This is fine however some of the areas just feel like hallways. it has the layout and vertical paths of Dead Cells, but NOTHING else to find throughout it and no reason to really explore and clear out the whole floor. It all feels very small trying to appear open and explorable but there is really only one path, or two that just link back together.Yes the game is good, I LOOOOOOVE the idea of it and the art direction is phenomenal, but the game itself could be better.. While I am getting very very worn out and sick of rogue-lites flooding the market I've been more than curious about this game. The problem is that it feels like the gameplay mechanics are taking a back seat and very questionable design choices are being made. Nobody is saying to copy another games mechanics, but the problem here is there are parts of the game where they really could have taken some inspiration. The few problems with the game are very glaring and frustrating so I really hope the developers listen to this feedback as it moves through early access. I still say it's good to pick up given it's only $15 but I would take the problems into account and watch to see if any of them are fixed later on.

Top of the list the Shop is absolutely garbage. Garbage. Let me repeat myself when I say that it is worthless rubbish skip at all costs and a waste of prisms. I understand this is still in early access, but these are some other minor issues a bud and I have found with the game.:4a. I've managed to break the game three times: one where I was going up and down and inputting too many commands which glitched out my character, broke the sound, then ultimately crashed the game. _childDocuments_.review: Beautifully hand drawn art animations and exciting, fast-paced combat.I'd say it's a mashup of the beautiful Hollow Knight art with the combat system of Dead Cells, which it draws heavily from. That's not a knock though, it's praise. I feel like the mantra of these games tends to be "any build can work!" - and while true, some builds vastly outstrip others in OP'ness haha. The game favors high speed and aggression, and it feels good mastering fights.Themes center around overwork and repetition in the workplace, which plays well in to the gameplay loop itself.It's still early access, so the game isn't finished and doesn't have an ending yet, but I was intrigued enough to jump early. While not complete, it's easily the most solid early access game I've played.That being said: the difficulty is not for the faint of heart. I was feeling pretty confident finishing a run on my third try, but then the second win wouldn't come until 10 or so runs later. As you complete more runs you can add "Breakdowns" which ups the difficulty in various ways, currently up to level 10. I'm finishing on Breakdown 4 as I want to wait for more content. The dev has said they're adding difficulty options ahead of its march release, which is good, because more people should play this.I had a great time, and it runs super smoothly on Deck. I put about 23 hours in.Looking forward to more content! Would recommend for the hardcore seekers who enjoy some solid art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend. Visuals and audio details are there. There's lots of love and effort put behind them and I appreciate that, but as far as gameplay is concerned, this is not it. Upgrades don't feel relevant. Curse system is bloated to hell, so much so, that you have to rely on extreme amounts of RNG to even get something that may help your build, and even then you can get railed on the last few ranks. Most of the weapons you unlock are not satisfying to use, at least to me. I've found a couple of combinations that I enjoy, but most of the variety is there for variety's sake unfortunately. Spells are disappointing. Most of the ones that sound really cool end up being a bummer. Mana cost is too high to be able to use them reliably, especially when you start out with 50 MP, and the spell costs 50 MP. Unless you get lucky and get upgrades to your mana pool early on, you're most likely gonna swap. At least I did. Scaling between stages is not where it should be IMO. Even if you upgrade your arsenal, some weapons don't scale as well, especially if you weren't lucky in getting the relevant curses. Some arena encounters can take longer, especially if your dps is behind, you can get creamed because of it. In addition to that as your health increases with each boss and mini-boss encounter; your armor does not scale with the increase in health. Unless you got the relevant food buffs and curses, your armor is gonna stay at nothing and getting hit in later stages, especially in arenas, could end your run prematurely. Also, putting equipment in your stash, but being unable to use it later on if you change your mind, is just a bad design decision tbh. Especially if you want to try out new weapons/ spells you cannot keep them as a plan B. You either sell, or put something else in their spot, in which case they just disappear. No materials, no nothing. The controls and overall feel of the game feel very smooth, certainly unfitting for the bad gameplay loop unfortunately.TL;DR: Great sound, visuals and controls. Poorly thought out upgrade system and gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to talk about something that is really pissing me off and, in my opinion, that is a fatal flaw in the game design. First off, I like the game. i have a good time even though it is repetitive, even though the gameplay isn't that new between two run, but the atmosphere, the fluidity, I have a good time. Why am I giving this a negative review then? SPOILER ALLERT/!\ _ /!\/!\ _ /!\/!\ _ /!\Now, what in my opinion makes a rogue-lite a good type of game ?1 - The feeling that the more you progress the more strong you become2 - The diversity of gameplay, forcing you to optimise your build based on what your run has to offer3 -  The replayability. Since each run is different, each obstacle, enemy will feel different as well because you will have different tools to face them.Even though the game is not perfect on all of these items, it checks some marks.Let's talk about the final boss. The REAL final boss. they though it is a good idea to make the final boss strip you of all your items, spells and, i am not sure, curses (upgrades).In a rogue-lite. You heard me right. BUT WHAT IS THE POINT OF THAT???It completely destroy the feeling of power. It will force you to have the same gameplay whatever you do during your run (auto attack that is). It destroys your items and spells; but guess what, what happens if you happen to base your run on spells and secondary weapons? Well, you are screwed my dear. What are you supposed to do then? Well, upgrade your auto attack (your scythe) and be a master at using it. But guess what, if you do that, all of your run start to feel the same, because you will have to use the same upgrades, take the same routes, and to the same thing all over again. This design alone kills the game, and this design alone is keeping me from continuing the game. Because you can increase difficulty and replay... But why would you do that if every run looks the same? I Hate this. I truly do. So yeah, there you have it. A decent game destroyed by a fatal flow (still according to my opinion). Have a nice death.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun honestly, the gameplay is the main point of enjoyment here 7.5/10 for me. (Read below for more details) The art style is really unique and cute, it mixes a really cartoon look with its own indie spin on it and it makes the more dark and gory parts of the game stand out more and makes them look better for some reason. (There's not much gore tho so don't worry)I really like the gameplay, idk why but its really fun to just run around stabbing people with the different weapons you have, the sound design and way of combat is really satisfying. The large amount of weapons also help in this aspect, there's a TON of different weapons u can use that each have their own uses and appeal. I may not like the rapier a lot, but the hammer has an oomph to it that is really nice. Not to mention, there's not only melee weapons, there's a handful of ranged weapons if that's ur thing like bows, shurikens that kind of thing. There are also magic weapons that use a different mana system that's also really cool, I usually just use a strong slow side weapon with a spammable magic weapon to do some ranged damage but there's a lot of variety here.There's not much character depth in this game (quite a given since its a rogue like) but the characters are all really cool, i like Pump Quinn and Brad the most, they have a really enjoyable personality and the Brad boss music is a bop so that helps. You'll mostly see them around the start of each level or in the breakrooms, talking to each other about company matters which is quite entertaining. They're entertaining enough that they make the gameplay loop not too monotonous.I'm not too sure about the enemies in this department, most of them can be killed by just stabbing them hard with most of them having a thing or gimmick to watch out for. For example, there's enemies that explode after u kill them or enemies that don't get staggered so u have to dodge their attack to avoid damage but for the most part the stabbing is quite the same. Majority of the enemies are quite similar, some of them follow the same archetype, the only exception are the enemies in the  department which really sort of forces u to watch out for attacks or risk getting pummeled by fire, bombs and punches.The bosses on the other hand are really fun, especially the mini-bosses for some reason. Honestly, some of the mini-bosses are more fun to fight and have more enjoyable personalities than the major ones (The major ones being the bosses who close off a department). Brad's the most fun to fight and read the dialogue of. However, it feels kinda bad that only Brad gets harder the more u play and the rest don't. When u beat brad enough times, he turns into a more professional version of himself and the boss is harder but this isn't really present in any other boss other than him.Although I've mostly talked of the enjoyable parts of the game, the game needs a bit of work, some weapons and curses are  more useful than other ones so there's a bit of changes needed there. All the areas are kinda samey with only visual differences, would be a lot nicer if there were some environmental hazards to watch out for or grounds that u couldn't stand on (such as Hades for example). Also while the game is nice, a RM 75 price tag is a bit much for what u get, there's many games that offer more for less so would be nice to get more content out of itOverall 7.5/10 would recommend but maybe get a discount on it

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece among indie games, especially rogue-likes.I saw this game pop up a couple of times in my steam homepage, it immediately caught my attention, the graphics are top notch, even to the point where it's hard to tell at times if this is an indie game or not. The game has something to it's aesthetics that i simply cannot put into words and for an early access game it's most definitely a well polished one. Gameplay wise the game isn't that hard at first glance, but later on it keeps on getting harder and harder the deeper you get into it, but never hard enough to discourage you from keep on playing. After you die the first couple of times, you can clearly begin to see and put together the rouge-like elements of the game which are really simply and neatly done. I would say that the composition of this game is perfect to the point where you can sit back, relax and sink in some hours upon hours into this gem. The game doesn't seem to have much problems at the moment, not only that but you can play it perfectly fine on keyboard (just today 11.03.2022, the devs have released an update that made the mouse and keyboard experience even better), althought it isn't fully optimized, I'am sure it will be sooner or later. My conclusion is that this game is most definitely worth the money, however if your not in a rush to play it, you can probably just wait out a sale and buy it then.

_childDocuments_.review: Well it's definitely a cute game, and artistically it's quite nice. Gameplay is smooth and responsive, enemies are well articulated except for a select few, but they're designed that way. Sound direction is top-notch, as is the elevator music. Overall the feel, and the story are on point. However, it's a Rogue-Lite game, with no permanent unlocks after death? As fas as I can tell, the only thing that you keep permanently are weapon unlocks? Maybe I'm just missing something entirely, or maybe it hasn't been implemented into the game yet, after all it is Early Access. But when comparing other side-scrolling Rogue-Lights, Have a Nice Death just isn't stacking up. Part of the fun of a Rogue-Lite is to face difficult challenges that wipe the floor with you initially, but you get stronger overtime, and over many deaths, until you can overcome the adversary. to try out, but there are huge issues with this game just about anywhere you lookIt's hard to describe this game entirely, nothing here is properly badly designed, but, it feels like the devs weren't too sure what they wanted this game to be, it seems like they mostly took ideas from similar titles that worked well, and put them together without any understanding of what makes those ideas good.From room selection to enemy type including (but not limited to) level design, progression, controls, traversal, the game feels very rough.At base value the game looks really nice but, mastering a game that is this inconsistent on so many levels is extremely frustrating, 90% of the time it feels like you've died from a lot of small reasons that really you had no way of controlling, a lot of the time you do things without even wanting to do them, your character gets stuck in a certain animation, or the screen freeze when you get hit causes your inputs to get deleted, messing up what you were doing, in most games it'd be okay to lose a few runs like this, but this game has NO META PROGRESSION, unless you can actually progress in the game you'll likely unlock nothing at all, and even then, what you unlock aren't upgrades, they're weapon unlocks, and like in most games with unlocks, a lot of them are terrible, and unlocking them makes the run harder.One other big problem I have so far with the game is the lack of explanation, the game uses a lot of terms unique to it with close to no explanation on what things do, buffs you collect don't even have the slightest text attached to them, upgrades for weapons often don't have a description, and a lot of things in general are unclear, it's a major issue when the game never explains to you some of the core mechanics.Speaking of explanation, the tutorial of this game is... Very annoying, it doesn't last super long, but it's a "tell don't show" kind of tutorial, you get walls of text flavored with useless dialogues that just drag on, to tell you base stuff like how to jump or move, but no matter where you look it's impossible to know anything about how healing exactly works in this game!I could go on and on about enemy variety being very limited and poorly exploited, bosses being absurdly RNG dependent, useless map and poor level design... But I'm not going toSo here's what I'm going to say about this game : It has amazing potential, it can be amongst one of the greatest roguelikes out there being a game as pretty and intriguing as hades, and with gameplay as varied and deep as dead cell, but for now, it ain't any of that, but given time, perhaps, and if that's the case, I'll be sure to update my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine being Death, the grim reaper, and getting fed up with the monotony of a desk job. That's the amusing premise of "Have A Nice Death," a rogue-lite action platformer. As Death, you embark on a mission to clean up souls and ensure your staff is doing their jobs.The game features cute and well-written characters, offering a refreshing change from the typical dark theme associated with the grim reaper. "Have A Nice Death" allows you to customize your office hub between runs, affecting more than just the aesthetics. For example, changing to the Halloween theme not only decorates your office with pumpkins but also influences character dialogues and interactions.While the extra levels are somewhat linear, they offer different options. As you finish one floor, you can choose from various options for the next one, like visiting the armory for better weapons, fighting minibosses, or raising your max mana.In each run, you select a scythe, which can be standard or various other forms. Sub weapons like throwing stars, hammers, and magic can be found or acquired on each floor. The combat allows for dodging through enemy attacks, but be cautious with weapons that feel like dodges but don't grant invulnerability.One issue is the noticeable frame rate drop when traveling between floors, which can disrupt the flow of the game."Have A Nice Death" boasts a fantastic soundtrack that matches the game's style and aesthetic. The cute, well-detailed graphics create a lighthearted atmosphere, helping players overlook the game's darker themes about accidents and death.The game's humor shines through Death's exasperation with his office job, offering a relatable theme. Mini-bosses have satirical names, adding to the game's humor.Overall, "Have A Nice Death" offers an enjoyable gaming experience with cute graphics, engaging gameplay, and a great sense of humor. While it has some minor issues, it's a fun roguelike that could become a beloved indie title with continued developer support."Have A Nice Death" is a game that will delight fans of roguelike action platformers with its cute characters, engaging gameplay, and a great sense of humor.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is pretty good, but it took me a little bit of time to get used to the mechanics and the health system.The health system seems to be what people complain about the most, but after playing for a decent amount of time I found it to actually not be too bad. I think the biggest thing a player has to do is acquire curses that allow them to build their defense, give them life steal abilities, or increase their health, as well as visit certain floors that will grant them more health and mana.In almost every play through, I will skip the store, I don't find it rewarding to spend a prisimium (sp?) to upgrade the store either. I only go to the store when I need an Anima. I usually skip thanagers as well since I have unlocked every weapon and food item in the game.After clearing floors, you'll have the task of choosing which floor to go to next, and the reward from each floor is represented as seen in the icon beside the floor. Ex: Weapon storage has an axe. therefore there will be a weapon on that floor as a reward of clearing it.The builds are fun, and the more you play the more weapons you unlock. The weapons you unlock can be upgraded to make them stronger, and will also unlock more abilities for that weapon. I found some weapons don't get any effects applied to them even when fully upgraded though.I find the break rooms in between floors to almost be irrelevant. You are only allowed to take 1 item from the fridge per playthrough, and the only time I take items from the fridge is when they award me pure heals or fill my Anima bar. I think it would be nice if you were given an item per break room fridge, and if that were to decrease the difficulty of the game substantially, then decrease the effects given from the items in the fridge.All-in-all, for an early access game I find this to be fun and I imagine that it only gets better from here.Thanks for listening to my TED Talk.EDIT: Animas are healing orbs.Also to elaborate on the health system, it is almost like you have two health bars. One health bar, "The foreground health bar" is the total amount of health your character has. If this health bar decreases to 0, your character dies.The other health bar, let's say the "background health bar" decreases the total amount of health that your character can recover when your character takes any damage. The only way you can recover this health is if you can acquire a yellow anima. or find an item that gives you a "pure heal".Sorry if this seems convoluted.

Didn't like this, so I decided to change to keyboard control.Keyboard Problem (opinion) ~To me, game like this, a 2d platformer, having arrow button control was a no brainer. With arrow button control, other buttons would be assigned in the "QWER,ASDF,ZXCV" area.However the default control was in WASD(no problem here) and other buttons were assigned in seemingly appropriate keyQ for special attack, E for other, SPACE BAR for jump.dash was assigned in LEFT SHIFT. slight problem here with sticky key setting, but ignorable after some window setting.You inevitably end up spamming dash button, because it gives you invincibility for a short while, so assigning it to left shift is a bad idea. The attack buttons.They were assigned in mouse buttons.Left click for default attack, right click for secondary, wheel click for tertiary.Now games such as Dungreed or Enter the Gungeon has this control because you have to be aiming at something, and/or change the direction your character is attacking.In Have a Nice Death, your character doesn't change the way he's facing. Your character just attacks the way he is facing,regardless of your mouse movement.After finding this out, I rebound my keys to what I think would be optimal binding.I changed it so that It is similar to Hollow Knight control.Which, I think, this game seems to have most in common.Movement to arrow key and others in "QWER,ASDF,ZXCV" area.But changing the movement key does not change the option(the window that shows up when pressing ESC) navigation key, which remains to be "WASD" and SpaceBar to confirm.This is kinda weird to me, because I am moving my character with arrow button, then I need to change to WASDto see what new information has been unlocked.As this is an Early Access Game, I see room for improvement, such as character death seem impactless ~ goes out with stylish pillar of light but no audible sign, so most of the time, It's justblack screen and "Rest In Papers" all of a sudden.skippable cutscene ~ this is not a big problem, but could be considered quality of life change.Overall, for now, 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Have A Nice Death (HAND) is a beautifully hand-drawn Roguelite action platformer teeming with humour, character, charm but most importantly: fluidity. I could ramble over how besotted I am with the animation and environment quality of the game for several paragraphs alone. More importantly, here are my impressions and compliments from playing the game. Death's moveset is silky-smooth and every move can be chained into another: You can string together a scythe combo, dash, spell, alternate attack, upward and downward movement all in the span of 2 seconds. When you start mastering your movement and start recognizing enemy movements, the sky is the limit for how brazenly you can play; chaining together every attack and dodge/dash in a beautiful balette of Death (himself). Oh, did I mention that your primary weapon has multiple forms with different movesets? Yeah, well, your secondary/alternate weapons most often have several moves too by holding up/down and/or by being in mid-air. To top it all off, EVERY primary, alternate weapon and spell have their own unique Super attack triggered by filling a meter which you charge up faster by mixing up your attacks with different moves and/or weapons. It's crazy. Combat is fast-paced and hectic, especially when encountering arenas ("minion hordes") and bosses. If you're unfamiliar with action platformers it's easy to get overwhelmed at first: You will most likely die a fair couple times until you start seeing progress. However, every enemy attack has a visual tell, and said attacks (wherever applicable) vary depending on distance to the player. Practice and knowledge allows you to outmaneuver even the hardest of boss patterns. Combine this with the fact that your primary attacks stun most smaller enemies in a couple hits, and you have a fantastic combat flow potentional where hyper-aggressiveness is heavily rewarded when executed properly. Additionally, charged attacks and heavier alternate weapons (aquired randomly and by choice every run) have the capacity to even easily build up to stunning bosses if you pile enough attacks on them. That being said, the game is not easy by any means. Each enemy has their own, unique attack(s). Hordes and bosses will always keep you on your toes unless you have aquired a particularly broken build, and even then you can easily die if you aren't careful. Speaking of which... Let me start this off by stating the following: The game is perfectly fair in all the challenges it presents, but balance-wise it is not perfect in its current state. It is definitely is a work in progress and the developers are perfectly aware of these problems. Some weapons/builds underperform without certain upgrades, others overperform with certain upgrades to the point of nullifying a lot of the challenges the game has to offer. This problem is further exacerbated by weapons+upgrades being somewhat RNG and the fact that basic enemies gain a flat damage reduction at higher difficulty settnings once every world, resulting in chip-damage weapons doing zero damage on later worlds/departments in a run without the proper upgrades. You need to complete the game multiple times for you to reach this level of difficulty settning, however.Additionally, to the player's advantage you have plenty of influence over the RNG in question: You can choose the primary reward for every level/floor you play, in every world. Be it extra currency, guaranteed drops for a weapon and/or spell, guaranteed stat upgrades, ability upgrades/additions, shops (which may include healing, stats upgrades, abilities and weapons), forges(where you upgrade your equipment) as well as mixes with random but often multiple rewards or levels with more enemies that have increased chances of dropping pickups.About upgrading abilities, or "curses". This is where you choose how to build your character every run, the curse system has three different ability upgrade trees where each upgrade type on every step of said upgrade tree is random but predictable and influenceable with clear power progression. The more curses you pick for a single upgrade tree, the more powerful the curses for that tree offered to you become. The trees are primarily focused on weapon damage, utility/economy/defense and spell useage+damage respectively, but may grant abilities that heavily benefit the player by mixing things up. A full run usually lasts 1-2 hours in the games current state. Which, for being a roguelite is perfectly fine in my opinion. It really feels like the game respects your time. Speaking of respecting your time, every run is a fresh start with new possibilties. As previously mentioned, there are no permanent upgrades which carry over runs. But there are unlocks. New weapons, spells, food items (boosts offered to you after every boss fight), risk vs. reward challenges/"contracts" and stacking difficulty settnings hades-style. The one area where game noticeably lacks in content is that the amount of different room layouts available is rather limited. The excellent moveset and varying playstyles provided by the arsenal of alternate attacks available makes up for this however. It took me 35 hours to reach and beat the highest difficulty of the game with the current content available as of writing this review. And I had a blast all the way through. I still have a select few unlocks to go, and will keep on playing experimenting with builds and challenging myself to different playstyles. The promise of future worlds, items and content throughout early access and hopefully further on will only add to this playtime further still.

_childDocuments_.review: I was extremely looking forward to this game because it looked ABSOLUTELY GORGEOUS. After playing for a while and also watching some gameplay videos, I now see that there's not much to it other than stunning visuals. First of all, the fact that the rooms aren't randomly generated is a HUGE problem for an action roguelite genre. To add to that, levels are way too short and way too similar. It gets extremely boring after a while.Though, my bigger problem with this game is the repetitive, button-mashing and non-challenging combat:The enemies (although I haven't seen the ones after zone 2) are pretty easy to defeat, dodging is a piece of cake and once you stun-lock the enemies you're basically invincible. The different types of weapons and spells didn't make much of a difference.I've only beaten Brad, but I've watched a gameplay video of all boss fights; and I'm sorry to say this but the bosses are an absolute joke. They take WAY TOO LONG to attack and their patterns are so easy that you could think this game was made for infants.And there are no permanent upgrades. So basically every run is the same, with the only difference being "having unlocked more weapons", which as I said, doesn't make much of a difference except visually.Overall, I see this as a huge waste of talented artists' efforts, solely due to the lack of fun. I was expecting a fast-paced, challenging and visually amazing game, but all I got was visually amazing. The gameplay is BAD. This game tried to be Dead Cells + Hades + Hollow Knight but fails hard. I hope the devs listen to feedbacks and try to improve the gameplay while it's still in early access. However, currently I wouldn't pay for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent quite a few hours in this game as you can tell, which is abnormal for Roguelite games not named Hades, Slay the Spire, or FTL. However, I think it is time to clock out, while the hours were mostly enjoyable, it feels like there are too many glaring issues with balance and mechanics that are just frustrating in the end. Will keep it spoiler-free. The games strength lies in its presentation, enemy design, and dialogue with a mostly well-designed combat flow underlying it all. But the game has horrific balancing decisions that are head scratching. I dunno where to start with mana, just awful and I sighed every time I got offered a mana upgrade/spell over health/equipment. The Skulls are pretty good, the rest just get in the way of good options. The other problem are the scythes - don't unlock more of them when offered. One of the greatest pitfalls that roguelites fall into is that as they expand your options through unlocks, they make the pool of choices you pick from worse overall. I enjoy precisely two of the scythe types - sickles or diss scythe, if I don't get randomly offered either of them, I restart. Unlocking the parasol was a mistake, as well as the weird big one you can power up. Now that might seem a bit extreme, and the sickles are primarily suited to my playstyle. The Diss Scythe? It is always, **always**, the right choice. It has long range, poor movement in the air, but that doesn't matter - it is the only weapon in the game (that I know of around 30 hours in) that deals **percentage damage**. Due to how bosses scale this gives it a huge advantage over every other scythe which need full upgrades to keep up with it. I will say again, these are the reasons that eventually led me to quietly quit - I don't overall enjoy roguelites but this one hooked me for a bit, longer than most. Take a look, see if it is your thing. If the Devs read this, there are some strange balance quirks throughout, but nothing that can't be changed.

The setting definitely has potential and the game manages to portray it in a fun and humorous (if macabre) way in the beginning; but beyond that the game just feels... hollow? Soulless?I'm fine with the rogue-like nature of few improvements between runs, but the runs themselves severely lack in variation. Fighting through an area boils down to wailing your scythe (or whatever additional weapons you've got with you) at the same 3-4 enemy types in similar sub-areas, interrupted by a few items and possibly a miniboss, until you reach the area boss and proceed to the next area; aaand repeat. As a result, each run feels like a lengthy marathon rather than an entertaining experience.The few character interactions at the beginning and between areas don't really do much to keep the motivation going, either; especially with the humorous tone the game seems to want to strike in the first place.That being said: the game is still in its Early Access phase (about halfway through, judging by release date and EA FAQ) - if the devs manage to expand the areas to offer players a bit more variation, I can definitely see myself coming back to play it more.I do look forward to future updates and won't refund the title, but in its current state I just can't recommend it.

Oyuna günde 4 saat gömecek kadar eğlenemedim çünkü kaybetmenin acısı gerçekten büyük oyunda ama yarın olduğunda direkt tekrar giresim geliyor oyuna.Oyunun eksileri diyebileceğim şeyler.Bazen dash atmıyor ya da dash buga giriyor erken erişimde oyun düzeltileceğine eminim basit bir hata çünkü.Bir de başta bug sandığım ama aslında mekanik tercihi olan bir şey var. Yanınızda bir kitap var ve o kitap sayesinde yetenek atabiliyorsunuz. Eğer sola döndüğünüzde kitap sağa dönük ise yeteneği attığınızda yeteneği sola değil sağa atacaktır. Açıkçası akıcılığı bozduğunu düşünüyorum ama alışınca ona göre oynamaya başlıyorsunuz. Diğer akıcılığı bozduğunu düşündüğüm şey ise eğer fury atmak istiyorsanız 1 saniyelik basılı tutuşun ardından fury atabiliyorsunuz bu da mekaniksel bir tercih ama direkt atılsa daha iyi olurdu diye düşünüyorum.Eklenmesi gereken şeyler:BaşarımlarTürkçe dil desteğiSilahları deneyebileceğimiz bir odave yeni içeriklerNOT: Erken erişim olduğu için içerik eksikliği hissedebilirsiniz ama size şunu söyleyeyim. Buna rağmen 9 saat oynattı 10-20 saat daha oynarım diye düşünüyorum. Dead cells ve hades erken erişimden çıktığında çok farklı oyun olmuşlardı bununda böyle olacağını düşünüyorum.EN: (Google translate)Actually I wasn't going to write a review until I won/finished the game but I spent 9 hours and couldn't finish it. I feel like it will take a long time to finish the game, so I'm writing. The game is an extremely fun rogue-like. The only part of the rogue-lite is when you die, you open in-game items that can drop, no other upgrades, it's a game entirely dependent on your skill. The game is a mixture of dead cells and hades, especially some bosses are definitely inspired by dead cells bosses.When the game first came out, it was 150 lira. At that time, my friend and I wrote to the producer's facebook, instagram, twitter accounts to bring regional pricing, and we also sent an e-mail. I don't know if we have influence, but the game dropped to 50 liras and I bought it as it fell. I definitely think it deserves the money. I couldn't have fun enough to bury the game for 4 hours a day because the pain of losing is really big in the game, but when tomorrow comes, I have to re-enter the game.What I can call the cons of the game.Sometimes the dash doesn't throw or the dash gets into a bug because I'm sure the game will be fixed in early access because it's a simple bug.There is also something that I thought was a bug at first, but actually has a mechanical preference. You have a book with you, and thanks to that book, you can throw talents. If the book is facing right when you turn left, when you throw the skill, it will throw the skill to the right, not to the left. Frankly, I think it breaks the fluency, but once you get used to it, you start playing accordingly. The other thing that I think disrupts the fluency is that if you want to throw fury, you can fury after holding down for 1 second, which is a mechanical choice, but I think it would be better if it was thrown directly.Things to add:achievementsTurkish language supportA room where we can test weaponsand new contentNOTE: You may feel a lack of content as it is early access, but let me tell you this. Despite this, it played 9 hours, I think I can play for 10-20 more hours. Dead cells and hades were very different games when they came out of early access, I think this will be the case.

There should be an option where you can at least try to beat a boss several times before you are punished so severely. Also, you can't really choose what rooms you can go to. You are very limited in that capacity. The main weapon in the game is really weak and upgrading it is difficult because you lose all your items and upgrades every time you die. The really nice thing about the game is the graphics. I have to give it to them. The graphics are beyond amazing and really cute. They manage to turn a difficult and depressing subject like death into something funny. Having said that, is the graphics only worth saving a very problematic and time wasting gameplay experience. Not for me! _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the hardest games ever for me to decide whether I'd recommend it to someone or not. The sense of style that this game oozes, the exceptional options menu, the charming and immersive music and character that this game has is some of the best in a 2d game. It just radiates character. The moveset that Death uses is also absolutely amazing. It feels like playing mini simplified Devil May Cry because of quick combos that you can pull off and how many moves each weapon has. If this is enough to get you excited to play this game, it is probably gonna be a game that you'd enjoy at least to some extent. But the issue comes from the fact that the strategies to deal with 90% of 'minion' enemies is to dash into their face while evading 1 attack and then hitting them. Once you hit them they are stunned and you just need to spam click or use a spell that is off cooldown and you are done. So all the amazing moves that you have at your disposal just come down to passing a dps check on a static enemy, and it completely shut down my will to play the game after I've realized that. That being said, the game is reviewed overwhelmingly positive and even I love so many things about this game that I am so torn whether or not to recommend it. If you resonate with what I've written here and you're someone who is a rogue like or character action enjoyer, I've made a more in-depth video because nobody (including me) will read a wall of text.

_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind that the game is in early access so some of the critiques are related to this but how do I feel about this game?Overall it's just a quick paced action game. The shining gem of this game is the combat; its fast and fluid, as you're able to easily cancel animations and use momentum to keep moving and dodging without sacrificing damage or it being too complex.However, despite being labelled a "roguelike" the rogueness of it is VERY very light. I think this is because the stages are too short. It takes about 5 stages (less in higher levels) to reach a boss in a floor, and in each stage there's about maybe 20 enemies. In the stages you can find weapons to swap or equip which add to the sweet combat and you can upgrade all of these to make them even better however this is the problem. Once you upgrade your weapons you have very little incentive of switching them out which kind of defeats the purpose of the roguelike, and although you can get "curses" (aka buffs for your playthrough), they don't do much in the way of feeling unique or changing much aside from being dificulty sliders in my opinion.Also when you are inevitably defeated and respawn, the currency you accumulate only unlocks new weapons for your next run. So you might actually invest on stuff you might not even find hours later in your playthrough so a lot of times it feels like you did nothing. What's more you're depicted as not only Death incarnate but also a corporate boss yet the power fantasy isn't really there. You never really unlock amazing god like powers and all the characters around you kind of disrespect you or have no regards for you.I think I'd enjoy this game a lot more if there was a way for me to use the resources I get from constantly running to gradually get stronger powerups that you could actually feel right away to pair with the whole concept of you being Death and all. There's also a couple parts of the game that aren't translated from French yet and the game doesn't really do a good job of explaining which room does what (Still unsure what HR Rooms do but okay!)
