_childDocuments_.review: Skunkape Games are back at it again with the Second Season of Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space. Now completely remastered; this season takes our freelance duo to new heights now with the the world rules being laid out in Save the World. Sam & Max will go all over the universe in this next journey which will take them to the likes of the North Pole, Bermuda Triangle and even Germany! All of this spans five-episodes of brain teasing spine chilling fun.Once again, the game is a standard point-and-click adventure just like the last Season. In fact, a lot of familiar elements from Save the World are retained in this second outing, meaning that everything should feel at home if you're jumping in from the first season's remaster. All control schemes from the last game are still present in this version.The graphics have gotten a great facelift. Even with the production of a sequel, the graphics back in 2008 were nothing to write home about. All the graphical improvements you've experienced in the last season is here and accounted for, even including some flashing effects which were never present in the original game (these can be turned off in the accessibility settings). The new lighting and model touch ups help to bring new life into Beyond Time and Space, just as much as it did for Save the World.The presentation as always is top notch. All sorts of additions have been made to make this season even cooler than before, like the bigger hole in the Office wall for example, which gives us an intriguing view of the office. There are a sprinkling of new Easter eggs to find this time around.  And since I might not get to mention it elsewhere, the new soundtrack pieces are a delight to listen to. The new street theme is enthusiastically toe-tapping and the addition of new music tracks for action scenes and different time periods is a very welcome change.With the arrival of this second season comes even more ballistic writing. The jokes get raunchier this season thanks to the wider variety in locales and the overall story is as wacky as ever, even getting meta at more times than not. It's best you experience it for yourself, trust me. There's a lot more visual gags to giggle at too. The arrival of Banang was imminent, but the famous recurring jokes in Telltale's Games has come back to grace us in it's original appearance.On the subject of original appearances, some of you may be highly miffed on the return of Ogie Banks as Bosco. You definitely won't have to fear this time as despite his involvement, no other change had been made to anyone's voices, or even the script for that matter. All that raunchy dialogue you've come to love is still here. And Ogie's improved performance makes up for it even more. The voice direction definitely has a noticeable improvement over the first iteration heard in Save the World. If you still don't sit right with the voice change however, a mod to restore the original versions of the lines is available.(And don't worry about any changes for Season 3, Bosco isn't in the next season at all)Overall, this was another great effort from the devs at Skunkape Games to reintroduce the gaming public to another chapter in the story of Sam & Max. This version comes highly recommended from me, the changes to visuals and presentation are too good to pass up. Season 2 in general is a great step up from Season 1. I'm highly anticipating the final chapter in this remastered trilogy, The Devil's Playhouse, the best possible conclusion to the Telltale Saga. But until then, the best version of Season 1's continuation awaits you! Experience Telltale at their next peak (before all the other ones)!
_childDocuments_.name: Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space

_childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy my time with this series, Season 2 was not major improvement over the first season. Despite it's attempt to spice things up, you still have to visit the same handful of locations and talk to the same few characters in the same street to get things done, this can make things feel small and inconsequential. However, Skunkape's modifications to the lighting and atmosphere of each chapter made everything feel like time had passed between each episode and that things were actually happening.Unlike with the comparatively more primitive first season, It's much harder to tell what the new changes and additions are (minus the most obvious ones). Things like new external building shots and similar are mostly redundant due to either not needing them or already having them. This suggests one way this season is better than the original.Definitely worth a look if you are a fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review:
Join the Freelance Police for a second season of adventure, crime-fighting, and chaos. Sam & Max Season Two starts with a giant battle robot attack and never lets up, taking our valiant crime-fighters on a gut-wrenching mission from the North Pole to Easter Island, from outer space to Hell and back.
Babies will dance. Mariachis will sing. The undead will roam the streets. And Sam & Max will risk their souls to bring you the most fun you've had playing a video game. Ever.
